100211.label: Project Objectives
100211.value: Extension of the optimal theoretical rates of convergence of the algorithms studied in [14], [5], [22], [1], [11], [3] and others to the 'outer case' (target function not in the RKHS) in the semi-supervised setting using integral operator estimates. Development of new effective algorithms in the semi-supervised setting, using the insight obtained by the theoretical analysis of the optimality of rates of convergence. Numerical testing of the performance of the algorithms on synthetic and real datasets. To develop and sharpen existing integral operator estimates for the 'effective dimension' of a distribution from random samples. The rates of convergence of existing results should be improved, and the functional form of the 'effective dimension' specialized to the analysis of different algorithms (the definition in [6] is based on RLS). To improve existing adaptation results using the empirical effective dimension to select the regularization parameter (or number iterations) of algorithms.

100211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
100211.value: The proposal considers the error analysis of various learning algorithms on Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces, and focus on those recent results available in the literature which make use of functional analytical techniques such as integral operator estimates or concentration inequalities for Hilbert space valued random variables. The purpose of the project is to show that this techniques can be conveniently extended to the semi-supervised setting, in particular regarding the problem of convergence rate optimality over suitably defined classes, statistical adaptation and effective dimension estimates for regularization parameter selection. 提案考慮對在再生產的仁希耳伯特空間的各種各樣的学习算法的错误分析，並且在利用功能分析技术例如缺一不可的操作員估計或集中不平等的Hilbert空間的那些最近結果的焦點可利用在文學重視了随机变量。 項目的目的將顯示那 這技術可以方便地延伸到半被監督的設置， 關於在適宜地被定義的類的收敛速度最優性，統計適應的問題的特殊性和 經常化參量選擇的有效的維度估計

100211.label: Realisation of objectives
100211.value: The objectives involving (adaptive) quasi-optimal rates of convergence were essentially not achieved. It resulted that the anticipated results from a previous report were in fact not correct due to a flaw in the adopted deductive argument. In fact in the derivation of "Theorem 1" from the previous report a more accurate analysis has shown the presence of an additional term proportional to -|1/2-r-s|_+ in the rate of convergence. Obviously this revised result provides some new rates of convergence in the outer case when r+s<1/2 (and therefore improves on previous results) however the new rate is never optimal (that is 2r/(2r+s)), and therefore I believe not suitable for publication. Consequently "Theorem 2" from the previous result (which was actually a corollary of "Theorem 1") resulted greatly weakened. Subsequent trials to bypass the encountered technical difficulties proved ineffective and eventually I was convinced that perhaps the type of mathematical technique involving integral operators estimates, which is the focus of the present project investigation is probably not suitable to derive the type of outer case quasi-optimality results.

100311.label: Project Title(Chinese)
100311.value: 石墨烯自旋電子學的理論研究

100311.label: Project Objectives
100311.value: To understand the spin transport and other spin properties in graphene nanostructures under the influence of spin-orbit interaction and ferromagnetic interaction so as to investigate how these effects can be used to make useful graphene spintronic devices.
rows: To understand the spin transport and other spin properties in graphene nanostructures under the influence of spin-orbit interaction and ferromagnetic interaction so as to investigate how these effects can be used to make useful graphene spintronic devices.

100311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
100311.value: Graphene has attracted a great deal of research interest for its special electronic properties. Particularly, graphene is regarded as an important material for making spintronics devices for its long spin relaxation time. There are some studies of how graphene nanostructures can be used to build qubits for making quantum computers. The spontaneous occurrence of magnetizations due to defects, doping and the edge states were also studied in detail for fundamental understanding as well as application reasons. Recently, strong spin splitting due to spin-orbit interaction was found in graphene grown on a metal substrate with a gold intercalation layer. Potentially this is a method for spin control. On the other hand, the ferromagnetic proximity effect has been investigated as a means to generate spin splitting in graphene for spintronics applications. Despite these research efforts and the importance of this research direction, our understanding of how to build effective spintronics devices for the detection, generation and manipulation of spins in graphene nanostructures is still rudimentary. It is important for the development of graphene quantum computers as well as other spintronics applications to have this knowledge. The objective of this project is to study how spin interactions such as spin-orbit interaction and ferromagnetic interaction can be used to achieve these functions in graphene nanostructures. The results obtained in this project can be used by experimentalists in the design and fabrication of graphene spintronics devices. 石墨烯的特別電子結構吸引了高度的研究興趣。因其自旋及有較長的弛豫時間，它也被認為是一種重要的自旋器件材料。除了近來一些研究怎可用石墨烯量子點來製造量子比特之外，我們對怎樣在石墨烯納米結構操控和產生自旋的了解是非常初步的。因此，怎可用自旋軌道偶合和磁鐵相互作用來產生和操控自旋是一個重要課題。本研究計劃正是研究如何做出有特別自旋功能的器件，而得出的成果可用在操控量子比特中的電子自旋及建造量子電腦。

100311.label: Realisation of objectives
100311.value: The objective of the project is 100% achieved, because we have studied important problems in the following three areas in graphene spintronics and the understanding gained can be used in the making of graphene spintronic devices: (1) creation or injection of spin or spin current, (2) detection of spin or spin current, (3) manipulation of spin or spin current. Some details about our studies are: (i) We studied the generation of pure spin current in graphene by quantum adiabatic pumping. Without the help of spin-orbit interaction, it is very difficult to generate pure spin current in graphene. Pure spin current is a very useful in spintronics as it has the up spin and down spin electrons moving in opposite directions with the net charge current being zero. So the information is purely carried by the flow of spin. We show that pure spin current can be generated by quantum adiabatic pumping. The method uses ferromagnetic proximity to cause exchange splitting in graphene and when the graphene is adiabatically pumped by two ac potentials, the up spin and down spin pumped currents depend differently on the Fermi energy. If the Fermi energy is chosen suitably a pure spin current is produced. The results were published in Journal of Applied Physics v.112 073701 (2012). (ii) Using negative refraction and internal reflection in electron optics in graphene, we can focus electrons of one spin-species into a small region and suppress the flow of electrons of the other spin-species. This device structure enables the focused injection of one spin species, which is a useful technique in spintronic devices. For example, this can be used to inject spin polarized electrons into a ferromagnetic tunneling contact or modify the magnetization of a small magnet. The results were published in Physical Review B v.86 245413 (2012) (iii) We show that pseudoparity in graphene nanoribbons can be used to spatially separate the two spin current components in a pure spin current generated by rotating magnetic field. This approach is novel as it does not require any magnetic field or spin-orbit interaction for the detection of pure spin current and can be used for pure spin current due to spin bias too. The results were published in Physical Review B (Rapid Communication) v.86 081402 (2012) (iv) Since sizable spin-orbit interaction was created in graphene through the intercalation of gold atoms between graphene and nickel, we also studied the spin transport in graphene with spin orbit interaction, which is modulated to create single barrier and multi-barrier structures. In single barrier structures, the transmitted current is highly spin-polarized when only the lowest conductance channel is occupied and when the barrier is thick enough the spin polarization is perpendicular to the direction of propagation. In multi-barrier structures, the spin polarization of the transmitted current is an oscillatory function of the Fermi energy. At some Fermi energies, the polarization is a sensitive function of the Fermi energy and as a result, we can control the spin polarization of the transmitted current by varying the Fermi energy by a small amount. This enables us to control the spin polarization of the current electrically. The results were published in Physics Letters A v.377 632 (2013) and Applied Physics Letters v.102 142407 (2013) (v) The effect of spin-orbit interaction on spin transport in a graphene Y junction was investigated. The spin polarization can be around 100% when the spin-orbit interaction is strong enough. The spin polarization can be controlled by changing the structural parameters. The conductance of the first channel is strongly suppressed by the edge states at the edges of the zigzag ribbon leads and can be significantly enhanced by the spin-orbit interaction. The results were published in Journal of the Physical Society of Japan v.82, 074711 (2013) (vi) An electron spin beam splitter was investigated using the Goos-Hanchen effect. Two ferromagnetic strips are deposited on graphene, which can have parallel or anti-parallel magnetization configuration. The separation between beams of different spin species is enhanced by the number of transmission resonances between the ferromagnetic strips. The separation can be hundreds of wavelength, which means the device can have practical application in separating spins. The results were published in Applied Physics Letters v.105 212408 (2014) (vii) We investigated a large spin-filtering effect in a graphene zigzag ribbon with a Rashba spin-orbit region. The spin polarization along the y direction of the transmitted current is large when the incident electrons or holes occupy only the lowest subband and the transmitted carriers occupy two subbands. This can be achieved using a width constriction or a gated potential barrier to the left lead so that the incident carriers occupy only one subband. This is an effective way of filtering electron spins. The results were published in Nanotechnology v. 23 095201 (2012) (viii) We investigated the spin dependent transport properties of edge-fluorinated graphyne nanoribbons. When the fluorination is asymmetric, the nanoribbons are perfect spin filter and spin negative differential resistance. They also has high magnetoresistance and spin rectification effect. When the edge-fluorination is symmetrical the spin properties depend on the width. Spin filtering can be found in even ribbons but not in odd ribbons. These properties can be used to make graphyne based spintronic devices. The results are published in RSC Advances v.6 15008 (2016) (ix) We have investigated the generation of valley current and valley beam splitter in graphene. As there is a strong interest in the effect of spin-valley coupling on the spin properties, these studies are relevant for the development of spintronic devices. The results were published in Applied Physics Letters v.104 013105 (2014), and RSC Advances v.5 8371 (2015). (x) We have also investigated some related problems in two dimensional materials and topological insulators, such as the topological edge states in silicene, carrier mobility of MoS_2 nanoribbons, Cross Andreev reflection in spin-valley topological insulators, the results were published in New Journal of Physics v.16 045015 (2014) , Phys.Chem.Chem.Phys., v.17, 6865, (2015), Physical Review B v.91, 085415 (2015).

100311.label: Major findings and research outcome
100311.value: Owing to the word number limitation, for some details, please refer to Part B section 5.3 and the papers attached in Part C. We have studied important problems in the following three areas in graphene spintronics and the results obtained can be used in the development of graphene spintronic devices: (1) creation or injection of spin or spin current, (2) detection of spin or spin current, (3) manipulation of spin or spin current. For (1), we have carried out the following studies: A. We studied the generation of pure spin current in graphene which is not easy as graphene has very small spin-orbit effect. Pure spin current has zero charge current and thus carry the information purely through spin only, which is important for spintronics. We designed a structure which can be used to generate pure spin current using quantum adiabatic pumping. This approach will play an important role in the spintronic applications. Details can be found in (i) of 5.3. B. We designed a structure in which electrons of one spin species can be focused into a point or a small region using electron optics in graphene. This can be used to inject electrons of one spin species into a small spot which can be used to make very small spintronic devices. Details can be found in (ii) of 5.3. C. We studied the separation of spin using the Goos-hanchen effect and the Rashba spin-orbit interaction in a graphene nanoribbon. These designs can be used in the injection of spins in graphene spintronic devices. Details can be found in (vi) and (vii) of 5.3. D. We showed that pseudo-parity in graphene ribbons can be used to separate spin generated by a rotating magnetic field. The technique can be used to detect spin. Details can be found in (iii) of 5.3. E. In graphene with modulated spin-orbit interaction (with a multi-barrier structure), the spin polarization of the transmitted current is a sensitive function of the Fermi energy. This result shows that we can use the Fermi energy to control the spin polarization in graphene. This result is very important for the development of spin switching devices in graphene as it shows how to control the spin polarization in graphene electrically.

100311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
100311.value: Recently there is a strong interest in the integration of graphene with other two dimensional materials in van der Waal heterostructures. It is of both fundamental and application interest to investigate the spintronic properties in van der Waal heterostructures as the combination of different materials allows higher flexibility in the design of special material properties. The understanding gained in this project can be used in the study of van der Waal heterostructures.

100311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
100311.value: Graphene, which has been isolated recently, has attracted a lot of research interest owing to its potentials in electronic and spintronic applications. The use of electron spins in devices can lead to faster devices with lower power consumption. This is the reason why spintronics is currently a very active research area in condensed matter physics and applied physics. In this project, we have studied the spin properties of graphene for the development of useful graphene spintronic devices. We have studied some important problems in the generation, control and detection of spin in graphene nanostructures. Results obtained in this project can be used in the development of useful graphene spintronic devices.

100411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
100411.value: The rapid advances in the miniaturization of chip-scale packaging technologies have prompted a rapid increase in the density of solder joints in microelectronic devices. The integrated circuits (ICs) are beginning to move to nano-scale with less than 100nm lithography, 100 million transistors, requiring more than 10,000 input/outputs (I/Os) on a 10-40 micrometers area array pitch. Downscaling traditional solder bump interconnects will not satisfy the thermo-mechanical reliability requirements at very fine pitches (<20 micromeres). Lead-free interconnect reliability has been a concern due to interfacial intermetallic compounds and high temperature reflow problems. The reliability of electronic products relating to the mechanical properties of intermetallic compound layers is even more important now than before. This is especially true for portable products, which frequently experience mechanical shock loadings caused by dropping. There is no way to solve future problems except with an increasing knowledge-base for lead-free interconnect through an in-depth of understanding the relationship between the microstructure and mechanical behavior. As new materials emerge, and the industry incorporates many different materials into the assembly process, it is also critical to be able to describe the interactions between materials and process parameters, and accurate characterization is an important pre-requisite to achieve high yield and reliability. However, nanophase and nanostructured materials, a new branch of materials research, are attracting a great deal of attention because of their unique properties and improved performances. This project will explore the modification of interconnect microstructures to nanostructures in ultra-fine lead-free solder joints for high density chip-to-substrate interconnections under combined electro-thermo-mechanical-chemical loading. Therefore, systematically modifying interconnect microstructures to nanostructures will be investigated with various service loadings individually as well as cumulatively in the proposed project. Under-bump-metallization (UBM) dissolution, intermetallic compound (IMC) formation, current crowding, atomic migration, plastic flow, and void formation in solder joints will be investigated using a Physics-of-Failure (PoF) approach in conjunction with revolutionized concepts of high temperature aging, various temperature/relative humidity (RH) (65 deg C/65%, 85 deg C/85%) testing, thermo mechanical fatigue (TMF) testing, vibration and mechanical shock via dynamic mechanical testing. Failure distribution during accelerated tests will be extrapolated to reveal the service life of electronic products based on the PoF mechanisms. It is expected that this novel PoF approach coupled with carefully planned Design-of-Experiments (DoE) will revolutionize the reliability in nanostructure interconnects and interfaces, thus laying a strong foundation for a better scientific understanding of the capabilities and limitations of such physical phenomena in nanoelectronics applications. 小型化芯片級封裝技術的快速發展促使了微電子器件中焊錫結點密度的增加。集成電路正邁向納米尺度的集成度：在一個10-40平方微米的範圍內應用小于100納米光刻工藝，集成多于1億個晶體管以及多於10,000個輸入/輸出引腳。傳統的焊錫凸點連接將無法滿足在高度精細間距的熱機械可靠性要求。無鉛焊接互聯因為金屬間複合物以及高溫迴流焊等問題引起人們許多的重視。與金屬間複合物層機械性能相關的電子產品可靠性問題變得比以前更加重要。這一問題在便攜式電子產品中尤其值得重視，因為這類電子產品遭受跌落衝擊的可能性更大。只有通過更深層次理解微細結構和機械行為間的關係來增加對無鉛互聯的知識才能解決這一將來必將面臨的問題。隨著新材料的出現和各種不同材料被融入在工業組裝生產過程中，描述材料與組裝過程的相互關係和準確表徵是達到產品高良率和可靠性的一個非常重要的前提。納米相和納米結構材料作為一個材料研究的新分支引起了研究者的高度關注，因為這些材料擁有獨特的性能和改良能力。這一項目將探索用於高密度芯片與基底互聯的超微細間距無鉛焊結點中材料從微結構到納米結構的改變影響，并將通過電，熱和化學負荷下的特殊現象來進行考察。因此，在本項目中，互聯微結構到納米結構的系統性的改變的影響將通過各種負荷獨立及綜合因素來研究。焊球下金屬化層溶解，金屬間複合物的形成，電流擁擠現象，原子遷移，可塑流動以及焊結點中空隙形成將通過物理失效方法來研究，這些方法結合了全新概念的高溫老化，各種溫度濕度測試（65 deg C/65%, 85 deg C/85%），熱機械疲勞測試，以及藉助於動態力學測試的震動和機械衝擊測試等。基於物理失效的機制將被用于推測加速測試中的失效分佈，由此來揭示電子產品的服務壽命。基于以上研究可以期待的是：這一新穎的物理失效方法結合周密計劃的實驗設計將徹底改變納米結構互聯和介面可靠性。由此為更好而科學地理解納米電子應用中的這些物理現象奠定了一個堅實的基礎。

100411.label: Realisation of objectives
100411.value: While focusing on the revised objectives, the research outcome has met them in full as indicated by the research output, and the training of PhD students as indicated in Part C, namely having developing a few preparation method for fabricating new nanostructured interconnects, its characterization, and having established a better scientific understanding towards the reliability and performance improvement for nanoelectronics on a wider basis. In addition, the graduated PhD students have ventured to a few innovative ideaas of expanding the research direction sych as particle doping, graphene addition and others for further enhancing the interconnects in terms of its various reliability performance while achieving the cost-effectiveness and viability for manufacturing. Thus, the applied research nature of the project is demonstrated, with great potential applications for industry.

100411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
100411.value: The research outcome of this project has direct benefits for the current manufacturing practice in miniaturized electronics products typically uses nanostructured interconnects to effectively connect different functional parts, in the form of joints - electrically, mechanically or thermally. This is because In the near future, more than tens of thousand input/output terminals through solder interconnects will be needed in advanced logic devices to achieve superior performance. It so happens that when only one such interconnects fails to perform well in mechanical, electrical or thermal property, the entire expensive electronic system must inevitably fail. These poor reliability phenomena of nanostructured solder interconnects will not only lead to huge waste of cost and time, also constrain the development of advance electronic products. The achievement of the project aim has provided a better solution and platform for alleviating the reliability problems of nanostructured interconnects for nanoelectronics, and yet having established a better and sound scientific understanding of the related Electronics Science, Physics, Materials Science and Engineering.

100711.label: Project Title(Chinese)
100711.value: 非線性Korn不等式及相關的問題

100711.label: Project Objectives
100711.value: It is well known that the linear Korn inequality plays a key role in the mathematical theory of linearized three-dimensional elasticity. Recent research indicates that, likewise, there are good reasons to believe that nonlinear Korn’s inequalities could play a key role in the mathematical theory of nonlinear three-dimensional elasticity. However, while the genesis and analysis of linear Korn’s inequalities rest on very firm foundations, those of nonlinear Korn’s inequalities are still at an early stage. This proposal intends to address this issue, notably through the following objectives: Further exploring and elucidating the (sometimes intriguing) differences that exist between the linear and the available nonlinear Korn inequalities; Seeking whether the continuity (for specific topologies) of the mapping that associates a deformation to its Cauchy-Green tensor can be established by direct means when there is no available nonlinear Korn inequality; Seeking whether new nonlinear Korn’s inequalities can be found (only very few such inequalities have been derived so far).

However, while the genesis and analysis of linear Korn’s inequalities rest on very firm foundations, those of nonlinear Korn’s inequalities are still at an early stage. This proposal intends to address this issue, notably through the following objectives:

Seeking whether the continuity (for specific topologies) of the mapping that associates a deformation to its Cauchy-Green tensor can be established by direct means when there is no available nonlinear Korn inequality;
Seeking whether new nonlinear Korn’s inequalities can be found (only very few such inequalities have been derived so far).

100711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
100711.value: 三維彈性理論的中心目標是找出在體力和面力及特定的邊界條件下，一個在零力的參考構形為 的彈性體的平衡狀態。此目標通過解決未知向量場為 （表示參考構形的變形）的特設方程（一個邊值問題或者最小化問題）來實現。這裏， 表示 的一點 在平衡態的新的位置。 實際上，通過一個測量或Cauchy-Green張量場 （控制和變形相關的體積、表面、長度的變化），未知 得以出現在非線性彈力方程中。 因此，很自然要去尋求作為Cauchy-Green張量場的函數的一個變形是否連續變化。這就是這個所提項目的主題。 解決此類題的一個做法是通過非線性Korn不等式。此不等式可看成是對應於線性Korn不等式（很自然在線性三維彈性理論中出現，即只保留方程中的一階項），而後者的成因和分析有著堅實的基礎。 另一種做法是通過Cauchy-Green張量場的知識恢復一個變形。 這樣的結果（連續性結果或新非線性Korn不等式）可對比較新和有前途的內稟非線性理論（其用Cauchy-Green張量本身做主要未知）做出闡明。

100711.label: Realisation of objectives
100711.value: All the objectives have been realized, and have resulted in four publications in two major journals: Mathematical Models and Methods in Applied Sciences (Ref. [1]), and Journal de Mathematiques Pures et Appliquees (Refs. [2], [3],[4]). Completely new nonlinear Korn inequalities have been found over a two-dimensional open set, with application to nonlinear plate theory (cf.[1]), and over a domain in R^n, in the spaces W^1,p and W^2,p (cf. [3], and [4]). The continuity of the recovery of a deformation from its Cauchy-Green tensor has also been established in the absence of a nonlinear Korn inequality, in the space W^2,p_loc (cf. [4]). The relation between the linear and the nonlinear Korn inequalities has been elucidated (cf. [3] and [4]). Finally, the linear Korn inequality has been put in a new perspective, by means of a new "equivalence theorem" (cf. [2]). References: [1] P.G. Ciarlet; S. 100911.value: Starting from the field equations, we shall first derive the asymptotic normal form equations (ANFEs) by the method of coupled series-asymptotic expansions. Derive the equation for determining the eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix of the ASFEs. Examine when a hyperbolic equilibrium point changes into a non-hyperbolic equilibrium point. This may yield a necessary condition for the first bifurcation. Derive the corresponding asymptotically-valid boundary conditions for the ANFEs when the two ends are lubricated/clamped/welded with/without an end twist. Then, a linear perturbation analysis can lead to the conditions for the first bifurcations. Various cases for varying parameters will be examined. Use the method of mutiple scales to obtain analytical post-bifurcation solutions. Then, the analytical formulas for the amplitudes can be obtained. Use a sixth-order difference scheme as well as the software package AUTO to compute the solutions of the boundary-value problems of ANFEs numerically. Comparisons with analytical results will be made. The approach developed will be used study some related problems mentioned above.

100911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
100911.value: When instability occurs, it can induce damage to the material or structure. Sometimes, one can also use instabilities for advantages. An example is the design of a car driver's wheel such that it will buckle under certain threshold impact so the driver can be protected. Theoretically, it is also important to study instabilities in nonlinear elasticity. Mathematically, instability is associated with a solution bifurcation, and nonlinearity is essential for the post-bifurcation solution behavior. So, studying instability is an important aspect of "understanding and exploring nonlinearity". Although it has been a research topic for a long time, analytical solutions for post-bifurcation states are rarely obtained within the framework of two/three-dimensional nonlinear elasticity. The difficulty is that the governing equations are coupled nonlinear partial differential equations and there lack of mathematical tools to solve nonlinear PDEs analytically. Analytical solutions can shed light on the physical roles played by material and geometric nonlinearity and provide clear pictures how the geometric parameters influence the post-bifurcation states. In this project, we shall study instabilities in thin tubes composed of nonlinearly elastic materials under compression and end twist. Tubes are common in numerous devices and structures, while instabilities are often observed in tubes. We intend to construct analytical (asymptotic) solutions for the post-bifurcation states within the framework of three-dimensional field equations for nonlinearly elastic materials. A methodology of coupled series-asymptotic expansions developed earlier by us will be used to derive asymptotic model equations. These equations with lubricated end conditions will be first studied analytically and numerically. We shall analyze the equilibrium point and do a linear bifurcation analysis to obtain the bifurcation condition. The multiple scale method will be used to construct the analytical post-bifurcation solutions, which will lead to analytical formulas for the amplitudes. Then, we can have clear pictures on the post-bifurcation states; in particular, it is interesting to determine when the tube bulges inward or outward. A variety of cases can arise, probably including bifurcation phenomena not reported before for nonlinear boundary-value problems. Numerical computations will also be carried out, and the numerical solutions will be compared with the analytical ones for the verification purpose. A few related nontrivial problems will also be treated in this project. It is hoped that this project could help to further understand the effects of nonlinearity on instability phenomena in solids and the analytical formulas for the amplitudes could be useful for engineering designs. 當不穩定性發生時，材料或結構可受到損害。有時也可以用不穩定性造成好處，一個例子是設計車的方向盤，讓它在一定的衝擊力下屈曲從而達到保護司機的目的。理論上研究不穩定性也很重要，數學上不穩定性是和解分叉相關的，非綫性對分叉後的形為是本質的，所以，研究不穩定性是理解和探討非綫性的重要一面。雖然這作為研究課題已經很長時間，但在二維或三維非綫性彈性框架下後分叉狀態的解析解很少得到過。解析解可以闡明材料和幾何參數對後分叉狀態的影響。在此項目，我們會研究非綫性彈性薄管在壓和扭作用下的不穩定性。薄管在很多結構和裝置中出現，也經常觀察到不穩定性，我們的目標是在三維彈性理論下構造後分叉的解析(漸近)解。一個耦和的級數及漸近展開會被用來推導出簡化的模型方程，在合適的邊界條件下我們會對此模型做解析和數值研究，我們做綫性化從而得到分叉條件，多尺度方法會被用來構造後分叉解析解，從而得到幅值的解析公式，因此，我們會對後分叉狀態有清晰的闡明。特別是我們能決定管是外凸或內凸，各類情況會被考慮，可能會發現新的分叉現象，我們也會做數值計算，並和解析解做比較，我們希望此項目能進一步幫助理解固體中的非綫性對不穩定的影響，幅值的解析公式可以有工程設計的應用。

100911.label: Realisation of objectives
100911.value: Objective 1 is completely realized. By using a series expansion in the thickness variable and asymptotic expansions for the coefficients, the asymptotic recursion relations are derived and then the traction conditions at the outer radius finish the asymptotic normal form equations (ANFEs). The procedure is also used to handle the end boundary conditions, which completes the objective 3. By linearizing the ASFEs around a pre-compressed state, we obtain the eigenvalue problem governing the bifurcation load, so objective 2 is addressed. The amplitude equations at near-critical loads, as stated in objective 2, are derived by using a multiple-scale technique for two different cases. Then, we examine in detail the influences of geometrical parameters and a new finding is that at the post-bifurcation regime a thicker tube may be softer. the singularities theory is adopted to study imperfection sensitivity, which explains why a thinner tube is usally imperfection sensitive, while a thicker tube is usually not. The analytical results are compared with the numerical ones obtained from the package AUTO (as stated in objective 5), and good agreements are found. We also take this opportunity to tackle a few other problems by using a similar methodology developed in this project, including first and second bifurcations of a nonlinearly elastic layer, buckling and wrinkling of a hyperelastic layer-substrate structure, swelling of a core-shell hydrogel structure, wave propagation in a two-material bar and phase transition in a shape memory wire.

100911.label: Major findings and research outcome
100911.value: We study the axisymmetric deformations of a nonlinearly hyperelastic tube subjected to axial compression, aiming at investigating the critical buckling stresses and modes, deriving the analytical solutions for the post-bifurcation deformations and studying the imperfection sensitivity. For a general isotropic hyperelastic tube, a coupled series asymptotic method is utilized to derive two simplified model equations with specified constraints on the tube geometry. Then, we specialize to the Blatz–Ko material. With greased end conditions, through linear bifurcation analysis, we obtain the critical stress values and the corresponding mode numbers. The analytical solutions for the post-bifurcation states are constructed by the multiple scales method. By examining the solution behavior in the post-bifurcation regime, it is found that a thick tube could be considerably softer than a thin one. The singularities theory is used to consider the imperfection sensitivity, which reveals the mechanism is the existence of two modes corresponding to the same critical stress. Numerical solutions are also obtained which confirm the validity of the analytical solutions. In another piece of work, equilibrium states of a compressible hyperelastic layer under compression after the primary and secondary bifurcations are studied by using the methodology developed in the above work. Comparisons among the obtained analytical solutions, numerical solutions based on 2D finite elements and solutions obtained by the Lyapunov–Schmidt–Koiter (LSK) method in the literature are made and good agreements for the displacements are found, which valid the correctness of this methodology. The secondary bifurcation is studied analytically by WKB method, which is verified by the numerical solution by using AUTO. By modeling a fruit/vegetable with exocarp and sarcocarp as a hyperelastic layer-substrate structure subjected to uniaxial compression, the geometrical constraint for buckled and wrinkled shapes is established. It is found that if the thickness ratio is smaller than this critical value a fruit/vegetable should be in a buckled shape (under a sufficient stress); if a fruit/vegetable is in a wrinkled shape the thickness ratio is always larger than this critical value. To verify the theoretical prediction, we consider four types of buckled fruits/vegetables and four types of wrinkled fruits/vegetables with three samples in each type. The geometrical parameters for the 24 samples are measured and it is found that indeed all the data fall into the theoretically predicted buckling or wrinkling domains. The other problems considered in this project include swelling of a core-shell hydrogel structure, wave propagation in a two-material bar and phase transition in a shape memory wire. The analytical results constrcuted reveal various important physical insights.

100911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
100911.value: The approach developed in a weakly nonlinear setting can be extended to a fully nonlinear setting and for a general shell structure (instead of a circular tube).

101111.label: Project Objectives
101111.value: To synthesize high-mobility InSb NWs with controlled stoichiometry, crystal quality and surface morphology utilizing catalytic solid-source chemical vapor deposition (CVD). To characterize InSb NWs to investigate the effect of NW composition, diameter, morphology and gate dielectric materials on the transport properties such as the carrier mobility and gate coupling efficiency. To assemble highly dense, uniform, well aligned parallel arrays of InSb NWs on Si substrates in large-scale with the NW contact printing technique. To fabricate and directly characterize NW parallel array transistors to evaluate the high-frequency response. This assessment is essential to explore the high-mobility InSb NW arrays for ultrahigh speed electronics.

101111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
101111.value: Device scaling has been the driving force for technology advancements in the semiconductor industry over the last few decades. However, silicon device dimensions cannot be scaled indefinitely and thus there is an urgent need to explore alternative device materials for future electronics. In this regard, due to the unique physical properties like excellent carrier mobility and gate electrostatics, III-V compound semiconductor nanowires (NWs) have attracted significant attention in the area of next generation devices. Notably, high performance indium arsenide (InAs) NW arrays assembled in defined locations with preferable alignment and density on silicon substrates have been demonstrated for gigahertz device operation, which elucidates their potential applications. Fundamental studies on the higher mobility nanowire material indium antimonide (InSb) are still very limited. In this proposal, we will emphasize InSb NWs to understand their fundamental properties and ultimate electrical performance limits. The aim is to achieve high-mobility and low-operating-power NW field-effect-transistor parallel arrays through a series of well-designed and systematic experiments ranging from NW synthesis and characterization to device integration studies. Such InSb NW parallel arrays are expected to induce significant impact and potency for future ultrahigh frequency electronics. 在過去的幾十年中，器件尺寸的縮小已經成為半導體行業技術提高的驅動力。然而，由於矽材料器件的尺寸不能無限制的縮小，因此我們急需為將來的電子產品開發其它的器件材料替代品。就這一點而言，三-五族複合物半導體納米線由於擁有獨特的物理特性，比如優異的載流子遷移率和柵極可控性，而被應用為新一代器件材料，已經引起了巨大的關注。值得注意的是，組裝在矽基底上的砷化銦納米線陣列具有整齊的排列和較大密度，展示了優良的性能，已經運用在千兆赫茲運作中。目前對於具備高遷移率銻化銦納米線材料的基礎研究還十分有限。在本計劃書中，我們將致力於研究銻化銦納米線的基礎屬性和電學性能的極限。我們的目標是通過一系列精心設計的和系統的合成，表徵和器件集成實驗的研究，以獲得具有高遷移率和低功耗納米線陣列場效應晶體管。我們期望銻化銦納米線陣列可以對將來的高頻電子產品帶來巨大的衝擊。

101111.label: Realisation of objectives
101111.value: In this project, we have successfully achieved all the objectives with 100% of completion. Specifically, we have developed a unique solid-source chemical vapor deposition (SSCVD) technique to synthesize III-V compound semiconductor nanowires with controlled crystallinity and morphology, especially the notorious InSb nanowires (NWs), which is known to be difficult for the synthesis in NW communities. By simply varying the amount of source powder, growth temperatures, process pressure and substrate position, etc, crystalline InSb NWs with a wide diameter range of 20 to 200 nm have been successfully obtained (Objective 1). It is noted that when fabricated into NW field-effect transistors (FETs), they demonstrate the respectable electrical performance with the electron mobility of up to 8,000 cm2V-1s-1, high on/off current ratio and on current density (Objective 2). However, most of the NW devices are functioned in accumulation or depletion mode since it is necessary to deplete the intrinsically high free carrier concentration in the NW channel in order to achieve the device OFF state. In general, FETs can be constructed in two distinct operation modes, namely depletion mode (D-mode) and enhancement mode (E-mode), and both device modes are needed for electronic circuits. At the zero gate bias, D-mode transistors exhibit a non-zero current while their E-mode counterparts operate with off current; as a result, E-mode devices are highly preferred for energy-efficient and large-scale circuit integration design as there is no need to apply a gate voltage to switch off the transistors. Here, a facile and reliable scheme is explored and developed to control the device operation by manipulating the NW device threshold voltage via a metal cluster decoration approach, which is based on the work function difference between the metal clusters deposited and the NW materials to modulate the carrier concentration in the device channel (Objective 2). Specifically, since Au metal has a higher work function than InSb NWs, its cluster decoration would shift the device threshold voltage positively to transform into E-mode operation, while the Al counterpart has a much lower work function that would negatively move the device threshold voltage to exhibit D-mode behavior. At the same time, we demonstrate a simple and effective in situ doping technique in the solid-source chemical vapor deposition of InSb nanowires on amorphous substrates employing carbon dopants. The grown nanowires exhibit excellent crystallinity and uniform stoichiometric composition along the entire length of the nanowires. More importantly, the versatility of this doping scheme is illustrated by the fabrication of high-performance p-channel NWFETs. High electrically active carbon concentrations of 7.5E17 cm-3 and hole mobility of ~140 cm2V-1s-1 are achieved which are essential for compensating the electron-rich surface layers of InSb to enable heavily p-doped and high-performance device structures (Objective 2). In addition to single NW devices, we have as well utilized the contact printing technique to achieve well-aligned, regular, dense and uniform InSb NW parallel arrays on silicon substrates in order to scale up the device output current. The NW print density and alignment can be controlled precisely by the processing condition such as the printing pressure, speed and lubrication chemicals (Objective 3). This way, several circuit component s including the n-channel metal oxide semiconductor (NMOS) inverters, employing the Au-decorated E-mode NWFETs driver and an original D-mode NWFETs load with the gate and source/drain terminals connected, can be readily achieved (Objective 4). More importantly, due to the impressively high carrier mobility and on/off current ratio of the individual NW devices, the inverters can be operated efficiently with a high frequency and a high gain. The power dissipation can be estimated as low as around 4 μW, which is comparable to the other NW NMOS reported values and being much lower as compared to their planar counterparts (Objective 4). In summary, all these findings have indicated the technological potency of these high-mobility InSb NW arrays for the active channel materials of future high-frequency electrical devices.

101111.label: Major findings and research outcome
101111.value: In this project, there are several key findings, which lead to 10 high-impact journal publications (1 Nature Communications, 1 Advanced Materials, 3 ACS Nano and others) as well as 11 presentations at various international conferences (7 invited talks). Specifically, as reported in Nature Communications 2014, we have developed a simple but unique surfactant assisted chemical vapor deposition approach to obtain crystalline Sb-based (e.g. InSb and GaSb) nanowire with the diameters down to 20 nm. As well known in the nanowire community, since Sb has a relatively large atomic size, they tend to float on top of the growing surface during the CVD synthesis. Also, due to the Gibbs-Thomson effect, small-diameter nanowires would typically initiate from small-diameter seeds with high supersaturation. This required high precursor concentration combined with the surfactant effect of Sb constituents would lead to uncontrolled nanowire radial growth. In this work, we employ sulfur as another surfactant to passivate the surface Sb atoms, which can then enable the growth of crystalline, long, uniform and thin Sb-based nanowires, exhibiting their superior intrinsic electrical properties. In addition, further CMOS applications are still limited by the lack of efficient p-doping in these nanowire materials for high-performance p-channel devices. As reported in Nanoscale 2013, we demonstrate a simple and effective in situ doping technique in the solid-source chemical vapor deposition of InSb nanowires on amorphous substrates employing carbon dopants. The grown nanowires exhibit excellent crystallinity and uniform stoichiometric composition along the entire length of the nanowires. More importantly, the versatility of this doping scheme is illustrated by the fabrication of high-performance p-channel nanowire field effect-transistors. High electrically active carbon concentrations of 7.5E17 cm-3 and field-effect hole mobility of around 140 cm2V-1s-1 are achieved which are essential for compensating the electron-rich surface layers of InSb to enable heavily p-doped and high-performance device structures. All these further indicate the technological potency of this in situ doping technique as well as p-InSb nanowires for the fabrication of future CMOS electronics. In summary, all these major findings are significant, which would bring forward the deployment of InSb nanowires for high-performance next-generation electronic devices.

101111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
101111.value: Even though there are many important findings generated from this work, there are still several major areas for the further utilization of these InSb nanowire devices. One is to evaluate the performance limit of optimized InSb nanowire devices, such as configuring them into the top-gated or wrap-gated nanowire transistors with high-k dielectrics. At present, all the studies performed are mainly focused on the back-gated transistor structure; therefore, appropriate high-k dielectric deposition directly onto InSb nanowires with minimized interface states is needed. In this case, the gate coupling and corresponding nanowire device performances are expected to improve significantly when configured into top-gated or wrap-gated configurations. Another one is to further explore large-scale utilizations of these InSb nanowires for electronic devices. Since impressive electrical performances have been demonstrated with InSb parallel nanowire arrays, it still requires a scale-up to aim for large-scale applications, such as fabricating different large-area circuit components including ring oscillators, random number generators and others. Due to their high carrier mobility and device on/off current ratio, InSb nanowires would be predicted to result in superior circuit response when they are fabricated into large-scale circuit components. All these works would push further the technological development of InSb for practical applications.

101111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
101111.value: III-V compound semiconductor nanowires (e.g. InAs and InGaAs) have been extensively explored as alternative device channel materials for next-generation electronics due to their low effective electron mass and corresponding high carrier mobility. However, InSb nanowire materials have been few reported as they are notoriously difficult to be synthesized, even though their thin-film counterparts are demonstrated with the highest electron mobility among all III-V materials to date. In this project, we have established the successful synthesis of crystalline Sb-based nanowires, such as InSb, with controlled physical properties and diameters via the surfactant assisted chemical vapor deposition on amorphous substrates. Specifically, the sulfur surfactant can passivate the surface Sb dangling bonds during the synthesis to ensure the formation of long and dense InSb nanowires without any tapering or uncontrolled radial growth. When configured into field-effect transistors, these nanowires exhibit impressive electrical properties such as high carrier mobility and on/off current ratio. Combining with the contact printing technique, nanowire parallel arrays can be readily obtained for the fabrication of various circuit components with respectable performances. All these would indicate the technological potency of employing these InSb nanowires for next-generation high-performance electronic devices.

101111.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
101111.value: In this work, we have successfully synthesized high-quality InSb nanowires utilizing the unique surfactant assisted chemical vapor deposition. When fabricated into field-effect transistors, these nanowires demonstrate superior electrical performances. Because of these interesting properties and impressive device characteristics, we have thus established many fruitful collaboration with other research groups world-wide, including Wuhan University, National Laboratory for Infrared Physics, Shanghai Institute of Technical Physics, Institute of Process Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences, and etc to further develop the potential applications of these nanowires for other practical utilizations. In addition, we have hired undergraduate students working part-time for this project, in which they have been involved in the synthesis of semiconductor nanowires and evaluation of their corresponding electrical properties. All these trainings have not only provided them early research exposure at the cutting edge of materials science, but also help accelerating the project forward at a faster pace.

101211.label: Project Title(Chinese)
101211.value: 非線性微分–差分方程准週期解的構建方法

101211.label: Project Objectives
101211.value: To develop systemically approaches to construct quasi-periodic wave solutions for differential-differnce equations. Theoretical analysis on the asymptotic property and stability of the quasi-periodic solutions will be performed. To develop an efficient numerical algorithm for the construction of exact solutions to nonlinear discrete equations. This algorithm will then be used to solve many practical problems such as discrete Schrödinger equation, Toda lattice, and Ablowitz-Ladik lattice etc.

To develop an efficient numerical algorithm for the construction of exact solutions to nonlinear discrete equations. This algorithm will then be used to solve many practical problems such as discrete Schrödinger equation, Toda lattice, and Ablowitz-Ladik lattice etc.

101211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
101211.value: Most of the physical phenomena and dynamical processes, such as particles vibration in lattices, currents in electrical networks, pulses in biological chains, can be modelled by differential-difference equations. The search for exact solutions of differential-difference equations plays an important role in the study of modern physics. Based on the recent development in constructing exact solutions for nonlinear equations, we attempt to develop in this proposed research project a systematically algebraic method to effectively construct quasi-periodic solutions of differential-difference equations. Symbolic computational technique can then be devised to tackle the complicated and tedious algebraic computation for feasible numerical simulation of these kinds of nonlinear physical phenomena. 大部分的物理現象和動力過程，如粒子晶格振動、 電網絡電流，生物鏈中的脈衝可以被微分–差分方程模擬。尋找微分–差分方程的精確解在現代物理學的研究中發揮了重要作用。基於構建非線性方程的精確解最新的發展，我們試圖在這項研究專案開發系統代數的方法構建微分–差分方程的准週期解。然後可以擬定符號計算技術處理複雜而冗長的代數計算。

101211.label: Realisation of objectives
101211.value: The investigation of discrete integrable systems has recently become active in research areas such as statistical mechanics and discrete analogues of integrable systems arisen from classical mechanics and solid state physics. The use of integrable system technique to determine explicit exact solutions for these kinds of nonlinear equations has recently drawn the attention of many scientists and engineers. This project aims at establishing a new computerizable algebraic method to deal with the complicated discrete equations and state-of-the-art numerical algorithms for the approximation of the solutions to these nonlinear equations. By introducing the Lenard recursion equations, we first derived a coupled nonlinear Sasa-Satsuma hierarchy and obtained a third order algebraic curve Km-2 of arithmetic genus (m – 2), from which we established the associated Baker-Ahhiezer functions, meromorphic function and Durbrovin-type equations for analogs of Dirichlet and Neumann divisors. A paper of title “#1: Algebro-geometric solution for a generalized Sasa-Satsuma equation” had been submitted for journal publication. The first objective of the project was realized. For numerical simulation, we extended the recently developed global meshless radial basis function collocation method (RBFCM) for solving various kinds of partial differential equations to local radial basis function collocation method (LRBFCM) that tackles the well-known ill-conditioning problem of RBFCM. The LRBFCM had been applied successfully to solve high-dimensional ill-posed problems with theoretical convergence proof and support vector technique on parallelization. A papers of title “#2: Multiscale support vector approach for solving ill-posed problems” had been published. Based on the intrinsic stable and efficient advantages of numerical integration over numerical differentiation, the LRBFCM was further extended to a brand new finite integration method (FIM) with potential to solve stiff problems with shock waves, boundary layers, and soliton-like solutions. Three papers of titles “#3: Improved finite integration method for multi-dimensional nonlinear Burgers’ equation with shock wave”; “#4: Reconstruction of inaccessible boundary value in a sideways parabolic problem with variable coefficients-Forward collocation with finite integration method” and “#5: Adaptive least squares finite integration method for higher-dimensional perturbation problems with multiple boundary layers” respectively had been published. We expect that the LRBFCM and FIM will achieve a state-of-art numerical algorithm for solving high-dimensional complex discrete system of nonlinear equations. A draft paper has been on itinerary and will be submitted later for journal publication. The second objective of this project was realized.

101211.value: Discrete integrable systems are important in many branches of engineering sciences. An accurate simulation of these complex physical phenomena requires more advanced mathematical theories and numerical tools for efficient and effective computation. This proposed research project provides a mathematical approach for obtaining exact solution on theoretical analyses and state-of-the-art computational method for feasible numerical solver.

101411.label: Project Title(Chinese)
101411.value: 正交多項式与 q 級數

101411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
101411.value: We explore several ideas involving orthogonal polynomials and orthogonal functions. We identify new functions and polynomials that have many interesting properties. These functions have the potential to appear in applied problems. We plan to study these functions in detail. Another problem is to determine the behavior of standard polynomials (of the Askey Scheme) when the degree tends to infinity and we also consider the case when a degree dependent parameter depends on the degree. We also intend to identify isochronous systems using our newly discovered biorthogonal rational functions. We also intend to use new ideas to classify combinatorial identities using the so called Rodrigues type formulas.

101411.label: Realisation of objectives
101411.value: First, by applying and developing the J-matrix method, we studied the spectrum and the spectral measures for various difference and q-difference operators and second order Askey-Wilson type operators. The corresponding eigenfunction expansion is written down explicitly in most cases. Some new orthogonal polynomials emerge, whose three-term recurrence relations are given explicitly. Next, the spectral decomposition for 5-term recurrence operators is also considered. They are related to matrix-valued orthogonal polynomials. Two examples of matrix-valued orthogonal polynomials with explicit orthogonality relations and three-term recurrence relation are studied, which both can be viewed as 2×2-matrix-valued analogues of subfamilies of Askey-Wilson polynomials. Then, we investigated some biorthogonal polynomials and rational functions as well as well as their applications in combinatorics. By using the theory of basic hypergeometric functions, we exploit the theory of polynomial expansions in the Wilson and Askey-Wilson bases to derive new identities which are not in the hierarchy of basic hypergeometric series. We also obtain combinatorial interpretations for the linearization coefficients of products of complex Hermite polynomials. We use the combinatorial interpretations to give new proofs of several orthogonality relations satisfied by these polynomials with respect to positive exponential weights in the complex plane. Finally, we derived Plancherel-Rotach asymptotics for complex Hermite polynomials, q-polynomials in the Askey scheme, as well as some other polynomials from indeterminate moment problems. Different methods are applied to obtain our asymptotic results, such as the Deift-Zhou steepest descent method for Riemann-Hilbert problems and the turning point theory for difference equations. The applications of the asymptotic results in random matrix theory are also investigated.

101411.label: Major findings and research outcome
101411.value: The J-matrix principle says that the spectrum of a tridiagonalizable operator is the same as the tridiagonal matrix representing it. Such a tridiagonal matrix can be split into irreducible blocks, and to each of these blocks there is a corresponding set of orthogonal polynomials. Moreover, the eigenfunctions of a tridiagonalizable operator can be expressed using these corresponding polynomials, and in the self-adjoint case the spectral measure is related to the orthogonality measures of the orthogonal polynomials. In this project, by considering different operators, we study their spectrum and spectral measures. Moreover, some new orthogonal polynomials are obtained; see [1] and [7]. The interest in combinatorial identities goes back a long way, but the interest in the combinatorial q-identities is of a more recent vintage. Since the 1970’s, it was realized that combinatorial identities and special function identities enrich and complement each other. In this project, we successfully give new proofs and generalizations of the combinatorial identities, and identify their origin within the theory of basic hypergeometric functions. Our discoveries also indicate the depth of these combinatorial identities. Moreover, the relation among q-series and polynomial expansions are also investigated. See [3] and [12]. The Askey-Wilson polynomials are the most general classical orthogonal polynomials in the sense that they have raising and lowering operators independent of the degree, satisfy a Rodrigues-type formula, and are eigenfunctions of linear operator which lowers the degree of a polynomial by 2. They are 4φ3 polynomials in one variable. In the 1990’s it was realized that the Askey-Wilson polynomials have a generalization consisting of a pair of biorthogonal 10φ9 rational functions. In this project, some of the deeper results about these polynomials are obtained. See [4], [13] and [14]. The asymptotics of orthogonal polynomials are always important problems in applied mathematics due to their important applications in different areas. In this project, by using different methods, we derive asymptotics for various polynomials and q-polynomials. These results are also applied to study the partition functions and critical edge behaviours in random matrix theory. See [6], [8-10] and [15]. In addition to our main work mentioned above, we also obtain some other results about orthogonal polynomials and q-series, such as their relation to coherent states in quantum optics, the Turan type inequalities and some monotonicity properties of determinants and Pfaffians. See [2], [5] and [11].

101411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
101411.value: Based on this project, there are several possible research problems in the future: 1. Study properties of the new orthogonal polynomials arising in this project. In this project, we obtained several new orthogonal polynomials who do not belong to the Askey scheme. Except the three-term recurrence relations, we don’t know too much about them. It would be interesting to find their weight functions, integral representations, zero distributions and asymptotic expansions. 2. Study biorthogonal polynomials and their applications. Recently, it is realized that biorthogonal polynomials play an important role in various areas in mathematics and physics, such as number theory and random matrix theory. So, it is of great interest to derive more properties and have a better understanding about them.

101411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
101411.value: Orthogonal polynomials and q-series are important subjects in applied mathematics. They play a significant role in many areas like combinatorics, random matrix theory, stochastic process, quantum optics and integrable systems, etc. In this project, we explore several ideas involving orthogonal polynomials and orthogonal functions. By making use of different methods, we identify new functions and polynomials that have many interesting properties. Some of these functions have already appeared in applied problems. We also determine the behavior of standard polynomials (of the Askey Scheme) when the degree tends to infinity and consider the case when a degree dependent parameter tends to infinity, too. These asymptotic results are applied to solve some universality problems in random matrix theory. With our newly discovered biorthogonal rational functions, we identify several isochronous systems. Finally, we classify combinatorial identities using the so-called Rodrigues type formulas.

101611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
101611.value: Supramolecular chemistry has tremendous impact in chemistry for the past few decades. With its very rapid development, a shift in focus among chemists working in the area from single molecules to supramolecular self-assemblies has occurred and a large number of supramolecular systems have been synthesized. One way of constructing these systems is to use metal-ligand interactions to “stitch” together organic components into larger assemblies. A very large number of these metallo-supramolecular systems have been reported, which included knots, catenanes, helicates, metallo-rings, squares, grids, ladders and boxes. The popularity of these systems probably comes from the substantial thermodynamic stability associated with them, their easiness of preparation and their beautiful structures. Also, their ability of self-healing makes them very interesting systems for applications in certain areas. We propose here to develop syntheses of new chiral pyridine-containing ligands based metallo-supramolecular self-assemblies for asymmetric catalysis. 在過去的幾十年中,超分子化學對化學產生了重大的影響｡隨著它的快速發展,在此領域中的化學家的研究焦點從單個分子轉移到超分子自組裝中來,並且合成了數量眾多的超分子體系｡其中的一種構建方法是利用金屬-配體之間的作用力把有機部份“縫合”成更大的聚合體｡大量的這類金屬超分子體系已被報導,其中包括連鎖結,連鎖環,螺旋,金屬環,正方狀,網格狀,梯狀以及盒狀｡這些體系成為研究熱點可能是基於它們的熱力學穩定,製備簡單以及結構漂亮｡此外,超分子體系的自我修復能力使得它們在某些領域的應用有非常大的吸引力｡在此我們提出發展新型含手性吡啶配體的金屬超分子自組裝體系在不對稱催化中的應用｡

101611.label: Realisation of objectives
101611.value: The objectives of the research are: 1) We have synthesized several different classes of ligands and use them for supramolecular assembly. 2) New metallocage and helicate complexes with metal centers have been prepared and studied. 3) The host–guest property of the metallocages and helicates that we have developed have been carried out and their uses in catalyzing organic reactions have been examined. All of the objectives have been achieved. Three publications based on the findings of the project have been published. The findings are very important and have lead to further development of new ligands and self-assembly that we are studying at the moment.

101611.label: Major findings and research outcome
101611.value: With a chiral quaterpyridine, a A ΛΛΛΛ-M4L6 tetrahedral manganese cage with a captured perchlorate or trifluoromethanesulfonate anion was synthesized; the captured anion is exchangeable and the removal of the captured ClO4 and theoretical calculation was carried out to study the exchange. Also, work has been carried out to develop hydrogen generation catalysts using similar tetrahedral cages. With commercially available pyridinecarboxaldehyde and m-xylenediamine, dodecanuclear hexagonal-prismatic M12L18 cages were prepared by a subcomponent self-assembly Process using cadmium(II) perchlorate and manganese(II) perchlorate. The NMR spectrum of the Cd cage shows that there are three independent ligand sets, and the X-ray crystal structure of the Mn cage reveals that the structure has both fac-Δ- and mer-Λ-configured metal centers in a 1:1 ratio. The cage structure also has a large cavity that contains five perchlorate anions. Work is still being carried out for guest recognition. With a series of chiral tetradentate pyridyl-thiazole ligands, three types of binuclear helical metal complexes were synthesized. They are the Re(I) single-stranded complexes of formula [Re2(L)(CO)6Br2], the Ag(I) double-stranded complexes of formula [Ag2(L)2](ClO4)2 and the Cu(II) triplestranded complex of formula [Cu2(L)3](ClO4)4. Each type of them has been characterized using CD spectroscopy and if possible 1H NMR spectroscopy. Three single crystal structures, one from each type, have been determined. These complexes have been used to develop new catalysts more organic transformation. In the case of the triplestranded complex of a different metal, work is being carried out for hydrogen generation.

101611.value: New catalysts based on the supramolecular self-assembles have been developed and we are in the process of developing more useful catalysts based on the new findings.

101811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
101811.value: This project is mainly concerned with fundamental studies of the reactivity of transition metal cyanamide complexes, including osmium, ruthenium, manganese and iron. Although complexes containing cyanamide (NCNH2) and its conjugate bases, hydrogen cyanamido (NCNH-) and cyanoimido (NCN2-) are known, there are very few studies on their reactivity. Similar to metal-oxo species, metal-cyanoimido species may be capable of C-H activation, e.g. via H-atom transfer, M=NCN + R-H → M-N(H)CN + R•. It may also undergo NCN group transfer to organic substrates, e.g. alkenes or phosphines. Like metal-oxo species, M=NCN may also be activated by Lewis acids, e.g. M=NCN-BF3. Thus a new class of highly active and selective catalysts for C-H activation and NCN group transfer reactions may be developed based on M=NCN. Coordinated cyanamide may be susceptible to nucleophilic or electrophilic attack by various substrates, but there have few studies of this aspect. In our pilot work we found that an osmium(III) hydrogen cyanamido complex (OsIII-NHCN) readily undergoes acid-catalyzed addition of a variety of nucleophiles. Notably it reacts with NH4+Cl- and NH2OH.HCl to generate OsIII-N=C(NH2)2 and OsIII-N=C(NH2)(NHOH), respectively. These are the first examples of metal complexes containing the parent guanidine and the hydroxyguanidine ligands. We propose to prepare a series of transition metal hydrogen cyanamido complexes and to study their reactions with various nucleophiles in order to explore the use of coordinated cyanamide as a synthon for the preparation of novel organic compounds with useful properties. In particular we would like to design a series of transition metal hydroxyguandine complexes in order to study the mechanism of oxidation of these complexes to nitric oxide. These reactions could serve as model reactions for nitric oxide synthase, which is the enzyme that catalyzes the production of nitric oxide in mammals. We also plan to use the oxidation of hydroxyguanidine complex as a strategy to synthesize a series of M-NO complexes in order to investigate their potential as photochemical NO precursors that can deliver NO to specific target tissues to suppress tumor growth. Our studies should contribute to the development of a new class of catalysts based on metal cyanamide complexes for C-H activation and NCN group transfer reactions. It should help to develop coordinated NCN/NHCN as a synthon for novel organic compounds. It should also provide insight into metal-mediated oxidation of guanidine to nitric oxide. This project could also lead to a new class of photochemical nitric oxide precursors. 此項目主要是關於一些過渡金屬包括鋨，釕，錳和鐵的氨腈化合物的反應活性的基礎研究。儘管一些含氨腈(NCNH2)以及它的共軛鹼氰胺基(NCNH–)和氰亞胺基(NCN2–)的配合物以被人報導，但是只有極少數的工作集中在它們的反應活性研究上。 與某些金屬的氧化物相似，它的金屬氰亞胺基化合物能夠激活C-H鍵。例如，通過氫原子轉移反應：M=NCN + RH → MN(H)CN + R·。同時，它也能發生NCN官能團轉移到有機底物（例如烯烴和磷化物）上的反應。與金屬的氧化物相似的還有，它能激活劉易斯酸（例如：M=NCN-BF3）。因此，以M=NCN為基礎，我們將發展一類高活性的選擇性的C-H鍵活化的催化劑和NCN官能團轉移的反應。 配位的氨腈同時對各種親電和親核試劑較為敏感，但這方面的研究較少報導。在先前的工作中，我們發現鋨(III)的氰胺基化合物經過酸化後能夠和一些親核試劑發生反應。值得注意的是，它能和NH4+Cl–和NH2OH·HCl反應分別生成OsIII- NH=C(NH2)2和OsIII-NH=C(NH2)(NHOH)。 這些是第一例含胍和羥基胍的金屬的化合物。我們打算合成一系列的金屬的氰胺基化合物並研究它們與各種親核試劑的反應。從而開發利用配位的氨腈作為合成子去製備一些帶有有用性能的有機化合物。特別重要的是，我們將設計一系列的羥基胍的金屬的化合物並研究它們經過氧化後形成一氧化氮的反應機理。這些反應將可用作一氧化氮合成酶(在哺乳動物體內，一種催化形成一氧化氮的酶)的模型反應。我們也打算利用氧化羥基胍的金屬化合物作為一種策略去合成一系列的金屬亞硝酰基的化合物(M-NO)。 我們的研究將以金屬氨腈化合物為基礎，發展一類新的活化C-H鍵的催化劑和NCN官能團轉移的反應。這將進一步發展利用配位的NCN/NHCN作為合成子去得到新奇的有機化合物。這也將對金屬協助的氧化胍形成一氧化氮的反應提供一些見解。同時，此項研究將得到一系列的光化學反應的一氧化氮的先驅體。

101811.label: Realisation of objectives
101811.value: Objective 1: Novel osmium and ruthenium cyanoimdo complexes have been synthesized and characterized by various spectroscopic techniques, as well as by X-ray crystallography. Objective 2: The C-H activation reactions of a number of cyanoimido complexes of ruthenium(III) and osmium(III) have been investigated. Objective 3 and 4: The reaction of an osmium(III) cyanoimdo complex with various electrophiles and nucleophiles have been studied. In particular it reacts with NH4Cl and NH2OH.HCl to generate the first examples of a transition metal guanidine and hydroxyguanidine complex, respectively. These complexes have been characterized by various spectroscopic techniques and by X-ray crystallography. Objective 5: The oxidation of an osmium(III) N-hydroxyguanidine complex has been investigated in detail. We found that this complex readily undergoes aerobic oxidation at ambient conditions to generate NO. The oxidation is pH-dependent; at pH 6.8 the NO produced is bound to the osmium center, while at pH 12 free NO is produced. Our findings suggest that N-hydroxyguanidine complexes are potentially a new class of NO releasing agents.

101811.label: Major findings and research outcome
101811.value: In this project fundamental studies of the synthesis and reactivity of transition metal cyanamide complexes have been carried out. The main results are summarized below: 1. We have synthesized an osmium(III) cyanamide complex. This complex readily undergoes acid catalyzed addition of a variety of nucleophiles. Notably it reacts with NH4+Cl- and NH2OH.HCl to generate OsIII-N=C(NH2)2 and OsIII-N=C(NH2)(NHOH), respectively. These are the first examples of metal complexes containing the parent guanidine and hydroxyguanidine ligands. 2. We have investigated the aerobic oxidation of the osmium(III) N-hydroxyguanidine complex. This complex is readily oxidized by air at ambient conditions to generate NO. The oxidation is pH dependent; at pH 6.8 the NO produced is bound to the osmium center, while at pH 12 free NO is produced. Our findings should provide insights into how NO is produced in our body. 3. We have prepared a novel 7-cooordinate osmium(V) oxo complex, which is the first example of a seven-coordinate group 8 metal-oxo species, [OsV(O)(qpy)(pic)Cl]2+ qpy=2,2’:6’,2’’:6’’,2’’’-quaterpyridine, pic=4-picoline). The X-ray crystal structure of this complex shows that it has a distorted pentagonal bipyramidal geometry with an Os=O distance of 1.7375 Ǻ. This oxo species undergoes facile O-atom and H-atom-transfer reactions with various organic substrates. Notably it can abstract H atoms from alkylaromatics with C-bond dissociation energy as high as 90 kcal mol-1. This work suggests that highly active oxidants may be designed based on group 8 seven-coordinate metal oxo species. This complex can be used as a precursor for the synthesis of novel 7-coordinate osmium cyanoimido complexes. 4. The oxidation of phenols by HFeO4− proceeds via a hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) mechanism, as evidenced by a large deuterium isotope effect and a linear correlation between the log(rate constant) and bond dissociation free energy (BDFE) of phenols. The Marcus cross relation has been applied to predict the rate constant of HAT from hydroquinone to HFeO4. This result will provide insight into the use of ferrate as a precursor for cyanamide, guanidine and hydroxyguanidine complexes.

101811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
101811.value: In the present study the cyanoimido complexes prepared are mostly in +IIII oxidation state. In future high-valent manganese, iron and ruthenium cyanoimido complexes in +IV to +VI oxidation states will be investigated. These complexes are anticipated to be highly active species for C-H activation, e.g. via H-atom transfer, M=NCN + R-H → M-N(H)CN + R•. It may also undergo NCN group transfer to organic substrates, e.g. alkenes or phosphines. Like metal-oxo species, M=NCN may also be activated by Lewis acids, e.g. M=NCN-BF3. Thus a new class of highly active and selective catalysts for C-H activation and NCN group transfer reactions may be developed based on M=NCN.

101811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
101811.value: Although complexes containing cyanamide (NCNH2) and its conjugate bases, hydrogen cyanamido (NCNH-) and cyanoimido (NCN2-) ligands are known, there are very few studies on their reactivity. In this project we have studied the reactivity of a number of these complexes. Our results show that these complexes are potentially a new class of catalysts for C-H activation and NCN group transfer reactions. Useful organic compounds may be synthesized using this strategy. We have also demonstrated that cyanamide complexes are useful precursors for guanidine and N-hydroxyguanidine complexes, which are potentially a new class NO releasing agents. NO is a very important signalling agent in our body, and NO deficiency may lead to various diseases.

102211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
102211.value: Metamaterials are man-made composites which have been found to have exotic and interesting optical properties, such as negative refractive indices and invisibility cloaking. Actually, a lot of these properties come from the fact that these materials take parts in artificial magnetism. While the magnetic responses of conventional atomic and molecular media are too weak to be considered at the infrared and at the visible frequencies, metamaterials provide an effective route to create stronger magnetic responses at these frequencies. It also becomes interesting to ask whether the artificial magnetic response can have an influence back on the atomic dipole transitions including both the electric and the magnetic ones. Unlike using the conventional structures such as photonic crystals and common plasmonic structures without magnetic response, this will add an extra dimensionality in controlling the radiative decay rates. In this project, we are interested to use artificial magnetic metamaterials to control both electric and magnetic dipole transitions near optical frequencies. Such an approach has remained not much explored except for some simple structures like a metallic mirror or a nanoparticle. We need to first develop the corresponding theoretical and three-dimensional simulation tools in order to study the radiative decay rates with metamaterials. We will study the response of the metamaterials regarding the radiative decay rates at different levels of complexity, ranging from the individual artificial atoms to the whole metamaterial and the corresponding effective medium description. Such investigations will allow us to understand the interaction between the light, the metamaterials and the atom placed near or inside the metamaterials. To the end, these will help us to design realistic three-dimensional magnetic metamaterials that can be used to enhance the magnetic dipole transitions and to suppress the electric dipole transitions at the same time. As metamaterials have already been proven to be very useful in dispersion engineering , subwavelength focusing and transformation optics, the same should also apply to the control of the photon density of states and hence the radiative decay rates which will be useful in considering processes like spontaneous emission and photoluminescence. These investigations will not only expose the interesting physics of magnetic metamaterials in controlling radiative decay rates but will also be important to develop future experiments and designs of many quantum optical devices, such as efficient light sources and sensitive magnetic probes. 超材料是一種人工複合材料，具有很多天然材料所不具备的光學性質，比如左手材料和隱身材料。事實上，很多這些特異性質都取決於超材料所提供的人工磁性。在紅外線和可見光頻率，由於傳統原子和分子的磁性反應太弱，這使得超材料所提供的人工磁性格外重要。這也使得我們不禁要問超材料能否反過來影響包括電和磁的原子偶極躍遷。與一般非磁性光子晶體和等離子體結構不同，這將給我們額外的渠道控制電磁波輻射衰減率。在這個項目中，我們有興趣以人工的磁材料控制光波段附近的電和磁偶極躍遷。除了一些簡單的金屬鏡或納米粒子的結構，這種做法一直沒有太大的探索。我們首先需要制定相應的理論和三維模擬工具，以研究超材料中的電磁波輻射衰變率。我們將研究超材料在不同層次的複雜性對電磁波輻射衰減率的影響，範圍從簡單的人造超材料原子結構到整個超材料和相應的等效介質。這將讓我們了解光，超材料和超材料附近或內部的的原子之間的相互作用。到最後，這些將幫助我們設計出可制備的三維磁性超材料以提高磁偶極躍遷和抑制電偶極躍遷。由於超材料已經被證明對能帶結構工程，亞波長聚焦和變換光學非常有用，同樣超材料也應能適用於調控光子態密度和電磁波輻射衰減率，從而有用於控制自發輻射和光致發光等過程。這些研究不僅會突出磁性超材料有趣的物理性質，而且也將對發展未來的實驗和許多量子光學器件如高效光源和高靈敏度磁探頭的設計起重要的作用。

102211.label: Realisation of objectives
102211.value: The main objective of this project is to address the question on how magnetic metamaterials can be used to control radiative decay rate. To achieve our main objective, we have carried out a hierarchy of investigations from the individual artificial atoms up to the bulk metamaterials in order to study the emission physics and to develop the design rule and method for optimal control structures. We are pleased to report that at the completion of this project, we have achieved our main objective and resulted in producing four journal publications from the results of this project. Regarding our first objective, we have developed a Green's function formulation in calculating spontaneous emission enhancement for both electric and magnetic dipole transitions using the finite-element method. The method is capable of predicting the enhancement factors for spontaneous emission and photoluminescence. To understand the interaction between electric and magnetic dipole transitions, we designed an artificial current based atom that exhibiting magnetic resonance that can enhance magnetic dipole transition. The subwavelength structure/atom can be used to enhance the spontaneous emission rate for dyes at the structure with an enhancement factor of over 3 order of magnitudes. We have successfully obtained an understanding of the interaction and applied our understanding to design metamaterials for inhibiting electric dipole transitions with small volume, thus successfully achieved the second and third objectives of the project. For the last objective, we like to study the effective medium approach in discussing the radiative decay rates including factors such as local field corrections. To this end, we have investigated optical responses when magnetic and electric artificial structures are assembled into an array to form metamaterial of single layer of atoms. Using the top-down design, we are able to design structures tin manipulating the far-field properties to obtain polarization wavefront modification, tunable polarization control and absorption. This completes the final objective of this project.
