102211.label: Major findings and research outcome
102211.value: Developed a Green's function formulation in calculating spontaneous emission enhancement (Purcell factor) for both electric and magnetic dipole transitions using the finite-element method. This allows one to obtain the enhancement factors for spontaneous emission and photoluminescence. Using the developed formulation we have proposed and designed a magnetic plasmonic structure with enhanced magnetic dipole transitions. The structure consists of a periodic gold/glass/gold sandwich has a small volume with subwavelength in size that can significantly enhance the spontaneous emission rate for dyes by over three orders of magnitudes, including both radiative and non-radiative decay rates. In the proposed structure, the enhancement of the radiative part is a few times higher than those previously reported in the literature. From the investigation of optical responses of a metamaterial when magnetic and electric artificial structures are assembled into an array to form a metamaterial of single layer of atoms, we have gained valuable experience in manipulation of far-field properties, modification of polarization-dependent wavefront, widely tunable polarization control and the complete absorption of using a dual coupled resonators. The above optical responses investigation also allowed us to design and demonstrate a symmetrical and anti-symmetrical coherent perfect absorption structure for acoustic waves. A Helmholtz resonator structure with resonating effective bulk modulus allows one to obtain the symmetrical coherent perfect absorption effect, while a membrane structure with resonating effective density can be employed to generate the anti-symmetric scattered waves to cancel out the incident wave.

102211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
102211.value: We have carried out a thorough investigation on how magnetic metamaterials can be used to control radiative decay rate. Through the course of the project, we have derived the governing formulation for the spontaneous emission calculation emission calculation and designed a variety of metamaterials that have enhanced optical properties, such as artificial Kerr effect, spontaneous PT symmetry breaking, wave front engineering, spontaneous emission enhancement and coherent perfect absorption. In view of the achieved findings and outputs, further development of this research will be carried out in two paths: 1) One the theoretical side, we will continue to develop basic atom structure for metamaterials with exotic optical properties along with advanced theories and models to predict these optical phenomenon. 2) One the experimental side, collaboration with experimentalists on the realization our proposed metamaterials structure for emission enhancement in the optical regime. With the advances in the field of nanophotonics, the combination between our developed design methodology and the state-of-the-art nanophotonics fabrication techniques, one can foresee the possibility of realization of practical devices for commercial applications.

102211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
102211.value: Metamaterials are man-made composites which have been found to have exotic and interesting optical properties. In this project we have successfully derived the governing formulation for the spontaneous emission calculation emission calculation and developed tools to design metamaterials with various optical properties. Using the developed metamaterials design tool we have designed and analyzed metamaterials that have enhanced optical properties, such as artificial Kerr effect, spontaneous PT symmetry breaking, wave front engineering, spontaneous emission enhancement and coherent perfect absorption. These novel material systems can potentially find applications in nonlinear and physical optics.

102311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
102311.value: The aim of this project is the design of novel phosphorescent inorganic and organometallic transition metal polypyridine complexes for use as a new generation of molecular probes and bioimaging reagents for nitric oxide. Nitric oxide is a free radical that serves as a messenger molecule in the cardiovascular, neurotransmission, and immune systems. Since it plays a key role in various important physiological and pathological processes, accurate and sensitive detection of nitric oxide is required. Among the many methods available, fluorescent nitric oxide probes have been attracting tremendous interest due to the rapid development of and advances in confocal laser microscopy, which allows real-time bioimaging with high spatial and temporal resolution. Whilst a number of fluorescent probes have been developed, applications of phosphorescent transition metal complexes in nitric oxide sensing and bioimaging are just emerging and consequently this area is still unexplored. We believe that phosphorescent inorganic and organometallic transition metal complexes are attractive choices as nitric oxide probes owing to their highly environment-sensitive emission properties, high photostability that minimizes photobleaching, and long emission lifetimes that enable the probes to be studied by fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy with enhanced sensitivity. In this project, we will design new nitric oxide probes and bioimaging reagents derived from phosphorescent inorganic and organometallic transition metal complexes. Various probes will be developed and their reactivity toward nitric oxide will be investigated. Additionally, the cellular uptake, cytotoxicity, intracellular nitric oxide sensing, and bioimaging properties of the probes will also be examined. The favorable photophysical properties of phosphorescent inorganic and organometallic transition metal complexes, together with the strategic design of nitric oxide-specific ligands, will render the proposed probes a novel generation of biological tools that can be utilized in a range of sensing and bioimaging applications. 這個項目的目的是設計新型的磷光性無機和有機過渡金屬多吡啶絡合物作為新一代一氧化氮分子探針和生物成像試劑。一氧化氮是一種在心血管、神經遞質及免疫系統中擔任信使分子的自由基。由於它在各種重要的生理病理過程中起著關鍵作用，我們需要準確並靈敏地檢測一氧化氮。在眾多可選擇的方法中，熒光性一氧化氮探針一直吸引了巨大的研究興趣。高速發展的共聚焦激光顯微鏡技術可應用於高時空分辨率的實時生物成像。雖然一些熒光性探針已經發展起來，但是磷光性過渡金屬絡合物在一氧化氮的傳感和生物成像上的引用才剛剛興起，而且並未開發。磷光性無機和有機過渡金屬絡合物具有高度的環境敏感發光性能、高耐光性和長發光壽命，因此它們可以抵禦光漂白，並且被應用於靈敏度更高的熒光壽命成像顯微鏡。基於這些優點，我們相信，作為一氧化氮探針，它們是一個極具吸引力的選擇。 在這個項目中，我們將利用磷光無機和有機過渡金屬絡合物設計各種新型一氧化氮探針和生物成像試劑，並研究它們對一氧化氮的反應活性。此外，我們還將研究它們的細胞吸收、細胞毒性、細胞內一氧化氮檢測以及生物成像性能。磷光性無機和有機過渡金屬絡合物出色的光物理性質，連同特定的一氧化氮配體戰略設計，一定會使得我們提議的探針成為可用於探測和生物成像的新一代生物工具。

102311.label: Realisation of objectives
102311.value: All the objectives of the project were successfully achieved. In this project, a range of new luminescent transition metal complexes were modified with a diaminoaromatic group, which can react with nitric oxide. These complexes were synthesized and fully characterized. The electronic absorption, photophysical, photochemical, and electrochemical properties of the complexes were also investigated. Unlike their structural counterparts without the diaminoaromatic groups, these complexes were not emissive upon photoexcitation. Based on the photophysical and electrochemical data, the quenching mechanism was identified to be photoinduced electron transfer in nature. The dependence of emission behavior of the complexes on the pH of the solution was also studied. Impressively, all the complexes underwent facile reaction with nitric oxide resulting in the formation of triazole derivatives. Importantly, since the triazole is not an emission quenching group, the reaction mixture revealed significant emission enhancement. Such a drastic change of photophysical properties enabled the complexes to function as luminescent probes for nitric oxide. The detection of NO was not interfered by the presence of other reactive oxygen and nitrogen species. Additionally, the water solubility, lipophilicity, cellular uptake behavior, and cytotoxic of all the complexes were evaluated using various methods. We found that the complexes can be readily internalized by live cells, as indicated by ICP-MS measurements. Also, the cytotoxicity of the complexes can be manipulated by using different ancillary ligands and substituents on the ligands. Confocal microscopy studies showed that live cells stained with the complexes did not show any emission. However, upon treatment with exogenously and endogenously generated nitric oxide, the complexes were converted to their triazole counterparts, leading to significant emission of the cells, which can be monitored by confocal microscopy and flow cytometry. Our results showed that the diaminoaromatic complexes serve as a new generation of intracellular sensors and imaging reagents for nitric oxide. These complexes have very high potential to be applied in time-resolved detection and fluorescence-lifetime imaging microscopy, which can offer much higher sensitivity.

102311.label: Major findings and research outcome
102311.value: The diamine complexes [Re(N^N)(CO)3(py{NH2}2)](CF3SO3) (N^N = phen, Me2-phen, Me4-phen, Ph2-phen) were synthesized and characterized. Upon photoirradiation, these complexes were only weakly emissive due to the diaminoaromatic moiety that quenches the 3MLCT emission by PET. However, in the presence of NO, these complexes were converted to the triazole derivatives [Re(N^N)(CO)3(py-triazole)](CF3SO3), which revealed intense emission upon excitation. The cellular uptake properties and cytotoxicity of these complexes were studied by ICP-MS and the MTT assay, respectively. The Ph2phen-diamine complex was used to visualize exogenously generated NO in HeLa cells. However, after the complex-treated cells were incubated with NOC-7, the intracellular emission displayed no significant difference. To increase the reactivity, we used a methoxy substituent to enrich the electron density of the diaminoaromatic unit, and prepared the complexes [Re(N^N)(CO)3{py-CH2NH-C6H3(NH2)(OCH3)}]+. Addition of NOC-7 to a solution of the phen-diamine complex led to substantial emission enhancement (I/Io = 64). No significant emission was observed upon incubation of HeLa cells with the Ph2phen-diamine complex. However, after the cells were further treated with NOC-7, intense intracellular emission was detected. This complex was successfully applied to sense endogenous NO in murine macrophage RAW264.7 cells. We designed related iridium(III) diamine complexes where the diaminoaromatic unit was on a bidentate ligand [Ir(N^C)2{bpy-CH2NH-C6H3(NH2)(OMe)}]+. The emissive states of these complexes revealed 3MLCT/3LLCT or 3IL character, depending on the nature of the N^C ligands. These iridium(III) complexes exhibited very low emission quantum yields and short emission lifetimes, due to quenching by the diaminoaromatic unit. Upon treatment with NO, these weakly emissive complexes were converted to strongly luminescent triazole derivatives. Results of the confocal microscopy studies indicated that the diamine complexes can also detect exogenous and endogenous NO in live HeLa and RAW264.7 cells, respectively. In other related studies, we developed luminescent iridium(III) complexes containing a carbohydrate pendant such as fructose, glucose, and galactose. These strongly emissive complexes revealed facile cellular uptake properties. Most importantly, we discovered cell line-dependent cellular uptake; for example, the uptake of the glucose complexes was facilitated by the membrane proteins GLUTs. The fructose complexes also revealed preferential uptake by breast cancer tissues such as MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231, which overexpressed the fructose transporter GLUT-5. Additionally, we designed luminescent iridium(III) complexes containing a poly(ethylene glycol) pendant. Upon the modification, these complexes showed greatly enhanced water solubility and biocompatibility. Most importantly, all these complexes generate singlet oxygen upon steady-state irradiation, enabling them to exhibit interesting photocytotoxicity, which will assist in the development of photodynamic therapeutics.

102311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
102311.value: We have demonstrated in this project that the modification of luminescent transition metal complexes with a diaminoaromatic unit can allow them to undergo selective reaction with nitric oxide and modulate their emission properties. These important results will be useful in the development of luminescent probes for NO in live cells. There has been a rapidly emerging interest in the use of luminescent transition metal complexes in biological studies. Many of them show controllable cellular uptake and specific organelle-target capability. These features, together with the favorable photophysical properties of transition metal complexes such as long-lived emission and large Stokes shifts, will facilitate the development of efficient sensors and probes for NO in specific locations inside the cell. Of particular interest is the mitochondria because an unregulated generation of NO at this organelle has been linked to a wide range of neurodegenerative diseases and cancer. In this project, we have also shown that the modification with carbohydrate and PEG units renders the complexes to display cell line-dependent and controllable (photo)cytotoxicity. With all these interesting results, we believe that this project can be further developed and new classes of NO sensors and related therapeutic reagents can be ultimately developed.

102311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
102311.value: There is much interest in understanding the fundamental roles of nitric oxide (NO) in mammalian biochemistry such as the regulation of physiological and pathological processes. Thus, the development of NO sensors is of paramount importance. Optical methods involving the use of fluorescent probes and confocal laser microscopy have been commonly employed because excellent spatial and temporal resolution can be achieved in real time. Hence, a number of fluorescent probes for NO have been developed. However, most of these probes are fluorescent organic dyes and the use of luminescent transition metal complexes has not been explored. In this project, we have designed new nitric oxide probes and bioimaging reagents derived from luminescent inorganic and organometallic transition metal complexes. Different probes have been developed and their reactivity toward nitric oxide has been evaluated. Additionally, the cellular uptake, cytotoxic activity, intracellular nitric oxide sensing, and bioimaging properties of the probes have been examined. The favorable photophysical properties of phosphorescent inorganic and organometallic transition metal complexes, together with the strategic design of nitric oxide-specific ligands, have rendered the probes a new generation of biological tools that can be utilized in a range of sensing and bioimaging applications.

102411.label: Project Title(Chinese)
102411.value: 係數為週期或部分週期的偏微分方程的數值方法

102411.label: Project Objectives
102411.value: To extend the Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) map method for two-dimensional (2D) structures to three-dimensional (3D) structures; To extend the recursive doubling technique for 2D structures with one periodic direction to 2D structures with two periodic directions, and to 3D structures with one periodic direction; To extend the Bloch mode expansion technique from 2D structures to 3D structures; To develop and improve domain truncation techniques for terminating unbounded homogeneous or periodic media.
rows: To extend the Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) map method for two-dimensional (2D) structures to three-dimensional (3D) structures;
To extend the recursive doubling technique for 2D structures with one periodic direction to 2D structures with two periodic directions, and to 3D structures with one periodic direction;
To extend the Bloch mode expansion technique from 2D structures to 3D structures;
To develop and improve domain truncation techniques for terminating unbounded homogeneous or periodic media.

102411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
102411.value: Partial differential equations with periodic or partially periodic coefficients arise from many applications in science and engineering. In particular, those equations describing waves (such as acoustic, elastic, electromagnetic and light waves) in artificially designed periodic media and related devices have periodic or partially periodic coefficients. Efficient numerical methods for simulating waves in these structures are needed in the design and optimization processes in engineering applications. Standard numerical methods, such as the finite difference and finite element methods, are very general, but fail to take advantage of the periodicity. For many large scale three-dimensional problems, these methods require very long computation time and produce solutions with limited accuracy. As a result, many designs appeared in the literature are not fully optimized. For two-dimensional structures, there are some efficient numerical methods specially developed to take advantage of the periodicity. However, most of these methods have not been extended to the more realistic three-dimensional structures. In this project, we propose to extend a number of these methods to three-dimensional structures. The proposed methods will be applied to practical examples of current interest. 係數為週期或部分週期的偏微分方程在很多科學及工程的應用中會出現。比如，描述波（包括聲波、彈性波、電磁波及光波）在人工製造的週期介質及相關設備中傳播的方程就具有週期或部分週期的係數。這些週期結構的設計及優化需要快速有效求解相關偏微分方程的方法。標準的數值方法，像有限差分法、有限元法等，適用性很強，但無法利用方程係數為週期的特性。對很多大尺度的三維問題，這些方法需要很長的計算時間也只能給出很有限的精度。因此，在工程文獻中很多利用週期介質的設計沒有得到充分的優化。對於二維結構，現在已經有一些有效的數值方法可以充分利用週期性。但是這些方法還沒有被推廣到三維。本項目的目的是將一部分方法推廣到三維，並將它們應用到當今科研人員最感興趣的具體例子中。

102411.label: Realisation of objectives
102411.value: The project is concerned with the development of efficient numerical methods for solving partial differential equations with periodic or partially periodic coefficients. In particular, we study the Helmholtz equation and the Maxwell's equations in periodic or partially periodic media. The specific topics are related to the Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) map method, the recursive-doubling method, the Bloch mode expansion method, and domain truncation techniques. Objectives 1, 2 and 3 are mostly realized in papers [4], [7] and [12] as listed in Part C. In these works, we reported the recent development of numerical methods for 3D structures. In paper [7], we developed a mode reduction technique, so that for 3D structures, operators such as the DtN map can be represented by matrices of much smaller size, and the method based on operators become more efficient. In paper [12], we implemented a new method for 3D periodic structures. The method performs better than previously developed methods. The paper also includes a new formulation which is more robust. In paper [4], a technique is introduced to expand the scope of the traditional mode expansion methods. The 4th objective is realized in paper [1] as listed in Part C. In that paper, we developed a new boundary condition for terminating periodic structures, such as a photonic crystal waveguide. The new boundary condition is more efficient, especially for 3D structures, since it requires to calculate only the propagating Bloch modes. Previous boundary conditions require the calculation of many Bloch modes, and are expensive to used.

102411.label: Major findings and research outcome
102411.value: For papers listed in Part C. Paper [1]: A new boundary condition is introduced to terminate periodic structures such as a photonic crystal waveguide. The condition is basically a local condition, and is easy to use. Paper [2]: For scattering by a finite number of cylinders on a lattice, the DtN map method can be used to take advantage of the possibly identical unit cells. A new technique is introduced to calculate the DtN maps of the boundary unit cells, so that the computational domain can be truncated and the efficiency of the DtN map method is retained. Paper [3]: For diffraction gratings, the modal methods are widely used. The pseudospectral modal method outperforms other modal methods. In this paper, the method is developed for conical diffractions. Paper [4]: In this paper, the vertical mode expansion method is introduced (for a relatively simple structure). The method is much more efficient than traditional mode expansion (or modal) methods for 3D structures. Paper [5]: The lasing threshold can be studied as an unusual eigenvalue problem. In this paper, an efficient method is developed for lasing eigenvalue problem of 2D periodic structures. Paper [6]: The pseudospectral modal method for diffraction gratings (of Paper [3]) is revised as an optical waveguide mode solver. The method delivers very accurate results. Paper [7]: For a large class of 3D structures, it is possible to use mode expansion in one spatial variable. However, if many modes are needed in the expansions, the method will not be efficient. In this paper, a mode reduction technique is developed to speed up the related method. Paper [8]: New boundary integral equation methods are developed for optical waveguides with high index-contrast and sharp corners. The new methods give high order convergence and produce highly accurate results. Paper [9]: As an application of our method (the DtN map method and the new boundary condition of paper [1]), we proposed a compact wavelength demultiplexer. Paper [10]: Photonic crystal heterostructure devices are based on photonic crystals with slight different periods. In this paper, we apply the DtN map method to study some devices which are difficult to simulate by conventional numerical methods. Paper [11]: Using the DtN map method, we analyzed standing waves on a periodic waveguides. The standing waves are guided modes above the lightline, and they are related to a number of interesting physical phenomena. Paper [12]: For 3D structures involving crossed arrays of cylinders, we developed a new method which is simpler than the previous DtN map method, and also new formulations that are more robust.

102411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
102411.value: For 3D structures with some periodicity, it is possible to take advantage of the (partial) periodicity. However, using various existing techniques, the final linear problem may be still very large and expensive to solve. Further effort is needed to develop fast iterative solvers.

102411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
102411.value: Periodic structures appear widely in applications. It is also likely that the periodicity is broken intentionally to create useful devices. To analyze physical phenomena, such as the propagation of electromagnetic wave or light in a (partially) periodic structure, standard numerical methods (for solving partial differential equations) are often too expensive to use. In this project, a number of special and more efficient numerical methods that take advantage of the (partial) periodicity have been developed and demonstrated. These methods can be used by engineers to design useful devices based on periodic structures.

102711.label: Project Title(Chinese)
102711.value: 高頻渦流的自旋轉移振盪器

102711.label: Project Objectives
102711.value: To fabricate novel spin transfer oscillators that can deliver output powers as large as that delivered by vortex-based nano-contact oscillators but in the frequency range of gigahertz; To characterize and model these devices in laboratory to gain basic knowledge of the spin transfer torque effect; To test the potential of these new devices as microwave generators for radiofrequency telecommunications.
rows: To fabricate novel spin transfer oscillators that can deliver output powers as large as that delivered by vortex-based nano-contact oscillators but in the frequency range of gigahertz;
To characterize and model these devices in laboratory to gain basic knowledge of the spin transfer torque effect;
To test the potential of these new devices as microwave generators for radiofrequency telecommunications.

102711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
102711.value: The exploitation of the quantum spin of the electrons, together with their charge, has led to a new class of electronic devices. These so-called “magneto-electronic" or “spintronic” devices have found application in data storage and sensing. Their field of application can be extended to radiofrequency telecommunications. In nanometer-scale spintronic devices the application of an electrical direct current generates an alternating voltage in the radiofrequency range, because of the physical effect known as spin transfer torque. Spin-transfer radiofrequency oscillators have been, so far, proposed and studied in two device geometries: nano-pillars and nano-contacts. In both systems, either a uniform magnetic configuration or a magnetic vortex is excited through the transfer of spin angular momentum. Uniformly magnetized spin-transfer nano-oscillators can reach frequencies as high as 50 GHz or above but deliver too small output power to be of use in practical applications. A magnetic vortex that is made to gyrate into a patterned nano-magnet generates an output signal with larger power and still in the range of the GHz. A substantial increase of the power, in absence of an externally applied magnetic field, is obtained by making the vortex gyrate around a nano-contact to a magnetoresistive multilayer. Unfortunately, in vortex-based oscillators in nano-contact geometry the frequency is limited to a few hundreds of MHz. We here propose to study a novel device geometry, which can combine the power performance of the vortex-based nano-contact oscillators with the high-frequency performance of the vortex-based nano-pillar oscillators. The system consists of a hybrid geometry in which a magnetic vortex is made to gyrate into a patterned nano-magnet, like in the case of a nano-pillar, but outside the electrically-active area, like in the case of a nano-contact. The power delivered by these oscillators would be comparable to that delivered by a vortex-based nano-contact oscillator, but the output frequency is enhanced because of the lateral confinement of vortex due to the patterned geometry. These devices will be fabricated, characterized and analytically modeled. This will allow us, on one side, to contribute to the basic knowledge of the spin transfer torque and, on the other side, to demonstrate practical application of this new effect in radiofrequency telecommunications. 利用电子的电荷及其自旋开启了新一代电子器件的广泛研究。这类被称为“磁电子”或者“自旋电子”的器件主要应用在信息存儲和传感器方面。近年来，因为发现自旋传输矩这一物理效应，也就是当自旋极化的直流电流通过纳米级的自旋阀结构时，会产生稳定的微波发射，在片上微波源和移动通信领域有着广阔的应用景。 目前，处于研究阶段的基于自旋转矩的微波振荡器主要有两种结构：纳米柱和纳米点。在这两种结构中，通过自旋角动量的转移，可以激发磁化态均匀分布或者磁涡旋态。磁化态均匀分布的代表是纳米柱型振荡器，它可以产生等于或者大于50 GHz的频率，但是发射功率太小很难实现实际应用。磁涡旋态就是涡旋核围绕平衡位置进行螺旋式的运动，此类振荡器同时具有较大的发射功率和较高的发射频率。在没有外加磁场的情况下，通过基于涡旋态具有纳米点接触磁阻多层膜结构的振荡器可以增大发射功率。然而遗憾的是，该类型振荡器发射频率只有几百MHz。 在这里，我们提出一种具有新型结构的微波振荡器件，该器件结合了涡旋态纳米点接触型振荡器发射功率大以及纳米柱型的发射频率高的特点。本项目将进行具有新型结构的器件制备，表征以及建模分析。一方面，通过该项目的研究，可以让我们更加深入的了解自旋转矩的物理本质，另外，也可以更好的开发其在移动通讯等领域中的实际应用。

102711.label: Realisation of objectives
102711.value: Spin transfer torque oscillators have been successfully fabricated (objective 1), characterized and thoretically modelled (objective 2). We demonstrated that they can generate substantial output voltage in the range of the radio frequency and therefore be used as radio frequency generators (objective 3). Overall, the objectives have been achieved. In order to characterize the devices, we assembled a completely new setup in our labs that is now available for characterisation of high frequency spintronic devices. This unique setup is currently used by another group from a sister university in Hong Kong, within the framework of a scientific collaboration. In the first part of the project we fabricated and characterized devices in nano-pillar and nano-contact geometry. While the former could deliver output signals in the microwave range, their output power was too small for applications. The latter could deliver large power but at sub-GHz frequencies. We therefore conceived and proposed a new hybrid geometry which could satisfy both requirements. The proposed device geometry is a nano-pillar but the current is injected through a nano-contact at the center of the free layer. The vortex is made to gyrate in the geometrically confined pillar but outside the contact area. In this way, the delivered output is that of a spin torque oscillator in nano-contact geometry and the frequency is pushed up above 1 GHz because of the geometrical confinement. This idea was published in a top-tier engineering journal. In order to achieve full integration of these devices with semiconductor technologies, we functionalized semiconductors, instead of metals, to fabricate spin-transfer torque oscillators. In this effort, the research team discovered new effects regarding interaction between electrical, magnetic and optical properties of magnetic semiconductor thin films. These findings have been published in top tier journals. One paper, in particular, has been listed as top-downloaded paper in Applied Physics Letters in both 2013 and 2014 and is receiving a large number of citations.

102711.label: Major findings and research outcome
102711.value: We found that spin transfer torque oscillators in a typical patterned pillar geometry can oscillate at microwave frequency but do not deliver an output power high enough to drive an antenna. On the contrary, spin transfer torque oscillators in a nano-contact geometry can deliver an output power high enough to drive an antenna but the frequency is limited to the sub-GHz range. We therefore first conceived and developed a new geometry device that can deliver performance good enough for application in radio frequency communications. The devices we fabricated in the first phase were based on magnetic metals. In order to pursue faster integration with the semiconductor-based circuitry, we investigated magnetic semiconductors, as well. We found that, introducing a magnetic moment in a semiconductor alters its band structure. In other words, magnetism can be used a tool for band-gap engineering. In particular, a magnetic moment lowers the bottom of the conduction band because of giant Zeeman splitting, with an overall reduction of the band gap. This effect, observed for the first time at room temperature in this project, can be used in a variety of applications where alignment of energy levels at the interface between two films is required.

102711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
102711.value: There exist great potential for further research because of the newly discovered spin-orbit torque effect. Spin torque can be induced at the interface between a magnetic film and platinum or tantalum because of the large spin-orbit interaction in these two metals. Thanks to this effect, devices with performance similar to those developed here can be fabricated in a much simpler geometry. These so-called spin torque oscillators are completely new and therefore their investigation requires submitting a new proposal. The research team will apply for a new grant to develop and investigate these devices.

102711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
102711.value: We have developed a novel type of electronic oscillators for radio frequency telecommunications. These oscillators are based on magnetic materials and exploit an effect called spin transfer torque. The materials we used are magnetic metals. In these devices, the trade-off is between output power and frequency of oscillation. The challenge was to generate powers suitable to drive an antenna while retaining high oscillation frequency. We successfully conceived and studied a new device geometry that delivers sufficient output power in the radio frequency range. We finally investigated the possibility to use magnetic semiconductors, which allows faster integration with the current electronics. In doing so, we discovered novel physical effects that led to high impact publications and invitations to conferences.

102911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
102911.value: 蛋白自由基是生物體內酶催化氧化過程的重要中間物質。其特定結構模序的固有性質可以通過考察相關氣相蛋白自由基片段在質譜的碎裂情況來獲得。自由基多肽正離子的裂解機制也被作為科學依據引入到以質譜為基礎的蛋白質組學研究中。理解其解離機理對深入研究和發展蛋白質測序策略有著十分重要的意義。如同偶電子數的多肽正離子一樣，奇電子數的多肽自由基正離子也可以通過解離得到特徵離子，並應用於基於質譜技術的蛋白質組學研究中。氣相多肽自由基正離子可以通過多種不同的方式獲得，但很可能由於其結構以及隨後分子重排反應在時間尺度上的差異，導致最終得到不同的解離產物。從長遠角度講，本研究以期建立一個可以描述不同實驗方法生成蛋白質自由基正離子自由基遷移反應的動力學模型。就現階段為期三年的研究來說，則主要側重於利用基於密度泛函理論的分子動力學方法，考察電子捕獲解離過程產生的自由基相似片段的超價多肽自由基模型的動力學性質。包括甘氨酸、包含N―Cα鍵的寡聚甘氨酸衍生物、含有S―S鍵的胱氨酸，以及同時包含N―Cα鍵及S―S鍵的胱氨酸衍生物都將被系統的研究。

102911.label: Realisation of objectives
102911.value: Dynamical structures of various molecular radical ions at different temperatures have been theoretically examined by means of density functional theory based molecular dynamics methods and/or classical molecular dynamics, performed on a home-built high-performance computing cluster (with a total of 3.2 TGLOPS computing power, partially supported by this proposal) managed by the PI's team members. These trajectories predicted critical structures which were further optimized based on the variational principle by minimizing the total internal energy of the molecular geometries in the framework of density functional theory. Thereby, potential energy surfaces (PESs) associated with the isomerization and dissociation of molecular radicals were constructed. Competitions among some of these reaction pathways on the theoretically predicted PESs were then modeled with the Rice-Ramsperger-Kassel-Marcus kinetic theory. The theoretical models established in this study were also ratified experimentally using collision-induced dissociations performed with a linear-quadrupole ion-trap mass spectrometer at the University of Hong Kong (Hong Kong, China) and Blackbody infrared radiative dissociations performed with a Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometer at Leopold-Franzens-Universität Innsbruck (Austria) / Christian-Albrechts-Universität zu Kiel (Germany). In combination of the theoretical and experimental approaches, the mechanism, energetics and dynamics of the reductive cleavage of the S―S and S―H in model systems have been investigated in the gas phase. These reductive cleavages were induced by different electron sources, including both free and hydrated electrons and also other free radicals such as hydrated CO2•− or O2•−. Their reactivity differences as revealed in our gas-phase models have also provided fundamental insights into the radical-induced damages of proteins in aqueous media on the molecular level. In addition, the radical being transferred to the β-carbon of an amino acid residue of a peptide molecule can induce β-scission of the N―Cα and Cα―C bonds of that amino acid residue. The present theoretical investigations have demonstrated that the properties of the amino acid residues and the availability of labile protons around the cleaving sites are important factors controlling the ease of such radical-induced peptide-backbone cleavages and the competition between the cleavages of the N―Cα and Cα―C bonds.

102911.label: Major findings and research outcome
102911.value: Two gas-phase reactions with relevance for biological radiation damage, namely cleavage of the disulfide bond of CH3SSCH3 and activation of the thiol group of CH3SH, were induced by reactive radical anions, including free and hydrated electron and other free radicals such as O2•− and CO2•− [1]. The latter is also a prominent free radical reagent for electrochemical activation and functionalization of organic compounds [2, 3] and they can be prepared in situ under gas-phase conditions through the redox reactions with monovalent main-group [4, 5] or first-row transition [6] metal ions. The hydrated O2•−, usually viewed as major source of oxidative stress, is unreactive toward all small sulfur-containing compounds studied. Theoretical calculations and nanocalorimetric experiments indicated that the conversion of free electron and CO2•− to O2•− can deactivate highly reactive species and may actually reduce oxidative stress. For reactions of hydrated electron with CH3SH as well as hydrated CO2•− with CH3SSCH3, the reaction products in the gas phase are different from those reported in the literature from pulse radiolysis studies, which is rationalized with the reduced cage effect in reactions of gas-phase clusters. Unpaired electrons in protein/peptide radicals can induce peptide backbone or side-chain cleavages, forming a large variety of peptide fragments [8, 9]. Of particular interest is selective cleavages of N-Cα and Cα-C bonds in a β-radical tautomer. Theoretical calculations [7] suggested that majority of the bond cleavages is homolytic via β-scission. Their energy barriers depend largely on the radical stability in the transition states and the availability of a mobile proton around the β-radical. Generally, cleavage of N-Cα bond is less favorable comparing with that of Cα-C bond for systems without a mobile proton. It is because (1) homolytic cleavage is less favorable for the more polar N-Cα bond and (2) a less stable σ-radical localized on an amide nitrogen is formed for the former, while a more stable radical delocalized in a π*(CO)-like orbital is formed for the latter. With a mobile proton, the barriers to the polar N-Cα bond cleavage is reduced, while the Cα-C bond cleavage is significantly suppressed. With basic residues, the Cα-C bond cleavage can be re-activated. Cleavages of the N-Cα bond induced by the β-radical tautomer of Trp and Tyr are often preferred as compared with cleavages of the Cα-C bond in peptide radical cations containing mobile protons.

102911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
102911.value: The present proposal has led to two parallel research areas: (1) the reactivity of various sources of free radical anions toward biological relevant molecules and (2) the selectivity of peptide cleavages controlled by the peptide properties and the availability of labile protons. For the area (1), our discoveries have shown that the reactive radical species leading to damage of biological molecules can be generated from different sources including hydrated low-valent metal ions, which are also important transient intermediate in electrochemical processes. The reactivity of these radical species will be presumably influenced by the presence of the metal ions. It will be interesting to further investigate the interplay among the radical species, substrates, metal ions and solvent molecules, on the overall reaction mechanism and dynamics. For the area (2), we have demonstrated that the properties of amino acid and the availability of a labile proton in the vicinity of the radical center and bond-cleavage sites are important factors governing the selectivity of bond dissociation. Better quantifying these factors using different peptide sequence models is useful for more accurate interpretation of the mass spectra of biological molecular ions, which is actually the underlying scientific principle applied in mass-spectrometric based protein identification.

102911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
102911.value: Free radicals involve in many enzymatic activities that are essential in biological systems. On the other hand, reactive radical species can also damage proteins causing a wide range of human disorders, such as neurodegenerative disease and aging. Hence, better understanding the redox chemistry of radical proteins is of fundamental importance for deciphering many biochemical processes in life. These redox processes can be influenced simultaneously by many factors, for examples, the physical and chemical properties of the proximity of the active centers and solvation, making detail investigation challenging. The intrinsic properties of particular structural motifs of radical proteins can be effectively revealed by examining the redox processes performed by relevant functional groups or peptide segments isolated in the gas phase. In this work, mechanisms, energetics and dynamics for the radical-induced bond cleavages of biologically relevant functional groups, namely the N―Cα and Cα―C bonds of amino acid residues and the disulfide linkage S―S in proteins, have been investigated theoretically by means of quantum chemical calculations and experimentally using mass spectrometric techniques. Our results have demonstrated that the amino-acid residue sequences and the cage effect arising from the solation environments may play significant contributions to the redox reaction of protein radicals.

103311.value: 陽極氧化蝕刻曾經是預備一維納米結構最方便途徑。這些簡單氧化納米棒／納米管， 可以在綠色應用有很大突破，如染料敏化太陽能電池，光催化二氧化碳還原，太陽能水分解，有毒氣體感應以至環境修復。 一維陣列的好處很微妙, 由簡化光伏應用中的電子擴散路徑以至調較光催化應用中反應物停留時間。儘管這個方法受普遍關注, 但這個方法對預備單一元件氧化物很大程度受主金屬薄片限制。 因此， 在此提議一個新穎概念—反應陽極氧化。這個方法在保留慣用的陽極氧化蝕刻所產生的並列納米棒／納米管的同時，反應陽極氧化集合了透過在主金屬薄片和隨意選取的第二種金屬陽離子之間的直接電化學反應所形成的氧化複合物 (兩種或以上金屬元件)。換句話說，這簡易反應陽極氧化技術能實踐並列氧化複合物結構，例如金屬鈦酸鹽，铌酸鹽，鉭酸鹽，鉬酸鹽及釩酸鹽。這技術亦打開了一個未開發的氧化複合物納米棒／納米管通用合成法的領域，更重要是這技術的豐富化學性質及應用。 在這建議書裏， 新穎反應陽極氧化技術將會應用於合成光解水催化劑(用於太陽能由水製造氫氣)，而這催化劑會被各種氧化複合物材料所控制。雖然這技術能方便地延伸至合成其他用途的氧化複合物，但由於潔淨製氫技術最為重要，設計光解水催化劑將會備受關注。與標準固態反應預備法比較，創造垂直並列氧化合成物催化劑納米棒／納米管的表面面積有很大程度的增加。更重要的是，特別是應用於分解氫及氧的光電化學配置，一維陣列容許電荷更有效地傳送。 這建議的研究成果將能有效地單由太陽能及海水／污水來製造氫氣，後者更同同時製氫及處理污水。到最後階段，反應陽極氧化合成光電極組件將會用來建造戶外太陽能水分解系統。該示範系統將會作為朝着商業化成果及保障能源未來的先驅。

103311.label: Realisation of objectives
103311.value: All the objectives as laid out in the proposal have been fully met. Under objective 1: We have developed various modified methodologies pertaining to the reactive anodization to create oxide semiconductor arrays of nanotubes, nanorods, nanoflowers and nanocones. Under objective 2: In coming up with the modified anodization technique, we investigated and elucidated the mechanisms of the oxide semiconductor. This allowed us to come up with various avenues to overcome limitations such as excessive dissolution (no formation of oxide layer) and the control of pore size. For the first time, we also introduced the in situ doping to the oxide layer, and developed the methodology in such way that it is possible to apply it across various dopants and with controlled amount. Under objective 3: Based on Objectives 2 and 3, we developed a number of anisotropic oxide semiconductor arrays that are highly active toward photocatalytic water splitting (at least 2-fold higher in efficiency than the relevant control). Importantly, we established the synthesis-physicochemical-performance relationships for the different semiconductor systems.

103311.label: Major findings and research outcome
103311.value: Through the proposal, we have developed a number of novel techniques for the fabrication of anisotropic oxide photoelectrodes with high photoresponse. Among the classes of materials covered include those of pristine metal oxides (both n- and p-type), doped metal oxides and composite coupled semiconductors. We introduced for the first time, a statistical optimization of the anodisation synthesis of well-aligned TiO2 nanotubes, Nb2O5 nanorods and WO3 nanoflowers based on the 2k Factorial method. As a result, we established the model for the optimization of the n-type oxide materials while accurately predicting the expected photocatalytic water splitting efficiencies of these electrodes. The novelty of the work received excellent reviews and appears as the Cover of ChemSusChem (2015). The modified anodization synthesis of highly efficient p-type NiO photoelectrode was further fabricated. Here, we resolved the long-standing problem of high dissolution of Ni during conventional anodization that prevented the anodization synthesis of NiO, by introducing the alkaline-based anodization. Not only did it minimize dissolution, the methodology resulted in highly stable and active p-NiO (quantum efficiency ~25%) for water splitting. The work was published in ACS Applied Materials and Interfaces (2014). To enhance the water splitting activity of the oxide semiconductor, we introduced yet another creative technique to simultaneously dope the metal oxide with a secondary metal during the anodization synthesis of the former. This allows the creation of new class of materials which we demonstrated the flexible synthesis of A+-doped Nb2O5 (A+ = Li+,Na+,K+,Rb+,Cs+) in a modified voltage pattern that allows controlled amount of doping and creating the hierarchical nanocones. The photocatalytic water efficiency was improved by at least two-fold as a result of improved charge carrier density and favorable interfacial charge transfer. The work has been accepted in the first-ever Thematic Issue in AIChE Journal (2015). The Type II charge transfer was further demonstrated in this project by depositing QD sensitizers on the semiconductor oxide nanotubes. We introduced the in situ deposition strategy that allows improved the charge injection efficiency from different sizes QDs. To further improve the photostability of the QDs, the same in situ deposition was applied but using a bulky POSS ligand. The long photostability of QDs in aqueous environment is a breakthrough and is much longer than any previously reported methods. The works were published in the Advanced Functional Materials (2012) and the Journal of Physical Chemistry C (2013), the former appearing as the Cover of journal.

103311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
103311.value: The outcomes achieved in this proposal have opened up a number of avenues in terms of the manufacturing of high efficiency photoelectrodes for solar water splitting. By presenting creative solutions to a number of hurdles associated with conventional anodization, e.g., swift statistical optimization, limiting photodissolution, enhancing charge transport, and going beyond simple oxides, the technique can now be readily applied to solar water splitting. Importantly, the solutions developed here tackle the issues at the fundamental levels so that they can be easily extended to a wider range of general semiconductor materials for water splitting. In other words, higher water splitting efficiencies would be possible by extending these concepts and solutions to the exploration of active materials. Besides water splitting, the concept shall be extended to other critical photomediated processes such as environmental remediation and carbon dioxide reduction. All of these form the basis for further developments, both at the explorative as well as application levels. Further funding applications (GRF and ITF) are currently underway to take the outcomes of the project to the next level of investigations and applications.

103311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
103311.value: The project resulted in the development of highly active materials for the photocatalytic water splitting, a technology critical for securing clean and sustainable fuel in the near future. Using a scalable technology, that is, reactive anodization, we developed a range of aligned oxide semiconductors such as TiO2 nanotube, Nb2O5 nanorods, WO3 nanoflowers, doped Nb2O5 nanocones. More importantly, we solved a number of limitations previously associated with the anodization technique by introducing the statistical optimization and prediction of the relevant semiconductor materials, enhancing the bulk and surface charge transport, doping of secondary metals and performing hetererojunction engineering. The aim was to improve the photocharge separation so that they can be used to split water (instead of recombining). As a result, we achieved enhanced water splitting efficiencies by at least two-fold relative to the conventional standard (some even up to 10 fold). The outcomes garnered from this project set the field in a great step forward in the continuous effort to secure clean and sustainable energy resources in the near future.

103511.label: Project Objectives
103511.value: Theoretically simulate TPyB coordinated with Cu and Fe on the chosen surfaces in order to determine their molecule-molecule binding properties, molecule-substrate interactions and molecular diffusion barriers. Experimentally measure domain size distributions of TPyB coordinated with Cu and Fe on the chosen surfaces grown at different molecular deposition flux and substrate temperature using scanning tunneling microscopy, and model these results in order to derive information about the inter-molecular bond strength, molecule-substrate interaction and molecular diffusion. 103511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
103511.value: The proposed research aims to substantially improve the capability of forming high quality two-dimensional supramolecular self-assembled structures, in order to expand the potential of this very promising technology. The self-assembly of metal-ligand coordinated (MLC) supramolecular structures has for many years been used successfully for the bottom-up fabrication of novel three-dimensional (3D) functional materials. Recently, metal-ligand coordination has also proven to be a viable strategy for the design and assembly of two-dimensional (2D) supramolecular structures on metal surfaces. These 2D-MLC systems provide opportunities beyond those available with 3D systems, since 2D systems are particularly relevant for a wide range of technological applications such as solid state devices. However, fabrication of these 2D systems frequently generates inhomogeneities, such as structural defects, polymorphic phases and orientational domains, that would generally limit performance in practical device applications. The difficulty of fabricating high quality 2D-MLC systems can be attributed to insufficient control over their growth. In the proposed research, we will address this key issue by investigating pertinent factors that determine the growth dynamics and self-assembly of 2D-MLC systems. These investigations will be carried out by means of a close coupling of calculations using density functional theory and experimental measurements using scanning tunneling microscopy and low energy electron microscopy. Our complementary theoretical and experimental investigations will focus on understanding the fundamental intermolecular and molecule-substrate bonding interactions that give rise to 2D-MLC self-assembly and define the energy landscape on which growth takes place. We will also investigate experimentally the kinetics of 2D molecular mass transport, which plays an integral role in growth on crystalline surfaces. These experimental studies of kinetics are expected to provide quantitative information about kinetic energy barriers that originate in the intermolecular and molecule-substrate bonding energetics, which we will model at the first principles level. This research will contribute a deeper understanding of the growth dynamics of 2D-MLC supramolecular systems at metal surfaces. Such knowledge is crucial for optimizing the quality of 2D-MLC systems, an essential step toward realizing their potential in numerous applications. 本研究旨在大幅度提高形成高质量二维超分子自组装结构的能力，以进一步提高其技术应用潜力。多年来，金属配体超分子结构的自组装已被成功用于自下而上的三维新型功能材料的制备。最近，在金属表面上设计和组装金属配体二维超分子结构也被证明是可行的。这些二维金属配体系统优于三维系统，因为二维系统在诸如固态器件等技术领域应用更加广泛。然而，制造这些二维系统经常产生不均匀性，如结构上的缺陷、多态相和取向域，都会限制实际器件应用的性能。制造高品质的二维 金属配体系统的困难可以归因于对他们生长的控制不足。本研究将解决这个关键问题。我们的思路是研究决定生长动力学和二维金属配体系统的自组装相关因素。我们的研究将通过把密度泛函理论计算和扫描隧道显微镜及低能电子显微镜实验测量紧密结合来进行。我们的理论和实验协同研究将侧重了解分子间和分子与基底间的基本氢键作用。这些作用会引起二维金属配体的自组装和决定生长发生的势能面。我们也会实验研究二维分子质量运输动力学，这对晶体表面生长起着不可或缺的作用。这些动力学实验研究将提供起源于分子间和分子与基底间成键能的动能能垒之定量信息。该信息将通过第一性原理模拟获得。本研究将有助于更深入了解二维金属配体超分子体系在金属表面上的生长动力学。获取该知识对优化二维金属配体系统的质量至关重要，是实现其众多潜在应用中的关键一步。

103511.label: Realisation of objectives
103511.value: Most objectives have been successfully achieved as planned, resulting in a very substantial series of publications and presentations at conferences and institutions. The collaboration was effective and is still now producing very valuable analyses which will be published in due course with appropriate acknowledgement of this project funding. 1) Extensive modeling was performed on various systems to understand and further develop the methodologies needed to properly represent the various phenomena present in the complex adsorption systems. Besides the molecules of TPyB and the closely related LTPyB on Cu surfaces, we thus also investigated various relevant aspects of Br adsorption structures to study aspects of interadsorbate interactions, as well as graphene systems since TPyB is structurally closely related to graphene. 2) Scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) measurements as well as related scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS) data and low energy electron microscopy and diffraction (LEEM and LEED) images were obtained for the intended molecular deposition on Cu surfaces. For LTPyB molecules on the Cu(111) surface the initial goal was to obtain quantitative information about diffusion and self-assembly kinetics through studies of growth and coarsening. Since electron beam induced effects were observed on growth and coarsening behavior that interfered with quantitative studies, we focused on more qualitative studies, and exploited the electron beam effects to learn about some aspects of kinetics. 3) The recorded STM and STS data have been analyzed and are now being written up for publication, while the measured LEEM and LEED data need further analysis.

103511.label: Major findings and research outcome
103511.value: In this project, we have investigated assemblies of the molecule TPyB and related systems to explore interactions that operate in the growth and dynamics of layers thereof. This includes useful systems related to the basic hexagonal carbon network structure of graphene underlying the TPyB molecules at the center of this project. Thus, we performed advanced simulations of graphene-like systems that incorporate important ingredients relevant to the molecule TPyB. We applied state-of-the-art scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy to TPyB and the related TBD, the results of which have been analyzed theoretically and will soon be published in high-impact journals. Highlights include the following: 1) TPyB, LTPyB and TBD Assemblies on Cu(111). We have experimentally and theoretically compared the assembly behavior of the closely related TPyB, LTPyB and TBD molecules to analyze the key interactions operating in such systems adsorbed on metal surfaces like Cu. We find in particular that these molecules are highly sensitive indicators of their coordination geometries and acceptor vs. donor properties. This work provides understanding for selecting other molecules and metals to serve as highly sensitive indicators of bonding properties of such molecules on metal substrates, e.g. for functional organic electronic devices. By choosing appropriate molecules with suitable MO levels and by selecting particular coordination geometries with metal atoms, molecular orbitals can be adjusted for specific purposes. 2) Inhomogeneous Phase Stabilized by Competing Interactions. We have experimentally and theoretically studied the dependence of surface growth phenomena on adatom-adatom interactions for the system of Br adsorbed on Cu(111) at various temperatures and coverages, up to one monolayer thickness. This system exhibits short-range ordering as well as long-range interactions between islands and between holes in the Br layer, causing structures with a characteristic equilibrium repeat distance of about 5 to 6 nm under all conditions which we have explored. Our analysis finds that the short-range ordering can be well reproduced by quantum-mechanical calculations that include ionic (dipolar), VdW, wave function and elastic effects, while the longer-range interactions are best explained by elastic effects. 3) Further Applications. The methods developed for this project have been very useful beyond the original scope of the project. They were particularly helpful in studying and predicting most interesting properties of adsorption on and defects in graphene layers, in muscle-like “[c2]daisy chains” as well as in tip functionalizations for high-resolution non-contact atomic force microscopy. This GRF is therefore also acknowledged in the corresponding publications.

103511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
103511.value: Our results suggest many possibilities for further investigations. The variety of adsorbed molecules and molecular interactions which our approach can explore is large, even within the realm of graphene-like molecules similar to TPyB, LTPyB and TBD. Also, the influence of other atoms and of the STM tip itself offer fascinating possibilities, for example in terms of affecting the local properties of molecular fragments, and of inducing excitation of parts of molecules.

103511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
103511.value: The goal of this project is to study the structure and electronic properties of aromatic, graphene-like molecules arranged on metal surfaces. The main experimental techniques used were scanning tunneling microscopy (STM), scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS) and low-energy electron microscopy and diffraction (LEEM and LEED), while ab initio density functional theory and molecular dynamics were applied to model relevant structures.

103911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
103911.value: 多吡啶釕（Ⅱ）配合物是一類重要的過渡金屬配合物發光體。源於釕（II）至吡啶的金屬到配體三線態電荷轉移（3MLCT）激發態，它們具有豐富的光物理和光化學特性。對於以 [釕（多吡啶）x（L）y]n+ 為分子式的多吡啶釕（Ⅱ）配合物，室溫能激活的金屬中心激發態（3dd態）已被廣泛視為一種失活3MLCT激發態的高效途徑，而提高3MLCT激發態的布居為發展功能性多吡啶釕（Ⅱ）發光體的重要方向。我們設想，採用σ鍵合的有機配體為 L 將是一個很有為的策略，因為這些好的σ-捐助者應有效地提升非發光3dd激發態的能級。然而，大概因為釕（II）中心的豐富及多樣的有機金屬化學，要合成空氣穩定的釕（II）發光體並不容易，故此聘用非環金屬化的有機配體來操縱 [釕（多吡啶）] 核心的發光特性的報告比較罕見。 我們以前曾證明通過精心的分子設計，可以合成空氣穩定、明確、並發光的有機釕（Ⅱ）多吡啶配合物，其中 L 為炔基，烷氧基卡賓，亞丙二烯基，氰化物和異氰。最近，我們的初步結果表明，酰基配體甚至會比上面列出的 L 優越。這不但因為酰基是更強的σ-捐助者，而且通過調節釕（Ⅱ）-酰基配體的π鍵相互作用可以有系統地操縱 [釕（多吡啶）] 核心的光物理性質。在這個項目中，我們將會開發發光釕（II）-酰基複合物和進行詳細的結構、光物理、電化學、及理論性的研究，以深入了解釕（II）-酰基π相互作用如何干擾釕（Ⅱ）dπ的能級及其衍生的光物理。另一方面，我們預料 [釕（多吡啶）（酰基）] 基團的光物理性質也可以通過“超分子”的方法操縱。因此，我們將會開發以多吡啶釕（II）-酰基作基礎的金屬配體，其中酰基團包含有配位/離子結合特性，並研究外來金屬離子/配合物與 [釕（多吡啶）（酰基）] 基團耦合後的光物理效應。這個項目的成功將不僅提供金屬-碳鍵相互作用上的基楚認識，而且還提供了分子材料理性設計對於太陽能電池、光化學、螢光傳感和分子電子組件應用的有用見解。

103911.label: Realisation of objectives
103911.value: Through this project, we initiated a program to study the bonding and spectroscopic properties of several classes of ruthenium organometallic complexes. More specifically, we prepared ruthenium–acyl, −alkoxycarbene, −indolizine zwitterion, −indoline, −indole zwitterion, and ruthenafuran complexes. Among these organometallic complexes, ruthenium−indolizine zwitterion, −indoline, and −indole zwitterion complexes reported by us represent the first examples of isolated metal indolizine zwitterion, −indoline, and −indole zwitterion complexes in the literature. Our report on the preparation of ruthenafuran also represented a general synthetic strategy for the preparation of metallafuran. The photophysical properties of all these complexes were investigated by different spectroscopic techniques and theoretical methods. All these findings highlight the advantage of employing organometallic ligands to modulate the photophysical properties of transition metal-based luminophores. Overall, all the objectives stated above have been addressed successfully.

103911.label: Major findings and research outcome
103911.value: Through this project, we successfully developed the synthesis of transition metal–acetylide, –acyl, −alkoxycarbene, −indolizine zwitterion, −indoline, −indole zwitterion, N-heterocyclic carbene, and metallafuran complexes. Among these organometallic complexes, ruthenium−indolizine zwitterion, −indoline, and −indole zwitterion complexes reported by us represent the first examples of isolated metal−indolizine zwitterion, −indoline, and −indole zwitterion complexes in the literature. Our report on the preparation of metallafuran also represented a general synthetic strategy for the preparation of metallafuran. The photophysical properties of all these complexes were investigated by different spectroscopic techniques and theoretical methods. With the support of this research grant, a total of 13 international publications were produced, among which 3 publications (output number 1, 2, and 5) were one of the most accessed/downloaded articles for the journals they published for one/two months. The work on metallafuran (output number 11) was also chosen by the journal editor to be the front cover of Organometallics, a leading journal in the field of inorganic and nuclear chemistry. In this project, 2 PhD students were trained. Collaborative works with renowned institutes including Max-Planck-Institut für Chemische Energiekonversion and National University of Singapore were also initiated. Overall, the success of this project not only provides basic understanding on fundamental issue regarding the metal-carbon bonding interactions, but also offers useful insight to the rational design of molecular materials for applications including solar cells, photochemistry, luminescent sensing, and molecular electronic building blocks.

103911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
103911.value: The success of this project has already demonstrated that fundamental understanding on the metal−carbon bonding interactions can provide useful insight to the rational design of molecular materials for solar cells, photochemistry, and luminescent sensing applications. Further development should focus on the application of the molecular materials developed in this project. As an example, some metal complexes developed in this project can be converted into luminescent chemosensor for the detection of different analytes.

103911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
103911.value: Polypyridyl ruthenium(II) complexes represent an important class of luminophore based on transition metal complexes. They exhibit rich photophysical and photochemical properties which originate from the ruthenium(II)-to-polypyridyl triplet metal-to-ligand charge transfer excited state. We have initiated a program to employ new organometallic ligands to manipulate the emission properties of a [Ru(polypyridyl)] core. Through this project, we successfully developed the synthesis of several classes of new organometallic ligands, including indolizine zwitterion, indole zwitterion, and indoline. Detailed photophysical studies and theoretical calculations suggested that metal complexes with these ligands show superior photophysical properties over many analogues known in the literature. The success of this project not only provides basic understanding on fundamental issue regarding the metal-carbon bonding interactions, but also offers useful insight to the rational design of molecular materials for applications including solar cells, photochemistry, luminescent sensing, and molecular electronic building blocks.

104211.label: Project Objectives
104211.value: Derive the long-wavelength equations for generic stretched filaments. Use asymptotic methods to determine the solution of the full initial-boundary value problem for a Newtonian drop that is attached to a fixed ceiling and is falling under its own weight. Develop a numerical method to numerically solve the long-wavelength equations and compare the results with the asymptotic solutions. Generalise the results to include other geometries, thermal effects and non-Newtonian rheology and investigate the physical importance of these effects. In cases in which the long-wavelength equations break down, numerically solve the full axisymmetric equations and determine the underlying mechanical effects that arise.

104211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
104211.value: We will investigate the classical problem of the extension of an axisymmetric viscous filament with small initial inertia and small initial surface tension forces. We will determine how inertia and surface tension affect the dynamics of the stretching process when the filament becomes highly extended and these forces can no longer be neglected. We will adopt a long-wavelength approximation and derive leading-order asymptotic expressions for the solution of the full initial-boundary value problem for arbitrary initial shape. We will generalize our apporach to include thermal and non-Newtonian effects and use our method to understand how these effects impact the stretching process. We will compare our asymptotic results with the numerical solution of the long-wavelength equations. In cases in which the long-wavelength equations break down, we will also numerically solve the full axisymmetric problem and determine the important dynamical effects that arise in this case. 我们考察了具有较小初始惯性力和表面张力的轴对称黏性细丝在伸展过程中的经典问题。分析了惯性力和表面张力对伸展过程动力学性质的影响。当细丝在高度伸长时，这些力不能再被忽略。我们采用长波长逼近方法推导出具有任意初始形状的初-边值问题解的首阶项渐进表达式。这种方法继而被推广到包括热效应和非牛顿效应时的情形，进而用于分析这些效应如何影响伸展过程。我们对比了渐进结果与长波长方程的数值结果。在长波长方程失效的情形下，我们仍可以数值地解出整个轴对称问题并确定此情形中所呈现的重要动力学效应。

104211.label: Realisation of objectives
104211.value: We derived the long-wavelength equations for generic stretched filaments and found that the equations can be expressed in a particularly convenient form. We then used asymptotic methods based on the smallness of the aspect ratio and the initial Reynolds number to derive the solutions of the full initial-boundary-value problem for such flows. We examined these solutions and showed that there are two very different generic ways that inertia can become important. The asymptotic techniques required to obtain these solutions proved to be very challenging, but we nonetheless were able to complete the work and gain significant insight into such asymptotic problems. We also developed a numerical method that can solve the long-wavelength equations using a finite difference technique and were able to obtain good agreement with our theoretical predictions. We showed that thermal effects can readily studied in our framework. Non-Newtonian rheology can also be studied, but care needs to be taken when considering Bingham fluids. Finally, we developed an algorithm for solving the full axisymmetric equations, but the computationally expensive nature of the computation meant that careful comparison with our theoretical predictions proved to be difficult. We also used the asymptotic techniques to examine ion flow in thin membranes and were able to show (contrary to previous claims) that steady-state solutions for three ions are unique. Our techniques allowed us to show that the non-unique solutions obtained by previous authors were nonphysical. This further allowed us to study the spreading of ionic traveling waves in a number of different contexts. During the study, one of the co-Is (Robert Miura) experienced extremely serious health problems that have meant that he has been unable to participate in any scientific activities during the last 18 months of the project. This has naturally led to some serious delays. However, the PI and other co-I have managed to complete the required work.

104211.label: Major findings and research outcome
104211.value: We obtained asymptotic solutions of the full initial-boundary-value problem for a slender axisymmetric viscous thread of arbitrary initial shape that is supported by a fixed horizontal surface and extends under gravity. We have shown the inertial terms must ultimately become important and used asymptotic techniques to show that the thread can develop a long thin region that joins together two large fluid masses. In this case, we have shown that surface-tension-driven pinching will not occur if the square root of the Reynolds number is much greater than the initial aspect ratio divided by the Bond number. The results are carefully compared with the results of numerical simulations. This analysis gives a number of important insights into the mechanisms that give rise to the highly persistent and stable filaments that are observed in experiments. A less detailed version of this work had been submitted for publication prior to the mid-term report. However, the referees requested a significantly more detailed analysis of the numerical results. Unfortunately, one of the co-Is (Robert Miura) experienced extremely serious illness along with acute cognitive difficulties that have prevented him participating in the project during the last 18 months and this caused some serious delays. After it became clear that he would not recover within a reasonable time frame, the PI and other co-I completed the required work and resubmitted the paper and it is now under review. We also used the techniques from our above asymptotic study to determine exact solutions for the Poisson-Nernst-Planck (PNP) system with an arbitrary number of ion species with arbitrary valences. Previous studies have claimed that multiple solutions exist for three ions, but we were able to rigorously prove existence and uniqueness for this case. This work has been accepted for publication. The asymptotic techniques also allowed us to determine solutions for the equations that govern traveling wave propagation phenomenon known as cortical spreading depression (CSD). We examined a number of proposed mechanisms using both discrete and continuum models consisting of coupled nonlinear differential equations for the ion concentrations. This work has been accepted for publication. We also studied how the fluid mechanical effects of the vasculature interact with the CSD wave propagation. We showed that during CSD, the metabolic demands of the cortex exceed the physiological limits placed on oxygen delivery and that vasoconstriction and vasodilation play important roles in the propagation of CSD and its recovery. This work has been accepted for publication.

104211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
104211.value: There are still a number of outstanding issues when comparing the solution of the long-wavelength equations with the numerical solution of the full axisymmetric equations. In order to compare the two at very low Reynolds number, with highly extended threads requires a highly efficient, robust and flexible numerical method. We will examine ways in which this can be achieved. We also found that small initial disturbances decay diffusively, whereas larger initial disturbances can trigger traveling waves. This also represents a highly important scientific question and we will use theoretical and numerical techniques to examine this in detail.

104211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
104211.value: We have obtained exact mathematical solutions for the problem of a drop of viscous fluid falling under gravity. These solutions show that inertia must always eventually become important. Using a number of novel techniques, we were able to show that there are two ways in which inertia can become important: one in which inertia only plays a role near the boundary and the other in which inertia only plays a role in long thin filament that joins two large fluid masses. For fluids with sufficiently high surface tension, threads always pinch, but for low surface tension fluids, highly extended filaments occur in experiments. By examining the surface tension terms in our equations, we were able to predict under what circumstances pinching will occur. We used these ideas to examine the transport of ions. Previous studies had claimed that multiple steady states could occur, we were able to use our mathematical techniques to show that the results that they found included unphysical cases with negative ion concentrations and we were further able to prove uniqueness. Moreover, we applied our results to traveling wave propagation and obtained a number of important insights into what effects control the speed of the traveling wave.

104411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
104411.value: Aging and a sedentary lifestyle conspire to osteoporosis, a progressive bone disease characterized by loss of bone strength, resulting in an increased risk of fragility fractures. Although bone diseases have become an important public concern in civilized societies with aging population, the exact mechanism is far from being well understood. It is partially attributed to the fact that bone researches have been conducted with simplified experimental models that consider only the interaction between two cell members in a bone system and such models have recently been found to cause atypical function in bone forming cells (osteoblasts). The objective of this proposal is to develop a microfluidics-based biomimetic platform to create in vivo microenvironment of bone tissues and maintain the natural neighborhood among different members of bone cells. We believe this “bone-on-a-chip” system is a more faithful representation of bone tissues and will allow in-depth studies in bone researches. 本研究课题的目的是建立一个可以用来研究基质干细胞通讯和分化的仿生平台,通过模拟干细胞生长环境,观测分析细胞增长,迁移,分化的时间与空间过程.

104411.label: Realisation of objectives
104411.value: The objectives of the project have been achieved successfully. We have developed low-cost methods for fabrication of multi-level structures for cell manipulation, designed microfluidic-based platforms for cell co-culturing and mechanical stimulation, synthesized silicon nanowires for study of molecular mechanism of proliferation and differentiation of mesechymal stem cells in vitro. The low-cost fabrication method could generate fine channel features and high aspect ratio structures. Microfluidic devices with multi-level structure could be fabricated by multi-steps photolithography using this approach, which has been demonstrated for cell patterning and long-term cell culture. Using this method, we have designed and fabricated microfluidic device, which enabled co-culturing of mesenchymal stem cells and osteoblast/osteocytes in the confined microchannels. The two layer assembled device consisted of five thousand microwells for cell patterning and microchannel networks for regulation of cell-cell communications. Different widths of the microwells and the co-culturing chambers were altered to control whether two types of cells would directly contact or communicate by the cell secretions. The viability and differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) were evaluated by MTT assay, ALP activity, mineralization, and adipogenic differentiation respectively. As we found mesenchymal stem cells behaved differently in the presence of various hydrodynamic forces in the microchannels, we further investigated the role of mechanical microenvironment for the MSCs adhesion, proliferation and differentiation. We have developed a microfluidic device to exert mechanical stimulation on an individual cell for mechanosensation research. By controlling the buffer environment surrounding the trapped cells, the source of [Ca2+]i increase in mechanically stimulated cells was studied. Influence of cytoskeleton on mechanosensitive channel was also investigated at single cell level. We have also synthesized silicon nanowire arrays to study the underlying mechanisms of mechanical stimulation exerted on MSCs. Our results revealed that stretch-mediated transient Ca2+ ion channel activation and cytoskeleton reorganization during stem cell-nanowire interaction may be early events of lineage-specific potentiation of MSCs in determining the fates of mesenchylmal stem cells cultured on microenvironments with specific mechanical properties. Mechanical stimuli of SiNW array on MSCs activated a number of nonspecific mechanosensitive pathways (including Integrin, TGF-β, IGF, and Insulin pathways), the activities of which converged to stimulate the osteogenesis and chondrogenesis via the Ras-Raf-mitogen-activated protein kinase (MEK)-extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) cascade.
