104411.label: Major findings and research outcome
104411.value: 1. We have developed a microfabrication method that retains high channel quality and aspect ratio by exploring a rarely used solder resist material in combination with screen printing technique to generate masters. Using screen printing, fine channel features and high aspect ratio structures were prepared within three hours. Microfluidic devices with multi-level structure could be fabricated by multi-steps photolithography using this approach, which has been demonstrated for cell patterning and long-term cell culture. (Biosensors and Bioelectronics, 2013, 41, 675-683.) 2. We have designed microfluidic-based device for co-culturing of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and osteoblast cells (3T3E1). The chip was assembled by two layers: the bottom layer containing five thousand microwells for MSCs and 3T3E1 patterning respectively and the top layer with control channels for regulation of 3T3E1 and MSCs communication. The density and spatial distribution of 3T3E1 cells were both controlled by microwells in the two chambers. The viability and differentiation of MSCs were evaluated by MTT assay, ALP activity, mineralization, and adipogenic differentiation, respectively. (Manuscript in preparation.) 3. We have designed and fabricated a microfluidic device to exert mechanical stimulation on an individual cell for mechanosensation research. The device was capable of precisely control of the microenvironment and exertion of whole-cell compression for qualitative and quantitative study of mechanosensation in individual suspension cells. By controlling the buffer environment surrounding the trapped cells, the source of [Ca2+]i increase in mechanically stimulated cells, influence of cytoskeleton on mechanosensitive channel were investigated at single cell level. (Lab Chip, 2013, 13, 1060-1069.) 4. We have constructed vertically aligned silicon nanowire (SiNW) arrays for MSCs growth and studied the role of mechanical microenvironment for the MSCs adhesion, proliferation and differentiation. Our results revealed that stretch-mediated transient Ca2+ ion channel activation and cytoskeleton reorganization during stem cell-nanowire interaction may be early events of lineage-specific potentiation of MSCs in determining the fates of mesenchymal stem cells cultured on microenvironments with specific mechanical properties. (Nanomedicine: NBM, DOI: 10.1016/j.nano.2014.02.003) 5. We further revealed that the interactions between MSCs and the SiNW arrays caused the stem cells to preferentially differentiate towards osteocytes and chondrocytes but not adipocytes in the absence of supplementary growth factors. Mechanical stimuli of SiNW array on MSCs activated a number of nonspecific mechanosensitive pathways, the activities of which converged to stimulate the osteogenesis and chondrogenesis via the Ras-Raf-mitogen-activated protein kinase (MEK)-extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) cascade. (Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2013, 5, 13295−13304.)

104411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
104411.value: The research project has developed microfluidic-based devices and nanomaterials to study the mechanosensation, differentiation and cell communication of mesenchymal stem cells in bone formation. The microfluidic-based platforms have facilitated cell-cell communications with precise control of cell-cell distance and exertion of mechanical stimulation on single cell. As in-vivo biomimetic systems, microfluidic devices could be further used as universal platforms to study other types of cells, such as neurons, synapses, and cancer cell microenvironments, which will provide insights on the basis of cellular behaviors in tissue engineering, disease development and drug discovery. The silicon nanowires have provided mechanical stimulation on cells for the study of molecular regulation of mesenchymal stem cell proliferation and differentiation. Further applications could be investigated to explore the feasibility of the silicon nanowires as biocompatible materials for bone tissue regeneration.

104411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
104411.value: The research project has utilized different advanced biomedical tools study the mechanosensation of mesenchymal stem cells, cell communication and osteogenesis during bone formation. The microfluidic-based platforms have facilitated cell-cell communications with precise control of cell-cell distance and exertion of mechanical stimulation on single cell. The silicon nanowires have provided mechanical stimulation on mesenchymal stem cells for the study of molecular regulation of cell proliferation and differentiation. The results have increased our understandings on developing biomimetic platforms for reconstruction of in-vivo microenvironment for cell growth and communication, and understanding the mechanism of mesenchymal stem cells differentiation and osteogenesis. The project has emphasized the importance in the areas of material science, analytical chemistry and cell biology, and has direct relevance to the development of tissue engineering. This project has provided a basis for further development of microfluidic-based device and nanomaterials as useful platforms for understanding cellular behaviors and molecular mechanisms of stem cells proliferation and differentiation in the mimetic natural neighborhood. This project has also trained researchers with multi-disciplinary knowledge and experience in cell biology and biomedical engineering.

104511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
104511.value: 雖然關於包含Boltzmann方程、Landau方程、Vlasov-Poisson (Maxwell) -Boltzmann(Landau)方程組等經典的動力學方程和方程組的數學理論已有很多結果，但是關於這些方程和方程組的存在性結果中的大多數（如果不是全部的話）都是在如下的框架中得到的：要麼是真空的擾動，要麼是一個整體平衡態的擾動，要麼是在一個有界區域中，要麼是空間週期解（在一個環上），要麼是全空間問題但是當空間變元趨於無窮時趨於給定的平衡態。 一個自然和有趣的問題是：如果上述假設不成立時如何建立相應的數學理論？在本項目中我們將研究當空間變元趨於無窮時解不滿足具體的漸進性態時一些經典的動力學方程和方程組Cauchy問題的適定性，即解的存在性、唯一性和穩定性。 以統計物理學中的基本方程和動力學的基石Boltzmann方程為例，其整體解的存在性已在如下框架下得到了解決： 1、在一個有界區域或一個環上； 2、全空間或外區域上真空或一個整體Maxwell分佈的擾動； 3、由於外力項等所導致的一些非平凡profile或在空間變數趨於無窮時趨於不同 的整體Maxwell分佈的一些基本波模式的擾動。 本項目擬研究的問題之一是研究當初值只是一些函數空間中的有界函數時其Cauchy問題的適定性。為此，除了利用一些已知的分析技巧外，我們還得發展一些新的數學技巧。 為了得到適定性理論，我們將首先從局部或整體解的存在性理論開始。相關的一些想法將在後文給出。一旦得到了存在性理論，我們將研究這些解的定量性質，諸如穩定性、唯一性、正則性和大時間性態等。

104511.label: Major findings and research outcome
104511.value: The research outputs have been written in six research papers, among them, four have been accepted/published in international refereed journals, including some top journals, such as Journal of American Mathematical Society. Some details of the research findings are given as follows. In the first paper, by identifying a norm capturing the effect of the forcing governed by the Poisson equation, we give a spectrum analysis on the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann system. It is shown that the spectrum structure is genuinely different from the well-known one of the Boltzmann equation. In the second paper, we develop an approach to study the well-posedness of the Prandtl boundary layer equation in the Sobolev spaces by using a direct energy method instead of the Crocco transformation. The existence of classical solutions to the Cauchy problem for the Boltzmann equation without angular cutoff has been extensively studied in the framework when the solution has Maxwellian decay in the velocity variable. In the third paper, we prove local existence of solutions with polynomial decay in the velocity variable for the Boltzmann equation with soft potential. In the fourth paper, without Grad's angular cutoff assumption, the local existence of classical solutions to the Boltzmann equation is studied without assuming that the initial data is close to a global equilibrium. In the fifth paper, we analyze the spectrum structure of some kinetic equations qualitatively by using semigroup theory and linear operator perturbation theory. The models include the Boltzmann equation for hard potentials and the Landau equation. The purpose of the sixth paper is to introduce a new characterization of the characteristic functions for the study on the measure valued solution to the homogeneous Boltzmann equation so that it precisely captures the moment constraint in physics. In addition, the global in time smoothing effect of the infinite energy solution is justified as for the finite energy solution except for a single Dirac mass initial datum.

104511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
104511.value: The existence, stability and regularity for the solutions to some kinetic equations including the Boltzmann equation as a typical example were studied in some general settings. It will be interesting and challenging to further develop the theories in the direction of measure valued solutions. So far, the existing mathematical theories are basically limited to space homogeneous and most of them are about the Maxwellian cross section. How to establish a framework for the space inhomogeneous problems can be further pursued.

104511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
104511.value: The Boltzmann equation is a fundamental equation in kinetic theory that describes the time evolution of the particles in rarefied gas through elastic collision. There have been extensive studies on the mathematical theories of kinetic equations. On the other hand, most if not all of the existence results on these equations and systems are obtained in the frameworks of perturbation of vacuum, or perturbation of a global equilibrium, or in a bounded domain, or space periodic solutions (in a torus), or the Cauchy problem with equilibrium states specified at infinity in space. One natural and interesting question that can be raised is that how about none of the above assumptions are satisfied. In this project, we will study the well-posedness theory, that is, existence, stability and uniqueness of solutions to some classical kinetic equations and systems in some general settings, including those about measure valued solutions that only required some moments up to some extent. We hope the mathematical theories established in this project will not only enrich the mathematical theories of the kinetic equations but also enhance the understanding of the gas motions in rarefied gas in some general settings.

104911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
104911.value: Wide bandgap semiconductors have extensive applications in high-temperature high-power electronics. Thus far, GaN- and SiC-based optoelectronic and power devices have been commercially available: Such devices can operate in hostile environments where conventional Si- and GaAs-based electronics cannot function. The increasing requirements on applications of electronic and optoelectronic devices under more extreme conditions prompt further research on the development of innovative semiconductor materials and devices. Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) has many characteristics superior to GaN and SiC, which makes it a very attractive material for fabricating high-power electronic devices being able to work under even harsher conditions. The direct bandgap of hBN also enables fabrication of high-efficiency optoelectronic devices emitting deep-UV light. Moreover, hBN films can be grown on a variety of substrates by different deposition methods, which makes the applications of hBN films more practicable and more cost-effective. However, the study of the electronic and optoelectronic applications of hBN is still in its infancy and lots of open questions remain. This project will focus on the fabrication of high-temperature high-power hBN-based electronics, such as field effect transistors (FETs), and p-n diodes, based on the synthesis of high-quality hBN films by chemical vapor deposition (CVD) and doping by ion implantation. The doping efficiency and activation energy of selected dopants will be evaluated, and the effects of deposition, ion implantation and annealing parameters on the electrical and transport properties of hBN films will be systematically studied. The outcome of the project is expected to provide enhanced fundamental understanding and new process guidelines for the fabrication of hBN-based devices for practical applications. This proposal is based on the extensive experience of the investigators in the areas of thin film synthesis and doping techniques of relevant wide bandgap materials such as diamond, cubic BN and AlN in particular, and as well of the characterization and studies of electronic and transport properties of materials in general. The preliminary results from our research have already demonstrated the feasibility of preparing p- and n-type hBN films by ion implantation. Combination of the multi-disciplinary and complementary expertise among the participating members of this research team further guarantees the successful outcome and significant impact of the project. 寬頻隙半導體在高溫、大功率電子器件中有著廣泛的應用。目前，基於氮化鎵和碳化矽的光電和功率器件已經實現了商業化，並可以在矽基和砷化鎵基器件無法勝任的惡劣環境中工作。然而，由於對電子器件在更加極端條件下工作的需求不斷增加，使得新型寬頻隙半導體材料和器件的研製和開發成為一個重要的研究方向。六方氮化硼（hBN）具有許多優於氮化鎵和碳化矽的性能，非常適用於製造在更極端條件下工作的大功率電子器件。由於hBN是直接帶隙半導體材料，也可以用它來製備高效的深紫外發光器件。前期工作表明可以用不同的方法將hBN薄膜沉積在多種襯底上，因此其低成本的實際應用也將更容易實現。目前，對於hBN電學和光電性能方面的研究仍處於探索階段，還存在不少問題需要解決。 本課題擬在化學氣相沉積法合成高品質hBN薄膜及離子注入摻雜工作的基礎上，研製基於hBN的高溫、大功率電子器件，如場效應電晶體、二極體等。我們將評估各種相應摻雜劑的摻雜效率和激活能，並系統地研究薄膜沉積、離子注入和退火工藝對hBN薄膜電學及輸運特性的影響。本項目的實施有望對hBN器件的製備及實際應用提供理論基礎和工藝指導。項目組成員在寬頻隙半導體薄膜（如金剛石、立方氮化硼和氮化鋁等）的合成和摻雜，尤其是材料的電學、輸運特性的研究方面積累了長期的經驗。我們初步的研究結果已證實了利用離子注入對hBN薄膜進行p型和n型摻雜的可行性；項目組成員間多學科專長的互補也將對項目的成功實施並取得有影響力的成果提供保障。

104911.label: Realisation of objectives
104911.value: We have deposited hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) films on different substrates by fluorine-assisted electron cyclotron resonance microwave plasma chemical vapor deposition (ECR MPCVD) in a gas mixture of BF3-N2-H2-Ar-He and radio-frequency magnetron sputtering (r.f. MS) with a BN target. The influences of growth parameters on the phase composition, crystallinity and microstructure of hBN films have been studied systematically. Based on that, high-quality hBN films with high phase purity, high crystalline quality and wide bandgap have been synthesized. We have achieved n-type and p-type doping of hBN films through ion implantation followed by post-implantation thermal annealing. A variety of impurities including beryllium, silicon, and sulfur have been doped into hBN films. The doping efficiency of dopants has been demonstrated to depend strongly on the ion implantation and annealing processes, e.g., ion dose, implantation energy, and annealing temperature and duration. Beryllium and silicon have been identified as effective dopants for the p- and n-type conductivities of hBN films, respectively. After doping, the conductivity of hBN films has been tuned over a wide range of 3~7 orders magnitude. We have studied the electrical and transport properties of doped hBN films by using four-point probe method and Hall Effect measurements. The activation energy and electronic structures of hBN films doped with different impurities and their dependence on microstructure, ion dose and energy, and annealing conditions, were investigated experimentally and theoretically. The doping mechanism has been proposed based on the experimental observations and simulation. We have fabricated diamond/hBN p-n heterojunction diodes and studied their performance up to 400 oC. The p-type boron-doped diamond layers were grown epitaxially on single crystal diamond by microwave plasma CVD; the hBN films were prepared on the diamond layer, and n-type conductivity of hBN films was achieved by silicon implantation. Electrical measurements revealed obvious rectifying characteristic between n-type hBN and p-type diamond.

104911.label: Major findings and research outcome
104911.value: The substrate temperature, bias voltage and gas composition have strong impacts on the stoichiometry, phase purity, and crystalline quality of hBN films grown by CVD: 1) An elevated substrate temperature is beneficial to achieving high crystallinity and improving transport properties of hBN films. 2) A high negative substrate bias can switch the hBN basal planes from being parallel to being perpendicular to substrate surface. 3) The gas composition is predominant in determining the desired stoichiometry and deposition speed. The CVD hBN films are polycrystalline with the grain size in the range from tens to over hundred nm. The films show excellent transparence to visible light and their band gap is close to that of single crystal hBN. Beryllium and silicon have been verified to be promising dopants to introduce p- and n-type conductivities of hBN films by ion implantation. By elaborating the conditions for ion implantation, including ion energy and ion dose, the desired depth profile and concentration of implanted ions could be achieved. A threshold of ion dose is demonstrated for triggering the conductivity increase of hBN films, and the post-implantation annealing is necessary to activate the dopants and recover the damages induced by implantation. As compared to sp3-bonded cubic BN, the dopants can be activated at lower annealing temperatures and for shorter durations. The conductivity of doped hBN films can be enhanced by 3~7 orders of magnitude, and the minimum resistivity of hBN film obtained is 0.5 Ω·cm at room temperature. . Analysis on the electronic structure of doped hBN revealed multi shallow donor/acceptor levels induced in the bandgap. Based on the experimental observations and simulations by density function theory, the shallow dopant levels are suggested to be due to the substitution of lattice B or N atoms by implanted dopants. However, the formation of impurity-vacancy complexes may also make contribution. p-n heterojunction diodes are fabricated using B-doped diamond and Si-implanted hBN film, and they show clearly rectifying characteristic up to 400 oC. However, the rectification ratio decreases from 400 (±5V) at room temperature to 10 at 400 oC. It is also revealed that graphitization of diamond during ion implantation and high temperature annealing might deteriorate the rectification of the heterojunctions.

104911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
104911.value: Although the controlled doping process for hBN films via ion implantation has been achieved experimentally, more effort are still needed to control the conductivity of hBN films in a wider range, and the doping mechanism should be further investigated. More experiments are required to study the distribution of dopants in hBN films, in particular to explore the impact of grain boundaries. These studies may facilitate our understanding why a threshold ion dose is required to trigger the conductivity increase. Theoretical calculations about diffusion, occupying sites, and defects in hBN are also needed to understand heavy doping effects . The ion implantation process for device fabrication should be further optimized to eliminate possible damages and graphitization of diamond which make the device unstable. Studies on the fabrication of devices such as field effect transistor and homojunction diodes are also attractive tasks. Moreover, due to the direct bandgap of hBN, the hBN-based light-emitting devices working in the deep UV range will have great research interests and diverse applications.

104911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
104911.value: The increasing requirements on applications of electronic devices under extreme conditions prompt research on the development of innovative semiconductor materials and devices. Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) has an attractive combination of outstanding physical and chemical properties, such as a wide direct bandgap, high thermal conductivity (in basal planes), and excellent thermal and chemical stabilities, which makes it a very promising material for fabricating high-temperature electronic devices. However, the capability to synthesize high-quality hBN and to effectively control its electrical properties is a necessary foundation for the development of hBN devices. In this project, we have successfully developed chemical vapor deposition and physical vapor deposition techniques for the synthesis of high-quality transparent hBN films, and we have also demonstrated an effective approach to tune the electric properties of hBN films via ion implantation. We have systematically studied the electrical properties of doped hBN films and proposed the doping mechanism based on experimental observations and theoretical simulations, which provides fundamental understanding and process guidelines for the fabrication of hBN-based devices. The construction of hBN/diamond p-n heterojunctions further explores the applications potentials of hBN films in high-temperature electronics.

105011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
105011.value: Sparsity enables efficient representations and processing of data or functions relations of large variables. This project aims at sparse approximations produced by some learning algorithms. We shall first consider sparse approximations expressed as linear combinations of empirical features with coefficients generated by some regularization schemes. Empirical features allow the scheme to be efficiently implemented in terms of a general regularizer. Sparsity and error analysis will be conducted by methods from learning theory and approximation theory. Then we shall study spectral algorithms related to graph Laplacians and clustering. Ideas of frequency analysis from wavelets can be used to derive sparsity and learning rates of these learning algorithms. Finally some learning schemes involving parameters associated with scaling operations or frequency ranges will be investigated. These include regularization schemes or online algorithms associated with insensitive loss and kernel-based algorithms with scaled kernels. Methods from approximation theory and properties of reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces will be applied in our analysis. 稀疏性提供多变量数据或函数关系的有效表示和处理。本项目研究由一些学习算法产生的稀疏逼近。我们首先考虑由正则化算法产生系数作经验特征的线形组合所产生的稀疏逼近。经验特征允许该算法通过一般正则化项有效执行。稀疏性和误差分析将利用学习理论及逼近论方法得以实现。然后我们研究与图拉普拉斯和聚类相关的谱算法。小波中频谱分析方法可用来得到这些学习算法的稀疏性和学习率。本项目最后研究几类带有相应于伸缩算子或频率范围的参数的学习算法。其中包括由非敏感损失导出的正则化或在线算法及由伸缩核产生的核方法。我们的分析将利用到逼近论方法及再生核希尔伯特空间的性质。

105011.label: Major findings and research outcome
105011.value: For coefficient-based regularization schemes, interacting stochastic processes may generate valuable empirical features and sparsity of the learning algorithms. In [1], we studied a theoretical approximation theory problem concerning extinction probabilities of interacting branching collision processes, and showed that the asymptotic behaviour of these extinction probabilities follows an elegant and homogeneous power law which takes a very simple form. In [2], L. Q. Li and the PI proposed a learning theory approach to the topic of estimating transfer functions in system identification. A frequency domain identification problem was formulated as an atomic norm regularization scheme in a random design framework of learning theory. Such a formulation makes it possible to obtain sparsity and provide finite sample estimates for learning the transfer function in a learning theory framework. Error analysis was done for the learning algorithm by applying a local polynomial reproduction formula, concentration inequalities and iteration techniques. The best convergence rate was obtained and some interesting connections to spectral algorithms were found from our study. The paper provides some interesting interactions among the areas of system identification, learning theory and scaling-based frequency analysis. In [3], Christmann and the PI gave learning rates for regularized kernel based methods in additive models which play an important role in semiparametric statistics and sparsity analysis. The obtained learning rates compare favourably in particular in high dimensions to recent results on optimal learning rates for purely nonparametric regularized kernel based quantile regression using the Gaussian radial basis function kernel, provided the assumption of an additive model is valid. In [4], B. Z. Li and the PI considered approximation on variable Lp spaces associated with a general exponent function p and a general bounded Borel measure on an open subset of a Euclidean space. We studied approximation by Bernstein type linear operators. Under an assumption of log-Holder continuity of the exponent function p, we verified a conjecture raised previously about the uniform boundedness of Bernstein-Durrmeyer and Bernstein-Kantorovich operators on variable Lp space. 110311.value: Objective 1: Improvement of recently proposed vector-valued convex relaxation methods. We have recently proposed a generalization of our convex relaxation methods to a larger class of problems including image registration and multi-phase segmentation. Besides, we expect the algorithm to be fast because the regularization term related to the Hodge decomposition is convex. Objective 4: Convex watershed method. 110311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
110311.value: This research project proposes to develop novel optimization algorithms to solve problems arising in image processing (IP). Most fundamental problems in IP can be cast as energy minimization problems such as image denoising (which removes noise in images), image segmentation (which partitions the image into important objects), image registration (which is used for object tracking or medical imaging), and 3D surface reconstruction (from a set of data points or a set of images). Except the image denoising problem, all IP problems are defined as non-convex minimization problems, which are highly dependent to the initialization and can also be slow to minimize such as the popular level set method. The ultimate objective of this project is to overcome the bottleneck problem of non-convexity in IP problems. In other words, we want to "convexify" the original non-convex problems to find exact global solutions. This is a challenging mathematical problem because it is known that all convex relaxations do not provide global solutions of the original problems. However, we have recently designed convex problems whose minimizers can be used to easily obtain global solutions of non-convex geometric IP problems. These new convex models are very promising because they can guarantee global solutions (independent of the initialization), fast algorithms and accurate solutions (sub-pixel precision). Usually, it is difficult to get all three advantages simultaneously but our framework can guarantee all in many cases. These proposed convex methods work for several important problems (there is a new and growing literature about these new methods) but we do not know how general it can be. This is the objective of this proposal. We propose to extend our convex methods to new non-convex image processing problems.

110311.label: Realisation of objectives
110311.value: Objective 1: This objective was achieved at 100% with the paper “Completely Convex Formulation of the Chan-Vese Image Segmentation Model" published in International Journal of Computer Vision. This work has introduced breakthrough ideas that were essential to achieve the other objectives of the grant. Objective 2: This objective was also completed at 90% with the paper "Fast Geodesic Active Fields - A Splitting Scheme for Geometric Image Registration" published in IEEE Transactions on Image Processing. Although the proposed medical imaging registration model has not been fully convexified, it has produced state-of-the-art results in this field. Besides, the contribution of this work was further extended with the paper “Enhanced Compressed Sensing Recovery with Level Set Normals", published in IEEE Transactions on Image Processing, which offers one of the best image recovery techniques. Objective 3: This objective was achieved at 70% with the paper "An Efficient Algorithm for Level Set Method Preserving Distance Function", IEEE Transactions on Image Processing. Although the registration method is not directly based on the Hodge decomposition, as it was proposed in the original proposal, we found that the level set method could provide even better and fast-to-compute registration flows. Objective 4: This objective was completed at 80% with the paper "Convergence and Energy Landscape for Cheeger Cut Clustering", published at the Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS). The original methodology proposed in the grant application suggested to convexify the watershed method. We discovered that it was a better approach to find a tight continuous relaxation of the Cheeger cut energy to achieve the objective of data segmentation/clustering.

110311.label: Major findings and research outcome
110311.value: The major findings and research outcome are quantified by the 4 following journal papers and 1 conference paper (listed in Part C): Publication 1: "Completely Convex Formulation of the Chan-Vese Image Segmentation Model", International Journal of Computer Vision. We propose a convex relaxation of the popular K-means segmentation algorithm. Our approach is based on a vector-valued relaxation technique for non-convex and non-smooth energies. Our experiments show that our method computes tight approximations of optimal solutions, unlike the popular method proposed by Chan et al., which quality of solutions depends on the choice of the initial condition. Publication 2: "An Efficient Algorithm for Level Set Method Preserving Distance Function", IEEE Transactions on Image Processing. We introduce a fast algorithm to preserve distance functions for the well-known level set method. The main advantage of our algorithm lies in the fact that it is not limited by the CFL condition. Our method proves to be 5–6 times faster than standard distance preserving level set techniques. Besides, our method stays generic and can be applied to any level set methods that require the distance information. Publication 3: “Enhanced Compressed Sensing Recovery with Level Set Normals", IEEE Transactions on Image Processing. We propose a compressive sensing algorithm that exploits geometric properties of images by estimating normal vectors of the image level curves to recover images of high quality from few measurements. Experiments show a clear improvement over related state-of-the-art algorithms in the quality of the reconstructed images and the robustness of the proposed method to noise, different kind of images, and reduced measurements. Publication 4: "Fast Geodesic Active Fields - A Splitting Scheme for Geometric Image Registration", IEEE Transactions on Image Processing. We present an efficient numerical scheme for the Geodesic Active Fields for geometric image registration. The numerical scheme uses a splitting approach where data and regularity energy terms are optimized over two distinct deformation fields that are constrained to be equal via an augmented Lagrangian approach. We compare the Geodesic Active Fields method against the popular Demons method and three more recent state-of-the-art algorithms. Over the range of example applications, it also consistently produces results not far from more dedicated state-of-the-art methods, illustrating the flexibility of the proposed framework. Publication 5: "Convergence and Energy Landscape for Cheeger Cut Clustering", Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS). This work provides both theoretical and algorithmic results for the L1-relaxation of the Cheeger cut problem. The L2-relaxation, known as spectral clustering, only loosely relates to the Cheeger cut; however, it is convex and leads to a simple optimization problem. The L1-relaxation, in contrast, is non-convex but is provably equivalent to the original problem. The L1-relaxation therefore trades convexity for exactness, yielding improved clustering results at the cost of a more challenging optimization.

110311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
110311.value: There are several possible developments of the ideas and contributions introduced in this research grant. We provide a few potential developments here: 1. Future development for the work "An Efficient Algorithm for Level Set Method Preserving Distance Function". The proposed algorithm can be speed up significantly using a narrow-band approach and a parallelized version of the algorithm on graphics processing units (GPUs). Besides, there are several applications of this generic work in medical image segmentation, satellite segmentation with higher order geometric features or Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). 2. Future development for the work “Enhanced Compressed Sensing Recovery with Level Set Normals". The introduced normal guided recovery method offers state-of-the-art results in the important field of compressed sensing. However, we could not provide a rigorous proof of convergence of the algorithm. We will investigate a rigorous algorithm in the future. 3. Future development for the work “Convergence and Energy Landscape for Cheeger Cut Clustering”. The proposed algorithm obtains excellent results for two-class partitioning problems. Unfortunately, these recursive extensions have yet to produce state-of-the art results for multi-class clustering problems. A future work is to develop a multiclass total variation clustering that does not rely on a recursive procedure.

110311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
110311.value: This research project has developed novel optimization algorithms to solve problems arising in image processing and machine learning. Most fundamental problems in these fields can be cast as energy minimization problems such as image segmentation (which partitions the image into important objects) and data clustering (which partitions data into sensible groups). Most of these problems are defined as non-convex minimization problems, which are highly dependent to the initialization and can also be slow to minimize. The ultimate objective of this project is to overcome the bottleneck problem of non-convexity. In other words, we want to find exact global solutions in a very efficient way. This is a challenging mathematical and algorithmic problem, and the project was able to deliver new breakthrough algorithms that have been published on top research journals and international conferences.

111411.label: Project Objectives
111411.value: Develop new pinning-controlled strategies of choosing informed agents and design effective pinning controllers for complex networked systems to reach predesigned flocking patterns. Design effective observers using only local and partial state information of agents for pinning-controlled flocking. Develop new adaptive techniques on coupling strengths and control gains for distributed control of multi-agent complex networked systems towards pre-desired flocking. 111411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
111411.value: This proposal aims to design some effective distributed flocking algorithms for pinning control of complex networked systems of multiple autonomous agents. First, the pinning control approach initiated by the Principal Investigator will be incorporated into the conventional flocking algorithms to choose a suitable fraction of pinned agents called informed agents such that the whole network of mobile systems can reach a predesigned flocking pattern, for which both rigorous mathematical analysis and numerical simulations will be performed. Then, some fundamental problems in pinning control of such flocking systems will be investigated, such as what which portion of informed agents should be chosen towards efficient flocking, and what kind of pinning controllers should be designed? Also, as an efficient approach, some observer-based pinning controllers will be designed using only local and partial state information of some agents for practical situations where other information may not be available. Moreover, based on adaptive strategies, several distributed adaptive laws will be designed without requiring global network information to relax some existing conservative conditions for flocking. Finally, the designed algorithms will be extended to studying more practical and yet more challenging flocking systems with time delays, switching topologies, communication noises, and intermittent measurements. The approach and methodology are based on algebraic graph theory, dynamical systems theory and automatic control theory.

111411.label: Realisation of objectives
111411.value: All three objectives have been completed with satisfactory results.

111511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
111511.value: This proposal initiates a comprehensive research program into the study of networked control systems, with a particular orientation toward wireless networked systems. Our principal goal is to investigate the fundamental design constraints and performance limits of wireless networked feedback control, and the design of communication components such as coder/decoder to circumvent the constraints and thus to improve performance. We employ the benchmark performance index of tracking as our performance measure, and attempt to accomplish the following technical objectives: (1) To quantify the fundamental constraints and limits imposed by essential wireless characteristics such as packet loss, random delay, fading and multipath propagation processes on control design, and to develop computational solutions and analytical bounds for optimal tracking over feedback channels with these characteristics. (2) To develop a mean-square small-gain approach for the analysis and design of networked feedback systems with random logarithmically quantized and random multiplicative channels, which are known to capture a variety of wireless phenomena and provide a unified framework addressing packet loss, random delay, fading and multipath propagation. (3) To investigate how coder/decoder may be designed to improve tracking performance, and in particular how controller and coder/decoder may be jointly designed to optimize tracking performance. (4) To develop a multirate filterbank small-gain approach, and lifting techniques for the analysis and design of wireless networked feedback systems. Underlying these objectives is the central task that seeks to investigate how wireless networks may result in design constraints and hence degrade control performance in ways unfound previously, and to find ways to design coder/decoder to circumvent the constraints and improve the performance. We propose a research plan that addresses and incorporates key characteristics of wireless communication channels, and employs key wireless technologies such as multirate filterbank coders/decoders. We develop a mean-square small-gain approach particularly relevant to these problems, which draws upon theories and techniques of robust control, multirate signal processing, and optimal functional approximation. The project seeks to advance significantly the current state of networked control research, and is believed to hold considerable academic interest and practical importance. Indeed, as wireless communication technology is continuing to grow at a breathtaking speed, control over wireless networks promises to have an enormous scope of applications. The project seeks to provide answers to key and fundamental issues facing the design of wireless networked control systems, and thus has the potential to impact a variety of these areas in both theoretical and applied research. 本項目旨在深入、廣泛地研究網絡控制系統，並特別專注於無線網絡系統。本項目的主要目的，乃是研究無線網絡反饋控制的根本性約束與性能極限，以及諸如編碼、解碼器等通訊組件的設計，使能突破此類約束從而改進系統性能。我們擬採用跟蹤這一標尺性性能指標，嘗試達到如下目標： （1） 確定由無線網絡之主要特徵如丟包、隨即延遲、衰減及多徑傳播等導致的設計約束與性能極限，為此類無線網絡控制系統的跟蹤問題發展計算解決方案及解析下界； （2） 對具有隨機對數量化及隨機乘性通道之網絡反饋系統，發展均方小增益分析及設計方法。現已知此類通道可刻畫多種無線網絡特徵，因之能提供一個統一的框架，以資探討丟包、隨即延遲、衰減及多徑傳播等現象； （3） 研究如何設計編碼、解碼器從而改進跟蹤性能，尤其是控制器和編碼、解碼器聯合設計問題； （4） 針對無線網絡反饋系統，發展基於多率濾波器庫的小增益分析與設計方法，以及相應的“推舉”方法。 貫穿於以上諸目標的中心任務，是探索無線網絡將如何對反饋系統設計施加前所未有的約束，進而降低控制性能；更進一步，如何相應地設計編碼、解碼器使能克服這些約束並改進性能。我們提出此研究計畫，旨在探討無線通訊信道的關鍵特徵，並採用如多率濾波器庫的編碼、解碼器結構。我們擬綜合魯棒控制、多率信號處理及最優函數逼近中的理論和方法，發展針對於上述問題的均方小增益方法。我們相信，本項目蘊含重大學術意義及實用價值，將極大地推動網絡控制研究的進步。的確，隨著無線通訊技術以驚人的速度進一步發展，通過無線網絡實行控制將有極為廣泛的應用。本項目旨在給無線網絡控制系統設計中面臨的關鍵性問題提供答案，因此也將潛在地影響網絡控制理論和應用研究的一系列課題和領域。

111511.label: Realisation of objectives
111511.value: We believe that this project has been highly successful. All objectives except Objective 4 are completed near to perfection, resulting in seven journal publications and eleven conference papers. Of the seven journal papers, all are published or accepted for publication by the two top journals in the field of systems and control, that is, the IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control and Automatica, with six of the seven papers being Full Papers and two of them being a two-part series. This sheer outcome is by no means short of being extraordinary, and it spells out an very high level of scholarship in addition to an extraordinary level of productivity. Major results and findings are summarized in Section 6.1-Major Findings and Outcomes. While still under pursuit, Objective 4 was overridden by more important issues discovered as our research proceeded. The resolution of these more important problems has led to the greater success of the project as alluded to above. In the due course, a high quality Ph.D. student, Dr. Song Fang, was produced, who has had one full paper accepted for publication in the IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control and another full paper under review by Automatica. Additionally, based on his Ph.D. thesis, Dr. Fang is currently preparing a manuscript for publication of a research monograph by Springer.

111511.label: Major findings and research outcome
111511.value: This project has helped resolve several important problems in the research of networked feedback control systems. Among other successes, two of the highlights are summarized below. Perhaps the most important results generated from this project are the two-part papers [2, 3]. In these papers, we studied in depth the stabilization and optimal control problems for linear systems subject to structured multiplicative stochastic uncertainties. Apart from their own interest, which are longstanding open problems since the early 1970s in the area of stochastic control, these problems have been found closely relevant to networked control problems; multiplicative stochastic uncertainties can be used to model effectively transmission losses (e.g., data dropout, random delays, fading) in the so-called erasure communication channels. We solved the stabilization problem in [2] to the extent where possible. Specifically, the problem is completely resolved for minimum phase systems with possible time delays, while for nonminimum phase systems, an example is constructed to show that the problem is in general nonconvex and hence is unlikely to be solvable. The solution led to necessary and sufficient conditions for a system to be stabilizable despite the presence of structured multiplicative stochastic uncertainties, or for a feedback controller to stabilize an unstable plant over erasure channels. These conditions furnish fundamental bounds on the channel noise variances in terms of the plant unstable poles. Furthermore, in [3], we solved the optimal control problem similarly. Our results serve the dual purpose in that (a) they solve the longstanding optimal stochastic control problem, and (b) they provide the fundamental bounds for stabilization and the optimal performance of networked feedback systems with erasure channels. These results are believed to be a major triumph over a problem that has been long known to be open and exceedingly difficult. An equally important development in this project is the derivation of Bode-type integral inequalities and power attenuation bounds in the networked control setting, reported in [6, 7]. In this endeavor, we developed a general information-theoretic paradigm for analyzing the limitations and tradeoffs imposed by communication channels. The integral inequalities quantify the tradeoffs in disturbance attenuation for broad classes of systems. The channel blurredness, a newly developed information measure for the quality of multi-port communication channels, is used to characterize the effect of communication constraints on the integrals and henceforth the tradeoff in disturbance attenuation. Moreover, channel blurredness also plays a central role in quantifying the fundamental limit in power reduction of a networked feedback system.

111511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
111511.value: Nearly all objectives are accomplished to satisfaction and to their fullest. Further investigation may be carried out along two directions: (1) It remains desirable and highly beneficial to develop more refined and thus more informative Bode type integrals which will incorporate and highlight the directional impact of the MIMO plant as well as the MIMO channel on the performance limitation and tradeoff of MIMO networked feedback systems. Also of significant interest is an analog to the conventional Poisson integral relations, which will characterize the pole and zero interactions in a networked feedback setting. (2) It will be of significant interest to investigate the fundamental limits of stabilization and tracking using periodic controllers for feedback over communication channels, as opposed to the LTI controllers used in the current work. In this vein, it will be particularly interesting to see whether and how the channel noise variance bound necessary for stabilization may diminish. Equally noteworthy is how sampling aliases may degrade the tracking performance. We plan to undertake these studies in a future project.

111511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
111511.value: This project sets out to investigate fundamental problems concerning networked feedback systems, which seek to integrate communication channels and feedback controllers. This is an area of research that has not been addressed until very recently and one that poses a daunting challenge to both theoreticians and practitioners alike. The project solved a number of open problems in both the classical stochastic control sense and in the networked control setting, which led to fundamental findings for stabilization and performance of such systems in the forms of analytical or readily computable conditions and expressions. The Bode-type integral inequalities are developed and linked to newly proposed information-theoretic measures, which serve to characterize the fundamental tradeoff in disturbance attenuation over different frequency ranges.

112111.value: 可靠評價及判斷各種的不確定性是對傳統的多準則決策（MCDM）理論和方法的重大挑戰。證據推理（ER）方法提供了一種新穎、嚴謹和一致的方式為不確定性建模，在最近幾年在MCDM領域上，已獲得了越來越多的關注和廣泛的應用。在ER方法中，主觀判斷、不確定性和數值數據等，都建模在一集成信度的結構以作證據推理和決策。 目前使用ER解決複雜的MCDM問題仍然受到限制，但具有提升的空間。首先，判斷不確定性時，有時需要同時使用信任和懷疑結構來進行建模，而現有的ER模型只考慮信任度。第二，ER處理缺失數據時，只當他們是徹底無知，沒有適當的方法來解決，這就受到很大的不確定性影響，增加了所作決定的風險。第三，ER不能確定權重的標準，只能假定他們是已知或已被指定。第四，ER需要把數值數據轉換為對定量決策標準的信任度的結構，這需要額外的計算工作，目前並沒有方法直接或簡化這步驟。第五，複雜的MCDM問題可能偶爾含有有序數據，ER目前不能理想地處理有序數據的建模。最後，現有的ER評估不同的決策方案時，需要在每個評估等級的標準或數據是已知或指定，這些標準和數據通常是較主觀的釐定。 組織創新管理（OIM）的評估是一個典型的複雜的多準則決策問題與定量和定性考核標準。 OIM需要大量的主觀判斷，從決策者或專家作出判斷，不可避免地涉及到各種不確定性因素，如不完全判斷，單純無知，主觀等等。因此，OIM的評估往往包含很多的不確定性。 本項目擬解決上述ER的限制，改進現有的ER方法以致能更理性的、可靠的和靈活的處理各種不確定性的判斷，從而建立一個有效的OIM評估制度。首先提出一個新的綜合ER方法可同時使用信度和不信任度結構，和一種新方法處理和確定缺失的數據。建議一種新方法去決定評估準則的權重，和提出一種分析算法集成信度和不信任度合的數值數據，而不需要繁瑣的數據轉換，也包括對有序數據建模的研究。建議的新的ER方法，模型和算法可應用於開發OIM評估制度與審定。項目成果可以促進香港的創新事業發展。

112111.label: Major findings and research outcome
112111.value: Attribute weights are proportional to the incompatibility among attributes, consisting of the deviation incompatibility and the decision incompatibility, and the optimization model of determining attribute weights is set Missing attributes are handled by solving the optimization model for determining attribute weights. Subjective constraints about attribute weights can be incorporated into the optimization model for determining attribute weights. Interval-valued utilities of assessment grades are considered when confirming whether an alternative can be the best alternative and determining intervals of attribute weights to guarantee a specified best alternative. Details of the outcomes were reported in Paper 8(1) BRB structures could be divided into three categories, namely (i) the incomplete structure which is associated with too many rules, the second category; (ii) the over-complete which is related to too few rules; and (iii) the complete that contrasts to the former two structures. Note that the complete structure can guarantee BRB system is capable of providing excellent inferential performance. To illustrate the correctness of the classification, we proved that the number of rules in the complete structure is always lower bounded and upper bounded. Hence, the number of rules in the complete structure is not a specific value. Instead, its number of rules is essentially an interval. To adjust a BRB achieving the complete structure, the current study analyzes a large quantity of the trained BRB system and summarizes several BRB features that is equipped with the incomplete structure or the over-complete structure. Based on these features, this paper proposes a dynamic rule adjustment approach, including mainly density analysis and error analysis, to construct the complete structure of a BRB. Notably, density analysis is used to prune the belief rules and error analysis is used to add the belief rules with the complete strategy, especially the process of new belief rule addition take the situation of multiple antecedent attributes into consideration. Both are the important components of the dynamic rule adjustment approach. (Paper 8(5)) In addition, a robust evidential reasoning approach was proposed to solve uncertain MADM problems without knowing attribute weights (Paper8(3)); A weighted cautious conjunctive rule (WCCR) was proposed for considering relative weights of belief functions (Paper 8(2)); An integrated evidential reasoning (IER) approach was developed to solve uncertain MADM problems in the presence of complete or incomplete cardinal and ordinal preferences (Paper 8(4)); and a case study of user satisfaction evaluation with the ER methodology was done (Paper 8(6).

112111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
112111.value: The Evidential Reasoning (ER) approach, combining conjunctively multiple pieces of independent evidence with various weights and reliabilities, could be applied in a wide range of decision-making problems under uncertainty, multiple criteria decision analysis, risk analysis, information fusion, medical diagnosis, and fault diagnosis. Under the ER framework for conjunctive combination of independent evidence, the results generated from this project could benefit the probabilistic inference process to determine generalised likelihood inference in order to deal with inaccuracy and ambiguity inherent in sample data and possibly incurred in an evidence acquisition process. Similar development is being developed by Yang J B in fault diagnosis for railway track maintenance management, while the PI’s research group in CityUHK is exploring the ER based forecasting methodology in healthcare services with evidence acquired from sample data. The developed OIM assessment framework as well as a proposed implementation plan has been formulated and being proposed to solicit Hong Kong Government funding (ITC General Support Fund)for a pilot run in Hong Kong high-technology industry in order to enhance the organizational innovation management capability of the in Hong Kong companies.

112111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
112111.value: This project studied a new integrated ER methodology for complex MCDA (multi-criteria decision analysis) using both belief and disbelief structures. An approach for determining the missing data is proposed. Methods for assessing the weights of decision criteria from decision data are suggested. Analytical algorithms for aggregating belief and disbelief structures and numerical data without the need for data transformation are derived. Procedures for modeling ordinal data under the framework of D-S theory of evidence are investigated. The proposed new ER approaches, models, and algorithms have been studied in developing an OIM (organizational innovation management) assessment system. The project results contribute to the applications in MCDA and OIM areas.

112611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
112611.value: Advancements of powerful sources and detectors in the terahertz frequency range, between 300GHz to 3 THz, has allowed access to this previously uncharted region, known as the THz Gap. The terahertz band which contains rich radiation energy from thermal emission of light-weight molecules has long been of interest to molecular and astro-physicists. Recent terahertz research has revealed techniques and results that opened up many new applications in molecular spectroscopy, imaging, detection and sensing of chemical and biological materials. In turn, the potential of these applications has generated interests from many industries ranging from security to health science. The research effort proposed here is to develop and demonstrate a CMOS compatible platform technology for the fabrication of terahertz integrated circuit (TIC) and sub-system. The TIC platform will allow the integration of both dielectric and metallic waveguide components on the same substrate and consists of a toolkit of standard building block structures that allows rapid design and prototyping. This approach provides both design flexibility and allows the miniaturization of these circuits for potential mass production. The proposed research plan is focused on building the foundation of this technology in both design and fabrication to support future research and innovation of advanced systems. 300GHz的到3赫茲之間，強大的源和探測器在太赫茲頻率範圍的進步，已獲准進入這個以前未知的區域，被稱為赫茲峽的。其中含有豐富的熱發射重量輕分子的輻射能量太赫茲波段一直感興趣的分子和天體物理學家。最近太赫茲研究發現，開闢了許多新的應用，在分子光譜，成像，檢測，化學和生物材料的傳感技術和結果。反過來，這些應用的潛力，產生了許多行業，從安全健康科學的利益。這裡提出的研究工作是一個太赫茲集成電路製造（議會）和亞系統的CMOS兼容的平台技術開發和示範。議會平台將允許同一基板上的電介質和金屬波導元件的集成，並包括一個標準的構建塊結構的工具，允許快速設計和原型。這種方法提供了設計靈活性，並允許這些電路潛在的大批量生產的小型化。集中建設在設計和製造先進的系統，以支持未來的研究和創新的這項技術的基礎上提出的研究計劃。

112611.label: Realisation of objectives
112611.value: The main objective of this project is to develop a dielectric platform for the fabrication of guided wave devices from the traditional metal based structures which demand increasing precision in the THz regime. In the process of carrying out this research it has come to the realization that a CMOS compatible platform to fabricate dielectric THz devices, such as in silicon-on-insulator adds significant cost to the final products making such platforms less attractive than a low cost platform. A platform that is suitable for mass production has tremendous advantages in view of the current cost of simple THz and sub-mm wave waveguide components. The project then focused on the investigation and to develop such a low cost platform instead. We like to report that we have successfully achieved our main objective and developed and demonstrated such a low cost platform. The demonstrated THz and Sub-mm wave platform is based on the commercially available injection-molding process where the waveguide components are fabricated with thermoplastics. The state-of-the-art injection-molding techniques can now produce plastic parts having critical dimension to within a few tens of microns, which is suitable for applications in the lower parts of the THz frequency band. Dielectric waveguides were designed, fabricated and measured showing propagation loss of approximate 0.3 dB/cm in the range of 140 GHz to 220 GHz. This shows that the platform is suitable for the fabrication of simple components such as power splitters, couplers and adaptor. In view of the commercial potential of the proposed platform technology, a patent on the above invention ‘waveguide’ (Part C.11) has been filed to protect the developed intellectual properties, which also serves as evidence on the completion of our first objective. To be compatible with the conventional microwave apparatus, the developed plastic waveguide structures must be able to couple effectively with the metallic waveguide applicators. We have designed and fabricated plastic power adaptor that demonstrate broadband and low-loss energy transfer between metallic and dielectric waveguides, with as low as 1 dB per transition. An US provisional patent on this invention ‘waveguide coupler’ (Part C.11) was also filed. We have also investigated and demonstrated functional devices such as power dividers that are suitable for sub-mm wave application and is preparing the manuscript ‘Design and Fabrication of Broadband Y-Junction Power Splitters for Sub-Millimeter Wave Application’ for publication (Part C 8.1). The prepared manuscript along with the filed patent fulfilled the final two objectives.

112611.label: Major findings and research outcome
112611.value: The absorption coefficients of common thermoplastics such as polyethylene and polypropylene decrease with frequency in the THz band and can be kept to below 0.2 per cm at frequency below 300 GHz. This makes them ideal candidates as material for making dielectric waveguides. Using the commercial injection molding method, dielectric waveguides with propagation loss of approximately 0.3 dB/cm in the sub-millimeter range of 140GHz to 220GHz. This finding was reported in C.9.1. To build a platform technology, the devices result from the new platform must be compatible with the existing system. With the modal structures of the conventional metal waveguides and the new plastics dielectric waveguides being so different, power adaptors are needed to transfer the power smoothly between the conventional metal waveguide and the dielectric waveguide. By properly designed a adiabatic structure having a probe that can slowly evolve the mode in the metal waveguide to the dielectric waveguide mode, we have demonstrated low loss transition of below 1 dB per transition between the rectangular metal waveguide mode to circular dielectric wave mode and we have reported this result in C.9.2. We also fabricated building block structures such as power dividers based on the Y-junction design as a proof of concept for the developed plastic dielectric waveguide platform for sub-millimeter/THz applications. The device shows ideal 3dB splitting of the input power with reasonable loss performance. The report is in preparation and attached in C.8.1. In summary, we have developed a new platform for the fabrication of sub-millimeter/THz waveguide devices. Specially designed power adaptors were developed to allow the new device to be compatible with the conventional system. With the new platform, we have also demonstrated functional devices that are common in the sub-millimeter/THz wave applications.

112611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
112611.value: We have proposed and carried out a feasibility study of an alternative platform for the fabrication of sub-millimeter wave devices. These devices have a substantially cost advantage over existing components and from the initial evaluation, some of these devices show that they have comparative performance as the conventional counterparts. Further development of the research will be carried out in two paths: 1) In the research front, focus will be placed on the continuation of expanding the capabilities of the developed platform. For example, complex materials such as plastic embedded with nanoparticles will be used to enhance the capability of these devices. 2) In view of the commercial potential of the developed technology, we are actively soliciting partner from the industries to work toward commercializing components such as power dividers and waveguides for sub-millimeter wave applications which we believe can find a niche in the overall wireless communication market.

112611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
112611.value: As application such as wireless communication moves into the millimeter and sub-millimeter regime, between 30 GHz to 300 GHz, metallic waveguide circuits will need to be scaled smaller and smaller to satisfy the associate operation conditions. As this size reduction requirement becomes more severe, it creates a major challenge in the fabrication of small dimension metallic waveguides using conventional milling method. Subsequently, the cost of even the simplest components such as waveguides, power dividers and couplers, becomes very expensive. In this project, we have proposed and successfully demonstrated a platform technology for the fabrication of low cost sub-millimeter waveguide components with comparable performance with conventional devices but at a substantial lower cost. Our proposed platform technology uses plastics instead of the more expansive and difficult to fabricate metal structures. Well established industrial injection-molding technique is used to fabricate the proposed devices making them mass producible and economical. Specially designed power adaptors were developed to provide smooth power transition between the plastics structure and the conventional metallic applicators to make them compatible with the conventional apparatus. We have also demonstrated functional devices such as power divider and couplers having encouraging performance showing that the commercial potential of the developed platform.

112711.value: 在当今世界对环境保护日渐关切的趋势下，寻求新型可再生能源，以及改进电力系统质量的技术成为一种迫切的需求。其研究趋势之一，即为将现有的基于大型发电厂的电网结构，向由靠近用电侧的分布式小型发电机构成的微电网结构转变。该结构的优势在于可以优化设施的利用率，改进电能质量，以及系统的可靠性，柔性和容量。 无论在何种可再生能源的技术条件下，用于与电网连接从而将能量从发电设施输入电网的逆变器都是整个系统的核心部件之一。该逆变器的功率转换部分一般由高频开关电路以及输出滤波器构成。其中开关电路将输入的直流功率转换为高频的交流功率，输出滤波器则用于滤除功率中的高频谐波，而允许电网频率的功率通过。在减小滤波器重量和体积设计，以及改进控制策略以满足稳态和动态功率要求方面，人们进行了大量的研究 在原理上讲，当输出滤波器的阶数增加时，其整体的体积可以相应的减小。因此采用高阶滤波器来提高逆变器的功率密度，能量效率，以及动态响应是一项具有吸引力的策略。然而，高阶滤波器会具有多个不同的谐振频率，从而会引发输出震荡，现有的应对措施主要为在功率变换环节采用被动的阻尼器，或者在控制环节采用主动的阻尼技术，但是他们都会带来更多的功率损耗并限制系统的动态特性。因此，该领域的主要研究依然着眼于使用低阶的滤波器。 本项目将通过对逆变器控制技术的研究，从而为与电网连接的具有高阶输出滤波器的逆变器应用提供技术上的突破。研究将提供一种通过利用输出滤波器固有功率传输特性和谐振特性，从而实现有功功率和无功功率的独立控制，以及输出谐振控制的新型逆变器控制策略。该技术将使逆变器不受传输线阻抗影响地调整输入电网的功率以及端口电压。同时该技术也将使逆变器能够在微电网与主电网并网或分离的瞬间立即响应，从而无缝的适应本微电网的用电需求。

Full mathematical analyses on the systems have been conducted. The inverters have been applied to a modular and scalable series compensation technique for enhancing controllability and flexibility in power transmission in distributed power systems. Detailed description on the major findings and research outcomes can be found in Section 6.

112711.label: Major findings and research outcome
112711.value: The power stage of an inverter is composed of three main parts, including the switching network, controller, and filter. Semiconductor switches are basic units in the switching network. a comprehensive study on the influences of parasitic elements on the MOSFET switching performance. A circuit-level analytical model that takes MOSFET parasitic capacitances and inductances, circuit stray inductances, and reverse current of the freewheeling diode into consideration is given to evaluate the MOSFET switching characteristics. The equations derived for emulating MOSFET switching transients are assessed graphically, which, compared to results obtained merely from simulation or parametric study, can offer better insight into where the changes in switching performance lie when the parasitic elements are varied. The results have been disseminated in [J1] and [C2]. A new gate drive has been proposed in [C9]. The inverters have been applied to a modular and scalable series compensation technique for enhancing controllability and flexibility in power transmission in distributed power systems is proposed. The concept is based on paralleling multiple static synchronous series compensators (SSSC), which are constructed by inverters, through daisy-chained transformers to perform reactive power compensation, and thus control the amount and direction of the power flow over the transmission link. The results have been disseminated in [J2], [C1], [C3], [C6], and [C11]. Based on current sharing technique presented in [J2], the current sharing technique has been applied to a lighting application in [J3], [C5], and [C8]. The performance of inverters with high-order filters and damping techniques has been studied. The grid-injected current harmonics and the conducted EMI noise are investigated for the conventional LCL-filter-based system. Based on this, a modified LCL-filter topology using an extra parallel LrCr resonant circuit is proposed in [J4], [C4], [C7], and [C10] to reduce the total inductance value, without increasing the capacitive reactive power. Then, the relationship between the maximum gain of the controller that still keeps the system stable and the Q-factor for a grid-tied inverter with an RL series or an RC parallel damped high-order power filter is investigated. Then, a robust passive damping method for LLCL-filter-based grid-tied inverters is proposed in [J5], which effectively can suppress the possible resonances even if the grid inductance varies in a wide range. A modified LLCL-filter with reduced conducted EMI noise is proposed in [J6]. Finally, a new perspective of using boundary control with second-order switching surface to reduce the order of the plant viewed by the deadbeat controller is given in [J7], [C12], and [C13]. The structure hybridizes the merits of the deadbeat control in its simplicity and the boundary control in achieving wide control bandwidth.

112711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
112711.value: In order to offer a high degree of modularity, scalability, adaptability, maintainability, and autonomic behavior, it is more advantageous to use multiple low-power parallel-connected inverters than a single high-power inverter unit. In many applications, such as small-scale wind farms and wave generator systems, those low-power inverters are connected together through long cables. Due to possible mismatch among the output impedances of the inverters, cable characteristic impedance, load characteristics, and grid impedance, the entire system could be dynamically unstable. Furthermore, high-order output filters exhibit multiple resonant frequencies that would cause output oscillation. An existing remedial measure to alleviate this problem is to apply a passive damper in the power stage or an active damping technique in the controller, but they would cause either extra power loss or limit the system dynamics. Thus, further research effort should be placed on studying 1) interactions among the inverters, cables, loads, and power grid, 2) predictive control algorithms for controlling active and reactive power flow, 3) an active damping technology at the point of common coupling, and 4) a fault diagnosis technique for DERs.

112711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
112711.value: In today’s environmentally-conscious world, there is an urgent need to find ways to improve the quality of electrical power system and explore new sustainable renewable power sources. Regardless of the type of renewable power source, the grid-connected inverter is a crucial component that converts the energy generated by the source to the grid. The power conversion stage of the inverter mainly consists of a high-frequency switching circuit and an output filter. In principle, the physical size of the output filter decreases with an increase in the system order. It is thus an attractive strategy to use a high-order filter to increase the power density, energy efficiency and dynamic response of the inverter. However, high-order filters exhibit multiple resonant frequencies that would cause output oscillation. This project aims at enabling a breakthrough in grid-connected inverter technology by the research of the methods for controlling inverters with high-order output filters, allowing the inverter to regulate power flow to the grid and the voltage at the interface independent of the value of the transmission line impedance, and picking up appropriate share of load in a rapid and seamless fashion.

112911.label: Project Title(Chinese)
112911.value: 砂土和風化土的“過渡性”土体行爲

112911.label: Project Objectives
112911.value: To establish how the behaviour of sands of various mineralogies evolves as the particle size distribution changes from poorly to well graded. To understand the types and roles of particle damage that occur for each grading. To investigate which element(s) of the soil fabric are responsible for the differences in void ratio at similar stress states when transitional behaviour is seen. To establish whether transitional behaviour can occur in decomposed granite and volcanic soils and how this affects their potential for static liquefaction.

112911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
112911.value: Over the past five decades, critical state models of soil behaviour have been developed which link a soil’s strength directly to the combination of its current volumetric state and the stresses it is experiencing. The initial volume of the soil at deposition and fabric of the soil might affect the stress-strain behaviour but not the ultimate strength. These models were initially developed largely for clay soils, but during the 1980s and 1990s were adapted for sands with modifications that account for the breakage that sand particles can undergo when loaded. There was perhaps a tendency to assume that since both sands and clays generally followed critical state modes of behaviour, soils with intermediate gradings might too. However, more recently a class of soil behaviour has emerged that is termed “transitional” which seems to apply to many intermediate graded soils. Transitional soils have strengths that are not uniquely defined by the current stress and volume state, but which are also controlled by the initial volume at deposition. While it was initially believed that this type of behaviour applied to more complex soils of mixed mineralogy it has now been observed in simple one-dimensional compression tests on well graded sands of single mineralogy. The proposed project seeks to investigate this important phenomenon in greater depth by using triaxial tests to separate out the effects of shearing and compression, so defining for the first time a complete framework for the behaviour of these soils. The micro-mechanical mechanisms responsible for this behaviour will also be examined through an analysis of the damage that the particles undergo, investigating how this changes as the type of soil behaviour evolves from a “sand” mode for uniform sand to a “transitional” mode for well graded sands. Based on the emerging literature on transitional soils, engineers of AECOM and the Hong Kong Geotechnical Engineering Office have made a preliminary analysis that has revealed that in some Hong Kong Decomposed Granite soils there may be transitional behaviour. If so, this would have a significant impact on their potential for static liquefaction and therefore on slope stability. The second main objective of the project will therefore be to examine in detail under what conditions these soils might show this newly identified form of behaviour and how that would affect their susceptibility to static liquefaction. 摘要 過去五十年來，土力學發展出了一系列臨界狀態模型。這些模型直接把土体強度與它當前的應力和體積狀態聯係起來。土体在沉積狀態時的初始體積和組織結構可能會影響土体的應力-應變行爲，但不會影響最終強度。這些模型最初主要是為粘土建立的，但是在1980~1990年間被修改成砂土模型，考慮了砂土加載時的顆粒破碎。也許有可能認爲，既然砂土和粘土普遍都符合臨界狀態模型，那麽具有中間顆粒級配的土体也應該符合。然而，最近發現了一種被稱做“過渡性”的土体行爲。這種行爲與許多具有中間顆粒級配的土体有關。過渡性土体的強度不僅僅由當前的應力和體積狀態決定，也受到沉積狀態時初始體積的影響。原本認爲這種行爲是比較複雜的混合礦物質土才具有的，現在已經在良好級配的單一礦物質土的一維壓縮試驗中也觀察到了。本項目試圖採用三軸試驗更加深入地研究這種重要的行爲，將剪切和壓縮的作用區分出來，從而率先為這類土体的行爲定義一個完整的框架。同時，通過對顆粒破碎進行分析，研究這種行爲的微觀力學機理，以及當砂土行爲類型從單一粒徑的砂土行爲轉變到良好級配時的過渡性行爲，這種微觀力學機理如何變化。 基於現有的過渡性土体的文獻，AECOM和香港岩土工程署的工程師們作出初步分析，發現香港的某些風化花崗岩土可能具有過渡性行爲。如果是這樣，這將對土体出現靜態液化的可能性以及隨之而來的邊坡穩定性具有顯著影響。因此，本項目的第二個目的是要仔細分析在何種條件下這些土体可能出現這種新發現的行爲模式，以及這種行爲如何影響土体對靜態液化的敏感性。

112911.label: Realisation of objectives
112911.value: The project was very successful in achieving all the original objectives, with only the usual slight shifts of emphasis in response to the developing data. It may be fairly stated that all the objectives were 100% achieved. These objectives did however require an enormous amount of high quality testing to be carried out and a total of about 180 triaxial tests and over 200 oedometer tests were conducted on the various soils, training two PhDs and providing final year projects for eight undergraduates. This is a remarkable total given that the quality of the triaxial tests required test durations of up to several weeks. Publication of much of the project is complete, with papers in leading journals, and there only remains two final papers to be written now the last PhD is complete and examined. The project addressed the “transitional” behaviour of soils, particularly clastic soils (i.e. sands). These are soils that have normal compression and critical state line locations that are dependent on their initial specific volumes when they are created. Early in the project it was found that in contrast to earlier work by the PI, many soils actually have compression paths and critical state lines that are not simply parallel for different initial volumes, but actually converge very slowly, and that the convergence is often so slow that it only occurs at 100s of MPa when the soil state approaches the zero voids asymptote, leaving no space to define a usable normal compression or critical state line in the void ratio : log mean stress plane. This therefore broadened the meaning of “transitional” to include soils that are slowly convergent. It was also confirmed at an early stage that there was no detectable particle damage in such soils, so emphasis shifted slightly from quantifying that damage towards quantifying rates of convergence, this being a necessary step towards making a modification of the critical state model to accommodate such soils. The research concentrated on six main soil types; a biogenic carbonate sand from the Philippines, a crushed limestone, Leighton Buzzard quartz sand, Hong Kong decomposed granites and volcanics and clastic sediments from the Venice lagoon, along with a small number of tests on a sand with a smaller proportion of fines, which had been used extensively in previous research by the PI. The opportunity to test and analyse data for the Venice lagoon sediments arose early in the project and was in collaboration with the University of Brescia, Italy. The soils were especially interesting and of practical engineering interest as they were from the sites of two of the gates on the inlets to the lagoon being built for the MOSES project. This part of the project led to innovative ways being proposed to quantify rates of convergence in shear and compression for both reconstituted and intact soil specimens that were applied to both the Venice soils and artificial sand-fine mixtures (Ponzoni et al., 2014, Géotechnique; Shipton & Coop, 2015; Géotechnique). Plastic volumetric strains were found to be more effective than plastic shear strains in bringing about convergence of void ratios. A key objective of the project was to identify to what extent local soils in Hong Kong might undergo transitional behaviour, since their well graded nature that results from their origin through weathering would suggest that they should do. A very extensive series of tests was therefore carried out on the Hong Kong Completely and Highly Decomposed Granites (CDG and HDG) along with a smaller number of tests on the corresponding Volcanics (CDV and HDV). Transitional behaviour would mean that liquefaction prediction would be problematic and also that it would be difficult to understand to what extent the behaviour of the soil in situ resulted from its intrinsic properties and to what extent from its natural structure, because there would be no unique intrinsic properties. The research found that for all the weathering grades the CDG/HDG and CDV/HDV are rarely transitional in behaviour and that the behaviour is dominated by a sand mode of mechanics with substantial amounts of particle breakage associated with the plastic volumetric strains, despite their being well graded. The effect of intact structure may therefore be quantified with conventional means (Rocchi Thesis; Rocchi & Coop, 2015, Géotechnique; Rocchi & Coop, 2016, Bulletin of Engineering Geology and the Environment and three conference papers). A major difficulty in research on transitional soils is establishing that non-convergence of void ratios during compression and/or shearing is actually due to an intrinsic soil behaviour and not simply inaccuracies in the measurement of the void ratios. Another early goal of the project was therefore to establish techniques for establishing and guaranteeing the accuracy void ratio measurements (Rocchi & Coop, 2014; Geotechnical Testing Journal). The project then moved on to examining convergence in very well graded sands, concentrating on the Leighton Buzzard sand and crushed limestone because early work showed that the Philippines biogenic sand was more rapidly convergent than the others. This work required an enormous amount of testing but has led to very innovative methods of quantifying rates of convergence that should lead to robust modifications to the critical state framework. In conjunction with quantifying convergence rates the fabric responsible for slow convergence or transitional behaviour has been identified in several of the soils. This part of the work has been done with the collaboration of the Ecole des Ponts, Paris. Mercury Intrusion Porosimetry combined with triaxial tests using multi-directional bender elements identified that the fabrics are not anisotropic but are heterogeneous, with differences of pore size distribution that persist even at very large volumetric and shear strains. This part of the work was completed in the thesis of Todisco, which was recently examined and papers from it are currently in preparation. The project has led to a large amount of interest internationally and apart from the collaborations with the Ecole des Ponts, Paris and the University of Brescia, Italy, mentioned above, other collaborative work on this topic is currently in progress for Chinese loess soils with Dr. Xu Ling of the China University of Geoscience, Beijing, and for rockfill with Dr. Xiao Yang of Chongqing University.
