112911.label: Major findings and research outcome
112911.value: The project has identified that there is a variety of different behaviours of soils within those that might be referred to as “transitional”, from those soils where the compression paths and critical state behaviour remains robust and linked to the initial void ratio of the soil to those where convergence of void ratio occurs at large strains. For many sands which are very well graded convergence of void ratios during either compression or shearing in typical laboratory tests can occur so slowly that unique lines are only approached at stresses well outside the engineering range of 100s of MPa, and at void ratios approaching zero, so that it becomes impossible to define a unique and usable critical state model. For such soils the quantification of the rates of convergence then becomes a cornerstone to formulate modifications to critical state models of behaviour and new methods of quantifying the convergence in shearing and compression have been proposed (Ponzoni et al., 2014, Géotechnique; Shipton & Coop, 2015; Géotechnique). Of key importance when quantifying transitional behaviour is to establish the accuracy of the void ratios measured so that non-convergence through inaccuracy can be eliminated (Rocchi & Coop, 2014; Geotechnical Testing Journal). In transitional soils the particle damage that is associated with the behaviour of more poorly graded sands and causes convergence of volumes is absent. The soil fabric that causes this non-convergent or slowly convergent behaviour has been shown with bender element and Mercury Intrusion Porosimitry tests to be a heterogeneous but isotropic fabric that is only broken down by extremely large volumetric and/or shear strains. Tests on Hong Kong decomposed granite and decomposed volcanic soils showed that they are rarely transitional and each soil generally has unique normal compression and critical state lines that depend on their degree of weathering. Despite their very well graded nature their mode of behaviour is therefore more similar to more poorly graded sands with behaviour dominated by particle breakage (Rocchi & Coop, 2015, Géotechnique; Rocchi & Coop, 2016, Bulletin of Engineering Geology and the Environment).

112911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
112911.value: The key next step in this research direction will be the reformulation of the critical state soil mechanics framework to account for the wide variety of natural soils that are well graded and have varying degrees of transitional behaviour. This will involve building into the framework some measure of the effect of plastic volumetric and shear strains in disrupting the initial fabric and bringing about convergence to unique void ratios for one stress level. The “destructuration” model that has been derived here for transitional soils will also have applications in defining the breakdown of structure of natural intact soils.

112911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
112911.value: A key tenet of current soil mechanics is that if a soil undergoes sufficient compression or shearing it will reach a unique volume for a give stress, no matter what its starting volume. A large range of very well graded soils with a wide mixture of coarse to fine particles have been found not to follow this framework and the convergence towards unique volumes is so slow that it only occurs beyond the range of stresses and deformations that are relevant to civil engineering. The project has shown how these slow convergences may be quantified and that the arrangement of particles within the soil that causes it is one that is heterogeneous but not one with a preferential orientation. The project also found that despite their well graded nature the common Hong Kong soils, decomposed granites and decomposed volcanics, do not show significant transitional behaviour.

113311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
113311.value: Networked control systems (NCSs) are spatially distributed systems in which plants to be controlled, sensors, actuators, and controllers, are remotely positioned and communicate with each other through shared band-limited digital communication networks. Compared with traditional point-to-point control systems, the main advantages of network structured control systems come from their low cost, flexibility and easy re-configurability, natural reliability and robustness to failure, and adaptation capability. Consequently, NCSs have been finding applications in a broad range of areas such as transportation networks, power grids, mobile sensor networks, water distribution networks, unmanned aerial vehicles and so on. However, there are also some drawbacks caused by the very nature of communication networks such as transmission delays, packet dropouts, data quantization errors, data rate constraints, etc. Currently engineers, control engineers in particular, have to deal with many network-induced new and challenging issues arising from analysis and synthesis of complex networked control systems. During the past few years, increasing attention has been paid to the study of networked control systems in terms of stability analysis, controller synthesis, state estimation, and performance optimization under various network-induced constraints. However, analysis and synthesis of networked control systems are still in the early stage of development and many critical issues remain to be further investigated. This project will investigate and develop novel approaches to analysis and synthesis of networked control systems with these network-induced constraints. The outcome of this project is expected to enrich theoretical foundation on analysis and synthesis of networked control systems, and, in turn, the proposed approaches will provide control engineers in practice with more and/or better analysis and controller design tools. 网络化控制系统是一类空间分布式系统，其中系统的被控对象、传感器、执行器以及控制器之间通过一个带宽有限的网络互相定位和通讯。和传统的点对点控制系统相比，网络化控制系统的主要优点体现在其能耗低、配置灵活、可靠性高、并对故障具有很好的鲁棒性等。因此，网络化控制系统在很多领域都得到了很好的应用，比如交通调度系统、电力系统、移动传感器网络、供水网络、无人驾驶机系统等。但是，由于通讯网络本身的特性，网络化系统也有一些其固有的问题存在，比如系统会有信号传输时滞，数据丢包，量化误差、数据率限制等。目前，工程师们，特别是系统控制工程师们，在分析和设计网络化系统时不得不考虑因为网络引起的这些新的富有挑战性的问题。过去几年来，网络化控制系统吸引了越来越多的关注，比如系统的稳定性分析、控制器设计、状态估计、以及在各种条件限制下的性能优化等等。但是，到目前为止，网络化系统的分析与综合还处于一个发展和研究的初级阶段，很多关键性的问题仍然亟待解决。本项目将会研究并提出一些新的方法来分析和综合在各种条件受限情景下的网络化控制系统。这个项目的研究成果将进一步丰富和完善网络化系统的理论基础，并为系统控制工程师们提供更多更好的分析设计工具。

113311.label: Major findings and research outcome
113311.value: We have first investigated the issues of networked control systems with isolated network-induced delays, packet dropouts, quantization, and data rate constraints respectively. We have then investigated the issues of networked control systems with co-existenace of some of those network-induced limitations. A number of novel and less conservative approaches to analysis and synthesis of networked control systems with various networked-induced limitations have been developed. One of key findings of the project is that it is desirable and also critical to fully exploit the properties of the communication network to achieve less conservative results in analysis and synthesis of networked control systems. One effective way to reduce the design conservatism and improve the overall system performance is to co-design the control strategy and communication network. The proposed approaches have been applied to a number of typical networked control systems and the simulation results have demonstrated their advantages over the existing approaches.

113311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
113311.value: Although a number of approcahes have been developed for design of networked control systems with simultaneous consideration of various networked-induced limitations, the issue on how to optimize the performance of such networked control systems has not been addressed. This could be a potential research direction.

113311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
113311.value: Networked control systems (NCSs) have wide applications in a broad range of areas such as transportation networks, power grids, mobile sensor networks, water distribution networks, unmanned aerial vehicles and so on. However, there are also some drawbacks caused by the very nature of communication networks such as transmission delays, packet dropouts, data quantization errors, data rate constraints, etc. Currently engineers,control engineers in particular, have to deal with many network-induced new and challenging issues arising from analysis and synthesis of complex networked control systems. During the past few years, increasing attention has been paid to the study of networked control systems in terms of stability analysis, controller synthesis, state estimation, and performance optimization under various network-induced constraints. This project has investigated and developed novel and less conservative approaches to analysis and synthesis of networked control systems with these network-induced constraints. The outcome of this project is expected to enrich theoretical foundation on analysis and synthesis of networked control systems, and, in turn, the proposed approaches will provide control engineers in practice with more and/or better analysis and controller design tools.

114011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
114011.value: Total cooling load based chiller sequencing control has been developed to stage chillers on or off in multiple-chiller plants by matching the maximum cooling capacity provided by the chiller plants to building instantaneous cooling load. It optimizes the number of operating chillers to satisfy thermal comfort requirement and simultaneously achieve energy efficiency. This research will investigate uncertainties associated with this type of chiller sequencing control which significantly affect the control performance, and explore a systematic strategy to deal with those uncertainties. A laboratory test-rig will be set up and two types of uncertainties will be considered: measurement uncertainties associated with the cooling load estimation and model uncertainties associated with the online estimation of chiller maximum cooling capacity. Data fusion will be investigated and developed to reduce the measurement uncertainties. A model-based method will be employed to online estimate the chiller maximum cooling capacity; and uncertainties associated with the model will be evaluated using data collected from the test-rig. A method of online tuning the model parameters will be developed to reduce the model uncertainties. Decision making under uncertain information will be reviewed and a suitable approach will be developed for chiller staging operations. 114011.label: Realisation of objectives
114011.value: Objective 1: we systematically studied measurement uncertainty and its influences on chiller sequencing control, where the uncertainty was quantified using field data and available technical data and propagated using the Monte-Carlo simulation. A data fusion algorithm to reduce measurement noises and outliers and an algorithm of optimizing calibration frequency of sensors to reduce measurement biases were developed and validated. Objective 2: we carried out a literature review on existent methods of online estimation of chiller maximum cooling capacity, which reveals that there are very few publications on online estimation of chiller maximum cooling capacity. A grey-box model to estimate the maximum cooling capacity was therefore developed. To improve the model accuracy, a hybrid technique to improve measurement reliability in HVAC systems was developed. Simultaneously, as chiller capacity is highly related to building cooling load, we re-evaluated building load prediction models using a case building and Hong Kong weather condition. Objective 3: We carried out a literature review on existent decision making techniques under uncertain information as well as robust optimization techniques, which reveals that typical methods include fuzzy logic and stochastic programming. To improve the reliability of the decision making, two ways were considered. One was to improve the optimization strategy. We therefore developed a multiplexed optimization approach for complex AC system. Another one was to take uncertainties directly in decision making. We chosen stochastic programming and developed a stochastic control of chiller sequencing operation. Objective 4: To evaluate the performance of the stochastic chiller sequencing control, we carried out a uncertainty/robustness analysis of typical chiller sequencing control strategies. A simulation platform, which includes a six-story office building located in Hong Kong and a chiller plant of three identical chillers, was developed. Monte-Carlo simulation was performed to produce data. Comparing with a conventional method, the developed method can improve the reliability of chiller sequencing operation as well as its energy performance. Objective 5: We developed a computer program to realize the stochastic chiller sequencing control and software, which can select the best sequencing control strategy subject to various uncertainties.The software was developed using TRNSYS.

114011.label: Major findings and research outcome
114011.value: In commercial and office buildings, multiple-chiller plants are always equipped to provide cooling for occupied spaces. In a multiple-chiller plant, chiller sequencing control plays a key role in achieving overall energy efficiency. However, chiller sequencing control suffers from many uncertainties, which significantly deteriorates the performance of the control and energy performance [3]. This project aims to systematically investigate the influences of uncertainty on the performance of chiller sequencing control and develop methods to improve the robustness of chiller sequencing control. The main achievements are listed below: First, a simple method to analyze the influences of uncertainty on chiller sequencing control has been developed based on the technique of uncertainty shift [4]. Our studies show that chiller sequencing control suffers mainly from measurement uncertainty, control uncertainty, operational uncertainty and threshold uncertainty. All those uncertainties can be shifted to the load indicator of chiller sequencing control, and then the analysis can be focused only on the uncertainty associated with the load indicator. This significantly simplifies the uncertainty analysis. Based on this method, robustness of chiller sequencing control has been analyzed and a simple method to select the most robust sequencing control strategy under uncertainty has been developed and validated using field data [7]. Second, a preventive approach to reduce measurement uncertainty has been developed. This approach identifies the importance of the measurement variables to the system energy performance using standardized regression coefficients (SRCs), and then optimizes the calibration frequency of the sensors based on their importance [2]. Meanwhile, based on this preventive approach, a data fusion technique was adopted to improve measurement accuracy [6], and hence to reduce the influences of measurement uncertainty on the performance of the sequencing control. As chiller sequencing control is relative to building cooling load, typical building cooling load prediction models were evaluated under the weather condition of Hong Kong [1]. Third, a stochastic chiller sequencing control has been developed, which deals with uncertainty in both the load measurement side and the capacity supply side using stochastic programming [5, 8]. Algorithms to realize the stochastic control was tested using a computer simulation and field data. Compared with the traditional method, the developed method can improve the robustness and flexibility of chiller sequencing operation. (all the references are listed in Part C)

114011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
114011.value: Through this research, we realized that to improve the robustness of chiller sequencing operation is not easy. We currently focus on chiller plants with a typical configuration: the primary side, which uses constant speed pumps and has a constant flow, is bypassed using a bypass line with the secondary side, where variable speed pumps are always used. As more and more new chiller plants use variable speed pump in both the primary side and the secondary side, in which the bypass line is no longer needed, future development may consider how to improve the robustness of chiller sequencing operation of this type of chiller plants. To carry out this research, the methodology that should be adopted should be similar to the one that we developed in this project. Simulation platform needs to be built, field data need to be collected, and uncertainty analysis will be carried out for uncertainty quantification and propagation. Then, a simple approach will be developed to select the most suitable sequencing control strategy as what we have done in this project.

114011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
114011.value: Chiller plant represents the largest primary energy end-use in a central air-conditioning system. In typical commercial buildings, chiller plant accounts for 10–20% of the overall facilities usage. In the subtropical area like Hong Kong, this percentage climbs to about 40% of the total annual electricity expenditure. If the chillers are staged improperly, energy will be wasted (when the chillers staged on are more than necessary) and the indoor thermal comfort will be degraded (when the chillers staged on are less than necessary). This research investigated the factors that will cause the improper operation of chiller sequencing control, which is able to help HVAC engineers, researchers and operators to understand the reasons; and developed a method that can improve the robustness of chiller sequencing control, which will improve the energy efficiency of HVAC systems and the indoor thermal comfort.

114111.label: Project Objectives
114111.value: i. Development of a theoretical model with which to investigate the large-amplitude vibration of MLGSs. This model will be used to study the in-phase and anti-phase resonance characteristics of MLGSs of various sizes and number of layers. The resonant information obtained from the proposed theoretical model will be used as a guideline for the experimental work to measure the dynamic characterics of MLGSs of specific sizes and numbers of layers. An improved experimental process for measuring the vibration properties of MLGSs will be established to verify the theoretical predictions, which will be vital for completing the theoretical model. The experimental process will include the design and fabrication of an AFM probe for the accurate measurement of the frequency-response curve of MLGSs and the electrode patterns to oscillate the probe. Correlation of theoretical analysis and experimental measurements will finally yield a systematic theory for the static and dynamic responses of MLGSs. The anti-phase resonant response of MLGSs will be explored by using the developed theoretical model for the control of the number of layers in the mechanical exfoliation of MLGSs.

114111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
114111.value: The proposed project aims to develop a continuum mechanics model for the large-amplitude vibration of multi-layered graphene sheets (MLGSs) using a combination of theoretical and experimental investigations. The emphasis will be placed on the anti-phase large-amplitude vibration which has the potential of overcoming van der Waals (vdW) interaction between layers for the exfoliation of MLGSs. A nonlinear explicit expression will be derived for the vdW interaction between layers because the nonlinear term in the Taylor expansion of vdW force function cannot be ignored when the amplitude of vibration is large. Based on the vdW explicit formulation, a nonlinear stacked plate model will be established for the stack and dynamic responses of MLGSs. This theoretical model will be validated by a nanoscale experiment in which the excitation frequencies will be selected from the resonance frequencies of the theoretical predictions. The implementation of the proposed continuum method and the experimental process will be explored in this project for splitting apart MLGSs into few- or even single-layered graphene sheets. 本项目将建立一个连续的力学模型用于分析多层石墨烯的大挠度振动.重点分析多层石墨烯的反向共振,因为石墨烯的层与层之间的反向共振有助于克服层间的范德华力,从而能够剥离出单层的石墨烯.该课题将导出一个显示表达式用于模拟非线性的层间范德华力,该显示表达式是建立多层石墨烯的大挠度振动模型的关键.所建立的理论模型将用来探讨获得一定层数的石墨烯的新方法.

114111.label: Major findings and research outcome
114111.value: A nonlinear continuum model for analyzing forced vibration behaviors of MLGSs is developed on the basis of the derived nonlinear vdW interaction model and von kármán equation of motion of shells. The nonlinear forced vibration behavior of DLGS is investigated. From the nonlinear frequency–amplitude relationship of MLGSs subjected to external harmonic excitations, it can be found that the first and second layers of DLGSs vibrate in-phase and anti-phase, respectively, when they are excited in the neighborhood of different natural frequencies. Furthermore, the model is applicable to a larger number of layers of GSs also. The model presented here is expected to be helpful for analyzing nonlinear vibration behaviors of SLGS and MLGS nanomechanical resonators.

114111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
114111.value: The established theoretical framework could be extended to the multi-scale analysis of super carbon nanotubes or graphene sheets based on the combination of molecular dynamics (MD), cellular automata (CA) algorithm and continuum model established in this project. In the hierarchical super structure, the primary structure is the single walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT). The secondary structure is the super CNTs (SCNTs) fabricated from the primary structure. The tertiary structure can be the hierarchical super graphene (HSG) generated from the secondary structure. Through the synthesis of hierarchical super structure, the macroscale HSG can be fabricated from nanoscale CNTs. At the nanoscale, both primary CNTs and secondary SCNTs are treated as a discrete system in which the constitutive model can be developed by MD and CA algorithm based on many-body potential for CNTs. At the micron scale, since the solution framework of CA is based on the conventional continuum mechanics, it can also be used to develop a continuum constitutive model. With the linkage among MD (nanoscale), CA (nanoscale and micron scale) and continuum mechanics model developed in this project (micron scale and above), the multi-scale constitutive model can be developed to provide a comprehensive understanding of the system of HSG.

114111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
114111.value: Graphite's layered structure consists of graphene sheets bound by weak vdW forces. To overcome the vdW force between layers for mechanically exfoliating graphites through resonance characteristic, it is essential to have a comprehensive understanding of a large-amplitude vibration behavior of multilayered graphene sheets (MLGSs) and multiwalled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs). However, an efficient mechanics model for the analysis of the nonlinear vibration characteristic of MLGSs/MWCNTs is lacking, and this has motivated us to propose a project to develop an nonlinear computational model to study the large-amplitude vibration of MLGSs/MWCNTs. In addition, characterization of the dynamic response of MLGSs/MWCNTs is crucial for the design of graphene-based NEMS. The successful development of the computational model will help to study the graphene-based device design and the separation of an MLGS into individual single-layer sheets. This is the key towards achieving practical application of this new class of materials.

114411.value: 這項目研究發光二極管能達到可特續發展的關鍵要素，包括發光二極管系統的「光、熱和電」的互動關係，系統壽命限制的原因，涉及元件壽命、推動器設計和散熱功能。目的是認定相關的關鍵要素，以便研究解決方案。

114411.label: Realisation of objectives
114411.value: This project focuses on critical issues that prevent LED systems from being reliable and enjoying long lifetime. Several issues have been identified as: 1. High junction temperature 2. Current imbalance in parallel LED string 3. The use of electrolytic capacitors in the LED driver 4. Poor thermal design and the lack of a good system design tool. As a response to these critical issues, the project focuses on 4 aspects of research, namely 1. New technique for dynamic modeling and prediction of the internal junction temperature so that the condition of the LED junction can be monitored. This information can be used to check the health of the LED devices. 2. A system design tool which can keep the junction temperature low if necessary. 3. Study of a passive LED driver without using any electrolytic capacitors. 4. Study of a new current-mirror technique for reducing current imbalance in parallel LED strings. During the project period from 2011-2014, we have successfully developed a new technique for monitoring the internal junction temperature based on external measurements. This technique provides a new tool for design engineers to check the internal junction temperature of LED devices without using expensive equipment. We have also extended the photo-electro-thermal theory so that it has become a design tool for LED system designs. This allows design engineers to choose the heatsink designs so as to keep the junction temperature below a certain value for long lifetime and high luminous output. We have developed and filed a patent application on a passive LED driver for outdoor applications. It has no electrolytic capacitors, switching devices and auxiliary power supply. In addition, we have developed and filed a patent application on a re-configurable current-mirror circuit that can reduce current imbalance in parallel LED strings. In summary, we have achieved the objectives of the project. The research outputs include: 4 IEEE Transactions Papers 2 IEEE Conference Papers 2 Patent applications (both have been licensed to industry through CityU and HKU).

114411.label: Major findings and research outcome
114411.value: Although critical to the lifetime of LED, the junction temperature of LED cannot be measured easily. Based on the general photoelectrothermal theory for LED systems, we have successfully related the coefficient for the reduction of luminous efficacy with junction temperature to the characteristic temperature of the LED. Then, we developed a noncontact method for estimating the internal junction temperature Tj and junction-case thermal resistance Rjc of LED from the external power and luminous flux measurements. Since these external measurements can be obtained easily, the proposal provides a simple tool for checking Tj in new LED system designs without using expensive or sophisticated thermal monitoring equipment for the LED junctions. The proposed method has been checked with measurements on LED devices from three different brands with both constant and nonconstant Rjc . The theoretical predictions are found to be highly consistent with practical measurements. With the use of wall-plug efficiency, we have developed new estimation techniques for the optical power and heat-dissipation coefficient of LEDs to enrich the photoelectrothermal theory, which has provided a framework for analyzing LED systems. The estimation methods consist of simple procedures for optical and electrical power measurements, which are easy for LED device manufacturers and system designers to follow. The extended theory has been tested with several types of LED devices, with reasonably good agreements between theoretical and practical results. Traditional current-mirror methods require one fixed current reference for controlling other current source or sources. We invented a new self-configurable current-mirror method that can dynamically determine the best current branch as the current reference in order to ensure good balance of all parallel current sources. The operating principle involves a dynamic and self-configurable transistor-based current-balancing circuit that can be operated in saturation or linear mode. In either operating mode, good current balance or sharing among all parallel-connected current sources can be guaranteed. The novel current-balancing circuit does not require a separate power supply for powering their control circuits. The proposal is a modular one that can be expanded to any number of parallel current sources. Its principle has been successfully applied to current balancing of parallel LED strings. Based on recent works on the photoelectrothermal theory and its extensions, we published a comprehensive LED system theory with physical explanations for electronics engineers and researchers working in LED system designs, with the emphasis on general and public lighting applications. The physical meanings of essential parameters are explained. Practical test procedures for extracting parameters not readily available in data sheets are included. It is envisaged that this LED system theory will form the basic design guidelines for future LED system designs.

114411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
114411.value: Because of the successes arising from this GRF project, we have successfully obtained a Theme-based Research Project on Sustainable Lighting Technology: From Devices to Systems. While this GRF project touches upon the critical issues of LED systems, the Theme-based Project ($21.7 Million) involves detailed analysis and broader research, linking LED device structures, LED drivers and thermal designs. It also extends the photo-electro-thermal theory to cover chromaticity (color) of the LED systems. More new results are reported through the Theme-based Project reports.

114411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
114411.value: In this project, we have successfully identified some critical issues that affect the lifetime and reliability of LED systems. We have come up with new extended LED system theory to calculate the system parameters, find a non-contact approach in monitoring the internal junction temperature and design new LED drivers that enjoy high reliability and long lifetime. 114811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
114811.value: 鑒於質量較輕，鎂材在航空航天、汽車製造、計算機硬件及近年來發展迅速的生物可降解植入物等領域的應用前景極為可觀。在眾多已研製出的鍛壓鎂合金中，針對Mg-3Al-1Zn (AZ31)的研究在過去十年中最為廣泛。然而，與其它輕質合金相比，該種鎂合金仍存在些許限制，如抗蠕變強度、微型結構的不勻性以及強度水平等。此外，由於鎂合金可塑性低，加工及轉變鍛壓條件成為鎂材研製的一項重要挑戰，而鎂合金組織結構的差異性也使研究面臨更多挑戰。本研究計畫旨在開發加工高強度AZ31鎂基複合結構材料，以解決上述三個問題。首先，研究建議在AZ31合金中添加Ca，在金屬基材中形成如(Mg,Al)2Ca等穩定的金屬間顆粒，從而賦予合金良好的高溫抗蠕變強度。其次，納米氧化鋁顆粒彌散可裝飾並強化合金金屬粒子之原始界面，以獲得較佳之強度水平。在上述兩項工序中，Ca及納米氧化鋁的添加值極為關鍵，需找出既可提高合金的強度水平，而又不嚴重降低合金延展性的最佳條件。該種合金及複合材料可通過粉碎熔融沉積法（DMD）及熱擠壓技術加工而成。最後，運用動態材料模型，著重於控制微型結構和優化可塑性，可研究出此新型材料的完整加工技術，該技術可使材料在熱態環境下良好工作。因此，加工圖和動力學分析將分別應用於優化可塑性及評估熱態工作機制。熱壓測試將用於獲得必要的實驗數據，從而更好地應用此類鎂材。針對變形試樣的詳細微型結構測試則用於驗證實驗結果。本研究的成果，是合成一種含納米複合材料的新型高強度鎂合金，此種材料於生產環境中可重複地以熱加工製成具有穩定微型結構和機械性能的構件。此外，該鎂材在各種使用溫度下的機械性能也將逐一評估，以此與同類競爭材料的機械性能作出比較。

114811.label: Realisation of objectives
114811.value: The three major routes of processing magnesium alloys to obtain components for end usage are: (i) casting the alloys directly into final component shapes, (ii) casting the alloys into ingots or billets and convert them into products with wrought microstructure by imparting large scale deformation through hot working/forming methods, and (iii) use of powder metallurgy route by consolidating the elemental or alloys powder materials, sinter, and hot working to obtain wrought microstructure in the components. While the first processing route is relatively well established for processing a large number of metallic materials, the engineering properties obtainable through such methods are limited. It is the category of wrought materials, largely obtained through the second route involving hot working, makes up over 90% of metallic materials in day-to-day usage. The third processing route, though more expensive and involves hot working as the important end step, offers the advantage of producing components with tailored microstructures and the possibility of developing metal matrix composites, including the use of non-metallic materials. The current research project involves the third processing route for studying the hot working behaviour of the most popular magnesium alloy AZ31 alloy (Mg - 3 wt.% Al -1 wt% Zn) by incorporating small quantities of Ca and/or nano-Alumina (Al2O3). While the major benefit of adding Ca is to increase the strength and creep resistance of the alloy, ceramic nano-Alumina controls the grain growth so as to obtain wrought microstructure of fine grain size in the finished product that could significantly enhance the mechanical properties. The simultaneous addition of Ca and nano-Alumina is to find out their synergistic effect. The following studies have been taken up to accomplish the stated objectives of this project: (a) Study the hot working behavior of the base magnesium alloy AZ31 alloy from some of the works undertaken by the Principal Investigator (PI) as well as those from the literature and collaborators of PI. This would establish the base line for comparing the hot working behaviours of the new alloy compositions as well as the mechanical properties. It may be noted that hot working of magnesium alloys is extremely difficult due to their hexagonal crystal structure that offers very few slip planes for deforming an alloy. This also results in strong textures that further limit the deformation or plasticity in magnesium alloys. Therefore, an understanding of the texture development and its control strategies assume significance. (b) Producing the required starting alloys through powder metallurgy route by the External Investigator (EI), Dr. M. Gupta at the National University of Singapore (NUS). Initially, three compositions were produced under optimized processing conditions using Disintegrated Melt Deposition (DMD) technique followed by extrusion to obtain rods of about 10 mm in diameter. The developed alloys are: (i) AZ31, (ii) AZ31-1%Ca, (iii) AZ31-1% nano-Alumina, and (iv) AZ31-1%Ca-1% nano-Alumina. All of these alloys were successfully produced and all further investigations were carried out at the City University of Hong Kong. (c) From the extruded rods supplied by EI, specimens for carrying out the compression tests to study both the mechanical properties and hot working behaviours of the four alloy compositions were prepared. The mechanical properties were obtained in the application temperature range (25-200 oC) by conducting tests at a low test speed (translates to a strain rate of 0.001 s-1 or the so called static tests) and the tests at high temperatures (250-500 oC) were conducted at six different strain rates in the range 0.0003-10 s-1 that largely cover speeds adopted in metal forming processes. (d) The data obtained from the compression tests of the four alloy compositions was converted into flow curves (stress vs. strain variations) for all the six strain rates and six temperature combinations. After accounting for the continuous adiabatic temperature rise with deformation, relevant at the three high strain rates, the results were further analysed to address two important aspects related to the hot working of all four alloy compositions: (i) develop constitutive relationships and activation energies in different temperature - strain rate ranges, and (ii) develop processing maps on the basis of dynamic materials modeling technique. (e) From the results obtained from activation analysis and processing maps, the operative mechanisms over the entire ranges of temperature and strain rates have been determined so as to establish the domains of good workability and regimes of fracture/failure. These findings were corroborated with the help of microstructural investigations of all the tested specimens. In particular, the conditions leading to dynamic recrystallization (DRX), localized flow and fracture have been confirmed. Among these, DRX is a coveted phenomenon responsible for high workability and grain refinement leading to uniform and consistent microstructure and mechanical properties. Tension tests were also conducted at specific deformation conditions to further support the findings of processing maps of the three alloys. (f) The development of texture during hot working has been established by conducting electron back-scattered diffraction (EBSD) studies on the specimens deformed at several conditions for the alloys. Again, this study corroborated the domains of high workability for the alloys. The texture of alloys deformed within domains of high workability is weak, i.e. more isotropic, compared to other deformation conditions that result in stronger textures or anisotropy. These findings can be used to obtain desired mechanical properties with tailored microstructures. (g) The results obtained from the studies mentioned above have been compared directly with the corresponding cast alloys for two compositions, namely, AZ31 and AZ31-1%Ca in terms of hot workability and other properties. With the research studies mentioned above, we are able to largely accomplish the three target objectives of the project. We have also produced two more compositions AZ31 alloy with higher Ca contents of 2% and 3% through the powder metallurgy route at NUS. However, the alloy with 3% Ca has developed surface cracking during extrusion. It has been reported in the recent literature that high amounts of Ca and nano-Alumina do not offer any additional benefits in terms of mechanical properties. In the case of addition of nano-Alumina, EI has found that the optimal content is about 1.5%, and this amount was used in this study. The three set objectives have been achieved in this project. The major findings of this research are mentioned in the next section (6.1) and the publications arising from this project are listed in Part C. The support received from this GRF project was acknowledged in all the six papers published in journals and one paper in conference proceedings listed in Part C.

114811.label: Major findings and research outcome
114811.value: The influence of manufacturing route on the hot working and development of texture of the base alloy AZ31 in cast and wrought forms was studied, as mentioned in section 5.3(a), with results published in Metals (2012) (see Part C). The synthesis of the four selected alloy compositions was done by EI using powder processing route. First alloy studied was AZ31-1.5% nano-Alumina. Following the methods mentioned in section 5.3(b)-(d), the hot workability was determined through (i) kinetic analysis to estimate the activation energies for determining the deformation mechanisms, (ii) processing maps to reveal domains of good workability, (iii) EBSD analysis to understand the texture development under different hot working conditions. The findings were presented at ACEM’ 12 (2012). A comprehensive paper on this alloy was published in Materials Science and Engineering A (2014). The results obtained through similar analysis of hot workability for the other three alloy compositions and the findings were published in Materials Science and Engineering A (2013; AZ31 alloy), Materials Science and Engineering A (2015; AZ31-1wt% Ca alloy in both cast and power processing routes), and Materials and Manufacturing Processes (2015, AZ31-1wt% Ca-1.5% nano-Alumina). In addition, AZ31 alloy with higher Ca addition (2%) has been studied and the results are published in Materials & Design (2014). The important findings are: AZ31 alloy: The processing map exhibits 3 domains in the temperature and strain rate ranges (1) 250-350 oC/ 0.0003-0.01 s-1, (2) 350-500 oC/ 0.0003-0.01 s-1, and (3) 350-450 oC/ 1-10 s-1. The alloy may be hot worked safely in domains #1 and #3, and grain boundary sliding occurs in domain #2. While domain #3 is preferable for industrial processing in view of the higher strain rates, the product properties will be anisotropic in view of the texture. AZ31-1% Ca alloy: The processing map developed on DMD-processed alloy exhibited three domains, but the as-cast alloy has only two domains because of large grain size. The yield strength of the DMD alloy is more than double the strength of cast alloy up to 175 oC. AZ31-1.5% nano-Alumina alloy: The processing map exhibits three domains, but domain #3 has moved to lower temperatures by about 50 oC. These differences are attributed to the lower intensity of starting texture in the nano-composite compared with the base alloy. AZ31-1%Ca-1.5%nano-Alumina alloy: This alloy exhibited one extra domain and all of them offer workability, showing the synergistic effect of simultaneous addition of Ca and nano-Alumina.

114811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
114811.value: It is desirable to study the hot workability of slightly higher addition of Ca to understand its effect individually and in combination of nano-Alumina. The proposed compositions are: (i) AZ31-2%Ca, and (ii) AZ-2%Ca-1.5%nano-Alumina. We plan to study these two alloys for their mechanical properties and hot workability.

114811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
114811.value: Magnesium materials are increasingly sought for structural applications in aerospace, automobile, and more recently for bio-degradable implants due to their light weight, and Mg-3Al-1Zn (AZ31) is the most extensively used wrought magnesium alloy. However, this alloy has limitations with regard to creep strength, microstructural homogeneity and strength compared to other light alloys. These three issues have been addressed in this project by modifying the alloy composition: (i) addition of Ca to AZ31 alloy to form stable intermetallic particles in the matrix to impart high temperature strength, and (ii) incorporating nano-alumina particles that decorate and strengthen the particle boundaries. The alloys and composites were prepared by disintegrated melt deposition (DMD) technique followed by hot extrusion, i.e. powder processing route. The processing technology for hot working of these newer materials has been developed using dynamic materials modeling technique with emphasis on microstructural control and workability optimization. While the addition of either Ca or nano-Alumina increased the strength of the alloy, their simultaneous addition (AZ31-1%Ca-1.5%nano-Alumina) provided higher workability ranges (temperature and speed of forming) for the alloy showing their synergistic benefit from a processing perspective as well as exhibiting superior mechanical properties at application temperatures of up to 175 oC without sacrificing ductility.

114911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
114911.value: Slender beams and plates are the most commonly used structural components in civil engineering. Initial cracks and geometric imperfections in the existing structures make them vulnerable to buckling instability or failure due to excessive post-buckling deflections when subjected to compressive loads. Active repair and control of these imperfect structures have great potential in regaining and enhancing their load-carrying capacity. The proposed project will investigate numerically and experimentally the active control of the post-buckling behavior of imperfect slender beams and plates through the use of repair patches and surface bonded piezoelectric sensors and electroactive polymer actuators. The theoretical formulation will be based on von Karman nonlinear kinematics and takes into account the effects of various imperfection modes and material nonlinearity in the adhesive layer. An optimization algorithm will be used for the design of repair patch and sensor/actuator array rendering maximized critical buckling load and minimized post-buckling deflections. The research outcome will lead to not only an in-depth understanding of the nonlinear electro- mechanical characteristics but also an effective and economical control technique of structures with initial cracks and imperfections, thus improving the performance reliability and extending the service life of existing structures. 薄壁细长杆板是土木工程中最为广泛应用的结构。在压力载荷作用下，构件中的初始裂纹和几何缺陷会使结构易于产生过量屈曲变形进而发生失稳破坏。主动修复与控制技术可有效地恢复并增强此类结构的受压承载能力。本项目将通过实验与数值分析对使用修复片，压电传感器和电致聚合物作动器对含缺陷薄壁轻质受压杆板进行后屈曲行为控制的技术加以研究。理论分析中采用冯-卡门几何非线性关系并考虑了粘结层材料非线性和各种不同几何缺陷形式的影响。修复片铺设方式，压电感应器/作动器的位置及连接方式则通过优化设计以达到使结构临界屈曲载荷最大但屈曲挠度最小的结果。研究成果不但有助于深入了解此类结构的非线性机-电耦合响应特性，发展出对含初始裂纹和几何缺陷结构进行修复控制的经济有效的方法，并可大大改善现有 结构的可靠性和使用寿命。

114911.label: Realisation of objectives
114911.value: 1. Studies have been conducted to investigate the effects of initial geometric imperfections in the form of initial curvature [8.1, 8.2] and inter-laminar delamination [8.3]. 2. Extensive research work has been done to explore the effective ways to enhance the buckling, post-buckling and vibration behaviors of structures with or without imperfections using piezoelectric materials [8.3, 8.5, 8.6] 3. Theoretical formulations and numerical analyses have been carried out to gain an in-depth understanding of the complicated nonlinear electro-mechanical behaviour of functionally graded piezoelectric actuators [8.1, 8.2, 9.1] and laminated cylindrical thin shells integrated with piezoelectric materials [8.3]. 4. Preliminary work has been done in the active control and repair of imperfect slender structural elements under compressive loading [8.6, 9.2]. The optimization design approach is yet to be developed due to the very limited time (one year only) we had and PI1's (Prof Kitipornchai) retirement from CityU in December 2012. 5. The validation of the developed theoretical formulations and numerical analysis has been partially completed through direct comparisons in all of our published papers with experimental and/or analytical results published in previous studies on single beams, plate strips and cylindrical shells with and without geometrical imperfections in the form of initial curvature and delamination.

114911.label: Major findings and research outcome
114911.value: Our studies [8.1, 8.2, 8.3] show that geometric defects such as initial curvature (either global or localized) and interlaminar delamination play an important role in the critical buckling load, post-buckling equilibrium path, free vibration frequencies and dynamic response of the slender structures. These defects, especially those located at or near the center of the structure, significant weaken the structural stiffness consequently, lead to lower critical buckling load, less post-buckling strength, and natural frequencies but result in higher deformation. Based on the numerical results we obtained so far and published in [8.1-8.3, 8.5, 9.2], the buckling, post-buckling and vibration behaviors of structures with or without imperfections can be improved using piezoelectric materials with appropriately designed layer thickness and applied voltage. The wave dispersion of the functionally graded plates containing carbon nanotube reinforcements has been discussed [8.4] by employing three-dimensional elasticity theory and space state approach. Numerical results show that the wave dispersion is remarkably influenced by the material distribution and the volume fraction of the carbon nanotubes. Very good agreement has been achieved in direct comparisons of our results with the experimental and analytical ones published by others, indicating that the theoretical models and the numerical analyses developed in our studies are both reliable and effective. Due to the limited time, the experimental validation on tensegrity frame made of single compressed members is yet to be finished.

114911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
114911.value: The possible further development of the research work includes: (1) rigorous validation through experiment; (2) exploration of the great potentials of emerging nano-piezoelectric materials in structure repair and active control applications.

114911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
114911.value: Slender beams and plates are the most commonly used structural components in civil engineering. Initial cracks and geometric imperfections in the existing structures make them vulnerable to buckling instability or failure due to excessive post-buckling deflections when subjected to compressive loads. Active repair and control of these imperfect structures have great potential in regaining and enhancing their load carrying capacity. The proposed project will investigate numerically and experimentally the active control of the post-buckling behavior of imperfect slender beams and plates through the use of repair patches and surface bonded piezoelectric sensors and electroactive polymer actuators. The theoretical formulation will be based on von Karman nonlinear kinematics and takes into account the effects of various imperfection modes and material nonlinearity in the adhesive layer. An optimization algorithm will be used for the design of repair patch and sensor/actuator array rendering maximized critical buckling load and minimized post-buckling deflections.

116111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
116111.value: Every year Hong Kong generates 1.3 million tons of food waste and the majority of it is disposed of in landfills. Diverting food waste to landfills is problematic as such management practice is rapidly exhausting the valuable landfill spaces in Hong Kong. Therefore, the Hong Kong government has set forth a goal to reduce the total volume of municipal solid waste disposed of in landfills to less than 25% by 2014. More importantly, with climate change looming on the horizon and our desire for a sustainable future that is free of fossil fuels, there need to be a paradigm shift to no longer view organic waste materials as dead end products that require disposal. By coupling innovative advances in science and engineering, food waste is in fact a valuable biomass feedstock that can be transformed into value-added bioproducts. In response to the need to better manage the food waste problem in Hong Kong, the proposed research aims to use microbial consortia and state-of-the-art genome-enabled systems biology approaches to investigate the microbial processes that biotransform food waste into bioenergy and bioplastics. Specifically, we will prospect the vast and often unexplored biodiversity in the environment and screen microbial communities for the appropriate combination of organisms and genes that can yield a high concentration of bioenergy and bioplastics from food waste. Bioenergy in the forms of ethanol, butanol or methane and the biodegradable plastics polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) that can be produced from food waste are significant business and economic opportunities. The successful production of these renewable bioproducts will hinge on whether we can thoroughly understand the microbial reactions that are catalyzing the biotransformation and the proposed laboratory-scale research is positioned to query the population structures, dynamics, genetics, and physiology of the complex microbial consortia to gain a comprehensive system-level understanding. The research efforts to study the biotransformation of food waste will ultimately enable us to address both the sustainability and municipal solid waste challenges that Hong Kong faces.

116111.label: Realisation of objectives
116111.value: The overarching goal of the proposed project is to study diverse microbial communities enriched from the environments on how they convert organic waste to useful energy and bioproducts. Through laboratory experiments, we successfully demonstrated that methane, hydrogen and polyhydroxybutyrate (bioplastics) could be produced by these enrichment cultures using organic waste such as cellulose, xylan and food waste as the starting materials. By applying state-of-the-art high-throughput DNA and RNA amplicon sequencing methods, the microbial ecology of the communities during the conversion process was studied. Specifically, we queried the effects of the inoculum, substrates and operating conditions on the yield of the final products and how these factors influenced the ecology in the microbial communities. Detailed experiments were also conducted to simulate the interactions in an artificial microbial community and the high-throughput sequencing approach enabled the clarification of microbial functions. Overall, through this project, we gained insights and a better understanding on the complex microbial communities that can convert waste to valuable bioproducts; hence, the objectives of waste reduction as well as establishing new knowledge in the biology of microbial communities have been achieved. As part of the education plan, doctoral and master students were trained and a number of undergraduate students participated in the research project.

116111.label: Major findings and research outcome
116111.value: The results from this project have been published in a number of journal publications (see Part C). The manuscript of Lu et al. (2013) illustrates that food waste, cellulose and xylan can be effectively converted to methane by a microbial community that originated from a wastewater treatment plant anaerobic digester. We noted that different active bacterial and archaeal members were promoted when different substrates were introduced, illustrating that the diversity within the microbial community allowed it adapt to the change in conditions. We further queried the relationships between the composition of the inoculum, organic feedstock and the ability to generate methane in the work of Wilkins et al. (2015a). This work shows that complete and efficient methane-generating system could be assembled from different microbial inocula consisting of diverse members that nevertheless perform similar functions. In a follow-up study, we also demonstrated that long-term culturing would cause initially different methane-producing communities to converge (Jia et al. (2015)). Given that the methanogenic populations in the anaerobic digesting communities have been poorly characterized, in the work of Wilkins et al. (2015b), we used an innovative method of sequencing and analyzing both the archaeal 16S rRNA gene and the methyl coenzyme M reductase (mcrA) gene in concert to better clarify the functions of the methanogens. Interestingly, we found that the uncultured WSA2 group, which is commonly found in anaerobic digesters, could be a methanogenic population, which has not been previously reported. In order to better understand the inner working of a microbial community, we reported the interaction of an artificial dark and light fermenting co-culture that converts cellulose to hydrogen in Lu et al. (2015). The results from this work demonstrate that the constructed co-culture could lead to improved hydrogen yield and the strategy of co-culture could be used as inoculum in industrial bioprocesses. Through a collaborative work, we prospected the ability of enriched marine sediments to consume methane to produce polyhydroxybutyrate (bioplastic) and we reported the key members in the microbial communities (Karthikeyan et al. (2015)). Given the importance of the topic of waste to resources and the application of advanced systems biology tools, we published a review article summarizing the recent findings (Sales and Lee, 2015). Overall, the results from this project have not only demonstrated that waste to resources is feasible, but also provided fundamental insights into the microbial communities that catalyze the biological reactions.

116111.value: Results from this project have led to a funded proposal as indicated below to further study the conversion of organic matters to methane by complex microbial communities using systems biology approaches. 1.) PI: Patrick Lee; HK$500,000; 1/1/2015 – 31/12/2017. Furthermore, in collaboration with the industry, we have received funding to develop a pilot system to convert food waste to methane. 2.) 116111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
116111.value: In Hong Kong, over 1.3 million tons of food waste is generated every year. These along with other waste organic matters such as plant materials are disposed of in landfills, which is problematic as landfill spaces are limited and expanding landfills is not feasible in the long run. An alterative sustainable solution is to convert the organic waste to energy and bioproducts so that the waste is diverted from landfills and useful materials are produced. In this study, we studied how microbial communities consisting of multiple microorganisms can perform the biotransformation of the labile food waste or the recalcitrant plant materials to methane, hydrogen and bioplastics. Overall, complex microbial communities that originated from the natural environments can effectively carry out the biological processes and produce the desired products. Furthermore, by applying sequencing technology, we investigated the biological mechanisms of the conversion and queried how the microorganisms in the community interacted with each other. Overall, we gained a detailed understanding of the microbiology of the biotransformation so that more effective processes can then be developed to not only treat the organic waste generated in Hong Kong, but also produce renewable products with commercial values.

116511.label: Major findings and research outcome
116511.value: [Objectives 1-3] We separate the light effect into reflectance and shadow. Reflectance can be constructed based on environment mapping or texture mapping. Besides, texture mapping can enrich the surface detail. The conventional texture mapping approach considers raster images which are limited by the texture resolution. A color adjustable gradient mesh representation was proposed to solve this problem. The result was reported in a journal [3] (mainly supported by this research grant). Furthermore, to allow graphics designers to edit the color information, a user scribble-based recoloring method was developed. A journal paper [8] for this work is under preparation. For soft shadow, we develop a concentric spherical representation. To provide better rendering results, a spherical summed area table filtering scheme was proposed. To further improve the filtering quality, we utilize unicube mapping. The result was reported in a journal [5]. To further reduce the seam-artifact, we develop the summed area cube map (SACM). The key idea is to convert the integration of a region over the cube map surface to the integration of a rectangular cuboid over a 3D auxiliary function. A journal paper [7] for SACM technique is under preparation. [Objectives 3 and 4] As there is no effective method to synthesis the vector graphics at non-vertex point, we turn the methodology to the illumination adjustable image (IAI) concept. But an IAI consumes a lot of graphics memory. In [2], we use a PCA technique to compress those illumination data. An IAI is converted into a few PCA-images and a number of eigen-coefficients. Those data are further compressed by spherical transform coding techniques. During local relighting, we need to locate a reference light vector. We can use a winner-take-all (WTA) approach to locate the light vector. The property of the WTA was reported in [1]. Since the extracted coefficients are sensitive to compression noise, a noise injection algorithm should be used. The property of the general noise injection approach was reported in [4]. Furthermore, we extend our noise injection works and report the result in a book chapter [11]. To handle missing data in an IAI, we may need some tensor completion algorithms. A tensor completion algorithm is developed. We submit the result to a journal [6] (under minor revision). During the development of our systems, we gain a lot of graphics processing unit (GPU) experience. We then develop some GPU applications which are reported in two book chapters [9,10].

116511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
116511.value: [1] Nowadays, many data, such as spherical videos and geographical data, are defined in the spherical domain. The SACM technique has a lot of potential applications in other reserach areas. Besides, the data compression methods for IAIs can also be used for compressing other spherical data. [2] The tensor completion technique developed in this project is to handle rectangular data. It is interesting to develop some data completion methods that can directly handle missing data spherical domain. [3] Editing color information of a gradient mesh could be extended to filling texture into a gradient mesh. [4] The noise injection algorithm can be extended to handle a general learning system.

116511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
116511.value: Illumination effect and texture mapping can enrich the scene in virtual reality applications. For example, in a horrible game, the illumination effect is able to creating a dramatic atmosphere. In other graphics applications, such as animation, we also need controllable lighting effects. However, it is always difficult to achieve illumination effect for time varying scene and time varying lighting condition. With our concentric spherical representation, the rendered results can be achieved in a real-time manner. For our IAI representation, it can provide high quality lighting effects under manageable data size. Nowadays, many computer vision applications involve spherical videos or spherical images. In these applications, we need some spherical filtering process to modify the spherical data. Our spherical filtering techniques can also be used for handling those spherical videos or spherical images.

116911.label: Project Title(Chinese)
116911.value: 用于无线通信的全向介质谐振器天线的研究

116911.label: Project Objectives
116911.value: Investigation of dualband/wideband omnidirectional dielectric resonator antennas (DRAs); Investigation of circularly polarized omnidirectional DRA; and Investigation of using the transparent omnidirectional DRA as a light cover.
rows: Investigation of dualband/wideband omnidirectional dielectric resonator antennas (DRAs);
Investigation of circularly polarized omnidirectional DRA; and
Investigation of using the transparent omnidirectional DRA as a light cover.

116911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
116911.value: The demand for wireless communications has been growing faster than ever, as RF/microwave technology has undoubtedly become a part of our daily lives. In wireless communications, the antenna is very important because it directly affects the signal transmission and reception. Recently, the dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) has been studied extensively due to the inherent merits of its low loss, small size, low cost, and ease of excitation. Studies of the DRA have mainly concentrated on the broadside radiation mode. In some applications, such as indoor wireless communications, the omnidirectional radiation mode is more important because it provides a better coverage. However, much less attention has been received for the omnidirectional DRA. Since today the dualband antenna still plays a very important role in wireless communications (e.g, 2.4/5.2GHz WLAN systems), the dualband omnidirectional DRA will be investigated in this project for the first time. The wideband omnidirectional DRA will also be investigated by merging the two bands of a dualband DRA. Ansoft HFSS will be used to simulate the antennas and measurements will be carried out to verify the results. Thus far, all reported omnidirectional DRAs are linearly polarized (LP), but circular polarization (CP) is more welcome for certain applications including satellite communications because the polarization of a signal may be changed during its propagation. In this project, the CP omnidirectional DRA will also be investigated. A CP polarizer will be integrated with the LP omnidirectional DRA to give a very compact and simple CP design. In this project, the single-/dual-/wide-band omnidirectional CP DRAs will all be investigated. The simulated results will be checked by measurements. The dualfunction omnidirectional DRA that serves as a light cover will be investigated for the first time. The transparent DRA fabricated with glass will be used in this part. By integrating the antenna with the light cover, the installation process can be simplified substantially. The idea will be applied to both the LP and CP DRAs. In the CP case, the transparent indium tin oxide (ITO) film will be used to realize the loading conducting strips, making the whole CP antenna transparent. Since the measured frequency usually deviates from the design value due to manufacturing tolerances, frequency tunings of omnidirectional DRA will be investigated in this project. The result will be of great practical importance. Design guidelines will be provided to facilitate the designs of the omnidirectional DRAs. 现今射频/微波技术无疑已成为我们日常生活的一部分，因此对无线通信的需求与日俱增。天线在无线通信中非常重要，因为它直接影响信号的发射和接收。最近介质谐振器天线（DRA）由于其固有的低损耗、小尺寸、低成本和易激励等优点，得到广泛研究。 DRA的研究主要集中在正向辐射模式。在某些应用中，譬如室内无线通信，全向辐射模式因可提供更大的覆盖范围，显得更为重要。但是，全向DRA并没有受到太多关注。由于如今双频天线在无线通信中（譬如2.4 / 5.2GHZ WLAN 系统）仍然扮演重要角色，所以本项目将首次探讨双频全向DRA。同时也研究通过合并双频天线的两个频带而形成的宽带全向DRA。我们用Ansoft HFSS来仿真天线，并将通过实验测试来验证这些结果。 迄今为止，所有报道过的全向DRA都是线极化，但是对某些应用包括卫星通信，圆极化更有优势，因为信号的极化可能在它的传播过程中发生变化。本项目也将研究圆极化全向DRA。圆极化器将与线极化全向DRA集成，实现一个非常紧凑和简单的圆极化设计。单频/双频/宽频全向圆极化DRA都会在本项目中一一探讨。仿真结果将通过测量结果来验证。 首次研究可同时充当灯罩的双功能全向DRA。这部分将使用由玻璃制作的透明DRA。通过把天线和灯罩集成在一起，极大简化安装过程。这个想法会同时应用在线极化和圆极化DRA。在圆极化天线中，将用透明氧化铟锡薄膜(ITO)作为加载的导电条从而使整个天线都透明。 测量频率通常会因为加工误差和设计值有些偏差，所以在本项目中也将研究频率可调谐的全向DRA。所得结果具有重要的实际价值。 将提供设计指南以便于全向DRA的设计。

116911.label: Realisation of objectives
116911.value: The three objectives have been achieved successfully. The first objective consists of two parts, namely the dualband and wideband dielectric resonator antennas (DRAs). The hemispherical DRA, centrally fed by a coaxial probe, was used to design a dualband linearly polarized (LP) antenna for 2.4/5.8 GHz WLAN applications. Both of its fundamental TM101 mode and higher-order TM103 mode are excited to provide the two frequency bands. The commercial package ANSYS HFSS was used to simulate the antenna, and a prototype made of glass was fabricated to verify the simulation. Reasonable agreement between simulation and measurement has been obtained. For the wideband part, an omnidirectional transparent two-layer hemispherical DRA was studied. Acrylic and glass are used for the inner and outer layers of the DRA, respectively. Again, it is centrally fed by a coaxial probe, and only the single TM101 mode was considered in this part. A prototype was fabricated and the measured and simulated results are in good agreement. The second objective has been achieved by using a compact omnidirectional circularly polarized (CP) rectangular DRA excited by an axial coaxial probe. To generate CP fields, a conducting patch is placed on each sidewall of the DRA. Since the fields of the probe-fed DRA are predominantly vertically polarized, the patches are inclined diagonally to cut the E-fields effectively. Again, the DRA is fabricated with glass and simulated using HFSS. Next, the wideband omnidirectional CP rectangular DRA has also been studied. On each sidewall of the DRA, an inclined slot was fabricated for the generation of omnidirectional CP fields. A parasitic conducting strip is placed inside each slot to broaden the axial-ratio (AR) bandwidth. Prototypes of both the compact and wideband CP DRAs were fabricated and tested, and good agreement between the measured and simulated results is observed for each case. To achieve the last objective, transparent omnidirectional DRAs serving as the covering of lighting system have been demonstrated. In the demonstration, LEDs were used as the lighting source, and holes were drilled inside the DRAs for insertions of the LEDs. Apart from making prototypes to verify the HFSS simulations, a practical table-lamp antenna was also made. The table-lamp antenna works very well, with no interference between the antenna and lighting parts.

116911.label: Major findings and research outcome
116911.value: (a) Investigation of dualband/wideband omnidirectional (i) Dualband omnidirectional DRA Two design formulas for determining the radius of the DRA and frequency ratio have been obtained. The errors of the formulas are less than 1% over the range 6 ≤ εr ≤ 38, where εr is the dielectric constant of the DRA. Using the formulas, a dualband hemispherical glass DRA with a radius of 33.3 mm and r = 6.85 was designed successfully. The results have been summarized in the first paper of Section 8 (Part C). (ii) Wideband omnidirectional DRA Our wideband omnidirectional two-layer hemispherical DRA has a bandwidth of 31.9%, which is 126% of that of a single-layer DRA. A new engineering formula that determines the outer radius “a” of the DRA has been obtained, from which the inner radius “b” can be found easily from the given radius ratio. The result is valid over the ranges 6 ≤ εr1 ≤ 15, 2 ≤ εr1 /εr2 ≤ 6, and 0.1 ≤ b/a≤ 0.67, where εr1 and εr2 are the dielectric constants of the outer and inner layers of the DRA, respectively. The error is less than 2.5%. This work has been submitted to a journal (the last paper of Section 8, Part C). In addition, an omnidirectional building-shape glass DRA has also been investigated, which has a wide impedance bandwidth of 36.5%. The work has been presented in a conference (Section 9, Part C). (b) Investigation of circularly polarized omnidirectional DRA The measured and simulated impedance bandwidths of the compact omnidirectional CP rectangular DRA are 6.6% (2.352.51 GHz) and 6.7% (2.322.48 GHz), respectively, while the measured and simulated AR bandwidths are 6.9% (2.372.54 GHz) and 6.6% (2.352.51 GHz), respectively. The results have been published (second paper of Section 8, Part C). A wideband omnidirectional CP rectangular DRA has also been studied, with a very wide AR bandwidth of more than 25%. This part has been published (third paper of Section 8, Part C). (c) Investigation of using the transparent omnidirectional DRA as a light cover It has been demonstrated that using glass (transparent) omnidirectional DRAs as the covering of lighting system is feasible. For each design, there is no virtual effect on the antenna performance when the LEDs are turned on or off, making designs of the light-covering DRAs very simple. The results are given in the papers of Section 8, Part C (except the third paper).

116911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
116911.value: The investigated omnidirectional DRAs are centrally fed by a coaxial probe. This feeding method can excite fields which are similar to those of an electric dipole, giving omnidirectional radiation patterns. However, this approach requires drilling a hole in the DRA to accommodate the probe, which can be troublesome in some cases. To solve this problem, we can employ two pairs of collinear slots to excite the DRA. The two pairs of slots are perpendicular to each other, forming a sequential rotation of slots. Each slot can be fed by a microstripline. This feeding approach gives an equivalent vertical magnetic dipole that can be used to excite the omnidirectional DRA. To obtain an equivalent vertical electric dipole, the slots can be replaced by conducting strips. One end of each strip is shorted to the ground, whereas the other ends of the four strips are connected together. The resulting cross can be fed at its center by a probe. Since these two excitation methods can be implemented on a planar printed structure, the need of drilling a hole in the DRA can be avoided. This is a new research direction of DRA.

116911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
116911.value: Over the last two decades, the dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) has received tremendous attention due to the inherent merits of its low loss, small size, low cost, and ease of excitation. This project investigates new DRAs that provide omnidirectional radiation patterns, which are useful for indoor wireless communications. Both linearly polarized (LP) and circularly polarized (CP) designs have been studied in the project. The former is simpler in structure, whereas the latter can relax the requirement of alignment between the receiving and transmitting antennas. In addition, the wideband and dualband omnidirectional DRAs have been investigated to meet different needs of modern wireless communication. The DRAs were simulated and reasonable agreement between the measured and simulated results has been obtained. Today, indoor wireless systems such as WLAN have been installed in modern buildings. Since the lighting system is indispensable for a building, this project has innovatively investigated combining the antenna and lighting systems. It has been achieved by using the glass DRA as the covering of a light source. With this idea, the antenna and lighting functions can be provided at a single point, saving the space and installation cost. Prototypes were fabricated and the idea has been demonstrated very successfully.

117111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
117111.value: 對於無線通訊設備吸收比率的相關測定步驟，國際非電離輻射防護委員會（ICNIRP）標準、國際電機電子工程師學會IEEE1528標準和EN62209-1標準中都有詳細的介紹。然而目前以上資料都只是針對單頻率情況下的操作。 現在多種無線通訊方式常常會被集成到一個電子設備中進行多功能操作，比如掌上型電腦(PDA)既有無線區域網路(WLAN)功能，又有藍牙功能，同一個設備會同時在多個不同的頻率同時工作。對於使用無線通訊設備時，輻射對人體健康威脅的關注也必須延伸到了多輻射源或者多頻率並存的情況之下。因為假定不同頻率的輻射吸收比率值可以疊加在一起，像ICNIRP 或者 IEEE C95.1 標準中介紹的以均方差的形式將不同頻率的輻射功率值簡單相加，常常不會得到正確的結果。原因在於測定輻射吸收比率時兩個主要的參數：人體組織的介電質常數和導電率，隨著頻率的變化不是恒定的。由於非直線性作用，人體某一局部產生的多模多頻率共振使得身體組織內電磁場分佈變得異常複雜。對於同一部個人無線通訊設備產生的多頻率輻射的情形，現有的輻射吸收比率測定資料還沒有完全涉及到。不過今年六月國際電子電機委員會（IEC）公佈的新標準IEC 62630中包括了一些多輻射源的情形，同時一些相應的前期規範也已推出。 本建議書旨在提出對於具有多頻率輻射的無線通訊設備在人體內產生吸收比率的測定方法，並根據新的測試方法集中探討同時工作的多輻射源在人體內產生的吸收比率所帶來的影響。

117111.value: In general the project objectives of investigating the impact of simultaneous multiple frequency radiations from electronic devices on the corresponding SAR of the human bodies have been achieved; the approach taken and the methodology have been adhered closely to those in the submitted proposal. The outcomes and findings have been published in referenced conference papers and journal papers.

117111.label: Major findings and research outcome
117111.value: The objective of the project in evaluating the SAR concern in human safety when using wireless communication devices with simultaneous multiple frequency has been carried out. As discussed in the published journal paper in Part C, results have shown that the maximum SAR value induced in the mobile phone user inside a vehicle increased by 5% in comparison to the use of a mobile phone in free space, and the highest SAR is mainly located at the head and shoulders of the human body. It was also observed from the study that the difference of the SAR values between variations in handedness is insignificant.

117111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
117111.value: It has been identified that related investigation work is to be carried out in 4G LTE applications, and funding for initial investigation is being allocated by the City University of Hong Kong SRG funding in Analysis of Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) of 4G Long Term Evolution (LTE) Mobile Devices.

117111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
117111.value: This project has addressed the concern of human safety when using wireless communication devices with simultaneous multiple frequency radiation. Results also demonstrated that the highest SAR, as related to human safety, is mainly located at the head and shoulders of the human body, and that the SAR values between variations in handedness is insignificant. The project has demonstrated that the change of passenger count inside a vehicle can alter the maximum SAR value induced in the bodies of passengers, and that the induced level of the SAR value to the non-users is directly related to the distance between the users and non-users.

118311.label: Project Objectives
118311.value: To set up an active stereo vision system. This new visual sensing system can provide robust 3D information with the stereo and pattern projection system. Furthermore, the sensor settings can be adjusted on-line. Suitable methods of automatic recalibration of the sensing system will be developed. To acquire 3D trajectory data via tracking using the active stereo visual sensing. To develop the method for activity modeling using trajectory description. To implement the system and methodology for activity observation on experimental systems. Dynamic view planning will be implemented to maximize the aggregate observability of motion trajectories of the activity to observe.
