118311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
118311.value: Most of today’s surveillance systems use 2D images from fixed cameras, which cannot perform adequately in many situations. In this project, an active stereo vision system will be developed to achieve enhanced performance in activity observation and perception for advanced surveillance applications. The proposed system is designed to observe target motions and percept/recognize its activities by dynamically changing the viewing pose and the settings of the sensing system on-line. Methods for automatic recalibration of the vision system will be developed. This project will focus on the target motion trajectory including its extraction, description, analysis in activity perception/recognition. A new activity modeling method will be developed based on trajectory description. The proposed system can plan its next view to best observe the predicted activities of the target, which is useful for many applications of advanced surveillance involving activity recognition/perception such as robot learning by demonstration, human activity monitoring and security control. 现有的监控系统多用二维图像和固定像机而难于满足要求。本项目立于采用主动立体视觉以增强对目标活动的监测。本系统在工作时可在线改变其观测姿态和系统参数。对此本项目将采用相应的自动标定方法在线标定。本项目将从轨迹的获取，描述，分析，以实现目标活动的识别。本系统可自动规划其观测姿态以取得最佳观测效果。本系统在机器人任务学习，人行为观测，安全检查等方面具有广泛应用。

118311.label: Realisation of objectives
118311.value: 1, In this project, an active stereo vision system was set up with its pattern projection incorporated to obtain robust 3D measurements. The stereo vision system is implemented and tested in applications including tracking [J1]. Pattern projections were studied for visual sensing, with a new method proposed for 3D surface measurements [J7]. The calibration and re-calibrations issues were addressed to the depth for active vision systems in general [B1] and for those with pattern projections in particular [J3,J8]. To acquire 3D information from visual sensing and integrate it in tracking, an active stereo vision system is developed and to enhance the tracking performance [J1]. The above is related to Objective 1 which has been almost fully achieved. 2, Objective 2 is extensively explored. In studying tracking, simple 3D trajectory data [J1] and more complex data as object models [J4,J11,C2,C4,C5,C6,C7] can be used in the tracking. In dealing with the data for tracking with omni-directional vision, a contour coding based Rotating Adaptive Model is developed to extract the contour feature for enhancing the tracking performance [J6]. The issues in multi-target visual tracking are extensively addressed [J9,J10,J13,C3,C9,C10]. These are related Objective 2 which has been fully achieved. 3, In-depth studies were conducted in complex motion tracking and modelling. Trajectory description [C8] was explored at high level for activity modeling using a novel indexing method [C1,C10]. Trajectories are segmented into basic segments and represented in segment level rather than point level. The trajectories are indexed by their segment sequences for recognition. In this way, the computational cost is significantly decreased so that it can be used for real time recognition. With the accuracy preserved for long term trajectories. These are related Objective 3 which has mostly been realized. 4, Methods are studied for adaptive observation of object motion by controlling the visual sensing system during tracking [J1]. With controlled motions of the vision system, the object’s images can be located at the centers of the image planes to achieve the desired tracking performance [J1]. Adaptive modelling approach was also investigated for enhancing the tracking performance [J6]. The tracking task is also formulated as a dynamic view planning problem and optimal tracking is achieved by on-line controlling the viewing parameters of the vision system [J1]. Implement the methodology for motion observation on experimental systems was also conducted [C8] with articulated human motion as testing case. The above are related Objective 4 which has mostly been realized.

118311.label: Major findings and research outcome
118311.value: The following lists the findings: • An active stereo vision system was set up [J1]. The system configurations can be controlled for enhancing the 3D tracking performances. • For tracking applications, a model was developed incorporating segmented regions and pixel descriptors for Background Subtraction [J2]. • A new method was developed to measure the surface of an object, which just requires one colour patterned image [J7]. In the decoding method, colour identification is modelled as an unsupervised classification problem and K-means are adopted on a new colour feature. • A generic distorted fringe model was developed for calibration [J3], to compensate for the errors from distortion for another type of projection system. With this new calibration method, the measurement precision is much enhanced. • A structured sparse representation model was developed for object tracking [J4], via modelling the appearance of an object as a sparse linear combination of structured union of subspaces. This observation model is integrated with a stochastic affine motion model to form a particle filter framework for robust visual tracking [J11,J12]. • A multi-target visual tracking framework and system was developed [J9,J10,J13]. The individual targets within the occlusion region are regarded as the players in the game based method [J9] to compete for the maximum utilities. • A tracking system was also set up with omni-directional vision [J6]. This is a special system consisting of a thermal camera and a hyperboloid catadioptric omnidirectional mirror, giving rise to a novel vision system based on Thermal Catadioptric Omnidirectional (TCO) Vision. • A modelling method was developed to achieve well focused image for omni-directional vision [J5]. Based on the special optical geometry properties of catadioptric systems, the model describes the shapes of the best focused image regions in multi-focal images by a series of neighboring concentric annuluses. Estimating the model parameters, an overall well focused image can be obtained by combining the best focused regions with a fast and reliable online operation. • An invariant trajectory descriptor was developed for motion tracking and activity modelling and recognition [C1,C8], which can deal with multiple motion trajectories using kinematic relation among multiple moving parts [C8]. Two kinds of kinematic relation among multiple trajectories are modelled: articulated and independent trajectories. The new descriptor is constructed by incorporating both the differential invariants of root trajectory and orientation, distance variations of each relative trajectory. The effectiveness of the new descriptor under complex circumstances has been validated by experiments in human action recognition [C1,C8,C11].

118311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
118311.value: In this project, an active stereo vision system is set up. The methodologies in incorporating pattern projections to obtain 3D measurements are developed. The relevant issues in the system calibration and 3D reconstruction are investigated. Based on the 3D visual sensing data, extensive studies are conducted in motion tracking, trajectory description, and motion and action recognition. With the trajectory descriptor developed, motion tracking and activity modelling and recognition can be studied with multiple motion trajectories. The 3D visual sensing and tracking methods developed here will be useful for many applications including advanced surveillance and robotics. We plan to further explore some practical applications of the methods developed in some applied work. Efforts are being made in patenting the system and methodology. Extending the 3D visual sensing work, some issues for micro scale applications are being studied. Some more studies are also conducted in motion tracking, trajectory perception and action recognition for robotics applications. These further works are expected to pave way for advanced motion tracking and action recognition in practical applications. Meanwhile, a project is being planned in developing another type 3D visual sensing system and method for 3D motion tracking to follow up the explorations relevant to this project.

118311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
118311.value: In this project, we have developed the 3D visual sensing system for motion tracking. Using pattern projections, we can obtain the 3D measurements that cannot be achieved with traditional vision. This is important for tracking applications, as the object surfaces, like human body, are often featureless. The robust tracking achieved will be of practical significance for many applications including motion tracking for advanced visual surveillance, and robotic applications, activity or behavior recognition for security surveillance, motion retrieval for web applications.

118411.label: Project Title(Chinese)
118411.value: 大分子结构体系生物力学性能的理论分析及实验研究

118411.label: Project Objectives
118411.value: Develop a technique for evaluating the inter-atomistic potential between the macromolecules tubulin and guanosine and the concept of the fictitious bond. Develop an atomistic-continuum model and build a higher-order gradient continuum constitutive relationship for microtubules to predict their highly orthotropic elastic moduli. Carry out a series of experiments to study the mechanical response of microtubules under typical loading situations. Establish a mesh-free computational framework for implementing numerical simulation for microtubules, and develop an associated computational code. Carry out a systematic study of the biomechanical responses of microtubules in terms of their elasticity, statics, dynamics, buckling, and post-buckling phenomena. Train graduate students and publish high-quality research papers in refereed international journals.

118411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
118411.value: 本项目将从理论分析及实验测试两方面着手对大分子结构体系的生物力学性能进行全面而深入的研究。通过实验研究，将得以观测到微管的微观形态，以及在各种不同荷载激励下的结构反应。实验研究的结果将被作为理论分析的事实基础及验证实例。在理论研究方面，本项目将建立一个可对细胞骨架微管进行准确生物力学分析的多尺度计算模型。并将此计算模型与无网格方法相结合推导出一套具有普遍适用性的理论体系，用于微管力学性能的数值模拟。通过编制大型计算程序，细胞骨架微管的各项力学性能将得到全面的计算和模拟。通过将数值计算结果与实验结果相对比并进一步完善，本项目将使大分子结构体系的生物力学性能得到系统而彻底的研究，并为生物医学及生物工程的发展提供有价值的参考。

118411.label: Realisation of objectives
118411.value: 1. The interatomic potential was introduced directly into the continuum model based on the proposed fictitious bond. Without tracking every single atom, the atomistic interaction between tubulins was considered using a homogenization technique. This approach has overcome the limitations of atomistic simulations on different time and size scales, and it would not need parameter fitting of atomistic simulations results and continuum elements. 2. The atomistic-continuum model was derived based on the constitutive relationship and predicted orthotropic elastic properties of microtubules. The structure and atomic composition of microtubules were quite unique; the built-up atomistic-continuum model was based on the proposed fictitious bond and homogenization technique. Within the polyatomic structure of microtubules, the tubulin monomers and guanosine molecules were treated as spheroids and the fictitious-bond vectors were introduced to represent the mutual atomic interaction and were further evaluated through the higher-order Cauchy-Born rule. The microtubule was then viewed as an equivalent lattice structure, of which the interatomic potential energy was introduced to the corresponding continuum body. Thus the gap between these two simulation regimes was bridged. 3. Experimental investigations of microtubules were started from the study of cytoskeleton in cells. It was found that the mechanical behavior of the cytoskeleton was primarily governed by inner filaments that control the cell mechanics. For the purpose of exploring the intricacies of the cytoskeleton network, experimental results were obtained for the validation and comparison with the numerical simulations. 4. A mesh-free theoretical framework was developed for simulation of the mechanical properties of microtubules. Unlike the conventional mesh-free approaches for continuum mechanics, this theory has particular advantages, founded on two different scales: atomistic and continuum levels. Material properties were described on the basis of the proposed fictitious bond in the atomistic level, and the atomistic-continuum constitutive relationship was incorporated to introduce a lattice model into the continuum framework and conduct mechanical analysis in the continuum level. Furthermore, the higher-order deformation gradient continuity was actualized by employing a higher-order Cauchy-Born rule adopted to determine the fictitious bond vectors emanating from a given evaluation point during the deformation process. 5. With the proposed methodology, elastic properties, transverse and longitudinal buckling and post-buckling behavior, vibration modes, natural frequencies and dynamic responses were numerically simulated by the proposed method. Case studies were conducted. The response of microtubules under hydrostatic pressure was also determined. 6. One PhD student was trained, and five high-quality research papers were published in refereed international journals.

118411.label: Major findings and research outcome
118411.value: The main contribution of this work lied in the originality of the new efficient atomistic-continuum model for numerical simulations of mechanical properties of polyatomic microtubules. For a very long period in history, there existed many theoretical mechanical modeling attempts before the this proposed study; however, all of these efforts have unavoidable drawbacks that made either results accuracy or computing efficiency unsatisfactory. As the microtubule is a typical polyatomic bio-composite and a single microtubule with regular length normally contains billions of different kinds of atoms, conventional atomic simulation methods and traditional continuum mechanical modeling approaches would have certain limitations in dealing with the polyatomic bio-structure. The establishment of the new model started from the proposed fictitious bond to evaluate the interatomic potential energy between the fundamental subunit of the microtubule, the tubulin dimmer. Without tracing every single atom, homogenization technique was adopted to consider the large quantities of different types of atoms. A lattice model then constructed by fictitious bonds was formed as a substitute for the polyatomic microtubule structure, which contained the atomistic interaction in microscopic scale and could be integrated into continuum mechanical computing at macroscopic level. The microscopic structure and its macroscopic continuum counterpart were considered simultaneously by making energy in both scales equal. With this attempt, different scales have been schematically bridged to smooth away drawbacks. At this point, the present study has made further progress to formulate a more advanced simulation. By considering a representative unit, an atomistic-continuum constitutive model was derived especially to accustom the atomic structure to a reciprocal continuum body. This material description was quite different from classical definitions; elastic constants were not explicitly provided because these material constants in continuum description were related to intrinsic atomic interaction for microstructures. A higher-order Cauchy-Born rule was utilized to evaluate the deformation of fictitious bond during the deformation process, which successfully made up for deficiency of the classical Cauchy-Born rule in describing inhomogeneous deformations. A bridging-scale mesh-free numerical scheme was developed for simulation of overall mechanical properties of microtubules where unlike the finite element methods, the mesh-free method automatically satisfies the higher-order gradient continuum and there are no element-induced problems. The first and second derivative of MLS shape functions could be derived easily for numerical computing. The developed mesh-free scheme matched well with the proposed atomistic-continuum constitutive relationship.

118411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
118411.value: Much work has been done at this stage, meanwhile, there still could be broaden prospects for future research. First, this research is built up of an atomistic-continuum model that is totally a new and capable of exploring the overall mechanical properties of microtubules. Thus, besides the investigations about elastic properties, buckling, post-buckling, vibration and dynamic analysis that have already completed in this work, it is strongly desired that the wave propagation behavior, fracture and bond breaking problems, multiphase reactions, synthesizing with other materials to build micro mechanical devices, interfacial contacts and mutual functions can also be studied in future research work, in order to contribute a complete and rounded system for microtubule mechanical research. Second, since microtubules are immersed in cytoplasm in vivo cells, it is better to take into consideration the influence of the cytoplasm to the elastic properties. With the support of the cytoplasm, microtubules combined with the cytoplasm to provide an overall stability. It is attainable to model the cytoplasm as viscous, elastic and viscoelastic material. Together with the proposed model for microtubules, the critical compressive force can be obtained and compared with experiments.

118411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
118411.value: The proposed research investigated the biomechanical behavior of microtubules, which are macromolecular structures that are ubiquitous cytoskeletal elements in eukaryotic cells. Investigations have been carried to understand the microstructure of microtubules and to investigate their responses under different loading conditions. Research works have been performed by developing an accurate continuum model that is applicable to atomistic-continuum simulations of microtubules. A mesh-free general computational framework embedded with an atomistic-continuum constitutive model has been developed for the numerical modeling and simulation. Using the developed computer code, the biomechanical behaviors of microtubules have been intensively studied. Through the research work and the experience gained in establishing an atomistic-continuum model for macromolecular structures, the proposed research resulted in a thorough unveiling and systematic comprehension of the biomechanical behavior of microtubules, and provided useful information for the advancement of biomedicine.

To arrange experiments and evacuation drill exercise with the assistance of mass transit company for calibrating the model parameters and comparing the output of the simulation model. It can also provide insight for the design of smoke extraction and formulating appropriate means of access for firefighting and rescue strategies. 119011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
119011.value: The mass transit system in Hong Kong carries over 3.7 million passengers everyday. With the rapid development of the community, its network has been extended over the years. New lines in the territory and connection to the Mainland are constructed. While the system is carrying huge volume of passengers per day, the safety of passengers in case of fire and emergency is one of the major concerns of the mass transit company as well as the government. The operator has endeavored to avoid accidents to happen in the system, yet zero risk situation cannot be guaranteed. To mitigate the ill-effect of an accident, provision of an efficient egress system is necessary. The design of fire and emergency egress system usually refers to the Guidelines prescribed by NFPA130 - Fixed Guideway Transit and Passenger Rail Systems for tunnel emergency egress provisions. The 2010 edition of the standard denotes that "emergency exits shall be provided from tunnels to a point of safety" and that "within underground or enclosed trainways, the maximum distance between exits shall not exceed 762 m. In view of the complex urban topography and existing building configurations, the orientation and design of tunnels for the subway system can be restrictive and the prescriptive guidance in NFPA130 can sometimes hardly be met and performance evaluation may sometimes be required in order to obtain the approval from relevant government authorities. Fire safety strategies are established for the design and operation of each line. However, the performance of the strategies, in view of the complexity of the system, may not be objectively evaluated in all aspects. The aim of this proposal is to develop an agent-based egress model to explore the evacuation pattern of evacuees in rail tunnels and associated facilities. The simulation results can be adopted to evaluate the effectiveness of different tunnel egress design and assist the establishment of trackside emergency egress strategies. It can also provide insight for the design of smoke extraction and formulating appropriate means of access for firefighting and recue strategies. 由于近年不断发展，香港地铁网络延伸到新界各地。每天乘客量超过3百多万，乘客和地铁人员在紧急情况的安全极为重要。香港地铁公司积极确保安全，但我们清楚明白绝对的安全是不能达到。也不可能完全避免意外的发生。在紧急情况下有时候需要把地铁内乘客和人员疏散。传统上地铁的紧急疏散是参考美国NFPA130的标准设计。如在隧道内最远疏散距离为762米。但在复杂的城市环境，有时候不一定能达到这处方式的标准。这时性能化设计有需要考虑。本研究是开发基于个体的隧道疏散模型，提供模拟工具对隧道疏散设计进行评估，同时也可以对疏散策略进行优化。

119011.label: Realisation of objectives
119011.value: Five objectives were proposed and they had basically been addressed. (1) Problems of evacuation strategies for rail tunnels and the associated facilities were reviewed and identified. In particular, review on the cross-passage requirements given in NFPA130 and other fire safety codes have been made. Computer simulation modeling has been proved as a powerful tool to address this kind of problems. In fact, evacuation modeling has been studied for many years so far, and large number of simulation models has been developed to modeling the movement of people under various kinds of environment conditions. Based on the methods of representing and discretizing of the floor plan or the time, these models have usually been categorized into continuous models and discrete models. In continuous models, such as the Agent-based model (ABM), people are allowed to move at any directions in a continuous represented space, while in discrete models, such as the Cellular Automaton model (CA), the floor plan are discretized into regularly distributed grids and people are only allowed to move from one grid to another. Both of these two kinds of models are proved to be qualified to reproduce many crowd movement behaviors, and to some extent, their simulation abilities are even proved to be similar with each other, but both of them are also criticized for some of their flaws. Efforts have been made to analyze the effectiveness of using different types of simulation models, CA or ABM, for modeling the evacuation pattern in rail tunnel and stations. [Ref. Part C, 9 (1)]. To improve the simulation outputs, the team has commissioned to develop a comprehensive ABM – CityFlow and the details of the model have been published. Two PhD students were trained for the development of the ABM. [Ref. Part C, 10 (1) & (2)]. (2) An agent-based egress model to simulate various tunnel evacuation processes and pedestrian movement pattern was established. Simulations have been adopted to analyzing the effect of codes requirements on the escape process. [Ref. Part C, 8 (2)]. As evacuation process would link to the escape process in stations, the works were extended to study the effectiveness of various evacuation strategies for the system including evacuation process in metro stations and the pedestrian moving patterns in stations. [Ref. Part C, 8 (8) & (9)]. The agent-based pedestrian movement model—CityFlow was developed and adopted for the simulations [Ref. Part C, 8 (3), (6) & (7)]. The tool has been demonstrated that it is useful for evaluating the performance of different alteration proposals and to study the fire escape process. In particular, we proposed the concept of ‘transit line’ to make the egress as a whole instead of targeting at single level, leading to more practical simulation results. Moreover, the dynamic density maps were prepared on the basis of the simulation outputs which could provide certain implications to the designers/ architects, and valuable insights to facility manager to plan the emergency evacuation and rescue strategies. In future study, we will further develop the model by optimizing the egress route assignment. (3) A comprehensive evacuation drill exercise in associate with the Hong Kong Mass Transit Corporation (MTRC) was arranged on November 19th, 2014 at Mongkok Station. Over 2,000 participants have been arranged to take part in the evacuation drill exercise. RFID cards were issued to the participants to record their dynamic positions during the escape process. Videos, on-site counting and after-exercise questionnaire survey information have been collected. Data and other information were collected and reported to MTRC, and had been used to compare with the simulation outputs. (4) Computer simulations were performed to evaluate the effectiveness of various fire safety design for rail tunnel and stations strategies. Moreover, studies on various aspects of pedestrian movement were also carried out. This includes studies on the bidirectional movement of people, people movement on gradient road, next-nearest-neighbor effect on people’s movement, people movement on crowd-quakes and etc. [Ref. Part C, 8 (1), (4), (5) & (10)]. Such works would be useful for future studies on evacuation process involving movement of people. (5) The findings were published and disseminate in some conferences and talks to international and local fire safety professionals and fire officers. In particular, part of the works were collaborated with MTRC and the information was recorded by them for future usage. Further analysis to the evacuation drill exercise is undergoing and will soon be published subject to MTRC agreement.

119011.label: Major findings and research outcome
119011.value: The NFPA 130 standard has given limited suggestions on the design of means of egress in rail tunnels. In this study, an agent based continuous crowd simulation model, CityFlow, was developed to study the evacuation from rail tunnel with cross-passageways. [Ref. Part C, 8 (3), (6) & (7)]. We initially focused on the influence of the walkway width and cross-passageway spacing on the egress time and queuing patterns during the evacuation. We found that if the width of walkway was added by every 100 mm, the egress time would decrease accordingly, but with different sensitivity at different width. [Ref. Part C, 8 (2) & 9 (1)]. The continuous model was proved to be eligible for identifying the continuously change of the dimensions of egress element. The study also revealed that the distance between cross-passageways was highly relevant to the optimized evacuation route choice strategy and certainly was an important parameter for egress time. Studying evacuation process from tunnel linked to the escape in stations. Indeed, the evacuation pattern is more complicated in large complex stations, especially when shopping and other facilities exist in the stations. We have further developed the agent-based model to simulate people movement in stations and the corresponding behavioral responses. [Ref. Part 8, (3), (6), (7), (8) & (9)]. To further investigate the movement characteristics of people under normal and emergency situations, other words relating to pedestrian movement, such as bidirectional flow in various conditions and crowd-quakes, have been initiated. [Ref. Part 8, (1), (4), (5) & (10)]. The density and population loading on each metro station may have significant effect on evacuation strategy in case of emergency. The metro company has comprehensive data collected from the automatic fare system. Works have been initiated to study how the automatic fare collection record may affect the metro trip pattern of people. [Ref. Part C, 8 (11)]. This provides insight on the population level of metro stations at various period of time and, in turn, provides valuable information for emergency mitigation planning.

119011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
119011.value: Guaranteeing a safe, efficient, and comfortable traveling system for passengers and other users is one of the most important aspects of an intelligent rail transportation system. Microscopic simulation of passenger flow in rail system may initiate insights that greatly benefit engineers and operators in the planning and management of the system. In this research, an agent-based microscopic pedestrian flow simulation model, CityFlow, has been developed. The building floor plan in the model is represented by a continuous space constructed in a network approach, and each pedestrian is regarded as a self-adapted agent. Agent movement is implemented in a utility maximization approach by considering various human behaviors. The influences of parameters in the model on the simulation results are investigated. Typical pedestrian flow phenomena, including the unidirectional and bidirectional flow in a corridor as well as the flow through bottlenecks, can be simulated. The model outputs have been validated by field data. The simulation results can serve as a good basis for the design and management of facility setting in mass transit systems. It can also be applied for the design and planning of complex buildings, urban layout and many facilities such as passenger ships, aircraft and etc.

119011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
119011.value: To study the evacuation from rail tunnels is vital for saving human lives when trains are forced to stop inside the tunnel in case of emergency. Although NFPA130 standard has guided the design of means of egress in rail tunnels, very rare other references can be found about the tunnel evacuation. In this research, an agent based continuous crowd simulation model, CityFlow, was developed to study the evacuation from rail tunnel with cross-passageways. The study has initially focused on the influence of the walkway width and cross-passageway spacing on the egress time and queuing patterns during the evacuation. The simulation results have revealed that if the width of walkway was added by every 100 mm, the egress time would decrease accordingly, but with different sensitivity at different width. Such simulation model can identify the continuously change of the dimensions of egress routes. The study also revealed that the distance between cross-passageways was highly relevant to the optimized evacuation strategy and was an important parameter for egress time. The simulation model has further applied to study the passenger movement and evacuation pattern in stations. Moreover, the model can also be applied to study pedestrian movement in complex urban and building settings.

119411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
119411.value: As the remanufacturing is becoming an important activity for our sustainable development, it is no surprise that in the last few years, we have witnessed an emergence stream of research in the field of remanufacturing. However, there are some gaps between the academic research and industrial practice. For example, in the current academic research, the new product and the remanufactured product are charged at the same price by assuming that customers do not distinguish the new product and the remanufactured product. But in practice, the remanufactured product is usually offered at a discount price because most of the customers prefer to buy the new product if there is no price difference. Therefore, companies use prices to make the new product and the remanufactured product substitutable to each other. Although there is a stream of research on coordinating pricing and inventory decisions on substitutable products, those models are not applicable to the remanufacturing setting where the selling price of the remanufactured product is always lower than the new product's price and the inventory level of the remanufactured product is subject to certain randomness constraint as the product return in each period is random. We try to fill in these gaps in this project. This project aims to offer an intelligent solution that optimizes pricing and inventory decisions for a system selling both new and remanufactured products. We assume demand for both new and remanufactured products is stochastic and substitutable in the sense that the price of one product not only affects its own demand but also the demand of the other product. We consider finite and infinite horizon models, in which a company dynamically coordinates prices and inventory levels of both new and remanufactured products to maximize its total profit. The optimal joint pricing and inventory policies will be derived to provide operational guidelines of pricing and inventory replenishment actions. In the meantime, efficient algorithms will be developed based on the optimal policies to solve these optimization problems. Finally, the value of integrating pricing and inventory decisions of both new and remanufactured products will be examined. These models are abstracted fairly general and therefore will find themselves a wide variety of industrial applications. 再制造行业对我们的可持续发展起到了至关重要的作用。在过去几年中，越来越多的研究把目光投到了这个领域。然而，学术研究和实际应用总有些距离。比方说，现在的研究中假设顾客对新的产品和再制造的产品愿意付同样的价格。但在实际中，绝大多数的顾客都倾向于新的产品，于是商家总是给再制造的产品一些折扣。这样使得两种产品可以互相替代。虽然有一些研究可替代产品的库存和价格的文章， 但是这些模型不能应用到再制造业上。因为在再制造业里，再制造产品的价格总是要低于新产品的价格。而且再制造产品的库存受到回收产品的数量限制。同时回收产品的数量是不确定的。这些都是这个项目要解决的问题。 我们把新产品和再制造产品放在一个系统下进行最优的价格和库存的决策。他们之间的需求是可以相互替代的。于是一个产品的价格不仅影响自己的需求，也会影响另一个产品的需求。我们考虑多个时期或无穷多个时期的最优决策。公司在每一个时期都做出价格和库存的决策，目标是最大化多个时期的利益总和。我们将刻画出最优策略的结构，并且根据这些结构发展出有效地算法。最后，这些模型的价值将被检验，而且可以应用到很多行业中去。

119411.label: Realisation of objectives
119411.value: The ojectives of this project have been fully achieved. For the make-to-order system, we have fully characterized the structure of the optimal policy. We derived managerial insigts on how the optimal price depends on the the inventory of the core of the remanufactured product. These structures and insights are used to develop an effective heuristic policy for the make-to-stock system. We also considered the substitution effect of new prodcut to the remanufactured product. We have characterized when this substitution should be used and how it can increase firm's profit. We also studied how this substitution affects the optimal price and inventory decisions. All of these results have been summarized as a paper which is now under revsion in Production and Operations Management.

119411.label: Major findings and research outcome
119411.value: Coordination of inventory and pricing decisions of both new and remanufactured products is not easy but doable. Well-structured optimal policy exists for the make-to-order system. And the same policy can serve as an effective heuristics for the make-to-stock system. Some monotonic properties of prices on the inventory level do exist. Substitution strategy can play an important role on matching the demand of the remanufactured product and increasing the firm's total profit. The study of this project has two byproducts that we want to mention here. When we study the remanufactured product, we find that random yield in prodcution (or supply uncertainty of the core of the remanufactured product) can be a major concern. Hence, we have studied the the effect of supply uncertainty in price-setting newsvendor models. The result is published in European Journal of Operational Research (we are sorry that when we acknowledge the project, we accidently used the CityU internal no instead of the RGC no). There is another byprouct. When we develop the utility model to characterize the demand for the new and remanufactured products, we find that same model can be used to characterize the demand for unit-sales and quantity-sales modes. Hence, we have studied the optimal pricing and inventory control policy with quantity-based price differentiation. The result is published in Operations research. We acknowledged this project.

The optimal joint pricing and inventory policies derived in project provide operational guidelines of pricing and inventory replenishment actions. In the meantime, efficient algorithms are developed based on the optimal policies to solve these optimization problems. These models are fairly general. We expect that they can find themselves a wide variety of industrial applications.

119511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
119511.value: 過去，毫米波技術主要被應用在具有精密部件和系統的軍事領域。近年來，由於低成本高頻硅基集成電路的成功研發，許多用於大眾服務和商業應用的毫米波系統被提出。它們包括60GHz免牌照室內寬頻個人區域網絡，77GHz汽車感應系統，以及用於安全監控的亞毫米波成像陣列。爲了減小成本，所有這些系統都需要使用低功耗信號源。而且，毫米波頻段有非常高的傳播路徑損耗。所以爲了保證足夠的覆蓋範圍，通常來說具有波束掃描功能的中高增益毫米波天線更受歡迎。對於商業應用，由於毫米波移相器的高成本和高插入損耗，通過移相器來激勵相控陣的傳統途徑是不被提倡的。相反，MIMO天線系統被認為是毫米波應用的最佳解決方案。在這個項目中，我們將為有小型天線技術的毫米波通信系統開發若干新型高性能天線。

With the assitance of the Ph.D. student, we have studied the performance of the L-probe patch antenna and array operated at 60 GHz. It is well known that the L-probe patch antenna is wide in bandwidth and simple in fabrication. The result is useful for benchmarking the magneto-electric dipole antennas and arrays developed in this project. We have successfully developed a new feeding structure for the magneto-electric dipole, which makes the realization of dual-polarized magneto-electric dipole array possible. The new element is highly efficient and can achieve a gain higher than 7 dBi even printed on a thick substrate, which is not the case when a patch antenna is printed on a thick substrate. The new antenna element can be fed by co-planar wavegude feed network, so a low cost single-layer magneto-electric dipole array have been realized. 119511.label: Major findings and research outcome
119511.value: The magneto-electric dipole (MED) is a special kind of complementary antenna that can perform with very wide bandwidth and excellent radiation characteristics. Initially, a differentially-fed MED antenna for UWB applications was developed with bandwidth over 110%, operated from 2.95 – 10.73 GHz [1], and a low-profile wideband planar complementary antenna with 10% wavelength in thickness and over 50% bandwidth (SWR<1.5) were invented [4] . More importantly, a new dual-polarized MED operated at lower microwave frequency was invented, with impedance bandwidth of 48% (SWR<1.5) and an average gain of 8.5 dBi [2]. By mounting 5 elements of this new antenna on a grounded metallic cubic structure, a four-port wideband diversity antenna capable of radiating two broadside patterns and two omnidirectional patterns was realized with 39% bandwidth [3]. The new antenna element has a simpler feeding structure than the previous design in which the two feed probes need to passing through the metal plates of the antenna. In contrast, the feed probes of the new design are installed in the channels between the vertical plates of the antenna. The result paved the way to develop millimeter-wave MEDs with different polarizations. By replacing the vertical side walls of the MED with shorting vias and the gamma-shaped feed and an L-shaped feed, a high-performance MED operated at 60 GHz with 51% bandwidth was realized by standard PCB technology [5]. It is encouraging to find that the antenna can achieve 8 dBi gain even printed on a thick dielectric substrate of a quarter wavelength in the dielectric. This is due to the fact that excitation of surface wave is weak in this new structure, which is an advantage for constructing high gain antenna arrays. The new MED can be fed by a co-planar waveguide. Due to this attractive feature, a 4 x 4 antenna array of the MEDs with co-planar waveguide feed network was realized on a single layer printed circuit board (PCB) [6]. This low-profile high-gain antenna array exhibits 18 dBi gain and 37% gain bandwidth. It is extremely low-cost in fabrication in contrast with other designs using LTCC technology. The result also confirms that this antenna element can be used for designing millimeter-wave MIMO antenna systems. The MED can radiate with circular polarization by modifying the shape of the horizontal patches. With this approach, a single-fed circularly polarized millimeter-wave antenna element with 41% bandwidth and a gain of 7.5 dBic was achieved by standard PCB technique [7].

119511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
119511.value: The research has high potential for further development at high millimeter-wave frequencies. Recently, we have demonstrated that the MED can be fed by a substrate-integrated-waveguide-fed aperture-coupled slot. The result provides the possibility to develop dual-polarized multi-beam low-profile antenna array operated at higher millimeter-wave frequenices as the antenna array is simple in structure and can be fabricated by standard PCB technqiues.

119511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
119511.value: In the past, millimeter wave technology was mainly used for military applications with sophisticated components and systems. Recently, due to the success in developing low cost silicon-based integrated circuits operated at higher frequencies, many millimeter wave systems have been proposed for civilian and commercial applications. Examples include the 60 GHz license-free indoor broadband personal area networks, 77 GHz automotive sensor systems, and the sub-millimeter wave imaging array for security. For cost reduction, all these systems require to use low power signal sources. Also, propagation path loss at the millimeter wave frequency band is severely high. To maintain reasonable coverage, medium or high gain millimeter wave antennas with beam steering capability are preferred in general. The conventional approach of using phase shifters to implement phased arrays is not recommended for commercial applications as millimeter wave phase shifters are very expensive and high in insertion loss. Instead, MIMO antenna system is believed to be the best solution for millimeter wave applications. In this project, we have successfully developed an innovative high performance antenna and array for millimeter wave communication systems.

119611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
119611.value: Innovation is identified as one of the six strategic areas that Hong Kong should be well positioned with so as to integrate with the Chinese economy and compete globally. A research and innovation social network (e.g. http://scholarmate.com) has been developed by the project investigator and his team to promote innovation resource sharing and collaboration among governments, industries, universities and research institutions in Hong Kong and mainland China. However it is an extremely challenging task to recommend suitable experts for research and innovation activities in a research and innovation social network environment. Currently content-based, collaborative and hybrid approaches have been used for making recommendations, but they ignore the vitally important human interactions in social network environments. This project aims to develop a hybrid method for profile-based recommendation in research and innovation social networks. Profiles of individuals, organizations and objects will be generated based on the integration of subjective information (e.g. user-self claimed research areas), the objective information (e.g. research areas as generated from his/her publications and projects) and social information (e.g. tagged information contributed from online friends and groups). These profiles can then be used to classify and cluster the expertise of researchers, and to make recommendations based on the matching of profiles among individuals or objects (e.g. proposals, patents and question answers). The proposed methods can be implemented and used to facilitate the interaction and collaboration among governments, industries, universities and research institutions in Hong Kong, the mainland China and rest of the world, it is to enhance the effectiveness of collaboration in research and innovation social networks. 由于与中国大陆的经济联系越来越紧密，香港特区政府将创新列为重点发展的六大领域之一。在过去的几年中，我们开发了科研社区网络（科研之友，http://scholarmate.com）, 并且将它用于官、产、学、研之间资源共享和人员合作的桥梁。可是，如何为科研人员推荐他们想要的服务是急待解决的问题。目前的解决方法主要基于内容的分析与推荐，但对于社区网络中的活动考虑不周。 本项目将主要分析人们在创新活动中的行为特征提出问题和一种集成的解决方法。主要从主观信息（即用户自己提供的信息）、客观信息（如本人发表的科技论文和专利）以及社会化信息（如好友或群组成员对自己的评价信息）的集成角度来研究推荐的问题。提出的方法将不仅适合于人与人之间（如科研合作者）的推荐，同时也适合人与物之间（如为科研项目申请书推荐合适的评议人）的推荐应用。本项目的成果将提高香港与中国大陆官、产、学、研之间的信息共享与合作交流。

119611.label: Realisation of objectives
119611.value: We have reviewed the literature on recommendation systems for research and innovation activities. In particular, we find that traditional methods focus on one aspects of research relevance (e.g. content-based) or collaboration, but it lacks the integration from different aspects. Based on the comparative studies on the existing methods, we have proposed a new big data research analytic framework (RAF) for recommendation systems in research and innovation activities. The proposed RAF define research objects (e.g. researchers, projects, publications, and patents) from three aspects of Research Relevance, Research Quality and Collaboration, it uses a recommendation formula to compute the similarity degrees. The proposed methods and theories have been applied to practical recommendation applications for research and innovation activities, for example, 1) recommendation of academic articles to researchers (objects to people) ; 2) recommendation of PhD candidates to supervisors (people to people) and 3) assigning reviewers to research proposals (people to objects). Through various experiments, we have demonstrated that the methods and theories are useful and effective in recommendation applications.

119611.label: Major findings and research outcome
119611.value: In this project, we have proposed and defined the Research Analytic Framework (RAF) for recommendations in research and innovation applications. The proposed RAF framework consists of the three aspects, including Quality matrix, relevance matrix and connectivity matrix. Profiles of research entities (e.g. researchers, research projects, papers and patents) can be described using the Research Analytic Framework. For example, in reviewer assignment, peer reviewers’ profile can be described by: Quality of reviewers and principal investigators can be defined by no of refereed journal articles, SCI citations; Relevance can be specified by the subject disciplines and research keywords that are obtained from self claimed, projects and publications; Connectivity can be defined by the degree of connections including co-authors and project collaborators. After normalization of the quality, relevance and connectivity, the two objects' similarities can be computed by the geographic means of the three aspects.

119611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
119611.value: The project can be further developed in the following two areas: 1) to consider the information quality first before the recommendation decision, i.e. completeness, correctness and currency of the information should be taken into consideration when defining the quality, relevance and connectivity in the RAF framework; 2) fuzzy set theory can be applied to address the above issues when information is incomplete, and it is very important to consider the time factor when doing the recommendaions.

119611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
119611.value: Recommendations play an important role to facilitate the collaboration and information sharing in research and innovation activities. This project proposes a research analytic framework for recommendations in a research and innovation social network. It defines the profiles of research objects (e.g. researchers, research projects, publications and patents) in three dimensions of quality, relevance and connectivity. Mutual recommendations for a business purpose is based on the similarities of the profiles. The proposed research analytic framework has been used in the practical applications for recommendations in a research social network (i.e. www.ScholarMate.com) and in the reviewer assignment applications. Experiments based on the applications have shown to be effective.

120611.label: Project Objectives
120611.value: Quantify the relationships between film thickness, microstructure (grain size and distribution), stress, and amorphous volume fraction of two-phase nanocrystalline composite thin films on silicon and/or steel substrates fabricated by using unbalanced magnetron sputtering by systematically varying process parameters. Determine the stress distribution across the film thickness as well as the bonding strength in the interfacial region through nanoscale experiments (SEM, TEM/HRTEM, XPS, AFM, nanoindentation, etc.). Identify the onset of the geometric instability and material instability as a function of stress in the delamination process, with a focus on the effect of film thickness on the critical state. Thus, a better understanding could be achieved on the size effect with the proposed experiments. Investigate tensile behaviors and plastic deformation properties of nanocrystalline thin films or nanowires or nanotubes with various possible microstructures by molecular dynamics simulation. Microstructures of nanocomposite thin films comprising of nanocrystalline (nc) grains surrounded by amorphous matrix (a) will also be studied by using Monte Carlo simulation based on the modified Q-state Potts model. Formulate a MPM-based constitutive model via the grain structure of thin film, and calibrate the computational model with the freestanding thin film subject to pure tension and bending, respectively. Verify and improve the proposed model-based simulation procedure with experimental data, and investigate the interaction between geometric and material instabilities during the film delamination process.

120611.label: Realisation of objectives
120611.value: Through an international interdisciplinary effort involving material science, mechanics and computational science, the project four objectives have been successfully achieved by performing a combined analytical, experimental and numerical effort with multi-scale modeling and simulation. Firstly, the relationships between film thickness, microstructure (grain size and distribution), stress, and amorphous volume fraction of two-phase nanocrystalline composite thin films on silicon substrates fabricated by using unbalanced magnetron sputtering were quantified by systematically varying process parameters. Secondly, the stress distributions across the film thickness as well as the bonding strength in the interfacial region were determined through nanoscale experiments (SEM, TEM/HRTEM, XPS, AFM, nanoindentation, etc.). Identify the onset of the geometric instability and material instability as a function of stress in the delamination process, with a focus on the effect of film thickness on the critical state. Thus, a better understanding on the size effect with the proposed experiments was better understood. Thirdly, the mechanical properties including tensile behaviors and plastic deformation of nanocrystalline thin films or nanowires or nanotubes with various possible microstructures were modeled by molecular dynamics simulation. The typical achievements were reported in the top journals. (i) The tensile test on the self-healed GaAs NW showed that the tensile strength can reach 7.19 GPa. In comparison with the original strength of 9.27 GPa for the virgin nanowires, it was seen that 77.6% of its tensile strength was restored [EPL 98, 16010 (2012)]. (ii) Deformation of SiC nanowires with different stacking fault fractions was successfully calculated by molecular dynamics simulations. [EPL 110, 36002 (2015)]. (iii) Length-dependent brittle-to-ductile transition in GaAs nanowires was also calculated [Engineering Fracture Mechanics 50, 135-142 (2015)]. (iv) Deformation-induced phase transformation in 4H-SiC nano-pillars was found for the first time and also confirmed by molecular dynamics calculations [Acta Materialia 80, 392-399 (2014)]. In addition, microstructures of nanocomposite thin films comprising of nanocrystalline (nc) grains surrounded by amorphous matrix (a) were also studied by using Monte Carlo simulation based on the modified Q-state Potts model [Scripta Materialia 69, 662-665 (2013); 87, 33-36 (2014)]. Fourthly, the physics behind the strain-released buckling patterns including telephone cords and straightsided wrinkles with and without cracks, as experimentally observed in sputter-deposited Ti-Si-N thin films on Si substrates was investigated with model-based simulations by varying the mechanical properties of the interface. The interaction between geometric and material instabilities during the film delamination process was also investigated. Our calculations reveal that the location of the cracks depends on the normal stiffness, the interfacial toughness, and the normal strength of the cohesive interface. These properties determine the geometrical shape of the buckles such as width, wavelength, and deflection, and hence the local bending-induced tensile stresses. Buckling patterns with cracks at the apexes occur for low-stiffness interfaces as well as for high-stiffness interfaces with high toughness. On the other hand, cracks at the bottom of the buckles were more likely to occur for interfaces with high stiffness and low toughness. By using an elastic material model with a fracture criterion for brittle behavior, we found that the crack followed the path where the bending-induced principal stress exceeded the flexural strength of the film.

120611.label: Major findings and research outcome
120611.value: • Determined the stress distribution across the film thickness as well as the bonding strength in the interfacial region through nanoscale experiments (SEM, TEM/HRTEM, XPS, AFM, nanoindentation, etc.). • Identified the onset of the geometric instability and material instability as a function of stress in the delamination process, with a focus on the effect of film thickness on the critical state. • Achieved a better understanding on the size effect with the proposed experiments. • Investigated tensile behaviors and plastic deformation properties of nanocrystalline thin films (also nanowires and nano-pillars) with various possible microstructures by molecular dynamics simulation. • Studied microstructures of nanocomposite thin films comprising of nanocrystalline (nc) grains surrounded by amorphous matrix (a) by using Monte Carlo simulation based on the modified Q-state Potts model. After the completion of the project, 13 research papers have been published in the top SCI journals (4 A+ and 9 A articles).

120611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
120611.value: Through this project, our further research can verify and improve the proposed model-based simulation procedure with experimental data, and investigate the interaction between geometric and material instabilities during the film delamination process. As a result, a better understanding could be obtained on the failure mechanisms of thin film delamination from micro- to macro-scales.

120611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
120611.value: This international interdisciplinary research project involving physics, materials science, mechanics and computational science is to perform an integrated molecular and continuum study of thin films. A combined analytical, experimental and numerical effort have been made to explore the interaction between geometric instability (buckling) and material instability (decohesion), and to identify the transition from continuous to discontinuous failure modes of different discontinuities in the delamination of compressed solid thin films. As a result, a better understanding has been obtained on the failure mechanisms of thin film delamination from molecular to continuum level, which may yield an impact on designing and fabricating useful micro-devices under extreme conditions.

120811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
120811.value: 變電站、架空電力傳輸線等電力設備所產生的極低頻電磁場（ELF）對於人體健康的影響在近些年來成為備受關注的一個問題。為了預防極低頻電磁場對人體健康產生有害的效應，世界衛生組織、國際非電離輻射防護委員會和國際電機電子工程師學會都曾發佈過相關的準則來限定磁場輻射值的大小。電力設備工作頻率下輻射出的磁場強度建議值為100μT以下。 一般來說，架空高壓電力傳輸線會從發電廠一端接入高電壓，在超高層大樓中之變電站一端降至較低的電壓，並且增加電流值來滿足大樓中用戶的各種用電需求。架空電線產生的強電場曾被認為是一個安全威脅，而近些年在超高層大樓中有大量電流流過的電線所產生的磁場也成為了一個擔憂。 一座現代的超高層大樓所需要的電力大致相當於一座中等大小城鎮所需的電量， 通常可達高層大樓 所需的全部電力都在大樓內部進行上下傳遞，大樓內的辦公室距離與攜帶著數千安培電流的電線只有幾米的距離。在這種情況下，電流流過的導體呈並且豎直方向，與標準方向的電力架空傳輸線有所不同。我們提出的研究項目會對高層建築中工頻磁場輻射所帶來的影響進行深入探討，同時也會在對高層建築中豎直方向的電力傳輸線周圍產生的磁場測定過程中建立相應的人體模型。

120811.label: Major findings and research outcome
120811.value: A study on the magnetic field radiations to an axis-symmetric homogeneous numerical human body model implanted with a unipolar or bipolar cardiac pacemaker has been evaluated by FEM. Result have shown that the induced voltage of human body implanted with an unipolar pacemaker is much higher than that of human body implanted with a bipolar pacemaker. The results of the study have also indicated that the induced voltage of the pacemaker is highly dependent on the body orientations. In summary, pacemaker would induce a low voltage under power frequency exposure, both cable arrangements and human body orientations are also the important parameters on the induced voltage.

120811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
120811.value: In this project, we have looked into the impact of magnetic field radiations at power frequency inside high-rise buildings as well as related aspects to EMI on human safety. The study has consolidated much fundamental research information, based on the analysis and parametric modeling, on the levels of magnetic field radiations due to current carrying conductors. For further research in this topic, it is expected that a new GRF proposal shall be submitted in this topic for a more in depth investigation.

120911.label: Project Title(Chinese)
120911.value: 多維諧波恢復的先進信號處理研究

120911.label: Project Objectives
120911.value: To develop efficient algorithms for multidimensional parameter estimation of sinusoidal signals. Our starting point is to tackle the two-dimensional data models via exploiting the principal singular vectors of the corresponding data matrices. The parameter pairing issue, particularly when two or more frequencies in both dimensions have the same value, will be addressed. We will then extend our development to higher-dimensional sinusoids with the use of tensor algebra. Devise robust methods for joint estimation the number of harmonics and sinusoidal parameters when the former is unknown. Produce the theoretical performance measures, particularly biases and mean square errors of the parameter estimates, for the developed algorithms. Evaluate the devised multidimensional HR methods by comparing with the state-of-the-art schemes in terms of identifiability, estimation accuracy, threshold signal-to-noise ratio, computational complexity, and frequency resolution in different application scenarios.

120911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
120911.value: 在科學研究和工程應用中，諧波恢復是一個重要的課題。諧波恢復是從在噪聲中的正弦信號提取參數，而此正弦模型可以描述很多現實世界中的信號。在這個參數估計的問題中，一維是最常見的，但是多維的參數估計也有大量的應用，包括無線通信信道估計，核磁共振（NMR）光譜分析和多輸入多輸出（MIMO）雷達成像。例如，核磁共振光譜這個在食品和營養產業裏作為研究蛋白質的一個常用的工具，相關信號是可以看作為一個多維的衰減正弦波，其頻率和衰減因子對於蛋白質結構的分析非常重要。此外，MIMO雷達數據中的正弦參數包含了需要定位目標的位置信息。 類似於一維的諧波恢復，在多維的情況下，最關鍵的一步是估計衰減因子和頻率，因為它們都是非線性的。然而，多維的諧波恢復比一維的存在更多的問題。首先，準確的估計各維上的參數是非常困難的，特別是在某維度上存在相同頻率的時候。其次，處理多維數據需要巨大的運算量，因此算法的複雜性是一個非常重要的關注點。最後，雖然真實的數據是二維以上的，但是在現有的估計方法中，這些數據是被看作一列接一列的存儲在一個矩陣裏面的，因此這類方法不能充分利用到數據的結構而得出準確的估計。 本研究的目的是開發有更高準確性和更低複雜度的多維諧波恢復的方法。為了實現這個具有挑戰性的目標，我們提出以有效地利用適合於分析多維信號的多維張量這個代數模型，同時結合由接收到的數據計算出來的奇異向量和奇異值時，來得到最優的參數估計結果。還有，我們會將此方法延續到估計數據中的信號數量，和在信號數量未知的情況下的參數估計問題，同時也會對這些新的方法進行數學上的分析，和將其應用到不同的領域裏。

120911.label: Realisation of objectives
120911.value: For (1), we have devised a new subspace approach called principal-singular-vector utilization for modal analysis (PUMA) which can perform estimation in a fast and accurate manner. The PUMA technique is first utilized for the two-dimensional (2-D) harmonic retrieval problem. The developed algorithm can work well even when there are identical frequencies in one of the two dimensions. It is shown that our method is superior to the state-of-the-art schemes in terms of estimation accuracy and computational complexity. With the use of tensor algebra, we have successfully extended the PUMA methodology to R-D harmonic retrieval where R>2. Apart from the PUMA approach, we have devised a more computationally attractive harmonic retrieval approach which is based on correlation. Moreover, an effective prewhitening technique has been devised for multidimensional harmonic retrieval in colored noise environments. For (2), via the introduction of the multi-mode matrix unfolding, we have devised a new source enumeration approach for the scenario where the number of harmonics is unknown a priori. Based on the estimated tone number, we can then use the developed estimation methods for harmonic retrieval. On the other hand, we have derived a nonparametric subspace scheme based on the iterative adaptive approach (IAA) to achieve joint harmonic number and sinusoidal parameter estimation simultaneously. For (3), bias and mean square error analysis has been performed on the developed algorithms. The theoretical calculations have been validated by computer simulations. For (4), we have compared our proposed methods with the state-of-the-art algorithms in different aspects. In summary, our proposals at least outperform them in terms of accuracy and/or computational complexity. Furthermore, with the use of subspace methodology, we have designed an accurate attitude estimation algorithm for unmanned aerial vehicles.

120911.label: Major findings and research outcome
120911.value: We have devised a new subspace approach called principal-singular-vector utilization for modal analysis (PUMA) which can perform estimation in a fast and accurate manner. The PUMA technique is first utilized for the two-dimensional (2-D) harmonic retrieval problem [8-3]. The developed algorithm can work well even when there are identical frequencies in one of the two dimensions. It is shown that our method is superior to the state-of-the-art schemes in terms of estimation accuracy and computational complexity. With the use of tensor algebra, we have successfully extended the PUMA methodology to R-D harmonic retrieval where R>2 [8-2]. In particular, the bias and mean square error analysis is examined for the single tone case. Apart from the PUMA approach, we have devised a more computationally attractive R-D harmonic retrieval approach which is based on correlation [8-1]. By exploiting the Kronecker correlation structure of the colored noise, we have derived an effective prewhitening technique for multidimensional harmonic retrieval [8-4]. Based on subspace methodology, we have designed an accurate attitude estimation algorithm for unmanned aerial vehicles [8-5]. Moreover, a novel tensor-based technique [8-6] has been devised for joint symbol and channel estimation in space-time-frequency wireless communication systems. On the other hand, via the introduction of the multi-mode matrix unfolding, we have devised a new source enumeration approach for the scenario where the number of harmonics is unknown a priori [9-1].

120911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
120911.value: In this project, we mainly focus on the algorithm development and analysis of the general multidimensional harmonic retrieval models. A future work is to extend our study to specific signal models in different real-world applications. Apart from dealing with multidimensional data, it is of considerable interest to perform harmonic retrieval in a multiple-channel setting. Development of effective algorithms for finding the harmonic number using advanced source enumeration methods, prior to performing parameter estimation, is also a promising research direction.

120911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
120911.value: The problem of harmonic retrieval (HR) is to extract the parameters from noisy sinusoids, which has been an important topic in science and engineering because many real-world signals can be well described by the sinusoidal model. Although one-dimensional (1-D) HR is the most common, multidimensional HR in fact has numerous applications such as wireless communication channel estimation, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar imaging. For example, the measurements in NMR spectroscopy which is a powerful technique for protein research in food and nutritional industries, can be modeled as a sum of multidimensional damped sinusoids where the frequencies and damping factors are crucial to determining the protein structures. Moreover, the sinusoidal parameters of the MIMO radar data contain the position information of multiple targets of interest. In this research, multidimensional HR approaches, which are efficient in both aspects of accuracy and complexity, are derived and analyzed via the exploitation of advanced signal processing techniques and tensor algebra. It is expected that our produced research results will be able to contribute to the advancement of multidimensional HR algorithms and applications, and provide a significant value in the field of statistical signal processing.

122011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
122011.value: Ropes and cables are widely used to hoist or support heavy objects. They must bear heavy loads during operation, but repeated loading and unloading make them prone to fatigue. The saline and humid environment of Hong Kong escalates the wear on ropes and cables, which can lead to their sudden breakage. For instance, rope accidents have caused hoist lifts to suddenly plunge to the ground, resulting in human casualties. The structure of ropes is complex, as they are formed by many twisted and inter-locked wires. Currently, lift maintenance still mainly depends on human visual inspection, which is obviously unable to detect sub-surface defects in ropes and cables. Other existing inspection techniques suffer from shortcomings such as difficulty in installing the sensors, and often generate inaccurate results. There is thus an urgent need for a well-designed sensor that is easy to install and provides accurate detection results for sub-surface defects in ropes and cables. Recently, ultrasonic guided waves have become popular due to their long-range inspection ability and high degree of sensitivity in detecting defects. Magnetostrictive sensors (MsS) are promising guided wave technology applications because they are non-contact and can cover long distances during inspection. Conventional MsS are made from hard coils. This means that each sensor is tailor-made to fit a particular diameter of rope/cable, and must be mounted to a rope/cable that has a free end. We propose an innovative MsS that is made of flexible printed coil (FPC) to replace the conventional hard-coil MsS. The FPC-based MsS is flexible, and can form any cylindrical shape to fit different diameters of rope/cable, and can be mounted onto a rope/cable without a free end. Most importantly, the FPC-based MsS can be wrapped around itself to form multiple layers of coil, which substantially increases the excited wave energy. A major problem that must be overcome is the dispersion effect of guided waves, which inevitably introduces a high level of complexity into the process of detecting rope defects. This effect becomes more severe with the complexity of the structure of the rope/cable under inspection. We propose an innovative optimization scheme embedded with an effective algorithm to adjust the operating parameters of the FPC-based MsS and its excited guided wave. Our FPC-based MsS can excite guided wave that has a minimal dispersion effect and contains high wave energy, which significantly increases its accuracy in defect detection. 鋼絲繩和鋼纜廣泛應用於提升或支持重型物體。它們在操作過程中需要承受重荷，而反復加載卸載使得這些纜繩易疲勞受損。香港的環境潮濕且鹽分高，這會使得纜繩損傷加劇，並進一步導致突然斷纜。而在鋼絲繩事故中電梯可能突然墜地，造成人員傷亡。纜繩由多股線繩扭合在一起，因此結構比較復雜。目前電梯纜繩的維護主要依靠肉眼檢測，很顯然這種方法不能發現纜繩內部缺陷。其它現有的檢測方法都或多或少存在缺點，例如傳感器安裝困難，檢測結果不準確等。因此，急需設計一種新型傳感器可以安裝簡便並能提供纜繩內部缺陷的準確檢測。 超聲導波目前被廣為關註，這項技術不僅具有檢測距離長的特點，而且檢測缺陷的敏感性高。磁致伸縮傳感器(MsS)是一種極有發展前景的超聲導波傳感器，因為它可提供無接觸檢測。傳統的磁致伸縮傳感器由硬線制成，必須通過纜繩的自由端才能安裝到位。在本項目中，我們設計了一種新型磁致伸縮傳感器，該傳感器采用柔性印制線圈(FPC)制成。這種新型FPC磁致伸縮傳感器應用靈活，可直接安裝到纜繩上，而無需借助纜繩自由端，而且它可改變配置以配合不同尺寸的纜繩使用。尤為重要的是，FPC磁致伸縮傳感器可卷成多層使用，這樣可大大提高激勵能量。檢測中需要特別註意的問題是導波在纜繩中頻散的影響，因為這毫無疑問會增加檢測缺陷的復雜性與難度。而纜繩的結構越復雜，頻散的影響也就越大。因此在本項目中，我們提出了一個優化方案以及相應算法以調整FPC磁致伸縮傳感器和激勵信號的相關參數。我們所設計的FPC磁致伸縮傳感器可產生高能量低頻散的超聲信號，從而大大提高纜繩缺陷檢測的準確性。

122011.label: Realisation of objectives
122011.value: Objective 1 has been achieved 100%. A new type of flexible printed coil (FPC)-based magnetostrictive sensors (MsS) (hereinafter named FPC-MsS) for cable/rope defect inspection was designed. To verify its capability, several experiments were conducted by using normal and partially broken ropes. In these experiments, a rope that had increasing number of broken wires was tested. The results showed that the amplitude of reflected guided wave signal generated at each defect location begins to grow proportionally when the number of broken wires increased. To facilitate the proper mounting of FPC-MsS on cables/ropes, a special segmented mounting device was designed. Both the designs of the FPC-MsS and its mounting device are found to be suitable for the common in-service lift ropes and has a high level of sensitivity in detecting defects. Objective 2 has been achieved 100%. Several effective algorithms for generating appropriate dispersion curves for different type of complex ropes were developed. These algorithms include the morphogram, blind fault component separation algorithm, enhanced ensemble empirical mode decomposition, adaptive wavelet stripping algorithm, and optimal wavelet filter that were designed by the PI and his research team. These algorithms could separate overlapped guided waves and reveal the dimension parameters of various types of defects after the process of signal separation. Further, the energy dispersion curves for guided waves traveling along ropes were derived via the help of simulation. Hence, the characteristics of the energy dispersion curve for each type of rope can be determined, especially for twisted lift ropes that have helical structures. With the helps from the identified dispersion curve and effective algorithms, the dimensions property of each type of defect can be evaluated. Hence, the severity of damage caused by each defect to the rope can be known prior to final broken of the entire rope. Objective 3 has been achieved 100%. By observing the results generated by simulation and real experiments, we developed several methods to optimize the performance of FPC-MsS. The optimization methods include the use of sparse representation to find the proper center frequency for emitting the desired guided wave, the avoidance of notch frequency range, the proper arrangement and distribution of magnetic fields for the sensors etc. By using these methods, the performance of FPC-MsS has been enhanced. Hence, the defects embedded in the reflected guide wave signals can easier to be revealed.

122011.label: Major findings and research outcome
122011.value: As aforementioned, a new FPC-MsS for cable/rope defect inspection was successfully implemented. Although conventional Piezoelectric Transducers (PZT) generates stronger guided waves to detect rope defects than that of FPC-MsS, it is not convenient to mount PZT on the rope surface as it needed a tight contact with the tested rope. From the experimental results, they proved that the FPC-MsS and its mounting device could be easily mounted on a lift rope and effective in inspecting the integrity of cables/ropes. We also found that if a defect in the rope has a cross-sectional area higher than 2.6% (4 broken wires) of the total area (152 wires), then the defect signals starts to be observed by FPC-MsS. The amplitude of signal increase when the number of broken wire is increasing. Hence, the FPC-MsS is sensitive to the severity of rope defect. Moreover, a transduction system was developed that is tailor-made for the inspection of lift rope with applied loads. Various effective algorithms were developed to separate the overlapped guided embedded in the overall reflected wave signals and then reveal the dimension parameters of each type of defect. After knowing the dimensions of the defect, the severity of damage caused to the rope can be evaluated. For optimizing the parameters of the emitted guided wave, the sparse representation was applied to determine the optimal center frequency of the emitted guided wave that is tailor-made for a particular type of rope/cable. The required value of center frequency can be obtained by adjusting the values of the FPC-MsS circuitry. From the dispersion curves, we found that for helical structures, such as steel strands and wire ropes, there is a notch frequency range. In this frequency range, a portion of guided waves frequency spectrum will disappear as a result of applied tensile load to the rope. Hence, the desired center frequency should not be located in this notch frequency range. It is a well-known that the bias (static) magnetic field has an important role in MsS’s performance. The static magnetic field of MsS is usually provided by permanent magnet bars. For the common size of lift ropes used in Hong Kong, we found that the optimal number of magnetic bars should be distributed at 90 around the inspected ropes. By using these optimization methods, the performance of FPC-MsS has been enhanced. Besides, this project leads to the publications of 15 SCI-indexed journals and 9 conference papers.

122011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
122011.value: When using FPC-MsS to inspect life ropes, they must be stable or not moving. However, in reality, most of the lift cables are moving during operation. In this proposal, we stated that the tested rope should stop moving so that the sensors can be applied to the rope’s surface and performed the necessary inspection. Nonetheless, such practice is time consuming. Currently, we are proposing the use of non-touching sensor by using laser to create the required guided wave modes. The laser beam, after smart modification, can be made from a spot beam to grid type of beams with its wavelength matching to that of the desired guided wave mode. If it is successful, the laser-based guided wave can replace all mounted sensors. However, such research work is seldom reported. Hence, a lot of foundation research must be done. In future, we will focus our research effort to design such laser-based guided wave sensor to generate the desired guided wave modes. For future action, we will submit a new proposal to the Research Grant Council. The research work is focused on developing the laser-based and non-touching new transducers to generate the required guided wave modes for inspecting moving ropes and cables.

122011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
122011.value: Ropes and cables must bear heavy loads during operation, but repeated loading and unloading make them prone to fatigue. Rope accidents have caused hoist lifts to suddenly plunge to the ground, resulting in human casualties. Currently, lift maintenance mainly depends on human visual inspection, which is obviously unable to detect sub-surface defects in lift ropes. A new technique called Guided Waves (GW) has become popular due to its long-range inspection ability and highly sensitive in detecting defects. Magnetostrictive Sensors (MsS) are promising sensor to emit GW for rope/cable inspection. We developed an innovative MsS made of flexible printed coil (FPC-MsS). It is flexible, can form any cylindrical shape to fit different diameters of rope/cable, and can be mounted onto a rope/cable easily. We also developed optimization methods to smartly adjust the operating parameters of FPC-MsS so that it can emit GW with minimal energy dispersion but contain high wave energy that can significantly enhance its accuracy in defect detection. Because of the success in generating useful research outcomes, it attracted 13 newspapers/bulletins and even TVB news to report the outcomes. The principal investigator was also invited by several professional organizations to present 12 keynote speeches on the project outcomes.
