142911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
142911.value: Recent economic theory and empirical evidence all point to the importance of political institutions in shaping policymakers' incentives and policy outcomes. This literature has particularly focused on majoritarian institutions, in which a policy choice is made once a majority of legislators votes for it. In reality, however, it is common in democratic democracy that minorities are allowed, or at least not legally forbidden, to take obstructive actions aiming to delay or block the vote on the policy reforms that are in favor of the majority. Throughout the twentieth century there were notorious filibusters in the U.S. Senate that successfully and substantially delayed the passage of some civil rights acts. Since the democratization of Taiwan in the late 80s, its congress has also been characterized by occasional physical clashes, normally initiated by the minority party, to stop the vote or discussion on certain bills. Minority rights in the form of filibusters or other similar obstructive behaviors have played critical roles in democratic policymaking. Yet there are still few economic theories, if any, that attempt to study the economic effects of minority rights in a democratic institution. This proposed research project is aimed to bridge this gap. In particular, an analytical framework based on dynamic games is being developed to model legislative institutions that incorporate both majority rules and minority rights. Such modeling framework will host positive theories that explain how the occurrence, frequency and duration of filibusters are determined by the specific institutional arrangements, preference polarization, heterogeneity of party members, the strength of the majority party, congressional workload and patience of the legislators. Such analysis will also provide theoretical foundations that guide rigorous empirical studies of filibusters and measurements of the related variables. Findings from this proposed project are also expected to shed lights on constitutional reforms in old democracies as well as the constitutional design for countries/regions, such as Hong Kong, that are in transition to democracy. 截至目前為止，關於民主國家立法程序和政策制定的理論文獻，都是假設任何議事提案只要能取得國會都數議員同意即可通過。但是在許多民主國家(比方說美國參議院)的議事規則允許少數持反對意見的議員用冗長演說等方式來杯葛議事進行，進而達到阻擋多數人支持的議案進入表決。在這個研究計劃當中，我擴充既有的分析立法程序的賽局理論模型，同時放入多數決與允許少數人杯葛這兩種制度，來嚴謹分析杯葛制度對於政策制定的效率、時效與福利分配會造成什麼影響。這樣的分析結果，可以用來比較不同立法程序制度的利弊得失。

142911.label: Realisation of objectives
142911.value: 1) I develop a tractable model in which the majority party has the authority to propose and enact a bill whereas the minority party can filibuster to stop the passage of the bill. This model hosts rich results, allowing us to understand the interaction between majority rules and minority rights. 2) I characterize the subgame perfect equilibrium of the model and offer a positive theory of filibusters. See Section 6.1 of this report for the details of my theory. 3) My analysis of comparative statistics suggests several testable implications, which will have the potential to guide future empirical studies on filibusters. 4) My findings indicate that allowing filibusters has the effect to redistribute benefits from the majority to the minority. Such insight will help us think about the reform of real-life legislative reforms.

142911.label: Major findings and research outcome
142911.value: 1) I construct a dynamic model of filibusters with complete information and characterize the subgame perfect equilibrium of the model. 2) I demonstrate that, even though payoff functions are common knowledge, filibusters may be initiated and can persist for a long time. Explanation: opponents of a measure filibuster not to block the bill perpetually, but only to delay the passage of the measure so that they can benefit from the status quo for a longer period. At the same time, expecting such incentives from the opponents, the majority may still prefer to propose this measure, as it is still profitable to incur the costs of filibusters and reap the benefits of a new policy outcome in a later date. 3) I identify the following trade offs. Assuming sufficient preference polarization between the majority and the minority, I show that as the majority proposes a policy that is more favorable to itself, the longer the filibusters would last. Therefore, upon making a policy proposal, the majority in fact trades off a more favorable policy and a more speedy passage of the policy it proposes. 4) I prove the following insight mathematically. Even if a filibuster does not occur, the possibility of filibusters would make a substantial impact on the policy choice. This is because the majority may want to make substantial compromise in its policy proposal to avoid the delay of the bill. 5) I derive the following comparative statics. The duration of filibusters is weakly decreasing in the majority's filibuster costs and weakly increasing in the majority's patience. On the other hand, it is ambiguous how the duration of filibusters is affected by the minority's filibuster costs and patience.

142911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
142911.value: 1) The current model is stylized and abstract, and it does not refer to any specific policy issue. We can apply the modeling technique developed here to understand specific anecdotes of filibuster. 2) The comparative statics derived in my theory can be brought data, for example, the U.S. congressional data, for empirical tests. 3) The current model does not address to normative questions, i.e., it does offer welfare analysis and its comparison. The current model has the potential to be extended for the study of welfare implications of filibusters.

142911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
142911.value: Recent economic theory and empirical evidence all point to the importance of political institutions in shaping policymakers' incentives and policy outcomes. This literature has particularly focused on majoritarian institutions, in which policies are made by majority rules. In reality, however, it is common in democratic democracy that minorities are allowed, or at least not legally forbidden, to take obstructive actions aiming to delay or block the vote on the policy reforms that are in favor of the majority. Various filibusters have occurred, for example, in the U.S. Senate and the Legislature in Taiwan. Yet there are still few economic theories that attempt to study the economic effects of minority rights in a democratic institution. This project is aimed to bridge this gap. In particular, an analytical framework based on dynamic games is developed to model legislative institutions that incorporate both majority rules and minority rights. Such modeling framework explains why filibusters happen, and how frequency and duration of filibusters are determined by the specific institutional arrangements, preference polarization, heterogeneity of party members, the strength of the majority party, congressional workload and patience of the legislators.

143011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
143011.value: The experiences, attitudes and aspirations of Hong Kong`s younger generations have become increasingly prominent academic, policy and popular concerns. In the transition from dependence to independence, from school to work, from childhood to adulthood, housing plays a pivotal role. Access to affordable and satisfactory accommodation affects patterns of departure from the parental home, household formation, marriage rates, fertility rates and has broader impacts on intergenerational relations and the social structure. Differential patterns of access to housing can also create divisions and differences in terms of lifestyles, living standards and general life chances within the younger generations. These issues have strong international resonance as young people face more challenges in housing and labour markets across the world. This project will explore these issues in the context of Hong Kong but set within this broader international context. The project will employ a mixed methodology of secondary analysis of census data with social survey and focus groups to examine housing circumstances, expectations and constraints among different groups within the 18-35 age range. 房屋與香港八十後世代：心態，诉求與發展軌跡 Housing and Hong Kong's Post-80s Generation: Attitudes, Aspirations and Future Trajectories 香港《八十後世代》的經歷，心態與訴求成為最近熱門話題和社會關注，他們從依賴到自立的過程中，無論在就學到就業或從孩童到成人，房屋都起著重要的作用。能夠獲取滿意和能力所能負擔的住所，對年輕人脫離家庭自立，結婚率，家庭形成，出生率的形態以至世代關係及社會結構等，都有廣泛的影響。從不同途徑獲取房屋也會對年青一代的生活方式，生活水平以及一般的生命機遇，產生分化與差異。香港年青一代在高樓價，超擠逼居住空間，漫長教育期，高度竟爭勞動市場及收入和財富分配嚴重不平均的背景下進入成年期，而年青人面對房屋與就業的挑戰等問題，在國際間亦有相當回響。本研究希望以國際大環境作為研究背景，探討與分析這些問題在香港的成因與發展。香港年青一代的住屋情況及對房屋的期望，對社會穩定與和諧有著長遠的策略影響。他們也有相當重要的政策含義，這在2010-11施政報告中房屋對重要的重視可見一斑。但香港在這方面缺乏系統的研究，本研究正好作為補充。本研究尤其關注有關香港與國際對房屋的政策和學術討論，並希望對【八十後世代】的學術辯論作出貢獻。

143011.label: Realisation of objectives
143011.value: The project addressed successfully all the objectives. An edited book was completed including two chapters from the PI and Co-I which contributed substantially to Objectives 1 and 5. Further outputs included four working papers available on the Urban Research Group website, papers in the Journal of Youth Studies and Urban Studies and papers at international conferences and workshops in Taiwan, Amsterdam,Korea and Yokahama. Further journal articles/ book chapters are in preparation from the working papers and analysis of qualitative interviews. The cohort paper using census data has been delayed for minor technical reasons. The original research design had anticipated major difficulties in contacting young people on landlines and considered that mobile phones would be the necessary and expensive route. In practice, however, this proved not to be the case. The rationale was explained fully in the last annual report. Two landline telephone surveys of young people were undertaken instead. A total of 2023 interviews were achieved. It should be noted that the change in survey strategy significantly reduced fieldwork costs and is the reason for the project underspend. Addressing objectives 2-4 also required more in depth work to explore different subgroups of young people. A total of 45 in depth interviews were undertaken spread across: • Those who had applied for public rental housing • Those living away from home • Those staying with their parents • Those who had moved away and then returned for a variety of reasons. Two focus groups were also held with two groups of young Mainland Professionals living in Hong Kong. The project also set out to actively engage with local debates about housing and youth policy in Hong Kong (objective 6) and youth issues came very much to the fore in late 2014 with the Occupy movement. Indeed, housing was mentioned as an important element of youth dissatisfaction. The team met this objective in numerous ways: Prof Yip met with youth volunteers of HK Federation of Youth Groups;a copy of our book on Young People and Housing was sent to the Secretary of Housing and duly acknowledged; two Press releases were produced;Yip appeared on the documentary for the TVB Newsmagazine on the 17 Jan 2015 with the title "Where would young people live? ;Forrest and Yip also wrote an article for the South China Morning Post for Insight page on January 7th, titled What Young People Really Think About Housing; the research was featured in Youth Hong Kong (Dec 2013). .

143011.label: Major findings and research outcome
143011.value: The findings from this project can be differentiated between more conceptually oriented aspects of the research and the more specific, empirical findings of particular relevance to Hong Kong. The research sought to engage with broader theoretical debates in relation to youth transition as well as offer insights into the housing situation of young people in Hong Kong which would be locally and policy relevant. With regard to the broader objectives, the edited book and the Urban Studies and Journal of Youth Studies articles explored inter alia the conceptual robustness of the idea of a 'post eighties generation', the nature of contemporary youth transition and offered a cautionary, and culturally nuanced, understanding of the importance of housing in this transition. Both the broader conceptual work and the more Hong Kong specific findings reinforced the view that housing costs are merely one, albeit important, factor in the equation. The changing behaviour of young people in the housing market also reflects shifting social norms and priorities. Changing labour market conditions and the rising costs and longer duration of education are also very important. These and other factors coalesce in different ways and with varying impacts for different groups of young people. With regard to Hong Kong and more generally, the research indicates that differences within cohorts are as important as differences between cohorts. For example, and significantly, the ability of parents to offer financial assistance to their children with regard to housing has grown in importance as the costs of home purchase have increased. In relation to Hong Kong, many of the more specific findings have been disseminated via working papers, press releases and other popular media. Two findings can be highlighted. First, almost 80 per cent of our respondents were living with their parents or other relatives and 12 per cent were living with their partner. Very few lived alone. In sharp contrast with many other societies, hardly anyone was sharing with friends-or wished to do so. Second, apparently contradicting the idea of a more individualistic youth, the vast majority said they liked living with and looking after their parents. They also liked to be looked after. However, the research also cautions against painting too rosy a picture of family relationships. Among those living away from home, almost a third refer to ‘a lot of disagreements’ when they lived with parents and 40 per cent say they wanted a ‘different kind of lifestyle’.

143011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
143011.value: The housing situation of young people is high on the political agenda in Hong Kong and internationally. The PI and Co-I are continuing to work on housing affordability issues for young people and have extended their research to encompass debates around 'generation rent' and 'generational fractures'. A PPR proposal on housing access and mobility has been submitted and is currently under consideration.The PI is also in the process of co-authoring a book, The Commodified City (Macmillan) which will be focusing on the shifting housing prospects for different generations in the post war period. It will make considerable use of (and acknowledge) the data collected on this research project. The PI is also developing international research on young people and housing with a colleague at the University of Amsterdam-the theme Solo City-again with a book prospect in mind. The edited book from this research (Forrest/Yip) and the associated papers have provided a strong platform for further collaborations and given the PIs a high international profile in wider debates about young people in contemporary society.

143011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
143011.value: The cost of housing presents a major challenge for young people seeking adult independence in Hong Kong. As in many societies,young people are staying at home longer, marrying later and having children (if at all) later. There are thus complex interactions between the housing market and the transition to adulthood. This project explored the attitudes, experiences and expectations of young people (18-35) in Hong Kong. A variety of methods were used including analysis of waves of the census, two telephone surveys of over 2000 young people and in depth interviews with specific groups of young people. The research suggests that many young people are pessimistic about their prospects of owning a home. However, the data also show that the majority are not unhappy about living with their parents-at least well into their young adulthood. Young people would appear to value the financial and other advantages of living at home and many also like looking after their parents. Few would appear to feel trapped although most regard marriage/starting a family as incompatible with living with parents.Thus, the research suggests that frustration with housing prospects will increase as this generation ages-unless access to independent housing for young people is made easier.

143411.label: Project Objectives
143411.value: Provide an overview of the unique features of Chinese firms going public process. Discuss the political connection of Chinese underwriters and its potential role in helping the client firms in the IPO process. Analyze the potential value of the underwriters’ political connection in two aspects: 1) whether it can help the underwriters gain more market share; 2) whether it can allow the underwriters to charge a fee premium for their underwriting businesses. 143411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
143411.value: Political connections are considered to be pervasive around the world and play an important role in economic life, especially in emerging markets with less developed legal systems, more government interventions, and weak investor protection (e.g., Claessens et al. 2008; Fan et al. 2007; and Faccio 2006 etc.). Prior studies mainly investigate the implications of firms’ political connections for their economic behaviors and performance in various aspects, including access to bank loans, terms of borrowings, bailout events, long term performance, and market values etc (e.g., Fisman 2001; Faccio et al. 2006; and Ferguson and Voth 2008 etc.). In this research project, we attempt to explore political connection of financial intermediaries and its economic consequences by focusing on the role of underwriters’ political connection in Chinese IPO market. China presents itself as an ideal experimental field to examine this important issue since Chinese government imposed many restrictions on the IPO process and firms need to obtain approval from Chinese Securities Regulation Committee (CSRC thereafter) to go public. Bountiful anecdotal evidence suggests that political connection of underwriters’ has a significant impact on the approval process of IPOs. We thus plan to utilize this setting to address the following research questions: 1) whether the likelihood of IPO application being approved is greater for IPOs underwritten by politically connected underwriters; 2) whether politically connected underwriters experience superior market share growth; 3) whether the politically connected underwriters enjoy a fee premium for their underwriting businesses; 4) what is the impact of underwriters’ political connection on the underpricing of IPOs; 5) whether information risk of IPO firms underwritten by politically connected underwriters is greater; 6) whether the post IPO performance is poorer for firms underwritten by politically connected underwriters. The empirical findings would shed light on the role of financial intermediaries’ political connection in capital market, as well as its implications for the overall economy. It thus adds to the growing literature on the value of political connections. Our study also contributes to the extensive underwriters’ literature on underwriting fees, underpricing, and post-IPO performance etc., comparing the importance of political connection vs. professionalism in securities markets with strong government intervention. In addition, our study would generate important insights on the process of Chinese firms going public to enhance our understanding of the unique features of the China’s securities market. 政治联系在全世界普遍存在并且在经济生活中扮演着重要角色，尤其是在法律体系不发达完善，有较多政府干预，以及投资者保护较弱的新兴市场当中 (e.g., Claessens et al. 2008; Fan et al. 2007; and Faccio 2006 etc.)。早前这方面的研究主要着重于考察公司的政治联系对于其经济行为和业绩的不同层面的影响，包括对获取银行贷款，贷款的条款，政府的救援，长期的业绩表现，以及市场价值等方面 (e.g., Fisman 2001 ; Faccio et al. 2006 ; and Ferguson and Voth 2008 etc.)。 我们在本研究项目中将着重通过分析承销商的政治联系在中国IPO市场中的作用来探究金融中介政治联系及其经济后果。中国政府通过证监会的审批机制在IPO过程中实行诸多限制，这使得中国市场成为研究这项重要问题的理想试验场。丰富的观察证据显示承销商的政治联系在IPO审批过程中具有重要作用。我们因此计划通过这一个背景环境解决以下的研究问题：1）由具有政治联系的承销商所承销的IPO申请是否具有更高的通过概率？2）有政治联系的承销商是否经历更快速的市场份额增长？3）有政治联系的承销商是否可以收取更高的IPO承销费用？4）承销商的政治联系如何影响公司IPO的发行抑价？5）由具有政治联系的承销商所承销的IPO公司是否存在更高的信息风险？6）由具有政治联系的承销商所承销的IPO公司在上市后的业绩是否相对差一些？关于这些问题的发现将让我们对金融中介的政治联系在资本市场中的作用及其对整体经济的含义有深层次的认识。本项目将对政治联系方面的文献做出积极贡献，也将通过对比政治联系和专业性在政府干预较强的证券市场中的重要性对关于承销商在承销费用，IPO 抑价， IPO 后的业绩等方面的文献有所贡献。 另外，本研究项目也将让我们对中国公司上市过程有透彻的认识并更深化对中国证券市场特征的理解和把握。

143411.label: Realisation of objectives
143411.value: The main objectives of this research project have been achieved. We acquired a good understanding of the Chinese capital market and incentives of Chinese firms to go IPOs. We obtained substantial institutional knowledge about the IPO approval process in China, specifically as regards to how political connection of the Chinese underwriters may play a role in helping their client firms in the IPO process. We hand collected the political connection (PC) status of the underwriters (our main test variable), as well as the PC status of the auditors, and that of the client firms as important control variables. Empirical tests allow us to document important evidence showing that PC of underwriters can help client firms to obtain IPO approval, allow them to charge premium underwriting fees and client firms of PC underwriters experience post-IPO underperformance.

143411.label: Major findings and research outcome
143411.value: Using a sample of Chinese IPO applicants from 2006 to 2009, we document that the probability of obtaining IPO approval from the regulator is much higher for deals underwritten by politically connected (PC) investment banks. This result is robust after we control for a number of other variables that may affect the approval decision. We also control for the TOP10 status of the underwriters as a proxy for their reputation. However, the estimated coefficient on the TOP10 variable is never statistically significant, implying that the political connections are more important than professional reputation in the IPO approval process. Our empirical results show that the PC underwriters charge premium underwriting fees over their clients as compensation for their political capital. We also find that the IPO firms underwritten by PC investment banks underperform those underwritten by non-politically connected (non-PC) investment banks in the post-IPO period. The post-IPO (up to two years after IPO) stock performance is also significantly lower and the change in accounting performance considerably worse for the client firms of PC underwriters. Overall, this evidence suggests that PC underwriters help inferior companies gain access to the equity capital markets by using their political resources to handle bureaucratic regulation and supervision, which defies the professionalism requirement of financial intermediaries. We also find that the clients of PC underwriters are more likely to change the use of proceeds proposed in an IPO prospectus and engage in less efficient investments. Further analyses show that the IPO underpricing does not exhibit significant differences between the clients of PC and those of non-connected underwriters, implying that minority investors cannot price protect themselves. We submitted our paper generated from this research project to multiple top journals including Review of Financial Studies, Management Science, Journal of Finance and Quantitative Analysis and Journal of Business and Finance. We received a rather positive R&R from Journal of Business and Finance and we are currently revising the paper for resubmission.

143411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
143411.value: Given that China is shifting towards the new IPO registration system, we may explore how other forms of social networks may affect the IPO process. For example, we are planning to collect the hometown information for the IPO sponsors and identify the hometown effect in the IPO underwriting process.

143411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
143411.value: This study contributes to the literature in the following ways. First, it expands the limited literature on the value of relationship (political connection in particular) to financial intermediaries with evidence obtained from the Chinese IPO market, which can also be generalized to apply to other relationship-based economies. We show that professionalism gives way to political connection in China’s IPO market. In the long run, it may impose a direct threat to the healthy development of market institutions. Second, our study extends the literature on political connection by shedding light on the role that financial intermediaries’ political connections play in capital markets, along with its implications for the overall economy. We offer additional evidence to the literature on political rent seeking by documenting how the benefits of political capital are enjoyed by underwriters and their clients at the expense of minority shareholders’ interests. Third, findings from our study add to the rich literature on IPO underpricing, underwriters’ professionalism and reputation effect, post-IPO performance, the use of IPO proceeds, post-IPO investment efficiency and the role of underwriters in general. Finally, our study generates important insights into the IPO process of Chinese firms and expands our knowledge of the unique features of China’s security markets.

143611.label: Project Objectives
143611.value: How many of these cases are there in the five locations? How do the plaintiffs organize protests in housing-demolition litigation? What claims and languages do they employ? What responses and patterns do the courts and the state display in dealing with this type of litigation in the five locations? More importantly, what variations are disclosed? What are the underlying reasons behind these variations? Specifically, to what extent does the bottom-up perspective help us understand the dynamics of conflict and evolution of rule of law in China? What conditions allow the courts to bring about social change? The law and development movement has emphasized judicial reforms and judicial independence as necessary for economic growth, poverty reduction, the protection of human rights, social justice, and the consolidation of democracy. Judicial independence has long been regarded as essential for establishing the rule of law in transitional countries (Carothers 1998). Yet the debate on how it should be understood has never been settled (Shapiro 1981; Rodrick 2003; He 2004; Upham 2003; Ginsburg and Mustafa 2008; Peerenboom 2010). The findings of this Project will thus also help in exploring theoretical questions such as: Why does the role of courts vary in different countries? What is the proper role of the judiciary at this stage of development? Should transitional countries follow the ideal model of an independent third-party adjudicator as drawn from the developed countries, or must their role be context-specific? Is the global trend toward judicialization social and economic disputes advisable in low and middle income countries where institutions, including the courts, are weak to provide adequate remedies to socio-economic claims? In general, law and development and rule of law promotion efforts have emphasized prescriptive “international best practices” based on the institutions, laws, rules, practices and values currently found in economically advanced countries primarily in Euro- America. Yet even the most cursory of historical overviews demonstrates that institutions, regulations, practices and values have evolved over time in these countries, and that the advancement of social and economic rights has been a protracted and ongoing struggle. Together with our previous projects looking at courts and disputes resolution from various angles, this Project, by examining the politically charged housing demolition cases from a bottom-up perspective, will shed light on hotly contested current debates regarding whether there is a single model of development, whether universal standards for socio-economic rights are possible and desirable given differences in levels of development. Answers to these questions will not only generate meaningful policy recommendations for reforms to China’s property rights, civil rights, and other aspects of the legal system, including the long-term institutionalization of social protest, but also provide a solid basis for broader theoretical debates about the relationship between the court, the state, and society, and specifically about law and development, the evolution of rule of law and judicial independence in authoritarian states such as China.

143611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
143611.value: Housing demolition has been a major source of social conflicts in contemporary China. The current literature has primarily focused on the defective procedure in the demolishing process and residents’ resistance outside the courtroom. Consequently, little is known about how affected residents integrate collective energy into litigation and the changes of the court and other state institutions in responding to such conflicts. This Project aims to expand our preliminary research on protest-supported litigation in housing demolition to five locations with representative profiles of different levels of economic development, state resources and political ideology. Through systematically and empirically examining how the plaintiffs organize themselves and how local courts and related state institutions respond to them in these places, this Project will document variations of the case numbers and outcomes, state responses, identify their respective characteristics, and explore their underlying causes. The findings of this Project will shed light on how litigation is politicized, how legal strategies are innovated, and the evolution of rule of law in China from a bottom-up perspective. They will also shed light on the evolving relationship between state and society in China, the challenges and opportunities for political reform, including increased public participation and political accountability, and the evolution of rule of law including judicial independence in authoritarian countries such as China. 房屋拆迁是当代中国产生社会冲突的重要源头。已有的研究很少触及法庭内的抗争。本项目将扩大初步的研究至经济发展水平、国家资源和意识形态均不同的五个地区。通过系统地考察法院的有关诉讼，本项目将记录案件结果、国家反应以及相关的原因。本项目的发现将从下至上的角度探究中国法制是如何政治化的。同时也将对国家和社会的关系、政治改革的可能性和挑战提出洞见。

143611.label: Major findings and research outcome
143611.value: Housing demolition has been one of the major sources of social conflict in contem- porary China. Drawing on evidence collected in fieldwork investigations, this article examines the pressure of protest-supported housing demolition litigation and its impacts. It finds that under the pressure of litigation, the courts have devised coping mechanisms to constrain the housing demolition authorities, and that social change angling toward more transparency and accountability has occurred. The project finds that this change is made possible as the maintenance of social stability has become not only the paramount concern of the regime, but also the performance assessment criterion for local officials and judges. The findings deepen our understanding of the causes and consequences of judicial empow- erment in China and shed light on the dynamics of judicial politics in other regimes.

143711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
143711.value: 最近几年越来越多的公司意识到他们可以在供应链管理上合作以大幅度提高表现。有报告称运输公司们通过整合他们的小量及频繁的货物可以显著减少它们的运输及库存费用。库存共享也是一种减少备用库存和提升顾客服务的有效方式。通过共享他们的库存，这些公司可以减少经常在生产，采购及运输中产生的联合准备成本。特别来说，联合补货问题也就是决定有共同准备费用时的补货策略问题，在供应链管理领域中是一个已经被研究的很透彻的问题。但是，不同的公司之间的合作意向经常取决于一个对大家都有利的公平的分配费用或收入的机制。在实践中很多人面临的一个最大的障碍就是如何使各方同意合作。我们希望研究如何在零售商之间公平分配系统费用以促进合作。一个合适的分配机制在零售商分属不同的机构或同一机构的不同分支时尤其重要。所以此情况下合作博弈论是研究费用分配事宜的一个自然的选择。有一类特殊的合作博弈被称为次模博弈，在此博弈中自然存在一类公平的分配机制，更重要的是此机制（PMAS）保证每人都会得益于任何的新人加入。我们本项目的第一个主要目标就是建立合作联合补货博弈的次模性。 从另一方面来说，某些公司只愿意共享与联合准备成本相关的信息，而不愿意公开公司的私人信息。在基于公开信息的联合准备成本分配规则被确定后，公司们一般都以自己的利益出发来独自行动。所以在这种情况下非合作博弈模型是一个很自然的选择。但是这种模型下决策变量和目标函数往往是非连续的所以我们不能使用常用的Nash均衡的存在性定理。对于非连续非合作博弈，Nash均衡点的存在性往往取决于博弈的次模性。次模性能保证博弈存在最好及最差均衡点，而且这两个均衡点均可以通过一个非常简单的最优反馈机制得到。所以建立非合作联合补货博弈的次模性是我们的第二个主要目标。 另外值得注意的是，我们研究中使用的一个主要方法--多矩阵类优化在优化理论及应用上有着相当的影响。在此项目我们将会致力于建立多矩阵类优化方面的一些结构性的结果及其应用。

144411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
144411.value: The proposed research aims to provide systematic evidence on the relation between “excessive” analyst coverage and stock price crash risk. Investors regard analysts’ research reports as a primary source of firm-specific information and researchers find that analyst research reports have a direct effect on stock prices. Previous research also suggests that security analysts reduce informational asymmetries between managers and investors. As such, high analyst coverage should lead to a greater amount of private information disseminated to investors. Consequently, such securities with large analyst coverage should be more transparent. However, this view of security analysts’ roles does not take into consideration a possible link between excessive analyst coverage and crash risk. To the extent that analysts have an effect on stock prices and analyst coverage is influenced by analysts’ economic incentives, analyst coverage of a particular stock may become excessive with expectations of potential investment banking relations. Security analysts may compel stocks to trade above fundamental values by issuing excessively optimistic earnings forecasts. Markets heavily penalize firms for missing analysts’ forecasts by a penny. Higher share prices could provide higher managerial compensation or discourage takeovers. Thus, managers have incentives to overstate firm performance to meet or beat the analysts’ optimistic expectations by withholding bad news. Managers stockpile negative information until its accumulation reaches a tipping point. Once managers’ incentives for bad news hoarding fail, accumulated bad news will be suddenly released all at once. As a result, stock price crashes occur. As such, excessive analyst coverage has the potential to exacerbate price crash risk. The primary research objective is to test the hypothesis that excessive analyst coverage reinforces the likelihood of future crash occurrences rather mitigate it. In addition, the proposed research also aims to provide evidence on whether the adverse effect of excessive analyst coverage on the likelihood of future crash occurrences is attenuated by the extent of product market competition. Given the dearth of evidence on the issue, the proposed research intends to provide the possible link between excessive analyst coverage and price crashes. We attempt to provide evidence that excessive analyst coverage is responsible for future crash occurrences. 本项研究旨在为“过度的”分析师追踪（analyst coverage）与股价暴跌风险（stock price crash risk）之间的关系提供系统的证据。投资者认为证券分析师研究报告是公司特有信息的主要来源，而研究者也发现分析师研究报告对股价有直接影响。以前的研究指出证券分析师可以降低经理与投资者之间的信息不对称。就其本身而论，较高的分析师追踪应会将较大数量的私有信息传播给投资者。因此，分析师追踪程度大的证券会更加透明。 然而，以上有关证券分析师角色的观点没有考虑到过度的分析师追踪与股价暴跌风险之间可能存在的联系。由于分析师对股价有影响而且分析师的追踪会受到其经济动机的影响，怀有建立或维持与投资银行关系的分析师会对某一特定股票过度追踪。通过发布过于乐观的盈余预测，证券分析师可以促使股票以高于基础价值的价格被交易。以前的研究表明市场会惩罚与分析师预测相差哪怕仅一分钱的公司。另一方面，高股价可以给经理带来高薪或者阻止公司兼并。这样，经理就有动机为了达到或超过分析师的乐观预期而通过隐瞒坏消息夸大公司绩效。经理堆积负面信息是有临界点的。一旦经理隐瞒坏消息的动机不复存在，所有堆积起来的坏消息就会一次性的被披露出来。股价暴跌就这样发生了。因此，过度的分析师追踪有可能大大提高股价暴跌的风险。该研究的主要目的是检验如下假设：分析师过度追踪增大了未来股价暴跌发生的可能性。该研究的另一目的是为分析师过度跟踪对未来股价暴跌发生可能性的影响是否会随着产品市场竞争的激烈程度而减弱这一问题提供证据。 鉴于以上问题缺乏经验证据，本项研究力图建立分析师过度追踪与股价暴跌之间可能存在的联系。我们将尝试为分析师过度追踪对未来股价暴跌的发生负有责任这一论点提供证据。

144411.label: Realisation of objectives
144411.value: We have achieved the first project objective by empirically documenting that excessive analyst coverage increases the likelihood of future crash occurrences. To our best knowledge, this is the first study providing empirical evidence that excessive analyst coverage is responsible for the occurrence of crash risk. Analysts are conventionally viewed as information intermediary to reduce informational asymmetries between managers and outside shareholders. However, this conventional view of security analysts’ roles does not take into consideration the possibility of dysfunctional excessive analyst coverage creating information frictions, due to their economic incentives reinforced by the excessive concentration of analyst coverage. We have also achieved the second objective by finding that the adverse effect of excessive analyst coverage on crash risk is mitigated by product market competition and institutional ownership.

144411.label: Major findings and research outcome
144411.value: We find that excessive analyst coverage increases the likelihood of future crash occurrences. We also find that the adverse effect of excessive analyst coverage on future crash risks is exacerbated by opaqueness, but mitigated by product market competition and institutional ownership. Our findings are generally consistent with the notion that excessive analyst coverage is responsible for future crash occurrences, opaque information aggravates this dysfunctional analyst coverage, and product market competition and institutional ownership attenuate the counterproductive influence of excessive analyst coverage on crash risk.

144411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
144411.value: Our research can be further developed by aligning firm-level crash risk to more specific analyst economic incentives including management relation, investment banking, reputation incentives.

144411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
144411.value: This study tests the hypothesis that overly concentrated analyst coverage exacerbates price crash risk. We provide evidence that excessive analyst coverage is responsible for crash risk through the dysfunctional analysts’ roles fueled by too much concentrated analyst coverage. This study also provides evidence consistent with the notion that the adverse effect of excessive analyst coverage on the likelihood of future crash occurrences is exacerbated by the extent of opacity. Further, we document that product market competition and institutional ownership attenuates the counterproductive influence of excessive analyst coverage on crash risk. Given the dearth of evidence on the issue, the study contributes to analyst research and capital market research by providing the possible link between excessive analyst coverage and price crashes. This link is also related to the transparency of financial statements and the market competition a firm is operating in. The evidence is generally consistent with the notion that excessive analyst coverage is responsible for future crash occurrences.

144511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
144511.value: Of late, issues surrounding offshore firms, in particular, the complex and opaque nature of offshore operations, have received much attention from the global investment community, international organizations such as the OECD and the IMF, securities regulators, tax authorities, legislators, and other public policymakers. However, little has been known about the causes and consequences of offshore operations. To this end, the proposed research aims to provides useful insight into important aspects of offshore operations, namely their impacts on the delayed recognition of bad news as losses and stock price crash risk. In so doing, the proposed research focuses on the asymmetric disclosure incentives of offshore firms with respect to bad versus good news, namely offshore firms' incentives to withhold bad news and to accelerate the release of good news. Specifically, we investigates two distinct, but related, questions: Our first objective is to investigate whether and how the asymmetric disclosure incentives lead to the delayed recognition of bad news as a loss and the accelerated recognition of good news as a gain. Our second objective is to examine an important, but not yet explored, aspect of the stock market consequence of offshore operations, namely the impact of offshore operations on stock price crashes. The asymmetric disclosure, in particular, the bad news hoarding, allows offshore firms to accumulate bad news within the firm. However, there is an upper limit to bad news hoarding. When the accumulated amount of hidden bad news crosses this limit, as manifested in the Enron debacle, the firms are forced to release bad news to outside investors all at once, which causes a large and abrupt decline in stock prices, or stock price crashes. Further, the hiding of bad news deters outside investors and the board of directors from discerning bad projects and exercising their abandonment options at an early stage. As a result, the bad outcomes of negative NPV projects accumulate over time, which, anew, increases the likelihood of crash occurrences. One can therefore predict that offshore firms are more prone to experience stock price crashes than non-offshore firms. Given the lack of empirical evidence on the above issues, the proposed research could provide public policy makers, tax authorities and/or securities regulators with potentially useful insights into the dark sides of offshore operations, namely aggressive reporting and high crash risk. 最近，有關離岸公司的問題特別是離岸業務的複雜性與不透明性引起了國際投資界、經濟合作與發展組織（OECD）和國際貨幣基金組織（IMF）等國際組織、證券監管者、稅務機關、立法者以及其他公共政策決策人的廣泛關注。然而，離岸業務的起因和影響仍鮮為人知。為此，該項研究旨在深入探討離岸業務的重要方面——離岸業務對壞消息在會計盈餘中的延遲確認及股價暴跌風險的影響。該項研究的中心是離岸公司不對稱地披露壞消息與好消息的動機，即他們隱瞞壞消息並且加速發佈好消息的動機。具體來說，我們將研究以下兩個不同但高度相關的問題。第一，我們將研究非對稱資訊披露的動機是否會導致會計盈餘對壞消息的延遲確認和對好消息的加速確認；如果確實如此，我們將進一步研究非對稱資訊披露的動機是如何導致延遲損失確認和加速利得確認的。 第二，我們將研究離岸業務對股市的一個重要的卻未經探索的影響——離岸業務對股價暴跌的影響。非對稱披露尤其是隱瞞壞消息會使離岸公司的壞消息累積起來。然而，壞消息的堆積是有上限的。當被隱藏和累積起來的壞消息超過一定限度的時候，公司將不得不向外部投資者一次性地公佈所有壞消息。如此大量的壞消息會導致股價突然大幅下跌，即“股價暴跌”（stock price crashes）。美國安然公司（Enron）的崩塌正是這一論點的例證。另外，壞消息的隱瞞會妨礙外部投資者和董事會覺察不良投資專案並在專案早期行使放棄期權（abandonment options）。這會導致具有負淨現值（NPV）的投資項目的不良後果逐漸累積起來，就又提高了股價暴跌的可能性。因此，可以預期的是，離岸公司比非離岸公司更有可能經歷股價暴跌。 鑒於上述問題缺乏經驗證據，該項研究可以就離岸業務的黑暗面即樂觀高估財務報告和較高的股價暴跌風險為公共政策決策人、稅務機關以及證券監管者提供有用的見解。

144511.label: Major findings and research outcome
144511.value: This GRF project brings about three papers: The first paper (attached with this report) focuses mainly on whether and how offshore operations by multinational firms affect firm-specific information flows, and whether their motives for tax avoidance engender financial reporting opacity which is known to be a main source of stock price crashes. The second paper (attached with this report) focuses mainly on multinational firms with dual class ownership structure. Dual-class ownership structure is known to create divergence between cash flow and voting rights, thereby creating high agency costs as well as financial reporting obfuscation or opacity. In this paper, we investigate whether and how this ownership-control divergence leads eventually to bad news hoarding and thus increases stock price crash risk. The third paper (attached with this report) develop a new measure of stock price crash, that ex ante expected crash risk perceived by investors in the option market, and implied by the Black-Scholes option pricing model. In this innovative paper, we show that financial reporting opacity indeed increases Options Implied Volatility (IV) Smirk which is the difference between Out of Money Put Ooptions IV minus At the Money Call Option IV.

144511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
144511.value: I am currently extending the basic ideas of this GRF funded project to examine: (1) whether financial reporting comparability increases or decreases Ex Ante Expected Crash Risk measured b y Options Implied IV Smirk; and (2) whether and how analysts' role of external monitoring and infortmation dissemination influence Ex Ante Stock Price Risk. Prelimiary results shows that comparability decrease crash risk and analyst monitoring also decreases crash risk.

144511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
144511.value: Multinational firms' offshore operations, often motivated by tax avoidance, create managerial incentives to obfuscate financial reporting, particularly, incentives for bad news hoarding. This bad news hoarding behavior eventually increase the likelihood that a firm experiences an abrupt, large scale drop in stock prices, which is called stock price crashes. Our research further shows that stock price crash risk is positively associated with the divergence between cash flow and voting right rights. Finally, we also show that investors in the option market correctly anticipate the adverse consequences of financial reporting opacity on stock price crash risk, and take protective actions by allocating more resources to put options than to call options they they are faced with financial reporting opacity of the underlying stock.

145111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
145111.value: 身体适宜是人们康乐幸福的关键，它不仅影响人们的日常生活习惯而且影响工作效率。 身体健康适宜意味着一个人有更多的精力，更能适应在艰苦条件下长时间的工作；所以，身体健康适宜在改进个人工作效率方面起到关键作用。但不幸的是，由于在传统健身环境中缺乏“行动暗示”，所以员工经常缺乏在工作场所进行体育锻炼的动机。 根据健康信念模型、自主理论和计划行为理论，“行动暗示”是激发个人参与健康活动（如健身）的触发器。有影响力的暗示能使个人动机由外在驱使转为内在能力，形成自主动机，从而直接决定具体活动实施与健身愉悦感。 本项目使用设计科学方法开发和评价虚拟健身教练系统，该系统能够提供有影响力的“行动暗示”来激发个人自主动机，促使个人参与每天三到四分钟的办公室健身活动 ，从而改进他们的工作效率。 本项目提出的虚拟健身教练系统，将计算机视为“社会角色”，弥补了现有系统缺乏人性化因素的不足。新的设计属性具体体现在虚拟教练的外表形象和沟通风格。基于相似吸引理论和领导力文献，虚拟教练人物形象和个人偏好越吻合，采用更多的变革性交流风格，则个人自主动机就越强，参与和坚持虚拟教练推荐的健身活动的可能性就越大。所以，通过提升员工动机，虚拟健身教练系统能够改进员工的康乐水平和工作效率。 本课题拟采用纵向现场实验，辅以问卷、访谈和观察等研究方法评价提出的新系统。对新的设计属性的合理性评价，将贡献于人际交互研究与实践；组织对虚拟健身教练系统的接受水平评价，将贡献于人力资源管理和健康管理研究与实践。

145111.label: Realisation of objectives
145111.value: Our two objectives have been achieved. To achieve our first objective related to the design and implementation of the Virtual fitness Trainer (VT) system for improving work productivity in office-based environment, we did a study on the preliminary evaluation on sampled existing VT applications based on the American College of Sports Medicine (ACSM) guidelines for exercise professionals, and theories of social support and persuasive technology. According to the results of this study, we then designed and implemented the VT system with human-like factors which are missing from existing VT applications, e.g. VT avatars of specific profiles and appearance that allowed the users to select to be their VTs based on their own preferences. Also, we developed the SMS reminding module of the VT system with two human leadership styles: transformational versus transactional. Also, the VT avatars could generate different tone of voice and spoken content/script. The development was done with strong collaboration with my Co-I from the Chinese University of Hong Kong. To achieve our second objective related to the evaluation of the effects of the VT system on individual’s self-determined motivation, health behaviors and work productivity, we did our first full scale experiment to pilot run and test the use of VT system in a local company “Chine Light and Power Limited”. Although there were problems in the pilot run as reported in the last progress report, we further revised our system according to the results of this pilot run, and the system was then ready for its formal evaluation in the later stage of the project. Finally, we did the second interesting full scale experiment in a University campus. Based on the subjects’ choice of fitness avatars, we divided the subjects (staff and students) into four treatment groups according to the two different setting of the SMS reminder style (transformational vs transactional) and similarity (high vs low) of selected VT avatar with users. Also, the subjects were encouraged to perform simple office/classroom fitness exercises by following the VT’s suggestion and the subjects’ own choices for a period of eight weeks. The fitness exercises consisted of cardio-respiratory endurance, muscular strength, and flexibility. The experiment was completed successfully, and we had done the data collection and analysis. Our results indicated that our hypotheses were mostly supported. Overall, we have one conference paper published, one journal article under review in a reputable journal, and one working paper drafted.

145111.label: Major findings and research outcome
145111.value: For the first objective, we did a preliminary evaluation on sampled existing VT applications based on the ACSM guidelines for exercise professionals, and theories of social support and persuasive technology. Results indicated the sampled VT applications mainly covered the stages 2 (Pre-exercise evaluation and exercise prescription) and 3 (Program monitoring) of the ACSM-based training workflow. But, the average scores of the sampled VT applications in social support and persuasiveness were relatively low. To fill in the gap, we then designed and implemented our VT system with the focus on the stage 1 (Pre-participation assessment) and 4 (Program evaluation) of the ACSM-based training workflow, and designed the VT avatars with specific profiles and appearance, and the SMS reminders with specific leadership styles, in order to enhance the social support and persuasiveness of the VT system. For the second objective, we have conducted two full scale experiments, one in a local company and one in a University campus. Following our experimental design, we have successfully collected data from 108 subjects, in terms of their self-determined motivation, health behaviors and work productivity before and after our 8-week experiment. Data were analyzed using ANOVA (using SPSS 17) and PLS (using SmartPLS 2.0). In general, our results indicated that our hypotheses were mostly supported. Regarding the hypothesis set 1, our PLS path analysis shows that VT similarity has statistically significant relationship with self-efficacy (Table 25 in our attached working paper). Also, from our ANOVA results, we have found that the High VT similarity group shows a higher level of self-efficacy when compared with the Low VT similarity group (Table 19 in our working paper). An interesting result shows that there is a statistically negative relationship between motivation and work performance, and an interaction effect on work performance by behavioral and VT similarity (Table 35 in our attached working paper). Regarding the hypothesis set 2, our PLS path analysis shows a statistical significant relationship between VT similarity and self-determined motivation in the transactional style reminder group, while there is no statistical support to the same relationship in the transformational style reminder group (Tables 36 and 37 in our attached working paper). Regarding the research outcome, for the objective 1, we have one conference paper published, and one journal article under review in a reputable journal. For the objective 2, we have finished a working paper with high potential to be published in a top-tier journal.

145111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
145111.value: Although the findings of our experiments are mostly positive, there are two major limitations of the VT system that are all related to the self-reporting of exercise records by the users. The first limitation of the current VT system is that the self-reporting mechanism is not convenient. Although the SMS reminders are sent to the mobile phones of the users, they have to self-report their exercise records using a computer, but not their mobile phones. In fact, there is quite a good number of subjects requesting for a mobile app version of the VT system so that they can self-report their exercise records easily and timely. Therefore, there is a need to develop a mobile app of our VT system. The second limitation of the current VT system is that the self-reported exercise records of the users may not be accurate so that the VT system can provide appropriate feedback to users. There is a need to develop a device that can detect actual exercise engagement of the users, and automatically upload the exercise records to the VT system via telecommunication technologies like Bluetooth using the mobile phones of the users. Such device has both academic and commercial value.

145111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
145111.value: In general, this project has developed and evaluated a Virtual fitness Trainer (VT) system that is able to motivate users to participate in health behavior in the form of three to four minutes of office-based fitness activities, in order to contribute to improvement in their productivity at work. Firstly, we have developed the VT system with human-like factors, e.g. VT avatars (with specific profiles and appearance) and SMS reminders (with specific human leadership styles), which are missing from existing VT systems. We hypothesize that the more similarity there is between the VT avatar’s appearance and individuals’ preference, and the more transformational the SMS reminders, the more self-motivated, participative in health behavior and productive at work the users will be. To evaluate the proposed VT system, this project has conducted two full scale experiments, one in a local company and one in a University campus, and successfully collected data before and after our 8-week experiments. Our results indicated that our hypotheses are mostly supported. The findings are expected to provide significant implications to health management research and practices. Overall, this project has one conference paper published, one journal article under review in a reputable journal, and one working paper drafted.

145311.label: Project Title(Chinese)
145311.value: 貨幣政策和利率期限結構的連續時間DSGE模型：理論與估計

145311.label: Co - Investigator(s)
145311.value: Prof Li, Haitao Prof Yu, Cindy

145311.label: Project Objectives
145311.value: The main objectives of the current project are (i) to develop a tractable continuous-time regime-switching DSGE model with rich term structure implications, and (ii) to estimate the model based on Treasury bond yields using Bayesian MCMC methods. Our modeling choices are mainly motivated by Li, Li, and Yu (2010) who document distinctive regimes in US monetary policy in the past 50 years. They show that the Fed is proactive in controlling inflation in one regime but is accommodative for growth in another. The regime-dependent monetary policy significantly improves the explanatory power of macro variables for government bond yields. Without the regimes, inflation and output can explain less than 50% of the variations of contemporaneous bond yields. With the regimes, the two variables can explain more than 80% of the variations of contemporaneous bond yields. They also show that macro variables are more stable under the proactive monetary policy, which therefore could have contributed to the “Great Moderation.” Our regime-switching DSGE model captures important new empirical facts documented in Li, Li, and Yu (2010) and at the same time endogenizes the pricing kernel and the dynamics of the macro variables in a general equilibrium setting. Though term structure in existing DSGE models tend to be either too simple to fit the data or too complicated to solve, our continuous-time model generates rich term structure dynamics and yet is highly tractable. We introduce preference shocks, which can be better identified using the full term structure data, and study their implications for monetary policy, pricing kernel, and the term structure. We also investigate the impacts of monetary policy on macro variables such as inflation and real output. This is possible because the term structure data enable us to identify the past monetary policy more precisely. Our framework allows us to address the question of whether monetary policy has contributed to the “Great Moderation,” an issue that is difficult to resolve under the “reduced-form” model of Li, Li, and Yu (2010).

145311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
145311.value: In this project, we first develop a continuous-time New Keynesian, dynamic stochastic general equilibrium (DSGE) model with regime-switching monetary policy. Compared to existing DSGE models, our model provides a rich and yet tractable characterization of the term structure of interest rates using continuous-time techniques. We then provide a rigorous estimation of the model based on the Treasury yield curve using Bayesian MCMC methods. Our project contributes to both the macroeconomic literature on monetary policy and the finance literature on term structure. The New Keynesian DSGE models have become the dominant approach used by both academics and central bankers around the world for monetary policy analysis (see, e.g., Gali and Gertler (2007)). Under the sticky price equilibrium of these models, monetary policy is not neutral and has important impacts on the real activities of the economy and direct implications for the term structure. However, the existing macroeconomic literature on DSGE models has mainly focused on the real activities and ignored the term structure implications. Since the yield curve contains market expectations for future economic activities, we can better identify monetary policy by incorporating term structure data in the estimation of DSGE models. The term structure also provides an alternative perspective to examine potential shortcomings of these models: If the DSGE models make counter factual predictions on term structure dynamics, then one should be careful in using them for policy analysis. While traditional term structure models in finance have relied on latent variables to explain bond yields, the fast growing macro term structure literature (e.g., Ang and Piazzesi (2003)) typically introduces macro variables into term structure models using the no-arbitrage Taylor (1993) rule approach. Recently, Li, Li, and Yu (2010) document regime-switching Taylor rules and stable macro variables under the aggressive inflation control regime for the US economy. Without a well specified DSGE model, however, it is not clear that the exogenously specified pricing kernels in these “reduced-form” models are consistent with general equilibrium. It is also difficult to identify any causal relations between monetary policy and the volatility of the macro variables despite the apparent correlations between the two. Our regime-switching DSGE model captures important new empirical facts documented in Li, Li, and Yu (2010). By endogenizing the dynamics of the macro variables, it allows us to answer fundamental questions such as whether monetary policy has contributed to the “Great Moderation.” 在這個項目中，我們首先建立一個連續時間的新凱恩斯主義，動態隨機一般均衡（DSGE）模型與體制轉換的貨幣政策。相比現有的DSGE模型，我們的模型使用連續時間的技術提供了豐富利率期限結構的特性。然後，我們提供一對國債收益率曲線的基礎上嚴格估算模型使用貝葉斯 MCMC方法。我們的項目有助於雙方就宏觀經濟文獻貨幣政策和財政上的期限結構的文獻。 新凱恩斯主義的DSGE模型已經成為主導方式的同時使用 學者和央行行長對貨幣政策的分析（見，例如世界各地， Gali and Gertler （2007））。根據這些模型的粘性價格均衡，貨幣 政策是不是中立的，對經濟的實際活動中的重要影響，並 對於期限結構產生直接影響。但是，現行的宏觀經濟 在DSGE模型的文獻主要集中在實際活動，忽視 期限結構的影響。由於市場預期收益率曲線包含了 未來的經濟活動中，我們可以更好地識別，納入長期貨幣政策 在DSGE模型估計結構的數據。期限結構還提供了一個 另類的視角來審視這些模型潛在的缺點：如果DSGE 就期限結構模型的動態反事實的預言，那麼我們應 在政策分析中小心使用这些模型。 雖然傳統的財務期限結構模型都依賴向潛變量 解釋債券收益率，快速增長的宏觀期限結構的文獻（例如，Ang和 Piazzesi（2003））通常引入期限結構模型的宏變量使用 無套利泰勒（1993）规则的方法。近来，Li, Li, and Yu （2010）发现 體制轉換下的积极的通貨膨脹泰勒規則和穩定的宏觀變量 控制制度的美國經濟。沒有一個良好规范的DSGE模型，它是難以確定因果關係的任何 在貨幣政策和宏觀變量，儘管明顯波動 兩者之間的相關性。我們的體制轉換DSGE模型捕獲重要 新的經驗事實。通過内化動態 宏觀變量，它使我們能夠回答的基本問題，如是否 貨幣政策是導致“大穩定”。

145511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
145511.value: The recent financial tsunami has highlighted the needs of more active management of credit portfolios. In many financial institutions, the measurement of portfolio credit risk has been a standard practice. However, risk measurement is only a first step towards active risk management. For purposes such as evaluating the risk of a subportfolio and optimizing the portfolio, one also needs to know how to decompose the total credit risk into a sum of risk contributions for individual transactions or counterparties. These risk contributions can then be used to allocate capital. Typically, value-at-risk is often used as a risk measure for credit portfolios, and it can be decomposed into a sum of risk contributions for individual transactions or counterparties. For most commonly used models, there are no closed-form formulas available for the calculation of risk contributions, and hence one needs to resort to numerical methods, among which Monte Carlo simulation is the most commonly used one. However, simulating risk contributions is computationally challenging. The major challenge is that risk contributions are expectations conditional on rare events, which makes it difficult to estimate them by using crude Monte Carlo estimators. To the best of our knowledge, current methods in the literature on simulating risk contributions mainly focused on the use of importance sampling (IS), a well-known simulation technique, to reduce the variances of the estimators. IS was used to twist the probability measure such that there would be more samples dropping in the domain of the rare event. However, theoretically these methods may not achieve the fastest convergence rates, and empirically it has been documented that their computational results are not yet satisfactory. This project aims to develop efficient methods for simulating risk contributions. The main idea is to use IS in a very different way so that all the samples generated will drop in the domain of the rare event. By doing so, we expect that the proposed method can achieve the fastest convergence rate. Hopefully it will perform better than the available methods in the literature, both theoretically and empirically. Although the method is proposed under the context of capital allocation for credit portfolios, it may also be useful in some other important applications, including fixed-income portfolio selection problem, and the measurement of systemic risk of financial systems. Incorporating the proposed method into these two applications will also be an important part of the project. 最近的金融海啸在某种程度上强调了金融业对更加主动灵活的信贷资产组合管理的迫切需求。在很多金融机构中，信贷资产组合的风险度量已经被广泛应用。然而，风险度量只是管理信贷资产组合风险的第一步。如果需要评估某一部分资产的风险或者最优化整个资产组合，人们就需要知道如何把整个资产组合的风险分解为单独的交易或者单独的债务人的风险。这些风险贡献(risk contribution)可以被用于分配资本。 风险值(Value-at-Risk)通常被用于度量信贷资产组合的风险。它可以被分解成单独债务人的风险贡献的总和。对大部分常用的模型，计算风险贡献的显式表达式并不存在，因而人们需要用数值方法去估算风险贡献。在这些数值方法中，蒙特卡洛模拟方法被广泛应用。然而，模拟风险贡献在计算上非常困难。最大的困难在于风险贡献是稀有事件上的条件期望，因而通常的蒙特卡洛估计量偏差非常大。 据我们所知，已有文献上面关于模拟风险贡献的方法主要是通过应用重要抽样方法来降低估计量的方差。重要抽样方法通过改变概率空间使得更多样本落在稀有事件附近。然而，理论上这些方法都难以达到最快的收敛速度。而且实验观察显示这些方法的计算结果还有很大的改进空间。 这个项目的主要目的在于设计用于计算风险贡献的更有效方法。核心的想法在于通过另外一种方式的重要抽样方法使得在模拟中稀有事件百分之百出现。我们预期这种方法所构造的估计量能获得最快的收敛速度。此外，我们预期本项目所提出的方法，不管在理论上还是实验计算上，都优于现有的方法。 虽然本项目提出的方法主要用于解决信贷资产组合的资本分配问题，它同样也有其他的重要应用，包括固定收益资产组合的选择，以及金融系统风险的度量。本项目的另外一个重要课题是如何把所提出的方法用于解决上述问题。

145511.label: Realisation of objectives
145511.value: We have achieved the project objectives. In particular, we have developed an importance sampling (IS) method for simulating risk contributions for credit portfolios, which leads to unbiased estimators of risk contributions. The problem being tackled is a challenging one, because the risk contributions are indeed conditional expectations given a probability-zero event. In other words, crude simulation estimators would be extremely inefficient. The proposed methodology resolves this problem by developing a state-dependent IS scheme in a way that it ensures all observations generated will be within the probability-zero event. By doing this we improve the simulation efficiency dramatically, and the resulting estimators perform much better than existing ones. Theoretically, the new estimators have faster rates of convergence, compared to existing ones. We further use the cross-entropy method to further improve the efficiency of the IS estimators. The proposed methodology has provided a way to simulate the gradients of a fixed-income portfolio optimization problem, which can be easily plugged in some gradient-based optimization tools for finding the optimal fixed-income portfolio. Another application of the methodology is on the use of risk contributions to quantify the contributions of individual banks to the overall risk of the banking system. It turns out when defaults of entities within a banking network are modeled as Bernoulli random variables under conditional-independence framework, the proposed methodology can be applied. However, recently there has been criticism on the conditional-independence framework, especially due to its inability to capture the contagion effect of defaults within the banking network. Development and simulation analysis of models to capture the contagion effect is beyond the scope of the current project, and is left as a topic for future research.

145511.label: Major findings and research outcome
145511.value: In this project, we work with the widely used conditional-independence models for credit portfolios and provide a new methodology for estimating the risk contributions of individual obligors in credit portfolios. By using importance sampling, we develop a new scheme to simulate the credit portfolio, leading to efficient estimators for risk contributions. These results are summarized in a research paper titled "simulating risk contributions of credit portfolios", which is currently under third-round review with Operations Research. Other than the above IS method, we also explore the possibility of applying other simulation techniques to estimate the risk contributions. One direction we have explored is on the use of conditional Monte Carlo. It turns out using conditional Monte Carlo, the loss of the credit portfolio could be smoothed in some sense, making it possible to apply typical derivative estimation methods to estimate risk contributions. These results are summarized in the second half of the thesis of Dr. Shaolong Tong, who was my PhD student. Currently we are working on writing up this part of the PhD thesis as a research paper. The proposed IS methodology is an extension of our previous work on sensitivity estimation of risk measures, to a very unique but very important setting of credit portfolios. In addition to presenting the above findings in research papers and Dr. Tong's PhD thesis, we have also summarized the findings in a review paper titled "Monte Carlo methods for value-at-risk and conditional value-at-risk: A review", which has been accepted for publication in ACM Transactions on Modeling and Computer Simulation.

145511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
145511.value: One potential extension of the project is on the development of similar methodology for credit risk models that are not within the conditional-independence framework. In recent years, the conditional-independence framework has been criticized for its inability to capture the contagion effects. Towards this direction, we plan to look into some typical models in which the conditional-independence assumption is violated, such as self-exciting credit risk models. It is left as a topic for future research.

145511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
145511.value: In this project, we have developed a simulation methodology for efficiently estimating risk contributions of credit portfolios. The newly proposed methodology is centered around the combination of simulation techniques and unique structures of the models for credit portfolios. With the new methodology, we provide efficient estimators for risk contributions, which play an important role in capital allocation. In practice, capital allocation is an important risk management tool to evaluate the risk-adjusted returns of different investment activities, which serve as the basis for making investment decisions.

145911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
145911.value: Evidence shows that interpersonally harmful behavior, defined as “behavior that goes against the legitimate interests of another individual in the organization” (Venkataramani & Dalal, 2007, p. 925), severely compromises employees’ psychological health, work attitudes, and job performance, and may also reduce team effectiveness (Lim, Cortina, & Magley, 2008; Pearson & Porath, 2005). Recent research has conceptualized interpersonal harming as a dyadic phenomenon or “a function of a relationship between a perpetrator and a victim” (Hershcovis & Barling, 2007, p. 268). However, very little is known about what causes interpersonal harming behavior. Those few studies which have examined the dyadic antecedents of interpersonal harm have suggested that an actor is more likely to harm a target when he or she feels envy or dislike for the target (Cohen-Charash & Mueller, 2007). However, such studies have generally overlooked the reasons why specific individuals may have intense feelings toward some of their coworkers but not others, which in turn may drive them to engage selectively in harming behavior. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel, multilevel model to better understand the development of interpersonally harmful behavior in coworker dyads in work teams. Based on insights from social comparison theory and research (Buunk & Gibbons, 2007), we suggest that comparison with a higher-performing team member induces harming behavior when individuals believe that they can never achieve a similar level of performance in the future (future performance similarity) and when the teams’ goal interdependence is low. Furthermore, a substantial body of work suggests that different patterns of social comparison will elicit distinct interpersonal emotions, such as envy (Smith, 2000). More importantly, our own recent studies (Lam, 2009; Lam, Huang, Walter, & Chan, 2010) have shown that envy may activate or suppress harmful behavior depending on teams’ cooperative context. Building on this foundation, we propose that (1) a focal team member’s harming of another may depend interactively on his or her comparison with, and the level of expected performance similarity to, the target; (2) envy may mediate this moderated linkage; and (3) a team’s goal interdependence may function as a contextual, cross-level moderator influencing this mediated, moderation relationship. We propose to examine these issues in a series of multi-method studies, combining longitudinal field surveys with quasi-experiments. The project aims at enabling scholars to better understand the origins of interpersonal harming and aiding organizations in their efforts to confine this “dark” side of organizational behavior. 团队中的互相伤害行为：攀比，嫉妒，以及目标的相互依赖性 研究表名，相互伤害的行为——定义为“损害组织中其他个体的合理利益的行为”—— 严重危害了雇员的心理健康，工作态度，和工作表现，也有可能减低团队的工作效率。近期的研究已经定义“相互伤害”为一种二元现象，或者说一个由“害人者与被害人关系”所决定的函数。然而，什么导致了相互伤害的行为？我们对此知之甚少。仅有很少的研究考察了相互伤害行为的二元前因，这些研究表明，当人嫉妒或不喜欢某人时，更可能产生伤害性行为。但是，这些研究基本都忽视了为什么一个人只会对某一些人产生强烈的情感，并且在这种情感的驱动下，他们选择性的采取了伤害行为。 为了克服这些不足，我们提出了一个全新的，多层次的模型来更好的解释两个同事间的互相伤害关系是如何逐渐形成的。根据社会比较(攀比)理论和研究，我们提出：当人与表现更好的组员比较，认为自己将来不可能达到同等表现（将来表现相似性），并且彼此间目标依赖性很低的时候，这种比较行为会引发伤害行为。更重要的是，我们的近期研究表明，嫉妒可能引发或抑制伤害行为，取决于团队的合作氛围。基于此，我们提出：1) 一个特定组员对另一组员的伤害行为可能取决于他／她如何与该组员比较工作表现及预期将来会否达到同等表现；2) 嫉妒可能是这个调节关系的中间介质；3) 团队目标的相互依赖性可能是该关系的环境调节因素。 为了检验这些问题，我们建议进行一系列多种方法的研究，结合纵向实地调查和准实验。此项目的意义在于帮助学者去更好的理解相互伤害行为的起源，以及协助企业来限制组织行为中的“黑暗”面。

145911.label: Realisation of objectives
145911.value: Across two field studies, we investigated how social comparison between two co-workers in terms of their leader-member exchange relationships with their supervisor (LMX) may influence their emotional reaction toward each other (envy and contempt) and how these emotions mediate the relationship between social comparison and harming/helping behavior. These investigations have satisfied both objectives 1 and 3. In addition, we further examined how these mediation relationships will be moderated by other contingent factors (e.g., social comparison orientation, goal interdependence and expected future performance similarity). These investigations have satisfied objectives 2 and 3.

145911.label: Major findings and research outcome
145911.value: The results of social relations analyses revealed a curvilinear relationship between social comparison and contempt. That is, coworker A experiences more contempt for coworker B at both low and high (rather than medium) levels of LMX social comparison. In contrast, social comparison was not related to envy. In addition, our results demonstrated that contempt was negatively related to interpersonal helping (but not harming). Besides, contempt mediated the relationship between social comparison and perceived helping behavior. These interactive effect and mediation relationships were particular salient when individuals’ social comparison orientation was high. Based on these results from two field studies, we have produced a journal article published at a top-tier journal (Journal of Applied Psychology) and two conference papers that were presented at the Annual Meeting of International Society for Research on Emotion in 2013 and the Annual Conference of the Society of Industrial and Organizational Psychology.

145911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
145911.value: Future research could expand the present model by considering other moderators. Of particular interest are relational factors such as asymmetry in task dependence (de Jong et al., 2007) and expertise diversity (Van der Vegt et al., 2006) that convey a power difference between two individuals (Emerson, 1962). For example, the low-power individual (e.g., low skill, less experiences) may see the social comparison LMX differences as normative and legitimate in the hierarchy, making him/her conform and submit (submission rather than contempt) to the coworker who has higher LMX (Keltner, Gruenfeld, & Anderson, 2003). By considering the role of power-related factors, scholars can explore the differential effects of LMX comparison on employees’ emotional experiences. Besides, future research may benefit from further examining how social comparison of LMX shapes different types of positive and negative interpersonal emotions, thereby addressing calls for greater consideration of discrete emotions in organizational research (Gooty, Gavin, & Ashkanasy, 2009).

145911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
145911.value: When a leader has a better relationship quality (LMX) with, and thus provides more support and resources to, subordinate A than to subordinate B, the comparison of LMXs between the two employees may result in hostile sentiments and poor social interactions between them. Therefore, the main contribution of this study is to increase our understanding of the consequences and psychological processes of social comparison in the aspect of LMX on the interpersonal interactions between employees. Our results suggest that, when subordinate A perceives that he/she has a higher or lower level of LMX compared to subordinate B than when A perceives that his/her level of LMX is similar to B’s, subordinate A is more likely to experience contempt for and less likely to receive help from B. Our study also adds value to the existing literature by showing that perceptions of poor interactions resulting from the social comparison of LMX may hinder the performance of individuals over time (reduced sales performance).

146311.label: Project Objectives
146311.value: Examine the syntax-semantics mappings of universal quantifiers in Mandarin Chinese and Cantonese, to find out the correspondence between the syntax of different types of universal quantifiers and their semantics. Examine and compare the semantics of multiple universal quantifiers in Mandarin Chinese and Cantonese. Examine the co-occurrence of universal quantifiers in different syntactic forms. Find out whether properties of universal quantifiers in English as claimed in previous analyses are exhibited in Mandarin Chinese and Cantonese. Derive a paradigm of quantification to help shape quantificational patterns across syntactic categories and languages.
