146311.label: Realisation of objectives
146311.value: The five objectives have basically been achieved, which are summarized as follows: Objective 1: the syntax-semantics mappings of universal quantifiers in Mandarin Chinese and Cantonese For objective (1), our focus has mainly been on cai and jiu, with both translated as English “only”. Previous analyses consider cai and jiu be similar in their semantics, but our study found that the two cannot be the same. As a focus adverb, cai demonstrates the unique property of being flexible in its direction of association, with its associated item possibly being an element either to its right or to its left, or even the entire sentence, with focal mapping triggered. In the scalar use of cai, the quantificational domain of cai will be determined by the relevant scale. For the adverb jiu in Mandarin Chinese (henceforth “Mandarin”), we found that unlike cai, the basic semantics of jiu is to build up a relation between two units, leading to three jiu’s: focus adverb jiu, sufficiency operator jiu and jiu with the ‘close to’ meaning, depending on the units to which it relates. For universal quantification, Cantonese appeals to the A-quantifier dou1 "all", and the affixal universal quantifier –saai3 "all". Like Mandarin, universal quantification by Cantonese dou1 is subject to its Leftness Condition. However, unlike dou1, -saai3 can perform universal quantification on all the grammatical functions in a sentence, which is governed by a grammatical function hierarchy. The different conditions governing the quantification of dou1 and –saai3 to a certain extent can account for their natural co-occurrence in the same sentence. In sum, findings in this respect show that multiple forms of quantifiers in Mandarin and Cantonese exist due to their different semantics and syntax-semantics mappings. Arising from Objective (1), interesting findings are found in relation to the following issues: (i) the grammaticalisation of affixal universal quantifier –saai3 and (ii) semantics of two Cantonese approximative sentence-final particles. For (i), affixal quantifier –saai3 has been argued to be a universal quantifier or a verbal complement conveying the meaning of “completion”. Our study found that in Guangxi dialect, the verbal suffix or complement -saai3 was originated from it being a verb, meaning “complete”, and the verb –saai3 entered the grammaticalization process in its occurrence in the serial verb construction [V1 + V2]. The diverse semantics of Cantonese –saai3 may also be due to the influence of a similar grammaticalization process, making meanings of –saai3 vary among the peripheral or core meanings in the path of grammaticalization. For (ii), what is special in Cantonese is that it has two approximative modifiers appearing in the sentence-final position, namely mat1-zai6 ‘wh-over’ and gam3-zai6 ‘that-over’, both expressing “almost” meaning. Mat1zai6 and gam3zai6 show distinct selectional restrictions regarding the sentence polarity. In the case of mat1zai6, its occurrence needs the presence of an overt negator in the predicate to give a negative proposition. A negative approximate meaning is then given, with the value of the degree variable minimalized. In contrast, gam3-zai6 is not restricted by the negative contexts, and gam3-zai6 shows a positive orientation in the scale and its semantics requires a reference point or boundary which denotes a higher or the highest point in the scale. Further work can be done to reveal their semantics and their semantic differences with “almost” in Mandarin and English, and their interaction with universal quantification. Objective 2: the semantics of multiple universal quantifiers in Mandarin Chinese and Cantonese We have compared the semantics of multiple universal quantifiers in Mandarin and Cantonese. Besides other universal quantifiers, detailed study has been conducted on the co-occurrence of quan ‘all’ and dou ‘all’ which has been the puzzle of studies related to quantification. Our study has resulted in an important finding: with these seemingly universal quantifiers co-occurring, it may not be the case that all of them serve solely as universal quantifiers. While dou is a universal A-quantifier, quan is a dual-function operator. It serves as a universal quantifier when (i) it can find an appropriate quantificational domain, including a set of individuals denoted by plural NPs or a set of degree triggered by the predicate, and there exist no other adverbial quantifiers or distributive operators occurring to the right of quan, which can serve as a quantifier; (ii) when quan follows dou; and/or (iii) there exists a focus in the sentence with which quan associates. Quan will be a domain restrictor when its co-occurring predicate is able to host a distributive operator, be it a covert or an overt one. Ambiguity would arise when quan functions as both a domain restrictor and a universal quantifier. Our analysis can account for not only the similarities between quan and dou, but also, more importantly, their differences in semantic properties and sentence distributions. In sum, in the respect of multiple forms of universal quantifiers, we have reached a conclusion that these seemingly universal quantifiers may not all be universal quantifiers, though they do play a certain role in quantification, they may not be quantifiers by themselves. Objective 3: the co-occurrence of universal quantifiers in different syntactic form We have also examined the co-occurrence of universal quantifiers in different syntactic forms. It is widely acknowledged that Chinese uses reduplicative classifier to perform universal/distributive quantification giving a reading on a par with English “every/each”, and in the case of Cantonese reduplicative classifiers, they are generally found to be co-occurring with or be licensed by universal A-quantifier dou1 "all" or affixal quantifier –saai3 "all". Our preliminary research on reduplicative classifier found that the basic semantics of reduplicative classifiers cannot be considered as a distributive/universal quantifier, but a domain restrictor. Cantonese dou1 and the reduplicative classifier divide their labor as follows: dou1 is an A-quantifier performing universal quantification, and licensed by dou1, the adnominal reduplicative classifier serves a non-quantificational domain restrictor to overtly restrict the universal quantification of dou1, which then guarantees the output of the domain denoted by the nominal be a maximal collection. In sum, the above further echoes what we have claimed above: with these seemingly universal quantifiers co-occurring, it may not be the case that all of them are universal quantifiers, though they may serve a certain role in the universal quantification. Objective 4: Universal quantifiers in Chinese with those in English Co-occurrence of different forms of universal quantifiers generally renders ungrammaticality or unnaturalness if relevant sentences are literally translated into English. Conclusions drawn from the above four objectives have led to one important conclusion: while the scope relation among quantifiers in Mandarin and Cantonese is one prime factor giving the complicated scopal relationship among multiple universal quantifiers in Mandarin and Cantonese, word order is the basic parameter for determining their scope relation. Our results further support the linearity principle for Chinese scope interpretation under the Isomorphic Principle of S. F. Huang (1981). Objective 5: A paradigm of quantification For objective (5), focus is on negation. We found that negation performed by bu ‘not’, mei(-you) ‘not-have’ and bu(-shi) 'not-be' reveal two possible types of negation in natural language: (1) negation solely determined by semantics, with semantics overriding any possible syntactic constraints, as in bu; and (2) negation pre-determined by syntax, with semantics failing to override syntactic constraints, as in mei(-you) and bu-shi. Based further on their relation with eventualities, a paradigm of negation has been built up.

146311.label: Major findings and research outcome
146311.value: Major findings and research outcome of the project: (i) Multiple forms of quantifiers in Mandarin and Cantonese exist due to their different semantics and syntax-semantics mappings, making their independent existence necessary. (ii) Regarding the syntax-semantics mappings of quantifiers in Mandarin and Cantonese, the case of Cantonese –saai3 "all", -dak1 "only" and Mandarin cai "only" and jiu "only" reveals that relevant mappings may be governed more by syntax, with semantic factors failing to override the syntactic factors. (iii) Quantifiers claimed to be universal quantifiers previously may not be universal quantifiers. They play a certain role in quantification, with themselves not conveying any quantificational force. While English “all” is considered to be a domain restrictor, at this stage, these seemingly universal quantifiers, like reduplicative classifier in Cantonese and quan in Mandarin Chinese, are found to be domain restrictors, which reflect that Cantonese and Mandarin Chinese may have more domain restrictors than English. Importantly, domain restriction in Chinese can be done in grammar, and Chinese may not be a covert strategy language in terms of domain restriction. (iv) The co-occurrence of universal quantifiers in different syntactic form in Mandarin and Cantonese suggests a very complicated scopal relation among these quantifiers. Relevant interpretations can be derived only through sophisticated scopal interpretation, which can be achieved through word ordering if one considers this as the basic parameter for determining scope relation in Chinese. This further supports the linearity principle for Chinese scope interpretation given in the Isomorphic Principle, which was pointed out as early as S. F. Huang (1981). (v) Regarding negation, while bu ‘not’ is widely assumed to be a focus-sensitive operator, it is found that interpretation of mei ‘not’ does not lexically encode a dependency on the placement of focus. This is due to the failure of semantic focus to override the syntactic constraint of mei, which requires mei attach to its adjacent lexical verb you ‘have’, making mei inherently a negative existential quantifier of situations. This echoes the finding in (ii), which states that relevant mappings of universal quantifiers may be governed more by syntax, with semantic factors failing to override the syntactic factors. Moreover, it is found that negation performed by bu, mei and bu(-shi) ‘not-be’ reveal a preliminary landscape of negation: (1) negation solely determined by semantics, with semantics overriding any possible syntactic constraints, as in bu; and (2) negation pre-determined by syntax, with semantics failing to override syntactic constraints, as in mei and bu-shi.

146311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
146311.value: The research can be further developed in at least the following directions: (i) Reduplicative classifier can be further studied to verify the finding that Chinese may not be a covert strategy language in terms of domain restriction, which has already gained support from our detailed study on quan "all". (ii) It is found that the syntax-semantics mapping of universal quantifiers in Cantonese may be governed more by syntax, with semantic factors failing to override the syntactic factors. The relevant findings can be extended to other kinds of quantifications, including proportional quantification and more complex A- and D-universal quantifications, to find out the role of syntax and semantics in determining their quantificational structures. (iii) The landscape of quantifiers can be further worked out to include more quantifiers, such as existential quantifiers, more universal quantifiers, proportional quantifiers, more complex D-quantifiers and A-quantifiers. (iv) More cross-dialectal and cross-linguistic data can be included to enrich the landscape of quantifiers and to further examine the division of labor between syntax and semantics in the mappings of quantifiers in natural language.

146311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
146311.value: Quantifiers are used to express quantity of things in human language, and languages may differ with respect to types of quantifiers and strategies of quantification. This project conducts an in-depth study on universal quantification in Mandarin Chinese (henceforth “Mandarin”) and Cantonese so as to not only broaden our views on quantifier types and quantification strategies, but also reveal the general principles that regulate the syntax-semantics mapping in quantification. Mandarin and Cantonese are significant because of their richness in multiple forms of universal quantifiers, and universal quantifiers in different syntactic forms can co-occur in a single sentence, with no redundancy in meaning. The project examines: (i) the semantic differences between different universal quantifiers in Mandarin and Cantonese; (ii) universal quantifiers in different syntactic forms, and the division of labor between syntax and semantics in determining their meanings, (iii) the reasons leading to presence of multiple forms of universal quantifiers in Mandarin and Cantonese; and (iv) the reasons leading to the natural co-occurrence of quantifiers in Mandarin and Cantonese. It represents the first theoretical study which systematically examines universal quantification in Chinese from the semantic perspective, and contributes to the current linguistic endeavor by refining existing theories on quantification and syntax-semantics mappings.

146611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
146611.value: An event of far-reaching influence in phonetics was the publication of the seminal works on the quantal nature of speech by K.N. Stevens of M.I.T. Stevens’ model-based quantal theory claims that relations between articulation and acoustic output are non-linear. In some regions of the vocal tract, formant frequencies are exceedingly sensitive to variation in articulation, but in other regions, such as the regions for the point vowels [i a u], formant frequencies are relatively insensitive to variation in constriction location and degree of constriction. The point vowels that exhibit acoustic stability are said to be quantal, which explains why cross-linguistically the point vowels are preferred. Beckman, et al (1995) and other studies evaluate the quantal theory by examining variability in articulatory-acoustic relations in English point vowels. Results support the quantal theory and reveal that formant frequencies are less sensitive to variation in constriction location than degree of constriction. There have been other studies investigating the articulatory-acoustic relations in vowel production in general. Fant (1960) establishes the correlations between formant frequencies and sizes of front and back cavities of the vocal tract during vowels. Lindblom and Sundberg (1971) and other studies offer findings such as compensatory articulation and acoustical consequences of vowel reduction. To our knowledge, there have not been any investigations of (i) the quantal nature of Cantonese point vowels [i: a: u: i a u] and (ii) vocal tract configurations during Cantonese long, medium-long, and short vowels. This study proposes to research into both. Two parts make up the proposed research. PART (A) investigates whether quantal relations are observable in Cantonese. It evaluates the quantal theory by determining the sensitivities of formant frequencies for Cantonese point vowels to variation in constriction location and degree of constriction by analyzing the variability in articulatory-acoustic relations during the point vowels. PART (B) investigates the articulatory-acoustic relations in each of the 18 (seven long, seven medium-long, and four short) Cantonese vowels. It (i) obtains for each of the 18 Cantonese vowels the vocal tract configuration, encompassing positions of the tongue, lips, and jaw, and its corresponding formant frequencies, and (ii) determines the difference in variability in articulatory-acoustic relations between Cantonese point and non-point vowels. The proposed research is expected to contribute to evaluating the quantal theory with data on articulatory-acoustic relations in Cantonese vowels. It will establish corpora of vocal tract configurations for all the 18 Cantonese vowels with corresponding formant frequencies. 美國麻省理工學院K.N. Steven提出的語音量子理論(quantal theory)對語音學有著廣泛的影響. 這建基於模型的量子理論聲稱發音與聲學之關係是非綫性的. 在口腔聲道中的某些區域, 共鳴頻率對發音的改變是非常敏感的, 但在其他區域, 比如在發尖端元音[i a u]的區域, 共鳴頻率對聲道收窄位置和收窄程度的改變相對地不是那麼敏感. 尖端元音顯示的聲學穩定性被稱為量子, 這解釋了為什麼在各個不同的語言裏, 尖端元音是優先被採用的. Beckman等(1995)和其他一些研究曾經對量子理論進行測試, 分析英語的尖端元音去查察發音與聲學之關係的變異性. 所得的結果是支持量子理論的, 並揭示出共鳴頻率對聲道收窄位置的改變比對收窄程度的改變的敏感度為低. 有不少其他的研究也曾對發音與聲學之關係從元音產生方面進行了分析. Fant(1960)對元音共鳴頻率和聲道前後聲腔的大小建立了相互關係. Lindblom 和 Sundberg(1971)及其他一些研究發表了發音和元音弱化互補性的聲學資料. 據我們所知, 至今尚未有對(i)廣州話尖端元音[i: a: u: i a u]的量子性質及(ii)在發廣州話長, 中長和短元音時的聲道形態作研究. 這些正是本研究計劃的研究工作. 本研究計劃由兩部份構成. (A)部份是研究量子關係是否在廣州話中存在. 這是對量子理論進行測試, 確定廣州話尖端元音的共鳴頻率對聲道收窄位置和收窄程度的變化的敏感度, 分析在發尖端元音時發音與聲學之關係的變異性. (B)部份是研究廣州話18個元音(7個長元音, 7個中長元音和4個短元音)各自的發音與聲學之關係. 這需要(i)取得每一個廣州話元音的聲道形態, 包括舌頭, 上下唇和下巴的位置, 及各元音對應的共鳴頻率, 並(ii)決定廣州話尖端和非尖端元音在發音與聲學之關係的變異性的相異之處. 本研究計劃預計可以透過廣州話元音在發音與聲學之關係的資料去對量子理論作測試. 本研究計劃也會建立廣州話所有18個元音的聲道形態與其共鳴頻率之關係的資料庫.

146611.label: Realisation of objectives
146611.value: This research project, entitled ‘Articulatory-acoustic relations in Cantonese vowels’, investigates the articulatory-acoustic relations in the production of Cantonese vowels. It consists of two parts. Part I determines whether the quantal relations between articulation and acoustics as claimed in Stevens (1972, 1989) are observable in the two sets of Cantonese point vowels, the long vowels [i: y: u: a:] and the medium-long equivalents [i y u a], through (a) measuring the variations in location and degree of the tongue constriction along the vocal tract during the articulation of the vowels and (b) relating the articulatory measurements to those of vowel formant (resonance) frequencies. Part II presents the articulatory-acoustic relations in all the 18 Cantonese vowels, including seven long vowels [i: y: u: a: ɛ: œ: ɔ:], seven medium-long vowels [i y u a ɛ œ ɔ], and four short vowels [ɪ ɵ ʊ ɐ]. The study aims (i) to establish the relations between the vocal tract configuration - the tongue, lip, and jaw positions - and the corresponding vowel formant frequencies and (ii) to determine the variability in the articulatory-acoustic relations during the vowels of different lengths, point and non-point, in Cantonese. All the objectives of this research project have been achieved through collection and analysis of (a) the articulatory data on the location and degree of tongue constriction along the vocal tract and (b) the acoustic data on the formant frequencies of all the point and non-point vowels in Cantonese. Speech samples were collected from a group of native Cantonese speakers, male and female university students of 18 to 21 years of age in Hong Kong, considered as representing the present day younger generation. Over a hundred candidates were screened for their language background and performance in articulating Cantonese speech sounds. Twelve of them were selected, including six males and six females. They were all born to the monolingual Cantonese-speaking families and have lived their whole life in Hong Kong, and they had no history of speech and hearing difficulties. The selected speakers participated in individual recording sessions, each reading a randomized list of meaningful test monosyllabic words at a normal rate of speech. The test words contained the Cantonese point vowels [i: y: u: a: i y u a] and non-point vowels [ɛ: œ: ɔ: ɛ œ ɔ ɪ ɵ ʊ ɐ] of different lengths. The method of multiple repetitions of test words was adopted. Each speaker uttered 20 repetitions of each of the test words presented on the reading list yielding a total of 4,320 test tokens (18 test words x 20 repetitions x 12 speakers) for subsequent articulatory and acoustic analysis. An advanced research tool, Electromagnetic Mid-sagittal Articulograph (EMMA) AG500 manufactured by the Carstens of Germany, was used for synchronized digital recordings of (a) the movements and positions of the articulators - the tip, tongue, lips, and jaw, and (b) the audio signals during the articulation of the Cantonese vowels. The mid-sagittal contour of the palate of each speaker was also obtained for determining the location and degree of tongue constriction, i.e., tongue-palate constriction, relative to the palate during the vowels. The recorded articulatory data provided the vocal tract configurations showing the tongue, lip, and jaw positions during the test vowels, and the recorded speech data provided the corresponding first and second formant frequencies, F1 and F2, of the test vowels. The relations between the vocal tract configurations and formant frequencies patterns were established for all the 18 Cantonese vowels, with reference to the claims of the model-based quantal theory (Stevens, 1972, 1989). They were found to be supporting the theory, which claims that the articulatory-acoustic relations in vowel production are non-linear. This is true of all the Cantonese vowels, where the acoustic consequences of the vertical or horizontal displacement in tongue constriction in the vocal tract are non-linearly correlated, for instance, a moderate shift in constriction location or constriction degree of the tongue may result in a large spectral change. Furthermore, the articulatory-acoustic relations vary across different vowel types. The Cantonese high point vowels [i: y: u: i y u] with a narrow tongue constriction are considered quantal, exhibiting greater acoustic stability and smaller within-category variability than the non-point and non-high vowels [ɛ: œ: ɔ: a: ɛ œ ɔ a ɪ ɵ ʊ ɐ]. The data on the articulatory-acoustic relations in the Cantonese vowels provide information on the sensitivity of formant frequencies to variations in tongue displacement in both the x-dimension and y-dimension. The pattern of the varying degree of sensitivity in the Cantonese vowels is similar to that in the English vowels reported in the past studies (Perkell and Nelson, 1985; Perkell and Cohen, 1989; Beckman, et al., 1995), in that (a) the variability is greater in tongue constriction location in the x-dimension than in tongue constriction degree in the y-dimension, and (b) formant frequencies are relatively less sensitive to a variation of tongue displacement in the x-dimension than in the y-dimension. The Cantonese vowel data obtained in this study are also used to test the theory of vowel target undershoot proposed in Lindblom (1963), which says the vowels undergo centralization in the acoustic vowel space when shortened. The Cantonese vowel data demonstrate that the effect of shortening on the vowel production is not wholly predicted by the theory and the effect differs across different vowels. This is also found to be true of the vowels in other languages, such as German (Mooshammer and Geng, 2008) and Creek (Johnson and Martin, 2001). Furthermore, the vowels in different languages may behave differently under the effect. That the effect differs across the vowel types and varies across languages may be due to “the involvement of language-specific phonetic properties” as pointed out in Beckman, et al. (1995). In short, firstly, this project, based on the experimental - articulographic and spectral - data from Cantonese, has evaluated one of the most widely known theories in the field of phonetic sciences, that is, the model-based quantal theory. While all the previous studies bearing on the theory through analysis of the vowels in the European languages, notably English, this study is based on the vowel data from Cantonese. The essence of the quantal theory is that the relations between variations in articulation and corresponding acoustic pattern are non-linear. The findings of this project are consistent with those in the previous studies supporting the theory. Secondly, the project for the first time makes available detailed information on the articulatory and spectral characteristics of the vowel sounds in Cantonese, which are useful to (a) linguists analyzing the structure of the Cantonese sound system, (b) speech engineers researching on speech synthesis and recognition of Cantonese, and (c) speech pathologists assessing speech deficits in Cantonese speakers who are unable to produce speech sounds correctly. The findings of this project have been disseminated through presentations at internationally conferences and publications in the conference proceedings and peer-reviewed journals. A list of the research output arising directly from the project has been presented in Part C of this report.

146611.label: Major findings and research outcome
146611.value: A summary of the main findings of this research project is presented below. Most of them have been published in the journal articles and conference proceedings papers as listed in Part C of this Completion Report. First, the relations between articulation and acoustics in the Cantonese vowels support Stevens’ (1972, 1989) quantal theory, which claims that the relations between acoustic consequences and variations in vertical or horizontal displacement of tongue constriction in the vocal tract are non-linear. Also, the strength of such articulatory-acoustic relations varies across different vowel types. Those Cantonese high point vowels [i: y: u: i y u] with a narrow tongue constriction along the vocal tract are considered quantal, as they show greater acoustic stability and less within-category variability than the non-point and non-high vowels [ɛ: œ: ɔ: a: ɛ œ ɔ a ɪ ɵ ʊ ɐ]. Second, the findings of the non-linear relations between the variations in articulation and the corresponding acoustics in Cantonese vowels in this study are similar to those reported in the previous studies of the English vowels (Perkell and Nelson, 1985; Perkell and Cohen, 1989; Beckman, et al., 1995). The high point vowels in both Cantonese and English exhibit the quantal characteristic, where the variability tends to be larger in the tongue constriction location in the x-dimension than in the tongue constriction degree in the y-dimension. Furthermore, the formant frequencies are relatively less sensitive to variations in tongue displacement in the x-dimension than in the y-dimension. In both languages, the quantal nature of the articulatory-acoustic relations is not observed in the non-point and non-high vowels. Third, a comparison of the long vowels and their shorter equivalents in Cantonese shows that the shorter vowels undergo vowel target undershoot relative to the long vowels. The extent of vowel target undershoot varies across different vowel types, greater in the non-point vowels than the point vowels and greater in the back vowels than the front vowels. Lindblom’s (1963) theory of vowel target undershoot says that vowels of all types undergo vowel centralization in the acoustical vowel space does not wholly predict the Cantonese case, as in Cantonese some but not all the shorter vowels undergo vowel centralization. Also, it has been shown that shorter vowels of the same type in different languages undergo target undershoot in different ways. This according to Beckman, et al. (1995) is attributed to the involvement of language-specific phonetic properties in vowel production.

146611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
146611.value: The present research project serves as the basis for a future enlarged study through analysis of the acoustic-auditory relations in addition to the articulatory-acoustic relations in Cantonese and in the other Chinese dialects. In fact, Stevens’ (1972, 1989) model-based quantal theory predicts non-linear relations not just between variations in articulatory dimension and corresponding acoustic dimension, but also between acoustic and perceptual dimensions. Thus, to have a more complete evaluation of the quantal theory and to have a better understanding of the relations between articulation, acoustics, and perception of the vowel sounds, an analysis of the acoustics-to-auditory relations in addition to the articulatory-to-acoustic relations needs to be carried out. To enlarge the scope, the future study also analyzes the articulatory-acoustic-perceptual relations in the vowels of the other major Chinese dialects, such as Beijing Mandarin, Hakka, and Shanghai. Furthermore, to increase the reliability of the study, there will be an increase in the size of speaker population, including speakers of different age groups. Upon completion of the enlarged project, a more accurate and comprehensive evaluation of the quantal theory and a much better understanding of the articulatory-acoustic-auditory relations of different vowel types in different languages are expected to be achieved.

146611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
146611.value: This research investigates (i) the relations between variations in the tongue position in the mouth cavity and the corresponding changes in the resonance frequencies of the Cantonese vowels during speech, and (ii) the effect of shortened duration on the resonance frequencies of the Cantonese vowels. It evaluates (a) the ‘quantal theory’ which claims that the said relations are non-linear, and (b) the ‘vowel target undershoot theory’ which claims that the vowels undergo centralization in the acoustical vowel space when shortened. Phonetic data collected from young adult Cantonese speakers in Hong Kong include (a) measurements of variations in the location and degree of tongue constriction during the articulation of each of the Cantonese long, medium-long, and short vowels, using the ‘articulograph’, a sophisticated instrument for phonetic research, and (b) measurements of the corresponding resonance frequencies of the Cantonese vowels of different lengths. Results of a comparison of the two sets of measurements show that (i) the Cantonese vowel data generally support the claims made by the quantal theory, (ii) some Cantonese vowels are more stable acoustically than the other types, and (iii) the change in the Cantonese shorter vowels are not wholly predicted by the vowel target undershoot theory.

146811.label: Project Title(Chinese)
146811.value: 華人的創意表現: 以社會適應的觀點檢視調節效應

146811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
146811.value: Some scholars believe that traditional Chinese culture is not conducive to creativity, and considerable empirical evidence supports this view, showing that East Asian students in general, and Chinese students in particular, have lower creativity test scores than their Western counterparts. Interestingly, there are also some studies showing that East Asian students are as good as, or even better than, Western students in creativity tests. On the macro level, East Asian cultures rank high in innovation according to the 2009-2010 Global Competitiveness Index: Japan ranks second, Taiwan eighth, Singapore tenth, Korea sixteenth, and Hong Kong twenty third. A simple cultural explanation seems unable to account for these inconsistent empirical findings. We propose that although creative performance is affected by individual difference variables, it is more useful to conceptualize it not as an ability that is fixated, but as a type of performance that is malleable to the influence of the context. The major objective of the proposed project is to develop a model that explains how contextual forces shape the creative performance of Chinese people. To this end, we adopt a social adaptation perspective and posit that in a performance situation, people are motivated to choose the most adaptive course of action to maximize their chance of success. Generally speaking, there is inertia towards creativity, and conformist approaches tend to be default choices for many people. Extrapolating from the theoretical arguments and empirical evidence that attempt to explain the lower creative performance of East Asian students, we propose that performance pressure, task difficulty, and perceived competition tend to suppress creative performance through heightening fear of failure. In addition, we note that different lines of research provide compelling theoretical arguments and evidence for the positive effects of performance pressure, task difficulty, and competition on creative performance, pointing to the operation of moderating variables that shape the effects of these three contextual variables. To address these diverse findings, we propose that support for innovation, pro-creativity norm, and creative self-efficacy can buffer the negative influence of performance pressure, task difficulty, and competition. The first two studies proposed will test these theoretical predictions in the work context as well as in the school context to evaluate their generality. The third study, to be conducted in the work context, will test an extended model developed from the findings of the first two studies. This project has significant theoretical and applied significance. 有些學者認為傳統中國文化不利創新，也有一定的証據支持這觀點，東亞學生，包括華人學生，在創意測驗的分數一般比西方學生為低，不過也有部份結果顯示東亞學生比西方學生的創意測驗分數為高，從宏觀角度來看，東亞國家在創新的表現很好，跟據2009-2010 的全球競爭力指數，日本排行第二，台灣第八，星加坡第十，南韓十六，香港二十三。簡單的文化差異不能解釋這些不一致的結果。 我們認為創意表現雖然受到個人差異的影響，但創意不是固定的能力，而是受到環境影響的一種表現，我們希望建立一個模型去解釋環境因素如何影響華人的創意表現，我們以社會適應的觀點，提出在一個抨核的環境，人會選擇最具適應性的行動，以爭取最高的成功機會。一般而言，大部份人對創意缺乏動力，傾向於從眔，從解釋東亞學生創意分數較低的理論分析入手，我們建議表現壓力，工作困難度，及競爭程度傾向於透過導致害怕失敗而降低創意表現，不過也有証據及理論支持這些環境因素有時會提高創意表現，顯示有調節變量可以影響這些環境因素的效應。顧及這些研究結果，我們提出對創意的支持，支持創意的規範，及創意自我能力，可以緩衝表現壓力，工作困難度，及競爭程度的負面影響。首兩個研究會在工作及學校環境檢驗這些理論預測及其普遍性。第三個研究會在工作環境進行，檢驗跟據首兩個研究的結果所開拓的模型。這個研究項目具有重要的理論及應用價值。

147111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
147111.value: Using the insights from upper echelons theory, resource-based view of firm and agency theory, this project explores how management demography and board composition can shape organizational outcomes. By employing data about the imposition and removal of reprimanding sanctions, we examine the characteristics of management and board which can lead the firms for better or worse. The upper echelons theory, resource-based theory and social capital literature emphasize that top management demography is an essential intangible asset and social capital of performance to achieve efficiency (Hambrick 2007; Hitt, Bierman, Shimizu and Kochhar 2001; Shipilov and Danis 2006). Combining these management theories, we examine how top management demography may affect performance and corporate governance of Chinese firms. We use the data about reprimanding sanctions (e.g., disclosure of “Special Treatment” status due to poor earnings; enforcement action announcement due to company violations such as embezzlement) to differentiate firms with good and poor performance/governance. Agency theory puts forward the importance of the board in monitoring the management (Fama 1980). We explore the relation between top management demography (age, gender, tenure, education level, professional status, multiple positions) and incidence of reprimanding sanctions, after controlling for the difference in board governance structure (board size, independent directors, female directors, CEO duality, managerial share-holdings, frequency of board meetings). When the firms are under reprimanding sanctions, the market reacts negatively (Cheng, Leung and Yu 2010). Therefore, it is of interest to further explore what type of demography can rescue firms from reprimanding sanctions. For the firms which recover from poor performance/governance (i.e., removal of reprimanding sanction), we examine the change in demographic characteristics and if the board would replace top management. In particular, we compare the difference in management demography before and after the removal of reprimanding sanction. The findings of this project should have potential implications for the design of board governance structure. We examine if management demography is an important determinant in affecting performance/governance and explain why some firms have a higher likelihood of reprimanding sanctions. In addition, we also explore the type of management demography which helps improve performance/governance by comparing the demographic characteristics before and after the removal of reprimanding sanctions. As management turnover is a direct outcome of corporate governance, we assess if the firms under reprimanding sanctions voluntarily dismiss top management to improve performance/governance. These results may provide insights to regulators about the effectiveness and design of the current disciplinary, enforcement and prosecution systems. 本課題借鑒了高層梯隊理論、基於資源的公司觀和代理理論的觀點，探尋管理人口統計學和董事會的組成是如何影響企業的表現。通過採用加諸和去除譴責制裁的數據，我們探討可給公司帶來正面或負面影響的管理層和董事會的特點。 高層梯隊理論、基於資源的理論和社會資本文獻強調，為實現高效運作，高層管理人口統計學是必不可少的無形資產和社會資本（Hambrick 2007; Hitt, Bierman, Shimizu和Kochhar 2001; Shipilov和Danis 2006）。結合這些管理理論，我們研究高層管理人口統計學可能會如何影響中國企業的業績和公司管治。 我們使用有關譴責制裁的數據（例如，由於低收益而披露的 “特殊待遇”的地位;因為公司違規行為（如貪污）而導致的執法行動）以區分具有良好的和不良的業績/管治的公司。代理理論提出了在監督管理層時董事會的重要性（Fama 1980）。在控制了董事會管治結構上的差異后（董事會規模，獨立董事，女董事，CEO兩職狀態，管理層控股，董事會會議密度），我們探討高層管理人口統計學（年齡，性別，任期，教育程度，職業狀況，多位置）與譴責制裁的發生率之間的關係。 當企業受到譴責制裁時，市場會有消極反應（Cheng，Leung和Yu 2010）。因此，進一步探討如何的人口統計學可以從譴責制裁中拯救公司是有意義的。對於從不佳業績/管治中恢復的公司（即譴責制裁去除），我們檢查了人口統計學特徵的變化以及董事會是否變更高層管理人員。特別地，我們比較了譴責制裁去除之前和之後管理人口統計學的變化。 本課題的研究結果應可給董事會管治結構的設計帶來一些啟示。我們研究管理人口統計學是否一個影響業績/管治的重要決定因素，並解釋為什麼某些企業會有較高的受到譴責制裁的可能性。此外，通過比較譴責制裁去除之前和之後管理人口統計學的變化，我們還探討了有助於提高業績/管治的管理人口統計學的類型。由於管理層離職是公司管治的直接結果，我們評估在受到譴責制裁時公司是否自發解雇高層管理人員以提高業績/管治。這些結果可能為監管者就現有的懲戒、執法及檢察系統的有效性及設計提供一些見解。

147111.label: Major findings and research outcome
147111.value: For the first research question, we examine the types of quality of chairpersons and CEOs, which lead the firms to be under financial distress. These results suggest that the chairpersons who are younger in age and without title ownership and the CEOs with shorter tenure and low education level run the firms poorly and lead the firms to be under financial distress. Firms with younger chairpersons are more likely to be under financial distress. The findings support our first hypothesis that management quality is related to incidence of reprimanding sanction. For the second research issue, we hypothesize that chairperson turnover is related to reprimanding sanction and management demography. We observe that chairperson turnover is related to age, education level and title ownership. These results suggest that there is a higher likelihood for chairpersons who are old, have low education level and no professional title to be replaced. We find that chairpersons are more likely to be replaced when the CEOs have shorter tenure and higher education level. For the forced turnover subsample, we find a completely different result from other turnover cases. None of the chairperson characteristics are significant. These results support our second hypothesis that turnover is related to the characteristics of top management and incidence of reprimanding sanction. In short, we find that management demography and incidence of financial distress jointly affect the probability of chairperson turnover. For the third research issue, we examine what factors determine the turnover choice: chairperson versus CEO. We show that the choice of top management turnover (chairperson versus CEO) is significantly related to management demographic quality. Our results suggest that CEOs are more likely than the chairpersons to be replaced when chairpersons are younger in age and more educated as well as have shorter tenure and professional qualification. We find that CEOs are more likely to be replaced when they are older and less educated.

147111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
147111.value: Our paper contributes to the literature on corporate governance and monitoring activities of firms in a transitional economy. It is a challenge to measure the effectiveness of corporate governance mechanism. We make use of the incidence of reprimanding sanctions to examine if the Chinese firms under financial distress have a higher propensity to replace their poorly performing top executives. Our findings generate implications for boards and investors on what would happen to top management when firms are under financial distress in China. Our finding lends support for the regulatory role of improving corporate governance in China. We add to the turnover literature that, besides profitability, reprimanding sanctions from regulatory bodies is also a significant factor relating to turnover. International firms should find such a result useful in deploying their executives in China. In addition, overseas stock market investors considering investments in China should also find our results helpful when making portfolio decision in selecting Chinese stocks. Future research can explore the post-turnover performance of these financially distressed firms.

147111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
147111.value: The literature shows the importance of top management and board characteristics on firm performance. We extend this literature by examining top management turnover for financially distressed firms. China has a unique sanction rule, which publicly labels financially distressed listed firms to provide the market with a warning signal. Controlling for board characteristics and governance, we evaluate how relational management demography affects turnover of financially distressed firms in China. Our results first show that the demographic characteristics of top management for distressed firms differ from those of normal firms. Second, management turnover is positively related to financial distress. Finally, we show that the departure of either the chairperson or CEO depends on their demographic differences. We conjecture that our findings provide support to the upper echelons theory and scapegoat argument.

148411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
148411.value: Purification straw is a device one can use to drink water directly from raw sources. It removes bacteria as water is sucked through it. One might still taste some of the algae, but at least the water will be bacteria-free. It costs around US$3.5 a piece, and lasts for around six months to a year. Purification straw typifies a class of products that are noticeably missing in traditional economic models of trade and development. These products, like purification straw, although safe to use in principal, are never used by anyone in the developed world. They are used exclusively in extremely poor areas. Yet, their deceptive simplicity notwithstanding, their development requires knowledge that is way beyond the level mastered by people living in poor areas. Indeed, they are developed and sold for profit almost exclusively by innovators from the developed world. Overlooking these products can lead to very misleading world views and their accompanying policy recommendations. For example, a traditional view is that poor countries benefit from the growth of rich countries. The underlying trickle-down theory is that, as innovators invent better and better products for the rich-country consumers, poor-country citizens also stand to benefit by imitation. Natural implications of this view include that increasing inequality among countries is not a reason for concern, and policies that facilitate imitation are in general recommendable for developing countries. However, products like purification straw suggest that “inventing for the richest 10%” can be very different from “inventing for the other 90%”. As inequality among countries increases, consumers in poor countries will find that inventions made in rich countries are increasingly irrelevant, and the question of how to incentivize “inventing for the other 90%” increasingly pressing. Not only that inequality among countries can mean direct harm on poor countries, simplistic recommendations to facilitate imitation could bring perverse incentives to innovators who may otherwise be willing to “invent for the other 90%”. This project aims at providing a new framework to think about trade and development policies, with the full recognition of products like purification straw, and their implication that “inventing for the richest 10%” can be very different from “inventing for the other 90%”. We intend to use this new framework in investigating (i) the impacts of inequality among countries, (ii) desirable policies regarding intellectual property rights protection in developing countries, and (iii) the political economy of trade and development policy formation in developing countries. 富裕與貧窮國家由於購買力的懸殊差距導致消費商品貨物集合大為不同.這個現實也導致多數利益導向的工業研發與產品設計都針對富裕國家的需求制定開發方針.如此一來,貧窮國家負擔得起的商品貨物集合,相對而言,變更佳匱乏.本研究目的致力於分析適切的貿易與經濟發展政策以期減少不均衡研發成果所導致貧富福利水準加速分歧的現象.並探討現行的智慧財產權的利弊及世界貿易框架下貿易相關智慧財產權協議的功能與角色.

148411.label: Realisation of objectives
148411.value: The four main project objectives have been achieved. This study shows that how and why the benefits and costs of intellectual property rights protections are non-monotonic and actually depend on the development level of the countries in questions. It suggests that the harmonization of international intellectual property right protection along is likely to be rejected by less developing counties for different reasons. For the least develop countries, the reason is the constraint of government capacity; for developing countries, the reason is the lack of incentive. Our study argues that combing the market access negotiation with intellectual property right protection negotiation, such as the TRIPS agreement, may effectively address the lack of incentive problem facing developing countries and free riding problem simultaneously.

148411.label: Major findings and research outcome
148411.value: This project has generated one paper, which is conditional accepted by the Journal of Development Economics. The major findings are summarized below. We study the two opposite views regarding whether stronger protection of intellectual property rights (IPRs) will benefit or hurt the South. We provide a unification using a model of directed innovations with identical but non-homothetic preferences. For the South, a major benefit of protecting IPRs is incentivizing Northern innovations that better address its needs (the directed-innovation benefit), and a major cost is yielding monopoly rents to Northern producers (the monopoly-rent cost). When preferences are non-homothetic, the directed-innovation benefit decreases in South's income, because consumption baskets of the South become more similar to those of the North; while the monopoly-rent cost increases in South's income, because lower income admits smaller monopoly markups. The combined effect implies that costs of IPRs protection tend to outweigh benefits for mid-income Southern countries, while the opposite is true for low-income ones. We also discuss the policy implications of this observation.

148411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
148411.value: One important extension of the research is to integrate the current model to quality-ladder, endogenous growth model in which the number of potential innovation is un-bounded. Using the model, we will be able to investigate whether and how the degree of global inequality affects not only the type/direction of innovation but also the speed of innovation, which will have important implication of long run growth.

148411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
148411.value: Using a model of directed innovations with identical but non-homothetic preferences, we argue that the costs of IPRs protection tend to outweigh benefits for mid-income countries, and the opposite is true for low-income ones. What is the policy relevancy of this observation? When we see a decision maker not taking an action, there are at least two explanations. Either he is capable of taking that action, but doing so is not in his interest; or it is in his interest to take the action, but he is incapable of doing so. Distinguishing the unwilling from the incapable is important, especially if we genuinely want to help. The same is true when the decision maker is a Southern country, and the action in question is to protect IPRs. Using market access, or the denial of it, as a threat to induce stronger IPRs protection may amount to extorting the unwilling, while leaving the incapable unassisted. This research provides valuable insights, which will help better design and implement international intellectual property right protection.

148711.label: Project Objectives
148711.value: To analyze whether busy investors are effective monitors, we examine if busy investors increase or decrease the forced CEO turnover sensitivity to firm’s performance. Specifically we run a logistic regression where the dependent variable is set to one if the firm experiences a forced executive management turnover in the year and otherwise zero. We expect the busyness measure to be positively related to the sensitivity of forced CEO turnover to performance, whereas a negative relation is expected when busy investors are less effective in monitoring. To check whether the busy investor effects are from their different monitoring effectiveness, we break down our sample firms depending on their independence or on their trading style. The literature of institutional investors reveals that not all institutions monitor or influence management but only certain types of them such as independent and long-term investors do. To address this issue, we divide the institutional investors into potentially active investors (independent) and potentially passive investors (dependent) following Almazan, Hartzell, and Starks (2005) and compare their busyness effects on the forced CEO turnover sensitivity to past performance. We also follow Yan and Zhang (2007) to estimate churn rates for institutional investors as a measure of how frequently they rotate their equity positions in their portfolios. Using the churn rates, we classify the institutional investors into short-term and long-term investors and compare their busyness effects. To investigate if the learning effect explains the monitoring effectiveness of busy institutions, we classify institutions depending on whether they hold largest block ownership in another firm within the same industry. We hypothesize that the busy investor effects would be concentrated in the subsample of the institutions with another largest block in the same industry since their learning effects would be larger when they have monitoring experiences in the same industry. We examine the announcement returns on forced CEO turnovers and post-management turnover long-run performance and explore how the existence of busy investors affects the valuation and performance changes. Positive effects of busy investors on these performance measures would support their monitoring effectiveness further.

148711.label: Realisation of objectives
148711.value: To examine the effect of multiple blockholdings on institutional monitoring, we use the following residual approach and measure the number of blockholdings conditional on institution size and type. First, using the 13F institutional holdings database, for each firm, we identify the largest institutional blockholder that owns at least 5% of the firm’s outstanding shares. We then count the number of firms that each institutional investor holds as their largest institutional blockholder (“raw number”). Next, we regress the raw number on the total market value of the institution’s equity investment and indicators for institution types and years to obtain the residual holding number. We define the residual holding number for a firm’s largest institutional blockholder as the “institutional blockholding number.” Finally, we define an indicator that takes the value of one if the firm’s institutional blockholding number is greater than the sample median and zero otherwise (“multiple blockholding indicator”). We use this multiple blockholding indicator as our key explanatory variable of interest in examining the monitoring effectiveness of institutional investors with multiple blockholdings. It is set to zero for firms with no institutional blockholder. To construct a sample of forced CEO turnovers, we consider a top executive turnover event as occurring in a given year when a firm’s CEO ID in ExecuComp differs from that in the prior year. Following Denis, Denis, and Sarin (1995), Parrino (1997), and Jenter and Kanaan (2012), we classify a management change into nonroutine and routine CEO turnovers. This procedure yields a total of 1,989 CEO turnover events, 467 of which are classified as nonroutine.

148711.label: Major findings and research outcome
148711.value: We first find that the number of stocks that the institutional investor holds as the largest institutional blockholder significantly improves its monitoring incentives and capability. Specifically, the forced CEO turnover sensitivity to performance is significantly higher when the firm has an institution with a larger blockholding number as its largest institutional blockholder. Second, to achieve the second objective, we divide our sample firms according to whether their largest institutional shareholder is a dedicated investor or not (Bushee, 2001). We find that the effect of multiple blockholdings on the sensitivity of forced CEO turnovers to performance is significant only when a firm’s largest institutional blockholder is classified as a dedicated investor. Moreover, following Cornett et al. (2007), we divide our sample firms according to whether a firm’s largest institutional blockholder is an independent investor or not based on its legal type. Our results show that the multiple blockholding effects are significant only when a firm’s largest institutional blockholder is classified as independent. Regarding the third objective, we find that the sensitivity of forced CEO turnovers to performance is higher when institutional investors have multiple largest blockholdings in the same industry. This finding suggests that information spillover and learning are important channels through which multiple blockholdings enhance institutions’ monitoring incentives and capabilities. Finally, we find that firms with a larger institutional blockholding number realize higher abnormal returns around a forced CEO turnover announcement. These findings are more evident for firms with the largest institutional blockholders which hold another largest block in the same industry. Overall, our results support the view that multiple blockholdings increase institutional investors’ monitoring effectiveness and firm value. We are currently trying to publish a research paper from our project at a high-quality academic journal.

148711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
148711.value: We are trying to simplify the measure of multiple blockholdings, so it can more clearly capture institutional investors with multiple blockholdings and can be more easily constructed and used in other studies. We also can apply this idea of multiple blockholdings to other settings. For example, we can examine the effects of institutional blockholders with multiple blockholdings on merger gains when their portfolio firms undertake mergers and acquisitions. Our findings suggest that merger synergy gains would be larger when acquirers are monitored by institutional shareholders with multiple blockholdings.

148711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
148711.value: In the stock market, institutional investors are very important since they hold a lot of stock shares in many different firms. They also play important roles in monitoring firms to protect their investments. They have strong incentives to monitor firms they are investing in and ability based on their superior information and experience. In this project, we check whether they can be good monitors when they have large share holdings in many different firms at the same time, which is very common these days. We can expect that they are poor monitors because they have too many firms to monitor, so their attention is limited. Or we can expect that they can be better monitors because they accumulate more experiences and information by monitoring many firms together. Our study supports the latter story. For example, if the firm's largest institutional shareholder has many large holdings in other firms at the same time, the firm's CEO is highly likely to be fired and replaced when the firm performs poorly. This finding suggests that institutional investors holding large shares in many different firms are actively monitoring firms and putting strong influence over those firms when the firms are not doing well.

148911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
148911.value: One of the critical challenges facing businesses in the manufacturing and service sectors is uncovering consumer preferences for products and services. Quantitative methods are being increasingly used in the analysis of consumer choice behavior with discrete choice methods emerging as the de facto standard. These methods are used to estimate the willingness to pay for goods and services and to develop new products and pricing strategies. Discrete choice methods can be used to estimate the effect of consumer and product attributes on consumer valuation. In the simplest choice design, a consumer is asked to state their most preferred alternative from a set of alternatives. However, even in this case, the evaluation of choice probabilities is a challenging task especially when the alternatives have correlated utilities due to shared attributes. Except in special models such as logit, simulation techniques remain the only way to analyze choice behavior. The computational challenges are compounded in more sophisticated choice designs such as asking consumers to select the best and the worst alternative. This approach known as Maximum difference scaling (Maxdiff) has become popular over the last decade due to consumers propensity to identify extreme options while revealing more about their preferences. In this project, we will build on advances in convex optimization to address such choice design problems. Currently, we have developed a convex optimization based approach to predict choices when consumers pick a single alternative from a set of alternatives. Our goal is to extend this to the Maxdiff setting. Unfortunately, the logit formula does not naturally extend to this case making the prediction problem a challenging one in itself. Furthermore, techniques that can capture the effects of correlations in this model are not known. Our objective is to develop a theoretically sound and a computationally tractable method to do prediction and estimation in this context. Then, with primary/secondary data, we will test this model and compare it with the state of art approaches. We believe that this project will be of interest to academics and practitioners due to the rising number of empirical applications that are based on Maxdiff methods. This is evidenced by commercial conjoint software such as Sawtooth integrating the Maxdiff approach into their codes due to demand for such tools to analyze sophisticated choice designs. N/A

149511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
149511.value: The past few years have seen a significant development of service-centric computing. In such a new IT paradigm, software components are packaged as independent, self-contained, and reusable services that can be delivered and consumed on demand. New value-added applications can be developed dynamically and flexibly by combining and integrating the existing services in order to automate complex business processes and to address the rapidly-changing needs of end users. Given the growing number of services provided by different service providers, many services can offer a similar and compatible functionality with different price, response time, availability, reliability, and other non-functional attributes to accommodate different modes of use. These non-functional attributes together are referred to as Quality of Service (QoS), applicable to not only atomic services but also composite services, i.e., services composed of other services. When creating a new composite service based on a user request, the QoS of the resulting composite service has to meet certain constraints to satisfy the end user. The existing works in service composition mainly focus on the methods for selecting component services based on the QoS properties pre-defined by service providers, making it difficult for a service provider to offer services with the QoS properties customized to the requests from different users. Negotiation provides the channel to let service users and providers discuss what is possible at the time of the request. More importantly, when a feasible solution is not directly available on the service market, negotiation can help service users and service providers resolve their conflicts and dynamically reach agreements at runtime. In this project, we aim to develop a method to enable negotiation for service composition. Our method can support the use of the tactics of both concession and trade-off to generate offers not only valuable to service users but also appealing to service providers. The project will advance the state of the art mainly in two perspectives. First, the existing methods to negotiation for service composition are very preliminary. The method to be developed in this project will make it possible to take the full advantage of negotiation for the purpose of flexibly developing new value-added software services. Second, to the best of our knowledge, this study is the first attempt to address coordination of multiple bilateral negotiations and the method developed in this project can help find more novel applications of automated negotiation. 在过去的几年中，以服务为中心的计算取得了重要的发展。在这样一个新的IT模式下，软件组件被打包成独立的，完备的，可重复使用的服务，这些服务按照需求交付和使用。通过组合和集成已有的服务，可以动态地和灵活地提供新的增值服务，并自动完成复杂的商业流程，来满足不断变化的客户的需求。由于不同的服务提供商提供的服务越来越多，许多服务都可以提供相似和兼容的功能，只是价格，响应时间，可用性，可靠性，和其他非功能性属性不同, 以适应不同的使用模式。这些非功能属性一起被称为作为服务质量（QoS），不仅适用于原子服务，同时也适用于由其他服务组成而成的合成服务。当基于用户请求创建一个新的组合服务时，所产生的组合服务的服务质量，需要满足一定的约束，从而满足终端用户的需求。现有的服务组合的工作主要集中在如何选择预先设定好的服务提供者，因此很难让一个服务提供商提供服务质量层次不同的服务，并根据不同用户的需求订制服务。 协商提供了一个让服务使用者和提供者在请求的时间讨论交付协议的渠道。更重要的是，当一个可行的组合不能直接在服务市场上直接获得的时候，协商可以帮助服务使用者和服务提供商解决他们的冲突并动态地在运行时达成协议。在这个项目中，我们的目标是设计一种支持协商的服务组合方法，这种方法可以使用让步和权衡的策略来生成提议，不仅对使用服务的用户有价值，同时也吸引服务提供商。这个项目的创新主要在以下两个方面。第一，现有的使用协商进行服务组合的方法是非常初步的，而在这个项目中使用的方法，使得充分利用协商来动态地开发新的增值组合服务成为可能。第二，据我们所知，这项研究首先尝试去解决多个双边谈判的协商，而且这个方法可以使得自动协商应用到更多的领域。

150111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
150111.value: In this study, we investigate whether and how a firm’s cost of equity capital is influenced by the extent of a firm’s real earnings management (REM) and accrual-based earnings management (AEM). Using a large sample of Hong Kong and Chinese listed firms, we study whether our implied cost of equity estimates are positively associated with both the extent of REM and AEM, and whether the positive association is stronger for REM than for AEM. We also investigate whether this cost-of-equity-effect is stronger in Hong Kong market than in Chinese market, and whether this effect changes temporally in Chinese market. To provide a theoretical link between earnings management and cost of capital before the formal hypothesis tests, we investigate the effect of REM and AEM on the variance and level of future cash flows. As robustness checks, we repeat the above analyses using realized returns and REM/AEM factor returns to address possible concerns on the implied cost of equity estimate as a noisy proxy for the expected return. We also differentiate the component of REM representing optimal business decisions from that representing manager’s opportunistic incentives. We expect that the cost of equity has a positive relation with REM and AEM, and that this positive relation is stronger for REM than for AEM. We posit that this positive and stronger effect comes from the fact that REM increases the variance of future cash flows (direct effect) and decreases the level of future cash flows (indirect effect) to a greater extent than does AEM. We also predict that, due to stronger institutions and their enforcement, this cost-of-equity-effect will be more pronounced in Hong Kong market than in Chinese market, and that, owing to the adoption of new accounting and auditing standards in China, this effect will be larger in post-2007 than in pre-2007 period for Chinese firms. 本研究主要考察上市公司的权益资本成本是否受到真实盈余管理和应计盈余管理程度的影响以及怎样受到影响。我们以香港证券市场和中国大陆证券市场的上市公司为样本，考察真实盈余管理和应计盈余管理的程度是否与上市公司的隐含权益资本成本正相关，以及真实盈余管理程度对公司权益资本成本的影响是否比应计盈余管理更大。同时，我们也考察香港证券市场上市公司的权益资本成本受盈余管理和应计盈余管理程度的影响是否比中国大陆证券市场的更大，以及这种差异是否会随着中国大陆证券市场的发展而缩小。在提出假说之前，为了构建盈余管理与权益资本成本的理论联系框架，我们分析真实盈余管理与应计盈余管理对公司未来现金流量和及其波动程度的影响。以隐含权益资本成本来衡量预期收益可能带来一些噪音。为了检验主要结果的稳健性，我们用公司实际收益与真实/应计盈余管理要素收益重复以上的分析。我们也尝试把提高经济效率导致的真实盈余管理和经理机会主义行为导致的真实盈余管理区分开来。我们认为，公司的真实盈余管理和应计盈余管理与公司的权益资本成本都具有正相关关系，而且这种正相关关系在真实管理方面表现得更强。我们认为可能的原因是，相对于应计盈余管理，真实盈余管理更会减少未来现金流并加剧公司未来现金流的波动程度。最后，由于香港证券市场和中国大陆市场在制度上的差异，香港证券市场上市公司的权益资本成本受到盈余管理的影响程度会与中国大陆市场不同。由于中国大陆市场的制度环境比香港市场弱，我们认为，香港证券市场上市公司的权益资本成本受盈余管理程度的影响更大。另一方面，由于中国大陆证券市场的上市公司在2007年采用了新的会计和审计准则，整个制度环境得到加强，中国大陆证券市场的上市公司权益资本成本受盈余管理程度的影响会相应提高。

150111.label: Major findings and research outcome
150111.value: This study investigates whether and how a firm’s cost of equity capital is influenced by the extent of a firm’s real earnings management (REM). Using a large sample of Hong Kong and Chinese firms over the 9-year period 2001-2008, we find that our implied cost of equity estimates are positively associated with both the extent of REM and the extent of accrual-based earnings management (AEM), but the positive association is stronger for REM than for AEM. We also provide evidence suggesting that the effect of AEM and REM on the cost of equity is more pronounced for Hong Kong firms than Chinese firms, and within Chinese firms, it is less pronounced for the state-owned enterprises (SOEs). Collectively, our results suggest that while both REM and AEM exacerbate the quality of earnings used by outside investors, REM does so to a greater extent than AEM, and thus the market demands a higher risk premium for REM activities than for AEM activities and that this cost of capital-increase effect is more prominent in a developed market like Hong Kong and mitigated by state ownership in China because of investors’ expectations for a lower level of detriments to firm fundamentals by REM due to government’s protection in a less developed market like China.

150211.label: Project Title(Chinese)
150211.value: 营销渠道中的行为控制与信任感知：与朋友角色有关吗？

150211.label: Project Objectives
150211.value: This research has four major objectives. First, drawing upon embeddedness theory and role theory (Granovetter 1985; Heide and Wathne 2006; Montgomery 1998), we differentiate between a friend role and a businessperson role for firm boundary spanners in marketing channels. We propose that a friend role may invoke a stronger reactance to behavior control than a businessperson role would, because behavior control violates the role expectations to a greater extent for a friend than for a businessperson (Heide and wathne 2006). Specifically, a controlled friend would arouse a weaker perception of trust than a controlled businessperson because of a distinct psychological contract that entails trust for a friend (Hill et al. 2009). We decompose behavior control into activity and capability control (Challagalla and Shervani 1996), and trust into goodwill and competence trust (cf. Mayer et al. 1995). We then observe the differential effects of different control modes on dimensional trust perceptions. We propose that activity control as a more obtrusive control mode invokes weaker perceptions of both goodwill and competence trust on the controlled channel member; whereas capability control undermines the controlled party’s perception of competence trust, it enhances his perception of goodwill trust in a channel dyad. We then observe the moderating effects of relationship roles on the link between behavior control modes and trust perceptions. Specifically, we observe a friend role and its moderating effects on the control-trust nexus. Compared with a controlled businessperson in a channel dyad, a controlled friend would have a weaker perception of goodwill trust for an activity control but a stronger perception of goodwill trust for a capability control. Echoing Grayson’s (2007) and Heide and Wathne’s (2006) proposition that relationships that begin as friendships may respond to conflicting role demands differently than those that begin as business relationships, we propose that compared with a controlled business friend a pure friend (defined as having a friendship first) would have a weaker perception of goodwill trust for an activity control, but a stronger perception of goodwill trust for a capability control. In addition to the above theoretical contributions, the project also has practical implications for doing business in Hong Kong and the Chinese mainland which are relationship-oriented. The findings of this study can provide practical guidance for managers to design their control modes and strategies to enhance their cooperative relationships with the local channel partners. We target at Journal of Marketing Research.

150211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
150211.value: Control is important in business transactions to ensure desired business performance. However, control seems to conflict with another important business element, trust. Control as an obtrusive action undermines trust because control seemingly signifies suspicions about the controlled party’s intention and/or ability in conducting the business transaction. To clarify this confusion, scholars classify formal control in business into output control and behavior control. Output control monitors the visible consequences of a partner’s actions, whereas behavior control involves regulating behaviors by evaluating the processes and methods that produce the focal outcomes (Anderson and Oliver 1987). Research finds that output control functions to mitigate opportunism, whereas behavior control is elusive in its effects on trust and opportunism (Das and Teng 1998; Heide et al. 2007). This project proposes that there are three reasons that lead to the above inclusive results of the control-trust relation. First, prior research simply assumes that the two parties involved in the control play a single role of businessperson (Granovetter 1985). Businesspeople can also become friends because of long-term cooperation (Heide and Wathne 2006); if a friend or business friend is put under control, what is his/her reaction to the control action in terms of his/her perceptions of trust. A friend may have different role expectations than a businessperson has and thus control may invoke different trust perceptions between a friend and a businessperson (Grayso 2007). Second, behavior control can be further classified into activity control and capability control. Activity control involves the monitoring of firm marketing activity-related behaviors; capability control emphasizes the controlled party’s capability development that enables performance (Challagalla and Shervani 1996). These two behavior control modes may have different effects on trust perceptions for the controlled party. Third, prior research treats trust as a global concept without discerning its dimensions. Trust can be decomposed into goodwill and competence trust. Competence trust requires the trustee’s ability to do what he is expected to do, whereas goodwill trust emphasizes the trustee’s benevolence to consider the trustor’s interest (Mayer et al. 1995). Thus, we have a 2x2 (activity vs. capability control; businessperson vs. friend role) matrix in which different modes of behavior control may cast varied perceptions of trust on the controlled party (Hill et al. 2009), which in turn are the function of his/her perceived relationship roles (Heide and Wathne 2006). This research attempts to unravel this matrix to shed light on the aforementioned control-trust controversy. 商业交易中的控制是为了保证商业的绩效，但商业控制似乎和商业的另一重要因素--信任，发生冲突。控制作为一种介入行为可能降低信任，因为控制传递了一种对商业伙伴能力与善意的怀疑信号。为了澄清混淆，学者们将控制分为结果控制和行为控制。结果控制监控可见的商业结果，而行为控制包括监控结果得以产生的过程和方法。研究发现，结果控制有助于减轻机会主义行为，而行为控制对于信任的产生和抑制机会主义的效果却是人言人殊。 本研究认为，至少有三种因素，导致了上述行为控制-信任关系的不确定性结果。第一，以前的研究均基于一个简单的假设，即介入控制过程的两个主体均仅扮演单一的商人角色。然而，通过长期合作接触，商人可以变成朋友。那么，对一个朋友或商业朋友进行控制，他（她）会有何种反应并产生何种信任感知呢？相对于纯粹的商人，一个朋友会有不同的角色期望因而对行为控制产生不同的信任感知。第二，行为控制可以进一步细分为活动控制和能力控制。活动控制是指对企业营销活动相关的行为进行监控；而能力控制强调对被控制企业能力发展的指导和监控，因为这些能力有益于提高合作绩效。这两种不同的行为控制可能对被控制企业产生不同的信任感知。第三，以前的研究一般将信任看做单一维度的构念，没有区分其不同的维度。信任可以进一步细分为善意信任与能力信任。能力信任要求被信任者有能力进行所要求的商业活动，而善意信任强调被信任者有诚意兼顾信任者的利益。综上所述，我们就有一个2X2矩阵（活动信任vs. 能力信任；朋友角色vs.商人角色）：不同的行为控制会产生不同的信任感知，而这些信任感知又同时是被控制企业的感知角色（朋友或商人）的函数。在本研究中，我们试图解析这个矩阵，从而为上述控制--信任争论提供答案。

150211.label: Realisation of objectives
150211.value: This study had four major objectives: 1) examining the effect of role perception (a friend role vs. a businesspeople role) on trust perception when behavior control is implemented; 2) examining the effect of specific behavior control modes (activity control vs. capability control) on trust perception; 3) examining the moderating effect of role perception on the link between behavior control modes and trust perceptions; and 4) distinguishing between a relationship dyad that begins as friends and one that begins as business partners and then friends in terms of their effects on trust perception when different behavior control modes are conducted. Specifically, we contend that the distributors who develop friendship with suppliers through business activities may have higher tolerance for the activity control, because they are more likely to regard the activity control as a requisite of business. Based on the two studies (one experimental simulation and the other longitudinal filed study), we generally confirmed the research hypotheses for the first three research objectives. Specifically, we found that different behavior control modes will produce different trust perceptions, that role perception (friend role vs. businessperson role) will have different effects on trust perception when behavior control modes are conducted, and that the role perception will moderate the effects of behavior control modes on trust perception. These finding shed fresh light on the long-standing controversy on the control-trust nexus. However, our data were unable to uncover the two types of friendship-pure friendship and commercial friendship-in terms of their differential effects on trust perception given the different behavior control modes. We leave this as one of the future research directions that draws upon innovative research methodology.
