rows: This research has four major objectives. First, drawing upon embeddedness theory and role theory (Granovetter 1985; Heide and Wathne 2006; Montgomery 1998), we differentiate between a friend role and a businessperson role for firm boundary spanners in marketing channels. We propose that a friend role may invoke a stronger reactance to behavior control than a businessperson role would, because behavior control violates the role expectations to a greater extent for a friend than for a businessperson (Heide and wathne 2006). Specifically, a controlled friend would arouse a weaker perception of trust than a controlled businessperson because of a distinct psychological contract that entails trust for a friend (Hill et al. 2009).

We decompose behavior control into activity and capability control (Challagalla and Shervani 1996), and trust into goodwill and competence trust (cf. Mayer et al. 1995). We then observe the differential effects of different control modes on dimensional trust perceptions. We propose that activity control as a more obtrusive control mode invokes weaker perceptions of both goodwill and competence trust on the controlled channel member; whereas capability control undermines the controlled party’s perception of competence trust, it enhances his perception of goodwill trust in a channel dyad.

We then observe the moderating effects of relationship roles on the link between behavior control modes and trust perceptions. Specifically, we observe a friend role and its moderating effects on the control-trust nexus. Compared with a controlled businessperson in a channel dyad, a controlled friend would have a weaker perception of goodwill trust for an activity control but a stronger perception of goodwill trust for a capability control.

Echoing Grayson’s (2007) and Heide and Wathne’s (2006) proposition that relationships that begin as friendships may respond to conflicting role demands differently than those that begin as business relationships, we propose that compared with a controlled business friend a pure friend (defined as having a friendship first) would have a weaker perception of goodwill trust for an activity control, but a stronger perception of goodwill trust for a capability control.

In addition to the above theoretical contributions, the project also has practical implications for doing business in Hong Kong and the Chinese mainland which are relationship-oriented. The findings of this study can provide practical guidance for managers to design their control modes and strategies to enhance their cooperative relationships with the local channel partners.
We target at Journal of Marketing Research.

150211.label: Major findings and research outcome
150211.value: This study argues that trust product in the process of business control will depend on the specific behavior control modes chosen and the role perceptions of the controlled parties. Based on a 3 (control: activity control, capability control, and output control) × 2 (perceived role: friend versus businesspeople) matrix, this study conducted two studies ( a simulated laboratory experiment and a longitudinal field study) to cross-validate the following findings: 1)Activity control will erode both goodwill and competence trust in marketing relationships; 2)Capability control will undermine competence trust; however, it will enhance goodwill trust; 3)Activity control will erode more goodwill trust for a controlled friend than for a controlled businessperson; 4)Activity control erodes competence trust equally for a controlled friend and for a controlled businessperson; 5)Capability control enhance goodwill trust more for a controlled friend than for a controlled businessperson; 6)Capability control erodes competence trust equally for a controlled friend and for a controlled businessperson

150211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
150211.value: Because we were unable to examine the effects when behavior control modes are used upon business-friends vs. friend-businesspeople (Grayson, 2007), future research may tap into this issue. Also, future research may take a dynamic perspective to look at the control-trust nexus during the course of relationship lifecycle. A network perspective is also promising as the third-party may affect the controllers' choice of different behavior control modes.

150211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
150211.value: Control is necessary and important in business relationships. Without proper control, business partners may not be willing to make commitment and may act in an unethical way in the cooperation. However, too much control such as tight control over the process or behavior may reduce partners' perception of trust. Previous studies have produced much confusion about the relationship between behavior control and trust. This study tries to resolve the controversy by distinguishing between businesspeople and friends who are under control. Also, we tell apart two types of behavior control into activity control and capability control. We then investigate the trust production under different behavior controls between controlled businesspeople and controlled friends. We find that trust perception will vary because of different role perceptions as well as different behavior control modes. The findings of this study alert managers who aim to cultivate trust to pay attention to behavior control modes when cooperating with different types of partner, e.g., firends or business partners.

150511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
150511.value: 数量就是力量。在商业领域，聚合产品需求的能力已经成为一种获得划算的交易的本领，例如，更低的购买价格（Sandler 1992）。网上的团购机构就是这种观念的一种体现。它通过聚合众多对同一种商品有需求的买家的订单，从而获得价格上的折扣（Geoffrion和Krishnan 2003）。通过聚合一大群买家的需求，团购机构能够比让买家单独进行购买更快速，更大量地销售产品。可以预计，这种够给消费者和商家带来价值的网上团购机构（团购网站）将成为一种新兴的销售方式。 然而，从90年代末建立开始至今，西方国家的团购机构发展的经历跌宕起伏。最早的两家团购机构，Mobshop和Mercata，甚至还为这种新型商业模式的专利争论不休（Gottlieb 2000）。它们以及它们的追随者，例如 www.actBIG.com, www.zwirl.com, and www.shop2gether.com，所采用的团购商业模式是一种类似于B2C（Business to Consumer; 商家对客户）的商业模式。这些团购机构的运营情况更像是一类网上商店，它们向客户提供一系列的产品并负责相关的买卖交易和发货。然而，这类团购机构的发展并没有持续多么长的时间。到2001年，Mobshop和Mercata接连地停止了它们的业务（Flynn 2001；Sandoval和Kawamoto 2001）。 有趣的是，东方的一些国家，尤其是中国的商家在此时对团购产生了浓厚地兴趣。中国的第一家本土团购网站liba.com于2003年建立，至今仍然运作良好。和早期的团购机构相比，中国的团购机构的作用更像是一种媒介。消费者通过它可以和销售商或生产厂家直接议价。在香港，我们同样地见证了团购机构的兴起和发展。如ubuyibuy.com和funshare.com等团购机构在2010年7月份开始运营。正因为团购机构在东西方发展的差异，使得学者和企业家有兴趣来理解为什么团购能够在东方（例如，香港）的国家里兴盛和流行（例如，Arredy 2006；Tang 2008）。同时，团购机构的发展在西方国家里也有复苏的迹象。例如，近期在美国流行的Groupon.com和LivingSocial.com等团购机构。 综上所述，本项目旨在研究能够导致可持续发展团购业务的团购机制和市场差异？换句话说，本项目设法回答这个问题：如何通过积极的消费者反映来推动和促进网上团购的可持续型商业发展力？ 为了做到这一点，本项目以互赖理论为核心（Rusbult和van Lange 2003），提出了一套建立网上团购的可持续型商业发展力的总体指导原则。即，通过吸引和聚合有高亲和力的消费者进行团购，进而使得团购机构形成一种可持续的商业发展力并且给消费者，商家以及团购服务提供商带来利益。本项目的研究主要分为两部分。第一部分将重点关注以下几个方面：1）发展一套适用于研究团购机构的理论基础（包括回顾团购机构发展初始至今，中西方学者有关团购机构技术和制度上的研究进展）；2）在香港开展一系列相关的实证研究。这些实证研究关注于理解不同的团购机制会不会对消费者对于团购行为的感知产生影响，以及这种影响是如何产生的。本项目研究的第二部分将建立在第一部分的研究成果之上，通过在中国大陆地区大规模的实地实验增强理解团购机制对消费者感知团购行为的影响。通过本项目的研究，我们不仅能够获得针对香港团购从业者的管理启示，而且我们能够向即将进入团购市场的商家和寻求可持续发展团购业务的商家提供管理启示。

150511.label: Realisation of objectives
150511.value: This project studies group-buying institution that is prevalent in the electronic commerce platform in Hong Kong and elsewhere globally.Three objectives are proposed and followed during the execution of the research. Objective 1 seeks to identify pertinent design principles for GBI and a paper, co-authored by the research collaborators, is written and presented in an international human-computer interaction conference. Objective 2 seeks to understand consumers' procurement choice when facing GBI. A laboratory experiment was conducted by the principle investigator and a paper was written and recently accepted by Journal of Associations for Information Systems (a top 4 journals in the Information Systems discipline) for publication. Objective 3 seeks to build on the earlier two objectives and conduct a larger scale empirical investigation. A large set of data on GBI, involving users from two major cities in China, is collected and analyzed. The findings are reported in a working paper appended in this report.

150511.label: Major findings and research outcome
150511.value: GBI is a form of electronic commerce shopping outlet that allows consumers to aggregate their purchase demands to gain significant price discount. Several important findings based on the two journal papers (one accepted by Journal of the Association for Information Systems and another paper currently revising) can be made. They include: (1) the mere provision of GBI may not be sufficiently motivate consumers to buy and the provision of information on other buyers may lead to polarized behavior; (2) however, the concurrent presence of conditional cue, i.e., a buyer is not required to commit to a purchase if the best price is not met, could somewhat alleviate the buying concern; (3) GBI should be cautioned of how far (geographically spatial) a promotional message should be sent with less concrete promotional messages to effective in inducing purchases. Taking together, the entire research highlights the importance of the GBI mechanisms as well as the GBI promotional message formulation.

150511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
150511.value: This research project opens up windows of opportunities. For example, this research has examined two GBI mechanisms, namely information cue and conditional cue, and there are many other cues that are put in place in the GBI, including the product details and assurance. Further works could validate how these additional product and merchant information can induce prompt purchases from consumers. Also, we observe from our findings that purchases could be concentrated on several specific time of a day and it will be interesting to see which kinds of products will be more well-received on different time of the day.

150511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
150511.value: GBI is a form of electronic commerce shopping outlet that allows consumers to aggregate their purchase demands to gain significant price discount. This research project identifies and evaluates features of GBI, in the forms of providing purchase assurance and information, as well as analyzes consumer responses to to GBI promotional messages. Overall, this research addresses the questions of (1) how to attract consumers to visit GBI purchases through promotional messages, and (2) how to encourage these consumers to make a purchase at GBI upon landing at the GBI website.

150811.value: 本研究旨在探索和評估非專家群體通過社交媒體網站（比如google，維琪百科或者twitter，微博）上的群體行為，來預測未知事件或者解答困難問題的能力。眾所周知，準確地判斷未知事物是相當困難的。作為一個獨立的個體，無論是專家還是非專家，都不擅長預測未知事件。更有甚者，在其他方面表現已經很優秀的團隊表現也不能保證預期的協作效果，更不用說超出預期的效果了。 然而，令人驚訝的是，非專家群體似乎能夠很好地判斷是非，精確地評估未知事物或者預測不確定事件。 這些非專家群體在某些方面甚至比專家預測更加準確，比如，電影票房成功與否 （如：好萊塢證券交易所網站上的預測）；體育賽事的結果（Yahoo！Pickem）；政治大選；商品價格 （如：黃金，油價）；以及新產品的延期發佈（波音787）。更有意思的是，這種情況不僅出現在非專家群體直接針對問題發表他們的看法的時候，還會出現在當他們的行為被注意到的時候（例如在社交媒體上搜索資訊）。因此，本文的目的在於研究非專家群體通過在社交媒體中的行為預測及判斷的能力。 本研究共有三個目的。第一，建模並驗證以上現象；第二， 找出最關鍵的假設以及影響集體智慧成敗的因素。例如共用多重性，最初的個人見解以及多樣性所扮演的角色（或者是不同成員在集體中的獨立性）；第三，發掘在集體智慧中，內在獨立個體的評估方法，以及群體構成方式如何影響總體結果。 我們的三個研究目標是分別探索這三個問題的答案。為了達成這些目標，本文採用了三階段的研究，其中集體智慧的表現是通過三個實驗來評估的。我們希望通過本研究，證明個體在獲取知識，或者獲取其他價值這些興趣的驅動下，所進行的社交媒體行為，將會很好的預測未知事件。由於現有的假設還存在疑點，我們還希望在本研究中用更公允的觀點來看待觀念的多樣性以及集體的多樣性。通過這些探索，本研究將啟發關於個體表現，名義群體以及真實群體的討論。最後，本研究將在個體預測及判斷方法，合作的特性及調整，以及專業背景的重要性等方面提出新的看法。 這是一個有價值的研究，因為本研究提高了當前學者在個體判斷以及決策上得研究興趣。我們試圖用更好的資訊系統來支援這種很難實現的行為，並且用持續的組織實踐來支援在不確定且資訊缺乏的情況下的決策行為。這種技術在香港已經被廣泛應用，例如，我們可以更好的預測房地產市場，或者對即將發生的疾病（例如甲型流感）更早地發出預警。

150811.label: Realisation of objectives
150811.value: 1. Empirically validate a model of collective intelligence exhibited through activity in social media. (100% achieved) The research employed a model, which was empirically validated. The model defined judgment quality (of the collective) as dependent variable, and collective size and expertise as independent variables. Task difficulty was modeled as moderating the impact of expertise and collective size. The model was tested and validated with 478 subjects. To validate the model, the research had to develop quality measures for collective intelligence, so as to enable judgments on the quality of collective intelligence and to make comparisons between collectives and individuals. For the measurement of collective intelligence, the challenging question is “how close (to the true value) is close enough”? The answer cannot be given in absolute terms. For example, a collective judgment 50% higher than the true value may be considered poor, but if all individuals are further from the true value, then the collective intelligence is still superior. Thus, the measurement of collective intelligence quality used two separate relative measures, independent of the details of individual problems. One measure was based on the overall size of the collective error vs. individual errors, the other based on the number of times the collective performed better than individuals. Two core measures were defined: collective intelligence quality, and “win ratio”. The first measure relied on the formulation by Page, which identifies two measures, collective error (CE) and individual error (IE). Collective error, the squared error of the collective prediction, represents the difference between the true value and the averaged estimates of all individuals. The individual error aggregates the squared errors (difference between their estimates and the true value) of all the participants. It thus captures the average inaccuracy of individual guesses. Individual error (squared-average) is a benchmark to compare the performance of the collective. Using IE and CE, one can define a single measure, collective intelligence quality CIQ = IE/CE, as an overall measure of the collectives’ superiority. The theoretical minimum for CIQ is 1.0. At 1.0, the collective’s aggregate error is equal to the sum of all individual errors, thus reflecting no collective intelligence. CIQ values < 10 identify moderate quality improvements. CIQ is useful when comparing different judgment problems whose mean results and thus errors differ widely, and as an expertise benchmark. Second, when the aggregate judgment of a number of N individuals in a collective is compared to the judgment of each of the individuals in that collective, we can compute how many times out of the N comparisons the individual judgment is (as good or) better and how many times the collective is better. Thus one can define a “win ratio” (WR), following earlier research. 2. Challenge collective intelligence assumptions by determining the importance of shared insights versus collective diversity for performance. (100% achieved) Collective intelligence typically refers to the high task performance of large aggregates of loosely connected individuals. In a broader sense, it encompasses a host of meanings, related to the behavior of a “complex adaptive system” and the distributed knowledge or capability in human systems where the whole is greater than the sum of the parts. Recently, research has focused on how digital networks and information technologies are enabling collectives to create valuable knowledge and to make better decisions. The ability of the Internet to connect large numbers of diverse individuals, combined with electronic collaboration technologies that facilitate aggregation of responses from many parties are opening a new era of collective intelligence. While many studies support the notion of the wisdom of crowds, it does not mean that collectives always outperform individuals in terms of judgment quality. In particular, diversity and expertise are necessary properties for a collective to be wise. Diversity is important so that the collective has access to different individual skill sets and different sources of information in order to avoid bias. Furthermore, the collective must have expertise in that individuals understand the problem and collectively make positive contributions to solving it. If everyone guesses randomly, due to a lack of expertise, no valuable information can be extracted from the responses. In addition, no amount of diversity and expertise will matter if individuals are completely unfamiliar with the task at hand, thus being unable to apply their information and expertise. Accordingly, the research conjectured that the co-existence of diversity, expertise, and task familiarity are key to tapping into collective intelligence. Specific assumptions that were (correctly) challenged included the size of the collective, and the impact of task difficulty. The research was able to demonstrate that size did not matter beyond a relatively moderate number, e.g., 100-200, and that task difficulty was best in a medium range, not too difficulty, but also not too easy. The research was further able to demonstrate that subjects used simple yet collectively powerful algorithms for prediction, but also that some biases were introduced through the processing of information from others (which should be minimized through independence). 3. Identify the reasoning methods and aggregation mechanisms underlying collective intelligence and use of social media in the process. (100% achieved) The collective appeared most effective when tasks required access to a wide range of specialized information. In such situations, the collective performed significantly better than the average individual. When tasks became easy, differences between collective and individual problem solving narrowed substantially, not because of poor performance of the collective, but because of high performance by the average individual, thus leaving less room for improvement. Still, easy tasks yielded more benefit from the collective than the most difficult task. This fits the assumptions, as high difficulty would lead to random guessing, whereas low difficulty would lead to heuristic problem solving, and thus would have improvement potential, although limited. Correspondingly, one reasoning method was to decompose a problem to effectively reduce task complexity. Decomposition allows more specialization, better contextualization, and thus better use of information. Each individual task is therefore better defined and thus easier, yet in aggregate, their result will provide the desired answer. Judgments may likewise be simplified by restricting the solution set, such as by setting upper and lower bounds (solution shaping). Problem and solution shaping are well known techniques in task completion and even problem solving. Results clearly show that collective intelligence is not the result of random-error prone guessing and thus not a trivial outcome of the Law of Large Numbers, i.e., the reduction of error terms through aggregation. Collective intelligence is also not a mysterious property that emerges when collectives come together, but is explained through the aggregation of partial explanatory models, which taken together explain increasing amounts of variance. Furthermore, because collective intelligence requires the existence of partial models whose aggregation leads to improvement, collective tasks cannot be too easy (allowing everyone to formulate complete models) or too difficult (preventing anyone from creating a partial model). In addition, because collective intelligence relies on the weighted aggregation of partial models, diversity and independence within the crowd are required to generate a rich, unbiased aggregate model. Thus, by explaining the imperfect algorithmic nature of solution finding, one can also explain the need for large enough, but not infinite size collectives, the degradation of performance when tasks become too difficult, and mechanisms to enable collectives even on difficult tasks.

150811.label: Major findings and research outcome
150811.value: Model The research empirically validated a model that explained judgment quality based on collective size, subject expertise, and task difficulty. Collective Size It was conjectured that collective size improved collective judgment quality, but with diminishing returns as the collective size increased. Results suggest that for moderately difficult problems a sample size beyond 100 did not matter. For difficult problems, outside the “collective range”, collective size mattered up to N = 200. Role of Task Difficulty Task difficulty has often been ignored in the research on individual and group or collective problem solving. More precisely, task difficulty has been frequently controlled or randomized, rather than treated as an independent or moderating variable. This research departed from that approach and explored the impact of task difficulty on the phenomenon of collective intelligence effectiveness. Specifically, the collective appeared most effective when tasks required access to a wide range of specialized information. In such situations, the collective performed significantly better than the average individual. When tasks became easy, differences between collective and individual problem solving narrowed substantially, not because of poor performance of the collective, but because of high performance by the average individual, thus leaving less room for improvement. Thus, it was learnt that collective intelligence is not unequivocally better than individual intelligence, even if conditions of diversity, non-randomness of solution, and individual knowledge availability are present. We thus note that collective intelligence as a digital ecosystem has most “survival strength” in situations where task difficulty is moderate. Therefore, if task difficulty can be actively managed, and reduced from high levels down to moderate levels by members of the collective, we should expect increased performance and thus increased sustainability of such collective intelligence digital ecosystems. Reasoning Mechanisms Reasoning mechanisms in collectively are surprisingly simple. Subjects frequently apply anchor-and-adjust as a mechanism to transfer expertise from the known to a less understood problem. When drawing on evidence from available sources, subjects update their beliefs in an asymmetric manner. Essentially it appears that subjects welcome any information that helps them increase or maintain their confidence level, thus suggesting a confirmation bias. Information that can help increase confidence is weighted almost twice as strongly as confidence lowering information, a finding that echos the asymmetry in people’s treatment of probabilities identified by Kahnemann & Tversky (1979).

150811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
150811.value: The project revealed several interesting results, all of which will benefit from further exploration in future work. Three are mentioned here: First, collectives benefit from larger numbers in their midst, to compensate for systematic errors of some individuals who judged without knowledge and thus would have introduced too much bias. This goes somewhat counter the underlying assumptions of collective intelligence, and emphasizes error correction as an important element of crowd problem solving. Second, collective performance differs significantly based on performance, but not as expected based on prior research, which conjectured advantages for very familiar or very unfamiliar tasks. Instead, rather the tasks whose difficulty lies between the familiar and the unfamiliar. For those problems, the impact of collective size is strongest, as is the effect of expertise transfer on judgment quality. Future research should identify factors that explain task difficulty and performance degradation a priori. Finally, judgment quality appears to deteriorate in stages. When collectives are familiar with the task, their judgment models are highly consistent and accurate. More difficult tasks still provide relatively consistent, but more biased and less accurate results, whereas very difficult tasks lead to random guessing, and inconsistent as well as inaccurate judgments.

150811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
150811.value: The research sought to understand and evaluate the ability of collectives of non-experts to predict the outcome of uncertain events or to answer difficult questions, exhibited through their aggregate actions in social media sites (i.e., websites on the Internet such as Google, Wikipedia, or Twitter). Making judgments about unknowns is difficult. Individuals, non-experts and experts alike, are not particularly good at it, and even group performance does not provide expected synergies and performance increases. Surprisingly, collectives of non-experts seem to perform judgment tasks well, accurately estimating unknowns or forecasting uncertain events. Collectives outperform experts on questions such as estimating movie box office successes or failures, outcomes of sports events or political elections, commodity prices, as well as new product delays. Three objectives were targeted. First, the research identified a model for collective performance. Second, it surfaced critical assumptions, which determine success or failure of collective intelligence, i.e., the multiplicity of shared, previously private insights, the role of diversity and collective size, as well as task difficulty. Third, the research explored individual estimation methods underlying collective intelligence and the aggregation impact on overall outcome.

151111.label: Project Title(Chinese)
151111.value: 您真的擔心您的信息隱私嗎？在線社交網絡平臺中隱私態度-行為矛盾的研究

151111.label: Project Objectives
151111.value: The first objective is to identify dimensions of a privacy attitude-behavior gap. I will extend the taxonomy of information privacy concerns that have been established in privacy literature and identify corresponding user behaviors in the context of SNS. The second objective is to validate the dimensions of the privacy attitude-behavior gap identified. Given that personality traits of individuals have been widely confirmed to affect their online behaviors, including privacy behaviors, a nomological model with three salient “Big Five Personality Traits,” namely, extraversion, conscientiousness, and neuroticism, as predictors of various dimensions of the privacy attitude-behavior gap will be proposed and empirically tested. The third objective is to investigate the antecedents of privacy-threatening behaviors of users. A bounded rationality perspective will be used. Due to the complex online environment and their limited processing capability, SNS users often utilize simple and available cues and heuristics rather than conduct rational assessment of all factors for or against all possible courses of privacy actions. As such, the bounded rationality perspective will help identify a set of decision factors affecting privacy-threatening behaviors of individuals in SNS. An empirical study will be conducted to validate the set of antecedents of privacy-threatening behaviors in SNS. A survey will be administrated and respondents’ behaviors in SNS will be coded. With these data collected, the project will reveal most influential decision factors that affect a particular type of privacy-threatening behaviors in SNS.

151111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
151111.value: Despite concerns of Internet users on online information privacy, they often do not live up to their self-reported privacy concerns. They often engage in many paradoxical privacy-threatening behaviors (e.g., excessive self-disclosure of personal information, and overlooking of privacy practices and privacy-enhancing technologies). This inconsistency between privacy concerns of individuals and their own privacy-threatening behaviors is called privacy attitude-behavior paradox. This project will explore the nature and dimensions of individuals’ privacy attitude-behavior gap and investigate the antecedents of their privacy-threatening behaviors. This project will be conducted in the specific context of online social networking sites (SNS). With half a billion active users of Facebook (a leading SNS in Hong Kong and worldwide) around the world who use it as a social, expressional, and entertainment platform, privacy leakages and violations have increasingly become a critical concern for SNS users. The existence of a privacy attitude-behavior gap will lead to illusory controls and misperceptions of users about their own privacy behaviors in SNS, and ineffective privacy practices, policies and privacy-enhancing technologies, which are often based on individuals’ self-reported privacy concerns. Two subprojects are proposed herein. The first subproject is to explore the nature and dimensions of a privacy attitude-behavior gap. Although there are studies that have reported the presence of such a gap, few of those have comprehensively and theoretically investigated the nature and dimensions of this gap. By extending a well-established taxonomy of information privacy concerns, I will identify specific dimensions of the gap. To validate these dimensions, a nomological model with three salient “Big Five Personality Traits,” namely, extraversion, conscientiousness, and neuroticism, as predictors of various dimensions of a privacy attitude-behavior gap will be developed. The second subproject will investigate the antecedents of privacy-threatening behaviors from a bounded rationality perspective. Due to their limited processing capability, SNS users often utilize simple and available cues and heuristics rather than conduct rational assessment of all factors for or against all possible courses of privacy actions. Based on this perspective, a set of antecedents will be identified and their effects on various privacy-threatening behaviors will be tested. This proposed research will fill a theoretical gap in a privacy attitude-behavior paradox and help understand factors leading to privacy-threatening behaviors of SNS users. The results will address the emerging online privacy leakage and violation issues, and hold great implications for privacy policymakers and legislators, SNS practitioners, and users to protect their online information privacy. 盡管網民表達了對網上信息隱私問題的擔憂，但是他們的實際行為卻並不與他們自己所表達的隱私擔憂一致。網民經常作出許多對隱私有威脅的行為，例如過度的展現個人信息、忽視隱私條款和隱私保護技術等。隱私態度-行為矛盾指的就是這種個體對隱私的擔憂和采取對隱私有威脅行為之間的不一致。本研究就將探索個體隱私態度-行為差距的本質和維度，並且辨識導致采取對隱私有威脅行為的原因。 本研究將于在線社交網絡（SNS）的環境下展開。隨著全世界範圍內近5億用戶通過Facebook——一個在香港和世界範圍內領先的社交網絡，進行社交、情感表達，以及娛樂，隱私泄漏和侵害已經愈發成為在線社交網絡使用者最為擔心的問題。隱私態度-行為差距的存在將會導致對用戶在在線社交網絡上隱私行為的虛假控制和錯誤認知，使得基於個體表述對隱私擔憂的隱私條款、政策和隱私保護技術形同虛設。 本研究包括兩個子研究課題。第一個子研究課題將探索隱私-行為差距的本質和維度。盡管已經有研究反映了這種差距的存在，但是對這種差距本質和維度的全面系統分析還十分缺乏。通過對一個較為成熟的信息隱私擔憂拓撲結構的擴展，本子研究課題將辨識這種差距的維度。第二個子研究課題將從有限理性角度分析隱私受威脅行為的影響因素。由於受到處理能力的限制，在線社交網絡用戶通常應用簡單易行的啟發式方法而不是理性對隱私行動所有可能過程中牽涉到的因素進行評估。從這個角度出發，本子研究課題將辨識一系列的影響因素，並且分析它們對各類對隱私有威脅行為的影響作用。 本研究將填補隱私態度-行為矛盾方面存在的理論空白，並且有助於理解在線社交網絡用戶采取對隱私有威脅行為的理解。研究結果將闡述越來越嚴重的在線隱私泄露和侵犯問題，能夠為隱私政策制定方、在線社交網絡運營商，以及用戶保護自身的在線信息隱私提供有益的啟示與借鑒。

151411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
151411.value: The proposed research aims to provide systematic evidence on the firm-level relation between the use of Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) and stock price crash risk. An SPV is a legally distinct entity with a limited life created for a special purpose to carry out limited activities for a ‘‘sponsor’’ company. SPVs were originally created to serve the purpose of economic benefits such as lowering financing costs. However, investigations on Enron and other Enron style corporate scandals find that firms have been using SPVs in financial statement window-dressing. When a sponsor company avoids consolidating the SPV in its financial statements, it can improve its balance sheet by reporting less debt and its income statement by reporting higher earnings. For example, in a typical sale-leaseback transaction, the SPV borrows money to purchase the sponsor’s fixed asset. Then the sponsor leases the asset back from the SPV under operating lease. These transactions first help the sponsor reduce leverage by not consolidating the SPV’s borrowing in its balance sheet, and second facilitate the sponsor in managing earnings by recognizing gains on the sale and controlling the timing and amount of the lease payments. When management engages in earnings management to conceal bad news and overstate performance, bad news will be stockpiled within the firm. The complex structure and insufficient disclosures on SPVs facilitate managers withholding and accumulating bad news. However, there is an upper limit to the amount of bad news that managers can absorb. Once the amount of accumulated bad news reaches the upper limit, it will come out at once, leading to large, negative, price movements - stock price crashes. Our primary research objective is to test the hypothesis that SPV use increases the likelihood of future crash occurrences. In addition, we also aim to provide evidence on whether effective external monitoring mechanisms can mitigate the effect of SPV use on crash risk and whether firms that have foreign SPVs have even greater crash risk. While case analyses on Enron and others show that SPV use has caused their collapse, there is a lack of evidence on whether SPV use in general is associated with higher crash risk. The proposed research, to the best of our knowledge will be the first to provide general results on this broader issue using large sample analyses. The results will offer important policy implications for accounting regulations in the US, China and other economies. 本研究为特殊目的机构的使用和股价急降风险的关系提供系统的证据。特殊目的机构是赞助公司为了执行某些有限业务所成立的在法律上独立有年限的个体。赞助公司成立特殊目的机构最早是为了一些经济上的利益，比如降低融资成本。但是，对安然公司丑闻和类似丑闻的调查表明特殊目的机构被大量使用来美化公司报表。如果赞助公司可以不用将特殊目的机构合并在报表上，就可以在资产负债表上少报负债，在损益表上多报盈余。举个例子，在一个典型的卖出租回的交易中，特殊目的机构可以借钱来购买赞助公司的固定资产。然后赞助公司再把卖出的固定资产租回来。这些交易首先能帮助赞助公司降低负债因为特殊目的机构的借款不用合并进赞助公司的报表，其次还可以方便赞助公司通过控制卖固定资产的收益数目和租金的数目和时间来操纵盈余数目。 当管理层通过从事盈余管理来掩盖坏消息和夸大好消息的时候，坏消息会积累在公司内部。特殊目的机构由于结构复杂和披露不足更加有利于管理层用来延迟和积累坏消息。 但坏消息的积累不是无限的。一旦达到上限， 它们会一次性涌现出来，造成大的负面的股价下跌，称作股价急降。我们的研究首要目的就是要考察是否特殊目的机构的使用会增加未来股价急降的概率。而且，我们还要研究是否有效的外部监控机制可以降低特殊目的机构的使用对股价急降概率的负面影响和是否在国外成立的特殊目的机构对股价急降概率的影响更大。虽然对安然和其它机构的案例研究表明特殊目的机构的使用导致了它们的崩溃，但是还缺乏对特殊目的机构的使用和股价急降概率之间关系的广泛研究和系统证据。 我们的研究，就我们所知， 将会是首次用大样本来研究这个课题以提供更加广泛的研究结果。我们的研究结果会对美国，中国和其它经济体有着重要的政策含义。

151411.label: Major findings and research outcome
151411.value: Two studies are developed from the proposed research. In the first study, we examine the relation between the use of Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) and stock price crash risk. SPVs were originally created to serve the purpose of economic benefits, for example, to isolate financial risk and raise fund at lower interest costs. However, investigations following the collapse of Enron and other corporate scandals reveal that firms have been using SPVs in earnings management by exploiting the loopholes in SPV accounting. Because of the complex structure and insufficient disclosures of SPVs, managers are able to withhold and accumulate bad news for an extended period and bad news will be stockpiled within the firm. However, when the amount of accumulated bad news reaches the upper limit, it will come out at once, leading to large, negative, price movements - stock price crashes. Since SPV use facilitates managerial opportunistic behavior, we predict and find a positive association between SPV use and crash risk. Moreover, we show that the positive relation between SPV use and crash risk is attenuated when firms have stronger external monitoring mechanisms such as higher institutional ownership, higher analyst coverage and higher take over treat. The PI and one of the Co-Is developed another paper based on the data and theory of the proposed research. The proposed research focuses on the equity market consequence of SPV usage. The PI and one of the Co-Is also conducted analyses on the credit market consequence of SPV usage by linking SPVs to bank loan contracting. More specifically, we find that (1) the use of SPVs negatively affects loan contracting terms, including higher loan rate, collateral requirement, and covenants; (2) the above associations between SPV use and bank loan contracting, are more pronounced if the borrower reports foreign SPVs, if the borrower has higher default risk, or if the borrower borrows term loans rather than non-term loans.

151411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
151411.value: it is possible to develop more studies from the proposed research. For example, it will be interesting to look at the reaction from credit default swap (CDS) market to the initiation of SPVs. CDS spreads (prices) depend critically on firm value and the quality of information about firm value. Since we argue that SPV activities will decrease the quality of information about firm value, we expect a negative reaction from the CDS market toward SPV initiation.

151411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
151411.value: The findings from the two studies developed from the GRF grant show that SPV usage has negative consequences on both equity and credit market. Therefore, our findings provide useful insights to regulators on the disclosures and accounting treatments of SPVs. In the first paper, we show that mangers use SPVs for earnings management and bad news hiding, which leads to future stock price crash. In the second paper, we show that banks and other private lenders perceive SPVs as a tool of hiding debt and manipulating earnings so that they charge higher interest rate and set more restrictive terms for loans made to firms with SPVs. The evidence documented in both papers suggests that FASB should push for more effective and reliable guidance on SPV disclosures.

151511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
151511.value: 供应链整合（SCI: Supply Chain Integration）已成为企业运营管理的核心，并有大量的资源正被投入到其采纳中。然而，虽然人们普遍认为SCI可以有效改善企业绩效，但有关报告指出，在SCI采纳企业中，只有不到一半的企业能真正实现SCI的价值。同时，现有的SCI和企业绩效间关系的实证研究结果还比较混乱，甚至是相互冲突的。以前的研究往往认为SCI对企业绩效的影响是无条件的，从而忽略了SCI与其它与人相关（Human-related）的因素的交互作用。由此推论，当前有关影响SCI与企业绩效间关系的因素的认知还很欠缺。管理者还无法得到有效的理论指导，从而帮助采纳了SCI的企业有效实现SCI的价值。 为了弥补上述研究缺陷，本研究将着重揭示 (1)是什么原因导致了现有的关于SCI和企业绩效间关系的实证研究结论不一致；（2）SCI的维度是如何差异性影响企业绩效的；（3）与人相关的因素，如组织文化，是如何影响SCI各维度与企业绩效的关系的。基于组织文化，运营管理和信息系统方面的理论，我们提出了一个包括了SCI维度（即信息分享，协同规划，流程协作），组织文化和企业绩效（即运营绩效和客户服务）的理论模型。具体而言，我们认为，除了因为SCI的不同定义方式，忽视了行为性因素也是以前有关SCI和企业绩效关系的实证结果不一致的主要原因。因此，我们提出，组织文化能调节SCI维度和企业绩效的关系。同时，我们还剖析了SCI的不同维度对企业绩效不同方面的差异化影响。 为了检验上述假设，我们将同时采用案例分享和纵向调研的方法。调研将持续12个月，主要选取500个左右在中国境内已采用SCI的企业为样本。研究结果预期有以下理论和实践意义。通过分析软的人的因素在SCI和企业绩效关系中的调节作用，本研究将解决供应链管理研究中有关SCI结论不一致的问题。另外，据我们所知，该研究第一个考虑了组织文化在SCI和企业绩效关系中的调节作用。本研究将有助于管理者了解如何通过组织文化来促进SCI对企业绩效的改善。

151511.label: Realisation of objectives
151511.value: The research objectives of this research project are: (1) to understand what causes the inconsistent empirical findings on the relationship between SCI and firm performance in the extant literature; (2) to examine how individual dimensions of SCI are differentially related to different dimensions of firm performance; (3) to investigate how organizational culture moderates the relationships between SCI dimensions and firm performance. Although many studies have found that the use of power and inter-organizational trust can promote IOS adoption, others report weak and even negative relationships between power, trust and IOS adoption. Research findings from this project reveal how organizational culture moderates the relationship between power, trust, and a firm’s SCI adoption. Building on multiple theoretical perspectives, we examined how organizational culture moderates the relationship between power, trust, and a firm’s SCI. Our findings based on survey data collected from senior executives in China reveal that a target firm’s perceived mediated power would negatively impact its trust toward a dominant firm, while its perceived non-mediated power would positively affect its trust. Meanwhile, trust can positively influence the target firm’s electronic SCI adoption. Further, an internally focused culture weakens the negative effects of mediated power on trust. Meanwhile, an externally focused culture weakens the positive relationships between non-mediated power and trust, and between trust and electronic SCI adoption. The externally focused culture could weaken the negative relationship between mediated power and trust either. We examined how individual dimensions of SCI would affect firm performance. While supply chain (SC) exploitation and exploration have been playing an increasingly important role in SCI, there is a dearth of research examining their antecedents and outcomes. Drawing upon the boundary spanning theory, we theorize how top management, as boundary spanners, and three types of information technology (IT) capabilities as boundary objects, enable SC exploitation and exploration. We found that both SC exploitation and exploration have significantly positive effects on firm performance. Also, top management participation directly affects both SC exploitation and exploration. In addition, IT business partnerships and external IT linkages positively affect both SC exploitation and exploration, whereas IT infrastructure is not significantly related to either SC exploitation or exploration. We have also examined the relationship between market orientation (as organizational culture) and SCI (forthcoming JGIM paper) and have a working paper focuses on the moderating effects of organizational culture on SCI-performance relationship.

151511.label: Major findings and research outcome
151511.value: Our research findings suggest that the two types of organization power, namely mediated power and non-mediated power have differential effects on inter-organizational trust. Specifically, non-mediated power has positive influence on inter-organizational trust, while mediated power has negative impact on inter-organizational trust and it may lead to conflicts and negative feelings, while non-mediated power produces fewer conflicts in inter-organizational relationships, and thus enhances the quality of the dyadic relationship. This finding further indicate that organizational culture (i.e., internally focused or externally focused culture) moderates the relationships between power, trust, and SCI adoption. Specifically, externally focused culture could significantly weaken the negative relationship between mediated power and trust. We found that internally focused culture could significantly weaken the negative relationship between mediated power and trust. The possible explanation may be that an internally focused culture may treat the relationship with a dominant partner as the internal issue. Given this culture favors the control of business processes, it may be inclined to improve itself through expending resources on optimizing existing operational equipment and practices. Thus, this culture would help weaken the negative influence of mediated power on trust. Our research also reveal that individual dimensions of SCI (i.e. SC exploitation and exploration) would positively affect firm performance. SC exploitation and exploration can be regarded as firms’ higher-order competencies directly influencing both firm’s financial and operational performance. Our results show that SC exploitation contributes more to both financial and operational performance than SC exploration. Also, jointly conducting exploration with SC partners may not be as efficient and effective as exploitation in the short run since identifying new opportunities and developing new SC competencies are time-consuming processes. The findings suggest that top management participation directly improves firms’ SC exploitation and exploration. Building on the theory of market orientation (MO) and the literature of IS and operations management, we investigated how different dimensions of MO as an organizational culture affect different types of SCI. The findings suggest that, as an organizational culture, MO could facilitate the development of an idiosyncratic, inimitable capability of the firm, namely SCI in e-business. Specifically, the demand process integration could be significantly affected by customer, competitor, and inter-functional coordination orientations and the supply process integration could be significantly affected by customer and inter-functional coordination orientation.

151511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
151511.value: First, our research tests the hypotheses with cross-sectional data. For example, in our study on how SC exploitation and exploration would positively affect firm performance. Given that in this study, IT capabilities reconfiguration, top management involvement, and SC practices are complex activities, a longitudinal study may help better understand the mechanisms of how top management affect IT capabilities configuration and how the three types of IT capabilities may influence each other over time, and thus enriching our understanding of SC exploitation and exploration. Meanwhile, a longitudinal design can also reduce common method bias. Second, we might wish to perform theory building work based on our findings. Using our study on SC exploitation and exploration as an example, we draw on boundary spanning theory to investigate how top management and IT capabilities facilitate the SC exploitation and exploration. Although our findings show top management and different types of IT capabilities have differential impacts, the boundary spanning theory itself does not touch upon the ambidextrous capability needed for SC exploitation and exploration. Therefore, future research should advance theory to generate a more holistic and comprehensive understanding of the nature of exploitation and exploration in the SC context.

151511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
151511.value: Our research findings show that externally focused culture could significantly weaken the negative relationship between mediated power and trust, and internally focused culture could significantly weaken the negative relationship between mediated power and trust Supply Chain (SC) exploitation and exploration have been playing an increasingly important role in supply chain management. Both SC exploitation and exploration have significantly positive effects on firm performance. Also, top management participation directly affects both SC exploitation and exploration. In addition, IT business partnerships and external IT linkages positively affect both SC exploitation and exploration, whereas IT infrastructure is not significantly related to either SC exploitation or exploration. Market orientation (MO) plays a critical role in developing SCI in e-business in China. Chinese managers should pay attention to the imbalance of the effects of the three dimensions of MO on the two forms of SCI in e-business. Managers should realize that competitor orientation does not help to promote supply process integration directly although the type of MO facilitates demand process integration.

152611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
152611.value: Although modern organizations consider the management of risks to information security to be a critical issue, IT security professionals in the front-line often lack clear ideas about the nature of the threats that they face. These days, firms carry an immense burden of preventing information security breaches as attacks are increasingly sophisticated and multifaceted, and understanding these threats is the first major step in the management of information security risks. Given that hackers routinely share attack techniques and tools online, it is interesting to find out whether hacker forums represent a good resource for firms in learning more about the security threats. Also, observing activities in hacker forums could improve understanding of the type of attack information being shared online, the characteristics of the people who share the information and to what degree their knowledge constitutes real risks to firms. The objective of this project is two-fold: to shed more lights on the inner workings of the hacker forums and to study whether the information shared in the online forums translates into real risks for firms. The research requires extensive effort in collecting data from hacker forums, and communicating with corporate IT security professionals to gauge the nature of the threats encapsulated in the messages posted in hacker forums. Following the IT security risk management framework (Stoneburner, Goguen and Feringa, 2002), a comprehensive approach is designed to answer the question of whether online hacker forums pose security risks to firms. The approach focus on the two critical factors in threat analysis typically seen in IT security risk management – threat source (message author) and threat action (message content) – decipher how each of these factors would impact the actual level of risks faced by firms. Understanding these issues is critical for firms in formulating effective protection strategies. First, the significance of information disseminated through hacker forums is illustrated. The types of authors who would potentially pose the highest level of risks to firm are also identified. The overall threat sources and threat actions observed in the study can also help firms to better understand the nature of the risks faced. These insights are critical as they could serve as inputs in formulating risk mitigation strategies. Finally, the framework designed in the study presents a first attempt to investigate how security firms or professional organizations can rely on online hacker forums to monitor risks. 盡管現代機構已經認識到針對信息安全的風險管理的重要性，但是信息技術安全方面的一線專業人士依舊無法清晰地認識其所面臨的威脅的性質. 隨著攻擊手段的復雜化和綜合化，信息安全侵襲防御已經成為企業巨大的負擔，深入了解這些威脅成為管理信息安全風險的首要步驟。既然黑客通常會在網絡上共享攻擊技術和工具，那麼企業是否能夠通過黑客論壇來了解更多系統威脅。此外，企業可以通過觀察黑客論壇裡的活動來進一步了解網絡上共享的信息的類型，以及信息共享人的特性和其在多大程度上構成了對企業的實際風險。 這個課題的目標包括兩個方面：深入了解黑客論壇的內部運作情況以及其中的信息共享轉化成為企業的現實風險的可能性。.這項研究需要從黑客論壇搜集大量的數據，並且通過與信息技術安全專家的交流來估計黑客論壇上的信息裡包含的威脅的性質。 本文沿襲信息技術安全風險管理的構架（Stoneburner, Goguen andFeringa, 2002），設計了一種綜合的方法來探尋網絡黑客論壇與企業安全威脅的因果關系。該方法專注於威脅分析中在信息技術安全風險管理領域裡經常出現的兩個關鍵因素--威脅源和威脅體--探尋這些因素如何影響企業所面臨的風險水平。 理解以下內容對於企業採取有效的保護策略非常重要。首先，通過黑客論壇的信息散布的重要性已被闡明。同時，那些可能對企業帶來最大風險的作者類型已被確定。此外，通過了解研究中觀察到的全部威脅源和威脅體，企業可以更深入地認識它們所面臨的風險的性質。 這些內容之所以重要是因為它們可以在風險弱化策略的設計中作為輸入的部分。最后，該研究是率先嘗試研究安全企業或者專業組織依靠網絡黑客論壇進行風險控制的問題。

152611.label: Realisation of objectives
152611.value: We have completed two manuscripts using the dataset that we collected for this project. In the first paper, we study and classify the different types of users in the hacker forum. In the second paper, we examine the relationship between hacker forum posts and real-world DDoS attacks. The first paper achieves the third objective, and achieves the second objective marginally. We constructed the user profiles of the hacker forum using text-mining techniques. We are able to classify the users into four main types, and we determined that the hacker community is very much represents a learning community where meritocracy is in place. The second paper fulfills first objective. It fulfills the second objective moderately. We established that hacker forums do disseminate attack knowledge as hacker forum posts are found to be linked to real world DDoS attacks. However, such an effect depends on whether the posts are located from the tutorial or non-tutorial categories. Our results show that the attack knowledge, disseminated through the hacker forum, can be applied in a different ways, albeit by different users with different intentions. From the two manuscripts, we have accomplished the first objective and third objective completely and the second objective moderately. We have spent a lot of effort and resources to conduct text-mining analysis on the dataset to classify post content, and construct user profiles. Thus, we have achieved the third objective completely. We find empirical evidence that hacker forum disseminate attack information that is linked to real-world risks. Hence, we have achieved the first objective completely. We achieved the second objective moderately. We were able to draw insights into how messages are tied to specific DDoS attacks, but not the general attacks seen by firms. The original plan was to use the vulnerability information from a public database to surrogate attacks seen by firms. However, the tasks seem to be much harder than we thought as we have to determine how a particular vulnerability translates to low or high risk. In the absence of precise firm level attack data or inputs by a number of IT security professionals who are willing to rank the risk level of the millions of posts seen in the hacker forum, we cannot achieve the objective completely. Nevertheless, we have accomplished the objective of linking message to attacks.

152611.label: Major findings and research outcome
152611.value: We find that hacker forum users can be classified into four types based a number of features. Two features, knowledge acquisition and knowledge provision, are noted to be particularly informative. The user types are: guru hackers, casual hackers, learning hackers, and novice hackers. Guru hackers are knowledgeable and respectable. They usually share ideas and advice with others. Casual hackers tend to act as observers. They can be skilled hackers who show interest mainly in deriving usable information from the forum. Learning hackers are also expert hackers who utilize the forum basically for learning. They actively seek knowledge and tend to share more of it over time. Novice hackers are new learners who typically join the forum for a short period. Overall, it is found that hacker communities very much represent learning communities where meritocracy is in place. We are also able to determine the impact of knowledge sharing in hacker forums on security attacks. Focusing on DDoS attacks, our study finds evidence that hacker forum discussions generally lead to fewer attacks. However, in some forum segments, discussions could lead to more attacks. The results suggests that there is an intricate ethical perspective when it comes to hacking information. Different information shared in hacker forums can be applied in very different manners, presumably by different people.

152611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
152611.value: We can perform more text-mining analysis with the dataset. We have just been able to classify whether a post is discussing technical attack oriented topics with acceptable classification accuracy. We also plan to do further forum post classification such as whether foul words were used, whether trading of hacking service or hacking software were involved. These additional dimensions could allow us to answer additional questions related to the behaviors observed in hacker forum. There are other user behavior related topics that we may be able to study with the dataset. For example, what factors would lead to higher reputation in the hacker forum. We are currently doing some analysis in this aspect.

152611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
152611.value: We want determine whether information posted in the hacker forum could pose a threat to the society. Studying an easily assessable hacker forum website, we find evidence that the forum discussions can lead to more distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks. However, such an effect is only limited to specific tutorial segments of the forum, where users typically share attack instructions and attack programs. We also examine the user profiles of the forum and find that the hacker forum is very much like other knowledge collaboration forum, where users engage in knowledge seeking and provision behaviors. We are able to classify users into four main types based on the changes of their knowledge sharing patterns and their online forum status.

153011.label: Co - Investigator(s)
153011.value: Prof Gul, Ferdinand Akthar Khan Dr Wu, Donghui

153011.label: Project Objectives
153011.value: Construct a database that contains the personal information of auditors who sign audit reports and the client information of those auditors. Assess the incremental impact of individual auditors on audit quality as measured using proxies: modified opinion, discretionary accrual, non-operating income, and regulatory sanction. Assess the explanatory power of observable auditor attributes such as age, education, gender, and experience on audit quality by replacing auditor dummies with variables that proxy for those characteristics. 153011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
153011.value: It is important to understand the determinants of audit quality. Early studies use the dichotomy between Big N and non-Big N audit firms, and examine the difference in audit quality between the two types. More recent studies examine how audit quality differs among local offices of Big N firms and how audit firms’ industry expertise affects audit quality. The heterogeneity in individual auditor attributes and their possible impacts on audit quality have been largely ignored. A number of recent studies find that individual economic agents matter to a wide range of policies and decisions of business organizations such as investment and financing policies and financial reporting practices. This suggests that unobservable managerial characteristics, along with observable characteristics, explain the cross-sectional variation in firm policies to a large extent. The proposed project intends to bridge these two streams of the literature. Specifically, we borrow concepts and methodologies from the literature on the importance of individual managers on firm policies, and apply them to examining the significance of individual auditors in determining audit quality. An important contribution of our study is that we evaluate the effects of not only observable but also unobservable auditor characteristics on audit quality. We focus on audit quality because it is likely to heavily involve personal judgment about audit complexity and risk. We use multiple measures for audit quality: the tendency to issue modified opinions, the magnitude of accruals and non-operating income, and the likelihood of audit failure. We first investigate the importance of auditor fixed effects. We include auditor dummies along with economic determinants of audit quality in the regressions, and test the extent to which auditor dummies contribute to the overall explanatory power of the regressions. The magnitude and significance levels of the coefficients on auditor dummies in these regressions measure the importance of both observable and unobservable auditor attributes in explaining audit quality. We then link the coefficients on auditor dummies with observable auditor characteristics (such as age, gender, education, and the year of obtaining a CPA license), and test the extent to which those characteristics explain auditor fixed effects. Previous studies find that audit firm size, practice office size, and audit firm industry expertise explain the cross-sectional variation in audit quality. Our work contributes to the literature by examining the importance of individual auditors in determining audit quality, and would thus be of interest to academics, practitioners, and policy-makers. 审计研究中一个很重要的课题是寻找审计质量的决定因素。早期研究把审计师事务所分为国际大所和非国际大所，然后比较这两组事务所的审计质量差异。最近的研究开始审视分所之间的审计质量差异以及审计师事务所行业专长对审计质量的影响。然而，审计师个体特性和这些特性对审计质量的可能影响还尚未被深入研究。 为数众多的最近研究发现个体经济人对经济组织的政策和决定有一定的影响。这些政策和决策包括投资，融资决策和财务报告政策。这些研究表明未知的和已知的经理人个体特性差异在很大程度上解释了公司间的政策差异。 本研究项目试图跨越上述两个研究分支。具体地说，我们借鉴上述个体经济人文献的概念和方法来研究审计师个体对审计质量的影响程度。我们研究项目具有一个很重要的贡献，那就是我们不但估算已知的审计师个体特性，而且估算未知的特性对审计质量的影响。我们研究审计质量是因为它深受审计师个人对审计复杂性和风险的判断的影响。我们应用了审计文献中常用的审计质量的衡量指标。这些指标包括：签发非标意见门槛的高低，非正常应计项目的大小，非经营性损益的大小，和审计失败的概率。 我们首先评估审计师个体影响的程度。我们在审计质量模型中加入个体审计师哑变量和其他决定审计质量的经济因素，然后研究这些审计师哑变量在多大程度上提高审计质量模型的解释能力。这些哑变量的系数和显著性水平反映了已知和未知的审计师个体特性对审计质量的影响。我们然后以这些系数作为应变量，审计师个体特性（如年龄，性别，教育，获得CPA资格证书的年限等等）作为自变量，研究这些特性在多大程度上可以解释个体审计质量差异。 以前的审计质量研究文献多着眼于事务所或者分所大小和审计师事务所行业专长对审计质量的影响。我们的着眼于审计师个体差异对审计质量的影响，因此推进了这个文献的发展。会计学者，会计实务人员和政策制定者都可能对我们的研究产生兴趣。

153011.label: Realisation of objectives
153011.value: All of the project objectives have been achieved desirably. Details are as follows. Objective #1：We construct a database consisting of more than 4,000 individual auditors in China with their demographic data such as gender, education, birth date, and the starting year of their practice. A detailed description about the data is included in Gul, Wu, and Yang (2013, TAR). Objective #2: We use a fixed effect model by including individual auditor dummies, and show that the explanaotry power of audit quality models, where audit quality is measured by modified audit opinions, discretionary accruals, non-operating income and regulatory sanctions, increases significantly. These findings and related tests can be found in Gul, Wu, and Yang (2013, TAR). Objective #3: When we replace individual auditor dummies with observable auditor characteristics, we find that these characteristics do not significantly increase the explanatory power of the models. We believe this is because auditor dummies capture the effect all auditor characteristics, while observable characteristics such as age, education, and gender are only a small subset of all characteristics. These findings are not reported in the paper for the brevity. Objective #4: We show that observable auditor characteristics such as age, education, gender, experince, and political affiliation can partially explain auditor fixed effects. However, a large portion of fixed effects remain unexplored. We call for future research along this line. These findings and discussions can be found in Gul, Wu, and Yang (2013, TAR).

153011.label: Major findings and research outcome
153011.value: We use multiple audit quality measures, including audit reporting (AR) aggressiveness, clients’ abnormal accruals and non-core earnings, and the presence of a small profit and include auditor fixed effects in audit quality models. We find that individual effects are significant both statistically and economically for all quality measures. The inclusion of individual auditor indicators in the base model increases explanatory power by 7.02 percent to 33.82 percent relative to the base model’s adjusted R-square. The frequency of individual auditors exerting significant effects on audit quality is much greater than what would be expected by chance. For example, the percentages of the individual effects for AR aggressiveness that are significant at the 0.05 and 0.10 levels are 12.7 percent and 18.2 percent, respectively. There is also considerable variation in the magnitude of individual effects. For example, the abnormal accruals reported by clients for an auditor at the 75th percentile of the distribution of individual effects would be 2.6 percent higher than for an auditor at the 25th percentile. After showing that audit aggressiveness varies across individual auditors, we next explore whether this variation can be explained by auditors’ demographic characteristics. We consider several personal characteristics, including education, gender, birth cohort, Big N experience, rank, and political affiliation, assuming that these characteristics are associated with one or more of the attributes relevant to auditor JDM. We find that partners exhibit a relatively conservative style of audit reporting, consistent with prior findings that partners take a tougher stand in requesting accounting adjustments than non-partner auditors (Trotman et al. 2009). Educational background also makes a difference with auditors who hold graduate degrees tending to be more aggressive. Auditors who have worked in Big N firms tend to be more conservative, consistent with the findings that Big N firms are more conservative than others (Francis 2004). The generally conservative environments in Big N firms may influence their auditors’ judgment and decisions, or auditors recruited by Big N firms may be inherently more conservative. Auditors who have political affiliations, proxied by membership in the Chinese Communist Party (CCP), are associated with more aggressive audit outcomes. In additional analyses, we show that the individual auditor effects estimated based on the above four audit quality measures are positively correlated with the likelihood of regulatory sanctions and the frequency of accounting restatements made by clients.

153011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
153011.value: The data obtained from this project allow us to do more research on how individual auditors affect audit quality. Currently, these data are used in two other projects. First, we identify companies in which their exectuives and auditors graduate from the same university, and examine how school ties between auditors and executives affect audit quality. We show that school ties negatively affect audit quality. This paper is under revision for the second round review at Journal of Accounting & Economics. Second, we construct auditor experience variables and examine whether auditors with IPO expertise or IPO specialists can improve IPO audit quality.

153011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
153011.value: We examine whether and how individual auditors may affect audit outcomes using a large set of archival Chinese data. We analyze about 800 individual auditors and find that they exhibit a significant variation in audit quality. The effects that individual auditors have on audit quality are both economically and statistically significant, and are pronounced in both large and small audit firms. We also find that the individual auditor effects on audit quality can be partially explained by auditor characteristics, such as educational background, Big N audit firm experience, rank in the audit firm, and political affiliation. Our findings highlight the importance of scrutinizing and understanding audit quality at the individual auditor level.

153411.label: Project Objectives

153411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
153411.value: With a large proportion of baby boomers (those born between 1946 and 1964) entering middle and old age, it is estimated that more than one third of the workforce will be composed of adults aged above 45 years in the next two decades. This imposes an immediate need to investigate motivational and work behaviors of older employees (relative to their younger counterparts) in order to maintain work efficiency and team performance in organizations. Socioemotional selectivity theory (SST) emphasizes that older adults focus more on emotionally meaningful goals when they perceive future time as increasingly limited (Carstensen, 2006). When handling conflict with social partners, older adults’ greater emphasis on emotional goals may motivate them to concern more for other parties, instead of personal interest. It is speculated that the way individuals handle interpersonal conflict would be guided by their goal orientation and therefore older employees’ responses to workplace conflict would be different from those of younger employees. This proposed project seeks to shed light on conflict responses across adulthood and assess their impacts on work-related outcomes and psychological well-being. Study 1 will examine conflict styles and motivational orientation in two hypothetical conflict situations between younger and older employees. It aims at investigating whether there are age differences in conflict styles and motivational orientation when dealing with the conflict, and whether motivational orientation would mediate the effect of age on conflict responses. Study 2 will make use of the daily diary method to record actual experiences of conflict management at work, as well as assessing daily work-related outcomes and psychological well-being. It is anticipated that age would moderate the impact of conflict styles on work-related outcomes and psychological well-being. Findings of the proposed project will provide insights and recommendations to employers and management personnel for understanding workplace behaviors of older workers and enhancing team performance in the organization. 隨著大多數的嬰兒潮一代(於1946至1964年之間出生的人)邁入中年和老年, 預計在未來二十年,45歲以上的成年人將佔市場勞動力三分之一或以上。這趨 勢反映探討年長僱員的工作動機和行為的迫切性,以保持機構的高工作效率和 團隊表現。 社交情緒選擇理論(Socioemotional Selectivity Theory)強調,當 長者感到時間越來越有限,他們會比較注重追求有意義的情感目標 (Carstensen, 2006)。當處理人際衝突時,著重情感目標的長者較關注別人的利 益,而不是個人的利益。以此推測, 人際衝突的處理方式或會受個人目標的取 向而有所影響,因此年長僱員在處理工作上的人際衝突時可能有別於年輕僱員 。本研究旨在探討不同年齡僱員如何處理人際衝突,並評估這些衝突處理方式 對工作表現和心理健康的影響。第一個研究會探討年輕和年長僱員在假想的人 際衝突情景的處理方式和動機傾向。第二個研究以日記方式記錄員工在實際工 作時處理人際衝突的經歷及心理狀況。此研究的目的是了解人際衝突的處理方 式和動機傾向有否年齡差異,與及動機傾向能否解釋不同年齡之衝突處理方式 之差異,以及評估對日常工作表現和心理健康的影響 。

153411.label: Realisation of objectives
153411.value: The three objectives have been achieved satisfactorily. Objective 1 has been realized through the conduction of a cross-sectional survey in 297 younger and older employees. By using hypothetical conflict vignettes and recalling a personal conflict incident at work, the use of five conflict strategies (integrating, compromising, avoiding, obliging, and dominating) and motivational orientations (cooperative, competitive or independent goals) were recorded and compared between the two age groups. The mediating effect of motivational orientations on the relationship between age and conflict strategies was also assessed. Objectives 2 and 3 have been achieved through the implementation of a daily diary study in a subsample of participants who also took part in the survey study. One hundred and fifty younger and older employees completed an online survey which lasted for 15 consecutive work days. Over the sampling period, over 90% of participants reported more than one interpersonal conflict at work. By analyzing their responses to each conflict incident, Objective 2 could be realized by examining the within-individual variability in the use of conflict strategies across conflict situations. By recording their job satisfaction, self-reported job performance, interpersonal relations, and affective well-being in each report, the research question on the moderating effect of age (Objective 3) could also be tested.

153411.label: Major findings and research outcome
153411.value: This project investigated the effects of age on conflict management at work as well as the explanatory role of motivational orientations in such relationships. Two studies were conducted in younger and older Chinese managerial and executive employees: Study 1 is a cross-sectional survey study and Study 2 is a daily diary study over 15 consecutive work days. Results of Study 1 showed that relative to younger employees, older employees utilized more avoiding to deal with conflicts with supervisors and less dominating with subordinates. Such age differences in avoiding and dominating strategies could be explained by cooperative and independent goals held by the participants in the conflict incident. Consistent with our prediction, no age differences were found in the use of integrating and compromising strategies. In addition, the negative effect of avoiding on interpersonal relations was only shown in younger employees but not in older employees. It suggests that unlike younger adults, older adults’ use of avoiding would not harm their relationship with coworkers. The aforementioned findings have been reported in Yeung and Ho (2015) and Yeung, Fung, and Chan (revised and resubmitted) (the first and the second papers, respectively, in Part C). By adopting a daily diary approach, Study 2 recorded participants’ emotional and behavioral responses to conflicts in the real-life work environment. Multilevel analyses showed that there was substantial within-individual variability (ranging from 52%-72%) in the use of the five conflict strategies when conflict arose, implying that the selection of conflict management strategies is largely dependent on the actual context and the conflict partner. Similar to the findings in Study 1, this study also revealed age differences in responses to actual conflicts at work. Specifically, compared with younger employees, older employees reported more positive but fewer negative emotions and utilized more passive strategies (avoiding and obliging) when experiencing conflicts in the workplace. In addition, consistent with our prediction, the perceived future interaction with the conflict partner predicted more positive emotional and behavioral responses. These findings have been reported in Yeung, Fung, and Chan (under review) (the third paper in Part C).

153411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
153411.value: This project is the first study in Hong Kong to compare emotional and behavioral reactions to workplace conflict between younger and older Chinese working adults. In view of a growing number of older employees in the workforce, intergenerational conflict is not uncommon at work. This project has created a valuable data base to understand behavioral tendency of older employees relative to their younger counterparts, while it has also generated new research directions to explore age variations in conflict management when age of the conflict partner varies. Based on the findings of the present project, a new GRF proposal will be submitted in the fall of 2014 to investigate the underlying mechanism of age differences in affective and behavioral reactions through an objective examination of attentional preferences during intergenerational conflict.

153411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
153411.value: Our workforce is rapidly aging, especially when baby boomers enter middle and old age. To advance our understanding of work-related behaviors of older employees, this project integrates the theoretical concepts of lifespan development and organizational psychology to compare younger and older employees’ behavioral responses to workplace conflict. Results of both cross-sectional survey and daily diary study have shown that older employees in general handle the conflict with greater utilization of passive strategies (e.g., avoiding) and fewer use of confrontational strategies (e.g., dominating) than do younger employees. These age differences could be explained by goal orientations held by the employees. Moreover, the present project has also demonstrated that the effects of conflict strategies on work-related outcomes and affective well-being would vary by age. For example, the negative effect of avoiding is only shown in younger employees but not older employees. This finding supports the proposition of socioemotional selectivity theory (Carstensen, 2006) that when the use of conflict strategies is consistent with one’s developmental goal, positive work-related outcomes and psychological well-being are observed. It provides important implications to future research on organizational psychology to take age into account when examining work-related motives and behaviors.

153711.label: Project Title(Chinese)
153711.value: 用户原创内容(UGC)的创造和消费：网络朋友的影响

153711.label: Project Objectives
153711.value: To investigate the influence of online friends on adoption decision of online content To identify factors that moderate the above friend influence, if any To investigate the influence of online friends on generation of online content To evaluate the consequence of social interaction on the collective outcome of online content within a network

To identify factors that moderate the above friend influence, if any
To investigate the influence of online friends on generation of online content
To evaluate the consequence of social interaction on the collective outcome of online content within a network

153711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
153711.value: 近年兴起了很多社交性的内容分享网站，比如YouTube, Filckr和Digg。在这些网站上，用户可以上载和下载文字，图片，视频等 - 常称为用户原创内容。同时，这类网站也具有基本的社交功能，每个人都可以结交朋友。这里引出一个研究问题，当用户们建立了朋友关系后，朋友是否影响互相的内容创造和消费。 首先，我们探讨朋友对内容消费的影响。比如，在Flickr网站用户可以查看互相间的照片和收藏。我们想看是否朋友关系会导致同样的消费行为。类似的问题在其他领域也调查过，如电视收看，接受新药的行为。然而，之前的这些调查大都基于小样本，有效性不高。我们准备从网络收集一个大的样本，进行更严谨的分析。该次研究着眼于音乐，图片，视频此类网络文化，探讨病毒类营销对这些原创文化的宣传是否有效。 其次，我们探讨朋友对内容创造的影响。目前的文献对内容创造的决定因素研究的较少。我们想看是否朋友会影响一个用户的参与程度，原创的类别和质量。这类问题对内容分享网站如YouTube和Flickr尤为重要，因为他们的内容主要来源就是用户。更进一步，一个网站的社交网络如何影响这个网站内容的呈现，是更加多样性还是趋于一致性？这对整个网络文化市场的发展很重要。 我们将用实际收集的网络数据进行实证分析。我们将从Flickr收集数据，包括用户的上载和收藏行为，以及他们的社交网络。数据收集将持续一段时间，所以我们可以观察用户的动态变化，更易于推测影响因子。我们的分析将严格控制其他变量。为研究内容创造，我们会测量照片的类型和质量，以及整个网站的多样性等。

153711.label: Realisation of objectives
153711.value: Among the four project objectives, three have been completely achieved and one is almost achieved. For the last objective, one challenge is that social influence and social network structure interact with each other (e.g., people form friendship and then influence each other but the influence of one person on the other also leads to certain social relationships). Such process cannot be easily captured through a simple static model. We have tried to build up a dynamic model but the estimation becomes very complicated. Nevertheless, we are still able to achieve the fourth objective to a great extent by drawing inferences based on the results that we obtain under Objectives 1-3.
