242411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
242411.value: In the past two decades, the evolution of new media technologies has resulted in the rapid development of online journalism, which requires journalists to have a wider variety of skills and newsrooms to be restructured in order to integrate multi-media. Accordingly, journalism programs around the world have started to provide online journalism courses or trainings. While it has long been recognized that there exists a gap between journalism education and practice, this gap may have become even wider in this era of new media. As the industry undergoes revolutionary changes, it is important for journalism education to catch up with the demands of the industry. Hong Kong has a well developed media industry due to its open society and press freedom. It is home to many Asia's biggest media players. Journalism education is popular in Hong Kong. Among the eight UGC (University Grants Committee of Hong Kong) funded institutions, four provide journalism or related programs for bachelor’s and higher degrees. The purpose of this project is to investigate the current status of online journalism education and practice in Hong Kong. Three surveys on the level of skills, perception of concepts and duties for online newsrooms will be conducted among working online journalists, exiting college seniors, and journalism instructors in Hong Kong respectively. The survey data will be analyzed quantitatively and the gap between online journalism education and practice will be identified and studied. The findings of this project will help journalism educators and students better understand the current status and demands of online journalism in Hong Kong. It will provide an important reference for the journalism programs in Hong Kong’s universities to improve or reform the curricula in order to catch up with the evolution of new media. Moreover, it will facilitate the communication among journalism instructors, students, and professionals towards a common goal of ensuring competitiveness of the media industry of Hong Kong. 在过去的二十年中，新媒体技术的演变导致了在线新闻的快速发展。这就要求新闻从业人员装备更多样的技能，也要求新闻编辑部重组以便整合多媒体。长久以来存在的新闻教育和实践之间的差距在新媒体时代可能变得更大。由于新闻行业发生的革命性变化，新闻教育赶上行业的需求显得非常重要。 由于其开放的社会和新闻自由，香港有一个发展良好的媒体行业。这里云集了许多亚洲最大的媒体机构。新闻教育在香港很受欢迎。在香港大学教育资助委员会资助的八所院校中，有四个提供新闻及相关学科学士及以上学位。本研究项目的目的是调查目前香港在线新闻教育和实踐的状态。三个问卷调查分别了解在綫新闻从业人员，即将毕业的大学生，和在綫新闻课程教师的技能水平，对概念的理解和对职能的看法。项目通过对调查数据进行的定量分析来确定和研究在綫新闻的教育和实践之间的差距。

242411.label: Realisation of objectives
242411.value: I am proud to report that all the four objectives set forth in the original proposal have been fully achieved. A twin survey of the online journalism students and online journalists in Hong Kong was conducted in attempt to achieve all the four research objectives proposed. The survey itself was carried out within the period from April 20 to June 16 in 2012. In order to investigate for the current status of online journalism education and practice in Hong Kong higher education institutions, the project team designed the survey instruments specifically aimed to collect data in the following areas: (Ja) assessment of skill proficiency in their journalism practice: how journalists evaluate their own proficiency level of each one skill; (Jb) assessment of duty performed in their journalism practice: how journalists evaluate the importance of each one duty; (Jc) assessment of importance of concept in their journalism practice : how journalists evaluate the importance of each one concept; (Sa) perceived importance of skills in the journalism course: how students evaluate the importance of each one skill (i.e., the same item list as perceptions of skill proficiency) being taught in the online/digital journalism course, compared to their assessment of own proficiency level; (Sb) perceived duty practice in the journalism course: students evaluate how much they get to practice for each one duty (i.e., the same item list as perceptions of duty performance) in the online/digital journalism course, compared to what they think it should be; (Sc) perceived attention to concept in the journalism course: students evaluate how much the online/digital journalism course attends to each one concept (i.e., the same item list as perceptions of concept’s importance), compared to what they think it should be. The data collection process went smoothly and the response rates for both groups fell within the normal range. The study results well reflect on the four objectives and therefore allow us to make sense of the inquiries. We will further elaborate the findings in the following section.

242411.label: Major findings and research outcome
242411.value: This study examined and compared the perceptions of online journalists and online journalism students on journalism skills (proficiency in audio and video reporting, traditional writing and webpage production), duties (performance in business management, traditional writing, story work and multimedia) and concepts. The study finds that there is much discordance regarding skills and duties between journalists and students in Hong Kong. Research results showed that online journalists prioritised the importance of skills as traditional writing, audio and video reporting, and webpage production while online journalism students ranked audio and video reporting, traditional writing, webpage production in descending order of importance. The study also revealed that online journalists perceived the performance in traditional writing and story work as more important than business management and multimedia while online journalism students perceived that the order of importance should be story work, traditional writing and multimedia, then business management. A variety of duties related to multimedia works and business management are performed by journalists far less in reality than the students presume. In line with these findings, journalists are far less proficient than students in the skills of webpage production. However, journalism professionals are more proficient in the traditional writing skills than students, which is not surprising at all. These research outcomes imply that, in Hong Kong, journalists tend to focus more on traditional backbone skills and duties such as those in writing and news judgment, but less on technical skills and duties, than students. Based upon the present research findings, the administrators of journalism schools in Hong Kong, and probably in other Asian countries, are urged not to directly adopt the approaches for online journalism education suggested in the Western literature. Perhaps the online journalism educators in Hong Kong should continue curricula that emphasize traditional backbone skills and duties pertaining to writing and news judgment. This does not mean, however, that journalism schools should neglect teaching new technical skills to students, as this is now an essential part of journalism training. As the findings in this study suggest that today’s journalism students are already fairly proficient in new media skills (possibly acquired from both inside the specific online journalism classroom and the pervasive digital environment), journalism curricula should not forgo training students in traditional journalistic skills for the sake of computer skills.

242411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
242411.value: This study recommends that researchers continue to revisit the “practice–education gap” regularly in the ever-evolving field of online journalism, in Hong Kong and elsewhere.

242411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
242411.value: In the last two decades, the rise of the Internet and other new media technologies has brought more massive and profound changes to the field of journalism than ever before. This driving force has been affecting journalism practice and journalism education in every way imaginable. Journalism professionals and journalism educators hold different views on the professional skills journalism graduates should be equipped with. A study by Dr Roselyn Du of Hong Kong Baptist University, and her research team confirmed the discordance between online journalism education and practice. The research also revealed that traditional journalistic skills such as writing and news judgment were still more important than technical skills used for multimedia and website in online newsrooms in Hong Kong. Based on the research results, researchers suggest that online journalism educators in Hong Kong should continue curricula that emphasise the traditional backbone skills and duties pertaining to writing and news judgment. However, the teaching of new technical skills to students should not be neglected as this is now an essential part of journalism training. The findings also suggest that today’s journalism students are fairly proficient in new media skills, so journalism curricula should not forgo training students on traditional journalistic skills for computer skills.

242511.label: Project Objectives
242511.value: To provide a theoretical model to explain and predict the positive (vs. negative) affective and behavioral responses of non-VIP customers when they are excluded from the preferential treatment. To identify and verify the personal and cultural contingency factors of non-VIP customers, which qualify their desire of the preferential VIP treatment and their subsequent buying behaviors.
rows: To provide a theoretical model to explain and predict the positive (vs. negative) affective and behavioral responses of non-VIP customers when they are excluded from the preferential treatment.
To identify and verify the personal and cultural contingency factors of non-VIP customers, which qualify their desire of the preferential VIP treatment and their subsequent buying behaviors.

242511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
242511.value: The provision of preferential treatment to VIP customers is a widely adopted practice in the tourism and service industry. Leading service firms, such as Starwood Hotels, Hilton Hotels, American Airlines and Cathay Pacific Airways, have set up different VIP or preferred guest programs to delight their valuable customers, strengthen their business rapport, and reinforce their loyalty behaviors. Without doubt, these VIP service programs are successful and have contributed to the profit growth of service firms. However, the conventional practice of preferential treatment is challenged by researchers. Some studies show that when a consumer observes someone else receives better treatment, the consumer will have negative affective responses of unfair feeling, jealousy and envy toward the firm (Feinberg et al. 2002; Lehmann 2001). These negative affective responses, in turn, may even lead to switching behavior. In this proposal, I aim to unveil factors and conditions that support the adoption of preferential treatment strategy in the tourism and service industry. I argue that previous research has neglected the positive aspect of envious responses of non-VIP customers. I propose a theoretical model which explicates the antecedent and contingency factors that jointly determining the positive affective and behavioral responses of non-VIP customers. Specifically, I predict that when the non-VIP customers consider the VIP customers being similar (e.g., in terms of business background or social-economic status), and when they believe the VIP treatment/status is attainable, they would have a higher level of benign envy (vs. malicious envy) toward the preferential treatment. The affective response of benign envy, in turn, leads to positive (vs. negative) behaviors, such as upgrade motivation, commitment, cross-buying, and word-of-mouth. I further posit that the interaction effect of perceived similarity and attainability on the elicitation of benign envy is contingent upon the long-term (vs. short-term) orientation values of the non-VIP customers. I propose a survey and a scenario experiment with tourists visiting Hong Kong to test our propositions. This practice allows field evidence and experiment data to triangulate each other and validate our proposed conceptual model. 在旅遊服務行業，向尊貴客戶（VIP）提供優惠待遇已被廣泛接受採用。服務行業的龍頭公司，例如喜来登酒店，希爾頓酒店，美國航空和國泰航空等，已經設立了不同的尊貴客戶專案服務計劃來取悅他們的重要客戶，穩固與客戶的業務關係，和增強客戶的忠誠行為。毫無疑問，這些VIP服務專案是成功的，而且為服務行業的公司帶來了利潤增長。 然而，設立優惠待遇的傳統策略和做法受到了部份學者的質疑。一些研究顯示，當一個顧客觀察到其他人受到了更好的待遇，他或她會對這人的特殊待遇產生不公平的感受和嫉妒 (envy) 等負面反應（Feinberg et.al.2001; Lehmann 2001）。這些負面的情緒反應可能會導致該顧客轉移到其他公司，成為其他公司的顧客。 在這個研究計劃中，我希望發掘出一些支持在旅遊服務行業採用優惠待遇策略的因素和情況。我注意到以往的研究忽略了非VIP客戶的羨慕反應 (benign envy) 的正面作用。為此，我提出一個理論模型，用以解釋引致非VIP客戶的正面情感和行為反應的前因和制約因素 (contingency factors)。我預測當非VIP客戶認為VIP客戶和他（她）相似（例如，商業背景，社會經濟地位），而且這些VIP待遇/身份是可以得到的，他們會對優惠待遇產生更高程度的正面羨慕反應（vs.負面的嫉妒）。正面羨慕的情感反應能夠導致正面（vs.負面）的行為，例如升級購買的動機，購買承諾，交叉相互購買 (cross-buying) 和口諀。我進一步推斷客戶相似度 (similarity) 和優惠待遇可獲得性 (attainability) 的相互作用 (interaction effect) 是由非VIP客戶的個人長遠（vs.短期）價值方向 (long term orientation) 制約的。 我設計了一個問卷調查和情境實驗，以訪港旅客作為研究樣本，來測試我們的論點。調查的資料和實驗證據可以互相協同，確認我們提出的理論模型。

242511.label: Realisation of objectives
242511.value: REALISATION OF OBJECTIVE #1: This objective has been fully achieved. A theoretical model was developed and empirically tested for explaining and predicting the elicitation of envy. Details of the theoretical model are reported later in Section 6.1. Since the size of this grant is small, I recruited a PhD student instead of a full-time RA to support my research activities. Under my supervision and guidance, my model is incorporated and tested in his thesis research. In addition to this thesis, this project leads to a conference paper and a journal manuscript. These documents are attached in Part C of this report. Other findings of this project are to be included in another manuscript for submission to a reputable journal later (work-in-progress). REALISATION OF OBJECTIVE #2: This objective has been partly achieved with findings that are different from the prediction of my original proposal. My proposal suggested that long term orientation (LTO) serves as a cultural factor which moderates the influence of "belief of attainability of VIP treatment" on the relationship between "the effect of perceived similarity with VIP customers" and "envy". As mentioned in my progress report in 3/2014, an initial finding from my survey revealed a significant three-way interaction among similarity, attainability and LTO on benign envy. Unfortunately, this effect of LTO could not be replicated in subsequent experiments. Hence, the findings related to LTO were mixed and excluded from my current manuscript. Yet, during the research process, my PhD student and I have identified a novel cultural factor, namely cultural ascription-orientation, which was found to be a moderator influencing the elicitation of benign envy. Our findings showed that the prestigious VIP status offered by airline is more benign envied by passengers of cultural ascription-orientation than their counterparts of cultural achievement-orientation. This outcome has become part of the manuscript submitted to the Journal of International Business Studies (draft manuscript attached in Part C of this report). Unfortunately, the manuscript was later rejected by the JIBS editor in 4/2015 after two rounds of review. The manuscript has been further revised and would be submitted to Journal of Cross Cultural Psychology after a peer review in this summer. In sum, whereas the findings related to the original proposed cultural moderator (LTO) were mixed, my research objective #2 regarding the cultural contingency factors has been partly achieved by a newly identified factor moderator, cultural-ascription orientation.

242511.label: Major findings and research outcome
242511.value: A theoretical model explicating the elicitation of benign envy was developed and tested with a survey, a field study and two experiments. Our findings showed that benign envy of non-VIP customers is elicited by a joint effect of their perceived attainability of the privilege, perceived deservingness of the privilege received by the envied VIP customers, and perceived similarity with the VIP customers (a graphic summary of the model is presented in Figure 1 of my PhD student’s thesis; attached in Part C of this report). First, although the roles of attainability and deservingness on eliciting envy have been demonstrated in a recent consumer study (Van de Van et al., 2011), our findings further advanced this line of research by a re-examination of the construct of similarity and its relationship with the design of the VIP scheme. Similarity is regarded as an important factor in previous envy research because it is a key to trigger upward social comparison against VIP customers and ignite the envy emotions of non-VIPs. Our literature review showed that previous researchers operationalized similarity as a unidimensional perception although it should be more complicated in daily life. A non-VIP customer may find him/herself similar to a VIP customer in some aspects but different in others. Our empirical evidence showed that whether a non-VIP considers him/herself similar to the VIP customers is contingent upon the personal attributes (dimensions of similarity) made salient by the design of VIP granting method. This finding contributes to the literature of envy and social comparison theories. Second, our findings advance the literature of preferential treatment (e.g., Jiang, Hoegg & Dahl, 2013) by revealing the role of VIP granting methods. Specifically, we showed that VIP status can be granted either based on unchangeable ascribed or changeable achieved attributes. When ascribed attributes were made salient by the granting method, non-VIPs who are dissimilar to the VIPs in this dimension would maliciously envy and consider the VIP privilege less deserving than the case when achieved attributes were made salient. This is because people should earn their benefit by effort instead of inherited at birth according to the equity principle. Contrary, when the non-VIPs consider themselves similar to those VIPs, the VIP privilege would be considered more deserving disregard of the type of salient attribute in use because the non-VIPs believe that they are similar to the VIPs and would have a chance to enjoy the privilege.

242511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
242511.value: There are at least two directions for further development. First, although the moderation effect of LTO cannot be fully verified by experiment approach at the current stage of my research, the initial survey findings hinted that LTO may likely be a moderator influencing the elicitation of envy emotions. I expect, if more time is given to me, I can develop a strong experimental design with LTO priming technique which may help verify the LTO moderation effect in envy theory. Second, during the research process, the cultural ascription-orientation was found as a cultural factor which moderates people’s perceived values of prestigious VIP status. Further research in this novel cultural dimension may help improve our extant understanding of the idiosyncratic behaviors of managers in many business decisions (e.g., acquisition and merging; employee hiring and assessment), and consumers' purchase preferences (values of brands as an ascribed attribute) across Eastern and Western societies.

242511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
242511.value: Recent research evidence shows that the effect of preferential treatment to VIP customers is inconsistent. While researchers tend to agree that preferential treatment enhances loyalty behavior of the valuable VIPs, the prediction of responses of majority envious non-VIPs who are excluded from the preferential treatment is far from conclusive. This research offered a theoretical model with antecedents and contingency factors to explain and predict the positive (benign envy) and negative (malicious envy) responses of non-VIPs. Our findings reveal that marketers can make use of the design of VIP granting methods to guide the thoughts of non-VIPs, and convince them that they are similar/dissimilar to the VIPs. When the non-VIPs consider themselves are similar to the VIPs, they would feel benign envy and perceive a high chance to attain the preferential treatment by engaging in upgrading purchase behaviors. Our findings also show that if non-VIPs feel the VIPs do not deserve their preferential treatment, the non-VIPs will have malicious envy instead of benign envy. Our study not only answered the controversy of preferential treatment effects but also provides practical advice to marketers for them to elicit benign envy and upgrading purchase behaviors of the majority non-VIPs.

243311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
243311.value: The recent economic crisis and the dissolution of the permanent employment contract between individuals and organizations has made job insecurity (JI) an extremely relevant topic for academics and practitioners. In the proposed study, we employ social cognitive theory (Bandura, 1986; 1991; 2001) to develop a conceptual model of the relationship between job insecurity and employee counterproductive work behavior (CWB). Specifically, we propose that JI increases individuals’ propensity to perform CWBs by disengaging the self-regulatory processes that ordinarily sanction and prevent counterproductive behavior. We also suggest that aspects of the organizational context (organizational moral climate) and the individual experiencing the job insecurity (emotional intelligence and resistance to change) will influence the extent to which job-insecure individuals disengage from their organizations and hence their level of CWB. We conclude by describing a plan to test our model in Chinese organizations. 近年來的經濟危機以及雇主雇員之關係的變化使得工作不安全感成爲學術界和業界共同關注的問題。在此項研究中，我們基於社會認知理論（social cognitive theory, Bandura, 1986; 1991; 2001）發展一個模型用於解釋工作不安全感與員工反生産行爲之間的關係。具體來説，我們提出：員工的工作不安全感會增加他們產生道德疏離的可能，從而導致他們的反生産行爲。進一步的，我們認爲組織的環境因素（組織道德氛圍）以及個人的因素（情緒智能和拒絕變化的程度）會影響工作不安全感與員工反生産行爲之間的關係。我們計劃在中國大陸的企業進行取樣檢驗所提出的研究模型。

243311.label: Realisation of objectives
243311.value: All of the project objectives have been achieved. Based on a thorough review of the literature, we have developed a conceptual model to explain the impact of job insecurity (JI) on employee counterproductive work behaviors (CWB) and empirically tested the model. Drawing on social cognitive theory (Bandura, 1986), we propose that JI will cause individuals to morally disengage from their organizations and hence make them more likely to engage in CWB. Further, another important goal of the proposed research is to identify aspects of individuals and organizations that influence the extent to which individuals experiencing JI engage in counterproductive behavior. In the original proposal, we have suggested organizational moral climate as a potential situational variable and emotional intelligence and resistance to change as individual difference variables. We conducted two studies in various organizations and industries in China to examine the proposed mediation and moderation effects. Results from the two studies consistently support the mediation role of moral disengagement between JI and CWB (measured as organizational and interpersonal deviance behaviors at the workplace). This achieves the primary objective of this project, that is, to identify the psychological processes through which job insecurity produces counterproductive work behavior. Also, results provide support for the validity of the measures in the Chinese context. As for the boundary conditions to the effect, although the proposed moderators were not very well supported by our data, we found support for another set of interesting and important moderators— individual hostile attribution, perceived employability, leader-member exchange (LMX) and coworker exchange (CWX). The two studies have been presented in two primary international conferences in the Management field respectively (the Society of Industrial and Organizational Psychology Annual Conference, and the International Academy of Management and Business). We have combined the two studies in one paper and submitted it to the Journal of Applied Psychology. The journal editor and reviewers have provided constructive comments for us to revise and resubmit the paper to the journal. We are now preparing the revision. Unrelated to the above, through the assistance of the same contact person, this project also finally supported data collection for another study about the relationships among psychological contract, organization-based self-esteem, and employee outcomes, which has been accepted for publication in Human Resource Management.

To identify aspects of individuals and organizations that can reduce the extent to which job insecurity results in counterproductive work behaviors.
To validate a measure of moral disengagement and CWB for use in Chinese organizations.
To empirically test the conceptual model in a Chinese context.

243311.label: Major findings and research outcome
243311.value: In this project, we examine when and why employees might respond to job insecurity by engaging in workplace deviance – behavior that harms their organizations and/or their coworkers. Major findings from this research are, first of all, we demonstrated how job insecurity increases the tendency to engage in two forms of deviant behavior. Prior job insecurity research has shown how experiencing job insecurity decreases positive employee behavior in the workplace, be it task performance or OCB (Lee, Bobko, & Chen, 2006; Sverke et al., 2002), but has generally not considered the relationship between job insecurity and intentional negative behaviors. Deviant behavior is a form of negative behavior that is both theoretically relevant [in that it is conceptually and empirically distinct from OCB and traditional job performance (Sverke et al., 2002)] and practically important [as it is extremely costly to organizations and their other members]. Across two studies, our findings show that employees who experience high levels of job insecurity are more likely to engage in interpersonal and organizational deviance. Another major finding of this project is the moral disengagement explanation of the JI effect on employee workplace deviance behaviors. This provides support for the basic mediation effect in our conceptual model which is mainly built on the social cognitive theory. Finally, by drawing on social exchange theory and research on individual differences, we further propose that these effects are contingent upon both individual and contextual factors. Two time-lagged (data collected in three waves) studies of employees at various Chinese organizations provide support for the hypothesized moderated mediation model. Specifically, the effect of job insecurity on organizational and interpersonal deviance via moral disengagement is positive and significant when individuals are high in hostile attribution bias, when leader-member exchange / co-worker exchange is low, or when employees perceived employability is low, but not when individual are low in hostile attribution bias, when LMX/CWX is high, or when employability is high.

243311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
243311.value: First, in addition to the moral disengagement cognitions captured in this research, future research should explore other theoretically plausible mechanism. For example, employee attributions regarding the cause of the organization's actions creating the job insecurity (e.g., attributing them to managerial ineptitude or necessary reactions to a general recession or) might be an attractive focus for future research. Future research can also continue to examine other potential boundary conditions of the mediation effect, in addition to the three factors we found in this research. Thirdly, past research on the antecedents of moral disengagement has focused primarily on individual characteristics (such as moral identity, trait cynicism and chance locus of control orientation. Our findings suggest that, in addition to these individual factors, job insecurity – aspects associated with the organizational context – can also influence the likelihood of moral disengagement. Thus, an interesting opportunity for moral disengagement research to study both individual and contextual factors, and their possible interaction, simultaneously is also suggested. Finally, data were all collected in Chinese organizations. Considering the different cultural and economic development, additional research that compares and contrasts the consequences of job insecurity for Western and Chinese employees would be useful.

243311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
243311.value: Our study illustrates that job-insecure employees may be more likely to morally disengaged in the workplace and, as a result, more likely to engage in deviant behavior subsequently. This mediation effect of moral disengagement on the job insecurity - deviant behaviors relationship was strengthened by individual’s hostile attribution styles and perceived employability, and buffered by the quality of employees’ relationships with their leaders and coworkers. Given that the experience of job insecurity is increasingly prevalent in the modern business environment globally, researchers and managers will want to further explore how it influences employees, so that we can better manage workplace deviance.

243511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
243511.value: Where a product is originated from (country-of-origin effect, COO) is a topic that draws intense efforts in international marketing research. Studies show that this effect is salient and persistent (Bilkey and Nes 1982; Klein 2002). While products originated from developed economies are favored, those from “developing” economies, such as BRICs (Brazil, Russia, India, and China, Verlegh 2007) are unfavorably evaluated (Brouthers and Xu 2002). To reduce the unfavorable effect, products from developing economies need to carry internationally established brand names (Pappu et al. 2007) or sell at major price discounts (Sharma 2010). Interestingly, the above generalizations could not explain how or why Chinese-made products proliferate globally. While studies (Sharma 2010) and executive interviews (Walmart’s CEO) remarked that Chinese-made products could only be marketed at the low-end, value-based segment (Tan and Tse 2010), some newly established Chinese brands, such as Shanghai Tang (fashion clothing brand) and Herbalist (cosmetic brand), have succeeded in affluent markets. In short, why Chinese-made products globalize is a phenomenon the COO literature has yet to explain. There are three conceptual issues that need to be addressed. First, the quality (safety) of Chinese-made products is a well-known concern. Thus, why would affluent market consumers accept Chinese-made products in spite of these concerns? A second challenge emerges from the consumer ethnocentrism literature that suggests that some consumers would adopt a nationalistic bias and reject foreign-made products (Shimp and Sharma 1987; Klein 2002). As China becomes the world factory eroding jobs in affluent economies, it breeds an unfavorable sentiment against China (Verlegh 2007). The third issue relates to a more accepting worldview involving China and other emerging economies. According to Pew's polls, such tendencies are already taking place (Pew Global Attitude Project 2007). We postulate that an expanded worldview will reduce ethnocentric bias and enhance consumers’ product evaluation. We propose empathy (for made-in country) and an expanded worldview are core constructs in understanding the proliferation of Chinese-made products. Using a model that integrates existing COO literature, we examine our hypotheses by sampling consumers from affluent (American and British) and developing markets (Indian and Filipino). With the help of a multinational research firm, Millward Brown, we test our hypotheses using a multi-country survey with 400 consumers from each country. In sum, our study aims to validate an expanded COO model that integrates the effects of made-in-country empathy and expanded worldview in the acceptance of Chinese-made product. 國際市場營銷研究表明,一個產品源於國家原產地的效應是顯著和持久的.雖然起源於發達經濟體的產品受消費者青睞,發展中經濟體，如金磚四國（巴西，俄羅斯，印度和中國）的產品，國家原產地是營銷的不利因數. 我們建議(對製造國的)同理心和世界觀是了解中國製造產品擴散的核心因數。我們整合現有的運營文學,設計了一個模型.通過抽樣調查富裕（美國和英國）和開發市場（印度和馬來西亞）的消費者,研究我們的假設.

243511.label: Major findings and research outcome
243511.value: This project investigates the acceptance of Chinese-made products; a phenomenon that the current Country-of-Origin (COO) literature does not readily explain. We reviewed related literature and published a paper in Journal of Advertising. Using a human values framework with insights from stereotyping literature, we delineate a model of how consumers’ higher order values of Empathy and Openness to Change moderate and alter the negative and positive effects of consumer ethnocentrism and made-in country perceptions, respectively, on the buying intent of Chinese-made products, which face low quality stereotypes. We tested the model in large-scale surveys on consumers from developed and emerging economies. The findings in general supported the hypotheses in developed economies that gave consistent results. The findings contribute to the COO literature and provide insights for researchers and firm managers.We intend to publish these findings in a journal related to international business and are finalizing a draft targeted at the Journal of International Business Studies. Further, we were able to extend this investigation to include not only perceptions of Chinese-made products not also the image of China itself. We published these findings in a book chapter as well as presented them in two conferences.

243511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
243511.value: Interestingly, the findings showed that emerging economies were considerably more varied; not only were they different from developed economies but they were different among themselves, across different emerging economies. These findings may suggest that economic condition (i.e., emerging economy) is but one factor consistent across countries with emerging economies. People's perceptions of Chinese-made products in these countries may be driven by many other factors, be they cultural, historical, geographical, or religious. These issues provide interesting directions for future research in this area and could enrich our understanding of COO effects beyond developed economies.

244211.label: Project Title(Chinese)
244211.value: 無權與受壓的話語：論述香港外來工人的生活

244211.label: Project Objectives
244211.value: To analyse the life stories of domestic helpers in Hong Kong as presentations of self. Themes expected to be identified in these narratives include the perception of self and other, social and cultural hegemony and the repression of self, and the appearance of conflicting identities (the ‘old’ life at home vs. the ‘new’ life in diaspora). To analyse how identities are negotiated in discourse in terms of group allegiances (‘us’ vs. ‘them’) and intergroup differentiation, and how identities are compromised in the face of repression, discrimination and fear. To analyse how taboos, unarticulated shame and repressed experiences (like sexual abuse) become verbalised, and thus cognitively 'real', as joint discursive accomplishments in group discussions. To analyse the importance of crying and laughter as communicative tools in the process of humanising dehumanising experiences. To explore the importance of strong social networks, education, and religious faith in empowering domestic helpers to deal with unacceptable circumstances. To publish several articles in international journals, and a monograph, in which the findings from this research project are presented and discussed. To bring the findings 'back to the community' by sharing with domestic helpers how they may empower themselves to oppose abuse, exploitation and marginalisation. This will be done through popular articles in magazines for domestic helpers (such as HerStory), and through workshops in the shelter.

244211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
244211.value: Immigration is an essential premise of life in a global world. Many professionals choose to work abroad, but for some people, immigration is not a choice but a necessity. People from underdeveloped countries are often faced with grim alternatives: either their children are kept in poverty with no prospects of a better future, or they leave their country to become migrant workers, but, at the same time, suffer the pains of being separated from their families. This project focuses on one group of migrant workers in Hong Kong – domestic helpers. There are about 230,000 maids in Hong Kong, most of them from Indonesia and the Philippines. The aim of the project is to tell the life stories of some of these migrant women by analysing group conversations in which domestic helpers, who have run away from their employers, or who have had their contracts terminated, share their experiences. The venue for data collection is a church shelter for migrant workers where PI is working as a volunteer, and the project analyses migrant worker life stories as evidence of displaced identities. Domestic helper narratives from informal group discussions will be recorded, and (a form of) Discursive Psychology (Potter and Wetherell 1987; Wetherell 2001) will be employed as the analytical framework focusing on themes such as identity-construction and displacement, discrimination and prejudice, powerlessness and abuse, and the externalisation of repressed experiences. The analyses will also focus on the importance of fellowship, religious faith and empowerment for reinventing identities in diaspora. Many of the stories told by domestic helpers in Hong Kong (and elsewhere) are trauma naratives about physical assaults and sexual abuse, harassment, starvation, underpayment, and exploitation. The tellability of these narratives is compromised by the unacceptability of the events, and the project seeks to explore how repressed experiences become externalised and thus, become cognitively 'real' events which require some form of action. It is hypothesised that crying and laughter are important communicative tools in the process of reversing, or humanising, dehumanising experiences. It is also hypothesised that the articulation of shame and the verbalisation of repressed experiences (such as sexual abuse) are joint discursive accomplishments in the group where group members construct their narratives together, as it were, as well as respond to the rhetorical needs of the local context (Billig 1996).

244211.label: Realisation of objectives
244211.value: All the project objectives have been achieved (except for the monograph which is 50% completed). I have collected and recorded stories from close to 300 foreign domestic helpers in Hong Kong which makes my data set one of the largest of its kind. I'm not aware of any other study of (domestic) migrant workers that has collected so much evidence, and this has provided a unique opportunity to explore aspects of domestic helpers' lives and experiences through a detailed analysis of their discourse. Some of these themes are under-explored in the literature (such as project objectives 4 and 5). I have published five journal articles (all in top international journals) and one book chapter is forthcoming. I have also given three papers at major international conferences, and I have organised a panel on Domestic Labour at an international conference. I have given two public lectures, and one invited keynote address at an international conference (the 14th International Conference on Language & Social Psychology, University of Hawaii at Manoa, 19-22 June 2014). I have also given several interviews to the press about my research on foreign domestic helpers, including the South China Morning Post, ATV News, BBC World News, and the Wall Street Journal, and I have held talks for domestic worker NGOs and thus, taken research findings back to the community. I think research goals and research expectations have been met through the six high-quality publications that have appeared/will appear, and through conference papers. The monograph - which has always been seen as a long-term goal - was not expected to be completed within the project period. However, five chapters out of ten are completed, and a detailed book proposal will be submitted to Routledge's Cultural Discourse Series within the next couple of months. I hope to compete the book manuscript within the next year.

244211.label: Major findings and research outcome
244211.value: The analyses found that the lives of foreign domestic helpers are precarious and for many, associated with various forms of exploitation and abuse. The following main findings have been identified and analysed: 1) The identities available to foreign domestic helpers (FDHs) in the diaspora are often enforced rather than a matter of choice. Forced in exile by poverty in their home countries, they embark on a journey which forces them to reinvent themselves in order to provide for their children and other loved ones. Thus, migrant women define themselves in relation to their families as sacrificial mothers, daughters and wives. They also see themselves first and foremost as 'helpers' who are in Hong Kong to serve God, their families and the people of Hong Kong (see part C, 8.1 & 6). 2) The analyses also show that FDHs appear to be untouched by the ethics and equity of Hong Kong society. They are denied the rights that apply to other people, such as the right to eat, rest and talk to their peers. They are often humiliated and denigrated and the analyses show that this affects their self-perception. The analyses have explored local stereotypes and ideological representations as a possible cause for legitimising the exploitation and abuse of FDHs (see part C, 8.2 & 4). 3) The research has also studied how laugher and crying are used as means to humanise dehumanising experiences in FDH storytelling. Both laughter and crying are used repeatedly in the narratives, and the analyses consider the different functions served by these paralinguistic features. Quite surprisingly, they seem to serve similar functions: as a way to deal with trauma without being destroyed by it (see part C, 8.3 & 5).

244211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
244211.value: Because of the size of the data set, there is potential for further development. Themes have been identified which could be analysed in more depth, such as identity transformation and faith as resources for survival for distressed domestic helpers in the diaspora, and social activism as part of a research agenda on, for and with FDHs. The concept of choice, or, as I have argued in a paper (Part C, 9.4), 'choiceless choice', could also be further analysed, as could conceptualisations of 'home' and what it means to be deprived of one's home. These and other themes will be further explored in the monograph on life stories of domestic migrant workers in Hong Kong, expected to be completed in 2015. Other questions that have been identified through this project will be analysed in the follow-up project which looks at alienation and identity transformation in domestic helper returnee narratives (GRF project HKBU/244413). Close to 100 narratives from Indonesian and Filipina returnees have been recorded and are currently being translated and/or transcribed.

244211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
244211.value: The project has provided evidence of the wide-spread abuse and exploitation of domestic migrant workers in Hong Kong. Because of the size of the data set, it has been possible to identify consistent patterns in the abuse. Hunger and fatigue in combination with loneliness and fear were identified as the main sources for FDH's distress and anxiety. The research has also demonstrated that for migrant women identity is often enforced rather than a matter of choice. The research also considers how local stereotypes and ideologies may legitimise the exploitation of FDHs, and it shows how laughter and crying are used as a means to deal with trauma without being destroyed by it. The value of the research lies first, in providing documentation for the wide-spread abuse and/or exploitation of FDHs; second, in explaining how dehumanisation may be used to legitimise abuse and exploitation; and third, in showing how FDHs talk about and deal with their trauma. The many interviews I have given to the press, as well as invitations to give public lectures and a keynote address at an international conference, bear witness to the significance of the research.

244411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
244411.value: Current research on either Hong Kong history or Hong Kong identity are fallen within at least one of the four grand narratives: (i) social narrative: former British colonial legacy; (ii) economic narrative: the rising Asian economic city; (iii) political narrative: part of greater China and (iv) cultural narrative: crossroad between East and West. This research, however, aims to deconstruct the conventional narrative, especially the dichotomy of East and West, so as to reflect upon the conventional narrative and to re-establish a more authentic one. Hence, the research focuses on understanding the expression and manifestation of art. To comprehend the two approaches, the methodologies used in this research would mainly be literature review, archival analysis and oral history, focusing on artists,and institutions as well as the policies. The literature review will look into details of the historical events of Hong Kong to have an overview of the history, history of art and cultural history of Hong Kong. The archival analysis and self-reflection of artworks by selected visual artists will also be done. The oral history will be in the form of semi-structured and in-depth interviews with selected visual artists. The first set of question will be targeting on how (if at all) artists’ works were influenced by a consciousness to produce native “Hong Kong art”, and the second set of questions will be aimed at the institutional influences artists might have felt in the production process of their artwork. 近期香港史或香港身分認同皆陷於以下四大論述其一之中：(i) 社會論述：基調以前英國殖民遺思為主；(ii) 經濟論述：藉香港敍述亞洲經濟城市的掘興；(iii) 政治論述：以香港為大中華的一部份；(iv) 文化論述：把香港置於東西交叉路上為據。這個研究旨在秉棄東西二分法的對立論證；從而解構上述慣性的論述，並藉此構建一個真實的論述。因此本研究將聚焦於藝術的「表現與顯證」的認知。 本研究將立足於對藝術家及其相關機構政策，並就相關文獻回顧、檔案分析及口述歷史為主要研究方法，以此理解「表現與顯證」兩種論述的方案。文獻回顧將深究香港的歷史事件，從而對香港的歷史、藝術史及文化史有全面的認知。研究亦將由選擇部份視覺藝術家對其藝術作品進行自我反思及檔案分析。 口述歷史則將對部分視覺藝術家作半結構及深度面談。第一組問題旨在解答藝術家的作品如何受其意識影響而產生本土的「香港藝術」；第二組問題則旨在解答機構制度對藝術家的創作過程的影響。

244411.label: Realisation of objectives
244411.value: This research focuses on the role of institutions and its policy towards the formation and development of Hong Kong art. The team’s literature review and archival analysis into the history of art in Hong Kong reveals the cultural dynamics in curatorial approaches. Our literature review has also revealed a gap in documentation of the private art organizations and associations compared to public institutions and government funded art organizations. Hence, our team directed its focus towards these private art organizations and associations. The gap in the lack of primary sources and documentation on these organizations such as the Circle Group, New Ink Movement, One Art Group, Modern Literature and Art Association, and Hong Kong Visual Arts Society is overcome by integrating archival research with oral history. Through oral history, the team was able to observe the effect of institutions on the artists’ production and manifestation of their artworks. Oral history not only fills the gaps between various documents, files and records, it also proves the reliability of existing sources and information. The interview findings have contributed to an important area of research on institutional factors towards Hong Kong art. This is in line with our objectives of adopting an institutional approach to studying the history of art by integrating the methodologies of archival research with literature review and oral history. The results of our research also lay the groundwork for future research into the art history of Hong Kong and the use of oral history as a methodology.

244411.label: Major findings and research outcome
244411.value: This research attempts to construct an alternative narrative to the history of Hong Kong art and identity by focusing on the expression and manifestation of art. This is achieved by using a combination of methodologies involving literature review, archival analysis and oral history. While the archival research provides a more objective account of the historical events and reception of artworks in Hong Kong, the use of oral history has yielded interesting findings, which stands in contrast to the objective narrative of archival research. The PI discovers that the development of art does not necessarily display a close connection with the then socio-political or economic factors. The impact of a historical event on the production of arts may not be as pronounced as it appears in the archival research. The findings of the oral history also reveal differing opinions on the meaning of Hong Kong arts. The findings are neither to define Hong Kong Art and its development nor to adopt a grand narrative approach. Rather, the significance of the findings reflects a diversity of views amongst the many artists involved which question the dominant view that Hong Kong culture is passively shaped by the East and the West. The main outcome of this research is the publication of a two-volume book by Joint Publishing (H.K.) Co., Ltd. titled 《與香港藝術對話1960-1979》 and 《與香港藝術對話 1980-2004》that was published in June 2014 and January 2015 respectively. The PI shared the research findings in an interview with arts magazine 號外 (Issue 452, May 2014, pages 70-73). In May 2014, the PI curated an exhibition, “The Wind Shifts: Dialogues with Hong Kong Artists” in which over thirty artists involved in the research were invited to exhibit their artworks to express their concepts. This is accompanied by an exhibition publication published by the Arts in Heritage Research Limited. The PI has also written two journal articles. “A Dialog with Hong Kong Arts: 1842-1960” was published in the Hong Kong Visual Arts Yearbook 2013 (pages 49-63). The other article, “Reconstructing the Hong Kong Landscape: Paintings in Response to Colonialism, Decolonisation and Post-colonialism” has been accepted and is scheduled to be published in the International Journal of Art and Art History. The PI also presented the article at the public symposium, “Expanding the 1980s: The Landscape of Art in China and East Asia”, organized by M+ Matters on 13 January 2015 and an internal workshop on 14 January 2015.

244411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
244411.value: The results of the research, specifically the oral history component comprising more than 45 transcriptions of interviews lay the groundwork for future experts and scholars to compile the art history of Hong Kong. In addition, the research findings on the role of institutions could be a potential input for the West Kowloon Cultural District and its development of M+, which embraces the development of visual culture.

244411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
244411.value: This research constructs an alternative narrative to understanding Hong Kong history and identity through the expression and manifestation of art. This is achieved by using a combination of methodologies involving literature review, archival research and oral history. The conventional narratives have tended to neglect the study of the institution. This research fills the gap by focusing on the role of institutions in the production of art. The use of oral history not only fills the gap between various documents, it also proves the reliability of existing sources and information. The findings reflect a diversity of views of Hong Kong Art and question the dominant view that Hong Kong culture is passively shaped by the East and West. The main outcome is the publication of a two-volume book, which comprises more than 45 transcriptions of interviews with individuals active and renowned in the Hong Kong art sector. The significance of the research has been recognized by the publication of research findings in academic journals and conference presentation. The choice of oral history demonstrates a show of respect to the forerunners and practitioners of Hong Kong Art and laid the groundwork for future research to compile the art history of Hong Kong.

245511.label: Project Title(Chinese)
245511.value: 中国城市的空间重构与居住不平等

245511.label: Project Objectives
245511.value: To inform policy making by providing an update analysis of the nature and extent of housing inequality in Chinese cities under marketized housing provision. Hedonic techniques will be used not only to control for quality differences but also take explicit account of residential location in the computation of inequality indices; Complementing the above is a detailed analysis of accessibility to jobs and urban amenities among socioeconomic groups in light of housing and labour market segmentations. Of special concern are rising car ownership and the extension of metro lines, which obviously impinges on the question of jobs-housing balance and spatial mismatch; To train postgraduate as well as undergraduate students interested in Chinese cities; To present works based on the study in international conferences, and to publish works in leading journals in Geography and Urban Studies and as book chapters; To hold workshops or conferences based on the theme of the project, which will form the basis of journal special issues or book projects.

245511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
245511.value: Ever since the implementation of the paid transfer of land use rights in the late 1980s, China’s major cities have undergone immense spatial structuring. A coalition between municipal governments and real estate interests has emerged to exploit the huge rent gaps, arising largely from institutionalized segmentation of urban and rural land tenures. To counteract the Asian Financial Crisis of 1997-98, the Chinese government designated real estate and auto production as growth engines. Accompanying this was the ending of the welfare allocation of housing in 1998. Accession to the World Trade Organization in 2001 implied the subjection to the full force of globalization, a consequence of which was world city formation. The world’s largest transnational corporations (TNCs) have since scrambled to set up regional headquarters in China’s leading metropolises. They are joined by China’s own emerging TNCs, primarily large state-owned enterprises corporatized under the enterprise reform. Typical of world cities are workforce polarization, growing income spreads, rapidly rising housing costs, and increased spatial segregation. In China the contrast between traditional work-unit compounds and gated commodity housing estates is particularly striking. Complicating the picture is the proliferation of migrant communities on urban-rural fringes. Growing economic and housing inequalities have brought widespread discontents, as testified by repeated efforts by the Chinese government to cool down the overheated housing market. The discontents are particularly severe among the urban poor, many of whom were forced to move to inaccessible suburban locations due to redevelopment programmes, and young professionals who were too young to benefit from the housing reform of the 1990s. The proposed study aims to conduct a multi-facet analysis of the changing nature of residential inequality in China cities under phenomenal spatial restructuring. More specifically, two major dimensions of residential inequality will be examined. The first concerns the extent and nature of housing inequality, especially after the 1998 housing reform and under increased workforce polarization. In relation to the above, the second concerns how this inequality is exacerbated by spatial segmentations in the housing and labour markets. Phenomenal suburbanization, massive investments in urban freeways, and rising car ownership have further enlarged the differences in mobility over space and hence accessibility to jobs, housing and other urban amenities between socioeconomic groups. Surveys conducted by the PI in Guangzhou will form the primary data source for the proposed work. 自从土地有偿使用政策实施以来，过去二十年中国城市经历翻天覆地的空间重构。城乡分割的土地权属和由此而产生的巨大地租差，为城市政府和房地产开发商提供极大的诱因，以前所未有的速度把市郊的农地转换成建设用地。再者，为了抵御亚洲金融风暴对中国的冲击，中国政府于1998年订定房地产开发和汽车制造为经济增长点；同时，宣布停止福利分房。2001年中国加入世界贸易组织，自此更积极参与经济全球化。全球最大的跨国企业纷纷在华设立地区总部；而在造大造强的政策下，中国本身的大型国有企业也进入跨国企业行列，并把总部设在北京、上海、广州等大城市。该等城市因此而晋身成为世界城市的一员。 伴随着世界城市的出现是社会和空间的两极化和空间分割。在中国，传统的单位大院和新建的商品房小区之间的对比特别明显；分布在城郊结合部、以脏乱和握手屋闻名的众多城中村更加剧了居住空间分化的复杂性。今天，社会充斥着对于收入和住房分布不公的不满情绪。其中，哪些未能享受1990年代补贴出售公房的民众，包括城市贫困户和年轻住户，尤其不满。 本研究尝试从多角度分析中国城市住房分布不公的现象；主要从两个方面进行。 首先，研究的重心放在1998年停止福利分房后，影响住房分配的因素和住房分布不公平程度的变化；第二，探究过去一段时间住房与就业市场和空间分布出现的巨大变化，特别是急剧的郊区化、私家车普及化、以及城市高速公路和轨路交通的修建，对住房消费公平性产生的影响。研究的主要数据来自项目主持者前在广州进行的多次大型问卷调查，包括2010年的调查。

245511.label: Realisation of objectives
245511.value: 1. To address objective 1 and to certain extent objective 2, statistical analysis based on survey data collected previously in Guangzhou in 2001, 2005 and 2010 was conducted. While housing inequality did not show major increase between 2001 and 2005, the latter part of the first decade of the 21st Century saw substantial increase. Multivariate analysis further reveals that the nature of housing inequality in Chinese cities become increasingly akin to those in most market economies (Li, 2012 and 2016; Li and Du, 2014; Huang and Li, 2014). However, hukou, land tenure and other institutional factors quite unique to China continue to exert major influences on residential differentiation in both spatial and socioeconomic sense (Wang, Du and Li, 2014; Li and Zhu, 2014). 2. A major factor underlying residential differentiation and changing accessibility to jobs and urban amenities in China is economic restructuring both in the sectoral and spatial sense. In particular municipal governments in the country's leading metropolises have made strenuous efforts to build a knowledge-based economy, emphasizing creativity and cultural production. In line with objective 2, the PI and his collaborators examined the case of Dafen Cultural Village, Shenzhen, exploring the multi-scalar relationships governing the transformation of the painting industry in the village and the plight as well as agency of the migrant-painters under Shenzhen's unprecedented urban development and economic restructuring (see Li, Cheng and Wang, 2014; Wang and Li, 2016). 3. For objective 3, one Phd student, Dr Huimin Du, and one undergraduate student, Miss Hung-ha Cheng, were trained under the project. See Li and Du (2014), Wang, Du and Li (2014), and Li, Cheng and Wang (2014) for examples of the works published under the PI's supervision. 4. For objectives 4 and 5, in addition to the numerous journal articles on various aspects of housing inequalities published, the project has also led to the publication of an edited book (Huang and Li, 2014), two guest-edited journal special issues (Li, Chan and Li, 2014; He, Li and Chan, 2015), and the holding of several paper sessions of a major conference on Chinese cities, as well as the holding of two conferences/workshops. The latter formed the basis of the subsequent book and journal special issue projects. These works further enhance inter-institutional and international academic collaborations.

245511.label: Major findings and research outcome
245511.value: To provide a detailed account of the changing extent and nature of housing inequalities and residential differentiation in Chinese cities, statistical analysis based on the survey data collected previously in Guangzhou in 2001, 2005 and 2010 was conducted. While housing inequality did not show major increase between 2001 and 2005, the latter part of the first decade of the 21st Century saw substantial increase. Multivariate analysis further reveals that the nature of housing inequality in Chinese cities become increasingly akin to those in most market economies (Li, 2012 and 2016; Li and Du, 2014; Huang and Li, 2014). However, Entitlement to work-unit housing prior to the 1998 housing reform, hukou, land tenure and other institutional factors quite unique to China continue to exert major influences on residential differentiation in both spatial and socioeconomic sense as well as on housing ladder climb subsequent to attainment of homeowenership (Wang, Du and Li, 2014; Li and Zhu, 2014; Li, 2016). A major factor underlying residential differentiation and changing accessibility to jobs and urban amenities in China is economic restructuring both in the sectoral and spatial sense. In particular municipal governments in the country's leading metropolises have made strenuous efforts to build a knowledge-based economy, emphasizing creativity and cultural production. In line with objective 2, in addition to studying residential differentiation per se, the PI and his collaborators examined the case of Dafen Cultural Village, Shenzhen, exploring the multi-scalar relationships governing the transformation of the painting industry in the village and the plight as well as agency of the migrant-painters under Shenzhen's unprecedented urban development and economic restructuring (see Li, Cheng and Wang, 2014; Wang and Li, 2016).

245511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
245511.value: An outgrowth of the project was an inter-institutional and international joint venture to study neighbourhood governance, residential attachment, and social capital formation in Chinese cities, particularly with the proliferation of commodity housing estates and the institutionalization of homeowners association as a constituent part of local governance. For this a large-scale survey comprising 1800 households distributed in three distance zones of Guangzhou was conducted in 1200. This rich dataset not only resulted in the publication of Fu et al (2015) and other works of the international study team, but also formed a major data source of the PI's next GRF project, which focusses on residential mobility and neighbourhood change. Two PhD students are currently working on the latter project. Some early findings have been presented in international conferences and submitted to leading journals for publication consideration.

245511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
245511.value: Statistical works based on the survey data collected in Guangzhou show that while housing inequality did not major change between 2001 and 2005, the latter part of the first decade of the 21st Century saw substantial increase. Also, while the nature of housing inequality in Chinese cities become increasingly akin to those in most market economies, entitlement to work-unit housing prior to the 1998 housing reform, hukou, land tenure and other institutional factors quite unique to China continue to exert major influences on residential differentiation in both spatial and socioeconomic sense as well as on housing ladder climb subsequent to attainment of homeowenership.

Preliminary findings based on the survey have been presented in international conferences, in addition to leading to the publication of Fu et al. (2015). 246111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
246111.value: This research project investigates the historical developments of Asianism from the nineteenth century till the present as a manipulable ideology, an emancipatory cause, and a mechanism through which people in the region negotiate and construct their unique identity. It examines how China interacts with the changes of Asianism and in what ways the notion can shed new light on China’s developments and problems. Other than considering the conceptual writings about Asianism, the project also makes use of the cultural productions in the region, such as transnational films, and other cultural exchanges, in order to analyze how Asian collaborations and the region’s drive for unity are operated and perceived in concrete reality. While Asianism has been (and is still being) appropriated by the state to serve the interests of ruling class for aggressive expansion and by those (individuals and groups) motivated by nationalist ideology to claim hegemonic position over other Asians, this research attempts to focus more on the ideas of the non-state or transnational agencies and their movements for the cause of Asianism and exploring its emancipation potentials and deep cultural implications not only for the Asian races but also for other peoples in the world. The project aims to i) understand and analyze Asianism as a concept, an ideology and a movement within its appropriate historical contexts; ii) examines the implications of Asianism to China especially in the twenty-first century; iii) conceptualize Asianism, with the focus on the non-state or transnational agencies, as a vibrant internationalist alternative to nationalist ideology that is prevailing in the cultural-political scene of today’s world; iv) seek the potential of Asianism for a possible emancipation project by rediscovering its revolutionary and utopian spirit that has been dismissed and manipulated in the past; v) rethink Asianism in order to find out a new momentum for changing the existing hierarchy and hegemonic order, and look for the possibility of a more egalitarian and just form of human community; and vi) go beyond the elite-driven or state-oriented Asianism to investigate the connections between Asianism and non-state forces in order to examine their multiple voices and enormous possibilities through the study of various cultural forms, film in particular, circulated and exchanged in Asia. 本研究計劃分析十九世紀以來，亞洲主義在過去歷史上，如何被挪用作意識形態工具、自由解放運動理想，以及區內人民建構身份的媒介。集中探討中國以往怎樣面對亞洲主義，並展望崛起中的中國對亞洲主義未來發展的影響。除了在理念思維上探究，本研究計劃亦具體地從文化產品，特別是泛亞洲電影製作，討論亞洲主義引伸的各種問題。一路以來，亞洲主義論述總受各國政府所把持操控，故本研究計劃試圖將焦點放在非官方的、民間以至國家以外的個體或群體力量上，希望藉此釋放亞洲主義的其他進步的可能性。

246111.label: Realisation of objectives
246111.value: While the notion of Asianism means many different, if not conflicting, things to many different people, the project focuses on the historical Chinese understanding in reference to the Japanese discourse of pan-Asianism. The study thoroughly analyzes that Asia is historically never a single entity, and there has never been universal agreement on what Asia means and includes. While Asia-in-itself is like the Kantian notion of “thing-in-itself,” something that cannot be understood by human perception, Asia-for-itself is a self-consciousness, self-identification with “Asia” as the master signifier. This consciousness of “Asia” is, in the Chinse context, an ideological imagination. The East-West or Orient-Occident dichotomy or mapping by Eurocentric ideology reinforces such Asian imaginary or differentiation. China’s state-led economic achievement paradoxically dilutes Asia-consciousness since its success only means a further integration into the global system of capitalism and the surge of national pride. On the surface, nationalism seems to be in opposition to Asianism. But Asian nationalism was also a kind of anti-imperialist nationalism, or decolonization movement implying a solidarity of oppressed Asian peoples against the imperialist encroachments and epistemological bias. The study finds that nationalist ideology alienates Asian nations from one another. Modern Japanese state historically was able to use nationalism as a powerful means to challenge the Western supremacy in Asia. This study finds that the recent emergence of Chinese nationalism could be understood better in reference to Japan’s Asianist discourse, but is seeking non-state actors to be the driving force of an ideal Asianism. Asia was once a significant place for revolutions and liberation movements. Pan-Asian solidarity first happened among radical revolutionaries who have strong commitment to internationalist anti-colonial movement. The epicenter of revolution has moved in the 20th century from the advanced industrialized countries of the West to the economically backward lands of Asia. The tendency to identify with something larger than a nation, like a civilization, religion, or even the oppressed people, seems contradictory to the age of rising nationalism but constitutes an important vision. (Pan-)Asian thoughts are not merely anti-Western critiques expressing discontent with the Eurocentric international order, or nativist rejection of Western-originated modernity. Asianism may also orient towards revolutionary and utopian visions in our age that suffers from a paucity of political and cultural imaginations.

246111.label: Major findings and research outcome
246111.value: Pan-Asian consciousness could be traced back to the late nineteenth century, and after WWII it manifested again in Bandung conference of 1955. The identification served as a source of inspiration for the growth of political movements against (Western) colonialism and imperialism, and the search for different models to development and international relations. It stands for a new momentum for changing the existing hierarchy and hegemonic order, and to look for the possibility of a more egalitarian and just form of human community. The project has examined the way how the idea of Asia is grasped in very diverse ways, if not contradictory and conflicting, in the cultural-historical contexts of (trans-)national cinemas in different Asian communities, and beyond. While the self-definitions or self-understandings of the peoples of Asia are still very much under the parameter of the Western form of knowledge production, there have been some different paths taken, or at least desires ever expressed, to construct a somewhat self-contradictory “Asian idea of Asia”, that is to say, to claim back an alienated concept imposed upon by the West and other hegemonic powers throughout the modern history of the region, and to search for a non-derivative kind of epistemology and self-recognition. However, Asian nationalist impulses also intensify the relations among many Asian nations, bringing adverse effects to the possible solidarity. The project has discussed how Asian popular culture—no matter it is in traditional or digital forms—is a fundamental operator of contemporary ideological state apparatus. The creative and cultural industries may not serve well both for economic development and the growth of soft power. In general, Asian modernity is still largely a copy of the Western one, especially the way how Asian nations construct their past in a linear historical trajectory, which was very much shaped by Western enlightenment ideals of progress. There’s an argument that since the West is incapable of fulfilling the enlightenment ideals (universal freedom, global equality), Asia should take up this mission to realize these ideals originated from the West on a greater scale. The research finds out that the East-West dichotomy in Asianism is only a cover-up of the opposition between premodern-modern, precapitalist-capitalist systems. Precisely because utopian Asianism has not been realized in history that provides its utopian urge with intellectual and historical vitality. It is the striving for utopia, not its realization or accomplishment, that offers the dynamic in Asian history.

246111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
246111.value: If utopian Asianism has ever been realized, it would lose its significance, for reality or history (i.e. an imperfect state of affairs) means process and change. And utopia realized (a perfect state) would mean static, changeless, lifeless and boring. Utopian ideals make people aware of the imperfections of the present and move them to transform it. The thinking on the Asian region as one single geopolitical unit could provide a way to embrace Asia to overcome nationalism (and its exclusiveness), move away from Eurocentrism, and apply the Third World perspective in the region by realizing the double project of adapting to and overcoming modernity. The future study of Asianism may be a key to go beyond the world system of which modernity is a capitalist world system, and to establish a new analytical category beyond the level of the nation-state as a basic operational unit of world system. Asia discourse is to accomplish a mid-term agenda of building an unconventional state which would be a bridge between long-term agendas involving sweeping transformation of the world system and short-term reform agendas.

246111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
246111.value: This study examines how, from the nineteenth century of European imperialism, some Asian thinkers already strived to conceive a possible world after Europe. Tenshin’s concept of “Asia is one,” Tagore’s promotion of Asian spiritualism, and Sun Yat-sen’s “kingly way of Greater Asia” were inspired by Asian nationalism resisting the powers of Europe. Asianism as a general term referring to a wide range of ideas and movements has created consequences in much of Asia since then. The postwar left-wing intellectuals have been insistently reconfiguring the notion of “Asia” as a persistent form of resistance against the Western hegemony. The notion of Asia is understood as an important vision to strive for emancipation and for a better human future. Under the historical contexts of Nehru’s advocacy of pan-Asian non-alignment and Mao’s promotion of Asian-African-Latin American Third-Worldism, the thoughts of Asia are orienting towards revolutionary and utopian visions in the Cold War age. The ideal of Asianism provides a new incentive to theorize a global relationship between the liberation practice of people and the epistemology of knowledge. The scholarly research of Asianism seeks a different configuration of knowledge through which the truth and the complex reality of Asia can be viewed and understood.

246311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
246311.value: War and peace is such an important issue for humankind that we need to make use of the richness of global cultural resources for our collaborative moral thinking about this topic. China’s military has long been the object of worldwide China watch. This research focuses on Chinese military ethics in general and just war ethics in particular by investigating the rich ideas as contained mainly in "The Seven Military Classics" (wujing qishu) and its commentaries. The key questions are: only under what circumstances should a government initiate the legitimate use of military force? What are the moral constraints on the way that such force is legitimately employed? This research further seeks to analyze how contemporary military force, both in mainland China and in Taiwan, interpret and appropriate the traditional military ethics in this set of books. Finally, after scrutinizing the nuances of contemporary Western (mainly American) just war ethics, this research critically assesses the relative merits and shortcomings of the Chinese just war ethics vis-à-vis American just war ethics. 戰爭與和平對人類來說是一個非常重大課題，因此需要動員全人類不同文化思想資源來反思。中國歷史文化中對“義戰”、“義兵”、“義軍”有非常豐富的討論。本研究以《武經七書》（包括《孫子兵法》、《吳子兵法》、《司馬法》、《六韜》、《尉繚子》、《黃石公三略》、《唐太宗李衛公問對》）及其註解為焦點，探討兵家對合理動用軍事武力的道德條件，及使用軍事武力時有何道德約束的思想，以及當代人對這些思想的闡釋。另一方面，本研究也會詳細分析西方當代正義戰爭倫理，及與中國義戰傳統對比，批判性地評估雙方思想的優缺點

246311.label: Realisation of objectives
246311.value: 1. The various discussions related to just war (or righteous war, “yi zhan”) in 《The Seven Military Classics》as well as in some other classical texts have been thoroughly researched. To a large extent these discussions are analogous to the components of “ius ad bellum” and “ius in bello” in the western just war traditions. 2. Contemporary Western just war ethics is at a crossroads, especially on “just cause” and “legitimate authority” of the “ius ad bellum” component. The diverse developments are occasioned by both the “War on Terror” and the “Responsibility to Protect (R2P).” 3. Ancient Chinese just war ethics, as investigated in this research, has both relative merits and shortcomings vis-a-vis Western just war ethics. It predated the emergence of just war discourse in Europe, but suffered from the lack of sufficient developments. However, the imperative of humanitarian intervention is very strong in the Chinese discourses, which is significant for contemporary reflection.
