310111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
310111.value: 遺傳編程法(GP)自動地進化及編寫電腦程式。它成功應用於軟件再工程，電子綫路合成，生物信息學及數據挖掘。而理想的自動編程系統除了能編程外，亦能由此過程中學習知識並找出優良程式的特點。它能準確地組織知識並能講解如何編寫設計優良的程式，以及為何某些程式不適合。如要發展此類系統，則需要研究知識表示方法及學習演算法 為了達成此具挑戰性的目標，我們發展了文化為基適應性遺傳編程法(GBGP)。它以文法來表示知識並通過改變文法以學習知識。雖然它有大量成果，它不能有效應用於高依存度問題。由於其文法形式不能精確地表示電腦程式元件與元件間的不確定依存關係，此法會產生複雜的文法。由於文法代表解難過程中獲得的知識，我們可以通過分析學習來的文法以理解難題的特性，並明白如何發展好及優雅的程式。但是複雜的文法會妨礙其分析及再用。此法亦偶會不當地改變文法。由於文法亦代表著所有解難方案，而每當文法改變，其相應解難方案亦會改變。如不當地改動文法，將不能產生有效解難方案，亦妨礙學習更佳文法。 為了解決以上問題，我們提議進行全面及有系統的實驗，以了解以上現象的成因，亦會研究新的文法形式，以有效地表示依存關係，並會發展一系列依存關係學習方法。我們會製作新系統以融合新的文法形式，學習方法及其他技術。此系統會應用於商業，科學，市塲直銷及生物信息學上。我們會執行實驗以比較新系統及現有方法。我們會與學科專家及業者討論解難過程中學習來的新知識。而且，以上新的文法形式及學習方法可應用於分佈估計演算法(EDA)及分佈估計編程法(EDP)，以改善其效用及效率。此研究對遺傳編程法(GP)，分佈估計演箅法 (EDAs)，進化演箅法及其應用將有深遠影響。總而言之，此項目將使香港在這些學科上有優勢。

310111.label: Realisation of objectives
310111.value: We have compared traditional GP, POLE, PAGE-EM, PAGE-VB and adaptive GBGP on a number of benchmark problems including the symbolic regression, six-multiplexer, MAX, deceptive MAX, royal tree, deceptive royal tree, asymmetric royal tree, and asymmetric royal tree problems. The asymmetric royal tree and deceptive asymmetric royal tree problems have been proposed for this research study and they have very high degree of inter-dependence. It has been observed that the deceptive MAX, deceptive royal tree, asymmetric royal tree, problems are difficult for traditional GP and adaptive GBGP. Moreover, complicated grammars may be generated by adaptive GBGP for these problems. The issue is caused by the high degree of inter-dependences within these problems. We have developed a new formalism for representing dependences among different components of programs. In the formalism, two levels of dependences can be represented. For the local level, every grammar rule having non-terminal symbols at its right hand side will be associated with a Bayesian network or a Bayesian classifier. It represents the probabilistic dependences among the non-terminal symbols at the right hand. Bayesian networks learning algorithms is used to learn the model structure and parameters. For the global level, one or two networks are used for the whole grammar. The networks represent the probabilistic dependences among all non-terminal symbols of the grammar. One network is used if the dependences are learnt from good programs only. Two networks are used if the dependences are induced from both good and poor programs. During the evolution process, the structure(s) of the networks(s) will be used to represent the global level dependences. An EDP approach is used to learn the dependences among different parts of the grammar rules. After defining a modeling formalism and identifying some benchmark problems for evaluation purpose, we have implemented a version of a new GP system, called BGBGP, based on the modeling formalism. BGBGP applies Bayesian networks to represent dependences. Experiments have been performed to compare BGBGP with traditional GP, POLE, PAGE-EM, PAGE-VB and adaptive GBGP on the symbolic regression, six-multiplexer, MAX, deceptive MAX, royal tree, and deceptive royal tree problems. It has been observed that BGBGP outperforms traditional GP and adaptive GBGP on the MAX, deceptive MAX, royal tree, and deceptive royal tree problems. On the other hand, traditional GP and adaptive GBGP outperform BGBGP on the six-multiplexer problem. For this problem, BGBGP may sometimes learn an inappropriate probabilistic structure from some sub-optimal programs generated in the early generations. The inappropriate probabilistic structure will significantly reduce the probability of applying a grammar rule which is essential in the generation of optimal programs. Thus, some methods have been studied to avoid the learning of some inappropriate probabilistic structures. Since we have observed that BGBGP had issues in handling the six-multiplexer problem, we have hypothesized that Bayesian networks may not be the appropriate models for this problem. Thus the modeling formalism have been revised and the context variables have been introduced. Experiments have been done to compare BGBGP with and without the context variables on a number of problems. It has been observed that BGBGP with the context variables performs better. However, BGBGP with the context variables still cannot solve the six-multiplexer problem very well. Thus we have developed a new system called GBGPBC that applies Bayesian classifiers. A new sampling method has been proposed to reduce the possibility of generating poor individuals. We have used GBGPBC with and without the context variables to solve the six-multiplexer, deceptive MAX, royal tree, deceptive royal tree, and asymmetric royal tree problems. It has been observed that GBGPBC with the context variables outperforms BGBGP with the context variables on some problems. We have compared GBGPBC with traditional GP, POLE, PAGE-EM, PAGE-VB, and adaptive GBGP. It has been found that GBGPBC outperforms the other systems on the deceptive MAX, royal tree, deceptive royal tree, and asymmetric royal tree problems. However, traditional GP and adaptive GBGP outperform GBGPBC, POLE, and PAGE-EM, PAGE-VB on the six-multiplexer problem. A number of potential causes of this phenomenon have been identified. They are 1) the sampling bias, 2) the presence of introns, 3) the selection method, and 4) multiple semantically equivalent forms for an individual. Since the development of new approaches to tackle these issues is beyond the scope of this research, we will study these approaches in other projects. We have designed some methods to modify and learn grammar rules dynamically. The codes for splitting grammar rules and Bayesian networks have been implements. The other program components to implement the methods have been developed. The new system is called BGBGP-HL. Experiments have been performed to compare BGBGP-HL with other systems on a number of benchmark problems including the deceptive royal tree and asymmetric royal tree problems. It has been observed that BGBGP-HL outperforms the other systems on these problems. Moreover, some new grammar rules representing hierarchical problem solving knowledge have been discovered. The learnt grammar rules and Bayesian networks have been further analyzed to ensure that problem-specific domain knowledge has been acquired and represented in the grammar rules and Bayesian networks. The systems have been applied in some real-life business and scientific applications. The new systems have been used on Direct Marketing problems. Experiments have been conducted to compare the performance of the models induced by the new systems and other existing methods including logistic regression, artificial neural networks, Bayesian networks, Bagging, Boosting, etc. It has been observed that the performance of the models generated by the new systems outperform the performance of those induced by other methods. We have also identified that the new systems outperform adaptive GBGP for this problem. We have also used our systems to perform proteomic analysis on the light-sensing compartment of photoreceptors called the outer segment (OS) in the retina. The data provide the profile of proteins identified in the retina from mice in the experiment. Given a set of proteins (represented using protein sequences) obtained, our goal is to predict whether a given protein can be found in OS segment. The prediction model reveals the sequence information with the functions of these proteins for them to detect light. Since OS segment is responsible for vision and visual perception, it is expected that an accurate prediction model gives insight on the photo transduction properties of the proteins, i.e. whether a protein emits signals in the presence of light. Given the prediction model, the molecular biologists will know why the proteins colocalize in the OS rather than the other regions. Furthermore, drug manufacturers can also design new proteins (or drugs) that can be controlled via light.

310111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
310111.value: It has been observed that different PMBGP (Probabilistic Model-Based Genetic Programming) systems, such as POLE, PAGE-EM, PAGE-VB, BGBGP, and GBGPBC, have difficulties in solving the six-multiplexer problem and some other problems, although traditional GP can tackle these problems. Based on our analysis, we hypothesize that the reasons for this phenomenon are 1) the presence of introns, 2) the selection method, 3) multiple semantically equivalent forms for an individual, 4) the positional restriction and 5) sampling bias. The difficulty in solving these problems raises an important issue in that it hinders PMBGP from being an effective general problem solver that can deal with problems having various characteristics and levels of difficulty. Therefore it is necessary to identify and develop novel methods to tackle this issue. This difficulty is also a concern for PMBGAs, as similar phenomena may occur in these systems as well. We suggest a comprehensive investigation of the actual causes for the problematic phenomenon. We can develop a framework inspired by the latest advances in PMBGP, multi-objective optimisation, behavioural programming and semantic methods of GP to handle the issue. A new PMBGP system can be implemented and it can be employed to solve real-life problems.

310111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
310111.value: Genetic Programming (GP) evolves computer programs automatically. Many real-world applications of GP in software re-engineering, electronic circuits synthesis, bioinformatics, and data mining have been succeeded. Not only can an ideal automatic programming system generate programs automatically, it can also learn from the experience in writing different programs and identify the patterns of elegant programs developed. Moreover, it can organize the acquired knowledge accurately and give appropriate explanations on how to write well-designed programs as well as why some programs are inappropriate. The keys in achieving the challenging goal of building an ideal automatic programming system are the knowledge representation methods and the learning algorithms. In this project, a new formalism has been proposed to represent knowledge in grammars and Bayesian networks. The formalism can represent probabilistic dependences among different components of programs. A number of methods for learning grammars and Bayesian network have been developed. The formalism, learning methods, and other techniques have been implemented in new GP systems. We have compared our systems with existing approaches and observed that our systems outperform the others in many problems. The project has an impact on GP and evolutionary algorithms as well as their applications.

340011.label: Project Objectives
340011.value: To investigate whether the quality of financial audits can constrain tax noncompliance and how the effectiveness of this monitoring mechanism changes as book-tax conformity changes. To investigate whether the provision of tax services by CPA firms can constrain tax noncompliance and how the linkage between tax services and tax noncompliance changes as book-tax conformity changes. To investigate whether a more independent board of directors can constrain corporate tax noncompliance and how the effectiveness this monitoring mechanism changes as book-tax conformity changes.

To investigate whether the provision of tax services by CPA firms can constrain tax noncompliance and how the linkage between tax services and tax noncompliance changes as book-tax conformity changes.
To investigate whether a more independent board of directors can constrain corporate tax noncompliance and how the effectiveness this monitoring mechanism changes as book-tax conformity changes.

340011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
340011.value: Accounting scandals and corporate tax avoidance and evasion activities in the U.S. have led to calls to explicitly link taxable income to book income. For example, one of the alternatives considered by the President’s Advisory Panel on Federal Tax Reform in the U.S. is taxing book income. It has been argued that linking the two income measures thereby increasing the book-tax tradeoff will lessen corporate incentives to engage in tax noncompliance activities because public firms are generally unwilling to reduce their reported book income to accommodate an aggressive tax position. If they do, they could incur significant financial reporting costs such as negative capital market effects and violations of debt covenants. In China, the situation is the opposite, i.e. moving from a system that closely links book and tax incomes to a delinked system due to the need for harmonization. Using China’s tax and audit environment as the research setting, we propose to empirically investigate how the change in book-tax conformity caused by China’s adoption of the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) affects the effectiveness of monitoring mechanisms in constraining corporate tax noncompliance behaviors. The monitoring mechanisms we propose to study relate to auditors, tax service providers and board of directors (proxy for corporate governance). 出于國際化的需要，中国正由一个账面所得与课税所得紧密结合的系统向一个（二者）独立的系统转化。以中国的税收与审计环境为研究背景，我们提出实证地研究由中国采纳国际财务报告标准而引起的财税一致的转变会如何影响限制公司违反税法行为的监管机制的有效性。我们提出研究的监管机制与审计师，税收服务提供者，以及董事会（代表公司管制）有关。

340011.label: Realisation of objectives
340011.value: We have fully realized Objective #1 and were able to identify the nature of the relationship between audit quality and tax noncompliance. For Objective #2, as explained in our 2013 Annual Report, our investigations discover that Chinese CPA firms do not normally provide their audit clients tax services. Therefore, there was not enough data to test whether the provision of tax services by Chinese CPA firms can constrain tax noncompliance. For Objective #3, we have obtained some useful results in assessing the relationships among different aspects of corporate governance, audit quality and tax noncompliance. In reviewing Chinese tax systems for this research grant project, I have obtained comprehensive information on the Chinese tax system including tax incentives provided by the Chinese government. I used those background information to contribute to the development of a tax policy paper comparing the effectiveness of Chinese vs. US tax reduction policies. While this research grant project deals with factors that affect tax noncompliance, the tax policy paper touches on factors that affect the effectiveness of tax policy implementations. Serious noncompliance is one variable that affects the effective implementation of a tax policy.

340011.label: Major findings and research outcome
340011.value: Prior studies have shown that high-quality auditors are effective in reducing clients’ earnings management which involves mainly overstatements of earnings. This study examines whether high-quality auditors can also constrain clients’ tax noncompliance. Defining high quality auditors being non-local or large auditors, we find that high-quality auditors are associated with client firms’ better overall tax compliance. Particularly, high-quality auditors are effective in constraining book-tax conforming noncompliance which relates mainly to understatements of both book and taxable income. The constraining effect is more significant at the lower book-tax conformity period suggesting a need to improve audit quality as many transition economies depart from tax-based accounting to adopt International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) which will lower book-tax conformity. The results contribute to the literature by providing evidence that high-quality auditors are effective not only on detecting overstatements of earnings, but also play an important role in constraining tax-motivated understatements of earnings. For Objective #3, we determined that the independent director ratio (number of independent directors over the total number of directors on the board) has no significant effect on the choice of quality auditors. On the other hand, the percentage of shares held by senior executives had a significantly negative impact on the choice of a high quality auditor which in turn affects tax noncompliance. We also do not find that the political connections (appointments) of the CEO have a significant impact on tax noncompliance.

340011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
340011.value: In the future, we can further assess other more macro factors that affect tax noncompliance. These factors can include difference in culture and difference in legal systems (eg. civil law vs. common law vs. Islamic law) particularly with respect to tax law enforcements. This will expand the horizon of the research from China to the international arena. We will need to study the characteristics of different cultural and legal systems as they relate to tax compliance.

340011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
340011.value: Tax noncompliance is a common problem for many developed and developing countries. This problem is particularly serious for developing economies including China because of their lack of experience or resource in dealing with tax evasion and the relatively week enforcement efforts. The recent trend that many profit making companies report little or no taxable income by manipulating transactions to avoid taxes has attracted attention not only from tax authorities, but also from investors and other financial statement users. This research mainly assesses whether high quality financial auditors who are not involved in preparing the tax return of their audit clients can help reduce the tax noncompliance of their clients. High quality auditors are normally the larger or the more independent auditors. We find that overall high quality auditors can indeed constrain tax noncompliance as compared with low quality auditors. In particular, high quality auditors are specifically effective in constraining the kind of tax noncompliance that affects financial statements such as the understatement of sales or the overstatement of cost of goods sold. Furthermore, as a country departs from tax-based accounting towards the adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards, (IFRS), this constraining effect becomes more significant.

340111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
340111.value: Authoritarian leadership has generally been found to undermine employee commitment and productivity. However, some researchers have concluded that paternalistic and other forms of directive leadership can be useful under certain conditions and may be appropriate for developing collectivist societies such as China. Researchers and practitioners have long been skeptical about the applicability of Western participative management practices in the Chinese context. Recently, theorists and practitioners in China have begun to see participative leadership as an effective way to secure employee commitment and loyalty. Participative leadership may be an important way to adapt to the changing labor market in China. Research is needed to directly examine and understand the dynamics by which authoritarian leaders and participative leaders have their effects and the conditions that impact them in both Chinese and Western settings. Previous research suggests that the approach to conflict management is a useful way to understand the mechanisms by which authoritarian and participative leaders have their effects. Participative leaders invite an open discussion of views and work to try to integrate them; this cooperative approach to conflict results in employee commitment and productivity. Authoritarian leaders rely on a competitive approach to conflict as they unilaterally decide and require employees to allow them to impose their resolutions without directly considering the ideas and interests of employees. Employees are forced to agree and to submit. The proposed studies examine how conflict management approaches mediate the relationship between leadership styles and employee commitment and performance in State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) in China, Sino-Western joint ventures in China, and private companies in the West. Theorists from the West have recently joined Asian ones in arguing that the nature of the interpersonal relationships has dramatic effects on the coordination of resources between organizational members. The proposed studies argue that guanxi, which is a strong interpersonal relationships, may moderate the effects of leadership styles on conflict management in Chinese settings. The proposed studies suggest that the influence of Western values on Chinese people’s reaction to authoritarian leadership should be more prevalent in Sino-Western joint ventures where Chinese people interact with Westerns continually and are being socialized into Western management. This proposed study investigates the extent authoritarian leadership and participative leadership influences employees, how conflict management mediates the relationship between authoritarian and participative leaders and employees, and how the Chinese concept of guanxi moderates this relationship in Chinese state-owned companies. 大部分研究认为威权式的领导风格不利于促进生产力及员工的积极性，但也有一些学者提出类似威权式领导的家长式领导和其他长官式领导在某些条件下，特别是在集体主义盛行的地方也是有正面作用的。 不少学者和业界人士长期以来对西方管理学理论是否适合中国社会的实际情况持怀疑的态度。近年来，学界和业界人士逐渐看到西方的参与式领导风格也有助于提高中国员工的积极性和忠诚度。参与式的领导风格也许在中国迈向市场经济体制的过程中发挥着越来越重要的作用。研究者应该就威权式领导及参与式领导的机制以及产生效用的条件在中西方同时进行研究。 过往的研究建议通过对冲突管理的认识来理解领导风格及其产生效用的机制。参与式领导通常鼓励开诚布公的对话和交流，可能更倾向于以合作的方法有利于增强员工的积极性和生产力。威权式的领导可能更倾向于采取竞争的方法来解决冲突，在没有考虑下属意见和处境的情况下单方面做出决定强迫下属执行。本研究将在中国的国有企业、中西合资企业以及美国的民营企业中采样，并探求冲突管理对领导风格（威权式领导和参与式领导）及其效用的中介作用。随着西方学界对中国“关系”概念的兴趣逐渐加深，越来越多人认识到“关系”的作用。本研究也将就“关系”在领导风格（威权式领导和参与式领导）及冲突管理之间的调节作用进行研究。

340111.label: Realisation of objectives
340111.value: All the objectives of this project were realized. First, the findings of this project provide empirical support that the Western developed theory of cooperation and competition can help us understand the dynamics of authoritarian leadership and participative leadership in China and identify conditions under which they can be effective. This project conducted a series of studies and found that cooperative and competitive conflict approaches had significant moderating effects on the relationships between the two leadership styles and leadership effectiveness. Specifically, authoritarian leadership had a significantly negative relationship with leadership effectiveness when the leader’s cooperative approach to conflict was high, yet it had a non-significant relationship with leadership effectiveness when the leader’s cooperative approach to conflict was low. By contrast, authoritarian leadership had a significantly positive relationship with leadership effectiveness when the leader’s competitive approach to conflict was high, yet it had a significantly negative relationship with leadership effectiveness when the leader’s competitive approach to conflict was low. We also found that participative leadership had a significantly positive relationship with leadership effectiveness when the leader’s cooperative approach to conflict was high, and it had a non-significant relationship with leadership effectiveness when the leader’s cooperative approach to conflict was low. Participative leadership had a significantly positive relationship with leadership effectiveness no matter whether the leader’s competitive approach to conflict was high or low. Therefore, the first research objective that “document that the Western developed theory of cooperation and competition can help to understand the dynamic of authoritarian leadership and participative leadership in China and identify conditions under which they can be effective” was well realized. Second, results of data analysis suggested that the examination of the mediating effects of cooperative conflict management between leadership styles and outcomes was successful. Results of a series of studies indicated that participative leadership style was positively related to while authoritarian leadership was negatively related to cooperative conflict management approach that in turn contributed to leader effectiveness. Therefore, the second research objectives that “examine the mediating effects of cooperative conflict management between leadership styles and outcomes”was also well realized. Third, this project identified the moderating effects of guanxi on the relationship between leadership styles and conflict management approaches in Chinese settings. The findings suggested that guanxi had a significantly moderating effect on the relationship between authoritarian leadership and leadership effectiveness. Good quality guanxi between leaders and subordinates would buffer the negative effects of authoritarian leadership on leader effectiveness and strengthen the negative effects of authoritarian leadership on leader effectiveness through constructive controversy between leaders and followers. Therefore the third research objective that “identify the moderating effects of guanxi on the relationship between leadership styles and conflict management approaches in Chinese settings” was also realized. Last, one of the studies of this project was conducted in joint ventures in China. Results found that although authoritarian leadership was negatively related to constructive controversy between leaders and subordinates, developing good relationship between leaders and subordinate would buffer this negative relationship and contributed to employee performance and happiness. Therefore, the forth research objective of “provide a platform to enhance leader effectiveness in cross-cultural settings in China” was also well realized.

340111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
340111.value: Studies of this project address the important issue of leadership styles in different cultural background. The values of these studies include: First, the studies of this project strengthen the leadership literature by identifying the mediating effects of conflict management approach and the moderating effects of guanxi. They tested the mediating effects of cooperative conflict management as well as the moderating effects of Chinese guanxi on the relationship between leadership styles and leadership effectiveness and empirically linked the literatures on conflict management and leadership studies. These studies also added to the emerging empirical research on the mediators and moderators that facilitated leadership styles. Second, the studies of this project also enrich our understanding of cross-cultural leadership by investigating relationships between Western managers and Chinese employees as well a comparison of the effects of different leadership styles in Sino-foreign joint ventures in Chinese contexts. They developed knowledge directly useful for helping people from diverse cultures work together cross-culturally. Third, findings of this project challenge the traditional cultural theorizing that participative leadership and open discussion are ineffective in China and support the theorizing that adopting conflict management approach that matches leadership style helps leaders make their style more effective.

340411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
340411.value: In Hong Kong, South Asians and other ethnic minorities have achieved a more heightened visibility in recent years, notably through wide public debates during and after enactment of the Race Discrimination Ordinance in 2008. However, scholarly research on ethnic minorities in HK remains chronically underdeveloped, even as the struggle for assimilation and recognition among these communities (e.g. in education, employment, social adaptation, cultural survival) continues to generate a growing social tension and threaten social harmony. To date, there is little attention paid to the minorities’ own sense of subjecthood, such as their construction and articulation of self-understanding formed through lived experiences, sensibilities, emotions, sentiments, empathy, and even tempers and moods. Social misunderstanding, not to mention stereotyping, mystification, and discrimination, often stems from a neglect of the surprising and enlivening texture of minorities’ emotional world. This study attempts to explore the “private sphere” of minority cultures through an in-depth firsthand account of their affective energies and expressions. Taking the important cue of the “affective turn” in cultural theory over the past 15 years or so, this study asks: in light of the present and future need of social recognition of ethnic minorities in HK, what are the representations of affective/emotional energies and intensities surrounding the ethnic figures/strangers in HK films (e.g. passivity, shame, anger, joy, charm, belonging, etc.), how do ethnic minorities respond to these visual narratives, and how can their self-representation through visual discourse reveal and transform their lived experience? Using multiple qualitative research methods, we shall (1) produce a critical annotated inventory of the representations of race, ethnicity, and affect/emotion in HK cinema since 1970s; (2) conduct a series of focus group interviews of select ethnic minorities living in HK, to explore their reception of a “landscape of ethnic emotions” through film screening and discussion; (3) study the visual self-portraiture of ethnic affects and attachments (via short videos and photography) produced by a group of carefully chosen ethnic minority persons; and (4) explore the interaction between scholars and HK’s ethnic minority groups by holding, and collecting data from, a two-day international symposium of presentations, screening, and dialogue. The research results will provide intellectual bearings for understanding ethnic minorities’ feelings and need of social recognition, expression, and freedom, and ultimately will have policy implications for reconsidering resource allocation in various social services as part of the government’s leadership for creatively enhancing the city’s multicultural life and harmony. 近年，在港的南亞裔和其他少數族裔人士開始受到了社會的注意，尤其在２００８年有關《種族歧視條例》制度過程的公眾辯論期間與其以後。然而，有關香港少數族裔的學術研究仍然長期落後。在社區中，同化與認同的角力（如在教育、就業、社會適應、文化傳承）依然持續，產生日益嚴重的社會緊張，並且影響社會和諧。迄今，少數族裔的自我主體意識仍然沒有受到多大的重視，當中所涉及的，包括她們的生活經驗、感性、情緒、感傷、移情，甚至脾氣與心情的形成與自我認知。社會對於少數族裔的誤解 (如定型化、神秘化和歧視)，往往源於大眾忽視少數族裔那予以驚喜的情感世界。本研究嘗試透過有關少數族裔情感流動與表現，探究少數族裔文化的「私人空間」。受到文化研究過去約十五年「情感轉向」理論 (affect theory) 的啟發，本研究提出了以下的問題：鑑於對少數族裔社會認同的需要，少數族裔情感的量度與強度（包括無力感、羞愧、憤怒、歡樂、魅力、歸屬感等）是怎樣再現於香港電影的若干民族角色呢？少數民族如何回應這般視覺敘述呢？這些自我再現又是如何透過視覺論述，揭示與改變少數族裔的生活經驗呢？透過多重質性研究，我們將會（１）整合一份從７０年代至今，有關種族、民族與情感／情緒的香港電影目錄，並附註說明；（２）透過電影放映與討論，跟若干生活在香港的少數族裔人士，進行一系列的小組訪問研究，以探索她們「少數族裔的情感面貌」；（３）研究由一班精心挑選的少數族裔人士所提供，有關她們民族情感與依附的自我寫照（通過短片與相片）；（４）透過舉辦為期兩天的國際研討會，以及觀察與記錄會上的報告、電影放映、對話的過程，研究當中學者與少數族裔之間的互動。本研究的成果將成為了解少數族裔對情感、社會認同、自我表現與自由等需要的學術基礎，並最終有助於有關社會服務與資源重新分配的政策考慮，以符合政府所提倡提高本港多元文化生活與和諧的創意性。

340411.label: Realisation of objectives
340411.value: This study explores ethnic minority cultures in Hong Kong through an in-depth firsthand account of their affective energies and emotional expressions. The significance of studying affect/emotion is that it offers a new and innovative template with which to trace the contours and texture of identity and difference in relation to power. Our project was the first empirical investigation in HK that directly addressed the affective/emotional as a condition of possibility for recognizing ethnic minorities as a particular kind of “cultural citizens” of HK. We focused on three target groups of ethnic minority persons residing in HK, namely Indians, Filipinos, and Nepalese. They represent some of the largest minority groups in HK, according to the government’s Race Relations Unit. Throughout the literature research about the ethnic minorities’ visual images in HK movies and film reception studies, we realized the paucity of cultural research on their images, creative energies, and access to local media industries. This study therefore filled an important gap. For revised objective 1, we spent six months working at the Hong Kong Film Archive to select and screen over five hundred Hong Kong films (criteria-based sample; period: 1970s-2010s). This process helped us to uncover the roles and characterizations of ethnic figures and narrative settings that mark – and help to shape – the filmic landscape of Hong Kong cinema. This, we believe, would contribute to a broader understanding of the cross-cultural and international nature of HK films, raising new questions about “local identity” and artistic values. As a result, we completed objective 1 by producing the first ever FILMOGRAPHY that contains 187 feature films marked by substantial representation of non-Chinese ethnic characters. Each entry provides details of each leading, supporting, or minor/background ethnic characters, and places these in the overall narrative synopsis of the film. The filmography has been refereed and will be published in Chinese, entitled 若隱若現：香港電影的非華人形象（1970至2010 年代）by Cinezen Publishing. It is expected that this book will be in print around August 2016 (Contract signed in September 2015). In it, the 187 entries are accompanied by critical discussions of the changing patterns of ethnic representations across four decades over a variety of genres. This useful reference will be of interest to film lovers of Hong Kong cinema, as well as academic researchers and students in film studies, ethnic studies, communication, and cultural studies. For revised objective 2, which was a film reception study, a total of thirty-nine south Asians subjects (in six groups) were invited to join the film screening and focus group discussion that took place over two months. The participating ethnic groups included Indians, Pakistanis, and Nepalese in age groups ranging from 15 to 53. (We also included a few Filipino subjects, as they had heard about our project and were keen to participate in the study). This film reception study enabled us to collect valuable firsthand experiences of EMs’ emotional responses to the film clips we had assembled showing EM presence on the silverscreen. A thorough analysis about their perspectives and responses to the images of ethnic minorities was conducted. As a result, we successfully completed objective 2 through publishing a research article entitled “South Asian minorities and the mainstream media,” which was included in the book UNDERSTANDING SOUTH ASAIN MINORITIES IN HONG KONG, published by HKUP in 2014 (the Chinese edition will also be published in 2016). Moreover, throughout the continuous literature search on reception studies, we discovered that some similar projects were being pursued by others, proving that the topic was gaining increasing research value. Those projects included, for example, “The Whispering from the South” organized by Lumenvisum and Christian Action; “All About Us” organized by ifva (of the Hong Kong Arts Centre); and "Do you read me," a photo exhibition organized by Oxfam. For revised objective 3, we undertook to work with ifva (Incubator for Film & Visual Media in Asia) as a research partner in “All About Us” (a video creativity camp for EM youth) in 2013/14 and 2014/15. This collaboration has helped us to disseminate or transfer our knowledge to the community, especially through ifva which is a well-known visual art incubation project of the Hong Kong Arts Centre, aiming at developing young film and videomakers in Hong Kong. The said collaboration has led to the production of a 30-minute DOCUMENTARY FILM, which included some of our research findings as well as critical self-reflection on the relationship between affect/emotion and visual expression among EMs. In addition, to consolidate all the data we have collected, and in continuation with our attempt to engage in knowledge transfer to the community, an ONLINE BLOG entitled https://ethnicityhk.com was established by our research team that is a digital output of the project. The blog features major findings of this project, including the videos made by EMs, reports and reviews on their cultural events, and many featured articles written by our team as well as invited EMs and other cultural critics. For revised objective 4, as a finale of this multi-year project with the explicit aim to bring this research to academic discussion, we conducted a THREE-DAY SYMPOSIUM in October 2014 featuring local and non-local scholars and community stakeholders, as well as EM participants and filmmakers. Besides scholars giving academic papers, there was a day of video screening and community engagement, where media industry representatives, art groups, EM NGOs, and a good number of EM youth exchanged views and engaged in dialogues on minority affect and visual expressions. As a result, we completed objective 4 successfully by producing an edited book, entitled VISUALITY, EMOTIONS, AND MINORITY CULTURE: FEELING ETHNIC (edited by the PI), which is forthcoming in late 2016 by Springer (Contract signed in November 2014). This book will be part of a new series called Humanities in Asia published by Springer. In conclusion, we are pleased to report that we successfully completed the goals we set forth, with printed, visual, and online deliverables, for impact in the academic circles in humanities and cultural studies as well as impact in the community. Empirical work on affect is relatively rare compared to the volumes of theoretical writings on it. In view of this, we have been particularly focused on engaging in this area empirically. Throughout, we hope our research can open up a new cultural approach to studying the emotional worlds of EMs, realizing how affect theories offer a hopeful alternative to social determinism and structural prohibition, by positioning the minority individual as possessing a degree of control over their future, rather than as passive recipient of cognitive or learned phenomena.

340411.label: Major findings and research outcome
340411.value: There are three main areas of research findings in this project. First, the images and character of non-Chinese roles in Hong Kong films continue to be limited in terms of visibility, variety, and narrative significance. For instance, of the 1,725 non-Chinese characters we studied in the filmography project, 78.4% was of minor roles while there was only 6.8% or less than 100 characters playing the lead over the forty-year span. Many ethnic roles appeared as members of a group of gangster, triad members in an action film, policemen in a police film, soldiers in a historical movie, or competitors in a comedy film. This kind of visibility-qua-stereotyping, we argue, stems from a “veiled racialization” whereby ethnic characters are visibly racialized but hidden or distorted at the same time. Second, in our reception study, the major findings chiefly center on the role of watching family dramas have on the expression of emotions among EM viewers. Besides using the internet and broadcast television for consumption of news, many informants concur on the importance of watching family dramas together at home. Despite their ethnic difference, the Indian, Pakistani and Nepalese converge on their tastes for Indian dramas, as most of them understand Hindi. The popularity of Bollywood cinema also added to the prowess of Indian dramas, or essentially, the supremacy of things “Indian” in general. Complaining about the dramas being very formulaic, they nonetheless rationalized them as the only way to keep the dramas going. Emotional resonance is ever-present in the depiction of family crises. Our subjects’ discussion of their frustration over the lack of South Asian images on mainstream TV also brought them to a digression on the only “successful” Indian TV and film actor in Hong Kong’s media history. They were referring to Mr. “Q BoBo” – the actor’s screen name. Third, by locating similar projects in the community, a network and collaboration with different organizations/institutions which are keen to help ethnic minorities was developed. The collaboration with ifva of Hong Kong Arts Centre for two years in organizing "All About Us," a video creative project, enabled us not only to reach out to the EM community (video-making project centered on emotional explorations) but also helped us to derive an understanding of the various aspirations, emotional investments, and obstacles they encountered when trying to enter the media industry.

340411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
340411.value: This study opens up a research domain rarely attempted in HK, by investigating EMs’ visual images and visual expressions as a means to explore their emotional worlds. Much more research is needed. The filmography, scholarly book, and documentary film we produced, as well as the network we have developed with the EM communities, help lay the groundwork. Further development should center on creative expression and the yearning for access to media (as viewers and as members of the media industry). “Cultural participation” thus becomes an important concept to anchor future related projects. The PI has begun to map out the next phase of research around questions of CULTURAL RIGHTS, i.e. recognition of cultural citizenship by participation. Questions of affect/emotion and cultural citizenship could be explored together. Several sequential projects can be developed, including a mapping of the cultural resources and infrastructures available in HK for developing EMs’ cultural interests, followed by a qualitative study of their views of what constitutes meaningful cultural access/participation, then followed by a larger-scale project of EM visual creativity, dialogue, and analysis. It is hoped that this present completed project can set a new research agenda for media and cultural studies of ethnicity in HK.

340411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
340411.value: This study opens up a research domain rarely attempted in HK, by investigating ethnic minorities’ visual images and expressions as a means to probe their emotional worlds. Scholarly research on ethnic minorities in HK remains chronically underdeveloped, even as the struggle for assimilation and recognition among these communities (e.g. in education, employment, social adaptation, cultural survival) continues to generate debates in discrimination and threaten social harmony. In this project, we paid attention to the minorities’ own sense of subjecthood, such as their construction and articulation of self-understanding formed through lived experiences, sensibilities, emotions, sentiments, empathy, and even tempers and moods. Social misunderstanding, not to mention stereotyping, mystification, and discrimination, often stems from a neglect of the surprising and enlivening texture of minorities’ emotional world. This study helps us to understand the “private sphere” of minority cultures through an in-depth firsthand account of their affective energies and expressions. The research results should be able to provide intellectual bearings for understanding ethnic minorities’ feelings and need of social recognition, expression, and freedom, and should have policy implications for reconsidering resource allocation in various social services as part of the government’s leadership for creatively enhancing the city’s multicultural life and harmony.

340411.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
340411.value: We have collaborated with IFVA (Incubator of Film & Visual media in Asia) of the Hong Kong Arts Centre for a video creative project called “All About Us” in 2013/14 & 2014/15. The chief goal of “All About Us” is to let teenagers of ethnic minorities express their creativity as well as discuss and comprehend issues about racial harmony through gaining knowledge in creative media. One of the project’s results is a documentary film made as a self-reflection process for the organizers and important data for the study on ethnic minorities’ affect and feelings in Hong Kong. The documentary was screened in an international symposium in October 2014, and has been shown in film screenings organized by IFVA in 2014/15. More importantly, the project “All About Us” has won The Hong Kong Arts Development Awards presented by The Hong Kong Arts Development Council (ADC) in 2013. Moreover, we have collaborated with HKSKH Lady MacLehose Centre Services for Ethnic Minorities in a project called “Living Together: Study on Ethnic Integration among Chinese Locals and South Asians in Kwai Tsing District” by recruiting university students to take part in this project. It helped to train the students in exploring the in-depth stories or firsthand account of lived experience, feelings, and histories of ethnic minorities in Hong Kong.

341111.label: Project Title(Chinese)
341111.value: 現代身體、現代國家：二十世紀中國游泳文化史

341111.label: Project Objectives
341111.value: The project aims to address the following questions: How the modern state promoted and regulated swimming as a means to remake people’s bodies, and the ensuing process of control, confrontation, and negotiation between the state and the individual’s body. This leads to the question of the contested nature of beaches and swimming pools as a space for public leisure, a space of modernity, and a space of social control. How swimming as a modern sport developed and adapted to the social and political needs of China in the age of nationalism, anti-imperialism and revolution, and contributed to changes in the body culture of modern China. The interplay between swimming, the construction of the female body, and the remaking of gender relations in modern China. This leads to the question of the changes in the style of swimsuits and the changing social attitudes towards “nakedness” of the body in Chinese society. The significance of the bodily dimension in understanding major political mobilization campaigns in twentieth century China, namely, the New Life Movement in Republican China and the Cultural Revolution in Communist China. This requires visual analysis of the propanganda materials used in the political campaigns (please refer to 2(c) for examples) Why and how the colonists in Hong Kong, including the British community and the colonial government, popularized swimming among the local Chinese, which consequently empowered the body of the latter and helped undermine the racial barriers between the colonists and the colonized.

The significance of the bodily dimension in understanding major political mobilization campaigns in twentieth century China, namely, the New Life Movement in Republican China and the Cultural Revolution in Communist China. This requires visual analysis of the propanganda materials used in the political campaigns (please refer to 2(c) for examples)

Why and how the colonists in Hong Kong, including the British community and the colonial government, popularized swimming among the local Chinese, which consequently empowered the body of the latter and helped undermine the racial barriers between the colonists and the colonized.

341111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
341111.value: In 1956 and 1966 when his vision of socialist revolution was challenged by other party leaders, the aging Mao Zedong swam across the Yangzi River to show his physical vigor and to rally the masses in support of his revolutionary cause. Mao’s swimming demonstrations contributed to the emergence of a national swimming craze, and turned swimming into a political ritual. In fact, swimming in the earlier Republican China had already served a national function, though in a different form. During the New Life Movement in 1935, Chiang-Kai-shek invited Yang Xiuqiong, a swimming beauty from British Hong Kong, to give demonstrations of swimming skills in Nanchang, Jiangxi. These two examples show the importance of swimming in both politics and the construction of the body culture in modern China. In Nationalist China, a young female modern body was used as a showcase of national vigour. In contrast, in Communist China, Mao promoted his revolutionary agenda with his own body. The substitution of Yang’s body with Mao’s as China’s icon of swimming also shows the repression of female sexuality under the PRC. The body can therefore be seen as one of the most visible embodiments of the values and beliefs of the time. This project explores the relationship between the modern body and the modern state through the lens of swimming, a sport that can best show the malleable and contested nature of the body. Modern regimes in twentieth century China attempted to remake people’s bodies as a means to remake politics and society, and swimming served as one of the tools in this process. However, swimming was as much a challenge as a tool to the political authorities in their reforming mission. Male and female bathers swimming together in revealing swimsuits posed a threat to the existing gender relationships and raised discussions about norms of public behavior, proper bathing dress codes, and sex segregation in swimming places. The history of swimming therefore provides a useful lens to examine gender relations, the multi-faceted and contentious nature of modernity, social control, and public presentation of the body in modern China. State power was neither a monolithic entity nor the only agent of socio-cultural change. Hence, the political authorities’ promotion and regulation of swimming was filled with tensions and ambiguities. This project will shed light on the complex process of control, confrontation and negotiation that took place between the state and the individual’s body. 在1956年及1966年，毛澤東游泳橫渡長江，當時正值其革命理念及政治權威被其他黨領袖所挑戰。毛澤東通過渡江的壯舉，告訴群眾他雖然已日漸年邁，但仍然十分健壯，他同時希望藉此動員群眾支持他的革命理念。結果，全國上下紛紛效法毛澤東，為革命而游泳。游泳不再單純是一種有益身心的運動，而成為一種充滿政治意涵的儀式和符號。但事實上，早在民國時期，游泳已被賦予了為國家政權服務的功能。在1935年，當時正值新生活運動，蔣介石邀請了人稱「美人魚」的香港女泳手楊秀瓊到江西南昌作泳術表演。以上兩個例子反映了游泳在現代中國的政治及身體文化的建構的重要性。在民國時期，國民黨通過一年輕女性的身體來展示國家的力量。到了「新中國」時期，毛澤東卻選擇以自己的身體來宣揚他的革命理念。這種身體文化的轉變可視為1949年後中國共產政權對女性性徵的壓抑。 身體因而可以說是其身處時代的價值觀及信念的載體。此研究計劃通過游泳去探討現代國家與現代身體之間的關係。運動當然離不開身體，而眾多運動中，游泳可說最能夠表達身體如何被不斷模塑及被各種力量所爭奪。二十世紀中國相繼出現的現代政權，均嘗試通過模塑民眾的身體，以改造政治及改造社會，而游泳成為此過程中的其中一項工具。然而吊詭的是，對統治者來說，游泳既是一種工具，也是一項難題。在公眾場所穿上游泳衣、混在一起的男女，挑戰了既有的兩性關係與界線，亦因而引發了男女應否被允許在同一泳池游泳的爭論。游泳的歷史因而為我們提供了一個很好的切入點，去了解現代中國一連串的重要課題，包括兩性關係、現代性的爭議性和多面向性，社會對個人的規訓，以及身體在公共空間的展示等。 國家政權既不是鐵板一塊，也並非社會及文化改變的唯一動力。因而，政府官員對游泳的鼓吹及規管，便無可避免地充滿了矛盾衝突及模糊含混的地方。此研究將會展示國家政權與民眾身體之間的監控、反抗與協商的複雜過程。

341111.label: Major findings and research outcome
341111.value: This research explores the interplay between the body, modernity, and the nation in modern China through swimming. It analyzes the process through which swimming, a modern sport and leisure activity that originated in the West, turned the “bodyscape” and the seascape into sites of contestation. Modern discourses of health, leisure, and nationalism helped legitimize and popularize swimming among the Chinese, both the elites and ordinary folks alike. Modern transportation linked the city to coastal areas, and enabled the Westerners and later the Chinese local governments to refashion the seascape into popular seaside resorts, such as Qingdao, Beidaihe, Shanghai's Gaoqiao, and Hong Kong's Repulse Bay. Used to be seen as a space of uncivilized wilderness, the seaside now became the most sought-after site that different interest groups scrambled for ownership or management rights. The most notable example is Beidaihe, where a group of Chinese elites, by adopting the rhetoric of nationalism and public interest, successfully took over the beach of the Germans when Germany was busy fighting the First World War in Europe. The symbolic meanings of swimming were never fixed and stable. Swimming was seen as both a modern, healthy sport and an erotic activity in Republican China. Swimming created a modern, tantalizing female body that was difficult to "tame". Debates over whether mixed bathing (i.e. both sexes swim together) should be allowed reached the climax in 1934, reflecting public (and mainly male's) anxiety about the increasing freedom that women enjoyed as well as women's exposure of their bodies in the public. In this year, the Guangdong provincial government banned mixed bathing, and the central government in Nanjing forbade the women from exposing their legs in public. These regulations were results of the tensions arising from growing modernity on one side, and the Kuomintang’s conservative turn (or Fascist turn, as some scholars argued) on the other. After the communists came to power in 1949, swimming paradoxically meant a mass political ritual to show one’s bodily conformity and a form of defiance to Maoism. When Mao Zedong propagated mass swimming for the communist revolution, his people employed the very same technique to swim in droves to the capitalist world (mainly Hong Kong and Macau) for their own freedom. Hence, in 20th century China, swimming was much more than a sport; it became an arena where the authorities and ordinary people contested for control over the body of the individual.

341111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
341111.value: The long-term goal of this research project is a book-length study in English, and the working title is Body, Leisure, and Politics: Swimming and Sea-bathing in 20th Century China. It will consists of five chapters, and the tentative titles are as follows: Chapter 1: Swimming, Colonialism, and Modernity Chapter 2: Swimming and Nationalism: From Hong Kong's Cross Harbor Swim to the Olympics Chapter 3: Swimsuits, Public Morality, and the Making of the Modern Body Chapter 4: Creating Seaside Resorts: Sea-bathing and Spatial Politics Chapter 5: Swimming for the Revolution: Mao Zedong’s Yangtze Swims and the National Swimming Craze

341811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
341811.value: With the advance in Internet development, more and more adolescents actively participate in gambling and an identifiable proportion of them develop problem gambling, which is associated with financial strains, interpersonal conflicts, physical complaints, psychological distress, as well as suicidal ideation/attempt. Despite the constantly high prevalence rates of gambling among Chinese communities, adolescent gambling research in the Chinese context is still in the infancy stage. More empirical investigations are called for in order to better understand the risk and protective factors of problem gambling as well as to devise effective prevention strategies to reduce the harm of gambling among Chinese adolescents. Based on previous findings in both Western and Chinese gambling research, three psychological risk factors (impulsive personality trait, negative affects, and cognitive biases) of problem gambling are identified in this proposed study. All three factors are hypothesized to positively contribute to higher gambling involvement and more problem gambling symptoms among Chinese adolescents. The impact of these factors and their interactions on gambling involvement (particularly on the Internet) and gambling problems will be examined. A better theoretical understanding of gambling behaviors and problems among Chinese adolescents can result. In order to provide practical recommendations of responsible gambling strategies in Chinese communities, the proposed study will also test the effectiveness of two distinct types of computerized educational messages which are designed for intervening with poor impulse control, negative affects, as well as irrational cognitive beliefs of adolescent gamblers. The effectiveness of these messages will be evaluated in terms of behavioral task performance as well as self-reported cognitive biases immediately after the presentation of educational messages. A three-month follow-up assessment is also proposed to evaluate the continuous impacts of the messages. It is hypothesized that those receiving the educational messages will evidence a greater level of rational beliefs and a better decision making in a gambling task than those in the control. They are also expected to be less likely to engage in gambling activity even when they are invited. Moreover, in the three-month follow-up, they are expected to report a decrease in actual gambling involvement and gambling problems. The findings can provide practical suggestions on whether, and which type of, educational messages is effective in reducing the harm of gambling, particularly on the Internet, to our next generation. 341911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
341911.value: In today’s global economy, few issues have attracted more media attention than China’s renminbi revaluation. What is the role of the renminbi exchange rate in the spectacular growth of Chinese exports? How much did the renminbi appreciation against the dollar after 2005 help reduce China’s trade surplus? Will renminbi appreciation hurt China’s export sector? Instead of answering these questions using the standard macroeconomic approach, we take a micro approach and investigate Chinese firms’ export behavior in response to exchange rate movements. In particular, we provide micro-level evidence at the monthly frequency on China’s exporting firms’ decisions on export supply, pricing, product and country choices, as well as entry and exit across export markets and industries. We make use of a monthly firm transaction level dataset from China Customs that covers the universe of Chinese exporters and importers between 2000 and 2006. The dataset reports export (import) value, price and quantity of about 7,000 products for over 200,000 firms each year. This dataset is supplemented by an above-scale firm dataset from China National Bureau of Statistics. An accounting identity implies that a country’s total exports can grow on two margins: the extensive margin through increases in the number of exporters, products or destination countries, and the intensive margin through growth in export volume of existing exporters. In this project, we will study firm responses to exchange rate movements through these two margins. The project consists of three parts (see figure 1). First, we estimate a probit model to study the effects of exchange rate movements on firms’ decision to enter or exit an export market, including adding or dropping a product or a destination country. Second, we examine how continuing exporters’ export volume changes in response to exchange rate fluctuations. Third, we further decompose the firms’ responses on the intensive margin into changes in export prices and quantities. Firm heterogeneity, such as differences in productivity, will be explored in our analysis on both margins. The decomposition of the relation between exchange rate movements and China’s aggregate trade flows into different margins can deepen our understanding of the micro mechanism of trade adjustments to exchange rate shocks. Contributing to policy discussions, our results will offer quantitative benchmarks to gauge the impact of a renminbi revaluation on China’s aggregate exports in the future. 在當今全球經濟中，人民幣升值問題引起了媒體的廣泛關注。人民幣匯率在中國出口奇跡中扮演了什麽角色？2005之後的人民幣升值是否減少了中國的貿易順差？人民幣升值是否會損害了中國的出口企業？現有文獻普遍採用宏觀經濟方法來回答這些問題。本項研究將採取微觀經濟方法研究匯率變動如何影響中國企業的出口行為。我們提供匯率變動的微觀實證研究結果，關係到中國的出口企業如何調整出口供應、定價、產品、出口市場、以及進入和退出出口市場的決定等。 我們的主要數據是來自從中國海關的企業月度進出口數據庫。這個數據庫涵蓋了2000年到2006年間中國所有的出口企業和進口企業。 數據內容包括了每年超過20萬家企業約 7000多種產品的出口（進口）總額、價格和數量。本研究的其他數據還包括來自中國國家統計局的規模以上工業企業數據庫。 一個國家的出口增長可以分解為兩個維度：一是擴展邊際，即增加新的出口企業、產品或出口國家；二是集約邊際，即來自現有出口企業、產品和出口國家的出口增長。我們將對這兩個維度分開來研究。具體而言，本項目可以分成三個部分：（1）我們通過probit模型來估計匯率變動如何影響企業進入或退出某個產品或市場的決策。（2）匯率變動如何影響現有企業出口總額的變動。（3）我們進一步把集約邊際分解為價格和數量的變動。在研究上述兩個維度的同時，我們也會考慮企業生產率等方面的差異性。將出口增長分解為擴展邊際和集約邊際，可以幫助我們更好地理解匯率對出口影響的微觀機制。本項研究也具有了重大的政策含義。利用我們估計的結果可以對未來人民幣匯率變動如何影響出口進行量化分析。

400311.label: Project Title(Chinese)
400311.value: 高分子聚合物對湍流狀態的瑞利-貝納爾對流中熱傳送量的影響

400311.label: Project Objectives
400311.value: Study the effect of polymer additives on heat transport in homogeneous turbulent thermal convection in two dimensions using the shell model. We shall further explore the possible enhancement of heat transport and, in particular, the possible new interesting feature of the polymers changing the scaling behavior of the system. Study the effect of polymer additives on heat transport in laminar boundary layer flow for forced convection using a FENE-P model. We shall particularly explore the possible new interesting feature of the saturation of the effect of polymers at high concentrations. Study the effect of polymer additives on heat transport in laminar boundary layer flow for natural convection using Oldroyd-B model. 400311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
400311.value: More than 60 years ago, it was discovered that the addition of polymer additives in turbulent fluid flows can reduce the frictional drag significantly. This intriguing drag reducing effect of polymer additives has been put into practical use, for example, to reduce the energy needed in transporting oil in the Trans Alaska Pipeline System. Extensive research has been carried out on this problem. Drag reduction is an enhancement in mass transport. In turbulent thermal convective flows, together with mass, heat is also transported. It is thus interesting to study and understand whether polymer additives can influence heat transport. While there is extensive research on the drag reducing effect of polymer additives, little is studied and known about the effect of polymer additives on heat transport. We propose to study such effects in this project. Experimentally, turbulent thermal convection is often investigated in a container of fluid heated from below and cooled on top. Such a set-up is known as the Rayleigh-Bénard (RB) convection. Turbulent RB convection is highly inhomogeneous, consisting of a central bulk region and boundary layers near the walls of the container. Heat transport is related to the kinetic and thermal dissipation rates, which are made up of contributions from the bulk as well as from the boundary layers. In this project, we propose to study the effect of polymer additives on heat transport in turbulent RB convection. We shall consider homogeneous turbulent thermal convection without boundaries to study the case when heat transport is dominated by dissipations in the bulk as well as boundary layer flows to study the case when heat transport is dominated by dissipations in the boundary layers. 超過六十年前，科學家發現把高分子聚合物加進湍流流動中可大大減低流動的阻力。高分子聚合物此一引人入勝的湍流減阻特性己經被成功應用，其中一個例子便是用於縱貫阿拉斯加原油管道中。科學家亦進行了大量有關高分子聚合物湍流減阻作用的研究。流動中減阻相等於增加流體的傳送量。在湍流對流運動中，除了流體的傳送，還有熱的傳送。因此高分子聚合物如何影響熱傳送量是另一個有趣而值得探究的研究課題。相對於湍流減阻這一特性，科學家對高分子聚合物如何影響熱傳送量所知甚少。我們將在這一研究計劃中探究此一問題。 科學家經常把載有流體的密封容器加熱以進行湍流對流運動的實驗研究。這種流動便是瑞利-貝納爾對流。在湍流狀態的瑞利-貝納爾對流是不均勻的，主要由容器中心的流動和容器壁附近的邊界層流動組成。容器中心的流動近似於均勻湍流對流運動。在這一研究計劃裏，我們將會分別研究高分子聚合物對均勻湍流對流運動和邊界層流動中熱傳送量的影響。

400311.label: Realisation of objectives
400311.value: Objective 1 is completely realized. We have found that polymers extract energy from the flow and, as a result, destroy the thermal balance between power injected by buoyancy and the energy transfer rate. This leads to a change in the scaling behavior of the velocity and temperature fluctuations for scales below the modified Bolgiano scale. Hence, in the presence of polymers, we are able to observe the coexistence of both the Bolgiano-Obukhov and Kolomorogov-Obukhov-Corrsin scaling and the crossover from one scaling behavior to the other. Moreover, our theoretical analysis predicts that heat transport is not much altered in two dimensions and this result is confirmed in our numerical study. Objective 2 is completely realized. We have generalized the classical Prandtl-Blasius-Pohlhausen boundary layer analysis to study boundary layer flow with polymers described by the FENE-P model. In the FENE-P model, the finite extensibility of the polymers is measured by the ratio of the maximum to the equilibrium values of the trace of the polymer conformation tensor. When this ratio is very large, heat transport is reduced as found in our earlier study using polymers that can be stretched indefinitely without a limit. When this ratio is small, heat transport is enhanced. We have shown that this transition can be explained in terms of the functional form of the space-dependent effective viscosity due to polymer stretching. Regarding objective 3, we aim to explore how the presence of buoyancy might alter the effect of polymers on heat transport. We have found that the same objective can be achieved by studying the simpler problem of polymers in laminar boundary layer flow along a vertical plate. In this simpler problem, there is both forced convection as well as natural convection driven by buoyancy and their relative contribution is measured by an additional parameter. We have found that buoyancy enhances heat transport with and without polymers. When the relative contribution of forced and natural convection is held fixed, the effects of polymers on heat transport are qualitatively the same as those in the case when there is no buoyancy. We have studied a problem simpler than the one originally proposed but the original objective of exploring the effect of buoyancy has been fully realized.

400311.label: Major findings and research outcome
400311.value: We have studied two-dimensional homogeneous turbulent convection with polymers using a shell model and shown that polymers can change the scaling behavior by destroying the thermal balance in Bolgiano-Obukhov scaling. Thus in the presence of polymers, both the Bolgiano-Obukhov and Kolmogorov-Obukhov-Corrsin scaling can coexist and there is a transition from one to the other. In two dimensions, heat transport is not altered much by polymers as predicted by our theoretical analysis. This work led to publication 1. We have generalized the classical Prandtl-Blasius-Polhausen (PBP) boundary layer theory to study the effect of finitely-extensible polymers on heat transport. The finite extensibility of polymers is measured by the ratio of maximum to equilibrium values of the trace of the conformation tensor. When this ratio is very large, heat transport is reduced and when this ratio is small, heat transport is enhanced. We have shown that this transition can be explained in terms of the functional shape of the space-dependent effective viscosity due to polymer stretching. When polymer stretching is mostly within the thermal boundary layer, heat transport is reduced. When the region of polymer-stretching extends outside the thermal boundary layer, heat transport is enhanced. This work has been submitted for publication. We have carried out direct numerical simulations of turbulent Rayleigh-Benard (RB) convection with polymers of varying relaxation time. For small Weissenberg number (Wi), which is the ratio of the polymer relaxation time to the typical time scale of the flow, heat transport is reduced but for sufficiently large Wi, heat transport is enhanced. For small Wi, the stretching of polymers is confined to a region close to the top and bottom boundaries and when Wi is increased, the region of polymer-stretching extends into the central bulk region of the flow. By carrying out the classical PBP analysis using the effective viscosity profile evaluated from the numerical data, we have provided a theoretical explanation of the observed transition of heat reduction to heat enhancement when Wi is increased. This work has been submitted for publication. The classical PBP theory was developed for steady-state boundary layer flow. To account for the fluctuations in boundary layers in turbulent RB convection, we have used the idea of eddy thermal diffusivity and derived a new thermal boundary layer equation. Using this equation, we have obtained analytical mean temperature profiles that are in excellent agreement with numerical results. This work led to publication 2.

400311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
400311.value: There are various issues worthwhile for future research. 1. We have explained the transition from heat reduction to heat enhancement as Weissenberg number increases in turbulent Rayleigh-Benard (RB) convection at moderate Rayleigh numbers using the classical Prandtl-Blasius-Pohlhausen boundary-layer theory with the effective viscosity profile evaluated from the numerical data. It would be interesting to directly confirm our ideas by carrying out direct numerical simulations of turbulent RB convection with such a space-dependent effective viscosity but without the polymer stress tensor. We would pursue this work in the future. 2. We have derived new thermal boundary layer equation and obtained analytical mean temperature profiles in the limits of Prandtl number (Pr) close to 1 and much larger than 1. We are now working to study the other limit of Pr <<1, which is an even more challenging problem.

400311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
400311.value: Adding polymers to turbulent fluid flows can change the flow properties significantly. One well-known effect is the reduction of drag by polymers in turbulent wall-bounded flows, which has been studied extensively and put into practical use to reduce energy, for example, in the transportation of crude oil in the Trans-Alaska Pipeline System. Compared to drag reduction, which is equivalent to mass transport enhancement, the effects of polymers on heat transport in turbulent thermal convection are much less explored. In this project, we have investigated how heat transport in moderately turbulent thermal convection is affected by polymers. We have shown that heat transport is reduced when the polymer stretching is mostly close to the boundaries and heat transport is enhanced when the polymer-stretching region moves outside the thermal boundary layers into the central bulk region. We have explained this transition from heat reduction to heat enhancement in terms of a space-dependent effective viscosity due to the stretching of polymers. Our theoretical results and understanding of how polymers can modify heat transport can lead to useful practical applications.

400411.value: 模擬在非均勻介質的波傳播的高效多尺度方法

400411.label: Project Objectives
400411.value: Our first objective is to construct and analyze a general framework based on a mixed finite element approach for the scalar wave equation with heterogeneous coefficients using coarse-scale formulation. The framework should be able to capture the fine scale behavior on coarse grids. We will use a formulation that provides energy conservation which is a desirable property for wave. Moreover, we will use discontinuous finite element basis functions so that the resulting scheme is explicit, which provides a fast numerical algorithm. Easy-to-construct multiscale basis functions will be ultilized to demonstrate our new framework. Our second objective is to investigate ways to capture subgrid behaviors and how to incorporate these ways to improve our algorithms by representing local features more accurately. The central idea is the construction of multiscale basis functions. These basis functions will capture vital local information and result in a coarse-scale system that can be solved efficiently.

400411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
400411.value: The aim of this project is to develop and analyze a class of multiscale discontinuous Galerkin methods for simulating waves in highly heterogeneous media. Simulation of waves in heterogeneous media is needed in many real applications, such as the simulation of seismic waves in fracture media for geological applications. For realistic scenarios of heterogeneities, direct simulation of waves is impossible even with the superior computing power nowadays. Multiscale methods are thus essential for solving these problems. In general, multiscale methods aim at capturing fine scale features by solving coarse problems, hence reducing computational costs. The major ingredient of multiscale methods is a subgrid capturing mechanism that bridge the fine and coarse variables. However, existing multiscale methods are forced to rely on upscaling procedures to estimate effective properties of the media on a coarse grid, and there is no guarantee that this will provide accurate and reliable results. In the presence of complex heterogeneities and high contrast, the accuracy of upscaling methods deteriorate. For example, some complex fracture networks can form severe non-local effects that can not be approximated via traditional upscaling methods. To capture the effects of these features, more complex subgrid models need to be introduced that can take into account important non-local features. In this project, we will develop a class of multiscale methods for simulating waves in heterogeneous media by the discontinuous Galerkin approach. Moreover, we will provide a rigorous mathematical analysis for the uniform convergence of the new method. We will also perform careful numerical studies for a wide variety of simulations and comparisons for problems arising from realistic applications. The proposed method has several advantages, namely, energy conservation, explicit time stepping and the ability of capturing fine scale on a coarse grid. While there are many multiscale methods in literature, our method seems to be the first one that contains all the above three properties. Preliminary experiments have shown considerable success in applying our method to simulate waves in heterogeneous media. Thus, there are incentives for further development of our approach due to the need of an efficient solver for realistic applications that involve wave simulation in more complex media. The results of the proposed research will significantly advance the state of the art of multiscale methods for wave simulations and provide an efficient tool for solving industrial problems that could not be done via current technologies. 這個項目的目的是開發和分析一類用於模擬波浪在高度異質媒體中傳播的多尺度間斷 Galerkin方法。 模擬在非均勻介質的波傳播，有很多實際的應用，如模擬地震波在裂縫介質的傳播。對於實際情況的非均質性， 即使現在有卓越的計算能力，直接模擬是不可能的。 因此，必須用多尺度方法去解決這些問題。在一般情況下，多尺度方法的目的是通過粗網格去捕捉精細尺度特徵，從而降低計算成本。但是，現有的多尺度方法不得不依靠有效像素提升近似方法，也不能保證，這將提供準確和可靠的結果。在存在複雜的非均質性和高對比度，像素提升方法的準確性下降。例如，一些複雜的骨折網絡可以形成嚴重的非局部效應，無法通過傳統的像素提升近似方法去解決問題。為了捕捉這些非局部效應的影響，需要引入更複雜的子網格模型。 在這個項目中，我們將開發一類用於模擬在非均勻介質波傳播的多尺度間斷 Galerkin方法。此外，我們將提供一個嚴格的數學方法去分析一致收斂。 我們建議的方法有幾個優點，是能量守恆，明確時間步和在粗糙網格捕捉微小效應的能力。現有很多多尺度方法，我們的方法似乎是第一個包含所有上述三個屬性。初步實驗已經表現出我們的方法是相當的成功。因此，有進一步發展我們的方法的需要。

400411.label: Realisation of objectives
400411.value: The first objective is successfully achieved. In particular, we have successfully developed a general framework for the multiscale simulations of the scalar wave equation using a mixed finite element approach. In this approach, the mixed form of the scalar wave equation is considered. The method is constructed based on a coarse mesh, which does not have to resolve the media heterogeneities. Moreover, the framework allows the solution to retain the energy conservation property. Besides the conforming basis, we develop a framework that is based on a discontinuous Galerkin formulation. The formulation uses discontinuous basis functions and gives block diagonal mass matrices. The coupling of the solutions in coarse regions is achieved by using interior penalty. The second objective is also successfully achieved. The main idea is to construct multiscale basis functions, which are locally supported in coarse grid elements. For the mixed formulation, we will construct multiscale basis functions for the velocity, which has continuous normal component across coarse grid edges. To do so, we will solve cell problems on the support of the basis functions, with all boundary conditions or randomized boundary conditions. One can also use oversampling strategy. The above will give the snapshot space, which is a large space can approximate the full solution well. In order to obtain a space reduction, we design a local spectral problem. By solving this problem, one can obtain the dominant modes, which are defined as the first few eigenfunctions and are used as the multiscale basis functions. The dominant modes have the property that the approximation solution can be well represented by the span of these basis functions. Also, the convergence rate is obtained. For the discontinuous Galerkin framework, we also construct suitable snapshot spaces, multiscale basis functions and local spectral problems. We see numerically that these basis functions provide efficient and accurate representation of the solutions.
