400411.label: Major findings and research outcome
400411.value: In this research, we have successfully developed several important methodologies for multiscale wave simulations. First of all, we developed and analyzed multiscale finite element methods for wave propagation in highly heterogeneous media (Papers 1, 4 and 5 in Part C). The method allows one to capture important details of solutions with a small number of degrees of freedom. Moreover, these methods are developed based on some snapshot spaces and some dimensional reduction procedures. The aim is to represent the complicated solutions with only few degrees of freedom per coarse element. Secondly, we have constructed multiscale approaches for the seismic wave simulations (Papers 3, 5, 6 and 7). These are novel methods for geophysical applications, which require sophisticated technique for forward and inverse modeling. Thirdly, we introduce multiscale approaches for wave propagation in fracture media (Paper 9), which appears in common applications. For these applications, one needs a very fine grid if a traditional method is used. By using our method, one can reduce the computational cost significantly. Finally, we have developed some adaptivity ideas for multiscale methods (Papers 2 and 8). The idea allows one to adaptively construct and add basis functions in region with poor solution quality. The idea is based on the computations of local residuals, and use them as error indicators.

400411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
400411.value: There are several possible future developments based on the results of this project. First, it is very important to develop online basis functions waves in order to capture the solution well with small unknowns. Online basis functions can be constructed and used to reduce the error substantially. This is developed for fluid flow, but has not been done for wave propagation. On the other hand, the idea of adaptivity is crucial. One need to add and remove basis functions at suitable locations, so that the computational cost will remain low.

400411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
400411.value: The results of this project give a class of efficient solvers for wave propagation through highly heterogeneous media. With the traditional methods, the number of unknowns is proportional to the heterogeneities. That is, the more complicated the media, the larger number of unknowns. In order to effectively compute the solution with lower computational time and memory, one needs a solver that has fewer degrees of freedom. In this project, we propose a multiscale finite element approach, in which the solution is approximated by some multiscale basis functions. The main idea is that, we will encode some of the multiscale features of the media in the basis functions, and we do not need to use many of these basis functions to capture the solutions. As a result, the method is very efficient and is able to produce very accurate solutions.

400511.label: Project Title(Chinese)
400511.value: 碰撞动力理论中广泛位势下的渐进稳定性

400511.label: Project Objectives
400511.value: Time-decay property of the linearized solution operator for the Boltzmann equation with the self-consistent electromagnetic field both for hard and soft potentials. Stability and rate of convergence of near-equilibrium solutions to the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann system both for hard and soft potentials. To study the above issue when there is an electromagnetic field, that is, for the Vlasov-Maxwell-Boltzmann system, and in the mean time for the Landau-Maxwell system.

400511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
400511.value: The aim of this project is to develop the mathematical theory of dilute gases and plasmas near equilibrium, particularly focusing on the stability and large-time behavior for general collision interactive potentials. The study of collision processes in dilute gases can be viewed as a branch of kinetic theory which is part of the huge field of nonequilibrium statistical physics. The kinetic approach dates back to Bernoulli and Clausius, and was first laid down by Maxwell. A fundamental equation in collisional kinetic theory is the Boltzmann equation, which was derived in 1872 to prove Boltzmann's celebrated theorem about entropy. The Boltzmann equation has proven fruitful not only for a study of the classical gases on the basis of the binary elastic collision but also for studying plasmas transport for the dilute weakly ionized plasmas. An important physical model to describe the dynamics of this kind of plasma is the Vlasov-Maxwell-Boltzmann system, where the plasma responds strongly to the self-consistent electromagnetic field through the Maxwell system. It is mathematically and physically justified to work in a perturbative setting when the particle distribution function is sufficiently close to equilibrium. Extensive theoretical research has been conducted in the area of perturbative Boltzmann equation such as the well-posedness of the Cauchy problem with or without Grad's angular cutoff assumption. However, when the electromagnetic field is present, so far the asymptotic stability of solutions is established only for the hard-sphere model, and it still remains open for general collision potentials, especially including the physically interesting soft potentials. The Landau-Maxwell system is in a similar position when the Boltzmann collision term is replaced by the Landau collision term which is more realistic for the fully ionized plasma. We have been working on the above-mentioned relative field. Recently, we have obtained the optimal large-time behavior of the Vlasov-Maxwell-Boltzmann system for the hard-sphere model. The approach we have developed is also applicable to some other physical contexts such as the relativistic and angular non-cutoff cases. In this project, we will be mainly concentrated on a continuous development for the general potentials, particularly the soft potentials. The challenge of plasma physics comes from the fact that many plasma properties result from the long-range Coulomb interaction. Therefore, the research results of this project should provide valuable insights into the nonlinear stability of plasma equilibrium.

400511.label: Realisation of objectives
400511.value: The original three objectives have been completely achieved. For item 1 we obtained the time-decay properties of the linearised Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann system and Vlasov-Maxwell-Boltzmann system with/without angular cutoff for both hard and soft potentials. This part is indeed an important and fundamental step for studying the corresponding nonlinear problems. The main difficulty is that for instance, for the linearised VMB system with soft potentials, the electromagnetic fields are degenerate in the energy dissipation and the kinetic dissipation of the Boltzmann operator is also degenerate at large velocity. To overcome them we have made full use of the structure of the macroscopic fluid-type equations and developed the time-frequency weighted Fourier energy method to recover the algebraic time-decay rate in the case of the whole space. For item 2 and item 3, we established the small perturbation theory of those two nonlinear systems and even the Landau-Maxwell system around global Maxwellians. The main analytical approach is the energy method. As the direct energy method does not work, we developed the delicate time-velocity weighted energy estimates to treat different kinds of difficulties arising from the structure of nonlinear systems and from the special feature of collision operators. Indeed, we need the enough time-decay of solutions to close the global-in-time a priori estimates, so that the delicate time-weighted energy functionals are designed to be consistent with the linear dissipation structure and also resolve those difficulties in the nonlinear estimates by interpolations of order of differentiation or weight functions.

400511.label: Major findings and research outcome
400511.value: 1. We derived some optimal energy dissipation rate functionals. Due to the coupling structure of systems, the electric/magnetic fields are generally degenerate. We recovered the dissipation structure of all degenerate components both in the Fourier space for the linearised case and in the high-order Sobolev space for the nonlinear case. Such optimal dissipation structure inspires the study of the nonlinear systems. See the paper No 1 in Section 8 of Part C. 2. We found out a time-frequency weighted approach to obtain the time-decay property of the linearized VPB or VMB system in the case of soft potentials. See the papers No 1 and No 5 in Section 8 of Part C. 3. We found out an exponential time-velocity-dependent weight to control the large-velocity growth effect in the nonlinear term. The finding of such weight function is a key point for the completion of the project. See the papers No 4 and No 5 in Section 8 of Part C. 4. We developed the time-weighted nonlinear energy estimate on the Boltzmann equation. Such time-weighed estimates are essentially needed to treat the nonlinear VPB and VMB systems in the non hard-sphere case. Indeed we succeeded in designing some time-weighted energy functionals to describe the nonlinear smooth dynamics of those complex systems under small perturbations. See the papers No 1, No 7, No 8 and No 9 in Section 8 of Part C.

400511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
400511.value: A few related problems motivated by the project could be still interesting to be investigated. First of all, in all obtained results of the project, one of the main assumptions requires that the initial perturbation is sufficiently regular and decays in velocity with a fast enough rate. It is then a problem to develop the perturbation theory in some function space with lower regularity and lower velocity integrability. Second, the dissipation structure of systems found in the project should be useful for understanding the case of the bounded domain. In that situation, the problem is much harder since the solution is generally not smooth enough. Finally, as the perturbation theory around constant steady states has been well studied, it should be more challenging to consider the large-time stability of some nontrivial asymptotic profiles, particularly in the spatially one-dimensional case. We expect to do related research in other projects in the future.

400511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
400511.value: In the project, motivated by series of works by Guo in recent years, we have further developed the mathematical theory of small perturbations in the study of the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann and Vlasov-Maxwell-Boltzmann systems arising from plasma physics, particularly with focus on the stability and large-time behavior of solutions in the case of general collision interaction potentials. The difficulty of the problem is mainly due to the complex structure of the system, in particular, the degenerate dissipation at large velocity for soft potentials, the velocity-growth of the nonlinear term induced by the self-consistent force for non hard-sphere models, and the regularity-loss of the electromagnetic fields. The main significance of the research project is to find out a new time-velocity weighted energy method to overcome those difficulties and treat the nonlinear stability of classical solutions around global Maxwellians for the full range of angular cutoff or non-cutoff intermolecular interactions. We believe that the current project provides a good understanding of energy dissipation structure of those nonlinear systems in plasma around constant states and induces one to further investigate the stability issue on nontrivial time-asymptotic profiles.

400711.label: Project Title(Chinese)
400711.value: 自相似與自仿射分形上的重分形分析及平衡測度

400711.label: Project Objectives
400711.value: It is proposed to conduct the multifractal analysis of overlapping self-similar and typical self-affine measures. The multifractal analysis of a measure concerns with the dimension spectrum of such measures, which is a continuum parameters characterizing the size of the sets where the mass concentration has a given power law singularity. There is a simple and elegant principle proposed by physicists, called multifractal formalism, which relates the multifractal spectrum and the L^q-spectrum (which is more efficient to calculate) as a pair of Legendre transform. However, except some simple cases (e.g. self-similar measures satisfying the open set condition), the multifractal formalism is either unjustified or needs to be adjusted. It is proposed to study the equilibrium measures on self-similar sets and self-affine sets (and their invariant subsets). An equilibrium measure on a fractal set is an invariant measure (with respect to the coding dynamics) on the set attaining the same Hausdorff dimension as the set itself. Such a measure, if it exists, will carry the most important geometric and dynamical information among all the invariant measures on the fractal set. The PI intends to consider dynamical properties (e.g., the existence, uniqueness and mixing and Gibbs properties) of ergodic equilibrium measures on self-similar sets with overlaps and self-affine sets (and their invariant subsets).

400711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
400711.value: 自相似與自仿射分形（集合與測度）是最有興趣及重要的一類分形對象。儘管其生成方式十分簡單， 這類集合與測度具有高度非正則的分析及拓撲結構。在過去的三十多年期間，它們得到許多數學領域（如分析，幾何測度論，動力系統，數論，概率論）的廣泛研究。 在此計劃中，我們將研究自相似與自仿射測度的重分形結構，以及自相似與自仿射集合（或不變集）上平衡測度的動力系統結構。粗略地講，一個測度被稱為重分形如果它具有多於一個標度律。對於這樣的測度， 我們可以把它們的支撐按標度律劃分為互不相交的子集合。重分形的目的之一在於刻畫這些集合的豪斯多夫維數（即維譜）以及它們與測度的整體譜之間的聯繫。對於一個給定分形集，如果它支撐一個滿維數的不變測度， 該測度被稱為分形集上的平衡測度。在分形集上的所有​​不變測度之中，平衡測度（如存在）最能刻畫分形集的幾何及動力系統信息。 在已有文獻中，該研究課題只在某些簡單情形下（例如滿足分離條件的自相似分形，及某類特殊自仿射分形）得到部分研究。我們將側重於研究具有重疊結構的自相似分形，以及更一般​​的自仿射分形。這一研究將加深對分形維數論以及非共形動力系統維數論的理解。

400711.label: Realisation of objectives
400711.value: We initiate the study of multifractal analysis of typical self-affine measures. For the first time, we succeed in obtaining the precise formula for the dimension spectrum of a class of typical sell-affine measures, and we prove that the folklore multifractal formalism holds partially for these family of measures. The main difficulty part of the project comes from the fact that the underlying measures are only self-affine, and not self-similar as in the well-studied case. The classical methods using large deviation arguments or additive thermodynamic formalism in the multifractal analysis no longer work in our models considered in the project. The innovation parts of our approach are the following: we first manage to apply the sub-additive thermodynamic formalism established earlier by the PI and the collaborates to our models to obtain some auxiliary measures (more precisely, equilibrium measures associated with some potentials) which has certain Gibbs properties, and use them to estimate the size of level sets of the typical self-affine measures; then we apply geometric measure theory to further compare the projections of the auxiliary measures and the self-affine measures so that their local behaviours can be estimated simultaneously. The methods we apply here also keep partially valid in studying the multifractal structure (including the L^q spectrum and dimension spectrum) of overlapping self-similar measures. Some of the ideas can be even extended to study the thermodynamics (topological entropies) of subsets in an abstract topological dynamical systems. Overall we have achieved the major parts (75%) of our original objectives. A further understanding of multi fractal analysis for typical affine measures and self-conformal measures with overlaps is still deserved to be investigated.

400711.label: Major findings and research outcome
400711.value: In [1], the PI and the collaborator succeed in verifying the multifractal formalism for typical self-affine measures for certain range of the parameter q. This is the first positive theoretical result about the multifractal structure of typical self-affine measures. One of main difficulties comes from the lack of self-similarity or self-conformity. To overcome this obstacle, we apply the sub-additive thermodynamics to analyse the derivative of the L^q spectrum and to characterise the equilibrium measures, and also use geometric measure theory to compare the projections of auxiliary measures and self-affine measures. In [2], we study the local dimension of measures defined via cones rather than balls. As a most basic concept used in the characterisation of multifractal structures, the classical local dimension of a measure is defined as the point-wise logarithmic decay rate of the measure restricted on balls. It is a natural question to consider how the local dimension will change if we replace balls by cones in the definition. In this article, we show this change is ignorable when the angle in the cone is large enough. The result can apply to a broad class of measures of which the conic distribution can be estimated. In [3], we study the variational principle of topological entropy for subsets. In a general topological dynamical system. We introduce the concepts of measure-theoretical lower and upper entropies for any Borel probability measures. We establish the variational principles which link the Bowen's topological entropy (and packing topological entropy) to these local measure-theoretic entropies for all subsets. This extends the classical variational principle of topological entropy for compact invariant sets. It provides as a basic tool to use measure-theoretical entropies to approximate topological entropies. It might have potential applications in the multifractal analysis of measures and potentials in a abstract topological space rather than in Euclidean spaces. In [4], we study the existence and uniqueness of equilibrium measures supported on a family of self-affine repellers which include, for instance, the limited Rademacher graphs associated with some Pisot parameters. We explore systematically the dynamical structures of these equilibrium measures, as well as the Gibbs properties of these measures and their fibres. Besides some theoretical results (like the uniqueness properties), we give also many concrete examples illustrating the complexity of the corresponding equilibrium measures.

400711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
400711.value: There are several issues on typical self-affine measures which are deserved to be further studied: (1) the L^q spectrum of the measure for the range q>2. (2) the dimension spectrum of more general self-affine measures which are not covered in settings. The equilibrium measures on concrete models of invariant sets on more general affine carpets (like the graph of limited Rademacher functions associated with Salem numbers) is deserved to be further investigated.

400711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
400711.value: Self-similar and self-affine fractals (sets and measures) are among the most interesting and important fractal objects. They can be generated by very simple algorithms using iterated function systems (IFS), but have very complicated geometric structures. These fractals sets and measures have been broadly used in the simulations of complex objects appeared in natural sciences and mathematical fields. In our project, we mainly conduct the multifractal analysis for typical self-affine measures and overlapping self-similar measures. We succeed in determining the sizes (in term of different dimensions) of the level sets consisting of points which have the same scaling law for these measures, and verify partially the heuristic multifractal formalism proposed by physicists last 80's. This is the first positive result regarding of the validity of multifractal formalism of typical affine measures. We also study the local dimensions of measures defined via cones, and variational principle for topological entropies of subsets. These result may provide as useful tools to further study the dimensional properties of sets and measures, as well as the dynamical structure of equilibrium measures lying on fractal sets or in abstract dynamical systems.

401011.value: Formulation of nonlinear optical responses of surfaces/edges of TIs. Systematic theoretical investigation on nonlinear optical effects in realistic TIs, with numerical simulations of materials such as HgTe quantum wells, Bi2Te3, Bi2Se3, and Sb2Te3. The target is to detect the helical liquids on the surfaces and to confirm and discover exotic phenomena in TIs (such as exciton condensation and vortex excitations).

401011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
401011.value: Topological insulators (TIs) are a new state of matters with non-trivial topological structures in energy bands, in which conduction of electrons is forbidden in the bulk by an energy gap but is allowed at surfaces via gapless surface states protected by the time-reversal symmetry. TIs have rapidly become a thematic topic of condensed matter physics in recent five years, owing to their exotic physical effects and potential applications in spintronics and magneto-optics. Research of TIs, for both fundamental knowledge and new technologies, however, is still hindered by limited experimental tools. In particular, notwithstanding enormous applications of nonlinear optical spectroscopy in physics research, nonlinear optics of TIs is still a virgin land. Here we propose a systematic research on nonlinear optical effects of TIs. This project is motivated by the discovery by two of us that pure spin currents have non-trivial linear and nonlinear optical effects. Since the edge states in two-dimensional TIs form pure spin currents, and the surface states in three-dimensional TIs are helical, they should have novel optical effects. We will first formulate the nonlinear optics theory and investigate systematically the dependence of the nonlinear optical susceptibilities on polarizations, frequencies, nonlinearity orders, and the topology of the materials. Design of experiment schemes compatible with the setup in the experimental team will then be in order. We will also investigate nonlinear optical effects of certain exotic states in TIs (such as exciton condensation in biased thin-film TIs). Novel optical devices based on TIs will be designed. The methodology includes symmetry analysis, the standard perturbation theory for nonlinear optics, and numerical simulation based on realistic models. The theoretical research will be carried out in close collaboration with the experimental team. This project will unveil an unexplored aspect of TIs. As long-term impacts, it may open up a new field of nonlinear optics and lead to inventions of novel optical devices. 拓撲絕緣體是一類新型物質，其能帶結構具有非平凡的拓撲性質。在拓撲絕緣體內部電子無法導電，但由於時間反演對稱性保護下無能隙表面態的存在，其表面卻是導電的。由於其具有奇異物理性質以及在自旋電子學和磁光學方面有巨大的潛在應用價值，拓撲絕緣體在過去五年迅速成為凝聚態物理的主題方向。對拓撲絕緣體的研究，無論是在基礎科學還是應用方面，都受到缺乏有效實驗工具的限制。特別是非線性光譜學在拓撲絕緣體方面的研究還是一個處女地，儘管在物理學其他領域光學手段應用極其廣泛。 在此項目我們將開展對圖譜絕緣體非線性光學性質的系統研究。該研究只動機來自本研究組之前對自旋體光學效應的發現。二維拓撲絕緣體的邊緣會形成純自旋流，三維拓撲絕緣體表面態則有螺旋性，因而它們類似自旋流會有新奇的光學性質。在本項目中，我們將首先建立非線性光學的理論框架，進而系統研究光偏振、頻率、非線性階數、以及材料拓撲性質對非線性光學響應的影響。之後我們就會設計實驗驗證理論的方案。我們還會研究拓撲絕緣體中奇異態（如薄膜中的激子凝聚態）的非線性光學特徵。設計基於拓撲絕緣體光學性質的新型器件也是我們的研究目標之一。 本項目將會採用對稱性分析、標準微擾理論、數值模擬等作為主要的研究手段。在研究過程，我們將和實驗家保持密切合作。 我們預計本項目將揭示拓撲絕緣體新的一面。長期而言，本項目或可開創非線性光學新的領域，而且導致新奇光學器件的發明。

401011.label: Realisation of objectives
401011.value: All the objectives have been achieved, with a number of interesting discoveries. Objective 1: We have formulated a general theory on linear and second-order nonlinear optical effects of spin currents. Using both the symmetry analysis and the eight-band microscopic calculation, we studied the optical birefringence effects on the symmetry properties of semiconductors. Moreover, we studied the second-order nonlinear optical processes due to the inversion-symmetry breaking caused by a spin current. These findings facilitate measuring a pure spin current, providing toolbox to explore physics in topological insulators. Objective 2: We considered a particularly interesting nonlinear optical configuration, namely, the interaction between a weak near-infrared (NIR) light and a strong terahertz (THz) field. Our collaboration with experimentalists in UCSB has led to the first observation of high-order THz sideband generation in semiconductors. This study establishes a new platform to study topological properties of insulators using quantum trajectories of electrons. Thus we chose the THz nonlinear optics as the main platform. We systematically studied the effects of Abelian and non-Abelian Berry curvature of insulators in the third-order nonlinear optics. We also studied the global geometric effects. In the extreme nonlinear optics in the THz waveband, we discovered that the Berry curvature would lead a novel Faraday rotation of the weak NIR probe field. The theories apply to a broad range of time-reversal symmetric insulators and semiconductors, including topological insulators. Objective 3: We investigated the geometric effects on THz nonlinear optics in realistic material systems. A new class of materials (transition metal dichalcogenides) has emerged with very interesting optical properties related to the time-reversal symmetry and Berry curvatures of the materials. On the other hand, it is still challenging to prepare topological insulator materials with a bulk gap and with the Fermi surface lying within the gap, which makes the experimental optical studies very difficult. So, for experimental schemes, we have applied the general theories to novel 2D materials including bi-layer graphene and transition-metal dichalcogenides. The schemes are now under pursuits of several experimental groups (including our collaborators in UCSB and University of Washington). We also discovered a topological quantum optics effect, namely, topological superradiance lattices in electromagnetically induced transparency, which can simulate a broad range of topological systems including the famous Haldane model. Several experimental groups (including one in Shanxi University, one in Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, and one in University of Science and Technology of China) are planning on implementation of the scheme we proposed.

401011.label: Major findings and research outcome
401011.value: (1) We have developed a general theory on linear and second-order nonlinear optical effects of spin currents. Using both the symmetry analysis and the eight-band microscopic calculation, we studied the dependence of optical birefringence effects on the symmetry properties of semiconductors (including inversion symmetry and time-reversal symmetry). Moreover, we studied the second-order nonlinear optical processes due to the inversion-symmetry breaking caused by a spin current. These findings facilitate measuring a pure spin current, providing toolbox to explore physics in topological insulators. The results are published in Physical Review B 86, 045215 (2012). (2) In collaboration with experimentalists in UCSB, we observed the high-order THz sideband generation in semiconductors, which demonstrated the effects of quantum trajectories of electron-hole pairs under a strong THz field that drives the electron and hole to move in the momentum and real space with large amplitudes. This study establishes a new platform to study topological properties of insulators using quantum trajectories of electrons. These results were published in Nature 483, 580 (2012). (3) We have established the effects of Berry curvatures on third-order nonlinear optical responses time-reversal symmetric insulators. We studied both the nonlinear optical effects due to local Berry curvatures and the global geometrical effects. Based on the general theory we established, we predicted non-trivial interaction between a near-infrared light and a THz field in insulators with non-trivial Berry curvatures. We applied the theory to novel 2D materials including bi-layer graphene and transition metal dichalcogenides. The results are published in Physical Review B 90, 245205 (2014); New Journal of Physics 15, 115005 (2013); and New Journal of Physics 16, 043014 (2014). (4) We discovered a novel optical effects of quantum fluctuations due to quantum phase transitions, namely, the Faraday echo effect. This finding can be used in experiments to investigate the quantum fluctuations of spins in interacting systems, including topological materials. This result was published in Scientific Reports 4, 4695 (2014). (5) We discovered a topological quantum optics effect, namely, topological superradiance lattice. We first developed a theory of superradiance lattices which lays the foundation for studying condensed matter problems in a quantum optics analogue using a lattice in momentum space. The superradiance lattices can be realized in conventional configurations of electromagnetically induced transparency. This result has been published in Physical Review Letters 114, 043602 (2015). Based on that work, we discovered the toplogical superradiance lattices, in particular, a superradiance lattice that simulates the famous Haldane model. This work is currently under peer review in Optica.

401011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
401011.value: The topological superradiance lattices are a newly discovered topological effect. It has stimulated a lot of interest in the field. Several leading experimental groups have been planning on experimental implementation of the scheme. We will carry out collaboration research with these groups and also develop the theory to a more general theory of topological quantum optics.

401011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
401011.value: Topological insulators differentiate from conventional insulators by their intrinsic topological structures of energy bands. Optical spectroscopy has been a very useful tool to study insulators. Thus we were motivated to investigate the nonlinear optical effects of topological insulators. In nonlinear optics, an electron can be excited from the valence band to the conduction band with a hole left behind in the valence band. The electron and hole can be further driven by other optical fields, which is similar to the acceleration of particles in vacuum, but with a distinct property in topological insulators - the intrinsic quantum states rotate when the electron and hole are accelerated in topological insulators. Therefore, the electron and hole accumulate special geometric phases, called Berry phases. We discovered a series of non-trivial effects of the geometric phases on the nonlinear optics, which are particularly relevant to the study of the intrinsic energy band structures of topological insulators. The schemes proposed in this project have stimulated a lot of interest in the field, especially from some leading experimental groups. We expect novel nonlinear optical effects to be discovered based on the theoretical study in this project.

401211.label: Project Objectives
401211.value: A systematic investigation on the coordination chemistry of guanidinate anions with lanthanide(II) ions will be carried out in this work. A series of unsymmetrical guanidinate ligands of the formula [(RR'N)C(NR')(NAr)]– will be employed in this study. Effects concerning the steric and electronic properties of these ligands on the structures of the corresponding lanthanide(II) guanidinates will be examined. The redox chemistry of these lanthanide(II) guanidinates will also be investigated. Current literature on the chemistry of lanthanide(II) guanidinates has indicated that the reaction chemistry of this class of compounds is a relatively unexplored area (please see Adv. Organomet. Chem. (2008) vol. 57, p.183 and Dalton Trans. (2007) p.187). An initial study in our laboratory has shown that reactions of an Eu(II) and Yb(II) guanidinate with iodine or copper(I) chloride can lead to the corresponding mixed-ligand lanthanide(III) halide complexes. The latter complexes can serve as good starting materials for other mixed-ligand compounds through metathetical reactions of the halide ligands with other anionic ligands. Guanidinate ligands have a good pi-donor property. They have been used to stabilize metal ions of unusual oxidation states (Please see Science (2007) vol. 318, p.1754, and Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. (2009) vol. 48, p.7406). In this proposed research work, attempts will also be carried out to study the coordination properties of our guanidinate ligands with highly reducing Tm(II), Dy(II) and Nd(II) ions. We hope results obtained in this study as well as those from our previous work on amido and amidinate ligand sets can give us a good understanding on the coordination behavior of these three classes of anionic N-donor ligands with lanthanide(II) ions. Finally, an initial exploration on the chemistry of lanthanide(II) complexes supported by the closely related bis(2,4,6-tri-tert-butylphenyl)triazenide ligand [Ar”NNNAr”]– (Ar” = 2,4,6-tri-tert-butylphenyl) will also be carried out.

401411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
401411.value: Geometry of special holonomy is the study of spaces with rich algebraic structures. Calabi-Yau manifolds and G_2 manifolds are examples of such. These spaces play very important roles in mathematics. They also arise naturally as internal spaces in string theory and M-theory in physics. Manifolds with most restricted holonomy groups are Riemannian locally symmetric spaces. They are important moduli spaces in mathematics and in physics when many supersymmetries exist. The principal investigator had developed a unified method to describe all these structures in a systematic way using normed division algebras. This method has proven to be very useful in uncovering many geometric structures and relationships among these geometries. The PI plans to continue these studies and apply this method to further improve our understanding of the geometry of these important spaces. 特殊和樂幾何研究有豐富幾何結構的空間。它們包括卡拉比丘空間和G2空間。這些空間在數學中扮演極重要的角色。它們也是物理學中的弦理論及M理論的內置空間。 黎曼局部對稱空間擁有最特殊的和樂群。它們經常出現在具有多個超對稱的數學和物理理論的模空間。 本主研究員已經發展一套統一方法用范除子代數來系統地描述所有有關結構。這方法已有效地用作發現各種新的幾何結構及它們之間的關係。本主研究員計劃繼續這方面的研究及用這方法去增加我們對這些重要空間的幾何的認識。

401411.label: Realisation of objectives
401411.value: For calibrated cycles in G2 manifolds, we had related associative submanifolds bounding coassociative submanifolds with Gromov-Witten invariants and we have now found new nontrivial examples. For G_2 geometry, or more generally manifolds with special holonomy, Cao and I had developed the foundation of Donaldson-Thomas invariants for Calabi-Yau fourfolds, giving us a better understanding of such geometries. For the further development of Riemannian symmetric spaces, the PI has applied this theory to quantum cohomology of these spaces and described the geometry of ADE bundles. Besides realizing a large part of the original objectives, during the course of carrying out this project, new directions and applications has been discovered as well.

401411.label: Major findings and research outcome
401411.value: In joint work with Wang and Zhu, the PI had further our understandings of associative submanifolds bounding coassociative submanifolds. In particular, new nontrivial examples of such associative submanifolds had been constructed in [1]. In a series of joint works with Cao Yalong, the PI has developed the foundation of Donaldson-Thomas invariants for Calabi-Yau fourfolds and computed many nontrivial examples in [5], solving the orientability issue of moduli spaces in [6], studied the relative invariant and TQFT structure in [7] and described some relationships with mirror symmetry in [8]. In [10,11], Li Changzheng and PI studies quantum cohomology of flag varieties. Among other things, we established Quantum Pieri rules for tautological subbundle. In [2,3,4], Chen Yunxia, Zhang Jiajin and the PI studied the geometry of ADE bundles over algebraic surfaces. In [2] such bundles are constructed using ADE singularities, generalized earlier result of Friedman and Morgan for del Pezzo surfaces. In [4] we established relationships between the geometry of ADE bundles and the geometry of the underlying surface. In [3] we generalized the work of Batyrev on a correspondence between del Pezzo surfaces and embedding into flag varieties of type E to all ADE types.

401411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
401411.value: All the these foundings have big potential for further development. Both existence, uniqueness and moduli problems for calibrated cycles are still poorly understood. They are important geometric objects and play important roles in duality, including mirror symmetry. The PI plans to further develop tools to describe their geometry. Also geometry of special holonomy, including G2 geometry, Spin(7) geometry and Calabi-Yau geometry are important and require many different new ideas and tools. Our DT4 theory should be an important ingredient in this whole picture and therefore deserved much further understanding. Other speical types of geometry, including symmetric spaces, flag varities, ADE geometry and so on are also relevent everywhere in geometry and physics and PI plans to continue these directions of research on them.

401411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
401411.value: Special geometry is an important branch in mathematics as well as the studies of string theory in physics. The project has sucessfully further our understanding of this area by analyzing natural classes of cycles in these spaces, making many nontrivial calculations and constructing new examples. In doing so, the PI had employed a wide range of mathematics, including algebraic geometry, differential geometry, representation theory and mathematical physics. It is amazing to see how all these different branches of mathematics unified in the understanding of special geometry in a harmonious manner.

401511.label: Project Objectives
401511.value: Study the effects of the structural parameters of the lattice and building units on the collective plasmons of metal nanostructure arrays through electrodynamic calculations. Develop numerical methods for calculating and understanding the interactions between the plasmons and the optical transitions of quantum systems. Fabricate metal nanostructure arrays according to the calculation results and study their plasmonic properties by measuring the reflection, transmission, and scattering spectra. Deposit dye molecules and QDs on the arrays, investigate the interactions between the absorption and emission and the collective plasmons by measuring the steady-state, polarization- and direction-dependent absorption and fluorescence spectra and transient absorption and emission dynamics, and compare the measured results with our theoretical calculations.

401511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
401511.value: Optoelectronic devices have been finding wide applications in various aspects of our daily lives. Tremendous efforts are currently being made to improve the energy conversion efficiencies of these devices, especially solar cells and light-emitting diodes. The key component in these devices, the active layer, typically consists of organic or inorganic chromophores. An essential aspect in developing high-efficiency optoelectronic devices lies in enhancing and controlling the absorption and emission of these quantum systems, including the wavelength, intensity, polarization, and direction. Noble metal nanostructures exhibit rich plasmonic properties. The excitation of their plasmons squeezes the light in the nanoscale regions adjacent to individual or closely spaced nanostructures. Previous single-particle studies have shown that the squeezed light can strongly couple with and modulate the absorption and emission processes of various quantum systems. However, the localized plasmons of individual metal nanostructures can only be tailored by changing their materials and geometries. In addition, the light squeezing is limited in the subwavelength regions close to individual nanostructures. Chromophores have to be precisely positioned within these regions for their optical transitions to be modulated, which has yet remained challenging. Moreover, most of practical optoelectronic devices operate at the macroscopic level. There exists a clear spatial gap between individual metal nanostructures and macroscopic devices. We propose using metal nanostructure arrays to control and enhance the optical transitions. In the arrays, the interactions among the localized plasmons of the individual nanostructures can not only further enhance the local electric field, but also remarkably extend the enhancement region away from the nanostructures. Moreover, the plasmonic wavelength, linewidth, scattering polarization and direction can be tailored by varying the array lattice besides the composition and geometry of each unit. We will first perform electromagnetic computations to study the effects of the various structure parameters on the collective plasmons. Numerical methods will then be developed to generally calculate the plasmon-exciton interactions in a variety of hybrid systems, understand the underlying physics, and guide the design of metal nanostructure arrays to achieve desired emission properties. We will then fabricate metal nanostructure arrays lithographically according to our theoretical studies, and investigate their plasmonic properties. Dye molecules and quantum dots will be further deposited on the arrays and the interactions between the collective plasmons and the optical transitions will be studied. The obtained results will pave the way for the design of metal nanostructure arrays for enhancing the performances of various optoelectronic devices. 在当今人类日常生活中，光电子器件扮演着不可或缺的角色。长期以来，人们在提高这些器件的能量转换效率方面投入了巨大的研究精力。其中，太阳能电池和发光二极管是两个最受关注的方向。这些光电子器件的有源层通常由各种有机或无机的生色团（染料分子、半导体量子点）组成。因此，开发高性能光电子器件的一个关键技术便是调控这些生色团的发光行为，包括其发光波长、强度、偏振以及方向。 贵金属纳米结构具有丰富的表面等离子体共振（表面激元共振）特性。通过激发该共振，金属纳米结构可以将入射光场高度压缩于其周围极小的区域，从而实现极大的场增强效应。以往的研究结果表明，这种光场压缩效应可以有效地应用于调制各种量子系统（如荧光染料和半导体量子点）的光吸收和辐射。然而，对于单个金属纳米结构而言，其激元共振只能通过改变相应的材料和结构参数来进行调制，调节自由度很小。另一方面，单个纳米结构只能在其附近亚波长区域内实现有效的光场压缩。只有当生色团处于这些特定区域，其发光行为才能受到纳米结构的调制。而至今为止，精确控制生色团和金属纳米结构之间的相对位置仍然是一项极具挑战性的课题。此外，从实际应用层面来看，目前的光电子器件绝大多数都工作在宏观尺度。因此，单个金属纳米结构和宏观量级的光电子器件之间仍然存在着一个鸿沟，阻止了其有效应用于改良光电子器件的性能。 在本项目中，我们提出利用金属纳米结构阵列来调控量子系统的光学过程。在阵列结构中，激元共振之间的相互作用可以更进一步提高结构单元附近的光场，同时该场增强效应还可以扩展到整个阵列之中。此外，我们还可以通过调节阵列结构单元的材料和结构、阵列的周期以及阵列的对称性来系统地调制激元共振的波长、谱宽、散射的偏振特性以及散射的方向。在具体的研究中，我们将首先利用电磁场数值模拟的方法来系统研究阵列的各种结构参数对其激元共振的影响。基于对金属纳米结构阵列激元共振特性的理解，我们将进一步发展数值计算方法来描述激元共振与生色团激子的相互作用，并深入理解其物理本质。在理论工作的基础上，我们将设计能够实现特定激元特性的阵列结构，并利用微加工的技术进行相应阵列的制作。得到阵列结构之后，我们将采用各种光学手段对其激元共振特性进行表征，从实验上探讨其等离激元特性。最后，我们将各种染料分子和半导体量子点组装到金属纳米结构阵列上，研究其光跃迁和阵列激元共振之间的相互作用，以获得激元共振对量子系统发光行为的调制。这一系列研究的结果将有望为利用激元共振改良各种光电子器件的性能提供坚实的理论基础和重要的实验指导。我们相信，这是一项具有原创性的研究，对深入理解纳米尺度光与物质相互作用的物理过程以及发展新型发光器件的技术储备有着重大的意义。

401511.label: Realisation of objectives
401511.value: (1) We carried out finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations to study the plasmonic properties of individual metal nanostructures and metal nanostructure arrays with varying shapes (nanodisks and nanorods), sizes, gap distances and arrangement symmetries (square, hexagonal and rectangular). We also performed intensive FDTD simulations on the magnetic plasmon resonance properties of triangular gold nanorod trimers and investigated the effects of the nanorod size and gap distance on the occurrence of the magnetic plasmon mode. (2) We carried out FDTD simulations to understand the interactions between the plasmon of gold nanorods and fluorescent dye molecules. Gold nanorods of different sizes were considered. A Hertzian electric dipole source was employed to simulate the fluorescent dye molecule that was placed close to the surface of gold nanorods. The near-field interactions between the dipole and the plasmon of gold nanorod are expected to be strongly dependent on the location and orientation of the molecular dipole relative to the nanorod. In principle, a number of simulations with varying dipole locations and orientations need to be performed to fully understand the interactions. However, this is a formidable computational task. We therefore considered only two representative cases, where the dipole source is located at one end of the nanorod along the length axis, or at the side and half length of the nanorod. Moreover, we also simulated the emission patterns of a fluorescent dye molecule placed at varying distances away from a gold nanorod. (3) We learned to fabricate gold nanostructures and gold nanostructure arrays using electron-beam lithography in conjunction with thermal metal deposition. We successfully fabricate gold nanodisk and nanorod arrays with different lattice symmetries, lattice constants and gap distances. We measured the reflection and scattering properties of the fabricated metal nanostructures and arrays in order to understand their plasmonic properties. On the other hand, we also developed methods for depositing colloidal metal nanocrystals onto various substrates, including soft, flexible ones (cotton and silk) and hard ones (glass slides, silica and titania). (4) We studied the plasmonic properties of the physically fabricated gold nanorods and compared them with those of chemically synthesized gold nanorods. The physically fabricated gold nanorods were found to exhibit much poorer plasmonic properties than chemical counterparts with similar shape and sizes. Because of this result, we mainly studied the interactions between chemically synthesized gold nanorods and fluorescent dye molecules as well as between the nanorods and inorganic HgTe quantum dots.

401511.label: Major findings and research outcome
401511.value: (1) We found that the collective plasmons of the nanostructure arrays are much narrower and red-shifted with respect to that of the individual nanostructures. The maximum field intensity enhancements of the arrays are much larger than that of the single nanostructures. Moreover, The field intensity enhancements are present in between the neighboring nanostructures in the arrays, while they generally decay exponentially away from the metal surface for single metal nanostructures. (2) The emission of organic fluorescent dye molecules were found experimentally and through FDTD simulations to be affected strongly by the plasmon of gold nanorods, including the emission spectral shape, emission peak energy and emission polarization. (3) Lithographical gold nanorods were found to exhibit much weaker scattering, largely broadened spectral widths, and considerably reduced electric field enhancements in comparison with chemically synthesized gold nanorods. The reduction in the plasmonic performance of the lithographical nanorods is caused mainly by the use of an adhesive metal layer and slightly by their polycrystalline nature. This work was published on Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys.. Our quantitative comparison results will be very helpful in guiding the selection of proper types of metal nanostructures for targeted technological applications. In addition, methods were developed for the deposition of colloidal metal nanocrystals on various substrates. The results were published on Small and Nanoscale. (4) Gold nanorods were incorporated into HgTe quantum dot/ZnO heterojunction photodiode photodetectors. More than 80 and 240% increments of average short-circuit current density were observed in the devices with gold nanorods covered by ~7.5 and ~4.5 nm ZnO layers, respectively. The exciton dissociation and charge extraction efficiencies were found to be also enhanced by gold nanorods, due to local electric field effects. The plasmonic structure improves the overall infrared detectivity of the HgTe quantum dot photodetectors without affecting their temporal response. This work was published on ACS Nano. (5) We prepared core/satellite nanostructures from large and small gold nanospheres. These nanostructures exhibit interesting surface-enhanced Raman properties. We also fabricated gold nanosphere/graphene/gold film sandwich structures. The graphene-loaded nanoantennas show dramatic resonance red shifts, which can be modified by varying graphene dielectric screening effect. Such nanoantennas can therefore not only strengthen light-graphene interactions drastically but also exemplify an electroplasmonic system naturally. These two works were published on Adv. Opt. Mater.. In addition, We also summarized recent works on plasmonics, including our own together with others', in two review articles on Chem. Soc. Rev. and Physics (Chinese).

401511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
401511.value: We can fabricate highly ordered metal nanostructure arrays with controlled shapes and lattice constants with physical methods. However, the plasmons of physically fabricated metal nanostructures are severely damped, owing to the use of Ti or Cr adhesion layer and the polycrystalline nature of the deposited metals. In addition, physical metal nanostructures generally have rough surfaces. The gap distances between neighboring metal nanostructures are difficult to be made at a few nanometers or even smaller. This limit precludes the study of my important phenomena arising from both plasmonics and quantum mechanics. Chemically synthesized, colloidal metal nanocrystals are mostly single-crystalline. They possess strong plasmon modes. Moreover, their plasmonic properties can be readily controlled synthetically. However, the ordering and positioning of chemical metal nanocrystals has remained challenging, in spite of a great deal of effort made worldwide. In the future, a direction in the field of plasmonics would be to combine the precise positioning capability of physical fabrication methods with the high plasmonic quality of chemically synthesized metal nanocrystals. This is expected to be a fruitful direction. Efforts devoted to this direction will lead to many advanced devices and applications in utilizing, guiding and manipulating light waves over a wide spectral range.

401511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
401511.value: Fluorescent organic dye molecules and inorganic semiconductor quantum dots can emit light upon excitation at a higher energy. The emission color can be varied by use of different molecules, semiconductors or control of the quantum dot size. This light emission is very important in many aspects for human being, including illumination, display, information communication, solar energy utilization and many sensing devices. However, a molecule or quantum dot usually emits in all directions. Its emission color and efficiency are fixed. To be able to control the emission properties of molecules and quantum dots and increase their emission efficiencies would be very attractive for the above-mentioned applications. In this project, we used the plasmons of metal nanostructures to control and manipulate the emission properties of molecules and quantum dots. The plasmons of metal nanostructures can be synthetically tailored. They exhibit extremely large extinction cross-sections and electric field enhancements. Through this project, our understanding of the interactions between plasmon and fluorescence has been improved greatly. Our results show clearly that the use of the plasmons of metal nanostructures to control the light emission behaviors of molecules and quantum dots is highly feasible.

401811.label: Project Objectives
401811.value: Design algorithms for the shape analysis of 2D multiply-connected objects. The goal is to define a suitable metric on the space of multiply-connected shapes, such that accurate detection of shape variations between multiply-connected objects can be achieved. Design and implement algorithms for 3D shape analysis which facilitate the process of registration and measuring shape variations. This includes (i) multi-scale representations for surface registrations; (ii) optimized parameterizations with controlled squeezing; (iii) algorithms for high-genus surface analysis; and (iv) algorithms for volumetric-based shape analysis. Practical applications of the algorithms to medical imaging for disease analysis. This includes (i) the shape analysis of genus-3 vestibular systems for Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis(AIS) patients; (ii) the detection of shape changes in brain MRIs in Alzheimer's disease; and (iii) algorithms for shape-based medical image classification/retrieval.

401811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
401811.value: With the development of 2D imaging and 3D acquisition techniques, objects in the real world can now be captured accurately. The demand for shape analysis to automatically analyze the captured geometric shapes is thus ever increasing, with various applications such as in computer vision and medical morphometry. It is therefore necessary to develop mathematical models to analyze shapes efficiently. Quasiconformal(QC) geometry, which studies the distortions of deformation patterns between shapes, is useful for this purpose. In this project, our goal is to develop effective mathematical algorithms for shape analysis, using QC geometry as a tool. This research can mainly be divided into two parts. In the first part of the research, we are interested in developing efficient algorithms for 2D and 3D shape analysis. For 2D shape analysis, we will focus on analyzing multiply-connected shapes, which are comparatively less studied in the literature. In this project, we will design a suitable metric for the space of multiply-connected shapes. This allows us to compare and analyze 2D multiply-connected objects accurately. For 3D shape analysis, we will develop algorithms which facilitate the process of shape matching (registration) and measuring shape variations. We will firstly develop a multi-scale representation for surface registrations. It will be useful in shape analysis to adjust and analyze registrations at multiple scales. Secondly, a common approach for shape analysis is by parameterizing the surface onto a simple parameter domain. One major drawback is the squeezing effect under the parameterization. To solve this problem, we will develop algorithms to obtain an optimized parameterization with controlled squeezing and least amount of conformality distortions. Thirdly, we are interested in developing algorithms to analyze high-genus surfaces. It is generally challenging due to the complicated topology of the surface. In this project, we will design algorithms to obtain feature loops on these surfaces and compute registrations between them with complete geometric matching. With these, comprehensive shape analysis of high-genus surfaces can be achieved. Furthermore, internal structures of shapes usually embed important information. Volumetric-based shape analysis is thus necessary. For this purpose, we will design different shape indices to capture shape variations between 3D volumetric objects. Lastly, in the second part of our research, we will apply our algorithms to practical applications in medical image analysis. This will include:(i)the shape analysis of genus-3 vestibular systems for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients; (ii)the detection of shape changes in brain MRIs in Alzheimer's disease; and (iii)algorithms for shape-based medical image classification/retrieval. 隨著二維成像和三維獲取技術的發展，現在我們能夠精確地捕捉真實世界中的物體。在很多應用如計算機視覺和醫學形態學中，自動分析所獲取形狀的需求不斷增長。因此，發展高效的形狀分析的數學模型是非常必要的。拟保角（Quasiconformal）幾何對於這一目標是非常有用的，它研究的是形狀之間的形變模式。本項目中，我們的目標是利用拟保角幾何這一工具來發展形狀分析的有效數學算法。 本研究可以被劃分成主要的兩部分。在第一部分中，我們的興趣在於開發二維和三維形狀分析的高效算法。對於二維形狀分析，我們將會專注於多連通區域的分析，這在文獻中的研究相對較少。本項目中我們將會設計一個適用於多連通形狀空間的測度，這使得我們能夠更精確地比較和分析二維多連通物體。 對於三維形狀分析，我們將會開發計算形狀對應和度量形狀差異的算法。首先，我們會提出曲面配準的多尺度表示，這可以用於在多個尺度上調整和分析形狀匹配。其次，形狀分析的一個常用的方法是把曲面在一個簡單區域上重新參數化。參數化的一個主要的缺點是具有面積壓縮效應。為了解決這個問題，我們將會設計獲得最優參數化的算法，其具有可控的面積壓縮效應和最小的保角擾動。第三，我們有興趣發展分析高虧格曲面的算法。這非常具有挑戰性，因為曲面具有複雜的拓撲。本項目中我們將會設計算法獲取這些曲面上的特徵閉曲線，利用純粹的幾何匹配來計算形狀曲面之間的配準。利用這些，可以獲得對高虧格曲面的全面分析。此外形狀的內部結構通常蘊含了重要的信息，因此立體形狀分析也是很有必要的。對於這一目的，我們將會設計不同的形狀指數來捕捉三維立體物體之間的形變。 最後，在研究的第二部分，我們會將我們的算法應用於醫學圖像分析的實際應用中。這包括：(i)青少年特發性脊柱侧凸患者的3-虧格前庭系統的形狀分析；(ii)阿耳茨海默氏病的腦部核磁共振成像中的形變檢測；(iii)醫學圖像分類/檢索算法。

401811.label: Realisation of objectives
401811.value: In this project, we have three main objectives. The PI has tackled each proposed problems successfully. Details are as follows. Objective 1: The first objective is to develop mathematical models based on Riemannian metric for remeshing digital surfaces with highly irregular triangulation. The PI has successfully achieved this goal. More precisely, we have developed an algorithm, called the Hooke’s mesh optimization, to obtain an optimized mesh based on the input (discrete) metric. Each edge is treated as an elastic spring associated with some elastic forces. The mesh optimization is based on a modified version of Hooke’s laws, whose stiffness coefficients are different depending on the displacement of vertices. This avoids flipping of triangles during the mesh optimization process. A filtering scheme called the Newtonian Filtering is developed based on the high-dimensional Newton’s method to further preserve the local geometry of the optimized mesh. Results show that the combinination of the Hooke’s Optimization and the Newtonian Filtering significantly enhance the mesh quality, while both smoothness and local geometry of the surface are greatly preserved. Another advantage of this algorithm is that it can handle surface meshes with any topologies, including multiply-connected or high-genus surfaces. Besides, surface remeshing can be achieved through a global conformal parameterization. A high-quality triangulation on a simple parameter domain can be projected onto the original surface to get a good remeshed surface. However, an efficient and accurate algorithm global conformal parameterization algorithm is necessary. To achieve this goal, the PI has developed effective numerical algorithms using Beltrami differentials to compute global conformal and quasiconformal parameterizations for simply-connected open or closed surfaces. In addition, a remeshing algorithm, called the Teichmuller remeshing algorithm, has been developed. The main idea is to optimally project a regular triangulation to the original surface, which balances between angle distortions and area distortion. The projection is based on a landmark-matching Teichmuller map that minimizes the conformality distortion subject to the landmark constraints. The algorithm has shown to be effective for remeshing a simply-connected surface mesh with highly irregular triangulation. Objective 2: The second objective is to design algorithms for computing the isometric embedding associated to a given metric and curvature function. The PI has successfully achieved this objective. More specifically, an iterative algorithm has been developed to reconstruct a surface from the conformal factor (associated to a given Riemannian metric) and mean curvature. The iterative scheme is guided by the Gauss-Codazzi equation. The algorithm has shown to be effective in computing the embedding associated to an admissible pair of metric and curvature function. With the algorithm, many mesh editing tasks can be effectively done. More specifically, the mesh can be edited by adjusting the metric and curvature function of the original mesh. An edited mesh can be reconstructed from the processed metric and curvature function. With this idea, the PI has successfully designed algorithms to solve the surface inpainting problem as well as the shape morphing problem. By inpainting the curvature function and the conformal factor function on the 2D parameter domain, an inpainted surface mesh that follows the overall geometry can be reconstructed using our developed algorithm. Besides, the isometric embedding problem is also solved by formulating the problem as finding suitable coefficients associated to the Laplace-Beltrami eigenfunctions using an iterative algorithm. Objective 3: Our third objective is to develop fast algorithm for effective shape matching. One of the tasks in this objective is to develop fast method to compute the Beltrami Holomorphic flow. The idea is to obtain the variation of the quasiconformal map under the variation of the Beltrami differential. Conventional approach computes the variation using an integral formulation. The computation of integration is time-consuming. To compute the Beltrami Holomorphic Flow efficiently, we propose an efficient algorithm by minimization and energy functional involving the quasiconformal map and the Beltrami differential, using the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM). The obtained quasiconformal map and the Beltrami differential are associated with each other by adding the Beltrami energy in the energy functional. The method has shown to be effective and efficient for computing the Beltrami Holomorphic Flow. The fast method is useful for obtaining the shape matching between surfaces efficiently. Another task is to develop an efficient algorithm based on a multi-level approach. In this project, the PI has successfully developed a multi-level formulation for computing the surface registration. Intuitively, a coarse shape matching is firstly computed and the coarse registration is further refined using the proposed registration model. The method can significantly speed up the computation of the shape matching problem. Objective 4: This objective is to apply the developed algorithms to practical applications. This objective has been successfully achieved. Firstly, the efficient shape matching algorithms have been successfully applied to register anatomical structures, such as the brainstem surfaces, brain cortical surfaces and hippocampus surfaces. Secondly, the mesh editing algorithm has also been successfully applied to remesh the hippocampal surfaces, which can then be used for further disease analysis. The surface inpainting algorithm is also applied for filling occlusions on anatomical structures, such as the brain cortical surfaces. The remeshing algorithm is also applied to obtain a surface mesh with regular triangulation, so that the partial differential equation involved in the surface registration problem can be accurately solved.

402011.label: Project Objectives
402011.value: To synthesize a series of aryl tetracenes, which are designed to be both an organic semiconductor and a clathrate host. To resolve aryl tetracenes with commercial resolving agents through the formation of diasteromeric salts and with enantiomerically pure guest molecules through the formation of diastereomeric clathrates. To find the relationship between the molecular structure of aryl tetracene and the supramolecular structure of clathrate. To resolve chiral molecules using the enantiomerically pure aryl tetracenes as resolving agents through the formation of diastereomeric clathrates. To fabricate single-layer and double-layer thin film transistors with aryl tetracenes as active components and to apply these transistors as chemical vapor sensors. To test the sensitivity and selectivity of the above OTFT-based sensors when responding to various volatile organic compounds; to elucidate the fundamental links between molecular structures of aryl tetracenes and their performance in these sensors.

402011.value: 有機薄膜晶體管則是有機電子器件中不可或缺的結構單元，是製造廉價的大面積柔性電子器件的基礎。有機薄膜晶體管的最具前途的應用之一是化學與生物傳感。這是因為基於有機薄膜晶體管的傳感器可以把靈敏的電信號輸出與簡單的器件製備相結合，從而克服大多數光學檢測方法對笨重而又昂貴儀器的依賴。有機薄膜晶體管應用於傳感有一個特別的優勢，即通過有機合成可以讓有機半導體分子具有專門的識別單元來檢測選定的待測分子。儘管基於有機薄膜晶體管的傳感器潛力巨大，這類器件的發展才剛剛起步。它們在實際應用中的最終成功有賴於大幅提高檢測的選擇性、靈敏度、可重複性及穩定性。 把客體分子束縛在主體分子的固體網絡裡就會形成晶格包合物。這是一種結合待測分子的有效方法，但是還沒有在基於有機薄膜晶體管的傳感器中應用過。在此我們提出一種新的方案來構築基於有機薄膜晶體管的傳感器，即利用一類特殊的有機半導體分子來把待測分子束縛在其晶格中。我們的前期研究發現5-(1'-萘基)並四苯（NT）就是一個這樣的特殊分子。為了增強對待測分子的束縛能力和選擇性，我們在NT的基礎上設計了三類芳基並四苯分子。由於保持了NT分子的重要結構特徵，我們預期這些分子將同時具有半導體和主體分子的性質。針對這些新穎的芳基並四苯分子，我們制定了跨學科的研究計劃，旨在提高基於有機薄膜晶體管的氣體傳感器的靈敏度和選擇性。這項研究計劃包括新穎功能分子的合成、晶格包合物的晶體工程以及有機薄膜晶體管的器件工程。利用芳基並四苯分子的單一對映體，原則上可以實現手性傳感器。與這一目標相聯繫，我們還計劃利用芳基並四苯分子的單一對映體來做為拆分試劑，特別是用來解決分子識別研究中的一個難題， 即拆分手性的碳氫化合物。 這項研究計劃提出了新的傳感原理來設計基於有機薄膜晶體管的傳感器，將有助於拓展有機半導體材料的功能。它的成功將有可能為發展高靈敏度、高選擇性的廉價化學氣體傳感器（比如輕便的室內空氣質量檢測器）開闢新的方向。

402011.label: Realisation of objectives
402011.value: We have successfully realized most of the objectives. We synthesized a series of aryl tetracenes and systematically studied the composition and structure of the clathrates of these aryl tetracenes. Particularly, we obtained 10 single crystal structures of clathrates and 3 single crystal structures of aryl tetracenes without guest molecules. By comparing these crystal structures, we were able to understand the relationship between the molecular structure of aryl tetracenes and the supramolecular structure of clathrates. We successfully fabricated organic thin film transistors (OTFTs) using aryl tetracenes as active components and studied their response toward varied chemical vapors for sensing application. We tested the sensitivity and selectivity of these OTFTs when responding to various volatile organic compounds, and studied the relationship between molecular structures of aryl tetracenes and their performance in the OTFTs for sensing. However, we met difficulties in realizing the objectives of resolving aryl tetracenes through forming diastereomeric salts and diastereomeric clathrates. We tested a series of enantiomerically pure acids, which, however, did not form crystalline salts with basic aryl tetracenes. We also tested a variety of enantiomerically pure guest molecules, which, unfortunately, always formed clathrates with a racemic mixture of aryl tetracenes as found from the crystal structures. Although the two enantiomers of aryl tetracenes can in principle be separated by chiral HPLC, this method cannot yield a sufficient amount of products for the subsequent experiments. The key objective of this project is to develop new strategies for chemical sensors based on OTFTs. For this purpose, we extended this project in two directions. First we studied n-channel OTFTs of a series of N-rich polycyclic heteroarenes, which have N atoms as the potential binding site embedded in the semiconductor backbone. Second, we developed novel monolayer field effect transistors based on an unusual brickwork arrangement of non-planar organic semiconductors. This type of monolayer transistors have the conduction channel exposed to analyte molecules in environment and thus provide a good platform for sensing application.

402011.label: Major findings and research outcome
402011.value: In this project, we explored three strategies for chemical sensors based on organic thin film transistors (OTFTs). The first strategy utilized aryl tetracenes, a unique class of semiconducting molecules able to trap analyte molecules within their crystal lattice. We synthesized a series of aryl tetracenes, obtained 13 single crystal structures and fabricated organic thin film transistors (OTFTs) using these aryl tetracenes. From this study, we have found that this strategy is limited by the fact that formation of clathrates requires a high concentration of organic vapors. The second strategy is to use N-rich polycyclic heteroarenes as organic semiconductors in the conduction channel of OTFTs since the basic N atoms embedded in the semiconductor backbones are potential binding sites for acidic analyte molecules. A group of these N-rich polycyclic heteroarenes are novel chlorinated cyclobuta[1,2-b:3,4-b']diquinoxalines, which were synthesized and investigated by us in this project. It is found that their molecular packing can be tuned by varying the number and position of chlorine substituents, and 2,8-dichloro-cyclobuta[1,2-b:3,4-b']diquinoxaline either in pure form or as a mixture with its regioisomer functions as n-type semiconductors in organic thin film transistors with field effect mobility of up to 0.42 cm2/Vs and 0.20 cm2/Vs, respectively. The third strategy is a monolayer nanosheet of organic semiconductors, which allows the conduction channel of OTFTs exposed to analyte molecules in environment and thus provide a good platform for chemical sensing. It is found that twisted hexabenzoperylenes (HBPs) containing proper substituting groups self-assemble into lamellar semiconductors with an unusual brickwork arrangement of twisted π-faces. As a result of this brickwork arrangement, through a dip-coating process, these HBPs easily formed one-molecule-thick nanosheets, which behaved as p-type organic semiconductors in monolayer transistors with field effect mobility of up to 0.076 cm2/Vs . This project has led to four publications in high-impact journals. We have also presented results related to this project at three international conferences. Moreover, one M. Phil. student and one PhD student, who graduated in July 2012 and July 2015, respectively were trained in this project. These outcomes are detailed in Part C.

402011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
402011.value: With the conduction channel directly exposed to environment, the monolayer transistors of twisted HBPs developed in this project provide a promising platform for sensing applications. Covalently linking recognition sites to the end of the alkyl chains in these molecules may lead to new semiconducting nanosheets as selective electrical sensors. We will develop efficient synthesis to allow suitable functionalization of the semiconductor nanosheets for highly sensitive chemical sensing.

402011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
402011.value: Organic thin film transistors (OTFTs) are essential building blocks of large-area, flexible, and low-cost organic electronics. One of the most promising applications of OTFTs is chemical sensing because OTFTs can convert chemical interactions into electrical outputs with a simple device structure. In this project, we explored three strategies to construct OTFT-based sensors. The first strategy relies on unique semiconducting molecules that can trap analyte molecules within their crystal lattice to form clathrates. By investigating a novel series of aryl tetracenes as active components in OTFTs, we have found that this strategy has a rather limited application for chemical sensing because formation of clathrates requires a high concentration of organic vapors. The second strategy is to fabricate OTFTs using N-rich organic semiconductors, which have basic N atoms embedded in the conjugated backbones as potential binding sites for acidic analyte molecules. The third strategy is a novel monolayer nanosheet of twisted organic semiconductors, which is formed by an unusual brickwork arrangement of the twisted π-faces. OTFTs containing this type of semiconductor monolayer as the conduction channel is a better platform for sensing application than the conventional multilayer OTFTs because analyte molecules can directly interact with the conduction channel.

402211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
402211.value: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is a promising therapeutic modality for the treatment of various premalignant and malignant diseases. It utilizes the combined action of three individually nontoxic components, namely a photosensitizer, light, and molecular oxygen to cause cellular and tissue damage. Singlet oxygen generated through the photosensitization process is believed to be the major cytotoxic reactive oxygen species (ROS) responsible for the damage. With a view to improving the therapeutic outcomes, various strategies have been explored to enhance the ROS generation efficiency of the photosensitizers and more importantly their selectivity toward malignant tissues. For cancer treatment, an alternative approach involves the use of smart photosensitizers which can be selectively activated by tumor-associated stimuli. The effects of combined PDT with the traditional chemotherapy have also been briefly evaluated. The aim of this proposal is to secure fund to develop activatable anticancer agents for dual chemo- and photodynamic therapy. We plan to study conjugates of hydrophilic distyryl boron dipyrromethenes (DSBDPs) and ferrocenyl diphenol butene derivatives, which are connected by the acid-labile hydrazone and/or reductively cleavable disulfide linkers. Owing to the many favorable characteristics, DSBDPs have emerged to be a new class of efficient photosensitizers. The ferrocenyl moieties have antiproliferative effects and can quench the excited state of the DSBDP core when they are in close proximity, thereby inhibiting the ROS generation by DSBDP. On the basis that the extracellular region of solid tumors and some intracellular compartments are acidic, and the intracellular reduced glutathione concentration is substantially higher than extracellular levels, particularly for tumor tissues, the hydrazone and disulfide linkers of these compounds are expected to be cleaved selectively in tumor cells. The separation of the DSBDP and ferrocenyl moieties can restore the photosensitization process and lead to dual cytotoxic effects induced by these two components. In this project, we will synthesize and characterize a series of these conjugates, and study their cleavage kinetics at different pH and concentrations of glutathione in aqueous media by monitoring the fluorescence and ROS generation efficiency of the DSBDP unit. 402211.label: Realisation of objectives
402211.value: The first objective of this project is to design, synthesize, and characterize a series of pegylated distyryl boron dipyrromethenes (DSBDPs) which are conjugated to two ferrocenyl quenchers via acid-labile and/or thiol-sensitive linkers. A series of three of these compounds and a non-cleavable control compound were prepared and spectroscopically characterized. For synthetic convenience, the proposed ferrocenyl diphenol butene derivatives were replaced with ferrocenyl chalcone moieties, which are also chemotherapeutic agents. In addition, a related series of compounds with phthalocyanines as the photosensitizing units were also synthesized. Hence this objective has been achieved. We then studied the effects of pH and dithiothreitol or glutathione on the fluorescence intensity and reactive oxygen species generation efficiency of these compounds in phosphate buffered saline (PBS) and inside MCF-7 human breast cancer cells. The results revealed the rate and extent of cleavage of the linkers upon interaction with these stimuli. The activation of fluorescence emission of two of these compounds in tumor-bearing nude mice was also demonstrated. The results showed that these compounds functioned as pH- and/or thiol-responsive activatable photosensitizers. Therefore, the second and third objectives have also been exceedingly achieved. Finally, we also examined the photocytotoxicity of all these conjugates against MCF-7 cells and compared the results with those of some reference compounds. While these conjugates exhibited high in vitro photodynamic activities and dithiothreitol-enhanced photocytotoxicity was observed for the disulfide-linked analogues, the cytotoxicity due to the ferrocenyl chalcone moieties was not significant, preventing the use of these compounds for dual chemo and photodynamic therapy. It was difficult to find a potent antitumor agent which is also strong quencher for DSBDPs and phthalocyanines. As an alternative approach, we prepared another photosensitizer in which a zinc(II) phthalocyanine was substituted with an oxaliplatin derivative via a triethylene glycol chain. The two components worked in a cooperative manner in the antitumor action. The IC50 value of the conjugate against the HT29 human colon adenocarcinoma cells was as low as 0.11 micromolar, which was 5-fold lower than that of the reference compound without the platinum complex. Hence the last objective of this project has also been addressed.
