402211.label: Major findings and research outcome
402211.value: We prepared and spectroscopically characterized three triethylene glycol-substituted DSBDP derivatives which were conjugated with two ferrocenyl moieties via acid-labile ketal and/or thiol-sensitive disulfide linkers (unpublished results). The ferrocenyl units could effectively quench the fluorescence and photosensitizing properties of these compounds by photoinduced electron transfer. Upon interaction with acid or dithiothreitol, the ketal or disulfide linkers of the two symmetrical analogues were cleaved. The separation of the DSBDP core and the ferrocenyl moieties restored the fluorescence and singlet oxygen generation of the former. For the unsymmetrical derivative, which contains both the ketal and disulfide linkers, it could be activated by both stimuli and a greater enhancement could be attained under a more acidic (pH 5.0) and reducing ([dithiothreitol] = 10 mM) environment. The stimuli-responsive effects of these compounds were shown not only in PBS, but also inside MCF-7 cells, both in terms of intracellular fluorescence emission and photocytotoxicity. A related series of compounds in which a silicon(IV) phthalocyanine-based photosensitizer was axially substituted with two ketal and/or disulfide-linked ferrocenyl chalcone moieties were also synthesized (Chem. Commun. 2013, 49, 4274 and J. Med. Chem. 2014, 57, 4088). They exhibited a similar pH and dithiothreitol-responsive behavior in PBS and at the cellular level. For the dual activatable analogue, the fluorescence activation was also demonstrated in tumor-bearing nude mice. Upon illumination, it could also effectively inhibit the growth of tumor. Apart from these smart photosensitizers, we also prepared another simple yet very efficient thiol-responsive photosensitizer in which a zinc(II) phthalocyanine was substituted with a 2,4-dinitrobenzenesulfonyl quencher (Chem. Eur. J. 2014, 20, 6241). Upon interaction with glutathione, the quencher was detached from the phthalocyanine. Its fluoresence emission and singlet oxygen generation were greatly enhanced in PBS and inside MCF-7 cells. The compound could also be activated in term of the fluorescence emission in vivo. To achieve dual chemo and photodynamic therapy, we also synthesized a novel zinc(II) phthalocyanine substituted with an oxaliplatin derivative via a triethylene glycol linker (J. Med. Chem. 2012, 55, 5446). The conjugate showed a cytotoxic effect in the dark due to the cytostatic oxaliplatin moiety and an enhanced cytotoxicity upon illumination due to the photosensitizing phthalocyanine unit. The IC50 value of the conjugate against HT29 cells was as low as 0.11 micromolar, which was 5-fold lower than that of the reference compound without the platinum complex.

402211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
402211.value: This study has shown that photosensitizers can be activated by tumor-associated stimuli, such as acid and glutathione. This can enhance the efficacy of the photodynamic treatment and reduce the undesirable side effects. To achieve better quenching efficiency, the photosensitizing unit and the quencher should be carefully chosen by considering their spectral and redox properties, and linked in proximity. The ferrocenyl DSBDP/phthalocyanine systems developed in this study can be improved further, for example, by shortening the separation between the two components and introducing additional ferrocenyl units. The cleavable linker can also be replaced with a peptide that is specific toward a certain cancer-related protease so that the photosensitizer can be activated in a more specific manner. In addition, a tumor targeting group can also be introduced to further enhance the tumor selectivity of the photosensitizers. It is believed that all these approaches can shed light for further development of smart multifunctional photosensitizers for photodynamic treatment of cancer.

402211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
402211.value: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) has emerged as a promising treatment modality for cancer. It involves the combined action of a photosensitizer, light with appropriate wavelength, and molecular oxygen to generate cytotoxic reactive oxygen species that destroy tumors by multiple mechanisms. The use of “smart” photosensitizers that can only be activated by tumor-associated stimuli can confine the cytotoxic effect at the tumor and spare the normal tissues, thereby improving the therapeutic outcome and reducing undesirable side effects. To this end, we have developed a number of efficient photosensitizers that can be activated by acid or thiols, such as glutathione and dithiothreitol. It has been documented that tumors generally have a lower extracellular pH than normal tissues and glutathione is the most abundant cellular thiol and is often elevated in tumor tissues as compared with normal tissues. The responsive effects, in terms of fluorescence emission and reactive oxygen species generation, are remarkable and can also be observed in tumor-bearing nude mice. It is envisaged that these photosensitizers can serve as lead compounds for further development of advanced therapeutic agents for targeted PDT.

402911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
402911.value: Chemicals related to nucleosides (nucleoside analogs) have received great attention as they show potent biological activities towards infectious viral diseases such as AIDS epidemic. Therefore, the preparations (syntheses) of modified nucleosides for biological evaluation are warranted. One important class of modified nucleosides is carbanucleosides (carbocyclic analogs of nucleosides) which have been developed to be anti-viral agents, e.g. abacavir, an anti-HIV agent and entecavir, an anti-hepatitis B agent. The present proposal describes the construction of novel bicyclic carbanucleosides containing two fused carbocyclic rings. These substances have not been made so far and their antiviral activity has therefore not been investigated. The successful research results will form the basis of a general method for the construction of bicyclic carbanucleosides and will allow the bioactivity of these synthetic chemicals to be studied. In summary, our research results are (a) important for the advancement of the science of synthetic organic chemistry, (b) useful for the chemical industry which may employ our synthetic method for the preparation of bicyclic carbanucleosides of pharmaceutical interest or for other industrial applications, (c) contribution to the discovery of new antiviral agents. Chemical preparation (synthesis) of novel bicyclic carbanucleosides will give substances for biological evaluation as a means of providing new or improved antiviral drugs and novel structure-inhibitory activity relationship. Continued testing of new synthetic compounds that may lead to useful medicines is essential to continuing progress in antiviral chemotherapy and therein lies the significance of this project.

402911.label: Realisation of objectives
402911.value: Two novel types of bicyclic carbanucleosides were proposed to be synthesized, one with a 4-membered ring fused to and the other with a 6-membered ring fused to the core 5-membered carbocycle, a bicyclo[3.2.0]heptane and a bicyclo[4.3.0]nonane, respectively. We had complete success with the syntheses of bicyclo[4.3.0]nonane type and 7 such carbocyclic adenosine nucleosides have been made. Since the bicyclo[4.3.0]nonane skeleton is now available, the corresponding syntheses of 42 carbobicyclic analogues of ribavirin, carbobicyclic triazole nucleosides bearing a bicyclo[4.3.0]nonane framework, were achieved. These works are documented in the 2015 PhD thesis of Li Fanglin. Three more carbocyclic adenosine nucleosides have been constructed and described in the 2016 M. Phil. thesis of Chan Yuk Cheung. The syntheses of bicyclo[3.2.0]heptane bicyclic cabanucleosides posed problems. Construction of the 4-membered ring using [2+2] cycloaddition via photolysis or thermal ketene conditions failed miserably. After a great deal of experimentation, a mixture of inseparable he bicyclo[3.2.0]heptane could only be made in a very low yields and the corresponding carbanucleosides are still elusive. More time and efforts are needed to modify the structure of the starting di-alkene for photolysis or thermolysis in order to facilitate [2+2] cycloaddition. We have had problems with biological evaluation. The Co-I lost our compounds forced us to ask Prof. Paul Chan to help us out and to do the testings. However, due to limited resources, only one virus Coxsackievirus B3 has been used for the bio-evaluation. Since the bio-assays of the synthetic bicyclic carbanucleosides have not been thoroughly performed, we are reluctant to publish these materials because publication will prevent us from patenting. Time is required to bio-evaluate our synthetic nucleosides thoroughly which leads to a low publication of only two papers. The project is still in progress. When extensive bio-evaluation of the synthetic carbanucleosides is complete, we will decide whether to patent or to publish our findings.

402911.value: We had complete success with the syntheses of bicyclo[4.3.0]nonane type and 10 such carbocyclic adenosine nucleosides have been made. On the basis of ready availability of bicyclo[4.3.0]nonane skeleton, the corresponding syntheses of 42 carbobicyclic analogues of ribavirin, the triazoles, were achieved. The carbocyclic adenosine nucleosides show insignificant antiviral properties, whereas 3 carbobicyclic triazole nucleosides bearing a bicyclo[4.3.0]nonane framework (carbobicyclic analogues of ribavirin), showed interesting anti-viral activity against one virus, Coxsackievirus B3. However, their cytotoxicity against normal cells caused concerns and diminishes its potential development into useful medicines. More publications on the carbocyclic adenosine nucleosides and the corresponding triazoles are anticipated when their bio-evaluation on other viruses is completed.

402911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
402911.value: The antiviral properties of all the synthesized bicyclo[4.3.0]nonane type carbocyclic nucleosides and their corresponding triazoles have not been thoroughly explored. They require further tests against other viruses since at the moment only one Coxsackievirus B3 was used. The potential use of these compounds as antiviral agents awaits investigation. Cytotoxicity is a major concern. Structure modification of the potent compounds to tune down the cyctotoxicity will be the future work. The project is still in progress. Publication or patent of research results will be implemented when the bio-evaluation of the target molecules is completed.

402911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
402911.value: Chemicals related to nucleosides (nucleoside analogs) have shown potent biological activities towards infectious viral diseases such as AIDS epidemic. In this research, the preparations (syntheses) of new nucleosides as carbanucleosides (carbocyclic analogs of nucleosides) and triazoles (ribavirin aanalogs) were achieved and their biological evaluation on one virus was performed. However, further bio-assays against other viruses are warranted in order to explore their therapeutic potential. Three triazoles demonstrated interesting antiviral properties, but they are toxic to normal cells. Further chemical preparation (synthesis) of these compounds will give substances for biological evaluation as a means of providing improved or non-toxiic antiviral drugs and novel structure-inhibitory activity relationship. Continued testing of new synthetic compounds that may lead to useful medicines is essential to continuing progress in antiviral chemotherapy and therein lies the significance of this project.

403011.label: Project Objectives
403011.value: Structure of Kähler manifolds : to study the Kähler-Ricci flow and complex Monge-Ampère equation on complete noncompact Kähler manifoläd with nonnegative curvature in order to understand problems related to the uniformization conjecture of Yau on complete noncompact Kähler manifolds with positive holomorphic bisectional curvature. To study some problems on the structure Kähler manifolds with nonpositive curvature. Quasi local mass and geometry of compact manifolds with boundary: to study properties of, and relations between, different kinds of notions of quasi local mass, e.g. the relations between Brown-York mass and Wang-Yau mass and asymptotically behavior of certain quasi local mass quantities and to study relations between scalar curvature and other geometric properties, e.g. volume, mean curvature of the boundary of compact manifolds.

To study some problems on the structure Kähler manifolds with nonpositive curvature.

403011.label: Realisation of objectives
403011.value: For the first objective: With the collaboration of Chau, Ni, Fan, Yu, and Huang, the PI has been able (i) to obtain necessary and sufficient conditions of Kähler C-spaces to have nonnegative quadratic orthogonal bisectional curvature; (ii) to construct U(n) invariant Kähler-Ricci flow with initial data on C^n without assuming the curvature is bounded; (iii) to understand U(n) invariant Kähler-Ricci flow with initial data on C^n and quadratic orthogonal bisectional curvature; (iv) to solve the Ponicaré-Lelong equation with optimal condition which is related to a gap phenomena on noncompact Kähler with nonnegative curvature; (v) to understand product of almost Hermitian manifolds and Hermitian metrics with negative curvature. For the second objective: With the collaboration of Miao, Cox, Jauregui, Chan, the PI has been able (i) to compare Wang-Yau quasilocal mass and Brown-York quasi-local mass for large spheres in asymptotically manifold and for small spheres on three manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature; (ii) to solve some scalar rigidity problems on compact manifolds with boundary in terms of the scalar curvature, the mean curvature at the boundary and in some cases with volume constraints; (iii) to understand the problem finding a compact three manifold with boundary so that the boundary is given and mean curvature function is prescribed, which is related to the study of Bartnik quasi-local mass; (iv) to derive a formula for ADM mass in terms of Ricci tensor using elementary method; (v) to provide examples which clarify the question whether the center of mass in well-defined in asymptotically Schawarzschild space. In addition Fan, Yu and the PI has studied the Steklov eigenvalue. I think the objectives have been achieved.

403011.label: Major findings and research outcome
403011.value: (a) In [5], Chau and the PI give necessary and sufficient conditions for an irreducible Kähler C-space with second betti number equal to 1 to have nonnegative or positive quadratic bisectional curvature, including all classical cases and exceptional cases. (b) In [9], [10] Chau, Li, Huang and the PI (i) produce solutions to the Kähler-Ricci flow with complete initial C^0 Hermitian metrics, without the assumption of bounded curvature, and for U(n) invariant Kähler metrics on C^n with non-negative or non-positive holomorphic bisectional; (ii) show that the nonnegativity of quadratic orthogonal bisectional curvature is preserved under the Kähler-Ricci flow of U(n)-invariant metrics on C^n with bounded curvature. (c) In [7], Ni and the PI solve the Ponicaré-Lelong for (1,1)-forms on complete noncompact Kähler manifold, which is optimal for manifolds with nonnegative bisectional curvature, and give an alternate proof of a gap theorem of Ni. (d) In [2], Fan, Yu and the PI prove the nonexistence of almost Hermitians complete metrics with negative curvature on the product of two manifolds under some growth restriction on curvatures. (e) In [1], [3] Cox, Miao and the PI (i) give a better estimate than known results on the bound of radii of geodesic balls being locally rigid; (ii) prove Min-Oo's conjecture for upper hemisphere under an additional condition on volume, without which the conjecture is false. (f) In [4], [6] Jauregui, Miao and the PI (i) prove that Brwon-York mass is a local minimum of the Wang-Yau mass for large spheres and for small spheres under reasonable assumptions; (ii) obtain some extensions results related to Bartnik quasilocal mass. (g) In [12], [13] Chan, Miao and the PI (i) derive the formula for ADM mass and the center of mass in terms of Ricci tensor for asymptotically flat manifolds; (ii) give necessary and sufficient conditions so that the center of mass is well-defined; (iii) construct counter-examples with positive scalar curvature to a well-known result of Huisken-Yau. (h) In [8], Miao and the PI prove that a complete static metric on a simply connected AF manifold is flat in dimension 3. (i) In [11], Fan, Yu and Tam study the Steklov eigenvalues on annuli which are related to the study of minimal surfaces.

403011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403011.value: It is interesting to understand more on the existence and properties of Kähler-Ricci flow on noncompact complete Kähler manifolds without assuming the curvature is bounded. Short time existence of such a flow is basically solved for U(n) invariant metric on C^n. One would like to study questions on long time existence and on convergence. There are known results on existence of Ricci flow on noncompact Riemannian manifolds without assuming the curvature is bounded. The question is whether similar results are true for Kähler-Ricci flow. The problem of preservation of nonnegative orthogonal bisectional curvature is still open, except in the case of U(n)-invariant solution with bounded curvature. There are counter examples to a conjecture of Min-Oo on the rigidity of standard upper hemisphere. If the geodesic balls are small enough, then one can formulate and prove a local rigidity result. One question is whether one has global rigidity if the geodesic balls are small enough. In some case, we know that Brown-York mass is local minimum of the Wang-Yau mass. But it is unclear if it is a global minimum. One would like to prove that static asymptotically flat end must have zero mass, using elementary methods.

403011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403011.value: There is no way to put the unit disk in the plane in such a correspondence to the whole plane which preserves angles. Part of this project is to study relations between this phenomena for higher dimensional `surfaces’. One way to study this is to under the dynamics of the geometry of ‘surfaces’ . That is, by change the way to measure the length while keeping the so-called complex structure the same and to see if ultimately the structure of the `surfaces’ will be clear. When one rides a bus, and the bus suddenly stops, then one may fall forward as if there is a `gravitational’ force from the front part of the bus. So one cannot distinguish between gravitation and acceleration (or deceleration) if we only confine to small region. However, gravitation is real. So, people want to measure the total energy of a bounded region—quasi-local energy. In this project, some relations between them have been found. It turns out the study of quasi-local energy is closely related to the study the geometry of bounded regions with boundary. In this project, some results in this direction are obtained.

403111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
403111.value: 相互作用是量子气体研究中最重要的参数。通过不同的方式控制相互作用，以调控量子气体的特性，是量子气体领域的一个研究重点。超冷极性分子具有长程，各向异性并可操控的电偶极相互作用，这种相互作用和原子间的接触相互作用是完全不同的，因此超冷分子的获得成为了最近的一个研究热点。很多理论工作已经预言了，利用具有偶极相互作用的量子气体，可以观察到很多原子气体中没有的奇异现象。为了充分的研究量子气体的偶极特性，必须使偶极作用比其他的效应更强，这就需要制备高密度，超冷温度并有大电偶级矩的分子样品。 在过去的三年中，本主要研究者在科罗拉多大学的JILA研究所工作，我们发展了一套制备，探测和操控高相空间密度的超冷极性40K87Rb分子的方法。针对其后的研究中发现的40K87Rb分子由于超冷化学反应而导致的分子寿命过短，以及40K87Rb电偶极矩较小等问题，我们在这里提出制备23Na87Rb分子以克服这些困难。依据J. Hutson小组的计算，23Na87Rb分子没有双分子间的化学反应，因而更适宜用来进行有强偶极相互作用的量子气体的研究。 本项目将用激光冷却的Na和Rb原子展开，通过光阱中的蒸发冷却，我们可以获得超冷（～100 nK）的温度；通过外加磁场引起的Feshbach共振，Na和Rb的原子对首先形成弱束缚的Feshbach分子；再通过受激拉曼过程实现分子到最低能态的转移。在最低能态，NaRb分子有一个大的电偶极矩(> 3 Debye)和长的寿命。 本项目的长期影响在于有偶极作用的量子气体可以被用来进行量子相变的研究。这些相变通常发生于固态物质系统中，利用量子气体体系的完全可调控性，可以对它们进行更干净的研究。超冷分子也可以用来进行量子信息处理，可以用来研究受控的超冷化学反应，很多其他的非弹性极性碰撞也可以用NaRb分子展开。

403111.label: Realisation of objectives
403111.value: Our research progress since the starting date of this grant followed closely to our plan. The majority of the revised objectives were addressed. As the amount of fund is only half of what we requested, some of the original objectives, especially the investigation of ground-state molecule production, were postponed. They were only realized in late 2015, with the help of other funds, nearly a year after the completion date of this grant. We already had a basic setup before the starting date of this grant. With the help of this grant, we further optimized this system and produced the 1st Bose-Einstein condensate of our lab in April 11, 2012. The double BEC of Na and Rb were also produced in December 2012. We wrote a paper on the double BEC production, which is now in press in Journal of Physics B. Before achieving the double BEC, we also investigated the Feshbach resonances between Na and Rb with an ultracold thermal mixture. We found several broad s-wave resonances at very convenient field. With theoretical support from Dr. E. Tiemann from Hannover, we were able to fully understand our results. This result is published in Phy. Rev. A as a Rapid Communication. The s-wave resonance at 347.8 Gauss for atoms in their lowest hyperfine level is selected for molecule creation. We use the normal field ramping method for molecule association. The residual atom removal is realized with a strong magnetic field gradient, taking advantage of the small magnetic dipole moment of the Feshbach molecules. It took us half a year to confirm the existence of Feshbach molecules. The molecule to atom conversion efficiency is still low, despite lots of investigations. This is mainly limited by the atom-molecule collisions as it takes time to remove the high density residual atoms. We also investigated some basic properties of the molecules and found they are mainly of closed channel character. A paper on this result is published in New Journal of Physics. Starting from Feshbach molecules, the molecular transition strengths can be greatly enhanced so that small power external cavity diode lasers are enough. We thoroughly studied the excited state spectroscopy in this way and found the best level for Raman transfer. With two photon spectroscopy, we also found the ground-state level. We are setting up the narrow linewidth lasers and trying the STIRAP now.

403111.label: Major findings and research outcome
403111.value: 1. Achieved the first Bose Einstein condensate of Hong Kong with Rb87 atom. We achieved this in a hybrid quadruple+optical trap. 2. Produced the world's first and so far only Double BEC of Na and Rb. This is achieved by sympathetically cooling in a hybrid quadruple+optical trap. 3. Investigated Feshbach resonance between Na and Rb atoms. Both s-wave and p-wave resonances are observed and the collision between Na and Rb is now fully understood. 4. Produced a pure Feshbach molecule sample of NaRb. We also studied basic properties of these molecues. 5. One-photon and two-photon spectroscopy for population transfer to the ground state.

403111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403111.value: We will continue work on realizing ground-state molecule production with Stimulated Raman population transfer of Feshbach molecules. Once this is achieved, we will try to improve the number of molecules and study collisions between them. If they are stable and long lived, we will then try evaporative cooling to reach quantum degeneracy. If they are not, then we will have to apply the optical lattices to isolate them. Further ahead, we will investigate collision with various loss channels including hyperfine exchange, rotational quenching, vibrational quenching and chemical reaction. These investigations will be built on our ability of controlling the internal state of the molecules. The most exciting direction is with the dipolar physics. NaRb has a large permanent electric dipole moment, which will allow us to enter the true long-range interaction regime. This effect can be studied with a thermal gas as well as with a degenerated molecular gas.

403111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403111.value: At a temperature near absolute zero, the behavior of a dilute sample of atoms is govern by the particle's quantum nature. In such a regime, the effect of interaction becomes really pronounce. A prominent manifestation of this is the superfluity behavior of atomic Bose-Einstein condensates as a result of the weak short-range van der Waals atom-atom interactions. Even more fascinating phenomena can be explored if the interaction strength and range can be increased. This can be achieved with heteronuclear molecules, which can have a large electric dipole moment and thus provide long-range and strong dipole-dipole interactions. In the current work, we are trying to addresses this possibility by producing a sample of ultracold bosonic NaRb molecules. As direct cooling of molecules is not possible, to achieve this, we start instead from a mixture of ultracold Na and Rb atoms. The plan is to first associate pairs of Na and Rb into weakly bound Feshbach molecules and then transfer them into the deeply bound levels. Up to now, we already finished several key steps toward this goal including the preparation of the mixture, the production of NaRb Feshbach molecules and the molecular spectroscopy investigation.

403211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
403211.value: The aim of this proposal is to develop a new heating platform for the use in microfluidic chips. Microfluidic chips, which are capable of manipulating and analyzing fluids in microchannels, have been heralded as a revolutionary technology in laboratory experimentation. They can offer the benefits of miniaturization, integration, and automation to research and diagnostics industries. Envisioned applications range from nanomaterials synthesis, bioanalysis, point-of-care diagnostics to drug discovery. In many of these applications, temperature control plays a critical role in the overall chip performance. Moreover, localized temperature gradients can generate thermocapillary driving forces to guide fluid flow and move droplets. So far, on-chip heating has relied mainly on resistive and optical means. The use of resistance elements and necessary wiring increases the complexity of microchip fabrication. Effective heating also requires resistance elements to be millimeter-sized or larger. The optical means can allow for localized thermal control, but strongly light-absorbing materials are often needed. The use of these materials introduces additional fabrication steps and often interferes with on-chip optical analyses. Here we propose to develop a simple and efficient, plasmon-based photothermal heating method for the use on microfluidic chips. Plasmonic gold nanocrystals will be embedded inside poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS), attached on PDMS microchannel walls, or suspended in fluids. When they are resonantly excited, gold nanocrystals can convert the light into heat at efficiencies up to 100% to raise the local temperature around them. Moreover, the photothermal conversion wavelength can be synthetically tailored. We will develop methods to measure the temperature and temperature distribution in microfluidic channels by using either patterned Pt microwires or colloidal upconversion nanocrystals. Various parameters will be studied to understand the photothermal heating and thermal dissipation processes for the three incorporation manners of Au nanocrystals (in PDMS, on the walls, and in fluids), and optimize the heating performance in terms of both the heating rate and temperature distribution. We will further demonstrate the drive of liquid flow and droplet movement in microfluidic channels with controlled speeds and paths. There are currently more than 100 companies working on microfluidics. Most of them focus primarily on bioanalytical and medical diagnostic applications. Our studies will lead to the development of simple, low-cost, and highly efficient photothermal heating on microfluidic chips. We believe that the success of this proposal will undoubtedly help Hong Kong to gain a foothold in the fast growing lab-on-a-chip technology and its commercialization. 这份研究计划的目的在于为微流芯片开发一种全新的微型加热控制平台。 微流芯片可以被用来操纵和分析微米尺寸空腔里面的微量流体。作为一种崭新的技术，微流芯片可以实现样品处理的小型化和集成化，并且为研究和诊断行业中的自动化铺平道路。其潜在的应用范围涵盖了纳米材料合成、生物分析、护理诊断和药物开发等领域。在很多应用中，微流芯片上的加热和温度控制起着关键的作用，往往能够对整个芯片的性能产生重大影响。局部的温度梯度还可以产生毛细驱动力，这种热致的驱动力可以用来引导微流腔内的流体流动，从而操纵液滴或气泡。目前，微流芯片上的加热控制主要是通过电阻加热和光学加热来实现。对前者而言，电阻元件的集成和布线使得芯片的制造更加复杂；此外，由于能提供有效加热的电阻元件一般在毫米大小，很难实现微米级的局域加热控制。相比之下，光学加热手段可以方便地实现局部的温度控制，但往往需要强吸光材料。吸光材料的使用需要额外的加工工艺，并对样品的光学分析带来干扰。 鉴于以上诸点，我们提出了一种简单有效的微流芯片加热方法，这种方法是基于表面等离子体共振的光热转换效应，能够有效地解决传统加热方法的不足。纳米金颗粒具有表面等离子体共振效应，在共振激发时，纳米金具有高达100%的光热转换效率。为利用这一性质以及考虑不同的应用需求，我们将通过如下三种方法将金纳米颗粒和微流芯片结合起来：1）将金纳米颗粒嵌入到制备微流芯片的聚合物材料中；2）将金纳米颗粒附着到微流通道的管壁上；3）直接将金纳米颗粒分散到流体中。由于我们已经可以制备不同的金纳米颗粒来实现不同的表面等离子体共振波长，我们可以设计工作在不同吸收波长的微流芯片光加热平台，从而避开样品光学分析的波长区间。这种加热方法一方面保留了传统光加热方法的优点，另一方面又尽可能少地牺牲微流芯片本身的优良特性。在本研究计划中，我们还将发展新的方法来测量微流芯片中的温度及其空间分布。这一微米级别的温度测量将通过微米尺寸的铂电阻丝温度计或是基于上转换稀土纳米颗粒的荧光温度计来实现。我们还将对各种系统参数进行研究，详细分析对应三种金纳米颗粒引入方式的光热转换性能和微流控芯片上的散热过程，从而从升温效率和温度场空间分布两方面来优化芯片上的加热性能。更进一步，我们将设计基于此种加热方法的微流芯片中的微量液体驱动和液滴运动控制技术。 目前国际上有超过100家的商业公司在开发和应用微流芯片技术，并提供相关的服务。它们中的大部分都是面向生物分析和医疗诊断方面的应用。我们的研究将使微流芯片上的加热和温度控制变得结构更加简单，成本更加低廉，光热效率更加高效。这项研究计划的成功无疑将有助于香港在迅猛发展的微流芯片技术及其商业化的过程中占有一席之地。

403211.label: Realisation of objectives
403211.value: (1) Methods were successfully developed for embedding gold nanocrystals into PDMS, onto the surface of PDMS, and dispersing gold nanocrystals in solutions for plasmonic photothermal studies and applications. We also realized 'ship-in-a-bottle' growth of various metal nanocrystals by use of hollow mesoporous silica microspheres as microscale fluidic containers. The inner volume of these containers is on the order of femto-litre. The confined metal nanocrystals can function as semi-homogeneous catalysts with largely improved recyclability. Moreover, we immersed gold nanorods in agar hydrogel and demonstrated silver coating on gold nanorods at different temperatures and with different weak acids. The distinct color change induced by silver coating was demonstrated to function as time-temperature indicators for perishable products, such as milk, meat and medicine. (2) A method for measuring the temperatures and temperature distributions in microfluidic channels was developed on the basis of fluorescence intensity reduction of organic dye molecules with increasing temperatures. An analytic equation was first obtained. The temperatures inside microfluidic channels were then determined according to the pre-calibrated equation by measuring the fluorescence intensity. (3) The temperature measurement method was applied to microfluidic chips that were made of PDMS containing gold nanocrystals by adding fluorescent dye molecules in liquids in the microfluidic channels. (4) Upon plasmon excitation with a laser, the liquid in the microfluidic channel was heated through plasmonic photothermal conversion. The temperature rise and drop were studied when the laser was turned on and off. In this way, the factors affecting the plasmonic photothermal conversion efficiencies and performance were investigated. We also compared the photothermal conversion performances among plasmonic gold nanocrystals, carbon black, semiconductor nanocrystals and organic dyes. (5) Optofluidic switching on gold nanocrystal/PDMS microfluidic chips was realized by adding a thermorheological fluid in a T-shaped channel. A thermoreversible gelation polymer, (ethylene oxide)106-(propylene oxide)70-(ethylene oxide)106 triblock copolymer (F127), was chosen as the thermorheological fluid. The gelation temperature of aqueous F127 solutions can be varied by changing the polymer concentration. Above the gelation temperature, the solution exhibits a sol-to-gel transition. The gelated solution can block the fluid flow in the channel. The flow switching can be realized anywhere along the channel. We also fabricated microfluidic chips and studied the sulfidation behavior of silver nanocubes by embedding silver nanocubes in microfluidic channels and recording their scattering spectra as a function of the reaction time.

403211.label: Major findings and research outcome
403211.value: (1) We prepared gold nanocrystal/PDMS composites by uniformly dispersing gold nanocrystals in PDMS and demonstrated fast and localized heating on the microfluidic chips made out of the composites. An optically controlled fluid flow switch with fast and reversible switching was realized with the hybrid composite. This work was published on Advanced Materials. (2) We studied and compared the photothermal conversion performances of different materials at the same mass concentrations. Both the mass-normalized extinction cross-section and the photothermal conversion efficiency of gold nanocrystals decrease as their size is increased. The photothermal conversion performance of carbon black is comparable to that of relatively small gold nanocrystals, while the photothermal conversion performance of organic dyes and PbS nanocrystals is inferior to that of gold nanocrystals. These results were published on The Journal of Physical Chemistry C. (3) We developed methods for the growths of many different bimetallic nanocrystals in both macroscopic and microscopic containers, observed the plasmonic percolation behavior of bimetallic nanocrystals, and studied the recyclability of the metal nanocrystals confined within microscopic containers. These works were published on Nanoscale, Advanced Functional Materials and ACS Nano. (4) We studied the structural and plasmonic evolutions during the sulfidation process of silver nanocubes at both the ensemble and single-particle levels, for which silver nanocubes were dispersed in bulk solutions and deposited on microfluidic chips, respectively. The sulfidation process and the associated plasmonic changes were understood clearly. We studied the effects of temperature and weak acids on the sharp-contrast color change brought by silver coating on gold nanorods. The coating reaction was immobilized successfully in agar hydrogel, which led to the demonstration of time-temperature indicators for advanced quality control and assessment of perishable products. These works were published in two ACS Nano papers. (5) We unified the two types of coupling behaviors between plasmonic metal nanocrystals and organic dyes, that is, plasmonic splitting and energy transfer, which are commonly manifested in experiments as peak splitting and a quenching dip, respectively. We also studied the plasmonic effect on the Förster energy transfer process by embedding donor and acceptor dye molecules in the silica shell that was coated on gold nanorods. These two works were published both on The Journal of Physical Chemistry C. Moreover, we prepared a comprehensive review article on the recent developments, including the works of both our own and others, in colloidal plasmonic metal nanocrystals. This review article was published on Chemical Society Reviews.

403211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403211.value: Plasmonic metal nanoparticles possess extremely large absorption/scattering cross-sections per particle at their plasmon resonance wavelengths. Their plasmon wavelengths can be synthetically tailored from the visible to infrared region. Moreover, their absorption can be tuned or maximized according to specific needs. Over the last two decades, the field of plasmonics has undergone tremendous progresses in the synthesis and fabrication of an enormous number of noble metal nanoparticles. These progresses have provided unlimited ability to control the plasmon wavelengths and absorption cross-sections of metal nanoparticles. On the basis of this ability, I believe that there are two future directions for the method developed in this project for uniformly dispersing metal nanoparticles in PDMS. The first is to apply our technique to analytical and sensing problems in life sciences and medical diagnostics. Many reactions for sensing and detection require fine control of temperature and/or local heating. Our method is particularly suitable for local heating, which is compatible with the goal of microfluidics. The second is to apply plasmonic photothermal conversion to other materials or technologies, such as thermochromism and local vaporization, where precise temporal and spatial temperature control is required or beneficial.

403211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403211.value: A strong motivation for the research in microfluidics is to develop low-cost, reliable point-of-care diagnostic devices for use in under-developed and remote regions on the world. For many sensing reactions in medical diagnostics, such as DNA denaturation and renaturation, precise control of temperature both temporally and spatially is very important. On microfluidic chips, such control is especially preferential, because a number of units that perform different separation and analysis functions are integrated in microscopic surface areas or volumes. These units need to function at different temperatures or profiles. With our heating method developed in this project, fine temporal and spatial temperature control can be readily realized. Moreover, because of the large interacting capability of plasmonic metal nanoparticles with light, our approach can even potentially eliminate the use of lasers or any light sources. Sunlight can be directly employed by use of focusing lenses. This is especially attractive, since electricity might even be problematic in under-developed or remote regions. On the other hand, noble metals are generally thought to be expensive. Considering their extremely large absorption cross-sections, only a small amount of noble metal nanoparticles in our method. Therefore the cost associated with noble metal nanoparticles will not be a problem.

403311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
403311.value: Pseudogap is a gap-like feature appearing in an energy spectrum. In high temperature superconductors (HTS), the pseudogap near the Fermi level occurring at temperatures higher than the superconductivity transition temperature has attracted great attention and was one of the hot topics in HTS. While its origin is still in debate, it is often believed to be essential for the understanding of high-Tc superconductivity. The pseudogap state has not been observed in conventional bulk superconductors. However, we have recently discovered such pseudogap state in thin Pb films/islands, the bulk of which is a conventional superconductor. In another nanostructured conventional superconductor, namely 2 dimensional (2D) TiN film, a French research group has independently observed the pseudogap state. These results stimulate our interest to propose this project. The aim of this project is to uncover the formation mechanism of the novel pseudogap state in metallic nanostructures through a set of experiments designed to reveal the various influence factors including geometric and material properties. We propose experimental studies to investigate i) geometric effects on the pseudogap of Pb islands from lateral size, vertical size and interface; ii) material effects on the pseudogap by varying the electron-phonon coupling strength. For the latter, the existence of pseudogap in Ag, Al, and In thin islands will be explored. Through the experiments we proposed, we will find out the generality of the pseudogap state; we will consolidate or modify the previous models or mechanisms proposed to explain the formation of pseudogap in the nanostructures of conventional superconductors with a more complete set of information on various aspects of the pseudogap. We hope our findings can shed light on the understanding of pseudogap phase in HTS. 赝能隙是能谱中出现的一个类似能隙的现象，通常是指当高温超导体的温度高于其超导转变温度，在其费米面附近出现的异常结构。赝能隙吸引了广大物理研究者的关注，并且成为高温超导体研究的热点之一。虽然其产生原理仍然不清楚，但是广泛认为对赝能隙的理解将会是解释高温超现象的重要基础。赝能隙态在宏观的块状常规超导体里是不存在的。然而，我们此前的发现表明典型的常规超导体铅的纳米薄膜或纳米岛当中却存在类似与高温超导体赝能隙的态。在另一种2维薄膜纳米结构的常规超导体氮化钛中，一个法国的研究组也发现了类似的赝能隙态。这些结果表明赝能隙态有可能广泛存在于常规超导体的特殊纳米结构中，这是我们提出这项研究计划的动机。 这项研究项目的目的是通过一系列实验来研究这种新赝能隙态的产生机制。这些研究将包括铅纳米岛几何构型对赝能隙的影响；不同种材料构成的岛对赝能隙的影响等方面。 其中铅岛几何结构效应的研究将包括改变铅岛横向尺寸、厚度、铅与衬底之间的界面结构等观察赝能隙的相应变化。通过这种对赝能隙更加全面的了解来巩固或者修改我们之前提出的赝能隙形成机理，并解释常规超导体纳米结构中赝能隙态存在的根源。另一方面，不同材料会有不同的电子-声子相互作用强度，根据我们之前提出的观点这种相互作用会直接影响到赝能隙的表现。因此我们将选择银，铝和铟的纳米岛来进行对比研究。通过对比实验，我们可以了解这种赝能隙是否广泛存在于常规超导体甚至普通金属的纳米结构当中，进而理解其产生机制。希望我们的结果可以对高温超导体中的赝能隙态的理解有所帮助。

403311.label: Realisation of objectives
403311.value: The objectives of this proposal have been reasonably achieved. The properties of pseudogap state in metal islands have been investigated through a number of experiments. The physical mechanism of the novel pseudogap state is now clear. The lateral and vertical size effect of pseudogap state in Pb islands on Si(111) surfaces have been studied on a number of 8ML and 9ML Pb islands grown on Si(111) surfaces. With high energy resolution scanning tunneling spectroscopy, their superconducting transition temperatures are measured. By fitting the experimental dI/dV data, a critical region in superconductivity was observed together with the special temperature-dependent behavior of pseudogap states. To study the interface effect, we have tried to grow metal islands on different pre-treated substrates. However, most of the substrates are not good conductors at low temperature (4.5K), which is essential for the study of pseudogap state near Fermi level, including In and Al wetting layers. In this case, an alternative method was used to study the interface effect. A 4ML Al film was prepared before the growth of Al islands. Although Al is frequently used for ohmic contact with silicon, the Al/Si(111) interface shows a electron barrier. To understand this phenomena, we have studied the tip/silicon contact by allowing the metallic tip to penetrate a Si(111) sample at 5 K. A transition from rectifying to ohmic behavior was observed. The Al/Si interface was found to greatly enhance the pseudogap state. To study the pseudogap on In islands, another attempt has been used to overcome the conductivity problem. A Pb wetting layer is grown on the silicon surface prior to the growth of In islands. The observations of the pseudogap states in the dI/dV spectrum taken on Al and In islands provides clear clues on the formation mechanism of the pseudogap state. On the way to study Ag islands, the conduction problem and the strong surface states prevent us in getting valuable results on the pseudogap state. We then extended our studies to Ag clusters and Co atoms adsorbed on Si(111) surface. These studies also provide some valuable results. By analyzing the former experimental results, it is now clear that the interplay between the quantum confinement and the electron-phonon interaction is responsible for the formation of the pseudogap state while the co-existence of the dynamic Coulomb blockade effect induces the size dependence.

403311.label: Major findings and research outcome
403311.value: With high energy resolution scanning tunneling spectroscopy, the superconducting transition temperatures of 8 and 9 ML thick Pb islands was found to follow the same trend of gradual suppression when decreasing the island lateral sizes, despite their different density of states (DOS) at Fermi level. A critical region in superconductivity that originates from fluctuations was observed. The pseudogap state was found to follow a temperature dependent behavior when the temperature is higher than the superconducting transition temperature Tc, while it becomes temperature independent (or weak dependent) when the temperature is lower than Tc. (Publication 1). Further studies on In, and Al flat top islands grown on Si(111) surfaces indicate that the pseudogap (or pseudopeak in special cases) is a universal state in all the metal islands as long as the quantum confinement exists. The width of the pseudogap state on large islands shows a linear dependence on the width of the Debye window. Al has the widest Debye window and hence a widest pseudogap. The electron barrier in the interface, which is known to play an important role in the forming of quantum well state, is found to also affect the depth of the pseudogap state. Based on the former results, a clear conclusion can be made that the interplay between the quantum confinement and the electron-phonon interaction is responsible for the formation of the pseudogap state. For a given temperature, as the lateral size of Pb islands decreases, the width of the pseudogap is observed to increase. This is explained as the co-existence of the dynamic coulomb blockade effect in these islands. These results have settled the dispute of the generation mechanism of pseudogap state on such systems (Publication 6, in preparation). By studying the tip-silicon contact, a transition from rectifying to ohmic behavior between the metal tip and the Si(111) sample was found. The result suggests that the Schottky barrier height can be affected by the doping concentration in the semiconductor. (Publication 4) Extended studies on the Ag clusters grown on Si(111) have broadened the concept of “magic cluster”. Studies on the thermal motion of Ag atom in the vicinity of Ag clusters reveals the Friedel oscillatory interaction between Ag atoms and Ag clusters (Publications 2and3, under review). By using the atomic manipulation technique, we have demonstrated the ability to fully control both the position and magnetic state of single Co atoms (Publication 5, under review).

403311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403311.value: The following directions can be further developed in the future. One is to explore the enhancement methods of this novel pseudogap/pseudopeak state and the other is to explore its applications. Since the existence of pseudogap/pseudopeak further modifies the density of state of the metal films/islands in addition to the quantum confinements, it will further modify the physical and chemical properties of the films/islands. However, the observed pseudogap/pseudopeak is relatively weak that is insufficient to cause strong effects. The recent results on Al islands show an enhancement caused by the interface. This provides a clue that by modifying the interface as well as the surface, this pseudogap/pseudopeak state is possible to be further enhanced. The STM technique that requires conduction on both surface and back contact may not be a good method in these studies. Photo spectroscopic techniques will be considered.

403311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403311.value: Electron density of state (DOS) near Fermi level dominates the physical and chemical properties of a material. Any physical phenomenon that modifies the DOS near Fermi level is worth studying since its mechanism may provide new directions in developing functional materials. The recently observed pseudogap state in Pb thin films is such a new physical phenomenon. To understand this physical phenomenon, several mechanisms have been proposed and dispute aroused. In this project, we have demonstrated that the interaction between electron and phonon together with the quantum confinement effect which is caused by the reducing of the material size are responsible for the appearance of the pseudogap state, while the co-existence of a dynamic Coulomb blockade effect explains the size dependency. Through the works accomplished in this project, we have provided a clear explanation to the novel pseudogap state and settled the dispute on the formation mechanism.

403411.label: Project Title(Chinese)
403411.value: Allen-Cahn方程的行波解以及拋物De Giorgi猜測

403411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
403411.value: The celebrated De Giorgi Conjecture provides an intricate relation between the study of semilinear elliptic equation and the theory of minimal surfaces. Over the last twenty years, the De Giorgi Conjecture has been (almost) completely solved: the critical dimension turns out to be eight. Below night, positive answers are due to Ghoussoub-Gui 91998), Ambrosio-Cabre (2000) and Savin 92006). Above eight, del Pino, Kowalczyk and the PI (2008) have constructed counterexamples, using the newly developed infinite dimensional reduction method. In this proposal, we consider the parabolic version of De Giorgi Conjecture on traveling waves. This case turns out to be considerably harder, since there are nontrivial axially symmetric solutions (constructed by Chen-Guo-Hamel-Ninomiya-Roquejofre (2007)). The corresponding parabolic Bernstein conjecture has not been completely solved yet. It remains a mystery what the critical dimension is. The main objective of this proposal is to further develop the parabolic version of infinite dimensional reduction method, and to find non-cylinderically traveling solitons for the mean curvature flows as well as traveling solutions for the Allen-Cahn type equations. We shall also consider the corresponding vectorial Allen-cahn type equations (which becomes Gross-Pitaevskii equation). Our goal is to use the infinite dimensional reduction method to establish the relation between self-translating surfaces in the mean curvature flows and the traveling wave solutions of Allen-cahn. Our ultimate goal is to solve completely the parabolic Bernstein conjecture and the parabolic De Giorgi Conjecture. The study of these conjecture involves techniques from geometric analysis, nonlinear PDEs, nonlinear functional analysis, dynamical systems, variational methods, etc. Conversely, the ideas and techniques in solving these conjecture will have direct impacts in these fields as well. 本計劃的目的是要研究拋物Allen-Cahn的恒常解對於相對應的橢圓情形, De Giorgi猜想已被完全解決(N=2, 由Ghoussoub及Gui解決;N=3, 由Ambrosio-Cabre解決;4<=N<=8,由 Savin解決;N>=9, 由Del Pino, Kowalczyk及Wei解決). 拋物情形更複雜. 首先它有對稱的解, 第二對應的曲率流方程也有非對稱的解. 我們的目的是將橢圓的無窮維的約化方法推廣到拋物情形, 並最終解決對應的Bernstein及De Giogi猜測.

403511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
403511.value: Financial mathematics mainly contributes to the study of derivative valuation, portfolio policies, and risk management. This project focuses on theories, applications and implications of co-integrated asset dynamics to the field of financial mathematics. There is evidence that co-integration exists among international financial indices, among exchange rates, and among oil products. The importance of co-integration has become recognized and has resulted in a Nobel Prize in Economics for Granger in 2003. This project establishes the theory of co-integration option pricing with multiscale stochastic volatility using Fourier analysis. More specifically, the principal investigator (PI) derives conditions for which the characteristic function of the joint asset dynamics can be presented in an exponential affine form. This helps understanding how co-integration relationship is connected to the notion of stochastic convenient yield in futures contracts, and rendering an efficient computation for option prices using Fast Fourier Transform. When the concept of co-integration is applied to mean-variance portfolio selection problems with insurance or financial liabilities, the PI shows that the solution is related to a backward stochastic differential equation which solution can be linked to an exponential affine form as well. As there is empirical evidence that the mortality rates of insurance companies are correlated and co-integrated with the national mortality rate, insurance companies are interested in hedging their mortality risk by national mortality derivatives. This last problem can be solved by combining the aforementioned co-integration derivative pricing method and the co-integration portfolio selection theory. Empirical studies are performed to validate the use of the developed theories and numerical methods. 金融數學主要貢獻於洐生工具定價、投資策略和風險管理。這項目針對共積 (cointegration)在金融數學的各個領域，定立應用及理論基礎。共積是一種常見的經濟現象。無論是金融指數、外匯及石油產品中都可找到數據支持。正因共積在經濟學中的巨大貢獻，創始人 Granger 便籍此獲得2003年的經濟學諾貝爾獎。這項目的目標如下。首先，研究員會建立在共積與多變量波幅模型下的期權定價理論，並利用快速傅利葉轉換 (FFT)建構快速並準確的數值方法計算期權值。其次，建立共積資產投資策略的理論和數學模型。按一般經濟學研究，本項目採用平均報酬 (mean) 及變異數 (variance) 作目標函數。研究員計劃以逆隨機微分方程 (BSDE) 求出其投資策略的解釋解。結合以上理論並推廣至保險業死亡索償的風險管理。研究有效利用國家死亡率及其洐生工具對沖個別保險公司之索償風險。這是基於國家的死亡率往往與個別保險公司客戶的死亡率是共積的。最後，以數據分析核實理論的精確性及其應用性。

403511.label: Realisation of objectives
403511.value: I would like to thank the Research Grants Council of Hong Kong for granting me the research funding. This comprehensive project on the application of cointegration in asset pricing is completed by addressing all project objectives mentioned above. There are a total 13 journal articles generated from this project. In Part C, the research outputs of [1], [3], [4], [8] and [10] are devoted to Objectives 1 and 2. In particular, [1], [3], [4] and [8] develop some preliminary techniques for [10], which is a major representative output for Objectives 1 and 2, and includes a comprehensive empirical study using data from the commodity market. Objective 3 is fully addressed by [7], [11] and [13] in Part C. The article [13] develops all necessary mathematical tools for this purpose and [7] considers stochastic interest rates. Article [11] typically proves the statistical arbitrage with cointegration using the developed mathematical tools. The extension to Objective 4 is done in [2], [5] and [9] of Part C. Article [2] mainly considers the insurance liability and cointegrated assets with utility maximization while [5] uses the backward stochastic differential equation framework to solve the mean-variance ALM problem with cointegration and jumps. Article [9] investigates the cointegration effect in the variance-covariance matrix. Objective 5 is addressed in various different papers including [10]. Numerical simulation is conducted in [11]. The extension to mortality and longevity risk management is documented in [6] and [12]. Using mean-variance portfolio selection concept, the PI considers the minimum- and mean-variance hedges with longevity securities. He considers the time-consistent mean-variance hedging in [6] but precommitment hedging strategy in [12].

403511.label: Major findings and research outcome
403511.value: Major findings include developing real time implementable trading strategies for cointegrated financial assets (see [2], [5], [7], [9], [11] and [13] in Part C), and pricing formulas for derivatives on multiple cointegrated assets (see [1], [3], [4], [8] and [10] in Part C). The procedure of developing trading strategy is also relevant to the development of hedging strategies for the insurance industry as shown in [6] and [12]. Apart from the 13 published academic papers, the results are reported in various international conferences as shown in Part C.

403511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403511.value: The cointegration system considered in project is linear type. My future goal is to extend it to nonlinear cointegration models. For instancet, I am targeting threshold cointegration in my research agenda. I am also working on cointegration with model uncertainty.

403511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403511.value: Cointegration is a statistical concept describing how two or more financial assets are moving together. This concept is different from the conventional correlation in the way that the comovement will converge to the long-term equilibrium. Cointegration resulted in a Nobel Prize in Economics in 2003. This project aims to fully utilize the cointegration technology to advance the algorithmic trading and pricing of financial assets in the practical financial market. It develops trading algorithms, numerical pricing schemes and rigorous scientific justification to the associated applications. In turns, it advances the financial technology (FinTech) by smoothing decisions with cointegrated financial assets. The results obtained from this paper not only benefit the academic development but also have great potential for practical financial implementation.

403611.label: Project Objectives
403611.value: To measure the temperature dependence of the relative contribution of the internal motions of typical polymers in different solvents and locate the maximum or turning temperature (T*) in each case. To investigate the effects of polymer concentration, chain length and polydispersity on T* by using a set of narrowly distributed polystyrenes and their proper mixtures in cyclohexane. To correlate each T* to its corresponding "theta" and to compare these two “ideal” conditions that are respectively determined from dynamic-and-intrachain and static-and-interchain properties. To establish a protocol that will allow us to use dynamic LLS to quickly and conveniently locate the “ideal” state, i.e., the -condition, of a given polymer solution. To formulate a theoretical model to interpret how the relative contribution of the internal motions of a single polymer chain in solution varies when the solvent quality changes. To elucidate theoretically the relationship between the intra-chain and inter-chain second virial coefficients so that we are able to understand how T* is related to "theta".

403611.label: Major findings and research outcome
403611.value: We have confirmed that the relative contribution of the internal motions of polymers in dilute solutions in different solvents has a maximum or turning temperature (T*) that is corresponding to the "theta" (ideal) temperature by comparing the two “ideal” conditions respectively determined from dynamic-and-intra-chain and static-and-inter-chain properties. It should be emphasized that this is one of the unique intellectual problems for polymers because of the chain connectivity. Namely, even in the one phase and stable region, the solvent can change from good to theta (ideal) and then to poor solvent, while in the solutions of small molecules, there is no good or poor solvent problem because the solution exists either in the one-phase or two-phase region, soluble or non-soluble. We have established a protocol of how to use dynamic LLS to quickly and conveniently locate the “ideal” state, i.e., the theta-condition, of a given polymer solution; obtained semi-quantitative explanation; formulated a semi-quantitative model to interpret how the relative contribution of the internal motions of a single polymer chain in solution varies when the solvent quality changes; and elucidated the relationship between the intra-chain and inter-chain second virial coefficients so that we are able to understand how T* is related to the "theta" temperature. Our novel method not only contains some intellectual values, but also enables others to quickly determine the boundary between a good and a poor solvent in everyday’s practices.

403611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403611.value: The method established in this study can be used to measure the theta conditions of most of our conventional polymers in most of common solvents to correct and complete polymer handbooks. Our finding should lead to the rewriting of polymer textbooks.

403611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403611.value: The solutions made of small molecules exists either in the one-phase region, in which a solute is soluble in a solvent, or in the two-phase region, in which the solution separates into two layers: one is a solution of the solute saturated in the solvent; and the other, the solvent saturated in the solute. While in a polymer solution, the solvent quality in the one-phase region can change from good to theta (ideal) and then to poor because of the chain connectivity, i.e., all the monomers on a chain are connected together by chemical bonds. Our newly developed method provides an easy and quick way to locate the boundary between the good and poor solvent. More importantly, our finding has solved an intellectual problem.

403711.label: Major findings and research outcome
403711.value: A protein labeling strategy has been solidly developed based on the coiled coil peptides. It has been successfully applied to covalently label proteins expressed on the surface of cells. The tag does not change the property of the protein on the surface of cells. This method is expected to be generally applicable to many proteins, and are likely highly used by others in the field. Several papers have been published. One key paper has been highlighted on the cover of an ACS journal (see attachment in Part C). Following the same strategy, we also extended the objectives listed in this project to two more directions. First, we designed a new protein labeling strategy based on SH3 proteins. We sought to further improve the efficiency of the covalent conjugation reaction, because the binding affinities of the coiled coil peptides are moderate. Unlike peptide-peptide binding interactions, protein-peptide binding interactions have higher affinity and are more versatile. We also observed that the covalent reaction between a mutant of SH3 protein Abl(N31C), and its peptide derivative p41X are highly efficient and rapid. It requires only several minutes to achieve >50% covalent reaction in solution. Utilizing this tagging system, we also covalently labeled receptor proteins that express on the surface of cells. Notably, labeling by the peptide probe persisted after extensive washing steps, indicating high specificity and biocompatibility of the bioconjugation reaction. Finally, we extended the research to the development of a more versatile protein labeling strategy based on synthetic WW domain. Notwithstanding that much success has been achieved using coiled coil peptides and SH3-peptide conjugating pairs, each has some limitations. The low affinity of coiled coil interactions leads to the incompletion of the covalent reaction. We then consider developing another general strategy with (1) a short peptide tag, and (2) higher specificity. We turn to WW domains this time. WW domains are 30-40 residues long, so they can be synthesized. We synthesized a WW3 domain and its peptide ligand, with a chloroacetyl group installed at an appropriate position of the WW domain based on the structure of dNedd4 WW3 domain. Taken together, we successfully completed all the objectives listed here, and successfully published the results. In addition, this project leads to a significant extension to several systems, which allows us to elevate the objectives to a higher level that is even beyond the scope of the proposal.

403711.value: Further development of the research has proven to be feasible. We extended from the proposed research to more advanced areas. We have garnered great success in these new directions.

403711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403711.value: A new protein labeling strategy allows the protein to be visualized and tracked. We then know where the protein goes simply by looking at the microscope. It will help answer many biological and medicinal questions that are previously unattainable.

403811.value: Prof Zhou, Shengqi Prof Zhou, Yu

403811.label: Project Objectives
403811.value: Investigate experimentally the large-scale circulation in horizontal convection in the presence of surface thermal forcing. Study the upwelling process of the convective flow by measuring the fluid mixing and turbulent diffusion. Study the influence of wind stress to the dynamics and pattern of the large-scale circulation by applying a variable wind stress to the fluid surface and probe the response of the convective flow to the applied wind stress in the presence of thermal forcing from the measured velocity and temperature fields.

403811.label: Realisation of objectives
403811.value: We have successfully built a horizontal convection apparatus. We made both heat transport and local temperature measurement, including temperature, thermal boundary layer and temperature fluctuation statistics. Both quantitative velocity field measurement using particle image velocimetry (PIV) and flow visualization measurement using tracing particles have been made. The results show that it is possible for the flow to have a returning circulation below the thermal boundary layer, i.e. without penetrating the thermocline. We have investigated the influence of bottom heating on global heat transport, thermal boundary layer (corresponding to thermocline in the oceans), and the global circulation in horizontal convection. We found that a small amount of bottom heating can significantly perturb the bulk flow and enhance the global circulation flux in horizontal convection. We have studied the aspect ratio dependence of both global heat transport and bulk flow field in horizontal convection.

403811.label: Major findings and research outcome
403811.value: Our first result is the scaling of the global heat transport efficiency Nu with the Rayleigh number Ra. Classical analysis has suggested that the Nu should scale with Ra with an exponent of 1/5. But previous numerical and experiment studies have given mixed results, which are likely due to the very limited parameter range and numerical resolution and experimental precisions. We have found scaling exponent of 0.3, which has been suggested for the asymptotic high Ra regime. With the high precision and accuracy of our measurement, this is a very convincing result. Our local temperature profile measurements have found a boundary layer temperature profile very similar to that found in the oceans, i.e. the thermocline. Suggesting that our laboratory apparatus is relevant as a simplified model for the study of ocean circulation. Our results also suggest that the main features of the temperature field in the oceans are determined by the surface heating. The almost constant temperature in the upper ocean could be ascribed to the strong mixing due to the winds. An important question in the study of horizontal convection is whether surface thermal forcing alone is able to generate a full penetration large-scale circulation. Our results show that indeed such a circulation exists in our horizontal convection apparatus with just surface heating. Moreover, our flow visualization studies show that it is not necessary for the returning flow to penetrate the strong stratification in the thermal BLs. In other words, the returning flow is separated into two branches, namely cold-water path and warm-water path. For the warm-water path, it penetrates the thermal BLs via diffusion and goes back to the surface. For the cold-water path, its kinematic energy dissipates mainly due to the viscous drag while returning to the destabilization buoyancy source, it does not make the ‘useless’ vertical mixing since its goal is returning to the destabilization buoyancy source rather than to the surface. In other words, it seems that the flow can find a lesser energy-cost path to maintain its strength and survive. Globally, the geothermal heat flux (GHF) is extremely comparing to the total surface heat flux (SHF). In the ocean research community, there has been a debate regarding the importance of GHF. In horizontal convection, we mimic the geothermal heat flux by a small bottom heat flux (BHF). In the study of bottom heating effect in horizontal convection, we have found that while energy generated by a small amount BHF is unable to perturb the thermal boundary layer due to the strong density stratification; outside the thermal boundary layer weak density stratification is easily eroded by a small amount of BHF. A destabilizing force generated near the bottom promotes a broader upwelling returning flow and a more vigorous vortex in the deep water. As a result, the overturning circulation becomes much stronger. Specifically, we have found that a BHF equal to only 2% of the SHF is able to more than double the kinetic energy of the bulk circulation, which shows that BHF, while small, is very efficient to stir deep water circulation and upwelling.

403811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403811.value: A future direction in the study of horizontal convection is to systematically investigate its aspect ratio dependence. The large-scale circulation in real oceans is extremely and a laboratory model mimicking ocean circulations can never have such a large aspect ratio. On the other hand, our study has found that the ratio between the thermal boundary layer thickness and the cell depth is about 0.01, which is about the same as the ratio between the depths of the thermocline and the ocean. This suggests that laboratory horizontal convection experiment may indeed be relevant to oceanic circulation in certain aspects. To explore this further, we plan to build an apparatus that is capable of widely varying the aspect ratio and adapted for both heat transport and velocity field measurement.

403811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403811.value: An important issue in the studies of oceanic circulation is how dense water sinking in poles return to the surface near equator. A related question is whether surface thermal forcing is sufficient to drive the deep penetration in the oceanic circulations. In this project a simple laboratory model system, the horizontal convection, has been used to address the above and related questions. Our studies indicate that a deep penetration is possible with thermal heating alone and suggest that it is not necessary for the returning flow to overcome the stratification. Moreover, our studies suggest that geothermal heating, while consisting of only a very small fraction in the ocean energy budget, could play an important role stirring and driving circulation in the deep ocean.

404011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
404011.value: Zirconacycles, in particular zirconacyclopentadienes, are a class of very important versatile intermediates for construction of carbon-carbon/carbon-heteroatom bonds. They are finding many applications in organic transformations. In view of the very rich reaction chemistry of zirconacycles, we became interested in developing a carborane version of these reagents for the synthesis of a variety of functionalized carboranes. Very recently, we found that alkynes R1C≡CR2 can readily react with Cp2Zr(μ-Cl)(μ-C2B10H10)Li(OEt2)2 to give the mono-insertion products 1,2-[Cp2ZrC(R1)=C(R2)]-1,2-C2B10H10, a class of zirconacyclopentene incorporating a carboranyl unit, in very high isolated yields with very good chemo- and regioselectivity. Preliminary results show that this class of zirconacyclopentene resembles their analogs zirconacyclopentadienes in some reactions, and on the other hand, they have unique properties of their own due to the presence of highly sterically demanding carboranyl unit (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2009, 131, 3862-3863.). This work demonstrates that such zirconacyclopentenes are important intermediates for the preparation of a range of functionalized carborane derivatives. We propose in this proposal to explore systematically the reaction chemistry of this new class of zirconacycles and to develop new synthetic methodologies for the preparation of functionalized carboranes. It will also be fascinating to discover what lies beyond. 鋯雜環特別是鋯雜環戊二烯是一類用于構築碳-碳/碳-雜原子鍵的重要中間體，可應用于多種有機轉化過程。鑒于鋯雜環豐富的化學反應性，我們對碳硼烷相關的鋯雜環及通過其合成各種官能團化碳硼烷産生了興趣。最近我們發現炔烴R1C≡CR2可以很便利的與Cp2Zr(μ-Cl)(μ-C2B10H10)Li(OEt2)2反應，高化學選擇性及高區域選擇性的生成單插入産物1,2-[Cp2ZrC(R1)=C(R2)]-1,2-C2B10H10，一類含有碳硼烷基團的鋯雜環戊烯。初步研究結果表明，此類鋯雜環戊烯與其類似物鋯雜環戊二烯在一些反應中具有相似的反應性，但另一方面由于碳硼烷基團的大位阻效應，它們也有一些自己獨特的性質 (J. 404011.label: Realisation of objectives
404011.value: Zirconacycles in particular zirconacyclopentadienes are a class of very important versatile intermediates for construction of carbon-carbon/carbon-heteroatom bonds. They are finding many applications in organic transformations. In view of the very rich reaction chemistry of zirconacycles, we have developed a carborane version of these reagents for the synthesis of a variety of functionalized carboranes. We found that alkynes R1C≡CR2 can readily react with Cp2Zr(μ-Cl)(μ-C2B10H10)Li(OEt2)2 to give the mono-insertion products 1,2-[Cp2ZrC(R1)=C(R2)]-1,2-C2B10H10, a class of zirconacyclopentene incorporating a carboranyl unit, in very high isolated yields with very good chemo- and regioselectivity. This class of zirconacyclopentene resembles their analogs zirconacyclopentadienes in some reactions, and on the other hand, they have unique properties of their own due to the presence of highly sterically demanding carboranyl unit. This demonstrates that such zirconacyclopentenes are important intermediates for the preparation of a range of functionalized carborane derivatives. Furthermore, transmetalation of Zr to other metals such as Ni and Cu opens up new opportunities for the construction of complex molecules via multi-component approaches. Subsequently, Zr/Ni co-mediated two-component [2+2+2] cross-cyclotrimerization of carboryne with alkynes and a three-component [2+2+2] cross-cyclotrimerization of o-carboryne with two different alkynes or with one alkene and one alkyne have been developed. Furthermore, through the cooperative mediation of both Zr and Ni, a three-component [2+2+1] cross-cyclotrimerization has also been realized. The corresponding reaction mechanism is proposed on the basis of experimental and computational studies. These new synthetic methodologies lead to the preparation of a variety of functionalized carboranes.

404011.label: Major findings and research outcome
404011.value: (1) A series of neutral group 4 metal-carboryne complexes were synthesized via a salt metathesis reaction of (amidinato)2MCl2 with Li2C2B10H10. They reacted with polar unsaturated molecules such as ketone, nitrile, carbodiimide, isocyanate, thioisocyanate, carbon disulfide and azide to give mono-insertion products. No double insertion products were observed. However, they did not show any activities toward pyridines, alkynes, and alkenes due to steric effects imposed by amidonato ligands. Transmetalation of zirconacyclopentenes to Cu resulted in the formation of carborane-fused cyclobutenes and cyclobutanes. The chemical properties of metallacarboranes of Fe and Co were also examined (Pubs #6, #7 & #9). (2) Efficient Zr/Ni co-mediated three-component [2+2+2] cycloaddition of carboryne, unactivated alkene and alkyne for the preparation of dihydrobenzocarboranes was developed, offering an example of how to control the selectivity among different alkenes and alkynes to assemble complex molecular architectures (Pub #1). (3) We have developed an efficient three-component [2+2+2] cycloaddition protocol for the preparation of a new class of highly substituted benzocarboranes in one pot or two-step manner via transmetalation of zirconacyclopentenes incorporating a carboranyl unit to nickel or iron. The reaction mechanism is proposed after the isolation and full characterization of the key intermediate nickelacycle. The results show that both electronic and steric factors play a role in the regioselective formation of benzocarboranes. This sets an example for the conversion of traditional zirconocene-based stoichiometric reactions into a catalytic one (Pub #2). (4) A density functional theory (DFT) study was carried out to elucidate the mechanism of [2+2+1] cyclotrimerization of o-carboryne with CH2CHnBu and TMSAr co-mediated by Zr/Ni. The calculated results reveal that the commonly proposed mechanism via a nickel vinylidene intermediate is kinetically and thermodynamically disfavored. An unprecedented reaction mechanism involving alkyne insertion, 1-alkenyl to 2-alkenyl rearrangement and TMS migrations is found to be responsible for the favorable [2+2+1] cycloaddition (Pub #8). (5) Reaction of carboryne with alkylbenzenes, ferrocenes and styrenes was investigated, affording a series of functionalized carboranes. These results indicate that carboryne is a very useful synthon. On the other hand, Ir-catalyzed selective cage B-H activation/functionalization was achieved, giving a class of cage B(4)-functionalized carboranes (Pubs #3-5 &10). Research Outcome: This original work has resulted in 10 peer-reviewed articles published in international chemistry journals including JACS (x 2), Angew Chem Int Ed (x 1), Organometallics (x 4), Tetrahedron (x 1), J. Organomet. Chem (x 1) and Sci China Chem (x 1). PI was invited to give one keynote and three invited lectures at international conferences. Four PhD students were trained.

404011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
404011.value: Zr/Ni co-mediated multi-component reactions involving heteroatoms need to be further investigated, which may lead to the synthesis of carborane-fused heterocycles with potential applications in medicine and materials science.

404011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
404011.value: Icosahedral carboranes constitute a class of structurally unique molecules with exceptionally thermal and chemical stabilities and the ability to hold various substituents. These properties have made them as useful basic units for boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) drugs, supramolecular design, and ligands for transition metals. On the other hand, these properties also make the functionalization of carboranes difficult. Only limited methodologies for the derivatization of these clusters are known. In this research, we have developed several new synthetic methodologies using zirconacycles as key reagents for the preparation of a variety of functionalized carboranes which cannot be prepared by conventional methods. The resultant new functionalized carboranes may find applications in BNCT and materials science. This research not only largely expends the reaction scope of zirconacycles but also enhances our basic understanding of the chemistry of boron clusters.
