404111.label: Project Title(Chinese)
404111.value: 粘性可壓縮Navier-Stokes方程組中的一些問題

404111.label: Project Objectives
404111.value: One goal of this project is to study the global in time well-posedness and large time behavior of classical solutions to either the Cauchy problem or initial-boundary value problem (IBVP) for the full multi-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system with constant viscosity coefficients provided that the data are close to a uniform non-vacuum state only in the energy-norm and thus may have large oscillations, in particular, vacuum states in the interior are allowed. It should be noted that this is a long standing difficult open problem since the seminal work of Matsumura-Nishida. Indeed, all the previous works on the existence of classical solutions require at least smallness of the oscillation of the data from a uniform non-vacuum state, and the uniform (in time) of the control of the gradient of the density plays a key role. However, the supernorm of the gradient of the density may grow unbounded in time in the presence of the vacuum. Thus new ideas and techniques will be needed. We will start with the isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes system first. The case of the full compressible Navier-Stokes may become more challenging due to the strong nonlinear coupling with the temperature. Both 2-dimensional and 3-dimensional problems will be investigated. Our next objective is to investigate the global (in time) existence of classical solutions to the Cauchy problem for the compressible Navier-Stokes system with initial data whose far fields are vacuum. This is very important since a positive answer will imply the regularity and uniqueness of the weak solutions constructed by Lions' theory. However, this is a subtle since any non-trivial smooth solutions to the full Navier-Stokes system in any space dimensions will blow-up in finite time for compactly supported initial data. However, for the isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes system, recent studies of radial symmetric solutions seem to indicate that the answer to this problem may depend on the spatial dimension. Our focus will be to prove the global well-posedness of the classical solution for 3-dimension isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes system for initial data with small total energy but possible large oscillations. We then also investigate whether such a theory holds in other cases such as 2-dimensional space or the case that the viscosity coefficients may depend on the density. Another major goal is to study the well-posedness of both strong and weak solutions to initial or initial-boundary value problems for the multi-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes system with density-dependent viscosity such as the viscous Saint-Venant system. First, we will study the local well-posedness theory of strong and classical solutions. Then we study the global existence of weak solutions. The structure and large asymptotic behavior of solution will be investigated with focus on whether the vacuum-vanishing phenomena found in the 1-dimensional case holds true in multi-dimensions. Finally, we will study the problem of viscous fluid expanding into vacuum in multi-dimension with either stress free or continuous conditions on the interface separating vacuum. Both strong and weak solutions will be treated with emphases on the motion of the free boundary. Other related problems, such as formation or vanishing of vacuum, large time asymptotic stability of basic wave patterns, etc. will also be investigated. In particular, we will study the large time asymptotic nonlinear stability of a rarefaction wave connecting a non-vacuum state to a vacuum state for the viscous compressible Navier-Stokes system.
rows: One goal of this project is to study the global in time well-posedness and large time behavior of classical solutions to either the Cauchy problem or initial-boundary value problem (IBVP) for the full multi-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system with constant viscosity coefficients provided that the data are close to a uniform non-vacuum state only in the energy-norm and thus may have large oscillations, in particular, vacuum states in the interior are allowed. It should be noted that this is a long standing difficult open problem since the seminal work of Matsumura-Nishida. Indeed, all the previous works on the existence of classical solutions require at least smallness of the oscillation of the data from a uniform non-vacuum state, and the uniform (in time) of the control of the gradient of the density plays a key role. However, the supernorm of the gradient of the density may grow unbounded in time in the presence of the vacuum. Thus new ideas and techniques will be needed. We will start with the isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes system first. The case of the full compressible Navier-Stokes may become more challenging due to the strong nonlinear coupling with the temperature. Both 2-dimensional and 3-dimensional problems will be investigated.

Our next objective is to investigate the global (in time) existence of classical solutions to the Cauchy problem for the compressible Navier-Stokes system with initial data whose far fields are vacuum. This is very important since a positive answer will imply the regularity and uniqueness of the weak solutions constructed by Lions' theory. However, this is a subtle since any non-trivial smooth solutions to the full Navier-Stokes system in any space dimensions will blow-up in finite time for compactly supported initial data. However, for the isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes system, recent studies of radial symmetric solutions seem to indicate that the answer to this problem may depend on the spatial dimension. Our focus will be to prove the global well-posedness of the classical solution for 3-dimension isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes system for initial data with small total energy but possible large oscillations. We then also investigate whether such a theory holds in other cases such as 2-dimensional space or the case that the viscosity coefficients may depend on the density.

Another major goal is to study the well-posedness of both strong and weak solutions to initial or initial-boundary value problems for the multi-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes system with density-dependent viscosity such as the viscous Saint-Venant system. First, we will study the local well-posedness theory of strong and classical solutions. Then we study the global existence of weak solutions. The structure and large asymptotic behavior of solution will be investigated with focus on whether the vacuum-vanishing phenomena found in the 1-dimensional case holds true in multi-dimensions. Finally, we will study the problem of viscous fluid expanding into vacuum in multi-dimension with either stress free or continuous conditions on the interface separating vacuum. Both strong and weak solutions will be treated with emphases on the motion of the free boundary.

Other related problems, such as formation or vanishing of vacuum, large time asymptotic stability of basic wave patterns, etc. will also be investigated. In particular, we will study the large time asymptotic nonlinear stability of a rarefaction wave connecting a non-vacuum state to a vacuum state for the viscous compressible Navier-Stokes system.

404111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
404111.value: Many important phenomena are governed by the compressible Navier-Stokes system and its variants, which are fundamental nonlinear partial differential equations in continuum mechanics. Their studies have been and will continue to be some of the focus of the theory of nonlinear partial differential equations and applied analysis. Some of the major difficulties in dealing with such a system lie in the strong nonlinearities in both the inertial term and the stress tensor, the strong coupling of hyperbolicity with parabolicity, and the degeneracy in the presence of the vacuum. Despite the tremendous progress in the past two hundred years, the well-posedness theory and qualitative understanding of the solutions for such systems in the multi-dimensional setting remain to be challenging problems in this area. Thus we propose to investigate the well-posedness theory of the initial-value problem, initial-boundary value problem, and free-boundary-value problems and qualitative structure of weak and/or strong solutions for the case that the data may have large oscillations and contain vacuum states, and to develop methods and techniques to analyze the corresponding nonlinear systems which are type of hyperbolic-parabolic coupling and have strong degeneracies near vacuum states. These studies may lead to the resolution of several long standing open problems in this area and new wave phenomena which are important in the mathematical theory of fluid-dynamics. 連續介質力學中的許多重要現象都是由可壓縮Navier-Stokes方程組及其變型來描述的，這是一類最基本的重要的非線性偏微分方程組，其研究一直是非線性偏微分方程理論及應用分析中的核心問題之一。而慣性項及應力張量中的強非線性和真空出現時的蛻化性是處理這類方程組時的一些基本困難。盡管在過去兩百年中，這類方程的理論研究已取得了巨大成就，但高維問題解的適定性及其定性分析仍然是領域中的挑戰性問題。在這個建議書中，我們將研究高維可壓縮Navier-Stokes方程組的初值問題、初邊值問題和自由邊值問題，重點是當數據具有大振盪和真空時的全局適定性和解的漸近性質，並發展新的處理含有蛻化的抛物―雙曲耦合方程組的方析方法，這些研究可解決該領域一些重要公開問題並發現新的現象。

404111.label: Realisation of objectives
404111.value: Through rigorous analysis and collaborate with students, post-doctors and other researchers, the PI has achieved all the objectives in this project. Our research results give complete and satisfactory answers to the major scientific problems proposed in the proposal. In partial, we have solved several difficult and important open problems in this field and achieved important understandings of the main challenges, and developed new ideas and methods which will be useful for the further development of the field.

404111.label: Major findings and research outcome
404111.value: With the main support of this RGC grant, the PI has achieved all the objectives in the project. Some new phenomena have been discovered and some important problems in the field have been solved, and we have developed new ideas and methods which are useful for the further development of the area. In particular, with Jing Li, we have proved the global (in time) well-posedness of classical solutions to the Cauchy problems or both 2 and 3 dimensional isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with initial data which may contain vacuum either at interior or at far fields, under the only assumption that the initial total energy is small, but the initial oscillation may be large. These results not only generalize the classical theory of Matsumura-Nishida to the case where vacuum may occur, but also give the uniqueness and regularity of the weak solutions of Lions-Feireisl (see Li-Xin 1). Surprisingly, we have shown such a theory fails for the full compressible 3-D Navier-Stokes system in general by identify a class of initial data which contain vacuum such that any classical solutions with such an initial data blows-up in finite time. This is a first blow-up result whose regularity requirements are consistent with the theory of local existence of classical solutions (see Xin-Yan). Jointly with my collaborators, Zeng and Luo, we have made some important progress on the gaseous star problems. First, we have shown the un-conditional uniqueness of the classical solutions to the motion of ideal gases expanding into vacuum (see Luo-Xin-Zeng 1). Second, we proved the nonlinear asymptotic stability of the Lane-Emden solutions for the viscous gaseous star problem in the radial symmetrical setting, this is achieved by discovering some new weighted nonlinear functional which are used to obtain global uniform regularity both up to vacuum free boundary and large time (see Luo-Xin-Zeng 2). Finally, we have solved a long standing open problem by proving the global existence of weak solutions to the multi-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes systems with viscosity coefficients depending on the density which become degenerate near vacuum. This solves an open problem due to P. L. Lions. Besides, we have made substantial progress on other important problems related to this project, such as, boundary layer analysis, interval viscous layers and vanishing viscosity limits, transonic flows, and liquid crystal flows, etc.. We have produced 25 research papers, and most of them have been published in top research journals.

404111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
404111.value: The results obtained in this project give rise to more profound problems for the compressible Navier-Stokes systems such as: global strong (or weak) solutions to the full compressible Navier-Stokes systems in multi-dimensions; can singularity form in finite time for the full multi-dimensional viscous compressible fluids with smooth initial data which do not contain isolated mass group? What are the uniqueness and regularity of the weak solutions to the compressible Navier-Stokes system with degenerate density dependent viscosity constructed by Li-Xin? Can the Lane-Emden solution be nonlinearity asymptotically stable under more generic perturbations etc.. The ideas and techniques developed here at this project should be very useful to attack these interesting problems.

404111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
404111.value: Many important phenomena are governed by the compressible Navier-Stokes system and its variants, which are fundamental nonlinear partial differential equations in continuum mechanics. Their studies have been and continue to be some of the focus of the theory of nonlinear partial differential equations and applied analysis. Some of the major difficulties in dealing with a system lie in the strong nonlinearities the strong coupling of hyperbolicity with parabolicity, and the degeneracies in the presence of vacuum. Despite the tremendous progress in the past, the well-posedness theory and qualitative understanding of the solutions for such systems in the multi-dimensional setting remain to be challenging problems in this area. In this project, we have successfully investigated the motions of vacuum dynamics for such systems and the well-posedness theory of both strong and weak solutions to the multi-dimensional Navier-Stokes systems in the presence of vacuum and with possible large oscillatory initial data. We found the finite-time blow-up of classical solutions to the full Navier-Stokes system for a large class of initial data. New global well-posedness and large time behavior of solutions are obtained for isentropic case with vacuum and large oscillation which solved several long standing open problems. We also give the first rigorous stability analysis of the Lane-Emden solutions for the viscous gaseous star problem. These studies lead to the resolution of several long standing open problems in this area and new wave phenomena which are important in the mathematical theory of the fluid-dynamics.

404211.label: Project Objectives
404211.value: Visualizing the detailed air invasion dynamics at different drying stages as well as in several commonly encountered systems, to clarify the underlying dynamical details of drying at the microscopic level. Two different drying stages have been generally observed in most complex systems, during which the evaporation rate varies dramatically. However, the fundamental microscopic pictures of each stage are still lacking. With confocal microscopy and high speed photography, we will directly image the detailed air invasions in each stage and settle this fundamental question. We will also closely examine the drying of several commonly encountered systems, such as the hard particle system, the soft particle system, and the gel system, to study the general drying properties in various structures. 404211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
404211.value: The aim of this project is to study the dynamics of drying in complex systems using direct imaging techniques, and to create novel drying-related materials, such as smart coating materials, crack-resistant paints, and hierarchical structures. Drying is a ubiquitous process constantly taking place in our daily life. It is of great importance technologically, having deep connections with paint drying in coating industry, soil drying in agriculture, and spray drying in food and pharmaceutical industries. In most of these applications, drying occurs in complex combinations of solvent, particles and droplets. For example, in the coating industry, most paints are multi-component colloids and droplets suspensions which dry in rather complex manners; similarly, soil drying also occurs in complex solid-liquid mixtures. These various components typically scatter light significantly, making the system totally opaque. As a result, it is very difficult to directly visualize the drying dynamics deep inside complex systems, and our knowledge of the actual drying behavior is quite limited. Therefore, the direct observation of the drying dynamics inside complex systems is an urgent call from both the fundamental research and the practical applications. We propose to address this important issue by directly imaging the drying process in optically index-matched samples, using the techniques of confocal microscopy and high-speed photography. By preparing complex systems with optically index-matched components, that is, substances with similar refractive indices, we can directly visualize regions deep inside the system and solve the visualization difficulty. We will investigate the detailed drying behaviors at both the single particle level and the macroscopic scale, focusing on two fundamental questions: (1) what are the underlying dynamical details at different drying stages and in various structures; and (2) what are the microscopic mechanisms of the cracking formation and propagation induced by drying. For the dynamics too rapid to resolve with conventional methods, we will use high speed photography and achieve the time resolution up to 100,000 frame/s. With the high spatial and temporal resolutions achievable from direct imaging, we aim to bring unprecedented details to the drying and cracking dynamics. Moreover, by applying the fundamental drying mechanisms, we also propose to create novel drying-related materials. Possible examples include materials that can dry in well-controlled sequences which could be used for smart paints, and hierarchical structures which may mimic natural hierarchical materials. 404211.value: (1) For objective 1, we have studied the dynamics throughout the drying of colloidal systems at single-particle level. Interestingly, as drying proceeds, colloid concentration increases and particles self-assemble into either disordered structures or various colloidal crystals. By tracking the motion of every single particle, we have studied the situations in both the disordered and the crystalline structures, and successfully illustrated the dynamics at microscopic level: in the disordered system, we found similar dynamics as in glassy and jammed systems(Phys. Rev. Lett. 108, 095501, 2012); and in the colloidal crystals we illustrated the kinetics of crystallization at single-particle level(Nature Physics 10, 73-79, 2014). For soft and hard particles' drying dynamics, we have used emulsion droplets as special "soft particles" and PMMA colloids as "hard particles". Surprisingly, when the "soft particles" are mixed with "hard particles", they can completely eliminate cracking throughout drying! This phenomenon can serve as a promising approach to make crack-resistant paint and also addresses the key issues in objective 2 and 3 on crack resistant paints(Eur. Phys. J. E. 36, 28, 2013). (2) For objective 2, by combining direct imaging and rheology, we have clarified the cracking mechanism from the aspect of system moduli. We demonstrated that the storage modulus (G') and the loss modulus (G") are crucial quantities which determine whether or not cracking occurs. As more “soft particles”(i.e. emulsion droplets) are added the importance of loss modulus increases and more energy can dissipate instead of store in the system, which eventually eliminates cracking and successfully addresses the objective 2 (Eur. Phys. J. E. 36, 28, 2013). (3) For objective 3, by using particles with different sizes, we have successfully made smart paint material which can dry in well-controlled order. We have also successfully achieved the crack-resistant paint by combining emulsion droplets with solid particles. These findings address objective 3 satisfactorily.

404211.label: Major findings and research outcome
404211.value: (1) As drying proceeds, concentration increases and particles can self-assemble. The dynamics of these structures at microscopic level is very interesting. We studied the vibration dynamics of disordered systems and established an experimental link between glass and jamming, as well as illustrated the origin of the low-frequency quasilocalized modes in glass. This work was published in Phys. Rev. Lett. 108, 095501, 2012. (2) We have also studied the drying of systems composed by hard and soft particles. We used emulsion droplets as special “soft particles” and observed their effect on drying. Surprisingly, when such “soft particles” are mixed with solid particles, they can completely eliminate cracking throughout drying! This phenomenon can serve as a promising approach to make crack-resistant paint. The relevant work was published in Eur. Phys. J. E. 36, 28, 2013. (3) Moreover, solid particles and emulsion droplets self-assemble into Pickering emulsions which exhibit novel coalescence behaviors. We have revealed two distinct coalescing routes: the normal coalescence which is similar to liquid droplets and the abnormal coalescence which exhibits oscillatory cycles. This abnormal property comes from the geometric constraint of the particle coatings. We have published this work in Phys. Rev. Lett. 110, 064502, 2013. (4) For many practical applications, liquid drops first impact on a solid surface and then dry on it. Therefore the impact immediately before drying may have an influence on the drying process. Using direct imaging technique, we investigate this impact process systematically and illustrate that a high- pressure air film is trapped under the drop, which shrinks into an air bubble eventually. This research is published in J. Fluid Mech. 716, R9, 2013. (5) For the dynamics of particle self-assembly during drying, another important structure is crystalline structure. We again obtained single-particle level understanding on this process by directly visualizing the kinetic pathways of the crystallization process. The relevant results were published in Nature Physics 10, 73-79, 2014. (6) We also studied the impact process before drying on various porous substrates. We found that the air flow trapped under the liquid drop causes splashing, which may provide important guidance for surface coating. The relevant results were published in Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA (PNAS) 112, 3280-3284, 2015.

404611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
404611.value: Domain decomposition methods (DDMs) have been proved to be one of the most natural and successful methodologies to design efficient numerical solvers for boundary value and initial-boundary value problems of partial differential equations (PDEs). Through an iterative procedure, the solution of PDEs on a global domain is reduced to the solution of some PDEs on a finite number of subdomains, which can be realized in parallel on processors of a high performance supercomputer. Inverse problems arise widely from many applications, and often are mathematically ill-posed. One of the most stable and effective approaches to solve the ill-posed inverse problems is to transform them into stabilized output least-squares minimizations with some Tikhonov regularizations. Therefore inverse problems are usually much more challenging to solve numerically than direct problems. A large number of domain decomposition methods have been developed for efficiently solving the large-scale direct problems. But little mathematical and numerical studies have been done in the literature on how to effectively solve the stabilized minimization systems of inverse problems. Some investigations are available, which proposed to apply the classical iterative algorithms to solve the the stabilized minimization systems, then apply the DDMs to solve the direct PDE problems involved in each iteration. Such approaches do not improve the efficiency of the outer iterations as they are classical algorithms and targets still towards the global nonlinear minimization system. In this proposal we would like to propose several new algorithms for solving some important mathematical inverse problems. The algorithms will be constructed to meet the true spirits of DDM, namely they are iterative procedures for solving the stabilized minimization systems, and at each iteration only smaller minimizations will be solved on subdomains of the original global domain. Each outer iterative procedure is constructed in a way that the number of its iterations for a specified accuracy grows very slowly when the degrees of freedom of the global minimization system and number of subdomains increase. So these DDMs are especially important for solving large-scale inverse problems. The PI and Co-I both have a long track record in the research areas like DDMs and inverse problems and have gained a rich experience in solving and analyzing the large-scale inverse problems. Furthermore, several mathematical problems that are involved in the project are basic and quite suitable for postgraduate training. 區域分裂法是求解初邊值問題的最自然和有效的並行算法。通過迭代過程，將一個物理區域上的初邊值問題化為許多子區域上的小規模問題求解。 大量的實際應用中，我們經常需要求解數學反問題。反問題通常是不適定的，所以求解時需要引進適當的穩定性項。最常用的有效方法是最小二乘加上Tikhonov正則法，轉化為最後求解一個穩定的非線性優化問題。為了便於在高性能並行計算機上求解此非線性優化問題，我們將設計新型的區域分裂法，使整個求解過程的每一步可充分並行實現。這是一個全新的想法，文獻上至今從來未有過這方面的研究。 区域分裂法是求解初边值问题的最自然和有效的并行算法。通过迭代过程，将一个区域上的初边值问题代为许多子区域上的问题求解。 大量的实际应用中，我们经常需要求解数学反问题。反问题通常是不适定的，所以求解时需要引进适当的稳定性项。最常用的有效方法是最少二乘加上Tikhonov正则法，导致最后求解一个稳定的非线性优化问题。为了便于在高性能并行计算器上求解此非线性优化问题，我们将没计新型的区域分裂法，使整个求解过程的每一步可充分并行实现。这是一个全新的想法，文献上至今从来未有对这方面的研究。

404611.label: Realisation of objectives
404611.value: We have fully realized the objectives of this research project, and actually achieved much more than those expected in the original proposal. We have constructed a parallel space-time domain decomposition method (DDM) for recovering unsteady heat sources, and a two-level space-time DDM for identifying intensities and locations of moving source distributions in parabolic equations. Especially, we have constructed effective preconditioners for large-scale discrete systems from electromagnetic scattering. When combined with the nonoverlapping DDMs, the method can speed up the numerical resolution of electromagnetic scattering significantly, and are hence able to accelerate the numerical resolutions of highly nonlinear inverse scattering problems essentially as the forward scattering system needs to be solved for possibly hundred times in most applications. Furthermore, we have developed several efficient additive- and multiplicative-type overlapping DDMs for solving many inverse problems governed by general elliptic and parabolic systems, including the recovery of source profiles, heat fluxes, Robin coefficient, initial data and partial boundary data. Motivated by the general principles of DDMs, we have proposed some novel robust and stable direct sampling-type methods for solving several highly challenging nonlinear inverse problems, such as electrical impedance tomography, inverse acoustic and electromagnetic scattering, diffusive optical tomography, imaging wave-penetrable objects. These new sampling methods have the important features: they are easy to implement, very robust against the noise in the observation data, computationally very cheap as they do not involve any matrix inversion and nonlinear optimization. Furthermore, we have developed two novel multilevel sampling algorithms for locating inhomogeneous media occupied by multiple acoustic subdomains, and for recovering multiple multiscale scatterers which may be represented by separated small or large electromagnetic subdomains. New operator-splitting methods are developed for convection-dominated diffusion and Navier-Stokes equations.Very interestingly, we are able to constructe randomized algorithms for large-scale linear inverse problems with general Tikhonov regularizations, and adaptive finite element methods for recovering Robin coefficients in general parabolic equations in a way that the adaptively generated meshes can accurately predict and capture the discontinuity and singularity of the forward solutions and Robin coefficients. We have tested and studied these new methods sufficiently many times for the relevant inverse problems, then proposed their improved variants based on their numerical performance in terms of convergence, stability, accuracy and some algorithmic parameters. We have fully tested all our DDMs in two fastest supercomputers in China and demonstrated their satisfactory parallel speed-ups and scalability with the total number of cores and CPUs used.

404611.label: Major findings and research outcome
404611.value: We proposed a parallel space-time domain decomposition method (DDM) in [5] and a two-level space-time DDM in [6] for recovering unsteady sources and the strength and location of moving sources in heat conduction systems. This first space-time DDM eliminates all sequential steps in KKT systems from Tikhonov regularized formulations of inverse problems, hence enjoys high parallel speed-up and scalability. We developed in [9] parallel overlapping DDMs for various elliptic and parabolic inverse problems. PMLs are effective techniques that help truncate unbounded domains when solving electromagnetic scattering problems, but result in large-scale discrete systems. We constructed efficient preconditioners in [7] for the systems. When combined with DDMs, they can accelerate numerical resolutions of nonlinear inverse scattering problems significantly. We developed novel robust direct sampling-type methods for inverse acoustic and electromagnetic scattering [1,8,10], diffusive optical tomography [3], electrical impedance tomography [2], imaging wave-penetrable objects in ocean [11]. These methods enjoy the nice features: they are computationally cheap, robust against data noise, easy to implement, work even with data only from one single incident. By some elegant multilevel techniques, we proposed new multilevel sampling algorithms, which have same desired features as direct sampling methods, for identifying multiple multiscale inhomogeneous media [10,12]. When an inverse problem involves convection-dominated diffusion or Navier-Stokes or Maxwell equations, its inversion becomes highly challenging and unstable due to convection-dominancy or non-physical reinforcement of Gauss’ laws. Hence we developed two new operator-splitting methods for these convection-dominated systems [13] and a stable edge-element formulation that avoids solutions of any saddle-point system for time-harmonic or time-dependent Maxwell equations [4]. When solving inverse problems, most existing methods that involve SVD decompositions may not work well if the problems are large-scale with general Tikhonov regularizations. Therefore we constructed several randomized SVD algorithms that transform large-scale inverse problems into much smaller and more stable problems but still achieve the same accuracy as the existing methods [14]. Solutions of many nonlinear inverse problems often encounter strong discontinuity or singularity and standard discretization schemes may generate poor solutions. We developed adaptive methods for recovering Robin coefficients in elliptic and parabolic equations, which can adaptively refine meshes based on error estimators such that the resulting meshes can accurately capture the discontinuity and singularity of the forward solution and Robin coefficient [15]. Our research results were published mostly in the best applied math journals, such as SIAM (5), IP (4), IPI (1), M2AN (1), JMPA (1), JSC (1).

404611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
404611.value: We have developed and studied in this project one-level and two-level parallel space-time domain decomposition methods for the inverse problem of recovering the intensities and locations of moving source distributions in heat conduction systems. This is the first space-time DDMs that get rid of nearly all sequential steps in the KKT systems arising from the Tikhonov regularized minimization formulations of inverse source problems, and they enjoy very satisfactory parallel speed-ups and scalability. In addition, we have also constructed in this project some effective preconditioners for the edge-element discrete systems arising from the PML electromagnetic scattering problems. When the preconditioners are combined with our new DDMs they can accelerate the numerical resolutions of the highly nonlinear inverse scattering problems essentially. These DDMs and preconditioners are very promising and rather general and should be developed also for many other severely ill-posed nonlinear inverse problems as well. This will be very important research projects for our future research, and the results and theories we have achieved and developed in this project should be fundamental to our future research.

404611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
404611.value: The current high-performance supercomputers require highly parallel numerical algorithms in order to fully develop their parallel efficiencies. But most existing stable and popular methods for large-scale physical, engineering and scientific computing are of severe sequential nature, hence have very low parallel speed-up and scalability with respect to the total number of cores and CPUs used. Domain decomposition methods (DDMs) are proved to be one of the most natural and successful methodologies to design efficient parallel algorithms for mathematical PDE (partial differential equation) models that are widely used in physical, engineering and scientific computing. However, DDMs have been developed so far only for direct PDE problems, and little has been done in literature for DDMs for linear and nonlinear inverse problems of PDEs. Inverse problems are frequently encountered in many areas of applications, and are mostly mathematically ill-posed and much more challenging to solve numerically than direct problems. In this project we have developed and studied a series of new efficient DDMs for solving several practically important inverse problems, including inverse acoustic and electromagnetic scattering problems, diffusive optical tomography, electrical impedance tomography, imaging wave-penetrable objects in ocean, and recovering intensity and location of moving heat sources.

404711.label: Project Title(Chinese)
404711.value: 变换结构方程模型及非正态数据的统计分析

404711.label: Project Objectives
404711.value: To establish a novel transformation SEM for analyzing various kinds of highly non-normal data. The proposed model will have the following features. (i) Nonparametric transformations are applied to the response variables to satisfy common model assumptions of SEMs in the resulting model, thereby producing more reliable results. (ii) Fixed covariates are incorporated in both measurement and structural equations to achieve a better model. Moreover, some extensions of the proposed model will be developed to cope with complicated real data. To develop novel and sound statistical methods for estimation of the proposed model. A Bayesian approach, coupled with P-splines and efficient sampling techniques, will be developed to estimate unknown transformation functions, parameters, and latent variables. To develop efficient computer programs for producing accurate results and to post these programs onto freely available websites for general use. We will try our best to make the codes user-friendly through freely available software, such as WinBUGS and R. To apply the developed methodologies in the analysis of real datasets that are relevant to Hong Kong and elsewhere. The current project is motivated by a study of the dropout behavior on a treatment program preventing polydrug use in UCLA. The main interest is to investigate how drug use and convicted crime affects treatment retention, and how this retention will affect future drug use. One difficulty is that the distributions of most variables are extremely non-normal. Hence, results cannot be obtained by existing SEMs and packages. Another motivated example is a study on diabetic kidney disease conducted by the Institute of Diabetes at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. In this study, some interesting phenotype latent variables that affect kidney disease were measured by highly non-normal observed variables; hence, the proposed transformation SEM is important for achieving correct results.

404711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
404711.value: In behavioral, social, and psychological sciences, the most widely used models in assessing latent variables are the structural equation models (SEMs). When analyzing SEMs with continuous variables, most existing statistical methods and software have been developed based on the crucial assumption that the response variables are normally distributed with constant variances. Although some recently developed parametric and nonparametric methods can partially address the violation of this assumption, they encounter serious difficulties in handling data with extremely non-normal distributions, such as highly skewed, U-shaped, and other irregular distributions. The transformation model is a useful tool for building a relationship between response variables and a bundle of explanatory variables, which will allow the resulting model to justify the model assumptions and thus produce more reliable results. One problem with the parametric transformation model is that the choice of transformation is usually restricted to the power or shifted power family. The limited flexibility of this parametric family could cause important features of the distribution to be missed. A more comprehensive approach is to estimate the transformation in a nonparametric way. However, no statistical methods have been developed for analyzing these kinds of transformation SEMs. Our main objective is to address the above problems adequately from both theoretical and practical perspectives. Our goals are as follows: (1) To establish a novel transformation SEM for handling various kinds of highly non-normal data and stabilizing error variances simultaneously. The proposed model will have the following features: (i) nonparametric transformations will be applied to response variables so that the resulting model can justify the model assumptions in SEMs; (ii) fixed covariates will be incorporated both into the measurement and the structural equations to help establish a better model. Various extensions of the proposed model will also be investigated. (2) To develop novel and sound statistical methods and efficient algorithms for the (i) estimation of unknown transformations, parameters and latent variables, and (ii) model comparison. (3) To develop efficient and dependable computer programs to produce statistical results and post these programs onto freely available websites for general use. (4) To apply the developed methodologies to analyze real datasets relevant to Hong Kong and elsewhere.

404711.label: Realisation of objectives
404711.value: We have fully achieved the project objectives specified in the proposal: 1. A novel transformation SEM for analyzing various kinds of highly non-normal data has been established. As specified, the proposed model has the following features. (i) Nonparametric transformations are applied to the response variables to produce highly reliable results. (ii) Fixed covariates are incorporated in both measurement and structural equations to achieve a better model. We have also developed various extensions of the proposed model to cope with complicated real data. The features in Item 1 of Section 5.2 (related to model establishment) are fully incorporated in the proposed model. 2. Sound statistical methods for estimation of the proposed model have been developed. A Bayesian approach, coupled with P-splines and efficient sampling techniques, has been developed to estimate unknown transformation functions, parameters, and latent variables. The satisfactory performance of the proposed methodologies has been well demonstrated by simulation studies in the publications listed in Section 8. The objectives in Item 2 of Section 5.2 (related to methodological development) are fully achieved. 3. We have developed efficient computer programs for producing accurate estimation results. The computer codes, many of which were written in freely available software such as WinBUGS and R, have been published or provided in freely available websites for general use (see the corresponding papers in Section 8). The objectives in Item 3 of Section 5.2 (related to computer programs) are fully achieved. 4. We have applied the developed methodologies to analyze a large number of real datasets that are relevant to Hong Kong and elsewhere. The real-life applications include but are not limited to (1) a study of the dropout behavior on a treatment program preventing polydrug use in UCLA. (2) A study on diabetic kidney disease conducted by the Institute of Diabetes at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. (3) A study of the National Longitudinal Surveys of Youth in the US. (4) A study of the medical cost for chronic heart failure patients. (5) A study on the Interuniversity Consortium for Political and Social Research. (6) A study of osteoporosis prevention and control for old Chinese men. (7) A study of the daily S&P 500 Composite Index. Important findings and insights have been obtained through these real applications. The objectives in Item 4 of Section 5.2 (related to applications) are fully achieved.

404711.label: Major findings and research outcome
404711.value: Our major findings and research outcomes are represented by 15 publications; see "Research Output" in Section 8 of Part C). Specifically, 1. We have established a novel transformation SEM to analyze highly non-normal data. Several extensions of the proposed model, such as transformation nonlinear SEMs and transformation SEMs with missing data, have been developed. Please refer to Items 2, 3, 4, 7, and 15 in Section 8. In addition, we have established other semiparametric SEMs and statistical models for analyzing non-normal, longitudinal, heterogeneous, and/or survival data. These outcomes are relevant but beyond the objectives of the original proposal. They are novel and important developments in statistics and other fields. Please refer to Items 5, 8, 10-13 in Section 8. 2. We have developed sound statistical methods, including Bayesian methods, P-splines smoothing techniques, and efficient sampling procedures, to estimate unknown transformation functions, parameters, and latent variables. Please refer to Items 1-4, 6-8, 10, and 15 in Section 8. In addition, some important issues beyond estimation, such as model comparison, variable selection, and statistical diagnosis, have been considered. Please refer to Items 1, 3, 4, 9, and 14. 3. We have applied the proposed methodologies to many real studies and obtained important findings. The real applications includes (1) a study of the dropout behavior on a treatment program preventing polydrug use in UCLA (Items 2 and 4 in Section 8) . 404711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
404711.value: A possible extension of the current transformation SEM is to consider a joint modeling approach, which combines the transformation SEM and other statistical models to analyze longitudinal or other complex data. We aim to develop Bayesian approach to conduct the analysis. As a new project, this further development requires substantial effort in the future.

404711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
404711.value: Structural equation models (SEMs) are the most important models to assess the interrelationships among latent and observed variables. Most existing SEMs assume that data are normally distributed with constant variance. However, this assumption is often violated in practice, which may lead to incorrect results and/or divergence of computer programs. Although some recent methods can partially address this issue, they encounter difficulties in handling extremely non-normal data. This research project proposed a novel transformation SEM to tackle the problem. The new statistical methods developed in this project contribute significantly to the field of SEM and statistical modeling. The methodologies have been applied to many real studies, and important findings and new insights were obtained. The major results are represented by 15 publications in highly ranked international journals, such as Structural Equation Modeling: A Multidisciplinary Journal (1/99, rank top 1%), Statistical Methods and Medical Research (1/122, rank top 1%), Journal of the American Statistical Association (14/122, rank top 11%), and IEEE Transactions and Automatic Control (6/58, rank top 10%), as well as other prestigious international journals, such as Psychometrika, Statistica Sinica, Scandinavian Journal of Statistics, and Statistics in Medicine. Important extensions of the proposed model (beyond the project objectives) have been considered.

410111.value: 隨機、半隨機、穩定及偽隨機的實例：啟發式方法的局限性

410111.label: Project Objectives
410111.value: To analyze heuristics for combinatorial optimization problems from the perspective of pseudorandomness To discover deterministic ways of generating hard instances for heuristics To initiate a study of hardness for typical instances based on the pseudorandomness perspective, by applying new and existing tools from the theory of probabilistically checkable proofs
rows: To analyze heuristics for combinatorial optimization problems from the perspective of pseudorandomness
To discover deterministic ways of generating hard instances for heuristics
To initiate a study of hardness for typical instances based on the pseudorandomness perspective, by applying new and existing tools from the theory of probabilistically checkable proofs

410111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
410111.value: In the theory of computation, NP-completeness is usually viewed as the gold standard of intractability for computational problems. However, hard instances of computational problems are rarely typical and large instances of NP-complete problems can sometimes be tackled by heuristics. On the other hand, there are NP problems such as those used in cryptography that are believed to be intractable even for heuristics. The theory of average-case complexity has so far been unable to explain why certain NP problems are hard to solve even on typical instances. On the algorithmic side, there has been more progress in designing rigorous heuristics for typical instances of NP problems. The limitations of these heuristics are, however, not well understood. We propose to study the computational complexity of typical instances of NP-problems through the perspective of pseudorandomness. Our starting point is the observation that heuristics for random instances of NP problems also work for *pseudorandom instances*, as their analysis merely relies on combinatorial properties that the random instance is likely to possess. We view the task of identifying these pseudorandom properties as crucial in understanding the success of the heuristics. Potentially, this perspective could lead to a useful theory of computational hardness for typical instances: By abstracting away the randomness, we would bypass the obstacles of average-case complexity and be left with the task of constructing *worst-case* hard instances of NP-problems with a certain pseudorandom structure. We sketch an approach for obtaining such hard instances of the planted clique problem using existing tools like PCPs of proximity. 在計算理論中，NP 完全問題通常被視為計算問題難解度的黃金標準。然而，計算問題中比較難的實例往往不具有代表性，而 NP 完全問題中存在大量實例是可以用啟發式方法去處理的。另一方面，實例中也存在即使使用啟發式方法也是很難解決的 NP 問題，例如那些被應用於密碼學上的問題。 平均情況複雜性理論至今仍無法解釋為甚麼在某些 NP 問題上，即使是其典型實例，都很難解決。而在算法方面，人們在 NP 問題的典型實例上設計嚴格啟發式方法已經取得較多的進展。 然而，啟發式的局限性並沒有被人們充分理解。 我們提出通過偽隨機的角度來研究 NP 問題上典型實例的計算複雜性。我們的出發點是觀察到應用於NP 問題隨機實例上的啟發式方法，也同樣可以應用於偽隨機實例上。這是因為相關的分析，僅依賴於隨機實例中很可能擁有的組合性質。我們認為確認這些偽隨機性，對瞭解啟發式方法是至關重要的。 這種觀點有可能開創一個用於典型實例的計算複雜性理論：通過把隨機性抽象化，我們可以繞過平均情況複雜性這個障礙物，而只需要構造具有某種偽隨機結構的 NP 問題最難實例 。我們用已存在的工具，如接近性的概率可驗證明 (PCPs of proximity)，去描述一個獲得嵌入團 (planted clique) 問題最難實例的方法。

410111.label: Realisation of objectives
410111.value: Early on in this project we realized that the most productive way to tackle algorithms for random instances is by looking at combinatorial examples from cryptography, so we tackled the objectives from this direction. Several of our works completed as part of this project give new examples of functions that are simple to describe and calculate, but are difficult for heuristics such as linearization and statistical query learning to handle. We concluded that such heuristics fail even on very simple types of instances. At the beginning of the project we had high hopes for applying insights from the study of probabilistically checkable proofs to gain insights on the behaviour of algorithms on typical instances. However, as it is becoming apparent in the work on this project as well as in other studies, these methods do not appear to be suited for understanding the behaviour of random instances. Therefore this objective was only partially realized.

410111.label: Major findings and research outcome
410111.value: Our work shows that, as a general rule, even very simple types of instances can be intractable for heuristics. Specifically, we obtain the following conclusions for the given type of instance and model of computation: * In the work "Sparse extractor families for all the entropy", we show that an extremely simple probabilistic construction is a randomness extractor, i.e. its output looks statistically random to any test. * In the work "Hard Functions for Low-degree Polynomials over Prime Fields" we give a class of functions that have extremely low correlation with all low-degree polynomials, so such functions appear random any heuristic that can be modeled by a polynomial in this class. In the work "Pseudorandomness for width two branching programs" we give examples of low-entropy distributions that look random to a width two branching program, which can be viewed as a specific low-complexity heuristic. * In the work "Candidate Weak Pseudorandom Functions in AC0 ◦ MOD2" we design, in some sense, the simplest possible functions that appear random when random input-output samples of the function are available. Moreover, we prove unconditionally that two important classes of heuristics -- linearization techniques and statistical query learning techniques -- cannot distinguish samples of our function from random ones. * The work "Limits of provable security for homomorphic encryption" gives a different type of negative conclusion: Homomorphic encryption schemes, while believed to be secure not only theoretically but also against various heuristics, cannot be proved secure under the assumption that P does not equal NP. * In "Negation-limited formulas", an example of a function is given that is hard to compute, even on average, by any formula that uses a small number of negations.

410111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
410111.value: Our research indicates that the obstacles in understanding the power and limitations of heuristics are fundamentally complexity-theoretic, as there is no tractable model that unifies the two most powerful types of heuristics we know of: linear algebra and combinatorial optimization. An important, long-term objective for future research is to bridge this gap.

410111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
410111.value: Heuristics are algorithms that cannot be proved to work, but often perform well in practice. Cryptography gives a way to create conjecturally intractable instances for all types of algorithms, including heuristics. In this projects, we leverage the insights from cryptography and computational complexity theory to demonstrate that in many cases, even very simple problem instances can be difficult for heuristics to handle.

410211.label: Project Objectives
410211.value: To develop a unified model and study its properties, for the problem of stochastic scheduling with uncertain loss of work subject to machine breakdowns; To characterize index policies and investigate their optimality by theoretical analysis and computational studies; To develop solution algorithms to compute exact or approximate solutions for extended and generalized problems; To apply the general theory to specific industrial problems to produce more structural results and deeper insights.

410211.label: Realisation of objectives
410211.value: (1) The main challenge in our modelling part is how to formulate the uncertain loss of work due to machine breakdowns. Our key idea is to model the uncertain losses of work caused by breakdowns as a semi-Markov transition process. This treatment enables us to tackle various situations with uncertain loss of work in a general and unified framework, and allows us to develop a unified model to deal with any level of uncertain losses due to machine breakdowns. (2) To derive the optimal dynamic polices, we have utilized the methodology of multi-armed bandit processes. As a result, a set of Gittins indices have been established as solutions to a system of integral equations. Optimal solutions for a number of problems with specific loss patterns are consequently derived. (3) By exploiting the structure of the problems being studied, we have developed algorithms to compute optimal or approximate solutions. Numerical studies are conducted to evaluate these solution algorithms. (4) Applications to experience rating problem in general insurance, optimal production and delivery problem in transportation systems subject to random breakdowns, and operations management problems in supply chains subject to uncertainties and randomness, are investigated. Insights about the applicability of the theory in real problems are obtained.

410211.label: Major findings and research outcome
410211.value: (1) We established a model based on semi-Markov transitions, to formulate the stochastic scheduling problem subject to random machine breakdowns with partial loss of work. The model is a general and unified one, which can deal with jobs with arbitrary random processing times, general stochastic breakdown processes, and uncertain losses of work with general transition probabilities. It subsumes the two categories of stochastic scheduling models that have been extensively studied in the existing literature: (i) no loss, and (ii) full loss. (2) We characterized the optimal dynamic policies, in both the class of restricted policies, and the class of unrestricted policies. We found that the optimal dynamic policies can be constructed with a set of Gittins indices governed by a system of integral equations. We further found that the solutions for the integral equations are unique and can be expressed by an infinite series, and the integral equations reduce to a finite set of linear algebraic equations when the processing times take a finite number of values. (3) We obtained optimal static and nonpreemptive dynamic policies, which generalized the previous results in the literature to situations with partial losses of work. Furthermore, we examined the structural properties of a number of problems, and developed algorithms to compute optimal or approximate solutions. Numerical experiments were also conducted to evaluate the performance of the algorithms. Results in Items (1)-(3) above have been summarized in journal papers [1]-[3] and conference paper [1] (see Part (C) ) for publication. (4) We investigated a stochastic scheduling problem, where perishable products are to be processed for an export market, whereas the transporter for the export market is experiencing a major breakdown with unknown recovery time. We developed the optimal policies on the optimal waiting time on each finished product, and the optimal postponement and sequencing decisions on the unfinished products. Initial results on this probem were derived before the start of this project, and had been revised and enhanced substantially as a part of the work we conducted during this project. A paper was subsequently accepted and published [1]. (5) Applications of the theory to other practical problems, including the credibility estimation problem in general insurance, service channel choice problem, core sorting problems in remanufacturing systems, trade credit insurance problem in manufacturing systems, and dynamic lot-sizing model for durable products, were investigated; see papers [3]-[8]. Significant results were obtained for solving these problems.

410211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
410211.value: Further research can be conducted in the following two directions: (1) Characterizations of index-based policies, or analytical policies, that are optimal or sub-optimal, given the structure of a class of problems. (2) Models involving multiple machines. For (1), the key idea is how to exploit the structure of the problems, to identify the policies and prove their optimality under certain conditions. For (2), we can try to generalize the results obtained in this project for the single-machine setting to the multi-machine cases. A kind of decomposition-coordination approach may be considered, which might decompose the multi-machine problem into a set of decoupled single-machine problems, then coordinate to tackle the couplings among these single-machine problems.

410211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
410211.value: Many industries require scheduling decisions to process jobs on available machines, which are subject to stochastic breakdowns. Extensive studies have been conducted on problems in two calsses: (i) the no-loss models, assuming that the work achieved before the breakdown is not lost; and (ii) the full-loss models, assuming that the work achieved is totally lost. In reality, however, the work achieved is neither fully preserved nor totally lost after a breakdown. The main objective of this project is to develop a general approach that can deal with any partial loss of work. We have established a unified model that can formulate any level of losses of work due to random breakdowns. We have characterized the optimal policies in numerous situations. Furthermore, we have applied the theoretical results to several practical problems, including optimal production and delivery in a transportation system subject to random breakdowns, experience rating in general insurance, and operational decisions in manufacturing/remanufacturing systems. The theoretical work of this project provides a general framework for solving problems with partial loss due to breakdowns, and the application work not only reveals insights about the theory, but also provides valuable results to support the decision making on the respective problems in practice.

411011.label: Project Title(Chinese)
411011.value: 理解和优化P2P系统的延时性能

411011.label: Project Objectives
411011.value: To develop a P2P system model that enables systematic delay analysis. Such model should allow full characterization of the delay region of P2P systems. (Recall that delay region is the set of all possible user delay vectors that can be achieved). Moreover, this model should also allow us to jointly study throughput and delay performance. We have successfully established one such model for several cases out of the 16 cases in Fig. 1. Based on the promising results, we hope to be able to extend our model to cover the rest cases. To formulate delay optimization problems and develop algorithms for attain the optimal performance. We are particularly interested in optimizing two system-wide delay performance, namely the worst user delay and average user delay. These investigations are relevant to P2P streaming and file sharing systems. For instance, the average user delay corresponds to the average start-up delay in a P2P streaming system and the average downloading time in a file sharing system. To design algorithms to attain the optimal throughput-delay trade-off of P2P systems. In particular, we plan to maximize the throughput given a user delay requirement, and to optimize user delays given a required throughput. We believe these two conditioned optimizations are important for maximizing video quality in P2P conferencing systems and minimizing the worst-case start-up delay in P2P streaming systems, respectively.

411011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
411011.value: By utilizing the user upload bandwidth to help distribute content at low server infrastructure cost, Peer-to-peer (P2P) techniques have enabled cost-effective content distribution in the past decade. Recent studies [35, 30, 16, 17], however, indicate that the practical performance of P2P systems can be far from their theoretical optimal. There has been work studying the performance limit of P2P systems, namely throughput and delay, to understand and unleash their potential. Many of these work focus on maximizing system throughput subject to user capacity constraints (see [12] for a recent survey). Compared to throughput, delay performance of P2P systems is much less understood. Only very recently, researchers started to bound the worst-case delay in P2P streaming systems [24, 9], and to reduce the average-case delay under various settings [31, 19]. These pioneering results are exciting, yet a comprehensive understanding of the delay performance is still lacking. This project aims to fill in this gap, and seek answers to the following fundamental open questions: - How to characterize and attain the feasible region of user delays, i.e., the set of all possible delay vectors that can be achieved by appropriate design of the P2P protocols? - How to characterize and achieve the optimal throughput-delay trade-off in P2P systems? These questions are challenging, but of great practical importance. For instance, consider a P2P conferencing system where a group of users interact through video and audio communications. It is critical to maximize the aggregate throughput subject to a user-to-user delay constraint in order to enable effective interactions among users. This corresponds to characterizing and achieving a single point on the optimal throughput-delay trade-off curve. Our preliminary results are encouraging, and indicate that it is possible to achieve our objectives by combining calibrated graph modeling, elegant tools from network coding theory, optimization, and combinatorial algorithms. For example, we are able to characterize the delay region of P2P file sharing systems and show how to optimize delay performance [32]. We are also be able to characterize and achieve the optimal throughput-delay trade-off in certain P2P streaming systems [20, 22, 23]. We plan to build upon these initial results and further develop a framework for understanding and jointly optimizing the throughput-delay performance in P2P systems. We also plan to work with major US and Chinese online communication companies to implement our solutions in practice. P2P内容组播技术，通过利用用户上行带宽来协助分发内容，可以有效减小在服务器基础设施的投入。这项技术在过去十年中已被成功应用到商业领域减小大规模文件及视频组播的成本。然而，最近的研究[35，30，16，17]表明P2P系统的实际性能远远尚未达到它们的理论最佳。已经有工作学习的P2P系统的性能，即吞吐量和延迟限制，来理解和发挥他们的潜力。许多这些工作的重点放在最大限度地提高系统的吞吐量（见最近的一份综述，[12]）。 相比吞吐量， 对P2P系统的延迟性能的了解是要少得多。仅仅在最近，研究人员才开始在研究P2P流媒体系统的最坏延时表现[24, 10]，并研究如何减少各种设置下的平均延迟表现[31，19]。这些开拓性的成果令人振奋，但对延迟性能仍然缺乏一个的全面了解。 该项目旨在填补这一差距，并寻求下列基本的悬而未决的问题的答案： - 如何判断一组用户延迟是否可以被系统实现，如何通过设计适当的P2P协议来实现任何一组可被实现的用户延时？ - 如何实现最佳P2P系统中的吞吐量-延迟的综合表现？ 这些问题都具有挑战性，但具有十分重要的现实意义。例如，考虑一个P2P会议系统，一组用户通过音频和视频通信交互。最大化的总吞吐量受到用户到用户的延迟约束。这对应到实现最佳的吞吐量，延迟权衡曲线上的一个点。 我们的初步结果是令人鼓舞的，表明一个全面的理解是可能的。并且我们可以把网络编码理论，优化和组合算法相结合，来设计符合我们需求的算法。例如，我们能够描述的P2P文件共享系统的延迟区，并显示如何优化时延性能[32]。我们也能在某些P2P流媒体系统中实现最佳的吞吐量-延迟的综合表现[20，22，23]。 我们计划在这些初步结果基础上，进一步完善理解和共同优化的P2P系统中的吞吐量-时延性能。我们还计划与主要的美国和中国网络通信公司工作，在实践中实现我们的解决方案。

411011.label: Realisation of objectives
411011.value: For objectives 1 and 2, we have successfully developed delay models for P2P system (modeled as either an edge-capacitated graph or a node-capacitated graph). Based on these models, we developed systematic technique to characterize the delay-region and delay-constrained capacity region by solving optimization problems. Solving the optimization problems also allows us to design solutions for maximizing delay performance or delay-constrained throughput performance for various P2P systems. Out of the 16 cases, the 8 cases without node degree bounds are addressed by solving LPs or convex problems; the 8 cases with degree bounds are combinatorial in nature and challenging to solve. We tackle the difficulty by applying our recently-proposed Markov approximation framework to design practical algorithms to solve the combinatorial problem approximately with tune-able performance gap. The results are very refreshing in my home opinion and we have applied them to successfully develop solutions for file transfer and streaming scenarios, with average delay and worst-case delay as performance matric. For objective 3, we have developed optimization-based algorithms for delay-constrained maximum-throughput communication and throughput-guarantee minimum-delay communication for P2P systems. Our algorithms also extend to regular communication scenarios beyond P2P. Some results are under submission to premier venues. We are applying the overall results to application domains beyond P2P systems as well, for example, in delay-constrained wireless communication.

411011.label: Major findings and research outcome
411011.value: Recent development of Peer-to-peer (P2P) systems calls for optimized design for delay-sensitive applications. This project aims at answering this call. In particular, we have developed delay models for P2P system and leverage these models to characterize the user-delay region and delay-constrained capacity region, by solving corresponding optimization problems. We also obtain solutions for maximizing delay performance or delay-constrained throughput performance during the process. We have applied the solutions to solve problems in file transfer and streaming scenarios with delay performance in consideration.

411011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
411011.value: Our project focuses on delay-minimization and delay-constrained throughput maximization under static settings where users and network typologies are fixed. In practice, however, systems have dynamics in users joining/leaving and link capacity and topology fluctuation. How will such dynamics affect the delay performance of the system, and how to exploit the dynamics to improve performance of the systems are two intriguing and important questions to answer. We believe the answers deserve a thorough investigation in the future.

411011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
411011.value: Our developed delay models enable systematic modeling of delay performance of P2P systems, as well as regular networks that can be modeled as directed acyclic graphs. Our models allow one to characterize the delay-related performance of the systems (such as throughput of delay-sensitive multimedia communication). We believe that our results are important for the research community as well as the practical system designer to understand the fundamental limit of delay-related communication over P2P systems as well as over conventional underlay networks, and to release the full potential of P2P system on supporting delay-sensitive applications.

411211.label: Project Title(Chinese)
411211.value: 挖掘和查询异质及多维的信息网络：算法及应用

411211.label: Project Objectives
411211.value: Designing an information network analysis engine for mining large-scale heterogeneous and multidimensional information networks. We plan to construct large-scale information networks from two data sources: the DBLP bibliography data (http://www.informatik.uni-trier.de/~ley/db), and the SourceForge open source software development portal (http://sourceforge.net). We will extract different types of objects, object attributes and their relationships from the above data sources to form heterogeneous and multidimensional information networks. We plan to evaluate our proposed mining and querying techniques on the two information networks. Clustering heterogeneous and multidimensional information networks. Information network clustering is very effective for analyzing and visualizing large networks, as well as for many other tasks including community detection, name disambiguation, etc. The task is more challenging than the traditional graph clustering problem, because the clustering algorithm needs to handle different node and linkage types, which may carry different semantic meanings and have different degrees of importance. The algorithm also needs to combine the link-based structure information and node associated multidimensional attribute information into the clustering objective function, and achieves both structural cohesiveness and attribute homogeneity within clusters. In addition, we plan to use the information network clustering approach to solve the name disambiguation problem, by modeling the DBLP bibliographic data into a heterogeneous and multidimensional information network. Mining discriminative graph patterns from heterogeneous and multidimensional information networks. In many applications, we can attach a class label to an information network according to a certain criterion. For example, given an information network representing an open source software project and the collaborations between the developers, we can attach a class label "successful" or "unsuccessful" based on the number of downloads or the rating of the concerned project. It is beneficial to combine the information network and the class label for indepth analysis. We propose to take a discriminative graph mining approach to analyze the difference on collaboration patterns between successful and unsuccessful projects and potentially identify the socio-technical factors that determine the success or failure of an open source project. We will design a discriminative graph mining algorithm that can handle heterogeneous and multidimensional information networks efficiently. Querying network statistics on heterogeneous and multidimensional information networks. Users may be interested in querying various information network statistics. We propose to support two types of queries: shortest path distance query and structural similarity query. To efficiently support a shortest path distance query, we propose to use a reference node embedding technique for offline indexing, and use the embedded distances to provide an estimated shortest path distance based on triangle inequality. To efficiently support a structural similarity query, we propose to design a novel index structure and an approximate match model which allows approximate match on nodes and edges.
