411211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
411211.value: The aim of this project is to study the modeling and construction of large-scale heterogeneous and multidimensional information networks, as well as efficient mining, indexing and query processing techniques on the information networks. In the modern information age, many large-scale networked systems are available for analysis from different application domains, including the Internet, social networks, sensor networks, road networks, biological networks and communication networks, etc. These networked systems usually involve objects of heterogeneous types interconnected by different types of relationships. In addition, the objects and the linkages can be associated with multidimensional attribute information. Without loss of generality, we call such networked systems as heterogeneous and multidimensional information networks. Such gigantic information networks usually contain rich information of the involved objects and their interactions. To discover the hidden knowledge from the information networks and further enhance our understanding, we need indepth, efficient and scalable mining and analysis tools. In this project, we plan to construct two information networks from two real data sources: the DBLP computer science bibliography data and the SourceForge open source software super-repository. We propose to investigate the methodologies and algorithms for the construction, mining, indexing and query processing on heterogeneous and multidimensional information networks based on the two information networks we construct. We will also investigate the broad applications of the proposed mining techniques. We plan to build an information network mining and query processing engine to support various functionalities, including information network clustering and its application to name disambiguation, discriminative graph pattern mining, information network indexing and query processing techniques. This project is much more challenging than traditional graph mining and search problems, because the information networks involve (1) heterogeneous objects and relationships which carry different semantic meanings, (2) multidimensional attribute information associated with nodes and linkages which could be categorical, numerical, textual, or spatiotemporal information, rather than a single node or edge label, and (3) temporal information which causes the evolution of network structures. Through this study, we believe the construction, mining and querying of heterogeneous and multidimensional information networks will discover the rich hidden knowledge from information networks and thus largely enhance our understanding of the gigantic and complex information networks. The proposed mining techniques, for example, name disambiguation, will substantially improve the quality of the information networks by reducing noise, uncertainty and duplication, and hence benefit other related tasks such as data cleaning, data integration, information retrieval, etc.

411211.label: Realisation of objectives
411211.value: The four project objectives have been achieved satisfactorily with rich and comprehensive research output. The realisation of each objective is described below. Objective 1. We have constructed a set of large information networks including bibliographic networks, social networks, road networks, programming API networks, and so on. We have extracted different types of objects and attributes, for example, authors, papers, conferences/journals in the DBLP bibliographic network, and their relationships. In these information networks, we studied various interesting problems with practical applications. They also serve as the testbed for evaluating our algorithms. Objective 2. We studied clustering heterogeneous and multidimensional information networks with attribute information, and did the following investigations in this direction. (2.1) We proposed a model-based clustering framework which combines the link-based structure and node associated multidimensional attribute information. The clustering problem can be transformed into a probabilistic inference problem. This work was published in SIGMOD’2012 Conference, and it was further extended and published in TKDD journal in 2014. In addition, we studied subspace clustering in attributed graph where only a subspace of attributes are considered for clustering the networks. We proposed an algorithm SCMAG using a cell-based subspace clustering approach. This work was published in Information Sciences journal in 2015. (2.2) Furthermore, we studied the clustering of information networks from a new perspective. In particular, we studied, given a user in an information network, how to search the communities that the specific user participates in. This is a more user-centered and personalized search of community structures in an information network. We proposed to use, k-truss, a concept of dense subgraph, to model the communities due to the nice structural properties brought by k-truss. Then we designed compact index of the truss values of the edges in an information network. Community search can be processed efficiently based on the index. This work was published in SIGMOD’2014 Conference. Later, we continued the research along this direction, and proposed to search closest communities with very tight diameters by removing free riders. This work was published in PVLDB journal in 2015. (2.3) In addition, we attempted to solve the name disambiguation problem under this framework, and our solution appeared in PVLDB journal in 2014. Objective 3. To mine discriminative subgraphs from information networks, we took a feature selection approach. We proposed to select discriminative graph features among a set of subgraphs. We also took diversity into consideration in the feature selection process. We showed the superior performance of our selected discriminative and diversified subgraph features in classifying graph data. The work was published in CIKM’2012 Conference. Such discriminative subgraphs can also be used as clustering features, as shown in another work published in DASFAA’2012 Conference. Further along this direction, we studied how to extract discriminative subgraphs as features for link prediction in information networks with positive/negative opinions. Such discriminative subgraphs are elementary graph motifs with positive/negative signs on the edges. This work was published in WWW’2013 Conference. Objective 4. We studied various types of queries on information networks, and did the following research. (4.1) We studied the shortest distance query and designed a local landmark scheme to answer this query. This scheme uses a query-dependent local landmark, which is defined as the lowest common ancestor of the two query nodes in a shortest path tree. The local landmark scheme can greatly reduce the shortest distance estimation error to 0.0001-- 0.001, which is significantly more accurate than the state-of-the-art landmark embedding approach. This work was published in ICDE’2012 Conference, and it was further extended and published in TKDE journal in 2014. Along this direction, we employed the shortest distance estimation technique for solving other related, more complex queries, such as k-hop reachability (with papers published in PVLDB 2012 and VLDB Journal 2014), weight constraint reachability (with paper published in VLDB Journal 2013), and top-k nearest keyword search (with paper published in PVLDB 2013). (4.2) We studied the structural similarity query and designed a method for finding top-k graphs in a graph database that are most similar to a query graph. We defined a new similarity measure based on the maximum common subgraph of two graphs. We proposed an algorithm to answer the top-k graph similarity query using distance lower bounds, and evaluated its efficiency on real graph datasets. This work was published in EDBT’2012 Conference. Another related query we studied is top-k structural diversity search in an information network. The structural diversity of a node is defined as the number of connected components that the node is involved in. Such a measure reflects the diversity of a user in social contexts. We designed a novel index structure that can support the search of nodes with the highest structural diversity scores efficiently. Our work appeared in PVLDB 2013. (4.3) In addition, we studied subgraph search in an information network that satisfies a user’s information need expressed in natural language phrases. A useful application of this query is searching the usage patterns in the API library of a programming language, given a user’s query intention on some classes/methods. To find a suitable subgraph that matches a user’s information need, we must ensure not only the textual similarity between the nodes and the user’s query, but also the structural cohesiveness of the returned subgraph. This work was published in FSE’2012 Conference. Overall, we achieved these four project objectives adequately with solid research output.

rows: Designing an information network analysis engine for mining large-scale heterogeneous and multidimensional information networks. We plan to construct large-scale information networks from two data sources: the DBLP bibliography data (http://www.informatik.uni-trier.de/~ley/db), and the SourceForge open source software development portal (http://sourceforge.net). We will extract different types of objects, object attributes and their relationships from the above data sources to form heterogeneous and multidimensional information networks. We plan to evaluate our proposed mining and querying techniques on the two information networks.

Clustering heterogeneous and multidimensional information networks. Information network clustering is very effective for analyzing and visualizing large networks, as well as for many other tasks including community detection, name disambiguation, etc. The task is more challenging than the traditional graph clustering problem, because the clustering algorithm needs to handle different node and linkage types, which may carry different semantic meanings and have different degrees of importance. The algorithm also needs to combine the link-based structure information and node associated multidimensional attribute information into the clustering objective function, and achieves both structural cohesiveness and attribute homogeneity within clusters. In addition, we plan to use the information network clustering approach to solve the name disambiguation problem, by modeling the DBLP bibliographic data into a heterogeneous and multidimensional information network.

Mining discriminative graph patterns from heterogeneous and multidimensional information networks. In many applications, we can attach a class label to an information network according to a certain criterion. For example, given an information network representing an open source software project and the collaborations between the developers, we can attach a class label "successful" or "unsuccessful" based on the number of downloads or the rating of the concerned project. It is beneficial to combine the information network and the class label for indepth analysis. We propose to take a discriminative graph mining approach to analyze the difference on collaboration patterns between successful and unsuccessful projects and potentially identify the socio-technical factors that determine the success or failure of an open source project. We will design a discriminative graph mining algorithm that can handle heterogeneous and multidimensional information networks efficiently.

Querying network statistics on heterogeneous and multidimensional information networks. Users may be interested in querying various information network statistics. We propose to support two types of queries: shortest path distance query and structural similarity query. To efficiently support a shortest path distance query, we propose to use a reference node embedding technique for offline indexing, and use the embedded distances to provide an estimated shortest path distance based on triangle inequality. To efficiently support a structural similarity query, we propose to design a novel index structure and an approximate match model which allows approximate match on nodes and edges.

411211.label: Major findings and research outcome
411211.value: The research outcome is as follows. Overall, there are 20 journal papers and 24 conference papers published from the research investigations in this project. 3 Doctor of Philosophy students and 4 Master of Philosophy students were trained over the past four years. The major findings are, heterogeneous and multidimensional information networks are a medium that carries rich and complex information in both structures and semantic meanings. They can model the entities, their profiles and their relationships in between in various application fields. In many such networks, community structures are manifested. We proposed a series of approaches and models that can detect or search meaningful communities in information networks (Objective 2). Also, different definitions of a community model lead to communities with different structural properties, and also lead to different mining techniques to discover them. The detected communities are useful for us to understand the network structure, and also useful for other downstream applications such as targeted advertising, recommendation, and so on. Discriminative subgraphs can be used as features for graph classification, clustering, link prediction, and so on. We proposed mining techniques for generating such discriminative features from information networks, and evaluated and demonstrated their effectiveness in graph classification, clustering and link prediction. (Objective 3) Many kinds of queries, including shortest distance, reachability, structural similarity search, can be issued on large-scale information networks to query the network statistics and structures. Such queries can be very useful for users to understand the networks. In this project, we studied a series of network queries, and designed corresponding index structures to support such queries. To operate on massive networks, the index should be compact in size but efficient in query processing. With the index and efficient search methods, we can process the network queries very efficiently on large information networks with tens of millions of nodes and edges. (Objective 4)

411211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
411211.value: With the rapid evolution and growth of information networks in various application fields, new and richer types of information and content are emerging from them. We believe there will be more opportunities and challenges arising from this prosperous field. Thus there is a lot of potential for further investigation in this direction. Based on our current research findings and expertise, we can continue to address new challenges. As a particular example, some social network platforms, such as Sina Weibo, allow users to follow others either publicly or privately. Thus the formed friendship network contains both public structures (visible to all) and private structures (only visible to the user himself). How to perform mining and analysis on such networks is still an open question, as the goal is to discover meaningful patterns while preserving privacy at the same time. It is a potential direction for further development, and we are considering to combine the graph mining techniques with privacy preserving techniques.

411211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
411211.value: The nature of this research project is to study the modeling and analytics of networks from different applications, such as social networks, road networks, with rich information, so that we can gain deeper understanding of such massive and complex networks. Accordingly, we designed models and methods for discovering hidden but useful knowledge from such networks. Our research outcome advances the state-of-the-art of research and makes contributions to the field. The research findings from our project can bring benefits to different user groups. For example, the network administrators can apply our techniques for better management and monitoring of the networks; the merchants can leverage the network properties to design their marketing and advertising strategies; and the end users can also use our solutions for acquiring useful information and satisfying their information needs.

411611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
411611.value: Video content delivery is an important application of the Internet. Various services are provided, including (a) file-downloading (and watch later); (b) multicast (watch together); and (c) Video-on-Demand (VoD) (watch whatever you want), with (c) being the most preferred when available. A pure client-server implementation is not scalable. Instead, various distributed service models are commonly adopted, including Content Delivery Networks (CDN), Local multicast (IPTV), and Peer-to-peer (P2P). With each of these distributed models, as long as the volume of content is large (larger than what a single server or peer can store), the content replication strategy is at the heart of the system design. P2P content replication, the decision of how to place content in the largest number of stores to satisfy changing patters of user requests, is the most challenging version of this problem. There are a few key thrusts in our focus that are different than previous studies. We focus on a streaming VoD service, in which the most important goal of content replication is to balance and exploit the peer uplink bandwidth used to serve a large number of video objects. In such a setting, our base model is able to derive general scaling laws relating server bandwidth requirements to number of videos and local (peer) storage size, based on different levels of correlation in video access patterns. In addition to such basic properties of streaming P2P VoD, we also study practical replication strategies that are suitable for implementation in a content distribution platform; namely the system is able to collect various information such as request rate, correlation in demand for different objects, current replication state etc, which can be used as input to the replication strategies. This allows the replication strategy to adapt to user request behaviors. Previous studies have focused on stationary video popularity models (including the study that won the best paper award in Infocom 2009), whereas we will try to formulate a dynamic popularity model through measurement. The dynamic popularity model will then allow us to compare our replication strategies to others studied under a stationary model. This is a very practical as well as academically interesting research problem. The PI has extensive research and consulting experiences in this research area. In the PI's opinion, good algorithms will be easily patentable. 411611.label: Realisation of objectives
411611.value: We are quite satisfied with our work in object 1 and 2. We have made important theoretical contribution towards the understanding of scaling laws and general properties of P2P-VoD systems. We have also analyzed a large scale contend distribution system from our collaborator (Tencent), and developed a novel and interesting workload model (Video Browsing Model) and proposed new strategies for optimizing the system in view of the workload. Regarding objective 3 and 4, we feel there are still interesting work to be done, which are indeed what we are working on at the moment. The popularity model we have used, though stochastic, is a stationary one. In other words, the most popular video remain most popular etc. In reality, video popularity changes over time, but the dynamics depends on many factors, such as how videos are recommended, how many videos enter the system each day, the time users spend on watching videos etc. We have some very recent publications on this topic which are outside the project period, and hence not included in this report.

411611.label: Major findings and research outcome
411611.value: In this research project over 2-3 years, we developed a general and practically useful theory of how to do content replication in a CDN-based (with P2P assistance) Video-on-Demand system. We have found theoretical bounds for CDN server load for given number of videos, number of peers, and storage at each peer. We have also unified the results under different assumptions of load scheduling. Another important result is how the CDN system and P2P system should complement each other in offering the VoD service - the P2P system should try to satisfy the hot videos and leave the cold videos for the CDN servers. For the user behavior modeling and analysis, we have done some interesting work, in identifying the users are browsing most of the time. This observation has opened up some new directions of improving video streaming strategies in optimizing system performance. The PI has also engaged in collaboration with researchers from other universities (Beijing Jiaotong University), and industry (Tencent) in research on this topic, resulting in several publications.

411611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
411611.value: We feel there are still lots of potential in building more sophisticated models of video popularity. In this project, we have assumed video popularity, while power-law distributed, is stationary. This is true for the short-term, but over longer term, video popularity changes over time. This is quite an interesting direction for further research. In fact it is something we are working on right now. Another direction for further research, beyond resource allocation strategies, is how to improve Quality of Experience (QoE) for users. It is also something we continue to work on. Finally, we also find that video recommendation is very important in a VoD service. Recommendation policies also affect video popularity and resource allocation policies. It is interesting to study a high level question of how to maximize user utility, taking into account of recommendation and QoE of streaming.

411611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
411611.value: Online video service is increasingly replacing traditional method of delivering video by broadcasting. The current strategy of this online video service is through a combination of different overlay networks (on top of the Internet), including CDN and P2P methods. In our research, we build models to analyze resource allocation and strategies to improve user experience. We try to develop more realistic user load models based on system measurement.

411811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
411811.value: 特發性青少年脊柱側彎（AIS）是最常見的脊柱彎曲類型，並主要影響年輕女性。AIS患者肺部圖像的分割相對于直脊椎病人而言是更加困難的。連續監測AIS患者的肺功能是可以通過計算機斷層掃描（CT）來完成的，但這並不可取因爲涉及到一個顯著的輻射劑量（包括對正在發育的乳房）。一個無輻射的替代方案是磁共振（MR）成像。由於肺部的MR信號比CT更異構，這大大增加了圖像分割的難度。我們的主要目標是根據Lenke分類建立脊柱側彎患者胸曲線不同形狀和嚴重程度的肺形態統計模型。這種模型將被應用到基於模型的新AIS患者的肺MR圖像分割。我們的第二個目標是要利用這個統計模型，進一步探討肺吸入和呼出的動態模式。本項目的研究成果將提高MRI評估矯正手術前後肺功能的實用性。此外，本研究也將有助於進一步研究AIS患者肺功能受損的病理生理。本研究採用的針對AIS患者的研究成果和方法，經過驗證和測試之後，也可以應用到管理其他形式的脊柱側凸，如具有不同年齡和嚴重程度的先天性脊柱側彎和神經肌肉性脊柱側凸患者。

411811.label: Realisation of objectives
411811.value: The curvature of the spine in patients with Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS) could restrict the function of lung due to the space occupied by the deformed vertebral column and negatively affect other related organs. As the full spine images captured by MRI were divided into 3 sections during the acquisition, we created an algorithm to stitch the spine images especially for the fiber track. Also, as lung inhaled and exhaled consistently, motion artifacts could be a major factor affected the quality of MR images even though the breath-hold sequence was implemented. To improve the image quality, an algorithm was successively developed to correct and reduce motion artifact. As the curvature of spine progressed in many cases of AIS and the severity of spinal curve affected the volume of lung in different degrees, we studied the growth of spine in AIS and aimed to investigate whether there was any prognostic factor to predict curve progression. We also studied the spine in a mechanical basis included torsion and overgrowth of the vertebral disc. The volume of lung in AIS was measured on a group of severe AIS patients before and after the fusion surgery.

411811.label: Major findings and research outcome
411811.value: Several technical works were conducted in the project. A stitching algorithm based on MRI data was completed for the purpose of connecting the spine images [1]. This program allowed us to connect the spine images acquired from different parts of the body into one single image and facilitated the analysis of AIS subjects. A MRI-guided navigation and positioning algorithm was developed for the purpose of tracking location and orientation of body parts. The spatial relationship between actual sites of the body and MRI data had been studied [2]. Due to the movement of the lung, MRI frequently captured images with noise and artifacts even though the protocol was a breath-hold sequence. Denosing was an important step in image pre-processing [11,C1] (C denotes Conference publications). We developed a denosing method based on MRI data which could be implemented into our projects in AIS. Also, the curvature of the spine could affect the lung volume in patients with AIS. A group of severe subjects performed spinal fusion and their lung volume were measured before and after the surgery. Our preliminary findings indicated the total lung volume statistically significantly increased from an average of 2.74 liters before surgery to 3.04 liters after surgery [C2]. We also studied the mechanic factors of the spine that directly induced pressure to the lung and the progression of the spine in AIS. Our results indicated that the spinal cord to vertebrae length ratio could be a factor to predict the progression of AIS [9,C8]. The torsion on the vertebral disc was approximately 3 times more than the vertebrae, and anterior overgrowth and coronal wedging were also determined in the discs of AIS [10,C7]. To make best use of the recruited subjects, a pediatric brain atlas and a functional MRI based brain template were created for future brain mapping [5,8]. Besides, cerebellum, cortical network and fiber track of the spinal cord in AIS were investigated. The morphology of the cerebellum, the connectivity of the brain network and the integrity of the spinal fiber track near the cervical regions in AIS subjects were statistically significantly different from normal controls [3,4,6,C3,C5,C6].

411811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
411811.value: Lung constantly moved to support the pulmonary function, and therefore breath-hold MRI sequences were used to obtain images of lung. However, it was not an easy task for subjects to perform very consistent breath-hold even thought for a short period of time. Movement caused artifacts which blurred the images especially near the edge of the organs. Denoising technique was investigated but the efficacy should be tested on more subjects. To study lungs of AIS, another approach would be using a new 3D reconstruction technique provided by bi-planar x-ray scanner. The low dose x-ray captured full body images to provide enough information for 3D lung reconstruction. The advantage of using low dose x-ray was to perform lung reconstruction by avoiding high dose CT scanning. Both the denosing technique and the application of bi-planar low dose x-ray to improve lung image quality are possible in our center as we have experience in developing denoising algorithm. Our current denosing method could be improved to especially aim on correcting lung motion artifacts. Also, a bi-planar x-ray system is available, but to reduce the tedious workload of manual reconstruction, an automatic algorithm should be developed for this purpose.

411811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
411811.value: In this project, we used an engineering approach to study the physiological and biological changes in patients with Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS). The shape change of the spine could possibility affected the morphology and function of lung and other organs related or connected to the spine including the spinal cord, vertebral disc, medulla oblongata and cerebellum. At first, image stitching technique and positioning technique on MR imaging have been studied. Then the volume of cerebellum and diffusion of medulla oblongata were compared between AIS and healthy controls. The vertebral disc was also investigated in terms of torsion and asymmetry. Our findings also indicated that spinal cord tethering could possibility predict curve progression in AIS. Furthermore, we measured the lung volume using MRI on patients with AIS before and after their spinal fusion surgery. In summary, we studied the effect of spinal curve in patients with AIS to their organs including lung, vertebral disc and column and other related neurological regions.

412211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
412211.value: The overall objective of this project is to investigate novel and cost-effective ranking algorithms for Information Retrieval (IR) by harnessing the combinative power of active and transfer learners. Learning ranking functions is an important problem in machine learning, known as learning to rank or rank learning. The goal is to induce a mapping from a given set of instances to a set of partial or total orders. In this project, we are interested in ordering search results for IR applications. Ranking functions are commonly derived in supervised fashion that requires large training set of relevant judgment prepared manually. However, such kind of annotation is expensive and impractical for real applications, especially when a ranking model needs to be deployed quickly in different search domains, such as text, image and movie. To address this problem, we consider (1) how to effectively use the training data available in a related (or source) domain for transferring ranking knowledge to the target domain (where rank prediction takes place); (2) how to select a small amount of unlabeled data in target domain that once annotated are believed most informative to the learning function. Transfer learning and active learning are two general directions that aim at reducing the labeling effort while maintaining the effectiveness of learning from these two separate perspectives. Nevertheless, there is no existing research that attempts to take the advantage of both strategies either for rank learning or for general machine learning. We have explored rank transfer learning by only using training data from a related domain. Some other studies have demonstrated that annotating small amount of data in target domain can be helpful in learning. However, existing methods were based on the passive mode of transfer, i.e. the data were not selectively annotated, which renders transfer quality unreliable. In this project, we hypothesize that active transfer is crucial for rank transfer learning. We aim to show that with source training data as seeds, it is feasible to proactively sample the set of most informative target-domain instances for annotation, thus reduce the labeling cost to minimum and keep the rank transfer effective. This is the first attempt that naturally intersects rank learning, transfer learning and active learning. Our findings should shed valuable light on the complementary power of active selection and knowledge transfer for adaptive ranking in IR. This, in turn, will provide essential enlightenment for the study of general active transfer learning. N/A

412511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
412511.value: The aim of this project is to analyze the economic viability of dynamic spectrum management (DSM) in future wireless networks. Spectrum resources are scarce, as most spectrums have been allocated through static and exclusive licenses. Extensive field measurements show that, however, most spectrums are heavily under-utilized. This dilemma motivates the study of DSM, which encourage primary licensed and secondary unlicensed entities to share spectrums efficiently. Successful implementation of DSM is not a pure engineering issue. It is also a complicated economic and policy issue, as it affects the interests of wireless end-users, commercial wireless service providers, and government regulatory bodies. Providing proper economic incentives for everyone involved is vital for the successful adoption of DSM schemes. However, there does not yet exist a conceptually unifying, mathematically rigorous, and practical relevant framework for analyzing the economic viability of DSM. The goal of this project is to build such a framework with a deep understanding of related technology issues. We will answer the following two key questions. (a) What is a primary entity's economic incentive to open up the spectrum for sharing? (b) How should a secondary entity choose the spectrum to best trade off the Quality of Service and costs? We will answer these questions under various practical network scenarios, including complete/incomplete network information, loose/tight decision couplings, user/operator interactions, and static/dynamic decision processes. We will also consider the key features of the wireless technologies such as time/frequency/space variabilities, user heterogeneity, and elastic/inelastic applications. The proposed research intends to bridge the gap between the classical microeconomic analysis and the pure engineering design of DSM. The PI and his research team have strong research expertise in wireless communications, game theory, pricing, and network optimization, and thus are very well placed to tackle the proposed research topics. The outputs of the proposed research will lead to a new design and analysis framework of DSM, which would provide good economic incentives for all parties involved and increase spectrum efficiency. The study's findings will spur the development of exciting new technologies and business models, and further strengthen Hong Kong's position as a leading regional telecommunication hub and perhaps a future global player in this field. 本项目的研究目的是分析未来无线网络中动态频谱管理（DSM）的经济可行性。 由于绝大多数频谱已通过静态排他的使用许可证方式予以分配，无线频谱成为了一种稀缺的资源。然而广泛的实地测量表明大多数频谱的利用率严重不足。这种困境推进了DSM的研究。在DSM中，持牌主用户和无牌从用户之间将有效地共享频谱。由于DSM影响到无线终端用户，商用无线服务供应商，和政府监管机构的利益，它已经不仅仅是一个单纯的工程问题，而同时也是一个复杂的经济和政策的问题。DSM成功实现的关键是为所有参与者提供适当的经济诱因。然而，目前尚不存在一个概念统一，数学严格，并与实际紧密联系的理论体协来研究DSM的经济的可行性。 这个项目的目标就是要建立这样一个理论框架，并增进对相关技术问题的深刻理解。我们将回答以下两个关键问题： （1）什么样的经济激励体制能促使主用户开放共享它的频谱？ （2）从用户应如何选择频谱来获得最好的服务质量和成本之间的接合点？我们将在回答这两个问题时考虑各种实际的网络情况，包括完全/不完全的网络信息，松/紧决策关联，用户/运营商的相互作用，以及静态/动态决策过程。我们也会考虑无线技术的各种主要特点，包括时间/频率/空间上的多变性，用户异质性，以及应用的弹性。 本研究项目将在古典微观经济分析和DSM的纯工程设计之间建立起一座理论的桥梁。本项目的负责人黄建伟教授和他的研究团队已经在无线通讯，博弈论，定价策略，和网络优化等方面拥有雄厚的科研基础，因此有能力在该研究项目中大有作为。该项目将建立一个全新的DSM的设计和分析的体系，并为所有相关的参与者提供良好的经济诱因。这项研究的结果将激励令人兴奋的新技术和商业模式的发展，并进一步加强香港作为一个领先的地区性甚至是全球通信产业中心的地位。

412511.label: Realisation of objectives
412511.value: We are pleased to report that the project team has achieved all four project objectives, through collaborations with many top researchers around the world. This project is theoretical in nature. The team has conducted research related to a wide range of dynamic spectrum sharing scenarios, focusing on the economic mechanisms. We have used methodologies including pricing theory, noncooperative game theory, bargaining theory, mechanism design, nonlinear optimization, and graph theory. The key conclusion is that dynamic spectrum sharing is highly economic viable, and the proper design of incentive mechanism is the key to the success of large scale deployment of dynamic spectrum sharing in the commercial network. Results related to this projects have appeared in 3 monographs, 4 book chapters, 26 top IEEE Transactions, journals and magazines, and 31 leading conference papers. This project also trained 5 PhD students and generated two Best Paper Awards. Detailed summary will be given in Part C.

412511.label: Major findings and research outcome
412511.value: (1) We modeled and analyzed the multi-channel spectrum access using tools from evolutionary game theory, congestion game theory, online recommendations, auction, and contract (journal publications 1, 2, 4, 6, 12, 15, 22, 23 and conference publications 1, 2, 3, 6, 8, 12, 20, 24). (2) We analyzed the economic mechanisms for the cooperative spectrum trading using pricing, bargain, auction, and contract mechanisms (journal publications 7, 11, 14, 18 and conference publication 16). (3) We proposed effective carrier sensing mechanism for CSMA networks to improve the network performance (journal publication 8). (4) We proposed energy efficient transmission mechanisms for MIMO cognitive radio networks (journal publication 9). (5) We proposed robust spectrum sensing schemes for cognitive radio networks (journal paper 10). (6) We analyzed and proposed new mechanisms for database-assisted spectrum sharing (journal publications 13, 26, conference publications 5, 11, 19, 29, 31). (7) We analyzed the competition among wireless operators when facing atomic mobile users (journal publication 16). (8) We analyzed the dynamics and user behaviors in the cognitive virtual network operators (journal publication 17 and conference publication 26). (9) We analyzed the competition and cooperation between local and global Wi-Fi operators (journal publication 19 and conference publication 13). (11) We analyzed the competition among cellular operators when upgrading to new technologies, considering the impact of user adoption and network effect (journal publication 24 and conference publication 14). (12) We analyzed the economics models of mobile data offloading and the impact on the operators' pricing strategies (journal publications 20, 25 and conference publications 17, 18, 21, 22, 28). (13) We explored how to design economic mechanisms for user-provided networks to improve the network efficiency (journal publication 21 and conference publications 23, 30). (14) We explored how to balance the revenue and social welfare when a regulator allocates spectrum resources (conference publication 15). (15) We proposed new time and location dependent pricing mechanism to shape the traffic in cellular networks (conference publication 25). (16) We proposed economic mechanism that encourages users participatory sensing to improve the network performance (conference publication 27). (17) We studied how (graphical) congestion game can help us to better understand the incentives and game theoretical interactions among secondary users (journal publications 3, 5 and conference publications 4 & 9). (18) We studied how femtocell and macrocell operators compete and cooperate in a spectrum market (conference publication 7).

412611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
412611.value: For over two decades, the global stabilization problem and global output regulation problem have been two of the central nonlinear control problems. The solvability of such problems has been dictated by the property of the inverse dynamics of the nonlinear system under consideration. To date, the most standard assumption on the inverse dynamics is that it satisfies certain input-to-state stability (ISS) condition. Under this assumption, the inverse dynamics can be treated as a dynamic uncertainty and can be circumvented by the small gain theorem or the changing supply pair technique. However, it is known that the integral input-to-state stability (iISS) condition is strictly weaker than the ISS condition, and many practical nonlinear systems such as the shunt motor system possess an inverse dynamics which is iISS but not ISS. Therefore, in this project, we will aim to achieve three objectives. First, we will establish a framework for handling nonlinear systems whose inverse dynamics is iISS but not ISS. This framework contains three ingredients, namely, a changing supply pair technique for iISS systems, a special version of the robust small gain theorem in the context of iISS, and a fundamental lemma that deals with the global adaptive robust stabilization for a class of nonlinear systems with unity relative degree whose inverse dynamics is iISS. This framework will lay a foundation for tackling the global adaptive robust stabilization problem for some more complex nonlinear systems with iISS inverse dynamics. Second, we will apply the framework to the global adaptive robust stabilization problem for two important classes of nonlinear systems, namely, output feedback systems and strict-feedback systems whose inverse dynamics is iISS but not ISS. Both of these two classes of nonlinear systems are allowed to contain both dynamic and time-varying static uncertainties. Since the global output regulation problem of a given system can be converted into the global stabilization problem of an augmented system containing dynamic and time-varying static uncertainties, the solvability of the global adaptive robust stabilization problem for such systems will also lead to the solvability of the global robust output regulation problem for output feedback systems and strict-feedback systems with iISS inverse dynamics. Finally, we will apply the framework to the disturbance rejection problem of a shunt-DC motor and some other pactical control design problems. Success of this project will make a major breakthrough to the nonlinear control research and enhance our capability to control practical uncertain nonlinear systems. 412611.label: Realisation of objectives
412611.value: This project aims to achieve the following three objectives: 1. Establish a framework for handling nonlinear systems whose inverse dynamics is iISS but not ISS. This framework contains three ingredients, namely, a changing supply pair technique for iISS systems, a special version of the small gain theorem in the context of iISS, and a fundamental lemma that deals with the global adaptive robust stabilization for a class of uncertain nonlinear systems with unity relative degree whose inverse dynamics is iISS but not ISS. This framework will lay a foundation for tackling the global adaptive robust stabilization problem for some complex nonlinear systems with iISS inverse dynamics. 2. Apply the framework to solve the global adaptive robust stabilization problem for the class of output feedback systems whose inverse dynamics is iISS but not ISS. Since the output regulation problem of a given system can be converted into the global robust adaptive stabilization of an augmented system containing dynamic and time-varying static uncertainties , the solvability of the global adaptive robust stabilization problem of this class of nonlinear systems will also lead to the solvability of the global robust output regulation problem for output feedback systems with iISS inverse dynamics. 3. Apply the theoretical result to solve the disturbance rejection problem of a shunt-DC motor. So far all three objectives have been successfully achieved, and can be summarized as follows: We have established a framework for handling nonlinear systems whose inverse dynamics is iISS but not ISS. This framework contains three ingredients, namely, a changing supply pair technique for iISS systems, a special version of the small gain theorem in the context of iISS, and a fundamental lemma that deals with the global adaptive robust stabilization for a class of uncertain nonlinear systems with unity relative degree whose inverse dynamics is iISS but not ISS. This framework has laid a foundation for tackling the global adaptive robust stabilization problem for some complex nonlinear systems with iISS inverse dynamics. The research results have led to three chapters in the following book, Zhiyong Chen and Jie Huang, Stabilization and Regulation: Robust and Adaptive Approach, Springer, 2015, 3 journal papers, 3 conference papers, and several keynote speeches or invited talks. Two PhD students have been supported or partially supported by this project. Additionally, we have further expanded the scope of the research to study the output regulation problem for a multi-agent system via a distributed control scheme. This problem is called cooperative output regulation problem. We have shown that our results include the leader-following consensus problem as a special case, and published a paper in IEEE Transactions in Automatic Control.

412611.label: Major findings and research outcome
412611.value: The major findings of this project are summarized as follows: 1. Extended the changing supply pair technique for ISS systems to iISS systems. This result can be viewed a special version of the small gain theorem in the context of iISS. Established a fundamental lemma that deals with the global adaptive robust stabilization for a class of uncertain nonlinear systems with unity relative degree whose inverse dynamics is iISS but not ISS. The research has led to the following paper: D. Xu, J. Huang and Z-P Jiang, “Global adaptive output regulation for a class of nonlinear systems with iISS inverse dynamics,” 2012 Chinese Control Conference, July 2012, Hefei, China, pp. 1024 - 1029. 2. On the basis of the main finding 1, we further considered the output regulation problem for output feedback nonlinear systems with iISS inverse dynamics of any relative degree. For this purpose, we need to develop a recursive procedure to design an output feedback controller. The research has led to the following paper: D．Xu， J. Huang, and Z-P. Jiang, “Global adaptive output regulation for a class of nonlinear systems using output feedback,” Automatica, 2013. 3. We further considered the cooperative output regulation problem for nonlinear multi-agent systems. The result has led to the following papers: Y. Su and J. Huang, “Cooperative adaptive output regulation for a class of nonlinear uncertain multi-agent systems with unknown leader,” Systems and Control Letter, Vol. 62, 2013, pp. 461-467. Y. Su and J. Huang, “Cooperative global adaptive output regulation for nonlinear multi-agent systems with iISS inverse dynamics,” The10th IEEE International Conference on Control & Automation, Hangzhou, China, June 2013, pp 1644 – 1649. 4. We have expanded the scope of the research by considering the cooperative global robust output regulation problem for a class of nonlinear multi-agent systems with switching network. By using the average dwell time method, we have found a set of solvability conditions for the solving problem. We have also applied our theory to the synchronization problem of a family of Lorenz systems subject to a harmonic exosystem. The research has led to the following paper: W. Liu, and J. Huang. “Cooperative global robust output regulation for a class of nonlinear multi-agent systems with switching network,” IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control, Vol. 60, No. 7, July 2015, pp. 1963-1968. Our research results have also entered the following Chapters 2 to 4 of the following monograph: Zhiyong Chen and Jie Huang, Stabilization and Regulation: Robust and Adaptive Approach

412611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
412611.value: A standard assumption on the solvability of many nonlinear control problems is that the inverse dynamics of the system under consideration is the so-called input-to-state stability (ISS) condition. Satisfaction of this condition guarantees that the solution of the inverse dynamics starting from any initial condition will be bounded under bounded input. However, many nonlinear systems are not bounded-input, bounded state stable, yet their equilibrium is globally asymptotically stable when the input is set to zero. One class of such systems is the so-called integral ISS. Many practical systems such as the shunt-DC motor systems possess an inverse dynamics which are iISS but not ISS. Thus it is of great interest to consider the global stabilization problem or global output regulation problem for such systems in order to be able to handle a larger class of practical nonlinear systems. In this project, we have developed a framework for handling nonlinear systems with iISS inverse dynamics. This framework has led to the solution of the global stabilization and global output regulation problem for typical nonlinear systems including output feedback systems and strict-feedback systems. We have also successfully solved the control problem of the shunt-DC motor system.

412911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
412911.value: Finding how pixels (in a low level) or objects move/transform in a sequence is a fundamentally important and yet challenging computer vision problem, and are generally referred to as motion estimation. 2D optical flow is one essential strategy to estimate dense pixel-wise motion projected from the apparent motion of the world, and provides explicit interpretation of object appearance deviation. Ideally, if optical flow estimation could yield accurate results, as efficient as what human brain can accomplish effortlessly, it will be an indispensible tool for various purposes and greatly profits solving quite a number of transformation-related computer vision and graphics problems, such as video analysis, segmentation, stereopsis, and understanding. Nevertheless, although optical flow estimation has been studied for decades, by and large, it is still technically difficult to handle due primarily to several inherent challenges, including noise suppression, occlusion detection, textureless region modeling, boundary preserving, and large-displacement motion estimation. We in this project will systematically investigate new strategies for computing optical flow from both the theory and algorithm perspectives, aiming to overcome the above obstacles and develop a practical, robust, and high-quality motion estimation system, especially for sequences that are traditionally regarded as intractable. Unlike previous work focusing on improving models or optimization methods only, this project will research a new principled framework to simultaneously cope with large and small motion together with many other aspects that can affect the inference accuracy. We have made concrete and workable plans, which were initially assessed in our preliminary investigation and experiments, to handle optical flow in the traditional two-frame and more complicated multi-frame configurations. We expect to ultimately construct a comprehensive system to enable faithful motion computation even when occlusion and non-rigid motion exist. Our computation framework as well as the results will be extended and instrumented in several high impact applications, such as video editing, understanding, and recognition, to validate their practicality and effectiveness. 在計算機視覺領域里，如何從一個圖片序列中，找出其中像素（低層次的圖像元素）或者物體的運動、變形，是一個很基礎、很重要，而且具有挑戰性的問題。這也就是我們通常所指的運動估計。2D光流法是解決這個問題的一個關鍵方法。它能估計出，現實世界中的運動投影到圖片中后，形成的密集的像素點運動，同時明確地解釋物體外觀上的變化。理想的情況下，如果光流法能夠像人腦一樣快速地計算出精確的結果，其將成為一個具有諸多用途且不可缺少的工具，極其有利於計算機視覺及圖形處理領域里一系列變形相關的問題，比如視頻分析、圖像分割、立體成像，及圖像理解。 光流法已經有幾十年的研究，然而總體上來說，問題的處理依舊存在技術上的難度，這主要歸結于運動估計問題本身存在的幾個大難點，包括噪聲抑制、遮擋檢測、紋理不足區域建模、邊界保持，及大運動估計等。 在這個項目中，我們將從理論和算法的兩方面出發，系統地研究計算光流的新方法，旨在克服以上難題，同時開發一套切實可行的、高魯棒性、高品質的運動估計系統，以用於處理傳統方法不能解決的圖像序列。不同於以往僅關注與改善模型和優化方法的工作，我們將研究致力於開發一套新的框架去同時解決大、小運動估計，找出影響計算精度的其他因素。目前為止，我們已經製作好了詳細可行的計劃，來處理傳統的幀與幀以及更複雜的多幀之間的問題，並在我們的初步調查和實驗中進行了驗證。我們所期望的是，最終構建一個綜合性系統，保證即使存在遮擋和非剛性運動也能如實的給出運動估計。對於這一基本計算框架及其結果，我們將對其進行擴展並集成到一些重要的應用中，例如，視頻的編輯、理解、辨識，以驗證其實用性及有效性。

412911.label: Realisation of objectives
412911.value: For the first objective to propose new fundamental constraints that boost the flow estimation efficiency and reliability, we designed a selection scheme to compute extended initial flow vectors in each image level. This makes the following optimization not completely rely on the result at the previous scale, and is thus capable of refining the estimation correctly in a top-down fashion. We also used robust sparse features, together with patch matching, to produce extended flow initialization, which helps enforce the linearization condition in the variational setting. More specifically, we addressed the general flow initialization problem in each image scale by finding multiple extended displacements through sparse feature matching and dense patch matching to improve estimation on the flow field computed in the immediately coarser level. SIFT feature detection and matching can efficiently capture large motion for objects undergoing translational and rotational motion. Instead of computing a dense descriptor field, we only employ sparse matching of discriminative points, which avoids introducing many ambiguous correspondences and outliers. Although some matches could still be wrong. But this is not a problem as we will eventually employ discrete optimization to only select the most credible candidates. During the course of feature selection, the computed displacement vectors by feature matching are new potential flow candidates except those that already exist in the initial flow field. To robustly screen out the duplicated vectors, we compute the Euclidean distance between the flow estimates. If results are greater than a threshold, we keep them as new flow candidates. This strategy significantly reduces the system dependence on the coarse-scale flow estimation. It is notable as well that feature matching initially produces many vectors distributed in the whole image. But they reduce to less than 15 candidates after local comparison. Only the most distinct flow vectors are retained. SIFT Feature matching, albeit very effective, sometimes still misses motion vectors. This is because small textureless objects may not have distinct features, making their detection problematic. Another main reason is that to let SIFT descriptors gather enough information for 128D feature vector formation. The size could be too large for nonrigid motion as edge statistics may change a lot for successive two frames. We resort to dense nearest neighbor patch matching for amelioration. The patches we use can be as small as 5x5. They are more flexible to describe motion of small textureless regions. All new motion fields, together with the original one, comprise several motion candidates for each pixel in the present image scale. Selection of the optimal flow among them for each pixel is a labeling problem, with our new objective function. It is solved by discrete optimization efficiently because, on the one hand, the number of candidates is small, thanks to the carefully designed selection process; on the other hand, the function is designed to simplify computation. For the second objective to develop a novel principled framework for accurately estimating optical flow, we propose the selective combination of the color and gradient constraints in defining the data term, robust to outliers. As the color constancy constraint is often violated when illumination or exposure changes, combining the gradient constraint was adopted. We proposed functions to selectively combine two terms for color and gradients, which only use the more fitting constraint, but not both of them, to model pixel correspondence. It is much more robust than summing them together. It then comes the new data function involving a weight map. Our regularization term for optical flow estimation is the edge preserving one. Minimizing the final objective function involves simultaneously computing two fields: continuous flow estimate and binary weight map, which is computationally challenging. We employ the Mean Field approximation to simplify the problem by first canceling out the binary process by integration over the weight map. We then compute the sum over all possible weights with the saddle point approximation with a series of derivation. It indicates that the flow estimate by minimizing the derived function is actually the MF approximation of minimizing the original one. We optimize it using an iteratively reweighted optimization strategy. The difficulty stems from the nonconvex data function. Fortunately, our proof shows that the energy can be minimized by iteratively updating the new weight in the outer loop and solving for flow with the computed weights afterwards. In addition, although the approximation function is nonconvex and difficult to solve using continuous optimization, there is no obstacle to applying discrete optimization if candidate labels can be obtained. We propose a robust algorithm to estimate flow. For the final objective to investigate effective optimization methods, we propose very powerful algorithms and systems. Given the new motion fields obtained in phase one of this project, we adopt the Quadratic Pseudo-Boolean Optimization (QPBO) to solve this problem. The fusion move step is used to repeatedly fuse the candidates until each gets visited twice. Also, to suppress the checker-board-like artifacts commonly produced near motion boundaries in discrete optimization, we employ the anisotropic representation of the TV regularizer with 8- neighbor discretization. This method turns the checkerboard-like boundaries to octagons, a better approximation of the original smooth boundaries. The output is the flow map, which contains better recovered motion structure compared to traditional fields. Note that an alternative is to directly discretize the original 2D solution space and fuse all candidate flows. It, however, may suffer from expensive and possibly unstable computation because hundreds of labels can be produced simultaneously in the original resolution. We then refine flow through continuous optimization by iteratively updating weight and flow. We propose decomposing the optimization into three simpler problems, each of which can have the globally optimal solution. The key technique is a variable-splitting method with auxiliary variables, representing the substituted data cost and flow derivatives, respectively, to move a few terms out of the non-differentiable L1-norm expression. This scheme is efficient and is crucial to produce high-quality results. Our method iterates among optimizing the three sub-problems until convergence. Note that cost function decomposition with auxiliary variables in our scheme consists of a set of simpler subproblems, each with guaranteed global optimality. It thus differs from previous methods in the way of formulating the problem and of proposing the solver to each subproblem. In post-processing, we propose "occlusion-aware refinement" for occluded pixels that generally cannot be determined due to the lack of correspondences. In this step, we handle occlusion in the computed flow field. Although cross-checking is effective in occlusion detection, it needs to compute optical flow bi-directionally. Our strategy is based on an observation that multiple pixels mapping to the same point in the target image using forward warping are possibly occluded by each other. We detect occlusion using the mapping uniqueness criterion. The occlusion-aware flow refinement is applied at each scale with the computed vectors from the continuous estimation step. The final results are with very high quality. In short, our method remarkably improves optical flow estimation. All objectives stated in the proposal have been achieved successfully with these new techniques. The final performance of our system is even higher than expected in our original proposal.

412911.label: Major findings and research outcome
412911.value: During this project, we invented quite a number of important techniques, belonging to fundamental and practical research in computer vision and machine learning. These techniques are published in prestigious conferences and journals. Using depth and motion information, we propose scale invariant optical flow and novel multi-body multi-view stereo methods to simultaneously recover dense depth maps and perform segmentation with the input of a monocular image sequence. Unlike traditional multi-view stereo approaches that generally handle a single static scene or an object, we show that depth estimation and segmentation can be jointly modeled and be globally solved in an energy minimization framework for ubiquitous scenes containing multiple independently moving rigid objects. These techniques were published in ECCV, ICCV and CVPR. In our paper "Multispectral Joint Image Restoration via Optimizing a Scale Map" published in IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (TPAMI), we consider color, infrared and flash images captured in different fields that can be employed to effectively eliminate noise and other visual artifacts. We propose a two-image restoration framework considering input images from different fields, for example, one noisy color image and one dark-flashed near-infrared image. This series of work involves multi-modal and multi-spectral registration for natural images and structure extraction from texture published in SIGGRAPH Asia’12, ECCV’14, and ICCV’15. The work of mutual-structure for joint filtering was selected as oral presentation with the acceptance rate lower than 4%. Based on flow information, we show a new direction for fast video superresolution (VideoSR) via a SR draft ensemble, which is defined as the set of high-resolution patch candidates before final image deconvolution. We renovate traditional feedforward reconstruction pipeline and greatly enhance its ability to compute different super-resolution results considering large motion variation and possible errors. Then we combine SR drafts through the nonlinear process in a deep convolutional neural network (CNN). These methods were published in ICCV’15. Finally, we study a set of learning problems based on vision applications. We propose a new online framework enabling the use of L1 sparse data fitting term in robust dictionary learning, notably enhancing the usability and practicality of this important technique. We proposed methods for saliency detection, which is closely related to selective processing in human visual system. In theoretical research, we couple generative and discriminative clustering to model the partition boundaries explicitly and make the method adaptive to data and robust against outliers. This set of work was presented in CVPR’13, AAAI’12, and CVPR’14.

412911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
412911.value: The potential for further development is twofold. First, although sparse feature matching and dense patch matching complement each other in proposing new flow candidates, they could still be insufficient, especially for motion in textureless or regularly patterned regions, where large matching ambiguity could occur. It is possible to explore other information such as simple user input and more advanced optimization strategy in learning systems. We have conducted experiments with simple user interaction. It can decisively improve flow estimation in challenging regions. Second, motion inference for large occluded regions is still an open problem in this community due to lack of correspondence. Our current occlusion handling relies on a heuristic smoothness assumption, which could fail in texture or color-rich regions when occlusion is significant. Incorporating other clues, such as color segmentation, may remedy the problem, which will be further studied by us and in follow-up work of other researchers.

412911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
412911.value: Finding how pixels or objects move/transform in a sequence is a fundamentally important and yet challenging computer vision problem, and are generally referred to as motion estimation. 2D optical flow is one essential strategy to estimate dense pixel-wise motion projected from the apparent motion of the world, and provides explicit interpretation of object appearance deviation. Ideally, if optical flow estimation could yield accurate results, as efficient as what human brain can accomplish, it would be an indispensable tool for various purposes and greatly profits solving quite a number of transformation-related computer vision and graphics problems, such as video analysis, segmentation, stereopsis, and understanding. We in this project systematically investigate advanced strategies for computing optical flow from both the theory and algorithm perspectives. They overcome the above obstacles and develop a practical, robust, and high-quality motion estimation system, especially for sequences that are traditionally regarded as intractable. We develop a new principled framework to simultaneously cope with large and small motion together with many other aspects that can affect the inference accuracy. Our computation framework as well as the results are instrumented in several high impact applications, such as video editing, understanding, and recognition. They validate the practicality and effectiveness.

413411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
413411.value: Algorithms for basic combinatorial optimization problems (e.g. the shortest path problem, the graph matching problem, the maximum flow problem, etc) are important tools in almost all areas in computer science and engineering. Faster and simpler algorithms have significant impact in pushing the frontiers of many practical applications. Moreover, progress on these classical problems usually brings important new ideas and techniques for the development of algorithmic theory and other branches of theoretical computer science. Despite extensive research has been done in the last 40 years, there are still many exciting developments in obtaining faster and simpler algorithms for basic combinatorial optimization problems in recent years. Early results from 1970s and 1980s are usually based on new combinatorial ideas and novel data structures. In the last two decades there have been major advances in using probabilistic techniques to obtain fast randomized algorithms for many problems. More recently there are new algebraic techniques that bring considerable improvements in different problems. These new techniques not only improve the running time of the algorithms, but often provide much simpler algorithms that can be implemented in practice, which is crucial for the algorithms to have impact in practice. In this project we plan to develop new algebraic and probabilistic techniques to obtain faster and simpler algorithms for fundamental combinatorial optimization problems. We have recently obtained some results in this direction, and have identified many promising problems for future study. In the short term, we have found some interesting connections, new ideas, and new areas to investigate. (1) We have discovered a new connection between graph connectivity and network coding, and plan to use it to design faster algorithms for both problems in graph connectivity and network coding. (2) We have some new ideas to use expander graphs to design faster algorithms for graph problems. (3) We will focus on algorithmic problems in network coding, an important application area where faster and simpler algorithms are useful in its development. In the long term, we will investigate new ideas to design better algorithms for classical problems such as the maximum flow problem and the weighted graph matching problem, as well as to investigate new directions to design faster and simpler exact and approximation algorithms for NP-hard problems. 413411.label: Realisation of objectives
413411.value: The second objective has been achieved in the mid-term report. The research has led to two publications, one in using network coding to compute graph connectivity (appeared in SICOMP), and another in using expander graphs to compute matrix rank (appeared in JACM). This first objective has been achieved after the mid-term report. My students and I have studied spectral methods in designing fast algorithms. We have shown that the performance of the popular spectral partitioning algorithm is better than its worst case guarantee in practical instances. This answer a long standing open problem in finding a theoretical justification of the success of the spectral partitioning algorithm in practical applications such as image segmentation and data clustering. Our approach is to relate the k-th eigenvalue of the Laplacian matrix to the performance of the spectral partitioning algorithm, and argue that in practice the k-th eigenvalue is large for some small k, and our result implies that it is a much better approximation to those instances. Our results generalize the well-known Cheeger's inequality in spectral graph theory, and were presented in STOC 2013. My PhD student Kwok and I also study the random walk graph partitioning algorithm, and prove that it almost achieves the same performance of the spectral partitioning algorithm. This proves that there is a local graph partitioning algorithm with similar performance as the spectral partitioning algorithm, leading to a sublinear time algorithm for the problem which is very useful in solving graph partitioning problems in massive graphs (e.g. community detection in social networks). The results were presented in RANDOM 2013.

413411.label: Major findings and research outcome
413411.value: A fast algorithm to compute graph connectivity using network coding. This leads to an algorithm to compute all pairs edge connectivities in directed graphs in one matrix multiplication time, improving over previous results for this fundamental problem. A fast algorithm to compute matrix rank and finding linear independent columns using expander graphs. This leads to a significant improvement for this fundamental problem when the matrix rank is small. It has various applications in combinatorial optimization, and it also leads to follow-up work in numerical linear algebra. A new analysis of the spectral partitioning algorithm using higher eigenvalues. This leads to a theoretical justification of its good empirical performance in image segmentation and data clustering, answering a long standing open question in the area. It generalizes the well-known Cheeger's inequality in spectral graph theory and leads to follow-up work in the area. A new analysis of the random walk graph partitioning algorithm. This shows that the local graph partitioning algorithm almost matches the performance of the spectral partitioning algorithm, and this implies a sublinear time algorithm for finding a small sparse cut in a massive graph, which is potentially very important in real-world applications.

413711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
413711.value: Real-time traffic monitoring is essential for network administrators to characterize the behavior of data traffic, and more importantly, react to network anomalies such as failures and attacks in a timely manner. To make real-time traffic monitoring feasible in practice, one can leverage parallelization technologies, such as multi-core CPUs, to improve the throughput of packet processing. On the other hand, realizing the full potential of parallelization remains a challenging issue, due to the inter-process synchronization overhead and design sophistication of coordinating multiple processes to satisfy different requirements of traffic monitoring and analysis. In this project, we aim to explore how to effectively utilize parallelization to achieve real-time traffic monitoring of network anomalies in practice. This project will involve substantial algorithmic design, theoretical analysis, and system prototyping and implementation. In particular, we focus on two key issues. First, we plan to design algorithmic primitives (including algorithms and data structures) that exploit parallelization for network traffic monitoring. In addition, we plan to design and implement an extensible parallel traffic monitoring system that can dynamically integrate different algorithmic primitives to fulfill different types and needs of operational networks, while still maintaining the effectiveness of parallelization. The contribution of this project is to facilitate network administrators and telecommunication providers to have a better view of the “health” of their managed networks, including the traditional wired networks and the emerging 3G/4G wireless data networks. We believe that the project will make promising local impact in Hong Kong and China, where the telecommunication industry has played an important role in the economic development. 實時流量監測對網絡管理員十分重要，它可偵察數據流量的行為，更重要是，及時應對網絡失效和攻擊。為了使實時流量監控可行，我們可以充分利用並行處理技術，如多核心處理器，以提高了數據包處理的速度。另一方面，全面實現並行化潛力仍然是一個具挑戰性的問題，尤其面對程序間的同步負擔和複雜協調等問題以應付流量監控和分析的不同需要。在這個項目中，我們探討如何有效地利用並行化實現實時網絡異常流量監測。此項目將涉及大量的算法設計，理論分析和系統原型實現。我們集中在兩個關鍵問題。首先，我們計劃設計算法原型（包括算法和數據結構）以幫助並行網絡流量監控。此外，我們計劃設計和實現一個可擴展的並行流量監控系統，可以任意整合不同的算法原型以滿足不同網絡的需求，同時仍然保持並行化的效果。這個項目的貢獻是促進網絡管理員和電信供應商有效管理其網絡，包括傳統的有線網絡和新興的3G/4G無線數據網絡。我們認為，該項目將有助香港和中國的電信業的長遠發展。

413711.label: Realisation of objectives
413711.value: As per Objectives 1, 4-6, we propose LD-Sketch, a compact data structure designed for accurate and scalable traffic anomaly detection using distributed architectures. We prove the theoretical properties on the accuracy, space complexity, and time complexity. We build LD-Sketch on a distributed architecture that inherently takes into account the scalability and performance overheads, including the inter-process overhead, CPU cores, memory usage, and I/O overheads. We compare LD-Sketch with state-of-the-art sketch-based techniques by conducting experiments on traffic traces from a real-life 3G cellular data network. As per Objectives 2-3, we propose protocol inference algorithms that leverage machine learning to unveil the protocol formats of unknown network protocols (which potentially imply anomalous protocols). We propose different algorithms: ProWord, which identifies the protocol keywords of any protocol based on statistical distributions, ProGraph, which identifies bit-level protocol fields in a fine-grained manner, and ChatDissect, which proposes specific techniques to discover the protocol formats and semantics of the popular messaging application WeChat. As per Objective 7, we are in collaboration with Huawei Technologies. In particular, we validate LD-Sketch on the 3G operational network traces provided by Huawei. We also note that LD-Sketch is now a key component in Huawei’s streaming product called StreamSmart (http://www.noahlab.com.hk/topics/StreamDataMining). We filed two patent applications based on this work (CN201310513394.6 and CN201410175828.0) .

413711.label: Major findings and research outcome
413711.value: We mainly explore three areas of research along real-time traffic monitoring: (i) sketch-based anomaly detection, (ii) protocol inference in traffic classification, and (iii) measurement studies of network applications. In the first work, we observe that real-time characterization of network traffic anomalies, such as heavy hitters and heavy changers, is often challenged by the ever-increasing volume and diversity of network traffic. We address this problem by leveraging parallelization. We propose LD-Sketch, a compact data structure designed for accurate and scalable traffic anomaly detection using distributed architectures. LD-Sketch performs detection in two phases: local detection, which guarantees zero false negatives, and distributed detection, which reduces false positives by aggregating multiple detection results. We derive the error bounds and the space and time complexity for LD-Sketch. We further analyze the impact of ordering of data items on the memory usage and accuracy of LD-Sketch. We build a distributed system that realizes LD-Sketch, and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art sketching algorithms. Our findings are published at IEEE INFOCOM 2014 (acceptance rate: 19.4%) and Elsevier Computer Networks. In the second work, we extend real-time traffic monitoring for traffic classification, which is critical for network management, especially for deep packet inspection. However, how to systematically and efficiently extract protocol feature words from network traffic remains a challenging issue. We propose two protocol inference algorithms: (i) ProWord, an unsupervised approach that extracts protocol keywords from traffic traces, and (ii) ProGraph, which exploits intra-packet dependency to accurately infer protocol formats and semantics in a fine-grained manner. The findings of ProWord are published at IEEE INFOCOM 2014 (acceptance rate: 19.4%) and JSAC 2014; the findings of ProGraph are published at IFIP Networking 2015 (acceptance rate: 23.3%). In the third work, we adopt our developed traffic classification techniques to characterize real-world network traffic. Our early work has studied the traffic characteristics in both data planes and control planes, and the findings are published at IFIP Networking 2012 (acceptance rate: 28.4%) and ACM MSWiM 2012 (acceptance rate: 26%). We recently design and implement ChatDissect, a protocol inference tool specifically designed for characterizing WeChat, the most popular mobile messaging application in mainland China. ChatDissect combines existing protocol inference techniques in a seamless manner to dissect the protocol specifications of WeChat. Our results are important for network operators (e.g., Huawei) to understand how WeChat potentially degrades the quality of the network. Our findings are published at IEEE IWQoS 2015 (acceptance rate: 22.5%).

413711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
413711.value: We focus on the area of network traffic analytics, which enables network operators to identify network anomalies and characterize new network protocols that potentially create new security problems. We have proposed algorithms and built distributed systems to validate our work from both theoretical and practical perspectives. Future work will include addressing the scalability of our designs, for example, through the integration into existing streaming architectures such as Spark Streaming. Our current results focus on the network traffic analytics, and they could actually be generalized to other domains such as stream database queries and online machine learning.

413711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
413711.value: We mainly explore three areas in the area of real-time network traffic analytics: (i) sketch-based anomaly detection, (ii) protocol inference in traffic classification, and (iii) measurement studies of network applications. First, we propose LD-Sketch, a compact data structure designed for accurate and scalable traffic anomaly detection using distributed architectures; second, we propose ProWord and ProGraph, the protocol inference algorithms that unveil the keywords, formats, and semantics of general network protocols; finally, we conduct measurement studies on 3G operational networks to characterize the behaviors in both data and control planes, and propose a tool called ChatDissect that is especially designed for analyze WeChat traffic. Our results enable network operators to make better decisions on resource provisioning, capacity planning, and network management, especially in the presence of network anomalies. Our findings have been published in several prestigious conferences and journals.
