413811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
413811.value: Hearing impairment is an epidemic that is affecting and will continue to affect millions of people in the world. Although hearing aids and cochlear implants have provided significant benefits to the hearing-impaired population, hearing in noise remains a big problem for most of them. In this project, we will develop new signal processing techniques to improve the speech perception of hearing-impaired people under adverse listening conditions. We argue that pitch information is a robust and reliable cue for human speech recognition in the presence of strong noise or concurrent voices. A novel method of robust pitch estimation will be developed. The estimated pitch track will be used to facilitate the extraction and enhancement of periodicity-related signal components in noisy speech. To alleviate the effect of undesirable signal artifacts caused by periodicity enhancement, we will develop a method of noise filling-in to leverage on the phonemic restoration mechanism in human auditory perception. In the past, studies that link algorithm development closely with real clinical populations are very rare. We will carry out extensive psychoacoustic experiments at different stages of algorithm development to assess the effectiveness of the proposed methods. We are particularly interested in the speech recognition performance of tonal language speakers, to which pitch information plays an important role. Our project team consists of experienced researchers in the areas of speech signal processing, audiology and hearing science. The investigators have done a lot of work in related areas and been closely collaborating in the past few years. We seek for a funding of HK$1.53 million to support the project for three years. 全世界有數千萬人患有不同程度的聽力障礙。助聽器和電子耳蝸雖然對改善聽覺有很明顯的效果，但是聽障患者在嘈雜環境下仍然遇到很大的困難。本項目的工作為開發新的信號處理技術提高聽障患者在惡劣聲學環境中的言語感知水平。我們認為在強背景噪聲或有干擾聲源的情況下，音高信息對言語識別至關重要。我們將開發一個高性能的音高提取方法，所得到的語音音高曲線用來對信號進行週期性增強。另一方面，語音增強處理過程中無可避免地對信號造成損害。我們將基於聽覺感知中的語音重建機制，開發一個噪聲屏敝的方法，消除信號破損所造成的聽覺效應。過往很少研究能把信號處理與患者的要求真正結合起來。我們將開展一系列生理聲學實驗，驗證算法在實際應用中的效果，並對改進的方向提供具體依據。本項目的獨特性之一是針對聲調語言的言語識別，探討音高信息的重要性。我們的研究團隊包括了來自信號處理，聽力學及聽覺科學等方面的專家，他們過去在有關領域做過大量的合作研究。本項目預算經費為港幣一百五十三萬六千元，項目期為三年。

413811.label: Realisation of objectives
413811.value: All of the project objectives have been addressed and achieved. Toward Objective 1, a new method of robust pitch estimation for speech signals at very low signal-to-noise ratios (< 5 dB) was developed. The new method has two novel elements that contribute to its noise robustness. First, it uses a temporal-spectral representation of pitch derived by accumulating spectral peaks over consecutive time frames. Second, prior knowledge of speech and noise is incorporated in a simple yet effective way with the use of sparse estimation techniques. In addition, the sparsity-based pitch estimation framework was extened and applied to tackle the problems of multipitch tracking for speech mixture, and pitch estimation for speech separation output. Toward Objective 2, a novel algorithm of transform-domain periodicity enhancement for noisy speech was developed. The algorithm makes use of an automatically extracted pitch track to separate the periodic component of speech from the aperiodic one. An adaptive method was developed to adjust the balance between the periodic and aperiodic components and produce periodicity-enhanced natural speech. On the other hand, an effective strategy of temporal periodicity enhancement was developed for improving Chinese tone perception of cochlear implant (CI) uses. The strategy was implemented on a research platform that can be connected to commercial CI devices. Toward Objective 3, our investigation was focused on the top-down processing mechanism of speech perception. Psychoacoustic experiments were carried out with periodically interrupted Cantonese speech with and without noise filling. Different strategies of inserting noise to the interrupted speech were compared. Due to the limited time and funding resource, the findings of this part of investigation could not be incorporated into the periodicity enhancement algorithm as planned in the project proposal. Therefore Objective 3 is considered to be 80% achieved. Toward Objective 4, a series of subjective listening tests were carried out. Subjective evaluation with normal-hearing subjectives was performed on the transform-domain periodicity enhancement algorithm. The effectiveness of the periodicity-enhanced CI strategy for Cantonese tone perception was evaluated with hearing-impaired listeners. In addition, different speech enhancement algorithms were compared with subjective listening tests on normal-hearing subjects.

413811.label: Major findings and research outcome
413811.value: 1. Robust pitch estimation and tracking Pitch estimation and tracking is a critical step in periodicity enhancement of speech. In this research, it is found that temporal accumulation of spectral peaks is a robust feature representation for pitch estimation and dictionary-based sparse estimation is a good approach of incorporating prior knowledge into pitch estimation of noisy speech. Experimental results showed that our proposed methods outperform most of the existing pitch estimation algorithms for different kinds of real-world noises, especially at very low signal-to-noise ratios. For details of this part of research, please refer to Journal Publications No. 1, and Conference Publications No. 1, 3 and 6. 2. Periodicity enhancement of noisy speech Periodicity enhancement aims at making pitch and tone related information more prominent and hence improving speech perception. In this research, it has been shown that enhancement of speech and/or suppression of noise can be effectively achieved by processing the LP parameters and the residual signal separately. With pitch track robustly estimated from noisy speech, the proposed method demonstrates significant improvement in both the signal-to-noise ratio and the perceptual quality of speech. For this part of research, refer to Journal Publications No.3. 3. Improving pitch and tone perception of cochlear implant users Temporal periodicity cues are important to tone perception in noise. Pitch and tone perception by CI users could be improved when listeners received enhanced temporal periodicity cues. In our research, it is shown that temporal periodicity enhancement in cochear implants can be achieved by replacing noise-corrupted periodicity cues with pure sinusoidal waves that carry the target pitch contours. This strategy is found to improve Cantonese tone perception of cochlear implant users, especially for female voice. For details of this part of research, refer to Journal Publications No.2. 4. Subjective and objective evaluation of enhanced speech Speech distortion and noise reduction are the two key metrics to assess the performance of speech enhancement algorithms and evaluate the noise-suppressed speech quality. It is important to separately evaluate the capabilities of speech enhancement algorithms in preserving the original speech, reducing noise level and achieving good overall quality. Our proposed objective measures are found to be well correlated with subjective ratings. The details of this part of work can be found in the Journal Publications No.4 and Conference Publiction No.7.

413811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
413811.value: 1. Periodicity enhancement as post-processin of speech source separation Single-microphone speech separation is of practical importance in hearing assistive devices. We have developed different approaches to speech source separation based on statistical models. The periodicity enhancement algorithm could be extended for post-processing on the speech separation outputs. The goal is to suppress the residue part of the interfering source. A preliminary attempt has been made to estimate pitch track of separated speech source (refer to Conference Publication No.3) 2. Improving music perception by hearing impaired listeners It is believed that periodicity enhancement is helpful to make pitch cues more prominent and hence improve music perception. A possible follow-up work is to investigate the effect of temporal periodicity enhancement on pitch perception of music signals.

413811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
413811.value: Hearing impairment is an epidemic that affects a large population. This research addresses the problem of hearing in noise. We develop new signal processing algorithms that can be implemented on hearing aids and cochlear implant systems to improve speech perception of hearing-impaired people under adverse listening conditions. In view of the importance of pitch information as robust and reliable cue for speech recognition, the problems of robust pitch estimation and pitch enhancement have been tackled. The new signal processing methods were proven effective through both objective and subjective evaluation. In particular, through inter-disciplinary collaboration, we successfully carried out listening tests with cochlear implant users and demonstrated significant improvement in tone recognition accuracy for Cantonese speech. The research results will be useful to the design of next-generation hearing assistive technology.

414911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
414911.value: 研究目的： 該項目研究目的為：通過對非同步物理層網絡編碼系統的研究，來簡化物理層網絡編碼（PNC）原型機的實現。 研究背景： 物理層網絡編碼技術，最早由本次項目負責人（PI）的研究團隊在2006年的國際移動通信與網絡峰會（Mobicom）上提出[1]。自PNC原創性文章發表以來，物理層網絡編碼逐漸發展成網絡編碼（Network Coding）研究領域中非常重要的一個分支，並且引申出了許多後續的研究工作：截至2010年11月，根據Google學術搜索引擎（Google Scholar）做出的引用文獻數目統計，我們的PNC原創性文章已經收到超過300次的引用，並且引用該文章的科研文獻的數目近年來以每年180篇以上的速度遞增。從信息論的角度分析，物理層網絡編碼技術能夠非常接近雙向中繼網絡（TWRC）信道容量的理論上限。具體來說，物理層網絡編碼與TWRC信道容量上界的距離不超過1/2比特。然而，一個非常重要的問題是，上述理論性能優異的物理層網絡編碼技術，如何在實際的通信系統中實現並應用。在物理層網絡編碼研究領域中，一個廣為人知的挑戰性難題是如何使多個終端節點完全同步地發送信息至共同的中繼節點。到目前為止，研究人員對於以上同步問題的分析還不夠深入和完善：特別是，物理層網絡編碼究竟有多高的同步要求；還有，如何設計出一種可實現的解決方案，來使得物理層網絡編碼系統可以對抗由不同步而產生的各種性能損失。本提案正是為解決上述的理論及應用難題而提出的。 項目概述： 物理層網絡編碼技術能夠提升通信系統性能的一個非常重要的原因在於，PNC可以使“多個終端節點可以同時傳輸不同的信息”至一個共同的中繼節點。中繼節點在收到這些疊加的信息之後進行處理，將其轉換為一個網絡編碼數據流，最後再將網絡編碼後的信息廣播回終端節點。到目前為止，大部分研究工作都假定不同的終端節點之間可以同步地傳輸的信息，以使得中繼節點收到的信息碼元及射頻（RF）載波相位完全重合。然而，載波相位同步的實現在實際系統中具有極大的挑戰性，因為載波相位在極小時間尺度上就會發生極大變化（例如，頻率為5GHz的載波，其相位在0.2ns間就變化一個週期）。因此，更加符合實際考慮的研究工作應該集中在，一個不要求載波相位同步的，非同步物理層網絡編碼系統上。我們提出此項研究的目的在於：1）對非同步物理層網絡編碼技術進行深入的理論分析，重點在於解決碼元非同步和相位非同步的性能損失問題；2）設計並實現一個基於軟件無線電設備的物理層網絡編碼系統原型機，以此來驗證我們對非同步物理層網絡編碼系統的理論研究。 研究意義： 自PNC原創性文章發表以來，雖然許多研究從理論上證明了物理層網絡編碼的優異特性，但是如何將PNC應用於實際的無線通信系統與PNC的理論研究之間依然存在著一個可觀的差距。因此，我們提出上述非同步物理層網絡編碼方案，來嘗試解決物理層網絡編碼系統中非常重要的實際問題。如果我們的研究最終獲得成功，它將會是物理層網絡編碼技術從理論分析到實際應用的發展過程中非常重要的一步。

414911.label: Realisation of objectives
414911.value: For this project, all four objectives have been met, with some research outcomes extending beyond the four original objectives. Objectives 1 and 2 -- With respect to objectives 1 and 2, we have been able to characterize the impact of various asynchronies, including symbol misalignment and phase offset, for both non-channel-coded PNC and channel-coded PNC systems. Besides the investigation of asynchronous LDPC-coded PNC, we also studied asynchronous convolutional-coded PNC. See further details in Section 6.1 Objective 3 and 4: The reason for the study of convolutional-coded PNC is that our PNC prototype on software-defined radio follows much of the WiFi standard, for which the convolutional codes are used. This theoretical focus paved the way for meeting objectives 3 and 4 of this project. Both objectives 3 and 4 have been met. Indeed, going beyond this project which focuses on a specific aspect of PNC – i.e. asynchronous operation – our PNC prototype is now TCP/IP compatible and can support real applications like web browsing and video conferencing. Overall, the investigations in this project have been very fruitful. They result in much insight into the design of PNC systems, which in turn feeds into our PNC prototype. In addition, additional areas that deserve further attention are uncovered. I will provide further details on the new frontiers in Section 6.2.

414911.label: Major findings and research outcome
414911.value: Overall, this project yields nine journal publications and seven conference publications, as listed in Part C. Most publications are in the IEEE venues. In addition, a PhD student of mine, L. Lu, received the “Best Research Output Award by Postgraduate Students” and “Best PhD Thesis Award” at CUHK in 2013 for work related to this project. L. Lu is now a research assistant professor with the Institute of Network Coding at CUHK. Our work provided a comprehensive answer to the challenge of asynchronous operation of PNC systems. First, we have been able to show that if the symbols of multiple users do not arrive at the receiver perfectly aligned, then the phase penalty is significantly ameliorated. Then, we further showed that once channel coding is incorporated into the PNC system, the phase penalty becomes a phase reward. That is, in channel-coded PNC, having phase asynchrony is actually good! These results are significant because they show that asynchronies are not the Achilles heel of PNC, and that PNC systems could work well even in the absence of a perfect synchronization mechanism. In other words, PNC is closer to practice than originally thought. For asynchronous channel-coded PNC, we also explored the use of convolutional codes because convolutional codes are widely used in real practical systems, including our current PNC prototypes. Our study of convolutional-coded PNC resulted in a publication in IEEE Trans. on Wireless Communications (see Part C). This paves the way for implementation in our PNC prototype on the software-defined radio platform. Our efforts in pushing PNC on the practical front have yielded many “first-of-its-kind” PNC prototypes. Journal paper 2 in Part C, for example, reports the first PNC implementation. We devised many simplifying techniques to enable this implementation on the software-defined radio system. Notably, we recently demonstrated a first real-time TCP/IP compatible PNC system that supports standard TCP/IP applications like web browsing and video conferencing. Going beyond the scope of this proposal, we even made strides in the optical domain. In Journal papers 3 and 4 in Part C, we reported two first-of-its-kind optical PNC prototypes. Part C also listed other works going beyond the above objectives. For example, in journal papers 5, 6, and conference papers 1, 3, 6 in Part C, we investigated PNC systems with more than two terminal nodes.

414911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
414911.value: An insight from this project is that we could deliberate introduce asynchrony into PNC systems to make their operation more robust against small deviations in channel gains and errors in channel estimation. We recently exploit this insight in high-order modulated PNC systems. A paper along this line is under second review for potential publication in IEEE Trans. on Information Theory. Phase asynchrony is also prevalent in OFDM-based PNC systems. In such systems, the relative phases from the two users in different subcarriers are different (e.g., in subcarrier 1, the relative phase difference of the two signals from the two users is theta1; in subcarrier 2, the relative phase difference is theta2; and theta1 is theta2 are not equal). This is the case even for single-path channels. How to deal with and exploit such phase asynchrony is an interesting direction for future investigation.

414911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
414911.value: “Simultaneous transmissions by multiple users” is an important feature in the Physical-Layer Network Coding (PNC) system that enables it to have higher throughput than the traditional system. Since PNC was first proposed (by my group in 2006), the research community had largely believed PNC to be viable only if the simultaneous transmissions by multiple users were perfectly synchronized. In practice, however, it would be hard to synchronize the carrier frequencies, phases, and symbol arrival times of the signals of multiple users to a common receiver. The investigations in this project resulted in comprehensive answers to the above challenge, not just in theory, but in practice: our PNC prototypes on software-defined radio can now support standard TCP/IP applications like web browsing and video conferencing. Our results are significant because they show that asynchronies are not the Achilles heel of PNC, and that PNC systems could work well even in the absence of a perfect synchronization mechanism. On the bigger picture, my past decade of research focus on PNC has made my group a leading group on PNC research. With various co-authors, I have had 58 publications related to Network Coding, with particular focus on PNC, since the inception of PNC in 2006 (see http://www.ie.cuhk.edu.hk/people/soung2.shtml).

415011.value: 軟組織操作醫療機器人的基於受動性力控制研究

415011.label: Project Objectives
415011.value: Model a robot manipulator interacting with unknown deformable objects using the port-Hamiltonian formulation and develop the concept of “constrained and unconstrained energy ports” Design a hybrid position and force controller for the robot manipulator using the energy-shaping method and prove convergence of the interaction force and passivity of the system. rows: Model a robot manipulator interacting with unknown deformable objects using the port-Hamiltonian formulation and develop the concept of “constrained and unconstrained energy ports”
Design a hybrid position and force controller for the robot manipulator using the energy-shaping method and prove convergence of the interaction force and passivity of the system.
Implement the passivity-based controller on a robot manipulator and verify its performance by experiments on unknown deformable objects including soft tissues.

415011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415011.value: In robotic surgery, a medical robot needs frequently interact with elastic objects such as soft tissues and organs. The safety of robotic surgery heavily depends on how the interaction forces between the robot and the objects are controlled. To guarantee operational safety, it is important to ensure passivity of the system under sensory control of the interaction forces. Since existing passivity-based force controllers rely on the exact models of both the robot and the environment, they cannot be applied because the models of soft tissues or oranges are unknown. It has been an open problem for a long time how to strictly achieve passivity of a force-controlled system with unknown environmental models. In this project, we will use the port-Hamiltonian approach to formulate the dynamics of the robot interacting with unknown deformable environment and develop a force controller that strictly guarantees the passivity of the system using the energy-shaping approach. A novel concept called constrained and unconstrained energy ports will be proposed so as to achieve both position and force regulation. Unlike traditional hybrid controllers and impedance controllers, this controller, because of its port Hamiltonian nature and energy-based design, will strictly preserve passivity of the system for all the time. Experiments will be conducted on a 6 degrees-of-freedom (DOF) manipulator to verify performance of the developed controllers. The research outputs will make great impacts to research and development of medical robotics and contribute to development and applications of advanced technology in Hong Kong. 機器人在進行醫療手術時需要經常操作軟組織和器官，而手術機器人的安全性取決於它與這些變形物體之間的作用力是如果控制的。為了確保手術安全，需要保證在力反饋控制時整個系統滿足受動性的要求。目前所存在的基於受動性力控制方法依賴機器人和環境的完整模型，而軟組織和人體器官的變形模型是無法預知的。如何設計一個可以保證與未知變形環境交互作用機器人的受動性的力控制器是長時間沒有解決的一個難題。本項目研究將先利用哈密頓法對與未知變形體交互機器人的動力學進行建模，在此基礎上利用能量構建法設計能夠嚴格保證系統受動性的力控制器。為了實現力和位置的同時控制，我們將提出受約束能量口和不受約束能量口的概念。因為基於能量設計力控制器，跟傳統的阻抗控制、力和位置雙向控制器不同，我們研究的方法可以嚴格保證系統的受動性。我們將在一個六自由度的機械手上通過實驗驗證所研究的方法的有效性。本研究將對醫療機器人的技術發展及香港的科技創新作出貢獻。

415011.label: Realisation of objectives
415011.value: The objectives set in the project have been fully realised. As to be explained in details, we have developed an approach to model a robot manipulator interacting with unknown deformable objects using port-Hamiltonian formulation and proposed a new position and force controller that does not rely on the deformation model by the energy shaping method. Furthermore, we developed an image-based controller for controlling deformation of soft objects without knowing the model and proved the stability of the controller using an energy-based Lyapunov function. A model-free controller that uses uncalibrated visual feedback was also proposed to control deformation of unknown soft objects. We have implemented the controllers on a robot manipulator and verified their performance by experiments on several types of deformable objects including soft tissues. Therefore, we can conclude the 100% realisation of the objectives.

Implement the passivity-based controller on a robot manipulator and verify its performance by experiments on unknown deformable objects including soft tissues.

415011.label: Major findings and research outcome
415011.value: (1) We have developed a dynamic model of a robot manipulator interacting unknown deformable objects including soft tissues using Hamiltonian formulation. A potential function is proposed to represent the deformation of the soft objects and an energy-based model is used to model the interaction forces. Based on the model developed, we have developed two approaches for controlling the interaction force and position of the robots interacting with deformable objects. The first controller uses a static-state feedback regulator with the robust energy shaping design, and the second approach controls the force by adaptively estimating the unknown Hessian matrix and compensating for the environment’s reaction force. The stability of the approaches has been proved theoretically and the performance has been confirmed by experiments. The results led to one publication at IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology. (2) We developed an energy-based controller for controlling deformation of soft objects using image feedback. The controller does not need any model on deformation of the soft object and can deform the soft object to a desired shape. The basic ideas are to shape the convergence of the deformation error as a potential function and to estimate the mapping from the robot motion to deformation of the object on-line. The stability of the controller has been theoretically proved and its performance has been verified by experiments using a 6 DOF manipulator. The results were presented at 2013 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation and has been published on IEEE Transactions on Robotics, the best journal in robotics. (3) We proposed a novel kinematic controller for robot manipulators performing active deformation tasks with unknown elastic objects. This controller achieves the deformation control by estimating the deformation Jacobian matrix in real-time through minimizing the error between the measured and estimated deformation flows. The on-line estimation of the deformation Jacobian matrix makes it possible to control the deformation without the model of the soft object. This work led to one publication in International Journal of Robotics Research, one of the best two journals in the area. (4) The controllers were all validated by experiments on deformable objects. In addition, we also verified the performance of the controllers using an assistive surgical robot handling an endoscope in the nasal surgical procedures. (5) A Ph.D. student has been trained under the support of this project.

415011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
415011.value: First, the methods can be further developed to manipulation, dissection and suturing control of soft tissues in surgical robots. Second, the current controllers assume that the image feature points can be traced accurately during the control process, but this assumption is not practical in real applications. How to control deformation using natural features and to cope with various uncertainties in feature detection and tracking are important directions for further investigation. Third, applying the model-free controllers of deformable objects to real applications is another important direction.

415011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
415011.value: Position and force control of a robot manipulator interacting with elastic/soft objects such as cloths, soft tissues, etc. is an important problem in many robot applications including robotic surgery, cloth manipulation, etc. The challenges in designing such controllers lie in the difficulties in modelling the deformation of the soft objects for the models depend on many physical parameters and constraints which are hardly identified/measured. In this project, we developed an energy-based method to model dynamics of a robot manipulator interacting with soft objects from the viewpoint of energy flows. Based on this model, we proposed a controller for controlling position and force of the manipulator without knowing the deformation model of the soft objects. Furthermore, we developed two image-based controllers for controlling deformation of the soft objects using uncalibrated image feedback. The performance of the controllers has been confirmed by experiments. The work led to three publications at top journals in robotics, presentations at major international conferences and training of a Ph.D. student. The objectives set in this project have been fully achieved.

415211.label: Project Title(Chinese)
415211.value: 分佈式識別理論在於通信網絡的惡意節點：數學理論，算法與應用

415211.label: Project Objectives
415211.value: Develop a general mathematical theory to identify and detect malicious nodes in large scale communication networks and/or large scale network applications. To validate the mathematical theory that we develop can be applied to communication networks with tens of millions of nodes, we plan to develop a fluid-like parallel simulator on multi-core clustered machines so that we can test and validate the theory on different range of network topologies and network protocols. We plan to apply the detection and identification theory to several important networking applications or services, they are: (a) Detect and identify malicious and colluding nodes which spread bogus packets in a P2P live streaming systems[6] as well as P2P video-on-demand systems[17]. (b) Detect and identify malicious users who intentionally inject corrupted packets in wireless mesh networks so to deplete the system resources. (c) Detect and identify nodes which inject false and misleading product recommendation in large scale online social networks (e.g., Facebook). (d) Propose randomized algorithms so as to quickly identify these malicious nodes, and at the same time, avoid counter-measure by the attackers. To apply the identification and detection algorithms we develop for real life online social networks and P2P streaming systems. We are in the process of collaborating with "Tencent Inc.", which has the largest online social network in China (e.g., QQ software), to test malicious users identification. We are also collaborating with Huawei Inc (e.g., the largest network equipment manufacturer in China) to identify malicious users in P2P streaming systems. Note that currently, there are millions of users in China who are using P2P software and this creates an interesting testbed to validate our theory and show its impact.

415211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415211.value: 當我們研究許多新興的網絡協議和網絡應用，一個根本的和共同的特點是，在這些網絡節點與其他節點溝通和互動，以實現共同的任務。為了說明這個重要的屬性，讓我們考慮下面的例子： - 在一個P2P網絡節點互動和互相協助，以實現一個可擴展文件分配或視頻流。 - 在無線網狀網 (WMN) 需要互相幫助，提供數據包從源到目的地。 - 在社會網絡 (OSNs) 上節點經常相互溝通因為朋友們熱衷的關係。 然而，相互作用，可能也暗示了安全漏洞的可能性。考慮以下情況： （1）在一個 P2P網絡惡意節點可以上傳的作品注入了一些損壞的代碼, (2）一個數據包轉發到另一個節點，無線 Mesh網絡攻擊中的一個節點可能會提出一個損壞的數據包, (3) 一個惡意節點集可能注入好建議在OSN產品質量差上。 這項研究的目的是提出一個正式的數學理論，分佈式識別惡意攻擊，特別是在節點上的行為, 和那些網絡協議或網絡應用，需要節點互動或合作。我們的目標是建立一個正式和分析方法，模型和分析的基礎網絡協議或應用程序的行為。這個數學理論將提供網絡工作研究人員在需要設計安全可靠的協議，即不受惡意攻擊的基本認識。

415211.label: Realisation of objectives
415211.value: In this project, we produced fundamental results on how to accurately identify malicious and colluding nodes in P2P distributed systems, for example, when one is using P2P file sharing or P2P streaming or P2P Video-on-Demand services, if one or more malicious nodes try to send out corrupted packets (e.g., corrupted encoded signatures or coded information), we have a "distributed" algorithm to accurately and quickly identify the set of malicious nodes. This provides a neat way for many companies to launch their P2P services without worrying about malicious people who intentionally want to damage their services. Furthermore, our distributed identification algorithm is a special class of randomized algorithm which has low computational complexity.

415311.label: Project Title(Chinese)
415311.value: 开发可靠云计算之框架，技术与实验

415311.label: Project Objectives
415311.value: Provide general architectural design paradigms for reliable cloud computing. We will work out general paradigms in architectural design reusable for building reliable cloud computing systems. We are particularly interested in the mechanisms that can seamlessly integrate remote cloud-side computing entities (i.e., components) and local ones into an executable to perform the specified tasks reliably. We will investigate how to model the relationship of the components, either remote or local, of a cloud computing system, and how such a relationship, together with the component deployment strategies, influences the reliability of the whole system. Propose new reliability evaluation and prediction approaches, and design new fault tolerance techniques for enhancing cloud computing reliability. Components in a cloud may be identical in functionality, but diverse in Quality-of-Service (QoS) metrics from an end user’s perspective. Our objective is to leverage the feature of cloud computing that these user-specific QoS metrics can be conveniently measured by the cloud components, so as to work out new reliability evaluation and prediction approaches in real time. We will solve how to dynamically learn a fault tolerant structure by a series of new techniques based on the reliability evaluation and prediction results, which can be adapted on-line to meet the reliability requirements of the end user applications. Work out new testing and fault localization methodology for cloud computing. Testing maintains its key role as a natural, viable, and critical means in locating and eliminating software faults so as to achieve high reliability in cloud computing. Traditional testing techniques cannot handle a complicated cloud computing system which involves a large number of components. Our objective here is to formulate a novel methodology, including a set of customized testing and fault localization approaches, in fighting against actual and potential cloud computing faults. In particular, we will investigate how to leverage user experiences in testing cloud components, how to track system status and integrate the program traces collected by components in different locations, how to perform anomaly detection in system behaviors, and how to conduct effective fault diagnosis when a fault is detected.

415311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415311.value: Cloud computing is a trend taking shape in the IT industry which will significantly change the way people use the IT facilities in the coming decades. Through the provisioning of dynamically-scalable and seamlessly-virtualized resources (e.g., storage and computing capacities) as Internet-based services, cloud computing emerges as a cost-effective paradigm to offer infrastructure-free computing, where people can run customized services and access personal data from any locations – offices, homes, trips, or within other organizations. Embraced by many software providers (e.g., Google, IBM, Amazon, and Microsoft), cloud computing has been adopted to implement more and more software products recently. The “pay-as-you-go” business model of cloud computing makes it particularly attractive for the financial, business management, logistics and supply chain, and many other business entities playing centric roles in Hong Kong’s economic systems. Towards maturing such a modern computing paradigm, reliability is inevitably a critical consideration for software providers before they would move their products to the clouds, as well as for end users before they would trust their data and everyday computing tasks to the clouds. However, a comprehensive approach to building reliable cloud computing systems is still at large. How to achieve reliability in cloud computing is yet to be clearly understood and effectively addressed. This is an urgent call for attention to the software reliability engineering community. This project will tackle the challenges and exploit the opportunities ahead of us due to the emerging characteristics of cloud computing so as to make it a reliable next-generation computing paradigm. Specifically, in order to combat system faults that jeopardize reliability, we will provide a systematic methodology in which faults in cloud computing systems can be effectively avoided in architectural design, predicted and tolerated during system runtime, and localized and removed eventually. Our research output will be a reliable cloud computing framework and a toolkit, which can be conveniently adopted by both the industrial and the academic communities for building reliable cloud systems. The cloud computing based software providers and end users will benefit from our research outcome accordingly: It gives the providers a set of effective measures to render their reliable software products, and mitigates the sufferings of the end users from unreliable system usage. 415311.label: Realisation of objectives
415311.value: All the project objectives have been either completely achieved or exceedingly achieved. In addition to the proposed reliability engineering techniques for cloud computing, we employed the proposed approaches on service-oriented computing, which is a major technique for building distributed systems, such as cloud computing platforms. Moreover, we extended the proposed techniques for other application domain, including wireless sensor network, location-based social network, and Web search. To achieve the project objectives, a number of machine learning and data mining techniques are employed and proposed, including collaborative filtering, matrix factorization, online learning, etc.

415311.label: Major findings and research outcome
415311.value: Totally 1 book, 6 journal papers, and 19 conference papers have been published, all acknowledging the support of this grant. These publications cover the project’s objectives in various aspects. We describe the resulting outcomes as follows (We use [J1] label to refer to journal publication [1], and [C1] label to refer to conference publication [1], etc. Note [J7] is a book publication). The first objective focuses on providing general architectural design paradigms for reliable cloud computing. Firstly, the problems of optimal deployment of cloud applications are investigated, including spectral clustering-based deployment approach [J1], latency-aware co-deployment mechanism [C12], topology-aware deployment approach [C13], and so on. Moreover, machine learning methodologies, such as online learning methods [C8], and matrix factorization methods [C10] are also investigated, which can be employed to help build reliable cloud applications. The second objective proposes new reliability evaluation and prediction approaches for enhancing cloud computing reliability. We systematically investigate the problem of reliability prediction and propose several approaches, including model-based approach [C15], online approach [C4, J6], ranking-based approach [J3], time-aware approach [C1], network coordinate-based approach [C11], and hierarchical matrix factorization approach [C19]. To enable comprehensive experimental studies, we collect and publish reusable research datasets [J4]. We also extend the proposed approach to instantaneous amplitude [C17]. Moreover, a book [J7] has been published to comprehensively introduce our reliability prediction and evaluation approaches. The last objective attempts to work out new testing and fault localization methodology for cloud computing. We have proposed a set of methods, including mobility-assisted diagnosis [J2], congestion performance improvement approach [C3], mining test oracles [C2], and online verification [C14]. Moreover, we also extend the problem to community question and answering services ([C5] for classification, [C6] for quality prediction, [C7] for community comparison, and [C9] for question subjectivity identification), application reachability [C18], click models [C16], and Tag mining [J5].

415311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
415311.value: In this project, we have investigated the development of reliable cloud computing, including architecture design, reliability evaluation and prediction, and fault localization. The techniques applied cover various machine learning and data mining approaches, such as matrix factorization, collaborative filtering, online learning, SVM, and so on. Further research can be investigated for the design and dissemination of a reusable toolkit with a collection of demonstrable datasets. This would allow our formulated cloud reliability techniques to be implemented and distributed for wide adoption among researchers and developers. Developers of cloud computing platforms can effectively apply suitable reliability techniques, while researchers can further investigate based on our proposed research problems.

415311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
415311.value: We successfully formalize a systematic and efficient design paradigm for reliable cloud computing. Included in this paradigm are architecture design, reliability prediction, and fault localization. The effectiveness of this paradigm in advancing the current state-of-the-art cloud reliability engineering has been demonstrated through the design and implementation of the proposed techniques therein. This project enables cloud reliability engineering to build reliable cloud applications, whose achieved reliability can be accurately predicted. The resulting paradigm is both comprehensive and systematic. It formulates methodologies to modern cloud applications. The proposed techniques in this project promote the development of cloud reliability research in general, and facilitate the ongoing research in the Internet era.

415511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415511.value: 本項目旨在開發一套支援電腦輔助發音訓練(CAPT) 中發音錯誤的自動檢測和診斷技術。據估計, 自2010全球有2億英語學習者, 僅在亞洲的比例已超過英語為母語的人數。這巨大的需求導致英語教師的嚴重短缺。加上發音訓練是需要學習者頻密的練習及得到老師的糾正反饋。語音識別（ASR）技術能在線 CAPT平台上提供全天候的, 晝夜不停的,個人化學習平台。然而，ASR的性能有限制，特別是在處理非母語學習者的語音。練習時重複的語言常有細微的差異, 但可能會導致非常不同的識別結果。ASR 在CAPT中的應用, 一般是為學習者的輸入語音自動打分。若輸入的語音較長, 自動打分與人工打分可以達到良好的相關性。然而，若輸入的語音較短, 相關性很容易會下降。因此現有的ASR技術很難針對節段性的發音(即音素為基礎的) 提供足夠的分辨能力。我們建議制定有效的節段性發音錯誤檢測和診斷的ASR技術, 從而產生局部的糾正反饋, 對學習者更有幫助。我們的目標是母語(L1) 為中文（粵語或普通話）的英語(第二語言L2)學習者。雙語能力是一個重要的競爭優勢，能鞏固香港作為國際都會的地位。我們計劃從語料庫發挖常見的節段性發音錯誤, 並研究如何在聲學模型中捕捉正確及錯誤的音素間細微的偏差。此外，我們亦將制定有效的發音錯誤檢測和診斷 ASR聲學建模的判別性訓練技術。

415511.label: Realisation of objectives
415511.value: Pedagogically, computer-aided pronunciation training (CAPT) systems can be improved by giving effective feedback prioritized based on the “severity” of mispronunciations. We model the processes of phonetic mispronunciation productions by phonological rules and attempt to associate each with a score. We propose a linear regression model, where the gradation of a word mispronunciation is a linear combination of the gradation scores of the corresponding phonological rules. Perceptual gradation of word-level mispronunciations in non-native English speech are crowdsourced from many listeners. A “WorkerRank” algorithm is devised identify reliable workers in crowdsourcing. Running a least-square linear regression analysis can generate rule scores which are used to predict gradation of word-level mispronunciations. Reasonable correlation and agreement found between human-labeled and machine-predicted gradations show our approach is promising. We have also developed a two-pass framework with discriminative acoustic modeling for mispronunciation detection and diagnoses (MD&D). The first pass of mispronunciation detection does not require explicit phonetic error pattern modeling. The framework instantiates a set of anti-phones and a filler model to augment the original phone model for each canonical phone. This guarantees full coverage of all possible error patterns while maximally exploits the phonetic information derived from the text prompt. The anti-phones can be used to detect substitutions. The filler model can detect insertions and phone skips are allowed to detect deletions. As such, there is no prior assumption on the possible error patterns that can occur. The second pass of mispronunciation diagnosis expands the detected insertions and substitutions into phone networks and another recognition pass attempts to reveal the phonetic identities of the detected mispronunciation errors. Discriminative training (DT) is applied respectively to the acoustic models of the mispronunciation detection pass and the mispronunciation diagnosis pass. DT effectively separates the acoustic models of the canonical phones and the anti-phones. Overall, DT reduces the error rate by about 40% relative. Additionally, we investigate the use of Multi-Distribution Deep Neural Networks (MD-DNNs) for integrating acoustic and state transition models in free phone recognition of L2 English speech. Preliminary experiments show that the integration can reduce the error rate by over 41% compared with separate models. We have also extended our study to include suprasegmental aspects of non-native English, specifically in rhythmic aspects of CAPT.

415511.label: Major findings and research outcome
415511.value: It is of pedagogical importance to be able to detect mispronunciations, diagnose them and generate corrective feedback to help the learner. It is also important to be able to prioritize the errors and focus on a few in training before moving to others. This avoids presenting too many errors at the same time such that learners may be confused or discouraged. Once criterion for selecting errors is perceptual relevance because perceptually serious errors hamper communication and must be corrected promptly. Hence we have devised a model for predicting gradation of L2 English mispronunciations using crowdsourced ratings at the word-level but then transformed into phonological rule scores that can be used for prediction. Reasonable correlation and agreement are found between the human-labeled and machine labeled predictions which reflects that our proposed approach is promising. This work is published in O-COCOSDA 2012, APSIPA 2013 and SLaTE 2013. Effective mispronunciation detection and diagnoses (MD&D) for computer-aided pronunciation training (CAPT) relies on strong acoustic models that can discriminate between the deviant productions from the canonical productions. We have developed a two-pass framework with discriminative acoustic modeling for MD&D. The first pass can detect errors of all kinds – substitutions, deletions and insertions. The second pass is for diagnosis, which is achieved expanding detected insertions and substitutions into phone networks and running another recognition pass. Overall, DT reduces the error rate by about 40% relative. This work will be published in APSIPA 2015 (forthcoming) and also submitted to IEEE Transactions in Audio, Speech and Language Processing (under second review). We have also investigated the use of deep learning for MD&D. The use of free-phone recognition covers all error types and can be approached with an Acoustic Model (AM) and a State-Transition Model (STM), which are generally trained independently and hence contextual information may be lost. We propose a joint Acoustic-State-Transition Model (ASTM) which uses a MD-DNN to integrate the AM and STM. Preliminary experiments show that the ASTM can reduce the error rate by over 41% compared with separate AM and STM models. Related work has been published in Interspeech 2012, ISCSLP 2014 and SLaTE 2015. In addition, we have extended out study to include suprasegmental aspects of non-native English, specifically in rhythmic aspects of CAPT, which has been published in Computer Speech & Language in 2015.

415511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
415511.value: In the recent years, deep learning has rapidly gained popularity in speech processing. We will conduct a thorough investigation in deep learning for MD&D and the development of CAPT systems. We plan to cover both segmental and suprasegmental aspects of non-native English. Also, we will attempt to model non-categorical mispronunciations in non-native English speech from Chinese learners.

415511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
415511.value: Non-native language learners are eager to attain high pronunciation proficiency of the target language. However, learning the unfamiliar sounds and prosody of a new language is not easy. High proficiency is attained through extensive practice with guidance from language instructors but good language instruction is often a scarce resource. Automatic speech recognition technologies can support online computer-aided pronunciation training (CAPT) that supplements teachers’ instructions with round-the-clock accessibility and individualized feedback. An essential technology for CAPT is mispronunciation detection, which refers to locating a speech segment that is incorrectly articulated. To provide useful feedback for the learner, another important technology is mispronunciation diagnosis, which involves telling the reader in what way is a speech segment incorrect. This project investigates the use of discriminative training that effectively separates the canonical productions from the deviant productions to improve the performance of both mispronunciation detection and diagnosis (MD&D). We have also devised an approach that predicts the gradation of mispronunciations (from subtle to severe) based on crowdsourced human perceptions which are then decomposed into scores for phonological rules. In view of the recent popularity of deep learning approaches to speech processing, we have also investigated the use of deep neural networks on the problem of MD&D, as well as extending our work to cover CAPT in the rhythmic aspects of non-native speech.

415611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415611.value: Natural Orifice Transluminal Endoscopic Surgery (NOTES) involves accessing the abdominal cavity via one of the bodies’ natural orifices, e. g. mouth, anus or vagina. It represents a major paradigm shift in general surgery by operating inside the peritoneal cavity through small holes performed in hollow organs. This new approach is very appealing from patients’ perspectives because it eliminates completely abdominal wall aggression and promises to reduce postoperative pain, in addition to all the advantages brought by laparoscopic surgery. However, the constraints imposed by both the mode of access and the limited technology currently available makes NOTES very challenging for the surgeons. So far the devices used are simply based on improvements of current endoscopic platforms. The long and almost completely flexible instruments allow only limited force transmission for traction and tend to buckle away from their target when force is exerted. Besides, the limited visual field and lack of triangulation between the imager and the tools restricts the surgeons to judge the depth and therefore degrades the dexterity further. The challenges introduced by natural orifice approaches require invention of novel instruments in order to make this emerging operative access safe and reproducible. The convergence of miniaturization, communication and micro-mechatronics technologies brings the possibility to realize the revolutionary concept of cooperative micro-robotic systems. In this project we will develop a reconfigurable cooperative micro-robotic system to provide an effective and efficient solution to solve the critical problems of retraction and triangulation during NOTES procedures. An extensible framework will be designed and developed to make a stable support by magnetic coupling with the external magnets and provide a platform to carry multiple surgical instruments. Miniature modular robotic tools will be magnetically guided and configured by the operators on the framework to provide extra vision and task assistance without the constraints of the entry incision. The wireless feature of the imaging and lighting module can avoid the confliction with other equipments and ensure the dexterity. The overall objective of the proposed research is to develop a magnetically guided reconfigurable cooperative micro-robotic system capable of providing retraction and triangulation assistance during NOTES procedures. 自然腔道內窺鏡手術利用人體本身的微小自然腔道，如口腔、肛門、和陰道進入人體腹腔內進行手術。只是一個全新的無傷痕微創手術技術，給病人帶來微創腹腔鏡手術所有的好處之外，在病人的身體外部不產生任何疤痕，同時手術的痛苦程度大大降低。但是，自然腔道的狹小和相關專用器械和技術的不成熟給做手術的醫生帶來很多新的挑戰。為了使自然腔道內窺鏡手術安全可靠和程序規範化，在此研究項目中，我們將研制一套專門用於自然腔道內窺鏡手術的模塊化可重組微小型機器人系統。每個模塊由自然腔道一一送入腹腔後，在外置磁鐵的固定下，組成俱有視頻、牽引、精確三角定位、以及遙控手術操作功能的可重組微小型機器人系統，幫助做手術的醫生安全、高效的完成自然腔道內窺鏡手術，減少病人的痛苦，造福于人類。

415611.label: Realisation of objectives
415611.value: We completed all the project objectives. We developed the strategy for the reconfigurable cooperative micro-robotic system to provide original solutions to the critical problems of retraction and triangulation during NOTES procedures. We designed and constructed an extensible framework to make stable support with mechanical and magnetic couplings to provide a platform to hold multiple surgical instruments, with the associated localization algorithms. We connected the wireless imaging and lighting modules coupled with the extensible framework to provide triangulation for better vision and illumination to improve the safety and efficiency of NOTES procedures and to eliminate the disturbance brought by the tethered modules. We built the end-effector tools to help to achieve suitable surgical filed to ensure success and safety in NOTES procedures. Finally we developed a prototype of the reconfigurable cooperative micro-robotic system to provide the enabling technology to facilitate the success and improve the safety of NOTES procedures.

415711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415711.value: During the last decade, detailed measurements of daylight availability have been made throughout the world. Hong Kong participated fully in this programme. A task now is to reduce the data into information and guidelines for practical use. A better use of daylight is a crucial factor in sustainable design. The Commission Internationale de l'Eclairage (CIE) publishes an international standard method for classifying sky brightness patterns (CIE, 2003). It is known as the CIE General Sky, and its purpose is not only to provide an agreed method of analysing measured data but to make possible international comparison of daylight climates. This is a key aim both in daylighting research and in practical applications(He & Ng, 2010; Ng, Cheng et al., 2007; Ng, Gadi et al., 2007), and it is the basis of the project that we propose. CIE General Sky can be defined by sky scans from ground stations. However, it is resource intensive to run and maintain. And it can only cover one location at certain time. To test out the feasibility of utilizing weather observation data for daylight and sky type prediction, we have developed a method to predict daylight availability dynamically based on forecasts of weather observatory for Hong Kong(Ng, Gadi et al., 2007) which indicates a way forward. To improve accuracy and application, this study will further investigate the relationship between more different types of meteorological data from HKO weather statistics and CIE Standard General Sky under subtropical climate conditions. This investigation is based on the sky scans from June 2003 to May 2005 collected by CIE International Daylight Measurement Programme (IDMP) station in The Chinese University of Hong Kong. Simultaneous meteorological data such as solar irradiance, sunshine duration and cloud cover from Hong Kong Observatory (HKO) will be correlated to the measured sky scans. Such work is seen by the CIE as an essential follow-up of the IDMP(CIE, 2010). Other countries are making this type of analysis so international comparisons will be made. This study will conduct an experimental study for cross-comparing the vertical sky component (VSC) and interior daylight performance of modelled and calculation data. A study of daylight performance in typical residential buildings of Hong Kong will also be conducted to investigate the improvement of prediction under the real sky types predicted by meteorological data against that under the CIE overcast sky. 過去的十年中，世界各地開展了詳細的天然光測量，香港也參與了這一計劃。現在的任務是將數據轉化為相關資訊和指導原則便於實際應用，在可持續設計中，充分利用天然光是一個至關重要的因素。國際照明委員會（CIE）出版了一個國際標準方法進行天空分類(CIE,2003)，它被稱為CIE標準一般天空，其目的不僅是提供了一個共識的方法分析測量數據，而且使國際間的天然光氣候比較成為可能。這是在採光研究和實際應用中的一個關鍵目標(He&Ng,2010; Ng,Cheng et al.,2007; Ng,Gadi et al.,2007)，也是我們此申請項目的基礎。 CIE一般天空可以由地面觀測站的天空掃描器獲得，但是地面站需要大量資源來運行和維護，並且它只能局限在某段時間和某個位置。為了測試利用氣象數據來預測天然光和天空類型的可行性，基於香港天文臺的天氣預報資料，我們已經提出一種動態的方法來預測天然光可用性(Ng, Gadi et al.,2007)，這種方法預示了進一步研究的方向。為了提高預測精度和進一步應用，本次研究將進一步調查香港天文臺不同類型的氣象資料和CIE標準一般天空之間的關係。此次研究將採用在香港中文大學設立的國際照明委員會國際天然光觀測計畫（IDMP）觀測站的天空掃描資料，時間從2003年6月至2005年5月，以及同時間香港天文臺的氣象數據，例如太陽輻射，日照時數和雲量。國際照明委員會(CIE)把此類工作當作國際天然光觀測計畫的一個重要的後續研究(CIE, 2010)。其他國家正在開展這種分析，以便進行國際間比較。 這項研究將進行實驗來對比從模型和軟體計算獲得的垂直天空分量（VSC）和室內採光性能資料。這項研究也將調查相對於CIE標準陰天空下，在由氣象資料預測的實際天空類型下，香港典型住宅樓宇的採光性能的改善。

415711.label: Realisation of objectives
415711.value: For classifying CIE standard general sky types based on meteorological data and deriving longer sky data to enrich the daylight data set of Hong Kong, the objectives have been achieved. In the first step, a clear sky index (kc) is derived from global horizontal irradiance simultaneously measured with the scanned sky data from 2003 to 2005. In the second step, the clear sky index is related to the measured hourly Hong Kong Representative Sky (HKRS), which is a subset of CIE standard general sky, to obtain a kc -HKRS relation. Finally, the hourly HKRS is predicted by the kc -HKRS relation and the kc derived from the hourly global horizontal irradiance from the Typical Meteorological Year (TMY) data, which are based on hourly measured weather data over a 25-year period (1979 to 2003) in Hong Kong. For conducting an experimental study for cross-comparing the vertical sky component (VSC) and indoor daylight performance with modeled and calculation based data, and a study of daylight performance in typical residential buildings of Hong Kong to investigate the improvement of VSC and indoor daylight performance under the real sky types predicted by meteorological data against that under CIE overcast sky, the objectives have been achieved. The Perez all-weather sky model is the most widely used sky model for dynamic annual daylight simulations. This study analyzes the influence of HKRS on estimating VSC compared with the Perez all-weather sky model. This study estimated the VSC in four cardinal directions to compare the VSC under the HKRS and Perez all-weather sky model. The two-year measurements of irradiance data, illuminance data, and sky luminance distribution were utilized to calculate the VSC of the HKRS and Perez all-weather sky model, as well as the VSC of the real sky luminance distribution (observed VSC). The sky luminance distributions calculated by the Perez all-weather sky model and the HKRS in the VSC study were generated from the same observed horizontal illuminance data.

415711.label: Major findings and research outcome
415711.value: This study has presented a method to predict the Hong Kong Representative Sky (HKRS), which is a subset of CIE standard general sky, by hourly irradiance data from the Typical Meteorological Year (TMY) data. The evaluation of sensitivity of vertical sky component (VSC) has demonstrated that the HKRS can provide better results than the Perez all-weather sky model. Nine to twenty-three percent error reduction can be expected. The east and west window orientations obtain greater error reductions than the north and south orientations. Given that the sky data in dynamic daylight simulation are typically derived from the TMY data by using the Perez all-weather sky model, the evaluation of sensitivity of VSC indicates that for dynamic daylight simulation, the HKRS could provide better accuracy than the Perez all-weather sky model if both are derived from the same TMY data. Three HKRSs can be classified by the clear sky index based on the kc -HKRS relation by considering the solar altitude effects: kc ≤ f(C1), f(C1) < kc ≤ f(C2), and kc >f(C2), corresponding to skies 1, 8, and 13 of the HKRS, respectively. Here, f(C1) and f(C2) can be defined by a function of the solar altitude. Given the hourly sky types, the absolute sky luminance distribution can be obtained if the zenith luminance is provided. The zenith luminance can be derived from Perez’s zenith luminance model by using the irradiance data. The predicted hourly HKRS can be utilized to assess the annual daylight performance of buildings in high-density Hong Kong to provide the “real” daylight performance during a whole year. One paper in international scholarly journal and two refereed conference papers have been published based on this study (See attachments in Part C).

415711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
415711.value: The current study can only classify three CIE standard general skys. Further study can be conducted to predict more sky types by using more meteorological parameters. The study proposes a method applicable for Hong Kong to classify the sky types. This method could be further evaluated in other places under other climate conditions. International comparisons can be made to propose a universal method to be used more broadly.

415711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
415711.value: This study proposes a method to predict the hourly Hong Kong Representative Sky (HKRS), which is a subset of CIE standard general sky, from Typical Meteorological Year (TMY) data. An evaluation of the sensitivity of the vertical sky component demonstrates that the HKRS can provide better results than the Perez all-weather sky model, which is the most widely used sky model for dynamic daylighting simulation. Nine to twenty-three percent error reductions can be expected in the four cardinal directions. To predict the HKRS from the TMY data, a clear sky index (kc) can be derived from global horizontal irradiance. Three HKRSs can be classified by the clear sky index corresponding to skies 1, 8, and 13 of the HKRS, respectively. The predicted hourly HKRS can provide the sky luminance data for the dynamic simulation of buildings.

415911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415911.value: Spaceborne Synthetic Aperture Radar Interferometry (InSAR) has become nowadays a very powerful technique to monitor ground motions and to recover Digital Elevation Models (DEM). The microwave signal sent by satellites can in fact penetrate clouds and does not need the light of sun to record pictures of the ground. Moreover, due to the coherent nature of the radar signal, images can interfere with eachother revealing possible millimetric displacement of the observed terrain (and thus detecting landslides, subsidence, earthquake precursors, building stability, …). Depending on the characteristics of different sensors, areas of several thousands sqkm can be imaged at once, with up to 1m resolution. One of the major sources of noise in InSAR is the Water Vapor (WV) content of the atmosphere. The radar signal can in fact penetrate it but it is slightly delayed resulting in a distortion of the detected ground displacement. As a consequence, to successfully apply interferometric techniques, the atmospheric WV delay must be estimated and removed from radar data. In the past years researchers tackled the atmospheric mitigation problem in InSAR from different points of view. In this work, we exploit the novel unique availability of SAR and Atmospheric data in the region of Hong Kong (HK) to study the local spatio-temporal characteristics of WV. As an outcome, we expect not only to improve the mitigation of radar delay, but also to retrieve high-resolution WV maps to better tune Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) models. The core idea of the work is taking advantage of all SAR data acquired over HK with three different wavelengths (and thus different sensitivity to WV delay): L, C and X band. The available time series will be processed with advanced multi-temporal techniques (as the Permanent Scatterers -PS- one) that allow precise estimation of spurious delay in interferograms. The obtained maps will be analyzed together with GPS series of Zenith Wet Delay (ZWD) and vertical profiles taken with Radiosondes. The three techniques are complementary with eachother: InSAR has high spatial resolution but poor temporal sampling, conversely GPS data have poor spatial resolution and almost continuous sampling. Radiosondes acquire twice per day giving also vertical resolution. Data will be cross-validated and merged with the aid of NWP models like Wolf and MM5. The expectation is to be able to drive NWP models with GPS and Radiosondes to mitigate WV delay on interferograms, and to use PS WV maps to improve NWP modeling. 目前，在地表形變檢測及數位高程模型的建立過程中，星載合成孔徑雷達干涉測量技術(InSAR)已經發展成為一項強有力的工具。由星載雷達發射的微波信號可以穿透雲霧，並全天候、不分白晝地接收地表資料。此外，由於雷達信號所特有的相干特性，對其影像進行干涉處理後可以監測到毫米級別的地形形變，因此該項技術尤其適用於在滑坡、地陷、地震前兆和建築物穩定性等目標的監測。在監測範圍及解析度方面，基於不同感測器的特性，每景影像可以覆蓋到數千平方公里的範圍，同時解析度達到一米。 InSAR監測中的雜訊主要來自大氣中的水汽。儘管微波信號可以穿透雲霧，但其相位會產生延遲，從而對結果造成影響。為了能夠精確地測量地表形變值，大氣水汽對微波信號造成的相位延遲就必須被準確地計算出來、並以此對初始結果進行校正。 在過去的若干年中，不同學者從多方面研究了計算大氣延遲的問題。在本專案中，我們將利用香港地區的SAR資料和大氣資料研究大氣水汽含量的時空分佈特徵。目的不僅在於計算出大氣水汽造成的延遲，同時也能得到高解析度的大氣水汽含量圖，以便更好地調整數值天氣預報（NWP）模型。 研究的核心思路是分別研究三個不同波段，即L、C和X波段的SAR資料（因為不同波段對於同樣含量水汽的延遲不同）。我們將利用多時空序列技術來處理這些資料，從而在干涉圖中精確地計算延遲值。所得結果將被用於與GPS測得對流層濕分量延遲資料以及無線電探空儀所測得垂直方向資料加以比較分析。事實上，這三項資料有很好的互補關係：InSAR資料擁有較高的空間解析度，但是採樣時間間隔過長；GPS資料的空間解析度很低，卻可以連續採樣；而每天兩次的無線電探空儀測量可以得到垂直方向上的資料。分析的結果將用來驗證並完善MM5模型和Wolf模型等數值天氣預報模型。本課題的最終目的是借助GPS資料和無線電探空儀資料來削減干涉影像結果中大氣水汽造成的信號延遲，並且利用計算的大氣水汽含量圖來完善已有的數值預報模型。

415911.label: Realisation of objectives
415911.value: This research studied the information of water vapor extracted from Atmospheric Phase Screen (APS) obtained by Permanent Scatterer SAR Interferometry (PSInSAR), and was comparatively studied with synchronized water vapor data, including GPS observations, radiosondes and NWP simulated products. The cross-validating between APS and synchronized external data showed strong correlation. Firstly, the water vapor maps over Hong Kong were derived at three different wavelength (L, C and X band) and four different types of SAR images (ALOS, Envisat ASAR, TerraSAR-X and COSMO) applying the PSInSAR technique. A water vapor component model was proposed for comparison between SAR and non-SAR water vapors by separating the APS derived from PS analysis into orbital error, stratification and turbulence. Besides the typical mixing turbulent and stratification terms, the spatial liner trend and ground feature related stationary term has been accounted for in mixed water vapor. Based on this model, a logical strategy of differentiation between spatial linear trend and height dependent stratification, and between stationary term and turbulence signal, was developed. Secondly, the spatial statistical properties of water vapor components have been investigated by analyzing water vapor signal obtained from SAR APS, and that from NWP Integrated Water Vapor (IWV) model in differential comparison mode and in different spatial scales. Furthermore, in a demonstration example, we find nice correlation between X-Band InSAR estimated APS and the accumulated total grid scale precipitation from NWP model. In addition, InSAR derived water vapor maps also showed correlation with radiosondes data. Thirdly, point-based precipitable Water Vapor (PWV) from SAR APS and GPS meteorology are compared based on the proposed model in order to assess the precision of water vapor signal obtained from SAR. Two implementation methods, a differential and a pseudo absolute mode, were proposed to build the comparison links between SAR differential water vapor and GPS absolute water vapor. The comparison between pro-corrected and post-corrected interferogram demonstrated that most part of large atmospheric noise have been reasonable mitigated. The coherent point target technique was also employed to validate the mitigation improvement. From deterministic statistics, more than 88% coherent points’ two-way LOS tropospheric residual delay declined to less than 10 mm after the mitigation with GPS tropospheric map derived from PWV. At last, we come to the conclusion that the APS at small scale derived is promising in improving of atmospheric error modeling for synchronized water vapor data.

415911.label: Major findings and research outcome
415911.value: The major findings and research outcome in this project are as following: 1) Exploratory study in a comparative perspective for water vapor from Permanent Scatters SAR Interferometry and synchronous data set. The research perspective is innovative among similar studies in this topic. In our research, credible SAR APS in form of transformed water vapor is compared with external synchronized data to study the compensating feasibility of InSAR atmospheric effect. More than 100 APS maps from 3 tracks, NWP water vapor maps, radiosondes and synchronous GPS campaign data were collected for the research analysis. Results demonstrated that water vapor from InSAR presents unparalleled superiority with its highest spatial scale, e.g. tens of meters, which would be highly valuable in regional water vapor study or meteorological service. 2) Precision of water vapor measurements from SAR APS is evaluated by comparing with synchronous data. Point-based comparison results provide us the individual precision of water vapor from APS. It then implies the potential and limitation of atmospheric compensating of SAR interferometric measurements with external water vapor data. Map-based comparison results provide us the coherence and difference of spatial temporal statistical characteristics of water vapor field from multiple sources. The spatial temporal decorrelation of water vapor turbulence signal has been studied with NWP maps using correlation analysis. The result shows that 1~2 hour of turbulence in all scales are highly correlated. Stationary term and mixing turbulence term have been distinguished with two approaches-temporal periodic averaging and spatial spectral filter-based on spatial and temporal difference of characteristics between both terms. This would provide valuable predictions in water vapor mutual calibration or data synergy, especially when employed data have spatial resolution discrepancy or temporal gaps. 3) A logical strategy of differentiation of water vapor components and implementations for comparison were introduced as useful reference in atmospheric probing in interferometric SAR. We in this research proposed water vapor component model to serve for comparative analysis between differential water vapor signal from SAR APS and absolute water vapor. Based on this model, components in total water vapor can be discriminated and the analyzing target can be focused on each component instead of mixed signal. The proposed rational strategy to differentiating of water vapor components and the implementation of comparison way (differential mode and pseudo-absolute comparison) between SAR and non SAR data can be taken as valuable reference in technical operations of atmospheric compensating in SAR interferometry.

415911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
415911.value: Future work includes: 1) Ground feature related signal validation The influence of ground feature (especially in Hong Kong) related to water vapor signal have not yet been demonstrated quantitavely, and how to model such water vapor signal composition still need more work. The external validation of ground feature related stationary term is suggested to be taken using fine scale Land use classification map or coinstantaneous high resolution Remote Sensing Images to validate the stationary term. 2) Finding meteorological application for the different terms of APS including not only temporal reference, but also nominal terms of spatial linear trend, stratification and stationary term. 3) GPS data is valuable to provide point-based atmospheric information. But such GPS data only provides sparse samples for atmospheric compensating in map-based SAR interferograms; The performance of mitigation using GPS data only still depends on other factors, which should be improved in the future. 4) The understanding of water vapor spatial temporal characteristics in different scale and for each component still requires more effort to improve. Water vapor behavior described by decorrelation would be significant to predict that with which data atmospheric signal component can be mitigated and in which extent such mitigation can be achieved.

415911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
415911.value: In the first place, the research provided a detailed scope into the distribution and composition of Atmospheric Phase Screen (APS) derived from PSInSAR technique over Hong Kong with high spatial resolution. In addition, APS is separated into different components by their physical properties, namely the orbital error, stratification and turbulence for better understanding and comparing with external data. In the second place, the APS was cross validated with synchronous external data including GPS, NWP model and radiosondes. The results showed a consistent correlation between APS and external models, so that it is possible to correct atmospheric noises in SAR interferometry with synchronous external products. The significance lays in that the precise modeling of water vapor signal directly help break through the obstacle of atmospheric decorrelation in detection by conventional SAR interferometry, and the statistical characteristics of atmospheric phase screen components in SAR interferometry helps better understanding the physical composition of water vapor, thus we can better mitigate the water vapor effects using multi-temporal analysis or with the help of external synchronous data. The outcome of the research is an enhancement of atmospheric correction and will improve the applicability of InSAR technique.

416011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416011.value: Aim The aim of this project is to conduct research into boosting the energy efficiency of pipelined analog-to-digital converters. Project Background Analog-to-digital (A/D) converters play a crucial role in bridging the real world which is analog and the exponentially expanding digital world. Among different types of A/D converters (ADC), the pipelined architecture has been proved to be advantageous for high-speed and energy-efficient A/D conversion of signals requiring medium resolution; their applications range from wireless base station receivers to high-definition (HD) video acquisitions. The performance of these converters is advancing on several fronts, including resolution, bandwidth and energy efficiency. In this project, we propose to develop a new technique to boost the energy efficiency of the pipelined ADCs. Traditionally, closed-loop high-gain amplifiers are needed in pipelined ADCs to amplify residue quantization signals between the pipeline stages. They play a crucial role in determining the speed and energy efficiency of the ADCs. As the feature sizes of CMOS technologies are scaling down into the nano-meter region, the intrinsic gains of transistors decrease, thereby making high-gain amplifiers very costly in terms of energy consumption. Together with the fact that amplifiers consume static power, this limits the energy efficiency of the conventional pipelined ADCs. Brief Project Description In this project, we will investigate a new amplifier-less pipelined ADC technique. The technique uses a passive way to realize the essential function of residue quantization signal amplification; it does this both by stacking capacitors and exploiting a comparator-controlled charging circuit to buffer the amplified signal to the next pipeline stage. In principle, the circuit consumes only dynamic power and is amenable to technology scaling. The technique will be demonstrated by designing and fabricating such pipelined ADCs in a nano-meter CMOS technology with a targeted application of HD video acquisition. Significance of Project It will enable a plurality of devices which employ this technique to improve their overall energy efficiency, and thus contribute to a greener environment and a longer battery time for hand-held devices. 目標 此項目旨在研究一種新技術以提高流水線型模擬／數字轉換器(ADC)的能源效率。 項目背景 ADC在彌合模擬的自然世界和快速擴張的數字世界中發揮了至關重要的作用。與其他類型的ADC比較，流水線型ADC已經被證明在高速、低能耗和要求中等分辨率的模／數轉換應用中具有優勢，其應用範圍包括無線基站接收器和高清視頻採集等等。一直以來，ADC的性能在以下三方面不斷獲得提高：分辨率，帶寬和能效。在此項目中，我們將開發一種提高流水線型ADC能效的新技術。 傳統上，流水線型ADC需要閉環的高增益放大器以將每級的量化剩餘放大以供下級繼續量化。這些放大器很大程度上決定了ADC的速度和能效。隨著 CMOS技術的特徵尺寸縮小到納米區域，晶體管的內在增益減少，從而使高增益放大器需要非常大的能耗。另外，放大器有很大的靜態功耗。這些問題都限制了傳統的流水線型ADC的能源效率。 項目簡介 在此項目中，我們將研究一種新的無須放大器的流水線型 ADC技術。該技術使用一種被動的方式來實現剩餘量化信號的放大這一基礎功能；此方法利用堆疊電容器來進行信號放大，然後用一個用比較器實現的緩衝器來驅動下一級。理論上，此電路僅消耗動態功耗，並經得起CMOS技術尺寸縮小的檢驗。我們將在納米級CMOS工藝上設計以高清視頻採集為目標應用的這種流水線型ADC來驗證該技術。 項目意義 此項目會提高採用這種技術的設備的整體能源效率，從而有利於環境保護。

416011.label: Realisation of objectives
416011.value: The first objective has been fully accomplished. We have established theoretical analysis on the energy efficiency of both single-ended and differential charge-pump and comparator-based (CPCB) amplification circuits for pipelined ADC. Specifically, we have related the power consumption to the speed, load, supply voltage and thermal noise. The theoretical analysis has been verified with behavioural simulations in Matlab. The second objective has also been fully accomplished. We have developed two 11-bit 25 MSps pipelined ADCs in a 0.18 um CMOS technology. The first one is a single-ended version. It consumes 3.5 mW from a 1.8 V supply at 25 MSps while achieving a signal-to-noise-plus-distortion ratio (SNDR) of 39 dB. Although the measured SNDR is low, it is the first ever CPCB circuit, and the functionality of the new CPCB concept is proven. The second one is a fully-differential version. It operates from 1.8 V supply and achieves widely scalable power consumption and effective resolution bandwidth (ERBW). It consumes 54 uW at 125 kSps and 4.94 mW at 25 MSps while measuring a constant SNDR of 52 dB, independent of the sampling rate. The ADCs were targeted for video signal acquisition applications. The third objective is also accomplished. We have made system design and behavioural simulations of a high-speed CPCB ADC in a 90 nm CMOS. However, it is found that the input capacitance nonlinearity and the signal-dependent delay of the comparator adversely affect the performance of the CPCB pipelined ADC at high sampling rates. For this reason, only circuit design and simulations were conducted but the circuit is not realized in silicon. The fourth objective is fully accomplished. The CPCB amplifier can be used in any applications where power-efficient signal amplification is needed. The CPCB pipelined ADC, due to its frequency-power scalability, is particularly suitable for variable bandwidth analog-to-digital conversions, such as the baseband conversion in time-division Long Term Evolution (TD-LTE) wireless receivers, where the signal bandwidth is adaptive, varying from 1.4 MHz to 20 MHz.
