416011.label: Major findings and research outcome
416011.value: First of all, we have discovered a new voltage amplification technique, namely, the charge-pump and comparator-based (CPCB) amplification circuit. We have been the first to propose, analyze, design and verify the technique. The average power consumption of an ideal CPCB circuit is found to be the same as that of a digital circuit with the same load, speed and supply voltage. The results are reported in publications 8.3. The thermal noise performance is established in publication 8.3, equation (12). We identified that a part of the thermal noise in the CPCB circuit is a Wiener process, and revealed the relationship between the thermal noise and various design parameter. The results provide a basis for power optimization. We have proposed a passive fully differential circuit implementation of the CPCB concept without using a complex common-mode feedback circuit. Through a special arrangement of differential charge pump capacitors, the input common-mode voltage is completely rejected at the output of the CPCB amplifier. The circuit is reported in publication 8.3. We have validated the CPCB technique with two prototyping 11-bit pipelined ADCs in 0.18 um CMOS, one single-ended and the other differential. The single-ended version proves the feasibility of the CPCB technique while having a limited SNDR. The fully-differential version significantly improved the SNDR. It fully demonstrated the dynamic nature the CPCB technique. Its power consumption scales directly with the sampling rate for a frequency range of two decades, which is reported for the first time for amplifier-less pipelined ADCs. The outcomes are reported in publication 8.3. Second, we have developed a systematic optimization technique for pipelined successive approximation register (SAR) ADCs that use conventional amplifiers. We have revealed allocating about one quarter of the overall number of bits to the first stage is optimum in most practical situations. The results are reported in publication 8.4. Third, we have developed a calibration methodology for high-precision SAR ADCs. We have been the first to develop a systematic analysis on the complex design relations between various design parameters. The outcomes are reported in publication 8.2. Last, we have identified a new technique to suppress the clock feed-through and charge injection from switches. The technique is demonstrated in a 2nd order capacitance-to-digital converter (CDC) fabricated in 0.18 um CMOS. Enabled by the new technique, the CDC achieves the best energy efficiency and the highest linearity compared to other CDCs, as reported in publication 8.1.

416011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416011.value: We can exploit the frequency-power scalability feature of the CPCB pipelined ADC to develop ADCs for variable bandwidth applications, such as the baseband A/D conversion in TD-LTE wireless receivers. It is also worth to design CPCB amplifiers for other applications which need fixed-gain power-efficient amplifications. A constraint is that the CPCB amplifier drives only capacitive load. Another potential further development of the project is to investigate CPCB pipelined ADC with resolution greater than 11 bits. The nonlinear input capacitance of the comparator affects the gain, linearity and thermal noise of the CPCB amplifier. A small input capacitance is the key for higher resolution CPCB pipelined ADCs. We shall conduct further research on this.

416011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
416011.value: In this project, we have discovered a new voltage amplification technique, namely, the charge-pump and comparator-based (CPCB) amplification circuit. We have been the first to propose, analyze, design and verify this dynamic amplification technique. Signal amplification is a very fundamental function for most analog circuits, including the pipelined analog-to-digital converter (ADC). The dynamic CPCB amplification technique provides circuit designers with a completely new approach for power-efficient signal amplification, and is more amenable to CMOS technology scaling than traditional operational amplifiers. The CPCB technique has been demonstrated by two pipelined ADCs fabricated in a 0.18 um CMOS process for video signal acquisition applications. While the CPCB ensures high power efficiency, a passive fully differential circuit implementation has been developed to enable a high performance for the ADC. The designed ADC achieves a power consumption that scales directly with the sampling rate for a frequency range of two decades, which is reported for the first time for amplifier-less pipelined ADCs. The CPCB technique can improve the overall power efficiency of a plurality of electronic devices that requires signal amplification, and thus contribute to a greener environment and a longer battery time for hand-held/wearable electronic devices.

416311.label: Project Objectives
416311.value: * Dynamic texture synthesis in wavelet analysis and controls -- We propose the Gabor feature space in synthesis, based on the local texture direction analysis by Fourier transform. By maximizing the energy function in local windows, the generated Gabor filters are angle-calibrated, reflecting texture directions. We will work on adaptive resampling on surface vector fields to reduce distortion, and our study supports the intuitive controls of dynamic texturing guided by the aniso-scaling offset, without runtime updates of surface patches. * Interactive design of natural textures with efficient optimizations – Our study will explore the multi-way transition among more textures; control the local variants of textures for the natural distortion; model the intuitive process of dynamic texture synthesis. We will develop elastic transforms and optimization to control the local variants of textures, for interactive texture synthesis with constraints. We will extend the sketch model into deformable surfaces by incorporating the geometry features, so the surface synthesis directed by structures to facilitate the interactive texturing. * Complex solid-material texturing using hierarchical modeling -- To enhance the representation capability of solid texturing function, we introduce the novel approach for creating multi-solid textures and solid-texture graph, so complex materials could be represented with multiple solid textures mixed seamlessly and in hierarchical structures. Based on the analysis, the distribution and appearance of the cells will be modeled by composite cluster processes. For complex materials, we support the simple user input to guide the synthesis system, but hard to be determined. * Fully exploration of parallel synthesis using GPUs acceleration -- Lately, the advent of GPUs realizes that mainstream processor chips are now parallel systems. Texture synthesis on dynamic models involves large sets of pixel processing and floating point operations, which make it natural in GPUs parallel computing. We will investigate the optimizations and the interactive synthesis, and directly apply parallel texturing on surface/solid models to explore the strengths of GPGPU computation and highly efficient. The innovative natural texturing system to be developed is the first of its kind in which the state-of-art technologies from mathematical modeling, interactive sketching, realistic rendering and synthesis, and GPU-based accelerator are tightly coupled in a seamless manner. It has been the grand challenge to remodel the natural realism of natural texturing directly on object surfaces/bodies. Lately GPUs are arguably the most powerful and affordable computational hardware, and they are advancing at an incredible rate compared to CPUs. The advanced natural texturing tools to be developed will provide the efficient framework for applications including rich-media production, interactive games, special natural effects, and augmented design. The outputs of this project if funded will promote the local industry in Hong Kong to further develop advanced digital technologies, for low-cost and high-efficient natural texturing applications.

416311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416311.value: Texture synthesis, usually investigated in regular 2D grids, is seldom the end goal for interactive graphics/VR applications. Most modeling tools adopt texture mapping to wrap 2D textures onto a given surface. But, globally consistent texture mapping is rather difficult, either distortions or discontinuities are often introduced in such texturing strategy. Example-based texture synthesis now gains widespread popularity for their capability to take a small sample and create perceptually similar and pleasing textures. The major issue is that the synthesis of 3D texture or patterns is very difficult. Furthermore, the complex appearance of the materials could not be captured by the traditional procedure solid texture, and the setting of the parameters for complex material texturing is not easy. Our aim is to build the efficient 3D texturing tools for end users that incorporate the multi-disciplinary research and advanced GPUs technology in natural-texture modeling and synthesis, so more intelligent and creative texturing surfaces/bodies to be re-rendered from limited small samples. In this project, we will focus our study in innovative algorithms for interactive natural-texture modeling and synthesis on the latest GPUs, and carry out research in wavelet analysis/transform, optimized natural texturing, interactive sketching, realistic material modeling, and parallel synthesis computing. We will investigate optimal Gabor space in synthesis, based on the texture analysis by Fourier transform. Structured with the parallel synthesis, we will further work on intuitive controls including multiscale randomness, spatial modulation over examples and output, feature drag-and-drop, and periodicity constraints. We will investigate the efficient ways to better preserve/restore the sketch-guided global structure and texture appearance at the same time. To enhance the capability of solid texturing function, we introduce the novel approach for creating multi-solid textures and solid-texture graph, so complex materials could be represented with solid textures mixed seamlessly, also in hierarchical structures. We will investigate the vector-field optimizations and the interactive synthesis, and apply parallel 3D texturing to fully explore the strengths of GPGPU computation and highly efficient. We hope that advanced natural texturing techniques to be developed can offer long-term benefits of high quality, lower costs, and optimal efficiency for interactive texturing applications in Hong Kong. The proposed project will contribute significantly to the basic and applied research in the fields of realistic rendering, interactive synthesis, parallel computing, and augmented natural modeling. The advanced tools will facilitate the local industry to exploit many related 3D applications, thus further enhance the competitive edge of Hong Kong.

416311.label: Realisation of objectives
416311.value: Obj-1: We have proposed the novel method to construct the efficient wavelet transform based on loop subdivision. Using the basis function vectors, we introduced the control parameters to the new wavelet transform. We construct the lazy wavelet transform by reversing the subdivision for efficiency. To improve the fitting quality, it is the effective way to enhance the orthogonality of the lazy wavelet. Once the template is given, the lifting weights are pre-computed to accelerate the compression. The subdivision wavelet transform that we developed is stable, in-placed and efficient. The core challenge of colorization is to assign similar colors to texture-similar regions. We have investigated the novel approach for video colorization in rotation-invariant Gabor feature space, to preserve spatiotemporal coherence even for disjoint regions with similar textures. In this feature space, color similarity is established and Gabor flow is then used to compute the temporal connectivity of the pixel graphs. The optimization problem is approximated through per-pixel linear iteration in the feature space, thereby satisfying the user inputs. We further worked on computing the Gabor feature space for the 2D/3D exemplars, to determine the k-coherence candidate pixels in texture synthesis. Most of the supervoxel methods cannot perform well in regions with complex textures or weak boundaries. We have presented the supervoxel generation algorithm using partially absorbing random walks for more accurate results in these regions. Obj-2: We have worked on the challenge by incorporating the users’ intent in outlining the source patch, where the boundary drawn generally has different appearances from the interest. As the generated contents in the transition region may be different so causing artifacts to impair the composite, we have designed the cloning method to suppress such structure conflicts in the over-included region in the composite. Our processes are accelerated by grouping pixels in clusters and also using hierarchical sampling techniques. The interactive approach is intuitive for users and fast interpolation measure for parallel computing. We have proposed the global spatiotemporal optimization framework that shifts active objects in the spatiotemporal space. Using the multi-level patch relocation in Markov Random Field networks, the moving space of dynamic object is expanded into a compact background based on environmental content. Using the synthesized compact background and simple user interactions, our approach can produce more condensed video scenes with crowded but non-colliding objects. Previous warping method only considered feature correspondences and mesh regularization in the energy. We have worked on the new warping method that directly models on the triangle color similarities and tries to minimize the total color difference between the warped meshes. We have designed color and plane constraints in the unified optimization framework, to eliminate ghost artifacts in the visual effect. Obj-3: Directly applying 2D texture to natural material results in evident artifact because of the issue of synthesizing solid material or patterns usually very difficult. We have proposed the efficient and scalable approach to synthesize solid materials with discrete particles. Our method generates warping particles and stores them with a few points based on cellular texture. The particle distribution is directed by stereological techniques and spring system, which enable our solid synthesis with low memory footprint and resolution independence. Our method expands cellular texture to some more complicated and irregular scenes. Moreover, we present the two-scale shaping model to automatically and accurately reconstruct 3D particle outlines from 2D cross sections. Low frequency spherical harmonics are used to morph smooth outlines while high frequency ones model particle surface details. Particle volume color is represented by radial basis functions, and our cell-building algorithm constructs containers and computes scale for each particle instance, so to generate vector solid textures with plausible 3D particles. We have worked on vein-tissue texture synthesis for reproducing the realism of leaf surface textures with structure constraints. We generate a larger size blade texture and randomly select patches to fill the blanks on synthetic leaf blades divided by veins. Our technique can effectively capture the hierarchical structure of example leaf textures, and synthetic realism is highly correlated to these structures. Obj-4: We have developed the multiresolution rendering approach, which can perform the parallel GPU rendering based on sole-cube maps. The quadtree structure of the maps and normal-map atlas are constructed using the resampling, then by packing the quadtree nodes into the map texture atlas, we realized the parallel multiresolution rendering on the latest GPU in two rendering passes. Our rendering approach generates adaptive textured meshes dynamically, and is fully implemented on GPU. We have developed vector-represented results to avoid blurring, and GPU-based rendering for interactive synthesis of aggregate solid materials. Stereological technique and spring system are used to automatically guide the synthesis procedure. With designed GPU storage and accelerating structure, we can render solid objects with synthesized material textures in real-time on a common graphics card. We have proposed parallel optimization in rotation-aware Gabor feature space for producing high-quality colorized videos, to achieve real-time performance of color optimization. We introduced the Gabor feature space for capturing the texture appearance characteristics, leading to structure-preserving synthesis. We have designed the parallel texture synthesis over arbitrary surfaces, generating consistent and spatially-varying visual appearances. As the Gabor feature space is not only low dimensional but capturing multi-resolution texture structures, we directly apply multi-pass correction for each vertex according to its local neighborhood for order-independent purpose, leading to structure-preserving and efficient parallel synthesis.

416311.label: Major findings and research outcome
416311.value: The new surface texturing framework is proposed to directly synthesize texture on a polygonal surface, creating the geometry-coherent texture appearance without the need for extra parametrization. The Gabor feature space is introduced for capturing the texture appearance characteristics, leading to structure-preserving synthesis. The approach to construct the novel wavelet transforms based on Loop subdivision is designed, which can better control the shape of resulted surfaces and improve the fitting quality of the wavelet transforms. By adopting the local lifting scheme, the new wavelet transforms is efficient and uses less memory space (C3,C5,J2). The image cloning algorithm can effectively suppress the structure conflicts and remove the artifacts around the objects of interest in the interactive composite result. Our method can speed up the interpolator by treating pixels in clusters and using hierarchical sampling techniques, so that the user’s intent in outlining the source image patch is used efficiently (C6,J7,J9). The new scheme for video colorization developed for using optimization in rotation-aware Gabor feature space, to preserve spatiotemporal coherence even in disjoint texture-similar regions. The parallel scheme on graphics hardware is also facilitated to achieve real-time performance of color optimization. The novel approach for compact video synopsis provides the unified spatiotemporal optimization, which can preserve relative spatiotemporal relationships and avoid motion collisions. It expands the movement space of shifted objects into the compact background in an environmentally context-aware fashion (J3,J5,J6). Our approach for simple and effective solid synthesis can efficiently utilize the procedural texture and exemplar-based synthesis seamlessly in one system. We develop vector-represented results to avoid blurring, and GPU-based rendering for real-time synthesis on a common graphics card. Furthermore, two-scale shaping model is introduced to automatically and accurately reconstruct 3D particle outlines from 2D cross sections. Our approach can directly synthesize vector solid textures comprising 3D particles from 2D examples efficiently. Textures on leaves demonstrate obvious hierarchical structures due to the existence of veins. Our work on vein-tissue texture synthesis can efficiently generate similar series of leaves from examples with realistic vein structures (C2,C4,J4,J1). The multiresolution rendering of sole-cube maps is processed in GPU parallelization, with the visual quality of complex models and highly efficient. Our texture synthesis approach produces the parallel iso/aniso-scaling surface texturing guided in the Gabor space. The surface synthesis pipeline is fully order-independent and can be naturally parallelized on GPU platform (C5,J8). C#: Conf. paper, J#: Journal paper.

416311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416311.value: Current methods are limited in generating vector solid texture for aggregate material. We will further work on synthesizing vector solid texture with general examples by designing the typical volume representation. Anisotropic solid textures which vary with underlying geometry would be another further research direction. We will extend the method proposed to synthesize more variety of complex solid textures. Our work on vein-tissue texture synthesis of natural leaves can be extended for the general structure patterns and learning from large database samples, also synthesis from a set of real examples from different growing stages. We will also study on more structure-aware methods for synthesizing compact backgrounds from videos. Gabor filters known as Gabor feature space unify the frequency and multiresolution spatial analysis of texture features. We have introduced the Gabor feature space in surface texturing and image/video colorizations. Our work using the Gabor space can be further directed to let users to control the texture orientation by specifying different kinds of vector fields on the surfaces. We will further investigate the use of more sophisticated monochrome texture descriptors in video sequences, and further improve the color propagation capabilities in such applications.

416311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
416311.value: Textures are ubiquitous and stochastic visual experiences, and can describe a variety of surface characteristics such as terrains, plants and skin. Solid textures provide texture information throughout the volume, so well suited for many materials modeling as they are intrinsically 3D such as marble/stone objects. In this project, we have developed the techniques that can effectively model realistic solid textures of aggregate material from 2D example, using vector representation to avoid blurring and frequency control of titled synthetic details. Our research on vein-tissue texture synthesis can efficiently generate hierarchical structure of example leaf textures intuitively. We have developed editing and optimized control tools that can eliminate the structure conflicts in interactive image cloning, compact video synopsis in spatial and temporal domains, motion synopsis to compress redundancy and synthesize seamlessly, and accurate video supervoxels to tackle weak boundary/complex texture. Gabor feature space is introduced to capture texel’s multiresolution characteristics, leading to structure-preserving synthesis. Our surface synthesis supports parallel iso/aniso texturing over arbitrary surfaces, guided in Gabor space for geometry-coherent texture appearance without parametrization. The video colorization using optimization in the Gabor space allows fast Gabor flow even in disjoint regions with similar textures, and highly parallelizable.

416511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416511.value: A spatial network database (SNDB) manages geometric objects that are positioned in a road network. For instance, the road network may include all the roads, streets, and freeways in the US, while an object can be a gas station, restaurant, hotel, etc. SNDB is nowadays an active research topic in the database community, due to its profound importance in many traditional and merging applications. For example, in-car navigating devices, which have become a popular accessory today, can in fact be regarded as a small SNDB with the basic functionalities. Other, more powerful, representative SNDB systems include Google/Bing/Yahoo Maps, MapQuest, and so on. In general, SNDB efficiently supports queries that extract information based on the network and/or geographic properties of the underlying objects. Some example queries are "Return the turn-by-turn driving directions from Harvard to CMU", "What is the nearest, in traveling time, gas station of my location?", and "Find the nearest gas station of every location on the fastest route from Harvard to CMU." This project aims to carry out systematic investigation in this exciting area. Topics expected to be covered include the whole line from query specification to development of efficient solutions. Our ultimate objective is to develop a SNDB prototype capable of processing efficiently a great variety of queries on massive road networks. 一個空間網絡數據庫（SNDB）管理的是那些定位在道路網絡中的幾何對象。例如，一個道路網絡可能包括美國所有的高速公路，街道，和支路等，而一個對象則可以是加油站，餐館，和酒店等。由於其在許多傳統和新興應用中的重要性，SNDB是時下數據庫領域一個活躍的研究課題。例如，已成為當今流行配件的汽車導航設備其實可以算是一個小型的擁有基本功能的SNDB。其他的，更強大的，SNDB系統包括谷歌/Bing/雅虎地圖，Mapquest，等等。一般來說，SNDB能有效地支持那些基于網絡和/或地理屬性的查詢。查詢示例包括“返回從哈佛大學到CMU大學的車行路線”，“離我行車時間最近的加油站在哪裏？”和“告訴從哈佛到CMU的路上每一個位置的最近的加油站。“本項目旨在對SNDB開展系統的研究。涉及的課題預計將涵蓋有效的查詢之定義，它們的解決方案，等等。我們最終的目標是建立一個SNDB原型去有效地支持種類繁多的在大型公路網絡上的查詢。

416511.label: Realisation of objectives
416511.value: This project's scientific findings have been published in 4 journal articles (1 in TODS, 1 in VLDBJ, and 2 in TKDE), and 8 conference papers (2 in SIGMOD, 2 in VLDB, 2 in PODS, 1 in SODA, and 1 in SoCG) -- please see Part C of this report for a detailed list. All these journals and conferences are top-tier venues in the database area and/or theoretical computer science. Next, we discuss how the objectives (as stated above in Section 5.1) have been achieved by referring to these papers: - Regarding Objective 1, we have advanced the community's understanding on a list of individual problems that were encountered during the development of this project, including: triangle enumeration (SIGMOD'13), skyline (SODA'13), uncertain clustering (TKDE'13), and range query indexability (PODS'12, VLDBJ'14). Our improvements over the previous state of the art are in at least one of the following forms: reduced time/space complexities in theory, accelerated softwares, and/or new hardness results. - Regarding Objective 2, the specific contexts of this project have provided the initial motivation for several new problems, including, e.g.: ray stabbing (SoCG'12), dynamic top-k range reporting (PODS'12), maximum range sum (TODS'14, VLDB'13), and minimal mapreduce algorithms (SIGMOD'13). For these problems, we have developed the first, non-trivial, solutions, which have laid down the foundation for subsequent studies. - Regarding Objective 3, the techniques proposed in all our papers listed in Part C -- with a single exception of the one published in TKDE'13 -- have attractive theoretical assurances. More specifically, our algorithms are guaranteed to perform well even on the hardest, most adversely designed, "hard" inputs, while our lower bound results hold up against all solutions that can be possibly designed by human beings. - Regarding Objective 4, all our SIGMOD, VLDB, VLDBJ, TKDE, and TODS papers feature extensive experimental results obtained from our system prototypes. These results confirm the efficiency and feasibility of our techniques in practice.

416511.label: Major findings and research outcome
416511.value: We will discuss the outcome in two categories: scientific and practical. The scientific findings, as mentioned earlier, have been documented in 4 journal articles (1 in TODS, 1 in VLDBJ, and 2 in TKDE), and 8 conference papers (2 in SIGMOD, 2 in VLDB, 2 in PODS, 1 in SODA, and 1 in SoCG), all in top-tier venues of the database area and/or theoretical computer science. We have developed a systematic set of theory on the topic of data retrieval from massive networks. The theory mainly involves two types of techniques: graph-theoretic and geometric -- echoing two main keywords in this project's title: spatial networks. Perhaps the best way to illustrate this within the tight space constraint is to show a representative example for each type, as we do next. [Graph] Our SIGMOD'13 paper, which won the best paper award, studies I/O-efficient algorithms for settling the classic triangle listing problem, whose solution is a basic operator in dealing with many other graph problems. Before our work, the state-of-the-art solutions relied on a set of crippling assumptions to guarantee good performance. We remedied the problem with a new algorithm that is provably I/O and CPU efficient at the same time, without making any assumption on the input at all. [Geometric] Our PODS'12 paper studied the top-k range reporting problem. The input set S consists of n points in the real domain, each of which is associated with a distinct real-valued score. Given an interval q = [x1, x2] and an integer k in [1, n], a query returns the k points in q having the largest scores. We presented a structure in external memory that uses linear space, answers a query in O(lg_B n+k/B) I/Os, and supports an update in O(lg_B n) amortized I/Os, where B is the disk block size. This structure played a crucial role in implementing the ranking mechanism of our system. Our practical findings involve system prototypes that can be deployed to answer a large variety of queries on spatial networks. Our source code has been tested by extensive experiments that were designed to scrutinize our algorithms' behavior in numerous tough situations. The empirical results, which confirmed the efficiency and reliability of our implementation, were very well received by the community.

416511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416511.value: Data retrieval in spatial networks is a fascinating topic. During the 3 years of this project, the area has been through very rapid development, as is evident from the large number of high quality papers in prestigious venues. The joint efforts of the community have led to the a great number of working systems that are capable of processing a huge variety of queries that are likely to arise in reality. Many of these systems are fairly efficient and robust. On the other hand, the community's understanding about the theoretical characteristics of many problems still remains rather limited. This, partially, is due to the wide recognition that I/O-efficient algorithms with solid guarantees are much more challenging to design, compared to their main-memory counterparts. Indeed, currently the most efficient I/O-efficient graph algorithms even for fundamental problems such as Breadth First Search, Depth First Search, and Single Source Shortest Path are still rather expensive. There has been wide speculation that those algorithms have actually achieved the optimal performance; namely, it is just that matching lower bounds are yet to be established. Breakthroughs in this regard will be hailed as extremely important discoveries in the field.

416511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
416511.value: Spatial networks are just around us -- think about the streets, highways, and even the hiking trails up in the mountains. All these paths, big and small combined, together form a massive "web", rendering it time consuming to do simple but popular queries such as "find the shortest path from location A to location B", even with the state-of-the-art technology. The problem becomes significantly more challenging when these networks are dotted with a huge amount of additional information such as gas stations, shops, schools, residential areas, etc that must be stored separately in a conventional database, and hence, retrieved at higher cost. How to integrate all such information to permit extremely fast, real-time, answering of advanced queries -- ones that not only retrieve path information but also allows filtering with sophisticated predicates on the auxiliary data -- is an exceedingly intricate and challenging topic. This project tackles exactly this challenge with a suite of novel techniques that overcome a list of difficult theoretical problems in computer science. Our solutions have led to a full-blown system that support a great variety of efficient and effective data retrieval on massive networks.

416811.label: Project Objectives
416811.value: Mathematical modeling of the physical properties of the memristor: To investigate memristor-based recurrent neural networks, first we have to understand and quantify the features of the memristor thoroughly. The first objective of the proposed research is to model the nonlinear and nonunique properties of the memristor mathematically. Quantitative characterization of stability conditions of memristive neurodynamic systems: As stability is usually a prerequisite of most successful applications, the second objective of the proposed research is to analyze biological plausible dynamics to determine their stability conditions. Various algebraic criteria will be derived for the global stability, asymptotic stability, uniform stability, exponential stability, complete stability, and robust stability of memristive neurodynamic systems. Quantitative characterization of oscillation in memristive neurodynamic systems: Oscillatory dynamics is a common phenomenon in both biological and artificial neural networks. The third objective of the proposed research is to investigate the periodicity of self-sustained oscillatory dynamics in memristive neurodynamic systems in the presence of the pinched hysteresis. Systematic development of design methodology for memristor-based recurrent neural networks: The theoretical results from the above analyses will be used as the basis for the design of memristor-based recurrent neural networks. The fifth objective of the proposed research is to determine a set of design principles, guidelines, and procedures to enable the designed memristor-based recurrent neural networks to have desired dynamic properties such as global stability for successful applications.

416811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416811.value: Neurodynamics underlies many aspects of neural computation which is a preeminent paradigm in numerous areas of science and technology today. A deeper understanding of neurodynamics will lead to a better construction of neural networks for either brain modeling or information processing. Besides neurobiological experiments and theoretical analyses, electronic emulation of neurodynamics can facilitate understanding and creating the brain, following the footsteps of the pioneering Nobel-Prize work of Hodgkin and Huxley. However, due to the large scale and complex nature of neurodynamics, whole brain emulation is still far from ready. In the 2009 May issue of Nature, a research team at the Hewlett-Packard Laboratory presented a prototype design and fabrication of a new type of circuit element called “memristor” (a contraction of memory and resistor) that was conceived and analyzed by Leon Chua 39 years ago. In addition to numerous potential applications, Chua and the Hewlett-Packard researchers indicated that the memristor might play a significant role in novel analog circuits for emulating the functions of the brain in real time. While the invention of the memristor will definitely facilitate the electronic emulation of the brain, it also brought in tremendous challenges in analysis and design, as the memristor exhibits complex characteristics of nonlinear and nonuniqueness. This proposed project will focus on the analysis and design of memristive neurodynamic systems with three cohesive parts. In the first part, the theoretic analysis of memristive neurodynamic systems will be conducted. The nonlinear and nonunique features of the memristor will be characterized mathematically and various dynamic behaviors of memristive neurodynamic systems will be analyzed using systems-theoretic methods. The results of neurodynamic analysis in will help us to decipher and regulate the temporal behaviors of memristive neurodynamics. The development and applications of memristor-based recurrent neural networks will benefit significantly from the in-depth understanding of the memristive neurodynamics. In the second part, based on the results from the first part, a “reverse-engineering” approach will be applied to develop a novel methodology for designing memristor-based recurrent neural networks exhibiting desired dynamical properties. In the third part, specific memristor-based recurrent neural networks will be designed as new paradigms, based on the results in the preceding parts, for several important information processing tasks such as dynamic optimization and pattern association. It is expected that the research outcomes of the proposed project will result in deep insights on memristive neurodynamics, new design methods and specific models for problem-solving with memristor-based recurrent neural networks. 以神经动力学为重要基础的神经计算已经被广泛应用于当今科学技术的诸多领域并取得巨大的成功。深入了解神经动力学有助于更好地构建用于大脑建模或信息处理的神经网络。根据诺贝尔奖得主霍奇金和赫胥黎 的开创性工作，除神经生物学实验和理论分析之外，基于神经动力学的电子模拟也是研究和够造大脑的有效方法。然而， 由于神经动力学的复杂性和庞大规模， 脑模拟的许多问题还远未解决。 2009年5月，惠普实验室的一个研究小组在自然杂志上宣布成功设计并制造出美国科学家蔡少棠三十八年前构想的一种新类型的电路元件 - 忆阻器。蔡少棠和惠普的研究员们均相信忆阻器或将在脑模拟领域发挥重要作用。虽然忆阻器的发明无疑将促进大脑电子模拟的发展，但由于其复杂的非线性及不唯一性等特点，在忆阻器的设计与分析等诸多方面仍然存在着巨大的挑战。 该研究项目将专注于分析和设计忆阻器神经动力系统。本项目可以分为三个阶段：第一阶段进行忆阻器神经动力系统的理论分析，侧重于研究系统非线性和非唯一性的数学表达及其多种动力学表现。神经动力学的分析结果将有助于我们破译和调节系统的行为特征。神经动力系统的深入研究将大大有利于开发并应用基于忆阻器的递归神经网络。在第一阶段研究成果的基础上，我们将在第二阶段应用“逆向工程”原理，开发新的设计方法从而构造具有某些特定功能和性质的的忆阻器递归神经网络。根据前两个阶段的研究成果，忆阻器递归神经网络将在第三阶段被应用于信息处理的多个方面，如动态优化和模式识别等。此研究项目预期将会有助于获得对忆阻器神经动力系统的深刻见解，并且提出忆阻递归神经网络的新型设计方法与模型。

416811.label: Major findings and research outcome
416811.value: In the project, several dynamical behaviors of memristor-based recurrent neural networks (termed memristive neurodynamics) are theoretically analyzed. Specifically, the research started with the mathematical modeling the key element: memristor, with a general model that captures the signature feature of memristor: pinched hysteresis in its voltage-current relation. Based on the memristor model, many sufficient conditions for dissipativity, attractivity, passivity, passification, stabilization, and synchronization of memristive neurodynamics are derived and characterized. Besides individual memristor-based on neural networks, global exponential and robust synchronization of multiple memristor-based on neural networks are also investigated with verifiable criteria. These conditions serves good criteria for designing memristor-based recurrent neural networks for practical applications. In addition, global stability, multiple stability, and periodicity of complex-valued and parameter-switching recurrent neural networks are also investigated with many derived criteria as byproducts of the research.

416811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416811.value: Many avenues are open for further investigations. For example, it is difficult to prove the existence of stable equilibria in memristive neurodynamics based on the memristor model with pinched hysteresis feature, due to the lack of available mathematical tools. As a result, stability property have not directly investigated in this project. The existing results on stability of “memristive neurodynamics” in the recent literature by others are based on highly simplified memristor models without pinched hysteresis feature. Therefore, a further investigation along the stream of the research is to investigate the global, or semi-multiple stability based on a memristor model with pinched hysteresis feature. In addition, specific design guidelines and procedures should be developed based on all available theoretical results for memristor-based neural networks in some given applications and software design tools could be developed to facilitate designs and verifications.

416811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
416811.value: As the fourth circuit element besides capacitor, resistor, and inductor, memristor was conceptualized in 1970’s and prototyped and popularized in recent years. It is envisioned that its interesting properties could play an important role in emulating the brain. In this project, several interesting dynamical behaviors of memristor-based recurrent neural networks are rigorously characterized with many verifiable criteria. These criteria are viable for designing memristor-based recurrent neural networks in practical applications. It is expected that research findings will provide a theoretical basis for memristor-based emulation of the brain.

417011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
417011.value: The aim of this project is to conduct research into developing and implementing a video surveillance system which is able to automatically adapt general pedestrian and vehicle detectors to a specific traffic scene on target and to significantly improve its robustness and accuracy without requiring manually labeling training examples from that scene. Hong Kong is a large city with a very high population density. Traffic management is one of the major issues to be considered for its sustainable development. The effective detecting and counting of pedestrians and vehicles moving along different paths in traffic scenes has important applications for the detection and prediction of traffic congestion, optimizing the timing of traffic signals, urban planning (e.g., designing roads and developing public transportation infrastructures) and safety control. With the fast increase in widely installed surveillance cameras, there are escalating demands on automatically detecting pedestrians and vehicles from video streams by computing algorithms. Existing computer vision works focused on developing generic object detectors applicable to different scenes without being changed. However, due to variations of backgrounds, view points, light conditions, resolutions and occlusions, the performance of such generic detectors may decrease significantly when being applied to a specific scene. Although it is possible to retrain the detectors through manually labeling training examples from the target scene, the labeling work is costly and time-consuming. These systems cannot easily switch between different scenes. We propose to develop scene-specific pedestrian and vehicle detectors which require little human intervention. In traffic scenes, the movements of pedestrians and vehicles are regularized by scene structures. Benefiting from the outcomes of our previous work, where the models of pedestrian and vehicle paths were automatically learned from a video sequence without detecting and tracking objects, the models of scene structures together with other important cues are used to adapt a general pedestrian/vehicle detector to a specific scene. The pedestrian detector and the vehicle detector will be bootstrapped in different ways in accordance to the proposed new frameworks. Integrating with web-based surveillance cameras, an online real-time pedestrian/vehicle detection system will be developed to monitor traffic scenes through Internet. It will seed other research topics on traffic management in the future. The outcome of this research will significantly improve the current intelligent video surveillance systems used in the applications of traffic management in terms of accuracy, robustness, scalability and transferability. It will have a long-term impact on the city’s sustainable development. 本項目將研究開髮用於車輛和行人檢測的智能視頻監控系統。該系統可以將一個普適的行人與車輛檢測器自適應到一個特定的交通場景，以提高其魯棒性和準確性，而不要從該場景中手動標註任何訓練數據。 香港是人口密集的大城市。交通管理是可持續發展需要解決的重要問題。能夠在交通場景中有效的檢測行人和車輛並對其記數對於預測交通堵塞，優化交通信號燈的變化時間，城市規劃和安全控制等應用有著重要意義。隨著監控攝像頭數量的迅速增加，迫切需要研究可以從視頻流中自動檢測行人與車輛的計算方法。現有計算機視覺的研究工作主要集中在開發可以用於不同的場景的普適的物體檢測器。但是由於不同場景的背景、視角、光線、分辨率和遮擋情況變化很大，當這些普適的檢測器用於某一特定場景時，其性能會發生顯著下降。雖然可以通過從該場景中手動收集訓練樣本並對檢測器重新訓練以提高其性能，手動標註訓練樣本代價高且費時。這些系統不能再不同場景間方便地切換。 我們將要研究在無需人工干預的情況下建立針對特定場景的行人和車輛的檢測器。在交通場景中，行人和車輛的運動受到場景結構的限制。基於我們已有的研究成果，無須檢測和跟踪物體，行人和車輛的模型可以從視頻中自動無監督學習得到。利用這些場景結構的模型和其它的線索可以將一個普適的車輛和行人的監測器自適應到一個特定的場景。 該項目的研究成果可以在準確率、魯棒性、可擴展性等方面顯著提高現有智能視頻監控系統的性能。它將對香港未來的可持續發展產生重要影響。

417011.label: Realisation of objectives
417011.value: All the objectives in this project have been realized successfully. (1) The performance of a generic pedestrian detector drops significantly when it is applied to a specific scene due to the mismatch between the source training set and samples from the target scene. We propose a new approach of automatically transferring a generic pedestrian detector to a scene-specific detector without manually labeling samples from the target scene. Compared with a generic detector, it improves the detection rates by 48% and 36% at one false positive per image (FPPI) on MIT Traffic and CUHK datasets, respectively. In recent years, deep learning has achieved great success. We develop multiple deep models, i.e. joint deep learning, multi-stage deep learning, and DeepID-Net, to improve generic object detection. They are extended by automatically learning scene-specific features and visual patterns without any manual labels from the target scene. It jointly learns a scene-specific classifier and the distribution of the target samples. Both tasks share multi-scale feature representations with both discriminative and representative power. We also propose a cluster layer in the deep model that utilizes the scenespecific visual patterns for pedestrian detection. It significantly improves the detection rates at 1 FPPI by 10% compared with the state-of-the-art domain adaptation methods on MIT Traffic Dataset and CUHK Square Dataset. (2) We develop and implement a new framework to detect and count vehicles through tracking and clustering feature points and utilizing multiple cues related to scene structures. First, an algorithm is proposed to automatically learn the models of scene structures. A traffic scene is segmented into local semantic regions by exploiting the temporal co-occurrence of local motions. Local semantic regions are connected into global complete paths using the proposed fast marching algorithm. Sources and sinks are estimated from the models of semantic regions. Second, an algorithm is proposed to cluster trajectories of feature points into objects and to estimate average vehicle sizes at different locations from initial clustering results. Third, trajectories of features points are often fragmented due to occlusions. (3) We have built four large scale datasets, i.e. MIT traffic dataset, Grand Central Train Station Dataset, CUHK Dataset, and Shanghai World Expo Dataset, for experimental evaluation. These datasets include hundreds of videos from around 100 scenes. The pedestrians and vehicles are annotated on 8100 frames sampled from these videos. (4) All the detectors have been implemented with GPU and can run in realtime in the prototype system.

417011.label: Major findings and research outcome
417011.value: As research outcome, 8 journal papers and 24 conference papers are published. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (PAMI), and International Journal of Computer Vision (IJCV) are the two best journals on computer vision and machine learning. We published four papers at PAMI and IJCV. 24 papers were published on the top three conferences on computer vision (CVPR, ICCV, and ECCV). Four large scale datasets with annotations are built. A prototype realtime pedestrian and vehicle detection system is built. We found that the performance of pedestrian and vehicle detectors can be significantly improved by automatically adapting them to target scenes. The scene-specific pedestrian detectors can be learned by automatically selecting positive and negative training samples from target scenes according to scene structures, behaviors and spatio-temporal priors. Along this line, several papers have been published (Part C.8 No. 4-6, Part C.9 No. 1-2,5-7,13). We find that deep learning can significantly improve the performance of object detection. Multiple deep learning based detectors have been developed by us in the following papers (Part C.9 16-17, 21-22, 24). They can also be extended to scene-specific detectors under our proposed deep learning framework (paper in Part C.9 15). Besides detection, we are also able to recognize the identities of pedestrians by matching their appearance (refer to papers in Part C.9 No. 3-4, 23). Scene-specific vehicle detectors can be learned tracking and clustering trajectories of feature points on vehicles as studied in the paper (Part C.8 No.1). When automatically learning the scene-specific pedestrian and vehicle detectors, clustering trajectories and modeling the crowd behaviors and motion pattern play an important role, since they provide prior information to provide positive and negative training samples from the target scenes. We have done a lot of works in this direction (papers in Part C.8 No. 1, 3, 7-8 and Part C.9 No. 8-12, 14, 18-20). Experimental evaluation on a large number of scenes has shown that scene-specific pedestrian and vehicle detectors can improve the detection accuracy substantially compared with generic detectors. The proposal methods have good generalization capability and robustness. It also shows that scene structures, motion patterns and behavior priors are effective in improve detection.

417011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
417011.value: Because of the emergence of deep learning technology, the generic object detectors have been improved a lot. The idea of learning scene-specific detectors can potentially be applied to all the new detectors. Moreover, since the lighting, background and crowdness of a scene change over time, we could also update the detectors dynamically over time. Therefore, scene-specific and dynamically updated detectors will be developed in the future work. The developed detectors will be incorporated into surveillance systems by collaborating with industry. We plan to apply for an ITF project to transfer research to products. Pedestrian and vehicle detection is the basic element for traffic scene modeling and analysis. On the top of it, there are other tasks to be further developed, such as pedestrian/vehicle attribute recognition, identity recognition, object tracking, abnormal event detection, and behavior analysis. All the tasks face similar problems encountered in detection, i.e. generic classifiers and models do not perform well in a specific scene because of the variation of viewpoints, camera settings, lightings and background. The ideas and methodologies developed in this project could also be generalized to these tasks.

417011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
417011.value: Traffic management is one of the major issues to be considered for its sustainable development of large cities like Hong Kong. The effective detecting and counting of pedestrians and vehicles moving along different paths in traffic scenes has important applications for the detection and prediction of traffic congestion, optimizing the timing of traffic signals, urban planning. However, due to variations of backgrounds, viewpoints, light conditions, resolutions and occlusions, the performance of generic pedestrian and vehicle detectors drop significantly when they are applied to specific traffic scenes. On the other hand, it is costly to manually label training samples for each camera view in order to training a scene-specific pedestrian or vehicle detector. In this project, we have developed new methodologies and algorithms which can re-train a generic detector by automatically collecting training samples from a target by making use of multiple cues of scene structures, motion patterns and behavior priors. Without increasing the human labeling effort, it improves the detect accuracy dramatically. It has large impact on management of traffic scenes.

To develop a set of algorithms and tools that facilitates fast image and video retargeting.

417411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
417411.value: Abstract With the wide popularity of portable display devices, images and videos are often visualized through small displays of various resolutions and aspect ratios. On the other hand, images and videos are typically captured for large display. Naive image resizing of the whole image results in over-squeezing of prominent image content and loss of details. Several image retargeting methods have been proposed to selectively reduce less salient image region while preserving the salient image region. However, the definition of saliency is usually vague and based on the low-level image features that may not be related to the semantics. Although high-level semantics analysis (such as automatic recognition of arbitrary objects) is infeasible in the near future, analysis of certain middle-level semantics, such as symmetry and foreshortening, is feasible. In this project, we propose a semantics-aware retargeting framework. Based on the detected semantics, the image can then be retargeted in a more sensible way that preserves the detected semantics. In particular, we first analyze one type of middle-level semantics, translational symmetry. By understanding the symmetry in an image, we may retarget the image by deleting or replicating the repeated “cells” in the symmetry, instead of deleting or replicating the semantics-less pixels as in existing approaches. In other words, such retargeting can be regarded as summarization. Knowing the semantics not only allows us to resize images and videos more intelligently, but also opens up a new space for retargeting. This new space of cell-by-cell processing provides much flexibility to avoid over-squeezing, over-stretching, and undesirable bending of prominent symmetric structure. The major challenge of this project is the ability to efficiently and rapidly identify meaningful “cells” as our goal is for interactive applications. Identifying feature points is not effective for identifying meaningful cells, as a cell may contain a collection feature points. In contrast, we need to identify suitable region-based features (blobs) efficiently and effectively. In addition, we shall extend the framework to video retargeting. Video retargeting is even more challenging due to the temporal coherence constraint. This restricts the way we retarget the frames. Over-aggressive deletion or replication of cells may easily introduce temporal discontinuities in the resultant video. By solving these challenges, we believe the outcome (the knowledge, publications, and algorithms) from the proposed project should motivate further study along the direction of semantics-aware retargeting by the community. Besides the developed algorithm should be directly applicable in mobile computing and movie production.

417411.label: Realisation of objectives
417411.value: The goal of our image and video retargeting is to reduce the image resolution while retaining the prominent visual content. This really depends on how humans understand the visual content and recognize what is “prominent.” This is also why, in this project, we propose to analyze the semantics of the visual content. To do so, we first adopt the findings from psychologists on gesalt phenomena, the human visual behavior on recognizing “forms.” For instance, it explains how humans recognize a dashed line as a line, instead of a set of unrelated line segments. Gestalt phenomena are the most crucial theory for identifying “cells” in a regular grid, as mentioned in our proposal. However, most of the existing psychological literatures are qualitative. They cannot be directly applied for computational usage. So in this project, our major research contribution is to design, develop, and evaluate multiple quantitative computational models. Note that there are multiple gestalt laws found so far, but existing literatures mainly study and explain them individually. It is not well studied on how multiple gestalt laws interact with each other during the process of human visual recognition. We achieve the semantic analysis of the visual content by first modeling individual gestalt laws. Then we design a framework in which multiple gestalt laws can plug into it, so that they can interact with each other. We apply this semantic analysis framework to vector graphics. The experiment is quite successful. For instance, our system is able to understand the regularly distributed squares as part of the grid, instead of a set of unrelated squares. On the other hand, randomly distributed squares are not interpreted as a grid. With this computed semantics, we are able to summarize the regularly placed windows by reducing the window count. So that, the original meaning of the grid can be retained. This allows us to synthesize a much effective retargeting result. We publish the findings in two ACM SIGGRAPH publications ([J01] and [J04]). In one publication, we demonstrate how the complex interaction of multiple gestalts can obtain sensible semantics that can be directly used for abstraction (simplification) of architectural drawing. So the complicated drawing can be retargeted and visualized on a much smaller display. In another publication, we further demonstrate that how two gestalt laws, law of closure and law of continuity, can be used to effectively deduce the semantic regions and semantic strokes from arbitrary rough sketches. Note that, analyzing rough sketches is very challenging. A semantically meaningful region may not necessarily be closed and a semantically meaningless region can be closed and accidently formed. Without a sensible semantics analysis, it is hard to tell whether the region is intentionally drawn by users. With our computed semantics, we can immediately remove those regions that are not intentional and simplify the overcrowded strokes, so as to facilitate the retargeting purpose. This semantic region analysis basically accomplishes our first objective. Our findings are recognized by scholars and experts in our field, as our two papers are presented in the most prestigious graphics conference in our field, ACM SIGGRAPH, and published in leading journal, ACM Transactions on Graphics. While gestalt laws can be used to identify the middle-level semantics in the visual content so as to facilitate the retargeting, it is still possible such simplification is not sufficient when the image is too crowded and/or the retargeting image resolution is too small. The only way to further squeeze the visual content to fit in a small screen in such case is to drop less prominent object(s) in the image. So in the latter stage of the project, we move forward to study the visual attention. We attempt to model the visual attention of human visual perception. So that we can identify less prominent objects, such that even removing/deforming them for the retargeting purpose, the users are not aware of such change. This is why in [J05] we propose a computational model to simulate the change blindness behavior of humans. We successfully demonstrated its effectiveness in synthesizing change blindness images. We are able to control the degree of change blindness with the proposed model. With the model, we are able to further remove less prominent visual content so as to achieve a more effective retargeting. With the analyzed semantics, we proposed multiple methods to synthesize retargeted images and videos. For image content that can be summarized, we develop a patchmatch based image retargeting algorithm to synthesize images of target resolution. We also developed a method to first rectify the image façade, before applying patchmatch based summarization to achieve results with much better visual quality. All these accomplish our second objective. In both gestalt law and visual attention studies, we conduct user study at the final stages. Through the user study, we are not just able to evaluate the quality of the computed semantics. But the collected data from users is also used to fine tune the parameters of both models. For instance, the user data can be used to tune the multi-gestalt law framework, so that we have a better idea on which gestalt law may dominate in the complex interaction. The user data can also be used to tell, in what condition, content removal or deformation is more favorable in applying the visual attention model. This accomplishes our third objective.

417411.label: Major findings and research outcome
417411.value: To facilitate the reference to publication, each paper listed in Part 8 is labeled with a unique ID, e.g.[J01]or[C01], in their title field. 1. In order to analyze the semantics, we studied the findings in gestalt psychology. Psychologists have theories (some are conflicting) on how humans recognize forms (gestalts) instead of uncorrelated fragments. But these theories are mostly qualitative. We proposed the first computational framework to allow multiple gestalt laws interact with each other in a complex manner [J01][J04]. 2. As the first attempt, we applied the semantic analysis on vector graphics. We model the gestalt laws of proximity, regularity, and similarity quantitatively, and study their complex interaction in a newly proposed framework. We successfully applied this multi-gestalt law framework to analyze the semantics of architectural drawing and able to summarize and abstract the drawing to obtain a simplified version for retargeting purpose. The work is published in the prestigious conference ACM SIGGRAPH Asia 2011 and top journal ACM Transactions on Graphics [J01]. 3. We continue the semantic analysis study on more challenging rough sketches. Here in the sketch, semantic regions and semantic strokes cannot be easily identified due to the sketchiness. We model the gestalt laws of closure and line continuity, and more importantly, their interaction. We can successfully simplify the rough sketch while retaining the prominent fine details, for the retargeting purpose. The work is recently presented in ACM SIGGRAPH Asia 2015 and published in top journal ACM Transactions on Graphics [J04]. 4. For real images, we need to overcome the overwhelming details such as textures. We developed a method [J03] to retain prominent detail and smooth out the unwanted details for raster images. 5. Due to the visual richness of real photograph, gestalt analysis alone may not be sufficient in reducing the overwhelming visual content. So we further propose to remove or deform the visual content based on the visual attention phenomena. We propose a change blindness model to effectively measure and control the degree of blindness to the change of visual content. With this model, we can modify/deform/remove the visual content to facilitate the retargeting, without being aware by the users. This work is published in IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics [J05]. 6. We have attempted to extend the retargeting to stereo images. In such case, the consistency or fusibility in terms of color, contrast, and texture, between the left and right views is a major concern. We proposed a novel fusibility metric [J02].

417411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
417411.value: Further development: In this project, we attempted to analyze the semantics of visual content, via gestalt analysis. We found that gestalt laws are especially useful in grouping elements in images to identify grid and symmetry. By summarizing the repeated elements, we can achieve the retargeting without loosing the visually prominent content. However, the gestalt analysis alone may not be sufficient when the visual content is overcrowded. We believe that visual attention model is a promising direction to further rank the prominence of objects in the images. Human is less sensitive to modification to less attended content. Course of action: We believe more study should be done along the direction of visual perception modeling, especially on visual attention models. Although in this project we have preliminarily studied the feasibility of applying change blindness model for the purpose of image retargeting, there are actually much more visual attention behaviors not addressed. By developing more sophisticated quantitative models for visual attention, we should be able to achieve more effective retargeting. In the future, we shall also actively seek for additional funding support from other external source such as Hong Kong Innovation and Technology Fund to transfer our developed technologies to industry.

417411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
417411.value: With the wide popularity of portable devices and the wide variety of display resolutions, intelligently adapting the visual content to various display screens become more and more important. By saying intelligent, we mean an image retargeting methodology that adjusts the image resolution without losing the original semantics of the images. To achieve this, our project analyzes the visual semantics by quantifying the psychological findings of gestalt phenomena. Through our computational model, the computer system is able to identify what is “prominent” content and preserve it during the image retargeting. The immediate impact of our work is that user can enjoy the same visual content on various portable devices, without the viewing difficulty of losing prominent content, and without being aware of the change of image resolution. We believe the work can benefit the local mobile app industry by improving their technological competitiveness.

418111.label: Project Title(Chinese)
418111.value: 針對電路關鍵路徑時序故障進行原位糾錯的設計與優化研究

418111.label: Project Objectives
418111.value: To investigate novel in-situ timing error correction circuit designs that are both applicable to general logic circuits and scalable to large IC designs. To develop novel CAD tools to support cost-efficient timing error detection and correction on speed-paths. To investigate novel cross-layer timing error resilience solutions.

To develop novel CAD tools to support cost-efficient timing error detection and correction on speed-paths.
To investigate novel cross-layer timing error resilience solutions.

418111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
418111.value: With technology scaling, integrated circuits (ICs) suffer from increasing process, voltage, and temparature (PVT) variations and aging effects. In most cases, these reliability threats manifest themselves as timing errors on speed-paths (i.e., critical or near-critical paths) of the circuit. Traditional design methodology requires designers to embed considerable design guardband to prevent any timing failure, diminishing the benefit of technology scaling. Consequently, there is a growing research interest in online timing error detection and correction (TEDC) for variation-tolerant designs. Most of existing TEDC solutions try to restore the state of the system to a known-good pre-error state. These techniques are very effective for timing error correction in processors with microarchitectural support such as instruction replay, but they are very difficult, if not impossible, to be applied to general logic circuits, due to the high cost to checkpoint error-free states in such designs. In-situ timing error correction techniques that are able to mask errors without any rollback, are therefore very attractive. The few in-situ TEDC techniques presented in the literature, however, either rely on certain assumptions about the circuit structure and hence limit their applicability, or suffer from scalability issues and can be only applied to small logic blocks. Moreover, the design overhead to achieve online timing error detection and correction may be quite large, but there is nearly no computer-aided design (CAD) support to facilitate this task today. Motivated by the above, we plan to investigate novel circuit design and optimization techniques for cost-efficient timing error detection and correction in this project. Specific tasks include: (i) novel in-stiu timing error correction circuit designs that are applicable to general logic circuits and scalable to large IC designs; (ii) CAD solutions for cost-efficient timing error detection and correction. As worst-case design methodology that prevents timing errors caused by PVT variations to occur severely limits the performance and energy efficiency of today's IC designs, the success of this project is of great value to the semiconductor industry. 隨著半導體工藝尺寸的持續縮小，集成電路的延時特性日益受到制程變異、溫度和電壓變化以及電路老化的影響，經常表現為關鍵路徑上的時序故障。為解決該問題，當前集成電路設計中不得不加入很大的余量來容忍這類錯誤，對電路性能有很大的影響。針對上述問題，在本項目中，我們準備設計一種能夠對關鍵路徑時序故障進行原位糾錯的電路，並進行優化。具體研究的問題包括：（1）能夠廣泛使用于各種電路的設計；（2）相應的電子設計自動化解決方案能夠自動插入我們的設計電路並盡可能的減小其開銷。我們預期達到的目標是通過我們的設計使得集成電路的性能以及能效得到大幅提高。

418111.label: Realisation of objectives
418111.value: The objectives of this project is to investigate novel in-situ timing error correction methodologies and computer-aided design solutions. We have successfully realized the above objectives. 1. We proposed a novel in-situ timing error masking circuit wherein we add small approximate circuit to mask timing errors on circuit speed-paths. 2. We proposed another novel in-situ timing error masking circuit, by adding circuit to correct timing errors on circuit speed-path with error effect prediction capabilities. 3. We proposed novel logic synthesis techniques for cost-efficient timing error detection and correction. Given a circuit, our CAD tool is able to transfer it to be another circuit with more timing margin in an automated fashion. 4. We proposed an optimization algorithm for timing-speculative circuits with the help of the so-called redundancy-and-removal technique.

418111.label: Major findings and research outcome
418111.value: In our ICCAD'12 paper, we propose to conduct logic synthesis for timing-speculated circuits from the ground up. Being able to manipulate circuit structures during logic optimization, the proposed solution is able to dramatically reduce circuit timing error rates and hence improve its throughput, as demonstrated with experimental results on various benchmark circuits. In our ETS'13 paper, we propose to use redundancy addition and removal (RAR) technique to optimize timing-speculated circuits. By intentionally removing wires on those frequently-exercised critical paths and replacing them with wires on less critical ones (if possible), the proposed technique is able to greatly reduce the timing error rate of the circuit and improve its overall throughput, over our ICCAD'12 work. In our DAC'13 paper, we present a novel in- situ timing error masking technique, namely InTimeFix, by introducing fine-grained redundant approximation circuit into the design to provide more timing slack for speed-paths. The synthesis of the redundant circuit relies on simple structural analysis of the original cir- cuit, which is easily scalable to large IC designs. Experimental results show that InTimeFix significantly increases circuit timing slack with low area/power cost. In our ICCAD'13 paper, we present a new forward timing error correction scheme, namely ForTER, which predicts whether the occurrence of timing errors would propagate to the next level of sequential elements and corrects them without necessarily borrowing timing slack. The proposed technique can be combined with other timing error resilient circuit design techniques (e.g., InTimeFix) to further improve circuit performance, as demonstrated in our experimental results with various benchmark circuits.

418111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
418111.value: We have an on-going follow-up project that focuses on optimization techniques for timing speculated circuits with possible timing errors.

418111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
418111.value: With semiconductor technology scaling, it is increasingly expensive to ensure "always correct" operations for integrated circuits. Since systems usually operate at nominal conditions where worst-case scenarios rarely occur, this project investigates novel circuit design and optimization techniques to enable more energy-efficient computing, by judiciously adding low-cost error detection and correction scheme into the system.

418311.label: Project Objectives
418311.value: Characterize allocation and sharing rules for supply chain contracts with rigorous mathematical models; define the channel profit allocation with degrees of flexibility, and further identify contributions to the supply chain coordination literature with respect to degrees of flexibility. Characterize the robustness of coordination contracts with precise models by evaluating the coordination sensitivity to the structure of contract terms/competitive game settings. 418311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
418311.value: Contracts are one of the most fundamental business instruments that suppliers and retailers have to deal with. The existence of double marginalization in the vertical supply chains and inventory competition in the horizontal supply chains has inspired considerable interests in designing and analyzing coordination contracts that optimize the performance of the associated supply chains. However, most existing studies focus on the design of coordination contracts, whereas investigations on their robustness are rare. It has been advocated that these robust properties have a great impact on adopting and implementing coordination contracts. For example, one of the most noticeable and publicized contracts is the buyback contract, which is robust in the sense of being flexible in dividing channel profit and being in the voluntary compliance regime. Therefore, in this project, we plan to set out research questions of the robustness of coordination contracts, namely 1) the robustness of the profit allocation with respect to the expected value and sample path, 2) the robustness of the competitive structure to coordination contracts, and 3) the robustness of contracting agents to the compliance regimes. We intend to identify structure properties and sufficient conditions for these robust properties. Our final aim is to develop the taxonomy of coordination contracts in terms of their robustness. 供應合約是一種廣泛應用於供應鏈管理的工具。由於供應鏈的合作者有不同的目標和贏利方式，造成了供應鏈效率的下降。供應鏈協調一直是供應鏈管理中的核心問題。供應鏈管理的研究主要成果就是有關於供應合約的設計和分析，尤其是發現了一批所謂的協調合約，這些協調合約可以改善供應鏈的效率，但是如何評價這些供應鏈合約的魯棒性卻是一個沒有研究的問題。供應鏈合約的魯棒性可以包含下述內容：1）供應鏈合約是如何劃分供應鏈收入的，這種劃分是否輿合約執行的數目有關？ 2）這些合約是否輿決策過程，特別是決策順序有關？ 3）這些合約的執行是否存在欺騙性或依賴強迫性的條款等。我們準備就這三類魯棒性的問題進行深入研究，力圖確定供應鏈管理文獻中所記載的協調合約的性質，以及確保合約具有魯棒性的條件。

418311.label: Major findings and research outcome
418311.value: We start with an investigation of a number of supply chain contracts on the performances of these contracts in terms of the channel profit allocation and the degree of flexibility. We make use of the group decision-making theory developed by Raiffa (1970) and LaValle (1978). We first differentiate the notion of allocation rule and sharing rule. We then develop the notion flexible contract: coordination, flexible coordination in expectation, and flexible coordination in sample-path. We included the detailed definition, analysis, examples and extensions in Section 2 of a manuscript (Lu, Sethi and Yan, 2012), which was subsequently submitted to Management Science for a possible publication. With the above result, we explore the nature of coordination and its robustness in competitive game settings. We focus on three possible game settings: one static and two dynamic games. We are particularly interested in a special desirable situation known as a robust contract, which has an identical equilibrium with different decision-making sequences. We continue with our query to the nature of the compliance of a contract. We consider that voluntary compliance is robust since the incentives of agents are complete aligned. We then develop a second notion of robustness, that is a contract is compliance consistent, deviating from the system optimal only makes both agents worse off. The result and associated definition, analysis, examples and extensions were included in the manuscript of Lu, Sethi and Yan, (2012). The above progress addresses objective 1, 2 and 3 in the proposal. The manuscript (Lu, Sethi and Yan, 2012) was sent to Management Science. We received a detailed report. The review team “agreed that a further classification of supply chain coordination contracts by their robustness properties is important and relevant to supply chain contracting research.” However, the review team wanted us to further explore the design guideline for contract robustness rather than sufficient conditions for robustness and consistency. To address the design matter, we notice that there is a strong correlation between the robustness of a contract and its transaction times. The contracts with transactions occurring both before and after the realization of the random factors exhibit desirable properties. We would like to report that all objectives that we proposed to study are all addressed. The revised manuscript has been sent to Management Science. Sufficient conditions for sequence independency and compliance consistency will be organized for a possible publication at a more technical journal in near future.

418311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
418311.value: In this project, we have limited our analysis to two-agent supply chains. However, concepts developed here could be extended to supply chains with N agents. This is being studied by the student co-author of this paper as a part of his dissertation. Moreover, we have focused on contracts with inventory and capacity decisions given the retail price, the cost parameters, and the demand distribution. The retail price decision is important in supply chains. Also, the consistency of some of the coordinating contracts analyzed in this project rests on specific demand distributions. It would be of interest to generalize our analysis to allow for price decisions and distributions other than the ones used in this paper.

418311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
418311.value: The presence of the vast supply chain coordination literature motivates us to study the robustness of the coordinating contracts. We focus on three aspects: consistency in the channel profit distribution, consistency with respect to the decision making sequences, and consistency with respect to the compliance regimes. We define two notions of flexibility: expectation flexibility and sample-path flexibility. We distinguish between an allocation function and a sharing function. We further introduce the notion of the consistency of coordinating contracts in the decision-making sequence. Our third and last concept is that of the compliance consistency of a contract, which ensures that it is in the interest of each agent to fulfill the contract. For this project, we have come up with a taxonomy of coordinating contracts, and characterized a number of well-known coordinating contracts in a 3~3 matrix. We have classified contract mechanisms based on the transaction time and the time of the uncertainty resolution. We have learned that the contracts that execute transactions before and after the uncertainty resolution exhibit stronger consistency properties.
