418511.value: 這個研究計劃的主要目標是建立一些機器學習方法，利用嶄新的數據，來從人類基因圖譜中找出尚未發現的作用元素，及它們間的互動。自從二零零三年第一個人類基因圖譜完成以後，人類基因圖譜計劃（Human Genome Project）正努力嘗試明白這組長三十億個單位的脫氧核糖核酸（DNA）在細胞中是如何運作。當中一個清晰的目標是找出這組脫氧核糖核酸中的作用元素以及它們的相互影響。雖然這類研究於人類基因圖譜計劃開始前早已進行，但要有系統地研究所有作用元素一直受制於大型數據的缺乏而不可能進行。這障礙近年被數項科技上的突破所衝破，當中包括晶片實驗（microarray）及第二代排序方法（second-generation sequencing）。此後，國際組織脫氧核糖核酸元素百科（Encyclopedia of DNA Elements, ENCODE）正式成立。這個組織成員來自各大洲的研究團隊，目的是利用這些新式實驗方法來製造大量數據並進行有系統的分析。這些數據大部分於過去數月才剛剛產生。作為ENCODE的成員，我們這個研究計劃的主持人（principal investigator）和共同主持人（co-investigator）會和其他ENCODE的成員合作找出所有出現在人類基因圖譜中一種稱為增強子（enhancer）的作用元素，即基因圖譜中能夠增加基因活躍度的區域。我們還會組成一個研究團隊去（一）研究這些增強子如何透過長距離互動方式去影響其他作用元素，及（二）根據這些相互動作預測基因在不同細胞線的活躍度。嶄新的大型數據對這兩個項目來說都不可或缺。這些分析工作除了能增進我們對一些生物現象於分子層面的認識，也有助我們理解這些現象如何導致疾病等可以觀察的結果。憑著我們過往建立機器學習方法作全基因圖譜生物網絡研究的經驗，我們會設計一些計算方法來有效率地找出前所未知而有生物學意義的作用元素和相互作用。我們設計的計算方法會充分利用已知的生物學知識及從數據中發現的規則。我們所作的預測部分會送交ENCODE和其他合作伙伴作進一步的實驗驗證，以評估我們的方法是否有效及所作的預測最否有意義。在我們早前的試驗階段，大部分我們所作的預測都已被實驗證實。由於新型數據已經產生而我們又具備相關經驗，我們認為這項研究計劃既合時又可行。

418511.value: Objective 1: We have developed the methods for predicting enhancers and identifying DNA long-range interactions, and applied the methods to human cell types. The accuracy of enhancer prediction has been confirmed by experimental reporter assays. The method for DNA long-range interactions has been compared with several other methods, and was shown to identify cluster of genomic locations closer to each other based on simulated data, and the clusters identified were found to be correlated with various molecular activities. Objective 2: We have packaged the methods into computer software that other researchers can use. Our enhancer prediction software is available on the supplementary web site of our corresponding publication. Our software for analyzing DNA long-range interaction will be available when the corresponding manuscript is officially accepted. Objective 3: We have used our method to predict potential enhancers in multiple human cell/tissue types for the ENCODE consortium. A random sample of our predictions were experimentally validated by ENCODE. Objective 4: We have tested the idea of using DNA long-range interactions to improve statistical models of gene expression regulation. The results show that epigenomic features at enhancers can predict the expression of genes linked by long-range interactions according to ChIA-PET data with reasonable accuracy.

418511.label: Major findings and research outcome
418511.value: This project has led to the development of new methods for predicting transcriptional enhancers and identifying DNA long-range interactions from noisy Hi-C, TCC and ChIA-PET data. When applying our methods to human cell types, our enhancer predictions were found to be reasonably accurate (with about 67% validation rate), and the clusters of genomic regions predicted to have physical contacts were found to be highly correlated with various molecular activities, including DNase I hypersensitivity, gene expression, super enhancer activities and replication timing in a cell type specific manner. The project has also helped established a collaboration with the ENCODE consortium by contributing to the analysis of their large-scale sequencing data set on the transcriptomes, epigenomes and other chromatin features of many human cell types. The project has led to two publications in the journal Genome Biology (2014 ISI impact factor: 10.810). A third manuscript has been submitted and undergone one round of review, and is currently under revision.

418511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
418511.value: Based on the experience in this project and the methods developed, additional aspects of transcriptional enhancers can be studied. For example, how multiple enhancers cooperate to regulate the same target gene and the relative amount of expression variability that can be explained by enhancers as compared to other regulatory components can be studied. With the recent publication of new data sets by the ENCODE, FANTOM5 and Roadmap Epigneomics consortia, it is also possible to extend the study of enhancers to hundreds of human cell and tissue types, and to use the results to study the roles of disabled enhancers in diseases. Based on these ideas, I have written and submitted a new GRF proposal for carrying out this extended research project.

418511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
418511.value: Genes are basic units in our DNA that code for RNAs and proteins. Careful control of gene activities is crucial for proper functioning of our cells. One control mechanism is by having some proteins binding to DNA regions called enhancers, which has an effect analogous to tuning up the volume of a CD player, and thus producing more outputs (music or RNAs/proteins). One interesting property of enhancers is that they do not need to be close to the genes they regulate, which is similar to a remote control. In this project, we developed computational methods that identify the locations of enhancers using a large amount of experimental data produced by an international research consortium called ENCODE (Encyclopedia of DNA Elements). We also studied DNA long-range interactions, which can bring an enhancer close to its target gene in the 3D space when it is operating, similar to bringing a remote control close to the CD player so that the infra-red signals it emits can be detected by the player. Our research results help understand how enhancers work, which is important for studying diseases such as cancer, in which enhancer activities can be disrupted by DNA mutations and other abnormalities.

418611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
418611.value: The quality of a clock network is of vital importance to a VLSI system as the clock signals co-ordinate the pace of almost every operation in the system. Its performance will determine the performance of the whole system in both speed and power. Clock skew is the maximum difference between the arrival times of the signals at any two sinks and this metric is an important one to be optimized because it makes up a significant portion of the clock cycle time. There have been many good traditional works on generating zero-skew clock trees but unfortunately, clock skew is very sensitive to variations caused by factors like manufacturing process, temperature and voltage supply. As the VLSI technology advances into the ultra-deep sub-micron era, a clock skew variation of just a few pico-seconds will make a design fail. Traditional methods, though producing clock trees with very small skew under nominal cases, may not be applicable when the system is subjected to variations. There is an urgent need to solve this variation-tolerant clock network synthesis problem. It was found that clock mesh technology can achieve lower skew clock distribution with higher tolerance to variations than classical clock tree technology. Clock mesh uses to be manually designed and employed by high performance systems because of its intensive resource requirements. The need to control on-chip variations is driving this clock mesh technology to general mainstream ASIC designs. However, there is a lack of research on this automatic clock mesh synthesis and optimization problem. To make clock mesh a feasible option, more study and research in this direction are needed. The IBM Research has organized a High Performance Clock Network Synthesis Contest in the year 2010 because of the importance of this problem and our team has received the first runner-up prize in the contest. This experience has motivated us to continue working on this challenging and interesting problem. Our objectives are to understand and find out the trade-off between performance and power in a clock mesh under the effects of on-chip variations for different mesh structures from an analytical perspective. Based on that, we will develop methodology to construct and optimize a holistic clock distribution network that has low skew variability and is power-efficient. The success of this project will absolutely be beneficial to the designs of both high performance microprocessors and ASIC designs. 时钟信号协调着系统中的几乎每一个操作，因此时钟网络的质量对于大规模集成电路（VLSI）系统是至关重要的，时钟网络的性能直接关系着整个系统的速度和能耗。时钟偏差指的是时钟信号到达任意两个时钟输出端的时间差的最大值。由于时钟偏差占据了时钟周期的一大部分，因此时钟偏差是时钟网络优化中的一个重要指标。迄今为止已有不少关于如何产生0时钟偏差的时钟树的研究工作，这些研究的问题在于时钟偏差对于生产过程，温度和电压等变化十分敏感。随着超大规模集成电路技术进入超深亚微米时代，短短几微微秒的时钟偏差就会导致一个失败的设计。传统的构造在标称情况下时钟偏差非常小的时钟树的方法，在存在变化的系统中已经不再适用。如何产生能够适应系统变化的时钟网络已成为一个迫切需要解决的问题。 时钟网格技术，不但可以提供较低的时钟偏差分布，而且比传统的时钟树技术能更好地适应系统变化。由于其对资源的密集需求，这项技术往往使用人工设计并且只适用于少量高性能系统。随着技术的发展，对于控制芯片的片上变化（OCV）的需求越来越大。这一需求推动了时钟网格技术向一般主流的ASIC设计发展。然而，现在阶段却十分缺乏对于时钟网格综合和优化自动化的研究。为了使时钟网格成为一个可行的技术，需要在这个方向上投入更多的科研力量。由于这一问题的重要性，IBM研究所在2010年举办了高性能时钟网络综合竞赛。我们的团队在这次比赛中获得了亚军。这次宝贵的经验促使我们继续对这一有趣而又具有挑战性的问题进行研究。我们的目标是从分析的角度了解并找出，在片上变化的影响下，不同时钟网格在性能和能耗之间的权衡。在此基础上，我们将应用时钟网格技术，建立一个从整体上构建和优化具有低时钟偏差变化的时钟网络的方法。这一项目的成功无疑将有利于高性能微处理器和ASIC设计的发展。

418611.label: Realisation of objectives
418611.value: There are three major objectives as stated in the application. The first and second one are related to the development of methodology for clock distribution network construction and its implementation based on the clock mesh technology. This work was successfully performed in collaboration with the co-PI from IBM Research. In this problem, a master clock grid is given on the topmost layer which is assumed to provide zero-skew clock signals. It is then needed to connect all the ports to the sources by making use of those reserved tracks with different wire types, and the objective is to satisfy the constraint on the maximum delay bound at every sink (skew variability), and to minimize the total wire capacitance (power). A graph G is used to model the virtual grid of reserved routing tracks. The edges in G represent the wire segments on the reserved tracks connecting ports, vias, or sources. We developed a partition-based delay-driven path expansion algorithm to solve this problem. In our approach, we first partition the ports into clusters according to their positions and the surrounding routing tracks. For each cluster, the ports are simultaneously propagated in selected directions. During this expansion process, we always select the path with the smallest Elmore delay to proceed. This path expansion step is repeated until all the ports are connected, or no more ports can be connected without violating the delay constraint. These are the basic steps of our partition-based delay-driven path expansion algorithm. It is invoked repeatedly with a pre-processing step to connect up some critical ports first. Finally, some post-processing techniques are performed to further reduce the total wire capacitance and thus to reduce the power consumption. We implemented our tool using C++ and use it to construct clock distribution network on circuits with thousands of sinks. We tested it on three cases (test1–test3) provided by industry and on eleven cases obtained from the benchmarks used in an international clock tree synthesis contest organised by IBM by setting the clock grid and routing tracks according to the conventions used in the first three industrial test cases. Results show that our approach provides significant improvement in both the total wire capacitance (24.6%) and the total wire length (23.6%) compared with the most updated previous work on this problem. The major contribution of this study was published in: [0] Haitong Tian, Wai-Chung Tang, Evangeline F. Y. Young and Cliff C. N. Sze."Postgrid Clock Routing for High Performance Microprocessor Designs". IEEE Transaction on CAD of Integrated Circuits and Systems 31(2): 255-259, 2012. [1] Xu He, Tao Huang, Linfu Xiao, Haitong Tian and Evangeline F. Y. Young. "Ripple: A Robust and Effective Routability-Driven Placer". IEEE Transaction on CAD of Integrated Circuits and Systems 32(10): 1546-1556, 2013. The third objective is on study and analysis of different clock network structures. In the project, we have studied a general type of non-tree structures that can be obtained by inserting cross-links between different pairs of sinks. Link based non-tree clock network is an effective way to reduce clock skew caused by variations. It is interesting to understand where the links should be inserted in order to achieve a large skew variation reduction with small extra resources. In our approach, clock skew in a non-tree clock network is analyzed based on a high order delay model for accuracy and the delay information is used to select the node pairs for link insertion. Tradeoff between crosslink length (power) and skew variability reduction is explored. Based on the analysis, we proposed a new algorithm to insert crosslinks into a clock network. We proposed a new method using linear program to solve the problem. Experiments show that our method can reduce skew variations effectively. The major contribution from this study was published in: [2] Fuqiang Qian, Haitong Tian and Evangeline F. Y. Young. "Crosslink Insertion for Variation-driven Clock Network Construction". ACM Great Lakes Symposium on VLSI 2012: 321-326. Finally, we have studied the construction of rectilinear Steiner tree, which is a back-end process in constructing a clock tree. We consider the problem of constructing a rectilinear Steiner tree spanning all the sinks in the presence of obstacles. These obstacles are potentially macros or IPs that may block all or some metal layers so that only limited wiring are allowed and dropping of buffers is impossible. Therefore, we need to consider the signal quality (slew constraint) at the same time while routing besides minimizing the total wire length (power). The study of this routing problem was later extended to parallel computation and to 3D chip interconnect planning. The major contributions of this study were presented in: [3] Tao Huang and Evangeline F. Y. Young. "ObSteiner: An Exact Algorithm for the Construction of Rectilinear Steiner Minimum Trees in the Presence of Complex Rectilinear Obstacles", IEEE Transaction on CAD of Integrated Circuits and Systems 32(6): 882-893, 2013. [4] Tao Huang and Evangeline F. Y. Young. "Construction of Rectilinear Steiner Minimum Trees with Slew Constraints over Obstacles". ICCAD 2012: 144-151. [5] Wing-Kai Chow, Liang Li, Evangeline F. Y. Young and Chiu-Wing Sham. "Obstacle-avoiding Rectilinear Steiner Tree Construction in Sequential and Parallel Approach". Integration, the VLSI Journal 47(1): 105-114, 2014. [6] Johann Knechtel, Evangeline F. Y. Young and Jens Lienig. "Planning Massive Interconnects in 3-D Chips". IEEE Transaction on CAD of Integrated Circuits and Systems 34(11): 1808-1821, 2015.

418611.label: Major findings and research outcome
418611.value: We have studied two general kinds of clock distribution network constructions. One type of construction is on a regular and hierarchical clock grid, and the other one is an irregular clock tree with cross-links. Unlike traditional clock trees, both are non-tree clock network. We studied the problem of clock network construction with an objective to minimize skew variability and power. In general, regular clock mesh gives low variability in skew but power consumption is high because of the large amount of clock wires. On the other hand, clock trees with cross-links need less wiring resources, i.e., lower power, but it is non-trivial to determine where the cross-links should be inserted to reduce skew variability. Different network structures give different trade-off between variability and power. We have studied this clock network construction problem on both regular mesh structure and irregular tree structure with cross-links. We developed the methodologies and implemented the tool to construct clock networks of different structures given thousands of sinks on a chip. The objective is to minimize both power and skew variability. Our works have been published in [0], [1] and [2]. (Please refer to section 5.3.) Finally, we also researched on a routing problem that is related to clock tree construction, The clock network is usually the biggest net connecting the largest number of pins in a circuit. It is thus also a major source of power dissipation. Power can be saved if the clock tree wire length is minimised. This corresponds to a rectilinear Steiner minimum tree. We proposed a method to generate an optimal obstacle avoiding rectilinear Steiner minimum tree that also considers buffer insertion to maintain signal integrity (slew constraint). The study of this routing problem was also extended to parallel computation and to 3D chip design. The major contributions are published in [3], [4], [5] and [6]. (Please refer to section 5.3.)

418611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
418611.value: Clock tree construction is always a very important problem in VLSI design. Besides power and variability, noise is another concern that can be considered in our construction methods and analyses. Besides, scalability is another essential issue in modern VLSI designs. It is interesting to see how the construction method can be extended to cases with hundreds of thousands of timing elements. These are all potential directions for further development of the research on this topic.

418611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
418611.value: In a VLSI circuit, it is needed to provide a clock signal to all timing elements in order to provide synchronization. A clock network is designed for this purpose. Usually the clock network is the biggest net connecting the largest number of sinks in a circuit. For this reason, it is also a major source of power dissipation, and power can be saved if the clock tree wire length can be reduced. It is also desirable to construct a clock network that can have as little skew variability as possible under variations in voltage, current, temperature, etc. The major objective of this project is to study the problem to study the problem of constructing clock network with low power consumption and variability. We studied two general kinds of clock distribution networks in this project. One is a regular and hierarchical clock mesh with clock twigs at the lowest level. The other one is a tree structure with cross-links between some sink pairs. The idea in both is to have more than one paths to connect to each sink in order to reduce variability. The mesh structure will consume more power but with less variability, while the cross-link approach is power efficient but is non-trivial to determine the positions of the cross-links. In this project, we study this clock network construction problem and propose methods to construct different kinds of clock networks.

Achieve rFOV T1rho spine imaging with a spatial resolution of 0.4mm/pixel within 3 minutes, a factor of three in scan time reduction. Perform MDRF-enabled rFOV DCE-MRI bone marrow perfusion on 10 patients with two-fold improvement on spatial and temporal resolution compared to the normal imaging protocol. Simultaneous fat suppression and rFOV for MRgFUS temperature mapping. Temporal resolution increases by 4-fold with temperature uncertainty less than 1°C.

418811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
418811.value: Multi-dimensional radio-frequency pulses (MDRFs) for MRI have many valuable applications in clinical practice. MDRF-enable reduced field-of-view (rFOV) imaging can accelerate imaging speed, reduce scan time and improve spatial resolution significantly, valuable for applications like MR-guided focused ultrasound (MRgFUS) temperature mapping. MDRFs have the capability to selectively excite fat and water that helps to suppress fat or water signal for better diagnosis. MDRF is also able to improve 3D excitation profile and compensate in-plane B1 field imhomogeneities. Advances in MDRF design have been achieved in recent years. However, the use of MDRFs in routine clinical practice is still very limited. The primary reasons include the rigid design of MDRF, the longer pulse duration, the inflexibility in excitation pattern and spectral selectivity, the sensitivity to susceptibility, and user-unfriendliness for non-specialists. This proposal aims to develop high-efficient and user-friendly MDRFs using single and multiple transmitters to improve their usability and efficiency in routine clinical practice, especially for non-specialists. To achieve this goal, on-line dynamic MDRF waveforms will be designed according to the user prescription on desirable excitation profile, rather than the off-line designed fixed pulse for a rigid excitation. The associated excitation patterns will be shown simultaneously and intuitively. MDRF duration will be minimized to facilitate fast imaging by variable rate selective excitation, optimized gradient switching, and parallel transmission. A customized prescan will be designed for pulse calibration to automatically adjust MDRF sub-pulse phases to compensate susceptibility and timing-delay artifacts. MDRF pulses will be integrated with various pulse sequences. Their functionality and performance will be validated by phantom imaging. We propose to apply MDRFs for three distinct applications of rFOV spine T1rho imaging, dynamic contrast enhanced (DCE) MRI for spine bone marrow perfusion and MRgFUS temperature mapping. MDRF enabled rFOV benefits spine T1rho and DCE imaging in shorter scan time, higher spatial and temporal resolution because of spine’s long and narrow anatomy and small cross-sectional size. Furthermore, significantly lower RF energy deposit can be achieved for T1rho imaging to improve patient safety. Accurate and fast temperature mapping can be achieved by MDRF-enabled simultaneous fat suppression and rFOV, promising for real-time temperature mapping in moving organs for MRgFUS thermal therapy. In summary, success in MDRF development of this proposal is expected to overcome major restrictions of MDRF and benefit a broad range of routine clinical applications with ease and efficiency. 多維射頻脈衝（MDRFs）在磁力共振掃描MRI的臨床實踐中有許多有價值的應用。MDRF可用於缩小視場（rFOV）成像從而加快成像速度，減少掃描時間，以及顯著提高影像的空間分辨率。這些特性對於磁共振引導的聚焦超聲治療溫度映射有重要的應用價值（MRgFUS）。MDRFs還可用於在MRI掃描中選擇性地激發脂肪或水，以提高MRI影像的診斷價值。 MDRF亦能用於改善三維激發區域的空間輪廓，並減小掃描斷層內B1磁場的不均勻度。 近年來，MDRF設計已取得一定進展，但是其在日常臨床實踐中的應用還十分有限，主要的原因包括：缺乏靈活性的MDRF設計，較長的脈衝持續時間，固定的激勵模式和頻譜選擇性，對磁場不均勻度的高度敏感，以及用戶不友好的操作界面。 這項研究計劃書旨在發展高效率和用戶友好的單通道或多通道激發的MDRFs，以提高其在日常臨床實踐中的可用性和效率， 特別是對非專業人士而言。為了實現這一目標，使用者只需根據要求指定所需的激發模態，而相應的MDRF設計可在MRI掃描機上動態地自動完成，不同於以往的將脫線設計的具有固定波形的MDRFs上載到MRI掃描機的操作模式。MDRF脈衝時間可通過採用變頻選擇性激發，梯度磁場切換優化以及並行激發技術而有效縮短，以利於快速成像。我們還將設計自定義的MDRF脈衝校準的預掃描技術，自動調整MDRF子脈衝相位以補償由於易感度和時間延遲造成的偽影。MDRF脈衝將被整合於各種脈衝序列，其功能以及性能將通過水膜成像加以驗證 我們將在三個不同的臨床應用中使用MDRF，它們是應用rFOV技術的脊柱T1rho成像，動態對比增強（DCE）的脊椎骨髓灌注成像和MRgFUS溫度映射。 應用MDR的 rFOV成像，可顯著縮短脊柱T1rho和DCE的成像掃描時間，提高影像的的空間和時間分辨率。此外，使用MDRF可以有效地顯著降低射頻能量在人體內的積聚從而提高 T1rho成像技術的安全性。MDRF可同時採用rFOV和脂肪抑制成像技術，以實現準確而快速的溫度映射。此技術在針對運動器官的MRgFUS熱療法的實時溫度控制中有重要的應用前景。總之，此項研究的成功，將有望克服MDRF目前存在的主要限制，大大提高其易用性及效率，從而裨益眾多的常規臨床應用。

418811.label: Realisation of objectives
418811.value: We improved the T1rho spine imaging, achieved the spatial resolution of 0.4mm/pixel within 3 minutes. The results have been published and disseminated. Our work has been noted as ‘remarkable’ in an expert consensus report in 2014 < Eur Spine J (2014) 23 (Suppl 3):S315–S323; Advances in the diagnosis of degenerated lumbar discs and their possible clinical application>. The proposed MDRFs on single-transmitter and dual-transmitter MRI scanners for pulse sequences has been implemented in fast spin echo, fast field echo. The work has led to the 1st time implantation of CEST (chemical exchange saturation transfer) for liver imaging by our team. This funding has been associated with the following publications: 1. Amide proton transfer-weighted imaging of the head and neck at 3 T: a feasibility study on healthy human subjects and patients with head and neck cancer. NMR Biomed. 2014;27:1239-47. 2. MR chemical exchange imaging with spin-lock technique (CESL): a theoretical analysis of the Z-spectrum using a two-pool R(1ρ) relaxation model beyond the fast-exchange limit. Phys Med Biol. 2012;57:8185-200. 3. Quantification of T(1ρ) relaxation by using rotary echo spin-lock pulses in the presence of B(0) inhomogeneity. Phys Med Biol. 2012;57(15):5003-16. 4. 419011.label: Project Objectives
419011.value: To find the maximum increase of payoff when playing quantum strategies on the quantum superposition of a classical correlated equilibrium. To find the largest gap between the randomized and quantum correlation complexities of correlated equilibria. In particular, to pin down the largest randomized correlation complexity for correlated equilibria with quantum correlation complexity being 1. To study the relation between quantum correlated complexity and quantum communication complexity. In particular, to see whether there is any separation between these two measures. To study the efficiency of verification of quantum equilibria. To study the possibility of efficient representation of all correlated equilibria for graphical games. To understand and further develop the theory of quantum belief propagation during the process.

419011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
419011.value: 博弈論是一門研究多人不同目標下的交互的應用數學。經過幾十年的發展，博弈論已經形成了一個豐富的領域，而且在經濟學，政治學，生物，哲學，統計，計算機科學等分支發現了大量應用。策略型博弈是博弈論中最基本的模型。 納什均衡描述一種各人都已達到當前最優的狀態（假設其他人不變）。納什均衡和一些重要的擴充如相關均衡構成了博弈論中的中心解決概念。 在本項目中，研究人提出發展量子策略博弈論。雖然亦有類似研究，但是都是關於一些小規模的特定博弈。研究人的目標是一般的​​大型博弈。而且研究人提出了一個新的更加簡單的模型，避免了以前模型中的無理假設使得量子均衡的概念變得簡單乾淨。另一方面，本模型有著豐富的數學結構和問題值得研究。 在這個模型下，研究人希望研究下面的定量問題：如果用量子的方式進行博弈，能取得多大的優勢？優勢的不同的具體含義給出下面兩個不同的方向。 1.優勢是收益的增加。比如，如果一個經典均衡下每個人都無法增加自己的收益，但是在相對應的量子態下，可以有的人大大增加自己的收益。即使這個對應是非常簡單自然的量子疊加態。找出最大可能的收益增加意味著量子在博弈中的最終優勢。數學上，這是一個非線性規劃。研究人已經做出了相當進展。 2.優勢是生成相關性的難度。研究人提出一個新的複雜性度量，相關複雜性，而且發現了有的n位相關性需要至少log(n)位的經典相關種子才能生成，但量子種子只要1位即可。這個新的方向和量子力學中著名的貝爾不等式，代數中的非負秩，計算機科學中的通信複雜性都有著密切關係。其研究很可能在其他領域有所發現。

419011.label: Realisation of objectives
419011.value: The objectives are mostly achieved, summarized as follows. 1. We have already found the maximum increase of payoff when playing quantum strategies on the quantum superposition of a classical correlated equilibrium. Actually, we considered the increase in two measures, additive and multiplicative, and have successfully pinned down the maximum increases in both cases. Results published in the prestigious conference ITCS (2012). 2, 3: We have found some correlation with randomized correlation complexity n but quantum correlation complexity only log(n). This gives an exponential separation of the two complexities, implying that in generating classical correlations, quantum communication could be exponentially more efficient than classical communication. In addition, we completely characterized both the randomized and quantum correlation complexities, by nonnegative rank and psd rank, respectively. Results published in the prestigious conference ITCS (2012), SODA (2013) and journal IEEE Transactions on Information Theory (2013). 4. We found a complete characterization of a quantum state being quantum correlated equilibrium by a system of positive semi-definite conditions. Results published in journal Quantum Information and Computation (2013). 5. We considered hardness of generating classical and quantum correlated states in multi-player settings, assuming that any pair of players can send messages to each other. This corresponds to the important special case of complete graph. We plan to investigate the general graph case in future. Results submitted to journal Quantum Information and Computation in 2014.

419011.label: Major findings and research outcome
419011.value: The major findings are summarized as follows, with emphasis on results not covered in the above "Realisation of objectives" part. We organized existing results in the messy body of literature on quantum games, and proposed a simpler yet much richer model for studying quantum strategic games. The model is now considered as "the correct" one for quantum games. After setting up the model, we are interested in central solution concepts such as Nash equilibrium and correlated equilibrium. We identified some natural correspondences between classical and quantum states, and found how these correspondences preserves the equilibrium properties. In particular, we found that all quantum equilibrium induces classical equilibrium by measurement in the computational basis. We then considered the case that one player is classical and the other uses a quantum computer. It is interesting to see that in this setting, the quantum player has a huge advantage in winning the game, even if she doesn't have any advantage when using classical computer. We found the maximum increase of payoff when playing quantum strategies on the quantum superposition of a classical correlated equilibrium. The increases are measured both additively and multiplicatively. Recently, we went further to consider the case when both players use quantum computers. While in simple strategic games there is no advantage when both using quantum computers, we showed that in Basysian games, when using quantum computers, both players can achieve a higher payoff in a quantum equilibrium, compared to what they can get in any classical equilibrium. (Published in Physical Review Letters, 2015) We found a complete characterization of a quantum state being quantum correlated equilibrium by a system of positive semi-definite conditions. Results published in journal Quantum Information and Computation (2013). We initialized systematic studies on complexity of generating a classical distribution or a quantum state. We completely characterized both the randomized and quantum correlation complexities, by nonnegative rank and psd rank, two measures recently drawing much attention in optimization and theoretical computer science. Results published in ITCS (2012), SODA (2013) and IEEE Transactions on Information Theory (2013). We further extended the study to the settings where more than two players need to generate a joint multi-partite state. We give bounds of minimum amount of communication or seed correlation needed in both classical and quantum scenarios. Some bounds are completely tight, and some are tight up to a constant. Results submitted to journal Quantum Information and Computation in 2014.

419011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
419011.value: Many important problems are yet to be better understood. For example, in the multi-partite case, when the communication channels are not pairwise available, but only between neighbors in an underlying graph, what can say about the complexity? Another important direction is mechanism design. Can we design mechanism for quantum systems to achieve better efficiency, either computationally or socially, compared to classical systems? Investigations on these questions may yield important new discoveries of power of quantum information processing in the fundamental field of game and mechanism design theories.

419011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
419011.value: Game theory studies the scenarios where two or more players (people, companies, etc.) each have a potentially different goal and care about only his or her own payoff (profit, gain, etc.). While traditional game theory assumes that all players use classical computational devices to make their decision, this project aims to systematically study how players behave when at least one of them uses quantum device. In particular, we found out how much advantage one could have by switching to quantum devices. Our discoveries showcase some scenarios where a big advantage exist for the quantum player. We also found some games in which, if all players use quantum devices, then all of them can benefit compared to their classical situation. Finally, we considered the efficiency of generating a classical distribution, and showed that using quantum devices can generate some distributions with much less communication and much less seed correlation. These results show the power of quantum information processing.

419311.label: Project Objectives
419311.value: To design a set of versatile FET configurations that can be used for spectroscopic studies on donor-acceptor material systems that are of interest for solar cell application. To construct a comprehensive CMS measurement apparatus with which to characterize heterojunction FETs and to obtain unipolar spectroscopic data that is complementary to photoinduced measurements. To measure the degree of charge localization in different organic semiconductors using CMS and to correlate it with the morphology and polarizability of the materials. To determine the impact of interface modification on charge localization and the efficiency of charge separation at the donor-acceptor interface. To identify key parameters for improved solar cell performance based on spectroscopic characterization for a set of novel thiophene-based donor-acceptor copolymers, in order to establish criteria for the design of new material systems to achieve high efficiency in organic solar cells.

To identify key parameters for improved solar cell performance based on spectroscopic characterization for a set of novel thiophene-based donor-acceptor copolymers, in order to establish criteria for the design of new material systems to achieve high efficiency in organic solar cells.

419311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
419311.value: Organic solar cells offer great opportunity toward the widespread use of solar energy because they can be inexpensively fabricated on flexible substrates and over large areas by means of low-cost printing and coating technologies. In an organic solar cell, photogenerated electron-hole pairs are dissociated at a heterojunction interface formed by a donor and an acceptor material, after which the electrons and holes are collected at the electrodes of the device. The localized nature of charge carriers in organic semiconductors can limit the efficiencies of these processes, and therefore the overall performance of the organic solar cell, by hindering the transport of electrons and holes away from the interface and to the electrodes. In this project we seek to understand the mechanisms that cause charge localization in the proximity of a donor-acceptor heterojunction. We propose to do this using charge modulation spectroscopy (CMS) to directly interrogate the degree of localization of charge carriers in the molecular lattice. CMS measurements on two-component, donor-acceptor material systems that are of interest for solar cell applications have not been pursued previously. We will develop several field-effect transistor structures as the CMS testing configurations, which will enable us to separately probe electrons and holes and to vary their locations from the bulk donor and acceptor phases to their interface. We will also study how film morphology, polarizability of the materials and molecular interactions at the donor-acceptor interfaces affect charge localization for different organic solar cell systems. In particular, we will focus our study on a new class of high performance thiophene-based copolymers. The results will be the establishment of criteria for the design of new material systems to enable improved solar cell performance.

419311.label: Realisation of objectives
419311.value: We have fully accomplished the objectives of the proposal. -We have designed and fabricated well-performed FETs with three different configurations, namely, single-layer, bilayer and bulk heterojunction. -We have set up a comprehensive CMS measurement apparatus, which includes CMS, photo-induced absorption, and electroabsorption modulation functions. -We have studied the morphological effects by comparing polymer/fullerene heterojunctions with highly-ordered and disordered molecular packing configurations. -We have correlated the interface intermixing morphology with the degree of charge localization, and proposed how it affects charge separation efficiency at the donor-acceptor interface. - We have studied six different thiophene-based donor-acceptor copolymers, with three of them showing good solar cell performance.

419311.label: Major findings and research outcome
419311.value: -We have set up a comprehensive CMS measurement apparatus, which includes CMS, photo-induced absorption, and electroabsorption modulation functions. This setup has enabled many fundamental charge transport and photophysics studies on organic and perovskite semiconductors. (Publications #1-7) - We innovatively introduced a heterojunction field-effect transistor structure in CMS, enabling probing of microscopic charge transport properties at polymer/fullerene interfaces. The study revealed two different interface charge localization mechanisms, which are governed by the molecular packing and ordering of the polymer component. (Publication #7) - We investigated the variation of polaronic states as a function of the intramolecular and intermolecular arrangements of the donor (D) and acceptor (A) moieties in D-A copolymers. The study provides foundation knowledge for new molecule designs as well as experimental references for theoretical studies. (Publications # 1&3) - We studied six different thiophene-based donor-acceptor copolymers, with three of them showing good solar cell performance. In general we found a thin amorphous-like polymer/fullerene intermixing interface is ideal for charge separation, while a crystalline polymer phase right next to the interface would make the following up charge transport process more efficient. (Publications # 3, 4, 5,7)

419311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
419311.value: The success of the project shows that the combination of heterojunction FETs and CMS provides a powerful tool to study interface charge transport phenomenon. We planned to extend this technique to study the electronic processes of organic/2D material interface and organic/liquid interface (for bioelectronics). The organic/2D material interface study is proposed in a CRF proposal (2015/16 exercise) and the is proposed in a GRF proposal (2016/17 exercise).

419311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
419311.value: This project developed an in-situ spectroscopic tool to study polaronic states and charge transport properties in organic semiconductors. The uniqueness of the approach is that it exploits a donor-acceptor heterojunction FET structure, which enables the spectroscopic measurement to be interface specific. Such feature is not available in the commonly used optical pump-probe spectroscopic methods. Through this project we studied polymer systems that respectively show good performance for FET and solar cell applications, and we specifically focused on the influence of intra- and inter-molecular configurations. The findings not only provide critical information about the electronic processes in organic heterojunction interfaces but also shed light on the design of new molecular semiconductors for various device applications.

419411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
419411.value: Sustainable development and corporate social responsibility have emerged as important priorities for business corporations. Among various activities to improve the social and environmental consequences of their operations, emissions and pollutants reduction plays an important role. Companies can no longer continue with business as usual in their daily operations because of stricter emissions regulations, increasing costs of carbon, and growing customer expectation on carbon management performance. In view of these, there is a need for research that studies supply chain systems integrated with carbon emission management. In this project, we investigate the impacts of emissions regulations in business practices and operational policies in supply chains. We first consider emissions trading for firms managing dynamic production systems with multiple production technologies differing in emissions and costs. Product demand and trading prices of emission allowances are both stochastic. Settings with finite production capacity, technology switching and idling costs, and product pricing decisions are modeled and analyzed. We aim not only to characterize optimal emissions trading, technology selection, and production policies but to quantify the value of green technologies and their impact on companies' emissions reduction. Furthermore, by using data of allowance trading prices and data of costs and emissions of different production technologies (e.g., fuel usage), we conduct numerical/empirical studies to illustrate and discuss the implications of the theoretical results. We then venture beyond single-firm models to analyze the interaction between the multiple firms that constitute a supply chain. We develop two-echelon models in which firms are subject to emissions tax/penalty for excessive emissions. We then apply a game theoretic framework to examine firms' emissions abatement, production and pricing decisions, and contractual relationships in a monopoly or competitive market environment. To study market drivers of emissions reduction, we further model consumer preferences of low carbon products and incorporate them into supply chains optimization. The outcomes of this project will provide valuable insights into how firms can simultaneously manage their carbon emissions and supply chain operations to not only comply with regulations but also remain operationally efficient and gain competitive advantages. 可持续发展和企业社会责任已经逐渐成为商业机构的优先领域. 在各种改进企业运作对环境和社会的影响的活动中, 减排占据了一个重要的角色. 由于日益严格的排放规管, 碳成本的上升, 和消费者对企业碳排放管理的高期望, 公司已不能继续以前惯有的日常商业运作. 这些因素导致对结合碳排放管理的供应链系统的研究的必要性. 在本项目中, 我们将研究排放权规管对供应链中各种运作带来的影响.我们首先将排放权交易考虑进拥有多种生产技术的企业生产系统中. 这些技术产生不同的排放量和生产成本.客户对产品的需求和排放权的交易价格都是随机的. 我们同时将考虑一些其他的系统特征, 比如有限产能, 技术转换成本和停顿成本, 已及产品的售价决策. 我们的目标不仅是要刻画最优的排放权交易, 技术选择, 和生产的策略, 同时将要量化环保生产技术对企业的价值极其对企业减排的影响. 通过收集和采用实际排放权的交易价格和企业生产成本, 我们将用数值计算及结果来展示和讨论相关的理论结果. 我们将进一步考虑多个企业的问题.我们将建立一个有上下游结构的供应链模型. 上游的供货商和下游的制造商都受到排放权税收的规管. 我们运用非协作博弈论的工具来研究公司的减排, 生产, 和定价策略, 以及在垄断或竞争市场环境下的合同契约关系. 为了研究企业减排的市场动力, 我们将进一步对消费者对环保产品的偏好进行建模 并将客户行为结合到供应链优化模型中. 本项目的研究成果将对企业如何同时管理其供应链和碳排放以达到服从规管和保持运作效率和赢得竞争力提供有价值的见解.

419411.label: Realisation of objectives
419411.value: The objectives of the project have been successfully achieved. The PI has developed quantitative supply chain models that incorporate carbon emissions management under cap-and-trade scheme in two papers, one published in Operations Research and the other one under review at POMS. Based on these models, we study the impact of emissions regulations on firms’ production, technology choices, and wholesale price decisions. The optimal (equilibrium) strategies are characterized. Meanwhile, we quantify the value of green technology to a production firm using representative data from the cement industry. We also study the interaction and wholesale price contract between a supplier and a manufacturer in a supply chain when either or both firms are under emissions regulation.

419411.label: Major findings and research outcome
419411.value: In the paper titled “Optimal Production Planning with Emissions Trading’’ published in Operations Research,, we develop a dynamic production model with random market demand. The manufacturer has access to both a green and a regular production technology, of which the former is more costly but yields fewer emissions. We first derive several important structural properties of the model and then characterize the optimal emissions trading and production policies that minimize the manufacturer’s expected total discounted cost. In particular, the optimal emissions trading policy is a target interval policy with two thresholds that decrease with the starting inventory level. The optimal production policy is of a base-stock type and the optimal base-stock level is independent of the starting inventory level and the allowance level when the manufacturer trades the allowance or uses both technologies simultaneously. A numerical study using representative data from the cement industry is conducted to illustrate the analytical results and to examine the value of green technology for the manufacturer. In the working paper titled “Production and Technology Choice under Emissions Regulation: Centralized vs. Decentralized Supply Chains,” we consider a supply chain where a supplier produces and sells raw material to a manufacturer who then uses it to produce a final product to satisfy random market demand. Both firms are equipped with two production technologies, of which one is more expensive but generates fewer emissions than the other. Each firm's emissions are capped by the amount of allowances it holds and if the firm over-emits, it pays a penalty. We solve the optimal solutions of both integrated (centralized) and decentralized systems when both firms are regulated. We find that a more stringent regulation always leads to a lower total production quantity in the centralized system but may result in a higher production quantity in the decentralized system. The quantity produced by the green technology at either firm is not monotonic in the amount of its allowances. The numerical results further show that the loss of supply chain profit (relative to the centralized system) due to decentralization is more significant with the emission regulation than without the emission regulation. In the scenarios where only one firm is regulated, we show that the centralized system produces more, uses more green technology, and generates more emissions than the decentralized one. More interestingly, the decentralized supply chain with the regulated supplier has higher profit and emits more than the one with the regulated manufacturer.

419411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
419411.value: We will continue working on the paper titled “Production and Technology Choice under Emissions Regulation: Centralized vs. Decentralized Supply Chains” and try to get it published soon.

419411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
419411.value: Increasingly stringent environmental regulations are urging companies to cut emissions from their business operations. Emissions trading, or cap-and-trade, is a regulation scheme that has been implemented in various countries. In this project, we develop quantitative supply chain models that integrate firms’ operational and emissions management decisions. When focusing on a single firm, we characterize the optimal dynamic emissions trading and production policies that minimize the firm's expected total discounted cost. Using representative data from the cement industry, we demonstrate that the green technology could significantly reduce costs and emissions. When studying a supply chain with one supplier and one manufacturer, we find that a more stringent regulation (fewer free allowances) always leads to a lower total production quantity in the centralized system but may result in a higher production quantity in the decentralized system. The loss of supply chain profit due to decentralization is more significant with the emission regulation than without the emission regulation. In the scenarios where only one firm is regulated, the decentralized supply chain with the regulated supplier has higher profit and emits more than the one with the regulated manufacturer.

419511.label: Project Title(Chinese)
419511.value: 解决连续时间行为金融组合选择之时间非一致性

419511.label: Project Objectives
419511.value: There are two overarching objectives in this project. The first one is to identify some dynamic optimisation problems that are time-consistent yet mathematically equivalent to the original CPT portfolio choice problem. There are two possible directions in this approach. One is to change the state variable from the wealth process to its quantile process. This change is expected to turn the nonlinear expectation (due to probability distortions) to the normal expectation, thus reducing to a time-consistent optimal control problem in a function space. The other direction takes an ``inverse approach'' of dynamic programming, where we first obtain the value function based on pre-committed optimal strategies, and then try to find an appropriate equation the value function must satisfy. The second objective is to employ a game theoretic formulation to our model. In this formulation an ``optimal'' strategy is an equilibrium strategy, one such that any deviation from it at any time instant will be worse off. We will characterise equilibrium strategies via Pontryagin's maximum principle and HJB-type equations respectively.

419511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
419511.value: Behavioural finance, developed since the 1980s, posits that emotion and psychology influence investors and create stock market anomalies such as bubbles and crashes. Kahneman and Tversky's Nobel-prize-winning cumulative prospect theory (CPT), the backbone of behavioural finance, captures human irrationality via gains and losses with respect to a reference point in wealth, different risk attitudes on gains and losses, and distortions of the probability scale. Behavioural finance has successfully explained many investor behaviours and market patterns that cannot be explained by the classical expected utility theory. Technically, however, behavioural theories bring in highly unconventional and challenging features for which the known techniques and machineries almost all fail. In particular, time consistency, which is a key assumption in conventional dynamic optimisation models and the very foundation of the mighty dynamic programming approach, is inherently violated in a bahavioural model due to probability distortion. Therefore, new theories and approaches, instead of mere extensions of the existing ones, are called for in formulating and solving behavioural models. The project aims to address and tackle time-inconsistency for a continuous-time CPT portfolio selection model. Two possible approaches are proposed in achieving this goal. One is to transform the CPT model into a mathematically equivalent one that is time-consistent, and the other is to give a proper definition of the ``dynamic optimality'' via a game theoretic formulation and then investigate the optimality accordingly. 本项目旨在解决连续时间行为金融之展望理论框架下组合选择的时间非一致性，为达此目的我们会在两个方面进行研究。一个是把原来的模型转化成数学上等价但具备时间一致性的新模型； 另一个是通过博弈理论来给出恰当的“动态优化”定义，然后研究相应的解。

419511.label: Realisation of objectives
419511.value: 1) The key issue in the first objective is to identify a certain class of stochastic control formulation that are time-consistent yet mathematically equivalent to the original CPT portfolio choice problem. In this research, we have integrated the martingale approach and quantile method to achieve this goal. When a market is complete, the martingale approach enables us to solve a time inconsistent financial decision making problem in two phases. We find first the optimal terminal wealth by solving a static optimization problem and to identify then the optimal portfolio policy to replicate such an optimal wealth distribution. More specifically, we propose a rank-dependent portfolio choice model in continuous time that captures the role in decision making of three emotions: hope, fear, and aspirations. Hope and fear are modeled through an inverse-S shaped probability weighting function and aspirations through a probabilistic constraint. By employing the recently developed approach of quantile formulation, we solve the portfolio choice problem both thoroughly and analytically. These solutions motivate us to introduce a fear index, a hope index, and a lottery-likeness index to quantify the impacts of three emotions, respectively, on investment behavior. 2) The core concept in the second research objective is to study time inconsistent financial decision making problems within a game framework. One of such a game framework is to identify an ``optimal'' equilibrium strategy such that any deviation from it at any time instant will be worse off. More specifically, we provide conditions on a one-period-two-date pure exchange economy with rankdependent utility agents under which Arrow–Debreu equilibria exist. When such an equilibrium exists, we show that the state-price density is a weighted marginal rate of intertemporal substitution of a representative agent, where the weight depends on the differential of the probability weighting function. Based on the result, we find that asset prices depend upon agents’ subjective beliefs regarding overall consumption growth, and we offer a direction for possible resolution of the equity premium puzzle. The second game formulation developed in this research is to adopt a planner-doer framework. When a stochastic decision problem is time inconsistent, the decision maker would be puzzled by his conflicting decisions “optimally” derived from his timevarying preferences at different time instants (with different time horizons). While the long-run self (LR) of the decision maker pursues the long-term optimality, the short-run selves (SRs) of the decision maker at different time instants lack foresight and bow to short-term temptations. While the current literature began to recognize the importance to strike a balance between LR’s and SRs’ interests, the existing results are not applicable to situations where the decision maker’s preferences involve non-expectation operators. As most risk measures are of a non-expectation nature, we take a step-forward to develop in this study an operable unified two-tier dual-self game model with commitment by punishment, which can cope with general time inconsistent stochastic decision problems with both expectation and non-expectation operators in the objective function. By attaching punishment terms to both the preferences of LR and SRs which quantitatively evaluate the internal conflict among different selves, our game model aligns the interests of the LR and SRs to a certain degree. The equilibrium strategy, termed strategy of self-coordination, achieves some degree of internal harmony among various selves. We demonstrate successful applications of our dual-self game model to two long-standing challenges in the literature, the investment and consumption problem with quasi-hyperbolic discounting and the dynamic mean-variance portfolio selection problem.

419511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
419511.value: For complete markets, the intractability caused by time inconsistency can be overcomed by adopting martingale approach. In other words, a class of time inconsistent financial decision making problems can be mapped into another class of time consistent stochastic control problems. This mapping enables us to investigate in the next step the optimal term structure of the risk attitudes in time inconstent financial decision making problems. The other important and more challenging future step is to extend the reach of the solution schemes for time inconsistent financial decision problems to INCOMPLETE markets.

419511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
419511.value: For general time inconsistent stochastic financial decision problems, a kind of paradoxical behaviors seems natural and inevitable. We have proposed in this research a mechanism design of self-coordination, a two-tier planner-doer game framework with commitment by punishment, into which a quantitative degree of self-coordination is integrated. The mechanism design aligns the interests of the planner and doers by applying penalty to both doers and the planner, thus reducing the level of paradoxical behaviors and achieving a degree of coordination among different facets of the decision maker. Our results actually provide a powerful theoretical framework and implemental solution tools to tackle generalized time inconsistent stochastic decision problems in real world. The developed two-tier planner-doer game framework can be readily applied to general time inconsistent stochastic decision problems, for examples, dynamic mean-variance portfolio selection, dynamic consumption problem with quasi-hyperbolic discounting and a class of stochastic programming problems under a (non-expectation) risk measure. Moreover, as social cooperation problems share similar features with the self-coordination problems, our two-tier planner-doer game framework may also shed light on resolving social cooperation problems in economics, finance and management science.

441511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
441511.value: Introduction: Due to the ageing population, palliative care is of greater importance of addressing our desire to achieve a good death in society . The success of palliative care relies on the quality of work of various helping professionals such as doctors, nurses and social workers who work with patients and families confronted with death, dying, and bereavement. To be competent in their work, helping professionals require not only knowledge and skills but also self-preparation in working with death, dying, and bereavement, for example, coping with the emotions and existential issues arising from their work. Surprisingly, existing death education and training seem to inadequately address the need of self-preparation in working with death, dying, and bereavement, and few studies have been conducted to explore the role of self-preparation. Lack of measures for the level of self-preparation in working with death, dying, and bereavement has also hampered helping professionals’ self-awareness and the possibility of examining the effectiveness of training that focuses on enhancing self-preparation in this area. To fulfill these knowledge and research gaps, this study aims: 1) To explore what self-preparation helping professionals perceive as necessary for competent practice in death, dying, and bereavement; 2) To develop and validate measurement that assesses helping professionals’ level of self-preparation in working with death, dying, and bereavement; and 3) To develop and evaluate the effectiveness of training on enhancing helping professionals’ self-preparation in working with death, dying, and bereavement. Methods: This study will involve three phases and last 36 months. A multi-stage, multi-method research design will be adopted. Three methods will be used. Phase 1: in-depth interviews with helping professionals who work with death, dying, and bereavement in palliative care. Phase 2: a survey for validation of a scale that measures the level of self-preparation in working with death, dying, and bereavement. Phase 3: a randomized control trial (RCT) to examine the effectiveness of training that aims to enhance helping professionals’ self-preparation in working with death, dying, and bereavement. This proposed study is the first systematic local study that aims to focus on the concept of self-preparation in working with death, dying, and bereavement. The outcomes of this study may enhance our knowledge in this area and provide remarkable implications for self-awareness, supervision, and training of helping professionals in palliative care. 助人專業者在與死亡，臨終及喪親有關工作中的自我準備 前言: 隨著人口老化，及達致「好死」的目標，紓緩照顧在社會中愈來愈重要。 以紓緩照顧能否成功，有賴一群服務末期病人及家屬的助人專業者，如醫生，護士及社工的服務質素。 這些助人專業者，如能有效地提供服務，不單需要知識及技巧，亦需要他們在死亡，臨終及喪親有關的工作上，作好自我的準備，例如處理在工作中所引發的情緒及存在意義的問題。 然而，現今的死亡教育及培訓，卻以乎不足以滿足他們在這方面的需要。 過去亦較少有研究探討在死亡，臨終及喪親有關的工作上，自我準備所扮演的角色。由於缺乏量度在這些工作中，自我準備程度的量表，助人專業者較難了解自己的情況，而我們亦較難檢視相關的培訓是否能提升助人專業者在工作中對死亡，臨終及喪親的自我準備。 因此，為回應有關之不足，本研究期望達致以下之目標: 1. 探索助人專業者認為什麼的自我準備，能協助他們有效地於與死亡，臨終及喪親相關的工作中工作; 2. 建立相關的量表，以評估助人專業者在死亡，臨終及喪親相關的工作中，自我準備的程度; 3. 發展能提升助人專業者在死亡，臨終及喪親相關的工作中，自我準備的相關培訓，並檢討其成效。 研究方法: 此研究為期36個月，分為三個階段進行。 研究以多階段，多方法形式展開。第一階段為深入訪問從事與死亡，臨終及喪親有關工作的助人專業者。 第二階段則進行問卷調查，以建立相關的量表，量度助人專業者在死亡，臨終及喪親相關的工作中，自我準備的程度。 在第三階段，將以隨機控制實驗的方式，檢視在此計劃中建立之培訓，能否提升助人專業者在死亡，臨終及喪親相關的工作中的自我準備。 這是第一個本地有系統地探討在死亡，臨終及喪親相關的工作中，自我準備這個概念的研究。 研究結果將有望加強在這方面的知識，及在紓緩照顧的不同範疇，例如督導及培訓，帶來實務上的啟示。

441511.label: Realisation of objectives
441511.value: The project objectives have been fully achieved. Objective 1 was achieved by conducting a qualitative study of 22 helping professionals. Through in-depth interviews, we have better understanding on what helping professionals perceived as necessary for competent practice in death, dying and bereavement. Objective 2 was achieved by conducting a validation study of 151 helping professionals. The Self-Competence in Death Work Scale was developed and validated. Objective 3 was achieved by conducting a randomized controlled trial that involved 112 helping professionals. Training was developed and was tested to be effective in enhancing helping professionals’ self-competence in working with death, dying and bereavement.

441511.label: Major findings and research outcome
441511.value: This project included three phases and the major findings in each phase were as follows: Phase 1 findings: Helping professionals perceived self-competence in death work from two major themes, “challenges” and “coping”. Emotional and existential challenges in working with death were identified. Emotional and existential coping were identified to cope with these challenges. Phase 2 findings: Based on the findings of phase 1, a “Self-competence in Death Work Scale” was developed and validated among helping professionals in Hong Kong. This scale was found to be reliable and valid. Phase 3 findings: A three-day training was developed which aims to enhance helping professionals’ self-competence in death work. A randomized controlled trial was conducted, and the findings showed that the training is effective in improving the overall score of self-competence in death work, the existential coping and the emotional coping in death work among the participants. The follow-up study indicated the training effect sustained three months after the intervention. One journal paper which described the validation of Self-competence in Death Work Scale was published in Journal of Pain and Symptom Management, and another paper which described the perceived self-competence in death work among helping professionals was accepted by Health & Social Work. Another paper which described the effectiveness of training for enhancing self-competence in death work was submitted and is now under review. Several conference papers were presented at different international conferences also.

441511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
441511.value: With the development of “Self-competence in Death Work Scale” from this project, further studies may adopt this scale as an outcome measure, and examine the level of competence of helping professionals in working with death, dying and bereavement. This scale can also be used as an outcome measure to examine the effectiveness of different training for enhancing self-competence of helping professionals in working with death. Future studies may also be conducted to examine the correlates of self-competence in death work. The PI will participate in a research study that involving heath care professionals in end-of-life care and the “Self-competence in Death Work Scale” may be used to examine the effectiveness of training provided to these professionals.

441511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
441511.value: When working with death, dying and bereavement, helping professionals may experience different challenges that may impact on the “self”. For example, they may experience heavy emotions, and show queries to the life meaningfulness. The key to cope with these challenges may depend on their level of self-competence in doing the death-related work, such as their ability of coping with aroused emotions and existential queries. This project examined this importance concept of “self-competence in death work” among helping professionals systematically. Findings of this project may enrich our understanding on what helping professionals perceived as necessary in coping with the challenges on “self” in death work. Also, this project developed a measurement that can be used to assess the level of self-competence in death work among helping professionals. Training was also developed in this project for enhancing the self-competence in death work among helping professionals, and this training was proved to be effective. With all these efforts, this project may help improve helping professionals’ self-competence in working with different service users, including terminally ill patients and families and also bereaved persons.

441811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
441811.value: Four experiments are planned to investigate the brain lateralization in processing Cantonese tones. These experiments differ in task demand (identification vs. discrimination) and method of measurement (behavioral vs. electrophysiological). In addition, we will investigate how acoustic properties and stimulus types affect tonal processing. Results from this study can inform us on what the critical factors are in tonal processing and how the related operation is done in the brain. This information will advance our knowledge about the perception of lexical tone and build the foundation for developing models of language processing in tonal languages. Such information will also be valuable for the speech therapist in the context of intervention, because tone perception is critical in processing tonal languages such as Cantonese. 本研究預期進行四個實驗來探討粵語聲調在人腦的認知歷程。 這些實驗將使用包含辨識及分辨的實驗作業和行為及電生理的研究方法。 此項研究還將探討聲調的聲學屬性及刺激種類對聲調認知的影響。 研究結果有助於了解影響聲調認知的重要因素和人腦如何加工粵語聲調。 相關信息可望為了解詞調知覺和建立聲調語言的語言認知理論做出貢獻。

441811.label: Realisation of objectives
441811.value: 1. To provide a systematic investigation of the hemispheric lateralization of tonal processing by manipulating task demand and measurement 2. To explore whether different types of stimulus and tone lead to different brain lateralization patterns in processing Four main experiments were conducted. In all of them, we manipulated both tonal type (level and contour tones) and stimulus type (syllables and hums). The first two were behavioral experiments (Experiments 1 and 2) in which a dichotic listening (DL) procedure was used to present two auditory stimuli at the same time to the two ears of a participant. The participants in Exp. 1 were required to report the stimulus that they heard more clearly among two simultaneously presented stimuli (i.e., explicit identification), whereas those in Exp. 2 needed to decide on whether the critical stimuli in two successively presented dichotic pairs were identical or not (i.e., stimulus discrimination). In addition, two electrophysiological experiments (Experiments 3 and 4) were done in which participants’ event-related potentials (ERPs) to different auditory stimuli were recorded when they were watching a silent movie. The participants in Exp. 3 were instructed to ignore the appearance of auditory stimuli, including both standard and deviant stimuli (i.e., the passive oddball paradigm). Those in Exp. 4, however, were asked to consciously monitor the presence of auditory stimuli and to press corresponding keys on a response box (i.e., the active oddball paradigm). By comparing the results obtained in the DL and ERP experiments, we can access the impact of measurement methodology on our understanding of tonal processing in Cantonese. Similarly, through contrasting the results of different behavioral (identification vs. discrimination) or ERP (passive vs. active oddball) experiments, we can obtain useful information about the possible effects of task demand. Finally, since we manipulated both tonal type (level and contour tones) and stimulus type (e.g., syllables and hums) in all experiments, the results can clarify the role of stimulus properties on tonal processing.

441811.label: Major findings and research outcome
441811.value: In the behavioral experiments with the dichotic listening paradigm, we found reliable effects of task demand, tonal type, and stimulus type on performance. For example, participants were more accurate in discrimination than in identification; the performance for syllables was faster than that for hums; and level tones were discriminated faster and more accurate than did contour tones. In addition, a robust left-ear (right hemisphere) advantage was found in processing lexical tones in Cantonese, irrespective of task demand, stimulus type, and tone type. These results seem to suggest that Cantonese speakers rely more on their right hemisphere in processing tonal information (Jia, Tsang, Huang, & Chen, 2013). In the electrophysiological experiments with ERP recordings, we also found reliable effects of tonal features, stimulus type, and task demand on the responses of participants, indicating that these factors have robust impact on processing Cantonese tones. For example, deviants of level tones and large deviations between two tones elicited stronger and earlier ERP responses relative to deviants of contour tones and small deviations in both passive and active oddball tasks. Moreover, syllables and hums produced similar patterns of ERP responses in the passive oddball task but different patterns in the active oddball task. These results indicate that unconscious processing of Cantonese tones is mainly driven by acoustic features, whereas conscious processing is sensitive to both linguistic and acoustic analyses. However, in contrast to the results of behavioral experiments, the results were very similar across the two hemispheres. In fact, we did not find any traces of brain lateralization of tonal processing across different time windows in the ERP experiments. These findings are reported in a manuscript, which has been submitted for publication and is currently under review (Jia, Tsang, Huang, & Chen, 2015). Together, the results of the present project indicate that both stimulus properties (e.g., tonal features and lexical status) and task demands play an important role in processing Cantonese tones. More importantly, different methods of measurement on tonal processing produced distinct patterns of brain lateralization, suggesting that lateralization is not stable and may not be the most fruitful way to understand acoustic and linguistic processing of lexical tones.

441811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
441811.value: The ERP technique used in the present project has relatively high temporal resolution, but its spatial resolution is relatively limited. Thus, one possible direction for further development of the present line of research is to use other methods of measurement with better spatial precision (e.g., fMRI) or relatively high temporal and spatial resolution (e.g., event-related optical signal) to study the related issues.

441811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
441811.value: This project investigates how Cantonese tones are processed in the brain. Four experiments have been conducted to identify and examine factors contributing to this process. The results shed light on tonal processing in Cantonese and the related cognitive and neural mechanisms. The information obtained advances our knowledge about the perception of lexical tones and contributes to developing models of language processing in tonal languages. Such information also has pedagogical, clinical, and engineering implications for various professionals working on issues relevant to language and speech, because tone perception is critical in processing tonal languages such as Cantonese.

443011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
443011.value: e-Service is of integrative importance in the e-business world. Its evolution can be traced to the beginning where service is rendered per user per site as a physical entity – software in a box. Conducting business online is now of a common practice rather than an exception in the integrative era, e-service, either as ASP, SaaS or as other service manifests, will continue to prevail as the trademark of developers for applications delivery. Yet, single-client e-services do not have provision to serve collaborative clients at the same time, and the interaction that may require with each other. Existing e-service serves each client individually, although at any one time, there could be more than one client accessing instances of the same service. A complex e-service can now be composed by stitching together different e-services choreographed to accomplish a complicated task. A holistic view of e-service however, must take hold with a conceptualization of e-service with not limited to one, but more parties participating and/or interacting among themselves to complete the functional realization of the service. Party e-service conceptualization is proposed to highlight the collaborative nature of e-business, and at current articulation, e-service, does not address interactivity nature of multi-party business processes. Concept of party e-service considers the nature of the provider, service targets, service availability, client relationship and client interaction. This study employs the design science approach to first establish the design theory for party e-services as 1st party and 2nd party as current practices, and 3rd party to complete the necessitated services online. The design theory will be presented as a set of principles which are grounded on existing body of knowledge in e-service and new requirements for facilitating collaborative e-business. We follow up with an architectural consideration, based on the conceptual principles, creating a design artifact as a model reference for technological innovation specification. Finally, we validate the artifact using an example of logistics shipment planning through an e-service platform only as a 3rd party e-service and not any other party e-service. Such e-service enables modern shipment planning that demands a forwarding agent not only to work closely with designated or any online shippers, logistics service providers and consignees to formulate a desirable shipment plan, but also to achieve real-time shipment monitoring, and in-process corrective actions for deviations of the shipping process.

443011.label: Realisation of objectives
443011.value: (1) We have developed a new conceptualization of e-service, which encapsulates collaboration through value co-creation. We expect that our conceptualization can introduce and substantiate a new e-service paradigm. (2) We have proposed a design theory for e-service based through abductive knowledge discovery and proposed design principles for our new e-service conceptualization. The design theory uses existing literature as its kernel theory, including e-service, SOA, and Service-dominant Logic. (3) We have instantiated our e-service conceptualization and design theory through with an instantiation in the form of an IT artifact. The instantiation is an e-service, which enables collaborative shipment planning. The instantiation demonstrates that our proposed design theory is viable and rigorous.

443011.label: Major findings and research outcome
443011.value: Our research show that there is a need for collaborative e-services and this need has also been echoed by the marketing literature in the form of Service Dominant Logic. Currently, the economy is service dominated and collaboration is needed to put forth attractive value propositions to customers. e-Service is predominantly realized through SOA (Service Oriented Architecture) and it is not originally designed to facilitate multiple collaborating parties. We therefore proposed a new conceptualization of e-service, which includes collaboration with multiple parties. We expect that our conceptualization can introduce a new paradigm for e-service. Our thoughts on the conceptualization has been documented in a manuscript "Towards Collaborative e-Service", which has been conditionally accepted by the International Journal of Electronic Business. Moreover, we have proposed an architectural framework, based on SOA, which can facilitate value co-creation with multiple collaborating parties. The proposed architectural framework is the result of a design theory, which can help to ensure our study's rigor and generalizability. We believe that our design theory for e-service can help academia and practitioners to develop e-services for value co-creation. The e-service conceptualization and design theory has been instantiated through an actual implementation. We developed an e-service for collaborative shipment planning. This e-service allows multiple parties to collaborate and come up with a greater value proposition to satisfy the customer's shipments. The design theory and its instantiation has been documented in a manuscript "Design Theory for e-Service" and has been submitted to MIS Quarterly. We have received valuable comments from the editors and are encouraged to consider their comments and resubmit our manuscript. We are currently finalizing the manuscript and preparing it for submission.

443011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
443011.value: The findings from this study warrants further development of our proposed third-party SOA. Our instantiation is only a proof of concept demonstrating that collaboration among multiple parties is possible for e-services. However, it would be interesting to further develop potential methods and mechanisms for the architectural framework. Moreover, our study is one of the first to use an abductive approach in design theory, it would be worthwhile to propose a process view for developing a design science research by articulating the existing views on design science, design theory and artifact along the foundational premises of SDL. At the same time, other critical issues in the integrative era such as dynamic partnership, any-to-any communication, and ad hoc collaboration must be facilitated or even supported, and if possible, ingrained into the concept of e-services.

443011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
443011.value: In this study we have proposed a new conceptualization of e-service based on the need from practitioners and other disciplines. We urge for an e-service paradigm, which includes collaboration among multiple parties in order to better facilitate value co-creation. Not only did we proposed a conceptualization, but we also suggested methods to realize it with existing technologies, e.g. enhanced SOA, through a design theory. The enhance SOA, which we call Third-Party SOA, is still based on the widely used SOA, but is also enriched with elements allowing multiple participants and interaction among them. We believe that our proposed Third-Party SOA can further alleviate existing e-services and propel open up new opportunities for value co-creation through e-service. We have also developed and implemented an e-service based on Third-Party SOA, a collaborative shipment planning e-service, to demonstrate the viability of our thinking.
