443111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
443111.value: This is a study of how boys construct their masculinities, or, how they become men, in one of the important sites of their growing-up process, i.e. the school. More specifically, we would research into the different dimensions of school life of teenage boys, and how these impact on their evolving gender and sexual identities. The study of masculinities, and how they are constructed in schools, had begun in English-speaking societies in the 1980s and the 1990s respectively. However, no such studies have been done in Chinese societies, and this study would be among the first. With the understanding that this process in boys-only schools will be different from that in mixed schools, we choose to study the former at this pioneering stage. A class dimension is built into this study by choosing two schools at both ends of the spectrum – an “elite school” with a predominantly upper-middle class intake, and a “Band 3” (i.e., academically poor) school with a working class intake. This cross-class comparison is important because existing literature reveals that there are multiple masculinities, and these are class-specific. Ethnography is adopted for our study because this enables us to observe and document the myriad details of school life experienced by boys, as well as the daily, repeated patterns of behaviour, feelings and thoughts that go into the making of diverse masculinities. This study also addresses the increasingly universal fear of “boys’ (academic) underachievement”. This fear, in turn, is believed to be linked to a “crisis of masculinity” afflicting mostly working-class men, who experience either unemployment and/or a high degree of financial instability amidst drastic economic restructuring and class polarization under global capitalism. In this regard, we would like to gauge teenage boys’ fears and aspirations related to their various goals in life (academic, career, emotional, etc), factors affecting their self-image and esteem, as well as how they position themselves in relation to gender stereotypes and popular discourses concerning manhood. While working-class men face the threat of unemployment and financial instability, we also witness the rise of elite “super professionals” (largely male) with their distinctive mode of masculinity. Through our cross-class study, we hope to explore the diversely different processes of construction of masculinities. Lastly, our study is also expected to contribute to the understanding of Chinese masculinities in a post-colonial context, and thereby to enrich the comparative study of masculinities and gender construction. 本計劃選擇以學校為背景，研究男孩子如何構築他們的男子氣質；換言之，是研究男孩子如何在這個重要的成長場域中成為男人。我們會探索學校生活的不同範圍，如何形塑青少年男孩不斷蛻變的性別和性身份。男子氣質及其在學校生活中的建構這方面的研究，早於上世紀八、九十年代在英語國家已出現，唯同類研究尚未見於華人社會。男女校的成長環境與男校的單性環境自有其不同之處，但在這個始創階段，我們選擇先在男校開展研究。本研究在兩所處於不同階級位置的男校進行—收取中上階層孩子的「精英」學校，和收取組別（banding）較低、勞工階級孩子為主的學校。這樣的設計，是基於前述英語國家研究的成果，顯示男子氣質是多元的，而其中階級因素產生著重大的影響。族誌學研究方法，容許我們深入而細緻地觀察男孩子在學校所體驗的種種生活細節，以及多元男子氣質所牽涉的、日常不斷重複的行為、感情和思維模式。本研究亦嘗試探討時下對男生「（學業）失利」的普遍憂慮。文獻顯示，這種憂慮與影響著勞工階層男性的「男子氣概危機感」相連。在資本主義全球化下，經濟結構大幅度重組與階級兩極化，勞工階層男性承受失業和經濟不穩定的打擊，導致某種傳統的男子氣質出現危機。循著這個方向，我們會審視男孩與各種生命目標（學業、就業和情感等）有關的憂慮與期望、影響他們自我形象與自信的因素，以及了解他們在刻板化性別形象及有關男子氣概的流行論述下如何自處。與勞工階層男性所體驗的失業和經濟不穩定狀態相對的，是精英「超級專業人士」（主要為男性）及其特有的男子氣質的冒升。我們期望通過這個跨階級研究，探索不同男子氣質的構築過程。最後，我們期望本研究能促進我們對後殖處境下多元男性氣質的理解，俾能豐富男性氣質與性別建構的跨國度比較。

443111.label: Realisation of objectives
443111.value: The first objective, i.e., to build up a dialogue with existing theories concerning the construction of masculinities, has been well met. This is necessarily so since this objective has been built into the research design from the very start. Ethnography enabled us to acquire rich materials regarding the myriad aspects of the boys’ schooling experience. Focus group interviews were used to gain familiarity with the boys and their concerns, and to gauge their social dynamics and positionalities. Based on these interviews, we were able to move on to individual interviews of boys selected via theoretical sampling, along the lines of social position, gender attributes, academic positions and popularity. Interviews of adults including school principals, teachers, staff and alumni were also conducted in order to help build up a concrete background for analysis. These interviews, particularly those with teachers and alumni, also allowed us to introduce a historical dimension into our study, thus allowing us to gauge the impact of social and economic changes brought about by the advance of global capitalism. Meanwhile, on-site observations and casual conversations with the boys and adults in the school helped us sharpen our analysis of the boys’ verbal responses and observed behavior, apart from generating useful data in themselves. With such a rich corpus of materials, we have ample room to converse with existing theories of different paradigms and at various levels. As for the second and third objectives, we anticipate that they could well be achieved. Again, this is due to the fact that we have been able to collect good quality data on the field. In fact, our research has already aroused the interest of policy-makers, and a meeting with Education Bureau officials is now being scheduled. The strength of ethnography lies in its richness and potential for breaking new theoretical grounds, due to its grounded-ness as well as the highly inductive nature of its analysis, and hence the possibility of surprise discovery. Its “weakness”, if one wants to put it this way, is the notorious amount of labour one has to put into processing and analyzing it. This explains the slowness in writing up (see Part C), and hence in drawing up policy implications (3rd objective) and giving practical advice to parents and practitioners (2nd objective). Fortunately, for academics, analysis and writing-up does not stop with the official “deadline” of the research project.

443111.label: Major findings and research outcome
443111.value: Analysis and writing-up of research findings is still ongoing, so this summary of major findings is a necessarily a tentative one. 1. Masculinities are, indeed, as many theorists have observed, multiple and fluid. Different boys negotiate different modes of masculinities, and these might change over time and vary among different social situations. Indeed, the fluidity is such that it is more appropriate to say that boys “negotiate their gender subjectivities”, a phrase that does more justice to the degree of fluidity as well as the boys’ agency in the process. As for the multiplicity of masculinities, the situation is actually more complex than this phrase, commonly used by theorists in the field, could convey. An attribute that appears to constitute a certain pattern of masculinity to the casual observer are, in fact, used by different boys in different ways. For some boys, this forms the core of their male subjectivities, while for others, it might only be a “ticket” for social acceptance, while they formulate their male subjectivities around other core attributes. 2. Hegemonic masculinity(ies) is a concept that has gained much ground in the field. Our study, however, queries the existence of a clear hierarchy of masculinities among teenage boys in the school context. Instead we find several modes of masculinities co-existing in a crisscross fashion at the school level. While some of them are clearly marginalized and subordinate, others are taken to be equally legitimate, regardless of the different forms they might take. 3. The different, but equally legitimate, forms of masculinities are found to be built on various cultural and social grounds. These include: physical toughness and dexterity, certain traditionally revered forms of Chinese masculinities such as the俠客 (knight-errant), the 書生/才子 (Geng Song [2004] termed it “fragile scholar”), position in the academic hierarchy (which also implies a social hierarchy), and the privileging of math and science in both Western and modern Chinese culture. 4. Social class has a major impact on boys’ negotiations of masculine subjectivities. In brief, boys in our middle class school seem to enjoy much greater room to negotiate their masculine selves. Within this space, they are able to manifest a greater variety of legitimate or acceptable masculinities. Meanwhile, boys in our working class school seem to be much more restricted in this regard, and physical toughness is a more visible, though not exclusive, attribute of acceptable maleness.

443111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
443111.value: This being the first empirical study of teenage masculinities in Chinese societies, it will no doubt inspire studies of similar kind, particularly qualitative and even ethnographic studies like this one. This study involves boys in single-sex schools, and studies done in co-educational schools would make a good comparison regarding how the presence of girls impact on boys’ negotiations of male subjectivities. While class comparison has been built into this study, we were able to study only two schools, so that more studies done with this parameter in mind would definitely broaden and deepen the knowledge about the impact of class on the construction of masculinities in Chinese societies. Another dimension we have not been able to touch on is race and ethnicity, mainly because our sample schools were rather homogenous in this regard. It would be interesting to replicate the study in schools with a greater ethnic and racial mix. On these two dimensions (class and race/ethnicity), as well as that of the need to study boys in a co-educational context, the P.I. is now supervising a PhD student who is doing a similar study which could well supplement this study, thanks to his choice of the site of study.

443111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
443111.value: This study investigates how Chinese teenage boys in Hong Kong acquire their self-image (and presentation to others) as boys or young men. This self-image and presentation necessarily vary among boys in terms of their gender attributes (i.e., how masculine or feminine they appear or behave), social class, academic achievement and degree of popularity. By conducting on-site, participatory study in two schools with different social class backgrounds, we are able to investigate, in their “natural habitats”, how social class shapes the development of boys’ identities. Through group and individual interviews, we are also able to look deeply into their group dynamics, and their inner thoughts and struggles. This study is significant in that it is the first of its kind in Chinese societies, and it will make valuable comparison with similar studies in Western societies. Such comparison will also help us understand how global capitalism, a worldwide trend, shapes boys’ growing up process, and yet how this is being mediated in different cultural settings. On a practical level, this study helps policy-makers, educators and parents to better understand the schooling experiences of boys, and the challenges they face as they grow up as young men in this fast changing world.

443211.label: Project Title(Chinese)
443211.value: 結構突變下Chow-Lin方法之應用

443211.label: Project Objectives
443211.value: Derive the optimal interpolation and extrapolation of high-frequency data in the presence of structural breaks. Examine the multivariate case of more than one series of interest. Examine the case where the contemporary aggregation is allowed. To estimate the break quarter and derive an inference procedure based on the available data.
rows: Derive the optimal interpolation and extrapolation of high-frequency data in the presence of structural breaks.
Examine the multivariate case of more than one series of interest.
Examine the case where the contemporary aggregation is allowed.
To estimate the break quarter and derive an inference procedure based on the available data.

443211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
443211.value: The collection of economic data is costly. Sometimes large sample survey can only be conducted annually, and data of higher frequency, such as quarterly and monthly data, can only be obtained via an indirect approach. An extreme case will be the population census, which is conducted every ten years. Another example is the GDP data at national level, which are only available quarterly and annually, but not monthly. At the provincial level, quarterly data are usually not available. Chow and Lin (1971) developed a method to interpolate and extrapolate the unobserved high frequency data (e.g., quarterly or monthly data) from the observed aggregate data (e.g., annual data). Their method assumes that the unobserved variable has a linear relationship with some observable variables of the same frequency. Chow and Lin (1971) method is still the most widely used method nowadays for data interpolation. However, their method and other methods proposed by the existing studies in the literature assume that this linear relationship is stable. This is unlikely to be the case, especially in a large time series sample, as structural breaks may occur due to policy changes and innovations in technology. The problem of structural break is important in macroeconomic modelling, but it is surprisingly understudied in the Chow-Lin method literature. In light of this, I would like to include structural breaks into the Chow-Lin procedure in this project, and derive the optimal interpolation and extrapolation of economic data in the presence of structural breaks. 收集經濟數據是非常費時費力的。有些時候大型的樣本調查只能每年進行一次，而季度和月度之類的更高頻率的數據隻能通過某些間接手段來獲得。每十年才進行一次的人口普查是一個極端的例子。而在國家層面上的GDP數據則是另一個例子：只有季度和年度GDP數據，而沒有月度數據。通常無法獲得省這一層面的季度GDP。Chow和Lin（1971）提出了一種對已有的總計數據（年度數據）進行插值和外推來獲得未知高頻率數據（季度或月度數據）的辦法。他們假設未知變量與一些同頻率的已知變量之間存在線性關系。Chow和Lin（1971）的方法直到現在仍是數據插值中使用最廣泛的方法。但是他們的方法和現有研究中提出的其它方法都假設這種線性關系是恆定不變的。而事實並非如此，尤其是對時間跨度較大的樣本，因為其間的政策變動和技術革新都會導致結構突變。結構突變問題在宏觀經濟模型中非常重要，但令人驚訝的是在Chow-Lin方法中並沒有對此進行研究。鑒於這點，在這個方案中我向Chow-Lin方法引入結構突變，期望得到存在結構突變時經濟數據最理想的插值和外推。

443211.label: Realisation of objectives
443211.value: This project incorporates structural breaks in the Chow-Lin procedure. The research objective is to derive the optimal disaggregation of the observed aggregate data, allowing for the existence of structural breaks. I have derived the estimation method for the break date and derive an inference procedure based on the observable data. I have shown in this project that the estimate are all consistent. I have derived the optimal optimal disaggregation of data in the presence of structural breaks. I am still workig on the multivariate extension of the model and the contemporary aggregation problem as the problems are complicated than I expected.

443211.label: Major findings and research outcome
443211.value: This project attempts to disaggregate the annual economic data into quarterly and monthly figures in the presence of possible structural breaks in the data. We propose a temporal disaggregation technique with structural break to disaggregate annual economic data. The method allows for structural breaks in unobserved quarterly and monthly economic data. It is able to accommodate underlying instability in economic cycles at both monthly and quarterly levels. It can disaggregate the annual data into quarterly and monthly figures and obtain optimal inferences of unobserved economic states on a high-frequency basis. Our model bridges the gap between temporal disaggregation techniques and structural break models. The estimates of the quarterly and monthly variable allow us to investigate economic questions when data of higher frequency are needed.

443211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
443211.value: For future research along this line, I will allow for multiple structural breaks in the framework. I will also extend the study to the factor model. Finally, I will also look into the problem of missing observations, where only part but not all the quarterly data are missing.

443211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
443211.value: Macroeconometric modeling normally employs a number of time series variables, some of which can only available at low frequency (e.g. annual data) due to high costs of data collection. Sometimes, large sample survey can only be conducted annually, and data of higher frequency, such as quarterly and monthly data, can only be obtained via an indirect approach. An extreme case will be the population census, which is conducted every ten years. Another example is the GDP data at national level, which are only available quarterly and annually. At the provincial level, quarterly data are usually not available. Chow and Lin (1971) proposed a procedure to generate higher frequency estimates from low frequency data. Empirically, structural break is commonly observed in time series sample. The breaks may occur due to policy changes and innovations in technology. Thus far, no attempt has been made to modify the Chow-Lin procedure in the presence of structural breaks. Temporal disaggregation techniques that do not allow for structural break in economic data may lead to unreliable disaggregation of data. It is therefore important to develop a model that can accommodate structural break when performing the temporal disaggregation.

443311.label: Project Title(Chinese)
443311.value: 中國語境下的自由平等政治

443311.label: Project Objectives
443311.value: Justify a conception of justice grounded on freedom and equality. Explore the plausibility of applying politics of liberal equality to China. Review the development of Chinese liberalism in the past three decades. Examine the debate between liberalism and other competing ideologies in the Chinese context. Consider the role of moral motivation and public discourse in political transformation.
rows: Justify a conception of justice grounded on freedom and equality.
Explore the plausibility of applying politics of liberal equality to China.
Review the development of Chinese liberalism in the past three decades.
Examine the debate between liberalism and other competing ideologies in the Chinese context.
Consider the role of moral motivation and public discourse in political transformation.

443311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
443311.value: This project aims to substantiate a Rawlsian liberal theory of justice to interpret and inform China’s social and political modernization. My theory takes freedom and equality as the core values of liberalism. It supports human rights, constitutional democracy, fair equality of opportunity and a comprehensive system of social welfare. Its major ideas stem from John Rawls’s theory of justice. It will argue against unconstrained market capitalism and one-party authoritarian state, and support reform for a liberal democratic welfare state. In order to establish its desirability and feasibility in the Chinese context, the project will offer a critical review of contemporary Chinese liberalism and respond to different challenges from anti-liberal thought, including New Left, Neo-Confucianism and Straussian conservatism. It will argue that the liberal tradition has sufficient moral resources to take social justice, community and culture seriously. The project will also consider the issues of social transformation from a non-ideal situation to a well-ordered just society. Emphasis will be placed on how citizens can develop an effective sense of justice in order to uphold justice itself and participate in social actions. In this connection, the work will discuss the significance of civil society and public reason. The proper relationship between justice and good life in a liberal society will also be explored. Throughout the project, a central principle is that freedom and equality should be the fundamental values that inform China’s social reform. This is a project combining moral justification with conceptual analysis, historical interpretation and empirical social studies. To my knowledge, this project will be the first attempt to develop a Rawlsian liberal conception of justice to understand and inform the political development of China. Its results will shed new light on the current heated debate about which paths China should choose. 此研究計劃將以當代政治哲學家羅爾斯的正義理論作為基礎，探索中國的社會和政治現代化之路。此理論視自由和平等為自由主義核心價值，並支持基本權利、憲政民主、公平的平等機會和廣泛的社會福利。它既反對毫無約束的資本主義制度，也不認同一黨專政的威權體制。為了論證這套理論在中國語境下的可取性和可行性，本計劃會嘗試回應新左派，新儒家和史特勞斯學派對自由主義的批評，並指出自由主義仍然有足夠理論資源去回應社會正義、社群和文化等重要議題。本計劃亦會考慮社會轉型問題，尤其關注如何培養出積極的公民去從事社會變革，因此會特別探究公民社會和公共理性的重要性，以及正義和幸福之間的關係。

443311.label: Realisation of objectives
443311.value: The five objectives have been satisfactorily realized through the completion and publication of Political Morality: From a Liberal Point of View by the Chinese University Press. In this book, I have attempted to justify a theory of liberalism grounded on freedom and equality, and argued for its desirability and feasibility for China’s political reform. I discussed a number of liberal thinkers’ political thought, including Isaiah Berlin, F. A. Hayek, Robert Nozick and John Rawls. I also compared liberalism with libertarianism, Confucianism and communitarianism, and showed their moral differences in dealing with different political issues. Finally, I studied the role of moral motivation in public justification, and showed how political morality is necessary and possible for the legitimate exercise of state power. It is fair to say that the objectives set in the research plan have been substantially achieved.

443311.label: Major findings and research outcome
443311.value: There are following major findings in this project. Firstly, I argue that the legitimacy of state power must be made sense of and justified by a conception of political morality through a process of reflective endorsement by free and rational beings. This idea of legitimacy is fundamentally different from Weber’s belief theory and social contract tradition. Secondly, I justify a conception of liberalism which takes both freedom and equality seriously and differentiates itself from libertarianism which has dominated the liberal discourse over the past three decades in China. Thirdly, I apply this conception of liberalism to deal with a range of issues, including social justice, democracy, toleration and multiculturalism, and show its moral superiority over competing political theories. Fourthly, I challenge Berlin’s famous distinction between negative and positive liberty, and argue that the importance of the former can only be justified by appeal to the latter. Fifthly, I argue that there is a very close conceptual connection between money and freedom, which would in turn fundamentally undermine a libertarian notion that in a capitalist society the rich and the poor enjoy equal freedom. Finally, I suggest that the liberalism I defended can offer the most reasonable direction for China’ political reform. The above research findings are all collected in my monograph Political Morality: from a Liberal Point of View (Hong Kong: the Chinese University Press, 2014). This book has been highly acclaimed as an original and important work by senior scholars in the discipline, including Prof. Joseph CHAN, Jiwei CI and Sinchi KUAN. It has been reviewed by academic journals and intellectual magazines. It was also a focus of discussion in a conference called “Left-liberalism and China: Idea and Practice” held at CUHK in 2014.

443311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
443311.value: I am now undertaking two projects based on the current research. The first is to produce a monograph on freedom. The aim is to develop a theory of freedom that can integrate negative and positive freedom, social justice and democracy into a coherent political system grounded on a conception of personal autonomy. The second is concerned with the issue of political legitimacy. I attempt to develop a different approach to make sense of the issue of political legitimacy in modern society and then examine what kind of moral reasons can justify the legitimate use of political power.

443311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
443311.value: The project aims to answer a question many people are deeply concerned about, namely, where China should go if the existing one-party authoritarian state is politically unsustainable and morally undesirable. My answer is we should go for a liberal democratic regime. This regime supports equal basic rights and liberties, representative democracy, fair equality of opportunity for education and social competition, market economy, and redistribution of wealth and high level of social welfare. This is a liberal project inspired by John Rawls, the most important political philosopher of 20th century. This position is fundamentally different from socialism, libertarianism, Confucianism and authoritarianism. That is perhaps why my articles have attracted many responses and caused heated debate over the past three years. To my knowledge, there are at least 35 reviews on my argument and countless discussion and sharing on social network such as Weibo and Facebook. My book Political Morality: from a Liberal Point of View was sold 6000 copies in half a year. This is probably a record for an academic political philosophy book in Hong Kong. It is also one of the most read and cited books during the Umbrella Movement.

443511.label: Project Title(Chinese)
443511.value: 信息不对称与杠杆收购融资结构

443511.label: Project Objectives
443511.value: Test if higher informational opacity of targets firms require greater equity contribution by private equity firms in leveraged buyout transactions. More specifically, using target firms’ listing status, size, distance from the lenders, the number of analysts following, and research and development spending as measures of information opacity, we test if private equity firms sponsoring the transactions provide more equity when target firms face higher uncertainty.

More specifically, using target firms’ listing status, size, distance from the lenders, the number of analysts following, and research and development spending as measures of information opacity, we test if private equity firms sponsoring the transactions provide more equity when target firms face higher uncertainty.

443511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
443511.value: Aim The aim of this project is to conduct research into how information asymmetry between private equity firms and lenders affects the financing structure of leveraged buyouts. Project Background A leveraged buyout is the acquisition of a target business by private equity firms using debt to finance a large portion of the purchase price. In a leveraged buyout, a private equity firm has to decide how much its own equity to invest and how much debt to borrow to acquire a target business. Private equity firms gather information about the target company through a due diligence process prior to the buyout, and they are also responsible for the monitoring, governing, and restructuring of the target firm after the buyout. However, the quality of the investments by the private equity firms and the monitoring efforts that the private equity firms exert are not readily observable to the lenders. Hence, there is asymmetric information between the private equity firms and the lenders. Theory on agency and moral hazard implies that an informed agent with monitoring responsibilities should obtain a large ownership of a project when the informed agent’s efforts are not observable by the uninformed principal. Put differently, when an investment project faces more informational opacity and requires more intense monitoring effort, lenders will demand greater “skin in the game” by the informed borrower to mitigate agency costs associated with moral hazard. Therefore, theories imply that when a target firm of a leveraged buyout requires more due diligence and monitoring effort, the private equity firm will have to retain a larger portion of the purchase price, i.e. contribute more equity by using less debt to finance the buyout. Brief Project Description We will test this prediction using detailed financing structure of leveraged buyout transactions in the U.S. from 1997 to 2010. We expect that when a target firm is a privately held firm, distant from lenders, smaller in size, followed by a lesser number of analysts, and R&D intensive, private equity firms sponsoring the transactions should provide more equity. Significance of Project This study will not only further our understanding of the determinants of the financial structure of leveraged buyouts but also provide empirical evidence affirming the importance of information problems in financial transactions. 研究目标：该项目的研究目标是对私募基金公司和贷款人之间的信息不对称问题如何影响杠杆收购中的融资结构进行研究。 项目背景：杠杆收购指私募基金公司通过债务融资偿付大部分购买价格从而收购目标公司。在杠杆收购中，私募基金公司必须决定投入多少自身股本、借贷多少债务来收购目标公司。私募基金公司在收购前进行尽职调查以获得关于目标公司的信息，并在收购后负责监控、治理、重组目标公司。然而，要观察私募基金公司的投资质量和监控力度对贷款人来讲并不容易。因此，私募基金公司和贷款人之间存在不对称的信息。代理理论和道德风险理论意味着当不知情的委托人无法观察到知情的代理人的努力时，承担监控责任的知情代理人应当大量持有项目的所有权。换言之，当一个项目面临更多的信息不透明问题、需要更强的监控力度时，贷款人会要求知情的借款人投入更多资金以减少同道德风险相关的代理成本。所以，理论说明在杠杆收购的目标公司需要更多尽职调查、更多监控的情况下，私募基金公司不得不自己负担更大一部分购买价格，也就是说，使用更多的股权融资、更少的债务融资进行收购。 项目简介：我们将利用美国1997年到2010年期间的杠杆收购案的详细融资结构对以上预测进行测试。我们预期如果目标公司是私有公司、远离贷款人、规模较小、有较少分析师跟踪研究、密集从事科研开发的话，赞助其交易的私募基金公司应提供更多股权融资。 项目意义：这项研究不仅将深化我们对杠杆收购融资结构的决定因素的认识，而且会为确认信息不对称问题在金融交易中的重要性提供经验证据。

443511.label: Realisation of objectives
443511.value: The project was transferred from my former CUHK colleague Ji-Woong Chung to me in early 2013. Ji-Woong joined Korean University as an Assistant Professor and we don't have any on-going collaborating projects. As the idea and the proposal was developed by Ji-Woong, I decided to differentiate from his proposal by doing a highly relevant yet also different project. Specifically, I explore how the change in information asymmetry affects the financing structure of the firms (not the LBO deals in the original proposal) using a natural experimental setting to build up the identification. In the original proposal, information opacity was proxied by some firm characteristics (geographical distance, R&D spending, etc.) and hence the endogeneity problem is not easy to address. Hence, from a methodology perspective, this study also makes a big improvement from the original proposal. Moreover, this study specifically explores firms' choice between public debt and private debt, which sheds important light on the significant change of the debt financing structure in U.S. (i.e. firms become much more reliant on bond financing). Specifically, using brokerage mergers and closures as natural experiments, we examine how exogenous change in information environment affects firms’ choice between bank debt and public debt. Our difference-in-differences approach shows that exogenous increase in information asymmetry makes firms to substitute away from public debt to bank debt. The finding is consistent with theoretical literature that public bondholders, compared with banks, are more sensitive to information asymmetry problems. Importantly, this paper directly tests the underlying assumption behind the theoretical framework by documenting an instantaneous negative bond market reaction and an insignificant change in bank loan spread. We also document that the impact of change in information environment on firms’ debt choice is more pronounced for firms with low initial analyst coverage, with high assets substitution risk, and with low quality of corporate governance. Although the budget was transferred to me in early 2013, we've made sincere and substantial efforts in developing the idea, reviewing the literature, compiling the very comprehensive debt structure database, designing the empirical strategies based on natural experiments and writing up the paper. The paper has been presented in many major research universities such as Chinese University of Hong Kong, HKUST, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics. We received many constructive comments and revised the paper accordingly. The paper is under review at the top finance journal Review of Financial Studies.

443511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
443511.value: According to the Flow of Funds data from the Federal Reserve System, new debt issuance has become the predominantly important source of corporate financing over the past decade. Moreover, the data indicate a significant change of the debt composition and secular increase in public bond financing. Using a natural experiment setting, we explore whether the change in corporate information environment is one plausible explanation to this pattern. Intuitively, when the information asymmetry increases (decreases), firms should substitute away from more (less) information-sensitive debt instruments toward less (more) information sensitive ones. banks have superior access to private information of borrowers and are better informed about the future prospects of the borrowers than public debt investors (Fama 1985, James and Smith, 2000). Therefore, relative to bondholders, banks have a comparative advantage in pricing the securities of firms with greater information opacity and are less sensitive to the public information changes. Our difference-in-differences approach shows that exogenous increase in information asymmetry makes firms to substitute away from public debt to bank debt. This evidence suggests that one plausible reason firms use more public debt is the improvement of information environment in recent years.

443611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
443611.value: 研究摘要 本研究的目的是要探討建築在城市製造過程中在香港文化想像上所扮演的重要角色，特别是與電影的對等關係。中環和油麻地，兩個具有豐富歷史，文物，文化生活和社區動態的舊城區，被選作研究範例，讓本研究可更深入理解城市內的日常文化生態演變的性質。 本研究將在這兩區進行都市形態及體驗的跨學科考察，結合具體城市形態與文化新陳代謝的實證紀錄，以及對描繪這兩區的電影作出詮釋性分析。城市好比一個文化複雜性的容器，而本研究會探索城市轉變在建築尺度上與文化論述的凝聚，以及通過電影中的故事敘事與拍攝場景間有序的相互影響去探討城市如何被記憶、體驗與想像。 通過研究建築（都市情景的具體衡量）和電影（幻覺形象）之間的根本張力就香港城市蛻變如何介導，本研究一個更廣泛的目標，是推測這範疇的研究工作如何能進一步開拓掌握多變的城市真實的可能性，並希望在當代文化思維下的城市秩序問題作出貢獻。

443611.label: Major findings and research outcome
443611.value: The research allowed the testing, refinement and elaboration of how to document empirical urban morphology and metabolism within an area. For Central’s Graham Street market area in particular, how the urban form together with its modern vernacular architecture plays a key role in giving spatio-physical dimensions to urban culture with respect to the richness of experience has been recorded in the two journal articles in 2013 and 2014. What it proves is that the scale of those ladder-street urban blocks allows sufficient concentration and differentiation in architectural constituents to reveal the rich tapestry of urban settings. In between the Graham Street and Wing Lee street, the research team discovered another type of perimeter block sitting on a slope that still harbours a rough metabolism within Central that offers a great opportunity for documentation, and further exploration of Central as a place of diverse gathering and exchange, before being replaced. Yaumatei is also a similar story that requires further attention, as the threat of the new ‘Central Kowloon’ tunnel connection to west Kowloon construction will definitely cause much urban upheaval. Thus on physical metabolism alone, there is much work to be done within the study area, not to mention other similar areas in Hong Kong facing urban renewal. As for mappings of filmic narrations with physical urban sites, again it is a fruitful exercise with much more rewards to come. Again to give the Central example, the filmed scenes of ladder streets (north-south hill to harbour) against those running east-west parallel contours show the richness of possibilities to connect physical infrastructure and dwellings with experiential connectedness versus interiority and alienation (more psychological) – linking place with plot that yields new understandings of Central’s urbanity. The Central Escalator further adds several layers of spatial complexity. (see conference papers) (Yaumatei’s street grid is also similar but without elevated walkways and slope, but more heritage monuments and density) While detailed analysis of scenes with filmic techniques may demonstrate the interconnected presences of ‘city in film’ and ‘film in city’ (such as in Wong Kar-Wai’s Chungking Express, or Fruit Chan’s Little Cheung), it is important to always refer to the actual urban settings to remember the gap between imagination and reality, that which allows both architects, filmakers and public to grasp the multi-perspective understandings of the city that one must be open to.

443611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
443611.value: This research studied how architecture and buildings make and remake the city and its culture through the years. In Hong Kong, we chose older districts in Central and Yaumatei as they also contain the richest history and heritage, and continue to be a lively place full of everyday culture. After studying old maps, photos, building plans and doing field survey to understand the areas’ physical changes, we watched local movies to find out how those same places have been filmed by different directors to tell different stories. Unlike architecture, which is mute, films have a powerful effect by recording past scenes or bring a place to life with sound and light, characters and stories in a life-like way. Comparing the actual architecture and city spaces with movie narratives shot on location, from larger scale neighbourhoods, urban blocks, streets to buildings and indoor sequences, we get the complete picture of how ‘plot’ connects with ‘place’, how real and imagined film scenes together gives us the full temperament or situational ambience of a place. Telling the architectural and filmic histories of a place together help both architects and the public to appreciate and imagine more vividly the life possible in our rapidly changing city.

443911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
443911.value: With tariffs and quotas becoming increasingly less important as the main trade barriers, the focus of the international trade community has shifted to non-tariff regulations that exist ‘behind the border’, especially heterogeneous product standards enacted by different countries purportedly for various social regulation purposes. To curtail the adverse effects of divergent product standards on international trade, a sophisticated GATT/WTO legal framework was concluded at the end of the Uruguay Round, imposing a range of disciplines on WTO Members in setting national product standards. The WTO's shift in focus toward regulating behind-the-border product standards has profound implications to WTO Members’ domestic regulatory processes, the consumers’ consumption choices in a globalizing world and to the WTO itself. On the one hand, there are protectionist elements at force in setting domestic trade policies and product standards may be contrived to shield domestic production from import competition. A failure to seriously consider the existence of covert protectionism undermines the integrity of international trade disciplines and provides a ready means of cheating with impunity. On the other hand, product standards are frequently set to protect important social values of the highest level such as human health and safety, consumer welfare and environment. From a WTO Member's perspective, the power to set product standards is inherent and inseparable for any democratic and accountable government and is at the social and political heart of their sovereignty. A broad intrusion into WTO Members' regulatory autonomy might place undue limits on non-protectionist regulatory processes and bring the WTO in direct conflict with domestic democracy. Indeed, the perception that the WTO has unreasonably constrained the ability of democratic communities to make unfettered choices about policies that affect the fundamental welfare of their citizens has generated much hostility towards the WTO and represents one of the most serious threats facing the international trade regime. This project intends to answer one fundamental question: to what extent should the WTO penetrate into the domestic regulatory order in the realm of product standards? Firstly, I will provide a comprehensive and detailed analysis of how product standards are regulated under GATT/WTO law. Secondly, I will evaluate to what extent the WTO has constrained WTO Members’ autonomy in setting product standards and whether such constraints are justified. Thirdly and finally, I will explore the policy implications of different approaches in balancing trade liberalization obligations and WTO Members's regulatory autonomy within the GATT/WTO framework. 随着关税和进出口配额逐渐不再是主要的国际贸易壁垒，国际贸易界的焦点转移到了国家内部的非关税管制制度上来，尤其是为了社会管理目的而实施的不同的产品标准。为了消减不同的产品标准给国际贸易带来的负面影响，世界贸易组织的成员方在乌拉圭回合结束的时候建立了一个复杂的法律体系，为世界贸易组织成员方政府制定国内产品标准制定了一系列的法律规则。 然而，世界贸易组织对其成员方内部的产品标准进行管制对其成员方内部的管制制度，消费者在一个全球化世界中的选择以及世界贸易组织本身带来了极为深远的影响。一方面，保护主义的幽灵在国内贸易政策中仍然存在，产品标准会被巧妙设计，从而对国内产业免遭进口产品的竞争进行保护。如果对这种隐藏的贸易保护主义没有严肃的考虑，则多边贸易纪律会遭到削弱，同时也提供了一种背离贸易纪律而不受到惩罚的方法。从另一个方面考虑， 产品标准的制定目的往往是为了保护一些极为重要的社会价值，例如国民的健康和安全， 消费者福利和环境保护。从世界贸易组织成员方的角度来看， 制定产品标准的权力是一个负责任民主政府内在的，不可分割的权力之一。实质上，这种权力是国家主权最核心的部分。对一个主权政府的管制自主权进行大幅度的干预有可能会对成员方非基于保护主义的管制施加不适当的限制，同时亦使世界贸易组织和成员方的国内民主程序发生直接冲突。在现实中已经产生了这一认识，即世界贸易组织不合理的限制了其成员方不受任何限制的选择影响市民根本福利的政策的能力。这一认识带来了对世界贸易组织的许多敌意。这也是世界贸易体系面临的最大威胁之一。这一认识同时也对世界贸易组织的合法性提出了质疑。 本项目旨在回答一个根本性的问题，即世界贸易组织的法律规则应该在何种程度内对国内产品标准的管制秩序进行干预？我将首先对世界贸易组织法如何管制国际贸易中的产品标准进行完整详细的法律分析；其次，我会讨论世界贸易组织法在何种程度上对世贸成员方政府制定产品标准的自主权进行了限制，以及这些限制是否合理。最后，我将对平衡贸易自由化和成员方政府管制自由的各种途径的政策意义进行探讨。

443911.label: Realisation of objectives
443911.value: The first three objectives have been achieved fully. I have examined how product standards are regulated under the GATT 1994, the TBT and the SPS Agreement. By examining both the WTO Agreements and the case law, I have provided an up-to-date and critical analysis of both the legal rules and the WTO court's interpretation of the legal rules. This analysis has provided a solid foundation for the last three objectives. The objectives 4, 5 and 6 have also been successfully achieved. I compared the EU case law to the WTO case law to see if the WTO has exceeded its mandate and become a global mega-regulator as many people suggested. I explored the different approaches that the WTO panels have adopted in balancing trade liberalization and national regulatory autonomy and the policy implications of such approaches. I also tried to relate the project to some fundamental themes in public internation law. For example, the project is an integral part of the scholarship on the allocation of power between sovereign states and international organizations, or the clash between ‘sovereignty’ and ‘globalization'. Another example is that many product standards setters in international trade are non-governmental entities. This project discusses how these NGOs set up product standards and the legitimacy of such product standards setting. This analyais is instrumental to the more broader topic of the place of non-state actors in international law. Admittedly, more could be done on objectives 4, 5 and 6. These objectives were set very broadly in the project proposal and the PI is reluctant to claim that these objectives have been achieved 'fully'. For example, the EU has a complicated regulatory system for product standards (including product eco-labels etc). Due to time constraints, the PI could not conduct a full analysis of all the relevant EU law and regulations. Instead, the PI only selected the issues that are most relevant to the main research question of this project. In addition, other than sovereignty and globalization, non-state actors and constitutionalization of international economic law, this project is also related to other more general PIL themes. Again, it is not realistic for the PI to conduct a thorough discussion of all relevant general PIL themes. Still, the PI is m satisfied that the most important questions closely related to this research project have been thoroughly addressed.

443911.label: Major findings and research outcome
443911.value: The GATT/WTO regime has incorporated a sophisticated toolkit to tackle the underlying tension between trade liberalization and domestic regulatory autonomy. These tools include the national treatment principle, weighing and balancing test, international standards, scientific evidence, permission for precautionary action, internal regulatory consistency, the least trade restrictive test and standard of review. I analyzed how these legal tools are interpreted by WTO tribunals in dealing with various categories of product standards (e.g., mandatory/voluntary; government/private and non-product-related production and process methods). In answering the central research question of this project: to what extent has GATT/WTO intruded into its Members’ domestic regulatory autonomy? I put forward four major findings. First, in a globalized world, it is not possible to delineate a clear contour for the 'sovereignty sphere'. The only feasible way is to assess the scope of domestic regulatory autonomy under the WTO Agreements by closely reading the WTO case law and to analyze its policy implications. My research further showes that to a very large extent it is unjustified to claim that the WTO has inappropriately intruded into WTO Members' domestic regulatory order. Second, despite textural and structural differences between the GATT, the TBT and the SPS Agreement, a jurisprudential cross-fertilization amongst the three Agreements has happened to the extent that, an emerging consistent approach has been developed in the WTO law in adjudicating the legality of product standards as well as in balancing trade and non-trade values. Third, in balancing free trade and the right to regulate, the GATT/WTO case law has oscillated between phases of varying severity and modesty. On the surface, the interpretive cycles may be explained by different interpretative methods. At a deeper level, however, the interpretative oscillation is due to a fundamental confusion of the purpose of the WTO. Fourth, the recent WTO case law has pointed to a growing consensus that the WTO epitomizes an anti- discrimination model, as opposed to a regulatory model. As a result, the early domestic regulatory autonomy unfriendly approach has been replaced by a more deferential approach which is far more respectful of domestic regulatory autonomy. This trend is illustrated, inter alia, by the partial resurrection of aim and effects test under Article III, a more nuanced weighing and balancing test under Article XX of the GATT and a much more deferential standard of review under the SPS Agreement. In view of these recent developments, it may be argued that the respect for domestic regulatory autonomy has come back with stronger force to the GATT/WTO system.

443911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
443911.value: The project has analyzed all the WTO case law on product standards to date and made some bold and potentially contentious conclusions. One further development of the research is to keep tracking the new WTO cases and to predict the likely outcomes of the disputes by referring to the conclusions drawn from this project. This exercise is very useful in testing the validity of the conclusions of this research project. The second possible development is to further theorize the concluisons of this research project by exploring the changing political, economic and philosophical foundations of the GATT/WTO system. Possible questions for further research include: why did the GATT/WTO tribunals interprete the same texts differently in different times? How were these interpretations influenced by the prevailing political economy ideas at different times? To answer these questions, it is essential to move beyond the legal texts and case law to international political economy. I will try to familiarize myself with the relevant IPE work on the GATT/WTO system (especially how ideas shape the current legal rules) and work with an IPE scholar to deal with these new questions.

443911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
443911.value: Increasingly, the focus of WTO law has shifted from tariff barriers at the national borders to heterogeneous product standards that exist ‘behind the border’. This shifting focus of the WTO law has profound implications to both Member States’ domestic regulatory process and the WTO. Frequently states set product standards to protect important social values of the highest level such as human health and safety, consumer welfare and environment protection.How should the GATT/WTO regime regulate heterogeneous product standards as potential trade barriers behind the borders of WTO members, whilst striking a proper balance between trade liberalization and domestic regulatory autonomy? As the WTO has admitted, this is one of the most fundamental questions facing the international trade law community and may represent one of the most serious threats to the GATT/WTO regime. This research project explores the interaction between global economic governance and national regulatory autonomy through the lens of WTO's regulation of heterogeneous product standards. The project is both practically and theoretically valuable. Practically, it offers the first comprehensive analysis of WTO's regulation of product standards in international trade. Theoretically, it contributes to the arguably the most important debate of our times: how does economic globalization affect the national sovereignty?

444111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
444111.value: Ownership structure plays critical roles in incentives and behaviors within organizations. Prior literature has linked firm ownership structures to conflicts between owners and managers. More recent family firm research has focused on conflicts between controlling family blockholders and minority shareholders. We extend this literature by examining the roles of ownership structure within a controlling family. Through marriages and having children, controlling families will grow large and complex and family ownership of firms tend to diffuse within the family. We examine whether or not intra-family ownership structure plays a role in family firm performance, investment, growth, and payout policies. Specifically, we focus on a family trust structure that is a popular vehicle for holding family ownership in many economies around the world. As will be discussed in this proposal, the trust structure locks controlling ownership within a family, but the lack of transferability of the ownership also make family disputes difficult to resolve. We propose to employ publicly traded family firms in Hong Kong as our sample, because the prevalence of both the trust and non-trust ownership structures facilitates our empirical tests. In doing so, we contribute new insights to the literature of family firms and ownership structures. Our research will help family firm owners, their managers and consultants in establishing better ownership structure and corporate governance. 股權結構於企業激勵和行為上扮演重要的角色。前文獻將公司股權結構與股東和經理人之間的衝突聯繫起來。近代的家族企業研究多重點討論家族股東和小股東的矛盾。我們則進一步探討控股家族內部股權結構所產生的影響。通過婚姻和生育子女，控股家族的結構變得龐大和複雜，家族的控股權亦漸漸分散。我們主要研究家族內部的控股結構會否影響家族企業的表現以及其投資、發展及股利政策。我們將重點探討家族信託。家族信託是一個普遍於多個經濟體系的家族控股工具。雖然家族信託可以集中家族控股權，但由於家族成員一般不能轉讓信託股權，家族糾紛因此難以解決。本研究將以在香港上市的家族企業作為樣本，其家族內部的持股方式可分為家族信託及非家族信託(例如直接持股)，有助我們分析兩者之差異及影響。本研究為家族企業和股權結構的文獻帶來新觀點，並能幫助家族成員、經理人和管理顧問設計及建立更優良的股權結構和公司管治制度。

444111.label: Realisation of objectives
444111.value: After several years of effort, we have put together a unique database of family and ownership structure for more than 200 family firms in Hong Kong. We spent one more year to understand and analyze the data, and finally fully addressed all the objectives stated in the grant proposal. In addition, we discovered interesting pattern between family trust adoption and founding family sibling number and gender structures, and how the family structure shape the governance and management of family firms. We have reported these results in two separate papers. Overall, the project has taken much longer to complete than our expectation, mainly because of the difficulty of collecting necessary data for empirical tests. However, we are confident that we will be able to publish the papers in good international journals. We are in process of presenting the papers in seminars and international conferences, and submitting the papers to journals.

444111.label: Major findings and research outcome
444111.value: We study a family trust structure that is a popular vehicle for holding family ownership around the world. The trust structure typically locks controlling ownership within a family for a very long period. Although ensuring family control, the share transfer restriction potentially induces family shirking problems, makes family conflict difficult to resolve, and distorts firm decisions. Based on almost 200 publicly traded family firms in Hong Kong, we report that trust controlled firms subject to high family conflict potential tend to pay higher dividends, invest less on the long term, and experience worse performance during difficult times, compared with firms owned directly by family members. In addition, we find that there is a non-linear relationship between number of founder’s children (particularly sons) and the probability of using trust. This implies that there is a tradeoff in optimizing control benefits and the cost of conflicts. Families considering internal conflict potential when choosing their ownership structures do not suffer from such distortions. We also find that there are more professional managers in the board when a family uses trust, indicating that these firms strategically use firm governance to mitigate the costs of using trust ownership.

444111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
444111.value: We believe that it is highly valuable to study detailed terms and conditions of a set of trust deeds. For example, we could investigate if trust deeds or associated documents incorporate terms that prevent various means of asset exploitation, decision making mechanisms, and conditions for family members to enter/exit the trust beneficiary list. This study would require collaboration from trust service providers and may require questionnaire or interveiw methodology if actual trust deeds are not available. Another important topic is whether and how trust adopting families implement family governance mechanisms to prevent family conflicts and/or their effects. Typical mechanisms include family boards, family funds serving various family needs including charity, family employment policy, etc.

444111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
444111.value: Family trust is commonly used for holding assets including business ownership. The trust structure protects assets from events such as divorce, bankruptcy, taxation, and hostile takeovers. However, it also lowers family beneficiaries' incentives to manage and invest the assets for the long term, while inducing short-term behavior such as paying high dividends or even tunnelling of assets. These distortions become more serious when family members are no longer in harmony. When family relationship turns sour, family members cannot exit their situations by selling off their shares under the trust structure. The lack of exit channel of the trust structure can prolong family conflicts and worsen firm decision efficiency and value. The research not only contributes to the academic literature of ownership structure but also provides pursuasive evidence to practitioners and business owners contemplating about ownership design.

444411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
444411.value: Environmental changes such as global warming, degradation of vegetation cover, soil erosion and desertification are key issues of environmental protection and sustainable development that need to be rigorously analyzed and monitored. Land use and land cover change has been reckoned a key driver of such changes. The classification of land covers and the detection of their changes have thus been important research problems in the analysis of remotely sensed images. Successful extraction of appropriate features from remote sensing data plays a crucial role in classification and change analysis. Since remotely sensed images can be captured at different levels of resolution, the effect of scale on feature extraction has to be analyzed. Differing from the conventional methods, the fractal approach treats remotely sensed images as fractals that are scale invariant, resolution and observer independent. The concept of fractal dimension has thus been successfully employed for classification and change detection. However, remotely sensed images are generally too complex to be characterized by one single fractal dimension. They generally display different patterns on different scales, with some being more dominant on one scale but less dominant on the other scales. Hence, feature extraction over a wide range of scales needs to be rigorously studied. The purpose of the proposed project is to construct a framework within which novel methods will be developed for multi-scale feature extraction in remote sensing data. Textural features such as the complexity and roughness of images measured by the fractal dimension, and spatial-metrics features such as long-range correlation quantified by the Hurst exponent will be extensively analyzed within one unified framework. In particular, two-dimensional multifractal methods will be developed to handle noise, trends and non-stationarity in vector-valued remotely sensed data, to uncover appropriate scale ranges for various surfaces, to identify hot spots, and to discover crossover scales for the identification of regimes/regions of distinct degrees of complexity. Multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis (MF-DFA) will be extended to the two-dimensional (2D) space by novel methods to extract global features of the entire remotely sensed image, and local features for individual land covers will be extracted by local MF-DFA method. A powerful software system will also be constructed for databases management, algorithms implementation and results visualization. The theory and the system will be applied to two real-life land cover classification and change analysis problems. The proposed study will advance the research frontier and practical applications of feature extraction in remotely sensed images. 環境的變化，比如全球變暖、植被覆蓋退化、土壤侵蝕和沙漠化等問題，是環境保護和可持續發展中的所面臨的關鍵性議題。同時，這些問題也是非常值得我們對其進行精細的分析和監測的。導致上述環境變化的一個關鍵因素是土地利用和土地覆蓋的變化。因此，土地覆蓋的分類和變化監測已經成為了遙感圖像分析里的一個重要研究問題。而為了進行相關的分類和變化分析，成功的從遙感圖像里提取出合適的特徵就變得至關重要。因為我們能夠在不同層次的分辨率上獲得遙感圖片，所以尺度因素在特徵提取里的影響也成為了一個必須考慮的問題。不同於傳統的方法，分形方法在處理遙感圖像時是將其作為一個具有分形特性的研究對象來對待的。這些分形特性包括，尺度不變性以及對分辨率和觀察者的獨立性。在既有的研究中，分形維數的概念已經被成功地引入到了分類和變化檢測的應用中。然而，在大多數情況下，遙感圖像都是十分複雜的，以至於不能被單一的分形維數來完整地刻畫。通常來說，遙感圖像在不同的尺度上會表現出不同的模式，其中一些模式在某一個尺度下會表現得十分顯著，但是在其他一些尺度下就表現得相對微弱。因此，如何在一個較大的尺度范圍上進行特徵提取進行精細的討論就變得十分必要。這份建議書的目的就是希望能夠建立和發展一個研究框架來釆用一些新的方法對遙感數據進行多尺度特徵提取。在這個整合的分析框架內，我們將詳盡地分析和學習紋理特徵和空間度量特徵，比如用分形維數來度量的圖像的復雜度和粗糙度，以及Hurst指數來量化的長程相關性。特別地，我們將著重發展二維的多重分形方法。這些方法將被用來處理包含噪音，趨勢和具有非平穩性的向量值遙感數據；發現適用於各種表面分析的尺度范圍；確定熱點；以及用來識別交叉尺度以確定那些有不同於複雜度的區域。多重分形漲落分析（Multifractal Detrended Fluctuation Analysis (MF-DFA)）將通過一些新穎的方法被推廣到二維空間從而提取整個遙感圖像的全局特徵。於此同時，各種土地覆蓋類型的局部特徵也將會通過局部的MF-DFA提取。同時，我們將建立一個有效的軟件系統來實現數據庫管理，算法實施以及結果的可視化。上述的理論和軟件系統將會被應用到兩個實際的土地分類和變化分析的問題中。我們希望通過對所提出的問題的學習和研究，能夠對遙感圖像特徵提取的前沿研究方向和實際應用兩個方面都有所裨益。

444411.label: Realisation of objectives
444411.value: The project was conducted by the investigators with the assistance of two post-doctoral fellows, Dr. Deyu Meng and Dr. Yu Zhou together with a Ph.D. student, Miss Jie Xue. Dr. Meng and Dr. Yu worked with the investigators in conceptual development of feature extraction with multifractal analysis. Dr. Meng came for a short period of time and was succeeded by Dr. Zhou. Miss Xue is jointly supervised by Professors Fung and Leung, PI and Co-I of the project. She focuses on works related to the development of Spatial Temporal Bayesian data fusion method in handling multi-scale remotely sensed images. Under this research project, four journal papers (1 published, 2 under review and 1 will be submitted later) plus a conference paper are produced. 1. Zhou, Y., T. Fung and Y. Leung, 2016, Improved triangular prism methods for fractal analysis of remotely sensed images, Computers & Geosciences, 90: 64. 2. Zhou, Y., Y. Leung, T. Fung and L. Liu, 2017, Laws of urban growth by nighttime light, Annals of the Association of American Geographers, submitted, in revision. 3. Xue, J., Y. Leung, T. Fung, 2017a, The Bayesian data fusion approach to spatio-temporal fusion of remotely sensed images, IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing, submitted, in revision. 4. Xue, J., Y. Leung, T. Fung, 2017b, An improved Bayesian data fusion method by combining an unmixing-based algorithm for spatial and temporal remote sensing image fusion in complex heterogeneous landscapes, (paper to be submitted for consideration of publication in an international journal) 5. Xue, J. Y. Leung and T. Fung, 2015, The Bayesian Data Fusion Approach to Spatial and Temporal Fusion of Remotely Sensed Images, Poster Presentation at the 2015 American Geophysical Union (AGU) Fall Meeting, San Francisco. The Ph.D. candidate trained, Miss, Jie Xue, plans to submit her thesis in August, 2017. The project objectives are achieved. The followings are actual research works related to the six objectives. 1. We have constructed a feature extraction framework to effectively apply the fractal dimension to better characterize the texture information on remotely sensed images (Zhou et al., 2016). In addition, we have developed a Bayesian framework for the fusion of multi-scale remotely sensed images to obtain images which are high in both spatial and temporal resolutions (Xue et al., 2017a). This approach is able to capture the spatial and temporal correlation among images with different scales. It also enables us to efficiently handle the noise in the corresponding model and monitor the trends in the extraction of features in high resolution remotely sensed images under noise. 2. One existing fractal methods, namely the triangular prism method, has been rigorously examined. Furthermore, the method has been improved by our introduction of three different algorithms (Zhou et al., 2016). It is demonstrated that the existing algorithm may overestimate the fractal dimension in real-life cases and can only be applicable to images with specific sizes. Our proposed algorithms overcome both drawbacks and therefore can provide more reliable results and wider applications. 3. We have theoretically generalized the traditional 2D MF-DFA to the version for the vector-valued images. Different distances between two vectors have been employed and compared (paper under preparation). In addition, we have developed a fractal method which is demonstrated to be more insensitive to the noises in the images (Zhou et al. 2016). 4. We have proposed two enhanced spatio-temporal Bayesian data fusion approaches, which can fully extract possible information from the images under different scales with the help of unmixing-based algorithms. Unmixing-based algorithms are helpful in extracting details of features, leading to a good performance on the characterization of the land surface dynamics under fine scales. The developed approaches prove to be accurate in the monitoring of phenology variations and land-cover changes in a unified way, especially in heterogeneous regions. (Xue et al., 2017b) 5. The improved triangular prism methods have been applied to two real-life examples for uncovering the scaling information. The relevant codes of the algorithms have also been released with the publication of the paper (Zhou et al., 2016). In addition, the remotely sensed images have been employed to define cities and furthermore examine two fundamental laws of urban growth, namely the Zipf’s law and Gibrat’s law (Zhou et al., 2017). This study uncovers the relationship between two laws at different scales of cities. Also, the consistent results can be found in the study of changes in city ranks. 6. The improved performance of the proposed algorithms of the triangular prism method can be observed in two real-life remotely sensed images. It has also been shown that the proposed algorithms are more insensitive to the noises and can better uncover the land uses, such as roads and buildings (Zhou et al., 2016); as well as complex urban fringe where rapid industrial and residential development are replacing cropland, woodland and water bodies.

444411.label: Major findings and research outcome
444411.value: Feature extraction is important to ascertain the rich dimension inherent in remote sensing images which are multispectral, multi-spatial and multi-temporal. Fractal feature is a natural characterization of complex objects across scales. We extended the modified triangular prism (MTP) method for the estimation of fractal dimensions of remotely sensed image, taking into account the number of steps, step size and estimation accuracy jointly and develop three new algorithms, namely modification of the eight-pixel algorithm, the four corner and the moving-average MTP. The algorithms developed are able to quantify the complexity of remote sensing images for extracting textural features and estimate the real fractal dimensions. Our proposed algorithms overcome problems of overestimation and limited to specific image sizes of most existing algorithms. They are less influenced by noise and produce more reliable results. (Paper 1) We develop a Bayesian framework to fuse multi-scale remotely sensed images. This method takes into consideration the correlation and change tendency information embedded in time-series data. Tested with Landsat/MODIS data, this method provides an improved performance as compared to conventional STARFM and ESTARFM models. (Paper 3) We further develop two enhanced spatio-temporal Bayesian data fusion approaches incorporating unmixing algorithms. They are rigorously tested conceptually and experimentally in heterogeneous landscape. The robustness of the method is also subject to sensitivity analysis to investigate the level of impact of different parameters. These algorithms can extract details of features which characterize land cover changes under fine scales effectively. They can produce accurate result in monitoring phenological and land cover changes. (Paper 4) Relating scale to urban growth, we also used nighttime light (NTL) satellite images, as a composite proxy to unravel the scaling behaviours of urban growth in China and the US against two empirical laws, Zipf's law and Gibrat's law. We show that NTL results are similar to those of population-based analyses. Cities with NTL larger than the critical size and above the crossover point simultaneously follow both Zipf’s Law and Gibrat’s Law. Information extracted from is consistent with that related to changes in city rank. (Paper 2) We have written 4 journal papers (1 published, 2 under review and 1 will be submitted) and 1 conference paper. One Ph.D. student is trained under this project.

444411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
444411.value: Despite the importance of using fractal dimension for quantifying the complexity and roughness of images, it is still difficult to fetch its specific meaning. Future research works will attempt to ascertain the functional meaning behind fractals. The Bayesian method has great potential but is still restricted by the assumption of Gaussian distribution of error and temporal change tendency. In future work, other distribution model such as skew normal will be attempted. The method proposed will be further developed to take into account additional image elements such as shape and size changes. The experiment will also be extended to not only reflectance data, but also derived data such as various models of vegetation index, and biophysical parameters such as Leaf Area Index which can be more effective in highlighting changes in vegetation communities as well as in heterogeneous landscapes.

444411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
444411.value: Remotely sensed data are acquired in multi-spatial, spectral and temporal resolutions. This project develops multi-scale feature extraction framework to effectively extract useful information from images, as well as robust data fusion method to integrate these data for the environmental monitoring and urbanization studies. In addition to color appearance of these images, fractal dimension and texture are important information for which our improved triangular prism method is able to provide more reliable results with less impact from noises. The data fusion method developed can effectively integrate multi-scale and multi-temporal data for land cover changes studies in complicated landscape such as urban fringe. Our image based study is able to provide consistent result with those based on population data. The timeliness of image data, however, is able to provide more updated information.

444511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
444511.value: We all desire to make a difference with our actions. Missionaries travel to foreign countries to change people’s beliefs; athletes strive on the runway to set new records; politicians run for office to shape public policies; scientists do groundbreaking research to change the world. Nevertheless, despite the ubiquity and importance of this desire, we know relatively little about its unique effects on human behaviors. In this project, we define the need for influence as a basic human motivation to make a difference with one’s actions, either by changing others’ opinions or the outcome of events. Across a series of studies we will show that the need to influence others, independent of hedonic considerations of one’s actions, can systematically affect people’s voting decision, donation likelihood, product choice and evaluations. The first part of our research examines how the need for influence affects people’s voting decisions. Imagine that you are casting vote for a presidential election. It is the final day of voting but you dont' have strong preference toward either candidate. The latest national pool reveals that candidate A is leading by a very small margin, 50.5% versus 49.5%, over candidate B. Which candidate would you vote for? We show that people are significantly more likely to vote for the slightly weaker candidate. This is because when public opinion is closely split between the two candidates, additional votes appear more likely to impact the final result. Thus, a voter would perceive his action as potentially more influential if he felt his vote could potentially reverse the trend and help the weaker candidate win the contest. Next, we test perceived reversibility, accountability, one’s chronic need for influence, and culture as moderators of the need-for-influence effect. We also show that this motivation could sometimes lead people to override their preference in order to make more influential decisions. In the second and third parts of this project, we further demonstrate the need-for-influence effect on consumers' evaluation formation and action likelihood. We show that when participants perceive their actions as having a greater impact on others, they will derive greater satisfaction, evaluate the event more positively, and are more likely to act on similar events in the future. Finally, we show that if people perceive that their actions fail to influence others, they are more likely to conduct more impactful actions in a subsequent occasion in order to restore their personal influence. 我們都希望自己的行動能帶來變革。傳教士跋山涉水到遙遠的國度期冀能改變人們的信仰，運動員在競技場上拼搏為了能刷新記錄，政客們參與競選為了新的施政綱領，科學家做開創性的研究以改變世界。然而，儘管這一願望有它的普遍性和重要性，我們並不很了解其對人類行為的影響。在這個項目中，我們定義“影響力需求“為一種通過行動來改變他人觀念或事件結果的人類基本動機。我們將通過一系列的研究表明，這種對影響力的需求可以影響人們的投票決定，捐贈的可能性，產品的選擇和評價。 我們研究的第一部分探討影響力需求如何影響人們的投票決定。想像一下，你正在參加總統選舉的投票。這是投票的最後一天，但你對兩位候選人都沒有強烈的偏好。競選前的民意測驗表露，候選人A以微弱的優勢，50.5％和49.5％，超過候選人B。你會投票給哪一位候選人？我們的研究表明，人們更可能投票給候選人B 。這是因為當兩名候選人競爭激烈時，額外的選票更可能會影響到大選結果。因此，選民會覺得他這一票如果投給微微落後的候選人B，極有可能扭轉時局,幫助他贏得大選。那麼他這一舉動便是非常有影響力的。換言之，我們發現選民們由於對自身影響力的需求而更傾向於選擇微微落後的候選人。 接下來，我們將研究事件可逆性，個人影響力，影響力需求的個體差異，以及文化對於本研究核心結果的影響。我們也表明，人們有時會為了追求影響力而拋棄自己的喜好做行為決策。 在這個項目的第二和第三部分中，我們將進一步研究影響力需求如何作用於消費者對產品的評價和購買的可能性。我們顯示，當參與者認為他們的行為對商家或別的消費者產生更大的影響時，他們將獲得更高的滿意度，更積極地評價事件，並可能在今後繼續購買。最後，我們顯示，如果人們認為自己的行為沒能影響他人，他們更有可能隨後作出有影響力的舉動，以提高他們的個人影響力。

444511.label: Realisation of objectives
444511.value: The PI and Co-Is have conducted a series of studies to address the research objectives stated in the project proposal. The PI has also enlarged the investigation scope to conduct studies in a related research domain. At this point we have two papers published and three papers under review. The first objective of this project is to examine the impact of the need-for-influence motive on individuals’ voting decisions. The PI and Co-Is have conducted a series of experiments involving over 1000 subjects in both Hong Kong and the U.S. using both online and offline subjects across different age groups. We have also conducted a series of pretests to test our manipulations and ensure the validity of choice stimuli. The proposed Studies 1-4 have all been completed with findings supporting our hypotheses. The second objective of this project is to explore the impact of the need-for-influence motive on consumer judgment formation, satisfaction, and action likelihood. To achieve this goal, we have conducted a series of lab studies in Hong Kong. Two of the proposed studies have been completed with satisfactory results. The third objective of this project is to examine if failure to make an influence will trigger restorative processes, and lead to impactful actions and decisions in subsequent occasions. Based on proposal reviewers’ comments, we have revised the design for some of the originally proposed studies. A new study has been completed with satisfactory results. The fourth objective of this project is to sharpen the concept of the need-for-influence motive and construct a scale to measure this unique motivation. The PI and the Co-Is have created a list of scale items and completed a pretest. Two studies revealed satisfactory results. However, because the need for influence is correlated with some other concepts such as the need for power and control, we are still refining the scale items for further testing.

444511.label: Major findings and research outcome
444511.value: In this project we study how trivial situational factors may activate consumers’ basic motivations and subsequently influence their judgment and decision making. The PI and the Co-Is have studied how the need for influence can be triggered by subtle factors and subsequently affect consumers’ voting behavior. We also conducted related research on how incidental goal priming affects consumers’ motivation and subsequent decisions. Specifically, we show that when a health goal is incidentally activated, consumers are more likely to choose the more effortful option, which serves as a means to solve the self-control dilemma. Finally, in another project, we show that trivial situational factors can activate the concept of time or money, which in turn affect consumers’ product choice. Currently we have two papers published and three papers under review.

444511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
444511.value: Beyond the two publications, we have three more papers under review at peer refereed journals, among which two papers are in advance stages and one paper is under first-round review. We have just submitted one paper for second-round review at Journal of Consumer Psychology. We are currently writing up the revised manuscript of our paper which was invited for third-round review at Journal of Consumer Research. For the third paper which is under first-round review, we will wait for feedback from the reviewers and revise the paper accordingly. We hope to publish at least two more papers in the coming year.

444511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
444511.value: Our research suggests that consumer preference between two political candidates, two unhealthy food options, and two multi-attribute products are often determined by conscious and unconscious goals and mindsets triggered by subtle situational factors, such as a national poll result suggesting a close competition between two political candidates, a poster that features images of time or money, or an incidentally browsed health-related magazine. The various goals and mindsets, once triggered, can affect people’s judgment and decisions in later, often unrelated situations. Our findings advance research on goals, mindsets and motivations. Our findings also guide marketers to strategically influence consumer preference and decision making through goal or mindset priming.
