447411.label: Major findings and research outcome
447411.value: 1. A searchable on-line “Research Database of Chinese modernists’ Translations in the 1930s,” including the data of translations of Dai Wangshu and other four Chinese modernist writers, namely Shi Zhecun, Ye Lingfeng, Xu Xiachun and Liu Na’ou, has been made available to the public at the end of 2013. This search system includes the data of over 2800 titles of translated works published in 187 literary magazines, collections and literary supplements, which involve 148 publishing houses in 21 different cities. It includes also the data of less accessible works which appeared in Hong Kong during the Second Sino-Japanese War. The authors and the original texts of these translations have been carefully located and identified. Please refer to URL: http://www.transchimodern.hk/ Invited by the the Fondation Maison des Sciences de l’Homme (FMSH), the PI has served as visiting professor and researcher (enseignant-chercheur) under the programme of “Directeurs d’Etudes Associés” (DEA) (Associate Research Directors) from June to July, 2014 in Paris. The PI has presented the “Research Database of Chinese modernists’ Translations in the 1930s” and the findings of the project to scholars from different institutes in France and other countries during her academic visit. 2. A book entitled “Dai Wangshu’s Literary Translations in Hong Kong during the Second Sino-Japanese War” has been published in 2014. The publication of this book is supported by a publication grant offered by the Hong Kong Arts Development Council in 2013. The PI has compiled and edited Dai Wangshu’s translations of André Malraux’s L’Espoir, Paul Morand’s La Nuit des six jours, Jules Supervielle’s L’Inconnue de la Seine and David Garnett’s Lady into Fox etc., which had never been compiled in Dai’s Complete Works or any collection of his works. The PI has also written a critical introduction (32 pages) on Dai Wangshu’s literary translations during the Second Sino-Japanese War and their significance. 3. Based on the findings of the research project, three peer-reviewed journal papers have been or will be published. (Please refer to Part C8 for details) 4. Based on the findings of the research project, five peer-reviewed conference papers have been delivered at international conferences held in Taiwan and Hong Kong (Please refer to Part C9 for details).

447411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
447411.value: Based on the findings of the current research project, we propose to further investigate a group of modernist “writers-translators-editors” and their attachment to the leftist cultural movement in Europe. We include in this group Dai Wangshu, Shi Zhecun (1905-2003), Liu Na’ou (1905-1940), Xu Xiacun (1907-1986) and Ye Lingfeng (1905-1975). We propose to conduct this new research in two stages. First stage: We will first examine Chinese modernists’ reception of European leftist intellectuals, especially the French leftist writers, in the particular Chinese context in the 1930s and 1940s. This work is based on the data provided by the “Research Database of Chinese modernists’ Translations in the 1930s”. The Chinese modernists extensively translated the writings of Romain Rolland (1866-1944), André Gide (1869-1951), Henri Barbusse (1873-1935), Paul Vaillant-Couturier (1892-1937), Louis Aragon (1897-1982) and André Malraux (1901-1976). Second Stage: In this stage we intend to investigate the way Chinese modernists developed their own interest in revolutionary literature and proletarian literature under the influence of French leftist writers. This project will also investigate the heterogeneity of modernist writings developed in China under the influence of international leftist literature.

447411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
447411.value: Research on Dai Wangshu has been hampered by the relative inaccessibility of his Hong Kong output. Though he published prolifically in Hong Kong during his exile (1938-1949), most of these works have never been compiled in his Complete Work or any collections of his work. This research project tries to fill in the missing pieces of puzzles. A book entitled “Dai Wangshu’s Literary Translations in Hong Kong during the Second Sino-Japanese War” with a critical introduction has been published. It has compiled and edited Dai Wangshu’s translations published in Hong Kong which had never been compiled in his Complete Works or any collection of his works. Based on hitherto-neglected source material, the project will extend the study scope of Dai Wangshu by covering his works published in Hong Kong during the Second Sino-Japanese War. An on-line multi-purpose search system for the data of translations of Dai Wangshu and other modernist writers including Shi Zhecun, Ye Lingfeng, Liu Na’ou and Xu Xiacun has been established and made freely available to the public, thereby making a significant contribution to this field of study as well as facilitating future work in comparative literary studies and translation studies.

447611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
447611.value: The provincial city of Guangzhou is the largest city in the Pearl River Delta of south China. Temples have long been in evidence everywhere in the city and the neighboring thirteen counties. There have been large temples (gongguan 宮觀), found with affiliations to various Daoist schools and lineages, since the Ming Dynasty—for example, the Xuanmiao guan 元妙觀, Sanyuan gong 三元宮, Wuxian guan 五仙觀 and Chunyang guan 純陽觀. There have also been a large number of smaller temples dedicated to the worship of Daoist deities, such as the Dongyue miao 東嶽廟, Beidi miao 北帝廟 (Yuxu gong 玉虛宮), Chenghuang miao 城隍廟, Wenchang gong 文昌宮, Guandi miao 關帝廟, Tianhou miao 天后廟, Hongsheng miao 洪聖廟, and others. The proposed project is primarily based on collections of relevant material covering Daoist temples in the provincial Guangzhou city and the surrounding thirteen counties, mostly in the form of epigraphic records (including surviving unpublished rubbings and stele inscriptions gathered through extensive on-site investigation), and archival material derived from local gazetteers, Daoist priests, and provincial/county/city archives, and consisting of temple histories, historical maps, and liturgical manuscripts. Apart from further collecting, all that needs to be developed is a complete cataloguing and the input of all these data into electronic files, along with the construction of an appropriate presentation platform and management system through the application of Geographic Information System (GIS) to maintain, order, display and analyze the spatial and historical features of the temples concerned. The proposed project aims ultimately at the building of a Daoist Virtual Museum by using GIS tools to provide not only textual, historical and spatial data, but also 3-dimensional models/panoramic views/video clips related to the Daoist temples (from the Ming dynasty to the present) of Guangzhou city and the surrounding thirteen counties. Once this Virtual Museum is in place, researchers in the fields of Daoism, Chinese religions, and Guangzhou city itself will be able to trace the development and geographical change of individual Daoist temples so as to make quantitative studies about the geographical distribution of all the Guangzhou Daoist temples, their spatial/temporal relationships to their social and economic surroundings, demographic background, and landscapes and environment. 廣東省省會廣州是中國南方珠江三角洲地區最大的城市。長久以來，在廣州及與其接壤的十三個縣城境內，隨處可見各種道教廟宇。自明代以來，這些地方就出現了與多種道教流派譜系緊密相關的大型宮觀——如元妙觀、三元宮、五仙觀和純陽觀等。同時也有大量祭祀崇拜道教神祗的小型廟宇，如東嶽廟、北帝廟（玉虛宮）、城隍廟、文昌宮、關帝廟、天后廟、洪聖廟等等。 本研究主要建立在關於廣州及其附近十三個縣市境內道教廟宇的收藏資料之上，其中大部分材料多為碑文記錄（包括我們在多次田野調查中蒐集到的、尚未出版、現存拓本和碑刻資料），以及從地方志、道士道長和各省、州、市檔案中蒐集到的道教廟宇歷史、歷史地圖和道教禮儀典籍書稿等文獻資料。現階段，在進一步蒐集相關資料之外，我們需要將已有數據歸類建檔、建立詳細完整的目錄，並將它們存入電子檔案，同時利用地理信息系統（GIS）開發與之相宜的數據展示平台和管理體系，從而能夠保存、整理、展示和分析這些廟宇的時空特質。 本研究的最終目的是運用GIS工具建立一座道教廟宇虛擬博物館。該館不僅可以為觀眾提供文本、史料以及空間數據，也可以為人們展示自明代以來廣州及附近十三個縣市境內廟宇的三維立體全景影像。這座虛擬博物館建成之後，致力於道教研究、中國宗教研究及廣州市研究領域的相關學者們可以追溯每座廟宇的空間發展和變革，並藉此進行相關的量化研究工作，分析探索廣州地區道教廟觀的地理分佈，以及道教廟觀的時空沿革與當地社會經濟環境、人口背景、城市及自然景觀的相互聯繫。

447611.label: Realisation of objectives
447611.value: The PI has successfully constructed, developed and launched the first Digital Museum of Daoist tradition (DDM; http://dao.crs.cuhk.edu.hk/digitalmuseum) in the world today. The DDM is a Web-GIS platform currently hosted on the website of the Centre for Studies of Daoist Culture at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. Registered users (up to November 11, 2015, there are 280 registered users) have had access the DDM worldwide since 1 January, 2015. The system of DDM effectively implements modern networking technology, digital maps and Geographical Information System (GIS). Based on this Web-GIS platform, researchers can dispose of the geographical database of the DDM and conveniently search, browse, and study relevant materials and visual aspects of 132 Daoist and popular temples in the provincial Guangzhou city and the surrounding thirteen counties from the Ming up to the present. Because it employs advanced technologies in building networking, digital mapping, and geographical information, the DDM can now display historical, spatial, and visual information of these 132 Daoist and popular temples. The DDM is particularly characterized by its multimedia approach with a powerful search engine which can integrate different types of data of 132 temples and illustrate them visually and spatially on digitalized maps. As a result, researchers can now search, browse and study spatial and visual aspects of Chinese temples in Guangzhou, covering a database on temple locations, pictures, videos, steles inscriptions, historical documents, architecture, enshrined effigies, ritual texts, sacred implements, regional gazetteers, and biographical references. Given the unique features of the DDM, the digital museum has not only a collection of 132 Daoist and popular temples, it also contains data including 298 stele inscriptions collected from 132 Daoist and popular temples in Guangzhou city and the surrounding thirteen counties. These 298 stele inscriptions are catalogued with punctuated inscription texts, annotations, illustrations, index, and accounts of those who composed these inscriptions. Moreover, there are more than 1000 pictures of temple altars and deities images displayed in the DDM and they are panoramic pictures presenting in a three-dimensional temple environment. Finally, the DDM collects more than 30 rituals texts of Daoist tradition practiced in the Pearl River Delta of south China. Video recordings of some of ritual performances are also available in the museum. In conclusion, the DDM is a ground–breaking achievement in the study of Daoist and popular temples as it moves beyond the traditional textual-historical approach to a spatial-temporal visual-based dimension.

447611.label: Major findings and research outcome
447611.value: The provincial city of Guangzhou is the largest city in the Pearl River Delta of south China. Whereas throughout China in their early Republic period government officials and intellectuals condemned religious and cultic activities in traditional Chinese temples as “superstition” and many temples were afterwards closed and converted to public schools, markets, gardens, etc., during the official campaign to suppress superstition in the early Republican period, our research explicitly that temples and their cults have long been in evidence everywhere in the city and the neighboring thirteen counties from the Ming and up to the late Qing. Like many other cities in China, Guangzhou was a city of hundreds temples. Apart from official temples and the Buddhist and Daoist monasteries, all other Daoist and popular temples were located inside the city and the surrounding thirteen counties and belonged to the local communities, neighborhoods, guilds, or charitable associations for the public interest. Without exception, these temples were dedicated to specific patron saints of whom there were a great many, among them the Empress of Heaven, the Supreme Thearch of Dark Heaven or God of the North, Wenchang, the God of War, the City God, the God of the Eastern Peak, the God of Fire, the God of Medicine, Marshal Kang, Marshal Zhao, the Mother of the Dipper, the Dragon King, and so on. As the main research outcome of this project, PI has constructed a digital Daoist museum based on a Web-GIS platform (called the DDM), which is an innovative endeavor, transforming the traditional research method based upon historical documents into one that can allow searches for and analysis of spatial and visual data about temples and rituals. Researchers can search now search, browse and study spatial and visual aspects of 132 Chinese temples in Guangzhou and the surrounding thirteen counties from the Ming to the present, covering a database on temple locations, deity pictures, videos, steles inscriptions, historical gazetteers, temple architecture, enshrined effigies, ritual texts, and sacred implements. The digital museum has a collection of 132 Daoist and popular temples, and there are 58 temples still existed up to the present day. The searchable database also includes 298 stele inscriptions collected from 132 Daoist and popular temples in Guangzhou city and the surrounding thirteen counties. More significantly, about 120 stele inscriptions are doscovered by PI and firstly publicized to the public.

447611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
447611.value: Until now, there has been no GIS database applied specifically to studying temple rituals such as those in Hong Kong. Based on the platform of the DDM, it is believed that the digital museum can take a further expansion in terms of geographical coverage and development of specialized functions on ritual‘s presentation. For geographical coverage, the PI has already spent over 20 years on studying Daoism and popular temples in Hong Kong and Macau. The PI has collected various relevant material covering Daoist temples and local temples in these two regions. With the ready-to-use technology and existing platform, the huge and various materials of the Daoist temples and local temples in Hong Kong and Macau can be integrated into the digital museum. For functional improvement, the DDM can develop a digital archive covering ritual texts and performance practiced in Daoist and local temples in Hong Kong and Macau. Two new functional modes of browsing on the DDM can be developed: the first, image-text parallel browsing and the second, text-video browsing. By constructing so, the DDM will provide a new way to study and investigate the ritual archive, from purely textual proofing-reading, image-text comparison, to further video-text browsing.

447611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
447611.value: This project has constructed a web-based Daoist Digital Museum (DDM) by using the Geographic Information System tools to provide not only textual, historical and spatial data, but also 3-dimensional model/panorama view/video clips related to the 132 Daoist and popular temples (from the Ming dynasty to the present) of Guangzhou city and 13 nearby counties. This allows the data searchable by locations, temples, deities, steles inscriptions via the internet, facilitating researchers in the fields of Daoism, Chinese religions and history of Guangzhou city to be able to trace the development and geographical change of individual Daoist temples so as to make quantitative studies about the geographical distribution of such temples in Guangzhou, their spatial/temporal relationships to their social and economic surroundings, demographic background, and landscapes environment. In brief, the construction and launch of the DDM has been a ground-breaking work on the study of Daoism and Chinese religions by moving beyond the traditional textual-historical approach to a spatial-temporal visual based dimension.

447711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
447711.value: The aim of this project is to investigate the learning-to-teach experiences of novice Liberal Studies teachers by following the trajectories of their development, from initial preparation to their first year of teaching practice. The proposed study is set against the backdrop of the most recent education reform in Hong Kong. Among the new educational initiatives is the introduction of a required, interdisciplinary subject called Liberal Studies in the new senior secondary curriculum. The Liberal Studies curriculum calls for fundamental changes in teachers’ thinking about curriculum, teaching and learning, and poses new challenges to the preparation of Liberal Studies teachers. Drawing on Lave and Wenger’s (1991) notion of legitimate peripheral participation as a theoretical framework, this project specifically focuses on how different settings (including the university-based teacher education coursework, teaching practicum, the first year of practice, and mentor-mentee relationships) contribute to novice Liberal Studies teachers’ knowledge base for teaching. Participants are students who take Liberal Studies as their major methods course in the Postgraduate Diploma in Education programme. Data collection will span two years, starting from the participants’ initial preparation to the end of their first year of full-time teaching, and will involve different well-established methods deployed at key points throughout the study period. The proposed study will generate knowledge of practical significance to the professional preparation and development of Liberal Studies teachers. It will also contribute to an understanding of the developmental processes of novice Liberal Studies teachers; the distinctive qualities of opportunities to learn afforded by various settings in which novice Liberal Studies teachers learn; and the characteristics of an effective learning environment for Liberal Studies teachers, which is of theoretical significance to research on teacher learning and development. 本計劃旨在明瞭新進的通識教育科教師學習施教的經歷，觀察他們從最初接受培訓到第一年的教學實踐的發展過程。 研究的建議正值香港最新的教育改革首次施行，其中革新項目包括在高中課程引入跨學科的通識教育科，定為必修課程。要教好這門學科，教師必須徹底改變對課程和教學的固有觀念；這要求對通識教育科教師的培訓工作則是新的挑戰。 本研究以Lave和Wenger (1991)的「合法理的周邊參與」（legitimate peripheral participation）概念為理論架構，集中分析不同的學習場景（包括大學師訓班的課業、教學實習、首年的教學實踐、指導導師－學員關係）如何增進新進通識教育科教師的教學知識。計劃參加者是修讀學位教師教育文憑課程的學生，主修通識教育科教學法。收集數據將歷時兩年，從參加者最初接受培訓開始，到他們完成首年的全職教學為止。於整個研究期間，會採用穩妥的方法在重要環節上搜集數據。 建議的研究將產出有用的知識，有助通識教育科教師的培訓與發展；包括了解通識教育科教師專業發展過程、認識各種形式學習機會的特質，確認促進通識教育科教師有效學習的環境特徵。並且，這些知識的掌握也有助教師學習和發展研究的理論建構。

447711.label: Realisation of objectives
447711.value: The project objectives have been fully achieved. The first objective of capturing the developmental processes of novice Liberal Studies (LS) teachers from initial preparation to the first year of induction has been achieved by collecting data on teacher learning at crucial times of development for these novice teachers. The data collected include: novice teacher logs; field notes on observed lessons; audio or written records of mentor-mentee conferences on observed lessons; teaching portfolios; interviews with novice LS teachers; and interviews with mentors. These data provide a wide spectrum of information on the learning of novice LS teachers at key points of their development. The second objective of identifying the distinctive qualities of opportunities to learn afforded by different settings which support the development of competence in LS teaching has been achieved by first identifying changes in the learning of these novice LS teachers at crucial times of their development and then relating such changes to the contextual conditions in which they occur. By building the links between instances of teacher learning and the contexts in which such instances occur, the distinctive qualities of opportunities to learn afforded by different settings have been highlighted. The third objective of understanding how mentor-mentee relationships shape the opportunities to learn for novice LS teachers has been achieved by collecting records on mentor-mentee conferences on observed lessons and interviewing both the novice LS teachers and their mentors on mentoring support during the two blocks of teaching practicum. These data shed light on how mentor-mentee relationships shape the learning of novice LS teachers. The fourth objective of identifying the characteristics of an effective learning environment for LS teachers has been achieved by identifying instances of effective teacher learning in the data and relating such instances to contextual conditions in which they occur. The fifth objective of theorizing novice teacher learning using the ‘legitimate peripheral participation (LPP)’ perspective has been achieved by using LPP as a theoretical lens in examining the data, with the aim of conceptualizing how novice LS teacher learning takes place in different contexts and how these contexts interact to support the development of competence in LS teaching.

447711.label: Major findings and research outcome
447711.value: During their initial teacher education coursework, the novice LS teachers in this study were engaged in most of the central tasks of learning to teach for preservice teachers highlighted by Feiman-Nemser (2001). However, their engagement with the central tasks of developing subject matter knowledge for teaching and developing pedagogical content knowledge had been intensified due to their lack of equivalent disciplinary backgrounds in the subject, the broad and open nature of the curriculum framework, the dynamic nature of the subject matter and their unfamiliarity with the issue-enquiry approach adopted for the subject. During their teaching practicum, the novice LS teachers developed their teaching competence through delivering lessons in authentic classrooms; interacting with their mentors, other teachers and fellow student teachers; interacting with students and attempting to build positive student-teacher relationships; and participating in class, subject and school activities. Among these various learning opportunities, classroom teaching was found to be most beneficial for their professional development, due to increased practice in lesson planning; the need to strengthen subject matter knowledge for teaching; the need to understand students and adjust teaching; and increased practice in the use of different teaching and learning strategies. Pedagogical content knowledge (PCK) has been recognized as a distinctive body of knowledge for teaching (Shulman, 1997). The findings show that during their first year of teaching, the novice LS teachers varied in how they put PCK into practice. Factors such as teacher knowledge, learner characteristics, mentoring support and school culture helped explain the differential manifestations of PCK. Findings of this study echo with what has been widely recognized in the literature that mentoring is an important aspect of the professional preparation of novice teachers. In this study, the novice LS teachers had benefitted most from mentor-mentee relationships that attended to their development needs; engaged them in both practical and intellectual tasks of teaching; involved them in joint work with their mentors; and were aimed at helping them develop skills and practices that would support sustained teacher learning in and from practice. Using the concept of legitimate peripheral participation to understand teacher learning, it shows that an effective learning environment for novice LS teachers is constituted by a coherent and continuous curriculum for teacher learning spanning initial preparation, induction and early years of practice so that their learning in practice situations will be built on their learning in university-based education coursework.

447711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
447711.value: From a curriculum implementation perspective, there has been a critical need for research into the preparation and professional development of LS teachers. The present study is an exploratory one. The findings of this study raise further questions, such as: Given the important role of pedagogical content knowledge (PCK) in LS teaching, how does PCK actually develop in LS teachers? How do novice LS teachers mature into expert LS teachers? How do school-based teacher development efforts contribute to the professional growth of LS teachers? What are the distinctive qualities of expert LS teachers and the contextual conditions supporting their development? These questions are waiting to be addressed in future research. The findings of this study have important implications for teacher education. Currently, the design of initial teacher preparation programmes for LS is underpinned with the assumption that preparing LS teachers attending these programmes are content prepared. Unlike most other major methods students who hold an undergraduate degree in their respective major methods subjects, preparing LS teachers do not possess equivalent disciplinary backgrounds. In other words, preparing LS teachers have limitations in their content preparation. Such limitations need to be acknowledged and addressed in initial teacher preparation.

447711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
447711.value: A required, interdisciplinary subject called Liberal Studies (LS) has been introduced in the senior secondary curriculum in Hong Kong since 2009. The broad and open nature of the LS curriculum framework, the dynamic nature of the subject matter and the adoption of the issue-enquiry approach for the subject have called for fundamental changes in teachers’ thinking about curriculum, teaching and learning, posing new challenges to the preparation of LS teachers. Since the commencement of LS, little research has been done on how LS teachers develop competence in teaching the subject. This gap of research has led to the focus of this study, which sets out to examine how novice LS teachers learn to teach by following their development from initial preparation to their first year of teaching practice. Findings of this study show how initial teacher education coursework, teaching practicum, the first year of practice and mentoring relationships have contributed to the learning of novice LS teachers; and shed light on what constitute an effective learning environment for LS teachers. The findings will inform the design of teacher education progammes for LS and the design of a curriculum for teacher learning spanning different stages of LS teachers’ career development.

To provide suggestions on how to manage socially dirty workers and to help these workers develop strong occupational identification and work meaningfulness.

448411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
448411.value: 在社会型厌恶性工作中，员工需要接触被社会所疏离或者隔离的人群（例如问题青少年；精神病人；监狱里的犯人等等）。虽然这一类型的工作不是那么吃香，但它们对社会的运行而言是非常重要和必要的。深入的了解这种厌恶性工作的机制有助于管理层向员工提供资源和制定相关政策以支持他们。 基于社会学习理论，我们认为社会型厌恶性工作者会“学习和揣摩”他们工作对象的行为和思维方式，这或许能让员工更胜任他们的工作，但同时也给员工塑造职业认同感和建构工作意义带来巨大的挑战。 在员工去适应他们自身由于工作带来的变化的过程中，管理层或者上司可以帮助他们去理解这些变化从而让员工能建构良好的职业认同感和工作意义。基于过去的一些研究，我们提议研究在员工“学习和揣摩”过程中的职业规范及价值观，组织诚信度和同事的诚信度。这三个因素分别代表了研究社会型厌恶性工作者的三个角度：职业层面，组织层面及同事层面。我们计划去探究这三个因素是否有助于员工维持正面的自我认同。 通过这个研究项目，我们希望加深对社会型厌恶性工作者面临的挑战和困难的认识。我们也会去探求如何从职业层面，组织层面以及共事者层面为这类型工作者提供可能的支持和帮助。

449011.label: Project Title(Chinese)
449011.value: 重構抗爭範式:分析社運社會中傳媒對集體行動的報導

449011.label: Project Objectives
449011.value: Documenting and explaining the continuities and changes in the news media's coverage of social protests in the years after the handover. Examining media discourses surrounding protest actions in order to gain an understanding of the emerging protest culture in Hong Kong. Contributing to a theoretical understanding of media-protest relationship in an emerging "movement society."
rows: Documenting and explaining the continuities and changes in the news media's coverage of social protests in the years after the handover.
Examining media discourses surrounding protest actions in order to gain an understanding of the emerging protest culture in Hong Kong.
Contributing to a theoretical understanding of media-protest relationship in an emerging "movement society."

449011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
449011.value: Media researchers in Hong Kong and elsewhere have, for decades, analyzed how media cover protest actions. Based on the theoretical argument that the mass media are agents of social control, early studies suggested that the media follow a conservative "protest paradigm" when covering citizens' collective actions which challenge the established power structure and status quo. Under the paradigm, protesters are portrayed negatively as deviants and/or trouble-makers. Their goals and the reasons behind their actions are often lost in the reporting, while their violent or novel actions are often highlighted and problematized. Nevertheless, in the past decade, some social movement scholars have noted that protests have become more and more frequent, diversified, normalized, and routinized in contemporary societies. In Hong Kong, while the history of social movements dated back to at least the late 1960s, social protests have also seemingly become more and more prominent in the past decade. The news media, on a daily basis, report various protest actions seemingly aiming at an increasingly diverse range of targets and making an increasingly wide range of claims. At this historical juncture, there are signs indicating that Hong Kong is becoming a movement society. Focusing on the media, can the concept of "protest paradigm" still capture the nature and characteristics of media coverage of protests? What are the roles played by the media in the articulation and negotiation of the protest culture in Hong Kong? How do media influence public perceptions of protests? This proposed project addresses the above questions by a combination of research methods: content analyses of media coverage, case studies of media discourses surrounding prominent protest campaigns, in-depth interviews with journalists and activists, as well as representative surveys of citizen attitudes toward media and protests. The project shall inform us about the possibly changing relationship between media and protest actions and contribute to our understanding of the emerging protest culture in Hong Kong. Theoretically, our project ties together the analyses and discussions about "movement society" and "protest paradigm." It shall illustrate, on the one hand, how the analysis of media coverage can inform the debates about movement society, and on the other hand, how the conceptual framework of movement society may guide an analysis of media coverage of protests, potentially leading to new and important findings. Putting it most broadly, this project will enhance our understanding of the changing relationships between media, power, and social resistance in contemporary societies. 過去十年，不少香港和各地的傳播研究學者都曾就媒介如何報導抗爭行為進行分析。在批判的觀點出發，媒介常被視為實踐社會控制的代理人，因此早期的研究認為，媒介在報導公民嘗試挑戰既有權力結構的集體行動的時候，會依循保守的「抗爭範式」（protest paradigm），把抗爭者負面地描繪為異類或麻煩製造者。報導的焦點往往放在他們的暴力或奇異行徑，而行動背後的目標和理據則被忽略。 一些研究社會運動的學者在這十年間已經指出，抗爭行動在當代社會出現得越來越頻密、多樣化、正常化、常規化。在香港，若以六十年代作為社會運動的起點，也可以觀察到，社會抗爭在這十年裡日益被看重，而每日更新的新聞媒介，也報導了各種對象和訴求日趨多樣、光譜越來越闊的抗爭行動。在這個歷史時刻，一些有跡象似乎顯示著香港也正邁向成為一個「社運社會」（movement society）。如果把焦點放在媒介，我們要問的是，「抗爭範式」這概念是否仍能捕捉到媒介報導抗爭活動的性質和特點？媒介在香港抗爭文化的扣連和協商當中，扮演了甚麼角色？媒介如何影響公眾對抗爭行為的認知？ 這個計劃主張透過各種研究方法的組合去分析上述問題，這些研究方法包括對媒介報導的內容分析、集中於媒介論述的個案研究、跟新聞工作者和社運人士進行深度訪談、就大眾對媒介和抗爭的態度進行有代表性的問卷調查。這個研究可以讓我們知道媒介和抗爭行動之間正在轉變中的關係，也讓我們對的抗爭文化有更多認識。在理論層面，這個研究緊扣著關於「社運社會」和「抗爭範式」兩者的討論和分析。一方面，本研究嘗試通過分析媒介報導介入「運動社會」的辯論；另一方面，「社運社會」的概念框架又可以指導有關媒介如何報導抗爭行動的分析，並可能帶出新的重要研究成果。而在最宏觀的層面上，這個研究可以讓我們對當代社會中媒介、權力、社會抗爭三者轉變中的關係有更深入的了解。

449011.label: Realisation of objectives
449011.value: The project addressed the three stated objectives through a range of empirical studies: 1) a general content analysis of newspaper coverage of collective contentious actions in Hong Kong from year 2000 to 2012, 2) a content analysis of media coverage of three specific movement industries (the environmental movement, the women’s movement, and the LGBT movement), 3) case studies of two environmental collective actions in 2012, encompassing textual analysis of media coverage and in-depth interviews with activists, and 4) population surveys examining common citizens’ perceptions of and attitudes toward social movements and collective actions. More specifically, the content analysis of news coverage of collective actions allows the investigators to address objective 1, i.e., to document and explain the continuities and changes in news coverage of protests after the handover. The case studies of the two environmental collective actions allow the investigators to tackle objective 2, i.e., to examine news discourses surrounding more specific protest actions in the city. The above research work and the population surveys, taken together, help the investigators to address objective 3, i.e., to develop an overall understanding of the evolution of media-movement relationship in Hong Kong. It should be noted that the amount of funding approved for the project did not permit the investigators to tackle objective 2 in a comprehensive manner as originally envisioned when the project proposal was submitted. Instead of examining a full range of discourses surrounding different types of protest actions, the project opted for a case study approach and focused on the environmental movement in particular due to the environmental movement’s size, prominence, and relative maturity (The content analyses of news coverage of the women’s movement and the LGBT movement were conducted to serve as points of comparison for the content analysis of news coverage of the environmental movement). The objective, with its scale adjusted, was considered as achieved adequately. Moreover, in the process of conducting the case studies of the environmental movement and the two cases of environmental collective actions, the investigators found that the resource mobilization processes behind the collective actions deserve special attention. Besides, the role of new media technologies has emerged in recent years as a highly important issue in the study of social mobilization. The investigators thus also ventured into these two problematics. Specifically, a small part of the project funding was utilized for a survey on social media usage and political attitudes among university students.

449011.label: Major findings and research outcome
449011.value: The project aims at examining whether the argument that the news media helps the dominant power to exercise social control by covering social protests following a conservative “protest paradigm” remains valid in an age when social mobilization has arguably become normalized and routinized, as the “movement society” thesis suggests. The research provides evidence that news coverage of protests and movements are indeed changing. Content analysis shows that, over the years, Hong Kong media coverage of contentious collective actions focused on disruptiveness and violence to lesser extents, emphasized the protesters’ voices to larger extents, and portrayed the interactions between the protesters and their targets to larger extents. Moreover, there is no sign that the trend varies among newspapers with different political and market positions. These findings, on the whole, support the overall contention that when social movements and protest actions become accepted by citizens as legitimate means to express public opinion, the mainstream media also become more neutral or even positive in portraying social movements and collective actions. Surveys of public opinion and case studies of two environmental collective actions show that the idea of “self-mobilization” is particularly important in the discourses surrounding social protests in Hong Kong. The public sees collective actions mobilized by citizens themselves as particularly representative of public opinion. The case studies of environmental collective actions, however, show that in reality “citizen self-mobilization” and organization-based mobilization processes often work closely and dynamically with each other. Citizen self-mobilization efforts are arguably more capable of responding to new and emerging issues. But from a resource mobilization perspective, conventional movement organizations remain crucial in social mobilization because successful movement campaigns still rely substantially on the amount and types of material, financial, human, intellectual, and social resources that only conventional movement organizations are likely to be able to mobilize. News media attention, in particular, remains important to social mobilization and conventional movement organizations are more capable of maintaining media attention to issues. On the whole, the findings of the project suggest that the rising prominence of social movements and collective actions in Hong Kong has been accompanied by the development of new forms of social mobilization and the formation of new ways of talking about movements and protests. The news media is part of the dynamic processes of social mobilization for specific collective actions. They also played important roles in legitimizing social protests and promulgating new understanding about collective actions in general.

449011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
449011.value: Three areas are worth further examining in future research. First, the finished project did not examine media and public discourses surrounding social movements and protest actions comprehensively. The evolution of many “keywords” and themes in contentious politics in Hong Kong, e.g., civil disobedience, public space, etc., are worth more systematic and in-depth examination. Further studies in this area can help document the accumulation and development of symbolic resources that organizers and participants of contentious politics use to justify and make sense of their goals and actions. Second, while the finished project focused mainly on conventional news media, new media technologies, such as social media sites, are playing increasingly important roles in social mobilization in Hong Kong. The finished project has already conducted some preliminary research on the topic. Further research on how movement organizations and ordinary citizens utilize new media platforms for social mobilization is definitely needed. Third, although this project involved two surveys, it did not systematically address issues of “media effects” on public opinion toward social protests. Theory-driven examination of how news media consumption and new media usage relate to understanding of, attitude toward, and actual participation in social protests can constitute a meaningful project on its own.

449011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
449011.value: Hong Kong has witnessed the rising prominence of social protests and movements in the past 15 years. More citizens and social groups have become active in collective actions addressing a wider range of issues. Against this background, this project examines how the news media cover social movements and protest actions and what roles the media play in processes of social mobilization in Hong Kong. Through content analysis, the project finds that media coverage of protest actions since 2000 has indeed become less negative. More specifically, media coverage of protests focused on disruptiveness and violence to lesser extents, emphasized the protesters’ voices to larger extents, and portrayed the interactions between the protesters and their targets to larger extents. Besides, project findings also suggest that the news media play an important role in promulgating new ideas and discourses about social protests. Moreover, in specific cases of collective actions, the mainstream news media interact dynamically with movement groups, self-mobilizing citizens, and new media to drive social mobilization. On the whole, the project provides evidence about the changing media-movement relations in Hong Kong, which is crucial to a broader understanding of the development of social movements, collective actions, and public opinion in the city.

449511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
449511.value: Attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a common psychiatric disorder, characterized by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsivity, which affects 5% of the population. It is a chronic condition associated with considerable psychosocial impairments, leading to comorbid anti-social/emotional disorders, social rejection, school failure/dropout, unstable employment, etc. ADHD has multiple biological etiologies, including genetics. Twin studies have reported a high heritability estimate. However, despite the publication of the human genome in 2000, genome-wide association study (GWAS) has failed to either report consistent findings or identify genetic variants of significant association to ADHD. Traditional candidate gene approach can only identify genes of small effects. So, there is considerable “missing heritability” unaccounted for. It is proposed that rare genetic variants (<1% frequency) with moderate (or higher) effects may account for this missing heritability, as in the case of some other complex diseases. Unfortunately, study of such nature with ADHD is rare. This study proposes to embark an extensive search of such rare variants for ADHD via deep re-sequencing. Whole-genome or whole-exome re-sequencing is still prohibitively expensive nowadays. So it is most cost-effective and scientifically logical to choose 19 candidate genes, which have compelling theoretical and empirical reasons for their association to ADHD, and re-sequence their coding regions, splice-sites and 5’-3’ UTR sequences. This would give us the best chance of finding rare variants with greater effects on ADHD. Our research team is in an excellent position to embark such a study because our overseas co-investigators (Swanson/Moyzis) reported the first study that identified rare variants associated to ADHD. Our local team (Leung & associates) had worked with them in successful pilot studies of an ADHD candidate gene, dopamine receptor D4 (DRD4) gene in a Chinese population. These pilot studies showed that ethnicity played an important part in ADHD genetic research. We found a DRD4 allele (2-repeat allele) associated to Chinese ADHD children, differing from the one (7-repeat allele) identified by Swanson/Moyzis in European-ancestry ADHD children. However, it was found that both alleles in Asians were in fact linked in evolution, so that behind the ethnic difference, common evolutionary pathways explained their link to ADHD. These findings shed important light on the genetic etiology of ADHD across ethnic groups. So it is imperative to study ADHD genes in Chinese, instead of wholly relying on research findings from other ethnic groups for our knowledge on ADHD. 專注力不足/過度活躍症(ADHD)是一種普遍的精神病，約有5%的人口患有這種病。此病的主要症狀包括專注力不足、過度活躍及容易衝動。患者的心理及社交功能不僅會長期受到負面影響，還往往會引致反社會行為、情緒病、社交障礙、學業及就業等問題。 專注力不足/過度活躍症有不同的病因，遺傳基因是其一。雙胞胎研究顯示此病有高度的遺傳性。縱然2000年發佈了人類的基因組, 全基因組關聯研究（genome-wide association study，GWAS）卻未能針對專注力不足/過度活躍症的基因組找出一致的結果，也未能找出相關的遺傳變異（genetic variants)。傳統的候選基因法亦只能找出一些較小影響力的基因。因此，ADHD在基因研究中仍有很多不能解釋的遺傳現象。 猶如其他較複雜的疾病，過往的研究曾提出具中（或高）度影響力的罕見遺傳變異（<1%）或許可以解釋專注力不足/過度活躍症的遺傳現象。可惜，現時相關的研究並不多。故此，是次研究嘗試以深度測序技術(deep re-sequencing)廣泛搜尋專注力不足/過度活躍症的罕見遺傳變異。由於現今全基因組或顯子組測序的價格相當昂貴，因此選出較具研究證據支持與專注力不足/過度活躍症有關的19組候選基因，再重新為它們的基因编碼區（coding regions)、接合點 (splice-sites)和5‘-3’ UTR 序列测定，是最科學並具成本效益的方法。這將讓我們更能找出與專注力不足/過度活躍症有較大影響力的罕見基因。 我們的是次研究擁有有利的時機。我們的海外合作研究者Swanson 和 Moyzis 已發表第一項有關專注力不足/過度活躍症的罕見遺傳變異研究。我們的本地研究團隊亦已與他們於試驗研究中成功地於華人社會找出 專注力不足/過度活躍症的一種候選基因 - dopamine receptor D4 (DRD4) 。這些初步結果顯示種族因素於專注力不足/過度活躍症的基因研究中擔當一個很重要的角色。我們發現DRD4 allele (2-repeat allele)與華裔兒童中的專注力不足/過度活躍症有關，但Swanson及Moyzis於歐裔兒童研究中卻找出不同的結果- 7-repeat allele。但是，我們發現那兩組基因在亞裔人仕進化路途中是有相連關係。所以，雖然不同種族發現不同基因與專注力不足/過度活躍症有關，但是他們有同樣的進化路途，可以解釋他們與專注力不足/過度活躍症的關聯。這些研究結果充分地反映了研究有關專注力不足/過度活躍症的遺傳病因學於不同種族中的重要性。故此，我們不能單靠於其他種族的研究。要增加對專注力不足/過度活躍症的認識，研究華人專注力不足/過度活躍症的基因是極為重要的。

449711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
449711.value: The transportation of dangerous goods (DGs) can significantly affect human life and the environment if accidents occur during the transportation process. Such accidents can result in traffic disruptions, fatalities, property and environmental damages. Therefore, safe DG transportation is of paramount importance, especially in high-density-living environments. Decisions regarding DG transportation are difficult to make because of its catastrophic consequence and public sensitivity. This makes it important to carefully study such risks for strategic decision-making. In the study of DG transportation, risk assessment and route planning are, among other issues, two important and closely related problems of high academic and practical values. Though various risk models have been developed over the years, few of them are specifically designed for high-density living with respect to various risks. DG transportation is a multi-objective problem with stakeholders playing different roles and having different objectives. These objectives are generally conflicting so that a single “best” solution that can optimize every single objective is impossible. The solution of such problem is to search for one or a set of “compromise” solutions rendering the best possible trade-offs for conflict resolution among different objectives. Given the multi-objective nature of the DG routing problem, multi-objective optimization thus becomes a sound framework for analysis and decision-making. However, non-linearity and non-convexity often exist in such optimization problem which cannot be appropriately solved by conventional models such as the weighed sum approach. The purpose of the proposed research is to construct a general framework for optimal route planning for DG transportation in high-density-living environment. Within the framework, multi-criteria risk assessment and multi-objective route planning can be efficiently solved by novel compromise programming models and high performance algorithms. In addition, uncertainty and the issue of constraints pertinent to DG transportation in high-density living will also be addressed. To facilitate analysis and decision-making, a prototype of an intelligent decision support system will be constructed and employed to solve a real-life problem for evaluation and improvement. Since different types of DGs possess different characteristics whose risk assessments and routings call for a wide spectrum of technical knowledge and practical considerations, the proposed research will concentrate only on the transportation of petrochemical-type of DG. The framework can, however, be extended to solve more complicated problems involving the transportation of a large variety of DGs in a high-density environment. The proposed study will advance the research and applications of optimal route planning for DG transportation for high-density living. 危險品在運輸過程中如發生意外將會給人民生活及周圍環境造成嚴重影響, 如:交通中断、人员伤亡、财产损失以及环境破坏等等。因此, 危險品的安全運輸非常重要, 特別是在人口和社會經濟活動高度密集的地區, 這一重要性顯得尤為突出。由於其可能導致災難性後果以及公眾對此類事件反應敏感,危險品運輸決策往往很難制定。因此, 對此類風險進行認真分析與研究對於制定有效決策十分重要。在有關危險品運輸的研究中,風險評估與路徑規劃是兩個重要而又密切相關的問題。近年來, 儘管各種風險模型不斷被開發和利用, 但專門針對高密度環境下的風險評估並不多見。危險品運輸是典型的多目標問題,涉及不同的利益相關者。這些目標之間往往存在一定衝突, 因此, 要找出一個能使所有目標同時達到最優的最佳方案是不現實的。切實可行的方法是尋找一組“妥協解”使目標之間達到某種最佳平衡。鑒於危險品運輸的多目標特性, 多目標優化為風險分析和決策制定提供了一個有效框架。但是, 危險品路徑選擇常涉及非線性和非凸性的問題,傳統的優化模型,如加權疊加,無法有效解決這些問題。本研究旨在建立一個高密度環境下危險品運輸路徑優化的有效框架, 在這一框架內, 多標準風險評估以及多目標路徑優化可通過新穎的妥協規劃模型及高性能的算法得以實現。另外,對高密度環境下危險品運輸的不確定性以及相關的約束問題也將進行研究。為便於分析與決策, 將建立智慧決策支援系統, 對實際問題進行求解, 並對系統進行評價與改進。不同危險品具有不同特性,相應的風險分析與路徑決策需要豐富的知識和實踐經驗,鑒於此,本研究將主要側重于石油化工類危險品的分析,但該框架可擴展至解決更複雜的各類危險品運輸問題。本研究將對高密度環境下危險品運輸路徑優化的研究與應用作出積極貢獻。

449711.label: Realisation of objectives
449711.value: A general multi-objective optimization framework for dangerous good (DG) route planning for high-density living environment has been constructed. A compromise programming method for multi-objective routing of DG transportation with appropriate risk assessment strategy has been formulated (Li et al., 2012,2013). Within the framework, routing of DG vehicles not only considers the operating cost, but also the safety of travelers in the network, the population potentially exposed, and the possible damage inflicted to the surrounding properties and facilities in the event of a DG incident. This part of the research achieves Objective 1. In the context of DG transportation, risk refers to the likelihood of incurring the undesirable consequences of a possible accident. Since the probability of an accident in a link of a route might depend on a variety of factors, it is necessary to find a way to combine the pieces of evidence/probabilities to estimate the composite risk for the link. Instead of using the Bayesian approach, commonly used in the literature, which requires decision-makers to estimate prior and the likelihood and cannot differentiate uncertainty from ignorance, we have developed a novel approach based on the extended Dempster-Shafer theory of evidence by constructing an adaptive robust combination rule to estimate the accident probability under conflicting evidence (Leung and Li, 2014). This work achieves Objective 2. To efficiently solve the complex multi-objective DG transportation problems formulated under the general framework, we have developed a compromise programming method and the corresponding algorithm to search for the optimal solution for decision making (Li et al., 2012). To assist decision makers in identifying Pareto-optimal paths, particularly for non-convex problems, we have constructed an adaptive method and the corresponding algorithm to provide an unbiased approximation of the Pareto-optimal alternatives by adaptively changing the origin and direction of search in the objective space via a dynamic updating procedure (Li et al., 2012). We have further developed a multi-objective genetic algorithm for the determination of optimal routes for DG transportation under conflicting objectives (Li et al., 2013). This part of the research accomplishes objectives 3 and 4. The general framework, the novel methods and the solution algorithms have been applied to the transportation of liquefied petroleum gas in the road network of Hong Kong. All experimental results in the case studies substantiate the conceptual arguments and demonstrate the good performance of the proposed approach ( Li et al., 2012, 2013; Leung and Li, 2014). This achieves objective 5.

449711.label: Major findings and research outcome
449711.value: A general multi-objective optimization framework for dangerous good (DG) route planning for high-density living environment has been constructed. A compromise programming method for multi-objective routing of DG transportation with appropriate risk assessment strategy has been formulated (Li et al., 2012,2013). Within the framework, routing of DG vehicles not only considers the operating cost, but also the safety of travelers in the network, the population potentially exposed, and the possible damage inflicted to the surrounding properties and facilities in the event of a DG incident. In the context of DG transportation, risk refers to the likelihood of incurring the undesirable consequences of a possible accident. Since the probability of an accident in a link of a route might depend on a variety of factors, it is necessary to find a way to combine the pieces of evidence/probabilities to estimate the composite risk for the link. Instead of using the Bayesian approach, commonly used in the literature, which requires decision-makers to estimate prior and the likelihood and cannot differentiate uncertainty from ignorance, we have developed a novel approach based on the extended Dempster-Shafer theory of evidence by constructing an adaptive robust combination rule to estimate the accident probability under conflicting evidence (Leung and Li, 2014). To efficiently solve the complex multi-objective DG transportation problems formulated under the general framework, we have developed a compromise programming method and the corresponding algorithm to search for the optimal solution for decision making (Li et al., 2012). To assist decision makers in identifying Pareto-optimal paths, particularly for non-convex problems, we have constructed an adaptive method and the corresponding algorithm to provide an unbiased approximation of the Pareto-optimal alternatives by adaptively changing the origin and direction of search in the objective space via a dynamic updating procedure (Li et al., 2012). We have further developed a multi-objective genetic algorithm for the determination of optimal routes for DG transportation under conflicting objectives (Li et al., 2013). The general framework, the novel methods and the solution algorithms have been applied to the transportation of liquefied petroleum gas in the road network of Hong Kong. All experimental results in the case studies substantiate the conceptual arguments and demonstrate the good performance of the proposed approach ( Li et al., 2012, 2013; Leung and Li, 2014).

449711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
449711.value: In terms of theoretical undertaking, the general framework developed in this research can be further extended to account for dynamic situations in the transportation of dangerous goods under uncertainty. To entertain dynamic changes of road conditions, stochastic optimization methods can be developed to dynamically determine the optimal path for DG transportation in high density environment. Corresponding solution algorithms can also be constructed for its implementation. To extend the framework to real-time monitoring and routing, we have also looked into the potential of using multi-target sensor network for real-time or near real-time DG transportation planning. With respect to real-life applications, the formulated approach can be applied to other cities with more complicated transportation networks for evaluation and improvement. It can also be employed to study the transportation of other commodities under conflicting objectives.

449711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
449711.value: The transportation of dangerous goods (DG) can significantly affect the human and natural environment if accidents occur during the transportation process. Hong Kong is a large city with high population density and narrow streets. Due to the land constraints, vehicles carrying DG inevitably have to pass through densely populated areas or their vicinities. Therefore, safe DG transportation is of paramount importance in transportation planning. Routing of such vehicles should consider, for example, not only the operating cost, but also the safety of travelers in the network, the population potentially exposed, and the possible damage inflicted to the surrounding properties and facilities in the event of a DG incident. The significance of this research comes from our successful development of a general framework, together with rigorous methodologies and implementation algorithms, for the effective and efficient routing of DG transportation under conflicting objectives in high density cities. The research makes valuable contribution to the theoretical underpinning of the multi-objective route planning of DG transportation and its potential in solving more complicated problems under uncertainty. The research also provides a scientifically sound and practically appealing methodology to solve real-life problems.

449911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
449911.value: This project examines the transition of a Chinese family from the late nineteenth century to the end of the twentieth, covering three generations of the family saga with emphasis on how the family adapted to the political and cultural changes of the time on the one hand while trying hard to maintain their family identity and traditions on the other. The three generations of this family are represented here by Grandfather Ying Lianzhi(英斂之1867-1926), Father Ying Qianli (英千里1900-1969), and Son Ying Ruocheng (英若誠1929-2003). The family history of the Yings will be analyzed against the larger background of political and cultural change in China from the last days of the Manchu dynasty (of which the Yings were part of the Machu ruling clan) to the founding of the Republic and building of a new state ( during which the Yings were instrumental in social and educational reform) and through wars and revolutions to the "new China" created by the Communists ( the last Ying, Ying Ruocheng was a committed socialist who became vice minister of culture from 1986-1990). Grandfather Ying Lianzhi, originally from the Hega clan of the Manchu tribe and tied to the Manchu royalty by marriage, became a liberal reformer in the late Qing period. He was a Confucian scholar but later converted to Catholicism, and he founded the influential newspaper in Tianjin, the "Ta Kung Pao" (Dagong Bao大公報) and the Furen Daxue（輔仁大學, the first Catholic University in China. This project will analyze his consciousness of Manchu ethnicity and his changing identity from a Confucian scholar to become a Catholic. His son, born in the year of Boxer uprising, was raised a devout Catholic with a solid western education. He went to the United Kingdom and the Vatican for higher education and returned to China to take charge of the Catholic University teaching English language and literature. He rose to become a high-official in the Guomindang government and fled with the Nationalists to Taiwan in 1949, leaving his son, Ying Ruocheng, in China to pursuit a socialist path. Ying Ruocheng had gone through many struggles in the wake of cultural confrontations and political campaigns in the PRC, but survived to become a leader of culture particularly in drama and cinema in the Reform era. This project will anlyze both Ying Qianli and Ying Ruocheng's fate and choice in the context of the turbulent political drama of the time. 這個項目集中於研究一個滿洲家族在近代中國的故事， 包括祖父英斂之（英華），是晚清時期的名士，在天津及北京有顯赫的地位。他後來皈依天主教，民國後 創辦輔仁大學和大公報，對近代中國的社會改革和思想維新有很大的影響。他的兒子英千里，繼承家族中天主教及儒家的傳統，留學英國及梵蒂岡，對西方文化和中國社會的關係，有更深的認識，回國後參與高等學校的建設，也在推行英語教育及影視傳媒方面做出貢獻；其子英若誠再次兩方面皆能繼承父業，並在影藝戲劇方面大有所成。不過，英家三代所處的近代中國，是個極其政治紛亂和動蕩的年代，政治派系及意識形態造成知識分子的分裂和困擾，家族成員也難免各持己見或膈散東西，就如英千里在國民黨治下當官，隨之赴台，而英若誠則留在中共政權下服務新中國。本項計劃以英家三代之變故，以及其在滿漢之間，儒家與天主教之間，中國與西方之間，及共產黨與國民黨，中共與臺灣之間的頏頡與徘徊，作爲分析的基調。

449911.label: Realisation of objectives
449911.value: There are three objectives for this research project: (1) to construct a family history of three generations of the Yings: grandfather Ying Lianzhi, father Ying Qianli, and son Ying Ruocheng. This objective has been mostly achieved with published papers and conference articles on them especially on Ying Lianzhi; (2) to analyse the problems of enthnic, cultural and national identity confronted by the Ying family. In this regard, this project has produced one article analysing Ying Lianzhi's Manchu identity and another on his conversion from Confucianism to Catholicism; there is also one research output analysing the fusion of three cultural identities that shaped the family tradition of the Yings; (3)to analyse the role of "cultural middleman" in modern Chinese history using the Yings as illustrative cases. The PI has written several articles on the role of "cultural middleman"(or cultural comprador) in modern China, and this project attempts to examine the Yings in this particular context. The PI and the Co-I at this stage have been making an attempt to put together a book manuscript on the history of the Yings with the second and third objectives as central analytical themes. At this point about two third of the book has been completed. According to plan, the project will probably take another year to finalise the book manuscript and ready for submission for publication review.

449911.label: Major findings and research outcome
449911.value: This research project focuses on three generations of the Ying family. Grandfather Ying Lianzhi has been the better known person because of his role as founder of the Furen Catholic University and the popular newspaper "Da Gong Bao". However, only Father Fang Hao has done serious academic study on Ying before Hou Jie and I engaged in this project a few years ago. Father Ying Qianli has been the most interesting figure from the point of view of the Nationalist-Communist struggle as he was the only family member who sided with the Nationalists accompanying Chiang Kai-shek to Taiwan. Yet his life experience in Taiwan is basically an untold story, and this is also the most challenging part of our project. Ying Ruocheng is the most popular and internationally known member of the family because of his role as actor, director, producer of several films and dramas, and as deputy minister of Culture. However, this project covers the other aspects of his life----his family upbringing, his Catholic connection, and his cultural identity---- those dimensions relatively neglected in his biographies. Moreover, we believe that this family saga would reveal many social and political problems and agonizing decisions made by Chinese intellectuals during those turbulent periods of modern Chinese history. The PI and Co-I have been working together on a book-length manuscript comprising ten chapters plus footnotes, bibliography and appendices which is more than halfway done. We believe that the final manuscript will be ready for publication review in 2015.

449911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
449911.value: In the coming year the authors will concentrate on writing the remaining chapters. Further research agenda will include an investigation of the fate of the Manchus as a race and as a culture in modern Chinese history, inter-faith dailogues and interactions between Confucianism and Christianity, and the continuation of the family saga after Ying Ruocheng.

449911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
449911.value: This project is a study of the Ying family, or better described, a reconstruction of the family saga of the Yings in three generations. Grandfather Ying Lianzhi, was a Manchu warrior turned Confucian scholar in the late Qing period, who then became a devout Catholic who founded the "Da Gong Bao" a well circulated newspaper and the Catholic Furen University in Beijing. He lived in the turbulent years of reform and revolution, and maintained a delicate balance between the tensions of tradition and modernity, and between Christianity and Confucianism. Father Ying Qianli confronted a different set of contenting and contradicting forces presented by Republican China: culture and technology, Nationalist and Communist orientations, etc. When the CCP took over Beiing, he went along with the Nationalists to Taiwan where continued to be an educator, culturalist, and Catholic leader. However, his son Ying Ruocheng decided to take a diiferent path, remaining in Mainland China and pursued a career in drama and cultural performance in the new socialsit system. This is a facinating family story, but more important, it reveals many facets of social, cultural and political life of a rapidly changing China in the last two centuries, and how these politcal, social and cultural transformation impacted personal and familial relations and cultural identities.

450011.label: Project Title(Chinese)
450011.value: 外部性与多方议价：内生机制的作用

450011.label: Project Objectives
450011.value: To develop a multi-agent bargaining model with endogenous matching To investigate when the presence of externalities can cause bargaining delay To improve understanding of interactions among economic agents in thin markets To gain insights into the competition between two cable TV providers in Hong Kong
rows: To develop a multi-agent bargaining model with endogenous matching
To investigate when the presence of externalities can cause bargaining delay
To improve understanding of interactions among economic agents in thin markets
To gain insights into the competition between two cable TV providers in Hong Kong

450011.label: Realisation of objectives
450011.value: The first objective of this project is to develop a multi-agent bargaining model with endogenous matching. Towards this goal, I developed several game theoretic models of bargaining between one seller and multiple potential buyers. A common feature of these models is that the encounter between seller and buyers is endogenously determined. More specifically, I analyzed two models with an active seller, who can decide, at any time, which buyer to bargain with. I also developed a model with active buyers. The endogenous matching formulation stands in contrast to existing studies in which the encounter between seller and buyers is assumed to be purely random. It is a plausible and more realistic modeling choice for strategic interactions in non-anonymous thin markets. This objective is fully achieved. The second objective is to investigate when the presence of externalities can cause bargaining inefficiency. I analyzed the active-seller model with a deterministic deadline. The game has a unique equilibrium with immediate agreement regardless of whether the externalities are positive or negative. In a two-buyer game, the good is always sold to the efficient buyer when externalities are negative. With positive externalities, the equilibrium allocation may be inefficient. I further studied the model without a deadline. It is shown that with two buyers and negative externalities, delay may arise in a cyclic equilibrium provided that the seller is sufficiently more patient than the buyers. This objective is also fully achieved. The third objective is to improve our understanding of the interactions among economic agents in thin markets. My theoretical findings convey two messages: (1) seller’s strategic search for a best buyer leads to efficient outcomes in most cases; (2) most of the trading surplus goes to the active seller. Nevertheless, I also realized that other market mechanism such as auction may deliver different outcomes. Overall, I consider this objective as mainly achieved. Another objective is to gain insights into the competition between two cable TV providers in Hong Kong. My theoretical findings provide new insights into the welfare analysis of the local Cable TV market; however, to deliver useful policy suggestions, sufficient empirical analysis and good understanding of the legal environment are indispensable. Thus, I consider this objective only as partially achieved, and further exploration requires cross-disciplinary collaborations. Finally, I shall mention that the project has gone beyond its original objectives. As an extension, I studied a wage bargaining model with outside option and obtained several interesting results.

450011.label: Major findings and research outcome
450011.value: In this project I study the price negotiation between one seller and multiple potential buyers on the sale of one indivisible good with identity-dependent externalities. The main theoretical endeavor is to examine the role of endogenous matching. In various bargaining games, I investigate whether the equilibrium outcome is efficient, i.e., no delay occurs in equilibrium and the equilibrium allocation of the good is efficient. I first analyzed a finite-horizon bargaining game with an active seller. It is shown that the game has a unique equilibrium with immediate agreement regardless of whether the externalities are positive or negative. In a two-buyer game, the good is always sold to the efficient buyer when externalities are negative. When externalities are positive, the equilibrium allocation may be inefficient. This part of work is done jointly with an M.Phil student under my supervision. The main results are included in the student’s thesis submitted in March 2013. I also studied the model with an infinite horizon. It is shown that with two buyers and negative externalities, delay may arise in a cyclic equilibrium provided that the seller is sufficiently more patient than the buyers. The driving force behind the cyclic equilibrium here is very different from that in Jehiel and Moldovano (1995 RES). A working paper combining the results in both the finite horizon and the infinite horizon model is under preparation. As an extension, I studied a wage bargaining model with outside option. In reality, a job candidate often has to negotiate with several potential employers on a wage contract; thus, it falls into the bargaining framework studied in this project. In this paper, we simplify the situation by focusing on the negotiation between the job candidate and his current employer and replacing the outside job opportunities by a fixed-value outside option. We show that a continuum of wage level can be sustained in equilibrium. More interestingly, opting-out may also occur in equilibrium, and this finding stands in stark contrast to the existing studies. Our results provide a game theoretic explanation for the phenomena such as preemptive contract renegotiation and preemptive wage increase. The cyclic equilibrium that we construct in this paper shares features with that of the infinite-horizon bargaining game between one seller and two buyers with negative externalities. The paper, Opting Out in Wage Renegotiation, is now under revision and resubmission for the Journal of Economics & Management Strategy.

450011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
450011.value: The main goal of this project is to investigate efficiency implications of endogenous matching in bargaining between one seller and multiple potential buyers on the sale of an indivisible good. The idea of endogenous matching originated from my previous work on one-to-many bargaining, whereas the unique and crucial element of this project is the presence of externalities. The same idea can be further extended to various multilateral bargaining situations. In an ongoing project, my collaborator and I investigate efficiency implications of endogenous matching in network bargaining. More specifically, we consider the markets in which economic agents need to be in some specific relationships in order to trade. Such a market is modeled as a network. We show that on homogeneous networks, decentralized bargaining with endogenous matching always leads to an efficient outcome. Another direction for future research is to study dynamic legislative bargaining with endogenously determined agenda setter. The idea of endogenizing agenda setter is similar to that of endogenous matching in this project. My collaborator and I are currently working on some simple examples. If our preliminary analysis delivers promising results, we will start a new project on this topic soon.

450011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
450011.value: In recent years, two cable TV providers in Hong Kong, Cable TV and Now TV, have been actively bidding for the exclusive right to broadcast major sports events. When the winning company gains greater commercial revenue, a negative external effect is imposed on the rival. A similar situation is the sale of an innovation in an oligopolistic market: while the firm that obtains the innovation will get higher profit, other firms will suffer losses. It is both interesting and important to understand how economic agents interact in such thin markets. In particular, it is important to investigate under what conditions the outcome of market competition is efficient. My approach in this project is to study bargaining between one seller and several potential buyers on the sale of an indivisible good. I analyzed several game theoretic models and identified conditions under which the equilibrium outcome is efficient. A crucial feature and also a theoretical innovation of these models is that the seller can decide, at any time, which buyer to bargain with. The theoretical findings may deepen our understanding of strategic interactions of economic agents in thin markets and provide new insights into the welfare analysis of market competitions.

To examine how individual-level factors, such as education, transformative life experience, and involvement in popular contention, affect trust in the Center. 450111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
450111.value: The project aims to examine the patterns, significance and dynamics of change of public trust in Chinese central authorities. National surveys in China from 1993 to 2008 suggest that public confidence in the central government has remained strong and stable. Although they deserve credit for engineering continuous economic growth, the Chinese central authorities are also responsible for worsening political corruption, widening income inequality and deepening judicial injustice. Why does popular trust in the Center seem unaffected by these problems? Scholars have offered several explanations: (1) strong economic performance has delayed the emergence of “critical citizens”; (2) observed confidence in the central government represents diffuse system support rather than performance-based trust in government; (3) traditional cultural values cultivate trust in central authorities; (4) the ruling Party’s political propaganda shields central leaders from popular discontent; (5) government-controlled education and media indoctrinate confidence about the ruling party. The project addresses the puzzle by examining whether the measures of trust used in previous surveys are too broad and too general to capture subtle yet significant fluctuations of trust in the Center. Two hypotheses will be tested: (1) individuals who sound similarly confident about the Center may have different degrees of trust; (2) individuals who sound similarly confident about the Center may have different notions about what the Center is. The project employs qualitative and quantitative methods and will consist of four integral parts: (1) interviewing ordinary citizens and petitioners in Beijing to ascertain how they reflect on and adjust their trust in the Center; (2) surveying rural and urban residents randomly drawn from four purposively selected counties and districts; (3) surveying petitioners in Beijing; (4) adding county/district level data to the 2008 China Survey. The project will be completed in 36 months and it is expected to produce several articles in international refereed academic journals. The project aims to make three contributions to theories of political trust: (1) refine scholarly understanding of trust in the national government by investigating whether the object of such trust can be a hierarchy of central authorities rather than a unitary central state; (2) re-examine the relative importance of incumbent-based trust and regime-based trust in the light of evidence from China; (3) advance the debate about the impact of distrust of the national authorities on any preference for systemic changes by examining how distrust of the Center is associated with proactive claim against it. 過去二十年﹐歷次全國調查均顯示中國民眾對中央政府高度信任。對此現象﹐學者們意見分岐。有些學者認為中國的調查資料不可信。其他學者不質疑調查資料的可靠性﹐試圖從經濟發展﹑政治文化﹑政府治理﹑政治教育等方面探索原因。本課題着重從政治信任的測量方法角度探討民眾對中央政府的信任的類型﹑意義和變化機製。首先﹐本課題將探討通用的測量指標是否過於寬泛﹐以至於放大民眾對中央的信任。其次﹐本課題將分析運用細緻的測量指標能否改進有關政治信任與政治態度之關聯的分析。最後﹐本課題將結合量化材料和訪談分析政治信任的變化方式和背後的原因。本課題的操作時間是從2011年8月1日至2014年7月31日。
