450611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
450611.value: This study aims to examine the information content of limit order book and price discovery of the U.S. Treasury bonds. Most existing studies have focused on the informativeness of limit orders in the equity market. In this project, we focus on the US Treasury market. The US Treasury market provides a cleaner setting to examine the order strategy of informed traders. This is because it is a pure limit order market and does not have specialists competing with the limit orders. The other advantage of working on the U.S. Treasury market is that we can control for public information shocks and focus on private information flow. Using market survey data of pre-scheduled macroeconomic announcements and events, we can measure unexpected shocks of public information flow. In the Treasury market, private information results from certain investors’ superior ability of interpreting public information or access to exclusive trading information. Our focus is the role of private information in the price discovery process as well as its interaction with public information arrival. Finally, using the rich dataset from BrokerTec, an electronic trading platform of US Treasury notes and bonds, we are able to perform more powerful analysis than existing studies. The BrokerTec dataset contains information of all transactions and the entire limit order book of on-the-run U.S. Treasury notes and bonds. Motivated by existing literature, our empirical analysis focuses on the following issues: What is the information content in limit orders relative to market orders? In particular, does order flow have predictive power of future bond returns? Does the depth and dispersion of limit order book capture the information content in limit order book? Furthermore, if limit order book contains information about future bond returns, over what horizons such information has predictive power? Finally, since we are able to identify the days and time of pre-scheduled macroeconomic announcements, we can examine the information content of limit order book during the pre- versus post-announcement periods as well as announcement days versus non-announcement days. Our study will help to shed new lights on whether the limit order book is informative and, if so, which part of the limit order book is most informative. The results of this project will not only fill a gap in the extant literature but also help us to understand the information flow and its role in the price discovery of U.S. Treasury market. 本研究旨在探討限價市場的信息內容。現有的大多數研究都集中在股票市場。在這個項目中，我們專注於美國國債市場。美國國債市場提供一個更好的研究環境，研究知情交易者的策略。這是因為它是一個純限價市場市場，沒有交易員與限價訂單競爭。美國國債市場上的其他優勢是我們可以控制公共信息的衝擊，並注重對私人信息研究。使用宏觀經濟公告和活動的市場調查數據，我們可以衡量公共信息流的衝擊。 在國債市場，私人信息是指若干投資者解釋公眾信息能力或獲得排他性的交易信息。我們的重點是在價格發現過程中私人信息與公共信息到達互動。我們的實證分析以下問題上：在市場訂單相對限價訂單的信息內容是什麼？限價訂單的深度和分散的信息內容是什麼？此外，如果限價訂單包含對未來債券收益率的信息，有什麼預測能力？最後，因為我們能夠識別宏觀經濟公告的日期和時間，我們可以研究公告前及公告後以及公佈天與非公告天的信息內容。這個項目的結果將不僅填補現存文獻中的差距，也有助於我們了解在美國國債市場的價格發現及信息流動

450611.label: Realisation of objectives
450611.value: We list below how the objectives are realized: 1. In understand the type of orders informed traders use in the US Treasury market, the paper examines the informativeness of different types of orders by examining order performance in the US Treasury market around pre-scheduled announcement. If informed traders tend to place a particular type of order, then it should have better performance. We examine order performance in two senses. First, we examine the price improvement associated with posting a limit orders accounting for eventual risk of non-execution. This is the ex-ante measure proposed in Harris and Hasbrouck (1996). Then we examine how an order performs immediately after execution i.e. what is the price impact of an order. This is the ex-post measure proposed in Harris and Hasbrouck (1996). Thus our study is among the first which examine the performance of orders in a limit order market setting in the US Treasury market. 2. In understand how order submission strategies change under different market environments, this paper investigates order submission strategies around release of pre-scheduled macroeconomic announcement. One significant factor which affects order submission strategies is public information arrival, during which information environment changes drastically. We first examine the submission, cancellation and fill rates around pre-scheduled announcements. Then we examine the performance of orders under information uncertainty during the pre-announcement period and resolution of uncertainty during the post-announcement period respectively. Furthermore, we examine how order submission strategies vary with the magnitude of public information shocks. Thus our study sheds light on when informed traders enter market and how they response to public information shock. 3. In understand the predictive power of limit order book, we study the predictive power of orders using Kaniel and Liu test (2006). We divide the population of market orders and limit orders into two samples. The first sample consists of all market orders and aggressive limit orders i.e. limit orders submitted at the best quote and better than best quotes. The second sample consists of all market orders and all limit orders. The purpose is to compare the relative informativeness of market orders with limit orders of different aggressiveness. The study thus sheds light on the predictive power of market and limit orders under different information environment during the pre- and post-announcement periods

450611.label: Major findings and research outcome
450611.value: We find that submission of limit orders is more active than market orders, regardless of information environment. More than half the limit orders are posted behind the best quote. Furthermore, we find that traders tend to place larger and less aggressive orders after release of announcements. This is potentially related to the fact that the fill rate of these orders is higher during the post-announcement period. The number of orders submitted increase with the magnitude of public information shock. However, the size of public information shock does not seem to have significant effect on the distribution of order size and order aggressiveness. Looking at order performance at the time of submission, we find that aggressive orders, especially orders at the best quote, lose in terms of ex-ante order performance. This finding is contrary to Harris and Hasbrouk (1996) that aggressive orders perform better. Our results suggest that impatient traders tend to lose in terms of price improvement after announcement in the Treasury market. Instead, limit orders submitted at behind the best quote have better price improvement during the post-announcement period. This finding offers a potential explanation of why orders become less aggressive after announcements: after accounting for execution risk, the price improvement of submitting behind best limit orders is larger during the post-announcement period. Looking at ex-post performance ( i.e. immediate price impact) of orders, we find that market orders have negative performance. However, ex-post performance of market orders improves during the post-announcement period. This suggests that the price impact of market orders is smaller after resolution of uncertainty. We also find that limit orders placed more than 1 tick behind the best quote in general have the best ex-post performance. Looking at the return predictive power of orders, we find that market orders in general are more informative, particularly when spread is small. Moreover, market orders are more informative during the post announcement period. This finding contrast with findings from equity market such as Beber and Caglio (2005), Bloomfield et al. (2005) and Kaniel and Liu (2004) which suggest that limit orders are more informative. One potential explanation is that private information in the form of sophisticated interpretation of announcement tends to dissipates quickly after announcement. Thus traders tend to place market order when private information is transitory as suggested in Kaniel and Liu (2004)

450611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
450611.value: This study aims to examine order informativeness in the US Treasury market. In particular, whether informed traders tend to use limit orders or market orders. Electronic limit order book has become the prevalent form of market structure. In particular, the U.S. Treasury market has switched from a voice-brokered market to an essentially pure limit order market since 2003. However, given the size and importance of the Treasury market, few studies have examined private information in the Treasury market compared to the voluminous amount of research produced for the U.S. equity market. This study fill the gap in the literature by examining submission strategy in the U.S. Treasury market around pre-scheduled macroeconomic news release. Consistent with findings in literature, order submissions are more active after announcement. With release of public information, traders tend to place larger and less aggressive limit orders. We also find that impatient traders submitting aggressive orders tend to lose in terms of price improvement during the post-announcement period. Limit orders submitted at behind the best quote have better price improvement and lowest price impact. Nevertheless, contrary to findings using equity market data, market orders are found to be more informative, especially during the post-announcement period.

451311.label: Project Objectives
451311.value: To advance the theory of international business on emerging markets in three significant ways: 1) to construct a comprehensive framework to model the influence of institutional uncertainty and reference groups on an MNE’s strategic decisions such as the establishment of an HCHQ; 2) to explain how an HCHQ creates value by investigating the direct and contingent effects of the HCHQ on the performance of an MNE’s foreign subsidiaries across different subnational locations; and 3) to shift the research attention toward an MNE’s strategy, structure, and subsidiary performance within large emerging markets. To provide implications for managers of MNEs to better understand how MNEs transform from foreign entrants to strategic insiders in large emerging markets over time, and how they interact with local incumbents and host governments in the institutional context of large emerging markets. To provide implications for policy makers in emerging markets by highlighting the within-host-country heterogeneity among subnational regions of a large emerging market in terms of economic development and institutional uncertainty. To build a rich dataset for a series of future studies on MNEs’ operations in BRIC countries, and develop a set of longitudinal indexes on the national and subnational institutional environments of BRIC, which should generate important and long-term impacts for large audience of academic researchers, managers, and policy makers.

451311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
451311.value: Conventional research on multinational enterprises (MNEs) suggests that in an era of global competition, MNEs can no longer afford to have “kings of countries”. Not surprisingly, consistent with this popular wisdom, host country headquarters (HCHQ) became an endangered species, after most MNEs simplified their host country structures in developed countries. However, in apparent contradiction to the prevailing practice in developed economies, HCHQ has been increasingly adopted by many MNEs in large and important emerging markets such as BRIC countries (Brazil, Russia, India, and China). Given this trend toward the adoption rather than elimination of HCHQ in emerging markets, it is noteworthy that current research seems silent on examining this emerging and important organizational form. The primary goal of this proposed project is to help develop our understanding of why HCHQs have been re-emerging as an important organizational structure for MNEs, and to explore whether and how the establishment of an HCHQ influences an MNE’s foreign subsidiary performance in that market. Drawing on an institutional perspective, we propose that the establishment of HCHQ is an MNE’s strategic response to the national-level and subnational-level institutional uncertainty of an emerging market, and also a mimetic strategy employed by the MNE to model itself on its home peers and local partners. We then propose that the HCHQ will be used as an organizational infrastructure upon which an MNE can enhance its institutional capability to improve the foreign subsidiary’s performance in a large emerging market, and that such value will be contingent on institutional conditions across different subnational locations within that host country. This proposed project will be among the first to investigate a relatively unexplored organizational form – an MNE’s HCHQ in a large emerging market – which is a critical link in completing the picture of MNEs’ operations in foreign countries. Moreover, the shift of research toward the heterogeneous subnational regions within large emerging markets represents a new research direction and advances the theory of international business on emerging markets. Empirically, we will use a large longitudinal dataset from Japanese firms’ subsidiaries in BRIC countries during the 1990-2009 period. We will build a large longitudinal dataset and develop two sets of indexes – Subnational-level Institutional Uncertainty Index and Subnational-level Institutional Development Index for BRIC countries – which are expected to have important and long-term impacts for researchers, policy makers, and managers. 傳統的跨國公司研究認為，在全球競爭的環境下，跨國公司將無法再承擔成立“諸侯鼎立”的成本。與這種流行的觀點相一致，很多跨國公司將他們在國外的組織結構進行了精簡，以至於東道國企業總部這種組織形式在發達國家幾近絕跡。 而與在發達國家做法明顯不同的是，許多跨國公司在市場巨大的發展中國家，譬如金磚四國（巴西，俄羅斯，印度和中國），都采用了東道國企業總部這種形式。許多的商業報道也都在關註這些新興的東道國中心。在發展中國家，東道國企業總部這種組織形式非但沒有被摒棄，反而正被大量采用。但是現有的研究似乎忽視了這種重要的方興未艾的組織模式。 本研究旨在解釋為何東道國企業總部被重新視作一種重要的組織結構，並探索東道國企業總部的建立會對跨國公司海外子公司的績效產生何種影響。從制度理論出發，我們提出東道國企業總部的建立是跨國公司對新興市場存在的國家層面和地方層面的制度不確定性的回應，同時也是一種學習同行和當地企業的模仿性戰略。我們接著提出東道國企業總部可以作為企業的基礎結構，用來增強跨國公司的制度能力，從而促進在新興市場的海外子公司的業績。但這種作用的大小要視東道國內不同地方的制度環境而定。 本研究將為東道國企業總部這種組織形式今后的研究抛砖引玉。以往的研究中較少涉及建立在發展中國家的東道國企業總部，但這種組織結構卻對理解跨國公司的海外運作不可或缺。同時，研究的重心將會轉向發展中國家內部的地域差異，為國際企業管理的研究指出新的發展方向。在實證方面，我們選取了日本企業在金磚四國的子公司作為樣本，並獲取了1990年到2009年的縱向數據。我們將會建立一個大型的縱向數據庫，並建立兩組指標：地方層面的制度不確定性指標和地方層面的制度發展指標。這兩組指標將對研究人員、政策制定者和企業管理人員產生重要深遠的影響。

451311.label: Realisation of objectives
451311.value: We have fully realized the objectives set in the proposal and addressed the reviewers’ comments. Advancing the theory of international business in emerging economies. We made progress in three areas. 1) A paper to provide a power explanation of this important phenomenon, which is now under R&R at Strategic Management Journal (SMJ). 2) A paper to examine the extent to which subnational region effects can explain the performance variation, which is published in Journal of International Business Studies (JIBS). 3) A paper to argue that an MNE’s location choice for its HCHQ is determined by the interplay between the strategic roles of HCHQ in the organizational space of the MNE and the institutional space external and internal to the MNE. This paper is published in JIBS. Another paper is published in SMJ to further extend the work on subnational institutions. Providing implications for multinational managers. We have focused on two areas. 1) We had two papers published in JIBS, one in SMJ, and another one under R&R at SMJ. We also have a set of related papers presented in different conferences. All these papers are related to the importance of considering local business groups and governments as well as subnational contexts in emerging markets. In the Discussion sections of these papers, we also provide detailed implications and suggestions to multinational managers. 2) We conducted field work by visiting some MNEs’ China HQ. During the meetings with these senior managers, we shared our recent research on MNEs’ strategy, structure, and subsidiary in emerging markets. Offering suggestions for policy makers. To achieve this objective, we have made progress in two ways. 1) The papers we have developed highlight how subnational institutions may affect the attractiveness of the location, the behaviors of the multinational firms, and the outcome of the FDI activities. In the Discussion sections of these papers, we also provide detailed implications and suggestions to policy makers. 2) PI participated in forums and roundtable discussion with regard to the regional HQ location choice by MNEs in Asia Pacific. The arguments and comments made by the PI were largely based on the findings from this project. Building dataset and index. To achieve this objective, we have built the dataset on Fortune Global 500 Corporations’ subsidiaries in China and the parent firm information. we developed subnational-level index for China’s provinces, which has been used to develop a paper published in JIBS

451311.label: Major findings and research outcome
451311.value: The major findings and research outcome can been seen from the papers developed from this project, which are summarized as below. In a paper (under R&R at SMJ), using a sample of Fortune Global 500 firms in China from 1979 to 2005, we find evidence supporting the idea that the establishment of a national HQ in a large emerging market is a structural solution to increase the MNC’s power with status relative to local powerful actors. We further find that the high level of trade interdependence between the MNC’s home country and the focal host country serves as a condition that magnifies the power effects, and heightens establishment propensities for a national HQ. In a paper (published at JIBS), using data on a sample of Fortune Global 500 corporations in China (1979-2005), we find that MNEs operating in FDI restricted/global industries are more likely to choose Beijing over Shanghai as the HCHQ location. We also find that Beijing’s relative geographic proximity to an MNE’s global HQ/portfolio of subsidiaries in China is positively associated with the likelihood of the MNE’s choosing Beijing over Shanghai as the HCHQ location. Further, we find that An MNE’s home country-China administrative/cultural distance is negatively associated with the likelihood of the MNE’s choosing Beijing over Shanghai as the HCHQ location. In another paper (published at JIBS), we empirically decompose the variance of the performance of Fortune Global 500 Corporations’ subsidiaries in China during 1998-2006. Results show that not only are subnational region effects statistically significant in explaining the variation of subsidiary performance, but their interactions with industry, corporate parent, and home country effects are also significant and economically important. We further show that subnational region effects tend to be stronger in the period prior to China’s WTO accession and in the country’s less-developed subnational regions. Our findings highlight the importance of considering both the direct and indirect roles of subnational region in shaping firms’ strategy and performance in international business research. In a paper (published at SMJ), our empirical results, based on panel data analysis of Chinese listed firms, suggest that the level of interdependence between Chinese and foreign firms in China in multiple forms, including symbiotic, competitive, and partner interdependencies, is positively associated with the level of the Chinese firms’ OFDI activities. However, Chinese firms with higher levels of state ownership are less susceptible to the pressures imposed by foreign firms to invest abroad.

451311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
451311.value: We propose potential for further development course of action as below. Supplemental research will make this study even richer by using different settings. First, a useful extension might be using a sample of Fortune Global 500 firms in a single but different emerging market to further test the theoretical framework. Second, , examining MNEs from the same emerging market and investing in foreign countries might be an interesting extension. Third, it would be very insightful to use the data on Fortune Global 500 firms investing in both developed and emerging countries. Additional data will be collected for future studies. The new directions are the introduction of new dependent variables by looking at how the establishment of HCHQ could influence left-hand side variables. Future studies may examine the effects on performance at different levels of performance (i.e., corporate, host country, and individual subsidiary), and various dimensions of performance (i.e., survival and profitability, productivity, and innovation). Future studies may also revisit and shed new light on many of the classic issues that have been studied for decades, such as market entry, expatriate management, organization structures, subsidiary relations, and location choice. New theoretical lens might be adopted to examine these new issues.

451311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
451311.value: Conventional wisdom suggests that in an era of global competition, multinational enterprises (MNEs) can no longer afford to have “kings of countries”, leading to the removing of their host country headquarters (HCHQ) in developed countries. However, HCHQ has been increasingly adopted by many MNEs in large and important emerging markets such as China. Our project is among the first to explore underlying reasons and related strategic issues for this important phenomenon and the consequences of establishing HCHQ. We find strong evidence supporting the idea that the establishment of HCHQ in a large emerging market is a structural solution to increase the MNC’s power with status relative to local powerful actors. Further, we find that an MNE’s location choice for its HCHQ in the geographic space of host country is determined by the interplay between the strategic roles of HCHQ and the institutional space external and internal to the MNE. As we open the “black box” of an MNE’s portfolio of operations under the HCHQ in a large emerging market, we further highlight the importance of considering both the direct and indirect roles of subnational region in shaping firms’ strategy and performance. Our research has important research, managerial, and policy implications.

451811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
451811.value: Is it possible to have a reading difficulty in Chinese but not in English or vice versa? What does this dissociation (or overlap) indicate about cognitive and perceptual underpinnings of reading? The proposed study attempts to answer these questions by testing for reading difficulties in Chinese and English among 80 Hong Kong second graders with dyslexia (in Chinese) and 80 children without dyslexia matched by age, nonverbal IQ, and parental background measure s. All children will be tested on phonological processing, morphological awareness, and rapid automatized naming skills, measures typically linked to reading skills in one or both orthographies, as well as English word reading. Children scoring in the lowest 20% on the English word reading test (based on norms from other Hong Kong second graders) will be designated as having specific reading difficulties in English. Testing will yield a) an estimate of the co-occurrence of reading difficulties in Chinese and English and b) an indication of those cognitive tasks that best explain Chinese dyslexia, English word reading problems, and/or both, in Hong Kong Chinese children. We will also use event-related potentials (ERPs) to further explore the extent to which auditory and/or speech perception may underpin reading difficulties in Chinese as a first language (L1) and English as a foreign language (EFL). Here, 15 children each in one of four categories (1) dyslexic in Chinese; adequate English word reading, 2) dyslexic in Chinese; English reading problems, 3) low word reading in English only, 4) no reading difficulties in either Chinese or English) will be tested on four contrasts, two auditory (temporal processing and amplitude modulation) and two speech (voice onset time and lexical tone, both in Chinese) tasks. All will be administered as forced choice behavioral decision tasks, with both accuracy and speed data recorded. ERP responses to general auditory patterns and speech-specific responses will also be recorded . Data analyses will focus on distinguishing which tasks best identify those with and without reading difficulties in Chinese and English, demonstrating the importance of a) general temporal and rhythmic auditory processing and b) segmental and suprasegmental speech perception for reading in Chinese and English. Practically, such results may suggest optimal testing tools for diagnosing dyslexia in Chinese and/or reading difficulties in EFL. Theoretically, results will demonstrate similarities and differences in cognitive and perceptual correlates of reading difficulties in Chinese as compared to EFL, as well as links across these. 摘要 閱讀困難者是否可能只在中文方面有閱讀困難，而英文方面則沒有﹖或者，他們只在英文方面有閱讀困難，而沒有中文閱讀困難﹖在認知和感知層面上，是什麼原因令到閱讀困難者只在一個語言方面有讀寫困難﹖或者在這兩個語言方面都有閱讀困難呢﹖通過對80名在中文閱讀有困難的二年級香港兒童及80 名與閱讀障礙者在年齡，非語言智商及父母教育程度等方面相匹配的正常兒童進行測量，從而回答上述問題。我們將會對這兩組小學生進行多項測試，例如語音測試，語素測試，快速命名測試，一些關於閱讀技巧的拼寫測試和英文單字閱讀測試。在英文單字閱讀測試中得分最低的20%小學生（基準是從其他香港小學二年級學生來得來的），會被列為英語閱讀困難者。 通過此研究，一方面我們希望能夠對中英文閱讀障礙同時發生的可能性進行預測，另一方面希望通過此研究發現能夠預測中文或英文或者在二者上都有閱讀困難的預測變量。 同時，我們將使用事件相關電位（ERPs）的測量方法深入探討聽覺和/或言語感知在何種程度上能解釋以中文作為第一語言（L1）的閱讀困難，和英文作為外語（EFL）的閱讀困難。在這個部分共有四個分組，包括（1）中文讀寫困難，但有足夠英文生字閱讀能力；（2）同時有中文閱讀障礙和英文閱讀困難；（3）只有英文閱讀困難；（4）在中文和英文方面都沒有閱讀困難。每一組將有15名小朋友參與聽覺（包括時序及幅度感知任務）和兩個語言部任務（包括中文語音開始時間及聲調任務）的測試。在這些測試中，小朋友會選擇一個他們認為是正确的答案（行為選擇測試），準确度和速度都會被記錄，並同時記錄他們的事件相關電位（ERP）信號。數據分析主要用於發現哪些測試最能找出小朋友有或者沒有中文和英文閱讀困難。繼而得出a）一般時間和有節奏的處理；b）語音分割和前語音分割在中文和英文閱讀的重要性。 實際上，我們將會在這個研究的結果中找出最佳的診斷中文讀寫障礙和/或英文閱讀困難的測試工具。從理論上說，結果將會展示出認知和感知跟中文閱讀困難和英文閱讀困難的關聯的相同和不同的地方。

451811.label: Realisation of objectives
451811.value: We had five objectives for this project (see project objectives). Overall, we achieved these. Behaviorally, we have developed three English reading tasks. They were the silent word reading task without context, silent word reading with context and word reading aloud task. The three tasks can be successfully used to distinguish the poor English readers from typical developing English readers. These measures might be very useful for helping to develop a standardized English reading task for diagnosing and screening those children with English reading difficulties for Chinese-English bilingual children. Indeed, it would be nice to expand these to other places in the world that might want to test for English as a second language reading. The reading task data has led to one paper, which is under review (revise/resubmit). We also developed a 4-stage model for Chinese word reading and English word reading. We found that for Chinese word reading, auditory sensitivity was associated with speech perception, which was related to Chinese word reading mainly through its relations to morphological awareness and rapid automatized naming. In contrast, for English word reading, we found in addition to phonological awareness, Chinese speech prosody was also directly associated with English word recognition. At the neurophysiology level, we found that Cantonese-English speech children showed robust mismatch negativeness (MMNs) in processing Chinese lexical tones, place of articulation and VOT. They also showed robust MMNs in processing the violations of acoustic features of English lexical stress. These findings should be very useful in distinguishing those children with reading difficulties in both Chinese and English from the typically developing children.

451811.label: Major findings and research outcome
451811.value: A number of important findings, leading to several publications in some top journals in education and psychology research as well as in neuroscience (see the papers listed in Part C), have come out of this project. Specifically, the findings and outcomes of this study were the following: 1). We developed measures for English word reading. These measures are reliable in testing Chinese children’s ability in reading English. 2). We also found that some cognitive- and linguistic-related factors were uniquely predictive of Chinese children’s English and Chinese word reading. For example, pure copying skills and delayed copying as well as visual-spatial skills were found to be significantly correlated with Chinese word reading. 3). We also found that there was a transfer from Chinese metalinguistic skills to English word reading even though Chinese and English differ strongly from each other. For example, Chinese phonological awareness and Chinese speech prosody were found to directly associate with English word reading in Cantonese-English speaking Hong Kong children. 4). MMNs and p-MMN can be used as neural markers for Cantonese speech and English stress perception in Cantonese-English speaking Hong Kong children, which may be informative in identifying children with speech disorders in either Cantonese or English. 5). Our training study on Cantonese children showed that parent-child joint writing has positive effects on children’s Chinese language and literacy skill development and parents use different strategies in parent-child joint writing. Collectively, the findings and outcomes of this project are both of theoretical and practical importance for understanding Chinese children’s word reading and speech perception in both L1 Chinese and L2 English.

451811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
451811.value: Although there are several important findings reported in this project, much remains unknown regarding the mechanisms of L1 Chinese and L2 English reading in Chinese-English speaking bilinguals as well as their associations with some cognitive- and linguistic-related factors. For example, questions such as how L1’s linguistic features influence L2 speech perception, and whether Cantonese-English bilingual children use L1 strategies in perceiving L2 English speech information (e.g., stress) are not clear thus far. Particularly, there is very little research on the relations between L1 and L2 speech perception at the neural level. In addition, while we found that there is overlap between L1 Chinese and L2 English reading difficulty and some L1 language skills (e.g., tone identification) are important in distinguishing L2 reading difficulty from the reading in typically developing readers, questions of whether the overlap between L1 and L2 reading difficulty and factors associated with L1 and L2 reading difficulty would change with reading experience and language proficiency require more research in the future. We are examining this issue somewhat in a CRF grant on neuroscience and genetics of reading in Chinese and in English currently.

451811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
451811.value: Teachers, researchers, educators, and parents care about children’s literacy development in both L1 Chinese and L2 English in Hong Kong society. Designing proper L2 English testing tasks and identifying factors associated with L1 and L2 reading difficulties is very important in terms of both pedagogical and practical aspects. In our study, we designed three English word reading tasks and we tested the validity ad reliabilities of the three tasks for Hong Kong children’s L2 English reading skills. We found the three tasks were effective and efficient and could be carried out in a group. In addition, we found some factors that are uniquely associated with L1 Chinese and L2 English word reading. For example, tone perception uniquely explains English word reading and copying and visual-spatial skills are unique predictors of Chinese word reading. Moreover, we found MMNs and p-MMRs could be used as neural markers for speech perception in both Chinese and English in Cantonese-English speaking children. The findings from this study can potentially help teachers, educators, and parents better understand the problems of reading in both Chinese and English.

452911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
452911.value: Laborers’ skills are an increasingly important factor in Hong Kong’s economic growth and also have a great impact on individual earnings and the country’s income distribution. The proposed project will empirically examine the returns to different types of skills in HK over the last 25 years. The study will provide insight into the value of different skills in HK’s labor market over time. More important, it will shed light on how the country’s current educational reforms and curriculum development can respond to the changing demands and challenges in the new global economy. Finally, the study will extend the literature on HK’s wage inequality by examining the changes to returns to different skills across the region’s wage distribution. Using data from the HK Census and By-Census from 1981 to 2006 and from the Dictionary of Occupational Titles, we will perform regression analyses to estimate the value of skills required by different occupations. In particular, we will combine the task measures and occupational-skill-requirement measures developed by Autor, Levy, and Murnane (2003) and Bacolod and Blum (2005) to define six task-based skill indices: nonroutine-analytic-task-based and nonroutine-interactive-task-based cognitive skills; routine-cognitive-task-based, routine-manual-task-based, and nonroutine-manual-task-based motor skills; and the strength index. Furthermore, the study will use JMP’s (1993) decomposition of the wage residual to investigate whether the changing value of skills can explain the country’s wage inequality and the narrowing gender wage gap. The outsourcing to China has accelerated the relative demand and wages of skilled workers. Because skilled workers possess relatively more cognitive skills, this study will explore the extent to which changes in the value of different task-based cognitive skills can explain the rise in income inequality among workers with different educational attainment. On the other hand, the structural changes in HK have reduced the income gap because women have higher productivity in service-sector jobs that require less intensive physical labor. Our analysis will examine whether women tend to move into task-based jobs with rising returns and to the extent to which estimated changes in returns to their specific skills can explain the gender wage gap. Robustness checks will be conducted to test for potential measurement error. Finally, increasingly job opportunities have been concentrated in high-skilled, high-paying jobs and low-skilled, low-paying jobs in industrialized economies. This study will be innovative in that it will test the employment-polarization hypothesis in HK by investigating the impact of skill-biased and task-biased technical change in HK’s labor market. 鑒於勞動者技能對香港經濟發展、個人收入及國家收入分佈的影響日益深遠，此研究將透過實證檢視香港過去二十五年來各類勞動者技能回報，探討其隨時間在香港勞動市場的價值演變，並揭示當前教育改革和課程發展該如何在新環球經濟下就需求變化、挑戰作出應對。此研究亦將借各類勞動者技能回報在區域工資分佈中的變動來補充原有關於香港工資差距的報告。 我們將運用香港人口普查及中期人口普查數據以及Dictionary of Occupational Titles等數據,通過回歸分析評估各職業所需技能的價值，進一步結合Autor, Levy, and Murnane (2003)和Bacolod and Blum (2005)所提出的任務測度 (task measure)及職業技能要求措施來界定六項以工作任務為本的技能指標(task-based skill indices)：非慣常工作分析為本及非慣常互動性工作為本的認知技能；慣常工作分析為本、慣常手動工作為本及非慣常手動工作為本的運動技能；以及力量指標。 是項研究同時試用JMP (1993)的工資餘數結構去解釋技能價值轉變與工資不均、男女工資差距收窄的因果關係。技術工人的需求和工資上升源於中國外判。基於技術工人相對擁有較多認知技能，我們希望透過研究工作任務為本的認知技能價值的改變去解釋不同教育程度的工人工資不均等的上升現象。另外，因女性在需要較少體力勞動的服務性行業中更具生產力，得而令香港收入差距在結構改變上收窄。我們會在分析當中研究女性是否趨向選擇回報遞增的工作任務為本技能的工種，及各技能的預計回報改變是否得以解釋性別工資不均現象。穩健性檢查將被用以找出潛在測量誤差。 最後，基於在工業化經濟環境下愈多就業機會集中於高技能、高薪類工作及低技能、低薪類工作，此研究將創新地利用香港勞動市場的技能傾向和任務傾向的技制變化來試驗就業兩極化假說。

452911.label: Major findings and research outcome
452911.value: We documented the earnings/wage inequality of Hong Kong's labor market from 1990-2011 (Ou 2015). We find that the increase in overall inequality can be explained by the increase in the within-group variance of natives. Further, we find that a large part of the within-group inequality resulted from the change in the share of employees and that the reduced share of Chinese immigrant employees contributed to decreasing inequality among men. A large part of within-group inequality among women came from wage dispersion. A nonnegligible part of the increase in inequality among women was due to the expansion of between-group variance associated with the large inflow of foreign domestic helpers. Another working paper (Ou and Fok, 2015) examines returns to five different skills (nonroutine analytic, nonroutine interactive, routine cognitive, routine manual and nonroutine manual skills) in Hong Kong from 1991 to 2011. As part of this research, I developed a crosswalk of occupations from different waves of the Hong Kong Census, which will be useful for researchers using multiple years of Census data. We demonstrate that there is a large increase in the value of cognitive skills throughout the period even in jobs that only require little education. Motor skills were more important in low-skilled jobs for both male and female. In addition, physical strength was positively correlated to jobs held by male workers but not those by female workers. We also find that for male in the high-skilled jobs, interpersonal skills have become increasingly important with significant and positive returns over the period. Using data from the 1996, 2001, and 2006 years of the Hong Kong Population Census, we (Ou&Pong, 2013) also reported the nativity earnings gap among a synthetic cohort of immigrant and native male Chinese employees in Hong Kong. Consistent with previous research, we found earnings divergence for all workers. However, this earnings divergence masked a reverse trend for low-skilled workers. Over time, lowskilled immigrant workers gained earnings assimilation with low-skilled native workers, but high-skilled immigrant workers did not gain assimilation with high-skilled native workers. A decomposition analysis suggested that the relative skill prices cannot explain the overtime change in the relative mean-earnings gaps by nativity. Further separating pre- and postmigration education of immigrants did not improve the explanatory power of the relative skill prices. Our results for Hong Kong are consistent with the findings from recent research on the economic assimilation of low-skilled immigrants in other countries.

452911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
452911.value: To further examine the nativity gap in wages and human capital, I am continuing to investigate how returns to task-based occupational skills contribute to the wage assimilation of Chinese immigrants in Hong Kong.

452911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
452911.value: Skills possessed by workers are not only an increasingly important factor in economic growth but also have a great impact on individual earnings and the country’s subsequent distribution of income. This project documented the patterns of change and trends in wage structure to provide an up-to-date picture of HK's wage inequality in 1991-2011. We also investigated the returns to different types of skills in HK’s labor market and to explore how these skills are valued over time. Our findings have great implications for HK’s educational reform including the current curriculum development to meet the demands of a global economy. Further, we studied the differences in labor market outcomes by nativity and understand the economic and education assimilation of immigrants in HK. Our findings not only highlight the usefulness of separating workers by skill level when studying economic assimilation, but also stress the importance of considering how differences in the immigrant share of the population may affect nativity wage inequality, a consideration that had not previously been discussed in the wage inequality literature on HK. We are one of the first to analyze how returns to immigrants’ pre- and postmigration human capital contributed to recent trends in the nativity earnings gap.

453111.label: Project Title(Chinese)
453111.value: 古代埃及與中國死後世界之比較:信仰,想像與幸福之追求

453111.label: Project Objectives
453111.value: To investigate the idea of the netherworld in the religious systems of ancient Egypt and China. To investigate the relationship between ethical system and the idea of the netherworld in ancient Egypt and China. To investigate the relationship between the conceptualisation of the netherworld and the life experience of the people. To compare the expressions of the quest for happiness in ancient Egypt and China.
rows: To investigate the idea of the netherworld in the religious systems of ancient Egypt and China.
To investigate the relationship between ethical system and the idea of the netherworld in ancient Egypt and China.
To investigate the relationship between the conceptualisation of the netherworld and the life experience of the people.
To compare the expressions of the quest for happiness in ancient Egypt and China.

453111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
453111.value: Many parallels exist between ancient Egypt and ancient China, one of which is a belief in a netherworld. While the imagined netherworlds of these two civilizations differ in their detail, they nevertheless share a common source of inspiration, namely that they are drawn from and shaped by a fundamental collective understanding of the meaning of life for the living. This study will compare core values from each civilization in order to establish to what extent beliefs and values about religion, ethics and the nature of happiness are present in ancient Chinese and Egyptian visions of life after death. While ancient Egypt (c. 25th-10th c. BCE) and ancient China (c. 8th c. BCE-6th c. CE) have been studied in depth, a comparative approach is rare, particularly one such as this which roots the netherworld in the experience of daily life. The structural similarities between these two civilizations, each with rich funerary traditions, suggest that profitable comparison of the two cultures would yield mutually illuminating insights into their understanding of the meanings of life and happiness, for by imagining and describing the netherworld, the ancient Egyptians and Chinese reveal for us their beliefs about life. Methodologically, this project first examines religious texts and archaeological finds to reconstruct the conceptual architecture of the netherworld as a basic frame of reference. Second, ethical values and social norms that could have provided inspiration for the netherworld are examined, along with ideas about the nature of happiness and how it is attained. Third, I shall articulate how far people’s conceptualisation of the netherworld may be conditioned or influenced by their ethical values, social behavior and daily existence and how the collectively imagined netherworld evolved in step with changes in social values. The study hopes to demonstrate that the thematic examination of one ancient civilization can not only cast light on another, but on modern society too. By reflecting on the commonality/difference of two ancient cultures, we hope to show that without observing how people in different historical and cultural contexts managed to deal with similar problems, problems that still exist for us today, any interpretation of cultural phenomena such as the concept of the netherworld will likely remain one-dimensional. Moreover, the two ancient civilizations compared could each be understood for their special characteristics in the fresh light of a comparative perspective, one that could hardly be done without a project such as this proposed one. 古代埃及與中國文明有不少可相比較之處，其中之一為有關死後世界之信仰。這兩個古文明對死後世界的具體想像當然在細節上有諸多不同，但他們仍然共享一類共同的來源，也就是說，他們都受到該文化中人們對生命和生活之意義的集體瞭解的影響。本研究的目的就在探討及比較這兩個文明的核心價值，用以瞭解有關宗教，倫理和幸福之意義的信仰和價值在埃及和中國的死後世界觀中所占的位置和扮演的角色。 有關古代埃及(c. 25th-10th c. BCE)和古代中國(c. 8th c. BCE-6th c. CE) 的研究各自均有相當的成果，然而從比較之角度來探討兩者的研究則相當少，尤其是本研究計畫所設定的目標：從日常生活經驗來探索死後世界觀。古埃及與中國在文化結構上有其相類之處：兩者均有豐富的喪葬傳統。因而比較此兩種傳統，探討人們如何想像及描述死後世界，可以讓我們更加明白他們各自對生活和幸福的瞭解，同時也可以呈現他們對生命的信仰。 在方法上，本研究將首先探討宗教文獻與考古資料，以重建各自有關死後世界的基本架構。其次，探討那些有可能提供死後世界觀的想像基礎的倫理價值和社會習俗，以及有關幸福的概念和獲得幸福的方法。第三，進一步討論人們對死後世界的想像和建構如何被他們的倫理價值和社會行為以及日常生活所影響及塑造，而這集體的對死後世界的想像又如何隨著社會價值的轉變而產生變化。 本研究希望逹成一個目的，即有關某一個古代文明的專題研究不但可以幫助我們瞭解另一古文明，也可以對瞭解現代社會有用處。我們認為，探討不同文明某些方面的異同，可以讓我們瞭解在不同時代和文化脈絡中的人們是如何處理相類的問題，這些問題不但在古代存在，在現代也仍然有其重要性。對人文現象，譬如說對於死後世界的瞭解和解釋，如果缺少比較的瞭解，終究是一面之辭。

453111.label: Realisation of objectives
453111.value: The project proposed to investigate (1) the idea of the netherworld in ancient Egypt and China, (2)the relationship between the ethical system and the idea of the netherworld, (3) the relationship between the life experience of the people with their imagination of the netherworld, and (4) finally how the concept of happiness in these two civilizations could be revealed through an examination of their funerary practice. The PI has dealt with all these aspects in the course of this project, and have published three articles and presented three conference papers (one conference paper on China has subsequently been published, thus altegether five papers). Of these five papers, two are on ancient China (“Chinese Traditional – funerary” in Christopher Moreman ed., Routledge Companion to Death and Dying (New York: Taylor & Francis/Routledge, forthcoming 2016; “漢代之信仰,想像,與幸福之追求” in 邢義田，劉增貴編，《古代庶民社會》 (台北: 中央研究院, 2013), 299-323.), and two are on Egypt (“The Axial Age in light of the earliest burial customs of ancient Egypt,”(paper delivered at Comparing “Axial Breakthrough” in Ancient Civilizations: An International Workshop, Fudan University, Shanghai, 2015, 12, 5-6; “死後世界的想像--古埃及的信仰與幸福的追求”in 李奭學、黎子鵬主編, 《他界書寫論文集》(台北，中央研究院, 2015), 133-154.), and one on a specific study of the idea of happiness in China (“Mortuary Practice and the Search for Happiness in China”Paper delivered at the International Conference on In pursuit of wisdom: Ancient Chinese and Greek perspectives on cultivation. 15-18 January 2016 University of New South Wales, Sydney, Australia). Thus all the objectives of the project have been dealt with and given a balanced treatment.

453111.label: Major findings and research outcome
453111.value: (1) The comparative study of ancient cultures should be done based on firm empirical study of the sources, so that the comparison would not be built on superficial comparison of similarities and differences. This project tries to demonstrate this point by looking at the conception of the Netherworld in ancient China and Egypt, which could be an important key in understanding the religious and ethical idea of a culture, and therefore some of the most important aspects that hold the culture together as a coherent entity. (2) The similarities between the two cultures could be summarized as having an idea of a life hereafter that resembled this life, in terms of the imagination of a "physical life" that was very similar to the life on earth. (3) In both China and Egypt the Netherworld was imagined with reference to the world of the living, in particular the existence of a Netherworld bureaucracy. However, how that Netherworld bureaucracy was imagined differed according to their respective social and political situations. (4) If funerary set-up could be seen as the outward expression of the idea of a happy life in the hereafter, the funerary texts could be seen as the inner principle. Egypt and China had similar outward expressions, yet with quite different inner principle. As the texts reveal, the ethical principle that supported the funerary set-up in China was this-worldly concern, while those that supported the Egyptian funerary set-up were aspirations for a just life while alive, and a blessed afterlife when dead. The connection between ethical values and moral rectitude while alive and a happy afterlife was not at all strong in ancient China. This means that we should not give equal weight to similar phenomena, and hence we should reflect upon the meaning of the outward expression in each culture from a new angle. The happiness that the average ancient Chinese had may outwardly be quite similar to that of the ancient Egyptian, yet the inside principles differed from each other. (5) By comparing the cultural phenomena that are on the surface similar, we could re-examine each culture from a new light, to de-familiarize what we previously thought was a common sense: people adopt similar customs, therefore they must have similar social values. The contribution of this study is to question this common assumption and arrive at a more sophisticated understanding of ancient cultures.

453111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
453111.value: The basic research has been done, and outcome has been published or in the process of still being published. The eventual goal is to put all the material together and publish a monograph.

453111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
453111.value: This is the first scholarly attempt at comparing the conception of the Netherworld in ancient China and Egypt. The PI uses both archaeological and textual material to demonstrate how the mortuary customs of these two ancient cultures could reveal their idea of happiness. The conception of a netherworld and the search for happiness in ancient Egypt and China as we have seen in the sources represents the ideal or ideological construct, whereas the daily experience of all sorts of emotions, their hopes and fears, joys and frustrations, are the social reality that formed the bases for the construction of that ideal. The present project, therefore, tries to comprehend the ideals associated with the netherworld on the one hand, and the ethical values and social reality that formulated the ideals on the other. While thousands of years separate us from the ancient Egyptians and the ancient Chinese, we can nevertheless hope to approach their world because human beings as a species share a fundamental need for values and common aspirations for a happy life that are no less true today than thousands of years ago.

454111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
454111.value: Rising saving rate is a typical feature of rapidly growing economies. Salient observations from the East Asian economies such as Japan in the 1960s and 1970s, Korea and Taiwan in the 1980s have been repeatedly documented in the literature. The legend continues by the recent rise in saving rate in Brazil, China and India, three of the most rapidly growing economies over the past two decades. The Chinese household saving rate, for instance, increased from 16% to 27% from 1992 to 2007, a period when GDP per capital grows at an annual rate of 9%. The rise in saving rate has been widely believed as a major impetus for the growing trade surplus in China. Some economists even argue that it contributes significantly to the global imbalance. The observation that saving rate increases in high-growth environments presents a puzzle, however, because the standard representative agent model implies low saving when a household anticipates high income growth. In this project, we propose a resolution of the puzzle by documenting dramatic flattening of life-cycle earnings profiles in fast-growing economies including China and Taiwan, using a unique Chinese urban household survey conducted by National Bureau of Statistics and a Taiwanese household survey dataset provided by Academia Sinica. Our analysis will illustrate that, once the observed changes in earnings profiles are incorporated, an otherwise standard life-cycle model can account for the surge in household saving in recent China and in Taiwan in the 1970s and 1980s. Moreover, the model can explain, in a logically consistent way, the unusually high saving rate of young households in China and Taiwan. This research project has rich theoretical implications. It contributes to the literature of saving and growth by proposing a novel channel for growth to boost saving. It also contributes to the literature of age earnings profiles by not only presenting new evidence from fast-growing economies, but providing an explanation to the flattening of age earnings profiles in high-growth environments. In addition, this project may deliver important policy implications since the rise in saving rate in China is indeed an important factor for global imbalances. China has reached a critical moment of deciding how to reduce its trade surplus. Our analytical framework may help scientific policy decision making by evaluating quantitatively the effects on saving and surplus of various policy experiments. N/A

454911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
454911.value: This research project focuses on understanding the conditions, characteristics, and meanings of public space in Hong Kong’s older urban districts. The research documents the impacts of transformation processes on district identity and quality of life. The areas Sheung Wan and Sai Ying Pun are selected for study. Using an interdisciplinary approach and community workshops the Study aims to develop models for sensitive district planning establishing “Community Benefits Districts” (CBD). Sheung Wan and Sai Ying Pun are Hong Kong’s oldest urban districts where Chinese traditional shops and workshops thrive, and old customs survive. The intricate public space network within the area is comprised of alleys, terraces, ladder streets, squares, gardens, and parks. But, the most frequently used public spaces are the district’s street spaces. These are the spaces in which most of the community life and social interaction take place and which visitors enjoy exploring. The research project will document these spaces as central parts of Hong Kong’s unique heritage and living culture. Sheung Wan and Sai Ying Pun area continues to face strong transformation in context of urban renewal and infrastructure projects. These forces are related to its strategic location between Hong Kong’s business and tourist centre and the recently opened Western Tunnel. The construction of the MTR West Island Line combined with a new proposed escalator system similar to the Mid-Levels Escalators in Central will act as catalysts for further transformation of the area. Already the first renewal project (Island Crest) was completed and the second (Yu Lok Lane) will be constructed soon. These forces and their effects on public spaces will be explored to understand the impact on the district identity and quality of life. Based on the research results, urban strategies, design guidelines and form based codes for the district plan will be defined. These will have policy implications for a more sensitive approach to regeneration of older urban districts, ensuring a gradual transition that strengthens the vitality and character of public space and retains its sense of place. To unveil the complexity of the public spaces and factors of transformation an interdisciplinary research team with experiences in visual culture studies, community engagement, urban design and planning has been formed to undertake this study. The project will conclude with an international conference and publication. The district plan proposal is envisioned as a model for other older urban districts in Hong Kong and the mainland. 測量舊區重建中公共空間改造對社區的影響： 上環與西營盤的個案研究 本計劃的研究對象是香港舊區的公共空間，我們會集中考察其當前的情況、特色以及意義，尤其著重紀錄重建改造過程對舊區的身份和居民生活的影響。本計劃的焦點為上環與西營盤，兩者都是香港歷史最悠久的市區，當中至今還有一些傳統的中式商鋪和工場，而傳統習俗也仍然存在。在這些舊區内，公共空間網絡錯綜複雜，主要由橫街、高臺、樓梯街道、空地、花園、公園等組成，但最多人使用的公共空間卻是街頭巷尾，居民的日常社區活動大多在此進行，也自然吸引了不少遊客尋幽探秘。這兩區的公共空間是香港獨特的新舊交融文化的核心，本計劃將詳細研究並記錄之。 近年來，各區的市區重建和基建項目此起彼落，上環和西營盤也不例外，並預計將持續受到改造工程的巨大影響。改造動力之大，在於兩區的特殊地理位置：既在香港的商業和旅遊中心的毗鄰，也在開通不久的西區海底隧道附近。港鐵港島西綫的興建，以及類似中環半山行人電梯的建造計劃，都是加快兩區改造的催化劑。隨著第一個重建項目（縉城峰）的完成，第二個項目（餘樂里）也快要動工。本研究計劃將探討這些改造動力及其對公共空間的影響，從而了解社區的身份和居民的生活質量如何受到改變。本計劃還希望藉著研究結果，重新釐定市區發展策略、設計指引、地區規劃形式守則等，並在政策上有助制訂出一套更細緻的舊區重建大綱，好讓公共空間在改造過程中，能夠加強活力和保持獨特的地方風格。 最後，本計劃將透過參加國際學術會議和出版刊物來分享研究成果，而地區規劃建議則可望成爲日後本港以及内地的舊區重建藍本。

454911.label: Realisation of objectives
454911.value: 1) We surveyed all ground-level businesses in Sai Ying Pun, opening hours of around 200 of them, and ground- and upper-level community facilities; produced photo documentation of around 450 shop-fronts; captured usages of spaces with field notes and videos (Appendix 1). 2) For each space type (street, park, pocket park, alley, terrace and podium) we produced drawings, photo/video documentations, surveys of accessibility, ownership and management to highlight different spatial arrangements and design standards (Appendix 2). Users’ activities and experiences were assessed through ethnographic observation, community workshops, street exhibitions and video-interviews (Appendix 3, 5). We studied the transformation of public-private interfaces caused by recent developments (Appendix 4). Upon MTRC West Island Line’s opening, we will examine changes in the district over time using the same index. We also started to employ the index to study other districts. 3) Community building and empowerment were highlighted through teaching and outreach activities. In two Design Studios and Urban Processes courses, MScUD students joined the research as they developed design ideas and presented them in community workshops and street exhibitions to collect feedback from stakeholders (Appendix 3.1). These activities were linked to the “Magic Carpet” outreach project, where community views were captured through video-interviews, and a public screening was organized to strengthen social interaction and transform public space in real time. A website connected with social media was developed as a communication-cum-documentation means (Appendix 5). Research, teaching, outreach and online platforms were coordinated to inform the development of a Community Benefit Plan (Appendix 10). 4) We combined urban design/planning with cultural studies, ethnographic research and media documentation to investigate street activities, social interactions, spatial and traffic conditions. We also employed journalism (e.g. video-interviews), public screening, and social media to engage and empower the community (Appendix 1-5). 5) Responding to the reviewers’ comments, we decided to use photo and video documentation, as these methods gathered both quantitative data of vehicular/pedestrian movements and qualitative insights about social activities and everyday rhythms of the district (Appendix 1.4, 1.5, 2.1, 2.3). 6) Comments regarding new developments in Sai Ying Pun were collected through community building/empowerment programmes (Appendix 3, 5). With our new GRF project, we will capture changes after the completion of MTRC’s West Island Line and URA’s Yu Lok Lane project, while continuing to develop our Community Benefit Plan as a proactive, open-ended urban strategy (Appendix 10) to complete a comprehensive, thorough study on the transformation of public space in Sai Ying Pun.

454911.label: Major findings and research outcome
454911.value: Urban renewal (e.g. high-riser Island Crest) and infrastructure projects (e.g. MTRC West Island Line’s opening in 2015) induced intensive development in Sai Ying Pun, thus affecting the livelihood of people there. Through observation and interviews, we noticed a changing scene of local businesses (from small-scale, family-run traditional shops to chain stores and upscale restaurants) and demographic composition (more expatiates and domestic helpers), increasing social polarisation. Conditions of Sai Ying Pun’s public spaces changed over the same period: Overall, public spaces within the district decreased, so was their connection with the community (Appendix 2.5). Public-private interfaces decreased due to new developments. Our photo/video observations show how this change affected the quantity and quality of street activities, diminishing the role of streets to mere circulation (Appendix 4). These observations also captured mismatches between spatial design and human activities: People tended not to stay in sitting areas provided by pocket parks. Instead, they stayed along street spaces, especially the district’s main communal space Centre Street. With no seating provided, people here rest on low stone ledges, planters, steps and staircases (Appendix 6). Alley and terrace spaces remained underused, with a lack of seats, plants and proper management (Appendix 2.3). These spaces form an alternative circulation network without vehicular traffic. However, their potential as spaces for relaxation, children’s play and social interaction remains untapped. Although a new, well-designed public space was built along the waterfront (Sun Yat Sen Memorial Park), it is not well connected. A comprehensive open space network would help mothers/childminders and elderly people to reach this space more easily from the district’s upper parts and thus improve their quality of life (Appendix 10). With the lack of a holistic spatial planning, development projects tended to focus on economic growth, traffic efficiency and safety. Ironically, isolated safety measures (e.g. new railings) pushed infirm people unable to take the stepped sidewalks onto road surfaces, increasing the risk of accidents (Appendix 7). There is no consultation of urban designers or community planners in the district office. During our workshops and events, we experienced limited interest in community building and empowerment through spatial practices. Planning remained often limited to reactions to complaints rather than proactively searching for ways of how the quality of living in the district could be substantially improved. This project therefore developed a multifaceted strategy to create a Community Benefit Plan as an open-ended, proactive process based on research and outreach activities (Appendix 10).

454911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
454911.value: Our next GRF research will capture the impact of MTRC’s West Island Line and URA’s Yu Lok Lane project after their completion in 2015. Thus we will be able to capture the transformation process and its impacts in a longitudinal study. We also started to document other public spaces in Hong Kong with the same index system. We also proposed successfully to Urban Lab+, an international network funded by the European Union, to compare the research with international cases. Joined by Technical University Berlin and Pontifical Catholic University of Chile, a symposium titled “Impact of Public Transport Infrastructure Projects on Urban Inclusion and Community Benefit” will be organized by the PI in December 2014 at CUHK. Our Knowledge Transfer project in Sai Ying Pun, “Magic Carpet – Re-envisioning Community Space”, has been held in other districts: Tin Shui Wai and Wanhau (Taipei) (Appendix 5.2). Its next edition in Macau is forthcoming. As a further initiative, “Magic Tables” will be developed with CUHK’s BSSc in Urban Studies students, progressing from re-envisioning to re-making community spaces. With local resources, students and people in Sai Ying Pun will collectively design tables on the sloping Centre Street for the community event on November 9, 2014.

454911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
454911.value: Using Sai Ying Pun as a case study, the research measured the impact of large-scale urban renewal and public transport projects on Hong Kong’s old districts, and to formulate strategies for community benefit. The interdisciplinary team employed quantitative (e.g. statistics, survey, diagram and mapping) and qualitative (e.g. interview, ethnographic observation, photography and video) methods to understand the spatial arrangements and daily rhythms of the district, as well as behaviour, concerns and aspirations of its residents. From these outcomes, which combined urban data and life stories of the district, a Community Benefit Plan is developed as a community-oriented and proactive approach to urban planning and design (Appendix 10). With the belief that academic studies should have real-life impact, we linked the research with outreach activities, which substantially informed each other. Knowledge Transfer Fund project “Magic Carpet” was thus developed, in which local secondary students produced video-interviews of people in Sai Ying Pun. Its results were screened in a re-envisioning event on September 19, 2013 (Mid-Autumn Festival) on Centre Street in Sai Ying Pun. The open screening stood as a testament to how public space can be creatively transformed by interventions engaging community members, strengthening the feasibility of a proactive, open-ended Community Benefit Plan strategy.

454911.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
454911.value: As we had outlined in our proposal, related community engagement activities would be carried out to help us gather useful information for the research, and at the same time to increase impact of the research. One of them was “Magic Carpet – Re-envisioning Community Space in Sai Ying Pun”, a CUHK Knowledge Transfer collaboration with Prof Anthony Fung (Director of the School of Journalism and Communication, CUHK), Colin Fournier (Visiting Professor of the School of Architecture, CUHK), King’s College and the Conservancy Association Centre for Heritage (CACHe). The project was later selected as part of the CUHK 50th anniversary programme. A community filming-cum-screening project, Magic Carpet involved 20 local secondary school students conducting video-interviews with people in Sai Ying Pun. From April to September 2013, more than 40 video-interviews were produced by students of King’s College, in which people from all walks of life talked about their experiences and memories in Sai Ying Pun, as well as their concerns and aspirations for the district’s development (Appendix 3.2). An open screening of these videos was held on Centre Street on September 19, 2013 (Mid-Autumn Festival). The event did not only allow community members to gather and interact, but also transformed and revived the rather lifeless space of Centre Street, which used to be a vibrant centre of the district for more than a century before the 1990s (Appendix 5.1). The videos have been uploaded to the project website (www.magiccarpet.hk), which serves as an oral history archive for Sai Ying Pun, as well as an interactive platform where voices of residents and our research findings are combined, where history is registered with the links between social life, everyday culture and urban environment. In September 2014, we organised the second edition of Magic Carpet in Tin Shui Wai, once again to great response (Appendix 5.2). Following the success of Magic Carpet, we have gone on to develop Magic Tables in November 2014, returning to the sloping Centre Street in Sai Ying Pun. A collaboration with Kwang Hwa Information and Culture Center, the event will see the BSSc in Urban Studies (course: Urban Design & Place Making) students re-build community space through collective designs of tables involving local resources and skills. Exhibitions of various scales were also organised to present our research progress and outcomes. Starting with street displays in Sai Ying Pun that showcased students’ designs for the community in 2012 (Appendix 3.1), we had subsequently mounted a joint exhibition of master students of CUHK and National Taiwan University at Kwun Tong Ferry Pier, as part of the Hong Kong-Shenzhen Urbanism & Architecture Bi-city Biennale selection based on an international call for contributions. There we compared the current situation of Sai Ying Pun with that of Wanhua, an old district in Taipei that was also facing issues of urban renewal and redevelopment (Appendix 5.2, 8). Outside Hong Kong, we contributed our research findings and projects of the MSc in Urban Design students to the exhibition “Past, Present and Future of Public Space” in May 2013 in Rome curated by Luisa Bravo, as part of the Biennale of Public Space 2013, at the Faculty of Architecture Roma Tre. Further synergies were created with two studies by bachelor students of Worcester Polytechnic Institute, produced in collaboration with the GRF research team: 1) Dylan Barnhill, Meghan Farrell, Xueyang Lin, Maria Alexandra Rangel, “Characterizing Sai Ying Pun’s Markets as Forms of Public Space”, Worcester Polytechnic Institute, Advisors: C. Demetry, R. Vaz, Local Sponsors & Advisor: H. Tieben, CUHK, March, 2012. 2) Daniel Bouffard, Sarah Cook, Samuel Eisenberg, and Ransom Mowris, “Investigating the Relationships between Urban Design, Microeconomics, and Livability: A Case Study of Hong Kong (Comparison of Sai Ying Pun and Tin Shui Wai)”, Worcester Polytechnic Institute, Advisors: J.Y. Liang, S. Nikitina, Local Sponsors & Advisors: S. Govada & H. Tieben, CUHK, February, 2013. In the context of the research project we organized two study field trips to Taipei in 2012 and 2013 respectively. Having learned of Taipei’s “soft urbanism” approach to community planning, we organised “Urban Dialogue: Taipei x Hong Kong” in February-March 2014. A Spotlight Taiwan Project supported by Taiwan’s Ministry of Culture, Urban Dialogue comprised three forums, two community workshops (one of them focused on Sai Ying Pun) and a public screening event. There, social activists, urban designers and planners, educators, filmmakers, artists, architects and policymakers from Hong Kong and Taipei exchanged views on urban regeneration strategies and innovative means of social empowerment. Results of the project were published in a booklet. The contributions of the speakers and their discussions helped us to further develop our strategies for a Community Benefit Plan (Appendix 9-10). In addition, the research was linked and supported by a second Urban Design Studio with the topic of “Integrating Mass Transit Development in High Density Districts: Western District”, in which 30 masters students participated. The workshop was taught by Colin Fournier, Sujata Govada (Co-I), Daniel Patzold and Joshua Lau. Results of this studio were also exhibited at the Hong Kong-Shenzhen Urbanism & Architecture Bi-city Biennale 2013-14. Enclosure: Appendix for the Completion Report.

455311.label: Project Title(Chinese)
455311.value: 会计人员在全球财务报表质量中扮演的角色

455311.label: Project Objectives
455311.value: Various prior studies have shown the importance of institutional factors in affecting the outcome of financial reporting system in country-level. Academics and practitioners generally agree on the importance of the responsibilities and quality of accountants as an essential element of the financial reporting outcome, however there is little, if any, research investigating the quality of accountants and the ultimate quality of financial reporting delivered by accountants in an international setting. In this study, we will examine the role of accountants in the quality of financial reporting practices in a global setting. To examine the role of accountants in the quality of financial reporting practices, we will study the quality of accountants across countries and create measures to measure the differences in the quality of accountants of different countries. Specifically, we will examine the importance of qualification requirements, continuous support, professional training, and regulatory oversight on the quality of accountants in different countries. By showing the importance of the quality of accountants in affecting the quality of financial reporting in a global setting, this paper also calls for an improved monitoring, and enhanced support to the accounting profession.

455311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
455311.value: Financial markets are of international significance today. The globalization of business investment and capital markets has increased the need for high quality financial information. The provision of high quality financial information is crucial because it facilitates more efficient capital allocation in the economy and more efficient resource allocation decisions can, in turn, enhance overall market efficiency (FASB 1999; IASB 2008). Countries with high quality financial reporting and a strong information environment have been shown to garner significant benefits in terms of better corporate governance, greater economic development, lower costs of capital, better functioning capital markets, greater foreign investment and higher stock valuations (Piotroski and Wong 2009). A major responsibility of the accounting profession is to provide high quality accounting information. However, one impediment to being able to practice high quality financial reporting is a lack of qualified personnel. The objective of this study is to provide a deeper understanding of the role accountants play in financial reporting, and to describe the importance of qualification requirements, continuous support, professional training, and regulatory oversight for the quality of financial reporting practices around the world. Furthermore, we outline a number of possible prescriptive measures that can be enacted at the country level to improve the quality of accounting and thus enhance public confidence in the profession. 经济体系全球化增加了对高质量财务讯息的需要。高质量的财务资讯对每个国家都非常重要， 因为他们可以提高市场财务运作的效率和有效的资源分配。会计师的其中一个主要责任是提供高质量的资讯。 但是其中一个最大的阻碍是缺乏高资格的会计从业人员。 这个文章的主要目的是探讨会计人员在高质量的财务资讯中所扮演的角色并探讨如何可以提高会计从业人员的水平。

455311.label: Realisation of objectives
455311.value: On the Annual Progress Report for the period ending 31-12-2012, I have indicated that we will have to slightly adjust the research questions to achieve the goals specified in the RGC proposal given the fact that a paper entitled “The importance of audit profession development in emerging market countries” has been published on the last issue of The Accounting Review (2011, Vol 86(5) pp 1731-1764) which is after the official start date of the project. This published paper examines similar research idea which we were planning to examine and finds results very similar to our original predictions (i.e. the quality of accounting profession in a country affects the quality of financial reporting in that country). To better differentiate our study with the published one, and also to maximize the return of the effort devoted in examining the effect of country-level institutional development on financial reporting environment, after numerous discussions and attempts, we now focus on examining the effect of the development of the media environment on firms’ financial report quality. The rationale is that the existence of a strong media in a country (proxied by media competition, media dissemination and media freedom) will provide an external monitoring role to the accounting and auditing profession in a country and as a result, we expect a better developed media will be positively associated with better financial reporting quality/environment (proxied by analyst forecast accuracy – a common measure of financial reporting quality/environment of a country). Following this idea, we believe that we can successfully differentiate our study with the one that had been published on The Accounting Review and we are also very confident that our study and findings can contribute to the literature by providing a better understanding on factors affecting the quality of financial information in different countries. We have completed the study by end of 2013 and submitted the study to Journal of Accounting Research for review during February 2014. To emphasize the new focus of the study, we have relabeled the study as “The Effect of Media Characteristics on Analyst Forecast Properties: Cross-Country Evidence”.

455311.label: Major findings and research outcome
455311.value: Using data from 113,436 firm-year observations from 32 countries spanning 2000 through 2012, we find that firms in countries with stronger media competition, greater media freedom, and more extensive media penetration enjoy more accurate, less optimistically biased, and less dispersed analyst forecasts. In additional analyses, we find some evidence that the effects of media characteristics on properties of analyst forecasts are stronger for firms with lower institutional ownership, firms followed by fewer analysts or by analysts from smaller brokerage houses, and for firms with weaker financial performance. This suggests that the media plays a more pronounced role in shaping the information environment when information from non-media channels is likely to be limited or of lower quality. Our study contributes to research examining the effects of the media on capital markets and provides important insights regarding the crucial role that the media plays in improving analyst forecasts and thus, investors’ access to information about future earnings.

455311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
455311.value: In this study, we mainly examine the effect of country-level media development on firms' financial reporting quality proxied by analyst forecasts. A potential future research direction is to directly examine the effect of media development on managers and sharesholders' behavior. For example, it will be interesting to explore whether and how shareholders in a country with better developed media are more likely to be affected by information provided by firms.

455311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
455311.value: While prior studies generally focus on differences in firms’ accounting and disclosure practices across countries (e.g., differences in the enforcement of accounting standards, differences in national generally accepted accounting principles, the adoption of international financial reporting standards, and differences in the importance of non-financial disclosures), our study demonstrates that characteristics of the media affect analyst forecast properties. Results from our analyses enhance our understanding of how the media, as one of the major components of a country’s communication infrastructure, affects the information environment. This is important because the quality of the information environment can also affect the efficiency of international capital allocation, especially as capital markets become more integrated worldwide. Finally, our study contributes to the literature on the role of the media and financial analysts in the capital markets. Our results suggest that although both media and financial analysts serve as major information intermediaries in the capital markets (Bushee et al. 2010), there is a complementary rather than substitute relation between the media and analysts.
