455811.label: Project Title(Chinese)
455811.value: 中国县级间的非均衡发展:地理空间分析

455811.label: Co - Investigator(s)
455811.value: Prof Landry, Pierre Prof Xiao, Jin

455811.label: Project Objectives
455811.value: determine whether disparities at different tiers of regions (e.g. region, province, prefecture and county) retain similar patterns and measure their magnitude; determine how different socio-economic indicators of development identify particular patterns of inequalities; identify geographical factors in a county and consider their impact on local development; examine the interrelationship of geographical factors, hierarchical administration and development strategies at different localities and compare how the localities have performed in terms of socio-economic development.

455811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
455811.value: Over the last 20 years there has been a huge literature on regional disparities in China, which, mostly, is based on analysis of provincial level data. We propose to do yet another research project on this old issue only because we plan to examine the issue from an entirely new analytical angle by applying novel methodologies of GIS to a newly available dataset. Specifically, this study will use a new set of spatially integrated panel data at the county level to examine patterns of socio-economic inequalities in China. The existing literature suggests many factors that might have contributed to growing regional disparities, including decentralized style reforms, geographic constraints, demographic structure, educational attainment, local development strategies, fiscal capabilities, incentive structures, degree of openness, technology transfer and the like. We are now in a position to unpack the causal mechanisms that underlie inequalities by using a set of highly disaggregated panel data collected at the county level. While extant research has identified likely causes of inequality, such analysis has been marred with serious aggregation bias because data is mostly collected at the provincial level. This project makes use of the newly constructed Barometer on China’s Development at the Universities Service Centre for China Studies. Thanks to this unique database, we can map multiple dimensions of inequality across 333 prefectures and 2,862 counties using data going back to 1978. Leveraging such detailed data allows us to offer new perspectives about the causal mechanisms that underlie persistent disparities. Furthermore, we will use hierarchical modeling to identify how each level of government, in China’s nested bureaucracy, contributes to (or mitigates) observed dimensions of inequality. We will achieve this by: 1. measuring the magnitude of intra-provincial inequalities within 31 provinces and municipalities; 2. comparing of patterns of inequality with multiple spatially referenced indicators; 3. assessing the effectiveness of development strategies across counties in the light of the complex interrelationships between geographical factors and a hierarchical administrative structure that induces nested local government development strategies; 4. tracing the evolution of inequality over time. By bringing counties and prefectures into the analysis of regional inequalities, we can offer explanations and test them more effectively than has not been possible so far. 在过去20年里，学术界出现了大量关于中国区域差异的研究文献，但大多是具于省一级数据的分析。我们的研究提出一个新的分析视角来分析中国区域发展形成的差异，我们利用空间地理的方法和一组新的数据库，即：空间整合的县级数据，分析中国社会经济发展的非均衡化。 现有的文献说明，诸多因素都会导致区域差距拉大，包括放权改革的模式、地理因素的限制、人口结构、人口的教育程度、一个地区发展的策略、财政能力、激励机制、开发的程度、技术的转移等等。我们主张采用县级的面板数据，对中国的非均衡发展的因果机制重新做分析。现存的研究似乎找到了非均衡发展的一些原由，但由于采用的数据是省级的，那些高度聚合的数据会往往造成严重的分析偏差。本研究采用的数据是中国研究服务中心新开发的中国发展动态仪的数据库，采用这套特别的县级的数据，我们可以对中国的 333个地区和2862县从1978年以来的发展，做多维度的地理空间分析。这组数据具有更为细致的指标，可以让我们对中国持续的差异有一个新的认识。再有，我们会使用多层分析方法，分解中国复杂的科层机构中各级政府对于差异的作用，是加剧了还缓解了。我们将要完成下列分析： 1. 度量31个省内和地区内的非均衡发展的程度； 2. 以多维的空间指标来比较非均衡发展的的格局； 3. 以地理因素和行政科层结构之间复杂的相关作用—它们引起当地政府采用特定的发展策略—为依据，评估县级之间发展策略的有效性； 4. 追溯差异演变的过程。 在区域非均衡发展的分析之中有了地区和县引入，我们才能够更为确切地解释差异演变的过程。

455811.label: Realisation of objectives
455811.value: (1) With methods of conventional indices, i.e Theil index and Gini coefficient, we finds that disparities at deffirent tiers of regions show different patterns for all indicators. Overall, the magnitude of inequality depends on the geographical scale. Intra-provincial inequality accounts for the majority of overll inequality. (2) Using conventional Theil index decomposition and new spatial indicators, i.e local Moran's I, we compares the inequality patterns of socio-economic dimensions, including economy, government fiscal capacity, compulsory educaitonal spending and health care resources allocation. (3) Using econometrics models, we test the contributions of geographic factors to local development. The results show that some geographic factors have significant impacts. (4) With GWR tool, we examine how local government responds to the socio-economic and policy envioronments.

455811.label: Major findings and research outcome
455811.value: 6.1.1 Inequality in economic development is growing gradually, while inequalities in social development shrink in recent years.For economic development, the inequality across counties is growing year by year, and especially dramatically since 2003, a shifting year when the inequality climb up steeply.Compared with economy, the inequalities of other indicators are relatively smaller. For governemt spending and compulsory educational spending, the inequalities grows with the radical reforms of marketization and globalization, and start to decline in 2006 or 2007. As a special case, the health care resource (measured by hospital beds per 10,000 persons)is relatively equally distributed in regions during the whole period, and the inequality converges gradually. 6.1.2 The spatial pattern of economy differs with those of other three. The spatial pattern of county economy is featured by "coast-inland" structure. Although quite a few richer counties agglomerate in Inner Mongolia since 2000,the overall spatial pattern of "coastal-inland" dominates. Compared with the results of the aggregate data analysis, the analysis with county data shows that richer counties are also found in poorer province, and vice versa.For government spending and social development represented by education and health care, the spatial sturcture is shaped by "Huhuanyong Line", which seperates China into two regions obsviously different in geograhic conditions and population density.The hot spots are mainly found in the regions west to the line, and cold spots east to the line. For educational spending , some hot spots are also found in the costal regions. 6.1.3 Space and location contribute to regional inequalities.Agglomerations occur for economic and social developments. Development in one region is positively influenced by the neighboring regions.Located around a region with an initial higher level debelopment, the regions will benefited due to spillover effects.Economic agglomeration is caused by externalities, location or pecuniary, and reduced transportation cost. Social agglomerations are led by learning or immitation of policy making. 6.1.4 Geographic factors have significant impacts on local development. Slope, distance to the center city and nearby port is negatively related to the growth of productivity. The railway station changed the disvantaged locations and accelerates growth.Topology have significant role for government spending and social resources allocation. 6.1.5 The government, located in different regions, respond differently to the socio-economic and policy environments, shaping different development strategies.

455811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
455811.value: In the framework of the project, the research team members are now conducting a study that evaluates the impact of coordinated development policies on regional inequality. In this sduty, a quasi-experimental method of PSM-DID will be used. Since 2000, a series of coordinated development policies were implemented in succession, i.e. Western Expansion (2000), Northeastern Revitalization Plan (2003) and Rise of Central China Strategy(2006). Taking Western Expansion for example, we will construct a treatment goup of western regions influenced by the policy, and a control group as a reference. DID (difference in difference) mothod can measure the impact of the policy. DID method require a region is assigned in treatment group with random. However, this reqiurement is not satisfied. Western counties and non-western counties are heterogeneous at many aspects. PSM (propensity score mathcing) helps to find twin counties in non-western regions. PSM-DID is a good compounding method for evaluating impacts of coordinated policies targeting specific regions. This study will provide reference for policy adjustment.

455811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
455811.value: In a country as large as China, regional inequality is a major concern of the general public and policy makers. This project first measures spatial and temporal inequalities of economic and social developments during the reform era at different geographic scales-region, province, county, and then analyzes how local development inequality is caused in specific geo-socio-economic envioronment. As a contribution, this project mainly targets the inequality acorss counties. Inter-county inequality shows different spatial and temporal patterns form inequalities on larger scales. Another contribution of this study is to compare the spatial patterns of economic and social developments. Social development relates to the walfare of the general public and then in turn promote economic sustainability. Although economic development lays foundation, the patterns of social developments is quite different. Overall, the social development of the population densed area east to Huhuanyiong Line is at disadvantageous status. Space, location and geographic conditions are important factors of local development. The development and policies of one region is often influenced by its neighbors and the location relative to the central cities. Efficiency consideration denies the policies that encourage productive factors to enter poorer regions. To enhance the transportation facilities and better the transfer payment system are preferential options.

455911.label: Project Objectives
455911.value: Explore the mechanisms underlying the relationship between the tone space of production and that of perception for both native Cantonese and Mandarin subjects by identification experiment. 1.A. How do subjects categorize pitch contours (acoustic/phonetic variants of tones) into the tone categories of their native tone systems? 1.B. What is the perceptual salience of two dimensions of tone features, pitch height and pitch slope, in the identification of tones in different tone systems? Test the ADH at the behavioral level by discrimination experiment: Investigate the influence of the density of tone systems on pitch discrimination ability. Objectives 1 and 2 are complementary, Objective 1 being from an identification point of view, and Objective 2 being from a discrimination point of view. This will allow us to assess the influence of language experience on linguistic pitch perception. Test the ADH at the cortical level with active attention. Specifically, the categorical perception (CP) of phonological contrasts, as indexed by P300 (Sutton et al., 1965), for level vs. falling tones (see Figure 2(b)) is hypothesized to be exhibited by Cantonese subjects, but not by Mandarin subjects. If the ADH is applicable to the passive attention condition, we predict that a CP effect reflected by MMNs may only occur for Cantonese subjects. Test the ADH at the subcortical level. If the ADH is applicable to the subcortical level, we predict that Cantonese subjects will show generally better pitch-tracking ability for pitch contours than Mandarin subjects.

455911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
455911.value: There are thousands of languages in the world which make use of pitch patterns to build words much as vowels and consonants are used. The use of pitch patterns as lexical contrasts generally endows its users with better pitch ability, as indicated, for example, by the significantly higher prevalence of perfect pitch among native tone language speakers than among nontone language speakers. Numerous studies have shown that language experience has impact on various levels of human pitch perception. In particular, tone language experience has been found to shape pitch perception at the behavioral level (in terms of various response parameters, such as reaction time), at the cortical level (in terms of event-related potentials), and at the subcortical level (in terms of frequency following responses). In this project, our primary focus will be on the tone inventories of Hong Kong Cantonese (henceforth, just Cantonese) and Mandarin (a.k.a. Putonghua), examining the impact of different tone systems on linguistic pitch perception. The different densities of tone systems may influence pitch perception differentially at different levels. Cantonese has a denser tone system that comprises more tones than Mandarin. We hypothesize that the denser the phonetic system of a language, the better discrimination ability its native users possess, and term this hypothesis the Acoustic Density Hypothesis. Based on this hypothesis, we predict that Cantonese listeners have better pitch discrimination ability than Mandarin listeners even when presented with the same stimuli shared in both systems. This hypothesis has gained preliminary support from our recent studies, in which, for instance, we have discovered electrophysiological evidence that Cantonese listeners, but not Mandarin listeners, maintain a phonological discrimination between the high level and high rising tones, which exist in both the Cantonese and Mandarin tone systems. This finding reflects the fact that Cantonese listeners exhibit greater ease in discriminating changes in the stimuli due to better pitch discrimination ability than Mandarin listeners, although the two groups of listeners show no behavioral difference in discriminating the above two tones. In this project, behavioral experiments and electroencephalographic experiments at both the cortical (event-related potentials) and subcortical (frequency following responses) levels will be conducted to systematically examine the impact of tone language experience on linguistic pitch perception, including seeking further evidence for the Acoustic Density Hypothesis. This will lead to a deeper understanding of how language shapes perception. 世界上有數千种語言像利用元音和輔音一樣用音高模式來構詞。利用音高模式來構詞賦予它的使用者更好的音高能力，例如，母語為聲調語言的使用者比非聲調語言的使用者在完美音高方面更具有優勢。許多研究表明，語言經歷在各個層面上均影響其使用者的音高感知。聲調語言的經歷已被被發現在行為層面（體現為各種反應參數，如反應時間），在大腦皮層層面（體現為事件相關電位），和在皮層下層面（體現為頻率跟隨響應）影響音高感知。 在這個項目中，我們的要點將是香港粵語（廣東話）和囯語（又名普通話）的聲調系統，考察不同聲調系統影響音高的感知。聲調系統的不同密度可能會在不同層面上影響音高的感知。廣東話有一個較密集的聲調系統，包括比普通話更多的聲調。我們假定某種語言的語音系統越密集，以它母語的使用者的相應的分辨力越好，並把這種假說命名為聲學密度假說。基於這一假設，我們預測，母語為廣東話的使用者比母語為普通話的使用者有更好的音高辨認能力，即使所用刺激在這兩种語言的聲調系統中共存。 這個假設在我們最近的研究結果中已經獲得初步支持，例如，我們已經發現的電生理證據表明，母語為廣東話的使用者而不是母語為普通話的使用者，呈現高平和高升調的音系區分，而這兩個聲調既在廣東話又在普通話的聲調系統中。這一發現反映出母語為廣東話的使用者表現出更好的音高區分能力，儘管兩組使用者在區分這兩個聲調上不存在行為上的差異。 在這個項目中，行為實驗和在皮層（事件相關電位）和皮層下（頻率跟隨響應）的腦電圖實驗將被用來系統地研究聲調語言經歷對語言音調的感知，包括尋求聲學密度假說的進一步的證據。這將導致更深刻地了解語言對感知的影響。

455911.label: Realisation of objectives
455911.value: In this project, we hypothesize that the denser the phonetic system of a language, the better discrimination ability its native users possess, and term this hypothesis the Acoustic Density Hypothesis (ADH). Although ADH may be applicable to all phonetic inventories, such as lexical tones, consonants, and vowels, it is only tested with tone inventories in this project to simplify the situation. Tones distinguish lexical meanings much as vowels and consonants do. Therefore, the findings with regard to tones are likely to be applicable to vowels and consonants also. The use of pitch patterns to distinguish lexical contrasts generally endows tone language speakers with better pitch ability, as indicated, for example, by the significantly higher prevalence of perfect pitch among native tone language speakers than among nontone language speakers. Numerous studies have already shown that language experience has impact on various levels of human pitch perception. Mandarin has four distinctive lexical tones, whereas Cantonese has nine tones (or six tones if one ignores durational contrasts by merging the three short tones that occur only with checked syllables into their three long tone counterparts). In this project, we focus on the tone inventory contrasts between Mandarin tones (small tone inventory) vs. Cantonese tones (denser tone inventory). Behavioral experiments and electroencephalographic experiments have been conducted to systematically examine the impact of tone language experience on linguistic/non-linguistic pitch perception, seeking evidence for ADH. A series of experiments have demonstrated that the ADH applies to Mandarin and Cantonese listeners, who respond differently to acoustically identical tones, both behaviorally (Objective 2) and in terms of their cortical brain responses during active phonological processing (Objective 3) and in automatic feature detection without focal attention (Objective 4), and that these differences are mediated in terms of both pitch height and pitch slope (Objective 1). Pilot experiments to elicit the frequency following response (FFR) to Mandarin and Cantonese tone perceptions were carried out as an initial attempt to test the ADH at the subcortical level (Objective 5). However, we were unable to obtain FFRs with sufficiently high signal to noise ratio that would allow meaningful analysis. To determine whether this was due to our initially attempting to record FFR in electrically unshielded environments, we ran follow-up pilot experiments in an electrically shielded booth. However, the signal to noise ratio of the resultant FFR remained too low for meaningful analysis.

455911.label: Major findings and research outcome
455911.value: The acoustic density hypothesis has gained support from our several studies. From the discrimination perspective, we have discovered electrophysiological evidence that Cantonese listeners, but not Mandarin listeners, maintain a phonological discrimination between the high level and high rising tones, which exist in both the Cantonese and Mandarin tone systems. This finding reflects the fact that Cantonese listeners exhibit greater ease in discriminating changes in the stimuli due to better pitch discrimination ability than Mandarin listeners (Zheng et al., 2012. Language and Cognitive Processes; note that this study is supported by another project, rather than this project). We have also investigated the effect of tone inventories on brain activities underlying pitch without focal attention. We find that the electrophysiological responses to across-category stimuli are larger than those to within-category stimuli when the pitch contours are superimposed on nonspeech stimuli. This category effect in nonspeech stimuli is stronger for Cantonese speakers (journal paper #5). Results of the above two studies lead us to conclude that brain responses to the same set of pitch contrasts are modulated by speakers’ language experience, both in active phonological processing and in automatic feature detection without focal attention. More specifically, native Cantonese users show better pitch discriminability due to the denser Cantonese tone system. From the identification perspective, it may be possible that the denser is the phonetic/acoustic system of a language, the more difficult it is for native users of that language to perform accurate identification. Indeed, findings of Peng et al. (journal paper #4) show that, without the help of context information, native Cantonese subjects suffer more from acoustic variation induced by talker variability than native Mandarin subjects in a task in which the subjects are instructed to categorize tone stimuli into their native lexical tone categories. Zhang et al. (conference abstract #4) confirm that context information facilitates Cantonese tone perception. We also examine (journal papers #3, #6; conference paper #5) the effect of speech context and nonspeech context on Cantonese level tone perception, and show that only the speech context helps Cantonese level tone perception. Although ADH is so far only tested with tones, it may be applicable to different types of phonetic inventories, such as consonants and vowels.

455911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
455911.value: As mentioned previously, ADH may be applicable to any phonetic inventory, including tones, vowels, and consonants. From the World Atlas of Language and Structures Online (http://wals.info/feature/2A#2/19.3/152.8), the size of the vowel inventory varies dramatically across different languages. A potential development would be to examine two languages: one with small vowel inventory size, the other language with large inventory size. Behavioral and EEG experiments could then be run to compare the sensitivity to formant changes among the two groups of native language users, specifically to test the hypothesis that sensitivity to formant changes is greater for speakers of the language with large inventory size. A similar approach could also be applied to consonants. In different languages, the voice onset time (VOT) serves to separate different numbers of stop categories (Lisker & Abramson, "A cross-language study of voicing in initial stops: Acoustical measurements", Word 20:384~422, 1964). For instance, in some languages, such as Korean, VOT separates three stop categories: p, pc, and ph, while in other languages, such as Cantonese, VOT separates just two stop categories: p and ph. It is reasonable to hypothesize that the denser use of VOT may provide its users with better ability to discriminate durational changes.

455911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
455911.value: A far-reaching hypothesis in linguistics is the Linguistic Relativity Hypothesis (LRH), also known as the Sapir–Whorf hypothesis. The idea of LRH is that people tend to think and behave differently according to the language that they use. In this project, we look at this issue by examining whether differences in the use of pitch to signify lexical meanings influence linguistic/non-linguistic pitch perception. The use of pitch patterns as lexical contrasts generally endows tone language speakers with better pitch ability, as indicated, for example, by the significantly higher prevalence of perfect pitch among native tone language speakers than among nontone language speakers. Moreover, Cantonese has a much denser tone inventory than Mandarin. We hypothesize that the density of a tone system affects its speakers pitch discrimination ability; we term this the Acoustic Density Hypothesis (ADH). More specially, we ask whether Cantonese listeners exhibit better pitch discrimination ability than Mandarin listeners given the much denser Cantonese tone system. In this project, behavioral and electroencephalographic experiments have been conducted to systematically examine the impact of tone language experience on linguistic/non-linguistic pitch perception. Findings of our several studies provide support for ADH. The project therefore leads to a deeper understanding of how language experience shapes perception.

456011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
456011.value: This paper investigates whether the existence and characteristics of an explicit employment agreement between a firm and its CEO affect the extent of managerial myopic behavior. Prior study reports that not all CEOs have explicit employment agreements (EAs)(Gillan, Hartzell, and Parrino 2009). An explicit employment agreement can protect CEOs from short-term swing in performance. Therefore, CEOs with executive agreements, especially agreements with a longer term contract, are under less pressure to maintain short-term performance. These CEOs are thus less likely to engage in myopic behavior. We use three proxies to capture myopic behavior: meeting/just beating analyst forecasts, earnings management/restatement, and R&D expenditures.We first hypothesize that firms whose CEOs with employment agreements are less likely involved in accounting restatements, less likely to just meet or beat analysts' forecasts, and have lower discretionary dedcution of R&D expenditure. In addition,we hypothsize and expect to show that the effect of employment agreements on managerial short-termism is stronger for firms with longer contract duration, firms with outside CEOs, firms from homogeneous industries, and firms with higher transient institutional ownership. 过往的研究表明并不是所有的上市公司都与它们的首席执行官(CEO)签订了明确的雇佣合约。本文进一步研究是否CEO的雇佣合约影响到了CEO的短视行为。雇佣合约的存在使得CEO免于受到短期企业业绩的波动的影响，因而可以使得这些企业管理者着眼于更长远的规划。我们的第一个假设是：那些与CEO签订有明确雇佣合约的公司相对来说是更少的可能性有会计报表更改或者是业绩仅仅符合分析师预期。同时，这些公司不太做出削减研究成本的决定。此外，我们预期雇佣合约对管理层短视行为的作用会更强对于那些有更长合约期的公司，从外部市场招聘CEO的公司，以及那些有太多短期机构投资者的公司。

456011.label: Realisation of objectives
456011.value: We are very happy to report that we successfully achieved ALL the stated objectives. Our paper was accepted by The Accounting Review, which is an A+ journal in Accounting research field. Specifically, we realize the objectives of our paper by finding: (1) We find that firms with CEO contractual protection (i.e., employment agreement) are less likely to cut R&D expenditures to avoid earnings decreases and are less likely to engage in real earnings management. (2) This effect increases with the duration and monetary strength of CEO contractual protection. (3) Employment agreement compliments the other internal control mechanism such as board independence, in terms of mitigating managers' short-termism.

456011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
456011.value: Given that we have the unique dataset of the agreements between the CEO and the firm, we plan to pursue other research ideas based on CEO contractual protection. At this stage, we aim at the association between CEOs' management earnings forecasts (frequency and accuracy) and CEO contractual protection. Such a research topic is still based on the documented effects of CEO contractual protection on managerial myopia.

456011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
456011.value: In this paper, we examine whether CEO contractual protection, in the form of employment agreements and standalone severance pay agreements, helps to reduce managerial short-termism. We find that CEO contractual protection is associated with a lower likelihood of cutting research and development costs (R&D). Such an effect of CEO contractual protection increases with the duration and monetary strength of the protection. Our paper contributes to the literature by examining how CEO contractual protection affects managerial short-termism. The findings suggest that CEO contractual protection reduces managers’ incentives to engage in myopic behavior. Therefore, our study complements prior studies that investigate how board monitoring and CEO equity incentives address managerial short-termism and advances the emerging literature on the effects of CEO contracts on corporate decisions.

456311.value: 人類腹視覺徑負責物件辨認的功能性結構

456311.label: Project Objectives
456311.value: To investigate if a large-scale map exists in the ventral visual pathway such that different regions contain information diagnostic for object recognition at different levels of detail. To study how activity patterns in the ventral visual pathway changes across different situations, in an attempt to reveal the dynamic nature of object representations.

To study how activity patterns in the ventral visual pathway changes across different situations, in an attempt to reveal the dynamic nature of object representations.

456311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
456311.value: This project seeks to understand the large-scale organization of the human ventral visual pathway responsible for object recognition. Humans recognize objects effortlessly and efficiently under a variety of viewing conditions, an achievement hardly shared by the most sophisticated computer programs. The neural computations that support such ability, however, remain a perplexing issue. Recent advances in neuroimaging techniques like functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) have shown in different regions of the pathway preferential activations to certain object categories compared with others. The principles governing such layout of activations are still an issue of intense debate, partly due to the difficulty in studying the contributions of individual principles in isolation and the weaknesses of conventional data analysis techniques. In this project, I propose to study one candidate principle – level of recognition. Multivariate pattern analyses (MVPA), a powerful data analysis tool in revealing the information content of neural activity, will be used. Novel, artificial objects will be shown to participants while their brain activity is monitored with fMRI. Using MVPA, I will investigate which parts of the ventral visual pathway contain information optimal for object recognition at different levels of detail. It is hypothesized that the medial regions of the ventral visual pathway, sensitive to coarse input to the periphery of the visual field, should contain information suited for coarse, general recognition. In contrast, the lateral regions of the ventral visual pathway, sensitive to foveal input with a high acuity, should contain information suited for more specific, subordinate-level recognition. The effect of different task demands, as well as different types of perceptual training, on the activity patterns of the ventral visual pathway will also be examined, in an attempt to reveal the dynamic nature of neural computations for object recognition. Together, the findings of the experiments can promote the development of a comprehensive account of the way object recognition is supported by the visual system. 本研究旨在了解人類腹視覺徑負責物件辨認的功能性結構。相比設計精密的計算機程式而言，人類能不費吹灰之力有效地辨識物件。可是，我們對這種能力背後的運作所知有限。最新的功能性核磁共振造影研究發現，腹視覺徑上各部份會對不同類型物件特別敏感。由於種種的局限(例如很難單獨研究個別原則對物件辨認的貢獻及傳統研究技術的限制)，如何解釋不同類型物件在大腦活動的差異在學術圈內引起了廣泛的爭論。在這項目中，我建議研究其中一項原則 - 辨認的程度。我們會以多變量模式分析在腹視覺徑上不同部份負責物件辦認的程度。此方法能更有效分析腦活動數據。在實驗進行時，被試會看見一些從未見過的物件，與此同時，他們的腦部活動會被功能性核磁共振造影技術記錄下來。我們假設腹視覺徑內側的地方對視野周邊所輸入的粗糙信息特別敏感，因此，這個地方應是負責處理普遍和粗略的分類。相反，外側的部份對由中央窩輸入的信息較敏感，所以，這部份相信是負責仔細辨識相似的物件。是次研究也會調查任務要求和感知訓練對腹視覺徑活動的影響，研究結果不但讓我們更清楚關於辨識物件神經計算方法，更可增加對物件辨認與視覺系統的認識。

456511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
456511.value: The aim of this project is to conduct research to establish the hypothesis that Matthew, in contrast to Mark, ‘deprivatized’ the inner world of Jesus Christ in his Gospel. Jesus Christ is one of the most influential people in history. There are different images of him as expressed in films, novels, literature, and above all in the bible. However, we still know little of how he actually lived as a person in Palestine two millennia ago. For over two centuries, scholars have been examining different textual sources, employing different methods of investigation and utilizing different disciplines of knowledge, but there is still no consensus on who this Jesus was. Scholars call this the study of the historical Jesus. We observe preliminarily that Matthew, in contrast to Mark, discloses /eliminates Jesus’ private feelings, thoughts and experiences, which fall into the field of psychological concepts in personality. We believe that the Jesus of history had his own personality traits, even though there might not be such words or concepts articulated by the Gospel writers in the ancient world. Now we intend to examine systematically the entire Greek text of the Gospel of Matthew and its source texts [Mark, Q and M], in the hope to establish the hypothesis that Matthew deprivatizes the inner world of Jesus Christ. Our research proposal will employ the best known typology centering on extraversion - introversion dichotomy [R. W. Coan, Concise Encyclopedia of Psychology, page 648-9] as framework to describe the personality of Jesus depicted in the Gospels of Matthew [and Mark implicitly]. The disclosed inner world of this deprivatized Jesus in Matthew suggests that this personality of the Matthean Jesus is thus shaped and shifted faraway from introversion. The present research project will firstly contribute to the redaction history of Matthew, with some other evidences and discussion, which will further contribute to the historical Jesus research.

456511.label: Major findings and research outcome
456511.value: 1) Matthew modifies Jesus’ intention in some narratives in Mark. For example, Jesus receives the Baptism of John. Matthew changes the present participle “πειραζομενοs” in Mark as infinitive “πειρασθηναι”, and inserts the proper name for Jesus (in Nominative case) into the Markan passive voice, ‘he is led up’. The new phrase in Matthew, ‘Jesus …… to be tempted’ (4:1), allows the possibility of being interpreted as the Greek articular infinitive, expressing the purpose of this Jesus being led up into the desert, that is, to be tempted. 2) Matthew expresses the human characteristics of Jesus from some Logienquelle [Q]. For example, Matthew incorporates and extends the narrative of Jesus’ Temptation from Q in the parallel, where Mark has a shorter version: the Matthean Jesus is said to be hungry, like a common human. This is a strong evident expressing Jesus’ inner feeling (hungry) and action (fasting) world. 3) Matthew uniquely (among the Gospels) introduces a weakness of Jesus, which is escaping from severe circumstances. This is anticipated as early as in the narrative of the Wise Men coming from the East. Matthew reports the tragedy of Jesus’ birth, being persecuted by King Herod. The reason for his being persecuted by King Herod is at the same time the hidden message, that this new born will also be a king, at least comparable to Herod. Matthew chooses the Greek word αναχωρεω (escape) to describe the Wise Men’s responsive action to the King and the obedient deed of Joseph to God for bring the child Jesus escaping from Herod. With these two events, Matthew develops the idea of ‘escape’ and applies it to the ministry of Jesus. Jesus is said to escape when he hears the imprisonment of his teacher John the Baptist, when he encounters much frustration from his ministry, etc. details can be seen in the prepared book concerned. 4) Our findings: Matthew redacts and changes subtly the original sources (Mark, Q and M-Special Tradition) to show Jesus’ human characteristics. This includes Jesus’ biological / physical needs (hungry), his thoughts (intention, decision and conception, etc.) It is encouraging to discover that Matthew subtly introduces the weakness of Jesus, which in embedded in the whole Gospel of Matthew, which is deserved for further research. The above findings affirm our hypothesis, that Matthew externalizes many Jesus’ private events, where we see Jesus’ inner experiences.

456511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
456511.value: During the course of research, we encounter many undiscovered aspects of the Jesus as a human being in the Gospel of Matthew. Among them, we note one specific instance, that is, Jesus question to his followers, ‘Who am I?’ This is indeed a common question today, which is especially frequently seen among teenagers realizing their own identity, or among adults in case adverse painful event, like Middle Age Crisis, departure (divorce or death) of spouse, etc. Most New Testament scholars, intended or unintended overlooked this question from a human perspective, by shifting their attention to the divine purpose of Jesus’ question, e.g., for teaching his own disciples. Almost no commentaries ever dare or want to explore that Jesus might have identity crisis in terms of modern psychology. At this point, we would like to research and construct further this character of Jesus above in the future. In other words, the experience of this present research project enlightens us another yet lost dimension of reading the New Testament anew.

456511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
456511.value: Today, Jesus is believed worshipped as God in the Christian Faith. Although this Jesus Christ is regarded as fully human and fully divine since the Chalcedonian Creed of the 5th century, his human characteristics have never been taken seriously. But, from the New Testament, it is clearly recorded that this same Jesus Christ was a man living in history some two millennia ago. Our research tries to re-introduce in the exegetical arena the inner dimension and the irreplaceable development of its externalization. During our thorough study of all the ministry journey of Jesus, we try to demonstrate his personal image: his feeling, his vision, his previous experience. We find that there are lots of human traits of this Jesus Christ, even though the author Matthew intends to present him as the Messiah, Son of God, which is a figure superior to normal human beings. Besides Jesus Christ’s thoughts, feelings, we also discover that Jesus’ weakness, e.g., escaping from severe environment, is evident in the Gospel. Our findings will further contribute to the historical Jesus research.

457111.label: Project Title(Chinese)
457111.value: 基本心理概念在中國文化裏的譜系

457111.label: Project Objectives
457111.value: To embark on etymological and semantic analyses of the fundamental psychological concepts in Chinese culture. To identify and analyze related signs clustering around the selected psychological concepts. To analyze relevant discourses in a great variety of Chinese texts. The overarching aims range from achieving a new understanding of Chinese culture, through laying a sounder basis for cultural-historical psychology, to extending the possibilities of humanities research and demonstrating its educational values.

To identify and analyze related signs clustering around the selected psychological concepts.
To analyze relevant discourses in a great variety of Chinese texts.

The overarching aims range from achieving a new understanding of Chinese culture, through laying a sounder basis for cultural-historical psychology, to extending the possibilities of humanities research and demonstrating its educational values.

457111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
457111.value: What are the meanings of fundamental psychological concepts such as "awareness", "emotion", "intention", "intelligence", "morality", "beauty", and "self" as they have evolved and changed in traditional and contemporary China? This seemingly simple question carries profound implications when seen in the light of a neglected Vygotskian thesis — that "the meaningful word is a microcosm of human consciousness" (Vygotsky, 1934/1987, p.285). The proposed study will embark on a genealogical analysis of the aforementioned psychological concepts. The study is genealogical in the sense that it takes a critical stand on the origin and development of word meanings, echoing the groundbreaking works of Nietzsche and Foucault. It also goes beyond an understanding of collective consciousness to the reconstruction of real human practices. The research will consist of three distinct but related phases. In the first phase, the development of the meanings of the words that characterize the selected concepts will be examined by way of etymological and semantic analyses. In the second phase, clusters of related signs (including words) will be further identified and analyzed. For the analysis of the most important signs identified, the route mapped out by Benjamin in his Arcades Project will serve as the methodological guide. The results of these two phases will provide clues for tracing relevant effective statements and the formation of discourses in a great variety of Chinese texts; this will constitute the Foucauldian genealogical study in the third phase. The significance of the study lies in its implications for cultural studies in general and for understanding Chinese culture in particular. Furthermore, it will help to build a sounder basis for cultural-historical psychology, and to provide resources and stimulation for pedagogical endeavors. Knowledge about the role of concepts in human development sheds further light on the value of this study. Concepts, which first took shape in human beings’ making sense of the immediate environment and in their need to communicate, have evolved into a highly complex system throughout human history. Each concept is related with other concepts and images. Old concepts can turn dormant, giving way to the emergence of new ones. Such a system, which could either facilitate or confine human development in a subtle and persuasive sense, is often transmitted in a piecemeal way. Considering the dialectical relations between experiences and concepts, a genealogical analysis of fundamental psychological concepts is a significant key to unlocking a better cultural-historical understanding of human experiences.

457611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
457611.value: This aim of this project is to explore the ways in which globalization, Chinese national policies and interests of local actors have interacted to determine the trajectory of corporate law reform in China. Traditionally, Chinese company law was largely the product of a small coterie of officials and legal scholars. Recent economic reforms and social transformations in China have, however, radically changed the political economy of corporate law. An array of state and non-state actors have competed to exert their influence on the evolution of China’s corporate legal rules and institutions, making the process of law reform in this area of economic life much more complex. The particular focus of this project is the adoption and adaptation of the UK-style mandatory bid rule (“MBR”) as a key component of China’s takeover regulatory regime. Under this rule, anyone purchasing a controlling stake (30%, for example) in a listed company must make an offer (the “mandatory bid”) for the remainder of the company’s shares. China adopted MBR from as early as 1993. The rule has been enforced, however, in a way that differs significantly from how it is enforced in the UK. In 2005, amidst the sweeping company and securities law reform in China, the UK-style MBR was substantially amended and, as a consequence, China’s existing takeover regime has deviated considerably from its UK archetype. The project will focus upon the various local actors in China, both state and non-state, whose interests are affected by the imported UK-style MBR, and analyze how their preferences have influenced the way in which the MBR is actually enforced and how it has recently been reformed. It is anticipated that the project will, based upon its systematic, empirical and comparative analysis of the rise and decline of the UK-style MBR in China, propose a more grounded theory for understanding how the forces of globalization, national economic policies and the preferences of local actors interact to shape the trajectory of corporate law reforms in China. 本項目旨在研究全球化進程、中國國家政策與地方利益主體三者之間的相互作用，如何影響和決定中國公司法改革進程。一直以來，中國公司法律很大程度上是由為數甚少的官員和法律學者所決定。然而，伴隨著中國近年的經濟改革和社會變遷，公司法的政治經濟維度正在發生顯著變革。諸多國家主體和社會主體都在試圖影響中國公司法律條文和制度的演進，從而使得公司相關的法律改革進程尤為錯綜複雜。 本項目重點研究中國公司並購規管法律中的一項重要制度，即移植自英國並不斷本土化的強制要約收購規則。該規則的含義是，任何收購人在收購上市公司控股股份（例如，30%的股份）後，必須發出要約（即強制要約），收購該上市公司所餘全部股份。早在1993年，中國就採納並制定了英式強制要約收購規則。但其在中國的實施情況與英國大相徑庭。2005年中國公司證券法改革，大幅度修訂了之前採用的英式強制要約收購規則。這使得中國現行的公司並購規管法律越來越迥異於英國相關法律制度。 本項目著力研究移植自英國的強制要約收購規則對中國諸多國家主體和社會主體的利益的影響，以及這些主體的利益偏好反作用於該規則在中國的實施和改革。本項目將從系統分析、實證研究和比較研究等多個視角，剖析英式強制要約收購規則在中國的興衰命運。並在此基礎上進行理論建構，試圖解釋全球化進程、國家經濟政策與地方主體利益偏好三者之間如何互為作用，並深刻影響中國公司法律改革進程。

457611.label: Realisation of objectives
457611.value: The four project objectives have been fully achieved. The ways in which these objectives have been achieved are summarized as follows: Objective 1: A comprehensive collection of primary and secondary materials has been compiled, documenting the legislative, regulatory, and policy discussions and debates that informed the evolution of the UK-style MBR in China. A large number of the documents in this collection are not publicly accessible, yet unclassified. Moreover, elite interviews have been conducted with (a) the CSRC’s current and former officials involved in the making the 2002 and/or the 2006 Takeover Measures; (b) officials in the Legislative Affairs Commission of the National People’s Congress Standing Committee involved in the enactment of the 2005 Securities Law; and (c) Chinese and overseas advisors to the Chinese legislators and regulators. These interviews offer a rare glimpse into the otherwise opaque process of rulemaking in China. Objective 2: The empirical investigation of the CSRC’s enforcement of the MBR has based on a unique, hand-collected dataset, which encompasses all publicly accessible CSRC’s MBR waiver decisions taken during the period between 1993 and 2010. The CSRC decisions often times, however, contain only limited information, thus falling short of providing adequate information that is crucial for the quantitative investigation. Steps have been taken to enrich the dataset to the extent that the research questions can adequately be addressed with solid quantitative data. First, a wide range of variables have been identified and defined in relation the underlying transactions pertaining to the CSRC decisions. Second, data on these identified variables have been hand-collected to the extent that they are publicly available. Third, a coding scheme has been designed and implemented for the applicable variables. Research assistants have been engaged to hand-collect and process the data. A rigorous process of “quality control” has been put in place to monitor data collection and processing to ensure its integrity and reliability. Objective 3: Elite interviews are the primary method of empirical investigation. Interviewees have included senior executives of the companies concerned, rank-and-file bureaucrats of the local state-owned assets supervision and administration agencies, as well as legal and financial professionals involved in the transactions concerned. Amongst the interviewees are also current and former CSRC officials tasked with enforcing the MBR rules. Objective 4: Conceptualization and generalization on the basis of the qualitative and quantitative findings have led to important theory development.

457611.label: Major findings and research outcome
457611.value: Empirical and theoretical findings of this project are significant with respect to a number of academic discourses. Given the space limitation, three aspects are highlighted as follows. First, this research challenges and develops a prevailing theory – the interest group politics theory – for understanding the varying evolutionary trajectories of national takeover laws. This research shows that the existing theory, alone, is limited in capturing in full the political economy dynamics in developing and emerging economies. It proposes that the existing theory be extended to take in account the state capitalist approach to economic development as adopted by many emerging economies, including China. In these economies, takeover regulation is sensitive to changes in national approaches to industrial transformation. “Obstructive” takeover rules are typically prone to legal changes in favor of more “takeover-friendly” rules, in the interest of achieving greater economies of scale and concentration, and trumping the powerful vested interests that opposed reforms. Second, this research enriches the emerging and growing literature on the political economy of corporate law in China. For instance, in the context of corporate takeovers, it empirically supports the hypotheses that the higher the level of government that ultimately controls the acquirers/sellers, the better the acquirers/sellers fared in securing the waiver of the MBR obligation, and that the regulator favors systematically state-owned enterprises over privately-owned firms. In the case of shareholder voting, this research empirically shows that China’s approach to cumulative voting has been shaped, on the whole, by the majority/controlling shareholders of the Chinese listed sector, who exert considerable influence on the Chinese lawmakers. Third, this research establishes the usefulness of the political economy approach to law in newer areas of corporate law. This research suggests that China’s increasing assertiveness in participating in re-shaping international banking legal order has been driven, in part, by the “private” institutional interests of China’s banking regulator. On a broader level, it highlights the need for one to look beyond the general rhetoric of the state actor’s interests and preferences, and to identify the underlying interests and incentives of domestic-level players that play an important role in shaping the higher, and more visible, interests and preferences of the national states. Findings of this research have been presented in 13 invited conference presentations and invited public lectures, and published with leading international refereed journals and prestigious academic presses. Further, two more articles are under review and to be submitted for review, respectively.

457611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
457611.value: This research has strong potential for further development in two respects. First, the quantitative approach taken by this research and the ensuing unique dataset lay a solid foundation for interdisciplinary collaboration with colleagues in other disciplines, in particular, in finance and accounting. I have already collaborated closely with Professor Shanmin Li of Sun Yat-Sen University, a nationally renowned professor of finance, and his team to develop findings of this research into a journal article currently under review by a top-rated economics journal. I have been co-mentoring a research student of his whose PhD dissertation will draw largely from the quantitative findings of this research. Second, the political economy approach to law adopted by this research has proven its utility in various subjects of the broadly defined corporate law, including takeover regulation, shareholder voting, as well as financial law. I intend to further extend the application of this powerful analytical tool to other related areas of law and, where appropriate, develop them into new GRF proposals.

457611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
457611.value: Traditionally, company law in China was largely the product of a small coterie of officials and legal scholars. Recent economic reforms and social transformations in China have, however, radically changed the political economy of corporate law. An array of state and, gradually, non-state actors have competed to exert their influence on the evolution of China’s corporate legal framework. The recent company law reforms present a rare glimpse into the dynamics of commercial legal changes in China. The existing literature has yet to address an important issue: what are the forces that have shaped the evolution of corporate legal rules in China, and in what way have they done so? This research presents an empirical-based political economy assessment of the above issue by looking into the complex dynamics between the forces of globalization, Chinese national economic policies, and diversifying interests of local actors, and their influence on the making and enforcement of corporate rules in China. It contributes to a number of important discourses and debates in corporate law and comparative law, and in related disciplines. Its empirical and theoretical findings also inform the ongoing policy debates on corporate law reforms in China and beyond.

457711.label: Project Title(Chinese)
457711.value: 為自然議價：中國城市規劃制度對“環境”的處理

457711.label: Project Objectives
457711.value: To identify changes in the planning system in response to national and local environmental agenda. We want to understand new environmental concerns of the Chinese planning system, and to explore the difference between these concerns and earlier perceptions towards environment. We will focus particularly on the key instruments of the planning system. To determine the extent to which these changes contribute to form a planning regime for articulating spatial strategies which interrelate environmental and economic objectives in a diffused power context. The goals and scope of the planning system are decided by laws, regulations, state policies, and local interpretations, underpinned by a hierarchical review. One consequence is that no specific scope and contents of planning policies are clearly defined. Moreover, many organizations and agencies are involved in the plan-making process. The inter-connections of different actors comprise an ensemble of socially embedded, politically regularized and strategically selective forces in land use decision-making, which form another focus of our research. To produce a comparison of different pathways in and through which the environment is being treated by the planning regimes of selected cities. This has the merit to provide situated accounts to inform specificity and varieties, but at the same time, unravel generative conditions and circumstance. To critically analyze the research findings, and evaluate and theorize the functions of the urban planning system towards environmental protection. This can lead us to make recommendations on the improvement of the planning system to incorporate environment into spatial formation of cities.

457711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
457711.value: 中國城市正經歷著飛速發展、人口膨脹與環境惡化的動蕩時期。全球變暖、碳排放劇增、地方特色的消失、城市蔓延等已經成爲亟待解決的環境問題。因此，1990年代以來，各級中國政府都幾乎無一例外、信誓旦旦地將環境保護列爲最核心的政策内容。許多政界與學界人士認爲，城市規劃制度在實施環境保護政策過程中起著至關重要的作用。與此相應，政府主導的綠色規劃項目也開始興起。雖然環境議題越來越受到重視，但如何將這些議題轉變為可推行的政策卻是困難重重。環保理念挑戰著傳統發展觀，也衝擊著以推動資本積累為目的的規劃觀念。其實，新的綠色規劃政策與實踐已開始出現，但現有研究並沒有關注到這一現象，也沒有探討過其中的過程與爭議。學界與政界對規劃如何將環境議題融入到城市空間發展中還所知甚少。這主要表現在兩方面。其一，沒有系統研究與案例分析揭示現有的規劃體制到底如何界定和處理‘環境’這一要素；其二，沒有弄清規劃決策中有關落實環境保護政策的制度障礙。 本研究旨在系統分析中國城市規劃體制如何界定與處理‘環境’要素，以填補現有研究的空白。我們選取了珠江三角洲的若干城市作爲案例，評估各地方規劃實踐中，環境議題被賦予的涵義與被重視的程度，並與當地優先發展目標進行比較，探討這些議題在多大程度上融入到了空間發展政策中。爲此，我們將側重分析城市規劃制度中的四大工具，它們是規劃法規、發展方案、規劃機構與發展控制。這四大工具共同構成了一組關鍵的政策手段，推動著規劃體制的運作，並將規劃目標轉變為空間現實。本研究將分析各案例城市規劃體制中的四大政策工具，了解它們如何在商業驅動的空間發展現實中，處理有關環境議題。研究成果將有助我們評價到底在多大程度上，環境理念被最終付諸實現了。同時，研究具有很重要的政策意義，將提出建議如何改善中國城市規劃制度，如何更好地將環境理念融合到空間規劃中，並加快區域環境政策的制定與實施。

457711.label: Realisation of objectives
457711.value: We have fully achieved Objective 1 by examining the changing environmental concerns of the Chinese planning system. One key methodology is to systematically unravel major environmental discourses in master plans in selected cities. It is found that the meaning of environment in urban planning has snowballed over time. Other than the common argument of bureaucratic inertia in sustaining old discourses, we view environmental concerns and discourses being complementary and socially constructed. Objective 2 is mostly achieved (90%). We have traced the planning process of forming major environmental discourses, and the political representations of different stakeholders. We have also explored how powerful stakeholders have institutionalized their political projects into planning system through strategies such as installing new regulation, setting up new agencies, making new plans, and designating new territories. One PhD student is still working on how these are built into planning organization per se. Objective 3 is mostly achieved (80%). We have thoroughly compared the pathways of two major cities in the Pearl River Delta, i.e. Guangzhou and Shenzhen. They share similarities and differences. On one hand, political actors in both cities employ ‘scale’ as a discursive strategy to fulfil their political agenda and justify their political project. On the other hand, these scalar discourses leave their divergent imprints on the problematisation and spatial treatment of the environment in planning practice in Shenzhen and Guangzhou. One PhD student is still working on comparing other cities. Objective 4 is fully achieved. We have evaluated current theoretical debates on the functions of the urban planning system towards environmental care. We note that existing accounts have at least two inadequacies. First, there is a propensity to read environmental discourses in planning as a direct response to specific environmental problems or prevailing environmental rhetoric. Such reading is undesirable for obscuring the nature of environment as a social construct. Second, existing literature has a tendency to view environmental discourses in a singular logic. They are portrayed as either rhetoric to cope with local environmental constraints or struggles to meet demands imposed by higher administration. They are also conceived as local strategies to attract capital investors. These interpretations, though insightful, conceal the more extensive argumentative struggles occurring at multiple scales to define local environmental discourses. In view of these criticisms, we have developed a new theoretical perspective to read environmental governance in planning. Policy recommendations are drawn against the context of China.

457711.label: Major findings and research outcome
457711.value: We are still working on some journal papers and a PhD student is still finalizing her PhD thesis on this topic. At the time of writing this report, we have presented the research findings in 12 regional and international conferences. One MPhil thesis is completed. Two book chapters have been published by reputable publishers. Four journal papers have been published or accepted by top international journals, including Urban Geography, International Development Planning Review, Urban Studies, and Environment and Planning C. Thanks to the funding of this project, one paper, ‘Environment’ as an Evolving Concept in China’s Urban Planning System, which is co-authored by the PI and a team member, was awarded the prize for the best paper published in International Development Planning Review in 2014. According to the editors of this reputable journal, despite the competition being especially intense in 2014, they were unanimous in selecting our paper for the prize. They view that the paper deals with a topical issue in an engaging manner, building on strong case-study material on changing environmental discourses in the planning in Chinese cities to make important and wide-reaching conclusions regarding the role of the environment in urban planning. In additional to these outputs, the research has yielded some important research findings. Theoretically, we have developed a new theoretical perspective to interpret the environmental governance in planning for Chinese cities. We start this journey by looking at the environmental discourses in planning. Instead of treating these discourses in a technically-oriented manner, we propose using a scale-sensitive discourse approach to uncover their social construction. Our theoretical perspective is built on three premises. First, as argued by a growing rank of planning theorists, environmental discourses in planning are not ontological pre-given concepts. Rather, they are “selective abstractions which amplify one meaning of the environment and marginalize others. Their formation is infused with power relations”. Second, the formation of environmental discourses is not a singular process – whether as a local arena of governance or a milieu of central-local struggle – but rather a multiple scale one. Third, the emergence and subsequent reconfiguration of a particular scalar structure of environmental governance is the outcome of the discursive contest among various political actors, whose discourses acquire persuasive power through employing scale to frame how the world should be observed. The perspective built upon these premises has been further advanced to study other aspects of planning regimes regarding environmental governance.

457711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
457711.value: In recent years, environment has become a key issue in urban planning practice. This is partially revealed by the surging environmental narratives such as eco-cities, sponge-cities, and low-carbon cities. More people realize that technically-oriented view is no longer valid and adequate to explain this phenomenon. Our theoretical approach will have great potential in this regard. Furthermore, while most studies focus on coastal cities, inland cities are indeed facing more daunting environmental challenges due to high environmental vulnerability. Academically speaking, there is an urgent need to shift our research focus from coastal region to inland areas. The PI will follow these trends and propose new projects in the near future.

457711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
457711.value: This research has chosen the planning regimes of several cities in the Pearl River Delta (PRD) as case studies. So, the research is highly relevant to Hong Kong, which is an essential part of the PRD. Hong Kong has collaborated with a few PRD cities in addressing cross-border environmental issues, which remains a top policy priority. A deep investigation into the proposed topic is expected to facilitate the formation of a region-wide policy regime to help manage regional environmental quality. The proposed research is thus of important theoretical and practical value. Theoretically, the study will fill in a research gap and develop interpretations to understand how planning developed to formalize environmental governance. Currently, the western literature has dominated the study of this subject. This project is an important Asian contribution to the discipline in further understanding of the dynamic relationship between nature and space in a transitional society. Practically, the research will increase our knowledge on the changing environmental discourses within the planning system, and how planning decisions are made and implemented institutionally towards environmental care.

457911.label: Project Title(Chinese)
457911.value: 经济结构变迁对生育与教育投资的影响

457911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
457911.value: Over the past thirty years, the study of long-term growth has been one of the most active areas of economic research. Economists have identified two key mechanisms to explain the transition from pre-industrial stagnation to sustained modern growth. The first deals with structural transformation involving a falling share of agriculture in economic output and employment and the second with demographic transition featuring family fertility choices and investment in human capital. While each of the two factors plays a critical role in long-term growth, the intrinsic relationship between these two mechanisms has yet to be explored systematically. However, we believe that forging a linkage between family behavior and structural change can be a constructive step towards deepening the existing studies and improving our understanding about the micro foundation of long-term growth. The objective of this project is to investigate how families make decisions on fertility and educational investment in children in response to structural transformation. We will incorporate two prominent features of development into a model of parental investment in children. First, the structures of production differ across rural and urban sectors. While family farms are the dominant form of organization in agriculture, urban household members typically participate in factory-based activities in the labor market. Second, long-term development invariably involves persistent migration of rural workers to urban settings. By introducing these features of development into a model of intrahousehold resource allocation, we will study how organizations of production and migration expectations influence the allocation of educational resources among siblings and the joint decisions of fertility and schooling. Our empirical analysis will use the 1989 Taiwan Women and Fertility Survey, supplemented with our own collection of county-level data, to test the implications of the model and to document the trends in fertility, schooling attainment and sibling education distributions over six decades of rapid economic development in Taiwan. The theoretical and empirical findings on the linkage between family behavior and structural change will likely provide insights for future studies of long-term growth. The findings will not only illuminate the growth experience of a representative Asian economy but also shed light on the mechanisms of the general development process. Since the determination of fertility and human capital investment are fundamental factors behind poverty elimination and sustained growth, this project has the potential to help formulate informed development policies. 本课题旨在分析经济结构变迁对生育与家庭教育投资的影响。我们将长期经济发展的两个显著特征引入家庭对儿女投资的经济模型。首先，农村与城市部门的生产结构有所不同。在农业生产中，以家庭为单位的农户是最主要的组织形式；而在城市，工厂与公司是人们就业的主要机构。其次，长期经济发展总是伴随着城乡移民。我们把这些生产结构的特征纳入家庭内部资源配置的框架，从而分析家庭如何在经济发展的背景下选择生育数量、确定教育投资以及优化儿女之间的资源分配。我们采用《台湾1989年妇女与生育调查》数据，并补充丰富的县级统计资料，验证模型的假设，以求对台湾60年的经济发展、家庭决策机制做既全面又深入的剖析。

458111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
458111.value: Abstract The proposed project aims to undertake a critical study of the moral educational thoughts of Lu Jie (魯潔) and her community of scholars in Mainland China since 1980s. These scholars were former doctoral students and postdoctoral fellows under the supervision of Prof. Lu Jie, an eminent moral education scholar in China. Since the adoption of the reform and opening-up policy, moral education in China has undergone a process of depoliticization. The emphasis of moral education has been gradually shifted from ideology and politics to personal moral qualities and individual well-being. Teaching in key normal universities and involving in curriculum reforms, Lu Jie and her students have made considerable contribution to reconceptualize moral education for a reforming China. Their concerns are both critical and constructive. They are critical of the domination of the education system by “leftist” doctrinarism, which has led to the disappearance of human individuality and the failure of moral education. They are also alert to the rise of possessive individualism and soulless hedonism after the rise of market economy and see the need of rediscovering the spiritual dimension of moral education. Thus they have endeavored to reconstruct the moral education in China. Drawing on the contemporary Western resources, such as humanistic and religious philosophies, psychology, and educational theories, they have searched for a renewed moral education that can take individual happiness and human connectedness seriously. They have made a variety of attempts to expand the territory of moral education into hitherto uncharted areas like aesthetic education, affective education, character and virtue education, life-based education, and religious and spiritual education. The themes of self-transcendence, individual happiness, and human connectedness run through most of their works. This project will analyze the basic ideas and conceptual models in the academic works of these scholars. By so doing, this project aims to find out how these scholars have reinterpreted and appropriated the Chinese Marxist political-moral ideologies, traditional Chinese moral ideas, and Western ethical and educational thoughts in their reconceptualization of moral education, and how all this is interweaved with the socioeconomic development in the last thirty years. The project is expected to contribute to the critical and comprehensive understanding of the recent development of moral education in Mainland China and also facilitate the dialogues on moral, life, and spiritual education between the Mainland, Hong Kong, and other Chinese societies worldwide. 本建議計畫旨在對自1980年起，中國大陸著名教育學者魯潔及她的學者群的德育思想作批判性研究。這學者群成員都是曾受魯潔教授指導的博士研究生或博士後研究員。自中國實施改革開放政策以來，中國德育經歷了非政治化的過程，德育的關注重點漸漸從意識形態和政治轉移到個人的道德素養和個體的福祉。魯潔及她的學生都在中國的重點師範大學任教，為重新構思改革中的中國德育，作出了很大的貢獻。他們的關心既有批判的一面，也有重構的一面。他們批評「左」的教條主義一直主導了教育體系，使人的個殊性消失了，也導致了德育的失敗。他們同時警惕到在市場經濟的出現，使佔有式的個人主義和無靈魂的享樂主義過速擴散，故他們提出必須重新發現德育的精神內涵。因此他們致力重建中國的德育，吸取西方的資源，包括人文主義和宗教哲學、心理學及教育理論。他們期望能探索一個新的德育，能夠重視個體的福祉及人與人的聯繫。他們採取各種途徑，嘗試擴展德育，走進美學教育、情感教育、品格與德性教育、生命為本教育，及宗教與靈性教育等尚待發現的領域，讓自我超越、個人福祉、人際聯繫等主題貫穿了他們的作品。本計畫旨在透過分析這些學者的學術著作中的基本觀念和概念模式，找出他們在重新構思中國德育的過程中，如何重新詮釋和挪用中國馬克思主義政治道德思想、傳統中國道德觀念及西方倫理和教育思想，以及這些內容又如何交織於近三十年社會經濟發展。本計畫期望能豐富我們對中國大陸近期德育發展的批判和全面理解，以及促進大陸、香港和其他華人城市之間在德育、生命教育和靈性教育方面對話。

458311.label: Project Objectives
458311.value: To analyze the effects of factor substitution on economic growth within a multi-factor context as well as the effects of the nesting specification of the CES function. To study different concepts of the aggregate elasticity of substitution and to reconcile the conflicting findings of the existing literature in a unified framework. To investigate the effects of factor substitution (or complementarity) on income distribution and to study the tradeoff between distribution and growth of factor substitution.

458311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
458311.value: The neoclassical aggregate production function has played a decisive role in the modern theory of economic growth. Specifically, it is well documented that the sources of growth are either increases in factor per worker and/or improvements in the state of technology. However, what has been usually overlooked is the role played by the elasticity of substitution when the neoclassical production function takes a more realistic constant-elasticity-of-substitution (CES) specification. This research project studies how the elasticity of substitution affects economic growth and income distribution in the macroeconomy. Our investigation takes two channels. First, when there are more than two factor inputs in production, we consider the specification of a nesting CES function and examine the effects of nesting on growth and distribution in this multi-factor context. In addition, the concept of aggregate elasticity of substitution (AES) is introduced as an overall measure of factor substitution. Beside theoretical analytics, we also examine parameterizations of the models that are consistent with data observations so as to have a better understanding of our findings quantitatively. Second, we explore the consequences when the AES is endogenous. This involves the distinction between the concepts of partial and total AES. We compare these concepts of AES and examine their robustness in different popular models of economic growth.

458311.label: Realisation of objectives
458311.value: For the first two objectives, the important findings are published in two international refereed journals: Journal of Macroeconomics and Journal of Public Economic Theory. In the former publication, we have examined the relation between aggregate elasticity of substitution (AES) and capital accumulation (the AES-K relation) in a two-level, two-sector Solow growth model. There are two intermediate goods produced by capital and labor, while the final good is produced by combining the two intermediate goods. When capital (labor) is only used in producing one of the intermediate goods, then a negative (positive) AES-K relation is the likely outcome. Without specific factors in production, then we have to differentiate the concepts of "global" versus "local" AES-K relation. While the local AES-K relation is possibly monotone, the global AES-K relation is always non-monotone. When the intermediate goods are gross substitutes (complements) in the final-good production, the global AES-K relation is hump- (U-) shaped. In the latter publication, we have constructed a real business cycle (RBC) model to study the effects of balanced-budget taxation rules on capital and labor with normalized CES production technologies. Our focus is to study how the presence of factor substitution may change the conventional conclusions on the effects of factor taxation on important issues like income distribution. Using the two-step normalization procedure, we can identify two separate effects of factor substitution on the balanced budget rules, namely, the efficiency effect and the distribution effect. The former always enhances the destabilizing property of the balanced budget rules so that the steady-state equilibrium is more likely to be indeterminate as factor substitution improves. The latter depends on the relative abundance of the factors of production in the economy. For the economically relevant case where per capita capital is relatively more abundant so that these effects are opposing at work, then a larger elasticity of factor substitution instead makes the balanced budget rules less destabilizing. For the last objective, we have been working on the income distribution of the world economy under the constant-elasticity-of-substitution (CES) production technology. We focus on its application to world income disparity issues of development accounting. We have organized the findings in a working paper and have presented the results at several international conferences so as to get feedback from the peer for further polishing.

458311.label: Major findings and research outcome
458311.value: In this reporting period, we have focused our analysis on the application of how the concept of elasticity of substitution (EOS) can be reinterpreted as a mean of production efficiency, namely, the idea of technology assimilation in production. Thus, the concept of EOS can be understood as a measure of endogenous total factor productivity (TFP) based on the interaction of stage-dependent local knowledge of a country with advanced foreign technologies. We then perform development and growth accounting exercises to better understand the large and widening TFP gaps across countries and over time. By comparing our results with other popular models, we find that the lack of assimilation of frontier technologies can be instrumental in differentiating trapped economies from miracle economies. About 40-70% of the rapid growth experienced in miracle economies can be attributed to positive assimilation, and over 50% of the negative growth outcome in trapped economies is due to backward assimilation. This finding suggests that an adequate provision of correct incentives and institutional settings is crucial for domestic firms to assimilate relevant frontier technologies in a way that is suitable for their development stages.

458311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
458311.value: In our comparison with existing popular models in the literature, there is an idea of directed technical change which may be very similar to the idea of differentiated elastcities of factor substitution. One common question raised in our presentation in international conferences is that how one can differentiate the endogenous total factor productivity (TFP) that is based on popular factor-augmenting technical changes with CES production technologies from ours which is based on technology assimilation. In our future revision, we plan to attack this difficult issue by developing different accounting equations that come from these different approaches and perform level-income accounting. We need to assess quantitatively which approach can come up with a better TFP from the accounting exercises. Once this is done, we can wrapp up the paper for top-journal submission.

458311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
458311.value: Why, in the past half-century, have many countries successfully taken off, catching up with world leaders, while some have experienced growth stagnation? The world income distribution has widened over the last 50 years. From 1970 to 2007, the U.S. real GDP per capita relative to that of poor nations in the bottom 10 percentile was about 5.4 times on average, with the gap rising over time. Macroeconomists attempt to account for the income differences using an aggregate production function. They find that, even when controlling for the accumulation of physical and human capital per worker, an unusually large residual (known as total factor productivity or TFP) is still required to account for the income disparities. Over the past two decades, the field of development accounting has emerged to understand the problems; it focuses primarily on correcting the mismeasurements of factors inputs and identifying missing inputs in the production framework. In this research project, we base on the idea of factor substitution and technology assimilation to develop a constant-elasticity-of-substitution production function for quantifying the TFP gaps. This in turn provides an explanation to the world income disparities.

458411.label: Project Title(Chinese)
458411.value: 有中國特色的基督教話語: 中國政治與文化處境中的基督新教神學(1980-2010)

458411.label: Project Objectives
458411.value: To reconstruct an historical account of Protestant theology in the changing political, social, and cultural context of China from 1980 to 2010 on the basis of three decades of writings of pastors, church workers, and theologians published in Nanjing Theological Review and Tian Feng, as well as books written by individual theologians, supplemented by oral history obtained from in-depth interviews. To reconstruct major Protestant theological discourses in this period, highlighting their tensions and interactions, thus contributing to the understanding of church-state relations in China. To evaluate how the theological discourses have interpreted Christian theological traditions for the present situation of China, thus contributing to the study and development of Chinese contextual theology. To build up a comprehensive indexed database of articles in Nanjing Theological Review and Tian Feng, thus contributing to future research on Chinese Protestantism.
