462811.label: Major findings and research outcome
462811.value: The objectives of this study were to investigate the effect of LMHFV on the recruitment of intravenously administered MSCs to fracture sites in osteoporotic bones; to evaluate the mechanism of MSC recruitment through SDF-1; and to compare the expression of SDF-1 and CXCR4 between treatment and control groups. The labeled MSCs recruitment was assessed by bioluminescence imaging, while fracture repair was monitored radiographically, densitometrically, histologically and biomechanically. SDF-1 was reported to modulate homing and engraftment of circulating MSCs by binding to its receptor CXCR4, thus expanding the pool of osteogenic precursor cells in fracture site [Kitaori T, et al. Arthritis Rheum, 2009]. The major finding of the current research project was the confirmation of LMHFV capability in enhancing administered MSC to the fracture sites in osteoporotic bone. Results of this study proved the interactions between LMHFV and SDF-1/CXCR4 pathway in osteoporotic fracture healing. Comparing to MG and CG, vibration increased GFP-labeled MSCs in fracture site that might help promote callus formation at early stage (week 2 and week 4), and later on (week 8) increased BMD in osteoporotic bone. Moreover, the recruitment of MSC to the fracture site was related to SDF-1 and CXCR4 signaling pathway as shown by the antagonization experiments. As shown by our results, the promoting effect of LMHFV was attenuated when adding SDF-1 antagonist, AMD3100 during LMHFV treatment, as shown by weaker GFP signal intensity in fracture site and smaller callus (week 2 and week 4). The findings of this study showed that mechanical stimulation, in form of LMHFV, might be able to regulate SDF-1/CXCR4 pathway during fracture healing. It also provides strong evidence that SDF-1 mediated MSCs migration might be one of the crucial mechanisms through which LMHFV enhances osteoporotic fracture healing. The significance of this study is that it explored the mechanism of LMHFV effect on MSCs recruitment in osteoporotic fracture, and also demonstrated the potential of applying LMHFV for promoting osteoporotic fracture healing in the clinical settings. The major research outcome is that these results have provided further insight into the mechanism of enhancement of fracture healing by means of MSC recruitment via the SDF-1/CXCR4 signaling pathway. It provides further support to the clinical application of this technology in the community. This research project has also provided financial support to one PhD student (graduated in 2013).

462811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
462811.value: During the research project, it was also discovered by our research group that the expression level of estrogen receptor was also distinctive between normal and osteoporotic bone, thus characterizing the difference of fracture repair process between normal and osteoporotic fractures. As estrogen receptors are also responsible for mechanical signal transduction, a new research proposal that is extended from this current project has been funded by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC) in the year of 2014 (Ref: 81472097). Further research will be carried out to investigate the mechanism of LMHFV action in enhancing fracture healing, in both normal and osteoporotic fracture healing.

462811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
462811.value: In this study, we hypothesized that mesenchymal stem cell recruitment would be enhanced by low magnitude high frequency vibration (LMHFV), and the enhancement effect was due to the SDF-1/CXCR4 signaling pathway. Our results have demonstrated that LMHFV is effective in enhancing fracture healing through enhancing the recruitment of MSC to the fracture site by increasing the intravenously-injected MSC and the size of the fracture callus. By the data of antagonizing the CXCR4 with AMD-3100, it was confirmed that the enhancement effect by LMHFV was transmitted via the SDF-1/CXCR4 signaling pathway in both normal and osteoporotic bones. Therefore, the results of this study supported the clinical application of the captioned LMHFV intervention in both normal and osteoporotic fractures to ultimately achieve the acceleration of healing. Moreover, this study has led to an unanticipated discovery of the difference in estrogen receptors expression between normal and osteoporotic bones. This finding has initiated another research project in attempt to understand more on the pathology and potential therapeutic targets for treating osteoporotic fracture, which is related to importance of MSC recruitment during the fracture healing process.

463811.label: Major findings and research outcome
463811.value: We reported the first epidemiological study of nonsyndromic hearing loss in Chinese newborns indicating a notably high carrier frequency (one per 6.3 newborns) among these 15 mutant alleles ( Chen Y et al., Clin Genet. 2014). Considering the limited mutations screened by one method, we established the solution-based capture system with massively parallel sequencing to target more than two hundred genes related with hearing loss. In-house bioinfomatic analysis pipeline filtered candidate variants with high validation rate. Our designed Agilent Sureselect capture platform has been adopted for the mutation discovery of hearing loss genes in unrelated Chinese families with nonsyndromic hearing loss (Lu Y et al., J Hum Genet. In press). Based on our first 100 cases, our target enrichment MPS approach identified addition 28.6% unrelated Chinese families carrying novel mutations. Following increasing number of hearing loss patients get genetic diagnosis, one foreseeable growing demand is prenatal diagnosis for those hearing loss families. The standard prenatal testing needs invasive procedure to get fetal sample which has the risk of fetal loss. This is one of the biggest concerns from parents. Therefore in the last section of this thesis, we explore the application of noninvasive method on a family carrying GJB2 mutation. Using fetal haplotype analysis of the proximal and distal region of the GJB2 gene, we successfully deduced the fetal haplotype from the parental carrier alleles and exclude the paternal inheritance of the mutant allele. This non-invasive approach was further confirmed by the invasive testing in the second trimester. This work has been completed as being part of a PhD student thesis.

463811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
463811.value: To demonstrate the feasibility of the clinical application of a local designed targeted-enrichement next generation sequencing system as a comprehensive, robust genetic test for hereditary hearing loss; 2) To characterize the frequency of variants in local HL patients, establish a genotype-phenotype relationship database. Hypothesis to be tested: Hereditary hearing loss is unique compared to other hereditary diseases. In particular, a large number of genes are involved in hereditary hearing loss, which makes it very difficult to identify the genetic causes and pathological mechanism in clinical practice. We anticipate our established target enrichment massivley parallele sequencing method is more cost-effective and comprehensive and can be used as an alternative to Sanger sequencing or microarray in genetic diagnosis laboratories for detecting hereditary hearing loss. This study will also likely lead to the discovery of new mutations and sequence variants that define the genotype-phenotype relationship of hereditary hearing loss and helps local HL patients to make early genetics diagnosis. Design and subjects: This longitudinal study to recruit nonsyndromal hearing loss patient excluded with the common mutations of the four genes performed at clinical genetics service Department of Health and mircodeletion/microduplictaion syndrome by arrayCGH in our unit. Study instruments: A custom-deisgned targeted enrichment system and HiSeq massively parallel sequencer. Data analysis: Apply in-house designed bioinformatic pipeline to call pathogenic variants. Validated by Sanger sequencing. Interventions: Refer for Clinical genetic service for counselling and followup. Main outcome measures: Genetics diagnosis of hearing loss. Expected results:1)discover the candidate pathogenic variants for recruited patients; 2) demonstrate the clinical application of latest sequencing technology in clinical application .

463911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
463911.value: The treatment of Immunoglobin E (IgE) mediated food allergy remains a major enigmatic problem for patients and physicians. Shellfish allergy is one of the most common IgE mediated hypersensitive reactions which are often life-threatening. Our group has studied the immunology and molecular biology of shellfish allergy for over 15 years and was the first group to report the cloning, expression and identification of the major heat stable shrimp allergen. Recently, we have also succeeded in establishing a mouse model of shrimp allergy that resembles the clinical manifestations of human allergic responses to shrimp. In light of the lack of cure for shellfish allergies, we propose to apply cutting edge technologies of mimotope and gene therapy to develop DNA vaccines that will one day be used to prevent and cure shellfish allergies. Using shrimp allergy as a prototype, we will take advantage of our research experience and unique reagents and focus on shrimp tropomyosin, the major heat stable shrimp allergen. There are three main phases in this project. (1) We will define peptide mimotopes on shrimp tropomyosin using purified tropomyosin-specific IgE from shrimp allergic patients by one-bead-one-compound (OBOC) combinatorial peptide library method. The mimotopes will be characterized by comparing with the NMR structure of the known IgE epitopes of shrimp tropomyosin and determination of its binding specificities and affinities. Mimotopes that possess the highest IgE binding to shrimp tropomyosin will be chosen for mimotope vaccine design. (2) We will construct plasmids encoding the shrimp tropomyosin mimotopes and verify the mimotope expression in mammalian cells. (3) We will then determine the therapeutic efficacy of the mimotope-based DNA vaccines using our mouse model of shrimp tropomyosin hypersensitivity. 463911.label: Realisation of objectives
463911.value: Objective 1: We have successfully identified 25 mimotopes of shrimp tropomyosin Met e 1 by screening OBOC peptide libraries with human Met e 1-specific IgE. We were able to demonstrate that these mimotopes were specific to different immunodominant epitopes on Met e 1 by epitope mapping. The binding specificities of the mimotopes were validated by peptide ELISA. These mimotopes were potential therapeutic candidates for allergen-specific immunotherapy as they have the capacity to induce Met e 1 specific antibodies upon immunization in BALB/c mice. We believe mimotopes obtained by IgG antibodies are less clinically relevant, and the extensive time required to produce and characterize Met e 1-specific monoclonal antibodies is beyond the scope of this three-year project. We thus focused on the potential application of mimotopes identified by IgE antibodies. Objective 2: Based on the mimotopes identified, we constructed several mimotope-based DNA vaccines with different strategies to enhance the immunogenicity. However, it is much more difficult to induce antibodies using DNA vaccines than we anticipated, especially when a peptide antigen was used. In view of this, we have switched to design a therapeutic treatment by conjugating the mimotopes to an immunogenic carrier keyhole limpet hemocyanin (KLH). Using part of the funding, we have also constructed DNA vaccines encoding hypoallergenic derivatives of Met e 1 and investigated their prophylactic and therapeutic potential. Objective 3: We have developed a mouse model of Met e 1 mediated hypersensitivity using cholera toxin as an adjuvant, and the gastrointestinal immune responses of the mice were well characterized. Sucralfate and alum adjuvants could not raise high level of specific IgE and relevant clinical symptoms in mice while mouse model with cholera toxin could best simulate the clinical symptoms in human. We therefore selected this model to evaluate our vaccine constructs. The optimization of formulation and delivery of mimotope-KLH vaccines would be a lengthy process. Such investigations are on-going but beyond the scope of this three-year project.

463911.label: Major findings and research outcome
463911.value: We identified 25 mimotopes of Met e 1 by screening OBOC peptide libraries. The validity and specificity of mimotopes were confirmed by in vitro, in vivo and in silico analysis. This is a pioneer study demonstrating the use of whole serum from patients with allergy to obtain specific mimotopes using a novel OBOC library approach. These findings were presented in the EAACI Congress. A paper has been published online in Cellular and Molecular Immunology (Leung et al., 2015). We have developed a novel BALB/c mouse model of shrimp hypersensitivity and the histological and immunological changes in the gastrointestinal tract of the mouse to tropomyosin were characterized. This model provides an important tool for testing therapeutic interventions. These findings were presented in the EAACI Congress and published in 2015 (Lam et al., 2015). We have constructed DNA vaccines encoding mimotopes but fail to elicit a strong antibody response. We therefore turned to an alternative approach by delivering mimotopes conjugated to KLH as therapeutic treatment. It was found that treated mice have increased IgG1 antibody level and reduced splenocyte proliferation. However, clinical symptoms such as mast cell infiltration did not improve. These findings were presented in the World Allergy Congress held in Seoul, 2015. We have developed hypoallergen DNA vaccines as an alternative gene therapy approach. Two hypoallergens MEM49 and MED171 were constructed by introducing point mutations to IgE-binding epitopes and by deleting all the epitopes, respectively. These findings were presented in the APCAACI and published (Wai et al., 2014). Delivery of these hypoallergens in the form of DNA vaccines could effectively prevent the onset of shrimp allergy and alleviate shrimp allergy responses through the induction of IgG2a blocking antibodies and regulatory T cell responses. We have also identified T cell epitopes of Met e 1, where oral delivery of these T cell peptides also shows a therapeutic effect towards shrimp hypersensitivity in BALB/c mice. These findings were presented in the EAACI Congress and a manuscript has been submitted to Clinical and Experimental Allergy and currently under revision. Our team was invited to contribute review papers on the development of immunotherapy (Wai et al., 2012) and seafood allergy (Leung et al., 2014), respectively. A third invited review for Clinical Reviews in Allergy & Immunology on the different strategies of immunotherapy for food allergies is in preparation. Our team was also invited to present our work on different immunotherapy strategies in the World Aquaculture Society meeting held in Jeju, Korea, 2015.

463911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
463911.value: Although the mimotope treatment did not completely ameliorate the ongoing clinical symptoms in our mouse model of shrimp hypersensitivity, we believe the mimotopes could be of potential clinical interest and we look to further explore different conjugation and delivery schemes to optimize their therapeutic effect. Our study using the OBOC approach shed many insights on the advantage of OBOC libraries compared to the conventional phage-displayed libraries. The OBOC approach could lead to a revolutionary approach in allergen-specific immunotherapy by tailor-making the best treatment based on the patients’ sensitization profile. Mimotopes could also be developed into diagnostic tool for allergic diseases and detailed characterization of the allergens. We demonstrated therapeutic potential of the DNA vaccines of hypoallergens MED171 and MEM49 for the treatment of seafood allergy using the BALB/c mouse model. We are prepared to elucidate the detailed immunological mechanism behind the therapeutic effects of the hypoallergens. This project is currently supported by a grant from the Human Medical Research Fund, HKSAR.

463911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
463911.value: We explored the use of OBOC peptide library to identify mimotopes of the major shrimp allergen tropomyosin. The specificity and validity of the mimotopes were confirmed by both computational analysis and animal studies. Although our preliminary study to investigate the therapeutic effect of mimotopes resulted in conflicting results, we believe allergen-specific mimotopes could still be of interest in multiple applications. This use of OBOC approach in our study also highlights several advantages compared to the conventional phage-displayed libraries and sheds many insights over the potential application of allergen-specific mimotopes in the diagnosis and treatment of allergic diseases. We have also designed two hypoallergenic proteins of shrimp tropomyosin and constructed two hypoallergen DNA vaccines. Using a mouse model of shrimp allergy, these two vaccines are shown to be effective in preventing the development of shrimp allergy and also in treating the already-established allergic responses to shrimp.

464411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
464411.value: Stem cells hold great potential in healing tissue damage and degenerative diseases. But their application is impeded by limited donor cell sources. Successful reprogramming of somatic cells into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) by overexpression of embryonic stem cell (ESC) master factors OCT4, SOX2, KLF4 and c-MYC is a significant breakthrough. It has opened the possibility of custom-tailored regenerative medicine whereby patient-specific pluripotent cells can be derived from adult somatic cells and used as a renewable source for cell-based therapy. However, the clinical applications of human iPSCs have been hindered by the shortcomings of the current reprogramming methodologies, especially the inefficiency and permanent genomic alterations introduced by using the virus-mediated gene delivery approach. To overcome these limitations, screening for factors that can trigger rapid, efficient and safe reprogramming is highly demanded. In this study, we aim to perform a systematic screening to identify novel factors that can promote the reprogramming of human somatic cells, for the purpose of improving efficiency and generating human iPSCs in a shorter course of time. Candidate factors will be shortlisted according to their importance in the maintenance of ESCs as well as their pluripotency-associated expression. Relevant information will be extracted from our recent genome-wide RNAi screening and microarray datasets. Similar to our previous work in identifying new factors that contributed to reprogramming of mouse fibroblasts, we will use a retrovirus system to introduce the transgene expression in human somatic cells. The reprogramming potential of candidate factors will be examined and their effect will be quantified by the formation of iPSC colonies. The resulting iPSCs will then be validated from the aspect of their expression profile, epigenetic status and differentiation capacity by comparing to human ESCs. The most efficient candidates will be further investigated for their functional roles in controlling pluripotency, using, for example, the genome-wide location analysis approach. The discoveries made in this study are expected to identify novel reprogramming factors and establish new cocktails that can reprogram human somatic cells more efficiently and rapidly. The new reprogramming cocktails can then be combined with a DNA free approach (such as transient transfection of recombinant proteins), leading to a faster and safer methodology for generating human iPSCs for clinical applications. This research has tremendous potential to generate patents which can then be developed into commercially relevant applications. We expect that our work will contribute substantially to the scientific community in Hong Kong. 干细胞在组织损伤和退化性疾病的治疗方面具有很大的潜力，但是由于其来源有限，有关的应用和研究都受到很大的限制。导入外源基因使人类体细胞成功重编程（reprogramming）而转变成诱导性多能干细胞（induced pluripotent stem cells, iPS cells）的研究是一项重大的突破。 这使得制备病人特异性的多能干细胞成为可能， 并可由此进一步制备各种其它临床所需的细胞。然而，目前报道的iPS细胞诱导方法普遍存在着效率低和致癌风险高的问题。因此，为进一步克服这些障碍， 筛选新的可高效,安全诱导iPS细胞的遗传因子成为当务之急。 本课题拟对与干细胞多能性密切相关的候选因子进行系统的筛查， 以鉴定新的， 可高效诱导人类iPS细胞的遗传因子。 在前期工作中，课题组成员通过染色质免疫共沉淀及高通量测序研究技术构建了多个重编程因子的基因组结合位点图谱，并进行了人类胚胎干细胞（embryonic stem cells）基因组水平上的RNA干扰实验及基因表达芯片分析实验。以此为基础,本课题拟通过进一步的生物信息学分析,从前期工作建立的数据库中选取与干细胞多能性密切相关的候选因子，并以人类iPS细胞诱导实验为分析手段检测其功能，以筛选鉴定新的、可高效诱导iPS细胞的重编程因子。同时， 我们还将在分子学特征和细胞功能水平比较该种iPS细胞与人类胚胎干细胞的异同，以最终揭示新因子诱导重编程的作用机制。 本项目的研究将发现新的重编程诱导因子，确立新的重编程基因组合。这将有可能与非DNA介导的基因表达技术相结合，建立新的、更安全的、诱导人类iPS细胞的方法，并进一步拓展对重编程诱导机制的深入探究。本课题具备获得专利的潜力，并将推动干细胞技术的发展。

464411.label: Realisation of objectives
464411.value: Successful reprogramming of somatic cells into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) has opened unprecedented potential for custom-tailored regenerative medicine. However, clinical applications of human iPSCs have been hindered by the shortcomings of current reprogramming methodologies, especially the inefficiency. To overcome these limitations, discovery of new factors that can trigger more efficient reprogramming, and further depicting the underlying molecular mechanism are of high interest. In this study, we aim to perform a screening to identify novel factors that can promote the reprogramming of human somatic cells, for the purpose of improving efficiency and generating human iPSCs with higher efficiency. According to the proposed research plan, we have shortlisted 35 candidate factors according to their importance in the maintenance of embryonic stem cells (ESCs) as well as their pluripotency-associated expression, cloned their cDNAs into the pMX retroviral vector to introduce the ectopic expression in human somatic cells, and analyzed their potentials in promoting iPSC generation using the retrovirus-mediated reprogramming assays. Furthermore, the effective factors have been analyzed in various combinations for their combinatorial effect, and obtained iPSCs have been examined for the expressions of key pluripotency marker genes using qRT-PCR and immunofluorescence analysis. Collectively, these works have counted complete realization of the proposed Objectives. The obtained data are valuable for further improving the efficiency of iPSC generation as well as for depicting the molecular regulations that control the epigenetic reprogramming. Within the scope of this project, we have also performed gene expression analysis during stepwise neural induction from pluripotent ESCs, and identified a group of genes that underwent rapid up- or down-regulation upon initiation of differentiation and further neural commitment (Tsang et al., Stem Cell Res, 2013). This data have provided valuable information for identification of new factors that play critical function in controlling pluripotency. Furthermore, we have explored the potential of engineered transcription factors (TALE and CRISPR/Cas9 activators) in directly activating the master pluripotency gene Oct4, which is strictly silenced in somatic cells. We found that the most efficient TALE-VP64s/sgRNAs targeted a proximal region in Oct4 promoter. The optimized combinations of TALE-VP64s could enhance endogenous Oct4 transcription up to 30-fold in mouse cells and 20-fold in human cells. Moreover, the enhancement of OCT4 transcription ultimately generated OCT4 proteins, suggesting the established technical platform is valuable for further improving the epigenetic reprogramming (Hu et al. Nucl Acids Res, 2014).

464411.value: With the data obtained in these works, we have identified a group of genes that underwent rapid down-regulation upon the ESC differentiation and played important roles in iPSC generation. These genes are also likely important for pluripotency maintenance. Hence, we will move forward to perform the loss-of-function analysis on these genes in ESCs, using shRNA mediated gene silencing approach; and further elaborate the relationships between selected factors via simultaneously knocking-down two genes, or combining knock-down of one gene with overexpression of another gene. This will uncover the molecular regulations which interconnect within the network to support the property of cellular pluripotency. The established CRISPR/Cas9 system is also a powerful tool for gene targeting. With this technology, we have set up a technical platform for conducting efficient gene targeting in human ESCs/iPSCs, which was very inefficient and difficult previously. Next, we will further employ this new tool to study the newly identified factors and elaborate their functions in ESC maintenance, iPSC generation, as well as their differentiation.

464411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
464411.value: Generation of induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) from patients’ somatic cells has opened unprecedented potential for custom-tailored regenerative medicine. However, the low efficiency of current methodology has hindered the applications of human iPSCs. Hence, we proposed to identify new factors that could further promote iPSC generation and thus improve the efficiency. In this project, we have selected 35 candidate factors which are highly expressed in pluripotent stem cells, and examined their potential in generation of iPSCs, either on their own or in a combination with previously identified reprogramming factors. The obtained iPSCs have been expanded and the expressions of key stem cell marker genes have been assessed using various assays. In addition, we have extended our study by carrying out gene expression analysis during early differentiation of pluripotent stem cells as well as by exploring the potential of engineered transcription factors in directly activating the master pluripotency gene Oct4. Collectively, these studies have produced data valuable for understanding the molecular mechanisms that control the stemness, as well as for further improving the efficiency of iPSC generation. With this funding support, we have completed the proposed objectives, published two research articles (Tsang et al., Stem Cell Res, 2013; Hu et al. Nucl Acids Res, 2014), and trained one PhD student.

465111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
465111.value: In this study, we wish to further investigate the relationship between endothelial function, tissue oxygenation, marrow perfusion and osteoporosis in a clinical setting. Osteoporosis management is currently hampered by several limitations: (1) reliance on bone densitometry means that osteoporosis can only be diagnosed after it has become established and the bone is, in many respects, irreparably damaged; (ii) we have a limited ability to predict who will develop osteoporosis; (iii) there is a paucity of sustainable treatment options. These limitations prevent us from fully understanding the pathogenesis of osteoporosis. Over the past two decades, a link between arterial disease and osteoporosis has been established. One of the earliest manifestations of arterial vascular disease is endothelial dysfunction. Endothelial dysfunction results in impaired release of endothelial nitric oxide (NO) which in turn impedes vascular reactivity and the anabolic effect of NO on downstream bone. Impaired vascular reactivity may decrease marrow perfusion, thereby increasing oxidative stress within the marrow and shifting mesenchymal stem cell differentiation away from osteoblastogenesis and haematopoesis towards adipogenesis. Our MR-based clinical studies on the lumbar spine and proximal femur have shown how bone perfusion is reduced in osteoporosis. We subsequently conducted animal-based studies which showed that the two most likely causes of this reduced perfusion are (i) impaired endothelial function and (ii) a decrease in the amount of functioning marrow present in osteoporotic bone. This latter study was the first to show that abrupt sex hormone deficiency leads to a reduction in the amount of functioning marrow and impairment of endothelial function. In the present study, we intend to further investigate the relationship between endothelial function, tissue oxygenation, marrow perfusion and osteoporosis in a clinical setting. We will measure endothelial function using the traditional method of brachial arterial dilation. We will employ a new MR technique known as BOLD (Blood Oxygenation Level Dependent) imaging to assess the re-oxygenation of the bone and muscle following transient ischaemia. Our pilot studies have shown that BOLD imaging can routinely measure marrow re-oxygenation. If we can establish a link between endothelial function, tissue oxygenation and osteoporosis, we may be able to develop a unifying, coherent theory that satisfactorily explains the known clinical risk factors for osteoporosis. The results of this study may also allow the osteoporotic process to be recognised earlier, improve our ability to identify individuals likely to develop osteoporosis, and increase the possibility of treating osteoporosis with a nitric oxide donor.

465111.label: Realisation of objectives
465111.value: The primary objective has been fully investigated and achieved by carrying out a series of clinical experiments and data analysis. One hundred and forty-four elderly female subjects were recruited for the study. Raw data were obtained by different imaging modalities, such as ultrasound, MRI, and qCT. Quantitative parameters were extracted from the raw data to assess the endothelial function, tissue oxygenation, marrow perfusion and bone mineral density. The most challenging part of the study was the BOLD imaging at the calf location. BOLD signal from MRI can reflect tissue oxygenation level and was employed in the current study to evaluate the marrow and surrounding muscle’s oxygenation. The experimental design used an air-cuff to induce ischemia and assess tissue re-perfusion. However, susprisingly we found that the air pressure induced susceptibility changes, which influenced the imaging quality and affected the MR signal from the tissues under investigation. We designed and conducted several experiments to stabilize the imaging quality and finally found a special air-cuff device to overcome the problem. Although a lot of effort has been put on BOLD imaging, the BOLD signal was still very weak at the bone marrow. Overall, we could not firmly establish a relationship between endothelial function, tissue oxygenation, marrow perfusion and osteoporosis. For the secondary objective of this study (iii), we have completed all the perfusion data collection and analysis. Because this objective is based on longitudinal study, we will further continue investigating these patients in our later research.

465111.label: Major findings and research outcome
465111.value: 1) Air-pressure induces susceptibility changes in vascular reactivity studies using BOLD MRI. This finding is published as a journal paper (Part C/8/No3). 2) A muscle-based pharmacokinetic model was established for bone marrow and applied to the clinical data. Subjects with osteoporosis have comparable muscle perfusion to subjects with normal BMD or osteopenia. The findings have been published as a journal paper and as a conference paper (Part C/8/No1, Part C/9/No5). 3) Bone has a strong interaction with surrounding muscle in that muscle strength is counter-balanced with bone strength. This muscle-bone balance is altered in the osteoporotic patient. Bone strength reduces to a greater degree than muscle strength. As a result, osteoporotic bone sustains a relatively higher strain per unit area as a result of muscle contraction compared to normal bone, which may result in insufficiency fracture. The finding has been published as a journal paper and several conference papers (Part C/8/No2 , Part C/9/No1&3&6). 4) Bone marrow fat content increases as with increasing age. However whilst marrow fat content is higher in young males up to the age of 50 years. Females undergo a dramatic increase in marrow fat around the time of the menopause such that the marrow fat content of females is higher than that of males. This has been published as a journal paper Part C/B/No4. 5) Muscle surrounding bone showed a higher oxygenation in subjects with normal bone mineral density when compared to those with lower bone mineral density. This result has been published in a conference paper (part C/9/No1&6). 6) Cancellous bone comprising marrow can sustain a higher strain cancellous bone without bone marrow. This finding was deduced from stimulation work based on bone structure from QCT data. The finding has been published in conference papers (PartC/9/No2 & 4).

465111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
465111.value: This study achieved several very interesting findings. First is that bone and muscle oxygenation changes in subjects with different bone mineral density. Further studies will help to confirm if this change in oxuygenation is related to haematopoetic cell volume changes within the bone marrow as this is know to decrease with decreasing bone mineral density. Secondly, we need to explore fuirther what predictive values these oxygenation changes have on the likelihood of subsequent changes in bone mineral density and fracture. This will rely on future extension of the current project. Thirdly, through simulation analysis, it was shown that bone amrrow can affect the stength of the cancellous bone component. This is a new finding which does require further investigation as to the relative strenght component of red and yellow marrow.

465111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
465111.value: As bone mass reduces, there is a corresponding reduction in bone perfusion and also, to a lesser degree, perfusion in the adjacent muscle. Every day we all sustain microfractures in our trabecular bone network and these microfractures heal without any clinical effect. Bone is dependent on good bone perfusion to heal these fractures. This reduction in bone perfusion seen in osteoporotic bone clearly has implications for trabecular microfracture healing which can lead to trabecular microdamage accumulation resulting finally in a clinically evident fracture. Muscle mass also reduces as bone mineral density decreases though to a comparatively less degree than bone mass. This increasing imbalance between the amount of muscle present and the amount of bone present puts relatively greater force on already weakened bone and thus increases the likelihood of subsequent fracture. Clearly when on considers osteoporosis one need to consider these aspects as well as a actual bone strength. Modern BOLD MR techniques can quantity muscle and bone oxygenation which may provide a non-invasive measure of tissue perfusion. The BOLD signal obtained from bone marrow at the moment however is weak.

465611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
465611.value: 二型糖尿病和肥胖嚴重威脅人體健康，許多糖尿病患者由於心血管及腎臟並發症而死亡，因此，深入了解與糖尿病相關的心血管功能失調的生理病理機制，以及尋找更為有效的治療方法和新藥尤為重要。近期研究結果提示內質網應激可能參與代謝綜合症及心血管疾病的發病過程，但是內質網應激與血管功能異常的關係仍不明確。 本研究內容包括：（一）內質網應激在糖尿病血管功能異常中是否起關鍵作用；（二）骨形成蛋白4(BMP4)是否與內皮細胞內質網應激緊密相關；（三）運動訓練是否通過激活核受體(PPARδ)，抑制內質網應激而改善血管舒張功能。這些研究有助於了解糖尿病血管並發症的病理基礎及尋找新的治療方法。

465611.label: Realisation of objectives
465611.value: The primary aim of this project was to understand whether endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress plays an important role in maintenance of endothelial dysfunction in diabetes and obesity. We have clearly demonstrated that ER stress is one of key mediators of endothelial cell dysfunction in diabetic mice. ER stress induction impairs endothelium-dependent nitric oxide-mediated relaxation in mouse aortas via increased production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in the vascular wall and high-fat-diet-induced obesity elevated the expression of ER stress marker proteins, increased ROS accumulation and attenuated endothelium-dependent relaxations in mouse aortas. We have for the first time demonstrated that metformin, a popular anti-diabetic drug reduces ER stress to rescue endothelial function in diabetic and obese mice and this benefit is mediated through activation of AMPK-PPARδ pathway. This novel finding was published in Arteriosclerosis, Thrombosis and Vascular Biology (2014;34(4):830-836). Thus, ER stress could be a useful target for drug intervention. We have recently shown that angiotensin 1-7 protects against angiotensin II-induced ER stress and endothelial dysfunction in mice (PLoS One, 2015, accepted). We also studied how bone morphogenic protein 4 (BMP4) impairs endothelial function and found that BMP4 increases ER stress in vascular tissues. More recently, we showed that BMP4 stimulates production and release of PDGFAA in endothelial cells and PDGFAA contributes to BMP4-induced endothelial dysfunction. The new findings were submitted to Arteriosclerosis, Thrombosis and Vascular Biology and now are resubmitted after a minor revision. Physical activity benefits health. Experiments on rodents with trained exercise showed exercise improves vascular function and reduces vascular inflammation. We have demonstrated that exercise training preserves endothelial function in diabetic and obese mice through inhibiting ER stress via activation of PPARδ. We showed that PPARδ is a crucial mediator for exercise to exert beneficial effect on vascular endothelium in diabetic mice. In db/db diabetic mice and high-fat-diet-induced obese mice, four weeks treadmill exercise restores endothelium-dependent and flow-mediated vasodilation in arteries; whereas genetic ablation of Ppard abolished such improvements. Exercise induces AMPK activation and subsequent PPARδ activation that helps to reduce ER stress and oxidative stress thus to increase NO bioavailability in endothelial cells. 4-Phenyl butyric acid and tauroursodeoxycholic acid decreases ER stress and protects against endothelial dysfunction in diabetic mice. Our results demonstrate that PPARδ-mediated inhibition of ER stress contributes to the vascular benefits of exercise and provide potentially effective targets for treating diabetic vasculopathy. The new results were submitted to Diabetes for consideration of publication.

465611.label: Major findings and research outcome
465611.value: 1. We have elucidated an important pathological role of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress in the maintenance of endothelial cell dysfunction in diabetic and obese mice. 2. We have demonstrated that metformin, the most commonly used drug to treat patients with diabetes can restore the impaired endothelial function in diabetic mice through inhibiting vascular ER stress and this beneficial effect is most likely mediated through activation of PPARdelta, the latter could become a useful target for drug intervention against diabetic vasculopathy. 3. We also show that angiotensin 1-7, a peptide from the beneficial arm of the renin-angiotensin system benefits endothelial function against angiotensin II challenge through suppressing ER stress in mouse arteries. 4. We have shown that BMP4, a pro-inflammatory molecule impairs endothelial function via stimulating production of platelet-derived growth factors through activation of Smad4-dependent pathway 5. We have demonstrated that exercise training preserves endothelial function in diabetic and obese mice through inhibiting ER stress via activation of PPARδ. We showed that PPARδ is a crucial mediator for exercise to exert beneficial effect on vascular endothelium in diabetic mice. In db/db mice and high fat diet-induced obese mice, four weeks treadmill exercise restores endothelium-dependent relaxations and flow-mediated dilation in arteries; whereas genetic ablation of Ppard abolished such improvements. Exercise induces AMPK activation and subsequent PPARδ activation that helps to reduce ER stress and oxidative stress to increases nitric oxide bioavailability in endothelial cells. Our results demonstrate that PPARδ-mediated inhibition of ER stress contributes to the vascular benefits of exercise and we provide potentially effective targets for treating diabetic vasculopathy.

465611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
465611.value: ER stress is one of key mediators of endothelial dysfunction in associate with increased vascular oxidative stress in diabetes and obesity. The results of our animal studies clearly demonstrate that ER stress is a potential target for drug intervention to relieve diabetic vasculopathy. We are planning to screen whether other existing anti-diabetic or blood pressure-lowering drugs can also protect vascular function via inhibiting ER stress in endothelial cells to restore nitric oxide bioavailability and in the vascular smooth muscle cells to reduce adverse vascular remodeling usually occurring in cardio-metabolic diseases. Besides, our study also highlights the potential importance of PPARdelta activation in limiting ER stress in the inflamed blood vessels in diabetes, obesity and hypertension. We also wish to extend the current study to examine whether mechanical stimulation or laminar shear stress can reduce ER stress as another new cellular mechanism for vaso-protection against obesity and diabetes.

465611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
465611.value: Many diabetic patients die of cardiovascular and renal complications which are commonly resulted from progression of vascular pathogenesis after initial occurring of abnormal function of vascular endothelium (called endothelial dysfunction), a single layer of cells covering the lumen of blood vessels. Endothelial dysfunction is reflected by diminished production and release of vaso-protective substances, such as nitric oxide and prostacyclin in endothelial cells while increased production of free radicals in blood vessels is a major contributor to inactivation of nitric oxide. Endoplasmic reticulum is an important intracellular organelle while malfunction of endoplasmic reticulum can cause exaggerated production of free radicals to impair normal cellular function. Our study has demonstrated that endoplasmic reticulum stress is an important player of endothelial dysfunction in diabetic and obese mice. Targeting endoplasmic reticulum stress is effective to preserve endothelial function and limit vascular oxidative stress in diabetic mice. Several drugs and chemicals such as metformin (commonly used anti-diabetic drug) protect vascular function through inhibiting endoplasmic reticulum stress, thus maintaining nitric oxide bioavailability. It is possible that some other clinical drugs may also inhibit endoplasmic reticulum stress to benefit vascular function in cardio-metobolic diseases.

466011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
466011.value: Protein targeting and protein turnover are fundamental biological processes essential for biological functions in living organisms. In yeast and mammals, many plasma membrane (PM) proteins are ubiquitinated and targeted to vacuole or lysosome for degradation via multivesicular endosomes. However, little is known about the molecular mechanisms by which PM proteins are internalized via the endocytic pathway or membrane proteins are targeted via the secretory pathway for vacuolar turnover in plant cells. We have previously showed that the rice Secretory Carrier Membrane Protein 1 (SCAMP1) with four transmembrane domains (TMDs) is localized in both PM and trans-Golgi network (TGN), whereas the Arabidopsis endomembrane 70kDa Protein 12 (AtEMP12) with nine TMDs is localized in Golgi apparatus in plant cells. Our recent studies demonstrate that SCAMP1 is internalized from the PM to vacuole, while C-terminus mutation causes the Golgi-localized AtEMP12 to reach vacuole for degradation. Therefore, the central objective of this proposal is to use SCAMP1 and AtEMP12 as tools to study the molecular mechanisms by which PM-localized or Golgi-localized polytopic membrane proteins are targeted to vacuoles for degradation in plants. First, we will establish a transient expression system for protein turnover study; Second, using SCAMP1 and AtEMP12 as probes, we will test the hypothesis that the same prevacuolar compartment (PVC) or late endosome mediates the vacuolar degradation of polytopic membrane proteins for both endocytic and secretory pathways. Third, via loss-of-function and gain-of-function approaches, we will study the internalization mechanisms of SCAMP1 from PM and identify the targeting signals in AtEMP12 for Golgi to vacuole traffic; Fourth, using co-immunoprecipitation with antibodies and subsequent protein identification via LC-MS/MS analysis, we will purify and identify protein(s) regulating Golgi retention/export of AtEMP12; Last, we will use both transgenic Arabidopsis cells and plants to verify the major findings from transient expression and to study the function of newly identified regulatory protein(s). Our long-term goal is to use SCAMP1 and AtEMP12 proteins as probes to elucidate the molecular mechanisms of PVC-mediated vacuolar turnover of polytopic membrane proteins in the plant endomembrane systems. 蛋白的靶定和降解是基本的生物学过程，对于生物体正常的生理功能是必须的。在酵母和哺乳动物细胞中，许多细胞质膜蛋白被泛素化，并经过多囊泡内体被导向液泡或溶酶体来降解。然而，在植物细胞中，细胞质膜蛋白经过内吞途径进入细胞，或者膜蛋白经过分泌途径而导向液泡进行降解的分子机理却知之甚少。我们以前的研究表明，在植物细胞中，具有四个跨膜区的水稻膜蛋白（SCAMP1）定位在细胞质膜和反式高尔基体网络，而具有九个跨膜区，分子量为70ka的拟南芥内膜蛋白（AtEMP12）定位于高尔基体。我们近来的研究表明，SCAMP1从细胞质膜被内吞入细胞并到达液泡降解，而AtEMP12蛋白C末端的突变导致原定位于高尔基体的AtEMP12也到达液泡降解。因此，本研究计划的中心目标是，以SCAMP1和AtEMP12为工具，研究植物细胞中，定位于细胞质膜或高尔基体的多跨膜区膜蛋白被靶向液泡降解的分子机理。首先，我们将建立一个研究蛋白降解的瞬时表达体系；第二，以SCAMP1和AtEMP12为探针，我们将检测研究假设：同一种液泡前体或晚期内体介导内吞途径和分泌途径多跨膜区膜蛋白的液泡降解；第三，通过功能缺失和功能获得的方法，我们将研究SCAMP1从细胞质膜内吞入细胞的机理，以及识别AtEMP12的高尔基体滞留信号，并研究其从高尔基体到液泡的运输；第四，通过使用抗体免疫共沉淀，以及随后通过LC-MS/MS分析而进行的蛋白鉴定，我们将纯化和识别调节AtEMP12高尔基体滞留或输出的蛋白；最后，我们将使用转基因拟南芥细胞和植物来验证从瞬时表达体系取得的主要研究发现，并研究新识别的调节蛋白的功能。我们长期的目标是使用SCAMP1和AtEMP12蛋白为探针，阐明液泡前体介导的植物内膜系统中多跨膜区膜蛋白液泡降解的分子机理。

466011.label: Realisation of objectives
466011.value: We have achieved all the original research objectives and goals of this project successfully. Using the newly established transient expression system, we have demonstrated that the same PVC mediated protein turnover in endocytic and secretory pathways. We have also identified novel Golgi retention signal and its COPI-internating component of the Arabidopsis AtEMP12. Most of the important findings have also been verified and confirmed in transgenic Arabidopsis plants. In addition, we have also trained several graduate students with very good publication record.

466011.label: Major findings and research outcome
466011.value: 1) We have developed a transient expression protocol using the protoplasts derived from tobacco BY2 or the Arabidopsis suspension cells. This protocol relies on the transformation of DNA constructs into protoplasts via electroporation and can be used to quickly study protein turnover with confocal microscopy and immunoblot analysis. 2) Using the polytopic membrane proteins AtLRR84A and OsSCAMP1 as cargoes in endocytic pathway and the integral membrane protein EMP12 as a cargo in the secretory pathway, we have demonstrated that the same prevacuolar compartment (PVC) or multivesicular body (MVB) mediated the vacuolar degradation of the above three membrane proteins. Thus, we have proved that the same PVC mediates the vacuolar degradation of polytopic membrane proteins from both endocytic and secretory pathways in plants. 3) We have demonstrated that the vacuolar targeting of polytopic membrane proteins including AtLRR84A, OsSCAMP1 and EMP12 was achieved by the internal vesicles of MVB/PVC, which can be enlarged by wortmannin treatment or expression of ARA7(Q69L). 4) We have demonstrated that SCAMP1 undergoes a cargo ubiquitination-independent and prevacuolar compartment (PVC)-mediated internalization mechanism to vacuole for degradation. 5) We have identified a novel lysine based KXD/E motif, which locates in the C terminal cytosolic tail of EMP12 and functions as a Golgi retention signal to maintain the Golgi localization of EMP12 in plants. 6) Using the synthetic peptides corresponding to the C terminal cytosolic tail of EMP12 as bait to do pull-down assay, we have identified the COPI coatomers as binding partners of KXD/E motif to regulate the Golgi retention of EMP12 in plants. 7) Via studying a plant unique FYVE domain protein called FREE1, we have demonstrated the its roles in mediating the internalization of membrane proteins into MVBs for further vacuolar degradation in plants. 8) Taken together, we have achieved all the original objectives and goals of this project successfully. 9) With partially support from this project, we have also trained several very good postgraduate students with excellent research outputs as demonstrated by publications of their thesis work in international journals. 10) This project has resulted in very good publications in international journals including Plant Cell, Traffic, Journal of Experimental Botany, Plant Journal, Molecular Plant, and Trends in Plant Science.

466011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
466011.value: 1) Different organelles in a cell contain different lipids compositions and integral membrane protein, which maintain the organelle integrity and functional specificity. Thus the findings and publications about the targeting and degradation mechanisms of membrane proteins from this project have served as the basic foundation for future study of protein turnover and organelle biogenesis in plant cells. 2) Based on our findings, we will develop further into understanding the underlying mechanisms of the conserved Golgi retention mechanism for endomembrane proteins among different organisms including plant, mammal and yeast in the future. 3) This new research of membrane protein targeting and degradation and its potential usefulness in understanding Golgi function and biogenesis can be further enhanced and promoted via international collaboration with leaders in both yeast and animal fields. 4) The sorting signals identified in EMP12 and SCAMP1 will be helpful to understand the physiological functions of these two integral membrane proteins in plants in future studies.

466011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
466011.value: This RGC-funded project aims to study the targeting, retention and degradation mechanisms of two integral membranes EMP12 and SCAMP1 in plant cell using a combination of cellular, biochemical and molecular approaches. Results derived from this study have provided new insights about the molecular machinery in regulating membrane protein trafficking and degradation in plants, with potential implications in future study of organelle biogenesis and function in eukaryotes.

466111.label: Project Objectives
466111.value: Aim 1: To determine the role of CFTR in regulating the progression and EMT of breast cancer cells in vitro. Breast cancer cell lines MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231, which represent the luminal (good prognosis) and basal triple negative (poor prognosis) types of breast cancer cell lines separately, will be used to study the biological functions of CFTR in breast cancer progression and EMT. 1.1: To establish stable cell lines overexpressing CFTR or expressing shRNA targeting CFTR. 1.2: To evaluate the role of CFTR in breast cancer progression/EMT in vitro. Aim 2: To assess the role of CFTR in breast cancer metastasis in vivo. Aim 4: To evaluate the prognostic significance of TWIST1 and CFTR expression in breast cancer patients

466111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
466111.value: 乳腺癌是女性最常見的癌症, 也是發生在女性的第二大癌症死亡原因。乳腺癌患者死亡的主要原因是乳腺癌的轉移，然而目前我们对這個過程仍知之甚少。上皮间充质轉移（EMT）是在肿瘤轉移表型中获得的重要却又可逆的步驟，因此，提高認識EMT对获得肿瘤新的生物標誌物或新的分子靶點均具有重要意义。囊性纖維化跨膜電導調節器（CFTR）是一個受cAMP調控的陰離子通道， 它的突變導致囊性纖維化（CF）。CF是常見的常染色體隱性遺傳疾病，具有廣泛的嚴重程度和表現形式。雖然国外有研究组发现CF病人和CFTR基因突變携带者具有较高的患癌風險， 我们对CFTR在癌症發展中的生物作用仍然一无所知。 最近，我們的實驗室发现，抑制CFTR可以促進乳腺癌的進展。此外，我們發現，抑制CFTR功能本身可以誘導乳腺癌細胞发生EMT，而过表達CFTR可以下調EMT相關的各種基因，包括TWIST1。因此，我們推測，CFTR通過調節 EMT過程， 在乳腺癌進展 /轉移中起著重要作用。 CFTR的功能缺失或下调可能驅動一組具较强侵略性和轉移性的乳腺癌。我们的研究内容包括：1： CFTR在乳腺癌細胞发生EMT及转移中的作用；2：體內进一步研究CFTR在乳腺癌轉移中的作用； 3 ：為了闡明CFTR調節乳腺癌EMT的分子基礎，我們會研究CFTR是否通過調節 NF -B/TWIST1/E-cadherin信號通路的方式，抑制乳腺癌的發展； 4：評價TWIST1和CFTR的表達在乳腺癌患者中預後意義。 本研究將有望揭示CFTR調節乳腺癌EMT和轉移的作用机制。此外，研究可能有助于乳腺癌的诊治， 将为其提供更好的診斷，更準確的預測預後不良的可能性和開拓新療法。

466111.label: Major findings and research outcome
466111.value: We have found that interfering with CFTR function either by its specific inhibitor or lentiviral miRNA-mediated knockdown mimics TGF-β1-induced EMT and enhances cell migration and invasion in MCF-7. Ectopic overexpression of CFTR in a highly metastatic MDA-231 breast cancer cell line downregulates EMT markers and suppresses cell invasion and migration in vitro, as well as metastasis in vivo. The EMT-suppressing effect of CFTR is found to be associated with its ability to inhibit NFkB targeting urokinase-type plasminogen activator (uPA), known to be involved in regulation of EMT. More importantly, CFTR expression is found significantly downregulated in primary human breast cancer samples, and closely associated with poor prognosis in different cohorts of breast cancer patients. Taken together, the present study has demonstrated a previously undefined role of CFTR as an EMT suppressor and its potential as a prognostic indicator in breast cancer. (Zhang JT et al., BBA, 2013). On the other hand, loss of one of the key components of adherens junctions, E-cadherin, often occurs in later stages of tumorigenesis and contributes to EMT, which represents a crucial step in metastasis. In our study, we have clearly demonstrated that suppression of CFTR function leads to loss of E-cadherin whereas overexpression of CFTR results in upregulation of E-cadherin. Thus, we investigated whether CFTR could regulate other adherens junction complex in cancer. Interestingly, we have found that CFTR physically interacts with AF/6/afadin and plays critical role in colon cancer metastasis. (Sun TT et al., BBA 2013).

466111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
466111.value: Given that CFTR is extensively expressed in the epithelial cells of a wide variety of tissues and organs and hypomethylation of CFTR has been reported in various cancer, it is plausible that downregulation of CFTR promotes the development and progression of various cancers of epithelial origin. Our findings that CFTR regulates cancer progression and its expression inversely correlated with cancer progression warrant future investigations into CFTR methylation or mutation in cancer patients, which are likely to provide attractive and novel targets for prognosis and therapeutic intervention of different cancers. Thus, we have initiated a relative large scale retrospective clinical study investigating the correlation of CFTR with lung cancer progression in about 200 lung cancer patients. We have also started a basic research project studying the role of CFTR in the development of glioma, which is not of epithelial origin. This project is funded by RGC/GRF (CUHK 466413).

466111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
466111.value: Although there has been recent interest in the risk of various cancers in cystic fibrosis patients, studies on the role of CFTR in the pathogenesis of cancer are very limited. In the present study, we have revealed a previously undefined role of CFTR in breast cancer progression/metastasis. We have shown that suppression of CFTR promotes breast cancer malignant phenotype whereas over-expression of CFTR suppresses EMT and invasive properties both in cell model and breast cancer lung metastasis in mice model. More importantly, we have illustrated that CFTR expression is inversely associated with the progression and metastasis of breast cancer in patient samples. Our study has revealed a novel molecular regulatory mechanism involved in the progression of breast cancer and has the potential to provide novel target for prognosis and therapeutic intervention of breast cancer.

466511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
466511.value: Cells elicit genetic programs of adaptive cellular activities in response to changes in extracellular osmolality. These programs aim to adjust the content of intracellular electrolytes, restore altered cell volume, and maintain normal cellular functions. While in lower organisms such as bacteria and yeast the putative osmosensors and signal transduction cascades responsible for osmoadaptation have been identified, how mammalian cells detect and transduce osmotic stress signal remains elusive. The osmotic response element-binding protein (OREBP), also known as TonEBP or NFAT5, is an osmo-sensitive transcription factor in mammals and plays a central role in cellular adaptation to hypertonic stress via inducing expressions of enzymes and membranous transporters that are required to replace excess deleterious electrolytes with cell compatible organic osmolytes. Although numerous signaling pathways are activated by hypertonic stress, and OREBP is well recognized for its role in cell survival under hypertonic conditions, how the hypertonic signal is perceived and relayed to OREBP remains unknown to date. The central objective of this proposal is thus to characterize the role of Colony Stimulating Factor 1 Receptor (CSF-1R), a receptor tyrosine kinase, as a novel osmoreceptor for OREBP activation. Our earlier investigations showed that CSF-1R forms a feed-forward regulatory loop with OREBP to regulate osmoadaptation. CSF-1R protein is expressed at low, but detectable levels in many cell types, and is crucial for OREBP activation under hypertonic stress. Activated CSF-1R initiates cytoplasmic signaling cascades and undergoes cleavage to liberate a nuclear-targeting intracellular domain. Both events are crucial for OREBP activation. In view of these findings, this proposal aims to further delineate the molecular events underlying the hypertonic activation of OREBP mediated by CSF-1R. We will first characterize the molecular mechanism of CSF-1R activation and induction. Secondly, we will delineate the CSF-1R-OREBP cytoplasmic signaling cascade, aiming at establishing a spatiotemporal relationship for various signaling molecule implicated in OREBP activation. Thirdly, we will investigate the molecular mechanisms of receptor cleavage, nuclear translocation, and function of the intracellular domain. Lastly, we will probe for the physiological role of hypertonicity on macrophage function. Our proposed studies hold promise in the identification of the long-sought mammalian osmoreceptor and bridging the gap between osmosensing and OREBP activation. Our work could shed new lights on the cellular osmosensing mechanism in mammalian cells. Substantial evidence has suggested the existence of hypertonicity in tissue microenvironments, our work will ultimately provide insights into the emerging role of tonicity in human physiology and pathology. 當細胞外滲透壓改變時，細胞會發生壹系列適應性的遺傳學事件，從而調整胞內電解質的成分和含量，恢複改變的細胞體積，同時維持正常細胞功能。目前，在低等生物中（如細菌和酵母）已經發現了壹些參與滲透適應的滲透感受器以及相關的信號轉導通路，然後在哺乳動物中關于這方面的研究報道卻很少。滲透壓反應增強子結合蛋白（osmotic response element-binding protein，簡稱OREBP），也稱爲TonEBP 或者NFAT5，是哺乳動物細胞內已知的滲透壓相關的轉錄因子。OREBP通過誘導多種酶類和膜轉運蛋白的表達，調節細胞滲透性溶質進入胞內並取代胞內潴留的過量有害電解質，從而在細胞適應外界高滲透壓應激過程中起決定性作用。目前研究發現胞外高滲透壓環境能激活細胞的多條信號通路，而OREBP在維持細胞高滲環境中生存中的重要作用也得到研究者們的普通認可；但是這種高滲刺激信號是如何被細胞識別並傳遞給OREBP，目前尚不得而知。因此，本課題旨在研究CSF-1R（壹種受體酪氨酸激酶）作爲壹種新型的滲透壓感受器在OREBP激活過程中所起的重要作用。我們的前期研究發現CSF-1R和OREBP壹起組成前饋式調節回路，共同調節細胞的滲透適應性反應。盡管CSF-1R蛋白在多種細胞中僅有低水平的表達，但是對高滲環境下的OREBP激活卻起著關鍵作用。激活後的CSF-1R可以啓動壹系列細胞質信號級聯反應，並且自身通過發生斷裂從而釋出壹段靶向細胞核的胞內結構域，這兩個“事件”對OREBP的激活至關重要。鑒于以上前期研究結果，本課題將進壹步研究在高滲條件下CSF-1R調節激活OREBP的分子機制。首先，我們將研究CSF-1R激活的分子機制。其次，我們將詳細闡述CSF-1R—OREBP這壹細胞質信號級聯通路，藉此建立參與激活OREBP的各種信號分子時間和空間上的聯系。第三，我們將研究CSF-1R斷裂、核轉運以及由此産生的胞內結構域功能的相關分子機制。最後，我們將探索高滲透壓在巨噬細胞分化和功能發揮方面所起的生理學作用。本課題將有助于發現長久以來不斷尋找的哺乳動物細胞中滲透壓感受器，並在滲透感應和OREBP激活中建立起聯系的通道。同時，我們的工作也爲哺乳動物細胞滲透感應機制的研究提供有力證據據。另外壹方面，有研究報道高滲透壓也存在于組織微環境中，因此我們的工作最終將對認識滲透壓在人體病理生理學方面的新興作用提供理論依據。

466511.label: Realisation of objectives
466511.value: This project aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying the regulation of a mammalian tonicity-sensitive transcription factor, known as the Osmotic Response Element-Binding Protein (OREBP), also known as NFAT5, by changes in extracellular tonicity. Specifically, the original proposal aimed to delineate the role of CSF-1R, a tyrosine kinase receptor, in osmosensing and transduction of extracellular tonicity signals to regulate nucleocytoplasmic trafficking and transcriptional activity OREBP. However, after the commencement of this project when more data were collected we found that CSF-1R does not play a dominant role in the regulation of OREBP as anticipated. Although our preliminary data showed that CSF-1R may regulate OREBP activity as suggested by reporter gene assay, subsequent analysis suggested that endogenous expression of OREBP-regulated gene was neither regulated by the expression nor the activity of CSF-1R. After vigorous validation with different experiments, we decided to redesign our strategies to identify novel regulators for OREBP. Nucleocytoplasmic trafficking is one of the major mechanisms to regulate OREBP activity. Hypertonicity induces nuclear import of OREBP for the transcription of genes involve in osmoadapation, whereas hypotonicity induces its nuclear export. We therefore decided to conduct a thorough analysis to elucidate the nucleocytoplasmic trafficking mechanism and identify genuine regulator(s) for OREBP nucleocytoplasmic trafficking. Firstly, we aimed to define the minimal protein domain required for directing OREBP nuclear import. Using truncation mutants and site-directed mutagenesis, as well as fusion protein, we have defined a novel protein domain for directing OREBP nuclear import. We showed that OREBP utilizes an extended nuclear import domain comprised of the consensus nuclear localization signal (NLS) and two unique flanking protein domains for nuclear import activity. Interestingly, we further showed that nuclear import of NFAT5 involves atypical interaction between the NLS and nuclear import receptor importin-β1. To identify novel regulators for OREBP nucleocytoplasmic trafficking, we ectopically expressed FLAG-tagged dominant-negative OREBP (FLAG-OREBP132-581), which is devoid of the transactivating domain but remains responsive to changes in extracellular tonicity for nucleocytoplasmic trafficking, in HeLa cells. Cells were either challenged with hypotonic or hypertonic medium, followed by immunoprecipitation using anti-FLAG antibodies. Mass spectrometric analysis of OREBP-interacting proteins had led to the identification of a total of 204 non-redundant proteins. Among them, 68 and 41 proteins were specifically associated with FLAG-OREBP132-581 under hypotonic and hypertonic condition respectively, whereas 95 proteins were identified under both conditions. To explore the role of these proteins in the regulation of OREBP nucleocytoplasmic trafficking, we conducted a functional screen by depleting each of the candidate proteins by gene knockdown. Among others, we found that depletion of Inosine-5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase 2 (IMPDH2), RuvB-like 2 (RUVBL2), or ADP/ATP translocase 3 (SLC25A6) specifically inhibited nuclear export of FLAG-OREBP132-581 under hypotonic condition. On the other hand, depletion of the Heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein U (HNRNP U) selectively inhibited nuclear import of FLAG-OREBP132-581 under isotonic and hypertonic condition. The role of each of these putative targets in OREBP nucleocytoplasmic trafficking was further validated using independent siRNAs. Furthermore, we confirmed the interaction between OREBP and IMPDH2, RUVBL2, SLC25A6, HNRNP U by co-immunoprecipitation respectively. Subsequently, we further delineated the role HNRNP U in OREBP nuclear import. We showed that HNRNP U interacts with OREBP under isotonic and hypertonic conditions respectively, but not under hypotonic condition. Co-immunofluorescence analysis further revealed that HNRNP U is predominantly localized to the nucleus, and it is co-localized with OREBP under hypertonic and isotonic condition. In addition, we showed that HNRNP U interacts with the DNA-binding domain of OREBP. On the other hand, by comparing the nuclear import activity of OREBP fusion protein with or without DNA-binding domain, we are able to demonstrate that fusion protein without DNA-binding protein is less efficient in nuclear localization. Together our data suggested that HNRNP U acts as a nuclear retention factor for OREBP. Although our investigation into the mechanism of OREBP regulation deviates from the original plan due to unforeseen circumstances, we had taken another route to address this problem. Importantly we have identified a novel protein domain and a number of genuine regulators for OREBP nucleocytoplasmic trafficking. We have also taken one step further to characterize the cis-regulatory sequence required for nuclear import of OREBP. Importantly, with these changes in the strategies for investigations, the theme of this work, which is to address the regulation of OREBP in cellular adaptation to osmotic stress, remains aligned with the original plan. We are confident that via subsequent functional characterization of these putative proteins will provide novel insights into the mechanism of OREBP regulation. Therefore, we believed our study will impact the field as much as the original proposal should be.

466511.label: Major findings and research outcome
466511.value: The Osmotic Response Element Binding Protein (OREBP), also known as NFAT5, is a mammalian tonicity-responsive transcription factor that is critical for cellular adaptation to extracellular hypertonic stress. Like other transcription factors, nuclear trafficking plays a crucial role in the effective function of OREBP under hypertonic stress. However, the mechanisms underlying the regulation of OREBP nuclear import remain largely elusive. In this study, we identified and characterized novel nuclear import protein domains and factors required for nuclear import and retention of OREBP. We showed that although OREBP contains a consensus nuclear localization signal (NLS) that is crucial for directing nuclear import, it does not possess significant nuclear import activity per se. Instead, OREBP utilizes an extended nuclear import domain comprised of the NLS and two unique flanking protein domains for nuclear import activity. Nuclear import of OREBP involves atypical interaction between the NLS and nuclear import receptor importin-β1. In addition, in a protein-protein interaction screen, we identified Heterogeneous Nuclear Ribonucleoprotein U (hnRNP U) as a OREBP nuclear retention factor. hnRNP U promoted OREBP nuclear retention through interacting with the DNA-binding domain of OREBP. Collectively, these data suggested that OREBP utilizes distinctive nuclear localization domain and a complex mechanism for controlling its nuclear import and activation. Such regulation could ensure distinctive genetic programs are activated in response to hypertonic stress. Emerging evidence suggested that hypertonicity is playing a pivotal role in the regulation of blood pressure and innate immunity against pathogens in response to changes in tonicity. Therefore, our findings will generate a significant impact on our understanding of how these processes are regulated. Our study has led to the production of one review paper and one original paper (submitted to Journal of Cell Science). It also led to the training of a Ph.D. student.

466511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
466511.value: Our project can be further developed in the following aspects. Firstly, during proteomic and functional gene analysis we have identified and confirmed several OREBP interactors (IMPDH2, RUVBL2, SLC25A6). Gene knockdown of each of these targets led to significant retention of OREBP in the nucleus when cells were challenged with hypotonicity, suggesting that they are the putative regulators for OREBP nuclear export. Therefore, together with hnRNP U, these proteins may form a regulatory network for coordinating OREBP activity in response to changes in extracellular tonicity. In this study we have focused on the characterization of HNRNPU. To further understand how the other proteins are involved the OREBP regulation, we propose to elucidate the activity and function of each of these novel regulators, and to determine their functional relationship with OREBP in a spatial and temporal manner. To characterize the activity and regulation of IMPDH2 and RUVBL2 under different tonicities will be an important direction for further study too. On the other hand, our data suggested that nuclear import of OREBP is carried out via an unconventional mechanism involving an atypical interaction with KPNB1. We therefore propose to further define the interaction between KPNB1 and OREBP via X-ray crystallographic analysis.

466511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
466511.value: The Osmotic Response Element Binding Protein (OREBP), also known as NFAT5, is the only tonicity-responsive transcription factor known in mammals. OREBP is known to protect cells from the hypertonic environment in the kidney inner medulla where concentrated urine is produced. However, emerging evidence suggested that OREBP is also active in non-renal cells and is playing a central role in the sodium-dependent regulation of blood pressure and immunity. Because the activity of OREBP is primary regulated by its entry into the nucleus, understanding the mechanisms of nuclear trafficking of this transcription factor is crucial for advancing our understanding on its functions. Through comprehensive protein and gene analysis, this project has characterized a genuine protein domain of OREBP and identified a nuclear receptor for OREBP nuclear import. In addition, our work has led to the identification and elucidation of the function of a protein factor, known as hnRNP U, for regulating the activity of OREBP. The discovery of new players and mechanisms in OREBP regulation provide important information for advancing our understanding on the role of OREBP in health and diseases.

466611.label: Realisation of objectives
466611.value: 1. Objective 1: We have characterised the expression and subcellular localisation of GPR30 (GPER) in 16HBE14o- cells and primary human bronchial epithelial (HBE) cells using RT-PCR, Western blotting (whole cell lysates and fractionated cell lysates), and double immunofluorescence labelling for confocal laser scanning microscopy. 2. Objective 2: Using fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) measurements of intracellular cAMP level and a micro-spectrofluorimetric technique, we demonstrated that activation of GPER by 17β - estradiol (E2), or its specific agonist G1, rapidly attenuated a nucleotide-evoked increase in Ca2+ mobilisation. In contrast, the specific GPER antagonist G15 reversed this GPER-mediated inhibition. The inhibitory effects on P2Y receptor-mediated Ca2+ mobilisation are likely due to a GPER-mediated activation of the cAMP-dependent PKA pathway in human bronchial epithelium. With regard to the effect of E2 and G1 on the transepithelial ion transport activity of 16HBE14o- cells, our results indicate that both E2 and G1 can inhibit UDP-induced Cl- secretion in 16HBE14o- cells. UDP-induced Cl- secretion could be inhibited by G1 at concentrations as low as 100 nM. However, for E2, a supramaximal concentration (1 μM) was required for an inhibitory effect. 3. Objective 3: Damage to the airway epithelium by poly-L-arginine, a surrogate for major basic protein, stimulated the release of nucleotides such as UDP, which act on the P2Y receptors (including P2Y6) expressed on the cell membranes. P2Y6 receptor is connected to both Ca2+ and cAMP signalling pathways. Activation of the P2Y receptor in 16HBE14o- cells stimulated IL-8 protein release via p38, MAPK, ERK1/2, and NF-κB pathways. IL-6 release is coupled with the p38, but not the ERK1/2 MAPK, pathway. The P2Y6 receptor-mediated production of IL-6 and IL-8 was found to be dependent on Ca2+, but not the cAMP/PKA pathway. E2 and G1 inhibited nucleotide-induced cytokine release. The suppressive effects of E2 or G1 on P2Y receptor-mediated cytokine secretion are likely due to an inhibitory effect of GPER activation on P2Y receptor-mediated Ca2+ signalling pathway. In summary, this study has demonstrated for the first time the expression and function of GPER as an anti-inflammatory component in human bronchial epithelium, which is mediated by opposing effects on the pro‐inflammatory pathway activated by the P2Y receptors. Taken together, we believe that the three objectives have been fulfilled.

466611.label: Major findings and research outcome
466611.value: Expression and subcellular localisation of GPER in HBE cells: GPER mRNA and protein expression were demonstrated in 16HBE14o- cells and primary HBE cells using RT-PCR and Western blotting, respectively. GPER expression was also detected by immunofluorescence in 16HBE14o- cells and primary HBE cells. Data from colocalisation studies using double immunofluorescence labelling in 16HBE14o- cells, indicate that GPER did not colocalise with the Golgi, whereas there was a very small amount of overlap between GPER and the endoplasmic reticulum. In contrast, partial colocalisation was observed between GPER and the plasma membrane. Inhibitory effects of E2 or the GPER agonist, G1, on nucleotide-induced Ca2+ signalling in HBE cells: The increase in intracellular Ca2+ concentration ([Ca2+]i) in 16HBE14o- cells and primary HBE cells, evoked by different P2Y receptor agonists, including UTP (P2Y2 and P2Y4 agonist), UDP (P2Y6 agonist), and ATPγS (P2Y2 and P2Y11 agonist), was inhibited by E2 or G1 in a concentration-dependent manner. Using GPER specific antagonist G15, and lentiviral siRNA technology, we demonstrated that E2 could inhibit nucleotide-induced Ca2+ signalling via GPER. Effects of E2 and G1 on nucleotide-induced Ca2+ release and influx: We demonstrated that E2 inhibited nucleotide-induced Ca2+ release and Ca2+ influx, whereas G1 only inhibited P2Y receptor-mediated Ca2+ release. The inhibition of Ca2+ release by G1 was not due to a decrease in P2Y receptor-stimulated IP3 level. The effects of E2 and G1 on store-operated Ca2+ influx (SOC) were determined by FRET using 16HBE14o- cells co-expressing CFP- and YFP-STIM1. The results suggest that E2 attenuates SOC by inhibiting STIM1 oligomerisation. The role of the cAMP/PKA pathway in E2- and G1-mediated inhibition of Ca2+ increase: Data from real-time measurements of cAMP in 16HBE14o- cells using FRET imaging, suggest that GPER is connected to the activation of adenylate cyclase, likely via the Gs alpha subunit, to stimulate an increase in cAMP levels. The inhibitory effects of E2 and G1 on P2Y receptor-induced Ca2+ signalling are mediated via the activation of a cAMP-dependent PKA pathway. Anti-inflammatory effect of G1: The levels of two pro-inflammatory cytokines, interleukin 8 (IL-8) and IL-6, increased significantly after airway bronchial epithelial cells were stimulated by extracellular nucleotides or damaged by poly-L-arginine. Significant inhibition by G1 of ATPγS- or poly-L-arginine-stimulated IL-8 release was observed in 16HBE14o- cells. G1 also showed a significant inhibitory effect on ATPγS-stimulated IL-6 release in 16HBE14o- cells.

466611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
466611.value: Our findings suggest that P2Y receptor is a key player in airway epithelial inflammation. Respiratory virus (such as human rhinovirus, HRV) infection is the major common precipitant of exacerbations in asthma. Infection of the bronchial epithelium by respiratory viruses triggers the release of nucleotides into the mucosal surface through various mechanisms. Therefore, I have invited Professors Leung Ting-Fan and Chan Wan-Yi (Department of Paediatrics, CUHK) to initiate a pilot project to investigate the relationship between rhinovirus infection and asthmatic inflammation in the human airway. In particular, we will focus on a newly discovered HRV species, HRV-C. This new and potentially more pathogenic group of human rhinoviruses has recently been associated with the severity of acute asthma in children. With the advent of molecular diagnostic techniques and the development of a new HRV-C culture method, we will be able to study HRV-C infection in the human airway. We believe that this collaborative research group is one of the few in the world that can establish an in vivo culture system for HRV-C in the upper and lower airway epithelial cells. It is expected that either a GRF or HMRF grant proposal will be submitted in 2016/2017.

466611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
466611.value: This study has demonstrated that nucleotides released during the airway inflammatory processes (e.g. UDP) will activate cell membrane P2Y receptors, which will lead to further release of inflammatory cytokines. The secretion of cytokines and formation of such “cytokine networks” play important roles in prolonging airway inflammatory disease. This novel mechanism of UDP release, involving P2Y6 receptor activation, may represent an important cellular signalling pathway for regulating asthmatic inflammation in airway cells, and suggests that the P2Y6 receptor could be a therapeutic target for the development of anti-inflammatory strategies. In addition, a novel oestrogen (E2) receptor identified in different tissues, G-protein-coupled estrogen receptor (GPER), may play an anti-inflammatory role. This study has demonstrated for the first time the expression and function of GPER as an anti-inflammatory component in human bronchial epithelium, which it may mediate through its opposing effects on the pro‐inflammatory pathways activated by the P2Y receptors. These results will provide insight into the possible strategy of targeting GPER or the P2Y receptors as a novel approach in the treatment of lung diseases. The information obtained in the proposed study will thus provide opportunities for the further development of new and more effective therapies.
