466711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
466711.value: Sleep is an essential part of life. A healthy sleeping habit is crucial to human health. Increasing epidemiological evidences suggest an association between short sleep duration, diabetes and other cardiovascular risk factors. Local epidemiological data in this regard are relatively sparse. In addition, interventional trials exploring the role of sleep education, by normalizing sleep duration and improving sleep hygiene, on diabetes and its associated cardiometabolic risk factors are lacking. Moreover, the enigmatic link between sleep and cardiometabolic risk is under-explored. Against this background, using a multidisciplinary team consisting of endocrinologists, psychiatrist, respiratory physician, chemical pathologist and statistician experienced in conducting epidemiological studies and clinical trials, we propose to conduct a 2-stage study including 1) a cross-sectional study (stage 1) to examine the prevalence of sleep deprivation and insomnia in Hong Kong Chinese type 2 diabetic patients, and investigate the association between sleep behaviour, glycemic control and other cardiovascular risk factors in the study cohort; and then sleep deprived type 2 diabetic patients identified from stage 1 study are invited to enter 2) a randomized controlled trial (stage 2) with 12-month sleep education as intervention, followed by a 12-month observational period, to study whether sleep education would improve glycemic control and cardiometabolic profile of sleep deprived type 2 diabetic patients and evaluate the neurohormonal changes associated with sleep education. The proposed study will provide important public health information regarding the prevalence of sleep deprivation in Hong Kong Chinese type 2 diabetic patients. The data from the intervention with sleep education will provide evidence to support the implementation of sleep hygiene education as part of the holistic management of type 2 diabetic patients. By highlighting the association between mental health and diabetes, this study will potentially change the standards of medical care in diabetes management. 睡眠是生活的重要一環。良好的睡眠習慣對健康是很重要的。越來越多的流行病學數據顯示睡眠缺少，糖尿和心血管疾病風險是相關的。而且我們缺乏針對這相關問題的介入性臨床治療。此外，睡眠與心血管疾病風險之間的微妙關係仍存着很多未解的謎。 基於以上的背景，我們這個包括多種專科的團隊將建議進行一個兩階段的研究﹕ (1) 第一階段 - 橫斷面研究 - 旨在探討睡眠缺乏和失眠問題在香港華裔二型糖尿病人的普遍性，以及血糖控制及其他心血管病血險之間的關係; (2) 第二階段 - 隨機對照研究 - 從第一階段研究中，我們找到睡眠缺乏的二型糖尿病人參加這個第二階段研究。這將會是一個十二個月的睡眠研究，和一個十二個月的跟進觀察期。 參加的病人將隨機分配進入以下其中一個組別 - 加入睡眠教育的組別和一般性的糖尿教育組別。這部分的研究旨在探討睡眠教育是否能改善血糖控制及其他心血管疾病風險因素。 這研究建議將提供重要的公共醫學資料及支持數據提倡睡眠教育的重要性，從而提高對糖尿病人的醫療素質及水平。

466711.label: Realisation of objectives
466711.value: We completed the study with the objectives achieved. We recruited a total of 4,290 patients with type 2 diabetes as of July 2014 for the analysis of stage 1 cross-sectional study. Based on this cohort, we identified 267 eligible subjects for stage 2 study i.e. a randomized controlled trial (RCT) with sleep education as intervention versus usual or conventional care for 12 months. The recruitment of stage 2 study had been completed on March 2015. For stage 1 study, among 4,290 type 2 diabetic patients recruited, 3,508 subjects who were not shift workers and had complete biochemical and sleep data were included for the present analyses (475 were shift workers). Mean age of the cohort was 53.9 (standard deviation, SD 8.7) years and mean disease duration of diabetes was 8.3 (SD 7.1) years. 59.0% were men and 58.8% of the total cohort reported to have full or part-time employment. 21.1% of study subjects had mean sleep duration during weekdays <7 hours whereas 5.2% had mean sleep duration during weekdays <6 hours. Mean sleep duration during weekdays and difference of sleep durations between weekdays and weekends were 7.7 (SD 1.3) hours and 0.6 (SD 1.2) hours respectively. The respective figures for mean glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) and fasting plasma glucose (FPG) were 7.6 (1.5)% and 7.6 (2.5)mmol/l respectively. Hierarchical restricted cubic spline regressions were performed to examine the associations between glycaemic control parameters and sleep pattern parameters. After adjustment for socio-demographics, lifestyle and health-related factors, psychological confounding factors, and other sleep pattern parameters, only sleep duration difference between weekdays and weekends remained significantly associated with both HbA1c and FPG, while weekday sleep duration had a significant non-linear association with HbA1c. The fully adjusted models showed that there was a U-shaped relationship between HbA1c and weekday sleep duration, and between FPG and sleep duration difference, and a U-shaped (left arm flattened) relationship between HbA1c and sleep duration difference between weekdays and weekends. Of note, sleep duration of about one hour more during weekends when compared to weekdays was associated with beneficial effect in HbA1c (-0.13%,95% conference interval, -0.24 to -0.02), suggesting that modest sleep compensation might be beneficial to glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes. On the contrary, shorter sleep duration during weekend than weekday would be associated with higher FPG. Furthermore, short sleep duration during weekday (< 7 hours) was consistently associated with higher HbA1c and FPG. Regarding the prevalence of insomnia in our local Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes, using self-reported questionnaires (Insomnia Severity Index, ISI) and insomnia being defined as ISI score >14, we found that insomnia was a prevalent condition with 9.7% of the study cohort had insomnia. Furthermore, insomniac state was positively associated with HbA1c and FPG in Hong Kong Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes (please refer to the abstract accepted as poster presentation in International Diabetes Federation Western Pacific Region meeting to be held at Taipei October 2016 and the full paper is under preparation). For stage 2 study, a total of 267 patients with type 2 diabetes and short sleep duration (defined as weekday sleep duration <7 hours/day) were randomized into control group (usual or conventional care without sleep education, n=137) and intervention group (sleep education program as per study protocol, n=130). Mean age of the study cohort in this RCT was 53.1(standard deviation, SD 8.7) years. 52.4% were men. Mean weekday and weekend sleep durations were 6.8 (SD 1.0) hours and 7.7 (SD 1.3) hours respectively. Median HbA1c and FPG were 7.1 (interquartile range, IQR 6.5-7.9)% and 7.1 (IQR 6.0-8.6)mmol/L respectively. Interim analyses were conducted when 80% study subjects completed 12 months intervention. At 6-month, there were significantly more defaulters in the intervention group compared to the control group (18.5% vs 6.6%, p=0.003). Patients in both control and intervention group showed significant increase in weekday sleep duration compared to baseline (0.22 hours, 95% confidence interval: 0.05-0.39 hours, p=0.013 in control group and 0.32 hours, 95% CI: 0.15 – 0.49 hours, p<0.001 in intervention group) but there was no significant difference in the changes between the two groups. Moreover, there were no significant differences in glycemic control (both HbA1c and FPG) in the control and intervention group. The result of this interim analysis was submitted for abstract presentation in International Congress of Endocrinology, to be held in Beijing on 31 August to 4 September 2016. In addition, we did not find any significant improvement of cardiometabolic risk factors including obesity indices, blood pressure and lipid profile between control and intervention groups during the interim analysis. Due to insufficient budget (about -21% difference between budget applied and actual funding amount), neurohormonal changes of the study subjects (study objective number 4) were unable to be achieved at this moment. Nonetheless, aliquots of the subjects had been stored and effort to search for alternative source of funding has been in active progress. The achievement of this objective would be done once funding support to do the assays are available. In summary, the results of this study had been presented as oral or poster presentations in 9 local, regional and international conferences and resulted or will result in 4 full papers (one had been published as conference proceedings, one had been submitted/under review, one is under preparation while one will be written soon).

466711.label: Major findings and research outcome
466711.value: To our knowledge, this study is the first in Hong Kong which had provided epidemiological data regarding the prevalence of sleep deprivation and insomnia in Hong Kong Chinese type 2 diabetic patients. This large cohort had demonstrated that insomnia and short sleep duration are prevalent conditions in Hong Kong and are associated with negative impacts on glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes. The results of our study echo with a recently published meta-analysis (Shan Z, et al. Diabetes Care 2015;38:529-37) which shows that there is a U-shaped relationship between sleep duration and risk of diabetes. A novel message of our study was that regular sleeping habits with modest sleep compensation during weekends were associated with better glycemic control when compared to type 2 diabetic patients with irregular sleep habits and without sleep compensation. Despite the fact that intervention with sleep education program did not show any significant impact on glycemia and other conventional cardiometabolic risk factors at this juncture (during interim analysis of the data of RCT), further analysis including per-protocol analysis, when the total cohort had exited from the trial will be done and more sub-group analyses will be proceeded to explore for any effect of sleep education on health and psychosocial parameters of patients with type 2 diabetes.

466711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
466711.value: This study provides important information regarding the local epidemiological data of sleep deprivation and insomnia in Hong Kong Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes. Since there were blood aliquots stored from all participants (for genetic analysis and biobank as part of the Hong Kong Diabetes Registry) and a sub-cohort had assessments done for diet and physical activity (project of a PhD student who has a dietitian background), the sleep data from this study will potentially be included in the future analysis of gene-sleep-diet interactions and provide insights for the interactive effects of genes and environmental factors. Furthermore, the data of this study will throw insights regarding the long-term outcome of sleep deprivation and insomnia, as well as other sleep behavior abnormalities, including the impacts of shift work and irregular sleep patterns on cancers and mortality because all study subjects will continue to be included in the prospective follow-up as part of the Hong Kong Diabetes Registry. Efforts to seek future funding support to do genetic and other analysis, as well as periodic survey of long-term sleep habits behaviors, will be taken.

466711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
466711.value: Increasing evidence suggest an association between sleep, diabetes and other cardiovascular risk factors. Local epidemiological data in this regard are limited. Here, we conducted a cross-sectional study to examine the prevalence of sleep deprivation and insomnia in Hong Kong Chinese patients. Among 3,508 type 2 diabetic patients (mean age:53.9 years) included, 21.1% had mean sleep duration during weekdays <7 hours whereas 5.2% had mean sleep duration during weekdays <6 hours. There was a U-shaped relationship between glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) and weekdays sleep duration. Sleep compensation with about one hour more during weekends was associated with beneficial effect in HbA1c and FPG. We also found that insomnia was a prevalent condition in type 2 diabetic patients (9.7% of the total cohort) with insomniac state being positively associated with HbA1c and FPG. We further proceed to recruit 267 patients with short sleep duration (<7 hours/weekday) and randomized them into usual care (n=137) and intervention with sleep education program of 12 months (n=130). An interim analysis of 80% of the study cohort did not reveal any significant difference in glycemic control between the 2 groups. Our study provides important local epidemiological data about sleep and glycemic control in type 2 diabetic patients.

466811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
466811.value: Giant Cell Tumor of Bone is the most common bone tumor reported in the Asian population. This is an aggressive tumor that primarily affects the younger patient, particularly between the ages of 20-40 years and is characterized by a destructive lesion that affects the major joints at the end of long bones. The treatment of this tumor requires the surgical removal of large segments of the bone resulting in poor function of the limb. Often the tumor recurs even after repeated surgery with significant morbidity to the young patients. The use of some novels drugs may help reduce the aggressive potential of this tumor with obvious advantages to the patient. However, a major barrier towards the study of the effects of drugs and their combinations on GCT has been the lack of an animal model. Our group has successfully pioneered the use of drugs to combat the aggressiveness of this tumor and to help reduce the magnitude of surgery. For our proposed project we have piloted a novel animal model of the Giant Cell Tumor in which we propose to study the effects of a novel combination of drugs, Bisphosphonates (Zoledronate) and Prenyl Transferase Inhibitors (GGTI-298), and to evaluate their effects on the tumor. The use of this combination of drugs bases on the experimental results in our previous study, which showed the combination of bisphosphonates and GGTIs significantly inducing S-phase cell cycle arrest and caspase-3/7 activity. Furthermore, this combination also increased the OPG/RANKL ratio, which favored bone formation and may reduce bone resorption caused by the osteoclast-like giant cells in the tumor. We have developed an alternative model in which the GCT stromal cells continue their neoplastic proliferation. This shall provide an invaluable platform for studying the in-vivo effects of these drugs on the neoplastic cells of the GCT. Given that GCT is the most common neoplasm of bone reported in the Chinese and East-Asian population, in the long-term, the reduced recurrence following adjuvant drug therapy may translate to major economic benefits given that the scale and magnitude of surgery may be reduced in these patients and the need for multiple surgeries for repeated recurrences may also be reduced. 摘要 骨巨細胞瘤是在亞洲人口中最常見的骨腫瘤。這腫瘤主要影響年齡在 20-40 歲之間年輕的病人。骨巨細胞瘤是侵略性腫瘤，對主要關節的長骨造成破壞。 治療這個腫瘤需要手術切除大段骨肢，對病人造成不良影響。在較年輕的病人中，腫瘤往往再次復發需要進行多次手術，甚至手術後產生重大併發症。雖然使用一些新藥物可以降低這個腫瘤對病人的影響。然而，對這些新藥物的研究主要障礙是一直缺乏骨巨細胞瘤的動物模型。 我們研究團隊成功地開創了使用藥物，打擊這個腫瘤對骨的腐蝕性和明顯減少手術的嚴重程度。在這個專案中，我們已經試行建立骨巨細胞瘤的動物模型，用以測試我們研究的新型藥物、 雙膦酸鹽 (Zoledronate) 和代異戊烯基轉移酶抑制劑(GGTI-298) 的組合對骨巨細胞瘤的影響。我們使用這種藥物組合是基地在我們的研究結果，研究顯示雙膦酸鹽(Zoledronate)與代異戊烯基轉移酶抑制劑(GGTI-298) 的組合能顯著誘導 S 期細胞週期停止和減少半胱氨酸蛋白酶-3/7 (Caspase-3/7) 活動。 此外，這藥物組合也增加骨保護素/破骨比例，增加骨形成，能降低骨巨細胞瘤的破骨細胞所致的骨吸收。 鑒於骨巨細胞瘤是在中國和東亞人口中最常見的骨腫瘤，輔助藥物能減少病人的手術範圍和反復復發的機會，從長遠來看，這種藥物組合治療能減少醫療費用，轉化為經濟利益。

466811.label: Realisation of objectives
466811.value: Both the project objectives have been fully achieved. We successfully established a nude mice model of GCT stromal cells which allows non-invasive, real-time assessments of tumor development and testing the in vivo effects of different adjuvants for treating GCT. We also demonstrated the inhibitory effects of ZOL treatment alone or the co-treatment with GGTI-298 in GCT stromal cells in the new animal model. To achieve the objective 1, GCT stromal cell line G33, a highly proliferative cell line, was transduced with the V5-LUC Puro expression lentivirus vector containing the luciferase gene coding region and the puromycin resistant gene. The resulting cell line is referred to Luc-G33. Luc-G33 cells showed high bioluminescent imaging (BLI) signal after adding the D-luciferin potassium salt in vitro. After establishing the stable luciferase-expressing cell line, we used a three-dimensional (3D) matrix, extracel-X hydrogel to deliver the Luc-G33 cells either subcutaneously on the back or to the tibiae of the nude mice. In brief, Luc-G33 cells were resuspended in serum-free medium at 2 × 10^7 cells/ml for each 100 µl injection with hydrogel. The hydrogel concentration was optimized and each 30ul of cell suspension was mixed with 35 µl of Glycosil and 35 µl of Gelin-S to form a 70% synthetic hydrogel solution using an Extracel-X Hydrogel Kit. In the end, 17.5 µl of Extralink was added into the cell suspension immediately before injection to the animals. To achieve the objective 2, we also tested the in vivo antitumor effects of ZOL and GGTI-298 alone or their combinations in Luc-G33-transplanted nude mice. Thirty-two mice after Luc-G33 implantation were randomly divided into four groups with equal average body weight and drugs were given to each mice three days after cell injection. Eight mice per group were treated with either 0.9% saline (Control), ZOL (400 µg/kg), GGTI-298 (1.16 mg/kg), or the combination of ZOL at 400 µg/kg and GGTI-298 at 1.16 mg/kg, respectively at day 3 post cell transplantation, to determine the effects of single treatment alone and the combined treatment in both the subcutaneous and intraoessous models. Tumor growth under the dorsal skin and in the tibiae were monitored by BLI twice per week from day 3 (before drug administration) to day 35. The dorsal skin and the tibia samples were harvested on day 35 post cell transplantation to confirm the presence of the Luc-G33 cells by ex vivo BLI images and immunohistochemistry.

466811.label: Major findings and research outcome
466811.value: 1) ZOL, GGTI-298 and the co-treatment reduced cell viability of Luc-G33 cells in vitro A highly proliferative cell line of GCT stromal cells was used to create a stable and luciferase-transduced cell line, Luc-G33. Luc-G33 cells showed high BLI signal and its cell viability could be significantly reduced by ZOL at 0.8 µg/ml. The latter result is consistent with our finding [Ref. 1], indicating that the luciferase transduction did not affect the cell viability or drug sensitivity of GCT stromal cells. The IC50 was 1.50 ± 0.37 μg/ml for ZOL, and 5.41 ± 0.59 μg/ml for GGTI-298 in the 5-day treatment. Combination of ZOL with GGTI-298 led to synergistic inhibition and the cell viability was 25.97%, 16.09% and 0.17% of the controls under the low, middle and high concentration treatment conditions, respectively. 2) A new animal model of luciferase-expressing GCT stromal cells in nude mice After establishing the stable luciferase-expressing cell line, we used an extracel-X hydrogel to deliver the Luc-G33 cells either subcutaneously on the back or to the tibiae of the nude mice. The hydrogel provided a well-contained, growth-enhancing environment in which the tumor cells initially propagated and remained viable on site for 7 weeks in the subcutaneous tumor model. By BLI signal, the Luc-G33 cells were found to survive for more than 12 weeks in some nude mice. 3) ZOL alone and the co-treatment with GGTI-298 inhibited the growth of Luc-G33 cells in the subcutaneous tumor model In this study, we tested the in vivo antitumor effects of ZOL and GGTI-298 alone or their combinations in Luc-G33-transplanted nude mice. It was found that ZOL alone at 400 µg/kg and the co-treatment of ZOL at 400 µg/kg and GGTI-298 at 1.16 mg/kg reduced tumor cell viability in the subcutaneous tumor model, whereas, no significant inhibition was found by GGTI-298 treatment alone [Ref. 2]. 4) Immunohistochemistry demonstrated the presence of Luc-G33 cells in the subcutaneous and the tibial models The dorsal skin and the tibia samples injected with Luc-G33 cells were harvested on day 35 and the presence of Luc-G33 cells were confirmed by both the BLI and the immunohistochemistry examinations. BLI values obtained from the whole body images were well correlated with that from the corresponding tissue samples ex vivo. The immunohistochemistry data of human mitochondria identification also confirmed the presence of Luc-G33 cells in the skin and tibia tissues.

466811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
466811.value: We successfully developed a stable in vivo model of GCT stromal cells using luciferase-labeled, primary cultured GCT stromal cells. This model provides non-invasive and longitudinal investigation of subcutaneous transplantation of GCT stromal cells by BLI. To our knowledge, it is the first in vivo model that allows non-invasive and real-time measurement of GCT stromal cell survival and growth after transplantation. This model also facilitates to study the tumor development and allows the mechanistic evaluation of existing and novel targets for GCT. In the long term, this model helps to develop a safe and effective adjuvant in the treatment of aggressive GCT; to scale-down the magnitude of surgery required for GCT of Bone following adjuvant treatments thereby retaining joints and preserving good function; and to reduce the rate of debilitating multiple recurrences in patients with GCT of bone. Given that GCT is the most common neoplasm of bone reported in the Chinese and East-Asian population, the reduced recurrence following adjuvant therapy may translate to major economic benefits given that multiple surgeries for repeated recurrences are also reduced.

466811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
466811.value: Giant Cell Tumor of Bone (GCT) is a common neoplasm in Chinese patients, notoriously prone to recurrence following treatment. The use of some novel drugs may help to reduce the recurrence of this tumor. However, a major barrier towards the study of the effects of drugs on GCT has been the lack of an animal model. In this study, we created an animal model in which GCT stromal cells survived and functioned as proliferating neoplastic cells. A highly proliferative cell line of GCT stromal cells was used to create a stable and luciferase-transduced cell line, Luc-G33. We used a three-dimensional hydrogel to deliver the Luc-G33 cells subcutaneously on the back of the nude mice. The tumor cells initially propagated and remained viable on site for 7 weeks. We also tested the in vivo antitumor effects of ZOL and GGTI-298 alone or their combinations in the nude mice model. It was found that ZOL alone and the co-treatment of ZOL and GGTI-298 reduced tumor cell viability. In summary, we established a nude mice model of GCT stromal cells which allows non-invasive, real-time assessments of tumor development and the mechanistic evaluation of existing and novel adjuvants for GCT.

467511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
467511.value: 癌症相關的炎症可以促進腫瘤生長，因而成為研究標靶治療的目標對象。本研究項目的目的是探討細胞因子(淋巴毒素) 在卵巢腫瘤的微環境中所產生的調節趨化因子信號傳導作用。我們發現淋巴毒素在大多數人類卵巢上皮性腫瘤組織中過度表達，而它的受體(淋巴毒素-β受體)，亦在卵巢上皮腫瘤細胞及腫瘤相關基質成纖維細胞上表達。這些淋巴毒素和其受體在腫瘤微環境中的特別表達模式反映淋巴毒素可能使腫瘤細胞在其環境中產生交叉干擾作用。同時，我們也發現在卵巢上皮性腫瘤細胞中淋巴毒素並不是擔任自分泌生長因子。這說明腫瘤源性淋巴毒素在卵巢腫瘤微環境中擔當腫瘤細胞與基質成纖維細胞之間的溝通橋樑。我們初步研究結果顯示，基質成纖維細胞在經過人造淋巴毒素的處理後, 能激活細胞中趨化因子的表達。在被激活的趨化因子當中，最令我們產生興趣的是CXCL11。因CXCL11通過CXCR7受體會促進腫瘤細胞生長。同時，CXCL11也會通過CXCR3受體促進腫瘤轉移。我們初步的研究還表明，人造CXCL11處理會促進帶有CXCR3和CXCR7受體的卵巢腫瘤細胞的趨化作用。基於這些初步研究數據，我們假設腫瘤源性淋巴毒素會透過刺激基質成纖維細胞生產CXCL11，從而建立雙向的腫瘤-宿主相互作用, 加促卵巢腫瘤生長。在此研究項目中，我們會採用免疫組化檢測去確定腫瘤源性淋巴毒素和基質源性CXCL11 於原發性卵巢腫瘤中的臨床意義。此外，為了解淋巴毒素介導的腫瘤-宿主相互作用的機制，我們將使用異位表達和基因抑制的技術, 操縱淋巴毒素-淋巴毒素-β受體和CXCL11信號分子在卵巢腫瘤細胞和基質成纖維細胞的表達。利用體外混合培養和共同活體植入技術, 我們將會剖析腫瘤細胞和基質成纖維細胞之間的關係。這些方法能夠證明， 一. 腫瘤源性淋巴毒素透過淋巴毒素-β受體-NFKB信號傳導通路, 在基質成纖維細胞激活趨化因子CXCL11表達。二. 源自受淋巴毒素激活成纖維細胞的CXCL11可以進一步通過卵巢腫瘤細胞上的CXCR7促進腫瘤生長, 及通過CXCR3促進腫瘤轉移。我們的研究結果將確定腫瘤源性淋巴毒素在卵巢腫瘤微環境中控制腫瘤-宿主相互作用的獨特功能。重點是，這些研究結果將提供一個強而有力的理據，以進一步發展針對淋巴毒素的卵巢癌治療方法。

467511.label: Realisation of objectives
467511.value: For Objective 1 (To determine if the expression of tumor-derived lymphotoxin and stroma-derived CXCL11 are correlated with clinical features of primary ovarian tumors): We determined the expression patterns of lymphotoxin and CXCL11 in ovarian cancer. First, we examined the protein expression of lymphotoxin and LTBR in normal ovarian inclusion cysts (IC) and various ovarian cancer subtypes by immunohistochemistry. Our results indicated that lymphotoxin is over-expressed in ovarian cancer cells, whereas LTBR is expressed in both the cancer cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts. Second, we examined the expression of CXCL11 in clinical samples of normal ovarian ICs and primary ovarian cancer in situ. Immunohistochemical staining showed that CXCL11 was strongly expressed in CAFs in various ovarian cancer subtypes. Moreover, the expression of CXCL11 in tumour stromal was significantly and positively associated with the expression of LTA in the cancer cells of primary ovarian cancers. These results suggested that the expression of CXCL11 in CAFs is up-regulated by lymphotoxin which produced from adjacent ovarian cancer cells. We then investigated the CXCR3 expression in the cancer cells of primary ovarian tumours. CXCR3 is one of the two receptors of CXCL11. We found that CXCR3 protein was strongly expressed in the cancer cells of various ovarian cancer subtypes. We further revealed the importance of CXCR3 in progression of human ovarian cancer by studying the associations between protein expression of CXCR3 and clinicopathologic features in 78 cases of primary ovarian cancers, which included various subtypes. Our statistical analysis showed that the over-expression of CXCR3 was significantly correlated with the tumour grade and lymph node metastasis in ovarian cancers. For Objective 2 (To determine if paracrine lymphotoxin signaling derived from ovarian tumor cells regulates CXCL11 in stromal fibroblasts via LTBR): In our study, we used in vitro cultures and molecular experiments to demonstrate that 1) human non-malignant ovarian surface epithelial cells and ovarian cancer cells are not the major lymphotoxin-responsive cells; 2) lymphotoxin induces chemokine expression in stromal fibroblasts through LTBR-NFκB signaling; 3) cancer cell-derived lymphotoxin induces CXCL10 and CXCL11 expression in stromal fibroblasts through LTBR-NFκB signalling For Objective 3 (To determine if paracrine CXCL11 signaling derived from stromal fibroblasts promotes ovarian tumor growth and metastasis via CXCR7 and CXCR3): In our study, we also use co-culture systems to demonstrate the fibroblast-secreted CXCL11 promotes proliferation and migration of ovarian cancer cells via CXCR3-MAPK/AKT pathways.

467511.label: Major findings and research outcome
467511.value: We have investigated the role of cytokine lymphotoxin in tumor-stromal interactions in human ovarian cancer. We found that lymphotoxin over-expression is commonly shared by the cancer cells of various ovarian cancer subtypes, and lymphotoxin-beta receptor (LTBR) is expressed ubiquitously in both the cancer cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs). In monoculture, we showed that ovarian cancer cells are not the major lymphotoxin-responsive cells. On the other hand, our co-culture studies demonstrated that the cancer cell-derived lymphotoxin induces chemokine expression in stromal fibroblasts through LTBR-NFκB signalling. Amongst the chemokines being produced, we found that fibroblast-secreted CXCL11 promotes proliferation and migration of ovarian cancer cells via the chemokine receptor CXCR3. CXCL11 is highly-expressed in CAFs in ovarian cancer biopsies, while CXCR3 is found on malignant cells in primary ovarian tumours. Additionally, the over-expression of CXCR3 is significantly associated with the tumour grade and lymph node metastasis of ovarian cancer, further supporting the role of CXCR3, which interacts with CXCL11, in promoting growth and metastasis of human ovarian cancer. Taken together, these results demonstrated that cancer-cell derived lymphotoxin mediates reciprocal tumour-stromal interactions in human ovarian cancer by inducing CXCL11 in fibroblasts. This work has been published in Journal of Pathology in January 2004.

467511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
467511.value: Since we found a cancer-stroma-cancer interacting loop that promotes ovarian cancer progression through lymphotoxin and CXCL11, our findings suggest that lymphotoxin-LTBR and CXCL11-CXCR3 signalling represent therapeutic targets in ovarian cancer.

467511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
467511.value: Our study found that the cytokine lymphotoxin in ovarian cancer induce a positive interacting loop between ovarian cancer cells and their neighbouring tissues through another cytokine called CXCL11. This cytokine interacting loop in fact promotes ovarian tumour growth and spread. Therefore, the results of our study suggest that lymphotoxin and CXCL11 are potential targets for developing new therapeutic treatment of ovarian cancer.

468111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
468111.value: The aims of this study are to (i) investigate the mercury content of seafood commonly consumed by women of childbearing age and children in Hong Kong, (ii) the impact of “consumer apparent” characteristics of seafood on mercury content, and (iii) the association between estimated mercury exposure from seafood with actual mercury exposure as measured by hair mercury concentration. There is evidence to suggest that low-dose mercury exposure during the formative years may cause long-term adverse health effects in children. Some of these effects have been shown to persist even at 14 years of age. Seafood consumption is the major source of mercury exposure in most populations, including Hong Kong. However, although previous studies have been performed to determine the mercury content of seafood, several problems exist which limit the application of these results to our population: (i) small within species sample size, (ii) choice of seafood items without reference of local seafood consumption behaviour, (iii) lack of correlation between the individual subjects’ estimated mercury intake from seafood and their actual mercury exposure. In this project we plan to measure mercury content in seafood groups commonly consumed by local women of childbearing age and children. Consumer apparent seafood characteristics such as species, size and catchment area will be recorded and their impact on fish mercury content analysed. The contribution of different seafood products to actual mercury exposure as measured by hair mercury concentration will be analysed with multivariate regression models. Systematic investigation of mercury content in seafood and its major influencing factors will provide a firm body of evidence upon which to base seafood consumption recommendations to local women of childbearing age, especially during pregnancy, and young children. 本研究的目的在於研究：（1）香港市面上常被婦女兒童食用的海產品中汞元素的含量；（2）“消費者可知特點”對海產品中汞含量的影響；（3）因食用海產品導致體內汞含量預期值與經毛髮測得的汞含量實際值的關聯性。 有證據證明，幼年少量的汞暴露可對兒童長期健康構成危害，有些危害甚至可以持續到14歲。在包括香港在內的很多地區，食用魚類等海產品是汞暴露的主要來源。雖然已有一些研究測定海產品中的汞含量，但由於諸多問題尚難以應用於香港人口：（1）種類樣本量不夠；（2）樣本採集並未準尋本地海產品的消費食用習慣；（3）缺乏比較個體預期汞攝入和實際體內汞含量的關係。 本試驗擬測定本地常被妊娠婦女和兒童食用的海產品中汞的含量。研究者將記錄海產品消費者可知特點例如種類、大小、捕撈地等用於分析其與魚中汞含量的關聯性。各種海產品的食用對實際通過毛髮檢測得的汞暴露的貢獻程度將通過多元回歸模型進行分析。 系統的研究海產品中的汞含量及其相關影響因素將為正確指導本地幼兒、孕齡婦女，特別是孕婦食用海產品提供可靠的依據。

468111.label: Realisation of objectives
468111.value: 1. To determine the mercury content of seafood commonly consumed by high risk groups (women of childbearing age and young children) in Hong Kong Twenty-nine of the most popular seafood items consumed by women of childbearing age and young children in Hong Kong were determined by the phase 1 questionnaires. For each seafood item, between 9-45 specimens were collected. Although it was planned that each seafood item would require 20 specimens, for some seafood items, not all the markets visited had any to be purchased. However, total number of tested items exceeded the targeted total of 600 specimens when including seafood items and fish oil based products. 2. To evaluate the impact of “consumer apparent” seafood characteristics (seafood species, seafood size, approximate catchment area) on mercury content in commercially available seafood in Hong Kong Consumer apparent seafood characteristics that were obtainable included seafood weight and size. Catchment area and species often were not readily obtainable at retail level. For each seafood item, correlation analysis was performed for fish width, length and weight against methylmercury and total mercury content. For sizes of fish commonly available in HK wet markets, there was no correlation between these characteristics and mercury content, except for one or two species, where one influential specimen contributed to the significant association between fish characteristics and mercury content. Overall it seems that consumer apparent seafood characteristics are unhelpful when attempting to determine the mercury content. 3. To investigate the association between calculated daily intake of mercury from seafood consumption in vulnerable populations and mercury exposure as measured by hair mercury concentration. For preschool children, a total of 293 children were assessed. Significant correlation was found between calculated mercury intake from seafood consumption and hair mercury concentration. The correlation coefficient was 0.44 for calculated MeHg versus hair MeHg and 0.43 for calculated total Hg versus hair total Hg (P < 0.001 for both). For mothers, a total of 284 mothers were assessed. Significant correlation was found between calculated mercury intake from seafood consumption and hair mercury concentration. The correlation coefficient was 0.32 for calculated MeHg versus hair MeHg and 0.31 for calculated total Hg versus hair total Hg (P < 0.001 for both). Overall, the three objectives of this project were fully met.

468111.label: Major findings and research outcome
468111.value: 2245 preschool children (1061 were girls, i.e., 47%) were recruited for the phase 1. The children were recruited from 63 kindergartens distributed throughout the four geographic regions of Hong Kong. Seafood intake for preschool children median of 20 times per month (IQR 11, 32) and for their mothers the median was 22 times per month (IQR 12, 35). Based on the fish food frequency questionnaires collected, 29 of the most frequently consumed fish species (accounting for approximately 80% of the total seafood intake of the population) and 5 commonly consumed fish oil supplements were purchased from the markets or shops that were most frequently visited by the population. Overall, the mean (SD) total mercury content of the seafood items was 0.06 (0.04) ppm and mean (SD) methylmercury (MeHg) of 0.05 (0.04) ppm. Overall, most seafood available in HK did not exceed the 0.5 ppm stipulated by the HK government Public Health and Municipal Services Ordinance (Cap.132). There were only two types of fish (one marine fish species and one imported frozen fish species) with items exceeding 0.5 ppm. Five types of fish oil supplements commonly consumed by the mothers and children were purchased. Mean (SD) total mercury was 0.01 (0.01) ppm and mean MeHg was 0.006 (0.007) ppm. For phase 2, a total of 293 children and 284 mothers were successfully recruited. For mothers, mercury intake estimated from the food diaries exceeded US EPA recommendation (0.1 ug/kg bw/day) in 3.2%. Despite this, mothers’ hair MeHg and total Hg medians (IQR) were 0.61 (0.43, 0.83) ppm and 0.99 (0.73, 1.36) ppm, respectively. This means that mothers exceed US EPA exposure recommendations of 1 ppm in 16.1% and 49.3% for MeHg and total Hg, respectively. The correlation coefficient was 0.32 for estimated MeHg versus hair MeHg and 0.31 for estimated total Hg versus hair total Hg (P < 0.001 for both). For children, mercury intake estimated from the food diaries exceeded US EPA recommendation (0.1 ug/kg bw/day) in 14.3%. Despite this, the children’s hair MeHg and total Hg medians (IQR) were 0.60 (0.37, 0.91) ppm and 1.00 (0.65, 1.47) ppm, respectively. This means that children in our cohort exceed US EPA exposure recommendations in 20.1% and 50.2% for MeHg and total Hg, respectively. The correlation coefficient was 0.44 for estimated MeHg intake versus hair MeHg and 0.43 for etimated total Hg intake versus hair total Hg (P < 0.001 for both).

468111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
468111.value: Due to the restrictions in terms of consumer apparent characteristics available at the markets and the limited budget, only a restricted selection of seafood items and seafood characteristics were recorded. Further research may extend to wholesalers to identify further seafood characteristics such as speciation and catchment areas. This would increase the scope and accuracy of the results obtained. In view of our findings of a large proportion of individuals exceeding US EPA mercury exposure recommendations in terms of hair mercury concentrations, studies of dietary interventions to reduce high risk individuals’ mercury levels are warranted. With sufficient funding, we could invite back individuals with high mercury levels for dietary intervention trials.

468111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
468111.value: Our project results show that seafood consumption remains at a relatively high level amongst our population of young children and women of childbearing age. By measuring mercury levels in seafood items commonly consumed by local women and young children, we have found that estimated mercury intake levels are not very high in our local population when compared with many high mercury intake populations around the world. Despite the low mercury content of the seafood our population consumes, the mercury exposure level is still in excess of US EPA recommendations in a substantial proportion of children and women. Further, our study results show that estimated mercury intake is highly correlated with mercury exposure levels. In addition, mercury levels in fish oil supplements seem to be very low in the majority of brands and may serve as a viable method of supplementing polyunsaturated long chain fatty acids without increase mercury exposure. The high correlation between seafood intake and mercury exposure in our population suggests that dietary intervention may be a feasible way to reduce mercury exposure while maintaining dietary benefits of seafood consumption.

468411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
468411.value: We plan to perform a cross-sectional study to document the prevalence, lifestyle predisposition and bone health status for Vitamin-D(Vit-D) insufficiency among adolescents in Hong Kong. Vit-D plays a very important role in skeletal growth and bone mineralization for achieving normal peak bone mass to prevent osteoporosis and fractures in late adulthood. Vit-D deficiency (when serum 25(OH)Vit-D<25nmol/L) can result in rickets in children whereas Vit-D insufficiency is diagnosed when serum 25(OH)Vit-D lies between 25-50nmol/L. Although Vit-D insufficiency is very likely to affect skeletal health, the bone health status and evidence-based treatment of Vit-D insufficiency remain undefined. Since puberty is the time of rapid mineral accretion and our group has shown that low bone mass in adolescents could persist into adulthood, it is important to have a better understanding of Vit-D insufficiency, especially in adolescents, so as to provide the basis for planning evidence-based treatment and public health strategy for protection against Vit-D insufficiency. Prevalence studies in other countries found Vit-D insufficiency in 25-75% while our preliminary data on 46 normal adolescent girls revealed Vit-D insufficiency in 43.5% of subjects. Despite the likelihood that Vit-D insufficiency can be prevalent among our adolescents, to the best of our knowledge, no local study has been performed to document the situation and this potentially treatable condition remains under-recognized in Hong Kong. As for the bone health status in Vit-D insufficiency, previous studies gave inconsistent results. Most reports were confined to areal bone mineral density without separate evaluation of cortical and trabecular bone and its micro-architectures that are essential for accurate assessment of bone health. We therefore propose a cross-sectional study recruiting 600 normal adolescent boys and girls in summer. 25(OH)Vit-D assays, lifestyle questionnaires and high-resolution pQCT for assessing bone health status (including trabecular and cortical volumetric bone mineral densities and micro-architectures) will be performed. The prevalence of Vit-D insufficiency and its correlation with lifestyle factors and bone health status will be analyzed with control of confounders. One may argue that Hong Kong is a sub-tropical city with abundant sunshine and should be immune from Vit-D insufficiency. Our preliminary data strongly indicates the contrary may be true. A formal study looking into its prevalence, lifestyle predisposition and bone health status is highly important. The results can draw the long-awaited attention of the medical profession and public towards the importance of Vit-D and form the basis for further development of therapeutic and preventive strategies for Vit-D insufficiency.

468411.label: Realisation of objectives
468411.value: We are happy to report that achievement of all project objectives were completed as described below: Objective 1: 563 subjects (333 girls and 230 boys) were recruited indicating the prevalence of Vit-D insufficiency (25≤serum 25(OH)Vit-D≤50nmol/L) and Vit-D deficiency (serum 25(OH)Vit-D<25nmol/L) was 64.7% and 11.4% respectively. (Publication #2 [submitted, under review], Award #1 and #2, and the MPhil thesis) Objective 2: Lifestyle factors and attitudes towards sunlight and dietary intake and their correlation with Vit-D status were studied in details as depicted in Publication #3 [submitted, under review] and the MPhil thesis. Objective 3: Detailed analysis of bone health status in terms of bone density and bone quality and their correlation with Vit-D status were conducted as detailed in Publication #2, Award #1 and #2, and the MPhil thesis. Objective 4: Gender comparison on correlation patterns between Vit-D status and bone health parameters were studied and reported in Publication #2 and the MPhil thesis. Objective 5: We are grateful for permission to include appropriate subjects from another GRF project (Project no:468809) which is a case control study on AIS (adolescent idiopathic scoliosis) and non-AIS normal controls. Out of synergism from these two research projects, not only were more than 520 subjects successfully being recruited and studied, important findings on the bone health status in terms of bone density, bone quality and bone strength derived from advanced image and finite element analysis were accomplished resulting in a completed report corresponding to Publication #1 [published] and Award #3. The research outputs associated with this collateral result will also be included in this completion report.

468411.label: Major findings and research outcome
468411.value: 333 girls and 230 boys (12-16 years old) with normal health were recruited. Serum 25(OH)Vit-D levels, bone density and bone quality parameters, dietary calcium intakes and physical activity levels were assessed according to the protocol. 64.7% and 11.4% of subjects had Vit-D insufficiency [25≤25(OH)Vit-D≤50nmol/L] and Vit-D deficiency [25(OH)Vit-D<25nmol/L] respectively. The mean level of serum 25(OH)Vit-D in summer was significantly higher than that in winter (44.7±13.6 Vs 35.9±12.6nmol/L) without gender difference. In girls, areal bone mineral density (aBMD) and bone mineral content (BMC) of bilateral femoral necks, cortical area, cortical thickness, total volumetric BMD (vBMD) and trabecular thickness at non-dominant distal radius were significantly correlated with 25(OH)Vit-D levels. In boys, aBMD of bilateral femoral necks, BMC of dominant femoral neck, cortical area, cortical thickness, total vBMD, trabecular vBMD, BV/TV and trabecular separation at non-dominant distal radius were significantly correlated with 25(OH)Vit-D levels. (Publication #2, Award #1 and #2 and the MPhil thesis) In addition to bone health status, knowledge on Vit-D, lifestyle and sunlight exposure were evaluated for 361 subjects from the same cohort. Adolescents with Vit-D insufficiency had significantly lower physical activity level, and stayed indoor >4 hours at weekends. Moreover, they were not aware sunlight was a source of Vit-D, and provided less correct answers on the functions of Vit-D. They had less sunlight exposure in morning and late afternoon. Stepwise logistic regression showed performing sports activities, knowing sunlight as a source of Vit-D, and more sunlight exposure best explained 25(OH)Vit-D levels. (Publication #3 and the MPhil thesis) In summary, the results of this study provided strong evidences showing high prevalence of Vit-D insufficiency and inadequate knowledge on Vit-D and unfavourable lifestyles among adolescents in Hong Kong. Apart from the results related to Vit-D, novel findings on specific bone density and bone quality profiles that characterize AIS (adolescent idiopathic scoliosis) were also noted (Objective 5). In summary, AIS was associated with lower failure load and apparent modulus after adjusting for age. The association with lower apparent modulus persisted after adjusting for age, physical activity level and calcium intake. Further analysis indicated osteopenic AIS was associated with more rod-like trabeculae when compared with non-osteopenic AIS whereas such difference was not detected between osteopenic and non-osteopenic controls. These findings provided evidence on abnormal regulation and modulation of bone metabolism as well as bone modelling and remodeling in AIS. (Publication #1 and Award #3)

468411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
468411.value: Given the high prevalence of Vit-D insufficiency and inadequate knowledge on Vit-D and unfavourable lifestyles demonstrated among adolescents in Hong Kong, initiatives to address these clinically important and remediable health issues are warranted as follows: 1. Community-wide promotion exercises on normal Vit-D status and good bone health across all districts of Hong Kong SAR should be planned. 2. Various longitudinal studies and clinical trials to evaluate the effects of lifestyle modification, population-based food fortification with Vit-D or Vit-D supplementation on optimization of Vit-D status and achievement of good bone health should be conducted. 3. Given the association between AIS and suboptimal bone density and bone quality and that low bone mass is an independent and significant prognostic factor for curve progression in AIS, clinical trials to evaluate the therapeutic effects of Vit-D supplementation to optimize bone health and prevent curve progression in AIS are warranted.

468411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
468411.value: 563 healthy subjects (333 girls and 230 boys aged between 12-16 years old) were studied. Investigation with serum Vit-D assays indicated 76.1% had inadequate Vit-D levels. Scientific measurements of bone density and bone quality with advanced imaging techniques provided strong evidences on the association of suboptimal Vit-D status with poor bone health. Evaluation of knowledge on Vit-D, lifestyle and sunlight exposure indicated adolescents with Vit-D insufficiency had significantly lower physical activity levels, were not aware sunlight as a source of Vit-D and provided less correct answers on Vit-D functions. They had less sunlight exposure in morning and late afternoon. In brief, our research findings strongly indicated high prevalence of Vit-D insufficiency, inadequate knowledge on Vit-D and unfavourable lifestyles among adolescents in Hong Kong. The results of this study justify initiatives to increase awareness of the public especially the young population towards achievement of normal Vit-D status and good bone health by ways of knowledge transfer, lifestyle modification and other public health measures.

468711.label: Project Objectives
468711.value: To identify macrophage-myofibroblast transition (MMT) in human and experimental CKD and correlate this with progressive renal fibrosis. MMT cells will be identified by co-expression of α-SMA+ or collagen I with macrophage markers (e.g. a-SMA+CD68+CD11b+ and CD68+CD11b+collagen I+) in human kidney biopsies with different forms of CKD and in a mouse model of UUO by three-color confocal microscope and/or flow cytometry. MMT cells will be correlated with renal fibrosis and disease progression. To examine whether the transition of bone marrow-derived macrophages into myofibroblasts (MMT) is a major determinant of experimental renal fibrosis. The BMC origin of myofibroblasts in interstitial fibrosis of the UUO kidney will be determined using chimeric mice with GFP+ BM cells. The contribution of BM-derived MMT to renal tubulointerstitial fibrosis will be determined by BM depletion and adoptive transfer of GFP+ BMC and by conditional deletion of BM-derived macrophages using GFP-lysM-Cre/DTR BM chimeric mice. To determine whether TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling regulates MMT in vivo and in vitro. This will be studied in a mouse model of UUO using chimeric mice in which BMC are GFP+ and express with or without Smad3, and using adoptive transfer of GFP+ BMC that express or lack Smad3. In vitro studies of Smad3+ or Smad3- BMC under pathological conditions will enable identification of molecular mechanisms of TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling in the process of MMT.

468711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
468711.value: 肾脏纤维化是导致终末期肾病的标记和最后共同通路。 肌纤维母细胞（myofibroblasts) 是激活的成纤维细胞， 以高表达平滑肌动蛋白(a-SMA)为其标记，是公认致肾纤维化的主要细胞。 然而，其起源仍未清楚，是目前肾脏纤维化研究领域中的主要争论主题。目前认为，肌纤维母细胞起源于转化的上皮(EMT)或内皮细胞 ，是从血液中的fibrocytes或肾组织的pericytes来源。 但是，我们的初步研究发现，肾纤维化组织中的肌纤维母细胞是来源于骨髓巨噬细胞，并通过 macrophage-myofibroblast transition (MMT)转分化而来，在小老鼠阻塞性模型肾病(UUO)中占80%。此外，我们还发现MMT可能是由TGF-beta/Smad3信号所介导。因此，我们提出新的假说：骨髓巨噬细胞 (CD68+)-肌纤维母细胞 (a-SMA+)转分化(MMT)是肌纤维母细胞来源和肾纤维化的一条主要通路，并且由TGF-beta/Smad3信号所介导。我们将首先在病人和小老鼠阻塞性肾病（UUO）模型的肾纤维化组织中检测，辨认MMT （CD68+-SMA+)细胞，研究MMT与肾纤维化的关系。然后，应用荧光标记骨髓（GFP+ BMC）移植法，分别将Smad3+,Smad3-的GFP+ BMC移植至放射后（放射性弃除骨髓）小老鼠阻塞性模型肾病（UUO）中， 检测: 1)是否GFP+ BMC为肾纤维化组织中肌纤维母细胞 (GFP+a-SMA+) 的主要来源；2）是否骨髓巨噬细胞通过MMT转分化为肌纤维母细胞 （GFP+ CD68+SMA+)，是肌纤维母细胞来源和肾纤维化的主要通路；3）是否TGF-beta/Smad3介导 MMT. 另外， 我们将在巨噬细胞敲除小老鼠阻塞性肾病（UUO）模型中， 探索巨噬细胞敲除与MMT和肾纤维化的关系。通过本研究， 我们将得出：MMT是肌纤维母细胞和肾纤维化一条新颖和主要通路. TGF-beta/Smad3是介导MMT的一个关键机制。 这一新的重要发现将为肾脏纤维化提供新的理论证据和治疗方向。

468711.label: Realisation of objectives
468711.value: We have successfuly completed all 3 Specific Aims as originally proposed. We found that infiltrating macrophages are capable of becoming myofibroblasts as demonstrated by co-expressing CD68 and alpha-SMA antigens in both human and experimental CKD including chronic transplantation renal allograph rejection. This is important since the finding from this study is novel and identifies a new source of renal fibroblasts during renal fibrosis. We now term this process as macrophage-myofibroblast transition (MMT). By using updated macrophage lineage tracing techniques with adoptive transfer of GFP+ or dye-labelled macrophages, we reveaved that monocyte/macrophages from bone marrow can give rise to myofibroblasts via the process of MMT.The functional role of MMT in renal fibrosis was further confirmed by conditional deletion of bone marrow macrophages using GFP-lysM-Cre/DTR. We also extended our original proposal and performed a macrophage fate mapping study in LysM-Cre/Rosa 26-Tomota mice and identified 80% of MMT cells expressing Tomato gene during renal fibrosis. Furthermore, by generating GFP+Smad3 KO and GFP+ Smad3 WT BM chimeric mice, we showed that deletion of Smad3 gene from bone marrow macrophages is capable of preventing MMT and renal fibrosis in vivo and in vitro, identifying that MMT is mediated by TGF-beta/Smad3 pathway. These exciting findings have resulted in a successfully renewal of our CRF grant (CUHK3/CRF/12R) to study the role of MMT in other major end-organ diseases including chronic heart, lung, and liver diseases. We also develped new therapy by targeting the Smad3 signaling with a new Traditional Chinese Medicine compound which has also resulted in a patent filed (US 61/719,107; PCT/CN2013/086058; WO2014/063660). Role of TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling in renal fibrosis has been awarded for Ministry of Higher Education Outstanding Scientific Research Output Awards (2nd Class) in 2014. This proposal has also resulted in establishing a collaborative study with Zhejiang University to study MMT in chronic renal allograph rejection. With the support from this GRF, two PhD student (Zhang Yang) and postdoctoral fellow (Meng Xiao-ming) have been trained. Total of 14 publications are also generated as shown in the Part C.

468711.label: Major findings and research outcome
468711.value: 1. We have completed the studies as described in the Specific Aim 1 and found that infiltrating macrophages are capable of becoming myofibroblasts as demonstrated by co-expressing CD68 and a-SMA antigens in both human and experimental CKD including chronic transplantation renal allograph rejection. The finding is important and novel. We now term this process as macrophage-myofibroblast transition (MMT) with several high impact publications in Nature Review Nephrology [Part C:8-6], Kidney International [Part C 8-5], and Oncotargets [Part C 8-14]. Thus, MMT could be a key inflammatory process in renal fibrosis and may be a new therapeutic target for chronic kidney disease. 2. The Specific Aim 2 is to examine whether MMT cells are bone marrow cell origin and are a major determinant of renal fibrosis. By using GFP chimeric mice, we found that more than 90% of CD68+a-SMA+ MMT cells are highly expressing GFP, being bone marrow origin. Futhermore, macrophagel lineage tracing studies by adoptive transfer of GFP+ or dye-labelled macrophages identified that monocyte/macrophages from bone marrow can give rise to myofibroblasts via the process of MMT. The functional role of MMT in renal fibrosis was further confirmed by conditional deletion of bone marrow-derived macrophages using GFP-lysM-Cre/DTR. These data are under final analysis for publication. We also extended our original proposal and performed a fate mapping study in LysM-Cre/Rosa 26-Tomota mice. We identified that the more than 80% of MMT cells were highly expressing Tomato gene during renal fibrosis. This confirmative data will be submitted for publication soon. 3. The Specific Aim 3 is to determine whether TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling regulates MMT in vivo and in vitro. By using GFP+Smad3 KO and GFP+ Smad3 WT BM chimeric mice, we found that deletion of Smad3 gene from bone marrow macrophages is capable of preventing MMT and renal fibrosis in vivo and in vitro, identifying that MMT is mediated by TGF-beta/Smad3 pathway [Part C 8-14]. Targeting the Smad3 signaling with a new Traditional Chinese Medicine compound is capable of inhibiting renal fibrosis [Part C:8-10], which has resulted in a worldwide patent (US 61/719,107; PCT/CN2013/086058; WO2014/063660). Role of TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling in renal fibrosis has also resulted in The 2nd class Higher Education Outstanding Scientific Research Output Awards 2014 (see attached file-1) With the support from this GRF, we have recruited a PhD student (Zhang Yang) and postdoctoral fellow (Meng Xiao-ming). Total of 14 publications are also generated as shown in the Part C.

468711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
468711.value: Findins from this study have also resulted in successfully renewal of our CRF grant (CUHK3/CRF/12R) to study the role of MMT in other major end-organ diseases including chronic heart, lung, and liver diseases. We also propose that TGF-beta/Smad signaling may play a critical regulatory role in allograft rejection. This proposal has resulted in establishing a collaborative study with a renal transplantation team from Zhejiang University to study MMT in chronic renal allograph rejection. A Research Agreement between the Chinese University of Hong Kong and Zhejiang University on this project has been signed and research project is undergoing in the PI Lab in CUHK. Our ultimate goal is to establish MMT as a major source of myofibroblast origin during tissue scarring and is a key process from inflammation to fibrosis in many chronic disease. Thus, targeting MMT may be a new therapeutic target for renal fibrosis.

468711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
468711.value: Fibroblasts are the key cell type causing renal scar, which is a final common pathway leading to kidney failure. However, anti-fibrosis treatment remains non-specific and ineffective due to the unknown origins of these scar-producing cells. In this study, we found that infiltrating macrophages are capable of becoming collagen-producing fibroblasts in human and experimental chronic kidney disease including chronic transplantation renal allograph rejection. This finding is a new and important and we now term this process as macrophage-myofibroblast transition (MMT). By using updated cell tracing techniques, we identified that MMT cells originate from bone marrow and is caused by TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling. We also found that targeting this pathway is capable of inhibiting renal fibrosis. Thus, results from this study are highly significant both scientifically and clinically and may result in a novel and specific therapy for chronic kidney disease.

468811.label: Project Title(Chinese)
468811.value: 香港學童學校室內空氣污染與健康效應研究

468811.label: Project Objectives
468811.value: To provide systematic data on indoor air quality, pollutants, and allergens in a representative sample of Hong Kong primary schools. Scientific data are essential to develop relevant methods and policy to achieve and then maintain good air quality in the schools. To address this objective, we will randomly select 30 primary schools in Hong Kong, where we will measure indoor pollutants (microbial agents, chemical agents, and particulate matter). Data on micro-environmental meteorological factors associated with pollutant levels will also be collected. Finally, data about the physical characteristics of the school buildings and classrooms, as well as the children’s activities, will be collected through an onsite inspection and questionnaires. To evaluate the impact of the indoor air pollutants in the school environment on the prevalence of respiratory disorders. A health survey will be conducted on students in the sampled classrooms. The students will receive a health examination and be required to complete a detailed questionnaire. The health examination will include measurements of anthropometric parameters and pulmonary function. Data on asthmatic and other respiratory symptoms, respiratory diseases, and medication history will be collected by means of the questionnaire. Important factors associated with indoor air quality at home, as well as the socio-economic status and life style, will also be documented. The air quality and health data will be analyzed by the appropriate statistical methods to assess the health impact of indoor air quality in the school environment. To create a cohort to assess the long-term health effects of poor air quality in school children. Poor air quality is possibly associated with some long-term health effects in children, such as the development of lung function and the onset of some respiratory diseases. It is unlikely to be able to assess these health effects only by a cross-sectional study. The cross-sectional data collected in the proposed study will become the baseline for facilitating future investigations into these health effects. Additional funds will be sought to monitor the participants in the coming 2 or 3 years to investigate the impact of poor air quality on the development of lung function, upper respiratory tract infections (URTI), and newly acquired illnesses such as asthma, wheezing, and flu-like illnesses (FLI).

468811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
468811.value: Aim The aim of the project is to conduct research into characterizing the indoor air quality in primary schools in Hong Kong and to investigate the health effects of poor air quality on the children. Project Background Children typically spend around 6 to 8 hours per day in the school environment, second only to time they spend indoors at home. Poor school indoor air quality may cause short- and long-term health problems and aggravate asthma and respiratory diseases, increasing students’ absenteeism and affecting their performance. However, there is limited information on the health effects of indoor air quality in school environments worldwide. Most previous studies mainly focused on one single pollutant and did not evaluate health effects. In Hong Kong, to date, there are no systematic data on school indoor air quality and its health effects. On the other hand, Hong Kong has many unique characteristics that are closely related to air pollution, such as a tropical climate, a high population density, and tall buildings surrounding by narrow roads with heavy traffic. Preliminary data have revealed an unfavorable sign for indoor air quality in the Hong Kong school environment. Brief Project Description We have been investigating air pollution and health effects and have focused on ambient air pollution and air pollution in the workplace. In this project, we plan to extend our research in a representative sample of primary schools in Hong Kong. Specifically, we intend to: (1) characterize the indoor air quality by measuring the criteria pollutants and microbial agents, as well as inspecting the characteristics of the buildings; and (2) assess the health effects of poor air quality on the school children by conducting a health survey. Significance of Project Approximately 345,000 schoolchildren spend their daytime hours at 582 primary schools in Hong Kong. School indoor air quality is particularly important as a public health issue because children are more susceptible than adults to air pollutants. We expect that the results from the proposed study will enhance our knowledge about indoor exposure to microbial and chemical agents in schools, as well as the associated health effects. The scientific data will facilitate the development of effective policies to achieve and then sustain good indoor air quality in Hong Kong school buildings. The cross-sectional data collected in the proposed study will become the baseline for future investigation into long-term health effects. 目的 對香港小學室內空氣狀況進行調查並研究空氣品質對學童的健康影響。 背景 學生通常每天在學校學習生活約6至8個小時，在校園的時間僅少於在家的時間。校園空氣品質可以對學童造成長期和短期的健康影響、加重哮喘與其它呼吸疾病的病情，導致曠課或影響學童成績。但目前世界上關於校園空氣品質與學童健康影響的研究很少。以前的研究主要集中在單一的污染物，而且很少調查其造成的健康效應。目前在香港尚未有系統的關於校園空氣質量數據以及空氣品質與健康效應關係的資料。此外，香港是一個獨特的城市，有許多與空氣品質相關的特點，比如密集的人口與建築，狹小的道路伴隨繁忙的交通。以前一些初步的資料也顯示香港校園的空氣品質在某些指標上並不樂觀。 項目描述 我們計畫對香港小學進行抽樣從而獲得一個代表性的樣本，並調查香港小學的空氣品質狀況。我們計畫：1）通過檢測和檢驗，確定典型的化學與微生物污染物水準，並調查建築物特徵與污染物水準關係。2）調查空氣品質狀況對學童身體健康的影響。 重要性 目前香港有582間小學，在校小學生345,000名。校園空氣品質是一個重要的公共衛生議題。與成年人相比較，空氣品質對學童的影響特別敏感和重要。我們期望本研究能增進我們對校園空氣化學與微生物污染物水準的瞭解，並認識學童健康與這些空氣污染物的關係。這些資料將有利於決策者制定校園空氣政策，從而改進並持續保持好的空氣品質。此外，本研究可以作為基礎資料，以方便將來研究空氣品質對健康的長期效應。

468811.label: Realisation of objectives
468811.value: There were a total of three objectives in the present project and we have achieved all of them: 1. The first objective is to provide systematic data on indoor air quality, pollutants, and allergens in a representative sample of Hong Kong primary schools. During the implementation of the project, we randomly selected a representative sample of schools throughout Hong Kong and conducted air quality assessment for the schools. To address seasonal variation, we conducted two air quality assessment twice for each school. One was in the cool season and the other in the warm season. The pollutants measured include particulate matter (PM) of different sizes (PM10, PM2.5 and PM1), NOx, SO2, O3, CO, CO2, formaldehyde (HCHO), total volatile organic compounds (TVOC), and bio-aerosols (total bacteria and fungi count). Therefore, we have obtained systematic data on indoor air quality, pollutants, and allergens for Hong Kong primary schools. 2. The second objective is to assess the impact of the indoor air pollutants in the school environment on the prevalence of respiratory disorders. During the implementation of the project, we recruited 100 to 150 grade 2 or 3 students from each selected schools. Each student received a health examination, including measures of anthropometric parameters and pulmonary function. Parents were required to complete a detailed questionnaire covering a wide range of topics, such as respiratory health, socio-economic status, lifestyle, and disease history. We conducted data analyses and found that generally the prevalence of respiratory disease and symptoms were higher among the students from the schools with poorer air quality. Students studying in schools with poorer air quality generally had lower level of pulmonary function. 3. The third objective is to create a cohort to assess the long-term health effects of poor air quality in school children. During the implementation of the project, we recruited more than 2500 students. Therefore, we used the recruited 2500 students to establish a cohort. we successfully obtained funding from other sources and now we are following up the 2500 students to assess the long-term health effects of poor air quality in these 2500 students.

468811.label: Major findings and research outcome
468811.value: 1. Students in classroom facing the roadway are exposing to significantly higher air pollutants than those in classrooms sheltered from the roadways. 2. Children are often exposed to freshly emitted air pollutants generated by school buses during the morning drop off hours (7-8am). The findings 1 and 2 above were presented in the conference entitled “The fourth international Workshop on Regioinal Air Quality Management in Rapidly Developing Economic Regions” on January 14-17, 2014. 3. Higher level of bacterial bioaerosol in school environment is negatively associated with pulmonary function, especially for parameters PEF and MMEF, which are sensitive indicators for small airway function. This finding was presented in the 26th Annual International Society for Environmental Epidemiology Conference. The conference was held on the University of Washington campus in Seattle, Washington, USA on August 24-28th, 2014. 4. Exposure to cleaning products may be associated with lower pulmonary function in Hong Kong school children. This finding was presented in the 26th Annual International Society for Environmental Epidemiology Conference. The conference was held on the University of Washington campus in Seattle, Washington, USA on August 24-28th, 2014. 5. Frequent use of cleaning products at home is associated with rhinitis in primary school children. This finding was presented in the conference entitled “HKCCM Annual Scientific Meeting (ASM) 2015 ” in September, 2015 in Hong Kong. A manuscript about this finding has been submitted to a prestigious international journal “Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology”, and it is under second review 6. A diet with most of potato, butter and fast food is associated with an increased risk of rhinitis and wheezing in Hong Kong school children. A manuscript about this finding has been drafted and it is under internal review.

468811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
468811.value: One of the objectives of the present project is to create a cohort to assess the long-term health effects of poor air quality in school children. Therefore we will continue to seek for funding to follow up the students recruited in the present project and investigate the long-term health effects of poor air quality.

468811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
468811.value: The aim of the project is to conduct research into characterizing the air quality in primary schools in Hong Kong and to investigate the health effects of poor air quality on the children. The successful implementation of the present project has provided a profile of air quality in a representative primary school sample in Hong Kong. The results from the present project significantly enhance our knowledge about exposure to microbial and chemical agents in school environment. The relationship between school environment air quality and the health of the students has been assessed. Generally negative relationships were observed. The present project also created a cohort which enables us to investigate the long-term health effects of poor air quality in school children. The information arise from the study will facilitate the development of effective policies to achieve and then sustain good indoor air quality in Hong Kong school buildings.

469211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
469211.value: Medulloblastoma (MB) is the most common children brain cancer. Although 60-80% of the patients achieve a 5-year survival, the survivors suffer a number of treatment-related sequelae. Development of effective target-specific treatments with low toxicity is urgently needed. Our group has been focusing on deciphering the MB genome. With previous funding supports from UGC, we identified specific genetic and epigenetic alterations in MB shedding light into MB oncogenesis and leading to identification of molecular target candidates for drug developments. Our preliminary data revealed a frequent genomic gain at 6p21.22-p21.31 harboring HMGA1 that was over-expressed in MB and associated with poor clinical outcomes. Functional characterizations of HMGA1 by siRNA knockdown indicated the controls of HMGA1 in MB cell growth, migration, and invasion, suggesting that deregulation of these controls by HMGA1over-expression could contribute to MB oncogenesis. Exploration of molecular basis of these controls showed a positive relationship of HMGA1 with a cell cycle regulator cdc25A and an inverse relationship with an invasion-suppressor CRMP1 through direct interactions of HMGA1 onto their promoters for transcriptional regulations. Exact significances of cdc25A and CRMP1 in the HMGA1-mediated controls of MB oncogenicity and underlying mechanisms remain to be determined. Small molecule minor groove binding (MGB) drugs showed disruption of HMGA1–binding onto the target promoters resulting in blocking the expression. During bacterial infection in a murine model, the drugs showed survival benefits through blockades of the HMGA1-mediated target expression. Usages of MGB drugs in MB patients that the tumors frequently over-express HMGA1 remain unexplored. In this proposal, we aim to 1) determine the biological significances of HMGA1 in MB cell lines and intracranial MB xenografts regarding the controls of oncogenicity; 2) determine the involvements of cdc25A and CRMP1 in the HMGA1-mediated controls and the mechanisms for regulation of their expressions by HMGA1; and 3) explore the usages of MGB drugs to control MB oncogenicity and elucidate the molecular basis of the drug effects. We envisage results obtained from this project could enhance our understandings on the MB biology and the oncogenic properties of HMGA1 and its downstream targets involved in the disease. Importantly, the results support developments of future MB therapy exploiting HMGA1 as a therapeutic target and lay an essential foundation for novel usages of MGB drugs in MB patients. Hopefully, it may cure the disease in more patients alone or together with a regimen of reduced adjuvant therapy to ameliorate long-term adverse effects while maintaining cure rates. 髓母細胞瘤是最常見的兒童腦腫瘤。雖然病人的五年生存率有60-80%，但治療帶來的後遺症是相當痛苦的。因此，發展低毒性的有效和特異的靶向治療藥物成為迫切的需要。我們研究組已經致力於對髓母細胞瘤基因組的分析。在UCG資助下，我們已經鑒定了髓母細胞瘤的一些特異的遺傳學和表遺傳學改變。這些研究成果展示了髓母細胞瘤的腫瘤形成機制，並且為發展和篩選靶向治療藥物提供了依據。 我們之前的研究結果鑒定了在染色體6p21.22-p21.31存在HMGA1基因。這個基因在髓母細胞瘤過度表達並提示差的臨床預後。採用siRNA基因下調抑制的方法對HMGA1的功能分析提示，HMGA1的調控因子能調控細胞的生長，遷移和侵襲，提示HMGA1的過度表達可能與髓母細胞瘤的發生有關。分析這些調控因子的分子基礎，通過HMGA1對基因啟動子轉錄調節的直接作用，揭示了HMGA1與細胞循環調節因子cdc25A呈現正相關性，而與侵襲抑制因子CRMP1呈現負相關性。然而，cdc25A 和 CRMP1 在HMGA1介導的髓母細胞瘤發生的精確原理和潛在機制尚未清楚。 小分子的小溝結合物(MGB)藥物有阻止HMGA1作用于靶基因啟動子，從而導致基因表達的抑制。通過老鼠模型的細菌感染，這種藥物通過阻斷HMGA1的靶向介導表達，顯示了較好的生存率。然而，MGB藥物應用在HMGA1過度表達的髓母細胞瘤病人仍需要探討。 在本研究計畫，我們的目標是：第一，鑒定HMGA1在髓母細胞瘤細胞株和裸鼠顱內移植的人髓母細胞瘤異種移植物的有關腫瘤發生的生物學特徵。第二，鑒定cdc25A 和 CRMP1參與HMGA1介導的調控因子和它們通過HMGA1調節表達的機制。第三，探索MGB藥物在控制髓母細胞瘤的應用和闡明這個藥物作用的分子機制。 我們期待這項研究成果能增進對髓母細胞瘤生物學行為的瞭解，對HMGA1的致瘤機制和它下游靶分子對疾病影響的理解。重要的是，這項研究結果可支援發展未來的髓母細胞瘤治療，開拓HMGA1作為一種靶向治療，並且作為MGB藥物最新應用在髓母細胞瘤病人時的基本根據。展望這種治療能單獨或合併其它輔助治療可以治癒更多病人，並減低併發症，長期改善治療的副作用，提高治癒率。

469211.label: Realisation of objectives
469211.value: In this project, objective 1 is partially achieved. The biological significances of HMGA1 in medulloblastoma (MB) have been characterized through gain- and loss-of-function studies. In vitro assays revealed that depletion of HMGA1 in MB by gene-specific siRNA led to suppression in anchorage-dependent and –independent growth, induction of apoptosis, upregulation of cleaved PARP, inhibition in migration and invasion, and reduction in filopodial and intense stress fibers formation. In contrast, overexpression of HMGA1 resulted in increased cell growth, and migration and invasion potential. We attempted to elucidate the effects of HMGA1 knockdown on growth of intracranial MB xenografts using inducible system. Although we constructed a plasmid contained HMGA1-complementary shRNA oligonucleotides, we failed to establish stable clones with depletion of HMGA1 upon doxycycline treatment. Objective 2 of this project is fully achieved. We identified two downstream targets (cdc25A and CRMP1) of HMGA1 in controls of MB cell growth, migration and invasion through combination of expression array, bioinformatics software, qRT-PCR, and western blot analysis. We confirmed that HMGA1 directly interacted with the promoters of cdc25A and CRMP1 by EMSA and ChIP assays. We employed luciferase reporter assay to illustrate the role of HMGA1 in regulating transcriptional activity of target genes. Rescue experiment was conducted to show that HMGA1 mediated MB cell growth through regulation of cdc25A expression. And, stable cell clones overexpressing CRMP1 were established and examined for its functional role in cell growth, migration and invasion and filopodia and intense stress fibers formation. Lastly, correlation between HMGA1 and target genes was illustrated in clinical samples. For objective 3, we postulated that minor groove binding (MGB) drug, netropsin, is able to compete with HMGA1 binding on the promoters of downstream targets. Thus, we aimed to explore the potential usage of netropsin in MB therapy and studied the effects of netropsin on cell growth and binding to promoter of target gene. To achieve this objective, we employed MTT assay to demonstrate a dose-dependent growth inhibition of netropsin. By IVIS imaging system, we showed netropsin inhibited the growth of intracranial MB xenografts in nude mice. Lastly, mRNA level and promoter activity of target genes were examined in netropsin treated cells to show the biological effects were contributed to the reduction of transcription level and transcriptional activity of HMGA1 target genes.
