469211.label: Major findings and research outcome
469211.value: We showed upregulation of HMGA1 mRNA and protein in >80% of primary MB samples. Increased HMGA1 expression was associated with shorter overall survival. Knockdown of HMGA1 by gene-specific siRNA significantly inhibited anchorage-dependent and –independent MB cell growth, migration and invasion, and formation of filopodia and intense stress fiber. Depletion of HMGA1 resulted in increased sub-G0/G1 cell population and cleaved PARP abundance, suggesting induction of apoptosis. On the contrary, overexpression of HMGA1 increased cell growth, and migration and invasion capacities (Lau et al. 2012). By transcriptome analysis, we identified 17 upregulated and 36 downregulated genes in HMGA1-depleted cells. We further showed cdc25A is a downstream target of HMGA1. It directly regulated cdc25A expression by physically binding to the predicted binding sites at nucleotide -959 to nucleotide -851 of cdc25A promoter. Expression of cdc25A was upregulated in >80% primary MB, and its expression was significantly correlated with HMGA1. Functional characterization indicated cdc25A expression abolished the inhibitory effect of HMGA1-depleted cells. Taken together, upregulation of HMGA1 led to an increased cdc25A expression contributing to the loss of cell growth (Lau et al. 2012). We also identified CRMP1 as another downstream target of HMGA1. HMGA1 expression was inversely correlated with CRMP1 expression in primary tumors and MB retrieved from public database. Reduced CRMP1 expression was found in 38% MB and 100% MB cell lines. Interestingly, Group 3 MB, which is frequently showed metastasis, exhibited prominently downregulation of CRMP1. Furthermore, we showed that HMGA1 negatively regulated CRMP1 expression through physical interaction onto the putative binding sites at nucleotide -2378 to nucleotide -1981 of CRMP1 promoter. Stably CRMP1 expressed cells displayed reduced cell proliferation, migration and invasion and formation of filopodia and stress intense fiber. The results suggested that HMGA1 mediated MB cell growth and metastatic potential through regulation of CRMP1 (Li et al. 2015; Li et al. 2013; SNO 2015). Lastly, we showed minor groove binding drug, netropsin, was able to mimic the effects of knockdown HMGA1 in MB cells. In vitro, treatment of netropsin resulted in suppression of cell growth of MB in a dose-dependent manner. In vivo, netropsin administration to intracranial xenografts led to reduction in tumor growth without high toxicity. Importantly, expression and promoter activity of cdc25A were suppressed in netropsin-treated cells. These results suggested netropsin might compete with HMGA1 to affect regulation of downstream target, and netropsin might be a potential treatment drug for MB (Lau et al. 2012).

469211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
469211.value: In this project, we succeed in the identification of HMGA1 downstream targets by multiple experiments, including global gene expression array, quantitative RT-PCR, western blot analysis, electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA), chromatin immunoprecipitation assay (ChIP), and promoter activity assay. The established assays could be employed for identification of target genes in our coming funded National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC) project. In addition, there are few potential target genes of HMGA1 identified from transcriptome analysis required to be confirmed and their functional significances in MB remained to be elucidated. The results would reveal the comprehensive roles of HMGA1 in MB tumorigenesis.

469211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
469211.value: Medulloblastoma (MB) is the most common pediatric brain cancer. Although advancement in multimodal therapies has increased the 5-year survival rate to 60-80%, majority of survivors suffer from long-term neurocognitive and neuroendocrine complication as a result of aggressive therapy. Thus, improvement in our understanding of molecular mechanism underlying medulloblastoma pathogenesis is urgently needed in order to develop effective target therapy with low toxicity. In this study, we showed that dysregulation of HMGA1 involved in controls of MB cell growth and metastatic capacity. Importantly, HMGA1 expression is restricted to MB cells, suggesting that HMGA1 is a potential effective target for MB therapy. Furthermore, we applied multiple experimental approaches and identified two novel direct downstream targets of HMGA1 (cdc25A and CRMP1) that contributed to the ability of HMGA1 to drive MB cell growth and metastasis. And, we demonstrated the functional significance of the two targets in MB biology. Taken together, we developed strategies facilitating the identification of direct target genes in future study. The novel findings in this study would facilitate drug development to combat MB.

469411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
469411.value: Vitamin D, often known as the “sunshine vitamin”, is essential for optimal health. A low level of Vitamin D (due to inadequate exposure to sunlight from sedentary lifestyle and rapid urbanization, and a low Vitamin D-rich Chinese diet) has become a major public health problem in Hong Kong. There has been great interest in the associations between inadequate vitamin D levels, vitamin D supplementation and chronic pain conditions. Despite a high prevalence of inadequate vitamin D levels in the Hong Kong Chinese population aged 50 years or above (63%), vitamin D levels are rarely checked before surgery. With an aging population both worldwide and in Hong Kong, the frequency of joint replacement surgery continues to increase. In patients undergoing joint replacement surgery, little is known about the role of vitamin D on acute pain management, recovery and its impact on health-related quality of life. This prospective cohort of 245 patients undergoing total knee or hip replacement surgery will determine (1) the prevalence of vitamin D inadequacy (serum total 25- hydroxyl-vitamin D less than 80nmol/l) before surgery; (2) the association between preoperative vitamin D inadequacy and opioid analgesia-related outcomes; and (3) the association between preoperative vitamin D inadequacy and the level of postoperative recovery and health-related quality of life at 3 months. Patient outcome data to be collected include multidimensional measures of the overall benefit of analgesia, quality of recovery and health-related quality of life, using validated and reliable questionnaires during the perioperative period and at 3 months follow-up. The results of the study will be of great significance in planning effective patient education initiatives and designing clinical trials on the effectiveness of vitamin D supplementation before surgery to improve clinical and patient-centered outcomes for patients undergoing joint replacement surgery. 經常被稱為「陽光維他命」的維他命D是保持身體健康的必需要素。由於香港迅速發展，長時間缺少陽光的室內生活和進食低維他命D含量的中式飲食，使體內維他命D的水平降低，這個情况已成為公共健康的問題。維他命D不足、維他命D的補充與慢性疼痛這三者之間的關係也引起極大的關注。縱使年齡超過50歲的香港華人普遍有維他命D水平不足的狀況(63%)，但手術前為病人檢查維他命D的水平極不普遍。全球包括香港的人口正在老化，關節置換手術的次數正在不斷增加。在這類接受關節置換手術的患者中，有關維他命D在急性疼痛處理、手術後康復，及其對健康相關的生活質素之影響知之甚少。這項前瞻性隊列研究將會在245位接受全膝關節置換或全髖關節置換手術患者中試找出相關的聯繫： 1. 手術前維他命D不足的普遍程度 (血清 25-羥基維生素D少於80mmol/L); 2. 手術前維他命D不足和使用鴉片類止痛藥之有關效果; 3. 手術前維他命D不足和手術後的康復及3個月後與健康有關的生活質素。 在手術前和手術後3個月，我們會用可靠和已驗証的問卷收集幾項數據；如止痛藥的成效，復康的質素以及與健康有關的生活質素的結果。這項研究結果將有很大的意義。它有助規劃病人在進行關節置換手術前以病人為中心的教育活動和設計臨床試驗維他命D的補充成效，因而改善臨床的結果。

469411.label: Realisation of objectives
469411.value: While consecutive knee and hip arthroplasty patients were recruited into the prospective cohort study, we had not anticipated the profound effects of different prevalence rates of osteoarthritis and location of joints between ethnic groups. Chinese patients are more likely to have radiographic and symptomatic knee osteoarthritis than hip osteoarthritis compared to Caucasians (Nevitt et al. 2002). The main limitation of the study was that the majority of our patients (87%) underwent knee arthroplasty within the time allowed for the grant and there were brief periods of elective joint replacement surgery cancellations occurring from bed shortage during the influenza surge that affected the patient recruitment rate. We did not extend the study to recruit more patients undergoing hip arthroplasty as the agreed license for the number of patients approved to use the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities (WOMAC) osteoarthritis index questionnaires was set at 245. When we tried to report both knee and hip arthroplasty results in journal manuscripts, external peer-reviewers consistently recommended that only the knee arthroplasty results should be published. Therefore, while all the study objectives have been achieved during the conduct of this study, we underachieved in publishing the results. At the time of completion report submission, our article: Lee A, Chan SKC, Samy W, Chiu CH, Gin T. Effect of hypovitaminosis D on postoperative pain outcomes and short-term health-related quality of life after joint arthroplasty: a cohort study. Medicine (in press) is due to be published in the coming weeks. Corrected proofs are attached to this report. 469411.label: Major findings and research outcome
469411.value: In a cohort study of 191 consecutive patients undergoing 214 knee arthroplasty, the prevalence of hypovitaminosis D (<50 nmol/l 25-OHD) was 44% (95% CI: 37% to 51%); preoperative prevalence of mild hypovitaminosis D (30-49 nmol/l 25-OHD) was more frequent than moderate to severe (<30 nmol/l 25-OHD) hypovitaminosis D (36.4% versus 7.5%) (Lee 2015). In 25 consecutive patients (31 staged bilateral hip arthroplasty), the prevalence of hypovitaminosis D was 48.4% (95% CI: 30.2% to 66.9%). In the preliminary final results presented at the Singapore conference on the 245 elective knee or hip arthroplasty, we used mixed-effects regression model to explore vitamin D status groups and pain intensity scores in the first 72 hours after surgery (Lee 2014). The adjusted mean pain score [95% CI] on ward arrival was higher in the moderate to severe deficiency group by 1.3 [0.4–2.1] compared to the sufficient vitamin D group (P<0.01) but there was no overall difference in pain scores between sufficient vitamin D (3.3 [3.2–3.5]), mild deficiency (3.2 [2.9–3.4]) and moderate to severe deficiency (3.4 [2.9–3.9]) groups (P=0.50). In the final analysis in knee arthroplasty patients (Lee 2015), there were transient higher postoperative pain intensity scores in the moderate to severe hypovitaminosis D (25-OHD < 30nmol/l) group compared to the sufficient vitamin D group in the first three days. The subtotal and overall WOMAC index scores were calculated and transformed to range from 0 to 100, with higher scores indicating better health status. Vitamin D status had no effect on total WOMAC index (P = 0.22), WOMAC pain (P=0.97) and stiffness (P=0.56) subscales at three months after surgery. The effect of vitamin D status groups on WOMAC function was marginally significant (P = 0.07); preoperative WOMAC function was lowest in the moderate to severe hypovitaminosis D group compared to the sufficient vitamin D group (MD -13.1, 95% CI: -24.1 to -2.0) but was associated with the largest improvements over time (Lee 2015). The incidence of moderate to severe persistent pain was 9% (95% CI: 6% to 14%) in knee arthroplasty patients (Lee 2015). Hypovitaminosis D increased the risk of moderate to severe persistent pain (adjusted odds ratio 2.64, 95% CI: 1.03 to 6.77) adjusting for age, gender, obesity, type of anesthesia, preoperative moderate to severe pain and season (Lee 2015).

469411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
469411.value: We are currently revising a manuscript on the determinants of serum 25-OHD concentration in patients undergoing joint arthroplasty as there is a paucity of data in this population, which may be different from the general population. An understanding of the relative contributions of factors associated with preoperative serum 25-OHD concentration may be useful in developing local strategies to optimize 25-OHD level given that our study has found evidence supporting suboptimal 25-OHD concentration to be a risk factor for developing moderate to severe persistent pain after knee arthroplasty. Using causal mediation modelling, we wish to explore the role of hypovitaminosis D, obesity and persistent pain using the collected data. At present, the direction of the association between hypovitaminosis D and obesity is contentious. Obesity is a known risk factor for persistent pain after arthroplasty. If obesity is a significant mediator, this has implications for preoperative management. The results will be published in a peer-review journal.

469411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
469411.value: Vitamin D, often known as the “sunshine vitamin”, is essential for optimal health. A low level of Vitamin D (due to inadequate exposure to sunlight from sedentary lifestyle and rapid urbanization, and a low Vitamin D-enrich Chinese diet) is rarely checked before surgery. With an aging population both worldwide and in Hong Kong, the frequency of joint replacement surgery continues to increase. Little is known about the role of vitamin D on acute pain management, recovery and its impact on health-related quality of life. This prospective cohort of patients undergoing 245 knee or hip replacement surgery showed that one in two had vitamin inadequacy (serum total 25-hydroxyl-vitamin D less than 50 nmol/l) before surgery. Vitamin D inadequacy had subtle effects on pain intensity scores after surgery but there was no effect on health-related quality of life at 3 months. However, patients with vitamin D inadequacy before surgery were three times more likely to have moderate to severe chronic pain after surgery than those with normal Vitamin D levels. As there were few patients undergoing hip replacement surgery in this study, the results described above for pain outcomes and health-related quality of life apply only to patients undergoing knee replacement surgery.

469711.label: Project Objectives
469711.value: • To identify novel lncRNA candidates responsible for cellular differentiation and proliferation in mouse male germ cell development. Based on the preliminary data from SAGE analysis of a mouse male germ cell transcriptome, we have identified potential lncRNA candidates that demonstrate stage-specific expression. Our working hypothesis is that a subset of lncRNA species is critical to cellular differentiation in male germ cell development. We will design an efficient bioinformatic pipeline to identify potential lncRNAs by integrating recent genomic criteria and expression evidence from tiling microarray data. The shortlisted candidate will then be validated by in vitro and in vivo assays. • To determine signaling pathways and key regulators that govern lncRNA regulation. We postulate from our preliminary data that lncRNA is regulated by specific signaling pathways or key regulators. Here we will predict the lncRNA regulation-based supervised and unsupervised approaches. Firstly, we will apply our recent vitamin A deficient (VAD) study to evaluate the possible functional involvement of lncRNA by retinoic-acid dependent pathways. We will also examine other possible regulatory pathways or regulators in lncRNA regulation based on genomic evidence (unsupervised), such as promoter configuration, epigenetic regulations by DNA methylation or histone modification. A systems biology approach using de novo and knowledge-based gene network analysis will be applied to delineate novel signaling pathways for lncRNA regulation. • To establish a public germ cell lncRNA genomic database to facilitate genome-wide understanding of lncRNA regulation and promote international collaboration. To better understand the genomic features of identified lncRNA candidates, a novel lncRNA database devoted to germ cell development will be constructed. The database will allow mining and annotating functional/predicted lncRNA candidates. It will be also act as the central portal for international scientists to exchange ideas and encourage collaboration. This will further consolidate sour niche in lncRNA research and promote Hong Kong’s leading role in biomedical research.

469711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
469711.value: Aim: The aim of this project is to identify and delineate the functional regulation of long non-coding RNAs in male germ cell development. Project Background: Male factor accounts for at least 40% of infertility cases. A large number of cases are attributed to a failure of spermatogenesis, a complex developmental process that gives rise to mature spermatozoa (sperm). It not only provides an excellent model for studying male reproductive biology, but also for cellular differentiation and proliferation. The dysregulation of these two fundamental yet critical developmental processes is the basis for many disorders. Despite advances in genomics and molecular biology, previous attempts to delineate the developmental programs in spermatogenesis have had limited successes. This is largely because the focus is limited to protein-coding genes. Recent study suggested they only account for about 10% of the human genome. A significant portion of genome actually encodes many transcripts known as non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) of unknown functions. They were previously considered to be “junk”, but recent research has shown that they have various biological functions. Long ncRNAs (lncRNAs) are generally classified as ncRNAs with more than 200 base pairs. They have been recently demonstrated to involve in developmental regulations in stem cell, brain and cancer. The lncRNA candidates and its functional importance in male germ cell development are not known. Brief Project Description: Our central hypothesis in this study is a subset of lncRNAs of unknown function is required in various developmental processes in spermatogenesis. Our hypothesis has been formulated based on the preliminary data from a genomic assay called Serial Analysis of Gene Expression (SAGE), where we identified functional lncRNA Spga-lncRNA1/2 that regulate in cellular differentiation. Based on this promising result, we aim to apply comprehensive approaches to identify and delineate the functional regulation of novel lncRNAs in male germ cell development. The data will be deposited in a publicly available database (GermlncRNA), which serves as a portal for lncRNA data analysis and allows exchanging ideas through discussions and collaborations. Significance of the Project: The findings are expected to substantially change the concepts in developmental and cancer biology, which could lead to the development of novel therapeutic strategies. The research proposed in this application is also innovative because it provides a new and substantially different approach in addressing developmental mechanisms in spermatogenesis through identifying novel lncRNA-dependent regulations. 目的 這個項目的目的是識別和劃分長非編碼 RNA的雄性生殖細胞的發育功能調節。 項目背景 男性佔不孕症病例不少於百分之四十。大部份原因是精子發育過程發生問題。精子發育過程不但為男性生殖生物學提供一個很好的研究模型，它也為細胞分化和增殖過程提供研究模型。這兩個基本但重要的發育過程是許多疾病的基礎。儘管基因組學和分子生物學的進步，人們對精子發育過程解構仍然不成功。這主要是因為研究重點大多偏於研究蛋白質的編碼基因。最近研究表明蛋白質的編碼基因只佔人類基因組約百分之十。大部份基因組編碼的部分實際上是未知功能的非編碼 RNA。它們以前被認為是“垃圾”。但最近研究發現它們有多種生物學功能。 長非編碼 RNA（lncRNAs），一般定義為大於二百多個鹼基。他們最近已被證實涉及幹細胞，腦和癌症的發展，但對雄性生殖細胞的發育功能仍不清楚。 項目內容簡介 我們的研究假設是精子發育過程需要一些未知功能的lncRNA 完成 。我們的假設是基於基因表達系列分析（SAGE）的初步數據，我們發現 SPGA - lncRNA1 / 2 有調節細胞分化功能。在此基礎上，我們的目標是用綜合方法來確定和劃分的新型lncRNAs在雄性生殖細胞功能調節的發展功能。這些數據將被存放在一個公開的數據庫（GermlncRNA），它作為一個 lncRNA數據分析門戶網站，並允許討論和合作交流。 該項目的意義 調查結果預計將大幅改變發育和癌症生物學概念，有望發展新的治療策略。此項目富有創新性，因為是通過不同的方法去識別新lncRNA相關法規來處理精子發育機制問題。

469711.label: Realisation of objectives
469711.value: The majority of objectives has been addressed and has led to new findings, collaborations and publications. With regard to objective 1, we have developed a bioinformatics pipeline known as hybrid transcriptome assembly (HTA) to identify unique long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in male germ cell development by integrating the germ cell transcriptomes resources from GermSAGE, tiling microarray, and RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) datasets. HTA provides a number of advantages to conventional lncRNA annotations. It allows identification of male germ cell specific lncRNAs by filtering non-germ cell transcripts. To give a better picture on prediction quality, the lncRNAs were categorized into four classes according to the number of expression evidence. Using HTA, we have successfully identified annotated and novel lncRNAs associated with major male germ cell stages (germlncRNAs), including type A spermatogonia (Spga), pachytene spermatocytes (Spcy) and round spermatids (Sptd). Since recent studies have implicated that some lncRNAs could function by regulating expression of neighboring coding genes in cis or distal targets in trans. We further revealed the functional implications of germlncRNAs by studying the functional associations implicated in the cis- and trans- targets, and determined potential non-coding regulation of germlncRNAs. Selected lncRNA candidates were validated for stage-specific expression by real-time PCR and size confirmation by Northern Blot. For objective 2, we focused on the key biological pathways and functional implications in (1) normal development based on the coding gene targets identified in objective 1 and (2) in disease condition using previous vitamin A deficient (VAD) mouse model. We successfully confirmed novel stage-specific lncRNAs were associated with spermatogenesis-related genes in spermatogonia, pachytene spermatocytes, and round spermatids. This provided insights into a previously hidden network of molecular regulations on male germ cell development, and revealed a close relationship between lncRNAs and genes with stage-specific function. The VAD model also led to identification of a novel lncRNA, Gas5, which regulates spermatogonia proliferation and apoptosis through retinol acid-dependent pathway. To determine signaling networks involved in both studies, the interactions between the protein-lncRNA were predicted by RBPmap (http://rbpmap.technion.ac.il/) and other genomic evidence, followed by validation using RNA-immunoprecipitation assays. Due to multiple binding targets predicted by RBPmap, the validation took longer than expected, but we are confident this part can be completed within three months as we have got positive preliminary data. For objective 3, we have established the first public online resource, GermlncRnA database (http://germlncrna.cbiit.cuhk.edu.hk/) that allow searching, visualizing, downloading and analyzing mouse male germ cell-specific lncRNAs.

469711.label: Major findings and research outcome
469711.value: Major findings: 1. Identification of Annotated and novel lncRNA catalogues: We identified a total of 110 476 annotated lncRNAs and 2790 novel intergenic lncRNAs in male germ cell development. For annotated lncRNA populations, the RNA size ranged from 200 to 100 989bp with an average of 1628 bp. In total, 62.8% were gene-associated. Besides, 32.9% were intergenic, and 4.4% were associated with promoters. The size of novel lncRNAs ranged from 200 to 14 945bp, with an average of 800 bp. A total of 357 novel lncRNAs belonged to class four novel lncRNAs, which were supported by all three transcriptome sources. 2. GermlncRNA expression is highly related to spermatogenic functions: we also detected a higher percentage of stage-specific lncRNA candidates in the novel group rather than in the annotated group at every stage, suggesting novel lncRNAs could preferentially be involved in stage-specific functions. 3. Association with regulatory features: Analysis on DNA hypersensitive sites (DHS) showed roughly similar proportions of annotated and novel lncRNAs (33.1 vs. 36.1%; P = 0.001), indicating that they are comparably accessible by DNA-binding proteins. Other chromatin features including H3K4me1, H3K36me3 were significantly higher for annotated lncRNAs, indicating a smaller proportion of novel lncRNAs were enhancer-associated. The annotated lncRNAs also showed a higher association for active promoter features, H3K4me3 and H3K27ac. Subsequent analyses suggested a subset of germlncRNAs might involve in aging and epigenetic dynamics during male germ development. 4. Identification of a RNA-binding protein our bioinformatic study showed that Msi1 preferentially interacts with lncRNAs specifically expressed in spermatogonia. In vitro experiments confirmed two novel lncRNAs and two annotated lncRNAs were functional targets of Msi1 and promoted spermatogonial proliferation potentially via regulating the expression of p21 and Erh proteins. 5. lncRNA-Gas5 in spermatogonia maintenance and development. We identified a novel lncRNA, Gas5 significantly repressed in Type A spermatogonia from mice fed with prolonged vitamin A-deficient diet (VAD), suggesting retinonic acid is an upstream regulator of Gas5. Gas5 knockdown could also significantly reduce cellular proliferation; induce apoptosis; and repress differentiation in spermatogonial stem cells. Research outcome 1. Five publications (Three published. Two in preparation, manuscript drafts are also attached for reference in Part C) 2. Developed the first comprehensive lncRNA database (http://germlncrna.cbiit.cuhk.edu.hk/) on the key stages of male germ cell development. 3. Three conferences presentations (2 poster and 1 presentation) 4. Trained one Ph.D. student. One M.Phil. student in training. 5. Developed collaborations with industry and academic institutions (Part C) 6. Provided insights and data on aging and epigenetic regulation of lncRNA in male germ cell development and successfully applied for two GRFs in 2012 and 2013.

469711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
469711.value: The intriguing results have provided an important foundation for focusing on specific aspects of lncRNA regulations in male germ cell development. The cell type-specific lncRNAs in male germ cell development opens a new avenue to deliberating the biology at each major cellular stage. Our initial findings on spermatogonia-specific lncRNAs have suggested stage-specific lncRNAs in male germ cell development are highly related to the cellular function, such as proliferation and differentiation. We also showed some demonstrated age-dependent expression pattern and could be epigenetically regulated. In fact, our recent study on Gas5 has supported those hypotheses. Therefore we will continue to determine the role of germlncRNAs in aging regulation and their contribution to epigenetic dynamics during cellular transition. We will apply for new fundings to continue deliberate the biological roles of germlncRNAs. Our publications and presentations have led to establish new collaboration with other scientists. We have collaborated with Prof. Ji WU (BIO-X) to identity important lncRNAs in Female Germline Stem Cells (FGSCs) development by single-cell transcriptome approach. We also collaborated with Prof. Huayu QI (CAS) to determine the biological regulation of lncRNA and RBPs in spermatogonial stem cells. Both projects will apply for fundings from various grant resources.

469711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
469711.value: Spermatogenic failure is a major cause of male infertility, which affects millions of couples worldwide. Recent discovery of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) as critical regulators in normal and disease development provides new clues for delineating the molecular regulation in male germ cell development. However, few functional lncRNAs have been characterized. A major limitation in studying lncRNA in male germ cell development is the absence of germ cell-specific lncRNA annotation. Current lncRNA annotations are assembled by transcriptome data from heterogeneous tissue sources. Specific germ cell transcript information of various developmental stages is therefore under-represented, which may lead to biased prediction or fail to identity important germ cell-specific lncRNAs. In this project, we developed a new approach called Hybrid Transcriptome Assembly (HTA) for identifying important lncRNAs in male germ cell development and deposited to a public database known as GermlncRNA (http://germlncrna.cbiit.cuhk.edu.hk). GermlncRNA provides the first comprehensive web-based and open-access lncRNA catalogue for three key male germ cell stages, including type A spermatogonia, pachytene spermatocytes and round spermatids. Our study also led to identification of key signaling pathways and mediators that associate with various germlncRNAs for the maintenance of spermatogenic functions. The data could serve as potential targets for male reproductive therapy.

469911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
469911.value: Sarcopenia is the age-related loss of muscle mass, strength and thus impaired function. This is characterized with reduced fast-twitch skeletal muscle fiber type II and increased inflammatory interleukin-6 (IL-6). Sarcopenia is also a major risk factor of fall-induced osteoporotic fracture that may lead to increased morbidity and mortality. The prevalence was 12.3% in men and 7.6% in women aged >70 years in Hong Kong. To date, doing exercise is the only approach to retard sarcopenia but due to low compliance, this is not a useful way to resolve the problem. With increasing aging population, there is a need to pursue an alternative effective intervention to treat sarcopenia. Low-magnitude, high-frequency vibration (LMHFV) treatment is a non-invasive biophysical modality to provide systemic cyclic mechanical loading to stimulate musculoskeletal system, with good compliance (~80%). Our previous clinical cohort study confirmed that LMHFV could enhance balancing ability of postmenopausal women. Another on-going randomized controlled trial with 704 subjects further proves the beneficial effects of LMHFV on increasing muscle strength (+36.3% vs. -4.4%), reducing fall rate (7.9% vs. 17.5%) and fracture rate (0.5% vs. 1.6%) significantly, as compared with control group. The effect of LMHFV on significantly increased bone circulation during fracture healing was shown in our fractured rat model, which is also expected to have similar effects in muscle. These evidences strongly suggest LMHFV is effective to actively induce skeletal muscles to react and improve functions, yet the mechanism is not completely explored. An in vitro study revealed that vibration enhanced the myotube formation in C2C12 myoblast cell line, indicating the direct effect of vibration on cells. Together with other evidences including physical exercise could restore satellite cell proliferation in aging; reduce the muscle-catabolism-induced circulating level of IL-6; increase glucose transporter 4 (GLUT4) expression; increase type II muscle fiber area, we therefore hypothesize that LMHFV stimulates active contractions in skeletal muscles and thus improves functional outcomes, through increasing the proliferation of satellite cells, number of type II muscle fibers and muscle circulation, thus lowering the serum level of inflammatory IL-6. By using an aging rat model approved by National Institute on Aging, the effects of LMHFV on sarcopenic muscle tissues will be studied in details, in terms of the above parameters with muscle force as primary outcome. This will be the first study to elucidate the detailed mechanism of the effects of LMHFV on sarcopenic muscle tissues with correlation of cellular/biochemical to functional levels. 肌肉減少症是一種年齡相關的，以肌肉的組織量、肌力及功能下降的疾病。其特徵性改變為II型快肌纖維減少，同時有白介素-6 (IL-6)的增加。肌肉減少症同時也是摔倒誘發的骨質疏鬆性骨折的一個重要危險因素，而這類骨折的發病率和死亡率都很高。在香港70歲以上人群中，這類骨折的患病率男性為12.3%，女性為7.6%。目前，運動是唯一減緩肌肉衰老症的方法，但由於患者依從性不佳，這個方法並不奏效。在人口老齡化趨勢下，需要尋找其他可以有效治療肌肉減少症的方法。 低振幅高頻振動(LMHFV)治療是一種無創性的生物物理治療方法，可以對骨骼肌肉系統提供全身性循環機械負荷，並且具有良好的依從性 (約80%)。我們前期的臨床隊列研究確認LMHFV可以提高絕經後婦女的平衡能力。另一項正在進行的、有704名受試者參加的隨機對照研究進一步證明，與對照組相比，LMHFV可以提高肌肉力量 (+36.3% vs. -4.4%)，降低摔倒機率 (7.9% vs. 17.5%)及骨折機率(0.5% vs. 1.6%)。我們對大鼠骨折模型的研究發現，LMHFV可以顯著提高骨折愈合時的血液循環，同樣預期在肌肉組織中也有相似的結果。這些證據都強烈支持LMHFV可以刺激骨骼肌產生反應並提高功能，然而相關機制尚不完全清楚。 體外實驗發現振動可增加C2C12成肌細胞系中肌小管的形成，提示振動對細胞具有直接作用。還有其他的一些證據，包括運動可以恢復老年人衛星細胞增殖、減少細胞分解代謝介導的外周循環IL-6的水平、增加葡萄糖轉運蛋白4 (GLUT4)的表達、增加II型肌纖維的面積。通過這些證據，我們假設LMHFV可以刺激骨骼肌主動收縮並提高肌肉功能，其機制可能為促進衛星細胞的增殖、提高II型肌纖維的數量並改善肌肉循環、以及降低血清中IL-6的水平。通過研究美國國立老年研究所批准的老年大鼠模型，我們將以肌力為主要指標詳細研究LMHFV對肌肉減少症大鼠的肌肉組織的作用。這將是首個從細胞/生物化學水平到功能學水平闡明LMHFV對肌肉減少症的機理研究。

469911.label: Realisation of objectives
469911.value: 1. Fast-twitch type IIB fiber cross-sectional area (FCSA) was found significantly larger in LMHFV group than control group at Day 21 of reloading (p=0.031). Conversely, the type I FCSA of LMHFV group at Day 7 and Day 14 were smaller than control group (p=0.042 and p=0.028 respectively). Also, proliferative satellite cell counts increased significantly in type IIA fibers during the recovery period (p=0.027 at Day 14), as compared with significant decrease to undetectable level in the control group at Day 21. In type I fibers, the proliferative myogenic cell counts of LMHFV group at Day 14 and Day 21 were also higher than the control (p=0.046 and p=0.001). However, GLUT4 expression was not different between two groups. In conclusion, the effects of LMHFV on increasing fast-twitch type IIB FCSA and proliferation of satellite cells were confirmed in this study. 2. In the tail-suspension rat model, the tetanic force of soleus muscle was significantly larger in LMHFV group than control group at Day 14 of reloading (p=0.001). A 34.6% increase of tetanic force was found in the LMHFV group from Day 7 to Day 14 (p=0.033), showing a faster recovery of tetanic force than the control. Shorter contraction and half-relaxation time were also observed in LMHFV group at Day21 (p=0.022 for both); this may involve modification of contractile machineries to show fast fiber characteristic. Positive association between satellite cell counts and muscle FCSA was found. Also, the fiber type IIB FCSA was found positively correlated with the tetanic force measured (p=0.044), which suggested the possible contribution of activated satellite cells and type IIB muscle fiber hypertrophy for improving contractile force in LMHFV group during muscle recovery.

469911.label: Major findings and research outcome
469911.value: 1. Fast-twitch type IIB muscle fiber hypertrophy was stimulated by LMHFV with significantly larger fiber cross-sectional area (FCSA) in LMHFV group than control group at Day 21 of reloading (p=0.031). The fiber type I FCSA of LMHFV group at Day 7 and Day 14 were found smaller than control group (p=0.042 and p=0.028 respectively). [Supported by 8.1 and 9.1, 9.2, 9.3 and 9.6] 2. The specific tetanic force (normalized by FCSA) of soleus muscle was significantly larger in LMHFV group than control group at Day 14 of reloading (p=0.001). A 34.6% increase of tetanic force was observed in the LMHFV group from Day 7 to Day 14 (p=0.033). The recovery of force generating capacity in Soleus muscle was facilitated in the LMHFV group. Also, shorter contraction and half-relaxation time were observed in LMHFV group at Day21 (p=0.022 for both), showing a faster contraction reaction in recovering muscle. [Supported by 8.1 and 9.1, 9.2, 9.3, 9.4, 9.5 and 9.6] 3. Proliferative satellite cell counts of type IIA fiber significantly increased in the LMHFV group during the recovery period (p=0.027 at Day 14) when compared to control group that had satellite cell counts dropped to undetectable level at Day 21. In type I fibers, the proliferative myogenic cell counts of LMHFV group at Day 14 and Day 21 were also higher than control group (p=0.046 and p=0.001). [Supported by 8.1, 9.1, 9.2 and 9.6] 4. Correlations among satellite cell counts, muscle fiber cross-sectional area and tetanic force were observed in the recovering muscle of LMHFV group. Results showed a positive association between satellite cell counts and muscle FCSA. Also, the fiber type IIB FCSA was found positively correlated with the tetanic force measured (p=0.044), which suggested the possible contribution of activated satellite cells and type IIB muscle fiber hypertrophy for improving contractile force in LMHFV group during muscle recovery. 469911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
469911.value: In this study, the profound effects of LMHFV specifically on fast-twitch fibers, muscle hypertrophy and satellite cells were confirmed. Activated myogenic satellite cells and increased type IIB fiber cross-sectional area may contribute to the faster functional recovery of unloaded muscle after LMHFV treatment, with higher tetanic force gained during the recovery period. The results provide a solid basis for further study on treating loss of fast-twitch type II fibers in muscle aging (i.e. sarcopenia). Also, previous clinical studies suggested that LMHFV is well accepted by community elderly with negligible adverse effects. Further investigations (including randomized controlled clinical trial and basic science mechanistic study) are needed to study the effects of LMHFV on patients with sarcopenia and the potential application of LMHFV in community for sarcopenia prevention and rehabilitation.

469911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
469911.value: Muscle disuse is a common and serious public health issue affecting the aged population. The resulting muscle atrophy, loss of mobility and associated medical problems become a growing socio-medical problem, so an intervention that prevents or reverses muscle disuse is needed. This is the first study to investigate the effect of LMHFV on muscle disuse recovery, comprehensively from cellular level to functional outcomes. Results indicated LMHFV could enhance muscle force recovery, increase cross-sectional area of fast-twitch muscle fibers and promote proliferation of satellite cells. These help to understand the mechanism of LMHFV in enhancing skeletal muscle recovery and functional performance. Together with our previous clinical data, LMHFV can be further promoted in the general public at large to be an effective method to maintain and restore muscle functions. This will contribute to preventing fall and fracture significantly and hence promoting healthy aging.

470411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
470411.value: 題目： 高危栓塞源性症狀性顱內動脈粥樣硬化性斑塊的形態學研究 背景： 顱內動脈粥樣硬化性疾病（IAD）不僅是全世界範圍內引起腦卒中的常見原因，而且也是腦卒中復發的高危因素。早期識別具有繼發栓塞風險的不穩定斑塊，有助於制定最佳干預及治療方案。迄今為止，顱內不穩定斑塊的形態學特點尚不清楚，沒有可用於鑒別卒中復發風險的相關影像學標準。我們猜測高危性IAD斑塊的形態特點與穩定斑塊有所不同。 研究目的： 鑒別顱內不穩定斑塊的形態學特點。 患者篩選及研究步驟： 該研究預計錄入70例伴有重度顱內粥樣硬化性狹窄(≥60%)，經顱多普勒超聲（TCD）證實存在微栓子信號（MES）的急性缺血性卒中患者。時間窗設定為相關腦卒中或短暫性腦缺血發作1星期內。另70例伴有非症狀性顱內動脈重度狹窄的患者（核磁共振（MRI）顯示狹窄動脈同側無梗塞灶或TCD顯示無MES）作為對照組。所有的患者都進行以下檢查：1) 頭部MRI確定梗塞分佈特點；2) 持續30分鐘的TCD檢測MES；3) 數位減影血管造影（DSA）評估顱內斑塊形態學特點。對臨床資訊持盲的評估者獨立評估影像。我們預計通過邏輯回歸模型找出顱內不穩定斑塊的獨立危險因素。 錄入及排除標準： 錄入標準：症狀性缺血性卒中患者存在動脈血栓-栓塞性急性梗塞灶（彌散加權像顯示），相關顱內動脈狹窄≥60%，TCD檢測MES陽性。 排除標準：相關顱內動脈狹窄近端存在狹窄率>50%的串聯性狹窄或非顱內動脈粥樣硬化性腦卒中。 預計研究期限： 基於前期研究，每月分別錄入3例症狀性患者及3例非症狀性患者，預計28個月完成所有錄入。全部研究期限為32個月。 （關鍵词：缺血性卒中，顱內動脈粥樣硬化，經顱多普勒超聲）

470411.label: Realisation of objectives
470411.value: Through this prospective project, we identified the morphological evolution of acute symptomatic plaques leading to cerebral ischemia through digital subtraction angiography and 3D-rotational angiography. We studied the unstable plaques in intracranial arteries and radiation-induced vasculopathy. The study was completed on time and without severe adverse event (SAE) in all patients recruited. The findings were published in 3 original research papers: two in Stroke (impact factor 6.018) and one in Annals of Neurology (Impact factor 11.91). One PhD student and one MPhil student wrote their thesis partly based on the results of this project.

470411.label: Major findings and research outcome
470411.value: In the study of unstable intracranial plaques, we recruited 50 patients (mean age 63.4±9.0 years) with acute strokes attributed to high-grade (≥70%) intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis for 3D-rotational angiograms before and after intensive medical therapy for 12 months. Treatment targets included low-density lipoprotein <70 mg/dl; HbA1c <6.5%; and systolic blood pressure <140 mmHg. We analyzed infarct topography and monitored microembolic signal in recurrent strokes. We found that overall the stenoses regressed from 79% at baseline (IQR 71-87%) to 63% (IQR 54-74%) in one year (p<0.001). Specifically, the qualifying lesions (n=49) regressed (stenosis reduced >10%) in 24 patients (49%); remained quiescent (stenosis same or ±10%) in 21 patients (43%); and progressed (stenosis increased >10%) in 4 patients (8%). Patients with higher HbA1c at baseline predicted plaque regression at one year (OR 4.4 [95% CI 1.4-14.5]; p=0.006). Among the 6 patients with recurrent strokes pertained to the qualifying stenosis, 5 patients had solitary or rosary-like acute infarcts along the internal or anterior borderzones; and 2 patients showed microembolic signals in transcranial Doppler ultrasound. We concluded that a majority of symptomatic high-grade intracranial plaques had regressed or remained quiescent by 12 months under intensive medical therapy. Artery-to-artery thrombo-embolism with impaired washout at borderzones was a common mechanism in stroke recurrence. In the study of unstable plaques associated with prior radiotherapy (RT), we analyzed the digital subtraction angiography (DSA) of 96 patients who had first-ever ischemic strokes attributed to occlusive radiation-induced vasculopathy (ORV). Another age-matched 115 patients who had no RT but symptomatic high-grade (>70%) carotid stenoses were referent subjects. DSA was performed within 2 months from stroke onset and delineated carotid and vertebro-basilar circulations from aortic arch up to intracranial branches. We found that in referent patients, high-grade stenoses were mostly focal at the proximal internal carotid artery. In contrast, high-grade ORV lesions diffusely involved the common carotid artery and internal carotid artery, and were more frequently bilateral (54% vs 22%), tandem (23% vs 10%), associated with complete occlusion in one or both carotid arteries (30% vs 9%), vertebral artery steno-occlusions (28% vs 16%) and ECA stenosis (19% vs 5%) (all p<0·05). ORV patients showed more established collateral circulations through leptomeningeal arteries, anterior communicating artery, posterior communicating artery, sub-occipital/costocervical artery, and retrograde flow in ophthalmic artery. We concluded that ORV angiographic features and corresponding collaterals are distinct from atherosclerotic patterns at initial stroke presentation. Clinical decompensation despite more extensive collateralization may precipitate stroke in ORV.

470411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
470411.value: Through 3D-rational angiography, we captured the temporal dynamic evolution of unstable intracranial plaques in arteries that were mostly with a diameter of 2.5mm or below for the first time. The longer-term evolution of symptomatic carotid and intracranial plaques, however, remained largely unknown. This is crucial for understanding the stroke mechanism and tabulating the pros and cons of adjunctive surgical/endovascular treatment. In terms of future study, as 3D-rotational angiogram delineated plaque surface, morphology and luminal narrowing but not plaque composition, further studies with concurrent high-resolution MR may reveal how intra-plaque hemorrhage and signals of inflammation would evolve with treatment. Moreover, we did not monitor the effects of dietary control or lifestyle modifications like exercise that may contribute to plaque remodeling. A larger series of monitored medical treatment with lifestyle interventions and a longer study period is warranted.

470411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
470411.value: Atherosclerotic narrowing of brain arteries is highly prevalent among Chinese stroke patients, and high-grade carotid artery narrowing is a major cause of stroke in nasopharyngeal cancer survivors in Hong Kong. We revealed the attributes of these unstable plaques through advanced radiology techniques and delineated the temporal progression/regression of these vascular lesions under modern medical therapy. Our results provide guidance to the management of these patients.

470911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
470911.value: Glioblastoma (GBM) (Grade IV gliomas), a highly invasive and the most common and devastating brain tumor, is essentially incurable. Novel insights into the molecular mechanisms that drive GBM and Cancer Stem Cell (CSC) formations are urgently needed in order to develop new strategies for improved patient outcome. The emerging concept of generating Cancer Stem Cells from Epithelial Mesenchymal cells has attracted great interests. We have recently reported that miR-200a could regulate Epithelial-Mesenchymal and Stem-like Transitions (EMST) in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) cells. Furthermore, miR-200a controls EMT and MST by different mechanisms (Xia et al., JBC, in press). These results raised the possibility that microRNAs play a pivotal role in controlling the progression of EMST in tumor cells including glioblastoma. The brain enriched miR-124a has previously been shown to be down-regulated in glioma/glioblastoma tissues, and over-expression of miRNA-124a could promote the differentiation of brain tumor stem cells to express neuronal marker. We hypothesize that miR-124a may exert this effect by shifting the brain tumor stem cells through a reversed Proneural Mesenchymal and Stem-like Transitions (PMST), a process reminiscent to that of EMST. Consistent with this hypothesis, our preliminary data showed that over-expression of miR-124a in Mesenchymal-like GBM cells inhibited the migration/invasion and also reduced several Stem-like traits including CD133+ side population, neurosphere formation, and stem cell marker expressions. In this application, we aim to extend our observations and investigate the potential functions of miR-124a in GBM invasion and PMST by both gain of function and loss of function studies. We will further determine and compare the molecular mechanisms by which miR-124a regulates cell proliferation, invasion, PMT, and MST. Finally, we will examine the expression levels of miR-124a and correlate its expression pattern with clinical, pathological and prognostic parameters in glioma/GBM tissue samples from Hong Kong patients in our collection. Knowledge gained will provide new insights regarding the potential roles of miR-124a in glioma / glioblastoma carcinogenesis and may lead to the discovery of novel carcinogenic pathways, therapeutic targets, as well as prognostic biomarkers. 470911.label: Realisation of objectives
470911.value: Project Objective 1. To characterize the function of miR-124a in cell invasion, Mesenchymal Stem-like Transition (MST), and Proneural Mesenchymal Transition (PMT) in GBM cell lines by gain of function and loss of function studies. The miR-124 is a brain-enriched miRNA that has been broadly investigated in physiological neural development. In this study, we showed that miR124 expression level is lower in highly invasive glioma cells (U87, U118, U138 and U373 cells) than in glioma cells of low invasiveness (SW1088, SW1783 and CCF-STTG1 cells). We further demonstrated that overexpression of miR-124 in U87-124a and U373-124a cells significantly restrained U87-124a and U373-124a cells from invasion.To better understand the potential role of miR-124 in controlling the invasiveness and stemness of glioma cells, we analyzed the neurosphere formation ability, CD133+ cell population and stem cell markers BMI1, Nanog and Nestin expressions in our established stable cells with miR-124 overexpression. Collectively, our results indicate that miR-124 decreased the proneural and mesenchymal marker expressions and increased the stem cell marker and stem-like characteristics of glioma cells. Based on these results, one manuscript was published in J. Biol.Chem. (2012),287:9962-9971. Project Objective 2. To demonstrate the functions of miR-124a in suppressing GBM tumor growth, cancer stem cell level, angiogenesis, and tumor invasion, in vivo in a nude mice xenograft model. We assessed the effects of miR-124 overexpression on tumor initiation and growth in vivo. U87-124a as well as the respective control cells were inoculated into the back flanks of nude mice by subcutaneous injection. At 42 days post-injection, the mean volumes of tumors generated from U87-124a cells were significantly smaller than those originated from control cells. Further H&E staining studies indicated that U87-124a cells with miR-124 overexpression were less invasive with less angiogenesis, suggesting that miR-124 suppressed the stem-like traits and invasion of glioma cells in vivo. Based on these results, one manuscript was published in J. Biol.Chem. (2012),287:9962-9971. Project Objective 3. To determine and compare the molecular mechanisms by which miR-124a regulates cell proliferation, migration/invastion, MST and PMT. To elucidate the molecular mechanisms, we predicted its downstream targets using five prediction algorithms, namely TargetScan, miRDB, DIANA-microT, miRNAMap and miRNAviewer. Among the candidate target genes that were commonly predicted by all five algorithms, eight genes had been shown to be downregulated by miR-124 in microarray analysis. LAMC1 and PTBP1 have been reported as targets of miR-124 in neural development. We further demonstrated that SNAI2 - a member of the Snail family of zinc finger transcription factors is a downstream target of miR-124. Stably overexpressing miR-124 significantly downregulated the endogenous mRNA and protein expressions of SNAI2. We showed that miR-124 recognizes the 3’-UTR of SNAI2 mRNA by dual-luciferase reporter assay. We also examined whether the expression levels of miR-124a correlate with clinical, pathological and prognostic parameters in glioma/glioblastoma tissue samples from Hong Kong patients in our collection. We analyzed the expression of miR-124 in twenty-seven cases of glioma patient samples, twenty cases of non-glioma patient samples which included two non-tumor brain tissues by real-time qRT-PCR. Our results showed that when compared with non-glioma brain tissues, the expression of miR-124 was significantly lower by around 2-fold in all glioma samples examined. Taken together, our findings reveal for the first time the tumor suppressor activity of miR-124 could be partly due to its inhibitory effects on glioma stem-like traits and invasiveness through SNAI2. Based on these results, one manuscript was published in J. Biol.Chem. (2012), 287: 9962-9971. We have also investigated the transcriptional regulation of miRNA family in cancer. We demonstrated for the first time that in contrary to HepG2 and other liver cells, overexpression of MYC could not down-regulate the expression and the promoter activity of human microRNA cluster in GBM cells. Using chromatin immuno-precipitation (ChIP) and super-shift assays, they validated the loss of MYC and E-box 3 binding in GBM. It is the first time to demonstrate that GBM exhibited differential MYC mediated transcriptional inhibition. Based on these findings, one manuscript is accepted by Oncotarget. 470911.label: Major findings and research outcome
470911.value: The emerging concept of generating CSCs from Epithelial Mesenchymal cells has attracted great interests. In this study, we demonstrated that the brain enriched miR-124a is down-regulated in glioma/GBM tissues. Over-expression of miRNA-124a could promote the differentiation of brain tumor stem cells. We showed for the first time that miR-124a may exert this effect by shifting the brain tumor stem cells through a reversed proneural mesenchymal and Stem-like Transitions. We further determined and compared the molecular mechanisms by which miR-124a regulates cell proliferation, invasion. Our results suggested the potential roles of miR-124a in glioma / glioblastoma carcinogenesis and may lead to the discovery of novel carcinogenic pathways, therapeutic targets, as well as prognostic biomarkers. Based on our results, one paper has been published (J Biol Chem., (2012) 287(13): 9962-71). Furthermore, we also demonstrated for the first time that in contrary to other cancers (such as liver cancer), overexpression of MYC could not down-regulate the expression and the promoter activity of human microRNA cluster in GBM cells. Using chromatin immuno-precipitation (ChIP) and super-shift assays, they validated the loss of MYC and E-box 3 binding in GBM. It is the first time to demonstrate that GBM exhibited differential MYC mediated transcriptional inhibition. Based on these findings, one paper is published (Cancer Lett 2013), and one manuscript is accepted by Oncotarget.

470911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
470911.value: Based on these results, works are on-going to further study the functions, regulations, and application as biomarker of miR124 in many diseases of the brain, especially in GBM and Intracerebral Hemorrhage Stroke (ICH).

470911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
470911.value: A hallmark feature of the most common and lethal primary brain tumor, glioblastoma (GBM), is its highly invasive potential, immature differentiation state and a subpopulation of tumor-initiating Cancer Stem Cell (CSC) type. Novel insights into the molecular mechanisms that drive GBM and CSC formations are urgently needed in order to develop new strategies for improved patient outcome. In this study, our results suggested for the first time, the potential roles of miR-124a in glioma / glioblastoma cancer stem cell transitions, and may lead to the discovery of novel carcinogenic pathways, therapeutic targets, as well as prognostic biomarkers. Furthermore, we also demonstrate for the first time that GBM exhibited differential MYC mediated transcriptional inhibition.

471211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
471211.value: 鼻咽癌是南中國非常普遍和高死亡率的癌症。作為一種特殊頭頸部癌症,鼻咽癌與EB病毒感染和密集淋巴細胞浸潤有密切關係。腫瘤浸潤淋巴細胞主要是CD3+ T細胞, 包括不同比例的CD4+和CD8+細胞。雖然在鼻咽癌患者血液中發現有EB病毒特異性細胞毒性T細胞免疫反應，可是在腫瘤部位中出現細胞毒T細胞活性受損和缺乏細胞因子等現象。細胞毒T細胞功能缺陷是導致免疫系統控制EBV有關腫瘤失敗的主要原因。在我們早期研究中，已經證CD4+CD25highT細胞的擴增可能引致鼻咽癌逃避患者的免疫系統。我們最近調查鼻咽癌腫瘤細胞和腫瘤浸潤淋巴細胞上的免疫調節分子表達。其中HVEM是觸發BTLA的抑制信號和調節T細胞反應。初步研究在6/6EBV陽性鼻咽癌腫瘤細胞株和9/20原發腫瘤發現HVEM表達。更重要是發現EB病毒陽性細胞株C666-1釋放出來的exsomes含有大量HVEM和其他共同抑制分子PD-L1。研究亦顯示鼻咽癌患者腫瘤浸潤淋巴細胞和血液中HVEM和PD-L1受體:BTLA和PD-1的表達。根據初步調查結果，我們推測由鼻咽癌產生的exsomes通過多種抑制性受體途徑(如HVEM/BTLA，PD-L1/PD-1)抑制腫瘤特異性 CD8+T細胞。我們在此研究的目標是（1）調查在鼻咽癌腫瘤細胞和exosomes中共同抑制分子表達(2)確定鼻咽癌患者腫瘤特異性CD8+T細胞共同抑制受體的表達;（3）闡明含HVEM和PD-1的exosomes對腫瘤特異性CD8+T細胞的抑制功能。此建議的研究成果不僅提高我們對鼻咽癌發病機制的認識,亦推動EBV陽性惡性腫瘤的免疫治療，並提供發展有效的癌症疫苗的重要基礎。

471211.label: Realisation of objectives
471211.value: The study have comprehensively elucidated the expression of HVEM, PD-L1, PD-L2 and their receptors in the NPC tumor cells and infiltrating lymphocytes respectively. Recently, we re-examined the PD-L1 and PD-L2 using the new antibodies which were used in multiple clinical studies. Majority of primary NPCs expressed PD-L1 and/or PD-L2 while HVEM and IL4I1 was detected in few cases. The findings provide potential biomarkers for selecting the patients for clinical trial of PD1 inhibitor (Nivolumab). In addition, we have demonstrated the accumulation of PD-L1 and HVEM, but not PD-L2 in the derived exosomes. In the pilot study, we have demonstrated the PD-L1-containing exosomes inhibited the function of isolated CD8+T cells. However, the inhibitory effect of HVEM in the exsomes on the isolated CD8+T cells was not obviously detected. Currently, we are preparing the manuscript of the co-inhibitory molecules in EBV-associated NPC and will be submitted on April. In this manuscript, we will focus on PD-L1 and PD-L2 since the molecules play a major roles in immune evasion of NPC. We have also investigated the mechanisms for upregulating PD-L1, PD-L2 and HVEM in NPC tumor cells. The schedule of this section was greatly delayed because of the long-term leave of the research staff involved in the study. A new student was recruited for the study and she has demonstrated the LMP1-modulating HVEM expression. Since PD-L1 and PD-L2 are the major co-inhibitory molecules in NPC, we have examined the association of LMP1 and PD-L1 and PD-L2. However, no correlation was found between LMP1 and PD-L1/PD-L2 by IHC and transfection studies. Notably, the contribution of AKT pathway in regulating HVEM and PD-L2 expression were found in nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Our recent study has demonstrated that activation of PI3K/AKT signalling is common in NPC (Yuen et al. PLoS One, 9:e105163, 2014). Currently, we focus to study the mechanism of AKT modulating PD-L1 in NPC. For the LMP1-modulating PD-L1, our finding is different from that reported by Fang et al (Oncotarget 5:12189-202, 2014). We will repeat study on more immortalized NP epithelial cells.

471211.label: Major findings and research outcome
471211.value: In this study, we have characterized the expression of the co-inhibitory molecules in EBV-associated NPC. PD-L1 and PD-L2 were found as the major co-inhibitory molecules expressed in NPC by immunohistochemistry. We detected 54/114 (47%) and 62/114 (54%) cases with >5% tumor cells expressing PD-L1 and PD-L2 respectively. A total of 84/114 (73.7%) cases shows the expression of either PD-L1 or PD-L2 while HVEM only detected in >10% of NPC. Notably, abundant IDO1 expressing macrophages were noted in majority of the PD-L1/PD-L2 negative tumors. Furthermore, a correlation between the PD-L1/PD-L2 expression and poor outcome of the patients was noted. The findings suggested that the PD-L1/PD-L2 play the critical role in the immune evasion in NPC (Siu et al. manuscript is in preparation and will submit on April). As report in recent gastric cancer genome study, overexpression/amplification of PD-L1/PD-L2 is unique feature in EBV-associated gastric cancer (Nature 513:202-9). However, we did not detect any PD-L1/PD-L2 mutation or amplification in a total of 15 primary tumors and 8 cell line/xenografts. It is likely that PD-L1/PD-L2 are activated by either EBV latent genes or aberrant siganling pathways (Tsao et al. J Pathol, 2015). Among the primary NPCs, we also noted that PD-L1 or PD-L1 expression show similar prevalence in the cases with high (14/19; 73.7%), weak (29/39; 74.4%) and absence (41/56; 73.21) of LMP1 expression (Siu et al). Contradiction to the finding from Fang et al (Oncotarget 5:12189-202, 2014), we found the EBV-encoded oncoprotein LMP1 induced the transcription of HVEM, but not PD-L1 in the NP epithelial cells (HK1 and NP69). As reported in our recent study (Lo et al, J Pathol, 2013), we examined the role of LMP1 in regulation of its target genes. We found that LMP1 modulated HVEM expression is dependent on CTAR1 region and can be inhibited by the AKT inhibitor (LY294002). Interestingly, LY294002 suppressed both HVEM and PD-L2 expression in the C666-1 NPC cells. This indicates the potential role of AKT signaling in the immune evasion in NPC. We have demonstrated the presence of PD-L1 and HVEM in the NPC-derived exosomes. In our pilot study, we noted that the PD-L1 in these exosomes contributes to the functional inactivation of isolated T lymphocytes (Siu, et al). In these exosomes, we also identified multiple important proteins (e.g. Galection-3, Galection-9B, CCL5, and DLL4). The exosomes with DLL4 induced the proliferation of endothelial cells and may contribute to angiogenesis in NPC.

471211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
471211.value: Our findings indicate that PD-L1 and PD-L2 function as key co-inhibitory molecules that down-modulate the activated T-cell immune response in NPC. In the pilot study, the PD-1 antibody is also able to inhibit the function of PD-L1 containing exosomes in suppression of activated T lymphocytes. The findings suggest the targeting PD-1 signaling by the PD-1 inhibitor (Nivolumab) is an efficient immunotherapy for NPC patients. A multiple-center clinical trial of PD1 inhibitor (Nivolumab) in previously treated patients with recurrent and metastatic NPC was recently initiated. As one of the collaborator of this clinical study, we plan to elucidate the biomarkers for Nivolumab treatment. We will detect the expression of PD-L1, PD-L2, PD1 and other markers in the tumor and peripheral blood samples of the patients. The association of these potential biomarkers and the treatment response will be determined.

471211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
471211.value: In EBV-associated nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), the tumor cells suppress the EBV-specific cytotoxic T-cell mediated immune responses through the expression of the co-inhibitory molecules including PD-L1, PD-L2 and HVEM. By either EBV-encoded LMP1 or activated signalling pathways (e.g. AKT, NF-kappaB), these molecules are induced in the nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Among these molecules, PD-L1/PD-L2 expression is shown as the major mechanism for immune evasion in NPC. Our findings also confirmed the PD-L1/PD-L2 expression is associated with poor prognoses in NPC. In addition, we also demonstrated the function of PD-L1-exsomes in suppressing the activated T-cell immune response. The accumulation of PD-L1 in tumor- derived exosomes may serve as a novel mechanism for modulating the tumor inflammatory microenvironment. Our findings indicate that targeting PD-1/PD-L1/PD-L2 signaling is a potential efficient therapeutic strategy for EBV-associated NPC. Inhibition of PD-1 signaling can induce tumor regression in vivo, increase effector T-cell function and cytokine production theoretically by reactivating PD-1 expressing TILs. Based on our findings, a multiple-center clinical trial of PD1 inhibitor (Nivolumab) in previously treated patients with recurrent and metastatic NPC was initiated. The usefulness of PD-L1 and PD-L2 expression as biomarkers for immunotherapy will be confirmed in this new clinical study.

471411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
471411.value: 本课题旨在探索同种异体肌腱干细胞促进肌腱修复的前景。 肌腱韧带损伤在日常生活中很普遍并且容易致残。肌腱损伤后再生缓慢和修复效率低下。肌腱干细胞与骨髓间充质干细胞相比具备更高的克隆形成能力，增殖速度和更高的肌腱相关的基因表达。所以它可能是比骨髓间充质干细胞更好更安全的修复肌腱的细胞来源。在临床应用上，同种异体移植肌腱干细胞能够有效避免供体部位发病和保证充足的细胞用于移植。同种异体肌腱干细胞能够很容易从残余和废弃的移植组织中获得，例如前十字交叉韧带重建手术。我们的初步结果显示肌腱干细胞同骨髓间充质干细胞一样缺乏MHC二类分子和CD86的表达。所以我们推测肌腱干细胞的低免疫原性适合用于同种异体移植。在组织学和免疫化学水平上的初步数据显示，相比对照组肌腱干细胞移植组能够更好地促进肌腱再生。在移植后的第二周，组织学上观察到肌腱干细胞移植组比骨髓间充质干细胞组有更好的修复效果。而且在移植后的第四周，我们仍然能够观察到在伤口处有存活的肌腱干细胞。 本研究主要研究目的如下： 1，研究同种异体肌腱干细胞在急性肌腱损伤模型中促进肌腱修复的效果和机制（主要目的）； 2，鉴定肌腱干细胞的免疫表型； 3，研究移植物诱导大鼠T细胞及B细胞同种异体肌腱干细胞的反应效果。 我们将用肌腱开放损伤模型去评估同种异体移植表达GFP的肌腱干细胞（2x107个细胞每毫升纤维蛋白胶）促进肌腱愈合的效果。我们将在手术后的各个时间点收集髌骨肌腱进行体外荧光成像来追踪同种异体移植的肌腱干细胞，然后利用组织学，细胞外基质的免疫组织化学，生物力学来评价愈合效果。我们还将用GFP和PCNA共同免疫组织化学或原位末端转移酶标记技术来进一步研究同种异体肌腱干细胞的命运。另一方面我们利用流式细胞检测术来研究肌腱干细胞的免疫表型。通过收集相同肌腱损伤模型中的血清和脾细胞，进行一系列抗原抗体结合测试，补体依赖的细胞毒性测试，脾细胞介导的细胞裂解实验和脾细胞增殖实验等实验来研究同种异体肌腱干细胞引发的T细胞和B细胞的同种异体反应记忆效果。同时炎症细胞入侵伤口的情况也会利用免疫细胞组织化学来评估。 本研究独特并附有创新性因为它是首次研究同种异体肌腱干细胞在肌腱修复中的治疗前景和机制并且以骨髓间充质干细胞作为比较参考，同时还对肌腱干细胞的免疫表型和免疫原性进行了评估检测。 这些研究对同种异体移植用于组织修复非常重要。本研究的发现将为同种异体移植肌腱干细胞的肌腱组织工程及其进一步指导治疗应用提供重要的信息。

471411.label: Realisation of objectives
471411.value: All the project objectives have been achieved. To achieve the first objective, allogenic patellar tendon derived stem cells (TDSCs) were isolated from green fluorescence protein (GFP) expressing rat. Allogenic TDSCs were transplanted into the window would of an acute tendon injury model. Healing effect of TDSCs transplantation was examined by histology, mechanical test and immunohistochemistry. The fates of the transplanted GFP-TDSCs were examined by ex vivo fluorescent imaging and immunohistochemistry. Results of this part have been reported in “Allogeneic tendon-derived stem cells promote tendon healing and suppress immunoreactions in hosts: in vivo model.” Tissue Eng Part A. 2014 Nov;20 (21-22):2998-3009. To achieve the second and third objective, after allogenic transplantation, spleens were collected at 0, 2, 6 and 8 weeks post transplantation. Lymphocyte proliferation assay, lymphocyte-mediated TDSC lysis assay, CDC assay, antigen-binding assay, flow activated cell sorting analysis and measurement of soluble immune-modulatory factors were performed to characterize TDSCs with respect to their immunophenotype in vitro; and to study the effect of allogeneic TDSCs to elicit responses of T and B cells isolated from rats with TDSC transplants in vitro. Results of this part have been reported in “Immunogenicity and escape mechanisms of allogeneic tendon-derived stem cells.” Tissue Eng Part A. 2014 Nov;20 (21-22):3010-20.

471411.label: Major findings and research outcome
471411.value: The medium- to long-term healing effect and infiltration of inflammatory cells of allogenic tendon-derived stem cells (TDSCs) transplantation in tendon healing were examined in the first part of study. To chase the fate of the transplanted cells, allogeneic patellar TDSCs derived from a green fluorescent protein rat were used. The outcome of tendon healing and the infiltration of inflammatory cells were assessed by histology and immunohistochemistry up to week 16 post injury. The fate of the transplanted cells was examined by ex vivo fluorescent imaging and immunohistochemistry. We demonstrated that the transplantation of allogeneic TDSCs promoted tendon healing with no increased risk of ectopic chondro-ossification up to week 16. In addition, weak immunoreactions and anti-inflammatory effects in the hosts after transplantation were observed. A low infiltration of T cells, ED1 macrophages, ED2 macrophages, and mast cells in the window wound was obtained. The transplanted TDSCs were found in the window wound at week 1 and 2, but were absent after week 4 post injury. This implicated that allogenic TDSCs did not promote tendon repair through direct differentiation. Next, we investigated if TDSCs are immune-privileged cells that are suitable for allogeneic transplantation. The immunogenicity of TDSCs has implications for their clinical use for the promotion of tendon repair. Immunogenicity and escape mechanisms of rat TDSCs were examined after allogenic transplantation. We demonstrated that TDSCs exhibited low immunogenicity as evidenced by followings: (1) No antibody recognition and no complement-dependent cytotoxicity were observed after the incubation of target TDSCs with immunized serum; (2) target TDSCs elicited a very low level of lymphocyte proliferation and did not exhibit host lymopophocyte-mediated cytotoxicity; and (3) target TDSCs dose dependently suppressed the phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA)- and ionomycin-induced host lymphocyte proliferation. In the mechanistic studies, TDSCs expressed major histocompatibility complex (MHC)-I but a very low level of MHC-II, CD86 and CD80 for the induction of T-cell response. Also, intracellular Fas and FasL expression were found in TDSCs. MHC-II and CD86 were not increased for the upregulation of immune response after γ-IFN pretreatment. These results suggested that TDSCs were immune privileged. Moreover, in the escape mechanism of target TDSCs from host lymphocyte attack, immunosuppressive mediators indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO) and transforming growth factor-beta 1 (TGF-b1) were found not to be involved. In conclusion, allogeneic TDSCs exhibited low immunogenicity. Allogeneic TDSCs might be used for transplantation. These findings were reported in output (journal) 3 and 4.

471411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
471411.value: In the first part of the study, in addition to our previous observation in the early tendon healing, we have investigated the medium- to long-term healing effect of TDSCs transplantation. We included a validated histological scoring and semi quantitative image analysis for objective outcome evaluation in this study. However, we did not have gene expression outcome or protein expression of tendon remodeling markers. Further study on the expression of tendon remodeling markers could provide more information on how TDSCs transplantation improved tendon healing. Although the transplanted GFP-TDSCs used in this study carries different genetic pool compare to the wild-type SD rat (recipient), the rats used in this study might not be as variable as that would exist within a human population. Clinical studies are required. In the study of escape mechanism of allogenic GFP-TDSCs transplantation, in contrast to previous studies, which BMSCs were reported to promote immunosuppression by producing suppressive molecules such as TGF-β and IDO, and reducing in the secretion of inflammatory molecule TNF-α. We demonstrated that IDO, TNF-α, and TGF-β1 were not involved in escape mechanism of target TDSCs from lymphocyte attack. Further study is required to elucidate the mechanism by which TDSCs escaped from lymphocyte attack.

471411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
471411.value: Tendon/ ligament injuries are commonplace and disabling. Tendons regenerate and repair slowly and inefficiently after injury. Tendon derived stem cells (TDSCs) have been isolated from various species. TDSCs display higher clonogenicity, proliferative potential and expression of tenogenic markers than Bone-marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). TDSCs might be a better cell source than BMSCs for tendon repair. For clinical applications, allogenic TDSCs transplantation is essential to avoid donor site morbidity and reduce the time to reach enough cell number for transplantation. Allogenic TDSCs are readily available from the waste or residual graft tissue, during surgery (e.g. ACL reconstruction). The aim of this project is study the potential of allogenic TDSCs to promote tendon repair. In this study, allogenic TDSCs transplantation improved the medium- to long-term acute tendon healing in biomechanical properties and histologically. In addition, there was no increased risk of ectopic chondro-ossification after TDSCs transplantation. Allogenic TDSCs will be gone in 4 weeks after transplantation. Last but not least, TDSCs exhibited low immunogenicity. Taken together, allogenic TDSCs might be used for transplantation.

471911.label: Project Objectives
471911.value: The objectives of this study are to develop and validate a risk index for screening SBL in community-dwelling elderly persons without stroke or dementia.
rows: The objectives of this study are to develop and validate a risk index for screening SBL in community-dwelling elderly persons without stroke or dementia.

471911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
471911.value: Background: Subclinical brain lesions (SBL) refer to lacunes and white matter lesions (WML) found in otherwise healthy persons without stroke and dementia. SBL are common among elderly with reported prevalence between 22 and 96%. Although SBL were initially considered to be ‘silent’, recent studies showed that SBL may associate with subtle neurological signs (e.g. mild cognitive impairment). More important, its presence greatly increases future risks of dementia, stroke, functional decline and death. Therefore, it is important that persons with SBL are identified early for management or recruitment into preventive trials. SBL are best identified by MRI. However, large-scale screening using MRI is not cost effective. Methods to guide selective scanning are lacking. The objective of this project is to develop and validate a risk index for screening SBL in community-dwelling elderly persons without stroke or dementia. Methods: A total of 800 community-dwelling elders aged ≥ 65 without stroke or dementia will be recruited over a period of 36 months. A set of 32 clinical correlates of SBL and cardiovascular risk factors will be used as candidate risk markers for SBL. These markers include demographic and cardiovascular risk factors, neurological signs, and cognitive, mood and functional measures. All subjects will undergo brain MRI and be classified into groups of increasing severity of SBL in terms of number of lacunes and WML severity. Among the derivation cohort (n=400), we will explore the association between SBL severity and the candidate markers by a series of multivariate binomial logistic regression models so as to select markers for inclusion in the final risk index. A score will be assigned to each level of selected risk marker based on its ß coefficient in the multivariate model. The total risk score will be the sum of scores of individual risk marker. We will then validate the risk index among a separate cohort (n=400) by the receiver operating curve (ROC) analysis. We hypothesize that the risk index will have an acceptable area under the ROC of ≥0.75 in differentiating those with and without SBL. Significance: With an ageing population, stroke and dementia are expected to increase by more than 50% and 300% respectively over the next 30 years in China. A simple tool for screening SBL in the community is currently lacking. This risk index may help to identify at-risk subjects early and have the potential to contribute in the prevention of common elderly diseases. 亞臨床腦部病變（Subclinical brain lesions，SBL）是指在無中風或癡呆的健康人中發現的腔隙性梗死灶和腦白質病變 （white matter lesions，WML）。 據報導，SBL在老年人中很常見，患病率介於22-96%之間。雖然最初SBL被認為是無症狀的，但是最近的研究表明SBL可能與輕度腦神經症狀有關（例如：輕度認知功能損害），更為重要的是，它的出現極大地增高了未來患癡呆、中風、功能減退與死亡的風險。因此，及早發現SBL患者對早期治療或者入選預防性臨床實驗至關重要。 磁力共振檢查（magnetic resonance imaging, MRI）是SBL最有效的檢查。但是，利用MRI進行大樣本量篩查並不經濟實用。目前尚缺乏篩查SBL的方法。該研究的目的是創建並驗證一個風險指數用於篩查無中風或癡呆的香港社區老年人中的SBL。 方法：該研究將於36個月內在社區中入組800例65歲及以上無中風或癡呆的老年人。SBL候選危險指標由一組32項SBL臨床相關特徵和心血管危險因素組成。這些危險指標包括人口學資料、心血管危險因素、神經系統體征和認知功能、情緒及功能評定量表量表。受試者將行頭顱MRI檢查，並根據腔隙性梗死灶數目及WML嚴重程度劃分為不同嚴重程度的SBL小組。在衍生組（n=400）中，我們將運用一系列多元二項式logistic回歸模型分析SBL嚴重程度與候選危險指標之間的關係，用以選擇最終構成危險指數的指標。每一個入選的危險指標根據多因素模型中的ß係數而定義相應的分值。將所有入選的危險指標的分值相加可以得到總危險分值即危險指數。然後，我們會運用受試者操作曲線（receiver operating curve，ROC）分析在有效組（n=400）中驗證這個危險指數。 我們假設此危險指數將能夠合理的區分有或無SBL（ROC≥0.75）。 重要性： 隨著人口老齡化的發展，中國中風和癡呆的患病率在未來30年後預測將分別增加至少50%和300%。目前，我們尚缺乏社區篩查SBL的簡便工具。此危險指數可能有助於早期發現高危人群

471911.label: Realisation of objectives
471911.value: The project objective was to develop and validate a risk index for screening subclinical brain lesions (SBL) in community elderly persons. The objective was achieved according to the plans stated in the study protocol. In summary, our study was able to establish a risk index for screening community elderly persons with severe white matter lesions (WML). The clinical implication of this study is that, with the availability of a screening tool, clinicians can make use of readily available clinical data to screen elderly persons at high risk of severe WML for further brain MRI examination which is a costly procedure.
