471911.label: Major findings and research outcome
471911.value: The whole sample (n=800) was split in half into a derivation (n=400) and a validation (n=400) samples. The two samples were matched on age, sex and vascular risk factors including hypertension, diabetes mellitus [DM], etc). Risk equations were developed in the derivation cohort based on the logistic regression coefficients in predicting 1) severe WML; 2) 1 lacune and 3) >1 lacunes as outcomes and were applied and tested in the validation cohort. Multivariable logistic model included age (regression B coefficient 1.10, 95% Confidence Interval [CI] 1.05-1.15), hypertension (2.05, 1.21-3.47), current smoking (7.64, 1.9-31.3) and depressive symptoms (7.26, 2.03-26.3) as independent predictors for severe WML defined as Fazeka’s rating of 2 and 3. A risk equation was constructed based on regression coefficient of these variables to generate a risk score for each subject. A receiver operating curve constructed to examine the ability of the risk score to differentiate subjects with and without severe WML revealed area under curve of 0.72 (0.66-0.77) for the derivation cohort and 0.60 (0.54-0.66), p=0.004 for the validation cohort. The optimal risk score cutoff of 7.46 was associated with a sensitivity of 0.37, specificity of 0.72, positive predictive value (PPV) of 32% and negative predictive value (NPV) of 77% in detecting severe WML in the validation cohort. Multivariable logistic regression for 1 lacune revealed hypertension (2.55, 1.34-4.84), history of central sleep apnoea (2.10, 1.11-3.94) and executive dysfunction (1.09, 10.2-1.16) as independent predictors. The AUC of risk scores in the validation cohort was 0.46 and not statistically significant (p=0.285). For the model of >1 lacunes, DM (2.05, 1.15-3.65) and family history of stroke (2.50, 1.13-5.50) were found to be significant predictors. AUC of risk scores in the validation cohort was 0.46 (0.39-0.54), statistically not significant (p=0.337). Overall, in this study we were able to develop a risk equation that can be used to screen community elderly persons for severe WML. Higher age, history of hypertension, current smoking and presence of depressive symptoms were independent risk factors for severe WML. However, note that the differentiating ability of the risk scores is relatively low as suggested by the low AUC of 0.60. As the purpose of this risk score is to identify persons for MRI examination which is costly, a cutoff score of 7.46 favoring specificity over sensitivity was chosen. With an acceptable specificity of 0.72 but relatively low sensitivity of 0.37, the risk score could correctly predict 77% of negative cases but 32% of positive cases.

471911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
471911.value: The overall low classification value of the risk equation developed based on clinical variables in predicting SBL reflects the heterogeneous and multifactorial nature of this disease associated with ageing in the non-disabled elderly population. We shall further examine the utility of sensitive biomarkers such as Transcranial Doppler measures to predict SBL burden with and without combining clinical variables obtained in this study. Moreover, our findings may also reflect the possibility that the SBL measures we used as outcomes may be insensitive in the associative analysis. Accordingly, to increase power in the detection of relationships between clinical variables and SBL markers on MRI, volumetric measures of WML is underway to re-explore the development of risk equation using continuous volumetric WML as outcome.

471911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
471911.value: Subclinical brain lesions are an age-related brain disease related to a wide range of poor health conditions in older adults. SBL can be detected on brain imaging such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). However, as MRI is expensive, there is a need for doctors to be able to select elderly persons at high risk of SVD for MRI examination. The objective of this study is to develop and validate a risk index for detection of SBL in community older adults without stroke and dementia. In a sample of 400 older adults we found that people who are older, are hypertensive and currently smoking and are more depressed are more likely to have SBL shown on MRI. We developed a risk index based on these risk factors and applied it to another 400 elderly persons with similar background including age, sex and frequency of vascular risk factors. The results showed that, although a positive risk index score detected only 32% of persons who actually have SBL on MRI, a negative score predicted 77% of people without SBL. In other words, the risk index can inform clinicians that older adults with a negative rating on the SBL risk index are unlikely to have SBL so that MRI may be unnecessary to save healthcare resources. On the other hand, older adults with a positive score may be considered for further assessment by brain MRI. In summary, the present study has made available a clinically useful risk prediction index to inform clinicians in their decisions for prescribing MRI for older persons based on their risk profile.

rows: To assess the effect of different treatment protocols on the degree of renal injury in patients with renal stones receiving extracorporeal shockwave lithotripsy

472111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
472111.value: Background: Although extracorporeal shockwave lithotripsy (SWL) is regarded as the most minimally invasive stone treatment procedure, increasing evidence suggests that SWL could lead to various short- and long-term complications, especially to the kidney. Common short- and long-term kidney injury includes renal haematoma, haematuria, renal fibrosis, renal function impairment and hypertension. Recently, animal studies have suggested that modification of the treatment protocols (low energy shockwave pretreatment protocol and pause-protection protocol) could help to decrease renal injury but up-to-date there is no clinical data to confirm these animal data and its effect on renal fibrosis. Therefore, we would like to perform a prospective study to evaluate the impact of these protocols in human subjects. Objectives To assess the effects of different treatment protocols on the degree of renal injury in patients with renal stones receiving SWL. Methodology: 320 patients with solitary radio-opaque renal stone, < 15mm, will be recruited. Baseline spot urine will be collected for measurement of a panel of urine markers for renal injury and renal fibrosis. Patients will then be randomized to receive either one of the shockwave (SW) protocols, (1) receiving 80% power (19.2kV) from the beginning till the end of treatment; (2) receiving the first 100 shocks at 40% power (9.6kV), followed by SWs at 80% power till the end of treatment; (3) receiving 100 shocks at 40% power, followed by a 3-minute pause and then further SWs at 80% power till the end of treatment; (4) receiving 100 shocks at 80% power, followed by a 3-minute pause and then further SWs at 80% power till the end of treatment. Further spot urine samples will be collected immediately after SWL, then at Day-2, Week-4, Week-12 and lastly Week-24. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or non-contrast computerized tomogram (NCCT) will be done on Day-2 after SWL for the detection of renal haematoma. Incidence of unplanned hospital attendance/admissions and complications will also be recorded for analysis. Outcome assessment: The primary outcome assessed is the incidence of renal haematoma developed after SWL as assessed by imainging on Day-2 after SWL. Secondary outcome parameters assessed include the change in urine markers for acute kidney injury and renal fibrosis, and also the incidence of unplanned hospital visits and complications within 30 days after SWL. By these comprehensive assessments, the impact of these modifications of treatment protocols could be assessed and the best approach to minimizing SWL related renal injury could be identified.

472111.label: Realisation of objectives
472111.value: The study aimed to use a comprehensive approach, including clinical parameters, imaging assessment and urine markers measurement, to assess the effect of two proposed treatment protocols on preventing SWL related renal injury and complications. Recruitment goal was achieved and there was no major problem encountered in the performance of study procedures. The default rate for the subject was also relatively low, for example, default rate for Day-2 imaging was only 6 (1.9%) patients. 35 patients (11.2%) had haematoma detected on day-2 imaging., and all were either subcapsular or perinephric haematoma, with no parenchymal haemorrhagic lesion detected. The number of patients developing haematoma in the 4 groups was 11 (14.10%), 9 (11.54%), 8 (10.13%), 7 (9.09%) respectively. There was no difference for the incidence of haematoma among the 4 groups. In our initial sample size calculation, we assumed the incidence of renal hematoma in control arm being around 35%, based on our own data and previous reports. However, the overall incidence of haematoma in our study was only 11.2%. We did not know the reason for this relatively lower incidence of imaging detected haematoma. As a result, our sample size might not have enough power to detect the actual effects of the two protocols on the formation of renal haematoma. However, if we also took into consideration of other clinical and laboratory end-points in these 320 patients, the clinical effects of the two protocols on renal protection might be less substantial than that suggested in porcine models. There were no clinical significant difference in the urinary level of both acute renal injury and renal fibrosis markers. In our initial proposal, we were originally planned to include measurement of TGF-beta as one of the markers for renal fibrosis. However, the urinary level of TGF-beta was not detectable in most of the sample (26 out of 30 samples), even with the use of different ELISA kits. In view of the use of PIIINP, a better renal fibrosis marker, this part of study for abandoned. During our study, we have observed the urinary level of PIIINP was continually raised upto 6 months after SWL and so we have extended the follow-up of our patients till one year. We observed the level of PIIINP was continually rising till 12 months after SWL. This relatively new observation might provide some insight about the effect of SWL on kidney fibrosis.

472111.label: Major findings and research outcome
472111.value: During January 2011 and July 2013, 320 patients fulfilled all the inclusion criteria and were then randomized into 1 of the 4 groups, with 80 cases in each group. Patients’ clinical characteristics and stone parameters were comparable between the four groups. Data of treatment parameters including stone characteristics and ESWL treatment factors were also collected. The average alfentanil received by the recruited patients was 0.43 ± 0.22 mg, and no difference was observed between groups. For the incidence of post-SWL haematoma, 35 patients (11.2%) had haematoma detected on day-2 imaging. The number of patients developing haematoma in the 4 groups was 11 (14.10%), 9 (11.54%), 8 (10.13%), 7 (9.09%) respectively. There was no difference for the incidence of haematoma among the 4 groups. Logistic regression analysis was performed to assess the potential risk factors for the development of haematoma. Treatment protocols did not have any relation to the formation of renal haematoma. Therefore, neither protocols could help to decrease the incidence of post-SWL haematoma. Seventeen patients (5.35%) had unplanned hospital attendance related to SWL, and there was again no difference observed in the 4 groups. For the acute renal injury markers, urinary levels of NAG, MA and IL-18 were significantly raised after SWL. However, at all the time points after treatment, there was no statistically significant difference between the level of these three markers between the four treatment groups. On the other hand, there was no significant change in the levels of NGAL, when compared to baseline level, in all the groups over different time points. There was no difference between the baseline levels of PIIINP among the 4 treatment groups. However, the mean levels of PIIINP for patients with 2 SWL before was significantly higher than those had 1 or no SWL before. There was a significant rise in PIIINP from 6 weeks till 1 year after SWL for all 4 groups. Within one year after SWL, there was no statistical significance in the incidence of deteriorated blood pressure control among the four groups. All these data has been presented in some of the major international meeting in the past two years. Best Paper award was granted in the World congress of Endourology and SWL in 2014. The full publication had been prepared for submission. Moreover, another publication on the effect of renal cortical thickness had been submitted and is currently under review.

472111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
472111.value: Our study provided a model of comprehensive assessment of the effect of various shockwave lithotripsy protocol and would help the further development of SWL. Our study also demonstrated the two protocol, namely pause-protection and low-energy pre-treatment protocols, did not show any significant effect on renal insult and other complications. Therefore, further studies would be needed to identify better approach to minimizing the complications of SWL.

472111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
472111.value: Although extracorporeal shockwave lithotripsy (SWL) is regarded as the most minimally invasive stone treatment procedure, increasing evidence suggests that SWL could lead to various short- and long-term renal complications. Animal studies have suggested that modification of the treatment protocols (low-energy shockwave pretreatment protocol and pause-protection protocol) could help to decrease renal injury but up-to-date there is no clinical data to confirm these animal data and its effect on renal fibrosis. Therefore, we would like to perform a prospective study, involving 320 patients, to evaluate the impact of these protocols in human subjects, in particular renal injury. However, from our result, both protocols did not significantly decrease the adverse outcomes, including renal haematoma, urinary kidney injury markers and clinical parameters. Moreover, SWL might have long-term and cumulative effect on renal fibrosis, which might in turn affect the long term kidney function of the patients. Therefore, further studies might be needed to identify better approach to prevent kidney injury during SWL.

473011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
473011.value: 軟骨下骨塌陷是激素性骨壞死破壞性修復導致的結果，其外科預後很差。由於激素性骨壞死破壞性修復的病生機制不清楚，需要在理解其機制的基礎上開發有效的干預策略。 相關的前期工作如下：（1）激素性骨壞死患者局部病灶存在持續的骨髓水腫和骨吸收亢進；（2）在建立的激素性骨壞死家兔模型中，破壞性修復病灶除了存在持續的骨髓水腫和骨吸收亢進，還伴隨著持續高表達的VEGF（細胞外分子）和磷酸化的Src（細胞內分子）；（3）已有的證據顯示持續高劑量的VEGF可以引起健康小鼠血管水腫和體外破骨細胞骨吸收功能亢進，同時持續高磷酸化的Src可以介導VEGF引起的血管水腫，並且Src基因敲除小鼠的破骨細胞功能受到抑制；（4）篩選獲得的兔特異性Src小核酸干擾序列能夠分別阻斷經過VEGF處理的體外培養的兔破骨細胞的功能亢進和血管內皮細胞之間連接蛋白複合體的顯著分離。因此，本項研究的假設是啟動的VEGF-Src信號途徑參與了激素性骨壞死破壞性修復的病生機制。為了檢驗該假設，應用建立的家兔激素性骨壞死模型來開展如下兩個方面的工作：第一部分的工作是分別通過補充和中和VEGF來研究 VEGF在破壞性修復機制中的作用；第二部分的工作是在補充或者不補充VEGF的前提下，通過Src小核酸來研究阻斷Src在破壞性修復機制中的作用。灌注性核磁共振技術、基於顯微CT的血管造影和骨小梁三維結構測量、骨形態計量學參數、骨髓透射電鏡、免疫組織化學和western blot定量將用於檢驗我們的研究假設。 本研究的成果將有助於建立 VEGF-Src 信號途徑參與激素性骨壞死破壞性修復進程的機制以及開發潛在針對Src 的小核酸藥物向臨床轉化。

473011.label: Realisation of objectives
473011.value: As described in 5.1, we have realized all two main study objectives as sated above and listed with as well from the original proposal: 1 To determine the role of VEGF in destructive repair by supplement and neutralization of VEGF, respectively; 2 To determine the role of Src activation in destructive repair through blocking Src by Src siRNA with and without supplement of VEGF. For achieving objective 1: Destructive repair taking place in SAON was induced in male adult rabbit. At 2, 4, 6 weeks after induction, VEGF, anti-VEGF, and saline control were intramedullary injected into proximal femur respectively. Vascularization and permeability were quantified by dynamic magnetic resonance imaging (DCE MRI). At week 6 after induction, bilateral proximal femora were dissected for micro-CT trabecular architecture with finite element analysis (FEA), micro-CT-based angiography, and histological analysis. FEA was used to simulate the compression test on the subchondral bone. For histological analysis, destructive repair and reparative osteogenesis in each treatment group were evaluated, intraosseous blood vessel density, edema area and adipocyte area were quantified, the ratio of eroded surface to total bone surface (ES/BS), and the osteoclast number per bone perimeter (N.Oc/B.Pm) were determined by Histomorphometry. TRAP was stained to evaluate the morphology of osteoclasts in each group. In vitro study was also performed for the mechanism of the role of VEGF in destructive repair. For achieving objective 2: Destructive repair taking place in SAON was induced in male adult rabbit. At 2, 4, 6 weeks after induction, Src siRNA, Src siRNA+VEGF, control siRNA and the saline control were intramedullary injected into proximal femur respectively. Knockdown efficiency of Src was tested by real-time PCR and immunohitochemistry. Vascularization and permeability were quantified by dynamic magnetic resonance imaging (DCE MRI). At week 6 after induction, bilateral proximal femora were dissected for micro-CT trabecular architecture with finite element analysis (FEA), micro-CT-based angiography, and histological analysis. FEA was used to simulate the compression test on the subchondral bone. For histological analysis, destructive repair and reparative osteogenesis in each treatment group were evaluated, intraosseous blood vessel density, edema area and adipocyte area were quantified, the ratio of eroded surface to total bone surface (ES/BS), and the osteoclast number per bone perimeter (N.Oc/B.Pm) were determined by Histomorphometry. TRAP was stained to evaluate the morphology of osteoclasts in each group. In vitro study was also performed for the mechanism of the role of Src activation in destructive repair.

473011.value: As we proposed, our in vivo findings confirmed our pilot studies: Histological evaluations demonstrated that VEGF enhanced destructive repair while anti-VEGF prevented destructive repair; blocking Src by Src siRNA prevented destructive repair and enhanced reparative osteogenesis no matter with or without supplement of VEGF. The features of the intraosseous vasculature determined by angiography and histomorphometry were consistent with those determined by DCE MRI that Src siRNA inhibited VEGF-mediated vascular hyperpermeability but preserved VEGF-induced neovascularization. Bone resorption was enhanced in VEGF group and inhibited in anti-VEGF, blocking Src groups as determined by both 3D microCT and 2D histomorphometry. FEA showed higher failure load in Src blocking groups when compared to that analyzed for VC group. We summarized our findings in a manuscript that is about to submit to a leading medical journal (Appendix I – Paper 3). On the other hand, our in vitro findings confirmed our studies and showed the mechanism in cellular level: VEGF enhanced Src bioactivity through promoting the phosphorylation of Src at Y416. For maintaining endothelial junction integrity via decreasing VEGF-mediating higher vascular permeability, Src blockade significantly relieved actin stress and the formation of caveolae and VVOs induced by VEGF, and stabilized the complex-catenin/VE-cadherin/Flk-1 through decreasing phosphorylation of VE-cadherin. In addition, VEGF promoted osteoclasts formation and function without affecting the adhesion activity and cytoskeleton. Src blockade significantly impaired cytoskeleton resulting in a lower adhesion activity through down-regulation of phosphorylation of Src, Pyk2 and Cbl, and ultimately inhibited osteoclasts formation and function. The major findings were submitted to and are under review of a leading metabolic journal (Cao HJ, et al. Bone, 2014 – Appendix I – Paper 2). In summary, we have trained two PhD students with outcomes summarized in 3 SCI journal papers for leading orthopaedic and related medical journals (1 published in Nat Med with a copy submitted last time for our interim report – Appendix I - Paper 1, 1 under review, 1 prepared for submission) that fully addressed the study objectives of the funded proposal.

(http://www.ribobio.com/) to collaborate for clinical testing. We have jointly drafted an intention for large grant application for National High-tech R&D Program (863 Program) together with Prof. Biliang ZHANG to support our further development of the research (Appendix II).

473011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
473011.value: Steroid -associated osteonecrosis (SAON) often occurred in patients with an intensive corticosteroid taken for life-saving or disease- modifying. For example, about one third patients with Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) suffered from osteonecrosis after steroid treatment. In an advanced stage of osteonecrosis, patients will have total joint replacement when the dead bone collapsed. Our previous research showed that the destructive repair of osteonecrosis, which was causing collapse, accompanied with blood vessel leakages in the destructive repair region of osteonecrosis and highly activated bone resorption. We also fund high Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF) expression and highly activated Src with destructive repair. Furthermore, it was reported that VEGF enhances bone resorption and blood vessel permeability. Src, as a downstream molecule of VEGF, participates in VEGF induced blood vessel permeability. Src also participated in mediating bone resorption. Our current project successfully confirmed that blockage of VEGF-Src signaling pathway could inhibit blood vessel permeability and bone resorption so to be able to prevent destructive repair in SAON and the way of blocking Src could be a novel therapeutic strategy for patients in early stage of SAON osteonecrosis to prevent joint collapse.

473111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
473111.value: The recently ended H1N1 pandemic and the sporadic poultry-to-human transmissions of avian influenza H5N1 have been causing huge concerns in government, scientific communities and the general public. For combating the disease and increasing our preparedness against future outbreaks, it is essential to know more on how the influenza virus functions by studying the various protein it encodes. The ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complex is the essential transcription-replication machinery in influenza virus. It is composed of the trimeric polymerase (PA, PB1 and PB2), nucleoprotein (NP) and RNA. NP binds to PB1 and PB2 subunits within the RNP and the interactions are thought to be crucial for the proper functioning of the polymerase. In this proposal, we aim at investigating the interaction between NP and PB2 in details, in order to understand the role of NP in the RNP complex. We have recently solved the atomic structure of NP while other groups have determined the structure of PB2 C-terminal region. By surface plasmon resonance and nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, we have found that NP interacts with the PB2 C-terminal 627-domain spanning aa 538-693. As an effort to understand how NP interacts with PB2 to form the ribonucleoprotein, we propose to study the interaction of NP and PB2 C-terminal region in detail. We shall first identify the residues on NP and PB2 C-terminal region that are involved in the interaction by NMR chemical shift, molecular docking, chemical cross-linking and mass spectrometry. These residues will be systematically mutated and their functional significances towards RNP assembly, RNP activity and virus survival will be investigated by co-immunoprecipitation, RNP reconstitution assay, surface plasmon resonance and virus rescue technique. To show how NP and PB2 interact in accurate molecular details, we shall attempt to determine the complex structure by x-ray crystallography. Since the interaction between NP and the N-terminal region of PB2 is still uncertain, we shall re-visit this issue for planning our second phase of study. The proposed work will result in the identification of the interacting surfaces of NP-PB2 interaction. This will increase our knowledge in the assembly of RNP complex. The surfaces are also potential drug targets which may be used for in silico drug screening for the identification of anti-influenza agents. 最近爆發的H1N1流感和不時由禽畜傳染給人類的H5N1流感均引起社會各界的關注。為了更好的防治流感病毒，我們應加強研究它的蛋白質及其作用。 流感病毒的核糖核蛋白複合體(RNP)負責流感病毒的轉錄和複製。它是由一個三聚體的聚合酶(PA, PB1和PB2)，核蛋白(NP)和RNA組成。聚合酶的運作與NP和PB1及PB2的相互作用有關。此研究旨在深入考察NP和PB2的相互作用，以了解NP在RNP的角式。 我們和其它研究小組最近分別解析NP和PB2的C末端區域的結構。利用表面等離子共振技術和核磁共振技術我們發現NP和PB2的C末端aa538-693相互作用。我們建議首先找出進行相互作用的胺基酸並研究這些胺基酸對RNP的集合，活性和病毒生長的重要性。我們也嘗試生長NP和PB2複合物的晶體。因NP和PB2N末端區域的相互作用並未有定論，我們將重新檢示，為將來的研究作準備。 此項研究，使我們了解NP和PB2的相互作用區感，並增加對RNP集合的認識。NP和PB2相互作用區域的發現，將有助利用通過計算機篩選流感病毒的抑制物。

473111.label: Realisation of objectives
473111.value: 1. By ribonucleoprotein assay, we first found that R150 in nucleoprotein NP is important for maintaining an active polymerase in H5 background and changing it to R150A rendered the polymerase inactive. By swapping the different polymerase subunits of H1 and H5 subtypes, we showed that PB2 subunit is responsible for the active polymerase phenotypes. By swapping the different regions of the H1 and H5 polymerase PB2 and carried out ribonucleoprotein assay, we found that the C-terminal ‘627’ domains of PB2 is responsible for the interaction with NP. Positive charges at PB2 627 and 630 were then found to be important for forming a functional RNP. It is crucial to have R150 in NP, if there is a positively charged residue at PB2 630, but not a positive charge at PB2 627. With the positive charge at PB2 627 and 630, we also identified the increase binding of PB2 to NP in surface plasmon resonance study. Such effect was found to be direct and independent of RNA. Surface plasmon resonance study has been performed and confirmed that NP residues 146-185 are involved in interaction with PB2 ‘627’ domain. The role of this stretch of residue was further confirmed by the fact that deletion mutant of NP lacking these residues could not bind to ‘627’ domain. 2. Surface plasmon resonance study has been performed and confirmed that NP residues 146-185 are involved in interaction with PB2 ‘627’ domain. A nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) chemical shift perturbation (CSP) study has been performed. N15-labelled PB2 ‘627’ domain was titrated against NP 146-185 and full length. The resultant 15N-HSQC spectra have suggested the putative residues (aa 601 to 607) in PB2 ‘627’ domain interacted with NP 146-185. Surface plasmon resonance and ribonucleoprotein assay were employed to confirm the role of these residues by immobilizing mutant PB2C. We shall further confirm that the mutations in PB2 '627' domain have not perturbed the polymerase activity by a minireplicon system in Prof. Ervin Fodor's laboratory in Oxford, UK. 3. Attempts have been made to co-crystallize PB2 ‘627’ domain and either NP full length or NP 146-185, using various crystallization kits from Hampton and Jena Bioscience and temperatures of 4C, 16C and 20C. Purification of the two proteins separately and together have also been carried out. However, no diffractable crystals containing both proteins have been produced so far. 4. In co-immunoprecipitation study, the cap-binding domain of PB2 was found to interact with NP. This interaction was shown to be RNA-mediated and independent of the cap-binding activity of the domain. 473111.label: Major findings and research outcome
473111.value: 1. NP 150R, PB2 627K and PB2 630R are crucial to NP-polymerase functional association Using RNP reconstitution assay with gene swapped polymerase, we demonstrated that NP R150A could only form functional association with polymerase with H1, but not H5, PB2. Specifically, the functional association of NP and PB2 involved NP 150R, and either 627K or 630R of PB2. We further showed that PB2 contains more positive charges at 627 and 630 led to stronger NP-polymerase interaction and higher RNP activity. Using SPR, such interaction was found to be direct and independent of RNA. The above results have been published (Ng et al., 2012). 2. NP 146-185 is responsible for binding PB2 ‘627’ domain Residue 146-185 of NP has been identified to interact with PB2 ‘627’ domain. In surface plasmon resonance study, this stretch of residues interacts with PB2 ‘627’ domain with KD of 927 nM, which is about 3.6 folds higher than that of full-length NP (252 nM). Mutant NP with this region removed cannot interact with ‘627’ domain in vitro. 3. PB2 601-607 is perturbed by NP in chemical shift perturbation study A nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) chemical shift perturbation (CSP) study has been performed. N15-labelled PB2 ‘627’ domain was titrated against NP 146-185 and full length to determine PB2 ‘627’ domain residues involved in the interaction. Q601 to L607 of PB2 ‘627’ domain were significantly perturbed in both experiments, suggesting their possible role in interacting with NP. 4. Mutations on PB2 601-606 lowers RNP activity Residues 601-607 were mutated and assayed for their RNP activity. Mutations on PB2 601-606 resulted in partial to complete disruption of RNP activity, while mutation on PB2 607 resulted in insignificant change in RNP activity. 5. PB2 601-606 are involved in interaction with NP Surface plasmon resonance was performed to test for the importance of PB2 601-606 in interacting with NP. Wild type PB2C or variants were immobilized on CM5 chip surface. NP monomeric mutant R416A was injected into the system in ascending concentration. The KD of the interaction between PB2C WT and NP R416A was close to that of NP WT (279nM vs 252nM). All six variants of PB2C did not interact with NP. A manuscript covering point 2-5 has been prepared. 6. PB2 cap-binding domain binds to NP via RNA without the involvement of cap-binding activity In co-immunoprecipitation study, the cap-binding domain of PB2 was found to interact with NP. This interaction is RNA-mediated and is independent of the cap-binding activity of the domain.

This system consists of the polymerase complex only and has been shown to transcribe RNA without the involvement of NP. Shaw's team has found that the cap-binding domain of PB2 can interact with NP. 473111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
473111.value: The genome of influenza A virus is packaged into eight ribonucleoprotein complexes, which comprised of an RNA polymerase (a complex of three proteins: PA, PB1 and PB2), nucleoprotein (NP) and the RNA. The proper formation and functioning of ribonucleoprotein complex is critical to the survival of the virus. This study reveals the molecular details of the interaction between NP and PB2 C-terminal region by various biophysical experiments, and shows that a disruption of this interaction can be detrimental to the virus replication by measuring polymerase acvitity in live cells. Since all strains of influenza A virus share this same interaction, the results obtained in this study leads to the possibility of designing drug specifically to disrupt the interaction, and therefore develop a cure of the disease.

473211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
473211.value: Skeletal myogenesis or the development of skeletal muscles involves the specification and differentiation of muscle precursor cells (myoblasts) into myotubes. It is controlled by a complex regulatory network of interacting factors. Disruption of the regulatory network could result in muscle related disease. Transcription factor (TF) is a protein that binds to a specific DNA sequence, thereby controlling the transcription of genetic information from DNA to mRNA. microRNAs (miRNAs) are non-coding single-stranded RNAs of ~22 nucleotides and constitute a novel class of gene regulators that regulate gene expression at post-transcriptional level. Emerging evidence in recent years demonstrated the essential function of TF-miRNA regulatory circuitries in skeletal myogenesis. Previously we identified Yin yang1 (YY1) as a repressor of myogenesis which regulates muscle specific genes as well as miR-29 family. The dysregulation of YY1-miR-29 circuitry contributes to the formation of Rhabdomyosarcoma, a skeletal muscle originated tumor. Considering the prevalence of YY1 binding sites in the genome, we speculate that many other miRNAs could be regulated by YY1, forming numerous functional regulatory circuitries. To test the above hypothesis, we propose to conduct genome-wide identification of YY1-miRNA regulatory circuitries using a newly developed technology, ChIP-seq. Subsequently, we will validate the functionality of identified TF-miRNA regulatory circuitries by a number of complementary methods. Lastly, we will integrate our identified TF-miRNA circuitries together with other validated circuitries from the literature into a web-based database Myogenesis transcription factor-microRNA Regulatory Circuitry Database (MRCDB). Findings from the above proposed studies will enhance our understanding of gene regulation involving TF-miRNA regulatory circuitries, provide an invaluable database for community wide reference, and eventually offer potential avenues for the diagnosis and treatment of muscle-relevant diseases by targeting dysregulated TF-miRNA circuitries.

473211.label: Realisation of objectives
473211.value: This study was undertaken to identify transcription factor-microRNA regulatory circuitries in skeletal muscle differentiation using chromatin immunoprecipitation coupled with massively parallel sequencing (ChIP-seq). In the original grant proposal, we hypothesized that miRNAs can be regulated by transcription factor (TF) YY1, forming functional regulatory circuitries. To test the above hypothesis, we propose to conduct (i) genome-wide identification of YY1-miRNA regulatory circuitries using ChIP-seq; (ii) We will validate the functionality of identified YY1-miRNA regulatory circuitries by a number of complementary methods; (iii) We will integrate our identified YY1-miRNA circuitries together with other validated circuitries from the literature into a web-based database for community use. We are pleased to report that all three aims have been successfully completed.

473211.label: Major findings and research outcome
473211.value: The major findings and research outcome are: (1) we are the first to publish the genome-wide YY1 binding profiles during myogenesis using ChIP-seq (Lu et al., EMBO J. 2013); Furthermore, we demonstrate that YY1 can regulate miRNAs and form regulatory circuitries to control myogenesis and these circuitries can be extended to include a novel class of noncoding RNA regulators (i.e. large intergenic noncoding RNA (lincRNA)) (Lu et al., EMBO J. 2013, and Lu et al. PLoS One 2012, partially supported by CUHK direct grant MD09302 for preliminary data and declared in this grant application). Last, we integrated our findings as well as other published resources associated with YY1 and its target genes into an integrated database, namely YY1TargetDB (http://myogenesisdb.org/YY1TargetDB), as a community resources for YY1 and its regulated circuitries (Guo et al., Database, 2013). Overall, the major outcome from the grant has revealed both the regulation and the function of miRNAs and lincRNAs in muscle differentiation. It also demonstrated the functional roles of the YY1-miRNA/lincRNA regulatory circuitries in myogenesis. In addition, the results also provide an invaluable database for community wide reference. Together, the outcome of this grant enhanced our understanding of gene regulation mechanisms in myogenesis with genomic approaches and can open a potentially new avenue for the diagnosis and treatment of muscle diseases.

473211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
473211.value: Our study has identified YY1-miRNA regulatory circuitries and demonstrated their functions in myogenesis. In addition to miRNAs, we also identified a novel class of noncoding regulator, namely large intergenic noncoding RNA (lincRNA), which can also be regulated and integrated into YY1 mediated regulatory circuitries. Given the functional roles of many newly identified lincRNAs are unclear, the integration of key TF, miRNA and lincRNA into TF mediated regulatory circuitries togehter with other sequencing data (e.g., RNA-seq) has potential to be used for developing novel bioinformatics platform for lincRNA functional prediction, which has been urgently needed from the community.

473211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
473211.value: Transcription factors (TFs) and microRNAs (miRNAs) are two groups of key regulators of gene expression in eukaryotes. The interplay between TFs and miRNAs has been demonstrated to be instrumental for the control of cellular differentiation and embryonic development. A number of TF-miRNA circuitries were identified to function in regulating the skeletal muscle development (myogenesis). The dysregulation of these circuitries contribute to the development of muscle related diseases. However, the majority of TF-miRNAs circuitries still wait to be discovered in order to achieve a global understanding of the regulatory network in myogenesis. To fulfill the above purpose, we have generated the first high-resolution, genome-wide maps of binding sites for key transcription factor Yin Yang1 (YY1), a pleiotropic transcription factor, functions as a repressor of myogenesis by targeting both muscle specific genes and miRNAs, using massive parallel sequencing of chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP-seq). We further revealed the gene regulatory circuitries, which are regulated by YY1 and involve both miRNAs and large intergenic noncoding RNAs (lincRNAs), play functional roles in myogenesis. In addition, an YY1 target gene database (YY1TargetDB) has been launched as a resource for community use, which has been proven helpful as investigators continue to probe the roles of TFs and miRNAs in skeletal muscle formation, disease, and the therapeutic treatment.

473611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
473611.value: The goal of this research project is to reveal the function of EMB15 and the potential mechanism by which Emb15 controls embryogenesis in maize seed development. Embryo development is a highly orchestrated process that guides seed formation. Understanding its mechanisms has direct implications in agriculture because embryo contributes to seed viability, nutrition and yield. A major effort in recent years has been to identify the genes regulating this process. However, because mutations in these genes often cause embryo lethality, functions of many of them remain unknown or obscure. emb15 is a recessive embryo lethal mutant in maize. Loss of Emb15 function did not affect the endosperm development, but arrested the embryogenesis. We have cloned Emb15 by transposon tagging. Predicted EMB15 protein did not show significant similarity to any eukaryotic proteins with a known function, rather it showed similarity to a prokaryotic protein of obscure function by having a RimM domain and a PRC domain. These domains are implicated in protein-protein /protein-RNA interactions. Interestingly, EMB15 was localized in the plastid and the nucleus, implying a potential functional connection via EMB15 between the two organelles. Based on the preliminary data and circumstantial evidence, we hypothesize that EMB15 exists in a protein/RNA complex and functions in regulating plastidic gene expression. We reason that by identifying the EMB15 associated components together with functional genetic analysis will reveal the function of EMB15. Further molecular analysis on EMB15 during seed development will provide insights to the mechanism of EMB15 in controlling embryogenesis in maize. Maize has been a powerful model system for functional genomics on seed development in the grain crops, because its reference genome has recently been sequenced, mutants and transposon mutagenesis are available and functional tools are increasing. Elucidation of Emb15 function will facilitate understanding of the mechanism governing embryogenesis in a major crop; hence provides guiding information for crop improvement. Because EMB15 belongs to a class of RimM/PRC proteins with unknown functions, this study will potentially shed light on functions of related proteins in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes. 該研究的目標是揭示EMB15的功能並了解其在玉米胚胎髮生和發育過程中的潛在機制。在種子形成過程中，胚胎的發生和發育是一個高度協調的過程。由於胚胎髮育與種子活力，營養和產量密切相關，因此了解胚胎發生和發育的機制對糧食生產至關重要。近年來，鑑別控制胚胎發生和發育的基因一直是企業界和學術界的重點研究領域之一。然而，由於這些基因的突變往往導致胚胎致死，研究比較困難，因此許多基因的功能目前仍不清楚。 玉米emb15是一個隱性、純合胚胎致死的突變體。Emb15功能的喪失抑制胚胎髮育，但不影響胚乳的發育。利用轉座子標籤技術，我們克隆了Emb15。EMB15與已知功能的真核生物蛋白質沒有顯著的相似性，但與原核生物的RimM蛋白質有一定的相似性，都含有一個RimM結構域和一個PRC結構域。這兩個結構域被認為與蛋白質/蛋白質、蛋白質/RNA相互作用有關。EMB15蛋白質存在於葉綠體和細胞核中，意味著EMB15可能具有潛在的協調功能，同時在兩個細胞器發揮功能。根據我們的初步結果和間接證據，我們推測EMB15與RNA結合形成複合體，調節質體的基因表達。因此，查明與EMB15相結合的元件並結合遺傳功能分析將揭示EMB15的功能，而進一步的分子生物學分析將為揭示EMB15控制玉米胚胎發育的機制提供重要信息。 玉米一直是糧食作物種子發育功能基因組學的重要模式植物之一，這主要因為玉米有豐富的突變體資源、方便的轉座子突變系統、良好的遺傳背景累積，加上全基因組的測序，以及種子便於分析觀察等原因。對玉米EMB15的功能的研究將有助於揭示這一重要作物胚胎發育的機制。此外，由於EMB15屬於一種未知功能的RimM/PRC類蛋白質，查明EMB15的功能也將有助於揭示此類蛋白質在真核和原核生物中的功能。

473611.label: Major findings and research outcome
473611.value: Objective 1. The Emb15 mutation is embryo lethal such that the point of embryogenesis arrest in the mutant provides insights on the functional requirement of Emb15 for embryogenesis. We specifically analyzed the embryogenesis profile from 5 days after pollination (DAP) to detect early events by section and microscopic observation. The result indicates that the arrest of the embryogenesis in the emb15 mutant is very early. At 5DAP, the mutant embryo showed dramatic developmental retardation in comparison to the WT. And even at maturity, the embryo stays before reaching the transition stage. This suggests that Emb15 is required for very early embryogenesis process. Objective 2. We performed RT-PCR analysis on Emb15 expression in various tissues and during embryo and endosperm development. Both genes are highly expressed in various tissues especially green tissues such as leaves and stem, reflecting an essential role of Emb15 in plastid development. Emb15 was also found highly expressed in embryos and endosperms during seed formation. As emb15 mutant is embryo specific, the expression in endosperm tissues and no phenotype was detected is interesting. We believe that endosperm development was also affected, but at different extent. Hence we will analyze the endosperm development in our next analysis. Objective 3. The genetic analysis of EMB15 function in complementation to E. coli mutants has been finished. ΔrimM strain in the background of E. coli A19 was provided by Prof. Hyouta Himeno from Hirosaki University, Japan. Genotype of A19 is Hfr(PO21) rna19 gdhA2 his-95 relA1 spoT1 metB1, and that of A19ΔrimM is Hfr(PO21) rna19 gdhA2 his-95 relA1 spoT1 metB1 rimM::FRT, whose rimM gene was replaced with a short FRT sequence. We have constructed the coding region of EMB15 cDNA into pET28a and pUC19, and transformed the constructs into ΔrimM strain. As shown in Figure 5, although A19ΔrimM vector control grows very slowly, but A19ΔrimM with EMB15 grows much faster, only slightly slower than A19 vector control. This suggests that EMB15 works as rimM in E. coli, and function of this gene is highly conserved throughout prokaryotic organisms to higher plants. Objective 4. We propose that EMB15 protein may interact with a partner protein or RNA in exerting its function based on the presence of the RimM and PRC domain. Thus, identification of this partner molecule will provide key information to the function of EMB15. We employed a co-immuno-precipitation approach for this analysis. Two more papers are on the way to publish these results.

473611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
473611.value: In several areas, we exceeded our expectation. The following areas have been addressed but will need further experimentations: a. We found Emb15 codes for two proteins. What roles are they? b. EMB15 protein is dual-localized in the nucleus and the plastids. Again roles? c. Function of EMB15 homolgous gene rimM in E. coli is not clear. d. Function of UDPGP domain of EMB15 is worthy more detailed study.

473611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
473611.value: The Emb15 mutation of maize is embryo-lethal but the arrest of embryogenesis provides an opportunity to study the function of the gene involved. We therefore studied the detailed embryogenesis in the mutant, expressed the Emb15 gene in maize and E. coli and identified the EMB15 associated proteins/RNAs. At the start of this project, we proposed that the Emb15 encodes a RimM protein that likely functions in the ribosome assembly. During our cloning of the Emb15 cDNA, we found different versions of the cDNA, suggesting alternative splicing with Emb15. We found two major types of transcripts, a short version and a longer version with a part of last exon spliced. The longer version extended to include four more exons. The previous short version predicts a RimM like protein containing a Rim and PRC domain. Whereas the longer version predicts a larger protein that contains a domain has significant similarity to UDP-glucose pyrophosphotase (UDPGP). The fused version of RimM and UDPGP is unique to plants, not present in prokaryotes or animals. This finding suggests that there may be two proteins encoded by the Emb15 gene, depending on the alternative splicing of intron 4.

473711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
473711.value: This project aims at studying the effect of vitamin D and calcium supplementation on mammographic density among premenopausal Chinese women. Breast cancer is the most commonly diagnosed female cancer in Hong Kong. Animal studies have shown that vitamin D and calcium play important protective roles against breast cancer. Epidemiological studies reveal that the associations between vitamin D and calcium intakes and breast cancer risk may differ by menopausal status. Among postmenopausal women, most observational studies and several clinical trials find no significant reduction in breast cancer risk with higher intakes of vitamin D and calcium. Among premenopausal women, however, the majority of observational studies report a reduced breast cancer risk with higher intakes of these nutrients. Increased mammographic density is a factor strongly associated with an increased risk of breast cancer, and several cross-sectional and longitudinal studies indicate that higher intakes of vitamin D and calcium are associated with decreased mammographic density among premenopausal women. Therefore, epidemiological evidence suggests that intakes of vitamin D and calcium may reduce breast cancer risk through decreasing mammographic density among premenopausal women. Unfortunately, no randomized clinical trial has ever been conducted to investigate the effect of vitamin D and calcium supplementation on mammographic density among premenopausal, particularly Chinese women. We propose to conduct a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blinded clinical trial among premenopausal Chinese women in Hong Kong to address this research question. Women aged 40-49 years will be randomly assigned to either an intervention or a placebo group. The intervention group will take a daily dose of 800 IU vitamin D and 1000 mg calcium. Each group will have 218 participants and both groups will be followed-up for one year and receive baseline and follow-up mammograms. The effect size of the supplementation will be estimated as the difference of changes in percent mammographic density from baseline to follow-up between the intervention and placebo groups using intention-to-treat analysis. Given the strength of the association between mammographic density and breast cancer risk, the findings of this project would offer new insights on the current debate about the role of vitamin D and calcium in breast cancer etiology and prevention. The protective effect of vitamin D and calcium against breast cancer development through decreasing mammographic density, if established, would have important implications on public health. This would provide a safe, modifiable, and inexpensive way to prevent breast cancer incidence as well as reduce mortality and premature deaths. 此項課題旨在研究在絕經前婦女中補充維他命D及鈣劑是否會降低乳房密度。 乳癌是香港婦女中發病率最高的一種癌癥。動物實驗發現維他命D和鈣對乳癌有重要的保護作用。流行病學研究表明維他命D和鈣的攝入與乳癌的關係在絕經前和絕經后的婦女中有所不同。在絕經后婦女中，大多數的觀察性研究以及一些臨床實驗并沒有發現增加維他命D和鈣的攝入會降低乳癌的風險。而在絕經前婦女中，絕大多數的觀察性研究都發現增加這兩種營養素的攝入會降低乳癌風險。高乳房密度會大大增加婦女罹患乳癌的危險，而一些橫斷面和長期性研究表明增加維他命D和鈣的攝入會降低絕經前婦女的乳房密度。因此，流行病學證據顯示維他命D和鈣的攝入可能降低乳房密度，從而降低絕經前婦女罹患乳腺癌的風險。然而，到目前為止，并沒有任何臨床實驗專門研究在絕經前，尤其是華裔婦女中補充維他命D及鈣劑是否會降低乳房密度。 因此，我們擬開展一項隨機對照雙盲臨床實驗來研究這一課題。參加者為年齡介于40-49歲的絕經前華裔婦女。此臨床實驗將採用隨機分組的方法，將參加者分為兩組：一組為干預組，另一組為對照組。干預組將每天服用兩粒維他命D及鈣補充劑，每粒補充劑含400國際單位維他命D及500毫克鈣，每天補充總量為800國際單位維他命D及1000毫克鈣。對照組需每天服用兩粒安慰劑，但不含有維他命D及鈣或任何其它營養素。每組參加者人數為218人，服用和跟進時間均為一年。兩組參加者都需接受兩次乳房X光造影檢查：在服用補充劑或安慰劑之前有一次基線檢查，在服用補充劑或安慰劑一年之後則有一次跟進檢查，以此觀察維他命D及鈣補充劑是否會影響乳房密度的變化。補充劑的效果將通過計算和比較干預組和對照組平均乳房密度的變化而得出。 鑒於乳房密度是婦女罹患乳癌最強的危險因素之一，此項研究的結果對目前關於維他命D及鈣在腫瘤病因學以及腫瘤預防中的作用的討論將會提供新的依據。一旦維他命D及鈣通過降低乳房密度從而降低乳癌危險的保護作用能夠確立，這將會對整個公共衛生也有著重大意義，因為這對降低乳癌的發病率以及減少因乳癌導致的死亡提供了一個安全可行而并不昂貴的方法。

474111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
474111.value: Primary angle-closure glaucoma（PACG）is characterized by closure of the anterior chamber drainage angle by appositional or synechial approximation of the iris against the trabecular meshwork, blocking the access to aqueous humor, resulting in an elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) followed by the progressive development of irreversible glaucomatous optic neuropathy. The prevalence of angle closure glaucoma was highest amongst Chinese (1.26%), affecting over 7 million Chinese by 2010. Angle closure glaucoma was reported to be responsible for 91% of bilateral glaucoma blindness in China. In Hong Kong, glaucoma remains the most important cause of irreversible blindness, accounting for almost one-quarter of all cases of irreversible blindness. The treatment of PACG involves the lowering of IOP by drugs, laser, or surgery. Conventionally, the target of treatment is to lower IOP to within the ‘normal’ range, i.e. below 21 mmHg, whether in clinical practice or as a criterion for treatment success in PACG research. Recent clinical trials in primary open angle glaucoma (POAG) revealed that even within the normal range of IOP, maintaining the IOP within a lower bracket was associated with less visual field deterioration. This has been cited as evidence for the need to aim for a target IOP lower than the population mean (16 mmHg) in POAG eyes, especially in the more advanced cases. Similar published data are not available for PACG. Our earlier pilot study suggested a similar relationship between IOP and visual field progression in PACG, but our sample size, follow up duration, and study design did not allow a firm conclusion. A more recent study by Sharmini et al also suggested a similar relationship in PACG, but the retrospective nature and the suboptimal definitions of disease progression in that study resulted in only a suggestive conclusion. This study aims to clearly define the correlation between IOP and disease progression in treated PACG, especially within the ‘normal’ range of IOP. Disease progression is defined in accordance with internationally-recognized standards as for POAG, and also with the help of the state-of-the-art imaging technology (spectral-domain optical coherence tomography – SD-OCT) that allows quantitative documentation of the retinal nerve fiber layer thickness. This technology was not available to the earlier landmark studies that correlate IOP to disease progression in POAG eyes. The results of this study will have an important impact on the treatment strategy for PACG. 原發性閉角型青光眼(PACG)指以房角關閉為特徵的青光眼性視覺神經疾病，是由於虹膜異常肥厚堵塞小梁網或與小梁網產生粘連，房水外流受阻，引起眼壓（IOP）升高，進而導致進展性、不可修復的視覺損傷。閉角型青光眼在中國人群中的患病率最高（1.26%），2010年超過700萬的中國人患閉角型青光眼。據報導，中國因青光眼導致全盲的患者中有91%是由於閉角型青光眼。在香港，青光眼仍是導致不可逆性盲的最主要原因，約占四分之一。 PACG的治療主要是通過藥物、鐳射或外科手術降低眼壓。無論在臨床實踐中還是科研中作為一項有效治療PACG的指標，通常都將眼壓降至正常範圍內，即21mmHg 以下。最新的原發性開角型青光眼（POAG）的臨床研究顯示，即使將眼壓降至並保持在正常範圍，並不一定能有效控制視野缺損的進一步惡化。這為設定目標眼壓的必要性提供了依據，同時也指出，尤其是晚期POAG的患者，應將眼壓控制在正常人眼壓平均值（16mmHg）以下。但這些公佈資料並不一定適用於PACG。我們前期的試驗研究發現，PACG的眼壓與視野缺損的進展之間存在類似的關聯，但是基於我們的樣本量、隨訪時間以及實驗設計尚不能得出明確結論。近期，Sharmini et al 對PACG的研究也提出了相似的關聯問題，但因其為回顧性研究，且缺乏對疾病進展的標準化定義，因此也只能得出建議性的結論。 本項研究的目的是要確立治療中的PACG的眼壓和疾病進展的相關性。我們依照國際公認對POAG的標準定義疾病的進展，同時借助現代化成像技術（高清頻域光學相干斷層掃描器--SD-OCT）提供視網膜纖維層厚度的量化記錄。在先前POAG的眼壓與疾病進展關聯的重大研究中也沒能應用此項技術。本項研究的結果將會對完善PACG的治療策略起重要作用。

474711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
474711.value: Embryonic stem cells (ESCs), derived from the inner cell mass of blastocysts, are capable of self-renewal and are pluripotent, meaning that they can propagate indefinitely in culture and have the ability to give rise to all differentiated cell types in the body. ESCs can therefore be an excellent source of specialized cells for research and future therapeutic applications. A better understanding on how ESCs maintain their characteristics is therefore of importance. ESCs have uniquely high levels of telomerase activity. Previous studies have shown that deleting telomerase functions in ESCs led to reduced growth rates while overexpressing telomerase functions enhanced ESCs’ self-renewal ability, improved ESCs’ resistance to apoptosis and led to a more efficient differentiation. These results suggested that telomerase is important in maintaining the characteristics of ESCs. It has been suggested that human PinX1 (hPinX1) protein is a novel tumor suppressor. hPinX1 was shown to decrease tumor growth by inhibiting telomerase activity via a telomerase inhibitory domain presented on its C-terminal. However, it is unknown whether the telomerase inhibiting function is conserved in mouse. Since mouse genetics is well-studied and novel genes can be fully characterized by the later generation of genetically modified mice, it would be valuable to investigate the mouse PinX1 (mPinX1) gene. Also, the role of PinX1 in ESCs, which have uniquely high levels of telomerase activity, has never been investigated. Interestingly, we have recently identified a novel splice variant of the mPinX1 gene. This splice variant encodes a ‘truncated’ form of mPinX1 (mPinX1t) which contains mainly the N-terminal sequence of mPinX1. Whether mPinX1t would act on telomerase and whether it would have any function in ESCs are unknown. The overall objective of this proposal is to understand the role of mPinX1 and mPinX1t in maintaining the unique characteristics of ESCs and in regulating telomerase, and whether the effects of mPinX1 and mPinX1t on ESCs are mediated through regulating the telomerase. A combination of cell biology, molecular biology, and genetic manipulation techniques will be employed. This proposal will yield important and novel information on the roles of mPinX1 and mPinX1t in maintaining the unique characteristics of ESCs and therefore will be crucial for understanding the complex biology of ESCs. Moreover, the proposal may provide insights into the possible strategies for preventing tumor formation and enhancing ESC differentiation, two important issues concerning the practical use of ESC differentiation derivatives for future therapy and research. 胚胎幹細胞是從囊胚內的細胞團產生，具有自我更新能力，是萬能幹細胞，這意味著它們可以無限期地被培養，並有能力分化成體內的所有細胞類型。因此，胚胎幹細胞是專業細胞的極好來源。詳盡了解胚胎幹細胞是如何保持他們的特質具有重要的意義。 胚胎幹細胞獨特地擁有高水平的端粒酶活性。以往的研究表明，刪除端粒酶的功能會降低胚胎幹細胞的增長率，而超表達端粒酶功能會增強胚胎幹細胞的自我更新能力，提高胚胎幹細胞的抗凋亡能力，並導致更有效的細胞分化。這些結果表明，端粒酶對維持胚胎幹細胞的特徵是很重要的。 人類 PinX1（hPinX1）蛋白是一種新的抑制腫瘤基因。 hPinX1已被證明可以通過端粒酶C -末端以抑制端粒酶活性，從而減低腫瘤的生長。然而，現在還未知小鼠PinX1 （mPinX1）是否保留抑制端粒酶的功能。由於小鼠遺傳學已被充分研究，而新基因的特性也可以完全由轉基因小鼠來描述，所以調查mPinX1基因將是有重要價值的。另外，PinX1在胚胎幹細胞的作用從來沒有被探討。有趣的是，我們最近發現了mPinX1基因有新的剪接變異。這個由拼接變異體編碼而形成的截短形式mPinX1（mPinX1t）主要包含的是mPinX1 N -末端序列。mPinX1t是否作用於端粒酶以及它是否會在胚胎幹細胞有任何功能，現時尚未清楚。這項目的總體目標是要了解mPinX1和mPinX1t在維持胚胎幹細胞的獨特性和調節端粒酶中的作用，以及mPinX1和mPinX1t對胚胎幹細胞的作用是否通過調節端粒酶而導致的。這項建議將通過細胞生物學、分子生物學和基因操作技術進行。 這項目將揭示 mPinX1和mPinX1t如何維持胚胎幹細胞的獨特性，這將對於理解複雜的胚胎幹細胞生物學有關鍵的作用。此外，這項目將為今後使用胚胎幹細胞作研究和實際治療應用而可能出現的問題（如腫瘤的形成和低效率的胚胎幹細胞分化），提出重要的見解。

474711.label: Realisation of objectives
474711.value: (Due to the required format of the present report, figures of the data cannot be shown. All data are available upon request.) Aim 1. To investigate the role of mPinX1 and mPinX1t in maintaining the self-renewal and pluripotent characteristics of embryonic stem cells. Stable knockdown and overexpression of the mPinX1 and the mPinX1t in embryonic stem cells (ESCs) were done by lentivirus-mediated gene transfer. The stable ESC lines obtained were used to investigate the cellular role of these 2 transcript variants in the long-run. However, we could not find short hairpin RNA (shRNA) which can effectively knockdown mPinX1t without knocking down mPinX1 after we tried for all the potential sequences available as designed by the established computer algorithm. Overall, we have established four stable ESC lines for mPinX1 overexpression, three lines for mPinX1t overexpression, and another three lines as control lines for overexpression experiments. On the other hand, we have established three stable ESC lines for mPinX1 knockdown and three lines as the knockdown control ESC lines. Apart from the stable appearance of green color by GFP which indicated the successful integration of genes into the genome of ESCs, RT-qPCR was conducted to confirm the successful downregulation or overexpression of genes. mPinX1 and mPinX1t were successfully downregulated or overexpressed in respective cell lines. To study the long term effect on proliferation, the stable cell lines were kept on being passaged for 38-39 passages starting from the day of their establishment. The cell number was counted by trypan blue exclusion assays every time when the cells were passaged. Both overexpression of mPinX1 or mPinX1t, and knockdown of mPinX1 did not cause a significant change in proliferation in the long run. MTT assay and cell cycle analysis by flow cytometry were also performed on the stable cell lines. The results showed that both overexpression of mPinX1 or mPinX1t, and knockdown of mPinX1 did not exert a significant effect on the proliferation and cell cycle progression of ESCs in the long run. In addition, Western blotting analysis indicated that all stable cell lines did not significantly differ in their expression of several pluripotent markers, including Oct-4, Sox-2, and c-Myc. Taken together, altering mPinX1 or mPinX1t expression did not affect the self-renewal and pluripotent characteristics of ESCs. On the other hand, ESCs were also subjected to differentiation by embryoid body (EB) formation method. By counting the percentage of beating EBs, and by qPCR and western blotting of cardiac-specific markers (cardiac actin, cardiac troponin I, cardiac troponin T, -actinin and myosin heavy chain), we found that knockdown or overexpression of mPinX1 decreased while overexpression of mPinX1t increased cardiac differentiation. Because of the above important and interesting results on the potential role of mPinX1 and mPinX1t on cardiac differentiation, in addition to what has been proposed in the original proposal, we have also performed RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP), yeast-two-hybrid (Y2H) screening and co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) to find the potential interacting mRNA and protein partners of mPinX1 and/or mPinX1t (see below in Aim 3). Hopefully, the mechanisms of how mPinX1 and mPinX1t affect cardiac differentiation can be elucidated. Aim 2. To investigate the effects of mPinX1 and mPinX1t on the activity and subcellular localization of telomerase. By co-IP, we found that both mPinX1 and mPinX1t physically interact with mTERT. To investigate the subcellular localization of mPinX1 and mPinX1t, lentiviral plasmids encoding GFP fusion proteins were made. These constructs were used to package lentiviruses and the lentiviruses were used to infect ESCs. The infected ESCs were then stained with propidium iodide to label nucleus and with anti-fibrillarin to label nucleolus; they were examined under confocal microscope. Both mPinX1 and mPinX1t were found to mainly localize in the nucleolus, with some residing in the nucleoplasm. Immunostaining was performed to determine the subcellular localization of telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT; the catalytic subunit of telomerase) in the established stable ESC lines. Unfortunately, we could not find any good anti-TERT for such purpose even after testing several commercially available anti-TERT. On the other hand, by telomeric repeat amplification protocol assay, we found that altering the expression of mPinX1 or mPinX1t in ESCs did not affect the telomerase activity in the context of ESCs. Aim 3. To investigate if mPinX1 and mPinX1t mediate their effects on the characteristics of embryonic stem cells through affecting the telomerase. As described above, mPinX1 or mPinX1t did not affect self-renewal and pluripotent characteristics and did not affect telomerase activity in ESC context. Importantly, we found that upon differentiation, knockdown or overexpression of mPinX1 decreased while overexpression of mPinX1t increased cardiac differentiation. Therefore, we moved onto investigating whether mPinX1 and mPinX1t mediate their effect on cardiac differentiation through interacting with different mRNAs and/or proteins. By RIP, mPinX1 and mPinX1t proteins were found to interact with the mRNAs of Nkx2.5, Gata-4 and Tbx-5, the several well-known cardiac transcription factors. At protein level, Y2H screening and subsequent co-IP (for confirmation of interaction) were performed to identify novel protein interacting partners of mPinX1 and/or mPinX1t. A number of proteins have been found to interact with both mPinX1 and mPinX1t while some other proteins have been identified to preferentially interact only with either mPinX1 or mPinX1t. Interestingly, proteins that are important for mRNA transport are among these identified proteins. Further works are currently underway to elucidate if mPinX1t increases cardiac differentiation through enhancing the transport of mRNA of cardiac transcription factors from the nucleus to the cytoplasm. Altogether, we have discovered that mPinX1 and mPinX1t proteins, which contain the G-patch [G-patch is a glycine-rich motif that has been reported to bind RNA (Aksaas AK et al., 2011; Bauerova-Zabranska et al., 2005)] at their N-terminus, physically interact with mRNA of cardiac transcription factors. In addition, we found that mPinX1 and mPinX1t proteins have differential binding to some proteins for mRNA transport. The PhD student who is undertaking the project is expected to complete this novel part on investigating whether mPinX1 and mPinX1t differentially regulate cardiac differentiation through affecting mRNA transport. This student is expected to submit his thesis and full-length manuscript in 4 months. This project yields important and novel information on the roles of mPinX1 and mPinX1t in determining the cardiac differentiation of ESCs. In addition to understanding the complex biology of ESCs, this project provides novel insights into the possible strategies for enhancing the yield of cardiomyocytes from ESCs, an important issue concerning the practical use of pluripotent stem cells-derived cardiomyocytes for research and future therapy. 474711.label: Major findings and research outcome
474711.value: ESCs express mPinX1 and mPinX1t at mRNA and protein levels. We showed that mPinX1 and mPinX1t are actively transcribed as mRNA in ESCs by polysome fractionation followed by RT-PCR. In addition, western blotting by custom-made antibodies showed the presence of these two proteins in ESCs. Stable knockdown and overexpression of mPinX1 and mPinX1t did not affect the self-renewal and pluripotent characteristics of ESCs and did not affect the telomerase activity in ESCs. By altering the expression of mPinX1 and mPinX1t, we found that the mPinX1 and mPinX1t genes did not affect the self-renewal and pluripotent characteristics of ESCs. Both mPinX1 and mPinX1t were found to mainly localize in the nucleolus, with some residing in the nucleoplasm. While both mPinX1 and mPinX1t physically interact with mTERT, telomeric repeat amplification protocol assay revealed that altering their expression exerted no significant effect on telomerase activity in ESC context. Stable knockdown and overexpression of mPinX1 decreased while stable overexpression of mPinX1t increased the cardiac differentiation of ESCs. On the other hand, when ESCs were subjected to differentiation, both decreasing or increasing mPinX1 expression attenuated cardiac differentiation, suggesting that mPinX1 expression level has to be precisely maintained during cardiac differentiation. In contrast, increasing mPinX1t expression increased cardiac differentiation, suggesting that mPinX1t may be a positive regulator of cardiac differentiation. mPinX1 and mPinX1t proteins interact with the mRNA of cardiac transcription factors. Interestingly, by RIP, mPinX1 and mPinX1t proteins were found to interact with the mRNA of several cardiac transcription factors. mPinX1 and mPinX1t proteins preferentially interact with different protein partners, including proteins important for mRNA transport. By Y2H screening and subsequent co-IP (for confirmation), a number of proteins have been found to preferentially only interact with either mPinX1 or mPinX1t. Among these interacting partners with mPinX1 and/or mPinX1t, proteins important for mRNA transport (e.g. nucleoporin) and proteins which are regulated by calcium (e.g. calpain) will be further studied. Experiments are currently underway to elucidate if mPinX1t increases cardiac differentiation through enhancing the transport of mRNA of cardiac transcription factors from the nucleus to the cytoplasm. Most of the results and related studies described above have been published in form of conference abstracts and/or papers. The PhD student who is undertaking the project is expected to complete the part on elucidating the mechanisms of how mPinX1 and mPinX1t differentially regulate cardiac differentiation. He is expected to submit his thesis and full-length manuscript in 4 months.

474711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
474711.value: By Y2H screening, a number of proteins have been found to interact with mPinX1 and/or mPinX1t. These interactions have been further confirmed by co-IP experiment. These confirmed interacting partners belong to different types of proteins that regulate different cellular processes. Among them, some interesting interacting partners of mPinX1 and/or mPinX1t, including proteins which are regulated by calcium (e.g. calpain), proteins that have previously been shown to regulate differentiation processes, proteins involve in ubiquitination process, would be further studied. Expression of these proteins would be altered (knockdown and overexpression) by inducible lentiviral system during ESC differentiation. Further works by a combination of cell and molecular biology techniques (e.g. counting of percentage of beating EBs, qPCR and western blot will be conducted to determine the degree of cardiac differentiation in ESCs with altered expression of targeted proteins; confocal microscopy will be used to determine subcellular localization of targeted proteins and to measure intracellular calcium change; mutagenesis followed by co-IP would be used to determine the site of interaction of mPinX1 and/or mPinX1t and the targeted proteins) would be employed to investigate if the functions of mPinX1 and mPinX1t differ; if yes, how and why do they differ.

474711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
474711.value: Embryonic stem cells (ESCs) can self-renew and are pluripotent, meaning that they can proliferate and have the ability to differentiate into all cell types. ESCs are therefore an excellent source of specialized cells for research and therapy. Telomerase is important for maintaining ESC characteristics. Human PinX1 was reported to be a telomerase inhibitor. Recently, we have identified a novel splice variant of mouse PinX1 (mPinX1) gene, the mPinX1t ('t' stands for truncated). Objective of this project was to understand the role of mPinX1 and mPinX1t in maintaining ESC characteristics. We found that mPinX1 and mPinX1t do not affect self-renewal and pluripotent characteristics, and do not affect telomerase activity in ESCs. Interestingly, altering mPinX1 expression decreased while enhancing mPinX1t expression increased cardiac differentiation of ESCs. Further analysis showed that, while mPinX1 and mPinX1t interact with cardiac transcription factor mRNA, mPinX1t preferentially interacts with potential positive regulators of cardiac differentiation. This project yields novel information on the roles of mPinX1 and mPinX1t in determining cardiac differentiation of ESCs. In addition to understanding ESC biology, this project provides novel insights into possible strategies for enhancing the yield of cardiomyocytes from ESCs, an important issue concerning the potential use of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes for therapy.

474811.label: Project Objectives
474811.value: To investigate the relationship between night shift work and the risk of breast cancer among Chinese women in Hong Kong. To explore the interactions which could exist between night shift work and several major risk factors, including menopausal status, light-at-night, sleep deprivation, residential pesticides, occupational exposures to potential EDCs, diet, smoking, alcohol drinking, and family cancer history. However, we have to reduce sample size from the originally proposed 1066 cases and 1066 controls to 700 subjects in each group due to limited budget obtained (our originally proposed budget has been cut down by 58.8%). We re-estimated sample size using a relatively conservative approach, 636 cases and an equal number of controls will be recruited in order to detect the risk of a modest size of 1.45 for exposures with prevalence rates about 18% to reach a reasonable power of 80% at the 5% significance level (one-sided). To allow for 10% incomplete interviews and missing data, around 700 cases as well as 700 controls will be needed. With this newly proposed sample size, we shall be able to achieve the 1st primary objective and address the interactions with major risk factors of the 2nd objective; however, power may be limited to cover the interactions with minor risk factors. In addition, we will replace community controls by hospital controls because the cost of recruitment of community controls is much higher than the hospital controls. Another reason for not using community controls is the poor response rate, and our pilot study suggested a low response rate from the community controls (<40%). Using hospital controls with different diagnostic groups has been shown to have similar results to the community controls. We will recruit controls from the same hospitals of the cases with different diagnoses of disease. We will perform sensitivity analysis to test the robust results by excluding the diseases potentially related to night shift work from the controls.

474811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
474811.value: Aim Breast cancer is the leading cause of cancer morbidity and mortality among women in Hong Kong, and the rate is accelerating. Although the upward trend is considered to be attributable to the ‘westernization’ of lifestyles, this probably contributes to only 41% of the breast cancer risk in the female population in combination with various genetic factors. A larger majority fraction of breast cancer etiology is environmental in origin, and this origin remains poorly understood. We aim to rectify this lack of knowledge through our intended project. Project Background In 2007, the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) classified shift work that involved circadian disruption as probably being carcinogenic to humans (Group 2A); this, however, was on the basis of sufficient evidence from experimental animals but only on limited evidence from humans. Only two relevant epidemiological studies have been published since 2007, but they do not contribute much to addressing the limitations quoted by the IARC in 2007. None of the previous epidemiological studies has adequately captured the specific characteristics of nightshifts (e.g., the type, regularity, timing, frequency, and speed of rotating) in examining its association with breast cancer risk, and none has taken into account the potential confounding effects from environmental exposure to pesticides and other endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs), known or suspected occupational carcinogens, the use of cosmetics containing estrogens in the breast area, etc. Brief Project Description We will study about 1,066 newly diagnosed female breast cancer cases and an equal number of age-matched controls randomly selected from the community. A standardized questionnaire will be used to collect information on each participant’s lifetime exposure to night shift work, environmental exposures to pesticides and other EDCs, occupational exposures, reproductive and anthropometric factors, smoking, diet, alcohol drinking, family cancer history, etc. With a more reliable exposure assessment and a more adequate control of the confounding factors, we will be able to ascertain whether exposure to night shift work is associated with an elevated risk of breast cancer among Hong Kong Chinese women and to thereby better understand the potential interactions with the major risk factors. Significance of Project Night shift work is prevalent in Hong Kong women. There will be far-reaching implications if a causal link between night shift work and breast cancer is confirmed by this proposed study, because even a slight decrease in the risk would result in a great reduction in public health burden.

474811.label: Realisation of objectives
474811.value: 1. We successfully recruited 767 eligible breast cancer incident cases with a response rate of 91.1%; the main reasons for the non-responses were no interest or poor medical condition. All eligible cases were consecutively identified from the Department of Surgery or Clinical Oncology of three hospitals in Hong Kong during the period 11/2011 to 05/2014, and were interviewed within three months after the diagnosis was made. Each eligible case was frequency matched in 5-year age groups by a control patient selected from the same hospital where the cases came from. We recruited 792 eligible controls with a broad disease pattern of diagnosis, with the response rate of 93%. To be eligible, the cases and controls must have no previously physician-diagnosed cancer at any site. 2. The relationship between night shift work and the risk of breast cancer had been investigated in our study. The exposure-response relationship of breast cancer risk with the exposure to short, moderate and long terms of night shift work were evaluated in our study. 3. We further explored the interactions which may exist between night shift work and several major risk factors, including menopausal status, light-at-night, sleep deprivation, diet, smoking, alcohol drinking, and family cancer history. Because the usage of the residential pesticides was quite rare and the occupational exposures to potential endorine disrupting chemicals (EDCs) were low in our study population, the current study does not have adequate power to examine the potential interactions between exposure to residential pesticides or EDCs and night shift work on the risk of breast cancer. 4. Evidence has shown that nightshift work may be associated with some digestive system diseases like gastritis and gastric/duodenal ulcer. Thus, sensitivity analysis was conducted to test the robust results by removing controls whose diagnosis are gastritis and gastric/duodenal ulcer.
