474811.label: Major findings and research outcome
474811.value: Our study showed that there were 5.5% of breast cancer cases and 6.1% of controls who had ever worked at nightshift at least once per month for ≥1 year. There was no evidence for an association between ever nightshift work and breast cancer risk (OR=1.00, 95% CI: 0.58-1.71). Further analyses revealed that a possibly excess risk of breast cancer was restricted to women who had worked at nightshift for ≥15 years (adjusted OR=1.66, 95% CI: 0.70-3.90) but power is limited. Although this study tends to provide supportive evidence on a positive association between long-term nightshift work and breast cancer risk among Hong Kong Chinese women, this result would have to be confirmed by further larger studies. However, we failed to detect significant interactions between nightshift work and other major risk factors (e.g., menopausal status, smoking, alcohol drinking, and family cancer history) based on the current study scale with a relatively limited sample size. Nevertheless, this study showed some potential interesting associations when the analyses were further stratified by the menopausal status and family cancer history. For women having nightshift work ≥15 years, the relative risk of breast cancer in the post-menopausal women was much higher (OR=2.27, 95% CI: 0.73-7.04) than the pre-menopausal women (OR=0.95, 95% CI: 0.23-3.83), indicating a potential multiplicative interaction between menopausal status and nightshift work. Moreover, we found that the OR of breast cancer was higher in the long-term nightshift worker (≥15 years) who had a cancer history in the first-degree family members than those without a family history (OR=3.43, 95% CI: 0.66-17.92 vs. OR=1.11, 95% CI: 0.38-3.26); this indicates that a potential multiplicative interaction might exist between family cancer history and night shift work on the risk of breast cancer. Sensitivity analysis was conducted by excluding the controls with diagnoses of gastritis and gastric/duodenal ulcer, and the results remained unchanged, which suggests that the recruited controls are appropriate. In addition, two papers that are relevant to this GRF/RGC-funded project have been published in the peer-review journals (Annals of Oncology, 2013; Chinese Journal of Preventive Medicine, 2014). Another two relevant original manuscripts were submitted to the Journal of National Cancer Institute and European Journal of Cancer and now are under review (see Part C). Other relevant research outputs include three abstracts presented in the international conferences in Utrecht (06/2013) and Chicago (06/2014), and one invited speech to be presented in Guangzhou, China (11/2014) (see Part C).

474811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
474811.value: As night shift work is the necessary component for many occupations, understanding of which specific pattern of shift work increase breast cancer risk, and how night shift work influences the pathway to breast cancer risk is prerequisite for the development of healthy workplace policy. The association between long-term nightshift work and breast cancer risk obtained from this GRF/RGC funded study among Hong Kong Chinese women needs to be confirmed by larger studies, while further research should also be done to look into the relation with specific characteristics of shift work and the duration of exposure. As the chronotype and sleep pattern may play a role in night shift work and the carcinogenesis, more studies on the gene variants especially melatonin related genes should be conducted; furthermore, the joint effects between genetic polymorphisms and long-term nightshift work on the risk of breast cancer warrant further studies, in particular the Asian population where the nightshift work is prevalent and incidence of breast cancer is increasing.

474811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
474811.value: The shift work is prevalent in Hong Kong Chinese women, especially in the medical organization and service industry. Meanwhile, the breast cancer incidence in Hong Kong has been ranked as the second highest region in Asia, and the rate is increasing. This GRF/RGC funded project aimed to figure out whether exposure to nightshift work was associated with an elevated risk of breast cancer among Hong Kong Chinese women and to thereby better understand the potential interactions with the major risk factors. Results from this study demonstrated that a possibly excess risk of breast cancer was restricted to women who had worked at nightshift for ≥15 years (adjusted OR=1.66, 95% CI: 0.70-3.90), whilst there was no evidence for an association with the short-term nightshift work. We observed an enhanced risk of breast cancer (a possible multiplicative interaction) between the long-term nightshift work and post-menopausal status or women with a positive family cancer history on the risk of breast cancer, but there was no statistical significance due to limited power. Preventive lifestyles and the least damaging shiftwork schedules should be recommended to avoid the possible health consequences from the hazardous nightshift work.

475211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
475211.value: Background, hypothesis and aim: There is increasing in vitro evidence suggesting that thromboxane (TX) plays an important role in tumor growth and metastasis. The signal pathway of TX is associated with various molecules involved in cell migration and angiogenesis, such as vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF) and matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9). Experiments from our group have further shown that the level of thromboxane synthase (TXS) is significantly increased in human lung cancer tissues compared with the corresponding non-cancer lung tissues. Moreover, lung cancer cells stimulated with smoking carcinogen 4-methylnitrosamino-1-3-pyridyl-1-butanone (NNK) can express more TXS and produce more TX, compared with those without NNK treatment. The effects of NNK on TXS expression and TX production can be blocked by application of TXS inhibitors. With the reduction of TXS and TX, NNK-mediated lung cancer cell proliferation and growth is inhibited. However, these data have not been verified in vivo and thus the in vivo role of TXS in lung tumor development is yet to be confirmed. In this proposal, we hypothesize that TXS promotes the in vivo growth of lung tumor induced by NNK. The aim of the study is to analyze the in vivo role of TXS in the development of lung tumors and to explore the potential mechanism used by TXS to facilitate the tumor development and growth in vivo. We will thus establish a mouse lung tumor model induced by NNK to test our hypothesis and aim. The level of TXS will be modulated by its overexpression and its inhibitors. The significance: In Hong Kong, the incidence of lung cancer is the highest among other cancers and it is also the No 1 killers compared with other cancers. One of the factors contributing to the high mortality rate is lack of effective treatments to arrest the tumor and to prevent metastasis. We hope that uncovering the role of TXS will lead to the novel approach to effectively inhibit the lung tumor growth and metastasis via the modulation of TXS pathway.

475211.label: Realisation of objectives
475211.value: 1. to analyze the in vivo role of TXS in the development of lung tumors. This objective was achieved using smoking carcinogen NNK-induced lung tumor model in mice. All NNK-treated mice developed lung adenocarcinoma. It was demonstrated that the TX pathway was significantly upregulated in NNK-treated mice compared with the non-treated control. The level of TXS was positively associated with the size of tumors. Furthermore, mice treated with TXS inhibitor ozagrel developed significantly less tumors in term of tumor numbers and size, compared with mice received vehicle control. The inhibitory effect of ozagrel was dose-dependent. These results indicate a critical role of TXS in the development of lung cancer and also the potential therapeutic value of TX pathway inhibitors. 2. to explore the potential mechanism used by TXS to facilitate the tumor development and growth in vivo. This objective was also achieved using smoking carcinogen NNK-induced lung tumor model in mice. Our results showed that the expressions of CD133 and ALDH1A1 were positively associated with TXS. Similar results were observed in human NSCLC tumor samples and cultured NSCLC cells. NNK significantly stimulated TXS and enhanced the generation of LCSCs, evident by the upregulation of CD133 and ALDH1A1 expression, and the increase in the number and size of tumor spheres. NNK also promoted the expression of LCSC-related molecules including β-catenin and Nanog. All these NNK-mediated effects could be offset by ozagrel. In the colony formation assay, NNK increased whereas ozagrel decreased the number of colonies. Collectively, LCSCs and TXS participate in NNK-induced lung cancer. Our data suggest that TXS is a promising therapeutic target as it is a key molecular in NNK-mediated stemness of LCSCs.

475311.label: Project Objectives
475311.value: Localize insulin receptor signaling components and identify insulin specific actions in chondrocytes by conditional disruption of IR in vitro and in vivo. We hypothesize that IR signaling is an important regulator of chondrogenesis during bone growth and following injury and that it will function differently than IGF-1. We will first use immunohistochemistry and in situ hybridization to localize insulin receptor signaling components (IR, IRS-1) in growth plate chondrocytes during skeletal development and in the cartilaginous callus following fracture healing. To unequivocally identify essential insulin actions in chondrocytes, we will delete its receptor in chondrocytes using Cre-recombinase (Cre) mediated gene deletion. The impact of this genetic alteration on the growth plate will be analyzed using hiostology, histochemistry, immunohistochemistry and in situ hybridization analysis and compared to control littermates at selected time points during skeletal development. Primary chondrocytes and metatarsals expressing or lacking IR will be used to determine the requirement for IR in chondrocyte proliferation, apoptosis, differentiation, and matrix deposition in vitro. Intracellular signaling pathways that involve in the underling mechanisms will be defined. Determine the requirement for IR in chondrocytes on cartilaginous callus formation during fracture healing. We will explore the consequences of the loss of IR on healing long bone fractures in mice. A novel mouse model (tamoxifen inducible Cre) which enables temporal removal of the IR in chondrocytes will be employed to study the impact of IR deletion over various stages of the healing process by histology, quantitative cartilage histomorphometry and bone histomorphometry. Chondrogenic marker genes (Ihh, Sox9, and Col2) will be characterized by in situ hybridization in fracture callus in a defined time window of early phase of healing. Explore the role of insulin/IR in the pathogenesis and intervention of the impaired bone healing associated with diabetes. A long bone fracture model will be created in diabetic mouse strains representing type 1 (STZ-induced mice) and type 2 diabetes (db/db mice) to determine how dysfunction of insulin/IR is responsible for the impaired chondrogenesis associated with diabetes, and the therapeutic role of insulin or IGF-1 in cartilaginous formation during fracture healing associated with diabetic states.

475311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
475311.value: Bone disorders associated with diabetes mellitus including impaired fracture healing continue to be a major public health problem afflicting both adult and juvenile diabetic patients. Insulin/insulin receptor (IR) signaling regulates energy utilization and body composition. Humans expressing mutations in the IR (Leprechaunism) exhibit diabetes with profound growth retardation while mice with mutations of IR display severe postnatal growth retardation with impaired growth plate development. Moreover, insufficient insulin production or action associated with diabetic states is accompanied clinically or experimentally with impaired long bone fracture healing characterized by reduced cartilaginous callus formation. These abnormalities can be largely reversed by treatment with insulin. Despite such circumstantial evidence for a role of insulin in bone development, direct evidence for insulin/IR action on the process of chondrogenesis during bone development and repair is virtually absent. This proposal will test the hypothesis that insulin/IR signaling regulates chondrogenesis during skeletal growth and fracture healing. The project has three specific aims. Aim 1 will localize insulin receptor signaling components and identify insulin specific actions in chondrocytes by conditional disruption of IR in vitro and in vivo. Aim 2 will determine the requirement for IR in chondrocytes on cartilaginous callus formation during fracture healing. Aim 3 will explore the role of insulin/IR in the pathogenesis and intervention of the impaired bone healing associated with diabetes. The experimental plan will use genetically modified mice (Cre-loxp strategy and tamoxifen inducible mutagenesis) to define the cellular targets and establish the physiological roles of insulin signaling in chondrogenesis during skeletal development and following injury. The in vitro cellular and molecular studies will define the mechanisms of insulin/IR signaling in regulation of chondrocyte growth, differentiation, and proliferation. The diabetic fracture models will be performed to determine the role of insulin/IR in pathogenesis and intervention of the impaired bone healing associated with diabetes. We believe that these studies will facilitate the development of novel therapeutic approaches for defective bone formation and repair in diabetic patients. 糖尿病併發的骨骼疾病包括骨折癒合不良是影響成年和青少年糖尿病患者的重要健康問題。胰島素/胰島素受體信號參與調節能量利用和機體組織構成。表達突變的胰島素受體的病人表現糖尿病特徵及生長遲滯；胰島素受體突變小鼠也呈現類似病徵。而且，臨床及動物模型研究發現胰島素生成不足相關的糖尿病也伴發長骨骨折癒合不良，組織病理學表現軟骨骨痂生成減少。胰島素治療則可促進骨折癒合。儘管這些證據提示胰島素參與骨骼發育和修復，然而胰島素/胰島素受體信號對軟骨生成的調控機理仍未闡明。本課題將使用遺傳動物模型闡明胰島素信號在骨發育和再生過程中的細胞靶標和生理作用；在細胞與分子學層面探討胰島素/胰島素受體信號對軟骨細胞生長與分化的調控；應用糖尿病骨折模型確定胰島素/胰島素受體在糖尿病併發骨癒合不良病理機制與干預手段中的作用。希望該課題有助於探尋治療糖尿病骨生成或癒合不良併發症的新方法。

475311.label: Realisation of objectives
475311.value: For Objective 1, immunostaining in bone sections from mouse long bone and a long bone fracture model shows that IR is detected in chondroblasts and prehypertrophic chondrocytes in the growth plates and primary cartilaginous callus, respectively, but not in the hypertropic chondrocytes. We found that insulin treatment increased the total length of metatarsals over that of untreated controls, characterized by increased size of the proliferating zone and cellular proliferation indexed by the number of proliferating cell nuclear antigen immunoreactive cells. Deletion of IR elevated IGF-1R mRNA and protein levels. IGF-1 stimulated Akt and ERK phosphorylation in the control cells, and the effects were enhanced in the IR mutant cells. Deletion of IR decreased chondrogenic differentiation and proteoglycan synthesis, and the effects were rescued by IGF-1 but not insulin. Bot insulin and IGF-1 was shown to stimulate their cognate receptors, while they might also function through each other receptor mediated signaling. For Objective 2, we generated mice with conditional deletion of the IR in chondrocytes (CartIR−/−). The CartIR−/− mice had no discernable differences in total femoral length compared to control littermates. However, CartIR−/− mice exhibited an increase in chondrocyte numbers in the growth plate than that of the controls. Chondrocytes lacking IR had elevated IGF-1R mRNA and protein levels. At cellular level, IGF-1 induced phosphorylation of Akt and ERK was enhanced while this action was eliminated when the cells were treated with IGF-1R inhibitor Picropodophyllin. Deletion of the IR impaired chondrogenic differentiation, and the effect could not be restored by treatment of insulin. Intriguingly, the size of hypertrophic chondrocytes was smaller in CartIR−/− mice when compared with that of the control littermates, which was associated with upregulation of TSC2. In a femur fracture model in mouse that selectively expresses the TM inducible Cre-ERT recombinase under the control of Col2α1 promoter in chondrocytes, we also found that deletion of the IR in chondrocytes altered the formation of cartilaginous callus formation during bone healing which was caused by the changes in IR mediated signaling. These results suggest that deletion of the IR in chondrocytes sensitizes IGF-1R signaling and action, IR and IGF-1R coordinate to regulate the proliferation, differentiation, and hypertrophy of growth plate chondrocytes during long bone development or fracture healing. For Objective 3, a type 1 diabetic mouse model was generated using the STZ induction method, and a long bone fracture model was established in the diabetic mouse model to mimic the diabetic fracture healing process in the clinic. Insulin or IGF-1 was locally delivered to the fracture site every other day for five injections after day 4 post-surgery, with non-treatment as control. Radiographic and histomorphometric analysis showed that diabetic group had decreased cartilaginous callus formation and bony callus volume, local injection of insulin or IGF-1 dramatically increased cartilaginous callus and bony callus formation. The phenotype is accompanied by upregulation of insulin receptor (IR) and chondrogenic marker genes expression (Sox9, Col2α1 and ALP) in the cartilaginous callus at day 14 post-surgery. Local delivery of insulin or IGF-1 significantly increased proliferating nuclear antigen positive (PCNA+) cell numbers and decreased the expression of glucose transporter-1 (Glut-1) in chondrocytes of the cartilaginous callus compared with the diabetic control. At the end of consolidation, both insulin and IGF-1 increased the radiographic score and bone volume of the healing bone. To further define the mechanisms, we performed in vitro analysis, noted that high glucose decreased chondrogenic differentiation and increased chondrocyte proliferation. High glucose elevated phosphorylation of cyclin D1 and the level of Glut1 in chondrocytes. Interestingly, both IR and IGF-1R were shown to function in regulation of Glut-1 expression in chondrocytes, while IGF-1R seemed to exert more sensitive response than that of IR. Insulin and IGF-1 showed differential effect on Glut1 expression mediated by differential mode of IR/IGF-1R action. The results indicate that the enhanced diabetic bone repair by insulin or IGF might be associated with their distinct regulation of Glut1expression during cartilaginous callus formation. Local delivery of insulin or IGF-1 might serve as a therapy for promoting bone healing in diabetic patients with impaired bone repair.

475711.value: 在大腦統計分析中，腦模板或腦圖譜在基於模型的腦計算任務起著根本性的作用，包括從分割到分析，從診斷到治療，從術前應用到術中系統。此外，構造統計腦模板/圖譜還有助於了解由於種族、性別、生長/老化，以及不同的病狀引起的大腦變化。由於中國人和西方人在大腦解剖上存在差異，在中國人的大腦分析中，如果直接應用現有的基於西方人大腦圖像的統計腦圖譜集，將會導致分析結果的偏差。這個項目的目的是（一）開發基於多模態 MR圖像的全自動統計腦模板生成方案；（二）構建多模態正常中國青少年和老年人的統計腦模板和腦圖譜；（三）調查研究基於MS - CBT和MS- CBA幾個應用原型。

475711.label: Realisation of objectives
475711.value: Our first objective was to create brain templates and atlas using on data from MRI. A group of subjects were recruited and underwent resting-state functional MRI. After a series of image pre-processing and generation of anatomical brain templates and initial templates, iterative procedures for template refinement were carried out to generate a probabilistic DMN template. The proposed method demonstrated an effective and automatic pipeline to create DMN templates selection from independent component analysis (ICA) analysis. Besides, many commonly used brain templates and atlas were created based on Caucasian subjects. In this project, we created a pediatric Chinese population based brain template. It was created by a series of pre-processing techniques followed by atlas construction using a few existing software. Our in-house method to generate brain templates and atlas could extend the field of research in more neurological, psychological and psychiatric diseases. Furthermore, we studied the brain of patients with scoliosis, Acute Infarction, schizotypal personality disorder, developmental dyslexia, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Alzheimer’s Disease. We conducted segmentation and morphological analysis on the cerebellum of scoliosis patients. We implemented our fMRI analysis technique to study the functional changes of the brain in schizotypal personality disorder (STPD) and amnestic MCI patients. DMN in patients with (STPD) were studied using our in-house DMN template and the changes of activity in aging amnestic MCI patients were evaluated. Besides, the fiber tracks of the spinal cord in patients with scoliosis were successfully analyzed and compared with healthy controls. Also, we applied segmentation techniques to perform full brain white matter lesion analysis. The proposed method quantify white matter lesion using MRI images in T1W, FLAIR, and DWI with the presence of acute infarctions. Results from the automatic algorithm were comparable and validated to those obtained from visual scores from specialists. We also conducted a few image pre-processing studies to improve image quality by denoising and facilitated our MRI analysis by using stitching algorithm and intensity normalization techniques. We successfully carried out and completed many clinical and engineering based research studies and the results were reflected in our publications.

475711.label: Major findings and research outcome
475711.value: We published a method for generating atlas for Chinese pediatric population. Several special pre-processing techniques based on intensity and sulci landmark were conducted to improve the image quality of pediatric MRI brain images. The results of atlas maintained high anatomical details and showed better performance in atlas-based segmentation compared with other standard atlases. Our newly designed procedure demonstrated better performance included sharper atlas and higher segmentation accuracy, in atlas construction [8, C8-9, C13-15] (C donates conference abstracts). The Chinese pediatric atlas could be used to study the development of children's brains between healthy and those with autism or other neurological diseases. Also, we presented a new iterative method to create brain template of the default mode network (DMN) based on resting-state fMRI data of a large number of subjects. Our method used an iterative refinement with an effective similarity measurement algorithm to select the DMN component from the numerous independent components for each subject. The iteration process terminated until the difference between the templates of the current and previous stage was less than 5%. With all the masks of the DMN areas from each subject being averaged, the statistical DMN template was achieved [12, C1, C16-C19]. To allow fiber tracking of the full spinal cord, an image stitching technique was developed based on DTI data. The purpose of it was to connect DTI spine images obtained at different regions of the body into one single image. This stitching algorithm was based on feature-based registration and adaptive composition. It was tested and validated using real data sets and FA maps and fiber tracking results showed the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed framework [2]. Signal intensity of MRI could be varied due to machines from different manufacturers and magnetic field in different Tesla. To compare images from different machines or magnetic field, a histogram-based MRI intensity normalization method was presented [24]. This method was validated and demonstrated to improve the performance of image analysis and allowed cross center collaborations using different MR machine. Besides all our technical works, we applied many of our skills on clinical studies included brain structure network analysis on patients with Obstructive Sleep Apnea, automatic segmentation of left ventricle for assessment of myocardial iron loading, brain structural network in Chinese children with developmental dyslexia, functional connectivity study on schizotypal personality disorder and neurological studies on scoliosis [1, 5, 6, 10, 15, 18, 21, 22, C2, C4, C6].

475711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
475711.value: Brain templates and atlases were created from pediatric subjects. In the near further, a group of healthy adult subjects will be recruited to create brain templates and atlas based on adult Chinese subjects. Functional MRI was an unique MRI modality. Based on this technique, a probabilistic template was created for default mode network (DMN). DMN was especially important and useful to study psychological and psychiatric diseases. A few studies were conducted on Alzheimer’s Disease and schizotypal personality disorder. We could further study Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) using our DMN template as DMN could be one of the earliest changes in AD patients. Early diagnosis and early medication could be beneficial to not only the patients but also the caretakers and their family members. Furthermore, the brain templates and atlas created by our group could be applied to study the morphological changes in patients with neurological diseases. Task-based fMRI could measure network efficiency and connectivity on patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Therapeutic and rehab exercises could be quantitatively evaluated using the unique imaging modality. An accurate measure of the efficacy of different rehab exercises could allow physicians to select an optimal treatment for patients with MCI.

475711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
475711.value: The aim of the project was to create statistical brain templates and atlases based on MRI data and to investigate image processing techniques included brain parcellation, cortical structures segmentation, fMRI brain mapping, DTI fiber tracking and white matter lesion localization. We had successfully generated a probabilistic template of default mode network derived from resting-state fMRI and a brain atlas for Chinese pediatric population. Then we developed an automated algorithm to quantify white matter lesion using MRI on patients with Acute Infarction. To further implement our in-house techniques, we studied a group of patients with scoliosis on their cerebellum, cortical network, spinal cord and medulla oblongata. Our segmentation technique, DTI fiber tracking analysis and morphological comparison were applied into several studies over this project. Several other technical works were completed included imaging denoising, image stitching, and normalization technique to allow comparison of MRI data acquired from different MR machines. In summary, we had developed several techniques to improve image quality and applied our in-house techniques to study the etiology and anatomical difference in various diseases.

475911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
475911.value: Chronic liver disease is a major public health problem worldwide. Liver fibrosis, a common feature of chronic liver diseases, involves the accumulation of collagen, proteoglycans, and other macromolecules within the extracellular matrix. Ultimately, progressive liver fibrosis leads to cirrhosis or even hepatocellular carcinoma. Clinically, patients with liver fibrosis remain asymptomatic or have only mild, nonspecific symptoms until the development of cirrhosis. Originally considered to be irreversible, hepatic fibrosis is now regarded as a dynamic process with potential for regression. It is thus important to identify patients with liver fibrosis to control disease progression at a relative early stage. To date, liver biopsy is the standard of reference for diagnosis and staging of liver fibrosis. However, it is an invasive procedure, and is also an inherently subjective process, subjects to sampling error. These limitations make liver biopsy unsuitable for diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring in the general population. To better manage the individuals with progressive fibrosis, especially those who may benefit from early intervention, a noninvasive, reproducible and reliable method is needed to evaluate disease progression, to monitor responses to drug treatment, and to facilitate epidemiologic research. Recently, a mechanism for magnetic resonance (MR) tissue contrast, T1rho (T1ρ), has been investigated. In biological tissues, T1rho contrast is sensitive to macromolecular composition. Our preliminary result has shown that T1rho MR imaging is sensitive for evaluation of liver fibrosis in a rat model of biliary-duct-ligation induced liver fibrosis. The current proposal is composed of two parts. For animal based study, we aim to further evaluate T1rho MR imaging in three animal models including 1) biliary duct ligation induced rat liver fibrosis model; 2) carbon tetrachloride induced rat liver fibrosis model; and 3) thioacetamide induced rat liver fibrosis model. Upon the successful completion of the animal studies, T1rho MR imaging will be conducted in 16 healthy volunteers and in a small cohort of liver fibrosis patients (n=40). T1rho results will be correlated to the severity of liver fibrosis defined by histopathology. 475911.label: Realisation of objectives
475911.value: The research objectives have been largely achieved. We confirmed the possibility and sensitivity of using T1rho imaging for detecting and grading liver fibrosis, and monitoring progression and regression of liver fibrosis in rat models. We are the first to report that T1rho MRI can be used to assess liver fibrosis. We confirmed it with animal models. We developed the technique of T1rho human liver imaging, and established the normal T1rho values for healthy human subjects. Our work was recognised with The BJR Magnetic Resonance Radiologists Association (MRRA) UK New Technologies Prize. In 2014 our work was confirmed by two groups in Germany (Allkemper et al; Rauscher et al) and one group in Japan (Takayama et al 2014), all of them cited our pioneering work. We also developed fast data acquisition method to speed up scan for patients. Though further efforts are needed for wider clinical application, our work has received world recognition.

475911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
475911.value: Chronic liver disease is a major public health problem worldwide. Liver fibrosis, a common feature of chronic liver diseases, involves the accumulation of collagen, proteoglycans, and other macromolecules within the extracellular matrix. Ultimately, progressive liver fibrosis leads to cirrhosis or even hepatocellular carcinoma. Clinically, patients with liver fibrosis remain asymptomatic or have only mild, nonspecific symptoms until the development of cirrhosis. To better manage the individuals with progressive fibrosis, especially those who may benefit from early intervention, a noninvasive, reproducible and reliable method is needed to evaluate disease progression, to monitor responses to drug treatment, and to facilitate epidemiologic research. The results from this study will be important for identifying imaging biomarkers of liver fibrosis and enabling non-invasive liver assessment, hence expected to have an impact on clinical practice.

476411.label: Project Objectives
476411.value: The primary objective of this research proposal on experimental pathology and immunology is to elucidate intracellular signal transduction mechanisms mediating the activation of eosinophils and bronchial epithelial cells by ligands for NLR member NOD1, gamma-D-glutamyl-meso-diaminopimelic acid (iE-DAP) and NOD2, N-acetylmuramyl-L-alanyl-D-isoglutamine (muramyl dipeptide/MDP). The project will study the following in the co-culture of primary human peripheral blood eosinophils and bronchial epithelial cells. (1) The effects of iE-DAP and MDP on (i) the apoptosis of eosinophils, (ii) the production of essential allergic inflammation related inflammatory cytokines IL-1beta and IL-6, and chemokines CXCL8 and CXCL1 for neutrophils, CCL2 for monocytes, mast cells, basophils, eosinophils, CCL17 and CCL22 for Th2 cells, CCL11/eotaxin for eosinophils and thymic stromal lymphopoietin for Th2-related dendritic cells, (iii) the cell surface expression of adhesion molecules such as intercellular adhesion molecule (ICAM)-1 (CD54), vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1), L-selectin (CD62L), leukocyte function-associated antigen (LFA, CD11a/CD18) on eosinophils and bronchial epithelial cells, (iv) the adhesion of eosinophils onto primary human bronchial epithelial cells and (v) the eosinophil degranulation for the release of eosinophilic cationic protein and superoxides (2) The difference in the expression of NOD1,2 on eosinophils from patients with allergic asthma and sex- age-matched non-allergic normal control subjects will be investigated and compared. The in vivo activating effect of the injection of NOD1,2 ligands on the cytokine/chemokine concentration and the accumulation of eosinophils at bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid will also be investigated using allergic asthmatic murine model. (3) The relationship between iE-DAP and MDP mediated the activation of essential intracellular signaling molecules extracellular signal-regulated protein kinase (ERK), c-Jun amino-terminal kinase (JNK), p38 mitogen activated protein kinase (p38 MAPK), Janus kinase-signal transducer and activator of transcription factor (JAK-STAT) and phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)-AKT and transcription factor nuclear factor-kB (NF-kB) with the apoptosis, expression of cytokines, chemokines and adhesion molecules, and eosinophil adhesion and degranulation. (4) The specific inhibitors of ERK (U0126), JNK (SP600125), p38 MAPK (SB203580), JAK (AG490), PI3K (LY294002) and IkB-alpha phosphorylation inhibitor (BAY11-7082) on the apoptosis, degranulation, adhesion, expression of cytokines, chemokines and adhesion molecules of iE-DAP and MDP activated co-culture of eosinophils and bronchial epithelial cells.

476411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
476411.value: Aim The aim of this study is to elucidate the intracellular signal transduction mechanisms regulating nucleotide binding oligomerization domain (NOD) like receptors (NLR)-mediated activation of human eosinophils, the principal effector cells responsible for allergic inflammation, upon interacting with human bronchial epithelial cells. Project Background Allergic asthma is a chronically relapsing inflammatory disease, the prevalence of which is increasing both in Hong Kong and worldwide. Respiratory bacterial infection can cause allergen sensitization and subsequently amplify and sustain airway inflammation in allergic asthma. The innate immune system recognizes bacterial infection through pattern recognition receptors (PRRs), and one of the key intracytosolic PRRs in inflammatory and immune responses is NLR. NLR family member NOD1 senses the cytosolic peptidoglycan fragments in all Gram-negative and certain Gram-positive bacteria, while NOD2 senses the muramyl dipeptide in almost all bacteria. Our previous studies suggest a putative role of PRRs toll-like receptors (TLR) in the activation of eosinophils and the essential role of the interaction of eosinophils and bronchial epithelial cells in allergic inflammation, but the detailed intracellular signal transduction mechanisms regulating the link between NLR-mediated innate immunity and allergic inflammation remain to be elucidated. Brief Project Description We hypothesize that NLR is the crucial PRR in the process of allergic inflammation, and it acts by linking the bacteria-mediated innate immune response with the subsequent allergic inflammation through the activation of eosinophils and bronchial epithelial cells. We therefore propose to conduct a study aimed at determining the regulatory mechanisms for NLR-mediated activation of eosinophils and bronchial epithelial cells upon their intercellular interaction in allergic inflammation, in terms of the prolonging cell survival, induction of eosinophilic degranulation, intercellular adhesion, and the induction of essential allergic inflammation related cytokines, chemokines and adhesion molecules. Both clinical and animal studies will be used to confirm the NLR-mediated inflammation. We believe that the valuable experience we have gained during the past decade in our previous studies in this area provides a firm basis for this study. Significance of Project The study is expected to identify the unique intracellular mechanisms for the infection-mediated activation of eosinophils upon the interaction with bronchial epithelial cells in allergic asthma, and should advance our knowledge of the immunopathological mechanisms by which infection-mediated innate immunity can trigger allergic inflammation. Its results should therefore furnish a biochemical basis for the development of therapeutic intervention such as oligodeoxynucleotides targeting NLR for the treatment of eosinophils mediated allergic inflammation. 研究目標 嗜酸性粒細胞是過敏炎症的關鍵效應細胞，本研究擬闡明NLR介導的嗜酸性粒細胞和支氣管上皮細胞的相互和活化作用，並深入探索調節它們相互作用的細胞內信號通路。 研究背景 過敏性哮喘是一種常見的慢性反復發作型炎性疾病，其發病率在香港和全球呈增長趨勢。呼吸道細菌感染可引起機體對過敏原致敏，加重過敏性哮喘病人的氣道炎症反應。機體對細菌感染的先天性免疫應答反應主要通過模式識別受體(PRRs)所介導。 在炎症及免疫應答中，NLR是其中一種關鍵的細胞內PRRs。NLR 家族成員NOD1參與識別所有革蘭氏陰性菌和某些革蘭氏陽性菌中的胞內肽聚醣片斷，而NOD2則識別所有細菌中的胞壁醯二肽。我們前期的研究工作表明PRRs Toll-樣受體(TLR)在過敏性炎症嗜酸性粒細胞的活化中起著重要的重用，並且調節著嗜酸性粒細胞與支氣管上皮細胞間的相互作用。然而，NLR介導的先天性免疫應答與過敏性炎症之間的聯繫，以及調節這種聯繫的細胞內信號途徑，目前並不清楚。 主要研究內容 我們假定NLR是過敏炎症過程中關鍵的PRR，通過活化嗜酸性粒細胞與支氣管上皮細胞，連接由細菌引起的先天性免疫應答及隨後的過敏炎症。因此我們計畫進行本研究，目的在於闡明過敏炎症中，由NLR介導的嗜酸性粒細胞與支氣管上皮細胞活化作用的調節機制。主要研究以下幾方面：延長細胞存活時間，嗜酸性脫粒，細胞間粘附作用，以及過敏炎症相關的細胞因子，趨化因子及粘附分子。臨床實驗及動物實驗亦將用於證實NLR介導的炎症。相信過去十年我們在此研究領域所積累的寶貴經驗將為本研究奠定堅實的基礎。 本研究的重要性 本研究能夠為闡明過敏性哮喘中由感染介導的嗜酸性粒細胞與支氣管上皮細胞活化作用的細胞內機制提供解釋。也將增強我們對感染介導的先天性免疫所引發的過敏炎症的認識。本研究的結果將為過敏炎症藥物治療的發展提供生物化學理論基礎，比如：以NLR為靶向的寡聚去氧核苷酸，用以治療嗜酸性粒細胞介導的過敏炎症。

476411.label: Realisation of objectives
476411.value: (1) We have established the co-culture of human eosinophils with primary bronchial epithelial cells/BEAS-2B bronchial epithelial cells upon the activation by ligands for NOD1, iE-DAP and NOD2, MDP. Our studies showed that eosinophils constitutively expressed NOD1,2 receptors but exhibited non-significant responses to release chemokines upon the stimulation by NOD1 ligand iE-DAP and NOD2 ligand MDP. However, iE-DAP and MDP could significantly up-regulate the cell surface expression of CD18 and ICAM-1 on eosinophils and ICAM-1 on BEAS-2B cells, as well as induce chemokines CCL2 and CXCL8 release in the co-culture of eosinophils and BEAS-2B cells. Both eosinophils and BEAS-2B cells were the main source for CXCL8 and CCL2 release in the co-culture system upon iE-DAP or MDP stimulation. Direct interaction between eosinophils and BEAS-2B cells is responsible for CCL2 release, and soluble mediators are implicated in CXCL8 release. ERK and NF-kB play regulatory roles for the expression of adhesion molecules and chemokines in co-culture. (Objective 1, 3 and 4, Cellular and Molecular Immunology, 2013; 10: 317-329.) (2) Novel inflammatory cytokine IL-32γ exhibited synergistic effect with iE-DAP and MDP on the induction of allergic inflammation-related IL-1beta, TNF-alpha, CXCL8, CCL3 and CCL4. Moreover, IL-32γ and iE-DAP or MDP induced the significant up-regulation of the cell surface expression of adhesion molecule CD18 and ICAM-1 on eosinophils. The further enhanced CD18 and ICAM-1 expression and production of cytokines and chemokines were observed in eosinophils co-cultured with BEAS-2B cells upon combined treatment with IL-32γ and NOD ligands, via the activation of p38 MAPK and NF-kB pathways (Objective 1, 3 and 4, Journal of Leukocyte Biology 2014; 95:631-642.) (3) We have established the ovalbumin-induced allergic asthmatic mice model. Treatment with NOD1,2 ligand could further induce the subepithelial fibrosis and significantly enhance the serum concentration of total IgE, chemokine CCL5 and asthma Th2 cytokine IL-13 in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid of ovalbumin-sensitized allergic asthmatic mice (Objective 2, Cellular and Molecular Immunology, 2013; 10: 317-329.) (4) For the clinical study, we have been recruited 24 diagnosed allergic asthmatic children and 24 sex- and age-matched non-allergic normal control subjects. Significant positive correlation was identified between plasma eosinophilic airway inflammation biomarker periostin and asthma disease severity score. Down-regulation of NOD2 in CCR3-positive granulocytes was observed in allergic asthmatic patients. Ex vivo production of asthma-related chemokine CXCL8 of NOD2 ligand MDP-stimulated granulocytes from non-steroid treated asthmatic patients was found to be significantly higher than normal control subjects. (Objective 2, Inflammation, 2014 acceptable with minor revision).

(2) The difference in the expression of NOD1,2 on eosinophils from patients with allergic asthma and sex- age-matched non-allergic normal control subjects will be investigated and compared. The in vivo activating effect of the injection of NOD1,2 ligands on the cytokine/chemokine concentration and the accumulation of eosinophils at bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid will also be investigated using allergic asthmatic murine model.

(3) The relationship between iE-DAP and MDP mediated the activation of essential intracellular signaling molecules extracellular signal-regulated protein kinase (ERK), c-Jun amino-terminal kinase (JNK), p38 mitogen activated protein kinase (p38 MAPK), Janus kinase-signal transducer and activator of transcription factor (JAK-STAT) and phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)-AKT and transcription factor nuclear factor-kB (NF-kB) with the apoptosis, expression of cytokines, chemokines and adhesion molecules, and eosinophil adhesion and degranulation.

(4) The specific inhibitors of ERK (U0126), JNK (SP600125), p38 MAPK (SB203580), JAK (AG490), PI3K (LY294002) and IkB-alpha phosphorylation inhibitor (BAY11-7082) on the apoptosis, degranulation, adhesion, expression of cytokines, chemokines and adhesion molecules of iE-DAP and MDP activated co-culture of eosinophils and bronchial epithelial cells.

476411.label: Major findings and research outcome
476411.value: (1) We have established the co-culture of human eosinophils with primary bronchial epithelial cells/BEAS-2B bronchial epithelial cells upon the activation by ligands for NOD1, iE-DAP and NOD2, MDP. Our studies showed that eosinophils constitutively expressed NOD1,2 but exhibited non-significant responses to release chemokines upon the stimulation by NOD1 ligand iE-DAP and NOD2 ligand MDP. However, iE-DAP and MDP could significantly up-regulate cell surface expression of CD18 and ICAM-1 on eosinophils and ICAM-1 on BEAS-2B cells, as well as induce chemokines CCL2 and CXCL8 release in the co-culture system. Both eosinophils and BEAS-2B cells were the main source for CXCL8 and CCL2 release in the co-culture system upon iE-DAP or MDP stimulation. Direct interaction between eosinophils and BEAS-2B cells is responsible for CCL2 release, and soluble mediators are implicated in CXCL8 release. ERK and NF-kB play regulatory roles for the expression of adhesion molecules and chemokines in co-culture. (Objective 1, 3 and 4, Cellular and Molecular Immunology, 2013; 10: 317-329.) (2) IL-32γ exhibited synergistic effect with iE-DAP and MDP on the induction of allergic inflammation-related IL-1beta, TNF-alpha, CXCL8, CCL3 and CCL4. Moreover, IL-32γ and iE-DAP or MDP induced the significant up-regulation of the cell surface expression of adhesion molecule CD18 and ICAM-1 on eosinophils. The further enhanced CD18 and ICAM-1 expression and production of cytokines and chemokines were observed in eosinophils co-cultured with BEAS-2B cells upon combined treatment with IL-32γ and NOD ligands, mainly via NF-kB activation. This study provides pivotal immunological mechanisms by which bacterial infection-mediated activation of NOD1,2 together with IL-32γ can synergize the activation of eosinophils interacting with bronchial epithelial cells. (Objective 1, 3 and 4, Journal of Leukocyte Biology 2014; 95:631-642.) (3) Using murine model, treatment with NOD ligand iE-DAP or MDP could significantly increase the inflammatory response and disease severity in allergic asthmatic mice. Together with in vitro study in above part 1,2, bacterial infection-mediated activation of NOD1,2 can further exaggerate allergic asthma via the activation of eosinophils interacting with bronchial epithelial cells at inflammatory airway. (Objective 2, Cellular and Molecular Immunology, 2013; 10: 317-329.) (4) Using clinical study with allergic asthmatic children and normal control subjects, elevated eosinophilic airway inflammation biomarker periostin, dysregulation of NOD2 in granulocytes and elevated ex vivo production of asthma-related chemokine CXCL8 of NOD2 ligand MDP-stimulated granulocytes in asthmatic patients implied that the aberrant expression of NOD2 in granulocytes and innate immunity may contribute to the inflammatory process in allergic asthma. (Objective 2, Inflammation, 2014 acceptable with minor revision).

476411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
476411.value: (1) Our above established techniques for co-culture, paraformaldehyde fixation and transwell experiments can provide experimental basis and settings to facilitate further studies of the interaction between different immune effector cells with fibroblasts, endothelial cells and keratinocytes in different immunological disorders such as atopic dermatitis, rheumatoid arthritis, influenza infection etc. It also provides a cell-based platform to mimic the local inflammatory sites to evaluate the potential therapeutic agent including traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) for treating inflammatory diseases. Using the above techniques of co-culture, our research group has started the mechanistic and clinical study of the interaction of basophils with dermal fibroblasts of atopic dermatitis supported by RGC-GRF. Furthermore, study of TCM with anti-inflammatory activities is on-going. (2) The established ovalbumin-induced allergic asthmatic mice model provides an in vivo platform for the study of the immunopatholgical mechanisms of allergic asthma and the development of novel treatments using biological agents or TCM. We have obtained National Natural Science Foundation of China funding for the translational study of novel regulatory IL-35 for treating allergic asthma. (3) Our present findings from this study of immunopathological and innate immunity mechanisms of allergic inflammation should provide insights on the future development of therapeutic intervention such as signaling molecule/receptor inhibitor for allergic disorders.

476411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
476411.value: In this study of the immunological relationship between bacterial infection and allergic inflammation, especially in allergic asthma, we have found that eosinophils, the principal effector cells in allergic inflammation, constitutively expressed bacterial sensor NOD1,2. Crucial bacterial cell wall components iE-DAP and MDP (NOD1,2 ligands) could significantly up-regulate cell surface expression of adhesion molecules on eosinophils and bronchial epithelial cells, as well as induce inflammatory chemokines release upon the intercellular interaction between eosinophils and bronchial epithelial cells. Such bacterial infection-mediated allergic inflammation was found to be regulated by distinct intracellular signaling mechanisms. We also demonstrated that novel inflammatory cytokine IL-32 exhibited synergistic effect on the activation of eosinophils and bronchial epithelial cells to provoke allergic inflammation, thereby further implicating the novel immunological and mechanistic link between bacterial infections and airway inflammation in allergic asthma. Allergic asthmatic mice also showed that bacterial infection-mediated activation of NOD1,2 can further exaggerate the inflammation of allergic asthma. Allergic asthmatic children showed the aberrant expression of NOD2 in granulocytes and innate immune response against bacterial infections. Together, the above findings and established co-culture platform will facilitate the future development of selective inhibitors for cytokines, intracellular signaling molecules and natural products for the treatment of allergic inflammatory diseases.

476611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
476611.value: Urease hydrolyzes urea into ammonia, which neutralizes the gastric acid and allows the colonization of Helicobacter pylori in human stomach. The apo-urease undergoes a post-translation carbamylation of an active-site lysine residue, followed by the insertion of two nickel ions essential for catalysis. In H. pylori, four urease accessory proteins, UreE, UreF, UreG, and UreH, are essential to the maturation process of urease. The current model postulates that the apo-urease either bind a pre-formed UreG/UreF/UreH complex, or the individual urease accessory proteins sequentially to form a pre-activation complex. The Ni-binding protein UreE then interacts with the UreG of the complex, and triggers the GTP-dependent activation of urease. How these urease accessory proteins interact with each other and with the urease to form the activation complex is poorly understood, partly because of the lack of high-resolution structures available for these urease accessory proteins. The only urease accessory proteins whose structures are available are UreE and UreF. We have recently obtained a preliminary structure of the UreF/UreH complex. The novel structural information allows us to use the protein engineering approach to address the following questions: (1) Is the dimerization of H. pylori UreF/UreH complex essential to the maturation of urease? (2) Is the interaction between UreF and UreH essential to the maturation of urease? (3) Where is the interacting surface on the UreF/UreH complex that are responsible for binding UreG and the urease? As we have already obtained crystals of the UreG/UreF/UreH complex that diffract to good resolution, we propose to determine the crystal structure of this ternary complex. Through this work, the structures of all urease accessory proteins involved in urease maturation will be available, and together with the mutagenesis data, we will have a better understanding of how the urease accessory proteins associate with the urease to form the pre-activation complex for the maturation of urease. 尿素酶將尿素水解為氨，氨能夠中和胃酸並為幽門螺旋桿菌（Helicobacter pylori）在人類的胃部中繁殖提供條件。 Apo-尿素酶的一個賴氨酸殘基作為活性位點經歷了翻譯後氨甲酰化修飾，其後插入的兩個鎳離子對催化反應至關重要。在幽門螺旋桿菌中，四個尿素酶輔助蛋白UreE、UreF、UreG和UreH對尿素酶的成熟過程是必不可少的。目前的研究模型假設apo-尿素酶或是結合預先形成的UreG/UReF/UreH複合體，或是逐個結合這些輔助蛋白以形成一個激活前複合體。之後，鎳結合蛋白UreE再與復合體中的UreG相互作用繼而激活GTP依賴的尿素酶。 我們對於這些尿素酶輔助蛋白是如何相互作用以及它們與尿素酶怎樣形成活性複合體還知之甚少，部分原因在於缺乏這些尿素酶輔助蛋白的高分辨率結構。目前已知結構的尿素酶輔助蛋白包括UreE和UreF，最近我們獲得了UreF/UreH複合體的初步結構。這些新的結構使我們能夠利用蛋白質工程的方法解決以下問題：（1）UreF/UreH複合體的二聚作用在幽門螺旋桿菌尿素酶的成熟過程中是否是不可或缺的？ （2）UreF和UreH之間的相互作用是否在尿素酶的成熟過程中發揮了至關重要的作用？ （3）UreF/UreH複合體與UreG和尿素酶結合的反應位點在何處？我們已經得到具有良好分辨率的UreG/UreF/UreH複合體的衍射晶體並準備測定此三元復合體的結構。通過該項研究，尿素酶的成熟過程中涉及的所有輔助蛋白的結構將被測定解析，它們和突變實驗得到的數據將使我們能更好地了解在尿素酶的成熟過程中尿素酶輔助蛋白如何與尿素酶結合而形成預活化複合體。

476611.label: Realisation of objectives
476611.value: The main theme of this GRF project is to study the how urease accessory proteins UreF, UreH, and UreG facilitate maturation of H. pylori urease. At the start of this project, we have already solved the crystal structure of UreF/UreH complex. We showed that UreF/UreH form a dimer of dimers in solution (and in the crystal structures). Crystal structure of UreF/UreH revealed that homodimerization of UreF/UreH is mediated via UreF. By static-light scattering, we showed that R179A/Y183D mutations at the dimerization interface of UreF will break the homodimerization of UreF/UreH. Using this mutant of UreF, we have successfully showed that dimerization of UreF/UreH is essential to the formation of UreG/UreF/UreH complex and to the urease maturation (objective 1). Moreover, we found that the conserved C-terminal residues of UreF were essential to the interaction between UreF/UreH. We showed that UreF/UreH interaction is important to urease maturation because deletion of these C-terminal residues of UreF resulted in breakage of UreF/UreH interaction and abolished urease maturation (objective 2). Based on the crystal structures of UreF/UreH, we have identified conserved residues on the surface of UreF and UreH. Mutagenesis experiments showed that the conserved residues on UreF are responsible for binding UreG, while those on UreH are responsible for binding urease (objective 3). The most significant result of this project is the determination of the structure of UreG/UreF/UreH complex by X-ray crystallography (objective 4). The crystal structure reveals how conformational changes induced by UreF/UreH interaction prepares the UreF to recruit UreG. Most importantly, the structure reveals, for the first time, UreG also dimerizes in the UreG/UreF/UreH complex and brings together a potential nickel binding site within the dimerization interface. Inspired by this structural insights, we further showed that dimerization of UreG is promoted by the binding of GTP and nickel, and hydrolysis of GTP will result in dissociation of UreG dimer and the release of nickel. These findings were reported in PLoS Biology (Fong et al., 11:e1001678).

476611.label: Major findings and research outcome
476611.value: 1. Crystal structure of UreG/UreF/UreH complex reveals how these urease accessory proteins assemble together to facilitate urease maturation We determined the structure of UreG/UreF/UreH complex in its GDP-bound state to 2.35 Å resolution. The structure of UreG, as first revealed in our structure of UreG/UreF/UreH, adopts a fold representative of SIMIBI class GTPases containing the canonical G1 to G5 motif for guanine nucleotide recognition. Each UreG protomer makes extensive contacts with both protomers of UreF. These interacting residues are located near to the switch I and II (G2 and G3) motifs and the nickel binding motifs of UreG, suggesting GTP-dependent conformational changes may affect interaction between UreG and UreF. Each UreG protomer is in intimate contact with the conserved C-terminal residues of UreF, suggesting that binding of UreH induces the ordering of the F-tail loop structure is required for the recruitment of UreG. 2. Dimerization of UreF/UreH is essential to urease maturation Based on the crystal structures, we have introduced mutations at the dimeric interface of UreF and created a dimerization-deficient mutant of UreF (R179A/Y183D). Our results suggest that homodimerization of UreF/UreH complex is essential for the recruitment of two copies of UreG to form the (UreG/UreF/UreH)2 complex and urease maturation. 3. GTP-dependent dimerization of UreG provides a link between GTP hydrolysis to nickel delivery to urease We showed that addition of nickel and GTP to the UreG/UreF/UreH complex dissociated UreG from UreF/UreH, and formed a nickel-charged UreG dimer, which bind one molecule of nickel at the dimeric interface. C66A and H68A mutations at the metal binding motif abolished the formation of UreG dimer and nickel binding. Interestingly, GTP hydrolysis, induced by addition of bicarbonate, resulted in dissociation of UreG dimer and release of nickel into the solution. Our results suggest a plausible mechanism that couples GTP hydrolysis to the delivery of nickel to the active site of urease. 4. Conserved residues of UreH forms a binding surface for recruiting urease to the pre-activation complex Mutagenesis and pull-down assay have showed that conserved residues of UreH (D61, K84, R146 and E151) are important are important in recruiting the urease to the pre-activation complex. Moreover, these mutations on UreH also resulted in failure to activate urease in vivo, suggesting interacting between UreH and urease is essential to urease maturation.

476611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
476611.value: Through this project, we have determined the structure of UreG/UreF/UreH complex and showed that GTP hydrolysis induces dissociation of the UreG dimer and results in release of the nickel bound at the interface. It is expected that UreG should undergo significant conformational changes from the GTP-bound state to the GDP-bound state. It would be interesting to determine the structure of the nickel-charged UreG dimer to further understand the conformational changes required to couple GTP hydrolysis to nickel delivery. Moreover, the structural and mechanistic insights on urease maturation obtained through this study will provide a solid platform for the discovery of drugs that inhibit the maturation of urease in H. pylori. Since urease is essential to the colonization of H. pylori in acidic stomach, one can argue that the urease maturation pathway could be a potential target for novel anti-H. pylori treatment.

476611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
476611.value: Helicobactor pylori, which infects more than half of the human population, is the major cause for peptic ulcers. Urease, which neutralizes stomach acid by hydrolysis of urea into ammonia, is essential to the colonization of H. pylori in human stomach. In order to become active, urease undergoes post-translational modifications such as carbamylation of a lysine residue and the insetion of two nickel ions at the active site. This maturation process requires the protein-protein interaction among four urease accessory proteins, namely UreE, UreF, UreH and UreG. It was not known how these proteins interplay with each other to facilitate urease maturation. Our structure determination of the UreG/UreF/UreH complex represent a significant breakthrough in the understanding of how these urease accessary proteins interact with each other to activate urease. We have shown, for the first time, how the dimerization of UreG can create a nickel binding site at the interface and how GTP hydrolysis could be coupled to nickel delivery in the urease maturation process. Our structural and mechanistic insights may also serve as a foundation for the development of anti-H. pylori treatment.

476711.value: 在肝細胞癌（HCC）的病人中，腫瘤轉移是影響病人發病率和死亡率的主要原因。然而，我們對於腫瘤細胞擴散的分子基礎及生物學機制仍然知之甚少。早前我們關於基因組的分析結果顯示，在HCC的逐步發展過程中有特定的基因變異，如在染色體7q21-q22區域上的擴增與晚期腫瘤轉移有著密切關係。在此基礎上，我們在這個區域進一步確定了目標癌基因PFTK1，一個新的cdc相關蛋白激酶成員，并證實了PFTK1可以通過肌動蛋白細胞骨架重塑作用促進HCC細胞的遷移和侵襲能力。最近，我們的實驗結果揭示了PFTK1在肝癌生成過程中更為重要的功能作用。我們發現在HCC中，PFTK1可以激活包括Snail，ZEB1和ZEB2在內的轉錄抑制子，從而誘導HCC細胞的間質性轉變。同樣地，我們發現E-cadherin的表達下調以及間質標記物Vimentin的表達上調，此兩者均為上皮間質轉變（EMT）過程中的重要組分。我們的研究結果指出在PFTK1表達的細胞中，細胞高表達了幹細胞標誌物（Nanog，Oct2，Oct4和Notch1）并獲得了類似幹細胞的特性。功能上來說，PFTK1表達的細胞擁有克隆性，自我更新能力，抗藥性和體內腫瘤生成能力。最近有報導指出在果蠅中，PFTK1與cyclin Y結合，并一同介導跨膜受體LRP6的磷酸化作用。通過穩定胞漿beta-catenin并促進其轉運進入胞核內可以起始Wnt信號通路，而在此起始激活過程中，LRP6的磷酸化是一個重要的事件。在HCC中，我們發現PFTK1表達細胞中的活性beta-catenin水平更高，而通過RNAi介導抑制PFTK1后，Wnt通路中報告基因的TOPFLASH活性會同時減弱。在HCC中，Wnt信號通路是其中一條主要的致癌信號通路，我們假設PFTK1的上調對於beta-catenin的激活起著重要作用，並使癌癥持續發展。另外，越來越多的證據表明，具有幹細胞特性的細胞生成和EMT有著關聯，並且這可能是癌細胞發生轉移的先決條件。因此，我們的目標是進一步描述出PFTK1 在Wnt/beta-catenin信號通路中的作用機制。另外在HCC中，PFTK1在誘導EMT以及在細胞獲得幹細胞特性過程中的功能亦是我們研究的重點。

476711.label: Realisation of objectives
476711.value: In this study, we demonstrated the presence of protein interaction between PFTK1 and cyclin Y in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The PFTK1-CCNY complex activates the β-catenin-independent noncanonical Wnt pathway but keeps the canonical Wnt/β-catenin intact (Objective 1). The subsequent activation of Rho GTPases (RhoA, Rac1 and Cdc42) in the noncanonical Wnt pathways further leads to actin polymerization and stress fibers formation, and cell motility (Objective 2). To date, HCC is still a high malignant human tumor that is associated with high mortality rate due to frequent metastasis. In this study, we delineated the role of PFTK1 in HCC. Our work outlined a molecular pathway in HCC cells where PFTK1 binds with cyclin Y in activating the Rho GTPases in the noncanonical Wnt pathways, which result in the actin polymerization that underlies cell motility and migration. The identification of such signaling cascade could provide better understandings on HCC metastasis and novel information for development of new drugs and regimen. More recently, our data suggested PFTK1 could induce EMT changes in HCC cells. Essential EMT components, including lowered expression of adhesion molecule E-Cadherin and up-regulation of mesenchymal marker Vimentin, were readily observed in response to PFTK1 expression. Recent advances in the field of metastasis research revealed that induction of EMT can infact generate cells with stem-like properties. However, although the phenotypic association between EMT and cancer stem cell gene signature is now recognized, the underlying mechanism remains unclear. In investigating the objective on cancer stemness features from PFTK1, we found that activated Wnt pathway could specifically enrich ZFX over-expression. The zinc finger protein X-linked (ZFX) gene encodes a zinc finger protein of Zfy family, which is highly conserved in vertebrates. This transcriptional regulator is not only highly expressed in embryonic stem cells and hematopoietic stem cells, but is also upregulated in a number of human cancers where it is functionally related to cell proliferation and survival. In line with the pluripotency role of ZFX, we found silencing of ZFX readily inhibited self-renewal capability, colony formation ability and cell proliferation of HCC cells. In addition, suppression of ZFX sensitized HCC cells to chemotherapeutic agent cisplatin. Further investigation suggested ZFX affects the expression of two important mediators, namely Nanog and SOX-2 in HCC. Taken together, our results showed overexpression of ZFX in HCC likely contributes to stemness and pluripotent behaviors, conceivably from the induction of PFTK1. (Objectives 3 & 4).

476711.label: Major findings and research outcome
476711.value: The noncanonical Wnt pathways consist of the planar cell polarity pathway and calcium signaling pathway, both of which lead to the activation of Rho family of small GTPases (RhoA, Rac1 and Cdc42) and actin polymerization. Our data from this study verified activation of the noncanonical Wnt pathway by demonstrating an increased active form of RhoA, Rac1 and Cdc42 and marked polymerization of filamentous actin in PFTK1 and CCNY co-transfected cells. Because Rho GTPases regulate the processes of cytoskeletal dynamics and formation of lamellipodia, filopodia and actin stress fibers, it is conceivable these features are important in the dissemination of primary cancer cells. Our findings may be interpreted as PFTK1 promotes HCC metastasis through interacting with cyclin Y and activating the noncanonical Wnt pathway (Sun TT et al, 2014) We also investigated the stemness features induced from PFTK1 and showed a specific enrichment of ZFX over-expression. The ZFX gene is a transcriptional regulator for self-renewal, growth and differentiation. In line with its pluripotency role, we found silencing of ZFX readily inhibited self-renewal capability, colony formation ability and cell proliferation through G0/G1 cell cycle arrest of HCC cells. In addition, suppression of ZFX sensitized HCC cells to chemotherapeutic agent cisplatin. Further investigations suggested that ZFX bind on the promoter of two important mediators, namely Nanog and SOX-2, activating their expressions in HCC. Moreover, in vivo xenograft study demonstrated that overexpression of ZFX would promote the tumor growth. Taken together, our results showed overexpression of ZFX from the induction of PFTK1 likely contributes to stemness and pluripotent behaviors in HCC (Lai KP et al, 2014)

476711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
476711.value: It is well-known that canonical Wnt/β-catenin pathway plays an important role in human tumorigenesis. Nevertheless, increasing evidence has emerged to indicate components of the noncanonical Wnt pathways are also commonly overexpressed in breast, colon, lung and gastric cancers. We observed activation of the noncanonical Wnt pathways in HCC with PFTK1 and cyclin Y co-expression, while maintaining a quiescent canonical Wnt pathway. The expression of dishevelled segment polarity protein 2 (Dvl2) was markedly up-regulated in cells co-transfected with PFTK1 and CCNY. Although Dvl2 is able to activate both the noncanonical pathway and the canonical β-catenin pathway, we further found the protein expression level of naked cuticle homolog 1 (Naked1) was also up-regulated. Naked1 inhibits the canonical Wnt/β-catenin signaling by directing the protein activity of Dvl towards the noncanonical pathway upon binding with Dvl. Further investigations based on the findings from this research could potentially unveil important roles for the noncanonical Wnt signaling in HCC tumorigenesis. Also, the functions and downstream targets consequential to the activation of PFTK1-CCNY complex could yield valuable information in the regulatory network of EMT and cancer stem cell-like features.

476711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
476711.value: PFTK1 is a Cdc2-related protein kinase that is frequently upregulated in human hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) where it correlates with metastatic features and motile phenotypes. To understand the modulated pathway underlining the PFTK1 action, in this project we showed a physical interaction between PFTK1 and cyclin Y (CCNY) in promoting the noncanonical Wnt signaling pathway. In HCC cells, we found PFTK1 forms a direct complex with CCNY, and together readily upregulate key components of Wnt signaling (Dvl2 and Naked1). Exogenous expression of PFTK1 and CCNY activated Rho GTPases, which are known targets of the noncanonical path. In line with Rho GTPases activation, we also found marked actin polymerizations in cells with PFTK1–CCNY co-expressions. Our findings highlight a PFTK1–CCNY complex interaction in activating noncanonical Wnt signaling in HCC cells, which bestow these cells with motile and metastatic capabilities.

476811.label: Realisation of objectives
476811.value: The FOUR objectives of the project have been achieved after 42 months of study. The following results are obtained for these objectives. Objectives 1: The natural sphalerite (NS) has very good performance in visible-light-driven (VLD) photocatalytic disinfection of the selected bacteria, namely, Escherichia coli (Chen et al. 2013, Xia et al. 2013). Objectives 2: The major reactive species for photocatalytic bacterial inactivation are: H2O2 and e- for E. coli (Chen et al., 2013, Wang et al. 2012) and H2O2 for M. barkeri (Chen et al., 2013). Objective 3: The reactive species attack the cell membrane since the K+ leakage is observed as the first sign of cell damage, and then the cytoplasm and cell wall damage is observed under transmission electron microscopic (TEM) analysis (Gao et al. 2012, Chen et al., 2013, Xia et al. 2013) Objective 4: The NS-FT VLD photocatalytic system also has very good inactivation ability towards other water-borne bacteria such as Microbacterium barkeri (Chen et al., 2013)

476811.label: Major findings and research outcome
476811.value: There are several major findings of the project: (1) NS has very good performance in VLD photocatalytic bacterial disinfection (Chen et al. 2013, Xia et al. 2013). (2) Among all tested visible light sources (FT, LED lamp and Xenon lamp) at the same intensity, NS under FT irradiation shows better VLD photocatalytic bacterial disinfection ability. (3) The NS-FT VLD photocatalytic system effective inactivate various types of water-borne bacteria including E. coli and M. barkeri (Chen et al. 2103) (4) The major reactive (charged and oxidative) species to inactivate bacteria are H2O2 and e- (Chen et al. 2013, Xia et al. 2013). (5) The reactive species first attack the cell membrane of bacterial cell and lead to the leakage of K+, followed by the damage of cytoplasm and cell wall (Chen et al. 2013, Xia et al. 2013). (6) The activity of anti-oxidative enzymes such as catalase increases at the early stage of VLD photocatalytic disinfection and then decreases due to excess amount of oxidative species are produced. (Chen et al. 2013) (7) Screening among various NS samples collected from different mining site, one NS sample show very good VLD photocatalytic bacterial disinfection activity and has magnetic property (Xia et al. 2013). The presence of iron makes sphalerite (ZnS) to become VL active and have magnetic property.

476811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
476811.value: The large amount and low cost of NS provide an excellent opportunity to use it in large-scale VLD photocatalytic disinfection water (or wastewater) treatment. The discovery of magnetic NS sample (NMS) even greatly enhance its applicability due to the ease of recycling and reuse. The stability and reusability of NMS (and NS) lead to a success in applying of an ITSP Tier 3 Scheme support to develop a pilot-scale device for industrial application.

476811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
476811.value: A natural sphalerite (NS) sample is developed and characterized for a visible-light-driven (VLD) photocatalytic bacterial disinfection system. Fluorescent tube (FT), the most common and safe light system in most premises, is selected as the most appropriate visible light (VL) source for NS in VLD photocatalytic disinfection process. The major reactive species involving in bacterial inactivation of photocatalytic process are identified and the bacterial inactivation mechanism is obtained. Among the collected NS samples, one unique sample show magnetic property due to the presence of iron. This unique magnetic NS (NMS) has a good potential for developing a large-scale, cost effective VLD photocatalytic disinfection system for large-scale water (and wastewater) treatment.

477111.value: 本研究的主要目的是明瞭魚類如何適應環境鹽度的改變。魚類在稀釋環境下攝入氯離子，但在超鹽度下則排出氯離子。其中氯離子運輸主要是通過鰓及腸的囊胞性纖維症跨膜調節器(CFTR) 。已知在不同鹽度下，CFTR氯離子通道是位於滲透調節細胞內不同部位。本研究將詳盡地探討CFTR通道如何在鰓氯離子細胞、鰓表細胞和腸細胞操作以適應鹽度改變。除此，本研究也探討魚類CFTR是否也能調節滲透調節細胞的谷胱甘肽(GSH)運輸，以達成抗氧化效果。本研究也探討兩主要滲透調節激素(包括促乳素和皮質醇)對CFTR表現的影响。具體實驗包括 (i) 評測CFTR在鯛魚組織內的表現 (ii) 探討控制GSH通過CFTR通道的機制，(iii) 研究皮質醇和促乳素如何調控CFTR通道。本研究將對魚類CFTR功能、表達和調節提供一系列新的理解。

477311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
477311.value: The aim of this project is to study the mechanisms by which the BMP co-receptor repulsive guidance molecule b (RGMb) regulates BMP signaling in oocytes, and the effects of disruption of this regulation on oocyte function and follicle development. Fertility disorders in humans are a major health problem. The cause is unknown among 25% of those with infertility, underlining our lack of knowledge in the underlying mechanisms of reproduction. Genetic studies with mice, sheep and human have revealed crucial functions of bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs) in follicle development. However, the precise regulation of BMP signaling in different cell populations including oocytes within the ovary is poorly understood. BMP2 and BMP4 are expressed in granulosa cells and theca cells in the ovary. BMP2 and BMP4 normally signal through BMPRII but not ActRIIA. Surprisingly, ActRIIA, but not BMPRII, is the predominant BMP type II receptor in oocytes, thus providing a puzzle as to how BMP2 and BMP4 from granulosa and theca cells can efficiently signal oocytes. RGMb is a member of the RGM family, which also includes RGMa and RGMc (hemojuvelin). We recently identified the three RGM members as BMP co-receptors that enhance BMP signaling. Within the mouse ovary, RGMb is exclusively expressed in oocytes. Interestingly, we showed that RGMa and RGMc facilitate the use of ActRIIA by BMP2 and BMP4, while the mechanism by which RGMb enhances BMP2 and BMP4 signaling remains unknown. Importantly, our preliminary data show that the ovaries of RGMb knockout mice have significant defects in antral follicle formation. Our hypothesis is that the presence of RGMb in oocytes allows BMP2 and BMP4 to gain the ability to signal oocytes via ActRIIA, thus regulating BMP signaling in oocytes, which, in turn, influences the functions of granulosa cells. In this project, we will 1) study whether RGMb, like its homologues, enhances utilization of ActRIIA by BMP2 and BMP4; 2) determine the role of RGMb in regulating BMP signaling in oocytes and follicle development; 3) elucidate the underlying mechanisms of RGMb action in regulating oocyte function and follicle development. Knowledge gained in the regulation of BMP signaling by RGMb during follicle development would be important in furthering our understanding of mechanisms of follicle maturation. This research could also identify new targets and pathways for developing treatments for ovarian-based fertility disorders. 本项目旨在研究骨形成蛋白（BMP）辅助受体RGMb在卵母细胞中对BMP信号的调节、以及干扰这一调节对卵母细胞功能及生殖的影响。 不育是人类一大健康问题，而引起不育的病因在许多不育病人还不清楚，说明我们仍缺乏对生殖过程及其机理的了解。对小鼠、绵羊及人类的遗传学研究发现BMP对卵泡发育有极其重要的功能，但卵巢内各类细胞中BMP信号的精确调节尚不清楚。BMP2和BMP4分别在卵母细胞和颗粒细胞表达。BMP2和BMP4通常是通过BMPRII而不是ActRIIA来传导信号。但是BMPRII在卵母细胞并不表达，而ActRIIA却是卵母细胞中的主要II型受体。这样引出的问题就是，BMP2和BMP4信号如何在卵母细胞有效传导。 RGMb是RGM家族三成员之一。RGM家族还包括RGMa和RGMc（hemojuvelin）。我们最近发现RGM家族三成员都是BMP辅助受体，它们能增强BMP信号。在小鼠卵巢中，RGMb只在卵母细胞表达。有意思的是，我们的研究发现RGMa和RGMc可促使BMP2和BMP4通过ActRIIA来传导信号，但RGMb是否利用这一机理来增强BMP2和BMP4信号，则尚待研究。另外，我们初步研究发现，RGMb基因敲除小鼠卵巢中有腔卵泡发育存在严重缺陷。因此，我们提出的假设是，卵母细胞所表达的RGMb使得BMP2和BMP4能够通过ActRIIA来调节卵母细胞内BMP信号强度与卵母细胞功能，进而影响颗粒细胞功能与卵泡发育。 具体来说，我们将1）研究RGMb是否与RGMa和RGMc一样能促使BMP2和BMP4利用ActRIIA来传导信号；2）检测RGMb在调节卵母细胞内BMP信号及卵泡发育中的作用；3）查明RGMb在调节卵母细胞功能及卵泡发育中的作用机理。 通过本项目所获得的结果将有助于进一步理解卵泡发育机制。该研究还有可能有助于鉴定治疗卵巢性不育的新靶点。

477311.label: Realisation of objectives
477311.value: As proposed in Objective 1, we examined the BMP ligands and receptors used by RGMb (a. k. a., Dragon) to enhance BMP signaling. We found that RGMb primarily uses BMP2 and BMP4 as its ligands, and RGMb enhances utilization of ActRIIA by BMP2 and BMP4 as the other two RGM family members RGMa and RGMc do. Interestingly, we also found that RGMb functions through the neogenin receptor, a member of the immunoglobulin superfamily of transmembrane receptors, to inhibit apoptosis in cell culture. In Objectives 2 and3, we proposed to study the role of RGMb in follicle development using our global RGMb knockout mice (Rgmb gKO). These two objectives were based on our preliminary observations that there were no antral follicles in the ovaries collected from Rgmb gKO mice while there are many small antral follicles in the wild type littermates. However, Rgmb gKO mice die between 2 and 3 weeks after birth with systematic inflammation. The phenotypes we saw in Rgmb cKO mice may have been caused by the inflammation. To determine the specific role of RGMb in the ovary, we proposed to use in vitro ovary culture to study follicle development using ovaries from wild type and Rgmb gKO mice. However, we found that there were too much variations in the in vitro culture system. Therefore, we used a better approach, i.e., oocyte-specific Rgmb knockout mice (Rgmb conditional knockout, Rgmb cKO). We previously found that RGMb is expressed in the oocytes of secondary and antral follicles. In the present study, we found that RGMb is also expressed in the oocytes of primordial and primary follicles. We then crossbred floxed Rgmb mice with occyte-specific Cre mice. To our surprise, Rgmb cKO mice showed normal follicle development and fertility. Smad1/5/8 phosphorylation levels in the ovary were also similar between wild type and Rgmb cKO mice. These results led us to conclude that RGMb is not essential for normal follicle development under basal conditions. These unexpected results do not appear to support a significant role of RGMb’s BMP signaling function in the ovary. Whether loss of RGMb has been compensated by increased expression of other RGM family members or other components in the BMP pathway is still under investigation. In addition, whether RGMb plays a role in follicle development in mice exposed to adverse conditions may be an interesting topic to be investigated.

477311.value: 1. 477311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
477311.value: RGMb is a membrane-associated protein. We have found that RGMb is a co-receptor that enhances BMP signaling. BMP signaling plays an important role in the ovary. In the present study, we found that RGMb is highly expressed in the oocytes of all the follicles within the ovary in mice. However, specific deletion of RGMb in oocytes did not affect follicle development and fertility in mice. Therefore, RGMb is not essential for normal ovarian function. It is possible that loss of RGMb has been compensated by increased expression of other RGM family members or other components in the BMP pathway. The findings from the present study promote us to study whether RGMb plays a role in follicle development in mice exposed to adverse conditions.
