501911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
501911.value: The vital role played by peroxy radicals in the budgets of ozone, NOx, HOx and halogenated XO radicals throughout the troposphere is well documented and the importance of these species in determining atmospheric composition, the earth’s radiative balance and any future change in climate cannot be over-emphasised. However, recently our knowledge of the complex interplay between these important families of radicals has been augmented by field measurements and comparison of the results obtained has been made with results of sophisticated computer models. These comparisons show that reliable experimental rate coefficients and branching ratios are urgently needed for a number of important peroxy and related radical reactions. The free radical reactions chosen for study in this proposal have been selected because for each reaction at least two product channels are possible and because there are important questions concerning their product distributions relevant to atmospheric chemistry that need to be addressed. For example, reaction of alkyl peroxy radicals with XO radicals are important contributors to the ozone budget in the troposphere and reactions between XO radicals lead to ozone depletion in the stratosphere. Measurement of their branching ratios and channel specific rate coefficients will lead to a firmer understanding of their contributions to the ozone budget in the troposphere and stratosphere. The experimental work will involve measurement of reaction rate coefficients and reaction branching ratios with Chemical Ionization Mass Spectrometry (CIMS), and Photoelectron Spectroscopy (PES). PES will also be used to investigate the structures of the reaction intermediates. It is only by having the combined detection capabilities of CIMS and PES that all reaction products can be monitored, thus facilitating the full mass balance of a radical reaction to be quantified for the first time. Also, computation of the reaction surface and channel specific rate coefficients with electronic structure methods will lead to a detailed understanding of the reaction mechanism and allow a comparison between experimental and calculated rate coefficients. In summary, the objective of this work is to determine, both experimentally and computationally, the channel specific rate coefficients of atmospherically relevant reactions of alkyl peroxy and related radicals. The significance of this work is that it will improve understanding of atmospherically important radical reactions and will provide reliable channel specific rate coefficients which are needed for local, regional and global scale atmospheric models. This will allow reliable calculation of important atmospheric quantities such as ozone and greenhouse gas concentrations. 過氧自由基對大氣對流層中的化學物質如臭氧，氮氧化物，HOx和鹵氧化物 XO自由基的數量有重大的影響，其重要性被廣泛報導，這些物質對大氣成分，地球的輻射平衡和未來氣候的變化的影響是無容置疑。然而，我們對這些自由基之間複雜相互作用的了解，透過實地測量加上和先進計算機模型的結果比較，仍在不繼增長。這些比較顯示，對於一些重要自由基的化學反應，可靠的實驗反應速率係數與及反應支化比是十分迫切。 本項目所選擇的自由基反應，每個反應至少有兩個可能的反應通度，並且了解它們的化學產物分佈可助解決一些重要的大氣化學問題。例如，烷基過氧基與 XO自由基的反應對流層臭氧有重要影響，而XO自由基也是導致平流層臭氧耗盡的主因。測量不同反應的通道速率係數及其分支比幫助我們便確切了解這些自由基對對流層和同溫層的臭氧的收支的影響。 實驗的工作將利用化學電離質譜（Chemical Ionization Mass Spectrometry, CIMS）和光電子能譜（Photoelectron Spectroscopy, PES）測量反應速率和反應分支比。 光電子能譜亦將用於分析反應中間體的結構。透過結合CIMS和PES的檢測能力，可望監測所有的反應產物，道次建立一個能夠對自由基反應作出詳細質量平衡觀測的方法。此外，利用量子化學方法計算反應表面和特定通道的反應速率係數可對反應機理提出一個詳細的分析，並與實驗的結果互相比較。 總括而言，本項目的工作目標是利用實驗和計算的手段，測量烷基過氧基及相關自由基在大氣反應的特定反應通度的反應速率係數及支化比。這項工作的意義在於提高大氣中重要自由基反應的了解，並提供地方、區域和全球尺度大氣化學模型所需的特定通道反應率係數。以便能準確的預計一些重要的大氣數據，如臭氧和溫室氣體的濃度。

501911.label: Realisation of objectives
501911.value: Following the revised objective 1, temperature-dependent rate coefficients of the BrO + CH3O2 reaction and the branching ratios of the HOBr + CH2O2 product channel were measured with Chemical Ionization Mass Spectrometry (CIMS) by monitoring [BrO] and [HOBr] temporal profiles in the temperature range of 243 to 276 K. HOBr was detected and calibrated by CIMS, which enabled its temperature dependent branching ratios (0.73 to 0.84 at 246 and 296 K respectively) to be determined for the first time. Following revised objectives 2 and 3, the reaction energy surface of the BrO + CH3O2 → HOBr + CH2O2 reaction was investigated by DFT/ab initio calculations. The transition state (TS) structure for this channel, which could not be found previously, has now been located by using the M06-2X and BH&HLYP functionals. Further high level ab initio single-reference {RCCSD(T)/CBS+core+R/UCCSD(T)+SO) and multi-reference (CASSCF, MRCI-F12, NEVPT2 and CASPT2-F12) energy calculations were performed. Combining SR and MR results, the activation barrier (ΔEe‡) and reaction enthalpy (ΔH298KRX) were computed to be -7.19 and -22.57 kcal.mol-1, respectively. Reaction rate coefficients were computed employing variational transition state theory (VTST) including tunnelling and various computed DFT/ab initio reaction surfaces. Comparison between computed and measured rate coefficients suggests a negative barrier height of ca. -0.8 kcal.mol-1. The new kinetic and product data derived from this study have been incorporated into two global atmospheric chemistry models: STOCHEM-CRI for tropospheric analysis and TOMCAT for stratospheric analysis. This work has been published (see section C). Revised objectives 1 to 3 are largely achieved. Following revised objective 4, the reaction energy surfaces of the BrO + HO2 reaction was studied by DFT/ab initio calculations, namely M06-2X/AVDZ geometry optimization and harmonic vibrational frequency calculations, followed by single energy BD(T) and BD(TQ) calculation employing basis sets of up to AVQZ quality. By extrapolation to the complete basis set (CBS) limit, BD(TQ)/CBS//M06-2X/AVDZ level results were obtained. Among the five reaction channels to HOBr + 1O2, HOBr + 3O2, HBr + O3, OH + OBrO and OH + BrOO considered, the HOBr + 1O2 channel was found to be the major channel. Temperature dependent rate coefficients of this reaction channel were computed using VTST, as described above, and also the two TSs approach employing phase space theory for the loose TS using VERIFLEX. Reasonably good agreement can be obtained between our computed and available experimental rate coefficients. The manuscript of this work is in preparation. Revised objective 4 is largely achieved. Relating to peroxy radicals, ROO, and of atmospheric importance, spectroscopies of some simple Criegee intermediates, namely, CH2OO and CH3CHOO, and some of their reactions of atmospheric importance, were studied by state-of-the-art ab initio calculations. Three papers were published in journals of very high impact factors (Science and Chemistry-a European Journal), which acknowledge the present grant. In addition, related computational studies on methodology development (revised objectives 2 and 3) were carried out on the decomposition of hexafluoropropylene oxide, Cl + HCOOH and Cl + CH3COOCH3 reactions. These reactions are also of atmospheric importance. Lastly, high-level ab initio calculations on AlH2 and its anion, as well as Franck-Condon factor calculations, which include anharmonicity and Duschinsky rotation, were performed to simulate the photodetachment spectrum of AlH2−, with the aim of assigning the recently reported experimental spectrum [X. Zhang, et al., J. Chem. Phys. 138, 124303 (2013)]. Summarizing, for the present grant, eight papers have been published and one manuscript is in preparation.

501911.label: Major findings and research outcome
501911.value: For the CH3O2 + BrO reaction, kinetics measurements, product branching ratio measurements, and electronic structure calculations conclude H2COO + HOBr as the main product channel, which were neglected previously, because a previous computational study could not locate the transition state for this channel, and also the product, HOBr, had not been monitored in previous kinetics studies. Nevertheless, our higher level electronic structure calculations have located the transition state for this channel. With direct monitoring of the temporal profiles of the reactant, BrO, and the product, HOBr, by CIMS in this study, the measured temperature dependent reaction rate in Arrhenius form, k = (2.42−0.72+1.02) × 10−14 exp[(1617 ± 94)/T] cm3 molecule−1s−1 (243K ≤ T ≤ 296 K), is reported. Including this new kinetic data in modelling demonstrates the importance of H2COO, in giving rise to enhanced OH concentration up to 20% in the upper troposphere and lower stratosphere. For the HO2 + BrO reaction, five product channels to HOBr + 1O2, HOBr + 3O2, HBr + O3, OH + OBrO and OH + BrOO were investigated at higher levels of theory than previously. Similar to 1 above, the HOBr + 1O2 channel was found to be the major channel, contrary to a previous computational study, which could not locate the transition state of this channel. Rate coefficients were computed for the first time employing both VTST and the two transition state approach, and found to agree very well with available experimental values. Criegee intermediates (CIs): (a) CH2OO: The absorption, photoelectron and hexapole transmission spectra of CH2OO were computed and simulated for the first time. Our simulated absorption spectra of CH2OO and CH2XOO, X=Cl, Br and I, suggest that the absorption spectrum previously assigned to CH2IOO was wrong. It should be largely due to CH2OO. (b) CH3CHOO: The photoionization mass spectra (PIMS) of syn- and anti-CH3CHOO were detected for the first time and assigned by our spectral simulation. Conformer dependent kinetics studies of CH3CHOO with SO2, NO2 and water were carried out for the first time. Although CIs have long been implicated in tropospheric oxidation, they have only been detected in the laboratory recently. With the present grant, we have contributed much to the spectroscopies and kinetics of two lightest CIs, CH2COO and CH3CHOO. Overall, 8 papers were published and the work on CH3CHOO was published on in the high impact factor journal, Science.

501911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
501911.value: In the development of a reliable computational methodology for the calculation of rate coefficients in an ab initio manner, three reactions of atmospheric importance were investigated, contributing considerably to the understanding of the difficulties involved. The computational strategy established certainly lead to more applications of state-of-the-art ab initio methods to study reaction rates. More studies will be conducted related to the Criegee intermediates (CI) as the chemistry of them has huge impacts on the oxidation capacity of the atmosphere.

501911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
501911.value: Our investigations on the reactions of BrO with CH3O2 and HO2 have revised previously believed major reaction channels and mechanisms. Our finding of CH2OO, a Criegee intermediate (CI), being a major product from the BrO + CH3O2 reaction has important implications in atmospheric modelling, especially to the previous underestimation of OH concentration in the upper troposphere. The revisions of the major product channels to HOBr for these two reactions also have important implications to modelling ozone depletion in the polar and marine regions. Our computational and experimental studies on the spectroscopies and/or kinetics of the two CIs, CH2OO and CH3CHOO, have contributed considerably to their spectroscopic identifications, the understanding of their electronic structures and kinetics of their reactions in the atmosphere. New kinetic data obtained will revise and improve the reliability of the modelling of the atmosphere, which will allow a more accurate account for oxidation reactions of volatile organic compounds in the troposphere and marine environments, and for determining the lifetimes of key greenhouse gases and pollutants, and the formation of aerosols. Our extensive computational investigations on various reactions of atmospheric importance have contributed considerably to the development of an ab initio methodology in calculating rate coefficients reliably.

501911.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
501911.value: In the present project, in addition to our UK Co-Investigators of Manchester (Prof. Carl Percival) and Southampton (Prof. John Dyke), we have collaborated with two highly reputed research groups in atmospheric chemistry, namely, Prof. Dudley Showcross (Bristol University, UK; specialized in atmospheric modelling) and Dr. Craig A. Taatjes (Sandia National Laboratories, USA; specialized in photoionization mass spectrometry using synchrotron radiation in detecting unstable species). Collaborations with the American group allow us to have access to spectroscopic data (PIMS) on Criegee intermediates and kinetic data on their reactions, while collaborations with the Bristol group enable us to apply our kinetic data to atmospheric modelling. In this connection, the full potentials of the computational results obtained in Hong Kong can be exploited to experimental spectroscopic and kinetic applications and atmospheric modelling. These collaborations have resulted in a number of very important publications in atmospheric chemistry. Among them, the most outstanding one was published in Science (the work on CH3CHOO was published on 12/4/2013 in Science with 79 citations on 9/12/2015; see Section C). Also, though our collaborations with Dr. Taatjes, we further collaborated with Dr. W.G. Roeterdink of Institute of atomic and molecular Physics, Jilin University, Jilin, China, who invited us to join him to simulate the hexapole focusing spectra of CH2OO, resulting in a further publication on CH2OO (see Section C).

502111.value: Numerical multi-linear algebra is a new branch of computational mathematics, with wide applications in engineering, physics, mechanics, computer sciences, data analysis and mining, signal and imagining processing, etc. In 2005, independently, the PI of this project, Qi, and Lim, introduced the concepts of eigenvalues for higher order tensors. The concepts of eigenvalues of higher order tensors found applications in and/or links with automatical control, medical resonance imaging, solid mechanics, higher order Markov chains, spectral hypergraph theory and Finsler geometry, etc. However, the computation of the eigenvalues of a higher order tensor is in general NP-hard. This poses a difficulty to develop the theory and algorithms of numerical multi-linear algebra or tensor computation. Recently, linear convergence was established for algorithms for finding the largest eigenvalue of an essentially positive or weakly positive tensor. It was also seen that eigenvalues of nonnegative tensors have a close link with eigenvalues of homogeneous monotone maps. These opened a new and rich area of numerical multi-linear algebra: nonnegative tensors. It is expected a comprehensive theory and efficient algorithms for nonnegative tensors will be developed, parallel to the theory and algorithms of nonnegative matrices. In this project, we plan to develop a comprehensive theory and efficient algorithms for eigenvalues and eigenvectors of nonnegative tensors. We will absorb the theoretical results of eigenvalues and eigenvectors of homogeneous monotone maps and nonnegative matrices. We plan to investigate properties of various subclasses of nonnegative or related tensors, including essentially positive tensors, primitive tensors, essentially nonnegative tensors, M-tensors, stochastic tensors, doubly stochastic tensors, positive semi-definite nonnegative tensors, etc, to develop efficient algorithms for finding the largest/the smallest eigenvalue and Z-eigenvalue of a nonnegative tensor, and to discuss the relations of eigenvalues of nonnegative tensors with nonnegative approximiation of nonnegative tensors, and nonnegative tensor factorization. Nonnegative tensors have wide applications in statistics, computer sciences, high-order Markov chains, hypergraph theory and many other areas. Yet there are very limited theory and algorithms in the literature for nonnegative tensors. The success of this project will build a new fertile branch of applied and computational mathematics -- nonnegative tensors, and makes significant impact to the related application areas. We also expect to construct efficient algorithms for the eigenvalue problem of nonnegative tensors. The success of this project will be significant in both mathematical theory and applications. 数值多重线性代数是计算数学的一个新分支，在工程、物理、力学、计算机科学、数据分析与挖掘、信号与图像处理等很多领域都有广泛的应用。本项目的负责人祁力群于2005年和林力行分别独立地提出了高阶张量特征值的概念。之后，人们发现高阶张量特征值的概念在自动控制，医疗磁共振成像，刚体力学，高阶马尔科夫链，超图理论和Finsler几何等很多领域有直接的应用或紧密的联系。但是，高阶张量特征值的计算通常是一个NP难的问题。这对发展数值多重线性代数或张量计算构成了困难。 最近，对于求解基本正或弱正张量最大特征值问题的算法，其线性收敛性得到了证明。另外，非负张量特征值和齐次单调算子特征值之间具有紧密的联系。这些都为数值多重线性代数打开了一个全新的研究领域：非负张量。与非负矩阵的算法和理论相平行，关于非负张量的有效算法和广泛理论有望发展起来。 本项目我们计划发展有关非负张量特征值和特征向量问题的综合理论和有效算法。我们将吸取有关齐次单调算子和非负矩阵特征值和特征向量的理论结果，计划探讨各种非负张量的不同性质，包括基本正张量、素张量、基本非负张量、M-张量、随机张量、双重随机张量、正半定非负张量等等，探讨求解这些张量最大特征值或最小特征值或Z-特征值的有效算法，讨论非负张量特征值和非负张量非负近似以及非负张量分解之间的关系。 非负张量在统计、计算机科学、高阶马尔科夫链，超图理论等很多领域具有广泛的应用。但是目前有关这方面的理论和算法的研究还非常有限。本项目的成功开展将为应用与计算数学开辟一个新的分支----非负张量，对其它相关应用领域也将具有重要的影响。我们也期待对非负张量特征值问题构造有效的算法。本项目的成功对数学理论和应用都具有重要的意义。

502111.label: Realisation of objectives
502111.value: 1. We established a theory for symmetric nonnegative tensors. We proved a maximum property for the largest H-eigenvalue of a symmetric nonnegative tensor, and establish some bounds for this eigenvalue via row sums of that tensor. We showed that if an eigenvalue of a symmetric nonnegative tensor has a positive H-eigenvector, then this eigenvalue is the largest H-eigenvalue ofthat tensor. We also gave a necessary and sufficient condition for this. We introduced copositive tensors. This concept extends the concept of copositive matrices. Symmetric nonnegative tensors and positive semi-definite tensors are examples of copositive tensors. The diagonal elements of a copositive tensor must be nonnegative. We showed that if each sum of a diagonal element and all the negative off-diagonal elements in the same row of a real symmetric tensor is nonnegative, then that tensor is a copositive tensor. We applied the spectral theory of nonnegative tensors to the study of the geometric measure of entanglement for pure states. For symmetric pure multipartite qubit or qutrit states an elimination method was given. For symmetric pure multipartite qudit states, a numerical algorithm with randomization was presented. We also showed that a nonsymmetric pure state can be augmented to a symmetric one whose amplitudes can be encoded in a nonnegative symmetric tensor, so the geometric measure of entanglement can be calculated. Several examples, such as mGHZ states, W states, inverted W states, qudits, and nonsymmetric states, are used to demonstrate the power of the proposed methods. Given a pure state, one can always find a change of basis (a unitary transformation) so that all the probability amplitudes of the pure state are non-negative under the new basis. Therefore, our methods proposed here can be applied to a very wide class of multipartite pure states. We introduced M-tensors. This concept extends the concept of M-matrices. We denoted Z-tensors as the tensors with non-positive off-diagonal entries. We showed that M-tensors must be Z-tensors and the maximal diagonal entry must be nonnegative. The diagonal elements of a symmetric M-tensor must be nonnegative. A symmetric M-tensor is copositive. Based on the spectral theory of nonnegative tensors, we showed that the minimal value of the real parts of all eigenvalues of an M-tensor is its smallest H+-eigenvalue and also is its smallest H-eigenvalue. We showed that a Z-tensor is an M-tensor if and only if all its H+-eigenvalues are nonnegative. We also introduced strong M-tensors, and some corresponding conclusions were given. In particular, we showed that all H-eigenvalues of strong M-tensors are positive. We also investigated some other properties of M-tensors and strong M-tensors. 2. We considered the problem of computing the largest eigenvalue for nonnegative tensors. We established the Q-linear convergence of a power type algorithm for this problem under a weak irreducibility condition. Moreover, we presented a convergent algorithm for calculating the largest eigenvalue for any nonnegative tensors. We established global R-linear convergence of a power method for finding the spectral radius of a nonnegative tensor under the condition of weak irreducibility. We showed that for a nonnegative tensor T, there always exists a partition of the index set such that every tensor induced by the partition is weakly irreducible; and the spectral radius of T can be obtained from those spectral radii of the induced tensors. In this way, we developed a convergent algorithm for finding the spectral radius of a general nonnegative tensor without any additional assumption. For a general nonnegative tensor, we used a series of decreasing positive perturbations of the original tensor and repeatedly recall power-type method for finding the largest eigenvalue of a positive tensor with an inexact strategy. We proved the convergence of the method for the general nonnegative tensor. Under a certain assumption, the computing complexity of the method was established. Motivated by the interior-point method for convex optimization, we put forward a one-step inner iteration power-type method, whose convergence was also established under certain assumptions. We considered a new class of tensors called essentially nonnegative tensors, which extends the concept of nonnegative tensors, and examine the maximum eigenvalue of an essentially nonnegative tensor using the polynomial optimization techniques. We established that finding the maximum eigenvalue of an essentially nonnegative symmetric tensor is equivalent to solving a sum of squares of polynomials (SOS) optimization problem, which, in its turn, can be equivalently rewritten as a semi-definite programming problem. We proposed a quadratically convergent algorithm for finding the largest eigenvalue of a nonnegative homogeneous polynomial map where the Newton method is used to solve an equivalent system of nonlinear equations. The semi-symmetric tensor was introduced to reveal the relation between homogeneous polynomial map and its associated semi-symmetric tensor. Based on this relation a globally and quadratically convergent algorithm was established where the line search was inserted. 3. We introduced a new class of nonnegative tensors—strictly nonnegative tensors. A weakly irreducible nonnegative tensor is a strictly nonnegative tensor but not vice versa. We showed that the spectral radius of a strictly nonnegative tensor is always positive. We gave some necessary and sufficient conditions for the six well conditional classes of nonnegative tensors, introduced in the literature, and a full relationship picture about strictly nonnegative tensors with these six classes of nonnegative tensors. We introduced Laplacian tensors and signless Laplacian tensors for uniform hypergraphs. Laplacian tensors are M-tensors while signless Laplacian tensors are nonnegative tensors. We investigated their properties. We showed that the smallest H-eigenvalue of a Laplacian tensor is zero. We introduced odd-bipartite hypergraphs and identified a number of odd-bipartite hypergraphs such as cored hypergraphs, power hypergraphs, sunflowers, squids, loose paths and loose cycles. We showed that the largest H-eigenvalue of the Laplacian tensor of a uniform hypergraph is always less than or equal to the largest H-eigenvalue of the signless Laplacian tensor of that hypergraph. We showed that if the hypergraph is connected, then equality holds here if and only if the hypergraph is even-uniform and odd bipartite. This extended a classical result in spectral graph theory. We also applied these to bound the clique and coclique numbers of uniform hypergraphs. 4. Nonnegative tensor factorization has applications in statistics, computer vision, exploratory multiway data analysis, and blind source separation. A symmetric nonnegative tensor, which has an exact symmetric nonnegative factorization, is called a completely positive tensor. This concept extends the concept of completely positive matrices. A classical result in the theory of completely positive matrices is that a symmetric, diagonally dominated nonnegative matrix is a completely positive matrix. We introduced strongly symmetric tensors and showed that a symmetric tensor has a symmetric binary decomposition if and only if it is strongly symmetric. Then we showed that a strongly symmetric, hierarchically dominated nonnegative tensor is a completely positive tensor, and present a hierarchical elimination algorithm for checking this. Numerical examples are given to illustrate this. Some other properties of completely positive tensors are discussed. In particular, we showed that the completely positive tensor cone and the co-positive tensor cone of the same order are dual to each other.

502111.label: Major findings and research outcome
502111.value: In [1], we established a theory for symmetric nonnegative tensors. We proved a maximum property for the largest H-eigenvalue of a symmetric nonnegative tensor, and establish some bounds for this eigenvalue via row sums of that tensor. We showed that if an eigenvalue of a symmetric nonnegative tensor has a positive H-eigenvector, then this eigenvalue is the largest H-eigenvalue of that tensor. In [20], we applied the spectral theory of nonnegative tensors to the study of the geometric measure of entanglement for pure states. For symmetric pure multipartite qubit or qutrit states an elimination method was given. For symmetric pure multipartite qudit states, a numerical algorithm with randomization was presented. We also showed that a nonsymmetric pure state can be augmented to a symmetric one whose amplitudes can be encoded in a nonnegative symmetric tensor, so the geometric measure of entanglement can be calculated. In [8, 13], based upon the nonnegative tensor theory, we introduced M-tensors and strong M-tensors, and investigated their properties. In [14], we applied the nonnegative tensor theory to study convergence of second-order Markov chains. In [11], we introduced Laplacian tensors and signless Laplacian tensors for uniform hypergraphs. In [10], we introduced odd-bipartite hypergraphs. In [9, 12], we showed that a number of uniform hypergraphs are odd-bipartite. In [16], we showed that the largest H-eigenvalue of the Laplacian tensor of a uniform hypergraph is always less than or equal to the largest H-eigenvalue of the signless Laplacian tensor of that hypergraph. We showed that if the hypergraph is connected, then equality holds here if and only if the hypergraph is even-uniform and odd bipartite. This extended a classical result in spectral graph theory. In [19], we applied these to bound the clique and coclique numbers of uniform hypergraphs. In [3, 4, 6, 7, 17], we developed various algorithms for finding the largest eigenvalue of a nonnegative tensor, established their convergence theories and links with the main-stream algorithm in optimization such as semi-positive definite programming methods. In [4], we studied various subclasses of nonnegative tensors and established their relationships. In [1], we introduced copositive tensors. In [15], we introduced completely positive tensors, which are closely linked with nonnegative tensor decomposition. We showed that the cones of completely positive tensors and copositive tensors of the same order are dual to each other. We also showed that a strongly symmetric, hierarchically dominated nonnegative tensor is completely positive.

502411.label: Project Objectives
502411.value: Develop new separability criteria, mathematical results and techniques in quantum entanglement One important and typical question asked by experimentalists in quantum information science is how to ensure that an entangled state was indeed produced in their experiment. The problem of detecting entangled states as well as detecting separable states is still an open problem in quantum mechanics, which is called the separability problem. Separability problem can be viewed as a mathematical characterization of entangled quantum states in tensor product Hilbert spaces. In this project, the investigators will study problems related to quantum entanglement, especially the separability problem. With their experience in matrix and operator theory, the investigators will explore new separability criteria as well as improve and generalize some of those existing separability criteria. The investigators will collaborate with experimentalists and practitioners so that the research team will focus on important and useful problems. The long term goal is to provide simple, practical, and computational tools to experimentalists and develop new mathematical techniques with wide applicability in quantum entanglement. Details of research problems will be mentioned in research plan and methodology. Promote the separability problem and other problems relating entanglement to matrix and operator algebras community In the last decade, various separability criteria have been introduced by researchers and most of these criteria were formulated, proved, and verified in a matrix and operator approach. Matrix and operator theory definitely plays an important role in the development of separability problem. Exclusively, separability problem can also be viewed as a pure mathematical problem in multilinear algebra. It is also connected to the characterization of structure of positive map in Hilbert space, which is an important mathematical topics studied in operator theory. However, it was observed that most experts from matrix and operator algebras community were not aware of the importance of this problem in quantum information science. This situation may due to the lack of communication and the different notations and descriptions used between the two communities. Quantum information science is a highly inter-disciplinary research area, it is important for researchers from different areas to work together. Another long term goal of our project is to build up a network between mathematicians, especially matrix and operator algebraists, and quantum information scientists so that more mathematicians can be involved in the development of theoretical aspect of quantum entanglement. Also, the investigators will involve junior researchers and students in the project so as to build up the workforce in quantum information science.

502411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
502411.value: Quantum information science is a rapidly growing research area. It concerns information theory that depends on the quantum effects in quantum mechanics. One of the most well known processes involving quantum information is quantum computation. The quantum computing device (quantum computer) will store and handle data in quantum bits (qubits) and run quantum algorithms, which can solve problems much more efficiently than the digital computers (using binary bits). Entanglement is an essential feature of quantum theory that renders its crucial difference from classical information theory. Entanglement was formulated by Einstein, Podolsky, and Rosen in their famous Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen paradox, originally criticizing the completeness of quantum theory, while unexpectedly, quantum entanglement became a fundamental resource in quantum theory. In the last two decades, researchers have put a huge effort trying to better understand the properties of entanglement, which has many applications in quantum information science such as super dense coding, quantum teleportation, and quantum computation. Mathematically, entanglement is a complex property of quantum states defined on tensor product Hilbert spaces. Since Hilbert space theory is the theoretical basis, many problems in entanglement theory are connected to matrix and operator theory. In this project, we will focus on the mathematical aspect of quantum entanglement and study mathematical problems central to the development. One fundamental question in entanglement theory is to determine whether a state produced, for instant in an experiment, is entangled. This is called the separability problem. Various separability criteria have been proposed in the literature. However, there is still no any complete and operational separability criterion yet. The investigators will address this problem by explore new separability criteria as well as improve and generalize some of those existing separability criteria. Computer algorithms will be developed to test conjectures on the topic and provide tools for detecting and constructing new classes of entangled states. Further, the investigators will collaborate with experimentalists and practitioners so that the research team will focus on important and useful problems in the area. This project will lead to important new results, novel proof techniques, computer software, and solutions of open problems, in quantum entanglement. The findings will be communicated to non-mathematical researchers in the quantum information science community. Additionally, we will formulate the mathematical problems in quantum entanglement and bring in other mathematicians to study the problems. We also plan to work with young researchers and students so as to build up the workforce for quantum information science. 量子信息科學為現今一個迅速發展的科學研究課題。此學科以量子力學為基礎發展信息理論，其應用有量子計算。量子計算（量子電腦）以量子位元為單位，存儲、處理及運算數據，與現時電腦科技（使用二進制位）相比，量子電腦能更有效地解決複雜問題。量子糾纏為量子理論中一非常重要的特性 。量子糾纏最初由愛因斯坦（Einstein），波多斯基（Podolsky）與羅森（Rosen）於其著名EPR悖論中提出，以質疑量子力學完備性。但最終反成為量子理論一主要基石。在過去二十年，科學家投入了巨大的資源，試圖更好地理解量子糾纏。研究過程中亦發現量子糾纏能應用於不同領域，如超密集編碼，量子傳輸和量子計算。 數學上，量子糾纏是一個量子態在張量積希爾伯特空間的一個複雜特性。因此，許多量子糾纏理論問題都需運用矩陣和算子理論。在這個研究項目，我們將集中研究量子糾纏這領域上一些重要數學問題。在糾纏理論中，一個基本的問題為如何確定一個量子態是否糾纏。這稱為可分性問題。已經有各種不同可分性的準則在文獻中提出，但當中仍然未有一個為全面及運算中可行的。我們將針對這個問題，探索新的可分性準則及改進一些現有的可分性判據。我們將編寫電腦程式以提供參考數據，亦有助檢測和建構新的糾纏量子態。此外，研究人員亦將與實驗者和從業人員合作，使研究團隊將專注於重要和有益的問題。 此研究項目冀望能取得新的研究成果、新的證明技術及電腦軟件以解決量子糾纏理論中未解的問題。研究結果將以最有效的方式分享予領域中其他範疇的研究人員。此外，希望藉此研究項目，吸引更多優秀數學工作者參與研究量子糾纏的課題。我們還計劃引入青年學者和學生參與研究，從而培養更多量子計算的研究人員。

502411.label: Realisation of objectives
502411.value: The first objective of this project is to develop new separability criteria, mathematical results and techniques in quantum entanglement. In this project, the PI and Co-I achieved this goal and obtained many mathematical results in quantum entanglement, including results in linear preserver problems [Papers 1, 2 ,3 and 5] and new criterion on k-positivity of linear maps [Paper 4]. These results have been published in international peer-viewed journals and have been cited by other researchers in mathematics and physics communities. These results have also been presented in various meetings, workshops and conferences (see Part C). The second objective of this project is to promote the separability problem and other problems relating entanglement to matrix and operator algebras community. The PI and Co-I have achieved this goal through organizing workshops in Hong Kong (December 2012 & January 2014), attending international conferences and workshops (see Part C), and visit other institutions. During the project period, a workshop on quantum information science was held and more than twenty scholars from Canada, China, Japan, and USA joined the event and shared their works. In particular, the investigators have built up a strong collaboration with Professor Jinchuan Hou of Taiyuen University of Technology and Professor Xiaofei Qi of Shanxi University. They shared a common interest in the topic of criterion on k-positivity of linear maps, which has a strong connection to the separability of quantum states. Their collaborative work has been published in [Paper 4]. For training young researchers, a postdoctoral fellow, Dr. Zejun Huang, was recruited in this project. Huang has contributed in various parts of this project and is one of the co-authors of two published papers [Papers 6 and 7] in this project.

502411.label: Major findings and research outcome
502411.value: In this project, the investigators obtained a sequence of results in the area of linear preserver problems in related to quantum information. In particular, they characterized linear maps that preserve tensor product of unitary obits and numerical range [Paper 5], which extended the work of Friedland et al. on the automorphism group of separable states [S. Friedland, C.K. Li, Y.T. Poon, and N.S. Sze, The automorphism group of separable states in quantum information theory, J. Math. Phys., 52:042203, 2011]. The investigators also determined linear maps that preserve Ky Fan norms and Schatten norms [Paper 2], numerical radius [Paper 3], and higher numerical ranges [Paper 1] of tensor products. The investigators also studied the problem of k-positive maps. A new criterion on k-positivity in terms of the k-numerical range was obtained and it is used to improve some earlier results on k-positive maps related to quantum entanglement [Paper 4]. A special class of positive maps extending the construction of Choi on positive maps that are not completely positive was also introduced in the same paper. The investigators also studied other related mathematical problem. In [Paper 6], the PI studied graphs that associated with matrices over finite fields and the corresponding independence number, chromatic number and clique number. These results were used to characterize the endomorphism of the graph, which extended Hua’s fundamental theorem of geometry on matrices over finite fields [L.K. Hua, A theorem on matrices over a sfield and its applications, Acta Math. Sinica 1:109–163, 1951]. Finally, the problem of factoring a permutation as a product of special types of transpositions, namely, those transpositions involving two positions with bounded distances, is considered in [Paper 7]. In particular, the minimum number m such that every permutation can be factored into no more than m special transpositions is investigated.

502411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
502411.value: With the successful collaboration built during this project, the investigators will continue to work with the collaborators in various research areas in quantum information and quantum entanglement. The investigators will continue to explore new criterion on k-positiveity and separability as well as improve and generalize some of those existing criteria. On the other hand, based on the result obtained in this project, the investigators will also explore other linear preserver problems that are related to the study of quantum entanglement in the future.

502411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
502411.value: Entanglement is an essential feature of quantum theory that renders its crucial difference from classical information theory. In this project, the investigators obtained a sequence of results in the area of linear preserver problems in related to quantum information and also the topic of k-positivity criterion of maps in connection to separability criterion. These results provided a useful mathematical results for the study of quantum entanglement. The investigators have also obtained other mathematical results in graph and combinatorial theory. In short, the project has lead to important new results, novel proof techniques, and solutions of open problems, in quantum information.

502711.label: Project Title(Chinese)
502711.value: 生化趋向性模型行波解及其应用

502711.label: Project Objectives
502711.value: To develop new approaches to systematically study the traveling wave problem of the chemotaixs models with diffusing chemicals. By exploring a number of open questions, many new results will be obtained and a number of new questions will arise along the studies, which may open up a new direction for the future research. To investigate how the chemical diffusion affect the dynamics of traveling waves. In particular, the diffusion limits of wave speeds and traveling wave solutions will be investigated in detail for the first time. Hence, we are able to examine what would happen to the traveling wave solutions if the chemical diffusion tends to zero and elucidate the debate in the literature whether or not the chemical diffusion is negligible. To present the parameter analysis to examine the impact of model parameters on the wave traits and hence to test and validate the mathematical models. To perform the numerical experiment by which we interpret the experimental observations and enlighten the future research. The numerical experiments will not only confirm our new analytical results but also give new insight of interpreting the mechanisms driving the traveling wave pattern formations. To lay the groundwork for the future studies in more challenging topics such as the multi-dimensional traveling wave problem and local or global stability of traveling wave solutions. Also we hope our study may stimulate the emergence of more general methods to handle the remaining questions that are not solved by our approaches. To widely publicize our new approaches and results and foster collaborations by publishing our results in high quality journals. Through our publications and possible new collaborations, we shall seek more applications of our new approaches and results.

502711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
502711.value: Chemotaxis, the directed migration of cells along the external chemical concentration gradient, is a leading mechanism to account for the morphogenesis and self-organization of many biological coherent structures and propagating waveforms. The study of mathematical modeling and analysis of chemotaxis is one of the most prevailing topics in modern mathematical biology. The motivation of the first mathematical model describing chemotaxis, proposed by Keller and Segel in 1971, was to interpret the traveling bands (waves) of bacteria chemotactic movement observed in the pioneering experiment by Adler. In order to simplify the mathematical analysis, most of the existing analytical studies by now concerning the traveling waves of chemotaxis made a strong assumption that the chemical is non-diffusible, which means the chemical only possesses temporal dynamics. This is only true in a special process of so-called haptotaxis. In most chemotactic processes, the chemical is a signaling molecule which is intrinsically diffusible in the environment. Hence the Keller-Segel type models with diffusing chemical, which are referred to as the full chemotaxis models for convenience, have much wider applications and are more applicable to the real world. The profound challenge faced by the study of the full chemotaxis models is the high dimensionality of the traveling wave system which consists of four nonlinear ordinary differential equations and cannot be directly analyzed based on the theory of ordinary differential equations. Due to this difficulty, the existing results of traveling waves to the full chemotaxis model are very limited. A great deal of questions for the full chemotaxis models still remain open and are highly demanded to be explored. It is the purpose of this project to develop a series of technical variable transformations that reduce the traveling wave system of the full chemotaxis models to a tractable low-dimensional nonlinear system so that the existing mathematical theories can be applied. The chemotaixs models are numerous depending on the specific biological processes. In this project, we consider an integrated Keller-Segel type model which includes the chemical diffusion and describes three distinct biological processes: bacteria chemotactic movement, initiation of angiogenesis and reinforced random walks by assigning appropriate values to the model parameters. We establish the existence and non-existence of traveling wave solutions under different parameter spaces, examine the zero diffusion limits of traveling wave solutions, and perform numerical simulation to confirm our analytical results and to interpret the relevant biological processes. 生化趋向性描述的是细胞沿着化学物质浓度梯度方向的运动。 它是解释生物中的形态形成以及很多拟序结构和传播波形的主要机制。生化趋向性的数学建模以及分析是现代生物数学中最流行的主题之一。第一个生化趋向性的数学模型是Keller和Segel在1971年提出来的， 用来解释有名的Adler实验中发现的细菌的传播波带。 为了简化数学分析， 大多数现存的关于生化趋向性模型的行波解数学研究做了一个很强的假设：化学物质是不扩散的。 这个假设只对一个很特殊的生物过程是对的， 就是趋触性。在多数的生化趋向性过程中，化学物质是一个信号分子，它在本质上是运动扩散的。所以说带有扩散的化学物质的生化趋向性数学模型对现实世界有更广的应用， 这样的模型被称为完全的生化趋向性模型。 对完全的生化趋向性模型行波解的研究遇到的最大挑战来自于行波系统的高维度。这个系统有四个方程，现成的常微分方程理论不能直接去解。因为这个困难，目前得到的关于完全的生化趋向性模型行波解的结果很少，大量的有意思重要的问题亟待去解决。 目前的研究项目就是去发展一些巧妙的变量变换去降低行波系统的维度使得一些常微分方程能够被应用。根据具体的生物过程，生化趋向性模型有很多。目前的项目主要考虑一类经过整合后的模型。当参数取不同的数值时， 这个模型可以描述三个不同的生物过程：细菌的趋向性运动，血管再生和有倾向性的随机运动。这个项目将研究此模型的行波解的存在和非存在性，化学物质的扩散极限以及数值模拟，最后运用得到的理论和数值结果去解释相关的生物想象。我们的研究将是朝着完全的生化趋向性模型行波解的研究迈出的重要一步， 将会对生物现象解释提供新的见解，为将来进一步的研究打下基础。

502711.label: Major findings and research outcome
502711.value: The stability of traveling wave solutions of the well-known Keller-Segel chemotaxis model has been open for many years. In this project, the nonlinear stability of traveling wave solutions of a special case of the Keller-Segel model has been successfully established. The major novelty of our work is a Cole-Hoph type transformation which transforms the singular Keller-Segel model to a system of conservation laws without singularity, which enabled us to prove the stability of traveling waves via the energy estimates. Our results have been published in top journals like Journal of Differential Equations, Mathematical Models and Methods in Applied Sciences, Discrete and Continuous Dynamic Systems, and so on.

502711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
502711.value: The Cole-Hoph type transformation transforms the singular Keller-Segel model to a system of conservation laws without singularity. This allows us to study the transformed system in various aspects beyond the traveling wave solutions, for instance, the well-posedness problem, the pattern formation and large-time behavior of solutions.

502711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
502711.value: The project has established the nonlinear stability of traveling wave solutions of the well-known Keller-Segel chemotaxis model. This partially solved a long-standing open questions in the field of mathematical biology. The research results opened a new direction to study the singular chemotaxis model and will stimulate more interesting researches in this direction in the future. The ideas developed in the research will have a long impact to the research in the field.

502911.value: 圖與時空模型及其對環境之應用

502911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
502911.value: In Hong Kong and the Pearl River Delta problems for environment are closely related. It needs a holistic approach to cope with the environmental problems in this region. More and more people understand that the analysis and modeling of variables in the environment are extremely important to Hong Kong and China. For statistical models, causal relationships have to be analyzed and interpreted carefully, and constructing a good framework for such analysis is always a challenging job. To avoid confusion, we will focus on Granger causality in this research. Granger causality is a well established concept and tool in economics and linear system analysis, but much can be done on its extension to graphical and spatial-temporal models. The purpose of this project is to develop graphical time series models and spatial-temporal models, and apply them to environmental problems. Graphical time series models form an emerging field in research, with applications to biology, economics, environmetrics, medicine, etc. Causal/non-causal relationships between time series variables will be established via some existing graphical models, and the properties of these models will be studied. These properties in turn will be used to extend the time series models to their spatial-temporal counterparts. Spatial temporal statistical models studied in recently years focus on parametric models. A typical representative is the space-time autoregressive moving average model (STARIMA model). These models reflect the dependence between the N-dimensional time series consisted of univariate time series observed at N space locations. These models have the drawback, among others, of only applicable to time series of single variable. Our proposed model overcomes the drawbacks of STARIMA type model by using chain graph, graph selection and Bayesian method. We then use the proposed model to analyze the environmental data collected in Hong Kong and the Pearl River Delta, with a view to understanding the mechanisms generating these data. The data under our investigation are multivariate data. It is expected that the results will be useful to the policy makers of our region.

502911.label: Realisation of objectives
502911.value: All the objectives of project have been achieved. The project is to study and apply statistical and graphical techniques to the analysis of air pollution in Hong Kong and the Pearl River Delta. Graphical models, based on the approach of Dahlhaus and Eichler, have been extensively studied and developed, including the relevant computing programs based on MatLab and R. A paper "Modelling spatial time series by graphical models" was presented at 'The 24th Annual Conference of the International Envirommetrics Society', held in Guangzhou in 2014. A paper was published in the journal Computational Statistics and Data Analysis in 2013. A paper "Analysis of air quality time series of Hong Kong with graphical modeling" is disposed to publish in the journal of Environmetirics.

502911.label: Major findings and research outcome
502911.value: Air pollution has strong seasonal pattern and local characteristics. Different air polutants also have different seasonal and local behavior. Nitrogen dioxide (NO2), respirable air particulates (RSP) and sulphur dioxide (SO2) usually have high concentration in the winter months, and low concentration in the summer months. Ozone normally has low concentration in spring and summer, but high concentration in autumn and winter, espicially in autumn. These phenomena can be delineated by graphical and non-parametric statistical models. In this research we have studied and developed the graphical time series models of Dahlhaus and Eichler extensively. They were applied to time series data in the Pearl River Delta. They enable us to study the causal relationship between air pollution in the Pearl River Delta. We found that our present method needs a fairly large sample size, due to the need of non-parametric estimation of the spectral densities. In our future, we may research on regularized autoregressive models.

502911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
502911.value: The techniques employed in the project require fairly large sample size. More reserach can be considere on statitical techniques in this area with small sample size.

502911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
502911.value: This research shows clearly air pollution has strong seasonal pattern and local characteristics. The pollutants nitrogen dioxide (NO2), respirable air particulates (RSP), and sulphur dioxide (SO2) usually have high concentration in the winter months, and low concentration in summer months. Ozone (O3), on the other hand, has concentration in the autumn. Further, ozone has high concentation in rural area, whereas NO2, RSP and SO2 have high concentration in urban areas. Further, the same pollutants in different areas tend to affect each other, concentration of different pollutants in the same region are usually highly correlated, while different pollutants in different areas have rather complicated interaction patterns. These can be analyzed through graphcia and spatial statistical models.

503011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
503011.value: 細菌對抗生素產生抗藥性成為目前治療細菌感染的最大挑戰，並對人類健康做成嚴重的威脅。不斷增加的醫療成本和不斷降低的藥效，使抗藥性細菌感染變得越來越難醫治。因此，研發具有新的抗菌機理的抗生素變得更加重要。細胞分裂是細菌生長的重要過程，目前在臨床上尚沒有針對該靶點的抗生素。FtsZ蛋白在細菌中擔當著重要的角色，絕大部分品種的細菌都會利用FtsZ蛋白進行細胞分裂。由於FtsZ蛋白的氨基酸序列在不同品種的細菌之間的差異性不大，從而令到發展針對FtsZ蛋白的抑制劑變得可能。 在此次研究計畫中，新一代FtsZ蛋白抑制物的開發會從小分子化合物開始。利用電腦藥物輔助開發軟體─ICM，根據FtsZ蛋白的X-射線結晶結構從化合物資料庫中尋找可能的先導物，當中得分最高的先導物會對細菌進行實驗。從實驗所得的資料會用作微調FtsZ蛋白的X-射線結晶結構，從而令到電腦更有效率地尋找針對FtsZ蛋白的先導物。電腦會估計先導物如何與FtsZ蛋白互相結合，透過改變先導物的官能原子團,先導物能夠被優化,進一步加強先導物與FtsZ蛋白之間的結合能力。新合成的先導物會對不同的細菌品種進行抗菌測試，除此之外，先導物如何影響到FtsZ蛋白的活性可以根據不同的活體外實驗得知。 當有明顯活性的先導物經過一連串對FtsZ蛋白以及抗菌的測試之後，先導物會被用作測試其對哺乳類細胞的毒性，並且尋找相關毒性與先導物化學結構之間的關係。 最後，先導物與傳統抗生素會同時用作對付擁有抗藥性的細菌，以測試先導物與抗生素之間的協同作用。

503011.label: Realisation of objectives
503011.value: A number of FtsZ inhibitors including pyrimidine-quinuclidine, berberine and 3-aminobenzamide derivatives were identified from structure-based virtual screening of natural prodcut libraries, followed by chemical modification of structure and bioassays. Potent FtsZ inhibitors with low IC50 and antibacterial activity against various bacterial strains including methicillin resistant S. aureus were found. The antibacterial properties of these compounds and their synergistic activity with β-lactam antibiotics were studied. These new FtsZ inhibitors were found to possess improved potency against the GTPase activity and polymerization of FtsZ. The compounds perturbed the formation of cytokinetic Z-ring in the bacteria and interfered with in vitro polymerization of FtsZ. The cytotoxicity of these compounds towards different mammalian cell lines were also tested. Thus all objectives have been realized.

503011.label: Major findings and research outcome
503011.value: A new class of FtsZ inhibitors bearing the pyrimidine-quinuclidine scaffold was identified from structure-based virtual screening of natural product libraries. Iterative rounds of in silico studies and biological evaluation established the structure-activity relationships of the new compounds. Potent FtsZ inhibitors with low micromolar IC50 and antibacterial activity against S. aureus and E. coli were found (see part C, section 8, research output no. 1). We then further investigated the antibacterial properties of one of the most potent compounds (quinuclidine 1) and its synergistic activity with β-lactam antibiotics. Susceptibility results showed that quinuclidine 1 was active against multiple antibiotic-resistant bacterial strains including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium with minimal inhibitory concentrations of 24 μg ml−1. When quinuclidine 1 was combined with β-lactam antibiotics, synergistic antimicrobial activities against antibiotic-resistant strains of Staphylococcus aureus were found. Further in vitro studies suggest that prevention of FtsZ protofilament formation by quinuclidine 1 impairs the formation of Z-ring, and thus inhibits bacterial division (see part C, section 8, research output no. 3). Berberine, a benzylisoquinoline alkaloid widely used in traditional Chinese and native American medicines for its antimicrobial properties, has been recently reported to inhibit FtsZ. Using a combination of in silico structure-based design and in vitro biological assays, 9-phenoxyalkyl berberine derivatives were identified as potent FtsZ inhibitors. Compared to the parent compound berberine, the derivatives showed a significant enhancement of antibacterial activity against clinically relevant bacteria, and an improved potency against the GTPase activity and polymerization of FtsZ. The most potent compound 2 strongly inhibited the proliferation of Gram-positive bacteria, including methicillin-resistant S. aureus and vancomycin-resistant E. faecium, with MIC values between 2 and 4 μg/mL, and was active against the Gram-negative E. coli and K. pneumoniae, with MIC values of 32 and 64 μg/mL respectively. The compound perturbed the formation of cytokinetic Z-ring in E. coli. Also, the compound interfered with in vitro polymerization of S. aureus FtsZ. Taken together, the chemical modification of berberine with 9-phenoxyalkyl substituent groups greatly improved the antibacterial activity via targeting FtsZ (see part C, section 8, research output no. 2).

503011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
503011.value: The synergistic effect of FtsZ inhibitors with beta-lactam antibiotics deserves further study because this may open a new approach for development of antibiotics against drug resistant bacteria. The synergistic effect implies that by using FtsZ inhibitors together with beta-lactam antibiotics, bacterial strains which are resistant to beta-lactam antibiotics may become susceptible to beta-lactam again. Areas that are worthy for further investigation and development include (1) whether the synergistic effect can apply to a wide spectrum of different drug resistant bacterial strains, and (2) the molecular mechanism of the synergistic effect.

503011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
503011.value: The emergence of antibiotic resistance bacteria is a threat to human health. The bacterial cell division protein FtsZ is considered an attractive drug target to treat antibiotic-resistant bacterial infections. A number of potential drug candidates that inhibit the enzymatic activity of FtsZ have been discovered in this project. We found that by combining these FtsZ inhibitors with conventional beta-lactam antibiotics, some antibiotic resistant bacteria such as methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus will become susceptible to beta-lactam antibiotics again. This means that the addition of FtsZ inhibitor can restore the beta-lactam susceptibility of certain antibiotic resistant bacteria and this will open up a new approach to treat bacterial infection.

503111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
503111.value: 金是一種廣受歡迎的貴金屬，在多個世紀以來已經被廣泛用作貨幣及珠寶。但是，相比其他過渡金屬，金催化在有機化學的發展依然處於最初階段。自二千年起，金催化在有機化學的研究引起極大的關注。最重要的是金催化具有催化活性高、反應條件溫和，對大部份功能團有兼容性及選擇性高，以及能在水中進行而不需要惰性氣體的保護。在金催化裏面可以經常發現新的反應性和眾多未知的有機轉化反應。金催化提供了獨特的方法可用於複雜分子的結構，而使用其他過渡金屬催化是很難達到的。 在本項目中，我們計劃開發金催化之高選擇性的有機合成和開展肽生物正交修飾的應用研究。酰胺功能團普遍存在於天然產物、 蛋白質和治療藥物，及在化學、 生物學與醫學中有重要作用。我們研究發現了金作為催化劑可催化醛和胺以合成酰胺。選擇性功能化不活潑的碳-氫鍵是在有機合成中的一大挑戰，能發揮對學術研究和製藥工業的深刻影響，因為結構多樣化的有機分子的合成可以在碳氫化合物上使用策略性建構其中的功能團。我們研究發展金(III)的環狀複合物能夠在水相中進行直接炔基化反應。生物正交化學是一門研究複雜生物體系的學科，它屬於化學和生物學之間跨學科研究中快速成長的領域。在金催化以及化學生物學方面的研究基礎上，我們計劃利用金催化對肽和蛋白質進行生物正交修飾。這個項目的研究成果對有機化學和化學生物學的領域有重大的影響。

503111.label: Realisation of objectives
503111.value: (1) We have developed an efficient gold-catalyzed amide synthesis from aldehydes and amines with high functional group tolerance in aqueous medium under mild reaction conditions. This method allows an easy access to amides from the reaction of aromatic, aliphatic and polyhydroxyl oligosaccharide based aldehydes with secondary amines. To demonstrate the generality of the present amide synthesis reaction, a diversity of aromatic and aliphatic aldehydes were coupled with various secondary amines to afford the corresponding amides in up to 99% isolated yield. Amide products with ketal and trimethylsilyl ether groups remaining intact were obtained in 53–62% isolated yields. Given the high functional group tolerance and mild aqueous reaction conditions of the present KAuCl4-catalyzed amide synthesis reaction, we were pleased to find that the reaction of unprotected D-raffinose aldehyde (10 mM in H2O) with amines (5 equiv.) in the presence of KAuCl4 (50 mol%) and K2CO3 (10 mol%) in H2O at 40 oC for 12 h gave amides with the hydroxyl groups remaining intact with up to 90% aldehyde conversion as shown by LC-MS analysis. Gold-catalyzed amide synthesis from aldehydes and amines in aqueous medium. Gai-Li Li, Karen Ka-Yan Kung and Man-Kin Wong. Chem. Commun., 2012, 48, 4112–4114. (2) We have developed a new approach for alkynylation of the arylpyridine unit of 6-membered ring cyclometalated gold(III) complexes with terminal alkynes under mild reaction conditions in aqueous medium. The cyclometalated gold(III) complexes generate di-alkynyl gold(III) intermediates via reaction with terminal alkynes in the presence of base. Then, the di-alkynyl gold(III) intermediates with a 6-membered ring gold metallocycle undergo selective C-C bond cross-coupling to afford arylacetylenes by reductive elimination. We have developed a synthesis of arylacetylenes by ligand-controlled alkynylation of 6-membered ring cyclometalated gold(III) complexes up to 76% isolated yield in aqueous medium under mild conditions. By 19F NMR studies of the dialkynyl gold(III) complex isolated in the reaction mixture, it was found to undergo reductive elimination to give arylacetylene as a cross coupling product selectively instead of alkyne homocoupling. This is the first example of showing cross coupling selectivity in di-alkynyl gold(III) complexes over homocoupling reactions reported in the literatures. In addition, we found that stable biscyclometallated gold(III) catalysts are able to exhibit high catalytic activity in organic synthesis through two novel strategies: (1) formation of coordinatively saturated distorted square planar gold(III) complexes using bulky C,N donor ligands and (2) gold silver dual catalysis for substrate activation. (3) We envision that the selective formation of arylacetylenes from cyclometalated gold(III) complexes and terminal alkynes under mild reaction conditions would be further developed into a new method for selective modification of alkyne functionalized peptides and proteins. By increasing the amount of gold(III) complex from 1 to 2 equiv., the conversion was increased to 22% after 10 h. The conversion could be increased to 99% by treatment with 5 or 10 equiv. of gold(III) complex. By changing the pH values of the PBS buffer (50 mM) from slightly acidic (pH 5.3) to basic (pH 9.0), the conversion could be improved from 73% to 99% by treatment of peptide with gold(III) complex (5 equiv.), which was consistent to the previous findings that basic reaction conditions could facilitate the alkynylation reaction. Cyclometalated gold(III) complexes linked with dansyl and BODIPY groups, respectively, were synthesized for fluorescent labelling of alkyne-functionalized lysozyme by alkynylation reaction, and the fluorescent labelling were observed by LC-MS and SDS-PAGE analysis. According to the results of SDS-PAGE analysis, Dansyl-modified lysozyme and BODIPY-modified lysozyme were observed using fluorescent analysis. Employing Coomassie blue staining on the same gel, deep blue colour signals of Dansyl- and BODIPY-modified proteins could be observed, which indicated fluorescent tags has been labelled on the proteins using the alkynylation approach. (4) We have developed modular assembly of cyclometalated gold(III) complexes by choosing appropriate bidentate C,N-donor ligands and ancillary ligands for chemoselective cysteine modification of peptides and proteins via C–S bond-forming reductive elimination. In this work, the use of cyclometalated gold(III) complexes [Au(C4N)msen] allows the chemoselective cysteine modification of peptides and proteins via ligand controlled C–S bond-forming reductive elimination. A cyclometalated gold(III) complex [Au(bpy)msen] (Hbpy = 2-benzylpyridine; msen = N,N0-bis(methanesulfonyl) ethylenediamine) was synthesized according to literature procedures. Treatment of a cysteine-containing peptide STSSSCNLSK with [Au(bpy)msen] in PBS (pH 7.4)/DMSO (9 : 1) at 25 oC for 2 h afforded gold–peptide adduct with 99% conversion, which was confirmed by LC-MS. In addition, gold–peptide adducts of other cysteine containing peptides could also be formed by the reaction with [Au(bpy)msen]. The excellent chemoselectivity of the present reaction was demonstrated by the exclusive cysteine modification of these cysteine-containing peptides in LC-MS/MS analysis. A time course experiment studying the formation of gold–peptide adduct from [Au(bpy)msen] and peptide at different pH values was performed at 25 oC. In 2 h, 99% conversion was achieved at pH 6.2–9.3. These results suggested that the formation of gold–peptide adducts could proceed smoothly in a wide range of pH values at 25 oC. Studies on cysteine-containing peptides by C–S bond reductive elimination of gold–peptide adducts at 37 oC for 24 h were conducted. The gold–peptide adduct afforded the S-arylated peptide via the ligand controlled reductive elimination in 67% conversion at 37 oC for 24 h. We extended the scope of the C–S bond modification of peptides with gold complex in PBS solution (pH 7.4) by heating at 37 oC for 24 h. Excellent conversions (up to 99%) of the corresponding peptides in the cysteine modification were observed by LC-MS/MS analysis. Selective bioconjugation reactions of the single, surface exposed cysteine residue of bovine serum albumin (BSA) and human serum albumin (HSA) by dansyl functionalized gold(III) complex (10 equiv.) were conducted in PBS (pH 7.4)/DMSO (9 : 1) at 37 oC for 24 h. The selective modification of the cysteine residue of BSA and HSA was confirmed by LC-MS/MS analysis. Lysozyme containing no free cysteine unit was used as a control, and yet no modification of lysozyme was found. Thus, these results revealed that the present reaction exhibits excellent cysteine selectivity in protein modification.

503111.label: Major findings and research outcome
503111.value: (1) The amide functionality is commonly found in natural products, proteins, and therapeutic drugs. The conventional approach for amide synthesis involves coupling of activated carboxylic acids and amines that may require extra functional group interconversions and lead to poor atom and step economy. Transition metal-catalyzed amide formation from the reaction of aldehydes, alcohols, and esters with amines has also been reported. However, high reaction temperature, inert atmosphere, and/or anhydrous organic solvents are generally required. We have developed an efficient gold-catalyzed amide synthesis from aldehydes and amines in aqueous medium under mild reaction conditions. This method allows an easy access to amides from the reaction of aromatic, aliphatic and polyhydroxyl oligosaccharide based aldehydes with secondary amines. (2) Reductive elimination is one of the most fundamental reactions in organometallic chemistry. We have developed a new approach for alkynylation of the arylpyridine unit of 6-membered ring cyclometalated gold(III) complexes with terminal alkynes under mild reaction conditions in aqueous medium. The cyclometalated gold(III) complexes generate di-alkynyl gold(III) intermediates via reaction with terminal alkynes in the presence of base. Then, the di-alkynyl gold(III) intermediates with a 6-membered ring gold metallocycle undergo selective C-C bond cross-coupling to afford arylacetylenes by reductive elimination. Notably, our present work is the first example showing highly selective C-C cross-coupling reactions over alkyne homocoupling reactions in di-alkynyl cyclometalated gold(III) complexes. (3) The stability of gold(III) ions significantly increases upon complexation with ligands. However, stable gold(III) complexes generally exhibit poor catalytic activity. We have found that stable bis-cyclometallated gold(III) catalysts are able to exhibit high catalytic activity in organic synthesis through two novel strategies: (1) formation of coordinatively saturated distorted square planar gold(III) complexes using bulky C,N donor ligands and (2) gold–silver dual catalysis for substrate activation. (4) Selective biomolecule modification is an important chemical biology tool for manipulating the properties of biomolecules and investigating their functions in complex biological systems. We have applied the alkynylation reaction for selective modification of alkyne-functionalized peptides and proteins. This reaction has been demonstrated by labelling fluorescent tags on alkyne-functionalized lysozyme by using fluorescent dye-linked cyclometalated gold(III) complexes. (5) The sulfhydryl group in cysteine is an attractive target for bioconjugation due to its high nucleophilicity and rare occurrence (1.7%). However, the development of efficient cysteine modification via C–S bond formation remains a significant challenge. We have used cyclometalated gold(III) complexes [Au(C4N)msen] for chemoselective cysteine modification of peptides and proteins via ligand controlled C–S bond-forming reductive elimination.

503111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
503111.value: (1) We have developed an efficient gold-catalyzed amide synthesis from aldehydes and amines in aqueous medium. In this project, we have set up a reaction protocol allowing the easy access of different classes of amides with diverse structures including oligosaccharides. Effort will be directed towards the application of amide synthesis on more complex biomolecules such as glycans and glycoproteins. (2) We have developed a new approach for alkynylation of the arylpyridine unit of 6-membered ring cyclometalated gold(III) complexes with terminal alkynes under mild reaction. We will further expand the scope of reaction including more diverse cyclometalated gold(III) complexes. We also plan to investigate the catalytic version of this reaction. We have developed that bis-cyclometallated gold(III) catalysts as efficient catalysts for organic transformation reactions and will further apply these catalysts on organic synthesis. (3) We have employed selective formation of arylacetylenes from cyclometalated gold(III) complexes and terminal alkynes under mild reaction conditions as a novel method for selective modification of alkyne functionalized peptides and proteins. In addition, we have used cyclometalated gold(III) complexes for chemoselective cysteine modification of peptides and proteins via C–S bond-forming reductive elimination. Effort will be directed towards strategic incorporation of biophysical probes/affinity tags to bioactive peptides and proteins.

503111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
503111.value: Catalysis is of fundamental importance in our modern society, as most of the chemicals produced for the manufacture of commodity including functional materials, agrochemicals and pharmaceuticals are prepared by catalytic reactions. Note that catalysis is one of the most important principles of green chemistry and an enabling technology to support our sustainable society. Catalysis allows efficient conversion of renewable resources into diverse man-made materials and commercial products using minimum amount of energy under environmentally friendly conditions without generation of toxic chemical wastes. In this project, we have developed gold catalysis for efficient carbon-nitrogen and carbon-carbon bond formation reactions that facilitates the assembly of complex molecular structures. In addition, we have extended the scope of gold catalysis into chemical biology research by selective modification of peptides and proteins. It is envisaged that these new synthetic methodologies would have great applications in fine chemical and pharmaceutical industries. The novel approaches for selective modification of biomolecules would exert a significant impact on the fields of Protein Science, Chemical Biology and Medicine.

503211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
503211.value: 麻痹性貝類中毒(PSP)是香港和中國大陸最主要的海洋生物毒素疾病。麻痹性貝類中毒是由于食用了來自雙鞭甲藻的毒素的貝類所引起，近年來世界上發生麻痹性貝類中毒的事件在不斷增加。麻痹性貝類中毒研究所面臨的挑戰之一是環境中麻痹性貝類毒素檢測和監測，因此需要大量新的分析和成像方法去原位／體外／活體檢測麻痹性貝類毒素，從而應用于水産養殖和人類健康問題。 近年來，幾個含有二氮雜18-冠醚-6結構的光化學傳感器證實它們對麻痹性貝類毒素中的主要毒素石房蛤毒素(STX)具有特異性。但是這些材料的發射光譜寬、壽命短（納秒級）、信噪比低。在本研究中，我們將開發一種新的以稀土元素爲基礎的STX示蹤劑用于原位／體外／活體的檢測。我們團隊早前研究過多光子誘導的發光過程，金屬配位化學以及某些特定稀土配合物在體外生物學上的應用。跟常用的有機熒光團相比，稀土離子是一種很好的候選品，因爲稀土配合物表現出長的熒光壽命，大的Stokes 位移，尖銳的發射峰等特點。現有的STX示蹤劑信噪比低，而稀土配合物的這些特定的光物理性質可被用來解決低信噪比的問題。另外，我們還爲STX設計一些稀土配合物，它們可以通過多光子吸收來實現在近紅外區域被激發。 爲了支持這個工作，我們已經做了兩個重要的概念驗證的測試：(1) 合成含有二氮雜18-冠醚-6铕配合物並具有STX結合部位，證實它們通過線性和非線性（近紅外）激發對STX有高特異性和敏感性；(2) STX的結合會觸發雙光子誘導的f-f發射的增強。基于這些發現，我們提出建立一個新的STX示蹤劑，它具有更少的光毒性，並且能在生物窗口的激發光（700-1000 nm）範圍內觀察毒素；示蹤劑的效用將會在生物系統的體外和活體內證實。初步的結果證實稀土配合物作爲新壹代的生物示蹤劑用于STX的監測具有很好的前景，因爲他們具有很強的親和力(8 × 104 M-1)和ppb級檢測線(500 ppb)。這個示蹤劑對于STX檢測將具有科研和商業應用價值。

503211.label: Realisation of objectives
503211.value: For objective 1, more than 15 water-soluble lanthanide complexes with the ability of giving off in-situ responsive f-f emission for real-time monitoring purposes were synthesized, and were tailored to be specific for paralytic shellfish toxin(s), e.g. saxitoxin (STX). For objective 2, 10 organic chromophores based on small molecule designs were designed and made to achieve high light absorbing ability (extinction coefficient), good quantum efficiency – making them good antenna for sensitizing lanthanide emission – and specificity towards STX, paving way for a series of STX bio-probes. For objective 3, the mechanism behind the ability of our lanthanide-based probe in sensing STX was elucidated: The triplet state of our antenna, diaza-18-crown-6 for example, was shifted due to the electronic interaction arising from the STX binding to it, the shift has allowed energy transfer to take place and hence creating a luminescence response from the lanthanide probes that can be used to in situ monitor STX quantitatively and qualitatively. For objective 4, the detection limit of the designed complex for in situ and in vitro imaging of STX was found to be in micro-mole (ppb) level.

503211.label: Major findings and research outcome
503211.value: 1. A water-soluble europium(III) complex (1) has been synthesized and demonstrated to be a specific fluorescence probe for the paralytic shellfish toxin saxitoxin, a neurotoxin that blocks the voltage-gated sodium channels on cell membranes. Saxitoxin binds to the europium complex (KB = 6.1x104 M-1), triggering a two-photon induced f-f emission enhancement by over 100% and increases the two-photon absorption cross section from 9 to 36 GM. (Organic Letters, 2011, 13, 5036) 2. Five water-soluble cyclen-based europium complexes incorporated with the pendant chelating chromophore, 2-methyl-4-(2-(4-propoxyphenyl)ethynyl)pyridine (L), as the antenna in different ratio had been synthesized along with full structural characterizations, photophysical measurements and in vitro biological studies. The antenna-to-metal ratios are respectively 4 (Eu-4L), 3 (Eu-3L), 2 (1,4-disubstituted Eu-o-2L and 1,7-disubstituted Eu-p-2L) and 1 (Eu-1L). It had been found that the definitive distinction between Eu-o-2L and Eu-p-2L can be interpreted from the emission spectra of Eu3+ at room and low temperature; With all together the results from subcellular stability testing (via titrations), in vitro imaging, cytotoxicity assays and cellular uptake profile, Eu-4L with an overall +3 charge had been demonstrated subcellular localization towards lysosomes and potentials as a selective time-resolved bio-labelling probe, especially for PSP toxins. (Adv Healthcare Mater., 2013, 2, 1501; RSC Adv., 2015, 5, 1334)

503211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
503211.value: The work in this proposal provided a concrete platform for the further development of lanthanide complexes used in monitoring, checking and preventing food poisoning by designing and synthesizing various sensors capable of detecting STX by giving luminescence responses. It is hoped that the results could aid in advancing these sensors from research use into practical uses in food safety aspects. Nonetheless, our results showed that there is still room for improvement, such as enhancing the specificity and selectivity of other PSP toxins to expand the sensing practicality to new fronts, which could be achieved by chemical syntheses and knowledge in toxin interactions, before springing to next step – practical sensors and/or imaging agents for toxicology studies related to PSP toxins.

503211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
503211.value: PSP toxins causing food poisoning and poses a great threat on the public health. Current analytical means are often expensive, tedious and hard to reproduce, such as mouse assays, surface plasmon resonance (SPR)-based sensing and HPLC. We therefore believe direct visualization by imaging techniques would be more preferable. This work utilizes lanthanide complexes to blend multi-photon excitation and near-infrared luminescence in making a bioprobe that could monitor in real time STX and other derivatives, such as neosaxitoxin and decarbamoylsaxitoxin) and develop into high-throughput in situ screening sensors for STX. The project encompasses the design and syntheses of lanthanide complexes with the ability to selectively tag neurotoxins and respond quickly by means of changes in lanthanide luminescence. Our STX bio-marker could also be employed as a tracer to study the behavior of STX and its analogues in the biological systems.

503311.label: Project Objectives
503311.value: To investigate the effects of power ultrasound (US) irradiation on the higher-order structures of high molecular weight (MW) polysaccharides (PS) (β-glucans and PS-protein complexes) from medicinal fungi, i.e. changes in the conformation pattern and aggregate network during ultrasonication of the PS in an aqueous solution with respect to the major ultrasonic process parameters and conditions. To characterize the higher order structures of the native and sonicated PS molecules through experimental measurement and theoretical calculation, including the average MW, aggregate size and rheological properties, the morphological characteristics of aggregate network, and the chain conformation patterns and properties (triple and single helix or random coil, rigidity and geometry); to understand the mechanism of US-induced changes in the PS structures (i.e. sites of chain/helical strand cleavage and aggregate network disruption). To examine the stability of the sonicated PS structures during solution preparation for therapeutic application and under the effect of alkaline (NaOH), organic solvent (DMSO) and higher temperature. To assess the immunomodulatory activities of native and sonicated PS fractions with various conformation structures (i.e. their treatment effects on the immune responses of macrophages) and to elucidate the higher order structure and immunoactivity relationship.
