503311.label: Major findings and research outcome
503311.value: 1. High-power ultrasound (20 kHz) was applied to modify the physicochemical properties of a high-molecular weight (MW) exopolysaccharide (EPS) from mycelial culture of a medicinal fungus. The molecular weight of EPS and viscosity of EPS solution were decreased significantly within 30 min, and the water solubility of EPS was increased several times. The high order structures of EPS, e.g. chain conformation and aggregation were also changed. 2. Power ultrasound was applied to enhance the extraction of polysaccharides from edible and medicinal fungi without changing their molecular weight profiles.The extraction kinetics was fitted to simple empirical kinetic models. Compared with conventional hot water extraction, Ultrasonic extraction was more favorable for extraction of polysaccharides with relatively high protein content and antioxidant activity. 3. Power ultrosound was applied to depolymerize a high molecular weight (MW) exopolysaccaride (EPS) from the fermentation broth of a medicinal fungus Cordyceps sinensis Cs-HK1. From the degraded products a new polysaccharide molecule EPS1U was isolated and its structure was found to be a (1→3)-D-beta glucan. EPS-1U exhibited high moisture absorption capability and may be a potential moisturizing agent for food and cosmeceutical application.

503311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
503311.value: Power ultrasound is a clean and effective means for extraction and modification of polysaccharides. The project results provide useful references for further development and large scale application of power ultrasound for extraction and processing food and medicinal products.

503311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
503311.value: Polysaccharides represent the most diverse and abundant natural biopolymers with a wide range of biological functions in the living organisms and many applications in the food industry. The polysaccharides of edible and medicinal mushrooms (fungi) are valuable nutraceutical materials because of their notable antitumor, immunomodulatory and other medicinal activities. However, many of the fungal polysaccharides are large polymer molecules and can form even larger aggregates or gels in solution, exhibiting poor solubility and high viscosity, which are undesirable for medicinal applications. Partial depolymerization of the large biopolymers is needed to reduce the molecular size so as to reduce the solution viscosity and improve solubility. Irradiation with power ultrasound (US) or ultrasonication is a preferred means for controlled degradation of polymers, lowering the MW and narrowing the MWD but preserving the primary structure and functionality. Ultrasonication is also safer and more environmentally friendly (no use of chemicals) than chemical hydrolysis methods. Through this project we have investigated the effects of ultrasonication on the higher-order structures (conformation and aggregation characteristics) and immunoactivity of high molecular weight polysaccharides from medicinal mushrooms, and gained better understanding of the ultrasonic effects on the polysaccharide structures and properties, and the relationship between the structure and immunoactivity. The results are also useful for improving the application of ultrasonication as a viable and efficient means for processing and modifying bioactive polysaccharides from various natural sources.

503711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
503711.value: Natural products have inspired chemists and physicians for millennia. Their rich structural diversity and complexity has prompted synthetic chemists to produce them in laboratory, often with therapeutic applications in mind; and many drugs used today are natural products or natural-product derivatives. Chemical synthesis of natural products and their analogues has been a key tool in drug discovery and development. The synthesis allows verification of primary structure proposed on the basis of studies of natural product, and presents opportunities to modify the structure, with the ultimate aim of improving activity or physicochemical/biological properties of the lead molecule. Synthesis is also crucial in the establishment of structure-activity relationships, as the ability to make analogues of the lead compound chemically is a prerequisite of such studies. Our present studies focus on a newly isolated marine natural product called hoiamide A. Biological studies of this natural product indicated that it exhibits partial agonism at the neurotoxin site 2 on voltage-gated sodium channels (VGSCs). VGSCs are vital for the functions of the central nervous system. VGSC modulators are useful research tools for neuroscience, as well as therapeutic agents for neurological disorders. Hoiamide A possesses a stereochemically complex structure (15 stereogenic centers and a 26-membered macrocycle) with highly modified peptide and polyketide units as well as an unusual triheterocyclic section. The important biological properties of hoiamide A and its natural scarcity, coupled with its intriguing molecular architecture, render it an attractive synthetic target for further development. To the best of our knowledge, a complete total synthesis of hoiamide A has not yet been reported. The long-term goal of this research is to develop highly effective agents capable of promoting neuronal growth and plasticity through the molecular design, chemical synthesis and biological testing of simpler analogues of hoiamide A. We are directing our efforts to prepare hoiamide A by organic synthesis, employing strategies and methods that can be modified for the preparation of analogues. We are also going to carry out analogue synthesis that aims at determining the minimal molecular architecture of hoiamide A necessary for its biological activity. The investigation towards the total synthesis of hoiamide A and its analogues should have impacts on both the synthetic and medicinal communities. 幾千年來天然產物一直鼓舞化學家和醫生開展相關的研究。天然產物豐富的結構多樣性和復雜性，對於開發具有藥用價值的化學分子非常有利，也吸引合成化學家在實驗室中開展全合成研究。當前使用的許多臨床藥物也確實是天然產物或天然產物的衍生物。利用化學合成手段製備天然產物及其類似物在藥物開發領域已經成為主要的工具之一。通過全合成可以在天然產物結構的基礎上進行改進，並最終提高目標分子的活性以及先導化合物的理化性能和生物學活性。合成化學對於構效關係的建立也是至關重要，而化學合成先導化合物的能力則是完成這一研究的先決條件。 本項研究主要針對新分離得到的海洋天然產物hoiamide A。生物活性研究表明，hoiamide A具有靶向神經毒素位點2的電壓門控鈉離子通道（VGSCs）的部分激動劑活性作用。 VGSCs對於中樞神經系統的功能至關重要。 VGSC的調控在神經科學的研究，以及對神經系統疾病治療方法的研究和藥物研發中非常重要。 Hoiamide擁有高度修飾的肽和聚酮側鏈結構，包含特殊的三元雜環結構單元和復雜的立體化學特徵（15個手性中心和一個26元大環）。 Hoiamide A的獨特結構、重要的生物學活性和自然稀缺性等特點，使其成為一個有吸引力的合成目標分子。截止目前還沒有關於hoiamide A的全合成報導。本研究的長遠目標是通過分子設計、化學合成得到結構簡化的hoiamide A結構類似物，結合生物學測試研究，得到能夠促進神經細胞生長和可塑性的高度有效的藥物。本研究通過構效關係研究可以確定hoiamide A實現其生物活性所需要的最小分子結構。針對hoiamide A及其類似物的全合成工作將對合成化學和藥物化學的研究具有積極的促進作用。

503811.value: In this project, we have examined the migratory carbene insertion reactions of arylrhodium complexes with diazocarbonyl compounds for C-C bond formation. Employing structurally defined cyclopentadienylrhodium(III) complexes, we demonstrated the arylrhodium(III) complexes can be generated by transmetalation with arylboronic acids and direct arene C-H bond cleavage. These arylrhodium complexes reacted with diazomalonates to afford either alkylrhodacyclic complexes or metallaenolate complexes. These complexes have been characterized spectroscopically and by X-ray crystallography. The requirements (e.g. substrate and diazo structure requirements) for selective formation for either species have been delineated. Effective catalytic reactions with selective formation of quaternery stereocenters have been developed. In closing, all the objectives set out in this project have been realized.

503811.label: Major findings and research outcome
503811.value: The major findings resulted from this investigations are below: (1) A Rh-catalyzed intermolecular coupling of diazomalonates with arene C−H bonds was developed. The reaction is initiated by electrophilic C−H activation, which is followed by coupling of the arylrhodium(III) complex with the diazomalonate. In most cases, arenes with oximes, carboxylic acids, and amines as directing groups cross couple with diazomalonates with excellent regioselectivities and functional group tolerance, and thus, this reaction offers a new route to α-aryl carbonyl compounds for specific applications. The carbenoid arene coupling reaction should proceed by migratory carbene insertion to arylrhodium(III) complex, and the resultant alkylrhodacyclic complex has been structurally characterized by X-ray crystallography. This work has been published in Journal of the American Chemical Society. (2) A Rh(III)-catalyzed oxidative [4 + 1] cycloaddition of benzohydroxamic acids and α-diazoesters is achieved to afford benzolactams in up to 93% yields. With the N-OAc amido moiety as a directing group, the ortho-C–H is selectively functionalized and the catalytic reaction exhibits excellent tolerance to different functional substituents. A notable rhodacyclic complex is isolated and structurally characterized, suggesting that C–H/N–H cyclometallation is a key step in the catalytic cycle. This work has been published in Organic and Biomolecular Chemistry. (3) A Rh(III)-catalyzed cascade arylation and chlorination of α-diazocarbonyl compounds with arylboronic acids and N-chlorosuccinimide was achieved. The reaction exhibits excellent functional group tolerance on the organoboron and the diazo reagents; the functionalized α-aryl-α-chlorocarbonyl compounds were obtained in up to 86% yields. The cascade reaction should involve migratory carbene insertion of arylrhodium(III) to form some reactive rhodium(III)−diketonate complexes. Its subsequent reaction with N-chlorosuccinmide afforded the α-chlorocarbonyl products. This work has been published in Organic Letters. (4) Inspired by the success of migratory carbene insertion, a related RhIII-catalyzed direct ortho-CH amidation/amination of benzoic acids with N-chlorocarbamates/N-chloromorpholines was achieved, giving anthranilic acids in up to 85% yields with excellent ortho-selectivity and functional group tolerance. Successful benzoic acid aminations were achieved with carbamates bearing various amide groups including NHCO2Me, NHCbz, and NHTroc (Cbz=carbobenzyloxy; Troc=trichloroethylchloroformate), as well as secondary amines, such as morpholines, piperizines, and piperidines, furnishing highly functionalized anthranilic acids. A stoichiometric reaction of a cyclometallated rhodium(III) complex of benzo[h]quinoline with a silver salt of N-chlorocarbamate afforded an amido rhodium(III) complex, which was isolated and structurally characterized by X-ray crystallography. This finding confirmed that the CN bond formation results from the cross-coupling of N-chlorocarbamate with the aryl–rhodium(III) complex. Yet, the mechanistic details regarding the CN bond formation remain unclear; pathways involving 1,2-aryl migration and rhodium(V)– nitrene are plausible. This work has been published in Chemistry A European Journal.

504011.label: Project Objectives
504011.value: Develop a class of group variable selection methods for several important survival models with high-dimensional covariates. Develop a class of regularization methods for variable selection and estimation in a class of semiparametric survival models, including the partially linear proportional hazards model, partially linear accelerated failure time models, and partially linear proportional means model for panel count data which include interval-censored failure time data as special cases. Investigate the theoretical properties of the proposed methods in high-dimensional settings. Of special interest is when the number of covariates is much larger than the sample size and under reasonable sparseness conditions. Develop computational algorithms for computing the bi-level estimators. Implement them in R and make the programs available on the internet. Conduct simulation studies to evaluate the proposed methods and compare them with the existing methods. Apply the proposed methods to two important genetic data analysis problems: (a) genome-wide association studies using high-density single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) markers; and (b) genetic pathway regression analysis for linking a clinical outcome and gene expression data.

504011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
504011.value: In this project, we propose a class of novel variable selection methods in high-dimensional survival analysis models when there is group structure in covariates. The existing variable selection methods are designed for either individual variable selection or group selection, but not for both. The proposed methods are capable of simultaneous group selection and individual variable selection within selected groups. Computational algorithms will be developed for the proposed bi-level selection methods. Analysis of high-dimensional data presents novel and challenging theoretical and computational problems in statistics. Standard methods for evaluating a statistical procedure assume that the number of variables in a model is fixed and much smaller than the sample size. This formulation is not applicable to high-dimensional models. This project will study the theoretical properties of the proposed selection methods in a class of important survival analysis models, including the linear and partially linear proportional hazards models, linear and partially linear accelerated failure time models, and linear and partially linear proportional means models, in high-dimensional settings. The proposed methods are expected to be able to correctly select the important groups and variables simultaneously with high probability in sparse models even when the number of covariates is much larger than the sample size. Simulation studies will be conducted to evaluate the proposed methods and compare them with the existing methods. 504011.label: Realisation of objectives
504011.value: We have worked on all five objectives of this project. We have investigated the problem of variable selection in survival models with high-dimensional covariates being a possible group structure. The proposed group penalized methods are able to correctly select the important groups and variables simultaneously with high probability in sparse models. The proposed methods are capable of within selected groups. Computational algorithms are developed for the simultaneous group selection and individual variable selection procedures, and the theoretical properties of the proposed selection methods are established. In particular, when the number of covariates involved in survival data is much larger than the sample size, we have developed a fully nonparametric independence screening procedure using the generalized Kolmogorov-Smirnov test statistics, and established its sure screening property with high probability. The proposed screening approach can be used to effectively reduce the number of covariates in ultra-high dimensional survival models. We have studied efficient estimation for a general class of accelerated hazards models with bundled parameters and the semiparametric varying-coefficient partially linear regression model with panel Count Data, and established the asymptotic properties of the estimators. We have considered a new class of semiparametric mean models that allows for the interaction between the observation history and covariates, leaving patterns of the observation process to be arbitrary, and developed a spline-based least squares estimation approach for inference, and established the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimators. We also have developed robust estimation methods for irregularly observed longitudinal data in the presence of informative observation times. Noting that the sieve estimator of nonparametric component in low-dimensional and high-dimensional semiparametric models has a slower rate of convergence usually, we have developed a general asymptotic theory for this case. Extensive simulation studies and application results demonstrated that the proposed new methods perform well. We have achieved all the objectives of this project.

504011.label: Major findings and research outcome
504011.value: For the problem of variable selection in survival models when there is a group structure in a diverging number of covariates, we have developed variable selection approaches that are capable of simultaneous group selection and individual variable selection within selected groups, while most of the existing variable selection methods are designed for either individual variable selection or group selection, but not for both. We have developed computational algorithms for our proposed bi-level selection procedures. For the problem of variable selection in survival models with ultra-high dimensional covariates, we have developed a novel model-free independence screening method based on the generalized Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic. Our simulation results have demonstrated that the new approach outperforms over the existing nonparametric independence screening approaches. For generalized accelerated hazards models with bundled parameters, we have developed semiparametric efficient estimation methods for the parameters that are bundled inside the nonparametric component. Our simulation studies have demonstrated its efficiency gain over the conventional estimating equation approach. For the joint analysis of longitudinal data with informative observation scheme, we have developed some general and robust inference approaches that allow the correlation between the longitudinal response process of interest and the observation process in a general format. This is very important since the format of the relationship between the two processes is generally unknown in practice and could be very complicated and thus a flexible model may be more preferred. For the problem of asymptotic distributions of nonparametric estimators with lower rate of convergence in low-dimensional or high-dimensional semiparametric models, we have developed general large sample theory. We have used the new theorem to derive the asymptotic distribution of sieve estimators of functionals of a mean function from a counting process, which has not been addressed in the literature, and develop new powerful nonparametric tests for the problem of treatment comparison with panel count data. We have found that our developed theory is very useful for construction of nonparametric tests for treatment comparisons. In summary, the ten research papers associated with this project have been published/submitted in international peer-reviewed journals (Biostatistics, Bernoulli, Statistica Sinica, Canadian Journal of Statistics, Biometrical Journal, Computational Statistics & Data Analysis, Lifetime Data Analysis), and also presented in the international conferences.

504011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
504011.value: (1) Our approaches developed in this project can be used to make better identification of important features from survival data and recurrent event data. (2) Our developed semiparametric and nonparametric methods can be extended to analyze ultra-high dimensional longitudinal data in the presence of time-dependent covariates and informative observation and censoring times. (3) Our developed general theory on the asymptotic normality of Z-estimators can be widely used to derive the asymptotic distribution of estimators no matter whether the rate of convergence of an estimator is standard or slower, and to develop tests for checking functional form of covariates.

504011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
504011.value: In this project, we have investigated the problem of variable selection and estimation in high-dimensional survival models arising from survival or recurrent event studies. This research is significant in that it addresses more general situations which often occur in the real world but have not been adequately studied in the literature. A key advantage of our developed approach over existing methods is that it offers simultaneous group selection and individual variable selection within selected groups. Our new statistical inference procedures are more flexible and more robust, and so more applicable. The results of this project have a significant impact because they have filled the gap in the literature on survival analysis and recurrent event data analysis, and are also important to practical applications in biology, economics, engineering, genetics, medicine, and public health. In particular, our new approaches may bring better understanding of covariate effects on the survival time and the disease recurrence.

504111.label: Project Objectives
504111.value: To study and develop the chemistry and methodology for patterning conjugated polymers onto different substrates such as gold, silicon, and polymer films, by a single atomic force microscope (AFM) tip with sub-100 nm resolution and registration. To extend and modify the chemistry and methodology from single AFM tip writing to PPL to achieve large area (~1 cm2) nanopatterning of conjugated polymers. To control the molecular structures of the patterned features, such as crystal growth, chain alignment, and phase separation, by varying the patterning conditions such as stress, pressure, humidity, temperature, and solvent annealing. To study the molecular structures of the patterned features by spectroscopic and microscopic methods. Especially, we will focus on spectroscopic study because it gives statistical information which is difficult to obtain from small area patterning made by other low-throughput nanopatterning technique. To study the physical property such as pi-pi stacking, conjugation length and exciton lifetime of the patterned features by spectroscopic methods. To fabricate photovoltaics based on the polymer nanostructures and measure the device performance. To understand the device physics associated with the nanostructured polymers compared with spincoated polymer films.

504111.label: Realisation of objectives
504111.value: In summary, all the objectives have been addressed. The detail is described as follows: Objective 1. To study and develop the chemistry and methodology for patterning conjugated polymers onto different substrates such as gold, silicon, and polymer films, by a single atomic force microscope (AFM) tip with sub-100 nm resolution and registration. Dip-pen nanodisplacement lithography, a scanning probe-based nanolithography technique, has been developed in the project. We have successfully used dip-pin nanolithography (DPN) and dip-pen nanodisplacement lithography (DNL) to pattern conjugated polymers such as polyfluorene (F8Na) and polythiophene (PNT) on substrates including gold, Si and polymer thin films. Self-assembled monolayers have been used to modify the tip and the substrate for the patterning. Resolution as high as <100 nm has been achieved with fine tune of the patterning conditions. Objective 2. To extend and modify the chemistry and methodology from single AFM tip writing to PPL to achieve large area (~1 cm2) nanopatterning of conjugated polymers. We have developed parallel dip-pen nanodisplacement lithography (p-DNL) for high-resolution, large-area, and serial fabrication of the 2D and 3D polymer structures over areas as large as 1 cm2. Polymer pen lithography (PPL) has also been applied to fabricate similar polymer structure, but with lower resolution but much higher speed, over cm size area on gold and glass. This has been done by carefully extending the chemistry and methodology developed in objective 1. The resolution of PPL has been further improved significantly by developing new dual-tip design. Objective 3. To control the molecular structures of the patterned features, such as crystal growth, chain alignment, and phase separation, by varying the patterning conditions such as stress, pressure, humidity, temperature, and solvent annealing. The resolution and diffusion of polymers have been controlled by optimizing the contact time, humidity, use of additives, and surface modification of substrate/tip. The chain orientation of polymers is found to be well controllable by varying the grafting density and feature density. As such, we developed feature density method to fabricate 3D patterned polymer brushes, which can find many applications in optical, electronic, and biological applications. Objective 4. To study the molecular structures of the patterned features by spectroscopic and microscopic methods. Especially, we will focus on spectroscopic study because it gives statistical information which is difficult to obtain from small area patterning made by other low-throughput nanopatterning technique. The structures of these nanopatterned structures have been studied by atomic force microscope using lateral force, phase, topography, and surface-potential modes. In addition, spectroscopy including UV, FTIR, Raman spectroscopy has been used to characterize the large-size nanopatterns, which cannot be done with small size nanopatterns before. Objective 5. To study the physical property such as pi-pi stacking, conjugation length and exciton lifetime of the patterned features by spectroscopic methods. The conjugating information of the patterned polymers has been characterized by using FTIR, UV, and conductive AFM. Objective 6. To fabricate photovoltaics based on the polymer nanostructures and measure the device performance. The nanostructures have been fabricated on standard substrates for the fabrication of organic solar cells. Standard hole transport layer (PEDOT:PSS) and the active layer (P3HT/PCBM) were used for the fabrication. The device performance including external quantum efficiency, J-V, photoluminescent, and angular dependent measurement has been measured. Objective 7. To understand the device physics associated with the nanostructured polymers compared with spincoated polymer films. The transmittance spectrum was measured by UV-Vis spectrometer (Perkin-Elmer Lambda 18). The topography and thickness of spincoated layers are measured by non-contact mode AFM (XE 100, Park Systems). Moreover, the J-V characteristic curves of as-made organic solar cells are measured by using a Keithley 2400 source meter under illumination of 100 mW/cm2 (Newport 91160, 300 W, solar simulator equipped with an AM 1.5 filter). The light intensity is calibrated by a standard silicon solar cell. The external quantum efficiency (EQE) of the devices are tested by a standard system equipped with a xenon lamp (Oriel 76175_71580), and a dual channel power meter (Newport 2931_C).

504111.label: Major findings and research outcome
504111.value: 1. Dip-pen nanodisplacement lithography (DNL) was invented originally. DNL makes use of an AFM tip to nanodisplace inner self-assembled monolayer with functional surface-initiator molecules, which can be used for surface-initiated polymerization in a subsequent step to fabricate functional polymer surfaces. 2. Parallel form of DNL, namely p-DNL has been developed using multiple 1D and 2D tip arrays, which enables cm size DNL patterning capability in a very short amount of time. 3. New fundamental discovery that the height of polymer brushes is closely related to the packing density of the brush features, being denser the brush features, more stretched the polymer chains, higher the brushes. This has lead to the development of feature density method for the fabrication of 3D-patterned polymer brushes, which have been demonstrated as functional templates for fabricating 3D metal structures, 3D DNA and protein arrays, and for controlling cell behaviors. 4. Development of new tip structure for polymer pen lithography (PPL) on the basis of dual-elastomer tip design. This enables much higher feature resolution and uniformity over a large area. 5. UV light has been used to tune the ink flows in real-time at PPL experiments, which allows reversible and real-time photoreaction on the tip position. 6. Overall, 9 journal papers have been published under the project support, which are listed in Part C. These results have been delivered in many international/regional conferences and university seminars. 7. One US patent on the Dual-Tip structure has been filed.

504111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
504111.value: The developed large area patterning 3D polymer brushes is very unique and novel. Since the functionality of the polymer can be tailored made through chemical synthesis, it should find many applications in a wide range of fields from electronics, optics, to biology. In particular, we believe the large size patterned surface should be very useful for the study of cell biology and control cell behavior such as cell adhesion, orientation, migration and even differentiation. Therefore, the further development of this research can be placed onto biological applications. To proposed action can be further development and study on the fabrication of complicated chemical and 3D polymer surfaces, and to study their use in controlling cell behaviors. Should the cell work is demonstrated, it can be further extended to biomedical engineering research such as tissue engineering work.

504111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
504111.value: The large-area nanofabrication of functional polymers and the control of molecular configuration of the nano-patterned structures are important to a wide range of fields ranging from optoelectronics, sensing, to various life sciences. However, conventional nanofabrication such as electron beam lithography is difficult to fabricate large area nanostructures; it cannot control the molecular structures. To address the challenging, this project aims to develop massively parallel scanning probe based lithography tool for large-area surface patterning of different polymers on a surface with nanoscale resolution, as well as to study how to control the molecular organization (for example, alignment of the polymer chain) by careful control of the chemistry, reactivity, and pattern density. Significantly, dip-pen nanodisplacement lithography (DNL) has been developed from the proposed study, which allows large-area nanofabrication of many kinds of functional polymer with well control of the polymer density and configuration at very high speed. DNL enables spectroscopic study of nanopatterned functional polymers, and many applications such as 3D nanopatterning of polymers for the first time. This result is very important not only for fundamental understanding polymer nanoscience, but also for advanced optical and biological applications in the future.

510311.label: Project Objectives
510311.value: To develop the mathematical model of the robust integrated replenishment planning, production control, and distribution scheduling problem with the uncertainty coming from the inaccurate inventories of raw materials, WIP, and final goods. To develop a robust integrated replenishment, production, and distribution policy that can hedge against the inventory inaccuracy of raw materials, WIP, and final goods, so that the overall costs at all stages of a supply chain (including the costs of raw material ordering, raw material holding, raw material shortage, WIP holding, final goods holding, demand backlog, and final goods shipment) can be minimised. To conduct numerical experiments to validate the performance and robustness of the proposed policies by comparing them with other traditional policies.
rows: To develop the mathematical model of the robust integrated replenishment planning, production control, and distribution scheduling problem with the uncertainty coming from the inaccurate inventories of raw materials, WIP, and final goods.

To develop a robust integrated replenishment, production, and distribution policy that can hedge against the inventory inaccuracy of raw materials, WIP, and final goods, so that the overall costs at all stages of a supply chain (including the costs of raw material ordering, raw material holding, raw material shortage, WIP holding, final goods holding, demand backlog, and final goods shipment) can be minimised.
To conduct numerical experiments to validate the performance and robustness of the proposed policies by comparing them with other traditional policies.

510311.label: Realisation of objectives
510311.value: Objective 1 (100% achieved) The mathematical model of the robust integrated replenishment planning, production control, and distribution scheduling problem under inventory inaccuracy is constructed. In the model of robust replenishment of production control problem, the dynamics of the production/inventory system is captured by two differential equations: one is for the replenishment process, and the other is for the production and demand satisfying process. The state variables are the raw materials inventory level and the final goods inventory level. The inventories of raw materials and final goods are inaccurate, and we assume that the errors between observed inventory level and actual inventory level for the raw materials and the final goods are normally distributed with known means and variances. The control variables are the replenishment rate and the production rate. The objective of this problem is to minimize the average inventory and production cost, which includes the holding cost of raw materials, the holding cost of final goods, and the backlog cost of demand. For the robust distribution scheduling problem, we consider a distribution system that contains a vendor and multiple retailers. The vendor manages the inventory of multiple product-types by determining whether to deliver, how many items to deliver to each of the retailers, and how to combine them in vehicle routes at the end of each period. In the mathematical model of this problem, the objective is to minimize the average long-run cost in the considered time horizon. The cost element includes inventory cost and transportation cost. Each retailer experiences a stochastic demand that is independent and identically distributed in each period. For each retailer, stock loss may occur in each period but it is not reflected in the inventory records, which leads to inventory inaccuracy. The time for transportation is considered, which causes the lead-time of replenishment. This is actually a vehicle routing problem model with delivery lead-time and inventory uncertainty. Objective 2 (100% achieved) The stochastic dynamic programming method is employed to solve the robust integrated replenishment, production scheduling, and distribution scheduling problem, and we developed the robust integrated replenishment, production scheduling, and distribution policy, along with some techniques of the estimation or prediction of system states. The robust replenishment and production control problem of a single-stage production/inventory system with inventory inaccuracy and the lead-time of raw materials ordering has been solved in two steps. First, for a single-stage production/inventory system with ordering lead-time and uncertain production capacity, but without inventory inaccuracy, an approximate optimal replenishment, and production control policy is constructed. Second, we reveal that it is the discontinuity of the control variables in different domains of the state space that makes the policy sensitive to inventory data error. Consequently, we developed a robust replenishment and production control policy to eliminate this sensitivity. In addition, for the robust production control problem for a multiple machines and multiple product-types manufacturing system with inventory inaccuracy, we constructed an error-insensitive hedging point (EIHP) policy. In the EIHP policy, all the operations on a machine are given priorities, and the production capacity of the machine is assigned to the operations in the descendent order of their priorities. For every operation, the production rate is a function of the observed production surplus at this operation, and this function is designed to be insensitive to inventory inaccuracy. In other words, the production rate of every operation changes continuously and smoothly in the neighborhood of a hedging point of the observed inventory level. These hedging points are the parameters of this robust production control policy, which can be optimized so that the average production cost can be minimized. To solve the distribution scheduling problem under inventory inaccuracy and delivery lead-time, we proposed a robust inventory routing policy that makes a decision at the end of each period on whether to deliver, the replenishment quantity of each product-type to each retailer, and the vehicle routing. The solution to this problem contains the routing decisions and replenishment quantity decisions, which can be divided into three layers: (1) the route optimization layer; (2) the replenishment quantity optimization layer; and (3) the route evaluation layer. Objective 3 (100% achieved) Numerical experiments are conducted to examine the performances of the proposed integrated replenishment and production control policy, and the robust distribution scheduling policy. For the robust replenishment and production control policy for a single-stage production/inventory system with inventory inaccuracy, the results of the numerical experiments show that: (1) The average inventory and production cost under the robust replenishment and production control policy is usually less than the average cost under the approximate optimal replenishment and production control policy. This is true for different values of hedging points, lead time of raw materials ordering, unit holding cost, unit backlog cost, and variance of demand rate. (2) The advantage of applying the robust replenishment and production control policy is more obvious if the variance of the observation error of the raw materials inventory level or the final goods production surplus is large, or the lead-time of raw materials ordering is relatively long. (3) If the machine failure rate is relatively small, the robust replenishment and production control policy outperforms the approximate optimal replenishment and production control policy in producing lower average inventory and production cost. However, if the machine failure rate becomes large, the costs under the two policies are close to each other. For the EIHP policy of a multiple machines and multiple product-types manufacturing system with inventory inaccuracy, the results of numerical experiments are as below: (1) The average production cost under the proposed robust production control policy (EIHP Policy) is less than the average production cost under the traditional hedging point-based production control policy (Gershwin Policy) for a manufacturing system with inventory inaccuracy. (2) Sensitivity analysis is done for different values of the parameters of the system, e.g. hedging point (Z), failure rate of machines, unit cost of WIP or final goods inventory, unit cost of final goods backlog, maximum production rate of machines and bounds of observation error of inventory. In most cases, the proposed EIHP Policy outperforms the traditional hedging point-based policy in hedging against inventory inaccuracy. However, in some situations, the EIHP Policy does not outperform the traditional hedging point policy, which leads to the finding of the qualitative condition of employing the EIHP Policy. Namely, the EIHP Policy outperforms the traditional hedging point-based production control policy only when the machine failure rate and the unit backlog cost are relatively small. It does not outperform the hedging point policy when the machine failure rate or the unit backlog cost is relatively large. For the robust distribution scheduling policy under inventory inaccuracy and replenishment lead-time, numerical experiments are conducted to examine its feasibility. In these experiments, we designed a hypothetical distribution system located in eastern China, which is composed of a vendor and 14 retailers and the vendor manages the 3 types of fresh food of the 14 retailers. In each period the vendor needs to determine the appropriate route and right quantities, if the replenishment is necessary. This numerical experiment shows the feasibility of the proposed inventory routing policy. In addition, to examine the robustness of the proposed policy, we compare the expected average cost in different cases, and find that the proposed policy is insensitive to the invisible stock loss and inventory inaccuracy.

510311.label: Major findings and research outcome
510311.value: Major findings: (1) The robust replenishment and production control policy for hedging against inventory inaccuracy maintains the structural characteristics of the optimal replenishment and production control policy that is obtained by dynamic programming, but allows the control variables to change smoothly when the state variables cross boundaries between different domains in the state space and therefore becomes insensitive to inventory error. [Part C(8): items 4-5] (2) The average inventory and production cost under the robust replenishment and production control policy is usually less than the average cost under the approximate optimal replenishment and production control policy. The advantage of applying the robust replenishment and production control policy is more obvious if the variance of the observation error of the raw materials inventory level or the final goods production surplus is large, the lead-time of raw materials ordering is relatively long, or the machine failure rate is relatively small. [Part C(8): item 5 and Part C(9): item 1] (3) A robust inventory routing policy has been developed to solve the distribution scheduling problem under inventory inaccuracy and delivery lead-time. This policy contains the routing decisions and replenishment quantity decisions. [Part C(8): items 5-6 and Part C(9): item 3] (4) Numerical experiments verified the feasibility of the proposed inventory routing policy, and showed that the proposed policy is insensitive to the invisible stock loss and inventory inaccuracy. [Part C(8): item 5 and Part C(9): item 7] Other findings: (5) A logistic-based approach is proposed to solve a class of inventory problems with shortages and time decay functions, which could be the reason of inventory inaccuracy. A sensitivity analysis of the proposed optimization procedure is conducted to justify its advantages. [Part C(8): item 3] (6) To solve the production scheduling problem in distributed manufacturing environment, a new algorithm known as Hybrid Tabu Sample-sort Simulated Annealing (HTSSA) has been developed and tested on the numerical example. [Part C(8): item 2]. A common agent-based model is proposed for the simulation of Make-To-Stock and Make-To-Order supply chains with dynamic structures. [Part C(8): item 1].

510311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
510311.value: (1) We will go further to study the robust replenishment and production policy for multi-echelon production/inventory systems with inventory inaccuracy. Moreover, in this project, we only considered the situation that the capacities of the raw materials stock and the final goods stock are infinite. Actually, in real-world production/inventory systems, the capacities of raw materials and final goods are finite, which makes the replenishment and production control policy more complicated. In this connection, another research issue in the future is the robust replenishment and production control policy for finite raw materials and final goods stocks with inaccurate inventories records. (2) For the robust distribution scheduling problem, in this project we only considered the single-vehicle delivery case and assumed that the vehicle has sufficiently large capacity. Besides, the calculation time should be further reduced to have a quicker response to market. Therefore, the current research could be further extended to consider the capacity and number of vehicles, replenishment quantity for each retailer needs to be optimized further. (3) We will investigate the integrated robust ordering, pricing, and quality keeping policies for perishable products, which also takes inventory inaccuracy into consideration and therefore will be an extension of this project.

510311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
510311.value: Inventory inaccuracy means the discrepancy between inventory record and true inventory level. It happens due to theft, miscounting, misplacing, and deterioration, often exists in ERP or SCM systems, and has a significant negative impact on the control of a production/inventory system. Researchers have found that a very small rate of undetected stock loss might cause a very severe out-of-stock problem. To overcome the negative impact of inventory inaccuracy, we developed a robust replenishment and production control policy that has the similar structure of the optimal policy but is insensitive to inventory record errors. In addition, we also studied an inventory routing problem under replenishment lead-time and inventory inaccuracy, which exist extensively in distribution systems for fresh products. To solve this problem, at first, we proposed the methods of updating the probability of the current net inventory and predicting those in future periods. For each candidate route, an algorithm is developed to optimize the replenishment time, replenishment quantity, and replenishment stage length. Finally, a genetic algorithm-based method is developed to optimize the delivery route. Numerical experiments had been conducted to verify the robustness of the proposed replenishment, production control and inventory routing policies, and their potential of being applied in practice.

510611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
510611.value: Development and deployment of systems and applications for pervasive networking and computing (PNC) is challenging due to the need of creating various application specific smart environments. In many cases, it is very difficult and even impractical to experiment with and test the proposed mechanisms due to the overhead of managing a large number of smart devices. To cope with the above problems, it is highly desirable to build a test-bed or simulation system which will allow them to re-create the smart devices and environments in their table-top computers with unprecedented ease-of-use in designing, testing and managing the respective entities. However, existing test-beds and simulators for experimenting with PNC systems are limited in scale and consider only existing devices not including everyday physical world entities (e.g., smart table, etc) which are fast evolving and to be embedded into our surrounding environments. Moreover, they are mostly designed for simulating applications but do not consider PNC related protocols and algorithms. In this project we shall develop a generic framework and software environment for simulating different types of PNC applications, protocols and algorithms. Along with the traditional computing devices, sensors and actuators, we will propose to model everyday physical objects as smart entities called ubiquitous interacting objects (UIOs), and develop the simulation system based on the abstraction of UIO and their interactions. We will first provide a language to describe the characteristics, functions and services of those entities. We then model static and dynamic characteristics of PNC environments using the defined UIO model. With the design considerations of ease of use, flexibility and extendibility, the system will allow developers to use default environment settings provided by the simulator library or to define new devices and functionalities for their own settings based on the application requirements. Also, we will provide a visualization tool for users to graphically manipulate the application scenarios and display scenarios as well as actions induced by tested applications, protocols and algorithms. Pervasive computing is the next wave of computing paradigms. The results of this project will facilitate the development of high-performance pervasive computing systemns and applications, such as smart spaces, socal networks, pervasive healthcare, intelligent transpotation systems, and smart cities. As the Hong Kong SAR government has been greately promoting the development of innovative technologies, the contribution of this project is highly relevant to Hong Kong scientific and industrial community and society. 由于需要创建与应用密切相关的智能环境，给普适网络和计算（PNC: Pervasive Networking and Computing）相关应用的开发和部署带来了很大的挑战。在大多数情况下，由于需要管理大量的智能设备，使得对新提出的机制和方法进行测试和验证的任务变得非常困难，甚至几乎不可能完成。为了应对以上问题，十分有必要构建一个面向普适计算环境的测试平台或模拟仿真系统。该测试平台使得相关的开发和研究人员仅仅使用普通的电脑就可以设计、测试和管理智能环境中大量的相关智能实体，并且使得这些复杂过程的实现变得前所未有的方便。但是，现有的测试平台和仿真模拟器不仅在规模上受限且所考虑或支持的设备很有限（未考虑到正在快速变得日益智能化且布满我们周围环境的日常物理世界中的实体，如智能桌子等）。此外，很重要的一点是现有测试平台或模拟仿真器的设计主要关注于模拟仿真各种应用的行为而非强调对PNC相关的协议或者算法的仿真模拟。 在该项目中，我们将开发一个通用的框架和软件环境以模拟各种不同类型的PNC应用、协议和算法。在传统计算设备，传感器和驱动器的基础上，我们将提出一种对日常生活中的物理实体即无处不在的交互对象UIO(Ubiquitous Interacting Objects)的智能实体进行建模的方法，同时我们还将基于对UIO的抽象及其相互之间的交互模型开发相应的模拟仿真系统。首先，我们将提供一种语言来描述这些实体的特性、功能以及所能提供的服务。然后，我们基于所定义的UIO模型对PNC环境的静态和动态特征进行建模。由于在该仿真模拟器的设计阶段我们即考虑到易用性、灵活性及可扩展性，该系统将允许开发人员使用由仿真模拟器库文件所提供的默认环境设置来基于各类应用需求准确定义新设备和新功能。此外，我们将提供一个可视化工具来使得用户能够以图形化的方式操控应用场景并且展现所测试的应用、协议以及算法中的各种过程及行为细节。 普适计算是新技术的重要发展方向之一。该项目的实施将促进高性能普适计算系统和应用的发展，如智能空间，社交网络，普适医疗，智能交通系统以及智能城市等。秉承香港特区政府大力促进和发展创新技术的宗旨，该项目将对香港学术界、工业界和社会的发展作出相关的贡献

510611.label: Realisation of objectives
510611.value: Pervasive Networking and Computing (PNC) is rapidly expanding into our daily lives, from smart homes to smart cities. The development process for such systems is challenging due to the need of creating, deploying, and testing numerous and heterogeneous smart devices in differing environments and scenarios. Simulation systems can aid the development of PNC by emulating the behavior of smart devices. However, many open challenges remain with regard to usability and usefulness of such simulation systems. In this project, we investigate the requirements of different PNC systems and applications and their supporting functions for identifying the related issues, develop simulation models for PNC systems and applications, define the performance evaluation models along with the performance metrics, and implement a software environment for simulation. Our simulation environment takes ubiquitous interactive objects (UIOs) as a uniform model for smart devices, and utilize the Eclipse RCP platform to support dynamic adding to, deleting from, and updating of the simulation environment. The simulation system also can automatically configure and execute large-scale testing tasks using predefined scenarios. We realize our objectives by addressing the following issues: 1. We carried out comprehensive literature review of related work on existing simulation systems for pervasive systems and applications. Based on the review, we have studied and classified the existing issues and problems related to how to design and implement simulation environment for pervasive systems and applications. In particular, we have investigated how to build a generic simulation environment for better and reliable simulation results by building a unified model of smart devices, utilizing real devices and testbeds. We have also identified new research topics and potential issues in designing and implementing such a simulation. 2. We proposed a unified model called ubiquitous interactive objects (UIOs) that abstracts common features and functions of smart objects for their design and development. The aim of the UIO model is to easily create different smart objects with individual computing, sensing, and actuating capabilities as well as interaction functions, and integrate them into the simulation system. The model has three types of spontaneous interactions in the UIO model, between different UIOs, between the components of the same UIO, and between UIOs and the environment. Additionally, UIOs may require maintenance during simulation. Consequently, UIOs have the following four interfaces, inter-UIO communication interface, intra-UIO adaptor interface, local environment interface and maintenance interface 3. We proposed five dimensions as a performance evaluation model: generality, scalability, flexibility, plug-and-play, and dynamic composition. Generality means the simulator can provide developers a consistent abstraction of a vast amount of heterogeneous entities under different scenarios. Scalability indicates whether the simulator can support large-scale simulations. Flexibility describes whether the simulator can support simulation with autonomous, composable, and adaptive entities, which provides a flexible way to build and manage applications. Plug-and-play means the simulator can support various entities by different device manufactures without the need for physical device configuration or user intervention in resolving resource conflicts. Finally, dynamic composition is the ability of a simulator to discover every active entity on demand and on the fly, i.e., all necessary functions and services can also be discovered dynamically. 4. We implemented our simulation system based on OSGI (Open Services Gateway initiative) and its implementation utilizes Eclipse RCP (Rich Client Platform). Our simulation system specifies different reusable components in a system as well as the communications among them. In our simulation system, components can be remotely installed, started, stopped, updated, and uninstalled without having to reboot. A set of management functions, including component discovery, resource recycling, and life cycle management, are also provided. Generally speaking, our simulation system supports component-based architectures and that components can be dynamically added, removed, and updated. It also allows components to be changed without stopping and restarting a running simulation.

510611.label: Major findings and research outcome
510611.value: Our research outcome generated from this project is fruitful, mainly including five journal papers, two conference papers, and several demonstration systems. Meanwhile, 3 MPhil students have been trained owing to the funding support of this project. The students were all supported to attend the conferences, and our publications have received international recognition from the pervasive computing community. Supported by this project, we first made a comprehensive survey about middleware for pervasive computing and published our survey in [J2013]. In this survey, we investigated a large number of existing pervasive computing middleware solutions that can help the programmer develop applications. However, we found that although many pervasive computing middleware systems have been proposed, we hardly see widespread use of any in real applications outside the academic research labs. We realized that for a practical middleware system, smart devices with different kinds of functions must be associated together to provide the service described in the user requirement. We call this service composition. In addition, as the service composition environment may be dynamic and large scale, a centralized service composition algorithm is usually inefficient due to message cost, and a decentralized approach, which employs pre-determined coordinators to search and compose service, can also have high cost. Based the above observations, we proposed a unified model for designing intelligent objects called UIO. UIO is an abstraction of physical devices in pervasive computing environment with ability to find and collaborate with other devices through exposing their capabilities as services. This model helps to describe the intelligent objects in a generic level. It not only can describe the features and functions of intelligent objects, but also the interaction amongst them. Based on the UIO, we proposed a localized approach for service composition. In our localized service composition algorithm (LASEC), UIOs collaborate with each other in a bottom-up, localized manner to compose required service without requiring global knowledge. The UIO model with an application example was published in [J2015b]. Based on the UIO concept and various requirements of pervasive computing, we developed a simulation system called Mirror which can facilitate the design, development, and testing of pervasive applications in cyber-physical systems [J-under-review]. This system has the following advantages. First, it can ease creating and managing UIOs, environments, and scenarios. Second, it is based on OSGI and Eclipse RCP, and can simplify the integration with other systems. Third, it also can generate different test plans automatically and perform large-scale testing. We leverage our UIO model and Mirror to handle problems in some real applications including cache consistency problem in WMNs ([J2014]), range-free localization in wireless sensor networks ([J2015a]), intelligent traffic light control ([C2014a]), and describe the idea of UIO in [J2016a].

510611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
510611.value: The study demonstrates the benefits of our system Mirror with regard to developing pervasive applications, comparing the performance of different algorithms, as well as obtaining more reliable results. Thus, optimizing algorithms or mechanism via simulation can a promising direction for future work. Additionally, security and privacy mechanisms are necessary for UIOs, especially for those that are handling or providing access to sensitive data, and are deployed in real environments. Security and privacy are out of the scope of this project, but can be addressed in future work.

510611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
510611.value: Pervasive Networking and Computing (PNC) is rapidly expanding into our daily lives, from smart homes to smart cities. Simulation systems can aid the development of PNC by emulating the behavior of smart devices. In this project, we aim at developing a practical simulation environment for PNC systems. Our simulation environment takes ubiquitous interactive objects (UIOs) as a uniform model for smart devices. The aim of the UIO model is to easily create different smart objects with individual computing, sensing, and actuating capabilities as well as interaction functions, and integrate them into the simulation system. Based on the UIO concept, we developed a simulation system called Mirror which can facilitate the design, development, and testing of pervasive applications in cyber-physical systems. This system can ease creating and managing UIOs, environments, and scenarios, and it can generate different test plans automatically and perform large-scale testing. The simulation system Mirror has been successfully evaluated based on an intelligent traffic light control system application.

510711.label: Major findings and research outcome
510711.value: 1. Ten types of dress patterns, including collared or collarless long-sleeved shirt, collared or collarless short-sleeved shirt, sleeveless shirt, no shirt, long pants, shorts, high visibility clothing, and the shades on the head, face, neck and/or arms were observed from the field survey. 2. Inappropriate dress behavior and insufficient personal protection were observed on-site, such as semi-nude behavior, which may pose a high risk of skin cancer because of the direct exposure to solar ultraviolet radiation. Despite high sun exposure, outdoor workers’ sun protection tends to be poor and inconsistent and most construction workers did not engage in adequate and appropriate dress behavior against sun protection. 3. Thermoregulation is one of the critical parameters of human responses to heat. Core temperature, skin temperature, and heart rate are the basic physiological measures of heat strain, and the rate of body heat storage and the physiological strain index are often used as the indicators of thermal stress. In view of this, it is necessary to collect these physiological parameters in laboratory experiments to ascertain the effectiveness of wearing the newly designed clothing in reducing body heat strain. Apart from physiological strain, the rise in heat strain under hot conditions is also associated with elevated perceptual strain. The Rating of Perceived Exertion (RPE), which is based on subjective assessment, is a simple and valid method for regulating exercise intensity, physical stress, effort, and fatigue in relation to a specific task. Clothing comfort is related to the subjective perceptions of various sensations, which is determined by the interactions among clothing, human body, and ambient environment. 4. The newly designed anti-heat stress clothing (AHSC) exerts the capacity of alleviating heat strain and improving wearing comfort for the wearers. The T-shirt of AHSC has better ability in moisture management and ventilation than that of TRADE, while the pants of AHSC have better ability in moisture management than those of TRADE. Meshed reflective strip in the T-shirt of AHSC has superior air permeability. 5. The major findings of laboratory experiment manifested that the AHSC was effective in alleviating thermo-physiological strain. Particularly, a remarkable reduction of physiological strain by 16.7% and body heat storage by 28.8% and an improvement in overall comfort by 14.2% were achieved with wearing the AHSC. Overall, the anti-heat stress clothing exerts better capacity of alleviating body heat strain and improving wearing comfort for construction workers.

510711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
510711.value: The current study has established a research framework for developing appropriate anti-heat stress summer work uniform. This framework can be replicated in developing other heat stress precautionary measures, such as hydration, shields, portable fans, and personal cooling garments. The established research framework is highlighted below: 1) Literature review • Meta-analysis is a useful technique to generalize the results from different studies to obtain a better understanding of how well personal cooling garment works. • Content analysis can identify the important structures of large amounts of textual information. 2) Clothing design • Laboratory tests can be carried out to measure the thermal, moisture, and mechanical properties of sourced fabrics and cooling media. • Smart design takes account for different design patterns in terms of cooling effect and ergonomics. • Laboratory experiment can be performed to evaluate the ergonomic design of different design patterns. • The optimal design pattern can be determined by sweating manikin test. 3) Evaluation • Laboratory experiment can be conducted to ascertain the effectiveness in reducing body heat strain. • Field study can be administered to assess the usability and acceptability among construction workers. • By inviting the representatives of frontline workers and management staff, focus group meeting can be held to evaluate the practicality and applicability in the construction industry.

510711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
510711.value: Summer time in Hong Kong is hot and humid. Often construction workers have to undertake physically demanding activities in an outdoor environment. Working in such an environment poses a high risk for heat-related illness and even deaths. There is an urgent need to engineer and design a work uniform for construction workers. Based on a scientific approach with robust research methodologies, this study demonstrates that a newly designed anti-heat stress clothing (AHSC) not only exhibits better performance in alleviating body heat strain and satisfies the needs of construction workers. The findings of the current research demonstrate that the AHSC is applicable in industrial settings and eventually in large populations and locations. Thus, the convincing research findings enable both the academia and practitioners to improve work practice in the construction industry through developing an industry standard. Along with the development of textile science, the production of innovative fibers and fabrics with superior thermal and moisture performance and reasonable costs is anticipated. The fabric properties of the AHSC can be used as an industry standard in determining an appropriate summer work uniform in comparison with existing garments.

510911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
510911.value: The apparel industry relies extensively on model form (dummy or mannequin) for all tasks involved in apparel design. The accurate design and construction of the model form depends highly on the results of national anthropometric surveys. However, as the anthropometric profiles/measurements are changing due to various reasons such as secular trends, population movement, plastic surgery, and living standard, there is a need to continuous update and modification of the model form. Furthermore, consumer taste are changing and there is new trend in customized clothing design, hence the need for creating customized model form. Traditionally, dummy makers will scan a real human and output the profile of the scanned data to make the moulds and use the technique of injection moulding to produce the mannequins. This process is very time consuming and would be exorbitant for customized design. Hence, in this study we propose a digital mannequin and an interactive robotic mannequin design. The digital mannequin can be used for creating and testing virtual clothes. The interactive robotic mannequin will be manipulated based on the dimension of the digital mannequin and modified accordingly. Existing digital database of 3D human body will be used in the study. Additional data will be collected to account for the size ranges that are missing in our data base. The 3D human body shape will be analyzed and important anthropometric dimension needed for clothing design will be extracted. Similarly, a set of dummy are scanned to acquire the 3D surface data. The surface point data are then used to make a parametric model using Matlab programming. The aim of the parametric model is that when the important dimensions (example waist girth and bust girth) are modified, the 3D surface of the dummy is also generated. Since all the measures can be independently modified, the scaling is better than normal sizing which uses proportional grading. The digital dummy is linked to a controller of a robotic mannequin. The robotic mannequin will be built using separate sections (panels). When the digital dummy is modified, the offset of each panel will be computed in a Matlab program and a digital signal sent to the controller. The controller will receive the signal and cause a servo mechanism-based actuator to move the panel by the required offset. An interactive robotic mannequin linked with digital mannequin is essential for quick fashion product design, especially for customized fitting. 服装工业在服装设计的所有步骤中都需要用到人台（又称“模特”）。人台模型的设计主要是以国家人体测量数据为依据。然而，人体测量的结果会随着人类体型长期趋势性变化，人口流动，整形手术，生活水平变化等因素的变化而变化，所以人台模型设计也需要持续不断的更新。而且顾客对衣服和标准体型的审美标准也会随着时尚潮流的变化。传统上，人台制作企业会首先扫描真人的轮廓来制作生产人台的模具，然后用注入成型法生产出人台。这个过程非常的费时并且价格昂贵。所以，我们提出这项方案，用以研究一个虚拟人台和一个机器人人台。虚拟人台用以设计和测试虚拟设计的衣服。机器人人台会根据虚拟人台尺寸并加以改良设计而成。我们会用现有的3D人体测量数据库来进行研究，必要时，我们还会采集更多的3D人体测量数据来贴补现有数据库的缺失。这些数据库中的样本会被分析提取出关键的用于服装设计的人体尺寸数据。同样的我们也会扫描一些人台来获取相关信息。由此得到轮廓采集点信息数据会用于设计一个参数化虚拟人台（Matlab平台）。这个参数化虚拟人台的目的是模拟出当关键尺寸（例如腰围和胸围）发生变化时，身体体型轮廓的变化情况。因为每个尺寸都可以单独设定，所以它的外形会比一般的标准系列的人台更接近人体真实体型和覆盖更多体型。然后这个虚拟人台会被用于控制机器人人台。当虚拟人台变化时，机器人人台的每个运动模块上的控制器都会接收到由Matlab编写的程序发来的运动指令。控制器会接受处理这些信号并驱动运动模块运动，进而变化出各种体型。这个机器人人台将在快速服装设计和服装订做中起到重要作用。

510911.label: Realisation of objectives
510911.value: The above three objectives have been met completely. 1. The database of the 100 Hong Kong females body measurements were created using the TC2 body scanner to acquire the body profile of the female. In the scanned results it was found that body postures were varied with some slumbing forward or some moved sidewards. A programme was written to bring these varied posture to one of erect figure so that standardisation of the avatar can be carried out for the next step. Besides, the database was compared with anthropometric body sizes from the US and Japan to study any differences between races and the conclusion was that human beings no matter their race have almost similar proportion. When a person is tall, the limbs and body lengths will be longer and when a person is fatter, the girths measures will also be proportionately larger. Hence their correlations are very position and can be used all the time. However, one thing must be taken into consideration though there are features to take note on some physical distinctivety, i.e. there exist some special differences among races, e.g. those of African origin has stronger and rounder buttockes while the Oriental counterparts have flatter seats, northeners are more robust than the southeners. Despite these "minor" observations, human beings are basically proportionate entities and this leads us to think that a mannequin can be made robotic to change dimensions and shape as required. 2. These profiles were used to develop the digital parametric model using the software Solidworks. The model was also compared to existing mannequins used for garment fitting in the market. With the parametric model, the range of the required size range was developed so that the mannequin can expand and contract as desired by the user. The user through the interface will key in the required dimension so that the desired body profile can be obtained. This became the interactive parametric model and will be used to control the physical mannequin in objective 3. It has to note that in performing this task, the effective range is limited to a range of Sizes UK6 to 16 as outside the range a different body profile will beget, e.g. the Outsizes or "Mama" sizes. This will call for a different mannequin altogether. 3. The prototype of interactive robotic mannequin was next built. This physical mannequin consisted of the following parts; the mechatronics system (motors and actuators, gearing system, controller), panel design where the panels of different body parts were first made through 3D printing, the "Skin" which effectively cover the body of panels to smoothing the surface of the mannequin just like a person. An interface was written using Mathlab where a (Graphical User Interface) GUI was designed to allow a user to key in his or her desired measurements to control the changes made to individual body panels of the physical mannequin. The user can also build in a range of size measurements and save them for future retrieval and this is very ideal for brands with multi-national sales network where people or customers are different. Besides, individual panels can be interactively moved to allow local changes to a body position, eg. if we want a bigger bust shape and measurement but others remained, and this is good for haute couture or high-end tailoring where individual clients are entertained. Besides, it is a sustainable instrument as it occupies limited space and can be varied as time goes on. The population profile is very dynamic and can change frequently which traditional anthropometric study or survey cannot keep up to date. Overall, the objectives have been met and the robotic mannequin was licensed.

So the robotic mannequin developed can perform firstly the changes of the size profiles of various grouping but still can effected those differences via local panel movements to effect those changes, eg. bigger buttock shape and measurements. 511211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
511211.value: Bulk metallic glasses (BMGs) exhibiting unique properties such as high strength, high elastic strain and good corrosion resistance are currently a frontier in metals research. Over the past decade, there have been extensive research efforts to develop BMG matrix composites (BMGMCs) in order to address the issue of room temperature brittleness of BMGs. Martensitic transformation mediated BMG composites are the most recent development or breakthrough in the field of BMGs, which exhibit enhanced tensile ductility together with significant work hardening capability through transformation induced plasticity or twining-induced plasticity, and can greatly enhance the potential applications for BMGs. Similar to traditional shape memory alloys, martensitic BMGMCs consist of martensitic phases which undergo stress-induced martensitic transformation. As a new direction for scientific research, it is essential to fully understand the deformation mechanisms of martensitic BMGMCs, and the correlation between their structure and plasticity so as to tailor the martensitic structure of the composites for enhanced properties. It is also critical to further synthesize martensitic BMGMCs of larger size for structural applications. Based on the recent work of the project team on martensitic BMGMCs, the proposed research aims to further address the above issues. In this project, a Cu-Zr binary alloy system will be selected for investigation. Through the addition of doping elements, and the control of the processing parameters, martensitic composites of different sizes and distributions of martensitic particles will be achieved. The ductility and deformation behaviour of the composites with different martensitic structures will be examined by mechanical testing, and their microstructures will be characterized by advanced analytical techniques. The deformation mechanisms and the microstructure dependence of the plasticity of the composites will also be theoretically studied. To understand the shear strain transmission mechanisms between the martensitic phase and the amorphous matrix is one of the scientific challenges of the study. Based on the findings of these studies, an attempt will further be made to synthesize martensitic composites with larger sizes through spark plasma sintering. By adopting a new approach, new interfaces with diffusionless phase transformation will be firstly designed and synthesized by consolidating BMG powders coated with ultra fine martensitic particles. It is envisaged that by proper design of the matrix and the interface structures, large size BMGs with enhanced ductility can be achieved. The findings of the proposal will not only lead to new potential applications of BMGs, but also have significant academic value. 塊體非晶合金由於其獨特的性能，如高強度、高彈性和高的耐腐蝕抗力，目前成爲金屬材料領域的前沿問題。在過去十年裏，爲瞭解決室溫脆性，人們對塊體非晶合金複合材料開展了大量的研究。最近，馬氏體調製塊體非晶合金複合材料的成功開發，給塊體非晶合金領域帶來了突破性進展。在這一新型材料中，通過馬氏體相轉變或孿晶的形成而誘發塑形變形，進而使其表現出了明顯的拉伸塑形和加工硬化行爲。與傳統的形狀記憶合金類似，馬氏體非晶合金複合材料包含有馬氏體相，它在應力作用下能夠産生馬氏體相變。基於此，作爲一個新的科學研究方向，準確理解馬氏體非晶合金複合材料的變形機制，以及結構和塑形的關聯性，並進而改變複合材料中的馬氏體結構以求增強非晶合金的性能是其重要目標。更進一步，在變形機理研究的基礎上，合成具有較大三維尺寸的馬氏體非晶合金複合材料以達到應用於結構材料領域的目的。 基於上述的最新研究成果，本研究計劃將選擇銅－鋯二元合金體系作爲研究物件，對上述的塑形機制進行研究。通過在該二元合金體系中添加不同合金元素和控制製備工藝參數，獲得不通尺寸和分佈的馬氏體增強相顆粒。對不同馬氏體相結構的複合材料的塑性變形行爲進行測試，並利用先進的檢測技術對其微觀結構進行表徵。進而對變形機制和微觀結構的相關性進行理論分析，探索剪切應變在馬氏體相和非晶相之間的傳遞機制。最終，在上述的實驗及理論分析之上，本研究將通過放電等離子體燒結以合成大尺寸馬氏體非晶合金複合材料。通過採用材料加工新工藝，對非晶合金粉末和超細馬氏體顆粒進行燒結，在複合材料內獲得具有無擴散型相變的新介面。進而期望經過對基體和介面結構進行恰當的設計，獲得具有大尺寸的塑性非晶合金。本研究計劃的的研究結果不僅能夠拓展塊體非晶合金的應用前景，而且對其變形機理研究也具有極大的科學價值。

511211.label: Realisation of objectives
511211.value: Objective 1 (100% achieved) In this project, bulk metallic glass composites (BMGCs) with different martensitic structures were successfully synthesized by adjusting their composition and the process parameters. A series of ZrCu-based BMGs and BMGCs with chemical compositions of Zr47.5Cu46.5Al5Co1, Zr47.5Cu46Al5Co1.5, Zr47.5Cu45.5Al5Co2, Zr48Cu47.5Al4Nb0.5 and Zr48Cu46.5Al4Nb1.5 were successfully produced by arc melting and cast into copper molds. Their structure was further adjusted by annealing and plastic pre-deformation. Objective 2 (100% achieved) The structure of the as-cast, annealed and deformed ZrCu-based BMGCs was systematically characterized by X-ray diffraction with the CuKα radiation, and differential scanning calorimetry at a heat rate of 20 K/min. The detailed microstructures of the BMGCs including the volume fraction of crystalline phase were examined by optical microscope, scanning electron microscope, and transmission electron microscope. The mechanical properties and the ductility of the composites were characterized by uniaxial tension tests. Objective 3 (100% achieved) The correlation between the ductility and microstructure of the BMGCs and the deformation mechanisms was systematically analyzed. By studying the effect of ductile phase on the plasticity stability of the metallic glass composites using the concept of normalized strain-hardening rate, the critical volume fraction for stable plastic deformation of B2 or β-reinforced metallic glass composites was determined. In addition to the volume fraction, the effect of the density of the stress concentration sites and the distribution of the B2 phase on the deformation behaviour was also examined. Objective 4 (100% achieved) The stress (strain) transmission in both the amorphous matrix and the martensitic phase was studied through the introduction of the inhomogeneous stress distribution in the B2-BMGCs. The plastically predeformed composite is in a complicated microsopical internal stress state: the B2 phase is in a tensile stress and the MG matrix is in a compressive stress. Finite element modelling was carried out to understand the stress state of the matrix and the B2 phase in the composites and the stress concentration near the interface.
