511211.label: Major findings and research outcome
511211.value: 1) The tensile plastic deformation behavior of ZrCu-based metallic glass composites (MGCs) with various crystalline volume fractions was investigated. A tensile plastic strain of more than 10 % was achieved in a metallic glass composite with a crystalline volume fraction of 32.6 %. It was found that the B2 phase can effectively activate the formation of multiple shear bands and promote the density of the stress concentration sites. By using the concept of the normalized strain-hardening rate, the critical volume fraction for stable plastic deformation of B2 or β-reinforced metallic glass composites was determined. The related work has been published in Materials Science and Engineering A, 636 (2015) 502-506. 2) A BMGC with strong strain-hardening capability and large elastic strain limit was firstly reported. It was found that by plastic predeformation, the bulk metallic glass composite can exhibit both a large elastic strain limit and high strength under tension. These unique mechanical properties are attributed to the reversible B2 B19’ phase transformation and the complicated stress states of the MG matrix and the second phase. The related work has been published in Scientific Reports, 4 (2014) 5302. 3) The tensile plastic deformation behaviors of a Ti-based metallic glass composite (MGC) confined by a commercially pure titanium (CPT) was investigated. It was found a uniform plastic deformation was achieved in the CPT-confined MGC, where the strain localization and necking was effectively suppressed. The MGC sustained a true tensile strain exceeding 10% before fracture. The uniform plastic deformation of the MGC originates from a deformation mechanism of the dislocation pile-ups, inducing activation of the multiple shear bands in the MGC/CPT interface. The related work has been published in Philosophical Magazine Letters, 94 (2014) 233. 4) In the project, some work was also done to investigate the deformation behavior of monolithic metallic glasses, which is useful to understand the deformation mechanisms of BMGCs. Experimentally observations and linearly elastic strain field analysis suggest that the shear bands tend to operate cooperatively due to their enhanced mutual long-range elastic field interactions which activate localized yielding to bring out the shear bands in small length scales. Subsequently, these shear avalanches at small scales can knife the elastic energy in each serration event. Related work has been published in Journal of Applied Physics, 114 (2014) 033520, and Journal of Applied Physics, 114 (2014) 033521.

511211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
511211.value: Based on the findings of the present project, the following future work is proposed. (a) The present project revealed that by plastic predeformation, the bulk metallic glass composite can exhibit both a large elastic strain limit and high strength under tension. It is therefore important to further investigate the effect of complex loading modes on the stress distribution of the BMGCs and their properties. (b) The present project has also revealed the correlation between the structure and the ductility of BMGCs. It is most worthwhile to tailor their structure by other approaches such as laser treatment in order to enhance their mechanical properties. Preliminary work is being done to understand the deformation behavior of BMGCs under different loading modes, and work will be carried out to study the structure and deformation behavior of BMGCs after laser treatment. It is expected that based on the findings of the preliminary work, a new research proposal will be formulated.

511211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
511211.value: Bulk metallic glasses (BMGs) exhibiting unique properties such as high strength, high elastic strain and good corrosion resistance have attractive much research attention over the past few decades. There have been extensive research efforts to develop BMG matrix composites (BMGMCs) in order to address the issue of room temperature brittleness of BMGs. With the aim of addressing this issue, a series of BMGCs with different martensitic structures were successfully synthesized. By optimizing the chemical composition, the tensile plastic strain of more than 14% was achieved in the ZrCu-based BMGCs. A critical volume fraction for stable tensile plastic deformation was determined. In addition to the volume fraction, the density of the stress concentration sites and the distribution of the martensitic phase were also found to be key factors controlling the stable plastic deformation of the BMG composites. A BMGC with good tensile ductility and large elastic strain was also firstly reported in the study.The results of the present project do not only lead to a better understanding of the deformation behaviour of BMGCs, but also lay down a good foundation to further develop commercial BMGCs.

511511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
511511.value: 根據Espicom Business Intelligence的資料顯示，中國在2011年度的醫療用器械與植入件（MDI）的市場總額將高達232億港元，比2006年提高69%。這種植入件的巨額需求主要用於骨骼磨損的病人，特別是那些患有老年退化疾病的病人。事實上，在這些植入於人體的生物相容性合金（BCAs）中，有大約20%左右會由於不同的原因而產生機械性失效。其中的一個主要失效原因在於這些醫療用植入件是採用傳統的熔模铸造（IC）或金屬注射模壓（MIM）工藝製造的。當這些鑄造的或注射模壓的植入件應用於人體時，其耐用性和可靠性顯得不足。為了製造出高強度、高壽命的醫療用植入件（MDI），並進一步提高其生產效率，降低其生產成本，在此提出採用溫鍛（WF）工藝方法來製造那些輪廓形狀不太複雜的醫療用植入件。由於溫鍛工藝採用壓力成形，即可大幅度地消除零件中的微孔，切斷缺陷與裂紋的來源。此外，與熔模铸造（IC）件或金屬注射模壓（MIM）件相比，溫鍛件不僅能獲得高強度的流線型內部金屬組織，而且外形尺寸更精確，表面質量更好。然而，在常規生產條件下，獲得高質量的溫鍛件是不容易的。 根據上述理由，本研究的目的是通過溫鍛醫療用植入件的多層次分析方法，建立一個損傷預測模型，使得在模具製造之前，即可優化溫鍛工藝，提高材料的可鍛性，預先完善毛坯及中間工步的設計。這種多層次分析方法可以更有效地改善損傷的預測精度。所提出的損傷預測模型將建立在以不可逆過程熱力學為基礎的連續介質損傷力學之上，採用多層次分析方法，為溫鍛生物相容性合金（BCAs）提供可行性設計。該方法將微孔密度因子與損傷準則相耦合，可對塑形斷裂與損傷演變過程進行更精確的預測。本研究採用不銹鋼與鈦合金作為毛坯材料。一個包括兩級（微觀多晶粒結構及宏觀剛粘塑性連續介質結構）的多層次分析模型將建立起來。基於各向同性的包括微觀特性與宏觀行為的多層次有限元分析模型將被開發出來。具有微聚焦/納米聚焦的X线計算機斷層儀器將被用來採集圖像並跟蹤微細裂紋的產生與擴展。為了更好地進行層次變換，在多層次分析中將採用一個新穎的三維代表體元（RVEs）統計方法來定義微孔和裂紋。微層次下的微孔與裂紋實驗數據將用來取代傳統中的材料均質假設模型。從而，一組綜合考慮微孔與裂紋的膨脹、交互作用、形核過程的損傷演變方程將被開發出來。最終結果是通過本項研究成果來試圖生產出更可靠、質量更高的低成本生物相容性合金（BCAs）部件來，從而對與醫療用植入件（MDI）有關的部門與人員產生積極的影響。

511511.label: Realisation of objectives
511511.value: 1. A specific warm-forging (WF) tooling was designed for the trial fabrication of a specified MDI component. A basal thumb implant, which is used widely in MDIs, served as an example for the tooling design. The similar WF tooling design as well as the temperature control and monitoring system can be referred to the WF study of the Mg camera casing mentioned in the published paper [Chan, Lu, 2014]. The presented Mg-based alloy was biocompatible and temperature dependent. Thus, it was used as a preliminary attempt to investigate the tool chilling and the control of tool temperature, which could greatly influence the overall design of WF tooling system for MDI. The tooling consisted of upper and lower dies and was able to be installed onto a newly developed WF system, including a 160-ton mechanical press, an induction heating furnace, a temperature controller, and an infra thermal camera (FLIR Thermal Vision A20M). The upper die was equipped with load cells to measure the forming load during the WF process. Circular heaters were inserted into each die component, enabling the heat-up of the whole die set directly with the electric power supply. In addition, the specimen materials, stainless steel SS316L and Ti-based alloy Ti6Al4V, were heated by induction heating to the desired temperature (i.e., 800 ºC) and then placed into the lower die for WF. The temperatures of the component and the tooling were fully monitored by the infra-red thermal camera to ensure a more accurate temperature control leading to a more reliable outcome of properties whenever the thermal mechanical tests were carried out for the selected specimens. Details of this similar but modified WF tooling system for MDI made of SS316L and Ti-based alloy Ti6Al4V will be mentioned in the paper entitled "In-process monitoring tooling system with adaptive temperature control for warm-forging non-axisymmetric medical components", which will be prepared and submitted to the International Journal of Machine Tools and Manufacture. 2. A non-destructive, high-resolution X-ray CT system (i.e., GE Phoenix Nanotom CT/ YXLON FF35 CT system) was employed to investigate the initiation and evolution of micro-voids/cracks inside the cylindrical specimen at each deformation stage. Several selected regions of the specimen were scanned and their 3D CT images were captured by the digital image processing tool integrated with the system of VGStudio MAX 2.2. The comparison of relative pixel intensity values was adopted to separate various objects in the images. Two phases of the testing specimen, micro-defects and alloy material, were investigated. The effect of micro-defect geometry on the mechanical properties and formability in macro scales was monitored simultaneously, and the damage evolution of the specimen detected by the X-ray CT system was compared with the FE simulations for verification. For details, refer to the papers [Lu, Chan, 2015; Chan, Lu, Yu, 2015]. 3. A specific homogenization method, based on the concept of representative volume element (RVE), was employed to establish a critical linkage between the phenomenological damage parameters and micro damage evolution. The structure of the RVE, i.e. the shape, the spatial distribution, and the volume fraction of micro voids/cracks inside the specimen, had been depicted from the CT scanning and image processing. The damage was quantified by the relative area of the volume of micro-defects on the focused region. The stress-strain relation with the damage variables could be expressed; details are to be found in the paper [Chan, Lu, Yu, 2015]. 4. The damage evolution of the specimen, up to material instability or even rupture, was simulated and calculated using the continuum damage mechanics (CDM). The flow stress data of the specimen at elevated temperatures was obtained by the uniaxial compression test. Other mechanical properties, such as yield strength, ultimate tensile strength and maximum elongation at different strain rates were also acquired. Those experimental data had been employed to establish the material constitution model and to predict the damage evolution. The FE package ABAQUS was employed to investigate the multiscale damage-based failure of the specimen during the WF process. The FE analysis, under the consideration of damage-based constitution and failure model, was encoded as a user-defined material subroutine to simulate the process. Several types of void fractions for the RVE were simulated. The predicted results, in terms of the compressive and tensile stresses between the physical experiments and FE simulations, were expected to have a good agreement. Partial results related to the stress-strain behaviour of SS316L at room temperature have been published in the paper [Chan, Lu, Yu, 2015]. The findings regarded the progressive damage behaviour of a porous biocomposite have been included in the paper [Tsui, Tang, Wang, Chan, 2012]. The damage prediction of SS316L at room temperature have been reported in the prepared papers entitled “Micromechanics-based damage model for failure prediction in cold forming” and “Multiscale analysis of deformation in metal damage prediction”, which have been submitted to the Materials Science & Engineering A (under review) and 23rd International Symposium, Plasticity, Damage & Fracture 2017 (accepted) respectively. Those results and findings have laid down a solid foundation of the damage prediction for biomaterials and could be further extended to biocompatible alloys under WF process. However, the objective 4 is not fully achieved, an in-depth discussion of the material constitution model and the prediction of the damage evolution of biocompatible alloys under WF are going to be described in the manuscript entitled “Multiscale damage-based failure prediction in warm forging biocompatible alloys for implantation and traumatology”, which will be prepared and submitted to the International Journal of Plasticity. 5. The specific component of MDI (basal thumb implant), after WF with tailor-made tooling, was produced to validate the proposed multiscale damage-based failure prediction model. Some critical positions of the component were investigated. The flow stress of the SS316L at desired WF temperatures and different strain rates have been published in the paper [Kong, Chan, 2015]. The damage variables determined from the proposed multiscale technique were used in the CDM approach to simulate the material degradation during the process. The stress-strain responses, failure locations, and damage evolutions of the specimens under tensile and compressive deformations at different strain rates were identified numerically using the proposed multiscale damage approach. More details of the multiscale damage-based failure prediction model applied on the specific MDI component after WF forging process will be prepared and submitted to the International Journal of Plasticity entitled “Multiscale damage-based failure prediction in warm forging biocompatible alloys for implantation and traumatology”.

511511.label: Major findings and research outcome
511511.value: The developed multiscale damage-based failure model was employed for failure prediction in warm forging biocompatible alloys (SS316L and Ti6Al4V). The uniaxial compression and tension tests were carried out to derive the material parameters for FE simulation. It was observed that the strain rate had little influence on the elastic modulus of the material at the same temperature. However, remarkable rate-dependence and strain-hardening effects were found at different strain rates. For details, refer to the papers [Chan, Lu, 2014; Kong, Chan, 2015; Lu, Chan, 2016]. The average size and volume fraction of micro-defects for the specimen were identified through a micro-focus high-resolution X-ray CT system. With the critical linkage between the micro-macro scales, corresponding 3D RVE models were reconstructed. The results indicated that different sizes of RVE models tended to exhibit a similar trend of micro-defects distribution, i.e., following a normal distribution. The 3D RVE models were simulated using ABAQUS to compute the stress distribution and damage evolution during the WF process. It was found that the stress increased with increasing tensile deformation and the stress around the micro-defects exhibited greater values than the other regions, especially for the smaller micro-defects. It was also found that the limit strain and the yield strength of each RVE model decreased with the increase of volume fractions of micro-defects. For details, refer to the papers [Lu, Chan, 2015; Chan, Lu, Yu, 2015]. The stress-based damage model has been applied firstly on a porous biocomposite, details refers to the paper [Tsui, Tang, Wang, Chan, 2012]. Further, the multiscale damage model was implemented into ABAQUS via the UMAT subroutine for damage prediction in WF biocompatible alloys for MDI. WF experiments for the specific MDI were also carried out to evaluate the effectiveness of the developed damage model. A specific and modified WF tooling system has been developed to carry out those related experiments, whereas a simpler but similar design tooling design together with the temperature control and monitoring system can be referred to that WF study of the Mg camera casing [Chan, Lu, 2014]. More details of the damage-based failure model applied on the MDI component after WF process will be prepared and submitted to the International Journal of Machine Tools and Manufacture entitled " In-process monitoring tooling system with adaptive temperature control for warm-forging non-axisymmetric medical components" and the International Journal of Plasticity entitled “Multiscale damage-based failure prediction in warm forging biocompatible alloys for implantation and traumatology”.

511511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
511511.value: This study has demonstrated successfully the effectiveness and advantages of the developed multi-scale damage model, which was able to predict the deformation behaviors and damage evolution accurately in WF biocompatible alloys at elevated temperatures. This method and technique could be applied further to other warm forming processes of biocompatible alloys for fabricating the critical and high value-added MDI. This could result in a significant impact on relevant manufacturing sectors and users of MDI, particularly patients and surgeons, due to the extreme necessity to release rather critical psychological stresses of those suffering due to the uncertain service life of MDI and the high-cost reimbursements caused by medical emergencies. In addition, the critical linkage between micro and macro scales, X-ray CT techniques, RVE reconstructions, constitutive equations, and CDM damage models could be developed further and/or improved for other materials. The modified damage-based constitution and failure models could then be compiled as a user-defined material subroutine into FE package for failure prediction.

511511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
511511.value: Warm forging (WF) is an attractive manufacturing process, because it can produce components with denser structures, better dimensional accuracy and surface quality. It has been used widely for producing high-security products, such as MDI. However, almost defect-free components may not be easily to achieve in general practice, and the capability of semi-empirical damage models seems unable to effectively predict problems involving microscopic deformation and localised failure. Therefore, a predictive method of multiscale damage-based failure analysis in WF was proposed, enabling more accurate prediction of the ductile fracture and damage evolution under a micro porosity density factor coupled damage criterion. Stainless steel and Ti-based alloys were selected as the specimen materials in this study. A multiscale finite element (FE) analysis, based on the concept of the representative volume element (RVE), was then developed to link the microscopic characteristics with the macroscopic behaviours. A micro-focus X-ray CT system was employed to capture images and trace the evolution of micro-damage. The experimental data of the actual voids and cracks in the microscopic scale were then used to replace the traditional uniformity. Subsequently, the damage evolution relating to the expansion, interaction and nucleation of voids and cracks could be predicted and further verified experimentally.

511611.label: Project Title(Chinese)
511611.value: 新和可重用腳手架系統的穩定及二階分析與設計

511611.label: Project Objectives
511611.value: This project will use and extend the new type of element for stability analysis, named as the element of pointwise equilibrium polynominal element with initial imperfection developed by the applicant and his student a decade ago for highly nonlinear analysis, for checking of stability of slender steel skeleton like scaffolds so that end eccentricity can be considered as well. This element will be extended with end eccentricity to account for the effects of eccentric force arisen from eccentric connections. Formulation of a practical design method based on the elasto-plastic and large deflection effects for slender skeletons will be developed in this project. Recognising P-DELTA and P-delta effects are dominatant, initial imperfections for re-used scaffolds material yielding are also needed to be included since they affect the maximum elasto-plastic buckling load and the post-buckling behaviour. Dynamic effects are also required for refined analysis since loads, like laying of pre-cast concrete beams and concreting loads, are dynamic in nature and their effects have not been properly assessed. Although this elasto-plastic analysis may not be directly useful for daily design of steel structures under normal loads, they are important for visualising the collapse behaviour of a structure which refers to structural behaviour after buckling or failure of the first few members, which will be of great academic and practical interest. Apart from the availability of a reliable and robust numerical tool for stability analysis, methods to account for deteriorating structural resistance due to increasing imperfections from repeated loads, lack-of-fit tolerance for members for the purpose of easy fitting of scaffold units and for magnitude and directions of global and local imperfection are developed so that a reliable and sustainable design method for slender frames and scaffolds can be formulated and used in practical design. Testing of module of scaffolds will be carried out with structural response compared against the computer buckling analysis. This effort is to confirm the accuracy and reliability of the design method to be developed.

511611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
511611.value: Hundreds of people died in construction accidents due to scaffolding collapse in different countries. OSHA (Occupational Safety & Health Administration) reported an average of 4,500 scaffolding collapses every year in USA alone. Our current analysis and design method for this structural system are inadequate, especially for re-used scaffolding units which are very common in practice but design method does not account for this and various effects on structural stability of scaffolding like lack of fit between scaffold units, out-of-plumbness and member out-of-straightness. As permanent structures are theoretically loaded to their design load once every 50 years as their design live, scaffolds are always loaded to a high proportion of their ultimate design loads during construction that leads to structural fatigue from enlarged imperfections. Recently, the proposer successfully proposes his method for design of scaffolds and investigation of collapsed scaffolds and tower cranes. He has also put this new method to the code of practice for structural uses of steel 2005 used by all structural engineers in Hong Kong (www.bd.gov.hk). In this project, the important parameters as end eccentricity and imperfections for new and re-used scaffolds are assessed and it aims at reducing the casualty rate of scaffolding systems and thus save human lives. Surpirsingly there does not exist a rational design method for re-used scaffolds even though they are widely used in renovation of old buildings and in construction of new structures for supports of workers and other weights. 511811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
511811.value: Open biomedical literature database, PubMed, have long been archiving the essential information about the scientific texts, including their titles and abstracts. The findings obtained from experiments and clinical trials were reported in the abstracts, in which the associations between the values of biomedical concepts (e.g. blood pressure) and the diseases (e.g. coronary heart disease) or the survival after treatments (e.g. chemotherapy) could be found. However, these associations were implicitly embedded as unstructured biomedical terms in the abstracts. Text mining could be applied to extract these diagnostic/prognostic associations from PubMed and compute their probabilities. Patient similarity is a novel research topic, which has not been thoroughly explored in bioinformatics. The computation of patient similarity takes into the account the alignment of biomedical concepts contained in two health records. Biomedical ontology databases, such as Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine - Clinical Terms (SNOMED-CT), provide not only the definitions and classification of biomedical concepts but also their hierarchical relationships (“is-a”) curated by the biomedical experts. The overall alignment of two health records could be computed using these relationships. However, two records will be aligned without considering their association to a particular disorder or post-treatment survival if only ontology is used. Incorporation of text-mined diagnostic/prognostic associations into the derivation of patient similarity is the novelty of this study and the success will promote the clinical relevancy and usefulness of patient similarity. The research team proposes to establish a scoring system supported by the biomedical ontology databases and the text mining of PubMed literature database. The similarity score combines sub-scores individually computed using the independent ontology databases. The ground truth of patient similarity is generally defined as the disease, the post-treatment survival or the clinical endpoint that both patients of interest have or don’t have. The sub-scores will be calibrated using the ground truth of the training dataset. The proposed scoring system will be applied to search health record database for similar patients and will contribute in three aspects. First, the retrieved similar records provide reference cases for supporting clinical decision on the query case. Second, the biomedical concept profiling of the query and retrieved records facilitates the comparative analysis for identifying the key concepts in diagnosis or prognosis. Third, a panel of similarity scores will be provided for each record pair when multiple scoring systems are trained using multiple ground truths (e.g. atherosclerosis, Alzheimer disease and 1-year survival after chemotherapy). 開放的生物醫學文獻數據庫，醫學文獻檢索系統，長期以來收集和貯存科學文本的基本信息，包括它們的標題和摘要。文本摘要報告實驗和臨床試驗獲得的發現，其中可以找到生物醫學概念（如血壓）和疾病（如冠狀動脈心臟疾病）或治療後倖存（如化療）之間的關聯。然而，這些關聯隱藏在論文摘要的生物醫學術語中。文本挖掘可用於從醫學文獻檢索系統提取這些診斷或預後的關聯和計算它們的概率。 病人相似性是創新的研究課題，在生物信息學中一直沒有得到徹底探討。病人相似性的計算考慮到兩個電子病歷中生物醫學概念的比對。生物醫學本體數據庫，如臨床醫學術語，不僅提供了生物醫學概念的定義和分類，更表達了它們的層次關係。利用這些關係可以計算兩個電子病歷的整體比對。但是，如果只使用本體論，比對後的兩個電子病歷並未考慮到其與疾病或治療後倖存的關聯。加入文本挖掘及疾病或治療後倖存的關聯是這項研究的新穎之處，研究的成功將促進病人相似性的臨床應用。 研究小組建議設立一個評分系統，該系統的計算利用生物醫學本體數據庫和醫學文獻數據庫的文本挖掘。相似性總得分結合從個別本體數據庫所得分數。相似基準一般定義為病人是否患有特定的疾病，得到治療後倖存或臨床治療終點。訓練數據集的基準使個別分數標準化。建議的計分系統將應用於從電子病歷中搜索類似病歷，將有助於以下三方面。首先，檢索相似的病歷提供參考個案用作支持臨床決策。第二，生物醫學概念綜述的檢索便於比較分析，確認診斷或預後的關鍵概念。第三，當已知道一系列的相似基準，如動脈粥樣硬化，老年癡呆症和化療後一年生存率，計分系統將對每對病歷提供一系列的相似性分數。

512511.label: Project Objectives
512511.value: Upward lightning, including rocket-triggered lightning, usually involved an upward positive leader (UPL) that originates from a grounded-based object, such as a tall building or a tower, and propagates toward charged clouds overhead. As the leader channel extends upward, the charge in the leader channel causes electric field changes that can be measured on ground. Meanwhile, time-resolved optical observation may provide the information of leader spatial development. With this in mind, the general equations describing the relationship between leader charge density, leader current, propagation speed, and leader-caused electric field changes will be developed. With the equations developed in above, specific algorithm/approach for estimation of the leader channel charge density based on simultaneous electric field and high-speed camera observations of the leader will be established. Based on the proposed algorithm, adequate observations of electric field, high-speed camera as well as leader current of UPL in artificially triggered lightning will be arranged and implemented, in cooperation with the Laboratory of Lightning Physics and Protection Engineering (LPPE) of Chinese Academy of Metrology Science. The LPPE has been carrying out rocket-triggering lightning experiment in southern China since 2006 and the experiment will be continued for coming five years at least. With the data obtained and algorithm proposed, evolution of the leader charge density and leader current will be estimated for UPL in the triggered lightning. The extent of consistency of calculated leader current, leader channel brightness, and measured leader current will be used to validate the adequacy and effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. It is expected that the leader charge density obtained will be a function of the leader channel height and so does the leader propagation speed. Analysis and interpretation of these results will be done and possible circumstance for initiation and propagation of the UPL will be discussed.

512511.label: Realisation of objectives
512511.value: This project aims to develop an approach for computing the leader charge density and leader current based on simultaneous close-distant electric field and high-speed camera observations of upward leaders in classically-triggered negative lightning. There are 5 project objectives, all of them have been achieved. Specifically: a) In the first project year, based on thorough review of previous studies we succeeded in developing a new approach for retrieving the spatial and temporal evolution of the charge and current of UPL in triggered lightning, and specific algorithm was proposed. With these efforts, the Objectives 1 & 2 had been achieved. b) In the second project year, with the proposed algorithm and the data of electric field and high-speed camera record obtained for an artificially triggered lightning discharge in China, the evolution of charge and current of two upward positive leaders in the triggered lightning discharge were successfully retrieved. The retrieved leader currents were then compared with the measured leader channel brightness and leader currents, indicating the proposed approach is a physically sound and practically effective tool for indirectly measuring the leader charge and current. The results were reported at 31st International Conference on Lightning Protection held on 2-7 Sep. 2012, Vienna, Austria, with a title of “Evolution of Charge Density and Current of Upward Positive Leaders in Triggered Lightning”. With these efforts, the Objectives 3 & 4 had been achieved. c) In the third project year, based on the results in previous year the proposed approach was further generalized and refined. And a trial of applying the proposed approach to downward negative leaders was done. The results showed that the proposed approach were suitable to both upward and downward leaders in either artificially triggered or natural lightning discharges. The results were summarized as a paper entitled “Evolution of line charge density of steadily-developing upward positive leaders in triggered lightning”, published on Journal of Geophysical Research - Atmosphere., Vol.118, doi:10.1002/jgrd.50446, 2013. By these efforts, the Objective 5 therefore the whole project objectives had been achieved. d) Besides, we also extended our research into the assessment of lightning-caused electromagnetic environment in metro traction cars and buildings for the purpose of lightning protection scheme analysis. Relevant results were reported at XV International Conference on Atmospheric Electricity held on 15-20 June 2014, Norman, Oklahoma, USA, with a title of “Assessments of lightning protection scheme for a metro traction power system and lightning-caused electromagnetic environment inside a carriage” and at 9th Asia-Pacific International Conference on Lightning held on 23-27 June 2015, Nagoya, Japan, with a title of “Assessment Method for Building Electromagnetic Environment under Direct Lightning Strike and Its Easy Application’.

512511.label: Major findings and research outcome
512511.value: Firstly, we have developed a new approach for retrieving the temporal and spatial evolution of the charge density and the current of a steadily-developing upward leader based on ground observations of electrical fields and high speed camera images. The approach was applied to two upward positive leaders initiated by a classical rocket-triggered lightning before the wire disintegration. For a period of a few milliseconds, for the upward leader segments developing above altitude about 200 m, we obtained the leader speed, calculated the leader charge density and the leader current. For the two leaders, both the leader speed and the charge density, hence the leader current, showed a trend of increase as the leader propagated upward. There was a good consistency in the variation trend between the calculated leader current and the leader channel brightness. The leader current calculated agreed well with the current measured at the channel base, indicating that our proposed model for retrieving the leader charge density is effective and reliable. The major results were disseminated at ICLP2012 [Conference paper 1] and published in Journal of Geophysics Research [Journal paper 1]. Secondly, based on above approach, trial application of the proposed approach to downward negative has been done. With the measurements of electrical field change and leader spatial developments with a broadband interferometer system on ground, the evolution of charge and current for the two downward negative leaders in triggered lightning has been retrieved. For the channel section of about 300 m to 800 m above ground, which was in the air and above the triggering wire, the leader speed showed a trend of decreasing as the leader descending, with an average of 2.8 x 10^5 and 4.5 x 10^5 m/s respectively, for the two leaders. While the line charge density showed a trend of increasing as the leader descending, with the range being from - 0.01 to - 0.1 mC/m for both leaders. The results were reported at APL2013 [Conference paper 2], ICAE2014 [Conference paper 3] and ICLP2014 [Conference paper 5], respectively. Thirdly, we have also performed the assessment of lightning protection scheme and lightning protection electromagnetic environment for a metro traction system and a building under a direct lightning strike. The results were reported at ICAE2014 [ Conference paper 4] and APL2015 [Conference paper 6], respectively.

512511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
512511.value: With the proposed approach, we successfully obtained the leader charge density and the leader current for two upward positive leaders based on the camera and electric field observations of the leader. The retrieved leader currents are well consistent with the measured current, indicating the proposed approach is reliable and applicable. By modifying the proposed approach, we also succeeded in retrieving the leader charges and currents of two downward negative leaders based on interferometer and electric field observations. This means that the proposed approach may lead to an indirect leader current measuring technique via camera or interferometer and electric field measurements on ground, which well be one of our research direction in future. Besides, we found that the leader speed, charge density and current show a trend of increase as the leader propagate forward for both the upward positive leaders and downward negative leaders we studied, which are generally consistent with model predictions in literature. Therefore, the proposed approach provides us a useful and easy way for validation of various leader modeling theories, which will be another research direction for us in future.

512511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
512511.value: Cloud-to-ground (CG) lightning poses treats to objects and human beings on earth. A CG is generally initiated by a leader that originates from a cloud and propagates downward or a ground object and propagates upward. Knowing properties of the leader is essential to mitigation of the lightning disaster. However, the information obtained so far is focused on the properties of leader propagation and leader-caused electric field change. Little information on the leader charge and current has been obtained, mainly due to that there is no mean to measure directly the charge density. In this study, we have successfully developed a new approach for retrieving the leader charge density and current based on simultaneous close-distant electric field and highly-time-resolved leader propagation image observations. Comparisons between the leader current retrieved with the approach and that measured at the channel base for two upward leaders in triggered lightning show that the approach is reliable. The approach may be further developed into an indirect leader current measuring technique, which will be no doubt a very helpful tool for us to understand the mechanism of lightning initiation.

To meet this need,the proposed study aims to investigate the surface generation of 3D-structured surfaces by using CCUP.Hence,a model-based simulation system will be established for the modelling of the surface generation and the optimization of the polishing strategy in the CCUP of 3D-structured surfaces.The development of the system will be based on a tool path generator for the 3D-structure surfaces togeter with a surface topography simulation model and an optimization model for the polishing strategy.The tool path generator will be used to generate the polishing tool path,based on the design of the 3D-structured surfaces,the polishing schedule,and the polishing parameters.The surface topography simulation model takes into account the cutting mechanics, material factors,kinematics and the dynamic characteristics of the polishing processes.The optimization model allows the optimum polishing strategy to be arrived at.The performance of the system will be evaluated through a series of simulation and polishing experiments.The surface generation of the 3D-structured surfaces will be characterized according to the surface quality and the functional characteristics of the 3D-structured surfaces.This proposed research if success will contribute significantly to a novel technology for the fabrication of 3D-structured surfaces. 三維結構型表面已廣泛應用于不同領域，如自粘性傳感器、全息產品中的復合透鏡、仿生學應用、生物醫學領域等。儘管已有對各類三維結構型表面如溝槽、格陣、棋盤花紋等的研究，但關於製造和加工這些表面的研究仍然任重道遠。超精密數控抛光是加工具有亞微米形狀精度和納米光潔度超精密自由曲面的有效技術和手段，但之前絕大多數研究工作則集中在表面粗糙度以及面形控制方面。建模及優化三維結構型表面生成的研究卻相對較少。雖然抛光加工技術歷史久遠，但抛光機理尤其是納米級的抛光機理的研究仍然不多。因此，有必要進行更深入的研究來理解超精密數控抛光中表面生成機理。目前，儅使用新材料、新的三維結構型表面設計以及新的加工設備時，這些表面的超鏡面及面形精度的實現仍很大程度的依賴于費時昂貴的反復試驗性途徑，有必要通過建模與仿真的方法和工具來仿真預測不同因素對超精密抛光中表面生成的影響。為此，本項目針對超精密數控抛光三維結構型表面的生成展開研究。將建立一個基於模型的仿真系統來實現超精密抛光結構型面的表面生成建模以及抛光策略優化。該系統將主要基於三維結構型表面抛光路徑生成器、 表面拓撲仿真模型以及抛光策略的優化模型等。抛光路徑生成器將基於三維結構型表面的設計、抛光計劃和抛光參數而生成抛光路徑。表面拓撲仿真模型將考慮到切削機理、材料因素、抛光過程中的運動學及動力學特性。優化模型則實現抛光策略的優化。該系統整體性能將通過一系列仿真及抛光試驗來進行評估。三維結構型表面生成將根據其表面質量以及功能特性來進行分析和評定。本研究的成功完成將為製造三維結構型表面提供一個新穎技術作出重大貢獻。

513211.label: Realisation of objectives
513211.value: Three-dimensional (3D) structured surfaces have been widely used in different applications such as self-adhesive sensors, compound lenses for holography in phonics products, bionic applications, bio-medical areas, etc. Although there have been some research studies on the manufacture and machining of 3D-structured surfaces, the research work is still far from complete. The current fabricating process, for instance, laser and etching, for 3D-structured surface generation are expensive and time-consuming. Computer Controlled Ultra-precision Polishing (CCUP) is capable of fabricating ultra-precision freeform surfaces with sub-micrometre form accuracy and surface roughness in the nanometre range. CCUP consists of Mechanical Polishing (MP) and Fluid Jet Polishing (FJP) processes. However, it is found that the material removal analysis is clearly a fundamental element in achieving the corrective polishing and optimization of the polishing process. Nowadays, the acquisition of tool influence functions still depends largely on the expensive trial-and-error approach when new materials, new surface designs or new polishing parameters are used. Although studies on polishing mechanisms and nano-mechanics are still sparse, there is a need for methods and tools for modelling and simulation which can simulate and predict the effect of different polishing parameters on the material removal characteristics and surface generation in CCUP. The research project aims to gain a better understanding of the materials removal characteristics as well as the surface generation mechanisms for the generation of 3D-structured surfaces by different types of CCUP technologies such as bonnet polishing and fluid jet polishing, etc. For Objective 1, a critical literature review was conducted for studying the evolution of research on various polishing technology, the updated state-of-the-art knowledge in the process, material removal characteristics and surface generation mechanisms, as well as the methods and tools for modeling and analysis of materials removal characteristics and surface generation for different types of polishing technologies. The review provides a solid foundation for him to develop the sound methodology in the research work. Hence, theoretical models have been built for predicting the material removal characteristics and the surface generation in both fluid jet polishing and bonnet polishing. Basically, the research work undertaken by the research team starts from the experimental study of factors affecting material removal characteristics and surface generation in ultra-precision polishing (Objective 1). The objective (2) was realized through a series of experiments based on different polishing strategies. The results provide a better understanding the effect of various factors and process parameters affecting the materials removal characteristics, surface generation mechanisms and polishing strategy for different polishing processes and they provide a solid foundation for his theoretical study and modelling work. The effect of polishing strategy on surface generation in CCUP of 3D-structured surfaces was also investigated through a series of experimental study For the realization of objective (3), a comprehensive computational fluid dynamic (CFD)-based erosion model has been built based on a combination of CFD simulation, erosion model, and experimental research which is able to predict the material removal characteristics and surface generation in fluid jet polishing (FJP). In the computational fluid dynamic simulations, an Eulerian-Eulerian-Lagrangian method is used which treats the water and air as an Eulerian phase and the particles as Lagrangian particles. The coupled discrete phase model (DPM) and the volume of fluid (VOF) model are used to describe the multiphases in the FJP process. This CFD model also presents the application of the model, together with the level set method, to describe the slurry/air interface in the commercial finite element analysis package FLUENT. After solving the stream flow characteristics, the motion of individual particles is also calculated in order to obtain more accurate predictions of the trajectories of individual particles impacting on the surface. The predicted results are used to integrate with the developed erosion model for the prediction of the material removal characteristics. Hence, the polishing path planning is determined based on the desired surface integrity of the optical surface to be generated using the data of the material removal characteristics. The performance of this model has been successfully verified through a series of spot and pattern polishing tests as well as simulation experiments (Objective 4). The results demonstrate the technological merit of the theoretical model which makes the material removal characteristics and surface generation of the FJP to be more predictable and better explained. Moreover, a multi-scale theoretical model has been successfully built (Objective 3) for predicting and characterizing the material removal characteristics and surface generation in bonnet polishing based on contact mechanics, kinematics theory, abrasive wear mechanism, as well as the relative and cumulative removal process of surface generation. The multi-scale theoretical model attempts to capture much of the basic physics of the polishing process including the tool radius, polishing depth, head speed, precess angle, pad topography, polishing time, particle shape, slurry concentration, and the mechanical properties of the pad and workpiece. For Objective (4), the technological merit of the model has been realized through a series of spot and pattern polishing tests as well as simulation experiments. The results show that the relative and cumulative removal process is a key surface generation mechanism in bonnet polishing. Based on the results of spot and pattern polishing experiments, the multi-scale material removal model is found to predict well for the material removal characteristics under various polishing conditions. The originality and significance of this research lies in the provision of CFD-based modelling of the material removal characteristics and surface generation for fluid jet polishing and multi-scale modelling of the material removal characteristics and surface generation for bonnet polishing. The successful development of the theoretical model helps greatly to make the CCUP process more predictive, so as to further optimize the manufacturing process for different work materials without the need for costly trial and error polishing tests. Moreover, this is the first of its kind in which the deterministic model has been successfully built which acquires much of the basic physics of the polishing process. This contributes significantly to form the theoretical basis for the better understanding of the polishing process. On the whole, the research work undertaken by the research team demonstrates sustainable research effort for addressing some key issues in modeling and analysis of materials removal characteristics and surface generation in computer controlled ultra-precision polishing (CCUP) of 3D-structured surfaces. Basically, all the objectives have been successfully addressed in this research project. The outcome and results of the project not only provides a better understanding and well explanation of the materials removal characteristics and surface generation mechanisms for FJP and bonnet polishing processes but also contributes significantly to the state-of-the-art of new methods and tools for theoretical modeling and prediction of materials removal characteristics and surface generation in CCUP which make the CCUP processes to be more predictable.

513211.label: Major findings and research outcome
513211.value: Computer Controlled Ultra-precision Polishing (CCUP) based on fluid jet polishing (FJP) and bonnet polishing (BP) are complex processes which rely heavily on the planning of the process steps in terms of the use of the polishing conditions and polishing fluid on specific materials being cut (Cheung et al., 2012, Cheung, Kong and Ho, 2012 and 2014). This project attempts to conduct a theoretical and experimental study of material removal characteristics and surface generation in CCUP of 3D-structured surfaces. Firstly, Taguchi trials were conducted to identify the optimal level of combination and the significance of the individual operational parameters in FJP (Cao and Cheung, 2016a and 2016b, Cao, Cheung, and Ren, 2016, Cao et al., 2016, Ho et al., 2016) and BP. Hence, a series of experiments was performed to investigate the effects of the process parameters on the material removal characteristics in FJP as well as the material removal mechanism in BP. Secondly, a comprehensive computational fluid dynamic (CFD)-based erosion model (Cao, Cheung and Kong, 2016, Cao, Cheung and Ren, 2016) was developed by a combination of CFD simulation, erosion model, and experimental research so as to predict the material removal characteristics and surface generation in FJP. The predicted results are used to integrate with the developed erosion model for the prediction of the material removal characteristics. In the third part, a multi-scale theoretical model was established for predicting and characterizing the material removal characteristics (Cao and Cheung, 2016a) and surface generation (Cao, Cheung and Zhao, 2016) in BP based on contact mechanics, kinematics theory and abrasive wear mechanism. Specifically, the pressure and velocity distributions are determined based on the kinematics theory and contact mechanics at the macro scale, and the pad topography which affects the contact ratio and hence the material removal rate at the micro scale, while the micro- or nano-sized abrasive particles scratch the surface at the nano scale. Experimental results show that the theoretical model predicts well that the material removal amount. A pattern test was also conducted to validate the surface generation model. In this project, a Ph.D. student has been trained and graduated. Up to present, the research team has published 7 refereed journal papers and 3 papers have been presented in refereed international conferences. Some of them were published in prestigious SCI journals such as International Journal of Mechanical Sciences, Wear, Precision Engineering, etc.

513211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
513211.value: There are some topics which are worth further study as follows: (i) The material removal model would be further enhanced by taking into account the effect of curvature on the material removal characteristics. This is important for better predicting the form accuracy of ultra-precision surfaces being polished. Moreover, the established theoretical models of the material removal characteristics will be incorporated into the capability of the tool path planning and the optimization of the dwell time. They will be integrated into the model-based simulation system for the simulation and optimization of the surface generation in the CCUP process. There is a need for further research into the model-based simulation system to further enhance the capability of the models and systems so that they are able to cater for more factors which affect the surface generation. (ii) Polishing is a multi-stage process and the surface generation is usually realized by a series of polishing process steps. The surface generation in the current polishing process step will be affected by that of the previous polishing process steps. As a result, process chain modelling and analysis for computer controlled ultra-precision polishing of optical freeform surfaces should be further studied to optimize the polishing process.

513211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
513211.value: Computer Controlled Ultra-precision Polishing (CCUP) based on fluid jet polishing (FJP) and bonnet polishing are enabling processing technologies which are capable of fabricating ultra-precision freeform surfaces with sub-micrometer form accuracy and surface roughness in the nanometer range. Nowadays, the achievement of superior mirror finish and form accuracy still depends largely on the expensive trial-and-error approach when new materials, new designs of the 3D-structured surfaces or new machine tools are used. The research work undertaken by the project team demonstrates sustainable research effort for addressing some key issues in modeling and analysis of materials removal characteristics and surface generation in FJP and bonnet polishing of 3D-structured surfaces. In the project, a Ph.D. student was trained and graduated. Seven refereed journal papers have been published while three conference papers have been presented in international conferences. The outcome and results of the project not only provides a better understanding and well explanation of the materials removal characteristics and surface generation mechanisms for FJP and bonnet polishing processes but also contributes significantly to the state-of-the-art of new methods and tools for theoretical modeling and prediction of materials removal characteristics and surface generation in CCUP which make the CCUP processes to be more predictable.

513611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
513611.value: Open kitchens have been designed for many small residential units in tall buildings in Southeast Asia. This open design, without enclosing the kitchen with fire resisting walls has failed to comply with building fire safety codes in some places including Hong Kong. Performance-based design was adopted and it is specified that gas cookers with flames are not allowed. Additional fire protection systems such as water mist suppression or dry powder systems have to be provided above the kitchen stoves. However, kitchen fire physical hazards with and without fire resisting walls were not studied thoroughly. A survey on fire load density indicated that large amounts of combustibles are stored in small residential units. Experiments with electric induction cookers indicated that the cooking oil in a frying pan can be ignited within ten minutes. Fire would spread out from the open kitchen to burn up all stored combustibles in the residential unit to give a big fire. Authorities, developers and owners are now having deep concerns on whether such open kitchens in tall buildings are really safe when there is an accidental fire. Aspects of open kitchen fires both with and without fire resisting walls in small residential units of tall buildings will be studied in this project. Fire dynamics will be applied to study the possibility of flashover onset upon igniting the cooking oil and the consequences of the burning of adjacent combustible items. New fire phenomena, including the air pumping effect of the plume and flame whirling motion in an open kitchen will be explored. Fire models including both fire zone and Computational Fluid Dynamics models will then be used to study these new scientific phenomena. All results are applied to better understand the fire spread from the open kitchen to other parts of the unit to provide a post-flashover fire both in the residential unit, and outside the unit in other parts of the tall building. Full-scale burning tests will be carried out to confirm identified scenarios; to justify the model predictions; and to observe any new physical fire phenomena. Performance of the specified suppression systems including water mist and dry powder suppression systems will be evaluated. Venting by fire drainage is proposed and evaluated for the protection provided against open kitchen fires. New gas-solid composite particles developed recently will also be evaluated to check whether better suppression of an early cooking oil fire is achieved. 在東南亞各國家的高層建築中，開放式廚房廣泛設計於小型住宅單位內。但該種開放式的，無封閉防火牆的廚房並不符合包括香港在內等多地消防規範。性能化設計中規定該類廚房中不允許出現明火煤氣類廚具，並必須在廚具附近額外安裝細水霧或乾粉滅火系統。但是關於廚房火災的物理現象及防火牆存在與否的影響並未有相關的認真的研究。相關火災負荷調查顯示出，該類小型住宅單位中通常儲存有大量的可燃物品。而有關電磁爐火災實驗則證明，鍋中的食用油竟在10分鐘內燃燒。如果該火源從開式廚房中蔓延而出並點燃小型住宅單位內其他可燃物，則很可能發展成為嚴重火災。目前對於高層大廈中小型住宅單位內開放式廚房的火災安全性已受到相關當局，地產發展商及業主的關注。 本專案將會對高層大廈中小型住宅單位內開放式廚房有無防火牆的兩種火災情況進行研究，並運用火災動力學對轟燃及觸發室內火災的可能性進行詳細分析。對於該過程中的新火災現象，包括羽流中的氣湧和火旋風等將會分別進行模型研究。其結果有助於徹底瞭解開放式廚房火災的蔓延特性，以及高層大廈中的小型住宅單位及其他區域轟燃後的火災特性。為了進一步確定火災場景並對比模擬結果，以及直觀瞭解相關的新型火災現象，全尺寸燃燒模型實驗也將開展。相關滅火系統的特性，如細水霧系統，乾粉滅火系統等，也將進行實驗評估。並將對開放式廚房火災中的排煙系統進行分析，以及對新型氣固複合顆粒材料於早期食用油火災是否具有阻歇效果進行檢驗。

513611.label: Major findings and research outcome
513611.value: Key outcomes are as follows with references cited in Section 8 of Part C: 1. Open kitchen design in tall residential buildings in Asia-Oceania regions [J1,J2] storing large quantities of combustibles was found to be very hazardous in this project. A long post-flashover fire can result under the accidental scenario identified. The heat release rates [J3] of burning combustibles in residential buildings were modelled. 2. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) was applied to study kitchen fire and fire drainage integrated with ventilation design. Air pumping effect [J6] of the plume and flame whirling motion in an open kitchen were investigated by CFD. Flame swirling induced by a fire at the top of a kitchen stove was studied numerically. Fire drainage design with ceiling vents was observed to create an internal fire whirl under appropriate conditions. CFD modeling of sprinkler effect on kitchen fire was studied. Recommendations on the design of kitchen ventilation systems were made. 3. Experiments were carried out to study kitchen fires triggered by cooking oil with multiple fire sources under natural ventilation. Combustion characteristics were observed with average heat release rate, burning time and average oil mass flux investigated [J4,J8] experimentally. A mathematical model on heat transfer from the flame to the pan surfaces was developed. Modeling results [J8] were verified with experimental observations. 4. Open kitchen fires without fire resisting walls in small residential units of tall buildings were explored. Fire dynamics was applied to study the possibility of onsetting flashover upon igniting the cooking oil and burning adjacent combustibles. Nonlinear dynamics was used to study flashover in an example open kitchen fire. A mathematical model taking the fire compartment as a thermal system with a two-layer zone model [J7] was developed and programmed in symbolic mathematics software. Control parameters for flashover to occur have been identified for providing fire safety to open kitchens. Further, using façade materials with good thermal insulation was confirmed [J9] to give shorter time to flashover. 5. The effectiveness of a new clean fire extinguishing agent, degradable 2-bromo-3,3,3- trifluoropropene (BTP), in extinguishing liquid fuel fires was studied. Bench-scale experiments were conducted in a chamber with natural ventilation. Results showed [J5] that less than 60 g of BTP could extinguish all liquid fuel spray fires successfully. The extinguishing mechanism of how BTP suppress liquid fuel fires was also investigated 6. The fire scenario of dipping frozen food with high water content into a hot oil pan even without a naked flame is confirmed to be very hazardous in an open kitchen by experimental studies using canola oil. Vapour explosion can give a big flame volume. The fire developed rapidly with the upper part of the mock-up kitchen filled with flame. The flame could even extend to over 2 m out of the enclosure with strong radiative heat fluxes. 7. Fire safety associated with residential building with open kitchen was studied. Some results compiled from this project are very useful in providing appropriate fire protection. The requirement of installing sprinkler in an open kitchen of small residential units was reported to the Fire Safety Committee of the government Buildings Department.

513611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
513611.value: Many open kitchens were provided in small residential units in tall buildings in the Asia-Oceania regions. This open design without enclosing the kitchen with fire resisting walls is very dangerous. Although gas cookers with naked flames are not allowed, there is possibility of having big fires or explosion by dipping frozen food into a hot oil pan. Vapour explosion would spread fire out from the open kitchen and burn up all stored combustibles in the residential unit to give a postflashover fire. The fire can spread upward to involve rooms at the higher level. Wind effect will facilitate the fire spread. The big fires observed in this project from dipping frozen food into a hot oil pan even with an electric induction cooker should be further studied in more details. Exploring the associated fire dynamics in upward fire spread will be useful to determine appropriate fire protection systems. All these observations can be the objectives for future research projects.

513611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
513611.value: Fire hazards of open kitchens without fire resisting walls for small residential units in tall buildings in the Asia-Oceania regions were studied in this project. Fire dynamics with fire models was applied to study the possibility of onsetting flashover upon igniting the cooking oil and the consequences of burning the adjacent combustible items. Full-scale burning tests were carried out to confirm the identified scenarios; to justify the model predictions; and to observe new physical fire phenomena. Air pumping effect of the plume and flame whirling motion in an open kitchen were explored. Performance of the specified suppression systems including water mist and dry powder suppression systems were evaluated. Venting by fire drainage was evaluated for protecting against open kitchen fires. New gas-solid composite particles developed recently were demonstrated to be able to suppress an early cooking oil fire. Although gas cookers with flames are not allowed, there is a possibility of having big fires by dipping frozen food into a hot oil pan. Vapour explosion would spread fire out from the open kitchen and burn up all stored combustibles in the residential unit to give a big fire as demonstrated in this project.

513711.label: Project Objectives
513711.value: To clarify and empirically estimate how population, wages and property prices change with respect to productivity shocks at city level. Seventy cities in China Mainland of different elasticities of housing supply are chosen for study. To clarify and empirically estimate how population, wages and property prices change with respect to productivity shocks at district level. Fifty teritary planning units (TPU) in Hong Kong are chosen for study, to which the housing prices of the corresponding housing estates under the Rating and Valuation Department Price Indices for Popular Developments will be mapped with. From our empirical estimates, to derive urban policy implications which help policymakers better achieve sustainable and balanced urban growth.

To clarify and empirically estimate how population, wages and property prices change with respect to productivity shocks at district level. Fifty teritary planning units (TPU) in Hong Kong are chosen for study, to which the housing prices of the corresponding housing estates under the Rating and Valuation Department Price Indices for Popular Developments will be mapped with.

513711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
513711.value: In fast expanding economies like China and Hong Kong, the dynamics of the transformation of economic growth to urban growth are inadequately explored. A boost of productivity in a city may bring about an increase of labour demand, which in turn will trigger new housing needs. Depending on the elasticity of housing supply in a city, the productivity shock may be transformed into different formats in term of urban growth. In general, the elasticity of housing supply of a city is determined by the physical characteristics (e.g. boundary, barriers and land stock etc.) as well as the underlying institutional factors (e.g. planning law, demographic and socio-economic policies etc). In cities where the elasticity of housing supply is high, productivity shocks may induce city expansions. Housing prices and real wages could be left intact as a result. On the contrary, in cities where the elasticity of housing supply is low, an increase of productivity may cause escalation of both housing prices and real wages. In reality, a combination of the results is expected given the complexities and the very different natures of cities. Without a thorough understanding of the interplays between productivity shocks, housing prices and wages in cities, policy makers are made difficult as far as achieving sustainable urban growth is concerned. A city cannot be regarded as a sustainable one if housing prices keep on rocketing while real wages can never keep up the pace. Likewise, an overly expanded city may induce urban sprawl and brain drain problems due to the worsening environment and suppressing real wages. As far as academic contribution is concerned, this study attempts to fill the gap by producing empirical studies in two fascinating economic entities in the Far East. Following Glaeser, et al (2006), this project will carry out two independent sets of panel data analysis – one at city level that studies 70 cities in Mainland China, and another one at district level that investigates 109 statutory planning areas in Hong Kong. It is expected that the city level results are not necessarily the same with those in the US. This is largely due to the institutional constraints on labour mobility in China, which is attributed to the unique demographic and welfare policy - the hukou system. 這項目主要研究生產力的激增與實質工資和樓價的關系。跟據Glaser et al (2006) 的回歸分析方法，這項目將研究七十個中國主要城市，及五十個香港城市規劃分區的數據，嘗試歸納各城市及地區，如何將生產力的激增轉化成實質工資的增長，及可持續的樓市發展。

513711.label: Realisation of objectives
513711.value: This study attempts to study the interplays between productivity shocks, property prices and wages in the context of China and Hong Kong. We have engaged a Research Associate and a number of student helpers to collect data of more than 70 cities in China and 109 Territorial Planning Units in Hong Kong. A series of panel data analysis, desktop research and literature review have been conducted to achieve the three key research objectives. One journal article arising from this study has been published. Two articles are under review and one is under preparation. One of those articles is in the final stage of review and we are expecting acceptancy within a month or two. We have identified three key sources of productivity shocks for the current study. First, change of property right structure will boost manufacturing production and hence may increase property rental value. Second, net inflow of population to a region provides new labour force and hence may increase productivity and housing prices. Third, increase of degree holders in a region will foster the development of knowledge economy and hence may increase productivity, housing prices and real wages. Specifically, we have stipulated three research objectives for this study. The following is a summary how and to what extent the research objectives have been achieved. 1. The first objective is 100% achieved by conducting two panel data analyses of 35 major cities in China between 2002 and 2011 and 25 Guangdong cities between 2003 and 2010. Data have been obtained for 70 cities in China. However, due to the data structure, we have screened and merged some of the city level raw data. So eventually the two analyses embrace 60 cities in China. 2. The second objective is 100% achieved by conducting a panel data analysis of 32 Territorial Planning Units (TPU) in Hong Kong. Data have been collected for more than 50 TPUs in HK. Due to the data structure, we have screened and merged the raw data of some TPUs. Eventually, the analysis embraces 32 TPUs. 3. The third objective is 100% achieved by elaborating some policy proposals, implications and evaluations in the papers for publication and review.

513711.label: Major findings and research outcome
513711.value: 1. The first key source of productivity shocks we had identified is property right structure. A natural experiment has been conducted in the Shenzhen Special Economic Region in order to investigate whether a change of property right structure will bring about increase of productivity and hence property prices. A cross-sectional data analysis reveals that a vast difference in term of manufacturing productivity is observed for factories located in state-owned lands vis-à-vis collective-owned lands. Industrial value produced on collective-owned land is RMB6.6 billion less than that on state-owned land per sq km. In term of rental value, collective-owned land fetched 57% less than that of the state-owned land (Choy et. al 2013). 2. The second key source of productivity shocks is net inflow of population to a region. A panel data analysis of 25 Guangdong cities (Choy et. al., under review), however, found that there is no significant impact of net inflow to housing prices. A 1% increase of net inflow will only bring about 0.003% increase of housing prices. It may be due to the high elasticity of housing supply among the provincial cities. 3. The third key source of productivity shocks comes from increase of degree holders in a region. A fixed effect panel data analysis of 32 major cities in China (Choy and Li, under review) found that a 1% increase in the ratio of highly educated to the total population would lead to 1.1% increase of housing price. Nevertheless, increase of degree holder population in a region actually hampers pay rise. The same panel data analysis reveals that a 1% increase in the ratio of highly educated to the total population would lead to 0.467% decrease of real wages. It may be attributed to the hukou policy of major cities in China. On the one hand major cities embrace highly educated labour force, but on the other hand those immigrants may find their lives too competitive because their pay rises can never commensurate the increase of living costs. In intraregional context, in districts where housing supply elasticity is less, a 1% increase of degree holders will bring about 1.2% increase of housing prices in Hong Kong (Choy and Zhou, under preparation).

513711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
513711.value: In the course of pursuing the research objectives, we found that there is a unique factor in China which might have played a pivotal role to interpret intraregional and interregional migration and housing prices – the hukou system. Hukou is a population control policy in China Mainland. Each city has her own hukou policy. Holders of hukou will enjoy certain social rights in the city such as education and medical benefits while the flowing population of migrant workers do not. We find that there exists an intriguing migration pattern among the first, second and third tier cities. A filtering up process may be undergoing in Chinese cities. Rural migrants may wish to move to third tier cities. Hokou holders in the third tier cities may also want to move to second tier ones. Likewise, second tier city’s hokou holders may want to move to first tier cities. Tracking of the migration pattern in China may shed new light to interpret mobility, housing prices and wages. A number of funding proposals have been developed as a natural extension of the current study.

513711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
513711.value: This study attempts to better understand the interplays between property prices, wages and three key sources of productivity shocks, namely improvement of land titles, inflow of immigrants and increase of degree holders in a region. We manage to quantify and measure the real effects through a series of statistical analyses. We found strong positive relationships between property prices and obtaining formal land titles. Positive relationship is also observed between housing prices and increase of degree holders. However, we do not find a significant relationship between inflow of immigrants and housing prices. Nevertheless, higher proportions of well educated population may suppress real wages increment in cities. It infers that new degree holder immigrants in mega Chinese cities may face with great pressure of increasing housing prices and sluggish pay rise. These results pave the way for scholars and policy makers to pursue issues on sustainable development in cities. These issues include but not limited to population control, education policy, provisions of housing as well as land and city management.

514311.label: Project Title(Chinese)
514311.value: 基于布状微小FRP筋的钢筋混凝土结构的外贴补强技术

514311.label: Co - Investigator(s)
514311.value: Prof Leung, Christopher K Y Prof Teng, Jin-guang

514311.label: Project Objectives
514311.value: To achieve an in-depth understanding of the bond-slip behaviour of a single FRP micro-bar embedded in ECC and the tension-stiffening behaviour of an FSS/ECC overlay; To investigate bond behaviour between an FSS/ECC overlay and concrete and clarify the bond force transfer mechanism; and To understand the flexural behaviour of RC beams strengthened with an ECC-bonded FSS system through laboratory tests and advanced finite element (FE) modelling.
rows: To achieve an in-depth understanding of the bond-slip behaviour of a single FRP micro-bar embedded in ECC and the tension-stiffening behaviour of an FSS/ECC overlay;
To investigate bond behaviour between an FSS/ECC overlay and concrete and clarify the bond force transfer mechanism; and
To understand the flexural behaviour of RC beams strengthened with an ECC-bonded FSS system through laboratory tests and advanced finite element (FE) modelling.

514311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
514311.value: Use of externally bonded fiber reinforced polymer (FRP) composites to strengthen existing reinforced concrete (RC) structures has become a very popular technique over recent years. This technique has a number of advantages over traditional ones due to the high tensile strength-to-weight ratio and excellent corrosion resistance of FRP composites. However, FRP composites have their own weaknesses including the poor fire performance (such as the flammability smoke generation and rapid degradation in mechanical properties) of the polymer matrix (usually an epoxy resin) and the low compatibility in permeability between an epoxy bonding agent and the concrete substrate. The former poses certain limitations on the indoor applications of FRP strengthening technique while the latter can compromise the durability of an epoxy-bonded FRP system, particularly in a hot humid outdoor environment. For these reasons, recent attempts have been made to replace epoxy with a cementitious matrix material. The present project aims to develop a more advanced bonded system based on FRP strand sheets (hereafter “FSSs”) and engineered cementitious composites (ECCs) for the strengthening of RC members. FSSs are composed of properly spaced FRP micro-bars of 1~2.5 mm in diameter, which are aligned into a sheet form using transverse threads for convenient handling and deployment. ECCs represent a new generation of fibre-reinforced cementitious materials with pseudo-strain-hardening and significant multiple cracking properties. The proposed advanced bonded system is expected to possess greatly improved fire and ultraviolet (UV) resistance, ductility and durability than externally bonded FRP reinforcement. The use of FRP micro-bars in an FSS also avoids the premature failure and inefficient utilization of fibres in the existing cement-based systems, such as dry fibre sheets/textiles or FRP grids bonded with a cementitious material. Besides, the proposed system improves the bond performance, shortens the construction time, and minimizes the thickness of the strengthening layer. The proposed advanced bonded system represents a significant forward step in the development of the externally bonded FRP strengthening technique as well as the traditional cement-based overlay technique. Upon the completion of this project, an in-depth understanding of the complex interfacial behaviour in an ECC-bonded FSS system and advanced modeling approaches will be established; a preliminary design approach for the flexural strengthening of RC members will be developed to facilitate practical implementation. The project will lead to an attractive new method with a great potential for practical applications and open up a new area of research for the relevant international scientific community. 由于FRP材料的轻质高强以及耐腐蚀性能，利用外贴FRP增强钢筋混凝土结构技术已经得到广泛应用。但FRP材料由于使用有机树脂（通常是环氧），也存在防火及耐久性等方面的一些自身弱点。这些弱点尤其影响了外贴FRP增强技术对放火性能重视在建筑结构补强中的进一步推广。近年来，许多研究者正试图利用水泥基材料来代替环氧树脂，开发出了两种水泥基粘贴补强技术: (1) 水泥基材料粘接连续纤维或纤维网格技术；(2) 水泥基材料粘贴FRP栅格技术。 本研究基于微小FRP筋（直径为1到2.5毫米）织成的片材（简称FSS），拟开发一种先进的外贴粘接补强技术。在该技术中，超高韧性水泥基材料ECC将作为FSS的基体和粘接材料。ECC具有显著的微小多裂缝分布特征以及应变强化特性。和FRP外贴增强技术相比，拟开发的技术将在防火及防紫外线老化性能得到大大增强，补强体系的整体延性和耐久性亦会大大提高。使用微小FRP筋亦可避免上述两种水泥基粘贴补强技术中的易发生界面剥离和纤维利用效率低的缺点，同时可提高施工速度，优化补强层厚度。本项目将着重于阐明FSS、ECC以及已有混凝土结构的多层次的界面应力传递机理，并初步建立基于FSS和ECC的开发补强技术的设计理论。本项目 的成功完成将显著改善现有的FRP外贴技术和传统的增厚补强技术，对相关研究领域的学术发展会有积极的影响并将进一步推动FRP复合材料在土木工程中的应用。

514311.label: Realisation of objectives
514311.value: All the objectives set out for this project have been completely achieved. Engineered cementitious composites (ECC) were developed and their performance under normal and elevated temperature were studied. The bonding performance of FRP bars embedded in the ECC matrix was also studied. It was noted during the execution of the project that use of FRP in the grid form leads to a more effective and convenient solution than use of FRP in the sheet form as the reinforcing material of ECC matrix. Therefore, in the latter stage, FRP grids were used instead for development of the proposed new flexural strengthening technology. A comprehensive experimental program was organized which covered the following three major items: (1) Experimental study on the tensile behavior of FRP reinforced ECC composites; (2) Bond tests on the interfaces between concrete substrate and FRP reinforced ECC composites; and (3) Flexural tests on reinforced concrete (RC) beams strengthened with FRP-reinforced ECC composites. Through the above-mentioned experimental programs and advanced finite element modeling with deployment of material and interface constitutive laws at different levels, an effective flexural strengthening method for existing RC beams has been established and an in-depth understanding has been achieved on the interfacial and structural behaviors of RC beams strengthened with FRP-reinforced ECC composites.
