514311.label: Major findings and research outcome
514311.value: (1) A new technology has been sucessfully established for strengthening of existing reinforced concrete (RC) structures through the use of fiber reinforced polymer (FRP)-reinforced engineered cementitious composites. The developed inorganic strengthening technology possesses greatly improved fire and ultraviolet (UV) resistance, ductility and durability than externally bonded FRP reinforcement. (Refer to Output 1 in Part C) (2) ECCs with sufficient strength and ductility have been developed. A good understanding on their mechanical properties under normal and elevated temperatures has been achieved. (Refer to Output 1 and Output 6 in Part C) (3)Theoretical models have been proposed to simulate the bond behavior of FRP reinforcement in a cementitious matrix. (Refer to Output 3 and output 4 in Part C) (4)A tension stiffening model has been developed to simulate the behavior of FRP-reinforced ECC composites and a bond model has been developed to simulate the behavior of the interface between FRP-reinforced ECC and concrete substrate. (5)It was found that the intermediate crack-induced debonding failure can be sucessfully supressed by the developed strengthening technique so that the high strength of FRP can be fully utilized. A comprehensive finite element model has been developed to simulate the structural behavior of RC beams flexurally strengthened with FRP-reinforced ECC composites. Untill now five international journal papers have been published on this research project. One more international journal paper is under review and three more journal papers (related Outcomes 4 and 5)are under preparation.

514311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
514311.value: There are two potential further development of this research project: (1)To apply the developed high performance FRP reinforced ECC composites for new construction, such as using them as permanent formworks to develop high performnace building structural component in new constructions. The principle investigator of this project is seeking support from industry for joint research on this topic with the aim to transfer this technology to the building industry in Hong Kong and Mainland China. (2)A scientific issue remains unsolved for the proposed strengthening technology. It was found that the proposed technology can prevent sucessfully the IC debonding in the strengthened RC beams. However, a reliable anchorage needs to be provided at the ends of the strengthened beams to prevent the plate-end debonding failure. How to design a safe and cost-effetive end anchorage system is an important issue for further reserach.

514311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
514311.value: Recently using externally bonded fiber reinforced polymer (FRP) composites to strengthen existing reinforced concrete (RC) structures has become a very popular technique. This technique has a number of advantages over the traditional overlay strengthening method due to the high tensile strengthto-weight ratio and excellent corrosion resistance of FRP composites. However, FRP composites have their own weaknesses mainly associated with the poor fire performance of the polymer matrix and the low compatibility between the epoxy matrix and the concrete substrate, which have compromised their attractiveness in many applications. In this project, a new strengthening system has been developed which combines the advantages of both the FRP strengthening and the overlay technologies. In the system innovative engineered cementitious composites (ECCs)are used as the adhesive material to bond FRP reinforcement to concrete structures for improved strength and ductility, fire resistance and durability. Upon the completion of this project, an in-depth understanding of the complicated interfacial behaviour in the proposed strengthening system has been achieved. The project has led to an attractive new strengthening method for concrete structures with a great potential for practical applications in Hong Kong and the rest of the world.

514411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
514411.value: The use of direct expansion (DX) air conditioning (A/C) systems is advantageous because they are simpler, more energy efficient and generally cost less to own and maintain. However, currently most DX systems are equipped with single-speed compressors and fans, relying on on-off cycling to maintain indoor dry-bulb temperatures only. This results in an uncontrolled equilibrium indoor humidity, leading to a reduced level in the thermal comfort of occupants, poor indoor air quality and low energy efficiency. Although there have been extensive research efforts in developing various controllers for DX A/C systems for the simultaneous indoor air temperature and humidity control, including the extensive research work carried out by the Principal Investigator and his team, each controller developed / reported would have its own inadequacy. In this proposed project, a novel controller for the satisfactory simultaneous control of indoor air temperature and humidity in terms of control accuracy and sensitivity, through combining the complementary merits of various currently available advanced control / modelling algorithms, such as Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Fuzzy Logic Controllers (FLC) will be developed. The novel controller, which has a high potential of commercialization, can avoid the inadequacies of all current available control methods to ultimately resolve the problem of the simultaneous control of indoor air temperature and RH using DX A/C systems. The novel controller will be validated through extensive comparative lab-based controllability tests and its practicality demonstrated through on-site comparative annual performance evaluation. The successful carrying out of the proposed project would help achieve better thermal comfort for occupants, improved IAQ and reduced energy use. The long-term significance of the proposed project is its contribution to sustainability through reducing energy use for air conditioning in buildings while improving the thermal comfort of building occupants, and to the advancement of DX A/C technology. While the project outcomes are expected to be globally applicable, they will be particularly useful to Hong Kong where DX A/C systems are widely used and dehumidification using DX A/C systems has always been challenging. 直接膨脹式（直膨式）空調由於其結構簡單，能源效率高以及安裝維護費用相對低廉，能為用戶帶來諸多便利。然而，大多數的直膨式空調都只配備單速壓縮機，僅僅依賴簡單的開停循環來控制室內溫度。這使得室內濕度沒有受到任何控制，從而降低了用戶的熱舒適度，室內的空氣質量以及空調器的能源效率。雖然大量的研發工作致力於開發各種形式的直膨式空調控制器來同時控制室內溫濕度，這其中也包括項目負責人及其團隊所進行的大量研究工作，各個已經開發或者見諸於文獻的控制器都存在著一定的不足。 在目前所倡議的項目中，一個用於同時控制室內溫濕度的新型控制器將被開發，通過結合當今各種先進的控制方法，例如人工智能網絡，模糊邏輯控制器等的優點，將可確保其有令人滿意的控制敏感度和控制精度。這一具有高度商業發展潛力的新型控制器，將避免目前已有控制方法的所有不足，從而最終解決利用直膨式空調來同時控制溫濕度這一難題。大量的對比試驗將用來驗證此新型控制器的控制能力，而其實際的使用效果也將通過全年的實地安裝使用數據加以展示。 本項目的成功開展將可提升空調用戶的熱舒適度，室內的空氣質量以及降低空調器的能耗。而本項目的長遠效應將可促進直膨式空調技術的長足發展，在提升建築內熱舒適環境的同時，降低建築的空調耗能。雖然本項目的成果具有全球的適用性，對於大量使用直膨式空調，以及利用直膨式空調來進行除濕總是很具有挑戰性的香港來說，本項目的成果尤其具有實用價值。

514411.label: Realisation of objectives
514411.value: The objectives as stated in the original proposal have been realized. Firstly, A novel control algorithms for simultaneously controlling indoor air temperature and relative humidity using speed DX A/C systems has been developed, by introducing two interim control variables, i.e., sensible heat ratio (SHR) and the total cooling capacity (TCC) in order to decouple two highly coupled control loops for temperature and humidity; Secondly, a novel controller, based on the novel control algorithm developed, has been developed where the complementary merits of Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC) have been incorporated. Thirdly, extensive controllability experiments have been carried out to test the novel controller, in terms of its control accuracy, sensitivity and energy use performance. Experimental results have demonstrated that the controller so developed can achieve the expected control performances in terms of control accuracy and sensitivities. In addition, the controller's practicality has been demonstrated through a DX air conditioner controlled by the novel controller and its energy performance was compared to those of a typical on-off controlled DX air conditioner, suggesting a higher operating efficiency. In addition, as a by-product of the controller development, the inherent characteristics of a variable speed DX air conditioner linking its SHR and TCC at varied inlet air states to the DX air conditioner, have been experimentally studied. This has paved the way to facilitate the controller development when de-coupling the two coupled control loops.

514511.label: Project Objectives
514511.value: The interface between the catalyst and the CNT will be studied by ab initio and classical atomic calculations and simulations. This study should lead to a deep understanding of the interface between CNT and catalyst particle and the various shapes of catalyst particle observed in experiments. Beyond the conventional catalysts normally used, Fe, Co, Ni and their alloys, there are many new catalysts that have been employed in CNT synthesis recently. Since a growing CNT interacts with the catalyst through their interface, CNTs with lower interfacial energy should be synthesized more easily. Therefore we plan to explore systematically the interfacial energies between various SWNTs and many types of catalyst. The knowledge and data obtained in this study should lead to methods of catalyst design for chiraly-selected CNT synthesis. A hybrid Molecular Dynamic/Kinetic Monte Carlo (MD/KMC) Simulation method will be developed and used to simulate the growth of defect-free CNTs. By this study, we expect to explore the origin of CNT chirality and the parameters that dominate tube chirality. The newly developed method will be used to exam the assumption that energetically preferred CNTs have the highest probability of being nucleated.

514511.value: 除了少数几种情况之外, 催化剂在碳纳米管的生长中是必不可少的. 在碳纳米管的生长过程中, 催化剂是通过催化剂和碳纳米管的界面感知碳米管的螺旋结构的. 所以理论上存在通过调节催化剂-碳纳米管的界面结构以实现碳纳米管结构选择性控制的的方法. 在这个申请书中, 我们申请用理论方法, 包括第一原理计算,分子动力学模拟和蒙特卡洛模拟, 研究实现碳纳米管螺旋度控制的可能机制与方法. 第一步,我们将通过第一性原理计算和分子动力学模拟研究催化剂和碳纳米管的界面结构. 通过这一研究我们将会得到关于催化剂和碳纳米管的结构信息; 第二步, 我们将利用第一性原理计算系统研究不同碳纳米管和不同催化剂的界面能. 因为最稳定的界面将会更大的热力学记率存在, 所以这一研究将为我们实现碳纳米管的催化生长控制提供理论指导. 最后一步, 我们将会利用新的分子动力学-蒙特卡罗结合的方法检验这一假设的正确性. 这一研究的成功将会使我们对碳纳米管的催化生长机制有更为深入的认识. 我们进一步期望通过这一研究提供几种控制碳纳米管生长的实验方法. 这将对碳纳米管领域的研究和应用产生深远的影响.

514611.label: Project Objectives
514611.value: Develop and test methods based on space-borne InSAR technology for determining key parameters of the QTP glaciers, including glacier areas, terminus positions, ice and snow flow rates and surface elevations, and the changes in the parameters. New InSAR approaches including Temporarily Coherent Point (TCP) tracking and TCP Multiple Aperture Interferometry (TCP-MAI) will be developed in the research. The InSAR results will be validated against, and integrated with those from SA and other techniques such as optical remote sensing to derive optimal measurement results. Carry out detailed investigation of 50-80 glaciers over the QTP to determine their key parameters (i.e., glacier areas, terminus positions, ice and snow flow rates and surface elevations) and the changes in the parameters over the past two decades. Glacier-wide mass balances will be estimated based on the measured glacier parameters. The glaciers to be studied will be selected by considering their geographical locations (i.e., good coverage of the QTP) and sizes (i.e., different sizes to obtain more representative results) and the quality and availability of the data (i.e., SAR, SA and optical remote sensing).

514611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
514611.value: 青藏高原及周圍地區的冰川是繼南極及格陵蘭之後世界第三大淡水儲存地。多個起源於這里的河流，包括長江及黃河，為這個區域（包括中國的大部分地區）至少5億人口提供生活用水。 觀測跡象顯示青藏高原的一些冰川自20世紀初開始退縮。然而，由於觀測數據非常粗略，關於這些冰川消失的速度以及預期完全消失所需時間的理解仍然具有很大得不確定性。例如，在喜馬拉雅及喀喇崑崙地區的約20,000個冰川中，只監測了約15個以研究它們的變化（(Inman, 2010)。最近非常具有爭議性的政府間氣候變化小組（IPCC）關於喜馬拉雅山冰川消失的報告是這些不確定性的有力佐證(e.g., Cogley et al., 2010; Inman, 2010)。 本研究課題的主要目的是提供新的、更全面的冰川變化觀測數據。我們將利用兩個互相補充的大地測量技術，合成孔徑幹涉雷達（InSAR）及衛星測高（SA），研究過去20年青藏高原的冰川變化。我們將利用多個SAR及SA衛星數據研究多大量冰川，以確定它們在這段時間內的變化，以及它們的時間和空間變化規律。這些InSAR及SA觀測結果將與其它觀測結果（如光學遙感結果）相結合。我們清楚知道青藏高原的地表特征（如很多地區的陡壁）對InSAR及SA觀測具有很大的挑戰性。然而，過去的研究及我們的實驗結果表明這些技術在典型的青藏高原地區是可以獲得滿意的觀測結果的。我們將使用最好的數據處理方法，包括已有的及此課題發展的方法，如TCP點跟蹤及TCP與MAI結合的方法，以取得最優的觀測結果。 通過加深對於青藏高原冰川變化速率及它們空間和時間變化規律的理解，此項目的研究成果將充分補充已有的研究，幫助降低青藏高原冰川變化理解中的不確定性。 由於青藏高原冰川變化可能帶來巨大環境、經濟及社會問題，這些冰川的融化是科學界及社會大眾十分關心的問題。此項目一方面為理解這一重要問題提供科學依據，另一方面為政府的決策者提供重要的實測數據，幫助他們為冰川融化可帶來的巨大危害做好規劃和準備。香港的生活用水主要來自內地。青藏高原冰川融化可能為這個整個地區帶來巨大的環境變化。因此，這個研究課題與香港未來的發展密切相關。 Cogley, JG, Kargel, JS, Kaser, G, van der Veen, CJ (2010) Tracking the source of glacier misinformation, Science, 327, 522. Inman, M. (2010) Settling the science on the Himalayan glaciers, Nature, doi:10.1038/climate.2010.19.

514611.label: Realisation of objectives
514611.value: All the project objectives have been fully achieved. With respect to Objective 1, a set of innovative data processing models and algorithms have been developed for determining the various parameters of glaciers in the Qinghai Tibet Plateau (QTP), including the areas, surface topography and areal and volumetric changes. The new approaches have significantly advanced glacier mapping in the challenging mountainous environments. The accuracy that has been achieved with the new approaches has been unprecedented. An important breakthrough is the mapping of debris covered glaciers. It has been a task that has never been resolved properly in the past. Therefore, most of the debris covered glaciers have not been properly mapped. We developed a semi-automated method in this project that deploys data from radar and optical remote sensing and from topographic measurements for this purpose and the results from the method has been remarkably good. From our experiments, we have also seen that the Chinese Glacier Inventory contains significant errors. The QTP glacier areas have thus been overestimated by as much as 30%. This is an important discovery in terms of glacier research. With respect to Objective 2, we studied thousands of glaciers in three selected areas over QTP, the southeastern QTP, the central QTP and northwestern QTP. The number of glaciers studied was much more than that initially planned so that the results from the study are very reliable and interesting. We typically investigated based on data from radar and optical remote sensing, satellite altimetry and from topographic measurements, the glacier distributions, the changes of the glaciers over the time period covered by the datasets, the relationships of the glacier changes with the environmental conditions. Some interesting results have been achieved in the research. For example, it is found that the areas of some of the glaciers in central QTP have reduced over 10% over the past 15 years or so. It has also been found that the glaciers reacted differently to environmental changes. For example, the areas of some of the glaciers in Western Kunlun Mountains have been increasing instead of decreasing. Some good quality publications have been generated based on the research results. Some further publications are still being prepared.

514611.label: Major findings and research outcome
514611.value: 1. The project developed a series of approaches for mapping mountain glaciers and their changes based on a combination of data sources including optical remote sensing, radar remote sensing, satellite altimetry, and digital elevation models (DEM). The approaches developed represent some scientific breakthroughs.For example, we have provided a good solution for mapping the debris covered glaciers, a task that had been difficult to do until now with any remote sensing techniques. We can also better determine glacier changes due to climate changes. 2. We studied the recent change of glaciers over 2000-2011 in the Dongkemadi region in the central QTP and found clear evidence of glacier changes over the region based on optical remote sensing and satellite altimetry data (Ke et al., 2015a). The results show that the glaciers experienced notable recession in the last decade, at a linear shrinking rate of 0.21 square km (0.26%) per year in area and a thinning rate of 0.56 m per year. 3. The Western Kunlun Mountain region consists of 537 glaciers that are larger than 0.02 square km with a total area of 3137 square km in 2013. Out of these, 16 groups of glaciers covering an area about 1234 square km showed varying surface elevation trends ranging from −0.4 ± 0.20 m/a to 0.7 ± 24 m/a over 2003–2008. Analysis of the heterogeneity shows that such glacier dynamics were associated with local glacier parameters including altitude, aspect, glacier hypsometry and ice flow. (Ke et al., 2015b). 4. We derived a new glacier inventory for the southeastern region of the QTP (Ke et al., 2016). The inventory contains 6,892 glaciers that are larger than 0.02 square km, covering a total area of 6,566±197 square km. This new glacier inventory indicates that gross overestimation in glacier area (over 30%) in the previously published glacier inventories has been made.

514611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
514611.value: It will be very useful to study more glaciers in the QTP to have an overall understanding of the glacier changes in the context of global environment change. It is planned to apply for some further projects in this area to carry out the research.

514611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
514611.value: We developed some methods for mapping mountain glaciers in the Qinghai Tibet Plateau (QTP) and their changes over time due to climate change. This project has enabled us to make some breakthroughs in terms of the technology development and of the understanding of the trends of the glacier changes. Although QTP is far from Hong Kong, the glacier changes in QTP are related to the environment that could also impact Hong Kong. For example, they could affect the water supply of a large region including Hong Kong. They could also affect our sea level.

515111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
515111.value: Clothing thermal comfort is important, not only for functional clothing worn in extreme and hazardous environments where the protection provided by clothing could be a matter of life or death, but also for everyday clothing, since a primary function of clothing is to help maintain the thermal balance of the human body and create a sensation of comfort and well being. To optimize the functional design of clothing, it is necessary to have a clear understanding of the effect of clothing materials, garment design and fit on heat and moisture transfer through clothing. While abundant literature is available on the effect of the properties of clothing materials, the effect of garment design and fit is not well quantified and understood. The obvious way of investigating the effect of garment design and fit on comfort is to use wearer trials involving human subjects. Nevertheless, the results so obtained tend to lack consistency and accuracy and, furthermore, can expose human subjects to danger when conducting experiments under extreme conditions. Hence, it is highly desirable to have thermal manikins which can replace human subjects in such experiments. Although many thermal manikins have been developed around the world, the accurate simulation of human perspiration remains a major challenge. Existing sweating manikins, except for the one developed by PI’s group (viz. Walter), cannot ensure consistency in sweating over their entire bodies and over a prolonged testing period, as well as accuracy in the measurement of evaporative heat and water loss, and clothing moisture vapour resistance. Nevertheless, Walter also has shortcomings: it only resembles a male body and cannot simulate distribution of sweating over the different parts of the body. In the light of the above, it was decided to further develop Walter into a technology which will for the first time provide simulation of the female body shape and the distribution of sweating over the body surface as well as a method for measuring the localized thermal comfort properties of clothing. By accurately measuring both localized and overall thermal comfort properties of clothing using the male (Walter) and female (nicknamed as Wanda) version of the sweating manikins and by quantifying the clothing air gap profiles, using 3D body scanning technology, the proposed project will provide a quantitative understanding of the relationship between the air gap profiles and the clothing thermal comfort properties, which is essential in optimizing the functional design of clothing. 服裝的一個主要功能是幫助人體維持熱平衡，因此服裝熱舒適性能是至关重要的。这对于在極端和危害環境裡穿著的功能服裝，尤为重要。 要優化服裝的功能設計，必须明白服裝材料与設計对熱和濕氣透過衣物的传递机理。 虽已有相當多服裝材料方面的研究，服裝設計与合体度的作用不好量化和确定。 最直接的研究热舒適性的方法是人体穿著試驗。但此方法缺乏可靠性和準確性，在極端狀態下做試驗時，可能出现危險。 因此，有必要采用暖體假人。 雖然已有許多暖體假人，發汗模仿依然是一個难题。 目前，只有本小組研發的暖體假人(即 Walter)，能控制出汗並準確测试濕氣蒸发量和濕阻。 然而， Walter也有缺點： 它只類似男性身體，并且不能模仿不同的身體部位出汗的差异。 有鉴于此，本项目将利用Walter技术来研發女性出汗假人并模仿不同的身體部位出汗的差异，同时研發一种測量局部熱舒適性的技術。通过準確測量局部和整體熱舒適性，和使用三维人體掃描技術来定量衣物空氣与人体的间隙，本項目將对服裝設計与合体度对熱舒適性的影响有定量理解，有助于優化服裝的功能設計。

515111.label: Realisation of objectives
515111.value: We have achieved 100% towards the stated project objectives. We have accomplished the followings: For the first objective: • Developed a pattern for fabricating the skin of the female manikin-Wanda. After filling up the skin with water, the shape closely resembles a female body. • Developed male and female manikins of varying perspiration rates at different body parts using breathable fabrics of varying moisture vapor permeabilities. The new manikins better resembled the distribution of human perspiration at different body parts. Thermal properties of clothing measured using these new manikins are compared with those measured using the manikins with even perspiration rate around the body. For the second objective: • The hardware and software of the existing male manikin-Walter were modified to fit for the newly developed female manikin-Wanda. • The shape of the internal frame, heating and water flow system were altered to fit the female body shape. • The PID controls of the software were modified to fit the female manikin’s thermal inertia and heat loss. For the third objective: • Identified a specific type of heat flux sensor for attaching to different parts of the manikin body and developed a measurement system and protocol to measure the localized heat loss for determining the localized thermal properties. For the fourth objective: • Developed an experimental protocol to simulate a human subject exposing to a changing environmental condition. The existing manikin software is modified to enable the simulation of different metabolic rates and monitoring the transient responses of skin temperatures when the manikin is exposed to a changing environmental condition. For the fifth objective: • Investigated the effect of clothing microclimate volume and ventilation designs on the thermal comfort properties of clothing. The clothing microclimate volume was determined by scanning the unclothed manikin body and clothed manikin body.

515111.label: Major findings and research outcome
515111.value: • By using manikin tests and human subject wearer trials, we compared T-shirts of conventional design with T-shirts having a novel spacer and mesh structure in terms of thermal properties. It was found that a larger space (or greater microclimate volume) between the garment and the body skin surface with additional ventilation channels decrease thermal insulation (Rc) and evaporative resistance (Re) when the wearer in motion or under windy conditions. The work was published in Applied Ergonomics, Volume 48, May 2015, Pages 138–147. • By using the male body manikin-Walter and 3D body scanning technology, we conducted an experimental investigation on effects of air gap, wind, and walking motion on thermal properties of traditional Arabian Thawbs and Chinese Cheongsams. The results show that the relative changes of It and Re of Thawbs due to wind and walking motion are greater than those of Cheongsams, which provide an explanation of why Thawbs are preferred in extremely hot climate. This work is published in Ergonomics, DOI: 10.1080/00140139.2015.1111428, Published online: 14 Dec 2015. • Conducted a systematic investigation on the effect of clothing microclimate volume (CMV) on clothing thermal properties under windy conditions (<0.3m/s, 1m/s and 2m/s). It was found that (1) both thermal insulation (It) and evaporative resistance (Re) initially increase with the increase of CMV until reaching the maximum and after that further increase in CVM will result in a reduction in It and Re; (2) The CVM corresponding to maximum It is smaller under stronger windy conditions, meaning relatively tight-fitting garments are preferred for thermal protection in windy conditions; (3) At relatively low or no wind conditions, relatively tight-itting garments have greater permeability index. The manuscript of this work is under review by Ergonomics. • Compared the newly developed female manikin-Wanda with the male manikin-Walter in terms of heat loss, measured clothing thermal properties. It was found the curvaceous body shape of female manikin reduces the thermal insulation of the nude manikin, but add resistance to heat and evaporative resistance through the clothing ensembles.. The manuscript of work is under review by Applied Ergonomics. • Compared the male and female manikins with even perspiration rate around the body and those with uneven perspiration rates around the body in terms of heat loss, thermal insulation and evaporative resistance. A manuscript for this work is being prepared for publication.

515111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
515111.value: With the improved understanding on how clothing microclimate and ventilation channels affect clothing thermal properties, we can develop novel clothing designs and evaluate the effectiveness of new designs using the developed thermal manikins. With the newly developed female manikin-Wanda as well as the experimental protocol for measuring the localized heat loss and transient thermal responses, clothing (particularly female clothing) of various designs can be evaluated objectively under various conditions. We can also use these newly developed experimental techniques to better understand the effect of body motion and environmental conditions on heat loss from the human body and heat transfer through clothing.

515111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
515111.value: The newly developed female manikin-Wanda and the experimental protocol for measuring the localized heat loss and transient thermal responses provide objective and accurate experimental techniques for evaluating the comfort of clothing under various end use conditions. This is especially important to functional clothing used in extreme conditions, such as firefighter’s uniform, chemical and biological protective clothing. The knowledge gained from this study, particularly on how clothing microclimate and ventilation channels affect clothing thermal properties, provide insightful guidelines on the development of functional clothing for enhanced comfort. For example, it was found that a spRelative tight, but not snug fit may be preferred in functional clothing for greater permeability in low or no wind conditions and for greater thermal insulation in strong wind conditions.

516011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
516011.value: Three-dimensional (3D) negative stiffness textile structures are nonconventional fabrics that demonstrate unusual behaviors of decreasing force with an increase in deformation. When properly understood and integrated with the advanced textile fabrication technologies, this phenomenon can be exploited for special applications such as vibration isolators and damping materials used in transportation. The most important point to the realization of the negative stiffness of these fabrics is the proper design of the fabric architecture and its manufacturing process. A survey of the literature demonstrated that no work has been done in the study of this important phenomenon of textile materials. Therefore there is a need for a basic understanding of negative stiffness effect, mechanical performance and manufacturing process of such textile structures. More specifically, the project will deal with fundamental issues of the structure and performance of the 3D negative stiffness fabrics. Based on previous work done by the applicant, a special kind of 3D spacer textile structure will be developed to achieve negative stiffness based on the use of both elastic yarns and hollow monofilament as spacer yarns. Both theoretical and experimental studies will be conducted to study their negative stiffness behavior and mechanical performance. The nonlinear elastic model for the single hollow monofilament and the unit-cell model for 3D fabric structure will be established. The multi-scale approach and nonlinear elastic theory as well as the finite element method (FEM) will be used to analyze the negative stiffness behaviors and mechanical performance of 3D fabrics made of different elastic yarns and hollow monofilaments as well as structure parameters. As an example, the 3D negative stiffness fabrics with optimized structure design will be fabricated for vibration isolators and packing materials used in transportation 三维负刚度纺织结构属于非常规的纺织物。它们具有受力随变形的增加而减少的特性。当正确的理解和结合先进的纺织技术，这种特性能够开发用于一些特殊的应用，如隔振和交通用阻尼材料。使三维织物实现负刚度的关键是正确地设计织物结构和它们的制造工艺。文献分析表明还没有任何工作研究这种纺织材料的特殊现象。这样，有必要对这类织物的负刚度特性，力学性能和制造工艺进行研究。 具体地，该项目将研究三维负刚度织物的结构和性能的基本问题。基于申请者先前所做的研究工作和采用弹性纱和中空长丝作为间隔纱，一种具有负刚度的特殊的三维间隔织物将被开发出来。实验和理论研究将同时进行来研究这类织物的负刚度特性和力学性能。将建立中空单丝非线性弹性模型和三维织物结构单胞模型。多尺度方法，非线性弹性理论和有限元方法将用来分析由不同弹性和中空单丝以及不同结构参数制造的三维织物负刚度特性和力学特性。作为一个实例，用于隔振和交通用阻尼材料的三维负刚度织物将在优化结构设计后制造出来。

516011.label: Realisation of objectives
516011.value: Objective 1: This objective has totally been achieved. A new type of 3D fabric structures which could manifest quasi-zero and negative stiffness behavior were successfully designed based on knitted spacer fabric structures. In the first design, the hollow monofilament was suggested as spacer yarns to produce negative stiffness effect. However, after a preliminary study, it was found that the hollow monofilament was not suitable for this design concept due to two reasons. The first reason was that the hollow monofilaments which could be obtained from the market were generally used as fishing lines. These hollow monofilaments were too gross and stiff for knitting process. The second reason was that the elastic recovery property of the hollow monofilaments obtained was very low, making them unacceptable for spacer fabric use. Instead of using the hollow monofilament as spacer yarn, a new design of fabric structure was performed by using solid monofilaments as spacer yarns based on a comprehensive study of spacer yarns morphologies. With this new design, 3D spacer fabrics with quasi-zero and negative stiffness effect could be easily produced from available solid monofilament as spacer yarn and multifilament as outer layer yarn by using knitting technology. Objective 2: This objective has totally been achieved. A series of weft-knitted spacer fabrics with quasi-zero and negative stiffness effects in a special range of displacement under quasi-static compression were successfully fabricated with the use of computerized flat knitting machine by using elastic multifilament as outer layer yarn and solid monofilament as spacer yarn. Besides, a group of warp-knitted spacer fabrics with quasi-zero and negative stiffness effects were also fabricated using double warp knitting machine with six yarn guide bars. These warp-knitted fabrics fabricated exceeded our objective of this project. Objective 3: This objective has totally been achieved. The compression tests of both types of weft-knitted and warp-knitted spacer fabrics with positive, quasi-zero and negative stiffness were conducted under quasi-static and dynamic loading conditions. For the quasi-static compression tests, a tensile and compression device was modified by setting up two self-designed and fabricated compression plates. For the dynamic compression tests, an electromagnetic shaker was specially designed by us and built by a company in Taiwan to test vibration isolation behavior of these spacer fabrics since the vibration behaviors of these fabrics are mainly dependent on their stiffness. The effects of different factors including fabric structure parameters, yarn materials and testing conditions on the negative stiffness effect and vibration isolation performance were experimentally investigated in detail and the deformation mechanism of 3D fabric structure to achieve quasi-zero and negative stiffness effect was clearly understood from experiment. Objective 4: This objective has totally been achieved. The compression properties of 3D spacer fabric structure with quasi-zero and negative stiffness effect under quasi-static loading condition was analyzed using finite element method based on the precise geometry of a unit-cell structure obtained from a CT scanning and the deformation behavior in different compression stage was successfully simulated using ANSYS software. Meanwhile, the mathematical models were also established to analyze the vibration behaviors of 3D spacer fabrics under harmonic excitation conditions. Both analytic and numerical methods were used to solve the mathematical equations obtained from mathematical models and the effects of different factors which could influence the vibration behaviors of spacer fabrics were theoretically analyzed. Objective 5: This objective has totally been achieved. The results from both the mathematical modeling and finite element simulations of 3D spacer fabrics were compared with the experimental results obtained in both the quasi-static and dynamic loading conditions. The good agrees were obtained between the experiments and theoretical analyses. Both the finite element and mathematical models obtained were used to optimize the structure design of 3D spacer fabrics with different stiffness for vibration isolation.

516011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
516011.value: 3D negative stiffness textile structures are a type of 3D nonconventional fabrics in which their compression force decreases with the increase of compression displacement in a special range of deformation. In this research project, 3D textile structures with quasi-zero and negative stiffness for vibration isolation are designed and fabricated based on spacer fabric structures using both weft and warp knitting technologies. The compression properties and vibration isolation of these fabrics under quasi-static compression and harmonic excitation are experimentally and theoretically studied. Both the finite element and mathematical models are developed to understand their mechanical behaviors under these two loading conditions. The significance and value of the project is to provide a basic understanding on the structure characterization, design principle, fabrication method and mechanical performance of 3D quasi-zero and negative stiffness fabrics. Thanks to their unusual properties different from conventional 3D fabrics, these fabrics will enable new applications such as vibration isolation and packing materials for transportation, and many highly value-added and innovative products. The study will promote the new development of textile products using the latest concept and technologies to increase the competitive capacity of the Hong Kong textile and fashion industry.

516111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
516111.value: Driven by strong industrial demands and inspired by the environmental responsiveness of supramolecular entities, the reversible hydrogen bonding (HB) may be used as switch units to make shape memory polymers (supra-SMPs). Such switch units can both stabilize mechanical strain and endow low Water Vapor Permeability (WVP) in SMPs at low moisture contents when locked and lead to shape recovery with high WVP at high moisture contents when opened up, due to the association and dissociation of non-covalent bonds. The expected advantages of such supra-SMPs are: sharper transitions, higher sensitivity to moisture content and better controllability by using supramolecular switches than with traditional phase transitions in SMPs. Thus in the present project, a series of supra-SMPs will be synthesized using supramolecular HB entities. The resulting supra-SMPs will be characterized systematically including their moisture responsive shape memory effect (SME) and WVP controllability. Relationships between the structures and properties of Supra-SMPs will be studied both experimentally and theoretically using modeling and simulation. Textile applications of supra-SMPs will then be investigated particularly for WVP- controlling systems. SMPs have networks with switch units and netpoints. The switch unit is responsible for key features of the shape memory effect (SME), namely, deformability, fixity and strain recovery upon exposure to stimuli (responsiveness). The molecular design of SMPs has been focused mainly on constructing crystalline or amorphous phases as switch units in the past. It is understood that SMPs can not only memorize their original shapes but also have other attractive properties. One associated property is their responsive WVP due to stimulus sensitive free volume change in SMPs. The limitation with this material is that it is only responsive to heating usually hotter than body temperature while the need for moisture responsive apparel is widespread, particularly in sportswear. Although limited studies on water responsive SMPs with traditional phase transitions have been reported, they do not lead to materials with sufficient moisture/humidity responsiveness because of the small amount of water absorption from moisture. This original research will be the first to study the SME with humidity/ moisture sensitivity systematically in supra-SMPs using HB entities. Applications to WVP-controlling textiles provide a novel solution for meeting market requirements. It will represent a contribution to the development of supramolecular chemistry/physics for functional polymers, smart materials and textiles and reinforces its foundation for Hong Kong’s leadership in innovation of functional/smart textiles and apparel. 在工業需求的推動下和對環境響應的超分子现象的启发下，此项目拟采用可逆的氫鍵（HB）作为形狀記憶聚合物（超分子SMP）的開關單元。這種開關單元可以穩定機械應力，並賦予形狀記憶聚合物在低湿条件时为低透濕性（WVP），在高湿条件时为高透濕性。高湿条件下氫鍵單元的非共價鍵離解，導致形狀記憶聚合物发生从临时形变到初试形变的回复。這種新型超分子SMP預期的優點包括：更窄的轉变范围，对水份更高的靈敏度和更好的可控性。这种可控性是通過使用超分子开关機制而不是傳統的相變機制实现的。因此，在此項目中，将合成一系列的带可逆氫鍵的超分子SMP。所合成的超分子SMP将系统地检测多种特性，包括对水分和湿度靈敏的形狀記憶效應（SME）和WVP可控性。所合成的超分子SMP的結構和性質之間的關係將用實驗的方法和建模，仿真理論的方法进行深入研究。另外，超分子SMP在紡織品的應用也将進行研究，尤其是WVP的可控性。 SMP有開關單元和網絡节点。開關單元負責形狀記憶效應（SME）的主要特點，即，變形，固定性和刺激響應下的应变回复。 过去SMP的分子設計主要考虑构建結晶或無定形的高分子链段作为开关單元。已知地，SMP不僅具有能記住原始形狀的特性，同时也有其他吸引人的特性。比如刺激响應性自由體積的變化导致响應性WVP。用這種材料的限制是，它通常需要加熱到比體溫高的温度才能产生响應性，而对水汽响应性的需求是很普遍的，尤其是在運動裝领域。基于传统相變的水敏感型的SMP雖然已有零星的報導，但是因为从湿气中吸收的水分很少的缘故，这类材料尚未显示出足够的濕度響應。 该项目是第一個系统研究利用可逆氢健实现水汽，湿气敏感的超分子形状记忆效应的原創性研究。可控透濕性紡織品的應用为市場需求提供了一種崭新的解決方案。同时相关研究也將对超分子化學/物理在功能性聚合物，智能材料和紡織品领域的发展作出貢獻，並鞏固香港在創新型功能/智能紡織品和服裝领域的領導地位。

516111.label: Realisation of objectives
516111.value: For objective 1: (1) Materials: 2,6-dihydroxymethyl pyridine (DHMP) were purchased from Acros, hexamethylene diisocyanate (HDI), methylene diphenyl diisocyanate (MDI), 1,4-butanediol (BDO), dimethylformamide (DMF, HPLC Grade) and poly(4-vinyl phenol) (PVP) were purchased from Sigma Aldrich. MDI were kept at 50℃ oven and only upper layer liquid was used in experiment. All the rest chemicals were freshly used without further purification. (2) Synthesis of supra-molecular shape memory polymer (Supra SMP): The Supra-SMPs were synthesized with different hard segment contents. For example, DHMP (2.90g, 20.8mmol) were first solved in DMF (10mL) at 45℃ for 5 mins to get a transparent solution. Then HDI (3.34g, 19.8mmol) was added into the mixture dropwise with stirring. The solution was maintained at 45℃ for another 60mins with mechanical stirring. Then a solution with HDI (1.40g, 8.3mmol) and BDO (0.68g, 7.5mmol) in DMF (10mL) were poured into the reaction system. Then the reaction system was stirred at 45℃ for another 5 hours. Then the solution was casted into a pre-heated Teflon mold (10cm×10cm) and put into 60℃ oven for 24 hours, then transfer to vacuum oven at 50℃ for another 24 hours. (3) Preparation of film: The polymer with specific weight (say, 0.20g) was first resolved in DMF (10mL). Then the solution was transferred to a Teflon mold (8cm×8cm) which was preheated at 60℃ for 1hour. Then the mold was put into oven of 60℃ overnight and then apply vacuum to remove residue solvent. The outcome polymer was then put into open area with relative humidity around 70% for one hour and then peered off carefully. The synthesized polymer and equivalent amount of PVP were solved in DMF to form a unified solution with solid content of 10%. The solution was then casted into a teflon mold and moved to a oven of 70 ℃ for 24h to form polymeric film. The dried polymer film was then moved to open area with relative humidity around 50% for 2 hour before it was taken out of the mold for testing. For objective 2: (1) Thermal properties of the samples were studied with DSC (Perkin-Elmer, Diamond). A sample was first scanned from -45℃ to 140℃ at a scanning rate of 10℃/min, then cooling down to -45℃ at the same scanning rate to remove the thermal history. The sample was subsequently heated to 140℃ at the same scanning rate. (2) FTIR spectra were recorded using a Perkin-Elmer spectrum 100 FTIR spectrometer (Perkin-Elmer Instruments) with a universal ATR (attenuated total reflectance) sampling accessory. All samples were scanned 16 times in the range of 650–4000 cm-1 with the resolution of 2 cm-1. (3) Gel Permeation Chromatography (GPC) was performed using Breeze™ 2 HPLC System which is equipped with Waters 1515 isocratic HPLC pump, Waters 2414 refractive index detector, Waters 2489 UV/Visible detector and a column of Waters Styagel® HR 4 DMF. The column was calibrated by 10 groups of polystyrene standard solutions (dissolved in DMF) at room temperature with constant flow rate of 0.5mL/min. (4) WVP was conducted according to ASTM E96C, desiccant method with slight modification. The polymer films were covered to a glass cup filled with preheated calcium chloride and sealed. The gained weights were recorded every fixed period at different RH after 15 mins stabilization. PALS data were collected with pre-conditioned polymer samples and a fast-slow lifetime spectrometer (BaF2 detector). (5) The time resolution was about 200 ps (FWHM). 22Na with 10Ci was used as radioactive positron sources. About one million counts were collected for each spectrum. The source sample assembly was mounted on a liquid nitrogen cryostat. LT9 software was used to analyze the data. For objective 3: (1) Modeling of hydrogen bonding in SMP: In this work, the equilibrium geometries and interaction energies were calculated by B3LYP method using the 6–31G* basis set. The obtained binding energies of the complexes were corrected both for basis set superposition error (BSSE) by the Boys-Bernardi full counterpoise method, and for zero-point vibrational energy (ZPE) at 298.15 K. Harmonic frequency analyses have been carried out and all the optimized geometries have no imaginary frequency, which suggests that the optimized structure exists in the minimum state. All calculations were performed with the Gaussian 03 program. (2) Micro-phase separation morphology by dissipative particle dynamics (DPD) simulations: DPD simulations of the SMPU were performed in a cell of size 30× 30×30, with bead density ρ=3, containing about 8.1×10000 DPD beads, and periodic boundary conditions were applied. Although a larger simulation box would be better to avoid finite size effects, it was too time-consuming, and it was found that, the size of simulation box does not affect the radius of the phase domains. Thus this box was adopted. The finite size effects should not have been significant, since there were at least one domain in the present system for polymers of length N=30 studied in this work. For convenience, the particle mass m, and kBT were all taken as unit. The time step ∆t was taken as 0.0575, and adjacent particles in the polymer chain interacted via a linear spring with a harmonic spring constant of 4.0, according to Groot and Liu. Additionally, the friction coefficient γ was chosen as 4.578. A total of 8×10000 DPD steps were carried out for a DPD simulation in this work. All the DPD simulations were performed using the Materials Studio software package. (4) Calculation of quantity of hydrogen bonds by molecular dynamics (MD) simulations: For the molecular simulation of supra-SMPU system, the periodic boundary condition with an amorphous cell was applied, and ten independent configurations based on the method of Theodoreou and Suter were constructed at 298K and the initial density of 0.5 g/cm3 for each SMPU system. Each system in a cubic cell contains atoms in range of 2860 to 5335 for hard segment contents 10 wt% to 50 wt%.The potential energy of each configuration of different SMPU systems was minimized by use of the Smart Minimer method firstly, and the configuration with the lowest energy for each system was selected for the next steps. Next, NVT ensemble (constant number of particles, volume and temperature) at 1000 K for 1000 ps was used to equilibrate the polymer systems. Then, a constant–temperature, constant–pressure molecular dynamics simulation (NPT) molecular dynamics (MD) relaxation at 500 K lasting 1000 ps was performed. The pressure (0 GPa) was controlled according to the Parrinello–Rahman algorithm, while the temperature was imposed by Nosé method. This high–temperature relaxation procedure was suggested by Lee and Mattice to overcome the energy barrier. The following NPT MD simulations were performed at room temperature 298 K for 1000 ps at each temperature for every polymer system. Each trajectory was sampled every 1000 fs, and the last 50 structures were subject to analysis. In order to study the effect of quantity of hydrogen bonds in different segments on the phase separation of this SMPU, a script was written in the Perl programming language of Materials studio with the criteria of 2.5Å for the maximum hydrogen-acceptor distance, 90° for the minimum angle between the hydrogen covalent bond and 4Å for the minimum separation between the acceptor and the donor for intramolecular H-bonds in shape memory polyurethanes.

516111.label: Major findings and research outcome
516111.value: (1) A series of polymeric thin films with different supra-molecular switches were fabricated and explored their potential application as moisture management material. After careful study of supra-SMP with DHMP as proton acceptor, we found that the thickness of film plays the vital role for moisture management. While the external proton donor like PVP ARE NOT beneficial to the performance of moisture management. (2) The pyridine ring first formed HB with PD at dry state (or low RH environment) with the hydrogen-bonding energy -12.3 kJ/mol. However, with the addition of one water molecule (just like the moderate RH region), the water firstly participated into the HB connected with PD and PA, forming a PA…H2-O…PD structure with sharply increase in the total hydrogen-bonding energy -67.7 kJ/mol. When two water molecules were further added (just like the high RH) into the hydrogen bonded system, two water molecules form hydrogen bonds with PD and PA separately with some decrease in hydrogen-bonding energy -45.4 kJ/mol, which may helps the other extra water go through the supra-SMP film. (3) By DPD simulation, an evolutionary 3D netpoint-switch-frame unit-cell model is established. With the increase of HSC, from our simulated massive data, the diisocyanate phase develops a framework with netpoints evolving from spheres, to linked-spheres, linked-cylinders, then to linked-bi-crossing-cylinders at nanoscale while the soft segment as a switch evolves from a filling-matrix, to linked-layers, to tri-crossing-cylinders, then to linked-bi-crossing cylinders. The chain extender does not show regular geometry, but plays as an inter-phase between diisocyanate phase and soft segment phase, which supports the formation of a more perfect framework. (4) The quantity of hydrogen bonds and the hydrogen-bonding ratio for the functional groups in hard segment increase more largely than that between hard segment and soft segment with the increase of hard segment contents. Due to higher density of functional groups in hard segments and stronger hydrogen-bonding interactions, the forming of hydrogen bonds among hard segments is more preferable, which determines the formation of hard-segment domains in soft segment matrix with some interphase.

516111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
516111.value: As the materials designed in this project are relatively rigid with not so favorable mechanical properties, in further work, we would like to modify current material design with more flexible segments for wider applications. It is also discovered that the external proton donor from PVP cannot show any benefit to the performance of moisture management even though theoretically PVP can form HBs with DHMP in SMP easily. Through this comparative study, we can see that a HB switch responsive to water in any smart materials should have a bonding energy smaller than the HB between water and the switch, but much larger than HBs in water. The HB energy is too strong even stronger than that in the hard segments. Thus the HB formed with PVP cannot act as a switch. The SMP with HB switch formed with DHMP displayed high potential for textiles, medical and packaging applications, especially for sportswear, wound dressing and food storage. The results also provide practical insights for rational design of smart materials using HBs. Since H-bonded complexes are abundant in universe such as in DNA double helix, the conclusion regarding the switchable HB may provide a new angle to look into life and nature.

516111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
516111.value: Driven by strong demands for comfort wears and inspired by the environmental responsiveness of leaf guard-cell and supramolecular entities, the reversible hydrogen bonding (HB) are used as switches to make supramolecular polymers (supra-SMPs). The resulting supra-SMP films were characterized systematically including their self-adaptive water vapor permeability( WVP). Relationships between the structures and properties of Supra-SMPs have been studied both experimentally and theoretically. The SMPs have H-bonding as switch responsible for key features of the self adaptive WVP. It is also discovered that the external proton donor from PVP cannot show any benefit to moisture management and concluded that a HB switch responsive to water in any smart materials should have a bonding energy smaller than that in HB between water and the switch. The HB formed with PVP is too strong, thus cannot act as a switch. It represents a contribution to supramolecular chemistry/physics for functional polymers, smart materials and textiles and reinforces its foundation for Hong Kong’s leadership in innovation of functional/smart textiles and apparel. Since H-bonded complexes are abundant in universe such as in DNA double helix, the conclusion regarding the switchable HB may provide a new angle to look into life and nature.

517011.label: Project Objectives

517011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
517011.value: In this research we extend the classical scheduling problem by adding time-dependent processing times, making it a time-dependent scheduling problem. Scheduling problems, in general, consist in the allocation of resources over time in order to perform a set of jobs. Any allocation that meets all requirements concerning the jobs and resources is called a feasible schedule. The quality of a schedule is measured by a criterion function. The aim of scheduling is to find, among all feasible schedules, a schedule that optimizes the criterion function. A solution to an arbitrary scheduling problem consists in giving a polynomial-time algorithm generating either an optimal schedule or a schedule that is close to the optimal one, if the given scheduling problem has been proved to be computationally intractable. The scheduling problems are subject of interest of the scheduling theory, originated in mid-fifties of the twentieth century. The theory has been developing dynamically and new research areas constantly come into existence. The time-dependent scheduling is one of such areas. In time-dependent scheduling, the processing time of a job is variable and depends on the starting time of the job. This crucial assumption allows us to apply the scheduling theory to a broader spectrum of problems. For example, in the framework of the time-dependent scheduling theory we may consider the problems of repayment of multiple loans, fire fighting and maintenance assignments. In this research, we will discuss algorithms and complexity issues concerning various time-dependent scheduling problems. In this research project we would like to address the issues on machine scheduling problems with the time-dependent processing times. The first direction is connected with possible modifications of the basic assumption of time-dependent scheduling, concerning job processing time. For example, some authors assume that job processing time is a function of time and the position of the job in the schedule or a function of the waiting time of the job. The second direction of research is to consider, in the framework of time-dependent scheduling, the counterparts of the problems known in the classic scheduling. For example, we can consider time-dependent scheduling problems on machines with non-availability periods, time-dependent scheduling with batching, time-dependent versions of the common due-date assignment problem or time-dependent scheduling with two criteria. All these problems will be studied in this project. We will seek optimal solutions if they exist or near-optimal solutions if the problems are proved to be computationally intractable. 调度问题中, 加工时间传统上都认为不变.本课题研究加工时间变化的调度问题. 调度问题就是在不同的时间合理安排资源达到完成任务(工件)之目的.任何满足任务和资源要求的安排定义为可行解或可行调度. 可行调度的好坏或是否合理是由判断(或目标)函数决定的. 调度的目的就是在所有可行调度中,找出判断(目标)函数最优的调度. 加工时间时变的调度问题中, 任务的加工时间是变化的,与任务的开工时间相关. 加工时间时变的调度理论能应用的更加广泛的领域.如,多项贷款的还贷问题,救火问题,设备维修问题. 本课题中, 第一个研究方向是探讨改进加工时间时变调度问题的假设条件.例如,有人假设加工时间是加工时间和任务在加工顺序中所处位置的函数,或是任务等待时间的函数. 第二个研究方向是探讨传统调度问题在加工时间时变时的情况,如,批量调度,同一交货期的设置问题,多(双) 目标问题等.

517011.label: Realisation of objectives
517011.value: In this research project, we addressed the issues on machine scheduling problems with the time-dependent processing times. The 4 objectives of this project are as follows: 1. We extend a large number of very significant scheduling problems with time-dependent processing times; 2. We aim to establish the computational complexity of the scheduling problems with time-dependent processing times; 3. We propose a polynomial time heuristic algorithm with, according to our hypothesis, is asymptotically optimal. That is, the larger the number of variables there is, the more the solution of this algorithm converges towards the optimal solutions; 4. We aim to find special cases of the scheduling problems with time-dependent processing times that are solvable in polynomial time. Overall, we have achieved 100% of these 4 objectives. For the first objective, we investigated a bundle of scheduling problems with time-dependent processing times, such as, independent setup times; learning effects; dependent on position and starting time and allotted resources; both deteriorating jobs and learning effects; truncated position-based learning effect; time-dependent deterioration, etc. For the second objective, we proved that some regular and non-regular objective function problems can be solved in polynomial time. For example, we studied the parallel identical machines scheduling problems with deteriorating jobs and learning effects, i.e., job processing times are defined by functions of their starting times and positions in the sequence. For the cost function containing total completion (waiting) time and total absolute differences in completion (waiting) times, we showed that the problem remains polynomially solvable. For the third objective, we developed several polynomial time heuristics. We considered the single machine scheduling problems with job processing times dependent on position, starting time and allotted resource. The objective is to find the optimal sequence of jobs and the optimal resource allocation, separately. We concentrated on two goals, separately, namely, minimizing a cost function containing makespan, total completion time, total absolute differences in completion times, and total resource cost; minimizing a cost function containing makespan, total waiting time, total absolute differences in waiting times, and total resource cost. The problem is modeled as an assignment problem, and thus can be solved in polynomial time. For the last objective, we studied several special cases. For example, for the group scheduling problems with variable job processing times, that is, the processing time of a job is defined by the function that involves its starting time and position in the group, and groups’ setup time is a positive strictly decreasing continuous function of the amount of consumed resource. Polynomial time algorithms are proposed to optimally solve the makespan minimization problem under the constraint that the total resource consumption does not exceed a given limit and the total resource consumption minimization problem under the constraint that the makespan does not exceed a given limit, respectively. We investigated the flow shop scheduling problem with truncated position-based learning effect. For some regular objectives, we presented heuristic algorithms and analyzed the worst case bound of these heuristic algorithms.

517011.value: For publication 1, we studied the problem of scheduling n jobs with position-time-resource-dependent processing times, with the objective of minimizing a cost function containing makespan, total completion (waiting) time, total absolute differences in completion (waiting) times, and total resource cost. We formulated the problem as an assignment problem and solved in polynomial time [OBJ1 and OBJ4]. In publication 2, w corrected an error made by others and provided a right solution to a special single-machine scheduling problem [OBJ3]. In publication 3, we studied several flow shop scheduling problems with truncated position-based learning effect, and presented heuristic algorithms and analyze the worst case bound of these heuristic algorithms [OBJ1 and OBJ3]. Parallel identical machines scheduling problems with deteriorating jobs and learning effects are studied in Publication 4, the problems remain polynomially solvable under the our proposed model [OBJ2 and OBJ3]. For the single machine problem, we also found similar conclusion in publication 5 [OBJ2 and OBJ3]. The recent paper (publication 6) considered two resource constrained single-machine group scheduling problems. Polynomial time algorithms are proposed to optimally solve the makespan minimization problem under the constraint that the total resource consumption does not exceed a given limit and the total resource consumption minimization problem under the constraint that the makespan does not exceed a given limit, respectively [OBJ1 and OBJ4].

517011.value: For the single-machine group scheduling with resource allocation and deterioration effect, the objective is to find the job sequence within group, the optimal group sequence, and the optimal resource allocation such that the weighted sum of makespan and total resource cost minimization. We prove that some special cases of the problem can be solved in polynomial time. However, for the general problem, we have not given any results. In the real production process, the resource availability is limited, hence, we will continue the work, by considering limited resource availability constraint.

517011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
517011.value: In this research, we extended the classical scheduling problem by adding time-dependent processing times, making it a time-dependent scheduling problem. Scheduling problems, in general, consist in the allocation of resources over time in order to perform a set of jobs. Any allocation that meets all requirements concerning the jobs and resources is called a feasible schedule. The scheduling problems are subject of interest of the scheduling theory, originated in mid-fifties of the twentieth century. The theory has been developing dynamically and new research areas constantly come into existence. The time-dependent scheduling is one of such areas. In time-dependent scheduling, the processing time of a job is variable and depends on the starting time of the job. This crucial assumption allows us to apply the scheduling theory to a broader spectrum of problems. For example, in the framework of the time-dependent scheduling theory we may consider the problems of repayment of multiple loans, firefighting and maintenance assignments. In this project, we developed algorithms and complexity issues concerning various time-dependent scheduling problems, from single machine to multiple machines, from job-shop to flow-shop, and achieved many results, that is, we published several SCI journal papers from the support of this GRF project.

517311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
517311.value: The health and wellness of an individual are significantly influenced by the textiles encountered in their surroundings. Textile materials are carriers of microorganisms such as pathogenic bacteria and odour-generating bacteria. In the past, the basic approach for removing microorganisms was to clean the fabrics by boiling them. Today, antimicrobial agents can be applied to textiles. Various studies have shown that bacterial counts are decreased by as much as 75-99% as a result of the application of antimicrobial treatments. Different agents including metals and metal salts; quaternary ammonium salts; organic molecules (e.g. triclosan and chitosan) and N-halamines (which also enable a regenerable finish through different fabrication methods) are used to provide textiles with antimicrobial properties. Generally speaking, fabrication methods used for antimicrobial textiles can be classified into two categories, i.e. (i) the addition of an antimicrobial agent to the polymer before extrusion, or (ii) post-treatment of the fibre or fabric during the finishing stages. Plasma-based treatment used as a post-treatment can be employed to create antimicrobial coatings on textiles so that the modification of textiles will generate a great variety of properties depending on the process types and parameters. In this project, N-halamines will be applied to different cellulosic textile materials through the plasma-based treatment because N-halamines are regenerable. Although the current antimicrobial finishing techniques are effective, it still loses potency after repeated washings or field use. The use of plasma treatment offers several commercial advantages such as (i) it does not require the use of water and organic solvent as a treatment medium which, therefore, can be considered as a dry and clean technology, and (ii) the versatility of plasma-based treatment can lead to textile surface properties unobtainable by most of the conventional techniques. A unique feature of plasma modification is that the surface structure of the polymer can be selectively modified for a specific application without affecting the bulk properties of the polymer. Careful selection of plasma treatment process parameters can lead to specific surface functionalisation. Until recently, the study of the plasma-based deposition of N-halamines on cellulosic textile materials is seldom reported. Therefore, the aim of this project is to investigate and produce antimicrobial textiles using plasma treatment combined with the addition and fixation of N-halamines to generate good durability, effectiveness and regeneration characteristics. 紡織材料因微生物會產生致病性細菌和氣味，以往是用沸水去消除紡織品上的微生物，但現在可以利用抗菌劑去處理紡織品。使用抗菌劑於紡織品上有兩種方法：(i)在纖維生產時加入或 (ii)在織物整理階段加入。雖然當前的抗菌整理是有效的，但它的功能會在水洗或使用後失去。因此，在這項目中，鹵胺化合物(N-halamines)將通過等離子體處理應用於不同的纖維素紡織物上，原因是鹵胺化合物是有可再生的功能。同時，等離子體處理是一種不需用水的整理技術。

518511.label: Realisation of objectives
518511.value: Objective #1: To develop a family of electrolytic-less AC-LED drivers for general lighting. The research project starts with the development of different resonant inverters for driving AC-LEDs. A systematic design approach for developing LCC-based resonant inverter with current balancing is proposed and published in [J1, C2]. A systematic synthesis approach to generate different converter configurations is proposed with aim to aid circuit designers achieving better characteristics converters for LEDs [C1]. An alternative approach with high voltage driving of LED is also proposed with the aim of using non-electrolytic capacitor [J4, C4]. Finally, a two-phase driving approach is proposed to eliminate the use of electrolytic capacitor [J5, C5]. The approach uses two rectangular current sources working complementarily to supply a constant current to the LED string so that the output current can contain very low ripple in the driver circuit. Objective #2: To find solutions to the inherent problems with AC-LED drivers. The addition of current-balancing capacitors causes the properties of inverter circuits to change significantly. It is necessary to reformulate the design equations of conventional inverter circuits in order to meeting current balancing requirement [J1, C2]. The average currents of the three primary color (RGB) LEDs can become saturated when the RGB LEDs have undergone prolonged ageing. The saturation will cause the resulting white color point to go out of regulation. An optical-sensor-based color control method for maintaining the white color point is then proposed and verified experimentally [J2]. While investigating the ageing effect on LED display units, the research team finds that the driver of a full-color larger-area LED display panel can be implemented with the multi-level pulse-width modulation method through a low-cost modification of the existing hardware structure [J3, C3]. As mentioned, high-voltage driving and two-phase driving approaches are proposed to alleviate lifetime issue that is associated with the electrolytic capacitor. Objective #3: To innovate into various configurations of AC-LED arrays. Different configurations of AC-LED arrays have been investigated and compared in terms of power efficiency, luminous efficacy, and cost. A paper is currently drafted at the time of writing this final report. Objective #4: To develop IP-free AC-LED lighting technology for improving cost competitiveness. Based on the research results, an IP-free AC-LED light system is designed and implemented in an indoor hydroponic system. This project is aimed to develop an insect free environment wherein growth conditions can be precisely controlled to allow optimal growth.

518511.label: Major findings and research outcome
518511.value: The increasing use of LEDs for high-luminance applications implies that more LED modules are to be connected in the form of array for producing the required level of luminance. Series connection of LEDs forms a simple solution, but this method is often restricted by the high turn-on voltage. Currently, the most popular approach to alleviating this restriction is to arrange LEDs in series–parallel connection, thus forming a multi-string array. However, unequal sharing of current between individual strings is a common design issue. Conventional method for balancing current in LED array is achieved by means of linear regulators or switching converters. An accurate current sharing can be achieved with the use of linear regulators, but the overall system efficiency can be degraded seriously due to the power dissipation in the transistors. System efficiency can be improved by using switching converters, but the complexity, size, and cost incurred by this method becomes prohibitively high, in particular when the number of strings is large in high-luminance applications. Considering the above disadvantages, a more energy-efficient approach based on reactive components such as transformers and capacitors, or hybridization of the two, has been proposed to achieve quasi-lossless current balancing in AC-LED array [J1,C2]. In the development of better converters for LEDs, it is found that the average currents of the three primary color (RGB) LEDs can become saturated when the RGB LEDs have undergone prolonged ageing. The saturation will cause the resulting white color point to go out of regulation. An optical-sensor-based color control method is proposed to maintain the white color point by adjusting the color set points when a predefined threshold current is reached by one or more of the primary color LEDs [J2]. While investigating the ageing effect on LED display units, the research team finds that the driver of a full-color larger-area LED display panel can be implemented with the multi-level pulse-width modulation method through a low-cost modification of the existing hardware structure [J3,C3]. An average saving of 15% in energy is resulted as compared to the conventional PWM driving approach. A LED display prototype has been subsequently developed to verify the proposed driving scheme. The prototype has aroused some significant interest from our industrial partners. The high-voltage driving and two-phase driving of LEDs have been investigated thoroughly. Experimental results show that electrolytic capacitor can be eliminated from the driver circuits and the lifetime of lighting system can be extended significantly [J4,J5,C4,C5].

518511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
518511.value: As the luminous performances of LEDs improve and their prices continue to fall following their wide adoption in consumer electronics, the world is seeing a gradual penetration of LEDs into the general lighting market, where a major energy saving is possible considering that 20% of the world electricity generation is consumed by lighting. The introduction of AC-LED as a competitor to the existing technologies is expected to encourage the market penetration of LEDs by accelerating their price fall. The availability of LEDs at reasonable prices will further encourage their adoption for general illumination and gives rise to a major global energy saving. In this project, the investigators have developed a good understanding of AC-LEDs and the requirements of AC-LED-based lighting systems. Good experiences have been accumulated on the design of driver circuits and the optical properties of AC-LED under different driving signals. These experiences will enable the investigators to confidently purse research works in developing reliable and cost-effective LED lighting systems that are suitable to be used in different lighting applications.

518511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
518511.value: Since LEDs operate at low DC voltage, power converters are required to transform the AC mains power into DC power. Although high power efficiency is typically achievable in modern power converters, they generally suffer from premature failure due to the malfunctioning of electrolytic capacitors, which is a critical component in AC-DC power conversion. To the consumers, this is highly undesirable due to the high replacement cost involved and must be avoided. The concept of AC-LED lighting was proposed recently to enable AC operation of LEDs by employing arrays of bi-directionally connected LEDs, thus eliminating the need for electrolytic capacitors. This driving approach will ensure a long service lifetime of the power converters, which is critical for general lighting application, but it also leads to some practical issues that require solutions by power electronics and LED array designs. This project looks into these practical issues, theoretically and experimentally, and finds solutions to them. A family of specially designed electrolytic capacitor-less AC-AC power converters with very long lifetime is developed for general lighting. Its properties in terms of power efficiency, luminous efficacy, reliability and cost are thoroughly investigated and compared to its DC counterpart.

518711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
518711.value: 人臉是圖像及視頻中最常見的物體。對人臉進行表示，分析和識別的有效方法在不同的日常生活中都有著重要的應用，例如：圖像及視頻的存儲，編碼和變換；安全，娛樂領域等。在本項目中，我們將研究生成多視角超分辨率人臉三維結構的有效算法，並將其應用到人臉驗證或識別。 攝像頭拍攝到人臉結構的分辨率有限。即使增加攝像頭的分辨率，人臉在視場中往往只佔一小部分區域。因此，在不同可能的應用之前，有必要改善拍攝到的人臉的分辨率和圖像質量。然而，對在任意姿態情況下的低分辨率的人臉進行分辨率改善和識別是個挑戰。當前大多數的人臉超分辨率技術僅僅假設人臉圖像是正面的。一些多視角人臉超分辨率技術假設人臉可以表示為同一姿態下的樣本人臉線性組合，並且線性組合的係數被採用到其它的姿態去產生其它姿態的高分辨率人臉。然而，不同姿態下的人臉不能被精確地表示為一種線性關係。在本研究中，利用基於樣本的方法，我們將結合人臉的三維結構，從同一姿態或不同姿態的低分辨率人臉輸入去估計特定姿態的高分辨率人臉圖像。為了達到這一目的，我們將研究利用單一圖像或圖像序列去重建人臉的三維結構，並最終估計高分辨率的三維人臉。 人臉超分辨率的一個重要應用是識別低分辨率的人臉。因此，本項目的第二部分就是研究結合多視角超分辨率用於人臉確認/識別。我們將考慮相應人臉數據庫中的人臉作為樣本人臉用於多視角超分辨率算法中。通過此方法，重建後的三維人臉和估計的高分辨率人臉會更準確並具有更好的圖像質量，整體的確認率或識別率會更高。除了算法本身，依據圖像質量決定此類算法的性能是另一個重要的問題。我們將研究一種社交圖像的方法去替代傳統的客觀度量手段。 本項目包含一系列的基本研究，其產生的關鍵技術將服務在很大範圍的現實應用中。此外，基於本項目設計的算法，可以開發一種魯棒的，可行的身份確認視頻監控系統。

518711.label: Realisation of objectives
518711.value: We have almost completed all the objectives of this project, and have proposed an efficient algorithm for human face super-resolution, an algorithm for estimating the depth of face images, and a fusing-based face recognition algorithm. The realization of the respective objectives is described as follows: Objective 1: Devise an efficient algorithm for 3D face reconstruction We have devised an algorithm which can estimate the 3D coordinates of facial-feature points of a face image based on a number of its 2D images with different poses. The method is based on optimizing a 3D model using a nonlinear least-squares model. This method has been published in "IEEE Trans. on Image Processing". Objective 2: Devise efficient multi-view face super-resolution algorithms with the use of 3D face models Two face super-resolution algorithms have been proposed. The first is based on the eigentransformation for super-resolving frontal-view face images, and has been published in "Pattern Recognition Letters". The other method is designed for multi-view face super-resolution, based on sparse representation, and has been published in ICASSP2013. Objective 3: Investigate the integration of multi-view SR algorithms and face-recognition algorithms for enhancing performance Efficient face recognition algorithms based on feature fusion have been proposed. In addition, we have devised an approach for super-resolving facial features. We have published these methods in the journal "Pattern Recognition" and in a conference paper in ISPACS2011. Objective 4: Building image-quality metrics for SR algorithms A website called “Social Image Quality” (SIQ) has been constructed for comparing image quality based on different super-resolution algorithms. Based on this work, we can investigate the building of better image-quality metrics for the face images generated using different SR algorithms. This will be very useful for comparing the visual qualities of different SR algorithms.
