518711.label: Major findings and research outcome
518711.value: Following are the major findings and research outcome of the project: 1. Eigentransformation-based face super-resolution We have proposed a wavelet-based eigentransformation method [1] for face hallucination. Our algorithm uses the wavelet transform to decompose interpolated low-resolution (LR) images in the wavelet domain to obtain high-frequency information in three different directions, and employs the eigentransformation method to reconstruct the corresponding finer high-frequency content of the high-resolution (HR) images. By combining interpolation and eigentransformation, the reconstructed images are less dependent on the training set selected, and can better preserve the low-frequency content. 2. Multi-view face super-resolution based on sparse representation We have proposed a novel method [2] to generate the hallucinated multi-views of faces using the sparse-representation model. In order to render a faithful virtual view, we introduce centralized constraints into a variation framework for optimization. Intensive experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method can perform well in terms of both reconstruction accuracy and visual quality. This technique can be used for pose-invariant face recognition. 3. 3D face model estimated using the nonlinear least squares model We have proposed an efficient algorithm [3] to reconstruct the 3D structure of a human face from one or more of its 2D images with different poses. In our algorithm, the nonlinear least-squares model and similarity transform are employed. The regularization term, based on linear correlation, is added in the objective function to improve the estimation accuracy of the 3D structure. Further, a model-integration method is proposed to improve the depth-estimation accuracy when multiple nonfrontal-view face images are available. 4. Gabor-feature hallucination and fusion for low-resolution face recognition We have proposed an efficient "Gabor-Feature Hallucination" algorithm for low-resolution face recognition [4], and a novel face recognition approach [5] using information about face images at higher and lower resolutions so as to enhance the information content of the features that are extracted and combined at different resolutions. Our algorithms can avoid performing interpolation/super-resolution and high-resolution Gabor feature extraction. Experimental results show that the proposed methods have a superior recognition rate and efficiency to the traditional methods. [1] “Eigentransformation-Based Face Super-Resolution in the Wavelet Domain,” Pattern Recognition Letters, 2012. [2] "Multi-view face hallucination based on sparse representation," ICASSP'2013. [3] “Depth Estimation of Face Images Using the Nonlinear Least-Squares Model,” IEEE Transactions on Image Processing, 2013. [4] “Gabor-Feature Hallucination based on Generalized Canonical Correlation Analysis for face recognition,” ISPACS'2011. [5] "Multi-resolution feature fusion for face recognition," Pattern Recognition, 2014.

518711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
518711.value: In this project, we have developed algorithms for face super-resolution, 3D face reconstruction, and face recognition. The face super-resolution algorithms and the 3D face reconstruction algorithm can be combined to generate high-quality high-resolution 3D faces. Furthermore, the multi-view face super-resolution algorithm can combine with our proposed multi-resolution-based face recognition algorithm so that low-resolution pose-invariant face recognition can be achieved.

518711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
518711.value: The human face is the most common object in images and videos. Efficient ways of representing, analyzing, and recognizing human faces are important for various daily-life applications, such as image and video storage, coding, and transmission; and for security, entertainment, etc. In this project, we have developed the technologies to improve the resolution of face images with different poses, to produce high-resolution 3D face structures from face images, and to perform face recognition when the input face image is of low resolution and with a pose.

518811.label: Realisation of objectives
518811.value: Objective #1: Investigate the attitudes and concerns of building owners and Energy Services Providers (ESCOs) towards Energy Performance Contracting (EPC) in Hong Kong SAR; A comprehensive literature review was completed on the current Energy Performance Contracting (EPC) market globally to-date, including the perceived benefits, the market barriers, as well as possible measures to enhance the use of EPC. A total of 26 semi-structured interviews were carried out with different stakeholders, including key representatives from the local ESCO association, ESCOs’ experts, building owners and practitioners, to understand the latest development of the EPC market in Hong Kong. The interview questions were derived from the literature review, and the questions (some of which enable comparisons between owners and ESCOs) mainly focused on the scope of the local EPC market, potential energy retrofitting works, risk perception, project financing, procurement, measurement and verification (M&V), contract documents, etc. Two questionnaire surveys to understand the concerns of building owners and ESCOs on EPC were conducted separately. The clustered sampling frame of these surveys was developed based on sources from relevant associations (e.g. E & M contractors), websites (e.g. real estate agencies on industrial buildings), reports and directories (e.g. nursing homes and churches are potential EPC clients due to lack of finance). For the building owners’ questionnaire survey, a total of 168 valid questionnaires were returned, representing a response rate of 18.9%. For the ESCOs’ questionnaire survey, 34 valid replies were returned, representing a response rate of 24.8%. The findings of the above works were published in two refereed journal papers - Journal of Property Investment & Finance, and Energy and Buildings. Objective #2: Based on the above findings, compile a set of document templates for use in procuring Energy Performance Contracts for small to medium scale common energy retrofitting works with particular reference to commercial and institutional buildings in Hong Kong SAR; A comparative analysis of different standard forms of EPC contract in eight jurisdictions (including Australia, Canada, China, Japan, Singapore, Taiwan, the United Kingdom and the United States) was conducted. All the essential elements found in these contracts were summarised to reflect on the customised treatments of common contractual issues in energy retrofitting projects in these jurisdictions which have a sizeable EPC market each. Those elements include performance guarantee, excess savings, saving shortfalls, equipment ownership, equipment operation and maintenance, payment terms, change mechanism, as well as dispute resolution procedures. Two articles were published to disseminate the finding of the above comparative works in the Construction Law Journal. In addition, based on the questionnaire survey and interview results, an EPC contract template and associated guidance notes were developed for use in simple retrofitting works for commercial and institutional buildings. To ensure that the contract clauses are workable, comments by EPC experts were incorporated to improve the documents. Objective #3: Develop models for ascertaining the probabilities of performance shortfalls in EPC using Monte Carlo simulation as a risk pricing tool for building owners and ESCOs The performance risks associated with EPC projects were identified through the intensive literature review and interviews. A risk assessment approach was developed to evaluate the probability of energy saving shortfalls, taking into account possible variations in the influential parameters, including weather conditions, occupancy, operating hours, etc. The approach entails the use of a versatile building energy simulation program (e.g. EnergyPlus), correlation analysis and Monte Carlo simulation. Three case studies with different retrofitting measures, including chiller replacement, change of heat rejection system and lighting retrofit, were used to demonstrate the applicability of a probabilistic model for risk assessment. The findings of the first and second case studies were published in Energy and Buildings, whereas the lighting case is being reviewed for possible publication in Applied Energy. Difficulties arising from data privacy (such as project details) was overcome with the signing of non-disclosure agreements, which entailed vetting and clearance by the data providers before publication.

518811.label: Major findings and research outcome
518811.value: Most Hong Kong building owners want to improve energy efficiency, but they only carry out piecemeal retrofitting involving less capital and know-how. The current take-up rate of EPC is low (<10%). Central air-conditioning and lighting system retrofits are more commonly implemented under EPC, because the former can achieve a significant amount of energy saving, whilst lighting requires low upfront capital and a short payback period. ESCOs are willing to bear financial and performance risks when the building owners can repay (Paper II). In the HK EPC market, banks are not familiar with the risks involved. Unlike Singapore, there is no government guarantee on loans. Inflexible procurement procedures, M&V and legal complications, the absence of a clear market direction are attributable for the low take-up rate of EPC. Circumstances conducive to higher EPC uptake include: (1) Single or a few building owners; (2) building owners with strong engineering and legal backup; (3) building owners lacking upfront capital for retrofitting; (4) stable building operation patterns; and (5) a high expectation on energy savings. Suggested measures include ‘promoting success of EPC projects’, ‘modification of government procurement practices to facilitate EPC’, and ‘government backing up ESCOs’ guarantee to lending banks’ (Paper IV). The contract comparative study shows that the guaranteed saving model is more common than the shared saving model. Several standard contract forms worldwide provide ESCOs with an incentive to achieve energy savings higher than the guaranteed level (Paper III & V). Accordingly, an EPC contract template and associated guidance notes have been developed for use in simple retrofitting works. Positive comments have been received from practitioners. Applying the saving assessment model to two ongoing air-con case studies, the replacement of heat rejection system has <50% chance of meeting its target (Paper I). For the chiller replacement project, an estimated 95% chance of meeting its target is evidenced by the actual savings to-date (Paper VII). The lighting retrofit stands a 90% chance of meeting the guaranteed saving at 1.5 million kWh per year (Paper VIII). The key uncertainty factors for chiller retrofitting include: (1) CoP of chiller; (2) equipment load; (3) occupancy rate; (4) lighting load; (5) thermostat set-point; and (6) AC operating hours. For lighting retrofit, savings vary due to: (1) daylight availability; (2) occupancy rate; (3) lighting use patterns; and (4) lamp maintenance (Paper VIII). It is therefore recommended that ESCOs should increase risk premium, improve maintenance and have a clear contract.

518811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
518811.value: In EPC markets overseas, government promotion is crucial to the wider use of EPC in existing buildings. E.g., Taiwan has implemented the ‘EPC Subsidy Scheme’ in the public sector since 2006, resulting in a significant increase of such projects. Singapore has encountered a similar EPC boom with government incentives such as guarantee on EPC loans and an ESCO accreditation scheme. The US government also implemented many EPC projects successfully in federal buildings under the Clinton’s Climate Initiatives. These public EPC experiences provide good opportunities for private sector parties (the critical mass for energy saving) to better understand EPC practice, as well as to identify M & V and other contractual problems by using a local contract template. It is recommended that the HKSAR government should revisit its policy for enhancing energy efficiency and act as a market leader to adopt EPC. Particularly, it may consider launching a 50% loan guarantee scheme similar to Singapore. The risk may be assessed with the model developed in this research. EPC projects in Hong Kong follow international M & V guidelines, which do not enable local energy baseline adjustment due to the variable sub-tropical climate. Local M&V guidelines should be developed specifically for air-con retrofitting.

518811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
518811.value: Due to a lack of upfront capital and know-how, building owners (hosts) often hesitate to implement energy improvement projects in existing buildings. The adoption of Energy Performance Contracting (EPC) has been effective in tackling these problems globally, as Energy Service Companies (ESCOs) not only provide building owners with the capital for project implementation, but also promise an agreed level of energy savings when conservation measures are implemented. Yet, the take-up rate of EPC in Hong Kong is found to be low. This research investigated on factors affecting the current EPC market development in Hong Kong, including the concerns of hosts and ESCOs, the motivational factors, the risk inherent in EPC projects and recommends practical measures for enhancing their use. In addition, a simulation approach which considers annual climatic variations in the parameters affecting energy savings has been developed, enabling ESCOs to predict a range of possible energy savings at a known confidence level (including shortfall probabilities of different guarantee savings) for informing hosts. In addition, a set of EPC contract template and guidance notes to assist hosts who have little in-house engineering and legal supports have been developed. With these, the contracts for implementing EPC projects would be better managed.

519011.label: Project Objectives
519011.value: Propose and analyze a novel relay-selection criterion for cooperative communications with multiple relays. Analyze in-depth how the diversity gain, net-coding gain, error floor and encoder/decoder complexity are related in joint network-channel codes for cooperative communications with multiple relays. Investigate the causes of error floor at high SNR in full-diversity joint network-channel codes. Propose a systematic way of constructing full-diversity joint network-channel codes with low error-floor and/or high net-coding gain after taking the encoder/decoder complexity into consideration. Propose efficient and practical joint network-channel decoding algorithms.

519011.label: Realisation of objectives
519011.value: Over the project period, lots of investigation work has been conducted in order to accomplish the stated objectives. We estimate that Objectives #1, 4 and 5 have been fully accomplished while Objectives #2 and 3 have been 85% accomplished. A summary of our work is listed as follows. 1. In a two-way relaying network with multiple relays, we have considered selecting one ``best'' relay or a pair of ``best'' relays that broadcast network-coded information to other nodes (source or relay) such that information exchange between the two sources can be accomplished. We select the relay(s) based on the max-min criterion in both the Single Relay Selection (SRS) scheme and the Paired-Relay Selection (PRS) scheme. We propose a Distributed VIterbi Selection Algorithm (DVISA) that selects the pair of ``best'' relays in the PRS scheme. Both our analytical and simulation results show that when the path-loss exponent is large and/or there is a sufficient number of relays to choose from, using two relay nodes can provide a lower outage compared with using only one relay node even under the same total transmit power. To reduce the overhead of the PRS scheme, we have proposed an iterative-PRS (I-PRS) scheme in which the paired relay is selected in an iterative and opportunistic way. Simulation results show that the I-PRS scheme has nearly the same outage performance as the PRS scheme under time-invariant channels and significantly outperforms the PRS scheme under time-varying channels. (Objectives #1 and 2: “Selection of Spatially-distributed Relays for Two-way Relaying with Network Coding” published in WCNC 2013 and “Paired-Relay Selection Schemes for Two-way Relaying with Network Coding,” published IET Communications, 2015.) 2. In a cooperative communication network with multiple relays, two conventional ways of selecting the best relay are (i) maximize the minimum of the source-relay channel gain and the relay-destination channel gain, and (ii) maximize the harmonic mean of the two channel gains (max-harmonic-mean (MHM)). We have proposed a generalized selection criterion, termed as the max-generalized-mean (MGM) selection criterion, for selecting the “best” relay. Subsequently, we have analyzed the asymptotic outage probability of the amplify-and-forward opportunistic relaying. We show by analysis and simulation that the conventional max-min selection criterion is optimal under this generalized selection framework, while the MGM criterion can be regarded as a large class of selection criteria achieving the full diversity. (Objectives #1 and 2: “A Class of Selection Criteria Achieving Full Diversity in Amplify-and-Forward Opportunistic Relaying” published in ICACT 2013 and received Outstanding Paper Award.) 3. We have proposed two relay cooperation schemes for use in a multiple access relay channel (MARC) with two sources. The foundations of our proposed schemes are successive interference cancellation (SIC) and compute-and- forward (CAF). We have derived the achievable sum rates of the two proposed schemes, namely the CAF-SIC scheme and the SIC-SIC scheme. The proposed schemes have been studied under two channel settings. (Objectives #1 and 2: “Relay Cooperation Schemes for the Multiple Access Relay Channel: Compute-and-Forward and Successive Interference Cancellation” published in WCNC 2014.) 4. We have investigated the error-floor issue of low-density parity-check convolutional codes (LDPCCCs) which can potentially be applied to cooperative communication system. We have proposed and implemented two types of decoders/simulators --- one runs on graphics processing units (GPUs) and another runs on field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). In our GPU-based decoder architecture, by using efficient data structure and thread layout, the thread divergence is minimized and the memory can be accessed in a coalesced way. All decoders are flexible and scalable. Compared with the traditional serial CPU-based decoders, results show that the proposed GPU-based decoders can achieve 100 times to 200 times speedup. (Objectives #2, 3 and 4: “Implementation of Decoders for LDPC Block Codes and LDPC Convolutional Codes Based on GPUs” published in IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems, 2014.) 5. In our FPGA-based decoder architecture, we combine the memories in the pipelining processors into a large memory block so as to take advantage of the data-width of the embedded memory. A rate-5/6 LDPCCC has been implemented on an Altera Stratix FPGA. It achieves up to 2.0 Gb/s throughput with a clock frequency of 100 MHz. Moreover, the decoder displays an excellent error performance of lower than 1e-13 at a Eb/N0 of 3.55 dB. (Objectives #2, 3 and 4: “A 2.0 Gb/s Throughput Decoder for QC-LDPC Convolutional Codes” published IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems I, 2013; US patent no. 8,671,323 B2 “High-throughput decoder architecture for low-density parity-check convolutional codes,” granted in 2014.) 6. For a generalized joint channel-coding-and-physical-network coding used in a two-way relay system, we have developed a log-likelihood-ratio-based (LLR-based) decoder. Assuming that the same LDPC codes are used at the source nodes, the error performance of the proposed decoder has been simulated over AWGN channels and Rayleigh channels. Results show that the proposed decoder produces identical error performance as the probability-domain-based decoder. Since the proposed LLR-based decoder can be easily implemented by using hardware to realize the addition operations, max operations and simple table look-up operations, it has a much lower computational complexity compared with the probability-domain-based decoder. Moreover, no error floor is observed down to bit error rate (BER) of 1e-7 over AWGN channels and Rayleigh channels. (Objectives #3 and 5: “Decoding Generalized Joint Channel Coding and Physical Network Coding in the LLR Domain” published in IEEE Signal Processing Letters, 2013.) 7. We have proposed a joint finite-length EXtrinsic Information Transfer (EXIT) algorithm for analyzing joint channel-and-physical-layer-network coding (JCPNC) in AWGN channels under standard joint channel-and-physical-layer-network decoding (JCPND) algorithm. The major difference between the EXIT for channel coding and joint EXIT for JCPNC is that the former one is only related to the primary log-likelihood ratio (LLR), while the latter one is dependent on both the primary LLR and secondary LLR. The proposed algorithm therefore can facilitate the related design work. We observe that the EXIT bands can characterize the decoding trajectory with reasonable accuracy. We have also simulated BER curves of the JCPNC schemes based on the rate-1/2 accumulate-repeat-3-accumulate (AR3A) code and (3,6) regular LDPC code with information length K = 1536 in an AWGN channel. Simulation results indicate that the AR3A-coded JCPNC is remarkably superior to the regular-coded one and exhibits excellent error performance. We do not observe any error floor down to BER of 1e-6. (Objectives #3 and 5: “A Survey on Protograph LDPC Codes and Their Applications” published in IEEE Communications Surveys & Tutorials, 2015.) 8. We have investigated the protograph LDPC codes over quasi-static fading (QSF) relay channels with coded cooperation (CC). A new construction method is proposed for designing the full-diversity rate-compatible root-protograph (RCRP) codes for such a relaying protocol. The asymptotic word error rate and BER of the RCRP codes are analyzed by exploiting a new protograph EXIT algorithm. Furthermore, the expression of outage probability is also developed to characterize the error performance of RCRP codes. Both theoretical and simulated results suggest that the RCRP codes not only outperform the conventional regular rate-compatible protograph (RCP) codes in terms of error performance with code rates ranging from 0 to 1/2 but approach the outage limit as well. (Objectives #3 and 5: “Rate-Compatible Root-Protograph LDPC Codes for Quasi-Static Fading Relay Channels” IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology, 2016.)

519011.label: Major findings and research outcome
519011.value: We have proposed an Iterative Paired-Relay Selection (PRS) (I-PRS) scheme in which the paired relay is selected in an iterative and opportunistic way. Simulation results show that the I-PRS scheme has nearly the same outage performance as the PRS scheme under time-invariant channels and significantly outperforms the PRS scheme under time-varying channels. (One conference and one journal paper published.) We have proposed a generalized selection criterion, termed as the max-generalized-mean (MGM) selection criterion, for selecting the “best” relay in a cooperative communication network with multiple relays. (Conference paper received Outstanding Paper Award) We have investigated the error-floor issue of low-density parity-check convolutional codes. We have proposed and implemented two types of decoders/simulators --- one runs on GPUs and another runs on FPGAs. The advantage of GPU-based decoders is that they can be easily configured to simulate different codes. First, they can decode different codes by changing the parameters. Hence, the programs need very little modification. Second, they can be run on the latest or even future generations of GPUs which possess more hardware resources. For example, if there are more cores/memory in the GPU, we can readily decode more codes, say Gamma=64 codes (Gamma is a multiple of a warp) as compared with Gamma=32 codes used in our decoder, at the same time. On the other hand, FPGA-based decoders can produce a much higher throughput. It achieves up to 2.0 Gb/s throughput with a clock frequency of 100 MHz. Regardless of the type of decoders/simulators being used, we do not observe any error floor for the LDPCCCs being simulated, even at a bit-error-rate of 1e-13. (Two IEEE journal papers published and one US patent granted.) For a generalized joint channel-coding-and-physical-network coding used in a two-way relay system, we have developed a log-likelihood-ratio-based (LLR-based) decoder, which produces identical error performance as the probability-domain-based decoder. (One IEEE journal paper published.) We have proposed a joint finite-length EXIT algorithm for analyzing the protograph-based JCPNC under standard joint channel-and-physical-layer-network decoding (JCPND) algorithm, in which the mutual information (MI) is traced on each edge of the protograph. The major difference between the EXIT for channel coding and joint EXIT for JCPNC is that the former one is only related to the primary log-likelihood ratio (LLR), while the latter one is dependent on both the primary LLR and secondary LLR. The algorithm should therefore facilitate the related design work. (One IEEE journal paper published.)

519011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
519011.value: In this project, we have proposed two relay cooperation schemes for use in a multiple access relay channel (MARC) with two sources. In the future, we shall continue to study the performance of our proposed schemes under other channel settings. We are also extending our schemes to MARC with multiple sources. Energy efficiency of relay communications has attracted much interest recently. Most research efforts have focused on half-duplex systems. As there has been significant progress in practical implementation of self-interference cancellation, full-duplex systems will have a promising potential in the near future. The energy efficiency of a full-duplex relay system under certain constraints e.g., the total power constraint, can be studied in the future.

519011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
519011.value: In communication systems such as WiFi, 3G, 4G LTE and future 5G systems, errors are bound to occur during the transmission via the wireless medium. To ensure that the users can receive the data correctly and to improve the data rate, intermediate relays as well as error-correction codes should be utilized. This project has resolved some fundamental issues in such relay-assisted cooperative communication systems with error correction capability. In such systems, multiple relays exist to help users/base station exchanging information. Moreover, high performance forward-error-correction codes which can reduce the error rate down to 1 in 1 trillion bits have been investigated. The results will allow more efficient and effective wireless communication systems to be developed in the future.

519211.label: Project Objectives
519211.value: Characterization, design and fabrication of FMFs for long-haul transmission systems: We will analytically investigate the effect of index contrast, core diameter and bending of an FMF on coupling to higher-order modes, nonlinearity reduction/enhancement and mode division multiplexing. Optimized FMF design that maximize the Q-factor of an overall communication system will be derived and fabricated using the facilities in PolyU. Transmission performance using advanced modulation formats and receiver signal processing algorithms will be investigated. Waveguide design and communication strategies for MCFs: We will analytically study mode-coupling dynamics for 7-core MCF, illustrating the different coupling dynamics between signals launched in the center core and outer cores. For heterogeneous-core MCF, we will investigate the dependence of coupling strength on various core parameters. Bending induced coupling and crosstalks will be analytically or statistically characterized. Finally, optimal communication strategies and receiver signal processing techniques for MCF in presence of crosstalks will be investigated.

519211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
519211.value: The explosive growth in the volume and variety of multi-media rich applications continues to drive speed demands for Internet traffic and motivate research in backbone fiber-optic communication links. Major telecommunication service providers are desperately searching for new solutions to accommodate the unprecedented traffic demands and ensure high quality of service. Coherent communications and electronic digital signal processing(DSP)-based receivers have been accepted in recent years as next generation standards for long-haul systems due to their flexibility, scalability and ability to compensate for various transmission impairments including fiber nonlinearity. However, the proposed DSP algorithms for nonlinearity mitigation do not predict orders-of-magnitude performance improvements while they are already perceived as too complex for practical implementations. Meanwhile, for shorter-length links such as passive optical networks(PON), Internet servers, super-computers and data centers, increasing capacity demands are currently met by massive parallelizations using multiple fiber connections. However, such configurations are costly, bulky, hard to manage and lead to fiber congestion issues and are hence not scalable. Consequently, it is overwhelmingly clear that to continue powering fiber-optic communication systems into the next decade and beyond, new transmission media to replace standard single-mode fibers(SMF) are indispensable. Few-mode fibers(FMF) and multi-core fibers(MCF) have been studied for laser and short range applications in past decades and there is a resurgence of interest for their use in communication links. Preliminary investigations and proof-of-concept experiments are recently reported. Nonetheless, the interplay between waveguide optics and communication system performance of FMF and MCF are far away from adequately understood and characterized to enable practical designs that further scale up transmission capacities. The objectives of the proposed research is to combine the physics of guided-wave optics with communication theory and signal processing techniques to design new fiber structures for next generation optical communication systems. In particular, we will 1)theoretically characterize signal propagation in FMFs theoretically and design, fabricate and experimentally verify optimized FMFs and their transmission performance in long-haul systems;2)analytically investigate crosstalk dynamics in MCFs and derive appropriate composite waveguide structures and communication strategies to optimize MCF transmission capacity. The outcome of the proposed research will provide crucial insights on new fiber designs for next generation long-haul links and data centers. Together with their fabrication and experimental verifications, the completion of the proposed research will potentially shape a whole new research direction for substantial future developments and may serve as a starting point of yet another paradigm shift in optical communications research. 多媒体应用的容量和种类的爆炸性增长持续的推动着因特网的速度需求，并促进着光纤通信骨干网的研究。主要的电信服务供应商都在迫切的寻求新的解决方案来适应空前的流量需求并保证高质量的服务。相干通信和基于数字信号处理（DSP）的接收机在最近几年被认可成为下一代长距离传输的标准，因为它具有灵活性，可扩展性以及可以补偿包括非线性在内的各种传输损伤的能力。然而，已经提出的用于非线性补偿的DSP算法尚未获得足够的性能提升，其复杂度就已经超过了实际系统的可接受范围。与此同时，用于短距离的传输系统，比如无源光网络（PON），因特网服务，超级计算机和数据中心中，大量并联的光纤连接被用来满足持续增长的容量需求。这种方式不仅昂贵，笨重，难以管理并且容易造成光纤拥塞，因此具有很差的扩展性。以上原因清晰地表明，在未来十年，寻找新的传输介质来代替传统光纤通信系统中的单模光纤（SMF）势在必行。 在过去十年中，少模光纤（FMF）和多核光纤（MCF）被研究用于激光器和短距离应用。最近，人们重新认识到了他们在通信系统中的研究价值，并且已经有一些初步的研究和验证性的实验被公布。然而，对于FMF和MCF，人们对于光学波导对传输系统性能影响的理解远远不够，设计拥有更大传输容量的通信系统成为了难题。 我们的研究目标是通过结合物理波导光学和通信理论与数字信号处理，来设计用于下代光通信系统的新型光纤结构。具体来说：1）理论的描述信号在FMF中的传输并设计，制造和实验验证优化的FMF以及其在长距离通信系统中的性能。2)理论分析MCF中的动态串扰并推导出合适的复合波导结构以及优化MCF传输容量的通信策略。 预计的研究成果将会为下代长距离系统和数据中心为的光纤设计提供关键的见解。结合光纤制造和实验验证，我们的研究可能会形成一个关于未来发展的新的研究方向并可能成为新的光纤通信研究的模式转变的起点

519211.label: Realisation of objectives
519211.value: Objective 1: We have investigated the relation between fiber geometry on group velocity and coupling strength of FMF and designed and fabricated a FMF using the fiber drawing tower facilities at PolyU. Together with NEC Labs America, we demonstrated a 88 channel WDM transmission of 3-mode polarization-multiplexed QPSK signals with state-of-the-art digital signal processing techniques, and the experiment is also the world's first demonstration of WDM FMF transmission with inline few-mode EDFA. We further work with Corning to demonstrate the practical feasibility of quasi-single mode transmission. The objectives stated are achieved Objective 2: We have analytically derived the mode-coupling dynamics for 7-core homogeneous MCF and illustrate the aperiodic coupling behaviour between signals in outer cores. For heterogeneous-core MCF, we studied the dependence of distance separation and index contrast on the coupling strength. For both direct-detection and coherent detection scheme, we derived appropriate equalization strategies and crosstalk-induced performance limits. The objectives stated are achieved

519211.label: Major findings and research outcome
519211.value: We worked on deriving the mode coupling dynamics for multi-core fibers for homogeneous and heterogeneous cores, derived corresponding communication strategies for joint detection and signal processing and characterize the limits of MCF transmission with coherent and direct detection. It is found that the coupling dynamics is aperiodic with distance because of the irrational nature of sqrt root of 7. This impose a performance limit on direct detection 7-core MCF systems (journal item #1 in part 8) We also fabricated a 3-mode FMF using the fiber drawing facilities at PolyU. It is a step-index fiber with 2 km length. We then worked together with NEC Labs America and send our fiber to their facilities to setup the mode-division multiplexed systems. Eventually, we together demonstrated a 50km FMF transmission experiment with the world's first few-mode optical amplifier. (journal item #2 in part 8) Also, we investigated the use of FBG on few-mode fibers as mode converters brought about by the asymmetric refractive index change during the FBG writing process. Mode converters are an important component of mode-division multiplexed transmission systems (journal item #3 in part 8) we also collaborated with Corning Inc, the globally leading optical fiber manufacturer in using few-mode fiber (FMF) as Quasi-single mode (QSM) transmission. We experimentally demonstrate 256 Gb/s PM-16-QAM transmission up to 2600 km by using 100-km spans of FMF operating in QSM transmission and using an appropriate digital signal processing (DSP) algorithm called decision-directed(DD)- least mean squares (LMS) algorithm to compensate multi-path interference. The new FMF together with our DSP algorithm result in a new world record in transmission distance for 16-QAM transmission with longest span length and an invited conference presentation at the prestigious Optical Fiber Communication (OFC) Conference and a journal paper (conference item#1 and journal item #4 in part 8)

519211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
519211.value: For both FMF and MCF, We will further investigate joint frequency offset as well as carrier phase recovery algorithms for the purpose of DSP complexity reduction. The effect of crosstalk between signals due to mode coupling on frequency offset and phase noise recovery will be quantified. The amount of crosstalk as a function of transmission distance will be theoretically and experimentally investigated. For QSM transmissions, more computationally efficient algorithm to compensate MPI, such as frequency-domain algorithms as supposed to decision-directed least-mean squares, will be investigated.

519211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
519211.value: Transmission capacities brought about by conventional single-mode fibers are more or less at their limits after 30 years of advances in optical communication systems. Multi-core fibers and few-mode fibers are proposed as new fiber types to enable simultaneous transmission of multiple signals and break the speed limitation towards a next generation of optical communication systems. In our project, we analyzed how 7 independent signals propagate in 7-core multi-core fibers and their mutual influence on each other. Such insight is important to design signal processing strategies to overcome such influence and clean up the multiple received signals at the receiver. We also helped fabricate and incorporate key components such as mode converters and few-mode inline amplifiers and experimentally demonstrate the simultaneous transmission of multiple signals in a few-mode fiber system. We further propose and experimentally demonstrate a low-cost intermediate upgrade option called quasi-single mode transmission that use the new few-mode fiber while keeping all the other components unchanged and that already provide a considerable amount of capacity improvements

519911.label: Project Title(Chinese)
519911.value: 高鐵列車隧道相互作用下產生的氣動噪聲及其被動控制

519911.label: Project Objectives
519911.value: To develop a fully coupled numerical model for the train-tunnel aeroacoustics, and verify its accuracy as well as applicability in explaining the interaction events observed in experiments reported in existing literature. To uncover, using the numerical techniques developed in fulfilling the previous objective, the key physics of train-tunnel interactions and the resulting aeroacoustics. To develop, based on the results obtained in working for all previous objectives, a passive control solution that is able to significantly reduce the severity of tunnel noise and passenger discomfort.

To develop, based on the results obtained in working for all previous objectives, a passive control solution that is able to significantly reduce the severity of tunnel noise and passenger discomfort.

519911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
519911.value: Aeroacoustic problems arising from the speed-up of railway system have received considerable attention as urgent engineering issues to be resolved. With the speed-up of train, many engineering problems, which have been reasonably neglected at low speeds, are raised with regard to aerodynamic noise/vibrations, impulse noise at tunnel exit, ear/riding discomfort of passengers, noise nuisance to the residents close to railways, etc. These factors limit the further speed-up and wider adoption of high-speed railway networks in many countries. Presently only a few countries are operating the high-speed railway trains, such as the French TGV, the German ICE, and the Japanese Shinkansen for inter-city travels at 360 km/h. China has just launched her CRH380B model for her extensive high-speed railway networks. The worldwide demand, especially in Asia, for high-speed railway travels will see an unprecedented increase in coming decade. Among all aeroacoustic sources in current high-speed railways, those occurring during the train passage through a tunnel are dominating components and contribute to most of the noise and passenger discomfort complaints. When a high-speed train enters a tunnel, a compression wave is formed ahead of the train as a result of train-tunnel interaction and propagates along the tunnel at sonic speed. Part of it is reflected back from the tunnel exit as an expansion wave. Complex wave interference occurs inside the tunnel due to successive reflections at tunnel portals and multiple scattering from the tunnel structural discontinuities (e.g. air shaft). The pressure wave transients cause large fluctuating loads on the train causing discomfort to passengers. A part of the compression wave creates a low-frequency and short-duration impulse noise at tunnel exit. With the increase in train speed in recent years, the noise and vibration due to impulse waves have become a new type of environmental noise problem. Systematic work is highly needed to understand these train-tunnel aeroacoustics of high-speed railway train, to improve the existing train and tunnel designs and to develop a new generation of high-speed railway systems. Therefore, the aim of the present proposal is, by means of a combined experimental and numerical study, to enhance the understanding of nonlinear train-tunnel interaction and its aeroacoustics. It is envisaged that the knowledge gained from the project will provide a new design methodology for high-speed railway tunnel which is more environmental friendly, more comfortable yet more fuel-efficient. 隨著鐵路系統速度不斷的提升, 其所產生的氣動噪聲問題已演變成一相當嚴重的工程問題解以待決。當列車以高速行駛時, 經常發生一些在低速時看不見的問題。如果空氣動力誘發的噪聲及振動，在隧道出口處脈衝波的形成及擴散，乘客耳鳴及坐乘不適，以噪音滋近鐵路的居民等等，這些因素都限制了許多國家的高速鐵路網絡進一步發展。目前只有少數幾個國家，如法國的TGV高速火車，德國 ICE和日本新幹線以時速360公里運作。中國亦剛剛推出以CRH380B車種為基礎的高鐵網絡。在未來十年高鐵網絡在全球的需求持續增加，尤其是在亞洲區將會有可觀的增長。在目前高鐵所有關於噪聲的投訴當中，那些發生在列車高速通過隧道時所以產生的噪音佔大部分。當列車高速進入隧道時，車前形成脈衝壓縮波。這壓縮波以音速沿隧道傳播。部分波能量從隧道出口作為一個膨脹波反射回列車。這多重散射反射在隧道壁複雜幾何圖形下產生複雜波干擾。壓力波瞬變引起大的波動負荷會引起火車乘客的不適。近年來隨著列車的提速，脈衝波誘發的噪音和振動環境噪音問題已經成為一個新類的工程問題。因此本研究項目的目的是，通過聯合實驗和數值研究，以加強了解高鐵的非線性列車隧道相互作用和其氣動聲學原理。同時亦希望從研究中獲得的新知識，以助於提供一個更環保，更舒適但更省油高鐵隧道設計方法。

519911.label: Realisation of objectives
519911.value: In order to accomplish the objectives as stated in Section 5.2, the project was divided into three major tasks listed below. [1] To develop a modified direct aeroacoustic simulation solver for resolving in a single simulation both the flow-structure interaction encountered by a high-speed train approaching and entering a tunnel and the subsequent aeroacoustic generation at the far tunnel exit portal. We extended the capability of our existing direct aeroacoustic simulation solver based on conservation-element-solution-element (CE/SE) scheme that had been proven able to correctly resolve aeroacoustic problems over a wide range of flow Mach number. In the present project, the train was assumed to enter the tunnel with a constant velocity, the modified solver should be able to handle the moving boundary of the train surface and the associated flow-structure interaction. We developed a formulation and numerical implementation of moving surface boundary condition that coupled flow solution seamlessly for our direct aeroacoustic simulation solver. The boundary condition was found working very well for weak surface motion with amplitude comparable to the size of the grid next to the moving surface. However, when the surface motion went beyond the grid size, the simulation always went singular. The results of careful analysis revealed that relatively strong surface motion led to a violation of the conservation of compressible flow fluxes within a conservation element in contact with the moving surface which amplified the numerical errors until the simulation broke down. The analysis results also revealed that a complete re-formulation of our CE/SE scheme would be needed in order to circumvent the numerical difficulty which was impossible within the funding and duration granted with the project. Therefore, we decided to take another approach of modifying our direct aeroacoustic simulation solver for satisfying the objective of the projects. From existing literature a high-speed train is moving much faster than normal trains but the train Mach number is always kept within the range 0.3–0.35 due to practical and operational constraints. Such Mach number is considered pretty low as compared to those in aeronautical applications and consequently the aerodynamics involved can be considered essentially imcompressible. We leveraged on this observation and acted to transform our direct aeroacoustic simulation solver to a hybrid computational aeroacoustic solver for the project. In essence the hybrid computational aeroacoustic solver was a nonlinear acoustic perturbation propagation solver driven by the flow unsteadiness which was estimated from the results of a prior incompressible aerodynamic simulation of the problem. The incompressible aerodynamic simulation was carried out using a commercial CFD solver with established fluid-structural coupling capability. We derived the theoretical formulation of the propagation solver using the acoustic perturbation equation approach on a steady background flow (which was the quiescent ambient condition). We fully developed the hybrid computational aeroacoustic solver that was ready to take in the solutions from the CFD solver, and verified its applicability by compared its results with a model experiment for a high-speed train through a tunnel. [2] Having verified and validated the quality of the new solver, we carried out a systematic study that highlighted the effects of key parameters that affect the flow-structure interaction between the wake and boundary layer flow of the entering train and the eventual acoustic generation. [3] Based on the knowledge gained from [1] and [2], we developed several tunnel inlet portal and compared their effectiveness in suppressing the level of acoustic radiation from another end of the tunnel. We could then find out the an inlet portal geometry that gave the most effective control of high-speed railway tunnel noise in a fully passive manner. Work on these tasks were carried out and the objectives defined for were completed.

519911.label: Major findings and research outcome
519911.value: [1] We modified our existing direct aeroacoustic simulation code through adopting a simplified Courant number insensitive CE/SE scheme with suppressed dissipation with appropriate non-reflecting and no-slip boundary conditions. The new code was fully validated by comparing its results of a few selected benchmark aeroacoustic problems with the corresponding existing analytical/numerical solutions as well as experimental results (Papers 8–1 and 8–3). The new code was proven possessing numerical quality and stability required for resolving the aeroacoustics of train-tunnel interaction. We successfully developed a formulation of CE/SE boundary condition that coupled small-amplitude solid surface motion to flow solution, and testified them using the canonical aeroelastic panel under excitation (Papers 8–2, 8–4, 9–1). New nonlinear panel vibration modes were also found. The capability of the modified code in resolving the coupling of panel vibration, its aeroacoustic generation, and subsequent propagation in the confined domain, was fully confirmed (Papers 9–2, 9–3). Unfortunately we could not extend the boundary condition to cater for relatively large-amplitude motion due to the destruction of the numerical flow flux conservation as explained in Section 5-3. [2] Realizing the low Mach number frequently encountered in most practical high-speed railway applications, we overcame the mentioned numerical difficulties by developing a hybrid approach of computational aeroacoustics (HCA) to solve the train-tunnel aeroacoustic problem. We calculated the incompressible train aerodynamics using a CFD solver as the errors involved was very small at such Mach number. We went on to develop a nonlinear acoustic perturbation solver, using our CE/SE scheme in [1], to predict the acoustic waves excited by the incompressible flow unsteadiness (Papers 9–4, 9–5 & Thesis 10–3). The comparison of our HCA numerical results with those from a model experiment of train-tunnel interaction showed a remarkably favorable agreement, which confirmed HCA was a feasible tool for analysis of train-tunnel aeroacoustic problems. [3] The HCA success allowed us to evaluate the physics of three tunnel inlet portal designs for mitigation of noise from tunnel-train interaction of high-speed train. The best design obtained gave a reduction of aerodynamic pressure fluctuation on the train by ~30% (Thesis 10–1). The subsequent reduction of peak noise, which was found more sensitive to the temporal and spatial patterns of aerodynamic pressure rise/drop, at tunnel exit was around 3 db. The numerical results are being consolidated and complied for preparing another journal paper (Paper 9–5).

519911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
519911.value: With the achievements described in Section 6.2, the next step is to make use of the know-how and new code to develop and evaluate different combinations of train and tunnel designs for low environmental noise radiation as well as higher passenger comfort. In fact the ultimate impact along these two performance measures depends critically on the unsteady dynamics of flows confined between train and tunnel. Usually the train geometry is fixed due to other performance consideration so it is easier to make changes in tunnel design. The research outcomes reveal that low noise generation and low train aerodynamic pressure fluctuations come with big tunnel bore due to its weaker and smoother pressure fluctuations in the confined flow. However, the construction of such tunnel is prohibitively costly. Therefore, one may make use of the research outcomes and codes developed present project for a better understanding of the flow-structure interaction between a moving high-speed train during its entire passage through a tunnel, and its subsequent aeroacoustic generation, which may help open up new direction of tunnel design non-standard geometry (e.g. vented inlet and outlet with mid-tunnel wave trapper) for further suppression of environmental noise and passenger discomfort of high-speed railway.

519911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
519911.value: Aeroacoustic problems arising from the high-speed railway system have received considerable attention as urgent engineering issues to be resolved. With the train speed-up, many aeroacoustic problems are raised with regard to aerodynamic noise/vibrations, impulse noise at tunnel exit, ear/riding discomfort of passengers, noise nuisance to the residents close to railways, etc. The aeroacoustic source processes occurring during the train passage through a tunnel are dominating components and contribute to most of the noise and passenger discomfort complaints. When a high-speed train enters a tunnel, a compression wave emerges due to train-tunnel interaction and propagates along the tunnel. Complex wave interference occurs inside the tunnel due to successive reflections at tunnel portals and multiple scattering from the tunnel structural discontinuities, causing strong fluctuating train loads and discomfort to passengers. Part of the compression wave creates a low-frequency/short-duration impulse noise at tunnel exit. The present project has attempted to deepen the understanding of such nonlinear train-tunnel interaction processes, and their aeroacoustics, arising from train-tunnel interaction when a high-speed train passes through a tunnel. A new numerical analysis technique is developed which provides a promising method for developing new-generation high-speed train-tunnel system for low noise and discomfort impact, among other design constraints.

520911.label: Project Objectives
520911.value: To study the interactions among biodegradable chelants (EDDS, NTA, etc.), metal nutrient supply, and trace metal solubility in the rhizosphere; To evaluate the key factors controlling the uptake of metals by selected species of plants in the chelant-regulated phytoremediation process; and To assess the degradation and leaching behaviors of metal-chelant complexes in the soil-plant systems.
rows: To study the interactions among biodegradable chelants (EDDS, NTA, etc.), metal nutrient supply, and trace metal solubility in the rhizosphere;
To evaluate the key factors controlling the uptake of metals by selected species of plants in the chelant-regulated phytoremediation process; and
To assess the degradation and leaching behaviors of metal-chelant complexes in the soil-plant systems.

520911.label: Realisation of objectives
520911.value: (1) The interactions of biodegradable chelant EDDS in rhizosphere soil was investigated specifically with a multi-layer rhizobox. The soil was collected from an agriculture field adjacent to Cu mine in Nanjing, which was contaminated with 725 mg/kg Cu. Chemical properties including pH, DOC, concentration of metals, EDDS and low molecular organic acids (LMWOAs) were examined in soil solutions. The chemical speciation of Cu and EDDS was modelled using Visual MINTEQ version 3.1. The modelled results help to understand the complexation processes of EDDS and Cu with the consideration of potential competition from other metals (e.g., Zn, Fe, Ca and Mg) and LMWOAs in rhizosphere. To further understand the complexation mechanisms between EDDS and soil Cu, the distribution pattern and speciation of Cu were investigated with synchrotron-based micro X-ray fluorescence (µXRF) and micro X-ray absorption near edge structure (µXANES). In addition, the influence of EDDS on microbial activities in rhizosphere were featured by parameters including the soil microbial biomass carbon, microbial biomass nitrogen and enzyme activities (e.g., urease acid phosphatase and saccharase). Based on the above analysis, the objective on the interactions among chelants, soil metals and microbial activities was principally achieved. (2) To evaluate the key factors controlling the uptake of CuEDDS by ryegrass, a hydroponic experiment with ryegrass was conducted. Ryegrass was grown for 14 days and then exposed to CuEDDS from 0-3000 µM. It was found that Cu accumulation in ryegrass shoot was determined by the supplied concentration of CuEDDS. The mechanisms underlying absorption, transport and detoxification of CuEDDS in ryegrass were further explored according to µXRF and µXANES analysis. (3) The biodegradation and leaching risks were assessed in a pot experiment with ryegrass (Lolium multiflorum Lam.) and tall fescue (Festuca arundinacea) in combination with chelants (ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA), ethylenediaminedisuccinic acid (EDDS) and L-Glutamic acid N,N-diacetic acid (GLDA)). The biodegradation of chelants were tracked by the dissolved organic carbon (DOC) in soil between 1-4 weeks after the application of chelants. Simultaneously, the leaching risks of Cu induced by chelants were determined by CaCl2 extracted Cu from the soil after harvesting the plants from pot. Monitoring on the degradation and leaching risks of Cu-chelate complex was completed in this study. A number of interesting findings were also obtained on the use of EDDS and other chelants in soil washing processes of cotaminated soils.

520911.label: Major findings and research outcome
520911.value: Based on this project, a systematic understanding was achieved on the important process of EDDS and Cu involved in chelant assisted phytoextraction. To be specific, the major findings were listed below. (1) The study investigated the interactions among EDDS, soil metals and microbial activities, and shed light on the underlying mechanisms. Application of EDDS solubilized soil trace (e.g., Cu, Zn, Pb, and Ni) and major elements (e.g., Ca, Mg, Fe, and Mn). Plant transpiration induced mass flow resulted in the significant mobilization of Cu and EDDS from non-rhizosphere to rhizosphere soils. Molecular investigation on Cu speciation revealed that soil Cu was originally adsorbed on iron oxides (61-100%), and a minor proportion (0-39%) was bound with soil organic matter. EDDS formed complexes with Cu adsorbed on soil particles, and the fraction of Cu adsorbed on iron oxides appeared to be more easily to be extracted than that on organic matters. Consistently, Cu speciation analysis with traditional sequential extraction showed that EDDS mobilized Cu adsorbed on carbonate, Fe/Mn oxides and organic matters, and formed highly soluble Cu. In addition to the chemical transformation of Cu in the rhizosphere by EDDS application, microbial activities were also affected. Microbial biomass C and N were found to be enhanced by 0.73 and 2.90 times in the rhizosphere soil than in non-rhizosphere after the use of EDDS. In the rhizosphere, urease activities were increased by a fold of 1.3, while acid phosphatase and saccharase were not affected. (2) According to our experiments, the concentration of CuEDDS was found to be the most important factor in controlling Cu accumulation in ryegrass shoots. Furthermore, a comprehensive understanding on the absorption, transport and detoxification of CuEDDS was established. The results revealed that Cu hyperaccumulation in ryegrass was achieved only at high dosage of CuEDDS over 1500 µM, and plant biomass reduction was simultaneously observed. CuEDDS led to the accumulation of Cu in both root meristematic and mature zone in root apex, and facilitated Cu transport from root cortex to root stele. CuEDDS was partially transformed to other complex forms including Cu-histidine, Cu(I)-glutathione in ryegrass root and shoot. The chemical transformation were involved in intracellular transport or detoxification process of Cu in ryegrass. (3) The degradation and leaching risks of EDTA, EDDS and GLDA were assessed successfully in this project. It was found that the degradation of EDDS was faster than the other two chelants, and the leaching risks of Cu were largely reduced as the bioavailable Cu in soil decreased accordingly. Extracted Cu by chelants from carbonate, iron and manganese oxides and organic matters were resorbed to these soil components after degradation of chelants. EDDS was found to be more environmental sound in comparison with other two chelants.

520911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
520911.value: Theoretical and practical progresses has been achieved based on our current laboratory work. Future field studies on the application of this technique is well deserved to be explored. Pilot study on the application of EDDS in the field can be conducted, and the application dosage should be further tested, metal extraction efficiency and biodegradation of metal chelate complexes should be monitored during the field study. The production of collected plants to be biofuel materials or recycling useful metals from the biomass can be included to increase the economic profit from the planned phytoremediation. Long term (5-10 years) field work is suggested to gain enough experience on future applications of this technology in a large scale.

520911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
520911.value: Growing attention has been paid on the soil pollution by heavy metals around the world. An appropriate remediation technology is required for current risk control and future reuse of the polluted sites. This research project is an important study on a green technology using plants with chelants to extract heavy metals from polluted soils. The study focused on the mechanistic understanding on the process of Cu and EDDS (a biodegradable chelant) in the soil plant systems. Good progress has been achieved on the molecular interactions between EDDS and Cu in the rhizosphere soil and the uptake of CuEDDS complex by selected plants with advanced analysis technologies. New findings in this study provide valuable information on the understanding of Cu mobilization and uptake by plant in the chosen soil-plant system. The results are important for formulating new strategies in this technology in the future based on the in-depth understanding of critical biogeochemical processes. This study also provides guidance for the further use of this technology in a large scale remediation work in field.

521411.label: Project Title(Chinese)
521411.value: 高熵合金的原子構型及相穩定性

521411.label: Project Objectives
521411.value: To determine the atomic configuration in HEAs through coupled experimental and modeling methodology To understand the mechanisms controlling the phase stability in HEAs To establish the scientific principles to design HEAs with desirable FCC dominant crystal structures
rows: To determine the atomic configuration in HEAs through coupled experimental and modeling methodology
To understand the mechanisms controlling the phase stability in HEAs
To establish the scientific principles to design HEAs with desirable FCC dominant crystal structures

521411.label: Realisation of objectives
521411.value: Realisation of the first objective: It is known that various ordered and disordered solid solutions and phases are able to form in the FeCoNiCrCuAlx high entropy alloy (HEA) system, thus it is important to understand atomic configurations in these solid solutions and phases using atomistic models. Furthermore, on the formation of the simple solid solution matrix phase, nano-scale phase precipitation and separation have been observed in FCC or BCC-based HEAs. In order to understand the atomic configurations in these nanoscale phase particles, we have developed simplified models to characterize the precipitation reactions in the FCC-based FeCoNiCrCuAlx HEA, based on the first-principles calculations, and verified the simulation results from the-state-of-the-art scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) observations. The coherent nano-scale phase separation in FCC HEAs has been proven to be energetically favorable, showing that an FCC Cu-rich domain surrounded by Fe, Co, Ni, Cr-rich phases with the L12 ordering and the FCC random structure simultaneously, depending on the Al concentration in these HEAs. All the results have been written up and submitted for publication in open literature. Realisation of the second objective: The relationship between phase stability and physicochemical/thermodynamic properties of alloying components in HEAs has been studied systematically, and the rules on equilibrium phase selection within a certain temperature range have been carefully investigated. Both of the mixing enthalpy and atomic-size difference have been found to be the key factors controlling the formation of solid solutions or intermetallic compounds. And the stability of fcc and bcc solid solutions is well delineated by the valance electron concentration (VEC). Furthermore, a two-parameter physical scheme, utilizing the atomic size polydispersity and mixing enthalpy, has been found to be capable of capturing the mechanism of phase selection between solid solutions and the amorphous phase. Realisation of the third objective: Based on the above achievements, the scientific principles to design HEAs with desirable FCC dominant crystal structures have been established. The following principles should be satisfied simultaneously: the atomic size differences among the constituent elements δ < ~ 0.066; the mixing enthalpy ΔHmix is either slightly positive or insignificantly negative (~ -11.6 < ΔHmix < 3.2 kJ/mol); and the valance electron concentration (VEC) of the system has to be higher (≥8).

521411.label: Major findings and research outcome
521411.value: 1) The phase stability in HEAs and its relationship to the physicochemical and thermodynamic properties of constituent alloying elements have been systematically studied [3-8]. The mixing enthalpy determines whether the solid solution phases or compounds form in the nearly equi-atomic multicomponent alloy systems. Most importantly the VEC is found to be the physical parameter to control the phase stability for FCC or BCC solid solutions. FCC phases are found to be stable at higher VEC (≥8) and instead BCC phases are stable at lower VEC (<6.87). 2) A two-parameter physical scheme has been revealed capturing the mechanism behind the phase selection upon alloying in high-entropy alloys [2,3]. It has been found that solid solutions and the amorphous phase form below and above a critical δ of ~ 0.065, respectively. And a more negative mixing enthalpy ΔHmix (< -12 kJ/mol) favors the amorphous phase formation. The δ-ΔHmix phase selection rule articulates the necessary conditions to form solid solutions or the amorphous phase in HEAs. 3) The phase stability of solid solutions upon temperature effect in a high-entropy Al0.5CoCrCuFeNi alloy has been investigated [1]. The solid solution phases were found to be stable, against the intermetallic compounds, at high temperatures >850 °C and at low temperatures <300 °C. At intermediate temperatures, however, the intermetallic σ-phase co-existed with the solid solution phases. The experimental observations were verified by the thermodynamic calculation results. 4) The atomistic mechanism of nano-scale solid solutions and phase separation in the AlxCoCrCuFeNi HEAs has been investigated as a function of Al concentration (unpublished). Simplified atomic models have been developed, and the ground state formation energies of these atomic configurations were calculated based on the first-principles calculations. The simulation results imply the coherent nano-scale phase separation in FCC AlxCoCrCuFeNi HEAs is energy favorable at an atomic level, showing FCC Cu-rich nano-domains surrounded by Fe, Co, Ni, Cr-rich phase with L12 ordering and random fcc nano-structure, simultaneously. Furthermore, the simulation results agree well with the-state of the-art STEM observations. This work has been done on collaboration with Prof. MW Chen at the Tohoku University, Japan.

521411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
521411.value: The revealing of the effects of VEC, mixing enthalpy and entropy, and atomic size differences on the phase stability provides valuable input for understanding of the phase stability and designing ductile crystal structures in HEAs. Based on the completed investigations, the HEA with desirable FCC dominant crystal structures can be prepared for further development of this research. The alloy composition will be designed based on the established scientific principle: the atomic size differences among the constituent elements δ < ~ 0.066, ~ -11.6 < ΔHmix < 3.2 kJ/mol, and the VEC of the system is higher (≥8). Furthermore, HEAs with desirable mechanical properties (such as high ductility and strength) can be developed, on the basis of the completed research. The ductile FCC solid solutions can be formed in the HEAs based on the proposed scientific principles. Moreover, the investigations on the nano-scale phase precipitation and separation offer great contributions to the unusual mechanical behavior (such as high strength) of HEAs. Therefore, in the near future, HEAs with high strength and ductility will be designed by designing the alloy compositions and controlling the nano-scale phase precipitation. Furthermore, the potential use of these advanced HEAs will be explored.

521411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
521411.value: The study of conventional alloys containing a single major constituent element has been last for many years, and the alloy development effort has approached its maturity. The nature of this research project is an in-depth investigation on the mechanism of phase stability and phase separation in a new family of alloys containing multiple major constituent elements, referred as high entropy alloys, and the research effort has been focused on the development of scientific principles for designing advanced materials with unusual properties of these high entropy alloys. The successful completion of this project is of great significance and value in designing novel high entropy alloys with superior mechanical properties for structural applications in high-tech industries in Hong Kong and the Pearl River Delta Area. Furthermore, we have established CityU as a strong research group in the world active in the high entropy alloy research in Hong Kong.

The detailed 3D water vapor distribution and its variation in the space-time domain will contribute to improving Hong Kong and Mainland China’s capability of weather forecasting and climatologic change monitoring. To investigate a 3D water vapor modeling method by assimilating multi-sensor, multi-resolution water vapor data Owing to the complementary characteristics of the multi-source water vapor data, the assimilation of all the data sources will provide good horizontal and vertical resolutions for the 3D tomography. The optimal 3D grid size will be investigated using the criteria: availability of data, the required resolution of weather modeling, and the computational capacity and response time. 521711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
521711.value: Extreme weather events have caused significant casualties and property damage worldwide in recent times (Goklany, 2009). Floods, as a typical extreme weather phenomenon in China, have claimed more than 700 lives in 2010 alone and about 350 people went missing, resulting in US$21 billion loss and damage (Bloomberg, 2010). A reliable and precise weather forecasting system for extreme weather event is highly desired. The precision and reliability of a weather forecasting system is greatly affected by the amount, precision, and geographical uniformity of water vapor data that are input to numerical weather prediction (NWP) models to continuously update the NWP integration calculation. Water vapor is highly variable in space and time and significantly influences many processes of the weather and climate. It plays an important role in cloud formation, the heat budget of the Earth, redistribution of water, energy within the global system, and the control of temperature in the troposphere. In order to better monitor and predict extreme weather events, it is essential to elucidate water vapor information (including quantity & uncertainty in horizontal distribution, vertical profile, and in the time domain) through comprehensive and precise observation & modeling methods. Such an elucidation will provide crucial data to weather forecasting and climate modeling systems. The project aims to develop an innovative continuous three-dimensional (3D) water vapor tomographic modeling technique using a multiple sensor system based on both ground and satellite-borne observation techniques. It is expected that the continuous, precise and reliable water vapor 3D distribution and variation data for the mainland China and Hong Kong region can be numerically elucidated and characterized, and will provide key input parameters to NWP. The research will contribute to the improvement of NWP capability for Hong Kong and mainland China (particularly for extreme weather prediction) which will have an enormous potential for the reduction of casualties and property loss. The outcomes of this research are fundamental for climate change monitoring, hydrological cycle research, planning and prediction of agriculture production, water resource management, and environment related decision-making process. For instance, manmade rain operation is a commonly used technique in China. For such, precise knowledge of 3D water vapor is needed in cloud seeding as accurate locations and concentrations of water vapor should be known beforehand to ensure successful cloud seeding.

521711.label: Realisation of objectives
521711.value: Pursuing the above objectives, a lot of researches have been carried out in this project. The three main objectives listed above have been successfully accomplished. 1) For the first objective, an innovative multi-observational 3D tomographic technique was developed and performed by using water vapor observations derived from GPS (Global Positioning System), radiosonde, WVR (Water Vapor Radiometer), NWP (Numerical Weather Prediction), sunphotometer and synoptic stations in Hong Kong. Water vapor data from GPS, WVR, sunphotometer and synoptic stations are directly used as inputs for the tomography model. We developed methods to use GPS-inferred SWD (Slant Wet Delay) measurements with low elevation angles, which are normally discarded in previous research. In our study, we adopted the NWP data to calculate the part of SWD outside the tomography modeling area for those GPS signals with low elevation angles. For the radiosonde data, they are used as vertical a priori information in the tomography model. The Helmert variance component estimation method is employed to determine weights for the different types of observations. 2) For the second objective, a new method was developed to optimize the discretization of tomography model. This optimization method comprises four parts: top boundary determination, vertical layer discretization, horizontal boundary optimization, and selection of optimal horizontal and vertical resolutions. In this method, radiosonde profiles are used to determine the top boundary and discretize the vertical layers for the tomography model. We have analyzed 40 years of radiosonde data and have determined the optimal height for the top boundary in tomographic modeling to be approximately 8.5 km. The horizontal boundary optimization is achieved by moving the voxel location in latitude and longitude directions until the maximum number of voxels with ray crossings is reached. The optimal horizontal and vertical resolutions have been determined based on extensive tomographic experiments. 3) For the last objective, the performance of the developed tomographic method was evaluated based on extensive experiments covering a 6-month period from 1 May to 31 October of 2013 in Hong Kong. The tomographic results were comprehensively assessed by water vapor data from GPS, radiosonde and ECMWF (European Center for Medium-range Weather Forecasts). The performance of tomographic solutions was also evaluated in heavy precipitation conditions in Hong Kong and good agreements have been observed between the modeled water vapor data and observed ones.

521711.label: Major findings and research outcome
521711.value: The major findings and research outcomes of this project could be drawn: 1) Using the new developed voxel optimization method, the tomographic voxel of Hong Kong region was optimized. The top boundary of the tomography model is set as 8.5 km as the statistical analysis of 40-year (1973-2012) radiosonde profiles showed water vapor above 8.5 km can be negligible. The optimal tomography model discretization for Hong Kong was determined from a 20-day-long (2-21 October 2012) experiment. The horizontal resolutions are 0.08° in both longitude and latitude directions. For the optimal vertical resolutions, from ground upward the layer thicknesses are: 400 m for the bottom 5 layers, 500 m for 4 layers, 600 m for 3 layers, 700 m for 1 layer, and 1,000 m for the top 2 layers. 2) The multi-observational tomography was performed using water vapor data from GPS, radiosonde, WVR, NWP, sunphototmeter, and synoptic observations in Hong Kong from May to October 2013. We found that the best vertical water vapor a priori information is the average of 3-day radiosonde observations made prior to the tomographic epoch. In the evaluation by radiosonde profiles, the tomography yielded an overall accuracy of 7.13 mm/km. For vertical layers, RMS error generally decreased with altitude from 11.44 mm/km at the lowest layer (0 to 0.4 km) to 3.30 mm/km at the uppermost layer (7.5 to 8.5 km). 3) We investigated the evolution of water vapor during three heavy precipitation events occurred on 22 July 2010, 21 May 2013 and 30 March 2014 respectively in Hong Kong using tomographic solutions. It is found that the total ZWD increases prior to the onset of the heavy precipitation and experiences a decrease after the heavy rain pouring. The fluctuations in the total ZWD is observed largely from the water vapor variations in layers above 3 km. The remarkable water vapor fluctuations in vertical layers can be seen as precursors to detect precipitations as they reflect the atmospheric instability. 4) A comprehensive evaluation of 9 ZHD and 18 ZWD models was performed using 10-year (2003-2012) radiosonde data collected from 92 stations of China as references. ECMWF ZHD achieves the highest accuracy of 2.8 mm, while the Baby ZHD model is the second-best with an accuracy of 6.0 mm. ECMWF ZWD model has the best performance with an accuracy of 21.4 mm, followed by the Baby semi-empirical whose RMS error is about 33 mm.

521711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
521711.value: In the outlook of this research, the following work can be carried out for further studies: 1) With the upgrade of Russian GLONASS and the rapid development of Chinese Beidou and European Galileo, the number of satellites visible to any location at any time will increase greatly, implying more possible signals traversing the troposphere. This will improve the geometry of the tomography and thus have a profound influence on the tomographic solutions. It is recommended that research should be carried out to investigate the benefit of additional GNSS constellations to the water vapor tomography. 2) It is suggested that tomographic water vapor fields can be used in conjunction with other meteorological data such as weather radar and wind profiler to detect the extreme weathers. 3) Tropospheric delay is one of the major error sources in range measurements of many space geodetic observation systems. Further research should be undertaken to apply the tomographic water vapor data in the correction of wet delay for applications such as GNSS positioning and SAR data compensation.

521711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
521711.value: Water vapor is a precursor of cloud, rain, snow, sleet, hail and other precipitations. The water vapor distribution plays a key role in the evolution of atmospheric storm systems and vertical stability of the atmosphere. Water vapor also acts as a major error source in range measurements of many space geodetic observation systems as it can retard the microwave signals in the propagation through the troposphere. Therefore it is important to acquire the accurate 3D distribution of atmospheric water vapor, not only for short-term weather forecasting but also for compensating tropospheric wet delay in range measurements. This project developed an innovative tomographic technique to retrieve the spatio-temporal distribution of water vapor with high accuracy. The high spatial and temporal water vapor fields from the tomography are very useful for the short-term severe weather forecasting. The enhanced capability of severe weather prediction can contribute to hazard mitigation in view of social and economic benefits. In addition, the high accuracy tomographic results can be adopted to correct tropospheric wet delay for geodetic observations such as Global Positioning System (GPS). It is expected to improve the accuracy of these observations significantly.
