523511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
523511.value: Physical computing creates digital computing systems that are equipped with sensing and actuating functionality to respond and interact with the analog physical world. It helps us to make more interesting connections between the physical and computer worlds. In particular, it supports human creativity by using computers to “capture and support a person’s expression”, and, most provocatively, to change it. In this project, we propose the design and development of an integrated framework for customizable physical computing systems that are designed for social interactions. We envision user-composable systems digitally enhanced with computational, communication, sensing and actuating capabilities and functionalities that people can use to interact with other systems and people who may not be in the same physical space. Of especial interest to us are systems that are pervasive, integrated into the environment via everyday objects and activities and wearable, that interact with the full body of the user. The system supports and encourages social interaction and collaboration. An example of such a system could be a set of coupled virtual rooms in which people may interact with objects around them to create art or music. Another example could be a wearable system that collects emotions signalled by the wearer, and conveys them in various formats to a friend in another location. There has been much work in the area of physical computing, but much of it from the infrastructural/technological aspect, some of it from the interaction standpoint. However, very little attention has been focused on social interaction, which is known to involve issues different from that of generic human-computer interaction. The majority of these systems are also specialized-purpose, and there has been very little focus on systems that can be composed or constructed by non-experts. Our objective is to bring together concepts from human-computer interaction (specifically: tangible interaction), social computing and pervasive computing into the design of this framework. Specifically, we wish to design a coherent, consistent platform that will relate the functional, computational and social concepts in a manner that is understandable and learnable by novices and lay people. We believe that our framework has application potential in a number of areas, including creative design, digital toys and education. In this project, we will study two diverse application areas for our platform: computational education for children, and tangible social interaction for the elderly. 523511.label: Realisation of objectives
523511.value: The objectives of this project were the following (objectives have been renumbered for easy reference.) 1. To design and develop a platform for supporting pervasive, physical, user-composable system for social interaction, including: a. To propose a theoretical framework that will integrate computational concepts, physical functionality and social communication in a coherent and intuitive manner b. To design and develop a virtual platform and abstraction network that will intelligently extract semantic information from the incoming signals from the sensors, and translate semantic information into outgoing signals for the actuators; c. To devise an intuitive method for customizing the system. d. To evaluate the system empirically for usability and effectiveness We are pleased to report that the project has been successfully completed, and all the objectives have been fulfilled: Objective 1a: We investigated the link between computational concepts, physical functionality and social communication through several different kinds of physical input: writing dynamics and ink brush calligraphy (Li et al 2014, Huang et al 2012, Tang et al 2013), physical movement (Lo et al 2013), heart and respiratory rate (Fu et al 2014, Fu et al, in submission), mouse movements (Fu et al 2014, Fu et al, in submission, Li et al, 2016), and eye movements (Huang et al 2014, Huang et al 2016). We then investigated the correlation between these concepts and human perception, including writing errors (Tang et al 2013), volume and tempo of music (Huang et al 2012), and graphics effects in paintings (Li et al 2014). These correlations were proposed based on concepts from metaphoric congruence and synesthesia and validated empirically. We also investigated the linkage between heart and respiratory rate and stress/excitement in game playing and movie watching (Fu et al 2014, Fu et al, in submission), and between eye movements and interaction events (mouse clicks and typing) (Huang et al 2014, Huang et al 2016), as well as between human mouse movements and the human’s engagement in reading difficulties (Li et al 2016). The core concepts behind these findings were integrated into the overall platform and contributed to its development. Objective 1b: The input signals that we worked with in the work described in the previous objective are collected from diverse sensors, such as light sensors and cameras. These signals are analyzed for their semantic information. This includes the identification of heart and respiratory rate from light sensors (Fu et al 2014, Fu et al in submission), extraction of writing mechanics from infra-red depth images (Huang et al 2012, Li et al 2014), and the identification of human emotions from visual images (Huang et al 2016, Li et al 2016). On the output side, these signals were translated into music effects (Tang et al 2013, Huang et al 2012), graphics effects (Li et al 2014), visual attention (Huang et al 2014, Huang et al 2016). Objective 1, Objective 1c, Objective 1d The overall platform that resulted from this work is called i*Chameleon. This is a configurable and extensible multimodal framework for developing highly interactive applications that incorporates a comprehensive system development cycle. I*Chameleon uses a publish/subscribe middleware, based on the well-known MVC paradigm. The objective of i*Chameleon is to support and facilitate the development of multimodal applications through a middleware communication paradigm that supports user-composability by allowing components to be plugged-in to and detached from the runtime kernel dynamically. The platform supports pervasiveness through a kernel that is able to bind to different components according to the task or the content environment in order to provide the best experience for end-users at runtime. The multimodal nature of the components supports physical and tangible interaction. Since the development of such applications would be cumbersome and complex, i*Chameleon classifies components into different categories, based on their functionality, interaction style and clear delineation of development roles, with clear separation-of-concerns between four different roles: device engineers, modality designers, programmers and interaction designers that correspond to four concurrent tasks: (1) device interface modeling, (2) modality modeling, (3) signal processing algorithm implementation and (4) interactive command customization for application development. The platform has been validated in a prototype application system -- an interactive robotic exhibit -- that demonstrates the development process according to our suggested procedure. The results show that i*Chameleon can clearly separate the application into different components and each component can be deployed independently. This work has been submitted to the Journal of Systems and Software and it achieves all five project objectives. Student Training We admitted one PhD student, Li Jiajia, with the funding from this project. She has an MSc from Beihang University, which is one of the top engineering schools in China. She arrived at our department in Spring of 2012. Jiajia first encountered some challenges adjusting to the new environment and the new topic, but she has since adjusted and is performing well, and is producing research output. She has one paper in a highly-respected international conference (ACM Multimedia 2014), another one in SAC 2016, and there are two more papers in the pipeline. She is now being funded as a part-time research assistant under another grant and she is scheduled to submit her thesis this year. I believe that she will be able to defend successfully. We have been less successful on the undergraduate research front. First, we had difficult recruiting a suitable student. There are not that many undergraduate students who have both potential and ability, so those who do have both are under heavy demand from all colleagues. The first student whom we identified turned out to already be funded under the “undergraduate research provision” by another colleague. Even though he was interested in our project, he could not be paid, but since he very much wanted to get involved, he ended up working for us for free. Another student whom we almost recruited failed to turn in a “trial” project that we had set for her to test her commitment and abilities. Finally, the student who we ended up recruiting had problems with the “part-time only” regulation caused challenges, as he had to work full-time during the summer to meet financial obligations. We were willing to pay him to work for us as a full-time student helper, but this is apparently not allowed under the undergraduate research provision. The project ended that summer, so we did not finish the part of the funding designated to provide for undergraduate research. During the few months that he worked for us, the undergraduate student (Lui Kin To) helped us to run experiments and perform signal analysis from light sensors to extract heart rate and respiratory rate (Fu et al. 2014). He was very interested in the research and he has proposed to continue with this theme for his final year project.

523511.label: Major findings and research outcome
523511.value: This project has resulted in the following major findings and outcomes: 1. We have empirically confirmed a linkage between common physical activities (writing and body movement), and effects in music and art (tempo, volume, blurriness, level of detail), and developed an ontology that links together these artforms. (Huang et al 2012, Tang et al 2013, Li et al 2014) 2. We studied eye movements around different types of interaction events (mouseclicks on various targets and typing), and found evidence that the assumption of “users are looking where they click” that has been held in previous work is not accurate. (Huang et al 2016) We deployed these findings in a real-use eye tracking system. Compared with the state-of-the-art approach, the system gets better results using our revised assumption (Huang et al 2014, Huang et al 2016) 3. We studied human facial behavior, as captured by off-the-shelf webcams, and their correspondence to two interactive activities (movie watching, Huang et al 2016 and reading, Li et al 2016). We devised a novel method to capture the fine-grained affect annotations from coarse annotations (Huang et al 2016) and another multimodal method that combines facial expressions with mouse behavior to deduce user stress (Li et al 2016). 4. We developed i*Chameleon, a configurable and extensible multimodal framework that facilitates the development of highly interactive applications with a comprehensive system development cycle. The main contributions of the platform are as follows: • Classification of interaction components leads to separation of concerns: The pervasive multimodal interface can be classified into three conceptual components, modalities and interactive devices, interactive commands and fusion algorithms. A concrete role distribution can be defined at the early stage of development and provides a clear structure for each component within the interaction cloud. • Self-description modeling language supports declarative modeling of aspects: The language forms an integrating channel between modalities, devices, data and interactions. This approach allows fusion engineers, device engineers and interaction designers to build the system independently and plug-in their components into a common interaction cloud. • Dynamic binding among components: The platform provides a mechanism to support changes in the binding between interaction components from static to dynamic, according to the runtime execution environment and user preferences. The platform is validated through a proof-of-concept system which demonstrates the versatility of the framework and the ease of developing multimodal applications. (Lo et al, in submission)

523511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
523511.value: We feel that the next step for human-computer interaction is the adaptation to the human affective dimension. So far, most HCI work has focused on the development of new devices (e.g. the multitouch screen was a big step forward), or the integration of multimodal interaction (e.g. touch and voice, or tangible interaction). Some work (such as ours) has looked at the semantics and the human perception (e.g. the metaphors) behind the interaction commands. However, current interaction paradigms still treat the person as a static entity. There is much work in recognizing human affect, but most of this work looks at the human in one-way activities (e.g. watching movies or reading), or in interactive activities involving other humans (e.g. turn taking), but very little deals with the affective state of the user in human computer interaction. This is despite much research showing that emotion and perception play a significant role in human cognition and thus has a big impact on human performance. We thus feel that the next step should be expanding the framework to incorporate the human affect as part of the system.

523511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
523511.value: In this project, we looked at how we can make it easy for developers to create computer applications that use more than one form of input. Even though it is natural for human beings to communicate using multiple forms of input simultaneously (e.g. pointing and speaking), this is not easy for developers to implement, because the different sensors use different programming languages or require different forms of commands. Our i*Chameleon platform is a unified platform that takes care of the low-level details and lets developers focus on the high-level operations. It is modular and designed to let multiple people work on the same project effectively. In addition, we investigated into the meanings behind some innovative forms of input, such as calligraphy writing, and output, such as music and painting. We looked into human perception to see what sorts of input make sense to the human and are natural when translated to the output. We also studied how human beings behave when they are interacting with the computer, and discovered that some of the assumptions that people had about eye behavior were not correct. These findings were used to develop i*Chameleon, and were also validated in experiments.

523611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
523611.value: 在中国，中国政府坚持低碳经济和可持续发展的决定对制造商的监管环境意味一个重大的改变。加大节能和提高效率对制造商来说则越为重要。从商业的角度来看，自然资源的匮乏和日渐增加的成本迫使工业界要更加有效地利用能源。减少使用能源和公用事业能够帮助企业节约成本，变得更有竞争力。工厂需要对能源价格上涨和政府的严格政策迅速作出反应，因为中国一直致力于建立一个节能低碳的经济社会。从社会的角度来看，全球变暖是个每个人都应该关注的问题。 纺织制造工业需要大量的能源资源。因为在纺织过程中，能源成本相对于其他成本的组成部分来说比较高，因此若要减少成本来抵抗全球竞争，能源管理则变得越来越重要。要减少能源的损失并挽回失去的能源，在制造过程中测量和监控能源的利用则非常必要，尤其是在那些需要大量能源和水的行业，比如纺织业。所以，有效地进行能源管理是提高企业的竞争优势和促进绿色可持续方针的关键因素。然而，没有人将能源的使用与制造活动联系起来。将RFID与其他传感器网络技术（如，ZigBee）则有可能建立一个数据丰富的制造环境，来支持和提高能源管理中的决策过程。无线传感器网络（WSN）或基于射频识别（RFID）的智能决策支持系统（IDSS）需要为收集有关其使用的实时信息并运用所收集的信息发挥重要的作用，使得能源利用在制造过程中得到最优化。 本文的目的是研究智能决策支持系统（IDSS）的结构和决策模型基于纺织制造商实时车间的能量数据来对能量利用进行动态监控，分析和管理，以达到有效利用能源的目的。IDSS能够监控和测量与能源有关的绩效并与其他的关键绩效指标（KPI）一起评估。 它能够结合生产管理系统来提供可视化的能源消耗，因此能够帮助决策者提高能源效率和最优化。本项目能够： （1）为纺织制造过程中的能源管理而开发IDSS，在此过程中产生的复杂情况，利用软件系统方法进行分析； （2）为提高能源效率而开发的IDSS建立数学模型； （3）设计开发一个基于RFID/WSN的智能决策支持系统原型系统，通过收集和同步实时能源数据来支持制造过程中的决策。 本研究将会与研究用户进行有针对性地合作，它将会成为原型系统进行测试和评估的试验床。项目成果包括：（1）为纺织制造过程中的能源管理而开发IDSS，在此过程中产生的复杂情况，利用软件系统方法进行的分析；（2）为提高能源效率而开发的IDSS建立的最优化模型；（3）一个基于RFID/WSN的原型系统来监控和管理生产过程中的能源利用。

523611.label: Major findings and research outcome
523611.value: In the recent decades, the advancement of environmental technology and introduction of comprehensive environmental management systems have highlighted the intangible benefits of environmental management practices and their potential to drive organizational competitiveness. Accumulating evidence on the potential benefits of environmental protectionism has given rise to a series of environmental management practices and systems, such as energy informatics, environmental management standardization frameworks, and green supplier management and collaboration. However, existing literature lacks a clear conceptualization and a coherent theoretical framework of environmental management. In addition, no systematic framework exists for the design and implementation of environmental management practices that guide organizations in deciding on the practices or systems that they should implement given their organizational situations. Thus, this study aims to develop an energy and utility maturity framework for systematic measurement and management of natural resource consumption. Specifically, the proposed framework, energy and utility management maturity model (EUMMM), was designed based on the capability maturity model integration (CMMI). EUMMM has two major functions. First, it provides an assessment framework for analyzing the maturity level of energy and utility management in organizations. Second, it provides a progressive framework to guide organizational advancement in energy and utility management. A collaborative pilot study was conducted to validate the effectiveness, practicability, and convenience of the EUMMM. The results indicated that EUMMM successfully led the participating companies to move along the environmental management maturity path. Theoretically, this study extends the application of CMMI to the context of natural resource management and develops a progressive framework for energy and utility management maturation. Practically, this study provides a robust guideline for practitioners in analyzing and advancing energy and utility maturity levels to achieve a sustainable manufacturing process. The IDSS prototype system was built and tested in a pilot company. The results of the prototype system evaluation are satisfactory and support the contention that is more effective in supporting the decision making in the manufacturing process by collecting and synchronizing real-time energy data.

523611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
523611.value: Our findings are from the application of EUMMM and IDSS prototype system based on a single company which may not be generalized to different environments. Thus further research is necessary to verify EUMMM and prototype system in organizations with different scales, and business environments (e.g. different industries). We believe that future research can improve the proposed framework and further contribute to the field.

First, it provides an assessment framework for analyzing the maturity level of energy and utility management in organizations. Second, it provides a progressive framework to guide organizational advancement in energy and utility management. A collaborative pilot study was conducted to validate the effectiveness, practicability, and convenience of the EUMMM. The IDSS prototype system was built and tested in a pilot site. 523811.label: Project Objectives
523811.value: To experimentally investigate the polarization curves of H-SOFC cathodes made from different materials and preparation methods and operated under different operating conditions. Three representative cathode materials will be tested with different microstructures obtained using different preparation conditions. The 2D images of the H-SOFC cathodes will be characterized by scanning electron microscope. The polarization curves of the H-SOFC cathodes will be measured by the A.C. impedance method using an electrochemical station at intermediate temperatures (673K-973K). To establish the 3D microstructure of H-SOFC cathodes from 2D images by using a stochastic reconstruction technique. The density and distribution of electrochemically active TPBs, the transport properties, i.e. porosity, tortuosity and pore size, will then be evaluated. The effect of preparation conditions on the cathode microstructure will be examined. To simulate the coupled transport and elementary reaction kinetics at pore scale with the LBM model. The diffusion of gas specpoies in the pores, transport of electrons/ions in the solid structure and reactions at the active TPBs will be fully considered and simulated. The effects of material type, the material composition and sintering temperature on the density of active TPBs and the cathode polarization will be studied in detail.

523811.label: Major findings and research outcome
523811.value: Both experimental study and mathematical modelling study on solid oxide fuel cells with proton conducting electrolyte (H-SOFC) have been conducted. Advanced H-SOFC cathodes have been fabricated in Prof. Xia’s lab. The SDC+SSC composite cathode is infiltrated with SSC nanoparticles to achieve a high performance. The cathode microstructure has been characterized by SEM. The electrochemical performance of the H-SOFC with the SDC+SSC cathode has been measured by an electrochemical workstation. The H-SOFC consists of SDC+SSC cathode, BZCY electrolyte, and NiO+BZCY anode. Improved performance of H-SOFC have been obtained by controlling the nanostructure of H-SOFC electrodes. The nano/microstructure properties of the H-SOFC electrodes were characterized and obtained. The electrochemical performance of the H-SOFC has been characterized by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurement, polarization measurement and current-voltage measurement. Different numerical reconstruction methods have been examined. We believe that the electrode microstructure generated from numerical packing and sintering could yield the most accurate and reliable microstructure. Based on a Kinetic Monte Carlo model, we can simulate the sintering process of the SOFC electrodes and capture the electrode microstructure evolution with time. The microstructures of advanced nanostructured SOFC electrode are also numerically reconstructed. The percolation behavior of the reconstructed electrode is analyzed. It is found that the nanoparticles start to form continuous networks when the infiltration loading is higher than a threshold value. The important microstructure properties such as the triple phase boundary (TPB) length, effective conductivity, porosity, tortuosity etc have been analyzed for the reconstructed electrodes. For modeling the SOFC performance, some macroscopic models have been developed to capture the coupled transport and reaction phenomena in SOFCs. Simulations have been performed to analyze the reaction in the cell, gas diffusion and heat transfer in SOFCs for power generation. A three-dimensional lattice Boltzmann model (LBM) has been developed for simulating the transport and reaction processes in fuel cells. The model has been applied for SOFC and proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). In the LBM simulation, the three-dimensional microstructures of a porous layer are numerically reconstructed by a random generation method. The LBM simulations focus on the effects of the porous layer properties on the reaction and transport processes. It is found that the mass transport is strongly affected by the microstructure of the porous layer. Results indicate that an optimized design of porous layer porosity and the combination of various pore sizes may improve the gas transport and reaction kinetics in fuel cells.

523811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
523811.value: The research results offer insightful information on how the microstructure properties of the porous electrode affect the performance of electrochemical systems. The results are useful for enhancing the performance of various electrochemical systems by optimizing the porous microstructures. Based on the present project, the PI is now extending his research from SOFC to other types of fuel cells and other electrochemical systems.

523811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
523811.value: Solid oxide fuel cell with proton conducting electrolyte (H-SOFC) is promising for efficient energy conversion from fuel to electricity. The cathode microstructure is the key for H-SOFC performance improvement as the cathode is the limiting factor for H-SOFC and the cathode performance is highly dependent on its microstructure. This project aims to understand the microstructure of H-SOFC cathode by numerical reconstruction and its effect on fuel cell performance by pore scale simulation. The research is significant in improving the fuel cell performance by engineering the electrode microstructures. The results of the project can directly benefit the fuel cell community for developing high performance cells for efficient energy conversion.

524111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
524111.value: Maintaining thermal comfort and generating hot water in buildings consumes over 30% of global energy supplies. One of the key technologies that may help drastically reduce these consumption is thermal energy or cooling storage (TES). This project aims to develop phase-change-materials (PCM) based active TES technologies that can maximize the use of natural heating and cooling sources via solar thermal collectors and evaporative coolers, and raise the energy efficiency of the chillers operating at off-peak period. Utilizing the latent heat of melting/solidification processes, a PCM based TES system has two perceived advantages: it can store heat at a small temperature difference between the charging source and discharging user, and can potentially complete the charging in a short period. The former is critical in space-constrained urban applications, and the latter is critical in utilizing natural sources. Different PCM forms, namely bulk PCM, PCM/water emulsion and PCM micro-capsule/water slurry, will be experimentally investigated, and the storage unit involving heat-exchanger and fluid flow will be designed based upon optimization principles. This will be achieved through multi-disciplinary research collaboration, involving chemical engineering research and heat transfer investigation and optimization design. In the PCM preparation, nano-additives will be used to reduce the supercooling degree, which is related to the thermodynamic metastable phenomenon; and the optimization will be enhanced based on the constructal theory. In the optimization analysis, the material and preparation/processing costs of PCM media will be taken into account. It is expected that the new PCM and TES design to be developed will offer good life-cycle carbon reduction performances in building heating and cooling and hot water production. 维持建筑环境的热舒适及生活热水供应用去了三分之一的全球能源供应。蓄热及蓄冷（TES）技术则是一项可大量减少此类能耗的应用技术。 本项目旨在开发以相变材料（PCM）为蓄热介质的TES技术，以最大限度地利用太阳能及蒸发式冷却类的可再生天然冷热源，或低峰时段的电力制冷或供热。利用PCM的溶解-固化的相变潜热的TES系统有两项优点：冷热源与需求端的温差及蓄热段的时间可大大减小。前者对于空间紧张的城市建筑至关重要，而后者对于利用可再生天然冷源至关重要。我们会实验研究三种典型PCM应用形式，即纯PCM液体, 水基PCM乳液和水基微胶囊化PCM浆液， 并优化设计相应的蓄热设备。研究过程涉及到化工，传热及优化三方面的跨专业合作。PCM的制备则采用纳米添加剂，以减小热力学现象过冷度。而在优化蓄热设备方面，我们将采用构型理论。最终的目的是开发新一代生命周期内最低碳排放的建筑用主动式蓄热及蓄冷技术。

524111.label: Realisation of objectives
524111.value: 1. The PCM-water emulsion, using n-hexadecane as the core material, with working temperature at 17 oC was successfully developed by using a disperser with high rotary speed and proper surfactants. The droplet sizes of the emulsion, ranging from 1 to 10 μm, can be precisely controlled by changing the rotary speed of the disperser. Carbon nano tubes (CNTs) were used as additives to control the supercooling degree of developed PCM emulsion. Effective modification processes and proper surfactants were determined to achieve a desired effect that the modified CNT particles can be well dispersed in PCM at various concentrations. 2. The stable of the emulsion was evaluated and results show that it was stable for months, and there was no distinct growth in droplet sizes and phase separation occurred. The bi-surfactant system with Tween and Span was effective to enhance the stability of the PCM-water emulsion in multiple phase change cycles. 3. The thermal performance of PCM emulsions with different concentrations of nucleating agent was analyzed by differential scanning calorimeter (DSC). The results showed the heat capacity of the emulsion decreases with the water proportion correspondingly. Furthermore, the supercooling of the bulk PCM and PCM emulsion were both significantly decreased by adding nucleating agent. The results showed that there was a minimum effective concentration to reduce the supercooling for the PCM emulsion. The viscosity of the developed PCM emulsions was determined by a rotation viscometer. The appeared viscosities at low shear speed at 25°C could be from 150 to 320 mPa•s. 4. The new set of performance indices were used to evaluate the performance of active latent-heat storage devices. A small-scale air conditioning system integrated with a coil in tank system was used for the experiment. It is estimated that the volumetric thermal storage capacity of the MPCM slurry system is nearly twice that of water in the temperature range of 8 oC to 18 oC. However, the charging/discharging rate of the MPCM storage system was lower than the stratified water storage tank (SWST) system. NHT (Numerical heat transfer) analysis of the transient heat transfer process in a thermal storage unit was carried out, and methods to obtain the performance indicators were found with three different thermal storage media, namely water, soil and PCM. The analysis consists of the scale analysis of the early stages of natural convection in the liquid, and an analysis of the entire duration of the melting process.

524111.label: Major findings and research outcome
524111.value: Modified CNT particles showed a better performance in reducing the supercooling degree of PCM compared with original CNT particles [1]. Low concentrations of modified MWCNT nano-particles were effective to reduce the supercooling degree in the PCM/water emulsions. There was a minimum effective concentration of the nucleating agent, and it was around 0.2 wt% for the bulk PCM and 0.6 wt% for PCM emulsions. [2, 4] The latent heat of emulsion was at approximate 81.49 J g-1 and freezing temperature was around 16 °C. The apparent viscosities of the emulsions at low shear speed at 25 °C with SDS, Tween 80, and Tween 20 as surfactants were 340±87, 213±24, and 173±29 mPa s, respectively. An obvious shear-thinning phenomenon was observed. As the surfactants participated, the emulsions presented an obvious non-Newtonian fluid behavior. [4] There was no distinct droplets size growth observed and the emulsions could restore uniformity after being stirred. But after freeze/thaw treatments, a lucid oil layer over the emulsion could appear meaning a part of emulsion droplets were destroyed. By adding the Span as the co-surfactant, the stability of the PCM emulsion in the multiple phase change cycles was enhanced. The emulsion with Tween 80 and Span 80 could endure ten cycles with no obvious demulsification phenomenon appearing. The history of energy storage and the movement of the melting front agree well with the theoretical predictions was obtained by numerical analysis. A cylindrical body of PCM with vertical heated pipe in the center is perhaps the simplest possible configuration, and yet a common element of many complete storage designs, in which the fundamental characteristics of the melting process are involved [3]. It is possible to increase the global performance of the storage system by varying and selecting geometric features such as spiral pitch and diameter, and number of concentric spirals. In addition, scale analysis combined with numerical simulations is a powerful method for advancing the design of thermal energy storage systems. [5] Using the new set of performance indices, volumetric thermal storage capacity of the MPCM slurry system was nearly twice that of water system in the same temperature range of 8 oC to 18 oC. The charging/discharging rate of the SWST system was significantly higher than that of the coil in tank MPCM slurry system at a given heat transfer surface area to storage medium volume ratio, A/Vt = 5.6 m-1. [6]

524111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
524111.value: For the stability of the developed PCM emulsion, in spite of a cream layer appearing in the storage period, there was no distinct droplets size growth observed and the emulsions could restore uniformity after being stirred. Also the bi-surfactant system was effective to enhance the stability of the PCM / water emulsion in multiple phase change cycles. But emulsions are thermodynamically unstable systems and will separate into phases in a quite long run. (Nissim Garti, 1997) The better way to enhance the stability of the emulsion, especially after repeatedly phase change circles, is one of the proposed courses of action. For the NHT analysis of the transient heat transfer process in a thermal storage unit, the challenge is to properly model the potential convection that may occur in the liquid phase of PCM, though it may be neglected in most application conditions. For the coil in tank thermal energy storage (TES) system, the response time of the system was not as short as expected, especially when compared with the system using thermal stratification. Therefore, the enhancement of heat transfer of the TES system using PCM warrants further investigation.

524111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
524111.value: Maintaining thermal comfort and generating hot water in buildings consumes over 30% of global energy supplies. One of the key technologies that may help drastically reduce these consumption is thermal energy or cooling storage (TES). In this project, we developed novel PCM emulsions, and PCM based active TES technologies that can maximize the use of natural heating and cooling sources via solar thermal collectors and evaporative coolers, and raise the energy efficiency of the chillers operating at off-peak period. It can store heat at a small temperature difference between the charging source and discharging user, and can potentially complete the charging in a short period. The former is critical in space-constrained urban applications, and the latter is critical in utilizing natural sources. In the PCM emulsion preparation, nano-additives were used to reduce the supercooling degree, which is related to the thermodynamic metastable phenomenon; and the optimization was enhanced based on the constructal theory. In the optimization analysis, the material and preparation/processing costs of PCM media were all taken into account. The new PCM emulsion and TES design developed can offer good life-cycle carbon reduction performances in building heating and cooling and hot water production.

524211.label: Realisation of objectives
524211.value: Objective 1: A Cluster Beam deposited (SCBD) system was used to prepare the samples. The system was upgraded by adding a translator, mass flow controllers and quartz monitor. They are important components of the system. We determined the best conditions of (i) sample fabrication specified by the discharge frequency, duration of gas admission, delay time and duration of electrical pulses, discharge voltage V and expansion chamber pressure; and (ii) post-oxidation specified by the annealing temperature and duration. The films were characterized using atomic force microscopy (AFM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD). Objective 2: The original proposed idea of using SiO2 to form a water-resistive coating on SCBD ZnO for immersion dissolved oxygen measurements was replaced by using two other polymer coatings, namely a sprayed agent named as “NeverWet” from Rust-Oleum Corporation and spin-coated polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). They can form highly hydrophobic coatings and allow gas molecules to pass through. Objective 3: Room-temperature UV photocurrent measurements were measured for (i) uncoated and polymer-coated SCBD ZnO films in gas-phase environment (including vacuum), and (ii) polymer-coated SCBD ZnO films in water, as a function of oxygen concentration [O2]. The value of [O2] for the measurements in gas-phase and in water was varied from 0 to 20.8% (balanced in N2) and 0 to 9.1 mg/l, respectively. A system and procedures were set up for the measurements. We found some systematic features of the time dependence of the current in the samples under UV illumination and after the UV light was turned off. Objective 4: We proposed a simple model by assuming that the time dependence of the current was jointly controlled by (i) photo generation of electron-hole pairs (absent in dark), (ii) oxygen adsorption (desorption in dark) and trapping (release in dark) of electrons, and (iii) recombination of electron-hole pairs. The model has practical meaning for giving characteristic time constants and saturated current, which are all derived from curve fitting. They can be correlated to the [O2] value in the measurement environment, so that [O2] can be evaluated without the need of waiting for the measurement process to reach equilibrium. Difficulties: Objective 1 was not 100% achieved because (i) some time was spent to upgrade the SCBD system, (ii) the low melting point of Sn caused some difficulties in deposition and post-oxidation, (iii) the Research Associate and Research Student suddenly left the team to cause some delay.

524211.label: Major findings and research outcome
524211.value: Objective 1 We upgraded and use our SCBD system in the project period to produce the papers and pending patents as listed in Part C. Nano-crystallized nanocluster film exhibiting desired oxygen sensing properties were prepared by using 1% O2 in argon (Ar) as the reactant gas; with the gas pulse rate and width set at 4 Hz and 0.32 ms; time delay of electrical pulses and pulse width at 0.65 ms and 0.12 ms, discharge voltage V at 900 V, supersonic expansion pressure at 3-5 mTorr. The sample needed to be post-oxidized at 500-550oC for 30 minutes (see manuscript in Part C). Objective 2 We fabricated two types of water-resistive coatings on SCBD films to resist water in DO detection experiments. They are “NeverWet” and PDMS. We mainly focused on the former. It consisted of a “base part” and a “coat part”. The former contains mainly organic solvents and polypropylene, and the latter contains mainly acetone, silicones and siloxanes. The materials were sprayed and then spin-coated on a ZnO film at a rate of 500 revolutions/min. A semi-transparent hydrophobic coating allowing oxygen molecules to penetrate was formed. Objective 3 Room-temperature UV-assisted resistive response of uncoated SCBD ZnO films to oxygen was detected in gas-phase environment, with the O2 concentration varied from 0 to 20.8%. Results showed that the current in the film increased with time when UV LED was shined on the ZnO film surface (lasting for 30 min in this part of the measurement), and then decayed after the UV light was turned off. The current response was stronger when the O2 concentration in the detected environment was lower, supporting the concept that the presence of more O2 molecules adsorbed on ZnO surface caused more significant trapping of conduction electrons. NeverWet coated films were found to exhibit similar room-temperature oxygen sensing response when working in gaseous environment and water, except that the magnitude of the response was smaller. Objective 4 Curve fitting was performed to fit the observed current data based on a model combining the mechanisms of photo generation of electron-hole pairs, recombination of charge carriers and trapping of electrons by surface sorbed oxygen. The fitting parameters include the dark current, characteristic time constant describing the change of the current and saturated current. The last two are correlated to and used to evaluate the oxygen content in the gaseous environment or water samples.

524211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
524211.value: 1. We were supported to upgrade our SCBD system to reach the standard of a commercial one. The PI is invited by the inventor, Professor Paolo Milani, to discuss further development of the machine in a conference in July. 2. Photoconductivity of SCBD ZnO films can be used for formaldehyde detection. The PI will move forward to apply for a funding from the Public Serving Scheme of Hong Kong Industry Department for the fabrication of formaldehyde sensor prototype. The project will be the continuation of a previously completed project (2013) entitled “Development of Room-temperature Thin-film Volatile Organic Compound Gas Sensors for Environmental Health Monitoring”. 3. We will extend the work by doping nitrogen into SCBD ZnO films for improving the stability of the gas sensing signal, which is still not quite stable in a cyclic test. We will also extend the study to cover other direct bandgap oxide materials, like SnO2 and In2O3. 4. The model used for explaining the photoconductivity can be further improved. One deficiency of our present model is to assume that the dropping rate of photo-induced electron concentration depends linearly on the oxygen concentration in the environment. Further modification of the model should be done.

524211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
524211.value: 1. We determined the optimum preparation condition of ZnO films fabricated using our SCBD system. It is specified by the settings of the SCBD and post oxidation processes. Highly porous nano-structured ZnO films of excellent gas sensing properties were produced. 2. We applied two types of water-resistive coatings on an SCBD ZnO film. They are a sprayed agent, “NeverWet”, and spin-coated polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). They formed superhydrophobic polymer coatings to resist the influence of water. Oxygen molecules passed through the coatings and were detected. 3. The photocurrent of the films under ultraviolet illumination was observed. The uncoated and polymer-coated ZnO film were examined in gas-phase environment with O2 content varied from 0 to 20.8% (like in air). The polymer-coated SCBD ZnO film was examined in water with dissolved oxygen content varied from 0 to 9.1 mg/l. The photocurrent shows significant change with the oxygen content in all cases. 4. A model combining (i) generation of photo electron-hole pairs, (ii) surface absorption and desorption of oxygen and (iii) trapping and release of electrons was applied to explain the time-dependence of current in the film. The parameters used to fit the curves can be used to evaluate the surrounding oxygen concentration.

524511.label: Realisation of objectives
524511.value: The project has been successfully completed. The following outlines how and to what extent each objective has been achieved. For objective 1: Objective: To determine the influence of different vibration frequencies, amplitudes, and stroke severity on the transmission of vertical sinusoidal WBV signals to different parts of the body among chronic stroke patients. Methods: Thirty-eight people with chronic hemiplegia stroke underwent a single assessment session. For each participant, three vibration frequencies (20, 30, 40 Hz), two amplitudes (low and high), and three different postures (knee flexed 30°, knee flexed 60°, tip-toe standing) were tested (a total of 18 different conditions). Skin-mounted tri-axial accelerometers were placed at the bilateral medial malleolus, bilateral medial tibial tuberosity, bilateral greater trochanter, third lumbar vertebra, and head. The transmissibility of vibration was computed as the ratio of the root-mean-square-acceleration at different body sites to that of the platform. Results: The transmissibility of vibration signals was dependent upon the interaction between intensity and posture (p<0.05). The transmissibility was not significantly different between paretic and non-paretic side in the lower extremities except at the medial malleolus. Generally, the transmissibility decreased as the signals traveled from the distal part of the lower extremities to the head. Increasing vibration intensity was associated with lower transmissibility at all the measured body sites except the medial malleolus where there was a significant resonance effect. Among the three different postures, tip-toeing led to the lowest transmissibility. The transmissibility at the head was low (<0.1) during knee flexion at 60° and tip-toe standing. Conclusion: The transmissibility is highly influenced by vibration signal intensity and posture among people with chronic stroke. For objective 2: Objective: To assess the influence of different vibration frequencies and amplitudes on leg muscle activation among chronic stroke patients. Methods: Each of the 46 chronic stroke subjects was exposed to three WBV conditions of 1. no WBV, 2. low-intensity WBV protocol [peak acceleration: 0.96 unit of gravitational constant (G)], and 3. high-intensity WBV protocol (peak acceleration: 1.61G) while performing 8 different static exercises involving upright standing, semi squat, deep squat, weight-shifted-forward, weight-shifted-backward, weight-shifted-to-the-side, forward lunge and single-leg-standing. Bilateral VL and GS muscle activity was recorded with surface electromyography (EMG), and expressed as percentage of the EMG amplitude recorded during a maximal voluntary contraction of the respective muscles (%MVC). Another 36 individuals with chronic stroke participated in a similar experiment except that BF and TA muscles were measured. Results: Exposure to WBV (low- and high-intensity protocols) significantly increased VL and GS EMG amplitude (large effect size, partial η2= 0.135-0.643, p<0.001) on both the paretic and non-paretic sides in different exercise conditions, compared with no WBV. No significant difference in EMG magnitude was found between the high- and low-intensity WBV protocols (p>0.05). With a few exceptions, WBV enhanced EMG activity in the paretic and non-paretic leg muscles to a similar extent in different exercise conditions. For BF and TA muscles, the main effect of intensity was significant. Exposure to the low-intensity and high-intensity protocols led to a significantly greater increase in normalized BF and TA EMG magnitude in both legs compared with no WBV. The intensity × exercise interaction was also significant, suggesting that the WBV-induced increase in EMG activity was exercise-dependent. The EMG responses to WBV were similar between the paretic and non-paretic legs, and were not associated with level of lower extremity motor impairment and spasticity. Conclusions. Adding WBV during exercise significantly increased EMG activity in major leg muscle groups. The EMG responses to WBV in the paretic and non-paretic legs were similar, and were not related to degree of motor impairment and spasticity. The findings are useful for guiding the design of WBV training protocols for people with stroke. For objective 3: Objective: To assess the effects of WBV in relation to neuromuscular function and falls among chronic stroke patients. Methods: Eighty four people with chronic stroke (mean age: 61.2 years, SD: 9.2) who had mild to moderate motor impairment (Chedoke McMaster Stroke Assessment lower limb motor score: median=9 out of 14, interquartile range=7-11.8) were randomly assigned to the low-intensity WBV, high-intensity WBV, or control groups. The former two groups performed various leg exercises while receiving low-intensity and high-intensity WBV respectively. The controls performed the same exercises without WBV. All individuals received 30 training sessions over an average period of 75.5 days (SD=5.2). Outcome measurements included knee muscle strength (isokinetic dynamometry), spasticity at the knee and ankle joints (Modified Ashworth Scale), balance (Mini Balance Evaluation Systems Test, Mini-BESTest), mobility (Timed-Up-and-Go test, TUG), walking endurance (6-Minute Walk Test, 6MWT), balance self-efficacy (Activities-specific Balance Confidence scale, ABC), participation in daily activities (Frenchay Activity Index), perceived environmental barriers to societal participation (Craig Hospital Inventory of Environmental Factors), and quality of life (Short-Form 12 Health Survey, SF-12). The assessments were performed at baseline and post-intervention. Data on fall incidence were collected on a monthly basis via telephone interviews. Results: Intention-to-treat analysis revealed a significant time effect for muscle strength, TUG, distance and oxygen consumption rate achieved during 6MWT, Mini-BESTest, ABC, and SF-12 physical composite score domain (P<0.05). However, the time by group interactions effects were not significant for any of the outcome measures (P>0.05). Conclusion: The addition of the 30-session WBV paradigm to the leg exercise protocol was no more effective in enhancing body functions/structures, activity and participation than leg exercises alone in people with stroke who sustained mild to moderate motor impairments.

524511.label: Major findings and research outcome
524511.value: The major findings are: 1. The transmissibility is highly influenced by vibration signal intensity and posture among people with chronic stroke. 2. Adding vibrations during exercise significantly increased EMG activity in major leg muscle groups. The EMG responses to WBV in the paretic and non-paretic legs were similar, and were not related to degree of motor impairment and spasticity. 3. The 10-week high-intensity or low-intensity did not induce an overall significant treatment effect on neuromotor outcomes and falls. There was an association, however, between the size of treatment effect and poorer neuromotor function at baseline, indicating that whole-body vibration may only be useful for those who are more severely impaired. The project has resulted in 5 papers published in high impact journals. The findings have also been presented in 4 internationalconferences (5 abstracts in total). The PhD student trained has also received the Distinguished Thesis Award granted by the Faculty of Health and Social Sciences, the Hong Kong Polytechnic University. One of the abstracts was also selected as the best poster in the 21st European Stroke Conference, Lisbon, Portugal, 2012.

524511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
524511.value: It is important to study the neurophysiological mechanisms related to the applications of whole-body vibration, before further examining its clinical efficacy. In particular, we are interested in studying how different vibration parameters would affect the excitability of the corticospinal pathway, and the Hoffman reflex, as it may have important implications for stroke rehabilitation. A PhD student is currently working on a project examining the effects of mechanical vibrations on Hoffman reflex and stiffness in the gastrocnemius muscle. We would also like to explore how different vibration parameters would affect the level of bone turnover markers, and bone cells are highly sensitive to dynamic mechanical loading. This is also highly clinically relevant, as bone loss is often accelerated after the onset of stroke. A grant proposal is in preparation.

524511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
524511.value: This study examined how the transmission of mechanical vibrations is influenced by the vibration frequency, amplitude and body posture, and how mechanical vibrations would affect muscle function in individuals with chronic stroke. These issues are important because stroke patients often sustain impairments in muscle function, and mechanical vibrations may be a potentially useful treatment modality. We found that the transmissibility is highly influenced by vibration signal intensity and posture. Resonance effect was observed at the ankle joint, indicating that application of mechanical vibrations may not be appropriate for patients with ankle pathology. We also found that adding vibrations during exercise would further increase the activation of major leg muscle groups, suggesting that it may be a useful adjunct tool for exercise training post-stroke. There is some evidence that this modality may be more useful for those stroke survivors who are more severely impaired.

525011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
525011.value: 在过去几十年里，香港市区道路网络中的几个交通事故导致了严重的交通挤塞甚至gridlocks。此类事件突出香港的道路网络的脆弱性。这种脆弱性由多种原因诱发，其中包括高度密集的城市和缺乏道路空间。因此，香港运输署（运输署）一直在调研如何引入了一个交通事故管理系统（TIMS）以弥补城市道路基础设施的薄弱环节。这项研究计划旨在通过及时的开发一个在线的随机动态交通模型（SDT）来促成这一问题。制定一个有效的/稳健的TIMS系统的理论和实践的挑战之一是如何引进和处理在事故发生期间和之后道路网络的需求和供给的不确定性。事故期间和之后的路况往往变得不正常而难以预测。基于the Stochastic Cell Transmission Model (SCTM)，且通过引入适当的时空协方差结构到随机动态交通模型（SDT），这项研究计划将会解决这个问题。空间协方差是指在网络中的不同位置的历史交通数据的需求和供应的统计相关性。时间方差是相关路径/O-D在不同的时间段的供应和需求的相关性。结合这两种协方差提供了完整的交通历史数据的协方差结构。协方差结构将允许模型使用当前检测的交通数据及其交通特点的统计结构，实时调整其短期的随机预测。基于在香港收集的数据（作为这项研究的一部分）和其它可能的数据源，该项目将探讨一种可行的时空协方差结构。此项目提出SDT还将提供一个在交通事故环境下的高度不确定的交通状况（如延迟，密度，或排队长度）的随机预测。 基于传感器通测得的实际交通状态和假定正常条件下的随机预测的比较，该项目将应用开发的SDT框架开发一个在线的事故检测算法。在该项目中，在线事故管理系统将被阐述为一个随机动态规划。我们将使用近似动态规划（ADP）来解决这个随机动态规划问题。该项目还将开发一个基于ADP的multi-agent系统（MAS）以处理大型网络下的复杂网络交通流，以及执行器、传感器和交通控制中心之间的相互作用。该项目的最终目标是，制定一个理论上可行的且实际可行的TIMS框架。因此，该项目将建立一个在香港的案例研究区的动态交通数据库以验证开发的所有组件。这个数据库也将被用在离线更新在线TIMS系统与SDT。我们将为系统设计保留与近期由运输署开发的实时交通信息系统（RTIS）和未来可能在香港实施的智能交通系统融合集成系统的架构。该项目将得益于PI和CIs在香港实施的类似项目的实践经验。尽管该项目有理论性很强的组成部分，PI和CIs将在该项目的研究开发和验证阶段与来自香港运输署的工作人员接洽以确保该系统的可行性和实用性。

525011.label: Realisation of objectives
525011.value: This research project has achieved all objectives set above. We defined the most appropriate approach to estimate the statistical distribution of journey time as published in our paper in Transportation Research Part C. We found that the type of journey time distribution estimated from the Stochastic Dynamic Traffic model (SDT) is consistent with the empirical evidence presented in the literature under different traffic characteristics. The project then developed the SDT model for the short-term travel time prediction in which the work was published in a paper in IEEE journal. A particular structure of spatial-temporal correlation system was introduced in the prediction model utilizing the stochastic information of the SDT model. The SDT model is then extended to the network case as reported in our paper published in Transportmetrica A. Finally the project developed a feedback control framework for responding to abnormal circumstance in the network as modelled from the SDT. This work was also reported in our other paper published in Transportmetrica A.

526211.label: Project Objectives
526211.value: Test the standard barrage of complex network based methods on networks derived from time series. In addition to metrics such as path length, assortativity and betweenness, this work will focus on using existing techniques and developing new techniques to measure flow through a network. Scaling of network metrics as a function of network size (as the available time series data increases) will be studied. Complex network properties should be compared and related not only to the individual dynamical systems that have generated the systems, but to individual regions in the dynamical system: how do unstable periodic orbits (for example) manifest in the network? Provide an analytic foundation for the numerical complex network measures of time series data. Determine to what extent the network structure is invariant as a function of increasing time series length and distinct (differentiable) observation functions. To do this we will study the theoretical foundation upon which these complex network measures produce the observed behaviour. Why, for example, do we observe the super-family phenomena of motif distribution? We will address the question of which features of the complex networks genuinely reflect invariant properties of the underlying complex system. It is expected that certain properties: scaling features as well as the structural properties of the network (for example, network torsion and twist --- which we will describe below) or of the network skeleton (and percolation based features) appear to be invariant. These properties will be explored analytically and computationally. Develop techniques to generate surrogate time series from networks. Time series derived complex networks encapsulate important properties concerning broad classes of dynamical systems. It should be possible to use these networks to generate new (random but representative) time series which may then be used as a form of Monte Carlo hypothesis testing (that is, surrogate data). By using these networks to generate multiple time series which are typical of a general class of dynamics, we can use these for testing whether independently observed time series are generated by the same form of dynamics. Techniques to achieve this will be statistically validated, and an analytic description of the underlying null hypothesis developed. Apply these methods, and standard nonlinear time series analysis tools, to the study of granular media simulations. We will focus both on a quantitative description of the observed dynamics in terms of the underlying dynamical system, and also on links to previous analysis of structural response to shear stress (by the Melbourne Co-Is).

526211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
526211.value: A wide variety of natural, physical and social systems have been shown to exhibit complex network phenomena. In a complex system, the structural arrangement of individual components within the system is distributed in a heterogeneous and highly ordered fashion. The individual components, and the connections between them, may then give rise to a wide variety of coherent and emergent phenomena. Pattern formation in flocking animals, social dynamics and community behaviour, community spread of infectious diseases, panic in economic systems, and pattern formation in granular systems are all examples. Very recently, the project PI and co-authors have proposed techniques to allow these methods to be applied to the analysis of scalar time series observations of complex or chaotic system. This allows one to borrow tools from the field of complex network theory and apply them to the analysis of nonlinear time series. These new tools have been applied to provide new insight in the study of complex or chaotic time series problems. However, a strong analytical foundation for these methods is currently lacking. The focus of this project is on developing such a foundation and then advancing these techniques and applying them to a specific physical application. In this proposal we focus exclusively on the application to granular media. Granular systems consist of a large number of discrete particles each interacting with its geometric neighbours according to well understood physical laws. Nonetheless, the system as a whole can exhibit a wide variety of complex behaviours that are extremely difficult to predict, and for which there are few strategies to understand the underlying mechanisms. Granular systems occur in a wide variety of real physical systems --- from industrial and construction processes to mining and geophysical sciences. Such systems have long been described as an archetype for emergent phenomena in a complex system. Recently, complex network analysis applied to this system (by the Melbourne Co-Is) has shown that the evolution of shear stress can be understood based on the network structure. In this proposal we aim to apply a complimentary approach and explain the observed dynamics for the system under various dynamical regimes. In addition to the development of new tools from complex network theory for the analysis of generic time series data, we choose to study a specific physical system so that we can develop and advance these methods to the point where they can meaningfully be applied to such experimental systems. 大量的自然、物理或社会系统都被发现具有复杂网络现象。在一个复杂系统中，各个独立单元的结构排列倾向于呈现出异质化分布和高度有序的特点。因此，系统中的各个单元往往是相互连接的，并且有可能呈现出多种多样的关联方式和涌现现象。像动物集群行为的模式、人类社会的动态特征和集体性行为、各种传染性疾病在社团中的传播、经济系统中的恐慌行为、以及粒状系统的模式等等都是这样的例子。最近，本项目负责人以及合作者提出一些有效方法来分析从实际复杂或混沌系统中得到的具有尺度特性的时间序列。这些新方法允许我们借用复杂网络研究领域的各种统计工具来分析非线性时间序列，而且这些方法为我们理解各种时间序列的复杂行为和混沌特性提供了新的见解和视角。然而，以上这些方法的坚实分析基础目前仍然是不完善的。因此本项目的主要目的是为各种方法提供更好的理论基础，同时继续发展各种分析技术并将这些方法应用于特定物理问题。在本项目申请中，我们重点关注于颗粒状介质的研究。粒状系统中存在大量分离的微粒，虽然距离靠近的颗粒之间存在相互作用并呈现出很好理解的物理规律，然而整个系统却呈现出非常复杂的、多种多样的行为。因此粒状系统的集体行为是非常难以预测的，并且没有好的策略去理解其中的物理机制。粒状系统广泛存在于真实的物理系统中，比如在工业、建筑业、挖掘行业以及地球物理科学中就有大量这样的系统。长期以来，这样的粒状系统都是复杂系统涌现现象的原理性模型。最近，本项目在墨尔本的研究成员使用复杂网络分析粒状系统，并发现网络结构的变化可用来理解系统中切变应力的演化。在本申请书，我们提出应用更加巧妙的方法来分析和解释粒状系统处于不同状态时的动态特征。另外，我们也致力于使用复杂网络理论来分析通用的时间序列数据，通过研究粒状系统也有助于我们提出和发展更加有效的、可应用于各种实际系统的新方法。

526211.label: Major findings and research outcome
526211.value: The paper in Chaos vol. 23 provided an overview of the application of nonlinear time series methods in general, and time series to network transformations in particular, to the study of granular mechanics. This work continued with the application results given in the paper published in Chaos vol. 24. Intrinsic to this work was an assessment of the usual barrage of network measures for time series detection (Obj. 1). These two publications catalogue the major positive results and demonstrate that: (1) network communities could be associate with slip events and uncovered previously unreported dynamics, and (2) large strain behaviour of a granular ensemble may best be modelled by structures capable of exhibiting (hyper-) chaotic dynamics. In the paper in Frontiers of Computational Neuroscience, we extended these results to an entirely different domain and examined the problem of network construction for mutli-variable data sets. The particular application was a neuroscience one, but the methods generalise to other similar scenarios and the results we obtained address both Objs. 4 and 2. Objs. 2 and 3 were also addressed in the final publication published in National Science Review, where we provided a computational and semi-analytical exploration of the statistical properties of complex networks arising from this settings and from others. By framing this in the context of random complex network we were able to do more and provide a suitable null model (for the case null hypothesis of trivial dynamics in the observed time series) against which to test the complex structure we observed in these real systems. (Obj. 2 and 3). Hence, when we show that the unfolding structure is not expected of random realisations, we are able to infer that this is significant and important deterministic structure of the original system (Obj. 4)

526211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
526211.value: This project has highlighted the potential for the further development of these methods - in granular systems and elsewhere. Subsequent to this project, CI Small has continued his investigation of time series to network transformations in his new capacity as Australian Research Council Future Fellow at the University of Western Australia (the Future Fellowship is a competitive research grant funded to about $A900k to support his work in this area). CI Small is continuing to work on developing these fundamentals with two PhD students at UWA (and a second Australian Research Council grant of $270k). PI Tse and CIs Small and Tordesillas are continuing to work on the application of these methods to granular systems. This work was most recently highlighted at the 2015 Elizabeth and Fredrick White Research Conference (under the auspices of the Australian Academy of Sciences) in Melbourne.

526211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
526211.value: Granular systems arise in a variety of settings - from building on sandy foundations, packing of powders and earthquakes. This project seeks to understand these phenomena by applying a new tool kit in data analysis. These tools have recently been developed by this investigative team and provide a new way of viewing the data - we can view the data as a complex system (as, indeed, an ensemble of grains is) and infer the required complexity needed to describe the expected behaviour. This have lead to new insight in the understanding of stress-strain behaviour of tightly packed material and the stick-slip movement of a plate being dragged across a friction surface (the mechanics of intermittently overcoming and then succumbing to static friction). These methods, of course, are rather generic and we also demonstrate application of the same techniques to understanding interaction of different brain regions during physiological activity observed through mutli-electrode electroencephalography.

526511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
526511.value: 石墨烯自2004年被发现（于2010年获物理诺贝尔奖），即迅速成为研究热点之一。在2009年基于石墨烯的被动锁模飞秒光纤激光器出现后，石墨烯光子学（在2010年被Nature Photonics作为重点方向介绍）更是引起了科学和工业界光子学研究者的极大兴趣。石墨烯具有独特的光滑圆锥形电子态结构，且带隙为零。这种独特的带隙结构使其在非常宽的光谱范围内具有超快可饱和吸收特性。采用石墨烯制作可饱和吸收体可大大降低材料制备成本，而该器件较其他传统锁模材料，如半导体可饱和吸收镜、碳纳米管等具有很多优势。特别是其具有超宽的工作波长范围（从可见波段到太赫兹波段）、低饱和强度、可控的饱和深度、超短的恢复时间和高损伤阈值。 前人的研究工作主要集中在低功率毫瓦量级的1.5微米掺铒光纤激光器。本课题的研究重点则在研制基于零带隙石墨烯，工作于1微米波段的硅酸盐和2微米波段的亚碲酸盐玻璃高功率（>1W）光纤锁模激光器。这种高功率超快锁模光纤激光器在高精度微加工、光纤布拉格光栅写制、医疗、用于医学成像的非线性显微镜和超连续谱产生、太赫兹波产生、超快光谱学、超精细频率测量、以及泵浦工作于5微米波段的中红外光学参量振荡器等诸多领域具有广泛用途。 本课题的另一个研究重点是采用具有不同带隙能量的氧化石墨烯制作锁模激光器，并研究其输出特性与带隙能量的关系。氧化石墨烯的制备将在香港理工大学内完成，而其带隙能量可通过退火时间来控制。对带隙能量进行调控，将为控制激光器输出脉冲的宽度提供可能性，并可用于开发基于石墨烯被动可饱和吸收的Q开关。调Q激光器具有很高的脉冲能量，可在测距、传感、材料处理、激光打标、脉冲激光器全息、外科医疗、纹身清洗、医学成像等方面具有广泛用途。通常被动调Q脉冲可由插入掺杂可饱和吸收晶体，如Cr:YAG来实现。基于晶体的可饱和吸收体较石墨烯需要复杂而昂贵的生长过程以及贵重的原料，而且掺杂可饱和吸收晶体具有波长选择性，并难以与激光增益介质集成在一起。因此，研制基于石墨烯的调Q开关对于激光工业具有重要意义。 本课题属学科交叉研究项目，需要光纤激光器物理学、材料科学、光子器件工程和工业人员共同努力来开发基于新型石墨烯材料的高性能锁模光纤激光器系统。由于新型的石墨烯材料具有转化为商业产品的巨大潜力，本项目的研究工作不仅将发表一系列高水平学术论文，而且会为形成高商业价值的专利提供条件。而参与其中的博士后及博士生通过此研究项目的训练，将成为香港和中国紧缺的光子产业人才。

526511.label: Realisation of objectives
526511.value: Publications overviews: It is my first large research grant and I have spent the money carefully to ensure the project completed successfully. At the end this project fund has lead to 17 SCI journal publications including 2 papers for impact factors > 7, 2 papers for impact factors ≥ 4.7 (1 paper being highlighted by the editor in the front cover page), 4 papers for impact factors ≥ 3, and 8 conference presentations including 5 invited talks. This project has been completed successfully with fruitful research output and all the project objectives being achieved. We have successfully fabricated and characterized various types of graphene and graphene oxide based saturable absorbers with different bandgap energy and different number of layers in our lab (Objective 1 completed), some of which have been effectively used for producing passive mode locking and Q-switching pulses in various types of laser systems including diode pumped solid state laser and fiber laser with various operational wavelengths successfully. The above results indicate the capability of using graphene oxide based saturable absorber to produce pulsed laser and its broadband operational features. In terms of power scale, We have first demonstrated high power operation of mode locking output power of over one Watt by using graphene based saturable absorber and current output power have been further boosted to the new world record of 3W, a significant improvement over our initial targeted output power - one Watt. The output power and performance of these laser systems including fiber and solid state laser with various output wavelengths have been optimized with the experimental results published in some top quality journals in this field (objectives 2 and 3 completed). We have also done research on other novel passive Q-switching and mode locking laser systems, further study the nonlinear optical properties of 2D materials and we find that the size and layer structure plays a very important role on the nonlinear optical properties of the 2D materials and these research results have been published in some high impact factor journals.

526511.label: Major findings and research outcome
526511.value: Since its discovery about a decade ago, graphene has rapidly captured the attention of scientists and researchers for its many extraordinary properties. The ideas of using 2D materials to fabricate photonics devices have been attracting significant attention as it may dramatically reduce material and manufacturing costs with further performance enhancement. However, the high power passive mode locking and Q-switching operation by using these novel materials have not yet been investigated. Through this project, we have developed some useful techniques to fabricate graphene or graphene oxide based saturable absorber [1-4, 11, 12] with optimized features that capable of producing high power laser output. We have first demonstrated high power >1Watt operation at near 1 micron by using the graphene based saturable absorber [1], followed by further scaling it up to 3 Watt [2], a world leading record. It confirms the possibility for using the graphene based materials fabricated in our laboratory for high power mode locking or Q-switching laser operation. Additionally, we have also first demonstrated the graphene based Q-switching system that can simultaneously operate at five wavelengths peaks [3]. These results indicate the potential of using graphene based absorber as WDM source for optical communication system. The developed techniques have been employed to fabricate other carbon based saturable absorbers for high power operation at passive Q-switching and mode locking mode in various operational wavelengths [5] [6] [7] [13]. During the research, we have found that graphene did not exhibit saturable absorption sometimes. It shows optical limiting properties instead in specific host matrix and under high optical pumping intensity [14]. This phenomenon was observed in other more novel 2D materials as well therefore the research work have been extended into other 2D materials e.g. MoS2 and WS2 due to its novelty and more favorable features. Our research confirmed that MoS2 also exhibit strong nonlinear optical limiting properties [15] (Impact factor >7.3). These fundamental properties can be tuned by changing the size and layer structure of WS2 [16] (Impact factor >7.3). We have also found their nonlinear optical properties in NMP (liquid state) is not stable under laser excitation. However, the stability can be further improved by incorporated them into PMMA. This pioneer research has great importance for 2D materials laser photonic device development and we received a very good comments from the reviewers and this work is now being highlighted by the editor in the front cover page [17] (impact factor 4.7).

526511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
526511.value: The two dimensional, (2D), layered materials have attracted tremendous attention from the photonic research community as it can serve as building blocks for the next generation photonics devices e.g. high performance flexible micro-photonic devices. Because of its small bandgap and weak layer absorption, in this research we find graphene exhibits weak light modulation ability and is not favorable for nonlinear photonics applications. The research interests have currently been extended to other 2D materials with more favorable bandgap structure e.g. phosphorene, transition metal dichalcogenides. In this study, we have demonstrated the modification of the nonlinear optical limiting properties of WS2. It is a very important discovery which implies we can engineer its intrinsic optical properties. Additionally our recent studies indicate the instability of some few layer 2D materials and thus it is vital to explore some methods or packaging technique to isolate these 2D materials. The researches on the optical properties engineering and packaging techniques have great impact to various fields e.g. application of these novel 2D materials for renewable energy generation. Therefore, we plan to further explore the saturable absorption properties modification and packaging techniques of other novel 2D materials provided that further financial support is granted by RGC.

526511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
526511.value: This project provides insight into some new concepts and methods to modify the natural optical properties of some novel and very compact materials (atomic thick), 2D materials. These 2D materials have more favorable mechanical, electronic and optical properties compared with their bulk form. Such materials can serve as building block for the next generation laser photonic devices with enhanced feature and performance. We can significantly enhance the nonlinear optical properties of these novel 2D materials through controlling their size and layer structure. We have demonstrated some new methods to fabricate the carbon based critical competent for the ultrafast laser system that significantly boosts its output power to the world record. These ultrafast lasers have many important applications in our modern society including medical surgery, micro-machining, scientific research, high end electric products manufacturing e.g. i-phone, i-pad. Due to the wide range of applications of these 2D materials, the material engineering and packaging techniques or knowledge gained through this project could have great and long term impact on various fields e.g. renewable energy generation, photonic device development, optical communication and optical computer. Follow-up research plays a very important role in the development of the 2D materials and devices.

526811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
526811.value: Deindustrialization and economic restructuring have led to increasing obsolescence of industrial space in many modern cities. Transformation of this obsolete industrial property space into better uses becomes an indispensable part of urban policy in achieving sustainable urban growth. Hong Kong is no exception to these trends. During the past three decades, Hong Kong has evolved from a low-cost manufacturing base to become an international business and financial centre. However, its existing industrial property still occupies more than six times the total commercial-office land area and makes up more than twice the office floor space in the territory. The market is of the view that this slow progress of industrial space transformation is primarily caused by unresponsive government policies and regulations. Based on a methodological combination of historical review, quantitative analysis and case studies, this research examines the factors accounting for the dynamics of the industrial property market, and evaluates the extent to which the evolving urban planning strategies and development regulations of the Hong Kong government in the past three decades have contributed to the apparently lacklustre performance in industrial property market adjustment. This study is intended to shed light on how the interplay of government development policies and private market reactions has facilitated and constrained the restructuring of industrial property space in Hong Kong. 去工業化和經濟轉型導致許多現代城市的工業用地變得落伍過時，如何活化使用和轉化這些過時的工業用地，成為實現城市可持續發展政策中不可或缺的一部分。這些趨勢，香港亦不例外。過去三十年，香港已從一個低成本的製造基地，成為一個國際商業和金融中心。然而，其現有的工業用地仍是商業辦公室總土地面積的 6 倍多，辦公室占地面積的兩倍以上。市場認為，工業空間轉型進展緩慢主要是因為政府的政策和法規不足所致。這項研究結合歷史回顧、 量化分析和案例研究的方法，審查工業用地市場動態變化的因素，檢討香港政府城市規劃策略和發展條例在過去三十年對市場調節的影響。這項研究的目的，是闡明香港政府發展政策與私人市場反應如何促進和約束重組工業空間的相互作用。

526811.label: Realisation of objectives
526811.value: Research objective 1 was fully achieved. The study period was extended beyond the originally proposed period. Planning policies and industrial property market data within the study period from 1978 to 2012 were collated and reviewed. Assessment results and research findings were fully reported in the journal papers published in Environment and Planning A and Land Use Policy. Research objective 2 was fully achieved. The continued supply of industrial space in Hong Kong was explained by a longitudinal cross-sectoral interaction between industrial and office property markets and its relationship with planning policy. The substitutability between industrial and office accommodation explained the reasons why developers were willing to provide industrial space despite the trend of de-industrialization. The use of new industrial premises by non-manufacturing operators and its impact on industrial space market explained the dynamics of industrial property market. Research objective 3 was fully achieved. Liberal planning policy that permits land-use changes of industrial premises was found to lead to peculiar market adjustment in both the industrial and office development sectors. Enforcement policy and the subsequent planning relaxation were found to be instrumental in encouraging the development industry to generate more industrial space at at the expense of new offices. Research objective 4 was achieved. The study confirms that incremental land-use changes instigated by market forces and supported by flexible planning regulatory mechanism was more effective than a blanket rezoning policy in transforming industrial space into other uses. Private market had a much faster and earlier grasp of emerging economic opportunity from industrial upgrading than planning regulators. The current trend of planning relaxation in facilitating adaptive re-use of old industrial space is on the right track.
