526811.label: Major findings and research outcome
526811.value: This research produces two journal papers published in Environment and Planning A and Land Use Planning respectively. The latter paper received the Commendation Award in the Royal Town Planning Institute Awards for 2015 Research Excellence. Comment of the Jury on this paper was: "In-depth and illuminating study of property markets in one of the world's most dynamic cities". The trend of deindustrialization in many countries over the past three to four decades has left many modern cities with a considerable amount of obsolete industrial premises. How to make a better use of such space to facilitate the economic shift from manufacturing to a service-based economy has been a major question for both planners and the development industry. Hong Kong, where there is obviously a great pressure on the use of space, has managed to transform itself from an export-oriented manufacturing city into an international business and financial metropolis. However, most previous research has focused on office property rather than industrial property. This research uses sophisticated modelling techniques as well as data to examine how market forces in Hong Kong have reacted to the economic opportunity arising from the land-use conversion of existing industrial premises, and how planning regulations may have helped or hindered this. The industrial sector in Hong Kong has been extremely proactive in converting industrial premises into non-industrial and higher-value business uses. A Supply Adjustment Model is proposed to explain this unexpected market phenomenon. Empirical estimations by Johansen cointegration analysis and Vector Error Correction Model (VECM) confirm opposite movements in the supply and property prices of new industrial and office accommodation, indicating market competition and segmentation between these two sectors. The research reveals that, under the city's liberal and flexible planning policy, the development market has actually produced more rather than less industrial accommodation compared to the development of new office accommodation. Part of the reason for this seems to be that relaxations in the permissible land-use rights of property owners in using these types of premises had the effect of increasing the size of the market, and also that developers have shifted the 'burden' of securing land-use change of these premises to the final users or owners of the spaces. This also illustrates that the relationship between industrial and office sectors in a deindustrializing urban environment is more complicated than is often assumed.

526811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
526811.value: This study explores the relationship between land-use planning regulation, changing use of industrial space and market adjustment in a compact city of Hong Kong under deindustrialization over the past three decades. Planning regulation defines and attenuates the rights of property owners in the use of industrial premises. Property users need to secure additional rights, through planning applications, from the regulatory authority before converting the premises for higher-value non-industrial uses. This study reveals that, under a flexible planning regulatory regime of facilitating incremental land-use conversion by the users in industrial property, the development market actually produced more rather than less industrial accommodation. The study concludes that the industrial sector in Hong Kong was extremely proactive in converting industrial premises into non-industrial and higher-value business uses. Planning policy tended to facilitate and support such market initiatives, but such a liberal planning policy that permits land-use changes of industrial premises has led to peculiar market adjustments in both industrial and office development sectors. Finally, incremental land-use changes instigated by market forces and supported by flexible planning regulatory mechanism appear to be far more effective than a blanket rezoning policy in transforming industrial space into other uses.

527111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
527111.value: This proposal deals with a fundamental issue on improving the sound transmission loss of a wall mounted Helmholtz resonator in the presence of a low Mach number parallel duct flow, which is relevant to ventilation and air conditioning noise control in buildings. It is evidenced that the duct flow creates a shear layer at the mouth of the resonator, which interacts with the resonator cavity and produces sound. The sound so produced can be very strong if the shear layer instability mode matches the resonant mode of the resonator. Though this kind of strong feedback phenomenon can be avoided by careful design of the resonator and the flow speed, the presence of the shear layer does degrade the performance of the Helmholtz resonator as a duct noise control device at low Mach number. It is proposed to carry out a detailed study on the aeroacoustics of the Helmholtz resonator with focus on the sound generation mechanisms and their relative importance in building services applications. Effort will also be made to derive methods for weakening the coupling between the shear layer and the resonator cavity so as to improve the resonator performance in the presence of the duct flow. In addition, attention will be paid to weakening the vortices that shed into the duct flow stream due to resonator action so as not to affect any noise control devices downstream but close to the resonator. This work will contribute to future effort in the design of a broadband resonance-based silencer, which is extremely useful for indoor spaces where high levels of cleanness are required and in environments where the air is dirty or greasy. The results on the interaction between a shear layer and a resonator will also deepen current fundamental understandings on the topic and explain experimental observations in the existing literature. 這項目建議對亥姆霍茲共鳴器在低馬赫數氣流管道中聲音傳輸損耗進行詳細基礎性研究。研究成果在通風和空調噪聲控制工程上有很大的功用。現有文獻已證明共鳴器口的剪切流和共鳴器空腔之間的共鳴可產生強烈的噪聲。雖然這共鳴可從共鳴器和氣流動速度的設計上設法避免，但是共鳴器口的剪切流降低了亥姆霍茲共鳴器作為低馬赫數氣流管道噪音控制裝置的功能。 建議項目將開展對亥姆霍茲共鳴器聲音產生原理及其在建築設施的應用的詳細研究。也設法弱化剪切流層和共鳴器空腔之間的耦合，從而找出提高管道共鳴器在湍流情況下的性能的方法。此外，這研究項目也致力尋找削弱共鳴器所產生的旋渦的方法，以免影響任何下游噪聲控制設備的功能。這項工作將有助於今後發展寬帶共振型消聲器。這寬帶共振型消聲器是在清潔水平要求非常高或在環境空氣骯髒或油膩水平高的地方是必需的。 剪切流和共鳴器之間相互作用的研究結果也將加深對主題的理解和解釋現有文獻上的實驗結果。

527111.label: Realisation of objectives
527111.value: This project is done mainly using experiments. Apart from resonators, coupled cavities are added to the project scope as these cavities are found to be able to produce relatively broadband sound attenuation if they are offset. Both the actions of the resonators and the cavities include cavity resonance and feedback mechanism in the presence of a low Mach number flow. Several series of experiments have been carried out to understand the sound transmission across a duct section installed with resonators and coupled cavities in the presence of a low Mach number flow (0 to 22 m/s in intervals of 2 m/s). A preliminary experiment using narrow sidebranch array was conducted so as to help the research student get familiar with the measurement procedure before the test resonators were manufactured. For the coupled cavities, experiment was done using two 100 mm (streamwise) by 70 mm (depth) by 173 mm (spanwise) cavities. They were offset by a distance from 0 mm to 100 mm in intervals of 10 mm. The test duct has a cross-section dimension of 150 mm by 173 mm. Anechoic termination was used to reduce the acoustic reflection at the exit of the test rig. There were several sets of experiments without and with pressure sensors at different positions inside the cavities for a clear understanding of the sound field there and its relationship with sound transmission loss. To reduce the influence of aerodynamic pressure fluctuations on the results, a correlation method was derived to obtain the transfer functions between pressure transducer signals and the incident wave. The addition of a flap at the leading edge of each cavity, which was expected to be able to weaken the shear layer feedback mechanism, helped improving the sound transmission loss in the presence of the duct flow. However, the material of this flap was found very important. Flapping noise was also an issue. These are left to further investigations. Sound transmission loss experiments by coupling resonators of different resonance frequencies together were conducted using the abovementioned flow and duct facilities. Forty-three couplings were tested. Resonators were coupled approximately on the same vertical plane, keeping the lengths of the coupled resonators small. While broadband sound transmission loss can be achieved, the introduction of the duct air flow reduces this transmission loss. The physical mechanisms affecting the sound transmission loss are the shear layer activities at the mouths of the resonators and the resonant air oscillations in the resonator neck. The sound transmission losses were not changed much at low flow speed (< 8 m/s in general). The continuous reduction of sound transmission loss with increasing flow speed (stronger shear layer) afterward indicated that the former was dominant when the flow speed exceeded a certain threshold. In order to under better the mechanisms affecting sound transmission loss and to improve the performance of resonator for flow duct, a resonator was chosen and its neck was modified under basically two principles which tended to reduce the coupling between the neck flow oscillations and the shear layer fluctuations at the neck. The first principle was to reduce the strength of the flow separation at the leading edge of the mouth. This was done by rounding either one or two ends of the neck. The second was to change the flow impedance of one or two sides of the resonator neck (entrance and exit) by introducing fins of different edge forms on the cavity-side of the neck. These fins also restricted the air flow through the neck. Since the size of the resonator, especially its neck, was limited because of the flow facility, intrusive measurement devices, such as pressure transducer and hot-wires, will affect the aerodynamics of the shear layer and the neck flow. They were not used during the experiment. There were 10 modified resonators and one basic resonator (without neck modification) tested. Results show that those neck configurations which resulted in a shift of the resonance frequency of the basic resonator performed better in the presence of the low Mach number duct flow and when the flow speed was less than 10 m/s. However, sound amplification was found at higher flow speed at basically the resonance frequency of the basic resonator as if there was no neck modification. This can be due to the neck modification was only a minor change, such that the strong aerodynamic fluctuations excited by the stronger shear flow at the mouth were not affected much by the minor neck modification. Though further investigation will be required to better understand this phenomenon, the research student is working on it and trying to obtain some preliminary ideas for future research directions. This part will form the last chapter of his thesis.

527111.label: Major findings and research outcome
527111.value: The results indicate the possibility of creating a broadband sound attenuation device for low Mach number flow duct by coupling resonators, appropriate alteration of the resonator necks and coupling cavities. However, the air velocity is limited to at below 10m/s. All these devices offer only insignificant static air pressure loss across them. For the case of coupling cavities, the sound transmission loss is improved by offsetting the cavities and the larger the offset, the stronger the sound transmission. However, a larger offset will make the coupled cavities more susceptible to flow and stronger regeneration will be resulted. It is found that the sound transmission loss does not vary much at low air speed, and there is a threshold or critical velocity above which the regeneration sound becomes stronger and stronger. By considering observing the Strouhal number, a formula for predicting the effective length of the coupled cavity region is established. A journal paper on this issue will be submitted shortly. Broadband silencing is also possible by coupling resonators with the right sequence of resonance frequencies. This setup results in very small static pressure loss. The length of this coupled resonator section can be quite short. Again, the presence of a flow reduces the performance of this device. Strong regeneration is found at frequencies between those of the coupled resonators. A paper is being drafted at the moment. A total of 11 resonators with similar cavity volume and mouth area but different neck configurations are tested. These configurations, except that of the basic resonator, are believed to be able to reduce the strength of the flow separation at the leading edge of the resonator mouth and/or offer higher impedance to the interaction between the separated flow and the neck flow. It is found that the performances of the resonators with neck configurations, which result in large deviation of resonance frequency from the basic resonator, are better in the presence of the low Mach number flow (regeneration is less serious). However, regeneration at the basic resonator resonance frequency is still observed regardless of the neck configuration. A journal paper is being prepared at the moment. A novel experimental technique to capture the sound field pattern within the duct section where the above devices are installed in the presence of the low Mach number flow is derived.

527111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
527111.value: For the coupled cavities cases, it is only know that the out of phase pressure fluctuations inside the cavities play an important role in the sound transmission loss. The peak transmission loss frequency should relate to the effective length of the coupled cavities and the width of the coupled section. More detailed measurement within the coupled cavities section is required to provide a better picture of the physics. The addition of a flap to the cavity leading edge may help, but the material is very important to its performance. Further experiments are necessary. For the resonators, the current test rig is small and intrusive measurement devices will affect the air movement. Direct numerical simulation is a very useful method for better explanation of the underlying physics for the regeneration. Though it is shown that there are neck configurations which can stabilize a bit the performance of a resonator in the presence of a flow at velocity less than 10m/s, the reason for the strong regeneration at the basic resonator frequency at higher flow velocity is not clearly known. Further investigation is required.

527111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
527111.value: This project is aimed at understanding the aeroacoustics of helmholtz resonators and cavities when they are installed along an infinitely long rectangular duct at low Mach number. The sound transmission losses across these devices are also examined in details. Attempts are made to find out how the low Mach number duct flow affects the sound transmission losses. The major finding is that the present results confirm that it is possible to use reactive means to create a low static pressure loss broadband duct silencers, and the silencers need not to be bulky. This can be accomplished by coupling cavities and/or resonators. The introduction of the duct flow reduces the sound transmission losses across these devices. However, the increase in sound transmission loss of the coupled offset cavities is intrinsically high such that the corresponding sound transmission loss at a flow speed of 10m/s is still acceptable. For the resonators, the neck configuration has significant influence on the reducing the impact of the flow on their sound transmission losses. Coupling resonators with the right neck configurations and resonance frequency sequence is essential for practical flow duct application.

527211.label: Project Objectives
527211.value: To design and fabricate a multi-functional monitoring and warning footwear system for long-term normal use by the patients who have had or have a high potential to develop diabetic foot syndrome, in an attempt to reduce the risk of foot ulceration. To conduct experimental investigations, together with Dr. WC Wong's group at Orthopaedics and Traumatology Department in Kwong Wah Hospital, Hong Kong, to identify meaningful reference values of temperature, moisture, surface friction and plantar pressure distributions of human subjects as thresholds for sending warning signals to diabetic patients. To study new sensor structures for surface friction measurements, both theoretically and experimentally, by using soft polymeric composite structures integrated with optical fiber gratings and resistive e-fabrics. To develop a theoretical framework so that thermal/hygral mechanical analysis of the multi-parameter sensing network can be numerically implemented and provides guidelines for design and evaluation of fiber/fabric based sensor structures, flexible connection and the network as a whole. Collaborating with Dr. WC Wong's group at Orthopaedics and Traumatology Department in Kwong Wah Hospital, to conduct clinical trials with diabetic patients already having or having high potentials in developing foot ulcers. The MFIFS will be used together with the selected therapeutic footwear for evaluation of the therapy effects during a relatively long-term treatment.

527211.label: Realisation of objectives
527211.value: Objective 1: We have designed, fabricated and evaluated an intelligent footwear (I-Shoe) with monitoring function of plantar pressure mapping, temperature/humidity and 3-axial acceleration. For the pressure mapping, fabric pressure sensors developed by the PI's group have been used. Detailed investigation on the electro-mechanical connection was conducted using flexible printed circuit board and the electronic devices. The I-shoe was equipped with data acquisition and blue-tooth wireless transmission module, battery with a rechargeable port and data processing module. The I-shoe is capable of continuing working for 12 hours without charging the battery. Interface with smart phone and PC have been developed. It has been validated with satisfactory accuracy (7.7%), repeatability 6.4%) and wearing comfort. Three versions were developed and the final one was used for clinical trial at Kwong Wah Hospital. The I-shoe system can function well in normal daily activities. Objective 2 and 5: In the experimental study, Dr. Wong's group has actively participated in many discussions and setting up the threshold value of the pressure value. Under the guidance of Dr. Wong’s group, two clinical trials were conducted by Intelligent Footwear System in Kwong Wah Hospital. The first clinical trial involved a H group of 10 healthy subjects (male, 56±9.5yrs, 167.4±5.0cm, 67.6±9.2kg) and a DM group of 10 diabetic patients without peripheral neuropathy (male, 55.8±10.3yrs, 165.2±4.4cm, 71.2±10.0kg). peripheral neuropathy (male, 55.8±10.3yrs, 165.2±4.4cm, 71.2±10.0kg). There were no significant differences in age, height, weight, or sex between the two groups. This trial explored and identified differences of plantar pressure between the healthy and diabetic subjects in dynamic daily activities. Level ground corridor walking, up-sloping and down-sloping, and climbing up and down stairs with “the Shoes” on are tested. There were significant differences of the plantar pressure distributions among these activities. This trial further identified plantar regions where statistical significant higher plantar pressure between DM group than H group (p<0.005): left lateral forefoot (in corridor, slope and stairs activities), right lateral forefoot (in slope and stairs activities), and left central forefoot (in slope activity). These areas over the 1stand 5thmetatarsal heads were the common sites of ulcerations observed in clinical practice. For the second trial of high-risk diabetic patients, high pressures were found to be concentrated on forefoot and heel regions, especially in Metatarsal 1 (Ls7 andRs7), where the regions have very high risk in developing ulcers. Protection is needed to prevent these subjects from damage. A threshold value of peak pressure is defined as a high risk warning signal of developing diabetic ulcer. The threshold value of average peak pressure has been identified as 580kPa, the same as the clinically defined threshold value of neuropathy. There were not enough data for quantifying the effects of temperature and humidity, thus this will be a future topic for study. Medical doctors participated in this study comment that the obvious effects of continually monitoring on protecting high risk patients’ normal foot and the other foot recovered from ulcers. Objective 3: Step-index single-mode polymer optical fibers (POFs) were fabricated by the preform-drawing method. First, the photosensitivity of the core film was investigated by the refractive index reduction induced by UV irradiation and confirmed by formation of volume film gratings. Secondly, the refractive index profile of the fabricated fibers was directly measured, and step-index profile was achieved by prepolymerizing the monomer for fiber core. Thirdly, the diameter fluctuation of the fabricated POFs was significantly reduced by stopping natural convection in the heating jacket of the drawing tower with a cap. PFBGs have been inscribed by using phase masks that have a wide range of zeroth order diffractions, for example, a phase mask with zeroth order diffraction up to 49%, which is much higher than the maximum requirement for phase masks to write fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs) previously reported (<5%). In addition, the microstructure of the fabricated PFBGs was found dependent on phase masks. Hence, the near-field of phase masks was calculated based on their diffraction ratios. The calculation revealed that the near-field of phase masks was influenced by the zeroth order diffraction, but also the second and the third, and the calculated near-fields agreed with microstructures of the fabricated PFBGs to some extent. A sensor based on two PFBGs was developed for simultaneous measurement of shear stress and pressure by placing one PFBG horizontally and the second tilted in a silicone cube. Finite element analysis revealed that the induced strain along fiber axis was not uniform if the fiber was bonded to the silicone matrix. Hence, release agent was applied on the surface of POFs to prevent the bonding, and two gaskets were adhered to two ends of each fiber to stretch the fiber under loading. The measured sensitivity of pressure and shear stress were 0.82 and 1.33 nm/kPa, respectively. In addition, a biomimetic all-elastomer sensor array for three-axial contact force measurement was fabricated by injecting PEG 400 between two PDMS layers with stencil printed carbon/silicone strain gauges and silver/silicone conductive interconnects. Being composed exclusively of elastomeric materials and liquid, the sensor array exhibited a stretchability and elastic modulus approaching those of a human skin, which marks substantial progress of tactile sensors in this regard. The sensor was tested on an electromechanically coupled setup with a pulley to redirect loading. A sensitivity of 0.097 N-1 to normal forces below 1.62 N and an excellent sensitivity of 0.337 N-1 to shear forces below 1.3 N (with a normal force at 0.4 N) have been achieved, exceeding the best reported flexible 3D force sensors, especially for small shear force below 0.5 N. Such a soft shear force sensor can be used in gait analysis, slippage detection and dexterous manipulation of robots, etc, where friction measurement is of utmost importance. A geometric model on deformation of the sensor under compression further confirmed the arrangement of strain gauges on sensors. Objective 4: Following the coupled thermo-mechanical analysis, we have developed two methods for fabric sensing network. The first method is by physically linking distributed fabric sensors with stretchable knitted interconnects in a manner through helical connections. Flexible sensors with identical electro-mechanical behavior were packaged from knitted conductive fabrics coated by carbon nano-particle/ silicone elastomer/ dimethyl silicone oil pastes. Stretchable knitted interconnects were realized by intarsia knitting, electrically and mechanically connecting the distributed sensors in a predetermined configuration. Then, helical connections were studied for connecting the sensor electrodes to the knitted interconnects. Finally, a prototype was developed, consisting of an optimized electrical adapter, for an in-situ ballistic impact measurement, where reliability of the fabric sensing network was investigated. The corresponding theoretical analysis was conducted and compared with experimental results. Alternatively, sensor electrodes were integrated into a sensing element by sewing twisted conductive yarns as the bottom threads in a double-needle sewing machine, where a geometrical match between the electrode and the sensing element was established and mechanically fastened. The packaged sensor was flexible, bendable and can be repeatedly stretched to 60% strain in its wale direction with more than 100000 cycles. The electrical contact resistance between the sensor electrode and the sensing element was stable with applied pressure and tensile strain (60%). The reliability was measured and analyzed with respect to environmental, mechanical and fabrication conditions.

527211.label: Major findings and research outcome
527211.value: The intelligent footwear system has been refined for continuing monitoring of foot plantar pressure distribution, temperature, humidity and movement (conf paper 1). A new readout method was established with good performance (journal paper 4). Plantar pressure threshold of 580KPa was selected as the alarming value in consistence with the neuropalsy detection threshold value (conf. paper 3) Two clinical trials were conducted at Kwang Wah Hospital with promising results and positive feedback from medical doctors and patients. (thesis of MKY) Two kinds of novel soft sensors have been developed: silicone sensors integrated with polymer fiber gratings (journal paper 1 and 2) and silicone sensors with sensing bubbles (journal paper 3 and conf paper 4)). Both are capable of measuring pressure and shear force simultaneously. Theoretical analysis has been conducted for the design and optimization of the sensors and achieved consistent agreement (journal paper 2, 3 and 4). One MPhil and one PhD student have completed their study. Four journal papers and 4 conference papers have been published. An ITF project was funded based on the results of this study. Further exploration of application of the intelligent footwear system has been conducted and a private company has taken up the commercial development.

527211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
527211.value: The intelligent footwear system has attracted much attention both from academia and industry. Improvement of the new sensors is needed for the wearable applications. Engineered processing and facilities are required for industrial adaptation. Further funding support has been secured for this work.

527211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
527211.value: This study has developed a robust multi-functional intelligent footwear system (MFIFS) that continuously monitors, during normal daily activities, foot conditions and sends warning signals to diabetic patients who have already had or have a tendency to develop diabetic foot, based on solid scientific investigations and measurements of plantar pressure distribution. The key issues investigated include: (1) a robust and reliable system architecture suitable for long-term monitoring diabetic patients in normal daily activities; (2) fiber/fabric based multi-parameter sensing network for plantar pressure and friction; (3) effects of the measured parameters and warning signals on prevention of foot ulcers; (4) new sensors for measuring tangential force under foot; (5) theoretical framework for analyzing the multi-parameter sensing network made primarily from soft polymeric fibrous materials. Its findings will be very valuable to patients who can prevent damage to their foot and improve quality of life; to medical practitioners in diagnosis and design of orthotics and therapeutic footwear as well as evaluation of therapy effects; to tax-payers, it provides a tool in prevention of diabetic foot ulcers and has a high potential to save substantial resources in healthcare; to the industry, the new wearable technology adds values and competitiveness.

527311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
527311.value: The strong column/weak beam requirement is now widely accepted in the design of reinforced concrete (RC) frames to achieve good seismic performance. When subjected to seismic loading, such RC frames will develop the beam sway mechanism with plastic hinges at beam ends, which is preferred to the story sway mechanism with plastic hinges at column ends. However, many existing RC frames violate this requirement as they were designed according to inadequate design codes (generally previous codes). In particular, RC frames designed according to the current (or previous) Chinese code for seismic design are likely to violate this requirement as the contribution of a cast-in-place floor slab in tension is not included in assessing the moment capacity of the beam. Indeed, many RC frames failed by the formation of a storey sway mechanism during the 2008 magnitude 8.0 Wenchuan earthquake in China. To retrofit such RC frames, column strengthening is an obvious solution. Column strengthening, even if easily achievable, may simply shift the location of failure from column ends to beam-column joints and the foundation; the latter are very difficult to retrofit. This project is proposed to develop a novel seismic retrofit method for cast-in-place RC frames violating the strong column/weak beam hierarchy. The method is based on the weakening of the flexural capacities of the T-section beams at a joint using either or both of the following techniques: (a) separation of the slab in the corner region from each supporting beam by cutting a slit between them; (b) drilling of an opening on the web in each end region of a T-beam. Technique (a) involves simpler cutting operations than technique (b), but technique (b) does not disturb existing floor covering. In combination with the weakening operation, FRP strengthening (e.g. around a beam opening) is proposed to satisfy serviceability and limit state requirements. Beam weakening leads to reduced demands on beam-column joints and the foundation, and thus facilitates column strengthening. The overall strategy of the proposed method thus involves the combined use of beam weakening and FRP strengthening for enhanced system-level seismic performance. The proposed project will lead to the development of a novel, cost-effective seismic retrofit method for many existing RC frames in Hong Kong, the Chinese mainland and elsewhere. It will also lead to the creation of a significant body of new knowledge about the behavior and design of RC frames retrofitted using the proposed method. 为了获得良好的抗震性能，在钢筋混凝土框架结构的抗震设计中，“强柱弱梁”的设计思想已经被广泛地接受。这类框架结构在受到地震荷载作用时，塑性铰将出现在梁的端部，这比塑性铰出现在柱子端部对抗震更加有利。然而，由于设计规范（通常为旧规范）的不足，许多现役框架结构未能满足“强柱弱梁”的要求。特别是现行或更早的中国抗震设计规范在计算梁体的抗弯承载力时并未考虑现浇楼面板在受拉区时对梁体抗弯承载力的贡献，据此设计的钢筋混凝土框架结构也就往往不能满足“强柱弱梁”的要求。事实上，在2008年的汶川8.0级地震中，许多钢筋混凝土框架就是因为柱端出现塑性铰而倒塌的。 要对上述出现柱端破坏的框架进行加固，对框架柱进行加固是一个很直接的方法。对框架柱进行加固虽然可能较容易实现，但是加固之后可能会使破坏区域转移到梁柱节点或基础上，而对梁柱节点及基础进行加固难度很大。本项目拟为不符合“强柱弱梁”要求的现浇钢筋混凝土框架结构发展一种新型的加固技术。该技术单独或同时采用以下两种局部削弱方法以降低T型梁端部截面的抗弯能力：a) 在楼板角部附近切缝，将现浇楼板和梁分离；b) 在T型梁端部腹板上开孔。其中方法a)的实施过程较方法b)简单，但是方法b)的优点是不会影响到楼板铺装层。为了使结构满足正常使用及承载能力极限状态的要求，该技术还采用FRP对削弱后的结构进行补强（如在梁端孔洞附近实施FRP补强）。削弱梁端的抗弯能力将降低对梁柱节点以及基础承载能力的要求，也使对柱体实施加固变得更加方便、有效。由此可见，该技术是通过梁端削弱与FRP补强相结合的方法来实现结构体系整体抗震性能的提升。 本项目将为香港、中国内地及其他地区的许多现存钢筋混凝土框架结构提供一种新型、经济的抗震加固方法，同时将为采用该方法加固的钢筋混凝土框架结构建立力学模型和设计理论。

527311.label: Realisation of objectives
527311.value: Overall Achievement: We have fully addressed Objective 1. We have almost fully addressed Objective 2. We have completed most of the work for Objective 3. Realization of Objective 1: (1) A total of 14 full-scale T-section reinforced concrete (RC) beams were designed and tested under static loading to assess the effectiveness of the beam web opening (WO) (by creating an opening in the beam web near the joint) and the beam transverse groove (TG) (by creating a deep transverse groove on the soffit of the beam near the joint) techniques in reducing the flexural capacity of the beam. (2) A total of 9 three-dimensional (3D) beam-column joints (i.e., with transverse beam stubs) were designed and tested under combined axial loading and cyclic lateral loading to assess the effectiveness of the three potential beam-weakening techniques (i.e., WO, TG and slab slitting) in reducing the flexural capacity of RC beams at a beam-column joint. Slab slitting (SS) involves the separation of the slab in the corner region from each supporting beam by cutting a slit (including the severing of the steel bars crossing the slit) between them. Realization of Objective 2: (1) A two-dimensional (2D) finite element (FE) modelling approach was developed for the simulation of RC beams with a web opening under static loading. This approach was verified using the laboratory tests conducted in this project as well as those conducted by other researchers. (2) A 3D FE modelling approach was developed for the simulation of 3D beam-column joints retrofitted with different beam-weakening techniques. The approach was first verified using test results of RC beams and then verified using test results of 3D beam-column joints. (3) Numerical convergence was a great challenge in the FE simulations due to the existence of discrete local dynamic effects in these globally static problems, and a dynamic solution method was developed and employed in the FE simulations of these static beam tests to achieve convergence. (4) A simple FE model using a beam-column element in OpenSEES (http://opensees.berkeley.edu) was established for the simulation of RC beams with a web opening. (5) A simple FE model using a beam-column element has also been established for 3D beam-column joints under cyclic lateral loading although it needs verification and refinement. (6) An FE model for FRP-jacketed RC columns under cyclic and seismic loading using a beam-column element in OpenSEES (http://opensees.berkeley.edu) was developed, which together with (4) and (5) allows RC frames retrofitted with beam-end weakening techniques in combination with column strengthening to be simulated. Realization of Objective 3: (1) A simple design method for the flexural capacity of a T-section RC beam with a web opening was established and verified with test results. (2) A simple moment-rotation model for the region of a T-section RC beam weakened by a web opening was developed and verified with test results. (3) A design procedure that considers the combination of a web opening and local FRP strengthening for T-section RC beams to achieve a ductile failure mode was then established based on (1) and (2). (4) The development of a design procedure that caters for a combined use of web opening and slab slitting in a 3D beam-column joint is now under way. Two PhD students have been trained in this project. One of them (Mr X.F. Nie) is expected to submit his PhD thesis by the end of 2016, while the other student (Mr Q.K. 527311.label: Major findings and research outcome
527311.value: Findings Related to Objective 1: (1) The full-scale T-section RC beam tests showed that the WO technique can effectively reduce the flexural capacity of these beams. Increasing the height or the length of the opening can reduce the flexural capacity. Local FRP strengthening is needed for the opening to maintain the shear strength and ductility of the beam. (2) The 3D beam-column joint tests showed that all the three potential beam-weakening techniques can effectively reduce the flexural capacity of the beam. (3) The TG technique leads to a severe loss of ductility due to the slipping of longitudinal steel bars near the groove, so this method is not recommended. (4) The combined use of web opening and slab slitting, together with FRP jacketing of RC columns, should work very well for a frame to achieve the strong-column-weak-beam (SCWB) mechanism. Findings Related to Objective 2: A 2D FE approach for T-section RC beams with a web opening was developed and implemented in ABAQUS, in which the explicit dynamic solution method was used to arrive at a converged static response. Depending on whether flexural or shear failure governs, either the concrete damaged plasticity model (CDPM) or the brittle cracking model needs to be used to model the concrete. A simple rule to predict the failure mode was also proposed. The proposed FE approach was verified using test results of RC beams with a web opening from both this project and the published literature. The 3D FE approach was found to provide more accurate results than the 2D FE approach for T-section RC beams with a web opening. This is because the non-uniform deformation of flanges in a T-section beam can be better represented by a 3D model. It was found to be necessary to consider the confinement effect of the FRP jacket wrapped around the bottom concrete chord for local strengthening as the accuracy of the 3D FE model can be significantly improved as a result. Findings Related to Objective 3: The proposed design method for the flexural capacity of T-section RC beams with a web opening and the moment-rotation model for the beam region with a web opening were found to be reasonably accurate and reliable through comparison with test results. The moment-rotation model can also be expected to work well in predicting the behaviour of 3D beam-column joints.

527311.value: A set of design and construction guidelines needs to be developed to enable the proposed retrofit/strengthening techniques to be used in practice.

527311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
527311.value: Many existing RC frames violate the strong column/weak beam requirement as they were designed according to inadequate design codes (generally previous codes). For example, many RC frames failed by the formation of plastic hinges at column ends (i.e., storey sway mechanism) during the 2008 magnitude 8.0 Wenchuan earthquake in Sichuan, China. Against this background, this project has been undertaken to develop a novel seismic retrofit method for cast-in-place RC frames violating the strong column/weak beam hierarchy. The method is based on the weakening of T-section beams near a beam-column joint in combination with the FRP strengthening of RC columns. The research program included laboratory tests and finite element simulations to assess the effectiveness of three potential beam-weakening techniques for the seismic retrofit of RC frames and to study the behaviour of RC beam-column joints retrofitted with the proposed techniques. This research showed that the beam opening technique and the slab slitting technique can both reduce the flexural capacity of RC beams without significantly compromising its ductility. The combined use of these two techniques, together with column strengthening using FRP jackets if needed, can offer an effective seismic retrofit method for many existing RC frames.

527511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
527511.value: Effective motor recovery after a stroke depends on early intervention and intensive practice of the paretic limbs. Studies showed that overloaded training and stress in the early stages were found to increase the brain damage which could reduce the motor recovery. It is important to develop a well-controlled training load program in early stroke physical rehabilitation, which may optimize the rehabilitation outcome by maximizing neural recovery and minimizing brain damage. However, at present most the training is based on a fixed training program in the early stroke stage in hospital, and people after a stroke could experience different degrees of severity of impairments. There can be a more effective rehabilitation program by optimizing their ability in both brain and muscle in the rehabilitation training. The brain is known for its neuroplasticity, and the unaffected areas could learn the lost motor tasks after stroke by forming new neuron connections. We could encourage the growth and differentiation of new neurons and synapses through optimizing the training load with feedbacks from the subject biological signals. In this project, we will investigate the characteristics of brain waves and muscle activities during the early stroke period on a stroke rat model. Brain waves and muscle activities are recorded by Electrocorticography (ECoG) and Electromyography (EMG) respectively. Then, a Neuromuscsular Interface System (NIS) is developed with control strategies by incorporating the EMG and ECoG as the bio-parameters to indicate the workload and stress. Finally, the newly developed control strategy will be compared with different workloads and stress levels to find the optimized controlled environment to minimize the brain damage and to maximize the neuroplasticity during training. The results obtained from this project provide quantitative mechanism understanding on the interaction between the stress and fatigue levels during early post-stroke training. The training induced neuronal recovery is measured by the level of brain-derived growth factor (BDNF, an important chemical factor for neuronal growth) and motor function recovery after stroke. The findings from this project can help to optimize rehabilitation training based on the brain and muscle status on each individual subject to the design of a personalized training program after stroke. 有效的中風康復在於早期集中訓練。但是剛中風馬上訓練可能損壞腦細胞，所以如果可以找到最早在那時候開始做適當的訓練，可提高康復效果。醫院康復比較系統化，可能未必基於中風損傷而用同一康復程序。如果可以掌握腦部和肌肉信號從而選擇適當的訓練，可能容許更多其他未損壞的腦細胞從新學習。在這項研究可通過腦電波和肌肉電信號去選擇適當的訓練，實驗經過腦衍生神經滋長因子和功能康復的結果更了解康復過程，希望幫助每一位中風患者設計適當的訓練。

527511.label: Realisation of objectives
527511.value: Experiments in relation to ECoG-EMG pattern and stress have been completed. ECoG pattern from the brain signals from the acute to chronic stroke phases had been measured. The results have shown strong correlations with motor function recovery with the ECoG signals in the alpha-to-delta ratio (ADR). Specifically, around 60 adult male Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats (8-10 weeks old, 300-320g) were used in this experiment. All rats were subjected to 90 min transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAo) surgery followed by reperfusion for seven days. The ECoG signals were recorded at the pre-stroke phase (0 h), acute phase (3, 6 h), subacute phase (12, 24, 48, 72 h) and chronic phase (96, 120, 144, 168 h). This study analysed post-stroke seizures and polymorphic delta activities (PDAs) and calculated quantitative ECoG parameters such as the alpha-to-delta ratio (ADR). The ADR represented the ratio between alpha power and delta power on the ECoG activities. Forelimb and hindlimb motor functions were measured by De Ryck’s test and the beam walking test, respectively. Results in our journal paper [SJ Zhang, et al, 2013] showed 3 findings : 1) In the acute phase after stroke, delta power increased four-fold with the occurrence of PDAs, and the histological staining showed that the infarct was limited to the striatum and secondary sensory cortex; 2) In the subacute phase, the alpha power reduced to 50% of the baseline, and the infarct progressed to the forelimb cortical region. ADRs reduced from 0.23 ± 0.09 to 0.04 ± 0.01 at 3 h in the acute phase and gradually recovered to 0.22 ± 0.08 at 168 h in the chronic phase. 3) It was also found that ADRs have the highest correlation coefficients with the beam walking test (r = 0.9524, p < 0.05) and De Ryck’s test (r = 0.8077, p < 0.05). In conclusion, this study measured ECoG activities after focal cerebral ischemia and showed that functional recovery was closely correlated with the neural activities in the penumbra. Longitudinal ECoG monitoring at different phases after a stroke can provide information on the neural which are well correlated with the motor function recovery. We had designed a Neuromuscular Interface System (NIS) to find out the relationship between stress level and ECoG. We designed an experiment using different treadmill training intensities to induce different stress levels in the acute stroke phase; meanwhile daily ECoG signal was recorded.80 rats had been implanted with ECoG electrodes and induced ischemia stroke using MCAo technique, and then they were randomly assigned into 4 groups: control group (CG), low intensity group (LIG), gradually increasing intensity group (GIG), and high intensity group (HIG).Daily 30-minute forced treadmill training was provided to rats in all groups except the CG. Rats ran at the velocity of 5 and 26 m/min in LIG and HIG respectively, while rats in GIG ran at 5 m/min on the first day post stroke and gradually increased to 26 m/min on the 7th day. On the 7th day, all rats were sacrificed, and then their blood corticosterone and Brain derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) were extracted. It was found that rats in GIG had significantly better motor function recovery than others. Even though rats in GIG ran at the same velocity as the HIG on the 7th day, stress level was significantly lower than that in HIG and it was close to LIG. BDNF concentration had significant higher value in the GIG. Results showed that gradual increase of training intensity had lower stress level, higher BDNF and led to better rehabilitation. Results also demonstrated that if stress level could be monitored, appropriate training intensity based on subject’s stress level could be given individually, and eventually an optimized training protocol could be prescribed. This part of the study has been published in another peer-reviewed journal paper in 2014[Sun J, Ke Z, Yip SP, Hu XL, Zheng XX, Tong KY, Gradually increased training intensity benefits rehabilitation outcome after stroke by BDNF upregulation and stress suppression. Biomed Res Int. 2014;2014:925762] Another experiment has been conducted on 141 rats to compare different training programs to investigate the effectiveness. Combination therapies might increase the efficacy above levels achieved by single therapy. Therefore, we investigated whether the combination of bis(propyl)-cognitin, an uncompetitive antagonist of the N-methyl-D-aspartate(NMDA) receptor, and treadmill exercise could promote rehabilitation after ischemic stroke. Rats were randomly distributed into 3 treatment groups: infarct/bis(propyl)- cognitin(control group, DO); infarct/treadmill exercise(exercise only group, EO); infarct/bis(propyl)-cognitin+treadmill exercise(drug+exercise group, DE); and 2 control groups: infarct/no treatment (control group, Con); no infarct/no treatment (Sham). The results showed although all infarct groups improved over time, the combination of bis(propyl)- cognitin and treadmill exercise could effectively enhanced motor recovery during 14-day intervention. Early drug intervention has better recovery results, the group with drug intervention at 15-minute after stroke had better motor recovery than other groups. Both bis(propyl)-cognitin and treadmill exercise significantly elevated brain VEGF expression and decreased brain infarct volume at 14 day post-ischemia. This showed a combined drug intervention with exercise could lead to more effective neurorehabilitation with better recovery in the motor function after stroke in the rat model. [Another journal paper has been submitted]

The results have shown strong correlations with motor function recovery with the ECoG signals in the alpha-to-delta ratio (ADR). Another study with different treadmill training intensities showed that gradual increase of training intensity had lower stress level, higher BDNF and led to better rehabilitation. The last study investigated the effect of combination therapies with drug and exercise. The results showed the combination of bis(propyl)-cognitin, an uncompetitive antagonist of the N-methyl-D-aspartate(NMDA) receptor, and treadmill exercise could promote better recovery in the rehabilitation after ischemic stroke in the rat model. Two peer reviewed papers have been published and one is submitted to another journal. In additional, 3 international conference papers had been published and presented. All the publications were based on this project. Biomedical Engineering undergraduate student helper (Ms TSE Chui Han) had been recruited for 7 months and learnt how to conduct the ECoG signals analysis from the collected signals, which provide a research experience about neuroengineering and research application.

527511.value: The results demonstrate the ECoG signals from the brain could be used to monitor the brain damage continuously during the recovery process after stroke. We could apply this Neuromuscular Interface System (NIS) technique in further study with different intervention protocols for brain damage research. Different intensity of training and combination of inventions could be evaluated in the stroke rat model, which can support research to identity more effective intervention in future studies. .

527511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
527511.value: Brain signals from the cortex surface of the rat had been measured from the acute to chronic stroke phases. The results have shown strong correlations with motor function recovery with the brain signals in the alpha-to-delta ratio (ADR) parameters. Therefore we could use the brain signals from the brain to monitor the brain damage continuously during the recovery process after stroke. Another stroke rat study with different treadmill training intensities showed that gradual increase of training intensity had lower stress level, higher Brain derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) and led to better rehabilitation. Results also demonstrated that if stress level could be monitored, appropriate training intensity based on subject’s stress level could be given individually, and eventually an optimized training protocol could be prescribed which could lead to better recovery. The last study investigated the effect of combination therapies with drug and exercise. The results showed the combination of bis(propyl)-cognitin and moderate treadmill exercise could promote better recovery in the rehabilitation. This project has provided significant new findings about the feasibility and applications of using brain signals to monitor stroke damage process. Another important finding was appropriate training intensity based on the stress level could lead to better recovery after stroke.

528211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
528211.value: 通過超短高能量激光脈衝的發展，超快科學到目前為止已經產生了兩位諾貝爾學獎：分子過渡態的觀察和頻率計量的研究。隨著脈衝長度的進一步減少和脈衝能量的進一步提高, 預計會有更多的研究成果產生。另外, 高能量超快激光器在精密加工和衛生保健方面也被廣泛應用。 超短高能量的光脈衝源有助於超快科學的進步。因為光被限制在波導中，所以仔細對準光腔並不是必需的。正因為這一點,相對於固態激光器, 光纖激光器具有重大的現實優勢。光纖的發展潛力已經推動了近二十年的研究，但由於光纖激光器產生的脈衝能量和長度的限制,相對於固體激光器,短脈衝光纖激光器只發揮了非常小的作用。近幾年關於脈衝傳播的物理學新見解提供了飛秒光纖激光器的脈衝能量和峰值功率的數量級的增加。因此，設計節能,低成本, 可與現有的固態激光器競爭的短脈衝光纖激光器, 是有重大的現實意義的。然而,在腔內的能量比較大時，用於產生短脈衝的鎖模機制不再適用或單個脈衝分割成多個脈衝。這種所謂的多脈衝不穩定（MPI）的規定是對一個單脈衝鎖模能量的一個根本的限制。理論和實驗還證明了, 在多脈衝不穩定附近的一個窄的參數範圍內可以觀測到週期或混沌的行為。近日，我們提出一個迭代技術(提供了對於整個多脈衝隨著腔內能量增加的過渡行為一個簡單的幾何描述)。該模型可以捕捉實驗中觀察到的所有關鍵功能，包括週期性和混沌鎖模地區，更重要的是它提供了寶貴的見解(可以最大限度地提高光纖激光器的性能，即提高光纖激光器的鎖模脈衝能量)。 雖然對於大多數光纖激光器的配置，由於大多數光纖激光器離散和周期的性質, 要從激光動力學數值模擬中提取十分準確的結果是仍然困難的。所以將激光動態減少為可以由主方程描述的單個變量，是仍然重要的。並且，其理論研究成果可用於描述鎖模動力學特徵。研究激光動態的另一個有價值的方法是使用由主方程簡化而得到的低維方程。在這個項目中，我們建議使用從迭代的幾何描述中獲得的洞察力去聯繫主方程，降階模型和迭代模型，以指導以光纖激光器產生高能量超快脈衝的實驗。我們將調查商業上最成功的光纖激光器配置之一（使用偏振片和波片的被動鎖模實驗）。我們還將研究其他的被動鎖模模式，如使用非線性光纖環鏡的模式。其主要目標是產生能源與固態激光器相媲美，甚至高於固態激光器的超短脈衝光纖激光器。

528211.label: Summary of objectives addressed
528211.value: Objectives Addressed Percentage achieved 1.Engineering the cavity nonlinear loss to produce high energy pulsesYes100% 2.Master equationYes100% 3.Reduced modelYes100% 4.Connecting it all togetherYes100% A. Engineering the cavity nonlinear loss to produce high energy pulses: In the project, we used the proposed iterative geometric model to study a laser cavity mode-locked either by nonlinear polarization rotation using a set of waveplates and passive polarizer or nonlinear optical loop mirrors. We engineered the nonlinear loss in the laser cavity by incorporating a second set of waveplates and polarizer or nonlinear loop mirror into the respective laser cavity. The combination of the two transfer functions can form a more sophisticated transfer function which is capable of producing a multi-pulsing instability and chaotic dynamics suppressing behavior in the laser cavity which are responsible for limiting the energy of a single pulse. In both of the mode locking mechanisms investigated, by optimizing a single parameter the pulse energy per round trip can be doubled when compared with the laser cavity using only a single mode-locking mechanism. Global optimization of the laser output energy has been attempted but proven to be rather difficult because of the number of parameters involved. Much effort has been spent to determine if the multipulsing instability can be eliminated completely for example by adding more waveplates and polarizers or nonlinear optical loop mirrors. The computation complexity of the problem grows rapidly with the number of nonlinear loss added. We have managed to show analytically that the multipulsing instability cannot be eliminated in the case of using only two sets of waveplates and polarizer. Nevertheless, the objective to demonstrate that the cavity nonlinear loss can be engineered to produce high energy pulses is 100% achieved B. Master equation: For both mode-locking mechanisms investigated in this project, we had derived the partial differential equation governing the pulse evolution inside the fiber laser by assuming the laser operates near equilibrium such that the change in the laser pulse in each round trip is small and the discrete changes in the pulse shape and energy can be approximated by a derivative. We approximated the nonlinear transfer function of each of the discrete component, i.e. the amplifier, the fiber, and the nonlinear loss mechanism by Taylor expansion. We have also included the effect of birefringence. The resulting partial differential equation is in the form of vector Ginsburg-Landau equation. The equations were studied both analytically and numerically. The simulation results are compared with that obtained from the discrete geometric model. This objective is 100% achieved. C. Reduced model: For both mode-locking mechanisms investigated in this project, we used the projection operator method rather than the Lagrangian method to derive the reduced model, because the projection operator method does not require the use of a Lagrangian function. We have applied the reduced model to both the discrete geometric model and the master equation. In the discrete model, the reduced model is applied to the each individual component, and so it results in a discrete reduced model. The results from the reduced models are then compared with those from the master equation as well as the discrete geometric model. We found that the reduced models work reasonable well and can predict the multi-pulsing instability threshold in most cases. This objective is also 100% achieved. D. Connecting it all together – theory, simulation, and experiments: We have carried out experiments in both mode locking mechanisms. We have observed energy enhancement up to 60% when compared to the case when a single mode-locking mechanism is used. The discrepancy is not unexpected as the geometric models, the master equations, and the reduced models all involved many approximations making them difficult to make quantitative predictions of a real laser cavity. Thus this objective is considered 100% achieved.

528211.label: Major findings and research outcome
528211.value: We have proposed a general design and engineering principle that can potentially realize the goal of making fiber based lasers directly competitive with solid state devices. The technique is feasible and easy to implement without requiring a new cavity design paradigm. We showed that the cavity nonlinear loss can be engineered to produce high energy pulses. Although the results are far from the desired order-or-magnitude increase, it does suggest a clear method by which multi-pusling instability can be suppressed and the pulse energies can be easily increased. By sweeping a single parameter, an increase of 100% was easily in two different modelocking mechanisms when compared to that when only a single nonlinear polarization rotation or nonlinear optical loop mirror is used. Further engineering and optimization of the transmission functions by tuning the various parameters are expected to lead to further significant increases. This is the first major finding of this project. In the last three decades, theoretical study of lasers, fiber lasers in particular, has been dominated by using the so-called master equation which governs the near equilibrium laser dynamics for a laser cavity made up of discrete as well as non-discrete components. We developed an insightful way to consider the effects of dual transmission curves in the cavity through a geometrical model. The geometric model assumes that pulse shaping mechanisms in the cavity have balanced each other and focuses on the energy aspect of the cavity dynamics. Although the geometrical model is a highly idealized, its simplicity allows many of the key features associated with multi-pulse instability and its suppression to be highlighted. The predictions made with the geometric model hold in the full cavity simulation dynamics using the master equation. The success of the geometric model is another key finding of this project. The results of this project have attracted the attention of the laser modeling community. We had made four invited presentations. Of particular mention is the recent invitation of the PI by the Optical Society of America (OSA) to speak in an OSA internal workshop entitled “Incubator on Quantitative Modelling of Frequency-comb Sources” held in the OSA Headquarters in Washington D.C., United States. It is a gathering of the leading lasers scientists and engineers around the world to discuss the feasibility of quantitative modelling of lasers as frequency-comb sources. The PI was invited because of the recognition on the work achieved in this project.

528211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
528211.value: The success of the project opens up a different approach in the qualitative modeling of laser dynamics. An obvious way forward is the optimization of pulse output energy when more than one set of mode locking mechanisms are used to engineer the nonlinear loss of the cavity. First, more sophisticated optimization algorithms can be adopted to cope with the increase in the computation complexity when the number of mode-locker increases. Second, different type of nonlinear loss elements such as nonlinear polarization, nonlinear optical loop mirrors, carbon nanotubes, graphene, etc. can be combined in various ways and numbers in the search for the “ideal” nonlinear transfer function that can eliminate the onset of multi-pulsing stability and onset of chaotic dynamics. It will also be of particular interests, even within the limitation of the geometric model to determine analytically whether the multipulsing instability can be eliminated completely in any given laser configuration. Another direction of investigation, which is gaining popularity in the laser modeling community, is to carry out detail modeling, not just using the highly idealized geometric model, of the laser cavity in the attempt to match quantitatively the results from simulation with experiments.

528211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
528211.value: It is the goal of the fiber laser community to surpass the performance of solid state laser performance. Modeling and simulation are powerful tools in helping design next generation fiber lasers. Theoretical studies allow us to suggest concrete techniques for suppressing the ubiquitous multipulsing instabilities limitations. In this project, we studied both theoretically and experimentally a laser cavity mode-locked by a set of waveplates and passive polarizer or by a nonlinear optical loop mirror. We demonstrated that the pulse energy can be increased by incorporating a second set of waveplates and polarizer or a second nonlinear optical loop mirror in the respective laser cavity. The two nonlinear transmission functions acting in combination can be engineered so as to suppress the multi-pulsing instability responsible for limiting the single pulse per round trip energy in a myriad of mode-locked cavities. Theoretically, the sweeping of a single parameter showed that the energy can doubled. Further engineering and optimization of the transmission functions is expected to lead to further increases. Experimentally, about 60% energy increase is observed. The results suggest a general design and engineering principle that can potentially realize the goal of making fiber based lasers directly competitive with solid state devices.

529711.label: Realisation of objectives
529711.value: This project aims to study how the probability distortion in the investor’s target affects his/her investment strategies. It is a fairly new class of investment problems. It is an important yet challenging unexplored research field. Therefore, many fundamental problems remain open and new methodology needs to be developed. In this project, we have developed new methods to solve several interrelated problems and obtain many useful results both in theory and in practice. All the main target are addressed in our work. The main tool we have used is the quantile formulation which is often used to tackle investment problems when the probability distortion is involved in the target. We developed a change-of-variable and relaxation method to solve the quantile formulation problems without making assumptions. We have also used many classical tools such as stochastic control and viscosity techniques in the partial differential equations. One can see them in the published works in the report.

529711.label: Major findings and research outcome
529711.value: The most import result of this project is the work “A Note on the Quantile Formulation” by the principle investigator. In this paper, the author developed a change-of-variable and relaxation method to solve the quantile formulation problems without using the calculus of variations or making any monotonicity assumptions. Quantile formulation is the most useful tool to tackle investment problems when the probability distortion is involved in the target. The new method was demonstrated through a portfolio choice problem under rank-dependent utility theory (RDUT). The author showed that this problem is equivalent to a classical Merton’s portfolio choice problem under expected utility theory with the same utility function but a different pricing kernel explicitly determined by the given pricing kernel and probability weighting function. With this result, the feasibility, well-posedness, attainability, and uniqueness issues for the portfolio choice problem under RDUT were solved. The new method is applicable to general models with law-invariant preference measures including portfolio choice models under cumulative prospect theory (CPT) or RDUT, Yaari’s dual model, Lopes’ SP/A model, and optimal stopping models under CPT or RDUT. This work has been published in the top-tier journal Mathematical Finance in the filed. In this project, we have also made many other contributions and we list the published papers in the report.

529711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
529711.value: There are many potentials for further development of our research project. As mentioned in the major findings and research outcome, the new developed method is applicable to general models with law-invariant preference measures including portfolio choice models under cumulative prospect theory (CPT) or RDUT, Yaari’s dual model, Lopes’ SP/A model, and optimal stopping models under CPT or RDUT. We will follow this direction to extend our work to more research areas.

529711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
529711.value: The result of this project tells people how to choose the best investment strategies in practice. 529811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
529811.value: 中长跨斜拉桥中的斜拉索，由于具有柔度大、阻尼小的特点，在风雨气候下，容易发生大振幅的风雨振动。自从20世纪80年代以来，为了探索风雨振动的发生机理，桥梁工程界分别通过现场试验、风洞试验和数值模拟等方法对该问题进行了研究。尽管如此，人们对斜拉索风雨振的机理还不够明确。原因如下：首先，在风洞试验和数值模拟中，通常采用具有单个或两个自由度的刚性圆柱体来模拟斜拉索。但是，实际桥梁中风雨环境在时间上、空间上都发生变化，这种简化模拟后的拉索性能与实际桥梁拉索的性能有所不同。其次，斜拉桥的现场试验通常受到限制，例如桥梁主管部门不允许在桥上安装太多的仪器设备；至今绝大部分的现场试验仅仅局限于风速和斜拉索加速度响应的测量，而风和雨共同作用在实际桥梁拉索上的荷载仍是未知。此外，在风雨环境下，当振动频率满足一定关系时，全桥振动所导致的拉索支承位移同样会引起拉索的局部振动，而这种局部振动也会影响索的风雨振动。 本项目研究人员在主管部门的特许下，将在福建省青州闽江大桥（主跨605米）上安装各种不同类型的传感器，对该桥斜拉索的风雨振动进行全面的研究。试验中，将分别在拉索和桥面的不同位置安装微型压力传感器、风速计、加速度计、位移计以及摄像机系统。传感器和数据采集器的安装位置将避免干扰水线的位置以及尽量降低对拉索气流的影响。 安装的仪器将实时地对拉索的风压、荷载及其响应等进行全面的现场测量。将建立一个考虑荷载变化和支承位移等因素的拉索真实非线性三维有限元模型，而不是常规的只有一两个自由度的解析模型。通过真实测量得到的荷载来分析拉索的响应，并将有限元分析结果与现场测量结果进行对比验证。综合测得的荷载、响应特性以及数值模拟结果，将更好地理解拉索风雨振动的发生机理，从而进一步提高斜拉桥的安全性和可靠性。

529811.label: Realisation of objectives
529811.value: 1. A series of rain-wind induced cable vibration (RWIV) experiments have been carried out in the wind-tunnel laboratory of Southwest Jiaotong University, Sichuan, China. The cable vibration under various rain and wind conditions was investigated and large cable vibration was successfully observed. Two full-scale field testing have been carried out on the Jingjiang River Cable-stayed Bridge, Fujian, China. 2. A videogrammetry technique has been developed and extended to enable the measurement of the cable and rivulet simultaneously during RWIV. For the first time, the movement and geometry dimension of the upper rivulet along the entire cable are measured. The characteristics of the rivulet movement and thickness are investigated. 3. According to the experimental results, the relationship between the rivulet variation and cable vibration is analyzed. A new excitation mechanism of RWIV is proposed. A numerical model is established to verify the proposed mechanism. 4. A new cable finite element has been developed. With the element, the nonlinear finite element model of stay cables is established and the cable vibration is compared with experimental results.

529811.label: Major findings and research outcome
529811.value: Under the support of the grant, four refereed journal papers have been published and the other one is under review; three international conference papers have been published. The main findings and outcomes of the project include: 1) A videogrammetry technique has been applied to measure the vibration of stay cables on a real cable-stayed bridge. One paper is published in Geo-spatial Information Science, 15 (2), pp. 135-141. 2) The videogrammetry technique has been developed to measure the movement and geometry size of the upper rivulet along the entire cable. This is the first time in literature. The results have been published in Sensors & Actuators: A. Physical, 230, pp. 17-24 and Smart Structures and Systems (accepted). 3) According to the experimental results, the characteristics of the upper rivulet movement and the effects of this movement on RWIV are investigated. An RVIW excitation mechanism is then proposed, which shows that the rivulet–cable system is coupled and causes the cable and upper rivulet to vibrate at different amplitudes under the same wind speed. The upper rivulet harmonic movement changes the wind loading on the cable, causing the harmonic vibration of the cable, which in turn exerts a harmonic inertia force on the rivulet. A large vibration of the coupled system then develops. The findings have been published in Journal of Fluids and Structures, 59, 316-327. 4) An energy-based numerical model is established using the aerodynamic coefficients measured in dry cable tests, to verify the proposed mechanism. The numerical results are in agreement with the experiments. The findings have been written in one paper and submitted to Journal of Fluids and Structures for review.

529811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
529811.value: Flow field behind the cable will be studied in the laboratory to understand the interaction between the cable and flow in more detail. We actually have managed to measure it using the smoking technique whereas the background noise was so strong that the smoke – simulating the flow field – not detectable.

529811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
529811.value: The large vibration of stay cables has been observed in many cable-stayed bridges under the simultaneous occurrence of rain and wind, which is referred to rainwind induced vibration (RWIV). These vibrations may reduce the fatigue life of the cable and result in connection and protection system failures. Although a lot of numerical, laboratory, and field studies have been conducted, the precise excitation mechanism of RWIVs remains unclear. Some theories diverge or even conflict each other. A series of laboratory and field testings have been conducted in the project. In particular, RWIV of a cable model with the diameter of 160 mm was successfully reproduced in a wind tunnel. The videogrammetry technique has been developed and, for the first time, the movement and geometry size of the upper rivulet along the entire cable during RWIV were measured. The cable displacement was also measured simultaneously. From the obtained rivulet characteristics and the cable vibration, a new excitation mechanism of RWIV was proposed based on the existent knowledge on the flow passing an inclined cable. Finally, an energy-based numerical model is proposed to verify the proposed excitation mechanism.

530011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
530011.value: Removing moisture in the air by liquid desiccant rather than by low temperature condensation is a prominent way of air dehumidification at reduced energy consumption. Moreover, the use of liquid desiccant in air conditioning brings benefits to indoor air quality, indoor thermal comfort and health. Desiccant solutions are diluted after they absorb moisture in the air. Heat is required to concentrate them before being reused. Vapor compression heat pump is suitable for solution regeneration in case low grade heat sources are unavailable. The condenser of the heat pump provides heat for solution regeneration, and the evaporator cools down the strong solution to enhance its dehumidification capability. The liquid desiccant system has attracted extensive interests. However most of previous research on it focus on performance analysis under steady-state conditions. The lack of understanding of dynamic characteristics of such a system impedes optimization and control of it under dynamic conditions. Consequently, the system hardly achieves the expected benefits in real operation. Numerical modeling is an effective method to study system dynamics. However, dynamic modeling of the liquid desiccant system driven by heat pump is quite difficult because of multiple working fluids, a large number of parameters, complicated coupled heat and mass transfer process, strong interaction of various components and diverse operating conditions. This project will thoroughly investigate the dynamic characteristics and energy performance of the liquid desiccant system driven by heat pump. A dynamic simulator of the whole system will be developed on the TRNSYS platform. Effects of various parameters and process dynamics will be investigated by simulation and experimental study. Key parameters which significantly influence process dynamics and system performance will be indentified. Cost function of energy consumption, which relates the key parameters to total energy consumption of the system, will be built for systematic optimization. The genetic algorithm (GA) will be used to solve the multivariate nonlinear optimization problem and search for optimal running parameters, including the solution flow rate and concentration, regeneration temperature and refrigerant flow rate and etc. Robust control strategy will be developed to achieve stable and reliable operation. The research outcomes will evidently improve the performances of the hybrid system in terms of process stability and reliability, energy saving as well as indoor air quality and thermal comfort. 相对于冷凝除湿，利用液体除湿剂除去空气中的水分是一种更好的并节能的空气除湿方式。此外，在空调过程中利用液体除湿剂对室内空气品质、热舒适性以及健康都有益处。 在吸收空气中的水分后，除湿溶液被稀释，需要再浓缩后才能不重新利用。低品质的热源，比如太阳能和工业废热，是首选的溶液再生热源。但是，这类低品质热源并不总是能很容易而且很稳定地获得。另一方面，除湿过程中的溶解热通常会引起溶液和空气的温度上升而导致空气的显热负荷上升以及溶液的除湿能力下降。有鉴于此，本研究提倡一种液体除湿和常规蒸汽压缩热泵的复合系统，或称之为热泵驱动的溶液除湿系统。在这个复合系统中，热泵的冷凝器为溶液再生提供热，而其蒸发器可用于浓溶液预冷从而降低除湿过程中的温升并提高除湿能力。因而，该复合系统能有利于同时除去空气中热湿负荷。这种负荷系统引起了广泛的研究兴趣，但是，目前有限的研究工作主要集中在稳态下的性能分析，动态工况下的优化和控制研究很少。 本项目拟全面地研究热泵驱动的溶液除湿系统的动态特性，即考虑它工作在真实的变化的工况下，包括变过程空气状态和流量以及变显热和潜热负荷。通过仿真和实验的方法研究关键变量的影响以及过程的动态特性。本项目将为获得系统优化而建立能耗的目标函数，并采用基因算法来求解多变量非线性的优化问题和搜寻最优的运行参数，包括溶液的流速、再生温度、制冷剂流量及其它。本项目将开发鲁棒的控制策略以实现系统稳定可靠运行。本项目的研究成果将显著提高该复合系统运行的稳定性和可靠性，并更加节能和有助于改善室内空气品质和热舒适性。

530011.label: Realisation of objectives
530011.value: All five research objectives have been well realized. To address Objective 1 and 2, an experimental test rig of the counter-flow packing type liquid desiccant dehumidifier/regenerator had been built in the laboratory of Department of Building Services Engineering at the Hong Kong Polytechnic University. Comprehensive experimental tests in a broad range of operation conditions have been performed. A dynamic model and the associated numerical solution has been developed and validated using the experiment results. Considering that the packing material and the desiccant solution hold in the packing may store or release heat during the dynamic dehumidification process, their thermal mass is quantified and introduced into the dynamic model for the first time. The proposed model was tested and validated experimentally using three case studies under different transient operating conditions. The model and the validation results were reported in the paper submitted to Applied Energy. The validation results show that the model is accurate, reliable and computationally efficient. The model has been integrated into the TRNSYS platform for the system simulation. The experimental test rig and test results have been reported in the paper submitted Science and Technology for the Built Environment (STBE). Considering that the liquid desiccant and heat pump hybrid air-conditioning system can only remove the latent load, a parallel system for removal of the sensible load was investigated. Evaporative cooling and radiant cooling systems are possible choices. Research and applications on evaporative cooling in China have been reviewed and reported in the two papers published in Renewable & Sustainable Energy Reviews. To address Objective 3-5, dynamic characteristics of the liquid desiccant dehumidification have been studied both experimentally and numerically. Experiments were carried out to investigate the dynamic responses of the outlet air and desiccant solution to various changing inlet conditions. In addition, the influences of typical configuration and operation parameters on the dynamic dehumidification process were analyzed. The time constants of the heat and mass transfer process have been identified and they are very important parameters for design and tune controllers. The results are presented in the paper submitted to STBE. Control logic of the supply air humidity has been developed. The capacity matching in liquid desiccant and heat pump hybrid air-conditioning system was studied using simulation. Capacity matching among the four major heat and mass transfer components, i.e. dehumidifier, regenerator, evaporator and condenser, was studied. Novel matching indices are proposed to evaluate the matching effect. The results showed that a liquid desiccant and heat pump hybrid system with double-condenser, one solution-cooled and one air-cooled, was a feasible configuration for achieving capacity matching. The effects of three critical operating variables, including solution flow rate, revolution of the compressor and air flow rate in the air-cooled condenser, on capacity matching and energy performance were studied using simulation. Simulation results indicated that, there might be multiple feasible combinations of the three operating variables under a given operating condition, and the energy consumption as well as the energy efficiency under different combinations are different. When the process air handling load is high, there is an optimal combination of the three variables corresponds to the highest system coefficient of performance. Model-based energy cost function was developed and optimization of the settings of the three operating variables were realized. The results were presented in the paper published in journal of International Journal of Refrigeration. The research objectives were revised before the start of the project, because the approved budget was less than the amount requested. The major revisions were made on the experimental test rig. In the original proposal, a comprehensive test rig consisting of both liquid desiccant system and heat pump were planned. The current test rig only test the liquid desiccant system. However the heat pump system is modeled in the simulation platform. The revised objectives have been approved by RGC.
