530011.label: Major findings and research outcome
530011.value: Major findings are summarized as follows. Times constants of the dehumidification process concerning the outlet air temperature and humidity ratio are obtained. The time constants of the outlet air temperature (around 35s to 60s) are larger than that of the humidity ratio (around 30s to 50s) in all tests. In the air dehumidification process, the variable strong solution inlet temperature control method is found to be effective. In the desiccant solution regeneration process, the variable diluted solution inlet temperature control method is found to outperform that of the variable regeneration air flow rate control method under part latent load conditions. The heat balance analysis of the liquid desiccant dehumidification and regeneration processes shows that the conventional single-condenser heat pump is impossible to achieve capacity balance. Therefore, the double-condenser configuration is proposed. The simulation results indicated that, there are multiple feasible combinations of the three operating variables under a given operating condition. Model-based multivariate optimization method was developed for the optimal control of the solution flow in the condenser, the compressor revolution and the air flow rate in the air-cooled condenser considering process stability and energy performance. A larger fresh air ratio does not improve the coefficient of performance of a liquid desiccant based system that uses a heat pump as regeneration heat source. Considering both indoor air quality and energy consumption, the optimal fresh air ratio would be between 40% and 50%. One set of experimental test rig was developed. The test rig has been used to train several undergraduate students in their final-year research project, two graduated MEng students and one on-going PhD student. The PhD student will submit his dissertation by September 2016. It is expected that the test rig can be used to for teaching and research in the coming years. Three SCI journal papers have been published and two papers have been submitted to SCI journals. The funding support have been acknowledged in all five papers.

530011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
530011.value: This project primarily aims at systematic optimization of the liquid desiccant system driven by heat pump, i.e., to find the optimal set-points of key operating parameters to achieve optimal energy performance and indoor air quality. The implementation of the optimization largely relies on local controllers, which haven’t been studied due to the limited scope of current research project. Automatic real-time control is critically important to actual operation performance of the liquid desiccant system driven by heat pump. The PI plans to extend the current research in the area of local control. Digital programmable controllers will be installed and tested in both the simulation platform and the test rig. It will take a big step towards commercializing the proposed system.

530011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
530011.value: Air dehumidification is an important and energy-intensive air conditioning process for creating comfortable built environments, which normally accounts for 20-40% of energy use in air conditioning. The use of liquid desiccant rather than conventional low temperature condensation for air dehumidification brings significant energy saving. Owing to the reduced energy use in air dehumidification, more outdoor air can be introduced into the space and therefore indoor air quality (IAQ) can be improved. The liquid desiccant system driven by heat pump has been widely researched and commercialized products are emerging around the world. In practical applications, the liquid desiccant hybrid air conditioning systems work under dynamic conditions due to the changing outdoor and indoor parameters. The dynamic characteristics of the dehumidifier/regenerator is critically important to design and tune real-time controllers and hence the actual operation performance. Meanwhile, as a complicated hybrid system consisting of multiple key components, systematic optimization of the system is also very important to achieve optimal performance. This research lays a solid and applicable theoretical foundations for practical application of the hybrid system in terms of control and optimization, which can bring significant benefits to energy saving, IAQ and thermal comfort in built environment.

530411.label: Project Objectives
530411.value: To refine the currently-used conditional simulation algorithm for non-stationary typhoon wind fields over a complex topography for buffeting analysis of long-span cable-supported bridges. To develop a framework for predicting typhoon wind-induced non-stationary response of long-span bridges in consideration of the nonlinearity and span-wise correlation of aerodynamic forces. 530411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
530411.value: Many innovative long-span cable-supported bridges have been built in recent years, such as the Stonecutters cable-stayed bridge with a main span of 1018m completed in December 2009 in Hong Kong. If these bridges are located in typhoon-prone regions, the assurance of functionality and safety of the bridge during typhoons is of the utmost concern. This requires not only accurate modelling of the typhoon wind field at the boundary layer, of the aerodynamic and aeroelastic forces acting on the bridge, and of the bridge structural system, but also an elaborate method and efficient computation for typhoon wind-induced responses for reliability and performance-based design of the bridge. Buffeting analyses of long-span bridges under strong winds have been performed traditionally by invoking quasi-steady, strip, stationary, and Gaussian assumptions. Field measurements, however, manifest that typhoon winds over a complex topography are often non-stationary due to convective turbulence. Wind tunnel tests designed to study the spatial correlation of turbulence wind and aerodynamic force indicate that the strip assumption may not be valid. There is a need to revisit the current framework and to seek a more accurate understanding. Recent developments in structural health monitoring technology and advances in stochastic computational mechanics make this revisit possible. In particular, Stonecutters Bridge, equipped with an advanced structural health monitoring system (SHMS) of 1571 sensors, and located in a typhoon prone region with a complex topography, provides a unique and excellent platform for the revisit. In this context, this project aims to investigate non-stationary buffeting response of long-span cable-supported bridges to typhoon winds over a complex topography and will involve four major tasks: (1) the conditional simulation of a non-stationary wind field induced by typhoons over a complex topography for long-span bridges; (2) the formulation of typhoon wind-induced non-stationary response of long-span bridges in consideration of the nonlinearity and span-wise correlation of aerodynamic forces; (3) the computation of the extreme value of typhoon wind-induced non-stationary response of long-span bridges; and (4) the examination of feasibility and accuracy of the proposed framework by taking Stonecutters Bridge as a case study and using field measurement data from the SHMS. The findings will improve our understanding of the complicated nature of the interaction between typhoon winds and long-span bridges, and enhance our ability to assure the functionality and safety of such bridges. Research assistants involved will be educated as high-quality researchers throughout the course of this project. 大跨度缆索承重桥梁在台风作用下的非平稳抖振响应分析 近年来，世界各地建成了许多大跨度缆索承重桥梁。2009年12月，昂船洲大桥在香港落成，其主跨达1018米，为世界上主跨最长的斜拉桥之一。在类似香港这样的台风区， 如何保证这些大跨桥梁在台风作用下处于安全状态且能正常运营，是一个非常值得关切的问题。从研究的角度而言，为解决这一问题，需要首先为桥址附近的边界层台风风场以及作用在桥梁上的气动力建立准确的模型，其次为桥梁结构建立准确的有限元模型，并提出高效的非平稳抖振响应计算方法，最后根据计算所得的台风作用下的桥梁响应进行基于可靠性和性能的桥梁设计。 传统的桥梁抖振响应分析方法一般假定风场为平稳正态，风力则符合准定常理论和片条假定。但实测结果表明，由于强对流紊流的作用，在复杂地形下的台风风场通常是非平稳的，即不能满足平稳假定。另一方面，对脉动风速和脉动风力的空间相关性所进行的风洞试验研究已经证明，对大跨桥梁而言片条假定并不一定适用。基于此，有必要基于近年来桥梁结构健康监测系统的发展以及随机结构动力学的最近进展，重新审视目前的抖振分析框架，以对其形成更为科学的认识。特别地，昂船洲大桥处于复杂地形中，而香港又是典型的台风区，且该桥装备了一套由1571个传感器所构成的先进健康监测系统，这些都能为研究非平稳抖振计算框架理论提供良好的技术支撑。 本项目将详细研究复杂地形下大跨缆索承重桥梁在台风作用下的非平稳抖振响应，主要包含以下四个方面的工作：（1）实现大跨桥梁在台风作用下非平稳风速场的条件模拟；（2）建立直接考虑气动力空间相关性和气动力非线性的大跨桥梁非平稳抖振响应分析理论；（3）提出桥梁非平稳抖振响应的极值计算方法；（4）以昂船洲大桥为例，利用其监测系统所获取的数据，验证所提非平稳抖振分析框架的可行性与准确性。研究的预期结果可提升对台风与大跨桥梁之间的复杂相互作用的认识，从而进一步确保台风区大跨桥梁的安全性。此外，本项目还将培养出若干优秀的研究助理。

530411.label: Realisation of objectives
530411.value: A computationally efficient method for conditional simulation of non-stationary fluctuating wind speeds for buffeting analysis of long-span bridges has been developed from this project. The fluctuating wind speeds, with part of their time histories measured at some points, are regarded as a zero-mean non-stationary Gaussian vector process characterized by an evolutionary power spectral density (EPSD) matrix. The Kriging method is then applied to the random vector of the Fourier coefficients of the evolutionary vector process for conditional simulation. A mathematical proof of this conditional simulation is provided. A fast algorithm of the conditional simulation is further derived, by converting the Cholesky decomposition of a large size covariance matrix of the Fourier coefficients into the Cholesky decomposition of a series of small size coherence matrices with much less computational time. The procedure for implementing the fast algorithm-based conditional simulation method is detailed. This method is finally applied for the conditional simulation of typhoon-induced non-stationary wind speed time histories for buffeting analysis of the Stonecutters Bridge. The time domain buffeting responses of the bridge obtained using the conditionally simulated wind speed time histories indicate that the proposed simulation method is feasible and applicable. A framework for predicting typhoon-induced non-stationary buffeting response of long-span cable-supported bridges located in a complex terrain has been proposed. First, a non-stationary typhoon wind model is proposed based on observations from measured typhoon wind data. The wind model includes mainly time-varying mean wind speed, mean wind speed profile and evolutionary power spectral density (EPSD) function. Typhoon-induced wind loading on a bridge deck is then represented by time-varying mean wind forces, non-stationary buffeting forces associated with time-dependent aerodynamic coefficients and self-excited forces characterized by time-dependent aerodynamic derivatives. A nonlinear static analysis is performed to determine time-varying mean wind response, whereas the pseudo excitation method is employed to compute the EPSD-expressed non-stationary buffeting response of a long-span cable-supported bridge. The proposed framework is finally applied to predict non-stationary buffeting responses of a long-span cable-stayed bridge located in a complex terrain during a strong typhoon as a case study. The case study demonstrates how to apply the proposed framework and the results show that the proposed framework is feasible and necessary. The extreme value of typhoon-induced non-stationary buffeting response of long–span bridges has been investigated. The framework of non-stationary buffeting analysis is briefly introduced first, in which the non-stationary buffeting response is regarded as the summation of a time-varying mean response and a dynamic response that can be represented by a zero-mean evolutionary Gaussian process characterized by an evolutionary power spectral density (EPSD) function. The formulas for determining approximate probabilistic characteristics of extreme non-stationary responses are then derived by extending the currently-used Possion and Vanmarcke approximations. By comparing with the Monte Carlo solution, the extended approximations for extreme value of non-stationary responses are found reliable and accurate enough. Particularly, the extended Vanmarcke approximation can give closer results to the Monte Carlo solution than the extended Possion approximation. The extended Vanmarcke approximation is finally applied to the Stonecutters Bridge to find the extreme value of non-stationary buffeting response of the bridge to a strong typhoon. The results show that the extreme displacement responses of the bridge from the non-stationary buffeting analysis are larger than those predicted by the conventional stationary buffeting analysis, and therefore the non-stationary buffeting analysis is necessary. The feasibility and accuracy of the proposed framework have been examined step by step as described in each of the three papers.

530411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
530411.value: It shall be pointed out that the linear, quasi-steady and strip assumptions were adopted in the non-stationary buffeting analysis framework proposed by Hu et al. (2013). Li et al. (2014) recently applied turbulence dynamics theory to investigate turbulence spectra of tropical cyclones and presented a conceptual spectral model for typhoon winds. This conceptual spectral model reflects characteristics of strong convection carried by typhoons and is physically compatible with mechanism of turbulence. The influence of this finding on the non-stationary buffeting response of long-span bridges is worthwhile to be investigated.

530511.value: 用於多細胞信號測量的親水性高分子微流體膜片鉗陣列系統

530511.label: Project Objectives
530511.value: Aim 1: Fabrication of SU8-PEG patch clamp electrode partition array for multiple single cell recording. The patch clamp microhole array is fabricated by a two-step micro-molding method. The partition pore size is controlled by the contract between hard-PDMS sharp tips and the hard-PDMS coated glass slide. Aim 2: Fabrication of SU8-PEG microfluidic system. Firstly, three SU8-PEG layers are separately fabricated by UV-assisted micromodling method. Then, all layers, the planar Ag/AgCl electrode part and the patch clamp electrode partition are carefully aligned and covalently bonded together by UV-assisted sealing with a contact aligner. Aim 3: Characterization for the integrated hydrophilic microfluidic patch clamp system. Intracellular solution change is required to finish within a short time under a small pressure to keep patch clamp seals. The hydrophilic SU8-PEG based microfluidic channels can realize the pumpless intracellular solution exchange within a short time by capillary action. The flow rates within SU8-PEG channels with different channel sizes will be measured. The results will also be compared with theory predications. Aim 4: Testing of integrated PEG patch clamp array system for simultaneous recording of multiple single cells. The PEG electrode partition arrays have a common extracellular chamber, and the separated suction tubes, Ag/AgCl electrodes and intracellular solution chambers (trans compartments). Each PEG electrode partition can work independently and isolated by the PEG copolymer with high dielectric constant. This patch clamp array system design enables simultaneous recording for multiple single cells

530511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
530511.value: 在離子通道的生物物理機理及藥物篩選的研究中，一個現存的難點是實行高通量的電生理信號的記錄。基於矽材料的平面膜片鉗系統已經被用於並行測量。但是這些基於矽或玻璃的芯片生產成本高，尤其是制造微小孔結構的步驟要用到昂貴的設備及嚴苛的潔凈環境。近來，用於微流芯片的一種很流行的PDMS高分子材料被用來生產平面膜片鉗系統。 其擁有制造工業簡便及成本低的優點。但是，其憎水性的表面性質阻止了與細胞膜表面高阻抗的形成而且使快速換液不可能。 這個項目的目的是研發一種新的基於親水性高分子材料的微流膜片鉗芯片陣列用於多細胞的同時信號采集。真個系統完全是由親水性的SU-8和PEG高分子材料制成可以形成於細胞膜表面的高阻抗形成，高的信噪比以及高的防溶脹性能以及快速換液能力。這個項目的成功進行將會研發出一種基於新型高分子材料的膜片鉗芯片用於多細胞的同時信號采集。這將對於高通量的細胞電生理信號采集系統的研發有著重要的影響。而且，開創了對於新型親水性高分子材料的應用的新領域，這將對於生物物理以及醫藥行業有著深遠的影響。

530511.label: Realisation of objectives
530511.value: During the whole project period, all the 4 objectives have been fully realized. a) A SU8-PEG patch clamp electrode partition array was fabricated for multiple cell recording. A new force modulation based method is developed to control the microhole size and geometry via UV assisted curing on hard-PDMS coated glass slide. The size of the fabricated patch partition hole is from 0.5 micro-meter to 20 micro-meter. The small size of patch partition is preferred to have larger cell-patch sealing and better signal recording performance. b) The microfluidic polymeric system was also successfully fabricated. Multiple polymeric layers were partially UV-cured separately and then aligned together under a microscope. UV-assisted bonding was then applied to finish the bonding process. The planar electrodes were also integrated with the microfluidic device for easy cell electrical signal recording. This microfluidic polymeric system has 8 channels which can be used for multiple cell signal recording at the same time. c) The integrated polymeric microfluidic patch clamp system has been characterized for the pumpless flow without external pumping. Compared with PDMS based microfluidic system, PEG based microfluidic system had fast solution exchange without external pumping. High capillary flow rates with two orders of magnitude greater than those for PDMS channels with the same channel dimension. The flow rates inside PEG based microfluidic system matched well with theoretic prediction. The pumpless intracellular solution exchange with a Hela cell trapped inside the microhole was realized. d) The integrated polymeric microfluidic chip has been used for simultaneous recording of multiple cells using Hela cells as models. Good giga cell sealing rate was achieved with Hela cells with a success rate of 44% which is larger than that of common PDMS based chips under 30%. The whole cell current recording was successfully performed using Hela cells for intracellular solution exchange with various Ca2+ concentrations. The ion current change under extracellular ion channel blocking agent TEA was also successfully performed. e) The impedance signal was measured and analyzed for various polymeric and ceramic holes to understand the material and size effect on ion current signals through the microholes and nanopores. The impedance signals through the microholes and nanopores are also analyzed using equivalent circuit models to explore the pore geometry, size and material surface properties effect.

530511.label: Major findings and research outcome
530511.value: During this project, a novel SU-8/PEG polymeric patch clamp based microfluidic device was developed and fabricated. The related two step force modulation molding process was also developed to successfully fabricate micro to nanopore size from 500 nm to 20 um. The integrated polymeric microfluidic with patch clamp arrays were fabricated. It was found that PEG based hydrophilic microfluidic device could achieve rapid solution exchange without external pumping. Compared with PDMS based microfluidic device, the flowing speed was two orders of magnitude greater for PEG based microfluidic device. This microfluidic device was successfully used for the whole cell current recording of Hela cells. The effect of Ca2+ ion concentration and ion channel blocker TEA on the whole cell current were also successfully recorded. A high 44% cell giga sealing rate was achieved for PEG based polymeric patch clamp which was higher than that of PEG based patch clamp device which was under 30% (Xu et al., Biosensors and Bioelectronics, 2014, which is mentioned in Part C). We also explore the micro/nano holes size effect on the related electrical properties. Various polymeric and ceramic micro/nanoholes from 50 nm to 20 um were fabricated using force modulation molding approach and anodization method. The impedance signals through various polymeric and ceramic nano to microholes were measured and analyzed using equivalent circuit model. The effect of size, geometry and materials were successfully analyzed using the equivalent circuit model (Yang et al., Micro and Nanosystems, 2013, which is mentioned in Part C). We further explored the biological application of PEG microfluidic devices with nanopore arrays. A PEG based nanopore array microfluidic system was successfully developed for biosensing application. This PEG based nanopore array microfluidic device was demonstrated to have protein-repelling properties with low sample attachment and loss, which was suitable for bioanalysis (Tian et al., Sensors and Actuators B, 2016, which is mentioned in Part C)

530511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
530511.value: The further development of this PEG based micropore/nanopore microfluidic devices for cell analysis is to combine novel nanoparticle based optical probes such as graphene quantum dot and upconversion nanoparticles to realize the simultaneous fluorescence and ion current recording for the cells. The pore size can be even decreased to single nanometer range which may be suitable for DNA sequencing analysis. Another direction of PEG based micropore/nanopore microfluidic devices is for electrochemical application which may combine gold/silver nanoparticles as tag for signal amplification which may increase sensitivity.

530511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
530511.value: In recent years, PDMS based microfluidic devices has been widely used for cell analysis. However, PDMS based microfluidic devices suffer from low flow rate, high sample attachment and loss which need surface treatment and external pumping. In this project, PEG based microfluidic devices integrated with micropore/nanopores are developed for the whole cell current recording of cells, which realized rapid solution exchange without external pumping. This PEG based micropore/nanopore microfluidic system can also be adapted for other bioanalysis application with advantages of rapid sample loading without external pumping, easy fabrication and low sample loss.

530611.label: Project Objectives
530611.value: Objective 1 is to develop a generalized polyhedral theory. We will obtain a representation theorem of a generalized polyhedron via its vertices and extremal directions and show that the image/inverse image of a generalized polyhedron under a linear transformation is still a generalized polyhedron. We will study generalized polyhedral functions and generalized polyhedral Fenchel duality. We will show that the (weak) Pareto point/solution sets of multi-criteria piecewise linear programs is the union of finitely generalized polyhedra. We will then apply the solution structural results to establish the weak sharp minimum property of multi-criteria piecewise linear programs. Objective 2 is to design objective space algorithms for finding the (weak) Pareto point set of the continuous bi-criteria piecewise linear program and the discontinuous one respectively. Each subproblem of a continuous bi-criteria piecewise linear program is a standard linear bi-criteria program, which can be solved effectively and has a convex piecewise linear curve as its Pareto point set. The union of these convex piecewise linear curves forms an overestimate of the Pareto point set of the original problem. The key of our algorithms lies to determine the Pareto point set of the original problem from this overestimate. The continuous case algorithm will be extended to the discontinuous case via a non-homogenenous Farkas lemma. Objective 3 is to apply the bi-criteria discontinuous piecewise linear program algorithm for solving portfolio linear optimization problems with transaction costs. A subproblem of the corresponding bicriteria piecewise linear program consists of a subset of arbitrarily fixed stocks that are selected for investment. Thus the number of subproblems exponentially increases as the number of stocks increases. We will explore special solution structures of the portfolio linear optimization problems so as to avoid to compute all the subproblems of the bi-criteria discontinuous piecewise linear program.

530611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
530611.value: Polyhedral theory, an important topic in convex analysis and variational analysis, has been well established in the literature. Polyhedral theory has applications not only in optimization but also in many other mathematics fields. Multi-criteria programs have important applications in various decision-making problems in economics, management science and engineering. Under the framework of polyhedral theory, multi-criteria linear program theory and methodology have been extensively studied. Due to fixed charges and the integral nature of decision variables in real world applications, generalized/non-closed polyhedral and discontinuous piecewise linear structures have been used in various problem formulations. It has been shown that the Pareto point set of a continuous multi-criteria piecewise linear program is not necessarily the union of finitely many polyhedra, but the union of finitely many generalized polyhedra. Multi-criteria piecewise linear program is one, in which the objective function is a piecewise linear function, not necessarily continuous, and the constraint is a polyhedral set constraint. In particular, bi-criteria piecewise linear programs have specific applications to mean-variance analysis in financial engineering, cost-benefit analysis in management science and time-delay analysis in transportation science. It has been shown that objective space algorithms for bi-criteria linear programs have the advantage that the number of Pareto points in the objective space is much smaller than that of Pareto solutions in the domain space. It is the objective of this project to establish a generalized polyhedral theory and apply it study multi-criteria piecewise linear program theory and methodology. We will develop a generalized polyhedral theory and show that the (weak) Pareto point/solution sets of multi-criteria piecewise linear programs is the union of finitely generalized polyhedra. We will investigate the augmented Lagrangian duality theory of multi-criteria piecewise linear programs by using the sharp Lagrangian. We will design objective space algorithms for finding the (weak) Pareto point set of the continuous bi-criteria piecewise linear programs and the discontinuous one respectively. We will apply the bi-criteria discontinuous piecewise linear program algorithm to solve portfolio linear optimization problems with transaction costs. 作为凸分析和变分分析的一个重要课题，多面体理论已经创立、完善并且广泛应用于优化和诸多数学领域。多目标规划在经济学、管理学和工程中的各种决策问题上也有重大应用。在多面体理论体系里，多目标线性规划理论和方法也得到广泛研究。 在实际应用中，由于固定费用和决策变量的整数性质，广义（非闭）多面体和不连续分段线性结构出现于各式各样问题中。我们知道，连续多准则分段线性规划帕累托解集不一定能表示成有限个多面体集的并，却可以表示成有限多个广义多面体集的并。多目标分段线性规划是以（非连续）分段线性函数为目标函数，多面体集为约束集的规划问题。特别地， 在金融工程的均值方差分析，管理学的成本效益分析以及运输学的延时分析中，双目标分段线性规划都有着特殊的应用。我们知道，用于求解双目标线性规划的目标空间算法具有一个显著优点：帕累托点在目标空间中的数量远小于定义域中的数量。我们这个项目的目标就是创立广义多面体理论并应用之来研究多目标分段线性规划的理论和方法。 我们将推广广义多面体理论，并证明多目标分段线性规划的（弱）帕累托解集可表示成有限多个广义多面体集的并。我们也会利用锐利拉格朗日来研究多目标分段线性规划的增广拉格朗日对偶理论。除此之外，我们还会设计目标空间算法来求连续或非连续双目标分段线性规划的（弱）帕累托解集，并应用我们的非连续双目标分段线性规划算法去求解含交易费证券投资组合线性优化问题。

530611.label: Realisation of objectives
530611.value: A generalized polyhedron (or called a semi-closed polyhedron) is defined as the intersection of finitely many closed and/or open half-spaces. For objective 1, we developed a generalized polyhedral theory, including a representation theorem of a generalized polyhedron via its vertices and extremal directions, characterizations of the (weak) Pareto point/solution sets of multi-criteria piecewise linear programs, and minimal vertex-representation for a generalized polyhedron and characterizations of the nonemptiness and compactness of the solution set of a pseudomonotone vector variational inequality problem. We also established stable and strong dualities for DC (difference of convex) programs. Due to the disconnectness nature of the Pareto solution set for the multiobjective piecewise linear programs, it seems difficult to establish the weak sharp minimum property. For objective 2, we designed objective space algorithms for finding the (weak) Pareto point set of both continuous bi-criteria piecewise linear program and the discontinuous one. Each subproblem of a continuous bi-criteria piecewise linear program is a standard linear bi-criteria program, which can be solved effectively by the well-known multi-criteria simplex method and has a convex piecewise linear curve as its Pareto point set. The union of these convex piecewise linear curves forms an overestimate of the Pareto point set of the original problem. The key of our algorithms lies to determine the Pareto point set of the original problem from this overestimate. The continuous case algorithm was extended to the discontinuous case via a non-homogenenous Farkas lemma. For objective 3, we applied the bi-criteria discontinuous piecewise linear program algorithm for solving portfolio linear optimization problems with transaction costs. A subproblem of the corresponding bicriteria piecewise linear program consists of a subset of arbitrarily fixed stocks that are selected for investment. Thus the number of subproblems exponentially increases as the number of stocks increases. We applied an ideal point technique to avoid to compute all the subproblems of the bi-criteria discontinuous piecewise linear program. Our algorithm is able to plot the Pareto point set of the problem with 10 stocks within a few minutes.

530611.label: Major findings and research outcome
530611.value: As for a polyhedron, we obtained a representation theorem of a generalized polyhedron via its vertices and extremal directions and showed that the image/inverse image of a generalized polyhedron under a linear transformation is still one generalized polyhedron. We showed that the (weak) Pareto point/solution sets of multi-criteria piecewise linear programs is the union of finitely generalized polyhedra. See [1]. We established stable, strong and total parametrized dualities for DC (difference of convex) programs. See [6]. We obtained a minimal vertex-representation for a generalized polyhedron and showed its equivalence with a minimal half space-representation. See [4]. We designed objective space algorithms for finding the (weak) Pareto point set of the continuous bi-criteria piecewise linear program and the discontinuous one respectively. Each subproblem of a continuous bi-criteria piecewise linear program is a standard linear bi-criteria program, which can be solved effectively by the well-known multi-criteria simplex method and has a convex piecewise linear curve as its Pareto point set. The union of these convex piecewise linear curves forms an overestimate of the Pareto point set of the original problem. The key of our algorithms lies to determine the Pareto point set of the original problem from this overestimate. The continuous case algorithm was extended to the discontinuous case via a non-homogenenous Farkas lemma. See [1]. We applied the bi-criteria discontinuous piecewise linear program algorithm for solving portfolio linear optimization problems with transaction costs. A subproblem of the corresponding bicriteria piecewise linear program consists of a subset of arbitrarily fixed stocks that are selected for investment. We applied an ideal point technique to avoid to compute all the subproblems of the bi-criteria discontinuous piecewise linear program. Our algorithm is able to plot the efficient frontier of the problem with 10 stocks within a few minutes. See [1]. We presented two classes of equivalent conditions for local error bounds in finite dimensional spaces, which are formulated by using subderivatives for nearby points outside the referenced set and the various limits defined on the boundary of the referenced set respectively. See [2]. We developed an inexact subgradient algorithm to solve a nondifferentiable quasiconvex constrained optimization problem. By assuming that the computational errors and noise are deterministic and bounded and using the constant and diminishing stepsize rules, we obtained convergence results in both objective values and iterates, and finite convergence to approximate optimality. See [5]. We characterized the nonemptiness and compactness of the solution set of a pseudomonotone vector variational inequality problem in terms of that of the solution sets of a family of linearly scalarized variational inequalities. See [7].

530611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
530611.value: In our objective-space algorithms, every subproblem consists of a subset of arbitrarily fixed stocks that are selected for investment. Thus the number of subproblems exponentially increases as the number of stocks increases. We will study special solution structures of the bi-criteria linear programs so as to avoid to compute all the subproblems of the bi-criteria discontinuous piecewise linear program. We will explore the weak sharp minimum property of the multicriteria piecewise linear program.

530611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
530611.value: We obtained a representation theorem of a generalized polyhedron via its vertices and extremal directions. This property will be useful in future study of a generalized polyhedron. We showed that the (weak) Pareto point/solution sets of multi-criteria piecewise linear programs is the union of finitely generalized polyhedra. By using this solution structure, we designed objective space algorithms for finding the (weak) Pareto point set of both continuous bi-criteria piecewise linear program and the discontinuous one. We applied the bi-criteria discontinuous piecewise linear program algorithm for solving bi-criteria minimax portfolio selection problems with transaction costs. Our algorithm is able to plot the Pareto point set of the problem with 10 stocks within a few minutes.

530711.label: Project Objectives

530711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
530711.value: After the dedication of substantial research efforts to the study of metallic glasses (MGs) for over 50 years, the scientific community is now reaching the threshold of exploiting a variety of methods for alloy design and further broadening the applications of MGs into many industrial and engineering disciplines. However, critical issues still remain with regard to the basic mechanisms governing the processes of damage initiation and evolution in MGs during their pre-yielding deformation stage. Such a stage is characterized by apparent elasticity; however, it is also strongly connected to the confined inelastic motion of atomistic defects, such as free-volume zones. Despite the appearance of overall elastic deformation, the ‘undetectable’ and confined inelasticity may engender materials failure on the accumulative basis. For instance, the fatigue failure below the yield strength of a MG alloy is a well-known phenomenon that has not been well understood at the present time. As such, the revelation and study of such a subcritical inelastic deformation process is challenging but also of great value to today’s MG research. The outcome of the related research not only enables a deeper understanding of how catastrophic defects are initiated in an amorphous structure, but also provides the useful guidelines for materials scientists to search for the favorable structural/chemical features that an MG alloy should possess in order to frustrate such a defect initiation process and thus attain better plasticity. In the proposed research, we will team up with the research groups from three different countries or areas to tackle the above-mentioned issue. By combining our strengths in nano/micromechanics with alloy design and the state-of-art neutron-based structural characterization technique, we will extend the ultrafast cyclic microcompression approach, which we have developed recently for the study of the properties of free-volume zones, into the area directed towards stress-induced structural relaxation and irreversible damage in MGs at varying temperatures. 530711.label: Realisation of objectives
530711.value: The two objectives of this project have been successfully achieved. Through the research funding, we have published 12 journal papers, trained two PhD students, including Dr. Zeng and Dr. Wang, with the full or partial support from this project. (Note that these two were my PhD students at HK PolyU and I moved to CityU in 2012). On the experimental side, we characterized the atomistic free-volume zones through atomic force microscopy (Yang et al. Acta Mater 2012), nanoindentation (Huo et al. Acta Mater 2013)and microcompression (Ke et al. Acta Mater 2014; Yang et al. Sci Rep. 2014). To interpret the data and elucidate the mechanisms, physical models were developed and compared with the experimental results (Liu et al. Intermetallics, 2012; Huo et al. Acta Mater 2013, Ke et al. Acta Mater 2014) as obtained across a wide range of metallic glasses. We also related the atomistic defects we discovered and modeled to the macroscopic plastic behavior of the metallic glasses. For example, we successfully achieved the tensile ductility in metallic glasses (Wang et al. Sci Rep. 2014) by generating more atomic defects via surface treatment, which are otherwise brittle and show zero tensile ductility at room temperature. Meanwhile, there are also a few new phenomena we discovered which can be related to the atomic scale defects in the metallic glasses. For example, the size dependence of metallic-glass hardness (Wang et al. JMPS 2015), the minor alloying effect on glass formability of metallic glasses (Wang et al. Sci. Rep. 2014) and the delayed yielding behavior (Liu et al. APL, 2014). Combining all the findings, one can have a physical picture or knowledge of how metallic glasses deform elastically and plastically. Most importantly, with this knowledge, one can design ductile metallic glasses as we already demonstrated in one of the papers (Wang et al. Sci. Rep. 2014).

530711.label: Major findings and research outcome
530711.value: (1) a simple mean-field model is developed to formulate the anelastic deformation in metallic glasses (MGs). The modeling provides a analytical framework to explain the various phenomena related to the local rheological properties in metallic glasses due to their intrinsic structural heterogeneity. (2) the structural origin of the shear modulus and the underlying structural evolution process in MGs is elucidated. Consistent with the notion of intrinsic structural heterogeneity in MGs, here we show that there are two concurrent contributions, i.e. bonding strength and configurational transition (or fast dynamic relaxation), to their quasi-static shear modulus. (3) we develop the method for obtaining a high-resolution atomic force microscopy image of the nanoscale structure in an MG thin film through the correction of the surface adhesion and topography effects. We also provide in unprecedented detail experimental evidence of how atomic packing evolves in an annealed Zr–Ni MG thin film. (4) we demonstrate that the brittle fracture in BMGs under tensile loading can be overcome by introducing a gradient amorphous structure through the carefully controlled surface treatment process. Owing to the high volume fraction of the liquid-like atoms near the surface, shear banding is promoted while cavitation/fracture is suppressed, thus giving rise to the tensile ductility which cannot be obtained otherwise in the as-cast MGs. Most importantly, the tensile ductility enhancement so obtained does not sacrifice but rather boosts the fracture strength of the glass, which somewhat reconciles the longstanding strength-ductility paradox facing MGs. Since our method is in principle applicable to different alloy compositions, we envision that tensile ductility higher than 2–4% may be achievable in future, therefore paving the way for the structural applications of MGs. (5) we develop a theoretical model based on the notion of size-controlled shear band nucleation to account for the indentation size effect in MGs. Through the carefully designed experiments, this model prediction is justified on the Zr-based MG. By fitting the experimental data to the theory, we are able to extract the nucleation length for multiple shear banding from the trend of the indentation size effect for different indentation strain rates. Furthermore, our results show that the nucleation length for the Zr-based MG exhibits slight rate dependence, which can be rationalized by the rate-affected shear softening behavior in MGs. Finally, it is worth pointing out that the experimental/theoretical framework herein established is rather general, which should be applicable to other MG alloys or even other types of glassy materials.

530711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
530711.value: Further development of this research can be directed to the control of these atomic-scale defects to enhance the micro- and macro-scale structural/functional properties of metallic glasses (MGs). This involves a clear understanding of the interaction of these defects with the possible external fields, such as stress field, magnetic field, electric field and etc. Some of the research is now being undertaken in my lab and some of the preliminary results obtained to date are very interesting and promising.

530711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
530711.value: The atomic structure and associated deformation behavior of metallic glasses (MGs) have been long standing issues. Although recent computational/experimental results indicate that the structure of MGs is heterogeneous at the nano scale, the fundamental knowledge of the atomic basis for such structural heterogeneity and its impact on the overall properties of MGs is still lacking. Through this project, we unraveled the structure heterogeneity in MGs via theoretical modeling and the use of dynamic atomic force microscopy,nanoindentation and microcompression. The outcome of our research leads to the development of various methods for the characterization of the heterogeneous structures in glassy solids as well as the establishment of numerous correlations of the overall properties with the structural heterogeneity.

530811.label: Project Objectives
530811.value: To establish a thorough scientific basis for understanding the physiological mechanisms, psychological needs, responses and behaviours of diabetic patients in relation to various clinical situations, current development processes and difficulties of making custom-made orthotic insoles to protect the diabetic foot against impact, pressure and shear forces. To analyse the anthropometry measurements, morphologies and deformities of the diabetic foot and activity profiles of diabetic patients in relation to plantar foot pressures in order to develop optimally fitting orthotic insoles to relieve plantar pressures. To examine the psychological relationship between plantar pressure distribution and the subjective perception of sensory comfort of diabetic patients, and formulate a biomechanical model to simulate plantar pressure distribution in relation to the mechanical and stress-strain properties of orthotic insole materials, and 3D design and geometry of insoles. Factors such as thickness, hardness and structures of the insole materials, which influence the support, cushioning, comfort and functional performance of orthotic insoles, will be identified and associated with the monitoring of complication progression so as to determine the optimal plantar pressure distribution and the most desirable fabrication for the prevention of plantar ulcerations for diabetics. To design and develop, on the basis of clinical and textile science analyses, optimally fitting orthotic insoles which can improve the physiological comfort of patients, and accurately and reliably alleviate plantar pressures, thus reducing the risk of diabetic foot ulcerations for patients with different levels of pressure requirements and clinical practices. To undertake wear trials that will evaluate whether the intended objectives of orthotic insoles that prevent plantar ulcerations can be achieved, and determine the effectiveness and practical use of these orthotic insoles.

530811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
530811.value: The project aims to develop custom-fabricated orthotic insoles for patients with diabetes. The insoles that will be inserted into footwear are used to reduce and redistribute the plantar weight forces imposed on bony prominences with excessive pressure in order to prevent ulcerations in the neuropathic diabetic foot. The design, use of foam materials for fabrication, and fitting of the orthotic insoles are crucial because they influence the foot-orthosis interface pressures, comfort of walking, and eventually, the efficacy of foot orthotic treatment for prevention of foot ulcers. However, due to limited choices of fabrication materials and suitable characterisation technologies, the efficacy of orthotic insoles for fit and pressure still greatly depends on repeated trials and errors based on the experience of individual practitioners. With the rapid increase in the prevalence of diabetes, this project aims to design and develop orthotic insoles that can accurately and reliably redistribute and control plantar pressures with optimum fitting, comfort and functional performance, and thus provide optimum patient protection from pressure ulcerations. The dimensions used include physiological and psychological needs of patients, practical use and clinical procedures of the foot orthotic treatment, analyses of foot-orthosis interface pressure data in relation to different plantar regions and loading patterns, geometric design of the knitting structure of insole materials and their laminated composites, and precise determination of plantar pressure distribution which can prevent and reduce the risk of building excessive pressure and neuropathic ulcerations. Scientific characterization of the 3D foot geometry of orthotic insoles and a thorough understanding of the material mechanical and stress-strain properties on the surface of the foot will also be carried out. To achieve optimum comfort and functional performance, factors such as the psychophysical relationship between pressure distribution and subjective perception of sensory comfort, deterioration of material compressibility that influences functional performance and efficacy of orthotic insoles, are also analysed. Insole specifications, fabrication, structural features and biomechanical models of pressure simulation when orthotic insoles are applied will be formulated. Prototypes of orthotic insoles will also be developed. The efficacy of the treatment and patient compliance will be evaluated based on clinical wear trials. The outcomes of the project will advance our knowledge on the design or elements of orthotic insoles and/or medical textile products by incorporating modern textiles and garment technologies. More importantly, the project can enhance the quality of treatment and therefore, patients can be more easily reintegrated back into their homes and society.

530811.label: Realisation of objectives
530811.value: Clinical study was carried out to establish a thorough understanding of the physiological mechanisms and psychological needs, responses and behaviours of diabetic patients. The settings of prosthetic and orthotic units of hospitals, various clinical situations, current development processes and difficulties of making custom-made orthotic insoles were examined. A total of 4 subjects were recruited. Their clinical procedures for the casting, 3D design and development processes of orthotic insoles and the choice of foam materials and/or composites were recorded. Their comments toward the orthotic insole treatment over 3 months were also investigated. An objective and efficient method to obtain precise foot measurements during clinical practices in various locations in a hospital was proposed. A novel approach of evaluating foot-insole conformity and dimensional changes of orthotic insoles during the clinical study by using a reverse engineering software was adopted. On the other hand, a systematic approach to quantitatively assess the key properties of insole materials and a novel performance index were formulated to assess the suitability of orthotic insoles. A new approach of measuring the energy absorption performance of insole materials was developed by using a dynamic load cell at the bottom of the tailor made instrument to measure the impact force that acts on the materials. A new method of measuring the dynamic coefficients of friction and shearing angles was also adopted to simulate the contact condition between the plantar surface of the foot and the insole materials. To improve in-shoe thermal comfort and plantar pressure relieving property, a novel perspective on the use of spacer materials suitable for the construction of insoles is proposed and developed in this study. The open structure of the spacer fabrics not only could enhance the overall breathability and thermal conductivity by creating a moisture free environment so as to maintain thermal comfort, but also provide excellent resilience and recovery performance, thus enhancing the overall accommodation of the foot-insole when in direct contact with the foot. A model of a custom-made three-layer contoured insole that simulates foot-insole interactions was developed by using finite element analysis. The simulation model not only provides a promising solution to the modification of materials for insoles by predicting and visualising insole deformation patterns, but also effectively optimises the design and development process of orthotic insoles without the need to fabricate and test the insoles in a series of wear trials.

530811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
530811.value: As thermal comfort of insole material plays a crucial role in the efficacy of orthotic treatment, more laboratory studies can be carried out to test the thermal property and behaviors under simulated and standardized in-shoe conditions. Through variations of the temperature and humidity in the in-shoe microclimate, the thermal comfort performance of different foam materials and multi-layer insoles can be examined The transversal compressibility of spacer fabric design could be further intensified to enhance the structure for more applicability in interventions by using various orthotic insoles. More stiff monofilaments, such as polyethylene or polypropylene, may be used and a higher interlacing density may be adopted in the spacer layer structure to increase the pile height so as to improve the cushioning effect and durability during the orthotic treatment. Studies on the designing of orthotic insoles done on normal subjects may not replicate the real situation of diabetic subjects. Furthermore, wear trial studies could be carried out with follow-up sessions to investigate the changes in the plantar pressure, lower limb biomechanics, perceived comfort and more importantly, the effectiveness of the orthotic insoles in terms of shape or thickness as time passes.

532011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
532011.value: The proposed project aims to study the production of environmentally safe bio-materials such as chitosan-based and gelatin-based microcapsules for the removal of synthetic dyes and toxic heavy metals. The conditions of the removal processes, e.g. variation in pH, initial dye concentration and temperature, will be evaluated. The removal mechanism will be studied using mathematical models such as common equilibrium sorption isotherms and kinetic models. The present study will (1) explore the feasibility of using novel microcapsules containing oil compounds, water-soluble materials or microorganisms to remove dyes and toxic heavy metals from the waste water, (2) determine various parameters involved in the removal processes, and (3) assess the properties and toxicity of novel microcapsules. The key objectives to be addressed in the proposed project are: 1. To develop novel oil-in-water (o/w) and water-in-oil (w/o) microcapsules for the removal of dyes and toxic heavy metals using natural biopolymer. 2. To develop novel microcapsules embedded with microorganism and investigate the feasibility of using them to further enhance the removal ability of dyes and toxic heavy metals. 3. To establish systematic characterisation methods for evaluating the performance and assessing the toxicity of novel microcapsules. 4. To evaluate the effectivess and sorption capacities of novel microcapsules. The proposed research will contribute significantly to the advance of knowledge in the development of novel microcapsules with potential ability of removing dyes and toxic heavy metals from the effluent. It is expected that the application of various novel microcapsules can help enhance the efficiency and maximise the performance of waste water treatment. In the long run, it is anticipated that the novel microcapsules can be commercialised based on their effectiveness and sorption capacities of dye/heavy metal removal. At the same time, the development of novel microcapsules is expected to be a breakthrough to the application on both textile and waste water treatment industries. The empirical characterisation methods established in this research project are also expected to provide a guideline for commercial sectors and researchers to identify and evaluate the performance of novel microcapsules with potential dye/heavy metal removal effect in a systematic and objective way. As a whole, it is anticipated that the development of novel microcapsules containing oil compounds, water-soluble materials, or microorganisms will continue to grow mainly as new possibilities and alternatives for waste water treatment in the near future, and will be a challenging and exciting age for the textile colouration and finishing industries. 本項目的研究目的是生產基於對環境無害的生物源材料，例如殼聚糖和明膠等的微膠囊，用於去除污水中的合成染料和有毒重金屬。清除流程條件的變化，例如酸鹼值、染料濃度和溫度等都會考慮。清除機理將使用常見的平衡等溫線數學模型和動力學模型去表示。本研究將 (1) 探索利用含有油溶性或水溶性化合物或微生物的新穎的微膠囊去除污水中的染料和有毒重金屬的可行性； (2) 確定在清除過程中，所涉及的各種參數的關係和 (3) 評估新穎的微膠囊的屬性和毒性。 本項目主要目的是: （一） 利用天然的生物材料，以水包油和油包水的技術去研發新穎的微膠囊，用於除去污水中的染料和有毒重金屬。 （二） 研發將微生物封裝在這新穎的微膠囊內，進一步加強除去污水中的染料和有毒重金屬的成效。 （三） 成立一系列鑒證的方法去評估此新穎的微膠囊除污的成效以及其毒性。 （四） 最後評估此新熲的微膠囊吸附的能力及其有效性。 本提議的研究項目將大大有助於增進新穎的微膠囊知識的發展，並發揮其在去除污水中染料和有毒重金屬的潛在能力。預計各種新頴的微膠囊的應用可以提高污水處理的性能和效率。長遠而言，本項目研發的新穎的微膠囊是有很高的商業價值。同時，發展新頴的微膠囊預計是一個對紡織和污水處理行業的突破。設立這項研究的結果可望提供商界和研究人員有系統地識別和客觀地評估新頴的微膠囊用於去除污水中的染料和有毒重金屬的指南。作為一個整體計劃，預計含有油溶性或水溶性化合物或微生物的新穎的微膠囊將會是未來的發展方向，並在不久的將來替代或提供新的方法用於紡織染色和污水處理過程。

532011.label: Major findings and research outcome
532011.value: Water pollution is attributed to contamination from biochemical substances and chemicals. Synthetic dyes and heavy metal ions are common pollutants from the effluents of dyeing industries. These pollutants are even in a part-per-million scale, give rise to serious environmental damage. Although conventional methods such as precipitation, ion exchange, filtration, etc. are being used to treat polluted water, these methods have their own shortcomings or implementation is costly for satisfactory results. As an alternative, adsorption has been introduced into water treatment and this method is still being extensively explored by researchers. Biosorption is a kind of adsorption making use of biological adsorbents to physically or chemically remove the target adsorbates. Biosorbents have been explored in-depth in terms of utilizing their removal ability with physical and chemical treatments. Besides biosorption, biological functions from live cultures have also been one of the promising ways to treat synthetic dyes and heavy metals. The aim of this study is to encapsulate microorganisms as biosorbents for the removal of synthetic dyes and heavy metal ions. The research methodology follows several steps. Started with the selection of microorganisms for encapsulation and the encapsulating materials, the target synthetic dyes and heavy metal ions were then selected. Synthesis and characterization of the biosorbents were the next step. Finally, the evaluation and mechanistic study of the biosorption synthetic dyes and heavy metal ions were launched. The characterizations of the biosorbents include the use of FTIR spectroscopy, zeta potential measurement and SEM. The viability of the encapsulated culture is also examined in which live culture encapsulation is successfully achieved. The major findings are 1) Lactobacillus casei (L. casei) is encapsulated successfully into chitosan hydrogel beads through a coacervation process with alkali neutralization and ionotropic crosslinking. The effects of pH, temperature, crosslinking and encapsulating L. casei are examined to evaluate the biosorption of the combined biosorbents. 2) A yeast strain, C. krusei, is encapsulated successfully into alginate-based hydrogel beads and the viability of the culture is also maintained. The biosorption of heavy metal ions is carried out by using biosorbents. 3) A kinetic study reveals that these biosorbents follow pseudo second order kinetics. The isotherm modelling shows that the biosorption follows a Langmuir isotherm after encapsulating C. krusei. However, C. krusei and alginate hydrogel beads fit better with the use of the Freundlich isotherm.

532011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
532011.value: In this study, chitosan-and alginate-based hydrogel beads have been synthesized. A number of polymeric supports, such as polysulfonate, gelatin, and polyvinyl alcohol are also potential candidates for encapsulating different cultures for biosorption. From the view point of biodegradation, no suitable way is found in this study which would obtain biological reactions from the cultures toward the synthetic dyes. More work to examine the general conditions of dye biodegradation by using microorganisms is vital. Specific conditions to biodegrade specific groups of substrate from particular cultures with their biological metabolisms are not enough to deal with practical pollution control. A general method used to biodegrade different groups of synthetic dyes in one pot by culture is beneficial to the development in this study. Besides, pretreatment of microorganisms has not been studied for possible outcomes. However, it has been reported that pretreatment could bring about significant enhancements to the biosorption of synthetic dyes and heavy metal ions. Pretreatment without deteriorating the viability of the cultures could be one of the ways that combine both biosorption and possible biodegradation toward the pollutants.

532611.label: Project Objectives
532611.value: To develop a dynamic finite element model of foot and footwear which can simulate the foot and footwear interaction under impact loading. The model will take into consideration all dynamic issues and it may become an assessment and design platform for footwear; To conduct materials tests to obtain the viscoelastic and nonlinear elastic properties of foot tissues and cushioning materials. This will provide information for the FE model input; To conduct motion and impact experiments to understand the kinematics and kinetics during impact with different footwear for several landing situations for both FE boundary conditions and FE model validation; and To do parametric study for understanding the foot biomechanics and sole cushioning effects.

532611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
532611.value: Footwear should be able to provide a comfortable environment for foot, to protect foot from injury and to enable foot to function as support and to facilitate locomotion in varied surface conditions. Different design philosophies may have different functional aspects for different groups of people. No matter what design philosophy, it is useful to have a platform which can provide biomechanical information on how the footwear changes the load distribution within the foot structures and at the foot-shoe interface during locomotion and sport activities. Such information can help for evaluation and optimal design of the footwear. Because of the complexity of the foot and shoe structures and limited measurement techniques, consistent results regarding the biomechanical performance of foot and footwear cannot be achieved efficiently and effectively by experiments alone. Computer simulations based on finite element analysis have been identified as a potential tool for providing biomechanical information on foot and footwear system, especially on internal foot structures. The currently existed finite element models for foot and footwear are based on static or quasi-static analyses. These models cannot provide accurate information for the dynamic impact loading condition of the landing foot during walking, running, jumping or other sport activities. This impact loading is believed to be the most severe condition and one of the main causes of acute foot injuries. There are strong demands on the improvements of the existing finite element models which are capable to simulate this severe situation and provide biomechanical rationale to protect the foot from sports injuries. This project aims to develop a computational platform based on dynamic finite element analysis, using our previously developed geometrically detailed foot models with footwear. The finite element analyses will take into consideration all dynamic effects including viscoelastic material properties, inertia effect and impact boundary and loading conditions. These analyses can provide a clear picture of the profile of stress/strain responses within foot structures and between foot and footwear. It is very useful for evaluating and optimizing footwear designs. A series of experiments will be conducted in our motion analysis laboratory to obtain the information for the finite element model input and for the model validation. The models will be further used to perform parametric analyses for understanding the foot dynamics and provide information for footwear designs for industries and foot problem treatments in clinical applications. 鞋应能为足部提供一个舒适的环境，保护足部不受伤害，并在各种不同的路况充分发挥脚的支持和运动功能。不同的设计理念，可能针对不同人群设计出具有不同功能的鞋。不管是什么样的设计理念，拥有一个可以提供足部和鞋的相关生物力学信息的平台是非常重要的。这些信息可以帮助制鞋业进行评估和优化设计。 由于脚和鞋的结构极其复杂和生物力学测量技术极其有限，仅通过实验还不能完全了解鞋与脚的相关生物力学。基于有限元分析的计算机模拟已被确定为一种潜在的有效工具，可提供脚和鞋系统的生物力学信息，特别是足的内部结构的生物力学状况。目前存在的脚和鞋的有限元模型只是基于静态或准静态分析。这些模型不能准确模拟动态负载条件下，如行走，奔跑，跳跃或其他体育活动中脚着陆是的生物力学状态。这种冲击载荷被认为是最严重的受力情况和急性脚受伤的主要原因之一。急需将静态模型改进，建立动态模型，准确提供生物力学的信息，以减少脚的运动损伤。 该项目旨在基于我们以前开发的脚与鞋的静态模型，开发一个动态的有限元计算平台。该有限元分析将全面考虑所有的动态效应，包括材料的粘弹性性能，惯性作用和动态的边界及加载条件。这些分析可以提供清晰的足部结构和鞋之间的应力/应变的情况。这将是评价和优化鞋类设计非常有用的平台。我们也将进行一系列的运动分析实验，获得有限元模型建立的输入和模型验证信息。该模型将进一步研究脚的动态反应，并通过参数分析，为鞋类设计产业和病态足部的临床应治疗提供有用的生物力学信息。

532611.label: Realisation of objectives
532611.value: 1. A comprehensive dynamic computational foot model using dynamic-implicit finite element approach was developed for investigation of fat pad atrophy effect on foot pain. The plantar fat pad was separated from other soft tissues and assigned with different settings of material properties including hyperelastic and viscoelastic characteristics. Shock attenuation period (0%-2% gait cycle) of barefoot walking which was from initial contact to loading response was simulated. Finite element predicted peak ground reaction force about 60% of body weight within 0.015 second. Deformation and compressive strain at heel strike transient were reduced with soft sole. 2. In order to validate the finite element model, experiments were conducted to obtain the ground reaction force and the fat pad deformation during walking impact phase with different sole material supports using force platform and high speed camera. The results from the finite element model were comparable with the experimental results. Experiments were also conducted to measure the in-shoe plantar shear stress using mini tri-axial transducers which were fixed into the insoles of basketball shoe during different activities. 3. Finite element analysis of shock attenuation period using dynamic-implicit algorithm is challenging and still undergoing improvement. The simulation could further be tested and parametrically studied with different material stiffness, striking velocity, striking angle and proximal load. The muscle element could further enhance to a spring-dashpot element rather than string element. 4. The material tests were conducted to obtain the viscoelastic and nonlinear elastic properties of the cushioning materials. The test followed the ISO 20865:2002(E). 17 samples with diameters of 72.5±1 mm were tested. The results might be affected by the thicknesses and the shapes of samples, which are different among materials. The results will provide the essential input information such as the material properties and boundary conditions for finite element model. 5. Experimental study was conducted to evaluate the kinematics and kinetics during landing. Adidas Pro Model 08 (Adipro) and Nike Hyperdunk Supreme (Nikehyper) were selected for the test. Barefoot condition was the control group. The subjects landed from the platform with the heights of 0.2 and 0.4 m. The ground reaction forces, the hip, knee and ankle kinematics in sagittal, frontal, and transverse planes were obtained from five subjects. The preliminary results showed that the cushioning structures of the shoes could reduce the impact forces and the joint moments during landing. More subjects will be recruited for the further study. 6. The dynamic finite element model was used to simulate the experimental study mentioned above. The comparison between the measured and predicted can be as a type of validation. The model was provide more information commentary to experimental data. Parametric study was also conducted to find more information for the dynamic situation of foot and foot supports.

532611.label: Major findings and research outcome
532611.value: Motional analysis experiments have been done to understand the kinematics and kinetics during walking, running and landing. beside the general measurements done in Human Locomotion Lab, we have developed tri-axial force transducers and mounted into the insoles of sports shoes when athletes doing cutting maneuvers. This is the first time to provide such biomechanical information. The related findings were published in top sport science and biomechanics journals, (J of Sports Sci 2013, J of Biomechanics 2014). We have developed a very comprehensive finite element model of human foot and support, with full consideration of most structures of foot, nonlinear material properties, contact/slip, and dynamic effects. We are proud to say this is the best foot model in the world. The model can be used in understanding foot biomechanics and footwear design. The findings in the effects of heel height were published in J of Biomechanics 2013. Foot and ankle impact injury is common in geriatric trauma and often leads to fracture of rearfoot, including calcaneus and talus. A study was conducted using out dynamic foot model to assess the influence of foot impact on the risk of calcaneus and talus fracture via finite element analysis. At 5.0 m/s impact velocity, the maximum von Mises stress of the trabecular calcaneus and talus were 3.21MPa and 2.41MPa respectively, which was close to bone yield stress. The findings were published in PlosOne 2016. Due to our advance in foot modeling, an invitation was to us to write an review paper "Computational Models of the Foot and Ankle for Pathomechanics and Clinical Applications", published in Annals of Biomedical Engineering.

532611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
532611.value: Computational modeling is a very useful tool for understanding normal foot biomechanics and optimal design of footwear. The platform can be combined to shoe design industry to design better foot supports. It will also be useful tool for understanding of pathomechanics of foot for these persons with foot problems, such as flat foot, high arch foot, diabetic foot, arthritis foot etc, and provides useful information for clinical treatment of these foot problems, no matter conservative or surgical approach. This will be a potential direction for our biomechanical foot modeling.

532611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
532611.value: In this project, a dynamic computational model of human foot with support was developed to understand the impact effect on foot during walking, running or landing. The computational analyses involve the dynamic effects, such as viscoelastic material properties, inertia effect and impact loading/motion conditions. The effects of insole cushion materials were also investigated. The analyses provided a clear picture of the stress/strain responses within foot structures and between foot and footwear. Experiments were also conducted to understand the motion and loading during walking, running and landing, especially impact when barefoot or wearing normal or sport shoe. The insole plantar pressure and shear stress were also measured. The validated models were used to do parametric analyses which provided lots of biomechanical information for understand foot impact during landing and the etiological background for heel pain. The findings can also be used for high quality footwear design for industries and foot problems treatments for clinical applications

532711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
532711.value: 随着现代社会水平的快速提高，對清潔淡水的需求也逐年增高。而另一方面，污染和氣候變化導致天然淡水的供應每況愈下。因此，水淨化技術的重要性日趨凸顯。廢水的回收再用，雖然可以大幅提高淡水的來源，但是目前還受限於一些技術難題。特別是廢水裡面溶解的許多有害化學物質（如染料、農藥、洗滌劑等），還不能由現行的物理、化學和生物處理方法有效清除。在香港，處理過的廢水通常會被直接排放到河流和近海，導致水源的嚴重浪費，而且對環境造成潛在的危害。在眾多的水净化技術中，二氧化鈦光催化技術脫穎而出，被寄予厚望。這是因為它對很多種類的化學物質都有效，能夠把它们分解或者礦化成無害的終產物（例如二氧化碳、水或者是非溶於水的礦物）。然而，要達到實際的大規模工業應用，二氧化鈦光催化還有很長的路要走。當前存在的主要的限制因素包括：（1）吞吐量太小，（2）光反應的效率偏低，（3）使用人工紫外光源，（4）需要費時的後處理步驟，（5）成本偏高。例如，在很多展示過的光催化系統中，處理能力多数小於1升每小時，離實際應用的要求（1000升每小時）相去甚遠；表觀光子效率一般小于1％，導致光能利用率較低；而且人工紫外光源要耗費大量電力，增加了成本；另外，很多反應器採用漿態的二氧化鈦（即把二氧化鈦顆粒與廢水混合），光反應後需要額外的步骤以濾除水體中的二氧化鈦細顆粒（大小通常為 1 – 100納米）。這些局限導致光催化處理效率低而成本高，难以推广到實際應用。 為突破以上限制，該項目將以微流體技術為指導，設計新型的反應器，以合理利用太陽光中的可見光和紫外線兩個波段的能量。在前期的預研中，我們曾用紫外光照射微流體光催化反應器，發現相对於通常的反應器，光反應速率常數可以提高100倍以上。這表明，微流體和光催化兩者的協同作用可帶来許多優點，如高面積體積比、高光反應效率、簡便的流量控制。此外，我們已成功合成二氧化鈦和氧化亞銅的納米異質結材料，其吸收波段可擴展到可見光部分（620 nm），而且具有較高的光化作用。 該項目將主要分為兩個任務。在任務一中，我們將開發一個小型的反應器（尺寸20厘米  10厘米），以提高吞吐量到大於1升每小時，同時，將嘗試用氧化亞銅來敏化二氧化鈦薄膜，以同時吸收利用太陽光中可見光和紫外線。這個反應器雖然只是一個實驗性的系統，但它會處理兩個關鍵問題：尺寸放大和可見光敏化。在任務二中，我們計劃建造一個桌面大小的中型反應器（尺寸2米  1米），期望處理能力可達到或超過 1000升每小時。另外，考虑到将来应用的需求，此反應器將尽量採用廉價材料，简化維護工作。本項目的成功將提供現場供水的特殊能力，可以為野外作業、急發事件現場、或者是沒有公共供水的偏遠地區家庭提供淨水。這將同時推動光催化技術在吞吐量、效率和成本等方面，向工業級應用更進一步。該項目是第一次把微流體引入光催化技術，提供一種新的反應器設計思路，因此具有相當的科學價值。它同時也提供一種增加清潔淡水供應的實用方案，對香港社會和民生也有一定的貢獻。

532711.label: Realisation of objectives
532711.value: (1) In the physical study of microfluidic photocatalysis, we have found that the microfluidic reactors could solve some major problems of photocatalysis through different mechanisms. For instance, it overcomes the mass transfer limit via large surface area to volume ratio; it can eliminate the photon transfer problem by using a planar reactor design and by directly mounting a LED panel onto the planar reactor; and it can significantly enhance the stability/lifetime of the photocatalysts by the self-refreshing effect of the running flow. (2) In the synthesis of visible-light-responsive photocatalyst, we have prepared successfully BiVO4 nanoporous films, BiVO4/TiO2 heterojunction materials and Au/TiO2 plasmonic photocatalysts. The BiVO4 film has an absorption edge at 410 nm and in experiment, it shows high photoactivity in degrading methylene blue model chemical under the blue LED panel (central wavelength 400 nm). The BiVO4/TiO2 film under the sun simulator measures an enhancement of the reaction rate constant by more than 30% as compared to the TiO3 film. The reason is verified by measuring photoluminescence (PL). It is found that the BiVO4/TiO2 film has a PL only 1/4 of that of the TiO2 film, showing a strong suppression of the electron/hole recombination by the use of the heterojunction structure. The properties of Au/TiO2 films are under study. It is noted that the originally-proposed Cu2O material is replaced by BiVO4 because we have found in experiment that BiVO4 is more stable and more photoactive than Cu2O. (3) In development of small-scale reactors, we have fabricated the reactors using BiVO4/TiO2 and Au/TiO2 photocatalyst films. And, new method of photoelectrocatalysis is being investigated to overcome the oxygen deficiency problem and to selectively control the reaction pathways, which would further enhance the overall photoactivity. (4) In the processes for large photocatalyst films, we have home-made a pressurized dispenser system, which can fabricate a single TiO2 film with the size up to 0.5 x 1 m2. The chloroform soaking procedure is employed to enhance the adhesion of TiO2 nanoparticles to the PMMA substrate. (5) Regarding the bench-scale solar-light photocatalytic reactors, we have fabricated and assembly a large-sized reactor (2 m x 1 m x 1 cm) to test the photodecomposition of organic pollutants using sunlight. The reactor works best at a process throughput of 2 L/h but can be driven at much higher throughput up to 1,000 L/h.

532711.label: Major findings and research outcome
532711.value: Major findings : (1) In physical study, we have found that microfluidic reactors can solve the major problems of traditional photocatalytic reactors and can be further used for parallel screening and rapid test of photocatalysts. (2) In the material synthesis, we have developed the fabrication procedures of visible-light-responsive photocatalyst, such as BiVO4 nanoporous films, BiVO4/TiO2 heterojunction materials and Au/TiO2 plasmonic photocatalysts. (3) In the small-scale reactors, we have fabricated various designs of microreactors and have investigated the synergistic effect of photocatalysis and electrocatalysis. (4) In large-film process, we have innovated a new process – pressurized dispensing method for a single TiO2 film with the size up to 0.5  1 m2 and have found that the chloroform soaking is able to enhance the adhesion. (5) In bench-scale solar reactor, we have integrated a scaled-up reactor (2 m x 1 m x 1 cm) to test the photodecomposition of organic pollutants using sunlight. Research outcome: - Trained 1 PhD - Published 4 journal papers, 9 conference papers - Won 2 Best Paper Awards

532711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
532711.value: (1) In the application part, the bench-scale reactor may be used to process real wastewater. (2) In the material part, heterojunction of TiO2 film and rough Au film may be developed to obtain strong and broadband absorption to sunlight. (3) In the physical part, detailed mechanisms such as the charge transfer, the energy transfer and the functional ion groups on the photocatalyst surface may be worth further investigation.

532711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
532711.value: Water purification is of increasingly importance due to the rising demand of clean water for high quality of life. Reclamation of wastewater could significantly increase the water resource but is now still limited by technical challenges. This project aims to overcome the existing problems by designing new reactors guided by microfluidics principles and by utilizing both visible light and UV-A of solar light. Experiment experimental results have shown that the microfluidic reactor possesses many merits such as high surface-area-to-volume ratio, high photoreaction efficiency and easy flow control. In addition, we have successfully synthesized TiO2/Cu2O heterojunction nanomaterials, which absorb the visible light up to 620 nm and exhibit high photoreactivity. Scaling up the microreactors to large-size reactors (2 m x 1 m x 2 cm) have been accomplished after the technical problems for the fabrication of large films are solved. Tests of the large reactor in sunlight have shown good results. This project is believed to have general scientific significance since it is the first attempt to synergize microfluidics and photocatalysis and may offer a new approach for reactor design. It would also create beneficial social impact as it may provide a practical solution to increase the clean water supply.
