532911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
532911.value: The lasting high fuel costs and worldwide energy concerns highlight the necessity and urgency for drag reduction research. The project is a continuation of our earlier successful campaign aiming to control actively the skin-friction drag in a turbulent boundary layer over a flat plate (Bai et al. 2010a). An open-loop control of the flow has been experimentally implemented based on local wall-normal surface oscillation, generated by one row of 12 piezoelectric ceramic (PZT) actuators, achieving a maximum drag reduction of 50%. A conceptual model of the modified coherent structures has been proposed for the flow physics behind the control. Recent numerical studies (e.g. Lee et al. 1998) have established that the turbulent flow control can be significantly more effective if a closed-loop control is applied; no drag reduction has been physically demonstrated in a turbulent boundary layer under closed-loop control (Kasagi et al. 2009). This work aims to expand our open-loop control to adaptive closed-loop control. Specifically, (1) study the fluctuating wall shear stress, wall pressure, streamwise flow velocity, and their interrelationships, which will be connected to streamwise vortices and hence the drag; (2) develop a linear closed-loop control for drag reduction using the three quantities or their combinations as the feedback and feed-forward signals; (3) understand the physical mechanisms behind effective control. To this end, the three types of signals will be measured, both downstream and upstream of PZT-actuator-manipulated surface, using our recently developed carbon-nano-tube wall shear stress sensors as well as hotwires and high dynamic response miniature electret pressure transducers. Each actuator will be driven by the feed-forward and feedback signals. A non-linear controller based on an adaptive inverse neural network algorism may also be explored. Flow diagnostic techniques such as PIV, LIF flow visualization and hotwires will be used to characterize the boundary layer with and without control. The measured data will be analyzed in detail to gain insight into the flow physics and drag reduction mechanisms under control. 此项目是在已经取得重要突破（减阻达50%）的开环控制基础上进行， 将进一步研究：（１）湍流边界层中壁面脉动摩擦力、壁面脉动压力、近壁面流向脉动速度，以及它们之间的相互关系，这些物理量与近壁面流向涡和壁面摩擦阻力紧密相连；（２）以减少壁面摩擦阻力为控制目标，把上述三个物理量或者它们之间的组合作为前馈和反馈信号，提出一种有效的线性闭环控制系统并进行验证；（3）利用多种实验技术（热线、热膜、PIV，以及烟线流动显示）测量控制后的湍流边界层，并与控制前的数据进行分析比较（采用空间-时间互相关，条件采样与平均，以及本征正交分解（POD）等处理方法），以揭示流体物理及控制机理。

532911.label: Realisation of objectives
532911.value: Both Objectives 1 and 2 have been achieved. The fluctuating wall shear stress, wall pressure, streamwise flow velocity, and their interrelationships, along with their connection to quasi-streamwise vortices and the viscous friction drag, have been investigated based on particle image velocimetry and hot-wire measurements. Based on this investigation, the best feed-forward and feedback signals have been determined and the signals have been incorporated into the linear closed-loop control system, which is applied to control a turbulent boundary layer over a flat plate based on wall perturbation generated by piezo-ceramic actuators. Four schemes are investigated, with a view to suppressing the near-wall high-speed events and hence reducing skin friction drag. The open-loop, feed-forward, feedback and combined feed-forward and feedback controls achieved the local maximum drag reductions of 30%, 24%, 20% and 28%, corresponding to the duty cycles of 100%, 50%, 50% and 62%, respectively. The results suggest a good potential to cut down substantially the input energy under the closed-loop control schemes. In order to achieve Objective 3, a spanwise aligned array of piezo-ceramic actuators was employed to generate a transverse travelling wave along the wall surface, with a specified phase shift between adjacent actuators. Local skin-friction drag exhibits a strong dependence on control parameters, including the wavelength, amplitude and frequency of the oscillation. A maximum drag reduction of 50% has been achieved at 17 wall units downstream of the actuators. The near-wall flow structure under control, measured using smoke-wire flow visualization, hotwire and PIV techniques, is compared with that without control. The data has been carefully analyzed using techniques such as streak detection, power spectra, and conditional averaging based on the VITA detection. All the results point to a pronounced change in the organization of the perturbed boundary layer. It is proposed that the actuation-induced wave generates a layer of highly regularized streamwise vortices, which acts as a barrier between the large-scale coherent structures and the wall, thus interfering with the turbulence production cycle and contributing partially to the drag reduction. Associated with the generation of regularized vortices is a significant increase, in the near-wall region, of the mean energy dissipation rate, as inferred from a substantial decrease in the Taylor microscale. This increase also contributes to the drag reduction. The scaling of the drag reduction is also examined empirically, providing valuable insight into the active control of drag reduction. The above-mentioned work and achievement of the three objectives are reflected in three papers published in or submitted to archival journals and two book articles and one conference paper. Please refer to publication list produced out of this project.

532911.label: Major findings and research outcome
532911.value: Major findings are two parts: (1) Active control schemes, including the feed-forward, feedback and combined feed-forward and feedback schemes along with the open-loop control, have been successfully developed based on spanwise-aligned PZT actuators in a fully developed turbulent boundary layer with a view to suppressing the near-wall high-speed events and hence reducing skin friction drag. The maximum drag reduction achieved by the closed-loop schemes are close to that of the open-loop. However, the duty cycle is only about 50%, suggesting a substantial drop in the input energy. (2) Drag reduction mechanisms have been proposed. First, the transverse travelling wave formed by the wall-based discrete actuators generates a layer of highly regularized streamwise vortices, which acts to weaken or even completely sever the connection between the large-scale coherent structures and the wall, thus interfering with the turbulence production cycle and resulting in significant drag reduction. Second, all experimental data point to a significantly increased energy dissipation rate, in the near-wall region, which also contributes to the significant drag reduction.

532911.value: The work continues so that the drag reduction can be extended from the ‘local’ to entire plate.

533011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
533011.value: 確保土木工程結構的功能性與安全性，已成為現代社會的一個關鍵議題。在此背景下，結構振動控制和健康監測正逐漸成為災害防治和性能評估的重要技術手段。結構控制通常指通過某些方法減小由車輛、風、海浪或地震等引起的結構振動，從而避免主體結構由於過於劇烈的振動而引起的結構功能性或安全性的問題。一個被成功應用的方案是安裝各種能量耗散的裝置來減小結構的動能。而與此同時，能量的供給成為結構健康監測系統中一個普遍關注的問題，尤其是對於新興的無線傳感器或無線傳感網絡。目前有限的電池壽命極大的制約了無線傳感器在實際工程中的應用。許多學者正致力於尋找其他可靠的替代能源，來解決無線傳感器的這個瓶頸問題。 儘管阻尼系統和傳感器系統在能量上有著非常顯著的互補特性，把兩個系統進行結合從而解決能量問題的研究在土木工程領域却非常罕見，雖然很多新建的重大結構都同時安裝了結構控制系統和健康監測系統。有鑑於此，本項目提出開發一種新型的阻尼器-傳感器的整合系統，它利用一種新型的電磁阻尼器同時作為減振單元和能量收集單元，因此低能耗的無線傳感器可以直接由電磁阻尼器來驅動。申請人在過往的研究中對電磁阻尼器的力學和電學特性進行了初步的實驗研究和理論模擬，結果表明當電磁阻尼器的輸出能量可以被能量收集電路有效的保存時，它就可以形成獨特的雙功能的單元。 儘管初步的研究已經顯示了這一應用的良好前景，仍有很多實際問題需要解決，包括整個系統的完整實現。本課題的目的，就是要彌補目前研究與最終應用之間仍存在的差距，具體方案是通過一個斜拉索的振動研究，來實現一個自供能的振動控制與振動監測系統。這個新型系統的振動控制、能量收集的性能，將在這個項目中進行深入的研究。同時，會提出一個相應的雙目標的設計方法，來促進其在實際工程中的應用。

533011.label: Realisation of objectives
533011.value: This project investigated a novel application of electromagnetic dampers for structural vibration control and energy harvesting simultaneously. The proposed seven objectives have been fully achieved during the 3.5-year project period. The significant achievements of this completed project include: 1. A novel electromagnetic damper cum energy harvester (EMDEH) system, consisting of an electromagnetic device (EMD) connected to an energy harvesting circuit (EHC), was developed. When subjected to external excitation, EMD can convert kinetic energy into electrical energy; EHC can properly store the electrical energy in a rechargeable battery. Meanwhile, a reaction force in turn is imposed on the structure to suppress relative motion. [Objective 4] 2. Two small-scale linear EMDs connected to different representative EHCs were experimentally characterized and numerically modeled. EMDEH devices were dynamically tested on an MTS machine in different testing conditions. In particular, a fixed-duty-cycle buck-boost converter was studied and utilized as a promising EHC that can maintain a stable equivalent resistance in discrete current mode (DCM). The theoretical and numerical models of EMDEH devices were developed based on experimental results. [Objective 4] 3. A coupled dynamic model including stay cable, EMD, and EHC was built and analyzed using the MATLAB Simulink toolbox, in which the state-space models of full-scale stay cables were established using a finite difference method, the numerical model of EMDEH was based on experimental results, and the dynamic wind load on stay cables was simulated using the cross power spectral density (XPSD) matrix-based proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) method. [Objective 2] 4. The vibration control and energy harvesting performance of EMDEH devices were assessed through a series of numerical simulations of a full-scale bridge stay cable equipped with EMDEH device under actual wind excitation. The influence of equivalent load resistance on vibration control and energy harvesting performance was particularly highlighted. [Objective 3] 5. An optimal design method was developed for EMDEH installed on a stay cable. The fixed-duty-cycle buck-boost converter was employed as a performance optimization EHC to optimize both energy harvesting and vibration control performance. The optimal load resistance of EHC to achieve the maximum output power and cable damping was rationally determined in the design method. [Objective 5] 6. A 5.8-m long scaled stay cable with a EMDEH device was tested in laboratory under sine sweep and random excitations. The output power of EMDEH was evaluated in different testing scenarios and compared with power consumption of WSS. The vibration suppression was assessed in time and frequency domain. In particular, the effectiveness of the proposed optimal design method for EMDEH device was validated in the tests. [Objective 6] 7. A shake table test of a single-story steel frame with a regenerative tuned mass damper (TMD) and a WSS was conducted, where the regenerative TMD consists of a pendulum-type TMD, a rotary EMD and an EHC. When subjected random ground motions, the regenerative TMD could effectively reduce the frame vibration and successfully power the WSS that monitored the frame vibration simultaneously. Therefore, the regenerative TMD and WSS formed an efficient self-powered vibration control and monitoring system and validated the feasibility of using EMD for structural vibration control and power supply to WSS. [Objective 1] 8. The performance of EMDEH was evaluated in the simulations of two full-scale examples, namely, a 306-m long stay cable and a 76-story benchmark building. The vibration control performance was evaluated at different wind speeds. It is generally comparable to those of the optimally designed conventional dampers. But the potential performance degradation at high wind speed was also pointed out. The variation of energy harvesting efficiency was discussed. The feasibility of applying EMD-EHC-WSS system in full-scale civil structures was demonstrated by comparing the output power with typical power consumption of WSS. The output power obtained in this project was considerably higher than those of micro-scale energy harvesters reported in literature. [Objectives 1 & 7]

533011.label: Major findings and research outcome
533011.value: This project successfully developed a dual-function EMDEH device that serves both vibration control and energy harvesting functions. The modeling, testing, analysis, optimization, and implementation of the EMDEH device were systematically conducted in this project. Two application examples, a regenerative TMD for high-rise buildings and an EMDEH device for bridge stay cables, were investigated in terms of both vibration control and energy harvesting performance. The major findings and outcome of this project include: 1. Mathematical models of the dual-function EMDEH device connected with various types of circuits were established based on dynamic testing results. The optimal equivalent resistance of EHC to achieve the maximum harvesting efficiency was derived considering the parasitic damping effect. The theoretical upper limit of the harvesting efficiency was found to be constrained by the machine constant, parasitic damping, and the internal coil resistance. [Research Output: Journal Paper 1] 2. The dynamic test of a scaled stay cable-EMDEH system illustrated the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed EMDEH device for both cable vibration mitigation and energy harvesting. The results demonstrated that the EMDEH device with a performance optimization circuit exhibited comparable vibration control performance as the optimal passive viscous damper, and meanwhile efficient energy harvesting was also obtained. [Research Output: Journal Paper 5] 3. The numerical simulation of a wind-excited, full-scale, cable-EMDEH system indicated that the proposed EMDEH device can work optimally within a specific wind speed range. A prediction is that output power ranging from 82.5mW to 2.40 W, which is generally sufficient to power a wireless sensor, can be harvested at the optimal wind speed range (9m/s to 15m/s) under along-wind excitation. [Research Output: Journal Paper 4] 4. The shake table test of an SDOF model installed with a pendulum-type TMD demonstrated the feasibility of the regenerative TMD for both vibration mitigation and energy harvesting. An Imote2 smart wireless sensing node was successfully powered by the output of the regenerative TMD. [Research Output: Journal Paper 2] 5. A numerical simulation of a 76-story benchmark building with a regenerative TMD was performed. The effectiveness of the proposed simple design method employing a performance optimization circuit was validated. The vibration control performance of the regenerative TMD is comparable to that of the optimal passive TMD. The results show the promise of a self-powered vibration control and monitoring system based on the proposed EMDEH devices and wireless sensing techniques. [Research Output: Journal Paper 6]

533011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
533011.value: Further development of this research will be conducted in the following aspects: 1. The scalability of EMDEH devices shall be discussed and improved in order to enable their applications in large-scale civil structures. 2. The energy efficiency and optimal operation range of the EHC shall be further improved to maximize the output power from EMDEH devices. 3. It is promising to develop a self-powered semi-active control system using EMD because the damping force of the EMD can be easily controlled by changing external resistances.

533011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
533011.value: Structural control is a traditional research area aiming to protect primary structures against excessive vibrations induced by traffic, wind, waves and earthquakes; whereas energy harvesting is an emerging technique that extracts green energy from ambient environment to power electronics. Energy harvesting can provide sustainable power to wireless smart sensors (WSS), thus enabling long-term wireless monitoring. This project investigated a novel integration of structural control, energy harvesting and wireless sensing techniques. A self-powered vibration control and monitoring system, which consists of an electromagnetic damper (EMD), an energy harvesting circuit (EHC) and WSS, was successfully developed to fulfil vibration-damping, energy-harvesting, and wireless-sensing functions simultaneously. When subjected to external excitation, the kinetic energy of a structure is converted into electrical energy through the EMD. The electrical energy is then stored in a rechargeable battery, while a reaction force in turn is imposed on the structure to suppress relative motion. The stored energy in the rechargeable battery can be utilized to power a wireless sensor or other low-power devices. A systematical investigation, including the proof of concept, system development, theoretical and numerical study, experimental validation, and feasibility assessment, has been conducted for the developed self-powered vibration control and monitoring system within this project.

540211.value: 1958年中國高校的「拔白旗」風暴 （提要） 在1957年的「反右」運動中，超過50萬知識分子被打成了「右派分子」。到了1958年初，「反右」運動的倖存者一律被定性為「資產階級知識分子」，被逼在全國各地舉辦的無數「向黨交心」的集會中，「自願地」坦白交代自己「有毒的資產階級思想」及林林總總的「反動言行」。但毛澤東對知識分子的猜忌，並沒有因此而稍稍緩和。1958年5月初，毛在中共八届二全會上發表了一系列攻擊知識分子的講話。毛斷言：中國高校的教授大都思想上屬於資產階級，而且在政治上又和黨不是一條心；大都不僅不學無術浪得虛名，而且在學問上甚至還不如自己的學生；幾乎所有高校所插的旗幟，都不是「無產階級的紅旗」，而是「資產階級的白旗」。正因如此，毛警告中共的高幹：對教授們決不允許像以往那樣心慈手軟，而黨的任務，端在發動高校學生批判鬥爭自己的老師，拔掉所有的「白旗」，把紅旗插遍全國每一所高等院校！ 在毛一聲令下，由1958年5月中至12月底，波濤洶湧的「拔白旗」風暴橫掃大陸每一所高校。幾乎每一個高級講師、副教授和教授都被戴上「白旗學者」的帽子，以「思想反動」和「不學無術」的罪名，慘遭自己學生的猛烈批鬥。「拔白旗」風暴不僅在高校教師的心靈，留下了永難癒合的創傷，它還根本顛覆了傳統的師生倫理，毁壞了幾乎所有的學術規範，以及癱瘓了整個高等教育機構。 儘管「拔白旗」風暴造成了如此嚴重的破壞，但時下學界對此一課題的關注卻明顯地有所不足。至今仍沒有任何一本專書或論文特別為此撰寫，就是最好的證明。本研究計畫的目的，就是要填補此一中華人民共和國史上的明顯欠缺。本計畫將從中國東、南、西、北、中五個方位，刻意選取南大、中大、川大、北大和武大這五所重點大學，作為分析個案。五校的校刊、學報、檔案，以及相關的大字報、回憶錄、日記、書信、文章與書刊都將被予以系統性地蒐集、整理和剖析。五校黨委在「拔白旗」風暴中工作作風的同與異，以及五校教員在風暴中的屈辱辛酸、精神上的創傷、沉默的抗拒、彼此間的猜嫌、叛賣和內閧，還有五校學生在批鬥自己老師時的困惑不解、顧慮重重和天人交戰，也將同樣予以系統性的分析與檢驗。此外，本計畫還將從系統性地操控「心理工程」的視角，追蹤與考察毛澤東反智主義的淵源、形成和發展的歷史。1966年中爆發的震驚世界的「無產階級文化大革命」，以某種程度來說，也可被視為毛所發動的「拔白旗」風暴的續篇。如果把「拔白旗」風暴，看成是由毛主導的「心理工程」或思想改造運動的一個重要環節，本計畫將一如既往，繼續發掘其中某些極重要的但卻被長期湮沒的面相，並將在中共與知識分子相持相爭的脈絡中，把這些面相重新加以定位。

540211.label: Realisation of objectives
540211.value: Using Peking University, Zhongshan University, Nanjing University, Sichuan University and Wuhan University as samples for study and analyses, this project aims at arriving at an understanding of the overall picture of the Campaign of Wiping Out the “White Banners of Capitalism” of 1958. It focuses not only the commonalities between the campaigns at these locations, but their individual uniqueness. In addition to searching the archives and a large volume of publications of 1985 in these five institutions, the study uses the other thought reform movements that the Chinese Communist instigated in these five locations as the setting, and the thoughts, the action and the words of the professors of these institutions and the tragic events that descended upon them in all these thought reform campaigns as reference. Such wealth of materials are found in memoirs, autobiographies, biographical commentaries, selected papers, and various kinds of collections of writings in China as well as in a wide range of newspapers and journals overseas. Not only are they voluminous in quantity, the time they cover is wide-ranging. They are also scattered in such a random and fragmented fashion that they are difficult to locate. Precisely for these reasons, with the help of a research assistant, I spent three entire years collecting them, sorting them out, putting them into categories and making sense of them. Because some of the materials were obtainable only in person in China, and because interviews with the subjects of “thought reform” could make up for what is lacking in written materials, in the first three years of this project, I spent more than two months each year traveling to universities, libraries and archives in Guangzhou, Sichuan, Wuhan, Nanjing and Beijing. Archives on the victims of political campaigns throughout the ages are watched carefully, especially after Xi Jiping’s ascension to power. Most of the materials to be consulted for this project came to be tagged as “extremely sensitive” and were barred from the eyes of overseas scholars. Accordingly, I changed my strategy and resorted to field study instead of archival research, and devoted a longer time than planned to conduct a large number of extensive conversations with many students (perpetrators of violence) and teachers and their family members (victims) of the Wiping Out the White Banners Campaign. Altogether, I interviewed 96 subjects, 38 of whom for three or more times. The inevitable result is that I exceeded the projected time, which is also the main reason for my request to extend my three-year project to four years. The Wiping out the White Banners Campaign was an important facet of the Communist Thought Reform Movement, which subsumed under it complicated and intricate historical and social phenomena. In order to explore from various angles the internal relationship between the social status of Mainland intellectuals and the transformation of their thinking, this project adopts an interdisciplinary method in its research: using, in order words, historical theories in the main, and supporting them with theories of such fields as literature, philosophy, political science and sociology. This allows the research to be conducted a multi-layered and multi-dimensional manner from a multiplicity of perspectives. In order to engage in exchange of views with specialists in relevant fields, I participated in six international conferences giving six presentations. After the conferences, I proceeded to revise the presentations into seven papers that are highly relevant to this project. With the exception of "The Wiping Out of the White Banners of Captialism in Zhongshan University of Guangzhou in 1958,” which is yet to be published in an academic journal, and "In the Storm of the Wiping out the White Banners of Capitalism Campaign of Peking University," which has gone through peer review and will appear in New Asia Academic Journal, no. 34 (August 2017), the other five have already been published in first-rate academic journals. The seven papers mentioned above, now revised, constitute parts of the book The Wiping Out of the White Banners of Capitalism Campaign in Mainland's Instiutions of Higher Learning in 1958. The book consists of 7 chapters, and 350,000 Chinese words in length, and has already been submitted to the publishing branch of the Academia Sinica of Taiwan. External review is in process. Barring unforeseeable circumstances, the book will be in print before December 2017.

540211.label: Major findings and research outcome
540211.value: 1. Why did the majority of university teachers become so docile in the Wiping out of the White Banners of Capitalism Campaign? The Chinese Communists were able to exercise a relentless control over the thinking of university teachers and to reform them by relying on measures of red terror and the monopoly they hold over all production and living means of all people. More importantly, they also possess complete arbitration power over questions of morality. By means all these three “magic tricks,” which they employed in rotation, the Chinese Communists were able to exercise total control over Chinese society, people, and intellectuals, especially the university professors. Total control, moreover, is a sufficient condition of an authoritarian society. 2. That the Chinese Communists were able to monopolize moral arbitration is closely related to their self-proclaimed role as the only hope and redeemer in the salvation of contemporary China. We know that most university professors in China are nationalists. Salvation and survival are their religion, their God and their ultimate concern. The self-promotion on the part of the Chinese Communists in the cause of national survival and their manipulation of nationalistic sentiments undoubtedly exert a fatal attraction to the university teachers in China. The past ten years or so saw the blossoming of different schools of the study of Western nationalism – primordialism(史前派), modernism(現代派), ethno-symbolism(種符派) ---, all vying for attention. If the thinking of such scholars as Clifford Geertz, Ernest Gellner, Benedict Anderson, Eric Hobsbawm, John Armstrong and Anthony Smith could be brought together with the study of Chinese nationalism for mutual illumination, our understanding will deepen of the interweaving complexes that plagued university professors such as Feng Youlan, Zhu Guangqian, He Lin and Liu Dajie who exhibited a mixture of acting under coercion and willing participation, resistance and cooperation, vacillations and decisivenss, feelings of bitterness and the perverse pleasure of self-flagellation that they derived during the Wiping out the White Banners of Capitalism Campaign.

540211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
540211.value: On the basis of the present project, I plan to push my study backward to the thought reform movement and the campaigns against Wu Xun, Hu Feng, Hu Shi and Liang Shuming, the Let Hundred Flowers Bloom and Hundred School Contend Movement, and Anti-Rightist Campaign of the 1950s, and forward to the Four Cleanups, Anti-Revisionist Campaign and the Cultural Revolution of the 1960s in compiling a complete history of the thought reform of the intellectuals in the hands of the Chinese Communists.

540211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
540211.value: In 1958, Mao Zedong stated categorically that the institutions of higher education in China was under the rule of “bourgeois scholars,” and that the banners they flew were not the red banners of Marxism-Lennisims, but the white banners of the capitalists. For this reason, he launched the Wiping Out the White Banners of Capitalism Campaign where university teachers came under the attack and struggle sessions in the hands of students, sparing almost none of teachers above the rank of lecturers in all institutions of higher educations in China. My project takes as samples for analysis and study Peking University, Zhongshan University, Nanjing University, Sichuan University and Wuhan University to trace the unfolding of this Campaign, and uncover the deeper historical, social, institutional and personality issues hidden therein. This project will illuminate and serve as references to the study of these areas: 1. the history of the Chinese Communist Party and the People's Republic of China; 2. Mao Zedong and his thoughts; 3. the Cultural Revolution; 4. Communist China and its intellectuals and 5. the history of the academia, culture and thoughts in China of the modern period of recent past.

540511.label: Project Title(Chinese)
540511.value: 買賣雙方之協調策略用於高效率及環保供應鏈之設計。

540511.label: Co - Investigator(s)
540511.value: Prof Campbell, James F. Prof Langervin, Andre

540511.label: Project Objectives
540511.value: Firstly, we will investigate how a cost-minimizing vendor-buyer coordination policy affects the environmental performance of the supply chain when compared with a non-coordinated policy where the vendor and the buyer independently minimize their individual costs. We will consider the following three environmental performance measures: raw material waste, energy waste, and air pollution. Secondly, we will investigate the trade-offs between the economic and the environmental performance measures. The impact of one measure could have a strong effect on the other; for example, minimizing air pollution may increase system costs and vice versa. Finally, we will expand the basic vendor-buyer coordination model to consider a more detailed transportation carrier component, so we can explore the complex relationship between air pollution and the number of deliveries, quantity delivered and distance travelled.

We will consider the following three environmental performance measures: raw material waste, energy waste, and air pollution.

Secondly, we will investigate the trade-offs between the economic and the environmental performance measures. The impact of one measure could have a strong effect on the other; for example, minimizing air pollution may increase system costs and vice versa.

Finally, we will expand the basic vendor-buyer coordination model to consider a more detailed transportation carrier component, so we can explore the complex relationship between air pollution and the number of deliveries, quantity delivered and distance travelled.

540511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
540511.value: Can vendors and buyers coordinate for the benefit of the environment? A general result from analyses of coordinated vendor-buyer models is that coordination can produce a significant reduction in the total system cost, when compared with independent (non-coordinated) optimization of vendor and buyer behavior. Existing optimization models for single vendor multi-buyer coordination generally consider only traditional logistics/supply chain costs (ordering costs and inventory holding costs of the buyers and production set-up costs, inventory holding costs, and order processing and shipment costs of the vendor) and seek solutions that minimize total system cost. There is little work addressing environmental issues as an objective of vendor-buyer co-ordination. This research proposes to develop vendor-buyer coordination models that incorporate three new environmental performance measures (along with cost), and also incorporate reverse logistics via recycling. Because these new models include economic and environmental performance measures, multi-objective meta-heuristic methods will be developed to find high quality solutions. By exploring the tradeoffs between the performance measures, the results will evaluate the impact of vendor-buyer coordination strategies on the economic and environmental performance of supply chains and will lead to insights regarding the design of efficient and sustainable supply chains.

540711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
540711.value: Over the last two to three decades, many rapidly modernizing cities around the world are unwittingly demolishing their heritage resources under the demand of urban (re)development. Urban renewal is increasingly employed as a strategy to combat urban decay and to improve the living conditions of citizens and the quality of the urban environment. As part the urban renewal process, heritage conservation can contribute to urban redevelopment with the unique quality to create and sustain among citizens a strong sense of belonging and attachment to the city. However, the importance of heritage conservation is often overlooked and as a result, social issues, among other things arise as the prominent problems in urban renewal. This study focuses on the relatively neglected social component under the concept of sustainable development in a densely developed city. It aims to enhance better integration between built heritage conservation and urban renewal to promote the social well-being in society. The study outcomes include ascertaining the corresponding indicators which reflect socially sustainable conservation of built heritage in urban renewal. As a result, this study will establish an evaluation framework to help assessing the social sustainability of a built heritage conservation project in urban renewal. The study will appraise and short-list the major social sustainability considerations for built heritage conservation from literature. Opinions will be sought through semi-structured interviews with stakeholders including, local planning and conservation professionals, citizens, NGO, private developers and property owners. The data of this research will come from Hong Kong as a representative case of densely developed city that resembles many other rapid developing urban environments in the world. From analysis of the collected data, the key criteria for enhancing social sustainability of the built heritage to be conserved in urban renewal projects will be identified and prioritized with the aid of the Analytical Network Process (ANP) computer software. Qualitative and quantitative indicators for each of the social sustainability criterion will then be developed. The evaluation framework and the corresponding indicators for assessing social issues in the conservation of built heritage for urban renewal will provide important references from which many other cities will benefit. 研究摘要 在過去二三十年中，世界上許多現代化城市在快速的發展過程中，傳統的文物資源在逐漸消失。市區重建逐漸成為改變市區老化和改善人民生活條件與城市環境的策略目標。在市區重建過程中，傳統文物保育可以保留城市的獨特品質以及維持市民對城市的歸屬感和依戀感。然而，保護傳統文物的重要性往往被忽視，這一問題成為了市區重建中突出的社會問題。 本研究基於可持續發展理論對高密度的發達城市中這一社會問題進行研究。研究目的是爲了在市區重建時能夠更好的保育歷史建築促進社會和諧。研究成果主要是建立文物建築保育的社會可持續性指標。本研究最終將建立一個文物建築保育項目的社會可持續性評價體系。 本研究首先通過文獻綜述確定關於傳統建築文化保育的社會可持續發展條件。然後，通過半結構化訪談收集持份者的意見，持份者主要有地方規劃和保育的專業人士、公民、非政府組織、開發商等。本研究以香港為案例，香港是非常具有代表性的高密度發達城市。通過網路分析法（ANP）進行資料分析，文物建築保育的社會可持續發展準則將被確定和排序。最後，確定每個標準下的定性定量指標。本研究確定的文物建築保育的社會評價體系以及相應的指標可供其他城市參考借鑒。

541311.label: Project Title(Chinese)
541311.value: 外国人和本地人在中国酒店业的薪金差距:以感觉制造的角度分析

541311.label: Co - Investigator(s)
541311.value: Dr HON, Alice H. Y. Dr Lu, Lin

541311.label: Project Objectives
541311.value: To examine the extent of compensation differences between locals and expatriates in hotel industry in mainland China. To investigate the relationships of compensation differences and various work outcomes among local employees (i.e., job satisfaction, job performance, satisfaction with expatriates, and altruistic behaviors toward expatriates). To examine whether the moderating roles of cognitive and affective trust initiated by expatriates can mitigate the negative effect of compensation gap on the part of locals. To provide realistic and practical suggestions for hotel managers how to reduce the negative effects of compensation gap and enhance local employees’ work performance through building cognitive and affective trust. To suggest future research and strategic management practices for international hotels in developing countries.

541311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
541311.value: 随着酒店业的全球化和對外建立跨国公司的趋势,许多酒店业的跨国公司利用发展中国家低廉的劳动力成本和市场潜力所提供的优势纷纷在发展中国家设立业务，为了确保海外业务的效率，外籍人士通常担當重要岗位如酒店经理. 因此, 管理层面临的挑战往往是外籍人的薪金建立在他们国家劳动市场水平（如美国), 而本地人（如中国）則支取本地工资, 从而导致两者之间的的薪金差距. 本地员工认为薪金差距确实是一个不公平的現象, 然而，外籍人士的薪金必须與他们国家劳动市场看待, 所以, 跨国公司难以把两者薪金差距缩小. 因此，酒店经理首要工作是建立薪金以外的正面因素，從而把不公平現象和负面影响减到最少. 具体来说，本研究以感觉制造的角度分析并探讨外籍经理如能够在本地员工面前建立认知信任和情感信任的話, 就可以减少从薪金差距引致本地员工连锁负面效应, 最终并改善外籍人和本地人的工作关系和质量.

541311.label: Realisation of objectives
541311.value: Interview techniques via physical visit and telephone conversation were used to probe the extent of compensation difference in China hotels (Objective 1). Due to the dynamic change of social and economic forces in the past decades, there are remarkable changes in the terms of expatriates’ compensation, study thus classified the studying intervals into three-plus-one periods (i.e. analytical windows) including the 1985-1994, 1995-2004, and 2005-2014. The number of interviewees is up to thirty hotel executives who have entered or involved in mainland China’s hotel businesses in the 1980s or early 1990s. Their entry years to China’s hotel sector offer an objective background for them to recall the extent of compensation differences. The investigation also study adapted staff salary and benefit framework being published in the hotel accounting handbook to assist the identification of overseas expatriates’ package in the interviews. Basically, Objective 1 is completed in 100%. For objectives 2 and 3 regarding the study of relationship between compensation differences and work outcomes among local employees plus mediators of work deviances, investigators visited the participating hospitality firms in Shanghai, Beijing and Guangdong and met with over 80 the Human Resource Managers (HR) and senior executives who worked closely with expatriates. The HR managers were requested to identify expatriate colleagues in various departments. With the help of these HR managers, questionnaires were distributed to 50 expatriate managers in 31 companies, holding positions ranging from team supervisor to middle-level manager. Eventually, 46 expatriates completed their surveys, yielding a response rate of 92%. With the help of HR managers, the expatriates distributed surveys to all of the local subordinates in their teams, who were allowed to decide on their participation. In this manner, surveys were distributed to 350 locals. Since the moderating effect of trust on workplace behavior has recently been addressed in publication, the study include two more moderating cultural and power variables into questionnaire for investigation. For objectives 4 and 5 (practical suggestions, future research and strategy), the study harnessed interviews with experienced hotel executives to solicit their views on some existing practical tools to reduce the effects of compensation gap and increase local employees' work performance. In addition, the study also works out some suggestions to reduce the negative effect of compensation gap and to direct the future research based on the analytical results of the findings.

541311.label: Major findings and research outcome
541311.value: The study reveals that the intensity of differences in compensation package between locals and expatriates in the hotel sector has been narrowed over the past few decades mainly due to the reversal of the direction of foreign exchange rate between USD and RMB and raise in local compensation (Chan et al, 2015). Thus, local staff’s perceived injustice over hotel workplace with regard to expatriate managers in hotels has been weakening (Chan et al., 2015). This results in a less strong correlation between the compensation differences and work outcomes – job performance, job satisfaction and altruistic behavior towards expatriates. This is contrary to general expectation about effect of compensational differences on developing countries. The result further lead to a rethinking of the applicability of traditional theories, being originated from developed nations and even tested in developing areas, in emerging countries. However, the moderating roles of cognitive and affective trust initiated by the expatriates did alleviate the workplace deviance derived from the effect of compensation gap on part of the locals, especially the latter. This result confirms with previous findings (Colquitt and Greenberg, 2003; Hon and Lu, 2010). The survey further indicates that the perceived compensation gap is positively related to the organizational and interpersonal deviance of local staff (Hon et al., 2015). The result supports the social exchange theory. Analysis on the moderating effect of power distance orientation and traditionality in culture suggests a boundary for the application of justice theory and social exchange theory in the Eastern nation as represented by China (Hon et al., 2015). High traditionality may mitigate the effect of compensation gap on deviance. However, contrary to our expectation, high power distance exacerbates such effect. The managers have customarily attributed compensation gap to varied economic development stages of the country. However, this study indicates that the reasonableness and acceptance of the perceived gap positively predict workplace deviance. The result practically reminds that managers should thoroughly consider equity principle in designing the compensation system, particularly the use of knowledge about power distance and traditionality to facilitate design, communication and implementation of expatriate policy. To practically reduce compensation gap, some hotel groups have been paying more attention on hiring expatriates from nations where the salary is relatively lower than developed areas (Chan et al., 2015). It is also suggested that the pace of the localization programs can be quicken by providing more exposure and overseas exchange activities to local staff.

541311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
541311.value: The study examined the relationships in China hotels to address the practical problem of workplace deviance in this industry. This kind of work is worth duplicating in other industries. Future research should compare the findings based on samples drawn from the hospitality sectors with those drawn from other fields (Hon et al, 2015). Also the investigated cultural factor may cause the problem of limited variance. Meanwhile, the traditionality construct is rooted in the Chinese culture and has not been sufficiently examined in western cultural settings. Therefore, a multi-country sample is suggested to further examine the generalizability of the findings(Hon et al.,2015). This study only investigates views at the employees at supervisory - junior level. There is a need to look at the picture using a longitudinal perspective by extending study to probe the views of the staff who experienced the largest compensational gap in earlier decades. Since most of these employees have already moved up to senior positions enjoying "local expatriate" package, it is also worthy to investigate their present views on compensational difference when compared with foreign expatriates and their resulting behavior. The proposed research may consider the use of panel data and the approach of fixed effect modeling.

541311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
541311.value: This study examines the effect of perceived compensation gap on negative work place behavior, like poor performance and less job satisfaction, in a local hospitality employee-expatriate context and tests the negative behavior with link to social exchange and equity theories. The study reveals the existence of a relationship between the perceived reasonableness of compensation gap and negative behaviors of local employees in an expatriate context. This finding echoes to the social exchange theory's highlight that unfair treatment may turn into employees' revenge behaviors. The study represents the first of its kinds in hospitality sector to ascertain that local staff's high traditional value may mitigate the effect of compensation gap on negative behavior and vise versa for staff's high level of power acceptance. These findings not only reinforce managers understanding that unfair treatment and difference in compensation among workers may results in staff's negative behavior, but also suggest some directions in designing human resources programs to reduce such impact. Also, the study identified and suggested several practices to reduce the negative workplace behavior and compensation differences. These can serve as references for senior management in formulating expatriate management policy. The study further indicated the future research directions for expatriate management theories and practices.

542411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
542411.value: Channel coordination is known to be a core subject of supply chain management. Over the past decades, much research effort has been devoted to exploring the detailed mechanisms (such as incentive alignment schemes) of achieving coordination in a two-echelon supply chain setting with manufacturer-led supply contracts. Despite generating many analytical results, there are two critical issues under-explored: (i) Developing a coordination scheme that can achieve an optimal multi-echelon (N-echelon, N > 2) supply chain under stochastic price-dependent demands with all agents being benefited (all-win coordination), and (ii) determining the best party as the channel captain who is responsible for leading the coordination mechanism in the supply chain. In view of this, I propose to study both the all-win coordination mechanisms and the issues on channel captainship in multi-echelon supply chains with price-dependent demands. I will start by constructing the analytical multi-echelon supply chain model and derive the optimal joint pricing and quantity decisions in the supply chain. I will then conduct an industrial survey and a thorough literature review to reveal the existing forms of popular and practical formats of supply chain contracts (such as revenue sharing, returns, options, rebates, and a mix of some of them). After that, I will explore whether these contracts can coordinate the supply chain under the (most downstream) retailer-led and the (most upstream) manufacturer-led settings. For each kind of contract, detailed comparisons on its abilities of achieving coordination (and the respective conditions) between the retailer-led and the manufacturer-led cases will be made. I will further study whether supply chain all-win coordination can be achieved by a third-party or an intermediate supply chain agent and analytically demonstrate the respective conditions and information requirements. Afterwards, I will generate insights on the choice of channel captainship by comparing the performances and coordination mechanisms under the retailer-led (RL), the manufacturer-led (ML), the intermediate-party-led (IPL), and the third-party-led (TPL) cases. I will also investigate whether the coordination mechanisms under different channel captainship cases would require different kinds of information (such as demand and cost-revenue parameters) and discuss the impacts brought by the probable information asymmetry among agents on the coordination mechanisms. Finally, I will extend the analysis and findings by exploring the challenging cases with a non-linear multi-echelon supply chain and a stochastic sales-effort dependent demand model. I believe that this project will contribute significantly to the supply chain coordination literature and generate many useful academic and managerial insights.

542411.label: Realisation of objectives
542411.value: We basically achieved all the objectives. To be specific, we conducted both analytical and empirical research on the topic and derived many important results. Some concise details are listed below. For the main objectives of achieving coordination in multi-echelon supply chains with price dependent demands and different considerations, we analytically developed the quantity discount based incentive alignment contracts and derived the analytical conditions under which supply chain coordination under each different channel captainship can be achieved. In the presence of price-dependent demand distribution, both the information asymmetric and symmetric cases were examined. In addition, we considered in a separate paper a multi-echelon closed loop supply chain system which includes a retailer, a manufacturer, and a third party collector. We compared the supply chain coordination scheme and performance under different channel captainship and generated important insights on this problem. Furthermore, to achieve some other objectives and drill deeper into the topic, we investigated some related problems such as (a) the coordination challenge in service supply chains with pricing decisions and reveal the importance of having the retailer (instead of the manufacturer) as the channel captain, (b) the analysis of wholesale pricing contracts in a supply chain with price dependent demand with risk consideration, (c) the analysis of buyback policy in coordinating supply chains with a downward sloping price dependent demand function, (d) the returns policy in mass customization supply chains with service cost decision, (e) an agent-based negotiation model with price and delivery date considerations, and (f) the supply chain with advance selling strategy and strategic consumer returns. These explorations helped reveal more insights on the topic and achieved other objectives. Finally, we also examined empirically some publicly available data from listed fashion companies and investigated how some factors such as supply chain configuration and integration would affect their financial performances with and without market disruptions. This further enhanced the theoretical findings reported in this study. As a remark, an authored book on fashion retail supply chain management was published. This book focused on achieving the all-win coordination in the supply chain. Furthermore, an edited book on the newsvendor problem, including many supply chain coordination papers, was compiled.

542411.label: Major findings and research outcome
542411.value: For the major findings, we derived the quantity discount based incentive alignment contracts and established analytical conditions under which the coordination in a supply chain with price-dependent demands under different channel captainship can be achieved. Both the information asymmetric and symmetric cases were examined. We found that the retailer-led case would outperform the manufacturer-led case in many aspects and discovered the insights regarding information requirements to achieve coordination in the respective supply chain systems. In addition, we considered in a separate paper a multi-echelon closed loop supply chain which includes a retailer, a manufacturer, and a third part collector. We compared the supply chain coordination scheme and performance under different channel captainship and generated important insights. One interesting finding is that: Having the collector as the party to collect the used products for remanufacturing is not the best supply chain setting. In the extended problems, we generated important insights on various related problems such as the coordination mechanism in service retail supply chains with service commitment and pricing decisions, the mean-risk analysis of wholesale pricing contracts in a supply chain with price dependent demand, the analysis of the impacts of demand uncertainty on buyback policy in coordinating supply chains with stochastic price dependent demand, the optimal service charging decision under a returns policy in fashion mass customization supply chains, an agent-based negotiation model with price and delivery date considerations, and the optimal advance selling strategy in a supply chain with strategic consumer returns. This project generated many important research outcomes. To be specific, eight refereed journal papers (with seven published and one under 2nd round review), one authored book, and one edited book were completed. Moreover, a full time MPhil student was trained.

542411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
542411.value: Owing to time limitation, this project only collected empirical data from the fashion industry in verifying some theoretical results. It will be interesting to collect more data from other industries to further verify the findings.

542411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
542411.value: Channel coordination is a critical and well-explored topic of modern supply chain management. However, relatively little is known about the impacts brought by different channel leadership to the supply chain coordination mechanism and performance. Motivated by the real world industrial practice and the research gap in the literature, this research project focuses on exploring the channel captainship issue in supply chain systems with price-dependent demands. This topic is important as it explores a timely issue and extends the relatively simple supply chain models explored in the literature to the more realistic setting. We believe that the findings and insights generated by this project not only significantly contribute to the supply chain management literature, but they also help advance the knowledge on the optimal choice of channel captainship for achieving the most efficient and effective supply chain coordination mechanism.

542611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
542611.value: Traditional Chinese Ideas on Translation Explorations of translation problems in China have a recorded history of nearly 2,000 years. However, scholarship on re-examination of these explorations from a modern perspective is far from comprehensive and systematic, partly because a large portion of the primary source materials scattered in ancient books, old journals, magazines, and newspapers are not readily available to modern scholars. The proposed project aims to investigate the evolution of traditional Chinese thinking on translation from the perspective of recent development of translation studies. The scope of investigation covers the period from the Eastern Han dynasty (2nd century A.D.) to 1949, which includes four major translation movements: translations of the Buddhist sutras, Western missionary translations of Christian texts (the Ming and Qing dynasties), translation of science and technology (the late Qing dynasty), literary translation of the Republican period. Based on analytical and critical scrutiny of existing materials, the current study seeks to re-capitulate and re-assess the achievements and failures of translation scholars, offering categorization, description, explanation, and evaluation, not in terms of “right” or “wrong”, but in terms of contribution to theorization of the translational activity. This investigation will develop from case studies into discussions of broader theoretical issues concerning bilingual and bicultural communication in general and the phenomenon of translation in particular, language and culture, ideology and translation, translation and power, readership, translator's subjectivity, etc. As the contemporary “mainstream” theories of translation are largely—and hence incompletely—built upon European experiences, a critical evaluation of translation theories in a Chinese context offers dialogue with their Western counterparts with a view to complementing and rectifying existing translation theories worldwide. A by-product of this research is An Anthology of Traditional Chinese Theories of Translation, a multi-volume collection of articles on translation. The materials used in this project, collected over ten years and totaling over 800 articles and selected passages (many unknown to contemporary scholars), make an invaluable source book for future research. The outcome of this project will be a series of journal articles, conference presentations, and a multi-volume source book. 中國傳統翻譯思想 中國有兩千年的翻譯歷史，1949年以前就出現過幾次大規模的翻譯運動，如東漢到北宋的佛經翻譯、明清時期的科技和基督教聖經翻譯、清末民初的人文社會學科翻譯和二十世紀的文學翻譯。各個時期的翻譯實踐都引發出譯者和學者對翻譯的思考，發展出一系列翻譯思想。中國翻譯思想最大的特點是和實踐緊密結合。早期佛經翻譯理論中的“文質之辨”（即意譯直譯）、基督教翻譯中的“聖號論”（即上帝之名的譯法）、明清時期科技的翻譯思想、嚴復的“信達雅說”、到後來的神似、化境理論，目的都是要指導譯者的實踐。 此計畫從現代翻譯研究的角度重新審視中國傳統翻譯思想的發展軌跡，探討各個時期關心的翻譯問題和提出的解決方案。主要內容包括： 1 將歷史上提出的翻譯問題類型化、系統化，探討具體概念的定義（傳統理論概念一般都缺乏定義），並提出解釋和評價； 2 探討社會、意識形態、政治、宗教等因素對翻譯理論家及其翻譯思想的影響； 3 探討歷史上不同的翻譯觀對翻譯實踐的影響，以及對中國語言和文化發展起到的作用。 4 建立中國傳統翻譯理論發照的主線； 5 主要課題包括：佛經翻譯中的文質（意譯、直譯）思想，基督教聖號翻譯的爭論、嚴復的信達雅和後來的直譯意譯的爭論、神似化境思想的起源、影響和錯誤、清末科技翻譯的原則以及貫穿整個翻譯歷史的“名義”問題（即後來的“譯名”）； 6 以及討論翻譯所涉及的語言文化。

The publisher has agreeded to give us more time to include the newly found materials in the anthology. I have submitted Volume I to the publisher for typesetting, and will submit the rest in the coming months. Again I need to go over the remaining 5 volumes one more time in case there might still be errors.

542611.label: Major findings and research outcome
542611.value: The project consists of two parts, namely research papers and an anthology of traditional Chinese theories of translation. I have found many new materials unknown to modern scholars. I have written 5 journal articles (4 published), one monograph in which 12 chapters came out from this project, and some paper drafts which will develop into journal articles or book chapters. All these are listed in Part C. The traditional Chinese theories of translation were reviewed and re-evaluated in terms of their contribution to world theory of translation from a modern prospective. With regard to the anthology, I collected about 800 articles published during the period from the Eastern Han dynasty to 1949. The articles are inputted and proofread three times. A publication contract was made with Commercial Press, Beijing, and the book will come out in 2016.

542811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
542811.value: The purpose of this research is to explore the preferred combination of hotel rate restrictions as perceived by Mainland Chinese leisure travelers to Hong Kong. Mainland Chinese leisure travelers are becoming a major source of customers for hotels all around the world. In addition, there is evidence in the literature that Mainland Chinese customers’ perceptions of price fairness are different from others in relation to Chinese culture being characterized as highly collectivist and oriented towards in-groups. Hotel rate restrictions refer to rules and terms that allows hotels to segment their customers into different rate categories. Examples of hotel rate restrictions are advance requirement, refundability, required time of stay, minimum length of stay, room location, cancellation penalties. Considering many types of rate fences along with their layers, hotels are faced with the challenge of designing set of rate restrictions that can keep the market segmented when they create a set of logical scenarios to offer discount to their price sensitive customers. Besides, these fences should provide clear explanations for the customers that are charged different rates simultaneously. The findings of this study is of great importance to hospitality professionals when they design hotel rate restrictions for Mainland Chinese market that are clear, logical and easy to communicate that can minimize customer confusion and dissatisfaction. Furthermore, this study intends to contribute to the existing research in the context of hotel rate fences by providing more insight into the preferences of Mainland Chinese customers. 本研究的目的是探索针对到香港休闲旅游的中国大陆游客的酒店价格限制的优化组合问题。中国大陆游客正在成为全球酒店的主要客户来源。并且，已有文献证实中国大陆游客对于价格公平的认知不同于其他拥有类似中国文化，如高度集体主义和群体为先的国家的游客。酒店价格限制是指酒店为了将客户细分为不同等级而设立的规则和条款。例如，酒店价格限制可能包括提前预约服务，退款服务，强制逗留时间，最短逗留时间，房间位置，取消订房的处罚措施等。考虑到价格限制的不同类型和层面，酒店面临的一大挑战就是如何对其进行设计，在不同情境中为价格敏感的客户提供折扣的同时，还要维持市场的细分结构。同时，这些限制因素还要为在相同时间下支付不同价格的客户提供清楚的解释。本研究的结论将对酒店业专家起到重要作用，帮助他们为中国内地游客市场设计清晰、合理的价格限制制度，同时将客户的疑虑和不满意度降至最低。另外，本研究丰富了现有的酒店价格限制研究，为了解中国内地游客的偏好提供了更加广阔的视野。

542811.label: Realisation of objectives
542811.value: All three objectives of the study were successfully achieved. The data for the study was collected from Mainland Chinese travelers to Hong Kong. Upon collecting data from Mainland Chinese travelers to Hong Kong, we also collected data from the Western travelers to Hong Kong for comparison purposes. We found that preferences of Chinese and Western travelers with regards to hotel rate restrictions mostly do not differ. This indicates towards the globalization of the guest preferences given that Chinese and Western cultures are very different from each other.

542811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
542811.value: This study is the first of its kind to understand the preferences of travelers related to hotel rate restrictions. Future research should examine the preferences of travelers for rate fences in other industries such as airlines, spas, restaurants and cruise lines. Rate restrictions are very important for those industries that use revenue management practices.

542811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
542811.value: This study showed that the most important hotel rate restrictions Western and Chinese hotel customers value are refundability, advanced requirement, changes allowed and rule type, respectively. Please note that the current study included only these four rate restrictions attached to the hotel room rates. We found that Chinese and Western respondents do not express significantly different preferences concerning room rates, advance requirement, rule type, or refundability. They differ significantly only concerning the changes allowed policy. This result indicates that revenue managers of international hotel companies can take a globalized approach in designing rate restrictions. The identification of these customer preferences provides hotel revenue managers with empirical data on the attitudes of culturally diverse consumers, and this information can enable the design of hotel pricing policies that attract consumers in the global market.

543011.label: Project Title(Chinese)
543011.value: 需求不確定性對機場決策影響的經濟分析

543011.label: Project Objectives
543011.value: To investigate the effects of demand uncertainty on airport capacity choice and pricing under alternative airport ownership forms and regulatory regimes. To study the mechanism and potential benefits of the application of real option in airport planning. In addition to the theoretical contributions mentioned above, this study also seeks to provide practical policy and regulation recommendations on capacity choice related issues to the airport industry in particular, and the overall transport sector in general.

In addition to the theoretical contributions mentioned above, this study also seeks to provide practical policy and regulation recommendations on capacity choice related issues to the airport industry in particular, and the overall transport sector in general.

543011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
543011.value: This study aims to investigate the effects of demand uncertainty on airport capacity choice under alternative airport ownership forms and regulatory regimes. In addition, it will study the mechanism and potential benefits of introducing real option in airport planning. These objectives are achieved through two research modules: (1) design an economic model of airport capacity choice where future demand is stochastic, and (2) construct a new analytical model where airports have access to real option in capacity planning. Airport delays and congestion have become a major threat to the aviation industry world wide. In general, there are two approaches to address congestion problems: One approach is to expand airports to ensure supply of capacity. However, the planning and construction of major airport infrastructure is notoriously lengthy. Such time lag introduces great challenges in airport capacity choice as long term forecast of future demand is almost always wrong. Another approach aims to improve the pricing and/or allocating mechanisms of airport capacity, thus that social welfare is maximized given the capacity limit. However, achieving short run allocative efficacy alone via dynamic pricing does not guarantee long term optimality. Although demand uncertainty has well been recognized as one of the most important challenges in airport planning and management, existing economic studies on airport capacity choice, airport pricing and regulation, airport ownership forms have routinely assumed deterministic demand functions (i.e., no uncertainty in demand). The different temporal nature of (long term) capacity choice and (short run adjustable) pricing is not explicitly recognized neither. Such treatments have also been used in guidance for practical airport planning (e.g. manuals on Airport Master Plan). These unrealistic assumptions and modeling deficiency had real costs on the industry: some airports hit capacity limits again shortly after major expansion, yet numerous airports had experienced long periods of under-utilization due to capacity oversupply. This led to huge monetary wastes, and created great challenges in the implementations of airport budget plan and price regulation. Yet, no theoretical model has been proposed with which these issues can be formally analyzed. The two research modules proposed in this study will not only be the first step to formally address demand uncertainty in theoretical framework, but are also expected to offer important insights on public policies concerning airport capacity and price regulation. In addition, they may be used as practical decision tools for airport managements in forming long term strategies.

543011.label: Realisation of objectives
543011.value: We identified three objectives in this study: 1). To investigate the effects of demand uncertainty on airport capacity choice and pricing under alternative airport ownership forms and regulatory regimes. 2). To study the mechanism and potential benefits of the application of real option in airport planning. 3) Recommendations on capacity choice related issues to the airport industry in particular, and the overall transport sector in general. All three objectives have been fully realized in this study. In particular, Objectives (1) and (2) have been mainly achieved by an analytical/modeling study published in a top transportation journal (Transportation Research – Part B), which analyzed the effects of demand uncertainty in a multi-stage game. In this modeling work, airport capacity and price are sequentially chosen under alternative ownership forms, and the mechanism and potential of airport planning and regulation are discussed. In addition, a complex network model has been developed to analyze airport capacity planning, allocation and regulation. The results, including recommendation on airport capacity choice in particular, and transport infrastructure capacity choice in general, have been summarized in another top transportation journal (Transportation Research – Part A). This allows us to fully address Objective (2) and (3). In fact, we have achieved more than we planned in that the second study (in Transportation Research – Part A) not only offers analytical solutions, but also a case study on particular markets using real industry data. Such empirical work was not proposed in our initial proposal, but nevertheless adds great value to this project.

543011.label: Major findings and research outcome
543011.value: Airport delays and congestion have become major threats to the aviation industry. If demand could be perfectly forecast, an airport could start capacity investment well in advance and the right amount of capacity would be available at the right time. However, the long capacity lead time can cause major efficiency loss if there is substantial demand uncertainty. In this project, we first analyze the effects of demand uncertainty on airport capacity choices. It shows that demand uncertainty will not change optimal capacity choice if demand variation is low and capacity cost is high; otherwise the optimal airport capacity under demand uncertainty will be larger than the case when a deterministic mean demand is considered. These conclusions are robust with respect to the different market structures considered in this study and hold for both profit-maximizing and welfare-maximizing airports. The moderating effects of commercial revenue, capital cost, and airport operation cost on airport capacity choice are qualitatively the same in the cases of uncertain demand and deterministic demand. To analyze how airport capacity should be planned and used in a realistic market where multi-modal transport firms compete, in another study we develop a differentiated Bertrand network game which analyzes the effects of international air transport liberalization, regional open skies policies, domestic inter-modal competition and airport slot allocation when major airports’ capacity may have constraint, and thus, need to be optimized. The model is applied to the transport market in Northeast Asia using a counter-factual approach, demonstrating the model’s capability of evaluating practical policies utilizing market data observed on the routes under investigation. Our modeling results suggest much of the welfare gains are derived from higher frequency after liberalization, which increases service quality, hence consumer utility. Airport slot allocation policies play an important role in the realization and distribution of potential welfare gains related to liberalization. Therefore, government agencies should implement liberalization and airport slot allocation policies jointly, and use alternative regulation and policy instrument in airport capacity planning and allocation.

543011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
543011.value: Rich analytical and empirical results have been obtained in this project. However, there are still some important extensions can be made, which include: (1) The consideration of multi-airport region. Currently, more than half of world’s aviation demands are served by 80+ multi-airport regions. In a multi-airport region, several airports compete for the same / overlapping catchment area. Thus, modeling the effects of demand uncertainty over multi-airport region will be a very important extension to the current projects. (2) There is a vertical relationship between passenger demand, airlines and airports. That is, the demand of airports may be regarded as “derived” demand of passengers and airlines. Formally modeling such a vertical relationship will not only validate our analytical results in a more general setting, but will also offer relevant policy recommendations. However, the above two extensions are analytically very complex and challenging. We hope to secure more research fund in the near future thus that these important extensions can be carried out.

543011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
543011.value: Airport delays and congestion have become major threats to the aviation industry. In the United States alone, 400 fewer jet aircraft would have been needed in 1999 if there had been no congestion at its 29 busiest airports. If demand could be perfectly forecast, an airport could start capacity investment well in advance and the right amount of capacity would be available at the right time. However, the long capacity lead time can cause major efficiency loss if there is substantial demand uncertainty. This research project analyzes how airport should plan their capacity when there is significant demand uncertainty, what are the strategies and policies that can induce optimal outcomes, and how airport ownership and regulations influence airports' capacity choice. Therefore, this study not only provides a modeling tool for airport managers in choosing the right airport capacity, but also analyzes how alternative capacity choices influence airline competition and social welfare.

543911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
543911.value: This research examines the rise and fall of the eminent Li Clan which originated from the Shangdang Prefecture in the present province of Shanxi, but later migrated to the City of Kaifeng, the capital of the Northern Song Dynasty(960-1126). The Li Clan was a model family of generals achieving the prestigious status of imperial in-laws of the Dynasty. The project aims at reviewing the role played by this power group in the dynasty which is commonly perceived a being dominated by the new rising scholar-official class during the so-called Tang-Song Transition Period. The Li Clan came into prominence due to the tremendous contributions of its members, particularly General Li Zhuyun, the founder of the Clan, and his two sons General Li Jilong and General Li Jihuo, to the war of unification of the Song Empire as well as the resistence to the invasions form the Empire of Liao in the north and the Kindom of Xia in the northwest shortly after the unification of the nation. When the Li Clan was honored with the status of imperial in-laws through their intermarriage to the royal house of Zhao, its members were viewed as the tools of the Song rulers to counteract the influence of the civilian group who advanced their political careers mostly through the newly expanded Imperial Civil Service Examinations. During the reign of Emperor Song Renzong, the civilian officials launched a fierce attack on General Li Zhaoliang, the son of Li Jilong and one of the favourites of the emperor. The emperor was forced to compromise by sending General Li out of the capital. Li did not return to the core of power ever since. And the Li Clan began to lose its political influence which had been in its possession for three generations, lasting for more than 100 years since the founding of the dynasty. The Project aims to throw light on the relationship between the civiian official group and the imperial in-laws/military official group through the case study of the Li Clan. The project also aims to enrich our knowledge of the imperial in-laws in the Song Dynasty in the perspective of family and clan history. Traditional Chinese wisdom has reminded us that rich families were difficult to last for three generations. This case study might show that aristocratic families also could not substain their status for more than three generations. 李氏外戚將門的起家者是宋太祖從龍大功臣、官至樞密副使的李處耘。他和二子李繼隆、李繼和均在太祖、太宗、真宗三朝為宋室統一中國，抗禦遼夏立下極大的汗馬功勞。宋太祖讓太宗娶李處耘幼女為妻，到宋太宗繼位後，李氏女被冊為皇后後，李氏即成為戚里之家。太宗極為信任妻舅李繼隆，委以軍事重任。在太宗朝所有對遼對夏的戰役，他幾乎是無役不預。到了真宗朝，決定宋遼國家命運的澶州之戰，也是由李繼隆出任前敵主帥。李繼和在太宗晚年隨兄出征, 在真宗朝成為西邊名將，以建西邊要塞鎮戎軍成名，他禦戎的謀略為宋人所稱許。李氏將門的第三代傳人是李繼隆子李昭亮。他以功臣之子, 外戚之身份，一直受到真宗、劉太后, 特別是仁宗的信任，委他以統率禁軍的大權。但也為此受到仁宗朝的文臣的不斷攻擊, 亦是文臣反對仁宗任用外戚的一大目標。他在壓力下, 被迫離開朝廷, 出守邊鎮大藩。不過, 他得享高壽, 也獲得高官厚爵。他的兒子以李惟賢為首, 不再在政治或軍事發揮甚麼作用, 李氏外戚將門從第四代開始, 慢慢走向衰落，他們仍不斷與宋室宗室通婚，但已發揮不了任何影響力。到南宋時, 亦湮沒無聞。這亦是宋代外戚世家的常見現象：貴不過三代。

543911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
543911.value: There are very few study of eminent clans of generals and imperial-in-laws in Song Dynasty in the past. My study on the Li Clan from Shangdang Prefecture is in fact the first substantial study of this area which widens the horizon of the study of Family history in Song Dynasty. Besides publishing three other case studies of the same area, I have been working on another case study of eminent clan of generals and imperial-in-laws which came from the same prefecture of Li Clan, and having the same surname Li. The first part of the research findings had been presented at the conference held at Taipei in May 2013. The second part of the research findings had been also presented at the conference held at Hangzou in August 2014. The end product of this ongoing project will develop into another monograph.

543911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
543911.value: As the authors of the two book reviews pointed out, the role and the importance of the Song generals and imperial-in-laws in Northern Song Politics have long been neglected and underestimated. In the past, scholars who studied history of clans and families only focused on scholar-official families. And my study has significantly filled the gap.
