561011.label: Major findings and research outcome
561011.value: The major findings can be summarized as follows: Firstly, the effects of bis(3)-cognitin on activation of MEF2D were comprehensively characterized for the first time. Bis(3)-cognitin (1 μM) could stimulate the transcriptional activities of MEF2 gene under the basal condition in SN4741 cells. Moreover, we have further demonstrated that bis(3)-cognitin (1-10 μM) significantly restored the levels of MPP+-induced decline of mitochondrial MEF2D and prevented the MEF2D nuclear functions. (Refereed to publication 7) Secondly, we have carefully investigated the neuroprotective effects, as well as the underlying mechanisms, of bis(3)-cognitin against glutamate-, MPP+-, and K+ deprivation-induced neuronal loss in vitro. In addition, bis(3)-cognitin might promote neurite outgrowth in PC12 cells via the activation of Alpha7-nACh receptors. Moreover, we found that bis(3)-cognitin could prevent the MPP+- apoptosis in SN4741 cells via restoring the dysfunction of MEF2D, possibly through the inhibition of GSK3β. In addition, bis(3)-cognitin (1.0 mg/kg, i.p.) protected MEF2D function in brain against MPTP-induced toxicity in C57BL/6 mice. (Refereed to publications 7, 10, 11 and 22) Thirdly, we have studied the neuroprotective effects of indirubin-3-oxime, a synthetic derivative of indirubin, protect against 6OHDA-induced neuronal apoptosis in PC12 cells. It was found that indirubin-3-oxime (3-10 μM) might prevent the neuronal apoptosis induced by 6OHDA in PC12 cells. Moreover, we have further demonstrate that indirubin-3-oxime might restore the dysfunction of MEF2D induced by 6OHDA, via inhibiting the activation of GSK3β. (Refereed to publication 21) Finally, we have investigated the neuroprotective effects of SU5416 and SU4312, derivatives from Sunitinib. It was found that SU4312 (3-30 μM) might prevent the neuronal loss against MPP+-induced neurotoxicity via inhibiting the neuronal NOS in CGNs. In addition, using the luciferase reporter gene assay, SU4312 might enhance the transcriptional activities of MEF2 gene under the basal and pathological conditions. Moreover, our findings were further confirmed by evaluating the locomotion behavior in zebrafish. SU4312 (30 μM) might attenuated the deficit of locomotion behavior in zebrafish larvae induced by MPTP. (Referred to the publications 6 and 8, one to two manuscripts are still under preparation and will be submitted to the well-respected international journals soon)

561011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
561011.value: The findings associated with our research works might be applied to enormous clinical applications. We have shown that several candidates, including the novel dimeric compounds derived from tacrine and/or huperzine A are promising neuroprotective agents targeting MEF2D. Bis(3)-cognitin, one of the representatives, might enhance the transcription activities of MEF2 gene in the basal conditions. More importantly, we have further demonstrated that bis(3)-cognitin has been shown significant neuroprotective effects against the neurotoxins by regulating the MEF2D dysfunctions, indicating that our dimers might modify the PD pathogenesis by restoring the dysfunctions of MEF2D. Moreover, the fields of developing the new generation disease modifying anti-PD drugs are currently driven not only the academic but also the business attention. Taken together, out findings strongly indicate that the neuroprotectants including the novel dimers might be the promising candidates for developing the disease modifying anti-PD drugs.

561011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
561011.value: We have designed and characterized several promising neuroprotective compounds, which might effectively protect against the neurotoxins. Among these, bis(3)-cogintin and indirubin-3-oxime, two of the representatives, have been shown significant neuroprotective effects against neurotoxins in cellular and animal models. More importantly, we have further showed that bis(3)-cogintin and indirubin-3-oxime might prevent the neuronal loss by restoring the dysfunctions of MEF2D, indicating that these neuroprotective agents might be the drug leads for developing the new generation of anti-PD drugs. Therefore, this project can not only systematically characterize the molecular mechanisms of the neuroprotective agents as promising candidates for anti-PD drugs, but also help further understanding of the pathogenesis of PD.

561111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
561111.value: The long-term goal of our research is to understand the interaction between the thalamus and the cerebral cortex. The thalamus is reciprocally connected with cerebral cortex. Both thalamocortical and corticothalamic projections send collaterals to the thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN) of the ventral thalamus. The TRN consists of only GABAergic inhibitory neurons which only project back to the dorsal thalamus. Recently we found that neurons in both TRN and MGB showed great adaptation and the adaptation was stimulus specific, preferring deviant stimulus can called stimulus specific adaptation (SSA)[1, 2]. We have understood with extracelluar recordings that the deviant stimulus detection of TRN neurons either enhanced or suppressed MGB neuronal responses to the following auditory stimulus[1]. The SSA feature of the TRN has been proposed to induce attention shift to fresh stimulus at the dorsal thalamus, echoing the old ‘searchlight’ hypothesis [4]. Comparing with the SSA in the TRN neurons, that of the MGB neurons was much smaller [3]. The questions arise here. 1) Do TRN neurons have a modulation of the SSA of the MGB neurons? 2) The TRN inhibitory innervations to different subnuclei are different: strong inhibition to the non-lemniscal nuclei, weak or void inhibition to the central core of lemniscal nucleus [8, 9]. Whether TRN modulations are even on the SSA of MGB neurons in different subnuclei. 3) In the ventral MGB, ON and OFF neurons are segregated from each other [10, 11, 12], so how would the TRN innervations modulate differently on those two types of neurons? 4) There was a disagreement in the range of TRN innervations to the MGB [14-24]. The question is whether the SSAs in the TRN and MGB has any correlation; the questions will be addressed with both the extracellular and intracellular recordings from TRN and MGB neurons with oddball paradigm, while the TRN is manipulated with drug application. With intracellular recording, we would be able to measure the membrane potential of MGB neurons at the subthreshold level while they are modulated with TRN innervations. The results of the proposed study would advance our understanding on the deviance-detection in the TRN and its interaction with the dorsal thalamus, and thus the selective gating function of the thalamus. The results would also add an important piece of knowledge on potential functional implications of the highly integrative brain processes of attention. 我们研究的长期目标旨在了解丘脑和大脑皮层之间的相互作用。丘脑和大脑皮层存在交互的纤维联系，丘脑皮层和皮层丘脑投射的轴突都有侧枝支配属于腹侧丘脑的丘脑网状核团，该核团完全有GABA能的抑制性神经元组成，且只投射至背侧丘脑核团。我们最近的研究结果表明丘脑网状核和内侧膝状体神经元均表现出明显的适应现象，而且该适应是刺激特异性-偏好于新奇刺激,称之为刺激特异性适应。通过细胞外记录技术，我们业已了解丘脑网状核团神经元的新奇刺激检测特性可以增加或者减少内侧膝状体神经元对听觉刺激的反应。现在普遍认为丘脑网状核团的刺激特异性适应特性有助于背侧丘脑对新颖刺激的注意迁移，这与先前提出的“探照灯”假说也是一致的。研究发现与丘脑网状核团神经元相比，内侧膝状体神经元的刺激特异性适应相对较弱。由此产生的问题是：1），丘脑网状核团神经元是否对内膝体神经元的刺激特异性适应有调节作用？2）丘脑核团不同亚区的丘脑网状核团的抑制性输入模式不同，非丘系核团的丘脑网状核团支配较多，而在丘系核团核心区的该抑制输入较弱甚至缺失。那么丘脑网状核团对不同亚区的内膝体神经元的调制作用是否一致呢？3）内膝体腹侧核团存在着ON和OFF类型神经元，它们是互相分离的，那么来自丘脑网状核团的抑制投射式是如何差异性的调控这两种不同类型神经元的呢？4），目前关于丘脑网状核团对内膝体的支配范围尚存在一些争议。那么丘脑网状核团和内膝体的刺激特异性适应是否存在关联呢？我们将运用细胞外和细胞内记录技术记录丘脑网状核团和内膝体神经元对odd-ball模式的听觉刺激的反应，同时在丘脑网状核团施加药物以调控其神经活性。我们可以用细胞内记录方法测量到内膝体神经元在丘脑网状核团调控下阈下水平的膜电位。该计划的研究成果将会加深了解丘脑网状核团神经元偏离刺激检测特性、其和背侧丘脑的相互关系以及丘脑选择性门控机制。其结果同时也会增加我们对注意这种高度整合的大脑加工的潜在功能意义的了解。

561111.label: Realisation of objectives
561111.value: Stimulus-specific adaptation (SSA) is observed in many brain regions in humans and animals. SSA of cortical neurons has been proposed to accumulate through relays in ascending pathways. The objectives 1 to 3 of the present study were to examine whether thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN) TRN neurons have a modulation of the deviance-detection of the medial geniculate body (MGB) neurons, and to investigate the TRN modulation over the SSA of different subnuclei of MGB. The Objectives 4 and 5 were to investigate whether neurons in both TRN and MGB accumulate SSA during the ascending information pathway. The majority of MGB neurons responded to acoustic stimuli with an onset EPSP that followed by long-lasting IPSP components or with only IPSP components. We first examined the sources of thalamic and cortical inputs of TRN neurons were examined by investigating the responses of the TRN neurons to electrical stimulation of different sites in the thalamus and the cortex of the rat. Single TRN neurons responded to electrical stimulation of the thalamus over a large area and to cortical stimulation over a large area of the auditory cortex. We then investigated the influence of the TRN on the SSA of MGB neurons in anesthetized guinea pigs. Intracellular recording in subthreshold level showed SSA of MGB neurons in both excitatory (EPSP) and inhibitory postsynaptic potential (IPSP) forms. The majority of MGB neurons responded to acoustic stimuli with an onset EPSP that followed by long-lasting IPSP components or with only IPSP components. The IPSP components measured from the MGB neurons were synchronized with neuronal activities in the TRN. Inactivation of the TRN resulted in a changed neuronal response with minimized IPSP components and thus changed SSA of MGB neurons. The TRN innervations modulate differently on the auditory responses and the SSA of the ON and OFF neurons in the ventral MGB. Our results suggest that SSA in the MGB was strongly modulated by the inhibition from the TRN, which also received corticothalamic feedback, indicating SSA was a network product. We finally examined SSA at the synapse level using whole-cell patch-clamp recordings of rat neurons. We found that cultured neurons had high firing capability with 100-Hz stimulation and even higher firing capabilities with current injection. Neurons showed SSA to two separately placed puffs repeated at 10 Hz. Compared with EPSCs, GABAa receptor-mediated inhibitory postsynaptic currents showed weaker SSA. Our findings suggest that postsynaptic fatigue contributes largely to SSA.

561111.label: Major findings and research outcome
561111.value: Stimulus-specific adaptation (SSA) is observed in many brain regions in humans and animals. SSA of cortical neurons has been proposed to accumulate through relays in ascending pathways. The majority of MGB neurons responded to acoustic stimuli with an onset EPSP that followed by long-lasting IPSP components or with only IPSP components (Gao, He). We first examined the sources of thalamic and cortical inputs of TRN neurons were examined by investigating the responses of the TRN neurons to electrical stimulation of different sites in the thalamus and the cortex of the rat. Single TRN neurons responded to electrical stimulation of the thalamus over a large area and to cortical stimulation over a large area of the auditory cortex (Yu et al. 2011). We then investigated the influence of the TRN on the SSA of MGB neurons in anesthetized guinea pigs. Intracellular recording in subthreshold level showed SSA of MGB neurons in both excitatory (EPSP) and inhibitory postsynaptic potential (IPSP) forms. The majority of MGB neurons responded to acoustic stimuli with an onset EPSP that followed by long-lasting IPSP components or with only IPSP components. The IPSP components measured from the MGB neurons were synchronized with neuronal activities in the TRN. Inactivation of the TRN resulted in a changed neuronal response with minimized IPSP components and thus changed SSA of MGB neurons (Gao, He). The TRN innervations modulate differently on the auditory responses and the SSA of the ON and OFF neurons in the ventral MGB. SSA in the MGB was strongly modulated by the inhibition from the TRN, which also received corticothalamic feedback, indicating SSA was a network product. We tested SSA in the auditory cortex to the ear of stimulation using broadband noise. We show that cortical neurons adapt specifically to the ear of stimulation, and that the contrast between the responses to stimulation of the same ear when rare and when common depends on the binaural interaction class of the neurons (Xu et al. 2014). We finally examined SSA at the synapse level using whole-cell patch-clamp recordings of rat neurons. We found that cultured neurons had high firing capability with 100-Hz stimulation and even higher firing capabilities with current injection. Neurons showed SSA to two separately placed puffs repeated at 10 Hz. Compared with EPSCs, GABAa receptor-mediated inhibitory postsynaptic currents showed weaker SSA. Our findings suggest that postsynaptic fatigue contributes largely to SSA (Wang et al. 2014).

561111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
561111.value: Our work in the auditory thalamus has been extended to the auditory cortex recently. We have found that the auditory cortex have strong stimulus-specific adaptation, one kind of short-term neuroplasticity. We further explored the long-term neuroplasticity in the auditory cortex. We found that the auditory cortex can respond to the visual stimulus after some conditioned learning (Chen et al. 2013). That associative learning depended on the entorhinal cortex of the medial temporal lobe (Chen et al. 2013). The entorhinal cortex enables the associative learning in the auditory cortex via a neuropeptide cholecystokinin (CCK, Li et al. 2014). We are currently working on the mechanism how CCK switches memory-encoding in the neocortex.

561111.value: We try to understand the interaction between the thalamus and the cerebral cortex. The thalamus is reciprocally connected with cerebral cortex. Both thalamocortical and corticothalamic projections send collaterals to the thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN) of the ventral thalamus. The TRN consists of only GABAergic inhibitory neurons which only project back to the dorsal thalamus. Recently we found that neurons in both TRN and MGB showed great adaptation and the adaptation was stimulus specific, preferring deviant stimulus can called stimulus specific adaptation (SSA). We have understood with extracelluar recordings that the deviant stimulus detection of TRN neurons either enhanced or suppressed MGB neuronal responses to the following auditory stimulus. The SSA feature of the TRN has been proposed to induce attention shift to fresh stimulus at the dorsal thalamus, echoing the old ‘searchlight’ hypothesis. In the present study we investigated the interaction between the TRN and MGB. We used the extracellular and intracellular recordings from TRN and MGB neurons with oddball paradigm, while the TRN is manipulated with drug application. Our results advanced our understanding on the deviance-detection in the TRN and its interaction with the dorsal thalamus, and thus the selective gating function of the thalamus.

561211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
561211.value: <競爭性光學離焦對哺乳類動物眼部發育的調變> 研究項目摘要 動物模型 — 理解人類近視的關鍵 近視在亞洲多個地區廣泛流行，例如香港、星加坡、台灣、中國大陸等。現時大約有百分之八十的香港華人孩子患有近視。現今近視可以藉由鏡片和手術等方法矯正，然而該等方法未能防止眼球持續過度生長，也因而未能防治高度近視可能引致的視網膜病變、青光眼及早發性白內障等併發症。過往從各種動物身上的研究發現，大多數動物的視網膜具有獨立的基制，使其能夠判辨所接收之影像的前後位置，用以來指引眼球發育生長的速度。其中，當影象被聚焦在視網膜之後時（術語為：遠視性光學離焦），會產生使眼球加速生長的信號。反之，當影象被聚焦在視網膜之前時（術語為：近視性光學離焦），會產生使眼球減慢生長的信號。「遠視性光學離焦」與「近視性光學離焦」合稱「競爭性光學離焦」。 早前我們的團隊在小雞身上作的實驗，透過使用雙焦點鏡片，發現動物的眼睛能判辨同時存在的遠視性和近視性光學離焦，更能因應該等競爭性離焦在亮度和屈光度的相對強弱來調整生長。 運用相同的原理，我們進行了一個隨機分派的臨床試驗，以測試特製的雙焦軟性隱形眼鏡在抑制兒童近視加深的效果。初期結果顯示該方法能減慢加深速度平均百分之三十三。一方面這臨床結果令人鼓舞，與在鳥類身上的結果在本質上很近似，但另一方面也顯示鳥類動物模型的不足使其研究發現未能直接量化地套用於臨床應用。 因此，及早利用哺乳類動物模型來優化以上治療效果變得相當重要。而豚鼠正是適合用於近視研究的新動物模型，其眼球結構與小雞比較更接近人類，對光學離焦的反應也被反複證明為很可靠，因此，我們倡議利用特製的鏡片來仔細量度競爭性光學離焦對豚鼠眼部生長的影響。當中最重要的是，我們將找出最能有效地抑制哺乳類動物近視加深的光學條件。 此項結果將會成為制定先進近視臨床防治策略的重要參巧基礎，以及幫助科學界改良光學設計，使鏡片在提供清晰矯視效果同時，亦能抑制近視加深。

561211.label: Realisation of objectives
561211.value: A series of experiments were carried out to achieve the objectives. Two designs of optical lenses, both feature dual power for introducing competing defocus, were manufactured. The first lens utilized a concentric multi-zones Fresnel design while the second lens utilized a two zones center-peripheral design. In theory, the first lens produces defocus all over the retina while the second lens produces defocus at the peripheral retina only. We tested the first lens design and quantified its effect on eye growth in our first paper (published 2013). And we tested the second lens design and quantified its effect on eye growth in our second paper (written but not yet submitted). In general, competing defocus introduced through either design were able to influence eye growth in a dose-dependent manner. That is, the eyes were able to summate the defocus signals of both powers and then guide its refractive growth. In the second lens design, the refractive status of the central posterior region of the eye were also influenced by the peripheral defocus. However, not every animals fitted with the second lens designed were able to respond accurately to the introduced peripheral myopic defocus. Therefore we may conclude that the first lens design, compared to the second, is preferred to optimally inhibit myopic progression in guinea pig eyes. This implies that myopic defocus that cover the whole retina is more effective in inhibiting myopia progression in guinea pig. This finding will inspire the equivalent lens design for application in human children. We have extended a collaboration with the Laboratory of Ophthalmology, Zhongshan Ophthalmic Centre, Sun Yat-Sen University, China in studying some samples and results collected from the Australian collaborator McFadden. This resulted in a publication and concluded that induced myopia in guinea pig can be recovered and such recovery is related to the thickening of choroid. This findings impacts on further study of the role of choroid in maintaining emmetropization. There is another collaboration by Co-I CH To in exploring the dual focus lens effect on emmetropization with researchers from US and Australia, this resulted in a presentation at ARVO 2015. The team experienced several uncontrollable obstacles that have delayed our experiment and subsequent publication. At first the team planned to carried out all the experiments in the Hong Kong Polytechnic University (Lam and To's lab), however there was no local source of pigmented guinea pig. After that, the team attempted to import pigmented guinea pig from mainland China across the border but were unable to establish such channel in time due to the health and legal issues. That's why most of the animal experiment were eventually carried out in Australia (McFadden's lab). Another factor that has caused delay was that the co-I Dennis Tse, who was proposed to perform some of the experiments, was unavailable most of the time between 2011-2014 as he left PolyU to pursue his postdoctoral study in USA during that period. The PI Carly Lam was on sabbatical leave during late 2013 to late 2014, Prof To continues to oversee the study. These problems partly explained the remaining fund, as research staff time was greatly reduced. There are a couple of manuscripts being prepared for submission in the very near future. One is nearly completed that we have attached the draft manuscript. The other one is under preparation and it is based on our abstract presentation at ARVO 2013. The abstract is attached for reference under the research output column. We envisage that we will have 4 publications all together.

561211.label: Major findings and research outcome
561211.value: The study results in 2 peer-reviewed papers, of which one has been published in top vision journal and the other one in a Chinese Ophthalmology journal. The third one is nearly completed for submission, while the fourth one is now in circulations among the authors for revision. Three manuscripts (published or in-preparation are uploaded in Part C). The study also results in 1 family of patent, which describes the optical design believed to optimally inhibit myopia progression in children. The hypothesis of myopic defocus retarding myopia has also attracted a substantial industrial funding in the amount of HK$3.5M for a human clinical trial. The registration number of the clinical trial is NCT02206217.

561211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
561211.value: The current study has identified the preferred optical design for inhibiting myopia progression in guinea pig. The next step will be testing the efficacy of such optical design in human, which has started for about 12 months.

561211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
561211.value: The present study incorporated myopic defocus in normal optical lens to inhibit myopic eye growth in guinea pig. Several ways for optically incorporating the myopic defocus were compared and the preferred optical design that optimally inhibit myopa progression was determined.

562611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
562611.value: 近視是由多種因素引致眼球生長過長的眼睛問題，它是亞太地區最常見的屈光不正情況。目前中國的人口中有近4億人患有近視，而在一些亞洲國家，近視率更高得驚人，達到近九成之多，近視病發率和嚴重程度在區內不斷地增長。由於高度近視可導致的視網膜病變和永久性視力缺損，因此，無論在個人及社區方面，它對香港經濟和社會構成的影響都常被低估。事實上，近視引致的視網膜病變是本港主要的致盲原因之一，隨着近視人口不斷上升，令人擔心的是視障數字亦會急劇上升。 雖然現時有相當多的近視臨床研究數據，但其病生理學原因仍未被破解。驅使近視眼生長的生物化學的途徑現時仍然是不清楚的。蛋白學方法應用在識別癌症和糖尿病的蛋白質標誌物的診斷及治療上。蛋白學方法可提供分子“快拍”，有效地分析、分類和比較數以千計的細胞蛋白。 通過比較正常和近視之間的眼睛組織變化，當中關鍵的近視生物化學途徑便會揭示出來。以往的蛋白學研究主要集中於鳥類近視模型，而禽鳥眼睛跟人類眼睛在結構上有很大分別。因此，該項計劃將以豚鼠模型研究視網膜的蛋白質變化。從哺乳類動物的近視模型所獲得的數據，有助了解人類近視及其生物化學途徑。此外，該研究亦有助深入探討控制人類近視發展。

562611.label: Realisation of objectives
562611.value: Objective 1: We have successfully developed lens induced myopia (LIM) as well as form deprived myopia (FDM) in young guinea pigs using optical lenses (-4 or -5D) and diffusers respectively. Typically these eyes developed around -3.0 or -4.0D relative myopia in 8 days with corresponding increase in axial length in LIM. In the case of FDM, it continued to develop myopia up to four weeks (to about 10D myopia) with the diffusers on. We harvested the retinas at specific time points for protein analysis. Using two dimensional differential in-gel electrophoresis (2D-DIGE), we were able to profile retinal proteins in normal as well as myopic eyes and subsequently identified the global retinal protein profiles using MALDI-ToF/ToF MS and LC-MS/MS. Typically, more than 1000 protein spots (1356±55, Mean±SEM, n=16) could be detected from each retina in both LIM and FDM paradigms. These proteins can be classified according to their functional roles such as structural and enzymatic functions. This objective was considered achieved completely. Objective 2 and 3: We have compared protein changes between normal and myopic retinas using 2D-DIGE. With LIM paradigm, among all the profiled proteins, thirty-two of them showed differential expression between myopic and untreated retina. We were able to identify 8 of them which showed changes of at least 20% according to their fluorescent quantification. They are beta-actin; Enolase 1, Cytosolic malate dehydrogenase isoform 5, YPT3, Protein-L-isoaspartate(D-aspartate) O-methyltransferase, PKM2 protein X-linked eukaryotic translation initiation factor 1A and ACP1 protein. With FDM paradigm, we were also able to identify another 8 proteins that are differentially expressed. Significant increases in protein levels were found in myopic eyes for Septin-6, Fascin-1, Collapsin response mediator protein, Preproalbumin precursor, Succinate dehydrogenase complex subunit A and Vimentin; whereas protein levels were found to be decreased for soluble NSF attachment protein and Phosphoglycerate mutase 1. Four of these proteins (Septin-6, Collapsin response mediator protein and Phosphoglycerate mutase 1 and Vimentin) were found previously to be differentially expressed – in the same direction – in the retina of chicks developing lens-induced myopia. It was noted that the proteins identities were different between the LIM and FDM paradigms suggesting that these two paradigms do not share identical biological downstream pathways. However, a good number of these proteins are related to increase activities of metabolic and cytoskeletal proteins which suggested the myopia is, in general, an accelerated growth process. We were also able to conduct comparison between the young normal growing eyes (3 days) with adult eye (21 days) for differentially expressed proteins. The retinal proteins were separated and identified by nano-LC coupled tandem mass spectrometry. There were overall 28 proteins which showed significant change in expressions between the developing young retina and fully developed adult guinea pig retina. These proteins include similar proteins as found in myopic retina: structural proteins such as tubulin, dynamin & porin, and metabolic proteins such as enolase, hydrolyase and NADH-ubiquinone reductase. From bioinformatics pathway analysis, a protein called Apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1) appeared to be common and important in eye growth. ApoA1 was found to be consistently down regulated in myopic eyes in chicks but only marginally differentially expressed in guinea pig eyes (not met the criteria for differentially expressed protein in myopic guinea pig eyes). We zoomed into the physiology of ApoA1 and conducted experiment to confirm its importance in eye growth. By altering the expression of ApoA1 pharmacologically with cAMP, we were able to retard myopia development in animal (chicks). The data also suggested that ApoA1 may be a stop signal for eye growth and it is demonstrated that cAMP may regulate the expression of ApoA1 in the retina. Although this work is not proteomic in nature, it directly related to the third objective in highlighting the important of proteomic platform for subsequent validation of protein targets using physiological approaches as shown in this paper. These two objectives were considered achieved completely. Objective 4: In our earlier part of work, we were able to conduct myopia induction experiments in our collaborator’s laboratory in Australia. We have in fact induced a good number of LIM retinal tissues for proteomic work. However, these retinal tissues were mostly used up in those experiments for profiling global proteins with 2D-DIGE. We have later encountered difficulty in setting up guinea pig colony in Hong Kong because of importing issues. While early trials were conducted with those retinal tissues from outside Hong Kong, we do not have a constant supply of guinea pig tissues at the time. Therefore, while we continued to find solution to securing guinea pigs issues, we conducted the post-translational modification work using chicks which were readily available in the lab. Since the process of eye growth is quite conserved across many animal species, the idea was that we may be able to combine the chick PTM data with later guinea pig PTM data when available for better understanding the role of PTM in eye growth. In our PTM work, we focused on phosphorylation of proteins in myopic retina. Since the amount of phosphoproteins is small, an effective concentration strategy is required. We have tried many concentration methods and finally settled on using a titanium dioxide enrichment approach coupled to a next generation nanoLC Triple Time of Flight MS to study low-abundance phosphopeptides. A total of 381 phosphopeptides in myopic retina with 401 phosphorylation sites were detected. In the hyperopic retina, 347 phosphopeptides with 372 phosphorylation sites were detected. The overwhelming majority of phosphopeptides had single-phosphorylation, with a small minority of peptides showing double-phosphorylation (ratio approximately 9:1). Peptides with triple-phosphorylation were found only very rarely. These phosphopeptides belonged to 290 (myopia) and 249 (hyperopia) phosphoproteins. The classification patterns in terms of their molecular functions and biological processes were quite similar in both myopia and hyperopia. In myopia and hyperopia phosphoproteins with molecular functions in the groups of binding (32.9% and 36.4%), catalytic (6.4% and 25.0%) and structural molecule (17.8% and 15.9%) represented the three predominant groups. We have showed that our current protocol is successful in revealing differentially changed phosphoproteins during different modes of eye growth. Overall, subsequent to bioinformatics and pathway analysis, the data from quantitative proteomics and phosphoproteomics have indicated that there are significant changes in cellular metabolism in myopic eye growth which is suggestive of an activation of growth process. The last objective was only partly achieved with guinea pigs because of the lack of tissues but all of the intended PTM work was achieved its objective with chick model.

562611.label: Major findings and research outcome
562611.value: IOverall, the project has shown success in the quantitative profiling of retinal proteins in normal and myopic guinea pigs using different proteomic technologies. It also identified a host of phosphorylated proteins in myopic and hyperopic eye growth. This information is very important in unravelling the mechanism of myopia that may lead to novel myopia control strategies in the future. The first publication (output 1) described the success in identifying differentially expressed proteins in form deprived myopic (FDM) guinea pigs. Using two dimensional Differential In-gel Electrophoresis (2D-DIGE), we have discovered a number of differentially expressed proteins. Similarly, we have also identified protein changes in lens induced myopic (FDM) guinea pig (output 3). The data indicated that metabolic and structural changes are prominent during myopic eye growth. With the advanced in proteomic technology, we have analysed proteins in young and adult normal guinea pig using SWATH analysis and highly sensitive mass spectrometer (output 4). This experiment has successfully profiled over 3000 proteins. In this normal growing process, we have shown changes in proteins related to phototransduction in addition to activities related to development. The extensive network information may shed light on the relationship between eye growth and the development of specific retinal functions. We have also conducted a complete set of experiment on post-translational modification (PTM) in myopia with chicks. After refining the method of concentration with titanium oxide, we were able to identify around 370-380 phosphopeptides in myopic and hyperopic retinas and some were differentially phosphorylated in myopic eye (PhD student Fengjuan YU). Similar work on guinea pig is being conducted by another PhD student presently due to the lack of guinea pig tissues (Bingjie CHEN). The PTM experiment has helped open up new opportunity for eye researchers to study protein mechanisms in various conditions. Our experience with PTM on eye research has been written up and published as in output 2. The fifth publication was generated from our screening of protein candidates with bioinformatics and pathway analysis tools. We found that retinal apoA1 expression was down-regulated in myopic but up-regulated in hyperopic eyes. We used cAMP to artificially increase the retinal apoA1 and found that myopic eye growth was significantly retarded. This publication proposes a link between cAMP and ApoA1 in that cAMP may regulate the expression of ApoA1 in the retina. This discovery was made possible by the proteomic database from this project.

562611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
562611.value: The current project aimed to profiling protein changes during normal and aberrant eye growth. Proteins that were differentially changed in quantity and/or in their post-translational modifications (PTM) revealed two levels of proteomic discovery related to eye growth. These protein targets allows the generation of working hypotheses for the underlying biochemical cascades and mechanisms in eye growth. Our data have provided a comprehensive protein database as an important platform and resource for follow-up research work. Scientists can now zoom into these candidate cascades/compounds and design experiments to validate their physiological importance in regulating eye growth with mammalian myopia models. The future research will involve characterizing other forms of protein PTM such as methylation and glycosylation. The ultimate goal of understanding the molecular mechanism in aberrant eye growth such as myopia is to identify a clinically applicable therapeutic approach that has the optimal myopia control effect.

562611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
562611.value: Myopia is a highly prevalent condition in many East Asian cities including Hong Kong. The excessively large myopic eye is frequently associated with a number of sight threatening eye diseases such as glaucoma and retinal degeneration. However the exact mechanism of myopic eye growth is unknown. This project aimed to understand the molecular mechanism of myopic eye growth by cataloging changes in cellular proteins - this method is called a proteomic approach. Using a mammalian model, we have found a number of specific changes in cellular proteins which include protein quantities and their structural modifications. These findings are important in depicting substantial number of candidates that can help reveal the underlying molecular mechanisms of myopia. Most importantly, it helps to zoom into specific pathways and test if they are indeed crucial in regulating eye growth. One of the compounds we so identified is called apolipoprotein A1 (apoA1) which is a member of high density lipid. Further experiment has shown that by manipulating apoA1 level of the eye, one can slow down myopic eye growth. This discovery exemplifies the fruitfulness of applying proteomic approach in myopia research in that potential therapeutic targets may be elucidated for future clinical control of myopia.

563211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
563211.value: Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) is used to be a popular regime for prevention and treatment of postmenopausal symptoms. However, recent evidence suggests that HRT is associated with increased risk of development of breast, ovarian and endometrial cancer). Dietary sources of phytoestrogens (plant-derived compounds that have estrogenic properties) have recently received much attention due to its beneficial effects on human health and its potential use as an alternative for management of postmenopausal syndrome. Concern has been raised for the safety of using phytoestrogens as alternative to HRT. As many of the physiological effects of phytoestrogens are similar to those of estrogen and their effects are mediated through similar receptors and pathways, the use of phytoestrogens might carry similar risk-benefit profile as estrogen. Epidemiological studies suggest protective effects of isoflavones on breast cancer risk and yet short-term intervention studies suggest the stimulatory effects of isoflavones on breast tissue. The latter has raised the concerns of possible adverse effects of phytoestrogens in breast cancer patients. As many of the actions of phytoestrogen are mediated by estrogen receptors (ERs), a more detailed understanding of how individual phytoestogen interacts with the ER is critical for the assessment of the risk and benefits of using phytoestrogens. Recent studies indicated that estrogenic actions in different cell types and context are mediated by complex interplay between classical ER pathways and rapid signaling pathways. Latest findings also suggest that rapid nongenomic responses that involve either G-protein coupled membrane receptor (GPR30) or membrane ER alpha might play an essential role in mediating the actions of phytoestrogens in different cell types. Ginsenoside Rg1, an abundant active ingredient in Panax Ginseng, is previously reported to be a unique class of phytoestrogens which exert estrogen-like activities without direct interaction with the ER. The proposed study aims to delineate the mechanisms by which Rg1 initiates rapid signaling pathways and exert estrogenic actions: i) to delineate the mechanisms by which Rg1 activate mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathways; ii) to determine if membrane ER or GPR30 is involved in mediating the actions of Rg1; as well as iii) to determine if other signaling pathways are involved in mediating the activation of ER by Rg1. The characterization of the molecular actions of Rg1 will increase our understandings of the role of rapid signaling pathways in mediating the estrogenic actions and provide new evidence for the risk and benefits analysis of the use of phytoestrogens. 雌激素替代疗法曾是预防和治疗绝经后综合症的主要方法。但最近研究发现雌激素替代疗法能够增加乳腺癌、卵巢癌及子宫内膜癌的发病风险。植物雌激素是来源于植物，具有雌激素样作用的化合物。 饮食来源的植物雌激素由于其有益于人类健康及其治疗绝经后综合症的潜在作用而越来越受到重视。而且植物雌激素作为雌激素替代疗法的替代品，其服用的安全性也越来越受到人们的重视。由于植物雌激素可通过与雌激素类似的受体和通路发挥与雌激素相似的生理学作用，因此植物雌激素的应用可能会产生与雌激素类似的效应和危险性。流行病学研究显示异黄酮对乳腺癌具有保护作用，而且短期干预研究发现异黄酮对乳腺组织具有刺激作用，因此植物雌激素对乳腺癌病人可能的副作用也引起了人们的注意。植物雌激素主要通过雌激素受体发挥作用，因此单一植物雌激素与雌激素受体的相互作用对评估总体植物雌激素的效应和危险性具有重要性。最近研究显示植物雌激素主要是通过经典雌激素受体途径和快速信号转导通路的相互影响而在不同细胞系的发挥雌激素样作用。最新研究结果显示，参与G蛋白偶联膜受体（GPR30）和雌激素膜受体α的快速非基因途径在介导植物雌激素在不同细胞系中的作用具有重要作用。人参皂苷Rg1是人参中的主要有效成分，我们的前期研究结果显示Rg1是一种植物雌激素，它具有类雌激素样作用而不直接与雌激素受体结合。本课题旨在研究Rg1通过快速信号通路发挥雌激素样作用的机制：i) Rg1激活胞外信号调节激酶(MAPK)的机制研究；ii) 膜雌激素受体及G蛋白偶联受体(GPR30)是否参与介导Rg1的作用；iii) 其他信号通路是否参与Rg1对雌激素受体的激活。Rg1分子机制的研究能够增加我们对介导类雌激素样作用的快速信号通路的理解，并为植物雌激素的效应和危险性的分析提供新的依据。

563211.label: Realisation of objectives
563211.value: 1. For the objective 1, about 100% work done has been covered. In this objective, we have attempted to identify the upstream signaling pathways that are involved in activation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway by ginsenosides Rg1. By using siRNA to respective signaling proteins, we have demonstrated that linker protein (Shc), modulator of nongenomic activity of estrogen receptor (MNAR) and nonreceptor tyrosine kinase (c-src) are involved in Rg1 activation of MAPK in human breast cancer MCF-7 cells. In addition, we have demonstrated the involvement of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) in mediating the actions of Rg1 in MCF-7 cells by using chemical blocker (1 AG1478). Co-immunprecipitation studies demonstrated that Rg1 can induce the formation of ternary complexs (ER/IGFR/Shc) in MCF-7 cells. The results further confirmed the role of these signaling proteins in mediating the upstream signal for activation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway by Rg1 in MCF-7 cells. 2. For objective 2, about 95% of work has been covered. We have demonstrated that Rg1 induced the formation of complex containing MNAR, ERalpha and Src in MCF-7 cells using co-immunoprecipitation study. In addition, G-protein coupled estrogen receptor (GPER) is involved in mediating the rapid signaling of Rg1 in MCF-7 cells. However, due to the technical problem with the instrument (time-lapsed microcope), the study of the effects of Rg1 on ERalpha translocation to plasma membrane via interaction with caveolin-1 protein by time-lapsed microscopy is still ongoing. 3. For Objective 3, about 100% of work done has been covered. We have demonstrated that the involvement of PI3K/Akt-mediated pathways in mediating Rg1 activation of estrogen receptor in MCF-7 cells. Upon incubation with chemical blocker (LY294002), the effects of Rg1 on cell proliferation, pS2 and IGFR mRNA expression in MCF-7 cells were abolished. Rg1was shown to rapidly induce the expression of p85 andthe phosphorylation of Akt as early as 10 min in MCF-7 cells. In addition, Rg1 increased ER alpha phosphorylation at Ser 167 as early as 30 min in MCF-7 cells.

563211.label: Major findings and research outcome
563211.value: Major Findings: The rapid estrogenic actions of ginsenosides Rg1 in human breast cancer MCF-7 cells are mediating complex interplay of different signaling pathways. These include several membrane receptors (such as EGFR, IGFR and GPER) as well as intracellular signaling proteins (ERalpha, Shc, MNAR, c-Src, PI3K, Akt). It appears that upon Rg1 activation, a signaling complex containing multiple signaling proteins is formed rapidly to mediate the rapid actions of Rg1. These mechanisms explain how Rg1 can rapidly activate ER ligand independently and exert estrogenic actions in MCF-7 cells. Research Outcomes: We have prepared 3 manuscripts based on the results of the studies as shown in Part C section 8. 1.Differential ERalpha-mediated rapid estrogenic actions of ginsenosides Rg1 and estren in human breast cancer MCF-7 cells (published in J Steriod Biochem and Mol Biol in 2014). 2.GPER1 mediates the estrogenic actions of Ginsenoside Rg1 in human breast cancer MCF-7 cells (Under Review). We have been asked to supplement our study using siRNA against GPER instead of using chemical blockers to GPER only. The experiment will provide more evidence to support our hypothesis that GPER is involved in mediating the actions of Rg1 in MCF-7 cells. We are currently performing the make-up experiment. 3.Study of molecular mechanisms involved in mediating the ligand-independent activation of estrogen receptor by ginsenosides Rg1 in human breast cancer MCF-7 cells) (Under preparation). In addition, we have presented our research in three international conferences as shown in Part C Section 9 with two posters presentations in US and one invited talk in South Korea. The project also trained one graduate student, Dr. Quangui Gao. The research work carried out by Dr. Quangui Gao in the last year of her Ph.D study was based on part of our proposed study in this project.

563211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
563211.value: The results of the present study increase our understanding of the mechanism by which Rg1 activates estrogen receptor in a ligand-independent manner. The results suggest that Rg1 rapidly activate multiple signaling pathways at the cell surface which lead to the phosphorylation of ER at serine 118 and serine 167. However, the direct targets of Rg1 at the cell surface have not been identified. Further study to investigate the direct target of Rg1 will increase our understanding of the mechanisms by which phytoestrogen might alter estrogenic responses in a tissue-specific manner. The target being identified might also serve as potential drug target for treatment and management of estrogen receptor related diseases. Recent research suggest that a 36 kDa variant of estrogen receptor alpha might play an essential role in mediating rapid estrogen signaling and inhibits genomic estrogen signaling. Thus, in our future study, we will explore if Rg1 exert its effect via ERalpha36 in human breast cancer cells. In addition, we will try to identify the potential Rg1 interacting proteins in human breast cancer cells via affinity column chromatography followed by proteomic analysis.

563211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
563211.value: Ginsenoside Rg1, an abundant active ingredient in Panax Ginseng, is previously reported to be a unique class of phytoestrogens which exert estrogen-like activities without direct interaction with estrogen receptor(ER). Recent study indicated that Rg1 could activate growth related signaling pathways and activate ER without binding to it. It appears that Rg1 is a phytoestrogen that exert its effect via unique mechanism of actions.The characterization of the estrogenic actions induced by Rg1 provides new insights to understand the role of rapid signaling pathway in mediating the actions of phytoestrogens. The research of the funded project clearly demonstrate that ginsenoside Rg1 can rapidly activate multiple signaling pathways in human breast cancer cells. It can induce the formation of signaling complex near the cell surface and facilitate the communication between cell surface receptor and estrogen receptor leading to the rapid activation of estrogen-like actions in human breast cancer cells. This information will be useful for medical professional to assess the risk and benefits of using phytoestrogens.

563611.label: Realisation of objectives
563611.value: (1) The required sample size was reached. In fact, the study was powerful was powerful to identify CNVs associated with high myopia. (2) The second objective was also successfully achieved. We used the method of multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA) to quantify the copy numbers for 89 CNVs segments. Nine CNVs failed and the remaining 80 CNV segments could be typed successfully. Data analysis showed that 7 CNVs were associated with high myopia. We followed up 24 top-ranking CNVs in Stage 2 of the study. This served to maximize the multiplexing capability of MLPA with little increase in cost. (3) In Stage 2, 24 CNVs were followed up in a second group of case-control samples (with and without high myopia). Data analysis showed that 17 CNVs were associated with high myopia. Combined analysis of both stages was even more rewarding because 22 of the 24 followed-up CNVs were significantly associated with high myopia. This indicates that our sample size was adequate and the study was powerful to achieve the stated objectives. (4) Initially, we communicated with our Singapore collaborator for replicating our positive findings. It turned out that the sample collection had only a very small number of samples from high myopes. As such, we contact our Japanese collaborators and asked them to replicate our positive findings. 563611.label: Major findings and research outcome
563611.value: As a complex disease, myopia is the most common eye disease in the world. Many myopia susceptibility genes or variants have been identified in the past years by genome-wide genetic association studies GWAS), which focus mainly on the single-nucleotide polymorphisms. Little attention has been paid to examine the role of copy number variations (CNVs) in refractive error and myopia. This study adopted a systematic approach to investigate the role of CNVs in high myopia. In the discovery phase, a pilot GWAS suggests putative CNVs for follow-up. Multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification was then used to quantify the copy number of 89 CNV segments in 737 case-control samples and then 24 top-ranking CNVs in a second group of 1,029 case-control samples. This validation phase identified 22 significant CNVs. The replication phase used a cohort of 915 Japanese case-control subjects, and was able to confirm the 3 CNV segments; two are adjacent to each other on chromosome and another is on chromosome 6. Further work is needed to further the role of these few CNVs in myopia development.

563611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
563611.value: Only 3 out of 22 validated CNVs were replicated by the Japanese cohort. This is probably because the sample size of the Japanese cohort was smaller than our own collection of Chinese subjects. We expect that an even bigger sample size of the replication samples will replicate more CNS. Replicated CNVs are worthy of follow-up to characterize the boundaries of the CNV and explore the molecular mechanisms of how CNVs can influence the development of myopia, perhaps at least the molecular pathways involving these CNVs.

563611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
563611.value: Myopia is a very common eye disease. Its development is influenced by both genetic and environmental factors. Many human genes or sequence variants have been found in the past years to influence myopia development. Most of the research studies focus on the simple sequence variations, namely single nucleotide polymorphism (SNPs). Little attention is paid to the role of copy number variations (CNVs) in myopia. CNVs are larger stretch of DNA sequences that can vary in its copy number in different individuals. This study adopted a systematic approach to investigate the role of CNVs in the development of myopia. An initial pilot study identified 89 CNV regions to be followed up in the current study. A two-stage strategy identified in our Chinese subjects 22 CNVs that were associated with high myopia. These positive findings were partially replicated using a Japanese cohort.

564011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
564011.value: The Class III Phosphatidylinositol 3 Kinase (PI3K) complex is an essential component of the molecular machinery for autophagy, a cellular catabolic process that recycles cytosolic contents through lysosomal degradation to maintain homeostatic balance. The activity of this complex is tightly regulated at multiple steps of the autophagy process, mostly by protein factors that associate with this complex in dynamic and variable fashion to modulate its activity. Atg14L and UVRAG are the two central modulators of the Class III PI3K complex. Both proteins interact with Beclin 1, a core member of the complex, and form functionally distinct Atg14L- or UVRAG-containing subcomplexes with enhanced PI3K activity to promote autophagy. Currently there is no structural information available on Atg14L/UVRAG-Beclin 1 interaction to help understand how these two proteins modulate PI3K activity and regulate autophagy. Interestingly Atg14L, UVRAG, and Beclin 1 all contain predicted coiled coil domains and their interactions appear to rely exclusively on these regions that have natural propensity to form oligomeric assembly. Furthermore Beclin 1 is shown by our previous study to be a metastable homodimer that readily transits to monomer. We hypothesize that Atg14L or UVRAG interacts with Beclin 1 and induces change in its oligomeric state, possibly a dimer-monomer transition, to form hetero-oligomeric Atg14L/UVRAG-Beclin 1 complex. This change in oligomeric assembly might be correlated with enhanced PI3K activity and autophagy activation. We propose to carry out structural studies of Atg14L and UVRAG to obtain a comprehensive understanding of their regulatory mechanism on autophagy. Specifically we will first conduct in vitro biochemical characterization of the Atg14L/UVRAG-Beclin 1 complex to clarify the oligomeric assembly of each complex. Secondly we aim to characterize the structures of the coiled coil domain of Atg14L and UVRAG, as well as their respective complex with Beclin 1 coiled coil domain, to identify key residues for mediating Atg14L/UVRAG-Beclin 1 interaction; and to elucidate the mechanism by which Atg14L and UVRAG induces change in oligomeric state of Beclin 1. Lastly using the structures as guidance mutants of Atg14L, UVRAG and Beclin 1 with weakened or abolished interaction or impaired hetero-oligomeric assembly will be generated and their effect on modulating PI3K activity and regulating autophagy will be assessed by in vivo cell-based assays to confirm our structural findings. The outcome of this research will yield valuable information regarding the mechanism of Atg14L/UVRAG-mediated autophagy regulation; and provide clues for possibly harnessing this process for therapeutic treatment.

564011.label: Realisation of objectives
564011.value: The project has progressed very well through the 42-month period and is now completed. We would like to report our activities and results obtained according to the three revised objectives that have been approved by RGC. Objective 1. Biochemical characterization of Atg14L/UVRAG-Beclin 1 interaction in vitro This objective has been fully completed at 100%. Both Atg14L and UVRAG contain putative coiled coil domains that don’t fit the canonical heptad repeat sequence motif. Thus it is not clear how these domains would interact with Beclin1 and form coiled coil assembly. In order to identify the key regions responsible for the Atg14L/UVRAG-Beclin1 interaction, we have generated a series of constructs that scan through the coiled coil regions of Beclin1, Atg14L and UVRAG in systematic manner. The resulting binding affinities between these constructs have been measured by Isothermal Titration Calorimetry (ITC). Through these measurements, we confirm that the N-terminal half of the Beclin1 coiled coil domain is critical for Atg14L/UVRAG binding while the C-terminal half is dispensable. Furthermore, we compared the Beclin1-binding affinity between Atg14L and UVRAG using competitive pull-down assay. Our results show that UVRAG is a stronger binding partner for Beclin1 than Atg14L (Kd 0.24 µM vs. 3.22 µM). Sedimentation velocity analytical ultracentrifugation experiments confirm that Atg14L and UVRAG bind to Beclin1 in 1:1 ratio and form heterodimeric assembly. These biochemical findings lay solid foundation for our subsequent structural studies in Objective 2. Objective 2. Structural study of UVRAG coiled coil domain and the UVRAG-Beclin 1 complex This objective has been fully completed at 100%. We pursued structure determination of UVRAG coiled coil domain only and the UVRAG-Beclin1 complex in parallel. As shown in our previously submitted mid-term report, crystals of the UVRAG coiled coil domain were readily obtained and the native data sets were collected at synchrotron source at 3.2 Å resolution although diffraction reached 2.7 Å at best. The large unit cell size, coupled with the molecular weight of ~10kD for the coiled coil construct, implies 12-16 copies of the molecule in the asymmetric unit. Our effort to obtain phase information by heavy metal derivatization didn’t work because crystals suffered severe non-isomorphism after soaking. The phasing method of selenomethionine (SeMet) incorporation didn’t work either because SeMet UVRAG sample was prone to aggregation and failed to crystallize. We also carried out NMR structural studies of the UVRAG coiled coil domain. Its HSQC spectrum showed poor dispersion pattern, indicating that this region is likely in aggregate form. Furthermore, we also characterized the oligomeric state of UVRAG coiled coil region by analytical ultracentrifugation. The sedimentation profile was distinctively broad and suggested that UVRAG could exist in oligomeric state ranging from 8 to 16 copies. In summary, our effort to obtain the structure of the UVRAG coiled coil domain didn’t lead to high-resolution structure, probably due to the propensity of this domain to aggregate in absence of its binding partner Beclin1. The structure of the UVRAG-Beclin1 complex, on the other hand, was solved by x-ray crystallography after extensive work. To facilitate crystallization, we generated a construct in which the N-terminal region of Beclin1 coiled coil domain is tethered to the coiled coil domain of UVRAG via a flexible linker of sequence (GS)5. This design is to prevent spontaneous self-assembly among the Beclin1 and UVRAG coiled coil chains that would interfere with the formation of heterodimeric UVRAG-Beclin1 complex. This strategy worked well and crystals of the UVRAG-Beclin1 complex with diffraction to high resolution (2.1 Å) were readily obtained. To our surprise, these crystals showed varying degree of merohedral twining with the twinning factor ranging from 0 (no twinning) to 50% (perfect twinning). We overcame this technical difficulty by screening large number of crystals and selecting only those data sets with no twinning (about 5% crystals fit this requirement). Eventually the structure of the UVRAG-Beclin1 complex was solved at 2.1 Å with phase information obtained by Single Isomorphous Replacement Anomalous Scattering (SIRAS). The structure of the UVRAG-Beclin1 complex reveals a parallel coiled coil assembly with six leucine zipper pairs to form a stable hydrophobic interface. This is in sharp contrast to the imperfect metastable homodimer interface of the Beclin1 coiled coil domain that we reported previously. This structure provided critical information to guide our structure-based functional study in Objective 3. Additionally the structure for UVRAG coiled coil domain alone can be extracted from this complex as well, even though our previous effort to solve the UVRAG structure directly didn’t yield high resolution structure. Objective 3. Assessment of the functional significance of Atg14L/UVRAG-Beclin1 interaction in modulating Class III PI3K activity and regulating autophagy This objective has been fully completed at 100%. Using the UVRAG-Beclin1 structure as guidance we generated a series of UVRAG mutants in which the six leucine residues responsible for forming the hydrophobic coiled coil interface were replaced by glutamate. Our aim is to use these mutants to investigate the functional importance of the potent UVRAG-Beclin1 interaction in modulating Class III PI3K activity and in regulating autophagy. Our in vitro ITC results show that single or double Leu-to-Glu mutations (termed 1E or 2E in this report) can only weaken the UVRAG-Beclin1 interaction while complete abolishment requires replacement of nearly all the leucine residues (termed 5E and 6E in this report). In vivo Co-IP experiments using these UVRAG mutants reveal that all of them can be pulled down by Beclin1, probably because coiled coil domain is not the only region of UVRAG that associates with Beclin1. However, 5E and 6E mutants show less pull-down amount in presence of over-expressed Atg14L, suggesting that their interaction with Beclin1 has been weakened in vivo as well. The impact of weakened UVRAG-Beclin1 interaction on Class III PI3K activity and autophagy regulation was characterized by standard cell-based assays including confocal imaging of autophagosome marker molecule LC3 and western blot to track autophagy receptor protein p62 and LC3 lipidation. The impact of these mutants on Class III PI3K-dependent endosomal trafficking was characterized by epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) degradation assay. Our results show that the potency of the UVRAG-Beclin1 interaction is critical for Class III PI3K-dependent endosomal trafficking because over-expression of 1E and 2E mutants can enhance EGFR degradation in similar manner to wild-type. However, 5E and 6E fail to do so because their interaction with Beclin1 has been weakened. In contrast, the potency of the UVRAG-Beclin1 interaction is not absolutely required by the autophagy process as over-expression of 1E, 2E, 5E and 6E all yielded similar level of LC3 puncta and p62 as compared to wild-type. In summary our structure-based functional studies confirm that the potent UVRAG-Beclin1 interaction is required for UVRAG-mediated modulation of Class III PI3K activity and Vps34-dependent EGFR degradation via endosomal trafficking.

564011.label: Major findings and research outcome
564011.value: Our study on biochemical characterization of the Atg14L/UVRAG-Beclin1 interaction reveal that Atg14L and UVRAG bind to Beclin1 in mutually exclusive manner and form heterodimeric assembly via their coiled coil domains. Furthermore, our competitive binding assays confirm that UVRAG is a stronger binding partner for Beclin1 than Atg14L. These findings were reported in a publication in Autophagy in 2012 (Part C, item 8[1]). The structure of UVRAG-Beclin1 complex is a heterodimeric coiled coil assembly. Six leucine zipper pairs constitute the canonical hydrophobic interface while additional sequence complementarity between UVRAG and Beclin1 further strengthen their interaction. Structure-based mutational studies confirm that the potency of Beclin1-UVRAG interaction is critical because UVRAG mutants with weakened Beclin1 binding cannot promote autophagy or endosomal trafficking effectively. Furthermore, using the UVRAG-Beclin1 structure as guidance we designed stapled peptides that specifically bind to the C-terminal region of Beclin1 coiled coil domain outside of its UVRAG binding site. These compounds prevent the formation of Beclin1 homodimer in vitro and enhance autophagy response in vivo. Most excitingly, these compounds lead to enhanced lysosomal degradation of EGFR, a major drug target for cancer therapy. A manuscript reporting these findings has been submitted to Nature Struct. Mol. Biol in 2016 (Part C, item 8[5]). A provisional patent application for our designed stapled peptides was also filed with the US Patent and Trademark Office (Part C, item 11[4]). In collaboration with Prof. Zhenyu Yue, our long-time collaborator, we generated a Beclin1 mutant with its UVRAG-binding region deleted according to our structural information and found that it failed to rescue endosome maturation in Beclin1 knockout cells. This work was published in PLOS Genetics in 2014 (Part C, item 8[2]). We also conducted structural studies of an important autophagy receptor protein p62. This work was published in PLOS Genetics in 2015 (Part C, item 8[3]). In addition to our work on Beclin1 and autophagy, our lab has published a paper related to antibiotic resistance (Part C, item 8[4]) within the period of this project. Our lab has strong interest in structure-based drug discovery research, thus we consider this publication relevant for this reporting exercise. Our work on the Atg14L/UVRAG-Beclin1 interaction and its functional significance has been presented at multiple international conferences (Part C, item 9[1]-[3]). Two Ph.D. students have been financially supported by this project (Part C, item 10[1]-[2]). Wu Shuai has just submitted his Ph.D. thesis with oral defense tentatively scheduled in August 2016.

564011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
564011.value: A novel finding from our study involves structure-based rational design of stapled peptides that target the Beclin1 coiled coil domain and enhance Vps34-mediated autophagy and EGFR degradation. This finding has particular translational potential because EGFR signaling pathway is a major driving force for cancer cell proliferation and a primary target for cancer therapy. Our compounds, with their efficacy in promoting EGFR degradation, may present a novel approach orthogonal to existing anti-cancer therapies. For future work we plan to further optimize the potency of our designed peptides by computational modeling. This work will be carried out in collaboration with Dr. Renxiao Wang from Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry, Academia Sinica, P.R.China. Dr. Wang is a longtime collaborator of our lab and a co-author for our manuscript on the UVRAG-Beclin1 complex structure. To characterize the anti-cancer efficacy of our designed compounds we plan to use Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) model because EGFR is almost always over-expressed in NSCLC and even undergo mutations to develop resistance to existing therapies. We will test the efficacy of our stapled peptides using NSCLC cell lines like A549, HCC827 and H1975. EGFR transgenic mice will also be used for candidates with promising cell-based results.

564011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
564011.value: Autophagy is a cellular process that degrades and recycles cytosolic content through lysosome-dependent pathway. Autophagy has been shown to play essential roles in a host of physiological processes and its dysfunction has been implicated in human diseases ranging from tumorigenesis and neurodegeneration to diabetes and cardiomyopathy. Understanding the molecular mechanism of autophagy would help our effort to target this process for treating autophagy-related diseases. The Beclin1-Vps34 complex is an essential module within the molecular machinery of autophagy. Atg14L and UVRAG are two major regulators of this complex and directly bind to Beclin1 via their coiled coil domains. Such interactions lead to the formation of Atg14L/UVRAG-containing Beclin1-Vps34 complexes with enhanced lipid kinase activity to promote autophagy. Our project aims to conduct structural studies of the Atg14L/UVRAG-Beclin1 interaction in order to delineate the molecular mechanism of Atg14L/UVRAG-mediated autophagy regulation. We determined the structure of the UVRAG-Beclin1 coiled coil complex and conducted structure-based functional study to confirm that the potency of the UVRAG-Beclin1 interaction is critical for UVRAG-mediated autophagy and lysosomal degradation of EGFR in lung cancer cell model. These compounds offer the possibility of targeting the Atg14L/UVRAG-Beclin1 interaction for autophagy-targeting therapy.

600111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
600111.value: Improvements in the ability to manipulate electron spin in electronic devices are expected to drive future advances in information storage, processing and other technologies. The successful implementation of what are commonly called spintronics devices requires the capability to generate and inject a strongly spin-polarized current from a ferromagnetic spin source into a spin transport layer. Organic molecular spin transport layers that are under investigation for use as elements in molecular spintronics technology have the advantage that they can deliver greater spin coherence compared to conventional metals and semiconductors. In the proposed research, we will investigate the structural, electronic and magnetic properties that constitute the organic/ferromagnet spin-interface science of the molecular spintronics system. It is known that molecular adsorption on nonmagnetic metal surfaces can modify the structure and electronic properties on both sides of the formed interface. However, the possibility that molecular layers have an analogous impact on the magnetic properties of a ferromagnetic surface, hence the spin injection properties of the interface, has largely been overlooked. We will address this issue by examining how the adsorption of several types of relevant organic molecules on a variety of thin film magnetic nanostructures affects thin film magnetism. Ferromagnetism in thin film and other nanostructures is strongly influenced by reduced dimensionality, surface and interface effects. Our focus on thin films, therefore, will address looming issues that will become increasingly important as the dimensions of ferromagnetic electrodes in spintronic devices are reduced to the nanometer length-scale. The proposed research will be carried out using a combination of highly complementary experimental techniques – scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and spectroscopy (STS), low-energy electron microscopy (LEEM) and diffraction (LEED) and their spin-polarized variants (SPLEEM, SP-STM/STS) – and first-principles theoretical calculations. These tools will be used in part to determine the structure of the interface, knowledge of which is essential for developing an understanding of interface magnetic and electronic properties. We will also experimentally identify changes in macroscopic magnetic properties that are caused by molecular adsorption, such as the magnetic ordering temperature and magnetization easy axis. Theoretical investigations will help us to understand how the changes of macroscopic magnetization behavior that are observed experimentally may be related to modifications of electronic structure and fundamental magnetic quantities such as magnetic moment and magnetic anisotropy. The knowledge of organic/ferromagnet interface properties that this research can deliver is essential for understanding factors that affect spin injection in molecular spintronics devices. 提升操控電子自旋的能力，无疑会促进信息存儲、處理及其他科技的進一步發展。為了實現自旋電子元件，我们需要從鐵磁自旋源產生強烈的自旋極化電流，並把它注入到自旋傳導層中。目前，人們正在研究用有機分子製作自旋傳導層，使其成为分子自旋電子學技術中的基礎元件。相比常用的金屬和半導體材料，有機分子具备更強的自旋相干性。在擬議的研究中，我們將研究有機分子/鐵磁體組成的分子自旋電子系統在界面上的一些性質，包括結構、電学和磁学性質。雖然我們都知道，當分子吸附在非磁性金屬表面上，界面兩邊材料的結構和電子性質將發生改變。但常忽略分子層對鐵磁材料表面的鐵磁性質的影響以及对自旋注入性質的影響。我們將通過研究幾種有機分子對不同納米磁性薄膜結構磁性的影響来回答這個問題。薄膜和其他納米結構的磁性性質容易受到小尺度、表面和界面效應的影響。隨著自旋電子器件中鐵磁電極的尺寸縮小至納米尺度，一些相关問題變得越來越重要，研究薄膜材料將有助於解決這些問題。擬定的研究將結合第一性原理理論計算和一些高互補性的實驗技術，包括掃描隧道顯微技術(STM)和譜学技術(STS)、低能電子顯微技術(LEEM)和散射技術(LEED)以及相應的自旋極化技術(SPLEEM, SP-STM/STS)。這些工具將從不同方面揭示一些關於界面結構的信息，而這些知識對我們理解界面的磁性和電性性質十分重要。我們還將檢測材料整體的磁性性質是否因為分子的吸附而發生改變，例如磁有序溫度(尼爾溫度)和磁易軸。理論的研究將有助於我們了解實驗中觀測到的整體磁性行為的改變與電子結構、基本磁參量如磁矩、磁各向異性的變化之間的聯繫。整項研究將提供我們關於有機分子/鐵磁體界面性質的知識，對於我們了解分子自旋器件中自旋注入的過程是被何因素所影響是必不可少的。

600111.label: Realisation of objectives
600111.value: The project objectives were achieved by performing experiment investigations using spin polarized low energy electron microscopy (SPLEEM) and scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and theoretical investigations using density functional theory calculations. Investigations of the growth and magnetic properties of Fe films on various substrates provided an understanding that underpins further studies of the interaction of organic molecular overlayers with thin film nanostructures. The evolution of Fe film structure, morphology and magnetic properties on the W(111) surface were monitored during film growth at room temperature using low energy electron diffraction (LEED) intensity vs. energy curves, I(V), measurements of work function changes, and SPLEEM magnetic asymmetry vs energy, A(E), and magnetic asymmetry vs in-plane azimuthal angle, A(phi). This work identified the onset of ferromagnetic order due to finite size effects in ultrathin film nanostructures, the complex and sensitive interplay between film structure and threshold magnetic behavior close to the onset of magnetic order, and film thickness dependence of magnetization direction and magnetic domain morphology. Our investigations of Fe on W(110) explored the influence of 1 ML and 2 ML Cu buffer layers at the interface between Fe film and Cu substrate on the thin film magnetic properties. This effect was probed by studying quantum size effects (QSEs) in spin polarized electron reflectivity using SPLEEM. Intensity oscillations were measured as functions of film thickness and incident electron energy that occur due to spin polarized quantum well resonances above the vacuum level. The Cu monolayer is pseudomorphic and the Cu double layer on W(110) has fcc(111)-like structure, which makes it an interesting model for the bulk Cu(111) surface. Therefore, this work reveals how progressive interface modification from W(110) to Cu(1ML)/W(110) to Cu(2ML/W(110), which is the underlying theme of the project, can affect magnetic properties of thin film magnetic nanostructures. Other investigations focused on surprising aspects of magnetization orientation and magnetic domain structure in 3 ML Fe films on the 2 ML Au-covered W(110) surface. In this work, we studied the dependence of the apparent magnetization direction as a function of energy in the very low energy range, below 12 eV. In this energy range, the spin-dependent inelastic mean free path of electrons tends to be more strongly energy dependent. This approach therefore can provide some access to the magnetization depth profile of magnetic thin films. The information about magnetic properties of bare magnetic films obtained in these investigations can serve as the baseline for identifying how molecular adsorption modifies thin film magnetism. Investigations of molecular adsorption on magnetic films using SPLEEM were impeded by the instability of molecules under electron beam illumination. Electron beam effects on adsorbed molecules are not unheard of. These effects are apparently exacerbated in SPLEEM because of the relatively long signal integration times that are needed to obtain spin-dependent images. Due to the low magnetic asymmetry signal, on the order of a few per cent, image integration times of several seconds are needed to acquire images using electron beams with oppositely polarized incident electron beams, from which a purely magnetic image is formed. This is contrast to image acquisition times of 0.1 sec or less for conventional unpolarized LEEM. With such a long image integration time for SPLEEM, it turns out that electron beam effects cannot be neglected. In order to mitigate this problem, we reduced the incident electron beam energy as far as possible, down to nearly to the threshold for elastic backscattering at the onset of the mirror imaging mode as incident energy approaches zero. These energies are below the thressholds for many inelastic scattering processes. Nevertheless, the high beam currents and long integration times needed for forming magnetic SPLEEM images continued to plague the study of adsorbed molecules on magnetic films. Suggestions for overcoming this problem are identified in section B.6.2. We also carried out work on the development of spin polarized scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (SP-STM/STS). We planned to use SP-STM to study how molecular overlayers modify spin polarized tunneling current, either due to tunneling via molecular spin states or modification of thin film magnetism. We adopted an established approach to SP-STM based on chromium-coated polycrystalline tungsten tips. Cr-coated tips were prepared and their structure was characterized using high resolution transmission electron microscopy. A Cr(001) sample was chosen for testing the spin polarized tunneling of this tips because it is known to exhibit layered antiferromagnetism. Although the removal of carbon contaminants by standard sputtering and annealing procedures was confirmed using Auger electron spectroscopy, nitrogen contamination due to segregation from the bulk was persistent, despite extensive sputter/anneal cycles. Low energy electron diffraction also revealed a weak c(2x2) diffraction pattern, which is characteristic of nitrogen contamination. Despite these problems, spin contrast between antiferromagnetically coupled terraces with a spin polarization of 6.1% was obtained in our preliminary SP-STM experiments. Improvements to SP-STM capabilities were needed before this technique could be applied to study organic molecular layers on magnetic films. In particular, spin-polarized tip instability was a key issue. However, further SP-STM development was halted due to equipment failure. Coating a tip with Cr requires frequent tip transfers. Mechanical damage to the tip holder that prevented tip transfer undermined further progress. Furthermore, repairs would have required substantial funds, which were unfortunately not available. Because of the problem to develop SP-STM, we took a different approach to study spin states in adsorbed molecules on surfaces using cryogenic STM/STS, by measuring the electronic states and Kondo resonance of single Fe(II)-porphyrin (FeTPP) molecules adsorbed on a Au(111) surface with intramolecular resolution. These experiments were complemented by spin-polarized density functional theory (SP-DFT) to determine optimum adsorption geometry and electronic structure. These investigations revealed how substrate-molecule interaction modifies the magnetic properties of molecules and guide our understanding of how molecule substrate interaction can affect interfacial electron spin densities that might play a role in organic spintronic devices. We also investigated self-organization of poly-phenylene molecules on a hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) layer on the magnetic Ni(111) surface using STM. h-BN may decouple supported species electronically and chemically from the metal substrate underneath, and is considered a promising template for molecular electronic and spintronic devices. Further, to study the substrate structural modifications and their influence on thin film physical properties, we have investigated the self-assembly behavior of fullerene on the defects site of Au(111) by combining STM and DFT calculations. We chose Au (111), as it is a well-known substrate that can form nano-templates and thus promotes the formation of highly ordered C60 nano-chains. We systematically investigated the detailed geometries involving an apparent reduction of nearest neighbor distances between fullerene molecules residing at linear step sites of Au(111). Further theoretical studies were carried out to study the nature of the interaction and bonding of molecules and metals. This was done by calculating surface enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) of pyridine adsorbed on a series of gold-caged clusters. We used DFT to conduct detailed analysis of the nonresonant mechanism in SERS attributable to the molecule-surface chemical coupling, for a series of gold-caged clusters. Changing the core atom in M@Au12 has enabled us to modulate the direct chemical interactions between the pyridine and the metal cluster.
