600111.label: Major findings and research outcome
600111.value: Investigations of Fe/W(111) films revealed a complex evolution of magnetic properties with increasing thickness, particularly a surprising ferromagnetic thickness gap between 8-9 ML following the onset of magnetism at 6 ML thickness determined by finite size effects [Part C.8 – item 1]. We proposed that the ferromagnetic gap occurs due to the competition between finite size effects and transient influences on magnetic ordering arising from thickness-dependent structural changes. Unoccupied spin-split electronic bands in Fe/Cu(1ML)/W(110) and Fe/Cu(2ML)/W(110) were also determined from the quantum size effect in spin-dependent electron reflectivity [2,3]. These bands were shifted uniformly compared to bands in Fe films on bare W(110). Furthermore, low-energy electron interferometry revealed that the Cu layer in direct contact with the substrate remains intact, but the weakly-bound second Cu layer mixes or segregates freely. Magnetic depth profiling that exploited the spin and energy dependent inelastic mean free path of electrons also revealed a layered non-collinear spin configuration in 3 ML Fe/Au(2ML)/W(110) [6]. Kondo resonance amplitudes were observed in FeTPP molecules on a Au(111) surface that are attributed to the spatial distribution of spin states within the molecule [5]. Surprisingly, theoretical calculations showed that the S = 2 spin state is more stable that the S = 1 spin state in FeTPP/Au(111), which is reverse from the flat free-standing molecule. We proposed that the “spin switching” in FeTPP/Au(111) can arise from structural distortion of FeTPP on Au(111), the nature of bonding between Fe and the underlying Au and consequent modification of intramolecular bonding. TBB molecules that were deposited on h-BN/Ni(111) at room temperature self-assemble into closely-packed molecular layer with excellent long range order, suggestive of halogen-hydrogen intermolecular interactions [7]. This work revealed how an inert h-BN layer weakens the chemical activity while likely preserving the magnetic properties of the Ni substrate. We found that the magnitude of the nonresonant enhancement of SERS in pyridine adsorbed on gold-caged clusters is governed by the charge properties of the metal clusters [4]. Stronger nonresonant enhancement was associated with increasing polarizability. Site selective adsorption of C60 on Au(111) and the formation of one-dimensional C60 nano-chains at low coverage were observed experimentally [8]. Theoretical calculations provided a rationale that adsorption-induced elongations of certain C-C bonds in C60 and vacancy formation on the surface layer of Au (111) are responsible for the deformation of the C60 framework which causes a reduction in the nano-chain length compared to intermolecular distances in C60 crystals.

600111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
600111.value: Further studies using SPLEEM may be carried out after overcoming the detrimental electron beam effects on molecules adsorbed on magnetic thin film surfaces. Improvements that may help to achieve this goal are to employ a high spin polarization electron source and/or a high quantum efficiency direct electron detector. These solutions will reduce image integration time by improving magnetic signal, enhancing signal detection efficiency and reducing noise. Our results for FeTPP/Au(111) provide new insights about molecular spin state switching on metal surfaces that can be useful for designing molecular spintronic devices. We have also demonstrated that molecular adsorption on a h-BN buffer layer may be a new strategy for separating potentially disturbing aspects of the chemical activity of the underlying reactive metal substrate from its desirable magnetic properties. The methodologies demonstrated can be extended to study a wider range of substrate and molecular adsorbate systems relevant not only to molecular spintronics but also optoelectronic and nanoelectronics.

600111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
600111.value: The successful implantation of organic molecular spin transport layers in spintronics devices requires the capability to generate and inject a strongly spin-polarized current from a ferromagnetic spin source into the molecular layer. If this can be mastered, then molecular layers will offer several key advantages over other solid-state materials for use in spintronics technology. We investigated the structural, electronic and magnetic properties of molecular layers, magnetic thin film nanostructures and metallic crystalline surfaces that constitute the spin-interface science of molecular spintronics systems. An understanding of several sensitive magnetic phenomena in Fe thin film nanostructures was obtained that may be crucial to the spin injection process and should underpin further studies of interactions at the organic/ferromagnet interface. Spin switching of magnetic molecules that is induced by their adsorption on a metallic substrate also highlights the role of the interfacial interaction in determining molecular electronic/magnetic properties that should likewise be highly relevant. Numerous other geometric and electronic changes induced by molecular adsorption have been identified, and a new strategy was explored for forming the organic/ferromagnet interface that incorporates a chemically inert h-BN buffer layer. This research therefore reveals opportunities for engineering ferromagnetic nanostructures and molecular spin transport layers for molecular spintronics devices.

600311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
600311.value: Wave propagation inside a material is governed by the “dispersion relation”, which is the relationship between frequency (ω) and wave-vector (k). In this proposal, we seek to develop photonic crystals with a “Dirac cone” dispersion at zero wave-vector (k=0). The most famous example of Dirac cone dispersions can be found in the electronic band structure of graphene (Nobel Prize 2010). It turns out that photonic crystals, which are man-made materials designed to control light, can also have Dirac cone dispersions and many novel phenomena have been proposed for such photonic systems. However, Dirac cones are typically found at a finite value of k. A Dirac cone dispersion at k=0 is difficult because the rule of symmetry tells us that the dispersion is generally quadratic at k=0 but a linear dispersion is needed to get a Dirac cone. We will see that we can find exceptions to that rule if we tune the material parameters so that there are “accidental degeneracies”. We will see that a Dirac cone at k=0 is different from the usual Dirac cones, and there will be some new Dirac cone physics that deserves exploration. More importantly, we will show that a subset of such photonic crystals have properties similar to a material with a zero refractive index. A zero-index material is one in which light passes through without any phase change. We note that light wave experiences a phase change even when it passes through vacuum, and, thus, a zero-index medium is in a sense emptier than vacuum at one frequency, and there are many novel properties one can explore with such a strange medium. In the past decade, we witnessed the emergence of a new class of materials called metamaterials, in which the refractive index can be engineered at will. One can create zero-index metamaterials, but metamaterials typically carry metallic resonators and metals have absorption. Our photonic crystals can deliver zero-index material without metals, which has the advantage of being low-loss and there is a road-map for dielectric photonic crystals to go up to optical frequencies, which would be a big challenge for metallic metamaterials. We will also show that with some modification, photonic crystals with a Dirac cone at k=0 may also mimic “complementary media”, a novel pair of materials which can optically cancel each other. “色散关系”，即频率(ω)和波矢量(k)之间的关系，决定了波在材料中的传播。在这个提案中，我们寻求发展在零波矢量点(k=0)具有“Dirac Cones”色散关系的光子晶体。自然界中，最著名的Dirac Cones色散关系是石墨烯(2010诺贝尔物理学奖)的电子带结构。控制光的人造材料-光子晶体-同样可以具有Dirac Cones色散关系，而且在这种光子系统中已经有很多新颖的现象被提出。然而Dirac Cones通常在有限的k值处被找到，要在k=0点实现Dirac Cones则是困难的。因为要得到Dirac Cones，色散需要是线性的，但是对称性规则告诉我们在k=0点色散普遍是二次的。我们将会看到如果我们调整材料参数从而实现“偶然简并”，该规则的例外情况可以被发现。我们还将看到在k=0处的Dirac Cones与通常的Dirac Cones不同，这里有新的Dirac Cones物理现象值得我们去探索。更重要的是，我们将展示这种光子晶体的一个子集性质类似于零折射率材料。光波通过零折射率材料时不会有任何的相位改变。我们注意到光波即使是通过真空其相位都会经历改变，在某种意义上零折射率材料在一个频率上比真空更空虚，因而人们可以探索这种奇怪介质的许多新奇的特性。在过去的十年中，我们目睹了超材料的出现，在这类新材料中折射率可以按照意愿来设计。人们可以制造零折射率的超材料，但是超材料通常由金属谐振器组成而金属是有吸收的。我们的光子晶体可以提供无金属的零折射率材料，它具有低损耗的优势并且成为介质光子晶体提升到光频的路线图，而对于金属超材料而言这是一个很大的挑战。我们还将展示通过一些修改，具有k=0点Dirac Cones的光子晶体也可以模仿“互补介质”，即一对可以光学地相互抵消的新奇材料。

600311.label: Realisation of objectives
600311.value: 1. We used theory and computation to theoretically design photonic crystals that have a Dirac cone at k=0. Examples of such systems are photonic crystals comprising a collection of dielectric cylinders arranged in square or hexagonal arrays. 2. We used such photonic crystals possessing conical dispersion at k=0 to realize low-loss double-zero-index materials. The connection between “double-zero”, meaning zero permittivity and permeability at the same frequency, is established using effective medium theory. The photonic systems are purely dielectric, and no metal is needed. As such, low-loss double-zero-index materials can be realized from microwave frequency up to optical frequencies. 3. We explored and demonstrated various novel phenomena associated with this class of material. Interesting phenomena include “wave front transformer” effects, cloaking inside channel effect and Klein tunneling. We also showed that Dirac cone at k=0 system can lead to robust interface states. 4. We experimentally realized such photonic crystals in the microwave frequency regime. Experimental demonstration of focusing and cloaking inside channel were demonstrated. 5. We realized the Dirac point at zone center and double-zero-index materials in other kinds of waves, such as the acoustic wave or elastic wave. In addition, we extended the concept of Dirac cone from two dimension to three dimension and we showed the Dirac cone at k=0 can be realized in some 3D photonic/phononic crystals.

600311.label: Major findings and research outcome
600311.value: We used band theory, group theory and numerical computation to theoretically design photonic crystals that have a Dirac cone at k=0. We showed that such conical dispersion can be realized by purposedly tuned accidental degeneracy at the zone center. Examples of such systems are photonic crystals comprising an array of dielectric cylinders arranged in square or hexagonal array. The accidental degeneracy (via tuning system parameters) of dipolar and monopolar Mie resonances can lead to a 3-fold degenerate state at k=0, two of each will give rise to conical dispersion (Dirac cone) with one additional flat band of quasi-longitudinal modes. We used such photonic crystals possessing conical dispersion at k=0 to realize low-loss double-zero-index materials. We showed that if the triply degenerate state is formed by monopole and dipole excitations, the system can be mapped to an effective medium with permittivity and permeability equal to zero simultaneously, and this system can transport wave as if the refractive index is effectively zero. The photonic systems are low-loss as they are purely dielectric, and no metal is needed. We also showed that such systems with cones at k=0 are different from standard pseudospin ½ Dirac cone systems at zone boundary (for example, the Berry phases are different). [See papers #2,5,6,8] We explored and demonstrated various novel phenomena associated with this class of material. Interesting phenomena include “wave front transformer” effects, cloaking inside channel effect and Klein tunneling. We also showed that Dirac cone at k=0 system can lead to robust interface states at the boundary between two photonic crystals that have system parameters that are slightly perturbed from the Dirac cone condition. We also found that index-near zero material can have very novel wave transport properties and can be used to control the flow of EM flux. [See papers #4,7,8,9,10] We realized the Dirac point at zone center and double-zero-index materials in other kinds of waves, such as the acoustic wave or elastic wave. Effective medium theory finds that acoustic crystals with Dirac point at k=0 can have effectively zero reciprocal of bulk modulus and zero mass density. Phononic crystals possessing Dirac cone dispersion at k=0 exhibit super-anisotropy, meaning that only transverse waves are allowed along certain directions, while only longitudinal waves are allowed along some other directions. Effective medium theory finds that such phononic crystals have effectively zero mass density and zero 1/C44 at the Dirac point. In addition, we showed that while Dirac cone dispersions can only be meaningfully defined in 2D systems, the notion of a Dirac point can be extended to 3D classical wave systems. Using effective medium theory, we can map our structure to an isotropic zero refractive index material. We gave explicit design to realize the Dirac cone at k=0 can be realized in some 3D photonic/phononic crystals. [See papers #1,3,7]

600311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
600311.value: The Dirac cone dispersion in graphene can be mapped to a pseudospin 1/2 Hamiltonian. The Dirac cone at k=0 for classical waves possessing 3 degrees of freedom instead of two. The additional degree of freedom is due to the additional flat band cutting cross the conical point(corresponding to the double-zero frequency). Such system can be mapped to a pseudospin-1 Hamiltonian near the conical point. The physics related to this pseudospin-1 degree of freedom is worth exploring. It is worth going beyond periodic system and ask questions such as whether the conical dispersion at k=0 can be found in aperiodic systems such as quasi-crystalline environment. In addition, the transport properties of such system carrying conical dispersion should be worth investigating. These investigations are in progress.

600311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
600311.value: In recent years, the so-called “Dirac cone” have attracted a lot of attention in the science community. The Dirac cone is usually associated with graphene, which has novel electronic properties. Here, we explore the implication of “conical dispersions” in classical wave systems and see whether such systems can be designed, made and whether they have novel transport properties for light and waves. We succeeded in designing artificial systems which have conical dispersion at zero wave vectors. We further showed that this material has the very novel property of zero refractive index. The phase velocity of light inside the zero index material can approach infinity while the group velocity remains finite. This means that we have made a new medium in which light can travel without phase change. In some sense, such a medium is more "empty" than air as light will have a phase change even if it travels in air but light will have no phase change when it travels in a zero-index medium. Potential applications of these materials are diverse and include tailoring the phase pattern of radiation field, making light channels and bends of arbitrarily shapes, cloaking objects in channels, and building new types of resonant cavities.

600511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
600511.value: The goal of the proposed experimental research is to study the geometry dependence of Casimir forces using micromechanical devices. Casimir forces refer to the interactions between neutral conductors that arise from the changes in the quantum zero point energy in the presence of boundaries. Micromechanical devices are widely used as sensors and actuators in science and technology, from accelerometers to barcode scanners. Advances in microfabrication have produced ultra sensitive transducers, making it possible to explore novel interactions like the Casimir force with unprecedented sensitivity. On the other hand, the critical dimension and separation between certain commercial micromechanical components have already been reduced to the submicron scale. As miniaturization continues, a better understanding of the fundamental interactions between surfaces will be crucial for the successful fabrication and operation of micromechanical devices. The emphasis of the proposed research will be placed on revealing the strong dependence of the Casimir force on the shape of the interacting objects and the non-trivial interplay of such geometry effects with the optical properties of the material. A number of novel configurations will be measured, including parallel beams, beams with width smaller than the optical skin depth, two corrugated surfaces with arbitrary lateral shifts and interpenetrating geometries. Successful implementation of the proposed projects will not only verify the validity of various theoretical approaches, answer open questions and stimulate new theoretical research, but could also lead to new ways of controlling the Casimir interaction in micromechanical devices based on engineering the geometry of the interacting elements. The main technological innovation of the proposed projects involves the development of a new monolithic platform for Casimir force measurement where the force sensing element and the actuator that controls the separation are integrated on the same silicon chip. Since both the shape and the initial location of the interacting elements are defined by electron beam lithography, no external, manual alignment is required. Such capability will allow the measurement of the Casimir force between a wide range of nanostructured surfaces. The force sensitivity has already been verified in preliminary tests to be sufficient to detect the Casimir force. The PI has extensive experience with micromechanical devices and Casimir force measurements. Recently, his group demonstrated the geometry dependence of the Casimir force on a strongly deformed silicon surface. The PI will work closely with Prof. Johnson, a theorist at Massachusetts Institute of Technology, on the calculation of the Casimir force for novel geometries. 我們建議的實驗研究目標是運用微機械來研究卡西米爾力的幾何依賴性。卡西米爾力是指中性導體由於量子零點能量在邊界條件的變化之下而產生的相互作用。微機械在科學及技術領域均被廣泛應用作為感應器和傳動器，例如加速度計及條碼掃描儀等等。隨著半導體技術的進步，現今已可以生產超靈敏的傳感器，使探索新的作用力如“卡西米爾力” 成為可能。另一方面，坊間微機械元件之間的關鍵尺寸和距離已被降到低於微米的尺度。隨著小型化的繼續，使得更好地理解元件表面之間的根本相互作用成為微機械設備的成功製備和操作的關鍵。 我們建議研究的重點將放在卡西米爾力對相互作用對象的幾何形狀的強烈依賴性和此幾何效應與材料的光學特性之間重要的相互影響方面。實驗將會測量一些全新的結構形態，包括平行傳動桿及兩個波狀表面。擬議的研究項目若能成功，不僅可以驗證各種理論方法的有效性，解答各種未解決的問題，刺激新的理論研究，也能發展出一種通過幾何形狀來控制微機械器件間卡西米爾作用力的新途徑。 在技術創新方面，這計劃涉及發展一個測量卡西米爾力的新單片平台，使傳感元件和控制位移的執行器均集成在同一矽芯片上。兩者的形狀和初始位置都是由電子束光刻技術決定，無需外部或手動對齊。這種優勢將使測量多種類型的納米結構之間的卡西米爾力成為可能。初步測試中，已經驗證力的靈敏度足以探測到卡西米爾力。 主要研究者在微機械和卡西米爾力的測量上具有豐富的經驗。最近，他的研究組運用強烈變形的矽表面證實了卡西米爾力的幾何依賴性。主要研究者將與約翰遜教授（美國麻省理工學院的理論家）在對新的幾何結構之間的卡西米爾力的計算方面密切配合。

600511.label: Realisation of objectives
600511.value: During the reporting period, we carried out an investigation of the Casimir force on silicon components. We achieved the project objectives of developing an on-chip monolithic platform for measuring the Casimir force and studying the Casimir force between nanoscale corrugations. Our findings were presented in ten international conferences (1 plenary talk, 7 invited talks and 2 contributed talks) and published in Nature Communications and Physical Review A. The main technological innovation of the project involves the development of a new monolithic platform for Casimir force measurement where the force sensing element and the actuator that controls the separation are integrated on the same silicon chip. Both components were fabricated on the device layer of a silicon-on-insulator wafer by electron beam lithography followed by reactive ion etching. Movable silicon structures were then created by removing the silicon oxide underneath by hydrofluoric acid. The element for sensing the force is a doubly-clamped silicon beam that is 100 um long and ~ 1.42 um wide. It is excited into vibrations at small amplitudes by an ac current that generates a periodic Lorentz force in a magnetic field. By measuring the change in its resonance frequency, we infer the force gradient exerted on the beam. A silicon electrode of width 2.80 um is located close to the beam. Electrostatic and/or Casimir forces are exerted by the electrode on the beam depending on the voltage between them. The electrode is attached to a comb actuator so that it can be controllably moved towards the beam, reducing the separation d between the electrode and the beam from an initial distance of 1.92 um down to ~ 260 nm while maintaining parallelism. Measurements were performed at liquid helium temperature in a magnetic field of 5T. We also studied the Casimir force in nanoscale corrugations. A device with nanoscale corrugations on the beam and the movable electrode was designed and fabricated. The Casimir force between the nanostructured components was then measured using the monolithic platform. Furthermore, we work with our theory collaborators to compare calculations with measurements of the Casimir force on nanostructured surfaces. The problems encountered and solved include the imperfect etching profile of the silicon sidewall, detecting a small force on a silicon beam, controlling the distance between the two silicon structures and maintaining their parallelism, and minimizing the electrostatic forces due to trapped charges in the buried oxide layer.

600511.label: Major findings and research outcome
600511.value: The findings include demonstration that the Casimir force measured with the on-chip platform agrees well with theoretical predictions, provided that effects of patch potentials were taken into account. Our experiment showed for the first time that the Casimir force can be the dominant interaction between silicon micromechanical components on an integrated micromechanical chip, in the absence of external objects. Prior to our experiment, all measurements of Casimir force involve an external object that must be aligned and positioned close to either cantilevers or torsional balances. Bulky micropositioners and piezoelectric actuators are required to control the separation between the two interacting bodies. Such arrangements have hindered progress in the on-chip exploitation of the Casimir force. Conventional experimental setups also face a number of other challenges. For instance, maintaining the parallelism of two flat surfaces at small distances has proven to be difficult. In our experiment, both the force sensing element and the actuator that controls the distance are integrated on the same substrate. They are created by dry etching that produces sidewalls that are largely vertical. No external alignment of the interacting bodies is necessary because they are defined in a single lithographic step. The use of electron beam lithography ensures a high degree of parallelism between the interacting bodies in a near-planar geometry. Furthermore, this scheme also allows tailoring of the Casimir force in the future using lithographically defined components of non-conventional shapes. Our study of the Casimir force between nanostructured surfaces show that the nanoscaled corrugations can enhance the thermal contributions to the Casimir force and make the thermal corrections appear at shorter distances where the force is stronger. This finding provides an alternative approach to study thermal Casimir forces without having to reach separations on the order of micrometers where measurements are difficult due to the small magnitude of the force.

600511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
600511.value: Our results represent the first step towards on-chip exploitation of the Casimir force. The compact and integrated actuation and detection platform provides new opportunities of tailoring the Casimir force using geometry effects. Structures are defined by electron beam lithography, making it possible to create surfaces with complex shapes that are automatically aligned after fabrication. The research will be carried on to the next phase to investigate non-monotonic Casimir forces in a modified glide symmetric geometry, to design structures that can explore Casimir forces for two interpenetrating corrugations and to design a bridge capable of measuring the difference in the Casimir force on two types of surfaces.

600511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
600511.value: While it is well-known that opposite charges attract or repel each other, quantum electrodynamics predict that electrically neutral conducting surfaces also attract each other, leading to a measurable force called the “Casimir force” when the separation is reduced below a micrometer. The Casimir force arises from the changes in the quantum zero point energy in the presence of boundaries. Micromechanical devices are small, movable structures created with integrated circuits technology. They are widely used as sensors and actuators in science and technology, from accelerometers to barcode scanners. The critical dimension and separation between certain commercial micromechanical components have already been reduced to the submicron scale. As miniaturization continues, a better understanding of the fundamental interactions between surfaces will be crucial for the successful fabrication and operation of micromechanical devices. The research project demonstrates for the first time that the Casimir force can be the dominant interaction between silicon micromechanical components on an integrated micromechanical chip, without the need of positioning external objects close to the micromechanical force detector. The new measurement platform could also lead to new ways of controlling the Casimir interaction in micromechanical devices based on engineering the geometry of the interacting elements.

600711.value: 五次三維流形的 “卡拉比－丘” 和 “Landau－Ginburg ” 對應

600711.label: Project Objectives
600711.value: We will study the Landau Ginzburg model [C^5/Z^5] with A4 superpotential starting with the moduli of spin structures on orbi-curve constructed by Fan-Jarvis-Ruan and Chiodo-Ruan. We will construct the moduli of spin sections over the moduli of spin curves. In the case of genus being equal to 1 and arbitrarily marked points we describe the deformation theory and intrinsic normal cone of the spin-section moduli space. We will separate the components of the intrinsic normal cone into pieces. The main component forms one piece and boundary components form different pieces. We will apply the new methods of cosection localization to substitute the pertubation of Witten equation in FJRW theory. This way we can construct the contribution from each component to the FJRW invariant. We shall prove relations among these component-wise virtual class which are stated in Jarvis' conjecture. By studying the geometry of the cone we will represent the contribution from each boundary component as Euler class of Hodge bundle, psi and Kappa classes. For the main component we will use Euler class of bundle stacks and apply the modular blow of Zinger-Vakil and Hu-Li to define it. If possible we shall represent the contribution as Kappa and psi classes. We can take intersections of the class computed in objective 3 with itself five times and compute the genus one FJRW invariant. We can also develop the algebraic geometric tool for another group ( Ruan and Chiodo) to accomplish this self-intersection computation. After that their group will package the genus one partition function and compare it with quintic genus one partition function under the Chiodo-Ruan transformation formula. We will compare our GSW model with the quintic g=1 GW in geometry. Namely, we will prove the Li-Zinger conjecture for g=1 in GSW model. We shall look for conjectural relation for g=1 FJRW theory as well, by comparing the g=1 GSW model with the result from objective 4. We will look for a geometric link between FJRW and GSW theory in genus zero and one. We will look for moduli that connect the moduli of stable map to P^4 and the moduli of spin structure in FJRW theory. The deformation theory and virtual cycle shall be studied to form a blueprint to link the partition functions. This is the long-term goal.

600711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
600711.value: In this proposal we plan to study the transformation from Gromov Witten theory of Quintic Calabi Yau threefold to the FJRW theory of the respective Hybrid-Landau Ginzburg space. In mathematics physics, Edward Witten proposed a link between the two theories by a theory named Gauged Linear Sigma Model. The link thus proposed is based on the assumption that infinited dimensional path integral is well defined. Such an assumption requires correction by mathematics where the issue of renormalization and phase transition should both have a mathematical parallel formulation. This proposal is based on (1)a new observation to interprete FJRW theory by the method of cosection localization in Algebraic geometry (2)a new ingredient in study Gromov Witten invariant of quintic hypersurface named p-field. The first technique enables us to make all Landau Ginzburg theory in GLSM rigorous. The second objective enables us to substitute GW theory for quintic by a specific Landau Ginzburg theory appearing in GLSM program. Hence, overall, we are in a right position to geometrically explain the CY-LG correspondence, which is the goal of this proposal. 在這份計畫中我們針對 五次三維的“卡拉比－丘流形” 研究其 “Gromov-Witten不變量” 以及 對該流形的 “Landau－Ginzburg相點” 研究其 “Fan-Jarvis-Ruan-Witten 奇點不變量” 之間的聯繫。 在數學物理中 Edward Ｗitten 提出了一個藍圖以便連結上述的兩種不變量理論。 該藍圖的名稱為 “規範線性 sigma 模式”。 該模式的提出建立在“無線維路徑積分的收斂性”這個公理之上，而此公理只有在數學物理中被承認，在嚴格的數學理論中卻不能被使用。 如果要在嚴格的數學理論中建立類似的藍圖，那該模式中的 “重整化”和 “相變”必須也有對應的嚴格數學理論。 這份計畫的提出是根據研究者之前發現的 （1） 代數幾何中“障礙叢泛函局部化” 的技術可以被用來嚴格定義並處理 “Fan-Jarvis-Ruan-Witten 奇點不變量” （2）一種新的被稱為“p-場”的模空間技術可以被用來處理 五次三維的“卡拉比－丘流形” 的 “Gromov-Witten不變量”。 前者讓我們可以嚴格地處理 “Landau－Ginburg” 種類的 “規範線性 sigma 模式”。 後者使我們可以把五次三維的“卡拉比－丘流形” 的 “Gromov-Witten不變量” 表達為 一種特別的 “Landau－Ginburg” 形態的 “規範線性 sigma 模式”。 因此我們有希望建立 “卡拉比－丘 Gromov-Witten不變量”” 與 “Landau－Ginburg 相點的 Fan-Jarvis-Ruan-Witten 不變量” 之間的對應， 這便是本計畫的目標。

600711.label: Realisation of objectives
600711.value: The projects' goal is to establish algorithm for positive genus FJRW invariants of quintic singularity. The original proposal, as above objectives 2-5 is to imitate the study of genus one GW invariants via moduli spaces, to see what similars can happen for genus one FJRW cases. During the time of this project, PI and collaborators found a more general and universal proposed method , different from the one outline in above objectives 2-5, to fulfill the goal of enumerating the invariants, in ALL genus(i.e. the final goal objective 7). Thus it becomes more effective than the original proposal and surprisingly, provide more outcome as it also determine the quintic GW invariants to ALL genus, which is the ultimate difficult open problem in the field. For this reason PI and collaborators bypassed part of the proposed sequence of objectives 2-4 above, and head directly to the ultimate objective 6 with our new method: MSP moduli. This word MSP means Mixed Spin P fields, a combination of the ideas realized in moduli spaces. We used the grant to work on all details of this MSP (Mixed Spin P) moduli space. For example we showed it has degeneracy loci to be proper, and therefore can be used to extract invariants including those objective 2-5 above aimed to calculate. We spent two years on its setup in rigorous math foundations, and since then provided algorithms as like localization computation technique, Grothendieck Riemann Roch, e.t.c. to extract invariants out of the MSP setup (moduli). This outcome was not expected in the beginning of the project. In conclusion the last objectives in 5.1, namely " looking for a geometric link between FJRW and GSW theory in genus zero and one, i.e. a moduli that connect the moduli of stable map to P^4 and the moduli of spin structure in FJRW theory", is found (the MSP moduli). We achieve this ultimate objective 7 without passing into the objectives 2-5. For example, following the method stated in objective 4 above in 5.1, the other group of Y.B. Ruan take intersections of the class computed in objective 3 with itself five times and proposed this algorithm to compute the genus one FJRW invariant. However during this project this invariant is shown by PI's new proposal to be determined by MSP program, and the method is much more effective. Therefore the objective 4 above is achieved by the alternate MSP program. For each item in the objectives 5.2, we accomplish the following parts. 1. We construct the moduli of spin sections over the moduli of spin curves. For general cases we describe the deformation theory of the spin-section moduli space. 2. We did not do the separation of main component cone since it only works for genus one case. Instead our MSP algorithm head for all genus. 3. By studying the geometry of the cone, another group of Y.B. Ruan tried to capture contribution from each boundary component using the techniques of Pixton. 4. The group of Y.B. Ruan take intersections of the class computed in objective 3 with itself five times and proposed this algorithm to compute the genus one FJRW invariant. However this invariant is shown by PI's new proposal determined by MSP proposal. 5. We compare g=1 GSW model with the genus one FJRW invariants. This is done in the end of our paper . arXiv:1603.02092. 6. We found geometric link between FJRW and GSW theory in all genus, which is a moduli that connect the moduli of stable map to P^4 and the moduli of spin structure in FJRW theory.

600711.label: Major findings and research outcome
600711.value: The PI and collaborators found a moduli space of so called Mixed Spin P(MSP) field. or a geometric link between FJRW and GSW theory in full genus. This is the major finding of the project. It enables us to solve the ultimate question to enumerate quintic's invariants, which in the list of old objectives of the proposal are suggested to follow old complicated approach. Now that this new discovery of new construction, MSP field, the problem of all genus Gromov Witten invariants of quintics, and also the all genus FJRW invariants of quintics, can be achieved by recursive algorithm. It reduces one of the most difficult question in enumerative geometry to one algorithm package.

600711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
600711.value: The MSP method has hope to be adapted to other stabilities condition which then led to right approach to various other interesting problems related to the original one. For example it would have decisive counterpart in the stable quotient or quasimap theory for quintics. Also it may be applied to attack Virasoro conjecture for hypersurfaces. The MSP moduli also gives experience to us to extend it to negative stabilities as 0- stability. It also hints on how to setup the construction of broad sector theory in future. The discovery of MSP moduli therefore has great potential and expected large amount of application in future. We shall follow the above mentioned extensions and expand the theory to other fields.

600711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
600711.value: The string theory proposed that our universe is 10 dimensional. Other than the 4 dimensional space time there is an additional internal space of six dimension, called "Calabi Yau CY manifold". The physics we see in 4 dimensional time are consequences of interactions of strings inside this 6 dimensional internal CY manifold. One typical interaction is the the Gromov Witten invariants. This research is aimed to calculate such invariants for a typical kind of internal CY manifold, the "Quintic". This problem has been open for more than twenty years and is one of the main goal in the subject of enumerative geometry. Our project proposed to utilize different "moduli space technique", to approach this calculation. For example the "conformal field theory moduli" or "phase transition" were techinique we developed in pure math from physics idea. These machinery enables us to approach the difficult problem enumerative Gromov Witten invariants. Our long sequences of approaches and discoveries would make pure mathematics useful for physics world. They will also be extended to attack invariants other than Gromov Witten kind, by the community. They will also stimulate the interaction with other enumerating theories of different shape, as like Gauge theories.

600811.label: Project Objectives
600811.value: Arrangement of Finitely Generated Abelian Groups: Construct a universal valuation (finitely additive measure) with polynomial values on the Boolean algebra generated by cosets of subgroups of a fixed finitely generated abelian group. Introduce characteristic polynomial for group arrangement so the universal valuation of the complement of the arrangement is the introduced characteristic polynomial. Find possible combinatorial interpretations for the rational coefficients of the characteristic polynomial. Lattice Arrangements of the Rational Vector Space: Construct a universal valuation with polynomial values on the Boolean algebra generated by the affine sub-lattices of the rational Euclidean space. Introduce characteristic polynomial for the lattice arrangements with rational coefficients. Find possible combinatorial and geometric interpretations for the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial. Cartesian Product Arrangements: Construct product Boolean algebra and a universal valuation with multivariable polynomial values on the Boolean algebra of product flats of the product space of finitely generated abelian groups. Introduce multivariable characteristic polynomial for Cartesian product arrangements. Give possible combinatorial and geometric interpretations for the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial. Arrangements of Special linear Group over Integers: Find the counting patterns for the finitely generated subgroups of the special linear group SL(2,Z) over the ring of integers. Construct Riemann surfaces for the Cayley graphs induced from the Cayley graphs of SL(2,Z) by a finite set S of generators. Compute the genus of the Riemann surfaces constructed from the Cayley graphs.

600811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
600811.value: 线性子空间层的布局是近些年来活跃的研究课题. 这种研究使得离散数学(又称组合数学)中的某些基本问题得到了统一处理. 比如, 子空间层布局的特征多项式完美的统一处理了图论中的色多项式和流多项式. 但是, 当色多项式和流多项式在拟阵上讨论时, 我们会遇到挠率; 然而子空间层布局的特征多项式未能反映挠率现象. 因此, 我们需要引进子群层布局和其上的特征多项式. 本课题正是展开子群层布局的理论研究和应用, 并侧重于以下四个方面: 1. 有限生成阿贝尔群上的布局; 2. 有理线性空间上的几何格布局; 3. 卡氏积空间布局; 4. 整数环上线性群的布局以及在有限群上的模定.

600811.label: Major findings and research outcome
600811.value: (a) For finitely generated abelian group, we first introduced the relative Boolean algebra generated by taking intersection, union, and relative complement of cosets of subgroups of a given finitely generated abelian group. Next we constructed a unique valuation (finitely additive measure) on the relative Boolean algebra of a finitely generated abelian group such that the measure of a subgroup is the cardinality of the whole group divided by the cardinality of the quotient group of the whole group modulo the subgroup, where the cardinality of a subgroup is the cardinality of its torsion group times a variable whose power is the rank of the given subgroup. (b) For the lattice arrangements of the rational vector space, we have constructed a universal valuation with polynomial values on the Boolean algebra generated by the affine sub-lattices of the rational Euclidean space. We also introduced a characteristic polynomial for the lattice arrangements with rational coefficients. (c) For the Cartesian product arrangements, we constructed product Boolean algebra and a universal valuation with multinomial values on the Boolean algebra of product flats of the product of finitely generated abelian groups, we also introduced a multivariable characteristic polynomial for Cartesian product arrangements, and provided a combinatorial interpretation for the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial. (d) For arrangements of special linear group over integers, we found some counting patterns for the finitely generated subgroups of the special linear group SL(2,Z) over the ring of integers. We tried to construct Riemann surfaces from the Cayley graphs induced from the Cayley graphs of SL(2,Z) by a finite set of generators, all related results are not yet finalized. We obtained partial results such as computing the genus of the Riemann surfaces constructed from the Cayley graphs.

600811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
600811.value: The arrangements considered in the current project are usually some linear arrangements in vector spaces, finitely genrated abelian groups, Cartesian product spaces, and the modulo linear group SL(n,R). The potential for further development is certainly non-linear arrangements. The non-linear case is completely different from the linear case; it is much more difficult than the linear case, since there is no good specific method and technique to treat general patterns of hypersurfaces. A special type of non-linear arrangements is worth of a close look, that is, the toric arrangements. A toric arrangement is a finite collection of hypersurfices defined by monomial equations over the field of complex numbers and the field of real numbers. The four aspects of the current project can be considered for toric arrangements. New methods and techniques need be developed; certanly new results are espected. We plan to submit a future proposal to further studty toric arrangements.

600811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
600811.value: Measuring the size of a geometric figure such as a finite collection of hyperplanes is a fundamental problem in mathematics. Viewed as a set of points in a space, the set of such geometric object is usually infinite and it cannot be measured by counting its number of points. Instead, we consider the measure of a line as a symbol t, the measure of plane as the square of the symbol t, and the measure of a 3 dimensional subspace as the cubic power of the symbol t, etc. By using additivity, productivity, and invariance under rigid motion, we obtain a universal rigid motion invariant valuation which takes each geometric object (obtained from planes by taking union, intersection, and complement finitely many times) to a polynomial of the symbol t with integer coefficients. Along the way of the formal measurement under the rules of additivity, productivity and invariance above, we further studied the cases of finding measurements for the sets generated by union, intersection, and relative complement of cosests of a finitely generated abelian group. The measurement turns out to be a rigid motion invariant valuation whose values are polynomials with rational coefficients whose coefficients have combinatorial and geometric interpretations.

601011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
601011.value: In the past two years, the world has experienced a financial and economic crisis triggered by the collapse of some too-big-to-fall financial institutions. So far there have been numerous financial and economic analyses and models calibrating these ground-shaking events and their causes. In the eyes of statisticians, they illuminate the importance of statistical analysis of time-to-events, which aims at understanding and explaining the events occurrence and their relationships with many existing factors, called covariates in statistical terms. Indeed, time-to-event data are very common in biomedical, economic and social studies. The treatment effects of many diseases are evaluated in terms of the patients' survival times as time-to-events. The risk of company bankruptcy/insolvency as a time-to-event is a major concern of investors and creditors. But the time-to-event data are very commonly subject to right censoring. The increasing complexity of event-causing mechanisms, as in the current financial crisis, calls for the development of broader statistical models and finer methodologies. Transformation models are probably the most general statistical models for the analysis of time-to-event data. The popular models in survival analysis, such as Cox's model, can be viewed as special cases of transformation models. Transformation models may be separated into two categories, one with known or specified error distribution and the other unspecified. The latter, being broader than the former, will be the subject of this proposed research. Such transformation models are sometimes called generalized accelerated failure time (GAFT) models. This proposed project will focus on finding methods which achieve accurate estimation for such models with censored data. We intend to employ a counting process martingale-based methodology or likelihood methods that are common and powerful tools in survival analysis. However, their application to GAFT models is rather difficult. There are two nonparametric components in such models: the unknown monotonic transformation function and the unknown error distribution. A major complication arises from the latter. It is likely that curve estimation techniques such as kernel estimation will be involved. In view of the importance of transformation models, we believe the methods of handling the nonparametric components perfected in this project will be applicable to other types of statistical models and should have far-reaching impact. The output of this project will provide a useful statistical tool for evaluating and understanding the relationship between covariates and event occurrences. 过去两年，世界经历了由“大到不能倒”的金融公司的倒闭而触发的一轮金融和经济危机。至今已有很多关于这些震撼性事件及其原因的模型和分析。从统计学家的观点来看，这些现象反映了时间与事件的统计分析的重要性，因为这些分析着眼于理解和解释事件的发生及他们与很多其他因素的关系。时间与事件的数据在生物医学，经济和社会学研究中极为普遍。治疗效果常常以病人的生存时间为依据。公司的倒闭的风险是投资者和债权人关注的时间事件。时间事件经常出现右删失。导致事件发生的机制的复杂性，正像目前的金融危机，需要发展更为广泛的统计模型和更精细的方法。变换模型可能是统计中最为一般的用于分析时间事件的模型。它可分为两类：已知误差分布和未知误差分布。后者更为一般， 也是我们研究的课题。它也叫做广义加速度失败时间模型。本项研究将着重寻找达到极高精确度的估计方法。我们将利用生存分析中的计数过程鞅和似然方法。这些应用将会有一定的困难。因为有两种非参数成分：变换函数和误差分布。 主要困难来自后者。曲线估计的技巧可能在此很有用。从变换模型的重要性来看，我们相信此项研究中发展的处理非参数成分的方法可应用于其他统计模型并产生深远的影响。 此项研究的成果将对理解和评估协变量和事件发生之间的关系提供有用的统计工具。

601011.label: Realisation of objectives
601011.value: The primary objectives of this research are the analysis of transformation models with unknown distribution and its application to broader types of data more general than the traditional right censored data. We have conducted extensive research towards the objectives of this research. With unknown error distribution, the transformation models are broad enough to cover linear regression models, the Cox model and the proportional odds model as special cases. We found that the extended methods based on the maximum rank correlation can be successfully applied to various forms of data that are put into the framework of response-biased sampling. With mild conditions on the censoring or truncation variables, such response-biased data include as special cases the truncated data and right censored data. These types of data are very common in survival analysis. Except for the case-control logistic regression, there is no report in the literature that a prospective estimation approach can work for biased sampling without any modification. It is theoretically proved that the maximum rank correlation estimation is valid for such response biased sampling. The consistency and asymptotic normality are rigorously established. Unlike the inverse probability methods, the proposed method of estimation does not involve the sampling probabilities, which are often difficult to obtain in practice. For the numerical computation, without the need of estimating the unknown transformation function or the error distribution, the proposed method is numerically easy to implement with the Nelder-Mead simplex algorithm, which does not require convexity or continuity. The inference procedure using random weighting to avoid the complication of density estimation when using the plug-in rule for variance estimation. Numerical studies with supportive evidence are presented. We also applied our methodology to the Forbes Global 2000 data and the Stanford heart transplant data. For transformation model without censoring, it has not been theoretically proved that the maximum likelihood estimator is consistent and asymptotically normal. The main difficulty lies in the large error of estimation of the transformation function near positive and negative infinity. We proved that, with minimum condition on the error distribution, the maximum likelihood estimator is indeed consistent and asymptotic normal.

601011.label: Major findings and research outcome
601011.value: One of the major findings is that the maximum rank correlation method with little modification works for a broad class of data. The method is very simple since it does not rely on estimating the transformation function or the error distribution. Though the method itself is not originally discovered by us, we are the first to show that it can be applied to censored data, truncated data, case-control data and case-cohort data. The existing methods in survival analysis usually take advantage of the error distribution, which is assumed known. When the assumption of the error distribution is violated, these methods will lead to large bias. In this sense, the rank based methods have the advantage of robustness. We have not only proved theoretically that the rank based methods are valid for the response biased sampling. We also conducted extensive simulation to investigate the performance of the methods with finite sample. The simulation results provide positive evidence. Moreover, we find that the Nelder-Mead approach works for rank methods with reasonably large sample size at hundreds, even though the estimating functions are not continuous. For larger sample size at thousands or beyond, some smoothed version of rank estimation can be considered. The results are summarized in a paper, which is under review for publication in Statistica Sinica. It is notoriously difficult to show the maximum likelihood estimation is valid for transformation model without censoring. The unknown monotone transformation function ranges between negative infinity and positive infinity. In other words, the transformation function is unbounded. Without censoring, the estimation accuracy of the transformation function near infinity must be assessed, since it will in turn affect the estimation accuracy of the regression parameter. This is a technically quite challenging problem. With some nontrivial technical development, we are able to show positively that the maximum likelihood estimator of the regression parameter is consistent and asymptotically normal, under a broad class of error distributions. These results are summarized in a a manuscript which is submitted to the Annals of Statistics for publication.

601011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
601011.value: In theory, the most accurate estimator of the regression parameter for transformation model with unknown error distribution should still be the maximum likelihood estimator, but with the additional step of estimating the density of the error distribution. So far we have not been able to prove that, with unknown error distribution, the maximum likelihood estimation is still valid for transformation model. The main difficulties are the smoothing of the density estimation of the error distribution and how it affects the parameter estimation. We have carried out simulations, but the results are not all positive. The experience that we accumulate in this research may help us solve this problem in the future. We plan to continue our investigation on this problem.

601011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
601011.value: Survival analysis and econometrics are major branches of statistical science and economics. Transformation model is one of the most widely used regression models in survival analysis and econometrics. The most popular model in survival analysis, such as Cox's model or proportional odds model, are special cases of transformation model with known error distribution. More general transformation models, called generalized accelerated failure time models, are those with unknown error distributions that are particularly useful in econometric studies. We have shown that the rank based methods for transformation are applicable to a broad class of biased data that include censoring, truncation, case-control, case-cohort and length biased or size biased sampling. Moreover, for transformation model with known error distribution and without censoring, we proved theoretically that the maximum likelihood method is valid.

601111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
601111.value: In 1873 H. A. Schwarz solved L. Fuchs’s problem of characterizing when the Gauss hypergeometric equation admits a full set of algebraic solutions, that is, those solutions satisfy an algebraic equations. The Gauss Eqn includes differential equations such as the Hermite, Laguerre, Legender, Chebyshev, Ultraspherical, confluent hypergeometric, Bessel, Airy Eqn, etc which are amongst the most important ordinary differential equations known in the complex plane. The algebraic solutions include many classically known eigen-solutions of these important DEs. Schwarz’s list of admissible parameters was later simplified by F. Klein (1877), which is equivalent to having a finite projective monodromy group. The Heun equation and its confluent forms play an analogous role for many mathematical physics equations at an higher level than the Gauss equation. They are much more difficult to deal with when compared to the Gauss equations. For example, the same problem for the Lamé Eqn, a special case of Heun Eqn which has one more singular point, and thus immediately more general than the Gauss Eqn, is still a work in progress. Just like the Gauss Eqn, the equations in the Heun family found applications in numerous areas such as (band-limited) signal transmission, fluid mechanics, thermal diffusion, wave (quantum) mechanics, general relativity (black holes), etc. It is known that the equations at the Heun level not only admit polynomial-type eigen-solutions, but also eigen-solution in finite combination of transcendental functions at “lower level” which differ markedly from the classical eigen-value problems at the hypergeometric level. We call all these “finite-form solutions”. Thus, algebraic-geometric approach may not be effective. We propose to develop complex function theoretic methods to study more general finite-form solutions for the Heun Eqn. In particular, the PI and his coworkers have successfully applied the value distribution theory to study the special cases of the Gauss Eqn. in which known orthogonal polynomials were rediscovered from the Nevanlinna theory (Bank & Laine) approach. Recently, this approach allows the PI & G. Yu to discover new orthogonal polynomials to a transcendental form of the Biconfluent Heun Eqn. However, Bank & Laine’s theory does not distinguish the transcendental finite-form solutions. We propose to further develop suitable function theoretic tools to identify these important finite-form (transcendental or polynomial-types) solutions of the Heun equations. 此計畫以現代復變函数論來研究Heun微分方程的精确解及相关特殊函数的性质。Heun方程乃一在復平面上有四個正則奇點的線性微分方程，其四個正則奇點比極奇重要的高斯超几何微分方程多出一個正則奇點。高斯方程包含很多在數學物理中的特殊函数如厄密方程、勒讓德方程、貝塞耳方程等；我们對高斯方程的理解也比較全面，但我们對 Heun 方程的理解則顯得不足，其原因為Heun 方程遠比高斯方程复杂，其中著名方程拉梅方程為Heun方程的特殊形式，並有接近一百八十年的歷史，但我们對其還仍不十分理解。Heun方程和它一些特殊形式在應用中經常踫到，但因為我们對其不了解，所以在應用計萛上遇上很大困难，即使有高速運萛的電惱也不一定解決困難。基於我們早前成功地用复變函数論來研究合流超几何微分方程，故我們提意用現代复變函数論來研究 Heun 方程的特殊解。

601111.label: Realisation of objectives
601111.value: Let me rephrase the finite-form solutions problem of the Heun equation which is the main interest of this project by recalling a classical result of T. Kimura (Funk. Ekv. Vol. 12, (1969), 269-281). First we say that a DE is “reducible” if the DE has a “degenerate solution”, i.e., a solution whose logarithmic derivative is rational. Given a fundamental set of a DE, we consider differential field L=K, i.e., the smallest differential field generated by adjunction of {a, b} to the differential field K, called the Picard-Vessiot extension of K. The “differential Galois group” of L over K is defined to be the group of all automorphisms of L leaving K fixed. Further a differential field L is a “Liouville extension” of field K if there exists a chain of intermediate differential fields satisfying certain differential properties (which we omit). It is well-known that L is a generalized Liouville extension of K if and only if the differential Galois group of L over K with respect to {a, b} has the solvable connected component of the identity. Let L be a Picard-Vessiot extension of K for Gauss’s equation. Kimura’s result states that the necessary and sufficient conditions for the Picard-Vessiot extension L of K for Gauss’s hypergeometric equation to be a generalized Liouvillian extension of K is either (i) that the linear sum/difference of the three exponential differences corresponding to the three regular singular points of Gauss equation, is an odd integer, or (ii) that the three exponent differences are amongst the famous Schwarz’s list for algebraic solutions (with one exception). The case (i) corresponds to the hypergeometic equation to admit Jacobi polynomial solutions. That is, when the differential Galois group of Gauss’s equation has a solvable component, the monodromy of the DE degenerates so that the DE admits degenerate solutions. I have identified at the very last project duration period that our finite-form solutions problem correspond to part (i) of Kimura’s theorem for Heun equation with an appropriate accessory parameter (and sometimes with Stokes data). However, one needs more than Liouvillian solutions, as in the case of hypergeometric equation, in order to describe the structure/variety of the finite-form solutions for the Heun equations. This corresponds to a major revision of research methodology for this project. In short, we are able to show that the equivalence between complex non-oscillatory solutions to some Heun equations are precisely the solutions obtained by Picard-Vessiot extensions.

601111.label: Major findings and research outcome
601111.value: I believe I have met most of the four objectives in 5.1 above although there is a substantial deviation from the original approach, as mentioned in 5.3. We have established that in each case where a finite-form solution arises, it corresponds to a complex non-oscillatory solution in Bank-Laine theory for some Hill’s equations which are periodic Heun equations (objective 3). Objective 1: Publication 2 from Part C: We have extended the work of Ince (1940) in finding infinite series expansion solutions in terms of Jacobi elliptic functions for Lame’s equation to Darboux’s equation. Moreover, we have worked out the symmetry group of the Darboux equation, thus extending the work of Maier (2006) on Heun’s equation. Infinite expansion solutions in terms of general hypergeometric solutions (2F1) will be prepared in connection with Galiosian approach. Publication 4 of Part C (still under preparation): we have derived infinite series expansions solutions for the Whittaker-Hill (WH-) equation (CHE) in terms of Laguerre polynomials (special form of 1F1, the confluent hypergeometric functions). They play the role of general solutions to the WH-equation. This greatly extends the work of Ince (1923) about “normalized solutions” (i.e., solutions that satisfy both initial (i.e., even/odd) and (semi-)periodic conditions) of the WH-equation. Objective 2: We have established a Wiman-Valiron type estimate for infinite 1F1 expansions for the WH-equation which includes “central index/maximum terms” and use them to compute the growth order and exponent of convergence of zeros. This will be prepared as a sequel to Publication 4. Objective 3: Publication 3 is currently being revised to include Kovacic’s algorithm to compute the differential Galois group for biconfluent Heun equation (BHE). This would reinforce an analogue of Bessel polynomials for BHE found using purely Bank-Laine (complex oscillation) theory as in the current draft. Publication 4 shows that semi-finite gap solutions of the WH-equation arise if and only if they are the non-oscillatory solution (Bank-Laine theory) that satisfies both the initial and periodic boundary conditions (see sections 4 and 6). In particular, they assume the form finite 1F1 sum (cf Objective 1 above). Objective 4: Publication 3: We have found a complex orthogonality weight for the analogue of Bessel polynomials for the BHE. But we still need to revise that for the periodic BHE in the current revision. Publication 4: Section 5 establishes orthogonality of the finite-Laguerre polynomial (composed with exponentials) which plays the role of semi-finite gap solutions.

601111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
601111.value: As already mentioned the Galoisian interpretation is vital to the study of Heun and even hypergeometric equations as some of the most fundamental models (i.e., Legendre, Laguerre and Hermite equations) admit eigen-polynomial solutions (in L^2 sense) when their respective differential Galois group becomes solvable. We are dealing with case (i) of Kimura (see 5.3). We have purposely omitted some findings that we reported earlier concerning these infinite or finite hypergeometric (both polynomial and non-polynomial) sums. This is because each sum represents different monodromy. Termination at different “lengths” in a hypergeometric sum represents different entities in the same isomorphism class of a suitably constructed D-module. Sometimes the monodromy of the Heun equation is identical with that of the hypergeometric equation (with apparent singularities), but sometimes it is not. The symmetry group (publication 2) action can only transform terminated solutions (of suitable accessory parameters) of one monodromy type to terminated solutions of the same type. Transformation between terminated solutions of different monodromy type can only be achieved by “fractional derivatives” which are very far from being understood. These fascinating issues will be pursued in a newly funded GRF (2014-17) and a newly applied GRF (2015-16).

601111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
601111.value: We investigated several second order linear differential equations of very old and important physical origins, and of which are still greatly relevant to the discipline of pure and applied mathematics. Their solutions are amongst functions that are direct generalisations of the sine and cosine functions which many of us learnt in school, but their properties are much harder to understand. It is well-known that one can approximate a more complicated function in terms of a combination of infinitely many simpler functions (i.e., monomials {x^n}). We have demonstrated in this project that the solutions of the differential equations that we are interested in are more complicated, and require other families of functions at a next level of complexity other than monomials to approximate. We have consolidated such viewpoint using algebraic and function theories. In particular, these new approximations allow us to better describe the geometric properties (written in terms of monodromy and their differential Galois group) of the differential equations and their solutions. This geometric blueprint essentially determines the character of the differential equations and their solutions. We have used such new approximations to investigate certain spectra distribution of the differential operators and the orthogonality of the eigen-solutions.

601211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
601211.value: Palmyrolide A is a neuroactive 15-membered macrolide isolated from a cyanobacterial assemblage collected from Palmyra Atoll in the Northern Pacific Ocean. It consists of a novel ketide 7-hydroxy-5,8,8-trimethylnonanoic acid and 6-amino-2-methylhex-5-enoic acid. But the absolute configuration at C5 and C7 of the ketide has not been determined due to lack of suitable sample degradation method. Palmyrolide A is structurally related to the 15-membered laingolide family and the 17-membered madangolide, which commonly contain an enamide (or 1,3-dienamide) motif as part of the macrocyclic core. Stereochemistry of these macrolides has not been established as the result of limited quantities of available samples and instability of the macrolides during structural elucidation. Up to now, biological screening of these macrolides has not been performed except for a very preliminary study on neuroactivity of palmyrolide A. Interestingly, it exhibits significant inhibition of Ca2+ oscillations in murine cerebrocortical neurons with an IC50 value of 3.70 microM while being not cytotoxic to H-460 human lung adenocarcinoma cells up to 20 microM. For further pharmacological exploration on palmyrolide A and the related macrolides, efficient chemical synthesis processes are essential for accessing these novel molecular entities. As the first step toward the understanding of the mechanism of action, this proposed study focuses on development of efficient methods for synthesis of palmyrolide A and its structural analogues possessing 15- and 17-membered enamide macrocycle cores. Two methods are envisioned for investigation: (a) macroenamidation using the Cu-catalyzed intramolecular cross-coupling of amide with alkenyl iodide; and (b) ene–enanmide (or dienamide) ring-closing metathesis (RCM) catalyzed by Ru(II) alkylidene complexes. These two methods have so far been used in the synthesis of cyclopeptide alkaloids which feature a cis-enamide motif within 13- to 15-membered rings. It becomes much more challenging to construct the trans-enamide moiety required for palmyrolide A as the consequence of increased ring strain. The ene–dienamide RCM strategy has not been investigated in the literature so far. How to control the Z,Z-geometry in the dienamide motif is the key issue to be addressed. Therefore, this project will generate new chemistry on formation of the enamide-containing macrolide cores via macroenamidation and ene–enamide (or dienamide) RCM approaches. This should in turn lay down the chemical basis for synthesis and determination of the absolute configuration of palmyrolide A and for accessing to structural analogues of these macrolides for further biological studies. Palmyrolide A是從北太平洋小島Palmyra Atoll採集到的藍藻中分離到的、具神經活性的15元環內酯。它含有一個新的聚酮片斷，7-羥基5,8,8-三甲基壬酸，和6-氨基-2-甲基-己-5-烯酸，但是由於缺乏合適的樣本分解方法致使聚酮片斷C5和C7位的絕對構型未能確定。Palmyrolide A與15元環laingolide家族及17元環madangolide在結構上相關，其大環骨架均含有烯酰胺或1,3-二烯酰胺結構單元。由於缺乏足夠樣本或樣本在結構解析過程中不穩定等因素，這些大環內酯的立體化學都沒能建立。至今，除對palmyrolide A做過初步神經活性試驗，這些大環內酯的生物活性篩選尚未進行。有趣的是palmyrolide A對小鼠大腦皮層神經元中Ca2+ 濃度波動有明顯的抑製作用，IC50值為3.70 microM，但在高至20 microM以內它對 H-460 人肺腺癌細胞不顯示細胞毒性。Palmyrolide A及相關大環內酯的藥理學的進一步探索有賴於通過有效的化學合成工藝來提供這些新型分子實體。作為探索其作用機理的前提，本研究項目集中於發展合成palmyrolide A及其含烯酰胺結構15和17元環類似物的有效方法。我們將對兩種方法展開研究： （a）利用銅催化的分子內酰胺與烯基碘偶聯的大環烯酰胺化反應；及（b）通過烷基亞甲基Ru(II)絡合物催化的烯烴與烯酰胺或二烯酰胺的閉環復分解反應。到目前為止，這兩種方法僅限於合成含cis-烯酰胺的13或15元環肽生物鹼，由于環張力的增大，如用於構築含trans-烯酰胺單元的palmyrolide A就具有極大的挑戰性。烯烴與二烯酰胺的閉環復分解策略在文獻中至今尚未報道，如何控製形成的二烯酰胺單元所需的Z,Z-構型是本項目需要解決的關鍵課題。因此，本項目研究會豐富新化學知識，利用大環烯酰胺化和烯烴與烯酰胺或二烯酰胺的閉環復分解反應途經來形成含烯酰胺結構的大環內酯骨架，打好化學合成基礎將有利於通過palmyrolide A 的全合成來確立其絕對構型、並可得到這些大環內酯的結構類似物而開展進一步的生物學研究。

601211.label: Realisation of objectives
601211.value: Soon after we started our project in early 2012, the Maio’s group published the first total synthesis of palmyrolide A by using our proposed Cu-catalyzed macroenamidation method (Maio, W. A. et al., Org. Lett. 2012, 14, 2150–2153 & J. Org. Chem. 2012, 77, 6271–6289) and they revised the stereochemistry of (–)-palmyrolide A as (5R,7R,10R), which is different from (5R*,7S*,10R) as originally proposed (Gerwick, W. H., et al., Org. Lett. 2010, 12, 4490–4493). Since then, three other groups have published total synthesis of (–)-palmyrolide A and its diastereomers, including: (a) Brimble’s work using ring-closing metathesis (RCM)–alkene isomerization protocol (Brimble, M. A., et al., Org. Lett. 2012, 14, 5374–5377 & J. Org. Chem. 2014, 79, 11179–11193); (b) Sudhakar’s work using dehydrative cyclization (Sudhakar, G., et al., Tetrahedron 2013, 69, 2419–2429); and (c) Reddy’s work (Reddy, D. S., et al., Chem. Commun. 2013, 49, 3342–3344). Moreover, Maio’s group reported (–)-palmyrolide A and analogues as the voltage-gated sodium channel antagonists (Mehrotra, S., et al., J. Nat. Prod. 2014, 77, 2553–2560). We amended our synthesis plan stated in the objectives 1 and 2 after disclosure of the Maio’s work. We have now established a multimodule assembly strategy for diverted total synthesis of (–)-palmyrolide A and (5S,7S,10R)-isomer. Our synthesis relies on our Pd(OAc)2–Aphos-Y-catalyzed B-alkyl Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling and Brimble’s RCM–alkene isomerization. The objectives 3 and 4 are originally aimed for total synthesis and stereochemistry assignment of madangolide (Klein, D., et al., J. Nat. Prod. 1999, 62, 934–936). The task requires synthesis of EIGHT diastereomers. Due to shortage of manpower we selected the structurally closely related laingolide A (Klein, D., et al., Tetrahedron Lett. 1996, 37, 7519–7520 & J. Nat. Prod. 1999, 62, 934–936) as the target molecule. We have synthesized all FOUR possible diastereomers of laingolide A and determined its relative configuration as (2R*,7R*,9S*). Our work represents the first confirmed natural product which possesses 1,3-syn-Me/t-Bu relationship. Recently, synthesis of (2R,7R,9R)-laingolide A and its (Z)-isomer was reported (Pomey, G.; Phansavath, P. Synthesis 2015, 47, 1016–1023). As mentioned above, Maio’s group performed neuroactivity study of (–)-palmyrolide A and analogues as we proposed in the objective 5. Their results indicate that (5S,7S,10R)-isomer is less active. We will not repeat the same bioassay carried out by Maio's group for our samples of palmyrolide A and stereoisomers. We are currently continuing synthesis of laingolide stereoisomers. Upon completion of the synthesis work, we should submit all stereoisomers of laingolides for biological screening.

601211.label: Major findings and research outcome
601211.value: The signature structural units in palmyrolide A, laingolide, laingolide A, madangolide, and apratoxin A are the N-methylated trans-enamide and/or the t-Bu-substituted secondary carbinol with 1,3-Me/t-Bu substitution pattern. Before our accomplishment in this project, only the 1,3-anti-Me/t-Bu relationship is found in apratoxin A and palmyrolide A. As the first major finding, we have discovered that 1,3-syn-Me/t-Bu relationship also exists in Nature. Through diverted total synthesis of all four possible diastereomers, we have confirmed that laingolide A possessing a 1,3-syn-Me/t-Bu unit with relative configuration of (2R*,7R*,9S*). [See section 9, the conference papers #2–5] Our finding should provide a piece of evidence for studying biosynthesis of this class of natural products. In the current literature, there is no simple and efficient method for accessing the structural units with 1,3-anti-Me/t-Bu and 1,3-syn-Me/t-Bu relationships, respectively. As the second major finding, we have established one-step synthesis of trans-5-tert-butyl-3-methyldihydrofuran-2(3H)-one in both racemic and enantiomerically enriched forms by using SmI2-mediated reductive coupling reaction of methacrylates with aldehydes. The key factor for this successful reaction is use of our originally designed methacrylates of 2-amido arenols; it could efficiently suppress dimerization of aldehydes and improve the coupling stereoselectivity via a chelation effect. We could also get cis-5-tert-butyl-3-methyldihydrofuran-2(3H)-one through deprotonation–protonation sequence from the trans isomer. [See section 8, the journal publication #1] These readily available structural modules lay down a firm foundation for our diverted total synthesis. As the third major finding, we have developed a pentamodule assembly strategy for the diverted total synthesis of both palmyrolide A and laingolide A and their diastereomers. In particular, our Pd(OAc)2–Aphos-Y-catalyzed B-alkyl Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling reaction allows efficient and reliable assembly of the above mentioned unique structural modules with 1,3-anti-Me/t-Bu and 1,3-syn-Me/t-Bu relationships, leading to rapid synthesis of (–)-palmyrolide A and (5S,7S,10R)-palmyrolide A and all four possible diastereomers of laingolide A. [See section 8, the journal publications #2 and #3] As the fourth major finding, we have discovered that within the 15-membered skeleton of laingolide A, the original conjugated double bond at C12–C13 formed via ring-closing metathesis could isomerize into the C13–C14 positions to form the trans-enamide moiety for all four diastereomers. These results imply that the macrocyclic ring system containing the trans-enamide moiety is thermodynamically more stable than the conjugated enoate moiety. [See section 8, the journal publication #3]

601211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
601211.value: Our established multimodule assembly strategy is of general application value for diverted total synthesis of macrolides and it will be practiced in our future total synthesis projects. As the immediate continuation of our accomplished total synthesis of laingolide A, we are currently undertaking the diverted total synthesis of laingolide which possesses one more stereogenic center than laingolide A. It implies that a set of eight possible diastereomers might be synthesized in order to assign the relative configuration of the naturally occurring molecule. Several selected diastereomers of laingolide A will be synthesized first and then, depended on available manpower, other diastereomers might be synthesized. We estimate a period of 1–2 years is required for a skilled chemist to synthesize all eight diastereomers of laingolide A. If this can be achieved, we should be able to assign the relative configuration of laingolide A.

601211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
601211.value: Molecules originated from Nature are referred as to natural products and they serve as an important source of lead candidates for development of therapeutic agents. The very first phase of the drug discovery and development process requires determination of the molecular structure of a new natural product and attainment of the capability to produce the substance in chemistry laboratories in a sufficient quantity for biological studies. In this project, we have established an efficient protocol for synthesis of a neuroactive marine natural product, (–)-palmyrolide A. By using similar synthetic protocol, we have synthesized all four possible diastereomers (the structures with different three-dimension shapes) of another marine natural product, laingolide A, whose three-dimension structure has not been determined since its isolation in 1999. With these diastereomers made available in hand, we have determined, for the first time, the correct three-dimension shape of laingolide A. Our finding on the structure of laingolide A offer a new piece of evidence which might be valuable for understanding how these unique molecules, palmyrolide A and laingolide A, are produced by the marine microorganisms. Moreover, access to laingolide A and its structural analogues will facilitate others to study their biological activity.

601311.value: 设（G, X) 是一个有v个元素的群，D是G的一个有k个元素的子集合。如果G的每个非单位元都可以表示成lambda个乘积d_1d_2^{-1}，这里d_1和d_2是D的两个元素，D称之为G的一个(v, k, lambda)差集。 差集与数学的许多领域关系密切。这些领域包括有限域，有限几何，数论，和半域。同时，差集在工程领域有非常漂亮的应用。例如，差集在密码学，CDMA通信系统，纠错码，存储系统，和计算机网络领域得到广泛应用。 差集有一些超过50多年的难题，Ryser猜想是其中之一。解决这样的难题需要在代数数论或数学其它领域有新的突破。因而，差集是数学和工程的一个重要研究题目。 差集的研究有很长的历史。有一系列差集的构造和应用的文献。但是，差集有好多未解决的问题，有些应用中需要具有新参数的差集。构造差集的一个有效手段是利用特殊形式的函数。由于函数种类繁多，这是一个用之不尽的构造差集的途径。 在本项目中我们首先用特殊函数构造新差集， 然后寻找差集在科学和工程中的应用。我们同时探讨差集的性质和存在性问题。我们期望本项目的成果对差集的理论和应用有所贡献。

601311.label: Major findings and research outcome
601311.value: We constructed a family of new skew Hadamard difference sets with Dickson polynomials of order 7 and several families of almost difference sets with cyclotomy, and studied properties of these difference sets. We investigated the cyclic codes from the twin-prime difference sets and the cyclic codes from the two-prime almost difference sets. We constructed signal sets with good correlation properties. These resulted in seven research papers being published at top international journals. We gave a systematic study of linear codes from difference sets and almost difference sets. The outcome of this effort is the research monograph "Codes from Difference sets", published in 2014 by World Scientific. This is the first book on codes from difference sets.

601311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
601311.value: We will develop efficient decoding algorithms for the cyclic codes from difference sets and almost difference sets in the future.

601311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
601311.value: Difference sets are an interesting subject of study in combinatorics, and have applications in cryptography, coding theory, CDMA commutations and other engineering areas. In this project, a family of skew Hadamard difference sets and several families of almost difference sets are constructed, and their properties are investigated. Linear codes from difference sets and almost difference sets are systematically studied. Signal sets are also constructed. The outcomes of this project will enhance the current theory of difference sets and have applications in communications engineering and information security.

601411.label: Project Objectives
601411.value: Develop the control and detection system for the second MOT apparatus (MOT-II) that we have built up recently. We will prepare cold atoms trapped in the MOT-II as the medium to interact with single photons generated from the first MOT (MOT-I) that has been in operation for a year. Generate heralded narrow-band single photons with arbitrary waveforms with a controllable coherence time from 10 to 1000 ns. Demonstrate that optical free-induction decay can be observed at the single-photon level. We will verify that phase-amplitude coherence can exist in a single-photon state, which traditionally has been considered as a noncoherent state, without using conventional single-photon interferometry. Investigate directed spontaneous emission from an atomic ensemble with single photons. We will attempt to verify experimentally the theoretical prediction of directed spontaneous emission made by M. O. Scully in 2006. Generate photon-atom entanglement and realize single-photon switching by quantum interference. With electromagnetically induced transparency in cold atoms at a high optical depth, we will study how to switch a photon on and off by another single photon when they are simultaneously present with time-frequency entanglement. It will lead to the generation of photon-atom entanglement.
