601411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
601411.value: Precisely manipulating and controlling the interaction between a quantum device and single photons is a crucial step towards the realization of practical quantum information processing, quantum computation, and quantum communication through the use of single photons as the information carrier. In the past, most research was focused on the interaction between a single atom and the photons confined within an optical cavity. Recently the use of atomic ensembles for quantum memory and repeaters has attracted much research interest. Here we propose an experimental research plan of studying how to manipulate the quantum interaction between an atomic ensemble and single photons that have controllable waveforms. By tuning the time-domain shape of single photons, their collective interaction with an atomic ensemble (consisting of approximately 100,000,000 atoms) can be precisely controlled and engineered. Our research will help to answer some fundamental questions of quantum optics and may lead to potential applications in quantum information processing. 精確地操縱和控制量子器件與單光子的相互作用是實現以光作信息載體的量子信息處理，量子計算，和量子通訊的關鍵。在過去，大多數研究局限於光學諧振腔內的單原子和光子的相互作用。最近，利用原子系綜作量子存儲和中繼器的方案吸引了廣泛的研究興趣。在此，我們提出了一個操控原子系綜和可控波形單光子的量子相互作用的實驗研究計劃。通過調制單光子的時域波形，我們可以實現對其與原子系綜（大約由一億個原子組成）相互作用的精確控制。我們的研究結果將有助於回答一些量子光學中的基本物理問題，並可能應用在量子信息處理上。

601411.label: Major findings and research outcome
601411.value: We have achieved the following major findings and research outcome: (1) Optimal storage and retrieval of single-photon waveforms (world record) We have demonstrated an efficient storage and retrieval of single-photon wave packets using EIT in cold atoms at a high optical depth. We obtained an optimal storage efficiency of 49% for single-photon waveforms with a temporal likeness of 96% --- this is a world record of single-photon optical storage. Our result brings the EIT quantum memory closer to practical quantum information applications. Representative Publication: [1] Opt. Express 20, 24124 (2012). (2) Coherent control of single-photon absorption and reemission in a two-level atomic ensemble We have demonstrated coherent control of single-photon absorption and reemission in a two-level cold atomic ensemble. This is achieved by interfering the incident single photon wave packet with the emission (or scattering) wave. For a photon with an exponential growth waveform with a time constant equal to the excited-state lifetime, we observe that the single-photon emission probability during the absorption can be suppressed due to the perfect destructive interference. After the incident photon waveform is switched off, the absorbed photon is then reemitted to the same spatial mode as that of the incident photon. Our results suggest that the absorption and emission of a single photon in an atomic ensemble can be manipulated. Representative Publications: [1] Phys. Rev. Lett. 109, 263601 (2012). (3) Efficiently loading a single-photon into a single-sided optical cavity (world record) We have demonstrated that a single photon can be efficiently loaded into a cavity. Using heralded narrow-band single photons with exponential growth wave packet shaped by an electro-optical amplitude modulator, whose time constant matches the photon lifetime in the cavity, we demonstrate a loading efficiency of 87% from free space to a single-sided Fabry-Perot cavity. As compared to the previous others work of low efficiencies (<20%), we are holding a world record of the efficiency of loading a single photon into an optical cavity. Our result and approach may enable promising applications in realizing large-scale quantum networks based on cavity quantum electrodynamics. Representative Publications: [1] Phys. Rev. Lett. 113, 133601 (2014)

601411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
601411.value: The light-matter interaction lays down the foundations for atomic, molecular, and optical physics. Precisely manipulating and controlling the interaction between a quantum device and single photons is a crucial step towards the realization of practical quantum information processing and quantum communication. In this research project, we have demonstrated a new technique of manipulating the quantum interactions between an atomic ensemble and single photons by controlling and programing the photon temporal waveform. We have created two new world records: Storing single photons in a quantum memory with the highest retrieval efficiency (49%), and loading a single photon into an optical cavity with the highest efficiency (87%). We have also shown that, by manipulating the photon temporal wave function, its absorption and reemission by atoms can be precisely controlled. Our results have answered some fundamental questions of quantum optics and will lead to potential applications in quantum information processing.

601911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
601911.value: Melting and freezing are common phenomena in nature, however, their microscopic mechanisms are poorly understood [1,2]. The nucleation process at the initial stage of melting or freezing is central to the phase transition and is a hotly debated subject in physical science. A better understanding on this topic is of fundamental importance in condensed matter physics, and of practical interest for material science, nanotechnology, metallurgy and industries. Colloidal particles are particularly well-suited for investigating these processes because their thermal motions can be directly visualized and measured by video microscopy [3]. Specifically, novel thermal-sensitive diameter-tunable colloidal microgel spheres enable us to drive the melting and freezing transitions easily in a single sample [4,5]. This breakthrough opens a simple way to study melting and freezing at the single-particle level which is difficult to obtain in atomic systems. Recently we have studied the melting of microgel thin films at single-particle resolution for the first time [6,7] as well as the freezing of monolayers [8-10]. Here we propose to explore the melting and freezing in three-dimensional (3D) bulks and small clusters. How 3D crystals melt homogenously is a long-standing question, and one that is notoriously difficult to study experimentally because crystals always melt heterogeneously from the surface. To avoid the surface effect, we developed an optical heating technique to locally superheat the interior of a sample and generate a liquid droplet inside a crystalline matrix. This setup enables us to study two opposite and asymmetric processes: the melting of a superheated crystal and the freezing of a supercooled liquid. Many open questions can be systematically studied: What are the precursor defects and how do they evolve? How much can the colloidal crystal be superheated? Is there a forbidden gap in which superheated crystals cannot melt? Similar questions can be asked in the reverse freezing process. We will also study the structures and the melting and freezing behavior of free-floating microgel blobs. Making free-floating crystals is a long-standing challenge in colloid science. Recently we have successfully performed the self-assembly of these novel blobs in crystal, liquid and glass phases so that the melting and freezing in small clusters can be studied without substrate effects. These novel experimental systems provide a unique opportunity to study some open questions in melting and freezing with single-particle dynamics. The results can offer direct experimental evidence to the current debates for future refinement of the underlying theory. 融化和結晶是自然界常見的現象，但是，人們對其微觀機制了解甚少[1,2]。尤其是初始階段的成核過程對融化或結晶至關重要，而這正是一個有激烈爭議的問題。這個問題的深入理解對凝聚態物理有重要的基礎意義，也對材料科學，納米技術，冶金工業等現實應用上有指導意義。膠體粒子是特別適合研究這類過程，因為它們的熱運動可以直接通過光學顯微鏡測量[3]。特備是我們用的這種新穎的熱敏的直徑可調的膠體微球可以很容易實現在單個樣品中驅動融化和結晶[4,5]。這一突破使得我們可以用一個簡單的方法來研究每個粒子在融化 和結晶過程中如何運動，而這是很難在原子系統測量的。 最近，我們首次測量了膠體晶體薄膜在融化[8-10]和結晶[6,7]中單粒子的運動。在這裡，我們提出研究三維（3D）晶體和小顆粒的融化和結晶行為。 三維晶體均勻融化是一個長期的沒有很好解決的問題，而且實驗研究非常困難，因為晶體總是從表面或缺陷不均勻融化。為了避免表面影響，我們開發了一種光學加熱技術局部加熱樣品內部，造成過熱固體，最終生成一個包含在晶格內部的一個液滴。這種實驗能使我們研究兩個相反而又不對稱的過程：過熱晶體融化和過冷液體的結晶。許多懸而未決的問題可以被系統地研究：初始缺陷是什麼類型？他們如何發展？膠體晶體最多能被過熱到高於熔點多少？有沒有一個融化禁帶？反向結晶過程也同樣存在類似的問題。我們還將研究自由懸浮膠體晶體顆粒的融化和結晶。製備不受基底影響的懸浮結晶微顆粒長期以來是膠體科學中的一個挑戰。最近，我們成功地自組裝出懸浮結晶微顆，還可以把他們融化為液體或轉變成玻璃相。 這些新的實驗系統提供了一個獨特的測量融化和結晶中的單粒子運動的機會，從而可以研究一些長期沒有很好解決的問題。我們期望的研究結果可以為現有的爭議問題提供直接的實驗證據，並為今後的融化和結晶理論改進做出有效的指導。

601911.label: Realisation of objectives
601911.value: We successfully observed the homogeneous melting in 3D superheated crystals for the first time and quantitatively measure the nucleation kinetics in a broad superheating regime. We measured the superheat limit of hard-sphere crystals for the first time. These results about early-stage nucleation were published in Science in 2012. We further measured the later-stage nucleus growth in melting and found various deviations from the classical nucleation theory at strong superheating. We proposed a theoretical formula to describe the liquid nucleus growth in crystal. These results were published in Nature Communications in 2014. Hence objective 1 is successfully achieved. For objective 2, we performed the colloidal experiment about the crystallization in two dimensions and wrote a draft, but did not submit it for publication because it lacked of the theoretical explanation. Later on, a German group published similar experimental results with the theoretical explanation from a phase transition model in cosmology. Their work nicely connects colloids and cosmology and is published in PNAS. Therefore we did not explore along this direction. Instead, we moved to a more promising topic about surface premelting because we discovered a novel type of tunable attractive colloids. They can form high-quality crystal-vapor interfaces, thus open the door to study surface physics using colloidal model systems. Our first project along this direction is to study the poorly understood surface premelting, and the results were publish in Nature in 2016. In short, although we did not fully achieve objective 2, we wisely move to a new direction about another aspect of colloidal crystal melting which produces more important results. These results are closely related but beyond the objectives of this proposal.

602011.label: Project Objectives
602011.value: The PI plans to continue the study of minimal length elements in conjugacy classes of classical affine Weyl groups and to establish the special properties in the sense of Geck and Pfeiffer. The PI plans to study the abelianization of affine Hecke algebra and the class polynomials and to use these results to obtain information on the affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties in the critical strips. The PI plans to study the relation between the P-alcoves introduced by Goertz, Haines, Kottwitz and Reuman and De Concini-Procesi compactification of adjoint group. The PI plans to study the emtiness/nonemptiness pattern of affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties, especially those in the critical strips. The PI plans to study the dimension of affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties in the critical strips and in the admissible set, comparing the dimension with virtual dimension, and to apply these results to the study of supersingular locus of Shimura varieties with Iwahori level structure.

602011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
602011.value: The project aims to study affine Weyl groups and affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties. Minimal length elements in a conjugacy class of a Weyl group were first studied by Geck and Pfeiffer in the 90's for finite Weyl groups. They proved that these elements have remarkable combinatorial properties. Since then, these properties found many interesting applications in the representation theory. The PI plans to further develop the theory to affine Weyl groups. This new theory is expected to have important application to various topics: affine Hecke algebras, structure of loop groups and affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties, which is another major subject in this project. Both affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties and affine Springer fibers are certain subsets in the affine Grassmannian and affine flag varieties. Affine Springer fibers play a prominent role in Ngo's recent celebrated work on "fundamental lemma". Affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties, as Frobenius-twisted analog of affine Springer fibers, are also quite important in arithmetic geometry and representation theory. The PI and his collaborators plan to continue their study on the geometric structure of affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties in the affine flag varieties. We will study the emptiness/nonemptiness pattern of affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties in the critical strips and their dimension formula. We also plan to generalize these results to some non-split groups. Progress in this direction is expected to further our understanding of Shimura varieties and other aspects of the Langlands program. These subjects (affine Weyl groups and affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties) naturally sit in the intersection of representation theory, combinatorics and arithmetic algebraic geometry and have strong connection with number theory. In these areas, symmetry is a central theme and symmetry often comes from geometric objects. This is why we will combine algebraic method, combinatorial method together with geometric method in this project. And progress in this project is expected to have impact on various parts of mathematics. 本項目旨在研究仿射Weyl群和仿射Deligne-Lusztig簇。 Geck和Pfeiffer在90年代首次研究了有限Weyl群的共軛類中最小長度元素。他們證明了這些元素具有顯著的組合特性。從那時起數學家們陸續發現了這些特性在表示论中的許多有趣的應用。本項目負責人計劃進一步發展該理論到仿射Weyl群。這個新理論預計在以下領域將有重要的應用：仿射Hecke代數，loop群的結構和仿射Deligne-Lusztig簇，這些也是這個項目中的另一個重大課題。 仿射Deligne-Lusztig簇和仿射Springer纖維是仿射格拉斯曼流形和仿射flag簇中的子集。仿射Springer纖維在最近Ngo對“基本引理”的著名工作中發揮了突出作用。仿射Deligne-Lusztig簇， 作為仿射Springer纖維在Frobenius作用下的對應， 在算術代數幾何和表示論上也有非常重要的作用。 本項目負責人和他的合作者計劃繼續研究仿射Deligne-Lusztig簇的幾何結構。我們會研究仿射Deligne-Lusztig簇在關鍵帶上何時非空及維數公式。我們還計劃推廣這些結果到一些非分裂群上。在這個方向的進展，可望進一步增加我們對志村簇和朗蘭茲綱領的其它方面的認識。 仿射Weyl群和仿射Deligne-Lusztig簇是表示論， 組合數學和算術代數幾何的交叉領域， 並且和數論有很強的聯繫。 在這些學科中，對稱性是一個中心主題。 對稱性往往來自幾何對象。這就是為什麼我們將代數方法，組合方法與幾何方法在這個項目中結合起來。同時在這個項目上的進展預計將會對不同的數學領域帶來影響。

602011.label: Realisation of objectives
602011.value: Objective 5.1.1 is about the combinatorial properties of affine Weyl groups and the special properties conjectured in the proposal is established not only for the classical groups, as in the objective, but for exceptional groups as well. We also obtain a conceptual proof for the finite Weyl groups as well. The works are published in J. Algebra, Duke Math J. and Compos. Math. See articles 1, 2 and 5 from Part C. Objective 5.1.2 is about the cocenter of affine Hecke algebras. We give the Iwahori-Matsumoto presentation and Bernstein-Lusztig presentation of the cocenter. The works are published in Compos. Math and Selecta. Math. See articles 5 and 6 from Part C. Objective 5.1.3 is to study the important notion P-alcoves, introduced by Goertz, Haines, Kottwitz and Reuman. Some special properties of the P-alcoves and their applications to affine Hecke algebras and to affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties are studied. The works are published in Selecta. Math. and Annales scientifiques de l'ENS. See articles 6 and 9 from Part C. The application of De Concini-Procesi compactification to Shimura varieties is also obtained. The work is published in Duke. Math. J. See article 4 from Part C. Objective 5.1.4 is to study the affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties. The relation between affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties and affine Hecke algebras is established and several conjectures are verified. The works are published in Ann. Math., Annales scientifiques de l'ENS. See articles 3 and 9 from Part C. Objective 5.1.5 is about the dimension of affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties. The conjectural dimension formula is proved in article 3 from Part C. The supersingular loci of Shimura varieties are studied and the classification of basic loci of Coxeter type is obtained. The work is published in Cambridge Journal of Mathematics. See article 7 from Part C. Also the Green polynomials and representations of double cover of Weyl groups are studied. The work is published in Adv. Math. See article 8 from Part C. This part goes beyond the original scope of the proposal.

602011.label: Major findings and research outcome
602011.value: One major finding is the paper "Geometric and homological properties of affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties", article 3 from Part C, published in Ann. Math, which establishes the deep relation between affine Hecke algebras and affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties. Based on this relation, the PI proved several important conjectures on affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties. Another major finding is the paper "Normality and Cohen-Macaulayness of local models of Shimura varieties", article 4 from Part C, published in Duke Math. J., which solves a long-standing open problem on the geometry of special fiber of Shimura varieties. In a sequel of joint works with Sian Nie, published in Duke Math J., Compos. Math. and Selecta. Math, articles 2, 5 and 6 from Part C, we establish some important properties on the finite and affine Weyl groups and obtain some remarkable application on the affine Hecke algebras.

602011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
602011.value: The relation between affine Hecke algebras and affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties established in article 3 from Part C has found important applications and solved several important conjectures. The PI expect that it will have a long-term influence in the study of affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties. The approach of studying cocenter of affine Hecke algebras in a sequel papers of the PI and Sian Nie is very successful. The PI expect that it will shed some light to the study of some other problems in representation theory as well.

602011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
602011.value: In this project, the PI made considerable progress in the study of symmetries and obtain several important applications to arithmetic geometry and representation theory. Symmetries appear in most physical system, and has found applications throughout mathematics and the natural science, including particle physics, string theory, signal processing and genetics. By understanding several important aspects on the Weyl groups, the symmetry appears in many topics in the study of Shimura varieties and representation theory, the PI opens a new door to approach many important problems in these field. Combining the new knowledge on the Weyl groups, together with some novel ideas in arithmetic geometry and representation theory, the PI has successfully solved several important long-standing problems in these field. This project reveals the close relations between combinatorics, representation theory, and geometry and thus has an impact in these fields.

602111.label: Project Objectives
602111.value: To develop a novel electrochemical real-time PCR (ERT-PCR) technology based on the use of a hydrolysis probe modified with electro-active labels (the eTaq probe). The issues of low incorporation efficiency of modified nucleotides and low electron transfer efficiency found in our previously developed ERT PCR will be addressed by the new detection principle, which is based on a diffusion-controlled electrochemical reaction. The intrinsic advantages of simplicity, low cost and easy miniaturization provided by electrochemistry will enable the eTaq-based ERT-PCR technology to be applicable in portability-requiring situations such as point-of-care testings. To develop a design for signal enhancement and an efficient method for the synthesis of the eTaq probe. To obtain enhanced electrochemical signal for the detection of PCR amplicons, multiple electro-active tags will be incorporated into the eTaq probe. To make the synthesis of the eTaq probe more affordable by avoiding the use of the expensive DNA synthesizer, an alternative method for synthesizing the eTaq probe based on PCR and enzyme digestion will be developed. To improve the detection sensitivity of the eTaq-based ERT-PCR by using interdigitated array electrodes for signal amplification. In order for the detection sensitivity of the eTaq-based ERT-PCR to be able to rival with traditional fluorescent real-time PCR technologies, signal amplification mechanisms must be incorporated. Interdigitated array (IDA) electrodes, which provide effective signal amplification through multiple red-ox cycles, are perfectly compatible with the eTaq-based ERT-PCR to be developed in this study, as the latter is based on a diffusion-controlled electrochemical reaction of the electro-active tags. Therefore, IDA electrodes will be introduced to the eTaq-based ERT-PCR as the detection electrode, to further improve the detection sensitivity for PCR amplicons. To suppress the background signal in the eTaq-based ERT-PCR by immobilizing the eTaq probe on a second substrate. In order to improve the sensitivity of detection for PCR amplicon in the eTaq-based ERT-PCR by suppressing background signal, which is produced by the un-hydrolysed eTaq probe diffusing to the detection electrode, an alternative format will be investigated. The eTaq probe will be immobilized on a second substrate through hybridization with an immobilized DNA primer, resulting in a zero background signal and enhanced detection sensitivity. To achieve higher annealing and hydrolyzing efficiency in the eTaq-based ERT-PCR by immobilizing the eTaq probe on a micro/nano-structure array. An array of micro/nano-structures such as micro-pillars and nanotubes will be introduced as the second substrate on which the eTaq probe is immobilized. This arrangement would significantly reduce the density of the immobilized primer and eTaq probe, leading to higher annealing and hydrolyzing efficiency, and therefore, higher detection sensitivity. To develop a multiplexed ERT-PCR using eTaq probes labeled with electro-active indicators of different red-ox potentials. Development of a multiplexed real-time PCR would be of great value for high-throughput DNA analysis. rows: To develop a novel electrochemical real-time PCR (ERT-PCR) technology based on the use of a hydrolysis probe modified with electro-active labels (the eTaq probe). The issues of low incorporation efficiency of modified nucleotides and low electron transfer efficiency found in our previously developed ERT PCR will be addressed by the new detection principle, which is based on a diffusion-controlled electrochemical reaction. The intrinsic advantages of simplicity, low cost and easy miniaturization provided by electrochemistry will enable the eTaq-based ERT-PCR technology to be applicable in portability-requiring situations such as point-of-care testings.

To develop a design for signal enhancement and an efficient method for the synthesis of the eTaq probe. To obtain enhanced electrochemical signal for the detection of PCR amplicons, multiple electro-active tags will be incorporated into the eTaq probe. To make the synthesis of the eTaq probe more affordable by avoiding the use of the expensive DNA synthesizer, an alternative method for synthesizing the eTaq probe based on PCR and enzyme digestion will be developed.

To improve the detection sensitivity of the eTaq-based ERT-PCR by using interdigitated array electrodes for signal amplification. In order for the detection sensitivity of the eTaq-based ERT-PCR to be able to rival with traditional fluorescent real-time PCR technologies, signal amplification mechanisms must be incorporated. Interdigitated array (IDA) electrodes, which provide effective signal amplification through multiple red-ox cycles, are perfectly compatible with the eTaq-based ERT-PCR to be developed in this study, as the latter is based on a diffusion-controlled electrochemical reaction of the electro-active tags. Therefore, IDA electrodes will be introduced to the eTaq-based ERT-PCR as the detection electrode, to further improve the detection sensitivity for PCR amplicons.

To suppress the background signal in the eTaq-based ERT-PCR by immobilizing the eTaq probe on a second substrate. In order to improve the sensitivity of detection for PCR amplicon in the eTaq-based ERT-PCR by suppressing background signal, which is produced by the un-hydrolysed eTaq probe diffusing to the detection electrode, an alternative format will be investigated. The eTaq probe will be immobilized on a second substrate through hybridization with an immobilized DNA primer, resulting in a zero background signal and enhanced detection sensitivity.

To achieve higher annealing and hydrolyzing efficiency in the eTaq-based ERT-PCR by immobilizing the eTaq probe on a micro/nano-structure array. 602111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
602111.value: Real-Time and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assays have become an indispensable molecular biology based technique for a wide range of applications including disease diagnosis, detection of pathogenic species, monitoring of water and food quality, and forensic testing. Unlike end-point electrophoresis-based PCR that analyzes amplified DNA products after the reaction, real-time PCR allows in-situ measurement of the increased amount of DNA as it is amplified. Fluorescence-based methods underlie the detection principle of all the commercially available real-time PCR instruments, as they offer higher detection sensitivity than their electrochemistry-based counterparts. Nevertheless, a fluorescence-based assay demands complex and bulky instruments and tailor-made fluorescent reagent kits. Electrochemistry-based technologies, on the other hand, are known to be promising candidates for point-of-care applications, as they enjoy inherent advantages of simple instrumentation and operation, low cost and easy miniaturization. Electrochemistry-based real-time PCR assays would be a promising alternative if their detection sensitivity could reach a level comparable to that of their fluorescence counterparts. Although DNA biosensors utilizing electrochemistry-based detection methods have been widely reported in the literature, the challenges involved in achieving a homogeneous PCR assay without using fluorescent dyes mean that there has been, to date, very little progress in establishing an electrochemical platform for real-time PCR. In the proposed research, our team aims to develop a new platform to “electrochemically” monitor in real time the increase in amplified DNA product during PCR. Inspired by Taqman probe-based fluorescence assays, our approach will apply a sequence-specific hydrolysis oligonucleotide probe modified with electroactive tags (also called eTaq probe). Upon the nucleotide extension step during PCR, E-tagged nucleotides closer to the 5’ end of the hydrolysis probe would be cleaved away one-by-one as a result of the 5’ to 3’ exonuclease activity of the DNA polymerase. Unlike the negatively-charged hydrolysis probe, the released E-tagged mononucleotides, because of their weaker electrostatic repulsion with a negatively surface, would diffuse freely to the negatively charged electrode (e.g. indium tin oxide) contributing to an electrochemical signal. To improve detection sensitivity, new sensing strategies involving multiple E-tags and E- signal amplification have been proposed. The proposed study project promises to produce a sensitive electrochemical real-time PCR assay that would potentially rival its fluorescent counterpart. 實時定量聚合酶鏈式反應（PCR）是一種不可或缺的分子生物學技術，在疾病診斷，病原菌檢測，水質食品質量監測以及法醫鑒定等領域都有著廣泛的應用。不同於傳統的利用凝膠電泳技術對PCR 擴增終產物進行分析，實時PCR技術可以原位地對DNA擴增過程進行監測。基本上所有現有的商業化實時定量PCR技術都是基於熒光的方法。這是因為相對於電化學方法，熒光方法具有靈敏度高的優勢。然而，基於熒光的實時PCR技術不僅需要復雜龐大的儀器，而且需要定制的熒光探針試劑盒。相反，電化學檢測技術因為其具有設備需求簡單，易於操作，成本低和易於小型化等特點，非常有希望發展成為一種實時現場檢測的手段。如果可以達到與實時熒光PCR相當的靈敏度，基於電化學的實時定量PCR將是實時熒光定量PCR技術的一個很好的替代品。雖然近年來有大量的有關DNA生物傳感器的文獻出現，但是基於電化學檢測平臺的實時定量PCR技術卻鮮有報導。 在本研究計劃中，我們小組將致力於發展一種新型的電化學檢測平臺來實現對PCR擴增過程的電化學實時監控。受到熒光Taqman®探針的啟發，我們的方法利用電活性物質標記的水解型寡核苷酸探針來實現。在PCR的引物延伸階段，DNA聚合酶的5’-3’外切酶活性將靠近水解探針5’端的具有電活性物質標記的核苷酸逐個酶切降解。相對於帶負電荷的探針，被降解後的具有電活性物質標記的核苷酸因為受到較小的靜電斥力，更容易擴散到帶負電荷的電極表面來產生電化學信號。為了提高這個方法的靈敏度，我們計劃發展一些新的信號放大手段，例如在一個水解探針上標記多個電化學活性標記物。本研究計劃若成功實施，將有望發展出一種可以與現有的實時熒光定量PCR相競爭的電化學實時定量PCR技術。

602111.label: Realisation of objectives
602111.value: The PI and his team have achieved the objectives of the project. Most of their findings have been articulated through symposia in international conferences and research papers in peer-review journals. This research has also partly contributed to the training of an outstanding Ph.D. student, who is now a postdoctoral fellow in Harvard. Objective 1: This objective has been completed by the development of an electrochemical version of Taqman real time PCR technique. Instead of using fluorescent Taqman probes, our new method features an oligo-probe modified by an electroactive reporter (e.g. ferrocene or methylene blue). This electrochemical PCR technology offers potential for point of care applications. Objective 2: Successful synthesis of eTaq probe with multiple electro-active tags has been realized. Solid phase phosphoramidite method was used to modify DNA probe at its terminus with dendritic structured molecule including multiple ferrocene groups. This kind of probe is stable and generate much higher electrochemical signal after DNaseI digestion comparing with previous eTaq probe with single tag. Objective 3: We have completed this objective by designing and fabricating IDA electrode with crossed comb-like working electrode and counter one, they are in close proximity which could facilitate redox species recycling process, hence provide effective signal amplification. Objective 4: This objective has been investigated by the design and fabrication of 3D structured electrode with nano-scale chambers. Background signal could be effectively suppressed by immobilizing eTaq probe on the top of the chamber. Objective 5: Simple and feasible method of fabricating micro/nano-structure array has been established and investigated, which could be used as the second substrate for eTaq probe immobilization. Objective 6: Electroactive molecules with different redox potentials could be modified at 5’ terminus of DNA probe using solid phase phosphoramidite method. Probes labeled with several different ferrocene derivatives have been synthesized, purified and characterized.

602111.label: Major findings and research outcome
602111.value: In the project, the team has satisfactorily achieved the proposed objectives. Specifically, the team has demonstrated an “electrochemical version” of Taqman real time PCR. Strategy of probe modification of different electroactive tags has been established (objectives 1, 2, 6), fabrication of nano-structured electrodes have been investigated (objectives 3, 4, 5), in order to increase sensitivity. This electrochemical-based immobilization-free principle taking advantage of electrostatic repulsion effect between ITO electrode and DNA backbone has also been expanded to isothermal sensing area, developing one highly sensitive, cost effective mercury ion sensing platform which is suitable for POC application (paper attached).

602111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
602111.value: One of the challenges limiting the electrochemical-based sensing strategy is the use of enzyme. Firstly, its activity is easily to decrease with improper storage. Secondly, protein binding at electrode surface will block redox reaction, hence decrease electrochemical signal and sensitivity. Enzyme-free sensing strategies are promising in electrochemical-based areas and point-of-care (POC) applications. Enzyme-free sensing platform study is also one of the major initiatives undertaken in the PI’s lab.

602111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
602111.value: This novel ERT-PCR technique developed in the PI’s lab is a powerful sensing tool. Based on the use of hydrolysis of eTaq probe, it combines advantages of immobilization-free strategy, micro-structured portable device and classic qPCR. With increasing sensitivity, high throughput implementation and its compatibility with different techniques, ERT-PCT will certainly lead a promising trend in ultra-sensitive point of care applications.

602611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
602611.value: Aromaticity has fascinated chemists for over a century and is still attracting considerable current attention. The archetypical aromatic compound is benzene. Formal replacement of a CH group in benzene by an isolobal hetero atom/group can give heterocyclic aromatic compounds. In the past, many such compounds with a main-group element/group have been studied, for example, pyridines, silabenzenes, boratabenzenes. Recently, there has been much interest in the chemistry of transition metal-containing metallabenzenes. These compounds are interesting because they could display properties of both aromatic organic compounds and organometallic compounds. Although remarkable progress has been made in the chemistry of metallabenzenes of late transition metals, the chemistry of metallabenzenes of early and middle transition metals is much less developed. The isolation and direct observation of metallabenzenes with an early or middle transition metal (group 3-7 metals) has so far met with limited success. This project will focus on the development of the chemistry of rhenabenzenes (metallabenzene containing rhenium, a group 7 metal). The main objectives of the proposed research are (i) to develop synthetic methods to synthesize rhenabenzenes, and (ii) to explore the chemical properties of rhenabenzenes. 芳香性化合物是一类具有特殊化學性質的化合物。芳香性的概念是以苯分子为原型建立起来的。把苯分子中的基团用含杂原子的基团代替能得到杂环芳香化合物， 例如，吡啶, 硅杂苯, 硼杂苯。近年来，金属苯化学引起了化学家的兴趣。这类化合物可同时具有有机芳香性化合物及金属有机化合物的性質。尽管金属苯化学已有不少进展，前及中过渡金属苯化学的研究还很少。本项目的主要目的在于发展铼苯（含第七族元素铼的金属苯）的化学。主要研究内容包括（1）发展合成铼苯的方法，（2）探讨铼苯的化学性質

602611.label: Realisation of objectives
602611.value: The main objectives of the project are (i) to develop synthetic methods to synthesize rhenabenzenes and (ii) to explore the chemical properties of rhenabenzenes. To achieve the objectives, we have carried out the following research work. Reactions of metallacyclobutadienes with alkynes could potentially lead to the formation of metallabenzenes. We have therefore synthesized a series of low valent rhenacyclobutadienes and investigated their reactions with various alkynes, including PhC≡CPh, HC≡CPh, EtC≡CEt, HC≡COEt, MeC≡CNEt2 and PhC≡CSMe with the intention to obtain low valent rhenabenzenes. To provide guides to our experimental work, we have studied computationally the thermodynamics and kinetics of the reactions of alkynes with rhenacyclobutadienes. In principle, low valent rhenabenzenes could also be made from properly functionalized rhenium carbene, carbyne and metallabenzynes complexes. We have therefore made a lot of efforts in developing synthetic routes to make rhenium carbene, carbyne and metallabenzynes complexes. The reactivities of some of these newly synthesized complexes have also been investigated. To search for synthetic routes to make high valent rhenabenzenes, we have studied reactions of rhenium oxo complexes such as Re(O)Cl3(PPh3)2 and Re(O)Cl2(OEt)(PPh3)2 with both internal and terminal alkynols with the expectation of formation of rhenabenzenes through initial phosphine attacking on the alkyne carbon. To define chemical properties of rhenabenzenes and related metallacycles experimentally, we have investigated thermal rearrangement reactions of rhenebenzenes and metallabenzynes to cyclopentadienyl complexes. We have also studies reactions of rhenabenzenes and metallabenzynes with various electrophiles including Br2, NO2BF4, NOBF4 and HCl/H2O2. We have also studied reactivity of rhenabenzenes towards nucleophiles such as HNR2, and alkynes. To understand chemical properties of rhenabenzenes, we have carried out computational studies to define electronic structures of rhenabenzenes, the substituent effect on the thermodynamics and kinetics of the rearrangement reactions of rhenabenzenes to give the corresponding cyclopentadienyl complexes.

602611.label: Major findings and research outcome
602611.value: (1) Low valent rhenacyclobutadiene complexes Re{-C(Ar)C(CO2R’)C(OR)}(CO)4 can react with HC≡COEt to give the rhenabenzenes Re{-C(Ar)C(CO2R’)C(OR)CHC-(OEt)}(CO)4 that are stable enough to be isolated [Publications 7 and 9]. (2) The thermodynamics and kinetics of the rearrangement reactions of metallabenzenes Re{-C(Ar)C(CO2R’)C(OR)CXCY}(CO)4 to cyclopentadienyl complexes were found be dependent on the substituent X and Y [unpublished results]. (3) Rhenium oxo ylide complexes can be obtained in high yield from the reactions of both internal and terminal alkynols with ReOCl2(OEt)(PPh3)2 through phosphine attacking on the alkyne carbon [Publication 1]. (4) The vinylcarbyne complexes Re(≡CCH=C(R)C≡CH)HCl(PMe2Ph)3 can undergo isomerization reactions give rhenabenzynes Re(≡C-CH=C(R)CH=CH)Cl(PMe2Ph)3 [Publications 2 and 3]. (5) The hydrido carbyne complexes Re(≡CCH=C(tBu)C≡CR)HCl(PMe2Ph)3 (R = H, n-pentyl) undergo a 1,2-hydrogen shift from the metal to the carbyne carbon atom to give carbene complexes. In contrast, a similar transformation does not occur for the analogous complex Re(≡CCH=C(tBu)C≡CSiMe3)HCl(PMe2Ph)3 which has a SiMe3 group on the CC moiety. A theoretical study suggests that the difference is caused by steric effect [Publication 4]. (6) Metallabenzynes Os(CC(R)=C(CH3)C(R)=CH)Cl2(PPh3)2 (R = SiMe3, H) undergo electrophilic substitution reactions with reagents including Br2, NO2BF4, NOBF4 HCl/H2O2 and AlCl3/H2O2 to afford the corresponding bromination, nitration, nitrosation, and chlorination products [Publication 6]. (7) The reactions of ReH5(PMe2Ph)3 with terminal alkynes can give rhenium carbyne complexes Re((CCH2R)Cl2(PMe2Ph)3 and/or eta2-vinyl complex Re(eta2-CH2CR)Cl2(PMe2Ph)3. The reaction pathways were found to be kinetic-controlled [Publication 11]. (8) Rhenacyclobutadienes Re{-C(Ar)C(CO2R’)C(OR)}(CO)4 can react with ethoxyethyne to give unexpected coupling products [Publications 7 and 9]. (9) The relative thermal stability of metallabenzynes Os(≡CCH=CHCH=CH)Cl2(L)2 and the corresponding isomeric carbene complexes Os{=C(−CH=CHCH=CH−)}Cl2(L)2 as well as the chlorocyclopentadienyl complexes Os(eta5-C5ClH4)Cl(L)2 (L = CO, phosphine, pyridine, amine) are found to be strongly dependent on ligand L. It was found experimentally that the metallabenzyne Os{≡CC(SiMe3)=C(CH3)C(SiMe3)=CH−}Cl2(CO)(PPh3) can rearrange to the eta5-chlorocyclopentadienyl complex Os{eta5-C5HCl(CH3)(SiMe3)2}Cl(CO)(PPh3) [Publication 12].

602611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
602611.value: (1) We have successfully isolated and structurally characterized a series of low valent rhenabenzenes. It would be interesting to explore the possibility of isolating high valent rhenabenzenes, and metallabenzenes of other group 3-7 metals. (2) We have demonstrated that rhenabenzenes can be conveniently made from insertion reactions of alkynes with metallacyclobutadienes. It is worthwhile to explore the possibility of making other metallabenzenes using analogous insertion reactions. (3) We have discovered that the activation barriers as well as the outcomes of the reactions of alkynes with metallacyclobutadienes vary with metallacyclobutadienes and the substituents on the alkynes. It would be interesting to carry out further experimental and computational work to understand factors that control the kinetics and thermodynamic of different reaction pathways.

602611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
602611.value: Aromatic compounds are an important class of compounds in chemistry. The archetypical aromatic compound is benzene. Formal replacement of a CH group in benzene by an isolobal hetero atom/group can give heterocyclic aromatic compounds. In the past, many such compounds with a main-group element/group have been studied, for example, pyridines and boratabenzenes. More recently, there has been much interest in the chemistry of transition metal-containing metallabenzenes. These compounds are interesting because they could display properties of both aromatic organic compounds and organometallic compounds. Although a number of metallabenzenes of late transition metals such as platinum, iridium, ruthenium and osmium are known, well-characterized metallabenzenes with an early or middle transition metal (group 3-7 metals) are unknown prior to this work. In this project, we have successfully isolated and structurally characterized a series of rhenabenzenes, metallabenzene containing rhenium, a group 7 metal. We have also investigated the chemical properties of rhenabenzenes. The results obtained in this project clearly demonstrates that it is possible to isolate metallabenzenes with an early or middle transition metal and hinted that it is worthwhile to conduct research work in this direction.

603011.value: 高頻率波傳播的歐拉方法及其反問題

603011.label: Project Objectives
603011.value: Apply the Eulerian Gaussian beams summation method to boundary-initial valued problems including reflection and diffraction by obstacles; Develop a new PDE-based method for inverting a discontinuous velocity model. Since most tomography problems involve crust and lithosphere, it is therefore desirable to incorporate such assumption in the inverse problem; Invert the velocity model directly using the wavefield measured on the boundary of the computational domain. 603011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
603011.value: High frequency wave propagation is an important phenomenon in various fields including modeling of acoustic waves and obtaining the semiclassical solution to the Schrodinger equation in quantum mechanics. Since the computational mesh size should be in the same order of the frequency to resolve the oscillations, it is numerically very challenging to compute these wave propagation in the high frequency regime using typical algorithms. One remedy is to compute the high frequency asymptotic solution so that it satisfies the equation asymptotically in which the frequency tends to infinity or the wavelength tends to zero. Various asymptotic methods have been developed including geometrical optics expansion and Gaussian beam summations. These approaches have been shown to be computationally very efficient in capturing various high frequency wave propagation phenomena including multiple traveltime computations, wavefield construction in the occurrence of caustics, and multiple-slit diffraction. In this project, we propose to develop new numerical methods for computing high frequency asymptotic solutions to these wave propagation. Usual techniques are based on the Lagrangian ray tracing formulation. Complicated data structure is usually necessary to trace curved rays through each computational cell. The idea in this proposal is to develop an Eulerian formulation which adopts global Cartesian coordinates and level set equation, yielding uniformly distributed solutions. Based on this new formulation, we also propose to solve various related inverse problems including transmission traveltime tomography and Gaussian beam based inversion. The techniques developed will be important for seismic imaging, underwater acoustics and oil exploration. The methods developed in this project will significantly advance both the resolution of the inverted velocity and the robustness of the inverting algorithm. 高頻率波的傳播在包括聲波的建模和得到量子力學中薛定諤方程的半經典解在內的多個領域都是一個很重要的現象。由於計算時網格大小和解決擾動的頻率是同階的，使用典型的數值算法來計算高頻波的傳播就變得非常困難。一個糾正辦法是計算出方程的高頻漸進解，這些解的頻率趨於無窮大或它們的波長趨於0。各種各樣的漸進方法已經被提出來，包括幾何光學展開和高斯光束求和。這些方法已經被證明在捕捉各種各樣的高頻波的傳播現象方面是非常有效率的，這些現象包括多重移動時間計算，有焦散線出現時波場的構造和多縫衍射。 在這個項目中，我們提出一種新的數值方法來計算這些波的傳播的高頻漸進解。一般的方法都是建立在拉格朗日射線追踪法基礎之上的，需要復雜的數據結構來跟踪通過每個計算單元的曲線。而我們的想法是提出一種可以接受全局笛卡爾坐標和水平集方程的歐拉方法，從而獲得一致分佈的解。基於這個新方法，我們還可以解決各種相關的逆問題，包括傳播時間層析成像方法和高斯光束的反演。這些方法在地震成像、水聲學和石油勘探方面都很重要。這個項目中提出的方法將會大大促進解決反向速度的問題和提高逆向算法的堅固性。

603011.label: Realisation of objectives
603011.value: As per Objective 1 and Objective 2, we have developed a level set based method for solving two transmission tomography problems. Because of the level set representation, we are able to invert for the discontinuous velocity model without any assumption on the topology of the reflector. Two articles have been published in peer reviewed journals. To improve the computational efficiency of the Eulerian Gaussian beam summation method, we have also developed a new numerical method for solving Schrodinger equations in the semi-classical regime based on short time WKBJ propagators. As per Objective 3, we use field measurements for an inverse problem in the context of gravimetry. The inverse problem is solved based on a novel PDE based formulation. Two articles have been published to satisfy this objective. The computational efficiency of the approach has also been significantly improved in the second publication. Relating to Objective 4, we have also developed a new PDE formulation for an inverse problem relates to eikonal equation in isotropic media. The work has recently been published in SIAM J. on Imaging Sciences. Supported by this project, we have published 6 articles in total and have trained one PhD student. The PhD student is currently having his postdoc training at US.

603011.label: Major findings and research outcome
603011.value: In Li and Leung (2013), we propose a numerical algorithm for solving first arrival transmission traveltime tomography problems where the underlying slowness is piecewise continuous. We incorporate with the level set method to implicitly represent the discontinuity in the velocity. The evolution of the level set function will naturally take care of the change in the topology. To improve the computational efficiency, we also propose a local level set method so that most computer power of updating the level set evolution is spent near the discontinuity in the slowness. In Li, Leung and Qian (2014), we further incorporate reflection traveltime data into the formulation so that possible reflectors (slowness interfaces) in the targeted subsurface model can be recovered as well as the slowness distribution itself. In Leung, Serna and Qian (2014), we propose new numerical methods for solving Schrodinger equations in the semi-classical regime based on short time WKBJ propagators. Even though the WKBJ solution is valid only for a short time because of the occurrence of caustics, the Green formula allows us to construct and propagate the solution for long time. To improve the computational efficiency, we develop two approximations using a short time Taylor expansion. In Isakov, Leung and Qian (2013), we develop a numerical methods for solving a partial differential equations (PDE) based approach for an inverse gravimetry problem. In the paper we consider modeling (sea) ice domain with the snow covering a part of the upper boundary and approximated by density distribution. A new uniqueness result is also derived in the paper. An improvement in the computational complexity has also been proposed in Lu, Leung and Qian (2015). We also develop a new variational approach in Glowinski, Leung and Qian (2015) to solve the first arrival transmission tomography problem. The cost functional is penalized to enforce the nonlinear equality constraint associated with the underlying eikonal equation, biharmonically regularized with respect to traveltime, and harmonically regularized with respect to sound speed. To overcome the difficulty associated with the inherent nonlinearity of the eikonal equation, the Euler-Lagrange equation of the penalized-regularized variational problem is reformulated into an equivalent, mixed optimality system.

603011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
603011.value: Inverse problem is still an extremely active field of research. There are plenty of problems we can continue to work on. For example, we have been trying to extend the work in Glowinski, Leung and Qian (2015) to other related PDE related inverse problem. We are also going to look into a photoacoustic imaging problem.

603011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
603011.value: High frequency wave propagation is an important phenomenon in various fields including modeling of acoustic waves and obtaining the semiclassical solution to the Schrodinger equation in quantum mechanics. In this project, we have successfully developed various numerical approaches for computing high frequency asymptotic solutions to these wave propagations. Based on these techniques, we have solved several related inverse problems including transmission-reflection traveltime tomography problems for discontinuous media, inverse gravimetry and also a new tomography problem. The methods developed in this project are important for seismic imaging, underwater acoustics and oil exploration.

603111.label: Realisation of objectives
603111.value: The objectives of this research project are to synthesize heterometallic nitrido and imido complexes using metal terminal nitrido complexes as starting materials and to explore their organometallic chemistry and catalytic activity. We have demonstrated that a ruthenium(VI) terminal nitrido complex containing the Kläui tripodal ligand [(h5-C5H5)Co{P(O)(OEt)2}3]- (LOEt-), [LOEtRu(N)Cl2] (1), exhibits electrophilic behavior and can serve a versatile starting material for bridged nitrido and imido complexes. We have synthesized and structurally characterized dinuclear Ru(V)-Ru(IV) [{LOEtRuCl2}2(N)] and tetranuclear Ru(IV)-Ru(IV) [LOEtCl2Ru(N)Ru(H2O)Cl2]2 bridged nitrido complexes starting from complex 1 (Inorganic Chemistry, 2012, 10529−10535). We have synthesized and structurally characterized a trinuclear Ru/Rh imido complex by reaction of complex 1 with Rh(mes)3 (mes = mesityl) The formation of the Ru/Rh imido complex presumbably involves the insertion of the Ru(VI) nitride into the Rh-C sigma bond, which is a new reaction for a transition metal nitride (Organometallics 2013, 733−736). We have investigated the reactions of Re nitrides with the Rh(II) acetate dimer [Rh2(OAc)4]. The first dirhodium(II) bridged nitrido complexes [{Rh2(OAc)4}{NReCl(PPh3)LOEt}2}]n+ (n = 0 or 2) have been synthesized and structurally characterized (Dalton Transactions, 2015, pp 5479-5487). We have demonstrated that the Ru(VI) nitride can induce facile h5-h1 slippage of group 8 metallocenes. Thus, reactions of complex 1 with osmocene and bis(indenyl)ruthenium lead to the formation of trinuclear M(VI)-N-Ru(IV) (M = Os, Ru) complexes with h1-cyclopentadienyl ligands, which are rare examples of cyclopentadienyl osmium(VI) and ruthenium(VI) complexes (Inorganic Chemistry, 2013, pp 10449-10455). We have also isolated and structurally characterized a series dinuclear group 8 metal porphyrin nitrido complexes (TPP)M(N)RuCl2(TPP) by reactions of M(II)(TPP) (M = Fe, Ru, Os; TPP = tetraphenylporphyrin dianion) with complex 1. This new synthetic route provides an easy access to a series of M(IV) nitrido complexes containing symmetric M(IV)=N=Ru(IV) bridges. The electrochemistry of these dinuclear nitrido complexes has been investigated (submitted for publication). The catalytic activity of dinuclear nitrido porphyrin complexes is being investigated.

603111.label: Major findings and research outcome
603111.value: We have demonstrated that electrophilic Ru(VI) nitrido complexes can serve as useful starting materials for dinuclear heterometallic nitrido and imido complexes that display interesting organometallic, redox and catalytic chemistry. Major findings in this project are summarized as follows: (i) A novel mixed valence Ru(V)-Ru(IV) bridged nitrido complex has been isolated and structurally characterized. (ii) The Rh(III) aryl complex, tris(mesityl)rhodium(III), undergoes migratory insertion of a Ru(VI) nitride to give a trinuclear Rh(III)/Ru(IV) bridged imido complex. This is a new reaction for a transition metal nitride. (iii) We have synthesized and structurally characterized the first dirhodium(III) complexes containing bridged nitrido ligands. (iv) We have found that a Ru(VI) nitride can induce facile h5-h1 ring slippage of group 8 metallocenes. The first Ru(VI) and Os(IV) cyclopentadienyl complexes with bridged nitrido ligands have been isolated and structurally characterized. (v) We have synthesized a series of Ru chalcogenonitrosyl (NX where X = O, S, Se) with a bidentate thiolate ligands. De-chalcogenation of Ru-NX complexes leads to formation of bridged nitrido or phosphoraminate complexes. (vi) We have developed a convenient synthetic route to dinuclear porphyrin nitrido complexes of group 8 metals that display interesting redox and catalytic chemistry. (vii) We have synthesized and structurally characterized a novel Ce(IV)-V(V) oxo cluster that is a highly active catalyst for oxidation of thioethers.

603111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
603111.value: The results of this project have demonstrated that bridged nitrido complexes can stabilize high-valent metal complexes (e.g. Fe(IV), Ru(VI)) that display interesting organometallic and redox chemistry. For example, [{LOEtRuCl2}2(N)] is a rare example of mixed valence Ru(V)-Ru(IV) nitrido complex. It is of interest to elucidate the bonding (e.g. Ru(V)-Ru(IV) nitrido vs. Ru(IV)-Ru(IV) complex with a nitridyl ion) and investigate the reactivity of this novel nitrido complex. Organometallic chemistry of Ru(VI) and Os(IV) is not well developed. As such, it is worthwhile to explore the organometallic chemistry cyclopentadienyl Ru(VI) and Os(VI) complexes containing bridged nitrido complexes. Finally, we have synthesized a family of dinuclear nitrido porphyrin complexes of the type (TPP)M(N)RuCl2LOEt (M = group 8 metals, TPP = tetraphenylporphyrin dianion). Efforts should be made to explore the atom transfer chemistry of these novel nitrido porphyrin complexes. For examples, high-valent oxo-nitrido (TPP)(O)M(N)RuCl2LOEt and imido-nitrido (TPP)(NR)M(N)RuCl2LOEt can applications in organic oxidation and amination reactions, respectively.

603111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
603111.value: The bridged nitrido and imido ligands are of interest because of their ability to stabilize metal ions in high oxidation states. Molecular bridged nitrido complexes can also serve as building blocks for metal nitride materials. In this project, rational synthetic routes to bridged nitrido and imido complexes have been developed. Specifically, dinuclear heterometallic nitrido complexes have been synthesized by reactions of ruthenium(VI) nitrido complexes with organometallic precursors. Also, a bimetallic imido complex has been prepared by the reaction of a ruthenium(VI) nitride with a metal aryl complex, presumably via insertion of the nitride into the metal-carbon bond. Using this newly developed synthetic methods, we were able to prepare a series of bimetallic nitrido and imido complexes and to explore their reaction chemistry. Metal complexes with unusual oxidation states (e.g. iron(IV) porphyrins, ruthenium(VI) cyclopentadienyl complexes) stabilized by bridged nitrido ligands have been synthesized. This provides us an opportunity to investigate the organometallic and redox chemistry of high-valent metal complexes that can find applications in organic transformations, e.g. oxidation and amination of hydrocarbons.

603311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
603311.value: 细胞色素-c是一个单一结构域可溶性血红素蛋白，普遍存在于几乎所有的细胞类。它在细胞中主要参与三种不同的过程， 在线粒体中作为细胞呼吸链中的电子转移中介体，在细胞溶胶中作为细胞凋亡的触发器或中介体，以及作为细胞中活性氧质（ROS）的清除剂介入细胞内氧化还原的平衡。 细胞色素-c 分子为研究一系列生物化学现象 - 包括蛋白体调控的氧化还原及配位性质、血红素与蛋白体之间的相互作用、蛋白体中的长程电子转移、蛋白体可逆折叠等等提供了一个已具备精确结构的研究平台。 共振拉曼光谱已被证明是研究与细胞色素-c有关的问题的最有效的技术之一，包括细胞色素-c中血红素的结构和动力学、电子转移动力学、以及蛋白体折叠过程。 但是，共振拉曼光谱一直存在的一个缺点是它只能探索血红素的对称性振动模(gerade symmetry)，而血红素中铁离子的振动动力学完全由非对称振动模(ungerade symmetry)控制。 因而，对铁离子动力学重要的振动模或者不具有拉曼活性或者非常弱。 本课题项目的主要特点是利用双光子激发共振超拉曼光谱来研究细胞色素-c。作为一个三光子非线性散射技术，超拉曼光谱含有单光子红外光谱的选律，因而可以用来研究控制铁离子动力学的非对称振动模。 最终的目标是把双光子激发共振超拉曼光谱发展成为一个研究血红素蛋白结构和动力学的技术，并可以用来做高灵敏化学和生化分析检测，以及生物学和材料科学中的非线性光学成像。

603311.label: Realisation of objectives
603311.value: The objective of this project has been achieved by having successfully obtained the two-photon-excited surface-enhanced resonance hyper Raman spectra (SERHRS) and hyper Raman excitation profiles (HREPs) of three heme model compounds: Fe(III)-protoporphyirn-IX (Fe-PPIX), Fe(III)-hematoporphyrin-IX (Fe-HPIX) , and Fe(III)-deuteroporphyrin-IX (Fe-DPIX), respectively. To the best of our knowledge, our group is the first and the only one so far in the world to have achieved this goal. This achievement is significant in that it paved way for the study of two-photon-allowed electronic /vibronic excited states of metalloporphyrins and hemeproteins.

603311.label: Major findings and research outcome
603311.value: Our major findings include : (1) the two-photon-excited surface-enhanced resonance hyper Raman spectra (SERHRS) and hyper Raman excitation profiles (HREPs) for heme models such as Fe(III)-protoporphyirn-IX (Fe-PPIX), Fe(III)-hematoporphyrin-IX (Fe-HPIX) , and Fe(III)-deuteroporphyrin-IX (Fe-DPIX), can be obtained in high quality through appropriate sampling procedure. To the best of our knowledge, our group is the first and the only one so far to have achieved this goal which is significant for the application of nonlinear hyper Raman technique in chemistry, biology, and materials sciences; (The invited conference talk in 2013 and a paper in preparation). (2) the asymmetric effect of the peripheral substituents on porphyrin pi-skeleton to its electronic structure can indeed be revealed by SERHRS and HREPs; (The invited conference talk in 2013 and a paper in preparation). (3) the two-photon resonance effect alone is proven not strong enough to bring about the detectable hyper Raman scattering of asymmetrically-substituted porphyrins. The surface enhancement has to be invoked on top of the resonance effect to assure the successful acquisition of high quality hyper Raman spectra and HREPs of metalloporphyrins. (The invited conference talk in 2013 and a paper in preparation). (4) We therefore have spent a tremendous effort to develop plasmonic substrate(s) suitable for acquiring high quality hyper Raman spectra of metalloporphyrins and cytochrome-C. Two types of substrates have been developed and studied through this project. The first type is the size- and shape-controllable Cu2O nano-/meso-crystals which can serve as a sacrificing template for the fabrication of the dispersed Ag and Au nanoparticles for single-particle Raman and hyper Raman spectroscopy (This work is documented as a full article published in Journal of Physical Chemistry-C, 2014, and in a PhD thesis from my group in 2013) . The second type is the Ag fractals and dendrites for SEHRS and HREPs. High quality surface-enhanced Raman spectra (SERS) of cytochrome-c adsorbed on single Ag particles were obtained. (This work is documented in an invited conference talk in 2013 and in a PhD thesis from my group in 2011). (5) for the first time, a pure two-photon resonantly enhanced hyper Raman spectra and HREPs were obtained for a synthetic dipolar metalloporphyrin without the assistance of surface enhancement effect. (6) The interpretation of two-photon excited RHRS and HREPs turned out to be much more challenging than expected, due mainly the lack of a validated method for the estimation of the position and strength of two-photon allowed electronic states in metalloporphyrins.

603311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
603311.value: This project represents a persistent, painstaking and long-term effort in my group with an ultimate goal of developing the two-photon (and multi-photon)-excited nonlinear hyper Raman spectroscopy (HRS) into an optical technique readily employable in chemistry, biology, and materials sciences for both fundamental as well as application-oriented studies. It is a relatively long-term (and somewhat risky) project because it pursues the development of an unconventional nonlinear optical technique for which there are many "unknown" factors to be explored and studied systematically, from instrumentation to sampling, and from data acquisition to data interpretation and simulation. We believe that the HRS technique is worth our painstaking effort because, once developed and improved, it can be employed to acquire many information about molecules and materials that are otherwise not acquirable from any conventional linear optical techniques such as Raman and fluorescence spectroscopies. The achievements in this project represent a significant step forward along our ultimate goal. We are currently continue this project by seeking both internal and external fundings, and by a systematic exploration of all the major aspects of multi-photon-excited hyper Raman spectroscopy.

603311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
603311.value: Conventional optical techniques widely practiced in chemistry, biological science and materials sciences are linear in the sense that they all use one photon to excite the target molecules or materials for the signal generation. Such techniques include, for example, UV-visible and infrared absorption , fluorescence and Raman scattering(one-photon excited), among others. These techniques are relatively mature in terms of instrumentation, sampling, data acquisition and data interpretation, and are becoming routine techniques in research labs and various technological applications. On the other hand, a large realm of molecular properties, especially the nonlinear optical properties, are NOT acquirable from above linear optical techniques. Such properties are however critically important for many technological applications such as nonlinear optical (NLO) data storage, NLO imaging, and NLO optoelectronic devices. This project, as well as the long-term focus of my research group, is aimed at developing the nonlinear hyper Raman scattering (HRS) with two- or multi-photon excitation into a technique readily applicable in chemistry, biology and materials sciences.

603611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
603611.value: 在过去二十多年中，为了实现单分子电学器件，有许多关于测量单分子电导的报道。一个普遍接受的观点是单分子电导非常敏感的依赖于分子与电极的接触以及分子构型。因此，为了与理论作合理的比较，非常需要在测量单分子电导的同时能够在原子尺度准确分辨分子与电极的接触以及分子构型。但是，由于操纵及测量单分子很困难，实现完全满足这个要求的实验非常具有挑战性。在本研究计划中，我们目标发展一个有效的方法解决这一难题。 我们提议将特别设计的分子吸附在一个CuN/Cu(100)表面。这些分子的一端包含一个活性的功能团。表面具有有序分布的纳米尺度的CuN绝缘区和Cu导电区。当吸附在这样一个具纳米结构的异质表面，分子可以通过活性功能团与Cu紧密接触，而其余部分则弱吸附在CuN。这个吸附形态可以令我们使用扫描隧道显微镜及隧穿譜（STM/STS）研究分子中的电荷传输。当STM探针定位于分子的自由端时，分子被夹在金属衬底与探针之间。对于一个导电分子，隧穿电流经过真空结从探针流向分子，经过分子与金属接触点流到衬底。通过I-V譜就可以得到分子的有效电导。 有效电导包括了分子电导，真空结电导以及接触电导。通过系统的实验加上与有机合成及理论的合作，我们将研究一系列共轭分子体系，从而揭示分子电导与其构型及接触电极的关系。考虑到所有实验都是原位测量，并且在同一个分子上，这个方法为准确测量单分子电导提供了一个 解决方法。

603611.label: Realisation of objectives
603611.value: Object 1 is achieved in two studies: (1) vibronic-assisted transport of molecules with a tpe moiety anchored on CuN/Cu(100) surface, where the single molecular conductance was directly measured by G-z curve or deduced from a section of G-z curve with a certain molecular group attached to the tip.; (2) the satellite peaks in the differential conductance in the porphyrin oligomers measured using STM fishing technique. Object 2 is achieved in two studies: (1) using Cu and CuN as contact electrodes to manifest different conductance; (2) the delocalized empty molecular state is modulated by multiple metal contacts in a cooperative manner. We used coordination networks self-assembled on a Cu(111) surface provide a unique model system for systematic examination of molecules coupled with multiple metal contacts. Our studies, which discriminate the contribution of different contacts, reveal that a delocalized molecular state is modulated cooperatively by the electrodes. Object 3 is achieved in the study of using STM fishing technique to measure the conductance of single oligomers of different length. The molecular electronic structures, namely, frontier orbitals, of the bpo wires were spatially-resolved by tunneling spectroscopy. We found that, at resonant conditions, differential conductance decays with an exceptional low β of 0.017 Å−1 and with a remarkable high conductance exceeding 100 nS. Both values are, to our knowledge, records in the reported conjugated molecular systems. We observed rich characteristics including length-dependent conductance peak shifting and multiple satellite conductance peaks. Furthermore, we also measured the conductance of Y-shape branched bpo wires and found negative differential conductance (NDR) effects. We interpret our findings using a model in which resonant coupling occurs at the molecule-electrode junctions and hopping occurs at the molecular wire.

603611.label: Major findings and research outcome
603611.value: 1. We use cryogenic scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy and density-functional theory calculations to inspect the modulation of electronic states of aromatic molecules. The molecules are self-assembled on a Cu(111) surface forming molecular networks in which the molecules are in different contact configurations, including laterally coupled to different numbers of coordination bonds and vertically adsorbed at different heights above the substrate. We quantitatively analyze the molecular states and find that a delocalized empty molecular state is modulated by these multiple contacts in a cooperative manner: its energy is down shifted by 0:16 eV for each additional lateral contact and by 0.1 eV as the vertical molecule-surface distance is reduced by 0.1A in the physisorption regime. 2. Metal-molecule-metal junctions that contain molecular wires over distances of 5–10 nm are crucial components in molecular micro-electronic devices. Effective charge transport in this range is expected to be conceptually different from short molecules in which resonant conductance plays a central role. We study single-molecule conductance of biphenyl-linked poly-porphyrin oligomer (ppo) wires as long as 130 Å using scanning tunneling microscopy tip “fishing” technique The ppo wires were synthesized on a Au(111) surface through on-surface Ullmann coupling of 5,15-bis-(4-bromophenyl)-10,20-diphenyl porphyrin monomers. The molecular frontier orbitals of the ppo wires were spatially-resolved by tunneling spectroscopy. We observed multiple conductance peaks that are associated with resonant transport based on first-principles simulations. These peaks shift towards high bias voltage with increasing wire length. We found that the resonant conductance does not decay when the wire length exceeds 50 Å. We also investigated Fe-metalated ppo (Fe-ppo) wires and found the Fe centers do not affect the resonant conductance. Furthermore, we observed that Y-shape branched ppo wires exhibit negative differential conductance (NDR) effects.

603611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
603611.value: 1. Molecules connected with multiple contact electrodes are the key configuration in future molecule-based electronic devices. We have studied a system of a molecule with three contacts. It is a natural step to study molecules with four, five or more contacts in future. Our result clearly demonstrate such studies are feasible. 2. Molecular wires functionalized with metal centers are predicted to exhibit exceptional electric, magnetic and optic properties. Our investigation on the single-oligomer conductance opens door for similar measurements on the metal-functionalized molecular wires.

603611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
603611.value: Modern electronic devices (computer, ipad, iphone, etc) are made of silicon and other semiconductors. Nevertheless silicon technology is envisioned to be replaced by molecular technology in future owing to better energy efficiency, environmental friendly, lower cost and higher flexibility of the later. The major obstacle in the development of the molecule technology is it remains vague what factors control electric conductance of molecular wires. We have uncovered some fundamental insights of molecular conductance in this project. For the first time, we demonstrated that a molecular wire as long as 10 nm can conduct electric current efficiently without decaying. We also discovered that the conductivity of a molecule depends on the number of electrodes it is linked to. These findings will pave way of using single molecules or molecular wires in future molecule technology.

603711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
603711.value: Organoboron derivatives are useful synthetic intermediates in organic reactions with wide ranging applications from pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals to liquid crystals and conjugated materials. They can be prepared by metal-catalyzed hydroboration, diboration, dehydrogenative borylation and other boron addition reactions to unsaturated organics, as well as by metal-catalyzed borylation of carbon-hydrogen bonds in alkanes and arenes. Research over the past two decades has led to important advances in the direct conversion of unreactive carbon-hydrogen bonds in aliphatic and aromatic substrates to the carbon-boron bonds in alkyl- and arylboronates. Mechanistic studies of these reactions and their applications in synthesis have been extensive, but some phenomena associated with the borylation reactions cannot be explained from the current understanding of these reactions, in particular their regioselectivity issues. Further detailed investigation of the reaction mechanisms is needed to explain the experimental observations. In this project, we propose to undertake density functional theory calculations to explore some of the regioselectivity behavior observed in borylation reactions. This research work will guide future experimental work and help develop new applications in organic synthesis. 在有机化学反应中，有机硼衍生物是很重要的中间体。在制备药物，农药甚至液晶材料，都会用到它们。金属催化硼氢化，双硼化，去氢硼化，碳氢键硼化等是用来制备有机硼衍生物的方法。过去一二十年来，对碳氢键硼化方法研究很多，进展很快。对碳氢键硼化反应的机理研究也有很大的进展。尽管如此，很多有关碳氢键硼化反应的实验现象没能得到好的解释。这个研究计划主要是通过理论计算研究碳氢键硼化反应机理，从而解释实验中观察到的反应区域选择性现象。通过这个研究，我们希望能引导实验工作对碳氢键硼化方法发现新的应用。

603711.label: Realisation of objectives
603711.value: Objective 1: We have systematically calculated pKa values of C-H bonds in various arenes and heteroarenes and examined how C-H acidities affect the regioselectivity in transition metal catalyzed borylation/arylation reactions of arenes and heteroarenes. The correlation between C-H acidities and the regioselectivity in the borylation reactions has been well discussed. Objective 2: We have extended our theoretical studies to Pd-catalyzed C(sp3)-H and Cu-catalyzed aromatic C-H arylation reactions. In a recent book chapter (published in the book series of Structure and Bonding), we have systematically discussed reactivity and electronic structures of boryl ligands in various catalytic reactions.

603711.label: Major findings and research outcome
603711.value: DFT calculations have been carried out to study the Lewis base adduct of B2pin2 and the NHC (1,3-bis(cyclohexyl)imidazol-2-ylidene), which was proposed to act as a source of nucleophilic boryl groups in the β-borylation of α,β-unsaturated ketones. In solution, a rapid exchange of the NHC between the two boron centers was observed. Our DFT calculations reveal that the exchange involves dissociation and reassociation of NHC rather than an intramolecular process. DFT calculations have also been carried out to shed light on the reaction mechanism of copper-catalyzed reduction of CO2 with PhMe2Si–Bpin which leads to not only CO and PhMe2Si–O–Bpin, but also PhMe2-Si–C(O)–OBpin as an additional reduction product. With the aid of DFT calculations, we have studied the regioselectivity in Iridium-catalyzed C–H borylation of quinolines and unsymmetrical 1,2-disubstituted benzenes. We found a good correlation of the calculated pKa values for C–H bonds with the experimentally observed selectivity. We also carried out DFT Studies on Copper-Catalyzed Arylation of Aromatic C−H Bonds. The relationship between the overall reaction barrier and the acidity of the cleaved C−H bond was studied for various heterocycle and polyfluorobenzene substrates. Detailed mechanisms of the intramolecular C(sp3)–C(sp2) bond formation via C(sp3)–H bond activation of a trimethyl silyl (TMS) substituent catalyzed by palladium(0) complexes have been investigated. The results reveal that the favorable catalytic cycle includes oxidative addition, ligand substitution, concerted metalation deprotonation (CMD) and reductive elimination steps. During the deprotonation process of the TMS C(sp3)–H bond, the adjacent Si atom stabilizes the charge accumulated on the C(sp3)–H carbon and facilitates the C(sp3)–H bond activation due to the ability of Si to engage in Si–C hypervalent bonding. Transition metal boryl complexes play an important role as reactive intermediates in many catalytic processes. In a book chapter, we have discussed and reviewed the reactivities and electronic properties of boryl ligands, in particular their nucleophilic and electrophilic behaviors.

603711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
603711.value: Given the widespread applications of metal-catalyzed borylation reactions in synthetic organic chemistry, we expected that new catalytic processes towards practical applications will continue to be developed. The insights obtained from our studies of this project will contribute significantly to this expanding development. Therefore, expanding our research scope to establish a new face of atom economical C-H and C-C bond functionalization using rational catalyst design is apparently necessary.

603711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
603711.value: In this project, we've investigated issues related to transition metal catalyzed C-H bond activation reactions, which are important chemical processes in the synthesis of many pharmaceutical products. The results we've obtained are useful for researchers to find better catalysts for these important chemical reactions.
