604011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
604011.value: As pointed out by Ashkin, the significance of optical forces can be seen in a “back-of-envelope” calculation: by focusing a 0.1 W laser to a micron-sized particle and assuming a modest momentum absorption of ~10%, the resultant acceleration can reach 10^4 ms^-2. This “astronomical” acceleration implies a great potential. Indeed, this technique is having major impacts on many important fields that involve small particles. Our research is focused on optical micromanipulation – the manipulation of micron-sized particles by light. Optical micromanipulation has developed into a rapidly expanding branch of experimental science. However, the theoretical development is lagging significantly behind. For example, the modeling of the optical tweezers, invented 25 years ago, was not very successful until recent years. Indeed, the geometries and beams are difficult to model, and most theoretical works deal with over-simplified scenarios. We seek to model realistic experiments, and compare our results directly with published data and with our collaborators’ measurements. We will use the computational tools that we have developed, which include the generalized Mie theory for multiple spheres, boundary element method, discrete dipole approximation, vector Debye integral, and Maxwell stress tensor. We will also generalize these tools for some specific needs in modeling certain problems. We will expand the capabilities of our numerical programs to incorporate various realistic beams and geometries. Our final model will help predict new exciting phenomena in optical micromanipulation not yet realized by current experiments. We will be working closely with the experimental group led by Prof. Ou-Yang of Lehigh University. We aim at explaining experimental results from Prof. Ou-Yang at a quantitative level, and Prof. Ou-Yang will, in turn, conduct experiments to verify our theoretical predictions. We plan to carry out more research of this kind in this proposed project, with a focus on widely employed geometries and beams. Last but not least, the dynamics of light forces often give us new surprises, especially when complicated geometries or many particles are involved. As a complex system, multi-particle physics is always fascinating, but the non-conservative nature of light-induced forces adds to the complexity of dynamical phenomena, taking us to new frontiers that are not covered by the classical mechanics in standard texts. We seek to understand the complexity of having a non-conservative system, and to develop a comprehensive theory that is relevant to the light-matter interaction in the micron scale with forces induced by arbitrary geometries and beams. 正如Ashkin所說，光力的重要性明顯得可以從一個「信封背後的簡單計算」中得知:如果把僅僅0.1瓦的激光刀聚焦到一個微米大小的粒子上，即使假設只有10%的動量被粒子吸收，產生的加速度仍可達到10000 m/s^2。這種稱得上是天文數字的加速度暗示了這個領域的巨大潛能。事實上，光學微操控的技術已經對涉及微粒的許多重要領域產生了巨大的影響。 我們的研究主要集中在光學微操控方面，即用光對筷米量級的粒子進行操控。光學微操控已發展為實驗科學中一個快速發展的分支。然而，這方面的理論發展卻遠遠落後。比方說，早在25年前就被發明了的光镊，它的可理論要到最近才發展得比較完善。事實上，對實驗中的幾何體和光束的描述是很困難的，很多理論工作都是採用了過分簡化的模型。 我們的研究目的就是類比真實的實驗情景，從而可以直接用我們的計算結果來和已發表的實驗資料以及我們的合作者的測量資料相比較。我們使用的是我們自己開發的計算工具，包含的內容有：適用於多個球的推廣化Mie理論，邊界元方法，分立偶極近似法，向量Debye積分，以及麥克斯韋應力張量等。我們將豐富和完善我們的程式，以便能處理各種具體問題以及能包羅對多種真實光束和幾何體的計算。這種理論發展的意義在於，它能説明我們預測有趣的現象，而這些現象還未被實驗發現。 我們將會和Lehigh大學的歐陽教授實驗組開展緊密合作。我們詣在定量解釋歐陽教授的實驗結果，歐陽教授也能相應的通過實驗來證實我們的理論預測。我們計畫在這個方面做更多的研究，尤其針對廣泛採用的幾何體和光束。 最後要說的一個重點是，光學力的動力學性質經常為我們帶來新的驚喜，尤其是在我們考慮複雜幾何體或者多粒子問題的時候。作為一個複雜系統，多粒子物理總是很有吸引力，光致非保守力性質雖為研究其動力學問題增加了難度，但卻引導我們進入有別於教科書中經典力學的前沿領域。我們將嘗試理解非保守系統的複雜性，致力於發展一套有關在微米量級研究各種光和幾何體相互作用的全面理論。

604011.label: Realisation of objectives
604011.value: Objective 1: Computational tools were developed to handle realistic geometries and beams. For example, we developed the capability to compute forces on chiral structures (paper #2), light-induced stress on water droplet (paper #5), and the force induced by a pair of optical tweezers (paper #7). We considered realistic geometries (rotationally symmetric structures (paper #4), coated structures (paper #3), chiral structure (paper #2), etc) and beams (fundamental Gaussian beam, Lagurre Gaussian beam, etc in paper #2, #4, #5, and #7). We gained new and deeper understanding. For example, we discovered negative optical torque (paper #4), a novel type of optical binding induced by doubly scattered light (paper #7), etc. We computed results that can quantitatively agree with the experimental measurements (paper #7). Objective 2: We optimize and tailor the geometries and beam profiles in order to perform some specific tasks. By using chiral particle, we achieved optical pulling force (paper #2), where the chiral particle is pulled backward by a forward propagating beam. By using a core-shell structure, the optical force is optimized (paper #3). We discovered negative optical torque, which is easiest to find in structures with appropriate rotational symmetry. By using two focused beams, we achieved strong optical binding at low laser power, as well as a novel type of optical binding induced by doubly scattered light. Objective 3: We performed computational modeling of realistic trapping beams to optimize or achieve some novel functions. Beams we consider include fundamental Gaussian beam, Lagurre Gaussian beam, Bessel beam, etc. These beams are modified or combined to achieve different functionalities. For example, the low intensity optical binding in paper #7. Objective 4: This is achieved through paper #2, #4, and #7. The non-conservative force was found to induce a pulling force on a chiral particle (paper #2), and a negative optical torque on particles (usually with high rotational symmetries) (paper #4). In paper #7, the open or non-conservative nature of the system allowed the two partilces to emit radiation, which in turn induces the novel mode of optical binding. In short, we now gained deeper understanding in the nature of the non-conservative optical force, as well as its consequence and applications

604011.label: Major findings and research outcome
604011.value: (1) We proved the possibility of having negative optical torque: a particle can rotate in a direction opposite to the incident angular momentum, due to the recoil torque. Such phenomenon is non-trivil and totally unexpected. (2) We cooperated with the experimental group leaded by Prof. Daniel Ou-Yang (Lehigh University, USA) to work on optical bindng between a pair of particles illuminated by dual optical tweezers. In addition to the novel optical binding mode induced by doubly scattered light, we overcomed the non-trivial geometry and beam profile to achieve quanitative agreement between theory and experiment, which is rare in optical trapping. (3) We realized optical pulling force for a chiral particle, adding an additional control to chiral partcles when illuminated by light.

604011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
604011.value: As stated in objective 4. we gained deeper understanding about the theory of otpical binding and its non-conservative nature. The interplay between the nonconservative scattering and absorption force and the conservative gradient force is complex and exciting. Usually, the nonconservative scattering and absorption force is responsible particle transportation, while the conservative gradient force is responsible for particle trapping or localization. There is a lot room for fundamenal theories and practical applications to be explored.

604011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
604011.value: By overcoming the complicated geometry and beam profile involve in different types of optical trapping and binding, we study or discovered a series of phenomena, such as a novel form of optical binding, negative optical force, etc. We also ganed deep understanding about the theory of otpical binding and its non-conservative nature. Furthermore, we have made used of these fundamental understanding to achieve new applications.

604211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
604211.value: As free electrical charges are rarely stable, electrical dipoles (comprising a positive charge and a negative charge separated by a small distance, e.g., one Angstrom) are probably the most common form of electrical entities in Nature. There are many polar molecules so named because they possess permanent molecular dipoles. For example, the urea molecule has a fairly large dipole moment of 4.6 Debye (roughly an electronic charge separated from its opposite at a distance of one Angstrom), whereas the water molecule has a dipole moment of 1.9 D. The electrical manifestations of the molecular dipoles, however, are usually not very evident owing to either random orientations (such as in the liquid solution state) or to strong short range order (such as the anti-parallel coupling of two dipoles in a solid state). Both tend to cancel/mask molecular dipole's long-range electrical characteristics. Recently, it was discovered that under a moderate applied electric field, the molecular dipoles can be made to align at the contact regions of some especially fabricated nanoparticles, thereby leading to very large adhesion force between the nanoparticles. That is the basis of the so-called giant electrorheological (GER) effect, and it represents a manifestation of the tremendous energy present in molecular dipoles that may be harnessed. Continued research into this new class of materials, by using the GROMACS molecular dynamics package [1-9] to simulate a mixture of urea molecules with silicone oil chains (both known experimentally to be crucial to the GER effect) has resulted in the finding that the GER effect can be accounted for by the formation of aligned molecular dipole filaments induced by the confinement effect of silicone oil chains [10]. This recognition has broadened our horizon beyond the GER effect, into the realm of molecular dipole manipulations using nanoscale interfaces and electric fields. This proposal will build upon our understanding of the molecular dipole filament formation process obtained so far and explore, through both simulations and experiments, the interesting prospects of spontaneous filaments formation and the growth of aligned molecular filaments that are mesoscopic/macroscopic in length. Successful completion of this project will not only further enhance our understanding of this interesting phenomenon, but may also contribute to a strategy for harnessing the tremendous electrical energy stored in molecular dipoles for useful purposes. 由於大部分自由電荷是不穩定的,電偶極子(包括中心相互錯開的正電荷和負電荷)可能是自然界中最常見的電荷存在形式。許多分子具有固有電矩,這類分子因此被稱為極性分子。例如,尿素分子有一個4.6D的固有電矩,這是一個相當大的電偶極矩,大約相當於一個電子電量的正負電荷被分離一個埃米;而水分子的固有電矩為1.9 D。但是,由於分子的隨機取向(如溶液狀態)或強短程式(如兩個偶極子反平行耦合),分子固有電矩的表現通常是很不明顯的。二者都傾向于抵消或掩蓋分子偶極子的長程電學特性。最新研究發現,在適當的外加電場下,納米顆粒的接觸區域中的分子偶極子可以在電場方向排列起來,從而導致納米顆粒之間的非常大的粘附力。這是巨電流變(GER)效應的基礎,也揭示了分子偶極子體系中具有巨大的可利用能量。作為對這種新材料的進一步研究,GROMACS分子動力學套裝軟體[1-9]被用來類比矽油鏈與尿素分子的混合物。這兩種物質在實驗中對於GER效應是至關重要的。研究發現,矽油鏈約束效應引起的沿電場方向排列的分子偶極子細絲狀結構的形成可以導致GER效應 [10]。這一認識將我們的視野從GER效應拓展到一個新的領域,即利用納米尺度介面和電場來控制分子偶極子。這項研究計畫將建立在我們目前所取得的對分子偶極子絲狀結構的形成過程的理解的基礎上,通過類比和實驗來探討絲狀結構的自發形成過程和介觀/宏觀長度的極性分子絲的生長等有趣的現象。這一專案的成功完成將不僅進一步提高我們對這一有趣現象的理解,還可能有助於發展出利用儲存在分子偶極子中巨大電能的有效策略,具有應用前景。

604211.label: Realisation of objectives
604211.value: We have carried out investigations on all three objectives. On the first objective, the water filaments were found to be stable in silicone oil under an electric field, beyond nanoseconds. However, only very short segments of the urea filaments were found to be stable beyond a few picoseconds. On the second objective, we have carried out both simulations and experiments on using water molecules for the formation of the filaments, with gap size that varies from a millimeter down to a few microns. Amazingly, we found an all-liquid electrorheological effect that can be very large with small gaps. The implication is that water molecules can indeed form macroscopic filaments that penetrate the silicone oil, when an electric field is applied. However, attempts by using urea have all failed, indicating that urea molecules cannot form long filaments beyond 9 nm. These results are consistent with the simulation findings. The third objective is already covered by the above description.

604211.label: Major findings and research outcome
604211.value: The major findings of this project are that (1) under the application of an electric field, water molecules for form filaments that penetrate the silicone oil to bridge the two sides of a macroscopic gap, ranging from a few microns to a millimeter, (2) such filaments can give rise to the electrorheological effect, i.e., greatly impede the flow of the silicone oil, because the dipoles in these filaments are mostly aligned along the electric field direction, and (3) the above effect vanishes when the silicone oil is replaced by decane, a common hydrocarbon oil. The latter indicates that the effect is oil-specific. On the last page of this report, please see Figure 1 for how the experiments were done. By varying the gap size, we were able to obtain the electrorheological effect. The data are summarized in Figures 2(a) and (b) on the last page of this report. Through simulations the dipoles of the water molecules in the filaments are mostly aligned along the electric field direction. Hence, these filaments represent giant dipoles bridging the gap, as shown in Figure 2(c). A simple theory can be formulated by considering the electrical interaction energies of the charges. The net result is that whereas the experiment yields the experimental linear (dimensionless) slope of the quadratic electric field variation to be 6 (since pressure has the same unit as energy density, and electric field squared gives energy density as well), the simple theory yields 8.8. A patent application has been filed on this important result (see attached). Publication will soon follow. In a separate development, the PI of this proposal has also developed a new theory on a very old topic—the electrokinetic effect. By starting from first principles, the PI and his collaborators were able to re-derive the Poisson-Boltzmann equation and to extend the theory application into nanochannels. A major publication is the result of this effort and is hereby attached to this report.

604211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
604211.value: The all-liquid electrorheological effect is very novel and might have potential applications. A provisional patent application has been filed, and attached to this report is an IDF (Invention Disclosure Form) that we have filled out. In the IDF one might find additional details about our research results. Additional studies, both in theory and in experiment, are being pursued. Of course, a publication will certainly result from this project in due course. On our new theory of the electrokinetic effect, involving the charge-separation effect that can occur in some solid-liquid interfaces, we are currently pursuing many different directions, including the explanation of the so-called isoelectronic effect and the Donnan potential that was observed for nanochannels.

604211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
604211.value: Electrical dipole, comprising a positive charge and a negative charge separated by a small distance, like one Angstrom (10-8 cm), is probably the most common electrical entity in the physical world. This is because bare charges are energetically un-favored to have a long existence before being neutralized by a counter charge, whereas dipoles, being electrically neutral, can be stable. Many molecules in our universe possess permanent electrical dipoles, such as the water molecules or the urea molecules. However, although it is well known that the dipoles like to align and form a filament since such a configuration is energetically favored, up to the present no one has observed the physical formation of such long filaments of aligned dipoles, mainly owing to the unfavorable entropic considerations, as well as to the large energy involved in separating the head and tail charges in such giant dipolar filaments. In our present study, we have observed precisely the formation of such macroscopic dipolar chains, in the water/silicone oil system. This discovery has many implications. One is the all-liquid electrorheological effect, meaning turning liquid into solid-like by simply applying an electric field. And that effect has been observed.

604411.label: Project Objectives
604411.value: To design and synthesize a new family of chiral Brønsted acids featuring an unprecedented combination of high acidity and chirality; To evaluate their catalytic ability for intramolecular and intermolecular asymmetric hydrofunctionalizations of unactivated olefins; To evaluate the scope of these processes and optimize them when necessary, and ultimately achieve general and mild conditions for high chemical efficiency and excellent enantioselectivity.

604411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
604411.value: The ability to prepare functionalized chiral organic molecules efficiently from cheap materials is of central importance to organic synthesis, medicinal chemistry, and pharmaceutical industry. The aims of this work are (1) to design and synthesize a new family of chiral Brønsted acids with an unprecedented combination of enhanced acidity and chirality ("handedness"); (2) to evaluate the catalytic capability of these acids for asymmetric hydrofunctionalizations of unactivated olefins, a longstanding challenge that has not been solved by metal catalysis; and (3) to optimize these carbon-carbon and carbon-heteroatom bond-forming processes in terms of both chemical efficiency and stereoselectivity. The use of small organic (non-metal) molecules, such as chiral Brønsted acids, as catalysts represents an exciting alternative to metal-based approaches and plays an important role in achieving green chemistry. We anticipate that the catalysis enabled by these newly designed acids will not only open a conceptually different door for addressing this longstanding challenge, but also provide rapid and practical access to a wide variety of important families of chiral compounds that will benefit many aspects of human life, from public health to environmental protection. 由廉價材料開始高效合成手性有機分子對有機合成以及醫藥化學等具有重要意義。本項目將設計合成一類新型的同時具有強酸性和高度不對稱性的布朗斯特酸，並且通過對反應條件的優化等途徑將這類化合物應用於催化烯烴的不對稱官能團化反應中。將有機小分子作為不對稱催化劑是對金屬催化的一個非常重要的補充。該項目的成功實現將不僅實現烯烴的不對稱官能團化反應這一挑戰，更重要的是，從長遠來看，這類有機分子催化將對我們的公共衛生以及環境保護起重要的促進作用。

604411.label: Realisation of objectives
604411.value: In this project, we have successfully designed and synthesized a range of new chiral Brønsted acids and evaluated their catalytic ability in various type of reactions, including hydrofunctionalizations of olefins, desymmetrization of oxetanes and azetidines. In general, the objectives are realized with good understanding of these catalysts and reactions. (1) We have designed and synthesized a range of fluorinated chiral Brønsed acids. These chiral acids do have stronger acidity and catalytic ability. In the meanwhile, we also synthesize their analogues. A library of various chiral Brønsed acids has been established in our laboratory. (2) We have evaluated their catalytic ability in a wide range of organic reactions, including the intramolecular and intermolecular asymmetric hydrofunctionalizations of olefins. The fluorinated chiral Brønsted acids do have stronger acidity and show higher catalytic ability than normal chiral phosphoric acids. In the meanwhile, we also evaluated their catalytic ability in related reactions using strain ring substrates, such as oxetanes and azetidines. The properties of these new catalysts have been understood. (3) We have achieved a range of new catalytic asymmetric processes with the synthesized acids. After optimization, we found that best chiral induction could be achieved. With these processes, a range of chiral building blocks could be synthesis with excellent efficiency and enantioselectivity.

604411.label: Major findings and research outcome
604411.value: In this project, we have developed the following new catalytic processes and utilized these processes for the synthesis of biologically useful molecules. (1) Efficient catalytic asymmetric multicomponent aza-Diels-Alder reaction of indoles with oxetane as directing group and the utilization in the synthesis of complex bioactive alkaloid-type polycycles. It is the first catalytic asymmetric three-component aza-Diels−Alder reaction of indoles as the dienophile. In this reaction, oxetane has been demonstrated for the first time as a superb directing group. (2) Chiral phosphoric acid catalyzed enantioselective desymmetrization of meso-epoxides by thiols. It is the first chiral Brønsted acid catalyzed asymmetric nucleophilic ring-opening reaction of meso-epoxides. A range of cyclic and acyclic meso-epoxides could undergo smooth ring-opening reactions with moderate to high efficiency and enantioselectivity. The enantioenriched 1,2-difunctionalized products with vicinal stereocenters are versatile chiral building blocks towards useful molecules, such as chiral free thiols. (3) Catalytic enantioselective assembly of tetrahydroisoquinolines and their analogues bearing a C-4 stereocenter. Direct and general methods for the assembly of tetrahydroisoquinolines bearing a C-4 stereocenter was an unmet challenge before our work. In this reaction, we realized a new multicomponent organocatalytic process that not only establishes the THIQ skeleton efficiently, but also concomitantly generates the C-4 stereocenter with high enantioselectivity. (4) Enantio- and diastereoselective assembly of tetrahydrofuran and tetrahydropyran skeletons with all-carbon quaternary stereocenters. In this reaction we realized a new asymmetric desymmetrization reaction for the assembly of tetrahydrofuran and tetrahydropyran skeletons with simultaneous generation of two stereocenters (tertiary and all-carbon quaternary) with high efficiency and stereoselectivity. It also represents a new reaction type (acetalization) for the catalytic asymmetric desymmetrization of meso 1,3-diols. (5) Enantioselective formation of all-carbon quaternary stereocenters from indoles and ortho-quinone methides generated from tertiary alcohols bearing an ortho-hydroxy group. This is an unprecedented catalytic asymmetric intermolecular process for the efficient formation of acyclic all-carbon quaternary stereocenters from racemic tertiary alcohols. The reaction features excellent stereocontrol and intermolecular C−C bond formation efficiency, overcoming the competing elimination pathway (E1) and significant steric hindrance around the reactive center. (6) A highly efficient synthesis of dihydronaphthalenes from isobenzopyrylium ions. It is a new addition to the small family of catalytic asymmetric synthesis of the important dihydronaphthalene scaffolds. Our reaction represents the first demonstration of excellent asymmetric induction on the planar isobenzopyryliums without an anchoring group. The excellent stereocontrol is presumably attributed to the unusual chiral counteranion generated in situ from the chiral phosphate and the boronic acid nucleophile as well as the leaving group.

604411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
604411.value: As an extension of this project, the development of additional useful catalytic asymmetric reactions catalyzed by chiral Bronsted acids will continue to be our topic of pursuit in this area. In particular, we will employ the highly acidic fluorinated chiral Bronsted acids to demonstrate more useful and uniquely effective reactions. We already demonstrated some of the electron-rich and normal olefins to be possible good substrates compatible with these catalysts, further optimization to achieve better selectivity will be the next stage of optimization.

604411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
604411.value: In this project, enabled by the design, synthesis and evaluation of a type of chiral Bronsted acids, we have realized a range of new organic processes with excellent efficiency and selectivity. These processes demonstrated the ability of effective catalysts in the synthesis of useful chiral molecules that have potential utility in medicinal chemistry, and pharmaceutical industry. With chiral Bronsted acids. In these reactions, new bonds (such as carbon-carbon and carbon-heteroatom bonds) are selectively formed with excellent stereocontrol. With these non-metal catalysts, the reactions also have good potential to achieve green synthesis in view of their environmentally benignity. These findings will not only contribute to addressing this longstanding challenges in organic synthesis, but also benefit many aspects of human life, from public health to environmental protection.

604711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
604711.value: Much effort has been devoted to the synthesis of conjugated polymers due to their potential high-tech applications in organic electronics systems. A variety of polymerization reactions have been developed, many of which, however, suffer from difficult monomer preparations and troublesome product purifications. Other common disadvantages of the “conventional” polymerization reactions include regio- and stereo-irregularity in polymer structure and poor atom economy due to the generation of large amounts of byproducts that are often difficult to remove. This calls for exploration of new effective polymerization reactions. Our research group has been actively working on the utilization of acetylene reactions for the development of new polymerization processes. It is known that transition metal-catalyzed reactions of terminal arylacetylenes with aroyl chlorides or aryl aldehydes readily produce (chloro)vinylarenes, arylenones, and arylynones in regio- and stereo-selective fashion. In this research project, we plan to develop these organic reactions into useful polymerization tools for syntheses of new conjugated polymers. We aim to invent new polymerization techniques with such merit as simple monomer preparation, good atom economy, excellent structural regularity, and easy polymer purification. New monomers with high polymerizability will be designed, effective catalyst systems will be searched, and optimal polymerization conditions will be established, in order to synthesize new conjugated polymers with high molecular weights, good macroscopic processability, and excellent regio- and stereo-regularity. Functional groups will be integrated into the polymer structures, in an effort to create new materials with useful electronic, optical, photonic, and magnetic properties. The new polymers will be tested as active materials for the construction of polymer light-emitting diodes, photovoltaic cells, fluorescent sensors, etc. It is anticipated that this project will establish effective synthetic routes that enable ready access to a large variety of new conjugated polymers with novel structures and advanced functionalities. 聚合物在高科技有机光电子体系中有巨大的潜在应用价值，因而很多研究人员致力于共轭聚合物的化学合成工作。现已发展出了多种聚合反应方法，但仍然存在单体制备困难、产物提纯繁琐的问题。另外，聚合反应普遍存在着一些问题，如：聚合物结构的立构规整性差，大量副产物导致原料的浪费，并且难以除尽。因而，探索发展一种新型、高效的聚合反应方法就显得尤为重要。 我们研究组积极致力于以乙炔为反应物发展新的聚合反应过程的研究工作。采用金属催化反应的方法很容易将芳基乙炔与芳基酰氯、芳基醛反应制得立构选择性的氯化芳基乙烯、芳基烯酮和芳基炔酮。通过本项目的研究，我们将进一步发展这些化学反应方法，使其成为合成新型共轭聚合物的有效工具。我们的目标是发明一种新的聚合技术，使其具有单体制备简单、反应效率高、结构选择性优良以及易于聚合物纯化等优点。 我们将设计具有高反应活性的新单体，寻求有效的催化剂体系，优化聚合反应条件，从而制备高分子量的新型共轭聚合物，使其具有优良的宏观加工性能和良好的立构规整性。在共轭聚合物分子链中引入功能性基团，可以制得具有光、电、磁性能的新型功能材料，这些聚合物材料可以用于制备有机发光二极管、光电池和荧光传感器等。通过本项目的研究，我们将建立有效的合成路线，制备一系列结构新颖、具有先进功能特性的共轭聚合物。

604711.label: Realisation of objectives
604711.value: The purpose of this proposed research is to (a) develop new effective polymerization routes to conjugated polymers, (b) search for new catalyst systems and optimization of polymerization processes, (c) synthesize new polymers with structural regularity and advanced functionality, and (d) explore the potential technological applications of the new functional polymers. Through elaborate efforts in the past three years, we believe we have completed all the objectives. To achieve the goals, we develop an efficient one-pot three-component polymerization route to functional poly(arylene thiophenylene)s (PATs). The polymerization of aromatic diyne, diaroyl chloride, and ethyl 2-mercaptoacetate catalyzed by Pd(PPh3)2Cl2/CuI proceeds smoothly under mild conditions at room temperature without strict stoichiometric balance of the monomers, affording PATs with high molecular weights in excellent yields. The PATs possesses good solubility in common organic solvents, good film-forming ability and high thermal stability with aggregation-enhanced emission characteristics. Their thin films show high refractive indices in a wide wavelength region of 400−1000 nm. They exhibit very high modified Abbe´ numbers, which are indicative of very low optical dispersions in the telecommunication important wavelength region. Well-resolved fluorescent photopatterns can be generated by UV irradiation of the polymer thin films through copper photomasks. The polymers can serve as efficient fluorescent chemosensors for ruthenium(III) ion detection with high sensitivity and selectivity. We also synthesize soluble and regular poly(dipropargyl amine)s (PDAs) with high molecular weights (Mw up to 43 800) in high yields (up to 89%) by three-component polycoupling reactions of diynes, primary amines, and aldehydes catalyzed by copper(I) chloride in toluene at 100 °C for 2 h. The polymerization reaction is insensitive to moisture. All the PDAs are thermally stable and film forming. The tetraphenylethene or silole-containing PDAs exhibit a phenomenon of aggregation-induced emission, whose aggregates can function as sensitive fluorescent chemosensors for detecting explosives, such as picric acid, 2,4-dinitrotoluene and 4-nitrobenzoyl chloride with large quenching constants.

604711.label: Major findings and research outcome
604711.value: Development of new polymerization reactions for the synthesis of new polymers is a fundamental important research area in macromolecular science. In this investigation, we explored the utility of multi-component organic coupling reactions into useful tools for the construction of new conjugated polymers. We explore the first tandem polymerization for the synthesis of conjugated polymers. The three-component tandem reaction of alkyne, aroyl chloride, and ethyl 2-mercaptoacetate was developed into an efficient polymerization technique for the preparation of polythiophenes with structural regularity, processability and advanced functionality. Tetraphenylethene (TPE)-containing diyne was synthesized as one of the building blocks because TPE is a well-known fluorophore with unique aggregation-induced emission (AIE) characteristic, which will endow its polymers with strong solid-state emission and hence many high-technological applications. The polymerization of diyne, diaroyl chloride, and ethyl 2-mercaptoacetate can proceed under mild conditions to afford linear poly(arylene thiophenylene) with high molecular weights in high yields. The conjugated polymers exhibit good solubility, good thermal stability, high light refractivity and aggregation-enhanced emission property. It can generate well-resolved fluorescent photopattern under UV irradiation and can also be utilized as a selective and sensitive fluorescent chemosensor for the detection of metal ions with a superamplification effect. We also demonstrate that the polycoupling reactions of diynes, primary amines, and aldehydes can be carried out at a lower temperature of 100 °C for only 2 h in the presence of a less expensive catalyst of copper(I) chloride without the exclusion of moisture, furnishing soluble poly(dipropargylamine)s (PDAs) with high molecular weights in high yields. The obtained PDAs are thermally stable. Their thin films show high refractive indices. The PDAs carrying TPE and silole chromophores exhibit a phenomenon of AIE, and their aggregates can function as sensitive fluorescent chemosensors for explosive detection. As you can see in Part C of this report, more than 20 publications have arisen from this research project. Most of the papers are published in journal articles with high citation indexes. We are confident that further research in this field will lead to more fruitful result.

604711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
604711.value: Development of efficient organic reactions into useful polymerization tools has always been a hot topic in polymer research. In this investigation, we have developed new synthetic routes to conjugated polymers from alkyne-based organic reactions. By exploration of new catalysts and optimization of recation conditions, we have prepared poly(arylene ynonylene), poly(arylene thiophenylene), poly(dipropargyl amine)s and poly(triazole)s with high molecular weights in high yields. We have investigated their properties and found that they are soluble and thermally stable. They show unique functional properties, such as aggregation-induced emission, emission superquenching in the detection of explosives and metal ions, light refractivity and photopatterning, making them promising for use in electronics, optics and biological fields. Because we have obtained promising results, we are still working on the development of new synthetic tools to new conjugated polymers, investigating their properties and exploring their practical applications. If we are able to get further support from RGC, we will hire experts to explore further the high-technological applications of our polymers in the fabrication of optoelectronic devices such as photovoltaic cells and field-effect transitors and fluorescent biological probes.

604711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
604711.value: The development of new polymerization reactions is of critical importance to macromolecular science. Herein, new methodologies for the construction of poly(arylene ynonylene), poly(arylene thiophenylene) and poly(dipropargyl amine)s are proposed. All the conjugated polymers are synthesized with high molecular weights in high yields. They are soluble and show high thermal stability. Some of them display enhanced light emission in the solid state and work as fluorescent chemosensors for explosives and metal ions with high sensitivity. Most of the conjugated polymers show very high refractive indices. UV irradiation of their films through copper masks generates fluorescent patterns with good resolutions. Materials with such attributes are anticipated to find an array of high-technological applications.

605011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
605011.value: Topological insulators (TIs) differ from ordinary band insulators by the presence of gapless edge or surface states, which are protected by time reversal symmetry. As a new state of matter, it not only has potential applications in spintronics and quantum computing, but also provides a new and rich platform for fundamental physics studies. Recently, angle resolved photoemission spectroscopy measurement has clearly identified Bi2Se3 and Bi2Te3 as 3D TIs with only a single Dirac cone on the surface. However, the transport study of 3D TIs is just at the beginning. The magnetic impurity effect, the finite-size effect, the coupling effect between the surface and bulk states, and the hexagonal warping effect on the transport properties of 2D topological surface states are all waiting to be explored. The realization of the surface quantum Hall effect, the quantum spin Hall effect in the ultra-thin limit, and the new magneto-resistance effect present new challenges in the transport study of topological insulators. In this project, we propose to explore these new transport properties associated with 2D topological surface states in molecular beam epitaxy grown topological insulator Bi2Se3 and Bi2Te3. We will design and fabricate gated and mesoscopic devices. We aim to reveal and test theoretically predicted new transport phenomena including the surface quantum Hall effect, the quantum spin Hall effect in the ultra-thin limit, and the new magneto-resistance effect. We believe that the fulfillment of this project will greatly advance our understanding of the transport properties of 2D topological surface states, and the successful outcome of this project will pave the way for future applications of topological insulators. 拓扑绝缘体由于存在着没有带隙的受时间反演对称性保护的边缘或表面态而有别于一般的绝缘体。作为一种新的物质形态，它不仅在自旋电子学和量子计算方面有潜在的应用，而且给基础物理研究提供了一个崭新而且多样的研究平台。最近，角分辨光电子发射谱的研究已经清楚表明Bi2Se3和Bi2Te3是三维的拓扑绝缘体而且其表面仅有一个狄拉克锥。然而，对三维拓扑绝缘体输运特性的研究才刚刚开始。磁性杂质效应，有限尺寸效应，表面电子态和体电子态的耦合，以及表面电子费米面的六角形弯曲对二维拓扑表面态输运特性的影响还有待进一步的研究。在超薄的薄膜上实现表面量子霍尔效应和量子自旋霍尔效应，以及发掘新奇的磁阻效应都是对拓扑绝缘体输运特性研究提出的挑战。在这个研究计划里，我们将在分子束外延生长的拓扑绝缘体上研究与二维拓扑表面态相关的新奇输运特性。我们将设计并制备栅压调控的和位于介观尺度的器件。我们将揭示和检验理论上预言的各种输运现象，包括在超薄条件下的表面量子霍尔效应和量子自旋霍尔效应，还有各种新奇的磁阻效应。我们相信该计划的成功实施将极大的加深我们对二维拓扑表面态输运特性的了解，并且为将来拓扑绝缘体的实际应用打下坚实的基础。

605011.label: Realisation of objectives
605011.value: We have identified surface states associated transport properties such as weak antilocalization (WAL) effect and linear magnetoresistance (LMR). We have observed that LMR is quenched due to the coupling effect between the surface states and the bulk states when Bi2Se3 layers become ultra-thin. We have fabricated nano-patterned devices with anti-dots and we are able to tune electron-electron interaction in these devices. We have discovered the 2D interface superconductivity in Bi2Te3/FeTe bi-layer samples, which is believed to associate with surface states. We have also studied various growth mechanism of MBE TI thin films. We have made devices with front gate. However, due to very high bulk electron concentration the gate tunablity is limited (less than 20%). We have also attempted to make FM/TI tunnel junction devices but with limited success due to poor quality of tunnel barriers.

605011.label: Major findings and research outcome
605011.value: We have observed linear magneto-resistance in high magnetic field in topological insulator Bi2Se3 films. This linear magneto-resistance is associated with the gapless topological surface states. In the ultra-thin limit, the surface and bulk states coupling quenches the linear magneto-resistance. This work was published as No.1 in Part C. We have successfully obtained a high Miller index Bi2Se3 epifilm by MBE on an InP(001) substrate. ARPES measurements show an anisotropic Fermi surface. Transport studies show up to a factor of 4.4 difference between the parallel and transverse resistivity. This work was published as No.2 in Part C. We have grown single-domain epitaxial Bi2Se3 films on InP(111)A substrate by MBE. Nucleation of Bi2Se3 proceeds in the step-flow growth mode. The SdH oscillations observed are attributed to Landau quantization of the bulk states of electrons. This work is published as No.3 in Part C. We have investigated anisotropic transport in high index (221) topological insulator Bi2Se3 films. The nonlinear Hall effect at high temperatures and a non-saturating LMR are observed in high magnetic fields. This work is published as No.4 in Part C. We have investigated of the superconducting proximity effect in Nb/Bi2Te3 structure. Transport measurements show that an upturn of the resistance occurs below the Nb superconducting transition temperature. We explain these phenomena in terms of an energy barrier effect induced by the Nb superconducting gap and the suppression of Andreev reflection due to the low transparency at the Nb-Bi2Te3 interface. This work is published as No.5 in Part C. We have discovered 2D superconductivity at the interface on a Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructure. It is induced by the Bi2Te3 epilayer with thickness even down to one quintuple layer. Transport measurements show the two-dimensional nature of the observed superconductivity with the highest transition temperature around 12 K. This work is published as No.7 in Part C. We have found superconductivity in Fe1+xTe/Bi2Te3 bilayer samples. It is found that the growth is governed by a unique interfacial chemical reaction scheme. This work is published as No.6 in Part C. Transport study reveals the occurrence of a spontaneous vortex glass phase transition in the superconducting Fe1-xTe films. This work is published as No.8 in Part C.. We have fabricated the nano patterned Bi2Te3 devices with antidots. The main observation is that the denser antidots in TI thin films suppress the localization tendency of conduction electrons. This work is published as No.9 in Part C.

605011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
605011.value: What we have achieved so far indicating that reducing bulk carrier concentration in 3D topological insulators are the most important issue to be addressed in future. The ways to reduce bulk carrier concentration include to grow ternary or quaternary Bi-based alloys and to employ chemical vapor deposition growth technique. These should be future actions to be taken.

605011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
605011.value: Topological insulators (TIs) differ from ordinary band insulators by the presence of gapless edge or surface states. In this projects, we mainly studied transport properties MBE grown 3D TIs Bi2Se3 and Bi2Te3 thin film samples. We have identified surface states associated transport properties such as weak antilocalization effect and linear magnetoresistance. We are able to tune electron-electron interaction in TIs. We have discovered the 2D interface superconductivity in Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructure, which is believed to associate with surface states. All these results indicate the topological insulators are fertile ground for discovery new physics.

605311.label: Project Title(Chinese)
605311.value: 粗糙表面润湿现象的研究和数学模拟

605311.label: Project Objectives
605311.value: Develop and implement an efficient numerical method for simulation of the two-phase fluid flow on rough surfaces. We will design an unconditional stable numerical method with energy decaying property. The method will be implemented on domains with various rough surfaces with striped patterns, regular lattices of posts or chemical patches or random isolated heterogeneities in both two and three dimensions. Study roughness induced superhydrophobicity and liquid imbibition. We will study the behavior of the liquid droplets on rough surfaces and chemically patterned surfaces. The validity of the Wenzel and Cassie-Baxter equations will be studied. We will also explore the transition mechanism between the Cassie-Baxster and the Wenzel states, as well as the dynamics of the liquid imbibition. Carry out simulations and analysis of the contact angle hysteresis on rough surfaces. We will investigate contact angle hysteresis on the chemically patterned and rough surfaces, as the drop volume is changed or as the drop is pushed. We will study how the patterning, the position, size, and spacing of the posts affects the contact angle hysteresis. The effects of random patterning on the advancing and receding contact angle and the difference of the contact angle hysterresis of the collapsed drop (Wenzel state) and the suspended drops (Cassie-Baxter state) will also be studied. We will study analytically the contact angle hysteresis based on a phase field model on a simple chemically patterned surface. Explicit relation between the contrast of the pattern and contact angle hysteresis will be calculated from a reduced model obtained from the sharp interface limit. This will provide some insights on how the energy barrier relates to the roughness of the surface.

605311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
605311.value: Controlling the wettability of solid materials is a classical and key issue in surface engineering. One of the ways to increase the hydrophobic or hydrophilic properties of a surface is to increase the surface roughness, so roughness-enhanced wetting has become the subject of extensive investigation. Wetting of surfaces is characterized by a so called 'contact angle' (see Fig. 1). The contact angle on a flat surface is governed by the Young's equation. On rough surfaces, the contact angle is believed to be governed by the Wenzel and Cassie-Baxter equations. The contact angle hysteresis proves to be an important quantity that determines the motion and properties of the droplets on the surfaces. Understanding of how the patterning or roughness of the surface affects contact angle and contact angle hysteresis is of critical importance in surface engineering. A lot of progresses have been made recently on modeling multi-phase flow and fluid solid interfacial phenomena. In a recent work [26], we introduced a new mathematical model with generalized Navier boundary condition to resolve the long standing moving contact line problem for the two phase flow. In this project, this new model is employed to investigate the roughness enhanced wetting and contact angle hysteresis numerically and analytically. The results obtained will provide deeper understanding of wetting on rough surface. 控制固体表面的湿润性是表面工程学中一个极为重要的问题。增加表面的疏水或亲水性的一个方式是改变表面的粗糙度，这一课题近年来被广泛关注。 表面湿润性可由所谓的接触角来所描述。 粗糙面的接触角则应该由Wenzel和Cassie-Baxster方程来决定。接触角滞后量被证明对理解液滴在表面上的形态和移动有着决定的作用。近年来我们提出了一个以广义Navier边界条件为主的的新的数学模型并用以解决了两相流领域里长期悬而未决的移动的接触线问题。 在本研究项目中，这个新的模型将被用作数学分析和数值模拟来研究固体表面的湿润性和接触角滞后问题。 我们相信由此得到的结果将加深我们对粗糙表面的湿润性的理解。

605311.label: Realisation of objectives
605311.value: 1. We developed an efficient numerical method for the two phase moving contact line problem with variable density, viscosity, and slip length. To overcome the difficulties due to large density and viscosity ratio, the Navier–Stokes equations are solved by a splitting method based on a pressure Poisson equation [11], while the Cahn–Hilliard equation is solved by a convex splitting method. We show that the method is stable under certain conditions. The method allows us to simulate the interface problems with extremely small interface thickness. 2. We studied the quasi-static motion of two-phase flows on topologically rough surfaces is studied. By considering the Gibbs free energy of the system, we first consider the Cassie and Wenzel states transition on rough surfaces. It has been found that the crucial conditions for the two different states depend on the equilibrium contact angle, the droplet size and its initial position. Then the contact angle hysteresis on roughness induced superhydrophobic surfaces is investigated. We found that there are multiple local minimums and one global minimum for the Gibbs free energy landscape, which can reveal the mechanism of the stick-slip phenomena. When the scale of roughness becomes smaller, the stick-slip becomes weaker and the apparent contact angle will get closer to the Cassie-Baxter’s angle. Numerical simulations of a phase field model agree very well with the analytical results. 3. We derived a system for the dynamics of the contact angle and contact point in the sharp interface limit. From the behaviour of the solution of the contact angle dynamic equation, we observe stick-slip motion and contact angle hysteresis. Our analysis reveals the mechanism for the asymmetric speed dependent contact angle hysteresis observed experimentally.

605311.label: Major findings and research outcome
605311.value: We have developed efficient numerical methods for two phase field model in both finite difference and finite element formulations. Four papers ( see Part C [1,3,5,6]) are published. We provide rigorous justification for the classical Wenzel equation for the roughness enhanced effective contact angle. We also studied the quasi-static motion of two-phase flows on topologically rough surfaces. By considering the free energy of the system, we first consider the Cassie and Wenzel states transition on rough surfaces. It has been found that the crucial conditions for the two different states depend on the equilibrium contact angle, the droplet size and its initial position. Three papers are published (see Part C [2,8,10]). To study the contact angle hysteresis, we consider the interface dynamics and contact angle hysteresis in a two dimensional, chemically patterned channel described by the Cahn-Hilliard equation with a relaxation boundary condition. A system for the dynamics of the contact angle and contact point is derived in the sharp interface limit, which enables us to analyze the behavior of the solution using the phase plane analysis. We observe the stick-slip of the contact point and the contact angle hysteresis. Numerical examples are presented to verify our analysis. A paper is accepted for publication in DCDS (A) (see Part C , [8,9]).

605311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
605311.value: So far, we only consider the contact angle hysteresis driven by energy. One of the possible direction is to develop theory for the contact angle hysteresis with hydrodynamics. In this case, we will consider the dynamic model involves Cahn-Hilliard and Navier-Stoke's equations.

605311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
605311.value: Controlling the wettability of solid materials is a classical and key issue in surface engineering. In this project, we have made some progress in studing how wetting properties of the solid surface are affected by the roughness of the surface. Our research is based on analysis and numerical simulations of some mathematical models.

605411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
605411.value: This proposal presents a novel concept related to a fundamental liquid-electronic hybrid rheostat with which a hybrid voltage divider and processor can be derived. The applications for the above components used as the liquid-electronic information interface may be achieved. A basic liquid-electronic component named as the hybrid divider, a structure maintains the form of voltage divider, targets fast detection and precise manipulation of fluid, preferably microfluidic/nanofluidic droplets, the input signals of which are informs of both electric and fluidic, while the output can be also in both forms. The output of fluidic signal can be stored or displayed in a fluidic channel, which may be controlled by a connected valve. The voltage output signal can either be continuous or discrete in value, which could be decided according to different applications. The continuous output can be used to sense characters of different fluid/droplets and control information processing components, while the discrete signals could be control signals for actuators or pumps, or realize digitalized information processing. Therefore, effective integration of our components is a way to digitalizing fluidic information, as well as realize basic hybrid logic functions, such as switcher, logic gate, encoder, decoder, and multiplexer. Those base functions are prerequisites to achieve the final goal of fluidic computing or hybrid computing. 該項目提出一個新穎的基本液體與電子混合的混合分壓器及處理器研究方法。應用上述組件可以實現用作液體與電子線路的信息聯接。 液體/電子元件可以组成一個基本的混合分配器，其結構形式保持電分壓器特徵，可以作為快速檢測流體和精確的流體操控，最適合微/納流系統。其檢測的輸入信號為在電子及流體，而輸出也可以為這兩種形式。流體的輸出信號可以由連接閥控制存儲或顯示在某一個指定的流體通道。根據不同的應用，電壓輸出信號可以是連續或離散。連續輸出可用於檢測不同流體/液滴的控制信息處理組件，而離散信號可以控制信號驅動器或微泵的行為，實現數字化信息處理。因此，有效整合我們的組件是一種流體數字化信息，以及實現基本混合邏輯功能，如開關，邏輯門，編碼器，解碼器和復合器。達到流體計算或混合運算的最終目標。

605411.label: Realisation of objectives
605411.value: A simple on-chip logic function IF and NOT with hybrid operation by electric-fluidic divider has been successfully designed and fabricated, in which electrorheological (ER) droplet can indeed “think” logically. By using more delicate chip structure, we realize the first microfluid universal logic device, where all 16 Boolean logic operations (according to two inputs) can be achieved: operating functions are defined only by power supply. Giant electrorheological fluid (GERF), introduced as the computing media, translates fluidic information into electronic and mechanic information back and forth, making this microfluid universal logic gate fully compatible with electronic devices. Based on above results, we have developed a new type of logic gate by using fluidic-electronic hybrid divider. We demonstrated two-input microdroplet-based universal logic gates using a liquid-electronic hybrid divider. All 16 Boolean logic functions have been realized by manipulating the applied voltages. Such novel platform consists of a microfluidic chip with integrated microdroplet detectors and external electronic components. The microdroplet detectors perform as the communication media for fluidic and electronic information exchange. Presence or absence of microdroplet at the detector translates into binary signal 1 or 0. The embedded micro-mechanical pneumatically actuated valve (PAV), fabricated using the well-developed multilayer soft lithography technique, offers biocompatibility, flexibility and accuracy for on-chip realization of different logic functions. The microfluidic chip can be scaled up to construct large-scale microfluidic logic computation. On the other hand, the microfluidic chip with specific logic function can be applied to droplet-based chemical reaction for on-demand bio- or chemical analysis. Our experimental results have presented an autonomously driven, precision-controlled microfluidic chip for chemical reaction based on the IF logic function. Where, the conductive droplet (made of NaSCN solution) appears at the parallel electrodes, the output signal is “0”, representing by no droplet (made of FeCl2 solution). Only when a conductive droplet passes over the detecting electrodes, the output fluidic signal is activated and emerges as a colourless droplet. When two colourless droplets arrive at the array of the micropillars, mixing and reaction occur resulting in a colour change. The experimental results reveal that the chemical reaction based on droplet microfluidics can be well controlled and conducted with the help of logic functions realized by the design of the liquid-electronic hybrid divider. With the aid of these logic functions, a micro-reactor can be readily achieved with digitized microfluidic signals. The impact of micro-reactor can potentially be seen from customized on-chip manipulation of droplet-based chemical action for biological or chemical analysis. By employing above technique, We also designed other microfluidic devices such as the magnetically functionalized PDMS-based micropillar arrays chip which was implanted for controllable microfluidic mixing. The arrangement of PDMS micropillar arrays inside the microchannel can be flexibly controlled by an external magnetic field. As a consequence, the flow fields inside the microchannel can be regulated at will via magnetic activation conveniently. Our microfluidic system is capable of generating highly reproducible results within many cycles of mixing/non-mixing conversion. We believe that the simple mixing–triggering method together with rapid and controllable mixing control will be extraordinarily valuable for various biological or chemical applications in the future. The concentration gradient generators was also fabricated by transfer NIPAM concentration gradients onto native PDMS surfaces to produce the roughness gradients in a highly controllable manner with which the cell culture experiments have been well done by using such material. Ten journal papers have been published to date.

Recently, we have designed more delicate chip structure to realize the first microfluid universal logic device, where all 16 Boolean logic operations (according to two inputs) can be achieved: operating functions are defined only by power supply. We demonstrated two-input microdroplet-based universal logic gates using a liquid-electronic hybrid divider. All 16 Boolean logic functions have been realized by manipulating the applied voltages. Our experimental results have presented an autonomously driven, precision-controlled microfluidic chip for chemical reaction based on the IF logic function. Where, the conductive droplet (made of NaSCN solution) appears at the parallel electrodes, the output signal is “0”, representing by no droplet (made of FeCl2 solution). Only when a conductive droplet passes over the detecting electrodes, the output fluidic signal is activated and emerges as a colourless droplet. When two colourless droplets arrive at the array of the micropillars, mixing and reaction occur resulting in a colour change. The experimental results reveal that the chemical reaction based on droplet microfluidics can be well controlled and conducted with the help of logic functions realized by the design of the liquid-electronic hybrid divider. We also designed other microfluidic devices such as the magnetically functionalized PDMS-based micropillar arrays chip which was implanted for controllable microfluidic mixing. The arrangement of PDMS micropillar arrays inside the microchannel can be flexibly controlled by an external magnetic field. As a consequence, the flow fields inside the microchannel can be regulated at will via magnetic activation conveniently. Our microfluidic system is capable of generating highly reproducible results within many cycles of mixing/non-mixing conversion. We believe that the simple mixing–triggering method together with rapid and controllable mixing control will be extraordinarily valuable for various biological or chemical applications in the future. We have combined microfluidic concentration gradient generators and photo-polymerization process to graft NIPAM concentration gradients onto native PDMS surfaces which finally leads to roughness gradients in a highly controllable manner. 605411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
605411.value: The liquid-electronic hybrid divider can be sued for electric-fluidic control by when either electrical signal or fluidic flow status. It can be designed as logic component which could be brought into play in automatic microfluidic chemical reaction, materials synthesize, biological reaction and testing and drug screening etc. The hybrid chip can be scaled up to construct large-scale microfluidic logic computation. It is well known that the conventional method is difficult to combine the fluidic and electric signals by a single controller while using hybrid divider, we can realize the multiply droplet generation and manipulation simultaneously. We propose a new structure of the microfluidic chip how to fabricate functional nanomaterials as well as core-shell microspheres. The preliminary experiment is carrying out recently.

605411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
605411.value: Usually, the electronic signal is needed in controlling the fluid and biological analysis through a liquid-electronic information interface. Our currently device will provide a digitalized unit which can simultaneously process input information in forms of both electric signals and fluidic signals, and the outputs of this unit are also in both of the above two forms. We define this kind of processing component as a hybrid digital component. Our processing unit maintains the form of a voltage divider named as a hybrid divider. This hybrid divider could be a basic processing unit which can be used to perform all kinds of digital operations between electric fluidic signals, such as fluidic encoder and multiplexer. By connecting with a feedback and active control system, the hybrid divider can be used to realize fluidic or hybrid computing, within a portable size and inexpensive form.

605511.label: Project Objectives
605511.value: Synthesis of New Spiroborates: Various O-based chelating ligands have been used succesfully to prepare bis chelated organoborate anions. We plan to extend the members of the existing families, such as salicylates, as well as attempt new chelate types, eg from binaphthol. Formulation of Spiroborate Salts: Ideally the most useful organoborate anions will be formulated as simple salts eg with alkali metals, ammonium ions that can be used as starting reagents for direct metathesis crystallization. The best formulation for R-mandelic acid is NH4[B(S)(R-Man)2], which is non-solvated and has suitable solubility. This was found following preparation of over 15 simple [B(R-Man)2] salts. With funds for just 1 to 1.5 research staff the scope of this must be scaled back from 200 crystal structures, but sufficient work will be carried out to provide proof of concept. Chiral Resolution of Racemic Cation Mixtures: Our work from objective 1 will seek to form a library of pure homo-chiral spiroborate anions. Examples we have already available include [BS(R-Man)2], [BS(L-Lac)2] and [B(R,R-Hbz)2]. The application of the homochiral spiroborates to crystallization of chiral cations and the potential for separation of enantiomeric mixtures thereof will be explored. Examples will come from both natural product and metal-organic chemistry. Solution Stability and Dynamics of Spiroborate ions: The utility of the spiroborate ions as crystallization 'tools' that can be applied to a wide range of problems is dependent in part on the fact that they are chemically stable and robust to a range of physical and chemical environments. The solution chemical stability of all spiroborate ion types will be evaluated as well as the stereochemical lability where appropriate. Cation Selective Binding of Cyclic Boratartrate Anions: We are interested in finding the cation binding selectivity for the several cyclic tetramers synthesized and isolated to-date, as well as attempting to isolate new cyclic isomers based on different conditions, counter-ions and tartrate stereochemistries. This objective must be scaled back since development of computational methodology and calculation of energies of diastereomeric solids will involve a separate researcher from other tasks and there is insufficient budget. However we will carry out calulations on stability of diastereomeric molecular ions

605511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
605511.value: Crystallization is a means of purification of chemical substances and through X-ray crystallography an essential step in determining the structure of molecules. Our group has experience in developing novel crystallization methods by varying physical and chemical conditions. For charged molecules (ions) crystals must form through combination with counter-ions of opposite charge, so that electrical neutrality of the solid is maintained. In this project the utility of negatively charged chelated organoborate anions for crystallization of positively cationic molecules will be explored. Our revious work has shown that the organoborate anions can be readily prepared from many ligands bearing two proximal -OH functionalities, as found in diols,catechols, salicylic acids and tartaric acids. The boron chelates two such ligands deprotonating the oxygens and giving a central tetrahedral BO4 core. The ligand types we select are inexpensive or readily prepared and combine variable functionality. Three distinct applications of the organoborate ions will be pursued i) all the organoborate anions may act as crystallization agents for cationic species and have variable shape, size and functionality ii) secondly chiral organoborate ions can act as resolving agents for chiral cationic species. This can be applied to a wide range of molecules including alkaloid natural products to organometallic complexes. We have already developed two important chiral organoborates iii) finally we have prepared a novel family of cyclic boratartrates which have sub-nanometer cavities that can encapsulate metal ions such as potassium. The binding selectivity of these ionophores for different metals will be explored. Ligands may be symmetric or asymmetric and may possess chiral centers. Chelation of two asymmetric chelates also generates chirality at the boron. The stability and molecular dynamics of the organoborates in solution can be monitored through isolation of enantiopure borates and the kinetics of stereochemical inversion at boron. Favorable molecular crystallization is often regarded as much a black art as science since many factors are involeved in efficient molecular packing. Molecular shape and functional complementarity is important and for chiral ions we will attempt to rationalize the resolution power of chiral organoborates through quantitation of the shape differentiation of the two mirror image molecular ions. The utility of spiroborates as chiral resolving agents has already been proven by the facile separation of important pharmaceutical compounds derived from Traditional Chinese Medicinal sources as well as metal-organic complexes. If successful this project will impact both fundamental research and have potential commercial applications to drug purification and formulation. 结晶是純化化學物質的一种重要手段，也是X-射线晶体学测定分子结构必不可少的步驟。我们在研发新颖的结晶方法方面积累了丰富的经验。在本项目中，我们将探索利用螯合有机硼酸阴離子来结晶带正电荷的分子。 我们将研发具有如下三类獨特用途的有机硼酸根離子：(i) 作为结晶带正电离子的试剂，(ii) 作为拆分带正电手性离子的试剂,（iii）作为封裝金属离子的纳米空腔。 螺旋手性有机硼 酸根已被证实可用来从中药中分离和提取重要的药物分子。本 项目的结果不仅会对基礎研究产生影 响，也 有可能被应用到药物的純化及制备等商业领域。

605511.label: Realisation of objectives
605511.value: The project has been successfully pursued along all of the initial objectives note the objectives 3 and7 were modified in scope as per 5.2. A wide variety of ligands (around 40-50) have been used to prepare spiroborate anions. These have included a number of salicylates, mandelates, catecholates, diolates and a-hydroxycarboxylates, as well as completely new families. Salt formulations have been studied and solubilities and stability examined. We scaled back from the initial 200 structures in objective 3 to about 100 crystallizations and have found several good candidates for crystallizing anions. Notably since the interim report we have found boron bis-benzillate (from Ph2C(OH)COOH) has excellent general crystallizing ability. Some anions were found to be problematic for crystallization and several chiral anions led to gel formation. Anions with high conformational freedom do not crystallize well and this is also found with mandelates with substituents at 3- position which can suffer 3- /5- conformational disorder in the solid state. The best resolving agent developed was boron bis(mandelate) [BMan2]- which has given excellent resolution for over 10 racemic cations out of 15 studied. This can be achieved by either 1-pot reaction or cation metathesis from its sodium salt. The spiroborate anion from diphenyltartramide is also found to resolve several racemic cations, such as a-methylbenzylamine and sec-butylamine. Reaction of L-diethyltartrate with various amines and anilines allow formation of a family of chiral tartramide spiroborate anions that are now being explored. The solution stability of spiroborates has been studied both for enantiostability at boron, as well as for chelate ligand exchange. Both are found to be highly solvent sensitive. Enantio-scrambling at B can take place rapidly in protic media with t1/2 measurements (ca 30mins) derived from NMR or CD spectroscopies. We attempted to look at ligand exchange rates to make hetero- spiroborate anions by MS but finally found NMR was a better methodology. Such rates were again media sensitive and just slightly slower than enantio-scrambling. Various boratartrates have been prepared and cyclic tetramers with selective cation binding found from meso-tartaric acid (K, Tl). Some computational modeling of spiroborates has been carried out on boron bis-mandelate conformers and the relative stability of various cyclic boratartrates, finding R-Bs-R configurations more stable; computation of hinge angles in boron bis-salicylates, confirm experimental findings that bends of <30deg are reasonable and that slight bends of 10deg are more stable than coplanar rings. This impacts both shape and solubility of [BSal2] type anions.

605511.label: Major findings and research outcome
605511.value: The realization of objectives in 5.3 above has allowed us to make significant advances in understanding the scope, structure, stability and possible application of various spiroborate anions. This has formed the bulk of the work in two student theses PhD thesis of Mr. Lawrence Wong and MPhil thesis of Ms. Gemma Tam. Much of their work has been presented at international conferences over the past 2-3 years and is now being prepared / submitted as a number of manuscripts as indicated below. Our first publication has been submitted to Chemical Communications on the use of boron bis-mandelate as an inexpensive and versatile resolving agent. This details three resolutions (tetrahydropalmatine, 1,2-diaminopropane and cobalt tris-phenanthroline (III) and further publications on the resolution of canadine (tetrahydroberberine) and a variety of other amine and diamine cations by [BMan2] will follow to be submitted to Crystal Growth and Design and CrystEngComm. A paper on the use of spiroborate anions as crystallizing agents is under preparation (to Crystal Growth and design) following a grid of crystallizations based on 10 such anions and a wide variety of cations from simple inorganic (Na, K) to more complex organic (PPN, benzimidazolium, berberinium etc). Several spiroborates offer excellent crystallizing ability, chiefly we have found boron bis-benzillate, followed by boron bis-salicylate, which seemed superior to boorn bis-catecholate or bis-pinacolate. Our studies have underscored difficulties in the stability of spiroborates in protic and aqueous solution, but we have shown that chiral and resolved [BSal2] anions are indefinitely stable in polar aprotic solvents such as dmf and dmso. A paper on the resolution and B-chiral stability of R-[BSal2] and S-[BSal2] will preface a further publication on the resolution of various substituted [BSal*2] anions by sparteine, either as 1:1 or 1:2 salts. (CrystEngComm) Additionally we have explored a number of spiroborate systems with stable C-based chirality, apart from mandelate. The obvious target - tartrate itself - makes chains and oligomeric rings, since it can bind two B centers. Derivatization of the acid groups of L-tartrate leaves it as a chiral diol still capable of forming chiral spiroborates. We have prepared both spiro-boratartrate esters and tartramides. The latter -NHPh derivatives show similar promise as resolving agents to our successful [BMan2].

605511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
605511.value: We believe the effectiveness of [BMan2] as resolving agent is in part due to the fact that both BR- and BS- forms exist in solution and in a Dutch resolution way this may help suppress nucleation of one of the two diastereomeric salts. We are currently looking at a further 10 racemic cations that may be resolvable by [BMan2] and compare to our other favored chiral spiroborate the bis-diphenyltatramide [B(L-DPTA)2] . Chiral [BSal2] has been resolved and the anion transferred into a salt with an achiral cation [NBu4]. We are now looking into the possibility of using it as a highly effective resolving agent, but there is need to carefully choose conditions since the lability of the B chiral centre must be overcome. Success in this will rapidly expand the number of useful chiral spiroborates and their application to resolutions.

605511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
605511.value: Many useful molecules including many biological molecules are chiral or handed. We have succeeded in preparing various new and inexpensive molecules with negative charge (spiroborate anions) many of which are handed. These can then be used to resolve (separate) left and right handed molecules with positive charge (chiral cations) by crystal formation of neutral organic salts. Several excellent examples are for pharmaceuticals derived from Traditional Chinese medicine, such as tetrahydropalmatine and canadine (tetrahydroberberine). By separating them as left or right hands, our biotechnology team has been able to establish the different biological activity of the mirror image molecules. Our chiral spiroborate anions can also be applied to bulk industrial chemicals such as 1,2-diaminopropane or 2-methylpiperidine that are more useful when they have been separated into left and right handed molecules. Since for any new resolution many chiral anions may need to be tested to find an effective result, it is important to have an array of such molecules available. We have thus developed families of such anions based on i) mandelic acids and ii) tartrate esters and amides. These have the advantage that they can be either left or right -handed themselves and are all readily prepared and inexpensive.

606211.label: Project Title(Chinese)
606211.value: 函数域上L-函数零点的分布

606211.label: Project Objectives
606211.value: For the three explicitly defined families of L-functions in function fields, the proposer plans to study various statistics of their zeroes, such as the h-level density and h-level correlation, under the limit that the field size q is fixed and other parameters goes to infinity. For the family of quadratic twists of an elliptic curve over a function field with non-constant j-invariant, the proposer plans to study the behavior of the rank, with the aim to establish the analogue of Goldfeld's conjecture. The moments of the Hasse-Weil L-function and its derivative of quadratic twists of an elliptic curve over a function field at central value will also be studied.

606211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
606211.value: The proposal concerns the distribution of zeroes of L–functions of function fields over a finite field, a vast area of research motivated by the study of zeroes of the Riemann zeta function and its generalizations. For a family of L-functions in function fields, Katz and Sarnak provided a fascinating theory on the distribution of the zeroes based on the computation of monodromy groups and Deligne’s equidistribution theorem. However, this theory relies crucially on the limit that the field size q goes to infinity. What happens if q is fixed and other parameters go to infinity instead? Is there still a limiting distribution? What happens if q and other parameters go to infinity at the same time? These questions are equally important and arise naturally in many contexts and applications, however, they can not be treated by the argument of Katz and Sarnak. In recent years a number of authors have developed new ideas and new techniques to study this type of questions on some special families of L–functions in function fields. The proposer believes more questions of this kind could be explored and the results could be pushed much further. The proposal will focus on three important families, the family of hyperelliptic curves, the family of L-functions arising from an irreducible representation, twisted by quadratic chararacters, and the family of abelian extensions of the rational function field with a fixed Galois group. For each of the families, the proposer plans to investigate various statistics of the zeroes, such as the trace of the Frobenius endomorphism, the function counting the number of angles of zeroes in an interval, and most importantly the h-level density and h-level correlation of the zeroes, all of which have important implications in number theory. Quadratic twists of an elliptic curve over the rational function field and their rank will also be studied in the project under the same theme. 本课题研究的中心问题是关于函数域上一般L-函数零点的分布。这个问题来源于关于Riemann zeta函数和其推广的函数的零点的研究。基于monodromy群的计算和Deligner的均匀分布定理，Katz和Sarnak给出了对于函数域上一族L-函数的零点的分布的几乎完美和震撼人心的结果。然而，他们的结果非常关键的取决于让其中的有限域的势 q 趋于无穷。如果q固定，而让别的参数趋于无穷会怎么样？或者让q和别的参数一起趋于无穷呢？这些很自然的问题在相关研究中经常出现，而且也有很多应用，然而，Katz和Sarnak的结果并不能应用于其上。在最近几年，关于如上提出的问题，对于函数域上一些特殊的L-函数族，有一些学者提出了一些新的思想和新的解决问题的工具。本作者相信还有很多类似的问题值得研究，已有的结果也可以做得更好。本项目提出了函数域上的四族具体的L-函数，对每一族L-函数，作者计划研究关于他们零点分布的种种统计特性。

Xiong, ``Distribution of zeta zeroes for abelian covers of algebraic curves over a finite field'', J. Number Theory. 147 (2015), 789--823. Thorne, M. Xiong, ``Distribution of zeta zeroes for trigonal curves over a finite field'', preprint. In this paper we obtained the distribution of zeta zeroes for the family of trigonal curves over finite fields as the genus goes to infinity. The paper is unpublished because it relies on a result of Dr. Yongqiang Zhao which still remains unpublished. However, the PI has given talks on this work in conferences in France, Canada and U.S.A. in 2015 and the work was well received.

606211.value: The proposal has resulted in three published papers and one preprint. The results compliment the theory of Katz and Sarnak and show interesting phenomenon on the limiting behavior of zeta zeroes for natural families of L-functions over finite fields.

606211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
606211.value: The results can be naturally extended to automorphic L-functions over finite fields, which are important objectives of study in number theory. 606211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
606211.value: The proposal concerns the distribution of zeroes of L-functions of function fields over a finite field, a vast area of research motivated by the study of zeroes of the Riemann zeta function and its generalizations. Katz and Sarnak have provided a fascinating theory on the distribution of the zeroes in general, however, this theory relies crucially on the limit that the field size q goes to infinity. The proposed research complements the theory of Katz and Sarnak by studying what happens if the field size a is fixed and other parameters go to infinity, thus providing alternative approaches to an important problem in number theory. The proposal is interdisciplinary in nature as various tools and methods from analytic number theory and statistics/probability are applied to study important problems in algebraic geometry.

606311.label: Project Title(Chinese)
606311.value: 全等四邊或五邊形的球面拼貼

606311.label: Project Objectives
606311.value: To study the combinatorial, edge length and the angle aspects of tilings with a small number of tiles. It is often possible to completely list all the possibilities. To design some computer programs that does the classification routine for any given number of tiles. To gather the insight gained from the first two objectives and prove some general properties. The properties should reveals some unique characteristics of the edge-to-edge spherical tilings with congruent quadrilaterals or pentagons.
