606311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
606311.value: The history of tiling is as old as the human civilization. Tiling patterns appear in everyday life, in art and design, in engineering and structure, and in modern mathematics. Tiling has been studied by mathematicians for more than 100 years. Some major achievements include the solution to Hilbert's 18th problem, the classification of wallpaper groups and crystallographic groups, the classification of isohedral tilings of the plane, and the classification of monohedral tilings of the 2-sphere with triangles. The mathematical study of tilings has various applications in science and engineering, in addition to other fields of mathematics. We propose to investigate the monohedral edge-to-edge tilings of the 2-sphere with quadrilaterals and pentagons. Note that the triangle case has been completely classified, and the tiles in such tiling must either be quadrilaterals or pentagons. Unlike its planar counterpart, the literature on the spherical case is very limited. Our recent complete classification of the monohedral edge-to-edge tilings of the 2-sphere with 12 pentagons illustrates the rich, fascinating and complicated nature of the pentagon tiling. Our work also introduced some techniques that could be extended and become useful for further study. Given that a complete classification as in the triangle case is very unlikely for the pentagons and quadrilaterals, we will try to classify the tilings with a small number of tiles. Moreover, we hope to design computer programs to classify the tilings for any given number of tiles. Through such experience, we expect to gain some insight on the subject and come up with some general results. We hope that such general results will be useful for the development of the tiling theory and other fields of mathematics. The results may also be potentially useful to other science and engineering subjects. 自人類文明以來，拼貼就出現在日常生活的各個方面。在藝術，設計，工程，數學等領域，都可以看到拼貼。拼貼作為數學研究的對象，已經有一百多年的歷史。關於拼貼的主要數學成就包括希爾伯特第十八問題的解決，牆紙群和晶体群的分類，平面的等面拼貼的分類，以及球面的全等三邊形的對頂拼貼的分類。拼貼的數學研究已被廣泛應用於許多科技領域，也被應用於其它數學領域。 全等多邊形的平面拼貼一定是由三邊，四邊，五邊或六邊形做成的，這些平面的拼貼問題已有大量的研究文獻。在球面上，類似拼貼一定是由三邊，四邊或五邊形做成的。全等三邊形的球面對頂拼貼問題已經完全解決，剩下的是四邊或五邊形的拼貼問題，然而這方面的研究文獻卻是屈指可數。我們最近完成的十二個全等五邊形的對頂拼貼問題的分類，是這個研究方向的最簡單例子。儘管最簡單，這個例子的研究展示了五邊形拼貼的許多獨特複雜的結構。我們的分類也引進了一些新的方法和技巧，應該可以在全等五邊形的對頂球面拼貼的進一步研究中發揮作用。 目前看來，全等四邊或五邊形的球面拼貼的分類還是比較遙遠的事情，這方面的研究才剛剛起步。我們試圖將簡單的全等多邊形的對頂拼貼進行分類，以建立對問題的理解和研究經驗。在此過程中，我們也試圖設計一些電腦程序，以便處理一些繁複的計算，當全等多邊形的個數越來越多，問題越來越複雜時，這些程序將會相當有用。我們也希望通過總結這些理解和經驗而得到一些一般的結果，並將這些結果應用到其它問題。

606511.label: Project Objectives
606511.value: To develop methods to fabricate highly transparent conducting network films with a controllable porous structure but minimal defects, e.g., to assemble highly crystalline TiO2 nanoparticles with stable surfaces into the desired porous films to facilitate electron transport. To synthesize metal chalcogenide QDs, densely anchor the QDs onto the surfaces of the mesoscopic TiO2 networks by ligand-assisted linkage and/or by direct in-situ precipitation, and study their structural and optical properties. To explore new hole transporters to optimize their compatibility with the QD-sensitized porous nanostructures proposed in (1) and (2) above.

606511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
606511.value: Quantum-dot-sensitized solar cells (QDSSC) have the potential for efficient, cheap, and renewable generation of energy from sunlight with no carbon footprint. Compared to dyes used in dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSC), QDs have the advantages of high extinction, high photostability, band gap tunability throughout the ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared spectral ranges by size and shape control, and multi-exciton generation arising from single photon absorption. However, QDSSCs still lag much behind DSSCs in terms of efficiency. The way forward is undoubtedly to control the nanostructures to optimize the charge separation, transport and collection. Such photoanode nanostructure is construed to broadly comprise size, crystallinity, morphology, interfacial structure and energy band compatibility, which are central to cell performance. Therefore, engineering of the nanostructures is directly related to the optimization of the QDSSCs. This proposal aims to develop general bottom-up strategies to create integral semiconductor hetero-nanostructures, exploit their advantages and coordinate the roles of their constituents in photovoltaic applications. First, we will develop methods to fabricate highly transparent conducting network films with a controllable porous structure but minimal defects. This includes: (1) assembly of highly crystalline, stable-surface bound TiO2 nanoparticles into the desired bicontinuous porous films with enhanced electron transport; and (2) fabrication of well-crystallized, size-controlled, substrate-transferrable, vertical TiO2 nanowire arrays to be used as a highway for facilitating vectorial electron transport. Second, semiconductor QDs, especially the rarely studied but potentially exciting Sb2S3 and PbS QDs, will be synthesized and densely anchored on the surfaces of the mesoscopic TiO2 networks and the TiO2 nanowire arrays by ligand-assisted linkage and/or by direct in-situ precipitation. Detailed nucleation and growth mechanisms will be studied with reference to the above two objectives. Third, new hole transporters such as modified sulfide electrolytes, quasi-solid electrolytes and solid hole conductors will be explored to optimize their compatibility with the QD-sensitized porous nanostructures proposed in (1) and (2) above. The emphasis of the whole project will be placed on the interplay between the mechanistic understanding and control of the growth processes of the hetero-nanostructures and the performance of the corresponding QDSSCs. Implementation of these nanostructures in the QDSSCs will be carried out hand in hand with the synthesis efforts to provide feedback and facilitate optimization. This project will provide new atomic level knowledge of artificial photon-to-electron energy conversion devices and incorporate the modern day advances in nanomaterials and nanotechnology into the green and sustainable photovoltaic technology. 本项目致力于异质纳米结构的至下而上的发展， 从而拓展其在量子点敏化太阳能电池方面的应用。主要工作从以下几个方面展开。(1) 发展制备具有可控多孔结构但极少缺陷的透明导电网状膜的方法；将高晶化，具稳定表面的TiO2纳米颗粒组装成理想的具有优良电子传导性能的双通多孔膜；(2) 制备量子点并用新方法将其固定于上述多孔膜表面；(3) 探索新型的空穴导体用以发展固态及准固态的量子点敏化太阳能电池。

606511.label: Realisation of objectives
606511.value: 1. We have designed and synthesized TiO2 Nanowire arrays by hydrothermal method, mesoporous single crystals of TiO2 and SnO2 by templated method, mesoporous TiO2 from self-assembled sol particles, hierarchically branched ZnO films and 3D FTO nanocone arrays by hot press method. These films are ordered, crystalline, and with a controllable nanostructure. Hence they have good electron mobility but are not light absorbing, which are essential for photoelectrodes of sensitized solar cells. Indeed, high performance solar cells have been demonstrated with these films. 2. A linker seeding chemical bath deposition technique has been developed for quantum dot sensitized solar cells (QDSSCs), which nucleates special ionic seeds on a compact linker layer and thereby yields a full and even coverage of QDs on the TiO2 surface in large area. With this technique, we have significantly improved Voc and FF. The LS-CBD process has achieved compact coverage of QDs on a TiO2 matrix, leading to 4.23% PCE, nearly two times that with conventionally deposited control photoanode. Extension to a conceptually new quasi-quantum-well sensitized solar cells yielded a PCE of 6.2%. We later replaced the QD sensitizers with organometal halide perovskites because of their superior properties. We have synthesized a novel perovskite (CH3NH3PbI2Br) and used it to sensitize 1D TiO2 nanowire arrays for the hybrid solar cells. Such a solution processed solar cell has achieved a PCE of ~5%, much higher than that with its analogue CH3NH3PbI3. We also discovered that highly crystalline perovskite films can be grown from colloidal perovskite precursors with suitable sizes. We have revealed the nature of the colloidal precursors. 3. We have identified a polyfluorene copolymer (TFB) as an ideal alternative to spiro-OMeTAD as a hole transporter for sensitized solar cells, which enjoys low cost, high hole mobility and good processability. In particular, under the one-step perovskite deposition condition, TFB achieves a 10.92% PCE that is considerably higher than that with spiro-OMeTAD (9.78%). Our mechanistic studies have uncovered the higher electrical conductivity and lower series resistance of TFB than spiro-OMeTAD, accounting for the significantly higher FF, Jsc and Voc of the TFB-derived cells. We also explored a high-quality sol–gel-processed NiO NC film as the hole-transport layer in an inverted perovskite solar cell. With the NiO NC film, we obtained a cell efficiency of 9.11%, which is the highest at the time for planar perovskite solar cells based on an inorganic hole-extracting layer.

606511.label: Major findings and research outcome
606511.value: This project has not only realized the intended objectives but also achieved additional outcomes, resulting in a large number of high-quality publications. 1. We have designed and synthesized TiO2 Nanowire arrays by hydrothermal method, mesoporous single crystals of TiO2 and SnO2 by templated method, mesoporous TiO2 from self-assembled sol particles, hierarchically branched ZnO films and 3D FTO nanocone arrays by hot press method. These films are ordered, crystalline, and with a controllable nanostructure. (Nanoscale 5, 3245 (2013); Chem. Mater. 26, 5700 (2014); ACS Applied Materials & Interface 5, 4000 (2013); Energy & Environmental Science 7, 3651 (2014)). 2. High efficiency CdS/CdSe sensitized solar cells were demonstrated with a hierarchically branched double layer architecture, a ZnO nanorod array underlayer and a ZnO nanotetrapod top layer. A record PCE of 5.24% was obtained. (ACS Applied Materials & Interface 5, 4000 (2013)). 3. A linker seeding chemical bath deposition (LS-CBD) technique has been developed for quantum dot sensitized solar cells (QDSSCs), which nucleates special ionic seeds on a compact linker layer (TiO2-COORS-Cdx) and thereby yields a full and even coverage of QDs on the TiO2 surface in large area. (J. Phys. Chem. C 117, 92 (2013)). 4. Extension of QDSSCs to a conceptually new quasi-quantum-well sensitized solar cells supported on ZnO nanotetrapods yielded a PCE of 6.2%. (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 135, 9531 (2013)). 5. The fabrication of the quasi-quantum-wells supported on ZnO nanotetrapods in an organic media resulted in high crystalline quality with significantly enhanced photoluminescence. (ACS Nano 8, 3771 (2014)). 6. Replacing the QDs with new or highly crystalline organometal halide perovskites produced high-performance solar cells. (Nanoscale 5, 3245 (2013); Angew. Chem., Int. We have identified a polyfluorene copolymer (TFB) as an ideal alternative to spiro-OMeTAD as a hole transporter for sensitized solar cells, which enjoys low cost, high hole mobility and good processability. In particular, under the one-step perovskite deposition condition, TFB achieves a higher PCE than that with spiro-OMeTAD. (Adv. Funct. Mater. 24, 7357 (2014)). 8. We explored a high-quality sol–gel-processed NiO NC film as the hole-transport layer in an inverted perovskite solar cell. With the NiO NC film, we obtained a fairly high cell efficiency of 9.11%. (Angew. Chem., Int. Ed. 53, 12571 (2014)).

606511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
606511.value: This project has addressed some fundamental materials issues concerning QD sensitized solar cells. This includes the growth of wide band-gap nanoarrays as a porous scaffold for anchoring the QD sensitizers, the subsequent link-assisted growth of the QD sensitizers, and the development of new hole-transporters. We have largely achieved the goals, additionally gaining vantage to ride the tide of the meteorically rising perovskite solar cells. Opportunities certainly abound for further developments. One of the future research directions is the use of nanocarbon-base cathode for peroskite solar cells without use of any hole transports and the costly noble metal electrodes. The carbon electrode based perovskite solar cells have the greatest potential for realistic application because of their low-cost materials and manufacturing processes, high efficiency and the high stability due to the hydrophobicity for water rejection. Improvement of the perovskite crystallinity and the interface quality is necessarily the next target, which will bring the cell performance up to a higher level. Meanwhile, mechanistic understanding of the cell operation is essential to the solar cell development in general. Initial experiments have already been done in these directions. The up-coming experiments and perhaps theoretical modeling will definitely further the development of the solar cells.

606511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
606511.value: Solar cell converts sunlight directly to electricity and is the most clean and sustainable energy source for the mankind. The most important issue for developing the new generation of solar cells lies in the use of low-cost, environmental friendly, earth-abundant materials. This project has established the materials base of this type for sensitized solar cells. Wide band-gap metal oxide nanoarrays (such as TiO2, ZnO, etc.) have been developed as the scaffold. QDs (such as CdSe) and metallo-organic halide hybrid perovskites (such as CH3NH3PI3) are seamless coated onto the scaffold surfaces by solution processes. The resulting film is then topped by the newly developed hole transporters (such as semiconducting polymers) and metallic current collectors (such as Au), forming a sensitized solar cell. Such a type of solar cell, albeit radically different from, for example, the conventional single crystalline silicon solar cells, is demonstrated to perform rather efficiently and stably, raising the hope for the large-scale deployment to fulfill the global energy demands of the mankind.

606611.label: Project Title(Chinese)
606611.value: 彈性膜類介觀結構的有效聲學性質之理論和實驗研究

606611.label: Project Objectives
606611.value: Explore the mechanism and the microstructure of membrane-type metamaterials for realizing enhanced absorption of low frequency acoustic waves Explore the consequences of coupling in specially structured membrane-type metamaterials Develop an effective medium theory based on the eigenmodes of the unit cell of the membrane-type metamaterials

Explore the consequences of coupling in specially structured membrane-type metamaterials

606611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
606611.value: Almost all materials are inhomogeneous if examined microscopically, as it is well known that materials are composed of atoms and molecules and hence at least on the scales of Angstroms all materials are discrete and therefore inhomogeneous. For many composite materials the heterogeneity can be on a much larger scale, e.g., micrometers. Yet in our everyday experience many materials can appear homogeneous and be characterized by a few physical parameters that signify their responses to mechanical, electrical and other perturbations. How can these so-called response functions be deduced from materials' microscopic compositions? Ever since the first successful attempt in relating the dielectric constant of a material to the microscopic polarizability of its (discrete) components, by the so-called Claussius-Mossotti relation more than one century ago, there has been uninterrupted theoretical and experimental efforts in the study of the so-called effective medium properties of inhomogeneous materials. Such efforts have witnessed a burst of recent activities owing to the advent of the metamaterials, whose effective medium properties can take on values previously regarded as unphysical. For example, the optical refractive index of a material has long been regarded as a positive quantity, but the opposite has been proposed 40-50 years ago and demonstrated experimentally during the past decade. We have pioneered in the study of low frequency effective acoustic properties of composites comprising locally resonating units. More recently, we have extended this effort to very simple systems that are nearly two-dimensional, i. e., elastic membranes decorated with buttons or other types of more rigid objects. We have obtained some surprising results, such as the effective mass density of such membrane system can be negative in certain frequency regimes, which is opposite to the simple intuition. Such membrane type metamaterials provide an ideal medium for the further development of low frequency acoustic wave dissipative mechanism and the negative dispersion effect, which are the two main objectives in this project. The outcome of the investigations will provide guidance for the designs of new metamaterials for practical applications in the low frequency acoustic regime.

606611.label: Major findings and research outcome
606611.value: (1) By arranging semi-circular platelets in elongated unit cells, we have achieved near 100 % absorption and near zero reflection of sound waves incident on the metamaterials. We turned such metamaterials Acoustic Dark materials. The results were published in Nature Communications. Furthermore, we have demonstrated that the devices containing a single unit cell of the Dark Materials are excellent vibration dampers when attached to a host structure hundreds of times the weight of the devices. A US patent has been granted. (2) By using two single-membrane resonator to for a cavity, the device so constructed has both monopole and dipole resonance at low frequency, thereby creating the condition for double negativity, i. e., negative dynamic mass and modulus. The results are published in Physical Review Letters, and a patent has been formally filed to the US and China authorities. (3) A theoretical framework for effective medium has been established to use the eigenmodes to obtain the effective parameters. The framework can not only be applied to one-dimensional systems, but also to two-dimensional systems as well. The results were published in Physical Review B. (4) We have invented a super absorption metamaterials due to hybrid resonance between the membrane resonator and the air cavity. The effective unity-absorption area of the device can be 10 times larger than the physical area of the device facing the incident sound waves. The results were published in Nature Materials. A patent has been formally filed to the US and China authorities.

606611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
606611.value: We are further exploring the dipole and monopole coupling to create metamaterials with a number of novel properties, such as broad band high transmission loss achieved by membrane resonators no thicker than 10 mm, and mechanisms other than hybrid resonance to achieve super absorption.

606611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
606611.value: By exploring the structures that basically contain thin membranes decorated by some carefully designed platelets, we have experimentally demonstrated a number of novel acoustic and vibrational properties of these structures. These include Acoustic Dark materials, double negativity materials, super absorption materials. A theoretical frame work has also been established to reveal the physics behind these novel properties, and to guide further work for more exotic findings.

606811.label: Project Title(Chinese)
606811.value: 高維高頻數據的統計推斷

606811.label: Project Objectives
606811.value: Develop methods to estimate the empirical spectral distribution of the integrated covariation matrix when the observations can be both contaminated and asynchronous. Establish asymptotic results for risk measures under high dimensional setting. Develop methods to test ``sparsity'' assumptions and derive bounds for finite sample errors. Quantify the possible bias in using the ``plug-in'' estimators and find ways to correct for the bias in portfolio optimization.

606811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
606811.value: Nowadays high dimensional and high frequency data become increasingly available especially for financial securities prices. This provides an unprecedented rich source of information for people to understand the structure of the latent price process. This proposed research aims to develop a sound theory for making statistical inference for this kind of data. In particular, we shall study how we can estimate key quantities like integrated covariation matrices, which are of central importance in practical applications like risk analysis and portfolio optimization. Our goals, once achieved, will be of great interest to both researchers and practitioners who work in related fields. 近些年來， 尤其是在金融產品價格方面，高維，高頻數據變得日益普遍。這提供了前所未有的豐富的信息讓人們來理解潛在的價格過程。此項研究旨在建立可靠透徹的理論來對這類數據進行統計推斷。特別的一點，我們會研究如何估計一些關鍵性的數量比如綜合協方差矩陣。在實際應用比如風險分析及投資組合優化中，綜合協方差矩陣都是至關重要的。我們目標，一旦達成之后，對於相關領域的研究者及從業者都會很有價值。

606811.value: The project objectives have been achieved. Furthermore, the proposed research led to several other studies with fruitful and important outcomes.

606811.label: Major findings and research outcome
606811.value: 1. Developing methods in order to understand the covariance matrix based on possibly contaminated data has been a primary goal of this project. (1) In [C1] we studied the inference about the empirical spectral distribution (ESD) of integrated covariance matrix of high-dimensional diffusion process based on high-frequency data. We studied two estimators, for which we establish (generalized) Marv{c}enko-Pastur theorems regarding the asymptotic relationships between the ESDs of the estimators and that of the integrated covariance matrix. The paper has been published in Annals of Statistics; (2) In [C6], we further consider the situation with microstructure noise. We establish an asymptotic relationship that describes how the ESD of (true) sample covariance matrix depends on that of information-plus-noise-type sample covariance matrix. Based on this asymptotic relationship and a (generalized) connection between the ESDs of sample and population covariance matrices, we propose a two-step procedure to estimate the ESD of ICV. We further develop an extension of the second estimator in [C1] to the noisy setting, which possesses several favorable properties. The paper is under 2nd round review by Annals of Statistics. 2.One fundamental problem in portfolio allocation is the Markowitz optimization problem. In [C7] we propose a novel approach which combines sparse regression and estimation of maximum expected return based on random matrix theory. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first method based on which the goals of the Markowitz optimization problem can be simultaneously achieved in the high-dimensional setting. The paper is in revision for Review of Financial Studies. 3. To better understand challenges from high-frequency data, we investigated extensively into the issues due to irregular observation times and/or microstructure noise: (1) In [C3] we studied the volatility estimation when sampling times are endogenous, and showed that (in the noiseless case) endogeneity can lead to a (second order) bias. (2) The study was generalized to the noisy setting in [C2]; (3) In [C4] we studied the estimation of joint moments of microstructure noise. We discovered that microstructure noise exhibits rich structures. Our findings have important implications in various applications. The paper is in 2nd round revision by Econometrica; (4) In [C8] we developed a volatility estimator that works in the presence of dependent noise and irregular observation times; (5) In [C5] we proposed a novel approach that makes use of trading information to model microstructure noise and develop a more efficient volatility estimator. The paper is in 2nd round revision by Journal of Econometrics.

606811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
606811.value: We have identified several interesting and important questions to be further investigated along the direction. In particular, we plan to develop new methodologies based on high-dimensional statistics and high-frequency data to aid large portfolio management.

606811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
606811.value: The project, in general, is about extracting useful information from high-dimensional and/or high-frequency data for various financial applications. The results obtained in this projects are useful for portfolio allocation and risk management.

606911.label: Project Objectives
606911.value: In [6], we proved a generalization of Siegel-Weil formula for symplectic groups and orthogonal groups over Artinian rings, these groups are in general not reductive. We plan to derive some special examples of the formula and investigate the possible applications. We shall investigate the geometric meaning of the arithmetic quotient for loop groups. For the case GLn, the arithmetic quotient parameterizes the metrized bundle of rank n over the arithmetic surface P1 over Z with the sections 0 and infinity removed. We shall study the case of general arithmetic surfaces. And we shall study the theta series for a metrized bundle over an arithmetic surface. We plan to study the Eisenstein series on loop groups. In particular we will derive explicit formulas for Eisenstein series of loop groups of small rank like loop SL2. The explicit formulas may be helpful to understand better how automorphic forms on loop group behave. We will pay special attention to the important case of the Eisenstein series induced from the classical cusp forms.

We plan to study the Eisenstein series on loop groups. In particular we will derive explicit formulas for Eisenstein series of loop groups of small rank like loop SL2. The explicit formulas may be helpful to understand better how automorphic forms on loop group behave. We will pay special attention to the important case of the Eisenstein series induced from the classical cusp forms.

606911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
606911.value: The study of symmetry is systematized and formalized in the areas of mathematics called group theory and representation theory. The semisimple algebraic groups and the infinite dimensional generalizations, loop groups and Kac-Moody groups, are among the most important groups. The part of representation theory related to loop groups and the algebraic counterpart, affine Kac-Moody algebras, has been rapidly developing in recent years. The main results obtained in the last two GRF projects of which this proposed project is a continuation, are the following: We constructed a Weil representation for loop symplectic groups and proved that there is a theta functional that is modular invariant; we proved a version of the Siegel-Weil formula for loop symplectic and orthogonal groups (joint by Garland). We will continue to study the automorphic forms of loop groups in the following aspects: explicit examples and applications of the Siegel-Weil formula for loop groups, geometric meaning of theta functions for loop groups, and explicit formulas of automorphic forms for loop groups of small rank. 数学中关于对称性研究的学科包括群论和表示论. 半单代数群及其无穷维的推广Kac-Moody群, 圈群是最重要的几类群. 关于圈群, 及其对应的仿射李代数的研究, 是在近年很活跃的分支. 我们在前两个项目中获得如下结果: 1. 我们构造了圈辛群的Weil表示和Theta泛函，并证明了Theta泛函的模性. 2. 我们把Siegel-Weil公式推广到圈群（此工作和Garland合作）。 本项目将是上述前两个项目的继续和深人。 我们将会计算Siegel-Weil公式在圈群时的特殊和有用的例子。 我们还会研究圈群的自守形的几何意义， 和尝试构造小阶数圈群上的自守形。

606911.value: The objective 1 is achieved. We made a lot of computations about new versions of Siegel-Weil formula. Our results suggest a new direction in the theory of automorphic form for loop groups, that is, we should continue to study theta correspondence for loop groups. The objective 2 is mostly achieved and we actually have gone much further than the plan. We have two main results: 1. We generalized some of Weil's results to arithmetic surfaces. 2. We began to study an abelian harmonic analysis on infinite dimensional spaces, continuing Parshin-Osipov's work. We will return to this topic in near future. The objective 3 is not achieved. At the beginning of our investigation, we run some obstacles. The main difficulty is that the harmonic analysis on infinite dimensional groups is sufficiently developed at this stage. We failed to simplify the formula for loop group Eisenstein series and connect it to some familiar functions.

606911.label: Major findings and research outcome
606911.value: Our study of the Siegel-Weil formula for loop groups and truncated path groups indicate that the classical theory of theta correspondences have an analog in the loop group case. Another major finding of this project is that the classical theory of abelian harmonic analysis, which is for locally compact abelian topological groups, can be generalized to infinite dimensional abelian topological groups. We improved the results of Parshin and Osipov. And we studied the Fourier theory in the infinite dimensional setting. As an application of our infinite dimensional harmonic analysis, we proved (joint with Dongwen Liu) product formula for symbols on arithmetic surfaces.

610311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
610311.value: 信息通信技术在近期经历了革命性的进步，由此带来了无线通信服务的广泛应用。对于无线高速接入Internet的需求正在快速增长，这就要求在更高密度的新型无线网络中保持无缝接入网络的能力，同时要用更高效的频谱效率提供更高速度来迎合更严格的通信服务质量要求。当前各种可以接近信道容量的高级通信技术正在被研究用来提高通信系统性能，包括OFDM（频分多址复用），MIMO（多天线技术），链路自适应传输，dirty paper coding编码技术，和干扰消除技术。这些技术有些还在研发中有些已经在后3G通信网络中得到应用，例如802.16 WiMAX系统，3GPP LTE系统。这些后3G系统的一个特性是频谱复用率会接近于1，这也就意味着这些通信系统的性能受限与各种干扰，不管是同一小区内的或者来自于其他小区的。小区边缘用户的性能收到尤其大的影响。所以，干扰问题的解决将是下一代无线通信网络中的一大主要挑战。 处理干扰的传统方法是把它作为一个负面因素并且尽力消除它。但这不是一种最优化的处理方案，也不足以解决下一代通信网络中的干扰问题。干扰协作是最近提出的一项革命性的技术。它的主要原理是通过协调多个基站的传输与接收来消除干扰，这样可以把整个网络从干扰受限转化为噪声受限，从而极大的提高系统性能。但是要在实际系统中应用干扰协作的技术面临着多个挑战，而目前这些挑战并没有被克服。更重要的是，一旦我们考虑了实际系统中的各种限制，干扰协作是否还能带来很大的性能改进并不清楚。在这个项目中，我们会研究怎么样解决干扰协作在实际系统里面遇到的各项挑战。我们的目标是研发实用的基于协作的干扰处理方案来有效的解决干扰问题并提高频谱效率。我们提出的研究任务包括研发有效的信道反馈技术，研发易于实用的分布式干扰协作方法，研究有限容量的基站间通信对干扰协作的影响，还有研发基于干扰协作的预编码方法。我们还会开发分析工具和方法来衡量不同干扰协作方案的性能。

610311.label: Realisation of objectives
610311.value: With the popularity of smart mobile devices and the proliferation of mobile applications, the data traffic over wireless networks is growing at an unprecedented speed. One effective way to boost the network capacity to meet such strong demand is to deploy more and more base stations, so that the same spectrum can be reused more frequently. This is being carried out by mobile operators around the world. However, as the network density increases, the co-channel interference among different cells becomes the bottleneck, which will degrade the overall network performance, especially for cell edge users. This project investigated interference-aware coordination, which is a key technology to manage intercell interference, by coordinating the transmission/reception among multiple neighboring cells. Our investigation closely followed the research objectives. One main aspect is the development of interference coordination strategies for different wireless systems, which covered research objectives 2, 3 and 5. In particular, for two-hop interference networks, with either amplify-and-forward or decode-and-forward relaying protocols, we developed coordinated beamforming, as well as interference alignment algorithms, to improve both the throughput and diversity. Considering content caching at base stations, joint coordinated beamforming and backhaul data assignment algorithms were developed. We also developed scalable coordinated beamforming algorithms for cloud radio access networks. Another line of investigation is the analytical performance evaluation of wireless networks, related to research objective 4. We first analyzed spectral efficiency and energy efficiency in small cell networks, which revealed the impact of intercell interference. The analytical results were then used to develop an effective user centric interference coordination strategy. Considering the critical role of channel state information (CSI) for interference coordination, we also proposed an effective way to reduce CSI overhead, which only requires obtaining partial CSI for coordinated transmission, and it was related to research objective 1. Overall, we believe that we have satisfactorily completed this project. By covering all the 6 research objectives, we were able to produce academically and practically significant research while contributing meaningfully to the training of students in this important area. Specifically, as a result of this project, three PhD students (Xiang Chen, Chang Li, and Yuanming Shi) have been trained and graduated. In addition, we were able to publish 2 journal papers, as well as. 10 conference papers in IEEE flagship conferences. In particular, one conference paper received the Best Paper Award at 2014 IEEE International Symposium on Personal Indoor and Mobile Radio Communications (PIMRC).

610311.label: Major findings and research outcome
610311.value: Major research outcomes were achieved as described as follows: • Analytical Performance Evaluation of Wireless Interference Networks: We adopted a recently proposed random spatial model, where both mobile users and base stations are modeled as two independent Poisson point processes. In [journal#2], we developed new tractable expressions for outage probability in multi-antenna small cell networks, and evaluated both spectral efficiency and energy efficiency. The results were then extended to SDMA networks [conference#5] and intercell interference coordination [conference#6]. Average rate analysis was carried out in [conference#8]. • Coordination Beamforming for Two-Hop Interference Networks: In [conference#4], we proposed optimal coordinated relay beamforming algorithms to characterize achievable rate region and maximize sum-rate for two-hop interference networks with amplify-and-forward relaying. An interesting idea, which we referred to as interference neutralization, was proposed to cancel the interference at the second hop. In [journal#2], we investigated decode-and-forward two-hop interference networks. By allowing relays to exchange more information, we proposed different cooperation strategies with joint processing among relays. • Interference Alignment for MIMO Relay Interference Channels: In [conference#2], we investigated interference alignment (IA) in MIMO relay interference channels. We derived an upper bound for the maximum achievable degree of freedom (DoF) tuple with IA, and proposed an iterative IA algorithm to attain a given feasible DoF tuple. In [conference#3], we investigated the use of IA to achieve diversity gain over a diagonal interference channel in the time or frequency-domain. It was shown that IA can increase sum diversity gain of a K-user interference channel by K −1. • CSI Overhead Reduction in Cloud-RAN: Cloud Radio Access Network (Cloud-RAN) is a recently network architecture which can well support interference coordination. In [conference paper #7], we proposed an effective framework to reduce overhead of acquiring CSI. The main idea is to obtain instantaneous CSI of only a subset of all the channel links and statistical CSI for the others. To improve the computation efficiency of the beamforming design in Cloud-RAN, a general framework to support scalable coordinated beamforming was proposed in [conference#10]. . Joint Coordinated Beamforming and Data Assignment for Backhaul Limited Caching Networks: Caching at wireless access points is a recently proposed method to alleviate the backhaul burden in wireless networks. It can also create new opportunities for interference coordination. In [conference#9], we investigated joint coordinated beamforming and backhaul data assignment in a caching network. Based on a group sparse beamforming framework, we proposed low-complexity algorithms to solve the challenging design problem.

610311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
610311.value: In this project, we investigated interference coordination in different wireless networks, and covered various design aspects. While the outcomes are quite encouraging, there are lots of potentials for further development. One critical issue that may hinder the wide application of interference coordination is CSI. The acquisition of required CSI may induce significant signaling overhead, e.g., to send pilot symbols for channel estimation, and to feed back CSI, which will degrade the spectral efficiency. Inevitably there will be errors, and the design of interference coordination should take this into consideration. The CSI issue will become even more prominent as wireless networks get denser, as the channel dimension will increase. Given the recent development in content-centric wireless networks, caching at base stations has attracted lots of attention. It will not only reduce the transmission latency but will also enable interference coordination without increasing the traffic on the backhaul link. Thus, deploying low-cost cache storages at base stations can help avoid upgrading the backhaul network, which is quite costly. It also brings new design challenges. In particular, the cache content placement and coordinated transmission/reception should be jointly designed, which will typically be a mixed integer nonlinear programming problem, usually NP hard.

610311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
610311.value: To meet the exponentially growing mobile data traffic, mobile operators around the world are trying to boost the capacity of their networks, which, however, is fundamentally limited by inter-cell interference. This project investigated a main technique for interference management, i.e., interference-aware coordination. By coordinating the transmission/reception of multiple base stations, interference will not act as a detrimental effect, but can be exploited to increase the network capacity. This is especially important for cell edge users, which can now receive signals from multiple base stations. In addition, by effectively controlling interference, it will make the network operate in the noise-limited regime, which will help improve the network energy efficiency. The objectives of this project covered the key design issues for interference-aware coordination, including analytical performance evaluation, coordinated beamforming design, channel state information acquisition, etc. Meanwhile, our investigation covered several important types of wireless networks, such as small cell networks, two-hop interference networks, cloud radio access networks, and wireless caching networks. The methodologies developed in this project will be valuable for the further evolution of wireless networks. In particular, they will have the potential to be applied in the next-generation wireless networks, i.e., 5G networks.

610411.label: Project Objectives
610411.value: To model the MAC layer interactions between stations and APs and formulate the problem of channel assignment, association control, rate control and contention resolution as an optimization problem by invoking the NUM framework. We will separate this NP-hard problem into two sub-problems. The CA and the joint ARC. To propose approximation techniques to solve the CA and then the ARC iteratively by replacing the integer variables by continuous ones and then transforming the non-convex problem into a convex one. This approach will give rise to a distributed solution via gradient-based algorithms, known for their speed of convergence and their relative insensitivity to communication asynchrony. To design and implement the protocols in a simulator and validate our approximation models via computer simulation.

610411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
610411.value: Today, WLAN technology based on the IEEE 802.11 standards has become one of the fastest growing technologies ever. A consequence of the growth in popularity and speed of adoption of new IEEE 802.11 standards is that many of the techniques exploited in the operation of production WLANs today rely on rule-of-thumb methods. While many such techniques may be optimal in terms of performance when taken apart or used in a pure WLAN with a single BSS, because of their lack of mutual coordination, combining their use often results in poor performance in large WLANs where many access points (APs) interact mutually. For example, one typical such problem is the well-known throughput performance anomaly described in the literature, which is the result of the ARF rate adaptation interacting with the MAC backoff mechanism. With today's increased density of APs in deployment and the increased popularity of mobile personal hotspots such as the MiFi, the combined use of many such ad-hoc techniques, forewarns of an impending situation of chaos where the behavior of an AP may dramatically degrade the performance of an entire network. A practical example of this is what happened during the introduction of iPhone4 at the WWDC Conference, where it is reported that in a crowd of 5000 attendees there were no less than 500 WIFI hotspots in the room (most of them MiFis). A similar event is reported to have happened to Google during the introduction of Android. Without strong analytical studies to support and validate the co-existence of such techniques and the design of new ones to coordinate the APs in large scale WLANs, any further development of WLANs will dramatic performance challenges. More specifically, considering the combined use of rule-of thumb mechanisms, such as channel assignment based on the measured noise level at power-up, signal-strength based association, binary exponential backoff mechanism, along with the limited number of available orthogonal channels and the density of WLANs in deployment, today lead forcefully to the appearance of hidden terminals, and ultimately to throughput starvation. Our goal in this project is to study the interactions of channel assignment, association control policies, rate control and backoff in a holistic way to achieve optimal throughput-fairness in large scale WLANs with hidden terminals. We will invoke optimization techniques to design the policies for each of these mechanisms that will maximize the throughput of the network while maintaining spatial fairness eliminating thereby the throughput starvation problem. 如今，基於IEEE802.11標準的無線局域網技術已成為有史以來增長最快的技術之一。隨著新的IEEE802.11標準的普及以及速度的增長，許多現時正被使用的無線局域網的操作技術仍依賴於經驗法則。雖然很多這樣的技術可能在一個單一接入點的純無線局域網中有最優的表現，由於缺乏相互協作，其共同的效果會導致在大型無線局域網中（在其中許多接入點會相互作用）的低劣性能。例如，一個典型的問題是的文獻中所描述的著名的吞吐量性能異常問題。這是自動速率回退速率自適應方法與媒體介質層的避退機制相互作用的結果。隨著今日接入點部署的密度的不斷增加，以及移動個人熱點，例如MiFi, 的不斷普及，合併使用很多這樣的自組網技術，可以預見到會產生這樣一個迫在眉睫的混亂情景：一個接入點的表現可能會顯著降低整個網絡的性能。作為一個實例，這一現像已經發生在WWDC會議上iphone4的推介會上。據報導，在此推介會上，在一個5000人的參加者人群中，在房間裡有不少於500個WIFI熱點（大部分是MiFi）。據報導，在Goolge介紹Android時，也發生了類似的事件。 如果沒有深入分析研究以支持和驗證這樣的無線技術共存的可能性，以及設計新的在大型無線局域網中協調接入點的方法，無線局域網的任何進一步發展將會面對著巨大的性能挑戰。具體來說，考慮結合使用經驗技術，例如基於噪聲水平估計的信道分配，基於信號強度的關聯，二進制指數避退機制，以及有限的可用的正交信道和無線局網絡的部署密度，在今天導致了嚴重的隱藏終端問題，最終導致了吞吐率的飢餓。 我們在這個項目的目標是以全面的方式研究信道分配，關聯控制策略，速率控制以及避退算法，以在有著隱藏終端的大型無線局域網中實現最優的吞吐率和公平性。我們將使用最優化技術設計這些機制。對於每一機制，我們將最大化網絡吞吐率， 同時保證空間的公平性，從而消除吞吐率的飢餓問題。

610411.label: Realisation of objectives
610411.value: The project has achieved all its objectives and exceeded them by evolving the objectives with the evolution of wireless local area network standards. When we proposed the study, wireless LANs based on the IEEE802.11 protocol dominated the market. The success of 4G-LTE networks in providing the large bandwidth expected by the users and the explosive growth of the connected smartphone devices let network designers to investigating a fifth generation of wireless networks that integrate all available technologies horizontally. Among the proposed new WLAN technologies are the so-called Home e-Node B (HeNB) networks which are 4G/5G small cell base stations that are compatible with 4G/5G macro-cell base stations but that are destined to serve small areas like a home or a small business. While these HeNB networks are part of the wireless LAN landscape and are forecast to take a substantial market share, they use a different access technique to the transmission channel than IEEE802.11 WLANs, therefore they required specific treatment. As a result our publications derived from this project include not only papers on IEEE802.11-based multi-cell WLANs but also papers on LTE femtocell Home e-Node B networks with multiple cells and inter-cell interference. We also still have papers in the pipeline for this latter part. As indicated by the list of publications derived from this project, we conclude that: 1- We have successfully worked on objective 1, which is to model MAC layer interactions between base stations and clients and formulated the multi-dimensional resource allocation problem as an optimisation problem then divide the problem into sub-problems to address its complexity. We have further done the same since the mid-term report to home eNodeB based wireless networks that rely on LTE rather than IEEE802.11. 2- We have proposed approximation algorithms to solve the problem of channel assignment on one side and association-rate control on the other for IEEE 802.11, and sketched a method of deployment that would enable centralised control in an institutional network. We have further done the same in recent years to LTE-based home eNodeB networks. 3- We have tested all our optimisation-based proposed algorithms via numerical simulation and developed packet-level simulation models in ns2 and ns3 with realistic channel models and error models to assess their performance in more realistic environments. In addition to the above work, initially, to understand the interactions among uncoordinated hidden nodes in the wireless network, we have experimentally investigated how collisions and hidden terminals may affect the throughput of the network and of each other. This work was inconclusive in accurately modelling such interactions as our test environment was not large enough and the test area had a large amount of external interference, however, it led us to discover a possible security issues of Wireless LANs and as such we have also pursued this avenue and published the work under the umbrella of WLAN security. Despite having given raise to 8 papers by the project end date, there are still two additional journal papers in preparation. Overall the project has given raise to one PhD thesis that will be defended on August 2 2016 and one already completed MPhil thesis in addition to giving the opportunity to several other PhD students to further their knowledge of wireless networks by contributing to the project without working on it fully. It has also given raise to two Final year project reports.

610411.label: Major findings and research outcome
610411.value: We have proposed several novel algorithms for resource allocation in wireless local area networks and demonstrated their effectiveness numerically. We have also sketched and explained how such protocols can be implemented in real networks to provide coordination in the increasingly crowded wireless local area networks spectrum. In addition, contrary to common belief, from our model of IEEE802.11 we found that actually increasing the number of APs in a wireless network improves the network capacity if access to the network is coordinated following our algorithms. This is mainly due to the fact that under our algorithms, we distribute the clients on a smaller number of APs to reduce the number of hidden terminals and the additional inactive APs (that only send their beacon occasionally) add coordination ability to the network and thus reduce further the hidden terminals by transitivity. This is in opposition to what we and most researchers believed before. In addition, while objective 4 is not part of the revised objectives, we still have taken it into account and developed a scaled down version of our coordination algorithms in a small WIFI network through an undergraduate final year project.

610411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
610411.value: In our opinion, IEEE 802.11 WLANs are heading further and further towards reaching the limits of the available spectrum due to congestion. As the data rate increase (e.g., IEEE802.11ac) and the number of deployed AP increases dramatically, the medium access control that is based on contention is becoming more and more the bottleneck. We recommend coordination as proposed in our study. And while our solutions consisted in deploying such coordination on top of the uncoordinated CSMA method, in the future this will become prohibitive with the increased number of APs. A modification to the IEEE802.11 MAC protocol to enable coordinated access is necessary: while the physical layer has gone through several generations the basic access method of IEEE802.11 MAC is still the same as the first instance. Another possible direction that would keep the MAC protocol as is, is to explore a new standard based on software defined networking to deploy coordination and synchronisation between routers.

610411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
610411.value: Wireless local area networks operate in a limited frequency spectrum. The increased number of deployed routers is bound to degrade the communication quality in the same manner that several human conversations in the same room lead to confusion. Our work in this project consisted in trying to put some organisation within a network where wireless routers autonomously decide when to transmit, and may not realise that some other routers are already transmitting their data at the same time. The problem being multi-dimensional, it is computationally hard to come by optimal coordination; therefore we designed some approximate solutions that can be built in the hardware and software of WLANs to achieve good performance in terms of throughput and fairness in accessing the channel.

610611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
610611.value: Resistance spot welding systems are widely used to achieve inexpensive and efficient metal sheet joining in many industries. Welding quality, which is usually described by the final nugget size, is a very important criterion for estimating the welding actions. Although different feedback control schemes have been applied to the welding systems, the results of the feedback control are still unsatisfactory in terms of the energy efficiency and the quality of the weld, especially in mass production. This is because the critical information, which directly affects the quality of the weld (the nugget size), such as the internal temperature and phase change during the welding, cannot be directly measured and is not used in the feedback control. It is well known that the dynamic resistance of the weld during the welding process can reflect the internal properties of the work-piece. The characteristic shapes of dynamic resistance curves for satisfactory welds differ significantly from those for unsatisfactory welds. However, since it is very difficult to measure the dynamic resistant with high resolution and accuracy, no work has ever been reported on the use of dynamic resistance in the real time control of the welding process. Moreover, nothing has been reported on how to obtain the desired dynamic resistance for a given welding material and nugget size. In this research, based on our new developments in the measurement and real-time signal processing of the dynamic resistance, a new method for controlling the welding process is proposed. The proposed research consists of three parts. First, we propose to develop a mathematical model which can effectively predict or describe the desired dynamic resistance behavior given the material properties and nugget size. The desired dynamic resistance curve will be the control objective during the welding process. To track such desired trajectory in real time, a robust and high performance control scheme will be developed. The proposed control scheme should be able to effectively handle the nonlinear and modeling uncertainties and generate proper welds with the desired quality in the welding process and save energy in the meantime. Finally, a hardware device will be developed to implement the proposed algorithm. The technology developed in this proposal will provide a reliable, low-cost, nondestructive means for predicting and generating good weld strengths in real time for the manufacturing industries.

610611.label: Realisation of objectives
610611.value: (1). We developed a new method to online measure the power factor of the resistance spot welding (RSW) machine. This measurement can be employed to guarantee the safety operation of RSW machine. Also, this new method also can be extended to be applied in other electrical systems with similar structure. (2). According to theoretical analysis of the RSW process and thermodynamic principle, RSW process is a metal absorbing energy and then melting process. There are different controller design strategies. Through deeply understand the welding process based on the physical principle, constant current control was chosen as the principle control strategy, due to it can guarantee the nugget growth has a smooth and consistent rate. (3). We developed a new method to realize the constant current control for RSW machine. The method is based on the mathematical characteristics of the electrical system. The experimental results show the current control has a much higher accuracy when compared to that using the traditional method. Furthermore, according to the understand of the electrical structure and working principle, a new convenient root mean square (RMS) value measurement method of welding current in each control cycle can be developed, which can significantly save CPU times. (4). The shape of the nugget can be confirmed by metallographic experiments and serious observation. Then based on the mathematical and physical analysis, together with the newly developed method to online measure the dynamic resistance with a high resolution , the model of the relation between energy delivered and nugget growth can be established, and then an integrated control system for online control the welding quality was developed. Various experiments which used different welding currents show that the errors of nugget diameter were so small. In addition, based on realizing method of constant current control, constant heat control strategy can be correspondingly realized, relative comparison can be conducted to experimentally validate the constant current control is better than constant heat control. (5). We also extended this research to the workpieces with different sizes, the effect of different workpieces conditions has been summarized. The effect of different electrode force on the nugget formation and growth was deeply researched. The rules can be employed to establish the welding data library and improve the welding automation. (6). Some core algorithms and experimental results have been written into journal papers or were presented in international academic conferences. In addition, a PhD student has been trained.

610611.label: Major findings and research outcome
610611.value: Resistance spot welding (RSW) has been widely employed in industries where joining of sheet metal is commonplace such as automobile industry. However, the process is complicated as it involves some unexpected phenomena. The workpieces for welding have large individual differences, even in the same batch of workpieces. Hence, real-time control of the RSW process plays a critical role in obtaining welds with satisfactory quality. However, existing methods cannot successfully deal with the challenges. In this project, we developed an integrated control system for controlling nugget quality in real time. The system which is based on physical and mathematical analysis can handle the quality control with small errors under different operational conditions. By analyzing the characteristics of RSW process, constant current control was found to be the best control strategy to guarantee the smooth process of nugget formation and growth. To guarantee the safety of operating the machine, the power factor for each control cycle should be online measurement. Based on the deeply understand of electrical structure and working principle, a new root mean square value measurement method of welding current in each control cycle was developed to save the CPU time. Also, we developed a new algorithm to calculate the power factor based on the input and measurable variables. Final experimental results show the algorithm has a higher accuracy when compared to numerical simulation. The new algorithm was developed to realize the constant current control. The algorithm is based on the characteristics of electrical model and has simple structure. Experimental results validated the satisfactory performance can be obtained in different occasions. Using the metallographic experiments and corresponding analysis, nugget shape can be confirmed approximately a cylinder. Dynamic resistance with a high resolution was obtained to seek the beginning of nugget formation and growth. Then the model of the relation between the energy after the beginning point and the nugget growth was established based on physical and mathematical analysis, and then an integrated control system was developed. The experiment results show the control system can make the actual nugget diameter approach the desired value with small errors. Based on the operation, constant current control and constant heat control can be experimentally compared. The result validated the former can obtain higher efficiency. In addition, when the workpieces have different widths or thickness, or different electrode force are employed, corresponding effects of these elements on the nugget formation and growth were also researched.

610611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
610611.value: In this project, an integrated control system was developed to make the welding quality satisfactory. However, the workpieces have different sizes and resistance spot welding machines have different types, in the future, the following issues are worth investigating. (1).The mathematical model between energy delivered and nugget formation can be extended to the workpieces with different widths and thicknesses. In the future, the integrated model should combine the different sizes so that the control system can be used in the workpieces with different sizes. (2). In the project, the experiments were conducted on welds made of steel of a limited size. Whether the proposed model can be extended to other materials, such as stainless steel, zinc, aluminum, etc., need to be investigated in the future. (3) Based on accurate and high-frequency measurement of dynamic resistance, the detailed process of nugget formation and growth will be observed by means of electrode displacement and other measuring variables. It can make this complicate process observable in real time, which can benefit the current welding production. Also, though current work was based on single-phase AC RSW machine, it can be extended to be applied in three phase medium frequency direct current (MFDC) RSW machine.

610611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
610611.value: Resistance spot welding (RSW) is one of the most widely used and efficient methods for joining sheet metal objects, especially prevalently in automobile manufacturing occasions. Currently, over 90% of assembly work in a car body, which is about 3000-6000 spot welds, is contributed by RSW operation. However, the working process of RSW is very complex and highly nonlinear, as well as the process is full of disturbances and uncertainties, ensuring weld quality has been and remains a major challenge and a worthwhile goal for current weld operations. In this project, an integrated control system which can obtain welds with satisfactory quality was developed. Some important academic research results had been found and published. The project has both theoretical and practical significance. They will certainly have a profound impact on many areas, such as microcontroller design, data collection, automation, and manufacturing, etc. The techniques developed in this study can be directly used to improve current welding operations. Hong Kong’s industries will benefit from the result of the proposed research. Furthermore, the worldwide welding industry, especially the automobile manufacturing, will also benefit from this study because the new techniques developed in this project can save energy and improve the efficiency very much.

610711.value: 亚式期权的支付函数依赖于资产价格在一段时间内的平均值。这一特征使得亚式期权广泛应用于股权衍生品市场，商品市场和外汇市场上的股权，利率，货币，能源和商品问题。例如，如果一个公司的收入相当一部分来自于外币，那么该公司可以使用亚式期权来对冲他们在外汇市场的风险。再比如，亚式期权在商品市场上很流行也是因为它的结构使得它可以降低大户操纵市场的风险。因此，亚式期权的定价问题受到全世界学术界和工业界的普遍关注，包括香港地区 -- 世界第五大外汇市场。然而，如何在比布莱克-斯科尔斯模型(BSM)更优的资产定价模型下对亚式期权进行解析定价仍然是一个难题。这主要是因为在这些模型下我们很难得到平均资产价格的分布的解析形式。 该研究项目致力于在一个混合指数跳跃扩散模型(MEM)下对亚式期权进行解析定价。MEM是由该项目的主要研究者及其合作者共同提出。MEM假设资产价格服从一个跳跃扩散模型，而每次跳跃服从双边的混合指数分布，即向上或向下的跳跃幅度的分布都是有限个指数分布的加权平均。作为布莱克-斯科尔斯模型，双边指数跳跃扩散模型和超指数跳跃扩散模型的一种推广，MEM有以下三个优点。（1） MEM可以更好地描述资产收益尾部的实证特征。这是因为混合指数分布在弱收敛意义下可以逼近任意的分布。（2） 指数型的跳跃分布使得MEM在数学上更容易处理。（3） MEM在弱收敛意义下可以逼近任意的指数Levy模型，包括以下重要的资产定价模型，CGMY, NIG, VG以及Merton的正态跳跃扩散模型。 在该研究项目中，我们计划提出一种双重拉普拉斯变换的方法对亚式期权在MEM下进行解析定价。这个结果可以进一步推出在CGMY, NIG, VG以及Merton的正态跳跃扩散模型下亚式期权价格的解析逼近。首先考虑一个随进变量A -- 被指数分布截断的平均资产价格，我们要把亚式期权价格的双重拉普拉斯变换表示为A的实数阶矩的函数。然后我们准备尝试两种方法（一种是概率方法，另一种是复分析方法）去得到A的实数阶矩的解析表达式，这样我们就有可能得到亚式期权价格的双重拉普拉斯变换的解析表达式。最后，我们准备设计快速而准确的双重拉普拉斯逆变换算法和有效的MEM逼近算法，这样我们就可以得到亚式期权在MEM下的准确价格和在其他重要模型下的近似价格。

610711.label: Realisation of objectives
610711.value: In this project, I have achieved the project objectives by solving the analytical pricing problem of Asian options with jump risk, i.e., under jump diffusion models with general exponential-type jumps. More specifically, to price Asian options analytically, we have studied the distribution of the exponentially-stopped integral of the underlying geometric hyper-exponential jump diffusion process by considering two approaches, a probabilistic one and a complex analysis one, and managed to derive closed-form expressions for the real moments of the exponentially-stopped integral by investigating a closely related recursion. Based on this result, we have succeeded in deriving an analytical solution in terms of double Laplace transform to the pricing problem of Asian options. Moreover, we have also obtained analytical solutions to the associated important hedging parameters such as delta and gamma. Then a two-sided Laplace inversion based pricing method has been developed to implement the analytical pricing formula, and numerical results have demonstrated that our pricing method is accurate and efficient and that it performs well even in the case of low volatilities. This pricing method can also be used to produce approximate Asian option prices under some other important exponential Levy models by constructing a jump diffusion model to approximate the target model. As regards the related Laplace inversion problem, we have examined the extension of one-sided Euler inversion algorithm to the two-sided case as well as its applications in derivatives pricing. The obtained two-sided Euler inversion algorithm is attractive and particularly suitable to provide benchmarks as it usually has computable error bounds. In addition, we have also derived closed-form expansions for discrete Asian option prices under general one-dimensional diffusion models. This expansion method can be extended to diffusion models with jumps without much extra effort and is appealing because it is possible to explicitly calculate any general expansion terms in a systematic manner. Numerical experiments have suggested that the closed-form expansion formula with only a few terms can generate accurate Asian option prices efficiently.

610711.label: Major findings and research outcome
610711.value: Major findings and research outcome of this project are detailed as follows. We have derived analytical solutions in terms of double Laplace transforms to the pricing problem of Asian options under the hyper-exponential jump diffusion model as well as to the related important hedging parameters such as delta and gamma. This is possible primarily because we have obtained closed-form expressions for the real moments of the exponentially-stopped integral of the underlying asset price process. Theoretically, this result can be viewed as an extension of the celebrated result for the Laplace inversion based analytical pricing of Asian options under the Black-Scholes model to the jump diffusion model. We have also developed an accurate and efficient two-sided Laplace inversion based pricing method to implement the analytical pricing formula. For the related Laplace inversion problem, we have extended one-sided Euler inversion algorithm to the two-sided case. The obtained two-sided Euler inversion algorithm is appealing as it usually has computable error bounds and thus can guarantee the accuracy via error control. In addition, we have also derived closed-form expansions for discrete Asian option prices under general one-dimensional diffusion models. The crucial theoretical results involved are the development of a systematic method to compute general expansion terms and the proof for the convergence of the expansion under some regularity conditions.

610711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
610711.value: In this project, we have concentrated on the analytical pricing problem of Asian options with jump risk, i.e., under jump diffusion models. Potential future research problems might include the study of the analytical pricing of Asian options with both jump risk and regime-switching risk, i.e., under regime-switching jump diffusion models with exponential-type jumps. This analytical pricing problem is more difficult due to the more complicated model structure. A potential approach might be still to apply the double Laplace transform method by investigating the real moments of the associated more complicated exponentially-stopped integral.

610711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
610711.value: Option pricing has been a fundamentally important issue in finance both theoretically and practically. Asian options have wide applications in equity, currency, interest rate, energy, and commodity and are actively traded in various financial markets. However, analytical pricing of Asian options beyond the Black-Scholes model is very challenging. In this project, we have developed analytical pricing methods to price Asian options under flexible jump diffusion models. Numerical experiments indicate that our pricing methods are accurate and efficient. Theoretically, to the best of our knowledge, we provide one of the first approaches to deriving analytical solutions to Asian option prices under jump diffusion models. In practice, Asian options can serve as suitable hedging instruments for firms with periodic revenues or expenses associated with certain assets and can also help reduce the risk of possible market manipulation near the maturity. Our research provides accurate and efficient pricing methods for Asian options and therefore plays an important role in their applications.

611211.label: Realisation of objectives
611211.value: 1. Investigate this new biological P removal process through chemical and microbial analysis; The sulfur induced luxury P-uptake and P-release has been explored in two Sequential Batch Reactors (SBR): 1) Anaerobic SBR for LOS-EBPR investigation and 2) the optimized Anaerobic/anoxic SBR for DS-EBPR investigation. The phenomenon of Sulfur-induced P-uptake and P-release was confirmed by the following investigations: (a) determination of the molar ratio of potassium variation to P-release; (b) Microscopic observersation of the poly-phosphate (poly-P), PHB, poly-S inclusions in the cultivated sludge; (c) confirmation of the biologically P reactions via inactivation test. In addition, the unknown microbial communities in Sulfur-EBPR sludge was identified through 16S rRNA pyrosequencing. 2. Analyze the mass balance covering chemical oxygen demand (COD), P, S and biomass; The COD and Sulfur balance were analyzed for both LOS-EBPR and DS-EBPR processes: The novel phenomenon of COD stored as the compounds of PHA and poly-S2-/S0 in reaction phase R and subsequently utilized as an internal electron donor for biomass growth and P uptake in reaction phase U are found through the COD balance analysis; the Sulfate reduction and production occurred in phase R and U respectively. The P balance and P removal of the SBR system was examined by a P mass balance analysis. It was conducted by comparing the amount of P accumulated in the sludge with the difference between the cumulative P entering and exiting the system. The biomass and energy balance was calculated based on the bio-P metabolic model. 3. Establish a possible metabolic mechanism for this new biological P removal process for Bio-P SANI development. The biochemical behavior of the sulfur induced P-uptake and release process has been investigated in both LOS-EBPR and DS-EBPR systems. The biological convestions of the organic-carbon storage and degradation, sulfur reduction and oxidation, nitrogen denitrification were correlated with the phosphorus uptake/release process: (i) the poly-P degradation/P-release was induced by the carbon uptake/storage (in form of poly-hydroxyalkanaotes (PHA)) and sulfate reduction/poly-S storage; (ii) the P-uptake was observed in association with degradation of (PHAs) and possible oxidation of stored sulfur substance into sulfate; (iii) the electron acceptor O2 and/or NO3 were utilized for sulfur oxidation, PHA degradation, poly-P formation and biomass production. The poly-S storage played an important role as an electron and energy carrier in both LOS-EBPR and DS-EBPR systems. The electron and energy flow of the intracellular storage for biological P removal was investigated through an electron balance evaluation and thermodynamic calculation.

611211.label: Major findings and research outcome
611211.value: This study expanded the SANI process into an Enhanced Biological Phosphorus Removal (EBPR) process. Two lab-scale systems were investigated in this study: (i) Limited Oxygen Sulfur-associated Enhanced Biological Phophorus Removal (LOS-EBPR) system, used oxygen as electron acceptor, for organic and phosphorus removal; and (ii) Denitrifying Sulfur-associated EBPR (SD-EBPR)) system, used nitrate as electron acceptor, for organic, nitrogen and phosphorus removal. Firstly, in the LOS-EBPR system, a sulfur cycle associated EBPR was explored in an alternating anaerobic/oxygen-limited aerobic sequencing batch reactor with acetate fed as the sole electron donor and sulfate as sulfur source at a total organic carbon to sulfur ratio of 1.1~3.1 (mg C/mg S). Phosphate uptake and polyphosphate formation were observed in this reactor that sustained high phosphate removal (20 mg P/L removed with 320 mg COD/L). This LOS-EBPR process was supported by six observations: 1) anaerobic phosphate release associated with acetate uptake, poly-phosphate hydrolysis, poly-hydroxyalkanoate (PHA) (and poly-S) formation and an “aerobic” phosphate uptake associated with PHA (and poly-S) degradation, and polyphosphate formation; 2) a high P/VSS ratio (>0.16 mg P/mg VSS) and an associated low VSS/TSS ratio (0.75) characteristic of conventional PAOs; 3) a lack of P-release and P-uptake with formaldehyde inactivation and autoclaved sterilized biomass; 4) an absence of chemical precipitated P crystals as determined by XRD analysis; 5) a sludge P of more than 90% polyphosphate as determined by sequential P extraction; and 6) microscopically, observed PHA, poly-P and S globules in the biomass. (Wu et al., 2013, Water research, 47, pp. 3057-3069.) We further developed the DS-EBPR system, a denitrifying sulfur cycle-associated phosphorus removal bio-process in an alternating anaerobic/anoxic SBR for simultaneous removal of organics, nitrogen and phosphorus. The 211 day SBR operation confirmed the sulfur cycle-associated biological phosphorus uptake utilizing nitrate as electron acceptor. Comparing with the LOS-EBPR this new Bioprocess can not only reduce operating time, but also enhance volumetric, also, the system performed well at high temperatures of 30 °C and a high salinity of 20% seawater. The stoichiometric ratios and kinetic rates were determined for this new EBPR process from in-situ SBR-cyclic tests and the batch tests under different temperatures (10, 20 and 30 oC). Increasing temperature did not significantly affect the stoichiometric ratios, but kinetic rate increases with temperature. With both fluorescent in-situ hybrid (FISH) and 454-pyrosequencing analysis, we double confirmed that there were no conventional PAOs in the SBR sludge. (Wu et al., 2014, Water research, 49, pp. 251-264.)

611211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
611211.value: The present DS-EBPR, operated as a granular UASB reactor, can be integrated with an attached-growth bioreactor for nitrification, so that a BioP-SANI can be developed to simultaneously achieve effective removal of organics, nitrogen and phosphorus from saline sewage in warm climate regions with little biological sludge production and oxygen demand. To realize this BioP-SANI process, future studies will be focused on the microbial ecology, DS-EBPR mechanism and process optimization.

611211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
611211.value: Eutrophication caused by excessive P losses to aquatic ecosystems through runoff and erosion is a leading cause of impairment of many freshwater and coastal marine ecosystems in the world. For mega-cities like Hong Kong, the scenario of nutrient pollution (i.e. Nitrogen and phosphorus) and P-resource depletion is even worse. Thus, it is keen to remove and recover the Phosphorus from the wastewater before discharging to sea. In this project, we developed a novel sulfur cycle-associated biological nutrient removal process for wastewater treatment. This novel bioprocess could not only remove organics and nutrient pollutions, and recover phosphorus, but also minimizes sludge production and reduce energy consumption. In addition to the process studies, a new mechanism utilizing sulfur cycle for P removal was also proposed with sufficient evidences of different aspects. Hence the outcome of the development of this novel biological process is attractive in both engineering and academic field. We believe with further and in-depth studies, this novel biological process can be implemented in Hong Kong for full-scale wastewater treatment in the future.

611311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
611311.value: 基於寬禁帶半導體材料氮化鎵（GaN）的功率電子器件由於其優良的材料特性而被認為最有望應用於新一代高效率功率轉換系統。與現今主流矽基功率器件構建的功率轉換器相比，氮化鎵基轉換器在系統性能上具有顯著優勢。隨著材料生長和器件製造等方面的迅速發展與進步，許多來自工業界與學術界的研究團隊已能應用氮化鎵材料製造出在性能上超越新型矽基器件的功率器件。儘管如此，氮化鎵功率器件在實現商業化方面仍面臨許多難題。其主要挑戰有：（1）常關型（又稱增強型）工作模式；（2）低關態漏電流；（3）平面功率器件中表面態引起的電流崩塌效應。為此，全球各研究機構開展了廣泛深入的研究。常關型器件主要從工藝角度得以實現，而關態漏電流則通過研發高阻態緩衝層生長技術而減小。介質薄膜（如SiN）鈍化可有效抑制電流崩塌，適合於低關態電壓（例如漏極直流電壓為28 V或45 V），但尚不能滿足高壓（>100 V）開關的要求。 本專案提出一種新型器件結構，有望解決當今氮化鎵基功率器件所面臨的上述難題。該器件為金屬-二維電子氣（2DEG）隧穿結場效應電晶體，可由標準生產的AlGaN/GaN異質結構實現。與常規AlGaN/GaN HEMT(高電子遷移率電晶體)中的歐姆接觸不同，該器件的源極金屬從側壁直接與2DEG溝道相連形成肖特基接觸。由此形成的源端隧穿結的開關由覆蓋其上的柵電極控制。電流大小受控於柵控隧穿結的寬度，而不由2DEG溝道中電子濃度決定，從而實現常關型工作模式。在高漏極電壓的關斷狀態下，源極肖特基結反偏，可大幅減小漏電。將隧穿結場效應電晶體的概念應用於縱向器件結構，使器件有源區不存在表面態，從而可消除電流崩塌。

611311.label: Realisation of objectives
611311.value: In this project, we have conducted extensive studies on AlGaN/GaN metal-2DEG tunnel junction field effect transistor (FET). The source terminal is a metal contact in Schottky contact with the sidewall of a 2DEG channel. The tunneling coefficient (i.e. the tunneling current) can be controlled by the voltage applied to a gate electrode that is placed on top of the tunnel junction. The objectives of this project are achieved as follows: • The tunneling process has been validated by the weak temperature dependence of the source-drain current, a signature of tunneling process. • Lateral AlGaN/GaN tunnel FET has been successfully developed with superior performance including normally-off operation (Vth = + 1.35 V), low leakage current (~10 pA/mm) and high on/off current ratio (1010). A maximum ON-state drain current density of 320 mA/mm has been obtained. The off-state leakage current is effectively suppressed by the source Schottky junction that is naturally reverse biased at the OFF-state. • The Schottky barrier heights (SBH) at the tunnel junction were extracted and found to be gate-bias-dependent, varying from 0.57 eV at VGS = -0.5 V to 0.3 eV at VGS = 1 V. This gate induced Schottky barrier lowering (SBL) effect is explained by the image charge effect. The larger SBH at lower gate voltage enables off-state blocking, while the lower SBH at higher gate voltage leads to high on-state current driving capability in the AlGaN/GaN TJ-FETs. • Novel AlN passivation and nitridation interfacial layer techniques were developed to suppress the current collapse and improve the threshold stability in lateral AlGaN/GaN power FETs. • Vertical TJ-FETs have been designed (with simulation). Epitaxial wafers have been obtained from an external source (DOWA Electronic Materials, Japan). Photo masks with device layout were designed and fabricated. Vertical TJ-FETs were also processed. The measured results showed that the electron injection from the source electrode is through a tunneling process. However, voltage blocking is small at around 20 V. The root cause is the small pitch size required, at around 0.1 um. Another challenge stems from the metal spill-over from the tunnel junction to the top, which led to the screening of the tunnel junction from the gate electrode. Multiple runs of process optimization have been carried out with limited success.
