611311.label: Major findings and research outcome
611311.value: A metal–2DEG tunnel-junction FET (TJ-FET) using a baseline AlGaN/GaN HEMT sample grown on a Si (111) substrate has been successfully demonstrated. The source features a metal–2DEG tunnel junction controlled by an overlapping gate electrode. Since the current turn-on/turnoff is mainly controlled by the tunnel junction instead of the 2DEG channel, a positive threshold corresponding to a normally off operation is realized in the as-grown normally on structure. This method of realizing a normally off operation is fundamentally different from the previous approaches that require a positive pinch-off voltage in the 2DEG channel. Furthermore, since the Schottky junction at the source electrode is naturally reverse biased in the OFF state with positive drain voltage, low leakage current and high ION/IOFF ratio are obtained. (peer-reviewed journal publication #1 and conference publication #1) We also demonstrated a Schottky source/drain (SSD) Al2O3/InAlN/AlN/GaN metal–insulator–semiconductor HEMT (MISHEMT) with enhanced OFF-state breakdown voltage. The Al2O3 gate insulation layer was used to reduce the gate leakage of the devices. Because an InAlN layer as thin as 7 nm is able to deliver high 2DEG density, SSD contacts directly made on the InAlN layer deliver low forward onset voltage and respectable drain current. In addition, the Schottky contacts exhibit good metal morphology that resulted in the elimination of the metallic spikes that commonly occurred in thermally annealed ohmic contacts. A device with LGD = 10 μm exhibits a breakdown voltage of 460 V with an OFF-state leakage current smaller than 10 μA/mm. As the InAlN/GaN heterojunction can be grown on low-cost Si wafers, the SSD MISHEMTs in this work provide a feasible candidate for power electronics. (peer-reviewed journal publication #2) The tunnel-junction FET also features a gate-to-drain access region that has to be properly passivated. A novel AlN passivation layer deposited by low thermal-budget plasma enhanced atomic layer deposition has been proposed and developed. The passivation mechanism is based on polarization charge compensation of the surface traps, which is fundamentally superior to the conventional SiNx passivation. (peer-reviewed journal publication #3 and #4). As the tunnel-junction FET features a gate dielectric between the gate electrode and GaN surface, interface traps at the dielectric/GaN interface must be suppressed adequately to obtain stable threshold voltage. A nitridation interfacial layer technique has been shown to effectively suppress the formation of the detrimental Ga-O bonds. (peer-reviewed journal publication #5 and conference publication #2)

611311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
611311.value: The Schottky contact between metal and the sidewall of a 2DEG channel has been shown to deliver low turn-on voltage and suppressed leakage current at reverse bias, yielding a promising device structure for power rectifiers. Thus, it is rather straightforward to integrate power switches (with transistors) and rectifiers on the same chip, enabling integrated power converters. Such an integration platform is currently under development in PI’s group. The AlN-passivation technique and nitridation interfacial layer technique are beneficial to all the lateral GaN power transistors. We plan to develop a project to integrate these novel processing techniques into Si fabs.

611311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
611311.value: Gallium nitride and related wide-bandgap semiconductors are suitable for power devices that promise to deliver lower loss and compact size in power conversion systems. By implementing the a quantum mechanical concept, i.e. tunneling, into the conventional AlGaN/GaN heterojunction transistor, a novel AlGaN/GaN metal-2DEG tunnel junction FET is demonstrated for the first time. The current flow is controlled by the tunnel junction, allowing normally-off operation that is highly desired in power switching applications. Owing to the high 2DEG density, the metal-2DEG tunnel junction at the source can deliver highly efficient carrier injection via quantum tunneling, enabling high tunnel current drive. The TJ-FET also features a natural reverse biased Schottky source junction when the device is in the off-state, thus, leading to low off-state leakage and high ION/IOFF ratio. The temperature dependence of TJ-FET has also been measured. Both the on-state I-V characteristics and off-state breakdown voltage of TJ-FET show good high temperature stability, as a benefit of quantum tunneling at source electrode. Meanwhile, equally important issues regarding to surface passivation and gate-dielectric/semiconductor interface have been addressed by newly developed techniques such as AlN-passivation and nitridation interfacial techniques, leading to significantly improved device stabilities.

611411.label: Project Objectives
611411.value: Based on the characteristics of probabilistic data, we will define all possible repair semantics to handle inconsistent data. Based on all possible repair semantics, we will define various CQAs, including range, join, and top-k queries for effective data analysis. Given a query, we will design efficient pruning algorithms to avoid searching all possible worlds and their associated repair worlds. In addition to the independent model used in the previous work to model the instances of probabilistic databases, in this project, we will model the correlations that may exist in the probabilistic tuples and design efficient solutions to answer CQA according to the correlation model. We will implement a prototype system to demonstrate the usefulness of the proposed solutions for CQA on probabilistic databases.

611411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
611411.value: Nowadays, data often originate from multiple resources, such as the crawled Web data from Internet, news or rumors from personal blogs, data collected by wireless sensor networks, and data exchanged or bought from corporations. By integrating the data from difference sources, we can offer users comprehensive information about entities and events. However, data collected from different resources are often uncertain and may contain noise, thus, to model these facts, probabilistic databases assign an existence probability to each collected tuple to indicate the confidence in its source. In addition to the uncertainty, data often exhibit inconsistencies or conflicts. Probabilistic databases well represent data uncertainty, but the inconsistency still exists, which may lead to errors in query answers. In order to handle these inconsistent probabilistic data, there are mainly two approaches; repairing and consistent query answer (CQA). For probabilistic data, repairing may not satisfy various application needs, especially, in some applications, where we might need to get statistical data, such as census databases. Therefore, in this project, we study consistent query answering over inconsistent probabilistic database. In CQA, the inconsistent tuples are not changed physically, instead, a CQA integrates the query answers from different versions of the logically repaired databases. Intuitively, CQA tries to obtain answers which are consistent over different repairs of the database. Due to exponential nature of possible worlds (i.e. possible combinations of instances that may appear in the real world) and possible repairs in the probabilistic databases, we have to address the following critical issues in order to efficiently obtain consistent answers: 1) Based on the characteristics of probabilistic data, we define various CQA according to the all possible repairs semantics, with respect to different repair models, integrity constraints, and query types. 2) Given a query, we will design efficient pruning algorithms to avoid searching all possible worlds and their associated possible repairs. 3) In addition to the independent model used by the previous work to model the instances of probabilistic databases, in this project, we will model the correlations that may exist in the probabilistic tuples and design efficient solutions to answer CQA with tuple correlations under the different repair semantics and integrity constraints. We will apply these solutions to data analysis applications over inconsistent probabilistic databases and demonstrate the usefulness of real applications, such as web data integration and sensor data analysis. 现今， 数据往往来自于不同的数据源， 如网上数据，个人博客数据， 传感网路数据， 和公司交换或购买的数据。如果我们能够把这些数据有效的整合起来， 我们就能给用户关于实体或事件的整体信息。 但是数据在收集过程中往往存在不确定性和噪声，为了处理这样的问题， 概率数据库赋予每个收集的数据记录一个概率用来表达记录存在的可能性。但是即使是概率数据库， 数据之间还可能存在矛盾或不一致。 基本上， 有两种方法处理数据的不一致，修理数据和一致性查询。 但对不确定数据来讲， 单纯的数据修理不一定能满足所有应用的需求，因此在这个项目里,我们准备研究一致性查询在概率数据库中的应用。 在不一致查询中， 我们没有改变数据， 相反的我们研究怎样能够把不同版本修理的数据整合在一起。 一致性查询就是要在不同版本修理的数据中找到一致性的答案。 因为存在指数级的可能世界及其相对应的修理， 为了能够快速回答一致性查询， 我们需要解决以下非常关键的问题：1）根据数据特点， 针对所有可能的数据修理方法， 定义不同类型的一致性查询； 2）指定一个查询， 为了避免搜索所有的可能世界和相对应的数据修理， 我们将设计有效的剪枝策略和过滤算法； 3）对相关连的数据， 我们对相关数据进行建模并且设计快速一致性查询方案。我们将把解决这些关键问题的方法运用到不一致概率数据的分析同时展现这些方案在实际应用中的有用性。

611411.label: Major findings and research outcome
611411.value: 1. In order to detect inconsistency existed in the databases, we first investigated various data dependencies, including comparable dependencies [J3], differential dependencies [J5], matching dependencies [J7], metric dependencies [C1]. Rules can be derived from these dependencies to further capture data inconsistency. 2. We then studied various different probabilistic queries over probabilistic databases, including groups subspace skyline [J1] and top-k dominating queries [J2]. We proposed efficient solutions to address these queries and meanwhile we obtained knowledge about semantics of these probabilistic queries. 3. To study the correlation existed in probabilistic databases, we specifically investigated interval reverse nearest neighbor queries over correlated probabilistic data [C7]. Furthermore, we studied the problem of finding frequent itemsets over probabilistic databases [C2, C3]. The found frequent itemset can be used to infer correlation existed in the data. 4. We found that the characteristic of repair worlds shares the same spirit of possible worlds in probabilistic databases. Thus, in this project, we continued studying various pruning and indexing techniques to speed up query processing, the results published in [J9, J10, C9, J6]. We further investigated the distributed solutions to speed up queries [C4 , C8]. 5. Finally, we extended our work to study efficient solutions to speed up various query processing over graph data [J4, J8, C6]

611411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
611411.value: The techniques developed from this project, pruning, indexing and parallel speed up solutions, can be further investigated in other applications, such as social media and graph streams.

611411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
611411.value: Like certain databases, inconsistency also exists in probabilistic database. In this project, we first studied various data dependencies in order to capture inconsistency in probabilistic databases. Then we investigated different probabilistic queries in order to understand semantics. To capture the correlation existed in the probabilistic data, we also studied frequent itemset mining solutions in probabilistic databases. We further developed efficient pruning and indexing methods, even parallel solutions, to speed up query processing. Finally, we studied efficient solutions to speed up queries over graph data.

611711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
611711.value: Matching objects by their geometric shapes with theoretical guarantees is an active topic in computational geometry. When matching objects, translation and rotation may be applied to maximize the similarity measure and this calls for efficient algorithms to align the objects for matching. The alignment configuration space often has high complexity and there may be many local maxima. As a result, the running times of known algorithms to find the exact best match are prohibitively high in general. The presence of noise also diminishes the significance of the exact best match. This creates a demand and an opportunity for approximation algorithms. Our goal is to develop efficient algorithms to match objects and sets of objects approximately with rigid motion such that there is a theoretical guarantee of the match quality. 形體比擬是計算幾何其中一焦點課題。比擬兩個形體時，須移動形體，使其重疊得最多，從而得知相似程度。物體移動的配置空間異常複雜，往往要花大量時間在空間中尋找最佳的配置位置。 由於輸入可能有誤差，不一定須費時尋找最佳配置。故此焦點落於設計快速的算法去找近似最佳匹配。這研究項目的目標正是設計快速近似算法去比擬形體，並証明其準確度。

611711.label: Realisation of objectives
611711.value: We designed an efficient algorithm for matching two convex polyhedra P and Q in three dimensions under rigid motion (i.e., translation and rotation). If P and Q can be placed under rigid motion so that their overlap is at least a constant fraction of the maximum volume of P and Q, then our algorithm can place P and Q such that their overlap is at least (1-epsilon) times the best possible, where epsilon is a relative error parameter between 0 and 1/2 specified by the user. If P and Q cannot be placed under rigid motion so that their overlap is at least some constant fraction of the maximum volume of P and Q, our algorithm will output that P and Q are not similar. Overlap is a similarity measure that is robust under noise and perturbation. The running time of our algorithm is O(epsilon^{-3} * n * (log n)^{3.5}), where n is the number of vertices of P and Q. The significance is that the running time is nearly linear in n for a fixed epsilon. Note that it takes at least linear time just to read the entire input. We also designed an approximation algorithm for the largest common point set (LCP) problem. Given two discrete point sets P and Q in R^d of sizes m and n, respectively, the LCP problem seeks the largest subsets A of P and B of Q such that A and B have the same cardinality, and there exists a rigid motion that makes the bottleneck distance between A and B at most epsilon, where epsilon is an input parameter specified by the user. This problem finds application in aligning two sets of feature points. The time complexities of previous exact algorithms have high polynomial dependence on m and n. We propose algorithms for a relaxed version of the LCP problem. Let k be the largest subset size achievable for the given parameter epsilon. In the plane, our algorithm can find subsets A and B of size at least k such that the bottleneck distance between A and B under rigid motions is at most (1+eta)*epsilon, where eta is a relative error tolerance in the range (0,1) given by the user. The running time is O((n^2*m^2)/eta * (m+n)*log n). We also solved this relaxed version in d dimensions under translations. The running time is O((mn)/eta^r * (m+n)^{1.5}*log n), where r = 1 for d =2 and r = 2d-1 for d >= 3. We also studied two other variations of the shape matching problems. First, we studied the problem of matching two convex bodies P and Q in d dimensions with respect to symmetric difference under homotheties. That is, we can translate and scale P so that its symmetric difference from Q is minimized. (Note that both overlap and symmetric difference are similarity measures that are robust under noise and perturbation.) We showed that the problem can be solved by convex programming although the objective function is not convex at all. We also give a combinatorial algorithm in the plane that runs in O(n*(log n)^3) expected time, where n is the total number of vertices of P and Q. Scaling has rarely been allowed in the previous algorithmic results on shape matching. The second variation that we studied is the matching of two sets of polygons in the plane. Each polygon can be non-convex and may have holes. Our algorithm aligns the two sets of polygons using rigid motion so that their overlap is at least the optimum minus epsilon*min{area(P), area(Q)} with high probability. The running time is O(n^3*epsilon^{-4}*polylog(n)), where n is the total number of vertices. In all, we have achieved the three project objectives.

Our algorithm can produce an overlap that is at least (1-epsilon) times the best possible, where epsilon is a relative error parameter between 0 and 1/2 specified by the user, assuming that optimal overlap is at least some constant fraction of the maximum volume of P and Q. The running time is O(epsilon^{-3} * n * (log n)^{3.5}), where n is the number of vertices of P and Q. This result appears in the first conference article and the second journal article in Part C. We also designed an approximation algorithm for the LCP problem. Let k be the largest subset size achievable for the given parameter epsilon. In the plane, our algorithm can find subsets A and B of size at least k such that the bottleneck distance between A and B under rigid motions is at most (1+eta)*epsilon, where eta is a relative error tolerance in the range (0,1) given by the user. The running time is O((n^2*m^2)/eta * (m+n)log n). We also solved this relaxed version in d dimensions under translations. The running time is O((mn)/eta^r * (m+n)^{1.5}*log n), where r = 1 for d =2 and r = 2d-1 for d >= 3. This result is under review (see the third journal article in Part C). We propose an algorithm to match two convex bodies P and Q in d dimensions with respect to symmetric difference under homotheties. We show that the problem can be solved by convex programming. We also give a combinatorial algorithm in the plane that runs in O(n*(log n)^3) expected time, where n is the total number of vertices of P and Q. This result will appear in the second conference article in Part C. We studied the matching of two sets of polygons in the plane. Our algorithm aligns them using rigid motion so that their overlap is at least the optimum minus epsilon*min{area(P), area(Q)} with high probability. The running time is O(n^3*epsilon^{-4}*polylog(n)), where n is the total number of vertices. This result appears in the first journal article in Part C. We also obtained a faster algorithm for constructing the straight skeleton of a polygon from its motorcycle graph. Straight skeleton finds application in computer aided design. This result appears in the fourth journal article in Part C.

611711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
611711.value: There is potential in further devloping our algorithm for the LCP problem under rigid motion. Our algorithm works in two dimensions, and it may be possible to extend the algorithm to work in three dimensions. But if we extend the current algorithm naively, it would require dealing with spherical surface patches in the configuration space. While this is conceptually not difficult, doing it in a practical manner is quite challenging. Also, it would be interesting to study how scaling can be allowed. Our current result on matching two convex polytopes with respect to symmetric difference allows scaling and translations. It would be interesting to allow rotations as well. Rotations usually pose a problem for computing the exact optimum in shape matching. Therefore, one may need to settle for approximation algorithms. Since a straight skeleton can be cosntructed in nearly linear time from a motorcycle graph, it is an interesting problem to improve the state-of-art algorithm for computing a motorcycle graph of the vertices of a polygon.

611711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
611711.value: This project produces several exact and approximation algorithms for matching polygons, polytopes, and point sets in the plane and in higher dimensions. These algorithms are efficient as their running times depend on low-order polynomials of the input size. Shape matching problems arise in various context, including image processing, computer vision, and feature alignments. Therefore, we expect that our algorithms will be useful in such application domains.

611811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
611811.value: Spreadsheets are widely used by domain experts in organizations to perform critical business tasks such as accounting, resource management and financial modeling. As many of these tasks are similar to each other, domain experts often perform new tasks by reusing a group of cells from some earlier tasks’ spreadsheets and adapt them as needed. While such reuse has an obvious benefit in improving productivity, it is highly vulnerable to regression faults. This is because spreadsheets lack high-level abstraction commonly found in conventional programs, so that spreadsheet reuse typically involves low-level adaptations, which are tedious and error-prone. Furthermore, such adaptations can trigger silent changes to the cell formulas as side-effects. Such side-effects might deviate from the intention of the users and create regression faults. There is empirical evidence that regression faults in spreadsheet reuse are common in practice. How to detect these faults effectively poses an important research challenge. In the spreadsheet paradigm, the input/output interface of a group of cells is implicitly defined by cell coordinates. Such an implicit interface is prone to various differences between spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to apply conventional regression testing techniques, which assume that the two program versions have mostly the same input/output interface such that their executions are comparable. In this project, we propose to study the following research questions arising from the reuse of spreadsheets: What are the common changes arising from spreadsheet reuse? What the common patterns of regression faults induced by these changes? Can we expose these regression faults by comparing the execution behaviors of two spreadsheet versions? How to summarize behavioral difference in debugging aids? How to generate behavior-differentiating test case to supplement existing test suite? The study of these questions will help develop an effective framework that enables domain experts to reuse spreadsheets safely for a new application. Prototype tools will be developed to support the proposed framework. To evaluate the applicability of our research results, we will conduct experiments using real world spreadsheet applications from various domains. This project will benefit Hong Kong as a competitive financial and service center. 電子表格在各種行業中有著極為廣泛的應用。為了完成會計，資源管理和財務建模等任務，業務人員經常需要開發大量複雜的電子報表。這些任務往往彼此重復，所以一種常見的做法是復用已有的表格中的一組或多組表格單元。這種復用可以極大的提高開發效率。然而，它極易引入回歸錯誤。這是因為電子報表作為一種程序開發語言缺乏抽象，信息封裝等高級語言具備的特性，這就導致表格單元復用時往往需要做大量的修改，例如逐個調整表格單元引用。這些修改非常繁瑣而且極易出錯。另外，當表格單元被拷貝粘貼的時候，常用的開發環境(如Microsoft Excel)會對其中的公式進行自動修改。這種修改作為拷貝粘貼的副作用很有可能出乎業務人員的意料，引入回歸錯誤。有經驗証據表明，復用錯誤是電子報表中出現錯誤的一個常見原因。在一些已知案例中，復用錯誤直接導致企業蒙受經濟損失。因此，如何有效地自動檢測出這種錯誤是一個重要的研究問題。這個問題的難點在於在電子表格程序的輸入/輸出出接口被隱式的定義為公式中引用的表格單元地址。這種方式定義的接口極易被兩個電子表格之間的排版，輸入數據位置等差異而改變。這就導致了傳統的回歸測試技術很難在這裡被直接應用，因為這些傳統技術能應用一個前提條件就是程序的接口基本保持不變，從而使得原始程序和復用后的程序之間的執行結果可以被比較。在電子表格中，這個前提條件是很難成立的。 在這個項目中，我們建議研究以下幾個電子報表復用中產生的問題：在復用電子報表的時候，有那些對復用單元的修改是常見的？這些修改又會帶來何種可能的回歸錯誤模式？我們可否改進傳統的回歸測試技術以檢測到這些錯誤？如何可視化檢測到的錯誤以使得業務人員更加容易調試？如何自動生成測試數據以使得潛在的復用錯誤更加容易被檢測出來？這些問題的研究結果將有助於建立一個有效的框架，幫助業務人員更加可靠的復用電子表格。我們也將開發這個框架的原型系統。為了評估我們研究結果的實用性，我們將使用實際的電子表格進行試驗。這個項目將在各個方面幫助香港成為一個有競爭力的金融和服務中心。

611811.label: Realisation of objectives
611811.value: Spreadsheets are a popular computation paradigm used for data storage and analysis, decision support, financial reporting, and quality control. Despite their popularity, spreadsheets are subject to errors. However, conventional quality assurance measures for software such as unit tests and assert statements are generally inapplicable to spreadsheets. To understand the quality issues arising from spreadsheet, we approached the first objective by collecting spreadsheets over the web as well as acquiring the EUSES corpus used by a few research works. The EUSES corpus contains 4,037 spreadsheets over 11 categories. A Java tool based on Apache POI was developed to parse and process the collected spreadsheets. A research assistant was recruited to carry out these tasks. We encountered several major challenges. First, the spreadsheets collected are mostly unrelated to one another. Second, there are no documentation or specification of the collected spreadsheets. As such, we need to inspect each spreadsheet manually and infer its likely objectives. Third, these spreadsheets come with no test cases, bug reports, patches or comments. We need to identify potential spreadsheet issues by checking the cell formulas of a spreadsheet against its inferred objectives. We find that the values of some contiguous cells are not necessarily consistently evaluated by formulas. For example, some values are directly typed while some are evaluated by formulas. Even for those evaluated by formulas resulting in the same results, discrepancy can occur in the formula expressions. Some expressions include the references of blank cells but some do not. We term these issues as ambiguous computation smells instead of errors because these issues can induce errors when referenced cells in formulas are updated as the spreadsheet evolves. We made a systematic study of these computation smells based on the EUSES corpus and captured their patterns. Our experiments revealed that 27.3% of spreadsheets with formulas suffer from the ambiguous computation smells. We also identified the conditions under which these smells can manifest as errors. The work was conducted together with a PhD student from the Chinese Academy of Sciences when he visited HKUST under the PI's supervision in 2013. To achieve the second objective, we developed an automated framework AmCheck to detect and repair ambiguous computation smells in spreadsheets. First, AmCheck clusters contiguous cells with the same intended computation based on some heuristics. The heuristics manages to identify clusters in 44.7% of the experimented spreadsheets. Second, AmCheck deploys an algorithm to detect ambiguous computation smells among the identified cell clusters. Third, AmCheck tries to synthesize the correct formulas by mapping the problem into a constraint-solving problem, which can be handled by existing constraint solvers. AmCheck then repairs the smelly cells using the synthesized formulas. We also studied the constraint checking methodology. To achieve the third objective, we implemented AmCheck using Java on top of the Apache POI. Experiments using the EUSES corpus confirmed that AmCheck can repair 99.1% of the smelly clusters. AmCheck considers detected smells are errors if they cannot be repaired using the synthesized formulas. To evaluate the usefulness of AmCheck, we conducted a user study by applying it to 10 actively used spreadsheets provided by the finance office in an institute and invited the users of these spreadsheets for an interview to validate the detected smells as well as their root causes. As a result, AmCheck found 23 confirmed errors in 4 spreadsheets. Most users committed these errors due to inconsistent updates to cells created by copy-and-paste during spreadsheet evolution. CACheck extends AmCheck to handle in-homogeneous cell arrays where the cells referenced by a formula need not fall into the same row or column. An MPhil student was recruited to enhance the work of AmCheck. We found that the clustering heuristics used by AmCheck can be further improved. In particular, cells that are subject to the same computation are not necessarily contiguous. Further, tabulation styles vary significantly across users. Hence, a universal heuristics does not achieve a good balance of precision and recall across spreadsheets. In view of that, we clustered cells with the same computation based on their strong and weak features. Strong features can be used to cluster those cells that carry out the same computation. We then identify the set of weak features that are applicable to each cell cluster. Another cycle of clustering can be conducted based on the identified weak features. Note that these weak features can vary across cell clusters due to diversified tabulation styles. We implemented the enhanced technique as CUSTODES in Java and applied it to the EUSES corpus. Promising results were obtained. We release the tool and our experimental data set. In 2015, the Enron corpus was released based on the emails in the Enron court case. The corpus contains 15,929 spreadsheets used earlier by Enron employees. However, these spreadsheets were not maintained by a version management system. The corpus is not amenable to the study of regression faults in spreadsheets. We developed a methodology and successfully applied to the Enron corpus to recover the versioning information of the spreadsheets. We call it Versioned Enron corpus (VEnron), and release it to the public. At the end of our project, we conducted a systematic study to compare the effectiveness of existing spreadsheet checking methodologies and tools. We also explored how to carry out table clone detection to improve the effectiveness of revealing spreadsheet errors.

611811.label: Major findings and research outcome
611811.value: The findings of this project were/will be disseminated by three journal (TSE, JSS and IST) and four conference publications at ICSE and FSE. Two research students were trained. We made several major findings. 1. Ambiguous computation smells are a common type of regression spreadsheet faults. Experiments found that such smells occur in 27.3% of spreadsheets. 2. Ambiguous computation smells mostly arise from improper updates to cells created using autofill or copy-and-paste of cells from other spreadsheets. 3. Ambiguous computation smells can be effectively detected by an automated technique. Most of these smells can be automatically repaired using constraint solving. 4. Smells that cannot be repaired are likely errors. 5. Effective constraint handling requires knowledge of context consistency. 6. Users tabulate spreadsheet in diversified styles. It is difficult to formulate a universal heuristics to cluster cells that are subject to the same intended computation. 7. Users tabulate the cells subject to the same intended computation consistently using the same style. This enables cells to be effectively clustered based on strong and weak features. 8. Smells usually occur in minority. It is possible to detect smells in each cluster as outliers under a feature space. 9. Versioning information can be effectively recovered from an industrial spreadsheet corpus based on features and email contents. This allows recovery of a versioned spreadsheet corpus. We release this corpus as VEnron, which is the first versioned industry-based spreadsheet corpus. 10. The performances of existing spreadsheet detection tools vary a lot. Tools developed by this project are the most effective ones based on the evaluation using three public spreadsheet corpora: EUSES, Enron and Hawaii Kooker. Findings 1-4 were disseminated by an ICSE conference paper C1, an FSE conference paper C4 and a TSE journal paper [J3]. Finding 5 was disseminated by an IST journal paper J1. Findings 6-8 will be disseminated by an ICSE conference paper C2. Finding 9 will be disseminated by another ICSE conference paper C3. Finding 10 will be disseminated by a JSS journal paper J2.

611811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
611811.value: Our project findings can lead to the following future work. 1. Our tool implements intra-worksheet smell detection. It can be further enhanced to support inter-worksheet and inter-spreadsheet smell detection. 2. The current methodology focuses on computational smell. Extension of the methodology can focuses on data smells of those cells referenced by formulas. 3. The current version of VEnron recovers only the versioning information from user emails. We may re-examine these emails and recover fixes and update dependency from the emails. 4. The current project evaluates only the effectiveness of the methodology. It is possible to evaluate the methodology’s usability through more user studies.

611811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
611811.value: Spreadsheets are a popular computation paradigm used for data storage and analysis, decision support, financial reporting, and quality control. Despite their popularity, spreadsheets are found to be error-prone. Spreadsheet users rarely apply rigorous software engineering practice in maintaining the evolution of spreadsheets and keeping track of spreadsheet bugs. Conventional quality assurance measures for software such as unit tests and assert statements are generally inapplicable to spreadsheets. We made an empirical study of the spreadsheet issues. The study identified a type of smell commonly occurring when users prepare/maintain spreadsheets using copy-and-paste and autofill. The smell happens when a set of related cells is evaluated using different computation. We developed automated techniques to address the quality issue of spreadsheet in the absence of specification, test cases and bug management. The techniques were implemented as Java tools and applied successfully to detect spreadsheet smells and errors. Evaluations on spreadsheet corpus confirm that our techniques outperform the existing ones. We released our experimental results and data set publicly. In addition, we prepared and released the first spreadsheet corpus with versioning information based on the 15,929 spreadsheets used earlier by the Enron employees. The versioned spreadsheets greatly facilitate future studies on spreadsheet regression faults.

612011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
612011.value: For accurate diagnosis and prognosis of arteries diseases, e.g., aneurysm, stenosis and arteriovenous malformation, imaging of blood vessels including magnetic resonance angiography (MRA), computed tomography angiography, and three-dimensional (3D) rotational angiography plays an important role in the quantitative analysis of vasculatures. In particular, MRA is a non-invasive imaging method and can provide more accurate information about flow dynamics in brains. As such, vascular segmentation in MRA images has been a key technique for 3D patient-specific vasculature modeling in endovascular treatment planning and assessment. In this project, in order to improve the existing vascular segmentation techniques, we aim at developing methods for reliable and accurate detection of three-dimensional curvilinear structures, e.g., lines in 2D and tubes in 3D, by using the concept of optimally oriented flux (OOF). OOF is a new concept proposed by the PI and his student for quantifying the amount of image gradients flowing into a spherical region. Different from the conventional flux computation, the image gradients are projected along a specific direction before the OOF computation is performed and the projection direction can be computed analytically. This helps to make the OOF estimation more robust to curvilinear structures that deviate slightly from the round shape. By using our recently proposed efficient implementation of oriented flux, the estimation of OOF is computationally efficient even though the size of spherical region is relatively large. Because of these advantages, the concept of OOF has been currently extended by our group and the other groups, e.g., Benmansour and Cohen (CVPR09 and IJCV10) for curvilinear structure centerline tracking and vessel enhancement, and Mille et al. (MIDAS09) for coronary artery tracking. We plan in this project to enhance OOF in two aspects. First, OOF is sensitive to symmetric image gradient patterns. We recently discover that measuring image gradient anti-symmetry can help locate the structure boundary, namely oriented flux anti-symmetry (OFA), and OFA can complement with OOF in the structure detection. We will develop a new framework for combining OOF and OFA. Second, we have proved that the OOF estimation can be implemented as an image filtering process. We will extend this work to OOF filter bank for studying the behavior of different local image structures, in particular, bifurcations and aneurysms which are difficult to segment in angiograms. The proposed framework will be validated in experiments using phantoms, synthetic datasets and vascular images, and through comparisons with other related curvilinear structure segmentation methods. 爲了能夠準確的檢測并預知動脈疾病，例如，動脈瘤，血管狹窄和動靜脈的畸形，血管成像，包括磁共振血管造影(MRA)，計算機斷層掃描血管造影和三維（3D）旋轉血管造影，在血管系統的定量分析中起著很大的作用。特別是，MRA是一種非侵入性的成像方法，能提供大腦更準確的血流動力學信息。因此，一直以來，在血管內介入治療的具體規劃和評估的過程中，MRA圖像的血管分割是針對具體病人的3D血管系統建模的關鍵技術。在這個項目中，爲了提高現有的血管分割技術，我們希望能夠開發可靠準確的三維曲綫結構的檢測方法，例如，用最優有向通量（OOF）的概念，進行二維的曲綫和三維的管狀結構的檢測。OOF是由PI與他的學生提出的對圖像中指向球形區域內部的梯度流的量化的一種新的概念。 與傳統的通量計算不同的是，在OOF計算執行之前，圖像的梯度被投影到特定方向上，並且投影的方向可以通過分析計算得出。這有助於使OOF的計算對於與圓形稍有不同的曲綫結構更具魯棒性。通過使用我們最近提出的有向通量的高效率實現方法，即便是在球形區域較大的情況下， OOF的計算效率也會非常高。鑒於這些優點，OOF的概念目前已經被我們研究小組以及其他的研究小組進行了擴展，例如，Benmansour和Cohen (CVPR09 and IJCV10)將其擴展到追蹤曲綫結構中心線和血管結構的加強，Mille等人(MIDAS09)則將其擴展到追蹤冠狀動脈。在本項目中， 我們計畫在兩個方面強化OOF。首先，OOF對於對稱的图像梯度模式是敏感的。我們最近發現，度量圖像梯度的反對稱性能夠幫助確定血管邊界，這種方法稱為有向通量反對稱方法（OFA）。OFA可以彌補OOF在結構檢測方面的不足。我們將會開發一個新的框架來把OOF和OFA結合起來。其次，我們已經證明OOF的計算可以通過圖像濾波過程來實現。我們將擴展這種方法到OOF過濾，進而研究不同的局部圖像結構的行為，特別是，分支點和血管瘤這兩種在血管造影圖像中非常難於分割的情況。我們將在模擬，人工合成數據集和血管圖像集上對提出的框架進行實驗驗證，並與其他相關的曲綫結構分割方法進行比較。

612011.label: Realisation of objectives
612011.value: The project objectives have been achieved successfully. In this project, as stated in the first objective, we focused on developing new curvilinear structure detection methods for segmentation of blood vessels in angiograms. The methods we proposed can effectively help segmentation of normal blood vessel segments in brains and hearts, aneurysmal regions, and areas of stenosis with complex shapes and varying intensity profiles. The methods can also handle images acquired by magnetic resonance angiography imaging and computed tomography angiography imaging. We believe that the newly developed methods can have great potential to contribute in the development of computing tools for reliable and accurate medical image analysis and biomedical research. The segmented results can be utilized to build three dimensional numerical models for surgical and endovascular treatment planning. Details of the methods we developed can be found in the Section 6.1. As stated in the second objectives, our methods have been validated by using synthetic datasets and clinical images. Different synthetic datasets were generated to test our methods in different settings, e.g., noisy image regions, bifurcations and vessels with different sizes. Moreover, we used two publicly available databases, namely Rotterdam Standardized Evaluation Framework, and Coronary Artery Stenoses Detection and Quantification Evaluation Framework, for method evaluation and comparison. The published evaluation results, as compared with other related methods, show that our methods can give good performance in vascular segmentation. In this project, we have also developed new methods for image registration. First, with a new feature based on Crystal Dislocation Energy, image registration process can now incorporate orientation information (from gradient) and long-range pixel interaction. It is shown the new registration framework has fast convergence rate and high registration accuracy. Second, we have proposed a new registration method for liquid chromatography mass spectrometry images which are very useful in comparing proteomes for disease biomarker discovery. The new method is developed based on dynamic time warping and Kullback-Leibler distance, and validated on two real data sets.

612011.label: Major findings and research outcome
612011.value: In this project, we have developed and tested new methods for vessel segmentation in angiograms [1-4, see below] and image registration [5, see below]. In total, our findings have been published in 2 journals (IEEE Trans on Image Processing) and 5 conferences (ICIP, CVPR and MICCAI), and submitted to 3 journals for review. Details can be found in Part C of this document. [1] For segmenting intracranial vessels and aneurysms, we have proposed the use of multi-range filters and local variances to identify blood vessel segments in images. This method has been validated and compared more effective than other related methods. (IEEE Trans on Image Processing, 22(3), pages 845-859, 2013). [2] Partly based on the work in [1], we have extended the method with the optimally oriented flux for 3D curvilinear structure analysis which is shown very useful for detecting vessels with varying intensity profiles. (IEEE Trans on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, under preparation.) [3] For segmenting stenosis, we have exploited the deep learning concepts, Markov model and graph based segmentation method to detection stenosis with different complex shapes and varying intensity profiles. Methods have been tested in a publicly available evaluation framework and ranked high in the evaluation results. (Medical Image Analysis, Pattern Recognition, and IEEE Trans on Medical Imaging, all journals are under review.) (ICIP’12) [4] For segmenting major vessels on heart in computed tomography angiograms (CTA), we have developed methods by using graph based segmentation methods and adaptive cylinder flux based connectivity. The evaluation results on synthetic images and clinical datasets are encouraging and presented in MICCAI’13, CVPR’13 and ICIP’13. [5] In this project, new image registration methods have been proposed by using a new feature, namely Crystal Dislocation Energy, and Kullback-Leibler Distance. The methods have been tested on magnetic resonance brain images and multi-resolution liquid chromatography mass spectrometry (LC-MS) images. Results have been presented in ICIP’12 (oral) and IEEE Trans on Image Processing, 22(1), pages 229-243, 2013)

612011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
612011.value: The research work done in this project can be furthered developed in the following directions. [1] The segmentation methods are developed for different vascular diseases, e.g., aneurysm and stenosis, and different vessel segments, e.g., intracranial vessels in brain and coronary artery in heart. One possible direction is to build a framework for unifying different vascular segmentation techniques so that a more general segmentation framework can be developed for handling different imaging datasets. [2] The registration method we developed in this project is promising as the new feature can effectively capture orientation information extracted from the images and long-range interaction between images. This feature may become more useful when the method is applied to images with orientation information, e.g., phase contrast magnetic resonance images and diffusion weighted images.

612011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
612011.value: The goal of this research project is to develop new curvilinear structure detection techniques for vascular segmentation in magnetic resonance angiograms. The developed techniques will be extremely useful for the minimally invasive endovascular therapy of vascular diseases including aneurysm, stenosis and arteriovenous malformation. It is because the segmentation results can be used to build patient-specific computer models in which vessel size can be measured and vessel shape can be quantified. Also, with the models, clinicians can easily visualize the spatial relations between blood vessels in brains or hearts before disease is treated. Magnetic resonance angiography is a non-invasive imaging method and does not require contrast agent injection. However, vascular segmentation on magnetic resonance angiograms is challenging because image intensity can vary significantly and vessel shape can change greatly, e.g., tubes with different diameters, bifurcations and aneurysms. The new methods developed in this research project can help reliably detect blood vessel segments in brains and hearts, as well as abnormal regions, e.g., aneurysms and stenosis. We believe that the new methods can be very helpful for the diagnosis and prognosis of vascular, colonic or tracheal diseases.

612111.label: Project Title(Chinese)
612111.value: 高效費比的納米柱陣列太陽能電池

612111.label: Project Objectives
612111.value: To develop a practical process for fabricating 3-D nano/micro-pillar arrays. Engineered 3-D structures have broad applications in integrated electronics, optoelectronics, sensing, etc. The conventional methods to achieve well-controlled 3-D nano/microstructures primarily rely on lithography, which is costly and time consuming, so they are not suitable for solar cell applications. We are aiming at developing new cost-effective approaches to fabricating such structures with photovoltaic materials including Si, CdS, CdTe, copper-indium-gallium-selenide (CIGS), etc. These structures must have well defined geometry, in terms of pillar diameter, height, pitch and ordering. To understand light-structure interaction inside 3-D nano/microstructures. Understanding the propagation of light in 3-D structures is not only crucial for photonic applications, but also of significant scientific importance. The proposed structures have dimensions close to or less then the optical wavelength, so light-structure interaction cannot be described with classic optics. Through well-designed experiments, assisted by theoretical simulations we will further develop the understanding on light reflectance, transmission and absorption in ordered nano/micropillar arrays, to pave the way for future photonic applications. To build scalable solar cell devices with pillar arrays. After successfully fabricating nano/micro-pillar arrays and gaining enough knowledge of their fundamental optical properties, we will fabricate photovoltaic devices using these structures. In this three year study, we will explore several material systems, mainly including CdS, CdTe and CIGS. To develop a scalable process, we will explore different material synthesis technologies including chemical vapor deposition, electrochemical deposition and spin coating. The performance of these devices will be characterized and optimized systematically.

612111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
612111.value: As the demand for clean and sustainable energy resources has grown rapidly in the recent years, enormous effort is being invested on seeking next generation solar cell technologies globally. The conventional planar crystalline solar cells have decent energy conversion efficiency but high manufacturing cost. Planar thin film photovoltaic technologies come with relatively low cost but low efficiency. Recently, synthetic and artificial nano/micro-structured materials have been actively investigated as candidate materials for next generation solar cells, with potency to achieve high conversion efficiency at low manufacturing cost. In particular, three-dimensional (3-D) arrays of semiconductor nanorods/nanopillars have been demonstrated with significantly improved optical absorption, mainly due to light trapping inside the 3-D structures. Such enhanced absorption leads to improved performance over conventional planar structures. On the other hand, these 3-D structures can be fabricated on either rigid or flexible substrates with low cost and scalable processes, which results in attractive cost-effectiveness. In this study, we propose to explore well engineered 3-D nanopillar arrays for efficient light harvesting and photovoltaics. Specifically, we will develop a scalable process to fabricate ordered 3-D nanopillar arrays using low cost materials. More importantly, we will investigate the effect of the geometrical parameters of the nanopillar arrays, e. g. pillar diameter, height, pitch, etc., on the performance of solar cell devices through well designed experiments supported by theoretical simulations, in order to identify an optimal configuration for maximum energy conversion efficiency. Ultimately, we hope to be able to fabricate 3-D nanopillar solar cells on both rigid and flexible substrates to meet a variety of solar cell applications ranging from utility-scale power generation to portable electronics. 近年以來，隨著對可再生能源的需求的快速增長，全球各國都致力於開發下一代太陽能電池技術。傳統的平面硒太陽能電池有比較高的轉換效率，但是製造成本也比較高。平面的薄膜太陽能電池成本比較低廉，但是效率也相對較低。最近的研究表明，合成的納米/微米材料可以作為潛在的材料製造下一代太陽能電池，這些材料可以實現低成本和高效的太陽能光伏轉換。尤其是在我們的工作中，三維半導體納米柱陣列被發現有光學陷阱效應，可以實現高效的光吸收。納米柱陣列的這一特點可以被用來提供太陽能電池的轉換效率，從而實現對平面太陽能電池的超越。另外，三維半導體納米結構既可以被製作在剛性基板上，也可以被做在柔性基底上，其製作工藝具有低成本和可擴展性，所以適合于製造高效費比的太陽能電池。在這項提案中，我們提議繼續研發和改進三維納米柱陣列的設計和性能，以用於有效的光吸收和太陽能光伏器件。其中比較重要的是我們將利用理論模擬結合實驗的手段，具體研究納米柱的幾何尺寸對它們的光學吸收和太陽能電池性能有何影響。這個研究將有助於找到三維納米柱陣列的最佳設計方法。最終我們希望這項研究可以有助於將來開發剛性和柔性基底上的實用的納米結構的太陽能電池，這些電池既可用於併網發電，亦可用於便攜的電子器件。

612111.label: Realisation of objectives
612111.value: The objectives have been accomplished. We have developed a low cost process to fabricate 3-D nano/micro-pillar arrays. This process involves roll-to-roll nanoimprint and electrochemical anodization of aluminum. We have performed systematic investigations on the fabricated nanostructures using experimental and simulation tools. Understanding of how photon interacts with the structures was achieved. And we have successfully fabricated solar cell devices on these nanostructures. The devices demonstrated improved energy conversion efficiency as compared to the planar counterparts. All these results have been published on the top journals in the field.

612111.label: Major findings and research outcome
612111.value: Our major findings can be summarized as: 1. Photonic nanostructures can be fabricated in large scale with extremely low cost. In the past, photonic nanostructures have been fabricated mainly with lithographic methods, which are expensive with low throughput. In this project, we discovered that nanoimprint can be performed with a roll-to-roll fashion low cost materials such as aluminum, followed by solution processes including anodization and wet etch. The process has high throughput, and highly regular nanostructures, such as nanopillars, nanocones, can be achieved in large and practical scale. 2. Light structure interaction. We discovered that, in general, high aspect ratio nanostructures are able to capture more light, due to more internal scattering. Meanwhile, the periodicity of the nanostructures is also very important. Interesting, we discovered that when the periodicity matches the input photon wavelength, the optimal light absorption efficiency can be achieved. 3. Optimal device structure. Although in #2 we discovered that high aspect ratio nanostructures are able to capture more light, the performance of a solar cell also largely depends on charge carrier collection efficiency. We have found that it is challenging to achieve uniform active layer deposition on high aspect ratio nanostructures, and this uniformity affects carrier collection efficiency. Eventually, there is an optimal nanostructure design leading to the highest device energy conversion efficiency. In our work, we revealed that when the aspect ratio of nanostructure is 50% of their periodicity, an optimal device performance is expected. This is the first systematic study on the nanostructure device optimization in the field.

612111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
612111.value: This project has cast a solid ground for developing more practical high performance thin film photovoltaics. There are a few aspects worth more investigations and development in the future: 1. Process scale-up. We have demonstrated feasibility of roll-to-roll nanofabrication in a relatively small scale from industrial standpoint. Much larger scale fabrication should be demonstrated in the future, based on the process developed in this project. 2. Expansion on materials. In this project, we primarily worked on Si thin film material, due to budget constraint. In the future, other thin film materials, such as CIGS, and the emerging organometallic perovskite materials, should be explored. And for the new material systems, the device design rule might need to be re-investigated.

612111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
612111.value: Solar energy is a clean and renewable energy source. Solar cells can convert sunlight to electricity thus they can be used to build solar power station or power up our portable electronic devices. The nature of this project is to explore the applications of nanostructures for high performance solar cell devices. We investigated how to fabricate nanostructures with low cost and high throughput method, how the structural design will affect device light harvesting capability and sunlight to electricity energy conversion efficiency. Eventually we achieved device design guidelines which can help to fabricate devices with the optimal efficiency. The knowledge acquired from this project will certainly benefit solar photovoltiac industry, and eventually contribute to sustainable development of our society.

612211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
612211.value: 在現今國際化的娛樂、學術、商業社會中，混合語言現象越來越普遍發生。我們提出一個新的針對自然發生的混合語言語音的聲學和語言學建模方法，目的是建立一個非特定人混合語言語音辨識系統。這樣的一個系統可以識別嵌入有外來語言的語音，同時不影響母語語音辨識性能。 混合語言是說話人產生的一種異質的語言形態，說話人或者借用外來語言詞彙，在一句話中間從一種語言轉換到另一種語言（稱為：句內編碼混合）或者在句末從一種語言轉換到另一種語言（稱為：句間編碼切換）。先前混合語言語音辨識的研究主要集中在特定人說話系統，或者語音中少於2%的外來詞語的，或者具有語法約束的短語識別方面。在現實中，作為例子，我們發現有中文的會議語音中可以記錄到具有20%的英語詞彙的流暢的語音。目前還未有針對此類情況的非特定說話人語音辨識系統。 我們計畫收集和分析自然發音的並且包含混合語言的大規模資料庫，這些混合語言包含不同層面的雙語現象。我們將對基於統計模型的非特定說話人連續語音辨識系統的兩個核心部分提出兩種新的方法：（1）非對稱雙語言聲學建模，它使得系統能同時處理混合語言和嵌入式的語言，並同時提高兩種語言語音的識別率。我們將設計一種新的結合音子影射的聲學模型重構方法，它能從少量嵌入式語音的資料庫中，自動獲取並近似得到語言層面的混合資訊；（2）統計的基於特徵的語言模型和結構化的語言模型，將編碼轉換的概率結合到傳統形式的N元語法模型上。我們將通過統計詞法分析、句法分析和語義分析，從混合語言語音資料中自動獲取結構特徵和句內編碼轉換的約束。 混合語言是一類兩種不同語言發生內在聯繫的典型的現象。考慮到香港曾經是殖民地以及對中國傳統的傳承，它擁有大量的雙語說話者，他們在大量的各種不同的場合中使用混合語言來交流。同時，中文/英文的混合語言語音在大中華區的專業人士當中普遍被使用，也包括很多海外中國人。因此，中文娛樂節目中通常混合有英文詞。互聯網聊天室的討論以及博客等也是包含了很多非母語的詞彙。在美國，50%的兒童生長在多語言的家庭。在北非，課程教育中常常混有法語，而他們的日常對話使用母語阿拉伯語。我們計畫的研究將是第一個同時涉及聲學和語言學的混合語言語音辨識系統。

612211.label: Realisation of objectives
612211.value: 1. We designed and implement an asymmetric pronunciation and acoustic modeling for mixed language recognition. We first implemented a phone set extension method for pronunciation modeling of the mixed language using a hybrid of phonetic knowledge and data-driven statistics. To refine the pronunciation model, the acoustic model was reconstructed by state-tying. 2. Three previous approaches were implemented and compared: 1) Baseline Monolingual System 2) Phone mapping and phone set extension 3) Non-native adaptation 3. We implemented a language model using POS tags, n-grams, and semantic features. This language model provided insignificant improvement on the baseline language model. 4. We proposed a structural code switching language model using the WFST framework, the details are given in "Section 2. Code Switch Language Modeling in a WFST Framework" in the EMNLP-2014 paper "Language Modeling with Functional Head Constraint for Code Switching Speech Recognition". 5. We investigated and incorporated the Functional Head Constraint into code switching language modeling in a WFST framework. The details are given in "Section 3. Functional Head Constraint" in the EMNLP-2014 paper. 6. The baseline ASR system is systematically improved by both the asymmetric acoustic model (ICASSP-2013 paper) and the structured language model (EMNLP-2014 paper) The system was tested on a lecture speech dataset with 16% embedded second language, and on a lunch conversation dataset with 20% embedded second language. Our language models with lattice parsing and partial parsing can reduce word error rates from a baseline mixed language model by 3.72% to 3.89% in the first task, and by 5.85% to 5.97% in the second task. They are reduced from an interpolated language model by 3.69% to 3.74%, and by 5.46% to 5.77% in the first and second task respectively. WER reductions from an adapted language model are from 2.51% to 2.63%, and from 4.47% to 4.74% in the two tasks. The F-measure for code switch point detection is improved from the interpolated model's 6.25% to our model's 9.38%, and from the adapted model's 1.49% to our method's 4.48%. Our proposed approach avoids the need to make early decisions on code-switch boundaries and is therefore more robust. Our approach also avoids the bottleneck of code switch data scarcity by using bilingual data with syntactic structure. Moreover, our method reduces word error rates for both the matrix and the embedded language.

612211.label: Major findings and research outcome
612211.value: * Improved the language model with tree-based translation constraints * Designed and implemented the proposed structural language modeling by partial parsing. * A workshop on mixed language modeling was co-chaired by Prof Fung at EMNLP 2014. Many other researchers have entered the area.

612211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
612211.value: The research outcome has been discussed with researchers at Columbia University, University of Texas, Google, Microsoft Research, etc. Prof Fung has joined a planning workshop sponsored by the National Science Foundation of the US government to organize more follow up research activities and shared tasks for other researchers to participate. We are planning on working with industry partners to use the results in products for the financial industry.

612211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
612211.value: This project makes two major contributions. First, it empirically demonstrates and verifies the linguistic constraints of code-switching, previously thought of as a theory by linguists, for the first time. Secondly, we have developed the first ever computational model of structured language model for code-switching speech recognition and incorporated it into a run-time speech recognition system, enabling improved performance in recognition of mixed language speech. Our work on code-switch speech recognition led to other approaches to tackle the same problem and a workshop on shared tasks. We are among the pioneers in this new research field.

612511.label: Project Objectives
612511.value: Acquire and adapt a three-dimensional turbulence model for waves to the case of waterhammer flows. Verify the model using published data as well as data obtained from colleagues in New Zealand (see appended letter of support). Use the model to examine the interaction between an incident waterhammer wave and the turbulence at a defect along a pipe. Critical questions to be answered are: how does the wave alter the turbulence at the defect as well as the dissipation associated with it? What is the range of validity of the quadratic energy loss at a defect under unsteady conditions? How does the eddy structure at the defect scatter transient waves? What is the flow behavior at the defect during the phase when the flow reverses (i.e., when the flow direction is opposite to that of the original steady flow)?

612511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
612511.value: Defects develop with age in pressurized conduits, such as water supply lines and pumped drainage systems. Partially blocked valves, changes in pipe wall thicknesses due to bio-film build up, corrosion and material spalding and deposition are frequent causes. Such defects lead to significantly higher pumping costs due to increased skin and form drag and to potential deterioration in the quality of the liquid being transported. Transient-based defect detection methods are economical, long range and efficient. An essential ingredient for the success of such methods is the understanding of the interaction between the transient wave and the turbulence generated by the defect. Pressure wave laboratory experiments show that defect-wave interaction is complicated and presently not understood. The aim of the proposed research is to understand the interaction between a transient wave and the strong turbulence generated by flow separation at a defect. A large eddy three-dimensional turbulence waterhammer model will be constructed, verified and used to examine wave-turbulent interaction in a pipe with a localized defect. Detailed investigation of how an incident wave is scattered by a defect and how the turbulence at a defect interacts with a wave will be conducted over a wide range of flow parameters. The understanding gained will explain the complicated flow behavior observed in laboratory experiments and will be instrumental for developing reliable transient-based defect detection methods. 壓力管道中的缺陷會隨著時間發展。在供水管線或加壓排水系統中，形成管道缺陷的常見原因有管線中存在的非全開而引起阻塞的閥門和由於生物膜作用、腐蝕、材料變形以及沉積引起的管壁厚度變化等。這些缺陷將會增加管道沿線的管壁摩擦阻力因而會很大程度上增加泵站加壓費用。而且，這些缺陷導致的化學作用也會使得管道中傳輸的水質惡化。基於非恒定流的管道缺陷檢測是既經濟又大範圍高效率的方法。這些檢測方法將會成功的一個必要因素就是需要充分地理解非恒定壓力波和管道缺陷引起的渦流之間的相互作用。有關壓力波的實驗室實驗表明，壓力波與管道缺陷之間相互作用是非常複雜的現象並且至今還沒有被理解。 本提案研究的目標是爲了更好地理解非穩定壓力波與管道缺陷引起的強烈渦流甚至是管流分離現象之間的相互作用。本研究將建立一個以三維大渦渦流為基礎的水錘模型並將通過相關實驗數據證實。而被證實的三維模型將用於對壓力管道中的波與缺陷相互作用的詳細研究。例如，本研究將詳細研究入射波怎樣被潛在的管道缺陷散射，以及在不同流體參數條件下渦流與壓力波之間的相互作用。而後，從這些具體研究中得到的結論將用來解釋實驗室實驗中觀測到的複雜流體流動行為。同時，這些結果對於將來發展更加可靠的基於非恒定流管道缺陷檢測方法有至關重要的作用。

612511.label: Realisation of objectives
612511.value: The three objectives of this research are well met. A three-dimensional turbulence model for waves to has been acquired and applied. The model is the ADINA software and is used to solve the slightly compressible turbulent flow problem with complex geometry. A k-epsilon model is used. Computational results are validated by several examples. In practice, the water hammer wave generated by rapid valve closure usually exhibits wave front smearing. The numerical analysis shows that for a blockage length smaller than the wave front thickness, the magnitude of the incident wave may become severely reduced from interaction between the blockage and the wave front. By reflecting negative pressure waves toward the incident wave before its maximum pressure arrives at the blockage, the maximum transient pressure may be significantly reduced. Consequently, the blockage behaves as a discrete blockage. However, if the blockage length is large compared with the thickness of the wave front, the incident wave conserves its initial amplitude, and the blockage is behaves as an extended blockage. Therefore, the classification of discrete and extended blockage depends on the thickness of the wave front and thus on the rapidity of the maneuver that generates the transient. In order to study the interaction over a wide range of frequencies a high order finite volume numerical scheme is developed and applied to axi-symmetric waves in water-filled pipe. The results show that once the injected frequency exceeds the theoretical cut-off frequency, wave dispersion becomes significant and the group velocity, at which energy propagates, becomes very low. Therefore, the wave energy exhibits significant spatial spread and thus significant reduction in amplitude the further away one is measuring from the source. In addition, it is found that the size of the wave source has significant influence on the energy distribution over the different excited modes. The study gives some initial conclusions on the different aspect that practitioners must take into account if high frequency waves are to be used for TBDDM. A finite volume Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook Boltzmann scheme (i.e., BGK scheme) and the Kinetic Flux Vector Split-ting scheme (i.e., KFVS scheme) are formulated and applied for waterhammer problems. Both the KFVS and BGK schemes provide the time-dependent mass and momentum fluxes at the cell interfaces. The mesoscopic-based FV formulation guarantees the mass and momentum are conserved while the conservation of energy is automatically guaranteed. The KFVS and BGK scheme correctly captures discontinuity fronts in a classical reservoir-pipe system. The collision time in BGK scheme is modified in order to produce an oscillation-free solution. The reservoir and valve condition is numerically treated using ghost cell technique. The stability of the proposed schemes are satisfied when Cr < 0:5. The computations are carried out for various Courant numbers and grid numbers and the energy norm is used to evaluate the numerical accuracy of the schemes. The comparison between the efficiency of the conventional scheme (i.e., the Fix-MOC and Godunov schemes) and those of the mesoscopic-based schemes (i.e., the KFVS and BGK schemes) reveals that none of the proposed schemes is better than the 2nd-order Godunov scheme for classical waterhammer. Nevertheless, it is found that the CPU time needed by the 2nd-order BGK scheme to achieve a pre-defined degree of accuracy is not too far from that by the 2nd-order Godunov scheme. The KFVS scheme is more dissipative than the BGK scheme due to lack of particle collisions in the formulation. Carefully measured field data in Italy for the initial (i.e., pretransient) Reynolds number, R0, that ranges from 97,000 to 380,000 has been used to advance our knowledge of wave-turbulence interaction and new model was developed. This new model is used to formulate general, encompassing and theoretically-based dimensionless parameters to assess the importance of unsteady friction in comparison to the quasi-steady component. In addition, the new model analytical solution furnishes the similitude relations that allowed the damping behavior from existing laboratory tests, the field tests conducted as part of this research, and the weighting function-based (WFB) models to be investigated and compared in a coherent manner in a single graph. The analysis confirms that the magnitude of R0 has a significant impact on the damping for transients generated by flow stoppage. In addition, the results show that convolutional unsteady friction model that uses the frozen eddy viscosity hypothesis and R0 has accuracy that decreases with time. An improvement for this shortcoming is proposed and verified and involves the use of the instantaneous Reynolds number in lieu of the pre-transient Reynolds number in the evaluation of the WFB models. The result is a modified unsteady friction model that provides improved matches for both laboratory and field data compared with the original model. The wave-blockage interaction is studied in detail in this research. The impact of six different extended blockages under a range of different Reynolds numbers on the frequency response is used to confirm the theoretical behavior of an extended blockage. These experimental tests are conducted in the pipeline hydraulic laboratory at the University of Canterbury, New Zealand. An analytical simplification of the original SFR-based method is used to identify the key blockage parameters governing the frequency shifts and shows that the magnitude of the frequency shift increases with severity of blockages and is related to the changes in characteristic impedance and wave propagation coefficient of pipeline (pipe diameter, thickness, and/or wavespeed) imposed by the blockage. The experiments show that the length and location of potential extended blockages in the pipeline can be accurately predicted by the proposed method. Significant error exists, however, in the prediction of the pipe constriction diameter and is a result of the nonlinear operations in the experiments such as full valve closure in this study and the inability of existing models for perfectly replicating transient events in pipes with severe constrictions. Two previously developed techniques—pressure signal analysis (PSA) and frequency response analysis (FRA)—are experimentally tested in this study on systems of different pipe material and characteristics. Each method is validated using the experimental data, and the results show that PSA is most accurate for locating the blockage while FRA is most accurate for determining the radial constriction and length of the blockage section. To take advantage of the different strengths of the techniques, a coupling of the two methods is proposed. Experimental application results reveal that both detection accuracy and calculation efficiency are improved when the coupled method is used instead of the original techniques applied individually. Moreover, the results indicate that current TTBTs for partial blockage detection are more reliable in elastic (metallic) pipelines compared to viscoelastic (plastic) pipes. Laboratory and field data revealed that the frozen turbulence hypothesis works very well in waterhammer. This is because the wave time scale is much shorter than the turbulence time scale. As a result, no LES modeling was required and a k-epsilon model was found to be sufficient.

612511.label: Major findings and research outcome
612511.value: A range of multi-dimensional turbulence model for waterhammer waves have been developed and verified using data from New Zealand and Italy (Journal Papers 1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9). In addition, the models are used to examine the interaction between an incident waterhammer wave and defects along a pipe and the processes of frequency shift, Bragg resonance and local turbulence are analyzed (Journal Papers 1,2,3,4,5,6,9 and conference paper 1).

612511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
612511.value: The work focused on the blockage as a defect since blockages are ubiquitous in water supply systems and result in wastage of energy and financial resources, reduction in carrying capacity, and increased potential for contamination. This research investigates the physics of wave-blockage interaction in WSS by analytical, numerical and experimental means. Future work should consider leakage since this is another prominent problem in water supply systems.

612511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
612511.value: Defects develop with age in pressurized conduits, such as water supply lines and pumped drainage systems. Partially blocked valves, changes in pipe wall thicknesses due to biofilm build up, corrosion and material spalding and deposition are frequent causes. The aim of this research is to develop a new level of fundamental understanding of the effects of defects on transients in pressurized pipeline systems—an essential ingredient for making transient-based detection methods practical. To this end, a range of multi-dimensional turbulence model for waterhammer waves has been developed and verified using data from New Zealand and Italy. In addition, the models have been used to examine the interaction between an incident waterhammer wave and defects along a pipe. Processes of frequency shift, Bragg resonance and local turbulence are been analyzed. The understanding gained explains the complicated flow behavior observed in laboratory experiments and will be instrumental for developing reliable transient-based defect detection methods.
