612711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
612711.value: Development of new and innovative human-product interfaces will be of paramount importance as Hong Kong and Southern China emerge as centres for the design and manufacture of new footwear. In support of this goal, the proposed project will evaluate load bearing strategies that can reduce foot related pain and discomfort and advance the design process leading to safer and more efficient sports, fashion, leisure and military footwear products that will appeal to discriminating consumers worldwide Loads acting on the human body can be distributed ‘uniformly’ or concentrated in a way where the “stronger” parts of the body assume the majority of loading in order to minimize injury. Applying principles of structural mechanics would suggest that a distributed loading approach is most appropriate for homogeneous structures. However, such a distribution may not be ideal for biological structures since spatial summation, which is the ability of tissue to integrate nociceptor input from large areas, would cause a higher level of unwanted response resulting in subsequent pain or discomfort. Although there is a significant body of published research related to pressure pain mechanisms, there is only a limited understanding of the pressure distribution patterns required for ‘comfort’. The sensations of discomfort and pain are primarily determined by the magnitude of the load imposed on the tissue, by the area or geometry over which the load is being distributed, by the distribution of the load among differing loading sites, and by the spacing among the loading sites. Three experiments are proposed to evaluate the effect of these variables. The first experiment is designed to determine whether the contact area or the circumference of the loading stimulus determines the threshold of pain. This will be done using inter-spaced concentric cylindrical probes and solid probes, to produce controlled pressure conditions on the tissues of the foot. The second experiment will evaluate the separation effects of two–point loading conditions in relation to sensations of discomfort and pain. The third experiment will identify the load distribution effects using a multi-point loading configuration. The results of the three experiments will contribute to a better understanding of pressure related perception of pain and discomfort allowing the design and development of new footwear products in the future. 由於香港及南中國正發展成為設計和製造新款鞋類的中心,因此開發嶄新和富有創意的人類產品界面是非常重要的一環。為支持這個目標，建議項目將評估怎樣的承重策略能減少疼痛和不適;從而促進鞋類的設計過程, 以使鞋類產品(包括運動鞋, 時尚鞋,休閒鞋和軍用鞋類)更安全和更有效,以吸引全球各有不同特徵的消費者。 人體載荷可“均勻地”分佈或集中負荷在身體“較強”的部分以盡量減少傷害。運用結構力學的原理,在同樣的結構上,分散負荷是最恰當的方法。但是，由於空間總和,這樣分佈在生物結構上可能不是最理想的。這是由於人體的組織有能力合併大面積傷害感受器的輸入，因而導致更嚴重的疼痛或不適。雖然有很多研究發表有關壓力疼痛的機制,但壓力分佈模式對”舒適”需求的了解仍然有限。不適和疼痛的感覺主要取決於幾種因素,包括在人體的組織上所施加的負荷程度、負荷分佈的面積或幾何學、負荷分佈在不同的負荷點、以及負荷點之間的間距。 這項目建議通過三個實驗來評估這些因素的影響。 第一個實驗的目的是確定是否接觸面積或載荷刺激的周長決定了疼痛閾值。這項研究將採用空心同軸圓柱探頭和實心探頭來控制壓力產生在腳部的組織上。第二個實驗是在兩點載荷的程況下,評估別分兩點不適和疼痛的感覺。第三個實驗將採用多點載荷配置來確定負荷分佈的影響。三個實驗的結果將有助於對壓力相關的疼痛感知和不適有更好的理解,從而在未來能夠設計和開發新的鞋類產品。

612711.label: Realisation of objectives
612711.value: The project objectives were primarily related to pain and discomfort. Based on previous research, it seemed that discomfort and pain can be minimized through pressure distribution and lowering pressure magnitude over human tissue. It has been claimed that pain is generally preceded by discomfort. If this statement is true, then distributing force, thereby distributing pressure or reducing pressure at a particular location should result in a reduced level of discomfort. But the question that remained was whether the pain and discomfort experienced by every part is the same, and the corresponding relationship of that pain with the independent variables of area and speed of indentation. The revised objectives were to: 1. Investigate the effect of distributed loading patterns on pressure sensation of the plantar foot using concentric probes. 2. Investigate the effect of probe separation on pressure perception on the plantar foot. These objectives were achieved beyond what was stated. In fact, we achieved all the objectives stated in our original application. The process of achieving the objectives was quite complex. Many jigs had to be developed to conduct the various studies. One of them was a jig with four probes such that the four probes move the same distance. Probes of any size can be mounted. A maximum of 25 mm displacement can be achieved to allow a 50 mm center to center distance between two probes. The two-probe apparatus was used mainly to get different unequal load setting between two probes. In order to achieve different unequal loadings, springs with different stiffness were used. The Automatic Tissue Tester (ATT) that we designed and developed for this purpose was used in all experiments. This is a very specialized device that was built to replace the many hand-held pressure algometers that have little or no control. The ATT allows any body part to be stimulated at a controlled speed, at any angle with one or many indentors. Most shoe-related products attempt to distribute the load uniformly without much consideration to the bony and soft tissue regions. In other words, the assumption is that the pain thresholds are the same throughout the surface of the foot. An experiment was conducted (Rodrigo et al., 2013) to first determine the pressure pain threshold (PPT) and tissue deformation on the plantar surface of the foot. Three sizes of probes were used to stimulate the foot at three different speeds. The results showed that tissue stiffness is quite low for small deformations, but significantly higher at large deformations. The stiffness at the larger deformation region was positively correlated with PPT. The data were further used to develop a mathematical model for the stiffness in the differing regions and a hypothetical model for PPT. The study by Xiong et al. (2013) titled, “A model for the perception of surface pressure on human foot” was published in Applied Ergonomics in 2013 to validate the hypothetical model reported in Rodrigo et al. (2013). This study investigated the psychophysical relationship between the magnitude of pressure and the indentor area and indenting speed at thirteen locations of twenty healthy subjects’ feet. Thereafter, the pressure pain thresholds (PPT) on area, A, and speed, v, were mathematically modeled in a power form, The exponents were less than 1.0 and consistent across the 13 test locations with a mean of 0.82 and a range from 0.67 to 0.98. Given the existence of distinct patterns, we wanted to generate a methodology to achieve reliable and consistent results. One of the biggest issues is to be able to identify the same location on different feet. Even though researchers have proposed various axis systems, any particular point cannot be reliable identified. Hence, we generated a grid system that allows consistent point identification across subjects. Then the Pressure Discomfort Threshold (PDT) and PPT was evaluated at 95 points. Cluster analysis showed the existence of five distinct regions. This paper has been submitted to the Journal of Ergonomics and is awaiting review (Weerasinghe et al., 2016). A summary of the outcome of these experiments have been published as a chapter in the book “Science of Footwear”, titled, “Foot Characteristics and Related Empirical Models” (Xiong et al., 2012). Most articles on such a topic relates to issues such as anthropometry. But, ours was quite different as our emphasis was on a more important aspect of loading, structural deformation and sensation. An initial attempt was made to develop the footbed of high heel shoes and these results were presented at a conference (Weerasinghe and Goonetilleke, 2012) The other experiments involved concentric probes to evaluate if a space between loading will affect the PPT. Probes with curved edges were fabricated so that addition of metal sleeves allowed the contact are and the space between the contact area to be controlled. The results showed that the space or the inner radius had no significant effect on PDT or PPT. Instead, the effects were solely dependent on indentation velocity and contact area. The effect of probe area was consistent with neurotransmission findings such as local integration and neuron recruitment, where the increase in the stimulus area may integrate stimuli input within the receptive fields and increase the total number of nociceptive neuron activation, resulting in a decrease of pain thresholds. The lack of any effect of the space between concentric probes may be attributed a lack of nociceptor activation in those areas. These results led to our next experiment to investigate the effect of two-point adjustable probes on PDT and PPT. Different combinations of probe area and probe separation were tested in this experiment at two different speeds. The probe separation was less than 21mm, and there was no significant difference in the various separations that were tested. This was somewhat unexpected even though for heat stimuli a probe separation greater than 100mm has been reported to see differences in PPT. The last experiment evaluated pressure perception with unequal loading from two indentors to find out if uneven distribution of forces results in higher pressure thresholds as the most intuitive way to distribute is to make the loading evenly distributed. Three different levels of loading were tested between the two indentors by adding springs of different stiffness. Interestingly, when the spring stiffness was highest, the PPT was the highest as well. The differences among the two probes can significantly alter the PPT. This has significant impact on product design. It means that interspacing material of hard and soft materials can create higher PPT. the optimal level was found when the load between the two probes was one-third and two-thirds. This is a very important finding that has practical implications when developing insoles or midsoles in footwear. The related paper is currently in its final stages for journal submission.

612711.label: Major findings and research outcome
612711.value: A methodology was developed to reliably test the pain and discomfort thresholds on the foot (Rodrigo et al., 2013). This methodology may be used on any body part. It is known that discomfort precedes pain, and hence discomfort thresholds tend to lower than the pain thresholds. By measuring the discomfort and pain thresholds we were able to find that the discomfort thresholds are around 40-60% of the pain thresholds depending on the location. This is a very important result for designing footwear and footwear accessories especially since the pressures can be quite easily determined using commercial sensor systems. We also evaluated the relationship of these thresholds with the speed of loading and the area of the indentation. A mathematical model was developed as well (Xiong et al., 2013). This model has strong implications on how force should be distributed on the surface of the body. The common myth of distributing the forces may not be the optimal according to our results. But, knowing what we know now allows us to come up with differing designs to achieve an optimal footbed through proper material selection and varying area of contact depending on the load imposed. An issue that arose from these experiments was the issue of how to generalize our results for various populations and sizes of feet. Using the bony structure of the feet, a local coordinate system was developed that can consistently map the various locations among people. This system was tested and the results were very good (Weerasinghe et al., 2016). It is always worthwhile to bring all related material so that readers have a good idea of the similarities and differences of the various results and their implications. This was done through a book chapter in the, Science of footwear titled, “Foot Characteristics and Related Empirical Models” (Xiong et al., 2012). In that chapter most of our findings were captured and presented in a coherent manner, and an explanation of our results were provided using the known properties of mechanoreceptors, spinal cord fibers and the gate theory of pain. Overall, we did many exhaustive experiments and published our results in some of the top journals in Ergonomics, presented at one conference and published a summary article in a related book.

612711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
612711.value: All experiments except one were primarily performed with Chinese participants. There is a need to check the external validity with other populations. Also, the tests were done with the participant standing erect with equal load on both feet. When walking or running the various areas of the foot get loaded at different times. Hence, there is a possibility that the results may be different under some of those conditions. A system or equipment needs to be developed that will allow the pressure thresholds to be determined during activity as the time of loading will be short. The experiments mentioned above should also be performed with multiple probes to determine the ideal load distribution given what we know from two-point indentors. Lastly, the mapping of the results to footbeds should be determined to design the optimal footbed.

612711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
612711.value: Clinicians and orthotics strongly believe in distributing the load on the foot by increasing contact area. That is minimizing pain or discomfort by distributing the load and lowering pressure magnitude over human tissue by using softer material. This results in a sub-optimal system with similar intensity of forces everywhere even though the underlying structure of bony and soft tissue is different in every region. We found that differing parts of the feet have differing thresholds of discomfort and pain. These thresholds depend on the area that is subjected to the load and the speed at which the load is applied. Regions with higher pressure pain thresholds can bear higher loads than regions with lower pressure pain thresholds. In other words, materials with various stiffness can be used in differing configurations and their perception would be markedly different. In order to determine the ideal footbed, the pain and discomfort threshold maps should be used to generate an optimal configuration. Manipulating the stiffness of the material will allow a positive sensation of similar magnitude throughout the contact area of the foot. Thus, the result of the various experiments can be used to develop new footbeds or insoles of shoes.

613011.label: Project Title(Chinese)
613011.value: 基于高斯过程的随机搜索算法

613011.label: Project Objectives
613011.value: We will develop a framework of random search algorithms that use kriging metamodels (or Gaussian process models) to guide the search process and to automatically balance the exploitation and exploration tradeoff. We will show that algorithms conforming to this framework converge to the globally optimal solution when the simulation effort goes to infinity for DOvS problems. Typically stochastic kriging techniques focus on fitting a surface that minimizes the integrated mean square error (IMSE). Therefore, these algorithms are typically computationally slow when the number of solutions is large and numerically unstable when there are solutions clustered together. In OvS, however, the number of solutions increases quickly and the solutions tend to cluster around good solutions. Furthermore, a kriging surface needs to be fitted every iteration. Therefore, we need a stochastic kriging technique that is computationally fast and numerically stable, which may or may not minimize the IMSE. In this research, we will develop a stochastic kriging technique specific for optimization. The kriging metamodel will allow us to conceptually construct a sampling distribution for random search process and to balance the exploitation and exploration tradeoff. However, how to actually derive this distribution and how to efficiently sample this distribution are critical issues for algorithm design and implementation. In this research, we will also work on these issues and develop efficient sampling schemes that allow us to quickly sample from the sampling distribution. We will also compare our algorithm with other existing random search algorithms and give guidelines on how to select among these algorithms.

613011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
613011.value: Simulation is one of the most widely used management tools in practice. When it is used, the goal is often to find the best combination of parameters that optimizes system performance. This is what we call optimization via simulation (OvS). In the proposed research, we consider OvS problems with integer-ordered decision variables, which is known as discrete OvS or DOvS. There are many applications of DOvS problems in practice. For instance, many logistics problems, including terminal designs and vehicle assignments that are common for many Hong Kong logistics companies, can be modeled as DOvS problems. DOvS problems are generally difficult to solve because the objective function is embedded in a stochastic simulation model with no closed-form expressions, and it can only be estimated through running often time-consuming experiments whose outcomes typically include noise. Globally convergent random search algorithms, which search the feasible region for better solutions, are often used to solve DOvS problems. For these algorithms, a critical issue is how to balance the search effort spent in the neighborhood of current best solution and in largely unvisited regions. This is known as the exploitation and exploration (E&E) tradeoff. Although the existing algorithms have taken this issue into consideration, their ways of handlings this tradeoff are typically artificial and cannot entirely match our intuition. In this research, we propose to use the concepts of Gaussian process and stochastic kriging to balance the E&E tradeoff. In each iteration of the random search algorithm, we will apply stochastic kriging techniques to build a global response surface that is represented by a conditional Gaussian process, and use the Gaussian process to develop a sampling distribution for the random search algorithm that balances the E&E tradeoff. There are a few critical research issues in this approach. First, how to build a global response surface efficiently and effectively. Second, how to develop a sampling distribution that can be derived and can be sampled. Third, how to ensure the global convergence of the random search algorithm. In the proposed research, we will work on these important research issues, compare the performance of our algorithm to the performances of other existing algorithms, and provide more insights on how to solve DOvS problems efficiently. The successful completion of this project will represent a substantial advance over the state of the art in both theory and practice of DOvS. 计算机仿真是管理中的一项十分常用的数量化分析工具。它常常被用来解决优化问题。这就是所谓的仿真优化问题。在本项目中，我们着重解决离散仿真优化问题，即优化问题的变量只可以取整数值。因为优化问题的目标函数是隐含在计算机仿真模型之中的，这类问题总的来说很难解决。 在本项目中，我们将采用随机搜索算法来解决离散仿真优化问题。我们的着眼点在于如何设计出一个很好的搜索分布，让搜索过程更有效率。为了解决此问题，我们计划采用地理统计学中的高斯过程，使用此过程来设计出更加有效的搜索分布，并将相关算法应用到物流管理中的实际问题上。

613011.label: Major findings and research outcome
613011.value: We designed stochastic kriging based random search algorithms to solve discrete optimization via simulation problems. We showed that the sampling distribution used in the algorithm can balance exploration and exploitation effort well. Furthermore, we developed fast kriging method that avoids numerical stability issues that commonly exist in current stochastic kriging method, and our method works very well in optimization via simulation contexts. We also compared our algorithms with other available algorithms in the literature and we found that our algorithms have good overall performance and are competitive.

613011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
613011.value: We also discovered that the stationarity assumption of the stochastic kriging model is often violated, especially for queueing simulations where extreme nonlinear behaviors often exist. For these problems, stochastic kriging methods in general suffer from an overly estimated variance constants, leading to over exploration in random search algorithms. In the future, we will study how to combine simple stylised queueing models into stochastic kriging framework and see how they may be able to improve the fitting of the surface and the optimization of queueing problems.

613011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
613011.value: Simulation models often built by analysts to optimize system performances. However, these simulation models are in general quite difficult to optimize because building the performance surface is often very time consuming and often impossible. Therefore, to find optimal system designs, one has to use optimization via simulation algorithms that are typically based on smart random search ideas. In this project we have successfully designed algorithms based on the concepts of stochastic kriging that is capable of allocating simulation effort intelligently to find efficiently the optimal system designs.

613111.label: Project Objectives
613111.value: To have listeners discriminate between the original and piecewise-linear approximated tones in formal listening tests, and to analyze the resulting discrimination data. To have listeners judge dissimilarity in formal listening tests by asking them to judge distances between original and data-reduced sounds (e.g., on a scale of 0-10). To analyze the above listening test data to determine: - the thresholds of distinguishability for instruments when the tone has been data-reduced - why some instruments are more distinguishable than others - whether distinguishability is due to spectral shape or spectral variations - which instruments are confused more often when the details of their amplitude envelopes are simplified - the shape of the timbre space around A particular instrument when less data are used in additive synthesis - which instruments retain their identity better when fewer breakpoints are used for piecewise-linear approximation. To correlate the discrimination results with spectral incoherence, normalized centroid deviation, and spectral irregularity to determine whether these different measures of spectral variation are significantly related. To deepen our understanding of musical timbre as a result of the above analysis, potentially leading to new understandings of music perception and data reduction in sound synthesis.

613111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
613111.value: Additive synthesis is a classic sound synthesis method, and one of the most general. It can realistically synthesize virtually any quasi-harmonic musical instrument tone. However, its main drawback is that it uses a large number of parameters in the form of amplitude and frequency envelopes. For a typical musical tone, it may require 30-200 oscillators, which is not a problem for current CPUs, but it is a difficult control problem. Even experienced users find it difficult to manipulate such a large number of parameters in a meaningful way, where large changes to these parameters may not even make an audible difference. One of the simplest and most intuitive ways to reduce the number of additive synthesis parameters is piecewise-linear approximation (PLA) of the amplitude envelopes. The critical aspect of PLA is selecting amplitude envelope breakpoints such that the perceptible difference of the approximated tone is minimal. Various questions then arise: How many breakpoints are required to make the approximation indistinguishable from the original? Given the same number of breakpoints, are some instruments more discriminable than others? If so, what makes them more distinguishable? These are the questions we want to answer in the proposed study. A number of previous studies have evaluated various breakpoint selection methods. Both simple and more complex optimization-based methods were evaluated. However, only a few instruments were tested in these studies, and the evaluations were not perceptually-based. The proposed study will perceptually evaluate PLA synthesized tones using listening tests on a larger pool of instruments. The proposed research aims at enlarging knowledge about the perception of musical sounds by systematically evaluating how well listeners can discriminate PLA synthesized tones. We know that musical instruments are recognizable even when the sound has been substantially altered by a spectrum equalizer or room acoustics. Here, we will determine how detection of PLA synthesized tones varies with the number of breakpoints and instrument. Therefore, the proposal is basic research on human perception of musical tones. Analysis of the listening test results will deepen our understanding of musical timbre, which is not well-understood, by quantifying what listeners are hearing when they distinguish between similar data-reduced sounds. This will also potentially lead to new understandings of music perception and data-reduction in sound synthesis. 添加合成是其中一種最普遍及典型的聲音合成方法。然而，它的主要缺點是在波幅和頻率函數之中，它使用了大量的參數。對於一個典型的樂器聲音，添加合成可能需要30-200振盪器。對當前的中央處理器(CPU)，這不是一個問題，但是這是一個很嚴重的控制問題。即使是有經驗的用家也很難以有意義的方式，操控此等大量的參數。即使我們大幅度地改變這些參數，也可能得出相同的聲音。 其中一個最簡單，最直觀的方法來減少添加合成的參數數量，是使用逐段綫性近似波幅函數。逐段綫性近似的關鍵是選擇波幅函數斷點，以求將可聽的差異減至最底。隨後出現的各種問題：需要多少個斷點，可使合成的聲音不能從原來的區分出來？以相同數量的斷點，有哪些樂器更比較容易分辨？如果是這樣，是什麼讓他們更容易被區別？這些都是我們在這研究議案要回答的問題。 數個以前的研究已經評估過各種斷點選擇方法。他們評估過簡單和複雜而以優化為基礎的斷點選擇方法。然而這些研究中，只有少數樂器被評測，並沒有以感知評測為基礎。 這研究議案將逐段綫性近似合成的樂器聲音，以感知評測為基礎。聽力測試將包含大量的樂器。研究議案的目的是以系統地評估聽眾如可區分逐段綫性近似合成的樂器，以擴大我們對音樂感知方面的知識。我們知道，即使樂器的聲音已經大大改變了（例如頻譜均衡器或室內回聲），樂器也能被識別。在此，我們將評測人的耳朵如何分辨逐段綫性近似合成的樂器，和樂器及斷點數量的關係。因此，這研究議案是人類對音調感知的基礎研究。 樂器音色是不容易理解的。我們祈望聽力測試的分析結果，通過量化聽眾如何區分經過數據壓縮的樂器，加深我們對的樂器音色的認識。這也可能導致我們對音樂感知和聲音合成的數據壓縮有新的理解。

613111.label: Realisation of objectives
613111.value: All the project objectives have been achieved. First, harmonic amplitude envelopes of eight sustained musical instrument tones were approximated using piecewise-linear segments to investigate how the discrimination of approximated tones varied with the number of breakpoints and instrument. Relative-amplitude spectral error and relative-amplitude critical-band error were found to be the best error metrics for predicting discrimination. Strong correlations were measured between discrimination scores and spectral incoherence, with breath noise in the flute and bow noise in the violin appearing to cause increased discrimination. The dynamic amplitude envelopes of the flute and violin were smoothed more by line-segment approximations than were some other, more static, instruments (such as the horn and clarinet). For this reason, instruments with more dynamic spectra generally resulted in higher PLA discrimination scores. Next, we had listeners identify the musical instrument generating each data-reduced tone in formal listening tests, resulting in a matrix showing confusion between instruments as a function of the degree of data reduction. We found that for the flute and violin, confusion rates were significantly lower than the other instruments due to their high spectral incoherence. Similarly confusion rates were higher for the horn, clarinet, and bassoon, relatively static low-spectral incoherence instruments. As a third test, we had listeners judge dissimilarity in formal listening tests by asking them to judge distances between original and data reduced sounds (e.g., on a scale of 0-10). The dissimilarity results were significantly correlated to the instrument identification results. We then correlated the discrimination, identification, and dissimilarity results with spectral incoherence, normalized centroid deviation, spectral irregularity, and even/odd harmonic ratio to determine whether these different measures of spectral variation are significantly related. We found that spectral incoherence was significantly corrected to all three, indicating that time variations had a salient effect on all types of judgments. Spectral incoherence was shown to be correlated with discrimination in randomly altered spectra in previous studies of data reduction, while spectral irregularity was shown to be correlated with discrimination in MP3 encoded tones. The discrimination scores in the current study were also correlated with spectral incoherence. Spectral incoherence measures how much a spectrum differs from a coherent version of itself, and therefore how much the spectrum changes between adjacent analysis frames. In the current study data reductions were in the form of smoothed amplitude envelopes. This explains why spectral incoherence, measuring frame-to-frame spectral variation, was strongly correlated with discrimination.

613111.label: Major findings and research outcome
613111.value: Relative-amplitude spectral error and relative-amplitude critical-band error were found to be the best error metrics for predicting discrimination, accounting for about 80% of the discrimination variance. Strong correlations were measured between discrimination scores and spectral incoherence based on the three strongest harmonics, with breath noise in the flute and bow noise in the violin appearing to cause increased discrimination between original and piecewise-linear-approximated sounds. Among the instruments, the discrimination scores for the flute and the violin were significantly higher than the other six instruments. This suggests that the flute and violin are more sensitive to alterations caused by piecewise-linear approximation (PLA) of the harmonic amplitude envelopes. These results can be explained by the significant correlations that were measured between modified spectral incoherence and the discrimination scores. For example, the dynamic amplitude envelopes of the flute and violin were smoothed more by line-segment approximations than were some other, more static, instruments (such as the horn and clarinet). For this reason, instruments with more dynamic spectra generally resulted in higher PLA discrimination scores. Our results showed not only how discrimination varies with number of breakpoints for each instrument; they also provide useful information for synthesizing instrument tones using additive synthesis. For example, if we wish to synthesize a two-second clarinet tone which is nearly indistinguishable from an original, 8 breakpoints should be enough (taking 55% as the threshold for near-indistinguishability). However, if we want to synthesize a nearly indistinguishable flute tone, we need far more breakpoints (about 300). The current study deepens our knowledge about the relationship between the amount of data reduction in PLA and the discrimination of these eight representative instruments. We also found that for the flute and violin, confusion rates were significantly lower than the other instruments due to their high spectral incoherence. Similarly they were higher for the horn, clarinet, and bassoon, relatively static low-spectral incoherence instruments. Spectral incoherence was shown to be correlated with discrimination in randomly altered spectra in previous studies of data reduction. The discrimination scores in the current study were also correlated with spectral incoherence. Spectral incoherence measures how much a spectrum differs from a coherent version of itself, and therefore how much the spectrum changes between adjacent analysis frames. In the current study data reductions were in the form of smoothed amplitude envelopes. This explains why spectral incoherence, measuring frame-to-frame spectral variation, was strongly correlated with discrimination.

613111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
613111.value: One area for further development of the research is an evaluation of amplitude envelope data reduction on not just isolated instrument tones, but monophonic melodies. This will help address the following questions: How much data reduction makes the modified melody distinguishable from the original? How much amplitude envelope data reduction can we make and yet retain the identity of the original instrument? Given the same amount of data reduction, are some melodies more discriminable than others? If so, what makes them more distinguishable? Are some amplitude envelope data reductions easier to detect in a musical context as compared to individual isolated tones? Does melodic content make it easier or harder to hear data reductions by exposing or hiding the alterations?

Our study has found a strong correlation between discrimination and spectral incoherence (a measure of time variations). Spectral incoherence was shown to be correlated with discrimination in randomly altered spectra in previous studies of data reduction, while spectral irregularity was shown to be correlated with discrimination in MP3 encoded tones. 613211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
613211.value: Direct thermal-electrical energy interconversion based on thermoelectric effects is attracting great worldwide interest for potential applications in waste heat recovery and solid-state refrigeration. To achieve high energy conversion efficiency, thermoelectric materials with low thermal conductivity but high electrical conductivity and Seebeck coefficient are required, which are difficult to realize in bulk materials because of the strong interdependence of these parameters. Nanotechnology offers a chance to decouple the electron and phonon transport and to improve the efficiency by reducing the thermal conductivity while maintaining electrical properties through size/interface effects. Although high energy conversion efficiency has been reported for low-dimensional systems, they are expensive to fabricate and difficult to assemble for large-scale applications. Currently the efficiency and material cost limit the wide applications of thermoelectrics. Meanwhile, most thermoelectric materials are based on expensive heavy metals and are hazardous to the environment. It is highly desirable to develop low-toxity, cost-effective, high-performance thermoelectrics. Based on the decoupling of thermal and electrical energy transport in nanostructures and the fact that the reduced thermal conductivity in nanostructures mainly comes from the sequential interface scattering of phonons, we propose to nanoengineer silicon with in-situ grown silicide nanodots to make it an effective thermoelectric material. Silicon, despite its abundance and high electrical conductivity and Seebeck coefficient, is not suitable for thermoelectric applications in its bulk form due to its high thermal conductivity. However, the dramatic difference between the phonon and electron mean free paths in silicon provides an excellent opportunity to significantly reduce thermal conductivity without affecting electron transport much by introducing lattice-matched nanostructures with feature dimensions between the two length scales. High-performance silicon-based nanocomposites will be ideal for thermoelectric applications because of their scalability, low toxicity, and low cost. We will develop a scalable approach based on nanoimprint and ion implantation techniques to fabricate “defect-free” silicon/silicide nanocomposite thin films. The thermoelectric properties of the nanocomposite thin films will be characterized at different temperatures and the optimized process conditions will be explored. We will also use molecular dynamics simulations to explore the effects of various factors on thermal conductivity and to develop a fundamental understanding of the phonon transport and scattering in nanocomposites. This clarification will deepen the understanding of phonon behavior in nanostructured materials and guide the design of novel thermoelectrics, which is of both academic and industrial importance. 由於在廢熱回收和固態制冷方面的潛在應用，基於熱電效應的直接熱能電能相互轉換正在世界範圍內引起極大興趣。為了實現高效的能量轉換，熱電材料要求具備低熱導率，高電導率和高的西伯克系數。由於這些屬性之間的強耦合，這個目標對於體材料來說很難實現。納米技術可用來解耦電子和聲子傳輸，使得通過量子和傳統的尺寸/界面效應來降低熱導率同時維持電屬性以提升效率成為可能。盡管在低維系統中已實現了很高的能量轉換效率，低維系統制造成本很高而且難以集成用於大尺度應用。目前制約熱電廣泛應用的因素是效率和材料成本。同時，絕大部分熱電材料基於昂貴的重金屬，對環境有害。發展低毒，低成本，高效率的熱電材料迫在眉睫。 近來在低維結構的熱傳輸方面的研究表明，熱導率的降低主要是由於聲子的界面散射。因此，在體材料中加入適當的納米結構可望在大幅降低熱導率的同時不太影響電子的傳輸。我們幾乎用原位生長的矽化物納米點將矽改造成為高效的熱電材料。矽盡管儲量豐富並具有很高的電導率和西伯克系數，但因為它具有很高的熱導率，並不適合熱電應用。然而，矽中聲子和電子的平均自由程的巨大差異使得在體材料中引入與晶格相容的納米結構來降低熱導率並同時保持電性能成為可能。基於其可擴展性，低毒性和低成本等優點，高性能矽基納米復合材料非常適合熱電應用。我們將發展一種基於離子註入和納米壓印的技術來制造“無缺陷”的矽/矽化物納米復合薄膜。我們將測量這種薄膜在不同溫度下的熱電性能並探索最優的工藝過程。同時，我們將通過分子動力學模擬來理解聲子在這些新型聲子材料中的傳輸和散射機理。這將加深對納米材料中的聲子行為的理解並指導新型熱電材料的設計，對工業和學術發展都具有重要意義。

613211.label: Realisation of objectives
613211.value: We have used molecular dynamics simulations to explore the lattice thermal conductivities of porous Si and Si nanocomposites. The phonon transport process in those nanostructured structures have been explained by using spectral analysis. The influence of pattern arrangement, spacing as well as the size and impedance of the nano inclusions on the thermal conductivity has been clarified. It is found that the lattice orientation and space symmetry mismatch are most efficient factors that can reduce the thermal conductivity of the nanocomposites. Also, the anisotropic arrangement of the nano patterns will lead to significant anisotropy in the thermal transport. We also developed a low-cost method based on low-pressure chemical vapor deposition to grown high-quality nanostructured SiGe thin films with in-situ formed columnar nanograins. The grain size can be tuned by changing the growth conditions. This method doesn't require complicated nano fabrication process and its good uniformity and control on sample quality render it ideal for batch production. The Seebeck coefficient, electric conductivity, carrier mobility and thermal conductivity of the n- and p-type nanograined SiGe thin films have been clarified from 80 K to 350 K. A very high figure of merit of 0.2 has been achieved in the nanograined thin film, 100% higher than the previous record of SiGe thin films. The low fabrication cost and high performance make the nanograined thin films highly promising for future thermoelectric applications. Through theoretical investigation, we found that nanograined thin films may have similar performance to those embedded with quantum dots while the former are advantageous for the low fabrication cost and suitability for large-scale fabrication.

613211.label: Major findings and research outcome
613211.value: 1. Through molecular dynamics simulations, we found that the junctions in nanoporous structure may cause additional scattering due to the dispersion mismatch, which illustrates the importance of the phonon wave behavior in nanoporous structures. A two-part model that can be extended to macro sale has been developed to describe the influence of the junction effects. The junction effects provide a new strategy to engineer thermal transport in solids in addition to conventional diffusive boundary scattering. 2. Using non-equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations, the details of thermal transport in Si nanocomposites have been clarified. Ballistic phonon transport is found important in the border regime while the channel regime is the bottleneck for the thermal transport. Anisotropic patterning will lead to anisotropic thermal conductivity. Meanwhile, the lattice-structure-mismatch including the mismatch in lattice orientation and space symmetry is the most efficient mechanism to reduce the thermal conductivity. 3. Using low-pressure chemical vapor deposition, we have successfully synthesized SiGe thin films with naturally formed columnar nanograins. Characterization of the films from 80 K to 350 K shows that the grown SiGe thin films have superior thermoelectric performance due to the existence of nanograin boundaries. A high figure of merit of 0.2 has been achieved, which is 100% higher than the record of SiGe alloy, making the nanograined thin films promising for large-scale thin film thermoelectric applications. 4. A micro device that can be used to measure the thermal conductivity, Seebeck coefficient and electrical conductivity as well as the charge mobility and carrier concentration has been developed. 5. We have published 2 conference papers in international conferences and 7 papers in peer-reviewed international journals. 6. A PhD student has been trained.

613211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
613211.value: Based on our findings, films with nano grains may be more promising for large-scale thermoelectric applications. Unlike the hot-pressed nanocomposites, the in-situ formed nano grains don’t have insulating surface layer and have little influence on charge transport. Meanwhile, the nano grains can significantly suppress the phonon transport, leading to much reduced thermal conductivity. The reduction in thermal conductivity depends on the characteristic size of the columnar grain structure. Tuning the feature dimension of the nano grains by controlling the growth conditions will be a very promising and practical way to further improvement of thermoelectric performance. How the different factors affect the growth of nano grains will be important for developing high-performance nanograined thermoelectric materials.

613211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
613211.value: In this project, we have explored nanostructured Si-based thermoelectric films for low-cost thermoelectric applications by combining theoretical modeling and experimental synthesis and characterization. We have found that the thermal conductivity of Si embedded with lattice-structure-mismatched nano inclusions can approach the theoretical minimal for bulk materials. The wave behavior of phonons might play a role in these phononic crystals, leading to larger thermal resistivity than that purely caused by diffusive scattering. This provides a new strategy for tailoring thermal properties of materials for targeted applications. Meanwhile, we have synthesized and characterized n- and p-type SiGe thin films with naturally formed columnar nano grains, which show superior thermoelectric properties. A very high thermoelectric performance has been achieved in the LPCVD-grown nanograined SiGe thin films, which is 100% higher than the previous record for SiGe alloy. The low-cost and high-throughput of LPCVD make the nanograined SiGe thin films an ideal candidate for large-scale thin-film thermoelectric applications. We are now developing thermoelectric microcoolers and sensors based on the high-performance nanograined SiGe thin films developed.

These decentralized strategies not only will distribute the computational burden to the network but also save the energy consumed by wireless communication. Fatigue damage accumulation in metallic structures will be studied intensively. In recognition of the uncertainties present and the randomness inherent in the nature of the fatigue phenomenon, it is appropriate to conduct fatigue assessment in a probabilistic way, i.e., obtain a fatigue reliability assessment. Temperature measurements will be utilized to account for the correlation between temperature and other quantities of interest, such as modal parameters, and stress/strain. The use of additional excitation data, such as wind speed and traffic volume, that will yield refined statistical models for the excitation will also be investigated.

613511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
613511.value: Herein we propose the development of new methodologies for the robust reliability updating of civil infrastructures based on wireless sensor monitoring. Health monitoring of civil infrastructures is being recognized worldwide as an issue of great urgency and importance and has become a high-priority research area. Monitored data collected from sensory systems deployed within a civil structure contain valuable information which can be used to assess the current condition of the structure and predict its performance under current and future loads. As uncertainties are abundant in civil engineering, reliability analysis is employed to quantify and assess the effect of such uncertainties. The reliability of civil structures, defined as the probability of satisfying certain specified performance measures, is not only important to be calculated in the preliminary design stage, but needs to be continuously monitored over the lifetime of the structure. During such operation stage, the condition, and as a result the reliability, of civil structures may deteriorate due to fatigue or corrosion, or from damage induced by severe loading events such as strong wind loads or earthquakes. This project aims to provide an automated and reliable assessment of the condition of civil infrastructures by updating their system reliability based on monitored data. The hardware of the proposed monitoring system will comprise wireless sensors, which combine sensing, computing and communication capacities. Dynamic response data of the structure under operational conditions will be collected. These measurements will then be used to assess the safety of the structure by updating continually its reliability. This project will focus on developing state-of-the-art reliability updating algorithms based on response measurements under operational conditions and will also be specially designed to allow distributed processing of data by the various sensing units, keeping wireless data transmission between different units to a minimum. This is highly desirable in order to minimize energy consumption which is a major consideration in the design of such wireless sensor systems. It is believed that this project can make significant contributions in the area of reliability updating based on wireless sensor monitoring, a technology that is rapidly emerging and believed to hold bright future.

613511.label: Realisation of objectives
613511.value: The objectives of this project were realized. With regards to the first objective several model updating algorithms have been proposed. A fast Bayesian methodology is presented for structural model updating utilizing modal information from multiple setups. To this end, a two-stage fast Bayesian spectral density approach formulated recently is firstly employed to identify the most probable modal properties as well as their uncertainties. Besides this method, two other Bayesian model updating algorithms has been proposed, one is based on modal data, and the other one is based on modal flexibility. With regards to the second objective, a novel stochastic simulation method for updating robust reliability of dynamic structural systems with monitoring data has been proposed. This stochastic simulation strategy is based on Bayesian updating, subset simulation and kernel density estimation. In this method, the posterior failure probability is updated using a Bayesian approach which integrates the information of the prior failure probability and the likelihood functions of monitoring data conditioned on failure and non-failure states. In real applications, this algorithm enable one to quickly obtain the updated robust reliability when the new monitored data become available. With regards to the third objective, fatigue damage accumulation in metallic structures has been studied intensively. Cumulative fatigue damage is calculated using Palmgren–Miner’s rule, S-N fatigue curves, and different forms of distribution for stress ranges in terms of the power spectral densities (PSD) of the stress processes. A stress distribution model is developed based on field monitoring data, and stresses at unmeasured hot spot locations are estimated from the response measurements collected at a limited number of measured locations.

613511.label: Major findings and research outcome
613511.value: In the field of model updating, three algorithms based on a Bayesian statistical framework have been developed. The first one is a novel Bayesian approach for structural model updating utilizing statistical modal information from multiple setups (Journal article 1). To this end, a two-stage fast Bayesian spectral density approach formulated recently is firstly employed to identify the most probable modal properties as well as their uncertainties (Journal article 2 & 3). The model updating problem is then formulated as one minimizing an objective function, which can incorporate statistical information about local mode shape components corresponding to different setups automatically, without prior assembling or processing. The other two algorithms are also based on Bayesian statistical framework (Conf. paper 1 & 2). One utilizes modal data directly and the other one utilizes modal flexibility which is constructed from modal data. In both of these two algorithms, preliminary updating stage is performed first to facilitate the optimization problem in the Bayesian updating stage, which makes the algorithm more efficient and robust. In the field of reliability updating, a novel stochastic simulation method for updating robust reliability of dynamic structural systems with monitoring data is developed. This stochastic simulation method is based on Bayesian updating, subset simulation and kernel density estimation. In this method, the posterior failure probability (the complement of robust reliability) is updated using a Bayesian approach which integrates the information of the prior failure probability and the likelihood functions of monitoring data conditioned on failure and non-failure states. The failure probability required for the Bayesian updating is computed by means of subset simulation, an efficient Monte Carlo method for estimation of small failure probabilities. The likelihood functions of monitoring data conditioned on failure and non-failure states are estimated using kernel sampling density. In real applications, this algorithm enables one to quickly obtain the updated robust reliability when the new monitored data become available. This article paper is under preparation (Journal article 4). In the field of probabilistic fatigue assessment, fatigue damage accumulation in metallic structures has been studied. Cumulative fatigue damage is calculated using Palmgren–Miner’s rule, S-N fatigue curves, and different forms of distribution for stress ranges in terms of the power spectral densities (PSD) of the stress processes. A stress distribution model is developed based on field monitoring data, and stresses at unmeasured hot spot locations are estimated from the response measurements collected at a limited number of measured locations.

613511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
613511.value: The main concern of the future work will focus on implementing the proposed algorithms on wireless sensors. More time and efforts should be devoted to embedding programs and debugging for wireless sensors. The methodologies developed will be experimentally validated in a laboratory setting as well as on a pedestrian bridge at the HKUST campus.

613511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
613511.value: Herein the development of new methodologies for the robust reliability updating of civil infrastructures based on wireless sensor monitoring was pursued. This project provides an automated and reliable assessment of the condition of civil infrastructures by updating their system reliability based on monitored data. The hardware of the proposed monitoring system comprises wireless sensors, which combine sensing, computing and communication capacities. Dynamic response data of the structure under operational conditions are collected. These measurements are then used to assess the safety of the structure by updating its reliability continually. The main contributions of this project are developing state-of-the-art reliability updating algorithms based on response measurements under operational conditions and specially designing their implementation scheme to allow distributed processing of data by the various sensing units, keeping wireless data transmission between different units to a minimum. This is highly desirable in order to minimize energy consumption which is a major consideration in the design of such wireless sensor systems. It is believed that this project can make significant contributions in the area of reliability updating based on wireless sensor monitoring, a technology that is rapidly emerging and believed to hold bright future.

613711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
613711.value: The swash zone is that region of the coast that is periodically submerged by waves. On relatively steep, coarse-grained beaches, the flow is generated by plunging waves leading to bores that collapse onto the beach. This creates a very dynamic region, with high levels of turbulence and high sediment transport rates and therefore the swash-zone plays a very important role in the overall shaping and stability of the beach. For this reason, substantial research effort has focused on swash in recent years. Field-based measurements of the swash zone processes advanced our understanding of the gross characteristic of the swash flow. These studies have been complemented by detailed laboratory studies which investigated the important fundamental aspects of the swash processes. The focus of these studies has been on the detailed hydrodynamics, the turbulence and the bed shear stress, and to a lesser extent the effects of infiltration/exfiltration and sediment transport. Although recent laboratory investigations have significantly advanced understanding of swash zone processes, some aspects are still not fully understood. These aspects include the effect of the entrained air, entrained by the plunging wave, and the effect of swash-swash interaction on the hydrodynamics of the swash-zone. The current research proposal aims to further our understanding of the effects of air entrainment and swash-swash interactions on the swash zone hydrodynamics, thereby underpinning the development of engineering models. The proposal is based on a three stage, large-scale laboratory experimental investigation designed to measure detailed aspects of the swash hydrodynamics. The first stage will be used to isolate the effect of air entrainment. A single bore collapse will be generated and the development of the entrained bubble plume will be recorded. In stages two and three, experiments will involve a bore collapsing on a previous bore. Exploratory stage two will yield bulk flow characteristics for a broad set of initial conditions. Stage three involves detailed flow measurements for a few selected conditions of bore-bore interaction. Analysis of the experimental data will yield measurements of the gross characteristics, detailed kinematics and the temporal and spatial variation of the void fractions. These results will be used to parameterise the different terms responsible for the dissipation of energy in the swash-zone. An existing NLSWE (nonlinear shallow water equations) based numerical model for swash on impermeable slopes will be developed, further using the results and parameterisation from the experiments to include the effects of air entrainment and swash-swash interactions. 海灘沖流帶即上沖流週期性浸沒的海岸區域。崩捲型碎波到達相對陡峭、粗糙的海灘后演變生成雍波（上沖流）。雍波衝向海岸的同時崩塌在海灘上，当其達到一定高度后，由於重力作用又沿海灘迴流。整個上述過程的發生創建了一個有著高湍流強度和高輸沙率的獨特動態區域（海灘沖流帶）。因此，海灘沖流帶在關於海灘整體輪廓和穩定性研究中扮演著重要角色。 為此，最近幾年中已有大量科研文獻集中論述海灘沖流帶的問題。通過實測天然海灘沖流帶水流運動增進了我們對上沖流整體特性的認知。更為精細的物模實驗研究彌補了實測研究的不足并專門對上沖流的重要基本問題展開分析。上述研究主要集中在複雜的水動力學問題上，例如：紊流度、底床剪切應力、較小程度上的滲透影響和輸沙率。雖然最近的物模實驗研究對沖流帶水流運動已經有了相當詳盡的分析，但是某些方面還是沒有被充分認知。需要進一步研究的方面包括崩捲型碎波捲入的空氣和上沖流間的相互作用對海灘沖流帶水動力學的影響。 當前的研究目標是增進對上述兩個問題的認知，從而，支撐工程模型的發展。本研究計劃分為三個階段，擬設計大比例尺的物模實驗研究觀察沖流帶水動力學的各個具體方面。第一階段單獨考察空氣捲入的影響。實驗將記錄單個上沖流的運動過程及捲入氣體在水中的發育情況。第二、三階段實驗將考察兩個上沖流間隔時間小於單個運動週期時上沖流間的相互作用。其中，第二階段實驗將通過設置不同的時間間隔及初始條件，得到一系列相應的水流流動特性。第三階段則是對第二階段部份情況進行更為詳盡的水流特性觀察研究。分析實驗數據得到水流流態測量值、詳細的水動力學特性及空隙率隨時間與空間的變化。這些結果將用於海灘沖流帶動量公式能量耗散項的參數設定。進一步運用實驗得到的數據和參數對現有的不透水沖流帶的數學模型（非線性淺水波方程）進行修正。

613711.label: Realisation of objectives
613711.value: Objective 1 (100% complete): A double dam-break mechanism was built into an existing wave-flume that generated single or two interacting swash events that ran up and down a sand-rough impermeable 1:10 slope. For the single swash event, the hydrodynamics were measured using a combined PIV/LIF system which yielded the flow depths and velocities. The characteristics of the entrained air were obtained using an optical probe system. Ensemble and local time-averaging yielded the void fractions, bubble sizes and velocities. Objective 2 (100% complete): Analysis of the data showed that void fractions were up to 0.20 but decreased rapidly with distance up the slope and no air was present after flow reversal. The effects of the entrained air on the flow were evaluated by using both the hydrodynamics and entrained air measurements. The free surface increased by up to 6mm and the volume of the flow by 2.5L per meter width. A minimum of 1% of total energy dissipation is attributable to entrained air. Objective 3 (50% complete): Existing NLSWE codes were run for the single swash event and showed reasonably comparison with experimental data. Extensions of the NLSWE to include the effects of entrained air and swash interaction were put on hold as the experimental data revealed the importance of the bed-normal velocities in the behavior of the entrained air and swash interactions which cannot be included in NLSWE. Instead, focus shifted to a two-phase Volume of Fluid CFD model. Results showed reasonable matches until time of maximum backwash velocity, indicating momentum losses were not appropriately modelled. Simulations with different friction coefficients and turbulence models are still running. Extra Achievement 1 (original objective 3: 100% complete): For the interacting swash events, measurements of the flow depth for exploratory experiments with a range of initial conditions were obtained using acoustic displacement sensors at five cross-shore locations. For a typical wave-capture interaction case and weak wave-backwash interaction case, the detailed hydrodynamics were obtained using the PIV/LIF system at three cross-shore locations. Extra Achievement 2 (original objective 4: 100% complete): Analysis of the exploratory experiments enabled the types of interaction to be determined which were dependent on the relative strength of the bores and their arrival times. Analysis of the detailed hydrodynamics showed the effects of the interaction on the flow behaviour. The fluid of the first bore is advected upwards and then mixed with the fluid of the second bore by intense shearing and highly turbulent vortices.

613711.label: Major findings and research outcome
613711.value: The findings of the study of entrained air in the swash zone are presented in the manuscript “Entrained air in bore-driven swash on an impermeable rough slope” that has been submitted for publication in Journal of Coastal Engineering. For details see attachment to Part C. The major findings included the presence in the swash-zone of two compact bubble clouds. The maximum void fraction of the bubble clouds is approximately 0.20, the total volume of entrained air is 2.5L/m and up to 6mm of the flow depth are attributable to air. Further shoreward these values decrease rapidly as the air entrained escapes quickly and less air is entrained locally. The locally entrained air in the first bubble cloud results in large air cavities, with bubble diameters up to 20mm and velocities up to 4m/s, which develop rapidly into multiple smaller bubbles. The bubbles in the second cloud are of more homogeneous size, but have velocities that are smaller than the mean flow indicating that they are partly controlled by turbulence. A minimum of 1% of the total energy dissipation that occurs during the single swash event is attributable to entrained air. In general, the characteristics of the entrained air are similar to those obtained after wave breaking in the surf zone and deep water; however the dissipation of energy attributable to the entrained air is smaller. The findings of the study on swash-swash interactions are presented in the manuscript “Experimental study of bore-driven swash-swash interactions on an impermeable rough slope” that has been submitted for publication in Journal of Coastal Engineering. For details see attachment to Part C. The major findings included the dependence of the interaction type on the relative momentum of the two bores and their arrival times and that swash interaction cannot necessarily be described by a single interaction type along the whole beach. The interaction processes of wave-capture and weak wave-backwash interaction are similar. The arrival of the second bore creates very steep gradients in the bed-parallel velocity profiles. This results in a mixing layer with intense shearing and generation of turbulent vortices. Fluid from the first bore is advected upwards into the flow column where it is rapidly mixed with the fluid from the second bore by the intense shearing and turbulent vortices. During weak wave-backwash interaction the bores travel in opposite directions and therefore the overall effects of interaction are stronger than during wave-capture interaction.

613711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
613711.value: The current study shows that the overall effect of the entrained air on the hydrodynamics of the flow may be small, supporting the assumption that the flow is a single phase flow. However, this conclusion is based on only a single set of initial conditions. To confirm the general application of this conclusion, further experiments should be carried out in particular for initial conditions that may increase the total volume of entrained air in the swash zone. These include a plunging wave that breaks much closer to the initial shoreline, which means air entrained has much less time to escape before the flow reaches the swash zone, and larger diameter sediments along the slope, which increases the importance of the locally entrained air. The characteristics of the hydrodynamics during interaction confirm the potential of swash-swash interactions to suspend significant amounts of sediments high into the flow column and then transport the sediments shoreward with the second bore or interrupt the seaward transport of sediments. To quantify the sediment transport as a result of swash interactions requires more detailed measurements under controlled conditions to enable sediment transport models that take into account the effect of swash-swash interactions to be properly evaluated.

613711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
613711.value: The swash zone is that area of the coast that is alternatively wet and dry and plays an important role in the overall shape of a beach. The high sediment transport rates in the swash zone are caused by the flow which is complex because it varies with time and distance and is highly turbulent. Many processes that affect the flow in the swash zone have been studied. The entrained air and interactions between subsequent swash events are the focus of the current research. The characteristics of the entrained air are similar to that obtained after wave breaking in other parts of the ocean. The void fractions are initially high, but reduce quickly and the contribution to the total energy loss due to entrained air is a minimum of 1%. Hence the overall effect of entrained air on the flow may be small. Swash interaction types depend on strength of the incoming waves and the time between waves. The processes of the wave-capture and weak wave-backwash interactions are similar but intensity of the latter is stronger as the flows move in opposite directions. The characteristics of the flow during interaction confirm the potential to suspend significant amount of sediments.

613811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
613811.value: One of the most imminent challenges for today’s mobile society is to provide highly efficient, low-cost and environmentally-friendly energy conversion and storage devices to power increasingly diverse devices and systems, ranging from portable electronics, power tools to electric vehicles (EVs). EVs use electric motors and motor controllers, instead of the internal combustion engines that generate air pollution, and thus provide a sustainable and longer-term solution to address the air pollution problems. The power for EVs is currently derived from traditional battery packs made from lead acid or Ni-Cd batteries that are carried on board the vehicle. Other prominent energy storage methods that have emerged recently include rechargeable Li ion batteries (LIBs) and electric double-layer capacitors (EDLCs), also known as supercapacitors. LIBs and EDLCs are among the most promising energy storage devices, and the characteristics of their electrode materials determine the overall electrochemical properties. Although LIBs have many advantages over traditional batteries, the current level of energy/power densities, as well as their safety, cyclic life and charging performance, are far below the levels required to power demanding systems. Although the electrode materials in LIBs and EDLCs can be reversibly charged/discharged under intercalation potentials with sufficient specific capacity, their overall electrochemical properties need further improvement. To address the above issues, this project proposes to employ graphene in electrochemical energy storage devices. Graphene is the award-winning material which led to the Nobel Prize in Physics 2010 being awarded jointly to Andre Geim and Konstantin Novoselov "for groundbreaking experiments regarding the two-dimensional material graphene." It consists of densely packed carbon atoms in a plane form and has many useful electrochemical characteristics, including 100 times higher electrical conductivity than copper, extremely large specific surface area and very high capacity. Graphene is considered a potential alternative electrode material for carbon materials used in LIBs and EDLCs due to its unique nanostructure possessing excellent electronic conductivity. Furthermore, the large surface area of graphene makes it an excellent support for metal oxides, such as SnO2 and MnO2, which give rise to high specific capacity and capacitance by ensuring good contacts between the electrodes and electrolyte. Special emphasis should be placed on the alignment of graphene nanosheets to maximize their beneficial effects. These nanostructured composite electrodes containing perfectly-aligned graphene sheets will offer the ultimate solution to enhanced power/energy densities, fast charging as well as long cyclic life, which are essential to future mobile systems including portable electronics and EVs. 在今天这样一个如此高速发展的社会中，最迫切的挑战之一即为如何提供高效率、低成本以及环保的能源转换和储存器件，来供给日益发展的多样化的电力装置和系统，这其中便涵盖了便携式电子产品、电动工具及电动汽车。电动汽车通过使用电动机及电机控制器，以取代对空气产生污染作用的内燃机，从而提供了解决空气污染问题的一种既可持续又长期有效的方案。目前，电动汽车的能源来自于车载的传统铅酸及镍镉电池。最近刚刚出现的其他突出的能源储存方式包括可充电锂离子电池及双电层电容器，后者也被叫做超级电容器。 锂离子电池及双电层电容器是最有发展前景的储能装置，他们电极材料的特点，决定了其总体的电化学性能。尽管锂离子电池相对于传统电池相比有诸多优势，但目前的能量、功率密度的水平、以及它们的安全性能、循环寿命和充电性能仍然远远低于能源需求系统的目标要求。虽然锂离子电池和双电层电容器的电极材料在层间电位下可以实现可逆地充放电以达到所需的容量，但它们整体的电化学性能还需要进一步的提高。 为了解决上述问题，本项目提出在电化学储能器件中应用石墨烯材料。石墨烯是一种曾获大奖的明星材料，它直接导致2010年诺贝尔物理学奖被联合授予给安德烈•盖姆和康斯坦丁•诺沃肖罗夫，“为了表彰有关的二维材料石墨烯的开创性研究”。它由在一个平面上紧密排列的碳原子组成，并且有许多有用的电化学特性，其中包括高于铜材料100倍的导电性、非常高的比表面积及非常高的容量。鉴于石墨烯其独特的纳米结构具有优良的电子导电性，它被认识是一种潜在的电极替代材料，以取代目前锂离子电池和双电层电容器中应用的碳材料。此外，石墨烯的高比表面积使得其成为金属材料的优良载体，这其中包括二氧化锡及二氧化锰，它通过保证电极材料和电解液的良好接触来得到高比容量和电容。为了最大限度发挥其有利影响，应该着重关注于石墨烯纳米层的排列方式。这种由完美排列的石墨烯层组成的纳米结构的复合电极将会提供对于更高的能量、功率密度、快速充电及长的循环寿命需求的终极解决方案，而这些，也是包括便携式电子产品和电动汽车在内的未来移动系统的关键因素。

613811.label: Realisation of objectives
613811.value: The two objectives were fully achieved according to the original research plan without any problems encountered. Many original results have been generated and a number of high quality papers were published in prestigious journals and presented in conferences. The major outcome from the project is summarized in the below. We synthesized high quality graphene oxide (GO) films and papers and applied them in energy storage devices with drastically improved electrochemical performance. The monolayer GO sheets prepared by a chemical method showed an average size of about 32.7 μm, which were sorted into four groups of different sizes. Freestanding graphene papers were prepared by simple vacuum filtration of the GO dispersion. We found that the large-size GO sheets resulted in better self-alignment, higher electrical conductivity and mechanical properties of the papers. To mitigate the challenge of low conductivities of GO papers, self-assembled GO/CNT films were prepared for EDLCs application. The surpercapacitive performance depended on the presence of oxygenated functional groups, the interlayer spacing of GO sheets and their wettability with electrolyte. A moderate reduction of GO papers at 220 οC was proven to be beneficial to achieving a high capacitance. The thin GO/CNT films of 200 nm in thickness with 12.5 wt.% of CNTs delivered a much higher capacitance than graphene papers acting alone due to the shortened ion diffusion lengths and high conductivities of CNTs. The flexible, binder-free PANI/GO/CNT films further enhanced the capacitance, ascribing to the excellent electroactivity of conducting PANI. In addition, extensive studies have been made of combining GO sheets with active metal oxides, including SnO2 nanoparticles, Li4Ti5O12 nanoparticles, LiFePO4 nanorods and ɑ-MnO2 nanorods to improve the electrochemical performance of anodes or cathodes in LIBs and LABs. It is established that the graphene with high aspect ratios over 10,000, large surface areas and excellent electrical conductivities enabled to form extensive conductive networks for the active materials at a low content, leading to high reversible capacities, outstanding rate capabilities and good cycling stability.

613811.label: Major findings and research outcome
613811.value: Objective 1: Graphene oxide (GO) was synthesized from natural graphite using the modified Hummers’ method. The GO sheets were successfully sorted into four groups with similar areas of 272.2 (ultralarge), 32.2 (very large), 9.0 (large) and 1.1 μm2 (small) after a series of centrifugation at different speeds. Graphene papers were prepared by simple vacuum filtration of GO aqueous solutions. It is found that the large-size GO sheets imparted a tremendous positive impact on self-alignment, electrical conductivity and mechanical properties of graphene papers [J01], as well as optoelectronic properties of the Langmuir–Blodgett assembled thin films on a flexible substrate [J02]. Objective 2: To alleviate the drawbacks of low electrical conductivities and re-stacking of reduced GO (RGO) sheets, carbon nanotubes (CNTs) were introduced to GO papers to form GO/CNT hybrid films for supercapacitor or EDLC applications. The GO/CNT sandwich papers with 12.5 wt.% CNT exhibited a high capacitance of 151 F/g at 0.5 A/g and a capacitance retention of 86 % after 6,000 cycles [J03]. About 200 nm thick RGO/CNT films on a Ti substrate were also prepared, which presented a high specific capacitance of 428 F/g at 0.5 A/g along with excellent capacity retention of 98 % after 10,000 cycles [J04]. The freestanding polyaniline (PANI)/RGO/CNT films were synthesized by filtration and electropolymerization processes, which delivered better capacitance than the RGO/CNT counterpart [J05]. To improve the rate capabilities of LIBs, focused studies were made by incorporating GO sheets in SnO2, Li4Ti5O12 (LTO) and LiFePO4 (LFP) nanomaterials to form advanced composite electrodes. For example, SnO2/graphene/CNT composites were synthesized using GO as precursor and template for the growth of SnO2 particles. Owing to the synergy of the high capacity arising from SnO2 particles and the excellent cycleability of graphene/CNT papers, the SnO2/graphene/CNT composite anodes presented a stable capacity of 387 mAh/g at 0.1 A/g after 50 cycles [J06]. GO nanosheets with extremely high aspect ratios were employed as the conductive fillers for LTO anodes in LIBs, resulting in a much lower percolation threshold than the conventional carbon black additives [J07]. GO-wrapped LFP cathodes were prepared using a polyol method, presenting one of the highest electrochemical properties among all similar LFP electrodes reported in literature [J08]. ɑ-MnO2/reduced GO composites were also proven to be a great potential as the cathode in lithium-air batteries (LABs) [J09].

613811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
613811.value: In addition to the LIBs, EDLCs and LABs studied in this project, the research can be extended by employing graphene in other high energy density energy storage devices, like lithium-sulfur batteries (LSBs). Subsequently, we have applied and been approved in 2015 of an ITF project (ITS/318/14) entitled “nanocarbon/sulfur composite electrodes for Li-S batteries with exceptional long-term cyclic and environmental stability”. The graphene-based nanostructures with high electrical conductivities, large surface areas and abundant functional groups will serve as both high electric/ionic conducting path and effective polysulfide trappers. The three-dimensional (3D) graphene scaffolds will also be developed to address the poor rate capabilities and poor cyclic stability of the current LSBs. Furthermore, to reduce the fabrication/material costs of energy storage devices for electric vehicle (EVs) applications, sodium ion batteries (SIBs) have emerged as alternative to LIBs due to the much lower cost of sodium than lithium. Active materials of SIBs, like Sn, Sb and P, invariably suffer from huge volume expansion/contraction upon sodiation/desodiation as well as limited electronic conductivities. Graphene sheets with high flexibility, excellent mechanical properties and conductivities have great potential to mitigate these issues.

613811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
613811.value: Developing renewable and clean energy sources as well as finding ways to use energy more efficiently are part of the great challenges of making our economic activities sustainable. There has been increasing demands for developing more efficient and cost effective electrochemical energy storage systems with powerful outputs and long life. Graphene with unique properties, such as excellent electrical conductivity, large surface area and excellent chemical/mechanical stability, has been identified as promising additive or template for energy storage materials. Through this project, we have synthesized freestanding graphene oxide film/papers with high quality and large quantity by vacuum filtration. Substantially improved electrochemical performance has been achieved for several important rechargeable energy storage devices, including lithium ion batteries (LIBs), electrical double layer capacitors (EDLCs) and lithium air batteries (LABs), through successful design and synthesis of various graphene oxide nanostructures for different active materials. Continued efforts are being directed to explore further enhancing the energy/power densities of these rechargeable batteries for next generation electric vehicles. Based on the results obtained from this project, nine papers have been published all in high impact journals, and another seven papers have been presented in international conferences.

613911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
613911.value: 程序错误造成的问题，令每年经济损失数十亿。同时，质量保证（QA）例如测试和调试仍佔著整个软件开发成本的50％。自动化质量保证是提高质量保证生产力最有前景的方法。我们希望透過自动再现和修补软件崩溃大大減輕质量保证的工作。许多技术已经被提出以提供可靠的崩溃再现，其中大部分是基于记录和回放的方法。然而，这些技术不是带来昂贵的运行负载，就是需要特殊的硬件支持，使他们缺乏吸引力和不实用。另一方面，崩溃报告系统收集崩溃堆栈跟踪（CSTs）時几乎没有性能负载，被广泛配置在生产上，如在Microsoft Windows，MacOS和Mozilla Firefox浏览器里。然而，收集到的崩溃堆栈跟踪沒有被利用來自动重现崩溃，从而崩溃再现仍然需要不少的人为努力。 我们提出了一种新的技术称为RECAP，使用崩溃堆栈跟踪以再现和修补软件崩溃而不需要任何额外的外部信息或人为干预。反而，RECAP使用广泛应用于自动化测试的技术产生崩溃输入，如物件生成和最弱先決條件计算。RECAP创建单元测试，以产生的输入來调用崩溃堆栈跟踪里崩溃了的方法。RECAP执行生成的单元测试以重现崩溃。由于有些崩溃是非确定性的和搜索输入空间庞大，RECAP未必可以重现每一個崩溃和创建适合的输入以重现所有崩溃。但是，这不应该立即否認RECAP的效用。即使RECAP在崩溃报告系统重现只有30％的崩溃，它仍然能夠减少30％的人为努力。 在RECAP的再现阶段，它会创建大量的单元测试，以用来提出补丁基于delta调试，遗传编程和以历史为基础的方法。建议的补丁将使用生成的单元测试验证，成功的补丁會被报告给开发者。这些补丁将有助于进一步减少人为的努力。

613911.label: Realisation of objectives
613911.value: First, we spent a lot of time to understand crashes by analyzing stack traces and trying to locate the main causes of the crashes. One of the results of this effort is an ACM SIGSOFT Distinguished Paper Award winner, "CrashLocator: Locating Crashing Faults Based on Crash Stacks" published at ISSTA 2014 (C3). We developed a method to locate faulty functions using the crash stack information in crash reports. It deduces possible crash traces (the failing execution traces that lead to crash) by expanding the crash stack with functions in a static call graph. Then, we continued our research into two folds: automatic reproducing and automatic repair. For reproduction, we have developed a system called, STAR (Stack Trace-based Automatic Crash Reproduction via Symbolic Execution). STAR combines an efficient backward symbolic execution and a novel method sequence composition approach to generate unit test cases that can reproduce the original crashes without incurring additional runtime overhead. Our evaluation study shows that our approach successfully exploited 31 (59.6%) of 52 crashes in three open source projects. Among these exploitable crashes, 22 (42.3%) are useful reproductions of the original crashes that reveal the crash triggering bugs. A comparison study also demonstrates that our approach can effectively outperform existing crash reproduction approaches. This work is published at the top SE journal, IEEE Transactions of Software Engineering (J1). Finally, we also have a success in the automatic repair. Based on observations on crashes, their reproduction, and corresponding patches, we identified common fix patterns. We manually inspected more than 60,000 human-written patches and found there are several common fix patterns. Our approach leverages these fix patterns to generate program patches automatically. We experimentally evaluated our system on 119 real bugs. In addition, a user study involving 89 students and 164 developers confirmed that patches generated by our approach are more acceptable than those generated by GenProg. Our system successfully generated patches for 27 out of 119 bugs, while GenProg was successful for only 16 bugs. This is published at ICSE with the ACM SIGSOFT distinguished paper award (C2).

613911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
613911.value: In our opinion, our results are promising, but still we need further development for the practical use. First of all, we need to improve the performance. Currently, we can reproduce about 50% of bugs, and fix about 30% of bugs. We plan to improve them to 70% reproduction and 50% fixes.
