613911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
613911.value: As two ACM SIGSOFT Distinguished Paper Awards indicated, the value of our research outcomes is very significant. Crash reproducing and debugging (fixing bugs) are the most difficult and tedious tasks for software developers. Our research results can significantly reduce these burdens for developers. At the same time, our techniques can contribute to more reliable software since developers can locate and fix bugs more efficiently.

614011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
614011.value: Infilled frame structures are recognised as one of the most common structural forms for medium- and high-rise buildings. Although this structural form has been widely adopted for buildings for many years, it has been extensively reported that in every single disastrous earthquake during the past decades relatively poor seismic performance and severe damage of a considerable amount of infilled frame buildings, including many newly designed ones, were observed, particularly in the 1999 Izmit earthquake in Turkey, the 2008 Sichuan earthquake in China, and the 2010 Maule earthquake in Chile. It clearly reveals that inherent problems related to the design and analysis methods of infilled frame buildings have not yet been solved. In traditional analysis and design of frame structures, infill walls are normally considered as non-structural components. As a result, the contributions of infills to the overall seismic behaviour of the structure in the computational models are generally neglected owing to the following reasons: (1) adverse consequences of neglecting the infills’ contribution under earthquake excitation are not recognized; (2) most of the design codes of practice do not provide guidelines for modelling the infilled frames; and (3) analytical infill models available in the literature are either too complicated to be implemented in the daily design process or too general to reflect realistic loading conditions or geometric configurations in real buildings. The primary objective of the proposed research is to investigate thoroughly the seismic behaviour and performance of reinforced concrete infilled frame structures under realistic three-dimensional loading conditions with consideration of the infills’ effects, thus developing efficient and practical, yet accurate, analytical models for seismic analysis and design of concrete infilled frame buildings. In the proposed studies, extensive numerical and computational investigations will be conducted to assess the seismic performance and identify the vulnerability of concrete infilled frame buildings. The development of analytical models is strictly based on scientific approaches in order to retain the generalisability and applicability of the results of analysis. Hong Kong has recently been classified as a region of moderate seismicity with the earthquake intensity VII. In view of the large number of infilled frame buildings in Hong Kong, the proposed research is expected to provide crucial guidance for designing safer and well-performing frame structures with infills under earthquake actions. Results and design recommendations of the proposed research are also expected to benefit the infrastructural development in other countries and regions that are threatened by earthquake disasters.

614011.label: Realisation of objectives
614011.value: The research project under the RGC-GRF grant number 614011 is very successfully completed. All four principal objectives of the research have been attained. This research has led to twelve(12) refereed journal papers, where seven have been published in the prestigious international journals and five are submitted for review and publication, and thirteen(13) refereed conference papers. On the basis of this study, performance criteria for identifying the vulnerability of reinforced concrete infilled frame structures, and relevant design recommendations have been made. Moreover, the paper “Simulations of masonry-infilled RC frames failure”, published in the journal of Engineering and Computational Mechanics, ICE, 166(4), 179-193 (Research Output journal paper No.: 2), has been awarded the prestigious Telford Premium form the Institution of Civil Engineers, UK, in 2014. The PI attended the award ceremony and received the award at the ICE Headquarters in London. For the Objective 1: The structural response of infilled frames subjected to combined in-plane and out-of-plane loading is usually analysed by applying separately in-plane and out-of-plane loads. Because the interaction effect of in-plane and out-of-plane loads on the structural behaviour of the frames is usually ignored in structural analysis, errors in predicting the actual force-transfer mechanisms and modes of failure of the structures can be incurred. In this investigation, a discrete finite element modelling technique in association with the proposed damage-based cohesive crack model of fracture behaviour of masonry infill is adopted to solve the problem. The force transfer mechanisms and failure modes of the anchored and unanchored infilled RC frames subjected to interactive in-plane and out-of-plane loads are studied. This investigation has led to two(2) journal papers, one published (Research Output journal paper No.: 4) and one submitted (Research Output journal paper No.: 9), and three(3) conference papers (Research Output conference paper No.: 2, 3, 5). For the Objective 2: A theoretical damage-based cohesive crack model is developed for the analysis and numerical/computational simulations of structural failure of masonry-infilled RC frames. The approach employs the surface-based interaction modelling technique to simulate the interfacial traction-separation behaviour, including instance mixed-modes of fracture, crack propagation, post-fractured behaviour, and finite sliding and separation of the bonded surfaces, between contacting surfaces of masonry units. Moreover, a Fourier-based incremental homogenisation technique is derived, where the macromicro transformations of mechanical variables are derived by incremental variational problems to minimise the potential energy in RVEs. This study has led to three(3) journal papers (Research Output journal paper No.: 1, 2, 3) and five(5) conference papers (Research Output conference paper No.: 1, 4, 6, 8, 13) published. The paper “Simulations of masonry-infilled RC frames failure”, Engineering and Computational Mechanics, ICE, 166(4), 179-193 (Research Output journal paper No.: 2), has been awarded the prestigious Telford Premium 2014 form the Institution of Civil Engineers, UK. For the Objective 3: Based on the developed theoretical models, the seismic responses and failure mechanisms of infilled RC-frame structures with irregular arrangement of infill panels are investigated. Two-bay and three-bay, two-storey, typical infilled RC frames with different infill configurations, including full infills, 2/3-storeyheight infills, soft first-storey, infills with window openings and infills with door openings, are studied. The nonlinear response history behaviour of masonry-infilled RC frames under realistic earthquakes is performed using discrete-finite element analysis with the proposed damage-based constitutive relations. This investigation has led to two(2) journal papers, one published (Research Output journal paper No.: 6) and one submitted (Research Output journal paper No. 8), and four(4) conference papers published (Research Output conference papers No.: 7, 9, 10, 12). For the Objective 4: Based on the findings of nonlinear responses and seismic vulnerability of infilled RC frame structures, performance criteria for identifying the vulnerability of structural walls, columns, and beam-column joints in RC frames are addressed and design recommendations are made. This study has led to six(6) journal papers, three published (Research Output journal paper No.: 3, 5, 7) and three submitted (Research Output journal paper No.: 10, 11, 12), and one(1) conference paper published (Research Output conference paper No.: 11).

614011.label: Major findings and research outcome
614011.value: (1) A theoretical damage-based cohesive crack model is developed for analysing structural failure of masonry-infill panels in RC frames subjected to reversed-cyclic loading. The approach is derived based on the surface-based interaction modelling technique to simulate the interfacial traction-separation behaviour, and able to simulate the mixed modes of fracture, crack propagation, post-fracture behaviour, and finite sliding and separation of the bonded surfaces. The failure modes and load-deformation behaviour of masonry-infilled frame structures are successfully captured. The wide variety of applications of the model in solving non-linear and complex structural analysis problems of masonry structures and infilled frames has been demonstrated. The research outcome: Journal papers No. 1, 2 and 3; Conference papers No. 1, 4, 6, 8 and 13. The journal paper No. 2 is awarded the prestigious Telford Premium 2014 form the Institution of Civil Engineers, UK. (2) Under the combined action of in-plane and out-of-plane loads, a small initial out-of-plane deflection can significantly be magnified owing to the result of the P–Delta effect. The diagonal compressive thrust induced by the in-plane lateral load and gravity loads of the infill wall acts as the destabilising force, which causes buckling of the infill wall. The bracing action of the bounding frame can be greatly weakened by out-of-plane loading, thus leading to reduction in the in-plane lateral strength and stiffness. The research outcome: Journal papers No. 4 and 9; Conference papers No. 2, 3 and 5. (3) Under seismic excitations, full infill panels enhance the overall stability and energy dissipation of frames, while those partially infilled experience severe damage due to the infill effect. Irregular arrangements of infill walls incur serious stress and damage localisation. Infilled frames with openings exhibit shakedown or ratcheting phenomena in hysteresis behaviour due to the propagation of sliding cracks around the corners of the openings. The capacity design concept of ‘‘strong column–weak beam’’ may not always be applicable to infilled frames due to the effect of infills on the bare frame. The research outcome: Journal papers No. 6 and 8; Conference papers No. 7, 9, 10 and 12. (4) Based on the findings of nonlinear responses and seismic vulnerability of infilled RC frame structures, performance criteria for identifying the vulnerability of structural walls, columns, and beam-column joints in RC frames are addressed and design recommendations are made. The research outcome: Journal papers No. 3, 5, 7, 10, 11 and 12; Conference paper No. 11.

614011.value: The theoretical damage-based cohesive crack model, which is developed in this research project and awarded the Telford Premium from ICE, for the analysis and numerical/computational simulations of structural failure of masonry-infilled RC frames can be enhanced and further modified as a general damage-friction model for analysing micro composite construction materials. The initial work on deriving the modified model has been started. The modified theoretical model will be applied for the analysis of general micro composites subjected to reversed-cyclic loading.

614311.value: 多任务稀疏建模中的高效率特征分组提取方法

614311.label: Project Objectives
614311.value: To allow the efficient and automatic discovery of feature groups from high-dimensional multi-label data.
rows: To allow the efficient and automatic discovery of feature groups from high-dimensional multi-label data.

614311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
614311.value: Machine learning plays an important role in today's computer and information systems technologies such as data mining, bioinformatics, electronic commerce, computer vision and information retrieval. However, with the increasing complexity of real-world applications, machine learning is now required to derive models from more difficult and more difficult data sets. A prominent question along this direction is how to handle data sets that are high-dimensional and contain many spurious features. For example, in text / webpage processing, a document is often represented as a high-dimensional feature vector, whose dimensionality is equal to the number of unique words in the corpus. Such a huge number of features easily leads to the curse of dimensionality. Hence, feature selection, which selects a relevant subset of features, is indispensable in managing real-world high-dimensional data. Over the years, the machine learning community has developed various methods to address this important problem. In particular, the so-called embedded approach, which integrates feature selection with training of the learner in the creation of a sparse model, has attracted a flurry of interest in recent years. However, these sparse modeling techniques, such as the famous lasso method, does not perform well when the features are highly correlated or exist as groups. Specifically, instead of selecting all the relevant groups of features, typically only one feature from each group will be selected. This can be problematic in many applications. For example, in bioinformatics, genes function in co-regulated groups. The discovery of the entire group is essential to the understanding of pathways in gene regulatory networks. Another application is the location of regions of interest (ROIs) in images. Take pedestrian detection as an example. It is essential to select all the pedestrian objects in the image as important features, rather than just randomly isolating only one of them. The goal of this proposal to make fundamental advances in feature selection and sparse modeling. We will investigate a new approach that can discover feature groups simultaneously with regression shrinkage in an automatic and efficient manner. Besides, many of the real-world data sets involve multiple tags or labels, we will also study how the myriad of intrinsic correlations among labels can be utilized in this sparse modeling process. 机器学习在数据挖掘、生物信息学、电子商务、计算机视觉和信息检索等现代计算机和信息系统技术中扮演着非常重要的角色。随着应用需求的不断发展，机器学习算法需要从越来越复杂的数据中提取有用的模型。其中一个严峻的问题是如何处理高维并且冗余的数据。例如，在文本和网页数据处理中，一篇文章通常被表示为一个维数等同于文章词汇量的高维特征向量，而这在多数机器学习技术会造成维数灾难。因此，特征选择作为一种降低维数的有效途径，在面对涉及高维数据的实际应用的时候是不可或缺的。 在过去几年中，机器学习领域的学者们提出了若干方法处理高维数据。其中有一类被称作“嵌入式”的算法受到广泛关注，因为它们可以同时进行特征选择以及模型训练，最终获得一个稀疏模型。然而，当前主流的稀疏模型训练方法如LASSO等，在数据高度耦合或者存在分组的情况下会降低精度。实际上，它们会任意选择一组高度耦合的特征中的某一个单独特征，而不是整个分组。这在一些实际应用中存在问题。例如在生物信息学中，一组基因（特征）通常表征一个特定的功能，人们希望得到包含若干组基因（而不是若干个基因）的模型因为它更容易解释观测到的现象。另一个例子是在图像兴趣区域检测中，选择画面中的所有行人作为兴趣区域比任意选择某个人作为特征更有意义。 这计划的目标是在特征选择和稀疏建模领域的取得根本性的进展。我们将研究一种新的方法，它可以在高效地训练回归问题的稀疏模型，同时自动发掘特征向量中的分组信息。此外，因为许多现实数据包含了多个标签或者分类，所以我们还将研究稀疏模型训练中如何利用这些标签或者分类中的耦合信息。

614311.label: Realisation of objectives
614311.value: We proposed an efficient feature grouping method in which feature groups can be automatically discovered simultaneously with regression shrinkage, without the need to pre-specify the grouping structure as in group lasso. Computationally, we show that its key step can be solved by a simple iterative group merging algorithm which is highly efficient. To discover the feature groups, complicated regularizers (such as a sum of simpler regularizers) are often required. In this project, we proposed an efficient solver for this kind of optimization problems, which reduces the approximation error much faster than the state-of-the-art. While convex regularizers are often used for sparse modeling of high-dimensional data, nonconvex regularizers often perform even better. However, the resulting optimization problems are often challenging. In this project, we proposed an efficient method for optimization with a wide class of nonconvex regularizers. This strategy has guaranteed convergence and low per-iteration complexity. Moreover, hierarchical and structural relationships among features are often useful in high-dimensional models. In this project, we proposed an efficient optimization solver that can be used to either directly solve the problem or serve as a key building block. We demonstrated that these hierarchical relationships consistently improve generalization performance and parameter estimation. For efficient learning, stochastic algorithms are often used. In this project, We proposed a new stochastic alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm, which incrementally approximates the full gradient. Besides having a low per-iteration complexity, it improves the convergence rate on convex problems, but without the need to visit all the samples in each iteration. Besides grouping the features, it is also desirable to group the labels. We proposed a novel multitask formulation that captures label relationships at the feature-level. Different label clusters are constructed for different features, and is thus more fine-grained than existing methods that only capture label-level relationships. Moreover, we do not require the number of clusters to be pre-specified. Computationally, the proposed formulation can be efficiently solved by accelerated proximal methods. Finally, another approach is to group the training and testing tasks together, so that knowledge learned from the training tasks can be used in learning the testing tasks. However, the training and testing data may follow different distributions. We proposed to match two data distributions in the Hilbert space, which is then formulated as a problem of aligning kernel matrices across domains. In particular, we introduced the concept of surrogate kernel based on the fundamental Mercer's theorem.

614311.label: Major findings and research outcome
614311.value: In this project, we proposed a number of efficient solvers for the automatic discovery of feature groups from high-dimensional multi-label data. Specifically, - We proposed an efficient feature grouping method to automatically discover feature groups simultaneously with regression shrinkage, without the need to pre-specify the grouping structure. Experimental results demonstrate that it achieves comparable accuracy as state-of-the-art methods on both regression and classification problems (conference paper #1). - We proposed an efficient accelerated gradient method. On both general convex and strongly convex problems, the resultant approximation errors reduce at a rate faster than existing methods. This is also verified experimentally on a number of data sets (conference paper #5). - We proposed an efficient proximal gradient descent method for learning with nonconvex regularizers. This has guaranteed convergence and low per-iteration complexity. Experimental results demonstrate its effectiveness and efficiency, and also improved classification performance resulting from the nonconvex regularizers (conference paper #3). - We proposed the use of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) and accelerated gradient methods to discover hierarchical and structural relationships among features in high-dimensional models. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm is efficient and flexible (conference paper #6). - We proposed a new stochastic ADMM algorithm, which incrementally approximates the full gradient in the linearized ADMM formulation. Besides having a low per-iteration complexity as existing stochastic ADMM algorithms, it improves the convergence rate on convex problems, but without the need to visit all samples in each iteration. Experiments demonstrate that the new algorithm is significantly faster than state-of-the-art stochastic and batch ADMM algorithms (conference paper #4). - We proposed an efficient multitask learning formulation to capture label relationships at the feature-level. Depending on the interactions among labels and features, the proposed method constructs different label clusters for different features. Computationally, it can be efficiently solved by accelerated proximal methods. Experiments show that the accuracy of the proposed method is consistently among the best. Moreover, the feature-specific task clusters obtained agree with the known/plausible task structures of the data (journal paper #1 and conference paper #1). - We proposed to group training and testing tasks together by first matching the training and testing data distributions in the Hilbert space, which is then formulated as a problem of aligning kernel matrices across domains. Promising results are reported on several real-world applications (conference paper #2).

614311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
614311.value: Most existing solvers on multi-task sparse modeling are designed for single machines. However, in this big data era, tons of data are being generated everyday. Hence, it is no longer possible to store or process all information on one single computer. Instead, the workload needs to be distributed across multiple machines. However, as many sparse modeling solvers are iterative in nature, they are not well suited for the popular MapReduce programming model. Hence, there is a need to develop more flexible distributed learning algorithms. In the future, we plan to extend the methods proposed in this proposal to distributed architectures, so that the above-mentioned deficiencies on big data analytics can be alleviated. In particular, we plan to develop a distributed sparse learning algorithm that (i) allows the master and workers to run asynchronously; (ii) is scalable, and allows computing nodes to be dynamically added/removed; and (iii) fault-tolerant, as nodes in cloud computing environments may occasionally fail.

614311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
614311.value: Machine learning plays an important role in today's computer and information systems technologies. However, many data sets that are high-dimensional and contain many spurious features. For example, in text / webpage processing, a document is often represented as a high-dimensional feature vector, whose dimensionality is equal to the number of unique words in the corpus. Such a huge number of features easily leads to the curse of dimensionality. Hence, feature selection or sparse modeling is often indispensable. In this project, we developed a number of efficient solvers for the automatic discovery of feature groups from high-dimensional data involving multiple task labels. We developed a number of theoretical results on these new methods. Experimental results on both synthetic and real-world data sets also show that the proposed methods significantly outperform the existing state-of-the-art.

615411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
615411.value: Advancements in material science and engineering have made possible the development of pseudo-ductile cementitious composites (PDCC) with tensile hardening behavior up to very high strain (3-5%). Also, tensile failure is accompanied by the formation of multiple fine cracks rather than a few widely opened cracks. With high ductility, crack control ability, high toughness and shear strength, as well as good energy absorption, the use of PDCC in practice has been growing. There is hence a strong interest to further improve the performance of PDCC. In currently available PDCC, only polymeric fibers such as polyethylene (PE) or polyvinylalcohol (PVA) have been employed, as high ductility can be achieved with a relative low fiber volume fraction (about 2%) of these fibers. Recent test results at HKUST indicate that the strength and ductility of PDCC components can be further improved by replacing a fraction of PVA fibers with micro-steel fibers. With this promising finding, a comprehensive investigation on hybrid PVA/steel PDCC is proposed. The physical basis behind the synergy between PVA and steel fibers is first investigated with fiber pull-out tests. The findings should be applicable to other hybrid composite systems. Then, an approach is developed to identify the contents of PVA and steel fibers for achieving pseudo-ductility. This will involve the development of a new model for fiber bridging force that accounts for the synergistic effect. Ductile hybrid composites will be prepared accordingly and tested to verify the applicability of the modeling approach. Then, two hybrid fiber PDCC compositions with high strength and high ductility will be prepared and tested under tension, compression and combined tension/shearing, with a novel testing system to be developed in this study. The combined tension/shear behavior of PDCC, which is important for structural analysis, has never been reported before. The development of the new testing system and the test results to be obtained are therefore of both fundamental and practical significance. Based on the test results, an existing model for combined tension-shear of PDCC will be verified or refined. Various structural members, fabricated with normal concrete, PDCC containing PVA alone as well as hybrid PVA/steel PDCC, will then be tested under monotonic or cyclic loading to highlight the advantage of hybrid PDCC. Experimental results will be compared to results from nonlinear finite element analysis to assess the applicability of numerical analysis in the design of components made with hybrid PDCC. 材料科學與工程技術的發展已使得高延性水泥基複合材料(PDCC)達到了很高的極限應變率(3-5%)。PDCC具有應變硬化的抗拉特性，拉伸破壞時形成多重開裂的微細裂縫，而不是少數幾條寬裂縫。由於具有高延性、開裂可控性、高韌性、高抗剪強度以及優良的吸能性能，PDCC在工程上的應用日益廣泛，因此進一步提高PDCC的性能具有重要意義。當前應用的PDCC 通常只採用相對較低摻量(體積含量約 2%)的聚合物纖維來改善其延性，如聚乙烯纖維(PE)和聚乙烯醇纖維(PVA)等。而香港科技大學的最新實驗結果表明，用一定比例的微細鋼纖維替代PVA纖維可進一步提高PDCC的強度和延性。基於這一重要發現，本課題將展開採用PVA和鋼纖維複摻技術進一步增強PDCC性能的全面研究。首先，採用纖維拔出實驗對PVA纖維與鋼纖維協同作用的物理機理進行研究，該結果亦可用於解釋其他採用複摻技術製作的複合材料的性能改善機制。其次，為了最大程度地提高延性，將發展一種確定PVA與鋼纖維最優摻量的方法。為此，考慮兩種不同類別纖維的協同效應，建立新的纖維橋接應力預測模型。通過製備和測試這種高延性的混摻纖維增強複合材料试件，驗證該模型方法的適用性。然後，製備高強、高韌性的混摻纖維增強複合材料试件，採用本研究中擬開發的新的測試系統對其進行抗拉、抗壓和拉/剪綜合性能實驗。PDCC在拉/剪綜合作用下的行為特性對於結構分析具有重要意義，但此前從未見相關報導。因此這套新的測試方法及其實驗結果將在基礎性和應用性方面具有雙重的重要意義。基於這些實驗結果對已有的PDCC拉/剪綜合性能計算模型進行驗證或修正。接下來，分別採用普通混凝土、只含PVA 纖維的PDCC和複摻PVA/鋼纖維的PDCC製作多種混凝土構件，對其進行單調加載和循環加載實驗，對比實驗結果以凸顯複摻纖維的PDCC 的優越性。進一步，將實驗結果與非線性有限元分析結果進行對照，以驗證採用數值方法進行複摻纖維PDCC構件設計的可行性。

615411.label: Realisation of objectives
615411.value: All the project objectives have been fully achieved. For objective 1, an experimental set-up for the performance of single fiber pull-out test and a method to prepare the pull-out specimens were developed. Pull-out specimens with a straight steel fiber lying at different angles (0, 30 and 60 degrees) to the pulling direction were prepared with pure cementitious matrix and matrix containing 1% or 2% of PVA fibers. Theoretically speaking, the pull-out force consists of a debonding component along the fiber, and a bending component perpendicular to the fiber. For the 0 degree case, the pull-out load, which arises from the debonding component alone, is slightly decreased with the addition of PVA fibers, due to the difficulty in compacting the fiber reinforced matrix in small specimens. For the 30 degree case, the pull-out load is similar for cases with and without PVA in the matrix, indicating that the increase in bending component compensates for the reduction in debonding component. The increase in bending component can be explained by the reduced matrix spalling (which occurs when the inclined fiber is bent on the matrix) due to the toughening effect of PVA fiber on the matrix surrounding the steel fiber. For the 60 degree case, the pull-out load is higher for the cases with PVA in the matrix. This is because matrix spalling is more severe for this case and the reduced spalling due to the presence of PVA over-compensates for the smaller debonding component. In addition to straight fibers, we have also performed testing on fibers with hooked ends. When the end of hook is near the specimen surface, the addition of PVA fibers into the matrix can again reduce spalling and increase the pull-out load. For objective 2, a computational model is developed to analyze the pull-out behavior. The model is based on a former model developed by the PI for an elastoplastic fiber embedded inside a brittle matrix which will undergo spalling once a critical stress (sc) is reached. To modify the existing model, the matrix foundation is taken to exhibit softening behavior. After reaching sc, the foundation reaction will decrease linearly with a slope k. For different contents of PVA fiber in the matrix, values of sc and k are obtained by fitting the test results for the 30 degree case, and the same set of values are able to predict the pull-out curve and extent of spalling for the 60 degree case. The modelling approach is hence validated. Theoretical simulations are then performed with the new model to find the average bridging stress vs crack opening relation for PDCC with various steel/PVA combinations. For cases with available experimental data (obtained under objective 3), reasonable agreement between theoretical and test results can be achieved. For objective 3, plate and cube specimens have been prepared with various compositions of PDCC, containing PVA fibers alone as well as both steel and PVA fibers. The plate specimens were tested in direct tension to obtain the full tensile stress vs strain behavior. A very interesting observation from the tensile tests is that while the pure PVA fiber case often gives a higher tensile ductility, the use of hybrid steel/PVA fibers can result in a larger number of cracks with smaller crack width at the same strain. In other words, if very high ductility up to several percent is not necessary, the use of hybrid fiber can result in a member with better durability. Using the cube specimens, compressive strength was measured. While ductility is the major concern in designing PDCC, the compressive strength has to reach a certain level (e.g., 45MPa) for the material to be used in structural components. Based on our test results, compositions with good ductility (over 1%) and compressive strength above 45MPa have been developed. Besides the determination of direct tensile behavior, we are also interested in finding the bridging stress vs crack opening relation of the material. Conventionally, this is obtained from a plate specimen with a notch cut along one of its sections. A displacement transducer is placed across the notched section and the bridging stress vs crack opening relation is obtained from the load vs displacement curve. This method has the limitation that multiple cracks often form within the gauge length of the displacement transducer so the crack opening is significantly overestimated. In this study, we have developed a new technique based on photography and digital signal processing to find the opening of cracks at different load levels. This method enables the determination of stress vs crack opening relation at various sections of the member and thus allows one to also study the variation of this relation over the material. For PDCC, both our own results and results in the literature show that the tensile ductility may vary significantly for some mixes. To control the variation, an important step is to come up with a theoretical model that can predict the ductility from basic material parameters such as properties of fiber, matrix and interface as well as fiber volume and flaw size distribution in the matrix. One can then perform sensitivity analysis to see which parameter(s) will have the largest effect on ductility and control them accordingly. Although not part of the original proposal, such a model, which should be useful for optimizing the mix design of PDCC, has been developed. For objective 4, beam members were prepared for flexural tests and double-notched specimens (with constant shear force acting on the notched section) were employed for the shear test. Bending test results show higher ductility for the case with pure PVA fiber but higher stress at similar deformation for the case with hybrid fibers. In other words, if the deformation of a component is not excessive (i.e., still within the limit of the hybrid fiber PDCC), the hybrid fiber PDCC will have higher energy absorption. In shear, the hybrid fiber PDCC always performs better than the PVA PDCC. This can be explained by the higher stiffness of steel fiber which increases the resistance to the shear sliding of cracks. For objective 5, nonlinear finite element analysis of the specimens tested under objective 4 has been carried out with the program ATENA, which has the constitutive model of PDCC implemented. Using the measured bridging stress vs crack opening relation as input, the trend of bending behavior can be well predicted. For the shear behavior, results for the pure PVA case can be properly modelled but those for the hybrid fibers cannot be correctly predicted. This is not surprising because the constitutive model in the ATENA program is based on simple micromechanics which have not considered the possibility of using two different fibers. Through the comparison of numerical and experimental results, the objective of assessing the applicability of existing finite element approaches can be achieved. However, future studies should be carried out to improve the model in ATENA to make it applicable to hybrid fiber PDCC.

615411.label: Major findings and research outcome
615411.value: In this research study, a new model has been developed to derive the complete tensile stress vs strain relation of PDCC, as well as the crack spacing and width under different strain levels. The model provides an useful tool for the selection of material parameters to maximize ductility for energy absorption or minimize crack width under service condition for durability enhancement. Moreover, sensitivity studies can be carried out with the model to identify the factor with the largest effect on PDCC ductility, so it can be controlled in the fabrication process. Details of the work can be found in Journal Paper 1 of Part C. In most work on PDCC reported in the literature, the compressive strength of the material is 40MPa or below, making it inapplicable to tall buildings and major infrastructure which require Grade 45 concrete, the mean strength of which should be around 55MPa. We have developed new compositions of PDCC that can fulfil such a requirement. Details can be found in Journal Paper 2 of Part C. A new photographic method and a novel digital signal processing technique have been developed for the quantitative monitoring of crack number and crack width during the direct tensile test. These are very useful for the studying of PDCC and details can be found in Journal Paper 3 of Part C. Testing on PDCC members under direct tension and shear shows that while PDCC made with pure PVA often shows higher ductility, hybrid steel/PVA fiber PDCC exhibits more cracks with smaller spacing under the same strain before crack localization. As the localization strain is much higher than that under serviceability condition, the better crack control capability of hybrid fiber PDCC can enhance the durability of structural components. Also, the use of hybrid fiber is found to improve the performance of structural members under shear. These novel findings are reported in Conference Paper 3 of Part C. Results of fiber pull-out test show that the presence of smaller PVA fiber in the matrix can reduce local matrix spalling failure around the larger steel fiber. The synergistic effect of hybrid fibers has been reported in many previous studies, but a physical explanation is given for the first time. Details can be found in Conference Paper 4 of Part C.

615411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
615411.value: In this study, a major limitation on the hybrid fiber composite is found. Conventional finite element analysis of PDCC cannot properly model the shear behavior of PDCC components. This is mainly due to the simplification of crack bridging mechanism which assumes the part of fiber between the crack faces to be under pure shear, while the matrix surrounding the fiber stays undeformed. To improve the model, important micro-mechanisms such as (i) bending of the fiber with the matrix acting as a deformable foundation and (ii) plausible matrix spalling under high local stresses need to be considered. In addition, large deformation analysis of the fiber is required when the crack opening is small. The improvement of the micromechanical model is a major part of a new GRF proposal submitted by the PI to RGC in 2015. On the application side, the enhanced shear capacity of hybrid steel/PVA steel PDCC should make it useful for applications where failure occur under complex stress fields with significant shear effects, such as anchor bolts or regions of concentrated stress. We plan to perform experiments on such members to verify the advantage of hybrid fiber PDCC. Based on the preliminary results, industrial funding will be applied.

615411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
615411.value: PDCC is a kind of fiber reinforced cementitious composites with very high ductility under tension as well as the ability to control crack opening to very small values under service loading conditions. In practical applications, the high ductility gives rise to high energy absorption during impact and earthquakes to enhance structural safety, while the crack control is beneficial to durability as water and chemical penetration will not be expedited by the wide opening of cracks. As PDCC is a relatively new material, there is still a lot of room to improve its performance/cost. In this work, instead of using PVA fibers alone as in most conventional PDCCs, we study the use of hybrid steel and PVA fibers in the material. The results show that components made with hybrid PDCC exhibits better crack control under service condition as well as enhanced shear capacity under ultimate loading. As part of the work, a new model relating PDCC ductility and crack width to micro-parameters of the composite, and a new experimental technique to study the cracking process in PDCC, have been developed. These will be very useful for future studies on the mechanical behavior of PDCC.

615911.value: 双渠道收益管理的最优化定价和定量决策

615911.label: Project Objectives
615911.value: Help quantify the benefit/cost of a dual channel strategy and develop a firm’s channel strategy optimization model by incorporating customer channel choice behavior endogenously. Develop a theoretical rationale to better understand how a firm’s channel structure is affected by market characteristics and customer search behavior, and provide insights into how the firm may use rationing as a strategic tool to profitably segment the market. Examine the impact of the relationship/competition among different channel members on the firm’s operational decisions and the choice of channel structure, gaining insights into the role of public policy in regulating business conduct in a multiple-channel environment.

615911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
615911.value: Firms have been selling their products through different channels to reach a large base of potential buyers. For example, premium luxury goods such as luxury watches and bags are sold both through an exclusive distribution of their own boutique stores and at some selective major watch and jewellery companies, such as Prince, Oriental, Emperor in Hong Kong. The introduction of independent retailers provides the firm with an opportunity to increase the total market share. However, this comes at the expense of demand cannibalization from the existing direct sales channel due to competition. An interesting question arises of whether a firm should view the addition of an independent retailer as harmful competition, or a useful mechanism for segmenting the market profitably. In the proposed project, we look at a dual channel revenue management problem in which both a direct store and an independent retailer offer a homogeneous product at different prices and availability risk. We will first study customer search and purchase behavior and integrate the customer channel choice model with the firm’s operational decisions. We will then investigate the firm’s optimal pricing and capacity decisions in each channel, and particularly explore the role of rationing in the choice of channel structure. We will also examine how the firm’s channel strategy is affected by market composition, customer search behavior, and retail competition. Finally, we will conduct experiments to simulate customer search behavior and channel choice decision in order to validate the proposed model and its predictions. The successful completion of the project will provide decision-makers with insights into the strategic role that rationing plays in profitably influencing customer channel choice behavior and thus the resulting firm’s channel strategy. 为增加市场占有率，很多企业采取多种渠道的销售方式。例如，有些奢侈品牌产品既在专营店也在零售店销售。但是多渠道销售另一方面也引入渠道竞争以至于某些客户转向价格优惠的零售店。那么，多渠道销售到底是利大于弊还是弊大于利呢？这正是我们项目所要解决的主要问题。具体来说， 我们考虑一个企业有专营店和零售商两种销售渠道。两种渠道销售同一产品，但是价格不同。通常情况下，零售商的价格低于专营店，特别是奢侈品牌。此外，两种渠道的供货率也不一样，零售店的供货率要低于专营店。消费者为获取价格优惠，通常要尝试多个零售店才能买到理想的产品。那么，哪些消费者选择从专营店购买产品，哪些消费者选择从零售店购买？ 这是我们首要研究的消费者选择购买模型。基于消费者的购买行为，我们进一步研究企业在各个渠道的定价和定量决策，以及消费群体和市场竞争如何影响企业的定价和定量决策。 可能的话，我们要用实验仿真消费者的购买行为以验证模型。我们预见项目的成功实施可以帮助企业更好的理解如何用供货率来影响消费购买行为从而优化收益。

615911.label: Realisation of objectives
615911.value: We first study a dual channel revenue management problem in which a firm manages a direct sales channel and an independent retail channel. We analyze consumer search and purchase behavior under a dual channel structure and how it affects the firm's optimal pricing and capacity rationing decisions in each channel. Particularly, to capture customers’ search and purchasing decision, we use the micro-level utility model to formulate the expected payoff that a customer earns from purchasing at different channels. We then divide purchase outcomes of customers to four cases, depending on which segment (high or low) of customers to purchase from which channel, and whether they obtain the product or not. We then incorporate customer channel selection decision into the firm’s pricing and capacity rationing decisions. We consider both the centralized system (the firm owns the retailer store) and the decentralized system (the firm does not own the retailer store). Under the centralized system, we fully characterize the firm’s optimal prices for the direct channel and the independent retailer, and how to allocate capacity to each sale channel. In the decentralized system, the firm acts as the wholesaler and determines the wholesale price charged to the retailer, and each of them maximizes his own expected profit. To gain further insights into the impact of channel structure on customer’s search behavior and firms’ pricing and capacity allocation decision, we analyze two extensions: (1) Customers who do not obtain products at the retail store may not return to the direct channel. To tackle this problem, we introduce a returning probability and analyze its impact. (2) The firm introduces multiple independent retailers to facilitate the search of customers. We can analyze the problem under a symmetric distribution of retailers. To further explore the role of capacity rationing in affecting strategic purchasing behavior of customers, we study another problem of a firm selling products over two periods including a full price period and a markdown period. However, customers do not have rational expectations on rationing risk. We adopt the anecdotal reasoning model that is widely used in the economics literature to model such bounded rationality. That is, customers use a limited number of samples to form their estimates of rationing risk. We characterize the firm’s capacity rationing decision under both capacity commitment and dynamic capacity settings.

615911.label: Major findings and research outcome
615911.value: One major finding is that, in a dual channel, the firm normally charges a higher price in its direct channel than the retailer store does. However, in order to mitigate the demand cannibalization effect, the firm may create capacity rationing at the retail store. The optimal rationing level depends on the composition of the market, search cost of customers, and the channel structure. Particularly, we find that, in a centralized system, when the valuations of high-end segment and the low-end segment differ large, the firm should allocated limited capacity and induce rationing at the retail store. Meanwhile, the firm is able to fully extract consumer surplus from high-end customers in a direct channel. Otherwise, the firm should allocate enough capacity to the retail store and satisfy all its demand. This is however accompanied by a reduced price charged in the direct channel. In a decentralized system, the firm generally should not involve the retailer unless the high-end segment has only slightly higher valuations than the low-end segment, and it has a large market share. Another interesting result is on the impact of retailer competition. In a market with symmetric retailers, as the number of competing retailers becomes larger, a smaller amount of rationing is required if rationing is optimal; the direct channel has to lower the price to attract high-value customers if rationing is not optimal. Please see the paper Optimal Pricing and Capacity Strategies in Dual Channel Revenue Management for details. When customers do not have perfect information about rationing, instead they form boundedly rational expectations in the sense of anecdotal reasoning, we prove that strategic capacity rationing is generally not optimal. This result is in stark contrast to the exiting literature that shows that capacity rationing is an effective tool to counteract the negative effects of strategic customer behavior. Our results reveal that, when customers do not have full information about rationing, which is often the case in reality, the firm should be cautious about creating rationing deliberately. Please refer to the paper Strategic Capacity Management When Customers Have Boundedly Rational Expectations for details. On a related topic, we study customer choice behavior when a firm offers a menu of probabilistic goods based on a limited number of physical items. We propose a time-based fluid policy to solve the problem. Please refer to the paper Managing a Portfolio of Probabilistic Goods for details.

615911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
615911.value: Possible directions for the further development of this work are the following: (1) The composition of the market can be further generalized to finer segmentation rather than two point distribution as in the current model. Furthermore, the market size can be uncertain. This will help reveal the effect of heterogeneity of the market and the role of demand uncertainty in determining the firm’s pricing and capacity rationing decisions in dual channel. (2) We can conduct empirical and/or experimental studies to measure the search cost of different types of customers, and the likelihood of returning to the direct channel if a customer fails to obtain the product in a discount retailer. (3) Regarding how to model customer’s boundedly rational behavior, anecdotal reasoning is one of the commonly used and natural approaches. There are several other alternatives, for example, level-k thinking and the experienced-weighted attraction learning. It is interesting to employ these different approaches to model how customers form their estimates about rationing level and thus the firm’s capacity rationing decisions, and compare the results.

615911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
615911.value: Firms introduce alternative sales channels (e.g. independent retail stores) besides their own stores in order to reach a large base of potential buyers. Meanwhile, the addition of independent retailers introduces competition. In this project, we mainly analyze such tradeoff. We study a problem of the firm selling the same product via both a direct store and an independent retailer. We characterize customer search and purchase behavior and integrate customer channel choice into the firm’s pricing and capacity rationing decisions. We find that, whether the firm sells products in dual channel depends on capacity level and the ownership of the retailer. In the case of the firm owning the retail store, it should only sell at the direct store when it has limited capacity and customers differ largely in valuations; otherwise, the firm should introduce the retail store with a lower price coupled with rationing risk. When the firm does not own the retailer store, we show that the firm in general should not involve the retailer unless customer valuations differ slightly and the high-end segment has a large market share. We also investigate how the firm’s channel strategy is affected by market composition, customer search behavior, and retail competition.

616611.label: Project Objectives
616611.value: To iteratively design, fabricate and test liquid crystals so as to develop a novel LC that has a high birefringence at terahertz frequencies and can be switched in seconds. To achieve high quality LC alignment using existing alignment technology including photo-alignment developed at HKUST. To incorporate our new liquid crystal into a spatial modulator consisting of a matrix of liquid crystal cells that can be switched on or off to create different patterns. To modify our existing compressed sensing algorithms to match with the newly developed liquid crystal spatial modulator. To incorporate all the above into a terahertz system that can be used in either reflection or transmission geometry to image an area of a sample by switching the cells of the spatial modulator. To tailor the system for imaging of medical samples.

616611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
616611.value: We propose to develop a new approach to speed up terahertz image data acquisition and reduce the need for sample scanning with medical applications in mind. Our new method combines cutting edge liquid crystal (LC) technology with compressed sensing algorithms. Recent research has shown that existing LCs can shift the phase of terahertz light. However the reported LCs do not cause a large refractive index change (birefringence) at terahertz frequencies and so a thick layer of the LC is needed to create a half-wavelength phase change. The thicker the LC, the more difficult it is to achieve crystal alignment and the longer the switching time. We therefore propose to design and fabricate a novel LC that will have high birefringence at terahertz frequencies. We then propose to use the phase shifting properties of the LC to create a series of patterned spatial modulators which block out terahertz light. The pattern will be controlled by switching cells of a matrix composed of the LC. Although LC technology has been employed in compressed sensing masks for optical imaging modalities, it is a great challenge to design and fabricate a suitable LC for terahertz frequencies. Compressed sensing exploits the sparsity of an image: if an image is sparse (ie lacking in complexity) it can be reconstructed using fewer measurements than the number of pixels. This is particularly relevant to medical screening and diagnosis where the majority of tissue will be normal and homogenous, but small areas of tissue that are not normal may be present. These abnormal areas will be highlighted using our compressed sensing algorithms. Furthermore, in our proposed method, the sample will remain in a fixed position throughout all measurements: only the LC pattern on the spatial modulator will change. This again would be of benefit to medical imaging applications as patients could stand still and be imaged with the only movement being silent changes of the LC – unlike for instance, the loud noises from magnets switching positions in magnetic resonance imaging. With the interdisciplinary expertise of our team (terahertz imaging, LCs, signal processing and medical imaging), we are well positioned to make the first terahertz imaging system incorporating LC technology for compressed sensing. This will greatly advance terahertz imaging for many applications, especially medical imaging. 我们研究出一种新的方法以加快太赫兹图像数据采集和降低样本扫描的需要,并打算应用在医疗方面。我们的新方法将先进的液晶（LC）技术以及压缩传感算法相结合从而达到我们的要求。 最近的研究表明，现有的液晶能够使太赫兹光的相位转移。但是报告中的液晶并不能在太赫兹频率的范围内产生大的折射率变化（双折射），所以需要一层厚的液晶创造一个半波长的相变。液晶层越厚，就越难实现晶体的排列并且开关时间越长。因此，我们建议，设计和制造一种新的液晶层，使其在太赫兹频率范围内产生高双折射。然后，我们建议使用液晶相位转移的属性来创造一系列的不同的图案的空间调制器来阻断太赫兹光线.通过开关一个由液晶组成的方阵中的不同小格子,我们可以控制图案的变化。虽然液晶技术已使用在压缩传感膜上进行光学成像应用，设计和制造一个合适的液晶品种应用在太赫兹频率上仍是一个巨大的挑战。 压缩传感利用了图像稀疏的特性：如果图像是稀疏的（即缺乏复杂性），那么仅仅使用比像素数更少的测量数就可以重构这个图像。这个特性与医学甄别以及诊断密切相关,尤其是当大部分组织是正常且同质的,但有小部分面积并非这样的时候。这些不正常的地方将通过使用压缩传感算法被突出。此外，在我们提出的方法中，样品将在整个测量过程中保持固定.只有在空间调制器上的液晶图案会产生变化。这将给医疗成像应用带来的好处，比如病人可以静止站立而只需要无声的变换液晶图案就可以. 这并不像以往的情景,例如在核磁共振中不断变换磁体的位置以及其中产生的巨大噪音。 我们团队丰富的跨学科专业知识（液晶技术，太赫兹成像，信号处理和医疗成像），使我们处于有利位置创造第一个结合使用压缩传感以及液晶技术的太赫兹成像系统。这个系统将大大推进太赫兹成像在许多方面的应用，尤其是医疗成像。

616611.label: Realisation of objectives
616611.value: Objectives 1 and 2 have been fully achieved. This took longer than expected primarily due to difficulties in fabrication of the liquid crystal (LC) cells, long switching times and safely operating the cell with high voltages. Problems overcome included leaking liquid cells – this impeded the first stage of the project when identifying LCs with high birefringence, high transmission and good elasticity. Having identified a suitable liquid crystal for our spatial light modulator design, we worked on trying to improve the switching speed as although we could actively switch it quickly in one direction, the relaxation time for it to switch back was very slow due to the high thickness of the LC layer. We successfully used our expertise in photoalignment to fabricate the desired thicknesses of LC layers but to make a useful spatial light modulator we needed to improve the switching time. To address this issue we worked on our “Terahertz in Plane and Terahertz Out-of-Plane (TIP-TOP) Switching Liquid Crystal Devices” idea and a US patent was awarded. This improved the switching speed as it employs a novel electrode design to enable the LC to be switch actively in both directions thus switching significantly faster than via the relaxation process. Fabrication of the LC cell remained a challenge as, not only did we have to be careful to avoid leakage of the LC due to problems with both the sealant and window material, but we also needed to make sure the novel electrodes were carefully aligned. It took much longer than expected to demonstrate the switching of a LC spatial light modulator element at switching speeds of less than 2 seconds, but we managed this just before the end of the project in March 2014. Meanwhile, we prepared our THz system such that a spatial light modulator could be incorporated in transmission or reflection geometry. We did not fully modify the compressed sensing algorithms as they need to be based around an array of the LC cells, however we progressed all preparations as far as possible.

616611.label: Major findings and research outcome
616611.value: Major finding: We designed, fabricated and tested a liquid crystal cell that is able to provide a useful phase shift at THz frequencies AND be switched electronically in both directions within hundreds of milliseconds. The total switching cycle of the device was found to be less than 750 ms in total, leading to a greater than 40 times decrease in switching time when compared with the relaxation time of over 30 seconds. Five journal articles relating to the project have been published in international journals. Article 3 explains how we evaluated liquid crystal materials for suitability for use at THz frequencies. We identified the LC RDP 94990 as a good choice due to its low attenuation of THz light, high birefringence and fast switching time. Since separating out the ordinary and extraordinary components of THz light is important in this project, we have also developed some high transmission and high extinction ratio THz polarizers. The polariser properties and fabrication are detailed in journal publications 1,2 and 4 and an invited talk was also given at the IRMMW-THz 2012 conference held in Australia (conference list, item 1). This project has received international recognition in the liquid crystal research field – we have been invited to present findings at international conferences such as SPIE Photonics West 2012 (conference list, items 4&5) as well as to give invited talks at conferences in Hong Kong and China including at The Biomedical Engineering International Conference, Hong Kong Dec 2014 and The Chinese International Optoelectronic Conference (CIOEC), Shenzhen, Sept 2014.

616611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
616611.value: This project has opened up further avenues of research to optimise the switching speed. It has led to an ITF project to pursue the electrode design further. This will enable our spatial light modulator work even faster in future, along with minimising insertion loss of the device in THz systems. In addition, more advanced compressive imaging algorithms can be investigated to further optimise image acquisition speeds. Potential research into more optimised liquid crystal materials and mixtures is another additional avenue of research, which has yet to be done at THz frequencies.

616611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
616611.value: Imaging at THz frequencies, which is traditionally slow, can be speeded up by using a novel liquid crystal (LC) device, which changes the orientation of the liquid crystal and employs specially designed algorithms (compressive imaging) to reconstruct the image. Such LC devices are routinely used at visible frequencies but not yet at THz frequencies due to needing thicker layers of liquid crystal which in turn causes slow switching of the orientation. Our novel device performs active switching of the LC orientation for the first time in both directions, which significantly speeds up switching. This switching allows the device to modulate an incident THz beam, and thus compressive imaging can be used. This is significant, as it can lead to the potential for real-time medical THz imaging and can be retro-fitted to the majority of existing systems.

616911.value: 多输入多输出系统能够大幅度地提高通信系统容量，而不需要消耗额外的能量和带宽资源。在过去十年中，此技术引发了无线通信工业的革命。为了追求更高的数据速率和更优的系统性能，同时适应不同应用的需要，许多先进而通用的多输入多输出技术被提出来。其中一些重要的例子包括多用户多输入多输出技术，协作多输入多输出中继技术，以及协作多蜂窝处理技术。这些方法利用经典的多输入多输出技术的基本优势来提供额外的性能提升，例如改善系统的可靠性，扩大系统的覆盖范围，和提高系统对网络干扰的健壮性。这三项技术不仅成为理论研究的焦点，并且得到了工业界的广泛注意，将被整合到下一代和未来的无线通信标准中。 尽管对其有着很高的预期，为了使通用的多输入多输出技术能够在现实生活中被广泛地应用，我们仍然需要做很多的工作。和传统无线系统设计一样，基于一个严格的信息论框架去分析通信链路的极限非常关键。这对于帮助系统设计和提供性能指标也非常重要。这个框架尤其需要提供适用于非各态历经系统的度量，例如与实际应用相关的中断概率，分集复用折中，有限长度编码方案的极限性能等。但是，我们对于通用的多输入多输出系统中的这些度量仍然所知有限。在此，我们提议对这一重要但仍有待研究的问题进行解决。 建立通用的多输入多输出系统的非各态历经的信息论极限非常困难。从技术上来说，主要的挑战是评估有效信道互信息量的分布式特性；现有的方法似乎无法解决这一问题。我们将从随机矩阵理论领域引入两项最新的强大技术来解决这一问题。这两项技术都已被运用于统计物理并取得了巨大的成功。第一种方法基于研究正交多项式和随机矩阵特征值分布之间的内在联系；第二种方法基于探究随机矩阵的极限特征值分布和库仑流体中带电粒子的平衡密度之间的紧密联系。在最近的文章[1]中，PI和Co-I证明了这两种方法都具有很大的潜力，并且取得了一些适用于单用户多输入多输出系统的初期成果。本项目旨在将这些初期工作扩展到通用的多输入多输出技术中。 通过研究通用的多输入多输出系统的基本信息论极限，本项目的结果可能会在未来无线网络应用的设计中起到关键作用。

616911.label: Realisation of objectives
616911.value: All key objectives have been successfully met. The project has produced numerous key contributions, and has led to international journal and conference publications. Objective 1: This substantial objective was aimed at characterizing the fundamental non-ergodic information-theoretic limits of MIMO communication techniques. Numerous important contributions were made. [Journal Paper 1] presented a comprehensive analytic framework for characterizing the outage performance of both single- and multi-user MIMO systems. This was a substantial contribution, comprising over 40 pages in double-column IEEE format, and was published in one of the best journals in the field: the IEEE Transactions on Information Theory. The framework was further developed in a second major contribution in the same journal, [Journal Paper 2], as well as a substantial IEEE conference publication [Conference Paper 1]. This paper was selected as a Finalist for the Best Student Paper Award at the Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems, and Computers, which is a major international conference in the general field of signal processing. In these papers, advanced methods from statistical physics were introduced for the first time to the communications and information theory field, producing new closed-form formulae for the non-ergodic communication limits of MIMO systems. Objective 2: This objective aimed to give a preliminary study of more advanced MIMO configurations. Numerous models were investigated, including relaying systems, and it was found that the toolbox developed in relation to Objective 1 could be potentially applied. The non-ergodic performance of multi-user MIMO configurations with arbitrary unequal power interferers was also studied, under very general fading conditions. Fundamental outage results were derived for such models, under practical beamforming strategies, leading to a substantial contribution, [Journal Paper 4]. Objective 3: This objective aimed to introduce new powerful analytical tools to the wireless communications and information theory communities. This was successfully achieved. [Journal Paper 1] and [Journal Paper 2] introduced completely new tools from statistical physics, based on the so-called Coulomb Fluid and Ladder Operator approaches, which delivered the first comprehensive characterization of the non-ergodic limits of both single-user and multi-user MIMO systems. Numerous other tools from random matrix theory were also applied, including stochastic eigen-analysis methods in [Journal Paper 4]. An additional major contribution, [Journal Paper 3], utilized advanced random matrix tools to exactly characterize the so-called Demmel condition number distribution of certain random matrices arising in MIMO systems, which are useful for designing adaptive transmission strategies.

616911.label: Major findings and research outcome
616911.value: Below is a brief summary of the major findings in each of the journal papers: [Journal Paper 1]: This paper introduced a completely novel framework for characterizing the non-ergodic performance limits of MIMO communication systems. The framework employed two powerful approaches from statistical physics: The Coulomb Fluid approach and the Ladder Operator approach. The framework was applied to both single-user and multi-user systems, establishing deep connections between the outage capacity and classical Painleve differential equations. Under certain cases, new exact expansions for the moments of the capacity distribution were derived in closed-form. [Journal Paper 2]: This paper presented an extensive elaboration of the framework developed in Journal Paper 1; deriving new exact expansions for the cumulants of the MIMO capacity distribution. This in turn provided the first unified characterization of MIMO outage capacity, which bridged the gap between existing finite and asymptotic (large antenna) results in the literature. In particular, it was demonstrated, for the first time, scenarios for which the well-known Gaussian approximation is valid, and scenarios for which it fails remarkably (i.e., when the signal-to-noise ratio is sufficiently high). New analytical expressions were also derived for the tail distribution using large deviations techniques, which substantially corrected the well-known Gaussian approximation. The proposed framework was also shown to reveal the classical diversity-multiplexing tradeoff; further emphasizing the flexibility and power of the proposed approach. [Journal Paper 3]: This paper presented an exact and asymptotic study of the so-called Demmel condition number of complex Wishart random matrices, which are representative of MIMO communication channels. These mathematical results are useful for designing adaptive MIMO transmission techniques, and for designing robust spectrum sensing methods for MIMO cognitive radio applications. [Journal Paper 4]: This paper considered a very general multi-user MIMO scenario with arbitrary numbers of interferers having arbitrary powers, and under very general double-scattering fading considerations. In particular, an exact non-ergodic performance characterization was presented for multi-user beamforming techniques, by deriving exact expressions for the outage probability of each of the eigen-beamforming subchannels. These results were employed to gain fundamental insight into system performance; for example, to characterize the diversity order achieved under different fading conditions, to investigate the impact of the channel scatterers on the bandwidth requirements for a given transmission rate and power, among other results.

616911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
616911.value: There are numerous avenues for further development. In particular, the novel framework introduced for characterizing the non-ergodic (outage) limits of MIMO systems, thus far, is limited to communication channels with statistically-independent fading. In some practical scenarios, particularly those with antenna space constraints, this condition will be violated. Thus, the extension of the proposed methods, based on the Coulomb Fluid and Ladder Operator approaches, will be required in order to handle channel correlation. This is a difficult problem, and is one that has received little attention, even in the statistical physics literature. One promising approach could be to exploit very recent results arising in the multi-variate statistics literature based on so-called “spiked” random matrix models. This will be considered in the future. The results of this project may also be potentially extended to characterize the non-ergodic information-theoretic limits of large-scale wireless ad-hoc networks, by combining the Coulomb Fluid and Ladder Operator tools with advanced tools from stochastic geometry (i.e., to characterize network configuration). This is a very substantial and challenging problem, and one which could form the basis of a major subsequent project.

616911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
616911.value: Information theory provides a means of specifying the ultimate communication limits (i.e., the highest possible reliable transmission rates) of communication systems. This is critical, since once the achievable limits are known they can serve as an important benchmark for the design of practical technologies. This project focused on characterizing the communication limits for MIMO wireless systems, which utilize antenna arrays at both the transmitter and receiver. Such systems are representative of most current or emerging wireless standards. A key contribution was to provide a novel and powerful analytical framework which captured the communication limits of MIMO systems, by introducing tools from the field of statistical physics. This completely novel framework led to a clear understanding of the information-theoretic capabilities of MIMO systems under different conditions, which can help to facilitate new technology research and development. The proposed framework and associated results provided a unified theory encapsulating existing results in the literature as special cases. The project also investigated practical MIMO transmission techniques, providing practical insights under general modeling assumptions. The tools introduced in this project are fundamental, and they could potentially be utilized for the design and analysis of many more advanced MIMO communication scenarios.

617511.label: Project Title(Chinese)
617511.value: 基坑開挖對既有隧道影響的三維離心機模擬

617511.label: Project Objectives
617511.value: To investigate and understand the three-dimensional stress transfer and deformation mechanisms of a newly excavated deep basement on an existing tunnel in sand and clay. To study the influence of a deep basement excavation on an existing tunnel by considering key dimensionless groups including excavation width to depth ratio, aspect ratio (i.e., width to length on plan), cover-to-tunnel diameter ratios inside and outside the excavation site, relative stiffness of retaining wall to soil, and normalised distance between an existing tunnel and retaining wall by tunnel diameter. To provide high quality and comprehensive three-dimensional centrifuge test data for verifying numerical models and modelling procedures. To study and understand the mechanisms of basement-tunnel interactions by carrying out three-dimensional finite element back-analyses of centrifuge model tests. To develop design guidelines by carrying out parametric centrifuge model tests and numerical parametric analyses. To obtain high quality field monitoring data to verify centrifuge and numerical modelling results and findings and hence to improve design guidelines for the construction of deep basements adjacent to existing tunnels.

617511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
617511.value: Rapid and sustainable development in congested urban cities such as Hong Kong, Shanghai, Taipei and London often require efficient use of underground spaces for shopping centres and carparks. Underground basement construction not only can meet the demand of usable floor areas but it also reduces environmental impacts. For the convenience of shoppers and users, there is an increasing demand for the construction of deep basements close to or directly above existing tunnel lines. Any excavation for the construction of deep basements retained even by diaphragm walls will inevitably cause stress changes in the ground leading to ground movements in both horizontal and vertical directions. Damage to existing tunnels is often reported in the literature. In this proposed project, carefully designed three-dimensional centrifuge model tests will be carried out using the-state-of-the-art geotechnical centrifuge at HKUST and three-dimensional numerical simulations will be conducted to investigate and understand the basement-tunnel interactions and deformation mechanisms in soft ground. Key governing factors affecting the interaction and deformation mechanisms, such as different ratios of excavation width to depth and aspect ratios (i.e., excavation width to length ratios on plan), cover-to-tunnel diameter ratios, clearance distance between the tunnel and diaphragm wall inside and outside the excavation, will be simulated and studied. In addition, a suitable existing tunnel line close to and/or located directly underneath a new deep a new excavation site in China, will be selected for field monitoring to verify the results from both centrifuge and numerical modelling. It is aimed to improve existing design guidelines and to develop new calculation charts. Research findings and newly developed guidelines will certainly benefit the engineering profession directly and also will have major beneficial impacts to the environment and the economy worldwide. 在擁擠的城市如香港，上海，臺北和倫敦，快速和持續的發展往往需要有效地利用地下空間作為購物中心和停車場。建設地下室不僅能滿足使用樓層面積的需求，而且能減少對環境的影響。爲了方便購物者和使用者，在鄰近現有隧道或在隧道正上方建設深層地下室的需求日益增加。任何為建設深層地下室而開挖的基坑，即使是用地下連續墻作支擋，都將不可避免地造成地面應力的變化，從而導致地面水平和豎直方向的位移。經常有文獻報導深基坑開挖對現有隧道的破壞。 本項目將採用香港科技大學先進的岩土離心機進行精心設計的三維離心機模型試驗，並將開展三維數值模擬來研究和瞭解軟地層中地下室與隧道間的相互作用與變形機理。影響相互作用與變形機理的主要因素，例如基坑的寬深比和寬長比，覆土深度與隧道直徑的比值，基坑內外隧道與地下連續墻之間的淨空距離，都將進行模擬與研究。此外，還將選擇一條鄰近新深基坑或位於新深基坑正下方的現有隧道進行現場監測，用於驗證離心機和數值模擬的結果。本項目的目的是改良現有的設計指南及開發新的計算圖表。研究成果與新開發的設計指南無疑將使工程行業直接受益，並將對環境和世界經濟產生較大的有利影響。

617511.label: Realisation of objectives
617511.value: The prime project objective is to investigate the influence of deep basement excavations on existing tunnels (i.e., basement-tunnel interaction) by carrying out systematic three-dimensional centrifuge model tests together field monitoring and three-dimensional numerical analyses. The project objective has been achieved by obtaining high quality and comprehensive three-dimensional centrifuge model tests and field monitoring of the performance of existing tunnel due to adjacent basement and new tunnel excavations. The field monitoring was conducted via research collaboration with Professor Liu G.B. from Tongji University. The effects of a 22.8m deep excavation on the existing metro line 6 near the Fushan and Zhangyang roads in Shanghai have been monitored. In addition to dimensionless analyses and numerical parametric study to improve our fundamental understanding of three-dimensional stress transfer deformation mechanisms, the attained high quality centrifuge model test results and field data have then been back-analyzed and adopted to verify numerical model and model parameters for the development of improved design guidelines. In collaborating with Hohai University, one Ph.D student – Mr Sun Huasheng has joint HKUST as a visiting student for 5 months to carry out two centrifuge model tests and three-dimensional numerical back-analyses of his centrifuge model tests. In addition, one Ph.D student Mr P. Huang has been exchanged to the Hong Kong University of Science Technology (HKUST) to carry out some centrifuge model tests and numerical parametric analyses. On the other hand, Mr Hong Yi from HKUST went to Shanghai to participate in some field monitoring work and valuable data were acquired to verify centrifuge model test results and numerical simulations.

617511.label: Major findings and research outcome
617511.value: Based on novel three-dimensional centrifuge modelling technique developed and advanced numerical modelling and field monitoring (refer to Ng et al., 2013, Shi et al., 2015; Ng et al., 2015 and Liu et al., 2016 listed in Part C for details), the following major findings and outcomes can be summarised: For tunnel located directly underneath a deep basement, the maximum tunnel heave will be about 0.07% of the final depth of the basement excavation in sand. It is found that tunnel heave decreases as the cover-to-diameter ratio increase but at a reduced rate. On the contrary, a maximum settlement of 0.014% of the basement depth is expected in the tunnel located at the side of the basement. For the former tunnel, the influence zone by the basement excavation on vertical tunnel displacement along the longitudinal direction is 1.2 times the basement length. Due to stress relief from the basement excavation, the tunnel that located directly beneath the basement is vertically elongated but the one that lay at the side of the basement is distorted. When the basement is constructed directly above the existing tunnel, excavation-induced heave and strain are more sensitive to a change in soil density in the transverse direction than that in the longitudinal direction of the tunnel. Moreover, the tensile strain induced in the tunnel along its longitudinal direction is insensitive to the stiffness of the retaining wall, but that induced along the transverse direction is significantly reduced by a stiff wall. When the basement is constructed at the side of the existing tunnel, the use of a diaphragm wall can reduce the maximum settlements and tensile strains induced in the tunnel by up to 22% and 58%, respectively, compared with the use of a sheet pile wall. Under the same soil density and wall stiffness, excavation induced maximum movement and tensile strains in the tunnel located at a side of basement are about 30% of those in the tunnel located directly beneath basement centre. Key dimensionless groups to influence the effects on excavation on existing tunnel have been investigated. These dimensionless groups include excavation width to depth ratio and aspect ratio (i.e., width to length on plan), cover-to-tunnel diameter ratios inside and outside the excavation site, relative stiffness of retaining wall to soil, and normalised distance of the existing tunnel to the retaining wall (i.e., diaphragm wall). All these findings can be used to improve and verify design guidelines. Through the deep collaboration among Tongji University, Hohai University and HKUST, three Ph.D students have graduated, one each from the three participating and collaborating universities. Moreover, 10 refereed journal papers have been accepted and published.

617511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
617511.value: In previous studies reported in literature, existing tunnels and new tunnels often have similar geometries (i.e., circular shaped). However, it is not unusual to encounter large size horseshoe-shaped and oval-shaped tunnels. It is expected that more significant stress redistribution and deformation may be induced in horseshoe and oval shaped tunnels as compared with those in circular tunnel. Moreover, higher internal force would be mobilized in larger existing horseshoe shaped tunnels. It is thus worthwhile to investigate effects of basement excavation on existing horse-shoe shaped and oval-shaped tunnels.

617511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
617511.value: To sustain the development in congested urban cities such as Hong Kong, Shanghai, Taipei and London, efficient exploration and use of underground spaces such as deep basements are necessary. This is because underground construction not only can meet the demand of usable floor areas but it also reduces environmental impacts. In order to minimize adverse effects of deep basement construction on existing tunnels, highly quality of centrifuge model tests and field monitoring data have been obtained and analysed to improve our understand the three-dimensional stress transfer and deformation mechanisms of a newly excavated deep basement on an existing tunnel in sand and clay. Key dimensionless groups to influence an excavation on existing tunnel have been investigated. These dimensionless groups include excavation width to depth ratio and aspect ratio (i.e., width to length on plan), cover-to-tunnel diameter ratios inside and outside the excavation site, relative stiffness of retaining wall to soil, and normalised distance of the existing tunnel to the retaining wall (i.e., diaphragm wall). With the improved fundamental understanding and reliable field and centrifuge test data, new design guidelines have been developed. It is anticipated that the research findings and new design guidelines developed will benefit the engineering profession directly, and also will sustain the continuous development of urban cities environmentally, safely and economically worldwide.
