617811.label: Project Objectives
617811.value: Objective 1: hJam: General Side Channel technique In this task, we will design a new PHY layer technique called hJam. This technique leverages jamming for coordination. In this case, we can decode the original data message by using interference cancellation and energy detection techniques. Different from the traditional methods which consider the jamming as nothing but noise, we harness the jamming as coordination information. This hJam technique is modulation independent so that it can be adopted in high throughput protocols, e.g., 802.11a/g/n (OFDM based). Also under bad channel conditions, our technique can distinguish the normal interference from intended jamming by energy detection. Objective 2: Efficient modulation/demodulation schemes for general Side Channel To demonstrate the effectiveness of the free coordination channel, we plan to design some efficient jamming patterns to represent the coordination information. Moreover, there should be different modulation/demodulation schemes for different requirements. In this task, we will design some efficient modulation/demodulation schemes based on hJam and analyze their performance. Different from the traditional modulation schemes, our modulation/demodulation schemes are based on the jamming information which is a new communication paradigm. We will implement the modulation and demodulation schemes in a testbed and test the performance. Objective 3: Applying hJam to different protocols In recent years, many research efforts have been devoted to interference management. For instance, interference avoidance (e.g., CSMA, TDMA, FDMA) attempts to scatter the multiple transmissions along spatial, temporal and frequency dimensions so that severe interference is largely avoided. All these works are, however, limited by a critical assumption that a receiver with a single antenna can only receive one transmission at a time. Besides building the general Side Channel, hJam can also be used in conjunction with existing wireless protocols. It can help us to receive multiple transmissions per antenna. In that case, applying hJam to different protocols can enhance the network performance. Objective 4: A new MAC protocol based on hJam To demonstrate the effectiveness of hJam, we will design a new MAC protocol. In this new MAC protocol, the Side Channel will be used to coordinate data transmission on the Main Channel. As such, there is no need to perform the random back-off, a typical distributed coordination mechanism, in the Main Channel. Notice that the back-off is in fact one of the major sources of communication overhead. In this new MAC protocol, we will leverage the characteristics of hJam for the coordination-free design which should significantly improve the network throughput.

617811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
617811.value: In wireless communication, coordination among different devices is a necessity to avoid severe mutual interference and to utilize the shared medium efficiently. Such coordination costs precious communication resource, and may lead to a significantly degraded network performance. In traditional approaches, the coordination is addressed in either an in-band or out-of-band manner. For in-band approaches, the coordination traffic stays in the same communication channel as the data traffic, bringing a large amount of communication overhead such as the Distributed Coordination Function Inter frame Space (DIFS), Short Inter frame Space (SIFS) and random back-offs in carrier sense multiple access (CSMA). The out-of-band approaches are typically designed for multiple radio systems. These approaches, usually, dedicate one complete radio (and its associated channel resource) for coordination, and thus generate extra costs. In some experiments, we have observed that by generating intended jamming patterns, some simultaneous transmission can be successfully decoded without affecting the original communications. Motivated by this, in this research project we propose to use such jamming information obtained from the lower layer of the network protocol stack to build an extra, free coordination channel. Moreover, in this new communication paradigm, we will design a new PHY layer technique which is modulation independent, i.e., it can be used in 802.11a/g/n, WiMAX, and LTE. This technique can also be used under different channel conditions, especially the external interference environments. Jamming has traditionally been considered in an adversarial manner to prevent others from communicating over the wireless medium. In our free coordination channel communications, however, we will use the jamming to facilitate communication. Building such a free coordination channel brings a new paradigm of communications. Along this direction there are many new issues and challenges to be addressed. To achieve these goals, we will accomplish three critical tasks in this research project. We will first design hJam, a PHY layer technique which harnesses jamming to communicate and is modulation independent. Then based on hJam we will design and analyze some efficient modulation/demodulation schemes to maximize network capacity. We will also implement them in a test-bed and compare their performance with theoretical analysis. Finally, we will apply the hJam to existing protocols (e.g., CDMA and TDMA) to analyze and enhance the network performance.

617811.label: Realisation of objectives
617811.value: In the traditional wireless communication, jamming is considered to be nothing but noise. However, in this research we design a new communication paradigm by leveraging jamming for transmission. It offers another completely different way for wireless network operations rather than traditional coordination approaches. During the reporting period, we first designed a new PHY layer technique called hJam. This technique leverages the jamming for information communication. The traditional Side Channel technique can transmit the control messages in the code space but works for DSSS modulation only. To enable coordination information delivery in more general environments, we designed hJam on the modern OFDM modulation schemes. In hJam, the application data can obtain the full air time. Theoretical analysis confirms the general applicability of hJam in practical environments. The results of this work were published in IEEE Infocom 2012 and IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing 2013. In the second task, we designed two efficient jamming patterns to represent the coordination information, namely Pulse-Position Modulation (PPM) and Pulse-Interval Modulation (PIM), according to different synchronization granulations for different hardware environments. PIM uses the relative jamming positions of samples. When the precise synchronization is available, PPM is suitable because of the much higher channel capacity in Side Channel. Otherwise, PIM is suggested which is more tolerant to the unsynchronized time but has a lower data rate. The results of this work were published in IEEE Infocom 2012 and IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems 2013. In the third task, we first analyze the general applicability of hJam in different practical environments. We then implemented hJam on GNU Radio testbed. The performance evaluations as well as extensive simulations show that hJam outperforms IEEE 802.11 protocols by up to 200% under different traffic patterns. The results of this work were published in IEEE Infocom 2012. Finally, we design a new MAC protocol to send the coordination request through the Side Channel by using hJam. The key point is that the operations are placed consecutively along the time dimension with no gap in between, and the two kinds of operations are alternately scheduled. In that case, no coordination cost is needed in our new MAC design. And we conduct real experiments as well as extensive simulations to show that the throughput can be highly improved. The results of this work were published in IEEE ICDCS 2012.

617811.label: Major findings and research outcome
617811.value: In the course of this project, we have published 9 refereed conference papers, including IEEE Infocom, IEEE ICDCS, IEEE DySpan. We also published 4 IEEE Transaction papers, including IEEE JSAC, IEEE TMC and IEEE TPDS. Effective coordination can dramatically reduce radio interference and avoid packet collisions for multi-station wireless local area networks (WLANs). Coordination itself needs consume communication resource and thus competes with data transmission for the limited wireless radio resources. In traditional approaches, control frames and data packets are transmitted in an alternate manner, which brings a great deal of coordination overhead. In this paper we propose a new communication model where the control frames can be “attached” to the data transmission. Thus, control messages and data traffic can be transmitted simultaneously and consequently the channel utilization can be improved significantly. We implement the idea in OFDM-based WLANs called hJam, which fully explores the physical layer features of the OFDM modulation method and allows one data packet and a number of control messages to be transmitted together. hJam is implemented on the GNU Radio testbed consisting of eight USRP2 nodes. We also conduct comprehensive simulations and the experimental results show that hJam can improve the WLANs efficiency by up to 200% compared with the existing 802.11 family protocols.

617911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
617911.value: The use of convex optimization is now ubiquitous in communications and signal processing. The development of numerical interior-point methods during the mid-1990s, capable of solving convex problems in polynomial time, was a catalyst in the engineering community. Since then, a large number of very different problems in engineering have been reformulated in the form of convex optimization problems, which can then be efficiently analyzed in theory and solved in practice. Convex optimization has undoubtedly become a fundamental tool in engineering. Two key elements in the formulation of an optimization problem are the optimization variables and the fixed parameters, both of which appear combined in the cost function as well as in the constraints. In most of the current literature, these parameters that define the problem instance are assumed to be perfectly known. In practice, however, the parameters need to be estimated and they will be subject to estimation errors that may affect in a very adverse way the solution to the optimization problem. In fact, the effect of such errors can be catastrophic in some cases and needs to be properly handled. One can envision at least two ways to deal with the problem of uncertain parameters subject to estimation errors. One way is to make the problem formulation robust to parameter estimation errors. This falls within the topic of robust optimization methods and is attracting considerable attention in the research community. The other way is to improve the estimation of the parameters through sophisticated estimation techniques based on, e.g., structured and parsimonious modeling, resampling, multifactor regression analysis, coherent risk measure theory, spectral representation methods, and random matrix theory. This proposal aims at devising the effective combination of efficiently inferred parameters with optimization methods that are viable in real applications in two different ways: i) by making the problem solution robust to errors in the parameters, and ii) by developing more advanced estimation techniques properly tailored to the optimization problem at hand. 目前，凸优化在通信和信号处理领域应用非常广泛。二十世纪九十年代发展起来的数值内点法，由于其能够以多项式时间解决凸优化问题，早已经成为工程领域中的催化剂。自此以来，工程领域很多不同的问题都重新表达为凸优化问题，从而都能够进行有效地理论分析，并且可以得到实际高效地解决。在工程领域，凸优化毫无疑问已经成为解决实际问题最基础和重要的方法之一。 在凸优化问题表达式中，两个最为重要的元素就是优化变量和固定参数，它们都在代价函数和限制条件中同时出现。在大多数目前现有的文献中，这些决定的问题实例的参数是假定能够完全获取的。但是，实际上这些参数需要估计并且在估计中它们容易产生对优化问题结果有负面影响的误差。事实上，这些误差的影响在一些实例中又是灾难性的，因此这些影响需要得到适当地处理。 人们可以想象出至少两种方法来处理含有易于产生误差的不确定参数的问题。一种方法是让问题的表达式对参数误差具有鲁棒性。这个方法属于鲁棒性优化方法的范畴，并且逐步引起了研究领域相当多的关注。另外一种方法通过诸如结构化和简约模型，重采样，多因素回归分析，一致性风险度量理论，谱解法和随机矩阵理论等精细估计方法来提高参数估计精度。 本提案的目的在于通过使用的优化方法设计出有效的参数组合。这些优化方法在实际应用中的实用性体现在两个方面：1）使问题的答案对于参数误差具有鲁棒性；2）专门针对目前已有的问题合理地开发出更为高级的参数估计方法。

617911.label: Realisation of objectives
617911.value: The main two goals of this project were i) to develop robust estimators and methods, ii) to use random-matrix theory to optimize the shrinkage factor in robust solutions, and iii) to explore more sophisticate risk measures that take into account fluctuations as opposed to just average values. All the objectives have been satisfactorily completed and the output consists of nine IEEE journal papers and a couple of conference papers. Objective 1 was focused on developing robust estimators and methods. Several of the produced papers consider these two aspects: the robust estimation when the number of available samples is small compared to the dimensionality (for example in the estimation of covariance matrices) and worst-case robust optimization methods (for example in cognitive radio communication systems and in order execution in financial markets). Objective 2 was on the application of random matrix theory to estimate shrinkage factors in the estimation of covariance matrices in the small sample regime. This was applied in the context of multi-antenna communication systems as well as in financial systems. Three of the papers have addressed this particular problem. Objective 3 looked into more sophisticated measures of risk that include the fluctuations of the cost as opposed to using simply the mean value or the mean plus variance. In financial systems it is well recognized that the variance is a poor measure of the risk of investments and it is customary to consider value-at-risk measures and conditional-value-at-risk. Particularly, one paper has focused on optimization methods based on probabilistic constraints rather than just first- and second-order moments.

617911.label: Major findings and research outcome
617911.value: The major findings of this project are the development of robust estimation and optimization methods as well as to explore probabilistic objective/constraints as opposed to the traditional naive and worst-case optimization formulations. Robust estimation of covariance matrices has been studied, producing several papers in the context of filtering in communication systems and in the area of financial systems. Also the connections between information-theoretic and estimation aspects has been explored in one paper. Robust optimization has been considered in four journal papers in the context of communication systems, smart grid systems, as well as financial systems. Motivated by financial systems where the first- and second-order moments are not enough to characterize the fluctuations of the random prices, one paper has extensively considered probabilistic constraints also termed value-at-risk and conditional-value-at-risk, with very good practical results. To summarize, I think the objectives have been well achieved and the research outcome has been superb with nine IEEE journal papers and two conference papers.

617911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
617911.value: Our research group is currently further working on the topic of robust estimation of parameters in the context of non-Gaussian distributions and existence of outliers. The worst-case robust optimization formulations is now quite mature but the probabilistic constraints are still in their infancy and further work is necessary which we plan to pursue.

617911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
617911.value: Optimization problems are common in engineering and there are many efficient methods developed for their numerical resolution. In practice, however, such formulations may not be relevant as the parameters involved in the formulation are not known exactly due to estimation errors. There are two ways to address such important issue. One is to make sure that the parameters are estimated correctly using robust estimation methods. The other way is to formulate the optimization problem taking into account that the parameters are not well known, leading to robust optimization. These two aspects have been explored in this proposal. In addition, a more sophisticated measure of variability or risk, which appears in financial systems as well as communication systems, has been studied in detail, leading to the so-called probability constraints which are particularly critical in financial markets. Overall, the publication output has been superb with nine top IEEE journal papers.

618011.label: Project Title(Chinese)
618011.value: 帶有強位置隱私的空間數據查詢處理

618011.label: Project Objectives
618011.value: A spatial query processing framework that offers strong location privacy: We will design a general framework for answering location-based queries supporting strong location privacy. Our setting employs PIR functionality as a “black box”; therefore, any PIR protocol can be used in conjunction with our solutions. The proposed architecture involves a guided multi-step query process, where a spatial query is performed through a set of PIR queries. Implementation of an elaborate instantiation of our framework, using existing work: We show that existing work on spatial PIR is prohibitively expensive. Therefore, we will devise a sophisticated solution based on previous work, and use this scheme as a fair performance evaluation benchmark. Development of novel algorithms with strong location privacy guarantees: We will develop efficient spatial query processing algorithms. As a first step, we propose HRT, which leverages a R*-Tree augmented with Hilbert information. We will show that HRT drastically reduces the number of the expensive PIR queries required to execute a spatial query and ensures strong location privacy. We will also tackle the inherently high cost of spatial PIR with alternative implementations that utilize novel hardware platforms, including Graphic Processors and Cloud Computing. Security issues: We will formulate a powerful attacker, whose goal is to identify the query location with non-negligible probability. We will outline a set of plausible attacks specific to spatial PIR, and provide feasible solutions.

618011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
618011.value: The expansion of location-based services (LBS) has raised many concerns about user privacy. Similar to web searches or online purchases, location-dependent queries may disclose sensitive information about an individual's health, financial status, political/religious affiliations, etc. A user wishing to use an LBS without revealing his/her ID can transmit the query through an anonymizing network (e.g., Tor) that hides the real IP address. Nevertheless, simply removing the IP address is not sufficient to protect the user’s identity, which can be inferred by the coordinates of the query and background knowledge (e.g., user's home address). Hence, truly private location-based services necessitate location privacy. Additionally, location privacy is desirable independently of the concealment of the IP. For instance, a user may reveal the real IP address to the LBS, while still wishing to hide the fact that he/she has visited a specific area. Among the possible solutions that aim at protecting location privacy, only spatial private information retrieval (PIR) provides strong location privacy, which mandates that the query is indistinguishable from any other location in the data space. The project aims at the following contributions. (i) We will design a framework for answering spatial queries based on PIR, offering strong location privacy. The proposed system is independent of the underlying PIR protocol and, thus, flexible to multiple implementation choices and upgradable with future PIR methodologies. (ii) We will devise an elaborate framework instantiation based on existing work and will use this method as a performance evaluation benchmark. (iii) We will implement tree-based approaches and explain how they drastically reduce the expensive PIR operations required to ensure privacy, as compared to our benchmark method. (iv) We will identify privacy attacks that are specific to spatial PIR, and propose sophisticated solutions to tackle them. (v) Finally, we plan to investigate additional issues, including the utilization of modern technologies (e.g., Graphics Processors, Cloud Computing), to boost system performance. 基於位置的服務（LBS）的蓬勃發展使用戶隱私受到了廣泛關注。與網絡搜索和在線購物類似，依賴於位置信息的查詢可能暴露於個人的健康，經濟狀況，政治/宗教派別等相關的敏感信息。對於那些希望使用LBS同時不暴露身份（ID）的用戶，一種方式是將查詢通過匿名網絡傳送（例如Tor），以達到隱藏其真實IP地址的目的。儘管如此，僅僅隱藏IP地址不足以保護用戶身份隱私。用戶身份仍可通過用戶查詢的坐標以及背景知識（例如，用戶的家庭地址）被推斷得到。因此，真正保密的基於位置的服務必然要求保證用戶的位置隱私。另外，位置隱私獨立於IP隱藏，是用戶所希望的。例如，某用戶可能把真實IP地址透露給LBS，與此同時希望將他/她訪問過的某個特定區域隱藏。在所有針對保護位置隱私的可能解決方案中，只有空間隱私信息獲取（PIR）提供強位置隱私。PIR要求一個查詢的位置不區分與數據空間中的任意其他位置。 本項目的貢獻如下。（i）我們將設計一個處理空間數據查詢的框架。它基於PIR並且提供強位置隱私。此系統不依賴於下層的PIR協議，因此可以靈活應用不同的實現方式並且可以連同未來的PIR方法升級。（ii）我們將設計一個基於已有研究成果的詳盡的示例框架，並以此作為性能測試的基準方法。（iii）我們將實現基於樹的各種方法。我們將解釋相對於基準方法，它們如何大幅減少因保證隱私而進行的昂貴的PIR操作。（iv）我們將指出多種適用於任何算法的針對隱私的攻擊，並且提出相應的精密解決方式。（v）最後，我們計劃調研更多問題，包括通過應用現代技術（例如，圖形處理器，雲計算）來大幅提升系統性能。

618011.label: Realisation of objectives
618011.value: The main aim of the project is a comprehensive system where users can ask completely anonymous queries, i.e., the server cannot infer anything about their current location. We assume an untrustworthy location-based service (LBS) that possesses a database DB, and clients that issue nearest neighbor queries on DB. Each client initially determines a set of blocks to be privately retrieved from the LBS, using any PIR protocol as a black box. Subsequently, it transmits to the LBS the respective PIR queries. The LBS returns a set of blocks based on which the client generates the blocks to be retrieved at the subsequent round. However, the adaptation of existing work on strong location privacy is prohibitively expensive. Specifically, our implementation and experimental evaluation of PIR techniques based on Voronoi diagrams and grid based nearest neighbor algorithms revealed that such techniques are too slow, even for datasets of moderate size. To alleviate this problem we developed novel algorithms for efficient query processing. Specifically, the LBS builds an R*-Tree over DB, where the entries in every node are sorted on their Hilbert values. The client executes locally an optimal nearest neighbor algorithm and, whenever a tree node must be retrieved, it privately asks for this node from the LBS. Going one step further, we utilized the concept of e-differential privacy in order to further enhance efficiency through anonymized location statistics. Finally, we developed: (i) the concept of w-event privacy to protect user trajectories consisting of up to w timestamps, and (ii) differentially private histograms that can be used for querying aggregate user data without revealing the locations of individual users. For all our methods, we formulate powerful attackers and prove the security and feasibility of our solutions.

618011.label: Major findings and research outcome
618011.value: Depending on the data size and distribution, nearest neighbor queries that guarantee strong location privacy may require several minutes to terminate. In order to achieve efficiency, publication C1 proposes the adaptive query plan, which relaxes the need for answering all queries accurately. Instead, it computes a minimum data size, which guarantees that at least a predefined percentage of queries are answered correctly. The adaptive query plan changes periodically based on statistics of previously issued queries. However, utilizing statistics on sensitive location data may reveal the whereabouts of a user. To avoid this type of privacy breaches, we employ the notion of ϵ-differential privacy, which offers theoretical privacy guarantees. A range-sum query over a histogram returns aggregate information about all records in a range; e.g., such a query could ask for the total number of users in a geographic area. Private histogram publication aims at hiding the existence of particular users. Existing schemes are classified into “data-aware” and “data-oblivious”. Data-aware methods, that exploit data characteristic to increase utility, are expensive to build, and incur high error for large ranges. On the other hand, data-oblivious histograms are fast, but may yield lower utility for datasets commonly found in practice, especially for short ranges. To overcome these issues, publication J1 proposes histograms that combine and enhance characteristics of both approaches, aiming at both efficiency and utility. In J2 we focus on continuous monitoring of statistics, e.g., publishing the number of cars per area in real-time to allow for optimal route computation, without however disclosing individual trajectories. Specifically, we propose the concept of w-event privacy, which protects any event sequence occurring within any window of w timestamps (i.e., trajectory of w timestamps). Finally, in J3, we propose Agnostic Diagnosis, an online lightweight approach that detects silent node failures by observing violations correlation patterns.

618011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
618011.value: The proliferation of smartphones and the continuous emergence of novel location-based applications will further increase the importance of location privacy. A promising topic for research concerns privacy in geo-social networks (GSN). Assume for instance that users do not trust the GSN. Interesting problems in this setting are (i) how a user can publish his location only to his/her friends, (ii) how two friends can detect that they are in the proximity of each other. Moreover, in some cases, the location of a user may be revealed unintentionally by information posted by co-located friends. In the future, we plan to utilize our expertise on location privacy and geo-social networks (another GRF project by the PI), in order to address such issues.

618011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
618011.value: The embedding of positioning capabilities (e.g., GPS) in mobile devices has triggered several exciting applications. However, at the same time, it has raised serious concerns about the risks of revealing sensitive information in location based services (LBS). Consider, for instance, that a user issues a query about the nearest nightclub to an untrustworthy LBS, while s/he wishes to remain anonymous. Even if the ID of the user is removed (e.g., through a trusted anonymizer service), the LBS requires his/her coordinates in order to process the query. If the LBS is malicious (e.g., it collects and sells personal data and habits for unsolicited advertisements), it can relate these coordinates to the specific user through a variety of techniques (matching with previous queries, residential data etc). In this project we developed techniques that achieve strong location privacy, i.e., they do not disclose any information about user locations. As opposed to previous work, our methods are feasible in practice. In addition, we have addressed privacy concerns for other settings, such as publication of aggregate data through histograms (where an attacker with sufficient background knowledge could identify individual users) and event monitoring (where an attacker could discover the trajectories of individual users).

618311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
618311.value: I propose to study the cooperative and dynamic disruption recovery problem. The problem assumes multiple players running their operations using some infrastructure. A disruption happens, which damages the infrastructure, reducing its capacity and deteriorating the players' operational performance. The infrastructure can be repaired, but full recovery takes some time, given limited recovery resources. Before full recovery, the players can provide degraded services to their customers based on the partially recovered infrastructure. The first purpose of this project is to build models to optimally allocate the resource such that the infrastructure can gradually be repaired, with the objective of optimizing the evolution of the operating performance over the recovery period. The second purpose of the project is to use cooperative game theory to address the situation where the recovery resources are actually owned by the multiple players who can make decisions independently. Specifically, each player can decide how to allocate his resource to repair the infrastructure so that his operational performance can improve more quickly. At the same time, players can together make a globally optimized plan by sharing recovery resources. The implementation of such a global plan needs a binding agreement among all the players to share the benefits fairly, which falls into the field of cooperative game theory. So this study will address two new important issues in disruption recovery - the dynamic process over time, and the involvement of multiple decision makers. The results will provide both the optimal recovery solution and its implementation feasibility. In this proposal we will only discuss in detail two concrete examples from the logistics industry, a facility location problem and a multiple-pairs shortest path problem. Our general framework, however, will be designed to be applied in many similar applications. 本项目研究异常事件的动态合作修复问题。我们考虑多个决策者利用一个公共基础平台进行一些运营。某些异常事件的发生可能会损坏基础平台，例如降低它的容量，从而影响决策者的运营效率。基于有限的修复资源，基础平台可以被逐步修复。在基础平台被完全修复之前，这些决策者可以利用被部分修复的平台容量，进行一些低水平的运营。本项目的第一个目标是建立一个用来进行修复资源调配的决策模型，从而优化决策者们在整个基础平台修复过程中的动态运营效率。 本项目的第二个目标是研究修复过程中的合作博弈问题。假设每个决策者可以控制一部分修复资源，他将在决定其资源分配优先考虑自己的运营效率，由此会导致系统的非最优性。合作博弈将设计一种机制，使得每个决策者在不损伤其本身利益的条件下，按照系统的最优性分配其资源。 本项目将着重考虑两类具体的物流管理运营问题，仓库设置和最短路径。但是我们提出的研究框架将适用于很多其它的类似领域。

618311.label: Realisation of objectives
618311.value: There are five objectives proposed in this project. We have achieved all these objectives in doing the project. Since the first four objectives are closely connected with each other, we do not have any journal papers or conference presentations that are dedicated to a single objective; instead, our publish work often involves two or more objectives. In what follows, we will elaborate the main results that we have for each objective, with the reference as where they are published or presented. The first objective is to build a general disruption recovery model that considers the dynamic changes in the system's status. Since the limited resource is the fundamental reason causing the disruption recovery to be a dynamic process, we have focused on the problem of disruption recovery with limited resources, where we develop models and design optimization algorithms to solve the problems. Such results have been presented in international conferences such as POMS-HK International Conference (Research Output item 9, No. 1), and POMS Annual Conference (Research Output item 9, No. 2). The second objective is to apply cooperative game theory to the recovery process involving multiple decision makers. We find that the work for achieving this objective is more challenging and interesting because of both its theoretical value and practical relevance. The major technical difficulty, also the key contribution of this project, is how to calculate a minimum outside subsidy for achieving the global collaboration. To this end, we propose a generic framework by Lagrangian relaxation, an approach that is easy to implement and can be used to a broad range of problems. The results have been presented in international conferences such as INFORMS Annual Meeting (Research Output item 9, No. 4 and No. 5), and POMS International (Research Output item 9, No. 6). A paper has been accepted in INFORMS Journal on Computing (Research Output item 8, No. 4). The third objective is to study the facility location disruption recovery problem with the above two factors, including the optimization algorithms and the properties of the games. We have developed optimization algorithms based on decomposition techniques (Research Output item 9, No. 1, No. 2), and the solutions for the cooperative games, in particular, as one of the demonstrating cases for the generic framework in the second objective (Research Output item 8, No. 4, item 9, No. 6). The fourth objective is to study the multiple-pairs shortest path disruption recovery problem with the above two factors, including the optimization algorithms and the properties of the games. Our optimization algorithm is based on Lagrangian relaxation, and the result is presented in international conference (Research Output item 9, No. 1). The study on the game solution shows the game can be solved by our generic framework in the second framework (Research Output item 9, No. 4, No. 5). The fifth objective is to explore other possible extensions such as the general network flow problems or production planning and scheduling problems. We have successfully made four extensions, three of which are centred with the topic of the project, i.e., disruption recovery and collaboration, with another one going beyond the proposed scope of the project. Extension 1 is on collaboration in disruption recovery for production scheduling. Under mild conditions, we show that a global collaboration can be implemented among players. The results are presented in POMS Annual Conference (Research Output item 9, No. 3). A paper has been submitted to European Journal of Operational Research for review. Extension 2 is on the supply chain model where the supplier’s facility is subject to a disruption. We study how the buyer can use a cooperative scheme, claiming penalty and also offering help, to work together with the supplier for disruption recovery. The results are included in a paper accepted in Omega (Research Output item 8, No. 3). Extension 3 is using cooperative game to study the recycling operations when the recycling operation can generate multiple products. Using a cooperative game model, we show that different players are willing to pool their resource together for global collaboration. The results are reported in a paper published in European Journal of Operational Research (Research Output item 8, No. 1). Extension 4 is built on a model of nonatomic game where there are infinite number of players. The topic is motivated when we try to extend the cooperative decision for a very large number of players. During our study we find it more reasonable and practical to assume a non-cooperative game for such a situation. Although this exceeds the original scope of the project, we think it leads to some valuable results. So we work on it and finally publish one paper along this direction in Games and Economics Behavior (Research Output item 8, No. 2). In summary, we have achieved all five objectives of this project. Although the project is officially completed, we still have some on-going work related to this project. Details can be found in item 6.2 of this report.

618311.label: Major findings and research outcome
618311.value: One significant finding in this project is the development of a general algorithmic framework for calculating the minimum required subsidy to stabilize the grand coalition for unbalanced cooperative games. In studying our specific problems that were proposed in the project, we find such problems are unbalanced cooperative games which require outside subsidies. In the literature, the subsidy can be found theoretically by a method based on the LP duality, which needs a standardized formulation in a case-by-case way, making it hard to use. In this project, we successfully develop a more efficient method which is based on Lagrangian relaxation. Compared with the LP-based method, our method turns out to be easier to implement and have a broader scope of application. The results are reported in a paper that has been accepted in INFORMS Journal on Computing (No. 4 in Item 8 of Research Output).

618311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
618311.value: In doing the project, we have identified a new research direction, i.e., how to stabilize the grand coalition of an unbalanced cooperative game. By extending some extending concepts in the literature, we find that there are new ways of achieving stabilization, which are more flexible. For example, we show it is possible to combine subsidy and penalization simultaneously. This result is included in a paper which is currently under major revision of Operations Research. We will continue working on this direction, trying to get the paper published in the future.

618311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
618311.value: This project studies how to make multiple parties working together to cope with the damages to a common infrastructure caused by a disruption. Examples of the infrastructure include a flow network, a group of supplying sources, and so on. The key issue to enable the collaboration is a fair way of sharing the cost, which falls into the field of cooperative game theory. In other words, this project uses cooperative game theory to study the disruption recovery problem. In doing the project, we show it possible to achieve a full-scale collaboration, but it often needs the input of some outside resources. We also develop an efficient generic framework to compute the outside resources needed.

618511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
618511.value: Networked control systems are large scale distributed systems in which the subsystems are interconnected by communication networks. Networked control systems are under extensive studies in the past ten years. A large number of results have been obtained. One class of problems in networked control systems is on the feedback control of a plant by a controller physically located remotely from each other and interconnected by a communication network. This type of problems are similar to the traditional controller design problems except the presence of the network. The network serves as the communication media between the controller and plant. When signals are transmitted through the network, distortion, interferance, and delay inevitably occur. The new networked control problems, more difficult than the traditional controller design problems, have to take into consideration of the network features. So far, very nice results have been obtained in networked state feedback stabilization and networked estimation. Also it is envisioned that by combining state feedback and state estimation, the networked output feedback control problem could be solved effectively by the separation principle, so far the vision has not become reality. One major obstacle is that it is not clear what the best way is to model the bilateral comminnication network sitting in between the plant and controller. In this project, we propose to use a two-port network, a well-established concept in circuit theory, to model the comminication network. The admittance, impedance, and transmission descriptions of the two-port provide handy models to the communication network interconnecting the plant and controller. We plan to develop a complete theory addressing the analysis and design of networked control systems based on the two-port model. In particular, the following classes of problems will be considered. 1. Analysis: when the plant and controller are given, what is the effect of the communication network on system stability and performance? 2. Synthesis: when the plant is given, together with the understanding of the communication network, design the remote controller so that the stability and performance of the closed-loop system are satisfactory. 3. Channel/Controller co-design: when the plant is given, design the communication network and the controller, under possible physical and resource constraint so that the stability and performance of the closed-loop system are satisfactory. 网络化控制系统是将子系统通过通信网络连接起来的大规模分布式系统。近十年来，网络化控制系统得到广泛研究并取得了很多成果。其中一类问题是研究采用通信网络连接的远程控制器来实现的反馈控制。这类问题与传统控制器设计问题相似，不同之处在于采用通信网络作为控制器和控制对象的沟通媒介。当信号通过网络传输，会产生失真、干扰、延迟等不可避免的误差。考虑到网络的这些特性，新的网络化控制器设计问题比传统的控制器设计问题更有难度。目前，在网络化状态反馈镇定和状态估计问题上已取得了一些很好的结果。我们期望通过结合状态反馈和状态估计并利用分离定理能够有效地解决网络化输出反馈问题。然而，一个主要的困难在于我们尚不清楚如何针对存在于控制器和控制对象之间的双边通信网络建立最合适的模型。 在本项目中，我们提出采用二端口网络对通信网络建模。在电路理论中，二端口网络已发展成熟。它提供的导纳、阻抗和传输参数可以方便地描述连接控制器和控制对象的通信网络。我们计划提出一个基于二端口模型的完整的理论以解决网络化控制系统中的分析和设计问题。其中，我们特别考虑以下几类问题： 1. 分析：对于给定的控制器和控制对象，分析通信网络对于系统镇定和性能的影响。 2. 综合：对于给定的控制对象和通信网络，设计远程控制器保证闭环系统的镇定和性能 达到要求。 3. 通道/控制器协同设计：对于给定的控制对象，在可能的物理和资源约束条件下设计通信网络和控制器保证闭环系统的镇定和性能达到要求。

618711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
618711.value: 谷歌地球与微软虚拟地球服务的迅速发展对超大规模城市三维建模技术有着极为迫切的需求。谷歌地球的街景与微软虚拟地球的街景都只是二维全景图，而并没有对应的三维模型。虽然计算机视觉与图形学领域的研究人员提出了多种基于图像或者是三维扫描点云的三维建模技术，但现有的方法仍然有着很大的局限性，通常这些方法都只能处理小规模场景的少量图像数据或者是三维扫描数据。在本项目中，我们提出了一种同时利用地面街景图像和三维扫描点云的三维建模技术。综合利用图像与三维扫描点云使得我们所研究的技术能够适用于超大规模场景的三维重建，而这将是本项目的研究核心。首先，我们将研究利用车载数据采集设配初始位置和相关姿态参数的自动匹配校准技术来重新匹配对准图像和三维扫描点云，从而克服数据采集过程的匹配误差。然后，我们将开发一种识别分割图像和三维点云中各类不同物体的语义分割算法，识别分割出需要三维重建的各类物体。最后，利用基于模型的逆向流程方法来实现建筑物表面的细节重建。 本项目构建在我们之前在structure from motion, 基于图像的树木、建筑物及其表面的建模方面的研究工作之上。综合利用图像与三维扫描数据是本项目的关键创新，通过引入三维扫描数据，所提出的建模技术在适用场景规模、鲁棒性、重建模型质量方面都有了重大突破。方法的有效性将通过在最新的谷歌街景数据上的实验加以验证。

618711.label: Realisation of objectives
618711.value: We have proposed a large-scale integration approach for image and scan data by taking into account the prior information available at the data capturing. We have also investigated the fundamental structure from motion when the images suffered rolling shutter effects. After these, we have developed a joint segmentation method for targeting the large-scale urban environments. In particular, we have investigated the segmentation of the input joint data into sky, buildings, the ground and vegetation. We have also investigated and developed the procedural approach for rule-based reconstruction and modeling of architectural objects. All these developments have been demonstrated on both Google Earth and Microsoft data sets as initially proposed.

618711.label: Major findings and research outcome
618711.value: One of the first major results from the project is on the learning CRFs for data parsing with an adaptive subgradient descent method. The superior performance of the larned CRF models allowed the successful segmentation of our imagery sets. This part is related to the Part C publication of the ICCV 2013. Following this development, another important result related to the geometry part is the local readjustment for high-resolution 3D reconstruction method we have developed. This is a fundamental issue as with data scale increases, the accumulated errors in various parts of the scene become inevitable. Using our proposed local readjustment instead of the global ones, the reconstruction resolution has been significantly increased. This part is related to the Part C publication of CVPR work in 2014. another major result is the image-based modeling of unwrappable facades from multiple registered images. This is achieved on the accumulation of the several related works proposed in this project. It requires not only the registration of multiple images, but also requires the segmentation of the visual data. After that, it needs also the procedural modeling approach that guides the current approach for the efficient unwrappable facades modeling. This result is related to the Part C publication of the IEEE TVCG in 2013. Finally we would like to mention the most recent publication in the Part C IEEE TVCG 2015, in which we have developed a building regularization method by introducing the efficient structural linear features. This is a major step towards the ultimate vectorization of the reconstructed 3D objects in representations.

618711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
618711.value: We are continuing to develop the large-scale 3D reconstruction and the integration of both imagery and scan data, which is one of the major research directions in both computer vision and computer graphics communities. Our current efforts are targeting even larger-scale data sets, and also better segmentation method based on the labeled data for the semantic categorization of input data into the major man-made and non man-made objects in the urban scenarios. Increasingly, we have also a focus more towards on the visual data as it not only integrates the most recent machine learning techniques, but also creating more and more large-scale data for more detailed modeling as the UAV technology make the low-flight aerial data capturing much more affordable than it was before.

618711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
618711.value: We are reconstructing a 3D representation of our surrounding world from a collection of 2D photographs or images. This is both scientifically and technically challenging, and practically important for our city life in smart cities and urban planning.

619111.value: 基於大腦皮層視差表徵的感覺運動協調系統的發育

619111.label: Project Objectives
619111.value: We will develop a new mathematical model of populations of binocular disparity selective neurons in the visual cortex, which is the major area of brain devoted to vision. Binocular disparity is the displacement between two corresponding points in the retinas of the left and right eyes, and is an important cue used to infer the distance to objects in the environment. In order to guide our development of this model, we will rely on data collected simultaneously from large numbers of disparity selective neurons in cat collected using two photon imaging by Prof. Prakash Kara, a neurophysiologist at the Medical University of South Carolina. These mathematical model populations are an abstraction of the representation of binocular disparity information in the brain. In order to embody this abstraction for use in the behaving robotic system described in the third objective, we will develop a system that implements the neural population model in real time using graphics processing units. In collaboration with Prof. Michele Rucci, a psychologist at Boston University, we will elaborate the possible functional advantages of this new model in spatial perception. In particular, we will demonstrate that this representation facilitates learning of sensorimotor coordination. We will focus on enabling the robot arm equipped with an active binocular vision system to learn a 3D tracing task. In this task, the tip of the arm will follow the trajectory of a target in 3D space controlled by visual feedback from the model disparity population. By learning this task, the robot will have demonstrated that it is possible to calibrate this representation with the real environment automatically through behavior.

619111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
619111.value: The US National Academy of Engineering identified "Reverse Engineering the Brain" as one of the grand challenges now facing engineering. It is clear that this endeavor requires interaction between engineering and neuroscience. In addition, we argue that it is equally important to have an interaction between engineering and psychophysics: the relationship between physical stimuli and their subjective correlates. While neuroscience can give detailed insights into the mechanics of how the neurons in the brain interact, psychophysics has an equally important role in understanding how a collection or population of neurons give rise to perception and ultimately action by biological organisms. Engineering can play a critical and unique role in our quest to understand the brain, by linking these two levels of description. We propose to develop hardware that emulates the responses of neurons processing binocular disparity in real time. Binocular disparity is the displacement between two corresponding points in the retinas of the left and right eyes, and is an important cue used to infer the depth to objects in the environment. With this hardware, we will address two questions. First, the brain represents information about binocular disparity with a large population of neurons with different characteristics. How do these characteristics vary across the population? Answering this question will reveal the nature of the representation of disparity in the brain. We will work with the neuroscientist Prof. Prakash Kara, who is using optical imaging techniques to measure responses from large numbers of disparity tuned neurons. Second, can robots use a similar representation of disparity to interact with the environment effectively? We will work with the psychologist Prof. Michele Rucci, who is an expert on how perception influences behavior and vice versa. We will use the hardware and models developed through our collaboration with Prakash Kara to develop algorithms that enable a robotic arm system equipped with a binocular vision system to learn to reach for targets it identifies visually in the environment. 美國國家工程院將“大腦逆向工程”定義為目前工程學所面臨的最大挑戰之一。顯然，這需要工程學和神經科學的共同努力。此外，我們認為工程學和心理物理學之間的互動也是同等重要的，因為物理刺激信號和主觀觀測者之間也是相互聯繫的。一方面，神經科學可以對大腦中神經元相互作用的機制有詳細的認知；另一方面，心理物理學對於理解大量神經元集群如何引發感知以及最終導致生物有機體產生行為也起到了重要的作用。通過將這基於兩個層次的不同描述聯繫起來，工程學在我們認識理解大腦的探索中扮演了關鍵而獨特的角色。因此，我們提出開發一套硬件系統，可以對處理雙目視差的神經反應進行實時仿真。雙目視差是指左右眼視網膜上兩個相對應的點之間存在位移差，而這正是我們在環境中推斷物體深度的重要線索。一旦我們有了如前所述的硬件系統，我們就可以解決兩個問題。第一，在大腦中，關於雙目視差的信息是由大量具有不同特性的神經元所表徵的，那麼這些特性在神經元集群間又是如何變化的？回答這個問題將揭示大腦中視差表徵的本質。為此，我們將與神經科學家Prakash Kara教授進行合作，而他正致力於利用光學成像技術測量大量視差調諧神經元的神經反應。第二，機器人能否利用類似的視差表徵方式與環境進行互動？我們將與心理物理學家Michele Rucci教授進行合作，而他是在研究感知和行為是如何相互影響這方面的專家。基於與Prakash Kara教授的合作中開發的硬件系統和視差模型，我們將進而為一套裝備了雙目視覺系統的機械手臂系統開發算法，使其學習如何在環境中識別目標並移向目標。

619111.label: Major findings and research outcome
619111.value: With respect to the first objective, the new mathematical model of populations of binocular disparity selective neurons in the visual cortex. We developed a model of disparity tuned neurons based on sparse coding. We demonstrated that this model could account for the orientation alignment of receptive fields observed in rodents [C3]. We later extended this sparsity model to include the effect of slowness [J4]. This model also enables the natural integration of temporal information, which leads to models of neural population tuned not only to depth, but also motion in depth [J2]. With respect to the second objective, the system that implements the neural population model in real-time, we developed a real time system for face detection which integrated stereo disparity cues from the disparity tuned neurons developed in the first objective. Surprisingly, our results here demonstrated that despite the increased input associated with processing two images, the speed of face detection was actually increased in comparison with monocular face detection because the use of stereo information enabled the system to quickly eliminate a large number of image locations that were unlikely to contain a face [J1]. With respect to the third objective, an investigation of the possible functional advantages of this new model in facilitating the learning of sensorimotor coordination, we were able to demonstrate that when applied to binocular image sequences, the model neurons could be used to drive both smooth pursuit and vergence eye movements, which stabilize the images received by the eyes over time, and cause the two eyes to fixate on the same object in space [C1][C2][J3].

619111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
619111.value: The work in this proposal can be extended by integrating additional visual cues as well as non-visual cues. For example, vergence eye movements can be driven not only by disparity, but also by accommodation (focus). Image stabilization can be achieved not only through visual cues, but also through vestibular cues, which encode acceleration. It would be interesting to investigate the integration of these other cues into the model as a way of performing multisensory fusion.

619111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
619111.value: This project investigated a new model of the disparity selective neurons found in the visual cortex, which is the primary area of the brain where visual processing takes place. One of the key advantages of this new model is that it can be used in sensori-motor behavioral tasks, such as eye movements to fixate the two eyes on a moving target. This process gives important cues to the location and motion of objects within the environment, and have wide applicability in robotics.

619311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
619311.value: Power MOSFETs are widely used as switches in power electronics systems such as switch mode power supplies (SMPS) and motor drives. In these applications, the load of a power MOSFET is inductive. The power MOSFET will be forced into avalanche mode during switching with an unclamped inductive load. Under the avalanche mode, the power MOSFET has to withstand both large drain-to-source current and voltage. For an n-channel device, hole current is generated by avalanche impact ionization and flows through the p-body region to the source electrode. A potential drop will be developed across the p-body region by this current flow. If the potential drop is large enough to forward bias the p-body/n+-source junction, the parasitic Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT) in the power MOSFET will be forced to turn on, and thermal runaway will occur. This failure mechanism is characterized by the maximum avalanche current (IAV) which can flow through the power MOSFET without failure [1], and this operation is referred to as Unclamped Inductive Switching (UIS). To prevent the avalanche current limited failure during UIS, it is desirable to reduce the base resistance of the parasitic BJT [2]. A high body doping concentration helps to achieve this goal. However, the doping concentration of the body region is limited by the threshold voltage requirement of the device. To increase the doping concentration of the body region will alleviate the IAV limited failure, but it will also make the power MOSFET to have a threshold voltage that is too high. In this project, a novel Silicon-Oxide-Nitride-Oxide-Silicon (SONOS) gate power MOSFET is proposed. The body doping concentration of this structure is allowed to be increased by as much as an order of magnitude compared to that of conventional power MOSFET structures. The increase in threshold voltage due to the excessively higher doping concentration is compensated by the positive fixed charges created in the silicon nitride of the gate. Using this approach, the base resistance of the parasitic BJT is reduced significantly, but without increasing the threshold voltage of the power MOSFET. Preliminary results show that the much smaller base resistance in turn allows a much larger avalanche current to flow through without forward biasing the body/source junction, resulting in a significant improvement in UIS performance (4 times better than that of the conventional structure). 功率MOSFET作爲開關器件被廣泛應用于開關式穩壓電源(SMPS)、電機驅動等電力電子系統中。在這些應用中，功率MOSFET的負載呈感性。在感性負載不被鉗位的情況下,與之串聯的功率MOSFET在關斷時將發生雪崩擊穿。雪崩擊穿時，功率MOSFET必須同時承受大的漏源電壓和電流。對于N型功率MOSFET而言，雪崩擊穿狀態下的碰撞電離將産生經過P型體區進入源電極的空穴電流，該空穴電流將在P型體區中産生壓降。如果該壓降足夠大以致體區與源之間的PN結開啓，功率MOSFET中的寄生三極管（BJT）將開啓，最終造成該器件的熱失控。這種失效機制可以用能夠安全流過該器件的最大雪崩電流(IAV)來表征，與之對應的器件工作狀態被稱爲非鉗位感性開關（UIS）狀態。爲使更大的雪崩電流能夠在非鉗位感性開關狀態下安全流過器件，應該降低功率MOSFET中的寄生三極管的基區電阻。高摻雜體區有助于實現這一目標，但體區摻雜濃度受該器件阈值電壓的限制。提高體區摻雜濃度將使更大的雪崩電流能夠安全流過器件，但該器件的阈值電壓也隨之增加以致超出正常範圍。本項目提出一種新的矽-氧化矽-氮化矽-氧化矽-氮化矽-矽（SONOS）柵功率MOSFET。在這種新器件結構中，體區摻雜濃度將能夠比常規器件提升一個數量級，而由此引起的阈值電壓升高將被柵介質中的氮化矽所俘獲的固定正電荷所補償。該結構使寄生三極管的基區電阻得以降低，而器件的阈值電壓並不隨之增加。根據初步的結果，由于基區電阻的顯著降低，非鉗位感性開關狀態下能夠安全流過器件的雪崩電流得以顯著增加（比常規器件提高4倍）。

619311.label: Realisation of objectives
619311.value: We begun the project by first working on the design of a novel SONOS gate power MOSFET. We have used numerical simulators to study the process and structural characteristics of the SONOS device with different gate materials and structural designs. We then proceeded to do the layout design and fabrication of the novel SONOS structure. With the various process modules developed, we then proceeded to integrate them to form the complete process for the fabrication of the devices. We managed to obtain working devices after solving a lot of process issues occurring in the fabrication runs. More subsequent runs were carried out to optimize the characteristics of the novel device. Finally, thorough electrical characterization of the devices was carried out, and all the project objectives such as novel device design, numerical simulation, experimental characterization, and comparison with conventional power MOSFET were achieved.

619311.label: Major findings and research outcome
619311.value: In this project, we have invented, designed, and demonstrated a novel SONOS power transistor for consumer and industrial power switching applications [1-4]. In the novel device, the doping concentration of the p-body is increased by an order of magnitude compared to that of the conventional power MOSFET. However, the positive shift of the threshold voltage due to the heavily doped p-body is fully compensated by the positive fixed charges preprogrammed in the silicon nitride of the oxide-nitride-oxide gate dielectric. As a result, a normal threshold voltage can be obtained, and the avalanche energy absorption of the novel device at unclamped inductive switching is 5.2 times that of the conventional power MOSFET.

619311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
619311.value: The novel power transistor which was developed in this project has been demonstrated experimentally in our research laboratory. The fabrication process used is simple and practical. It is also compatible to industrial process, and does not require the use of unconventional equipment or facilities for production fabrication. Therefore, it is ready for technology transfer for industrial applications.

619311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
619311.value: Power semiconductor devices have a huge market (billions of USD worldwide). The power MOSFET is the type of power transistor that has the largest market share. Its applications cover a wide range, including motor control, power supplies, welding, power conversions, etc. In this project, a novel low cost, high performance power transistor was designed and implemented. A prototype of the novel structure was demonstrated and fully characterized. It is concluded that the structure is very promising for the above power control and switching applications.

619511.value: 圆管构型中二维相变界面动力学的实验研究

619511.label: Project Objectives
619511.value: Design and fabricate a tensile mini-testing platform that is capable of loading/unloading the small tube specimen in a wide range of stretching rate and in different ambient conditions. Synchronized measurement of mechanical and thermal quantities will be realized in the developed platform. Conduct tensile tests on NiTi tubes and to obtain firsthand repeatable systematic experimental data on the domain evolution kinetics. Development of scaling laws that govern the loading rate dependent domain evolution, so that an in-depth fundamental understanding of the observed 2D domain kinetics will be achieved through theoretical analysis and through critical comparison with the experiments.

619511.label: Realisation of objectives
619511.value: In this project, we first designed and fabricated a tensile mini-testing platform that is capable of loading/unloading the small tube specimen in a wide range of stretching rates. Synchronized measurement of mechanical and thermal quantities was realized in the developed platform. In addition, strain field measurement was realized by Digital Imaging Correlation (DIC). We then conducted tensile tests on NiTi tubes and strips to obtain firsthand repeatable systematic experimental data on the domain evolution kinetics. Through theoretical analysis on the important coupling between mechanical and thermal fields, scaling laws that govern the loading rate dependent domain evolution has been established. An in-depth fundamental understanding of the observed domain kinetics has been achieved through theoretical analysis and through critical comparison with the experiments. In summary, the objectives of the project have been achieved through the investigation and 5 journal papers have been published in international journals.

619511.value: Kinetics of phase transition of materials is very important for both academic research and practical applications. 619511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
619511.value: NiTi polycrystalline shape memory alloy (SMA) tubes are increasingly used in medical surgery and human implants due to the material’s excellent superelasticity and corrosion resistance. Experiments showed that the deformation of thin-walled NiTi tubes under tensile loading is realized by the formation and growth of a macroscopic helical domain of two dimensional (2D) nature. Under a high stretching rate, the domain in tubes grows rapidly with fast front propagation accompanied by heat release and heat conduction/convection. The intrinsic thermo-mechanical coupling in the phase transition process makes the domain evolution quite different from those under slow stretching. The complex interaction between the deformation (phase transition) and the created thermal field present serious difficulties in modeling the behavior of devices in real applications and in the control and reliability of the devices. Unfortunately, these important aspects remain much less explored and understood experimentally. In this project, we developed a mini testing system for small SMA tubes for synchronized high-speed data and surface image (both thermal and deformation) acquisition during the slow and fast domain evolution in the applied stretching rate range of 10-5/s-1/s. Systematic tensile tests were performed to obtain firsthand data on the loading rate dependence of domain patterns, front velocity and front temperature. Dimensional and thermo-mechanical coupling analysis were performed in parallel to reveal the roles of the phase transition time and the time scales of heat transfer in the observed rate-dependency. Front kinetics were examined and fundamental understanding of the phenomenon is achieved.

619611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
619611.value: Shape editing is useful for reusing existing 3D models and generating new shape variations for 3D games and computer animations. Over the last decade, many shape editing techniques that preserve geometric surface details have been proposed. They are highly successful for organic objects such as animals, faces, and body parts. Recently, the increased availability of man-made models in the public domain has switched graphics researchers' attention to editing engineered models. The design of editing tools for man-made models such as furniture, toys, electronic devices, and mechanical parts, is challenging because they typically comprise disconnected components and have numerous characteristic features (e.g., circular curves) and interrelations (e.g., coplanarity, symmetry) that need to be preserved during manipulation. Without prior analysis to understand the shape semantics and interrelations, editing can easily lead to meaningless shapes. An analyze-and-edit approach is therefore essential. This project aims at designing an editing framework that enables meaningful manipulation of multi-component man-made objects to produce a variety of shapes. We will develop powerful editing tools capable of faithfully delivering the user's intentions in modifying parts of an object while producing a variation that preserves the object’s original functionality. The main challenge is how to efficiently and effectively propagate the edit influence from the user’s manipulation to the rest of the object. We identify the key issues as how to analyze the shape, represent the characteristic features and inter-relations among parts, and translate them into modeling constraints. Some constraints may conflict with the user’s manipulation and therefore need to be prioritized. Moreover, as automatic shape analysis is challenging and cannot always capture the user's intent, user intervention must be allowed to make choices and produce alternative results. This requires designing a simple and easy-to-use user-interface (UI). The challenges of this project not only lie in designing effective algorithms and UI, the implementation of the system itself will take tremendous efforts. However, we are confident that we can complete the project as we have extensive research and development experience in shape editing and deformation. We expect the completion of this system to advance the state-of-the-art of semantics-based shape editing, making creation of shape variations easier for non-professional users. 在进行三维模型编辑时，模型本身的一些特征往往是需要保留的。例如模型局部轮廓的形状（如，圆形），或者模型不同组成部分之间的关系（如，共面）。一个好的模型编辑工具应该能够满足这些要求。然而设计这样的工具是具有挑战性的。这需要我们在编辑模型之前得到模型本身的特征信息。为得到这些信息，我们需要对模型进行分析。并且，为了更好的符合使用者的意图，自动分析之后的用户交互修改也是十分必要的。这项工作的目标是设计出一个可以让使用者更好的进行模型编辑的框架。我们会设计出强大的模型分析工具，以及友好的用户交互界面，从而帮助使用者在进行模型编辑时，按照其意图保留初始模型的特征。此外，我们会进一步扩展这个框架，使用户在这个框架下进行模型编辑时，能够将模型编辑为各种不同的风格，例如super-defomed 风格。

619611.label: Realisation of objectives
619611.value: Shape manipulation to produce variations of shapes is desirable as creation from scratch is time consuming. In this project, we investigate shape and structural preserving editing approaches that allow users to manipulate components while maintaining their relations. We introduce component-wise controllers that are adapted to the component characteristics inferred by shape analysis. A component-wise propagation algorithm is proposed to automatically preserve the established inter-relations while maintaining the defining characteristics of individual controllers and respecting the user-specified modeling constraints. We fulfilled the first objective by developing two shape segmentation techniques and a general shape analysis approach. The segmentation techniques are built upon simple concavity-aware harmonic fields and hierarchical spectral analysis, respectively. The general approach is based on analyzing a shape via computing shape descriptors for pairs of surface points rather than individual points as in previous approaches. We fulfilled the second objective by developing the dot-scissor interactive segmentation system and a scribble-based tool for quick selection of desired shape elements. The third objective has been fulfilled by a reduced model that propagates editing effect to other components through selective eigenvectors and two user interfaces for arranging and beautifying layouts of graphic elements. Our user studies confirm the intuitiveness of our interaction techniques and their performance improvement over traditional arrangement tools. We requested removal of the fourth objective since a research group in National Taiwan University has published a paper on super-deformed models and our attempts to develop a method of sufficient novelty than theirs was not successful.

619611.label: Major findings and research outcome
619611.value: We designed a shape manipulation framework that preserves relations between component-wise controllers as well as maintaining their definiing characteristics. For prior shape analysis, we designed two automatic algorithms to decompose shapes into meaningful components. The first algorithm stems from the idea of designing simple concavity-aware fields with the isolines naturally gathering at concave regions and serving as good segmentation boundaries. This work was published in the journal of IEEE TVCG paper [Au et al. 2012]. The second algorithm exploits a hierarchical spectral analysis to discover the relationship between the desired segmentation boundaries and the algebraic properties of its eigenvectors. We showed that eigenvectors derived from a concavity-aware Laplacian operator of a mesh can explicitly characterize the mesh concavity information. This work appears in the journal of Graphical Model [Wang et al. 2014]. In addition, we proposed a pairwise analysis approach that enables computation of discriminative descriptors from pairwise harmonic fields. This pairwise analysis approach leads to simple and efficient algorithms for various shape analysis applications, such as, intrinsic reflectional symmetry axis computation, matching shape extremities, and surface segmentation and skeletonization. This work appears in IEEE TVCG [Zheng et al. 2013]. To refine results of automaticl shape analysis, which cannot always reflect users' intent, we developed interactive tools. We designed an interactive segmentation tool which we call the Dot Scissors [Zheng et al. TVCG 2012]. This tool reduces the user's effort in segmentation to placing only a single click where a cutting boundary is desired. We also addressed interactive selection of shape elements, which is a frequently performed operation in many editing scenarios. Our scribble-based tool, which we call Lazy Selection, enables quick selection by only stroking roughly through shape elements, including 2D well-defined shapes and 3D segmented components [Xu et al. 2012]. In edit propagation, we proposed a reduced model that is independent of handle configuration, allowing the user to dynamically update the handle set without noticeable waiting time [Wu et al. 2014]. This solves the common problem of existing handle-based editing methods of requiring costly re-computation for every handle set updating. The challenge is to find propagation fields that are independent of the handle set. We use selected eigenvectors of the Laplacian operator as propagation fields and adopt the transformations of isolines sampled from the fields as the deformation descriptors. Finally, we presented a user interface for aligning and distributing graphic elements in a group-aware manner {Xu et al. 2015] and a user interface for beautifying a layout of shape elements. These works were presented at CHI conference [Xu et al. 2015] and UIST conference [Xu et al. 2014], respectively. These interfaces can be extended to editing and refinement of 3D shape elements.

619611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
619611.value: Structural and shape preserving manipulation has been widely studied and several effective approaches have been proposed in recent years. They are powerful for generating novel model variations from existing models. Such approaches have further inspired works on shape creation through part replacement or recombination, producing even more non-trivial and interesting variations. More recently, topology-varying shapes through structural blending has even been proposed. Maintaining functional plausibility in such topology-varying shapes however becomes more challenging. It would be interesting to conduct in-depth studies of functional plausibility of such synthesized shapes.

619611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
619611.value: Modeling of 3D shapes from scratch is cumbersome and difficult to most users. A desirable alternative is to create model variations through propagating modeling constraints from the manipulated component to the other components. We have developed a editing framework that supports structural-preserving manipulation and proposed several state-of-the-art segmentation methods, interaction techniques and propagation strategies that enable such editing. Our research works have led to several publications in top conferences and journals, and thus have achieved good visibility.

619711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
619711.value: The outcome of this research project will be an efficient and robust technique for performing various tasks in computer vision wherein large-scale 3D reconstruction is highlighted: the billions of photos on the Internet provides the fastest growing and most diverse image collection ever. These photos were captured at different times of the day and from almost every angle and location one could ever imagine. How can vision researchers effectively make use of such a rich image collection? Fundamental vision problems need to be revisited when operating on the Internet photo collection. For example, overlapping images of the same scene are usually available. Even for a single landmark, the diversity of these images renders scale-invariant matching insufficient. Useful constraints such as the epipolar constraint can help in delineating good matches from outliers, but non-existent epipolar geometry can easily be produced by matching similar structures (e.g., windows) on different objects (e.g., buildings). Presently, RANSAC and related techniques are used in outlier rejection, but random sampling is computationally infeasible in processing thousands of images. We propose to revisit tensor voting, a computational framework for robust feature extraction and segmentation in computer vision: • A closed-form solution to tensor voting We propose to first carry out theoretical study to develop a closed-form solution to tensor voting. This new solution promises a continuous, efficient and exact solution to tensor voting, suitable for large-scale vision reconstruction problems. • Robust and accurate parameter estimation The second phase of the project involves integrating the optimal tensor obtained at each site into an Expectation-Maximization (EM) framework, combining the advantages of EM and TV (tensor voting). The result will be a robust and accurate parameter estimation procedure which does not require the random sampling typical in existing techniques which can be very time-consuming. • Applications To demonstrate the promise of the new formalism, we will perform quantitative studies on epipolar geometry estimation and 3D reconstruction from uncalibrated images in large-scale reconstruction, and compare the results with those from conventional tensor voting as well as other state-of-the-art techniques, using challenging synthetic as well as real data. Some of the preliminary findings in this proposal were published in the proceedings of IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition 2010 (CVPR'10). 這個課題的研究成果將是一個高效並且可靠的多任務計算機視覺技術。該技術強調大規模三維重建任務：在互聯網上有數以億計的照片。它們是擴張最快，範圍最廣的數據庫。你能想像到的任何時間任何地點任何角度所拍攝的照片幾乎都可以在其中找到。 視覺研究員如何高效地利用這大量的圖片? 當對網絡上的圖片進行處理時，我們需要對視覺的根本問題重新思考。舉例來說，互聯網通常有同一場景重疊的多張圖片。即使對於某個地標，這些圖片的多樣性使得尺度不變的匹配算法顯得不足。有用的限制，比如外極線約束，可以幫助我們找到好的匹配、剔除異常匹配。可惜，通過匹配不同物體（比如大廈）上相似的結構（比如窗戶），我們會很容易得到不應存在的外極線幾何機構。現時，雖然RANSAC及相關的一些技術可以被用來去除異常值，但是對於處理上千張圖片，隨機抽樣算法在計算量方面是不可行的。 我們提議重新考慮張量投票，這是一個在計算機視覺裡具有強大的特徵提取和分割的計算框架。我們將會研究以下領域： - 張量投票的解析 - 強大而且準確的參數估計 - 具體的應用 這份提案裡面得到的初步結果已經發表在2010年的電氣與電子工程師協會會議中的計算機視覺和模式識別的論文集中。

Furthermore, based on the findings, we further research on relevant problems surrounding robust and accurate computer vision, which is the goal of the proposed closed-form tensor voting in the provision of a tool to benefit the computer vision society. Relevant research in image matting / segmentation and machine learning was performed, which has resulted in four high-quality conference publications in top computer vision venues: CVPR and ICCV.
