619711.label: Major findings and research outcome
619711.value: 1. A closed-form solution to tensor voting We prove a closed-form solution to tensor voting (CFTV): Given a point set in any dimensions, our closed-form solution provides an exact, continuous, and efficient algorithm for computing a structure-aware tensor that simultaneously achieves salient structure detection and outlier attenuation. The major finding was published in IEEE TPAMI 2012 (see Part C). 2) Robust and accurate parameter estimation using EMTV Using CFTV, we prove the convergence of tensor voting on a Markov random field (MRF), thus termed as MRFTV, where the structure-aware tensor at each input site reaches a stationary state upon convergence in structure propagation. We then embed structure-aware tensor into expectation maximization (EM) for optimizing a single linear structure to achieve efficient and robust parameter estimation. Specifically, our EMTV algorithm optimizes both the tensor and fitting parameters and does not require random sampling consensus typically used in existing robust statistical techniques. Relevant finding also published in TPAMI (Part C). 3) Applications While working on closed-form tensor voting we found a novel way to solve the image matting problem which also has a closed-form solution. Specifically, we are interested in a general alpha matting approach for the simultaneous extraction of multiple image layers. Our matting technique, aptly called KNN matting, capitalizes on the nonlocal principle by using K nearest neighbors (KNN) in matching nonlocal neighborhoods, and contributes a simple and fast algorithm giving competitive results with sparse user markups. Relevant closed-form solution and results are published in CVPR 2012 (Part C). Since the goal of computer vision is to understand (uncalibrated) images, in this project, we studied relevant problems in applying machine learning for image understanding. First, distance metric plays a key role in grouping superpixels to produce object proposals for object detection. We develop a novel distance metric for grouping two superpixels in high-complexity scenarios. Combining them, a complexity-adaptive distance measure is produced that achieves improved grouping in different levels of complexity. See CVPR 2015 paper (Part C) for this region-based method. We also proposed a method that locates at the other end of the spectrum as region-based method: to optimize a closed curve that predicts an object silhouette tightly bounded by a given image window. Relevant results are reported in ICCV 2015 (Part C). Finally, we enable the sliding window search by proposing compact square object images which relax the requirement where image windows of all possible aspect ratios have to be tested. Relevant results are also reported in ICCV 2015 (Part C).

619711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
619711.value: The success of this GRF research project can be translated into development in 1) further fundamental research and 2) technology transfer. For 1), the PI will strike to excellence in pertinent future academic and fundamental research in computer vision and machine learning, given the promise evidenced by the peer-reviewed and top publications in computer vision derived directly from the project: 1 TPAMI, 2 ICCV papers and 2 CVPR papers. Specifically, we will look into relevant problems in object detection and recognition and deep learning in computer vision, which are hot topics not only in academia but also in industry. For example, Facebook and other social media have been actively seeking technical solutions for robust object recognition (e.g. face). For 2), we will work with the technology transfer center at HKUST to explore possible patent applications for the most recent publications. For CFTV and EMTV that are directly derived from this project, we have made our source codes public via authors homepage and the IEEE digital libraries that accompany with the publications.

619711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
619711.value: This project concerns with fundamental research in compute vision, specifically on 3D reconstruction from 2D photos casually shot around a 3D object to be digitized, which can be large and tall buildings and landmarks. This GRF project and the results achieved are significant in academics evidenced by the high-quality and top publications in computer vision. The project has a significant potential in turning the pertinent research into products related to 3D cartography where intensive research effort are being devoted by the research teams in Google Maps and Apple Maps. We have studied relevant problems in image matting (which has applications in film and TV post-production), region-based and contour-based object proposals generation methods, and also proposed a novel and efficient strategy that can produce accurate solution to object detection and recognition. 619911.label: Project Objectives
619911.value: Cooperative Sensing Scheduling as Combinatorial Optimization One of the fundamental issues in cooperative sensing is how to appropriately assign different SUs to sense different PUs' channels (when CRNs are constrained by the number of SUs and the number of available PUs' channels). We will formulate this cooperative sensing scheduling problem as a combinatorial optimization problem. A specific utility function which reflects CRNs' energy efficiency will be introduced as the whole CRNs' objective function. Meanwhile, the SU's QoS provisioning and the PUs' incumbent protection serve as the constraints. We hope that the solution of our formulated CSS problem can provide the optimal policy which guides CRN to appropriately assign different SUs to perform cooperative sensing on different PUs' channels with the objective to maximize their collective utilities. To Perform Theoretical Analysis of the CSS Problem with Homogeneous SUs The CSS problem is essentially a combinatorial optimization problem. We will first consider the case of homogeneous SUs, i.e. the sensing performance of each SU is the same. Such combinatorial problem is difficult to solve in general, and previous works have mainly relied on heuristic algorithms which, however, sacrificed the optimality. Different from these previous approaches, we propose a theoretical framework to analyze the CSS problem. Based on the framework proposed, several interesting and important properties (e.g., the “threshold structure” of the optimal policy) will be identified to characterize the essence of CSS. Furthermore, we will develop novel algorithms to find the optimal policies efficiently. To Perform Theoretical Analysis of CSS Problem with Heterogeneous SUs In practice, the sensing performance of SUs differ from each other because of their different locations and channel conditions, etc. Based on our previous framework, we will further investigate the case of heterogeneous SUs. It is of great importance to investigate the impact of heterogeneous sensing performance, because inappropriate scheduling will limit CRNs' overall performance. Such extension is natural but highly challenging, which will greatly strengthen and generalize our framework. QoS Provisioning for Each Individual SU Previous works have usually ignored the QoS provisioning for SUs, even though a QoS guarantee is indispensable to the success of CRNs. From the spectrum sensing point of view, specific QoS requirements should be designed and incorporated into the CSS problem. We will first introduce the metrics that measure the QoS of each individual SU, and then analyze the CSS problem with QoS provisioning for both cases of homogeneous and heterogeneous SUs. Finally, we will develop efficient algorithms to solve the CSS problems with QoS provisioning. The joint consideration of QoS provisioning and energy-efficiency is precisely the novelty of our proposal. To Further Improve the Adaptive Sensing Duration and the Number of SUs for sensing Based on our previous results, we now aim to explore the CSS problem in depth. First, we will treat the sensing time as another decision variable in our CSS problem. Second, we will explore the possibility that not all SUs will be involved in the sensing procedure. The rationale is that some SUs may be located at unfavorable positions, and thus contribute little to the overall accuracy of spectrum sensing but may still lead to time-overhead and power consumption. The performance of cooperative sensing can be improved significantly when we jointly consider the aforementioned two extensions.

619911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
619911.value: With the rapid growth of wireless communication applications and services, the excessive energy consumption of wireless network infrastructures and devices has been a cause of concern for regulatory and engineering communities alike [1]. It has been widely recognized that the development of energy-efficient network architectures, protocols and transmission technologies, i.e. the so-called "Green Communications" (GC), is essential to the sustainable development of the communication industry. Cognitive Radio (CR), which aims to tackle the spectrum shortage problem [2] through intelligent secondary spectrum utilization, is a promising candidate to realize green communications [3] [4]. However, the special functionalities like spectrum sensing and spectrum management required by CR raise great challenges to achieving energy-efficiency. To improve the accuracy of spectrum sensing, a spectrum sensing technique with cooperation among multiple Secondary Users (SUs) is proposed. However, cooperative sensing incurs extra costs including time-overhead, power consumption, and burden of sensing-result feedback. Driven by the aforementioned reasons, our proposal aims to investigate the fundamental problem of Cooperative Sensing Scheduling (CSS). Our objective is to find the optimal sensing scheduling policy which achieves both sensing accuracy and energy-efficiency for Cognitive Radio Networks (CRNs) with guarantees of individual SU's Quality of Service (QoS). The fundamental question of CSS is how to select different SUs to sense different Primary Users' (PUs') channels, especially when CRNs are constrained by both the number of SUs and the prescribed incumbent protection for PUs. Two fundamental tradeoffs exist in this scheduling problem, namely, (i) tradeoff between achieving high sensing accuracy in individual channels and widely exploring transmission opportunities in different channels, and (ii) tradeoff between multiple-SUs sensing diversity and additional sensing cost (e.g., time-overhead, power consumption). In this proposal, we will focus on these two tradeoffs and investigate them in detail. We will formulate the cooperative sensing scheduling problem as a combinatorial optimization problem and establish a theoretical framework to analyze it. We aim to study the intrinsic structure of our CSS problem, and design efficient algorithms to find the optimal polices based on the structural results. More importantly, we will study the methods to improve the energy-efficiency of CSS with QoS provisioning for each individual SU. QoS provisioning is an important issue for CRNs, but so far it is not well explored by others as far as we know. We believe that our proposal will contribute novel designs and deep insights to the implementation of energy-efficient CRNs.

619911.label: Realisation of objectives
619911.value: (1) Realisation of objective 1: We have modeled the problem under the homogeneous scenario in two different aspects: throughput maximization and energy efficiency maximization. We designed the protocol for the system, modeled the wireless signals of interest and formulated the problem as a combinatorial optimization problem. This objective has been 100% completed. (2) Realisation of objective 2: We first mathematically analyzed the term of overall probability of false alarm in the objective functions and showed that under the constraint of required overall probability of detection, such term is a decreasing discrete convex function with respect to the number of cooperating Secondary Users (SUs) in many cases. We then derived the properties of the optimal solution indicating the number of channels that should be sensed and the number of SUs on sensing a certain channel. We developed a simple algorithm which enables the combinatorial problem to be solved efficiently and optimally. This objective has been 100% completed. (3) Realisation of objective 3: We extended the energy-efficiency maximization problem to different heterogeneous scenarios. For the case of channel heterogeneity (in terms of received SNR, achievable throughput and idle probability), we showed that the steepest descent algorithm for M-concave function maximization can be applied to achieve optimality. For the general case, we leveraged the insights gained from the investigation of homogeneous case to design a low-complexity heuristic method which shows little performance loss compared to the optimum and outperform the existing approaches. This objective has been 100% completed. (4) Realisation of objective 4: We considered the scenario where Primary User (PU) channels are heterogeneous and each SU has its own QoS requirement. The optimal solution can be found by trying sub-problems corresponding to different combinations of three or less channels and solving each sub-problem by applying Discrete Convex Analysis. This objective has been 100% completed. (5) Realisation of objective 5: We formulated the problem of joint SU sensing assignment and sensing duration optimization as a mixed integer nonlinear program. We resorted to the fractional programming framework to pave the way for solving the problem of interest. Based on the analytical results, we divided the optimization on the continuous variables and the integer variables into two subproblems which can be individually solved efficiently. It is shown that the energy consumption and the expected throughput of the cognitive radio network are well balanced. This objective has been 100% completed.

619911.label: Major findings and research outcome
619911.value: (1) Properties of the overall probability of false alarm We showed that under the constraint of required overall probability of detection, the overall probability of false alarm is a discrete convex function with respect to the number of Secondary Users (SUs) joining sensing in most cases. (Zhang&Tsang 2015, Section 8) (2) Optimal sensing assignment for throughput maximization in homogeneous networks We proved that the optimal number of PU channels sensed can be found using bisection method and the corresponding user assignment can be obtained in closed form. Under the practical network parameters, it has been demonstrated that spreading out SUs to sense as many channels as possible is the optimal policy in most cases. (Zhang&Tsang 2015, Section 8) (3) Relationship between number of channel sensed and overall number of cooperating SUs We found that for homogeneous networks, adding one more SU to join the sensing process leads to the same number of channels being sensed as before, or one more channel being sensed. The number of optimal number of channels sensed can then be determined incrementally with respect to the different overall number of cooperating SUs. This finding leads to the development of efficient algorithm and enables the network to easily adapt to the change of user population. (Zhang&Tsang 2015, Section 8; WICON 2011, Section 9) (4) Application of discrete convex optimization algorithms We showed that for the network with channel heterogeneity, the objective function of the optimization problem possesses the M-concavity property with given number of cooperating SUs and number of PU channels. The efficiency of the algorithm for finding the optimal solutions can be greatly improved. (Zhang&Tsang 2015, Section 8) (5) SU assignment in heterogeneous case We have the following findings. Firstly, most of the cooperating SUs are assigned to sense the channels with moderate received SNR. The ones with very low or very high SNR are allocated with only a few SUs. Secondly, more SUs are allocated to sense the channels with large expected capacity (by considering the idle probability) even the received SNR of such channels are very low or very high. The reason behind is that the expected capacity provides linear increase to the expected throughput achieved, while the sensing performance gained from more cooperating SUs increases in a concave fashion and the marginal increment is diminishing. (Zhang&Tsang 2015, Section 8; Sun&Tsang 2013, Section 8)

619911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
619911.value: (1) We study the slotted CRN synchronized with the primary users. It would be natural to consider performing sensing and transmission scheduling under asynchronous CRN environment. One possible direction is to combine the sensing outcomes with the state transition models of PU channels, so as to predict the PU activity during the transmission phase in a CRN slot. We conjecture that more PU channels may be exploited in this case since even several SUs perform sensing cooperation on a PU channel, the improvement gained at the sensing phase may be impaired due to the possible channel occupancy state alteration in the transmission phase. (2) In cooperative sensing procedure, each individual SU is required to transmit its own local sensing results to the BS for result fusion, and BS will distribute the final decisions on channel occupancy states back to the SUs. To further reduce the energy consumption, one possible way is to design a cooperative sensing protocol where SUs are not required to report their own sensing result if their sensing performance is lower or higher than certain threshold. The logic behind this design is similar to the transmission of only the ACK messages in the Internet protocol.

619911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
619911.value: This research studies the fundamental question in cooperative sensing: how to properly schedule the secondary users to sense the individual primary channels. We provide low-complexity methods for determining the policies including (1) the set of cooperating SUs, (2) the set of sensed channels, (3) the assignment of SUs on these channels and (4) the length of executing sensing, which fill a gap in the design of cognitive radio networks. Our findings add a new dimension to the cooperative sensing research, and several following works from the research society have been triggered. By utilizing the policies developed by us, the cognitive radio networks can transmit more data with the same amount of sensing resource and reduce the energy consumed on the mandatory sensing phase. Consequently, the operators can enjoy a lower operational expense and contribute to ICT sector’s efforts on energy consumption reduction. The methods proposed are well suited in real-time operations due to their shorter computation time compared to other methods. Specifically, our methods allow fast adaptation to the changes of user population size in the network, guaranteeing the network performance to be kept under the time-varying operation environment.

620311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
620311.value: Liquefaction refers to a range of phenomena in which the strength and stiffness of soils are significantly reduced during earthquake shaking. Liquefaction occurs most commonly in saturated loose granular soils under cyclic loadings. In the past, liquefaction has caused severe damages to civil structures, including overturning of buildings on liquefied ground due to loss of bearing capacity, flow failure of earth structures, large lateral spreading of liquefied soils that damaged port structures, and excessive post-liquefaction ground settlements. Although many important advances have been made, the basic procedures to evaluate liquefaction triggering and induced ground displacement are mainly empirical and based on the back-analysis of a few case histories that may not be similar to the site and earthquake scenario being analyzed. In these procedures, the transit, complex earthquake loadings are usually characterized using the peak value of the ground motion acceleration, while more important information such as the shaking energy, duration and frequency content of the earthquakes are neglected. On the other hand, the empirical approaches characterize a soil’s resistance to liquefaction using simple indices from in-situ tests without taking into account the fundamental stress-strain-strength mechanisms of liquefiable soil behavior. These shortcomings can lead to large uncertainties in liquefaction prediction and inadequate mitigation designs that are overly conservative or even unsafe. The proposed research will explore an innovative ground motion characterization and selection scheme that is more suitable for liquefaction analyses. The scheme can effectively capture the joint distribution of multiple key ground motion parameters to improve the accuracy of liquefaction prediction. Fully nonlinear dynamic analyses will be performed on various soil grounds and earth embankment systems, where advanced constitutive models will be used to realistically characterize the nonlinear soil behaviors. The proposed project will investigate the predictive capabilities of various intensity measures regarding pore pressure generation and permanent deformation in liquefiable soils, as well as the effects of ground motion characteristics on the evolution of important physical quantities during the liquefaction process. The project will help lay down the basis towards an improved procedure for liquefaction hazard evaluation and mitigation. The proposal requests HK$1,024,650 (equivalent to US$132,037 including 15% on cost) to support two graduate students to conduct a three-year research on this topic. Results from this project will be available to the public through data sharing and publications. 飽和鬆散沙土的強度通常在地震作用下會顯著降低，此現象稱之為土動力液化。土動力液化在過去曾對土木工程結構造成了嚴重的破壞，包括由於喪失承載力而引起的結構翻倒，土工結構的滑動破壞，液化引起地基產生過大水平位移而造成結構的嚴重損壞，以及液化後大規模的土體沉降破壞。 儘管對液化的研究有了很大的進展，然而，預測液化誘發及液化引起的相應位移的方法仍然是建立在對少數液化個案研究的經驗基礎上，而這些個案的場地及地震場景特性可能與實際情況完全不同。在經驗方法中，複雜的地震時變過程被簡化為峰值動力加速度特性，而更為重要地震波特性，例如震動的能量，時程和地震波的頻域特性則被完全忽略了。另一方面，經驗方法僅僅用某些簡單的物理量來描述土壤抗液化的能力，並沒有考慮土的應力-應變-強度的非線性力學特性。這些存在的種種不足導致難以準確的預測土動力液化，並由此造成不恰當的防治液化的工程方案。 本研究將探索一種適用於液化分析的新型的地震波特性描述和選擇的方法，以有效地描述多個關鍵地動參數的聯合分佈特性，提高液化預測的準確度。本研究利用先進的土力學本構模型来準確模擬土的非線性動力特性，並對多種土體結構進行非線性動力分析。本研究將探究多種地動參數對土體液化過程中水壓力的生成，重要物理參數的演化，以及液化引起的永久變形的影響，將有助於改進液化災害預測，評估和防治的方法。

620311.label: Realisation of objectives
620311.value: Project objective 1 is fully realized during the research. First, the PI investigated the efficiency and effectiveness of various ground-motion intensity measures, and identified Cumulative Absolute Velocity (CAV), Arias intensity and spectral accelerations are most critical intensity measures for the development of liquefaction and permanent deformations in soils under earthquake loading [cf. Journal publication No. 1 ]. These intensity measures contain important information such as the shaking energy, duration and frequency content of the earthquakes. In particular, CAV and Arias intensity take into account the cumulative effects of ground motion and total input energy. Therefore, these intensity measures are more appropriate to predict the buildup of pore-water pressures in liquefiable soils. In this project, the PI further explored characteristics of these important intensity measures using a large database containing thousands of recorded ground motion data: (a) A simple empirical prediction equation was developed to predict the statistical distribution of CAV given an earthquake scenario [cf. Journal publication No. 4]. We conducted validation tests on the proposed CAV model and found the CAV has higher predictability than other intensity measures. The proposed model employs only four parameters and has a much simpler functional form, meanwhile, it has a similar predictive capability compared with other more complicated models. (b) During the investigation, we found that considering these multiple ground-motion intensity measures is important in seismic hazard analysis and ground motion selection process. Since one intensity measure only presents certain attribute of the earthquake motion, using multiple intensity measures could significantly increase the accuracy of the prediction. However, the statistical properties of the joint occurrence of multiple intensity measures are not well studied. To overcome this difficulty, we spent considerable efforts to develop empirical correlations between Arias intensity, CAV, spectral accelerations and other intensity measures [cf. Journal publication No. 2, 5, 6]. The correlation allows joint occurrence of multiple intensity measures be predicted for a given earthquake. Geostatistics analyses are also performed using strong-motion data from 11 recent earthquakes that occurred in California, Japan, Taiwan, and Mexico. The results indicate that the spatial cross correlations of these intensity measures are strongly influenced by the spatial distribution of regional site conditions [cf. Journal publication No. 5, 6]. We also demonstrated that the permanent displacements in soil slopes during earthquakes can be more faithfully predicted when correlated intensity measures are incorporated in a fully probabilistic framework [Journal publication No. 9]. An illustrative example is presented to highlight the importance of the spatial correlation and the advantage of using spatially correlated vector IMs in seismic hazard analysis of soil slopes. (c) Correlation models developed in (b) paved a way to the successful development of an innovative ground motion selection and modification scheme for time-history analyses of soil deformation and liquefaction, as stated in Objective 1. The scheme jointly selects ground-motion time histories according to the distribution of these vector intensity measures (CAV, Arias intensity and spectral shape etc.) using correlation models. In the end, an interactive tool is developed for selecting earthquake ground motions for time-history analyses of soil deformation and liquefaction. The so-called Design Ground Motion Library (DGML) is equipped with a graphic user interface and has the broad capability of searching for time history record sets in the database on the basis of spectral shape and other ground motion characteristics [Journal publication No. 10]. It can be well used to select ground motions for time-history analyses of soil deformation and liquefaction. Objective 2 is also fully realized during the research. First, we developed an advanced constitutive model to realistically simulate nonlinear soil behaviors and liquefaction phenomenon under earthquake loading. The new soil model, termed as the “modified bounding surface model”, adopts a new modulus formulation and is capable of simulating dilative and contractive behaviors of both loose and dense sands, which is key to pore pressure generation during liquefaction process [Journal publication No. 7]. The model is fully validated using a series of undrained cyclic simple shear tests on Fraser river sand. In order to identify most important model parameters in liquefaction initiation and development process, the PI conducted study on the response sensitivity analysis of the bounding surface plasticity model, in collaboration with Prof. Quan Gu at Xiamen University. We developed new sensitivity analysis algorithm using direct differentiation method and implemented it in finite element framework [Journal publication No. 3]. The study identified key model parameters related to pore pressure generation and permanent deformation in liquefied soils, and the algorithm is systematically validated through simulation of a liquefiable soil site at Port Island, Japan, under earthquake loading. Finally, the advanced soil model was implemented in a finite element framework to study the predictive capabilities of various intensity measures regarding pore pressure generation, permanent deformation and the evolution of important physical quantities during the liquefaction process. During the course, we solved a number of numerical difficulties involved in fully coupled soil-fluid simulation. Particularly, a stabilized iterative scheme was proposed for coupled fluid-soil systems using Reproducing Kernel Particle Method [Journal publication No. 9]. Fully coupled numerical simulation were carried out to study the liquefaction mechanism and post-liquefaction deformation of loosely deposited seabed under earthquake wave recorded during the 2011 Tohoku earthquake in Japan. The computation results show that the numerical model is capable of capturing a variety of nonlinear interaction phenomena between the composite breakwater and its seabed foundation. This investigation demonstrates that an advanced numerical method is promising in realistic evaluation of seismic performance of liquefiable soils [Journal publication No. 11, 12].

620311.label: Major findings and research outcome
620311.value: Major findings: 1. Identified CAV, Arias intensity and spectral accelerations are most critical intensity measures for the development of liquefaction and permanent deformations in soils under earthquake loading [cf. Journal publication No. 1 ]. A simple empirical model is developed to predict the statistical distribution of CAV given an earthquake scenario [Journal No. 4]. 2. Developed empirical correlations between Arias intensity, CAV, spectral accelerations and other intensity measures based on recorded strong motion data [Journal No. 2, 5, 6], and discovered the spatial cross correlations of these intensity measures are strongly influenced by regional site conditions. 3. Developed a fully probabilistic framework to use multiple intensity measures in predicting the permanent displacements of soil slopes under earthquakes [Journal No. 9]. 4. Developed DGML -- an interactive tool to select ground motions for nonlinear analysis of liquefiable soils considering joint distribution of key intensity measures such as spectral shape, CAV and Arias Intensity [Journal No. 10]. Presently, the DGML has been adapted as an online application by the Pacific Earthquake Engineering Research Center (PEER) to manage its strong-motion database. 5. Based on observations from laboratory tests, a new bounding surface model was developed to improve the simulation of liquefaction behaviors of both loose and dense sands. The model demonstrates excellent capabilities through benchmarking with laboratory tests. [Journal No. 7]. Key model parameters related to soil liquefaction were also identified through a novel sensitivity analysis algorithm [Journal No. 3]. 6. A stabilized iterative scheme was proposed for coupled numerical simulation of fluid-soil systems [Journal No. 9]. Fully coupled finite element simulations demonstrated that the advanced numerical model can realistically simulate the liquefaction mechanism and post-liquefaction behaviors [Journal No. 11, 12]. The project resulted in a total of 12 SCI journal publications -- most of them are in top journals in this field, including 2 in Earthquake Engineering & Structural Dynamics, 3 in Soil Dynamics and Earthquake Engineering and 2 in the Bulletin of Seismological Society of America, 1 paper in Earthquake Spectra, Journal of Engineering Mechanics and International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering etc. In addition, the project also resulted in 9 papers published in prestigious international conferences, including 15th World Conference on Earthquake Engineering (2012, Portugal), 11th International Conference on Structural Safety and Reliability (2013, New York), 10th US National Conference on Earthquake Engineering (2014, Anchorage), and International Symposium on Geomechanics from Micro to Macro (2014 Cambridge, UK).

620311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
620311.value: Ground-motion correlation models were developed using the PEER-NGA strong motion database, which contains around 3000 recorded accelerations. In recent years, more recorded earthquake data and case histories of soil liquefaction become available. It is possible to further extend the current study using the updated strong motion database, and benchmark the numerical simulation with new case histories of liquefiable sites.

620311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
620311.value: Soil liquefaction refers to a range of phenomena in which the strength and stiffness of soils are significantly reduced during earthquake shaking. In the past earthquakes, soil liquefaction has caused severe damages to civil structures. Yet, the current design practice is primarily based on simple empirical methods, the complicated earthquake loading and fundamental mechanism of liquefiable soils are not well understood. The objectives of the project are two-fold. First, the study improves the characterization of earthquake loading. We identified the most critical ground-motion intensity measures for the development of liquefaction and permanent deformations in soils under earthquake loading. We further explored characteristics of these intensity measures and their inter-relationships using a large number of real recorded earthquake data. Method and tools for selecting ground motions using these measures are also developed. Second, the study improves the understanding of soil behaviors in liquefaction. We developed advanced numerical model to realistically simulate soil liquefaction by taking into account the fundamental soil mechanics. Using modern computational technology, the project successfully simulated liquefaction process and post-liquefaction behaviors of soils. The project help lay down a scientific basis towards an improved procedure for evaluating and mitigating liquefaction hazards worldwide.

620811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
620811.value: 我們提出了一種新型建模方法，同時學習音樂結構的多個方面，如旋律，節奏，諧波級數，或歌曲的結構，從訓練語料庫之間的關係的統一，獨立的任務模型的目的。 概率，信息理論，和貝葉斯模型近來紛紛進入電腦音樂學，完善基於非隨機的語法，偏好，約束，和其他純粹的邏輯方法的早期型號。概率模型的優點，包括噪音的可擴展性，魯棒性，歧義下選擇最優的假設，優雅降級的原則，在整合多種來源的證據，以及眾多的機器學習技術，自動訓練。 然而，仍有許多工作要做。概率模型的音樂是一個令人振奮，但仍然非常年輕的攻擊線。目前的做法往往是相當的限制，只要每個模型解決個別問題的關鍵發現，米發現，旋律識別，音高或節奏的期望，轉錄，音樂信息檢索，或類似的。 由於許多的概率音樂模型，我們的做法，個別方面的音樂旋律（間距序列），節奏（節拍序列），諧波級數（和弦序列），​​歌曲結構（作曲序列），等等，都可以接受的觀點建模為一個隨機語法生成的單獨的語言。使用傳統的隨機上下文無關文法，可謂相當複雜，嵌套結構。然而，我們的新方法的基本概念的關鍵是把我們的工作重點，明確學習這些單獨的語言之間的關係。 要做到這一點，我們將把學習傳導最近開發的建模技術。形式上，傳導是兩種語言，這正是我們希望誘使之間的關係。隨機轉導文法（STGs）傳導的概率雙語語法，描述兩種語言之間的概率結構的關係。這意味著，STGs不會受到非隨機傳導模型的過於剛性約束，並能自動學習。 在這樣做，我們將充分利用從模擬計算語言學和統計機器翻譯研究我們的研究小組率先STGs的工作，現在許多國家最先進的機器翻譯系統的基礎，但有突飛猛進的20年迄今為止利用電腦音樂學。我們的新的概率音樂模型將利用STGs的眾多應用，包括對齊的雙語語料庫，無人監督的分割和雙語語料庫，自動感應雙語書信，語法歸納為 STGs，以及許多其他的註釋。我們將開發新的STG為基礎的模型，最近這些技術的學習的旋律，節奏，節奏，歌曲結構，和其它樂器的子語言之間的概率關係，和MIDI / MusicXML音樂的大型語料庫實證檢驗。

620811.label: Realisation of objectives
620811.value: In computer musicology, we have advanced the state of the art by developing unified, task-independent, corpus-trained models that simultaneously integrate multiple aspects of music structure ranging from flamenco percussion and palmero languages to hip hop challenge and response languages. From the cognitive science standpoint, we have advanced our understanding of music not only by building computational models that explain how relations between different aspects of music can be learned, but also by showing that these same foundational competences simultaneously explain both our linguistic and our musical capabilities. In terms of computer music applications, we have demonstrated how stochastic transduction grammar (STG) based models can be exploited for new applications for computer music, with flamenco music recognition to the point where automatic accompaniment can be generated, and improvised freestyling responses can be generated to arbitrary hip hop challenges. From a formal language theory perspective, we have not only explored efficient new algorithms for learning STGs well-suited for representing the relations between musical sublanguages, but also further identified areas like musical pitch languages where continuous valued STGs would be highly desirable, leading to a newly developed type of STG employing continuous space vector encodings with extremely broad new potential.

(Computer music applications) Demonstrate how such new STG-based models can be exploited for new applications for computer music, such as music information retrieval, music recognition, automatic accompaniment, and/or other similar applications.

(Formal language theory) Explore new types of STGs (Stochastic Transduction Grammars), and show how their properties are particularly well-suited for representing the relations between musical sublanguages; and develop efficient new algorithms for applying and inducing such STGs.

620811.label: Major findings and research outcome
620811.value: This project has developed and evaluated the first ever compositional models of structural relationships between musical languages based on stochastic transduction grammars. The project has shown how the complex structural relationships can be learned via purely unsupervised methods exploiting a variety of new Bayesian and minimum description length techniques, top-down segmenting vs bottom-up chunking vs ternary segmenting search, and merging vs splitting of nonterminal categories [3, 5, 6, 7, 11, 14, 24, 25]. These techniques have been compared on learning improvisational structural relations between various musical language pairs including cajon and palmero languages in flamenco [13], between challenge and response languages in English hip hop freestyling [1, 2, 10], between challenge and response languages in styles of the French Maghreb [12, 18], and other musical languages in ongoing experiments.

620811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
620811.value: Our data analyses in the course of this project have led us to study the continuous values found in musical languages for pitches, resulting in unexpected and exciting new continuous space vector encodings of stochastic transduction grammars [25]. This new approach, which is closely related to recursive neural networks, opens vast new avenues for exploration in subsequent research projects. Approaches developed in this project are also impacting work on improved metrics for measuring the quality of learned structural relationships by integrating stochastic transduction grammars [15, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23] which can then be leveraged in improved learning algorithms by employing automated versions of the metrics as objective functions during training [4, 8, 9, 16]. The foundations laid in this project create broad opportunities for exploring a much wider range of musical languages. Collaborations are now being initiated with music technology groups/projects in India and Spain to experiment with learning structural relations within those improvisational musical styles.

620811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
620811.value: Music is not only made up of many musical languages, but more importantly, the relationships between multiple musical languages. Limitations on the mathematical modeling side have, however, inhibited modeling of the complex types of relationships generally found in musical languages. We have developed a novel modeling approach that simultaneously learns unified, task-independent models of the relation between multiple aspects of music structure from training corpora. A broad array of new unsupervised learning techniques that learn Stochastic Transduction Grammars of different kinds, with various performance tradeoffs, has been developed and studied. The automatically learned models are particularly well suited for modeling the challenging communicative and improvisational aspects of many music genres not previously well studied. The foundations developed here open numerous avenues of attack for modeling many under-studied phenomena in music across regions and traditions, and contribute to our understanding of the common key cognitive competences underlying both our unique language and unique musical abilities.

620911.label: Project Objectives
620911.value: Analyzing and modeling the complex temporal and spatial behaviors of transient P/G noises at system level: We will systematically analyze and model the complex temporal and spatial behaviors of transient P/G noises, the interactions of multiple overlapped P/G noises, and their effects on processing units and on-chip memories in different states. A P/G noise simulation and analysis platform will be developed for the modeling. A parameterized modeling template will be developed for the platform to capture both traditional two-dimensional MPSoCs and new three-dimensional MPSoCs with different configurations. The template will model MPSoCs along a large number of dimensions, including (i) power grid structures, (ii) number, sizes, and power consumptions of processing units and on-chip memories, (iii) 3D integration structures of on-chip memories and processing units, (iv) package structures, (v) number, locations, and connectivity of through-silicon vias in 3D MPSoCs. Establishing adaptive runtime protection protocols and developing a corresponding scalable architecture: We will establish runtime adaptive protocols and develop a corresponding scalable system architecture to protect MPSoCs from transient P/G noises through hardware-software collaborations. The protocols will coordinate hardware-software collaborations on P/G noise mitigation. Besides passively avoiding P/G noises, we will explore an active P/G noise mitigation technique and use PUs and memories as dynamic system-level decaps to suppress P/G noises. A scalable system architecture will be developed to effectively execute the protocols for MPSoCs with a growing number of PUs and memories. A cycle-accurate model will be developed for the system architecture. Developing an adaptive task scheduling scheme: We will develop an adaptive task scheduling scheme to manage the impacts of transient P/G noises on performance and energy efficiency. It will optimize task schedule at runtime based on the transient P/G noises detected by the sensors. Evaluating the dynamic runtime method and system architecture: We will perform rigorous evaluations of the dynamic runtime protection method and system architecture in multiple embedded application domains. We will compare the dynamic method with static protection methods and analyze the performance, area, and energy efficiency under different embedded system usage scenarios.

620911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
620911.value: All walks of human life have increasingly depended on embedded systems such as cellphones, digital video cameras, Internet routers, and wireless base stations. As the complexity of embedded systems burgeons, multiprocessor system-on-chip (MPSoC) has become an attractive platform for embedded systems, because integrating a system or a complex subsystem on a single chip with multiple processing units and memories provides better performance and energy efficiency and lower cost per function. The advancement of nanotechnologies and three-dimensional integration technologies will help to sustain this trend. While these technologies enable MPSoCs to integrate a growing number of processing units and memories, they also make MPSoCs more susceptible to various transient reliability threats such as power/ground (P/G) noises and soft errors. Without proper protection, transient threats can result in data corruption without notice, and severely compromise system reliability. For instance, P/G noises in MPSoC power grid caused by powering off a processing unit can result in timing violations and false results being latched in registers. This type of silent data corruption can cause unpleasant user experiences or even serious danger, and it is a challenging issue in embedded system design. Traditionally, static protection methods are used to protect MPSoCs from transient reliability threats based on static analysis at design time. They try to determine the scales of worst-case transient threats at design stages, and statically reinforce MPSoCs using more robust circuits. As the complexity of MPSoCs continuously grow, static methods dramatically increase MPSoC cost due to their significant protection overhead, and limit the scalability and flexibility of MPSoCs. The root of this problem is that static methods rely on fixed protections against transient threats. Fixed protections are designed for worst cases, but worst cases only account for a small portion of the total MPSoC run time. This makes static protection methods become burdens for MPSoCs in most of the time. This project aims to develop a systematic dynamic protection method and a scalable system architecture to adaptively mitigate transient reliability threats at runtime. We will use a major type of reliability threat, transient P/G noises, as an example. The dynamic protection method will predict and monitor reliability threats at runtime, share related information among processing units and memories, and mitigate threats through hardware-software collaborations. Preliminary results show that dynamic protections can improve MPSoC reliability with significantly lower overhead than static protections. This project will substantially extends our initial work along many new dimensions.

620911.value: This project developed a systematic dynamic protection method and corresponding scalable architecture to mitigate transient reliability threats at runtime. 621011.label: Project Title(Chinese)
621011.value: 求解高超声速流的高阶气体动理学方法的构造

621011.label: Project Objectives
621011.value: Based on the integral solution of the BGK-type Boltzmann equation, construct a time-dependent solution for the gas distribution function under the initial piecewise discontinuous high-order distributions of mass, momentum, and energy around a cell interface. Evaluate the time-dependent fluxes and develop a high-order finite volume method for the Navier-Stokes equations. Validate the above scheme in the two-dimensional viscous flow computations, such as the laminar boundary layer, Stokes flow, and viscous shock structures. At the same time, compare the current high-order scheme with the second-order gas-kinetic Navier-Stokes flow solver in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and robustness. Develop high-order boundary condition around a curved solid boundary. Apply the scheme in aerospace applications, such as hypersonic flow around a cylinder and shock-boundary layer interaction, and compare the numerical solutions with possible experimental measurements.

621011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
621011.value: The Navier-Stokes equations are the basic governing equations for a viscous, heat conducting fluid. They may be used to model the weather, ocean currents, tsunami propagation across an ocean, water flow in a pipe, the air's flow around a wing, and motion of stars inside a galaxy. The solutions of these equations can be obtained through numerical simulation, which demands the use of accurate numerical methods for solving the associated systems of partial differential equations. Even though significant advances have been made in the last two decades on the construction of conservative, non-linear schemes of high order of accuracy in both space and time, a dominant mechanism in the flux evaluation across a cell interface is still based on the Riemann solution for the inviscid flow. To approximate the dissipative terms across a cell interface with discontinuities has great difficulty. In the hypersonic flow computations, most Riemann solvers with low numerical dissipation encounter shock instability, i.e., the carbuncle phenomenon, which affects the capturing of strong shock and the flow field behind it. In this proposal, based on the Boltzmann equation, we are going to design a high-order multidimensional flux function under a discontinuous initial condition. In the Riemann solver, an equilibrium solution with infinite number of particle collision is assumed, and this solution may not be valid inside a highly non-equilibrium numerical shock layer. The gas-kinetic scheme follows a gas evolution process from an initial non-equilibrium state to an equilibrium one with the increasing of particle collision. The inviscid and viscous fluxes of the Navier-Stokes equations can be obtained together from the time evolution of a gas distribution function starting from piecewise discontinuous polynomials for the mass, momentum, and energy distributions. Subsequently, the mass, momentum, and energy transport across a cell interface can be evaluated by taking moments of the gas distribution function. The high-order (more than second-order) multidimensional gas-kinetic flux function constructed through this project can be used under many current existing high-order numerical frameworks, such as WENO-type finite volume, Discontinuous Galerkin finite element, and spectral volume methods. The application of the high-order methods will be concentrated on the challenging problems in the current computational fluid dynamics research, such as the accurate evaluation of viscous stress and heat flux in the hypersonic flow computation. Navier-Stokes（NS）方程是描述具有粘性和热传导性质的流体的基本控制方程。它可以用来描述空气流动，海水流动，海啸，甚至恒星在星系中的流动。NS方程的解可以通过在计算机上的模拟而得到。虽然过去20年计算流体力学有长足的进步，在其基本算法中，在网格界面处的通量还是基于求解无粘流的Riemann问题而构造的。在初始条件为间断的情况下， NS方程中耗散项的高阶离散变得十分困难。在高超声速流的计算中，大多数基于Riemann问题求解器的格式会遇到激波不稳定性。本研究是要构造一个基于Boltzmann方程的高阶气体动理学格式。Riemann解的成立需要有无穷多的粒子碰撞来支持，而这在有强非平衡效应的数值激波结构中不成立。而气体动理学方法考虑到气体分子通过碰撞从非平衡流到平衡流的演化过程。对应NS方程中的通量可以通过对随时间演化的分布函数的求矩直接得到。从而求得通过网格界面处的质量，动量，和能量的传输。通过本研究得到的高阶气体动理学流量也可以和其它高阶格式结合，像有限体积的WENO方法，有限元的间断Galerkin方法，以及谱方法等。同时高阶气体动理学格式也将应用于在计算流体力学中具有挑战性的流动问题，像精确求解在高超声速流中通过物体表面的摩擦阻力和热流。

621011.label: Realisation of objectives
621011.value: Based on the gas-kinetic theory, the Navier-Stokes equations can be derived from the Boltzmann equation using the Chapman-Enskog expansion. Therefore, a Navier-Stokes (NS) flow solver can be obtained by solving the Boltzmann equation, or simplified kinetic collision models. Since the kinetic equation is a first-order partial differential equation, it does not require the smoothness and continuity in its initial flow condition. It naturally fits with the high-order piece-wise discontinuous initial data from a high-order reconstruction. The initial piece-wise discontinuous polynomials of the flow variables can be directly used in the development of the high-order gas-kinetic scheme. In the kinetic formulation, a gas distribution function contains both equilibrium and non-equilibrium states, the inviscid and viscous terms are obtained simultaneously. With the support of the current research grant, we have developed a high-order gas-kinetic scheme for the Navier-Stokes solutions under the piecewise parabolic initial distributions for the mass, momentum, and energy, which are separated by discontinuities at a cell interface. The developed scheme has a third-order accuracy. Also, due to the inclusion of both normal and tangential derivatives of flow variables, the scheme is naturally a multidimensional method, which has excellent capability to capture the complicated flow evolution, such as vortex flow and boundary layer. Due to the kinetic dissipative mechanism in the shock layer, the gas-kinetic scheme is very robust and has excellent capability to capture shock wave. At the same time, the effect of the flux functions on the performance of high-order schemes has been carefully evaluated. Based on the same WENO reconstruction, two schemes with different flux functions, i.e., the fifth-order WENO method and the WENO-Gas-kinetic scheme (WENO-GKS), have been compared. The fifth-order finite difference WENO-SW scheme, which is based on the Steger-Warming flux splitting for inviscid terms, the sixth-order central difference for viscous terms, and three stages Runge-Kutta time stepping for the time integration, has been used for comparison as well. The finite volume WENO-GKS uses the same WENO reconstruction. But, it evaluates a time dependent gas distribution function along a cell interface, and updates the flow variables inside each control volume by integrating the flux function along the boundary of the control volume in both space and time. In order to validate the robustness and accuracy of these schemes, the methods are tested under a wide range of flow conditions: vortex propagation, Mach 3 step problem, and the cavity flow at Reynolds number 3200. Our study shows that both WENO-SW and WENO-GKS yield quantitatively similar results and agree with each other very well provided a sufficient grid resolution is used. With the reduction of mesh points, the WENO-GKS has less numerical dissipation and present more accurate solutions than those from the WENO-SW in all test cases. For the Navier-Stokes equations, since the WENO-GKS couples inviscid and viscous terms in a single flux evaluation, and the WENO-SW uses an operator splitting technique, it appears that the WENO-SW is more sensitive to the WENO reconstruction and boundary treatment. In terms of efficiency, the finite volume WENO-GKS is about 4 times slower than the finite difference WENO-SW in two dimensional simulations. The current study clearly shows that besides high-order reconstruction, an accurate gas evolution model or flux function in a high-order scheme is also important in the capturing of physical solutions. In a physical flow, the transport, stress deformation, heat conduction, and viscous heating are all coupled in a single gas evolution process. Therefore, it is preferred to develop such a scheme with multi-dimensionality, and unified treatment of inviscid and dissipative terms. A high-order scheme does prefer a high-order gas evolution model. Even with the rapid advances of high-order reconstruction techniques, the first-order dynamics of the Riemann solution becomes the bottleneck for the further development of high-order schemes. In order to further improve the efficiency of the high-order gas-kinetic scheme, a compact third-order gas-kinetic scheme has been developed for the compressible Euler and Navier-Stokes equations. The main reason for the feasibility to develop such a high-order scheme with compact stencil, which involves only neighboring cells, is due to the use of a high-order gas evolution model. Besides the evaluation of the time-dependent flux function across a cell interface, the high-order gas evolution model also provides an accurate time-dependent solution of the flow variable at a cell interface. Therefore, the compact scheme not only updates the cell averaged conservative flow variables inside each control volume, but also tracks the flow variables at the cell interface at the next time level. As a result, with both cell averaged and cell interface values, the high-order reconstruction can be done compactly. The cell interface time-dependent flow variables can be used for the initial data reconstruction at the beginning of next time step. Even with compact stencil, the scheme has a third-order accuracy in the smooth flow regions, and has favorable shock capturing property in the discontinuous regions. It can be faithfully used from the incompressible limit to the hypersonic flow computations, and many test cases have been used to validate the high-order compact scheme. In comparison with many other high-order schemes, the compact gas-kinetic method avoids the use of Gaussian points for the flux evaluation along the cell interface and the multiple stage Runge-Kutta time stepping technique. With the same stencil of a second order scheme, numerical tests demonstrate that the compact third order gas-kinetic compact scheme is as robust as well-developed second-order shock capturing schemes, but provides more accurate numerical solutions than the second order counterparts. The scheme has been applied in the studies of hypersonic flow around a cylinder and shock-boundary layer interaction. The numerical solutions have been compared with the experimental measurements, which fully validate high-order kinetic schemes for hypersonic flow computations. As a continuous study of higher order schemes, a fourth-order gas-kinetic scheme has been developed recently, which has excellent numerical performance in comparison with any other state of art higher order schemes.

621011.label: Major findings and research outcome
621011.value: With the support of the RGC project 621011, we have conducted the research related to the development of high-order gas-kinetic scheme for the Navier-Stokes solutions and the development of the unified scheme for the computational fluid dynamics in the whole flow regimes. The scheme developed is a time accurate method, which has third-order accuracy in the space and time. At the same time, the inviscid and viscous terms are coupled in a single framework. Most other high order schemes for the compressible flow simulations use first-order Riemann solver for the inviscid flux evaluation and central difference for the viscous terms. The time accuracy is achieved through the Runge-Kutta time stepping. Therefore, in comparison with other high-order schemes, the gas-kinetic method is more robust and efficient for the unsteady flow computation. Due to its kinetic approach, such as the inclusion of particle transport effect, the accuracy of the gas-kinetic scheme for hypersonic flow computations has been validated. In the current study, the high-order gas-kinetic scheme mainly uses the WENO reconstruction method for the initial data evaluation at the beginning of each time step. In order to improve the scheme in the applications with complex geometry, such as the flow simulation with unstructured meshes, we have further developed the scheme with compact support. Since a time accurate gas evolution model is used in the gas kinetic scheme, at the cell interface besides the construction of the numerical fluxes, the conservative flow variables on the cell interfaces can be updated as well. Therefore, the gas-kinetic scheme provides more information in the gas evolution, which can be used to develop a compact high-order scheme. The scheme has been successfully developed and used in the engineering applications.

621011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
621011.value: The third-order scheme has been successfully developed for the hypersonic flow computations. Theoretically, even higher-order scheme can be developed. Since the gas-kinetic kinetic scheme provides a time-accurate flux function starting from discontinuous piecewise polynomial flow distributions around each cell interface. With the use of time derivative of the flux function, a two-stage time stepping method has been recently proposed in the design of a fourth-order time accurate method for the Euler and Navier-Stokes equations. In comparison with the one-stage time-stepping third-order gas-kinetic solver, mainly developed under the current project, the fourth-order method not only reduces the complexity of the flux function, but also improves the accuracy of the scheme. Most importantly, the robustness of the fourth-order GKS is as good as the second-order one. Perfect numerical solutions have been obtained from the high Reynolds number boundary layer solutions to the hypersonic viscous heat conducting flow computations. At the current stage, we believe that the higher-order gas-kinetic schemes can be faithfully used in the engineering applications and many institutes start to use the kinetic schemes in their specific applications.

621011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
621011.value: The Navier-Stokes equations are the basic governing equations for a viscous, heat conducting fluid. They may be used to model the weather, ocean currents, tsunami propagation, water flow, aerodynamics, even stars motion in a galaxy. The solutions of these equations can be obtained through numerical simulation, which demands the use of accurate numerical methods for solving these partial differential equations. Even though significant advances have been made in the last two decades on the construction of conservative, non-linear schemes of high order of accuracy in both space and time, there is space to design even higher-order accurate schemes for the capturing of large spatial and temporal evolution of flow motion, such as aero-acoustics and turbulence. In the hypersonic flow computations, to accurately capture the viscous and heat conducting effect around the surface of aero-vehicle is still demanding higher-order schemes. In this project, based on the Boltzmann equation, we have developed higher-order multidimensional scheme for the hypersonic flow simulations. The scheme has been applied in the engineering applications, such as the aero-vehicles in the near space flights.

621111.label: Project Title(Chinese)
621111.value: 实现城市交通可持续发展的可自由交易电子路票系统

621111.label: Project Objectives
621111.value: To investigate tradable credit schemes with heterogeneous travelers in terms of their different valuations of travel time savings. To develop a practical implementation method of the tradable credit scheme when the demand functions and travelers’ valuations of travel time savings are not readily available as is the case in practice. To examine dynamic evolution and stability of price and flow under tradable credit schemes.

621111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
621111.value: Problems of sustainability in transportation are already quite noticeable in almost all large cities worldwide, and it is clear that the current unrestricted use of private cars is at the center of this problem. Due to congestion, more travel time is wasted on the roads, drivers are more likely to get stressed and frustrated, which in turn causes accidents. Forecasts of traffic condition are less reliable, so punctual arrival becomes difficult and travellers suffer losses from early departure or late arrival. Traffic congestion also contributes substantially to environmental problems. As an alternative or supplement to the road pricing for the reduction of traffic congestion and air pollution, this project proposes to develop a simple but forceful tradable travel credit scheme to curtail the unrestricted use of private cars. Such a scheme would have three parts. 1) The government initially issues credits to all eligible travelers. 2) The government predetermines the charge or the consumption rate for each roadway link. 3) Credits can then be traded freely in a competitive market without government intervention. This type of scheme now abounds in the realm of environmental policy (for example, in the Kyoto Protocol and the European Union Emission Trading Scheme) and its applications in traffic congestion management are being considered. The first part of the project will investigate tradable credit schemes with heterogeneous travelers. Compared with the case with homogeneous travelers, this becomes more complicated but more interesting when credits are freely traded not only among travelers on different paths and origin-destination pairs, but also among travelers with different incomes or values of time. The second part will consider practical implementation of tradable credit schemes with limited information. A trial-and-error method will be developed for implementing the tradable credit scheme when the demand functions and travelers’ valuations of travel time savings are not readily available in practice. The third part will study hybrid schemes for multi-objective network optimization, such as minimization of total network emissions and total network travel times. Alternative forms of credit charges, such as a distance-based or time-based charge, together with traditional congestion pricing, are considered as well for effective traffic control and management. The analyses and developments and the policy implementation of the results will be demonstrated with Hong Kong's urban network. The proposed study has the potential as a powerful tool to manage network mobility, traffic congestion and environmental quality in an effective, efficient and equitable manner. 如今，快速增长的私家车数量和不受限制的使用频率使得交通拥堵问题成为越来越多城市的一块心病。频繁的交通拥堵不仅造成大量的时间浪费，容易引起驾驶员的焦虑和抑郁增加交通事故的发生频率，还大大增加交通预测的难度，降低可靠性，给正确选择出行时间带来困难。同时，由于交通拥堵显著增加的汽车尾气排放，已经成为空气污染的重要来源。因此，如何让城市交通可持续性地发展问题成为一个迫在眉睫的课题。 为了限制过多的机动车使用，缓解拥堵，我们在这个项目中提出了一种全新的能够代替征收拥堵费的方案－ 可自由交易的电子路票系统。这个系统简单而有力：首先，政府在每个阶段（如每个月）初给所有符合资格的人发放免费的电子路票；之后，车辆在使用不同道路时会被扣取不同数额的电子路票（扣取数额的方案由政府事先决定并公示）；这些电子路票可以在市场上自由交易，而政府只负责市场监管。类似这样的系统在环境保护领域已经有不少例子，例如京都协定、欧盟排放权交易计划。 这个项目分为三个部分：第一部分我们研究上述电子路票系统在异质用户下的应用效果。跟只存在同质用户的情况不同，异质用户由于不同的时间价值，在行车路径和电子路票买卖的选择上会有差异，使得问题更加复杂化。第二部分，我们考虑当实际情况中信息量不完全的情况下（如需求和价格关系不明确，异质用户的时间价值不明确等），如何通过反复实验的方法来不断优化此电子路票系统并尽可能快速地达到最优。第三部分，我们讨论用电子路票系统与其他方式结合的办法来实现多目标优化（如最小化污染气体排放，最小化总体出行时间等）的可行性。此外，除了基于道路的电子路票扣取方案，我们还将考察基于车辆行驶距离或者行驶时间的扣取方案，以及与传统的拥堵费征收方案的结合，是否能够更为有效疏导和调控交通流量。 有关该电子路票系统的效果分析、结论以及实际应用我们将用香港的城市交通网络来展现。我们相信，该电子路票系统有极大的潜力成为缓解城市拥堵，减少环境污染，实现城市交通可持续发展的一剂良药。

621111.label: Realisation of objectives
621111.value: Throughout the three and half years research period; we were able to investigate all the study issues raised originally in the proposal. All aspects of the network mobility management with tradable travel credits in the original proposal were addressed. Through the project, we developed and evaluated the tradable credit scheme for urban traffic congestion control. This method has been proposed in the transportation literature but its rigorous quantitative analysis is rather limited. The proposed scheme have three parts. 1) The government initially issues credits to all eligible travelers. 2) The government predetermines the charge or the consumption rate for each roadway link. 3) Credits can then be traded freely in a competitive market without government intervention. This type of scheme now abounds in the realm of environmental policy (for example, in the Kyoto Protocol and the European Union Emission Trading Scheme) and its applications in traffic congestion management were first examined in a formal manner in this study.

621111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
621111.value: Through the study, we gained a better command of the economic and operations research approach to tackling the various traffic congestion and mobility management problems. We found that the methodology that we developed can be further extended to deal with the periodic adjustment of the tradable credit schemes with day-to-day flow dynamics. Further research is being carried out along this line.

621111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
621111.value: Problems of sustainability in transportation are already quite noticeable in almost all large cities worldwide, and it is clear that the current unrestricted use of private cars is at the center of this problem. Due to congestion, more travel time is wasted on the roads, drivers are more likely to get stressed and frustrated, which in turn causes accidents. Forecasts of traffic condition are less reliable, so punctual arrival becomes difficult and travellers suffer losses from early departure or late arrival. Traffic congestion also contributes substantially to environmental problems. As an alternative or supplement to the road pricing for the reduction of traffic congestion and air pollution, this project developed a simple but forceful tradable travel credit scheme to curtail the unrestricted use of private cars. Such a scheme would have three parts. 1) The government initially issues credits to all eligible travelers. 2) The government predetermines the charge or the consumption rate for each roadway link. 3) Credits can then be traded freely in a competitive market without government intervention. The study advanced the fundamental theory of traffic network analysis by providing an innovative method to manage network mobility based on solid theoretical background. The research results can help the planner identify when and under what conditions a tradable credit scheme or a hybrid between tradable credit scheme rationing and pricing can be Pareto-improving in a manner that reduces traffic congestion while making no travelers worse off. Therefore, the proposed topic is of widespread interest and has many potential applications.

621211.label: Project Title(Chinese)
621211.value: 长尾分布下的个性化标签推荐

621211.label: Project Objectives
621211.value: We will develop a novel and general transfer-learning framework for tag recommendation for user-tags in the long tail of an item-frequency/user-tag distribution where the tagging data are very sparse. In this framework, we will model a user as a learning task, different contents as domains, and different learning methods as models. A hybrid content-based and collaboration based approach will be designed, in which similar users and similar contents can be filtered from auxiliary tasks for a given target learning task (i.e. a target user). A number of similarity metrics will be evaluated and new metrics designed. Based on the above transfer learning framework and similarity metrics, our second objective is to develop adaptive task-selection algorithms for transfer learning under the condition of data sparsity. We will ensure that the algorithm is efficient and effective even when a large number of potential auxiliary tasks exist. Task selection filters will be designed to particularly address the data sparsity problem by using content-based similarity metrics in combination with the user-similarity based approaches. Active learning will be integrated with transfer learning to query the users when needed. Scalable task and domain selection strategies will be designed using distributed algorithms. Our next objective is to design model selection strategies for each pair of auxiliary and target learning tasks. The model-selection strategy must be able to filter out a large number of candidate learning models that one can use for transfer learning even when the distributions of the source and target learning tasks are different. Both density-ratio based methods and confidence-based methods will be designed for this new transfer learning problem. We will develop a scalable prototype system for personalized tag-recommendation based on distributed algorithms, and evaluate the developed framework and system on real-world social Web data. We will disseminate the research results in the form of high-quality publications.

621211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
621211.value: Tagging, a growing social phenomenon, allows millions of users to freely associate free-form keywords, known as tags, to Web objects such as songs, photos, videos, tweets and even friends. Personalized tag recommendation refers to the act of suggesting a set of tags to best describe a given item for a user, taking into account the individual’s preferences and interests. Due to the long-tail nature of social Web distributions, for a given user, many tags are only assigned to a few items. As a result, the available tagging data are often too sparse to build an accurate personalized tag recommendation model. In this project we propose to develop a personalized tag recommendation solution for tags that are new or sparsely used by a user in the past. These tags are often located in the long tail of a power-law distribution, which is built on item frequencies versus user-tag pairs. Making these long-tail recommendations can help users with emerging and niche interests tag their items, and can cater to new users of a social Web system. Making personalized tag recommendations for these items will be very challenging. Our solution will be a combination of content based classification and user-similarity based collaboration approaches. To account for a shortage of the training data for building the personalization model, we plan to design transfer-learning solutions where the tagging knowledge are extracted and filtered from a large number of users and items, and transferred to a target user. Our transfer learning solution will take into account users’ preferences and distribution differences. We will design new selection strategies for domains, tasks and models in order to facilitate transfer learning under the condition of data sparsity and to ensure positive knowledge transfer. A contribution to the social Web mining area is that our solutions can recommend tags to users when the user-tag-item data are very sparse; thus new users, new user interest and new items can be handled well. Furthermore, a contribution to transfer learning area is that in this research, we will consider a much larger number of tasks than has previously been encountered. We will use extensive real-world data to carry out this research, and develop and evaluate a scalable prototype system for tag recommendation in social Web applications. 越来越多的用户利用自由产生的关键字标签来标记如歌曲，图片，视频等网络对象， 以提供有效的标注。 这些标签的一个用途是， 可以利用它们以帮助搜索和推荐。 我们在这个项目中， 关心以下的关键问题： 如何利用大量的互联网上的标签， 帮助个性化标签的建议，以最好地为一个用户特定的个人提供服务？这一问题，由于社会网络分布的长尾性质，对于给定的用户，许多标签只分配到几个项目。因此，可用标记数据往往过于稀疏，从而难以建立一个准确的个性化标签的建议模型。 在这个项目中，我们建议制定个性化的标签建议的解决方案。我们将内容的分类和用户的相似度加以组合，协作的方法，用类似用户的数据，以补足数据不足的问题。 我们计划设计迁移学习解决方案的标记知识的提取和过滤，从大量的用户和项目迁移到目标用户。我们的迁移学习解决方案将考虑到用户“好和分布的差异。我们将使用广泛的现实世界的数据进行这项研究，并制定和评估标签建议，在社会Web应用提出可扩展的系统。

621211.label: Realisation of objectives
621211.value: We have developed a novel and general transfer-learning framework for tag recommendation. Typically, tag recommendation is understood as taking a social network of users and make collaborative recommendations based on the similarity relationship. In this work, we showed that tag recommendation is but a learning problem. In addition, we showed that to tackle the long-tail problems, we can use a mixture of collaboration and content based methods can be used for solving the cold start and data sparsity problems. Transfer learning can solve the problem of cross-domain and cross-tail recommendations in this problem, where we have developed a prototype system to show the approach's effectiveness. Thus, we have achieved all four objectives as stated below.

621211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
621211.value: The tag recommendation problem is widely applied in crowd sourcing projects, where the wisdom of the crowds are used to incentivize the population to provide the needed annotations for data. Such tag data are noisy but contains degrees of truth. In this case, machine learning and tag recommendation can be applied to filter out the noise and ensure that the true annotations are obtained. Thus, a future work is how to ensure that the tag recommendation methods can still work under noisy and incomplete data situation.

621211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
621211.value: In today's online world, the meaning of data is of critical importance because high quality annotations are hard to come by. To obtain the annotations, we can exploit knowledge from other domains, where the annotations have been obtained, and transfer the tagging knowledge to a new domain, or to parts of the data where annotation is sparse. In this work, we took a machine learning approach, whereby a computer system is designed to be adaptive in its ability to transfer from known annotations to parts of the data where we have sparse or no annotations. This solution combines machine learning, tag recommendation, and transfer learning. This work is critical for online shopping, online service recommendations, and mobile APP recommendations, as well as many other O2O services.
