621411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
621411.value: The Boundary Element Method (BEM) is a well-recognized powerful numerical method for solving engineering problems. With its reduced dimensionality and its ability in capturing the steep gradients of fields, the BEM, as compared to other methods such as the finite element method, is particularly advantageous for solving problems with rapidly varied fields, for example, stress at the crack front; and for problems with complex geometry or with moving boundaries. The recently developed matrix sparsification techniques have enabled large-scale simulation with the BEM, and the BEM has since become a leading method in several areas such as computer-aided design of very large system integration circuits and large-scale dynamic linear fracture analysis. The unique advantages of the BEM unfortunately have not been fully utilized in nonlinear problems. Most successful practical applications of the BEM have been linear and homogeneous problems. A major hurdle in the application of the BEM to non-homogeneous and nonlinear problems is the presence of volume integrals in the integral formulation. If a volume-fitting discretization is employed, the BEM would lose its advantage in solving problems with complex domains and moving boundaries. Despite a number of approaches that have been developed for the evaluation of volume integrals, a scheme that is both accurate and efficient is yet to be developed. The proposed research aims at the development of such a scheme so as to develop an efficient integral equation approach for non-homogeneous and non-linear problems. Our approach is based on a novel integration scheme for volume integrals. Accuracy is ensured because volume integration is performed directly without any approximation. The efficiency comes from the facts that no volume-fitting discretization is required and integration can be accelerated using matrix sparsification techniques. In addition, an improved matrix sparsification technique, the precorrected-FFT (p-FFT) technique, will also be developed to further reduce computational complexity in both surface and volume integration. If successful, this project will produce an improved p-FFT technique with a much reduced computational time and memory size, and a volume-discretization free evaluation scheme for volume integrals. With these two key elements, an efficient and accurate integral equation approach for nonhomogeneous and nonlinear problems is likely to result from this research. As such the application scope of the BEM could be much broader and the unique advantages of the BEM can be utilized in solving problems for which no satisfactory solution approaches are currently available, for example, large-scale nonlinear fracture analysis. 边界元法是一种公认的有效工程计算方法。和有限元方法相比，边界元法的优点在于它的低一级维数和高精度，特别是在处理存在高梯度的问题。因而边界元法特别便于处理具有复杂的区域, 无限域及移动边界问题。近期发展的快速边界元法更极大提高了其性能。因而在某些应用领域，譬如大型集成电路设计和线性断裂问题，边界元法都是首选的方法。 然而到目前为止，边界元法最成功的应用例子还仅局限于线性及齐次问题，它的各种优势并未能在非齐次和非线性问题中体现出来。其主要的原因是因为对于这些问题，相关的积分方程里出现了体积分项。如果按照常规方法去数值计算这项，域网格就不可避免。这样边界元法便丧失了其在网格分割上的优点。尽管一些计算体积分的方法已经提出并发展到一定程度，一个有效又精确的方法至今还未出现。 这个课题的主要目标是发展这么一种有效而又精确的边界元法。主要采用的方法基于一个新型处理体积分的方法。它的精度来自于这个体积分是直接计算的而不是近似的，有效度则是因为域网格在这个方法里根本不需要。另外，快速算法，譬如说，p-FFT方法将会被利用来加速体积分和面积分的计算。如果成功的话，这个课题的成果将可被利用来解决一些至今未能模拟的问题，例如，大型非线性断裂分析。

621411.label: Realisation of objectives
621411.value: The two objectives proposed in the proposal have all been achieved. We have successfully derived Galerkin tensors for Laplace and elastic kernels. These tensors are the key elements in the proposed integration method. Based on these tensors, the accelerated volume integration schemes that work for some common kernel functions arising in the boundary integral formulations have been developed and implemented. The acceleration technique employed is the pre-corrected FFT method, which is extended and implemented to accelerate the volume integrals as well as the boundary integrals present in the nonlinear problems. By combining the volume integration scheme with the standard Boundary Element Method, we have constructed boundary-only integral methods named the “Grid-based volume integration method” for solving nonlinear Poisson and thermoelastic problems. The performance of the method has been demonstrated through several benchmark problems related to nonlinear Poisson and thermoelastic problems. In addition, we have conducted a careful theoretical study of the accuracy and efficiency of the method for quasi-nonlinear problems. Out study concludes that the convergence rate of the method is the same as that of the standard boundary element method for solving linear problems, and the complexity of the method is comparable to that of the linear problems. These findings indicate the effectiveness of the method for solving nonlinear problems. In addition to the two objectives proposed in the proposal, we have also extended the method and applied it to solve geometrically nonlinear elastic problems. Such problems are frequently encountered in many engineering fields such as microelectromechanical systems (MEMS). This work was completed during the one-year no-cost extension. We have developed the algorithms and tested the method and code through a series of benchmark problems including a model problem involving a MEMS switch.

621411.label: Major findings and research outcome
621411.value: An accelerated boundary element method has been developed for solving nonlinear Poisson problems and geometrically nonlinear elastic problems. This is the first truly boundary method, that is, without the need for a volume fitting mesh for solving nonlinear problems. As such, it is particularly suitable for problems with moving boundaries and/or infinite domains. In addition, with the accelerated scheme, this method is much more efficient than meshless methods and can solve large-scale practical problems. A total of six journal papers have been produced from this work. Among them, four papers have been published and two are under preparation.

621411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
621411.value: The ultimate goal of the proposed research is to develop an efficient and accurate simulation method for nonlinear fracture analysis. It is well known that the BEM is one of the most successful methods for fracture analysis, particularly when there are multiple cracks and the structure is subjected to dynamic loading. However, the current application is limited to linear analysis only due to the difficulties associated with the volume integrals. With the developed volume integration scheme and the proven efficiency, we are confident that our method can be extended to model and simulate nonlinear fracture mechanics. This would be our future work. We plan to submit a GRF proposal next year on this topic.

621411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
621411.value: The Boundary Element Method (BEM) is a well-recognized powerful numerical method for solving engineering problems. With its reduced dimensionality and its ability to capture the steep gradients of fields, the BEM, compared to other methods such as the finite element method, is particularly advantageous for solving problems with rapidly varing fields and for problems with complex geometry or with moving boundaries. However, the unique advantages of the BEM have not been fully utilized in nonlinear problems. Most successful practical applications of the BEM have been in linear and homogeneous problems. A major hurdle in the application of the BEM to nonlinear problems is the presence of volume integrals in the integral formulation. If a volume-fitting discretization is employed, the BEM would lose its advantage on mesh generation. In this project, we have developed an efficient and accurate volume integration scheme and combined it with conventional BEM to construct an efficient integral approach for solving nonlinear problems. The performance of the integral method has been successfully demonstrated using various benchmark cases related to nonlinear Poisson problems and geometrically nonlinear elastic problems. The developed method could be extended to solve other nonlinear problems such as nonlinear fracture analysis, for which no satisfactory solution approaches are currently available.

621711.label: Project Objectives

621711.label: Realisation of objectives
621711.value: This was a fabrication intensive project and the devices proposed under both the objectives required non-standard wafers either in the form of silicon-on-insulator (SOI) or silicon-on-glass (SOG). They went through several iterations of process optimization to address the challenges. SOG wafers were prepared in house by anodically bonding standard silicon wafers on borosilicate glass wafers. Initially, the device prototypes for both the objectives were completed on SOI wafers. The devices for dielectrophoretic (DEP) separation (Objective 2) worked quite well whereas those for impedance analysis (Objective 1) did not meet the expectation. For the latter, further investigation suggested that the buried oxide layer is insufficient to shield the substrate parasitic capacitance. Hence, the devices were unable to distinguish the solutions of distinct conductivities based on their impedance measurements. The devices also suffered from a rapid roll-off in their frequency response. It became inevitable that these devices had to be fabricated on SOG to avoid the silicon substrate parasitic capacitance. After this corrective step, the devices fabricated on SOG were able to distinguish tumor cells from red blood cells based on their impedance signatures. Both the objectives were achieved using blood samples collected from healthy donors and spiked with human colorectal tumor cell line (HCT-116) as a model for circulating tumor cells (CTCs). Although we performed pilot experiments with blood samples collected from colorectal cancer patients in collaboration with Queen Elizabeth Hospital, the number of samples (below 10) analyzed was insufficient to draw statistically significant conclusion. This was mainly due to the emphasis placed on the device development that kept us from testing further clinical samples. While satisfactory performance was obtained in isolating tumor cells from lymphocytes through the interdigitated 3D silicon microelectrodes (Objective 2), we saw the pressing need to revise the design for the continuous-mode operation wherein tumor cells can be isolated from a constant supply of blood in one step; this was required because CTCs are rare cells and likely to be found in a large volume. In experiments, however, we encountered electrokinetic forces (e.g., electrothermal drag) that overshadowed the DEP forces and led to the enrichment of all blood cells regardless of their type. Therefore, this revised design was appropriately characterized for the plasmapheresis application instead. For the capacitance cytometer (Objective 1), the 3D silicon microelectrodes featuring linear sidewalls were used and impedance signals of individual tumor and blood cells were measured helping us correctly identify cell type.

621711.label: Major findings and research outcome
621711.value: A key outcome of our research is the development of electrodes with 3D castellated silicon blocks that bring immediate advantage to electrical and fluidic integration. Such design allows for electrode segments to be placed across the flow chamber without interrupting the flow and yet retain a monolithic construct that is electrically intact. Leveraging this unique profile, we built an interdigitated 3D comb array wherein the digits consist of repeating units of electrode segments with their castellated sidewalls giving rise to an array of round pores, so-called rings (Objective 2). The DEP devices based on these structures were initially fabricated on SOI wafers and their proof-of-concept demonstration was realized using polystyrene microspheres (JMEMS, 2013). We subsequently characterized the DEP devices with biological cells. We used human colorectal tumor cell line, HCT-116, and spiked these cells into lymphocyte suspensions prepared at known cell densities (centrifuged from whole blood). These samples were then delivered to the DEP devices built on SOI substrates. An important finding is that our DEP devices are capable of isolating cancer cells from lymphocytes at a high cell loading density as compared to the known DEP devices (Biosensors and Bioelectronics, 2014). We attribute this to the 3D profile of our electrodes. Subsequently we fabricated the DEP devices on SOG substrates to render them transparent for phase contrast microscopy. We characterized these devices for the DEP isolation of cells (Analyst, 2015). While developing the interdigitated 3D comb array, we discovered a comparatively simple design based on castellated silicon blocks, which we pursued for the continuous-flow isolation of cancer cells. However, during experiments, we encountered electrokinetic forces other than the DEP forces, mainly electrothermal drag that led to effective enrichment of cells as opposed to isolation of tumor cells from lymphocytes. Thus, we characterized this design for the continuous-flow extraction of blood plasma (submitted to a peer-reviewed journal, 2015). We also discovered experimental evidence of a previously postulated electrokinetic force during our investigation for the DEP characteristics of tumor cell line (Applied Physics Letters, 2015). As for Objective 1, we reported the first account of a single-cell impedance flow cytometry microsystem based on 3D silicon microelectrodes (MEMS, Shanghai, 2016). Lastly, on a more fundamental level, our findings regarding the influence of the substrate nanotopography on the morphogenesis of epithelial organoids might provide insights into the study of mechanosignaling in the epithelium during tumor progression (Scientific Reports 2015).

621711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
621711.value: In either objective, there is room for further development. In objective 1, 3D microelectrodes could be made of silicon blocks featuring castellated sidewalls (as in objective 2) rather than linear sidewalls. This will turn each microelectrode into a ring structure surrounding the stream of cells all around as opposed to pillars simply located on the channel side. An expected outcome of this configuration would be enhanced signal amplitude and subsequently enhanced signal-to-noise ratio. Fabrication of a cytometer device based on the microelectrodes featuring castellated sidewalls has already begun and will be characterized in due course using blood and tumor cells. In objective 2, the device based on the interdigitated 3D silicon ring microelectrodes performs well for batch mode operation but cannot be directly used for continuous-flow mode operation. This means that the device in a single run can process only a finite volume of sample in two sequential steps: trapping tumor cells first by the microelectrodes and then eluting (releasing) the trapped cells after processing the entire sample volume. However, a simple design modification can render the device suitable for continuous-flow separation where tumor cells can be continuously harvested from a given blood sample of unlimited volume.

621711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
621711.value: Cancer metastasis is responsible for the vast majority of cancer-related deaths unlike primary tumor masses, which claim only one out of ten fatalities. Tumor cells that acquire the ability to penetrate lymphatic and blood vessels end up in the bloodstream and potentially infiltrate distant organs. These cells are referred to as circulating tumor cells (CTCs). Recent studies suggest that the viable CTC count in peripheral blood is directly linked to cancer progression. Therefore, enumerating CTCs could become an approach that is used instead of invasive biopsies for the purpose of stratifying patients for adjuvant therapies and increasing the follow-up frequency during the course of the treatments. Isolation of CTCs from peripheral blood, given their extremely low abundance (a few to hundred CTCs among billion red cells and million white cells per mL) is a needle-in-a-haystack challenge. The classical techniques used to isolate CTCs to date have been determined to be inadequately specific and sensitive, and the task calls for the development of a technology that can be used to screen samples rapidly and deterministically at single-cell resolution. Microsystems demonstrated in this project address this call by isolating or distinguishing cancer cells from white blood cells based on their electrical phenotype.

622411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
622411.value: Models consisting of many-server queues have received much attention from both practitioners and researchers due to their practical significance in applications of many public and economic sectors. Yet, there are still many open questions in the network setting. In this project, we propose to study a simple network model which consists of two many-server queues in tandem, with the downstream server pool cross-trained so that its servers can also serve customers waiting in the upstream queue. The network model is motivated by applications in various complex systems such as call center outsourcing and patient flow management in healthcare. Taking the call center as an example, we can view the outsourcer call center as the upstream server pool. There is a possibility that the outsourcer may not be able to complete a customer’s request, so the customer needs to be transferred to the downstream in-house call center. To achieve economies of scale, the two centers are pooled together by allowing the in-house call center to serve arriving customers. This is exactly the model we propose to study. Most of such systems demand efficient solutions for their design and operation. A key issue in design is staffing. The number of servers to employ at both upstream and downstream pools in order to accommodate the demand must be properly determined. In many cases, the demand could vary significantly while the staffing is usually fixed. For example, the number of agents to be hired in a call center has to be determined in advance and fixed for a working shift during which call volume may change significantly. The operation of the system concerns with the policy for routing customers in various situations. For example, when a server at the downstream pool becomes available, which customer should this server serve if there are customers waiting in both the upstream and downstream queues? We propose to use stochastic processing networks to study the model. This research will not only lead to mathematical characterizations of the underlying stochastic processes, but also practical staffing and control policies that can make the design and operation of such systems efficient. In particular, we seek policies that is implementable and near optimal in the heavy traffic regime, where demand and capacity become higher and higher to balance each other out. The novelty of the research arises from the network model and joint optimality of staffing and control policies. 多服务器队列模型在许多公共和经济领域都有重要的实际应用意义，因而一直受到了商业领域和研究领域的重视。 但是, 在排队网络中仍然存在着许多悬而未决的问题。 在这个项目中，我们将会研究一个由两个串联的多服务器队列组成的网络模型，其中下游的服务器集群是多功能的，能为等待在上游队列中的顾客提供服务。这个网络模型的建立是出于它在各种复杂系统中的适用性，例如呼叫中心外包和医院病人流量管理等。比如呼叫中心, 我们可以把外包呼叫中心看做上游服务器集群。不过外包商可能无法满足客户的需求，此时需要将客户转移到下游的内部呼叫中心。为了实现规模效益，我们允许下游的服务器群服务直接到来的顾客，从而把上下游两个呼叫中心整合到一起。这就是我们的研究模型。 大多数此类系统的设计与运行的要求是获得高效的解决方案。系统设计的一个关键点就是人力配置. 例如上游和下游服务器集群里服务器的数量就一定要慎重确定。在很多情况下，需求量在剧烈变化而人力配置却维持着不变。例如，呼叫中心在一个工作时段所安排的人员是预先确定并且维持不变的，然而在此期间，呼叫需求却可能有很大变化。该系统也关注在不同情况下顾客的流向安排。例如，当下游服务器集群有服务器空闲，而此时上下游都有顾客在等待，那么服务器该选择服务那边的顾客呢？ 我们建议用随机处理网络来研究这个模型。这项研究不仅可以获得该模型深层的数学特性，还能提供实用的的人力配置与控制方案使得设计与运行这类系统变得更加高效。特别地，我们寻找在高负荷下，也就是需求与服务能力变得越来越高并达到平衡时，的可行且近似最优的政策。该研究的新颖之处在于在网络模型下获得人员配置和控制政策的联合最优。

622411.label: Realisation of objectives
622411.value: The objectives have been achieved with great success. In paper #4 (see Section 8 of the report), we developed an analytic framework for analyzing the fluid model underlying the many-server model with a single class of customers. In a subsequent paper #5, we extend such study to allow time varying arrivals. Paper #1 extend the study on asymptotic analysis to a more general type of stochastic networks. In this way, Objective 1 is achieved. In paper 4, we studied a more general type of multi-server queue where each agent can serve multiple customers simultaneously. It has applications in online instant messaging services. We consider the staffing problem in such systems with impatient customers where the objective is to minimize the number of agents while providing a certain service level. First we propose effective routing policies based on a static planning LP, both for the cases when the arrival rate is observable and for when the rate is unobservable. We show that these routing policies minimize the proportion of abandoning customers in the long run asymptotically for large systems. We also prove that the staffing solution obtained from a staffing LP, when used with the proposed routing policies, is asymptotically optimal. We also study the asymptotic optimality in a more general type of networks. Thus, we have successfully achieved Objectives 2 and 3. In paper #3, we propose a unified approach to establishing diffusion approximations for queues with impatient customers within a general framework of scaling customer patience time. This approach can allow both the service and patience time to follow general distributions. We also demonstrate the application of this unified approach to several widely used models. In this paper, we have successfully achieved Objective 4. In all these researches, extensive numerical experiments are performed based on a systematic simulation tool we have developed. So Objective 5 is achieved. Achieving the objectives is not an easy task. It took tremendous effort of myself and two of my PhD students. Both of them have already graduated, one became an assistant professor at Shanghai University after a year’s post doc at Technion, other other also because an assistant at Huazhong University of Science and Technology. The papers produced in this project were much improved by hiring research assistants and communicating with top researcher in the field. The grant allowed me to have English editors improve the exposition of all my papers. The travels made possible by this grant also help me collaborate quite extensively with my collaborator in Singapore and US, and present the research outcome in major conferences and workshops.

622411.label: Major findings and research outcome
622411.value: This project lead to significant development in both theory and application. The theory part are summarized in papers 3, 4 and 5. Papers 4 and 5 develop the theory on fluid model/limit of multi-server queues and paper 3 provides a unified approach for diffusion analysis. On the application side, we obtain operational insights into how complicated systems arising applications like call/webchat centers evolve and how to optimize the key performances by designing the optimal control and staffing policies. The major findings of this project are as follows: Paper #1 studies management of a service network with both parallel and sequential structures. Our study reveals that the non-idling policy may not always be optimal for such networks, and the optimal routing decision depends on the ratio of marginal costs of the queues. For a give cost structure, we also provide a procedure to design the optimal control and staffing policy. Paper #2 consider customer service chat systems where customers can receive real time service from agents using an instant messaging application over the Internet. We propose routing policies and show that they minimize the proportion of abandoning customers in the long run asymptotically for large systems. We also prove that the staffing solution obtained from a staffing LP, when used with the proposed routing policies, is asymptotically optimal. Paper #3 propose a unified approach to establishing diffusion approximations for queues with impatient customers within a general framework of scaling customer patience time. We demonstrate the application of this approach via several widely used models. Paper #4 show that the convergence of the fluid model to its equilibrium state holds under some general conditions, solving an open question in the area. Fluid models, in particular their equilibrium states, have become an important tool for the study of many-server queues with general service and patience time distributions. Our method builds on the framework of measure-valued processes, which keeps track of the remaining patience and service times. Paper #5 extend the measure-valued fluid model, which tracks residuals of patience and service times, to allow for time-varying arrivals. The fluid model can be characterized by a one- dimensional convolution equation involving both the patience and service time distributions. We also make an interesting connection to the measure-valued fluid model tracking the elapsed waiting and service times. Our analysis shows that the two fluid models are actually characterized by the same one-dimensional convolution equation.

622411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
622411.value: In this project, we have solved several major problem completely. So in the main theme, there should not be much left to do in the scope of proposed research. However, solving a problem always lead to more questions as how it usually goes in research. In particular, what are the most general condition under which we can obtain fluid and diffusion limit? This is a too big question and answering this may give lead to several big projects. Nevertheless, the method we developed in this project can help pave the way to solving that big question. This project has great potential for future research in applications. We only demonstrate the application of the theory we develop in several application in the scope of this project. The method we develop can surely be applied to other types of model. For example, bike sharing (or more generally business models in the emerging sharing economy) systems can be modeled as a multi-server system. The proposed course of action would be to study what are the important factor in those application, and the modify the model (sometimes with slight adaptation of the method) to obtain insights and results in those applications.

622411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
622411.value: This project demonstrated both theoretical and application significance. On the theoretical side, we advanced the state of art of analyzing the difficult yet widely used multi-server queueing model by proving the convergence of fluid model to the equilibrium state and establishing a unified approach to the diffusion analysis. Our research has been driven by real application in emerging areas, which leads to some innovative models such as the online web chat system, and service networks with both parallel and sequence structures. These models are new in the research literature and have their own distinctive features, thus we need to develop new method to analyze them. Based on the theory we developed, we are able to obtain operational insights to the applications. For example, we propose easy-to-implement and optimal staffing and control policies for webchat centers and call centers with outsourcing, both being important application in the modern society.

622811.label: Project Title(Chinese)
622811.value: 顾客支付时机对动态库存及定价决策的影响

622811.label: Project Objectives
622811.value: Gain a deeper understanding of various payment schemes in terms of their timing in business to business environment or business to consumer settings. More importantly, try to understand the rationales behind the different payment schemes and how well these rationales are aligned with the dynamic nature of the pricing and inventory decisions. Examine classical inventory models which assume that customers pay upon arrival and investigate how a change in payment timing will affect the optimal inventory policies. Examine the existing models on joint dynamic pricing and inventory decisions and investigate how a change in payment timing will affect these decisions. We expect the research to be quite challenging and may require the development of new mathematical approaches.

622811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
622811.value: In the past decades, there has been a substantial amount of research on dynamic pricing and inventory decisions. All the existing literature on dynamic pricing and inventory decisions assumes that customers pay at the time of placing orders even though their orders may be backlogged and delivered at a time when the prices are most likely to have changed. This assumption reflects certain reality and is mostly driven by technical tractability. However, in many real situations, customers will demand the “current price” when they pick up their backlogged orders if the prices have since dropped. Our primary study shows that, if customers are allowed to pay at the time when their orders are delivered (or become available), not only the seller’s decisions on inventory and price will be very different from if customers pay when they place orders, the widely used demand models (demand as a function of the price in the additive or multiplicative fashion) are no longer consistent. In particular, if customers pay at the price of when they actually receive their products, some backlogged customers may back out due to changes in prices. Even if customers pay at the price when they placed their orders, as long as they pay upon delivery, one needs to keep track of the prices for backlogged customers and the problems become very complicated. Therefore, there is a whole new line of research on dynamic pricing and inventory decisions that examines how the timing of the payments impacts these decisions in various scenarios: finite horizon vs. infinite horizon, limited vs. unlimited supply, deterministic vs. random yield, myopic vs. strategic customers, etc. Furthermore, it is not clear if commonly used demand models are consistent with the payment scheme. The answers to these questions will greatly enrich the existing literature on dynamic pricing and inventory decisions and provide guidelines for decision making in practice. The outcomes of this proposed project will substantially broaden the literature of dynamic pricing and inventory decisions and open a new line of research that has been ignored in the large amount of research in dynamic pricing and inventory decisions. Furthermore, the results have the potential to introduce consumer behavior into the dynamic pricing and inventory decision literature. That is, understanding how customers respond to price changes while waiting for their orders is critical in developing consistent demand models. 无论是个人用户还是企业用户，顾客的需求总是显著地受到销售价格的影响，因而销售者需要根据他打算采用的定价来计划其生产或库存量。另一方面，销售商应该根据其库存状况进行定价，譬如，他会希望在库存充足时降低价格，而在库存短缺时提升价格。因此，定价与库存的决策应同步进行。进一步地说，为了确保商业的长期与健康发展，销售商的最佳选择应该是周期性地调整其商品售价并补充库存，这一般被称为动态定价与库存决策。在过去的数十年里，在动态定价与库存决策的问题上已有大量的研究。以下我们将就与我们研究相关度较高的、关于此问题各个方面的文献做一综述。 在现有的关于动态定价与库存决策的文献中，所有研究均假定顾客在他们下订单时即全额支付，就算到实际配送时售价很可能已经变动也是如此。此假设反映了某种程度的现实，主要是出于技术可行性上的考虑。但在许多实际情况当中，顾客在预订的货物交货时，如果售价已经下降，他们会要求按“当前的售价”支付。我们的初步研究表明，如果顾客可以在他预订的货物交货时才支付的话，销售商的库存与定价策略均会与他必须在下订单时即支付的情况有很大的差异，而以往被广泛使用的需求模型（需求为价格的函数，表现为加法模型或乘法模型）不再保持一致性。特别地，如果顾客按他们实际接收货物时的价格来支付的话，部分顾客可能会因为价格的变动而撤回订单。就算顾客还是按照他们下订单时的价格来支付，但只要支付时机变为交货时才支付，销售者就要对其售价作完整的记录以便回溯，这将使问题变得极为复杂。因此，在多种不同情况下考察支付时机对动态定价与库存决策的影响将是该问题一个崭新的研究方向：有限或无限的计划区间、不受限或受限的供货量、确定性的或随机的产出量、短视的或具有战略眼光的顾客等等。进一步地，需求模型是否能对不同的支付方式保持一致性仍有待研究。以上问题的解决将极大地丰富已有的关于动态定价与库存决策的研究，并为现实决策提供指导。 本项目的成果将极大地拓展动态定价与库存决策问题的研究并开拓一个全新的、在以往的大量研究中均被忽略了的方向。而且，本项目可将顾客行为引入动态定价与库存决策的研究当中，即：了解顾客在等待他们的订单时会对价格波动做出何种反应，这将对建立具有一致性的需求模型起到关键的作用。

622811.label: Realisation of objectives
622811.value: We have accomplished all the objectives. The results are published in several papers and the funding was used to support several Ph.D students. In most business to business environment or business to consumer settings, there are two main types of payment schemes in terms of their timing: (1) ``Pay-to-order” where customers pay when they place their orders and (2) ``pay-to-delivery” where they pay when their orders are delivered. There may be some variations, for instance, where a customer is given a grace period for obtaining finance or preparing for paper work especially under the first scheme. However, such a variation only affects the accounting of the cash flows, not the operations and pricing decisions in general, unless the firm considered is financially constrained. Since financial constraint is beyond the scope of our project, we focused on the two main payment schemes. To understand the optimal inventory policies under the two payment schemes, in Chen et al (2015), we consider a single-product, periodic review, finite-horizon inventory system with multiple sources of uncertainty: stochastic discount factors, stochastic operational costs and prices, and stochastic demand that evolve based on the state of the world. In the presence of multiple sources of uncertainty within the business environment, it is unclear a priori what type of inventory policy a firm should follow under both payment scheme. When customers pay to delivery, our model implies that they place orders with the understanding they will pay upon delivery a currently unknown price. Although this type of contracts shifts some of the risk to the customer, it is becoming increasingly popular, especially in a global business environment. In general, an (s,S) policy fails to be optimal under both payment schemes. We thus provide sufficient conditions for an (s,S) policy to be optimal and their implications. This will help decision makers understand when an optimal policy may be nontrivial under multiple uncertainties. In Zhang and Zhang (2013), we study how the timing of payments affects joint replenishment and pricing decisions. Specifically, we consider a periodic review system in which customers pay upon receiving their goods, referred to as the collect- on-delivery scheme, as opposed to paying when placing their orders, referred to as the instant payment scheme commonly assumed in the literature. We show that a base-stock list price policy is optimal without a fixed ordering cost, and provide a sufficient condition for an (s, S, p) policy to be optimal with a fixed ordering cost. We then compare the policies under the collect-on-delivery and instant payment schemes. In general, the collect-on-delivery scheme requires higher inventory levels so as to reduce or avoid late payments due to stock-out. While the collect-on-delivery scheme leads to lower selling prices without a fixed ordering cost, it results in higher selling prices with a fixed ordering cost in our numerical examples to reduce demand and order less frequently.

622911.label: Project Objectives

622911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
622911.value: Plastic slip of dislocations and deformation twinning are major deformation modes of plasticity which accommodate a shape change of material under mechanical loading. Deformation twinning is a highly correlated atomic shearing process, meaning that atoms in a part of a crystal shear correlatively so that the sheared part has a twinning symmetry with respect to the un-sheared part. Ordinary dislocation plasticity involves dislocation storage, multiplication, motion, pinning, and nucleation, and these processes are much less correlated in comparison with deformation twinning. Deformation twinning may relate to and compete with ordinary dislocation plasticity and may completely control the plastic behavior of hexagonal close-packed (hcp) crystals. Although great progress in the understanding of deformation twinning has been achieved, the origin and spatio-temporal features of deformation twinning are still shrouded in mystery. Recent experimental observations on single crystalline metals show that the overall sample dimensions may limit the length scales available for plastic processes. The stress required for deformation twinning increases drastically with decreasing sample size, until the sample size is reduced to one micrometer, below which the deformation twinning is entirely replaced by less correlated, ordinary dislocation plasticity. Accompanying the transition in the deformation mechanism, the maximum flow stress of samples with sub-micrometer size is saturated at a value close to the ideal shear strength. These exciting experimental results encourage us to propose the present academic research. In the proposed research, we shall systematically investigate the size-dependent deformation twinning in hcp crystals by conducting designed experimental tests, atomistic simulations, and theoretical study. We shall conduct compression tests on hcp single crystalline samples with different diameters ranging from millimeters, micrometers, to nanometers, at various loading rates and at a variety of temperatures from liquid nitrogen to 200 C. We shall calculate the energy pathways of deformation twinning based on ab initio density functional theory and carry on atomistic simulations of compression tests at the nanometer scales. We shall perform theoretical modeling of deformation twinning including theoretically investigation of the surface effects on deformation twinning nucleation and growth, and on the competition between deformation twinning and ordinary dislocation plasticity. The anticipated output from this comprehensive investigation will greatly enhance the understanding of size-dependent deformation twinning and size-dependent plastic deformation, and advance momentously the state-of-the-art mechanism-based nanomechanics. Successfully accomplishing the proposed research will obviously be academically significant, but also substantial in a practical sense, especially to nanotechnology and micro/nanoelectromechanical systems. 位错引发的塑性滑移，这里简称为位错塑性，和形变孪晶是晶体塑性变形的主要方式。形变孪晶与原子剪切过程高度相关、意味着部分晶体中的原子关联性地剪切、以至于剪切部分和未剪切部分有着孪晶对称关系。位错塑性包括了位错的形核、增殖、运动、钉扎和存储。和形变孪晶相比，位错塑性的变形关联性较少。形变孪晶可能和位错有关并与位错塑性竞争。形变孪晶有可能完全是密排六方晶体的塑性变形机理。虽然人们对形变孪晶的理解已经取得了很大的进展，但是形变孪晶的起源和时空特征仍然笼罩着神秘的色彩。近来对单晶金属的实验观察表明：试样整体尺寸可能会制约塑性变形的机理。随着样品尺寸的减小，形变孪晶所需要的应力急剧地增加，直到样品的尺寸小于一微米，这时位错塑性是塑性变形的机理而且亚微米样品的最大流变应力接近于理想剪切强度。受这些令人兴奋的实验结果启发，我们提出了现在的学术研究课题。在此课题中，我们将通过实验测试、计算机模拟及理论分析系统地研究密排六方晶体中与尺寸相关的形变孪晶。我们将对密排六方单晶的试样进行压缩实验，其中包括了从毫米、微米到纳米的不同的试样直径，不同的加载速率和从液氮温度到200 C不同的测试温度。我们将通过基于量子力学的密度泛函理论来计算形变孪晶的能量路径，以及在纳米尺度上进行压缩实验的原子模拟。我们将构建形变孪晶的理论模型，包括系统地研究表面效应对形变孪晶形核和生长的影响，以及形变孪晶和普通位错塑性的竞争。经全面研究后的预期成果，将极大地加深我们对与尺度相关的形变孪晶和塑性变形的理解，并将推动最先进纳米力学的发展。该项目的圆满完成不仅将有着显著的学术意义，也将在实际工业应用中尤其是纳米技术和微纳米电子体系起着重要的作用。

622911.label: Realisation of objectives
622911.value: All objectives have been successfully achieved. A Somigliana dislocation dipole model was developed to study the size–dependent formation energy of an hcp twin nucleus in an elastically isotropic medium under applied compressive stress. The twin formation energy was divided into the self-energy of the Somigliana dislocation dipole, the interaction energy between the Somigliana dislocation dipole and the applied stress, and the twin-matrix interfacial energy. The twin formation first increases and then decreases with the twin size and the maximum is called the activation energy for the twin formation. Based on a constant value of the activation energy, we have the critical stress for mechanical twinning as a function of the sample dimension, showing the smaller the sample size is, the higher the applied stress will be required. The generalized planar fault (GPF) approach was used in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the effect of the sample size on the twinnability and the results were verifies by the first-principle calculations. From the GPF curves, we determined the intrinsic stacking fault energy, the unstable stacking fault energy, the unstable twinning energy and the twinning fault energy. The four energies are called the generalized stacking energies (GSF). For small sized samples, free surfaces induce normal (out-plane) and parallel (in-plane) relaxations, which may affect the twinnability. The simulations show that the parallel relaxation has more influence on the GSF energies than the normal relaxation. The nucleation and growth of deformation twins after a certain degree of ordinary dislocation plasticity was also investigated. These results, however, have not been published yet and the reason was that Dr. Hang REN, who did the work in his PhD study under the PI’s supervision, was busy on something else. The PI is trying to convince Dr. Hang REN to draft papers based on these results. In addition, we have developed a technology based on deformation twinning to improve the properties of ferroelectric materials. A novel thermomechanical treatment technique was developed to introduce {111} nanotwins into ferroelectric films with different twin densities. The increase in twin density increases the number of ferroelectric variants. A large number of ferroelectric variants improve the ferroelectric properties. The experimental results and the phase field simulations verified this novel approach and indicate that the developed twin engineering might be applied universally to all ferroelectric ceramics and films to substantially enhance their performance. We have also investigated the time-, stress-, and temperature-dependent deformation of coarse-grained (cg), nanograined (ng), and nanotwinned (nt) copper at five temperatures. On one hand, twins can be formed during deformation. On the other hand, twins play also important role in deformation. Our investigations conclude that nanotwins make the ng-Cu more thermally stable and improve greatly the creep property of ng-Cu. Mechanical twinning means that twins are formed in fcc metals by slipping partial dislocations on every {111} planes. If partial dislocations are glided on every second {111} planes, the deformation causes the fcc to hcp transformation. The mechanically induced fcc to hcp transformation is also studied on the atomic level in this project.

622911.label: Major findings and research outcome
622911.value: 1. A Somigliana dislocation dipole model was developed to study the size–dependent formation energy of an hcp twin nucleus in an elastically isotropic medium under applied compressive stress. The twin formation energy first increases and then decreases with the twin size. The critical stress for mechanical twinning is a function of the sample dimension, showing the smaller the sample size is, the higher the applied stress will be required. (PhD thesis of Hang REN) 2. The generalized planar fault approach was used in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the effect of the sample size on the twinnability and the results were verifies by the first-principle calculations. For small sized samples, free surfaces induce normal (out-plane) and parallel (in-plane) relaxations, which may affect the twinnability. The simulations show that the parallel relaxation has more influence on the GSF energies than the normal relaxation. (PhD thesis of Hang REN) 3. The crystal twin engineering has been applied to ferroelectric materials to increase the domain variants. A novel thermomechanical treatment technique was developed to introduce {111} nanotwins into the films with different twin densities. The experimental results show that the coercive field is 32% lower in the high twin density samples than that in the low twin density ones. (J1) 4. We have comprehensively investigated the time, stress, and temperature-dependent deformation behavior in nanotwinned copper by conducting stress relaxation and creep tests at five temperatures, high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), and MD simulations The comprehensive investigations provide sufficient information for the building-up of a formula to describe the time, stress, and temperature-dependent deformation and clarify the relationship among the strain rate sensitivity parameter, stress exponent, and activation volume. The determined activation parameters, HRTEM images, and MD simulations consistently suggest that the deformation mechanism varies with the level of applied stress and the test temperature (J4, J5). 5. Deformation induced martensitic transformation (DIMT) in AISI 304 austenitic stainless steel was studied to capture the atomic movement during the gamma (fcc) to epsilon (hcp) to alpha’ (bcc) transition. HRTEM observations confirm the crucial role of partial dislocations, and reveal tell-tale features including the lattice rotation of the martensite inclusion, the transition lattices at the interfaces that cater the shears, and the excess reverse shear-shuffling induced gamma necks in the epsilon martensite plates. These direct observations verify for the first time the 50-year-old Bogers-Burgers-Olson-Cohen model, and enrich the understanding of DIMT mechanisms. (J2, J3)

622911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
622911.value: More experimental and theoretical investigations should be conducted to further develop the novel twining engineering that is able to improve the ferroelectric properties. More experimental and theoretical investigations should be conducted to verify and apply the proposed formula for the time-, stress-, and temperature-dependent deformation, which is especially important for the applications of superalloys at high temperature. It is expected by the PI that the developed formula has the ability to predict the creep life and stress-relaxation life of superalloys.

622911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
622911.value: Deformation twinning is one of the major deformation modes of plasticity which accommodate a shape change of material under mechanical loading. Deformation twinning is a highly correlated atomic shearing process, meaning that atoms in a part of a crystal shear correlatively so that the sheared part has a twinning symmetry with respect to the un-sheared part. Deformation twinning may relate to and compete with ordinary dislocation plasticity and may completely control the plastic behavior of hexagonal close-packed (hcp) crystals. In the proposed research, we have systematically investigated the size-dependent deformation twinning in hcp crystals by conducting designed experimental tests, atomistic simulations, and theoretical study. The output from this comprehensive investigation greatly enhances the understanding of size-dependent deformation twinning and size-dependent plastic deformation, and advance momentously the state-of-the-art mechanism-based nanomechanics. The successfully accomplishment of the proposed research is obviously and academically significant, but also substantial in a practical sense, especially to nanotechnology and micro/nanoelectromechanical systems.

623211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
623211.value: The thermo-hydro-mechanical behavior of natural soils is highly complex but important to a wide variety of important geotechnical applications. Due to the existence of soil structure, natural soil is known to exhibit considerably different soil behavior and shear strength than a remolded soil does. The complexity is further compounded when natural soil is subjected to great variations in temperature in addition to mechanical loads. This may cause serious stability problems or even failure for many key infrastructures, such as those relevant to nuclear waste disposal, thermal energy storage, heat utility conduits, geothermal energy extraction, underground high-voltage electrical cables, as well as natural slopes. Relevant research on thermal failure in natural soil is hence of considerable practical importance but is theoretically challenging. The existing work on this topic is far from conclusive and a lot of issues remain unresolved. This project aims to develop a novel theoretical framework to account for the thermal effects on natural soils and apply it to the analysis of thermal failure of natural soil relevant to key geostructures. Particular emphasis will be made upon developing a thermodynamically consistent constitutive model which may enable the complex thermal, hydraulic and mechanical coupling behaviors of natural soil under combined thermal and mechanical loads to be accurately characterized. In doing so, a thermo-mechanics approach with internal variables is proposed to formulate the intricate thermo-elasto-plastic relation on account of the varying underlying mechanisms of energy dissipation associated with different processes and the anisotropic evolution of soil structure under complex loading conditions. A well-instrumented true triaxial testing system will be modified to calibrate and verify the proposed model. The proposed theory will be implemented in a displacement finite element using robust numerical algorithms and will be used to simulate boundary value problems of practical importance. The new theory so obtained will help advance our understanding towards the complex soil behavior in its natural state and subjected to complex loading conditions involving thermal variation. Improvement of knowledge in this respect will serve useful purposes in guiding us for safe design and hazard mitigation across many engineering areas and industries, both locally and globally. 原狀土體的熱-水力-力學特性異常複雜但對很多岩土工程又非常重要。原狀土體由於存在原狀結構，往往表現出與重塑土大為不同的土體特性和強度。如果正常受力之外加上溫度變化，原狀土的特性將進一步複雜化，常會導致土體穩定甚至破壞問題出現，嚴重影響到重要基礎工程諸如核廢料處理，熱能存儲，導熱管線，地熱開發，地下高壓管線以及自然邊坡等的運行及安全。因此，相關問題的研究具有非常重要實際意義，但其在理論上又非常有挑戰性，現有工作存在很多不足。 本項目旨在建立一個描述原狀土熱效應的理論框架，並將其應用於相關岩土工程的熱破壞分析中。我們將建立一個熱力學框架內一致的本構關係來準確描述原狀土在受熱和力學荷載共同作用下複雜的熱-水力-力學耦合性狀。我們將考慮各種變形過程中的能量耗散機理以及土結構複雜受力情況下的各向異性特徵，提出一個基於內變量的熱力學方法來推導複雜的熱彈塑性本構關係。我們將進一步改進已有的真三軸試驗儀來校準驗證該模型。我們還將用先進的數值方法將該理論在位移有限元中加以實現，並將其應用於實際工程的邊值問題。 該研究不僅能夠幫助我們加深理解原狀土複雜受熱受力情況下的力學性狀，而且可以指導岩土工程師在防災減災方面進行安全可靠的工程設計。

623211.label: Realisation of objectives
623211.value: All four objectives proposed in the project have been successfully achieved. Specifically, (1) we have developed thermo-mechanically consistent models to include the effects of fabric structure on both the elastic and plastic behaviour of soil under either monotonic or cyclic loading conditions (see Part C, Research Output. Journal papers No. 8.1, 8.2, 8.4, 8.6, Conference papers No. 9.1, 9.2, 9.5). These models provides rigorous theoretical frameworks for modelling the thermal and structural influences on soil responses. (2) The proposed models have been rigorously implemented in a displacement-based finite element method to model the thermo-related failure behaviour in practical geotechnical engineering (see Part C, Research Output, Journal papers No. 8.3, 8.5, 8.9, Conference papers No. 9.4). The implementation has been based on explicit stress integration scheme in conjunction with direct solving of the PDE of the finite element method discretisation of a boundary value problem, which proves to be effective and accurate in handling complex soil models such as these proposed in the mentioned papers. (3) The models have been calibrated and verified by available experimental data and have been further applied to predicting the soil responses under loading conditions which cannot be readily realised in laboratory. The various investigations have helped to gain deeper understanding of the complicated soil behaviour when a soil is subjected to both mechanical and thermal loads (see Part C, Research Output, Journal papers No. 8.7, 8.8, 8.10, Conference papers No. 9.3). (4) The implemented FEM models have been used to investigate relevant geotechnical problems of practical importance, based on which potential improvements on existing design and maintenance of geostructures are provided (see Part C, Research Output, Journal papers No. 8.7, 8.8, 8.10).

623211.label: Major findings and research outcome
623211.value: The project has led to novel and robust predictive constitutive models being developed for simulating the thermal and structural influences on fundamental behaviour of natural soils which are of considerable importance in geotechnical engineering. The research fosters not only fundamental understanding of complex soil behaviour in a natural setting when soil is subjected to combined, complicated loading conditions of variable kinds, but also leads to advanced and robust numerical tools for future geotechnical analysis and design. A total of ten journal papers and five conference papers have been published as an outcome of the proposed research in this project. The venues we chose to disseminate our research findings include prime geotechnical journals such as geotechnique (Part C, No. 8.5), Journal of Geotechnical and Geoenvironmetnal Engineering (Part C, No. 8.2) and Geotechnique letters (Part C, No. 8.8), prestigious engineering mechanics journals such as Journal of Engineering Mechanics (Part C, No. 8.1, 8.4, 8.6) as well as top engineering numerical journals such as Computers Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering (Part C, No. 8.10), Computers and Geotechnics (Part C, No. 8.9) and International Journal for Numerical and Analytical Methods in Geomechanics (Part C, No. 8.7). The conferences we chose to present our work include major constitutive modelling serious conferences such as Constitutive modelling of Geomaterials (IS-Model 2012), the 15th Asian Regional Conference on Soil Mechanics and Geotechnical Engineering and the 14th International Conference of the International Association for Computer Methods and Advances in Geomechanics. One PhD and one MPhil have graduated with support of the project. Our research outputs have been well received from both reviewers and the audiences of these journals and conferences as well the general soil mechanics community.

623211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
623211.value: Further research can be carried out following a micormechanical approach based on discrete element method and cross-scale modelling of the thermal behavior of soil. This proves to be a rather promising direction of research which may potentially lead to methodological breakthrough on soil modelling and characterisation.

623211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
623211.value: The project has led to the development of novel, advanced theoretical models for effective prediction and characterisation the complex responses of a natural soil when it is subjected to changes of external mechanical loadings and temperature changes. The developed models have also been implemented in advanced numerical tools to foster their application for relevant practical geotechnical problems. The research findings of the project can not only greatly improve our fundamental understanding of complex soil behaviour under complicated loading conditions, but also potentially lead to effective and economic next-generation design tools for practising geotechnical engineers to design and analyse thermal-related geotechnical applications. It is of both theoretical significance and practical relevance.

623311.label: Project Objectives
623311.value: Devise a unique electrochemical system, with which the water transport properties of the anion-exchange membrane, including the water uptake, water diffusivity, and electro-osmotic drag coefficient, can be characterized. Investigate the ethanol transport characteristics of the DEFC to understand how the design of the anode flow field and diffusion layer as well as operating conditions affect the ethanol transport behavior. Investigate the water transport characteristics in the DEFC. The goal is to maintain an appropriate water concentration distribution across the fuel cell system such that the cathode potential, associated with the water concentration loss as a result of low water permeation through the membrane and the oxygen concentration loss as a result of cathode flooding, can be maximized. Develop an advanced model for the DEFC so that effects of various design and operating parameters on cell performance can be investigated and the system can be optimized with the minimum cost and time period. Further improve the activity and stability of our developed non-platinum nanocatalysts for both the EOR and ORR in the DEFC. Optimize and advance the design of the DEFC. In summary, the most original and innovative aspects of this research include: i) the change in the electrolyte membrane from acid to base represents a new concept in the DEFC technology, which will certainly boost the performance of DEFCs and ii) addressing the above-mentioned critical mass-transport issues in this new power pack with the uniquely interdisciplinary approach will enable the cell performance and operating stability to be further improved. This research will not only bring about advances in our fundamental understanding of coupled mass transport and electrochemical reactions in multi-scaled porous structures, but will also establish the much needed scientific know-how in this cutting-edge fuel cell technology.

623311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
623311.value: 本项目旨在研究具有可持续、碳中和特性的下一代乙醇燃料电池中的传质现象。我们提出的新型直接乙醇燃料电池将使用碱性阴离子交换膜与非贵金属的催化剂。我们初步的性能测试已经证实这种新型燃料电池在60oC操作温度下的功率密度可超过180 mW/cm2，远高于直接甲醇燃料电池的性能。虽然我们的独特电池设计颇具吸引力，但是电池的性能和运行稳定性必须进一步提高和改善。电池性能的提高不但依赖于新型离子传输材料和电化学催化剂材料的发展，而且还取决于对燃料电池系统中质量、电荷传输的认识。由于酸性和碱性燃料电池的工作原理有着根本的区别，我们以前获得的对传统酸性质子交换膜燃料电池（如直接甲醇燃料电池）的认识不能直接应用到碱性燃料电池上。以水传输为例，水在阳极是生成物，而在阴极是反应物。阳极产生的水需要透过膜扩散到阴极以便克服电渗作用为阴极反应补给水。如果水透过膜的渗透量过低，将会增加氧还原反应中水的浓差极化损失，从而降低阴极电位。另一方面，如果水的渗透量过高，将增加阴极发生水淹的可能性，导致氧的浓差极化损失增加，同样使阴极电位降低。因此，实现电池高性能的一个关键问题是，如何使燃料电池膜电极中的水分布处于合适范围内，以便最小化水和氧的浓差极化损失。此问题和阴离子交换膜直接乙醇燃料电池中潜在的其它基础传质问题，将会在这个项目中通过创新构思实验和先进模拟计算来解决。通过此项研究，我们将会获得新型燃料电池优化设计方面的重要认识，为二十一世纪清洁能源的发展奠定基础。并且，该项目的核心技术将使包括香港在内的全世界收益。

623311.label: Realisation of objectives
623311.value: In this project, we have achieved much more than the objectives. A unique electrochemical system that allows the measurement of the water transport properties of the anion exchange membrane has been developed. With this system, we measured the key transport properties of the anion exchange membrane, including the water uptake, water diffusivity, and electro-osmotic drag coefficient. In addition, the effects of the design of the anode flow field and diffusion layer as well as operating conditions on ethanol transport behavior have been examined. We have also studied the water transport characteristics in the DEFC. We have achieved the goal of maintaining an appropriate water concentration distribution across the fuel cell system such that the cathode potential, associated with the water concentration loss as a result of low water permeation through the membrane and the oxygen concentration loss as a result of cathode flooding, can be maximized. An advanced model for DEFCs was also developed in this project. The effects of design and operating parameters on the cell performance can be investigated. The activity and stability of the home-made non-precious catalyst were also further improved. Finally, based on the understandings gained from the foregoing tasks, we optimized and advanced the design of DEFCs.

623311.label: Major findings and research outcome
623311.value: With the support of the present RGC grant, we have made significant contributions to the development of DEFC systems. The results obtained in this project have been presented in 6 top-rated journal papers, as listed in Sections 8. The major findings are summarized as follows: i) A unique electrochemical system that allows the measurement of the water transport properties of the anion exchange membrane has been developed. With this system, we measured the key transport properties of the anion exchange membrane, including the water uptake, water diffusivity, and electro-osmotic drag coefficient. ii) The effects of the design of the anode flow field and diffusion layer as well as operating conditions on ethanol transport behavior have been investigated. iii) We have also studied the water transport characteristics in the DEFC. We have achieved the goal of maintaining an appropriate water concentration distribution across the fuel cell system such that the cathode potential, associated with the water concentration loss as a result of low water permeation through the membrane and the oxygen concentration loss as a result of cathode flooding, can be maximized. iv) An advanced model for DEFCs was also developed in this project. The effects of design and operating parameters on the cell performance can be investigated. v) The activity and stability of the home-made non-precious catalyst were also further improved. vi) Finally, based on the understandings obtained from the foregoing tasks, we optimized and advanced the design of DEFCs.

623311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
623311.value: The present project has primarily focused on the development of a novel DEFC system that adopted an anion exchange membrane. The outcomes of this project have deepened our fundamental understanding of the water and ethanol transport in the DEFC and provided the needed information for the design of DEFCs with applications in portable electronic devices.

623311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
623311.value: A growing number of portable consumer electronics demand small, lightweight power sources with high power density and energy capacity. Current battery technologies, even the most advanced Li-ion batteries, are unlikely to be able to meet the growing energy demands of a mobile workforce due to their low energy densities. In this project, we developed a novel DEFC system that uses an anion exchange membrane. We optimized the DEFC so that both the specific energy and cell performance can be maximized under the conditions of a simple system design and compact size. To provide a simple but robust tool for the design and optimization of the DEFC, we have also developed advanced theoretical models that simulate ethanol and water transport in the DEFC. The DEFC in this project has shown promising applications in portable electronic devices.

640011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
640011.value: The relative importance of the mind versus the body in understanding human behavior has interested researchers for decades. Although the fact that there is a close connection between the body and the mind is incontrovertible, the importance given to the body (i.e., understanding how sensory perceptions affect behavior) is of relatively recent vintage. Sensory experiences are not only informative but can also lead to the formation of non-verbal knowledge structures that can then have an independent effect on judgments and behavior in other domains. Furthermore, if the sensations have been associated with pleasant or unpleasant experiences that the human body has adapted to in the past, re-exposure to a part of the sensory experience might elicit specific emotional reactions (fear, anger etc.). The proposed research will have three foci. One thrust of the research will be to investigate how sensory information affects the appraisal of a situation and behavioral dispositions that result from this appraisal. This is of particular interest when the sensations elicited are in two sense modalities and have conflicting implications. For example, a person who looks at a picture of a ski resort while holding a cup of hot coffee can experience the sensation of warmth as well as imagine the sensation of coldness. Whether and how these conflicting reactions influence overt responses to the stimuli (e.g., attraction to the ski resort) is unclear. A second component of our research will investigate whether sensory experiences reactivate previously formed metaphors that can then influence behavior in domains to which the metaphors are applicable. For example, the sensation of “resistance” experienced while having one’s hair brushed the wrong way might activate a concept of “being rubbed the wrong way,” the metaphorical meaning of which could affect the interpretation of a salesperson’s behavior if he uses excessive persuasion techniques in an attempt to make a sale. Finally, our proposed research will investigate how sensory stimuli elicit emotional reactions that influence judgments in situations that are unrelated to those that initially gave rise to the emotional reactions. For example, evidence exists that females are more inclined than males to react to threatening stimuli by seeking protection rather than fighting or fleeing because of the need to take care of offspring. To this extent, exposure to threat may be more inclined to activate dispositions to evaluate persons and products more favorably that are associated with protection, albeit in quite unrelated domains. 這幾十年來，思想和身體在理解人類行為的相對重要性上令研究員有感興趣。雖然身體和思想之間密切的聯繫是不容置疑的事實，但給予身體的重要性（即了解感官知覺如何影響行為）是相對較新的。感官經驗不僅內容豐富，亦可導致非語言知識結構的形成，然後影響在其他領域的獨立判斷和行為。此外，若某種感覺經驗與過往的開心或不悅經歷構成任何聯繫，當有關感覺再次出現時，可能會觸動個人的情緒(如驚恐、憤怒等) 。 這個將會進行的研究有三個重點。其中一個研究的重點是探究感覺資訊如何影響一個情況的評價和從這個評價中得出的行為性情。值得注意的是，當兩種不同主要感覺同時出現時，可能會引致互相矛盾的情緒反應。例如，當一個人拿著一杯熱咖啡在看著一幅滑雪勝地的圖片時能夠體驗溫暖感覺以及想像寒冷感覺。目前不清楚這些互相矛盾的反應如何影響對刺激的明顯的回應（例如，對滑雪勝地的吸引力）。 本研究的第二個元素將探討知覺的體驗如何導致隱喻的形成及影響在應用的領域上的行為。例如，當一個人的頭髮向錯誤方向梳理時的“抗拒”感覺經驗可能啟動了“被擦了錯誤的方向”的概念，如果營業員在嘗試銷售時使用過多的遊說技巧，這個隱喻的意思可以影響對營業員行為的詮釋。 最後，是次研究會探討在一些沒有關系的情況下，感官刺激如何引導出情感上的反應，及影響其判斷。例如：證據顯示由於女性要照顧後代，所以在遇上威脅刺激時，女性是較男性傾向於尋求保護，而不是戰鬥或逃離。為了達到這個程度，在暴露於威脅的時候會使其性情活潑起來，從而對有保護性的人物及產品有較高的評價。

640011.label: Realisation of objectives
640011.value: We were able to achieve all three grant-related objectives. We conducted not only the studies that were proposed but several other ones. This has led to several publications and manuscripts that will soon be submitted. A brief discussion is provided below. Objective 1: To understand how conflicting signals from different sense modalities activate concepts and influence behavioral tendencies. We focused our enquiry on examining conflicting signals both within a sensory modality and across different modalities. Conflicting sensory input within a single sense modality. Advertising often shows images from different perspectives (e.g., images of both the interior and exterior of a hotel). When consumers think about this ad, they often imagine themselves in the scene and engage in self-imagery while processing information. The goals that they have when they engage in such imagery (e.g., a goal to construct a story of the experience vs. a goal to acquire information can influence how the mental images they generate affect judgments. When pictures from very different perspectives are provided, those trying to imagine themselves in the scene in order to create a story of the experience have to shift visual perspectives in order to imagine the entire experience. This shift in visual perspective can increase processing difficulty and decrease evaluations of the product or service described. When individuals are simply imagining themselves acquiring information about the product or service, however, presenting information from different perspectives has a positive effect on evaluations. We confirmed these effects and the assumptions underlying them through four experiments. Conflicting signals from different sense modalities. Here we focused on situations where people might receive conflicting input from different sense modalities (e.g., they might be evaluating a trip to a ski resort which provides visual input of something cold while they are holding a cup of coffee which provides tactile input of something hot). We ran a field study and 5 additional experiments to show that attention to the background sensory cue leads to a desire for something different from that experience. Thus, although holding a cup of ice-water increases people’s evaluation of a cold ski resort, it decreases their evaluation of the resort when their attention is explicitly drawn to the water’s temperature. This effect appears robust across sensory modalities and suggests that attention to background cues can serve as a motivational trigger. A paper based on these findings is being written up. Objective 2: To determine if abstract concepts used for judgments are based on metaphorical extensions of image schemas that are formed through recurring sensory experiences We looked at two different types of metaphors in this research – going against the flow and saving face. Going against the flow. In this research we examined how bodily experiences simulating the feeling of going against or with the flow affect consumers’ preferences for options that are normatively less popular. Such sensorimotor experiences involve both movement and have direction. We conceptualized that such experiences are represented in memory as image schemas and suggested that re-experiencing similar sensations activates this schema and elicits subjective feelings that trigger behavioral dispositions of going against the norm. In seven experiments, we showed that when consumers experience sensations of going against the flow, they pick alternatives that are normatively not preferred. We also showed that these effects of consumer preferences are evident only when the sensations are experienced by the self, subjective feelings are elicited and no other objective norm information is supplied. The effects cannot be explained through the simple semantic activation of concepts and that a feeling based explanation is more supportive of the data. Saving face. In this research, we showed that people who feel embarrassed are often motivated to avoid social contact—that is, to hide their face. Although this is evident in linguistic expressions such as “hide one’s face”, how people attempt to repair such a situation is unclear. People might be motivated to restore the positive image that has been tarnished by the embarrassing event (or, in other words, to restore the face lost in the event). Individuals can symbolically employ these coping strategies by choosing commercial products that literally either hide their face (e.g., sunglasses) or repair it (e.g., restorative cosmetics). However, the two coping strategies have different consequences. Although symbolically repairing one’s face eliminates aversive feelings of embarrassment and restores one’s willingness to engage in social activities, symbolically hiding one’s face has little impact. Objective 3: To examine how sensory perceptions can activate wired-in dispositions and influence judgments in unrelated domains. This objective was the most challenging. We expanded our investigation to include a broader set of sensory perceptions. Our sensory cues included visuals suggesting predator threat, ambient temperature, and the concept of money. The ability of these cues to activate wired-in dispositions appeared important from an evolutionary perspective. Predator threat. Exposure to animal prints or fur elicited fear although men and women responded to this differently. In general, men appeared to be more uncomfortable when the threat came from the side (e.g., fur samples displayed on the wall) lending some support to the assumption in evolutionary psychology that men are more vigilant to threat. Interestingly, they also appeared to feel more capable of controlling the environment in this condition. In another experiment, we found a similar pattern where male participants responded more negatively to instructions to close their eyes and touch a sample of fur whereas women participants were more trusting. Female participants, however, were more likely to look to men for support in the face of predator threat. This was evident in more favorable evaluation of males when they had been incidentally exposed to animal prints. Ambient temperature. According to research in evolutionary psychology, warm temperatures were conducive to survival and led people to congregate and get along. We examined the effects of temperature on conformity. Our research shows that comfortable ambient temperatures influence consumer preferences for conformity. The results of three laboratory experiments suggest that warm (vs. cool) temperatures dispose consumers toward using others' opinions as the basis for product preferences, stock price forecasts, and betting. Warm temperatures increased the participants' perceptions of social closeness to other decision-makers, thus leading them to consider the opinions of those decision-makers to have greater validity. This enhanced validity, in turn, rendered them more likely to conform to the crowd. This effect was confirmed in an analysis of betting behavior at the racetrack over a three-year period. Bets were more likely to converge on the “favorite” (i.e., the majority-endorsed option) when the temperature at the track was warm. Symbols of wealth. Next, we examined the effects of symbols of wealth. Transactions using some medium have been around for a long time and we were interested in the effects they have on human behavior. In six experiments we showed that activating the concept of money influenced people's own expressions of emotion as well as their reactions to the emotional expressions of others. Thinking about money increased their disposition to perceive themselves in a business-like relationship with others in which transactions are based on objective criteria and the expression of emotion is considered inappropriate. Therefore, these individuals express less emotion in public and expect others to do likewise.

640011.label: Major findings and research outcome
640011.value: Objective 1: Conflicting input about a target can come through one sense modality. In Jiang, Adaval, Steinhart & Wyer (2014), we showed that pictures from different perspectives decrease processing fluency and hurt evaluations when people construct a story of the experience. They, however, help evaluations when people acquire information. Conflicting input can also come through different sense modalities (e.g., touching something warm while evaluating a picture of ice cream). A shift in attention to the sensory cue that was originally in the background provides a standard of comparison and acts as a motivational trigger to seek something different (Chinchanachokchai & Adaval 2016; manuscript under preparation). Objective 2: Metaphorical expressions of “going against the flow/tide” capture past sensorimotor experiences one has had. Re-experiencing these sensations increased consumers’ preference for normatively less popular options. The effects were evident only when they were experienced by the self, the experience was dynamic, subjective feelings were elicited and no other objective norm information was supplied (Kwon & Adaval, 2015; revision at Journal of Consumer Research). Other metaphorical expressions describing reactions to embarrassment exist (e.g., hide/save one’s face). Symbolic coping strategies through the use of commercial products that hide one’s face or repair it had different effects on the alleviation of such feelings (Dong, Huang & Wyer, 2013). Symbolically repairing one’s face eliminated feelings of embarrassment and restored willingness to engage in social activities whereas hiding one’s face had little impact. Objective 3: Evolutionarily relevant sensory cues such as visuals of predators, ambient temperature, and the money were examined to see if they activated behavioral dispositions. Exposure to animal prints and fur elicited a fear of predators among men and a disposition to be vigilant and less trusting (Adaval, Ha & Kwon, 2016, manuscript in preparation). Women, in contrast, showed more trust and appeared to cope with the threat by seeking protection (evaluating males more favorably). Other cues that were evolutionarily conducive for survival (warm ambient temperature) were also examined (Huang, Zhang, Hui & Wyer, 2014) and found to trigger dispositions to conform to groups as reflected in the use of others' opinions as the basis for product preferences, stock price forecasts, and betting. Exposure to a third cue (money) revealed an increased disposition to perceive oneself in a business-like relationship with others, engage in transactions based on objective criteria and show less emotion (Jiang, Chen & Wyer 2014).

640011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
640011.value: The effects of sensory cues on cognitions are evident at different stages of information processing. The current project focused on how conflicting signals from different senses (e.g., temperature cues that were different when one was touching something and looking at something else) are encoded. We would like to extend this to consider an abstract concept such as magnitude. Cues and measures of time, spatial distance, numerosity are available all around us but are automatically coded into one general and abstract unit of magnitude. It would be interesting to examine how this happens and whether this process of converting magnitude from one modality into the other is automatic. We would also like to examine other types of image schemas and metaphors and their effects on behavior. We are currently examining metaphors related to the concept of time. Finally, we will expand the work to examine cultural dispositions that appear to be activated spontaneously. Two papers (Kwon, Saluja & Adaval, 2016 and Saluja, Adaval & Wyer, 2017) have already been published. Follow up work will examine if cultural differences have an evolutionary basis. That is, do people learn to process sensory information in a way that makes sense from an evolutionary perspective?

640011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
640011.value: Our research looked at how multi-sensory experiences affect judgments and behavior. We first looked at cues that provide different or conflicting signals. We found that images from different perspectives hurt when people are trying to form a story of the experience but help when they are collecting information. We also showed that when conflicting signals are received through different senses, attention to the sensory cue in the background motivates people to want something different from it. A second part of our research examined the effects of activating sensory experiences that are metaphorically represented in language. We found that experiences of going against the flow affects participants’ desire to choose something that is different from what is normatively preferred. Similarly, feelings of embarrassment activate metaphors of saving face and the symbolic use of different products helps alleviate these feelings. Finally, we explored if wired-in dispositions are activated through exposure to evolutionarily relevant sensory cues such as animal prints, ambient temperature and money. Exposure led to increased vigilance, conformity and transactional dispositions. In sum, this research made some important forays into our sensory world to understand how it is represented and how it affects our thoughts and behavior without our awareness.
