640811.label: Project Title(Chinese)
640811.value: 在逃遁與同化之間：中國西南苗族身份認同與他者政治

640811.label: Project Objectives
640811.value: To develop a new, alternative perspective on ethnic frontier politics in Southwest China and Highland Southeast Asia, highlighting ethnic minorities’ diverse modes of adaptation to state institution. To develop a theoretical concept of “appropriating otherness” for the formation of ethnic identity as one particular mode of ethnic minorities’ adaption to state institution. To bridge archival historical study and ethnographic fieldwork research for scrutinizing the transformation of ethnic identities among some selected non-Han groups in Southwest China. To produce research papers for academic conferences and publications in academic journals, and a draft of a book manuscript for future publication. To build a repository of archival and fieldwork data for academic sharing and exchanges. To train students through providing job opportunities of research assistants.

640811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
640811.value: The development of the Chinese empire and civilization was predicated on the construction of non-Chinese cultural others that marked the Chinese frontier and its expansion. The Miao were one of the prominent ethnic other in south China, and defined largely in terms of lack and as a counter image to Chinese civilization during imperial expansion. The formation and transformation of ethnic frontiers has often been in the paradigm of sinicization from the imperialist perspective, motivating insurgency and escape from the native point of view. Through archival study and ethnographic fieldwork research focusing on the region of southeast Guizhou province, this proposed study will attempt to explain the interaction between non-Han natives and Chinese imperial/national agents centering on the Chinese conception of Miao otherness and the natives’ conception of Chineseness. It will test the proposition that in the face of imperial expansion and nation-building in early modern and modern Chinese history non-Han natives actively exploited Miao otherness to form their ethnic identity, through which a Miao ethnic boundary was constructed and demarcated within the Chinese state. We propose to examine Miao otherness and Chineseness in non-Han oral and written records, including epics of insurgency and migration, millenarian religious beliefs and practices, native interpretations of cultural products such as writing scripts and embroidery, and non-Han intellectuals’ writings on ethnic identities. We will attempt to document the natives’ exposure to the idea of the Miao identity as otherness in imperial discourses about “rebellions” throughout history, their exploitation of Miao otherness in their struggle for official recognition as an ethnic minority during the Republican period, their refashioning of Miao identity to accommodate the Communist regime’s discourses and institutions for ethnic minorities, and some native groups’ protest against imposed Miao otherness to struggle for a separate minority identity as a result of historical and contemporary local inter-group politics. This study will explore the idea that between total Sinicization and fleeing the Chinese state there existed a huge space of engagement in which non-Han natives maintained their identity, albeit not in the pure and original form usually imagined in discussions of identity politics. The investigation of non-Han natives’ agency in the politics of othering on the periphery of the Chinese civilization will contribute to our understanding of the formation of ethnic minority identities in the modern Chinese nation-state. 中華帝國與文明的發展離不開將非華夏族群建構為文化他者，用以標識帝國的邊緣。在中華帝國南向擴張的歷史過程中，“苗族”是中華異族想象中的重要他者，在歷史文献上常常以其負面意象來作為中華文明的反照。族際邊疆的形成和轉化經常顯露於帝國視野下的“同化”範式，或土著觀點中的反抗和遷徙論述。本研究透過文獻檔案和在貴州省東南部的實地田野考察， 嘗試圍繞著漢人概念中的苗族他者和土著概念中的漢人他者，來探討另一種涉及中華帝國及其近代國家的代理人與非漢人土著之間複雜的互動。 研究旨在分析論證在皇朝擴張和近代國族建构的歷史過程中，一些非汉人族群積極地採用漢人的苗族他者意象去塑造自己的身分， 促成在國家體制中苗族族群邊界的建構和規劃。 本研究將考察在非漢人土著的口頭傳統和書寫記錄中關於苗人和漢人的他者意像，資料包括土著起義反抗和遷徙定居的史詩、千年教的信仰和實踐、對文字和刺繡等文化產物的解釋， 以及非漢人知識分子關於族群身分認同的著述等。 考察著重探索土著所接觸在歷史上關於反抗叛亂的皇朝話語中作為他者的苗族身份意像、在民國時期土著精英如何採用苗族的他者身份來爭取官方承認其為少數民族， 在1949年後他們如何重塑苗族身份來適應共產政權的少數民族制度和話語，以及一些土著群體在歷史上和當代的地方族群政治中所產生的身分差異， 如何促使他們反對國家所識別的苗族身份和爭取與之不同的民族身份。 是項研究將探討非漢人土著與漢人國家的互動形態中，在攀附同化與反抗逃遁的兩個模式之間所存在的多元形態， 以及在這些型態中土著如何維繫自我族群的身分認同。 當然這些身分認同並不會如一般身份政治的論述中所想像的原本純正型態。 探討中華文化邊緣中的非漢人土著在身分政治中的能動性， 將有助我們了解近代中國民族國家中少數族群身分認同的形成。

640811.label: Realisation of objectives
640811.value: By critically examining different academic approaches that explain the interaction between numerous non-state ethnic groups and surrounding state civilizations in Southwest China and Mainland Southeast Asia, my project has successfully formulated a model of ethnic frontier politics as a continuum between escape and assimilation. Focusing on the Miao groups in Guizhou, China, the model covers the realities of state expansion and cultural assimilation, yet also accounts for native resistance and agency for the pursuit of autonomy. The variation along the continuum suggests how natives maintain their identities while engaging the state according to local conditions. Based on archival and historical studies, I have developed a theoretical concept of “appropriating otherness” to understand a particular native strategy, by which the natives formulate their own Miao ethnic identities during the construction of the modern Chinese nation-state in the first half of the twentieth century according to the Chinese imagery of their ethnic “others” on the frontier. After 1949, when the newly founded People’s Republic implemented its state project of ethnic classification and established the minority institution, there was no escape from being classified as either the Han or as one of the fifty-five officially classified minorities. My project focuses on the Ge group who have been fighting against state classification as a branch of Miao and striving for official recognition of their self-claimed identity. Through ethnographic fieldwork research, the Ge’s strategy of appropriating otherness to resist their assimilation into the officially defined minority system has been thoroughly investigated. My project has successfully bridged archival historical study and ethnographic fieldwork research for scrutinizing the transformation of ethnic identities among the Miao and the Ge in Southwest China. So far, eight conference papers have been produced, many of which have been published as journal articles and book chapters, and one book manuscript has been prepared, whose publication will be explored soon. As part of the repository of archival and fieldwork data generated by this project, an anthology of the writings of a prominent elite member of the Miao in western Guizhou will be published soon for academic sharing and exchanges. The successful realisation of this project’s objectives was partly based on the involvement of my seven postgraduate students, including one PhD and six MPhils, who served as research assistants at the various stages of my project. Meanwhile, they also received research training for their own thesis projects. So far, all of them have successfully graduated from their programs.

640811.label: Major findings and research outcome
640811.value: By formulating a theoretical model of ethnic frontier politics as a continuum between escape and assimilation, and the native strategy of appropriating the Chinese imagery of ethnic otherness to create the natives’ identities in their engagement with state civilizations, I published the journal article “Appropriating Otherness and the Contention of Miao Identity in Southwest China” and the book chapter “Between Escape and Assimilation: Miao Identity in Southwest China and the Politics of Recognition.” The recurrent Miao millenarian rebellion in history was based on a cyclical historical consciousness about the reincarnation of the Miao King and the mimesis of Chinese symbols of power and wealth related to state civilizations, as illustrated in the book chapter “Ethnic Identity and Historical Consciousness: The Cases of the Miao and the Ge in Guizhou Province.” I argue that mimesis served to strengthen the natives’ self-identities for resisting assimilation. I further contrast the natives’ strategy of “appropriating otherness” with that of “mimesis” in the book chapter “Mimesis and Appropriation: Tactics of Ethnic Identity Politics between Escape and Assimilation in Southeast Guizhou.” The two book chapters “From ‘Democracy of Civil Rights’ to ‘Democracy of Ethnicity’: On the Relationship between Liang Juwu’s Conception of Democracy and Ethnic Politics” and “Yang Hanxian’s Writings on the Identities of the Miao in Western Guizhou” are case studies on specific native elite members’ writings to present their native identities and strive for official recognition of their minority status. The Anthology of Ethnic Studies by Yang Hanxian is a compilation of the writer’s life history and his writings to contextualize his writing strategies of mimesis and appropriating otherness under particular historical circumstances. The book chapter “Miaowang, Sama, and Zhuge Liang: Religious Worship and Ethnic Interaction in Chejiang Basin of Southeast Guizhou Province, China” studies how the Miao and Dong ethnic groups employed different strategies in response to the encroachment of the Chinese empire, resulting in their differential topographic distribution in the basin area developed for wet-rice cultivation. Another book chapter “Re-ethnicizing Southeast Guizhou Migrants Community in the Pearl River Delta Region of Southeast China” examines how peasant migrant workers from Guizhou renounced their ethnic identities in the beginning of their settlement in the Pearl River Delta region during the 1980s and 1990s, and how their Miao identity re-emerged under the officially sanctioned development of multi-ethnic urbanism and their interaction with their home village. These major findings and research outcome constitute the core data and analyses of the book manuscript Between Escape and Assimilation: Miao Identity in Southwest China and the Politics of Recognition.

640811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
640811.value: 1) Potential research projects on the differential strategies of different non-Han native groups in the multi-ethnic setting of frontier regions will be proposed to further investigate the conditions that shaped the natives’ different responses toward the Chinese state civilization. 2) The writings of individual native elite members on non-Han native identities in response to the making of the modern Chinese nation-state during the Republican period and after the founding of the People’s Republic in 1949, together with the writers’ fully contextualized life history, will be collected and compiled for publication. They will bring further development of the research on different native strategies based on local conditions in relation to the development of Chinese nationalism and its local responses. 3) A conference on non-Han native elites’ writing on native identities in the different ethnic regions of China in response to the making of the modern Chinese nation-state will be organized. The conference papers will be compiled for the publication of an edited volume on the comparison among different native strategies toward Chinese nationalism under different local conditions.

640811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
640811.value: Due to its rough terrains divided by crosscutting mountain ranges and big river valleys, the region of Southwest China and Mainland Southeast Asia has long been the hub of numerous non-state native groups in constant interaction with surrounding state civilizations. This project aims to propose a new model of frontier ethnic politics constituting diverse native strategies in a continuum between escape from state rule to maintain native identity, at the one end; and assimilation into the state subject’s cultural identity, at the other end. With reference to the case of the Miao in Guizhou province, southwest China, the native strategies of mimesis and appropriating otherness to assert native identity while engaging the Chinese state are examined. The former adopted Chinese symbols of power and wealth to strengthen native identity in resistance against state rule, as found in the age-old recurrent Miao rebellions; the latter appropriated the Chinese imagery of the Miao as ethnic others to create native identity, as exemplified by native elites’ writing about Miao identity to strive for minority status in the making of the modern Chinese nation-state. A combination of these strategies was employed in response to the construction of a multi-ethnic Socialist state after 1949.

641011.label: Project Title(Chinese)
641011.value: 對信息衝擊的過度和不足反應：來自即場體育博彩交易的證據

641011.label: Project Objectives
641011.value: Show that bettors overreact to confirming evidence and underreact to disconfirming evidence in the in-play soccer betting market. The benchmark is the right level of reaction, which is estimated using actual match results. Test whether there is any correction in the betting market after bettors have overreacted and underreacted. Link the correction mechanism to profitable betting strategies. This documents evidence of the existence of arbitrageurs and their impact on market efficiency. Calculate the amount of profits made by arbitrageurs. The arbitrageurs are making profits at the expense of irrational bettors, and the amount represents the cost of overreaction and underreaction. Construct a dataset with soccer match events and real-time betting odds. With the advantage of observing the precise payoffs, the sports betting dataset allows researchers to perform analyses that cannot be done with stock market data.

641011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
641011.value: Our project will use the unique setting in the soccer betting market to study overreaction and underreaction to information shocks, as well as the potential correction mechanism by arbitrageurs. In a soccer match, goals provide new information about the final outcome: a team is more likely to win the match after it scores a goal. We will study how bettors react immediately after the goal. Moreover, we can compare the observed reaction to the estimated correct level of reaction. Any deviation between the two will imply overreaction or underreaction. The betting market offers an advantage over the financial market because the final payouts are well defined and the true probabilities can be estimated using actual match outcomes. In contrast, dividends and distributions of financial securities are a stream of income that does not have a clear end; overreaction and underreaction in the financial market are not easily identified because there is no benchmark to compare with. To test our predictions, we will obtain real-time in-play data from the largest internet betting exchange in the world. The in-play market allows bettors to place bets after the match starts and before it ends. For each match, we will collect data on all the bets, the outcomes they bet on, and the corresponding odds. The odds specify the payoffs bettors would receive if an outcome happens. For example, a bet on a draw with odds 5.00 will receive $5 for every $1 of bet if the match indeed ends in a draw (including the original $1 bet). In a fair game the implied probability of this event from the odds is 1/5. If bettors overreact to a goal, they rush to bet on the scoring team and bid down the odds; as a result the implied probability will be inflated and larger than the estimated true probability. We expect that bettors overreact to information consistent with their prior beliefs, that is, when the team favored by bettors scores. We expect that they underreact to information inconsistent with their prior beliefs. Any overreaction and underreaction in the betting market will likely to be short-lived and eventually reversed. We will test this reversal and determine whether any professional bettors are involved in the process. Profits could be made during the correction. If the overreaction and underreaction are due to psychological biases, the profits would measure the wealth transfer from irrational agents to more rational agents. 我們的計劃將利用足球博彩市場的獨特環境，去研究對信息衝擊的過度和不足反應，以及套利者可能的糾正機制。 在足球比賽中，入球為最終的結果提供新的信息：入球的一隊贏得這場比賽的機會將會增加。我們會研究投注者在入球後如何作出即時反應。此外，我們可以比較觀察到的反應及估計的正確反應，兩者之間的任何偏差將意味著過度或不足反應。比起金融市場，博彩市場提供了一個優勢，因為我們可以明確界定最終收入和使用實際比賽結果去估計真正的概率。與此相反，金融證券分派的股息是一連串沒有明確結束的收入；因為沒有基準來比較，反應過度和反應不足在金融市場是不容易識別的。 為了測試我們的預測，我們將獲取來自世界上最大的互聯網博彩交易市場的實時滾球盤數據。滾球盤允許投注者在比賽進行期間下注。在每場比賽中，我們將收集所有的賭注、他們賭的結果、以及相應賠率的數據。賠率界定了投注者在結果發生時將收到的收益。例如平局賠率是 5.00時，如比賽以平局結束每1元的賭注將獲得5元（包括原來的1元賭注）。在一個公平的遊戲，此事件從賠率推算的隱含概率為 1 / 5。如果投注者對入球有過度反應，他們會急於下注入球一方並使賠率下降，因此隱含的概率將大於估計的真實概率。我們預計，投注者對信息的過度反應將會符合其事先信念，那就是，當投注者所青睞的一方進球時。我們期望他們對不符合其事先信念的信息有不足反應。 在博彩市場任何過度和不足反應將很可能是短暫的及最終會被扭轉的。我們將對此進行測試，並確定是否有專業投注者參與了這一逆轉的過程。更正時會產生利潤，如果過度和不足反應的成因是心理偏見，這利潤將測量非理性和比較理性的行為者之間的財富轉移。

641011.label: Realisation of objectives
641011.value: All the objectives are achieved. We built a dataset with soccer match events and betting odds. We analyzed how bettors react to goals in an in-play soccer betting market. Market participants underreact to “expected” goals but overreact to "surprising" goals. We found that these biased reactions attenuate over time and disappear at around 5 min after the goal. Our findings are both statistically and economically significant: a strategy based on the bias earns a profit of 2.46% after commissions.

641011.label: Major findings and research outcome
641011.value: Previous research in finance has found evidences of both overreaction and underreaction to unanticipated events, but has yet to explain why investors overreact to certain events while underreacting to others. In this paper, we hypothesize that while market participants generally underreact to new events due to conservatism, the extent of underreaction is moderated by "surprise," thus causing market participants to overreact to events that are highly surprising. We test our hypothesis using data from an in-play soccer betting market, where new events (goals) are clearly and exogenously defined, and the degree of "surprise" can be directly quantified (goals scored by underdogs are more surprising). We provide both statistical and economic evidences in support of our hypothesis.

641011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
641011.value: With the advantage of observing the precise payoffs, the sports betting dataset allows researchers to perform analyses that cannot be done with stock market data. We plan to use the dataset to study other potential biases and arbitrage opportunities.

641011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
641011.value: We developed and tested a behaviorally motivated hypothesis of how investors underreact or overreact to unanticipated events. Specifically, we hypothesized that overreaction and underreaction are driven by conservatism and "surprise". When reacting to an event that is expected or only moderately surprising, market participants insufficiently update their prior beliefs due to conservatism and hence underreact. In contrast, a more "surprising" event, i.e., an event that strongly violates prior expectations, attracts more cognitive processing as participants attempt to "make sense" of the incongruence between the observed event and their current schema. This in turn amplifies the surprising event and attenuates other sources of information (i.e., their prior beliefs), thereby resulting in a higher "weight" being put on the new event when forming a judgment. Thus, underreaction is moderated by surprise; for extremely surprising events, market participants overweight the new information, leading to overreaction.

641111.label: Project Objectives
641111.value: Construct a small open economy model in which search frictions lead to a sluggish response of exports to external shocks.
rows: Construct a small open economy model in which search frictions lead to a sluggish response of exports to external shocks.

641111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
641111.value: In a globalized economy, the effectiveness of a country's response to the business cycle environment depends on the speed of adjustment of its trade balance. Consider Asian countries in the late 1990’s. Those countries ran large trade deficits with spending outstripping production, the gap was financed by borrowing abroad. The sudden withdrawal of funds in 1998 and the consequent decline in domestic spending faced these economies with two choices: increase exports or reduce output. The degree to which an economy finds itself able to adjust its exports in the wake of a current account reversal should determine how fast economic growth recovers from a financial crisis. This study proposes a new model of the dynamic export adjustment for a small open economy facing a need to adjust its external imbalances. Observation suggests that in many cases exports respond slowly to both current account reversals and to fluctuations in real exchange rates. Indeed, one of the central issues facing the global economy as this is proposal is being written is the need for a global re-adjustment of external imbalances by a wide variety of countries including many economies in North America and East Asia. This proposed study attempts to develop a theory of slow export adjustment. There are a number of building blocks. The first is that exports are traded through long-lasting relationships with importers in other countries. The second is that firms expanding their exports need to forge new relationships overseas to distribute their goods. The third is that forging such relationships takes both time and money. Further, given a limited number of potential trading partners, the likelihood of an individual firm finding a trading partner will be relatively low in a period in which many similar firms are also searching. When combined, these elements provide a model in which exports only grow slowly and in which the barriers to exports in terms of marketing costs and excess inventories rise during periods when aggregate export growth is high. This model will be incorporated into otherwise standard quantitatively oriented macroeconomic models of international economies. This is important as it will allow for an empirical assessment of the degree to which slow export adjustment will actually matter (in numerical terms) for explaining business cycle dynamics. This will also facilitate examination of the impact of monetary or fiscal policy on the dynamics of export adjustment. 在全球化经济中，一个国家的有效应对商业周期的环境依赖于贸易平衡的调整速度。考虑在1990年代后期的亚洲国家。这些国家跑了庞大的贸易赤字;与消费超过了生产，差距是由外国贷款融资。在1998年突然撤出资金，在国内消费随之下降受影响，面临着两种选择：增加出口或减少产量。一个经济体在何种程度上发现自己能够适应经常账户逆转后，其出口应确定的经济增长会从金融危机中恢复的程度。 该项目构建了一个小型的开放经济，面临着需要调整其外部失衡的动态出口调整的新模式。经验观察显示，在许多情况下的出口响应缓慢，同时经常账户逆转和实际汇率的波动。也不是为这个项目只是历史的动机。 ，因为这对全球经济所面临的核心问题之一是建议，是被写入的全球外部失衡的一个种类繁多，包括在北美和东亚的许多经济体的国家重新调整的需要。 这项建议发展缓慢调整出口的理论。有这一理论的积木数量。首先是出口交易是通过与其他国家的进口商的长期关系。第二是扩大出口的企业需要建立新的关系，海外分发货物。三是建立这种关系需要时间和金钱。此外，一个潜在的贸易伙伴的数量有限，个别公司寻找贸易伙伴的可能性将相对较低，在这个时期，很多类似的公司也搜索。这些元素结合时，提供的出口模式，只能出现缓慢和期间的障碍，出口营销成本和库存过剩的时期上升时，总的出口增长高。 这种模式将被纳入量化标准，否则面向国际经济的宏观经济模型。这是很重要的，因为这将使程度的实证评估，缓慢调整出口实际上将此事解释商业循环动力学（数值计算）。这也让我们研究如何实施货币政策或财政政策将影响出口的调整力度。

641111.label: Realisation of objectives
641111.value: The project objective was to construct a small open economy model with search frictions in export markets. To be more specific, the goal was to construct a dynamic general equilibrium model of a small open economy populated by optimizing agents with rational expectations. This model would attempt to explain why exports responded so sluggishly to the real exchange rate depreciation that tends to occur so dramatically during international financial crises such as that seen in the events in East Asia during the late 1990's. The project achieved this objective. A small open economy model has been constructed and solved. Many aspects of the dynamic behavior of the model is covered in a working paper being finalized for submission to an academic journal. The approach was to incorporate Pissarides style matching frictions into the standard export model equation. The challenge of this approach was to adapt a model that was developed for labor markets to an international goods market. Though, labor market search, in the standard model, requires the payment of fixed costs to post job vacancies of buyers of labor, employers. Developing the model to account for the potential for an endogenous internal set of agents (representing domestic exporters) and an external set of agents (representing foreign importers) and their interactions in search markets. The approach ultimately taken by this project (after some others were attempted) was to model both domestic exporters and foreign importers as searching globally. This means that domestic exporters were impacted by a mix of domestic and global conditions, but foreign importers take global events as given. In this set of circumstances, a rise in external interest rates impact incentives to invest in building customers which might offset the impact of those interest rates on real exchange rates. Further, the fact that global conditions do not change will also limit the impact on availability of international distribution channels for domestic export goods. These two things combined will slow the response of exports to external shocks.

641111.label: Major findings and research outcome
641111.value: We are primarily interested in understanding the dynamic response to an international financial crisis. The experiment to consider will be a simulation of an international financial crisis. Cook and Devereux (2005) show that external interest rates rose sharply for East Asian economies in the late 1990's. To model a financial crisis, we use a 400 annualized basis point rise in the external bond interest rate, lasting for exactly 8 quarters before reverting to the long-term steady state. A rise in external interest rates will (through well understood channels) result in a decline in domestic demand, a current account reversal and a real exchange rate depreciation. The real exchange rate depreciation will make domestic exports more attractive on international markets. However, search frictions limit this response along two key dimensions. First, according to the model of search frictions, sunk costs must be put into building distribution. A rising interest rate will increase the time cost of this fixed cost. Second, any increase in number of domestic firms seeking export markets will experience diminishing returns in their likelihood of finding them. Each of these will slow the expansion of markets. The model is quantitative and the effect is substantial. In the baseline case examined, exports jump immediately by 5% in a financial crisis in a standard model but by less than .5% in a model with search frictions. The equilibrium of the model with search frictions also has some additional qualitative properties which are interesting from the standpoint of the study of international financial crises. First, in equilibrium, the adjustment of real exchange rate and the terms of trade to an external interest rate shock are far larger when exports are sluggish to adjust. The price at which people will be willing to consume the domestic good falls more when export customers cannot absorb the good. When exchange rates depreciate more severely, the optimal labor decline is also more severe. Each of these are consistent with emerging market financial crises which saw large scale exchange rate depreciation and a large contraction in GDP. The paper is written up in a working paper "Searching for International Demand," which describes these results. The paper is in the final stages of preparation for submission to journals and conferences.

641111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
641111.value: A recent paper written by myself with Woon Gyu Choi titled "Jobs and Collateral: Financial Frictions and Unemployment," labor market search frictions are combined in a model with financial market imperfections to generate a model in which transitory shocks to wealth of borrows leads to a persistent movement in output and employment. One potential line of research would be to incorporate financial frictions into the model to examine the role of balance sheets in the dynamics of exports and trade credit.

641111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
641111.value: An emerging market beset by an international financial crisis must expand its trade balance due to changes in borrowing conditions. The trade balance can change either through reduced imports which negatively impacts the consumption and investment opportunities of the small economy. Alternatively, the trade balance could be improved by expanding exports. However, we are able to identify a channel which might cause exports to adjust slowly to the financial crisis, exacerbating the negative effects. Financial crises can be a unique opportunity to sharply identify the channels determining the dynamics of the economy. Our findings can help policy-makers and others understand the importance of stability in the trade balance for the smooth functioning of the economy.

641211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
641211.value: Inventory investment is an extremely important component of firms’ response to economic fluctuations. According to Blinder and Maccini (1991), on average, declines in inventory investment accounted for 87% of the drop in US Gross Domestic Product in US post-war recessions. When sales drop, firms may initially accumulate inventory, and then deplete inventory, cutting down on production. This might be one of the most important channels through which adverse economic shocks are propagated throughout the economic system in a downturn. Conversely, in an expansion, firms may initially run out of inventory and then replenish inventory by increasing production. Surprisingly, this type of behavior has been difficult to identify in the data. The behavior described above conforms to the intuition that firms pile up inventory so that they do not have to stretch production capacity when demand for their products surges. Thus, when demand surges, firms sell (and deplete) inventory, rather than increase it. This is known as “production smoothing”. However, evidence shows that not all firms behave in this manner. In fact, there is evidence that many firms behave in the opposite manner -- that is, increasing inventory when demand surges, called “production bunching”. In this research, we propose to examine to what extent firms' inventory investment is affected by their ability to raise capital and expand production capacity when they experience shocks to demand. If higher demand today is associated with higher demand in the near future, then we expect firms that find it easier to raise capital will expand capacity and also build inventory to serve future demand. Although this behavior has the appearance of “production bunching” (since production responds more than sales), it is likely to involve some element of production smoothing since firms carry inventory in anticipation of future demand. On the other hand, firms that find it more difficult to raise capital will mostly sell out of inventory and only add to capacity slowly when there is a favorable demand shock. Conversely, when there is an adverse demand shock, firms that find it difficult to raise capital will again deplete inventory more rapidly to generate cash flows to cover fixed production costs. Further, firms that find it more difficult to raise capital will adjust inventory behavior more in response to market conditions that affect the cost of financing, as well as to shocks to production costs which they find difficult to hedge against.

641211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
641211.value: It has been recognized that change in inventory contributes significantly to the drop in Gross Domestic Product during recessions -- some studies suggest that for the United States, inventory depletion accounts for as much as 87% of the drop in GDP in recessions. Our objective in this research is to study inventory behavior at the firm level to better understand aggregate inventory behavior. In particular, we focus on the role played by financing frictions (i.e., the difficulty in raising external financing) in affecting inventory behavior. We find evidence that the inventory behavior of financially constrained firms differ in significant ways from that of unconstrained firms. Capacity constraints, more binding on average for financially constrained firms, and capital adjustment costs play a critical role in explaining why financially constrained firms hold more inventory and also exhibit more volatility in inventory.

641311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
641311.value: The moral and ethical crisis in China is well-documented. In 2001, CNN reported that a university student illegally took a college entrance examination for a high school student in Shandong Province. Ironically, the student was asked to write about the significance of chengxin (honesty and trustworthiness) in the Chinese language exam. This was not an isolated incident. Guangdong’s Educational Department found that at least one-sixth of the certificates circulating in the province were fake. Other fake products of inferior (even poisonous) quality—such as rice, milk powder, liquor, medicine, TV sets, and computers—were reported by CNN to be widely sold in China. China is not the only nation suffering from such unethical scandals. In the North America, the Enron scandal resulted in multiple indictments. Barrick, the Toronto-based gold-mining corporation, was accused of manipulating land titles in Australia and Chile. The ethical crisis is clearly widespread across countries and continents, leading behavioral researchers to ask questions about the factors that lead to ethical and unethical behavior. In the last two decades, a large body of literature has accumulated on ethical and unethical behavior in organizations (see Trevino, Weaver, & Reynolds, 2006 for a review). Unfortunately, this research has predominantly been conducted in the West, with little research being done in China. Our knowledge about behavioral ethics in the Chinese context is still in its infancy. The purpose of the present proposal is to develop theory explaining employee moral behavior in Chinese organizations by drawing on recent advances in ethical and cross-cultural research. It is proposed that Chinese employees’ moral behavior is driven by the combined effect of organizational contextual factors (ethical leadership of supervisors and team ethical climate) as well as individual cultural values (power distance orientation). The effect of these contextual and individual factors on employee moral behavior is transmitted through employee ethical motivation (moral engagement and moral identity). The proposed project is expected to make significant theoretical and practical contributions. Theoretically, this project will enrich extant understanding of how ethical leadership and other organizational phenomena interact with individual cultural values to impact moral motivation and behavior. Practically, this research will offer advice to managers on how to create positive work contexts to facilitate employees’ moral behavior. 大量材料表明中國存在倫理道德危機。2001年，CNN報導一名大學生涉嫌非法替一名山東省高中生參加高考。諷刺的是在語文考試中這名學生要就誠信的重要性寫作文。與此相關還有同類事件。廣東省教育廳查明，該省內流通的教育文憑至少有六分之一系偽造文憑。據CNN報導，其他假冒偽劣產品，如大米、奶粉、白酒、藥品、電視機及電腦，在中國銷售廣泛。中國並非唯一遭受此類非道德醜聞的國家。在北美，安然醜聞引發多方控訴。來自多倫多的Barrick黃金公司在澳洲和智利被指控暗中操控土地所有權。顯然不同國家與地區均有遭受道德危機，這引發了行為學學者對於道德與非道德行為誘因的思考。過去二十年，組織行為學領域積累了大量有關道德與非道德行為的文獻（Trevino, Weaver, & Reynolds, 2006）。然而相關研究主要在西方開展，中國的研究甚微。就中國情境下行為道德的研究還處於萌芽階段。本研究計畫的目的是，基於近期倫理道德及跨文化研究的進展，發展解釋中國企業員工道德行為的相關理論。該計畫提出中國員工的道德行為由組織情境因素（即主管的道德領導和團隊的道德氛圍）以及個人文化價值觀（權力距離）共同決定。上述情境因素及個人因素對員工道德行為的作用效果由員工道德動機（道德認同與道德參與）仲介傳遞。該專案計畫預期會做出理論與實踐雙重貢獻。理論上，該專案有助於拓展對於道德領導及其他組織現象與個人文化價值觀交互影響道德動機與行為的理解。實踐上，該研究會為管理者提供如何構建積極工作環境以促進員工道德行為的建議。

641311.label: Realisation of objectives
641311.value: The major goals of this project have been achieved. Regarding Objective 1, I have examined the combined effects of ethical leadership and team members’ power distance orientation on team members’ moral behavior in Chinese organizations. In terms of ethical leadership, I examined not only ethical leadership (Brown, Trevino, & Harrison, 2005) but also leaders’ idealized influence and pro-organizational unethical behavior (UPB). In terms of the effects of individual differences in power distance orientation values on unethicality, I broadened the research scope to include the full range of individual personal values using Schwartz’s values framework as well as Dweck’s achievement motivation framework. Regarding Objective 2, I found that team members’ moral disengagement emerged as the sole individual-level mediating mechanism. After controlling for moral disengagement, moral identity no longer had any effect. Team unethical climate did not emerge as a useful mediator in multilevel modeling. Regarding Objective 3, I found a cross-level interaction between leaders’ UPB and employees’ power distance orientation in affecting employees’ moral disengagement and unethical behaviors. Regarding Objective 4, the project has produced several useful practical findings for managing employee ethics in the Chinese contexts. A major challenge in this study was the difficulty in obtaining objective data for unethical behaviors in the Chinese contexts. I found that Chinese supervisors and organizations were unwilling to provide such data even when confidentiality is guaranteed. I had to rely on time-lagged self-report data for employees’ unethical behaviors.

641311.label: Major findings and research outcome
641311.value: The research project has been implemented. In terms of research output, it has resulted in four meeting papers (Feldman et al., 2012; Chao & Farh, 2013; Liang et al., 2014; Yu et al., 2014), one publication (Feldman et al., 2015), one paper under review (Chao & Farh, under review at Academy of Management Journal), and one working paper (Farh et al., working paper). Several major findings were obtained in the Chinese contexts. First, ethical leadership (operationalized as idealized influence of transformational leadership) reduced employees’ unethical sales behavior (see Chao & Farh, under review, Study 1). Second, subordinates who observed their managers’ pro-organizational unethical behavior (UPB) tended to be morally disengaged, which in turn led to an increase in their unethical behavior (Farh et al., working paper). This detrimental effect of managers’ UPB on subordinate’s unethicality is especially strong for those subordinates who are high in power distance orientation (Farh et al., working paper). Third, ethical leadership as operationalized by Brown, Trevino, & Harrison (2005) increased employees’ positive work behaviors (i.e., conscientiousness and work performance) through employee organization-based self-esteem (Liang et al. 2014). Fourth, individuals’ personal value systems predicted their unethical attitudes and behavior (Feldman et al., 2015). Results from samples from China as well as around the world demonstrated that unethicality was positively associated with self-enhancement values and negatively with self-transcendence and conservation values. However, self-transcendence and conservation values were associated with the inhibition of different types of unethicality. The relationship of openness to change values with unethicality was generally positive but the effect size varied depending on context. Finally, amoral individual characteristics, such as achievement goal orientations, influenced ethical outcomes in organizations, even after controlling for social influence exerted by authority figures and individuals’ personal commitment to moral standards (Chao & Farh, under review). Across three studies, we found that learning goal orientation was associated with less unethical choices. Although both avoid and prove performance goal orientations showed positive effects on unethicality, it was the desire to avoid failure, not the motivation to succeed, that was significantly associated with more unethical outcomes.

641311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
641311.value: The following research directions are worth pursuing in future research. First, extant research on leadership has focused on ethical leader behaviors (such as leader’s integrity) with little attention to unethical leader behaviors. Future research should examine the influence of leaders’ unethical behaviors (such as pro-organizational unethical behavior) on employee and organizational outcomes. Second, individual personal values and differences in achievement motives have been found to predict unethicality in this project but their effects are not always strong. Future research should examine the conditional effects of social contexts (such as unethical leader/peer behaviors and moral intensity of the situation) in influencing the strength of these relationships. Third, the research findings in this project were obtained primarily through field surveys and thus weak in internal validity. Although time-lagged research designs with multisource data were used extensively in this project to boost causal influence, more experimental research is needed to isolate the exact mediating mechanisms.

641311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
641311.value: The research project has produced three important research findings for the Chinese contexts. First, while leader’s ethical behaviors can promote employees’ ethical conduct in organizations, leaders’ unethical behaviors can also have strong negative influence on employees’ ethical behaviors. This negative effect of leaders’ unethical behavior occurs even when leaders perform such behaviors in the interest of the company, and especially strong for those employees who have high respect for leaders’ hierarchical positions. Second, employees’ personal value systems predict their unethical attitudes and behavior. Unethical attitudes and behaviors are positively associated with self-enhancement values and negatively with self-transcendence and conservation values. Finally, employees’ achievement orientation affects their ethical conduct in work situations. Specifically, employees who are motivated by learning are less likely to behave unethically, whereas employees who are motivated to avoid failure are more likely to behave unethically.

641411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
641411.value: The received wisdom in corporate finance is that in countries where legal protection of outside investors is poor or well enforced, investors are not willing to provide financing to firms and that firms are passive recipients of the influences of weak investor protection. For example, when external financing is not readily available, firms may simply stop growing before they reach their attainable size. A question that naturally arises then is: can firms credibly commit to good governance practices to mitigate the negative impact of weak investor protection at the country level? If yes, to what extent does such a “substitution” mechanism work and at what cost? This project proposes to empirically examine possible commitment mechanisms that firms use to establish a reputation for good treatment of shareholders. Specifically, we attempt to show that in countries where legal protection of shareholders is weak, firms with good growth prospects establish capital-market reputation through commitments to generous dividends so that they can gain better access to the equity market in the future. We will also use the same methodology to explore other possible commitment mechanisms, including (1) accounting quality and (2) frequency and methods of equity issuance (rights offering vs. conventional seasoned equity offerings). This project has important academic and practical value. Academically, if we can show that that firms actively build reputation to (partially) compensate for weak investor protection, the project fills a gap in our understanding of the dynamics of how institutional factors and corporate finance are played in the real markets. It suggests a need to reassess the overall impact of country-level institutional factors on finance. Practically, it also suggests room for regulatory enforcement, such as mandatory dividends, as an (albeit imperfect) alternative to judiciary enforcement. 根據企業融資文獻的中的智慧，當國家法律保護外來投資者不善或是很好執行，投資者都不願意提供企業融資, 而且企業是投資者保護薄弱的被動接受者。例如，當沒有現成的外部融資時，企業停止生長，且不能到達他們預計大小。一個自然出現的問題則是：企業可不可以使用良好的治理實踐，以減輕國家對投資者保護薄弱的負面影響？如果有的話， 這樣的工作機制“替代”到什麼程度，以及有什麼樣的代價呢？ 該計劃建議對公司使用承諾機制建立良好保護股東聲譽進行實證研究。具體來說，我們 試圖表明，當國家保護股東的法律薄弱，良好增長前景的企業通過對承諾慷慨的分紅,建立資本市場良好的聲譽，使他們能未來更好的進入股市融資。我們也將使用同樣的方法來探索其他可能的承諾機制，包括（1）會計核算的質量（2）頻率和股權發行的方法（配股與傳統的股票發行）。 該計劃具有重要的學術價值和實用價值。在學術上，如果我們可以證明公司積極建立信譽(部分）補償薄弱的投資者保護，該計劃填補我們在了解體制因素和企業融資如何在市場操作。它建議我們需要重新評估國家一級的體制性因素對財政的整體影響。在實用價值上，這也表明監管執法的空間，如使用強制股息（儘管不完善）來替代司法機關執法。

641411.label: Major findings and research outcome
641411.value: The existing literature on law and finance generally assumes that firms are passive recipients of the influence of investor protections on their ability to raise external financing. In this paper, we empirically identify two commitment mechanisms, i.e., dividend payouts and accounting conservatism, which firms use to establish a reputation for better treatment of outside shareholders in order to compensate for country-level weak protection of shareholders and to obtain better access to equity markets. We show that, in weak-protection countries, firms with growth prospects tend to initiate dividends earlier and pay a higher level of dividends not only as compared to their counterparts in strong protection countries but also as compared to low-growth firms in the same legal regime. As evidence of better access to capital markets, in weak-protection countries, growth firms with a good dividend history (e.g., three years of consistently high dividend payouts) attain higher stock market valuation and raise more equity financing. We find similar empirical evidence in regard to accounting conservatism. In particular, firms with conservative accounting are more likely to acquire external financing in both equity and debt markets, especially when the firms have higher growth and operate in low investor protection countries. Our evidence further suggests a compliment relation between dividend and conservatism as commitment mechanisms in capital markets.

641411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
641411.value: Our study identifies two commitment mechanisms, i.e., dividend payouts and accounting conservatism, which firms use to establish a reputation for better treatment of outside shareholders in order to compensate for country-level weak protection of shareholders and to obtain better access to equity markets. Future research in the area might explore the regulatory impact of investor protection on dividend payouts and accounting conservatism. Adopting an exogenous policy-change setting enables the researchers to better understand the underlying social economic impact of regulations. Such empirical experiments thus provide insights at one side to the regulators for the evaluation of policies, and on the other side, to the investors on any necessary adjustment to their investment strategies following the political developments.

641411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
641411.value: The study empirically identifies two commitment mechanisms, i.e., dividend payouts and accounting conservatism, which firms use to establish a reputation for better treatment of outside shareholders in order to compensate for country-level weak protection of shareholders and to obtain better access to capital markets. Our paper makes important contribution to the law and finance literature. This literature generally presumes that firms are passive recipients of the influence of property rights on their external financing. What has been overlooked is the possibility that firms can mitigates the impact of weak legal protection by credibly committing to better governance and thus establishing a capital market reputation for decent treatment of shareholders. Such a commitment mechanism is important in our understanding of the dynamics of corporate finance under different legal regimes.

641611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
641611.value: The project examines the extent to which relationship finance substitutes for formal contracting in countries with weak legal protection. Creditor rights and contract enforceability affect a bank's monitoring incentives and its its ability to recontract in the event of a default. Thus it is not surprising that loan contracts adjust to variations in legal rights and contract enforceability. In countries with weak rights and poor contract enforceability, banks make smaller loans, offer shorter maturities, and charge higher interest rates. The question we ask is whether banking relationships overcome the contracting frictions that exist in countries with weak legal rights. Bank relationships involve repeated interactions between borrowers and lenders resulting in production of borrower-specific durable and reusable information. Consequently, the soft information that the bank accumulates over time gives it a comparative advantage over other lenders in providing its borrowers with better lending terms. If relationships substitute for formal contracting, then lending in countries with weak legal rights would be more relationship-based. By contrast, in countries with strong legal rights, we expect to observe more transactions-based lending. Our main test is to examine how relationship lending affects loan terms in countries that differ on creditor rights and contract enforceability. We predict that in countries with weak rights and poor enforcement, the effect of relationship lending on interest rates, loan maturity, and collateral requirements would be greater. In countries with strong rights and enforcement, the differences in loan terms offered by relationship banks and transactions-based banks would be relatively smaller. We also examine whether the presence of bank relationships affect the structure of loan syndicates and the willingness of foreign lenders to participate in such syndicates and if these effect vary across countries as a function of contracting environments. Since relationship banks have a strong incentive to monitor, we expect lead lender to hold a smaller fraction of the loan and the syndicate to be relatively more dispersed when it is led by a relationship bank. 該項目研究了在法律保護薄弱的國家中關係型融資對正式合同的替代程度。債權人的權利和合同的可執行性會影響銀行的監管激勵和對於違約事件重訂合同的能力。因此可以預見，貸款合同會根據法律權利和合同可執行性的不同而進行調整。在法律權利薄弱和合同可執行性差的國家，銀行會提供小額、短期且利率較高的貸款。 我們提出的問題是，借貸關係是否能克服在法律權利薄弱國家中的締約難度。借貸關係是指借款人及貸款人的重複交涉會導致借方特定、持久且可再利用的信息產生。因此，銀行隨時間而積累的軟信息，賦予了銀行（相對於其他貸款人來說）為其借款人提供更好的貸款條件的比較優勢。如果借貸關係替代了正式合同，則法律權利薄弱的國家中將存在更多的關係型貸款。相反，在法律權利較強的國家中將存在更多的交易型貸款。 我們主要考察的是，在有著不同債權人權利和合同可執行性的不同國家中，關係型貸款怎樣影響了貸款條件。我們預測，在法律權利薄弱和執法力低的國家中，關係型貸款對於貸款利率、貸款期限及抵押品要求的影響將更大；而在法律權利和執法力度較強的國家中，關係型銀行和交易型銀行提供的貸款條件的差異會相對較小。我們還研究是否借貸關係的存在會影響貸款財團的結構及外國貸款人加入這種財團的意願，以及這種影響是否取決於締約環境從而導致國際差異。由於關係型銀行具有很強的監管動機，我們預測貸款人將持有一小部分貸款，且當貸款財團被關係型銀行領導時會相對較為分散。

642011.label: Project Title(Chinese)
642011.value: 早期近代國家形成中的公共利益與制度發展：英國（1550-1688），日本（1700-1890），及中國（1700-1890）

642011.label: Project Objectives
642011.value: To demonstrate the importance of legitimating state power through providing social welfare and public works in the process of state formation To elucidate crucial parallels in state formation in early modern England, Japan, and China To delimit both the potential and the limits of a public-based yet non-democratic justification of state power as a rightful platform for the political particiption of a broader social actors
rows: To demonstrate the importance of legitimating state power through providing social welfare and public works in the process of state formation
To elucidate crucial parallels in state formation in early modern England, Japan, and China
To delimit both the potential and the limits of a public-based yet non-democratic justification of state power as a rightful platform for the political particiption of a broader social actors

642011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
642011.value: Studies of state formation have mainly focused upon how war-fighting leads to state-building. The process of legitimating and maintaining state power once established is under-studied, particularly the interplay between institutional development and efforts to justify state power in domestic governance. This neglect makes it very difficult to understand how the early modern state with highly decentralized fiscal institutions could effectively exert its political authority as the ultimate source of legitimate coercion in governing its territory. In this project, I propose to examine how the concept of “public interest” or “public good” was used to legitimate state power through improving social welfare in three well-established early modern states, England (1550-1688), Japan (1700-1890), and China (1700-1890). In each case, the state was not involved in prolonged and expensive international wars. All three cases had a central government which had undisputed political authority to coordinate the use of political power in localities. As each economy became increasingly commercialized, the state across the three cases adopted some surprisingly similar measures to justify state power. With increasing commercialization and consequent social dislocation and economic differentiation, surprisingly similar measures were adopted to justify state power. These included famine relief and plague prevention, maintaining public infrastructure such as river works, and poverty relief. These social policies were all justified by paternalist conceptions of state power, i.e., the state is obliged to provide welfare to its subjects as a benevolent father is to the household. In this comparative project, I will attempt to demonstrate that the three states tried to legitimate state power by providing concrete social welfare programs despite their different institutional arrangements, political traditions, and socio-economic circumstances. I will illustrate the importance of a normative basis accepted by both state and social actors to the operation of the early modern state. Upon this foundation the center, local officials, and social elites could cooperate in, negotiate, and even dispute the institutional means and ends of social policies. It provided a “rightful” channel for social actors to demand political participation, a phenomenon that we still see in the provision of public goods in contemporary non-democratic societies. 在社會科學領域關於國家形成的現有研究，大多強調戰爭對國家暴力機器建立所起的作用，而忽視了國家通過改善國內民生來維護其權力正當性的措施。這給我們如何理解和平時期國家制度的變化造成了相當的困擾。對國家形成的認識偏差，也使得我們難以理解財政高度分散的早期近代國家是如何保證其作為政治權力運作的最高權威。 本課題將考察公共利益這個概念如何體現在國家改善民生的各項政策的制定和實踐中，及其與維護國家權力正當性的密切聯繫。研究採用的方法為社會科學中的歷史比較分析，考察的三個案例為1550至1688年的英國，1700至1890年的日本，以及1700至1890年的中國。這三個案例的共同點在於政治上都已經具備了早期近代國家的形態，而且對外戰爭尚沒有成為維護國家權力正當性的壓倒性目標。而改善國內民生則成為國家向社會宣揚其權力正當性的重要手段，而市場經濟向社會生活滲透造成各種社會問題也對國家權力正當性的維護提出了新的挑戰。在這三個案例中，我們發現相似的很多政策手段，具體的措施包括賑荒救災、興修和維護水利和道路、提供和鼓勵慈善、甚至積極介入瘟疫的防護。 本課題企圖達到的目標有兩個。其一，通過比較研究三個案例中國家改善民生的社會政策的制定和實施中的利益衝突和矛盾如何得到解決的過程，來具體展現公共利益這一規範性概念在維護國家權力正當性中所起的關鍵作用。其二，重點考察公共利益這個規範性概念如何成為社會精英參與國家政策制定和實施的合法渠道，以及這一渠道對於增加社會政治參與的貢獻和局限性。

642011.label: Realisation of objectives
642011.value: I did most of my archival research in the Fu Sinian Library of the Institute of History and Philology at the Academia Sinica in Taipei. This library has purchased from the No. 1 Historical Archives in Beijing copies of all the microfilms of the Grand Council Memorial Copies. Due to excellent service and facilities in the Academia Sinica, it is far more efficient for me to do archival research in Taipei than in Beijing. In the Fu Sinian library, I went through the Grand Council Memorial Copies with respect to River Works during the reigns of Qianlong, Jiaqing, and Daoguang to collect materials on the Qing state’s advancement of expenditures for local water control projects. I also went through all the boxes of microfilms related to popular protests and petitions in the Grand Council Memorial Copies in the reign of Qianlong, Jiaqing and Daoguang. In the meantime, I went through the boxes on the management of domestic customs during the reign of Jiaqing and Daoguang. These archival materials are important for reexamining the supervision of the fiscal operation in the Qing dynasty. In the same time, I went through the microfilms of the Grand Council Memorial Copies on legal matters in the reigns of Qianlong, Jiaqing, and Daoguang. The materials that I have collected included cases of popular protests and cases of cross-regional conflicts in using water. I also made a research trip to the No.1 Historical Archives in Beijing to collect cases of cross-regional conflicts in using water in the Palace Memorials. In the library the Institute of Modern History, Academia Sinica in Taipei, I examined the Palace Memorials during the reign of Jiaqing and Daoguang to collect the memorials related to the management of state granary system (particularly the inter-province transfer of the stored grains for famine relief); popular petitions and collective actions related to the conflicts of using water or tax collection; management of government finance at the county level (particularly the local deficit and post-transfer bookkeeping audit. In my two research trips to Tokyo, where I was affiliated with the Waseda University and the University of Tokyo, I mostly collected materials from the huge secondary literature in Japanese on popular protests, famine relief, and river works in Tokugawa Japan. These materials would be used mainly for the purpose of comparing with similar phenomena in Qing China in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.

642011.value: In addition to revising my working papers for submitting to peer-reviewed journals, I will begin to work on a book manuscript to compare the role of the early modern state in England, Japan, and China. 642011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
642011.value: The state is not just a violent machine of fighting wars. The early modern state has played a vital role in improving the general welfare and public infrastructure, adjudicating conflicts of interests among different regions as the highest political authority, and to address the grievances made by the common people even in the form of collective petitions. The general characters of the early modern state is demonstrated in England (1550-1750), Japan (1700-1868), and China (1700-1850), three countries with different political cultures, institutions, and socio-economies. This research therefore highlights the normative aspects of the early state to legitimate its coercive power through social policies, an important continuity with the modern state.

642211.label: Project Title(Chinese)
642211.value: 创新，产品安全，和法律责任

642211.label: Project Objectives
642211.value: To systematically analyze how product liability affects a firm’s incentives for new product innovation and safety design: Such analysis will lead to predictions that are different from the literature, which mainly focuses on safety investment or costs of innovation. To examine how potential competition impacts the effects of liability on a firm’s safety choice and/or investment incentives. To provide policy implications on product liability, in particular, whether full product liability or partial liability would lead to higher social welfare.
rows: To systematically analyze how product liability affects a firm’s incentives for new product innovation and safety design: Such analysis will lead to predictions that are different from the literature, which mainly focuses on safety investment or costs of innovation.
To examine how potential competition impacts the effects of liability on a firm’s safety choice and/or investment incentives.
To provide policy implications on product liability, in particular, whether full product liability or partial liability would lead to higher social welfare.

642211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
642211.value: If the use of a firm's product results in consumer harm due to poor product safety, what should the firm's liability be? There have been substantial interests in product liability in economics. Most of the existing studies focus on how liability rules can have important impacts on firm incentives for safety investments and/or sales. This proposed research intends to examine how liability rules affect a firm’s incentives in developing new products, given interaction between innovation and safety design. The results will lead to essential welfare and policy implications. In addition, this project will address how competition from potential entrants affects the interaction between innovation and safety design. This project will include two parts. The first part will focus on a firm’s incentives for innovation and safety improvement, without potential entrants. The firm takes costly and multi-period search for a new product. In each period, the random search outcome includes two dimensions: innovation level and safety level. A more novel innovation provides higher expected functional value to consumers but is more likely associated with lower safety. The firm decides when to stop searching and sell a product. Heterogeneous consumers may differ in functional values and potential damages. If a consumer is harmed, the firm bears liability which may or may not fully compensate consumer damage. The firm’s search decision does not fully internalize consumers’ benefits. Increasing product liability may have two effects on the firm’s innovation incentive. On one hand, higher liability motivates the firm to increase safety, which may lead the firm often to stop with a less novel innovation. On the other hand, given the safety level, higher liability reduces consumers’ heterogeneity or leads to more sales, which can result in larger profit increase for more novel innovations. Thus, the firm’s innovation incentive may not be monotone in product liability. This project will predict what liability level is socially optimal. The second part will consider how potential entry influences the existing firm’s incentives for innovation and safety improvement, given product liability. Each period the entrant may arrive with a certain probability. The entrant's product may or may not be the same as the existing firm's. Such competition may motivate the existing firm to launch the new product more quickly, but also distorts the effect of increased liability on the firm’s potential profits. This project will examine whether the socially optimal liability should be increased or decreased given competition. 如果消费者因为使用低质量的产品而受到伤害，企业应当承担什么程度的法律责任？经济学研究对于法律责任问题有很大兴趣。大多数的相关研究主要关注法律责任如何影响企业产品安全投资以及产品销售。由于产品安全投资和新产品创新息息相关，本研究项目试图探讨法律责任如何同时影响企业产品安全投资以及新产品开发的意愿。未来的研究成果将产生关于社会福利以及政策方面的建议。另外，本研究项目也将说明来自潜在市场进入者的竞争如何与法律责任互动，从而影响产品安全投资以及新产品开发。 本项目将包括两个主要部分。第一部分研究在没有潜在市场进入者的竞争时，现有企业对产品安全投资和新产品开发的意愿。企业可以进行多期的产品开发。每一时期的产品开发包括了创新和安全程度。创新高的产品会为消费者带来更多的效用，但有可能有更多的产品安全问题。企业可以决定何时停止继续开发而销售现有研发产品。市场上，各个消费者的产品效用以及安全问题可能带来的伤害有可能互不相同。当消费者受到伤害时，根据法律规定的不同，企业有可能承担全部或部分的责任。因此企业产品开发的决策并没有充分考虑消费者的利益。提高企业的法律责任有可能带来两方面影响：一方面，提高法律责任使企业关注加强产品安全，而这可能导致企业采纳创新低的产品。另一方面，给定产品安全程度，提高法律责任将带来更多的销售，从而为创新高的产品带来更多利润。因此，提高法律责任有可能提高或降低企业产品开发与安全投资的意愿。本项目将分析什么程度的法律责任对社会福利更有利。 项目的第二部分研究，在考虑法律责任的因素后，来自潜在市场进入者的竞争如何影响现有企业产品开发和提高产品安全。每一时期市场有可能有新进入者。市场新进入者的产品有可能与现有企业的产品不同。这一潜在竞争促使现有企业更早的推广新产品，而这同时会改变产品安全以及法律责任对企业利润的影响。本项目将分析当竞争程度改变时，从社会福利角度出发，应当如何调整与产品安全相关的法律责任。

642211.label: Realisation of objectives
642211.value: All the objectives of the project have been realized and the results have been included in a research paper. In particular, (1) The first objective: We first reviewed more details about the relevant literature. Then we collected some stylized examples about firms’ behavior in product innovation and safety design, especially under oligopoly markets. Based on deeper understanding about the literature and the stylized examples, we have written a theoretical spatial model to analyze firms’ incentives in making innovation and safety investments when facing heterogeneous consumers. Different form most studies in the literature, our model involves firms’ dynamic incentives in a two-period framework. The model and the analysis have been revised several times after we got comments from colleagues and workshop attendants. The final analysis has successfully captured firms’ concerns about market reputation and liability costs when introducing new products and making safety investments. (2) The second objective: Extensive studies in the literature have examined firms’ incentives in safety investments and derived optimal liability rules under a given market structure. However, there has been little formal analysis of how competition (or changes of market structure) and liability rules may interact to affect firms’ investment incentives. In this project, we analyzed the relationship between competition and product liability. We find that competition and product liability are often complements. In particular, a firm’s reputation concern becomes less under the oligopoly market than under the monopoly market, and with multiple competitors, more intense competition due to less product differentiation can reduce firms’ incentive to invest in safety, leading to the need for higher product liability. More interestingly, when the number of competitors increases, the impact of product liability on firms’ investment incentives may vary non-monotonically. These results are different from predictions from the literature on law and economics. (3) The third objective: Consistent with the literature, we have shown in our model that the socially optimal liability can be partial liability, given firms’ reputation concerns. But different from the literature, we have compared the socially optimal liability under different market structures. The socially optimal liability under the oligopoly market is larger than that under the monopoly market. When the number of competitors increases in the oligopoly market, the socially optimal liability first decreases and then increases. These findings can provide rich policy implications, especially about the relationship between liability rules and deregulations which allow more firms to enter the market.

642211.label: Major findings and research outcome
642211.value: Stylized examples and formal empirical studies in the literature provide mixed evidence on the effects of competition and liability on firms’ investment incentives for product quality. Based on those observations, we created a two-period spatial model to analyze firms’ incentives in making innovation and safety investments when facing heterogeneous consumers. It is a generalization of the Hotelling model with non-localized competition. In the model, consumers cannot observe firms’ product safety. However, consumers in the second period can observe the damage levels in the earlier period and update their belief about product quality. Using the theoretical approach, we analyzed the relationship between competition and product liability, in increasing firms’ investment incentives and social welfare. The optimal liability rules are characterized under different market structures. It is shown that product liability and competition can often be complements. In the monopoly market, the optimal liability rule is often partial liability. If reputation loss from selling a low-quality product is not sufficient, then product liability should be increased to sustain the firm’s investment incentive. In the oligopoly market, however, the reputation loss is significantly smaller than that under monopoly. Therefore, the socially optimal product liability under oligopoly is higher than that under monopoly. Furthermore, the optimal liability under oligopoly may vary non-monotonically with the number of competitors. If a firm deviates to sell a low-quality product, the firm’s net cost saving in period 1 is the sum of fixed and variable production costs, minus the extra liability cost, but it suffers from the reputation loss in period 2. An increase in the number of competitors always reduces the reputation loss, but it has a non-monotonic impact on the net cost saving from deviation. As a result, the optimal liability may vary non-monotonically with the number of competitors, possibly first decreasing and then increasing. It is also shown that, given the number of competitors, if there is less horizontal product differentiation (i.e., less consumer heterogeneity), the reputation loss from offering a low quality product becomes smaller. Correspondingly, the socially optimal liability is larger when competition becomes tougher with less horizontal product differentiation. Our finding that competition and product liability can be complements is robust when firms’ products have positively correlated quality levels. All the above results have been included in the paper “Competition, Product Safety, and Product Liability” (See Part C). We are preparing to submit the paper to some good academic journal soon.

642211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
642211.value: All the current results have been included in the attached paper. We are preparing to submit the paper to some good academic journal. In addition, there are several potential directions for future research. The symmetric setting in this project allows us to abstract away from information issues. It would be desirable to explore how private information affects the interaction between competition and product liability. More generally, this project investigates the design of product liability when there are both horizontal product differentiation and vertical product differentiation, though vertical differentiation only happens in the off-equilibrium path. More future studies on product liability with both dimensions of differentiation would be meaningful. We are trying to develop models for some of these potential research topics.

642211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
642211.value: Firms can make investments to increase product safety and avoid consumer harm. Both market competition and product liability can impact firms’ investments in product quality. There have been policy debates on whether liability should be higher or lower when competition is tougher. By focusing on the interaction between competition and product liability in motivating firms’ safety investment and social benefit, this project provides valuable and significant policy implications. First, compared to the market with only one firm, the existence of competitors can make firms care less about future reputation, which would reduce firms’ incentives to invest in product safety. Therefore, product liability should be higher when competition exists. Similarly, given the number of firms in a market, if the firms are selling less differentiated products, product liability should be set higher. Second, in a competitive market, an increase in the number of firms not only affects each firm’s concern about future reputation, but also impacts the short-term production and liability costs. This project has shown that, with an increase in the number of firms in a competitive market, it is socially beneficial to first decrease product liability and then increase product liability when the number of firms is large enough.

642411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
642411.value: This project proposes a theoretical analysis of managed security services (MSS), which is increasingly popular because of its economic benefits (Allen et al. 2003). An MSS involves a client organization outsourcing information security functions to an external service vendor. Since the vendor and client often cannot observe each other's efforts in MSS, asymmetric information is prevalent in this setting. We will develop a new theory that endogenizes both the vendor's and client's security protection efforts in MSS under asymmetric information. In particular, departing from the extant literature which variously focuses on either the vendor's or client's incentives to protect information security, we will assume that MSS quality is jointly determined by their efforts. Hence, in our setting, not only can the vendor under-supply security protection, the client can also free-ride on the MSS vendor too. We shall derive the equilibrium behaviors of an MSS vendor and client under different information structures (the client can fully verify the vendor's effort, the client cannot verify, but assumes various degree of honesty of the vendor, etc.). Based on these equilibrium behaviors, we will examine whether policy instruments, such as the recognition of vendor liability in service-level agreements (SLA), or use of insurance, could help achieve better social outcomes. We shall seek to collect data on actual implementations of MSS and draw anecdotal/empirical evidence on the predictive validity of the theory developed in this research. The key contributions of this project are as follows. First, we will develop an integrated theory that incorporates joint service development by an MSS vendor and client under asymmetric information. Such an overarching theory allows us to gain a thorough understanding on the key factors that shape MSS quality. Second, based on our theoretical framework, we will critically evaluate the social implications of service attributes such as vendor liability (i.e., the compensation payable to the client when security breaches occur) or insurance. Third, we will draw practical insights for all relevant parties - MSS vendor, client, and regulators such as the government or relevant industry organizations. These insights will also be helpful for broader industries, e.g., the general service sector, that exhibit value co-creation between vendors and customers who independently decide the amount of effort to contribute to the service (Rust and Chung 2006). 此項目將進行對資訊系統保安服務（MSS）的理論分析。MSS乏指客戶組織把資訊系統保安外包給外部服務供應商。由於服務供應商和客戶往往不能觀察對方的努力，資訊不對稱普遍存在。我們將制定一套新的理論，在資訊不對稱的情況下，同時內部化買賣雙方對資訊系統保安質素的付出。現存文獻大部份側重於服務供應商或客戶單一對維護資訊系統保安付出的努力。我們將偏離這些文獻，並假設MSS質量是共同決定的努力。因此，在我們的研究中，不僅服務供應商可以逃避付出努力，客戶亦可以逃避自己應付出的努力。 我們將研究MSS供應商和客戶在不同資訊結構下的平衡點，並根據這些平衡點研究政策工具如何可以幫助實現更好的社會效果。 這個項目的主要貢獻如下：首先，我們將開發一個綜合理論，在資訊不對稱的情況下了解MSS服務供應商和客戶端付出的努力。這一個總體理論可以使我們對MSS獲得更徹底的理解。其次，根據我們的理論框架，我們將嚴格評估服務屬性對社會的影響，如供應商的責任條款或保險。第三，我們將以此為有關各方－MSS供應商，客戶和監管機構－提出實用的意見。

642411.label: Realisation of objectives
642411.value: All stated objectives are achieved. The PI and Co-I have conducted extensive analysis to study how contract structure would affect social efficiency when both the managed security service provider (MSSP) and clients are responsible for enhancing the quality of the security systems, and when the clients are subject to system interdependency risks. Our analysis gives rise to several sets of propositions that could inform information security outsourcing practices, particularly on how to design socially-efficient contracts that variously allocate the liability to the MSSP and clients. Our analysis also highlights the differences in social outcomes when the MSSP/clients can verify/not verify the other party's security protection efforts. Finally, we have conducted a survey of real information security outsourcing contracts and examined if our findings and propositions are consistent with industry practices.
