643811.label: Major findings and research outcome
643811.value: 1) When agents face both state uncertainty and parameter uncertainty, to keep the model tractable, it is useful to have agents perform a test each period to decide when to learn about the parameter. 2) Incorporating both state uncertainty and parameter uncertainty in asset pricing is crucial for a learning model with reasonable parameter values to match the moments of data returns. 3) It makes a significant difference in asset prices whether or not agents take into account their future belief updating when they price assets. If they ignore the belief updating, the model overstates the volatility of risky asset returns. 4) Learning is useful in explaining why we observe in the data that price dividend ratio can predict future returns but not future dividend growth. The research outcome is a working paper titled "Learning, Rare Disasters, and Asset Prices".

643811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
643811.value: We could potentially use the methodology in learning and asset pricing developed in this project to study how learning about disaster risk works in a production economy. To do so, we first need to estimate the U.S. TFP data using a Markov regime switch model to determine which data generating process is appropriate for the exogenous process. Depending on the data generating process, we need to decide how to model the disaster risk and in turn agents' learning.

643811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
643811.value: We incorporate rational learning into a consumption-based asset pricing model with rare disasters. Agents are uncertain if a negative shock signals the onset of a disaster or how much long-term damage the disaster will cause but they are learning. The rational learning mechanism endogenously generates time-varying uncertainty about future consumption and, in turn, time-varying equity returns. Our model thus accounts for the level and volatility of U.S. equity returns without relying on exogenous variation in disaster risk. Moreover, in the context of our model, we show that adaptive learning implies significantly more volatile equity returns than rational learning does. Our model provides an explanation for why economic uncertainty is time-varying. This project also develops a method for pricing both state uncertainty and parameter uncertainty, which could be used in other settings than our current model. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the asset price implications can be very different whether or not agents take into account their future belief-updating in pricing assets. It contributes to the debate in the learning literature on adaptive learning v.s. rational learning.

644011.label: Project Objectives
644011.value: Show that mutual funds tilt their portfolios towards stock styles currently in favor with their investors. If they do, then individual investors using sophisticated fund managers to invest their capital will not imply that their beliefs will cease to affect asset markets. Examine whether catering by mutual fund managers hurts portfolio performance. In other words, find out whether funds that do not cater offer better returns. Investigate whether catering to investor demand allow funds to extract rents from their investors by charging excess fees and/or loads. Show that fund management companies start new funds in styles that are currently in demand. Examine whether these funds subsequently underperform.

644011.label: Realisation of objectives
644011.value: We find evidence that mutual funds tilt their portfolios towards stock styles currently in favor with their investors. We also find that funds that tilt performance towards style recently in favor with investors underperform. We do not find any robust evidence confirming that funds that cater charge higher fees. Finally, we find that more funds seem to be started in styles that have recently been in favor, but these funds do not seem to especially underperform their peers.

644011.label: Major findings and research outcome
644011.value: In this paper we first examine whether mutual funds tilt their portfolios towards stock styles currently in favor with their investors. We use data from CRSP mutual fund holdings database, and construct measures of fund betas on 2 style types -- large vs. small stocks, and value vs. growth stocks. Next, we regress rolling fund betas on the total flows into funds following that style in the last 6 months, and find that the coefficients remain positive after controlling for various fund characteristics. This means that when more money is allocated to funds with small stocks, then the average mutual fund does indeed tilt its holdings towards small stocks. We next sort funds into quintiles based on the coefficient from the previous regression. Funds with high coefficients are those that have shown a greater propensity to cater to style preferences. We examine returns to a portfolio that buys the bottom quintile (least propensity to cater) and shorts the top quintile (most propensity to cater). The 4-factor alpha on this portfolio is 32 bps per month for size-tilt, and 34 bps for value tilt, significant at the 10% level.This shows that funds that tilt performance towards style recently in favor with investors under-perform. We do not find any robust evidence confirming that funds that cater obtain significantly higher flows in the future or charge higher fees. However, the fact that funds that cater the most do not get lower flows or fees -- in spite of their worse performance -- is noteworthy. This is consistent with the view that fund managers who are not particularly skilled avoid being penalized by investors when they cater to time-varying style preferences. Finally, we find that more funds seem to be started in styles that have recently been in favor, but these funds do not seem to especially underperform their peers.

644011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
644011.value: Some of our empirical analysis still needs to be refined further. The issue with a lot of our results is that they are not very robust across different specifications of the way in which tilt or abnormal flows are measured. This needs to be addressed more carefully. At this point, we are revising the draft paper containing our results. The PI has been to a few top conferences, where he has had the opportunity to talk about these results to experts on the subject. We are incorporating some of this feedback into our analysis now. One of the most prominent and common point that these experts have raised is that our analysis could benefit from a theoretical model. The model can generate sharper predictions, which can be tested by modifying our current tests. Also, while working on this project, we came across a pattern in the data which we are exploring in further detail in related, ongoing research. This pattern involves how investors seem to be allocating flows not only on the basis of performance of the fund they are invested in, but also performance of other funds the same manager manages.

644011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
644011.value: In this project, we find evidence that mutual funds tilt their portfolios towards stock styles currently in favor with their investors. We also find that funds that tilt performance towards style recently in favor with investors under-perform. We do not find any robust evidence confirming that funds that cater charge higher fees or get higher investor inflows. However, the fact that funds that cater the most do not get lower flows or fees -- in spite of their worse performance -- is noteworthy. Our results are consistent with the view that mutual fund managers who are not particularly skilled avoid being penalized by investors when they cater to time-varying style preferences.

644311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
644311.value: How likely is it that a severe economic disaster will occur in the next 100 years? With a relatively short sample of historical data, it is difficult to accurately estimate the likelihood of disasters or the size of their impact. This suggests that there is likely to be significant heterogeneity in the beliefs of market participants about disasters. Chen, Joslin and Tran (2010) model that due to the highly nonlinear relationship between consumption losses in a disaster and the risk premium, such disagreement can generate strong risk sharing motives among investors and significantly affect asset prices. In specific their theory work suggests that when there is a lot of disagreement among market participants about the risk of disasters: (1) there will be a lot of trading on disaster insurance; (2) the risk sharing will keep the risk premium at low levels conditional on that equity premium derives mostly form disaster risk. The objective of the this project is to empirically test above theory with out of money (OTM) puts as proxies for disaster/crash insurance. In specific, the prediction is that in the periods when there is a lot of trading for the OTM puts, there are likely to be large disagreement among investors about crash risk. In this case, the market risk premium should be low, so will the future returns. On the other hand, if there is little trading, there could be two possibilities: either there is little concern about crash risk (low risk premium), or everyone is concerned about crash risk and not willing to provide insurance (high risk premium). In another words, there’s an inverse U-shaped relationship between risk premium (future returns) and risk sharing. 未来100年发生严重经济灾难的可能性有多大？由于没有足够长的历史数据支持，准确估测这种灾难发生的概率及其影响程度是很困难的。这就导致了市场不同参与者对经济灾难存在显著的认识差异性。Chen，Joslin and Tran（2010）研究认为这种认识差异性会在投资者之中产生强烈的风险分担动机，并显著影响资产价格。进一步说，他们的研究认为，当市场参与者对灾难风险存在大量分歧时，将会出现：（1）灾难保险大量进行交易；（2）风险分担将促使风险收益维持在较低水平。 本课题研究目标是，将“价外（OTM）卖空期权”作为灾难/崩盘保险的代表，对上述理论进行实证测试。进一步说，要实证的预测结果是，如果市场上出现OTM卖空期权大量交易时，那么就说明投资者对崩盘风险可能存在很大分歧。在这种情况下，市场风险收益应该较低，未来收益也应该较低。相反地，如果OTM卖空期权很少交易，就有两种可能：一种可能是很少有人担心崩盘风险（低风险收益）；第二种可能是每个人在担心崩盘风险，没有意愿提供崩盘保险（高风险收益）。换句话说，风险收益（未来收益）与风险分担之间存在U型关系。

644311.label: Major findings and research outcome
644311.value: We propose a new measure for the variations in intermediary constraints by observing how financial intermediaries manage their tail risk exposures. Using a unique dataset on the trading activities in the market for deep out-of-the money S&P 500 put options, we identify periods when shocks to intermediary constraints are likely to be the main driver of the variation in the net amount of trading between public investors and financial intermediaries, which enables us to infer variations in intermediary constraints from the quantities of trading. Besides its effects on option pricing, our measure of intermediary constraint shocks is a strong predictor of future returns for a wide range of financial assets, and it is connected to existing funding constraint measures based on changes in broker-dealer leverage.

644511.label: Project Objectives
644511.value: To assess the value of a multi-directional communication channel such as a conference call as compared with a one-directional one such as a press release in providing market participants with an opportunity to search for new information in periods of high uncertainty. To document empirical evidence of horizontal information transmission, where the information in question is consistent with multi-dimensional interpretation proposed by Milgrom and Roberts (1986), among others. 644511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
644511.value: In the proposed study, we will explicate the benefits of multi-directional communication channels in addressing the problem of acquiring and aggregating complex (i.e., in general, multi-dimensional) information. An example of such a setting is a situation where decision makers are not aware of all relevant dimensions of the problem; we hypothesize that this is the case during periods characterized by high uncertainty. We will use conference calls and press releases as two contrasting settings, where the former allows for information to be transmitted in multiple directions (i.e., among the analysts and from the analysts to the managers) whereas the latter allows for information to be transmitted in one direction only. We argue that the former setting is more conducive to information aggregation and acquisition in periods of high uncertainty, where the decision makers have to find the relevant dimensions of the problem, as contrasted with the periods of low uncertainty, during which the relevant dimensions are usually known. The contribution of the proposed research is that we will use the theoretical framework developed in economics to study an important facet of the problem of information aggregation that has been largely overlooked by the accounting and finance literatures. 本研究旨在解釋多向的溝通管道在取得及彙集複雜多元資訊時帶來的好處。我們以業績說明會(conference call)與新聞稿發佈(press releases)做對比。前者容許資訊於多方之間傳遞（例如資訊可於分析師之間流通或從分析師流向經理人），而後者之資訊僅為單一流向。我們主張在高不確定性的時期，前者是較有用的取得及彙集資訊的方法，並研究此種管道對市場參與者（包含分析師）及經理人的價值。

644611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
644611.value: The goal of the proposed research is to better understand transitory price movements in asset markets at weekly, monthly, and annual frequencies. The term "transitory price movement" refers to a period of time when a given asset’s observed price is not equal its estimated "efficient value". Understanding such price movements is important for economic agents who are making allocation decisions and/or writing contingent contracts. Understanding these movements is important for academics who are carrying out asset pricing tests. The PI’s approach will combine theoretical models with rigorous empirical tests. In modern (traditional) asset pricing, markets are frictionless and there is little opportunity for prices to deviate from their efficient values. Therefore, the theory section of this proposal will specifically model frictions in asset markets. The PI will initially focus on limited risk bearing capacity and short-sale constraints. Empirical testing will use state-space (statistical) models and stock market trading data. The state-space approach assumes an observed stock price can be decomposed into two unobserved components. The first component is the stock's efficient price; the second is the transitory price. Trading imbalances (buys minus sells) from different investor groups are allowed to influence the efficient price estimation (informed trading) and/or the transitory price estimation. This grant proposal covers two (2) related projects, each of which should result in a separate, stand-alone paper, that can be submitted to a top finance or economics journal: Paper #1: Transitory Price Movements and Relative Prices: The Case of PRC- and HK-listed Stocks Paper #2: Transitory Price Movements of USA and Asian Stocks The first project will focus on a special type of dual-class shares issued by Chinese (PRC) firms and listed on both the Shanghai and Hong Kong Stock Exchanges. For a given firm, the efficient price is the same for both share classes. Thus, deviations in the shares’ relative prices represent transitory price movements. The second project focuses more generally on USA and Asian stocks including ADRs and baskets of stocks from the same industry. The PI will use baskets of stocks to estimate common movements of efficient prices. Again, deviations in stocks' relative prices represent transitory price movements. Output from the state space estimation will tell financial economists whether individuals’ or institutions’ trades are linked with movements of the efficient and/or transitory prices. The output will also help quantify the magnitude of the transitory price movements, thus providing “signal-to-noise” measures of stock price variance. 这项研究提案的目的是为了更好地了解资本市场上，以周，月，年为周期的短期价格波动。“短期价格波动”是指在某一时期，某一资产的市场观察价格偏离于其有效价格。研究短期价格波动对于经济中的资源配置和或有合同的制定十分重要。另一方面，短期价格波动对于学术界资产定价模型的检验也具有重要的意义。 PI 的研究方法将综合理论模型和严格的实证检验。在经典资产定价模型中，市场是没有摩擦的，价格也很难偏离有效价格。因此，提案的理论部分将具体对资产市场上的摩擦建立模型。PI将首先重点研究有限风险承受能力和卖空限制这两种市场摩擦。 实证检验部分将使用状态空间（统计）模型和股票市场交易数据。状态空间方法假定观测到的股票价格由两部分组成。一部分是股票的有效价格；另一部分是短期价格。在模型中，不同的投资者群体的交易外盘内盘差（买方发起的交易量减去卖方发起的交易量）可以影响有效价格的估计（知情交易）及/或短期价格的估计。 这项提案将包括两个相关的项目，分别可以产生两篇独立的可以提交顶级金融，经济学杂志的论文。 论文1： 短期价格波动和相对价格：中国大陆，香港两地上市股票 论文2： 美国和亚洲股票的短期价格波动 第一个项目将集中于一类特殊的股票。这种股票由中国公司发行，同时在上海和香港股票交易所两地上市交易。对于同一家公司，两地的股份的有效价格是相同的。因此，两种股份相对价格的变动可以代表短期价格的波动。 第二个项目重点研究更一般的美国和亚洲股票，包括ADR和一篮子同行业的股票。PI将用一篮子股票去估计有效价格的共同变动。同样的，股票相对价格的变化可以代表短期价格的波动。 状态空间模型的结果会告诉金融经济学家个人或者机构投资者的交易是否和有效价格/短期价格有关。结果还可以帮助度量短期价格波动的大小，以此来衡量股票价格中的信噪比。

644611.label: Major findings and research outcome
644611.value: We study difference between dual-listed share prices (mainland China vs. Hong Kong). When China has a short-sale ban, Chinese stock prices are 1.8x as high as Hong Kong prices (on average). We show that stock pairs with higher fundamental volatilities or more volatile order flows have higher price disparities (on average). The average stock pair's return difference is volatile and has a standard deviation of 8.8% per week. Our paper shows that order flows can affect both a company's fundamental price and/or its transitory prices. We further show that, in Hong Kong, transitory variance accounts for 39% of a stock's total variance. Such results are surprising because the average market capitalization is over USD 8 billion for the Hong Kong-listed shares and the turnover is over 2.5 per annum. Finally, we exploit a quasi-natural experiment in which the short-sale ban is lifted for some Chinese stocks but not others. After the ban is lifted, the affected shares trade at parity. We estimate that lifting the short-sale ban in China (mainland) reduces weekly transitory volatility in Hong Kong by 49 bp per week because it enables a hedging mechanism.

644611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
644611.value: There are numerous avenues for future development. Our research has implications for: 1) How regulators think about short-sale bans. 2) How volatility in an emerging market can affect prices in developed markets (cross market linkages). 3) The amount of information contained (or not contained) in stock prices. 4) The ability of trading to cause temporary distortions in prices.

644611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
644611.value: Using dual-listed shares from China and Hong Kong, our research is about to quantify exactly how trading affects prices. We look at days when a given share-pair has lots of trading in one market, but not in another. If prices move together, we can conclude that information, and not trading is moving prices. However, if relative prices move, we can estimate the marginal effect of trading imbalances on prices.

644711.label: Project Objectives
644711.value: Study the effects of forced and voluntary equity exposures of CEOs on future firm performance leading to an academic paper publishable in a top-tier finance journal Contribute to the literature on insider trading, effect of incentives on firm performance, and executive compensation.
rows: Study the effects of forced and voluntary equity exposures of CEOs on future firm performance leading to an academic paper publishable in a top-tier finance journal
Contribute to the literature on insider trading, effect of incentives on firm performance, and executive compensation.

644711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
644711.value: Equity exposure of top executives has increased substantially over the last two decades. This is partially due to grants of restricted stocks and options to top executives and target ownership requirements. In addition, executives often choose to hold their company’s stock voluntarily. Fahlenbrach and Stulz (2010) find that during 2006-07 many US bank CEOs voluntarily held substantial quantities of their company stock in addition to the large forced exposures through restricted stocks, options and target ownership requirements. This motivates our main question: Is there information in the CEO’s forced and voluntary equity exposure about future stock price performance and CEO’s risk taking behavior? Our study relates to a large literature that examines whether purchases and sales by top executives forecast future stock returns (e.g. Seyhun (1986, 1998), Lakonishok and Lee (2001)). While purchases and sales might be related to short term view of the CEO about stock performance, medium to long term views are also likely to be reflected in her level of equity holdings. A CEO who consistently believes that the stock would outperform might hold a large quantity of it in her portfolio, but might not purchase repeatedly. Further, a CEO whose view of the stock changes from very positive to a little less positive would sell some of the stock in her portfolio in response. However, this sale would not mean that the CEO thinks that the stock is going to underperform in the future. Therefore, high total equity holdings might forecast positive stock returns, especially when a large portion of that is voluntarily held. Our preliminary results suggest that the total equity exposure of the CEO is positively related to future stock returns. Further, this relation is stronger when a larger fraction of the equity exposure is voluntarily held. We propose to understand in greater detail the nature of information in level of holdings, and whether ability to predict returns is higher in firms where the insiders are likely to be relatively more informed than outsiders. We also propose to examine the effect of forced equity exposure on risk taking incentives, which in turn might affect future stock price performance. Our study would contribute to the literature on insider trading and effect of compensation on firm performance. The study would be of interest to shareholders of firms, market participants looking for profitable trading strategies and corporate boards interested in providing optimal incentives though appropriate compensation structures. 在過去的二十年中，高層管理人員的股權持有大幅增加。這部分是由於公司授予高管以交易受限的股票和期權，以及對於高管的持股所設定的一些目標。此外，管理人員往往會自願選擇持有公司的股票。Fahlenbrach和Stulz（2010）發現，在2006-07期間，除了被強制地持有交易受限的股票和期權以及達到高管所有權的目標之外，許多美國銀行的首席執行官自願持有了大量的他們公司的股票。這樣一個現象就使我們提出一個問題：在首席執行官強制的和自願的持有公司股票的資訊中是否包含關於未來股票價格的資訊以及有關首席執行官可能採取風險的行為的資訊？我們的研究與一大塊文獻有關，這些文獻考察高管的採購和銷售是否能預測未來的股票收益率（比如：Seyhun（1986，1998），Lakonishok和Lee（2001年））。雖然採購和銷售很可能與首席執行官的對於短期內的判斷有關，他們對於中期和長期的觀點也會反映在他們持有的股權上。一個首席執行官如果認為它們公司的股市會跑贏大盤的話，她可能會在她的投資組合中持有大量她們公司的股票，但可能不會多次購買。而一個首席執行官的觀點如果從非常積極變為不那麼積極時可能會從她的投資組合中賣出一些公司的股票。然而，這種出售並不意味著首席執行官認為她公司的股票的表現會比大盤差。所以，高管持有大量的股權可能預示著正的股票收益率，尤其是當大部份的股票是自願持有的時候。我們的初步結果發現，首席執行官持有的股票總股本與未來股票的收益率是正相關的。此外，當大部分的股票是自願持有的時候，這種正相關的關係更強。 我們建議更加仔細地考察高管控股中所包含的資訊，以及考察是否在那些內部人比外部的資訊更多的公司中，高管控股預測未來收益的能力更高。我們也建議考察強制持有股權對於高管採取有風險的行為的影響，而後者可能反過來會影響未來股價的表現。我們的研究將增加對於有關內部人交易以及高管補償對於企業績效影響的瞭解。可能會對此項研究感興趣的包括公司的股東，尋找盈利的交易策略的市場參與者，以及致力於通過適當的補償結構提供最優激勵的公司的董事會。

645111.label: Project Title(Chinese)
645111.value: 隨機共變異數之混合模型及其金融應用

645111.label: Project Objectives
645111.value: To develop a mixture stochastic covariance model for modeling time-varying covariance of financial returns and for forecasting realized covariance of high-frequency data. To study the time-series properties of the hidden states. This will help us understand how the dynamic structure of financial markets changes with economic variables. To develop statistical methods for determining the optimal number of hidden states in the mixture. To evaluate the proposed mixture stochastic covariance model using statistical and economic criteria. The ability of the proposed mixture model to forecast realized covariance will be evaluated. In addition, the performance in forecasting value at risk and the expected shortfall, in forming optimal portfolios based on high-frequency data and in determining minimum variance tracking portfolios will be considered. To study time-varying mixing probabilities which allow us to understand the driving factors for financial market returns to switch from one state to another.

645111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
645111.value: To quantify portfolio risk and to assess the risk exposure of financial institutions, measures of interdependence between financial assets and different investment vehicles is indispensable. Covariance, being a statistical device to capture both the market volatility and correlation among assets, is evidently time-varying as both volatility and correlation vary according to changes in the market environment and the risk appetite of investors. Therefore, it is mandatory for business analysts and market practitioners to derive a reliable way to model covariance. Because of the existence of structural changes in economic anticipation and monetary policies, market response to unexpected events, like catastrophic events or collapse of big companies and risk management regulatory reforms, the dynamic structure of covariance naturally follows a multiple-state process. This research will develop a new mixture stochastic covariance model to allow the covariance to have more than one state. We will investigate hidden factors, which govern the switching among states. With the understanding of the hidden factors, we can study how economic events, policy changes and financial news affect the volatility movement and the interdependence of different financial markets. We will also investigate the effectiveness of the proposed mixture stochastic covariance model on various financial applications like constructing risk measures and obtaining optimal portfolios. Findings from this project will provide useful resources and insights on the relationship among different financial systems, asset allocation and risk management, etc. 為了量化投資組合的風險及評估金融機構所承受風險的程度，量度金融資產和不同投資工具之間的相互關係措施是不可缺少的。統計學的共變異數是一種可捕捉市場波動及資產間相關性的方法。它明顯是隨時間變化的，因為波動性和相關性都會隨著市場環境及投資者風險愛好的變化而改變。因此，企業分析員及市場人士必需制定可靠的方式來制作共變異數的模型。 基於經濟期望及貨幣政策所存在的結構性變化、市場對突發事件如災難性事件或大公司倒閉的反應、與及風險監管的改革，共變異數的動態結構自然有著多種形態的過程。本研究旨在發展一套新的混合隨機共變異數模型。它的特點是容許共變異數有著多於一種形態。我們更會探討帶來形態轉變的隱藏要素。隨著了解這些隱藏要素，我們可以研究經濟事件、政策變化及財經新聞如何影響波動走勢和不同金融市場的相互關係。我們亦會探討擬議的混合隨機共變異數模型對不同金融應用如建立風險措施和最優質投資組合的有效性。這個研究項目的結果將會為不同金融體系的相互關係、資產配置和風險管理等問題上提供有用的資源及見解。

645111.label: Realisation of objectives
645111.value: In this project, a stochastic covariance model and its mixture extension have been developed to deal with objectives 1 and 2. In addition, objective 3 on model selection or the determination of the number of components have been achieved in So and Chan (2014) and in a working paper to be submitted. Financial applications stated in objective 4 and other extensions in objective 5 have also been studied. In particular, the dynamic property of the mixture component probabilities gives predictive power on market risk changes.

645111.label: Major findings and research outcome
645111.value: Major findings and research outcome of this project are reported in three papers published in international journals and one working paper. The first paper in part C, So and Chan (2014), developed a mixture of Pareto distribution and a symmetric distribution for capturing heavy-tailed characteristics in return distributions. While modeling stochastic covariance, the technique in So and Chan (2014) has been considered to model tail dependence in high-dimensional problems. The second paper in part C, So and Yeung (2014), studied dynamic dependence in a vine copula framework. Findings of the above two papers provide foundations for the mixture covariance model development and associated financial applications. In the third paper in part C, Asai and So (2015), the stylized facts of long memory property and asymmetry were incorporated in modeling stochastic covariance dynamically using a matrix-exponential process approach. Model selection methods for stochastic covariance models were also proposed. Finally, a working paper entitled 'A multivariate mixture stochastic covariance model' is being prepared. It summarizes statistical inference procedures, ways to identify the number of components and financial applications with high-frequency data using a mixture model. The paper was presented in The 21st International Conference on Computational Statistics, Geneva, 19-22 August, 2014 (see page 42 in http://compstat2014.org/auxil/Book-of-Abstracts-COMPSTAT2014.pdf). A final draft of the paper will be ready for submission early this year.

645111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
645111.value: There is potential for further research in several directions. 1. To introduce shrinkage in the dynamic covariance construction to enable high-dimensional applications; 2. It is possible to develop mixture of copulas for dynamic covariance modeling; 3. Extension of the mixture probabilities to have Markov switching states is possible.

645111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
645111.value: The nature of this project is to build statistical models for forecasting the level of dependence of financial returns via covariance. A particular attention is on the application to high-frequency financial data. In the mixture model construction, the dynamic of the covariance process is governed by hidden states which may be related to market conditions. In the practical point of view, the hidden states can help us understand what economic factors affect the dynamic of dependence between difference financial securities. Identifying a suitable number of mixture components in the modeling will likely improve forecasting performance of the models developed in this project. Since covariance is crucial in constructing efficient portfolios and in hedging exercises, adequate mixture model building for covariance can help derive sound procedures for asset allocation and market risk management.

645211.label: Project Title(Chinese)
645211.value: 社交網絡與用戶參與行為研究

645211.label: Project Objectives
645211.value: To empirically examine the effect of social networking function on user participation behavior with observations about users’ participation in online social networks. To implement large scale social network analysis and offer detailed analysis about various factors that may influence the effect of social networking functions. To establish a (socio-economic) theoretical framework to analyze the effect of social factors on user behavior, which is the foundation for future extensions and follow up studies.

To implement large scale social network analysis and offer detailed analysis about various factors that may influence the effect of social networking functions.
To establish a (socio-economic) theoretical framework to analyze the effect of social factors on user behavior, which is the foundation for future extensions and follow up studies.

645211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
645211.value: Modern Internet technology significantly extended the way consumers participate in the markets for information goods. User-generated-content flourishes in the virtual environment, changes the way information is provided and consumed and alters the market structure. The production of user-generated content is often organized mostly in loosely connected virtual communities. These communities, while growing rapidly in quantity, suffer from under-participation. To motivate user participation and to facilitate user retention, it is a common practice nowadays to implement social networking functions and create a social environment in these online communities. While it is generally believed that users are socially motivated, little previous research investigated the effect of social networking functions on users’ participation behavior. In this proposed research, we will leverage longitudinal observations of user participation and online social networking activities in one of the largest online communities in China, and empirically study the effect of social networking functions on user participation. To theoretically guide and interpret the empirical findings, a game theoretical model will be developed to describe and predict user participation behavior under social influences. We will also implement extensive social network analysis to characterize structural factors that may determine how users respond to social networking functions.

645211.label: Realisation of objectives
645211.value: The objectives are all met. In our final paper, we report that we were able to empirically examine the effect of social networking function on user participation behavior (Objective 1). We implemented a large scale social network analysis based on collected data (Objective 2) and found empirical support to the theoretical predictions of the impact of social factors on user behavior (Objective 3).

645211.label: Major findings and research outcome
645211.value: In this project, we propose and examine the effect of a new type of framing: social framing. Similar to the traditional framing effect that triggers different decisions depending on different ways of presentation, social framing triggers different user activities by using a different label for the same social relationship. The difference is that social framing takes place in an online social environment and the objective is not to trigger a decision, but some level of activities in the online social environment. We establish a theoretical framework to build a bridge between user activities in social media and their psychological needs. We argue that social framing can trigger some needs to be more salient and then alter user activities. Based on literature review and interviews, we created a classification of user activities. Our theory building suggests that social framing may trigger or suppress different needs at the same time, therefore affecting different types of activities in different ways. To offer empirical support to the main argument, we collect data from a major social media website in China. Our empirical analysis hinges on a natural experiment on the site that created a new label (therefore triggering social framing) for the same underlying online social connections. We use a within-subjects model and a between-subjects difference-in-differences model to offer corroborating evidence to support the theoretical conclusions. We find that the social framing indeed triggered different psychological needs from the users and changed their activities. Specifically, the social framing changed the online social connections to a kind of friend relationship. This triggered the psychological needs for relatedness and weakened the needs for competence. As a result, we find that users commenting and responding activities significantly increased and their reviewing activities dropped. This finding remains robust with various variable- and model-manipulations.

645211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
645211.value: This study has several limitations. First, for privacy protection, the site did not provide us with users’ demographical information and identifiable information about the products in the data set. This limitation in data access does not affect the analysis of the current study, but it does restrict us from examining moderating factors in users’ response to social framing. Future research should extend the current research and investigate how the social framing effect varies with users, products, or user-product pairs. Second, due to the nature of the empirical context, we focus on a specific type of framing effect on three types of user activities. Future research should investigate social framing of group identity on social welfare actions. Different types of framing should be constructed and tested. Third, this study primarily focuses on the empirical identification of social framing using field data. More elaborate theoretical discussions are needed to fully explore the framing effect in social media platforms. Finally, it is important to note that our results are obtained from field data of Chinese users. Cross-culture comparison will be an important research avenue for future studies of the social framing effect.

645211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
645211.value: This project examines the framing of social relationships, or social framing, and its impact on user activities in social media or online communities. We first build a theoretical framework to classify social media user activities into several categories and map these categories to users’ psychological needs. We argue that a change in social framing can alter users’ psychological needs and then influence different types of user activities differently. Leveraging on an exogenous change to the social networking function in a popular Chinese social-media web site, we empirically identify the social framing effect. When the web site changed the label of online social connections from “follow” to “friend,” the framing changed users’ psychological needs. Supporting our theoretical predictions, we find changes in three different types of activities: rating, review, response. Our empirical results suggest that merely calling online connections as “friends” is able to significantly increase rating and responding activities and reduce reviewing activities. Taken together, we argue that design features such as online social connection labels can be used strategically to create a social framing effect.

645311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
645311.value: Nature is often represented as human-like in environmental discourse. For instance, images of the earth are sometimes presented in the form of a human body or face, with limbs or facial organs, and narratives sometimes liken the current condition of nature to human sickness. Can representing nature in an anthropomorphic manner make people show more pro-environmental behavior? This proposed research will systematically addresses this question. There are two reasons why anthropomorphizing nature may be effective in promoting pro-environmental behavior. The first reason concerns people’s connection to nature. The nonchalance and environmentally irresponsible behavior some people show may be attributable to their physical and emotional disconnection from the natural environment. From this perspective, fostering connectedness to nature can enhance pro-environmental behavior. Past social psychology studies have shown that anthropomorphizing non-human entities (e.g., machines, pets) can satisfy people’s need for social connection. Accordingly, anthropomorphizing nature should be able to connect people to nature. The second reason concerns people’s empathy toward nature. Empathy is a robust cause of helping behavior. Past studies have shown that people find it easier to empathize with non-human entities which are similar to human beings. Accordingly, anthropomorphizing nature should be able to arouse people’s empathy toward nature. Taken together, it is expected that anthropomorphizing nature, through its effect on people’s connectedness to nature and empathy toward nature, will foster pro-environmental behavior. In a preliminary laboratory experiment, anthropomorphizing nature was found to enhance people’s connectedness to nature. This proposed research aims to extend this experiment in three directions. First, a correlational study is proposed to quantify the correlational association between a dispositional tendency to anthropomorphize and pro-environmental behavior. Second, three laboratory experiments are proposed to test the causal effect of anthropomorphizing nature on pro-environmental behavior. These four proposed studies will also examine the mediating roles of connectedness to nature and empathy toward nature. Third, to complement these studies and to obtain ecologically valid findings, a field experiment is proposed which will test the causal effect of anthropomorphizing nature in a real-life setting. This proposed research will contribute to theoretical understanding of pro-environmental behavior by identifying one of the causal antecedents of connectedness to nature and empathy toward nature. In addition, it will bear implications for the design of school curricula and public service announcements: changing people’s representation of nature may serve as a relatively low-cost, convenient strategy for promoting pro-environmental behavior. 環保的論述中，常見自然被賦予人形或人性。本研究旨在了解這類擬人化的論述對人類的環保行為的影響。 將自然擬人化或許會影響人類對自然的感覺。自然可能變得較可親，人類亦也許較容易對自然產生同理心。過往的研究指出，這些感覺都可以促進助人行為，由此推論，將自然擬人化的論述或許能推動環保行為。 初步的實驗發現，將自然擬人化確實令人類覺得自然較可親。本研究旨在從三方面更深入了解擬人化的論述的影響。首先，透過問卷調查，了解人類本身將自然擬人化的傾向與環保行為的關係。其次，透過實驗室實驗，了解擬人化的論述與環保行為的因果關係。最後，透過實地實驗，了解擬人化的論述在真實生活場景中有否影響。 本研究有助了解如何提高人類對自然的親近感覺及同理心，從而建立環保行為的理論，並提出有效的推動環保的策略。

645311.label: Realisation of objectives
645311.value: All three objectives are realized. We conducted a series of studies (in total, 14 survey studies and 4 experiments). Taken together, we found that anthropomorphism of nature is indeed associated with pro-environmental behavior, and this relationship seems to be causal (Objective 1). We also found that anthropomorphism of nature is associated with connectedness to nature and empathy with nature (Objective 2), and these concepts in turn mediate the relationship between anthropomorphism and pro-environmental behavior (Objective 3).

645311.label: Major findings and research outcome
645311.value: First, we took the individual difference approach. Our interest was on the effects of people’s dispositional tendency to anthropomorphize nature. We measured respondents’ dispositional tendency to anthropomorphize nature with a newly developed psychometric scale (this scale had been validated in an earlier series of studies). We also asked our respondents to report their environmental attitudes and everyday pro-environmental behavior (e.g., recycling, energy conservation). In one study, we also made an observation of their actual behavior: respondents were asked whether they were willing to donate part or all of their participation compensation to an environmental organization, and their donation was observed. Across all studies, with different measures of pro-environmental behavior and with other personality and individual difference variables (including personality, values, social desirability, and demographic variables) controlled for, a significant correlation with anthropomorphism of nature was found: Individuals who anthropomorphize nature tend to exhibit more pro-environmental behavior than those who do not anthropomorphize nature. After that, we attempted to identify the psychological mechanisms underlying the observed relationship. We found that dispositional anthropomorphism of nature was correlated with both connectedness to nature (the feeling that one is part of nature) and empathy with nature (the tendency to take the perspective of plants and animals in the natural environment and to empathize with them). Also, we found that these two psychological variables mediated the relationship between anthropomorphism of nature and pro-environmental behavior. In other words, individuals who anthropomorphize nature tend to feel more connected to nature and empathize more with the natural environment than do those who do not anthropomorphize nature, and these two psychological variables in turn motivate them to take pro-environmental actions. Our next goal was to examine whether the observed effects were causal. We were interested in knowing whether artificially leading someone to anthropomorphize nature could generate similar psychological effects. In our experiments, we led some participants to anthropomorphize nature (through having them read some anthropomorphic posters or articles) and some others not to anthropomorphize nature (through having them read some non-anthropomorphic materials). We were able to replicate the pattern of findings observed in the individual difference approach. That is, participants who were led to anthropomorphize nature subsequently reported stronger intention to perform pro-environmental behavior than those who were not, and this effect was mediated by connectedness to nature. These findings are now reported in 5 published articles in international refereed journals and 4 international conference presentations.

645311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
645311.value: Anthropomorphism enables people to interact with nature (e.g., empathy) as if they interact with other humans. With this theoretical basis, currently I am exploring the other psychological effects of anthropomorphism of nature. In particular, I am focusing on the possibility that people experience interpersonal emotions toward nature. Take gratitude as an example. Past research showed that gratitude stems from the receipt of a benefit resulted from the intentional actions of another person, and it motivates people to act prosocially toward the benefactor. Based on this research on interpersonal gratitude, I am now testing this hypothesis: When people are conscious of the benefits they receive from the natural world, they might feel grateful toward nature and thereby become motivated to take actions to protect it, particularly when they anthropomorphize nature. In four preliminary studies, I found support for this hypothesis. I found that after reading about the services that the natural world provides to humans, some participants spontaneously reported grateful feelings toward nature and subsequently exhibited a stronger intention to take pro-environmental actions. In addition, anthropomorphism of nature rendered gratitude toward nature more likely. I plan to continue this investigation and extend it to other interpersonal emotions (e.g., anger).

645311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
645311.value: The environmental crisis is perhaps the most pressing challenge facing the modern world. As some environmental thinkers note, the solution to this crisis resides in how humans think about nature. In this research, we explored the role of anthropomorphism of nature—the psychological tendency to consider nature as a human. In a series of survey studies and experiments, we found that when people anthropomorphize nature, they exhibit more pro-environmental behavior. Practically speaking, these findings provide valuable evidences for environmentalists’ considerations. Anthropomorphism is often seen in the environmental discourse. However, whether these tactics are effective or not have rarely been empirically tested. The present research is the first investigation that provides a systematic set of evidences in this regard. Theoretically speaking, the present research suggests that an anthropomorphic representation is one of the alternative ways people think about nature. In people’s mind, nature is not necessarily just a pool of resources or an object of scientific observation. People may see nature as a human, and thereby relate to it just as they relate to other humans. This view opens up new possibilities for the study of the human-nature relationship.

645511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
645511.value: Visual design is a key determinant of consumer behavior. Not surprisingly, companies invest huge amounts of time and money in the design of their packaging, ads, products, websites, and other marketing stimuli. Similarly, policy makers develop eye-catching logos and health warnings to educate and stimulate consumers to select better options. Because of its practical and theoretical importance, academic research extensively studied consumer reactions to visual design. An important limitation of this body of research is that it focuses in large part on verbalized responses, requiring extensive cognitive processing, while unconscious processes, not reflected in verbalized responses, are an important determinant of consumer reactions to visual design. In addition, previous research mostly studied visual design effects outside the natural context in which visual stimuli appear, and, therefore, does not take into account the effects of distracting visual stimuli. As a consequence, academic research still provides little insights on how visual design affects consumer behavior. The aim of this project is to investigate the effects of visual design on consumer decision making at the point of purchase, one of the most important tasks in which visual design plays a pivotal role. To do so, the project proposes to investigate the effects of visual design on the eye movements of consumers while they are making choices. To analyze the eye-movements of consumers, a newly developed neurologically plausible Bayesian statistical model is proposed. This model will be based on theories in experimental aesthetics, decision making and visual attention. The experimental eye-tracking approach, in combination with the Bayesian statistical model addresses the limitations of previous research on design and choice. Using robust optimization techniques, the proposed model is expected to be an important tool for practitioners to optimally design packages and in-store communication. Moreover, the modeling approach estimates how the effects of visual design on choice vary across consumers. In particular, we will test the moderating role of advertising and culture on the effects of visual design on decision making at the point of purchase. The outcomes of this research may result in practical tools for managers and policy makers to help consumers make better choices and to objectively judge whether consumers are mislead, for instance by copycat or imitation strategies that cause confusion. 視覺設計是消費者行為的主要決定因素之一。公司投放了巨額的時間和金錢在其包裝、廣告、產品、網頁和其他刺激市場營銷的設計上。同樣地，決策者用引人注目的商標和警告健康的字句來教育和刺激消費者作出更好的選擇。因為視覺設計有著實際和理論上的重要性，所以學術界廣泛地就消費者對視覺設計作出研究。這個研究範疇的主要限制為大部份的重點都放在口述回應中，並要求大量的認知處理，而沒有在口述回應中反映的潛意識則是消費者對視覺設計的一個重要決定因素。此外，過去的研究多數大多在非自然環境下研究視覺刺激對視覺設計的影響，所以並沒有顧及使注意力分散的視覺刺激影響。因此，現在學術研究對視覺設計如何影響消費者行為只有很少的見解。 這個研究計劃的主要目的是探究在採購點時視覺設計對消費者作選擇的影響。視覺設計在这种情况下擔當起着非常重要的作用。為此，這個計劃提議探究視覺設計對消費者在作選擇時眼球活動的影響。一個新建立的神經學上合理性的貝氏統計模型將被提議用作分析消費者的眼球活動。這個模型將建基於實驗美學、決策行為及視覺注意力的理論。此實驗性的眼球跟蹤方法加上貝氏統計模型論及過去研究在設計和選擇上的限制。利用可靠優化的技術，這個建議的模型能預計到是給從業者一個可最佳地設計包裝及店內傳播的工具。再者，此模擬方法能預測視覺設計在選擇上的影響如何因消費者而存有差異。尤其需要指出的是，我們會測試廣告和文化在採購點中令決定受視覺設計影響的角色。這個研究得出的結論可能作為經理及決策人幫助消費者作更好選擇及客觀地判斷消費者是否受模仿者或仿制品等誤導的實用工具。

645511.label: Realisation of objectives
645511.value: The objectives of this project have been successfully achieved. Two papers have been accepted for publication, one in the Journal of Marketing Research (a leading journal in the field) and a second in the Handbook of Marketing Decision Models. Moreover, three additional papers are currently in advanced stages of the review process in leading journals of the field: the Journal of Marketing Research (2 papers) and Journal of Consumer Research (1 paper). These three papers have also been presented at leading conferences and have received positive feedback. The research was conducted using laboratory experiments with eye-tracking methodology in Hong Kong and The Netherlands. In these lab experiments, we have researched several design factors (advertising, shelf design and design of shopping websites) on the choice process of participants. Moreover, we have also collected field data in an ice-cream store in Hong Kong, which allowed us to test design factors on choice in real life settings. Finally, I have supervised a PhD student (Xi Chen, PhD defended in May 2013) in which we worked on an extension of the proposed Bayesian choice model that we applied to decision making in social networks. This resulted in one published paper at the Journal of Marketing Research and a second paper that is currently invited for second-round review at Journal of Marketing Research. As specified below, this research proposed the four main research goals that we achieved as follows: 1. Development of a neurologically plausible choice model for eye-movements: This research problem has been addressed in the first stages of this research in which we developed a new neurologically plausible choice model for the analysis of eye movement data. The details of the model are described in a paper that is invited for second-round review at Journal of Consumer Research, and is also described in an overview paper of eye-movement models of choice and search that is accepted for publication in the Handbook of Marketing Decision Models. 2. Application of the model for visual design and shelf display: The choice model is used to investigate the effects of visual design elements (shelf display and advertising) on the eye-movements during choice. We found that the proposed model explains the choice process well, which provides a better understanding of how visual design affects choice. More specifically, we demonstrate how different design elements affect processing in three attention states: localization, identification at the broader brand level, and identification at the specific package level. In addition, we also tested implications of these visual design factors in a field experiment. In an ice-cream store, we manipulated shelf layout of different flavors and developed a Bayesian choice model. A challenging part of this data was that visual design affected purchase quantities, for which we needed to extend the modeling approach. Our model was able to recommend important marketing decisions (assortment design and pricing), which increased sales and profits of the store by 7 percent (a manuscript with this model is currently under review at the Journal of Marketing Research). 3. Moderating role of advertising: We investigated the moderating role of advertising on the choice process of eye-movements by developing different types of ads. We found that 1) advertising effects are strong in the short-term, but disappear relatively quickly after a few shopping tasks, 2) advertising effects the choice process through identification (i.e., consumers are able to reject products quicker that they do not want to buy, which facilitates the decision process). These findings have been described in the paper that is invited for second round review at the Journal of Consumer Research. In addition to the moderating roles of advertising on choice, together with a PhD student (Xi Chen), we extended the proposed Bayesian choice model to situations that can capture other influences on choice. More specifically, we focused on the effects of social influence on decision making. This has resulted in two manuscripts (one has been accepted for publication at the Journal of Marketing Research and a second manuscript is invited for second-round review). In these papers, we 1) extended the Bayesian choice model to identify the (reciprocal) effects of choices among friends in their social networks, and 2) identified the relative importance of different friends on the decisions of people. This model has shown to be powerful in targeting decisions, and reaching customers more effectively. 4. Cultural differences in the choice process: To investigate this, we collected eye-movement data both in The Netherlands and in Hong Kong. Both datasets are used in two separate studies. Interestingly, the results we find are robust across these two cultures, which suggest that there are no strong cultural differences in choice processes. Moreover, in the field experiment that we conducted, we observed both local and international customers. Similar to our previous findings, we found that our model and the choice process holds for both local as well as international students. Except for different preferences across these two groups, we did not find evidence for a different choice process. In sum, we have been able to address all objectives successfully. Three papers are still in the review process, but we believe that these will get accepted in the (near) future as the feedback on these projects was positive.

645511.label: Major findings and research outcome
645511.value: This research generated both methodological findings as well as substantial findings that were obtained by applying the modeling approach to different scenarios. First, regarding the methodological findings, we developed a neurological plausible choice model that is implemented using Bayesian modeling techniques. Theoretically, the model distinguishes between three latent attention states that are based on neurological principles (a localization attention state and two identification attention states). These attention states are important components of the choice process that can be identified using eye-movement data. In contrast to what we expected, our model demonstrated that the two identification states play a much more important role in consumer choice than localization. These findings have important theoretical implications to understand the effects of visual design on choice processes. Practically, the model is able to improve assortment displays, pricing decisions, and targeting decisions. For instance, in the field experiment, we used the model to improve the assortment design and pricing strategy of a local ice-cream store. These recommendations resulted in higher sales and profits (net profits increased by 7 percent). Regarding targeting decisions, the model was able to better identify influential customers (i.e., individuals whose choices have an impact on the choices of others). Targeting influential individuals that were recommended by the developed choice model, resulted in more effective marketing strategies that reached 10 to 92 percent more customers compared to more traditional targeting procedures. From a substantial point of view, application of our Bayesian choice model has provided deeper insights on the effects of visual design on choice. First, we found strong interaction effects between the visual design of advertising and packaging. This implies that it is important to align advertising with packaging. If aligned, people are able to make their choice more efficiently, as decision times are reduced by up to one third. Second, we found that these visual design effects are not persistent over time, but only hold for short periods of only a few minutes. This implies that such effects are especially important in online shopping environments, in which companies are able to show online ads shortly before (or even during) the shopping task. Third, application of the proposed model to choice in social network environments demonstrated that not all connections are equally influential on choice decisions. Especially recent relationships with frequent interactions are more influential.

645511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
645511.value: This project has great potential for further development. First, as illustrated above, there are three manuscripts that are currently in the review process. It is our priority to get these three manuscripts accepted within the next year or two. Second, there are several other applications and extensions possible of our modeling approach that we developed in this project and that have been discussed in the Future Research sections of our papers. One of these ideas is to apply our modeling approach to different research areas. More specifically, we have started a collaboration with the medical school in Maryland and aim to extend and apply our modeling procedure to how physicians scan chest x-rays that may contain cancerous nodules. This is a very difficult task in which trained physicians are accurate and efficient. Applying our model to the eye-movement data of these physicians may provide a better understanding of their attention and decision process, which may be used to train student physicians, but also automatically identify (using computer software) potential areas in the x-rays for investigation.

645511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
645511.value: Visual design is an important factor in consumer decision making, and companies invest heavily in designing ads, packaging and websites. This research has developed a methodology based on eye-movements to investigate the choice process of people and how this is influenced by visual design factors. The proposed method identified the importance of aligning the visual design of advertisements and packaging on the decision process. The research shows that efficiency of consumer decision making can be improved by one third in terms of decision time, if ads are designed optimally containing the image of products. This research also found that these design effects are short-term, implying that the effects of ad exposure on the choice process only hold for a few minutes. Such effects are therefore especially important in online shopping environments, because companies are able to combine online advertising and shopping more efficiently. Finally, the extensions of the proposed modeling framework have been used to optimize important marketing decisions: assortment design, pricing and targeting. Using a field experiment in a local ice-cream store, the proposed model was able to improve the quality of the assortment, leading to higher sales and profits.

645711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
645711.value: At different conditional quantiles (such as median and quartile) of an economic variable that we want to study, the impact of explanatory variables might vary. Quantile regression is a powerful tool to account for such heterogenous covariates effects. While Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) focuses on the conditional mean of a random variable, quantile regression studies the conditional distribution of the same variable and provides more informative results. However most of the current research is focused on cross-sectional data anaylsis. With the wide availability of panel data, where the researcher observes data for a large number of individuals over time, some unobserved heterogenous effects can be controlled for and thus yield more robust results than pure cross-sectional studies. While linear or nonlinear regression analysis of panel data has been a heavily researched area, quantile panel regression is only beginning to draw the attention of the academia. This proposed project will look at the panel data through the lens of quantile regression. I will contribute to the current literature by considering the case where the unobserved time effects have heterogeneous impact on individuals. A factor error structure provides a parsimonious way to model such a case. I will discuss the identification and estimation of the proposed model. The developed tools can be readily applied in empirical research of labor economics, finance, international economics where panel regression is becoming increasingly popular. 簡介：在通常情況下，解釋變量對某個經濟變量的影響常常隨該經濟變量的分位數變化而有所不同。分位數回歸是研究此異質影響的有力工具。傳統的最小二乘法僅僅著力於研究條件期望的性質，而分位數回歸則能研究整個條件分佈的性態。當前對於分位數回歸的研究大多集中在截面數據。考慮到當今數據的豐富，面板數據的研究實為當務之急。作為新興的研究分支，面板數據的分位數回歸方法開始吸引了愈來愈多的關注，這也是此項目研究之著力點。此項目考慮不可觀測的動態效應對不同的個體會造成相異之影響，並利用因子模型來對殘差項建模。我將會詳盡地討論識別問題和估計方法。此方法將能有效地應用於宏觀，國際金融，勞動經濟等實證領域。

645711.label: Realisation of objectives
645711.value: The objectives have been successfully achieved. In particular, we have derived the theoretical foundations of the quantile panel regression model with non-additive time-varying fixed effects using a random coefficient representation. Appropriate assumptions, such as high dimensionality, are imposed and are shown to achieve identification of the model. We propose a two-step estimator and have shown its consistency and asymptotic normality. We also write up the accompanying Matlab computer programs to implement our estimation algorithm. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate that our estimation method has favorable properties in finite sample. We propose a simple way to test the additive fixed effects against the non-additive effects in the first stage estimation. Using our framework, we empirically address the important issue on how bank deregulation impact the distribution of income. The results have shown noticeable heterogeneous impacts over different quantiles.

645711.label: Major findings and research outcome
645711.value: In this project we introduce a two-stage estimation method to estimate a high dimensional panel quantile regression model with interactive fixed effects where both the cross section dimension and the time dimension are large. We establish the consistency and asymptotic normality of the two-stage estimator. Monte Carlo simulations illustrate that our estimates perform well in finite samples. We also use an empirical application to demonstrate how to use our methodology in practice. Our methodology provides a convenient toolbox for the analysis of heterogeneous responses of individuals from different locations of the population.

645711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
645711.value: Potentially, the current method can be applied to a variety of empirical problems in economics and finance. We may also consider adding a richer dynamic setting in the current framework.

645711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
645711.value: Quantile regression method is a powerful tool to account for heterogenous covariates effects. However most of the current research is focused on cross-sectional data anaylsis. With the wide availability of panel data, where the researcher observes data for a large number of individuals over time, more unobserved heterogenous effects can be controlled for and thus yield better results than pure cross-sectional studies. While linear or nonlinear regression analysis of panel data has been a heavily researched area, quantile panel regression has just drawn growing attention from the academia. This project looks at the panel data through the lens of quantile regression. We contribute to the current literature by allowing for unobserved time-varying individual fixed effect which is modelled as a factor error structure. We provide theory of identification and estimation of such models. The developed tools can be readily applied in empirical research of labor economics, finance, international economics where panel regression becomes increasingly popular.

645811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
645811.value: The recent financial crisis showed that credit constraints can play an important role in macroeconomic fluctuations. However, existing studies find that the importance of credit constraints is limited (Kocherlakota, 2000; Cordoba and Ripoll, 2004). These findings seem puzzling and inconsistent with the recent turmoil in the global financial markets and concurrent worldwide recession. This project responses to this challenge by introducing firm heterogeneity and endogenous credit constraints into an otherwise standard real business cycle model. It aims to identify several new channels that financial frictions can affect real economy. Firm heterogeneity provides an new mechanism for credit constraints through a resource reallocation channel: more-productive firms benefit more by drawing resource from less-productive firms. The improved resource allocation, in return, relaxes the credit constraints. It turns out that this interaction between credit constraints and firm heterogeneities can quantitatively amplify and transmit small shocks into big business cycle fluctuations in a carefully calibrated model economy. The heterogenous firms approach also sheds new light on the firm's capital structure, resource misallocation, self-fulfilling expectation and asset price bubbles. 最近金融危機表明信貸約束是經濟波動的一個重要因數。然而，現有的研究卻發現信貸約束的作用十分有限。因此解釋當前的金融危機便成一個重要的研究課題。本研究課題著重於企業異質以及它與經濟週期的相互作用。初步結果表明企業異質能產生一種資源從新分配效果， 它能過幫助解釋以下的一些現象：資產價格泡沫、內生經濟週期。

645811.label: Realisation of objectives
645811.value: The project has yield very fruitful research output. With collaboration from world-class experts, all objectives proposed have been successful realized. In “Credit Risk and Business Cycles”, Jianjun Miao at Boston University and I address the first objective by incorporating long-term defaultable corporate bonds and credit risk in a dynamic stochastic general equilibrium business cycle model. We are working with one of my graduate student Zhou Jing on a related project that study sovereign debt. A preliminary draft is available. In the paper “Financial Constraints, Endogenous Markups, and Self-fulfilling Equilibria” , Jess Benhabib from New York University and I addressed the second objective by showing that Financial constraints can generate self-fulfilling Equilibria through procyclical markups. In the paper “Credit Constraints and Self-fulfilling Business Cycles,” Zheng Liu from San Francisco Federal Reserve Bank and I show credit constraints and firm heterogeneity can generate endogenous TFP and indeterminacy if the endogenous TFP is strong enough. To address the fourth objective, we also show that credit constraints can generate significant misallocation in the steady state. Finally, when it comes to the fifth objective, Jianjun Miao and I have worked out a series of paper on asset bubbles in a production economy with heterogeneous firms and borrowing constraints.

645811.label: Major findings and research outcome
645811.value: One of major findings of the project is that the interplay of borrowing constraints and firm heterogeneity can enhance our understanding on business cycles and economic development in several important aspects: 1. Borrowing constraint can lead to significant misallocation in an economy with heterogeneous firms. This misallocation of resource generates low TFPs in developing countries. 2. As the borrowing constraints tight, this misallocation becomes severer in economic downturn, amplifying the small shocks to create big fluctuation in business cycles. 3. Such misallocation can also be self-fulfilling. The credit supply will be abundant if the agents believe that the economy is in a good shape. The increased credit supply relaxes borrowing constraints faced by the productive firms, allowing them to expand. This improves the efficiency of resource allocation and hence leads to an actual economic boom. 4. Borrowing constraints can leads to asset bubbles. The project has generated two publications and several working papers. Some of these working papers are under revision of prestigious journals. The paper entiled “Financial Constraints, Endogenous Markups, and Self-fulfilling Equilibria” is published by Journal of Monetary Economics. The paper entitled “Credit Constraints and Self-fulfilling Business Cycles” is published by the American Economic Journal: Macroeconomics. The project also produced several working papers with good publication potential. The paper entitled “Bubbles and Credit Constraints” is under revision of Review of Economics Studies. The paper entitled “Banking Bubbles and Financial Crisis” is under the second revision of Journal of Economic Theory. The paper entitled “Housing Bubbles and Policy Analysis” is invited to submit to a special issue of Journal of Monetary Economics for publication. The paper entitled “A Bayesian DSGE Model of Stock Market Bubbles and Business Cycles” is recommended by the editor of Econometrica to Quantitative Economics. For a complete list of working papers please refer to part C.

645811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
645811.value: So far, I have focused on financial constraints on firms. Financial constraints on households will also be very interesting and important research topics. In addition, financial intermediary play an important role in modern economy. Much of future development will be devoted to understanding their role in shaping business cycle fluctuation.

645811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
645811.value: The project has generated many new insights on resource misallocation, self-fulfilling business cycles and asset bubble through the lens of borrowing constraints and firm heterogeneity. The research output includes two published papers in very prestigious journals and several promising working papers.

645911.label: Project Title(Chinese)
645911.value: 会计准则差异，强制性国际会计准则的采用及跨国并购

645911.label: Project Objectives
645911.value: To examine whether the accounting standard differences across countries deter cross-border mergers and acquisitions. To examine whether the mandatory adoption of IFRS is associated with increases in cross-border mergers and acquisitions .
rows: To examine whether the accounting standard differences across countries deter cross-border mergers and acquisitions.
To examine whether the mandatory adoption of IFRS is associated with increases in cross-border mergers and acquisitions .

645911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
645911.value: This study will investigate the relation between differences in accounting standards (“GAAP”) across countries and cross-border mergers and acquisitions (M&A), and how the recent mandatory adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) affects cross-border M&A. We propose that information asymmetry arising from GAAP differences impacts cross-border M&A in the following ways. First, GAAP differences increase acquirers’ searching and screening costs in spotting a foreign target with the greatest synergy. Firms seeking to pursue acquisitions abroad would first identify all the potential targets in foreign countries. GAAP differences between countries make it difficult for the acquirer to understand and evaluate a foreign target’s financial position and operating performance. Further, GAAP differences between potential targets from different countries diminish the comparability of the targets, making it difficult for the acquirer to spot the foreign target with the greatest synergy. Second, adverse selection problems diminish the likelihood that a cross-border M&A will be completed. M&A is a double-lemon scenario where both parties have incentives to misrepresent their own values. Acquirers have incentives to offer a stock when their stock prices are high, targets are thus likely to reject the offer and require acquirers to pay in cash. However, acquirers making cash offers are in danger of overpaying the targets. Therefore, the two-sided information asymmetry induced by GAAP differences discourages both sides of the transaction from making a deal. We expect that global accounting harmonization via mandatory IFRS adoption helps eliminate GAAP differences and mitigates information asymmetry between countries, hence promotes cross-border M&A. We hypothesize that (1) GAAP differences are negatively associated with the volume of cross-border M&A before IFRS adoption; (2) Mandatory adoption of IFRS in the target country will attract more foreign acquirers. The increase in the volume of cross-border M&A will be most pronounced if both countries involved in the transaction have adopted IFRS at the same time. To evaluate the above propositions, we will collect cross-border M&A completed between 1999 and 2008 from the Security Data Corporation (SDC) for 26 countries that have adopted IFRS since 2003 and 23 countries that have not adopted IFRS in 2005. We will examine (1) the association between the volume of cross-border M&A of every country-pair and the corresponding country-pair GAAP differences before mandatory IFRS adoption; (2) changes in the volume of cross-border M&A from the pre-IFRS period to the post-IFRS period in the 26 IFRS adopting countries, relative to the 23 non-IFRS countries. 该项目将研究国别间会计准则的差异与跨国并购的关系，以及近期推行的强制性采用国际财务报告准则对跨国并购的影响。我们提出，国别会计准则差异引起的信息不对称会通过如下途径影响跨国并购。 第一，国别间会计准则差异增加了收购公司欲找到最具有协同性的海外目标的搜寻和筛选成本。欲进行海外并购的收购方会先在海外市场搜寻所有潜在目标。但是国别间会计准则差异导致收购方很难了解和评估海外被收购目标的财务状况和经营业绩。而且，海外目标公司之间的会计准则差异降低了目标公司相互间的可比性，致使收购公司很难确认最具协同性的海外被收购目标。第二，逆向选择问题降低了海外并购成功的可能性。并购是一个“双柠檬”，由于并购双方彼此存在信息不对称，因而并购双方都试图歪曲自己的真实价值。 当收购公司的价格较高的时候，收购公司会试图出用本公司股票购买被并购方，但是被收购方很大可能会拒绝这种方式，而是要求收购方用现金支付。但是，如果使用现金支付，收购方有超额支付被并购公司的危险。所以，国别间会计准则差异引起的双向信息不对称阻碍了并购顺利完成。我们预测，强制性采用国际财务报告准则而产生的全球会计一体化会削减国别间会计差异，减缓国别间 的信息不对称，从而促进跨国并购。 我们假设：（1）在强制性采用国际财务报告准则之前， 国别间会计准则差异与跨国并购量存在负向关系； （2） 被并购公司所在国如果强制性采用国际财务报告准则，将会吸引更多的海外并购公司。如果收购公司所在国和被并购公司所在国同时强制性采用国际财务报告准则，那么两国间的跨国并购量的增长最为显著。 为了评估我们的假设，我们会从SDC收集1999年至2008年的跨国并购， 包括26个已经从2003年就已经强制性采用国际财务报告准则的国家和23个截止2005年还未强制性采用国际财务报告准则的国家。 我们会测试(1) 在强制性采用国际财务报告准则之前， 任何两个国家之间的跨国并购量和两国间会计准则差异的关系； （2） 相比23个未强制性采用国际财务报告准则的国家， 26已经强制性采用国际财务报告准则的国家，跨国并购量从采用前到采用后有何变化。
