660411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
660411.value: A receptor superfamily for extracellular adenosine 5’-triphosphate (ATP) consists of P2X nucleotide (ligand-gated ion-channels) and P2Y nucleotide (G-protein-coupled receptors) subtypes; these receptors mainly respond to ATP and play distinct physiological roles in different systems. In nervous system, ATP acts as a neurotransmitter as well as a neuron-modulator. Several lines of evidence showed that ATP, via different P2Y receptors (P2Y-Rs), exerts the “short-term” effects in neurons, such as the modulation of ion channel activity and neurotransmitter release. However, the “long-term” effects such as synaptic gene regulation have never been revealed. Previous studies from our laboratory indicated that P2Y1 receptor (P2Y1R) and P2Y2 receptor (P2Y2R) are co-localized at vertebrate neuromuscular junctions, and exert the “long-term” effect by controlling the synaptic gene expressions and post-synaptic specializations in muscles. Recent findings also support this notion that P2Y1R and P2Y2R are aggregated at the synaptic region along the neurites of cultured cortical neurons, and stimulate cholinergic and glutaminergic genes. Therefore, we extend our investigation on P2Y1R and P2Y2R in neurons. Specifically, we focus on the specific localization of P2Y1R in membrane raft in the brain and cultured cortical neurons, as well as the possible mechanisms in mediating this specific localization. Afterward, the role of membrane raft-localized P2Y1R and P2Y2R that mediates their synaptic aggregations and gene regulation will be revealed by cholesterol depletion. Lastly, the signaling cascade and transcriptional mechanisms of P2Y1R- and P2Y2R-mediated post-synaptic gene expression will be demonstrated by using NMDA receptor as the target. In summary, the current proposal aims to provide different lines of evidence to support the functional roles of membrane raft localization in mediating the synaptic aggregation and gene regulation effect of P2Y1R and P2Y2R in cortical neurons. In addition, the significance of P2Y1R and P2Y2R in regulating the post-synaptic gene expression will be emphasized by producing the functional NMDA receptor, with the provision of the underlying signaling cascade and the transcriptional mechanism. To the end, we hope to demonstrate that the ATP-mediated purinergic signaling, via P2Y1R and P2Y2R, in neuronal synapse may serve as one of the control mechanisms of synaptic plasticity in our brain. 三磷酸腺苷（ATP）受体家族包括P2X受体和P2Y受体，它们在不同的系统里具有不同的功能。在神经系统里，ATP可作为神经递质和神经调节剂。研究表明ATP可通过激活P2Y受体，产生短期效应，如调节离子通道的活性和神经递质的释放。然而，ATP的长期效应，如突触的基因调节，目前尚未有报道。我们的研究发现P2Y1受体和P2Y2受体共同定位在体外培养的大脑皮层神经元，并可刺激突触的特异性基因表达。本项目将重点研究脑和体外培养的大脑皮层神经元中P2Y1和P2Y2受体在突触膜筏上的定位及其定位机制，以及由P2Y1和P2Y2受体介导的基因表达及信号级联机制。我们希望通过研究神经突触中ATP激活P2Y1和P2Y2受体介导的嘌呤信号传导，阐释ATP可作为神经调节剂，调节大脑中突触的可塑性。

660411.label: Realisation of objectives
660411.value: ATP functions as an extracellular signaling molecule that is co-stored and co-released with neurotransmitters at central and peripheral neuronal synapses. Stimulation by ATP upregulates the expression of synaptic genes in muscle—including the genes for nicotine acetylcholine receptor (a-, d-, and «-subunits) and acetylcholinesterase (AChE)—via the P2Y receptor (P2YR), but the trophic response of neurons to the activation of P2YRs is less well understood. We reported that cultured cortical neurons and the developing rat brain expressed different types of P2YRs, and among these the UTP-sensitive P2Y2R was the most abundant. P2Y2R was found to exist in membrane rafts and it colocalized with the postsynaptic protein PSD-95 in cortical neurons. Notably, agonist-dependent stimulation of P2Y2R elevated the neuronal expression of cholinergic genes encoding AChE, PRiMA (an anchor for the globular form AChE), and choline acetyltransferase, and this induction was mediated by a signaling cascade that involved Ca2+ mobilization and extracellular regulated kinases 1/2 activation. The importance of P2Y2R action was further shown by the receptor’s synergistic effect with P2Y1R in enhancing cholinergic gene expression via the robust stimulation of Ca2+ influx. Taken together our results revealed a developmental function of P2Y2R in promoting synaptic gene expression and demonstrated the influence of costimulation of P2Y1R and P2Y2R in neurons. Moreover, in order to search the role of P2Y1R in cholinergic function in the brain, the expression of globular form AChE was determined in the brain of P2Y1R -/- mice. In contrast to that in muscle, the amounts of AChE activity, AChE catalytic subunit, structure subunit PRiMA, as well as the amount of ACh, in the brain were not significantly altered, suggesting the role of P2Y1R in neuron could have different function as that in muscle. But the expressions of a series of neuronal development markers, i.e. neurofilaments, were reduced in P2Y1R-/- mouse brain, indicating P2Y1R may be involved in neuronal development process. Remark: The former PI, Dr. Roy CHOI, had a heart attack in 2013, and he was in a deep coma at the hospital since Aug 2013, and then he deceased in Jan 2015. Under this urgent scenario, Dr. Choi was unable to continue with the research. Hence, Prof. Karl Tsim took over as PI and was approved by UGC on 24 Jan 2014.

660411.label: Major findings and research outcome
660411.value: 1. P2Y1R and P2Y2R were detected in rat E18 and adult cortex. The expression of the P2Y2R transcript in adult was higher than E18, where the protein’s expression increased from embryonic to adult stages. These results indicated that P2Y1R and P2Y2R were present in cortical neurons and up-regulated during neuronal differentiation. 2. The expression profile of P2Y1R and P2Y2R was increased during the differentiation of cortical neurons. The differentiation of cortical neurons was confirmed by the parallel up-regulation of two markers: NF-200 and PSD-95. 3. P2Y1R and P2Y2R were present in lipid raft-enriched fractions in both adult rat cortex and in mature cortical neurons. These raft fractions contained other synaptic markers, including AChE, mAChR M1, NMDA receptor subunits NR1 and NR2A, and PSD-95. These results demonstrated the cellular and subcellular localization of P2Y1R and P2Y2R in neurons and adult brain and suggested a potential role of the UTP-responsive P2Y2R, like P2Y1R, in regulating neuronal function(s). 4. Treatment of cortical neurons with ATP or UTP enhanced the expression of AChE, ChAT and PRiMA to different extents. Exposure to P2Y1R- and P2Y2R-specific agonists also significantly elevated the expression of these genes. The protein levels of AChE, ChAT and PRiMA were also up-regulated upon treatment with P2Y1R and P2Y2R-specific agonists. 5. The co-activation of two P2Y1R and P2Y2R under physiologic conditions can produce synergistic responses in terms of receptor signaling and gene expression in cortical neurons, which might account for the functional necessity of P2YRs being localized at the postsynaptic region in these neurons. 6. The depletion of P2Y1R resulted in a decrease of post-synaptic expressions in the muscle of mutant mice. The expression of AChE, PRiMA and ColQ in muscle was markedly decreased. Moreover, the immunostaining of AChE was shown to be co-localized with AChR-specific α-bungarotoxin binding site in both P2Y1R+/+ and P2Y1R-/- mice. Possibly due to the reduced AChE protein, the staining was weaker in the mutant mice nmj. These results strongly support that ATP acting on P2Y1R in muscle plays an indispensable role in maintaining AChE expression. In contrast, the alternation of AChE expression in the brain was not revealed in P2Y1R-/- mice. 7. In P2Y1R-/- mice, the expression of P2Y2R in muscle was significantly reduced. In P2Y1R-/- mice, both AChE and AChR were co-localized at the nmj. 8. The expression of SV-48 and PSD-95 were decreased in the mutant mice. These results suggested P2Y1R could regulate the synaptic protein.

660411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
660411.value: Few possible issues could be considered for a new direction of further study: 1. The specific physical interaction of P2Y1R and P2Y2R could be determined. The co-localization of two recpetors is possible mediated by a linker protein; however, the identity of this protein is not known. 2. The defect in neuron differentiation of P2Y1R-/- mice could be a possible cause of neurodegenerative diseases, e.g. depression. This signaling cacade has to be determined. 3. The interaction of P2Y1R and P2Y2R could be happened in other tissues, i.e. not restricted to nervous system.

660411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
660411.value: P2Y1R and P2Y2R were present in cortical neurons and up-regulated during neuronal differentiation. P2Y1R and P2Y2R could be co-localized with PSD-95 in primary cortical neurons. Moreover, P2Y1R and P2Y2R were present in the lipid raft-enriched fractions in both adult rat cortex and in mature cortical neurons. The synaptic markers, including AChE, mAChR M1, NR1, NR2A and PSD-95 could be regulated by P2Y1R and P2Y2R.

660711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
660711.value: Neuronal migration is critical for the lamination of cerebral cortex during early brain development. After differentiation, developing neurons adopt a bipolar morphology and migrate through the cortex. While precise cortical lamination is crucial for maintaining functional integrity of the cerebral cortex, mutations in several genes including dcx, flna or disc1 are associated with neuronal disorders such as X-linked lissencephaly, periventricular heterotopia and schizophrenia. Neuronal migration is achieved through rearrangement and coordination of microtubule and actin dynamics in response to extracellular cues. However, the signaling pathways that regulate neuronal migration have not been completely elucidated. In particular, little is known concerning the mechanisms by which extracellular signals are transduced from cell surface receptors to cellular cytoskeletal dynamics to regulate neuronal migration. We have recently demonstrated that a serine/threonine kinase Mst3 regulates differentiation of neurons. Interestingly, silencing of Mst3 expression by in utero electroporation resulted in a significant delay in radial migration in the developing neocortex. Moreover, our preliminary findings suggested that Mst3 interacts with actin regulators. These findings strongly suggest a critical role of Mst3 in neuronal migration during cerebral cortex development through regulation of actin cytoskeletal dynamics. In this proposal, we will examine the functional roles of Mst3 and its underlying mechanism in radial migration in the developing cerebral cortex. We will first dissect the functional roles of Mst3 in radial migration. The cellular signaling mechanisms by which Mst3 exerts its biological effects on radial migration will also be investigated. In particular, we will examine whether Mst3 regulates neuronal migration through actin reorganization. Finally, we will identify and characterize the functions of downstream targets of Mst3 in neuronal migration. 在腦部發育的早期，神經元遷移是大腦皮層分層過程的關鍵步驟。神經元在分化之後,就轉變成雙極性的形態並在大腦皮層中進行遷移。大腦皮層分層的精確性對維持腦部的功能至關重要。dcx、flna和disc1等基因突變與X-連鎖無腦回症、腦室旁異位症、精神分裂症等神經系統疾病有密切關係。在胞外因子的刺激下，神經元可通過調節微管和肌動蛋白的動態結構進行遷移。然而，我們對控制神經元遷移的信號通路缺乏足夠的瞭解，尤其是關於細胞表面受體將胞外信號傳遞到細胞骨架的機理等方面。我們最近發現一種絲氨酸/蘇氨酸激酶－Mst3 能夠調節神經元的分化。有趣的是，當我們通過子宮內電穿孔技術降低Mst3的表達之後，大腦新皮層中的神經元輻射狀遷移明顯比正常延遲。我們還發現，Mst3能夠與肌動蛋白調節因子相互作用。這些結果表明，在大腦皮層發育過程中，Mst3可能通過調節肌動蛋白細胞骨架的動態結構來控制在神經元的遷移過程。在本研究計畫中，我們將會深入研究Mst3在神經元輻射狀遷移過程中的作用及其分子機理。我們首先將分析Mst3在神經元遷移不同階段的功能，然後會探討Mst3調控這些生物學過程的信號機理，並重點研究Mst3如何通過肌動蛋白細胞骨架來調節神經元遷移。最後，我們將鑒定Mst3的下游靶點及其在神經元遷移過程中作用。

660711.label: Realisation of objectives
660711.value: To study the spatiotemporal profile of Mst3 (mammalian Ste20-like kinase) expression in the mouse cerebral cortex (Objective 1), we first examined its expression profile in the mouse brain during development. Mouse brains were collected at different developmental stages and subjected to western blot analysis and in vitro kinase assay. Mst3 protein was prominently expressed in the cerebral cortex from the early embryonic stages through adulthood; its kinase activity was particularly robust from embryonic day 14–17, when extensive active neuronal migration occurs. To explicate the functional roles of Mst3 in radial migration in the mouse cerebral cortex (Objective 2), we examined the effect of Mst3 deletion from migrating neurons in the mouse cerebral cortex. In utero electroporation of Mst3 shRNA in the mouse cerebral cortex during the embryonic stage resulted in migratory defects, which were rescued by re-expression of an shRNA-resistant Mst3-expressing construct. Furthermore, the migratory defect was associated with abnormal neuronal morphology. Notably, control neurons formed a single leading process pointing toward the pial surface, whereas most Mst3-knockdown neurons in the intermediate zone exhibited disrupted neuronal polarity with no extended process. The finding that most Mst3-knockdown neurons migrated up into the cortical plate during the postnatal stages suggests that Mst3 knockdown delays rather than arrests neuronal migration. However, although the Mst3-knockdown neurons were able to migrate up into the cortical plate, their final positioning was abnormal and their dendrite development was impaired. These findings collectively suggest that Mst3 is important for the precise positioning and morphogenesis of neurons in the cerebral cortex. To determine whether Mst3 knockdown leads to altered cortical excitability, we conducted whole-cell recordings of pyramidal neurons in upper layers II–III. Intriguingly, the frequency of spontaneous excitatory postsynaptic currents was significantly lower in Mst3-knockdown pyramidal neurons than the control neurons. Therefore, Mst3 knockdown impairs the excitatory synaptic transmission of pyramidal neurons in the upper cortical layers. To investigate the signaling mechanisms underlying Mst3-regulated neuronal migration (Objective 3), we examined how Mst3 activity is regulated during neuronal migration and how it exerts its action. The prominent kinase activity of Mst3 in the embryonic mouse cortex prompted us to investigate whether Mst3-regulated radial migration is dependent on its kinase activity. To generate a kinase-dead Mst3 mutant (Mst3-KD), the ATP-binding site (Lys53) was substituted with arginine. Notably, re-expression of wild-type Mst3 (Mst3-WT) but not the KD mutant fully restored normal migration and neuronal morphology in Mst3-knockdown cortices. This finding suggests that Mst3 kinase activity is important for radial migration. A computational method identified various potential phosphorylation sites in Mst3 recognized by various kinases, including GSK3, Cdk5, JNK, MEK, and PKA. After treating cortical neurons with different kinase inhibitors, only the Cdk5 inhibitor dramatically reduced autophosphorylation and thus Mst3 activity. Furthermore, Mst3 kinase activity was reduced in Cdk5-knockout mouse brains. These results suggest that Cdk5 regulates Mst3 kinase activity. Indeed, active Cdk5 phosphorylated Mst3 and endogenous Mst3 phosphorylation was significantly attenuated in Cdk5-knockout brains. These findings suggest that Mst3 is phosphorylated by Cdk5 in vivo. Three sites on Mst3 were identified as potential Cdk5 phosphorylation sites: Ser4, Ser79, and Ser369. We subsequently generated phosphorylation-deficient mutants by mutating one of these sites to alanine. Mutation of only Ser79 abolished Cdk5-dependent Mst3 phosphorylation, indicating that Ser79 is the major Cdk5 phosphorylation site. To corroborate this result, a phospho-specific Mst3 antibody was raised against phosphorylated Mst3 at Ser79. The p-S79 Mst3 antibody specifically recognized phosphorylated Mst3 protein after Cdk5 phosphorylation. Concordantly, Mst3 phosphorylation at Ser79 was dramatically reduced in Cdk5-knockout mouse brains, corroborating Mst3 as a substrate of Cdk5 in vivo. To investigate whether Cdk5-dependent Mst3 phosphorylation is important for radial migration, we re-expressed Mst3-WT and Mst-S79A mutant in Mst3-knockdown cortices. Mst3-WT fully restored normal migration, whereas re-expression of the Mst3-S79A mutant failed to rescue the migration defects and altered the neuronal morphology of Mst3-knockdown neurons. Hence, the results indicate that Cdk5-dependent phosphorylation of Mst3 at Ser79 is important for Mst3 kinase activity and thus proper neuronal migration. We subsequently investigated how Mst3 and its kinase activity regulate neuronal migration. Mst3 was enriched in growing neurite tips of neurons, where it co-localized with F-actin staining. Notably, Mst3 knockdown in neurons substantially increased the ratio of F-actin to G-actin, suggesting that Mst3 regulates the polymerization status of the actin cytoskeleton. To determine how Mst3 regulates the morphology of migrating neurons, growth cone morphology was examined after introducing Mst3 shRNA into cortical neurons. Mst3 knockdown remarkably increased growth cone collapse. Interestingly, such defects were largely rescued by Y27632, a pharmacological inhibitor of RhoA signaling. Together with the interaction between Mst3 and RhoA, but not the other 2 important Rho-GTPases, these results suggest that RhoA is a downstream signaling molecule of Mst3. Importantly, Mst3 knockdown led to RhoA activation, whereas Mst3 overexpression inhibited RhoA activity in cultured neurons. Thus, these findings suggest that Mst3 plays important roles in the regulation of actin dynamics and RhoA. Mass spectrometry and 3D structural analysis identified 2 potential Mst3 phosphorylation sites on RhoA: Ser26 and Ser160. Furthermore, an in vitro phosphorylation assay confirmed that Mst3 phosphorylates RhoA at Ser26. Blocking the Mst3-dependent phosphorylation of RhoA at Ser26 enhanced its GTPase activity, suggesting that RhoA phosphorylation at Ser26 negatively regulates its activity. To determine whether Mst3-dependent RhoA phosphorylation is important for neuronal migration, we overexpressed RhoA-WT or RhoA-S26A in embryonic day 14 mouse brains. RhoA-WT overexpression significantly inhibited neuronal migration and disrupted normal neuronal polarization, whereas RhoA-S26A overexpression led to more severe defects in neuronal migration and polarization. Similar to the effect observed in Mst3-knockdown cortices, RhoA-WT– or RhoA-S26A–expressing migrating neurons exhibited abnormal morphology with no neuronal polarity or processes. Moreover, inhibition of RhoA activity by suppressing its protein expression restored migration and neuronal morphology defects in Mst3-knockdown neurons. These findings collectively reveal a critical role of Mst3 in the regulation of radial migration via the inhibition of RhoA activity.

660711.label: Major findings and research outcome
660711.value: In summary, this project investigated the functional roles of Mst3 during cerebral cortex development and its underlying cellular mechanisms. The results unraveled the key molecular basis (regulated by various kinases) underlying neuronal morphogenesis and migration. Roles of Mst3 in neuronal migration Subtle alterations in neuronal morphogenesis may underlie the pathophysiology of various neurological disorders. Therefore, it is important to understand how pyramidal neurons acquire their dendritic morphology after terminal translocation (Ip et al., Neuroscientist, 2014). We showed that Mst3 knockdown retards cortical neuronal migration, resulting in the mispositioning of Mst3-deficient neurons. Importantly, Mst3-depleted neurons exhibit aberrant dendrite morphology. These findings collectively suggest that Mst3 plays multiple roles in different cellular events during corticogenesis, including neuronal migration and dendrite development, in a cell-autonomous manner (Tang et al., J. Neurosci., 2014). Mst3 activity is regulated by Cdk5 phosphorylation Our results demonstrate that Cdk5 phosphorylates Mst3 at Ser79, which results in increased kinase activity. Blockade of Mst3 phosphorylation at Ser79 severely perturbed neuronal migration. Thus, the coordinated activation of the Cdk5/Mst3 pathway controls the precise initiation of neuronal migration (Tang et al., J. Neurosci., 2014; Ip et al., Neuroscientist, 2014). Mst3 regulates neuronal morphology and migration via the modulation of actin cytoskeletal dynamics Silencing Mst3 in cultured neurons enhanced RhoA activity and increased F-actin content, whereas depletion of RhoA protein expression rescued the radial migration defect of the Mst3-knockdown neurons. These results support the hypothesis that the inactivation of RhoA activity by Mst3 causes F-actin depolymerization, ultimately enabling the polarization of neurons and their exit from the intermediate zone, which is a critical initial step in radial migration (Tang et al., J Neurosci., 2014; Ip et al., Neuroscientist, 2014).

660711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
660711.value: The current project characterized the functional role of kinase Mst3 in the development of cerebral cortex. Specifically, we showed that Mst3 is critical for the polarity transition of neurons, which is a prerequisite of radial migration. Our preliminary findings suggest that Mst3 mediates its function through the modulation of RhoA-dependent actin dynamics. Further research should investigate the cellular mechanisms of Mst3. Accordingly, it will be of interest to identify the substrates of Mst3 during neuronal migration in vivo. To this end, we will characterize the spatiotemporal profiles of the phosphorylation of specific substrates in cortical neurons upon differentiation and in the mouse cerebral cortex upon development. After identifying the substrates of Mst3, we will determine whether the phosphorylation of these substrates is critical for the regulation of neuronal morphology and migration in the developing cerebral cortex. Furthermore, live imaging analysis will be conducted to evaluate the cytoskeletal dynamics of Mst3-deficient neurons during the migration phase. These results will provide insights into how the observed cytoskeletal changes are associated with neuronal migration during cerebral cortex development.

660711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
660711.value: The functions of the cerebral cortex require the precise wiring of distinct layer-specific neural circuitry. Neuronal migration, in which newborn neurons migrate radially to their final locations in the cerebral cortex, is one of the key steps that determine cortical function. Disruptions of neuronal migration are frequently associated with malformation of the cortex and neuropsychiatric diseases such as schizophrenia and autism. Proper neuronal migration requires the precise and rapid reorganization of the actin and microtubule cytoskeleton. However, the underlying signaling mechanisms controlling cytoskeletal reorganization are not well understood. The present study revealed that Mst3, a serine/threonine kinase that is highly expressed in the developing mouse brain, is essential for neuronal migration and the final positioning of neurons in the neocortex. Reducing Mst3 expression in the embryonic mouse cortex by in utero electroporation greatly delayed radial migration. Although the kinase activity of Mst3 is essential for its functions in the shaping and migration of neurons, it is regulated through its phosphorylation at serine 79 by a serine/threonine kinase, cyclin-dependent kinase 5 (Cdk5). Our results show that Mst3 regulates neuronal migration through modulating the activity of RhoA, which is critical for actin cytoskeletal reorganization. Mst3 phosphorylates RhoA at serine 26, thereby negatively regulating the activity of RhoA. Importantly, reducing RhoA expression reversed the defective neuronal migration in cortices with reduced Mst3 expression. Thus, our findings collectively suggest that Cdk5/Mst3 signaling regulates neuronal migration via actin dynamics that is dependent on RhoA activity.

661011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
661011.value: Genetic information in all known organisms flows from DNA to RNA, and then to protein. Transcription, the synthesis of RNA from a complementary DNA template, is a key control point in gene expression. Misregulation of transcription is a major factor in cancer and other human diseases. Thus, understanding transcription is an important component of understanding fundamental cellular processes and many human diseases. Our proposed studies aim to elucidate mechanisms of two critical processes during RNA polymerase II transcription elongation: the release of pyrophosphate after nucleotide addition, and the translocation of DNA and RNA across the polymerase surface. We propose to use computer simulations to study these two processes because computer simulations can model the dynamics through the atomic level interactions, while current experimental methods are inadequate to describe this dynamic process in sufficient details. For example, X-ray crystallography have revealed the structures for both pre- and post-translocation states, however, these are only static snapshots and the mechanisms by which transitions between these states occur remain poorly understood. In order to overcome the timescale gap between experiments and simulations, we will apply and develop novel computational algorithms such as Adaptive Seeding Scheme and Markov State Models to extract long timescale dynamics from short simulations. An important emphasis of our theoretical work will be to generate hypothesis that will be tested by experimental collaborators, and these experiments will further help refine our theoretical models. 661011.label: Major findings and research outcome
661011.value: Objective 1: To elucidate the mechanism of pyrophosphate release. We have constructed MSMs to study the PPi release process in pol II (J. Am. Chem. Soc., 134, 2399, (2012)). PPi release is an important step for pol II to enter the next round of the nucleotide addition, while its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. We have constructed MSMs to simulate how PPi releases from the pol II secondary channel. We show that the trigger loop can aid the PPi release mainly by increasing its intrinsic motion after the formation of PPi. Once PPi exits the active site and enters the secondary channel, several highly conserved positively charged residues on pol II can form favorable interactions with PPi and serve as hopping sites to help its release. We have also compared the mechanisms of PPi release between the eukaryotic pol II and the bacterial RNA polymerase (PloS Comp. Bio. 9(4): e1003020, (2013)). Objective 2: To elucidate the mechanism of translocation. To our knowledge, we have for the first time revealed the millisecond dynamics of pol II translocation at atomic resolution by using MD Simulations and MSMs (Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. U.S.A., 111, 7665, (2014)). We show that pol II translocation is driven purely by thermal energy and does not require the input of any additional chemical energy. Our simulations suggest an important role for the Bridge Helix: large thermal oscillations of this structural element facilitate the translocation by specific interactions that lower the free energy barriers between four metastable states. Among these states, we identify two novel intermediates that have not been previous captured by crystallography. The dynamic view of translocation presented in our study represents a substantial advance over the current understanding based on the static snapshots provided by X-ray structures of transcribing complexes. Objective 3: To develop novel computational tools that can bridge the gap between experimental and simulation timescales. We have successfully developed a new Multi-Resolution Transition Network model, called the Hierarchical Nyström Extension Graph (HNEG) Method, to construct MSMs for conformational dynamics. The HNEG method is based on an algebraic principle for matrix approximation that can effectively eliminate the noise in MSM construction (J. Chem. Phys., 138, 174106, (2013)). Our HNEG algorithm is shown to greatly improve over the popular kinetic clustering algorithm in various systems from small 1-residue alanine dipeptide to a large 263-residue β-lactamase protein (published as: J. Chem. Phys., 139, 121905, (2013)).

661011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
661011.value: Genetic information in all known organisms flows from DNA to RNA, and then to protein. Transcription, the synthesis of RNA from a complementary DNA template, is a key control point in gene expression. Misregulation of transcription is a major factor in cancer and other human diseases. Thus, understanding transcription is an important component of understanding fundamental cellular processes and many human diseases. Our research has elucidated molecular mechanisms of two critical processes during RNA polymerase II (pol II) transcription elongation: the release of pyrophosphate after nucleotide addition, and the translocation of DNA and RNA across the polymerase surface. For the pyrophosphate release, we show that several highly conserved positively charged residues on pol II serve as hopping sites to help the release of pyrophosphate. For translocation, we show that translocation is driven purely by thermal energy and does not require the input of any additional chemical energy. In order to overcome the timescale gap between experiments and simulations, we have successfully developed a new Multi-Resolution Transition Network model, called the Hierarchical Nyström Extension Graph Method, for constructing MSMs to study conformational dynamics. Our new method consistently provides the best performance among methods of its kind.

661111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
661111.value: Cyclin-dependent kinase 5 (Cdk5), a proline-directed serine/threonine kinase, plays central roles in a plethora of neuronal functions including neuronal migration, synapse development and plasticity. In light of the reported deregulation of Cdk5 activity in neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s disease, it is essential to elucidate the precise mechanisms by which Cdk5 activity is regulated. Unlike other members of the cyclin-dependent kinase family, Cdk5 is not activated by cyclins, but rather, is activated through its association with the neuronal specific activators, p35 and p39. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the regulation of Cdk5 activity in neurons remain unclear. We recently found that Cdk5 can undergo post-translational modification by S-nitrosylation, which involves the reaction of attaching a nitrogen monoxide group to the cysteine residue(s) of a protein, and that S-nitrosylated Cdk5 exhibits reduced kinase activity. Thus, we speculate that S-nitrosylation of Cdk5 may emerge to be a key molecular control of neuronal development and function. In this proposal, we plan to examine if Cdk5 can be S-nitrosylated in neurons by endogenous NO under basal condition, and will attempt to identify the extracellular cue(s) that can trigger Cdk5 S-nitrosylation. We will also determine the functional significance of S-nitrosylated Cdk5 in neuronal development. Finally, we will study how Cdk5 reciprocally regulates the nitric oxide signaling through modulating the phosphorylation and activity of neuronal nitric oxide synthase (nNOS), and explore its biological significance. 週期蛋白依賴性激酶5（Cdk5）是一種脯氨酸引導的絲氨酸/蘇氨酸激酶。它在神經元遷移、突觸發育及可塑性等方面發揮著重要的作用。過去的研究表明，Cdk5活性失調與老年癡呆症等多種神經退行性疾病有密切相關，因此闡明Cdk5活性的精確調節機制顯得尤為重要。與其他細胞週期蛋白依賴性激酶不同的是，Cdk5並不是由週期蛋白激活，而是通過與其神經元特異性的激活因子p35和p39結合而活化。然而，我們對於Cdk5在神經元中的活性調節機制還缺乏足夠的瞭解。我們最近發現，在翻譯後修飾過程中，Cdk5蛋白上的半胱氨酸殘基能夠結合一氧化氮（NO）而被巰基亞硝基化，從而降低Cdk5的活性。因此，Cdk5的巰基亞硝基化可能是調控神經元發育和功能的重要方式。在本研究計畫中，我們將會檢測Cdk5是否能夠在生理條件下被神經元內源性的NO巰基亞硝基化，並鑒定能夠誘導Cdk5巰基亞硝基化的胞外因子。同時，我們將研究Cdk5巰基亞硝基化在神經元發育過程中的功能。最後，我們將探討Cdk5如何通過改變一氧化氮合成酶的磷酸化及活性來調控一氧化氮信號通路，並研究這些調節過程的生物學意義。

661111.label: Realisation of objectives
661111.value: In order to determine how Cdk5 S-nitrosylation is regulated in neurons and identify the upstream signals (Objective 1), we investigated whether nitric oxide (NO) signaling regulates the levels of Cdk5 and its activator p35 as well as Cdk5 activity in hippocampal neurons. First, we overexpressed green fluorescent protein (GFP) in primary pyramidal neurons from the hippocampal CA1 region of 3-month-old wild-type (WT) and nNOS−/− mice. Genetic depletion of nNOS significantly decreased spine density and the percentage of mature spines, suggesting excitatory synapses were reduced. Furthermore, western blot analysis showed that the surface expressions of both GluA1 and GluN1 (AMPA and NMDA receptor subunits, respectively) were reduced in the adult nNOS−/− mouse hippocampus. In addition, the frequency of miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents (mEPSCs) in cultured nNOS−/− hippocampal neurons was reduced, confirming that NO signaling is critical for excitatory neurotransmission. Next, we examined how NO signaling regulates Cdk5/p35 levels and Cdk5 activity. The changes of Cdk5 activity in the hippocampus were determined by examining the Cdk5-dependent phosphorylation of two well-known Cdk5 substrates at synapses: WAVE1 and DARPP-32. nNOS−/− mice exhibited increased WAVE1 and DARPP-32 phosphorylation in the hippocampus, suggesting an increased hippocampal Cdk5 activity. Western blot analysis unexpectedly showed elevated p35 protein expression in the nNOS−/− mouse hippocampus, suggesting that NO also controls p35 protein level to restrict Cdk5 activity. To determine if p35 protein level is regulated by endogenous NO, cultured rat cortical neurons were treated with the nNOS inhibitor, L-NAME; the resultant blockade of NO production substantially increased p35 level. These results collectively indicate that NO negatively regulates p35 protein level and its associated Cdk5 activity, and that blocking NO production hyperactivates Cdk5 in the adult mouse hippocampus. To examine how NO regulates p35 protein level, cultured rat cortical neurons were treated with the physiological NO donor, S-nitrosoglutathione (GSNO), which decreased p35 protein level in a time-dependent manner; this was blocked by co-treatment with a proteasome inhibitor, MG132, indicating that the NO-induced reduction of p35 occurs via proteasome activity. Next, to determine if p35 can be S-nitrosylated by NO donors, HEK293T cell lysate overexpressing p35 was incubated with the physiological NO donors, GSNO or S-nitrosocysteine (SNOC), which readily S-nitrosylate p35. Amino acid sequence analysis of p35 revealed 8 potential cysteine residues as possible S-nitrosylation sites. Accordingly, we generated mutants in which each of the 8 cysteine residues or combinations thereof were substituted with alanine (C→A), which cannot be S-nitrosylated. The cell lysates of HEK293T cells transfected with p35-WT or C→A mutants were subjected to the biotin switch assay. Incubating the cell lysate with GSNO robustly S-nitrosylated p35-WT. In contrast, the C92A mutant drastically reduced p35 S-nitrosylation, suggesting that Cys92 is the major S-nitrosylation site. Next, we determined if p35 S-nitrosylation at Cys92 mediates its GSNO-induced degradation. p35-WT or p35-C92A was overexpressed in COS7 cells using an inducible TetOFF system. The addition of doxycycline, which inhibits p35 protein synthesis, rapidly decreased p35. Furthermore, the addition of GSNO accelerated the rate of p35 protein turnover; however, this effect was abolished in p35 mutants lacking the C92 S-nitrosylation site. To investigate the functional significance of Cdk5 S-nitrosylation in neuronal development (Objective 2), we examined the role of Cdk5 and its S-nitrosylation in synapse development. Cdk5 negatively regulates the morphogenesis of dendritic spines, where excitatory synapses reside. Given the abnormal p35 accumulation and Cdk5 hyperactivation in the nNOS−/− mouse hippocampus, reducing Cdk5/p35 activity should rescue the synaptic deficits observed upon NO production blockade. Accordingly, silencing p35 expression in cultured hippocampal neurons from WT and nNOS−/− mice significantly decreased the density of total protrusions and percentage of mature spines in the latter; these spine deficits were rescued by the inhibition of Cdk5 activity using p35-shRNA. Thus, Cdk5 hyperactivation is at least partially responsible for the spine defects observed in hippocampal neurons under impaired NO production. As p35 S-nitrosylation at Cys92 regulates its degradation and p35 loss influences spine morphogenesis, we examined if p35 S-nitrosylation at Cys92 regulates spine morphology. p35-WT overexpression in cultured rat hippocampal neurons reduced dendritic spine density and maturation, while GSNO abolished this effect. However, GSNO affected neither spine number nor maturation in p35-C92A–expressing neurons, indicating NO regulates dendritic spine morphology and density via p35 S-nitrosylation and thus Cdk5 activity modification. The cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA)-mediated phosphorylation of GluA1 and GluN1 is required for their surface expressions and synaptic strength maintenance. Cdk5 activity can inhibit GluA1 and GluN1 phosphorylation via the Cdk5/DARPP-32/PKA cascade. Given the association of Cdk5 hyperactivation with reduced GluA1 and GluN1 surface expressions triggered by NO production blockade, elevated p35 and the resultant Cdk5 activity plausibly contribute to the synaptic dysfunctions due to NO production blockade. Indeed, blocking NO production by L-NAME reduced GluA1 and GluN1 surface expression in cultured rat hippocampal neurons; inhibiting Cdk5 activity by roscovitine abolished these reductions. Further elucidating the role of p35 S-nitrosylation at Cys92 in surface GluA1 regulation, overexpression of p35-WT or p35-C92A with GluA1 constructs in HEK293T cells reduced GluA1 surface expression, consistent with the inhibitory role of Cdk5 on surface AMPA receptor trafficking. More importantly, GSNO treatment abolished the reduction of surface GluA1 in cells expressing p35-WT but not p35-C92A. This suggests that p35 S-nitrosylation at Cys92 determines p35 protein levels and regulates GluA1 surface expression in a p35-dependent manner. To confirm these findings at the functional level, electrophysiological studies were performed on cultured WT and nNOS−/− hippocampal neurons, in which p35 expression was silenced. Quantitative analysis showed that the inhibition of Cdk5 activity by p35-shRNA rescued the mEPSC frequency but not the amplitude deficits observed in nNOS−/− neurons. While mEPSC frequency indicates the probability of presynaptic glutamate neurotransmitter contacting postsynaptic AMPA receptors, mEPSC amplitude indicates synaptic size. Thus, the results may suggest that NO signaling regulates synapse number by modulating p35 protein level and affects synapse size via an independent mechanism. These findings collectively indicate that p35 accumulation and Cdk5 hyperactivation contribute to the synaptic defects generated upon NO production blockade and that the inhibition of Cdk5 activity can at least partially rescue synaptic failure in nNOS−/− neurons.

661111.label: Major findings and research outcome
661111.value: This project investigated how Cdk5/p35 S-nitrosylation regulates the development of excitatory synapses. The results unraveled the key molecular mechanisms of Cdk5 in neuronal and synapse development. NO and Cdk5 signaling regulate dendrite and synapse development We showed that Cdk5 regulates of dendritic spine formation through the phosphorylation of tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB), p70 ribosomal S6 kinase (S6K), and Axin (Lai et al., Nat Neurosci., 2012; Lai et al., J. Biol. Chem., 2015; Chen et al., PLoS One, 2015). Furthermore, we demonstrated that Cdk5 regulates activity-dependent dendrite development through the modulation of transcriptional regulation (Zhao et al., PLoS One, 2014; Zhao et al., Neurosci., 2015; Liang et al., J. Neurosci., 2015). NO signaling is critical for the precise regulation of Cdk5 activity during dendritic spine formation (Zhang et al., Nat Comm., 2015). S-nitrosylation reduces p35 level and decreases Cdk5 activity NO signaling negatively regulates Cdk5 activity through the S-nitrosylation of p35, resulting in its ubiquitin/proteasome-dependent degradation (Zhang et al., Nat Comm., 2015). In particular, p35 is S-nitrosylated by NO at Cys92, the blockade of which abolishes the NO-induced protein degradation of p35. Cdk5 inhibition reverses excitatory synaptic defects induced by blockade of NO signaling While blockade of NO production causes synaptic defects including decreased numbers of dendritic spines, levels of glutamate receptor subunits, and neurotransmission, inhibition of Cdk5 activity by p35 knockdown rescues these observed synaptic defects. Thus, NO acts as a molecular switch that controls dendritic spine morphogenesis, glutamate receptor surface expression, and synaptic efficacy by restricting Cdk5 activity in a p35 S-nitrosylation-dependent manner (Zhang et al., Nat Comm., 2015).

661111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
661111.value: The current project characterized the functional significance of NO and Cdk5 signaling in the regulation of synaptic strength. Specifically, we identified an important role of S-nitrosylation of p35 at Cys92 in the modulation of dendritic spine morphology, glutamate receptor levels, and neurotransmission efficiency. Furthermore, our preliminary results suggest that S-nitrosylation is important for the regulation of synaptic plasticity, which is the molecular basis of learning and memory. To further elucidate the functional roles of p35 S-nitrosylation in vivo, it will be important to generate a p35 Cys92 knock-in mouse, in which Cys92 is mutated to alanine to block S-nitrosylation. Thus, the effect of blocking the p35 S-nitrosylation at Cys92 on dendritic spine morphology, glutamate receptor levels, and neurotransmission can be examined in the mouse hippocampus. Furthermore, whether p35 S-nitrosylation at Cys92 is critical for hippocampal synaptic plasticity and hippocampal-dependent cognitive processes such as learning and memory can be examined.

661111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
661111.value: Neurons communicate with each other at specialized structures called synapses. The precise regulation of the structure and function of synapses ensures proper communication among neurons and hence brain functioning. Structural and functional changes of excitatory synapses are often accompanied by changes in the number, shape, and neurotransmitter receptor contents of dendritic spines, where excitatory synapses reside. This requires the coordinated activity and functions of different synaptic proteins. The functions of synaptic proteins are precisely controlled by various post-translational modifications. This study shows that the S-nitrosylation (a post-translational modification) of p35, which is the activator of cyclin-dependent kinase 5 (Cdk5), induced by nitric oxide (NO) is important for the regulation of excitatory synaptic strength. Blockade of NO signaling resulted in deficits in the structure and function of synapses as indicated by a reduction of the number of dendritic spines and surface expression of glutamate receptor subunits as well as decreased neuronal communication. Furthermore, reduced NO production led to an aberrant increase in the phosphorylation of numerous synaptic substrates of Cdk5 and its activity. Our results show that NO S-nitrosylates p35 protein, causing its degradation and ultimately reducing Cdk5 activity. Silencing p35 protein in hippocampal neurons partially reverses the synaptic deficits induced by NO blockade. These findings collectively demonstrate that p35 S-nitrosylation by NO signaling is critical for regulating the strength of synapses in the hippocampus.

661611.label: Project Objectives
661611.value: Characterize the microbial community structures of natural biofilms developed from different tidal areas by using 16S amplicon sequencing. 661611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
661611.value: Biofilm (an aggregate of microorganisms enmeshed in a matrix of extracellular polymeric substances on submerged surface) has long been suggested to influence the settlement response of many marine benthic invertebrate larvae. It has been documented that biofilms from different areas, tidal levels, or of different ages showed different attractiveness or repellence to the larvae. Much research effort has been devoted to study the relationship between biofilm microbial community structure and larval settlement response. Early studies relied on cultivation technique to isolate microbes from biofilms for testing their settlement inductiveness. This approach is limited by the low percentage of cultivable microbes (less than 1%) in the natural environment. Some recent investigations employ nucleic acid-PCR-based fingerprinting approach or clone library to increase the coverage of microbial community. However, these methods are prone to PCR biases, leading to an underestimation of the true microbial diversity and an unrevealed portion of the microbial community. Furthermore, in many cases, functional information is lacking. Owing to these, an in-depth and exhaustive study of the genetic materials from the entire microbial community samples (i.e. metagenome) is essential for understanding the composition and function of natural biofilms. In this study, we propose to 1) characterize the microbial community of natural biofilms developed from different tidal areas and of different ages by using the high-throughput pyrosequencing approach commercialized by 454 Life Sciences; 2) to study the functional differences between these biofilms by comparing their metagenomes; and 3) to correlate larval settlement response with microbial community structure and metagenomes. This study will represent the first set of comparative metagenomic study on natural biofilms, which provides valuable information on functions and community composition of biofilms developed at different environments. It will also enable a better understanding on how biofilms regulate larval settlement, which is of great interest for marine ecologists and for applications on biofouling control and aquaculture. 生物膜是一層由微生物及微生物分泌於胞外的聚合物組成的薄膜，一段聚集在水中物體的表面。早期研究表明生物膜能影響很多無脊椎動物幼蟲的定殖。不同水域、潮水高度或不同生長期的生物膜對幼蟲有不同的吸引或排斥作用。有大量研究探索生物膜的微生物群體結構和幼蟲定殖的關係。早期研究通過純化並培養生物膜中的微生物，從而研究它們對幼蟲定殖的誘導作用。但由於自然環境中可培養的微生物所佔比例太少（低於1%），所以以這手法作研究策略受到很大的限制。近期有研究通過基於PCR的核酸指紋技術或克隆文庫技術來提高研究微生物群體的覆蓋率，但這些技術容易受到PCR偏性的影響，所以在一般情況下也低估了微生物的多態性，並且無法揭示整個微生物群體。另外，很多情況下也無法對微生物進行功能研究。因此，我們需要對生物膜微生物群體整體遺傳物質（即宏基因組）進行深入且詳盡的研究，從而清楚地了解生物膜的結構和功能。在這項研究中，我們計劃：1）利用高通量454焦磷酸測序技術測定不同潮間和不同生長期的生物膜微生物群體基因組序列及群體結構。2）比較不同生物膜樣品宏基因組序列，從而研究它們功能上的差異。3）研究幼蟲定殖與生物膜微生物群體結構及宏基因組的相關性。這項研究乃首次利用比較宏基因組學技術研究天然生物膜，讓我們更清楚地認識生物膜對幼蟲定殖的調節作用，並且可以應用於生物污垢控制和水產養殖產業。

661611.label: Realisation of objectives
661611.value: To realize our objectives, we developed the first batch of biofilms on polystyrene Petri dishes by submerging the dishes at intertidal (~1 m above the mean low-water level) and subtidal area (~1 m below the mean low-water level) of Port Shelter, Hong Kong (22°19’ N, 114°16’ E) during two seasons: spring (May) and summer (August). The four biofilms developed under this design were referred to as ‘spring intertidal’, ‘spring subtidal’, ‘summer intertidal’ and ‘summer subtidal’, respectively. The Petri dishes were retrieved after 7 days of submersion and the biofilms were used for microbial community analysis, larval settlement bioassays, determination of bacterial density and total organic carbon, and metabolite extraction. Results showed highly diverse biofilm bacterial communities that varied with season and tidal level. Over 3,000 operational taxonomic units with species estimates of up to 8,000 species were recovered in a biofilm sample, which is by far the highest number recorded in sub-tropical marine biofilms. Laboratory assays confirmed that cyrids of the barnacle Balanus amphitrite preferred to settle on the intertidal rather than subtidal biofilms. This preference was independent of the biofilm bacterial density or biomass but was probably related to the biofilm community structure and was likely chemically mediated. Chemical extracts of the biofilms were analyzed by ultra-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry and principal component analysis suggested that the possible metabolites that lead to the cyprid settlement preference might be amino acid-related compounds. The key findings were published in ISME J (top journal in ecology) as Chung et al 2010. The second batch of biofilms was developed on polystyrene Petri dishes at the same location in the intertidal and subtidal levels in July 2012. After submerged for 6 and 12 days, the Petri dishes were retrieved and the biofilms were used for larval settlement bioassay, microscopy analysis and DNA extraction. The larval settlement assay showed that B. amphitrite cyprids preferred settle on the intertidal biofilms rather than the subtidal ones, regardless the duration of development. Pyrosequencing the metagenomes of the four natural biofilm samples generated enormous sequence datasets for comparative metagenomic analysis. Taxonomic classification by MG-RAST revealed highly diverse (up to 600 genera covering bacteria, archaea, and eukaryotes) but different community compositions in biofilms varied with biofilm age and tidal level. Fourteen genera were highly enriched in the intertidal biofilms while 12 for the subtidal biofilms. Biofilms developed at these two tidal levels showed different COG functions. Nine abundant functions were highly enriched in the intertidal biofilms and 11 for the subtidal biofilms were detected (Lee et al 2014). Many of the microbes detected in our biofilm samples and their functions were reported to be related with larval settlement and biofilm formation, likely explaining the differential inductiveness of biofilms to the larvae and key findings were published in Microb Ecol (Lee et al 2014). This is the first report applying metagenomic analysis to characterize natural intertidal and subtidal biofilms and linking specific functional pathways with larval settlement patterns, which provides important basis to understand the interactions among environment, biofilm and larval settlement. The key findings were published in our paper in Scientific Report (Zhang et al., 2013). The third set of biofilms were developed in Thuwal cold seeps to test our hypothesis that that initiation of the biofilm formation and spreading mode of microbial structures differs between the cold seep and the other aquatic environments. PS and PVC plates were deployed on seepage outlets on the eastern bank of the pool (22.2836 N, 38.8983 E) by a remotely operated vehicle while the others were placed in the brine pool (22.2834 N, 38.8979 E), with two sites being about 50 m apart. Due to operational and technical constrains of ROV diving, the two platforms were deployed on different days but retrieved on the same day, resulting in different duration of biofilm development; the durations for biofilm development were 72 h and 100 h in the brine pool and on the seep vent, respectively. Biofilms on the same surface areas of each substrate type were immediately harvested for DNA extraction and laboratory analysis. Biofilms on different substrates at two deployment sites differed morphologically, with the vent biofilms having higher microbial abundance and better structural features than the pool biofilms. Microbes in the pool biofilms were more taxonomically diverse and mainly composed of various sulfate-reducing bacteria whereas the vent biofilms were exclusively dominated by sulfur-oxidizing Thiomicrospira. These results suggest that the redox environments at the deployment sites might have exerted a strong selection on microbes in the biofilms at two sites whereas the types of substrates had limited effects on the biofilm development. The key findings were published in Scientific Report (Lee et al 2014). The fourth set of biofilms were developed in Thuwal cold seeps on six different substrates including aluminum (Al), polyether ether ketone (PEEK), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), polytetrafluoroethene (PTFE), stainless steel (SS), and titanium (Ti) at two locations: the brine pool and the normal bottom water adjacent to Thuwal cold seeps II. A comparison between the biofilms developed in the brine and NBW based on metagenomic datasets identified polysaccharide fermentation, nitrate reduction, and proteolysis as enriched functions for brine biofilms. The genomes of one novel deltaproteobacterium and of one epsilonproteobacterium in the 6-day brine biofilms were reconstructed. The deltaproteobacterium possessed complete polysaccharide degradation and fermentation pathways, whereas the epsilonproteobacterium was a versatile nitrate reducer. Both the abundance and the expression level of key functional genes of these two bacteria were higher in 6d-brine biofilms than 3d-brine biofilms. Assessing environmental parameters, taxonomic successions, microbial co-occurrence relationships, and molecular analyses, we proposed that 1) anaerobic polysaccharide fermentation activated in 6d-brine biofilms is important for energy production, 2) nitrate becomes the preferred electron acceptor when oxygen declines during biofilm development, and 3) the interaction between polysaccharide fermentation, proteolysis, and nitrate reduction facilitates resource recycling. Species sorting, gene expression regulation and inter-species interactions are associated with biofilm development to circumvent carbon source limitations. In conclusion, we show for the first time in situ mechanistic evidence that biofilm development confers microbial adaptation to extreme subsurface conditions. The key findings were published in Env Microb. (Zhang et al. 2015). Furthermore, we obtained three groups of biofilms: the switched biofilms included S-brine and S-NBW biofilms; the brine biofilm included 3d-brine and 6d-brine biofilms; and the NBW biofilms included 3d-NBW and 6d-NBW biofilms. Analyses of 16S rRNA genes of 71 biofilm samples suggested that the microbial composition of biofilms established in new environments was determined by both the source community and the incubation conditions. Moreover, a comparison of 18 metagenomes provided evidence for biofilm community assembly that was primarily based on functional features rather than taxonomic identities; metal ion resistance and amino acid metabolism were the major species sorting determinants in the succession of biofilm communities. Genome binning and the metabolic reconstruction of Marinobacter sp. and Oleispira sp. further demonstrated metal ion resistance and amino acid metabolism as functional traits conferring the habitat generalists to survive in both the brine pool and the NBW. The present study shed new light on microbial community assembly in special habitats and bridged the gaps in the species sorting theory. The detailed findings can be found in our publication in Molecular Ecology (also one of top journal) (Zhang et al in press).

661611.label: Major findings and research outcome
661611.value: 1.1 We deciphered the extreme complexity of marine natural biofilm: When high-throughput sequencing technology became available for microbial ecology study, we successfully designed primers that are suitable for analyzing extremely complex community structures of both bacteria and archaea, but more importantly overcame the sequencing bias (long-lasting problems) caused by using inappropriate primers for analyzing microbial phyla in environmental samples. Using high throughput sequencing and bioinformatics analysis, we discovered that the number of microbial taxa in natural biofilms was almost 100 times higher than what had been reported, which revolutionized the general views on microbial community complexity in natural environment. We discovered that the natural biofilm could contain at least 10-100 times more species than the highest number reported previously. We showed the drastic community shifts between young and old natural biofilm development and found that both young and mature biofilm are dominated by different specific microbial taxa with specific ecological functions. Our novel results clearly showed that the changes in microscopic environment within this layer determined the dynamic nature of microbial community structure in these biofilms although a biofilm is only a thin layer of “biomaterials or a complex biological community” on a marine surface. 1.2 We showed the strong impact of dynamic changes in the biofilm on the initial colonization of marine benthos: With a comprehensive understanding of the dynamic nature of natural biofilms, we studied the impact of biofilms that were developed under different environmental conditions or at different developmental stages on the initial colonization of marine benthos; we discovered the bioactivity of biofilms were related to metabolitic processes of microbes in the biofilm. However, the chemical profiles of natural biofilm were very complicate. With limited information on marine bacterial metabolites available, it is almost impossible to faithfully link chemical profiles of biofilms with larval settlement behavior. As such, we have devoted substantial efforts in developing secondary metabolite fingerprinting database of marine bacteria, using bacterial isolates in our bacterial culture collection. The database has been made available world-wide as an online database, which can substantially aid our future studies to establish a solid relationship between biofilm dynamics and the initial colonization of various marine benthic organisms as well as discovered both inductive and inhibitive microbial groups.

661611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
661611.value: - over the last 4 years, we have developed the natural biofilm in subtidal zone environment and extracted the DNA and RNA from those samples, we are now conducting metagenomic sequencing work of these samples, which will allow us to reveal changes in microbial community structure and function over a longer-term. To support this ongoing project, we are developing a new grant proposal to be submitted to RGC in 2016; - through our work, we come to realize that signaling processes and mechanisms of interaction between microbes in natural biofilm have never been really explored. As such, we have submitted a new GRF proposal in 2015 to study signal molecules, particularly ones from uncultivable bacteria using metagenomic sequencing and genome binning techniques.

661611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
661611.value: When dissolved organic matters in water column attach to marine surfaces, they create localized nutrient-rich environment that attract microbes to attach and promote microbial growth, leading to the formation of biofilms made of very complex microbial community and diverse macro- and micro-molecules. Chemical signals (secondary metabolites) produced by microbes in biofilm attract or drive away the initial colonizers of marine sessile organisms, which determines early community structure of marine benthic ecosystem and future ecological functionality. Unfortunately, dynamic nature of marine biofilms and the response of microbes in biofilms to changing environmental conditions have never been closely examined before. In this project, we have used high-throughput sequencing technique and bioinformatics tools to characterize the microbial community of natural biofilms developed from different tidal areas, different ages, different environmental conditions. We founds that microbial diversity in biofilms was 10-100X higher than what has been reported in the past, indicating that natural biofilms are extremely complex ecosystem. Through detailed analysis of genes and metabolitic pathways of microbes in biofilm, we also gained substantial insight into the molecular mechanisms of biofilm formation, development, and functions. The information gained here provided solid basis for further study of biofilm development and how biofilms regulate larval settlement.

661911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
661911.value: 化石燃料在全球范围内的广泛利用使得大气中温室气体二氧化碳（CO2）的浓度增加，从而导致全球变暖以及其他环境方面的严重后果。在海洋中，微观的单细胞藻类——浮游植物可以通过光合作用将CO2转化为有机碳，就像陆地生态系统中的树木和草。尽管大部分被合成的碳在水体表层被呼吸利用和再循环，但还有一小部分有机碳通过沉降的颗粒物从水表层被输送到深海。 这些沉降的颗粒物包含老的或死的浮游植物细胞，摄食者的粪粒和其他一些有机聚集体。由于这些输送过程通过生物体将有机碳泵出（输出）到海洋的内部，因此这些过程叫做“生物泵”。生物泵过程降低了海洋上部水体中CO2的浓度和分压（pCO2），从而促进大气CO2向海洋扩散。 硅藻是海洋中最重要的初级生产者。它们具有由硅质形成的细胞壁，被浮游动物摄食后，硅石不能被消化，使硅藻的细胞壁存在于浮游动物的粪粒中。硅的含量在不同的硅藻物种中是不同的，即使是同一藻种，在不同的生长条件下硅的含量也不同。硅含量影响硅藻在水体中的浮力和沉降，也影响以它们为食的浮游动物的粪粒的沉降率。令人意外的是，目前还没有开展研究来调查硅藻硅含量对浮游动物摄食，生长，繁殖，粪粒生产力等方面的影响，以及跟他们相关联的浮游植物、浮游动物种群演替，食物网动态，颗粒沉降和碳循环等方面的影响。本研究计划将会开展室内和野外实验，第一次检验硅藻硅含量如何影响桡足类的表现（桡足类是一种小型甲壳类浮游动物，一般占超过2/3的总浮游动物生物量）。通过研究桡足类在不同硅化的硅藻作为食物的条件下的摄食行为、生长生理和繁殖生物学，我们会更好地理解桡足类在春季硅藻水华和后水华时期环境条件下的种群动态。由于摄食者粪粒的沉降速度和降解力取决于其食物的类型，浓度和质量（特别是本研究所关注的硅化水平），因此非常有必要调查浮游动物以不同硅藻为食物的情况下所生产的粪粒的数量和质量。本研究的结果或许能够解释以往在不同地区所检测到的海洋表层的初级生产力与深海颗粒有机物的输出通量之间的非耦合性。 此外，本研究之所以比较切题与硅藻在香港近岸海区是最占优势的群体有关。大型硅藻水华频繁发生在夏天，尤其在位于珠江河口外面的香港南部水域。研究会对未来关于香港水体水华的发展机制的模型和关于珠江流域营养盐和有机污染输入后果的物理-生物地球化学耦合模型的建立提供必不可少的信息，并协助对富营养化影响的管理。

661911.label: Realisation of objectives
661911.value: 1) We tested the Si content of diatoms grown under different conditions (different SiO4 concentration in media and different growth rate adjusted by light) and revealed that a model species Thalassiosira weissflogii had higher Si content when they grow slow under low light. T. weissflogii stop dividing at low media Si, but its cellular Si remained high. On the other hand, Phaeodactylum tricornutum, another common model species kept growing at Si depleted condition with reduced cellular Si contents. 2) We conducted a series of experiments using Thalassiosira weissflogii with different silicon contents to feed copepods. Copepod feeding rate, growth rate, egg production and hatching success, as well as fecal pellet production, sinking and degradation rates were measured. 3) We have also conducted field study during a research cruise on board a Japanese research vessel (RV Tansei Maru) to study the diatom silicification and its effect on zooplankton grazing during spring bloom in the Oyashio region. Spring bloom occurs annually in the Oyashio region in the northwestern Pacific Ocean. We have hypothesized that because the Si contents of diatoms at the early stage of the bloom and the decay stage of the bloom are different, the grazing impact of mesozooplankton, and consequently the carbon flux through direct sinking and zooplankton fecal pellets will be different. We surveyed two stations that were at different stages of the bloom and measured BSi concentration, as well as zooplankton grazing and fecal pellet production rates.

661911.label: Major findings and research outcome
661911.value: Results of laboratory experiment using a copepod, Parvocalanus crassirostris feeding on Thalassiosira weissflogii with different silica contents showed that copepod strongly preferred cells with low silica content over high silica-containing cells, with the ingestion rate on low silica diatoms being 2-3 times higher than that on high silica diatoms. Fecal pellet production rate was significantly higher for copepods feeding on highly silicified cells. Furthermore, copepod growth rate, egg production rate and hatching success were all severely compromised under a high silica diatom diet. Females of P. crassirostris feeding on a low silica diatom diet produced an average 90 eggs during a one day incubation, while those fed with high silica diatoms produced only 11 eggs per day. Similarly, the hatching success during a 3-day period was 82 ± 17% and 23 ± 36% for the low and high silica diatom treatments, respectively, with zero success observed in ~65% of the females. Our findings have important ecological implications for the biological pump and may alter our previous view of the role of diatoms in planktonic food webs and the role of the degree of silicification in controlling amount of POC flux to deeper waters. In a field study conducted during a spring bloom in the Oyashio region, we studied the diatom silicification and its effect on zooplankton grazing and fecal pellet production at early and late stage of the spring bloom. Our results partially supported our hypothesis. Diatoms dominanted phytoplankton community at the early stage of the bloom and zooplankton grazing and fecal pellet production were high. At the late stage of the bloom, other phytoplankton, such as haptophytes, were also abundant and zooplankton grazing and fecal pellet production rates were comparatively lower. However, we were not able to measure diatom cellular Si content due to technical difficulty, and consequently failed to establish a relationship between zooplankton grazing and fecal production rates and diatom Si contents. Future studies are needed to develop a quantitive method to measure diatom Si contents in field and to conduct mesocosmal simulation experiment to test our hypothesis through artificially induced diatom blooms. Due to the departure of the student, our paper publication was delayed. Two papers are currently in revision and preparation (expected submission time: June 2016).

661911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
661911.value: I will develop a new proposal to further study the diatom Si physiology and metabolism in coming years. We are working on gene expression of different genes for two diatoms, Phaeodactylum tricornutum and Thalassiosira pseudonana, which show different Si physiology. Genes, such as rbcL (Rubisco, carbon fixation), CDKs (cell cycle) and SIT1 and PtSIT2 (silicic acid transporters) will be monitored through the growth phases of Si replete and Si depleted condition using qPCR to elucidate the control mechanism of different model of growth when Si is scarce.

661911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
661911.value: Diatoms are the most important primary production in marine ecosystems. They are the major food for zooplankton and contribute significantly to vertical POC flux through sinking of dead cells, aggregates and zooplankton fecal pellets. The silica content of diatoms varies among different species and within a species growing under different environmental conditions and physiological status. However, to-date there has been no investigation of the effect of diatom silica content on zooplankton grazing, growth and reproduction. We conducted a series of experiments using the diatom Thalassiosira weissflogii with different silica content achieved by growth under high and low light and these cells were fed to several zooplankton species. Our results show that copepods strongly prefer cells with low silicon content over high silicon-containing cells. At the same time, fecal pellet production rate is significantly higher for copepods fed by highly silicified cells. Furthermore, copepod growth rate, egg production rate and hatching success are all severely compromised under high silicon diatom diet. Our findings imply that herbivorus zooplankton may not be able to feed on diatom efficiently during diatom blooms.

662011.value: 脊髓损伤后的功能恢复

662011.label: Project Objectives
662011.value: To assess the effects of inhibition of PTEN on anatomical and functional regeneration of descending axons after C5 contusion injury. To assess the effects of inhibition of PTEN on anatomical and functional regeneration of descending axons after T12 crush injury.
rows: To assess the effects of inhibition of PTEN on anatomical and functional regeneration of descending axons after C5 contusion injury.
To assess the effects of inhibition of PTEN on anatomical and functional regeneration of descending axons after T12 crush injury.

662011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
662011.value: To achieve functional recovery after spinal cord injury, injured axons must regenerate past the injury and reform functional connections. Even limited regeneration could improve function, enhance quality of life, and decrease the burden of disability for people who have suffered spinal cord injuries. Our recent studies result in major breakthroughs in that we discovered molecular pathways that can be targeted to induce robust axon regeneration in the adult CNS. The initial studies showed that inhibiting a molecular pathway called phosphatase tensin homolog (PTEN), which is involved in cell growth control, induces regeneration of damaged axons in the optic nerve. My further experiments demonstrate that targeting the same molecular pathway induced remarkable long distance axon regeneration in the injured spinal cord. These initial findings form a unique basis to assess the functional recovery of axon regeneration following spinal cord injury. I will test whether blockade of PTEN using genetic approaches will promote anatomical regeneration and functional recovery in rodent spinal cord injury models. Two clinically relevant spinal cord injury paradigms will be used: C5 contusion and T12 spinal cord crush. T12 crush injury transects all passing descending axons at the lesion level of the spinal cord and is ideal for assessing anatomical regeneration and locomotion recovery. Additionally, we will utilize a C5 contusion model and assess recovery of upper extremity function. Specific aims include: 1. To assess the effects of inhibition of PTEN on anatomical and functional regeneration of descending axons after C5 contusion injury. 2. To assess the effects of inhibition of PTEN on anatomical and functional regeneration of descending axons after T12 crush injury. Our proposed experiments might lead to the development of new repair strategies of promoting axon regeneration and functional recovery after both acute and chronic spinal cord injury. 脊髓损伤通常造成永久的功能丧失，神经轴突再生并形成连接提供了恢复功能的可能性。即使是有限的再生也可能提高病人生活质量，减轻生活压力。我们最近发现抑制一个基因PTEN可以促使视神经和皮质脊髓束神经轴突再生。这为我们去进一步研究脊髓损伤的功能恢复提供了独有的基础。 我将要用遗传学的办法去抑制PTEN，来检验是否能在小鼠脊髓损伤模型中促进神经再生和功能恢复。我会使用两种和临床相关的模型：颈5的挫伤和胸12的全夹断。 颈5挫伤便于测试上肢的精细功能恢复，而胸12全夹断有利于检测解刨学意义上的下行轴突再生和可能的运动功能恢复。 我们提出的实验可能会同时为短期和长期的脊髓损伤患者帮助提供新的治疗手段。

662011.label: Realisation of objectives
662011.value: We used conditional genetic deletion as in our original experiments. Accordingly, we assessed recovery of forelimb motor function following moderate contusion injuries at C5. Forepaw motor function was assessed for 3 months post-injury using tasks that assess forepaw flexor function, including the grip strength meter and the hanging task. All assessments were carried out in a blinded fashion. At the end of the 3-month testing period, mice received intra-cortical BDA injections to trace the CST. Mice that received AAV-Cre to delete Pten showed significantly enhanced recovery of forelimb motor function on both tasks in comparison to either lesion only or vector controls. These findings suggest that deletion of Pten in the sensorimotor cortex does improve recovery of CST mediated functions. We have completed the histological assessment for this experiment and the results indicate that Pten deletion does enhance CST axon growth following cervical contusion. In controls (either lesion only or vector controls), the main component of CST axons in the dorsal column terminated in characteristic retraction balls at the rostral boundary of the lesion. In dramatic contrast, in AAV-Cre treated mice, there was a robust bloom of CST axons rostral to the injury, and many axons extended into the lesion site and for a few hundred µm beyond. We also assessed whether Pten deletion after spinal cord injury would re-initiate CST growth after a complete thoracic crush injury. We injected AAV-Cre or AAV-GFP into one side of the hemisphere 12 months after the initial injury. CST was then traced 4 months later by BDA. In the controls rarely could a few fibers be seen approaching the injury site. In Pten-deleted mice, we did not see the obvious extension of the main CST bundle. However, a few axons grew into and even beyond the lesion, up to 1.5 mm. 7 months after the AAV-Cre injection, the main CST bundle extended up to the boundary of the lesion, and numerous axons regrew into the injury site and across the lesion for up to 3 mm. Some synapses reformed by regenerating axons could be detected by immunostaining of BDA, VGlut1, and Homer1. Unfortunately, we did not observe locomotor functional recovery from these mice. We believe one of the reasons could be that the CST does not play a major role in locomotion. We currently continue working on other descending axons and examine whether the regeneration can contribute to the locomotor recovery.

662011.label: Major findings and research outcome
662011.value: 1. Pten deletion after injury enables CST regeneration and enhances recovery of forelimb motor function. Part of the study is currently under preparation for publication. 2. Pten deletion promotes regrowth of corticospinal tract axons after chronic spinal cord injury, even at one year after lesion. Part of the study has been published in Journal of Neuroscince 2015 (please refer to Part C, 8, No 1). 3. Pten and Socs3 co-deletion promotes the injured optic nerve to regenerate and reform active synapses with suprachiasmatic neurons. Part of the study has been published in Neurobiology of Disease 2014 (please refer to Part C, 8, No 2).

662011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
662011.value: Our proof of principle experiments demonstrated that boosting the intrinsic growth capacity in neurons enable a robust regeneration, reconnection, and functional outcome. We are currently moving into two directions. One is to examine whether a functional recovery can be achieved in a chronically-injury model. Second is to develop non-genetic approaches including shRNAs, and small molecules to enhance growth-promoting signaling including mTOR activity. We will further examine whether these novel approaches can produce similar effects as Pten knockout. The future development will test whether it is possible to induce regeneration and functional recovery with a treatment delivered in a therapeutically relevant time frame and a translational manner.

662011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
662011.value: As one of the long descending tracts controlling voluntary movement, the CST plays an important role for functional recovery after spinal cord injury. The regeneration of CST has been a major challenge in the field. We developed a strategy to modulate Pten/mTOR signaling in adult corticospinal motor neurons in the post-injury paradigm. It promoted robust regeneration of injured axons past the lesion in a mouse model of spinal cord injury. Even when treatment was delayed up to 1 year after the original injury, axon regeneration can still be achieved. The results considerably extend the window of opportunity for regenerating CST axons severed in spinal cord injuries, and demonstrate that modulating neuronal mTOR as a potential strategy for axon regeneration after spinal cord injury.

662211.label: Project Objectives
662211.value: The main objective of this proposal is to test the general hypothesis that myogenic Ca2+ signals play an essential role in normal skeletal muscle development in intact developing zebrafish. This objective has been divided in three testable sub-hypotheses. Sub-Hypothesis #1: To test whether myogenic Ca2+ signals are generated at different times, in different locations, with different dynamics, and by different mechanisms, and that as a result they have specific triggers, targets and roles with respect to muscle development and function. To accomplish this task, we will continue to use complementary luminescent- and fluorescence-based Ca2+ imaging to characterize Ca2+ signaling during muscle cell differentiation, as well as agents and localized uncaging techniques to selectively trigger and block the Ca2+ signals identified. In addition to SMCs, we will expand our study to include fast and medial-fast muscle cells, and extend our study of all muscle cell types to 96 hpf. Sub-Hypothesis #2: To test whether cytoplasmic Ca2+ signals play a role in regulating the assembly of the contractile apparatus and its attachment to the vertical myosepta. Sub-hypothesis #3: To test whether dystrophin plays a role in normal myogenic Ca2+ signaling, both during muscle differentiation and function. To accomplish this we plan to image Ca2+ signaling in the dystrophin-deficient zebrafish mutant sapje, and by introducing morpholinos targeted to block dystrophin gene expression.
