662211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
662211.value: Dynamic localized changes in cytosolic and nuclear Ca2+ concentration have been reported to play a critical regulatory role in different aspects of skeletal muscle differentiation. Details of the precise mechanisms through which these myogenic Ca2+ signals contribute to the overall orchestration of muscle development, however, remain elusive. A variety of Ca2+ release channels/receptors have been implicated in this complex process. These include voltage- and store-operated channels, inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate and ryanodine receptors, and most recently identified, two pore channels. These channels/receptors are associated with a variety of Ca2+ stores, including the extracellular space, the sarcoplasmic and nucleoplasmic reticula, and acidic organelles, respectively, all of which in turn may contribute to the spatial and temporal characteristics of the myogenic Ca2+ signaling signature. The diversity of these channels/receptors and stores also suggests that a variety of intracellular and extracellular triggers may modulate Ca2+ release, thus adding a further degree of complexity to understanding the contribution made by Ca2+-mediated signaling to myogenic differentiation. Furthermore, slow, fast and medial-fast muscle cell types all contribute to adult skeletal muscle and it is not yet clear whether each cell type has a specific developmental Ca2+ signaling signature. The differentiation-dependent targets of the various Ca2+ signals have also proven to be difficult to identify. These targets may be located in either the nucleus or the cytoplasm, and may involve gene expression, or sarcomeric protein assembly and attachment, respectively. With regard to the latter, the situation is complex as functional contraction appears to be a key component of differentiation. Furthermore, the absence of the membrane-associated cytoskeletal protein dystrophin has long been associated with a loss of both function and Ca2+ homeostasis in mature muscle cells, suggesting a possible link between dystrophin and myogenic Ca2+ signaling. Thus, we plan to fully characterize the Ca2+ signaling signatures, from a temporal, spatial and mechanistic viewpoint, generated by the various types of differentiating skeletal muscle cells in intact zebrafish embryos. We also plan to test the hypothesis that these signals are essential for normal muscle differentiation. For example, we propose to explore the relationship between these signals and: The assembly of the major sarcomeric proteins; the attachment of contractile elements to the vertical myosepta; the expression of selected Ca2+-sensitive genes; and the role of dystrophin in early muscle development and function. 鈣濃度於細胞質和細胞核內的局部動態變化已發現在不同方面的骨骼肌分化中發揮著重要的調節作用。但是，這些生肌鈣信號於提升整體的肌肉發展的詳細精確機制仍有代理解。這個複雜的過程已發現跟各種鈣釋放通道/受體有牽連。這些通道/受體包括電感性離子通道、鈣池調控鈣離子通道、肌醇-1,4,5 -三磷酸肌醇和蘭尼鹼受體，以及最近發現的雙孔通道。這些通道/受體與各種鈣池有關，包括細胞外空間、肌漿和核質網，以及酸性細胞器，所有這些都可能影響生肌鈣信號的空間和時間模式。這些通道/受體和鈣池的多樣性也表明多種細胞內，外機制可能會調節鈣離子的釋放，這使得了解鈣離子調節的信號在肌肉生成分化中的作用難上加難。 此外，骨骼肌的形成有賴快速、緩慢和中速類肌肉細胞的參與。至於每種細胞擁有特定的發育鈣訊息與否則尚未清楚。不同鈣訊息的目標亦因細胞分化過程而異，大為增加鑑別難度。例如此等目標或處細胞核，協助解讀基因; 又或處於細胞質，參與組建肌原纖維節蛋白。後者的情況比較複雜，因為功能性收縮似乎是分化的一個關鍵要素。再者，膜相關的細胞骨架蛋白—肌縮蛋白的缺少，長期以來都跟成熟肌肉細胞的功能及其鈣的內環境穩定的喪失有關聯，這暗示肌縮蛋白可能與生肌鈣信號有聯繫。所以我們打算從時間的、空間的、機械性的角度，好好描繪這些由完整的斑馬魚胚胎中不同種類分化中的骨骼肌肉細胞所產生的鈣信號特徵的特性。我們也打算測試一下這些信號對正常肌肉分化的必需性的假說。比如，我們計劃探究這些信號間的關係，以及：肌原纖維節中主要蛋白質的裝配；收縮元素如何附着垂直肌節；對鈣離子敏感的特定基因的表達；以及在肌肉早期發育過程和肌肉功能中肌缩蛋白的作用。

662211.label: Realisation of objectives
662211.value: The main objective of this proposal was to test the general hypothesis that myogenic Ca2+ signals play an essential role in normal skeletal muscle development in intact developing zebrafish. The results we obtained demonstrated that Ca2+ signaling does indeed play a key role in the development of at least one type of skeletal muscle, called slow muscle cells (SMCs) in zebrafish. The data collected suggest that a new member of the voltage-gated channel superfamily, the two pore channel 2 or TPC2 (which is known to be located in the membranes of acidic organelles and is activated by NAADP), plays a crucial role in the normal differentiation of SMCs. Using a line of transgenic zebrafish that express the Ca2+-sensitive bioluminescent protein aequorin specifically in skeletal muscle cells, (as well as complementary high-resolution confocal imaging of wild-type embryos injected with the fluorescent Ca2+ reporter, calcium green-1 dextran), morpholino (MO)-based knockdown of TPC2 resulted in a significant attenuation of Ca2+ signals and gross morphological changes in the trunk musculature. The latter included: downward bending of the trunk; induction of U-shaped somites; disruption of the organization of myofibers and abnormal myofibril morphology. Furthermore, motor behaviour was also disrupted such that in TPC2 morphants, the normal spontaneous coiling and touch-evoked response of zebrafish embryos at 24 hpf was absent. Embryos were also treated with Ned-19, a specific and potent inhibitor of TPCs, or bafilomycin A1, a vacuolar-type H+ ATPase inhibitor, which is reported to deplete the Ca2+ store in acidic organelles. Such treatments resulted in a disrupted pattern of Ca2+ signals as well as an altered morphology of the SMCs. We showed via immunolabeling that TPC2 is expressed in the SMCs of intact embryos at 24 hours post fertilization, where it appears to have a striated pattern in the muscle cells. In addition, by isolating and culturing SMCs in vitro prior to immunolabeling, we also showed that TPC2 is expressed in both a perinuclear and cytosolic location in cells. In the latter location, TPC2 in the lyososomes is localized adjacent to the IP3R and RyR in the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR). Together, our data provide evidence to suggest that TPC2-mediated Ca2+ release might initiate or trigger the SR-generated Ca2+ transients shown to be essential for myofibrilogenesis as well as the overall development of the trunk musculature.

Sub-Hypothesis #1: To test whether myogenic Ca2+ signals are generated at different times, in different locations, with different dynamics, and by different mechanisms, and that as a result they have specific triggers, targets and roles with respect to muscle development and function. To accomplish this task, we will continue to use complementary luminescent- and fluorescence-based Ca2+ imaging to characterize Ca2+ signaling during muscle cell differentiation, as well as agents and localized uncaging techniques to selectively trigger and block the Ca2+ signals identified. In addition to SMCs, we will expand our study to include fast and medial-fast muscle cells, and extend our study of all muscle cell types to 96 hpf.
Sub-Hypothesis #2: To test whether cytoplasmic Ca2+ signals play a role in regulating the assembly of the contractile apparatus and its attachment to the vertical myosepta.

Sub-hypothesis #3: To test whether dystrophin plays a role in normal myogenic Ca2+ signaling, both during muscle differentiation and function. To accomplish this we plan to image Ca2+ signaling in the dystrophin-deficient zebrafish mutant sapje, and by introducing morpholinos targeted to block dystrophin gene expression.

662211.label: Major findings and research outcome
662211.value: We have previously characterized essential inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor (IP3R) and ryanodine receptor (RyR)-mediated Ca2+ signals generated during the differentiation of slow muscle cells (SMCs) in intact zebrafish embryos (Cheung, CY, Webb SE, Love DL, Miller, AL. (2011) Int J Dev Biol 55:153–174). In this project, we showed that the lysosomal two-pore channel 2 (TPC2) also plays a crucial role in generating, and perhaps triggering, these essential Ca2+ signals, and thus contributes to the regulation of skeletal muscle myogenesis. We used a transgenic line of zebrafish that express the bioluminescent Ca2+ reporter, aequorin, specifically in skeletal muscle, in conjunction with morpholino (MO)-based and pharmacological inhibition of TPC2, and a combination of Ca2+ imaging and immunolabeling in both intact embryos and isolated SMCs. MO-based knock-down of TPC2 resulted in a dramatic attenuation of the Ca2+ signals; whereas the introduction of TPCN2-MO and TPCN2 mRNA together partially rescued the Ca2+ signaling signature. Embryos treated with trans-ned-19 or bafilomycin A1, a specific NAADP receptor inhibitor and vacuolar-type H+ ATPase inhibitor, respectively, also displayed a similar disruption of the SMC Ca2+ signaling. TPC2 and lysosomes were shown via immunohistochemistry and confocal laser scanning microscopy to be localized in perinuclear and striated cytoplasmic domains of SMCs, coincident with patterns of IP3R and RyR expression. These data together imply that TPC2-mediated Ca2+ release from lysosomes acts upstream from RyR- and IP3R-mediated Ca2+ release, suggesting that the former might act as a sensitive trigger to initiate the SR-mediated Ca2+-induced-Ca2+-release essential for SMC myogenesis and function. This work has been presented at various local and international meetings (see PART C, Section 9) and it has recently been written up and a manuscript is currently being considered for publication in a Special Issue of International Journal of Developmental Biology on Ionic Messengers in Development & Cancer, as follows: Jeffrey J. Kelu, Hayley L.H. Chan, Sarah E. Webb, Arthur H.H. Cheng, Margarida Ruas, John Parrington, Antony Galione and Andrew L. Miller (2015) Two-Pore Channel 2 activity is required for slow muscle cell-generated Ca2+ signaling during myogenesis in intact zebrafish. Under Review in Int. J. Dev. Biol.

662211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
662211.value: We are continuing to work on this very exciting project with a new RGC grant that we were awarded in July 2014 where we are investigating the role of two-pore channel type 2 (TPC2) and ADP-ribosyl cyclase (ARC) in Ca2+ signaling during slow muscle cell and primary motor neuron development (GRF 16101714) with an updated set of objectives from those originally described in GRF grant HKUST 662211. We are currently preparing TPC2- and ARC-mutant lines of zebrafish using a recently-developed molecular technique called CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing where genes are completely knocked-out. CRISPR/Cas9 has several major advantages over the previously well-established morpholino (MO) antisense oligo technique, where gene expression was knocked-down (but not knocked-out completely) and where without the appropriate controls, the results were likely to be affected by various off-target effects. In our TPC2-MO experiments, good controls were used as the results we obtained were highly reproducible; they were confirmed using a pharmacological approach and the effect of gene knock-down could be rescued using a TPC2 mRNA. However, once the CRISPR/Cas mutant lines of zebrafish are generated, high-resolution Ca2+ imaging with fluorescent Ca2+ reporters will provide additional in-depth information regarding the precise intracellular source of the SMC Ca2+ signals.

662211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
662211.value: Ca2+ is a highly versatile intracellular messenger that regulates various cellular and developmental functions. While its requirement during contraction of mature muscle has been known since the 1880s, evidence is now accumulating to suggest that Ca2+ signaling also plays a critical role in many aspects of muscle development. Currently, three endogenous Ca2+ mobilizing messengers have been described: inositol-1,4,5-trisphosphate (IP3), cyclic adenosine diphosphate ribose (cADPR), and nicotinic acid adenine dinucleotide diphosphate (NAADP). Using transgenic zebrafish where apoaequorin (a Ca2+-sensitive bioluminescent reporter) is expressed specifically in the trunk skeletal muscles, we have previously shown that Ca2+ release via IP3 receptors and cADPR (or ryanodine) receptors, which are located in the sarcoplasmic reticulum of slow muscle cells, plays an important role in the differentiation of these cells. Here, we present the first evidence to suggest that NAADP-stimulated Ca2+ release, via two-pore channel 2, which is located in lysosomes, also plays a key role in muscle development, perhaps by acting as a trigger to initiate the IP3- and/or ryanodine receptor signal transduction pathways. Our new findings provide a significant breakthrough for elucidating the signaling pathways that control normal muscle development, and thus might reveal new information concerning muscle diseases, such as muscular dystrophy.

662311.value: 目標信號對神經細胞生長和突觸分化之調控

662311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
662311.value: Synapses are specialized cell membrane domains that facilitate neuronal communication. A major goal of current research in neurobiology is to elucidate, at a molecular level, how synapses are assembled. During the development of the nervous system, neurons generate cellular processes called axons, to grow toward their synaptic target cells. Once the contact with the target cell is made, the axonal growth must cease and its tip undergoes differentiation into a nerve terminal capable of efficacious release of the neurotransmitter when nerve impulses from the cell body arrive at this site. Previous studies have shown that the signal detected by the axon’s tip for growth arrest is derived from the target cell but its identity is unknown. To solve this problem, the cell culture of motor neurons together with skeletal muscle cells offers a particularly simple and elegant experimental model. When these two cells come into contact with each other, the neuromuscular junction (NMJ) is formed. The NMJ is one of the best studied synapses because of its large size and experimental accessibility. Using this model, we intend to identify muscle-derived signal(s) responsible for making motor axons stop their growth and transform into a nerve terminal. Our previous study has suggested that upon contact with the target muscle, the growing motor axon turns down the activity of Trk receptors and this triggers its development into a nerve terminal. Trk receptors are transmembrane proteins that are activated by proteins called neurotrophins and usually mediate the growth and survival of neurons. On the other hand, another receptor termed p75NTR is known to mediate the opposite effect associated with neuronal death. In this study, we are interested in finding out whether the target-mediated axonal growth arrest is also mediated by p75NTR and if so, what muscle-derived molecule can activate it to cause the braking action on neuronal growth. This study should contribute to better understanding on an outstanding question in developmental neurobiology and may also shed light on the control of neuronal growth and regeneration in the brain and spinal cord in health and disease. 突觸是神經細胞上的特殊結構，功用是促進神經細胞間的溝通。當前神經生物學研究的一個主要目標是在分子水平上闡明突觸是如何型成的。在神經系統發育過程中，神經元產生的軸突向其目標細胞生長，並與之型成突觸。當軸突在生長過程中與其目標細胞接觸後，必須停止生長並進行分化成為神經終端，轉變成能夠有效釋放神經遞質的突觸前。以往的研究表明，造成軸突生長停滯的信號是從目標細胞衍生，但其身份不明。為了解決這個問題，運動神經元與骨骼肌細胞的細胞培養提供了一個特別簡單和優雅的實驗模型。當這兩種細胞相互接觸，就會形成神經肌肉接頭（NMJ）。 NMJ是巨大且相對簡單的突觸，因此較易進行實驗。使用這個模型，我們計劃探索由骨骼肌細胞產生的分子信號和它(們)對神經軸突生長和突觸型成的調控作用。我們以前的研究表現，當接觸目標肌肉後，神經細胞上的Trk受體酪氨酸激酶活性下降，這將觸發其發展成一個神經終端。Trk受體的活性通常是調解神經細胞的生長和生存的機制。另一稱為 P75NTR受體是眾所周知的相反機制，與神經細胞死亡有關。在這項研究中，我們希望瞭解目標細胞導致神經軸突的生長停滯是否也由P75NTR受體調控。若然，肌細胞是用甚麼分子激活P75NTR受體使軸突停止生長。這項研究應該有助於更好地理解發育神經生物學中的一個重要問題，可能還揭示在健康或疾病情況下，大腦和脊髓內的神經細胞生長和再生的控制。

662511.value: γ-微管蛋白質環型複合體的一種新構成組分NM23-H7在細胞微管成核和組織中的功能研究

662511.label: Project Objectives
662511.value: To characterize NM23-H7 association with the γTuRC Experiments are planned to explore the following aspects: (1) stoichiometry of NM23-H7 in the γTuRC; (2) domain and structural element of NM23-H7 involved in the association with the γTuRC; (3) γTuRC component that binds directly to NM23-H7. Techniques ranging from molecular biology to proteomics will be employed to characterize NM23-H7 association with the γTuRC and to investigate the molecular basis of this association. Information derived from these analyses will facilitate the functional studies of NM23-H7. To investigate the function of NM23-H7 in γTuRC-mediated microtubule nucleation Assays are planned to explore the action of NM23-H7 within the γTuRC. First, we will perform microtubule nucleation assays in vitro to test whether Nm23-H7 will promote the microtubule-nucleating activity of the γTuRC. After assays, microtubules will be examined by microscopy to verify nucleation. Second, we will test whether NM23-H7 promotes the production of γ-tubulin-GTP from γ-tubulin-GDP within the γTuRC. Given that NM23-H7 contains two putative kinase domains, the function of each kinase domain will be assessed by mutation within or deletion of individual kinase domains. The assays of the mutated constructs will reveal which kinase domain is involved in γTuRC-mediated nucleation. To examine the role of NM23-H7 in microtubule organization The role of NM23-H7 in microtubule organization will be examined throughout the cell cycle in several respects. First, we will investigate the expression and subcellular localization patterns of NM23-H7 at different stages of the cell cycle. Immunofluorescence and time-lapse microscopy will be employed to reveal the localization patterns and dynamic behaviors of NM23-H7. Cell synchronization in conjunction with immunoblotting will reveal the cell cycle-dependent changes of its expression. Second, we will disrupt NM23-H7 expression by RNAi and evaluate its potential effect on microtubule organization in interphase and mitosis. To examine microtubule array organization, microtubules will be visualized by immunofluorescence microscopy. In addition, the dynamic organization of microtubules during cell cycle progression will be examined by time-lapse microscopy. Third, the requirement of the kinase activity of NM23-H7 will be assessed in a “rescue” experiment of NM23-H7 depletion using its kinase-dead mutant. The mutant’s failure to rescue the defects caused by the loss of the endogenous protein will indicate the involvement of the kinase action. Fourth, we will probe the involvement of NM23-H7 in chromatin-based nucleation of microtubules. Microtubule regrowth assays will be performed with mitotic cells to test chromatin-associated nucleation. If the kinase function of NM23-H7 is required, the RNAi-mediated depletion will impact such nucleation and the kinase-dead mutant will not be able to rescue the defect. Collectively, these assays will provide information on the function of NM23-H7 in microtubule organization.

662511.value: 在動物細胞中，作為細胞骨架的微管在各種各樣的細胞活動中起著重要的作用，這些細胞活動包括細胞分裂、極性化、運動，以及細胞形態生成。細胞中心體被稱為微管組織中心，負責微管成核和形成有組織的排列。這些功能依賴於一種名為γ-微管蛋白環形複合體（γTuRC）的大型蛋白質複合體，其核心組分γ-微管蛋白利用可交換的方式結合GDP或GTP。我們最近的研究發現，γ-微管蛋白從GDP到GTP的結合轉換調節γTuRC的微管成核活性。然而，控制這種轉換的分子機制仍然未能破解。 我們的研究集中於組織和調節細胞微管骨架的分子機制，本項研究申請計劃探索γTuRC介導微管成核和組織的分子基礎。NM23-H7是最近被發現存在於γTuRC中的一種新型蛋白質，並連同其結合的γTuRC定位於細胞中心體。蛋白序列分析預測NM23-H7屬於NM23核苷二磷酸激酶家族，這家族成員催化從核苷二磷酸形成核苷三磷酸的轉變。我們的實驗顯示該NM23-H7激酶在中心體微管成核中起著重要作用。此外，GTP的負載於γ-微管蛋白顯著提高了γTuRC的微管成核活性。基於這些發現，我們認為NM23-H7催化γTuRC中結合於γ-微管蛋白的GDP轉換至GTP，從而提高γTuRC的微管成核活性。本項申請計劃致力於研究NM23-H7與γTuRC的結合，探究NM23-H7在γTuRC介導微管成核中的功能，並分析NM23-H7在微管組織中的作用。我們將應用結合了生物化學、蛋白質組學、分子和細胞生物學的多學科方法去實現這些研究目標。 本項研究在以下幾個方面有重要意義。首先，本項研究工作將有助於了解γTuRC導致微管成核的機理。其次，這項研究將在分子水平上對依賴於微管組織結構的各種細胞活動提供信息。第三，本研究將推進我們對核苷二磷酸激酶的認識。因此，本項研究將有助於闡明多種涉及微管或核苷二磷酸激酶的基本細胞活動的分子機制。眾所周知，很多人類疾病是由於微管的組織和調節缺陷所導致，並且幾種廣泛應用於癌症治療的藥物也是以細胞微管為靶點。因此，闡明NM23-H7的功能及機理並從而獲得對微管調節更深入的認識將為開發治療藥物提供新的靶點。

662511.label: Realisation of objectives
662511.value: Objective #1. To characterize NM23-H7 association with the γTuRC To address this objective, we characterized NM23-H7 (also known as NME7) and its association with the γ-tubulin ring complex (γTuRC). Two transcripts of the nm23-h7 gene were found in the GenBank databases; these transcripts are identical except that isoform A contains additional 36 a.a. at the amino terminus. In asynchronous and mitotic cells, we have detected that isoform A is expressed but isoform B is not. In addition, NM23-H7 is expressed at similar levels at various stages of the cell cycle. To analyze the subcellular localization of NM23-H7, we performed immunostaining of the endogenous protein and also examined the localization of NM23-H7 ectopically expressed with a fluorescent protein (i.e. GFP) in living cells. NM23-H7 localizes to centrosomes and in the nucleus during interphase and attaches to mitotic spindles and the spindle poles during mitosis. The centrosomal content of NM23-H7 displays cell cycle-dependent changes, with the lowest level in the early G1 phase and the highest level in the metaphase, showing close correlation with the changes of γ-tubulin’s level. NM23-H7 also appears on the central spindle in late anaphase and in the midbody during cytokinesis. Our results indicate that the centrosomal localization but not the expression of NM23-H7 is regulated in a cell cycle-dependent manner. In animal cells, γ-tubulin exists in two complexes of distinct sizes, the γ-tubulin small complex (γTuSC) and the γTuRC. Using sucrose-gradient centrifugation in conjunction with coimmunoprecipitation, we have found that NM23-H7 associates with the γTuRC but does not associate with γ-tubulin present as the γTuSC or as a single molecule. Indeed, disassembly of the γTuRC by silencing the expression of GCP4, a γTuRC component that is required for the complex assembly, abolishes the coimmunoprecipitation of NM23-H7 with γ-tubulin and other γTuRC proteins. We have mapped the γTuRC-binding domain in NM23-H7. The protein contains a DM10 domain followed by two putative kinase domains (domains A and B). Both kinase domains are required for binding to γ-tubulin, whereas the DM10 domain is dispensable. Therefore, the γTuRC binds to a structure formed by both kinase domains of NM23-H7. Moreover, Arg322, a conserved residue in domain B, is crucially involved in γTuRC binding: changing Arg322 to Ala substantially reduced the co-immunoprecipitation of NM23-H7 and γTuRC components; changing Arg322 to Glu abolished the co-immunoprecipitation. Therefore, domain B is critical for interaction with the γTuRC. NM23-H7 is the only NM23 family member that contains two kinase domains. In addition, we tested several other NM23 members, including NM23-H1, H5, H6, and H10 and found that they do not interact with the γTuRC. These results suggest that the unique structure of NM23-H7 confers its binding activity toward the γTuRC. Objective #2. To investigate the function of NM23-H7 in γTuRC-mediated microtubule nucleation We have fulfilled this objective by demonstrating the role of NM23-H7 in γTuRC-mediated microtubule nucleation. We first conducted an in vitro assay of microtubule nucleation using purified γTuRC and α/β-tubulin. In the absence of NM23-H7, the γTuRC showed a small activity of inducing microtubule assembly from α/β-tubulin. The addition of the NM23-H7 recombinant protein significantly stimulated γTuRC-mediated assembly of microtubules. By contrast, the nucleating activity was unaffected after adding NM23-H7(R322A), a γTuRC-binding defective mutant of NM23-H7. Therefore, the association with NM23-H7 enhances the microtubule-nucleation activity of the γTuRC. To gain mechanistic insights into NM23-H7’s action, we analyzed its domain structure. The protein contains two putative kinase domains following a DM10 domain. In a phosphorylation assay, the recombinant protein of NM23-H7 displayed robust autophosphorylation, indicating that the protein possesses a kinase function. Sequence alignment with other NM23 members predicted that Lys-173 and His-206 of kinase domain A and Arg-322 and His-355 of kinase domain B are involved in kinase action. The single mutation K173A or H206F abolished autophosphorylation of the protein, whereas the single mutation R322A or H355F and the double mutation H355F/R322A did not affect autophosphorylation. These mutational analyses demonstrate that domain A possesses a kinase activity and that domain B is a pseudokinase domain. To explore whether the kinase activity of NM23-H7 is required for enhancing γTuRC-mediated nucleation of microtubules, the kinase-deficient mutant NM23-H7(K173A) was tested: the mutant protein showed a significantly impaired activity of promoting γTuRC-dependent nucleation. These results indicate that NM23-H7 requires its kinase action to promote γTuRC-dependent microtubule nucleation. Objective #3. To examine the role of NM23-H7 in microtubule organization In mammalian cells, centrosomes are the principal organizing centers of cellular microtubules and this function requires the γTuRC. We performed RNAi-mediated depletion of NM23-H7 in proliferating animal cells. The depletion affected neither the formation of the γTuRC nor its localization to centrosomes, showing that NM23-H7 is dispensable for the complex assembly and the centrosomal localization of the γTuRC. However, γTuRC disassembly resulted from the RNAi-mediated knockdown of γ-tubulin or GCP4 substantially decreased the centrosomal content of NM23-H7, which correlated closely with the reduced centrosomal levels of γ-tubulin. We also observed that the γTuRC-binding defective mutant NM23-H7(R322E) did not show centrosomal localization. Therefore, these two lines of evidence indicate that the centrosomal localization of NM23-H7 depends on its assembly into the γTuRC. The microtubule-nucleating function of centrosomes can be assayed by microtubule regrowth after depolymerization. We conducted microtubule regrowth after cold-induced depolymerization. RNAi-mediated suppression of NM23-H7’s expression significantly delayed microtubule growth at the centrosomes, showing that NM23-H7 plays an important role in the microtubule-organizing function of centrosomes. To further explore the function of NM23-H7, we silenced its expression and evaluated the effect on microtubules in living cells. As a plus-end tracking protein, EB1 is a widely used marker of growing microtubule distal tips. To monitor microtubule growth, a cell line stably expressing EB1-GFP was generated and used in conjunction with time-lapse microscopy. We found that the silencing of NM23-H7’s expression significantly decreased EB1-GFP signals emanating from the centrosomes. These experiments together with others described above indicate that NM23-H7 is required for the microtubule-organizing function of centrosomes. In quiescent epithelial cells, the centrosome migrates to the cell surface where it organizes microtubules to form primary cilia. We examined whether NM23-H7 is involved in the assembly of primary cilia. RNAi-mediated depletion of NM23-H7 reduced the ciliation rate and the cilium length of primary cilia on hTERT-RPE1 cells. We also generated NM23-H7-deficient cell lines by gene editing using the CRISPR/Cas9 system and observed similar ciliogenesis defects in the knockout cells. Therefore, the growth of primary cilia is impaired in the absence of NM23-H7. To assess whether the kinase action of NM23-H7 is required for its function in the formation of primary cilia, we performed rescue experiments by expressing the kinase-deficient mutant H206F. The expression of the wild-type NM23-H7 rescued the ciliogenesis defects caused by the depletion, whereas the expression of H206F was unable to rescue the defects. These observations indicate that the kinase activity of NM23-H7 is required for ciliary growth.

662511.label: Major findings and research outcome
662511.value: In this project, we have characterized the interaction between NM23-H7 and the γTuRC. NM23-H7 associates with the γTuRC but does not bind to the smaller molecular assemblies of γ-tubulin. The binding of NM23-H7 is dispensable for γTuRC assembly. The γTuRC-binding domain was mapped to a large region consisting of both domains A and B, with Arg322 in domain B crucially involved in binding. In the NM23 family, NM23-H7 is the sole member that contains 2 putative kinase domains, implicating that γTuRC association is a property unique to NM23-H7. Indeed, we tested several other NM23 members, including NM23-H1, 5, 6, and 10, and failed to detect γTuRC-binding activities. We have found that NM23-H7 localizes to centrosomes throughout the cell cycle of proliferating cells and to the basal body (centrosome) of quiescent cells in a manner dependent on its assembly into the γTuRC. We conducted in vitro and in vivo assays to reveal the role of NM23-H7 in γTuRC-mediated microtubule nucleation. In an in vitro microtubule nucleation assay, addition of NM23-H7 enhances the microtubule-nucleating activity of the γTuRC. In proliferating mammalian cells, depletion of NM23-H7 by RNAi causes defects in microtubule growth on centrosomes and thus impairs microtubule organization by the centrosomes. Furthermore, we have demonstrated that NM23-H7 possesses a histidine-kinase activity and that the kinase activity is required for its function to stimulate γTuRC-mediated microtubule nucleation. These findings have provided mechanistic insights into NM23-H7’s action in the γTuRC. We also investigated the function of NM23-H7 in quiescent epithelial cells in which the centrosome migrates to the cell surface where it becomes the basal body to organize microtubules for the formation of primary cilia, an organelle that functions in signal transduction and animal development. RNAi-mediated depletion of NM23-H7 reduced the ciliation rate and of primary cilia. In addition, we generated NM23-H7-deficient cell lines by gene editing using the CRISPR/Cas9 system and observed similar ciliogenesis defects in the knockout cells. Therefore, the growth of primary cilia is impaired in the absence of NM23-H7. In summary, this study has revealed the function of NM23-H7 in γTuRC-mediated microtubule nucleation and organization. Our findings contribute to understanding the molecular principles governing the organization of microtubule cytoskeleton in animal cells. Several research articles have been published or are being prepared for publication based on the findings from this study along with the training of postgraduate students.

662511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
662511.value: We have found that NM23-H7 possesses a protein-histidine-kinase activity and that this activity is required for its γTuRC-associated function. Thus, elucidation of the kinase action of NM23-H7 will contribute to the understanding of the molecular principles governing microtubule-dependent cellular activities. We plan to identify the substrates of NM23-H7 in the γTuRC. Following identification, we will validate the identified phosphorylation events and will investigate their biological roles using various approaches such as site-directed mutagenesis. We anticipate that the functional analysis of cellular phosphorylation mediated by NM23-H7 will inform how NM23-H7 exerts its actions. Proteins often mediate their physiological functions through interactions with their target and regulatory proteins, so systematic identification of such interactions for a given protein would help in understanding what cellular activities the given protein is involved in and how it exerts its actions in these events. To understand how NM23-H7 exerts its function, we will initiate systematic search for cellular proteins that interact with NM23-H7 using proteomic technologies. We will then demonstrate the identified interactions in vitro and in vivo and assemble protein networks associated with NM23-H7 in certain cellular contexts. Demonstration of the identified interactions will delineate the functional networks in which NM23-H7 participates.

662511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
662511.value: NM23-H7 is a highly conserved protein in vertebrates and a putative member of the NM23 family that is known as nucleoside-diphosphate and protein-histidine kinases. We have identified that NM23-H7 is a component of the γ-tubulin ring complex (γTuRC), a ring-shaped macromolecular structure that initiates microtubule growth and mediates microtubule attachment at the microtubule-organizing centers, such as centrosomes, in animal cells. NM23-H7 associates with the γTuRC to localize to centrosomes, where NM23-H7 promotes the microtubule-nucleating activity of the γTuRC. Furthermore, NM23-H7 possesses a protein-histidine kinase activity that is required for its function of promoting γTuRC-mediated nucleation of microtubules. In quiescent epithelial cells, primary cilia are built on the basal body (centrosome) to sense extracellular environment and to coordinate diverse signaling pathways. We have found that NM23-H7 is a ciliary protein that participates in ciliary growth. Therefore, NM23-H7 is a novel protein-histidine kinase that plays a regulatory role in the microtubule-organizing function of centrosomes. The findings described here generated novel functional data for NM23-H7, a gene required for vertebrate development. In addition, this research facilitated our understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying γTuRC-mediated microtubule nucleation and thus advanced our knowledge of various cellular events dependent on microtubule cytoskeleton.

662711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
662711.value: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Noninvasive diagnosis of early cancer is critical to the success of cancer treatment. Because most early cancers originate in epithelium, the superficial layer of tissue, optical imaging is ideally suited for early cancer detection. Extensive studies show that intrinsic optical signals from living tissue could provide diagnostic information for noninvasive detection of cancer at early stage. The proposed research aims to explore the diagnostic and prognostic value of the fluorescence signals from two intrinsic fluorescence molecules (protein and hemoglobin) which so far have not been well investigated and understood. HYPOTHESES AND KEY ISSUES: Cancer development induces morphologic and biochemical changes in tissue, which include the changes in content/profile of the proteins in cell and at the cell-to-cell junction sites, the changes in microvasculature caused by cancer-related angiogenesis and etc. Therefore, these changes in tissue can potentially provide valuable information for noninvasive sensing of early cancer development. We recently developed a short-wavelength ultrafast source to effectively excite protein fluorescence, and discovered the short-wavelength excited two-photon fluorescence from hemoglobin, the major component in blood. This short-wavelength two-photon fluorescence technology enables in vivo characterization of protein fluorescence and imaging of microvascular architecture in tissue. RESEARCH PLAN AND METHODOLOGY: In vivo studies will be conducted in the human cervix. Because cervical cancer is the second most frequent cancer in women, over 200 patients are diagnosed to have early cervical cancer lesions every year in co-I’s clinic at the Prince of Wales Hospital. Furthermore, human cervix could be considered as a good and natural model to study the early epithelial cancer. We propose to develop a time-resolved spectroscopic imaging system with endoscope-like probe that can easily access human cervix and to excite/analyze two-photon protein and hemoglobin fluorescence simultaneously. The research will focus on characterizing protein fluorescence signal and microvascular architecture from normal and precancerous epithelial tissues. This exploratory and preliminary study will aim to investigate whether the changes in protein signals and microvasculature can be potentially used as natural biomarkers for noninvasive detection of early epithelial cancer. SIGNIFICANCE: The proposed study uses cervical tissue as a model to obtain new biological insights into the understanding of early cancer development in epithelial tissue. The success of the proposed project will positively impact the development of new noninvasive technology for the detection of early epithelial cancer not only in human cervix but also generally in other important organ sites. 背景及目的：非侵入式的早期癌症诊断对于癌症的成功治疗非常关键。因为绝大部分的癌症源发自最外层的上皮组织，所以光学成像是早期癌症诊断的理想工具。广泛的研究显示人体组织的内生光学信号能够提供为早期癌症的检测提供有价值的诊断信息。本研究课题的目的在于探索两类荧光分子（蛋白质和血红蛋白）对早期癌症诊断和预见的价值。到目前为止这两类荧光分子的荧光特性尚未被深入的研究和理解。 假设和关键点：癌症的发展会在生物组织中引起形态和生物化学的变化，这些变化包括细胞内和细胞与细胞链接点的蛋白质含量和组分的变化，以及癌症相关的血管增生导致的微循环系统变化。因此，这些变化潜在地能够为检测早期癌症的发展提供有价值的信息。最近，我们为有效的激发蛋白质的荧光发展了一套短波长的超快光源，并且发现了血液的主要成分---血红蛋白在短波长激发下产生的荧光。这种在短波长范围激发的双光子荧光技术使得我们能够在活体状态下描绘蛋白质荧光并且对组织里的微血管结构成像。 研究计划和方法：活体研究将会在人体子宫颈上开展。因为子宫颈癌是女性的第二大癌症，每年在威尔斯亲王医院co-I的门诊有超过200位病人被诊断为患有早期子宫颈癌。并且子宫颈是一种标准的被广泛认可的研究早期上皮组织癌症的模型。我们提议发展一种内窥镜类似的时间分辨光谱成像系统。 它能容易地接近子宫颈并且同时激发和分析蛋白质和血红蛋白的双光子荧光。本研究将侧重于分析和描绘正常以及早期癌症上皮组织的蛋白质荧光和微血管结构。早期的探索和研究将致力于检验蛋白质信号和微血管系统的变化是否能够作为非侵入早期癌症诊断的一种潜在的天然生物标记。 意义：本研究用子宫颈作为模型来获取关于上皮组织早期癌症发展的新的生物理解。这个所建议的研究项目的成功将不仅极大的影响子宫颈早期癌症分侵入诊断技术的发展，而且对其他重要器官的癌症将有普遍的借鉴意义。

662711.label: Realisation of objectives
662711.value: The objectives of the research project have been achieved. In detail, we successfully developed a unique multicolor excitation-based multimodal nonlinear optical (NLO) microscopy, which can simultaneously collect two-photon excited fluorescence (TPEF) of reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH), keratin, collagen and tryptophan, and second harmonic generation (SHG) of collagen in biological tissues in vivo. The system was further equipped with time- and spectral- resolved detection modalities, facilitating sophisticated analysis of the complex NLO signals, thereby increasing the diagnostic power of the multicolor-based excitations multimodal NLO microscopy. In this GRF funded research project, we characterized the squamous epithelial endogenous signals probed from the multimodal NLO system at different epithelial mucosa tissue layers from stratum corneum to stroma. Additionally, we assessed the diagnostic efficacies of the NLO image-derived diagnostic parameters from the various excitation wavelengths alone and collectively for in vivo detection of pre-neoplastic lesion. In the in vivo study, 7,12 Dimenthylbenz(a)anthracene (DMBA) hamster cheek pouch carcinogenesis model was utilized to systematically evaluate the efficacy of multimodal system for in situ diagnosis of various squamous pre-neoplasia grades. We demonstrated for the first time (to our knowledge) that multicolor excitation based multimodal NLO microscopy system produced a great wealth of diagnostic information ranging from tissue architecture, cellular/sub-cellular morphology, to biochemical information emanating from different stratified tissue depths. In particular, our results elucidated stratum corneum to contain significant diagnostic information for identifying precancers in vivo. Furthermore, we showed the multitude of diagnostic information from the different tissue layers can be effectively integrated to provide high performance diagnostic algorithm for identifying squamous epithelial precancer. These results affirmed the efficacy of the novel multicolor excitation to produce a wide range of TPEF and SHG signals for clinical squamous pre-malignancy diagnosis application in vivo. In the study of NLO imaging microvsculature, we demonstrate a new label-free approach for in vivo imaging of microvasculature and blood flow, based on the unique spectral characteristics of the two-photon excited endogenous fluorescence. In particular, three-dimensional reconstruction of the microvascular networks was achieved with the depth-resolved two-photon excitation fluorescence (TPEF) imaging. The blood flow images, obtained by perpendicularly scanning the focal point across the blood vessel, provided accurate information for characterizing hemodynamics of circulatory system. The endogenous fluorescent signals of NADH enabled visualization of the circulating granulocyte (neutrophil) in blood vessel. The development of acute sterile inflammation could be detected by the quantitative counting of circulating neutrophils.

662711.label: Major findings and research outcome
662711.value: The major findings of this research project are that we demonstrated for the first time (to our knowledge) that multicolor excitation based multimodal NLO microscopy system produced a great wealth of diagnostic information ranging from tissue architecture, cellular/sub-cellular morphology, to biochemical information emanating from different stratified tissue depths. In particular, our results elucidated stratum corneum to contain significant diagnostic information for identifying precancers in vivo. Furthermore, we showed the multitude of diagnostic information from the different tissue layers can be effectively integrated to provide high performance diagnostic algorithm for identifying squamous epithelial precancer. These results affirm the efficacy of the novel multicolor excitation to produce a wide range of TPEF and SHG signals for clinical squamous pre-malignancy diagnosis application in vivo. In addition, we developed a new methodology for in vivo micro-vascular and micro-flow imaging by using two-photon excitation endogenous fluorescence. The 3D structures of fine microvascular networks were reconstructed based on the unique spectral characteristics of blood plasma TPEF signals. We demonstrated that the imaging flow cytometry provided the quantitative counting of circulating blood cells, which could be used for in vivo monitoring disease development and treatment such as acute sterile inflammation. The calibrated counting of circulating leukocytes (neutrophils) in the blood vessels of different flow velocity and size could potentially improve the accuracy of measurement of circulating cell in whole circulation system. Finally, using a single wavelength excitation at 650 nm and spectroscopic detection, we achieved simultaneously four-color imaging of multiple blood cells and vascular structures. The results of this research project have been published in three major journal papers and four conference proceedings as listed in Part C.

662711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
662711.value: Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), arising from various human anatomic sites, is the most common cancer capable of metastatic spread worldwide. Early diagnosis and localization of premalignant lesions along with effective clinical treatment is crucial towards improving SCC patients’ survival. However, current conventional clinical method to detect the high-risk lesions is usually based on visual inspection. Subtle tissue transformation may not be apparent, limiting diagnostic accuracy. Nonlinear optical (NLO) microscopy is a powerful imaging technique that has gained much attention from scientific and medical community for imaging of precancerous and cancerous tissues in various organ parts of animal models and human subjects. In this research project, we explored diagnostic utility of a multimodal NLO microscopy for noninvasive detection of squamous epithelial precancer in vivo. A total of nine and eight features from 745 and 600 nm excitation wavelengths, respectively, involving tissue structural and intrinsic biochemical properties were found to contain significant diagnostic information for precancers detection(p<0.05). Particularly, 600 nm-excited tryptophan fluorescence signals emanating from stratum corneum was revealed to provide remarkable diagnostic utility. Multivariate statistical techniques confirmed the integration of diagnostically significant features from multicolor excitation wavelengths yielded improved diagnostic accuracy as compared to using the individual wavelength alone.

662811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
662811.value: 基因組印跡是指子代中出現表觀沉默效應的等位基因源於親代中的一方。近期對精神病譜狀態（如精神分裂症，雙相障礙和重性抑郁症）進行的遺傳學和基因組學研究，得到的假設顯示病因是受印跡基因遺傳和表觀遺傳不平衡所影響。此外，也發現了母型表達印跡基因的相對影響較大。最近，我方研究組報道了GABRB2基因印跡與精神分裂症易感性的關聯，發現與疾病相關的單核苷酸多態性中，父系等位基因傳遞不足，以及對照組和精神分裂症患者之間的基因甲基化差異。另外，其他精神分裂症候選基因如DISC1和DTNBP1均顯示印跡特性。不過，也有對精神分裂症基因印跡的負面結果報道，所以印跡現象在精神分裂症的重要性和作用遠未完全清晰。 本研究項目意圖將我們先前對GABRB2印跡所造的研究，擴大至其他候選精神分裂症易感基因，從而探索對照組和患者之間的基因印跡和甲基化差異，會否是這些候選基因的共同特征。我們將使用相同的樣本對所選定的重要候選精神分裂症易感基因進行分析，測定傳遞不平衡和親代遺傳效應。此外，我們會進行基因表達與基因型的關聯分析，了解印跡的作用；還會應用亞硫酸氫鈉測序分析對照組和精神分裂症患者之間的表觀遺傳沉默差異。這些精神分裂症候選基因的印記效應證據將進一步顯示印跡基因對精神分裂症病因的重要性，從而使我們更了解疾病的演變。

662811.label: Realisation of objectives
662811.value: We recently demonstrated that the GABA(A) receptor beta2 subunit gene GABRB2 is an imprinted gene, suggesting that this epigenetic process may play a role in schizophrenia. In addition, evidence for and against imprinting in other candidate schizophrenia genes has been reported. In this study, we aimed to further analyze imprinting effects in schizophrenia. Following from our previous report of imprinting in GABRB2, in part based on simple clustering of gene expression data with respect to SNP genotype (Pun et al., 2010), we demonstrated that other quantitative traits such as the PANSS score as well as average antipsychotic dosage (both measures of symptom severity) could also be clustered into two tiers. Moreover, the distribution with respect to SNP genotype resembled that expected for expression data in genes with an imprinting effect, suggesting that GABRB2 also affected these traits (Tsang et al., 2013). DNA methylation whereby parent-of-origin specific alleles are silenced by methylation of the associated CpG sites is an important epigenetic mechanism through which imprinting can take effect. We applied our previously developed method for measuring global DNA methylation levels (Zhao et al., 2012) to compare methylation in 576 schizophrenia patients and 424 healthy controls. Significantly lower levels of methylation were observed in the patient group compared to the control group. Moreover, we performed AluScan sequencing with or without bisulphite treatment of DNA for a family sample consisting of two schizophrenia sibling patients and their two healthy parents. AluScan sequencing is our in-house developed method for genome-wide target capture coupled with next-generation DNA sequencing, and bisulphite treatment of DNA allows analysis of methylated sites. This allowed identification of 8 schizophrenia candidate genes that were hypomethylated and showed signs of imprinting, suggesting that imprinting via methylation is common in schizophrenia-associated genes. We also investigated gene expression for candidate schizophrenia genes in the GABAergic pathway, including different isoforms of GABRB2 and different subunit genes. Imprinting could be inferred from the expression levels of both the long and short forms of GABRB2. In this project, we also established a data analysis approach based o the likelihood ratio test to detect the presence of imprinting in situations where family or pedigree data is absent (Li et al., 2014). Given that common tests for genomic imprinting are based on the transmission disequilibrium test which utilizes pedigree genetic data to infer imprinting, such an approach would be very useful when such data cannot be obtained.

662811.label: Major findings and research outcome
662811.value: 1. We demonstrated that quantitative traits such as the PANSS score and average antipsychotic dosage (both are measures of symptom severity) for schizophrenia patients could be clustered into two tiers and the distribution with respect to GABRB2 SNP genotype resembled that expected for expression data of genes with an imprinting effect, suggesting that the gene also affected these traits (Tsang et al., 2013). 2. We established an approach to detect the presence of imprinting based on the likelihood ratio test (LRT). We first proved that the maximum likelihood estimator of the mixing distribution is consistent and that the LRT statistic has a distinct null limiting distribution for a finite normal mixture model, validating the LRT as is a suitable test of homogeneity for this model (Li et al., 2014). When the genotype distribution of three SNPs in GABRB2 were tested against the expression data of the beta2S subunit using our method, the presence of imprinting was detected, in concordance with our earlier conclusion of imprinting in this schizophrenia-associated gene. 3. Significantly lower levels of global methylation were observed in schizophrenia patients compared to a healthy control group. Although differential methylation between schizophrenia patients and controls for various genes, this is the first report of global hypomethylation in patients. 4. We performed AluScan sequencing with or without bisulphite treatment of DNA for a family sample consisting of two sibling schizophrenia patients and their two healthy parents, and identified 8 schizophrenia candidate genes including NRG1, DISC1, DAOA and GRIN2B that were unmethylated in the patients but were methylated in the DNA of only one of the parents. This demonstrates that imprinting is present in many schizophrenia-associated genes and that hypomethylation is common in these genes. 5. We measured gene expression for different isoforms of GABRB2 and different GABA receptor subunit genes. Imprinting could be inferred from the expression levels of both the long and short forms of GABRB2.

662811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
662811.value: The present study has demonstrated that imprinting effects can be observed in many schizophrenia-associated genes, thereby suggesting that imprinting plays an important role in schizophrenia. Moreover, our genome-wide sequencing results suggested an important contribution of methylation to imprinting and to schizophrenia etiology as a whole. This is in line with recent studies that report differential DNA methylation in schizophrenia patients compared to controls. These findings suggest that methylation profiles can potentially be used to distinguish between patients and controls, in a manner similar to that of copy number variation profiles for which we have reported can be used to predict cancer predisposition. In order to facilitate such development of methylation profiles for use as a prognostic tool for schizophrenia, we propose that an approach similar to that described in Ding et al. (Genomic Insights, 2014) can be adopted. Briefly, the methylation profiles for large numbers of case and control samples will need to be acquired and, by application of machine-learning algorithms to these profiles, a classification profile that can accurately distinguish case from control samples will be defined. This profile will then be the basis for the prognostic tool with which to predict whether test subjects are predisposed to schizophrenia.

662811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
662811.value: Genetic imprinting is an epigenetic phenomenon by which alleles in genes can be silenced according their parent-of-origin. The major mechanisms involved in this process include DNA methylation and histone modification. Evidence for and against imprinting has been reported for genes associated with the neuropsychiatric disease of schizophrenia. In this project, we established a statistical method based on the likelihood ratio test, to assist in the detection of imprinting in the absence of family genetic data. This approach infers the presence of imprinting by comparing SNP genotype distributions with the distributions of expression levels of the associated gene, and its application to the GABRB2 gene gave results in concordance with our earlier conclusion of imprinting for this gene. In addition, we showed that the global methylation levels in schizophrenia patients were significantly lower than that in healthy controls. Moreover, by performing genome-wide DNA sequencing for a family of two sibling patients and their healthy parents, we found that a number of schizophrenia-associated genes were hypomethylated in the patients and these genes also showed signs of imprinting. These findings demonstrate that imprinting occurs in many schizophrenia-associated genes and that the imprinting effects could be related to methylation status.

662911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
662911.value: Acetylcholinesterase (AChE) is a key enzyme in terminating cholinergic neurotransmission in nervous systems. Apart from this classic function, emerging evidence suggests non-enzymatic functions of AChE in other tissues. The low bone mineral density revealed in AChE knock-out (ACHE-/-) mice, the reduced differentiation of AChE-depleted osteoblasts and the expression of PRiMA-linked tetrameric AChE specifically in osteoblasts indicate a possible functional role of AChE in bone development. ACHE-/- mice and osteoporotic rodents will be used to reveal novel functions of AChE in bone development. The expression profile of AChE will be identified in different cell types of the bone in normal and osteoporotic mice during development and maturation. In cultured osteoblasts derived from either ACHE-/- or ACHE+/+ mice, the signaling cascade of AChE in facilitating osteoblastogenic differentiation will be revealed. The study of this novel function of AChE in bone development will not only provide new insight into the non-enzymatic functions of AChE, but also contribute to a full understanding of bone formation. Osteoporosis is a disease that leads to an increased risk of bone fracture affecting life expectancy and quality of life. The elucidation of the molecular mechanism for AChE-induced osteogenic differentiation will open new directions in developing therapeutic methods against osteoporosis. 乙酰胆碱酯酶（AChE）主要存在于胆碱能末梢突触间隙，是体内水解神经递质乙酰胆碱所必需的酶。同时，AChE也存在于其他组织中，并具有非酶性功能。近年来研究发现AChE基因敲除小鼠的骨密度显著降低；来自AChE基因敲除小鼠的原代成骨细胞分化能力减弱；成骨细胞特异性地表达PRiMA连接的AChE四聚体。这些研究共同表明AChE可能参与了调节骨发育的过程。本研究将利用AChE基因敲除小鼠模型和骨质疏松小鼠模型，研究AChE在骨发育过程的功能。首先，我们将检测正常和骨质疏松的小鼠在不同的发育阶段，骨细胞里AChE的表达变化。其次，我们将在正常的和AChE基因敲除小鼠的原代培养成骨细胞研究AChE如何促进成骨细胞发化。该项研究不仅可阐释AChE的非酶性功能，还有助于全面了解骨发育的过程。近年来，骨质疏松的疾病率呈上升趋势，严重影响了人们的生活质量。本项目以AChE为靶点，研究其刺激成骨细胞分化的分子机理，为预防和治疗骨质疏松疾病提供了新方向。

662911.label: Realisation of objectives
662911.value: Acetylcholinesterase (AChE) is a hydrolytic enzyme in cholinergic transmission of nervous system; however, emerging evidences indicate that AChE exerts other functions in different systems. Here, we demonstrated that PRiMA-linked AChE is playing a role in the differentiation process of bone cells. In ACHE-/- mice, a robust decrease of bone density and growth was revealed as compared with that of wild type. Bone tissues expressed mRNAs encoding AChE and PRiMA, and the PRiMA-linked AChE enzyme. In cultured rat osteoblasts and osteosarcoma MG-63 cells, PRiMA-linked AChE was the major form of enzyme being detected. The expressions of AChE and PRiMA mRNAs, as well as PRiMA-linked AChE, were stimulated during the osteogenic differentiation. Over expression of PRiMA-linked AChE in osteoblast induced the cell differentiation; however, this osteogenic effect of AChE did not require the enzymatic activity. In parallel, the differentiation process was markedly reduced in cultured AChE-depleted osteoblasts: the reduction was a result of defected signaling mediated by bone morphogenetic protein. These results, for the first time, show the existence of PRiMA-linked AChE in cultured bone cell and tissue, and which might participate in the osteogenic differentiation process regardless of its enzymatic activity.

662911.label: Major findings and research outcome
662911.value: [1] The bone mineral density (BMD) of femurs showed ACHE-/- mice at 3 weeks were proportionally shorter than WT. The BMD of total, trabecular and cortical bone were dramatically decreased in ACHE-/- mice. [2] Bone volume (BV/TV), trabecular thickness (Tb.Th.), trabecular number (Tb. #) and trabecular separation (Tb. Sp.), were dramatically reduced in ACHE-/- mice. ACHE-/- mice showed the reduction of osteoblast surface (Ob.S/BS) and osteoblast number (Ob/B.Pm) in femur. Mineral apposition rate (MAR) of ACHE-/- mice were slower than WT by using double calcein labeling, suggesting the possible retardation of cell growth of osteoblast. [3] In MG-63 cells and primary osteoblasts, significant amounts of AChET and PRiMA I mRNAs were revealed. Cultures were treated with bone differentiation inducer: Dex + Vit.C for 4 and 12 days. The alkaline phosphatase (ALP, a key enzyme for bone differentiation) activity was dramatically increased upon treatment. The expression of bone markers including osteocalcin, osteonectin and collagen1 A1 (COL1A1) was also enhanced, thus indicating the responsiveness of the established bone cell cultures to osteogenic differentiation. [4] In the differentiated MG-63 cells and primary osteoblasts, the amount of transcripts encoding AChET and PRiMA was induced. The molecular form of AChE in MG-63 cells was shown to be entire G4 AChE, while in primary osteoblasts was G1 and G4 AChE. Osteogenic differentiation process could boost up the amount of G4 AChE in both cultures. The culture extracts were immune-precipitated by anti-PRiMA antibody before analysis; G4 AChE was depleted specifically by the antibody treatment. Thus, these results indicated that the amount of PRiMA-linked G4 AChE could be stimulated by the differentiation process in bone cultures. [5] The ALP activity was dramatically increased in PRiMA + AChET over expressed cells. This could not be observed in the single transfected cells. The osteogenic ability of PRiMA-linked AChE was further confirmed by the increases of transcripts encoding osteocalcin, osteonectin and COL1A1. Based on these results, the relationship between AChE and osteogenic differentiation status were closely correlated. [6] The increase of ALP activity could not be affected by treatment of the AChE inhibitors, which indicated the enzymatic activity of AChE didn’t directly relate to osteogenic differentiation process. [7] The response of osteoblastΔAChE to BMP2 was reduced as compared to WT. These results suggested that AChE might be involved in the BMP signaling to regulate bone cell differentiation.

662911.value: Possible development of the research could be as follow: 1. The detail signaling mediated by AChE in bone development could be determined, in particular the signaling cascades triggered by BMP. 2. The age-induced osteoporosis could be related to AChE expression; this possible relationship has to be investigated. 3. Genes responsible for AChE-meidated bone formation could be further determined, e.g. the gene array analysis in osteoblasts between ACHE-/- and WT mice.

662911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
662911.value: By over expressing PRiMA-linked AChE in primary cultured osteoblasts, or its related cell line, we provided different lines of evidence to support a new function of AChE in mediating bone differentiation. This osteogenic effect is mediated by the PRiMA-linked AChE that is localized on the surface of osteoblasts, and the enzymatic activity did not involve in this osteogenic effect. Over expression of either AChET alone, or PRiMA alone, or only G2 form AChE, cannot affect the differentiation process of cultured osteoblasts. The unique expression of PRiMA-linked AChE in calvarias of rat embryos and the decrease of bone density in ACHE-/- mice also strongly support the osteogenic function of AChE. Moreover, the AChE might be involved in the BMP signaling to regulate bone differentiation. For the first time, the current study shows the existence of PRiMA-linked AChE in bone cells, and which participates in the osteogenic differentiation regardless of its enzymatic activity.

663011.value: 金属纳米材料在水生生物的生物动力学，生物有效性和慢性毒性

663011.value: To manufacture, characterize, and study the biokinetics of engineered nanoparticles in aquatic organisms using a unique radiotracer methodology; To study the chronic toxicity of nanoparticles in aquatic animals, and the underlying chemical, physiological and biochemical mechanisms; To study the biokinetics of toxic metals in direct interaction with engineered nanomaterials.

663011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
663011.value: Nanotechnology nowadays provides extraordinary opportunities in diverse areas such as electronics, energy, water purification, and therapeutics. The economic impacts of engineered nanomaterials in industrial, consumer, and medical products are estimated to be $300 billion dollars this year and will reach to $1 trillion dollars by 2015. These figures have underscored the rapid increase in the potential for human exposure and environmental disposal. Inevitably, these nanomaterials will find their ways to the aquatic environments and may significantly impact the aquatic organisms as well as the ecosystems. However, the interaction of these nanomaterials with the environment and living systems is largely unknown and difficult to predict at present. Thus, there is an urgent and compelling need for environmental scientists to develop the capability to accurately measure and understand the impacts of the new technology on the environment and living systems. Key questions surrounding the environmental risk analysis of nanotechnology include the fate, transport, and behavior of nanomaterials in environmental media and biological matrices; the route and rate of exposure; and the response of living systems to such exposure. This timely project aims to provide the first systematic study on the biokinetics and chronic toxicity of silver and zinc oxide nanoparticles (as AgNP and ZnO, respectively) as well as the interactions of toxic metals with selected nanomaterials (carbon nanotubes, titanium dioxide and cerium dioxide nanoparticles) in aquatic organisms, including phytoplankton, zooplankton and fish. We will: 1) manufacture, characterize, and study the biokinetics of engineered AgNP and ZnO in aquatic organisms using unique radiotracer methodology; 2) study the chronic toxicity of these nanoparticles in aquatic animals, and the underlying chemical, physiological and biochemical mechanisms; 3) study the biokinetics of toxic metals in direct interaction with engineered nanomaterials. This frontier proposed research will take advantage of the sophisticated radiotracer methodology available in my laboratory to provide fundamental yet critical information about the fate, transport, and toxicity of nanoparticles in aquatic ecosystems. With the first application of our radiotracer technique, we will provide fundamental results on the kinetics, accumulation, and exposure of nanoparticles in the aquatic animals. We will also provide the first data on the significance of trophic transfer of nanoparticles, as well as the chronic toxicity on the life history of aquatic animals. Overall, this study will be instrumental for our new understanding of the biological behavior, bioavailability, and toxicity as well as for the risk analysis of nanoparticles in aquatic environments. 当前，纳米技术为多个领域，如电子、能源、水处理和医疗等提供了广阔的前景。据估计，今年工程纳米材料在工业，消费品和医疗产品中的价值为3000亿美元，到2015年将达到1万亿美元。这些数据强调了纳米材料可能加剧了对人类的暴露和环境处理。不可避免地，这些纳米材料将进入水环境，并严重影响水生生物和生态系统。但是，目前纳米材料和环境以及生物之间的相互作用尚不清楚并难以预测，所以急需环境科学家来准确测定和明确新技术对环境和生物的影响。 该项目将第一次系统研究银和氧化锌纳米颗粒的动力学和慢性毒性，以及有毒金属和纳米材料在水生生物内的相互作用。我们将：1) 人工合成和表征纳米银和氧化锌，并利用特殊的放射性示踪技术研究纳米材料在水生生物中的动力学过程；2) 研究纳米材料对水生生物的慢性毒性，及其化学、生理和生化机理；3) 研究在纳米材料直接作用下有毒金属的动力学。该项目将利用成熟的放射性元素示踪技术来研究纳米颗粒在水生生态系统中的运输，归宿和毒性，解决一些基础的但非常关键的问题。我们可以提供纳米材料在生物体内的动力学，累积和暴露等基本信息。该研究将对我们理解纳米材料在水生生物体内的行为，生物有效性和毒性以及对风险评价有极大地帮助。

663011.label: Realisation of objectives
663011.value: There were three objectives in this project, specifically: 1: To manufacture, characterize, and study the biokinetics of engineered metal nanoparticles using a unique radiotracer methodology We studied the biokinetics of AgNP, TiO2, and ZnO with the use of radiotracers (110mAg and 65Zn). One very unique aspect of this project was to use the radioisotope technology to synthesize or radiolabel the nanoparticles and then follow their biokinetics and toxicity in the organisms. Radiotracers are known to be sensitive and, in the case of gamma radiotracers, can be used to trace particles non-invasively in living animals. With the application of radiotracer methodology, we measured the water uptake, dietary assimilation, and elimination of NPs in the organisms. With the quantification of the biokinetic parameters such as the uptake rate constant and the dietary assimilation, we then separated the relative importance of these two uptake routes in the animals, using the well established kinetic modeling approach. Objective 2: To study the chronic toxicity of metal nanoparticles, and the underlying chemical, physiological and biochemical mechanisms We conducted both acute and chronic toxicity testing of NPs in organisms (daphnids and fish) and compared the dissolved vs. dietborne toxicity of nanoparticles (which has been neglected in previous studies). An important aspect of these toxicity testing was to couple with the bioaccumulation measurements. This was critical for conducting the toxicity testings with nanoparticles. We also specifically addressed whether the acute or chronic toxicity of nanoparticles was due to any changes in the physiological and biochemical processes of the organisms, as well as due to the release of free metal ion into solution. The physiological mechanisms were examined based on the ion flux and the feeding rates of animals. Biochemical mechanisms were examined based on the measurements of a suite of biomarkers. Objective 3: To study the biokinetics of toxic metals in direct interaction with ENMs We tested whether the nanoparticles can affect the biokinetics and toxicity of toxic metals in aquatic organisms. We choose Cd and Zn as representative toxic metals mainly because we have accumulated very substantial knowledge regarding their biokinetics and toxicity. We selected different NPs such as carbon nanotubes and TiO2. We first quantified the sorption and desoption behavior of metals with these nanomaterials. Biokinetics of Cd and Zn in the organisms were then determined either in direct interaction with the nanomaterials or in the presence of nanomaterials.

663011.label: Major findings and research outcome
663011.value: Overall, a large body of works was conducted in this project, as reflected by our many publications in top international journals (including 3 papers in Environmental Science and Technology, 2 papers in Water Research, 3 papers in Environmental Toxicology and Chemistry, one paper in Environmental Pollution and one review paper). Some of the main results are summarized as the followings: We employed the radioisotope (110mAg) to trace the behaviors of commercial AgNPs in Daphnia magna. Influx rates of AgNPs into daphnids were size dependent. The accurate quantification of AgNPs influx rate suggested an uptake pathway entirely different from that of AgNO3 (Zhao and Wang 2013). We also examined the effects of salinity on AgNPs to marine medaka (Oryzias melastigma) (Wang and Wang 2014, ETC). We first time radio-synthesized the nZnO and followed its uptake and depuration in D. magna, and showed a distinctive uptake mode of nZnO (Li and Wang 2013). We exposed Daphnia to commercial AgNPs and found the significant influences of AgNPs (without cysteine) on Na and Ca regulations. Soluble Ag released from AgNPs played a major role in the ionoregulatory dysfunction (Zhao and Wang 2013, ETC). We then investigated the trophic transfer of AgNPs from brine shrimp (Artemia salina) nauplii to marine medaka. The low bioavailability of dietary AgNPs could inhibit the whole-body Na+/K+-ATPase. This study highlighted the potential of trophically available AgNPs in bringing toxicity to marine fish (Wang and Wang 2014) We tested the influences of carbon nanotube (CNT) on metal uptake kinetics in Daphnia magna. Different CNTs exposures led to distinctive metal accumulation patterns. CNTs could serve as a new pathway for metal accumulation (Yu and Wang 2013). The toxicity of Cd in the presence of CNTs was tested in another study (Liu and Wang 2015). The LC50 of the groups with normal CNTs was significantly higher than the control group. In another study, metal binding with f-nC60 as modified nanoparticles could serve as a new pathway for the elevated metal accumulation in Daphnia (Yu and Wang 2014). We quantified Cd and Zn kinetics in Daphnia adsorbed on nano-TiO2. Uptake and retention of toxic metals were enhanced when they were adsorbed on nano-TiO2 (Tan et al. 2012). Concurrent measurements of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and metallothioneins (MTs) suggested that the increased metal uptake was mainly due to the increased number of binding sites provided by nano-TiO2 presented in the guts (Tan and Wang 2014).

663011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
663011.value: The greatest risk of nanotechnology is that the interaction of these nanomaterials with the environment and living systems is largely unknown and difficult to predict at present. There is thus an urgent need for environmental scientists to develop the capability to accurately measure and understand the impacts of the new technology on the environment and living systems. Key questions surrounding the environmental risk analysis of nanotechnology include the fate, transport, and behavior of nanomaterials in environmental media and biological matrices; the route and rate of exposure; and the response of living systems to such exposure. In further studies, it is important to integrate physicochemical kinetics and uptake kinetics in evaluating the bioavailability and toxicity of both NPs and dissolved ions. Despite the need for more uptake kinetic studies, the overall understanding of the physiochemical kinetics of NPs (e.g. aggregation, sedimentation, dissolution) in aquatic environment is also needed in order to have a systematic evaluation of the bioavailability of NPs to aquatic organisms. In future toxicological studies, more chronic exposures at the environmentally relevant low concentrations are desirable. Transformation of MNs within biological tissues should also be investigated in order to better understand their toxic mechanisms.

663011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
663011.value: Nanomaterials have novel properties and functions attributable to their small sizes and have been used in numerous electronic applications and commercial products. Nevertheless, the interaction between these novel properties and the environment and living systems is largely unknown. Key ecotoxicological issues surrounding the study of emerging nanotechnology include the fate, transport, and behavior of nanomaterials in environmental media and biological matrices; the route and rate of exposure; and the response of organisms to such exposure. All these information is essential for the risk analysis, yet most of these issues remain unresolved at present. This timely project aims to provide the first systematic data on the biokinetics and chronic toxicity of nanoparticles as well as the interactions of toxic metals with selected nanomaterials in aquatic organisms. We for the first time developed methods to synthesize the radiolabeled nanoparticles to study their biokinetics in the animals. The impacts of different physicochemical properties of nanoparticles were revealed. Such a kinetics study helps to accurately assess the routes and the rates of exposure as well as the trophic transfer of nanoparticles in aquatic ecosystems. The results are instrumental for the assessments of exposure and risk of nanoparticles in aquatic environments.

663111.label: Realisation of objectives
663111.value: Proper cell fate choice is essential for generating correct numbers of distinct myeloid subsets (macrophages and neutrophils) manifesting a wide spectrum of subset-specific activities during development and adulthood. Studies have suggested that macrophage vs neutrophil fate choice is primarily regulated by transcription factors; however, new intrinsic regulators and their underlying mechanisms remain to be elucidated. In the proposed study, we utilized zebrafish, a tropical fish whose blood cell development share many similarities to mammals, to tackle this issue. To dissect the genetic network that control macrophage and neutrophil development, Drs. Hao JIN and Yiyue ZHANG (my former postdoctoral fellows) as well as Li LI (my former Ph.D. student) performed genetic and biochemical analysis on four myeloid defective zebrafish mutants, runx1w84x, cmybhkz3, pu.1hkz6 and cebp1smu1 we have in the laboratory. They first showed that low and high Pu.1 activities determine embryonic neutrophil and macrophage fate, respectively. Subsequent analysis revealed that Runx1 is a downstream target of Pu.1 and inactivation and overexpression of Runx1 in zebrafish uncovers Runx1 as a key embryonic myeloid fate determinant that favors neutrophil over macrophage fate. Thus, Runx1 is induced by high Pu.1 level and in turn represses pu.1 expression, constituting a negative feedback loop that fashions a favorable pu.1 level required for balanced fate commitment to neutrophils versus macrophages. They then showed that inactivation of cMyb function specifically impairs neutrophil but not macrophage development, leading to the failure of granule formation in neutrophils. They further document that cMyb, Cebp1 and Runx1 work cooperatively to regulate granule formation in neutrophils by modulating the expression of a subset of granule forming protein genes. Finally, another former student Dr. Bo YAN investigated the molecular basis underlying neutrophil migration in response to tissue injury by time-lapse imaging and molecular analysis in zebrafish, and he was able to show that IL-1b and NADPH oxidase–mediated reactive oxygen species (ROS) play important roles in the regulation of neutrophil migration to the wound. In sum, our proposed objectives have been well achieved.

663111.label: Major findings and research outcome
663111.value: There are three major findings from our studies. Our first important finding is to define a genetic regulatory loop of two critical transcription factors, Pu.1 and Runx1, which governs the fate choice of macrophages vs neutrophils. This work has been published in BLOOD (119:5239-5249; 2012), a top tier journal in hematopoietic research. Our second finding is to show that the Il-1b–Myd88 axis and NADPH oxidase–mediated ROS signaling are two independent pathways that differentially regulate neutrophil migration during sterile inflammation. This work has been published in The Journal of Immunology (192:5998-6008, 2014). Finally, our third major finding is the identification of cMyb, which work together with Cebp1 and Runx1 for modulating the expression of downstream genes, as a critical transcription regulator in neutrophil granule formation. A manuscript describing this work is currently in the process of preparation.

663111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
663111.value: It will be of great interest to investigate how these four transcription factors (Pu.1, Runx1, cMyb and Cebp1) interact with each other in detail to regulate macrophage and meutrophil development.

663111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
663111.value: In vertebrates, macrophages and neutrophils are subclasses of white blood cells which manifest a wide spectrum of specific activities during pathogenic infection and tissue regeneration. In physiological condition, the number and function of these two cell types are tightly controlled during development and adulthood and irregularities of their cell number and function can lead to the onset and progression of severe human disorders. It has been known for some time that macrophages and neutrophils are generated from a common precursor, yet the precise molecular mechanisms governing the formation of these two cell types from the common precursors remain unclear. In this proposed study, we have utilized zebrafish, a tiny tropical fish whose white blood cells share many similarities to human, to investigate the development of macrophages and neutrophils. Our study reveals that two important molecules, Pu.1 and Runx1 form a regulatory loop that control the equilibrium between macrophages and neutrophils. This work is published in BLOOD (119:5239-5249; 2012), a top tier journal in hematopoietic research. In addition, we have also uncover that the Il-1b–Myd88 axis and NADPH oxidase–mediated ROS signaling are two independent signaling pathways that differentially regulate neutrophil migration during sterile inflammation. This work is published a The Journal of Immunology (192:5998-6008, 2014). Finally, we have also identified a new protein cMyb that acts cooperatively with two known molecules Cebp1 and Runx1 to regulate neutrophil maturation. A summary of this work will be submitted for publication in a top tier scientific journal.
