663511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
663511.value: Rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) is the most common soft tissue sarcoma in children and young adults. It is characterized by defined genetic changes together with the expression of one or several muscle-specific genes including MyoD, muscle α-actin, and desmin. It is thought to be derived from deregulated muscle progenitor cells. As proliferation and differentiation are two mutually exclusive cell fates, promotion of myogenic differentiation could serve as a potential therapeutic strategy to treat RMS. Although progress has been made in the past two decades in understanding the disease, more remains to be learnt in order to effectively treat RMS. In recent years, microRNAs (miRNA) have emerged as important regulators of gene expression and are known to participate in various cellular processes. Deregulation of miRNAs is known to be associated with various human diseases including cancers. Here, we aim to systematically identify miRNAs that are downregulated in RMS by promoter methylation, as these miRNAs may possess potential tumor suppressor functions. Our preliminary work has already identified one such miRNA that has never been characterized in RMS. It was downregulated in RD and Rh30, two cell lines derived from two subtypes of RMS respectively. Importantly, it was also downregulated in five of the eight tumor biopsies from RMS patients. Consistently, over-expression of this miRNA in both RD and Rh30 inhibited cell growth and migration, yet greatly enhanced myogenic differentiation. For selected miRNAs to be identified from our screen including the one we have already identified, we will first verify their low expression status in RMS tumor biopsies, followed by establishment of their tumor-suppressing properties. In addition, we will also try to identify the direct targets of these selected miRNAs and to link these targets to the development of RMS. Our work should be useful not only in further elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying the tumorigenesis of RMS but also in providing new molecular targets for future therapeutic treatment of RMS. 橫紋肌肉瘤(RMS)是青少年中最常見的軟組織肉瘤。它有其特異的基因突變並表達一種或幾種骨骼肌特異的蛋白質包括MyoD, 肌肉a-actin，及 desmin. 科學家們認為RMS源自失控的肌肉前體細胞。因為細胞增殖及分化互相排斥，刺激腫瘤細胞分化有可能可以做為控制RMS的一種手段。雖然過去20年我們對RMS有了很多了解，為了有效治療RMS我們仍需做更多的研究。近年來科學家們發現microRNA是細胞內重要的基因表達調控因子並參與細胞的各種活動。microRNA的失調與各類疾病包括癌症密切相關。在本研究計劃中，我們準備系統地找尋那些因基因啟動子甲基化而下調的microRNA，因為此類microRNA極可能有腫瘤抑制的功能。我們的初步研究已發現了一個尚未在RMS中研究過的具有腫瘤抑制的功能的microRNA。此microRNA的表達水平在兩種源自RMS的細胞株（RD及Rh30）中皆低。另外在我們檢驗的8個RMS腫瘤樣本中，有5個含有低表達的此microRNA。若在RD及Rh30細胞中過量表達此microRNA不僅可以抑制癌細胞的增值及遷移而且還增強它們向肌肉分化的能力。我們準備先在RMS腫瘤樣本中驗證篩選出來的microRNA是否確實因啟動子甲基化而低表達，並檢驗它們是否有腫瘤抑制的功能。我們會找尋這些microRNA直接調控的靶標基因並將它們和RMS的發生發展相聯繫。我們認為我們的研究工作不僅可以更深入地了解RMS的致癌機理，還可為臨床治療RMS提供新的藥物靶標。

663511.label: Realisation of objectives
663511.value: All the objectives listed in the proposal have been addressed and fully achieved. To identify potential tumor-suppressive microRNAs, we treated both RD (derived from embryonal RMS) and Rh30 (derived from alveolar RMS) cells with vehicle (DMSO) or 5’aza-deoxycytidine and compared microRNA expression profiles between mock-treated and 5’aza-deoxycytidine-treated cells using a Taqman probe-based qPCR screening system (i.e., Taqman Array) from Thermo Fisher. This system allowed us to examine 754 human microRNAs at the same time. Among them, we identified a dozen or so microRNAs that were downregulated by promoter hypermethylation in either or both type of RMS cells. To prove that these downregulated microRNAs do have tumor-suppressive functions, we over-expressed individual microRNAs in RD and Rh30 cells and compared their effects on cell growth with a control microRNA. miR-203 fulfilled all the initial screening criteria and was selected for detailed functional analysis.

663511.label: Major findings and research outcome
663511.value: • By RT-qPCR and MS-PCR with or without 5’aza-deoxycytidine treatment, we showed that miR-203 is downregulated by promoter hypermethylation in both RD and Rh30 cells and a large fraction of RMS biopsies. • Re-expression of miR-203 by transient transfection in RD and Rh30 cells inhibited tumor cell growth, migration, and invasion in cell culture models, but promoted terminal myogenic differentiation. • By bioinformatics analysis with TargetScan and MiRanda followed by experimental confirmation with Western blot and luciferase-3’UTR-based reporter assays, we showed that genes encoding p63 and leukemia inhibitory factor receptor (LIFR) were directly targeted by miR-203 in both RD and Rh30 cells. While p63 regulates the Notch pathway by transcriptionally upregulating the expression of Jagged1, LIFR regulates the JAK1/Stat1/Stat3-mediated pathway. Both the Notch and LIFR/JAK1/Stat1/Stat3 pathways negatively regulate terminal myogenic differentiation. Our data provide an explanation why re-expression of miR-203 in RD and Rh30 cells promoted terminal myogenic differentiation. • Furthermore, using nude mice injected subcutaneously with RD cells on both flanks, we showed that repeated injection of miR-203 into tumors grown on one flank of mice decreased tumor growth in vivo compared to that of a control microRNA into tumors grown on the other flank of mice.

663511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
663511.value: In our Taqman-qPCR-based microRNA screening, in addition to miR-203, we also identified several other microRNAs that were downregulated in RD and Rh30 cells by promoter hypermethylation. Among them, miR-515-5p caught our attention and was selected for further functional characterization. Like miR-203, miR-515-5p was downregulated in both RD and Rh30 cells and a large fraction of RMS biopsies. Re-expression of miR-515-5p in RD and Rh30 cells not only slowed down tumor cell growth in culture but also promoted myogenic differentiation. Our data showed that miR-515-5p is another key tumor-suppressive microRNA that is downregulated by promoter hypermethylation in RMS. We are currently investigating the underlying molecular mechanisms. Such studies should give us a better understanding of microRNAs that are perturbed during RMS development. This will lay a solid foundation for future clinical intervention.

663511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
663511.value: Rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) is the most common soft tissue sarcoma found in children and young adults. It is characterized by the expression of a number of skeletal muscle-specific proteins, including MyoD and muscle α-actin. However, unlike normal undifferentiated muscle cells (i.e., myoblasts), RMS cells differentiate poorly both in vivo and in culture. As microRNAs are known to regulate tumorigenesis, intensive efforts have been made to identify microRNAs that are involved in RMS development. In this work, we found that miR-203 was frequently down-regulated by promoter hypermethylation in both RMS-derived cell lines and RMS biopsies and could be reactivated by DNA-demethylating agents. Re-expression of miR-203 in RMS cells inhibited their migration and proliferation and promoted terminal myogenic differentiation. Mechanistically, miR-203 exerts its tumor-suppressive effect by directly targeting p63 and leukemia inhibitory factor receptor in RMS cells, which promotes myogenic differentiation by inhibiting the Notch and the JAK1/STAT1/STAT3 pathways, respectively. Our work reveals that miR-203 functions as a tumor suppressor in normal cells and that its down-regulation promotes RMS development.

663811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
663811.value: PDZ domain scaffold proteins serve as platforms in signaling pathways by nucleating multiple proteins into macromolecular complexes and targeting them to specific regions within cells. They are thus are critical for both the efficiency and specificity of signaling events. The 5 PDZ domains of Drosophila INAD are capable of binding to individual proteins (e.g. the TRP channel, PLCbeta, PKC, and cytoskeletons) forming a large protein complex referred to as “signalsome”. Via the INAD-mediated assembly of the signaling complex, fly photoreceptor cells are capable of responding to light signals with extremely fast kinetics as well as exceptionally large dynamic ranges. The visual dynamic signaling in Drosophila visual system critically depends on INAD PDZ5 conformational cycling between reduced and oxidized states in a light-dependent manner. How INAD cycles between its functionally distinct conformers is conceptually challenging, as the redox potential of photoreceptor cells is not known to fluctuate in response to light. In this proposal, we plan to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying the light-dependent conformational cycling of INAD between the reduced and the oxidized forms by combining biochemistry, redox chemistry, structural biology and cell biology approaches. We also plan to determine the structure of the INAD PDZ345/TRP channel complex, and to elucidate the molecular basis governing light-induced, reversible INAD/TRP dissociation. Finally, we plan to characterize the binding partners of the remaining PDZ domains in INAD. The successful execution of the proposed research are expected to make significant contributions towards understanding how scaffold proteins actively participate in dynamic regulations of signaling events in addition to the well-accepted roles in signaling complex assemblies. 由PDZ结构域组成的骨架蛋白，作为信号传导通路的平台，可以将多种蛋白质大分子组装成多分子复合物，同时，将其定位到细胞内的特定区域。因此，由PDZ结构域组成的骨架蛋白，对信号传导的效率以及特异性，起到了极其关键的作用。果蝇INAD蛋白是一个由 5个 PDZ结构域组成的骨架蛋白。它能够结合多个光信号传导过程中的重要蛋白（如TRP通道，磷酸酯酶C beta，蛋白激酶C和细胞骨架等），形成一个被称为“信号传导体”的蛋白复合物。通过这种蛋白复合物，果蝇的感光细胞，能够以极快的速度，在一个极大的动态范围内对光信号做出响应。在这种动态的视觉信号传导的过程中，INAD 的第5个PDZ结构域的构象变化，起到了关键的作用，而这种构象的变化是由光依赖的可逆氧化还原反应所引起的。 INAD蛋白是如何在功能不同的氧化和还原的构象之间实现转化的呢？这一问题，具有极大的挑战性。因为，我们并不知道，感光细胞的氧化还原电位，是否会随着光的照射而产生波动。因此，在这份计划书中，我们拟通过运用生物化学、氧化还原化学、结构生物学和细胞生物学的方法，解析INAD蛋白的这种光依赖性的氧化还原反应导致构象变化的分子机制；通过解析在我们之前的初步研究中发现的INAD PDZ345/TRP复合物的三维结构，来阐明INAD /TRP复合物依赖于光照的可逆结合的分子机理；寻找INAD蛋白中其余PDZ结构域的结合蛋白。我们可以预计，如果这项研究获得成功，将对理解“传统意义上的骨架蛋白如何在信号传导复合物中积极参与信号传导的动态调控”这一领域作出重大的贡献。

How light-induced acidification leads to the dissociation of the PDZ345/TRP-CT complex; b). What is the structural basis for the formation of the PDZ345/TRP-CT complex; c). How do the PDZ345/TRP-CT interaction and pH-induced complex dissociation in fly visual signaling are correlated functionally.

663811.label: Major findings and research outcome
663811.value: We have completed all three objectives proposed in the proposal, and have made very good progresses in multiple areas. First, we have completed the first objective as this part is mainly based on the preliminary findings that we have already accumulated during the preparation of the proposal. We discovered that the redox potential of INAD PDZ5 is allosterically regulated by direct conformational coupling with PDZ4. Formation of the PDZ45 supramodule locks PDZ5 in the reduced state by raising the redox potential of the Cys605/Cys645 disulfide by ~330 mV, whereas isolated PDZ5 is stable in the oxidized form. Acidification, potentially mediated via light and PLCbeta-mediated hydrolysis of PIP2, uncouples the PDZ45 supramodule, and subsequently disrupts the INAD/TRP channel interaction due to PDZ5 oxidation. The conformation-coupled redox potential cycling of INAD demonstrates that, in addition to being passive redox sensors, proteins can actively modulate their intrinsic redox potentials of disulfide bonds to exert regulatory roles in signaling. This part of research has been published in Cell as a cover article. In the second part, we have been elucidating the interaction of TRP channel with INAD in detail. We discover a completely novel interaction mode between INAD PDZ3 and TRP. Unlike all previously known PDZ/target interactions, INAD PDZ3 strongly and selectively binds with Drosophila TRP channel C-termini, mediated by specific recognition of an unexpected long 15 amino acids carboxyl-terminal. The complex structure of INAD PDZ3 and TRP channel tail reveals that, instead of inserting into the canonical PDZ/target binding groove, the last 15 amino acids of TRP forms an unusual β-hairpin structure, and strongly binds to a surface formed by βB, βC and αA of INAD PDZ3. Our finding significantly expands the concept of the PDZ/target interaction mode, and has major implications in understanding other PDZ domain-mediated protein complex formations. This part of the work has been completed, and a manuscript is essentially completed (attached in this report) and will be submitted for publication shortly. We have also solved the structure of INAD PDZ2 in complex with the C-terminal tail of eye-PKC. We discovered that a ~65-residue fragment N-terminal to the canonical PDZ2 sequence is obligatory for the proper folding of the PDZ domain. The structure of the extended PDZ2/eye-PKC tail peptide complex not only reveals the extensive interactions between the N-terminal extension and the canonical PDZ2, but also uncovers the specific interaction between the eye-PKC tail and the extended PDZ2. We further showed that using a real-time NMR-based assay that Ser314 located at the center of the αB-helix of the extended PDZ2 can be rapidly phosphorylated by eye-PKC. Phosphorylation of Ser314 dissociates eye-PKC from the extended PDZ2, thus providing a potential mechanism for eye-PKC-mediated negative regulation of fly visual signaling. Finally, we showed that NPDZ2 undergoes an acid-induced unfolding due to uncoupling of the N-terminal extension and the canonical PDZ2 domain, suggesting that the light-induced acidification in microvilli can also dissociate eye-PKC from the INAD scaffold. A manuscript describing this part of the research has also been drafted (also attached in this report) and should be submitted for publication shortly.

663811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
663811.value: With the completion of target bindings of essentially all individual PDZ domains of INAD, the foundation for in vitro reconstitution of INAD-assembled Drosophila photo reception complex becomes more realistic. This is one of our long-term goal on this line of the project. The second line of the project is to further elucidate light-induced, acidification-mediated INAD complex dissociation. We plan to investigate whether acidification-mediated signaling process is a general paradigm in mammals in the future.

663811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
663811.value: The great majority of animals have visual detection systems known as photoreceptors of one sort or another for detecting food source, mate, predator/prey, orientation, etc. For example, it takes only a fraction of a second for us to catch a basketball in a game or to doge a car on a road. It is known that the visual systems of flies are able to detect vast environmental range of intensities spanning more than a million fold of magnitude from starlight to direct sunlight with extreme rapid speed of tens of millisecond time scale. We discovered in this project that a scaffold protein called INAD in the animal eyes can undergo a light-dependent architectural or molecular shape change, thereby regulating light signal detection speed as well as signal output amplitude. This light-dependent molecular shape change of INAD protein is resulted from a rapid oxidation/reduction cycle in animal eyes. Under dim light, the reduced INAD protein keeps the fly visual system at the highest sensitivity for light detection. Increasing light intensities proportionally convert INAD into oxidized form and thus tune down the signal receiving sensitivity of photoreceptors. Thus, the INAD scaffold protein functions as a “rheostat” in the animal visual detection system. The discovery made during this research has far more broad implications in many different types of biological signal transduction events that are related to human diseases including cancer, neuro-degenerations, various immune disorders, etc; as protein oxidations are known to be associated in these biological events.

663911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
663911.value: Organ development requires accurate control of total numbers and types of cells, that is, the precise regulation of cell proliferation and cell differentiation. Recent findings have linked these two fundamental processes of organism development. Understanding the molecular mechanism governing the linkage between these two processes will have profound philosophical and medical impacts. In eukaryotic cell proliferation, the periodic assembly and disassembly of crital pre-replicative complexes (Pre-RC) at the replication origins ensure that only one genomic DNA replication occurs in each cell cycle. The replicative helicase, minichromosome maintenance (Mcm) complex, is loaded to replication origin, which is in complex with origin recognition complex (Orc) and Cdc6, by Cdt1. However, the detailed molecular mechanism of this loading process is still elusive. In the case of regulating embryonic stem cell division, it is known that once a characteristic set of Hox genes is activated its expression is maintained in the progeny of that lineage. It is reported that the cell cycle regulator geminin associates transiently with Hox proteins. The interaction between geminin and Hox proteins prevents Hox proteins from binding to DNA, and inhibits Hox-dependent transcriptional activation of endogenous downstream target genes. Geminin also directly interacts with Cdtl preventing replication. Therefore geminin is coordinating cell proliferation and cell differentiation control through competitive interactions. We have been very interested in elucidating the structural mechanism that regulates cell proliferation and differentiation, especially, in understanding the structural basis of Mcm chromatin loading, inhibition of cell proliferation and differentiation, epigenetic control, as well as the replication origin recognition. Previously, we have determined the NMR structures of Hox-Geminin and Mcm6-Cdt1 complexes. These complex structures allow us to visualize the parts of molecular mechanism of genomic DNA replication, inhibition of Hox mediated cell differentiation, and the possible interplay between these two processes at molecular level for the first time. In this proposed research, we will extend our efforts to determine more NMR structures of proteins complexes involved abovementioned processes. More specifically, we will study the structure and function of Orc6/Cdt1, Hox/Cdc6, Mcm5/Stat, and newly identified Cdt1/Geminin protein complexes, and study the function of phosphorylation and acetylation of these proteins to further understand the detailed molecular mechanisms involved. 700311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
700311.value: There has been a rapid development in organic materials for photovoltaic cells in recent years. Compared to convention inorganic materials based photovoltaic cells, organic materials enjoy the advantages that they are highly processable, and the structure of molecules can be easily modified in order to optimize their properties. However, several major issues such as low carrier mobilities, low stability, and narrow optical absorption band still need to be addressed. In this proposal, we propose to design and synthesize various molecular and polymeric metal complexes that exhibit low electronic bandgap in order to harvest photons more efficiently in the near infrared region. A series of molecular and polymeric metal complexes with intramolecular charge transfer character will be synthesized. In the first approach, metal complexes will be introduced to the bridging group on the ligands, which connect electron donating and accepting units. In the second approach, the metal complexes will be positioned at the electron accepting units. The main design idea is to lower the electronic bandgap by introducing the metal complexes, which could perturb the excited state energy level of the complexes. The photophysical and electrochemical properties of the materials obtained will be thoroughly characterized, and the experimental and theoretical calculation results will be compared in order to understand the fundamental details of the light harvesting processes. For the promising materials obtained, they will be fabricated into multilayer thin film or dye-sensitized solar cells. 700311.label: Realisation of objectives
700311.value: Objective 1: In this project, we have developed different series of molecular and polymeric materials that exhibit great potential to be photosensitizing materials. These type of compounds include ruthenium complex containing polymers based ondifferent 2,2'-bipyridine ligand derivatives. The complexes were incorporated into conjugated polymer main chains by conventional palladium catalyzed coupling reaction. In addition, we have also developed other organic molecules based on truxene core units and donor-acceptor molecules with pyrazinopyrazine bridging units. These molecules exhibit different optical absorption in the visible and near IR regions. Objective 2: The photosensitizing properties of the new materials have been investigated. Theoretical computations were performed on some molecules in order to understand the origin of the electronic transitions observed. In addition some of the polymers are able to function as dispersants for carbon nanotubes, and the physical properties of the hybrid materials forms were also investigated in detail. Objective 3: The photovoltaic properties of some metal containing polymers were studied by the fabrication of multilayer devices. These molecules were introduced to the surface of titanium dioxide for the fabrication of solar cells. Other than solar cell performance, we have also performed detailed investigation in the fundamental photoexcitation and electron transfer processes occurred in the devices and the hybrid materials.

700311.label: Major findings and research outcome
700311.value: The project can be divided into two major parts: the synthesis of different photosensitizing materials and the characterization of them by both experimental and theoretical approaches. Different types of photosensitizing dye molecules were synthesized. They are based on truxene cores (ref 1), transition metal complexes (ref 2), and molecules with donor-acceptor structures (ref 4) that exhibit intramolecular charge transfer transition. In addition, functional block polymers incorporated with photosensitizers and pyrene were also synthesized. These types of polymers undergo strong pi-pi interaction with the surface carbon nanotube, and upon mixing carbon nanotube, new polymer-carbon nanotube hybrid materials were obtained. It was interesting to observe that the sensitizers are able to enhance the photoconductivity of the hybrid materials, which was confirmed by photoconductive atomic force microscopy. This is a new experimental method based on modification of existing atomic force microscope. In addition to photocurrent response, we also worked together with Prof. David Phillips's research group to investigate the fundamental photophysical and charge transfer dynamics in these polymer-nanotube hybrids (ref 3 and 6). Ultrafast time-resolved transient spectroscopy was used to probe the photoexcitation and the subsequent formation (and decay) of the excited state species. The results are of importance in understanding the charge generation and transfer upon photoexcitation, and will be helpful in designing new photosensitizers in the future.

700311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
700311.value: We report the synthesis of new donor-acceptor (D-A) type molecules by a new and versatile approach (ref 4). This is a general synthetic methodology to construct D-A type molecules in which the donor and acceptor are bridged by pyrazinopyrazine units. We are in the process of developing different series of new molecules by systematic approach. Different electron donor and acceptor units have been adopted. The nature of the charge transfer excited states will be studied by both experimental and theoretical approach. TD-DFT methods will be employed to study the electronic ground/excited states. In addition, new transition metal complexes may also be synthesized by this approach. We have previously demonstrated that the presence of transition metals could strongly perturb the excited state properties in this kind of molecules. We expect that new photosensitizers with broader optical absorption spectra could be synthesized by this approach.

700311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
700311.value: The development of new molecules that can absorb within ultraviolet-visible-infrared region has been a very interesting challenge to chemists/scientists. Those molecules that can absorb strongly in a specific wavelength are potential candidates for light sensing devices. The response of the device will be dependent on the optical absorption properties of the molecules concerned. In this project, we have developed different novel light absorbing molecules by new synthetic approach. It is possible to fine-tuned the light absorption properties by slightly changing the structural units in the molecules. We have also carried out experiments in order to understand the more fundamental processes related to the generation of excited states, and how fast are electrons being transported in these molecules. The results obtained will be very important for us to understand the structure-property relationship, and to design molecules with improved light absorption in the future.

700711.label: Project Objectives
700711.value: We will generalize our open system TDDFT and develop the numerical methods beyond the existing adiabatic wide-band limit (AWBL) approximation. Techniques in conventional Master equation approach will be adopted so that the resulting TDDFT will be applicable to finite temperatures. We will take into account of the effects of nuclei vibrations in our formalism. This can be done implicitly. Nuclei may be considered as a part of the environment, and their effects can be included implicitly into the self-energy. The resulting self-energy due to electron-phonon interaction can be simply added to the overall self-energy in the existing formalism. One crucial issue is the computational time. We have demonstrated that it is routine to carry out the TDDFT simulations of nano-devices containing hundreds of atoms up to tens of femtoseconds on a single CPU. To extend the simulation time up to picoseconds, we need to run our computer programs on parallel machines and the state-the-art GPU clusters. We will thus parallelize our computer programs and rewrite our codes for GPU computing. Another way to increase the computational efficiency is to implement our method with an approximate DFT method, density-functional tight-binding (DFTB) method. Since our TDDFT is integrated in time, we may simulate various dynamic processes directly in real time. Time-dependent current density distribution provides an intuitive picture of the electric response of an electronic device, and has important implications on electron migration and heat generation. The switch speed of the transistor is an important parameter. For the electronic devices of ~10 nm size, the switch time of the gate is expected on the order of 1~10 fs. However, recently there were evidences that it may take much longer time for the current to reach its steady state after the gate is switched on. As our TDDFT method will be generalized to be applicable for finite temperature, we will investigate systematically the ultrafast switching process of the emerging electronic devices operating at finite temperatures. We will also study the equivalent circuits, dephasing effects and the heat dissipation mechanisms of nanoscopic electronic devices at finite temperatures. The systems of study will be carbon-nanotube-, graphene- and silicon-based nanoelectronic devices.

700711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
700711.value: The remarkable miniaturization of semiconductor microelectronics over the past few decades has fundamentally shaped our everyday lives. If the miniaturization trend continues, devices are expected to reach their physical limit before year 2020. By that time, electronic devices will no longer work under the current designs, and may require conceptually different device structures and operation principles. In addition, new materials, such as low dimensional materials and spin materials, may be introduced. Modeling plays a critical role in these efforts. The main difficulty for the existing simulation software tools lies in the limitation of continuum models used in the current simulation tools. For the emerging electronic devices, atomic features lead to large device-to-device variability, and quantum effects become important. Existing simulation tools cannot account for, or even be patched up to address these effects. Therefore, next generation simulation methods and software are urgently needed. First-principles methods have been developed to simulate steady state currents in molecular and nanoscopic electronic devices. On the other hand, there are growing interests to understand the ultrafast processes in these devices, and thus an urgent need for accurate quantum mechanical methods to simulate these transient processes. Recently we developed such a method. As it is formulated as an equation of motion for reduced single-electron density matrix, its computational time is much reduced compared to those of conventional Master equation approaches, and has thus been applied successfully to simulate transient currents through various molecular and nanoscopic structures at zero temperature. In this project we will develop further our theory, and in particular, the numerical algorithms by adopting the existing techniques of conventional quantum dissipation theory, and apply the resulting method to study the ultrafast processes in nanoelectronic devices operating at finite temperatures. Besides the theoretical development and numerical algorithms, another key issue will be the efficiency of our computer programs, which will be parallelized and rewritten to run on graphics processing units (GPUs). To improve the computational efficiency further, our method will be implemented with an approximate density-functional theory method, the density-functional tight-binding (DFTB) method. With all these techniques developed and incorporated in our numerical codes, we will be ready to investigate various important issues in emerging electronics such as dephasing, heat generation, equivalent circuit, current distribution and switch speeds. To understand the physics of these processes, we will perform simulations on carbon-nanotube-, graphene-nanoribbon- and silicon-nanostructure-based electronic devices.

700711.label: Realisation of objectives
700711.value: 1) We have generalized our TDDFT method for open system and developed numerical methods beyond the existing adiabatic wide-band limit (AWBL) approximation. The resulting TDDFT method can now be applied to finite temperatures. 2) The effects of nuclei vibrations have been taken into account in two ways, implicitly and explicitly. In the implicit way, nuclei are considered as part of the environment, and their vibration effect is addressed by electron-phone coupling and contributed to the self-energy term of existing formalism. Meanwhile, we also implemented a TDDFT based Ehrenfest dynamics method to consider the nuclei motions explicitly. 3) Computational efficiency is crucial to put our method into the simulation of realistic systems. To achieve this goal, we have parallelized our code, employed density-functional tight-binding (DFTB) method and developed various algorithms to speed up the calculation. Parallelization has been applied to the energy integration of Green’s function. Over 90% efficiency is achieved since each energy point has high level of data independence and the communication overhead is low. For fast algorithms, we have implemented the Block-iterative algorithm for fast evaluation of self-energy matrices, and the Selected Inversion algorithm to fully consider the sparsity of the matrices used in NEGF calculations. On the other hand, an approximate computational framework has been developed. In the context of NEGF, by employing a newly developed X-formulation and a projection-based nonlinear model order reduction (MOR) approach, we successfully reduced the large number of energy points required for large applied biases simulations. The efficiency has been confirmed by numerical simulation, and the related work has been published. 4) With the theory development and fast algorithms implemented to speed up the simulation, we successfully applied our method to study many interesting phenomena and emerging electronics in time domain. For the first time in the world, we directly modelled the current of photovoltaic device and calculated the optoelectronic properties such as PCE, photo-absorption coefficient, mobility and recombination rate purely from quantum mechanical simulation. With the newly developed method, we also studied the quantum interference effect that occurs when electrons can follow more than one pathway through the molecular entity. The dynamical picture allows understanding how the interference are developed, and might suggest schemes for which switching could be attained.

700711.label: Major findings and research outcome
700711.value: Basing on our previous work, we have extended our time-dependent density functional theory for open system (TDDFT-OS) beyond the wide-band-limit (WBL) approximation. A major breakthrough is that we have developed a rigorous TDDFT formalism for open quantum system (OQS), with one and one only approximation: the environment is in thermal equilibrium. Subsequently the resulting TDDFT-OS has been generalized to include phonon effects or explicit nuclear dynamics by employing Ehrenfest dynamics. TDDFT-OS method has been implemented for parallel computing and DFTB model for simulating large open systems. Finally TDDFT-OS has been used to simulate realistic open quantum systems and interesting results have been obtained. In particular, we have studied the following two systems. Quantum mechanical simulations of realistic photovoltaic devices For the first time in the world, we developed a quantum mechanical simulation method to model directly the current of photovoltaic device [J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 5, 1272 (2014)]. It employs the DFTB method to describe the electronic structure, non-equilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) formalism to model the quantum transport and many-body theory to treat for electron-phonon interaction. Different from all the existing numerical methods for photovoltaics, our method provides a full quantum mechanical simulation of the dynamic photovoltaic processes and a direct calculation of the optoelectronic properties such as PCE, photo-absorption coefficient, mobility and recombination rate. It presents an important step towards the prediction of the properties of photovoltaic devices and the ultimate design of these devices from first-principles. Interference controlled molecular transistor and electronic coherence A key area in molecular electronics involves quantum interference that occurs when electrons can follow more than one pathway through the molecular entity. When the phases developed along parallel pathways are inequivalent, interference effects can substantially reduce overall conductance. A lot of related works have been done in energy-domain. But there has been little dynamical study of such interference effects. By employing our TDDFT-OS method, we investigated the quantum interference in benzene structures in time-domain. Through the simulation results, we show that interferences require time to develop. The dynamical picture allows understanding how the interference are developed, and might suggest schemes for which switching could be attained. The correlation between the magnitude of current and the electronic coherence reveals the quantum interference nature of such electronic structures, and the mechanism of switching. [J. Phys. Chem. Lett., 5 (15), 2748–2752 (2014).]

700711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
700711.value: TDDFT-OS theory and resulting numerical methods have been firmly established. The remaining challenges are to apply them to interesting realistic systems/devices and help experimentalists interpret their findings. One important area is the multi-dimensional spectroscopy for realistic systems and their interpretation, as the spectra are often complex and thus difficult to interpret. TDDFT-OS is an ideal tool for interpreting 2D optical spectra of complex systems. Another area is 2D X-ray spectra. We plan to apply TDDFT-OS to study the charge transport dynamics in organic devices, an area of intense debate.

700711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
700711.value: The most important breakthrough of the project is the development of a rigorous first-principles method for open quantum systems. A time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT) has been formulated for quantum transport, and the resulting theory is termed as TDDFT-OS. Moreover, we have developed two numerical methods to solve the complex differential-integral equations, among which is itself an important breakthrough in the field for it has solved a long-term problem in the field of quantum dissipation theory, the zero temperature bottleneck for simulating open systems. Building upon the rigorous TDDFT-OS theory, we have included the effects of phonons by treating them as a boson bath and introducing self-energy to account for their effects. We can also model explicitly the nuclear dynamics by employing Ehrenfest dynamics method. Besides these methodology developments, TDDFT-OS has been used to simulate the realistic devices. We studied quantum-interference controlled molecular transistor in collaboration with Mark Ratner of Northwestern University, the pioneer of molecular electronics. Our work has revealed the intriguing relation between coherence and transport. We have also studied a realistic photovoltaic device full quantum mechanically for the first time. This work is now been extended to study different photovoltaic devices and light emitting diodes.

700911.label: Project Objectives
700911.value: Study how the local properties including magnetic field structure, electric field, charge and current distributions and non-local parameters, e.g. surface magnetic field and temperature, inclination angle and viewing angle, can affect the phase average spectrum and pulse separation of gamma-ray pulsars. We also study the detailed phase-resolved spectrum of individual gamma-ray pulsar observed by Fermi satellite. Using the Monte Carlo simulation method to study the statistical properties of gamma-ray pulsars in terms of outer gap model to explain the possible correlations between observed parameters. Study the gamma-ray emission properties from millisecond pulsars and their relations of evolution, in particular how gamma-ray emission can affect the spin-up/spin-down evolution of pulsars. With the better understanding of gamma-ray emission from millisecond pulsars, we may be able to find more millisecond gamma-ray pulsars and more gamma-ray globular clusters, where millisecond pulsars are the emitters.

700911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
700911.value: 脈衝星是快速旋轉和強磁化的中子星。他們像單相發電機，年輕的脈衝星，其潛在脈衝星磁層下的電壓可以超過10 ^15 伏特。這種高電壓可以加速帶電粒子到極相對論速度，這些粒子被迫沿曲線強磁場中運動和發射光子的能量大於10 ^9eV。這些高能光子在理解脈衝星磁層的電動力學中發揮了非常重要的角色。其實大多數的脈衝星除了很年輕脈衝星-像螃蟹脈衝星，其伽瑪射線可以直接逃離脈衝星磁層，它可以提供直接探測的加速區域的屬性和磁場結構、本地電場強度、 密度等。當前在我們的星系中被觀測控到的穩定伽馬點源只僅有脈衝星。在2008年之前僅有7脈衝星 被證實為伽瑪射線脈衝星，只能提供非常有限的學習伽瑪射線脈衝星的屬性的資訊。在2008 年末發射的一個非常強大的伽瑪射線衛星稱為"費米"，當時在發射前，稱為"GLAST"，情況已完全改變。只在兩年觀察時間費米已檢測到超過70伽瑪射線脈衝。最重要的是伽瑪射線脈衝星中有許多是最快速旋轉的脈衝星稱為"毫秒脈衝星"，它們有很低的表面磁場通常是10 ^8- 10 ^9 高斯。雖然所有毫秒伽瑪射線脈衝星都是 不在球狀星團，但是銀河中發現八個球狀星團已檢測到伽瑪射線。人們普遍認為這些伽馬射線球狀星團的伽馬射線也是從球狀星團內部的毫秒脈衝星發射的。弱磁場毫秒脈衝星和強磁場典型脈衝星的形成過程是不同的。前者被認為是很老的中子星 (> 10 ^9 年），但它們是吸收其伴星物質達毫秒週期，後者是 出生通過超新星爆發。由於伽瑪射線可以直接探測發射地區的特性，通過比較這兩個脈衝星群體的光譜特性，我們就能夠瞭解毫秒脈衝星的演變。此外，我們要研究伽瑪射線的發射如何可以影響毫秒脈衝星在晚的演化階段。

700911.label: Realisation of objectives
700911.value: (1)For objective 1, we model the radiation from pulsars by using a 3D magnetospheric geometry, in which the local magnetic field, electric field, charge and current distribution will affect the radiation properties of pulsars. We have applied our model to large class of pulsars including normal pulsars, magnetars, binary millisecond pulsars and gamma-ray binaries (cf. publications 1,5, 8, 10,13). In addition we analyze the satellite data to compare our model results (pub. 2,3, 4, 11, 12). (2)For objective 2, we use Monte Carlo simulation method to generate a population of gamma-ray pulsars. We show that the radiation properties of the observed gamma-ray pulsars, i.e. the spectral index, cut-off energy, intensity, are greatly affected by the viewing angle. The main reason why these properties are viewing angle dependent because the total emission is summed over the contribution from various parts of the magnetosphere. All radiation by relativistic electrons/positrons are emitted tangent to the field lines. For a fixed viewing angle it represents the radiation come from the same tangent field lines. We have compared our model results with observed data and published in Pub.(1) (3)In objective 3, we study the gamma-ray emission from millisecond pulsars (MSPs) including MSPs in the galactic field and in the globular clusters. In Pub.6 and 13, we consider a general model of high energy emission from MSPs after accretion, we show that the time dependent temperature evolution on surface can affect the gamma-ray emission due to photon-photon pair creation process. We search the X-ray and gamma-ray emission from MSPs in globular clusters (pub. 15 and pub. 9). We also study the x-ray and gamma-ray properties of MSPs in the field (e.g. pub. 14) and in the binary system(e.g. pub. 15).

Study the gamma-ray emission properties from millisecond pulsars and their relations of evolution, in particular how gamma-ray emission can affect the spin-up/spin-down evolution of pulsars. With the better understanding of gamma-ray emission from millisecond pulsars, we may be able to find more millisecond gamma-ray pulsars and more gamma-ray globular clusters, where millisecond pulsars are the emitters.

700911.label: Major findings and research outcome
700911.value: (1)We use the Monte Carlo simulation to study the emission properties of gamma-ray pulsars including their spatial distribution, flux distribution, spectral index distribution, cut-off energy distribution by taking into account the possible distribution of inclination angle and viewing angle, which determine which part of pulsar magnetosphere we are observing. Our model distributions are consistent with the Fermi first gamma-ray pulsar catalog results. This is paper (1)in part C (2)We used the public available data including Fermi, Chandra, Swift, XMM to study the properties of known gamma-ray pulsars. In addition we are able to discover new gamma-ray pulsars by using the Fermi data, which are updated in their website every day and are open to public any time. For example we have discovered a new pulsar in M28, we are also able to identify new X-ray diffuse component 47 Tuc and pulsed X-ray component in PSR J2021 and PSR B 1957 etc. Most important we are the first group to discover pulsar wind component in the first Black Widow millisecond pulsar, PSR B 1957. These results published in paper 2-4, 6-13, 15. (3)By using pulsar gamma-ray properties, we are able to explain the detail orbital dependent multi-wavelength emission properties ranging from X-rays, GeV and TeV for two gamma-ray binaries, i.e. PSR B1259-63/LS2883 and LS 5039. We point out that in Superior Conjunction we should be able to detect pulsar wind contribution whereas in Inferior Conjunction the Doppler Boosting effect must be considered. These results published in paper 5 and 16. (4)We use the outer gap model to explain high energy emission properties of gamma-ray pulsar. In particular we give very detail model fitting for the first millisecond pular PSR B1937+21 and why some millisecond pulsars their radio pulse and gamma-ray pulse are aligned. Our results published in paper 14.

700911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
700911.value: We believe that the compact objects in many gamma-ray binaries are actually gamma-ray pulsars. With this assumption it is much easier to explain their orbital dependent energy spectrum. By fitting the observed properties we are able to constrain the rotation properties of these hypothetical pulsars. By searching their rotation period we will be able to point these compact objects are indeed pulsars. Some gamma-ray pulsars exhibit very unusual high energy spectrum in particular in the energy range >10 GeV, which does not match the expected power-law with exponential cut-off spectrum. In fact these gamma-ray pulsars their high energy spectra are better to be described by a steep power-law instead of exponential decay spectrum, most famous examples including the Crab pulsar, Vela pulsar and Geminga pulsar. We believe that the outergap is actually a dynamical gap not a steady state gap, which can produce photons with energy >10GeV. In our next GRF project we will study the above points.

700911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
700911.value: In this project we find that the general gamma-ray emission properties can be qualitatively described by the outer gap model, which suggest that there exists an electrostatic accelerator located in the outer magnetophere of pulsar near the light cylinder, where the co-rotation speed equals the speed of light. We also use the public available achival data in radio, optical, X-rays and gamma-rays to study the properties of pulsars or use these achival data to identify new gamma-ray pulsar and new emission component. We are the first group to discover a new gamma-ray pulsar in M28 and find a pulsar wind component in the first Black Widow pulsar system. We believe that our study makes our team become a reputable team in gamma-ray pulsar community. We are the team outside the Fermi instrumentation, which publish largest gamma-ray pulsar papers by using the Fermi public data. We find that some gamma-ray pulsar exhibit non-exponential decay spectrum which may suggest that steady state description for these pulsars are not appropriate instead the dynamical state is more suitable. We also believe that some gamma-ray binaries with un-known nature compact object, which may turn out to be pulsars.

701611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
701611.value: 氢原子迁移是阳离子自由基在气相裂解反应中的重要前体。在这项研究计划中，我们主要集中研究α中心的自由基在多肽中的特征，包括：（a）采用传统的串联质谱仪肽低能量碰撞诱导解离（CID）技术，调查的什么样的结构特征会促进多肽主链以及支链的的氢原子的转移（HAT）；（b）研究α中心多肽阳离子自由基如何转移到其他中心自由基，包括α-，β - 和γ-中心的自由基离子；（c）探索小到中型肽段中热力学和动力学如何影响竞争性的自由基迁移途径（自由基或质子诱导）。解离途径是多肽自由基架构和α中心为始发位点的重要反应基础。拟议工作的总体思路是，质子被囚禁在侧链上，从而降低氢原子迁移的能垒。通过使用CID质谱实验和理论密度泛函理论（DFT）计算，我们计划阐述统治裂解反应前的自由基迁移可行性的影响因素。这些研究将为发现该反应进程的内在因素、自由基位点的角色以及统治氢原子迁移的自由基迁移和随之发生的与质子诱导裂解相竞争裂解反应提供宝贵的见解。

701611.label: Realisation of objectives
701611.value: The project was started with the kinetics and energetics determination of the fragmentation of arginine containing peptides. We have examined the competition between the interconversion of other radical cationic tripeptide isomers and dissociation leading to α-radical migrations among α-carbon centers along the peptide backbones of the model systems using density functional theory (DFT) calculations and Rice–Ramsperger–Kassel–Marcus (RRKM) calculations in combination with low-energy CID experiments. The fragmentation of radical cationic peptides is considerably different from the dissociation of their corresponding protonated peptide ions, accelerating the possible implementation of novel peptide sequencing approaches for protein identification and peptide characterization. The energetics and dynamics of Cα–C, Cα–Cβ, and Cβ–Cgammabond cleavages after α-centered radical migration have been determined. A special configured Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometer (FTICR-MS) was utilized to perform a series of time –resolved and collision energy-resolved surface-induced dissociation (SID) experiments. These experiments demonstrated different kinetics of formation of several primary product ions of peptides with and without arginine residue, whereas the energetics and dynamics of which were determined by Rice-Ramsperger-Kassel-Marcus (RRKM) modeling of the experimental data. Our results showed that CIDs of the isomeric radical cationic tripeptides [with well-defined initial radical sites at their first α-carbon atoms, generate [b2 − H]•+ species as the predominant ions. Replacing the middle glycine residue with an arginine residue, giving [G•RL]+ and [G•RI]+, respectively, leads to the formation of a rich array of fragment ions and some diagnostic ions resulting from side chain losses. The distinct differences in the fragmentations of the arginyl- and non-arginyl-containing peptide radical ions reveal that the radicals migrate more readily in the presence of the basic arginine residue. This finding is supported by DFT calculations, which revealed that the arginine residue sequesters the mobile proton, resulting in (i) higher energy barriers against the charge-driven pathways and (ii) energy barriers for hydrogen atom transfers. It was followed by a study on the competition between the interconversion of other radical cationic tripeptide isomers and dissociation of them. Indeed, basic arginine residue could manipulate the fragmented ions n low energy collision induced dissociation (CID) experiments, and the observation has already been rationalized by density functional theory (DFT). Characterizations on the model systems of α-carbon–centered radical peptide analogues, both neutral and cationic have been used to investigate radical propagation mechanisms. Details of all these works have been published.

702511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
702511.value: We plan to carry out theoretical investigation on the thermodynamics of proton binding/exchanging in important biological and chemical molecules. Proton binding, along with the reversed process of proton releasing, is one of the most fundamental chemical processes. Accurate computer simulations on the thermodynamics of proton binding will help us to understand the basic physics behind this process. More importantly, they will help us to reveal the mechanistic roles of proton binding in many complex biochemical processes. The planned research is organized along two lines: developments of accurate, ab initio quantum chemistry based simulation methods for the modeling of the thermodynamics of the proton binding and applications of these methods to the simulation of important chemical and biochemical processes. Specific tasks for the current project include: (1) Development of combined ab initio quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical methods with the proper treatment of long-range electrostatic interactions; (2) Development of efficient free energy simulation methods for the simulation of concurrent multiple proton binding processes in proteins; (3) Free energy simulations for the pKa of small organic molecules in aqueous solution; (4) Simulations of the pKa of the hydroxyl groups of ribose; (5) Simulations of the concurrent proton titration process for the four Histidine residues of the staphylococcal nuclease; (6) Simulations of the proton binding coupled conformation selection in the substrate binding process of RGS12-PDZ domain. The methodology developments in this work will not only build up the foundation for the simulations planned here, but also make important contributions to the theoretical investigation of other important chemical processes, such as enzymatic reactions and heterogeneous catalysis. The pKa simulations also possess important significances in different ways. The pKa simulation of small organic molecules will establish a calibration standard for many related simulation works, such as the absolute solvation free energy of proton. The pKa simulation of ribose is intended to settle a longstanding question regarding the chemistry and activity of RNA molecules, which are very different from DNA. The simulation of proton binding processes in the staphylococcal nuclease and PDZ domain will address several important issues in protein science, such as how intra-molecular electrostatic interactions and ions affect the pKa of titratable groups in proteins, and how proton binding/releasing affect the relative stabilities of different conformations which may subsequently regulate important biological functions. 我们计划开展对生物和化学分子体系中重要的质子结合/交换的热力学性质的理论研究。质子结合与释放的可逆过程是一个最根本的化学过程。对质子结合热力学的准确的计算机模拟将帮助我们了解这个过程背后的物理根本。更重要的是将帮助我们揭示在许多复杂的生化过程质子结合的机理和调控作用。 计划进行的研究将沿着两个方向展开：发展准确的从头计算量子化学基于方法和应用这些方法去研究重要的化学和生物化学过程中的质子结合过程。具体任务包括：（1）发展基于组合从头量子力学/分子力学方法的长程静电相互作用的模拟方法;（2）发展高效的自由能模拟方法模拟多个质子并行结合过程;（3）在水溶液中的有机小分子的pKa的自由能模拟;（4）模拟核糖羟基的pKa;（5）模拟金黄色葡萄球菌核酸酶中并行的四个组氨酸侧链质子滴定过程;（6）模拟RGS12 - PDZ结构域的质子结合过程的构象选择。

702511.label: Realisation of objectives
702511.value: We have developed methods to treat long-range electrostatic interactions in ab initio QM/MM simulations, which is of great importance in the molecular dynamics simulation of charged molecules, such as proteins and nucleic acids. Then with the generalized-ensemble method developed in our group, an effective potential energy is constructed, which combines the contributions of all protonation states of the molecule and may greatly reduce the time cost in free energy simulation. With all these developments, we simulated the pKa of small organic molecules in water solution to calibrate our method, and successfully simulated the concurrent proton binding process. The related work has been published on the Journal of Computational Chemistry (2014, 35, 1491–1498)

702511.label: Major findings and research outcome
702511.value: The concurrent proton binding at multiple sites in macromolecules such as proteins and nucleic acids is an important yet challenging problem in biochemistry. We develop an efficient generalized Hamiltonian approach to attack this issue. Based on the previously developed generalized-ensemble methods, an effective potential energy is constructed which combines the contributions of all (relevant) protonation states of the molecule. The effective potential preserves important phase regions of all states and, thus, allows efficient sampling of these regions in one simulation. The need for intermediate states in alchemical free energy simulations is greatly reduced. Free energy differences between different protonation states can be determined accurately and enable one to construct the grand canonical partition function. Therefore, the complicated concurrent multisite proton titration process of protein molecules can be satisfactorily simulated. Application of this method to the simulation of the pKa of Glu49, Asp50, and C-terminus of bovine pancreatic trypsin inhibitor shows reasonably good agreement with published experimental work. This method provides an unprecedented vivid picture of how different protonation states change their relative population upon pH titration. We believe that the method will be very useful in deciphering the molecular mechanism of pH-dependent biomolecular processes in terms of a detailed atomistic description.

702511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
702511.value: With the developed effective potential energy method, we are able to simulate the free energy changes in those molecules with multi protonation states efficiently. This is of great importance in the investigation of the dynamics process of many biochemistry molecules, and will help biochemists to understand the mechanism at molecular levels.

702511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
702511.value: In summary, we have developed an efficient generalized-ensemble simulation method on the basis of previous works. The method can sample the important phase regions of all possible protonation states of the macromolecules in one simulation. With the availability of state-specific information for the target system, the method can be very useful in the investigation of the molecular mechanism of many important biomolecular processes.

702611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
702611.value: Submarine groundwater discharge (SGD) has been increasingly recognized as an important source of nutrients to coastal seawater, which has lead to numerous studies on the estimations of SGD and SGD-derived nutrients crossing the aquifer-seawater interface. The most popular approach to estimate SGD is a budget analysis of a geochemical tracer in the coastal seawater. In this analysis, the total tracer flux from SGD is estimated first and then the SGD rate is estimated by dividing the flux with the concentration of the tracer entering the seawater along the aquifer-seawater interface. Because the tracer concentration in the SGD at the interface is difficult to estimate, usually the tracer concentration in groundwater samples from existing wells within a certain distance of the shoreline is taken approximately as the tracer concentration at the interface. Some studies further estimate the fluxes of SGD-derived nutrients by simply multiplying the SGD rates by the nutrient concentrations in the wells. The pH, salinity, and redox conditions vary greatly in the freshwater-saltwater mixing zone in coastal aquifers. Some chemicals sensitive to the geochemical environment changes such as radium and nutrients may be added or removed before they enter the sea. Consequently, using groundwater chemicals from the wells may lead to erroneous SGD estimation because the well chemicals can be very different from those of SGD leaving right at the aquifer-seawater interface. The understanding of the dynamics of tracer and nutrients, their addition and removal processes in coastal aquifers, and the implications of these processes on SGD estimation is very limited. We propose to investigate the dynamic hydrogeochemical processes of flow, nutrients, radon and radium in the freshwater-saltwater mixing zones of Tolo Harbour by installing and then monitoring multi-level sampling piezometers and the implications of these processes on SGD estimation. Numerical models will be used to simulate the transport of nutrients in the mixing zone and predict the nutrients leaving at the aquifer-seawater interface. We will then estimate the amount of nutrients transported via SGD to Tolo Harbour using the nutrients at the aquifer-seawater interface predicted by the numerical models. The work will be conducted by an interdisciplinary team using multiple approaches, including multi-level monitoring piezometers, field hydrogeological studies, radioisotope tracers, and numerical modelling. Successful completion of this study will provide a deeper understanding of the hydrogeochemical processes of geochemical tracers and nutrients in the subterranean estuary and insights and methodology to better estimate SGD. 海底地下水排泄（SGD）已經逐漸被認爲是海水營養物質的一個重要的來源，它已經催生出許多關于海底地下水排泄的評估以及因海水地下水排放導致的富營養鹽在含水層和海水界面交換機理的研究。目前海水地下水排放的評估主要通過近海區天然地球化學示蹤劑的均衡來進行分析。這類分析中，首先估計因SGD導致的示蹤劑總通量，然後測量不同類型示蹤劑在淡水-海水交界面的濃度進而來估算海水地下水的排放速率。由于在淡水-海水界面處示蹤劑濃度很難估計，常規方法是通過測量離海岸線一定距離內井水樣的示蹤劑的濃度來大致反映交界面的地下水示蹤劑的濃度。 在沿海含水層的淡水—海水混合區中的pH值，鹽度，氧化還原條件差別很大。一些對地球化學環境敏感的化學物質例如鐳和營養鹽在進入海水前會富集或者稀釋。而近海區井水的地球化學條件與淡水海水界面的有較大的差異，因此，單純使用近海井水的示蹤劑的濃度容易導致不完善的評估。而目前針對淡水-海水區的地球化學示蹤劑和營養鹽的富集和稀釋的動態過程的研究都十分有限。 我們計劃通過在吐露港的淡水海水混合區安裝不同深度的鑽孔並對其進行監測來調查該區域的水流、營養物質、鐳、氡等水文地球化學動態過程，進而研究這些過程對海底地下水排泄的評估的影響。我們將采用數值模型來模擬營養鹽在混合區的運移和預測離開淡水-海水混合界面營養鹽的濃度。這項工作將由跨學科團隊引領，采用多種研究方法，其中包括對不同深度的鑽孔監測，水質地球化學過程的野外調查，放射性同位素示蹤元劑，和數值模擬等方法。這項研究將加深對同位素示蹤劑和營養鹽在地下河口的水文地質過程的了解，同時完善海底地下水排泄的研究方法。

702611.label: Realisation of objectives
702611.value: Objective 1: The objective has been fully achieved. We collected various geological, hydrogeological and chemical data that are relevant to the study site. We have also found that many areas around the harbor used to be paddy field about 30 years ago. It is believed that domestic and chemical fertilizers and pesticides were widely used. These chemicals may be still stored in the land. Groundwater may be contaminated and then pollute the seawater in the harbour. Objective 2: The objective has been fully achieved. Automatic pressure transducers were installed along the shoreline and show that groundwater level and tidal level fluctuate with time, so does the freshwater and saltwater mixing zones. Our numerical studies demonstrate that hydraulic properties of the unsaturated soil have significant influence on the process of variable density flow in an unsaturated-saturated aquifer system and that inland water level oscillation has a great effect on groundwater dynamics and land-sourced solute transport in a coastal aquifer. Objective 3: The objective has been fully achieved. We have observed the spatial distribution of the short-lived radium isotopes (224Ra and 223Ra) in the subterranean estuary near Ting Kok, Plover Cove, Tolo Harbor. The field measurements of short-lived radium isotopes for two months were conducted in a 100 m long and 3 m deep shallow aquifer at inter tidal zone. The results of field data and one-dimensional model indicate that the radium distribution in the shallow aquifer of the intertidal zone is affected by: 1) the desorption process caused by mixing with high salinity seawater and 2) the dilution processes induced by mixing with the low-activity radium seawater at the same time. Objective 4: The objective has been fully achieved. We studied nutrients in groundwater and porewater in the beach aquifer and in harbor water. We estimated that submarine groundwater discharge (SGD) derived DIN loadings and DIP loadings. Groundwater borne nutrients are 1-2 orders of magnitude larger than other nutrient sources and the inter-annual variation of nutrient concentration in the embayment is more influenced by the SGD derived loadings.

702611.label: Major findings and research outcome
702611.value: We first used 226Ra as a geotracer to study SGD in Tolo Harbour. Both fresh and saltwater component of SGD were estimated. The nutrient loading through SGD was also estimated, which was much more significant than its counterpart through the river discharge (Lee et al 2012). We then used both 224Ra and 223Ra as tracers to qualify SGD in Tolo Harbor. A two-layered radium mass balance model is used to estimate lateral SGD and bottom SGD (Luo et al 2014). After that primary productivity was estimated too, up to 50% of which is supported by SGD-induced phosphate fluxes. We further used multiple tracers, including radium quartet, 222Rn and silica to quantify SGD into Tolo Harbor in 2005 and 2011 (Luo et al 2016). All the models lead to an estimate of the SGD rate of the same order of magnitude. We found that there is a good spatial and temporal correlation between SGD and red tide outbreaks. We also conducted numerical modeling on variable density flow in in the freshwater and saltwater mixing zones in coastal unsaturated-saturated aquifers (Liu et al 2015). FEFLOW is used to systematically investigate the penetration process of the solute through the unsaturated-saturated aquifer system. The influence of the density difference of the solute on the penetration processes is insignificant in the unsaturated zone but significant in the saturated zone. We further modeled how inland groundwater level variation influence flow and solute transport in coastal aquifers (Liu et al 2016) and concluded that the hydraulic conductivity and the density of the solute are the dominant impact factors for the morphology, horizontal and vertical movements of the land-sourced solute plume. We further examined the possibility of fresh groundwater in the offshore aquifer. We characterized the hydrochemistry of the SGD in Hong Kong by looking into the major ion concentrations and the stable isotopic compositions of pore water extracted from offshore cores. A minimum Cl− level of ~1/3 of that in typical seawater was noted in the terrestrial sediments, suggesting the presence of offshore relatively fresh water (Kwong and Jiao 2106). Using the offshore stratigraphy and marine seismic data, we depicted the distribution of sand and gravel deposits and to estimate the average thickness of these aquifer materials. The extensive sand deposits in the study areas are often shielded by sufficiently thick marine clay against vertical salinisation, allowing fresh groundwater to be preserved (Kwong et al 2016).

702611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
702611.value: Tolo Harbour provides a good platform for SGD, or more general coastal hydrogeological, studies. In the past we focused on estimation of SGD and then SGD derived nutrients mainly based on mass balance model of geotracers such as radium. We feel that there is a need to understand exactly how radium reacts and transport in the freshwater and saltwater zones in the coastal aquifer before radium enters the sea. So we have written a new GRF proposal on “spatial and temporal characteristics of radium isotopes in subterranean estuaries”.

702611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
702611.value: We used natural tracers such as radium isotopes to estimate submarine groundwater discharge (SGD) and nutrient loading derived by SGD. The nutrient loadings from SGD are much more significant than its counterpart through the river discharge. We also estimated the primary productivity and concluded that up to 50% of primary productivity is supported by SGD-induced nutrients. We further studied the relation between SGD distributions and red tide occurrence and concluded that there is a good spatial and temporal correlation between SGD and red tide outbreaks. We also studied that dynamic hydrogeochemical processes of flow and chemical transport in the freshwater-saltwater mixing zones of Tolo Harbour and concluded that these processes are very complicated and requires further study. The study has various environmental and ecological implications. The great nutrient input to the harbour from coastal aquifer and the close correlation between SGD and red tide occurrence suggest that the current efforts for management of red tides in Tolo Harbour have to be reviewed and control of groundwater contamination is obviously required.

702711.label: Realisation of objectives
702711.value: We have made significant progress and our work is highly visible internationally. The discovery of complex organics in space was a surprise to the scientific community and we have played a major role in the study of the synthesis of complex organics during the late stages of stellar evolution. The book "Organic Matter in the Universe" (Wiley 2011) published by the PI is the first book published on this new subject. The pioneering nature of this work was recognized by our paper in Nature (Kwok and Zhang 2011) and the influence of our work was recognized internationally by the election of the PI as the President of International Astronomical Union Commission on Astrobiology.

702711.label: Major findings and research outcome
702711.value: We have made significant progress in identifying the chemical structure of interstellar organics. We have proposed that the carrier of the unidentified infrared emission features, a long standing mystery of astrochemistry, is a mixed aromatic/aliphatic organic compound. We have made analysis of the spectra obtained with the Infrared Space Observatory and Spitzer Space Observatory observations of a number of proto-planetary nebulae, planetary nebulae, reflection nebulae and novae and concluded that the observations are more consistent with this new model than the traditional explanation of the features being due to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon molecules. The results were published in the journal Nature and this discovery was widely reported in the international press, including BBC and MSNBC.

702711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
702711.value: Since this is a new field, much further work needs to be done, specifically in the determination of the exact chemical structure of the organic compound responsible for the unidentified infrared emission features. This will be carried out by further ground-based observations as well as by quantum chemistry theoretical calculations.

702711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
702711.value: We find that old stars are capable of synthesizing large quantities of complex organics. Based on infrared spectroscopic observations from space-based telescopes, we are able to determine that these organic particles contains a mixture of aromatic (ring-like) and aliphatic (chain-like) components. The compounds are so complex that their chemical structures resemble those of coal and petroleum. Since coal and oil are remnants of ancient life, this type of organic matter was thought to arise only from living organisms. The team’s discovery suggests that complex organic compounds can be synthesized in space even when no life forms are present. Most interestingly, this organic star dust is similar in structure to complex organic compounds found in meteorites. Since meteorites are remnants of the early Solar System, the findings raise the possibility that stars enriched the early Solar System with organic compounds. The early Earth was subjected to severe bombardments by comets and asteroids, which potentially could have carried organic star dust. Whether these delivered organic compounds played any role in the development of life on Earth remains an open question.

703011.label: Project Objectives
703011.value: We will investigate whether a model in which the Solar System started with five giant planets in a compact resonant configuration and ejected one of the planets during a phase of close encounters among the giant planets can explain the observed properties of the Solar System. We will examine whether a preexisting system of regular satellites around Uranus would be destroyed by the giant impact that tilted the spin axis of Uranus, leading to the formation of a debris disk around the tilted equator of Uranus and the formation of a new generation of regular satellites. We will assess the viability of a scenario in which the small satellites Nix and Hydra of Pluto-Charon formed from the collision of two Kuiper Belt objects in the vicinity of Pluto-Charon. We will investigate the evolution of solid material in the circumjovian disk in which the Galilean satellites of Jupiter formed. The interplay between magnetically driven turbulence and the coagulation and settling of dust grains will be studied.
