The gaseous starting material was the mixture of carbon dioxide and water steam, in which carbon dioxide was produced by the decomposition of Ag-oxalate salt. Using Ag-oxalate was convenient to add quantitative carbon dioxide to the sealed Au-capsule and could avoid contamination by the other gaseous phases. Olivine from mantle xenolith, komatiite rock, continental basalt with known mineralogy/geochemistry or those with pre-experimental investigations were used to react with the gaseous phases. Experiments were conducted from 200 to 450 degree Celsius with gradients of 50 or 100 degree Celsius. Some experimental systems were measured for the gaseous components by gas chromatography before being opened for analysis for solid phases. The solid phases were analyzed for mineralogy, morphology and chemical compositions by various methods, such as transmission electron microscopy, scanning electron microscopy and equipped electron dispersive X-ray spectroscopy.

Due to the constrain of the high pressure and high temperature cells use for the experiments, both the starting and the retrieved materials were of small amounts. The electron microscopes were the major facilities used to characterize the experimental products, while other instruments, such as Raman spectroscopy, synchrotron radiation facilities were also used to characterize some particular minerals of low abundance. The brief introductions on the using of these methods could be found in related publications attached to this report.

The synthesis of small organic molecules were observed in some batch experiments, which is an indication of the indigenous production of organic molecules by Earth itself. This part has been reported in one of our research paper (JGR-Planets, in revision). However, we cannot address the reduction of carbon dioxide by transition metal sulfide and the possible production of organic molecules because the abundance of sulfides in all materials was too low for high temperature and high pressure experiments. Therefore, sulfides in the experimental products, if there was any, could hardly be identified. Elemental carbon was not identified in any experimental system, so we did not discuss much of this hypothesized process on Venus.
As explained in Objective No.4, this objective has not been developed much because of the experimental limits and/or the difficulty in characterization of the products.

We addressed several important issues of the early evolution of the Earth toward a habitable planet: 1. the rapid reaction between rocks and the proto-atmosphere at high temperatures produced massive secondary minerals; 2. the production of carbonates implies a strong sequestration of atmospheric carbon dioxide that might have rapidly decreased the strong greenhouse effect of the early Earth; 3. the production of magnetite nanoparticles in the high-temperature experimental systems implies the production of abundant catalytic materials for the abiotic synthesis of organic molecules in the early Hadean age of the Earth; 4. we demonstrated that the precipitation of secondary minerals with or without the mediation of life (microorganisms) could be very different.

703911.label: Major findings and research outcome
703911.value: 1. We conduct the first experimental study on the interactions between the earliest crust and the proto-atmosphere at Earth's earliest time. Previous studies mostly focused on theoretical simulations because of the lacking of petrologic record. There were many experimental studies using the water-rock interaction systems that could not show the participation of carbon dioxide, neither the direct interaction between the atmospheric water steam and rock at high temperature. Our experimental systems provided the closest simulations to the early atmosphere-crust interactions. 2. We first observed the production of abundant carbonates as the result of the coprecipitation of carbon dioxide and cations extracted by water from the rock. Such experiments showed straightforward evidence that the early interactions between the Earth's crust and the proto-atmosphere could have happened very easily and has been a very effective way in fixing the atmospheric carbon dioxide, and therefore a very efficient way in cooling the Earth until the formation of an ocean. 3. Magnetite is known to be the product of serpentinization - the interaction between water and mafic/ultramafic rocks at high temperatures. However, magnetite was only occasionally indicated by X-ray diffraction measurements. In this study, we first identified magnetite crystals by detailed transmission electron microscopic investigation. We found that magnetite formed in our experimental system were nano particles, and with erosional structures. These observations explained why magnetite is thought to be the product of serpentinization but was rarely observed by conventional mineralogical or petrologic methods. 4. As this study is part of my astrobiological approach, I am interested to know if the earliest sedimentary rocks bear any evidence of the early microbial life. So we examined the minerals precipitated in hot springs as the result of not only the interaction between the hot water and the volcanic basaltic rock, but also with the mediation of microbial communities. We further propose that a collection of the complex crystal habits is an indication of microbial mediation, and therefore, in the point view of astrobiology, the mineral record of past life; We first reported the mineralization of apatite in the early sedimentary rocks with only microbial life. These studies suggest that the complex structures produced by microbial mediations in Earth environments of ancient and nowadays could be used as reference for the search for evidence of life on Mars.

703911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
703911.value: In this study, we observed the production of carbon hydrates (methane, ethane, and propane), which are organic molecules but do not contain oxygen on the structures. In the abiotic evolution toward life, organic molecules containing oxygen on the structures might be more important. Examples for these molecules are formate, acetate, formaldehyde, pyruvate, etc. Some of those molecules could have been produced in our experimental systems, but they were not detected because of the extremely low amount and/or the running conditions of gas chromatography we used. The further studies in characterization of carbon-oxygen bond-containing small molecules could be developed for a further study due to its importance in the abiotic synthesis of organic molecules in the prebiotic stage of evolution toward life.

703911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
703911.value: The earliest 700 million years of Earth's 4600 million years history is almost unknown because the intensive overprinting by the later geodynamic processes. In this study, we experimentally simulated the interactions between the earliest crust and proto-atmosphere. The aim is to understanding the important processes happened in this stage that turned the Earth from a hellish environment to a habitable planet. The earliest Earth was very hot because of the strong greenhouse effect, which also prevented the formation of an ocean. We simulated the interaction between the [water-carbon dioxide] atmosphere and rocks containing iron and magnesium. We found that the gaseous carbon dioxide were fixed to carbonates by cations extracted from silicates by water. This observation is important because the rapid removal of atmospheric carbon dioxide could lead to the rapid cooling of the Earth until the formation of the ocean. The ocean was the best bath for life to start. We also identified some iron oxides that have been proved to be important catalytic materials in making small organic molecules by geological process only. This result support that the life on Earth could be created by Earth itself without the necessary for seed of life from somewhere in the Universe.

704011.label: Project Objectives
704011.value: Origin Does the cool molecular gas originate from the relatively undisturbed intracluster gas, or does its formation involve a more complex process such as condensation from the backflow of hot intracluster gas compressed by an outwardly-moving X-ray bubble? Do different processes dominate in directions along and away from the radio jets? Our previous interferometric observations resolved out about half of the CO emission from the main body of molecular gas in NGC 1275: we need to recover the remaining portion to build a complete picture of the molecular gas, observe the gas at even higher sensitivities and angular resolutions than the levels already attained, and compare its distribution and kinematics with the other known gas components (in particular its warm ionized gas) to test and constrain different models for the origin of all these gases. Fate: Star Formation Are there any locations where the molecular gas is sufficiently dense to form stars? Intriguingly, the only known sites of star formation within the main body of molecular gas lies just inside the innermost tips of the two longest radial filaments. We plan to search for dense molecular gas as traced in HCN, which is usually a good marker for star formation, in NGC 1275. Fate: AGN Fueling Does the infalling molecular gas settle into the center of NGC 1275? We need to better separate the different filaments around the nucleus so as to better model their kinematics. This will allow us to confirm whether the radio jet from the AGN in NCC 1275 drives a bipolar molecular outflow, which if the case, indicates that the cool molecular gas reaches close to the AGN. We plan to search for a circumnuclear molecular torus, as has been tentatively detected in hot molecular hydrogen gas, that may comprise the reservoir for fueling the AGN. Gas Excitation A complete understanding of the origin and fate of the different gas components is not possible without a proper understanding of their excitation, which has long been a mystery. Testing models requires measurements of line intensity ratios, work that we and others are carrying out for NGC 1275. For the cool molecular gas, we plan observations in multiple transitions to constrain its excitation and find evidence for cooling along a filament.

704011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
704011.value: 星系的形成和演化， 包括他們在早於宇宙大爆炸之後數百萬年的早期形成階段及其後續發展一直到現在的一系列物理過程，是現代天體物理學中最重要的新領域之一。 目前比較流行的模型中，在早期宇宙的細小引力波動會導致暗物質隨著原始氣體造成崩潰到被稱為宇宙網的絲狀結構。 宇宙網的物質流入到絲狀結構相交地區使該地區重力較強并形成含有氣體的暗物質暈：而氣體形成恆星，隨之形成早期的星系。 隨後星系的增長：涉及繼續與暗物質暈兼併或者從宇宙網堆積形成當今宇宙的星系，比如我們的銀河系。因為絲狀結構相交的地方優先形成星系， 所以星系通常是捆綁在一起而形成或大或小的星系群。在那些星系團中央的橢圓星系通常是最重質量的星系。 星系團被非常熱的（約 107-108 K）具有強X－射線輻射的電離氣體所包圍。而這些氣體被認為是吸積自宇宙網，或者從一些星系中被牽拉出來，并且在吸積的過程中被激波加熱致高溫。關於 的演化，一個流行的模型認為星系團中央的橢圓星系的演化過程中，星系團間的氣體會冷卻并最終形成恆星。在 30多年前，Cowie & Binney (1977) Fabian & Nulsen (1977)研究展示了那些在星系團中心地區的原來很熱的星系間氣體會迅速冷卻并在失去壓力支持下向內流動，從而產生X－射線冷卻流。但如果在 星系團中央 有大量氣體冷卻而形成恆星，那裡的恆星質量就應該比觀察到的高得多。為此，目前的星系形成模型提出星系間的氣體可能會被來自超大黑洞的相對論性噴流再次加熱，從而大大降低冷卻流的速率。 因此，破譯熱氣體冷卻及再加熱的的過程成為了解星系大會的中心議題之一。在過去的十年中，此議題的重要一環就是發現了大量冷分子氣體，而這些氣體遠遠超過其他能在低於Ｘ－射線溫度下測量到的所有氣體 - 在這些星系團的中心懷疑有強烈的X射線冷卻流。最重要的是，我們在英仙座星系團中央的冷分子氣體的研究表明，這種氣體至少部分是呈放射狀下落的，並因此相信可能是來源自 星系間的氣體多於來源自與富氣體星系合併。此外，我們證明了在英仙座星系團中下落分子氣體的沉積速率與當前的X射線冷卻集群流量上限是一致的。 到目前為止，因為最近的星系團懷疑懷有強烈的X－射線冷卻流，在對於為闡明熱星系間氣體的冷卻再加熱的過程及其在恆星形成所擔當的角色，英仙座集群已成為最重要的測試平台 。儘管可追溯到50年以上，而我們只是基本了解在這個星系團的中央星系的各種氣體成分，雖然這種情況正隨著新的儀器和理論而在迅速變化 。我們的建議書旨在探討在英仙座星系團中央星系的分子氣體的起源，激發和命運，特別新穎的方面包括這種氣體是否形成恆星，如果沒有又是什麼阻止恆星形成呢，以及來自星系團中央的超大黑洞氣體燃料能否建立一個反饋循環去調節星系間氣體的冷卻。要解決這些問題，我們需要更詳細的不同過渡和物種的分子氣體的分佈和運動的研究。除此之外，亦需要了解在中央團星系之間的分子和其他氣體成份的關係，此方面除我們自己的工作外，亦有賴其他天文學家的工作。

704011.label: Realisation of objectives
704011.value: This program has resulted in the training of two graduate students for their MPhil theses and an undergraduate student for his research thesis; a groundbreaking paper; and another paper that due to a miscommunication did not acknowledge this grant. A lack of direct access to the SubMillimeter Array (SMA), albeit an Adjunct Fellow at the ASIAA, has limited completion of the program objectives. Recently, the new ASIAA Director endorsed my access to ASIAA facilities through collaborations, prompting my resumption of projects on the SMA. Despite this limitation, we have made important progress on Objective 1 by expanding our work to include atomic gas. In a critical step towards understanding the origin and morphology of the nebula in NGC 1275, we have measured the kinematics of the entire optical emission-line nebula for the first time (Chan 2012, MPhil thesis). The nebular kinematics defy notions and model predictions for the nature of long radial filaments. A robust interpretation of the nebular kinematics requires understanding the formation histories of their associated star clusters, work currently in progress as described next. We have made huge strides on Objective 2 by expanding our work to star formation throughout NGC 1275. Such studies are complicated by the presence of a foreground galaxy known as the High-Velocity System (HVS). In groundbreaking work based on imaging spectroscopy of optical emission-lines from this galaxy, we have resolved essentially all of the outstanding questions regarding the HVS. Although approaching NGC 1275, we showed that the HVS is not responsible for producing the nebula or triggering star formation in NGC 1275 (Yu 2014, MPhil thesis; Yu et al. 2015, ApJ). From a comprehensive search, we have cataloged all the star clusters towards NGC 1275 from multi-band (BVR) images with the Hubble Space Telescope, and showed that star clusters in NGC 1275 and the HVS can be separated based on their different colors and spatial distributions. Using this color information, we are working on addressing the formation histories of all these star clusters. In partial fulfillment of Objective 3, we have discovered that the radio jet in NGC 1275 drives a highly-velocity ionized outflow. A paper is currently under preparation reporting this result. As part of Objective 4, we have made a preliminary study of the optical emission-line ratios throughout the nebula, and submitted a SMA proposal to study the chemistry of its molecular gas, so as to test whether energetic particles energize the nebula.

704011.label: Major findings and research outcome
704011.value: The relatively cool gas in NGC 1275 forms a complex filamentary nebula that spans ~140 kpc (~400 arcsec) in the north-south direction. Only limited portions of this nebula have measured kinematics, including our work in CO showing that the inner filaments are radially infalling. Using the 3.5-m telescope at the Calar Alto Observatory (Spain), we have conducted imaging spectroscopy of the optical emission-line nebula in NGC 1275 (Chan 2012, MPhil thesis). Providing the kinematics of the entire nebula for the first time, this difficult but comprehensive work constitutes a major step towards addressing both the origin and complex morphology of the nebula. Overturning previous notions, we found that long and apparently contiguous filaments are actually composed of shorter strands having their own individual kinematics. Few if any filaments have kinematics consistent with model predictions for those dragged outwards behind rising bubbles. Instead, some of the outer filaments appear to be draped on the surfaces of rising bubbles. A robust interpretation of the individual filaments will require aid from dating their closely associated star clusters, work that is currently in progress. Discovered in the 1940s, the nature of the HVS and its role in producing the cool gas and triggering star formation in NGC 1275 have long been outstanding mysteries. From the aforementioned observations with the Calar Alto observatory, we also conducted imaging spectroscopy of optical emission-lines from the HVS (Yu 2015, MPhil thesis). In a groundbreaking and comprehensive work described in 26 journal pages (Yu et al. 2015, ApJ), we have resolved essentially all the longstanding questions about the HVS. For the first time, we show that the HVS is indeed experiencing strong ram-pressure stripping, placing it firmly in the Perseus cluster rather than being a chance foreground galaxy. Resolving conflicting reports about its kinematics, we showed that both its morphology and kinematics exhibit similar distortions as imposed by ram pressure rather than interactions with NGC 1275. Its measured rotation curve implies that the HVS was originally a low-surface-brightness galaxy, but that the cumulative effects of galaxy harassment or, more likely, the cluster tidal field have triggered two spiral arms along which star formation occurred. We showed that the HVS is likely making its first passage through the cluster, and that the relatively short time spent near NGC 1275 implies that the HVS cannot be responsible for either producing the nebula or triggering star formation in the central cluster elliptical galaxy.

704011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
704011.value: As part of our work on the HVS (Yu et al. 2015, ApJ), we have compiled a comprehensive list of over a thousand star clusters towards NGC 1275 from B, V, and R images taken with the Hubble Space Telescope (HST). We are currently working on understanding selection effects and separating star clusters belonging to NGC 1275 and the HVS, in preparation for addressing the formation history of all these star clusters. By comparing the formation histories of these star clusters with the kinematics of their associated gas filaments, we anticipate making a meaningful interpretation of the nebular kinematics. We also anticipate that knowledge of the formation history of these star clusters will provide important insights on the recent history of stellar mass assembly in NGC 1275. We have already expanded our work to the central elliptical galaxies of other clusters. Observations of NGC 5044 in CO using the Atacama Large Millimter and Submillimeter array (ALMA) reveals radial filaments having kinematics reminiscent of those in NGC 1275 (David, Lim, et al. 2014, ApJ; RGC grant not acknowledged due to miscommunication). We are studying the formation history of young stars in other cluster central elliptical galaxies using multi-band images from the HST.

704011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
704011.value: Massive galaxies come into two main types: roundish spheroidal and flattish disk galaxies. They are sometimes bound together in clusters that contain hundreds of galaxies. At the centers of galaxy clusters lie the most massive known galaxies, which resemble lower-mass spheroidal galaxies but often contain large amounts of cool gas and are actively forming stars. The origin and physical properties of this cool gas are poorly understood, as is the role this gas plays in forming stars and hence the assembly of stellar mass in the galaxy. Due in part to its proximity, NGC 1275 is the best object in which to study cool gas and star formation in cluster central spheroidal galaxies. In a major step towards understanding the origin and morphology of its cool gas, we have unveiled for the first time the motion of this gas throughout NGC 1275. Furthermore, in a comprehensive work that disentangles a foreground galaxy from NGC 1275, we have assembled a comprehensive list of all the star clusters in NGC 1275. We are now on the verge of deducing the recent history of star formation and hence stellar mass assembly in NGC 1275, and the role its cool gas plays in forming stars.

704411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
704411.value: 计划目标 我们计划利用我们早期积累的脉泽搜寻和红外数据对质量流失演化晚期恒星进行系统的研究。主要目标是1）增加已知水喷泉星的数目，2）利用脉泽发射调查红超巨星的质量流失现象。 背景和动机 具有大质量流失率演化的晚期恒星，例如渐进巨星和红超巨星，是研究各种天文问题的有力工具。这些问题包括星周包层的化学演化，星际介质的起源等等。在多一个单个大质量星团试探性的研究中，我们已经得到了两个重要结果：1）可以探测到更多的水喷泉星，2）可能发现大量具有水脉泽的红超巨星。水喷泉星是理解恒星在渐进巨星支演化的关键，但已知水喷泉星数目相当少。对在单个星团中红超巨星研究有助于我们得到重要的红超巨星的参数，比如距离和金属丰度。因而我们的这两个发现有可能对演化晚期恒星研究有重大影响。通过本计划，我们能够通过搜寻新的水喷泉星和收集单个星团中得红超巨星的观测资料加深对渐进巨星和红超巨星的理解。 方法 我们计划利用单天线和干涉射电望远镜观测水喷泉星和红超巨星的SiO, H2O 和OH发射线，从而研究脉泽与恒星演化之间的关系。我们将利用最新释放的红外数据研究水喷泉星的挑选标准，然后利用射电干涉观测进行验证。我们将检测红超巨星的红外和脉泽特性之间的物理关系，并研究利用脉泽发射研究红超巨星演化状态的可能性。我们还将搜寻已知大质量星团中得红超巨星，并系统地调查脉泽和红外特性的相关性。 观测天文人才培养 本计划的另一个重要任务是教育，我们研究小组在香港的射电天文领域处于领导地位，我们希望为本地、中国大陆和东亚各国的学生和年轻学者提供更多的机会使他们能接触观测天文的前沿领域研究。我们计划培养至少两名博士，我们还将与国外学者和研究机构建立紧密的联系以便于我们的科研和教育。

704411.label: Realisation of objectives
704411.value: In this project, we have conducted a systematic study on mass-losing evolved stars, utilizing accumulated data of our previous maser surveys and newly released infrared archival data. The primary goals of this project were (1) to increase the number of known water fountain (WF) objects, and (2) to explore possibilities of using maser emission to investigate the mass-loss phenomena of red supergiants (RSGs). Evolved stars exhibiting a large mass-loss rate (mass-losing evolved stars, hereafter), such as asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars and RSGs, are potentially a very powerful tool to study a wide variety of astrophysical problems, such as the chemical evolution of circumstellar envelopes and the origin of interstellar medium. In our pilot studies, we found two important results: (1) the possibility of finding many more WFs, and (2) a significant number of RSGs with maser emission are found in a single massive cluster. These two findings may potentially transform the situation of the research field of mass-losing evolved stars, because the number of known WFs, which are a key driver to understand the AGB evolution of stars, is currently quite limited, also because RSGs in a single star cluster enable us to derive essential stellar parameters of RSGs, such as distance and metallicity. In this project, we surely deepened our knowledge of AGB stars and RSGs by surveying new WFs and collecting observational information of RSGs in massive clusters. In this project, we planed to conduct further observations of WFs and RSGs in the maser lines of SiO, H2O and OH using single-dish and interferometric radio telescopes to investigate physical relations between maser properties and stellar evolution. Utilizing the newly released IR data, we tried to find effective selection criteria of WFs, and then confirm the WF status by radio interferometric observations. We checked physical correlations between IR and maser properties of RSGs to explore possibilities of using maser emission as a probe of the RSG evolutionary status. We completed the maser searches of RSGs in known massive star clusters, so that we could systematically investigate the correlation between maser and IR properties. Education through the present project was also an important mission. As a leading research group of radio astronomy in Hong Kong, our team has been eager to provide more opportunities for local students and young researchers, as well as for students from mainland China and East-Asian countries, to be exposed to the latest research projects of observational astronomy in intriguing fields. In this project, we nurtured a PhD student within the project duration, and we built a good and tight partnership with foreign researchers and institutions to facilitate our scientific and educational activities. In what follows, we summarize the final status of the project with respect to each objective: (1) Expand the region of the maser survey of cold mid-IR sources to increase the number of known WFs. We have acquired telescope times of common-use radio telescopes for this purpose. We used the Efflelsberg 100m telescope in Germany, the Nobeyama 45m telescope in Japan, and the Green Bank Telescope in the USA. In total, we observed roughly a couple of hundred new samples of cold mid-IR sources, and found several new candidates for WFs. The paper has been published in a peer-reviewed journal. (2) Find effective selection criteria of WFs, which are independent from the velocity range of maser emission, so that we can find WFs with a small inclination angle. For this purpose, we analyzed the newly released infrared data including AKARI and Spitzer/GLIMPSE by constructing one-dimensional radiative transfer model. We also adopted the Q-parameter method, which have been recently suggested by a German group. The paper has been published in a peer-reviewed journal. (3) Check correlations between IR and maser properties of RSGs to explore possibilities of using maser emission as a probe of the RSG evolutionary status, and check how mass-loss properties of RSGs behave in each different massive cluster to consider the dependence on metallicity. We finished the collecting the infrared data of RSGs newly found in massive clusters, and finished some initial analysis using the Q-parameter method. (4) Complete maser searches of RSGs in known massive star clusters, so that we can statistically investigate the correlation between maser and IR properties. The statistical study mention in the item (3) has been published together with the results of our pilot study. (5) Train 1-2 PhD students within the duration of this project, and build a good and tight partnership with foreign researchers and institutions to facilitate our scientific and educational activities. We hired Dr. Chih-Hao Hsia as a PDF, Mr. Thomas K. T. Fok as a RA, and Mr. Bosco H. K. Yung as a PhD student. Dr. Hsia was contributing to the analysis of the infrared data, also supporting supervision of students and RAs. Mr. Fok was contributing to the analysis of infrared data, and Mr. Yung worked on maser observations for newly selected cold IR samples. We also invited several visitors for discussions from Poland, Japan and India.

704411.label: Major findings and research outcome
704411.value: We observed roughly a couple of hundred new samples of cold mid-IR sources, and found several new candidates for WFs. We analyzed the newly released infrared data including AKARI and Spitzer/GLIMPSE by constructing one-dimensional radiative transfer model. We also adopted the Q-parameter method, which have been recently suggested by a German group. The paper has been published in a peer-reviewed journal (see, 2 and 4 in C-8). In addition, we executed follow-up studies on important objects found in our statistical studies (see, 1, 3 and 5 in C-8); in these studies, we revealed physical conditions of some objects at a transient phase between AGB and post-AGB phases.

704411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
704411.value: Through the present study, we found some concrete examples of stars in the transient phase between AGB and post-AGB stars. Some observational properties found in such stars are not naturally explained in the standard scheme of stellar evolution in its late stage. Further follow-ups are required.

704411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
704411.value: We have developed a methodology, which utilize maser emission to find candidates for stars with a bipolar jet. Follow-up radio imaging shows that some of the candidates really exhibit a bipolar jets. Physical properties of the stars newly found in the present study are not fully understood in the standard scheme of stellar evolution in its late stage. We need to reconsider the scenario of the stellar evolution.

704511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
704511.value: The development and continuing improvement of imaging techniques for the direct visualization of molecular distribution in biological tissues is of crucial importance for various aspects of Biological and Biomedical Sciences. Most conventional approaches, which are based on staining and/or antigen-antibodies interactions, are target-specific and require prior knowledge of the analyte molecules. In this research, we aim to advance the label-free imaging technique of Imaging Mass Spectrometry through an integration of the distinctive properties of metal nanoparticles with laser desorption/ ionization mass spectrometry for the direct detection and profiling of small molecules within intact biological tissues, and determining their spatial distribution for molecular imaging analysis. Instead of the conventional method of using metal nanoparticles in suspension, we will apply argon ion sputtering method for coating a thin and homongenous layer of metal nanoparticles on the tissue surface. This solvent-free approach allows the adoption of laser desorption/ ionization for molecular imaging without dissolving the analyte molecules or disturbing their natural distribution patterns in sample tissues. Using herbal tissues, the four noble metal nanoparticles including silver, gold, palladium and platinium are chosen for the molecular imaging analysis, and a comparison will be made of their performance on detection sensitvity. Fundamental study on the ion desorption mechanism(s) of these nanoparticles will have to be conducted for rationalizing their different performance. The current study will help provide a basis for a fundamental understanding of the laser desorption/ ionization processes of metal nanoparticles, and also advance the technical level of IMS so as to extend its scope of application. 開發和改良可直接分析生物組織的分子顯影技術對輔助生物學和醫學研究都十分重要。 一般的顯影技術，例如染色和免疫螢光顯影，都需要有預定的顯影標靶才能進行顯影。 在今次的研究中，我們將會透過結合和應用金屬納米粒子的不同特性，改良影像質譜法這項不需標定的顯影技術。我們希望能應用「金屬納米粒子輔助激光脫附離子化影像質譜法」直接在生物組織上偵測和分析小分子，並顯影出不同的小分子在生物組織中的分佈。 有別於一般應用金屬納米粒子懸浮液的傳統方法，我們將會使用濺鍍方法，直接從金屬靶材產生金屬納米粒子，然後在生物組織樣本上鍍上一層均勻的金屬納米粒子薄膜。 上述的方法能免除溶劑的使用，從而可保存生物組織樣本上的化合物的原有分佈，避免樣本上的化合物因被溶解而可能引起的干擾，提升分子顯影分析的可靠性。 我們會以草藥組織作為藍本，並選擇出四種貴族金屬（銀、金、鈀、鉑）的納米粒子，開發和優化「金屬納米粒子輔助激光脫附離子化影像質譜法」。我們會比較四種貴族金屬納米粒子對這分析方法的影響，例如對靈敏度的影響。 為加深了解不同貴族金屬納米粒子對這分析方法的影響，我們將會進行對離子脫附機制的基礎研究。 今次的研究希望能加強對「金屬納米粒子輔助激光脫附離子化」的基礎理解，提升這分析方法的技術和擴闊這方法的應用層面。

704511.label: Realisation of objectives
704511.value: When the project was started in 2011, Dr. Kwan-Ming Ng was the PI and Prof. Chi-Ming Che was the Co-I of this project. In late 2012, Dr. Ng left HKU to South University of Science and Technology of China and Prof. Che was asked to be the project PI. In early 2014, Dr. Ng returned to HKU. Both Dr. Ng and Prof. Che have been working closely to ensure successful completion of this project. Dr. Anna On-Yee Chan was appointed as Postdoctoral Fellow in HKU to help the development of this project when Dr. Ng was not at HKU. We have achieved the stated objectives; 4 papers have been published, 1 paper is under revision and 3 papers are under preparation. 2 presentations were delivered in international conferences. The important findings are summarized below: [Objective 1] We found that AuNPs give the best detection sensitivity and performance in SALDI-MS analysis for various analytes. [Manuscript under revision]. Based on this result, we applied AuNPs as coating substrate for imaging mass spectrometric analysis of mouse brain tissue, tumor tissue slices and Chinese herbal medicines. Imaging of sub-regions of mouse brain with resolution down to 100 µm was achieved [Rapid Communications in Mass Spectrometry 2011, 25, 3690]. The characteristic ions for differentiation between Cordyceps sinensis and its fake counterpart, Cordyceps hawkesii gray, have been identified [Manuscript under preparation]. By coating the IR sample with AuNPs, a bridge between IR and laser desorption/ionization (LDI) spectrometry has been achieved, which is useful for rapid analysis of drug and botanical medicines [Manuscript under preparation]. We have successfully developed tip-spray ionization mass spectrometry for direct analysis of explosives [Analyst 2014, 139, 1482]. Fundamental study on its working principle was also conducted [Rapid Communications in Mass Spectrometry 2013, 27, 713]. We have developed megavolt electrostatic ionization mass spectrometry for direct chemical analysis of living human body under ambient conditions. Through this method, illicit drugs and explosives on skin/glove, flammable solvent on cloth/tissue paper, and volatile food substances in breath could be directly detected [Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry 2014, 25, 1515]. [Objective 2] Along with our endeavor in understanding the mechanism of SALDI using noble metal nanoparticles as substrates, we observed that the ion desorption efficiency and the extent of internal energy transfer of the metal nanoparticles during laser application are positively correlated to the photo-absorption efficiency of the nanoparticles [Manuscript under preparation].

704511.value: Some of the findings from this project could be found in previous report. In essence, we have accomplished the followings. (1) Four publications in leading international journals with specification in mass spectrometry including Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry, Rapid Communications in Mass Spectrometry, and Analyst, one manuscript is under revision and three manuscripts are under preparation. (2) 2 presentations on this research topic were delivered in international conferences. (3) The paper entitled “Direct analysis of large living organism by megavolt electrostatic ionization mass spectrometry” [Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry 2014, 25, 1515] has been cited by Latest News of Science Magazine. (4) The methodology reported in “Direct analysis of large living organism by megavolt electrostatic ionization mass spectrometry” is filed as US provisional patent. [File No. 61/978,447; File Date 11Apr, 2014]. (5) The methodology reported in “Direct analysis of large living organism by megavolt electrostatic ionization mass spectrometry” is applying for International PCT patent [File No. PCT/CN2015/076322; File Date 10Apr, 2015]. (6) “Direct analysis of large living organism by megavolt electrostatic ionization mass spectrometry” has been selected as the front cover of the Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry Vol. 25, no. 9. (7) We developed the technique of AuNPs-assisted SADLI mass spectrometry for the analysis of biological tissue slices [Rapid Communications in Mass Spectrometry. 2011, 25, 3690] and Chinese herbal medicine slices [Unpublished result]. The latter leads to the identification of characteristic ions, which helps in differentiation of morphologically similar Chinese herbal medicines. By bridging IR and LDI-MS using AuNPs as the coating substrate, a rapid analysis of drug and botanical medicines is achieved using only one sample [Unpublished result]. (8) We found that there is a positive correlation of the ion desorption efficiency and the extent of internal energy transfer of the metal nanoparticles during laser application with the photo-absorption efficiency of the nanoparticles [Unpublished result]. (9) We developed the tip-spray ionization mass spectrometric technique for direct sample analysis. The fundamental study on its working principle was also conducted [Rapid Communications in Mass Spectrometry 2013, 27, 713]. (10) We developed megavolt electrostatic ionization mass spectrometry for direct chemical analysis of living human body under ambient conditions [Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry 2014, 25, 1515].

704511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
704511.value: The AuNPs-based SALDI analysis for IMS study of Chinese herbal medicines leads to discovery of new characteristic phytochemicals and their spatial localization on the sample slices. Such methodology could thus be a complementary method for more reliable authentication or differentiation between morphologically similar herbal samples. We envision that by expanding our substrate scope to different kinds of Chinese herbal medicine or herbal medicine from different cultivating sources, a database could be created for standardization of Chinese herbal medicine in the future.

704511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
704511.value: Factors that determine the efficiency of laser desorption/ionization (LDI) of a substrate coated sample surface are rarely studied. In order to have a better understanding of the process, we compared the performance of different metal nanoparticles as the substrate. We believe that through this fundamental study, a substrate with high LDI efficiency (i.e. extracting more chemical information from the sample surface) could be designed. Application of the methodology in analyzing Chinese herbal medicines results in a better understanding of the active ingredients in the Chinese herbs which lead to the biological activity, more reliable authentication or quality control of Chinese herbal medicines.

704611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
704611.value: Many physics and engineering problems involve finding zeros of polynomials and Newton’s method is widely considered as the most important zero-finding algorithm. In 1981, the Fields Medalist Stephen Smale published a seminal paper in which he started a new direction of studying the efficiency and computational complexity of Newton's method for one variable polynomials. Subsequently, he and Michael Shub also studied other zero-finding algorithms. In Smale’s 1981 paper, he proved a family of inequalities for polynomials and among them, the most famous one is his Mean Value Theorem which is an inequality relating the critical points and critical values of a polynomial. Smale also suggested six open problems related to finding the sharp constants in these inequalities. Over the past thirty years, much of the efforts have been focused on the study of Smale’s mean value conjecture which asks for the sharp constant in Smale’s Mean Value Theorem. It may due to its potential application to complex dynamics as well as the fact that it is listed (as a minor problem) in Smale’s famous problem list for 21st century. On the other hand, very little have been done on the other Smale’s inequalities although getting the sharp constants in these inequalities would have interesting implications to the efficiency of Newton’s method. In the first part of this project, the PI will introduce for the first time the theory of amoeba to the study of Smale’s inequalities. The theory of amoeba was first developed by Gelfand, Kapranov and Zelevinsky in 1994 and it is now a very important tool in the study of tropical geometry. The PI will apply this theory to give a unified treatment of proving the existence of the extremal polynomials for the sharp constant as well as showing that some of these extremal polynomials would satisfy certain nice property which may eventually help us to identify them. In Smale’s paper, he also introduced and suggested to study the so-call Pareto optimal points (or polynomials). So far, no one is able to prove the existence of them. In this project, the PI will also apply the theory of amoeba to search for them. In the second part of this project, the PI will apply the various methods in geometric function theory to obtain some new equalities on the critical points and critical values of a polynomial that are closely related to Smale’s mean value conjecture. 許多物理和工程問題都涉及尋找多項式的零點，而牛頓方法被廣泛認為是最重要的零點算法。費茲爾獎得主斯蒂芬.斯梅爾在1981年發表的開創性論文中，提出了牛頓方法的效率和計算複雜性的新研究方向。隨後，他和Michael Shub研究其它的零點搜尋算法。斯梅爾在 1981年的論文中，證明了一系列多項式不等式，其中最有名的是他的平均值定理，這是一個有關多項式臨界點和臨界值的不等式。斯梅爾還提出了六個尋找這些不等式中的常數的精確值問題。在過去的三十多年中，大部分研究都集中在斯梅爾平均值猜想: 即研究在斯梅爾平均值定理中的常數的精確值。這是由於其在複動力系統中的潛在應用，它更被列在著名的斯梅爾21世紀數學問題清單中。 另一方面，只有很少人考慮過斯梅爾多項式不等式中的常數的精確值問題，獲得這些常數的精確值具有重要的應用意義，它會給我們一個牛頓方法收斂速度非常快的更大區域。在這項目的第一部分，我們將首次引進一個新的工具 ── 變形蟲理論，來研究斯梅爾多項式不等式。變形蟲理論是首次由Gelfand，Kapranov和Zelevinsky在1994年提出，它是當今研究熱帶幾何的非常重要工具。此項目首席研究員將運用變形蟲理論來證明斯梅爾不等式問題中極值多項式的存在和這些極值多項式的特性，這最終可能會幫助我們確定它們的精確形式。在斯梅爾的論文中，他還引進並建議研究所謂的帕累托最優多項式。到目前為止，沒有人能夠證明它們的存在。在這個項目中，首席研究員將運用變形蟲理論來尋找它們。在這個項目的第二部分，首席研究員計劃用幾何函數論的新方法（例如，極值長度的方法），來獲得類似斯梅爾平均值不等式的新不等式。

704611.label: Realisation of objectives
704611.value: The PI has applied the theory of amoeba to give a unified treatment on the existence of the extremal polynomials for the sharp constants in two Smale’s inequalities (the mean value inequality and the one directly related to it) . The PI has successfully applied the theory of amoeba to study for the first time the Pareto optimal extremal polynomials for both inequalities. It was proved that under some assumptions, any extremal polynomials must be Pareto optimal and certain properties of these Pareto optimal extremal polynomials were obtained. All the results were reported in the paper “Smale's Mean Value Conjecture and Amoeba” which was submitted to Advances in Mathematics. The PI worked with his undergraduate project student Zhang Yong Quan to apply geometric function theory to study Smale’s mean value conjecture for finite Blaschke products. It turned out that the confirmation of the conjecture for finite Blaschke products will give solve the conjecture for polynomials. Using this connection, we were able to improve the bound for the dual mean value conjecture. The results were reported in a paper to be appeared in an issue of Journal of Analysis for David Minda’s retirement conference. While studying Smale’s seminal paper on Fundamental Theorem of Algebra which contains the Smale’s inequalities studied in this project as well as the problem on the Pareto optimal points (or polynomials), the PI noticed that the density estimates used by Smale in this paper can also be used to estimate the density of composite polynomials. This results is a joint paper (with CY Tsang and WS Cheung) on density of composite polynomials which has been published for the publication in Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society (Volume 95 / Issue 3) in 2013. The PI and his PhD student PL Cheung the Bezout type theorem used in Smale’s work on computational complexity of zero finding methods can also be used to study the number of fixed equilibrium configurations of point vortices in the plane with a background flow. This work has been published in Nonlinearity (Volume 27, Number 10) in 2014. PL Cheung then moved on to study some zero and critical point distribution problem of polynomials and finite Blaschke products and received his PhD degree in 2014. In conclusion, all the objectives of the project are realized

704611.label: Major findings and research outcome
704611.value: The PI introduced the theory of amoeba to the study of Smale's mean value conjecture for the first time and proved a necessary and sufficient condition for the conjecture to be true. By considering certain Max-Min and Min-Max problem on hypersurfaces in $mathbb{C}^n$, the PI considered a dual mean value conjecture and proved the existence of an extremal polynomial for this dual conjecture. The PI also studied Smale's Pareto optimal points among those extremal polynomials for the mean value conjecture for the first time and obtained a result which says that if the Smale's constant is strictly increasing as a function of the degree, then every extremal polynomial of Smale's mean value conjecture is Pareto optimal. Motivated by a dictionary between polynomials and finite Blaschke products, the PI studied both Smale's mean value conjecture and its dual conjecture for finite Blaschke products in this project using geometric function theory, in particular an inequality of Duren and Schiffer was improved and then applied to obtain a result on the dual conjecture for finite Blaschke products. This then allows the PI and his student Y.Q. Zhang to improve a bound obtained by V. Dubinin and T. Sugawa for the dual mean value conjecture for polynomials. This is the best result so far for the dual mean value conjecture for polynomials

704611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
704611.value: In recent years, there are some new results on the membership problem of amoeba, for example Schroeter and Wolff’s very recent paper “The Boundary of Amoebas” give a partial solution to this problem and it would be very interesting to see if their result can be used to improve the Smale’s constant through the amoeba approach of this project. The connection between the mean value conjecture for polynomials and finite Blaschke considered in this project stated a new research direction for Smale’s mean value conjecture. As it is easier to apply results in geometric function theory to finite Blaschke products, it is expected that this will be quite a fruitful direction and the PI will train a research student to work in this direction.

704611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
704611.value: Critical points of a polynomial are the zeros of the first order derivative of a polynomial and the values of the polynomial at the critical points are called critical values. They are fundamental concepts for polynomials and it is very important to how these concepts. The Fields Medalist Steve Smale conjectured a number of inequalities for them in 1981. In this project, amoeba theory and geometric function theory were applied to study these inequalities and some new results were obtained.

704811.label: Project Objectives
704811.value: Time-resolved (fs-TA, TR3) spectra will be acquired for both one and two meta methoxy substituted compounds so as to investigate the meta effect on the heterolytic cleavage in the benzylic single chromophore molecules versus the methoxy substituted bichromophoric benzoin systems. Various solvents will be used in these experiments to examine solvent and hydrogen bonding effects on the single and bichromophore containing molecules studied. These single and birchomophore benzoin molecules with various leaving groups will also be examined to see how these leaving groups influence the electronic excited state character, pathways and dynamics. Time-resolved absorption (fs-TA and ns-TA) and TR3 spectroscopy experiments will be done to study the photoredox reaction observed for the photolysis of 3-(hydroxymethyl)benzophenone in acidic (pH<3) aqueous solution so as to characterize the photophysics and reaction intermediates involved in this reaction. Analogous experiments will be performed with varying pH and solvent systems to study how other reactions like photohydration compete with this unusual photoredox reaction. Time-resolved spectroscopy experiments (fs-TA, ns-TA and ns TR3) will be done to characterize the electronic excited states and reactive intermediates involved in the photochemical deuterium exchange reaction reported for the 3-methyl group in 4-methylbenzophenone and 3-methylacetophenone to learn more about how the 3-methyl group is activated by this meta substitution. Molecular systems with meta methoxy or other groups added on one or both of the benzylic rings will be studied to investigate further meta effects on this reaction. Time-resolved spectroscopy experiments (fs-TA, ns-TA and ns TR3) will be performed to study why 3-acetylphenylacetic acid has a much more efficient photodecarboxylation (quantum yield of 0.60) than 4-acetylphenylacetic acid (quantum yield of 0.22) in neutral aqueous solutions. This work will directly examine the photophysics and photochemistry on the ultrafast time scale that are not yet available for these systems. TR3 experiments will be done to obtain structural information for the intermediates seen in these two compounds. This work will result in an improved under standing of this unusual meta effect for the activation of a methyl group. In order to gain an improved understanding of the experimental data obtained in objectives 1-4, we will perform ab initio calculations (like CASSCF) on selected molecular systems to study the character and nature of the electronic excited states and their reaction pathways that are involved in the different meta effect photochemistry investigated in this proposal. The combined experimental and computational results obtained in objectives 1-5 will be compared to help elucidate similarities and differences in the meta effect excited states and their associated photochemistry.

704811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
704811.value: Meta substitutions of functional groups in a number of different aromatic compounds have been observed to lead to unexpected and interesting photochemical reactions and reactivity. The employment of meta substitutions can result in significant increases in the efficiency and cleanness of the cleavage of a leaving group from phototriggers and other types of molecules. This meta effect photochemistry was used to develop the 3’5’-dimethoxybenzoin (DMB) class of compounds to be very effective photoremovable protecting groups (PRPGs) for many kinds of leaving groups that have found useful applications in drug delivery, lithographic synthesis, making biochips, initiating protein folding and unfolding. Meta substitutions were observed to substantially increase the efficiency of photodecarboxylation in several acetophenone molecules and result in efficient photoredox reactions for several meta substituted benzophenone compounds. In order to better exploit the potential of meta substitutions for useful photochemical applications, it is necessary to better understand how this effect works in the photochemistry of interest. Some time-resolved transient absorption experiments on the nanosecond to microsecond time scale as well as quenching studies and product analysis have been done to characterize the excited states and intermediates associated with the meta effect photochemistry. However, the identities of many intermediates are still not clear. In addition, the properties and chemical reactivity of the excited states and intermediates involved in the meta effect photochemistry reactions are still not characterized in detail especially their structures and properties. Thus, there is still uncertainty regarding the reaction mechanisms responsible for the meta effect photochemistry. We propose to use several time-resolved spectroscopy methods to directly probe the excited states and intermediates in more detail and over a wider range of time scales (from the ultrafast time-scale to the nanosecond and microsecond time scales) than has been done in the past so as to better characterize and elucidate the intermediates and reaction mechanisms of selected meta effect photochemical reactions. Substituent and solvent and hydrogen bonding effects on the meta effect photochemical reactions of interest will also be explored. This proposed detailed and extensive time-resolved spectroscopy study will achieve a better understanding of how the meta effect substitutions work and how the surrounding reaction environment affect the structure, properties and chemical reactivity. This new and detailed data will also enable us to develop improved structure-reactivity relationships that can be used to design and improve meta effect photochemistry of aromatic compounds for PRPGs and other applications. 大量研究發現，許多不同芳香化合物的間位取代官能團會導致不可預期/意外的、有趣的光化學反應和活性，間位取代能提高光觸發劑和其他類型分子的離去基團斷裂效率和清潔程度。間位光化學效應已被應用於改善3,5'-Dimethoxybenzoin這類化合物，使其能夠成為各種類型離去基團有效地光移除保護基團，這一特性使該類化合物已廣泛應用與藥物運輸、光刻合成、生物晶片製作、啟動蛋白的摺疊和展開中。另外，間位取代能夠提高苯乙酮分子的脫羧效率和間位取代的二苯甲酮光氧化還原反應效率。爲了更深入地探索間位取代效應在光化學的應用，有必要探索闡明它在重要分子體系中的工作機理。目前，微秒和納秒時間分辨光譜、淬滅研究和產物分析已被應用於間位效應光化學引起的激發態和中間體的表徵。但是，許多反應中間體的特性和結構還不清楚。至今，間位效應光化學引起的激發態和中間體的性質和光化學反應活性，特別是它們的結構特徵，還沒有被詳細的描述和闡明。因此，關於間位效應光化學反應機理，還有很多問題懸而未解。如今，我們實驗室已配置搭建了各種時間分辨光譜儀，極大地突破了過去技術的限制，可以更加徹底的表徵和闡明所選間位效應光化學反應中產生的中間體及其反應機理，我們設法使用各種不同時間範圍的（從飛秒到納米、毫秒時間範圍）時間分辨光譜技術更直接地更詳細地探測反應過程中的激發態和中間體。同時，我們也會研究取代基效應，溶劑效應以及氫鍵效應對於有重要意義的間位效應光化學體系的影響。廣泛透切的時間分辨光譜研究將有助於更好地理解間位取代作用機制和反應環境對結構，性質和光化學反應活性的影響。時間分辨光譜對於間位效應新的探索能夠構築結構和反應活性間的關係，這將有助於科學家設計，改進和提高離去基團的光移除保護基團芳香化合物的間位效應和其他應用。

704811.label: Realisation of objectives
704811.value: 3-(hydoxymethyl)benzophenone and 2-(1-hydroxyethyl) 9, 10-anthroquinone (2-HEAQ) were studied using femtosecond transient absorption (fs-TA), nanosecond transient absorption (ns-TA) and nanosecond time-resolved resonance Raman (ns-TR3) spectroscopy techniques and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. In water-containing solutions with varying pH values, an unusual photoredox reaction was investigated and characterized. The photoredox reaction prefers to take place in moderate acidic solutions compared to neutral solution and the protonation of the carbonyl group was the rate-determining step for the photoredox reaction. The reaction mechanisms and key reactive intermediates for the unusual photoredox reaction were deduced and have implications for using BP and AQ scaffolds for phototrigger compounds. This research is detailed in journal publications 1, 2 and 5 listed in part C of this report and addresses project objectives 2, 3, 5 and 6 and completed objective 2. The photochemical reactions of 3-methylbenzophenone (3-MeBP) and 4-methylbenzophenone (4-MeBP) were studied using time-resolved spectroscopy methods and DFT calculations. How the meta-methyl activation takes place after photolysis of 3-MeBP in acid aqueous solutions was elucidated and compared to related photochemistry of other meta substituted aromatic carbonyl compounds. These results were reported in publication 3 and addressed project objectives 3, 5 and 6 and completed project objective 3. Photo-excitation of 2-acetoxymethyl-2-(3-benzoyl-phenyl)-propionic acid (KP-OAc) and related compounds like flurbiprofen, norflacin and suprofen can lead to photodecarboxylation or other cleavage reactions with the help of water molecules or perchloric acid. These results provide new insights into the properties of using these platforms for phototrigger applications and how changing the pH can switch on and off the phototrigger reactions of KP derivative phototriggers. This work is reported in publications 4, 7, 10, 11, 12 and addresses project objectives 1,4, 5 and 6. Some methoxy substituted benzoin, and other selected meta substituted compounds were also made and examined using time-resolved spectroscopy experiments and DFT calculations to address project objectives 1, 5 and 6 and resulted in publications 6 and 13 in part C with a couple of other manuscripts to be published in due course. The results of all of the research described above have been presented at the international conferences 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and their details are given in section C. Two PhD students, Jiani MA and Tao SU had their PhD degrees based on this projects research (details are given on Section C. Essentially, all of the project objectives have been addressed and completed.

704811.label: Major findings and research outcome
704811.value: Many substituted aromatic carbonyl compounds were synthesized and studied using time-resolved spectroscopy experiments and theoretical calculations. This research has obtained useful spectra and data on a number of aromatic carbonyl derivatives. A brief description for some of the research outcomes are given below. 3-(hydoxymethyl)benzophenone and2-(1-hydroxyethyl) 9, 10-anthroquinone (2-HEAQ) were investigated by several types of time-resolved spectroscopy experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The observation of protonated species in neutral and acidic aqueous solutions demonstrated the carbonyl oxygen of both compounds triplet states were protonated and acted as precursors of the photoredox reactions of interest. The protonation of the carbonyl group was the rate-determining step for the photoredox reaction. But under stronger acidic conditions (pH 0), although the protonated triplet state was formed, the predominant reaction was the photohydration reaction instead of the photoredox reaction. The reaction mechanisms and key reactive intermediates for the unusual photoredox reaction were elucidated and implications for their use as phototrigger compounds were considered. This research is detailed in publications 1, 2 and 5 listed in part C. 3-methylbenzophenone (3-MeBP) and 4-methylbenzophenone (4-MeBP) were similarly examined to study an unusual acid-catalyzed methyl activation reaction of 3-MeBP that can compete with a photohydration reaction whereas only the photohydration reaction was seen for 4-MeBP under the acidic pH conditions studied. How the meta-methyl activation takes place after photolysis of 3-MeBP in acid aqueous solutions was elucidated and compared to related photochemistry of other meta substituted aromatic carbonyl compounds. These results were reported in publication 3. A range of drug related compounds such as flurbiprofen, norflacin, suprofen, ketoprofen (KP) and 2-acetoxymethyl-2-(3-benzoyl-phenyl)-propionic acid (KP-OAc) can be photolyzed in aqueous environments and result in photodecarboxylation or other cleavage reactions with the help of water molecules or perchloric acid. These results give new insights into the properties of using these platforms for phototrigger applications and how changing the pH can switch on and off the phototrigger reactions of KP derivative phototriggers. This work is presented in publications 4, 7, 10, 11, 12. Some methoxy substituted benzoin, and other selected meta substituted compounds were also synthesized and investigated using time-resolved spectroscopy experiments and DFT calculations to determine how the photocleavage reactions of interest are able to take place and what can influence their use in phototrigger applications. These results are detailed in publications 6 and 13 in part C with several other manuscripts to be published in due course.

704811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
704811.value: There is a lot of potential for further development in better understanding the range of meta effect photochemistry for a wide range of organic compounds and in the applications for these interesting met effect photochemical reactions. Several of the aromatic carbonyl compounds with meta effect photochemical reactions have been developed to serve as platforms for photodeprotection and phototrigger compounds in aqueous environments (such as some types of ketprofenate, benzoin and benzophenone derivatives). These kinds of compounds can be further explored for different types of substituents and substitution patterns to improve their properties for particular applications in organic synthesis as well in physiology and biology experiments. Also, several types of aromatic carbonyl compounds such as meta substituted benzophenones, anthraquinones and others exhibited unusual and very efficient photoredox reactions that can be further developed for applications in chemistry and biology. In addition, a number of drugs like ketoprofen, norfloxacin, suprofen and others display meta effect photochemistry that has an influence of their phototoxicity effects and a better understanding of this photochemistry in aqueous solutions provides a foundation for further research in how to reduce and mitigate the phototoxicitiy in the development of new and improved drugs.

704811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
704811.value: Meta effect photochemistry of selected organic photochemical reactions were studied in this project. Substitution at the meta position in aromatic carbonyl and related organic compounds have been found to lead to unusual photohemical outcomes in aqueous solutions and in particular, in acid aqueous solutions. Some of these meta substituted aromatic carbonyl compounds can undergo novel and unusual photoredox, methyl-activation or photocleavage reactions that do not occur in non-aqueous solutions or aqueous solutions that do not have their pH in a certain range. In order to better understand how these reactions actually work and what role the water molecules and acid environment has in making these unusual reactions possible, time-resolved spectroscopy experiments were done to directly observe the excited states and intermediate species involved with the unusual reactions of interest. Supporting quantum mechanical calculations were also done to help interpret this new experimental data. The results of these time-resolved experiments have allowed us to elucidate the key reactive intermediates responsible for the meta effect photochemistry which will help further development of these compounds to serve as platforms for photodeprotection and phototrigger compounds in aqueous environments for a range of applications in chemical synthesis as well as in physiology and biology experiments.

704911.value: Prof Dahlberg, E. Dan Dr Shull, Robert

704911.label: Project Objectives
704911.value: Objectives The goal of this project is to carry out systematic experimental studies on the influence of junction geometry (junction area, oxide barrier thickness, and magnetic free-layer thickness) on MTJ low-frequency (0.1 Hz to 100 kHz) noise which were not explored before. The specific aims are: 1. To calculate the influence of junction geometry on magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) noise based on the theoretical noise model, and then determine the design of experimental samples. 2. To investigate experimentally the dependence of low-frequency noise of MTJs on junction area and compare with the calculation. 3. To investigate experimentally the dependence of low-frequency noise of MTJs on thickness of insulating oxide barrier and compare with the calculation. 4. To investigate experimentally the dependence of low-frequency noise of MTJs on thickness of magnetic free layer and compare with the calculation. 5. To develop a MTJ sensor prototype that provides the minimized noise level with optimized junction geometry based on the research outcomes from objectives 2, 3, and 4.

704911.label: Major findings and research outcome
704911.value: As suggested by the RGC Panel Member in the previous progress report, all the analysis of the experimental results were completed and published in the journal paper "Comprehensive noise characterization of magnetic tunnel junction sensors for optimizing sensor performance and temperature detection" published in the SCI journal "Materials Research Innovations" and also presented these experimental results in the International Conferences of Asian Union of Magnetics Societies (IcAUMS) 2014. Major research outputs: 5 peer-reviewed journal papers (3 on experimental results, 2 on theoretical calculation results) 6 papers presented in recognized international conferences 3 PhD students trained and graduated Major findings: 1. We have investigated the influence of junction geometry on the noise spectrum of a magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) sensor. The fluctuation of the MTJ sensor was extracted from the micromagnetic simulation result. A noise analysis program was written in MATLAB to carry out fast fourier transform on the fluctuation to obtain the noise spectrum. The effect of the junction geometry, particularly the edge effect, was found to have significant influence on the noise performance of the sensor. 2. We carried out noise measurement on them to find out its relation between noise and junction area. The measurement experiments have been completed, and we completed the analysis of all the experimental results. Further physical insights on how junction area should be optimized to minimize the sensor noise were obtained. 3. We carried out noise measurement on them to find out its relation between noise and insulating oxide barrier. The measurement experiments have been completed, and we completed the analysis of all the experimental results. Further physical insights on how thickness of insulating oxide barrier should be optimized to minimize the sensor noise were obtained. 4. We carried out noise measurement on them to find out its relation between noise and magnetic free layer. The measurement experiments have been completed, and we completed the analysis of all the experimental results. Further physical insights on how thickness of magnetic free layer should be optimized to minimize the sensor noise were obtained. 5. We have made significant progress on optimizing the junction geometry. We have applied what we have learned from objectives 2, 3, and 4 in fabricating optmized MTJ sensors.

704911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
704911.value: For the past 20 years, magnetic sensors have found enormous applications in many aspects. Detection of ultralow magnetic fields between 1 femtoTesla to about 100 picoTesla has significant practical applications in weapon detection and biomedical imaging. Magnetoresistive thin film sensors are a very promising candidate for this purpose because they are low-cost, low-power, and portable. Learning from the results of this GRF research project, there are good reasons to believe that this type of sensor technology can be pushed into the 1 picoTesla regime by using magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) because MTJs have a large magnetoresistance (MR) and they can be made with low noise. We should move on to work on the ultimate fabrication of the ultrasensitive MTJ magnetic field sensors with 1 picoTesla sensitivity at low frequency.

704911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
704911.value: The research outcomes of this project created great impact in pushing forward the frontier of scientific knowledge on low-frequency noise and advancing spintronic magnetic sensor technology on noise reduction. The mechanisms of electronic 1/f noise and magnetic 1/f noise have been revealed. This study sheds light on the unknown 1/f noise mechanism and completes the theoretical model. The research results also provide clear design guidance for reducing sensor noise level and improving sensor sensitivity by fine-tuning the MTJ junction geometry.

705111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
705111.value: Solids are not pure. Imperfections such as vacancies, impurities, and disorders constitute most origins to resistivity in solids. However, recently discovered topological insulators possess time-reversal protected conducting boundary states that are believed to be immune to the weak imperfections. They are similar to the integer quantum Hall effect, in which the cyclotron motion of electrons in a strong magnetic field gives rise to insulating bulk states but metallic conducting states propagating along edges of the system. In the topological insulators, the role of the magnetic field is replaced by the strong spin-orbit coupling, a relativistic effect in which electrons experience an effective “magnetic field” when moving. Spin-orbit coupling preserves the time reversal symmetry. Due to Kramer’s degeneracy the resulting edge states appear in helical pairs, in which one state is the time-reversal counterpart of the other, propagating along opposite directions and with opposite spins. The symmetry guarantees that the propagating direction of an electron and its spin must flip simultaneously, leading to no backscattering between the boundary states by non-magnetic imperfections and interactions, thus promising to give the ideal conducting channels. Many materials are confirmed experimentally as topological insulators, such as HgTe/CdTe quantum wells, BixSb1−x alloy, stoichiometric crystals Bi2Se3, Bi2Te3, etc. In deep origin, the topological insulators are distinguished from the ordinary band insulators according to the so-called Z2 invariant classification of the time-reversal band insulators. One consequence of the Z2 classification is the bulk-boundary correspondence, i.e. the change of the Z2 index at the boundaries of topological insulator leads to the topologically protected edge or surface states. Imperfections, such as impurity, vacancy, and disorder, are inevitably present in topological insulators. They, in a way, can be viewed as small boundaries, thus may attract bound states around them due to the same bulk-boundary correspondence. These bound states should be also topologically-protected like the edge states in the quantum spin Hall effect and the surface states in three-dimensional topological insulators. The present project are devoted to explore the physical origin of the formation of the in-gap bound states, possible effects of these bound state to the transport properties of topological insulator, and possible application of the single-impurity bound states in quantum electronic devices. The project will be of fundamental interests. It will help us to explore the properties of new material and to enrich the knowledge of condensed matter physics. 固體不是純淨的。各種缺陷，如空位，雜質，和無序等構成了固體中電阻的主要來源。不過，近期發現的拓撲絕緣體具有拓撲保護的導電邊界態。這種邊界態不受弱缺陷等影響，它們的來源類似于整數量子霍耳效應中的邊緣態。在量子霍爾效應中，強磁場下的電子迴旋運動使體態局域化為絕緣體，而沿邊緣形成導電的邊緣態。在拓撲絕緣體中，磁場的作用被強的自旋軌道耦合替代。自旋軌道耦合是一種相對論量子力學效應，它使運動電子感受到一種與電子自旋相關的有效磁場。自旋軌道耦合保持時間反演對稱性，由此產生的邊緣態因為克萊默斯的簡並會成對出現，其中一個態是另一個態的時間反演態，沿相反的方向傳播的態具有相反的自旋指向。由於時間反演對稱性保證電子傳播的方向和它的自旋必須同時翻轉，因此非磁性的缺陷和相互作用都不會使邊界態產生向後散射，從而實現一種理想的導電通道。實驗已經證實許多材料都是拓撲絕緣體，如碲化汞/碲化鎘量子阱(HgTe/ CdTe)，鉍銻合金（BixSb1-x），硒化鉍（ Bi2Se3）和碲化鉍（Bi2Te3）晶體。在更深的層次上說，根據所謂的Z2時間反演不變指數對能帶絕緣體的分類，拓撲絕緣體有別于普通絕緣體。 Z2的分類的一個結果是體態與邊界態的對應關係，即在拓撲絕緣體的邊界由於Z2指數的變化會產生受拓撲保護的邊界態（二維稱為邊緣態，三維稱為表面態）。另一方面，各種缺陷，如雜質，空位，和無序，都不可避免地出現在拓撲絕緣體內。在某種程度上，他們可以被看做作微小的邊界，從而可以在它們周圍束縛微小的邊界態，即束縛態。這些束縛態也應像量子自旋霍爾效應的邊緣態和三維拓撲絕緣體表面態一樣受到保護，並且存在於能隙之內。本專案致力於探索能隙束縛態形成的物理根源，這些束縛態對拓撲絕緣體輸運性質可能產生的影響，以及單個雜質束縛態在量子電子器件中可能的應用。該專案對物理學研究具有基本意義，將有助於我們探索新材料的性能和豐富凝聚態物理知識。

705111.label: Realisation of objectives
705111.value: PI has realized all objectives in this GRF proposal. The main results have been published in 10 refereed papers, including 2 Physical Review Letters and 5 Physical Review B. In the objective 1, the solutions of the topological protected bound states were obtained in two- and three-dimensional systems. The physical properties of the bound states have been discussed in details. In the objective 2, the bound states induced by impurities can cause the resonant tunneling in quantum spin Hall system. This should be measurable experimentally. In the objective three 3, possible role of the bound states in transport has been investigated in several systems, including the quantum percolation, quantum transport, and weak localization and antilocalization induced by disorders in topological insulators.

705111.label: Major findings and research outcome
705111.value: The objective of this project is to investigate the topologically-protected in-gap bound state induced by impurities or defects in topological insulator and superconductors. So far 10 refereed papers have been published, among which 2 appear in Physical Review Letters, 5 in Physical Review B, 1 in EPL, 1 in New Journal of Physics, and 1 Review Article in Proc. of SPIE. The major findings of this project are 1. Vacancy-induced in-gap bound states in topological insulators: WE find an exact solution of a hole or vacancy in topological insulators. Coexistence of the in-gap bound states and the edge or surface states in topological insulators suggests that imperfections may affect transport properties of topological insulators via additional bound states near the system boundary.(Refs. 5, 9 &10) 2. Quantum transport and disorders in topological insulators: We obtained a conductivity formula for topological materials by taking into account the disorders and electron-electron interaction simultaneously. The formula shows that the temperature dependence of the conductivity is dominated by the interaction while the magnetoconductivity is mainly contributed by the quantum interference. (Refs. 7 & 8) The effect of disorders in quantum anomalous Hall effect, and extrinsic anomalous Hall effect were studied theoretically. We developed quantum transport theory for magnetic topological insulator thin films, which is a good agreement with the experimental observation of the quantum anomalous Hall effect. (Ref. 3 & 4) 3. Quantum percolation in quantum spin Hall antidote systems: We study the influences of antidot-induced bound states on transport properties of two-dimensional quantum spin Hall insulators. The bound states are found able to induce quantum percolation in the originally insulating bulk. At some critical antidot densities, the quantum spin Hall phase can be completely destroyed due to the maximum quantum percolation. For systems with periodic boundaries, the maximum quantum percolation between the bound states creates intermediate extended states in the bulk which is originally gapped and insulating. The antidot-induced bound states plays the same role as the magnetic field in the quantum Hall effect, both makes electrons go into cyclotron motions. (Ref. 1 &4) 4. Impurity influence in quantum spin Hall system: In a geometry of slab with finite width, electron in helical edge states protected by the time-reversal symmetry can tunnel through nonmagnetic impurities at two resonant energy levels. Electrons of one-side can tunnel to another side and the quantized conductance can be broken down. (Ref. 5)

705111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
705111.value: Impurity issue is still a crucial one in topological materials. The completion of the project provides us a new starting point to investigate further transport properties of the topological materials. This year PI has already submitted a GRF proposal to study newly discovered Weyl semimetals, in which the disorder and transport will be the focus.

705311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
705311.value: The Central Asian Orogenic Belt (CAOB) is the largest Phanerozoic orogen in the world with ~5.3 million km2 of accreted rocks formed in a variety of tectonic environments in the Paleo-Asian Ocean, which existed for more than 800 million years (Ma). Because these rocks are now mostly allochthonous to the region and were amalgamated at different times, we face a great challenge in understanding the geological evolution of this giant orogenic belt. An extended international debate exists on its complicated accretionary history which can only be solved through detailed study reconstructing the tectonic setting of each major geological terrane. Numerous world-class mineral deposits including gold, copper and rare metals, occur in the CAOB; therefore, its study has significant economic implications in term of guiding mineral exploration. The Altai Mountain Range is a very important part of the CAOB. Metasedimentary rocks are major components of the region, intercalated with some volcanic rocks and intruded by magmatic plutons. The tectonic nature of the Altai was interpreted as a Precambrian microcontinent by some researchers but is now regarded by some other researchers as a series of Paleozoic arcs built on an older continental margin. The controversy stems from the lack of precise isotopic age data. Only with the rapid advancement of modern analytical techniques in recent years can the above problems be settled on the basis of precise and systematic geological, geochemical and isotopic studies. A new state-of-the art Multiple Collector ICP-MS, coupled with a UV laser probe, has been set-up in our laboratory in 2009. The investigators of this project have combined field experience and analytical expertise on modern isotope geochronology. We will carry out field investigation in both the Chinese and Mongolian Altai. Systematic petrological work as well as elemental and Sm-Nd isotopic analyses and detrital zircon U-Pb dating and Hf isotopic study will be conducted on metasedimentary rocks. Our results will show whether the Altai contains old continental rocks. If yes, we shall further investigate from which continent these materials were derived – Siberia, Gondwanaland, or Tarim. If not, we shall further test whether the Altai was a continental margin in the Palaeozoic and what type of margin it was, i.e. active or passive and which continent it evolved on. Results of this study will considerably improve our understanding of the accretionary history of the CAOB and shed light on the history of crustal growth of Asia in the Palaeozoic. 在古亚洲洋存在的8亿年历史中各种构造环境形成的大约5.3百万平方公里的岩石增生到中亚造山带，从而使它成为全球最大的显生宙造山带。由于这些岩石大多是外来的，在不同的时间增生到此，对于理解这个巨型造山带的地质演化我们面对很大的一个挑战。国际学术界在这个复杂的增生历史的认识上存在重要分歧， 而这只能靠详细的研究恢复每个主要地体的构造环境之后才能得以解决。中亚造山带有大量的世界级的矿床包括金铜稀有金属赋存，因而它的研究对指导找矿具有重要的意义。阿尔泰山脉是中亚造山带很重要的组成部分，变质沉积岩是主要的岩石组成，与一些火山岩互层并被岩体侵入。阿尔泰的构造属性被一些研究者解释为前寒武纪微陆块，但近来的一些研究者认为其为形成于一个大陆边缘的古生代岛弧。争议来源于精确同位素年龄数据的缺乏。只有在现代分析技术快速发展的今天这些问题在精确和系统的地质、地球化学和同位素研究的基础上才能得以解决。目前最先进的与紫外激光探针连接的多接收等离子体质谱仪在2009年在我们的实验室建立起来。本课题研究人员具有野外和现代同位素年代学的研究经验，我们将针对变质沉积岩在中蒙阿尔泰进行野外、岩石学、元素地球化学、Sm-Nd碎屑锆石U-Pb定年和Hf同位素研究工作。我们的研究结果将证明阿尔泰是否有古老大陆岩石的存在，如果存在我们将进一步研究来源于那个大陆，是西北利亚，冈瓦纳还是塔里木。如果不存在，我们将进一步研究阿尔泰是否为古生代的大陆边缘，活动抑或被动边缘，以及与那个大陆有关。这项研究的结果将在很大程度上加深我们对中亚造山带增生历史和古生代亚洲地壳增长的认识。

705311.label: Realisation of objectives
705311.value: The field work was successfully conducted and representative metasedimentary and related intrusive rock samples were collected. Zircon Hf isotopic analytical method was successfully established on our Multiple Collector - Laser Ablation - Inductively Coupled Plasma - Mass Spectrometer. Zircon minerals were separated from the selected samples and analysed for U-Pb and Hf isotopic compositions. The selected whole rock samples were analysed for Sm-Nd isotopic compositions. Data for the analyzed metasedimentary rocks from the Mongolian Altai have been compared with all of our data for the Chinese Altai. The geochemical compositions and isotopic compositions indicate that the metasediments were immature and mostly derived from local/nearby juvenile sources. They do not represent Precambrian basement, but deposited in an continental arc environment. Our data show that the micro-continent did not exit in the Altai region, the region was an active margin on the Tuwa Mongolia microcontinent. We further traced the link of this microcontinent with large continents in the world and our data depict that the micro-continent was possibly part of North India. We have reported our results in international and national conferences, some results published in international journals. Our results are critical in evaluating whether a microcontinent existed in the Altai region and in reconstructing the Palaeozoic accretionary process for Central Asian Orogenic Belt, which is the purpose of this study.
