705311.label: Major findings and research outcome
705311.value: Our geochemical and isotopic research indicate answered that micro-continent does not exist in the study area, and the Chinese and Mongolian Altai represent an active continental margin possibly on the Tuva Mongolia Block. Our data from associated igneous rocks defined critical tectonothermal events in the region, which were resulted from accretion of multiple arc systems in the Central Asian Orogenic Belt. Our work on structural analysis indicates (1) contrasting litho-tectonic units with different metamorphism, such as the early Paleozoic low-grade Alegedayi Ophiolitic Complex (AOC) and the juxtaposed high grade Tarlang Granitic Massif (TGM), were initially detached and located in different structural levels, and were later deformed with distinct structural styles under contrasting P-T conditions. They were welded in the early Devonian and together underwent a ~WNW-ESE shortening event (D1) at ~390 Ma, which was followed by a ~NNE-SSW shortening event (D2) that marked the transition of tectonic regime. A later phase of sinistral shearing (D3) overprints the earlier structures. Our results provide solid field-based evidence for a model that the Chinese Altai initially underwent a ~E-W subduction-accretion event in the middle Paleozoic, followed by a ~N-S convergence. (2) The ~NW-SE Irtysh Shear Zone, one of the largest shear zones in Central Asia, represent a major tectonic boundary of the Central Asian Orogenic Belt. We recognized three episodes of deformation within the shear zone, which were interpreted to represent orogenic thickening (D1), collapse (D2) and transpressional thickening (D3) during the late Palaeozoic collision of the Chinese Altai with the East/West Junggar. On a larger scale, we emphasize that late Palaeozoic wrench systems in Central Asia are possibly linked with the convergence of multiple arc systems and continental blocks. Our results highlight the role of wretch tectonics during the termination of the accretionary orogenesis. (3) The Chinese Altai is characterized by the occurrence of kyanite- and andalusite-type metamorphic zones. Our structural work linked Permian transpressional tectonics with the development of metamorphic zones. We interpret that the Permian oblique convergence between the Altai and the intra-oceanic arc system of the East/West Junggar was responsible for the formation of zonal metamorphic sequences in the southern Chinese Altai. Our results highlight the role of oblique accretion in the juxtaposition of metamorphic rocks from distinct structural levels in the orogeny. The research outcomes have been published in more than 10 international SCI journals, and represented in international and national conferences (see the attached 13 meeting abstracts).

705311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
705311.value: The deformation timing has been poorly constrained by previous researchers, which significantly limits the temporal and spatial link of major structural events with regional tectonic evolution. Dating syn-deformation minerals via 40Ar/39Ar thermochronology provides a valid way to constrain the exact timing of deformation. However, this method has a long analytic period, and commonly takes one to two years in sample preparation and analysis. Our samples have been prepared in 2014, the chronological analysis has not been finished yet. Sample analysis and data interpretation/publication will be finished in 2016.

705311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
705311.value: The Central Asian Orogenic Belt is the largest accretionary orogen in the world and is dominantly made of oceanic (juvenile) materials from the mantle. In contrast, oceanic materials were mostly sub ducted back to the mantle in most orogenic belts such as the Himalayas. Therefore the mechanism of preservation of huge amount of juvenile materials in the Central Asian Orogenic Belt is a big scientific issue and it is critical for our understanding of Plate Tectonics and has a great implication in mineral exploration. In order to solve this problem, how much ancient continental materials and how many continental blocks exist must be accurately identified. The Altai mountain is the type region of the orogenic belt and was considered as a micro-continent in the orogenic belt, previous tectonic models were proposed based on this assumption. This study employed multiple disciplinary approached, clearly identified that the Altai mountain is not an ancient continental bock, instead it represents an active continental margin on the Tuva Mongolia block, which is in the northwest of the study area. The important Devonian tectonothermal event was identified and the way of accretion of different geological terranes are deciphered.

705511.label: Realisation of objectives
705511.value: This interdisciplinary project involved expertise, techniques and collaborations from ecology, molecular biology (proteomics) and materials science (biomineralization), has successfully addressed all the three objectives of this proposal. The project has quantified the effect of ocean acidification on settling oyster larvae at molecular (proteomics) and biomineralization levels using the objectives 1 and 2. The project also studied the ecological consequence of OA effect in the 3rd objective. These three interlinked objectives were executed as follows. First, graduate students have been recruited and their PhD thesis objectives aligned with this proposal aims. Secondly, we invited all our collaborators of this proposal and expertise related to this proposal for a symposium that was organized by the PI in 2012 (the symposium named “Interdisciplinary symposium on ocean acidification and climate change”). This symposium, organized specifically for this project, helped us to use the state-of-art new techniques and approaches to address our objectives. Importantly, objectives of this project were addressed through TRUE collaborations among graduate students worked in this project and across multiple institutions (within Hong Kong and overseas). The first objective, i.e. OA effect on oyster larval proteome, was achieved through the PhD thesis work of DineshRam, whose multi-disciplinary study used a variety of proteomics and modern bioinformatics techniques to study OA effect on oysters at molecular level. For example, effect of multiple climate change stressors (acidification, warming and freshening) on commercially important oyster species at molecular (proteome) level was quantified using a quantitative and comparative proteomics approach (iTRAQ labeling and LC-MS/MS). The second objective, i.e. OA effect on biomineralization, was fulfilled through three of our PhD scholars, Vera BS Chan, Roy Li and Abhishek Upadhyay. This group of graduate students with strong materials science training determined how OA could affect oyster larvae at biomineral (shell) structure, mechanics and importantly the shell organic components. Finally, the post-larval ecological fitness was determined through multiple measurements. This ecological measurement study was carried out by two scholars, Ginger Ko and Camilla Campanati. This 3rd objective was relatively challenging and we have faced numerous scientific obstacles, i.e. pacific oyster juveniles did not grow in Hong Kong’s tropical climate, and the typical oyster predators in Hong Kong do not eat the Pacific oysters that came from Northern China. We have overcome these obstacles through testing this hypothesis at a laboratory condition, using juvenile growth and survival as fitness measurements and through choosing a local oyster species as prey.

705511.label: Major findings and research outcome
705511.value: This interdisciplinary research project involving collaborations within Hong Kong and internationally, has successfully fulfilled not only the three primary research objectives but also trained several graduate students (Part C-10). This project has also engaged in a wide range of Knowledge Exchange activities to transfer the research findings to Hong Kong society. Major accomplishments of this project are outlined below under the headings “research, training and knowledge exchange”. Research: Results have been published through 11 research papers (Part C-8). Of these papers, 40% have been (or will be) published in journals ranked in the top 10% in their respective field. Besides, the PI has publicized these results through invited talks in several international conferences (Part C-9). Similarly, graduate students of this project presented their results in FIFTEEN conferences (not listed in Part C-9). This project has shed light on the molecular mechanism of how ocean acidification (OA) affects oysters. We have observed that warming can rescue the negative effects of OA on larvae by up-regulating the energy related proteins and biomineralization mechanisms. Our study of the OA effects has contributed to this new and exciting interdisciplinary research area and our use of proteomics and materials engineering tools is dramatically transforming many academic fields. Major findings could be summarized as follows: • Oysters have developed adequate mechanisms at proteomics and biomineralization levels to adapt near-future level of climate change, • The product of biomineralization, oyster shell organic matrix proteins and mechanics, however, are severely impaired or altered due to climate change stressors, especially OA, • Our shell proteomics study of closely related oysters expanded our understating of the mechanism behind the naturally occurring shells of oysters with different mechanical properties, • The pacific oyster larvae and juveniles are vulnerable to the interactions of OA with reduced salinity and warming in Yellow Sea coastal waters now and in the future. Training: The PI’s interdisciplinary collaborative approach in this project provided a conducive environment for FOUR graduate students (from engineering, medical and science faculties) to cross traditional disciplinary boundaries to expand their expertise in the research field of environmental science (Part C-10). Knowledge Exchange: This project brought together representatives from the aquaculture industry (oyster growers), academician (oyster researchers in the region) as well as policy makers (government officers) on a common platform and provided hands-on training and practical knowledge to Hong Kong’s oyster growers about the oyster seed production for a sustainable aquaculture in a changing climate.

705511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
705511.value: Due to the outcome of this project, the following new research developments are expected to happen in a very near future: • Interdisciplinary collaborations: The established strong collaborations within Hong Kong and internationally will allow the PI to carry out interdisciplinary research projects aimed at studying climate change effects on marine organisms at the developmental, biomineralization and proteomics levels, • Collaborative Research Proposal: The PI has called for a workshop on “marine shells in a changing climate: where are we heading? on September 18, 2014 to finalize our plan for the RGC’s Collaborative Research Grant Proposal in early 2016 with HKU medical school (Kelvin Yeung), City U Chemistry department (Yun Lam), HKU Civil Engineering (Kaimin Shih) and Poly U Mechanical Engineering (Hamin Yue). This naturally united group with strong enthusiasm and commitment for interdisciplinary work has already gained enough track-record such as “joint PhD student supervisions and joint publications through this project. • Links with industry: Using the HK-SAR’s recently launched Sustainable Aquaculture Fund, the PI has determined to work very closely with oyster farmers to examine the feasibility of a technology to assist local oyster growers in producing resilient oyster seeds in a cost effective and a sustainable ways.

705511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
705511.value: Increasing anthropogenic carbon dioxide taken up by the ocean is causing ocean acidification (OA) and threatening oyster survival and food security. The impacts of OA on oysters are already clear, e.g., the collapse of oyster production in the United States, and OA is at a tipping point for many oyster culturing regions in Europe and Asia. This is a serious warning to China, which produces >80% of the world’s oysters. Therefore, a mechanistic understanding of the effect of this stress on oysters is a pressing issue for scientists, oyster farmers and policy makers. This project has rightly recognized the importance of an interdisciplinary collaborative approach to understand the mechanisms of OA effect on oysters. The graduate students and the PI of this project joined hands with several Hong Kong and overseas scientists specialized in climate change, mechanical engineering, and molecular biology, which allowed us to pursue avenues that were otherwise unfeasible. This team has developed technologies for sustainable production of oysters that are healthy and safe to eat in HK under changing climate including ocean acidification. Ultimately, this interdisciplinary OA project with oysters as model has provided a holistic picture of the mechanisms that drive oysters in a changing climate.

705611.label: Project Objectives
705611.value: In this project, we will carry out a large scale numerical simulation to calculate the conductance and shot noise as well as their fluctuations in the presence of magnetic impurities using Landauer-Buttiker formula. Four different systems will be studied: (a). the graphene with Rashba SO interaction and exchange interaction. (b). the graphene with intrinsic SO interaction. (c). the TI such as HgTe/CdTe quantum well. (d). the Dirac model which has only one Dirac cone. In addition, we will use Kubo formula to study Hall conductance. In order to understand this new phase with conductance around 1/2, we will use current density as a probe to investigate current distribution and how edge states are destroyed. The critical behavior of this new phase will be studied. Theoretically, we will use the random matrix theory and the diagrammatic perturbation theory to understand the conductance fluctuation when the disorder is spin-dependent.

705611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
705611.value: Recently, the topological insulator (TI), a new state of matter, has attracted a lot of theoretical and experimental attention. The TI has an insulating energy gap in the bulk states which behaves like the general insulator, but it has exotic gapless metallic states on its edges or surfaces. The TI is first predicted in two-dimensional (2D) systems, e.g. the graphene and HgTe/CdTe quantum well. The 2D TI has the gapless helical edge states and exhibits the quantum spin Hall effect. This helical edge states, with the opposite spins on a given edge or opposite edges for a given spin direction containing opposite propagation directions, are topologically protected and are robust against all time-reversal-invariant impurities. While the spin orbit interaction is detrimental to the TI, it can also leads to another important topological phenomenon: the quantum anomalous Hall effect. Different from quantum Hall effect, the quantum anomalous Hall effect uses spin orbit interaction rather than magnetic field to break the time reversal symmetry. One of the most important features in mesoscopic system is that the conductance in the diffusive regime exhibits universal features with a universal conductance fluctuation (UCF) that depends only on the dimensionality and the symmetry of the system. Up to now, all of UCF studies focus on non-magnetic impurities. It would be very interesting and important to study the conductance fluctuation in the presence of magnetic impurities that break the time-reversal symmetry. In this project, we wish to address following issues: (1). What are the effect of magnetic impurities on edge states? (2). What are properties of conductance fluctuation for TI when magnetic impurities are present? Any universal behaviors? (3). What is the influence of magnetic impurities on quantum anomalous Hall effect in graphene systems? (4). What is the distribution of the conductance for TI and quantum anomalous Hall effect? In this project, we will study the quantum transport properties of 2D TI as well as systems that exhibit quantum anomalous Hall effect in the presence of magnetic impurities using Landauer-Buttiker formula and Kubo formula. In particular, we will investigate conductance and shot noise as well as their fluctuations. Two types of magnetic impurities will be examined: (a). non-spin flip impurity. (b). spin flip impurity. 近期，一种新的量子物态拓扑绝缘体受到了广大理论和实验研究人员的广泛关注。虽然拓扑绝缘体和普通绝缘体都有块体的带隙，但是在它的边缘或者表面存在着特殊的金属态，这些量子态位于块体能带结构的带隙之中。人们首先预言了在石墨烯和碲化汞/碲化镉量子阱中存在拓扑绝缘态。由于这些螺旋型边缘态的存在，在二维拓扑绝缘体中可以观察到量子自旋霍尔效应。对于在二维拓扑绝缘体同一边缘上的态，它们的自旋是相反的，而对于在不同边缘上自旋相同的态，它们的传播方向是相反的。由于其特殊的拓扑性质，这些边缘态基本不受具有时间反演对称性杂质的影响。自旋轨道耦合作用不仅对拓扑绝缘体的产生至关重要，而且它也可以导致另外一个重要的现象：量子反常霍尔效应。不同于量子霍尔效应的是，量子反常霍尔效应不是由外加磁场产生的，而是来源于自旋轨道耦合作用。介关体系的一个重要特征是，电导涨落在扩散区表现出普适的特性，它仅仅依赖于体系的维度和对称性。到目前为止，所有关于普适电导涨落的研究都集中在非磁性杂质上，因此对于存在破坏时间反演对称性杂质的研究是非常有趣和重要的。在这个项目中，我们致力于解决以下问题：（1）磁性杂质是怎样影响边缘态的？（2）在磁性杂质存在的情况下，拓扑绝缘体的电导涨落有哪些性质？有没有普适性？（3）磁性杂质对于石墨烯中量子反常霍尔效应的影响是什么？（4）在磁性杂质的影响下，电导在拓扑绝缘体以及存在量子反常霍尔效应的系统中是怎样分布的？在此项目中，我们将利用Landauer-Büttiker 公式 和 Kubo 公式去研究二维拓扑绝缘体和存在量子反常霍尔效应系统的输运性质。特别是研究在两种磁性杂质（非自旋反转的杂质和自旋反转的杂质）存在的情况下，电导和噪声以及它们的涨落问题。

705611.label: Realisation of objectives
705611.value: We have achieved all the objectives. In particular, we reported the effect of magnetic field on electron transport in the inverted band structure of HgTe/CdTe quantum well. Two quantum anomalous Hall-like phases were found. By tuning the Fermi energy, the system can transit between the quantum spin Hall phase and two quantum anomalous Hall-like phases, so the polarized direction of the edge current is well controllable. Due to the quantum spin and anomalous Hall-like effects, the longitudinal and Hall resistances exhibit quantum plateaus which are robust against Rashba spin-orbit interaction, Zeeman effect, and Anderson disorder. We reported the investigation of conductance fluctuation and shot noise in disordered graphene systems with two kinds of disorder. We developed an expansion method based on the coherent potential approximation (CPA) to calculate the average of four Green’s functions, and the results are obtained by truncating the expansion up to 6th order in terms of “single-site-T-matrix.” Since our expansion is with respect to “single-site-T-matrix” instead of disorder strength W, good result can be obtained at 6th order for finite W. Our formalism can be easily combined with linear muffin-tin orbital first-principles transport calculations for light doping nano-scaled systems, making prediction on variability of nano-devices. We carried out theoretical calculations of electronic and transport properties mediated by topological helical states on the walls of three-dimensional topological insulator (TI) nanowires. A universal regime of quantized conductance and fluctuations is found that is induced by disorder. The average conductance of the disordered nanowire scales as a function of the number of transmission channels N in a universal form = αN + β, independent of the system details. For instance, for Bi2Se3 nanowires cleaved along the x or y direction with the quintuple layers along the z direction, Gxx = (5/12)N + 1/2. The universal and quantized behavior is due to the topological physics happening on the walls of the nanowire under the influence of disorder. Using the non-equilibrium Green’s function formalism, we derived the current density formula for ac quantum transport by including the self-consistent Coulomb interaction. It was found that for the ac current density the Coulomb interaction contributes in two ways. The self-consistent Coulomb interaction has to be included in the conventional particle current density. In addition, we have to consider the displacement current density explicitly, which is proportional to the time derivative of displacement field.

705611.label: Major findings and research outcome
705611.value: In this project, we developed a first-principles approach based on nonequilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) combined with density functional theory (DFT) to investigate quantum transport properties of normal-metal–superconductor hybrid systems. As an application of our theory, we investigated the Andreev conductance of atomic wires consisting of 4–15 carbon atoms in contact with one normal Al lead and another superconducting Al lead from first principles. Numerical results show that the Andreev conductance oscillates between an even and odd number of carbon atoms [2]. Moreover, we presented a kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) investigation of an atomistic model for 3-dimensional structural configurations of TiO2 memristor, focusing on the oxygen vacancy migration and interaction under an external voltage. The results show that the electric field drives vacancy migration; and vacancy hopping-induced localized electric field plays a key role for the filament evolution [3]. Based on NEGF and time-dependent DFT (TDDFT), we proposed a formalism to study the time-dependent transport behavior of molecular devices from first principles. While this approach is equivalent to the time-dependent wave-function approach within TDDFT, it has the advantage that the scattering states and bound states are treated on equal footing. For the purpose of numerical implementation on molecular devices, a computational tractable numerical scheme is discussed in detail [5]. In addition, we reported the theoretical investigation of the shot noise of the spin current and the spin transfer torque for non-collinear spin polarized transport in a spin-valve device which consists of a normal scattering region connected by two ferromagnetic electrodes. Our theory was developed using the NEGF method, and general nonlinear shot noise versus voltage relations were derived as a function of the angle between the magnetizations of two leads [6]. Based on the NEGF coupled DFT, we proposed an efficient formalism to calculate the transient current of molecular devices under a step-like pulse from first principles. By combining NEGF-DFT with the complex absorbing potential (CAP), the computational complexity of our formalism (NEGF-DFT-CAP) is proportional to O(N) where N is the number of time steps [7]. Finally, we studied electron transport through a normal lead-quantum dot-topological superconductor-quantum dot-normal lead junction. We showed that two nonlocal processes can be directly controlled by gating the energy level of QDs. For instance, when both energies of QDs are equal to the coupling energy of Majorana Fermion (MF), the electron in the left lead can transport to the right lead via MFs [12].

705811.label: Project Title(Chinese)
705811.value: 基于冷原子的量子模擬和操控

705811.label: Project Objectives
705811.value: We intend to design an experimental feasible scheme to realize two (or three)-dimensional quantum systems of Dirac particles with ultracold atoms subject to the appropriate laser beams. We will then study profoundly and extensively quantum transport of the simulated Dirac particles under various controllable conditions. In particular, we will study the geometric phase accumulated in the Dirac particle’s motion for both adiabatic and non-adiabatic cases and present our predictions to be verified by future experiments with ultracold atoms. We plan to explore the superfluidity of Dirac fermions in optical lattices with various possible paring symmetries. In particular, we will use our expertise to work out an innovative but a simple feasible scheme to realize Majorana fermions and to test their non-Abelian fractional statistics with ultracold atoms. We plan also to address its possible application in quantum computation. Furthermore, it is expected to study the exotic vortex states of this superfluid by solving self-consistently the corresponding BdG equations derived for this kind of systems.

705811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
705811.value: Relativistic effects are well known to occur at the speeds of particles close to that of light. Can you image that relativistic effects may also be present for particles moving at ultra-slow speeds? Recently, scientists have been able to simulate effectively various exotic quantum phenomena including the relativistic effects at the ultra-low speeds of atoms at temperature very close the absolute zero. This kind of quantum simulation takes a distinct advantage that most relevant parameters can be well controlled experimentally, enabling us to explore and to observe more novel quantum effects that can hardly be seen before. Motivated by this, we propose (i) to design an experimental feasible scheme to realize controllable two (or three)-dimensional relativistic Dirac-type quantum systems with ultracold atoms and to study the geometric phase accumulated in the Dirac particle’s motion for both adiabatic and non-adiabatic cases; and (ii) to explore the exotic superfluidity of Dirac fermions in optical lattices with various possible paring symmetries and to address its potential applications. It is expected that the proposed research will make a timely and significant contribution to the interdisciplinary field related to quantum physics and cold atoms as well as condensed matter. 衆所周知, 相對論效應通常發生在物體的速度接近于光速時。但最近物理學家嘗試用速度遠低于光速的人造超冷原子系統來模擬新穎的相對論效應。 這種量子模擬的最大優點是相關的系統參數易于實驗調控, 以致于可觀察到一些還沒見過的新穎的相對論現象。 本研究計劃 (1)理論上設計可行的超冷原子實驗方案來實現參數可調控的相對論Dirac方程和相關的實驗現象。 (2)探索相關的Dirac 粒子的超流性及其應用。預期研究結果會對量子和冷原子及凝聚態物理的交叉研究起有意義的作用。

705811.label: Realisation of objectives
705811.value: 1. We designed an experimental scheme to simulate Dirac particles with ultracold atoms subject to the appropriate laser beams and addressed the fractionalization of particle number in optical lattices. Quantum transport phenomena of the simulated Dirac particles, including Klein tunneling and Josephson dynamics, were theoretically studied. 2. We explored the superfluidity of Dirac fermions in optical lattices. In particular, We established a unified theory of topological gapless modes, including Majorana fermions, and revealed the intrinsic connection to topological gapped systems, including superconductors and insulators. We proposed a new scheme to create and probe new topological types of Majorana fermions and addressed its potential application in quantum computation. Furthermore, some exotic vortex states of this topological superfluid was studied by solving the corresponding BdG equations.

705811.label: Major findings and research outcome
705811.value: 1. We designed an experimental feasible scheme to realize an exotic property of Dirac-like particles with ultracold atoms subject to the appropriate laser beams and studied the fractionalization of particle number. We studied macroscopic Klein tunneling and Josephson dynamics in spin-orbit coupled cold-atom systems and revealed some exotic quantum phenomena. In addition, we also investigated a new type of topological Bose-Mott insulators and disclosed an interesting edge state. 2. We obtained the exact results for the superfluid of spin-orbit coupled fermions. We also established topological classification and stability of Fermi surfaces and the intrinsic connection to topological superconductors and insulators, based on which we proposed a new scheme to create and probe new topological types of Majorana fermions that exhibit non-Abelian statistics. We studied Majorana fermion states of topological superfluid by solving either self-consistently the corresponding BdG equations or using our theory for boundary-bulk correspondence of topological superconductors, with applications to quantum computation/manipulation being addressed.

705811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
705811.value: Our established theory of topological Fermi surfaces has a great potential for exploring exotic topological quantum matter, especially for gapless ones including novel Z2 topological metals which we are mainly working on.

705811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
705811.value: As is known, relativistic effects occur at the speeds of particles close to that of light. Recently, however, physicists have been able to simulate effectively various exotic quantum phenomena including the mentioned relativistic effects at the ultra-low speeds of atoms. This kind of quantum simulation takes a distinct advantage that most relevant parameters can be well controlled experimentally, enabling us see more novel quantum effects that can hardly be seen before. In this project, we not only designed experimental feasible schemes to simulate relativistic quantum systems with ultracold atoms, but also revealed exotic superfluidity of relativistic fermions in optical lattices with potential applications in robust quantum manipulation. Remarkably, we established a topological theory of gapless modes, which has made a timely and important contribution to the field of solid state theory.

706011.label: Project Title(Chinese)
706011.value: 有限循環射影平面的幾何學

706011.label: Project Objectives
706011.value: To improve on the method developed and the results obtained in Law and Wong [25], in which it is shown that a cyclic projective plane of order m or m^2 is Desarguesian, for m a prime power at most 16 other than 13. In particular, to discover further necessary conditions imposed by the foliation structure and the web structure of a cyclic difference set of square order so as to narrow down the search for solutions determining the quadratic extensions of a cyclic projective plane. To extend the method of Wilbrink in the use of Minkowski circle geometry in the characterization of the classical unital of even order to the use of Laguerre circle geometry in the odd order case. In particular, to utilize and to extend the known relations between the circle geometry and generalized quadrangles of odd order and their antiregularity property to obtain further characterization results. To investigate the existence and types of unitals in a cyclic projective plane of square order, and to make use of knowledge gained to determine whether such a plane must be Desarguesian. In particular, to investigate whether or not the Hall's unital is isomorphic to the classical unital. In the affirmative case to investigate whether the isomorphism can be extended to the ambient plane with the result that the plane is classical. In the negative case Singer's Conjecture is proven to be false.

706011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
706011.value: 本計畫研究有限幾何學裏的一些問題。有限幾何學渉及編碼理論，有限域論，代數幾何學，有限群論，及實験區組設計。 研究對像是有限循環射影平面。研究問題是它們的存在性及類型。 有限射影平面是一個系統，包含一個點的有限集，一個叫造線的子集的族，及以下的關聯關係：（一）兩不同的點關聯於唯一線；（二）兩不同的線關聯於唯一點；（三）存在四點裏面沒有三點共線。在一個有限射影平面裏関聯於一線上的點的數目相等於関聯於一點上的線的數目。如果這數目是ｎ＋１，這個有限射影平面的階就是ｎ。一個直射變換是一個平面上的點的排列令到線映射到線。 一個射影平面是個德紮尓格平面如果裏面任何兩個中心透視三角形是軸透視。已知射影平面是德紮尓格平面當且僅當該平面可用可除環來設立座標。因有限可除環是一個域，有限德紮尓格平面可用有限域來設立座標，因而它的階是個素數冪。已知存在非德紮尓格平面，但所有已知存在的非德紮尓格平面的階都是素數冪，導致以下長達半世紀的猜想： 素數冪猜想（ＰＰＣ）：任何有限射影平面的階是素數冪。 一個有限循環射影平面（ＣＰＰ）是具有一個循環直射變換（將所有點排列成一置換圈的直射變換）的射影平面。已知有限德紮尓格平面是ＣＰＰ。它的逆就是以下著名的猜想： Ｓｉｎｇｅｒ’ｓ猜想：任何有限循環射影平面是德紮尓格平面。 因德紮尓格平面的階是素數冪，以下是一個較弱的猜想： ＣＰＰ素數冪猜想：任何有限循環射影平面的階是素數冪。 聚焦於循環射影平面是因已知具有兩個不同循環直射變換的平面是德紮尓格平面。本計畫探討具有一個循環直射變換的射影平面與德紮尓格平面的差距。基本調査個體包括循環射影平面裏的極卵形及平方階循環射影平面裏的酉形。平方階情況特殊因該等平面具有葉狀結構而且裏面存在Ｈａｌｌ極酉形。如能証明此酉形非経典型，則Ｓｉｎｇｅｒ’ｓ猜想不對。分析此等幾何及組合結構應能提供新的証據或反証據去支援或推翻ＣＰＰ素數冪猜想，甚至最終解決素數冪猜想。

706011.label: Major findings and research outcome
706011.value: A geometric proof is given in terms of Laguerre geometry of the theorem of Bagchi, Brouwer and Wilbrink, which states that if a generalized quadrangle of order s > 1 has an antiregular point then all of its points are antiregular. (Part C item 1.) The finite Figueroa planes are non-Desarguesian projective planes of order q3 for all prime powers q > 2. These planes were constructed algebraically in 1982 by Figueroa, and Hering and Schaeffer, and synthetically in 1986 by Grundh¨ofer. All Figueroa planes of finite square order are shown to possess a unitary polarity by de Resmini and Hamilton in 1998, and hence admit unitals. Using the result of O’Nan in 1971 on the non-existence of his configuration in a classical unital, and the intrinsic characterization by Taylor in 1974 of the notion of perpendicularity induced by a unitary polarity in the classical plane (introduced by Dembowski and Hughes in 1965), we show that these Figueroa polar unitals do not satisfy a necessary condition, introduced by Wilbrink in 1983, for a unitary block design to be classical, and hence they are not classical. (Part C item 2.) We give three proofs, two intrinsic and one extrinsic, that every Dickson–Ganley unital U(σ), parametrized by a field automorphism σ, is non-classical if σ is not the identity, extending a result of Ganley’s (Math Z 128:34–42, 1972); we prove that U(σ1) is isomorphic to U(σ2) if and only if σ_1 = σ_2 or σ_1 = σ_2 ^−1 ; and we determine the (design) automorphism group of U(σ) as the collineation subgroup of the ambient Dickson semifield plane stabilizing the unital. This contains as a special case the corresponding result of O’Nan’s (J Algebra 20:495–511, 1972) on the classical unital. (Part C item 3.) A necessary and sufficient condition is given for embedding a unital into a projective plane as a polar unital. A strengthened version of the condition is introduced and is shown to be necessary for a classical unital. Using the strengthened condition and results of Wilbrink (1983) and Grundh"ofer, Stroppel and Van Maldeghem (2013), a new intrinsic characterization of the classical unital is given without assuming the absence of O'Nan configurations. Finally, a unital of even order satisfying the first two intrinsic characterization conditions of Wilbrink is shown to satisfy the strengthened condition by an elementary (combinatorial-geometric) proof and without invoking deep results from group theory. (Part C item 4.)

706011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
706011.value: This research leads to the investigation in depth of unitary block designs, and it is proposed that this be the subject of a research project on the characterization and classification of unitary block designs. This proposal has been rewarded by an RGC GRF grant Number HKU704613P.

706011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
706011.value: The research project concerns the theory of designs which has roots in statistical experiments and has far reaching significance both in pure mathematics especially in the area of finite geometry and in applied mathematics especially in the area of coding. As a result, the research project leads to new insights and directions in the study of unitary block designs, and continuing work is being supported in the form of a new Research Grant Council project on unitary block designs which has special importance in the study of finite geometry.

706111.label: Project Objectives
706111.value: Studying the heteroepitaxial growth behavior of Bi2Se3 on chalcogenides and vice versa: To achieve successful growth of superlattices and other quantum structures, it is necessary to firstly understand the growth behavior of the heteroepitaxial systems. These include the epitaxial growth mode and strain relaxation, etc.. As the fabrication of superlattice and other quantum structures involves heteroepitaxy of Bi2Se3 on normal insulator as well as that of normal insulator on Bi2Se3, studies of the two complementary interfaces will be carried out. Growth of superlattice and quantum well, dot structures of Bi2Se3: Once the heteroepiatxial behaviors of the materials become understood, superlattice and other quantum structures consisting of the TI Bi2Se3 and insulating spacers will be fabricated by MBE. To access the size effect, structures with varying thicknesses of both Bi2Se3 and the spacing layers will be grown. Characterizations of the structures for their structural and physical properties: The structural quality of the superalttice and quantum wells/dots will be characterized by X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy. Their electronic and optical properties will also be investigated by Hall effect and magneto-resistance measurements, for example. New effects due to reduced sizes of the structure will be sought.

706111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
706111.value: Topological insulators (TIs) are of intensive research interests recently due to their unique properties and the potentials in future spintronic and quantum computing applications. Bi2Se3 compound has been identified as one of the most promising TI materials for its large bulk energy gap (~ 0.3 eV) and the simple single Dirac cone structure of surface electrons. A great deal of efforts has thus been devoted towards the growth and characterizations of such a compound in the past year. Bulk crystals, nanostructures as well as epitaxial thin films of Bi2Se3 have all been fabricated while properties related to surface electrons have been observed. Transport studies of TI crystals or films have, however, found contributions from the bulk. It remains challenging but important to suppress the bulk contributions in order to better explore the TI properties and applications. One way to proceed is to fabricate nanostructured materials with large surface-to-volume ratio. Alternatively, one may grow superlattices composed of thin layers of Bi2Se3 and normal insulator spacers readily achievable by molecular-beam epitaxy. Superlattice structures are not only suitable for device fabrication and transport measurements, they also provide a platform for studying quantum size effect. The individual layer thickness of the structure can be independently varied, thus coupling of states in different Bi2Se3 layers may be tuned conveniently. In this project, superlattice structures composed of Bi2Se3 and normal insulators as the spacing layers will be attempted by molecular-beam epitaxy. Chalcogenides, particularly selenide compound ZnSe, GaSe and InSe, will be experimented as the spacer material due to growth and structural compatibility with Bi2Se3. The heteroepitaxial growth behavior of Bi2Se3 on these compounds and vice versa will be followed. The specific growth mode, heterointerface formation and strain relaxation mechanisms will be studied. Other quantum structures, such as quantum wells or quantum dots, will also be considered. The properties of these heterostructures will be characterized, and potentials for applications will be explored.

706111.label: Realisation of objectives
706111.value: The three objectives of the project have been all met in this research. Firstly, extensive experiments have been carried out to follow the epitaxial growth mode and strain. Secondly, equipped with the knowledge of growth characteristics, superlattices composed of alternating layers of topological insulator Bi2Se3 and an ordinary insulator In2Se3 have been realized by molecular-beam epitaxy. Thirdly, the structural properties of the superlattice samples have been carefully studied by electron and X-ray diffraction techniques as well as by transmission electron microscopy. Superlattices of different constituent layer thicknesses have been investigated by transport measurements, such as Hall effect and magnetoresistance in collaboration with researchers in Hong Kong and in mainland China, and some interesting properties were discovered. In addition to the above, high-index Bi2Se3(221) films were achieved, for which the surface Dirac states and strain were probed.

706111.label: Major findings and research outcome
706111.value: 1. Bi2Se3 growth was found to follow the 'layer-by-layer' mode on most of the substrates investigated, including the (111) surfaces of InP, GaAs, Si, and graphene/SiC. Different substrates, however, resulted in different qualities of the epifilms. A stepped InP(111) surface was found to lead to single-domain Bi2Se3(111) epifilms with good structural and electrical properties [2,3]. 2. Due to the close deposition conditions between Bi2Se3 and In2Se3, we have successfully grown high-quality superlattice structures composed of alternating Bi2Se3 and In2Se3 of varying thicknesses [4,6]. The interface and strain of such superlattices were examined by electron and X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy [4]. 3. Transport studies of the superlattice samples have been carried out, unveiling an interesting 3D to 2D quantum transport crossover depending on the constituent layer thicknesses [6]. 4. High-index Bi2Se3(221) films were attempted and realized on both InP(001) and GaAs(001) [1,3]. Disorder-induced linear magnetoresistance in such a high-index Bi2Se3 film was discovered [5]. 5. We found a robust (1x2) surface reconstruction on Bi2Se3(111). Analysis of the data indicated Se-absorbate origin of such reconstruction. Some of the above results have been published in Appl. Phys. Lett., Nano Lett., and Adv. Mater., for example.

706111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
706111.value: Bi2Se3 films grown along [111] were found strain-free due to the characteristic van der Waals interaction between Bi2Se3 quintuple layers. On the other hand, high-index Bi2Se3(221) films grown on InP(001) and GaAs(001) were found to contain appreciable amount of strain for ultrathin layers, which would make it possible to access the strain effect on topological surface states. The latter will constitute a new direction of topological insulator (TI)research. Additionally, with the interesting properties discovered from the Bi2Se3/In2Se3 superlattice samples, an extension of the project will be for the "quantum dot" structures, such as that TI nanoclusters embedded in the matrix of an ordinary insulator (OI) or vice versa. For such samples, quantum size confinement and TI interaction effects may be probed.

706111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
706111.value: Topological insulator (TI) is a new type of quantum materials attracting extensive researches in late years. An interesting aspect of such materials is the robust 'metallic' states on the surfaces of bulk insulators, so the focus of previous studies have been on the surfaces of the samples (i.e., interface with vacuum). On the other hand, interfaces between the TIs and ordinary insulators (OIs) can also host the 'topological' states, realizing such samples that contain the TI/OI interfaces becomes technically important and physically interesting. In this project, the PI has adopted molecular-beam epitaxy (MBE), a modern and versatile thin film growth technique, to grow '...Bi2Se3/In2Se3/Bi2Se3/In2Se3...' superlattice structures and examined the structural and electronic properties. An interesting constituent-layer thickness dependent properties of the samples has been discovered. Additionally, a high-index Bi2Se3(221) film was realized for the first time. Different from the Bi2Se3(111) films commonly available and extensively studied, Bi2Se3(221) films can be made strained, so the effect of strain may be followed using such samples. The findings of this project will likely stir further researches on the TIs, particularly on the 'buried' interfaces between TIs and OIs. Such films may also be more practical for application purposes since, unlike the free surfaces, the "interfaces" are better protected and immune from the effect from the environment.

706411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
706411.value: Supramolecular chemistry has attracted an increasing attention, particularly with the growing knowledge of its relevance to biology and more recently, materials properties. Its dominating role in governing the secondary and tertiary structures of biological molecules has led to the fascinating diversity and function displayed by biological molecules. While there have been much efforts to reproduce the synthetic analogues of these basic biological molecules, the corresponding construction of non-naturally occurring synthetic analogues has been relatively less extensively explored. The study of non-naturally occurring synthetic analogues has been particularly attractive given the virtually infinite possible design and expansion of the building blocks to probe not only hydrogen bonding interactions, but also to focus on other non-covalent interactions. Systematic studies of such synthetic analogues not only would provide a fundamental understanding of these supramolecular interactions to enhance the understanding of the biological systems, but also would provide insights that would lead to the discovery of new functional materials with unique and previously unattainable properties. While there has been a growing interest in the construction and study of various supramolecular assemblies directed by metal-ligand coordination and the study of their host-guest interactions, corresponding studies on the design and construction of supramolecular assemblies based on metal-ligand chromophoric building blocks such as the platinum(II) polypyridine system are rare and unexplored despite emerging interests in metal-metal and π-π interactions in these classes of compounds. Thus an exploration of the spectroscopic and luminescence properties of platinum(II) polypyridyl complexes and their supramolecular assemblies and host-guest interaction would represent a challenging area of research. In this project, novel classes of platinum(II)-ligand chromophores will be designed and synthesized. Through the tuning of the ligand design and structures, metallosupramolecular assemblies with various dimensions and topologies can be obtained. Their spectroscopic, electronic absorption and luminescence properties will be explored. Attempts will also be made to correlate the spectroscopic, electronic absorption and luminescence properties of the metallosupramolecular assemblies with the structural and electronic aspects of the ligands, their supramolecular interactions, topologies, host-guest chemistry and the microenvironment. The proposed project should contribute not only to the design and synthesis of platinum(II)-ligand chromophoric supramolecular assemblies and the basic understanding of their spectroscopic properties, but also would serve to provide model studies for the understanding of the factors that govern the various interactions, which may provide insights into the utilization of these interactions for supramolecular assembly and construction of molecular receptors for host-guest interactions and functional materials. 隨着不斷增加的知識說明了超分子化學與生物學和材料特性的相連關係，超分子化學日益受到人們的關注。超分子化學在影響生物分子的二級和三級結構方面的主導作用令生物分子展現迷人的多樣性和功能。近年，很多化學家利用合成手段努力複製基本的生物分子。但是，非天然類似物的合成研究則相對較少。研究非天然合成類似物吸引人之處是可利用具無限創意的設計和構思來擴展構築塊以探測氫鍵相互作用，並對其他非共價鍵相互作用進行相關的研究。對這種非天然合成類似物系統性的研究不僅有助於從根本上理解超分子相互作用，從而增加對生物系統的認識，還有助於促進發展性能新穎且獨特和前所未有的新型功能材料。儘管很多化學家正積極利用金屬配合物來主導構建各種超分子組裝，並對其主−客體相互作用進行研究，然而，利用具有發光功能及金屬−金屬和π−π相互作用的金屬−配體載色體作為構築塊，如鉑(II)多吡啶體系，來設計和構建超分子組裝卻十分罕見。因此，探索一系列鉑(II)多吡啶配合物的光譜和發光特性，並對其超分子組裝及主−客體相互作用進行深入研究將是一個極具挑戰性的研究領域。在這個項目中，通過設計和合成多種新穎的發光鉑(II)−配體載色體分子材料，並藉調整配體的設計和結構來產生不同大小和拓撲結構的金屬超分子組裝。再通過一系列有關其光譜源由、電子吸收性能和發光性能的研究和分析，從而理解這類金屬超分子組裝的光譜源由、電子吸收性能和和發光性能跟配體的結構和電子特性、超分子相互作用、拓撲結構、主−客體化學和微環境的關係。此項目不僅有助於設計和合成發光鉑(II)−配體載色體超分子組裝及增加對其光譜源由的基礎認識，更可作為模型的研究來了解控制各種相互作用的原因。這些超分子發光鉑(II)配合物的基礎研究有望洞悉如何利用各種相互作用來控制超分子組裝和構建分子接受體，並應用於主−客體相互作用和功能材料等範疇。

706411.label: Realisation of objectives
706411.value: Various organic precursors, target ligands, functionalized alkynes, linkers, oligomers and platinum(II) precursor complexes of polypyridine, arylpyridine, pyridylbenzimidazole and other ligand derivatives have been successfully designed and synthesized. Incorporation of these ligands and linkers into the platinum(II) precursor complexes has afforded various platinum(II) linkers, clips/tweezers, double-clips/tweezers, foldamers, macrocycles, cages and supramolecular coordination assemblies. The spectroscopic, electronic absorption and luminescence properties and their supramolecular assembly properties have been studied. The effects of solvents, external stimuli, and guest molecules and their host-guest chemistry have been studied. Specifically, novel molecular clips/tweezers, double-clips/tweezers, foldamers, macrocyclic and cage complexes based on a phosphorescent cationic alkynylplatinum(II) terpyridine building blocks have been synthesized and characterized. Host–guest chemistry of the host complexes and various guest metal complexes with different ligands, charges and/or metal centres has been investigated. Spectroscopic changes with new absorptions and emissions in the lower-energy region were observed as a result of significant metal–metal, π–π, and electrostatic interactions. The sandwiched association mode of the host–guest interaction of the molecular tweezers, double-tweezers and macrocycles/cages has been established. Platinum(II)-containing complexes with chiral binaphthol-containing alkynyl linkers capable of folding have been synthesized, characterized, and shown to undergo supramolecular assembly. Extension of the work has also been made to explore the use of amphiphilic alkynylplatinum(II) terpyridine complexes and alkynylplatinum(II) terpyridine-polyelectrolyte ensembles for host-guest recognition. Induced self-assembly and disassembly of water-soluble alkynylplatinum(II) terpyridine complexes with switchable near-infrared emission modulated by metal–metal interactions have been demonstrated over physiological pH and shown to function as pH-responsive NIR luminescent probes in cell-imaging studies as well as for phosphate and enzyme sensing including ATPase, kinase and phosphatase. Extension of the work to other supramolecular assemblies of mixed-metal platinum(II)-silver(I) system as well as host-guest systems of ruthenium(II) for FRET energy transfer-based sensing of esterase, cytotoxicity and luminescence imaging has also been made. The present system has allowed the study and correlation of spectroscopic, electronic absorption, luminescence, self-assembly and host-guest binding properties with the nature of the non-covalent and donor-acceptor interactions, charges, structural and electronic aspects of the ligands, solvents and microenvironments, as well as their supramolecular assemblies. The outcome of the project has led to a number of publications in international SCI journals, invitations to contribute review articles, book chapters, plenary and invited lectures at international conferences, and training of two Ph.D. students. Realization of these important findings should give rise to important information and insights to the understanding of the self-assembly and host-guest binding properties.

706411.label: Major findings and research outcome
706411.value: Various target platinum(II) linkers, clips/tweezers, double-clips/tweezers, foldamers, macrocycles, cages and supramolecular coordination assemblies have been successfully synthesized. The spectroscopic, electronic absorption and luminescence properties and their supramolecular assembly properties as well as host-guest chemistry have been studied. Specifically, novel molecular clips/tweezers, double-clips/tweezers, foldamers, macrocyclic and cage complexes based on a phosphorescent cationic alkynylplatinum(II) terpyridine building blocks have been synthesized and characterized. Host–guest chemistry of the host complexes and various guest metal complexes with different ligands, charges and/or metal centres has been investigated. Various metal complexes including the negatively charged platinum complexes can interact with the cationic molecular clips/tweezers (Chem. Sci. 2012, 3, 1185-1191), double-clips/tweezers (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2013, 52, 14117-14120), multi-addressable molecular macrocyclic and cage complexes capable of pH-controlled guest release and capture (PNAS 2014, 111, 15900-15905) to form discrete, soluble molecular double salts. Upon addition of guests to the hosts, new absorptions and emissions in the lower-energy region were observed as a result of significant metal–metal, π–π, and electrostatic interactions. NMR titration and 2D NMR studies confirmed the host–guest interaction in the sandwiched association mode. The present system has also allowed the study of intermolecular metal–metal interactions between dissimilar metal–ligand moieties of different electronic and steric properties as well as different charges, providing a systematic understanding of the various factors that govern the host-guest interaction and the nature of the metal–metal interactions. Host–guest interactions of the alkynylplatinum(II) molecular clips/tweezers with planar aromatics have also been investigated, indicating the importance of π-surface in the host–guest interactions (Chem. Eur. J. 2013, 19, 390-399). Chiral platinum(II)-containing metallofoldamers with binaphthol-containing alkynyl linkers have been synthesized and characterized, and shown to undergo supramolecular assembly involving reversible conformational transitions between random coils and single-turn helical strands, controlled and assisted by Pt···Pt and π−π interactions of the alkynylplatinum(II) terpyridine moiety upon solvent and temperature modulation, which has been supported by DFT calculations (PNAS 2013, 110, 7986-7991). Employment of amphiphilic alkynylplatinum(II) terpyridine-polyelectrolyte ensembles for selective label-free detection of G-quadruplex structure of human telomere has been achieved under physiological condition through the FRET with Pt∙∙∙Pt, electrostatic and - interactions (Chem. Sci. 2013, 4, 377-387). Moreover, induced self-assembly and disassembly of water-soluble alkynylplatinum(II) terpyridine complexes with switchable near-infrared (NIR) emission modulated by metal–metal interactions have been demonstrated over physiological pH and shown to function as pH-responsive NIR luminescent probes in cell-imaging (Chem. Sci. 2013, 4, 2453-2462) as well as for phosphate, anion and real-time enzyme sensing including ATPase, kinase and phosphatase (Chem. Sci. 2013, 4, 2928-2935; ChemOpen, 2014, 3, 172-176 (invited article; highlighted as front cover and as a cover profile)). Extension of the work to other supramolecular assemblies of mixed-metal platinum(II)-silver(I) system (Dalton Trans. 2012, 41, 8773-8776) as well as host-guest systems of ruthenium(II) for FRET energy transfer-based sensing of esterase, cytotoxicity and luminescence imaging has also been made (Chem. Eur. J. 2012, 18, 8724-8730). The present system has allowed the study and correlation of spectroscopic, electronic absorption, luminescence, self-assembly and host-guest binding properties with the nature of the non-covalent and donor-acceptor interactions, charges, structural and electronic aspects of the ligands, solvents and microenvironments, as well as their supramolecular assemblies (Adv. Mater. 2014, 26, 5558-5568 (invited research news); Compr. Inorg. Chem. II 2013, 8, 59-130 (invited article); Pure Appl. Chem. 2013, 85, 1321-1329 (invited article); Struct. Bonding 2014, 165, 109-130 (invited article)).

706411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
706411.value: At least several areas may be identified. First, the work forms the basis for the study of new classes of metal-containing oligomers and supramolecular coordination assemblies that will give rise to desirable supramolecular assemblies and host-guest chemistry. The utilization of luminescent metal oligomers and supramolecular coordination assemblies as hosts that can undergo induced assembly via various non-covalent interactions is particularly interesting and novel in that it may serve as the basis for the design of novel classes of supramolecular assemblies and hosts for the binding, sensing and detection of substrates of interest. Second, the controlled assembly brought about by solvents, external stimuli and guests is particularly attractive. These may generate changes in the spectroscopic and luminescence properties and gives rise to multi-addressable hosts for responsive controlled guest capture and release. Thus one can envisioned the future development of these classes of compounds for applications in responsive sensors and probes with tunable host-guest chemistry as well as for the controlled release and capture of biological substrates and drugs for diagnostics and therapeutical applications.

706411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
706411.value: Novel classes of metal-containing oligomers and supramolecular coordination assemblies based on platinum(II)-ligand chromophoric building blocks have been synthesized. Unique spectroscopic and luminescence changes induced by solvents, pH, ions, human telomere DNA, enzymes and various guests have been observed. Correlations of the spectroscopic, electronic absorption, luminescence, self-assembly and host-guest binding properties with the nature of the non-covalent and donor-acceptor interactions, structural and electronic aspects of ligands, solvents and microenvironments have been made, which should provide a systematic understanding of the various factors that govern the host-guest interactions and the nature of various interactions for the future design of novel classes of hosts, oligomers, and supramolecular assemblies. The outcome of the project has led to a number of publications in high-impact international refereed SCI journals and plenary lectures at international conferences. The works of two Ph.D. students were associated with the project. The students have successfully graduated from their Ph.D. Realization of these important findings should give rise to important information and insights to the future design of novel types of metal-containing hosts and supramolecular assemblies for applications as responsive sensors and probes with tunable host-guest chemistry as well as for the controlled release and capture of biological substrates and drug delivery.

706511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
706511.value: Intense interest in the development of novel scaffolds with unnatural building blocks to construct well-defined secondary structures in aqueous media is currently being shared by chemists and biologists, as “foldamers” (or polymers that have a strong tendency to adopt specific and compact conformations) provide a basis for rational molecular design and afford both intensive and extensive applications in biology and medicine. Recently, peptidomimetic foldamers as one of the most important types of foldamers have attracted increasing attention for their excellent compatibility in biological systems and high potential in drug development. Compared with naturally-occurring short peptides which are normally in the random-coil state and readily degradable by proteases, oligomers of several types of unnatural amino acids can fold into well-defined secondary structures with limited number of residues in aqueous media and exhibit strong resistance to biodegradation. In our previous research funded by the Research Grants Council, we discovered an exciting new series of peptidomimetic foldamers based on aminoxy acids, a new class of unnatural amino acids displaying unique structural properties. With solid evidence gained from theoretical calculations and experimental studies, we have shown that aminoxy acids, when incorporated into peptides, induce novel secondary structures, including several types of turns and helices. In addition, these turns and helices are generally independent of the side chains and the length of peptides, thus providing flexible platforms for rational molecular design. In this proposed research, we plan to further explore aminoxy acids-based building blocks to construct novel secondary structures in aqueous media. Specifically, we will develop novel β-hairpin mimics, further explore the new secondary structures induced by β-aminoxy peptides, and investigate the potential of hybrid peptides containing aminoxy acids and other types of unnatural amino acids, such as β-amino acids, as peptidomimetic foldamers. Since peptides containing aminoxy acids intrinsically exhibit excellent biostability and compatibility in biological systems, aminoxy acids are of tremendous potential in the rational design of drug-like molecules and the combinatorial library construction of analogs of bioactive peptides for drug screening. It is expected that this project will lead to the discovery of a series of novel scaffolds with stable secondary structures in aqueous solution, consequently creating flexible and concrete platforms for further applications in biology and medicine. 有序折叠分子(或强烈偏好于特定紧凑构象的聚合物)为合理的分子设计提供了基础并在生物和医学领域得到了广泛和深入的应用，因此开发具有非天然结构单元并能在水介质中建立明确的二级结构的全新分子骨架引起了化学家和生物学家的强烈兴趣 。近来，作为有序折叠分子中最重要的类型之一，拟肽类有序折叠分子因其优异的生物系统相容性以及在药物开发中的广阔前景而获得越来越多的关注。自然存在的短肽通常以无规卷曲结构存在而且能被蛋白酶快速降解，而与之相比，由若干种非天然氨基酸组成的低聚物在水介质中以一定数量的残基就能折叠形成明确的二级结构并且表现出很强的抗生物降解能力。 在早前由RGC资助的研究中，我们发现了一个新拟肽类有序折叠分子系列，该系列的基础是一类新的拥有独特结够性能的非天然氨基酸——氨氧基酸。我们利用从理论计算和实验研究得到的可靠证据表明，氨氧基酸引入多肽后能够引导形成全新的二级结构，包括数种转角和螺旋结构。而且这些转角和螺旋结构通常不会受侧链和肽链长度影响，因而为合理的分子设计提供了一个弹性平台。 在这个研究提案中，我们计划进一步拓展以氨氧基酸为基础结构单元用于构建水介质中新颖二级结构。具体而言，我们将开发全新的拟β-发夹结构，深入探究由β-氨氧基酸引导的新二级结构，发掘含有氨氧基酸和其他类型的非天然氨基酸（例如β-氨氧基酸）的杂交肽作为拟肽类有序折叠分子的潜力。 含有氨氧基酸的多肽表现出了自身出色的生物稳定性和生物系统相容性，因此，氨氧基酸在药类分子设计和用于药物筛选的生物活性肽类似物组合库构建方面有巨大的应用前景。我们期望在这个项目中发现一系列在水介质中具有稳定二级结构的新型分子骨架，继而为在生物和药学领域应用创造一个具有弹性的坚实平台。

706511.label: Realisation of objectives
706511.value: Objective 1: To develop stabilized β-hairpin motif using aminoxy acids, we have applied two different scaffolds, γ-aminoxy acid and D-α-aminoxy-β2,3-amino acid dipeptide, as reverse turn mimic to induce β-hairpin formation. Among several γ-aminoxy acid turn candidates prepared and examined, R-γ4-phenyl aminoxy acid had been found to induce a minimal β-hairpin formation; however, in presence of polar side-chains or longer peptide, β-hairpin was poorly folded or even not formed. We thus turned our focus to the other candidate, dipeptide of D-α-aminoxy-β2,3-amino acid. A number of linear and cyclic oligopeptides with dipeptide of D-α-aminoxy-β2,3-amino acid had been prepared. Their conformations in aqueous and organic solvents were investigated and their inhibitory activity against p53-hDM2 interaction was evaluate using ELISA method. Objective 2: Water soluble cyclic β2,3-aminoxy peptides of different lengths with alternating (2R, 3R)-β2,3-aminoxy carboxyl cyclohexane and piperidinium residues have been prepared. The conformational studies revealed that those β N–O turns as well as a novel helical structure were formed in organic solvents and aqueous media. Excellent conformational stability of this series of compounds over a wide range of pH and temperature has been demonstrated. Objective 3: Using hybrid peptides containing alternating D-α-aminoxy acids and β-amino acids, we have successfully developed different secondary structures by changing substitution patterns on the β-amino acid residues. A novel 8/8 helix can be formed for an oligopeptide composing alternating D-α-aminoxy acid and β2,2-dialkyl amino acid whereas a novel reverse turn structure can be formed for an oligopeptide composing D-α-aminoxy acid and 3R-β3-alkyl amino acid/ 2S,3R-β2,3-dialkyl amino acid. The reverse turn can stabilize and nucleate β-hairpin formation when incorporated into L-α-peptides. In addition, the potential applications of hybrid peptides as synthetic ion channels have been explored. Objective 4: Since α- and β-aminoxy acid residues induced α and β N–O turns respectively, our research interest focused on their folding propensity in a hybrid manner, in order to deeply understand the conformational properties of aminoxy building blocks. Eight hybrid dipeptides and four tetrapeptides have been prepared and their secondary structures in solid state and organic solvents have been studied.

706511.label: Major findings and research outcome
706511.value: (1) Linear oligopeptide with dipeptide of D-α-aminoxy acid 2S,3R-β2,3-dialkyl amino acid folds well into a β-hairpin in methanol and acetate buffer. A cyclic oligopeptide with combined ornithine and dipeptide of D-α-aminoxy acid 2S,3R-β2,3-dialkyl amino acid as reverse turn units was identified as the best folded oligopeptide. One peptide exhibited good inhibitory activity to hDM2 with IC50 = 19 μM, which is similar to native p53 peptide. Thus we have successfully developed a novel reverse turn structure that is able to nucleate β-hairpin formation in water (Manuscript in preparation). (2) By using NMR spectroscopy, we found that water soluble cyclic β2,3-aminoxy peptides with alternating (2R, 3R)-β2,3-aminoxy carboxyl cyclohexane and piperidinium residues could fold into helical structure, consisted of consecutive β N–O turns. Those secondary structures were maintained in acidic and weakly basic aqueous buffer as confirmed by CD analysis. Furthermore, denaturation of these peptides was not observed at high temperature. Therefore, we have successfully constructed novel β-aminoxy helical secondary structure that is stable in water (Chem. Asian J. 2015). (3) By using various spectroscopic techniques, hybrid peptides composed of alternating D-α-aminoxy acid and β2,2-dialkyl amino acid have been found to form novel 8/8 helix, in which an α N-O turn induces another intramolecular 8-membered-ring hydrogen bond (Manuscript in preparation). Peptides composed of D-α-aminoxy acid and R-β3-dialkyl amino acid form novel reverse turn structure as reveled by previously mentioned methods. A minimal β-hairpin with a key 10-membered-ring intramolecular hydrogen bond between aminoxy amide proton and carbonyl of β-amino acid was observed. This conformation reversed the direction of peptide and nucleated β-hairpin formation (Manuscript in preparation). We have discovered that homochiral or heterochiral α-aminoxy acid oligomers can self-assemble into synthetic ion channels (Manuscript in preparation). (4) For those hybrid peptides containing alternating α-aminoxy acids and cyclic β2,3-aminoxy acids, NMR spectroscopy and X-ray crystallography studies revealed that both α- and β-aminoxy acid residues could induce typical α and β N–O turn formation in non-polar organic solvents and in solid state. Either helical or reverse turn structure could be constructed, depending on the chirality of α-aminoxy residues. CD study indicated that helical and turn structures were conserved for all peptides, regardless of side chain and configuration of compounds, peptide chain length and solvent polarity. Therefore, the conformational rigidity of aminoxy residues, as modular units in predictable manner to tune secondary structures, could become an advantage in peptidomimetics design in future (Manuscript in preparation).

706511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
706511.value: Aminoxy peptides are able to induce α and β N-O turn and even β-hairpin structure, depending on the substitution pattern. β2,3-Aminoxy peptides with polar side chain exhibit high tendency to adopt stable turn and helical structure in aqueous media. We plan to further develop hybrid peptides of diverse backbones and side chain types with stable and predictable conformations in aqueous media, by incorporating conformationally rigid aminoxy acid units. In addition, we plan to perform further peptidomimetic studies by employing those hybrid peptides for synthetic ion channel applications.

706511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
706511.value: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) mediate a wide range of biological processes and can be molecular targets for many different diseases such as Alzheimer’s diseases and cancer development. Special features of PPIs such as large binding surface area and protein residues at the binding surface are not contiguous in the protein backbone. This makes traditional approaches for drug discovery to PPIs inefficient as these approaches are specific to small molecules. The search of rigid and metabolically stable molecular scaffolds that could reproduce the binding epitope of the PPIs becomes an alternative approach to drug discovery. We have successfully developed a series of foldamers using α-aminoxy acids, β-aminoxy acids, and β-amino acids. Novel turns structures, helices, reverse turns and β-hairpin motif can be formed using these unnatural building blocks in organic solvents and aqueous buffer. We have also demonstrated the potential application of our foldamers in interfering PPIs by developing an inhibitor of a p53-hDM2 interaction.

706611.value: 界限期權及其相關的股票指數年金的定價，保險及金融投資組合的最優策略

706611.label: Project Objectives
706611.value: Pricing of double barrier options and geometric step options and related EIAs. Optimal investment strategy for a delta neutral portfolio containing derivatives, underlying risky asset and risk free asset. Optimal dividends and utility maximization problems in an insurance risk model with dividends payment and capital injection or reinsurance.

Optimal investment strategy for a delta neutral portfolio containing derivatives, underlying risky asset and risk free asset.

706611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
706611.value: Option pricing is one of the most important research areas in mathematical finance. Many exotic derivatives are traded in the market, among them barrier option is a popular one. In this project, we study the pricing of double barrier options and geometric step options under various models, as a byproduct, we shall provide the valuation results for the equity linked insurance products with embedded barrier options. The equity linked insurance products with embedded exotic derivatives have become very popular in major insurance and financial markets around the world, and pricing and risk managing of these products are not easy due to the exotic feature and the mortality effect of the products. Optimal investment-consumption problem is theoretically interesting and practically important. When the portfolio contains derivatives, the problem becomes more interesting. By using the delta hedging idea, we can keep the portfolio a delta hedged portfolio, then find an optimal strategy which maximizes the expected discounted utility function. In this project, various models, such as regime switching model, Levy process models will be considered, and applying the techniques of stochastic control, the optimal investment-consumption strategy can be obtained. For the insurance portfolio, we consider various models, including the diffusion process, the perturbed compound Poisson risk model, and the insurance risk models with two-sided jumps. We introduce the dividend payments into the insurance risk model, and further complex the problem by allow the company to inject capital if necessary in order the company to continue its business. This will allow us to consider the problem of optimal dividends and capital injection and formulate the problem in many different ways. We will introduce the proportional and fixed transaction in the model. In this case, the control problem becomes an impulse control problem. Another formulation is that we assume that the company pays dividends and can buy reinsurance, to solve this problem we again need to solve an impulse control problem. We propose to use the technique of quasi-variational inequalities to solve this kind of optimal control problems. In lieu of seeking closed-form solutions, we will study some simple models first and then extend the results to more general problems. Effort will be given to obtain some numerical results. 期權定價是金融數學中最重要的研究課題之一。市場有很多種特種期權，其中最常見的之一就是界限期權。在這個項目中，我們研究雙邊界限期權和幾何階梯期權的定 價，而且也研究與這些期權相關的股票指數年金的定價。在金融和精算學中另一個重要的課題是最優投資和消費策略。在這個項目中，我們將研究含有衍生產品的投資組合的最優投資策略。我們也會研究在各種模型下，保險公司資產的最優投資及最優分紅等問題。

Among the 16 papers, 5 papers are on the pricing of double barrier options and geometric step options and related EIAs. 3 papers are on optimal investment strategy for delta neutral portfolios containing derivatives, underlying risky asset and risk free asset, and 5 papers are on optimal dividends and utility maximization problems in an insurance risk model with dividends payment and capital injection or reinsurance. Other 3 papers are on related topics but not exactly on the problems of the topics listed in the objectives. We have obtained expected and some unexpected results during the investigation of this project.

706611.label: Major findings and research outcome
706611.value: We have worked out a lot very interesting results on the theme of this project. 16 papers have been published on the theme of this project. Most of the 16 papers are published in top actuarial science journals or related journals. In Gerber, Shiu and Yang (2012, 2013), a new method for valuing equity-linked insurance products is proposed and A substantial series of closed-form formulas is obtained, for the various contingent options under geometric Brownian motion model and jump diffusion model, respectively. In Xing and Yang (2013), we consider the American geometric step options with perpetual expiration and finite expiration. In the perpetual case, using the Feynman-Kac formula, the joint Laplace transform, a closed pricing formula is derived. In the finite expiration case, we show that the price of the American geometric step option satisfies vibrational inequalities. A modified explicit finite difference approach is developed to calculate the price of the option. In Fu and Yang (2012), by using equilibrium approach, we provide a framework of option pricing under Levy process. In Fu, Wei and Yang (2014), we consider the optimal asset allocation problem for delta neutral portfolios containing derivatives, underlying risky asset and risk free asset in a continuous-time regime-switching market. The problem is to maximize the expected utility of the terminal wealth. We introduce a functional operator to generate a sequence of value functions, and then show that the optimal value function is the limit of this sequence. The explicit form of each function in the sequence can be obtained by solving an auxiliary portfolio optimization problem in a single-regime market. Then the original optimal value function can be approximated by taking the limit. In another paper, we have discussed the similar problem using a discrete model. In Meng, Yuen, Siu and Yang (2013, the optimal portfolio problem is investigated using a continuous-time self-exciting threshold model. In Wei, Wang and Yang (2012), the optimal strategy for an insurance portfolio is considered and a representation of the value function and an integral equation satisfied by the boundary are obtained. In Jin, Yang and Yin (2013), numerical methods for finding optimal investment, dividend payment, and capital injection policies to maximize the present value of the difference between the cumulative dividend payment and the possible capital injections are investigated. We use Markov chain approximation techniques to construct a discrete-time controlled Markov chain to approximate the value function and optimal controls. Convergence of the approximation algorithms is proved. In Meng, Siu and Yang (2013), we consider an optimal dividend problem with nonlinear insurance risk processes attributed to internal competition factors. By solving the corresponding HJB equation, closed-form solutions to the problem are obtained in various cases. In Yao, Yang and Wang (2014), optimal dividend and financing strategy is obtained in a model using the variance premium principle.

706611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
706611.value: This project involves three important research topics, namely option pricing and valuing equity-linked products, optimal portfolio selection and optimal insurance policies. For the problem of valuing equity-linked products, we have investigated this much further, and a new RGC project is obtained on this direction and many considerable interesting results are obtained. For optimal reinsurance strategies, we have done a lot study and many new problems on this direction are formulated and many new results are obtained. We shall further investigate this and apply a RGC grant later.

706611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
706611.value: Many exotic derivatives are traded in the market, among them barrier option is a popular one. In this project, we obtain interesting results on the pricing of double barrier options and geometric step options under various models. A related problem in actuarial science is valuing equity-linked insurance products. We have developed a new method to value this kind product. A series of closed-form formulas are obtained for valuing various embedded options. The equity linked insurance products with embedded exotic derivatives have become very popular in major insurance and financial markets around the world. Optimal investment consumption problem is theoretically interesting and practically important. When the portfolio contains derivatives, the problem becomes more interesting. By using the delta hedging idea and some approximation techniques, the solution of this problem is obtained. For the insurance portfolio, we consider the problem of optimal dividends and capital injection. We use optimal stochastic control to solve this kind of optimization problems. Our results provide some insight to problems in actuarial science, finance and related areas. The results and methodologies in this project add significant contributions to the actuarial science and mathematical finance literature.

706711.label: Project Title(Chinese)
706711.value: 在自旋系綜中產生大尺度量子糾纏的新辦法

706711.label: Project Objectives
706711.value: Develop and explore a novel approach for generating large scale quantum entanglement in a general spin ensemble based on collective raising and lowering operations; investigate the emergence of entanglement between various parts of the ensemble, and the squeezing of collective spin and its uncertainties that accompanies the entanglement generation. Find efficient and technically feasible schemes for the implementation of this approach in nuclear spin systems and other physical systems; explore potential applications and develop schemes for utilizing the generated entanglement in these systems. Investigate the effects of loss mechanisms on the efficiencies of entanglement generation and spin squeezing, and methods to remedy such deleterious effects.
