710711.label: Major findings and research outcome
710711.value: The research outcome is very fruitful, namely 8 international journal papers [J1]-[J8] and 4 international conference papers [C1]-[C4]. Concerning the machine design, we have developed new machine topologies and their designs. By incorporating magnetic gears into double-stator permanent-magnet (PM) machines, two new double-stator magnetic-geared machines are proposed [J2], which can offer high torque density and low-speed operation. Also, based on the magnetic gearing effect, two PM vernier machines are proposed [J1]*, which can further improve the torque density and reduce the structure complexity. These topologies are particularly attractive for wave power generation [C1]. By incorporating an auxiliary DC field winding, a new linear hybrid PM vernier machine is proposed [J8],[C2], which can offer flexible air-gap flux control. Moreover, by borrowing the transverse-flux concept, a new linear transverse-flux-reversal PM machine is proposed [C3] so that the electric and magnetic loadings can be decoupled to further improve the force density. Furthermore, a new linear flux-controllable variable reluctance machine is proposed [J7], which can offer wide constant-power range for wave power generation. * As queried in the mid-term assessment, we would like to clarify that the IEEE Transactions on Applied Superconductivity not only covers applications of superconductivity but also magnet technology for power applications such as motors and generators. Concerning the machine modeling, we have developed two new analytical approaches. First, the concept of equivalent anisotropic magnetic permeability is newly proposed [J3], which is particularly suitable for the proposed linear magnetic-geared machines. Second, the magnetic equivalent network is newly proposed [J5], which is particularly suitable for the proposed linear PM vernier machines. Concerning the machine control, we have developed two new control strategies. First, the complex conjugate control is newly proposed [C4], which can enable the linear magnetic-geared machine to achieve the maximum power point tracking for wave power generation. Second, by tuning the DC field current of the linear hybrid PM vernier machine, the power factor control is newly proposed for wave power generation [J8]. Concerning the machine evaluation, a critical evaluation on using linear direct-drive machine topologies for wave power generation is provided [J4], which reveals that the linear PM vernier machines are preferred in long term. Moreover, a quantitative comparison between the non-rare-earth and rare-earth PM based linear magnetic gears is provided [J6], which reveals that the non-rare-earth PM is preferred for application to linear magnetic-geared machines when cost-effectiveness is emphasized.

710711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
710711.value: Fault tolerance is highly desired by modern electric machines for some specific applications. The wave power generators are either floated on the sea or submerged on the seabed, which are difficult to be accessed or maintained. Therefore, in order to avoid sudden blackout, more fault-tolerant control schemes of the proposed linear machines need to be explored. For example, during some open-circuit faults such as the phase-winding open-circuit fault and power device open-circuit fault, the machine should be able to operate at the remedial mode so that it can maintain the same power level with acceptable system efficiency. Meanwhile, during some short-circuit faults such as the turn-to-turn fault, phase-to-phase fault and phase-to-ground fault, the machine should be able to isolate the faulty parts and operate at the remedial mode to maintain the performance for a reasonable period.

710711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
710711.value: Two global issues, namely environmental deterioration and fossil fuel crisis, have forced researchers to develop renewable and sustainable energy sources. Therefore, the development of wave power generation is highly desirable, both globally and locally. Wave energy is in the form of low-speed reciprocating motion with very high forces. In order to capture this wave energy, a linear-to-rotary mechanism is usually employed to drive a conventional rotary machine for electricity generation. However, this mechanism not only suffers from bulky size and inefficient transmission, but also desires regular maintenance. Thus, the development of linear machines for direct-drive wave power generation is becoming attractive. Among various linear machines, they cannot simultaneously achieve the desired high force density, high efficiency and high power factor. This project has successfully developed novel low-speed high-force linear permanent-magnet (PM) machines for direct-drive wave power generation. The key is to incorporate the concept of magnetic gearing into the PM brushless machines. Hence, with the use of maximum power point tracking, the proposed linear magnetic-geared machines and linear PM vernier machines can simultaneously offer high force density, high efficiency and high power factor. They exhibit excellent technical performances and high commercial values for direct-drive wave power generation.

710711.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
710711.value: This project has successfully trained two PhD students (Miss Jiangui Li and Mr. Wenlong Li). Miss Jiangui Li focused on developing various permanent-magnet (PM) vernier machine topologies while Mr. Wenlong Li focused on developing various linear PM machine topologies, both are directly related to the development of low-speed high-force linear PM machines for direct-drive wave power generation. Because of her outstanding research work, Miss Jiangui Li was awarded the RGC/Fulbright Hong Kong Junior Scholar 2011/12 to conduct 10-month research in University of Michigan – Dearborn. On the other hand, after his PhD graduation, Mr. Wenlong Li continued to work as Research Assistant for this project.

711511.label: Project Objectives
711511.value: We will develop the technology needed to understand the role of Casimir force in stiction (static friction) force, and model actuators and switches in NEMS. Multi-physics calculations, done in nanometer lengthscales using the stress tensor/quantum electrodynamics/statistical physics/computational electromagnetic/computational mechanics approaches, will instill interdisciplinary knowledge in the participating PhD students. Advanced CEM techniques like the augmented electric field integral equation (A-EFIE), domain decomposition method (DDM) such as the equivalence principle algorithm (EPA), or contact region modeling (CRM) approaches will be used to perform broadband calculation of the dyadic Green’s function of complex, multi-scale structures. Fast solvers such as the fast multipole algorithm (FMA) will help accelerate the solutions to highly complex problems with large numbers of unknowns. We will couple the Casimir force to the equations of elastodyamics using the computational mechanics paradigm. This is used to ascertain the deformation of NEMS devices due to such a force. Iteration between Casimir force computation and elastodynamic computation is needed to reach a consistent convergent solution. We will apply the newly developed algorithms to real-world problems, such as actuators and switches in NEMS, and compare with experimental data obtained by leading laboratories around the world. This project will train human resource who understand the fundamental knowledge needed to advance sophisticated technologies. The research output and human resource training will spur the growth of high-end R&D in Hong Kong and the Pearl River Delta region. This project will align our research goal with those of the leading universities. We will disseminate the work with conference presentations, journal publications, and seminars, whenever opportunity arises.

711511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
711511.value: The study of Casimir force, a fascinating force, requires inter-disciplinary collaboration using knowledge from statistical physics, quantum electrodynamics, computational electromagnetics, and computational mechanics. It is a hot topic of research pursued by researchers at leading institutions such as Harvard [5], MIT [10], and Yale [72]. The force is important at nanometer lengthscales; hence, it is important in nanotechnology. It is increasingly important in understanding the stiction (static friction) force in NEMS (nano electromechanical systems) switches and actuators. It provides also an excellent training ground for the broadbased education of PhD students. The Casimir force originates from the fluctuation of the electromagnetic field which exists even at zero absolute temperature. This follows from the fluctuation dissipation theorem of statistical physics and quantum mechanics. The fluctuating field polarizes dipoles and hence gives rise to an attractive force like the van der Waals force. However, when retardation is taken into account, this is known as the Casimir force. The force exerted by the fluctuating field is calculated from the Maxwell’s stress tensor. The magnitude of the fluctuating field for different frequencies is ascertained from the dyadic Green’s function of the complex geometry. Recent advances in computational electromagnetics (CEM) permit the broadband computation of the dyadic Green’s function for increasingly complex geometry. The state-of-art methods will be used for such computations. The predominant contribution to the force is from the low-frequency spectrum; hence, low-frequency stable CEM techniques will be employed. Therefore, we adopt the recently developed augmented electric field integral equation (A-EFIE) [18]. For multi-scale structures where circuit physics mixes with wave physics, we will use the domain decomposition method (DDM) with the equivalence principle algorithm (EPA) [58] or the contact region modeling (CRM) [62] for accelerating the convergence of the solution. Furthermore, to accelerate the integral equation solutions, we use the broadband fast multipole algorithm [24]. Once the force has been calculated, we will input the force into the equations of elastodynamics. Computational mechanics methods, such as finite element, will be used to solve the elastodynamic equations for large deformations. NEMS switches will be deformed by such forces requiring that the Casimir force be recalculated. The equations of elastodynamics need to be consistently coupled to the Casimir force calculation such that iteration between two sets of calculations is performed until convergence is reached. Such calculations can be used to study the stiction force in NEMS. 卡西米爾力 (Casimir) 力是一種有趣和神奇的力学現象。對於卡西米爾力的研究，交叉學科之間的廣泛協作至关重要。卡西米爾力 (Casimir) 力的研究涉及诸多学科领域，包括統計物理，量子電動力學，計算電磁學以及計算力學在內的多個領域。目前，來自哈佛 [5]，麻省理工 [10]，耶魯 [72] 等世界頂級學府的科研人員正在致力于與該課題相關的研究工作。一方面，在納米尺度下卡西米爾效應通常會變得十分明顯，其對於納米製造工藝举足轻重。另一方面，該效應對如何科學地解釋NEMS（納米電機系統）開關和驅動器存在（之间）的靜摩擦力也愈加重要。另外，基於卡西米爾力的研究課題可以成为博士生培養過程中多維教育的参考平台和优秀典范。 卡西米爾力起源於電磁場的真空涨落，這種涨落甚至存在於絕對零度极限環境下。因而该現象服從統計物理和量子力學中的涨落耗散定理。涨落的電磁場會令物体内的偶機子極化，從而產生類似范德華 (van der Waals) 作用的吸引力。當計入滞后效應之後，這種吸引力就是所謂的卡西米爾力，其可以通過麥克斯韋應力張量計算得出。值得一提的是，不同頻率下涨落場的强度則是由複雜幾何目標（非均匀电磁环境中）的並矢格林函數所決定。 計算電磁學 (CEM) 的最新進展使得複雜幾何體並矢格林函數的寬帶求解成為可能。其中最先進的技術必将推动卡西米爾力的高效計算。采用复路径变换后，关于虚时间格林函数积分中的低頻部分對卡西米爾力的貢獻最大，因此能處理低頻問題的穩定精确的数值技術將大受歡迎。因此，我們拟採用本研究小组最近發展的增廣電場積分方程 (A-EFIE) 算法来解决低频崩溃问题 [18]。對於電路物理和波動物理共存的混合多尺度結構，我們則採用區域分解方法 (DDM) 和等效原理算法 (EPA) [58] 或者接觸區域建模法 (CRM) [62] 來加快解的收斂。此外，我們將使用寬帶的快速多機子算法來進一步加速積分方程的求解 [24]。 卡西米爾力一經解出，我們就將其代入彈性動力學方程，並應用計算力學的有限元方法求解目標的極大形變 。NEMS的開關受力會發生形變，從而引起卡西米爾力的變化，因此力需要被重新計算。换句话说，我們將彈性動力學方程和卡西米爾力的計算方程耦合起來進行自洽迭代求解直到收斂為止。該計算過程亦有助於NEMS中靜摩擦力的研究。

711511.label: Realisation of objectives
711511.value: For 1, 3, and 4, a new numerical method for calculating the Casimir force between large, complex 3D objects was developed. We use an integral equation, domain decomposition method (DDM) and argument principle to derive the Casimir force formula. The broadband integral equation DDM, which is the augmented equivalence principle algorithm (A-EPA), allows for an efficient broadband solution of large, complex objects. This yields a reduced number of unknowns for complex structures making them feasible with modest computer resources. We demonstrated the advantages of the A-EPA by simulating large, finite, 3D, unaligned corrugated plates for NEMS, which have previously only been modeled approximately as infinite plates using 2D techniques. For 2 and 4, a condensed Hamiltonian matrix constructed with reduced dimension is proposed to perform simulation of quantum carrier transport in nano devices with the non-equilibrium Green’s function approach. This greatly speeds up the calculation. The condensed Hamiltonian approach successfully takes advantage of the crystal structures together with the short-range interactions of tight binding schemes. The reliability of the methods has been demonstrated. Extensive numerical examples and comparisons have shown that the methods can speed up the decimation approach by 7 to 80 times and can also outperform the advanced eigenvalue approach by several times. For 2 and 5, based on the exponential decay of the surface wave, a novel method is developed for the large finite array problem through a much lower complexity and memory consumption. The method numerically reconstructs propagating Bloch waves and surface waves according to the Bloch-Floquet theorem of periodic structures and translation invariant properties of semi-infinite periodic structures, respectively. We further employed the surface integral equation (SIE) to evaluate the second harmonic radiation generated from metal nanoparticles with arbitrary shapes. The mutual coupling between fundamental and second harmonic field is captured. This method paves the way for accurate and efficient design of general SH nonlinear nano plasmonic structures. The novel discontinuous Galerkin time domain method for the new atomically thin graphene structure in electromagnetic waves is also developed for this new material for general scientific and engineering applications. All these efforts and achievements contributed to 6 and 7. Several Ph.D students have got trained from this project. This project together with others has made our group an awarding winning team internationally.

711511.label: Major findings and research outcome
711511.value: A method for calculating the Casimir force between large, complex 3D objects is presented. Difficulties have previously arisen in broadband multiscale calculation using CEM methods. To expand the range of problems that can be calculated, we use an integral equation, domain decomposition method (DDM) and argument principle to derive the Casimir force formula. The broadband integral equation DDM, which is the augmented equivalence principle algorithm (A-EPA), allows for an efficient broadband solution of large, complex objects. A-EPA subdivides a complex problem into separate smaller subproblems that are later recombined into a reduced matrix. This yields a reduced number of unknowns for complex structures making them feasible with modest computer resources. We demonstrate the advantages of the A-EPA by simulating large, finite, 3D, unaligned corrugated plates for NEMS, which have previously only been modeled approximately as infinite plates using 2D techniques [Ref.8.1, 8.2, Ref. 9.1, 9.2]. CEM method is leveraged into multiphysics atomic simulations. In electron-transport systems, a condensed Hamiltonian matrix constructed with reduced dimension is proposed to perform simulation of quantum carrier transport in nano devices with the non-equilibrium Green’s function approach. This greatly speeds up the calculation. The condensed Hamiltonian approach successfully takes advantage of the crystal structures together with the short-range interactions of tight binding schemes. The reliability of the methods has been demonstrated. Extensive numerical examples and comparisons have shown that the methods can speed up the decimation approach by 7 to 80 times and can also outperform the advanced eigenvalue approach by several times [Ref. 8.7]. Based on the exponential decay of the surface wave, a novel method is developed by connecting the solution to the large finite array problem with that to a relatively small one to achieve low complexity and memory consumption. The method numerically reconstructs propagating Bloch waves and surface waves according to the Bloch-Floquet theorem of periodic structures and translation invariant properties of semi-infinite periodic structures, respectively [Ref. 8.4, 9.3]. We further employed the surface integral equation (SIE) to evaluate the second harmonic radiation generated from metal nanoparticles with arbitrary shapes. The mutual coupling between fundamental and second harmonic field is captured. This method paves the way for accurate and efficient design of general SH nonlinear nano plasmonic structures [Ref.9.4]. The novel discontinuous Galerkin time domain method for the new atomically thin graphene structure in electromagnetic waves is also developed for this new material for general scientific and engineering applications [Ref.9.3].

711511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
711511.value: 1. Not only Casimir force can be solved using proposed numerical approaches, it shall also be solvable effectively using the characteristic modes based method. Further efforts could be extended in this direction. 2. Solving Casimir force pushes us to handle more nanomaterial problems, such as the second harmonic generation, new materials such as graphene, and distributive nonlinear problems. We have started efforts in nonlinear Maxwell’s equation solutions.

711711.label: Project Objectives
711711.value: Fabrication and growth of nanostructured LEDs: To fabricate ordered nanostructured LEDs, or photonic crystal LEDs, via the bottom-up (growth) and top-down (patterning + etching) approaches, and make comparisons between them in terms of electrical and optical characteristics. In either approach, the masking later/growth template will be patterned via our in-house developed technique of “jet-printing nanosphere lithography”, a self-assembly nano-patterning process that is both efficient and cost-effective. Characterization and tailoring of polarization properties for photonic crystal LEDs: To determine the polarization ratios of photonic crystal LEDs with different parameters including packing arrangement, dimension and pitch. Simulations will be performed to calculate the dispersion relation, or band diagram using the plane wave expansion method, from which rich information on both photonic bandgap AND polarization characteristics can be obtained. Based on the experimental and simulation results, a surface-emitting photonic crystal LED with high polarization extinction ratio AND extraction efficiency will be designed and realized. To study the reliability of nanostructured LEDs and to establish their mechanism of degradation: Through a range of electrical measurements, and in conjunction with Electron-beam Induced Current (EBIC), the role of interfacial defects in nano-LEDs, including photonic crystal LEDs, will be thoroughly investigated. The mechanism of device degradation and failure will be proposed, which will be useful for the prediction of device lifetimes. To overcome reliability issues, thus producing an “all-round” photonic crystal LED: To find optimal passivation solutions for nano-LEDs to overcome reliability issues, with the target of demonstrating a high performance photonic crystal LED with high extraction efficiency, high polarization extinction ratio and with lifetimes comparable to conventional large-area LEDs.

711711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
711711.value: The emphasis of this project is the investigation of the polarization properties of nanostructured photonic crystal Gallium Nitride (GaN) based light-emitting diodes (LEDs), together with their failure mechanism. Nanophotonics enables us to manipulate light at sub-wavelength dimensions, through photonic crystals or plasmonics. With greater control, one could not only increase light emission, but also potentially tailor the optical properties of devices. One such property of interest is polarization. LEDs that emit linearly polarized light are highly desirable for a wide range of applications including sensing, imaging, and 3-D displays. However, LED emission is generally un-polarized. This would be different if the surfaces of LEDs become regularly-structured. Nano-structuring, in the form of photonic crystals, has been widely studied in recent years with the target of enhancing light extraction by forbidding lateral photon propagation through an in-plane photonic bandgap (PBG). Apart from PBG properties, the photonic crystal structure can also serve as a grating that can modify the polarization characteristics of the device. One major shortcoming associated with nano-structuring is the creation of defects at the surface. Such defects will lead to degraded electrical and optical properties, which subsequently result in reduced lifetimes of the devices. In this project, a detailed study on the effects of interfacial defects on the reliability of nanostructured photonic crystal LEDs will be undertaken. This project will deepen our understanding of polarization characteristics and reliability of photonic crystal LEDs, with the objective of designing an LED with customizable and desirable polarization, together with enhanced lifetimes. This can be achieved by gaining insight into the relation between attributes of the photonic crystal and its polarization patterns. At the same time, device reliability will be investigated. In particular, Electron-beam Induced Current (EBIC) will be mapped to determine a correlation between defects and degradation in nitride LEDs. Such experimental data will be instrumental for the development of a model to explain the breakdown mechanism, which will be useful for the prediction of LED lifetimes. The fabrication of photonic crystals LEDs will also be innovative. We are employing ink-jet technology for the “printing” of nanosphere arrays- a powerful tool for nano-patterning. Concurrently, our Co-I will epitaxially grow nanostructured LEDs for comparison. The composition of the research team- a combination of a material specialist and an experimental physicist as investigators- ensures effective and successful execution of this project to deliver results useful for extending our knowledge in the field of nanophotonics. 本項目的重點是研究納米結構光子晶體氮化鎵發光二極管(LED)的偏振特性，以及其失效機理。納米光子學為我們在次波長範圍內，通過光子晶體或等離子體控制光提供了依據。通過更有力的控制，不僅可以提高光輸出，還能控制器件的光學特性。我們感興趣的其中一個光學特性就是偏振。能發出線性偏振光的LEDs在很多領域有著重要的應用，例如傳感器、成像系統和3D顯示。然而，LED發出的通常是非偏振光。但如果在LED表面做一些有規律性的結構，情況就會有所不同。以光子晶體形式存在的納米結構，近來被廣泛研究，通過阻止光子在平面光子帶隙上的橫向傳播來提高取光效率。除了光子帶隙的特性，光子晶體結構還可以作為光柵，改變器件的偏振特性。 與納米結構相關的一個主要缺點是，在器件表面引入了缺陷。這種缺陷會降低器件的電學特性和光學特性，這些會導致器件壽命的縮短。本項目將對界面缺陷對納米結構光子晶體LED可靠性的影響進行詳細研究。 本項目的目的是設計出可控制並能發出滿足需求的偏振光LED，同時提高其壽命，這將加深我們對光子晶體LED的偏振特性和可靠性的理解。我們將會研究光子晶體的屬性和偏振模式的關係。同時，我們還會研究器件的可靠性。特別地，我們將對點子束感生電流(EBIC)進行研究，以得到氮化物LEDs缺陷與老化之間的關係。這些實驗數據對建立一個失效機制模型將有很大的指導意義，也將進而有助于預測LED的壽命。 光子晶體LED的製造工藝也將具有創新性。我們正採用噴墨技術，這一納米圖案形成的強大工具，“打印”出納米球陣列。同時，我們的合作者將外延生長納米結構LEDs，以用於比較。 我們的科研團隊既有材料方面的專家，又有實驗物理學家，我們將共同保證此項目有效而成功的執行，並得出對我們更深入了解納米光子學有價值的結果。

711711.label: Realisation of objectives
711711.value: The objectives of this project have not been fulfilled, but has lead to further exploration into GaN nanostructures and nanoLEDs. Specifically: Objective 1: Nanostructured LEDs have been realized using a range of nanopatterning techniques. Also the different ways of fabricating the nanoLED have been explored; the optimal design was adopted. Objective 2: The polarization properties of nanoLEDs have been characterized. It was found that such properties can are indeed dependent on the ordering and pitch of the nanostructures. The structure was designed by FDTD simulations and experimentally verified. Objective 3: The mechanism of degradation of nanoLEDs have been studied, using conductive AFM to evaluate leakage current which is even more sensitive than EBIC. Objective 4: Different ways of passivating nanoLEDs have been investigated, with the target of minimizing leakage current which has been identified as a major cause of device failure. The research has lead to further investigation on various properties and functionalities of nanostructures and nanoLEDs, including strain-induced nanostructured broadband LEDs, as well as nanostructures for optical nano-cavities, which have subsequently received funding from the RGC for further study.

711711.label: Major findings and research outcome
711711.value: The following findings/ discoveries have been made: 1. The method of nanosphere lithography for nano-patterning is extremely cost-effective, especially for hard materials such as GaN. 2. Different methods of nanosphere coating have been explored; the method of freeze-drying was extensively experimented on, and was found to produce good results for large-scale patterning. 3. The polarization characteristics of LEDs with ordered nanostructures has been established; an integrated polarization ratio of 2.2 has been achieved. 4. The failure of nanoLEDs (and LEDs in general) is dependent on the leakage currents along sidewalls; thus nanoLEDs are more likely to fail compared to conventional large-area LED, despite improved properties in other aspects. 5. Conductive AFM was found to be a sensitive tool for the detection of leakage currents in nanostructures. 6. Passivation with oxides deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD) was found to be most effective, as the oxide molecules are most capable of passivating dangling bonds. 7. The ultimate way of passivation is achieved by overgrowing a crystalline layer of GaN over the nanostructures, which doubles as a contact layer.

711711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
711711.value: Nanostructuring of LEDs can enhance the efficiency and functionalities of LEDs. The efficiency and polarization aspects have been explored in this project. Nanostructuring can also bring about other aspects of improvement, particularly by exploiting strain relaxation of the strained InGaN/GaN quantum wells within LED structures. The highly circular nanostructures are also excellent whispering gallery mode resonators. These ideas are currently being explored, under the support of new GRF projects.

711711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
711711.value: The typical LED available in the market are planar structures, which sets a limit to the efficiencies and functionalities of LED products. These characteristics can potentially be enhanced by incorporating nanostructures into LEDs, which is the scope of this project. Two aspects of nano-LEDs are investigated: polarization and reliability. It was found that nano-LEDs are polarized, the degree of which can be tuned by adjusting the pitch of the ordered nanostructure. Polarized light is useful for reducing glare for illuminations. The reliabilities of nano-LEDs may also be degraded due to the introduction of defects during nano-processing. Such defects are effectively suppressed with a suitable choice of passivation.

712411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
712411.value: The increasing requirements for a reliable, secure, economic, efficient, environmentally friendly, and safe energy infrastructure enhance the interest in the establishment of smart power grids. As one of the most desirable features, self-heal is, in essence, the immune system of a smart grid. By online self-assessment, real-time risk analysis, and online strategy establishment, a self-healing smart grid can minimize the disruption of energy services and promise a reliable, resilient and responsive electric supply. In a smart grid, with significant renewable resources and responsive loads integration, the great variability and uncertainty aggravate the challenges for implementation of self-healing functions. Furthermore, as a series of sequential actions, correlations between each self-healing action should be considered. The traditional offline deterministic scenario-based healing strategy establishment methodology will be updated essentially. Subject to the acceptable risk level of the entire self-healing process, a new methodology, which supports online strategy establishment with stochastic system components, is critically needed. The proposed research project addresses the systematic self-healing smart grid construction problem in the context of a new energy paradigm. A new methodology called risk-limiting self-healing strategy establishment is proposed to meet the requirements of the smart grid. The major topics of this research are as follows: (1) Risk assessment methodology and associated information acquisition method. Accomplishment of this task will provide a risk assessment methodology to identify emerging risks of a self-healing action and potential risk of the system status. For risk indices identification, an information acquisition method is proposed as well to achieve observability of the system. (2) Methodology for risk-limiting self-healing strategy establishment. The strategy established in this task subject to the acceptable risk level of the entire self-healing process. Look-ahead risk constraints, i.e., not only risks of the action at this stage, but also potential risk caused by this action for the remaining self-healing process, are involved. (3) Sophisticated algorithm development. A series of analytical and numerical methods will be proposed to solve the risk-limiting self-healing problem. State-of-the-art stochastic analysis technologies, including, but not limited to, the Markov Chain Monte Carlo and scenario reduction method, will be employed based on the properties of problems. (4) Demonstration of the proposed methodology on some standard and actual power systems. The present proposed research is built on the experience of our past efforts and is more ambitious. In the long run, the accomplishment of this project will represent a systematic methodology towards implementing a self-healing smart grid. 随着对电力系统可靠、稳健、经济、高效、环保和安全需求的急剧提升，构建智能电网已经成为广泛关注的热点。电网的自愈性是智能电网的核心特征之一。从本质上说，自愈是智能电网的免疫系统。通过在线评估、实时安全分析以及在线决策生成，具有自愈性的智能电网可以最小化停电带来的损失，可望实现一个具有可靠、弹性且响应迅速的电力系统。 在智能电网的环境下，新能源和负荷响应的引入更加剧了系统中具有的可变性和不确定性，从而使实现自愈功能更为困难。另外，由于电网在故障后的自愈过程是一个包含一系列操作的贯序决策，不同决策之间的关系需要详细加以考虑。因此，传统的，基于确定性场景的自愈方案构建策略必须从根本上加以更新，急需建立一种以全过程风险水平为约束，同时可以兼容随机元件特性的在线自愈方案生成方法。 在智能电网的条件下，本项目旨在建立一种系统化的自愈智能电网构建方法。提出的新方法称为：风险约束的自愈智能电网构建方法论。主要研究内容包括：（1）风险评估方法和相应的信息获取机制。这个方面的研究成果将有助于评估系统自愈操作的风险，同时发现系统的潜在风险。（2）风险约束的自愈策略构建。在这个方面的研究中构造的自愈策略将以可接受的风险水平作为基础，采用一种前向的风险约束，即不仅当前决策的风险需要评估，同时未来策略的潜在风险也会被评估。（3）高效算法的提出。本研究将提出一系列高效的算法。其中包括随机分析的成果，如马尔科夫模拟技术，场景消减技术等，用于求解本课题的问题。（4）将本课题提出的方法在标准仿真系统和实际系统进行仿真。 本课题的研究建立在本人以往的研究积累之上，但是具有更高的目标。从长远看，本项目的研究成果将为最终实现自愈性的智能电网提供理论和实践基础。

712411.label: Realisation of objectives
712411.value: As the second project of inter-related RGC-support projects on self-healing smart grids, the objective of this project is to establish self-healing strategies with risk-related and realistic operating constraints. The accomplishment of this project provides essential components for implementing a resilient power grid. We believe these findings are critical for both theoretical study and power industrial practices. Based on the scope of this project, for establishing self-healing strategies, the information acquisition and risk assessment methods have been proposed; risk-based methods were introduced into the self-healing strategy construction; some highly efficient algorithms were designed; and a decision support system based on the proposed method was implemented with realistic constraints. The following coherent tasks have been completely accomplished. Sophisticated risk measures and associated information acquisition methods were established. The risk indices associated with implementing self-healing actions were categorized into event-driven indices (EDI) and condition-driven indices (CDI). The risk associated with each operating action is quantified by EDI; meanwhile, the CDI was used to measure the risk of a given operating condition. In this project, the availability of each component in a power system was used to construct the event-driven risk index. With the stochastic characteristics of renewable energy sources, the distance from the current operating point to the boundary of the security region and the associated stopping time were employed to establish the condition-driven risks. The proposed risk indices were used to construct self-healing strategies subject to risk constraints and operational constraints. The realistic self-healing strategy was established as an operating sequence of breakers with a graph theory-based method. Furthermore, a risk-limiting method was proposed for the entire process satisfying the risk constraints. For distribution systems, after identifying the operating states and associated risks, the self-healing strategies were developed. These strategies meet the physical constraints, as well as the potential risk constraints during implementation. A set of highly efficient algorithms were developed to solve the proposed self-healing problems. The interaction between generators and loads during self-healing process was modelled as a multiple time-interval optimal problem. A direct solution method was proposed. A load restoration strategy with sequential constraints, frequency security constraints, cold load pickup, and steady-state operational constraints was developed. The proposed methods were implemented by PI’s team with software entitled ‘System Restoration Navigator’(SRN). It has been used by some US and Chinese realistic power systems. The accomplishment has been highlighted by IEEE Power and Energy Magazine.

712411.label: Major findings and research outcome
712411.value: The major findings are risk-based self-healing strategies and applications. It provides essential components for self-healing smart grids. 1. Risk assessment methods for self-healing actions Risks for different operating states were categorized [Journal 1]. The EDIs and CDIs were defined to assess risks associated with self-healing process [Conference 14]. The component availability was used to construct EDIs [Conference 11]. With stochastic differential equation-based renewables model, the CDIs was defined as the distance or associated stopping time from the current operating point to the boundary of security region [Conference 14]. 2. Self-healing strategy construction with risk-limiting constraints (1) Risk-limiting vulnerability mitigation The vulnerability comes from uncertainty of renewables or availability of equipment. This project used robust optimization to determinate the tolerance of an operating state with deterministic set-based renewables [Journal 4]. The vulnerability and potential risks were categorized[Conference 16]. A risk-limiting method was proposed to mitigate the risk due to the stochastic inaccurate renewables predication with network constraints [Conference 7]. The risks from the equipment availability were modeled as a Markov chain and mitigated [Conference 9, 13]. To integrate large-scale renewables, vulnerability from new transmission technologies, such as HVDC, were also involved to implement self-healing functions [Conference 1, 5, 12]. Mitigation strategies can be established based on the available system information [Conference 8]. (2) Risk-based restoration strategies Risks and required self-healing functionality for different operating states were identified [Journal 1]. The component availability was integrated into restoration strategy to consider risk constraints [Conference 11]. Realistic restoration was implemented with a breakers’ sequence subject to risk constraints [Conference 6]. Frequency and network constraints were involved into the load restoration [Conference 15]. New generation technology can coordinate vulnerability mitigation and outage restoration [Conference 10]. 3. Highly efficient algorithms developed to construct proposed methodology For essentially sequential self-healing problems, the reduced KKT system is derived. Using Cholesky factorisation algorithm and reordering algorithm, the long time-horizon dynamic optimal power flow problems were solved [Journal 3]. Novel hybrid GPU-CPU based algorithm was employed to simulate transient stability for systems with renewables injection [Journal 2]. A branch-and-cut method was proposed to solve the mixed-integer nonlinear load restoration problem with discrete load increments. The ZIP, cold load and network constraints were involved [Conference 15]. To deal with the uncertainties of renewables, robust optimization [Journal 4], stochastic optimization algorithms [Journal 7,11,14] were improved. 4. Software developed and applications SRN was enhanced and used by US and Chines power systems [Journal 5, Conference 2].

712411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
712411.value: This project identifies the potential risk due to renewables. Based on the preliminary results from this project, future research should address the methods to fully utilize the advantage of renewables during self-healing process. Renewables can provide power with uncertainties. It is believed that the renewables can be integrated only after a strong system is constructed. It might be the load restoration stage according to GRMs-based self-healing methodology. The frequency violation due to inaccurate renewables prediction and discrete characteristic of loads should be carefully considered. The branch-and-cut method and robust optimization method might be useful. A systematic self-healing methodology should coordinate the vulnerability mitigation and outage restoration. The vulnerability of a system should be quantified first. The tradeoff method between system risk and the cost to implement a self-healing action should be established. The appropriate actions should be identified based on the identified risk and cost for implementation. More realistic considerations should be involved into the decision support system for restoration. It is believed that the breaker sequence-based model is critical for an on-line restoration tool. The theoretical research was accomplished of this topic. To implement it, the standards for breaker operation should be considered in the software.

712411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
712411.value: Due to the complexity of modern power systems, even a well-designed system might suffer from outages. The objective of the self-healing function, which is the key function of the future smart power grid, is to reduce or eliminate power interruptions To meet the requirements of the self-healing function, not only the traditional power system components, but also the new components, such as renewable energy sources, new transmission methods should be considered. More importantly, the established self-healing strategies cannot aggravate the current outage. In other words, the risk associated with self-healing strategies should be considered in the context of the future smart grid. The objective of this project is to study how to construct self-healing strategy subject to the potential risk constraints. The self-healing functionality requirements of different power system states were identified. The risks from system equipment and uncertainties of renewables were studied. The self-healing strategies were established under acceptable risk level. The proposed methods were implemented by a piece of software, which is used in US and Chinese power systems. It is believed that the accomplishment of this project provide critical methods and tools to implement self-healing function in the future smart grid.

712911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
712911.value: The recovery of the structure of a 3D scene from 2D images taken at different viewpoints, known as structure from motion, is an important problem central to computer vision with applications to image-based rendering, human-computer interaction, robot navigation etc. The structure-from-motion problem is well studied and the factorization approach has won recognition as the most successful approach. However, a fundamental limitation of structure from motion is that the scene is assumed to be static consisting of only rigid objects. This renders the structure-from-motion methods inapplicable to most real-world dynamic scenes containing moving and deformable objects such as walking persons or expressive faces. There have been some recent attempts to extend the methods for structure from motion, mainly based on the factorization approach, to non-rigid objects. The underlying principle of these extensions is to approximate the deformations of non-rigid objects by generic approximation techniques. Unfortunately, these approximations are not supported by physical justifications, but rather intended to reinstate an algebraic rank condition in order to enable the factorization method to become workable in the non-rigid case. Experiments on real image sequences show that the reconstruction results of existing factorization methods for non-rigid shapes are far from satisfactory. The non-rigid structure from motion problem is therefore still open with plenty of scope for development of better methods for this important area. Our proposal is to take a completely new approach to non-rigid structure from motion that is built upon the vision geometry and physical conditions of the problem. In general, non-rigid structure from motion is an ill-posed problem with infinite feasible solutions, and therefore a key issue is what constraints should be used to define the solution. In the project, we propose to exploit both geometric constraints for image projection and physical constraints describing structural characteristics of the non-rigid shape to provide a well-posed formulation of the non-rigid structure from motion problem. Such constraints remain largely unexplored in existing approaches to non-rigid structure from motion. Our aim is to provide a formulation that reflects the physical nature of the problem, with provisions for commonly encountered non-rigid structure, such as multiple walking persons in a scene, or dynamic facial expressions. This project is expected to lead to new scope for applications of NRSFM. 以不同觀點採集到的二維圖像去恢復三維場景的結構，稱為從運動恢復結構，是一個重要的計算機視覺問題，應用包括基於圖像的建模和渲染，人機交互，機器人導航等，從運動恢復結構問題已有很多的研究，因式分解是公認為最成功的方法。然而從運動恢復結構有一個基本的限制，就是假定場景是靜態的並且只由剛性物體組成。這使從運動恢復結構方法不適用於大多數真實世界包含移動和變形物體的場景，如正在走動的人或動態面部表情。 最近已有一些嘗試，把從運動恢復結構的方法擴展至非剛性的對象，這些擴展的方法主要還是基於因式分解，基本原則是以通用的近似技術去代表非剛性物體的變形。不幸的是，這些近似並非以物理的理由支持，而是旨在恢復一個代數的秩條件以便使分解方法在非剛性的情況仍然可行。實際圖像序列的實驗結果表明，現有的分解方法用於非剛性的形狀的重建結果遠遠不能令人滿意。因此從運動恢復非剛性結構仍是開放的問題，發展更好的方法是一個重要的領域。 我們的建議是採取一種全新的基於視覺幾何和物理條件的從運動恢復非剛性結構方法。在一般情況下，從運動恢復非剛性結構是一個病態問題，具有無窮多的可行的解答，因此，一個關鍵的問題是什麼限制應該被用來定義解決方案。在這項目中，我們提出利用圖像投影的幾何約束和非剛性形狀結構特點的物理約束，制定一個從運動恢復非剛性結構的良好的定問題。以上的約束在現有從運動到非剛性結構的方法仍未開發。我們的目的是提供一種反映物理性質的制定方法，包括照顧經常遇到的非剛性結構，如多個在場景走動的人，或動態面部表情。這項目預計將導致從運動恢復非剛性結構應用的新範圍。

712911.label: Realisation of objectives
712911.value: The objectives of the project have been fully realised. The main areas of work in accordance with the originally proposed objectives are as follows. (1) We have considered different reformulations of the non-rigid structure from motion (NRSFM) problem by including geometric and physical constraints, such as articulated structures and small deformations, with an aim to remove the ill-posedness of the NRSFM problem. The reformulated problems are then posed as optimization problems based on the shape/trajectory basis methods [C2] or articulated-structure representation [C3]. (2) To obtain a solution methodology for the NRSFM formulated in this project, we have developed new approaches to some basic front-end problems including camera self-calibration algorithm [J1] and 3D curve reconstruction from multiple images [J2], the latter of which can be used as a pointwise trajectory basis method for NRSFM. With these methods, we have developed optimization methodologies to solve different formulations of NRSFM problem as reported in [C2, C3]. (3) Software algorithms of the aforementioned solution methods for NRSFM have been implemented and tested comprehensively using real and synthetic datasets to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed methods. The experimental results, as well as comparisons with other existing methods, are provided in [C2, C3], showing that our solutions are able to exploit geometric and physical conditions to produce higher quality reconstructions of non-rigid objects.

712911.label: Major findings and research outcome
712911.value: The major findings and research outcome of this project include: (i) New camera self calibration method based on unified framework for multiview constraints [J1]; (ii) 3D curve reconstruction method [J2] that may be applied to pointwise-based trajectory-basis approach to NRSFM; (iii) New approaches with reformulations of NRSFM [C2, C3] that addresses the ill-posedness of the problem by incorporating prior geometric and/or physical constraints such as small deformations, articulated objects, etc.; (iv) New optimization-based methodologies [C2, C3] for solving reformulated NRSFM problems, hence overcoming obscure ambuiguities of existing shape/trajectory basis methods resulting in better quality reconstructions of non-rigid objects; (v) Software implementations and extensive evaluations of the proposed methodologies in comparison with existing methods, providing benchmark results for futher developments in NRSFM.

712911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
712911.value: There are plenty of scope for further research both in theoretical development and applications of NRSFM. Along the lines of this project, one may consider a new approach using a parametric model-based framework for formlating and solving NRSFM. In terms of applications, the reconstruction of human motion has always been a subject of intense interest. This project has laid the foundation for resonstructing human pose as NRSFM incorporating priorly known dynamic properties of human skeletal motion. We propose to explore the use of the results of this project in multiview vedio surveillance system for scenes with multiple walking persons and/or moving objects, some preliminary work of which has been reported in [C1].

712911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
712911.value: Although the recovery of a static 3D scene from 2D images taken at different viewpoints is well-established, the reconstruction of a dynamic scene containing non-rigid objects, known as non-rigid structure from motion (NRSFM) is much more difficult. In this project, we have addressed two key fundamental issues of NRSFM, namely ill-posedness and reconstruction ambiguities. Unlike exisiting methods that are purely based on generic approximation theory, we have exploited both geometric constraints and properties decribing real physical characteristics of the objects under reconstruction to provide a well-posed formulation of NRSFM. Consequently, we have developed optimization-based methodologies that provide reconstructions of non-rigid shapes of substantially improved quality when compared with existing shape/trajectory methods using benchmark datasets including articulated robot arm, facial expressions, walking human, etc. The findings of this project have many potential applications such as scene reconstruction for autonomous navigation, human pose estimation and intelligent surveillance system.

713011.label: Project Objectives
713011.value: Develop a new radiated emission modeling method for IC EMC using computational electromagnetics. Develop a generalized IC radiation modeling method from which most existing approximated solutions can be derived. Hence, it shall be useful for novel specialized method derivations. Develop a Huygens’ principle based inverse scattering method to recover the equivalent source distributions at the IC location. Instead of using PEC (Perfect Electric Conductor) or PMC (Perfect Magnetic Conductor), multilayer Green’s function is employed in the process. The PCB dielectric effect is naturally modeled by this approach. Develop IC EMC modeling for special cases (such as magnetic equivalent sources only, magnetic field or electric field measurement only), low frequencies, and thin substrates. The validation of their application range will be studied to provide EMC modeling guidelines. Develop the broadband integral equation simulation method for broadband IC EMC radiation. Relevant operators will be studied for their bandwidth. PEEC method and other methods will be employed to provide the broadband simulation engine. Study the IC radiated emission and its interference with the lumped and distributive circuit components in the half open space on PCB boards. Develop the simulation methods for the IC radiated emission through the slots or holes on the metal walls of the shielding box by the integral equation method and the mode matching method. The significant cavity effects of the shielding box will be properly considered in the shielding box.

713011.label: Realisation of objectives
713011.value: The proposed objectives of the project have been completely. The results are evidenced through journal publications and conference presentations. The radiated emission modeling method for ICs on PCBs (Objective 1, 2, 3) has been focused in our studies. The methodology is developed based on the Huygens’ principle and the near field far field transformation (Paper 1, 5, 12). The source reconstruction method (SRM) was developed with the consideration of various possible data measurement approaches so that it could be adaptive to many existing approximated solutions (Paper 10). Dyadic Green’s functions and integral equation methods form the core of the proposed methods. To deal with the layered structure frequently needed in the IC and circuit radiation modeling (Objective 3), a new Green’s function formulation for modeling homogeneous objects in layered medium is systematically developed (Paper 2). The low frequency issue in the emission modeling (Objective 4) is addressed by developing a new Coulumb based integral equation method (Paper 8) and a rigorous Helmholtz decomposition based method (Paper 11). The broadband radiation (Objective 5) is tackled by the alternation of the Augmented EFIE and regular EFIE (Paper 4). The broadband source reconstruction is solved by the Stoer-Bulirsch algorithm (Paper 6). The hybrid coupling between distributive parts and lumped circuits (Objective 6) is solved by the newly developed DGTD method (Paper 9). The radiated emission through slots or holes on the metal walls of the shielding box (Objective 7) is solved by a newly proposed two-step integral equation method (Paper 7) to avoid the needs of the Dyadic Green’s function with metal box presented. A generalized modal expansion method theory of the electromagnetic field in both bounded and unbounded media has been proposed to create more useful physical insight of the radiation and coupling mechanism for complex IC and PCB systems (Paper 3). Based on the above list, all objectives have been fully implemented. The GRF project funding code was acknowledged in almost all above published journal papers. Several conference papers were also presented at international symposiums and conferences. Close collaborations with the industry based on the developed technology have attracted over 1.0 million Hong Kong dollar industrial funding support.

713011.label: Major findings and research outcome
713011.value: The novel source reconstruction methods (SRM) is developed to recover equivalence sources for the general ICs and PCBs. It is used to characterize the radiated emissions for IC EMC. Both spherical and planar measurement surfaces are studied for the equivalence source construction [1,5,12]. To solve the radiation from ventilation slots on shielding boxes, a two-step integral equation method is proposed to compute the superposition of direct radiated fields from slots and scattered fields by the induced electric current on shielding box surfaces [7]. To avoid the phase measurement needed in conventional equivalent source reconstruction methods, a novel iterative SRM based on phaseless electric fields is proposed [9]. The reconstructed equivalent current source can be electric, magnetic current, or both. Because constructing near field equivalent sources through SRMs is time consuming over a broad bandwidth, we developed a novel SRM that is based on the Stoer-Bulirsch algorithm with the adaptive frequency sampling [6]. It overcomes the need for derivatives from regular asymptotic waveform evaluation. For the layered medium, we propose a new Green’s function formulation for modeling homogeneous objects in layered medium [2]. The dyadic form of the Green’s function is developed by applying the pilot vector potential approach, and all components are derived in terms of 0-order and 1-order Sommerfeld integrals. The matrix representation is further derived by applying integrations by parts and vector identities. To have a better physical insight to the radiation mechanism, a generalized modal expansion theory of the electromagnetic field in both bounded and unbounded media is proposed [3]. A reduced modal representation of the field response under excitation has been presented. Then excited fields can be represented approximately by a small number of trapped and radiation modes. For the lumped and distributive hybrid system, a hybrid full-wave EM-circuit simulator based on the discontinuous Galerkin time domain (DGTD) method and admittance matrix is developed [8]. The coupling between the EM solver and the circuit solver is enabled by introducing portal voltage and current sources. For cases where circuit details are unavailable, the fast relaxation vector fitting method is employed to obtain the approximated admittance matrix as long as frequency samples of its parameters are known. The resultant algorithm is very flexible and powerful in analyzing the EM radiation and coupling together with lumped subsystems for ICs and PCBs.

713011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
713011.value: With the foundation established by this project, there are many further developments that could be initialized. One direction is to include more parameters into stochastic analysis for the radiation modeling. We have implemented the stochastic modeling based on adaptive sparse grid collocation method for the electromagnetic and circuit hybrid system. However, we could only change the electric properties of lumped components and distributive materials. Including the uncertainty of geometries into the consideration is an interesting research topic. Another direction is to develop the numerical Green’s function under arbitrary boundary conditions. It will greatly simplify the integral equation modeling process for general radiation problems. We plan to propose the above mentioned and relevant ideas through future GRF proposals. We will try to implement them to make our proposed methodologies more powerful and flexible.

713011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
713011.value: Due to the soaring signal speed and channel bandwidth in modern electronic systems, there are more electromagnetic radiations from integrated circuits (ICs) and printed circuit boards (PCBs). It causes signal interferences and information leakage. It becomes necessary for all IC and PCB designs to consider the optimal radiation reduction from their prototype stage. This project is intended to develop advanced modeling methodologies based on first principles to characterize radiations in complex electronic environments with ICs and PCBs. It contributes to the electronic design automation (EDA) system that is indispensible for today’s IC and PCB designs. It also helps the reduction of unintentional radiations that violate domestic or international electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) standards. The approaches proposed in this project are based on fundamental laws of electromagnetics and modern computational electromagnetics (CEM) methods. It employs the computing power of modern computers and advances of numerical methods to numerically solve practical problems that have no simple analytical solutions.

713811.label: Project Title(Chinese)
713811.value: 計算全息成像系統的高分辨率圖像

713811.label: Project Objectives
713811.value: To advance compressive imaging in optical scanning holography: This includes both investigating how image data should be captured, and how they should be processed. The latter entails software implementation of an image reconstruction algorithm that also contributes to the vast compressed sensing literature. If time permits, we also hope to explore implementations in GPUs for accelerations. To advance coded pupil design in optical scanning holography: This includes investigating the properties that we need for the coded pupils, and exploring how they can be incorporated in the OSH imaging system. Both simulation with our current OSH imaging model and an experimental study when the pupils are in place in an actual system are planned. To broaden the use of optical scanning holography: We are encouraged by MIT's work to use digital holographic imaging in underwater applications, and hope to engage our colleagues involved in various applications (including but not limited to life science) to widen the use of OSH. We believe that identifying the appropriate applications will drive further developments in the right directions.

713811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
713811.value: A high-resolution and high-speed capture of small volumetric objects, particular dynamic biological specimens, can greatly enhance a scientist's perception of the microscopic world. However, these two goals are often conflicting. For instance, confocal microscopy provides excellent two-dimensional images with high lateral resolution at the expense of a shallow depth due to the inherent physics. To obtain a volume imagery, it requires sequential acquisition at different axial planes, a slow process and unsuitable for objects that might move during the scan. On the other hand, holographic imaging, although currently providing images with a lower lateral resolution, can capture the entire three-dimensional volume during a single x-y scan in a digital hologram, and the data can then be processed to obtain the individual two-dimensional sections for viewing and analysis. High-resolution volume imagery of dynamic objects is therefore a possibility with holographic imaging. In this proposal, we focus on a particular form of holographic imaging known as optical scanning holography (OSH). It has been shown that OSH can deliver better than one micrometer lateral resolution with fluorescent specimens, and the system has also been experimented for imaging various other biological subjects. Our goal in this proposal is to further enhance the capability of OSH through the development of advanced computational algorithms. By increasing the resolution and speed of image reconstruction, we can greatly expand the applicability of OSH as the system of choice in high-resolution volumetric imaging. Our computational algorithms mainly focus on two aspects. (1) In developing more sophisticated image reconstruction algorithms, we aim to suppress the defocus noise and consequently increasing our ability to differentiate adjacent objects. We intend to research on the coded pupils, and investigate how this methodology, when coupled with the appropriate computation, may lead to breakthroughs in OSH resolution. (2) For many practical imaging scenarios, the speed of acquisition is very important, particular when the object is highly dynamic. We plan to explore how it may be possible to reduce the data capture, and instead rely on prior information in a new paradigm called compressive imaging. We envision that outcomes of our study will advance not only OSH imaging but also other forms of digital holography, where high-resolution volume imaging has been a major focus. Our work also contributes to educating optical engineers in Hong Kong, benefiting the growth of the technology sector in the region. 高分辨率和高速度地採集微小物體特別是動態運動中生物樣本的數據，可以極為有效地幫助科學工作者對微生物世界的認知。然而在很多情況下高分辨率和高速度這兩方面的要求是相互矛盾的。例如，共聚焦顯微鏡可以提供近似完美的橫向截面高清晰度二維圖像，但是由於技術本身的物理機理，它的成像深度非常的小。為了得到一幅立體圖像，這項技術需要對縱深方向上不同平面進行一系列的數據採集，這緩慢不適用於掃描過程中可能發生目標移動的採集過程。另一方面，全息成像，盡管目前隻能夠提供低分辨率的橫向截面圖，但是隻需一次平面掃描就可以收集全部三維信息，並且通過對數據的處理可以還原物體各個二維截面從而用於觀察和分析。因此全息成像技術成為針對動態目標高分辨率三維成像問題的一種解決方案。 在這個項目中，我們著重研究一種特殊的全息成像技術，名為光學掃描全息。它已經被驗証可以對熒光染色樣本提供優於一微米的橫向成像清晰度，並且已經用於多種其他生物標本的成像實驗。在這個項目中，我們的目標是通過研發高級數學計算算法進一步提高它的性能。通過提高分辨率和加快圖像恢復的速度，我們可以極大的拓展光學掃描全息作為高清晰度立體成像實現系統的應用可能性。我們的計算算法研究主要集中在兩方面：（1）在研發先進的圖像恢復算法方面，我們致力於通過壓制散焦噪聲從而提高系統分辨臨近物體的性能。我們傾向於開展系統瞳孔平面上的編碼研究，並將這一方法與適當的算法結合，從而探索其突破現有光學掃描全息系統分辨率水平的可能性。（2）對於許多實際成像方案，數據採集速度是非常重要的，特別是在目標處於高動態狀況時。我們計劃採用一項稱為壓縮成像的新技術，而非依靠目標的先驗信息，對減低數據採集量進行探索。我們預期，我們的研究成果不但可以推進光學掃描全息成像研究，也可以對其他致力於高分辨率立體成像的數字全息技術提供借鑒。此外，我們的工作也將有益於香港的光學工程師教育，對這個地區的技術發展起到促進作用。

713811.label: Realisation of objectives
713811.value: The three objectives of the project have been satisfactorily achieved. Specifically, we have investigated the image acquisition in optical scanning holography, and developed an imaging model which allows us to gain insight into capturing data compressively to speed up the acquisition without sacrificing the reconstruction quality. The imaging model includes flexibility in designing different pupil functions, which we have explored several methods, such as random phase, and we developed the corresponding image reconstruction algorithms. We are also able to show how optical scanning holography can be used to image fluorescent objects, which is particularly important for biological applications.

713811.label: Major findings and research outcome
713811.value: In this project, we contributed on a broad scale the advantages and efficacy of digital holographic imaging system in capturing high-resolution volume imagery, and particularly its application in biological imaging. More specifically, we developed and demonstrated effective computational algorithms for optical scanning holography, which has the rare capability of volumetric capture of fluorescent objects. We showed mechanisms to improve reconstructed image quality, through a combination of modification to the imaging methodology and computational advances, such as the use of dual wavelength source, double axial position capture, and the design of a configurable pupil. The imaging model developed for optical scanning holography also allows for further development of this technology, such as in optical image encryption and remote sensing.

713811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
713811.value: The exploration of the role of computation to complement optical hardware in the overall imaging system design is a paradigm shift known as computational imaging, and this project demonstrates the strength of computational imaging in digital holography. The imaging model of optical scanning holography and the algorithms for image reconstruction, which involve efficiently solving inverse imaging problems, will prove useful for many further developments, including but not limited to other applications of optical scanning holography, and the use of computational imaging in other areas, such as biophotonics.

713811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
713811.value: Holography is a form of three-dimensional capture and display of an object, and has wide applications in scientific investigations. The advent of digital sensors allow holographic capture to be recorded digitally, which allows computational postprocessing of the captured data to reconstruct the 3D object. This project develops advanced computational algorithms for a form of digital holography known as optical scanning holography, which is very suitable for biological microscopy applications. Our algorithms are able to enhance the image resolution, allowing the users to have better views of the objects under investigation.

714011.value: 具有有限容量和不完全測量的受限泛函微分系統的綜合

714011.label: Project Objectives
714011.value: Establishment of Stability Conditions for Functional Differential Systems with Saturation Constraints The null controllability and null controllable region of functional differential systems with saturated control will be studied. Local and global stability results will be developed for retarded systems with saturation constraints. Development of Synthesis Approaches for Functional Differential Systems under Limited Capacity and Imperfect Measurement Stability and controllability results will be extended to various types of functional differential systems. Controllers and filters will be synthesized under environments with limited capacity and imperfect measurement. Various control and filter performances will be treated in the synthesis development. The robustness issues of the synthesis techniques will be addressed.

Local and global stability results will be developed for retarded systems with saturation constraints.

Development of Synthesis Approaches for Functional Differential Systems under Limited Capacity and Imperfect Measurement Stability and controllability results will be extended to various types of functional differential systems. Controllers and filters will be synthesized under environments with limited capacity and imperfect measurement. Various control and filter performances will be treated in the synthesis development. The robustness issues of the synthesis techniques will be addressed.

714011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
714011.value: Dynamic systems in engineering require constant regulation to ensure stability, operability, and optimality. To meet the ever-increasing demand for high accuracy and robust performance of control systems, controllers have to provide sufficient control gain that can be delivered instantly. However, physical controllers always suffer from saturation whenever the control gain is beyond the normal operating range. Constraints such as actuator/sensor saturation or state boundedness represent some of the many possible natural physical restrictions placed on control systems. These control constraints often impose significant limitations on the controllability and stabilizability of a system, not to mention the degradation of control performance. Much of the effort to deal with such constraints in the past has been devoted to finite-dimensional systems. Unfortunately, the results are not applicable to numerous important physical and social-economical processes described by functional differential equations such as heat flow in materials with memory, regulation of glucose-insulin, and commodity price fluctuations. In this project, we will extend the time-reversed system approach, as well as develop new ones, to overcome the technical difficulties and derive controllability/stabilizability results for retarded and neutral-type functional differential systems. Issues such as null controllability and characterization of regional controllability will form the fundamental part of the project. Apart from the theoretical solutions, emphases will be given to the numerical solvability of the conditions. Most control and filtering synthesis approaches available in the literature rely on the ideal assumption that there is a continuous flow of measurement signals with infinite precision. However, perfect communication is not always possible in industrial systems. Therefore, to provide the derived results with a more realistic platform aiming for a wider scope of applications, especially for those systems operating under networked environments, important features such as control and sensing under limited capacity and imperfect measurement will be incorporated in the design approaches. By considering signal quantization and stochastic loss/degradation of measurement data in the feedback loop, performance-based constrained synthesis results will be obtained through a stochastic absolute stability formulation. Several practical features on the intermittent disruption based on Markov transitions with dwell time will be studied. State-of-the-art techniques will be employed to minimize the conservatism of the mathematical conditions to be established. The theories and techniques developed in this project will be useful for designing control systems operating under less ideal situations. These results will considerably narrow the gaps between theories and applications, and offer more powerful control systems with higher reliability. 工程中的動態系統需要持續地進行調節以保證穩定性、可操作性和最優性等。為了滿足對控制系統的高精度和魯棒性能所提出的前所未有的要求，控制器必須提供足夠強的增益以便及時進行回應。只要是控制增益超出了正常的工作區間，任何物理控制器都要受到飽和非線性的約束。諸如執行器/感測器受到的飽和約束或者狀態的有界約束乃是控制系統受到的諸多自然物理約束的代表。這些控制約束通常對系統的可控性和穩定性施加了不可忽略的限制，更不必說引起閉環系統性能的下降。有鑑於此，控制科學家在過去的若干年中為了處理有限維系統中的此類約束而付出了大量的努力。但是，這些現有的結果並不能直接用於可用泛函微分方程描述的大量重要的物理和社會經濟過程，例如記憶材料的熱傳導、葡萄糖-胰島素的調節和商品價格的波動等。在本項目中，我們將拓展時間反轉系統方法並建立新的方法來克服存在的技術性困難，並建立受約束的滯後型和中立型泛函微分系統的能控性/可穩性結果。諸如漸近零能控性和區域能控性等問題將是構成本項目的基礎部分。除了理論結果之外，本項目亦重視所提出的條件的數值可解性。 幾乎所有現存文獻中的控制與濾波綜合問題都是基於量測信號是帶有無限精度和連續的基礎之上。但是，在工業系統中，理想的通訊並不總是可能的。因此，為了使得提出的理論成果在現實平臺上有更為廣闊的應用，特別是可用於那些工作在網路環境中的系統，一些重要的特徵(如具有有限容量和不完備量測的控制與測量問題)將在設計過程中做充分的考慮。通過考慮信號的量化和反饋回路中量測資料的隨機丟失/退化，利用隨機絕對穩定性方法解決基於性能指標的受約束控制系統的綜合問題。多種基於帶有駐留時間的馬爾可夫轉移的間歇中斷特徵將得到深入的研究。提出的數學條件其的保守性亦將利用最新的研究方法使得極小化。本項目提出的理論和方法將在工作於非理想情形下控制系統的設計中起重要的作用。這些結果將顯著地縮小理論與應用的差距，並更有效地提供具有更可靠的控制系統。

714011.label: Realisation of objectives
714011.value: All the objectives have been achieved. The details are listed below. Semi-global stabilization with an input delay and a constraint on the energy of its input has been investigated. A parametric Lyapunov equation based L2 low gain feedback approach has been developed for a linearized model of the relative motion in the orbital plane of a spacecraft. The problem of leader-following consensus of a linear multi-agent system with input saturation on a switching network has also been investigated. Low gain feedback based distributed consensus protocols have bene developed. Under the assumptions that each agent is asymptotically null controllable with bounded controls and that the network is connected or jointly connected; semi-global leader-following consensus of the multi-agent system can be achieved and the results have also been extended to semi-global observer-based leader-following consensus. Luenberger observer-based consensus control has also been considered. Novel stability results concerning functional differential systems have been developed. A new criterion for checking the global asymptotic stability of fixed-point state-space digital filters with time-varying delay and overflow arithmetics has been obtained. A significant approach to obtain delay-dependent stability with time-varying delays has been established, which is based on the observation that the positive definiteness of a chosen Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional does not necessarily require all the involved symmetric matrices to be positive definite. Moreover, based on the idea of partitioning the delay interval into non-uniform subintervals, new Lyapunov-functionals are established and an optimal partitioning method has been proposed. For synthesis of networked control systems (NCSs), a number of results have been produced. A delay compensation control approach has been proposed to actively compensate the network-induced delay in Markovian jump linear system framework. A probabilistic approach has been proposed to study the modeling, stability, and stabilization problems for NCSs with simultaneous random network communication delay and data dropout. Predictive control synthesis problem for constrained feedback control systems with both missing data and quantization have been completed by introducing a missing data compensation strategy and an augmented Markov jump linear polytopic model. Additional conditions to satisfy the input constraint in the presence of multiple missing data are also incorporated into the synthesis. The H∞ control problem for a class of discrete time-varying nonlinear systems with both randomly occurring nonlinearities and fading measurements over a finite-horizon has been studied. Robust quantized output feedback control problems have been considered for uncertain discrete-time systems with time-varying delay and saturation nonlinearity.

714011.label: Major findings and research outcome
714011.value: Semi-global stabilization techniques for functional differential systems are developed under null controllability assumption and performance constraints. Under the null controllability with vanishing energy, the parametric Lyapunov equation based L2 low gain feedback is adopted to solve the problem [1]. For the leader-following consensus of multi-agent systems with each agent having input saturation, Low gain feedback based distributed consensus protocols are developed. It is established that, under the assumptions that each agent is asymptotically null controllable with bounded controls and that the network is connected or jointly connected, semi-global leader-following consensus of the multi-agent system can be achieved [3]. Observer-based schemes are also developed [4, 7]. The project has produced new and significant results on stability criteria for functional differential equations arising from different control system application settings. A new insight into the delay-dependent stability for time-delay systems is developed to give improved delay-dependent asymptotic stability conditions [10,12]. Multi-bound-dependent stability criterion for fixed-point state-space digital filters using overflow arithmetics is established [5]. The problem of stability analysis for continuous-time/discrete-time systems with interval time-varying delay is studied based on the idea of non-uniform delay partitioning and stability conditions are proposed with the optimal partitioning method solved via genetic algorithm [11]. The sampling-interval-dependent stability of linear sampled-data systems with non-uniform sampling is established [17]. During the investigation of stability characterization using matrix equations, various results on the existence of positive definition solutions have been derived [2, 8]. Regarding synthesis, for systems with multiple input delays, a Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional which results in a condition with solvability equivalent to the asymptotic stability of the delay-free linear system induced from the predictor feedback control system [9]. Focusing on measurement imperfections and limited capacities, networked control system (NCS) is considered. A delay compensation control approach is proposed to actively compensate the network-induced delay in Markovian jump linear system framework [6]. A robust predictive control synthesis approach involving data missing, quantization, and recovering probabilities is developed by minimizing an upper bound on the expected value of an infinite horizon quadratic performance objective at each sampling instant [13]. A probabilistic approach is proposed to stabilize NCS with simultaneous random network communication delay and data dropout [14]. The H∞ control problem is solved for a class of discrete time-varying nonlinear systems with both randomly occurring nonlinearities and measurements transmitted through a modified stochastic Rice fading channel [15]. Quantized output feedback for time-delay systems with saturation nonlinearity is also tackled [16].

714011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
714011.value: Amongst the many potential applications and extensions of the results developed in the project, there are two areas where the results can be further developed (a) Nonlinear systems represented by Takegi-Sugeno fuzzy models have been extensively studied for control. It is a broad area where the results developed in the project may be extended. However, instead of the usual standard formulation, polynomial fuzzy-model-based stability and control can be considered for limited capacity and imperfect measurement when operated under a networked environment. The first step will be to develop a general polynomial Lyapunov function. The second step is to tackle the stability and synthesis conditions based on sum-of-squares techniques. (b) Switched systems with saturation is a topic with fairly little research results. In particular, the design of controllers as well as the switching sequence has been a difficult area. Two types of switching can be considered here for input saturation. First, the switching sequence belongs to the Markov type, and second, the switching sequence has a mixed fixed dwell time and Markov jump.

714011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
714011.value: Dynamic systems in engineering require constant regulation to ensure stability, operability, and optimality. To meet the ever-increasing demand for high accuracy and robust performance, controllers have to provide sufficient control gain that can be delivered instantly. However, physical controllers always suffer from saturation whenever the control gain is beyond the normal operating range. Network communication imperfections such as delay and packet loss have severely limited the performance of control systems. In this project, we have obtained stability characterization and stabilization results for functional differential systems under such constraints and imperfections. Semi-globalization control techniques have been developed to solve control problem with input delay and saturation, as well as consensus of multi-agent systems. Novel stability criteria for delay systems have been derived for fixed-point state-space digital filters using overflow arithmetics and sampled-data systems. These results are of low conservatism and widely applicable due to their generality. For networked control systems under limited capacity and imperfect measurements, we have provided new models which take into consideration of the signal delay, packet dropout probabilities, and the fading channel characteristics. Moreover, model predictive scheme and static output feedback control with quantizers have been established for minimizing transmission cost.

714311.value: To design the first distributed approximation algorithm for the minimum latency broadcast scheduling (MLBS) problem.
