714311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
714311.value: 我们目前居住的环境正在被越来越多的传感器节点所监控，正因为如此，无线传感器网络变成了一个非常重要的研究课题。在本项目中，我们研究无线传感器网络中一类非常基础的操作--数据查询。数据查询的一个简单例子就是询问当前传感器网络所监控的环境中最高温度是多少。本项目的研究问题是：怎样设计一个低延迟和低能耗的数据查询算法。数据查询的第一个步骤是基站节点Sink首先向网络中所有其它节点广播所要进行的查询函数，然后这些节点以聚集方式将所得数据传回基站节点。大体来说，一共有两类数据查询函数：（1）具有分布式或者代数性质的查询函数，譬如求最大值，最小值，计数，求和或者求平均值；（2）整体性查询函数，譬如求中位数，求不同值的个数和求众数（最常出现的数）。对于那些具有分布式或者代数性质的查询函数，可以在数据查询过程中进行一种网内(in-network)数据操作，但是对于整体性查询函数，这种网内数据操作并不适用，取而代之的是基站节点先需要收集所有网络节点中的原始数据（数据汇集操作）。这种数据汇集操作会导致“能量空洞”问题，也就是越靠近基站的节点会越早消耗所有能量，从而过早死亡。 本项目中研究的数据查询问题可以被细分成如下三个子问题：（P1)设计一个高效的广播算法；(P2)对具有分布式和代数性质的数据查询函数设计高效的数据聚集算法；(P3)对整体性查询函数设计高效的数据查询算法，并且该算法要能有效克服甚至避免"能量空洞"问题。我们的目标是要设计分布式算法，并且要假定每个节点只能知道有限邻域信息。以上P1和P2问题是数据查询延迟优化问题，而P3不仅考虑数据查询延迟还要考虑能量优化。此外，所设计的算法必须要具有最坏性能保证并且要优于当前最好的算法。本项目所采用的是一种更为实际的无线干扰模型，即物理干扰模型或者称作SINR模型。近些年的研究结果表明，相比于传统的基于图的干扰模型，这种物理干扰模型可能大幅提高网络吞吐率。而那些基于图的干扰模型因为没有很好刻画实际无线干扰，会导致很多无线消息需要重新传递。本项目的P3问题也是第一个基于物理干扰模型的解决"能量空洞"问题的尝试。本项目会在一个真正的无线传感器网络试验床中实现所有提出的分布式算法，这也是本项目的第四个研究目标（问题P4)。该算法实现操作要和清华大学合作完成。

714311.label: Realisation of objectives
714311.value: We have achieved 100% of the first three objectives. For the last objective (implementation of our algorithms in a real wireless sensor network), we managed to get some partial results, but because of some major change in circumstances that took place in our partner institution (Tsinghua's Institute of Interdisciplinary Information Sciences), we could not continue our implementation and experiments in the final months of our project. We thought about building our own here in HKU, but the budget simply wouldn't allow that. Nevertheless, we still think our project has been successful as our theoretical results have attracted a fair amount of attention in the international community.

714311.label: Major findings and research outcome
714311.value: Our major findings and outcome can be summarized by the papers we published: (1) a randomized distributed approximation algorithm for the local broadcasting problem with approximation ratio O(log n) under the SINR model [DCOSS2012]; (2) a randomized distributed algorithm with worst case performance guarantee for the multi-message problem [SIROCCO2012]; (3) a randomized distributed algorithm for the multi-message broadcast problem in single-hop networks with a O(k+log n) time guarantee (k messages, n nodes) [WWIC2012]; (4) we show that multiple-message broadcasting can be finished in O(log k * loglog k) time with Theta(n) orthogonal channels [WASA2012]; (5) the first distributed algorithm under the SINR model with scheduling latency O(K), where K is the logarithm of the longest link length over the shortest link length [AHN2014]; (6) the first deterministic distributed algorithm with latency O(D+Delta*log n), where D is the network diameter, Delta is the network degree and n is the number of network nodes [TAMC2012]; (7) for arbitrarily given topologies, such as the directed acyclic network and the tree topology, we analyzed the problem hardness and give both heuristic and approximation algorithms [JOIN2011, Adhoc-Now2012]; the first data collection algorithm based on our proposed Mobile Aerial Sensor Network (MASN), which meets both low collection latency and the low node memory requirement [Infocom2013]; (8) efficient distributed algorithms for information exchange in multi-channel, single-hop networks [JCO2014]; (9) a near-optimal asynchronous blind rendezvous algorithm for cognitive radio networks [SECON2013]; (10) algorithms for oblivious rendezvous in cognitive radio networks [SIROCCO2014].

714311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
714311.value: There is a lot that can be done especially when considering a special kind of wireless networks - cognitive radio networks (CRNs) which are becoming more practically feasible these days due to changes in regulations. In a CRN, links are transient, and so is the topology. This takes our original models, where everything is more or less static, to the next level, and hence it would present many challenges to distributed algorithm design.

714311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
714311.value: We have successfully developed a series of algorithms for carrying out information exchange in a wireless network where interference due to simultaneous transmissions could seriously affect the operation of the network. Our algorithms are shown to be optimal or mostly optimal in the theoretical sense (and backed by simulation results), of which some of them might be applicable to real life operations of wireless networks after some tuning. To really try them out in real networks however would require another project and additional funding. We have also extended some of our work to a relatively new type of networks - cognitive radio networks, which adds significance to our theoretical results as these networks are becoming more and more real.

714811.label: Project Title(Chinese)
714811.value: 鐳射激發螢光及粒子成像測速技術對生物絮體在水中變形和傳質的研究

714811.label: Project Objectives
714811.value: To investigate the deformable feature and shape change of individual bio-flocs in a sheared water flow using the advanced visualization-imaging technique of particle image velocimetry (PIV); To determine the importance of continuous shape change of bio-flocs, in comparison with molecular diffusion and internal permeation, to the mass transport for individual bio-flocs in water using the PIV and laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) techniques; To develop a comprehensive model to describe the material transport dynamics for bio-flocs accounting for the fractal feature and biological property of the flocs and the hydrodynamics of the shear flow condition in both wastewater treatment bioreactors and natural waters.
rows: To investigate the deformable feature and shape change of individual bio-flocs in a sheared water flow using the advanced visualization-imaging technique of particle image velocimetry (PIV);

To determine the importance of continuous shape change of bio-flocs, in comparison with molecular diffusion and internal permeation, to the mass transport for individual bio-flocs in water using the PIV and laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) techniques;

To develop a comprehensive model to describe the material transport dynamics for bio-flocs accounting for the fractal feature and biological property of the flocs and the hydrodynamics of the shear flow condition in both wastewater treatment bioreactors and natural waters.

714811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
714811.value: In biological wastewater treatment, microorganisms used in bioreactors are in the form of large aggregates, or bio-flocs. Molecular diffusion is considered as the main mechanism of substance transfer into individual bio-flocs. Due to the slow rate of diffusive transport, mass transfer limitation is often regarded as a primary limiting factor to the capacity and performance of biological treatment. However, in previous theoretical analyses and experimental studies, microbial flocs have been treated as rigid objects each with a fixed shape and volume. In actuality, bio-flocs are self-similar fractals with a highly porous and branch-like structure. Other than rigid objects, biological flocs suspended in water can be rather soft in structure and flexible in shape. Continuous shape change of bio-flocs in a sheared or turbulent flow would effectively enhance the material transport between the flocs and surrounding fluid. However, the deformable feature of bio-flocs has not been previously addressed, and the importance of continuous shape change to the mass transport of bio-flocs has not been recognized. The project is proposed to investigate the shape change of bio-flocs in water and its role in material transport for bio-flocs in a sheared environment. In theoretical study, a model will be developed to describe the rate of mass transport brought about by continuous shape change of bio-flocs. Using the dimensionless Sherwood number, the importance of shape change to material transport will be compared with diffusion and internal permeation. In experimental work, the advanced visualization-imaging technique of particle image velocimetry (PIV) will be employed to analyze the shape change details of bioflocs under different flow conditions. Moreover, the laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) technique will be used to directly determine the rates of different mass transport mechanisms for individual bio-flocs, including diffusion, internal convection and continuous shape change. Based on the theoretical analysis and experimental findings, a comprehensive model will be developed for the mass transport of bio-flocs accounting for the hydrodynamics of the shear flow and the fractal property and deformable feature of flocs. The research findings will greatly advance our understanding of the mass transport behavior of biological flocs in wastewater treatment systems and in natural waters. The improved understanding is essential to the development of new treatment technologies, such as use of soft biomass carriers to improve sludge-effluent separation and treatment efficiency. The study is also important to the understanding of the vertical transport of organic carbon by biological aggregates in ocean. 在廢水生物處理中，生物反應器中的微生物通常以聚集體或者生物絮體的形態存在。過去認為分子擴散是單個生物絮體中傳質的主要方式。由於擴散傳遞的傳遞效率很低，傳質限制也就因此被認為是影響微生物處理廢水能力和系統運行狀況的主要限制因素。在過去的理論分析和實驗研究中，都把微生物絮體設定為具有固定形狀和體積的剛性物體。但事實上，微生物絮體不但具有自相似的分形特征，還具有高度多孔和大量分支狀的結構。也就是說，在水中懸浮的微生物絮體並不應該是剛體，而是可以變形的柔軟物體。在剪切流或湍流中，柔軟微生物絮體連續地變形可以有效促進其與周圍液體之間的質量傳遞。但是到目前為止，微生物絮體的這種可變形特性還未有報道專門闡述，微生物絮體通過連續變形來促進質量傳遞的方式也還沒有得到認識。 本課題將主要研究水中微生物絮體的連續變形，以及這種變形在剪切流環境中對微生物質量傳遞的作用。在理論研究部分，將建立模型來闡述傳質率與微生物絮體的連續變形的關系。模型利用無量綱的舍伍德數，對比變形、擴散和內部滲透對質量傳遞的重要性。在實驗研究部分，先進的可視化成像技術——粒子成像測速（PIV），將被用來研究微生物絮體在各種流態中的形變細節。此外，鐳射激發熒光技術將被用來直接測定單個微生物絮體的傳質率（指包括擴散，內部對流和連續變形引起的總傳質率）。基於以上理論研究和實驗結果，將會建立和發展包括剪切流的水動力學、絮體的分形特性和可變形特性的微生物絮體傳質的完整模型。這項研究將顯著增強我們對廢水處理系統中以及自然水體中微生物絮體傳質的認識，這種認識的進步將有利於我們發展新的廢水處理技術，比如，我們可以根據此研究結果，選用柔軟的微生物載體來促進泥水分離和處理效率。這項工作同時也對理解海洋中有生物聚集體參與的有機碳的垂直遷移具有重要意義。

714811.label: Realisation of objectives
714811.value: • All research objectives have been well achieved. Following the proposal, a flow chamber with a section of variable cross-section areas was specifically fabricated to create a shear-flow condition for investigating the deformable features of fractal aggregates and bioflocs. By varying the flow rate through the flow chamber, different levels of the velocity gradients can be generated. The PIV system used for the laboratory study consisted of a high-speed CCD camera, a laser illumination setup and an image analysis system. Bioflocs and flow tracer particles suspended in water could be well illuminated by the laser sheet for the CCD camera. • The PIV recording of the bioflocs in the variable flow region provided a direct proof for the deformable features of the flocs. Image analysis using MATLAB was able to characterize the detailed shape change of the bioflocs. To quantify the irregular shape of fractal bioflocs, a porous ellipsoid model was established based on the least squares criterion method. The quantitative results indicated a positive relationship between the degree of floc deformation and the hydrodynamic shear exerted on the flocs. • For a single biofloc with a soft and porous structure, it would easily change its shape and volume to conform the hydrodynamic stress. During this course, liquid can be forced out of the compressed void space or into the expanded void space within the floc, resulting in a considerable liquid and material exchange. Thus, a more comprehensive model for mass transport process in bioflocs was established accounging for molecular diffusion, internal permeation and shape deformation. It is the first time to introduce shape change as an important mechanism for the mass transport of bioflocs in bioreactorst. According to the improved mass transport model, the mass transfer rate within bioflocs is closely related to the hydrodynamic conditions. • The LIF technique was employed to verify the impact of the shape deformation of bioflocs on the mass transport process. With a fluorescent dye and the LIF, material transfer through individual bioflocs could be visualized and quantified. When bioflocs saturated with the dye solution passing through the flow chamber, fluorescent dye would release into the surrounding water and excited by laser, which was recorded by the CCD camera. The mass transfer rate for deforming flocs subjected to shear flow can be greatly enhanced comparing to the stable flow, demonstrating the importance of shape deformation on the mass transport process for bioflocs.

714811.label: Major findings and research outcome
714811.value: • The PIV technique was employed to study the influence of the flow environment on the deformation behavior of individual bio-flocs. The shape change of the activated sludge (AS) flocs during a flow reversal in the observatory chamber was clearly observed (Ren et al., 2013; Xiao et al., 203; Sun et al., 2015). In the acceleration and deceleration flows, the fluid drag force exerting on the soft flocs led to obvious shape changes according to the PIV observations. • A variable flow, i.e. a contraction flow followed by an expansion flow, was generated to determine the effect of the hydrodynamic shear on the degree of floc deformation (Sun et al., 2015). Three flowrates were performed for the floc deformation experiments, resulting in velocity gradients, i.e. du/dz, of 9.4, 5.7, 3.0 s-1, along the centerline of the flow chamber. The experimental results indicated that the bioflocs were elongated in the contraction flow because of the hydrodynamic force, which tended to recover in the flow expansion region. The shape of the AS flocs changed by 18%, 13% and 5% for the three velocity gradients, respectively. It indicates that even weak velocity gradients would lead to a certain degree of shape change for bioflocs. • In addition, this research identified the importance of the continuous shape change to the mass transfer of large bioflocs in water (Ren et al. 2014, Sun et al., 2015). LIF, a spectroscopic method used for detection of selective species and flow visualization, was applied to examine the influence of shape change on the mass transfer rate for AS flocs. The clear LIF observation provided a visible proof for the enhancement of mass transfer rate for bioflocs in the sheared flow compared to the stable flow where molecular dominates the transport process. Image analysis shows that the rate of material exchange rate for flocs in variable flow could be up to 70 times higher than that of flocs in the stable flow. • A more comprehensive model for mass transport process in bioflocs was developed that accounts for shape deformation, internal permeation and molecular diffusion. For deformation ratio of 18%, mass transfer rate driven by deformation would be one order of magnitude higher than molecular diffusion, and 3 times higher than internal permeation. The shape deformation plays a dominant role in the overall material exchange process in bioflocs, particularly for larger flocs with lower diffusivity.

714811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
714811.value: • The PIV and LIF techniques developed in this research could be utilized to study the mass transport process of granular sludge in wastewater treatment (Xiao et al., 2012; Li et al., 2013). Granular sludge technology has been recognized as a potential alternative to the conventional AS technology due to its better settlability, resistance to toxicity and shock loading. With a compact structure, mass transfer rate is considered as a primary limitation to the capability and performance of bio-granules. In fact, bio-granules are highly porous with deformable shape other than a rigid object. The rate of mass transport driven by shape deformation can be determined following the method developed in this study. • Suspended biofilm carriers can achieve higher pollutant removal rates per unit reactor volume. The research findings in this study would help the selection and evaluation of biofilm carriers. Carriers with deformable and flexible structure would enhance the material exchange efficiency between the biofilm layer and fluid. Besides, flexible shape of the carriers can reduce the damage of biofilms by the frequent collision in bioreactors. The stability and efficiency of biofilm system can be advanced.

714811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
714811.value: Aggregates of activated sludge play a pivotal role in the transport and removal of particulate pollutants in biological wastewater treatment. However, mass transport mechanisms in the aggregates have not been well understood. Besides molecular diffusion, shape deformation could be a key factor for bio-flocs, which has not been previously recognized. In this project, the influence of the hydrodynamic conditions on the shape change of bioflocs was investigated by employing an advanced flow visualization technique of particle image velocimetry (PIV). With the high-speed imaging technique at a microscopic scale, detailed changes of biofloc in shape were clearly observed and quantitatively analyzed. The results indicate that bioflocs would easily change their shape to conform the hydrodynamic shear stress. As the fluid shear increased, the deformation degree of flocs would increase. Laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) technique was firstly employed to determine the mass transfer rate driven by the shape change of the bioflocs. LIF records provided a direct proof of the expected enhancement in mass transfer rate. The findings will lead to a better understanding and modeling of the mass transport process in bioflocs and help engineers to improve the design and operation of biological process in water and wastewater treatment.

715111.label: Co - Investigator(s)

715111.label: Project Objectives
715111.value: To examine how the magnitude of dimensions of innovation culture (creativity, attitude to change, vision, attitudes to learning, institutions power structure, perceptions of failure and mistakes, communication and tolerance for dissenters) affect the continuum of the ‘innovation-averse’ to the ‘innovation-conducive culture’ in the construction industry. To investigate how the evolutionary change in the meaning of values and norms affect an organization to move away from an innovation-averse culture through encouragement of specific culture dimensions. To identify how the ‘match’ between culture and context – the organization structure-culture fit – secures continuous improvement through sustaining creativity.

715111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
715111.value: Traditional metrics in ‘assessing’ innovation have focused on investment in research and development, and its outputs. However, it is now seen more widely to include hidden innovations, i.e., new business structure/models and innovative solutions to small scale problems which happen ‘under the radar', where the focus on human capital (such as learning, motivation for creativity etc.) and organizational issues (such as culture, climate, reward systems, leadership, empowerment etc.) are essential. Process structure and development of innovation depend on the cultural software of a thematic and spatial concept and the political framework, so, innovation is determined by culture in terms of affective frames of identity, cognitive frames of knowledge and normative sets of values, norms and beliefs. More importantly, learning (including learning from other sectors) and creativity are crucial for an innovation culture where leaders with vision have found to be pivotal. This proposal focuses on the promotion of an innovation culture in the construction sector – one of the drivers of a knowledge society – to advocate innovation creation and diffusion processes taking into account of variances between different sectors. More specifically, the project examines (1) how the magnitude of dimensions of innovation culture (creativity, attitude to change, attitude to risk, attitude to technology, attitudes to learning, institutions, acceptance of failure and mistakes, communication and tolerance for dissenters) affect the continuum of the ‘innovation-averse’ to the ‘innovation-conducive culture’ in the construction industry.; (2) how the evolutionary change in the meaning of values and norms affect an organization to change away from an innovation-averse culture through encouragement of specific culture dimensions; and (3) the ‘match’ of culture to the context – the organization structure-culture fit – thereby securing continuous improvement through sustaining creativity. The methodology involves quantitative approach to refine and verify existing measurement instruments for innovation culture and qualitative approach which adopts the ‘long interview’ method for longitudinal study to investigate the structure-culture fit. Further elaboration of research design is detailed in the proposal. The significance of this study lies in its potentially invaluable contribution to the understanding of innovation in the construction sector, traditionally regarded as a ‘low innovation’ sector in the economy, and sheds light in sustaining continuous improvement through culture change (and fostering positive innovative climate) for innovation. That is important for Hong Kong in the face of challenges to embed ‘sustainable development’ in all sectors of the economy. 社會與科技進步有賴于創新，而傳統量度體系評估創新亦主要關注科技研發(R&D)方面的投資與產出。然而有許多較潛藏隱蔽的創新在進行，如創新的商業機構運作模式、固有問題的創新解決方法等。這些非科技性的「潛創新」關注到人力資源方面的學習能力及創造力等，和組織理論如氛圍、奬勵、領導力、授權等。創新的進程結構和發展有賴於企業管理文化軟件內的一個理念--創新理念。此創新理念能否成為企業發展的導航，也需依賴政治框架將此創新理念溶入企業文化。因此，文化在很多方面決定了創新取向；在感性、理性，和一般客觀性認知的細節上，可固立創新文化的理念，為創新訂立意識方向。有洞察力的領導人應已了解到如何有效地學習（包括從別的行業學習）與發揮創造力對於營造創新文化及可持續發展是至關重要的。 這份研究計劃旨在促進建築行業建立創新文化，為建設知識社會提供動力，並提出創新氛圍的營造與傳播，同時了解不同行業的差異。這個項目具體探討：（一）如何將建築行業轉化成擁有創新文化作動力支持的創新型行業，包括對風險取捨度、抗拒變新度、挫折承受度、尤其對學習效能及創造力作出分析；（二）價值觀與社會規範的逐步發展如何影響一個組織開始關注企業文化因素，從而有效地學習且推行創新文化；（三）組織結構與企業文化的匹配度，如何保證可持續創造性，進而保證企業的持續發展。 研究方法包括定量分析和定性分析。定量分析精煉與驗證了現有創新文化的衡量方法；定性分析採用了縱向研究深度考核結構-文化匹配度問題。這個研究的重要性在於對發展歷來被視為「低創新」的建築行業做出有價值的貢獻，並且闡明通過文化創新變革（形成積極的創新氛圍）保持持續進步。正當香港各行業均面臨可持續發展的挑戰，推行創新對香港建築業是非常重要的。

715111.label: Realisation of objectives
715111.value: In order to examine how the various dimensions of innovation culture, the change in values and norms and the organizational structure-culture fit influence the evolution of innovation culture (objectives 1-3), the project team has conducted a series of systematic review for the context and driving forces of innovation and innovation culture (refer to items 8.2, 8.4, 8.5 and 8.7 in Part C). Based on this platform, a quantitative study is first conducted to investigate innovation culture in the construction industry (refer to item 8.1 in Part C), where a questionnaire survey is distributed to 300 construction professionals from more than 20 construction firms in Hong Kong. The results of linear regression modeling indicate that organizational support to innovation associates positively with innovation culture. However, it is interesting to find that there is no significant linear association between individual tolerance of differences and innovation culture. Curvilinear regression modeling is thus further conducted, which reveals a bell-shaped relationship between individual tolerance of differences and innovation culture. The study results verify existing measurement instruments of innovation culture, which can then be used in forthcoming studies in the construction field. Following the above, the project team moves on to explore some of the factors that influence innovation culture and innovation in construction (objectives 1-2). Since a case study conducted earlier has shown that a climate for innovation that influence championing behaviors amongst project managers would affect innovation outcomes (refer to item 8.3 in Part C), we subsequently conduct another survey study focusing on leadership and innovation climate (refer to item 8.6 in Part C). In this study, 130 valid responses are collected from construction professionals working in contractor firms in Hong Kong. The results of structural equation modelling reveal that innovation culture is related positively to transformational leadership, but negatively to development exchange leadership. In addition to the above leadership studies on innovation, the project team has also investigated the relationship of organizational learning and innovation in the construction industry through a survey where a hundred and forty seven data are collected [for objectives 1-2, refer to item 8.10 in Part C; the manuscript has been submitted to an ASCE American Society of Civil Engineers journal, reviewer’s comments have been received and the project team is currently revising the paper.]. The results support that learning climate, in terms of openness to change, performance-outcome expectation and performance self-efficacy are significant predictors of innovation. The study also indicates that different construction parties are influenced by different learning transfer climate to innovate; in which both clients and contractors are affected by openness to change, but consultants are affected by performance-outcome expectation; and clients are further affected by performance self-efficacy. Success of a construction project, and/or construction innovation often depends on the collaboration between different construction parties, who often operate through different cultural contexts. Their abilities to create and co-create innovation in the cross-cultural project environment are the key in fostering innovation (refer to items 8.8 and 8.9 in Part C). The results of all the above studies suggest the importance of organization structure-culture fit on innovation outcome (objective 3). In view of this, a theoretical model is developed to link innovation culture and structure using information processing theory (refer to item 8.12 in Part C). The match between organization structure and culture facilitates the effectiveness and efficiency of information processing within an organization, which is essential in fostering innovation outcome. Manuscript has been drafted. The project team is now finalizing it. Furthermore, we examine how the match between climate and context enhance innovation in construction (objective 3) by conducting a survey on the interplay of organizational climate and leadership in construction innovation (refer to item 8.11 in Part C). Nearly one hundred and sixty responses are received from construction professionals from client developers, construction consultants and contractors in China. It is found that support for innovation climate plays a significant moderating role on the influences of intellectual stimulation, individualized consideration, and contingent reward leaderships on innovation; and performance self-efficacy climate plays a significant moderating role on the influences of intellectual stimulation and contingent reward leadership on innovation. The manuscript has been submitted to an ASCE journal awaiting for reviewers’ comment.

715111.label: Major findings and research outcome
715111.value: To achieve the 3 objectives, the research team has conducted a series of studies including systematic literature review, case studies (qualitative) and survey studies (quantitative). First, a series of systematic review has been conducted to lay platform for examining the context and driving forces of innovation and innovation culture in the construction sector (for Objectives 1-2; refer to items 8.2, 8.4, 8.5 and 8.7 in Part C). Then, it is found that, amongst the various dimensions of culture, leadership, innovation climate and learning transfer climate affect the continuum of innovation-conducive culture in the construction industry (for Objectives 1-2). A bell-shaped relationship between the innovation climate of individual tolerance of differences and innovation culture is revealed (refer to item 8.1 in Part C). Middle manager’s innovation supporting behaviour is key to foster innovation climate (refer to item 8.3 in Part C). Amongst various types of leadership styles, innovation culture can be predicted positively by transformational leadership while being predicted negatively by development exchange leadership (refer to item 8.6 in Part C). In addition to innovation climate, learning transfer climate has also found to be significant predictors of innovation. Different construction parties are influenced by different learning transfer climate to innovate (refer to items 8.8 and 8.9 in Part C). For instance, clients are affected by openness to change and performance self-efficacy, contractors are affected by openness to change, and consultants are affected by performance-outcome expectation (refer to item 10 in Part C). Hence, to foster success in construction innovation, the interactions between different construction parties, who create and co-create values under different cultural contexts, must be taken into account (refer to items 8.8 and 8.9 in Part C). To continuously foster innovation in construction organizations, it is essential to maintain a fit between innovation culture and the organizational context (for objective 3). Our study results indicate that i) the match between organization structure and culture is essential in fostering innovation outcome because it facilitates the effectiveness and efficiency of information processing (refer to the case study as shown in item 8.12 in Part C); ii) support for innovation climate plays a significant moderating role on the influences of intellectual stimulation, individualized consideration, and contingent reward leaderships on innovation; and iii) performance self-efficacy climate plays a significant moderating role on the influences of intellectual stimulation and contingent reward leadership on innovation (refer to the survey study as shown in item 11 in Part C).

715111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
715111.value: Results of this research project, to certain extent, indicate that different construction parties, such as client developers, contractors and consultants, are influenced by different innovation culture and climate to innovate. It is thus postulated that the culture-climate interactions between construction parties from different organizations play an essential role in fostering innovation outcomes in the sector. Rapid changes in technology and knowledge often force organizations to depend on external resources and skills. Inter-firm co-innovation, in terms of resources, knowledge and capabilities exchange and value co-creation, thus becomes essential to innovation success. Business parties (e.g., construction parties including client developers, contractors and consultant firms), universities and government are the three pillars in the triple helix and the role of culture should be examined thoroughly in the quadruple helix interactions. Central to the triple helix should be the transfer and use of knowledge through intra- and inter-organizational collaboration, intertwined with the fourth helix of culture. Further studies are thus proposed to investigate the non-linear innovation (and knowledge transfer) process within the complex set of organizational ties with overlapping boundaries between organizations involved in n-druple helix culture.

715111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
715111.value: The construction industry is characterized by low levels of innovation, a lack of organizational learning and lack of creative climate for knowledge transfer. The research project thus examined ways of fostering innovation in construction by creating a climate and culture of innovation with a high culture-organization fit that enhances continuous improvement through sustaining creativity. Within an organization, organizational development emphasizes leadership and employee’s skills training and problem solving capabilities. Previous studies often indicated that transformational leadership, in contrast to transactional leadership, is an important determinant of employee’s innovation, however, evidence to this effect in the construction sector has been scarce and inconsistent. To address this issue, our studies have investigated the moderating role of organizational climate, in terms of both innovation climate and learning transfer climate, on the relationships between leadership and innovation in the construction sector. The research project goes beyond individual variables to develop the concept of leadership-innovation climate fit by revealing the intertwining relationships between leadership, organizational climate and innovation in the construction sector.

715211.value: LESThermoChem: 在熱成層下街道峽谷及城市邊界層內的化學污染物運移的大渦模擬

715211.label: Co - Investigator(s)

715211.label: Project Objectives
715211.value: Develop a robust large-eddy simulation (LES) model for the transport of chemically reactive pollutants over urban areas in thermal stratification. Examine the non-linear coupling among urban morphology, temperature stratification, and pollution physics and chemistry. Elucidate the pollutant removal mechanism of urban areas and improve the surface-to-ABL pollutant flux parameterization.

Examine the non-linear coupling among urban morphology, temperature stratification, and pollution physics and chemistry.
Elucidate the pollutant removal mechanism of urban areas and improve the surface-to-ABL pollutant flux parameterization.

715211.label: Realisation of objectives
715211.value: 1. LESThermoChem computer code development The computer code LESThermoChem was developed for the calculation of buoyancy/stratification (using Boussinesq approximation) on the flows/turbulence and the associated pollutant dispersion/chemistry. We performed a series of sensitivity studies, testing the validity of the newly developed computer code. Analogous to isothermal flows, the modeling results revealed the log-law behavior and the characteristic aerodynamic roughness length scales over idealized urban roughness in stratified flows. Moreover, street-level ventilation and pollutant dispersion are largely enhanced by unstable thermal stratification. In view of the enhanced mixing, pollutant chemistry is enhanced as well. We also attempted to decouple the effects of building morphology and thermal stratification on the flow structure. Functional forms for the profiles of wind and temperature were newly developed. 2. Non-linear coupling over urban areas It was reported in our last mid-term progress report (31-3-2013) that the chemically reactive plume dispersion apparently exhibits a non-Gaussian behavior. Afterward, in-depth data analyses were performed to verify the aforementioned hypothesis. We realized that, for a range of background ozone (O3) concentration, the dispersion behavior of nitric oxide (NO) plume can be partitioned into two parts based on the trajectory of plume centerline. A notable drop in O3 is observed below the plume centerline, exhibiting a non-Gaussian behavior. On the other hand, the change in O3 concentration is insignificant (less than 5%) over the plume centerline in which the NO plume dispersion can be estimated by the conventional Gaussian plume model to good accuracy. 3. Pollutant removal mechanism and surface-to-ABL pollutant flux parameterization The characteristic plume dispersion behavior mentioned above partly contributes to the parameterizations of pollutant removal mechanism and surface-to-ABL pollutant flux. Based on the mathematical modeling results, we realized that, in addition to street-level ventilation, pollutant removal and surface-to-ABL fluxes are enhanced by rough urban surfaces. They are roughly proportional to the friction factor and the Richardson number of the flow configuration.

715211.label: Major findings and research outcome
715211.value: A series of sensitivity tests were performed in this project to test the behaviors of street-level ventilation and pollutant plume dispersion in response to urban morphology and ABL thermal stratification. After an in-depth understanding of the flow/turbulence structure, it was found that aerodynamic resistance and thermal stratification are major factors affecting the ventilation and plume dispersion. The street-level ventilation and plume dispersion coefficient can be parameterized by two dimensionless parameters commonly used in fluid mechanics, friction factor and Richardson number, for engineering application. Although chemically reactive pollutants exhibit non-linear, non-Gaussian behavior over rough urban surfaces, the plume dispersion can be parameterized based on the trajectory of plume centerline to good accuracy. These findings serve the skeleton of the parameterizations for ventilation and reactive pollutant plume dispersion.

715211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
715211.value: The aforementioned mathematical scheme of parameterizations paved a foundation for the potential development of a non-computational-fluid-dynamics (non-CFD) model for quick and reliable estimates of ventilation and air quality at street levels in urban areas. Addition studies will be conducted, in particular in the validity and practicality, in order to refine the functional form of the parameterization.

715211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
715211.value: Pollutant dispersion over urban areas are complicated by both urban morphology and atmospheric thermal stratification. As such, the conventional Gaussian plume model for pollutant dispersion must be used with caution. The pollutant distribution is therefore full of complexity if pollution chemistry is considered alongside. Nonetheless, there is a need for innovation in the parameterization of chemically reactive pollutant transport because of the dense population and valuable assets in urban areas. In this project, in-depth diagnoses for the mechanism of street-level ventilation and the dispersion of chemically reactive pollutants were performed. It was found that the aerodynamic resistance and the thermal stratification are two major factors governing street-level turbulence intensities and thus transport processes. Two commonly used dimensionless parameters, friction factor and Richardson number, were then adopted to formulate a quick, reliable parameterization for street-level ventilation and dispersion. The parameterization was extended to chemically reactive pollutants because of the mild drop in concentrations of background pollutants. The findings were then used to serve as a skeleton for the development of a non-CFD model for urban air quality estimates in a timely manner. The outcome will be helpful to safeguard stakeholders in particular for accidental release of harmful gases in urban areas.

715711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
715711.value: Large quantities of historical temporal and spatio-temporal data are becoming available with the advances in hardware and telecommunication technologies. For example, sensing devices that produce streams of readings have become cheap and can be used even in everyday applications. Large-capacity storage devices can accumulate large quantities of temporal and spatio-temporal data. This project will investigate solutions to analysis tasks on large collections of such data. More specifically, we will study interesting extensions of the standard top-k and nearest neighbor queries, which traditionally apply on snapshot data, to timestamped sequences of values or locations. For example, consider the query: find stocks which are in the top-20 in terms of transaction volume for at least 80% of the days in the period May 2010 - September 2010. Such a durable top-k query, which seeks for time-series that are consistently in the top-k for a given time interval could serve as a valuable tool to a financial data analyst. As another application, consider a database that tracks the movements of objects in a city (e.g., cars) and seeks for cars that are consistently close to a pivot object during a given time interval. This query could be used for example by the police who may want to identify suspects that move within a close range from a given pivot suspect. Although there is ample work on evaluating top-k and nearest neighbor queries in (spatio-)temporal databases, to our knowledge, there is little or no prior work that addresses this new interesting class of durable queries. This project aims at filling this gap. A natural way to process such queries would be to evaluate one snapshot query for each time moment within the query time interval and then combine the results. Nevertheless, this solution can be too expensive if the interval contains a large number of timestamps. We seek for efficient and scalable solutions that rely on novel indexing and query evaluation techniques. The project will consist of several phases: (i) formal definition of consistent queries and investigation of the usefulness of their results, (ii) design and implementation of tailored indexing and query evaluation methods, (iii) design and implementation of a system prototype, which answers durable queries and presents their results to the user, (iv) experimental evaluation of the performance and scalability of the suggested methods. We believe that the outcome of this project with bring significant advancements to the area of (spatio-)temporal database management. 由於硬件及電訊技術的發展，大量的歷史時態和時空數據正變得可用。例如，那些產生讀入流的傳感設備已經變得便宜，可以用於日常的應用，而大容量存儲設備則可用於累積這些大量的時態和時空數據。本項目將要研究針對此類大量數據的分析任務的解決方案。更具體地說，我們將要研究標準top-k查詢和最近鄰查詢在數值或位置的時間序列上的有趣擴展，而這些查詢在傳統上通常只應用于快照數據。例如，考慮如下的查詢：找出2010年5月至9月期間交易量在80%以上的日子里都位列前20的股票。這類在給定的時間區間中查找那些持續位列top-k的時間序列的“持久性top-k查詢”可以作為金融數據分析師的重要工具。作為另一個例子，考慮這樣一個數據庫：它記錄城市中物體（例如車輛）的運動并在給定的時間區間中查找那些始終靠近某個目標物體的車輛。這樣的查詢可被諸如警察之類的人員用來識別出那些接近目標物體的嫌疑對象。 儘管目前在時態（空）數據庫的top-k和最近鄰查詢方面已有不少工作，但據我們所知，還沒有什麽工作能處理這一新型的持久性查詢。本項目旨在填充這一研究空白。處理這類查詢的一個自然方法是對查詢時間間隔中的每一個時刻執行一次快照查詢，然後再合併結果。但是，當查詢時間間隔包含大量的時刻時，這一解決方案的代價會過於高昂。我們依靠新穎的索引和查詢求值技術來尋求高效和可擴展的解決方案。本項目包含如下幾個階段：（1）持久性查詢的形式化定義及其結果的有用性調研；（2）定制索引和查詢求值方法的設計和實現；（3）系統原型的設計和實現，該系統回答持久性查詢并將結果呈現給用戶；（4）新方法性能和可擴展性的實驗評估。我們相信本項目的結果將能夠極大地推動時態（空）數據庫這一領域的發展。

715711.label: Realisation of objectives
715711.value: We have published one journal paper (Durable Queries over Historical Time Series Data, TKDE 2014) which presents our development of indexing and query evaluation techniques for durable queries over historical time series data. In this paper, we present and compare algorithms for evaluating durable top-k queries. Among them an approach based on precomputed rankings prevails. We tested the methods on real-life time-series data (like stock and weather data) and demonstrate the usefulness of the query. We also present an extension for multi-dimensional top-k search (i.e., NN search). This publication include the main results of the project. The project objectives 1 and 2 were achieved. Although the student who mainly worked on the project (Hao Wang) started the implementation of the system prototype (objective 3), it was not completed and released in the end because the student graduated and was experiencing personal problems during the last year before his graduation which prevented him from concentrating on the work. During the course of the project we published a number of works that are directly related to the project and its objectives. Publication "Efficient All Top-k Computation: A unified solution for all top-k, reverse top-k and top-m influential queries" (TKDE 2013) extends our work on the computation of multiple top-k queries in batch. It reveals an interesting observation that reverse top-k queries can also be accelerated by our framework. Publication "Size-l Object Summaries for Relational Keyword Search" (PVLDB 2011) applies top-k search to find a set of tuples in a relational join graph which have high importance in describing a given data subject. This publication is a side-product of the project, as it applies ideas from top-k search to improve the quality of presenting local information from the graph. Conference publication "Efficient Notification of Meeting Points for Moving Groups via Independent Safe Regions" applies aggregate top-k search to find the optimal meeting point for a set of moving users and maintain this point as the users are changing positions on a map. Thus, "durable" meeting points over time are identified and continuously updated as the data change. In summary, we objectives 1 and 2 have been achieved completely, while objective 3 was partially achieved. We plan to continue working toward completing the system and eventually release it.

715711.label: Major findings and research outcome
715711.value: We developed and compared algorithms for evaluating durable top-k queries. Among them an approach based on precomputed rankings prevails. We tested the methods on real-life time-series data (like stock and weather data) and demonstrate the usefulness of the query. We also present an extension for multi-dimensional top-k search (i.e., NN search). For durable top-k queries, we proposed a framework, which exploits time series smoothness to reduce query costs. For durable NN search, we developed a novel solution, which indexes the query space and avoids unnecessary snapshot k-NN queries. By experimentation with both real and synthetic data, we showed that the proposed methods are very efficient compared to naive alternatives and the previous state-of-the-art. Please refer to publication "Durable Queries over Historical Time Series Data" for more details. Durable top-k queries are a special case of multiple top-k queries. We extended our work on durable top-k queries to support the efficient computation of multiple top-k queries in batch. An interesting observation of our results is that reverse top-k queries can also be accelerated by our framework. Please refer to publication "Efficient All Top-k Computation: a unified solution for all top-k, reverse top-k and top-m influential queries". We also studied the application of aggregate top-k search to find the optimal meeting point for a set of moving users and maintain this point as the users are changing positions on a map. Thus, "durable" meeting points over time are identified and continuously updated as the data change. This is also a special application of durable top-k search in a multi-dimensional space. Please refer to publication "Efficient Notification of Meeting Points for Moving Groups via Independent Safe Regions" for more details.

715711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
715711.value: The system prototype (objective 3) is not yet finished. We plan to complete and release it soon. We intend to use it to collect user feedback and further support the use and importance of durable queries. The application of durable search in additional applications (especially for multi-dimensional data) will also be explored in the future.

715711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
715711.value: In this project we have studied the problem of finding objects with durable quality over time in historical time series databases. For example, a sociologist may be interested in the top 10 web search terms during the period of some historical events; the police may seek for vehicles that move close to a suspect 70 percent of the time during a certain time period and so on. Durable queries can be viewed as natural extensions of the standard snapshot top-k and NN queries to timestamped sequences of values or locations which have been extensively studied in previous work. We developed efficient and scalable algorithms for the durable top-k and NN queries, based on novel indexing and query evaluation techniques. Our experiments show that the proposed algorithms outperform previous and baseline solutions by a wide margin. We also partially developed a system prototype, which will be used to collect user feedback and confirm the value and utility of durable search.

716011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
716011.value: The building sector is the second largest emitter of greenhouse gases (GHGs) in the world, because a large proportion of existing buildings are poor in energy efficiency. To contribute significantly to emission reductions, ineffective building components and systems must be promptly replaced. Yet, the biggest challenge is convincing owners and occupants to take up sustainable actions as any refurbishment works inevitably involve cost and may affect their daily life. A sustainable building refurbishment scheme may fail if it focuses purely on reducing GHG emissions without addressing owners’ and occupants’ demands for keeping both the budget and disruption at acceptable levels. Unfortunately, due to the uniqueness of buildings and the divergent expectations of owners and inhabitants, anticipating the outcomes of a sustainable refurbishment proposal for a building is not easy. If experience accumulated from similar cases could be available for reference, owners and occupants may realise the potential benefits and drawbacks of a sustainable building refurbishment action and hence increase their confidence in adopting a proposal. Case-based reasoning (CBR) which solves new problems by retrieving, comparing and reusing the experience of old cases in a collective manner offers a good potential for modelling the complex and dynamic interactions amongst the building condition, human expectations and emission reductions. Once a seemingly suitable sustainable building refurbishment solution is derived by the CBR model, more detailed analyses can be carried out to establish the extent of reductions in GHGs and the lifecycle cost of the selected scheme before a final decision is made. The aim of this investigation is, therefore, to examine whether CBR is a suitable approach to assist decision-makers in devising pragmatic building refurbishment solutions to reduce the carbon, cost and contention. The research begins with a series of interviews to determine which building systems are most susceptible to GHG emissions and to identify the sustainable buildings refurbishment solutions that are relevant to Hong Kong. Through a series of forums and a questionnaire survey, the factors affecting the selection of sustainable building refurbishment decisions will be identified. Factual data and knowledge will then be captured through case studies. Finally, a CBR model will be built and tested. Through this research, it is envisaged that the reliability and relevancy of solutions for building refurbishment can be improved to meet emission targets as well as the economic and social expectations of owners and occupants. 大部分現存樓宇的能源效率都比較低，這是導致建築業成爲世界上産生溫室氣體第二最高行業的主要原因。爲了顯著減少溫室氣體的排放量，業主應盡快更新較低效能的樓宇部件及設備。然而，此類工程的成本及其對住戶所造成的不便都直接影響業主對不同整修計劃的接受程度。若方案僅以減少溫室氣體排放爲目標而卻忽略業主及住戶對控制工程成本及降低滋擾訴求的重要性，樓宇整修方案定必難以順利實施。但鑒于樓宇的獨特性及業主、住戶的期望有所差别，推測樓宇整修方案的實施結果（包括工程成本及對環境滋擾等）絕非易事。如果有類似案例的經驗作為借鑒，業主及住戶將會更容易瞭解樓宇整修方案的好處及缺點，從而提高其對落實該方案的信心。 案例爲本方法通過對過往案例的反思及綜合比較來汲取經驗教訓進而解决新的問題。該方法在構建一個能按照樓宇狀況，住戶要求及溫室氣體減排等複雜而互相牽引的因素而作出决策之模型具有極大潛力。决策者不單可以對案例模型所衍生的樓宇整修方案對溫室氣體減排程度及壽命周期成本等範疇進行詳細分析，而更可以此作爲最終决策的依據。 本研究旨于查考案例爲本方法是否可以協助决策者建立低碳、低價、低爭議性的樓宇整修計劃。 研究初期， 研究員首先採用訪談模式以辨識與溫室氣體排放有關的樓宇部件及確定適合香港的樓宇整修方案。研究員繼而通過一系列專題研討和問卷調查來確定影響决策者選擇樓宇整修計劃的主要因素，並透過分析案例取得實際數據和經驗。在此基礎上，研究員最終建立案例爲本模型和進行測試。 冀望透過本研究，樓宇整修計劃的可靠性和相關性可大大提高，從而實現低碳、低價、低爭議性樓宇整修計劃的目標。

716011.label: Realisation of objectives
716011.value: Objective 1: Collected carbon and energy data and modelled the data using the life cycle assessment approaches; conducted questionnaire survey with households to understand their energy usage pattern; interviewed experts to understand which building systems deserve greater attention; and conducted case studies to examine the design features of buildings in Hong Kong. Objective 2: Reviewed literatures related to sustainable refurbishment measures; drawn up a list of sustainable refurbishment measures and classified them logical categories; conducted questionnaire survey to determine the most relevant sustainable refurbishment measures for Hong Kong; and deliberated with experts and occupants the practicality of the identified sustainable refurbishment measures. Objective 3: Brainstormed with various stakeholders regarding the factors influencing the selection of sustainable refurbishment options; administered a questionnaire survey to solicit experts and occupants’ views on what would lead to the success of sustainable refurbishment; and developed structural equation models to interpret how human behaviour would influence the success of sustainable refurbishment. Objective 4: Analysed case features by referring to real building cases; interviewed owners and occupants to captured their knowledge related to the input and output parameters; designed the case structure to suitably represent the case features and input / output parameters; and entered the data identified from cases into the case structure. Objective 5: Devised a case-based reasoning framework for sustainable refurbishment; designed the system architecture based on the case-based reasoning concept; invented a social life cycle assessment model for building construction in Hong Kong; developed a new cost model using the fuzzy sets theory to predict the life cycle costs of various sustainable refurbishment options; analysed the business as usual building energy performance of the case buildings using an energy modelling tool called eQuest; compiled a series of formulas for calculating the energy savings induced by various sustainable refurbishment solutions; computed the anticipated energy savings of the case buildings using the identified formulas; representing the knowledge and information as cases; proposed a life cycle sustainability assessment approach to holistically assess the energy, cost and social aspects; and programmed the case-based sustainable refurbishment system using Apache Tomcat, JavaServer Pages and MySQL. Objective 6: Vetted the case structure and parameters by experts; confirmed the results of structural equation model with relevant stakeholders; tested the accuracy of the fuzzy life cycle cost estimation model by experts; presented the case-based sustainable refurbishment model to experts and conducted face validation with those experts; and entered data of case projects into the model for testing.

716011.label: Major findings and research outcome
716011.value: According to the results of a life cycle assessment model using both the end-point and endpoint methods (Journal-7) of ReCipe (Journal-2) and adjusted by local data (Journal-4), the carbon emissions of a public rental housing project amount to 637 CO2e/m2 (Journal-5). This has taken into account the emission-intensive materials like bar reinforcement and concrete (Journal-8). While significant reduction in carbon emitted from building is indispensable, e.g. through a carbon trading scheme (Conference-4), it is difficult to realise that in the construction sector. The major obstacles include a lack of awareness in the market, limited budget and client attitude (Journal-1). As stakeholders do not have sufficient knowledge on emission reduction, they have difficulties selecting suitable low carbon solutions for clients (Conference-1). In Hong Kong, space cooling is a major source for carbon emissions in buildings across different family sizes and income groups (Conference-5). Sustainable refurbishment strategies relevant to Hong Kong can be classified into building services, envelop and layout, renewable energy and user habits (Conference-7). Residents generally favour simple and cost effective sustainable refurbishment solutions like energy efficient appliances, low energy lamps, time switch, motion sensors are favoured by occupants in high-rise residential buildings (Conference-8). Replacing windows with inter-pane glazing systems is not welcomed due to the initial costs and disruptions (Journal-3). It is necessary to address the carbon emissions arising from the common areas (e.g. lift, lighting at corridor, etc.) and private-occupied areas (e.g. space cooling, lighting, behavioural change, etc.) in multi-storey multi-ownership buildings (Journal-11). Depending upon the age and condition of a building and its units, the refurbishment programme of a multi-storey multi-occupant building can be classified into major, cyclical and minor upgrading (Conference-2). For instance, major sustainable refurbishment may include changing the insulation materials, green roof, etc. (Conference-3). Since some refurbishment regimes could affect residents, a social life cycle assessment model was derived (Journal-6). To ensure the social aspect be considered alongside the environmental performance and life cycle costs, a genetic algorithm model was developed for design optimisation (Journal-9). A novel life cycle sustainability assessment model by taking into account the emissions, costs and social aspects was proposed (Journal-10). However, with different types of buildings, it is more effective to learn from previous successful examples. Therefore, a case-based sustainable refurbishment framework for multi-storey building was formulated (Conference-6), and the system architecture of the case-based reasoning system was designed (Conference-9). Finally, the low carbon-cost-contention sustainable refurbishment model was developed and validated (Journal-12).

716011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
716011.value: Some of the research outcomes outlined in the preceding section can be further developed if and when opportunities arise. The most relevant research direction is to extend the case-based reasoning model to different types of existing building types, e.g. commercial centre, office, industrial building, etc., as they should have different emission performance, life cycle costs, regulatory requirements, physical constraints, technical challenges, and user expectations. The case-based reasoning model can also be replicated for the design of new high-rise low carbon buildings as the actual performance of this type of building like the life cycle costs and user behaviour would help drive the development of similar buildings. While social sustainability has attracted increasing attention, it is imperative to examine its implications to new and existing buildings. The findings of this research can pave way for the development of a social life cycle assessment mechanism and a life cycle sustainability assessment framework which are tailored for the Hong Kong situation. Currently, much of the assumptions and data are borrowed from other countries which may not represent the unique culture and expectations of the Hong Kong society. A thorough analysis would help unfold the criteria and measurement required for the abovementioned framework and mechanism.

716011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
716011.value: At COP21 in December 2015, parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change reached an agreement of “limiting global temperature increase well below 2 degrees Celsius” to combat the adverse impacts brought by climate change. While buildings are responsible for around 60-70% of carbon emissions in Hong Kong, a substantial cut in carbon emitted from buildings is the only way to meet the emission reduction target set by the HKSAR Government. This research is, therefore, significant to the society and the Hong Kong context. Nevertheless, as sustainable refurbishment is rather new to average citizens, some may introduce a series of costly measures to renovate their property without even considering whether those measures would bring maximum reduction in carbon emissions and/or cause only little disruption to building owners / occupants while the renovation works are carried out. Should someone be able to share their experience regarding the performance of various sustainable refurbishment solutions, unnecessary misjudgement can be largely avoided. Therefore, building a case-based reasoning model which can store and reuse successful or failure examples to help owners and occupants of building facilities making an informed decision on which are the most suitable sustainable refurbishment solutions is valuable to the society.

716211.value: 基于结构方程模型探讨慢性心血管疾病患者對電子化疾病管理技术接受因素的纵向研究

716211.label: Project Objectives
716211.value: To investigate the antecedent factors affecting acceptance of a computerized self-management technology among patients with chronic cardiovascular disease in Hong Kong. To understand how the effects of the factors on acceptance change over time through a longitudinal study. To model patients’ CHIT acceptance using the technique of latent variable modeling with item parceling. To provide recommendations and strategies for effective design and implementation of patient-focused health technologies that can help create acceptance for the technology and increase the likelihood of implementation success.

716211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
716211.value: 这项研究的目的是:(1)探讨影响香港慢性心血管疾病患者對電子化疾病管理技术的接受因素；(2)通过纵向研究了解这些因素如何随时间而变化；(3)采用结构方程模型项目组合的方法建立病人中心医疗信息技术的接受模型。同时,这项研究也能提供设计和實施該医疗科技的建议和策略,从而提高病患者對該科技之接受度和增加成功實施的可能性。 在这项研究中，病人中心医疗信息技术是指以满足病患者需求为目的,运用网络通讯技术为媒介向病患者提供互动式的医疗信息服务的相关信息技术。该技术适合慢性疾病或其他主要疾病患者在家进行疾病自行管理。目前，病人中心医疗信息技术的运用已成为提高医疗保健质量的一個重要途径和方法。根据有关资料显示，由于该技术为自行管理提供了快速获取丰富多样的医疗服务的途径，从而促进了患者的身体康复。尽管医疗信息技术有许多潜在好处，病患者却沒有普遍接受和经常使用該科技。这是一个非常值得关注的问题，因为病人中心医疗信息技术要发挥其效能的一个基本前提是病患者首先要接受及使用該技术。为了增加該医疗信息技术的成功實施，研究者试图寻求該技术的接受因素。因此，测试這些接受因素成為近年来科研关注的领域。但是，很多现有的相关研究在研究方法存在着局限性，比如, 有限的样本容量，測試接受因素不是研究的焦點,或者測試方向限制於社會人口及部份與健康有關的因素。这些研究不能全面解釋病患者對医疗信息技术所接受的因素。另外，很多研究没有基於任何理论，这可能觸犯錯誤设定模型的問題。 针对这些问题，本研究用系统化的方法探讨更广泛的接受因素—技术、个体、社会变化过程和特殊健康指标在慢性心血管疾病患者中对病人中心医疗信息技术的接受。在这项研究中。最后，通过识别接受因素，医疗保健机构或系统设计师可以积极主动地规划和制定有效的用户界面，营销策略，技术评估和重新设计工具，培训，或在应用前进行其他相关的干预措施。

716211.label: Realisation of objectives
716211.value: All of the four objectives are achieved. For the first objective, Dr. Or carried out a test with 90 chronically ill patients to understand the factors that were associated with how the patients used the technology. A list of factors was identified, such as interface design characteristics and system usefulness. The findings about the factors were presented in the International Symposium of Human Factors and Ergonomics in Healthcare in 2014. For objectives 2 and 3, Dr. Or and his research team collected data to model the acceptance. The model was developed and presented in the 6th International Conference on Applied Human Factors and Ergonomics in July 2015. Also, the quantitative model of acceptance is done, and the research paper manuscript related to the model is composed and submitted to a journal for review. For objective 4, based on what we have found in the works for objectives 2 and 3, we have suggested the strategies in the paper manuscript. Also, two published review studies also provided information regarding the recommendations and strategies for effective design and implementation of patient-focused health technologies that can help create acceptance for the technology and increase the likelihood of implementation success.

717011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
717011.value: Multiferroics (MFs) possess two or more types of order parameters simultaneously that couple the electric, magnetic and elastic responses. The magnetoelectric (ME) coupling of such materials has attracted increasing attention due to possible manipulation of magnetization by applied electric field or polarization by magnetic field. In order to develop new MFs with enhanced ME coupling effect and unique properties; there is an urgent need to improve the understanding of the intrinsic ME coupling mechanisms in MFs. Moreover, it has been found that the increase of interfacial effects of such materials, by reducing the material or component size to nano-scale, would not only significantly increase the ME coupling effect, but also evoke the emergence of many novel properties due to the interactions of the charge, spin, lattice and orbital degrees of freedom at interfaces. Thus, we propose to study interface dominated multiferroic nanostructures (IDMNS), in which the interfacial effect is the dominant factor that modulates various properties of the material. Zero-/one-dimensional nanostructures, heterostructures or superlattices, and combinations of these structures, which possess interfaces that act as coupling medium, are the focus of the proposed study. Despite the fact that some MF materials have been fabricated, IDMNS are still hardly available due to the difficulty of fabrication. Thus, the fabrication method for IDMNS will be evaluated first. Subsequently, by combining the results of first principles calculations and experimental characterization, the components and structures of IDMNS will be optimized for attaining larger ME coupling and other possible unique properties. The interfacial effect will be one of the main focal points of the proposed numerical study, in which a multi-scale modeling framework will be established to investigate the ME coupling behavior of MF nano-composites (MNCS). At nanoscale, the existing mesoscopic phase field method will be modified to make it suitable for evaluating the evolution of domain structure and polarization of the system. At micro-scale, an energy approach will be used to study the interfacial influence on the ME effect of the system. Upon successful completion of the project, the interfacial effects on the ME coupling behavior and the induced novel properties will be better understood both theoretically and experimentally. Moreover, the approach to optimize the IDMNS for maximizing the ME coupling effect and/or other unique properties will also be established. The potential applications of IDMNS, especially in the scope of spintronics and energy storage and conversion devices, will also be explored and developed.

717011.label: Realisation of objectives
717011.value: Research on the magnetoelectric (ME) coupling behavior in multiferroics nanostructures (IDMNS) is still at its early stage. This project provides a better understanding of the interfacial effects on the ME coupling. The key issue in IDMNS is polarization and magnetization to be coupled. The three-dimensional numerical simulations has been carried out based on the determined inhomogeneous elastic solution and the chemical potential at the interfaces. Moreover, the multi-scale modeling framework and the evolution of domain and polarization patterns have been established.

717011.label: Major findings and research outcome
717011.value: (A) For theoretical modeling and numerical simulations, 1. The influence of mechanical and electrical interfacial conditions on the threshold field of ferroelectric nano-thin-films has been studied by employing Ginzburg Landau theory and the phase field method. 2. The influence of flexoelectric effects on magnetic field induced electric polarizations in multiferroic nanocomposite thin bilayer films has been investigated. 3. Ferroelectric control of magnetic domain pattern and domain wall properties has been successfully illustrated using the phase field method. 4. Exploration of the formation of nonlinear buckle-delamination pattern driven by concurrent buckling and interfacial decohesion processes using the phase field method. (B) For experimental studies, 1. Preparation of novel crack-free bulk Al(2)O(3)/Er(3)Al(5)O(12) (EAG) oxide compositeceramics using a modified laser zone remelting technique. The technology has been extended to fabricate the multiferroics materials. 2. Fabrication of BiFeO(3)-CoFe(2)O(4) nanocomposite thin film on SrTiO(3) (STO) substrate via the sol-gel technique and spin coating processing has been successfully carried out. Characterization of the nanostructure and magnetoelectric (ME) coupling has been done.

717011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
717011.value: According to the outcome of this project, the evolution of domain structures and other properties of ferroelectric and ferromagnetic nanostructures can be possibly predicted. The further development of the research will focus on the practical applications as spintronics and energy conversion and storage (eg. hybrid system made by IDMNS for storing hydrogen and hydrogen ions).

717011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
717011.value: In recent years, the magnetoelectric coupling effect in multiferroics has attracted increasing attention due to possible manipulation of magnetization by applied electric field or manipulation or polarization. It may become a promising materials in the filed of energy storage and conversion, eg. a hybrid system made by IDMNS for storing hydrogen may meet the required 9% set by the U.S. DOE. Thus, there is an urgent need to improve the understanding of the intrinsic ME coupling mechanism. This project provides a fundamental study for the ME coupling and unique properties arising from interface-mediated effects, leading to a progress in the potential applications of IDMNS in the scope of spintronics and energy storage and conversion devices.

717111.label: Project Title(Chinese)
717111.value: 在可變訂購成本是凸函數下的庫存控制

717111.label: Project Objectives
717111.value: Fully characterize the optimal inventory control policy for a periodic-review finite-horizon inventory model with convex variable ordering cost under the assumption that there is no fixed ordering cost. Fully characterize the optimal inventory control policy for a periodic-review finite-horizon inventory model with convex variable ordering cost under the assumption that a strictly positive fixed ordering cost is incurred whenever an order is placed. Identify sufficient conditions under which a standard (s,S) policy is optimal for a periodic-review finite-horizon inventory model with convex variable ordering cost. Develop efficient approximation algorithms to solve the period-review finite-horizon inventory model with convex variable ordering cost, and prove the worst case performance bound. Study the period-review infinite-horizon inventory model with convex variable ordering cost, which includes characterizing the optimal control policy, developing approximation algorithms and analyzing their performances. Study the period-review infinite-horizon inventory model where the variable ordering cost consists of two components: (i) a linear function of the order quantity and (ii) an additional cost for any unit exceeding a prespecified quantity q where the unit additional cost is a random variable. We plan to characterize the optimal control policy, develop approximation algorithms and analyze their performances.

717111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
717111.value: 在可持續發展成爲重大挑戰的今天，我們採取各種方案來解決環境問題和能源危機，而這些手段也影響著企業的運營。例如，當企業的能耗或碳排放超出一定範疇時，政府將通過徵收環境稅，進行碳排放量交易，或採用階梯電价等形式，令其支付額外的費用，以降低企業的能耗或碳排放量。但同時，一旦企業的產量或訂貨量超過一定水平，它所面臨的邊際生産或訂購成本將顯著增加，即相應的總成本是產量或訂貨量的凸函數。這就違反了運營管理中的一條常用假設：生產或訂貨成本是產量或訂貨量的綫性函數。 在此項目中，我們將研究可變訂購成本為凸函數的庫存系統，以此來應對環境或能源政策導致的成本結構變更。在前期工作中，我們已完全刻畫了在固定訂貨成本為零時的最優庫存控制策略。當存在固定訂貨成本時，通過分析動態規劃價值函數的某种特性，我們也部分地刻畫了相應的最優庫存控制策略，而價值函數的這一性質也是經典庫存控制文獻中定義的K-凸性的延伸。 同時，我們已確立在某些充分條件下(s,S)策略的最優性，並證明了(s,S)策略在固定訂貨成本趨於無窮時是漸近最優的。基於我們已發現的最優策略的結構特性，我們認為，如果改進傳統的(s,S)策略使其允許多個目标库存量或定購量，這一策略可演化為一種高效率的近似算法，我們也計劃分析它在最壞情況下的性能。 另外，在這項目中，我們還對可變訂購成本為凸函數的庫存模型進行拓展，例如，用無限期模型來分析長遠績效，以及在庫存模型中引入隨機的額外費用以適用於碳排放量交易。 顯然，在庫存系統中考慮凸函數的可變訂購成本是對經典隨機庫存控制的一種順理成章的推廣。它不僅解決了新的環境和能源政策所帶來的挑戰，也適用於所有面臨訂貨成本規模不經濟的決策者。最優策略的結構特性將對庫存管理者提供寶貴的管理理念，而近似算法將在日常運作中給予切實可行的解決方案。與此同時，在這樣的庫存系統下的最佳總成本有助於政策制定者估計新的能源環境政策給企業的帶來額外費用。因此，這一項目還能幫助政策制定者評估不同的能源環境政策，如環境稅與碳排放量交易。此外，在研究最優政策的結構時，我們提出了對經典K-凸性的新的衍生。這一概念也可用於其它設定下的庫存模型並刻畫相應的最優策略。

717111.label: Realisation of objectives
717111.value: The project objectives have been fully achieved. The details are provided as follows: - Periodic-review finite-horizon inventory model with convex variable ordering cost and zero fixed ordering cost: We have characterized the optimal inventory control policy. - Periodic-review finite-horizon inventory model with convex variable ordering cost and fixed ordering cost: We have characterized the optimal inventory control policy, identified the conditions under which a standard (s,S) policy is optimal, developed efficient approximation algorithms, and studied the worst case performance bound. - Period-review infinite-horizon inventory model with convex variable ordering cost: We have characterized the optimal inventory control policy, developed efficient approximation algorithms, and studied the worst case performance bound. - Period-review inventory model with convex variable ordering cost and stochastic additional cost: We have characterized the optimal inventory control policy, developed efficient approximation algorithms, and studied the worst case performance bound. Furthermore, we have also generalized the models proposed in the project in the following two aspects: - The models in the proposal only consider a convex variable ordering cost with two linear pieces. We have studied the generalized models where the convex variable ordering cost may have an arbitrarily number of linear pieces. This generalization allows us modeling diseconomies of scale resulted from overtime pay, multiple sourcing, and etc. - The proposal considers an ordering cost structure with convex variable cost and fixed cost, which essentially reflects economies of scale for low order quantity and diseconomies of scale for high order quantity. The general cost structure capturing this phenomenon is one that is first concave and then convex. Periodic-review inventory models with such an ordering cost have also been studied in this project.

717111.label: Major findings and research outcome
717111.value: This project has led to 1 paper published in Operations Research, 2 papers published in Production and Operations Management, 1 paper published in INFORMS Journal on Computing, and 5 presentations in international conferences. The major findings of the project are summarized as follows: - Finite-horizon model without fixed ordering cost. The optimal inventory policy has been completely characterized. The state space can be divided into 2n intervals, where n denotes the number of linear pieces in the ordering cost function. For each interval, it is optimal to either order up to a specific level or order a certain quantity. - Finite-horizon model with fixed ordering cost. The optimal inventory policy has been completely characterized for the single-period model (c.f. Theorem 1 in Lu and Song 2014). For the multiple-period model, we have identified the important properties of the optimal policy (c.f. Theorem 2 in Lu and Song 2014). Furthermore, the (s,S) policy is optimal under the conditions in Theorem 3 in Lu and Song (2014). A strongly performing approximate inventory policy has been proposed to solve the multi-period model (c.f. Algorithm 1 in Lu and Song 2014). Its computational complexity is much lower than that of the optimal policy. It is consistent with the optimal policy and optimal in various cases (c.f. Propositions 4 and 5 in Lu and Song 2014). In an extensive numerical study, the average performance gap between the approximate and optimal policies is only 0.02% and the worst gap is 1.37% (c.f. Section 5.2 in Lu and Song 2014). - Infinite-horizon model / model with stochastic additional cost. We have the same results as those for the finite-horizon model with fixed ordering cost. - Model with first concave and then convex ordering cost. If the ordering cost is piece-wise linear continuous and the demand is deterministic, the problem can be solved in O(T^(3n)), where T is the number of periods and n is the number of pieces in the ordering cost function. For the single-period stochastic-demand model, there exists a reorder point in the optimal policy, and the optimal order-up-to level is first increasing and then decreasing with respect to the initial inventory. For the multi-period stochastic-demand model, we have developed a strongly performing approximate policy, which is optimal for the single-period model as well as the multiple-period model with convex ordering cost. A worst case performance bound of the approximate policy has also been constructed.

717111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
717111.value: In this research, a new concept named strong (K,c,q) convexity is proposed to analyze the optimal inventory policy for the multi-period model with convex variable ordering cost and fixed ordering cost. An interesting endeavor for future research would be to use this concept or its variants to study other problems with a similar cost structure. One such example is the price adjustment problem. The fixed cost represents the physical cost associated with a price change, and the variable cost represents the managerial cost. It is commonly assumed in the economics literature that the management cost convexly increases with the size of the price adjustment because the decision and internal communication costs are higher for larger price changes. As the price can be either increased or decreased, we may need to generalize strong (K,c,q) convexity to study this problem.

717111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
717111.value: Piece-wise linear convex cost captures diseconomies of scale and has many applications in practice. For example, carbon emission or energy consumption can be discouraged by imposing additional costs when the emission or consumption exceeds a certain level, which may take the form of the carbon tax, the price to purchase carbon credit, or the tiered electricity pricing mechanism. To protect labor rights, labor standards acts all over the world state that employees who work overtime must be paid much more than their standard salary. All these policies and regulations result in a piece-wise convex cost with respect to the production/order quantity. This project studies periodic-review inventory systems in which the variable production/ordering cost is a piece-wise linear convex function of the production/order quantity. We analyze the structural properties of the optimal policies for these inventory models, which provide valuable managerial insights to the decision makers managing such inventory systems. Based on these properties of the optimal policies, we also develop strongly performing approximate policies, which are well-structured and so can be easily implemented in practice. From this aspect, this research also delivers cost-efficient and practical solutions for daily operations.
