717811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
717811.value: The growth of the Internet brings about new software applications whose behaviors are built on individual components (known as services), each of which is selected at runtime among a pool of candidate components provided by different service providers. These applications are known as adaptive service-based software (ASBS). Each involves a program-understandable interface such as a WSDL document, and machine-readable messages typically in XML format. Testing is the most widely practiced activity that assures software quality. Given a large pool of candidate services, a key property of ASBS is its ultra-late binding to a specific subset (which we call a configuration) at runtime. Reconfigurations may take place whenever necessary. A major difficulty in testing is the need to assure any possible configuration among the large pool of services. This is a fundamental challenge to traditional program testing, where only one implementation is tested at a time. We will collect ASBS from open-source repositories, comprehensively study viable mutation operators for ASBS, and conduct a data analysis of the effect of such operators to answer fundamental research questions. The empirical results will be useful not only for the latter part of this project but also other service-oriented research. Another challenge in the quality assurance of ASBS is the need to know when testing can be adequate in the presence of an open-ended number of services. We propose two different approaches: First, based on our research on XPath Rewriting Graph (XRG) patterns, we will develop algorithms to produce new XRG patterns that specify adaptive fault relations. We will organize the XRG patterns into a test adequacy subsumption hierarchy. The second approach involves data mining. We will mine failure correlation strengths of definition-use patterns, design XML similarity metrics that correlate with fault-revealing capability, and develop optimization algorithms that maximize the failure correlation strengths and XML similarities. We will also investigate the efficiency aspect of test case generation. We will construct a prototype system to validate the feasibility of the techniques, and evaluate the techniques by controlled experiments and case studies of industrial-strength applications. This project is innovative in several aspects. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first major project addressing the testing of ASBS. In particular, it is the first work that empirically studies the propagation of reconfiguration faults; tackles the test adequacy for ultra-late binding of adaptive services; and uses XRG and data mining techniques to unveil test adequacy properties. 互聯網的增長帶來新的應用軟件，其行為建立在多個組件（稱為「服務」），每一個都是在運行時，從不同的服務提供者提出的候選組件名單中選擇其一。這種應用程序稱為「自適應基於服務的軟件」（ASBS）。每一個都涉及程序可以理解的接口，如WSDL文檔，以及機器可讀的訊息，通常是XML格式。 測試是軟件品質保證中最為廣泛的活動。ASBS的主要屬性，是在超後期運行時才從候選服務名單中綁定一個特定的子集（稱為「配置」），並隨時可能須要重新配置。因此測試ASBS所面臨的一大困難是必須確保候選服務名單中任何可能的配置。這是一個根本性的挑戰，因為每次傳統的程序測試只能確保其中一項實施。我們將從開源庫收集ASBS，全面研究可行的ASBS突變運算符，並跟據運算符的的效果進行數據分析和回答基本的研究問題。實證結果不僅對此項目有益，還能幫助其他面向服務的研究。 另一個ASBS品質保證的挑戰，是需要知道在不限數量的服務中，什麼時候才有充足的測試。我們提供兩種不同的方法：首先，根據我們對XPath重寫圖（XRG）模式的研究，此項目將開發新的算法來產生XRG模式，從而指定自適應錯誤的關係。我們將把各類XRG模式組織成一個測試充足性的包容層次結構。第二種方法涉及數據挖掘。我們將挖掘定義使用模式的故障相關性，設計與錯誤揭示能力關聯的XML相似性度量，並開發優化算法，令故障相關性和XML相似性能夠最大化。 我們亦會研究的效率方面的測試用例生成。我們將建立一個原型系統，驗證此項目提出的技術的可行性，並通過控制實驗和工業強度的應用案例來評估這些技術。 此項目包括多個方面的創新。據我們所知，這是第一個測試ASBS的大型項目，尤其這是第一項有關重新配置錯誤傳播的實證研究，解決超後期綁定的自適應服務測試是否充足，並使用XRG和數據挖掘技術來顯示測試的充分屬性。

717811.label: Realisation of objectives
717811.value: EMPIRICAL STUDIES ON RECONFIGURATION FAULTS OF ADAPTIVE SERVICES (i) Our empirical studies in [11, 14] reveal that testing adaptive web services is very difficult. External services may evolve without notice. Existing test case prioritization techniques only verify the latest service composition using the not-yet-executed test cases, overlooking high-priority test cases applied before the evolution. We propose "preemptive regression testing" to address the challenges. Our pioneering article [11] was selected as the spotlight paper of the September/October 2015 issue of IEEE Transactions on Services Computing (impact factor 2.365). (ii) Location-based services adapt dynamically to the point of interest. However, location estimation algorithms are inaccurate. Our second paper in IEEE Transactions on Services Computing [8] proposes POI-aware metrics for test case prioritization. Empirical studies show the results to be significantly more stable and effective. (iii) Many web services not only communicate through XML-based messages but also may dynamically modify their behaviors by applying different interpretations on XML messages. In [5, 20], we exploit the insights on the structural similarity of XML-based artifacts between test cases in both static and dynamic dimensions, and propose a family of test case prioritization techniques that selects pairs of test case without replacement in turn. It is the first test case prioritization approach that selects test case pairs. Empirical results show that pairwise prioritization techniques can be more effective than traditional coverage-based techniques. (iv) Existing fault-localization techniques combine various program features and similarity coefficients with the aim of precisely assessing the similarities among the dynamic spectra of these program features. They often ignore the noise introduced by other features on the same set of executions. In [6], we develop a fault-localization framework that reduces the noise in fault-failure correlation measurements. Empirical results show that the synthesized techniques are more effective than base techniques by almost 10%. (v) Many existing studies measure the effectiveness of test case prioritization techniques using the average performance on a set of test suites. In real-life regression testing, however, a tester can only afford to apply one test case prioritization technique to one test suite against a service once, even if it results in an adverse scenario such that the actual performance in the test session is far below average. To what extent does the effectiveness of prioritization techniques in average scenarios correlate with that in adverse scenarios? In [9, 22], we report the first empirical study on this research question through more than 300 million APFD and HMFD data points produced from 19 techniques, eight WS-BPEL benchmarks, and 1000 test cases prioritized by each technique 1000 times. (vi) People increasingly use handheld devices to access web services. Many mobile versions offer only a subset of the features because of limited hardware capability and screen sizes. In [13], we present "JSCloud", which dynamically estimates whether a code segment should be reconfigured adaptively to execute remotely via cloud services. Empirical results confirm significant usefulness. TESTING ADAPTIVE MULTI-CANDIDATE SERVICE-BASED COMPONENTS (vii) Testing adaptive service-based components is very difficult. Our paper in IEEE Transactions on Services Computing [11] proposes "preemptive regression testing" to address the challenges. For any detected change in test coverage, we preempt the current session, create a sub-session to verify the changes, and then resume the suspended session with refined test case priority. FAULT CLASS SUBSUMPTION RELATIONS FOR ADAPTIVE SERVICES (viii) Our third paper in IEEE Transactions on Services Computing [10] proposes a subsumption hierarchy of test case prioritization techniques for composite services. Selecting prioritization techniques according to the hierarchical model enhances cost-effectiveness significantly. TEST ADEQUACY REQUIREMENTS FOR ADAPTIVE SERVICES (ix) Algebraic term rewriting is a useful foundation for testing composite services [10]. Our paper in IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering [3] presents precise theoretical criteria for real-world shortcuts in test adequacy of term equivalence to be exactly the same as ideal targets in test adequacy. The innovative finding enables the shortcuts to be used without compromising service correctness. (x) Our paper in ACM Transactions on Autonomous and Adaptive Systems [7] defines "context diversity" to capture the extent of context changes. We report one of the largest case studies on the effectiveness of data flow testing criteria for adaptive software. It shows that test cases with higher context diversity significantly enhance effectiveness. (xi) While test adequacy is vital for developers to assure that sufficient testing effort has been made, finding all the faults in a program as soon as possible is equally important. A tight integration between testing and debugging activities is essential. In [4], we find that test adequacy criteria and the percentage of prioritized test suites utilized are major factors affecting the effectiveness of statistical fault localization techniques. DATA MINING TECHNIQUES (xii) Energy efficiency at the software utility level has gained much attention. Existing energy-saving techniques often rely on simplified predictions. In [1, 19], we propose an innovative framework called "EClass" for general-purpose Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) processors by recognizing short and repetitive utilization patterns efficiently using machine learning. Our research results challenge an assumption in the research community that simple heuristics should be used to adjust the processor frequency. Our advanced approach not only compensates for the energy needed to run the algorithm, but also outperforms existing techniques. (xiii) A test oracle refers to the mechanism for determining whether the results of the software under test agree with the expected outcomes. In real-life situations, however, a test oracle may not exist. In [17], we present the use of metamorphic testing, pattern classification, and algebraic term rewriting to alleviate the problems. For example, we propose the use of reference model, which is an existing program that serves the same purpose as the software under test but not necessarily implemented using the same algorithm. We then train a pattern classifier to recognize the black-box features of samples from the reference model and its fault-based variations. AUTOMATED TECHNIQUES AND TOOLS FOR TESTING AND DEBUGGING (xiv) We have implemented the frameworks and strategies in the above papers. Empirical studies have shown that they are significantly more effective than existing techniques. Please refer to the papers for details. (xv) Automatic fault localization commonly relies on both passed and failed runs, but passed runs are generally susceptible to coincidental correctness and modern software automatically produces a huge number of bug reports on failed runs. In [2], we propose an effective new technique called "FOnly" that relies only on failed runs to locate faults statistically. It is a promising solution to the increasingly common situation where a huge number of bug reports are sent automatically to software developers through the Web. (xvi) Adaptive Random Testing (ART) algorithms make good use of the concept of even spreading and achieve 40 to 50% improvement in test effectiveness over random testing in revealing the first failure, which is close to the theoretical limit. However, efficiency is an issue when a large number of test cases are involved. In [18], we propose an innovative divide-and-conquer approach to improve the efficiency of ART algorithms. Experimental results show that the technique can provide much better efficiency while maintaining similar, or even better, effectiveness. REFERENCES The references are listed in Part C of this report.

717911.label: Project Title(Chinese)
717911.value: 用於高通量及定量生物醫學診斷的干涉測量時間編碼光學成像

717911.label: Project Objectives
717911.value: The demand for delivering rapid and high-throughput quantitative measurements is proliferating in life science research and clinical applications, e.g. hematology and proteomics [1-2]. However, revealing genuine information of the innumerable cells/biomolecules with high throughput has been a challenging task. With regard to optical microscopy, an indispensible tool for biomedical diagnostics, emphasis has been overwhelmingly placed on improving the spatial resolution [3-5]. Mostly overlooked is however the imaging temporal resolution [6-7], which limits the imaging throughput. It mainly attributes to that the typical CCD/CMOS imagers, the major workhorse in microscopy, are incapable of capturing fast dynamical processes with high sensitivity and resolution because of their fundamental trade-off between sensitivity and frame rate [8-9]. This project aims to develop a new high-speed quantitative imaging tool that can overcome the aforementioned limitation. The proposed system, called Interferometric Time-Encoded Microscopy (iTEM), is built on the recent demonstration of an entirely new imaging modality by the principle investigator (PI) and co-workers that has established the world record for frame rate and sensitivity for continuous real-time imaging [10-13]. This approach employs optical image amplification and other innovations to overcome the trade-off between imaging sensitivity and speed. Incorporated with the interferometric techniques, iTEM can provide simultaneously high-throughput and non-invasive quantitative measurements of the cellular/sub-cellular structure and the biomolecular interaction. Specifically, we aim to: Develop the iTEM system – Imaging in iTEM is accomplished by two key steps: (i) The spatial phase information of the cells is spectrally encoded onto the frequency spectrum of the optical broadband pulse based on interferometry. This non-invasive spatial phase encoding approach allows us to extract multitude quantitative information of the cells (e.g. refractive index, mass, and stiffness) with nanometer precision. (ii) Amplified dispersive Fourier transformation (ADFT) is then employed to map the spectrum, which is encoded with the image, into the time domain and performs optical image amplification simultaneously. ADFT is a powerful technique which was originally developed for ultrafast real-time spectroscopy with spectral acquisition rates of >MHz, a speed not achievable with conventional spectrometers [14-16]. Based on the interferometric spectrally-encoded imaging and ADFT, we will design and construct the iTEM system which enables ultrafast quantitative imaging with an unprecedented speed (>10MHz). Characterize the functionality and performance of the iTEM prototypes – We will employ the iTEM prototype to monitor high-speed microfluidic transport of the heterogeneous populations of microparticles/cells with flow rates > 1 m/s (with support from Faculty Core Imaging Facility and HKU–Pasteur Research Centre in Faculty of Medicine at HKU). We will also test the measurement accuracy of the prototype by providing the high-throughput statistics of the microparticle/cell size, morphology and other quantitative information, such as refractive index and mass. This microfluidic configuration can directly be applied in a compelling application of iTEM – imaging flow cytometry. Explore the potential applications of iTEM – In hematology, capturing images of cells during flow minimizes the need for qualitative, subjective, and laborious manual inspection and together with higher throughput will reduce the cost of healthcare [17]. However, most existing flow cytometers for such applications fall seriously short of imaging individual cell with sufficient throughput [18-19]. They also lack the quantitative information extracted from detailed cell morphology, which offers additional multiparater analysis capability. The ability of delivering high-throughput quantitative label-free imaging allows iTEM to address these downsides and to greatly expand the clinical diagnostics applications of cytometry. Having the support from and the collaboration with Faculty of Medicine at HKU (letters of support attached), we will explore the utility of iTEM in imaging flow cytometry in terms of high-throughput enumeration of blood cells in flow. Such a high-throughput platform would especially be transformative for rare cell identification from blood (e.g. circulating tumor cells (CTCs) [21]) with high statistical accuracy. Notably, because of the immense potential of imaging flow cytometry, it has been approved by Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for assessment of metastatic diseases [20]. Additionally, the interferometric feature of iTEM can be employed to detect the optical phase-shift due to the biomolecular interactions. This feature thus naturally makes iTEM an attractive platform for high-throughput, high-sensitivity, label-free biomolecular sensing – a valuable technique for proteomic study and drug screening [22-23].
rows: The demand for delivering rapid and high-throughput quantitative measurements is proliferating in life science research and clinical applications, e.g. hematology and proteomics [1-2]. However, revealing genuine information of the innumerable cells/biomolecules with high throughput has been a challenging task. With regard to optical microscopy, an indispensible tool for biomedical diagnostics, emphasis has been overwhelmingly placed on improving the spatial resolution [3-5]. Mostly overlooked is however the imaging temporal resolution [6-7], which limits the imaging throughput. It mainly attributes to that the typical CCD/CMOS imagers, the major workhorse in microscopy, are incapable of capturing fast dynamical processes with high sensitivity and resolution because of their fundamental trade-off between sensitivity and frame rate [8-9]. This project aims to develop a new high-speed quantitative imaging tool that can overcome the aforementioned limitation. The proposed system, called Interferometric Time-Encoded Microscopy (iTEM), is built on the recent demonstration of an entirely new imaging modality by the principle investigator (PI) and co-workers that has established the world record for frame rate and sensitivity for continuous real-time imaging [10-13]. This approach employs optical image amplification and other innovations to overcome the trade-off between imaging sensitivity and speed. Incorporated with the interferometric techniques, iTEM can provide simultaneously high-throughput and non-invasive quantitative measurements of the cellular/sub-cellular structure and the biomolecular interaction. Specifically, we aim to:

Develop the iTEM system – Imaging in iTEM is accomplished by two key steps: (i) The spatial phase information of the cells is spectrally encoded onto the frequency spectrum of the optical broadband pulse based on interferometry. This non-invasive spatial phase encoding approach allows us to extract multitude quantitative information of the cells (e.g. refractive index, mass, and stiffness) with nanometer precision. (ii) Amplified dispersive Fourier transformation (ADFT) is then employed to map the spectrum, which is encoded with the image, into the time domain and performs optical image amplification simultaneously. ADFT is a powerful technique which was originally developed for ultrafast real-time spectroscopy with spectral acquisition rates of >MHz, a speed not achievable with conventional spectrometers [14-16]. Based on the interferometric spectrally-encoded imaging and ADFT, we will design and construct the iTEM system which enables ultrafast quantitative imaging with an unprecedented speed (>10MHz).

Characterize the functionality and performance of the iTEM prototypes – We will employ the iTEM prototype to monitor high-speed microfluidic transport of the heterogeneous populations of microparticles/cells with flow rates > 1 m/s (with support from Faculty Core Imaging Facility and HKU–Pasteur Research Centre in Faculty of Medicine at HKU). We will also test the measurement accuracy of the prototype by providing the high-throughput statistics of the microparticle/cell size, morphology and other quantitative information, such as refractive index and mass. This microfluidic configuration can directly be applied in a compelling application of iTEM – imaging flow cytometry.

Explore the potential applications of iTEM – In hematology, capturing images of cells during flow minimizes the need for qualitative, subjective, and laborious manual inspection and together with higher throughput will reduce the cost of healthcare [17]. However, most existing flow cytometers for such applications fall seriously short of imaging individual cell with sufficient throughput [18-19]. They also lack the quantitative information extracted from detailed cell morphology, which offers additional multiparater analysis capability. The ability of delivering high-throughput quantitative label-free imaging allows iTEM to address these downsides and to greatly expand the clinical diagnostics applications of cytometry. Having the support from and the collaboration with Faculty of Medicine at HKU (letters of support attached), we will explore the utility of iTEM in imaging flow cytometry in terms of high-throughput enumeration of blood cells in flow. Such a high-throughput platform would especially be transformative for rare cell identification from blood (e.g. circulating tumor cells (CTCs) [21]) with high statistical accuracy. Notably, because of the immense potential of imaging flow cytometry, it has been approved by Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for assessment of metastatic diseases [20]. Additionally, the interferometric feature of iTEM can be employed to detect the optical phase-shift due to the biomolecular interactions. This feature thus naturally makes iTEM an attractive platform for high-throughput, high-sensitivity, label-free biomolecular sensing – a valuable technique for proteomic study and drug screening [22-23].

717911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
717911.value: 用於高通量及定量生物醫學診斷的干涉測量時間編碼光學成像 摘要： 光學診斷科技日新月異，令科學和生物醫藥發展一日千里。光學顯微技術的發展一向偏重提高空間解像度，得以開發出一系列「納米顯微」工具，成績驕人。然而，在顯微技術中，決定成像通量的動態解像度雖然與空間解像度同樣關鍵，但卻經常被（學者／研究人員所）忽視，主要是由於成像傳感器（即電荷耦合器（CCD）和互補式金屬氧化物半導體(CMOS)）基本上不能同時兼顧敏感度與幀率，此限制令傳感器無法捕捉快速動態過程，亦無法以高敏感度與解像度進行高通量計量，這表示所有光學成像系統發展均會因此受阻。 此外，從細胞結構和生物分子活動中抽取大量定量資料在生物醫學中亦愈趨重要，例如用於疾病診斷和創製藥物，惟計量無數細胞或生物分子包含大量資料，一般要求高通量的計量儀器，這再次陷入取捨計量敏感度與速度的窘境。我們的目標是開發出一個嶄新光學診斷平台，旨在為細胞／分子定量分析提供極速精密的成像，稱為干涉測量時間編碼顯微技術(iTEM)。iTEM建基於首席研究員與同僚近日就全新成像形式作出的示範，此項示範在連續實時成像的幀率和敏感度方面開創世界記錄。我們的技術利用光學影像放大，發掘其他創新技術，以解決上述取捨成像敏感度與速度的難題。技術應用單像素相片檢測器捕捉影像，從而突破CCD/CMOS成像器的速度限制。憑藉前所未見的成像速度，iTEM更可根據干涉量學，以非入侵性的形式，提供細胞／亞細胞結構和生物分子交互作用的定量資料，達致細微至納米的精確度。 我們將特別從iTEM的原型開發其於成像流式細胞技術的潛在應用。大部份現有的流式細胞儀因為缺乏兼備足夠速度與敏感度的攝影技術，因此嚴重未能追上以高通量拍攝個別細胞的速度（約每秒100,000個細胞），惟此速度卻是許多高通量血液學分析必須具備的功能。另外，iTEM的干涉測量特徵亦使其在高敏感度非標記生物分子感應方面成為值得關注的的高通量平台，在蛋白質組學（大型蛋白質研究）和藥物篩選應用擁有潛在發展空間。

717911.label: Realisation of objectives
717911.value: We have successfully demonstrated ultrafast iTEM imaging system operated in the NIR wavelength range (i.e. 1000 nm) which can be used for a number of optical imaging applications. In particular, we are the first group demonstrating iTEM of biological specimens in NIR with ultrafast line rate (20MHz) as well as cellular resolution. We also have applied this technology to optofluidic quantitative phase imaging of live cells – demonstrating the capability of delivering label-free quantitative single-cell imaging at a high throughput which cannot be achieved by any existing imaging flow cytometers. We also demonstrated that this technique can be used for quantitative phase whole slide imaging at ultrafast speed. It can find an immediate application in digital pathology.

717911.label: Major findings and research outcome
717911.value: We have successfully established the first iTEM system which could perform high- resolution and ultrafast quantitative phase imaging for biomedical applications, especially tissue-wide and single-cell imaging applications. We have published over 15 peer-reviewed publications, as well as over 30 international conference publications on the ADFT and iTEM techniques. Also we are the first group enabling ADFT operation in NIR which is significant as it opens up a new opportunity for ADFT to be utilized in a wide range of biophotonic applications. We are also the first demonstrating iTEM which shows sub-cellular resolution. We have established strong collaborations with medical colleagues, notably Prof. Godfrey Chan (Head, Department of Paediatrics & Adolescent Medicine) for working on minimal residual disease detection using our STEAM technology; Prof. George Tsao ( Head, Department of Anatomy) for exploring new high-speed imaging platform for cancer cell biology research.

717911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
717911.value: We will continue to develop the uniquely fast iTEM system and its variant configuration particularly in terms of improving the image resolution, specificity/sensitivity of single-cell analysis based on quantitative phase at such a high imaging speed. We will also explore the multimodal implementation to further advance the quantitative analysis capability, such as incorporating fluorescence detection in the iTEM system. And we will continue to explore the new applications of iTEM where high-throughput imaging or label-free single-cell analysis is critical.

717911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
717911.value: The research work demonstrated the potential of this technology particularly in high-throughput clinical diagnostics as well as fundamental life science research. It is the only available technology in the field that could achieve the quantitative phase imaging throughput compatible with the conventional non-imaging flow cytometers. It would have a profound impact on high-throughput and high precision rare cancer detection and label-free single cell analysis (which is an emerging field in biology and biomedicine - aiming to measure the true properties of the individual cells in a huge population).

718011.label: Project Objectives
718011.value: Unified execution model and work scheduling: We propose a Java-to-OpenCL code translator with a loop analyzer that performs automatic loop parallelization in a speculative manner, and a scheduling runtime that assigns workloads to CPU and GPU with symbiosis awareness and dynamic load balancing support. Virtual shared memory between CPU and GPU: We will investigate mechanisms along with optimization techniques like lazy-copy, and object migration to support transparent sharing of Java objects and arrays between CPU and GPU memory. GPU-friendly software-level speculative synchronization: We will examine and unite concepts of thread-level speculation and software transactional memory to develop a scalable memory consistency protocol for the massively parallel GPU threads as well as CPU threads. Space-efficient hierarchical conflict detection methods and resource-aware transaction retrying methodology will be studied.
rows: Unified execution model and work scheduling: We propose a Java-to-OpenCL code translator with a loop analyzer that performs automatic loop parallelization in a speculative manner, and a scheduling runtime that assigns workloads to CPU and GPU with symbiosis awareness and dynamic load balancing support.

Virtual shared memory between CPU and GPU: We will investigate mechanisms along with optimization techniques like lazy-copy, and object migration to support transparent sharing of Java objects and arrays between CPU and GPU memory.

GPU-friendly software-level speculative synchronization: We will examine and unite concepts of thread-level speculation and software transactional memory to develop a scalable memory consistency protocol for the massively parallel GPU threads as well as CPU threads. Space-efficient hierarchical conflict detection methods and resource-aware transaction retrying methodology will be studied.

718011.label: Realisation of objectives
718011.value: 1. Unified execution model and work scheduling: We propose a new compiler and runtime platform, called Japonica (Java with Auto-Parallelization ON graphIcs Coprocessing Architecture) to meet Objective (1). By means of simple user annotations, sequential Java source code can be analyzed, translated, and compiled into a dual executable consisting of CUDA (or OpenCL) kernels and multiple Java threads. Annotated loops are automatically split into loop chunks (or tasks) being scheduled to execute on GPU/CPU cores. Japonica supports speculative execution of loops with non-deterministic loop-carried data dependency. With the knowledge about inter-loop data dependencies, the scheduler can decide on the execution mode for each loop chunk: (1) sequential, running on CPU, (2) speculatively parallel, thread level speculation (TLS) on GPUs, or (3) truly parallel, DO-ALL in GPUs. Japonica implemented task stealing and task sharing schemes that allow swift load redistribution across GPU and CPU cores in a way to best balance their usage. 2. Virtual shared memory between CPU and GPU: To meet Objective (2), we apply a data allocation method for transparent data access across CPU and GPU memory address spaces. Data arrays accessed in the annotated for-loop are classified as: live-in (data read within the loops), live-out (data written within the loops), and temp (private data). For live-in or live-out arrays, we adopt a lazy-copy approach that avoids unnecessary data transfer over the PCI bus. These arrays are allocated using managed memory and they can be accessed on CPU and GPU using the unified memory feature in CUDA 6 (or OpenCL 2.0 SVM) without adding explicit code for data migration. As a result, Japonica can avoid copying the whole array, from host to GPU device memory, but only the data portion which is handled by the loop chunk be moved to GPU. 3. GPU-friendly software-level speculative synchronization: Japonica implemented a software Thread Level Speculation (TLS) library, named GPU-TLS, to meet Objective (3). GPU-TLS partitions a single for-loop into multiple loop chunks, and executes them speculatively as if there were no cross-iteration dependencies. During the execution, each thread buffers the possibly unsafe memory updates in local memory instead of updating the global memory. The dependency checker determines if the speculative execution has violated some inter-iteration dependencies and find where they happen by tracking the memory access (using read/write sets). For those threads not found to have violated dependencies, the committer copies their buffered memory updates to the global memory.

Both task sharing and task stealing were implemented to distribute workload among CPUs and GPUs to maximize the resource usage and achieve higher speedup. To achieve better co-scheduling of workloads between CPU and GPU, we have optimized our data dependency model. We have implemented this model into two parts: static and dynamic optimizations. Using the static part, we can get the data dependency density, which implies the static dependences in each loop. For the uncertain dependency, we use the dynamic part to estimate the overhead of execution on GPU. Therefore, we can get more accurate prediction to distribute the work between CPU and GPU.

Virtual shared memory between CPU and GPU: Japonica’s code translator could automatically generate necessary data movement APIs for instructing the scheduler to move-in and move-out data among CPU and GPU, and ensure the data consistency. We are in active progress of including the support of Java objects in Japonica.

GPU-friendly software-level speculative synchronization: GPU-TLS, a GPU-aware TLS execution engine, has been implemented. We add profiling support to the system for tracking the data dependency density across iterations, which provides useful insights into the potential for optimistic parallelization and algorithmic work scheduling. We develop a new adaptive concurrency policy, called Probing Throttle, which proves that changing concurrency according to the commit rate, rather than ratio, can achieve better performance results. In order to get better performance, we proposed the two abovementioned solutions to reduce the overhead of GPU-TLS. Then, testing and evaluations were carried out to determine which solution is better. And we find that decreasing the number of warps per block will give us 17.5% more speedup in the blacksholes application by setting the number of warps per block to 7 compared with the default 16 warps per block.

718011.label: Major findings and research outcome
718011.value: 1. Automatic Speculative Parallelization: GPU-TLS is distinct from various existing solutions, as it focuses on parallelizing loops with non-deterministic loop-carried data dependency on GPU. GPU-TLS guarantees correct results for loops with false dependencies and enable the possibility of execution on GPU for loops with light dependency. The dependency checking is lightweight as we only monitor those annotated variables and the detection is embedded in the normal execution path, while the overhead of mis-speculation recovery is bounded by the number of true data dependencies detected. Extensive evaluations using both micro-benchmarks and real-life applications on two NVIDIA GPU cards show that speculative loop parallelization using GPU-TLS can achieve speedups ranging from 5 to 160 for sequential programs with loops. (See Research Output 9.2) 2. Co-scheduling of Tasks on CPU and GPU: Japonica’s runtime scheduler implemented task sharing and task stealing, which enable CPU and GPU to share the workloads dynamically. The task allocation decision is made based on a new metric, called dependency density, for quantifying the relative overhead for executing tasks with potential data dependencies on GPUs. In particular, tasks with higher dependency density value are preferable to be assigned to CPU, thus minimizing the cost for mis-speculation recovery. We compare the performance of the two scheduling schemes using 11 benchmark programs. Experimental results show that Japonica can run 10x, 2.5x and 2.14x faster than the best serial (one thread on a single CPU), GPU-alone and CPU-alone versions respectively. We found task sharing scheme performs very well for applications with one or few compute-intensive loops, while task stealing performs better than task sharing for those with computations evenly distributed among multiple loops. (See Research Output 9.1). 3. Adaptive concurrency control (ACC) policies: To further improve speculative loop execution on Japonica, we conduct an in-depth analysis on the relationship between commit rate, commit ratio and active thread count. We confirm that changing concurrency level according to the commit rate, rather than ratio, is critical during different sections of program execution. Based on this finding, we develop a new adaptive concurrency control (ACC) policy, which results in excellent performance improvement on a well-known benchmark suite (STAMP). The degradation in the worst case can be much reduced. With results from a commercial profiler, we demonstrate concurrency control unit is sensitive to the processor cache hierarchy and our new solution has significant improvement over other similar works. (See Research Output 8.1 and 9.4).

718011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
718011.value: 1. As more than 90% of processors shipping today include a GPU on die (e.g., Intel HD Graphics on Haswell), we plan to extend our task scheduler to support parallel loop execution on the new CPU with on-die GPU. One of the key advantages is that the mis-speculation recovery cost can be done with near zero overhead. 2. We plan to leverage PPCG, a source-to-source parallel compiler using the polyhedral model, to generate the OpenCL code. PPCG supports multilevel tiling and is a more powerful code generator for the parallelization and locality optimization on GPU. The generated OpenCL code is potentially more robust and efficient.

718011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
718011.value: Loop carried dependencies are particularly important since loops are possibly the most common target of parallelization efforts in most applications. While existing parallelization solutions are able to support parallel processing of Java programs on GPUs, none of them can handle non-deterministic loop carried dependencies. Japonica is one of pioneer works that addressed the issue. Japonica implemented a framework which can parallelize the Java code into Java threads and OpenCL kernels automatically. The framework gives the programmers an easy way (just write Java code) to realize their algorithms. The speculative execution model used in GPU-TLS could maximize the power of the heterogeneous manycore architecture combining both CPUs and GPUs. The use of OpenCL also has several advantages. First of all, the OpenCL is a vendor-independent, open industry standard. Currently, OpenCL is supported by AMD, Apple, Intel and NVIDIA. Therefore, Japonica be easily ported to many hardware platforms.

718111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
718111.value: 进入21世纪，便宜且充足的原油供应时代已经终结，能源正成为人类所面临的最重大的挑战。而纳米技术将很可能在解决全球化能源危机的过程中扮演重要角色。其中，纳米流体技术由于可以很大程度上提高流体的传热特性，因此为人们应对能源挑战提供了一个有效的解决方案。 然而，目前纳米流体的效能仍不令人满意，其表现在：1、传统的纳米流体制造工艺不能有效地控制其微观结构和特性；2、尚无一种纳米流体具备可调且极高的导热系数。基于此，我们提出将一种新的微流体液滴生成技术用于合成水-聚N乙烯基己内酰胺纳米流体。由于其纳米颗粒的尺寸以及纳米流体的导热系数随温度的变化而变化，因此它将是一种温度敏感型（智能）纳米流体。另外，由于颗粒的独特多孔结构以及纳米流体中各种传递过程的相互耦合，这种纳米流体的导热系数甚至可以高于Hashin-Shtrikman边界的上限。我们希望充分发挥微流体技术所具有的液体精确快速混合的特点，令其能够有效准确地控制纳米流体的加工过程。 具体来说，我们将设计和制造三种用于加工上述智能纳米流体的微流体液滴生成系统并对这些系统的一些重要特性进行表征。我们还将采用最先进的仪器检测手段对纳米流体的微观结构和导热系数进行表征，找出它们和各种加工参数之间的相互联系。这里所指的加工参数包括微流体系统的几何参数，反应浓度，流速等；微观结构包括纳米颗粒的尺寸及尺寸分布，形状，水和颗粒之间的表面特性，以及颗粒的聚集情况。 本项目的成功实施将使人们能够根据纳米流体的具体应用条件设计并制造出具有相应微观结构的纳米流体，从而成为纳米流体制造和应用的一项革新发展，并代表着能源和环境课题研究的重大突破。

718111.label: Major findings and research outcome
718111.value: The project has yielded: (i) a continuous and scaleable (by numbering-up) microfluidic-droplet technique for effectively synthesizing nanofluids with a good repeatability and an accurate and effective control over nanofluids’ microstructures; and (ii) reliable correlations among synthesis parameters, nanofluids’ microstructures, and their thermal conductivities. Research outcome includes 18 peer-reviewed journal publications, 16 conference papers (6 of them are plenary/keynote papers), 5 PhD theses (2 in progress).

718111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
718111.value: The success of the project has changed the way nanofluids are synthesized and applied and blazed a path for precise synthesis and development of diverse multifunctional nanofluids. The project’s findings should also represent a significant step towards creating nanofluids by design, tailoring their microstructure to suit a desired application and producing nanofluids economically at a commercial scale.

718111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
718111.value: Unlike the past century that was blessed with ever-abundant cheap oil, this century energy has been rated as the single most important issue facing humanity. A global-scale energy crisis looms ahead. Nanotechnology will figure centrally in providing technological solutions. Nanofluid technology, one of the enabling technologies of the nanotech revolution, holds the promise of significantly enhancing the thermal properties of fluids and thus providing high quality heat-transfer fluids of the future that are vital for solving the terawatt challenge facing us. This project has successfully developed and characterized a microfluidic-droplet technique for precisely synthesizing high-quality nanofluids. The success of the project has changed the way nanofluids are synthesized and applied and blazed a path for precise synthesis and development of diverse multifunctional nanofluids. The project’s findings should also represent a significant step towards creating nanofluids by design, tailoring their microstructure to suit a desired application and producing nanofluids economically at a commercial scale.

718311.label: Project Title(Chinese)
718311.value: 一个产生三维六面体网格的新方法

718311.label: Project Objectives
718311.value: Develop a variational framework for defining a quasi-eigenfunction for a 3D bounded domain whose Morse-Smale complex has a highly regular structure and is well-aligned with domain boundary surfaces. Develop a fast numerical method based on parallel computation for computing discrete approximations of quasi-eigenfunctions. Develop a robust algorithm for extracting the Morse-Smale complex of a discretely represented quasi-eigenfunction. Effective topological and geometric optimization will be performed to further improve the regularity of the Morse-Smale complex, so as to enhance the quality of the output mesh. Extend this variational framework, by adopting a generalized form of the Laplacian operator, to generating anisotropic hex meshes. This will lead to a general method that allows adaptive control of mesh orientation and mesh element size.

718311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
718311.value: Hexahedral meshes, which are decompositions of a 3D domain into hexahedral elements, are highly demanded in numerical simulation in many fields of computational science and engineering for their superior numerical properties. However, due to the stringent connectivity constraints of hexahedral elements, hexahedral mesh generation is a very difficult problem. Despite decades of extensive research, it remains a challenge to automatically generate a high quality hexahedral mesh of a domain of arbitrary geometry. This problem is the Holy Grail of mesh generation research. We propose a fundamentally new approach to solving this important and challenging problem. Our innovation is the introduction of a new type of functions, called quasi-eigenfunctions, that inherit some useful properties of the Laplacian eigenfunctions but without their drawback of poor boundary alignment in a bounded domain. The key observations are that the structure of the Morse-Smale complex of a quasi-eigenfunction resembles a hexahedral mesh and that this structure can be controlled to achieve excellent boundary surface alignment by imposing appropriate boundary conditions. Therefore we use the topology suggested by the Morse-Smale complex of a quasi-eigenfunction to generate a hexahedral mesh. We define quasi-eigenfunctions using a novel variational formulation and propose to compute them using a fast multigrid solver. Preliminary studies show that our proposed method is general, highly automatic, and capable of generating meshes of much better quality than other existing methods. It applies to domains of general shapes, including those with curvilinear boundaries. Furthermore, the method can be extended to allow adaptive control of mesh orientation and mesh element size for generating adaptive hexahedral meshes and anisotropic hexahedral meshes. The outcome of this project stands to be a breakthrough in hexahedral mesh generation. 六面体网格有助于产生高精确度数值模拟结果，从而在计算科学和工程上有着非常广泛的应用。六面体网格是对一个三维定义域的剖分，其中每个剖分元素均是六面体。由于要求严格的网格连接关系，生成六面体网格在工程上非常困难。尽管在过去数十年中有这方面的大量研究，然而对一个任意形状的三维定义域自动产生高质量的六面体剖分仍然一个没有解决的问题，也是目前网格生成研究中最重要的问题。 在这个项目中我们将研究一个解决这个问题的新方法。我们提出了一种新的方程—拟特征方程，它在具有Laplacian特征方程的良好特性的同时避免了后者对定义域边界不能吻合的缺点。我们一个重要的发现是拟特征方程的解函数的Morse-Smale复形具有类似六面体网格剖分的拓扑结构。我们还提出了一种新的边界条件，使得这样产生的Morse-Smale复形能与定义域边界很好地吻合。因此我们可以使用拟特征方程所蕴含的Morse-Smale复形生成一个六面体网格。 在计算方面，我们把拟特征方程的解描述成一个等价的变分问题的解，并且提出一个快速的计算方法求解此变分问题。初步的实验结果显示我们所提出的方案具有普遍性好、高度自动的特点，并且其生成的网格质量好于现有的其它方法产生的结果。我们的方法还可进一步推广以对网格的方向及元素大小进行控制，从而生成具有密度变化和各向异性特征的六面体网格。我们相信这个新的方法将成为六面体网格生成研究中的一个重大突破。

718311.label: Major findings and research outcome
718311.value: We developed a versatile spectral algorithm for computing quad meshes and hex meshes of 2D and 3D domains, respectively. The work was published in a journal paper (ACM Transactions on Graphics, TOG), the top journal in the field of computer graphics. We further explore the properties of hex meshes and proposed a method of computing hex meshes based on frame field optimization, which was presented at SIGGRAPH Asia 2012 conference and published in another ACM TOG paper.

718311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
718311.value: We are extending this research by integrating a particle system with Morse-Smale complex to develop a faster method for generating high quality anisotropic hex-dominant meshes.

718311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
718311.value: In this project we developed a spectral method for generation hex meshes of 3D domains, as well as quad meshes of 2D domains. The uniqueness of our method is its ability of satisfying strict constrained imposed by domain boundaries or sharp features. This is realized by solving for the quasi eigen-functions of a PDE with specially designed boundary conditions. By extending the Laplace operator used in the PDE formulation, our method is also capable of generating anisotropic meshes.

718711.label: Project Objectives
718711.value: To develop efficient and robust nonlinear parametric model order reduction (NLPMOR) algorithms applicable to high-frequency analog/RF blocks. To check and enforce passivity of reduced-order nonlinear parametric models which in turn guarantees globally stable and physically meaningful system-level simulation. To construct process and EM variation-aware analog/RF models in collaboration with the industry, and utilize these models in validating the practicality of the above NLPMOR and passivation algorithms. Outcome and Long-Term Impact: The long-term impact of this project is guaranteed by the shrinking feature size and rising clock speed of modern/future ICs, and also by the dominant roles of analog/RF modules in setting the performance of state-of-the-art mixed-signal chips. As of the time of writing this proposal, NLPMOR is an emerging topic and there exist few algorithms for its efficient implementation as well as its integration/benchmarking with industrial EDA/CAD tools. Moreover, passivity preservation in NLPMOR remains an open issue. To achieve these project goals, a strategic team is formed between the PI and two Co-Is who possess strong and complementary expertise in chip parasitic and EM extraction, NLPMOR, and the corresponding passivity analysis and synthesis. The findings and outputs from this project will directly address the demand in highly accurate and computationally efficient variation-aware analog/RF simulator compatible with the continuous up-scaling of operating frequency into the tens-GHz regime. The project can also provide students and research assistants with the necessary knowledge to contribute to the EDA/CAD industry or academia. Research components of this project can readily be integrated into university graduate trainings and courses.

718711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
718711.value: Modern integrated circuit (IC) design flow relies heavily on electronic design automation (EDA) or computer-aided design (CAD) tools. This is especially true for high-frequency circuits operating at multiple or even tens gigahertz (GHz), since any on-chip geometry or process variation would be substantially felt by the electrical signals whose electromagnetic (EM) behaviors must be explicitly considered (e.g., both the skin depth and material irregularities are on the order of micrometers in the GHz range). This leads to the increased impact of process uncertainties and renders the design of analog and radio-frequency (RF) blocks in mixed-signal ICs highly challenging owing to their nonlinearities and complex EM interactions. Unlike the traditional process variational analyses by expensive Monte Carlo experiments and/or repetitive model order reduction (MOR) of high-order numerical models, parameterized small-order (yet accurate) analog/RF models allow one to efficiently perform characterization/verification of critical structures by simply jiggling parameters in their uncertainty/variational space. Despite the fact that various "high-level" algorithms are available in commercial tools for high-frequency nonlinear analog/RF simulation (e.g., shooting Newton and harmonic balance for steady-state analysis), these tools are faced with various limitations and do not fully support "low-level" nonlinear parametric models for the efficient capture of process variabilities prevalent in modern nanotransistor circuits. Subsequently, recognizing the importance of accurately modeling nonlinear analog/RF blocks in high-speed mixed-signal ICs, and the current lack of EDA/CAD support for their efficient parametric simulation, this project aims at three main objectives. They are: 1) to develop efficient and robust nonlinear parametric model order reduction (NLPMOR) algorithms applicable to analog/RF blocks in high-speed mixed-signal chips; 2) to check and enforce passivity of reduced-order nonlinear parametric models to ensure physically meaningful simulation; 3) to construct initial analog/RF models with explicit account of both geometrical and electrical process variations, which are then used to verify the practicality of the NLPMOR and passivation algorithms. The outcomes of this project will advance the state-of-the-art in the research and implementation of nonlinear analog/RF macromodeling driven by the continuous up-scaling of operating frequencies and impact of process/EM variations. Critical analog/RF blocks can subsequently be accurately captured and functionally verified before fabrication to avoid costly re-spin, which in turn facilitates the production of high-performance mixed-signal ICs. 現代集成電路（IC）設計流程在很大程度上依賴於電子設計自動化（EDA）或計算機輔助設計（CAD）工具。這一點尤其適用於工作頻率在數至數十千兆赫（GHz）的高頻電路，因為任何片上的幾何形狀或製造過程的變化將會大幅影響電信號的電磁（EM）的行為。這些影響在設計中必須明確予以考慮（例如，趨膚深度和材料缺陷的尺寸在GHz範圍內都同樣處於微米級別）。由於製程中不確定性影響的增加，以及非線性和複雜電磁作用的存在，在混合信號IC中設計模擬和射頻（RF）模塊變得非常困難及複雜。不同於傳統製程偏移變分分析中代價高昂的蒙特卡洛方法和/或對高階數值模型的可重複模型降階（MOR），參數化低階（但準確）模擬/ RF模型可以通過在不確定/變動空間內小幅擾動參數來有效地模擬/驗證電路中的關鍵部分。儘管針對高頻非線性模擬/射頻仿真的商用工具中應用了各種“高階”算法（如牛頓衝擊法和諧波平衡穩態分析），這些工具都面臨著各種限制以及不完全支持用於高效捕捉現代納米電路中常見製程變動的“低階”非線性參數模型。 因此，考慮到在高速混合信號IC中準確模擬非線性模擬/ RF模塊的重要性，以及目前缺乏對其參數化模擬的EDA/ CAD支持的現狀，本項目主要包括以下三個目標。它們是：1）開發高效強大的適用於模擬高速混合信號芯片中模擬/ RF模塊的非線性參數化模型降階（NLPMOR）算法; 2）檢查和增強降階後非線性參數模型的無源性，以確保仿真的物理意義; 3）構造明確考慮幾何和製程變動的初始模擬/ RF模型，並用於驗證NLPMOR和無源化算法的實用性。 該項目的成果將有力推動非線性模擬/射頻宏建模在日益提高的工作頻率及製程/電磁變動下的研究和應用。對關鍵模擬/射頻模塊在實際流片前的準確模擬和功能驗證可以避免花費巨大的重新流片，進而促進高性能混合信號集成電路的生產和製造。

718711.label: Realisation of objectives
718711.value: All objectives of the project have been more than successfully achieved. Objective #1 aims at developing efficient and robust nonlinear parametric model order reduction (NLPMOR) algorithms applicable to high-frequency analog/RF blocks. In this regard, the PI and Co-Is have worked closely with overseas (specifically UCSD, USA) and local colleagues in the electromagnetic (EM) regime, and also in the physics domain, to produce practical time- and frequency-domain simulation algorithms at system-, transistor- and ultimately down to the quantum-mechanics atomic levels, as borne out in the publications. These methods represent a wide range of speedups and tradeoffs at various levels of accuracy and computation per the request of the chip designers. Objective #2 concerns checking and enforcing passivity of reduced-order nonlinear parametric models which in turn guarantees globally stable and physically meaningful system-level simulation. This objective has been implemented both at the analytical level (i.e. intrinsic properties with respect to the model state-space representation) and at the numerical level (i.e. preservation of structural properties subject to inevitable numerical uncertainty). Objective #3 targets the construction of process- and EM variation-aware analog/RF models in collaboration with the industry, and the utilization of these models in validating the practicality of the above NLPMOR and passivation algorithms. This has been done through close interaction with one of the Co-Is from industry, Dr. Wim Schoenmaker, through his in-field verification. Moreover, we have developed and tested our system-level and transistor-level models with colleagues from HKU physics department through the use of quantum mechanics principles, too. This ensures the simulation methods and transistor modules in our work are practical while being physically coherent. Objective #4 then follows from success of all previous objectives. Overall, the project has led to the publication of top journal and conference papers. All of them are based on the analytical time- and frequency-domain techniques directly arising from the project objectives. Most algorithms have been coded in Matlab or C that can be readily incorporated into popular electronic design automation (EDA) tools like SPICE simulators in Cadence and Synopsys. One Master and two PhDs have been supported and graduated through the project.

This is especially true for high-frequency circuits operating at multiple or even tens gigahertz (GHz), since any on-chip geometry or process variation would be substantially felt by the electrical signals whose electromagnetic (EM) behaviors must be explicitly accounted for. Nonetheless, the designs of analog and radio-frequency (RF) blocks in mixed-signal ICs are highly challenging owing to their nonlinearities and complex EM interactions. Despite the fact that various ``high-level'' algorithms are available in commercial tools for high-frequency nonlinear analog/RF simulation (e.g., shooting Newton and harmonic balance for steady-state analysis), these tools are faced with various limitations and do not fully support ``low-level'' nonlinear parametric models for the efficient modeling of physical-level effects in modern nanotransistor circuits. Subsequently, recognizing the importance of accurately modeling nonlinear analog/RF blocks in high-speed mixed-signal ICs, this project has contributed substantially in the following aspects: At the system level-- 1. Innovated a matrix-exponential time-domain method that effectively handles the stiff numerical conditioning in time-domain transient simulation of transistor circuits, and allows large time-stepping not achievable before. 2. Developed a new analytical piecewise-polynomial associated transform method for the fast macromodeling of nonlinear circuits expressed in nonlinear ordinary differential equations (ODEs). A fast multi-dimensional inverse Laplace transform scheme has also been reinvented in this context, too. At the device level— 1. Proposed a ground-breaking dynamic multiscale quantum mechanics/electromagnetics simulation framework that spans across various device constituent materials like semiconductor and metals. 2. Developed both time-domain and frequency-domain versions of the above. Consequently, the project outcomes have advanced the state-of-the-art in the research and implementation of nonlinear analog/RF macromodeling and the capture of process/EM variations via quantifying uncertainty at the device level. These render better simulation of analog/RF blocks before fabrication to possibly avoid costly re-spin. Recognition of the project outputs is reflected in the high number of quality publications generated. The PI, due to his visibility in the EDA community, has also been invited to serve as an Associate Editor for IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems (TCAD).

718711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
718711.value: Some of the algorithms and research ideas from the project have been incorporated as the basis scheme in commercial multi-scale multi-domain electromagnetic (EM) simulation algorithms. In particular, a matrix-exponential time-domain method has been proposed that effectively handles the stiff numerical conditioning in time-domain transient simulation of transistor circuits, and allows large time-stepping not achievable before. Our team has also developed a dynamic multi-scale quantum mechanics/EM simulation framework that seamlessly interfaces different materials (e.g. semiconductor and metals) for simulating state-of-the-art power electronics and through-silicon-via (TSV) circuitries. Further polishing and optimization of these algorithms are underway, and outputs are readily welcome by the electronic design automation (EDA) community.

718711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
718711.value: This project has successfully addressed the important topic of accurate modeling and simulation of high-speed nonlinear analog/RF blocks in high-frequency mixed-signal circuits. The project outcomes have largely supplemented the current lack of electronic design automation (EDA) support for system- and device-level parametric simulation under process and electromagnetic variations. Research outputs from the project have resulted in: Industrial impact – a matrix-exponential solver approach is being studied and incorporated into commercial software for tackling difficult time-domain transient simulation (namely, large numerical dynamic range and slow time-stepping problems). Scientific impact – a dynamic multiscale quantum mechanics/electromagnetics simulation framework that features inter-domain (namely, silicon and metal) simulation has attracted physicists and industrialists into a joint investigation.

718811.label: Project Title(Chinese)
718811.value: 酒後駕駛對駕駛表現與受傷風險的影響及相關打擊措施的效果

718811.label: Co - Investigator(s)

718811.label: Project Objectives
718811.value: To measure the temporal relationship between the amount of drink, drivers’ alcohol concentration, and impaired driving performance. To reveal the relationship between drivers’ alcohol concentration and risk of severe injury in traffic accidents. To evaluate the attitudes and perceptions of drivers towards the deterrent effects of legislation and enforcement measures, both existing and planned, for combating drink driving.

718811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
718811.value: Drink driving is well recognized as one of the key human factors that increase the risk of traffic accidents and associated injuries and fatalities. Such risk rises rapidly when a driver’s blood alcohol concentration increases. Unfortunately, drink driving not only increases the risk of accident and injury to drivers themselves, but also increases the risk to innocent road users. Legal limits on the concentration of alcohol in drivers’ breath, blood, and urine were first introduced in Hong Kong in the 1990s. Since then, the number of traffic accidents involving drink driving has been decreasing. Despite this, there has been a lack of comprehensive studies analyzing the influence of alcohol on driving performance in Hong Kong. In addition, it is of paramount importance to understand the effects of alcohol on injury severity in traffic accidents. Recently, there has been public pressure in Hong Kong to impose heavier penalties to combat drink-driving behavior. It is thus timely to explore the deterrent effects of different legislation and enforcement measures in combating drink driving. In this study, we aim to reveal the relationship between the amount of drink, blood alcohol concentration, and driving performance, based on laboratory tests with a Chinese population. From this evidence, it will be possible to establish an appropriate legal limit of alcohol consumption that can depict impaired driving performance. Furthermore, based on the results of traffic accident analyses, the influence of alcohol on actual road safety performance in terms of the risk of severe injury can be estimated. Finally, the effectiveness of countermeasures to combat drink driving will be evaluated using a questionnaire survey. From this evidence, efficient and effective remedial road safety measures can be developed to enhance road safety performance in Hong Kong in the long term. 酒後駕駛是其中一個導致交通意外及傷亡的重要人為因素。交通意外的風險隨著司機體內酒精含量濃度增加而急劇上升。不幸的是，酒後駕駛不但會對司機自身構成傷害，更會危及其他無辜的道路使用者。在九十代，香港首次就司機的呼氣、血液及尿液中的酒精含量訂立法定限度。自此之後，本地涉及酒後駕駛的交通意外數目得以減少。儘管如此，我們對酒精含量與駕駛表現影響的關係一直缺乏認識，而且酒精含量與交通意外傷亡程度的關係也非常重要。目前，加重對酒後駕駛罰則的呼聲日益高漲，這促使我們針對打擊酒後駕駛措施的效果深入分析。是項研究，我們將通過模擬駕駛實驗分析司機酒精飲用量、體內酒精含量與駕駛表現的關係。結果將有助未來酒精限度及酒後駕駛法例的訂定提供重要數據。另外，基於交通意外傷亡的分析，可以進一步了解酒後駕駛、司機行為與交通意外傷亡風險的關係。最後，透過問卷調查，我們將明瞭不同打擊酒後駕駛措施和法例所發揮的效果及司機的態度，長遠將對策劃交通管理、立法及執法行動，提升香港的道路安全有極大裨益。

718811.label: Realisation of objectives
718811.value: To achieve Objective (1), a drink-driving simulation experiment was conducted to investigate the temporal profile of the alcohol concentration of Chinese adults after a light meal. A baseline model (based on the conventional Widmark equation) with zero-order alcohol elimination was initially constructed. Subsequently, a gamma model of the non-linear alcohol concentration profile was developed. The results of the model indicated that the personal characteristics of drinkers, including gender, body weight, and alcohol consumption, are correlated with the pattern and scale of alcohol elimination. An alcohol concentration profile is essential for the back-calculation of a potential drink-driver’s alcohol concentration at the time of driving, and hence improves the conviction rate of drivers committing drink-driving offenses. The actual alcohol-impaired driving performance of Chinese adults in terms of physiological responses such as the braking reaction time (BRT), standard deviation of lane position (LANE), and speed (SPEED) were measured. Generalized linear mixed models were established to identify the factors that affect driving performance, and demonstrated that alcohol-impaired driving performance is strongly correlated with the level of alcohol concentration and the drinking habit of drivers. To achieve Objective (2), comprehensive random breath test (RBT) data, crash attributes, traffic flows, and road design characteristics were used to establish the relationship between the crash risk and breath alcohol concentration. Negative binominal regression models were established that indicated that higher alcohol consumption significantly increases the risk of a more serious crash. The findings of the research provide justification for the development of more effective legislation and enforcement measures to combat drink-driving behavior and promote safe road use in the long term. To achieve Objective (3), an attitudinal survey was conducted to examine Hong Kong drivers’ perceptions of the existing penalties for drink-driving offenses, which include monetary fines, driver demerit points, license disqualification periods, and imprisonment. Stated preference games were used to measure the effects of possible penalties on the intention to drive after drinking. The results revealed that the presence of an RBT checkpoint and increases in driver offence points (DOPs), and periods of license disqualification and imprisonment are all positively correlated with better drink-driving deterrence.

718811.label: Major findings and research outcome
718811.value: To reveal the drink-driving situation in Hong Kong, the spatial-temporal variation in the distribution of drink-driving was established [J3], which is important for the development of targeted enforcement measures and campaign activities. Because impaired driving cannot be investigated without serious risk to participants, in road safety research driving simulators are typically used to monitor impaired driving performance [J5, J9, C2, C8, C10]. Drawing on these experiences, a drink-driving simulation experiment was conducted to investigate the physiological responses of Chinese populations to alcohol impairment. The experimental data obtained were used to establish a temporal profile of the alcohol concentration of Chinese adults after a light meal [C6]. A non-linear (gamma distribution) regression model that formulated the absorption phase, the elimination phases, and the peak alcohol concentration produces a better temporal profile than the traditional linear regression model [J8]. An alcohol concentration profile is essential for the back-calculation of a potential drink-driver’s alcohol concentration at the time of driving, and hence improves the conviction rate of drivers committing drink-driving offenses. Based on the simulation data, the alcohol-impaired driving performance of drivers in terms of physiological responses such as BRT, LANE, and SPEED were studied. The findings of the established generalized linear mixed models demonstrated that BRT and LANE are strongly correlated with the level of alcohol consumption [J7, C11]. Moreover, the results demonstrated that the degree of alcohol impairment of aspects of human attentional control varies, and that automatic action is less likely to be affected than voluntary action from a psychological point of view [C7]. In road safety research, crash prediction models are essential for examining the factors that influence crashes and injuries [C3]. Indeed, the relationships between the crash incidence, crash severity, and possible risk factors vary depending on the type of collision, and thus separate models would be needed to predict the risk of different crash types [J6, C9]. Time exposure is an important factor that must be investigated in analyzing the effects of drink-driving on the crash risk. Fortunately, by taking advantage of global positioning system (GPS) data it was possible to determine the time exposure on the Hong Kong road network [J1]. Crash prediction models were then established using the comprehensive RBT data, crash attributes, traffic flows, and road design characteristics [C1]. The established negative binominal regression models indicated that higher alcohol consumption significantly increases the risk of a more serious crash [J2]. Drivers’ attitudes to drink-driving were also explored to determine the effectiveness of severe penalties in combating drink-driving offenses. The data collected from the attitudinal survey were used to examine the perception of Hong Kong’s drivers of the adequacy of the existing penalties for drink-driving offenses, which include monetary fines, driver demerit points, license disqualification periods, and terms of imprisonment [C4, C5]. Most importantly, the results demonstrated that the presence of an RBT checkpoint and increased DOPs and periods of license disqualification and imprisonment are all positively correlated with better drink-driving deterrence [J4]. This finding should prove useful in the development of long-term targeted enforcement measures to combat drink-driving offenses in Hong Kong.

718811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
718811.value: The results of the simulation study demonstrated that older drivers show poorer physiological responses when drink-driving than younger drivers, and hence are likely to have a higher risk of alcohol-related road crashes. Numerous research studies have shown concern about age-related declines in the cognitive, mental, and physical abilities of older drivers, in particular drivers over 65 years of age, as such declines increase the risk of road crashes and the likelihood of unsafe driving performance. As population aging is a critical social problem both in Hong Kong and worldwide, future research that targets older drivers should be conducted to evaluate the impaired driving performance of this age group using measures such as distraction and fatigue. Research on this subject is essential to determine the effects of population aging on the transportation system of Hong Kong.

718811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
718811.value: Drink-driving is well recognized as one of the key human factors that increases the risk of road crashes. This risk increases rapidly with the level of alcohol concentration in the human body. However, few comprehensive studies have investigated the relationship between drivers’ alcohol consumption, the actual impairment in driving performance due to alcohol, and the resulting accident and injury risks. To better understand the relationship between drink-driving and traffic safety, this project evaluated the effect of alcohol impairment on traffic safety from different aspects. For the crash risk analysis, the impairment effects of alcohol on the severity of injuries and road crashes in Hong Kong were determined using random breath test data. A simulation study was then conducted to develop a temporal profile of driver alcohol concentration and to determine the relationship between that concentration and the actual alcohol-impaired driving performance among Chinese populations. Finally, a perception survey was conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of current legislation in reducing drivers’ intention to drink-drive. The findings of the project are useful for formulating effective legislation and enforcement measures to combat drink-driving in terms of drivers’ perceptions, observed driving performance, and actual road safety levels in the long term.

719111.label: Project Objectives
719111.value: To develop spectral efficient channel estimation algorithms in the fundamental three-terminal dual-hop AF relaying systems with terminals under high mobility. To design channel estimation algorithms for the challenging multi-hop AF relaying systems under high mobility, and to study the effects of noise amplification at relays. Long-term impact: The proposed project intends to make significant advances in channel estimation in multi-hop AF relaying systems over doubly-selective channels. The outcome would enable high-speed wireless data services anywhere and anytime, with speed compatible to wired service. By providing a thorough understanding on the fundamental issues, ideas and research on other aspects of relaying systems will be fostered in the research community. Furthermore, the results would also contribute to the estimation of mobile-to-mobile channel, which is important in the future intelligent transportation system.

719111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
719111.value: As wireless communication becomes an integral part of our daily lives, consumers are getting used to transferring data using their handheld devices anywhere and anytime. In next generation high-speed wireless systems (i.e., 4G), such as Long Term Evolution Advanced (LTE-A) and IEEE 802.16 standard, wideband orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signal will be deployed due to its simplicity of equalization in frequency domain. In order to enable low-cost coverage, relaying is a key part in 4G standards. Relays are either user devices or dedicated terminals assisting the communication between source and destination that cannot directly reach each other. In general, depending on the complexity allowed, a relay can perform decode-and-forward (DF), amplify-and-forward (AF) or compress-and-forward (CF). Due to the extremely simple operation at the relay and easy deployment, AF relaying is particularly suitable for future heterogeneous networks, and receives intense attention from both academia and industry. Channel estimation is an indispensable part in modern wireless receivers. Research on channel estimation in OFDM AF relaying systems began to appear in the past few years. Unfortunately, previous works mostly focus on scenarios when the channel is static or changing very slowly. However, when the mobile terminal is in high speed movement, previous results for slow-varying channel cannot be used, as the estimated channel becomes outdated very quickly. In fact, channel estimation in a rapidly changing point-to-point wireless link without relay is difficult enough. Channel estimation in AF relaying system under fast-fading is even more challenging. This project sets out to systematically study the problem of broadband channel estimation in dual-hop and multi-hop AF relaying systems under high mobility. The difficulties lie in the unknown effects of cascading multiple broadband fast-fading channels, and noise amplification at relays. Furthermore, in order not to cause loss of spectral efficiency due to pilot symbol, superimposed training in frequency domain is employed. The price for this desirable advantage is the challenge of separating pilot and data. By the end of this project, spectral efficient channel estimation algorithms for broadband AF relaying system under high mobility will be developed. They would enable high-data-rate wireless communications even when the terminal is traveling at very high speed. The results would bring new perspective to interference mitigation in superimposed training. Furthermore, they would also facilitate ideas and applications in existing relaying systems and other emerging wireless systems, such as the vehicle-to-vehicle communication in the future intelligent transportation systems.

719111.label: Realisation of objectives
719111.value: Objective 1 (100% completed): For the first objective, we successfully derived the iterative variational inference based receiver for joint channel estimation and data detection for dual-hop AF relaying system. Since the channel is changing from one OFDM to another, the obtained result completes the processing using information from one OFDM symbol only. Simulation results show that the performance is excellent and close to that of ideal case, where channel is perfectly known. This result is published in a journal paper. This part has been mentioned in the progress report before. Objective 2 (100% completed): For the second objective, we first studied the noise amplification effects at multi-hop relaying systems. In particular, we designed optimal MIMO relaying matrices in a multi-hop system under Gaussian channel estimation error. Commonly used relaying matrices design criteria including weighted mean-square-error (MSE) minimization, capacity maximization, worst-MSE minimization and weighted sum-rate maximization, are considered and unified into a single matrix-variate optimization problem. The result has been published in a journal paper. Then, we extended the variational inference based receiver in Objective 1 to multi-hop relaying scenario. After thorough investigation, it is found that under nontrivial transformation on the received signal model, the framework in Objective 1 can be easily put into use in multi-hop case. Since the general framework of variational inference based receiver has already been reported in a journal paper, and in order not to publish similar material again in a journal, we submitted the results on mutli-hop relaying receiver to IEEE International Conference on Communications (ICC) 2014, and the paper has been accepted.

719111.label: Major findings and research outcome
719111.value: The major findings from the two objectives are presented in two IEEE top journal papers, and one top IEEE conference paper. For the #1 paper in Part C, it presents a joint channel estimation and data detection algorithm in orthogonal frequency division mul-tiplexing (OFDM) amplify-and-forward (AF) cooperative systems under high mobility. Unlike previous works on cooperative systems in which a number of subcarriers are solely occupied by pilots, partial data-dependent superimposed training (PDDST) is considered here, thus preserving the spectral efficiency. A closed-form channel estimator is developed based on the least squares (LS) method with Tikhonov regularization and a corresponding data detection algorithm is proposed using the linear minimum mean square error (LMMSE) criterion. In the derived channel estimator, the unknown data is treated as part of the noise and the resulting data detection may not meet the required performance. To address this issue, an iterative method based on the variational inference approach is derived to improve performance. Simulation results show that the data detection performance of the proposed iterative algorithm initialized by the LMMSE data detector is close to the ideal case with perfect channel state information. For the investigation of noise amplification effects at relays, #2 paper in Part C reported on how to design the amplification matrices at relays in a multi-hop MIMO system when the channels are not perfectly known. The criteria of optimization include weighted mean-square-error (MSE), capacity, worst-MSE, MAX-MSE and weighted sum-rate at the destination. These criteria are put into a single matrix-variate optimization framework. A general robust design algorithm is proposed to solve the unified problem. Specifically, by exploiting majorization theory and properties of matrix-variate functions, the optimal structure of the robust transceiver is derived when either the covariance matrix of channel estimation errors seen from the transmitter side or the corresponding covariance matrix seen from the receiver side is proportional to an identity matrix. Based on the optimal structure, the original relaying matrices problems are reduced to much simpler problems with only scalar variables whose solutions are readily obtained by iterative water-filling algorithm. For the #3 paper in Part C, equalization at destination of a multihop relaying orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signal is reported under time-varying channel with unknown noise powers, channel orders and Doppler frequencies. An iterative algorithm is developed under variational expectation maximization (EM) framework. The proposed algorithm iteratively estimates the channel, learns the channel and noise statistical information, and recovers the unknown data, using only limited number of pilot subcarrier in one OFDM symbol. Simulation results show that, without any statistical information, the performance of the proposed algorithm is very close to that of the optimal channel estimation and data detection algorithm, which requires specific information on system structure, channel tap positions, channel lengths, Doppler shifts as well as noise powers.

719111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
719111.value: In the receivers studied in this project, no channel coding is considered. As a future work, we might consider incorporating channel decoding into the receiver structure. In particular, in order to make use of the powerful iterative soft-decoding, soft equalization is needed, instead of hard equalization studied in this project. We expect that this would result in a double-loop receiver, which could be used to explain the existing heuristic-based iterative soft equalization algorithms.

719111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
719111.value: This project investigated the equalization and data detection under fast fading multi-path channels, for dual-hop and multi-hop relaying systems. The studied receiver structure is based on variational inference technique, and the performance of such receiver is found to be very close to that of idea case, where channel is assumed to be perfectly known. This work is important since the results can be applied to relaying systems even all the entities involved are traveling at high speeds. Immediate applications include vehicle-to-vehicle communications on the highway, and signal relaying to and from high speed trains.
