719411.label: Project Objectives
719411.value: To modify the surface chemistry and topography of orthopaedic polymeric material (PEEK) by using novel plasma surface technology e.g. ammonium and water PIII, To systematically evaluate the bioactivity and bio-functional properties of the surface-modified PEEK short-term in-vitro study to attain the best biological performance for subsequent in-vivo biological studies, To study the short term in-vivo biological responses of the plasma-modified PEEK materials to pave the way for future human clinical trials.

719411.label: Realisation of objectives
719411.value: All objectives of this project have been successfully achieved. In brief, our team has successfully demonstrated the improvement of the surface bioactivity of PEEK by implanting ammonium and water plasma through PIII and deposition technology. We found that when polyetheretherketone (PEEK) materials were modified with water and ammonia plasma surface implantation, their surface properties such as morphology and chemistry had been significantly changed and therefore resulted to the enhancement of biocompatibility. However, the original Young’s modulus of PEEK material could be maintained even after the plasma treatment. Most importantly, incredible osseointegration between modified PEEK materials and host bone was found in the animal testing within 2 weeks of implantation. Surprisingly, the Young’s modulus of newly formed bone on modified PEEK surface was significantly higher than that of untreated. We propose that these promising research findings may attribute to the formation of nitrogen-containing and oxygen-containing functional groups on PEEK surface after plasma treatment. Furthermore, porous biomaterials with the proper three-dimensional (3D) surface network can definitely enhance biological functionalities especially in tissue engineering. Hence, we established a 3D porous and nanostructured network with bio-functional groups on PEEK by sulfonation and subsequent water immersion. This custom made 3D porous network significantly induced pre-osteoblast functions including initial cell adhesion, proliferation, and osteogenic differentiation in vitro as well as substantially enhanced osseointegration and bone-implant bonding strength in vivo and apatite-forming ability. Favorable outcomes have been identified by using these new approaches. We believe this will greatly benefit patients requiring orthopaedic implantation in the future, by allowing earlier mobilization and return to a normal lifestyle.

719411.label: Major findings and research outcome
719411.value: In this GRF project, we aimed at enhancing the biofunctionality of polyetheretherkytone (PEEK) materials by using plasma surface modification. Two different plasma sources including ammonia (NH3) and water (H2O) were chosen based on our preliminary data. In the mid-term report, we have already conducted a series of plasma treatment with various implantation voltages (i.e. 10kV, 20kV and 30kV) of both NH3 and H2O plasma treatment and characterized the surface chemistry and topography of the plasma-treated PEEK samples. Moreover, we have also conducted the cytocompatibility assay of the plasma-treated PEEK samples. The results showed that all the plasma-treated samples especially the 30kV NH3- and H2O-treated samples obtained superior cytocompatibility as well as adhesion and proliferation of osteoblasts as compared with the medical grade titanium and untreated PEEK samples. Therefore, these two groups were chosen for further osteogenic differentiation and in vivo studies. MC3T3-E1 mouse pre-osteoblasts were used to test the osteogenic differentiation ability of the plasma-treated samples. Significantly higher alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity was found on both NH3- and H2O-plasma treated samples after 7 days of culture as compared to the untreated PEEK control sample which suggested that the plasma-treated samples were more favorable for osteogenic differentiation. After that, the osteogenic differentiation properties were further assessed by real-time RT-PCR, the mRNA levels of various bone markers including ALP, type I collagen (Colα1) and runt-related transcription factor 2 (Runx2) were found to be significantly higher on days 2, 4, and 7 than the untreated control. The results further confirmed the bioactivity of the plasma-treated samples. Furthermore, the mineralization assay using alizarin red staining was performed to study the mineralization ability of the untreated and plasma-treated samples. Larger mineralized areas were found on the plasma-treated samples in particular to the H2O-plasma treated sample. Hence, all the in vitro data showed the superior bioactivity of the PEEK samples after plasma modification. The next step would be the short-term in vivo animal study. After 8 weeks of implantation, new bone formation was enhanced on the plasma-treated samples especially in the first and second week after surgery providing evidence that NH3- and H2O-plasma treatment were able to stimulate bone formation in a short period of time. This observation was in line with the in vitro studies, in which the higher ALP activity and the up-regulation of bone markers on the plasma modified PEEK surface at early time points was due to the introduction of the oxygen- and nitrogen-containing functional groups. Histology analyses revealed more bone formation after plasma treatment than on the untreated control being consistent with the Micro-CT data, indicating that the plasma-treated PEEK samples is more favorable to bone formation and growth. Furthermore, the elastic moduli of the newly formed bone on the plasma-treated samples were larger than that of the untreated control which indicated that there is highly mineralized bone formation. Further details of all these experimental data can be found in the publication list in Part C.

719411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
719411.value: With the current promising results, the next stage of work will be studying the long-term in vivo response of using both small and large animal models in order to test the long-term osteoconductivity of the plasma modified PEEK samples. Once we finish the in vivo studies and identify the functional groups to enhance the bioactivity of the PEEK materials, we plan to submit another proposal for industrial funding to carry out human clinical trial. Ultimately, patients requiring orthopaedic implantation will be benefited by allowing earlier mobilization and return to a normal lifestyle. Moreover, enhanced osseointegration may help reduce the risk of implant loosening from poor quality in osteoporotic patients as well.

719411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
719411.value: Polyetheretherketone (PEEK) is a newly developed polymeric biomaterial which is an ideal material for orthopaedic applications such as bone void filler, bone screws and plates, and hip prostheses. Unlike other metallic materials, PEEK has much similar mechanical properties to human bones, therefore the problem of the mechanical properties mismatch will be minimized. However, one of the major concerns of using PEEK material is its bioactivity. PEEK is bio-inert which is not favorable for bone apposition. Therefore, current PEEK implants require time to achieve bone-implant integration in order to allow patients to resume full range of body functions. To shorten the time for tissue-implant integration, enhancement of PEEK bioactivity is essential. Fabrication of new composites by incorporating PEEK and other bioactive materials is one approach, however, the mechanical properties of the original PEEK material will be altered. We therefore created a bioactive PEEK surface layer by using plasma surface treatment. We have successfully created nitrogen- and oxygen-containing functional groups on the PEEK samples with the use of the ammonia and water plasma modification. Superior bioactivity and bone forming ability were achieved especially in the early time points which showed the importance and effectiveness of our plasma modification.

719611.value: 三螺旋非编码RNA结构的比对和预测

719611.label: Project Objectives
719611.value: To provide a mathematical model to capture the triple helix structure; to develop algorithms for performing the structural alignment between a known ncRNA with triple helix structure with a target sequence with unknown structure; and to implement these algorithms and evaluate the effectiveness of the resulting tools using real data. To develop algorithm(s) to predict the secondary structure of a given ncRNA with triple helix structure and to implement and evaluate the effectiveness of the algorithm(s) using real data.
rows: To provide a mathematical model to capture the triple helix structure; to develop algorithms for performing the structural alignment between a known ncRNA with triple helix structure with a target sequence with unknown structure; and to implement these algorithms and evaluate the effectiveness of the resulting tools using real data.
To develop algorithm(s) to predict the secondary structure of a given ncRNA with triple helix structure and to implement and evaluate the effectiveness of the algorithm(s) using real data.

719611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
719611.value: 非编码RNA(nc RNA)是指各种不会被翻译成蛋白质的RNA分子。ncRNA的重要性已广为知晓，许多至关重要的生物过程它们都有参与。但其不能翻译产生蛋白质的特性，使得试图通过生化实验来识别ncRNA的过程变得很困难。不过同时，也有研究表明，从属同一RNA家族且功能类似的ncRNA，它们的一级序列（primary sequence）和二级结构(secondary structure)也类似。这为我们提供了一种利用计算方法来寻找ncRNA的新思路：为识别新的ncRNA, 基于一个已知的ncRNA和其二级结构, 先将它与基因组所有的子片段进行比对；如果某个片段与这个已知ncRNA有相似的一级序列和二级结构，其很可能是与已知nCRNA从属同一RNA家族的一种未知ncRNA，那我们可以将其列为潜在的新ncRNA。这种方法包括两个主要步骤：（1）已知ncRNA和目标序列（基因组子片段）的结构匹配；（2）已知ncRNA二级结构的预测（当已知ncRNA的二级结构未知时）。因此我们主要着眼于对应的两种计算问题。 ncRNA的一级序列可以看作是由四种字符（称作核苷酸，或碱基）{A，C，G，U}组成的字符序列。一级序列中，碱基之间可以通过互相作用形成氢键，而氢键连接形成的碱基对则组成了ncRNA的二级结构。通常我们认为，在这个过程中，每个碱基最多只会和另外一个碱基发生作用，这是现有的结构匹配和预测方法所都依赖的假设。但是，有证据表明，除一对一作用形式之外，有一种三级的相互作用形式存在：即已组成碱基对的碱基与另外一个单独的碱基发生作用，形成一种三螺旋结构，而这种三螺旋结构是ncRNA能实现很多功能的关键所在。因而，识别三螺旋结构的新ncRNA是非常重要，但目前，这方面的工作却尚未受到重视。 在这个研究计划中，我们期望系统阐述并解决关于带三螺旋结果的ncRNA的结构匹配和预测的难题。现有的对RNA二级结构的定义不能反应出碱基之间的三级的相互作用。在这个研究项目中，我们计划旨在完成以下事项: （1）给出能准确描述出碱基间三级相互作用的ncRNA的二级结构的数学定义；（2）设计解决带三螺旋结构的ncRNA结构匹配问题的算法；（3）基于（或不基于）生物实验得到的附加信息，设计解决带三螺旋结构的ncRNA二级结构预测问题的算法。 我们期望这项研究成果有助于生物信息领域的科研者研究ncRNA结构和功能。

719611.label: Realisation of objectives
719611.value: For Objective (1), in order to come up with a realistic mathematical model, we downloaded all available real data (i.e., non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs)) from well-known database and investigated known triple helix structures. Based on our study, we provided an abstract model for triple helix structure. Based on this definition, an algorithm was designed to align a target ncRNA sequence with unknown structure with an ncRNA with known structure. We implemented the algorithm and evaluated the effectiveness of the tools based on real data. The result has been published in a prestigious journal (Journal of Computational Biology). For Objective (2), we defined a local energy model to capture the stability of RNA molecule. Based on this model, we derived a dynamic programming algorithm to predict the secondary structure of a given cRNA with triple helix structure. The algorithm has been implemented and evaluated. The result has been published in a conference (PRIB 2013). Based on our study, we also develop a single grammar that can be used to capture all real secondary structures that can be found in the existing databases. A prediction algorithm based on this grammar was developed and evaluated based on real datasets. The result has been published in a conference (ISBRA 2015).

719611.label: Major findings and research outcome
719611.value: (1) We identified common features in existing triple helix structures based on known ncRNA data. We abstracted these features and defined a mathematical model to capture these structures. The result has been published in Journal of Computational Biology [8(1) of Part C]. (2) Based on the model defined in (1), we developed a structural alignment algorithm that can help to predict unknown structure of an ncRNA by aligning it to known structure of ncRNAs. The evaluation result has been shown to be promising [8(1) of Part C]. (3) We defined a local energy model for triple helix structure to capture the stability of the ncRNA molecule. Based on this energy model, we developed a structure prediction algorithm for triple helix structure. The algorithm and the evaluation result has been shown in [9(1) of Part C]. (4) Based on our study and knowledge in secondary structure, we also developed a generic grammar to model all available secondary structures that can be found in existing databases. Based on this grammar, a generic secondary algorithm has been developed. The result has been published in [9(2) of Part C]. (5) In addition, the funding has also been used to support the following research projects: (a) developing an efficient algorithm for aligning long RNAs and (b) aligning multiple protein sequences. Both results were published in well-known journals [8(2) and 8(3) of Part C].

719611.value: Secondary structure and triple helix structure prediction for RNAs are very important. It would be better if we could speed up all the algorithms developed in the project to make the prediction faster. And making the prediction and alignment more accurate is obvious an open problem to be investigated. We will continue to improve the algorithms and the models developed in the project in order to benefit the community in RNA research.

719611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
719611.value: RNA molecule is found to be critical in many metabolic processes in our body. It is known that the secondary structure of an RNA molecule is closely related to its functionalities. However, it is difficult and time-consuming to investigate the secondary structure of a given RNA molecule in laboratories. In this project, we developed computational methods that can help us predict unknown secondary structures (in particular, the triple helix structure which is known to be important but not well-studied) of RNA molecules. The results from this project could speed up the study of RNA molecules in various metabolism of human as well as their functionalities in diseases.

719711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
719711.value: Cold-formed steel structural members may lead to a more economic design than hot-rolled steel members as a result of their superior strength to weight ratio and ease of construction. Light weight cold-formed steel members are commonly used as wall studs and chord members of roof trusses in steel frame housing, industrial buildings, low-rise office and hospital buildings. One of the good examples of using cold-formed steel was during the outbreak of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) virus in the year 2003. A large scale low-rise hospital building for the SARS patients was constructed in approximately a week in the outskirts of Beijing, China. This example has shown the ease and speed of construction using light weight cold-formed steel. Cold-formed steel members are cold-rolled or brake-pressed into structural shapes to form channel section, Z-section and other sections. These sections are considered as “open” sections due to the cold-forming formation process. It should be noted that open sections have a relatively small torsional rigidity (weak in twisting) compared to “closed” sections and doubly-symmetric sections. However, built-up box-shaped sections are one of the closed sections that can be formed by two channel sections connected at their flanges. The closed sections have a relatively large torsional rigidity compared with open sections. Therefore, closed sections are structurally more efficient than open sections. Cold-formed steel sections could be influenced by local buckling depending on the plate width to thickness ratio. Cold-formed steel section formed by two open sections with web and edge stiffeners connected together can provide a structurally efficient section having large torsional rigidity and high local buckling stress. Therefore, cold-formed steel built-up sections with web and edge stiffeners will be investigated. The purpose of this project is to investigate the behaviour of cold-formed steel built-up closed and open sections with stiffeners through both experimental and numerical investigation. A series of column tests will be conducted. The numerical investigation using finite element analysis will be performed. Furthermore, design equations for cold-formed steel built-up sections with web and edge stiffeners will be proposed. The proposed design rules would lead to a more economical and safe design for cold-formed steel structures. This project would enhance the international competitiveness of China and Hong Kong in advanced steel construction technology.

719711.value: The cold-formed steel built-up sections with web and edge stiffeners have been investigated. A series of tests on cold-formed steel built-up sections was carried out. An advanced nonlinear finite element models for cold-formed steel built-up sections were developed and also verified against the experimental results. An extensive parametric study of cross-section geometry and the spacing of self-tapping screws on cold-formed steel built-up sections was performed. The appropriateness of the current direct strength method on cold-formed steel built-up sections was assessed. New design rules for cold-formed steel built-up sections with web and edge stiffeners are proposed. Reliability analysis was performed to evaluate the proposed design rules. The research findings have been published in SCI indexed international journal papers as well as international conference papers. The six objectives of the project have been achieved.

720111.label: Project Objectives
720111.value: To quantify the dynamic of ARB and ARG in different treatment units of municipal sewage treatment plants. The dynamic of ARG and ARB depends highly on the operations and designs of STPs and may be affected by many factors. Thus, it is hard to draw solid conclusions based on a few grab samplings. In this study, a systematic sampling program will be conducted to take samples from primary clarifier, activated sludge, effluent from secondary clarifier, effluent from disinfection unit, digested sludge and dewatered biosolids will be collected. The antibiotics resistant bacteria will be isolated and tested for their resistance spectrum. Antibiotics resistant genes will be quantified using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR). To investigate decay rate and stabilization efficiency of ARB and ARG in aerobic and anaerobic sludge digestion processes. ARB and ARG in activated sludge will eventually decay and be stabilized in sludge digestion under aerobic or anaerobic conditions. However, little is known about the decay rates and stabilization efficiencies in the two types of sludge digesters. In this study, continuous reactors will be operated to study the decay rate and stabilization efficiency of ARB/ARG using the methods established. To investigate joint selection of antibiotic resistance and disinfectant resistance during chlorination and ozonation. Although chlorination and ozonation is designed to kill all bacteria, it has reported that ARB may tolerate more than non-ARB, resulting in the selective prevalence of ARB in the effluent from disinfection unit. In this project, ARB and non-ARB will be characterized for their susceptibility to disinfectants, such as hypochlorite acid (chlorination) and ozone.

720111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
720111.value: Antibiotics resistant bacteria (ARB) and their resistance genes (ARG) are becoming a major global health issue as demonstrated by frequently reported superbugs having multi-resistance to antibiotics, such as β-lactam resistant Escherichia coli carrying NDM-1 plasmid. Environments which are most directly impacted by human activities showed higher concentrations of antibiotic resistant bacteria and antibiotic resistance genes, mainly due to municipal wastewater discharge. Biological wastewater treatment plants, such as the activated sludge process, may be significant sources of antibiotic resistance to the environment. The release of ARB into rivers through wastewater effluents and into soil/groundwater through biosolid has been reported. However, the role of sewage treatment plants (STP) in reducing the load of antibiotic resistant bacteria present in raw sewage is not well known. It has also been suggested that certain conditions within the STPs might increase the abundance of ARB in the total bacterial community during the biological treatment process, due to the horizontal transfer of ARG in activated sludge and selective disinfection of sensitive bacteria. So far, only limited information is available in literature on this problem and on its potential threat to the environment. This study is proposed 1) to quantify the dynamics of ARB and ARG in different treatment units of municipal sewage treatment plants; 2) to investigate decay rates and stabilization efficiencies of ARB and ARG in aerobic and anaerobic sludge digestion processes; 3) to investigate joint selection of antibiotic resistance and disinfectant resistance during chlorination and ozonation. The results could be used to estimate the burden of ARB and ARG released to environments and will also help the understanding of the possible joint selection of antibiotics resistance and disinfectant resistance. 抗生素抗性的細菌及其耐藥基因正在成為一個全球性的環境污染問題。已有報導證明一些超級病菌具有多重耐藥性，如大腸桿菌NDM–1就攜帶β-內酰胺類耐藥基因。廢水中存在的微量抗生素對細菌產生和維持抗藥性基因有重要作用，生物污水處理廠，如活性污泥，可顯著含有高濃度的抗生素抗性細菌和相關基因。排放到水體中的抗生素抗性細菌和基因會隨著污水進入土壤/地下水並進一步在環境中擴散。另外，由於細菌之間存在基因的橫向轉移，因此在一定條件下抗性細菌在廢水出水中的濃度會有所提高。尤其是加氯消毒過程會選擇性地增加對氯和抗生素都有抗性的細菌。因此有必要充分了解污水處理廠在減少抗生素抗性細菌方面的作用。目前，相關的研究十分有限。本研究將： 1）評估城市污水處理廠中不同處理單元對抗生素抗性細菌的去除; 2）調查好氧和厭氧污泥消化中抗生素抗性細菌的變化; 3）研究加氯消毒對抗生素抗性和抗氯特性的共選擇。其結果可以用來評估抗性細菌和基因在廢水處理廠中的歸宿，也有助於了解抗生素抗藥性及抗氯性共選擇的可能性。

720111.label: Realisation of objectives
720111.value: Objective 1: Activated sludge harboring dense and diverse microorganisms is an important part for reserving ARGs and the horizontal gene transfer of ARGs among different microbial communities. Existence of six β-lactam resistance genes were found through PCR and QPCR approach in activated sludge collected in 15 WWTPs in East Asia and North America. The abundance of the detected β-lactam resistance genes ranged from 5.34×10 copies/ng DNA to 5.49×104 copies/ng DNA. Broad-spectrum profiles ARGs in activated sludge in the time span of four years were further investigated through sequence-based metagenomic analysis. A total of 16 ARGs types were detected in the samples. Descending trend of total ARGs abundance was found but abundances of β-lactam resistance genes and quinolone resistance genes increased. Moreover, some ARGs types showed seasonal variation in summer and winter. Objective 2: Sequence-based metagenomic analysis was also applied to study the fate of ARGs in wastewater/sludge treatment process. Results suggested that 99.82% ARGs in influent could be removed by wastewater treatment process while only 20.70% of ARGs could be removed in sludge anaerobic digestion. Through redundancy analysis, the distribution of ARGs in WWTP was significantly correlated with six genera and five of which included potential pathogens. The processes in sequence-based metagenomic analysis were optimized to shorten the analysis time and simplified the ARGs-like sequences classification process. The widely used reference database of ARGs was optimized through removing error and redundant sequences. Structured database was constructed to realize the automatic classification of ARGs in metagenomic data. A hybrid alignment process was optimized for rapid ARGs or other specific functional genes annotation as well. Objective 3: The effect of chlorination and ozonation on joint selection of ARGs has been studied using the established metagenomic approach. The results has demonstrated the profiles of ARGs after chlorination. However, our results showed the decrease of total ARGs after chlorination compared with the total level before the chlorination. This is different from the results of previous reports. The main reason might be due to the approach used in previous studies, which is limited by the primers available in their researches.

720111.label: Major findings and research outcome
720111.value: The wide spread of antibiotic resistant bacteria (ARB) and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) have attracted great concerns around the world. Wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) are recognized as the reservoirs of ARGs while wastewater/sludge treatment process is also considered as important means to control these emerging biological pollutants. However, the full profiles of ARGs in WWTPs or the efficiency of wastewater/sludge treatment process in removing ARGs was not well characterized yet. Thus, the major tasks of this study were (1) to quantify the dynamic of ARB and ARG in different treatment units of municipal sewage treatment plants. (2) to investigate decay rate and stabilization efficiency of ARB and ARG in sludge digestion processes.to investigate the removal efficiency of ARGs in wastewater/sludge treatment process; (3) to investigate joint selection of antibiotic resistance and disinfectant resistance during chlorination and ozonation. Activated sludge harboring dense and diverse microorganisms is an important part for reserving ARGs and the horizontal gene transfer of ARGs among different microbial communities. Existence of six β-lactam resistance genes were found through PCR and QPCR approach in activated sludge collected in 15 WWTPs in East Asia and North America. The abundance of the detected β-lactam resistance genes ranged from 5.34×10 copies/ng DNA to 5.49×104 copies/ng DNA. Broad-spectrum profiles ARGs in activated sludge in the time span of four years were further investigated through sequence-based metagenomic analysis. A total of 16 ARGs types were detected in the samples. Descending trend of total ARGs abundance was found but abundances of β-lactam resistance genes and quinolone resistance genes increased. Moreover, some ARGs types showed seasonal variation in summer and winter. Sequence-based metagenomic analysis was also applied to study the fate of ARGs in wastewater/sludge treatment process. Results suggested that 99.82% ARGs in influent could be removed by wastewater treatment process while only 20.70% of ARGs could be removed in sludge anaerobic digestion. Through redundancy analysis, the distribution of ARGs in WWTP was significantly correlated with six genera and five of which included potential pathogens. Lastly, the processes in sequence-based metagenomic analysis were optimized to shorten the analysis time and simplified the ARGs-like sequences classification process. The widely used reference database of ARGs was optimized through removing error and redundant sequences. Structured database was constructed to realize the automatic classification of ARGs in metagenomic data. A hybrid alignment process was optimized for rapid ARGs or other specific functional genes annotation as well.

720111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
720111.value: The present study mainly focused on ARGs investigation in WWTPs environment, sequenced-based metagenomic analysis was the major technological mean used. Several recommendations are purposed for future studies based on the previously obtained experience. (1) The timely update and optimization of ARGs reference database is essential for the application of sequence-based metagenomic analysis in the investigation of environmental ARGs since the reference database of high quality is the basic for getting a reliable result from metagenomic analysis. (2) The combination of sequenced-based metagenomic analysis and the traditional PCR and qPCR approaches would be more powerful in studying the fate of ARGs through wastewater treatment process. (3) The detection of MGEs carrying ARGs is a noteworthy issue for the spread of ARGs in WWTPs environment. Applying sequenced metagenomic analysis, the existence of ARGs and MGEs, such as plasmid, transposon, integron and bacteriophage can be examined simultaneously. (4) The application of metagenomic analysis can be used in the removal of ARGs through advanced wastewater treatment or disinfection process, such as tertiary treatment, chlorination, UV treatment, etc. to reveal the effect of these now available treatment processes in the removal ARGs from wastewater.

Descending trend of total ARGs abundance was found but abundances of β-lactam resistance genes and quinolone resistance genes increased. Sequence-based metagenomic analysis was also applied to study the fate of ARGs in wastewater/sludge treatment process. Results suggested that 99.8% ARGs in influent could be removed by wastewater treatment process while only 20.7% of ARGs could be removed in sludge anaerobic digestion. Lastly, the processes in metagenomic analysis were optimized to shorten the analysis time and simplify classification process.

How does fear of crime or lack of it relate to expressions of trust, or distrust, in crime control authorities?
How do citizens make sense of their orientations to crime in light of efforts to promote citizenship and identification with Hong Kong?
How can conducting focus groups serve to promulgate knowledge generation amongst participants and other citizens, and advance theories of effective focus group design and implementation?

740211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
740211.value: This project will examine experiences and attitudes towards the related notions of fear of crime and trust in crime control among different social groups in Hong Kong. Hong Kong provides a curious case for criminologists. In contrast to many industrialised nations with high rates of crime, fear of crime and low levels of trust, Hong Kong maintains low levels of crime and a high degree of trust in police despite its dense urban environment, concentrated population and income disparity. Hong Kong’s criminogenic uniqueness is heightened by a geo-political history shaped by its proximity to Mainland China, the handover of the region to China from British governance in 1997, and related concerns regarding citizen identification with the region and social order. Although public surveys have consistently shown that Hong Kong citizens trust highly in their police and hold relatively low levels of fear regarding crime, we know relatively little about the actual meanings and local, situated contexts through which ‘fear of crime’ and ‘trust in crime control’ are interpreted and experienced by different social groups in Hong Kong. This project aims to fill this gap by exploring, through the use of focus groups, Hong Kong citizens’ ‘crime consciousness’ and the multidimensional aspects connecting expressions of fear of crime with trust in crime control authorities. We ask three inter-related sets of research questions: 1)How do Hong Kong citizens articulate their fears of crime? What reasons do they give for why they hold these fears? 2)How does fear of crime, or lack of it, relate to expressions of trust, or distrust, in crime control authorities? 3)How do citizens make sense of their orientations to crime in light of efforts to promote citizenship and identification with Hong Kong? Thirty (30) focus groups over a three year period will be assessed to study levels of trust in crime control and fear of crime among Hong Kong citizens. This research will advance knowledge regarding the ‘lived experiences’ of Hong Kong citizens with respect to trust and fear of crime, exploring connections between personal and collective histories of experience. In addition, it seeks to draw connections between these experiences and government efforts to promote citizenship in Hong Kong. Finally, this research will make a methodological contribution, advancing theories about focus groups as both a tool for knowledge generation with and between community members. 本项目致力于探讨香港社会不同群体对于犯罪的恐惧以及犯罪控制中的信任的相关观念的经验和态度。 香港为犯罪学家们提供了一个好奇的例子。和许多工业化的国家高犯罪率、高犯罪恐惧以及低信任相比，尽管香港有着密集的都市环境、集中的人口以及收入不均，它却维持着较的低犯罪率以及对警察的高度信任。香港犯罪状态的独特之处有着其特别的地缘政治与历史，这些因素包括毗邻中国大陆、1997年香港回归中国、以及市民关于区域的认同以及社会秩序的担忧。 尽管公共调查一直显示香港市民对于警察有着高度信任以及对于犯罪的恐惧度较低，但是我们对于其实际的涵义以及其本土的、具体的情境知之甚少。正是在这些具体的情境中，香港的不同社会群体来解读以和经历对“犯罪的恐惧”以及对“犯罪控制中的信任”。 使用小组访谈的方法，探讨香港市民的“犯罪意识”以及对于犯罪恐惧和犯罪控制部门的信任等多个方面，本项目力图弥补这一空缺。我们将致力于研究三组相互联系的问题： １） 香港市民如何阐述他们对于犯罪的恐惧？出于什么原因他们有这些恐惧？ ２） 对于犯罪的恐惧/不恐惧和他们对于犯罪控制部门的信任/不信任的表示有何相关？ ３） 在至力于推崇公民权以及对于香港认同的背景下，市民如何理解他们对于犯罪的态度？ 我们计划在三年时间内时行30个小组访谈来研究香港市民对于犯罪控制的信任以及对于犯罪恐惧的水平。 通过探讨个人以及集体的经历的历史，这项研究可以提升我们对于香港市民有关犯罪的信任和恐惧的“生活经验”的理解。而且，它致力于在这些经验和政府推崇公民权的努力之间寻找某种联系。最后，本研究在方法论上也有所贡献，提升小组访谈理论既作为与社区成员之间又成为其内部的理论生产的工具。

740211.label: Realisation of objectives
740211.value: The GRF study has achieved the project objectives through the completion of extensive fieldwork research. A total of 30 focus groups with 156 men and women over 16 years of age were conducted to investigate public perceptions of crime and policing among a broad cross-section of Hong Kong citizens ranging from those living in private and public housing in urban areas, middle class and working class communities, ‘satellite’ and border towns in the New Territories to outlying islands. A non-probability, snowball sampling design targeted a wide range of sources for participant referrals, including NGOs (e.g. community organizations and organizations advocating for children and youth, the socially disadvantaged groups living in ‘cubicle’ homes) as well as personal and professional networks (e.g. volunteers in local schools and highly skilled professional groups). Participants also helped refer us to other contacts to broaden the class and neighbourhood coverage of the project. We asked people what they think and feel about crime and disorder in Hong Kong; their views of the police’s ability to combat crime, maintain order, solve social problems, and reduce their fear of crime in the local neighbourhood; their encounters with the police if any, and the ways in which such interactions may impact upon their assessments of police and police action. All the focus group discussions were fully transcribed and professionally translated into English. Using NVivo software for qualitative data analysis, prominent themes emerged through the tracking of coding ‘nodes’ both across and within groups and were systematically analysed. The results have been disseminated through international conference presentations, publications and other knowledge exchange activities (including an exhibition and symposium for senior police officers and NGOs). In relation to the four specific project objectives, the methodology and findings: 1. Go beyond quantitative surveys that typically measure how 'safe' people feel when they walk alone after dark to reveal how men and women, the young and the old, actually think and feel about crime and the social meaning of their crime fears. We examined public perceptions and experiences of crime and policing through a series of focus group discussions conducted in different neighbourhoods. It was evident from the discussions that participants regard Hong Kong as a ‘safe city’ and do not feel frightened of crime. This was the case even when respondents have had personal experiences of victimization. However, discussions also reveal that people's feelings of (un)safety do not emerge solely from direct experiences of victimization nor only from events formally defined as crime. Instead, 'fear of crime' is multifaceted, changeable and embedded in people's everyday experiences. In appraising crime and safety, different social groups react to and make sense of a range of physical and social signal disorders in their neighbourhood which they regard as troubling, threatening and anti-social. 2. Advance our understanding of people's level of satisfaction and trust in different dimensions of policing work. The focus group discussions highlight the important distinction between people’s instrumental concerns about personal safety and their affective concerns about the process of policing and the symbolic role of the police. In general, participants in the study display a high level of satisfaction with and trust in the police which is based on their assessment of the technical competence and dependability of the police as crime-fighters. But this is only part of the story. The focus groups highlight the relevance of a multi-dimensional framework of trust where people care about fairness and respectfulness in direct encounters between police and members of the public. Young people were the most vocal in expressing dissatisfaction about personal encounters with street level policing especially in 'stop and search'. Similarly, participants revealed strong yet mixed opinions about the policing of public order events, especially politically charged protests. Disagreements about the process of policing and motives of the police are most notably related to public order policing, when citizens look to the police as a strong and active symbol of the values that underpin a particular way of life in HK. 3. Illuminate the ways in which different social groups make sense of crime fighting campaigns and police initiatives to promote good citizenship. Participants, especially those who were older and could compare their experiences of crime and policing today with the past, were able to reflect upon changes regarding both levels of crime (e.g. a consensus that levels of crime were higher in the past) and perceptions of police (e.g. a consensus that police professionalism has improved). Younger participants were able to assess the effectiveness of police initiatives such as the Junior Police Call and police efforts at citizen communication through social media and school liaison. 4. Highlight the value of focus groups in generating extremely rich data on crime fears grounded in citizens' meaning frames and everyday experiences in their neighbourhood. Focus group sessions lasted an average of 1.5 hours and were conducted in Cantonese. They were held at locations on or in close proximity to members’ own ‘turf’, in order to help participants feel comfortable and facilitate open and dynamic discussions. Venues included community centres, churches, private clubhouses and residences, university campuses, local schools and places of work. Groups were kept relatively homogeneous along the lines of age, gender and class. This ensured that participants will interact with others less likely perceived as threatening (e.g. in discussion about sexual assault). Group discussions create important interactional dynamics between participants, especially when they raised questions amongst themselves and helped to steer the discussion about neighbourhood problems and anxieties. Such dynamics reinforces research on focus group design and implementation conducted on 'crime talk' elsewhere (e.g. in the UK and USA), suggesting the methodological value of focus group research (within and beyond criminology) in Hong Kong. Specifically, we corroborated suggestions regarding ideal focus group size (between 3-6 participants) in order to facilitate communication, and as mentioned, the importance of keeping groups homogeneous to help participants feel secure in disclosing experiences and perceptions amongst others. Ethically the research underscores the importance for focus group research to secure both 'vertical' consent (i.e. between researcher and participants) and 'horizontal' consent (i.e. that members of the group agree to keep what is said confidential amongst themselves).

740211.label: Major findings and research outcome
740211.value: The study examines how men and women, the young and the old, think, feel and behave about crime and safety in Hong Kong. The focus group discussions confirm that citizens generally regard Hong Kong as a safe city. However, people also have anxieties about risks and insecurity which are embedded in their social perceptions and everyday experiences, including general assessment of the state of law and order in the larger society; general anxiety about the neighbourhood; subscription to the normative views in society and to the moral authority; their sense of identity and belonging amidst broader social and political changes in Hong Kong. Importantly, people's crime fears are based on perceptions and experiences of troubling behaviours and disorderly environments that send signals to them about the distribution of risks and threats in particular locales. These signals include signs of social disorder such as adults' encounters with troublesome youths or the presence of parallel goods traders; young people's encounters with bullies and young women's encounters with sex perverts in public spaces; physical signals of disorder such as discarded syringes in working class neighbourhoods. The study found that, in general, citizens have a high level of satisfaction with and trust in the police based on an instrumental assessment of the technical competence and dependability of police as crime-fighters in a low-crime society. However, people also care about the process of policing. In this context, the results of people's level of satisfaction are more mixed. Their assessments of the police in crime and non-crime related matters – and the behaviour of officers in relation to fairness, openness and respectfulness when dealing with members of the public – do matter in shaping people’s wider attitudes towards the police and their trust in policing. Differences in opinion about the process of policing and motives of the police are most notably related to public order policing, where citizens look to the police as a strong and active symbol of the values that underpin a particular way of life in Hong Kong. To date, these key findings have been published in two edited book chapters and an international journal, and disseminated through five international conferences, two local policing symposiums, an international seminar for scholars, Summer Institute for international university students, and a public exhibition at HKU (see Part C).

740211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
740211.value: The dissemination of the GRF study has brought opportunities for international collaboration in comparative study - for instance, the ongoing project (Jan 2014 – Jan 2018) by Co-Investigator Michael Adorjan (now at the University of Calgary, Canada) and an international team of researchers – Rose Ricciardelli (PI, Memorial University of Newfoundland, Canada), Mary Ann Campbell (Co-I, University of New Brunswick, Canada), Laura Huey (Co-I, University of Western Ontario, Canada), Nicole Power (Co-I, Memorial University of Newfoundland), Dale Spencer (Co-I, Carleton University, Canada), Wing Hong Chui (Collaborator, City University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong), Boyd Merrill (Collaborator, Royal Canadian Mounted Police), Wayne Newell (Collaborator, RCMP). The project is titled “Creating ‘best practice’ for policing youth: Discovering, re-evaluating, re-shaping and reviving hope for youth desistance through changing relational dynamics between youth and police, a bottom-up and top-down process.” RCMP B Division, CAN$866,682. With Dr. Adorjan now conducting research in Western Canada (currently a SSHRC Insight Development Grant examining perceptions of cyber-risk among adolescents), and with his graduate students currently involved in projects examining perceptions of police impacted through social media, there are opportunities to build comparative projects not only between Hong Kong and Canada but in the realm of cyberspace as well.

740211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
740211.value: The study examines how citizens think, feel and behave about crime and safety in Hong Kong. It is based on 30 focus group discussions with a total sample of 156 male and female participants across a wide section of society. The study shows that citizens generally regard Hong Kong as a safe city. However, people also have anxieties about risks and insecurity which are based on their perceptions and everyday experiences of anti-social behaviours, incivilities in the neighbourhood, general assessment of the state of law and order, and their sense of identity and belonging amidst broader socio-political changes. In general, citizens have a high level of satisfaction with and trust in the police as crime-fighters based on their assessment of the technical competence and dependability of the police in a low-crime society. However, people also care about the process of policing, fairness and respectfulness in police-public encounters. Here, the results are more mixed. Differences in opinion about the process of policing and motives of the police are most notably related to public order policing, where citizens look to the police as a strong and active symbol of the values that underpin a particular way of life in Hong Kong.

740211.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
740211.value: The study has made a significant and timely contribution to raising public awareness and policy debates about crime and safety and policing in Hong Kong through a number of scholarly presentations, policy-oriented dissemination as well as innovative knowledge exchange activities: 1. An invited talk in February 2012 for the Hong Kong Police Studies Forum titled "Fear of Crime and Trust in Crime Control in Hong Kong." The talk was geared to report on preliminary results from the project and receive feedback from participants, who included criminology graduate students and members of the PSF, including researchers from various universities of Hong Kong conducting research on police and policing. http://www.policingstudiesforum.com/Policing_Studies/Home.html 2. An invited talk in December 2012 for the Hong Kong Police Studies Forum titled "Women’s Views of Policing in Hong Kong: Some Preliminary Results." The talk was geared to report on preliminary results (this time with an emphasis on gender) from the project and receive feedback from participants, who included criminology graduate students and members of the PSF, including researchers from various universities of Hong Kong conducting research on police and policing. http://www.policingstudiesforum.com/Policing_Studies/Home.html 3. Presentation on 'Crime and Safety in Hong Kong: Citizen Perceptions and Challenges for the Police' at the Symposium on Policing Challenges in the 21st Century: Hong Kong held at The University of Hong Kong, June 2013. Audience included senior Hong Kong Police Force officers and representatives from other criminal justice agencies and NGOs from HK and overseas. 4. Presentation and dialogue with practitioners at a half-day Roundtable Symposium on 'Fear of Crime and Trust in Crime Control in Hong Kong' at The University of Hong Kong, November 2013. Senior representatives from the Hong Kong Police Force, Complaints Against Police Office and key NGOs (e.g. Unison) took part in the event to discuss the research findings and the implications for policy and practices. As a direct result of the two Symposiums, the PI and the Centre for Criminology at HKU (Prof Karen Laidler as Director) have been in ongoing dialogue with the HK Police College to explore the feasibility of conducting related research and training for police officers in relation to youth engagement. 5. Presentation on 'Becoming like China: Mainlandization and perceptions of disorder and political policing in Hong Kong' organised by Department of Sociology Committee on Scholarly Events and Presentations (COSEP) Speaker Series, University of Calgary, Canada, February 2014. This has consolidated links with international researchers in the field examining public perceptions of police. A new related project is currently underway, titled “Creating ‘best practice’ for policing youth' funded by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (see Full Report, Part B section 6.2). 6. An invited talk in Feb 2015 for the University of Calgary's Chinese Interdisciplinary Group, titled "Public Perceptions of the Hong Kong Police Force: Confidence and Legitimacy in the Post Colonial Era." The audience included students and faculty members involved with the CIG who conduct research on China and Chinese populations in Canada. 7. Presentation on 'Crime in Asia' at the HKU Summer Institute 'Asia as the Global Future', June 2015. Audience included top university students from overseas institutions. 8. The GRF study was included in 'HKU Criminology Through the Years' exhibition at MCCC@702 Creative Space, HKU, in April 2016. The exhibition showcased cutting edge research studies on crime and criminal justice in Hong Kong [https://www.facebook.com/HkuMccc/]. It was covered extensively by SCMP and Ming Pao and well attended by the general public, secondary school students (e.g. Maryknoll Convent School and Marymount Secondary School) and overseas delegation (Canadian Association of Chiefs of Police). We are currently in discussion with the Police Museum and Correctional Services Museum to see if the exhibition can continue at their sites.

740311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
740311.value: The 21st century has not ushered in a time of greater peace and increased racial equality, perhaps to the surprise of none. W. E. B. Dubois’s famous proclamation that “The problem of the twentieth century is the problem of the color line” is not only true for the United States of America, but also for other parts of the world. This project proposes a comparative reading of how “the problem of the color line” takes shape in the US, a major superpower, and Malaysia, a South East Asian nation in the developing world. My transnational comparison of racial formations in Asian America and Malaysia explores the contemporaneous emergence of narratives of victimization and ethics in divergent historical and socio-political contexts for an understanding of what makes those narratives plausible across such dissemblance. The project will contribute to our understanding of the role “ethics” and discourses about “ethics” or “morality” plays in the formation of our ideas about race and nation because cultural productions such as literature and film, as well as the debates that surround them, have a significant impact on political life and social life. However, as some critics argue, representations of race, its conflicts, and its effects, can sometimes take contradictory forms in popular discourse. Similar ideas about race as a “problem” materialize in nation-states with different social, political, and cultural institutions and I trace the flows of political and moral ideals that shape racial thinking in their contradictions as they appear in different geographical locations. While this project will provide historical narratives of the manifestations of these ideals, it also considers a comparison that does not rely on historical continuities between both locations nor will it reduce racial formations in both contexts to equivalence. In other words, the comparison of race relations between the US and Malaysia is not based on direct colonial relationships, and it aims to retain the singularities of both. This project will offer new ways of understanding race, literature, and what the practice of comparison can reveal in the way our disciplines produce knowledge. Such a comparison could arguably be taken up using different national examples and this is precisely the strength and relevance of the project because it models a form of argument not founded upon temporal or spatial contingence that presents either causal or analogic explanations. 《道德規範、種族和比較的問題》爭論了一個國家的少數族群的紀律是長久以來道德規範與道德權威建立同時並存的問題。通過倫理道德責任考驗了敍事者去合并和合法化“亞洲人”，這一本書探究了種族觀念在物質上及象徵意義上的影響。這本書就美國及馬來西亞所創作的文學與電影作品做了充分的研究，並以一個嶄新的角度去了解很多經典或鮮為人所知的文學及電影作品；透過這些作品如何運用倫理道德語言，間接地塑造和影响種族與國家的觀念。在比較種族研究和在美洲的亞洲人這兩個研究領域中，這本著作檢視了敍事的道德優越性、犠牲及宗教責任，並引領讀者去了解種族化及他或她與國家的關係。 透過比較及跨國研究方法，這本書揭露了種族及道德規範在美國及馬來西亞所被理解的相同及相異之處。這個比較亦超越了單一國家或單一區域框架那傳統應用在文學與電影研究方面的侷限，透過倫理的鏡頭，這個研究還提供了種族與種族關係的歴史性敍事，而這個比較並不是依靠兩個地方歴史的延續性，亦不是將兩個種族簡化為相等，而是旨在保留兩個國家的獨特性，而其關係並不是建立在直接殖民主義的或新殖民主義的關係上。這個研究亦對種族暴力的全球化問題之成因與影響提供了一個新的觀點，那就是在多元及有時候相互矛盾的情況下産生與維持它。通過不同國家的例子做比較相當受人關注，這也是此研究的長處與相關性，因為它塑造了一個爭論的形式，而這一個形式並非建基於時空的條件上，即因果或類推的解釋。這個在美洲的亞洲人與馬來西亞之間的比較實在恰到好處，因為這兩個民主體系均是依靠在種族的契約上。

740911.value: 中國的精神病院考(1898-1949): 追朔共和制时代歐美在中國早期精神病學發展史上的影響

740911.label: Project Objectives
740911.value: To identify the conflicting views on how insanity was articulated, understood, conceptualized and treated in China from both foreign and traditional Chinese perspectives and to examine the outcome. To understand how mental illness was perceived as a societal problem and therefore a public responsibility — in other words therefore amenable to a public health approach to disease treatment and control. To detail how it was that psychiatry – a modern discipline based upon western medicine — became accepted in China, the resistances it met and how it was practiced. 740911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
740911.value: This study will look in detail at formations of psychiatric classification, policies of containment and custodial care, and reactions to the emerging structure of psychopathology as a social problem in China from the first asylum set up in the end of the nineteenth century to the opening of mental health hospitals by the end of the Republican era. It aims to examine the development of psychiatry and neurology in this period through it models of pathology and treatment, understood both from a colonizing source (Europe and America) and indigenously in China. One of its foci will be the ‘mental health reformers’ of the period operating in the cities of Shanghai, Peking, Nanking and Canton seen as a site for explorations of these issues in order to understand how mental health problems and responses to them were shaped by cultural, economic, social, environmental and political factors. Although only a handful of such people were operating in this milieu between the 1920s and the 1940s their work which had a considerable impact has not been highlighted in previous studies. The long term impact of this study is to extend, and deepen our understanding of the complex interrelationships pertaining to psychopathology and mental health in China and how the non-medical context is important in the history of mental health and in the larger history of the country. [摘要] 本課題研究從十九世紀初中國第一所精神病院的誕生, 到共和制完成之際 (1949年)中國各地精神病院的建立與完善, 探索在此過程中中國精神醫學從分類、病员收入标准制定、到看護制度的形成，以及“精神病理学”作為一種社會問題被认识并作为一种新興概念被提出來後,社会群体對此现象及概念的反應等具體問題。本研究旨在通過瞭解精神病理與治療模式來揭示共和制阶段（1911-1949年），从殖民地源（欧美）以及本土源（中国文化）两个层面上了解中國精神医学及神经医學的形成与發展。其中一個焦點論題是探索在此階段, 在作為“精神健康變革”主要探索地的四大城市------上海、北平、南京、廣州等地, 社會、文化、經濟等環境因素和政治因素是如何影響和改變著這種“精神健康(心理衛生)”意識的形成與發展的。 儘管在1920至1940年代短短二十多年間,只有“一小撮”極其有限的學者在此重要時刻，在中國這片廣闊土地上關注和操作了這個重要議題,儘管他們的工作在開啟後世、承接未來的歷史進程中具有極其深遠的意義,然而在既往的歷史研究中,這種工作本身極其意義卻被忽略了。本研究的目的在於拓展和加深我們對於中國精神衛生與精神病學問題長久以來紛繁複雜的相互關係的理解, 從而帮助我們從更長遠的歷史角度、更清楚地認識“非醫學場景”是如何影響和改變了中國精神醫學的發展與進程的。

740911.label: Realisation of objectives
740911.value: Objectives 2,3, and 4 have been largely met as a result of archival research and preparation of two book chapters. Objective 1 has not been met due to time pressure constraints and inactivity of Co-I. Work at Peking Union Medical College revealed by visits to the Rockefeller archives in New York and the Lyman papers at Duke University Medical School as well as interviews conducted in Nanjing and Beijing with relatives of one of the early pioneers in psychotherapy, have enabled a fuller understanding of how psychological and psychiatric problems were understood, and treated. Also, how people got trained locally and overseas as a result of funding provided by the Rockefeller foundation through the China Medical Board. Additional archives consulted which rounded out the broader context for mental health initiatives were the Fanny Halpern archives in Simon Fraser University, Vancouver, the OSS archives in Washington for details of psychological assessments carried out during the Sino-Japanese war, and the Henry Murray papers at Harvard University.

740911.label: Major findings and research outcome
740911.value: The research sought to show how psychotherapy as both a theory and a practice took root in 1930s republican China. It uncovered a conjunction of interests involving psychologists, literati, and a new generation of doctors sensitive to their patients’ mental health who worked symbiotically in the fields of publishing, writing and practicing new ideas about persons caught in states of mental distress. Many wrote about and disseminated these ideas in a monthly magazine entitled West Wind [Xi Feng] while practitioners incorporated them into their everyday practices. Thus psychotherapy evolved from an activity of writing about ideas in theory to a method for treating patients in a clinic. Four individuals who contributed to both activities were identified as exemplars of this conjunction and their intellectual development and training traced back to American and European influences. They were Huang Jiayin [黄嘉音], the chief editor and publisher of West Wind; Su Zonghua [粟宗華], a psychiatrist and writer of articles in West Wind; Ding Tsan [丁瓚], an analyst and psychotherapist, who co-founded the Chinese Psychological Institute, and introduced medical psychology to China; and Cheng Yulin [程玉麟], one of the earliest Chinese psychiatrists who set up the first public psychiatric hospital in Nanjing, and who also contributed articles to West Wind. These four individuals worked in two distinctly different political climates and with varying degrees of political commitment. Although not part of the original objective, the research went on to show how subsequently their avenues of opportunity became closed off and they had to continue as best they could under the most trying of circumstances. In spite of their enthusiasm and devotion to their goal of developing psychotherapy, it brought them to unfortunate ends, in spite of their efforts to work within and adapt to the repressive orthodoxy imposed by the Communist Government at the end of its first decade. An outcome of this research has been to consider the question of whether the psychotherapeutic culture of the earlier (Republican) period was more collaborative than present day psychotherapeutic training in China which since the late 1970s has been revived.

740911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
740911.value: Three lines of further enquiry are envisaged: (i) from archival data already gathered, to trace the effects of the training possibilities set up both in China and abroad, for the individuals the project has already identified – how they were supported, what obstacles they encountered and what differences the overseas training made to their thinking and practices once back on Chinese soil (ii) to show how in the emerging and shifting political climate of the PRC, the students of these four individuals (and others) adapted to the demands of the system so as to determine what kinds of practice were possible and (iii) to compile a biography of Richard Lyman, a neuropsychiatrist from Duke University who worked in China at Peking Union Medical College in the 1930s. Lyman was responsible for amongst other things recruiting Dai Bingheung, a Chinese sociologist who had undergone a Neo-Freudian analytical training while studying for a doctorate in Chicago. Lyman stands as an agent provocateur who, through his encouragement of others and his own initiatives to foster the cause of western psychiatry and neurology, played a vital role in our understanding of what were the problems and prospects for these fledging disciplines in China, and how people coped with them.

740911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
740911.value: Knowledge of psychology, psychiatry, and neurology and their attendant practices came to China through its systems of universities, teachers, medical colleges, and hospitals. A further avenue was by way of journals written for the educated layman. Psychologists, literati, and a new generation of doctors sensitive to their patients’ mental health needs worked symbiotically in the fields of publishing, writing and practicing new ideas about persons caught in states of mental distress. Several scholars, doctors and psychologists wrote about these new ideas in the pages of a monthly magazine entitled West Wind [Xi Feng]; meanwhile several therapists were taking these ideas and incorporating them into their everyday practices. This project identified four such individuals and traced the roots of their intellectual development and subsequent progress through the 1930s when opportunities for training at home and abroad prevailed, and on through the hardening of the political climate in the first decade of the PORC when much of their work was outlawed. It concludes by considering the question of whether the psychotherapeutic culture of the Republican period was more collaborative than in even the present day where psychotherapeutic training in China, since the early 1980s, has been revived.

741111.label: Project Objectives
741111.value: The research will: - secure more robust data on the scale, types and intensity of private tutoring received by Hong Kong students; - examine students’ perceptions on the ways in which tutoring has shaped their schooling experiences; and - identify teachers’ perspectives on tutoring and their responses to it. The findings will contribute to identification of appropriate policies at classroom, school and government levels. For reasons of feasibility and focus, the research addresses the secondary level. A follow-on project may later be proposed in the light of the present study to address other levels of education.

The findings will contribute to identification of appropriate policies at classroom, school and government levels. For reasons of feasibility and focus, the research addresses the secondary level. 741111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
741111.value: This project will investigate the scale and nature of supplementary private tutoring and its implications for mainstream schooling as perceived by students and teachers. It will identify both positive and negative features of patterns and relationships, and will provide policy lessons for administrators and teachers. Private tutoring is commonly called ‘shadow education’, because it parallels and mimics official school systems: as the curriculum and scale of the mainstream change, so do the curriculum and scale of the shadow. Shadow education has long existed in Hong Kong, but has considerably expanded in the competitive society. Although it has attracted increasing public concern, the evidence on its impact and implications is scarce. The study will focus on secondary schooling. Much tutoring is received in pre-primary, primary and post-secondary levels; but the dynamics are different at those levels, and focus on one level will permit depth in investigation. In Hong Kong’s new 6+3+3+4 system (i.e. six years of primary, three of junior secondary, three of senior secondary, and four of tertiary), two major watersheds are at the end of junior and senior secondary (Secondary 3 and 6). The research will focus on these grades since tutoring is especially important at points of transition. Conceptually, the research will be framed by awareness of the links between economic, social and educational factors which are part of the ecologies of education. The work will also consider different forms of curriculum, and the dynamics of interactions between different forces. The researchers will first solicit data from students in a random sample of schools. Data collected through questionnaires will be supplemented by interviews. Questions will address the scale, intensity and nature of tutoring received, and the reasons for seeking it. The researchers will also solicit information from students who do not receive tutoring. Next, the researchers will secure data from teachers in the same schools. Tutoring may have a backwash on mainstream schooling. It can reduce disparities in classrooms (if it helps slow learners to keep up), or it can increase disparities (if mainly the high achievers receive tutoring). Pupils who receive much tutoring may have less energy for schooling, and the pedagogic approaches of tutors may clash with those of teachers. The perspectives of teachers will be sought on such matters. The study is primarily local in focus. However, it will also contribute to international understanding and to wider work being conducted by the PI and colleagues.

741111.label: Realisation of objectives
741111.value: The project was accomplished very smoothly and productively. Year 1 was devoted to design of instruments, piloting and collection of data from students in Grades 9 and 12. For the questionnaire data: • The planned sample (in the proposal) was 13 schools, two grades in each school, two classes in each grade, and 35 students in each class: i.e. a total of 1,820 (13 x 2 x 2 x 35) students. • The achieved sample was 16 schools, two grades in each school, two classes in each grade, and an average of 25 students per class. The number of students sampled per class was below the target because a significant number of students did not return parental consent. With the extra schools, the total sample of 1,624 was deemed sufficiently close to the target sample of 1,820. For the interview data: • The planned sample (in the proposal) was 13 schools, two grades in each school, and four focus groups of students with four students per group in each grade: i.e. a total of 416 (13 x 2 x 4 x 4) students. • The achieved sample was smaller because the piloting indicated that students felt inhibited in group interviews. The interviews were therefore conducted individually. The total sample was 101 individual interviews rather than 416 students in 104 group interviews, but greater depth of interview data were achieved in this way and the other conditions for diversity were achieved. Year 2 was devoted to the teachers’ perceptions of private tutoring. For the questionnaire data: • The planned sample was four teachers from each of Grades 9 and 13 in the 13 schools, i.e. 104 (4 x 2 x 13) teachers. • The actual sample was 153 teachers from nine schools. For the interview data: • The planned sample was two teachers from each of the 13 schools, i.e. 26 teachers altogether. • The actual sample was 48 teachers. Despite the research fatigue in many Hong Kong schools, some schools in the actual sample were enthusiastic and the researchers took advantage of this enthusiasm. The findings from were reported to each school to assist in identification of appropriate policies at classroom, school and government levels. Each school received a written report on its data in relation to the overall data. Year 3 comprised just six months, and was devoted to analysis of the findings and further preparation of publications.

741111.label: Major findings and research outcome
741111.value: Among the sampled students, 53.8% in Secondary Form 3 (Grade 9) had received some sort of private supplementary tutoring within the previous 12 months, and 71.8% in Secondary Form 6 (Grade 12) had done so. Among the students receiving tutoring, 65.2% did so in English, 52.7% in mathematics, 31.8% in Chinese, and 25.8% in sciences. Even Liberal Studies, which was designed to promote critical thinking and should not be amenable to examination-oriented tutoring, attracted 13.2% of Form 6 students and 5.6% of Form 3 students. This tutoring was perceived by the students and their families to help slow learners to keep up with their peers, and to stretch further the learning of high achievers. Parents may also prefer to pay other people to manage homework and related stresses. However, tutoring increases pressures on young people, and has a backwash on regular schooling. Some teachers welcomed tutoring, others considered it undesirable, and yet others had not thought about the matter. While the government advocates whole-child development and makes teachers responsible for it, the tutoring companies can focus on examination cramming and other narrow skills. Sometimes this leads to dissonance with the schools. The Hong Kong data have proved of considerable interest internationally as well as locally. They highlight the influence of school, family and individual factors on student demand, and indicate the responses of teachers. In addition to the conceptual contributions, the data have policy implications at school and system levels. Teachers and governments need to recognise more fully that large numbers of students receive tutoring and adapt their strategies to accommodate this fact. Society has become more competitive, and families do not feel able to opt out of the race. For these reasons, demand for private tutoring is likely to remain strong for the foreseeable future.

741111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
741111.value: The work has attracted great international interest, and researchers in Bangladesh, Dubai, Iran, Jamaica, Mainland China, Malaysia, and Philippines have adapted the instruments. The PI is engaged involved in follow-up work in Cambodia and Shanghai. An edited book on research methods for shadow education is being prepared. It draws on a Colloquium organised in April 2014 by the Comparative Education Research Centre (CERC) at HKU. The empirical work is helping not only to gain a clearer picture of the amounts of shadow education but also to highlight policy implications. Allied work focuses on regulations for the shadow education sector. A comparative study was jointly published by UNESCO and CERC in 2014. It was authored by Mark Bray and Ora Kwo (i.e. the PI and one of the Co-I’s). This work comes under the umbrella of the UNESCO Chair in Comparative Education at HKU. For further empirical data and comparative analysis, a new GRF proposal is being prepared for work in Shanghai. HKU has provided seed-funding. The work will be undertaken by the PI together with one of the Co-I’s for the Hong Kong project, with one of the PhD students who benefited from this project and is now a Post-Doctoral Fellow.

741111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
741111.value: Over half of Hong Kong’s secondary students receive private supplementary tutoring, and in the last grade of secondary schooling the proportion exceeds 70%. Such tutoring is widely called shadow education because it mimics the regular system − as the curriculum in the schools changes, so it changes in the shadow; and as the regular school system expands, so does the shadow. Some tutoring has benefits in helping slow learners to keep up with their peers and in stretching further the learning of high achievers. Parents may also prefer to pay other people to manage homework and related stresses. However, tutoring can also increase pressures on young people, and is not always effective. It maintains and exacerbates social inequalities since rich families can afford more and better tutoring than poor families. Shadow education also has a backwash on regular schooling, increasing disparities in the classroom and in some cases encouraging students to value their tutors more than their teachers. Providing empirical data on Hong Kong, this project has attracted strong international interest. It has permitted more accurate benchmarking of patterns in Hong Kong with those in other countries.

741311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
741311.value: Finance constraints matter because asymmetric information and moral hazard drive a wedge between the internal and external costs of funds. Despite their importance, it has been difficult to find a direct empirical measure of finance constraints. This project addresses this problem by constructing a novel measure that uses text-based information from firms' SEC filings. It compares and contrasts this measure's information content with other measures proposed in the literature and relates this measure to firm characteristics. This project thus provides important insights into the economics of financially constrained firms. Using this measure, this project then creates a financial constraints factor and investigates its implications for stock return comovement. Furthermore, this project explores how the constraints factor relates to other well-known factors such as the size, book-to-market, and momentum factors. It also investigates whether the constraints factor dominates and thus explains part of the size effect. The investigation of the size effect is important because it can provide an economically meaningful explanation of this stock market anomaly. Using a variant of the Daniel-Titman test, this project then disentangles effects caused by finance constraints from effects caused by other common properties. Examples of other properties include similar industries or regions. Finally, this project makes the finance constraints measure, the constraints factor, and the programming code used for analyzing textual data available on a public website, similar to the well-known Fama-French factors. It will thus be easy for other researchers to build upon the results of this project.

741311.label: Realisation of objectives
741311.value: All objectives have been achieved. We constructed a textual measure of financial constraints, investigated how it relates to firm characteristics and compared it to other measures in the literature, we constructed a factor-mimicking portfolio and performed time-series tests, conducted the Daniel-Titman test (omitted in current version of paper for brevity because of additional other tests carried out), related our factor to other known factors from the literature, and performed cross-sectional tests.

741311.label: Major findings and research outcome
741311.value: We were able to develop a textual financial constraints measure that captures the textual content of firms' annual filings and to extract the relevant content about financial constraints that each firm is facing. We showed that, in contrast to other measures in the literature, our measure is consistent with several firm characteristics. We also find that our measure consistently impacts stock prices, with more constrained firms having higher returns, after controlling for well-known risk factors.

741311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
741311.value: In our opinion, textual analysis of text documents in finance, e.g. company reports or the financial press, is still at its early stage, and much growth in this literature is to be expected. The reason is that now we have completely new datasets available, i.e. textual data, that was prohibitively difficult to analyze before. With advances of computational techniques in this area, the literature is growing rapidly, and we intend to continue to contribute to it.

741311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
741311.value: It is important to understand what makes stock prices move up or down, because stock markets process new information about the real economy and about each company on the stock market. We find novel results in that financial constraints, i.e. how difficult it is for a company to raise financing from outside investors (e.g. stocks or bonds), can predict how the stock behaves in the future. This is great economic importance, because it furthers our understanding of how our financial system functions. Specifically, our research provides important economic implications for investors, financial intermediaries, and regulators about how stocks incorporate novel information into stock prices.
