741511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
741511.value: The importance of physical activity (PA) for the physical and mental health of elders is well documented. Studies indicate that a large percentage of elders, in Hong Kong and elsewhere, do not meet the recommended PA guidelines for health. To promote PA and wellbeing in elders, it is essential to understand the individual, social and environmental factors that act as facilitators or barriers. Most recent studies have examined determinants of PA and health in elders living in Western countries with built and socio-cultural environments much different to those of Asian cities. Asian ultra-dense metropolises present unique environmental characteristics, such as extreme crowdedness, air pollution, developed public transport networks and extensive indoor areas for walking that may affect PA behavior and wellbeing in yet undocumented ways. This study proposes to systematically examine the associations and interactive effects of a variety of environmental, individual and psychosocial factors with levels of PA, quality of life, and mental wellbeing in Hong Kong Chinese-speaking older adults (aged 65+). The study will take advantage of the sampling, recruitment and data collection methods of two recently GRF-funded research projects aimed at studying the impacts of environmental factors on PA in adults. Main outcome (PA, quality of life and mental wellbeing), individual (e.g., socio-demographics) and psychosocial correlates (e.g., self-efficacy and social networks) will be measured via validated interviewer-administered questionnaires. In 40% of the sample, PA levels and places will be assessed objectively using accelerometers (motion sensors) and Global Positioning System (GPS) monitors. The combined use of GPS monitors and accelerometers in older adults is a unique study feature. Environmental factors (access to destinations, traffic safety, aesthetics, recreational places, social environment, pedestrian infrastructure and residential building characteristics) will be measured using interviewer-administered questionnaires, systematic observations (environmental audits) and Geographic Information Systems databases. Outcome assessments will be repeated with a 6-month interval so that seasonal effects can be studied and short-term changes in PA and other outcome variables can be examined. This will also be the first study to assess the effects of social network types on the relationships between environment, PA and mental wellbeing. It is expected that the multi-dimensional and multi-method approach adopted in this study will substantially enhance the understanding of the mechanisms by which contextual factors may influence PA levels and wellbeing in elders which, in turn, will assist policy makers and healthcare professionals in the development of PA promotion approaches suited to this population. 體力活動對長者身體和心理健康的重要性是有據可查的。研究顯示，在香港和其他地方，絕大多數的長者未能達到體力活動的健康指標。為了提升長者的體力活動及幸福，我們必需要了解促進或砠礙個人、社會和環境的因素。近期的研究已探討居於西方國家的長者的體力活動和健康原因，並發現西方國家的建築和社會文化的環境與亞洲城市大為不同。亞洲超密集的大都市帶來了獨特的環境特色，例如高密度、空氣污染、發達公共交通網絡，以及眾多可供散步的室內地方。這些特色可能會影響體力活動的行為及幸福，但仍未經實証。本研究的目的是有系統地探討各種環境，個人與社會心理因素對於香港長者(65歲 +）的體力活動水平、生活質數和精神健康的關係和相互影響。承接近期獲教資會資助的兩項研究，本研究將採用其抽樣、招募及數據收集的方式，目的是探討環境因素對於成年人體力活動的影響。我們將利用已驗證的採訪式問卷，量度主要結果（體力活動，生活質數和精神健康）、個人（例如社會人口）和社會心理（如自我效能和社交網絡）等因素。我們亦將利用活動紀錄儀和全球定位系統監測器，客觀地評估百分之四十樣本中的體力活動水平和地方。本研究的獨特之處是於長者身上合併使用全球定位系統監測器和活動紀錄儀。我們亦會採用採訪式問卷、系統觀察（環境審計）和地理信息系統數據庫，去量度環境的因素（前往目的地、交通安全、美觀、娛樂場所、社會環境、行人基礎設施和住宅特色）。研究結果將於六個月後再作評估，以探究季節和短期變化，以及其他因素對於體力活動的影響。這也將是第一項研究，以評估環境、體力活動和精神健康的關係對於社交網絡類別的影響。我們預計，本研究採用多維和多樣化的方式，將會大大提高了解環境因素可導致長者體力活動水平和精神健康的機制。那麼，我們可協助政策制定者和醫護人員建立提升長者體力活動的合適方法。

741511.label: Major findings and research outcome
741511.value: Objective 1: We have found that the neighborhood and home environments are important correlates of self-reported and objectively-assessed physical activity and sedentary behaviors in Hong Kong Chinese older adults. We have submitted two manuscript to international peer-reviewed journals regarding these findings and also will be presenting them at the World Congress of Active Ageing in Melbourne, Australia (see Part C). We have also found that the neighborhood and home environments are significant correlates of quality of life and depressive symptoms. These particular findings are the topic of a PhD dissertation (Mr JP Zhang, School of Public Health, HKU). We are planning 4-5 manuscripts on these specific findings (in progress). Objective 2: All individual, psychosocial and environmental factors independently contributed to physical activity, quality of life and depressive symptoms in Hong Kong Chinese older adults. Also, individual factors were found to moderate the associations of social and environmental factors with physical activity and quality of life. This was not observed for depressive symptoms. Fours manuscripts are being prepared for submission on these findings. Objective 3: Physical function and social networks in the neighborhood moderated the association between the environment, physical activity and depressive symptoms. However, the proportion of seniors living nearby did not. Part of these findings will be included in a PhD dissertation led by Mr JP Zhang. We are planning three manuscripts on this specific objective. Objective 4: Sedentary behavior and walking for transport and recreation mediated the relationships between neighborhood environmental characteristics and depressive symptoms. Also, social networks in the neighborhood mediated the relationships between access to services and recreational facilities and depressive symptoms. Two manuscripts are planned for publication reporting findings from this particular objective. Objective 5: Perceived barriers to engaging in PA, self-efficacy for PA and social networks in the neighborhood explained the relationships between several aspects of the neighborhood environment (access to services, pedestrian infrastructure, traffic safety and safety from crime) with walking for recreation and transport in the neighborhood. Two manuscripts are being planned to report on these findings. Objective 6: Changes in physical activity were positively associated with changes in quality of life and negatively associated with changes in depressive symptoms. Baseline health indicators, characteristics of the neighborhood and home environment and social network size (in the neighborhood) moderated these associations. Four additional manuscripts are being planned reporting on these findings. The richness of the data requires some time to convert all these important findings into publications.

741511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
741511.value: The findings from this project will inform public health and environmental interventions aimed at improving mental wellbeing and quality of life in Hong Kong Chinese older adults. Apart for being expected to result in a large number of publications reporting on the original findings, data from this project will be used in pooled analyses with comparable data from other countries (USA and Belgium). This project is also part of the PI's prestigious Australian Research Council Future Fellowship (awarded last year) on urban planning and active ageing. Data from this project will be used within an international capacity building program led by the PI (Cerin). Also, it will be used as part of a National Institutes of Health (USA) grant application to be submitted in June 2016 in collaboration with UCSD (Prof Sallis JF) and Stanford University (Prof King AC). A similar GRF project awarded to the PI (Cerin) and completed in 2009 has resulted so far in 14 high-caliber publications, one soon to appear in the Lancet. We expect this project to generate even a larger amount of high-caliber output as it has richer and more innovative data than the previous project.

741511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
741511.value: This project indicates that the neighborhood physical and social environments are very important determinants of older adults' mental and physical wellbeing. Safe neighborhoods with good access to services, a developed pedestrian infrastructure and access to affordable public transport can positively affect Hong Kong older adults' wellbeing by providing opportunities to be physically active, socialize and connect with family and other social networks. This is especially the case for older adults suffering from chronic diseases that limit physical capacity and mobility. Interventions aimed at supporting healthy, active and independent ageing in place need to be multi-sectoral and involve public health professionals as well as urban planners and transportation experts. Active and healthy ageing depends on the existence of a supportive physical and social environment.

741611.label: Project Objectives
741611.value: To investigate students’ perceptions of generic skills in two specific disciplines in higher education. This includes their rationale, awareness, prior experiences, expectations from the university and their experiences in relation to learning outcomes, learning and teaching activities, assessment and engagement on the acquisition of generic skills acquired during their undergraduate programme. To investigate teachers’ perceptions of generic skills in two specific disciplines in higher education. This includes their rationale, awareness, prior teaching and previous learning experiences, expectations from students and the learning outcomes, learning and teaching activities, assessment and engagement from their courses. Their understandings of their role, purposes and priorities, and how these relate to practice will also be investigated. To analyse the discrepancy between students’ and teachers’ perceptions on the skill-set, including the alignment of the skills’ learning outcomes, the learning activities, and the assessment of generic skills during the programme in each discipline. 741611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
741611.value: Recent decades have witnessed an international movement towards curriculum transformation and renewal in higher education, such as the UK Dearing Report in the mid-1990s and the Nelson Reforms in Australia in 2003. Hong Kong’s higher education system is no exception. In the current climate, these transformations include the need to raise the quality of undergraduate education to meet the demands of a knowledge-based economy. These transformations are not just within the discipline-knowledge, but also in the graduate attributes that students must possess to cope in this highly-evolving society. These graduate attributes(also known as generic skills/transferable skills/key-skills/soft-skills) are of growing concern to employers, government, students and teachers, and they are high on the agenda in the new Hong Kong 3+3+4 curriculum. Despite the assumption that generic skills are part and parcel of a graduate’s portfolio and that the skills agenda has been at the forefront of higher education provision for some time, there is a lack of direction on how generic skills are delivered and practiced in higher education. It is important to remember that generic skills are not by tradition part of a degree curriculum. Students and teachers are often puzzled by the rationale behind why these skills are required to be delivered through their already over-scheduled degree. A certain amount of haziness and mismatch exists in their perceptions and the development of generic skills, such as the learning outcomes. Students are known to perform better when their expectations are aligned with the learning outcomes. Thus, it is vitally important to understand the discrepancy between students’ and teachers’ perceptions on the skill-set to achieve positive learning outcomes. In addition, if generic skills are to be better developed, study needs to be discipline-specific. This proposed project aims to enhance the understanding of students’ and teachers’ perceptions of generic skills and the current teaching approaches in two specific disciplines in higher education. Surveys and interviews will be conducted. The perceived effectiveness of the teaching and learning activities employed in respect to learning transfer, student engagement and feasibility will also be identified. A summary of a curriculum design framework for the development of generic skills in the specific disciplines will be derived from the findings, and from adapting previous student learning experience models, which are often focused on and used in a subject-knowledge context rather than a generic skills context. The outcomes of the project will make tremendous contributions to all knowledge-based societies. 世界各地的高等教育學制近數十年經歷不少改革及更新，而這種改革已成國際趨勢，九十年代中期英國的狄林報告書 (Dearing Report) 及二零零三年澳洲的尼爾森改革方案 (Nelson Reforms) 便是一些海外學制改革的例子。為應付現時知識型經濟社會需要，香港的高等教育學制亦將跟隨這個國際趨勢，透過改革提升本科教育的水平。教育改革並非只限於更新學科的知識內容，而是更注重發展有助學生應付社會轉型的「畢業生特質 」(graduate attributes) (「畢業生特質」又被稱為 「共通能力」(generic skills)/「可轉移技能」(transferable skills)/「關鍵技能」(key-skills)/ 「軟性技能」 (soft-skills))。現時僱主、政府、學生和老師對發展「畢業生特質 」的關注及討論不斷增加，因此三三四新學制課程也重視「畢業生特質」的教授和發展。 雖然「共通能力」已被視作畢業生應具備的條件，而各高等教育院校近年也十分重視發展畢業生的技能，但在教授共通能力的議題上，各教育院校仍然欠缺清晰的方向。由於以往的學位課程並沒有教授「共通能力」，加上現時課程的編排已十分緊迫， 不少老師和學生並不明白在新學制中教授「共通能力」的原因。其實老師和學生對「共通能力」的認知和發展存有不同的見解。為達至最佳的學習成果，學生的學習期望與老師所訂下的教學成果必須互相配合。因此我們必須了解老師與學生對教授「共通能力」及其教學成果兩者認知上的差異。 是次研究目的在於加強學生與老師對「共通能力」的認知及對社會科學和工程學的教學模式之理解。研究以問卷調查及訪問形式進行。研究亦會了解受訪者對現時教學活動成效的意見，例如這些活動的教學成果、學生的投入程度及其可行性。研究結果相信有助編制教授「共通能力」的課程，而是次研究亦會參考以往以學科知識為本的學習模式，相信研究成果對現今知識型社會有莫大貢獻。

741611.label: Major findings and research outcome
741611.value: With regards to objective 1, 2, 3, a survey on students’ perceived importance and competency on generic skills was developed and validated. Questionnaire items were identified using multiple sources including existing questionnaires on generic skills competency and comprehensive review of existing literature. Representative sample of 1,232 from CUHK, HKUST and HKU first year engineering students. Exploratory factor analysis resulted in 8 factor model: a) academic and problem solving skills, b) interpersonal skills, c) community and citizenship knowledge, d) leadership skills, e) professional effectiveness, (f) information and communication literacy, (g) critical thinking, and (h) self-management. Confirmatory factor analysis demonstrated that the eight-factor model was a good fit and adequate internal consistency reliability was shown. It was revealed that engineering students find themselves in need of these skills for their future career as they understand the importance of these skills but have not yet acquired these skills at a competence level deemed appropriate prior to university. The full findings have been submitted to the Journal of Engineering Education and the paper is currently under review (Chan, Zhao and Luk, 2015). The expectation survey was modified and tested on 393 HKU first year business undergraduate (data analysis on construct is in progress). Student Experience Survey on generic skills was conducted on 506 HKU and HKUST year 2&3 undergraduate engineering students and compare business and engineering students’ perceived importance and competency of generic skills (paper in draft). It is unfortunate that we have experienced major delay in the peer-reviewed process for Chan, Zhao and Luk’s paper (2015, in review) which had knocked on effects in the subsequent delays in the other manuscripts. For objectives 4, 5, 6, three student focus groups and five individual interviews were conducted to determine students’ rationale, awareness, prior teaching and previous learning experiences, learning and teaching activities, assessments and engagement from their courses. The majority of the students felt generic skills are better developed through extra-curricular and out-of-classroom activities such as internship, community service-learning and hall education. The findings from the Teacher Survey suggest that while HKU engineering teacher staff acknowledges the importance of generic skills to students’ future career, there was a wide range of perspectives on whether generic skills should be formally assessed and credited. The outcomes of both quantitative survey data and qualitative findings were integrated to inform the development of curriculum design framework for generic skills, accounting for both students’ and teachers’ perceptions and needs (please see figure 1).The framework was adopted from presage process and product model on student learning approaches (Prosser & Trigwell, 1999) and existing generic skills frameworks (Barrie, 2004; Bennett et al. 2000; Drummond et al., 1998). The proposed model of student learning approaches to generic skills is also highly context-dependent. Student factors and learning context are two components within the presage phrase. Student factors include a whole host of factors such as a student’s personality, their prior learning culture (result- or process-orientated learning) and current life circumstances. Learning context includes course learning outcomes, assessment methods, quality of supervision and feedback, peer factors as well as the institutional culture. The interaction of the two presage components determine student’s motivation and in turn influence which approach (engage or avoid) he or she choose to adopt to learn generic skills. The framework will advance our work towards a research-informed approach to generic skills development, leading significant impact on education policy and pedagogy practice for higher education.

741611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
741611.value: It has been decided that the classroom exercise approach that was originally planned for students to discuss graduate attributes will be removed from the project. As findings from the project suggest that (1) student motivation and engagement is the key to students’ development of generic skills, and (2) students believe that generic skills are better developed through out-of-class activities, the PI recognized an evident need for further research to focus on how can we integrate out-of-class learning into a curriculum framework which can engage students in the development of generic skills. Given that research is conducted in an iterative process, the PI decided to conduct a follow-up study based on the findings which emerged from this project. It is believed that the objective of the classroom exercise in enabling students to gain more insights on generic skills in terms of what they expect to learn has been achieved to a large extent through self-reflection during the focus groups and interviews. Such focus groups and interviews will be extended to include more students in the follow-up study, which has already received support in the form of a continuous grant (Ref No.:17610215) from this first GRF.

742211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
742211.value: 自二十世纪八十年代以来，美国家庭储蓄率持续降低。与此相对的是，在过去的十五年中，中国家庭储蓄率却显著提升。众所周知，美国和中国分别位列世界第一大以及第二大经济体。如何理解世界上两个最大的经济体在家庭储蓄率上所展现出的截然相反的趋势，对于经济学家以及政策的制定者们来说就至关重要。Feldstein （2008）主张，想要完全理解全球性的经济不平衡（global imbalances), 就不得不进行针对家庭储蓄率的理论研究与量化研究。 依据这篇研究计划中我们所提出的猜想，中美家庭储蓄率的截然相反的趋势在很大程度上是由在房地产市场发生的不同的体制性变革造成的。然而，我们必须强调的是，在尽管改革措施不相同，其内在运作机制却并无二致。 此项目意在通过对我们过去研究工作（Chen and Winter,2010）中的量化模型的拓展进一步量化中美房地产融资改革对家庭储蓄和消费决定的影响。自上世纪八十年代，美国经济经历了房地产融资市场的大规模 ”金融自由化”,而在二十世纪九十年代末，中国政府也展开了一系列对房地产市场的自由化的举措。 二十世纪八十年代初，美国房地产市场经历了融资手段的显著变革，也就是“金融自由化” 又或者是”房屋金融解规“。 其显著特点为1. 再融资的机会显著增加；2. 持续降低的首期付款要求。基于我们先前的研究，我们计划在这个研究项目中得出以下结论：1. 2000-2007年房屋价格的升值放大了再融资 对于家庭储蓄率的影响；2. 在前述模型的基础上，如若加之在稳态之间间的转移动态， 模型所产生的结果能更好的符合解规后美国家庭储蓄率的变化状况。这对于有生命周期的 特点的模型来说至关重要。 另一方面，中国房地产市场改革的的核心便是允许城市家庭购买以及积累房产。此项改革带来的是城市住房拥有比例从17%大幅上升至80%。中国的房屋信贷市场的整体情形近似于八十年代前的美国市场，诸如：1. 住房仍然依照一份先前签订的房屋融资合约，需要一段很长的时间才能积累起相应的住房资产净值；2. 首期付款的比例很高；3. 相对稀缺的再融资的机会，使得住房拥有者无法提取他们拥有的住房资产净值来应对他们所面对的潜在不可能被保险的 收入风险。我们计划在这项研究中展示出：1. 由于存在于中国房地产市场的长期房屋融资合同，中国的住房拥有者不得不积累起过多的预防性储蓄（precautionary saving)来应对潜在的收入风险，这也是对于房屋融资市场上的摩擦的一种反应; 2. 高比率的首付使得家庭（尤其是年轻人）选择积累更多的存款来进行一次性付款买房。

742211.label: Realisation of objectives
742211.value: This project was proposed to explain the determinants of the high household savings rate in China. As one output of this project, the PI has completed a research paper, "The Great Famine and Savings Rate in China," with one of the Co-Is, Fabrizio Zilibotti and an additional coauthor Maelys Rupelle. In this paper, we have empirically shown how the Great famine in China impacted the formation of patience of households and how it can be transmitted over generations, which contributes to the observed high savings rate of Chinese households currently. One of the key findings is that households who reside in counties with higher mortality rate during the famine years tend to have a higher savings rate in 2002. This phenomenon is justified by the theory of preference formation and transmission. Our paper is in the stage of finalization and in preparation for submission to economics journals. Objective 1 and 2 were proposed originally to address why the household savings rate is low in the US, but high in China, by exploring the effects of institutional changes in housing finance market as well as increasing housing prices. The methodology is an application of the PI's early work on the low household savings rate in the US. However, in the process of carrying out this research agenda, the PI found that some new publications have taken advantage of similar ideas. For example, Wang and Wen (2012, Housing Prices and the High Chinese Saving Rate Puzzle), Wan (2014, Household Savings and Housing Prices in China), and Bussiere, Matthieu, et al. (2013, Understanding Household Savings in China: the role of the housing market and borrowing constraints). In view of those newly completed competing research, the PI considered that the scientific value of this specific methodology (housing finance) was heavily diminished. Therefore, the PI decided to focus on and substantiate the objective 2 with an alternative methodology (rare disaster) adopted in the current paper, which is more likely to produce a larger impact. The objective 3 is a byproduct of our new research methodology, given our work has some independent value for studies on both savings rate and impacts of rare disasters such as famines. The PI has reported to the committee this additional endeavor and the new methodology in the annual report of 2013 and reported the progress when we applied for an extension of this project.

742211.label: Major findings and research outcome
742211.value: We find that, in all specifications of our investigations, Chinese households tend to have a higher savings rate in counties where famine was severer and mortality rate was higher during the Great famine. Roughly speaking, a one standard deviation increase in the famine severity may raise the savings rate by more than one and half percentage point. We also find that the effect is largest for the poorest households, who are most likely to be threatened by the lack of food and whose savings are mainly motivated by securing subsistence consumption for the future. We test this idea also in an empirical design with instruments on the famine survival rate, i.e., we instrument the famine survival index with weather conditions and leaders' characteristics. Our results are still robust.

742211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
742211.value: This study adds one new perspective on the determinants of Chinese households savings rate. The same mechanism can be also applied to other countries with a famine history, such as India.

742211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
742211.value: This research demonstrates that the Great famine that took place in late 1950's in China significantly affected households saving behaviors now. The Great famine affected the patience level of households who were exposed to the famine and their investment in their children's time preference, i.e., patience. In other words, the time preference can be transmitted through generations and those young households now are still indirectly affected by the famine half century ago. The severity of the Great famine matters for the degree of such changes. This paper takes advantage of the variations in the famine at the county level and identify the effects of the Great famine on the savings rate of Chinese households in 2002 with a cross-section dataset. The findings help explain the high saving propensity of Chinese households now.

742311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
742311.value: 凱莉說 “無論你怎樣待他們，無論你是誰，其實你說話的方式已經給了別人一種高不可攀的感覺.” 凱莉 23歲, 在美國居住了幾年，是最近回流香港的土生土長中國人。和其他香港雙語的居民一樣，凱莉說話時，會遊走在廣東話和英語之間，可是她特有的夾雜方式，便把她和本地人分開了，而她，也成為了本地人所謂的”香蕉” (表面是黃的，而內裡是白的)。 李(1995)注意到社會語言學的雙語研究中，極少分析同一社區中的小群體的語言選擇。不少研究是探討語言如何與社會身份掛勾 (Hill & Hill 1986, Myer-Scotton 1993, Rampton 1995) 但卻少有論及語言轉換作為一種有社會指引意義的做法。本研究負責人曾探討香港的兩種語言轉變的模式，探討不同說話者及同一說話者的變化及其社會意義，與及語言學資源如何建構身份。 此研究擴充本研究負責人之前對國外回港的雙語人士的語言和身份研究，推及北美華裔香港人，並開啟了這群人的社會語言學研究。它探討(1)跨國及離鄉者的社會語言學(2) 雙語及語言選擇 (3) 雙語語料庫。它研究全球化下的跨國雙語，以探討本地-全球的對比及微觀-宏觀的社會語言學聯系。 很多中國移民不再在西方定居，反而成為流動人口；他們一旦獲得外國的公民身份，很多都會回到家鄉尋求更好的經濟和社會機會。據香港2001年人口普查，3.5%的華裔人口(超過24萬人)擁有外國護照。這些流動性和多種公民身份(參見 Ong 1999)引發了對香港移民回流人士的人口學、社會地理學和社會學的研究(Ley & Kobayashi 2005; Sussman 2005, 2010; Waters 2005, 2007; Salaff et al. 2010; Ip 2006)；惟語言學/社會語言學偏偏缺席(或者除了本文作者的有限研究) –由於沒有這方面的研究，一個跨社會學的方向便為這一個研究的範籌提供了一個獨特的角度。 本研究將有多項成果。本研究主要負責人專長於社會語言學的民族誌、雙語研究，以及運用多媒體科技。她在社會語語學研究(作為研究助理和博士生)有豐富的經驗，以往的語料庫訓練也令她能勝任這項研究負責人的角色。

742311.label: Realisation of objectives
742311.value: All four objectives have been achieved (except the corpus website, see below). The first objective is modified to include transnationals from any Anglophone countries rather than only North America who returned to Hong Kong. For the first and fourth objectives: A total of eight transnationals who returned to Hong Kong from North America and Australia are included in the 2012-2015 data collection period of this project, which is more than the number promised in the proposal. Over 160 hours of audio recording/data are collected from the research participants’ natural spontaneous speech in daily life as well as in ethnographic/sociolinguistic interviews. Four of the consultants included audio recordings made while they were in their respective host countries, and when they returned to Hong Kong. From these data the PI was able to qualitatively track their linguistic and social connection changes before and after their return migration, and to understand their identity negotiation associated with their transnational movements particularly through ethnographic interviews and analysing their natural speech. These data and findings are compared with the PI’s previous research on multilingual returnees done between 2002-2005, and allow for diachronic comparison of the linguistic, specifically code-switching patterns used by returnees in the two periods. Part of the data, about 140,000 words/characters, was transcribed, translated and synced with audio in ELAN format to build a mini-corpus (objective 4) which allow the PI to do more sophisticated linguistic analysis of the participants’ inter- and intra-speaker variation. The mini-corpus took up much longer than originally planned because the PI requested for partially outsourcing the transcription and translation work to use the remaining funding for data processing more efficiently. Undergraduate student RAs provided good research experience for the students but they had a high turn over rate due to overseas exchange or graduation. After training and working with a few dozen of undergrad RAs, the PI decided to increase the efficiency by outsourcing the more basic data transcription and translation work, and probably because it was an unusual request, the processing time and time the project was on hold waiting for the request outcome took many months, and further time was needed to restart the work after a period of project account hold. The PI was thankful for being allowed to outsource part of the data work and complete the mini-corpus in the extended time of the project. The mini-corpus provides an invaluable resource for researching both locals' and returnees' language pattern and social connections. Some of the main findings include: The returnees in this current project used similarly wide range of linguistic patterns (from insertion of both language direction, use of alternation, and using discourse markers as switch points, varying styles of their English phonology) in their code-switching behaviour compare to the data collected in 2002-2005, showing that the returnee styles of code-switching and usage continues in Hong Kong despite being socially criticised as being over-westernised. However, some of the current project consultants retain more local Cantonese phonological features in English, likely because of their migration to Anglophone countries at a later age compared to the returnees studied in the 2002-2005 period. In the original fourth objective, both a mini-corpus and a website were promised. The mini-corpus is 100% completed. But the PI decided not to carry out the corpus website (a small section of the 4th objective) because the audio data with personal names and frequent personal information mentioned cannot be efficiently anonymised the same way as written data, and therefore should not to be shared openly so as to protect the identities of the consultants. For the 2nd and 3rd objectives: The earlier research showed returnees struggled with locals' non acceptance of the returnees' language pattern and associated cultural/ethnic/class identities, and the returnees' manifestation in linguistic behavior of adapting and style-shifting as they interact with Hong Kong locals; while the returnee consultants in the current project are generally at ease with their positioning in the community as marginal members and worry less about accommodating in their language use. For example, one consultant considered his millennial generation of returnees as being “afloat”, which he describes as privileged and flexible because of the multiple citizenships they hold, and the freedom and independence they have for moving from one place to another between Hong Kong and the western countries they have right of abode to. Another consultant described herself as a “world citizen” and not willing to be pinned down as a specific social/national/ethnic category. In addition, the recent social and political development in Hong Kong seem to play a role in the consideration of the returnees compare to those in the earlier study. In the earlier project, the return migrants generally planned to stay and live in Hong Kong for good, while in the current project, the returnees seem to keep a more flexible and open plan for where they would stay long-term and have a different conception about “settling down” in a location. Aihwa Ong’s critique of using traditional diaspora study framework on current Chinese migration and remigration is applicable in this case: that it is more meaningful to talk about these returnees as transnationals with agency, and that they have access to knowledge and commodity to maneuver from one continent to another and/or back, rather than in the traditional sense of the study of Chinese diaspora as enclave of Chinese communities in the context of integration or adaptation to the host countries.

742311.value: The research outcome of this project include three peer-reviewed papers (one published, two commissioned), a first of its kind mini-corpus of Hong Kong adult multilingual spontaneous speech, an international roundtable on Englishes in multilingual Asia among scholars from major Asian universities, three peer-reviewed international conference presentations, one peer-reviewed international conference poster in an invited session, and three invited talks in South Africa, Sri Lanka, and Ningbo China respectively. 742311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
742311.value: This research will be further developed in two ways. First, the 140,000-word mini-corpus with Hong Kong Adult multilingual (mostly Cantonese and English, but some of the data include Putonghua and other Chinese languages/dialects) spontaneous speech from both locals and returnees across two periods (2002-2005 and 2012-2015) provides an invaluable resource for further structural linguistic and sociolinguistic analysis. In addition to the papers reported in this project as outcome, the PI plans to work on one additional paper incorporating data from this project as well as the PI’s earlier Cantonese language research on the changing language ideologies and identities; and another paper on gender discourse and stereotype (incorporating with the PI’s another project on “Kong Girls”) as the PI found the corpus contains relevant natural discourse about discussion of gender stereotypes in Hong Kong. RGC’s support will be duly acknowledged whenever the corpus data and findings of this project are used in future publications. Second, this project will directly inform and provide theoretical and methodological comparisons with the PI’s another GRF project on Indonesian Chinese transnationalism both in terms of our knowledge of multilingualism and discussion of transnationalism and new global movements in individual levels.

742311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
742311.value: Migration and population movement in modern times is no longer a one-way route. This project research Hong Kong people who once migrated to Anglophone countries and return to Hong Kong after years abroad. This research provides both local and global significance. Locally, this research helps us understand overseas returnees as a new social category, which is growing in number and influence in Hong Kong. And a perspective to local Hong Kong identity from those in the social periphery. Globally, this research contributes to the current discourse on transnationality and globalization, and offers an explanatory link between micro level individual movement and macro level sociopolitical changes through ethnographic study of the linguistic practices and ideologies of transnational bilinguals. In terms of linguistic scholarship, this research contribute to the study of multilingualism and language contact by providing a case study of Hong Kong bilinguals who move between continents, this research further our knowledge on multilingualism across communities. It aims to deepen our knowledge of intra- and inter-speaker practices by studying and following multilinguals up-close as they maneuver in their social worlds.

742411.label: Project Objectives
742411.value: To examine the discrepancy between people’s aggressive responses to social exclusion in public and in private context. To test the mechanism for the different responses toward social exclusion in public and private context. In particular, to investigate whether the discrepancy between public and private aggression to social exclusion can be attributed to impression management concerns, arisen from accountability and evaluation potential. To test whether the meditational role of hostile cognition on the association between social exclusion and aggression will be moderated by the context in which the aggression happens. To test whether these effects are due to changes in mood or self-esteem. To provide insights on helping people to reduce or inhibit aggression and to respond in a productive manner when facing exclusion, rejection, or other types of maltreatment.

742411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
742411.value: Man is a social animal and social exclusion or ostracism has often been used as a successful way for the group to make a person aware that he or she has done something inappropriate. Prior research using different research methods have, however, shown that individuals often respond to social exclusion aggressively. Over the last decade, we have gained more understanding about why social exclusion leads to aggression in some situations but not others. We have also learned more about why people become aggressive following social exclusion. Even with these advancements, our knowledge about the behavioral impact of social exclusion is still rather limited given the complexity and the significance of the issue. As Leary and colleagues (2006) concluded, considerable research is needed to understand fully the association between social exclusion and aggression. When socially excluded by others, people have the desire to boost their social connectedness. Therefore, they should be sensitive to how their behaviors are evaluated by others because these evaluations will influence their chance of future affiliation. The current investigation includes a series of experiments testing how and why people respond to social exclusion differently when they have evaluation concerns about their behaviors and when they do not have such concerns about their behaviors. Understanding how these evaluations or impression management concerns influence people’s behavioral responses to social exclusion can have important implications in developing programs to help people to reduce hostile actions and to respond in a more productive manner. Given the ubiquitous nature of social exclusion, rejection, and ostracism, educational programs of this kind have significant benefits to individuals and to the society as a whole. 人生活于社会群体之中。群体通常会用孤立或排斥来惩罚行为不当的个体。被孤立的人， 有的时候会表现出攻击性，而有的时候不会表现出攻击性 。虽然过去十年的研究揭示了一些排斥和攻击性行为的关系，但我们对于二者的关联需要进更深入的探讨。一个人受到排斥后通常会希望被人接纳，所以他应该会在意别人的评价，因为这会影响到他将来是否能和别人建立联系。本研究关注对别人的评价的在意程度如何影响个体在受到排斥后的攻击性行为。本研究的结果可以指导人们更好地应对排斥和孤立；帮助降低社会中的攻击性行为。

742411.label: Realisation of objectives
742411.value: Objective 1: We have sufficient evidence supporting our prediction that contextual factors influence how people respond to social exclusion. People are more likely to behave aggressively following social exclusion in public than private settings. Objective 2: We have accumulated evidence suggesting that individual factors (e.g., beliefs) contribute to people’s responses to social exclusion Objective 3: We found that the cognitive appraisal triggered by social exclusion is critical in guiding their coping responses. Objective 4: Our research showed that mood or self-esteem was not able to account for the behavioral responses triggered by social exclusion. Objective 5: Our research provided insights on helping people to reduce or inhibit aggression and to respond in a productive manner when facing exclusion, rejection, or other types of maltreatment. One effective way is to change the mindset typically associated with social exclusion.

742411.label: Major findings and research outcome
742411.value: Our major findings are below: First, personal beliefs shape people’s aggressive responses to social exclusion. As shown in Poon and Chen (2014), in four studies, we found that individuals with strong general just-world beliefs (either measured or primed) behaved less aggressively following ostracism than individuals with weak general just-world beliefs. In contrast, general just-world beliefs had no statistically reliable influence on aggression among participants in the inclusion or control (misfortune) condition. These multi-method convergent findings suggest that general just-world beliefs, either measured or primed, play a critical role in determining whether or not people would behave aggressively following ostracism Second, people’s cognitive appraisal is critical in understanding their responses following social exclusion. As suggested by Poon, Chen, and DeWall (2013), when people experience provocation, they often behave aggressively because they believe that doing so will bring some benefits to the self, such as feeling better. Socially excluded people may feel that they are especially entitled to benefits associated with lashing out at others, which may increase their aggression. Our findings suggest that entitlement functions an antecedent to aggression and a lack of prosocial behavior instead of conflating entitlement as a form of these behaviors. Entitlement may increase the likelihood of engaging in dishonest, aggressive, and selfish behaviors because people feel they deserve the rewards and pleasures that accompany such behavior. Third, our research showed that social exclusion not only influence the target, but also harms the source of exclusion. Chen, Poon, Bernstein, and Teng (2014) showed that rejecting others can lead to the experience of pain and distress to the source of rejection. Major research outcome: The project has led to publications in top tier journals, including Journal of Experimental Social Psychology and Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin (see Part C). In addition, findings of the project has been presented at international conferences, including the annual meeting of APS annual meeting and the general meeting of EASP (see Part C). Further, the PI of the project has presented some of the findings during invited seminars at South China Normal University (2013) and Beijing Normal University (2014). Finally, with the support of this project, one PhD student, Kai-Tak Poon, finished his PHD training and successfully secured a position of Assistant Professor at the Hong Kong Institute of Education.

742411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
742411.value: Our research demonstrates the power of the subjective perception in guiding people’s responses following social exclusion. Future research can examine whether a cognitive process can account for other types of responses triggered by social exclusion. Our findings also suggest an effective way to reduce detrimental behavior that accompanies social exclusion. By adopting a mindset that social exclusion can aid in one’s growth and development, socially excluded people perceive that they can benefit from the negative experience and do not feel compelled to seek out benefits elsewhere. Further efforts are needed to identify effective ways to reduce people’s tendency of aggression following social exclusion. Our research pointed out that social exclusion can has negative effects on the source of rejection. This is a less studied research area and should be further tested.

742811.label: Project Title(Chinese)
742811.value: 高密度城市門禁式住宅社區的社會可持續性：香港個案

742811.label: Project Objectives
742811.value: To analyse the evolution of housing estates in Hong Kong in the context of the gated community literature. To evaluate the planning and design considerations in the development process of housing estates of Hong Kong from the social sustainability perspectives. To evaluate the social sustainability performance of housing estates of Hong Kong from the perceptions of both the residents inside the housing estates and those nearby. To explain the differences in the sustainability performance among different types of housing estates in Hong Kong, with special focuses on the soico-politcial and institutional contexts of the housing production processes. To recommend ways of improving the social sustainability of housing estates in Hong Kong, and to pioneer the development of transferable frameworks for analysing gated communities in high rise cities.

742811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
742811.value: This study aims to analyse and compare housing estates in Hong Kong as distinctive forms of gated communities for improving their social sustainability and for pioneering transferable frameworks for examining similar planned residential communities in Asia. Given the increasing international prominence of gated communities as residential development forms, and the controversial issues around them, it is important to know whether these long-held residential forms in Hong Kong are working effectively, and why. Further, as Hong Kong aspires to achieve sustainable development, it is necessary to investigate what lessons for improving sustainability flow from this residential form. The analysis will use frameworks derived from the literature on gated communities, social sustainability, and neighbourhood planning and development. It will initially evaluate social sustainability issues in the planning and use processes of Hong Kong’s gated and semi-gated housing estates, notably environmental awareness, social cohesion, social order and safety, and social inclusion. The social sustainability performance of different housing estate types will subsequently be compared and the differences will be explained with reference to the socio-political and institutional contexts of housing estate construction, the then prevailing urban development and planning strategies, estate planning and design practices, property management practices, and the role and objectives of the government in the housing production processes. Apart from the use of secondary materials such as government policy statements, planning regulations and design guidelines, site observation and interviews with government officials, estate planners and designers will be conducted. Further, questionnaire surveys of residents inside and outside of the gated housing estates will be carried out to ascertain their environmental consciousness, social behaviour, perception and experience related to social sustainability and to understand the causal relationships between estate planning and social sustainability. Empirically, this study will inform stakeholders the social sustainability performance of the gated housing estates in Hong Kong, and unveil how the socio-political contexts of the planning and design processes and the estate planning and design themselves influence social sustainability. It will accordingly provide recommendations for improving these processes. Theoretically, it will construct a transferable framework for explaining the relationship between the institutional context of high density gated communities and their socio-spatial outcomes, and another for examining the social sustainability performance of gated residential communities in high rise and high density cities. Additionally, it will inform the sustainability literature whether, and to what extent, the gated community is a sustainable form of residential organization. 本研究從門禁式住宅小區的角度來分析及比較香港的屋邨及屋苑(下稱屋邨)。目的是增進它們的社會可持續性及制訂可轉移的研究架構來考查亞洲區內類似的住宅小區。基於門禁式的住宅小區在國際間日益普及，我們需要知道及解釋這在香港行之已久的主要住宅模式是否有效。再者，追求可持續發展既是香港城市發展的原則之一，我們應知道她的住宅模式是否使香港的發展更可持續。 本研究的分析模式乃是從門禁式住宅小區，社會可持續性及社區的規劃及發展的理論而衍生的。它首先評估香港全門禁及半門禁(下稱門禁)屋邨在設計及使用期的社會可持續性，特別是環保意識、社會緊密性、社會秩序、安全及社會包容性等各方面。然後，它會比較及分析不同種類的屋邨在這幾方面的表現，尤其是屋邨在規劃及建築期間社會及政治環境與架構組織對它們的影響。它也會分析城市發展及規劃，屋邨的規劃及發展，物業管理及政府在房屋建造過程的角色及參與目的對屋邨的社會可持續性的影響。 除了引用二手資料，例如政府政策文件，規劃法規及設計準則外，本研究也會進行實地考察，及與政府官員，屋邨規劃師及建築師進行訪談。再者，也會跟屋邨內及周邊的居民進行問卷調查，俾能了解他們的環保意識，社會行為，及對社會可持續性的理解及經驗，並可從他們的角度了解屋邨的設計與屋邨社會可持續性的關係。 在實踐方面，本研究將會讓香港屋邨的持份者知道這類住宅模式的社會可持續性，及將會揭示屋邨的規劃及設計和它們的社會及政治背景如何影響屋邨的社會可持續性。本研究將基於這些研究結果提出改善建議。在理論方面，本研究將建立一個可轉移的分析架構來解釋高密度門禁式住宅小區的建制背景與此等小區能達致的社會及政治功能的關係。另外，本研究也會建立一個理論架構，用以考查高密度及高層建築模式城市內門禁式住宅的社會可持續性。最後，本研究也會對門禁式住宅小區是否及有多大程度是可持續的住宅模式作出結論。

742811.label: Realisation of objectives
742811.value: Objective 1 and 2 were successfully completed. To realize these two objectives, two research questions giving special attention to the social implications of the planning and design of the housing estates were raised: how and why they differed from overseas gated communities; and why they have become a dominant housing form in Hong Kong. An inventory of all public and private housing estates in Hong Kong was initially compiled and site visits to different types of housing estates were conducted; their major design principles and concepts were subsequently identified and explained in relation to land, housing and planning policy and socio-economic factors. The distinctiveness of Hong Kong’s housing estates and their socio-spatial performance relative to other gated communities were then explained generally, and specifically by constructing and applying a meticulous framework focusing on design principles and management practices. Objectives 3 and 4 were successfully achieved. To realize these two objectives, three research questions were investigated: what is the social sustainability performance of large housing estates in Hong Kong; does the performance differ between public and private housing estates; and do the planning and design practices of housing estates constitute urban tools to advance socio-spatial justice, and why? A questionnaire survey based on a meticulous social sustainability performance framework and involving 600 residents and 300 outsiders in different types of housing estates were conducted. The survey results were analysed by applying correlation and regression statistical methods. Site observation and interviews were also conducted, in addition to consulting relevant documents and the websites of the Hong Kong Housing Authority and private developers. Objective 5 is also achieved. To address this objective, two questions were tackled: what causes the major weaknesses and strengths in the social sustainability performance of Hong Kong’s public and private housing estates, and specifically what have been driving the continuous improvement in the social performance of the public housing estates; and how transferable is Hong Kong’s housing estate development policy to other high density cities as an urban tool to advance social sustainability? To answer these two questions, the research findings under objectives 1 - 4 are critically examined within the socio-political, economic and geographical contexts of Hong Kong and the social sustainability concepts.

742811.label: Major findings and research outcome
742811.value: Objectives 1 and 2. Large housing estates in Hong Kong added a new type to the gated community (GC) typology - pragmatic GCs. They proliferated because of land scarcity, the emphasis on economic efficiency in land development policy, and the prospect of compensating small housing space by common facilities and space. Spatial segregation and social homogeneity were lesser problems in Hong Kong’s GCs because of: security controls usually installed at building entrance only; accessibility by public transport; shopping malls commonly built in larger GCs and were open to outsiders; mixed income groups in subsidized housing estates, and their good connectivity with neighbouring areas. Internally, increasingly well landscaped social space, interaction within shopping facilities, and security guards services and community activities organized by property management companies strengthened the sense of community (Part C 8(2), 8(3), 9(1), 9(2), 9(6)). Objectives 3 and 4. The questionnaire survey confirmed that Hong Kong’s housing estates, though less so in public rental housing, enjoyed a good sense of safety due to the security guard system and sufficient public surveillance incurred by the mixed land uses and well-designed social and recreation spaces. The sense of belonging and social cohesion was higher in the more gated private housing estates, but the sense of solidarity was stronger in open public and private housing estates and weaker in new or gated estates, regardless of whether public realms, social spaces and landmarks are better provided and designed. Social inclusiveness is stronger in public housing because of the universal design and good connectivity with the neighbouring areas, and also because of the participatory mode of governance. Though consumer sovereignty might drive private housing estates to be gated (segregated), but convenience and developer’s profit motive also led to the provision of shopping malls, thus making private housing estates more permeable and enabling a stronger sense of social inclusion (Part C 8(2),8(3),8(4),9(3),9(4),9(5),9(7),9(8)). Objective 5. This study recommends that except the fully-gated high-priced housing estates, the planning and design of high-rise housing estates in Hong Kong generally constitute effective urban tools to enhance socio-spatial justice - contrary to other GCs. Also, security control at building blocks not at estate entrance strikes a balance among privacy, security and avoidance of socio-spatial segregation. These findings forms the gist of recommendations for improvement and a transferable framework for designing high-rise residential communities and analyzing social development related to housing policy (Part C 8(1),8(4),9(7),9(8),9(9),10(1),11(6)).

742811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
742811.value: First, although high-rises are increasingly regarded as more environmentally sustainable, their livability is severely questioned by residents of low-rise cities. It is therefore useful to compare the social sustainability performance of Hong Kong’s housing estates with that of the common residential forms in other cities. Thus, an edited book on housing policy and social development in Asia was conceived and a proposal was submitted to Routledge (Part C, 11(6)). Second, the findings of this study would be useful to low-rise cities which have been experimenting with high rises, hence a comparative study will be useful. Third, Hong Kong’s residential form has been influential to housing developments in Chinese cities since the 1990’s. However, these new estates are more akin to gated communities in the West, especially the private ones, creating residential enclaves in the rural and peri-urban areas. A comparative study on production processes and social sustainability performance will enrich the gated community literature and have empirical implications. Two doctoral dissertation under the Principal Investigator’s supervision, due to submit in August 2016, are looking into the livability of affordable housing estates and the healthiness of private housing estates in Guangzhou respectively.

742811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
742811.value: The social performance of Hong Kong’s long-existed housing estates are seldom questioned. This study aims to fill this gap. Its objectives are to analyse their evolution in relation to other gated communities; to evaluate the planning and design considerations and their social implications; to evaluate their social sustainability performance based on the residents’and visitors’ views; to explain the differences in sustainability performance among different estate types, specially focusing on the social, political and institutional contexts at the development stage; and to recommend ways to improve the social impact and to develop transferable frameworks for analysing gated communities in high-rise cities. This study found that contrary to gated communities elsewhere, housing estates in Hong Kong facilitate social and spatial justice and sense of community because of the opening of retail and some community services to outsiders, the public transport linkage and their strong connectivity with the neighbouring areas, and the provision of property management services. Residents' participation in estate management is nonetheless weak due to the lack of major management problems, which shows that the housing estates are generally well managed. Based on these findings, the Hong Kong styles of housing estates are recommended for other high density cities.

742911.label: Project Title(Chinese)
742911.value: 統一招生制度中的優惠待遇：動機學校

742911.label: Project Objectives
742911.value: To study students’ application behavior when they know their rank-ordering will be used by schools in their admissions decisions. To study whether it makes sense to suppress the rank-ordering information from schools. (With such suppression, students know that how they rank schools will not influence schools’ decisions. As a result, the truthfulness property of the Gale-Shapley mechanism is restored, despite the drawback that schools no longer have any information about the applicants’ motivations.) To study the incentive of motive schools to adopt early admissions/decisions prior to the central round of admissions. We want to know to what extent their presence improves or exacerbates the overall performance of the admissions system.

742911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
742911.value: A large number of school places throughout the world are being allocated in a coordinated manner; examples include the Joint University Programmes Admissions Ssytem (JUPAS) in Hong Kong and the national college admissions system in mainland China. Instead of filing separate applications to different schools, each student is required to file only a single application (a rank-order list) indicating his/her preferences for schools; schools then allocate their places in accordance with a strict protocol, taking into account applicants' rank-order lists as well as other available information. A growing literature has been devoted to the design of the optimal admissions system, and some variants of the mechanism are adopted in practice. In this literature, it is normally assumed that schools’ preferences over students are well defined, depending on some observable characteristics (e.g., public examination scores). In reality, however, non-observable characteristics may also be important. In particular, because students’ motivations are an important factor to their success in their studies, it is conceivable that a school may want to admit an academically less qualified, more enthusiastic student to an academically more qualified, less enthusiastic student. We say that a school is a motive school if it values the motivation of the applicant; the school is a non-motive school otherwise. The presence of motive schools is not only theoretically possible, evidence can also be found. For instance, in Hong Kong, anecdotal evidence has it that schools which participate in centralized admissions warn potential applicants that they would not receive as much attention if they do not rank the school as their top choice. This is consistent with the interpretation that the school wants the students who want it most. In this project, we aim at understanding various issues related to the optimal design of a centralized admissions mechanism, assuming that some schools are motive schools. In particular, we examine whether the emphasis of student motivation is backfiring in the sense that students will lie about their true preferences in applications; under what circumstances it is a better system that schools not being informed of how they are ranked; and whether allowing schools to adopt early admissions/decisions will improve the performance of the system. Our project is expected to shed insight on how to reform actual admissions systems in HK, mainland China, and Taiwan. 統一招生制度在世界各地得到廣泛應用，比如香港的大學聯合招生辦法(JUPAS)和中國內地的高考制度。參與其中的考生只需填寫一份申請表，而無需向不同的學校分別申請，依照考生上交的申請表和其他的相關資訊，所採用的匹配機制將會實現學校名額與考生之間的配對。 現今，已經有越來越多的文獻致力於設計最優的匹配機制，其中的一些機制並已在現實中得到了應用。現有的文獻通常都假設學校之于學生的偏好(排序)是充分定義的，也就是說是建立在完全可觀測的特質的基礎上(例如,考試成績)。但在現實中，一些不可觀測的學生特質也可能同樣得重要，尤其是學生的學習動機和熱情。自身具備較高學習熱情的學生通常更加容易在長期的學習中獲得成功。因此，從學校的角度考慮，一個成績相對較差但熱情高漲的學生有可能比一個雖然成績較好但學習熱情較低的學生要更加可取，我們稱這類不僅考慮學生成績並且在意學生學習動機的學校為動機學校(其他的學校為非動機學校)。 這類動機學校在現實中也不乏實例。在香港，一些參加聯招的高校就告知申請者，如不將其列為首志願其申請可能不被同等考慮。這種做法與學校希望錄取到最具學習熱情的學生的解釋是一致相容的。 在這個研究專案中，我們就關注此類動機學校存在的情形，旨在探討與最優配對機制設計相關的各種問題。尤其是學校如此之強調學生的學習動機會否適得其反——反而招致虛報偏好的學生；進而，在何種情況下讓學校知道考生是如何對其排序的才是合適的，亦或，允許學校進行提前錄取是否能增進整個招生系統的效率。我們希望能給現實中的香港，中國內地和臺灣地區的高校招生體制改革提出更多洞見。

742911.label: Realisation of objectives
742911.value: This project focuses on a real world practise in centralized admissions systems known as preferential treatment (PT), whereby a school gives priority to applicants that rank it as their first choice over those that only rank it as their second choice, etc., even though the latter students may be academically stronger. Our interest is in situations in which schools adopt PT on their own volition, rather than by mandate. (Hong Kong's JUPAS is one example.) Endogenous PT has received very little attention from economic theorists. In an earlier paper (Chiu and Weng, 2009), we identified two strategic motives as to why schools may adopt PT: notably, a less popular school can use it to attract good applicants that otherwise would not rank it as their top choice (stealing motive), while a more popular school can use it to deter the less popular schools from using it, and thus prevent its applicants from being stolen (preemptive motive). These insights, however, are unlikely to explain all instances of why schools adopt PT, nor to explain why a central mechanism with a PT option would exist in the first place. In this project, we assume instead schools have an innate concern about their applicants' enthusiasm towards them, while students are characterized by their academic abilities and degrees of enthusiasm, which are private information. Building on our previous work, we assume there are two schools: a leading school and a non-leading school. We consider two models that capture different real-world scenarios. In the demand-uncertainty model, students know their own academic ability, but not exactly the other students' innate preferences. In the ranking-uncertainty model, they do not know their own academic ability/performance, either, before submitting their applications. We completely characterize students’ reporting strategies given the pre-announced PT policy (objective one of the project). We also characterize under what circumstances a school may use PT given the other does not use it, as well as the equilibrium outcome when both schools are allowed to choose PT simultaneously and independently. We determine which group of students may be better off when schools are allowed to choose PT. Thus we can answer to which group of students banning the use of PT makes sense (objective two). Finally, we also compare and contrast the present model with one in which schools can conduct early admissions. We find that the two share some similarity but are not identical (objective three).

742911.label: Major findings and research outcome
742911.value: We consider two models that capture different real-world scenarios. In the demand-uncertainty model, students know their own academic ability, but not exactly the other students' innate preferences. In the ranking-uncertainty model, students do not know their own academic ability/performance, either, before submitting their applications. We identify two effects through which a school finds using PT beneficial. The driving-out effect is realized when a school dissuades some unenthusiastic applicants that would otherwise be admitted, thus making room for the admissions of additional enthusiastic applicants. The internalization effect is realized when a school takes advantage of the other school's PT -- hence internalizing its external effect -- by also using the PT policy. Also intended to dissuade unenthusiastic applicants, this effect is achieved only when some other school uses PT. We find that the former effect exists in both models, while the latter effect exists only under the demand-uncertainty model. PT allows schools to value the enthusiasm that students show towards them as seen from their rank-order lists. If this results in separation, the school will be able to learn more about applicants' enthusiasm and PT is thus beneficial. If this results in pooling by unenthusiastic students, however, the rank-order lists are too noisy to reflect applicants' enthusiasm and using PT may be self-defeating. The two models studied differ in the possibility of such an outcome. In general, a less popular school is more likely to benefit from the adoption of PT, and students enthusiastic about a weaker school are more likely to benefit from the policy. This benefit is even more prominent under the ranking-uncertainty model.

742911.value: Thus far the research has been conducted for the audience among economic theorists. But a paper that targets for education researchers and policy makers should also be written for better knowledge dissemination.

742911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
742911.value: This paper focuses on a real world practise in centralized admissions systems known as preferential treatment (PT), wherein a school gives priority to applicants that rank it as their first choice over those that only rank it as their second choice, etc., even though the latter students may be academically stronger. Our interest is in situations in which schools adopt PT on their own volition, rather than by mandate (Hong Kong's college admissions programme JUPAS is example). Being informed of their applicants' rank-ordering of the schools to which they have applied, schools can just ignore this information or choose to consider it as one criterion, and weight it accordingly, in evaluating applicants. In this project, we have studied how students and schools behave (strategically) in such schemes. We are able to address questions such as which group of students would like schools to use PT and what types of schools might actually use it. Understanding it is of primary importance when we reform the present systems, evidenced from a small debate the PI triggered in a local media in 2012 (see the last section of this report for detail.)

743511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
743511.value: The present study intends to provide empirical evidence on how lawyers interact with their young clients by examining the young persons’ appraisal of their legal representatives and their experiences of the lawyer-client relationship. It is not difficult to imagine the stigma and stress that may amount in a criminal proceeding, especially on young persons. The role of the defence lawyer is vital not only in ensuring that due process is afforded to young defendants but that it also contributes positively to the young person’s perception of the criminal justice system. Given the possible legal and social implications, scarce empirical studies have been devoted to the relationship between a young client and his/her lawyer, particularly from the perspectives of young people themselves in Hong Kong. The present research will sample a number of young offenders, at-risk youths, and non-offenders aged between 14 and 20 and investigate the factors related to the young people’s appraisal of their legal representatives and their experiences of the lawyer-client relationship. A combination of quantitative and qualitative research design will be adopted in this study. The first stage of this study will examine through a self-administered questionnaire young offenders’ first-hand accounts of their views towards their lawyer’s services from the first meeting to the end of trial. For instance, a number of standardized scales measuring young people’s view of the criminal justice personnel, attitudes towards the law, knowledge of due process rights, perceived fairness in lawyer-client interactions, trust, and treatment with dignity and respect will be used. Wherever appropriate, a comparison group consists of non-offenders will be recruited to complete a shortened version of the questionnaire. In addition, young offenders’ understanding of the justice system (such as the roles of defence lawyers) and their constitutional rights, as well as the outcomes of their case, will also be measured to assess whether these factors predict their satisfaction or dissatisfaction of their lawyers. The second stage of the study is to conduct in-depth interviews with young offenders and lawyers in order to elicit their experiences on their lawyer-client relationship. In many respects, the findings will offer evidence of informed policy development to the improvement of the youth justice system and towards the promotion of the rehabilitation of young offenders. 是次研究目的在於透過研究青少年對他們的法定代表人(律師)的評價，以及檢視他們在律師客戶關係中的經驗。青少年在刑事訴訟中可能會感受到恥辱感和壓力，這是不難想像的。辯護律師的角色是重要的，不但要確保能提供合法訴訟程序予青少年被告，而且能使青少年對刑事司法系統的感覺有正面的看法。 是次研究將會抽樣年齡介乎14至20歲的青少年罪犯、邊緣青少年、非青少年罪犯，研究調查影響青少年對他們的法律代表的評價的因素，與及他們在律師客戶關係中的經驗。本研究將會一併採用定性和定量設計。 研究第一階段將透過自行填寫模式問卷，收集青少年罪犯對自己律師的服務的意見的第一手資料，包括由第一次與律師會議到結束審判整個過程的意見。研究將採用標準化尺度去量度青少年對刑事司法人員的意見、對法律的態度、有關合法訴訟程序的知識、律師與客戶的互動是否公平、信任、有否顧及青少年的尊嚴和提供治療。同時在合適的情況下，會招募對邊緣青少年、非青少年罪犯，完成一個較短版本的調查問卷。而且，本研究將會評估青少年罪犯對司法制度的認識(如辯護律師的角色)和他們於憲法中的權利，以及案件的結果，從而預測他們對律師的滿意度或非滿意度。 在研究第二階段，為了帶出青少年在律師客戶關係中的經驗，將與青少年罪犯和律師進行深入訪問。從多方面，研究結果將提供規劃政策發展的證據，改善青少年司法系統和促進青年罪犯的復康工作。

743511.label: Realisation of objectives
743511.value: Overall speaking, the scope of this study followed very closely what has been set out in the proposal. All the objectives have been achieved by executing the project according to the research plan outlined in the original proposal. There are two stages of the study. The first stage involves the collection of quantitative data by accessing three groups of young people, namely offender sample, at-risk youth sample and the school sample with the assistance of a number of non-governmental organizations and schools. The total number of valid samples collected from the young offenders, youth-at-risk, and secondary school students is 1,184; and there were more than 100 invalid questionnaires which contain a large number of missing data. In this survey, all respondents were asked to evaluate their direct and/ indirect experience with lawyers from the procedural justice perspective. Two sample groups, namely the at-risk youth and young offenders were also asked to examine the dynamics of the lawyer-client relationship if they had direct experience with publicly-funded and/ private lawyers. A number of standardized measurements of the concepts such as procedural justice, fairness, criminal sentiments, attitudes towards lawyers, and lawyer-client interaction were used in the survey questionnaire. The second stage involves the collection of qualitative data from 10 defence lawyers and 30 young offenders and ex-offenders. A total of 40 in-depth individual semi-structured interviews were conducted to see how lawyering can be improved to meet the needs of young people. The use of mixed method approach of understanding young people’s view of lawyers in Hong Kong yields very important data to inform how young defendants can better be represented in the courtroom and how young people in general see the role of lawyers in promoting procedural justice at the course of the criminal justice process.

743511.label: Major findings and research outcome
743511.value: This project has already produced 3 referred journal articles, 3 conference presentations and a research monograph. Another paper has been revised two times and is under review. Parts of the quantitative findings have been reported in in the Social Sciences Citation Indexed (SSCI) journal entitled: International Journal of Law, Crime and Justice. Major findings are: The aim of this study was to compare the understanding and perceptions of lawyers among three youth groups classified according to experience in instructing lawyers and varying degrees of delinquency – young offenders (the only group who had experience of hiring lawyers), youth-at-risk and students (N = 1,157), and to determine if perceptions of lawyers affect views on the legitimacy of the justice system. Students showed greater understanding about lawyers and more favorable perceptions of fairness in lawyer-client interactions compared with young offenders and youth-at-risk. Another paper that looks at young people’s offending behavior and their criminal sentiments towards crime has been published in a refereed journal entitled the International Journal of Adolescence and Youth. Its findings are: In this study, we tested the relationship between criminal sentiments and social factors and illegal conduct among 942 Chinese youths (aged 14 to 18) in Hong Kong using the Criminal Sentiments Scale-Modified (CSS-M). The results were mixed. While all the underlying factors of the CSS-M were found to be significant, only negative attitudes toward the Law-Court-Police and Identifications with Criminal Others had a positive relationship. Contrary to expectations, Tolerance for Law Violations had a negative correlation. Moreover, both social factors and criminal attitudes were found to be significant in influencing youths’ criminal behavior. The results are discussed in the Hong Kong Chinese context. Qualitative data generated from the interviews with 10 defence lawyers and 30 young offenders and ex-offenders have been published in a SSCI journal entitled Social and Legal Studies: This article examines the ways in which youth defendants and defence lawyers negotiate the welfare and justice imperatives of the Hong Kong juvenile justice system and end up accepting the disciplinary welfare model. Publicly funded lawyers have become primarily plea mitigators, assisting the state in seeing to the welfare and ‘the best interests of the child’. A study of Hong Kong will lead to a broader understanding of how a welfare-oriented system can work in a time when juvenile justice systems around the world emphasize human rights, due process and children’s rights.

743511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
743511.value: Findings of this study have implications for future research. For instance, a prospective research design will be proposed to further look at the association between young people’s perceived procedural justice and the subsequent offending behaviour. While young defendants’ interaction with the lawyer forms part of their perception of the legal proceedings in the criminal justice system, equally it is important to look at the interaction between young people and other criminal justice personnel such as the police and other law enforcement officers. By doing so, this will conjure up a more holistic picture how young offenders are dealt with in an adversarial criminal justice system that Hong Kong people are proud of. Funding may be sought to further investigate how procedural justice has been applied in the criminal justice process.

743511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
743511.value: Young people in are more likely than any other age group to come into contact with the justice system. The present study provides evidence on how lawyers represent their clients by examining the young persons’ appraisal of their lawyers and their experiences of the lawyer-client relationship. This study sampled young offenders, at-risk youths, and students (non-offenders) aged between 14 and 20. The finding shows that students showed greater understanding about lawyers and more favourable perceptions of fairness in lawyer-client interactions compared with young offenders and youth-at-risk. A better understanding of lawyers had a positive association with perceptions of fairness, and a higher perception of fairness had a positive association with legitimacy of the justice system. Regression analyses indicated that the young offender sample who had private lawyers were more satisfied compared to those who had duty lawyers. Two elements of procedural justice, participation and trustworthiness, demonstrated the strongest influence on youths’ satisfaction with their lawyers. Supplementary interviews with 40 young defendants and defence lawyers explained the discrepancy, revealing that the limited amount of time spent by duty lawyers in meetings and their detached focus contributed to clients’ low perceptions of participation and trustworthiness.

743711.value: 這個研究計劃的主要研究員已受法國巴黎Classiques Garnier出版社委託，以編纂瑞士哲學家讓––雅克．盧梭有關植物學的著作，作為權威性新編法語版《讓––雅克．盧梭全集》的一部份出版。作為一個自學的通才，盧梭不但以其《社會契約論》聞名於世，他也對不同學術範疇貢獻良多。他的影響是全球性的。在中國，他的《懺悔錄》在1925年首次被翻譯成中文，並自此大受歡迎。他所創製的數字譜仍為今日中國音樂界所採用。 這個版本的 《盧梭全集》會讓大眾認識盧梭的植物學著作，並為各範疇的學者，如哲學、文學、歷史、音樂、文化研究和科學，提供相關的研究材料。盧梭的植物學著作，將會以書籍和電子書的形式，於 《盧梭全集》的卷十七、卷十九(部份)及卷二十出版。2012年是盧梭的三百週年誕辰，而這部《盧梭全集》，正是為了紀念這個日子，由一班國際頂尖的學者所重新編纂。 這個計劃的主要研究員現尋求研究經費以作以下用途： (1) 撰寫一個總論以總結已出版的學術論著，尤其著重有關科學史的研究成果。主要研究員會說明盧梭的植物學著作在歷史學，哲學和科學三個範疇的重要性。 (2) 設計一個嚴謹而具學術性的工具，讓讀者更能明白當時盧梭曾參與過的，有關植物分類與命名的辯論、盧梭研究植物學的背景，以及這種非常視象化的科學的物質文化。 (3) 整理原始文獻，使其可以順利出版。在盧梭的手稿中，有不少原稿是殘缺不全，字跡難以辨認的，以致未能準確地按時序編排。此外，盧梭經典著作《植物學用語詞典殘片》的手稿，如其曾經存在的話，亦已遺失多時，使整理工作加倍困難。故此，我們需要經費去尋找並研究這失落的原稿。 (4) 介紹盧梭所藏植物標本 - 一份科學報告，依據其他植物學參考書，以核對盧梭對其藏品的命名，並找出其藏品現在的學名。 - 抄錄及詮釋盧梭所藏植物標本所附帶的按語，以供讀者所用。 - 跟進及研究已遺失的植物標本的下落 新編法語版《盧梭全集》的這些特點，使以上所計劃的工作，為學者以及一般讀者帶來極大的方便。直至現時為止，並未曾有一個《盧梭全集》的版本能如此透徹而細緻地涉及盧梭的植物學著作。

743711.label: Realisation of objectives
743711.value: The Œuvres complètes de J-.J. Rousseau (Classiques Garnier) is a critical edition of the complete works of Jean Jacques Rousseau comprising 21 volumes and involves contributors from Europe, the Americas and Asia. The presentation of the OC JJR is chronological rather than thematic. This feature entails a substantially longer preparation time because a variety of documents with different editors are co-mingled in most volumes. Furthermore, each document or group of documents require(s) a scholarly introduction and apparatus. Since most volumes have multiple contributors, coordination is indispensable. Note also that the presentation of material in later volumes depends on the careful presentation of material in earlier volumes. Unfortunately the OC JJR project directors are not coordinating work on the edition; their attempt to coordinate via a google site fizzled out in late summer 2012. Nor is the publisher providing any meaningful management or coordination. Hence: (1) the current status of the volumes to which the PI is contributing is unknown and there is no updated list of the contributors so the PI can coordinate her work directly with other contributors whose work may overlap with hers; a few months ago the PI attempted to contact the purported editor of one of the related texts to appear in vol. 15, but received no reply; (2) there is no house style sheet, and all attempts to obtain one have been fruitless; and (3) the project directors take an ad hoc approach toward all matters arising, including a critical reproduction permission issue involving 168 key images. One project director claims he alone can resolve this issue, and has promised several times to be on the verge of doing so; however, at this writing the permission problem remains unresolved 1.5 years after the PI pushed it onto the agenda. The outstanding status of this last matter precludes completion of vol. 19, the major vol. under the PI’s direction. An enormous amount of time, energy, thought and grant funds have been absorbed in attempting to address (1), (2) and (3), in addition to issues noted in earlier reports. These futile attempts to obtain information and resolve problems have distracted the PI and her SRA from their work and entailed keeping track of a voluminous correspondence for their own information and for this report. Unfortunately, the PI is therefore unable to estimate, much less state, when the volumes for which she has prepared material will appear in print.
