743711.label: Major findings and research outcome
743711.value: The major findings are: 1) A chronological order for Rousseau’s botanical works, including the purported botanical dictionary, discussed in item 4 below. 2) Omissions from texts published in earlier editions have been identified and corrected. 3) A long-ignored document concerning plants Rousseau collected with a Dr. Neuhaus of Neuchâtel is the first botanical text presented in the OC (vol. 15). The PI determined that this 1-page document merits close study. She found that the plant names Rousseau used in it derive from at least three different sources--Linnaeus, Haller and Garsault. This finding supports the PI’s argument that Rousseau was (1) a taxonomic pluralist rather than merely a devoted follower of Linnaean taxonomy, and (2) that the Swiss botanist Albrecht von Haller played an important role in Rousseau’s botanical thought. Moreover Dr. Neuhaus figured in the same Swiss botanical-medical network that the PI has been researching in conjunction with her work on Rousseau. The resulting 30-page introduction to the ‘Herborisation avec M. Neuhaus’ documents the influence on Rousseau of the scientific milieu in Neuchâtel and Switzerland more generally. The PI attributes Rousseau’s taxonomic pluralism to a large extent to his exposure in Switzerland to various classification systems. While the PI placed considerable stress on this point in her 2012 monograph, concerted study of the Neuhaus document and its background has added more weight to this argument. Note that the selection committee for the Thackray Medal (awarded to the PI in 2014) singled out this finding as of particular importance. 4) This edition of Rousseau’s botanical writings will be the first to elucidate the origins of the Fragmens pour un dicitonnaire des termes d’usage en botanique, previously considered canonical. The PI shows this work was probably a posthumous work fashioned from Rousseau’s notes, and contributions of unknown extent by two or three editors. See also publication 2 in Section C. 5) Inclusion of an organism index, making this the first edition of the OC JJR to contain such a list. 6) All plant names have been checked against The Plantlist, the most authoritative botanical names research database to date. Such a list has never been included in earlier editions. It gives the edition scientific value. 7) A significant expansion of the sources Rousseau used beyond the findings reported in Appendix I to JJR and botany. 8) Herbaria specimen names have been checked against eighteenth-century botanical reference works by Michel Adanson, Familles des plantes and Antoine-Nicolas Duchesne, Manuel de botanique, both important contributions to the natural method of classification.

743711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
743711.value: The research has revealed several directions for further development. 1) It has contributed further evidence to support the PI’s hypothesis that contrary to the received view, Rousseau adopted elements of the natural method of classification. 2) The research has revealed more about botanical works on which Rousseau relied, especially works from Renaissance authors based in England, Italy and the Low Countries; the PI will develop these findings further in an article on J.J. Rousseau as reader of Renaissance botanical works. 3) The research adds to our knowledge of the Swiss botanical-medical network that the PI explored in _Jean-Jacques Rousseau and botany_ (2012). There is great potential for future development of this under-researched area. Papers 4 and 6 reported in Sec. C directly address important figures from this network who have sunk into obscurity. One of these, Laurent Garcin FRS (1683-1752) of Neuchâtel, was a Dutch East India Company physician who collected Asian plants that he gave to the Dutch botanist, Johannes Burman, a friend of Linnaeus. A genus of Asian plants, Garcinia, was named for Garcin. The PI is working on locating these specimens as well as documents relating to Garcin in order to learn more about his work in South Asia and present-day Indonesia.

743711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
743711.value: The Œuvres complètes de J-.J. Rousseau (to be published by Classiques Garnier, Paris, France) presents the complete works of the Genevan (Swiss) philosopher Jean Jacques Rousseau (1712-1778). This edition comprises 21 volumes, drawing on the work of specialist editors from Europe, Asia and the Americas. The final presentation of the OC JJR is chronological rather than thematic, which enables readers to study the documents in temporal relation to other works, which yields extremely useful insights. In the funded project, the PI has prepared Rousseau’s botanical works for the OC. These include a wide range of documents such as letters and notes as well as dried plant collections, also known as herbaria. None of these works were published during Rousseau’s lifetime, so the PI has researched the most accurate way to present them supported by apparatus such as extensive explanatory footnotes and documentation of Rousseau’s botanical library. For the herbaria the PI has researched the modern plant names and key sources that Rousseau used in assigning vernacular and Latin names. She has demonstrated Rousseau’s adoption of elements of the natural method of classification, thereby establishing Rousseau's status as a serious botanist and important popularizer of botany as medicine for the soul.

743911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
743911.value: The key goal of this project is to capitalise on the opening up of a whole range of party archives in China in order to bring to life the social history of the early People's Republic (1949¬57). Surely the most momentous change in the history of modern China was the advent of a revolutionary regime in 1949. Yet we know surprisingly little about those early years, in particular in terms of what socialism actually meant for people on the ground. Besides the fact that subsequent events such as the Great Leap Forward (1958-61) and the Cultural Revolution (1966-69) have deflected attention away from these early years, there is another good reason for this relative neglect: party archives, until recently, have generally been closed to historians. The objective of the project is to capitalise on the opening up of party archives in China to move beyond a narrow focus on top leaders and analyse instead the many intricate encounters, alterations, misunderstandings, negotiations and conflicts which took place between different social goups and the revolutionary regime: how was the party line altered to accommodate the reality of local resistance, accommodation or support at the level of everyday life? Political scientists have looked at the grand designs for building socialism and at the policy formulations of the party leadership, while anthropologists have used interviews to look at life in the village, but a social history of the early years of the PRC cannot exist without a politics of everyday life. Newly opened party archives - whether at the provincial level or lower down at the county level - allow us to build up a social history of the momentous changes that took place from 1949 to 1957, including land reform in 1950, the campaign against counter-revolutionaries in 1951-2, the nationalisation of private companies after 1953, the first collectivisation of the countryside in 1955-7 and the Hundred Flowers in 1956 to the Anti-Rightist campaign in 1957. The significance of the project is multifold, generating new knowledge and fresh insights about the experience of revolution, regime consolidation and everyday life in the early PRC, publishing a series of research articles and possibly a research monograph, and expanding Hong Kong's reputation as a cutting-edge centre for China Studies. 这个研究项目的主要目的是利用最近在中国开放的共产党的档案来研究中华人民共和国建国初期十年的社会史。1949年是中国近代史上一个重大的里程碑。然而直到今天我们对这段历史知道的很少：当时共产党的政策到底是什么样的？以及建立社会主义对中国普通老百姓意味着什么？而最近开放的省一级以及县一级的档案给我们研究这些问题提供了极其重要的线索。这个项目研究的重点包括：1950年左右的土地改革；1951年至1952年的第一次镇反运动；1953年以后的公私合营；1955年至1957年在农村实行的合作化运动；1956年提出来的“双百”方针（百花齐放，百家争鸣）以及1957年的反右运动。这个研究项目的重要性是多方面的。为了对建国初期五十年代中国社会以及当时中国普通老百姓的生活有一个新的，透彻的认识， 这个项目将出版一系列这方面的书籍和文章。这个项目无疑会为香港成为研究中国问题的国际中心打下扎实的基础。

743911.label: Major findings and research outcome
743911.value: The key of the project was to turn to evidence from the archives to reinterpret the period from 1949 to 1957 with a much greater focus on the experiences of ordinary people. The book that results from the project is the first comprehensive history of the foundation years of the PRC, an era which is essential to understand the current regime in Beijing. Other studies have focused on separate episodes, say land reform or the anti-rightist campaign, but none have seen it in its entirety, making clear the links between different events. The project shows, from the point of view of people of all walks of life, how promises made by the communists were gradually broken, as basic freedoms of speech, movement, association, belief and trade were curtailed by 1957. Often protrayed as a “Golden Age” before the advent of such catastrophes as the Great Leap Forward (1958-1962) and the Cultural Revolution (1966-1976), this project has found a wealth of newly opened archives to show that the first years of the regime were an era of “systematic violence and calculated terror”. But the project also gives plenty of space to true believers and faithful followers. Even as every promise was broken, the party kept on gaining followers, and some of them displayed astonishing faith and almost fanatical conviction, sometimes even after they themselves had ended up being devoured by the party machine.

743911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
743911.value: The logical next step was of course to take further this and the preceding project on the Great Leap Forward to examine the Cultural Revolution, again using archival evidence to get closer to the pulse of social life, squarely placing ordinary people at the centre of history. This is now being done thanks to an ANR-RGC grant.

743911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
743911.value: The year 1949 is often portrayed as the defining moment of modern Chinese history, as the old order was swept away by a communist revolution, but we know surprisingly little about what happened to ordinary people once the red flag was hoisted by Mao Zedong on a pole overlooking Beijing's Forbidden City. There are excellent academic studies on the period, but they tend to focus on individual episodes, for instance land reform or the anti-rightist campaign, and are often based on a top to bottom approach in which the focus is squarely on elite politics. This project uses an abundance of recently opened archives from the PRC to look at the first years of revolution. The archives show that the era was not so much one of peace, liberty and justice, the promised values of the regime, but systematic violence and calculated terror. Between 1949 and 1957, basic freedoms were curtailed one after the other, while most obstacles that stood between the state and the individual were eliminated. By 1957 most people, whether farmers, monks or teachers, were state employees. But even as every promise was broken, the party kept on gaining followers, and some of them displayed astonishing faith and almost fanatical conviction, sometimes even after they themselves had ended up being devoured by the party machinery.

743911.value: Maybe this is the right place to add a few comments about the book, which is, after all, the main output of the project. It is 145,000 words in length and has been translated into Dutch, with translations into Mandarin, Portuguese, Korean, Japanese and Spanish underway. It was shortlisted for the George Orwell Prize in the UK, described as "Britain's most prestigious prize for political writing". It has been widely reviewed in the press, and academic reviews are also appearing, in particular one lengthy review and a rebuttal in the China Quarterly half a year ago. The book was selected in 2013 as one of the Books of the Year by both the Economist and the Sunday Times. The article to be published in the European Review of History sounds like it is much more on the famine of 1958 to 1962, but this is slightly misleading. What the piece does is build a bridge between the two projects (the preceding one on the famine and this one on liberation), pointing out how, from 1949 to 1958, many of the traditional strategies of survival (escape from the village, turn to charitable institutions, sell personal possessions, ask a wealthy neighbour for help, etc) were gradually stripped away, which explains, in part, the magnitude of the disaster in the following years. I am not sure what "recognised international conferences" are, but I have presented the project at invited talks at the University of Amsterdam, Harvard University, Yale University, University of Pennsylvania and Dartmouth College as well as at the Edinburgh Literary Festival, Asia House, the Blenheim Literary Festival, the Asia Society in Hong Kong, the Auckland Writers' Festival, the Sydney Writers' Festival, the Hong Kong Book Fair and the Hong Kong Literary Festival.

744111.label: Project Title(Chinese)
744111.value: 身体动作与服饰意识：动觉与中国的现代性

744111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
744111.value: “身体动作与服饰意识”研究计划主要分析十九世纪晚期到二十世纪前三十年中国感官世界的变迁。此研究项目采用有关“动觉”的主题，为变革现代中国的诸种现代化诉求提供新的视角。在这个时段内，中国关于身体通在不同情境需展示出适宜动作以及得体的服饰穿着会促进身体语言表达的认知有了巨大的变化。 此项目致力于：为城市的动觉文化的变迁作出全面的分析；分析大众流行层面对身体“适宜”动作的看法的变化；探讨服饰衣着与身体动作的相互影响机制；挑战欧美对于感觉官能的历史作用的主流看法，提出对应的中国动觉文化；为开创一个全新中国研究领域—— “官能意识”领域提供研究范式。 相较于在其他文化及时期中感觉官能历史得到的广泛研究，中国的感官秩序如何变迁这一议题还没有得到全面的研究。本项目的动觉研究将为弥补这方面的空白迈出重要的一步。 本项目通过借鉴以往学者们对于感觉官能的理论研究方法，展现出支撑这些理论与模式的文化与时间特异性，从而为中国研究打开一个新领域。 近年来，感觉官能对理解人类社会产生的作用逐渐引起学界的重视。“感觉官能”广义理解为“采集信息的身体性方式”（Guerts），对人们经验世界有重要作用。与此同时，人类对 “感觉官能”的特性，作用以及功能的观照不但随着文化的不同而产生差异，在特定的文化系统中也会因时间的变更而各异。对感觉的跨文化、超历史研究已经持续涌现。例如创刊于2006年的杂志《感官与社会》（The Senses and Society）的近期研究表明：感觉官能是一种文化与历史的建构，其研究不再局限于心理学以及神经生物学范围，触角伸向更为广泛的如文学、人类学、文化研究以及历史学等领域。 简·珍妮（Geaney, Jane）的《中国早期思想中的感官认识论》（On the Epistemology of the Senses in Early Chinese Thought， 2002）是目前东西方学界惟一一部研究中国感觉机制的著作。书中极具颠覆性的卓见挑战我们对前现代中国的理解。然而，有关中国“动觉”历史变迁的研究却不见于任何一本著作。本研究项目正是致力于这一被缺漏以及忽视的领域。正如高彦颐（Ko, Dorothy）等学者提出的“物质文化研究”为中国历史研究开创出新视角一样（Finnane 2007 and Ko 2007），本计划“身体动作与服饰意识”也将为中国历史以及中国研究开拓更为广阔的空间。

744411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
744411.value: This project argues that in a period of British imperial decline and increasing contact with a rapidly modernizing China, British middlebrow writers attempted to re-define imaginatively relations between East and West by specifically transposing cross-cultural relations into the realm of the domestic and the intimate. By revealing the disorganization of narratives of intimate relations both in Britain and China as a result of contact, middlebrow writing meditates on changing imperial structures of feeling in a global arena where white superiority was no longer a given. Middlebrow writing and culture has begun to attract scholarly attention as an important part of British modernity. A focus on highbrow modernists and lowbrow popular culture has resulted in the neglect of a spectrum of literary and cultural texts that appealed to the broad middle. Such texts were well-written and engaging, meant for intelligent readers who wished for reading material as pleasurable as lowbrow pulp fiction only better-written, yet who also shied away from the intellectual abstractions of the avant-garde. By the 1920s and 30s, as the term ‘middlebrow’ passed into popular parlance, the identity of the middlebrow reader and text was gradually coalescing round notions of pleasure, domesticity, femininity and conservatism. These markers of the middlebrow have thus resulted in it being seen as inferior to both highbrow and (perversely) lowbrow cultures. Yet as the domain of the dominant middle-classes, middlebrow culture’s broad reach was a means of both consolidating traditional values and transmitting emergent ideas to a wider audience. Middlebrow culture, so often dismissed as uninteresting for being narrow and merely concerned with preserving the status quo, had actually the potential to influence and shape existing social discourses, both conservatively and subversively. After all, middlebrow authors covered the entire range of political and social positions. With regards to the representation of China, the more conservative sectors of middlebrow cultures thus continued to peddle familiar stereotypes of China and the Chinese, allaying anxieties about the rise of the Chinese while the more progressive end of the middlebrow cultural spectrum could provide ways to re-imagine and re-educate the British about China and the Chinese. In examining a variety of long-forgotten middlebrow novels and plays, I intend to fill a gap in critical knowledge by showing how middlebrow cultures were alert to global shifts and attentive to the needs for new narratives about empire and China. 二十世紀初期英國想像中的中國 該項目認為，今後一個時期的英帝國衰落和增加接觸與迅速現代化中國，英國中庸作家試圖重新界定想像力東方和西方之間的關係。因此，熟悉的比喻東西方遇到這樣的異族戀情，歐亞和文明誰可以恢復到原始類型被重新調用，重動畫，有時甚至顛覆想像，一個現代化和全球化的世界。 中庸寫作和文化已開始引起學者關注的一個重要組成部分，英國的現代性。一個側重於曲高和寡現代主義和低俗的大眾文化造成了忽視頻譜的文學和文化文本的呼籲廣大的中間。這樣的案文寫得很好，引人入勝，這意味著誰希望智能讀者的閱讀材料作為紙漿愉快的低俗小說只有更好寫，但誰也迴避的智力抽象的前衛。到了20世紀 20年代和30年代，由於長期“中庸”傳遞到流行的說法，認同的中庸讀者和文本的概念逐漸凝聚輪的快感，家庭生活，女性和保守。 這些標記的中庸有這樣導致它被視為陽春白雪和下雙方（反常）低俗文化 。然而，作為域名的主導中產階級，中庸文化的廣闊範圍是指既鞏固傳統的價值觀和理念傳播給更廣泛的新興觀眾。中庸的文化，因此常常被斥之為乏味的狹隘，只關心維持現狀，實際上已潛在的影響和塑造現有的社會話語，無論是保守的，並且用。畢竟，中庸作者範圍覆蓋了整個政治和社會地位。 此外，針對代表的中國，更保守階層的中庸文化因而繼續兜售熟悉定型的中國和中國，緩解焦慮有關崛起的中國，而更進步月底， 中庸文化的頻譜可以提供的方式重新-想像和再教育，英國對中國和中國。在研究 各種長期被遺忘的中庸小說和戲劇，我打算以填補差距的關鍵知識通過展示如何中庸文化警覺全球變化和周到的需要為新的有關中國的敘述。

744711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
744711.value: This project explores the intersections of art, labor, technological information, economics, and politics in agricultural paintings from China during the Qing dynasty. Entitled Pictures of Tilling and Weaving these paintings, comprising a pair of handscrolls illustrates rice cultivation and silk production, originated in the Song dynasty (960-1279). Precise brushwork characterizes these images, with the agricultural processes illustrated in a step-by-step sequential arrangement and accompanied by a poem. These paintings and poems provide commentary on the relationships between farmers, officials, and monarch, drawing upon classical political theory to represent an ideal society. Reform movements in the Song vigorously re-interpreted the Confucian classics, seeking to apply them within a contemporary setting, and the Song Pictures of Tilling and Weaving endorsed the reform movements. By the Yuan dynasty (1279-1368), the genre was well established, but during the Ming era (1368-1644), their content was regarded as too technological and their style was deemed old-fashioned. During the Qing dynasty (1644-1911), however, the pictures of tilling and weaving regained their former canonical status. After the founding of the empire, three successive emperors commissioned different versions of these pictures, applying varying interpretative strategies to the images and poems and generating new iconographic programs. These three Qing versions of such pictures offer a focused perspective to investigate the intersection of art production and imperial patronage as it transformed along an historical continuum. The iconography of the pictures and their accompanying poems were manipulated to accommodate the differing political needs of the individual emperors. The pictures of tilling and weaving by virtue of their subject matter and patronage provide a unique combination of history of science, art, economics, and politics. This mix is further complicated by the introduction of painting styles that were identified with European modes of scientific inquiry. While labels within primary documents support a clear distinction between scientific approaches as either “western” or Chinese, the divisions were not so separate in Qing discourse. At times, the elite aligned European learning with earlier, classical scholarship. The pictures of the tilling and weaving genre, with its classical lineage and systematic representation of agricultural procedures, served to bolster claims to modes of knowledge that were indigenous, yet consistent with “European” science. This study positions the genre within its historical and court contexts in order to elucidate the ways in which representations of labor advanced Qing imperial interests and the court’s interactions with the “western” world. 是項計劃將探討中國清代（1644-1911）農業繪畫中，藝術、勞動者、科技資訊、經濟及政治之間的交切點。這些名為《耕織圖》的畫作，由一對分別說明種植稻米及生產絲綢的手卷組成，其起始源自宋代（960-1279）。這些圖畫的特色是筆致精密，將農業生產的每一個步驟按次解說，並逐一伴以詩句。這些圖畫及其題詩以傳統政治理論展現一個理想化的社會，為農民、官員及專制君主之間的關係予以論評。在宋代，改革運動將儒家經典大肆重新闡釋，務求將其應用於當時的社會環境，而宋代的《耕織圖》則是對這場改革運動的支持。至元代（1279-1368），這種題材已廣受認同。但到了明代（1368-1644），它們的內容卻被視為過於技術性，而其畫風亦被看作過時。 然而在清代，耕織圖恢愎了它們昔日的典範地位。在大清立國之後，連續三位皇帝都下令繪製不同版本的耕織圖，並向這些圖像及詩句施以相異的解說策略，產生了全新的圖像程式。這三個清版耕織圖沿著歷史的延續而演變，提供了一個鮮明的角度去探討藝術生產與皇室贊助的交切點。這些圖像及題詩被巧妙地處理過，從而配合個別君主不同的政治需要。 耕織圖由於其題材及贊助者，給予我們一個集科學史、藝術史、經濟史及政治史的獨特組合。隨著加入了以歐洲科學研究模式著名的繪畫風格，這個混合體變得更為複雜。雖然原始文獻中的標題確立了一個清楚分野，一種就是科學方法即「西方」的，另一種就是中國式的，但在清代的論說之中，兩者間卻不是那麼明確劃分。有些時候，精英名士會將歐洲的知識與早期的、傳統的學問相提並論。耕織圖一類題材，以其傳統典故以及有系統地展現農作步驟，被用作支持一種認知模式旳主張；這種認知模式既是固有的，但亦和「歐洲的」科學是一致的。這次研究將置這種題材於其歷史及朝廷的背景，用以闡明清代皇室從這種描繪勞動者的途徑而得以提升其利益，及清廷與「西方」世界的交互作用。

744711.label: Realisation of objectives
744711.value: I have achieved the project objectives in a book-length manuscript entitled “Empire at Work: Picturing Chinese agrarian laborers in the 18th to early19th century.” This manuscript consists of four chapters with a brief introduction, short epilogue and several appendices. The project objectives are addressed throughout the manuscript and first an introduction to the chapters and their themes with some mention of the appendices is provided in order to elucidate how these targets have been realized. Chapter One, “The Kangxi Emperor Reworks the Pictures of Tilling and Weaving,” considers the motivations for the revitalization of the Pictures of Tilling and Weaving (hearafter PTW) by the Kangxi emperor in the late 17th century. The Pictures of Tilling and Weaving are a series of paintings that depict the procedures necessary to cultivate rice and weave silk fabric. They were inaugurated in the 12th-century of the Song dynasty. This chapter explores Kangxi’s version of the PTW and the motivations for their appearance and his interests in reviving them. The Kangxi Emperor turned to culture and its companion learning for means to consolidate his position. After traveling to the south to assert his claims to this territory, he was given a version of the PTW. Seizing upon the PTW as a means to make claims to the history of Chinese agrarian heritage with is classical theory of government that validates an informed monarch, Kangxi reworked them. He took over Chinese culture and at the same time to demonstrate his excellent command of Western learning in the visual form of linear perspective as well as scientific knowledge or Scientia. This chapter has established a connection between the use of perspective in the Pictures of the Tilling and Weaving as a visual corollary between the legitimation of the Qing court Western-style calendar and Kangxi as the proper and enlightened ruler on the throne of China. Moreover the emperor wrote a new suite of poems to affirm the brilliance of his reign, providing a literary means to further indicate his great reign. Chapter Two titled “The Occupations of the Yongzheng Emperor” continues the story of the next iteration of the PTW. With a power struggle ensuing among the sons of the emperor for the throne, art historians have argued that Prince Yinzhen, used the PTW as part of his campaign to secure the emperorship. In an unusual twist, he placed himself and members of his family in the scenes as the farmers and weavers hard at labor producing a bountiful harvest of rice and silk. In addition he wrote a new suite of poems for the procedures. Once ensconced on the throne, the Yongzheng Emperor continued to deploy imagery of agrarian labor and its products to legitimize his reign. In annual public spectacles, the Yongzheng Emperor took a focused interest in repetitively re-enacting the Zhou-era ceremony of “Emperor personally pushing the plow” and had the scene commemorated in handscrolls. In addition to these representations of activities designed to promote his placement in the imperial position, Yongzheng also documented the results of agrarian productivity in the form of the painting “Auspicious Grains.” In his public relations as emperor he sought to affirm his right to his privileged appointment and used imagery of labor and its fruits to persuade all to agree. Chapter Three, “The Qianlong Emperor’s industry of labor and documentation,” explores the ways in which Qianlong comprehensively transformed the PTW from technologically-informed representations of an ideal society to objects that affirmed his divine right to rule. Qianlong settled into his reign with some ease, given the care with which Yongzheng had taken to setting it up. As a loyal son and grandson he worked to magnify his ancestor’s accomplishments through territorial and cultural expansion. He gained territories and further developed additional themes of art production to reinforce the contributions of Kangxi and Yongzheng to the Qing imperium. He used both text and image to document their grand largesse to the productivity of good government. In so doing, he worked to establish a Qing-identified canon of cultural production. This is exemplified in the further reproduction of the PTW and several printing projects. He printed Yongzheng’s poems and Kangxi’s agrarian essays in the monumental Si Ku Quan Shu (Complete Treasures of the Four Libraries). Qianlong complemented Yongzheng’s “Emperor personally pushing the plow” imagery with a series of paintings devoted to his wife portrayed in the ceremony of the “Empress personally attending to sericulture.” He added further majestic flourishes on the PTW, producing a set of his own in the now canonical European-Qing style with linear perspective. He also undertook a grand enterprise to reproduce the “miraculously” recovered Song versions of the genre, carved in massive granite stele displayed in the section of the Pictures of Tilling and Weaving in the Garden of Clear Ripples (presently known as the Summer Palace). Qianlong labored industriously to canonize the Pictures of Tilling and Weaving, both Song and earlier Qing versions in order to further consolidate cultural and political authority. Finally Chapter Four “Chinese farmers toiling at home and in Europe” brings the story up to the early 19th century. This chapter addresses the Jiaqing Emperor’s poems on the PTW that survive only as woodblock prints and as impressed in inksticks. Jiaqing did not embrace the PTW in the same grandiose manner as his father had. Jiaqing had inherited a depleted treasury’s funds and had to address internal conflict with in his territories and his family. While representations of the Chinese agrarian laborer did not enjoy enthusiastic imperial patronage at home by the early 19th century, they had experienced vigorous popularity in 18th- to early 19th-century Europe. This chapter explores the appeal of the Chinese farmer to European elites who in the mid 18th century sought to promote agriculture as the basis for prosperity. With increased knowledge of China, courtesy of the Jesuits and traders, Physiocrats regarded the Chinese farmer as the beneficiary of Confucian ideology that promoted a rational appreciation of the economy. With Confucius’s sagely vision, Quesnay argued China was a wealthy country that enjoyed great prosperity and its economic policies should be emulated. Representations of the Chinese agrarian laborers by Chinese image-makers were received in the courts of Europe in the forms of prints in agricultural book publications, as woodblock prints of the imperially commissioned PTW, as wallpapers, and as motifs on porcelain. European artists and engravers likewise produced imagery inspired by Chinese agrarian labor. As the importance of agriculture waned with the advance of the industrial revolution in Europe, by the mid-19th century, China was reconfigured as frozen in a primitive pre-industrial revolutionary state. Turning to consider the projects objectives, the manuscript is a lengthy articulation of point 1. Each individual chapter addresses goal 2. Chapter one especially and also chapters two and three discuss the motivations for the invocation of European formal qualities, objective 3. Chapters one and three investigate point 4. Objective 5 is discussed in chapter four and also revisited in the epilogue. Finally the appendices reproduce the suite of poems written by the four emperors. This includes two versions by Qianlong and the two different sets associated with Yongzheng.

744711.label: Major findings and research outcome
744711.value: The project’s research outcomes are presently in the form of numerous presentations at eight conferences as outlined in Part C. I have used the opportunities to present papers at conferences as a means to encourage me to refine my research findings and gather other scholars’ responses to them. In addition, I presented my research findings in a seminar at the University of Hong Kong’s Department of Fine Arts. I have given two public lectures, one of which was invited for publication in the Oriental Ceramics Society Bulletin. It is forthcoming. I presently have an article entitled “Kangxi’s Imperially Commissioned Pictures of Tilling and Weaving: Perspective and its roles in agrarian calendar imagery” under review with the Ming-Qing Studies journal. I have consulted with an acquisitions editor at a prestigious university press that is well known for publications on the history of Asian art. The editor is interested in publishing the book and has invited me to submit it, or at least one chapter, for review. I am working on bringing together reproductions of the images into chapter two in order to illustrate the research.

744711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
744711.value: My abstract “The Politics of picturing Chinese agrarian labor in China and in Europe during the long 18th century” has been accepted for the thirty-fourth World Congress of Art History, organized by the Comité International d’Histoire de l’Art (CIHA) in Beijing, China that will be held in September 2016. I will present research findings of chapter four in the panel on “The Other and the foreign: Contact, curiosity and creative exchange. My presentation will challenge static unqualified definitions of chinoiserie, suggesting that imagery of China could be decorative, but also actively functioned to promote enlightened governance, reforming unjust taxation and forced labor policies imposed on European farmers and weavers. A peer-reviewed compilation of papers from this panel will be published. The book-length manuscript will be published. I will submit chapter two for review in the month of June 2016. Should it not be deemed acceptable, I will revise and either resubmit or pursue alternative university presses.

744711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
744711.value: The Qing (1644-1911) Pictures of Tilling and Weaving are a suite of paintings that represents the stages of the cultivation of rice and the production of silk fabric. This painting was initiated in the Song dynasty (960-1279) and revitalized by patronage beginning with the Kangxi emperor and continued directly for the next three emperors. The new Qing versions displayed European formal qualities, namely linear perspective. It held great appeal to the Qing court as it engages with Zhou-era (traditional dating 1122-256 BCE, modern dating ca. 1100-256 BCE) ceremonial practices associated with agriculture and with classical theories of governance. The Qing Pictures of Tilling and Weaving, as imperial productions, served to testify to the cosmic approval for the virtuous emperor through bumper harvests and envision that society is prosperous. The virtue of the Qing emperors becomes sanctioned through the new Pictures of Tilling and Weaving. With the inclusion of linear perspective, the Qing imperium also heralded its great range of cosmopolitan knowledge and formulated a new, distinctive style of painting to affirm its identity. Finally these representations of farmers and weavers traveled to Europe to comment on the value of agrarian labor in the changing economies of 18th to 19th-century Europe.

744711.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
744711.value: Throughout the many conferences that I attended to present my research, I have located a number of scholars who are tackling related topics. I sent out a call of interest to some of these scholars for participating in a panel on the history of post 17th-century art and technology for the 14th International Conference on the History of Science in East Asia. I received great interest from my contacts. As a result I organised two panels with five presenters, including myself, in each session, all together bringing ten scholars together. One panel was entitled, "Ideology and Technology: Artistic visions constructing cultural identities and political authority" and the other was "Transfers of technology: Exchanging knowledge in visual and material culture." In addition, I greatly relished the opportunity to present my research at Academia Sinica and work with colleagues there. I also met with art historians at the Graduate Institute of Art History at National Taiwan Normal University, Taipei. We are planning to have future exchanges of research between NTNU and HKU in conferences, symposia or workshops.

744911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
744911.value: Encountering and meeting people who are different from us is one of the biggest social challenges of the 21st century. Whereas humans have lived for most of their history in small, closed, family-based groups, the global dimensions of society and economy mean that more people than ever must learn to interact with and trust others with whom they have little in common. One of the most salient factors that distinguish different people across the world is race. While the term “race” is problematic in the strictest technical sense, we use it in this proposal to refer to the self-identified groupings of people based on their appearance. Thus, many people will self-identify as “White”, “Black”, “Chinese”, etc. (for the purposes of this study we will ignore people who consider themselves biracial or mixed-race). Many studies of face perception have reported a finding known as the “own-race advantage” (or other-race effect, or own-race bias); people generally find it easier to recognize people of their own race than people of other races. This phenomenon is probably caused by a variety of factors, and in this proposal we aim to test a variety of them in order to gain more understanding. First, we investigate whether the own-race advantage is caused by similar mechanisms for all ethnic groups, or whether its causes vary. Specially, we test whether Asians and Caucasians show similar or different effects of holistic processing for own- and other-race faces, and whether such differences relate to memory differences for faces. Second, we test whether the own-race advantage is characterized by qualitative differences in processing for own-race and other-race faces, or whether processing differences are purely quantitative. Finally, we examine whether our tendency to naturally categorize individuals differently, depending on their social group status, affects perceptual processing of different faces. Here we will manipulate the social groups that faces appear to belong to, in order to investigate the perceptual processing of in-group and out-group faces. The current proposal will use behavioural experiments, including measures of eye-tracking, to uncover the basis for the own-race advantage. 與不同的人接觸和交流是我們在二十一世紀中最大的社交挑戰之一。以往，在人類歷史上，我們只以一個封閉的小家庭作為社交團體基礎；但現今經濟全球一體化的社會，我們再也不能像以往一樣固步自封，而是必需學懂如何與自己截然不同的人互動，從而建立互信的關係。其中一個最顯然易見的例子便是和不同種族的人交流。先不談 “種族” 一詞的深層意義，單從外表作區分，地球上的人便可分成：”白人”, “黑人”, “黃種人” 等… (暫且不談那些混血兒或混種人) 要與自己不同種族的人互動最先一步便是要辨識對方的臉孔。可是，許多研究指出人們辨識自己種族臉孔的能力顯著地比辨識其他種族臉孔的能力優勝；這就是同種臉孔優勢(或稱為異種族效應, 或同種專利)。本研究建議將透過不同的實驗，以及利用眼球追蹤儀器去剖析這現象，旨在探討導致同種臉孔優勢這現象的因素。首先，我們藉著探討黃種人和白種人對同種族及不同種族的臉孔整體性處理和臉孔記憶表現，從而研究在各種族團體中的同種臉孔優勢效應機制是否相同。然後，我們會研究同種臉孔優勢效應是因為臉孔五官組合不同，還是因為種族區分而出現。最後，我們會探究辨識不同臉孔的機制會否被我們與身俱來的區分不同社區團組能力而影響。我們建議透過隨機區分臉孔入不同社交組別，從而探究辨識與自己同組及不同組別的臉孔是否涉及不同的處理過程。

745211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
745211.value: This project builds on substantial work in progress, proposes further original research, and will culminate in a book-length project, the first of its kind, on anglophone Hong Kong literature in the twentieth century until the present. Informed by literary criticism, critical and cultural theory, and historical and archival research, the book aims to throw light on the uniqueness of anglophone Hong Kong literature. It will be divided into three sections, each focusing on literary productions around a crucial moment in Hong Kong’s history: 1911, 1949, 1997. This is an original approach to conceptualizing archival discoveries and reading positions. It will direct in-depth research and enable the coherent structuring of materials, to show how anglophone literature contributes to an understanding of Hong Kong culture. While the validity of this original approach needs to be demonstrated by more extensive archival, critical-theoretical research and the writing of the book, my studies so far show there are good reasons for choosing the three dates. First, many literary works were published around these dates, refer to them as historical framework, and represent how the political changes marked by these dates impact on Hong Kong people and society. Many works also use these dates as points of departure to longer-term visions about Hong Kong as community and culture. Second, anglophone literature is often perceived as the writing of expatriates, visitors, and transients. However, my research shows that much of this literature is actually very focused on relations between Hong Kong and China, and on Hong Kong as Chinese, and this focus is particularly intense around the three dates. At the same time, writing in English is, by definition, a non-Chinese move, and enables the finished text to circulate globally in extra-Chinese spaces. The texts often show how Chinese events and subjects engage with other cultures and ethnicities within and beyond Hong Kong. This cosmopolitan engagement takes on protean forms especially at the moments of tumultuous change inscribed in the three dates. Each section of the book project will contain 3-4 chapters that build on my published articles or are newly-written. I deploy perspectives opened up by postcolonial theories, diaspora and globalization studies to read better-known texts and recover archival and little-known material. This methodology ensures that theories of non-Hong Kong origin are appropriately localized, and local materials are presented in such a way as to show how they inflect widely-used literary and critical paradigms. 這項目建基於現存的研究成果, 以創新的思維整理結合, 深化發揮, 推展為一書本著述計劃。項目專題是二十至二十一世紀香港英語文學。 研究概念綜合近代文評、 文學文化理論、 歷史和檔案研究, 聚焦文本內容, 冀能特顯香港英語文學的獨特性及理解其對香港文化的貢獻。 研究將分三段進行, 各圍繞一個香港歷史的關鍵時刻, 即1911年，1949年和1997年。這計劃的原創性, 有待求證於更深入的檔案翻查和文本辯證, 但有理由相信其可行。 首先，許多文學作品圍繞這三個日期出版，以歷史事實為敘事的框架，探視當時的政局變化, 如何體現於民生社會, 同時反思香港在歷史洪流中的位置。又或以這些日期為出發點，以長遠深邃的願景, 想像香港社會和文化。第二，英語文學, 一般認為是居港外國人 、旅客、過客的作品。不過，我的研究顯示，大部分作品,其實是非常關注香港和中國的關係，以及香港的中國身份和思想領域。而這個重點, 在所選的三個動盪時刻, 尤為顯明。第三, 英語寫作，顧名思義，是「去中國化」的一種語言策略。 同時, 亦能讓文本流動於中國以外全球的空間, 促進香港的中國人和事與世界其牠族羣文化的交流分合。「世界性」與「中國性」在香港的建立與辯證, 在這三個年份的英語文學, 可見端倪, 但其獨特的表達方式和見解, 則有待詳細探討。 書本著述計劃分為3章, 每章有3-4卷, 內容會建立在我已發表的學術論文上, 或是從新書寫。過程中, 會參考後殖民理論、 散居和全球化研究等, 籍以開闢文本閱讀與評論視野, 亦會從事檔籍研究, 在整理存檔之時, 發掘鮮為人知的資料。這種方法, 望能保證非香港原產的理論得以適當的本地化，而本地的材料, 亦能為廣泛使用的文本閱讀和批評範式提供嶄新的體驗。

745511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
745511.value: Spirituality is often forsaken in psychiatric care with the preponderance of symptoms management under the current health care model leading to the negligence of this indispensible element of our holistic well-being. Yet, spirituality remains a salient issue for patients. Diagnosis and hospitalization disrupt their lives and cast negative identities whereby their experience of reality is invalidated as delusions, subsequently shaking their sense of self. Social exclusion threatens their connection with the world and for the religious, mental illness can affect their faith. Meanwhile, patients’ intrinsic spiritual resources can help them in various ways throughout rehabilitation, including coping skills, promoting coherence, and feeling supported. More intriguing are findings which suggest that psychiatric symptoms can be contained by calling upon one’s spirituality. Addressing spiritual issues in mental health research and treatment is hampered by inadequate understanding from the viewpoints of patients. With little research representing patients’ voices, especially from the Chinese population, we risk imposing our own understanding onto clients. What spirituality means to patients and the role it plays in the rehabilitation of mental illness remains unexplored terrains in both research and practice. The present study aims to expand understanding of this elusive construct among individuals rehabilitating from schizophrenia. This will be one of the first studies to integrate the perspectives of patients, mental health professionals and family members. The aims are to: (1)Understand what spirituality means to patients and (2)Explore the role of spirituality in rehabilitation Using a constructivist approach, the study will qualitatively interview 20 individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia. 20 mental health professionals, and 20 family members will also be interviewed to include the voices of those who play a role in the patients’ rehabilitation. Data saturation will determine the actual number of interviewees. Post-interview follow-up with participants will enable the provision of counseling support, if needed. Interviews will be transcribed verbatim and analyzed for emergent themes based on grounded theory. For the past decade, our research team has been advocating for an integrative body-mind-spirit health model as well as the conceptualization of spirituality in the cultural context. This study will be one of the first pieces of local research to systematically examine how spirituality affects or is affected by severe mental illness. This will help lay the foundation in promoting holistic health care models to psychiatric care locally and internationally. 研究撮要 雖然在全人健康的概念下，靈性是必不可缺的部分；但在當今醫療體系中，對精神分裂患者而然，處理病徵依然是首要的事，靈性往往是被忽略遺棄的一部分。不過，靈性在精神分裂患者中卻往往是非常特殊的。診斷和住院破壞了患者的正常生活，為他們扣上了負面的身份，而他們經驗的現實世界亦因為妄想而變得病態，從而動搖他們的對自我的感覺。社會排擠威脅患者與世界的連繫，而篤信宗教者，精神病多少影響著他們的信念。與此同時，患者內在的靈性經驗著實能夠幫助他們的康復，包括對應技巧、增進內在的連貫、及感受到支持。而更耐人尋味的是有研究指出於靈性上有依歸可以對精神病症狀有幫助。 有關靈性在精神病中的研究甚至介入治療一直因為對精神病人的看法而受到牽制及阻撓。而因為只有少數研究可以反映病人，尤其是中國藉或本土病人的聲音，我們常常會把自己對他們的理解硬套在他們身上。究竟靈性對他們來說有什麼意義？在精神病康復中扮演著什麼角色？這種種，在學術研究及實務上都仍是未有人觸及之地。 此研究旨在擴闊了解，康復中的精神分裂患者對靈性的獨立見解。是次研究將會首次融合來自精神分裂患者、他們的家人和精神科醫護人員的不同看法和解構。研究目的為: (1) 了解對精神分裂患者而言，靈性是什麼 (2) 探索在康復的過程中，靈性所扮演著的角色 通過建構性研究方法，我們會邀請20位精神分裂患者、20位病患者的家屬及20位精神科醫護人員進行質性訪談。確實的訪談人數以資料飽和為考量。如有需要的話，在訪談後，研究人員會提供相關的輔導支援。訪談過程會被錄音再逐字翻譯，透過植根理論的方法加以分析，再將類似內容歸類形成主題，最後衍生出主要概念架構。 過去十年，我們的研究小組致力於提倡身、心、靈全人健康概念，對靈性在本土文化中的概念化進行了很多工作。是次研究將會是本地首個研究，有系統地檢視靈性如何影響嚴重精神疾病或受其影響。研究結果將有助於本地或國際上在精神科護理中提倡全人健康關顧的理念。

745511.label: Realisation of objectives
745511.value: In our proposal, we proposed to recruit participants according to the grounded theory approach. Recruitment thus stopped when data saturation was achieved. Based on this principle, we successfully recruited 18 schizophrenic patients, 19 mental health professionals, and 11 family caregivers for in-depth individual interviews. All interview contents were transcribed verbatim. Since the data is very rich in content, within the limited time, we tried our best to look for the major outcomes. By integrating the perspectives from different parties, we found that the conceptualization of spirituality among people with schizophrenia can mainly be classified into 2 domains (personal domain and communal domain) with several components, which are equally important for patients’ recovery and their reintegration into the society (objectives/research question 1). Although all parties recognized that patients can benefit from engaging in most of the spiritual activities, discrepancies were found in the meaning and roles of spirituality in relation to patients’ illness experiences. One of them is that patients focused more on spiritual practices that help restore the inner peace and stabilize symptoms; while professionals and caregivers looked for meaning in life/existential quests. Some professionals mentioned about the possibility of the apparitional spiritual experiences in hindering the recovery in patients. The unresolved differences in understanding spirituality among patients and family caregivers might cause distress in patients and become an obstacle for relationship building (objectives/research questions 1 & 2). As a whole, we achieved all the objectives of demonstrating the meaning of spirituality for people with schizophrenia and its roles in the rehabilitation/ recovery process with multiple-perspectives by contrasting, comparing, and integrating the views of spirituality in schizophrenia among three parties. Finally, we have to admit that the nature of qualitative data is very complex and the integrative analysis is complicated. The data analysis process took longer time than we expected. Moreover, the research assistant who took care of this project departed for further study when the study approaching its end. This caused delay in final integration and writing up of the findings. Also, qualitative manuscript may require longer reviewing process for publication, thus we still have manuscripts under review when we are preparing this final report. We have been trying our best to resolve the difficulties we encountered for this project. We believe that our findings can go beyond the time limit of this project. We will continue to work on the data and try to develop a holistic care model which includes spiritual care in schizophrenic population.

Research question (1): From an integrated perspective of clients, professionals and family members, what is the meaning and core components of spirituality for people with schizophrenia in rehabilitation, in particular, for coping with the mental illness and reintegrating into society?
Research question (2): How does spirituality assist or hinder the rehabilitation process of schizophrenia?

745511.label: Major findings and research outcome
745511.value: Our findings suggest that spirituality was conceptualized as a human being immanent with personal and communal domains in people with schizophrenia. The personal domain includes a sense of self, peacefulness, philosophy of life, personal qualities, and personal growth; while the communal domain includes interpersonal relationships, religious practices/relations, and apparitional experiences. Most participants related the experience of connectedness to one’s richness of spirituality and holistic well-being (8.1, 8.2, 8.3, 8.6, 8.8, 9.1, 9.2, 9.5). Spirituality could also help make sense of the illness experience, shape help-seeking behaviors, strive for a sense of peace, cope with residual symptoms, and facilitate reintegration into society (8.1, 8.5, 8.8, 9.3, 9.5). On investigating the meaning and roles of spirituality in relation to illness experiences among patients and professionals, differences emerged. At the personal level, patients’ description was more factual, concrete, and affective (i.e. self-understanding, short-term goals, and peacefulness); while professionals’ description was more abstract, complex, and cognitive (i.e. self-esteem, meaning in life, and existential quests). At the communal level, two groups had similar understanding of spirituality but not its roles. Patients regarded spirituality as a platform of giving and receiving love and care; while professionals merely regarded it as a means for receiving support and symptom management (8.3, 8.6, 9.3). In a dyadic investigation of patients and family caregivers’ perspective, spirituality was understood differently and rarely discussed in most dyads. Caregivers generally assumed patients held the same perspective as they did; whereas patients were aware of the differences but pretended to hold the same perspective due to the fear of disrupting family harmony and losing family support. This created psychological distress in patients which impeded their recovery (8.2, 9.4). Findings also show that caregivers often engaged in struggles between preventing relapse (e.g. provide unconditional support for patients) and facilitating recovery (avoid over-indulgence), and battled personal beliefs about medication efficacy while advocating for dose reduction (8.7). Spirituality provided a psychological shelter for caregivers to rely on and became guidance for what role they should play during patients’ recovery (9.4). An integrative perspective of understanding spirituality and its role in illness recovery was constructed at the early stage of the study piloting the framework of data analysis (8.5, 9.1); and concluded as a discussion for developing holistic care in this population (8.4). Since spirituality plays different roles across the illness trajectory; a multiple-perspectives approach with special address to the culture and context is needed for future development of holistic care (8.4, 8.5).

745511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
745511.value: The meaning, components and roles of spirituality in illness recovery in people with schizophrenia had been examined with multiple-perspectives in this study. Future work can be conducted on developing and promoting mutual understanding of the needs and roles of spirituality in relation to patients’ illness recovery in all parties so as to minimize the discrepancies. Since spirituality relates closely to the context and culture, future investigations on patients of other races, cultures, and those who have been institutionalized for a long time also warrant conducting. Moreover, some participants emphasized that one’s experience of connectedness relates closely to the richness of spirituality and the holistic well-being; and may empower them to become helper besides care receiver. Intervention that helps enhance patients’ connectedness to oneself, others, and the universe can potentially be developed to enhance patients’ spirituality, holistic well-being, strength and ability. Further work can also include developing the sense of connectedness as one of the measuring parameters of spirituality. Finally, our findings reveal some limitations on cognitive and verbal articulation in people of schizophrenia; future research work should include exploration and development of alternative research methods and means of communication (i.e. art-based approach, non-verbal approach) when working with this population.

745511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
745511.value: Spirituality has long been ignored in psychiatric services probable due to the priority of symptom management as well as similarities between the nature of spiritual experience and the characteristics of psychotic symptoms. Yet, it is regarded as one of the core components of holistic health. A better understanding of the meaning and roles of spirituality in illness recovery in people with schizophrenia may help develop more appropriate holistic care for patients. This study demonstrates that spirituality is considered as an important component of human beings in people with schizophrenia from the perspectives of patients, healthcare professionals, as well as family caregivers. Unlike people who are functioning within normal limits, patients tend to associate spirituality to inner stability and peacefulness instead of meaning in life and existential quests. Experiences in spirituality can enable the patient to become helper rather than only be the care receiver. Although all parties acknowledge the beneficial effects of spirituality in different stages of recovery, discrepancies in understanding exist which may create distress in patients and hinder the provision of spiritual support in psychiatric services, thereby affecting patients’ recovery and reintegration into community. The findings provide insights for developing holistic care and future research for this population.

745711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
745711.value: In November 2010, Myanmar will hold its first elections in 20 years - and the first to generate a meaningful result in 50 years. By and large, these elections are dismissed as a sham, chiefly because the military leadership will retain extensive control of both the executive and the legislature. Nevertheless, there is something interesting in the elections that has not yet been widely picked up. Alongside national elections, there will also be provincial elections for 14 assemblies in 7 states and 7 regions. Indeed, citizens will cast three votes, one for a lower-house People's Assembly, a second for a territorially-based upper-house National Assembly, and a third for a provincial assembly. After 50 years of extremely centralized control, these elections will therefore mark quite an important institutional shift. The long-term consequences are likely to be substantial. This research project will focus on the National Assembly and the provincial assemblies to investigate three key issues. One is what can be learned about territorial politics as Myanmar starts slowly to reform its polity. This strand will mainly comprise an analysis of voting patterns, party representation and policy implications. The second strand is what might be learned from this experiment in territorial politics about the vexed issue of ethnicity and governance in Myanmar. The third is what the eveolving Myanmar case contributes to wider debates about ethnic relations in multiethnic states. I recognize that undertaking the research project will not be straightforward. While some basic data will be available in the public domain, much will need to be gathered on the ground inside Myanmar. While my grasp of the language extends only to basic conversation, and not to scientific research, this is something I intend to do myself through an individual research project. The research will draw on individual interviews conducted by me. I do not expect to be successful in accessing key provincial elites in all 14 states and regions. However, I am confident that my extensive contacts inside Myanmar will generate sufficient acess to make this a meaningful project based on solid primary data. Moreover, by drawing on my own earlier conceptual work, I am confident that I will be able to generate findings that are not only empirically rich, but also conceptually innovative. In this way I will make a substantial contribution to understandings of Myanmar as it undertakes a degree of political change, and also to wider conceptual debates. 2010年11月， 緬甸將舉行自1990年以來20年的第一次大選， 這也是50年來第一次有真正意義的大選。總的說來， 這次大選被預期為失敗的， 因為軍方還將持續其對行政機關與立法機關強有力的控制。 但是， 有關這次大選還有很多有趣的議題沒有被研究過。 與聯邦議會選舉同期，還有7省7邦的14個省（邦）議會的選舉。 實質上，選民手中有3票， 第一票選聯邦議會中的人民院議員， 第二票選民族院議員， 第三票選省（邦）議會議員。經過50年的中央集權治理， 這次大選將會為緬甸帶來制度層面的變革。長期影響將是巨大的。 此研究項目將會針對聯邦議會和省（邦）議會考察三方面議題。第一個議題是緬甸開始緩慢的變革她的政體， 這將對地域政治有何影響？這一議題將包括對選民投票行為，政黨代表性， 和政策影響三方面的研究。第二個議題是此次大選將會對緬甸的種族與治理這個原本就有爭議的議題帶來何種影響？第三個議題是考察緬甸的這個正在進行的個案將 會對多種族國家處理種族關係帶來何種思考和借鑒？ 我認識到承擔此一研究將不是簡單易做的。 一些基本的信息和數據可以在公共媒體獲得， 大部分的信息和數據只可以在緬甸實地考察獲得。 我對緬甸語言的掌握僅限於基礎交流， 還不能從事科學研究， 這方面我要盡快改善。此研究項目將主要基於深度訪談獲得的資料。 我預期到不可能聯絡到14個省（邦）的所有精英， 但我相信以我在緬甸內部廣泛的聯絡可以使此研究項目獲得足夠的第一手數據。 基於此前我發展的理論模型， 我相信此研究不僅會在實證意義上有所發現， 還將在理論上有所突破。 這樣此項目將會對緬甸政治變革研究作出實質性的貢獻。

745711.label: Realisation of objectives
745711.value: The project had seven major objectives (as stated in the original application). Objectives 2-5 were fully met. Objectives 1, 6 and 7 were only partially met for the following reasons: 1. This objective was roughly 80% met. I never did focus much on the National Assembly, finding rather that my fieldwork and analysis were skewed almost wholly to the 14 territorial assemblies and to ethnic politics more generally. I believe this is unproblematic for two reasons. One is that the National Assembly has been comparatively well analyzed (notably by Renaud Egreteau), whereas the territorial assemblies have drawn little academic attention beyond this project. The other is that ethnic politics is the most important issue facing contemporary Myanmar, and was therefore an appropriate focal point for the project (which, overall, took ethnicity and governance as its core topic). 6. This objective was roughly 50% met. In the end I did not spend enough time in-country to have the influence on domestic politics that I originally thought would be possible. That said, there was considerable dialogue between this project and key actors in the sphere of ethnic politics. 7. This objective was roughly 20% met. The research project remained focused throughout on a very dynamic political reform process inside Myanmar, and never really moved to a major comparative level. The articles in the Journal of Contemporary Asia and South East Asia Research did this to some extent, but I would not want to claim for them the wider impact that I originally laid down as a project objective. Overall, the project provided an important series of perspectives on ethnicity and governance in Myanmar in reform. The four indexed journal articles generated by the project looked successively at general reform progress with a discussion of the dimension of ethnicity (Asian Survey 2013), at the issue of transitional justice that is at the heart of many ethnic political claims (South East Asia Research 2014), at the citizenship crisis that is one of the most critical problems triggered by Myanmar's multi-ethnic composition (Journal of Contemporary Asia 2014), and at the emergence, establishment and initial functioning of regional and state assemblies (Asian Survey 2015).

745711.label: Major findings and research outcome
745711.value: The proposal for this project was submitted in October 2010, just ahead of Myanmar's managed November 2010 general election that led in March 2011 to a switch to quasi-civilian government and to a dynamic reform process that continues to unfold to this day. Five years ago, Myanmar's ruling State Peace and Development Council, a long-standing military junta, had published plans to form territorial assemblies and thereby launch a process that would evidently have a major impact on critical issues of ethnicity and governance. However, it was unclear precisely how the reforms would play out. The project was therefore cast in reasonably broad terms so that it could respond flexibly to changing circumstances inside the country. In the event, it has been able to generate four indexed journal articles that shed light on several key aspects of its central theme of ethnicity and governance. The brief article published in Asian Survey 2013 was scene-setting, in that it took the opportunity to look within the first full year of political reform at how issues of ethnicity and governance were faring. The much longer analysis published in South East Asia Research 2014 focused in detail on the agenda for transitional justice that is at the heart of many ethnic political claims. Highlighting six major options, it argued procedurally for local leadership supported by external engagement designed to ensure that basic global standards are met, and substantively for attention to be paid to tensions within transitional justice and across the wider reform process. The equally extensive analysis published in the Journal of Contemporary Asia 2014 examined the citizenship crisis that is one of the most critical problems triggered by Myanmar's multi-ethnic composition. To examine this crisis, it placed Myanmar in a comparative context, drawing notably on global experience with multiculturalism and enabling civic integration. It advanced a series of policy options focused on rights, duties and identity, and argued for domestic political leadership, backed by global political support, to address the crisis. The substantial article co-authored with two young Myanmar researchers and published in Asian Survey 2015 investigated the emergence, establishment and initial functioning of Myanmar's 14 regional and state assemblies. Discovering that these remain constrained political institutions that are not yet able to make much of an impact on the overarching problem of national reconciliation that faces Myanmar, it advanced realistic proposals for institutional reform.

746011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
746011.value: This proposal focuses on an important area of investigation for higher education in Hong Kong: the issue of the writing problems and challenges of novice and early stage researchers writing at the postgraduate level in their second language. Writing skills play a highly important role in determining research students’academic success, since this hinges on the quality of their thesis writing. However research has suggested that writing at this level is a complex and challenging skill, especially for second language writers. Supervisors also play an important role in mediating their students’ transition from writing as a novice to writing with an authoritative voice. The aim of this research is to investigate doctoral students’ major writing problems and the strategies that they develop to meet these challenges over a period of two years. The research also aims to investigate the role played in students’ writing development by their supervisors’ feedback. The study will adopt a longitudinal case study approach and track twelve first year doctoral students from a range of disciplines as they develop their skills as research writers in the first two years of their doctoral programme. Both students and their supervisors will be interviewed about their perceptions of the major writing problems students encounter. Students will be interviewed regularly over the two year period of the research to uncover the strategies they use to overcome their writing problems and improve their writing. In addition, an analysis of samples of each student’s writing will be carried out to triangulate the findings and also to provide a stimulus for discussion at interviews and students will be asked to keep a reflective e-journal. The findings from the interviews will be used to develop a questionnaire to be sent to all first year students currently enrolled at the graduate school at the University of Hong Kong. This will investigate the writing problems that students have across a wider range of disciplines and the strategies they use to deal with these problems. The overall aim of the research is to develop a better understanding of the writing challenges faced by doctoral students writing in their second language and the strategies used by them to deal with these problems. This will make a valuable contribution to our understanding of an important area for research in higher education contexts around the world and will enable supervisors and writing teachers to target their feedback and interventions more effectively. 摘要 这项研究旨在调查香港高等教育中的一个重要领域：研究生教育阶段中无经验及初级研究人员在运用第二语言写作时所面临的困难及挑战。写作技巧在研究型硕士生和博士生的学业成功上发挥着极其重要的作用。这是因为写作技巧决定了学生的论文质量，而论文质量的好坏直接关乎着他们学业水平的高低。然而，有研究表明，在研究生教育阶段，特别是对于用第二语言来写作的学习者来说，写作是一个复杂而富有挑战性的学习技能。学生在写作中会经历一个自我角色的转型—从初级研究者过渡到能发表一定权威性看法的研究者。在这一过程中，导师也发挥着重要的作用。这项为期两年的研究主要是探讨博士研究生在学术写作中遇到的困难以及他们为解决困难所采取的策略。这项研究还探讨了导师的反馈意见在学生的写作提高过程中所起的作用。 本研究采用纵向的个案研究方法，跟踪十二个来自不同专业方向的一年级博士研究生，探究他们在博士课程前两年写作技能提高和发展的轨迹。研究首先将通过访谈学生和导师的方式，挖掘学生们在写作中遇到的主要困难以及学生和老师对此的看法。在跨时两年的研究过程中，这些学生将定期接受访谈，以调查他们采用了何种策略来克服写作困难和提高写作水平。此外，研究还将结合每一个学生的书面写作样本进行分析。这样做一方面是遵循了三角研究法的原则，用写作样本来佐证访谈结果，另一方面也是为了利用写作样本来促进访谈效果。在此基础上，研究还要求学生们以电子日记的形式记录和反思自己的写作过程。研究还将进一步利用访谈结果，设计一个问卷调查。该问卷将发送到目前在香港大学研究生院的所有一年级在校学生手中，用以调查更多不同学科的学生所遇到的写作问题及所采取的措施。 该研究的总体目标是帮助我们更好地理解博士研究生在使用第二语言写作时所面临的主要困难以及他们所采取的应对策略。它对全球高等教育背景下，博士生导师和写作老师们如何更加有效的提供反馈意见和进行教学指导有重大的贡献和深远的意义。

746011.label: Realisation of objectives
746011.value: The research has revealed very interesting findings on the problems students face and the strategies they use and highlighted the important role of online resources and collaboration in terms of strategies for overcoming problems. The comparison of students according to year of study shows that students’ challenges changed over time and moved from language and academic writing concerns to wider concerns related to finding appropriate sources of feedback which would challenge and improve their work and making their writing convincing and interesting. The supervisors' data also points to great variability in their conception and enactment of their supervisory roles, due to individual, cultural and disciplinary differences. I have used my participation in conferences and international venues to promote the implications of this for teachers and supervisors. Students need to their supervisors to help them learn how to use articles and theses as language resources, since this gives them a resource they can use throughout their thesis writing and one which they can use to focus on different aspects, at the point of need. In addition supervisors and writing teachers should be aware of the importance of social and academic networking for students. In order to help students become autonomous writers, it is important for writing teachers focus more on helping students to manage all the linguistic, academic and social resources available to them in our networked and connected society, where sources of feedback are not limited to writing teachers and supervisors – instead the internet and social media offer great potential for students to connect and network with others on their writing and have great potential for assisting postgraduate students with their ongoing writing development and their research Problems and overcoming them One difficulty was with objective 3. I feel I failed to consider what success entailed when designing the project. Rather than students being successful or unsuccessful, they experienced issues which they overcame to become successful and used a variety of strategies to do this. In fact all students were successful in completing their theses, except one. Unfortunately she rejected my invitation for an interview to discuss her withdrawal from her programme of study and due to the sensitivity of the issue I was unable to fully investigate her case with her supervisor. I feel this objective needed to reconsidered as it was difficult to investigate this area. .

746011.label: Major findings and research outcome
746011.value: The findings show that major writing challenges related to linguistic, cultural, institutional and disciplinary issues. Students had problems expressing complex ideas and difficulties in developing a confident and authoritative academic voice. . A range of self- initiated strategies students developed to deal with their writing challenges were identified from the questionnaire and student interview data. The most widely reported were using academic articles and relevant theses as writing ‘models’, and the use of peer support networks for providing support, advice and feedback on writing. The data from the open-ended questions in the questionnaire and the case study participant interviews and analysis of the students’ work suggest a very wide use of the strategy of appropriation – this was both a self- initiated strategy and also one that students learnt from other students and their supervisors. These strategies could be seen as legitimate textual borrowing or transgressive textual borrowing, but the data suggests that these are generally productive learning strategies which enable students to develop their writing skills. The cases show that students’ focus when using these texts as models is not static, but dynamic and changes as students’ writing skills and knowledge of the research area evolve. The case studies also demonstrated the crucial role of social and academic networking as a way of developing critical writing skills and one’s academic voice and persona- moving from the periphery to a less marginal role in the academic community. Sources of feedback on doctorial writing were not limited to writing teachers and supervisors and included relationships made via academic connections and social media. These resources allowed students to make international connections with academics and peers in the same area, which in some cases lead to led to international collaboration and learning. I have given a three papers on the findings at international conferences and also I have given papers as part of a collaborative visit to the universities of Stockholm and Gothenburg in Sweden on my findings and I was invited to give a seminar by the Hong Kong Association for Applied linguistics which focused on this research. I have submitted a draft article to the Australian review of Applied Linguistics for their special issue on Postgraduate writing. This was by invitation and is currently being peer reviewed

746011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
746011.value: I have plans to write a further article from the research focusing on the feedback given by supervisors, since I found that there were great differences in the ways supervisors gave feedback and the ways they saw their role. As I am now retired I hope to have more time to do this.

746011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
746011.value: This research involves a study investigating ESL postgraduate students’ writing problems and the strategies they developed to meet these challenges. Nine postgraduate students were interviewed four times over a two year period and a questionnaire was sent to over 150 postgraduate students to investigate their major writing challenges and their self-initiated strategies. The findings suggested that students’ writing challenges related to linguistic, cultural, institutional and disciplinary issues. Main areas of concern were identified including difficulties with expressing complex ideas in a second language and difficulties with developing confidence and a convincing academic style. The research examines the strategies students developed to deal with their writing challenges and how these evolved. Strategies used consistently and successfully included using expert writing such as academic articles as writing ‘models’ and the use of peer support networks which provided advice and feedback on the students’ writing and also offered opportunities for academic collaboration. The study highlights the importance of teaching students how to use articles and theses as legitimate language resources, rather than plagiarizing them . It also highlights the role that online resources and interaction can play in terms of feedback and peer support.

746111.label: Project Objectives
746111.value: To validate and culturally adapt the Chinese Early Development Instrument (CEDI) which would serve as a useful tool for population and community study of school readiness in Chinese children. To study differences in the school readiness of Chinese preschool children studying in low income and high income districts in Hong Kong.
rows: To validate and culturally adapt the Chinese Early Development Instrument (CEDI) which would serve as a useful tool for population and community study of school readiness in Chinese children.
To study differences in the school readiness of Chinese preschool children studying in low income and high income districts in Hong Kong.

746111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
746111.value: The proposed research is the first study to test the hypothesis that preschool children in underprivileged area have lower school readiness than children in wealthy area in Hong Kong. Cross-national studies of achievement in children have documented the existence of wide and persistent gaps in the academic attainment of students from low and high socioeconomic status (SES) families all over the world. By the time children enter school there is already an achievement gap between children from low and high SES backgrounds. Such findings have led to early intervention programs, such as “Head Start”, to reduce disparities in school readiness and achievement. Against this background, the proposed study considers the relationship between socioeconomic circumstance and children’s school readiness and holistic development. Five-year-old (K3/upper kindergarten) children and their teachers from 12 randomly selected preschools in one low-SES district and 12 randomly selected preschools in one high-SES district in Hong Kong will be recruited. There are on average 15 children in each class and teachers will be asked to rate each child using the Early Development Instrument (EDI) adapted for the Chinese. The EDI is a widely used population-based measure of school readiness and holistic development. It has been applied to estimate and monitor children's healthy development at school entry in Canada, across Australia and on a smaller scale in many other countries. The Chinese version of the EDI (CEDI) will provide information about children’s school readiness, including the physical health, social competence, emotional maturity, cognitive development, communication skills and general knowledge. We will compare the CEDI domain and subdomain scores of children from high/low SES preschools. The effects of teacher’s qualification, family income and parental educational level as potential confounders would be adjusted in the analysis. The data generated from this study will enable us to examine whether underprivileged children are less ready for school and more vulnerable on each developmental domain of EDI than their wealthier counterpart. Given the importance of evidence-based policy, these findings maywould point to the need for further high-quality intervention study to ascertain the best programme and most appropriate policy to close the gap.

746111.label: Realisation of objectives
746111.value: Both objectives of this study have been fully achieved: Objective 1) Chinese Early Development Instrument (CEDI) has been successfully validated in this study which carefully examined the construct validity, internal consistency, concurrent validity and reliability of Chinese version of Early Child Instrument (CEDI). The evidence gathered in this study suggests that CEDI is a valid, reliable and psychometric sound measure for early child development and school readiness for Chinese population. Objective 2) The study successfully recruited 567 kindergarten children from 21 kindergartens located in two districts with dramatically different socioeconomic characteristics in Hong Kong, Yuen Long (YL) and Hong Kong Island (HKI). There were significant gradient relationship between school readiness of preschool children and family socioeconomic status,on average, one unit increment in socioeconomic status (one standard deviation) would increase the total CEDI scores by 0.69. The evidence provided support to the inequalities within kindergarten classes associated with family SES. In addition, a significant proportion of the socioeconomic gradients could be partially accounted by mediators from both family processes and kindergarten intellectual and material resources. The socioeconomic gradients in children developmental outcome could be partially attributable to family processes and kindergarten features/resources. The parent-child interactions with arts and sports activities, as well as parental control of digital device were both confirmed to be significant mediators at family level. Kindergarten charged annual school fees, teachers’ qualifications, and working experiences, together of which were deemed to describe kindergarten SES. All of these factors were found to be significant mediator at kindergarten level.
