746111.label: Major findings and research outcome
746111.value: This is the first ever study to validate and culturally adapt the Chinese Early Development Instrument(CEDI) which served as a useful tool in study school readiness of Chinese children. Our study found that there were significant gradient relationship between school readiness of preschool children and family socioeconomic status. On average, one unit increment in socioeconomic status (one standard deviation) would increase the total CEDI scores by 0.69. The evidence provided support to the inequalities within kindergarten classes associated with family SES. A significant proportion of the socioeconomic gradients could be partially accounted by mediators from both family processes and kindergarten intellectual and material resources. Evidence based on this main study data supported the existence of socioeconomic gradients, contextual effect of kindergarten, and mediating effects from individual and kindergarten levels. In futher investigation on possible mechanisms leading to difference in school readiness between underprivileged and affluent districts, this study identified the role of teacher's teaching experience, academic relevance and educational background (school factors), and parent-child interactive activities on arts and sports, management on children's digital use at home (family factors) as mediators accounting for the translation of socioeconomic gradients into difference in school readiness. Scientific manuscripts in our important findings and effectivness of CEDI have been published in peer-reviewed journals in 2013 (BMC Pediatrics 2013, 13:146 ; Child Indicators Research 2013, 6, 115-135). Meanwhile, key findings have been presented to academics, professionals and policy-makers in both international and local scientific meetings (14th Asia Pacific Congress of Pediatrics, 8-12 Sep 2012; Symposium on Childhood Poverty –Socioeconomic status and Early Child Development, Annual Scientific Meeting of Early Childhood Development Research Foundation, 11 Nov 2013. At the same time, principal investigator of this study has been successfully granted with another RGC GRF1 grant (started in 2014) to study the later life academic acheivements and psychosocial well-beings of this cohort in order to test whether formal education and family environment would narrow or further widen this gap.

746111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
746111.value: CEDI proves to be a valid tool which provides an exciting possibility to put the Chinese children's development on an international scale for comparsion. The new tool would be very useful in measuring holistic development of children from different communities and backgrounds and in evaluation of outcomes of early childhood development interventions. The finding of marked socioeconomic gradient in early child development and school readiness raised the need of further study to investigate the outcome of this cohort of children to understand whether formal education and family environment could narrow or widen this gap in their subsequent life. Indeed, PI of this study has been successfully granted with another RGC GRF grant to conduct a follow-up study of this CEDI cohort. This study also identified the role of teacher's teaching experience, academic relevance and educational background (school factors), and parent-child interactive activities on arts and sports, management on children's digital use at home (family factors) as mediators accounting for the translation of socioeconomic gradients into difference in school readiness. These inportant findings opened the window for intervention by modifying these modifiable environmental factors at the school and family level.

746111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
746111.value: Chinese Early Development Instrument is successfully validated and culturally adapted in this study. This new tool serves to be a useful tool in Hong Kong and Chinese communities to measure the hoslistic development of preschool children, and allows scientific monitoring of school readiness of children from different communities. In addition, it is also a useful too to evaluate successfulness of early childhood interventions. Our study found a significant gradient relationship between school readiness of preschool children and family socioeconomic status. It is the first study of such in Hong Kong to document the existence of socioeconomic gradients in early child development and provides the evidence on how socioeconomic disparities could be translated into developmental disparities through potential mediators. The identification of important mediators include kindergarten’s socioeconomic status and family processes provide an exciting opportunity for policy makers to break intergenerational poverty by targeting these important and modifiable mediating factors identified at the school and family level. The key research finding points out that government needs to implement long term policy in reducing socioeconomic inequalities in families with young children, especially in the most disadvantaged population in order to improve the developmental outcome of Hong Kong children.

746711.label: Realisation of objectives
746711.value: As stated in the first three research objectives, the primary goal of the project was to identify the exchange between music theory and psychology and establish the conjunction between the two spheres of natural and human sciences in the context of the turn-of-the-20th-century music theory. I identified the relationship between music theories proposed by Riemann, Helmholtz, and Kurth and the works by the early psychologists/scientists such as Wundt, Fechner, Herbart, Marey, and Stetson. The project further aimed to investigate the relationship between different traditions of music theory, i. e., speculative and practical traditions. With the help of the senior research assistant, I have identified also the pedagogical traditions (e.g., Clark, Ortmann, Truslit, and Sievers), which were heavily influenced by contemporaneous psychology and science, and examined them in light of the early-20th-century “energeticist” theoretical tradition (e.g., Kurth, Halm, Schenker). I also attempted to extend the significance of such historical investigation to the contemporary scene of the interdisciplinary relationship between music theory and psychology, which is lively now more than ever. The linkage from the works by early music psychologists to the current studies by Cone, Rink, and Godoy is addressed in my works published and presented at the journal/conference, which are mostly devoted to the current empirical studies in music psychology (e.g., Psychology of Music, International Conference on Music Perception and Cognition 13). Overall, all five research objectives are addressed. Nonetheless, the last two objectives, that is, the interrelationship between different music-theoretical traditions and the implication to the current scene of music psychology can be tackled more extensively and explicitly. This is what I plan to achieve when developing these research outcomes into the monograph.

746711.label: Major findings and research outcome
746711.value: The present research project aimed to investigate the conceptual foundation for the interrelationship between music theory and psychology in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The rise of the scientific psychology influenced music theory not only in terms of the empirical approach but also in terms of the conceptualization of musical mind as the subject of listening. I investigated the contemporaneous writings in psychology, music theory, music analyses, aesthetics, and the score editions to address the above issues. In the first half of the research period, I focused on investigating and identifying the exchange of ideas between various disciplines. In the second half, I concentrated on relating the speculative and philosophical tradition of music theory to the practical regulating traditions of music theory for performers. Some research outcomes were published in peer-reviewed journals or as a book chapter; some others, presented at international conferences both in musicology/music theory and psychology of music. 1. Papers published in peer review journals: -“Boundaries and Thresholds: Conceptual Models of the Musical Mind in the History of Music Psychology.” Psychology of Music 42/5, (2014): 671-91. -“‘The Voice in Silence’: Hugo Riemann’s Pausenlehre and Its Psychological Implications.” Journal of Musicological Research 32/4, (2013): 287–313. 2. Invited Chapter: - “Music in the Ear’s Mind.” In Music Perception and Cognition II, 5–58. Seoul: Eumaksekye, 2013. ISBN: 978-89-6685-059-4 3. Invited Talks: The two invited presentations in 2013 at the research colloquium series of Chinese University of Hong Kong and National Taiwan University are also based on the present research project. 4. Presentation at International Conferences: “‘The will sets in activity the nervous fibers, like the keys of a piano’ Music and force in early music psychological discourse.” The 3rd Conference of IMSEA. December 2015. “‘In Search of Lost Time’: Connections between Theories of Hearing and Performance Discourse.” The 13th International Conference on Music Perception and Cognition. August 2014. “‘Minding Gaps’: Theorizing Bodily and Musical Motions in the Early 20th Century.” The 2nd Conference of IMSEA. October 2013. “(De)Constructing the Disciplinary Identity of Music Theory: The Case of Theories of Rhythm at the Turn of the Twentieth Century.” The 19th Congress of the International Musicological Society. July 2012. Currently, I am piecing together all these research outcomes in the form of a monograph. The book proposal and sample chapters were sent to and are currently under review by a leading publisher in UK.

746711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
746711.value: The historical and analytical observations presented at different occasions are currently reorganized into the forms of book chapters. The connection between different sections will be tightened to produce a coherent narrative to form a monograph. During the course of the present research project, the theme of “origin of music” emerged as a potential area to illustrate the interdisciplinary relationship between music theory and psychology. As cases for this, I plan to focus on the issues of speech melody and continuity and further investigate on the theme in future. This part, hopefully, will constitute a chapter in the proposed monograph.

746711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
746711.value: The present research project investigated the conceptual foundations of the interdisciplinary relationship between music theory and psychology in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Psychology as the new “scientific” discipline not only substantiated contemporary music theory by providing empirical support but also, and more importantly, exerted significant influence on the construction of the musical mind. In addition to such conceptual as well as methodological dimension of interdisciplinarity between music theory and psychology, the present project also looked the juncture between speculative and practical music theories, which have been discussed independently in preceding literature. The research outcome constitutes a part of the history of musical listening. The significance of the project is not a mere exploration of the past, however. Through conceptual investigation and historical analysis, the current relationship between music theory and psychology, which is stronger than ever, is reflected upon. In doing so, the project brought historical reflections on music psychology more immediately relevant to the present.

747111.label: Project Title(Chinese)
747111.value: 理解中国新兴的慈善文化

747111.label: Project Objectives
747111.value: The objectives to be addressed in the study are: To investigate the emergence of an individualized philanthropic culture by studying individual philanthropists and their contributions and participation in education, welfare, health, poverty alleviation and others. We will investigate the moral discourses of the individual philanthropists in the development of philanthropy in China. To study the dialectic relationship (a) between the state (local, regional and central government) and the individual philanthropists and their foundations; and (b) the interaction between the philanthropists and the NGOs and the local communities that they work with. Specifically, this project will look into the legal and regulatory framework governing philanthropic contributions and activities as well as the various sets of social networks that facilitated such a development. It will also examine the tensions and conflicts arising out of these relationships. To study the development of social entrepreneurship and corporate social responsibility embedded in the philanthropic culture. This study will investigate how individual philanthropists influenced their own business corporations to adopt corporate social responsibility and social entrepreneurship as key goals as well as how they influenced other individuals to adopt philanthropy as their mission.

747111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
747111.value: In September 2010, Bill Gates and Warren Buffet, as leaders of Global Philanthropy, hosted a dinner banquet for the wealthy mainland Chinese tycoons but their invitation was met with unenthusiastic response. The media reported that many wealthy entrepreneurs declined this invitation as they were unwilling to part half of their fortune to philanthropy. While the media focus on this event, a more sobering scenario is the rapid and expanding philanthropic response by many known and unknown Chinese to the natural calamities (flooding and earthquakes), poverty, education and health problems that plighted China. The 2009 Hurun Philanthropy List showed a list of 100 top mainland philanthropists with total donations of 15.7 billion RMB since 2004. There are also many others who contributed money and efforts into philanthropic projects. These individual philanthropists are entrepreneurs who have made their wealth since the open door policy and have ploughed their wealth back into the community. Their donations have been used in the promotion of education, health care, disaster relief, poverty alleviation, social wealth, culture and sports. Their philanthropic works have gained the attention of the State, the NGOs and the local communities that have benefitted from such acts of benevolence. Despite this emerging philanthropic culture, criticisms were levied on the poor delivery of philanthropic aids because of the lack of strategic planning and rational approach to philanthropy and a lack of a legal and regulatory/tax incentive framework that impeded the development of the philanthropic culture. Hence, there are calls for a better legal framework to promote this emerging philanthropic culture. Cynics have also questioned the motivations of these philanthropic acts. There are two types of philanthropy: institutionalized philanthropy in the form of modern day foundations and benevolent societies; and individualized philanthropy where individuals performed the acts of charity. The proposed project aims to investigate individualized philanthropy, focusing on the following aspects of the emerging individualized philanthropic culture of a rising China: 1) Profile the philanthropists (who are these philanthropists, their background, their wealth and their motivations to become philanthropist) 2) To investigate the interaction between the philanthropists, the State, the NGOs and the local communities that they work with 3) To study the legal and regulatory framework for the development of philanthropy and emergence of social entrepreneurship and corporate social responsibility.

747111.label: Realisation of objectives
747111.value: ACHIEVEMENT OF OBJECTIVES: 1) Research have targeted the various groups of people who are essential to understand and realise the above 3 objectives. To this end, this research have been able to interview the relevant people (various types of philanthropists) and organisations (GONGOS and NGOs) and governmental organisations. 2) We have been able to obtain primary data from the various government and non-governmental organisations 3) We have been able to interview the relevant people that will shed light on the workings of a philanthropic culture 4) We have been able to investigate the various philanthropic and humanitarian projects and talk to the relevant beneficiaries of the projects 5) PI has also made trips to areas affected by the earthquake to understand how humanitarian works were carried out and the difficulties faced. PI has been able to witness first hand the works of the GONGO/NGO members and able to interview these members. 6) We have also been able to go into the interior to understand various Hope School projects and interact with the school children and the school teachers to understand how such projects provided education for the rural children. PROBLEMS 1) The study of philanthropy has led to visits and research in disaster zones. Security and risks in conducting fieldwork in disaster zones has to be taken into consideration in greater measures, otherwise, personal safety and safety of RA could be compromised.

747111.label: Major findings and research outcome
747111.value: MAJOR FINDINGS in relation to the objectives 1) The research has uncovered that there is a rising group of philanthropists in China. Many of them are in businesses and have become actively involved in philanthropic works through their active participation in the NGOs that they have come to identify and support. 2) Individual businesses have also embarked on CSR and that the business leaders who are philanthropists themselves have encouraged their staff to participate in this 3) There is an emergence of large number of big and small NGOs who have tapped into the rising philanthropic movement and are becoming involved in various social and humanitarian projects 4) This has resulted in the expanding of civil society in China where individuals now are also becoming involved in philanthropic work through voluntary participation POLICY IMPLICATIONS: 1)These major findings have great implications for governmental policy in relation to the various types of social, welfare, educational and humanitarians projects implemented/supported by the philanthropic organisations/foundations, NGOs and the individual volunteers 2) Chinese government has now implemented a comprehensive framework in dealing with philanthropic activities 3) Chinese government has also established policies and regulatory controls to ensure accountability, good practice and protection for the vulnerable in order to stamp out abuse 4) Some Provincial governments have also established framework to facilitate and popularise charity and encourage the development of the idea of "charity city" RESEARCH OUTCOME 1) One journal paper by PI in a special journal issue co-edited by PI 2) One chapter by PI in an edited book co-edited by PI 3) 4 international conference presentations 4) One sole author book (in preparation and forthcoming)

747111.value: There is great potential to further develop this research within China and on comparative basis with other Asian countries. Another focus could be on micro philanthropy, bulking the trend of individual philanthropists with great wealth, but concentrating on small players with lesser wealth or little wealth but are extremely active in social and humanitarian activities. This research could be tied to the understanding of the social and moral values of the community as well as the notion of social justice in modernity.

747111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
747111.value: NATURE - The nature of this research is to understand what motivate individuals in community to contribute and participate in philanthropic and humanitarian projects. Specifically, this research concerns the Chinese in mainland China and how the Chinese government plays a crucial role to encourage this. Mainland Chinese government established polices and a regulatory framework to facilitate the acts of philanthropy and to encourage the development of GONGOs and NGOs. At the same time, it encourages individual moral responsibility to the larger community by upholding the "Lei Feng spirit". In this sense, it has been successful in encouraging the development of a philanthropic culture in China. SIGNIFICANCE - This knowledge help us to understand the social moral fabric of modern China and enable comparative studies with other communities. VALUE - For China - philanthropy helps to fill the moral vacuum created as China embarked on rapid economic development after the Open Door Policy. Outside China - Through the various GONGOs, China has used philanthropic diplomacy to counteract its negative image and especially the criticism of economic colonialism in Africa. This is done through Project Hope and the construction of Hope Schools in various African countries.

748611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
748611.value: The exponential growth of electronic resources, while opening a new era of intertextual freedom, has exacerbated educators’ concern over the issue of plagiarism. To analyze how students write from sources and how this bears upon the issue of plagiarism, universities in Hong Kong and Mainland China are well-positioned research sites. In Hong Kong, students enter English-dominant universities with varying degrees of preparation for writing from sources as a result of their different educational backgrounds. Yet irrespective of their backgrounds, they are immediately presented with strict university plagiarism policies reinforced by the use of detection software. In Mainland China, a folklore of intertextual casualness is increasingly giving way to codes of ethical conduct and hence a growing awareness of the issue of plagiarism in the academy. Much like the extensive use of Turnitin.com in Hong Kong universities, Degree Thesis Academic Misconduct Detection System is a state-of-the-art development in Mainland Chinese universities. By operating in the overarching theoretical framework of the social practice view of literacy and by conducting a series of case studies, the proposed project aims to answer this overall question: how do students of varied disciplines and years of study engage in intertextual activities, and what are lecturer-student interactions on writing from sources like? Specifically, this project aims to find out: • how Mainland postgraduate students in humanities and social sciences use source texts in writing degree theses that will be checked by anti-plagiarism software • how linguistic plagiarism in doctoral science students’ initial draft of English papers is eliminated by their supervisor as he shapes students’ texts for international publication • how Hong Kong First-Year Semester 1 undergraduates understand plagiarism and use sources in writing assignments • how these undergraduates’ understanding of plagiarism and practices of writing from sources may change over time; and • how disciplinary professors address novices’ transgressive intertextual practices through face-to-face interactions Lack of research on the issue of plagiarism at the tertiary level in Hong Kong and Mainland China has been made all the more conspicuous by the policy-level actions addressing the problem of plagiarism as noted above. The contemporary technological transformation of the intertextual landscape of academia has made such research urgent, given its potentiality to raise and address various issues of imminent concern in higher education at both sites. 電子資源的飛速增長帶來了文獻參考的便捷，同時也增加了教育者們對抄襲問題的憂慮。我們有必要研究學生們如何利用文獻進行學術寫作，其過程又如何涉及到避免抄襲的問題。對於這樣一項課題，香港與中國大陸的大學則是理想的研究地點。在香港，由於教育背景的差異，學生們在進入英語主導的大學時，他們所具備的利用文獻進行寫作的能力也各有差異；但是無一例外地，他們將面臨嚴格的反抄襲條例和抄襲檢測軟件的監督。而與此同時，在中國大陸，文本借用的隨意性傳統也越來越被學術道德條款所替代，反抄襲的意識在大學日益強烈。香港的大學用Turnitin.com作反抄襲軟件，中國大陸的大學則有學位論文學術不端檢測系統。 本課題以讀寫是一種社會行為作為理論視角，通過一系列的個案研究，來回答以下問題：不同學科背景、不同年級的大學生如何利用文獻進行學術寫作？老師和學生之間就利用文獻進行寫作這一問題的交流是怎樣的？具體地說，本課題的研究目標即是為以下幾個方面尋求答案： － 中國大陸的人文和社會科學的研究生怎樣寫（在正式提交之前需要被反抄襲軟件檢測的）畢業論文； － 導師如何處理理科博士生的英文論文初稿中的文本抄襲； － 在香港，一年級的大學新生如何理解抄襲，如何理解文獻的使用與引用； － 這些大學生對於抄襲和文獻利用的理解如何隨著時間的推移而可能發生改變； － 學科的老師如何通過與學生面對面的交流探討合理規範地使用文獻進行學術寫作。 在香港和中國大陸，在大學層面對抄襲問題進行研究仍然是一項空白。而上文所描述的政策方面的措施使得這一空白愈加明顯。現今的網路技術為學術世界帶來的變革，使得這樣一項研究變得緊迫，因為它能夠發掘並促進對香港和中國大陸兩地高等教育中的各種緊要議題的探討。

748611.label: Major findings and research outcome
748611.value: My research demonstrated that the literate activities of university students and academics alike are fundamentally tool-mediated strategic activities. The study also showed that experienced members of disciplinary communities, be it course teachers, research supervisors, or gatekeepers (editors and reviewers) of target scholarly journals importantly mediate novices’ socialization into the target communities of practice. In addition, for both students and scientific researchers digital literacy practices are prominent in their processes of source-searching, reading, note-taking and writing. Yet it is revealed that novices and expert writers contrast starkly in their source-use capability, in that while novices’ texts may be characterized by plagiarism, experts are able to achieve recontextualization of sources as they construct new rhetorical contexts in meaning making.

748611.value: Further development of the research: -to further study the writing from sources practices of expert writers (productive academics) across the disciplines, to generate theoretical and pedagogical insights -to take a historical perspective upon the issue of plagiarism in Chinese-speaking contexts, to refine the culture-oriented debates found in the research literature on plagiarism Proposed course of action: -to continue to incorporate insights drawn from the research into teaching and sharing with colleagues (as the PI has been doing) -to carry on the research along the line and the dissemination of findings in the professional community through seminars, presentations and publications

748611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
748611.value: Writing from source texts is very important part of university students' life as a majority of their writing in the university is based on reading. In this GRF project, I researched a variety of scenarios of source-based academic writing: students across disciplines writing using web sources, students' activity of fulfilling a particular assignment in one discipline, first-year university students negotiating the concept of plagiarism and the role played by their lecturers, a scientist supervisor eliminating plagiarism in novice texts in their joint effort of getting published in international journals, academics' and supervisors' views on plagiarism and their related teaching practices, and an expert writer's 'recontextualization' strategies in writing review articles. The research reveals that novices make studious efforts in learning to write from sources, enlisting previous knowledge, support from teachers and peers, and learning from published texts. Teachers play a pivotal role in the students' progress on their path of endeavours. Yet there are missed opportunities of teaching and learning and this can happen in particular when the final result (e.g., good grades or publications), rather than the learning process of novices, is prioritized.

748711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
748711.value: This project focuses on the history and structure of English as used in contemporary Asian societies. In postcolonial, multilingual Asian contexts, varieties of English have developed that show peculiar characteristics; these varieties are referred to in general as New Englishes and, in the specific context of Asia, as Asian Englishes. This project relies on two complementary investigative thrusts: (i) a consideration of sociohistorical aspects, in particular demography and language policies during different eras, from the (pre-)colonial period through post-independence and into the new millennium; and (ii) a close examination of the linguistic features of the (local) languages that have come into contact with English as it has evolved. These factors together are considered as comprising the ‘ecology’ of the linguistic situation, within the ecology paradigm which applies the metaphor from population genetics and biology to linguistics. This project will use as case studies the following Asian Englishes: Singapore English (SgE), Hong Kong English (HKE), Sri Lankan English (SLE). The project will seek to demonstrate that the linguistic features of a variety of English can only be understood appropriately and in their entirety when the sociohistorical aspects are appreciated, and that such features can only be fully appreciated with an understanding of the grammar of the local languages that English comes into contact with. Further, the project aims to foreground the fact that new varieties of English, in particular those that evolve in multilingual contexts involving languages from different language families, naturally and inevitably change in ways quite distinct from ‘traditional’ ‘native’ varieties of English, and that this cannot be viewed as deviant or even different, but completely expected, given our growing understanding of the role of transfer in contact situations and/or second language use. A recognition and acknowledgement of the legitimacy of such varieties of English holds significant social implications for language attitudes, language planning and policy making, and language policy in education in multilingual contexts. Further, with an explicit recognition that other, non-linguistic factors in the external ecology, such as demography and language policies, play a significant role in manipulating the languages that are dominant in a context and which thus influence the evolving English variety, governing parties and educational institutions should then be mindful of the effects of factors such as immigration policies on the English language.

748711.label: Realisation of objectives
748711.value: (a) Focus. See Midterm report for problems in engaging the PhD student. Consequently, focus shifted to investigating English in China as one of the main locales, in addition to Singapore and Hong Kong, with Sri Lanka becoming a less major part of the project. This was a positive revisions: China, comprising the largest group of English learners and users in the world today, is a very significant site in Asia to investigate the evolution of Asian Englishes. The overarching objectives of the project remained unchanged. (b) Problems. During the PhD candidate's fieldwork in China (summer 2013), her accompanying husband contracted a virus (August), leading to a debilitating condition requiring emergency back surgery (October 2013), and rehabilitation thereafter (still ongoing) back in the US. This affected the candidate's research work especially from October 2013. She postponed the confirmation of her candidature (February 2014), and was on one year’s non-study leave (April 2014 to March 2015). Her domestic situation resulted in her developing medical problems of her own (spring 2015). The consequences of these cumulative circumstances were: (i) No further fieldwork in China (originally planned for summer 2014 and after) was conducted and no further data on English in China collected; (ii) The workshop with invited panel planned for the candidate’s benefit kept being postponed, and will now not be held; (iii) The candidate is withdrawing from the PhD programme. These circumstances have resulted in a large proportion of the budget (stipend, travelling, conferences, workshop) not being spent as originally planned for the candidate’s use. (c) Achievement of objectives. Research by the P.I. on Singapore and Hong Kong, plus that by the candidate on China, have contributed to an analysis and understanding of interaction between sociohistorical factors, including language policy, population dynamics, as well as the use of computer-mediated communication, and substrate typology, in influencing the evolution of structural aspects of contact varieties of English (Singapore/ Peranakan/ Hong Kong/ Chinese English). (Objectives 1 and 2.) The range of substrate languages examined (Cantonese in Hong Kong, Putonghua and regional languages in China, and Malay, Hokkien, Mandarin and other languages in Singapore) have allowed a more systematic analysis of competition and selection of linguistic features in the developing variety of English in contact situations. (Objective 3) Together these contribute to the development of a classification that takes into account both historical and contemporary external factors and contribution of the local language ecology. 748711.label: Major findings and research outcome
748711.value: This project investigates the development of linguistic features of varieties of English in Asia, focussing on multilingual contact contexts, and developing two integrated thrusts: (i) a consideration of sociohistorical aspects, in particular demography and language policies during different eras, from the (pre-)colonial period through post-independence and into the new millennium; and (ii) a close examination of the linguistic features of the (local) languages that have come into contact with English as it has evolved. These factors together are considered as comprising the ‘ecology’ of the linguistic situation, within the ecology paradigm which applies the metaphor from population genetics and biology to linguistics. This project has used as its main case studies Singapore, Hong Kong and China (studying Singapore English, Peranakan English, Hong Kong English, China/Chinese English), and has identified the factors significant for a systematic model: (a) External ecology: the institutionalisation or otherwise of English as a consequence of its colonial past; the greater or lesser extent of spread and penetration of English as a consequence of post-independence language and education policies; the homo- or heterogeneity of the population affecting the choice of English as main lingua franca and regularity of use, and multilingual language practices; the effect of globalisation (increased acquisition and use; computer-mediated communication); and (b) Typology of languages: main languages present and dominant in the three ecologies include Mandarin (China, Singapore, and to some extent HK), Cantonese (HK, and to some extent Singapore), Hokkien (Singapore), and Malay (Singapore), allowing closer examination of specific features found in some languages but not others, and consequent identification of the influencing language. The findings hold implications for language attitudes, language planning and policy making, especially in education. The explicit recognition that other, non-linguistic factors, such as demography and language policies, play a significant role in which languages are dominant in a context and which thus influence the evolving English variety, governing parties should then be mindful of the consequences of factors such as immigration policies on the English language. Research output includes: 8 peer-reviewed articles in journals and books, 1 book published with Cambridge University Press; and 3 invited keynote lectures and 6 other presentations at international conferences (see Part C). A book proposal has been invited by Routledge publishers on English in the Sinosphere (Singapore, Hong Kong and China), based on findings from this project.

748711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
748711.value: The project has identified important directions for future research, including the following: (i) Computer-mediated communication has been identified as a significant factor in Hong Kong’s language practices, leading younger Hongkongers to use English in CMC much more than they would in normal spoken interactions which are Cantonese-dominant. CMC thus holds implications for advancing the development of English in close contact with Cantonese. (ii) China as a site is diverse, with the cosmopolitan urban centres (e.g. Shanghai, Beijing) being quite distinct from other regions, in the external factors and in the languages present and dominant (e.g. global languages vs regional and minority Chinese languages). Further research needs to document the ecologies of these distinct sites for an account of ‘Chinese English’ that reflects the different varieties and the factors that influence their evolution. The P.I. is developing research plans for projects addressing these two areas.

748711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
748711.value: This project investigates the development of linguistic features of varieties of English in Asia in multilingual contact contexts, in two complementary thrusts: (i) a consideration of sociohistorical aspects, particularly demography and language policies during different eras of pre-/colonial and post-independence periods and the new millennium; and (ii) close examination of the linguistic features of the (local) languages in contact with English as it evolved. The main case studies of Singapore, Hong Kong and China afford comparisons and contrasts in sociohistorical factors and languages dominant in the ecology (Hokkien, Cantonese, Mandarin), as well as the impact of globalisation in current change. The research demonstrates how contact involving different language families brings about change in new Englishes in ways distinct from ‘native’ varieties of English – such change is however not deviant but natural and expected. Acknowledging the legitimacy of such Englishes holds implications for language attitudes, planning and policy making, especially in education. With an explicit recognition that other non-linguistic factors, e.g. demography and language policies, significantly affect which languages dominate an ecology and thus influence the evolving English variety, governing parties should then be mindful of the consequences of factors, e.g. immigration policies, language policy, on the development of English.

748911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
748911.value: Open innovation has taken a vital role in information technology. Not only has the open-source community grown to offer more high quality software, its impact has also reached profit-generating firms, which are re-engineering their business models in innovative ways to more effectively compete in rapidly evolving IT industries. We focus on the increasingly pervasive mobile commerce, such as the marketplaces for applications on mobile platforms. Wireless devices operate on different platforms. Some of the major wireless platforms in the current market include the iPhone OS, Android, BlackBerry, Symbian, Java ME, etc. Although the application marketplaces for these platforms all exhibit characteristics of two-sided markets by bringing together application developers and end users, and rely on a variety of network effects among their participants to generate revenues, the business models that underpin these two-sided markets may differ significantly. Most platforms are proprietary such as those developed by Apple for iPhones and the iPad, whereas Android is an open-source operating system developed by Google and open-source software (OSS) developers. Because Android is released under an open license, the platform owner, Google, exercises little control over the adoption and customization of this open platform by wireless device manufacturers, or proliferation of third-party application marketplaces (aside from the platform owner’s official application market). We are interested in examining the impact of open license adoption on platform pricing and revenues, and the competition between platforms operating under these different business models. A stream of literature has explored various pricing issues in two-sided markets and obtained fruitful results. However, most studies are based on a monopoly or symmetric competition setting, which is insufficient for analyzing the asymmetric business model competition between proprietary and open platforms. We aim to contribute to this literature by modeling competing platforms with asymmetric business models, and analyzing the role of open license in such settings. 开放式创新对信息技术起到重要作用。开源社区的发展不仅提供了更多的高质量的软件，其影响也扩展到企业圈里，这是许多公司在商业模式上创新来更有效的在迅速发展的IT产业竞争。我们的重点在于移动电子商务，如移动平台的app商场。 无线设备在不同的平台上运作。市场上的一些主要无线平台目前包括iPhone OS，Android的，黑莓，Symbian和Java ME的，等等。虽然这些平台的app市场都双面汇集应用程序开发人员和平台用户，并依靠市场各种参与者之间的网络效应产生收​​入，支撑这些双面市场的商业模式会有所不同。大多数平台，如由苹果开发的iPhone和iPad持专有执照，而Android是一个开放的操作系统，有谷歌和Open Source (OSS)开发。由于Android是由开放的许可发布的，谷歌作为平台所有者允许让无线设备制造商对Android进一步定制，应用程序的买卖也可由第三方自行交易（在平台的正式市场以外）。我们感兴趣的是研究开放许可证对平台上定价和收入的影响，及不同的操作平台之间商业模式的竞争。 学术研究在探索各种双面市场定价问题取得了丰硕的成果。然而，大多数的研究是基于垄断或对称 竞争的设置，这并不足于分析非对称商业模式及专有和开放式平台之间的竞争。我们将用不对称的商业模式平台竞争的模型来分析开放许可的作用，且希望从而为学术研究作出贡献。

748911.label: Realisation of objectives
748911.value: Most of the objectives have been achieved. In one of my published papers with collaborators, we analyze competition between platforms that provide online services to users and host ads for online advertisers. We look for the business models competing platforms should choose in order to co-exist and maximize their revenues. The results show that asymmetric business models are indeed feasible in equilibrium. We also solve for the platform's pricing strategy when advertising revenues are generated on a cost-per-thousand-impression (CPM) basis and on a cost-per-click (CPC) basis. The results offer interesting contrasts between platform's strategies and business models under these two revenue models. The findings generate significant managerial implications for designing platform business model given fierce competition and variation in advertising revenue models. However, our analysis on social welfare is currently limited. The result of welfare analysis would rely on parameter values. And the implications are more meaningful for economic journals. As we targeted business journals for this paper, we eventually removed that part from our manuscript. In another working paper, we examine how strategic decisions made by platform users during their transactions on the platform affect the platform's regulatory decisions. We allow sellers to compete in setting prices and analyze buyers' purchasing choices. This is an important contribution to the literature on two-sided markets because previous works abstract away from such competition and assume the linear form of network effects.

748911.label: Major findings and research outcome
748911.value: In my public paper (Part C, 8.1), we find that a platform of online service service provider should have different business models depending on whether a competitor exists. For a monopoly platform, it is best to offer two types of services, one without advertisements and the other with revenue support of ads. We also derive the optimal prices for these service offerings. For competing platforms, their strategies depend on the advertising revenue rate. We show a menu of equilibrium service offering for competing platforms. We also find that the advertising revenue rate of cost-per-thousand-impression (CPM) model leads to a lower service price more severely than that of cost-per-click (CPC) model. In my working paper (Part C, 8.2), we focus on a methodological contribution to the previous literature by taking into account competition of sellers on the platform, whereas past studies take the platform user interactions as given. We analyze the platform's regulatory decisions facing heterogeneous sellers. The main finding is that, rather than admitting only top-quality sellers, the platform should allow a wider range of quality levels among its sellers. As sellers differ more in terms of quality, their combined profits are higher, which offer the platform a higher profit as well. This result highlights the importance of analyzing competition on the platform.

748911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
748911.value: The platform-based business model has rich economic implications that generate increasing research interest. Among the many recent efforts to deepen understanding of platforms, I am extending the existing work to several directions. An important direction is to incorporate a microfoundation of trades on the platform in the platform owner's pricing problem. This allows characterization of platform users' strategic decisions in joining the platform and in trading on the platform. Such characterization endogenizes different types of network effects that are central in the platform economy. Another direction is to examine the dynamic pricing problem of the platform. The majority of existing studies uses a simplified approach assuming the platform only sets the price once. In reality, the pricing problem is dependent on the platform's previous decisions, the changing market conditions, and advancing generations of platform products (e.g., iPhones and iPads). It will be interesting to find how the platform owner strategize in this dynamic environment.

748911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
748911.value: The research carried out in this project leads to interesting and meaningful findings for online businesses and platform businesses. It shows these businesses how the fees they charge may depend on several key factors, such as profitability of advertisements that they may use to generate revenues, specific advertising models, whether a competitor in the same market is present, and how their users interact with one another. Our findings also offer strategic guidelines for these businesses. For online service providers, we show how many types of service offerings and what types of service offerings they should provide. By offering different types of services at different prices, these businesses can better segment the user market. The best business strategies are not obvious and depend on the competing business and several other factors. For platforms, we illustrate that selecting only high-quality sellers to transact with buyers on the platform is not the profitable strategy. The platform owner should attract a wider variety of sellers who offer a wide range of quality levels to not only better serve buyers of different needs, but also to lessen competitive pressure among one another.

749711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
749711.value: It is well known that inventory fluctuations account for a significant fraction of real GDP fluctuations. Understanding inventory behavior is thus essential to better understanding aggregate fluctuations. The production smoothing (PS) model of inventory behavior has been the basic paradigm within which many empirical studies on the joint behavior of production, inventories, and sales have been conducted. However, most empirical evidence shows that the stylized production smoothing model is often rejected at both the industry and aggregate levels. Specifically, the main problems are three-fold. First, the model cannot predict that production is actually more volatile than sales in most industries as well as at the aggregate level, i.e., firms do not in fact smooth their production. Second, it predicts that inventories are negatively correlated with sales because inventories are used to smooth production against the sales shocks, which contradicts the evidence that in most industries the covariances between inventory investment and sales are positive. Third, the model generates rapid inventory adjustment speeds, whereas the estimated adjustment speeds are very slow. Risk-sensitivity (RS) was first introduced into the linear-quadratic (LQ) control problem by Jacobson (1973) and extended by Whittle (1981, 1990) and Hansen and Sargent (1995). Specifically, in the RS model agents effectively compute conditional expectations through distorted lens, increasing their effective risk aversion by putting more weights on worst possible cases. Luo and Young (2010) showed in a consumption model that the stronger preference for RS, the more consumption responds to income and the more volatile consumption is. Since the main problem in the standard PS model is that given the estimated sales process, the model cannot generate observed production fluctuations and procyclical inventory investment, the implication of RS for consumption could also possibly improve the PS model's predictions. In this project we plan to study the effects of risk-sensitive control on production decisions and the joint behavior of inventories and sales in an otherwise standard production smoothing model. Specifically, we examine whether introducing RS into firms' decisions can help explain the model's performance in the following three dimensions at both the industry- and macro-levels: (1) the relative volatility of production to sales; (2) the contemporaneous correlation between sales and inventory investment; and (3) the adjustment speed of inventories. In an extension, we also want to investigate whether imperfect information about the state can further improve the model's predictions on inventory behavior via interacting with RS. 众所周知，经济生产中存货的波动可以解释很大一部分实际国民生产总值的波动。了解存货行为可以使我们更好地了解经济总量的波动。生产平滑模型(Production Smoothing Model)是关于存货行为的基本模型，简称PS。大量有关生产-存货-销售连带行为的实证研究都是在PS的框架内完成的。然而，大部分的实证结果都从产业和总体经济层面否定了程式化的PS模型。具体问题体现在以下三个方面。首先，在大部分的产业乃至总体经济中，生产比销售变化更剧烈，即厂商并不会平滑他们的生产；PS模型不能预测这一事实。其次，在PS模型中，存货与销售是负相关的，因为存货是用于应对销售的突然变化从而平滑生产的；然而我们观测到的证据显示存货与销售是正相关的。第三，该模型推测的存货调整速度要快于实际估算的速度. 风险灵敏性(Risk-sensitivity,RS)，是被Jacobson (1973) 首次用于线性二次控制问题并在Whittle (1981, 1990) 和 Hansen and Sargent (1995) 中得到拓展。具体地说，在风险灵敏模型中代理人能有效地计算条件期望值, 但是他们较为看重最坏的可能性因此实际的风险趋避度也就增加了。Luo and Young (2010) 在一个消费模型中得到的结果表明对RS 的偏好越大，消费就会越紧跟收入并且变化越剧烈。既然PS模型的主要问题在于，给定销售走势后，模型不能模拟出相对应的生产变化及顺周期的存货投资;那么引入消费的风险灵敏性有可能改进该模型。在这个项目中，我们计划在基本的生产平滑模型之上研究风险灵敏控制对生产决策和存货-销售连带行为的影响。确切地说，我们会调查在厂商的决策过程中引进RS是否能帮助模型从产业和宏观层面解释以下三个方面：(1) 生产相对销售的波动；(2) 销售与存货投资的同步变化；(3) 存货的调整速度。 作为主要工作的延伸，我们还想调查信息不完整是否能通过与RS的交互作用进一步改进PS模型对存货行为的预测。

749711.label: Realisation of objectives
749711.value: All of the objectives proposed for this project are realized. The project has generated four papers. The major paper entitled "Robustness, Inventory Behavior, and the Production Smoothing Hypothesis" generated from this project is in preparation for submitting to a macroeconomic journal. In this paper, we fully address how model uncertainty due to preferences for robustness (or risk-sensitivity) can help improve an otherwise standard production smoothing model's predictions on the joint dynamics of sales, inventories, and production in the U.S. economy. Specifically, using the U.S. data on manufacturing, wholesale, and retail sectors, we estimated the sales process. Given the exogenous sales process, we solved the robustness version of the production smoothing model and obtained robust inventory and production decision rules. Particularly, we have found that introducing robustness has the potential to resolve a puzzle in the literature: production is actually more volatile than sales in most industries as well as at the aggregate level even if firms have the production smoothing motive. The other three papers generated from this project are closely related to the major paper and have been published in peer-reviewed economics journals: Journal of the European Economic Association (2015), Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control (2014), and Economic Inquiry (2014).

749711.label: Major findings and research outcome
749711.value: In the paper entitled "robustness, inventory behavior, and the production smoothing hypothesis", we first estimated the sales process using the U.S. data on manufacturing, wholesale, and retail sectors and found that this process is very persistent across different sectors and different samples. Given the estimated sales process, we solved the robustness version of the production smoothing model of inventory behavior and obtained robust inventory and production decision rules using the robust dynamic programming method. We then explored how model uncertainty due to RB affects the joint dynamics of sales, inventories, and production in the U.S. economy. Specifically, we found that introducing RB has the potential to resolve a puzzle in the literature: The data show that production is more volatile than sales in most industries as well as at the aggregate level, whereas the model predicts that the production is less volatile than sales because firms have the production smoothing motive. In the other three publications related to this paper, we have the following research outcome: (1) Slow Information Diffusion and the Inertial Behavior of Durables Consumption. Forthcoming in Journal of the European Economic Association 2015. Inspired by the major paper, we examined how informational friction affects the joint behavior of durable consumption, non-durable consumption, and income in this paper. (2) Model Uncertainty and Intertemporal Tax Smoothing. Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control 45, 289-314. We explored how model uncertainty due to robustness affects the joint behavior of the government's spending, taxes, and deficits and showed that it can make the tax-smoothing model fit the data better. (3) Signal Extraction and Rational Inattention. Economic Inquiry 52(2), 811-829. We compared the traditional signal extraction problem with exogenous noises with Sims' rational inattention model in this paper.

749711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
749711.value: This paper examines the importance of model uncertainty due to preferences for robustness (or risk-sensitivity) in explaining the observed joint behavior of sales, inventories, and production in the U.S. economy. In the future, it is promising to apply this idea in another important macroeconomic: How this type of uncertainty affects optimal investment behavior at both the individual and aggregate levels. Once we can successfully incorporate this information friction into the optimal investment setting, we can address some very important issues in macroeconomics. For example, how robustness affects optimal investment decision and the investment volatility in an otherwise standard Abel-Eberly investment model with uncertainty, and what is the key differences between the traditional adjustment costs hypothesis and the informational friction hypothesis?

749711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
749711.value: It is well known that inventory fluctuations account for a significant fraction of real GDP fluctuations. Understanding inventory behavior is thus essential to better understanding aggregate fluctuations. The production smoothing (PS) model of inventory behavior has been the basic paradigm within which many empirical studies on the joint behavior of production, inventories, and sales have been conducted. However, most empirical evidence shows that the stylized production smoothing model of inventory behavior is often rejected at both the industry and aggregate levels. Specifically, the main problem is that the model cannot predict that production is actually more volatile than sales in most industries as well as at the aggregate level. Robustness (RB) was first introduced into economics by Hansen and Sargent (1995). Specifically, in the RB model agents effectively compute conditional expectations through distorted lens, increasing their effective risk aversion by putting more weights on worst possible cases. In this paper we have explored the effects of RB on production decisions and the joint behavior of inventories and sales in a PS model. Specifically, we have found that introducing RB into firms' decisions can help explain the model's performance in explaining the relative volatility of production to sales.

750111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
750111.value: This project aims to examine the place of Hong Kong women filmmakers as major figures in local, regional, and global motion picture culture since the establishment of the HKSAR in 1997. No recent examination of Hong Kong women behind the camera exists. This study fills this gap in the scholarship by focusing on women filmmakers in the HKSAR from its establishment up to 2010. Some current events have made this research particularly timely. Ann Hui won the best director award for THE WAY WE ARE at the 28th Hong Kong Film Awards (2009). At the 2010 Hong Kong International Film Festival, women filmmakers presented LIKE A DREAM and CROSSING HENNESSY, among other feature films. These directors were also recognized internationally in the touring program “Visible Secrets: Hong Kong’s Women Filmmakers.” Despite this visibility and international recognition, there is no sustained study in English of women directors in Hong Kong. Books on individual films and filmmakers can be found, and Yau Ching does have a book on the topic in Chinese. However, given the number and quality of the films made by Hong Kong’s women directors, an updated and detailed study of these filmmakers and their work is needed. Taking the change in sovereignty as a starting point, this project examines key films by established and emerging women directors, producers, and scriptwriters in order to explore the role played by these women in highlighting specific issues involving gender, sexuality, politics, and aesthetics. As a perusal of titles by women directors over the last twelve years or so indicates, they tend to be attracted to specific subjects and aesthetic forms; notably, women’s roles in the Chinese family, working women, women’s position in public life and politics, domestic violence, female sex workers, consumerism, women’s sexuality, lesbianism, romance and female desire. They have been very sensitive to women outside of Hong Kong, and many have chosen to look at women in the PRC or within the Chinese diaspora as well. In addition, they have been quite adventurous in their use of film form—adopting and transforming observational/direct cinema techniques, counter-cinema, and complex “puzzle” narratives. Taking up perspectives often marginalized within the industry, it seems that Hong Kong women filmmakers have been inclined to explore aspects of film language that would go beyond the “male gaze.” 本項目旨在研究自香港特別行政區在一九九七年成立以來，香港女性電影工作者在當地和全球電影產業中的地位。在近年的學術研究中並沒有對香港女性電影工作者的研究。而本項目計劃重點研究女性導演直至二零一零年為止在香港的發展，填補了這學術空隙。近年一些電影界的大事使本研究顯得尤為合時。在二零零九年許鞍華的《天水圍的日與夜》贏得第28屆香港金像獎最佳導演。於二零一零年的第34屆香港國際電影節亦展示了《如夢》、《月滿軒尼詩》等女導演的作品。在名為 “Visible Secrets: Hong Kong’s Women Filmmakers” 的英國巡迴節目中，這些女導演都獲得國際認可。 雖然香港女導演獲得如此的國際知名度和公認，到目前為止仍然沒有以香港女導演為題目，以英語寫成的學術研究。刊物只局限於探討單一電影或導演，其中作者游靜有出版一本關於香港女電影工作者的中文書。但鑒於香港女導演作品的質量，目前是有需要進行以香港女導演与其作品為題的近年詳細研究。為了探討這些女導演對帶出獨有的性別、性慾、政治與美學問題的角色，本項目旨在研究已確立地位或新晉的女導演，出品人和編劇的主要電影作品。 細讀過去十二年香港女導演的電影，她們傾向喜歡一些獨特的題目和美學形式。尤其是女性在中國家庭裡的角色、工作女性、女性在公共生活和政治中的位置、家庭暴力、女性性工作者、消費主義、女性情慾、女同性戀、戀情和女性欲望等。香港女導演對在香港以外的女性非常敏感，很多喜歡選擇探討在中國大陸或海外華語區的女性。在製片的形式與運用她們也相當冒險 — 採納和改革觀察性/直接電影手法技巧、“抗衡/反電影”(counter-cinema) 和錯綜複雜“拼圖”(puzzle)式的敘事手法。这些香港女導演看來傾向採用在电影界往往被边缘化的觀點，她们喜歡在“男性凝視” (male gaze) 的觀點以外探究電影語言的各方面。

750111.label: Realisation of objectives
750111.value: I am very gratified to report that I have successfully accomplished all of the objectives of my project on HKSAR women filmmakers. With the support of my research assistants funded by the grant, Derek Lam and Iris Eu, I was able to achieve my first objective by documenting contributions made by a wide variety of contemporary Hong Kong women filmmakers and putting this information up for public access on a website, "Hong Kong Women Filmmakers: Sex, Politics and Cinema Aesthetics, 1997 to the Present," hosted by the Women’s Studies Research Centre and the Department of Comparative Literature, University of Hong Kong (https://hkwomenfilmmakers.wordpress.com/). This site includes a list of filmmakers with biographical information, filmographies, and links to articles on their careers, specific films, and other documents. In addition to information on specific women filmmakers, the site serves as an academic resource by providing a bibliography of academic publications on Hong Kong women filmmakers, as well as pages devoted to news items and other documents. Because so much material on HKSAR women filmmakers overlaps with general scholarship on Hong Kong film, Derek Lam and I highlighted Hong Kong women filmmakers and their achievements in a general bibliography on Hong Kong film we compiled for the online Oxford Bibliographies in Cinema and Media Studies. My close analysis of specific films by noted female directors and screenwriters enabled me to achieve objectives two and five. I identified common themes, narrative structures, character types, stylistic approaches and aesthetic concerns quite clearly in my exploration of generational differences in three films dealing with marital infidelity (published in Feminist Media Studies). Ann Hui’s "July Rhapsody" (2001), Mabel Cheung’s "City of Glass" (1998), and Mak Yan-Yan’s "Butterfly" (2004) include the thematic similarities and differences necessary to illustrate the specific ways in which women across generations adjust to life in the HKSAR. Produced during the HKSAR’s first decade, these films dramatize the aspirations and anxieties associated with the years immediately following the Handover. The three films share flashback structures, coming-of-age plots, and an element of nostalgia linked to memories of growing up in the colony and its historical links to the other places associated with the Chinese diaspora. They reference mainland China, Macau, the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, France, and Japan, among other places, in order to contrast living in Hong Kong with the promises and limitations of life elsewhere. The focus on women’s role in domestic life includes the exploration of expectations based on gender, class, and ethnic traditions within these multicultural environments. Because of their cosmopolitan perspectives, these films indirectly dramatize the various ways women across generations have mirrored, responded to, reflected upon and absorbed transnational currents in feminism as well. In this research on these films, I highlighted issues of gender, sexuality, feminism, and women’s place in colonial, postcolonial and global consumer society. In my chapter for the Blackwell Companion to Hong Kong Cinema, I concentrated on recent developments in feminist film and cultural theory (objective four) by exploring three key films by Ann Hui, "The Way We Are" (2008), "Night and Fog" (2009), and "All About Love" (2010), as evidence of the director’s evolving engagement with feminism. Drawing on theories of cosmofeminism, I argued for a consideration of Hui’s films through an accounting of the complexities of dealing with women’s issues within Hong Kong’s transnational geopolitical position, as well as their precarious place within the global cultural economy. In my analysis of "All About Love" in particular, I drew on queer theory to come to grips with a romantic comedy about bisexual unwed mothers, while bringing scholarship on third world feminism into the mix to explore "Night and Fog," which deals with the plight of a rural Sichuan woman married to a homicidal Hong Kong man. Delving deeper into the question of feminism in HKSAR women’s filmmaking, I focused on the concept of “post-feminism” and “third wave” feminism in the work by women associated with a younger generation of filmmakers. I examined women’s sexuality and activism in my research into the work of screenwriter/scholar Elsa Chan (Yeeshan) in the films "Whispers and Moans" (2007) and "True Women for Sale" (2008), as well as my analyses of the role of television, the Internet, and the sex industry in Barbara Wong’s "Women’s Private Parts" (2000) and Yau Ching’s "Ho Yuk: Let’s Love Hong Kong" (2002). I looked at women activists in the broader political arena in analyses of Tammy Cheung’s "July" (2005) and "Election" (2008) as well as in Clara Law’s transnational rumination on women and refugees in "Letters to Ali" (2004). For objectives three and seven, I mapped Hong Kong women filmmakers’ position in local, regional, and global film circuits. Although I planned to gesture in the direction of Hong Kong women within the film festival circuit, I discovered that these international networks played a vital role in the ways in which HKSAR female filmmakers developed their careers. As a consequence, starting with Clara Law’s short film, "Red Earth" (2010), produced for the Hong Kong International Film Festival, I began to explore the relationship between Hong Kong women filmmakers, branding, and the role creative industries play not only in film production but distribution and exhibition as well. In the case of Law’s film, the Hong Kong International Film Festival “brands” the short, which was picked up and screened at the 67th Venice International Film Festival and put online as well. In addition to the festival branding, the film benefits from contributions from Canon, Blackberry and the Hyatt commercial trademarks as well, and the film gives these companies added publicity and prestige through their visual presence on screen in a clearly artistic venture. Commercial connections involving cultural capital and lifestyle choices play an important role in many film festival productions. Given the importance of intertextual allusions to contemporary film aesthetics, I delved into objective six by looking at the complex geopolitical references to various moments in film history in Hui’s "Ordinary Heroes" (1999) and Law’s "Like a Dream" (2009) in my monograph "Citing China" (University of Hawai'i Press). Although the book includes films that “cite” China in various fashions against the backdrop of contemporary world cinema, these two HKSAR female auteurs stand out for the way in which they blend gender politics, women’s struggle, and Chinese culture with specific aesthetic choices linked to Jean-Luc Godard, Chris Marker, and Alfred Hitchcock, among others. I was struck by the encyclopaedic film knowledge and deft use of film techniques in films by women in the Hong Kong New Wave and Second Wave. However, women working in experimental and independent film also stand on the cutting edge of contemporary cinema and digital culture. I delved deeper into Hong Kong women independent filmmaking through my close analysis of Yau Ching’s "Ho Yuk," and I was rewarded with a better appreciation of the continuing importance of feminist counter-cinema in Hong Kong. In achieving the objectives I set out in my initial proposal, I demonstrated the significance of HKSAR women filmmakers to contemporary local, regional, and international film art and industry. Commercially and through film festival exhibition, they have a global reach and recognition that merits continuing scholarly scrutiny.

Gesture toward further areas of inquiry involving women in Hong Kong film by looking at the work of these women within the context of Hong Kong New Wave cinema, the circulation of Hong Kong film in the festival circuit, the celebration of Hong Kong film auteurs and independent productions, the history of the Hong Kong studio system, and other creative industries in the territory

750111.label: Major findings and research outcome
750111.value: My major findings confirm the enormously varied contributions Hong Kong women make to the local, regional, and international film industry. Beyond lucrative careers, these women contribute to Hong Kong cinema’s reputation for aesthetic innovation, socio-political engagement, and flexible accommodation to the demands of arthouse audiences and festival programmers. I have documented this online, in print, and at international conferences. I have also used their films to critique contemporary feminist thinking in relation to women’s rights, sexual freedom, female labor, and global citizenship. I discovered many new voices emerging, and I was struck by the way a younger generation of filmmakers engages with gender politics through their transnational connections. For example, Barbara Wong’s "Wonder Women" (2007) serves to illustrate the way in which a woman filmmaker from Hong Kong imagines the lives of the territory’s career women through the rhetoric of American corporate feminist attitudes and assumptions. Like Sheryl Sandberg, who calls on women in American business to recognize the reality of the corporate world and accommodate their behavior to the needs of capitalist enterprise, the women in Wong’s film mirror the expectations of the men who have shaped their environment. Looking at Hong Kong in the decade beginning with the Handover in 1997 allows Wong to provide several contrasting and complementary models of patriarchal organization in transition. The film reveals a geopolitical dimension to the fortunes of the female characters in the film, and they must bend in order not to break as they navigate these changes. My monograph, "Citing China: Politics, Postmodernism, and World Cinema" (Honolulu: University of Hawai’i Press, in press), has been substantially transformed by my research on HKSAR women filmmakers. I originally embarked on the research for this book as part of a project to explore China-West transnational connections in contemporary world cinema. However, engaging more critically with the work of Clara Law and Ann Hui made me realize that Hong Kong’s contribution to these exchanges goes far beyond what I had originally imagined. By bringing in the gender politics at the heart of these cinematic citations, I became more sensitive to the way in which figures of ethnic Chinese women appeared on global screens less as exotic objects and more as agents of political change. I plan to continue this part of my work on Chinese women, political activism, and suffrage in future projects.

750111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
750111.value: The research funded by this grant serves as the foundation for my continuing exploration of women filmmakers in world cinema. For example, I plan to elaborate on my work on HKSAR women in international film networks. Focusing on Ann Hui’s deep connections with European and Asian international film festivals, I uncovered the ways she has consistently been showcased at in Europe in A-list as well as second tier and specialty festivals, and she has received the most prestigious awards available to Chinese-language directors at regional festivals. Born in the mainland, but educated at HKU as well as in film school in London, Hui communicates well in English as well as Chinese, and her extensive knowledge of film history and international cinema culture is clearly evident in her use of sophisticated film language and aesthetic techniques. Hui has been particularly successful dividing her career between Hong Kong and the PRC, and the next step of my research takes me in the direction of analyzing Ann Hui’s "The Golden Era" as an example of Chinese “soft power” in world film culture. I plan to expand on this research to include a younger generation of women filmmakers working between Hong Kong and the PRC.

750111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
750111.value: The aim of my project was to examine the place of Hong Kong women filmmakers as major figures in local, regional, and global motion picture culture since the establishment of the HKSAR in 1997. I accomplished this by documenting the contribution made by women working in the Hong Kong film industry. Although I included many commercially successful films in my study, I went beyond the mainstream to capture the contribution made by women to Hong Kong documentary, experimental, independent, and alternative motion picture culture. The study took account, too, of the role women filmmakers play in politics as activists, artists, and citizens with movie cameras in Hong Kong’s contested public sphere. Taking the change in sovereignty as a starting point, this project examined key films by established and emerging women directors, producers, and scriptwriters, and it shows how women, working within a male-dominated media culture, manage to thrive and seriously address issues involving gender, sexuality, politics, and aesthetics in their motion pictures. As my research shows, Hong Kong women, in fact, push the boundaries of feminism and film art far beyond the borders of the HKSAR.

750311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
750311.value: Elderly people navigating an obstacle in the environment may try to ensure that they do not fall by consciously monitoring and controlling their locomotor movements. Although conscious control can be functionally useful for overriding inappropriate responses (such as turning left instead of right), it can disrupt the smooth automaticity of well-practiced movements, potentially causing a fall. Movement specific reinvestment is a term used to describe the propensity that people have to monitor and control their movements consciously. The aim of this project is to use a culturally relevant Chinese version of the Movement Specific Reinvestment Scale (MSRS-C), which has been developed and validated in an on-going GRF grant, to examine whether the propensity to consciously monitor and control walking behaviour is related to allocation of attention and gaze strategies used by older adults in Hong Kong when navigating obstacles in the built environment. The findings will inform whether clinical tools should be developed to (a) reduce (or increase) the propensity for movement specific reinvestment or (b) modify attentional or gaze strategies in the fight against falling in Hong Kong elderly people. 老年人在有障礙物的環境中移動及導航的時候, 可能會有意識地監察及控制自己移動時的動作以確保他們自己不會跌倒. 雖然有意識地控制身體有修改不適當之反應動作(如在應向右走時向左走)的功能, 但它同時會破壞已熟練技能的自動執行性從而有機會導致跌倒的發生. 動作反思一詞是用來描述人們有意識地自我監控身體的傾向. 這個研究項目的主旨是在於運用一個配合華人文化的中文版動作反思量表(MSRS-C)去研究香港老人在有障礙物的建築物內移動及導航時, 有意識地自我監控步行的傾向是否與注意力的分佈模式及注視模式有關, 而這個測量表一直在GRF基金持續的資助下得到發展及驗証. 研究結果有望指導發展臨床工具(a)以減少(或增加) 動作反思的傾向 或 (b) 改變注意力分佈及注視模式以改善香港老人跌倒的情況.

750311.label: Realisation of objectives
750311.value: The objective of this project is to examine, with respect to allocation of attention and patterns of gaze behavior, the propensity of elderly non-fallers, fallers (objective 1) and pre-elderly non-fallers (objective 2) for conscious monitoring and control of their locomotor movements (i.e., movement specific reinvestment) when navigating obstacles in the environment. Using a well-designed research methodology in our project, we had successfully investigated the objective 1 and 2 of our project. Comparing to the elderly non-fallers and fallers’ population, however, it was unable to find out significant findings with rehabilitation implications in the pre-elderly non-fallers (objective 2). Therefore, the objective 2 cannot be completely achieved. It may be because of the reason that most of the pre-elderly non-fallers that we randomly recruited were with extremely good balance and walking ability which were very similar to the balance and walking ability of the middle-aged adults. Therefore, the pre-elderly group that we recruited may not be able to reflect characteristics of the pre-elderly population comprehensively. It is also noted that a request for change of Principal Investigator (PI) was done from the previous PI of the project (Prof. Rich Masters), just prior to the final six months of the project. Consequently, a six-month extension was requested and was approved. However, the objectives of the project have been completed satisfactorily.
