750311.label: Major findings and research outcome
750311.value: The objective of this project is to examine, with respect to allocation of attention and patterns of gaze behavior, the propensity of elderly non-fallers, fallers (objective 1) and pre-elderly non-fallers (objective 2) for conscious monitoring and control of their locomotor movements (i.e., movement specific reinvestment) when navigating obstacles in the environment. The findings can inform whether clinical intervention should be developed to (a) reduce (or increase) the propensity for movement specific reinvestment or (b) modify attentional or gaze strategies in the fight against falling in Hong Kong elderly people. The project’s results generally support our hypotheses. Additionally, it also provides us with further information about elderly non-fallers with high propensity for movement specific reinvestment. Walking in an environment that requires accurate stepping and navigation of obstacles causes elderly people who have not fallen, yet display a high propensity for movement specific reinvestment, to have greater internal focus of attention (i.e., they are more aware of their limb movements) and reduced awareness of the external environment compared to elderly people with a low propensity for movement specific reinvestment. Furthermore, elderly people with a high propensity for reinvestment also show prolonged stance phase duration prior to stepping on targets and decreased stepping accuracy compared to elderly people with a low propensity for reinvestment. Longer stance phase and decreased stepping accuracy potentially indicate that elderly people with a high propensity for reinvestment prioritize planning of upcoming movements over finalizing ongoing movements. Similarly to high reinvesting elderly non-fallers, elderly people who have fallen show greater internal focus of attention during walking. However, they appear to adopt significantly slower gait speed, which potentially gives them more time to finalize ongoing movements and plan upcoming movements. Comparing to the elderly non-fallers and fallers’ population, however, it was unable to find out major findings in pre-elderly population. The results suggest that elderly people with high movement specific reinvestment propensity would exhibit a relatively poorer stepping behavior and attentional strategies during walking. Therefore, it is essential to develop some effective gait rehabilitation methods in order to decrease the propensity for movement specific reinvestment from elderly people with high movement specific reinvestment propensity. It may not only improve the elderly people’s movement dynamics but may also decrease their risk of falling in an urban walking environment.

750311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
750311.value: Our project’s results suggest that elderly people with high movement specific reinvestment propensity would exhibit a relatively poorer stepping behavior and attentional strategies during walking. Consequently, it may indeed increase the risk of falling. As a result, the findings inform us that an effective rehabilitation strategy in gait rehabilitation is urgently needed to be developed in order to establish a potential way to decrease the propensity of movement specific reinvestment for elderly people with the problem of high movement specific reinvestment propensity and consequently reduce their risk of falling. However, to the best of our knowledge, there is no research investigating potential interventions to decrease the propensity for movement specific reinvestment by elderly people during rehabilitation. Substantial evidence in psychology literature showed that different methods of implicit motor learning can probably be used, which may decrease the propensity for movement specific reinvestment. Therefore, it will be extremely influential if we can investigate on the effect of dual-task and analogy trainings during gait rehabilitation by elderly people at risk of falling in Hong Kong. Our research team has already submitted a new proposal for the application of General Research Fund 2016/17 in this influential rehabilitation-related research topic.

750311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
750311.value: Elderly people navigating an obstacle in the environment may try to ensure that they do not fall by consciously monitoring and controlling their locomotor movements. Although conscious control may be functionally beneficial for overriding inappropriate responses (e.g., turning left instead of right), it can disrupt the smooth automaticity of well-practiced movements, potentially causing a fall. Movement specific reinvestment is a term used to describe the propensity that people have to monitor and control their movements consciously. The aim of this project is to use a culturally relevant Chinese version of the Movement Specific Reinvestment Scale (MSRS-C) to examine whether the propensity to consciously monitor and control walking behaviour is related to allocation of attention and gaze strategies used by elderly people in Hong Kong when navigating obstacles in the built environment. Results show that elderly people with higher propensity to consciously monitor and control walking behavior exhibits a poorer walking behavior with greater internal focus of attention (i.e., more aware of their limb movements) and it may result in higher risk of falling. It suggests that an effective gait rehabilitation strategy is needed to be developed in order to reduce the potential effects of movement specific reinvestment in elderly population.

750511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
750511.value: 這個項目的目的是從「學習者角度研究」項目 (Learner's Perspective Study LPS) 的數據庫中，研究有效的數學教學策略。來自澳洲、香港及新加坡的數據包括：教師和學生的訪談、教案和課堂實錄。 國際比較研究提供了解有效教學策略和實踐的機會。為了尋求對有效教學策略的理解，這個項目旨在比較澳洲、香港和新加坡的數學課堂，其重點在於分析課堂學習活動的學習片段；為「學習者角度研究」項目(LPS)的現有數據庫進行第二次分析研究。 LPS是一個由16個國家組成的國際合作伙伴，總部設在澳洲，目的以綜合和全面的方式研究初中二數學的教學模式。自從2006年起發佈的LPS結果，有關教學方面如：課堂結構、巡堂活動、課堂總結和教學限制等也曾報導。然而，有效教學策略的問題只是解答了一部分。為了填補差距，本項目將成為LPS團隊項目的一部分，比較亞洲和非亞洲的數學教室的差異，透過分析課堂學習活動找出在不同文化背景的有效教學策略；從而對世界各地的數學教學有更深的了解。

750511.label: Major findings and research outcome
750511.value: 1. Analysis was carried out for 90 lessons of eighth-grade mathematics. Australia, Hong Kong and Singapore each contribute 30 lessons, with a focus of mathematical learning tasks. 2. A framework of analysis consisting of the dimensions of task, instructional practice, mediation from a social perspective was generated. 3. Results showed that the number of Routine Task (RT) was very much higher than the number of Learning Task (LT) in the lessons by all the teachers in three places. Both LT and RT are essential for students’ learning to take place during the lessons. 4. RT in this study is not the same as learning by rote. The RT episodes was identified as repetitive because the teacher had already explained or demonstrated the specific concepts or skills in an earlier example that might be in an earlier lesson or in the same lesson. As a result, RT may take place in a variety of activities in the lesson that are important to learning, such as, exercises for practice in the lesson, instances when the teacher chose to repeat the explanation with additional examples, and instances when the teacher went through a test, seatwork, homework questions by questions. 5. As far as the distribution of time for different forms of instructional activities was concerned, the lessons by the Australian teachers had more time for students carrying out their work than instruction. In the lessons by the Australian teachers the proportion of lesson time spent on instruction was less than those in Hong Kong and Singapore; and the proportion of lesson time spent for students carrying out their work was higher than those in Hong Kong and Singapore. The proportion of time for feedback in the lessons by the teachers in Singapore was higher than those in Australia and Hong Kong. 6. The third comparison is the occurrence of mediated-learning episodes. It was found that there was little evidence of mediated learning in general for all the lessons. There were no typical patterns among teachers in the same place. The variation tended to be a result of the differences between individual teachers. The individual teacher’s pedagogical views were crucial. 7. The research findings were disseminated in publication of scholarly paper in international journals and edited books; renowned international conferences and invited seminars and lectures in university of high ranking (see part C). 8. Two news external funded projects were generated (see part C).

750511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
750511.value: The project presents an in-depth understanding of the use of mathematical tasks and pedagogy via comparative studies of the data generated in three places, Australia, Singapore and Hong Kong, providing a spring board for a new project for developing pedagogy for Hong Kong local context, funded by QEF, “Catering for students’ learning diversity through rich tasks and collaborative learning (junior secondary mathematics)”. The methodology of data collection, analysis and coding could be extended to a new project funded by GRF, “Fundamental challenges in using digital technologies in secondary mathematics classrooms: a comparison between different paradigms”

750511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
750511.value: Mathematical tasks are central to the learning of mathematics and major vehicles in the lessons for learning to take place. Analysis was carried out for 90 lessons of eighth-grade mathematics. Australia, Hong Kong and Singapore each contribute 30 lessons, with a focus of mathematical learning tasks from the perspectives of the nature of the tasks, instructional practice and teachers’ mediation in social learning theory. The data generated in the three places of diverse cultures provided a very good opportunity for the understanding of the feasibility of using mathematical tasks to provide an effective learning environment. Results showed that the number of Routine Task (RT) was very much higher than the number of Learning Task (LT) in the lessons by all the teachers in three places. Both LT and RT are essential for students’ learning to take place during the lessons. It was found that there was little evidence of mediated learning in general for all the lessons. Despite the cultural differences between the three places, there were no typical patterns among teachers in the same place. The variation tended to be a result of the differences between individual teachers. The individual teacher’s pedagogical views were crucial.

750711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
750711.value: The aim of this project is to examine the process by which Japanese products and services were assimilated into Hong Kong society, by conducting oral history interviews with Chinese and Japanese businesspeople who were involved in such pioneering efforts. The interviewees will include those pioneers who introduced Japanese restaurants, polyester for artificial flowers, pop concerts, watches, and Judo lessons into Hong Kong during the period from 1955 – when major Japanese companies opened or reopened their business operations in Hong Kong – to 1980 when Deng Xiaoping’s Open Door Policy boosted the transnational flow of Japanese products to mainland China via Hong Kong. These pioneers are now reaching their eighth or ninth decades, and I believe it is vital to record their memories before they are lost altogether. But since memories can be unreliable and fade over time, these interview accounts will be supplemented by official records and archival materials, including related advertisements that appeared in the Hong Kong press. The interviews will portray expatriates and locals who laid a foundation for the eventual flow of Japanese products and services which have made such an impact on the Hong Kong lifestyle. For example, in 2008, Hong Kong imported more Japanese food items than any other country and region in the world, amounting to 20.7% of Japanese total food exports (exceeding even the US, whose population is 40 times that of Hong Kong). In a city of 7 million people, there are now more than 700 Japanese restaurants. And yet, in spite of their tremendous impact, the first-hand accounts from the pioneers who introduced Japanese products and services into Hong Kong are scarce. While the Hongkong Japanese Club has been publishing some lived experiences of Japanese expatriates in its internal Japanese-language publications since 1963, they do not focus on the flow of Japanese products and services that were significant contributions to Hong Kong society. In addition, the contributions of Chinese people to this process, including those who grew up in Japan, are largely overlooked. As with my previous work on rice cookers, this study is motivated by a desire to examine the globalization of “Made in Japan” products and services from a less Japan-centric perspective. The outcome of this study will shed light on why and how Japanese products were assimilated into Hong Kong; and will contribute to a growing body of Asian studies literature based on oral history interviews. 這項研究的目的是要透過訪問參與開拓性努力的華人和日本商人的口述歷史故事以考察與討論日本的產品和服務被同化融入香港社會的過程。口述故事的主人翁包括那些從1955到1980年期間把日本餐館、聚酯人造花、 流行音樂會、 手錶和柔道等介紹到香港的開拓者們。1955年以來, 日本各大工商企業就在香港開或重開他們的業務營運, 到了1980年, 鄧小平的經濟開放政策更推動了日本產品經香港進入中國大陸的跨國流動。這些先驅者，現在已經達到了八十,九十的高齡，在他們的記憶還沒有完全失去以前記錄下來是至關重要的。由於記憶會隨著時間的推移漸漸模糊和變得不可靠，因此，這些採訪的資料將加入官方記錄和檔案資料，包括出現在香港報紙的廣告等補充。口述歷史故事將描繪駐港日本人員和本地商家，他們奠定了日本產品和服務在香港流動的基礎和對市民帶來生活方式的影響。例如，在2008年，香港比世界任何其他國家和地區進口更多日本食品項目，達到日本總食物出口的20.7％（超過人口是香港的40倍的美國）。僅僅在2010年的秋天，在這個700萬人口的城市，已經有超過700家日本餐館存在。儘管他們擁有巨大影響，但是引進日本產品和服務的先驅們的第一手聲音檔案甚為稀缺。雖然『香港日本人俱樂部』的內部刊物自1963年以來一直有出版駐港日本人士的生活經驗，但是，對香港社會有顯著貢獻的日本產品和服務並沒有得到重視。此外，華人，包括那些在日本土生土長的，在這個過程的貢獻大體上也被忽略。跟我以前研究電飯煲時同一願望，這項研究是要脫離以日本為中心的角度， 考察「日本製造」的全球化活動。這項研究結果將提示日本產品和服務是為什麼和怎樣地被同化到香港; 並可為以口述歷史為主的亞洲研究豐富文獻。

750911.label: Project Title(Chinese)
750911.value: ‘一河兩制’ - 深圳河流域的空間整合及環境管理問題

750911.label: Project Objectives
750911.value: to investigate, from the perspective of landscape ecology, the pattern of landscape changes observed in the Shenzhen River catchment in the past three decades and their impacts on the environment; to analyse the major driving forces—e.g., planning approach, political considerations, and economic interests—accounting for such landscape changes on both sides of the River; to examine the prospect of crafting a new, cross-border, institutional mechanism that could facilitate an integrated and sustainable landscape development process in the overall catchment under the “One Country, Two Systems” framework.
rows: to investigate, from the perspective of landscape ecology, the pattern of landscape changes observed in the Shenzhen River catchment in the past three decades and their impacts on the environment;
to analyse the major driving forces—e.g., planning approach, political considerations, and economic interests—accounting for such landscape changes on both sides of the River;

to examine the prospect of crafting a new, cross-border, institutional mechanism that could facilitate an integrated and sustainable landscape development process in the overall catchment under the “One Country, Two Systems” framework.

750911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
750911.value: The Shenzhen River originates in the Wulong Mountain and flows from the northeast to the southwest. It drains into the Inner Deep Bay, where the entire estuarine area is a wetland of international importance. The river forms the boundary between the Hong Kong Special Adminstrative Region (HKSAR) and the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone (SSEZ), two jurisdictions administered separately under the “One County, Two Systems” governance framework since July 1997. The Shenzhen River catchment area—the site of this study—covers an area of 640.5 km2 and its boundary is demarcated in Figure 1. The land mass situated to the north of Shenzhen River has undergone rapid urbanisation since the establishment of the SSEZ in 1980, while the long stretch of land lying to the south of the River, inside the HKSAR, has remained largely rural. An increasingly close economic integration between the HKSAR and the SSEZ has intensified the conflict between development and conservation because there is a rising demand for additional infrastructure investment and urban growth allowance inside Hong Kong’s restricted border area, which is currently a zone of cultural and ecological importance protected from development. Given the extreme contrasts in the degree of development on the opposite sides of Shenzhen River, balancing development pressure and the need for conservation to ensure long-term sustainability for the entire catchment area is particularly challenging in this cross-border zone. The dramatic contrast between the two sides of the Shenzhen River (shown in Figure 2) makes it a unique site for a cross-boundary landscape study. More importantly, as the border zone regime is undergoing rapid change, it offers an invaluable opportunity to study the transformation of the border landscape and its impacts on the environment. The research findings will offer useful insights for planning authorities on both sides of the border, who have thus far not considered development plans from a total catchment perspective. This study aims at (i) investigating, from a landscape ecology perspective, the pattern of landscape changes observed in the Shenzhen River catchment in the past three decades and their impacts on the environment; (ii) analysing the major driving forces—e.g., planning approach, political considerations, and economic interests—accounting for such landscape changes on both sides of the River; and (iii) examining the prospect of crafting a new institutional mechanism to facilitate an integrated and sustainable landscape development process in the catchment area under the “One Country, Two Systems” framework. 深圳河發源於梧桐山，由東北流向西南，流域佔地640.5平方公里，河口靠近於后海灣內的一處國際重要濕地。深圳河是香港特別行政區和深圳經濟特區的邊界河，自1997年7月起，香港和深圳在「一國兩制」的架構下分別由當地政府管治。深圳河則由深港兩地共管。 自1980年深圳特區成立以來，深圳河北岸經歷迅速的城市化；相反地，位於香港特區內的南岸仍保持著原來的鄉郊形態。基於當地文化遺產及生態的重要性的考慮，香港邊境禁區目前被界定為一個限制開發的受保護區域。隨著深圳與香港的經濟融合，鼓吹在香港邊境禁區內加大投資基礎建設和加快城市發展的聲音日漸增加，加劇了發展與保育兩者間的衝突。深圳河兩岸發展形熊的強烈對比，突顯出平衡發展壓力和保護環境、確保整個跨界流域的可持續發展的工作極具挑戰性。 這個經歷迅速變化的邊境區域，為學者提供了一個研究跨界景觀以及其對環境的影響的寶貴機會。深港兩地的規劃部門，迄今還未有從整個流域的觀點出發考慮發展規劃，是次研究結果將為有關部門提供獨到的見解。 這項研究的目的為：（一）從景觀生態學的角度來調查深圳河流域在過去三十年，景觀的變化模式及其對環境的影響;（二）分析深圳河兩岸景觀變化的主要推動力 － 例如規劃方法，政治因素和經濟利益等；（三）研究在「一國兩制」 的框架下，如何成立一個新的跨界合作機制，以促進流域的整合和可持續發展。

750911.label: Realisation of objectives
750911.value: Objective 1: Five sets of Landsat TM images taken in the years 1988, 1993, 1998, 2003 and 2008, and two sets of SPOT images taken in 1993 and 2013 were used for investigating the land-use and land-cover change of the study site, the Shanzhen River basin. The remote sensing data were processed, classified and then analyzed using GIS software. Major environmental impacts due to land use and landscape changes during the study period were investigated. The results of analyses of land use changes and the impact on wildlife habitats and their ecological value are reported in Ng, Xie & Yu (2013), and Choi & Ng (2015). Objective 2: Extensive literatures reviews and personal interviews were conducted in investigating the driving forces accounting for such land use and landscape changes on both sides of the River. The main drivers for the changes have been identified from political, economical and social perspectives (Choi & Ng 2015). In order to understand the mechanism of spatial variations across geographical space which is fundamental to nature conservation, this research has analyzed the spatio-temporal variations of human and biophysical factors of habitat loss in the catchment over the study period from 1988 to 2008 (Xie & Ng 2013). This research also examined the integration of landscape connectivity and ecosystem services. An area-based functional connectivity index, known as the possibility of connectivity (PC), was employed to examine the temporal and spatial dynamics of the value of ecosystem services for biodiversity conservation over the period from 1988 to 2008. (Xie & Ng 2013) Objective 3: The study has examined the prospect of crafting a new, cross-border, institutional mechanism that could facilitate an integrated and sustainable development process under the “One Country, Two Systems” framework. Some initial study results based upon applying the Trans-boundary Environmental Cooperation conceptual framework to analyse the case of regional smog in the HK-Pearl River Delta metropolitan zone, including the Shenzhen SEZ, is reported in Lee (2015). From a theoretical perspective, this research has explored how a physical mechanism, namely asymmetric payoff; and a social mechanism, reciprocity; simultaneously affect collective cooperation in theoretical water sharing interactions (Ng, Yu & Zhao 2013).

750911.label: Major findings and research outcome
750911.value: The project used remote sensing data and landscape metrics to examine land use and landscape changes in the Shenzhen River basin during the period 1988 to 2013. The results reveal that while the Hong Kong side of the river remains largely rural with a few new town developments and a well protected wetland reserve at the estuarine area, the Shenzhen side has lost most of her farmland and wetlands to urban development and causing significant loss of habitats of high ecological value. There are distinctive political, economic and social circumstances which have shaped the contrasting landscape in this border region (Ng, Xie & Yu 2013, Choi & Ng 2015). The degree of habitat loss is further investigated by referring to the loss of ecosystem services due to habitat alteration or destruction. In order to examine how influencing factors change with space, Geographically Weighted Regression model is employed which is proven to be effective in revealing spatially varying relationship and performs better than the conventional global regression model. The results also provide a detail site information of the different roles of related factors across different locations. Various factors, especially the human-related ones, play a significant role in determining both the “rate” and “location” of habitat loss, and the influences also varied during the entire study period. (Xie & Ng 2013). By using the Possibility of Connectivity function, this research has examined the temporal and spatial dynamics of the value of ecosystem services of the catchment over the study period. Results suggest that, compared with conventional method, our method can identify significant reduction of ecosystem services that is not only due to the decrease of habitat size, but also the destruction of connectivity among habitat patches. It can also identify priority sites for ecological restoration for biodiversity conservation (Ng, Xie & Yu 2013). Regarding the institutional mechanism for addressing transboundary environmental issues, our study argues that while the current project based approach has produced some marginal and short-term gain in, for example, enhanced air quality, such gains are easily negated by increasing levels of deterioration because the region’s overall environmental governance structure, which is ill-stated to tackle trans-boundary externalities, has fundamentally remained unchanged. (Lee 2015) From a theoretical perspective, this research has explored how a physical mechanism, namely asymmetric payoff; and a social mechanism, reciprocity; simultaneously affect collective cooperation in theoretical water sharing interactions (Ng, Yu & Zhao 2013).

750911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
750911.value: Future research can be focused on: 1. Further improvement and development of the methodology proposed in the present project for more accurate evaluation of ecosystem services and its dynamic change in such complex river basin. It is worth to further investigate the role of connectivity in determining ecosystem services. 2. The absorptive/carrying capacity and environmental risk assessment/management issues of the Sehnzhen River basin, in particular, the potential threats to the sustainability of the Mai Po and Inner Deep Bay RAMSAR site. 3. Further explore and develop a cross-border institutional mechanism that could facilitate an integrated and sustainable landscape development process in the whole catchment under the “One Country, Two Systems” framework.

750911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
750911.value: The project used remote sensing data and landscape metrics to examine land-use and landscape changes in the transboundary Shenzhen River basin from 1988 to 2013. The results reveal that while the Hong Kong side of the river remains largely rural with a few new town developments and a well protected wetland at the estuarine area, the Shenzhen side has lost most of her farmland and wetlands, which are of high ecological value, to urban development. There are distinctive political, economic and social circumstances which have shaped the contrasting landscape in this border region. Regarding the loss of ecosystem services due to habitat alteration/destruction, the study provides a detail site information of the role of various related factors across different locations. It also show that ecosystem services are not only affected by the decrease of habitat size, but also the destruction of connectivity among habitat patches. Regarding the institutional mechanism for addressing transboundary environmental issues, the study argues that while the current project based approach has produced some marginal and short-term gain, such gains are easily negated by increasing levels of deterioration because the region’s overall environmental governance structure, which is ill-stated to tackle trans-boundary externalities, has fundamentally remained unchanged.

751411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
751411.value: The 2009 Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC)’s 2010-2012 Action Plan announced the twinning of 20 Chinese and 20 African universities, with the partners having a history of collaboration with Africa and China respectively. The Plan also offered short-term training for 20,000 Africans and 5,500 long-term scholarships by 2012. It pledged, in addition, several other forms of China-Africa university partnership: in science and technology, research exchange, post-doctoral support, and language development for Confucius Institutes in Africa. This research will study the rationale, character, quality and coherence of this cooperation, using the 20+20 university partnership of FOCAC as a lens. FOCAC has been operating since October 2000 as a unique Pan-African mechanism for offering aid, trade, economic cooperation and investment to Africa, as well as cooperation in human resource development (HRD). While there has been substantial research on China’s economic relations with Africa, including those covered by FOCAC, there has been little on China’s HRD cooperation. This project will address this gap through analyzing the multiple dimensions of this new China-Africa inter-university partnership, and will pay particular attention to what is delivered in China. It will address the larger questions about FOCAC’s capacity-building programme for Africa: the rationale for prioritizing the two major components of short-term and long-term training; and the selection of the China-Africa university partnership as the principal vehicle for delivering so much of China’s plans for capacity development. More generally, there is the issue of how China’s preferred discourse about the importance of south-south learning, win-win economic cooperation, mutual benefit, and people-to-people exchange squares with the fact that the 20+20 China-Africa capacity-building programme appears, in some measure, to be more of a one-way flow, from Africa to China. The research will use case study methodology with qualitative interviews, focus group interviews, participant observation, as well as quantitative and documentary data to inventory all 20 of the selected universities in China, and to investigate in more depth the experiences and perceptions of African students, trainees, teachers and researchers in a subset of 8 of the 20 universities in China, and their Chinese counterparts in the 8 partner African universities. The project, through its training, dissemination and publications, will strengthen critical awareness and analytic capacity in Hong Kong and in the Mainland on China’s current human resources policies for Africa, and will raise implications for Hong Kong’s universities of these trends in the internationalization of Mainland universities. 751911.label: Project Objectives
751911.value: The research will determine the following questions: What is the underlying objective of the doctrine of undue influence in the enforcement of contractual promises? What is the role of the consent-based theory of contract law on the intention to form contractual relations and how does its application and use affect the utility of the doctrine of undue influence? What is the role of 'wrongdoing' that is imputed to the party seeking to enforce the contract to instantiate the vitiation of the contract and what is its doctrinal relationship to the consent-based theory underlying contract law? What is the role of culture and cultural forces in the application of the doctrine of undue influence? How does the court account for the cultural values that affect the application of the doctrine and what are the implications of the (mis)uses of the doctrine for the legal enforcement of contracts in Asia? Particularly, what is the impact of the doctrine's failure to account for cultural factors affecting the circumstances of entry into the contract, on bank guarantee contracts where family or friends pose as guarantors for the borrower? In light of the comparison of the approaches of different Asian jurisdictions and those of courts in the United Kingdom and Australia where cultural factors have been considered, what recommendations can be made for a due account of cultural considerations in the context of undue influence claims to ensure better alignment between the original objectives of the doctrine and its current applications by the courts? What are the implications of these findings for the receptivity of legal transplants in Asia in contract law.

751911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
751911.value: Numerous factors, such as the history of colonialism, the political environment and culture of a country, affect the nature and structure of its legal system as well as the viability of legal transplants. This study concerns itself with the reception and development of contract law principles in post-colonial states. Generally, the body of common law received in post-colonial states has already defined the applicable principles of contract law. However, numerous factors have affected the development of the transplanted maxims of common law in various Asian contexts. The family business model common among Asian enterprises continues to present unique challenges to the doctrinal underpinnings of contract law. Despite routine engagement in tansnational economic activity, very little work has been done on the receptivity of legal transplants pertaining to the enforcement of contracts in the Asian context. One of the main goals of contract law is to protect the freedom to contract and provide certainty. However, in some instances, when the law perceives there has been some wrongdoing in the procurement of the contract, legal enforcement of contracts is not possible, indicating the law's disapproval of the contractual arrangement. Here, the law applies the equitable doctrine of undue influence, which has the effect of releasing the party wronged from its obligations under a contract. The doctrine, essential to protect vulnerable parties, has produced some anomalous results in the Asian context, raising questions about the viability of the transplant. The proposed research aims to review the legal transplantation of the doctrine of undue influence in a selection of post-colonial countries in a comprehensive and systemic manner. This will entail a quantitative and qualitative study of the factors that affect the receptivity, entrenchment and effectiveness of the legal transplant. The research will draw on decided cases in these jurisdictions over a twenty-year period to track the doctrine's application and development. A comparative analysis with judgments from the United Kingdom and Australia where the doctrine was relied on to avoid contractual obligations for cultural or religious reasons will be conducted. Through a qualitative and comparative analysis and a close examination of the judgments, the research aims to gain a detailed understanding of factors which affect successful legal transplantation of the doctrine of undue influence to ensure better protection for vulnerable parties. The study will also produce important lessons for the viability of transplants in other areas of law. 一個後殖民國家的殖民歷史、政治氣候及文化背景，不但影響法律體制的結構，亦同時影響他國的法律能否「移植」到當地；此研究旨 在探討後殖民國家如何應用及發展他國的法律原則。 一般而言，後殖民國家行使的普通法，均已界定合約法的適用原則。不過，在亞洲，部分後殖民國家能否應用及發展他國的普通法原 則，均受不同因素影響。舉例說，亞洲人常用家族模式經營生意，便往往令合約法的基本精神備受重大考驗。在現今社會，跨國經濟活動多涉及商 業協定，卻鮮有研究觸及亞洲的後殖民國家，如何應用及實踐他國的法律原則。 合約法主要保障各方能夠自由訂立合約，並確立合約具有法律效力。不過，只要法律認定訂立合約的過程有差錯，合約便失去效力，並 不再受法律認可。此時，法律便會應用衡平原則，即出錯一方因受「不正當影響」，而獲免除履行合約的責任。衡平原則原意是保障弱勢的一方， 卻在亞洲引來不良的後果，令人懷疑法律原則應用到他國的可行性。 此研究將以數個後殖民國家作為研究對象，仔細及全面了解這些國家如何應用他國的衡平原則，並進行量化及質化研究，分析不同因素 如何影響這些後殖民國家應用他國的法律原則，以及這些法律原則在該國所發揮的效力。研究會參考這些後殖民國家於二十年期內的案例，以追蹤 衡平原則的應用情況及發展里程。另外，由於英國及澳洲均採用相同原則，以避免文化及宗教等因素導致各方須履行合約；研究亦會比較分析兩國 的相關判決。 此研究透過質化、比較及案例分析，深入了解衡平法則成功「移植」到後殖民國的關鍵要素。此外，在檢視其他法律原則能否「移植」 到他國時，此研究亦可作為一項重要參考。

751911.label: Realisation of objectives
751911.value: The objectives outlined have been achieved to a significant degree. Beginning with the first, an inquiry into the broader questions surrounding contract law and doctrine through a deep inquiry into the historical overview of contract law and its development and the underlying principles from a multidisciplinary lens was conducted. This fed into the development of an overarching perspective on the underlying objective of the doctrine of undue influence itself which could be viewed against the broader goals of the field of contract law. The second objective which aimed to assess more closely some of the features of modern contract doctrine insofar as they protect principles such as the freedom of contract, individual autonomy and market liberalism within the boundaries delimited by other goals of the legal system, such as not to be complicit in being used as a vehicle or front for illegality, and other reprehensible conduct, including fraud, misrepresentation, undue influence, duress, etc. To that end, the research delved into a comparative analysis of the boundaries between the different vitiating doctrines such as duress or undue influence or misrepresentation, which have similar roots in terms of applied overt or implicit pressure or other improper act or omission to achieve a contract, to get to the heart of contract law's use of such doctrines to mitigate against the enforcement of agreements that it would be unfair to enforce given these circumstances. This was done by looking at how different common law jurisdictions had been applying the undue influence doctrine and examining the jurisprudence to identify articulated factors which serve as flash points for consideration of the question of enforcement or vitiation of the contract. For example, Australian courts have preferred the application of the doctrine of good faith or the use of the doctrine of unconscionability to justify the outcomes in particular cases on the realisation that the doctrine of undue influence has moved beyond its original purpose which sought to defend vulnerable parties against unscrupulous persons who were in a position of trust and confidence to take advantage of their vulnerability by exercising some influence which the court characterised as 'undue' in the circumstances. In this manner, the third objective of identifying features which determine the presence or absence of consent or wrongdoing to make sense of fact patterns which triggered a successfully mounted defence of undue influence as opposed to those that did not, was achieved by compiling a table for each jurisdiction which was the subject of study under the scope of this project. This facilitated comparisons between factual distinctions which allowed diluted versions of consent or wrongdoing to be satisfactorily proved in certain instances to allow the courts to achieve 'just' outcomes or alternatively, the 'thick' interpretations of consent or wrongdoing which were applied to uphold the contract on the basis that on the facts, there was nothing which raised any reason for additional scrutiny. At this juncture, the research material was developed into an interpretive analytical framework mapping fact patterns onto factors identified as fulfilling or failing to meet the established criteria for the application of the doctrine and the corresponding judgment in the case. The fourth and fifth objectives which focused on examining the role that culture played, if any, in the determination of UI cases being decided in select Asian jurisdictions were achieved. The analysis of these cases was conducted and a comparison of how such cases play out where immigrants from Asian jurisdictions live in and are governed by 'foreign' principles such as UI was made. In achieving its seventh and final objective, the PI assessed and evaluated the impact of the failure to adequately account for cultural forces in the framing of the UI inquiry on parties' freedom of contract, the bank's services and role, the role of the courts and the legal system more broadly as a protective arm and the implications this had for certainty, predictability, rule of law, substantive justice and socioeconomic considerations that are germane to an international financial centre and its future. primary critique that given that the underlying purpose of the UI doctrine (absence of consent or tainting of consent as a result of a party's abuse of trust and confidence reposed in them), in a cultural and social context within which decisions are not necessarily based on 'consent' exercised by an autonomous legal subject but rather, on power dynamics, relational considerations or social hierarchies, attempts to frame these extraneous, non-commercial considerations within existing frames of analysis lead to a distortion of the issues and more crucially, undermine the original purpose of the UI which was to protect vulnerable parties against unfair bargains. It appears that the courts are inconsistent and ill-equipped to deal with cultural and social factors emanating from personal value systems which have a bearing on their contractual dealings. This, in turn, has significant implications for predictability, certainty, equality and the rule of law but more importantly, for prospects of substantive justice for vulnerable parties. In achieving its seventh and final objective, the project research has led to the conclusion that the failure to adequately account for cultural forces in the framing of the UI inquiry leads to putting banks in a precarious position in terms of the effectiveness of the guarantee contract as a viable legal instrument to protect itself against defaulting debtors. At the same time, however, an overly protective court may lead to banks concluding they do not wish to deal with particular groups and therefore, narrow the class of people fit to stand as guarantors. This may have an unduly negative effect on sureties from minority backgrounds and would be an unwarranted restraint on their freedom of contract and a deprivation of their prospects for socioeconomic mobility. This is an undesirable position for any free market economy that is committed to the rule of law and serves as an international financial centre to be in. One of the promised deliverables (3 international journal publications) has not been met. Three articles have been written, two of which have been submitted to international peer reviewed journals but pending outcome whilst a third has been substantially developed but is yet to be submitted to a journal. These have been published as Occasional Papers online. The delayed output is due in large part due to a pregnancy and complicated childbirth and recovery process, which intervened during the project period. I am also the Director of the Centre for Comparative and Public Law in office since 2013, overlapping with the project period. The CCPL is very vibrant and has held 137 events between 2014-2016, including numerous other activities, publications, grants and research assistants that have been managed at CCPL under my Directorship, keeping me heavily occupied. I have however, published two significant research reports relating to my work on ethnic minorities which feeds into this work on legal transplants: 1. The Status of Ethnic Minorities in Hong Kong 1997-2014, September 2015, the first Report of its kind presenting an evidence based, comprehensive review and analysis of the situation of ethnic minorities in Hong Kong across various areas of life, including discrimination, citizenship, education, employment, poverty, family and domestic violence and health, crime and law enforcement. 2. Delivering on the Promise of Equal Protection Under the Law.

751911.label: Major findings and research outcome
751911.value: The project makes a significant contribution to the discourse by outlining the core values of the legal system and the operation of the rule of law framework within a multicultural and globalised setting and articulating the urgent need to examine the impact of legal transplants in various contexts to reevaluate the workings of key principles to ensure they align with the broader goals of justice but also of a society's financial and economic vision in a manner that facilitates human flourishing for all. The findings show that the legal doctrines applied are not value neutral and that as they advocate particular values, there is a need to consider how those from outside the prevalent legal normative framework experience these norms and whether they serve equally especially where the law serves a protective function or as a vehicle to enforce rights and interests. The research has led to the development of a core interpretive framework to identify the different ways in which the formal inquiry into the relevant factors might be adapted to apply a more sophisticated lens incorporating a more complex model of inquiry to ensure that relevant contextual factors inform the juridical inquiry. Finally, the research has led to the development of key recommendations for courts in the consideration of cultural and contextual factors in decision-making in undue influence cases, and banks in developing better practices to ensure that the broader goals of economic prosperity, innovation and entrepreneurship are met with a healthy dose of due diligence to ensure contractual propriety and full knowledge of the relevant circumstances within which the guarantee contract was concluded so that it can withstand the court's scrutiny in such circumstances. This work, in turn, has opened up areas of inquiry in relation to the viability of legal transplants in post-colonial states in other areas of contract law. A deeper engagement incorporating an interdisciplinary lens to better understand and predict the behaviour of, and ultimately, the usefulness of legal transplants is needed. It has also foreshadowed the more important question of studying the evolving behaviour of legal transplants as they interact with the soil within which they are sown to take root. The following outcomes have been achieved: 1. International conference paper presenting the research 2. Three Occasional Papers 3. Two Journal Articles submitted to International Peer Review Journals 4. Mentoring 2 students to develop their research in this area

751911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
751911.value: The research findings and outcomes show significant potential for further development of this work. In particular, the inquiry into the multi-level transplantation occurring in legal transplantation identified through the research would prove groundbreaking as an area of in depth study determining how transplants evolve, take root and present themselves in their 'rooted' environments. This research also has potential to lead to the identification of cultural, social, political and other forces at work in ensuring successful transplantation where desirable and enable appropriate conditions to be created to work towards such a goal. This is of increasing importance as the Asian region remains the only one thus far free from regional harmonisation of economic, legal or other norms under a regional treaty framework to advance goals particular to this part of the world. There has been little to no groundwork done on understanding the process of norm harmonisation in culturally and politically diverse regions. This kind of work would make a significant contribution to theory and practice in the field. The findings will be used to develop a research proposal to study specifically intercultural transplants in the region in specific areas of law, such as domestic violence and children's rights.

751911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
751911.value: This research used an interdisciplinary approach to understand and evaluate judicial decision making in cases where sureties standing as guarantors sought to set aside guarantee agreements on grounds of undue influence. Examining the underlying objectives of law in general and contract law in particular, the research found that doctrines such as undue influence were developed to operate on the basis that contractual fundamentals such as freedom of contract, consent to a transaction and the absence of wrongdoing were upheld as core to the transaction's validity. However, in settings where sureties stood as guarantors for persons with whom they shared a relationship of trust and confidence, it emerged that there were particular applications of undue influence in cases involving legal transplants in Asia or as a result of immigrants' own value frameworks impacting the process of entering into contracts, which were not accounted for by contract theory. The findings show that the doctrine fails to account for non-commercial, extraneous factors that may be operative in the decision to enter into contract. Analysing the implications of this legal gap, this research presents tools for a complex interpretive analysis which incorporates culturally relevant considerations in jurisprudence in cross-cultural contexts such as Asia.

751911.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
751911.value: This research led to the discovery that ethnic minority residents in Hong Kong were having difficulties in securing banking facilities in Hong Kong. The PI partnered with an NGO, Hong Kong Unison, which services ethnic minority clients to assist them in seeking equal access to banking services with a view to better understanding the basis for differential treatment by the banks. This inquiry led to discussions with the Hong Kong Equal Opportunities Commission and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to determine the interaction between measures put into place to guard against banks in financial cities like Hong Kong being used as a base for money-laundering or funding terrorist activities. This led to a fruitful dialogue among some of the banks involved and presently, additional information is being sought from banks and the HKMA to clarify the guidelines in relation to these required international measures for financial risk management against crime syndicates and terrorists and how they may have a disparate impact on particular minority groups due the lack of a contextualised understanding of how to apply the guide or the rules on the frontline and internally. It is hoped that this dialogue will facilitate greater accountability and transparency in understanding the considerations applied by banks and their personnel in dealing with ethnic minorities in Hong Kong.

752011.label: Project Title(Chinese)
752011.value: 傳染性經濟：瘟疫與帝國危機

752011.label: Project Objectives
752011.value: To investigate how government officials sought to manage the plague in two colonial port cities (Hong Kong and Bombay) by restricting the movement of labour and closing down the pathways of infection, even as they strove to keep open the circulations of capital and commodities. To promote an understanding of how - and to what degree - commentators and bureaucratic elites interpreted the plague epidemics in Asia as both an economic and a health crisis. To re-contextualize the plague ‘pandemic’ within a number of economic debates, including: ‘free trade’ and concerns about the outflow of capital from the metropole to the colonies, the growing gulf between production and consumption, and the socially and politically destabilizing impact of international capital. To examine the manner in which epidemic episodes foregrounded intersecting and often competing discourses of mobility - economic, social, racial, and pathological - which in turn highlighted an imperial crisis of government. 752011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
752011.value: Focusing on responses to plague epidemics in Hong Kong and Bombay (Mumbai) between 1894 and 1914, this project will investigate how British imperial and colonial public health concerns became intertwined with economic debates about ‘free trade’, ‘fair trade’ and the priorities of New Imperialism. In so doing, the research will contribute to our understanding of the ways in which epidemics have been interpreted in the past, providing a much-needed historical context for the framing of contemporary epidemic episodes. Some 13 million people perished in the 'Third Plague Pandemic', which disrupted imperial networks and threatened the movement of labour, commodities and capital. In the words of the Governor of Hong Kong, Sir William Robinson, it was “an unexampled calamity” (1894: 730). The disease diffused westwards from China along trading networks, revealing the scope of global interconnectedness. Against this background, the project will examine how and why plague epidemics from the 1890s were understood by commentators and colonial bureaucrats in terms of a systemic crisis that revealed underlying weaknesses of empire, thereby prompting new measures and tools of governance. Most studies of the plague have concentrated on the socio-political consequences of the colonial state’s strategies to contain infection, or on the demographic impacts of disease. No monograph exists which investigates public health responses to the plague in relation to economic debates over tariff reform and the politico-economic arrangements of Britain’s Asian empire. In addressing this neglected but critical theme, the project has two aims: firstly, to compare official responses to the plague in two major colonial cities, exploring tensions in policy between a conviction in the indispensability of free circulation and fears about the threats such circulation posed to imperial cohesion. Secondly, to analyze debates among commentators and bureaucratic elites, in order to demonstrate how disparate events were constructed as a ‘crisis’ that served to underscore the interrelations between health, economic efficiency and wealth. The project will address such issues as the extent to which economic assumptions determined public health approaches, and the ways that public health models, increasingly based on a new microbial understanding of epidemic disease, impacted upon economic interpretations. The resulting monograph and article will explore the ‘pandemic’, not simply as a catastrophic biological event, but as a culturally produced ‘crisis’ - at once local and transnational - that framed socio-economic and political relations, thereby providing crucial insights into the ideological assumptions that shape, underpin and drive policy. 傳染性經濟：瘟疫與帝國危機 這項目的研究焦點放在1894至1914年間，香港和孟買對抗瘟疫蔓延的措施。項目將研究大英帝國和其殖民地對公共衛生的關注怎樣與「自由貿易」、「公平貿易」的經濟議題以及新帝國主義的優先次序相提並論。本研究有助我們了解流行病在過去如何被解讀，並提供所需的歷史背景，為當代流行病訂下框架。 「第三次鼠疫大流行」導致約 1千3百萬人喪生，破壞帝國的網絡，威脅勞動市場、商品和資本的流動力。按當時的香港總督威廉羅賓遜（William Robinson）的說法，這是一個「空前的災難」。疫症從貿易網絡，由中國向西擴散，揭示了全球互相聯繫的緊密程度。在這背景下，本項目將調查評論家和殖民官僚怎樣從系統性危機的角度，理解自1890年代起的瘟疫，及箇中原因。這理解揭示了帝國潛在的弱點，從而促使新的治理措施和手段。 大部份的瘟疫研究都是將重點放於殖民政府在遏制感染的過程中，所引致的社會政治後果，或是集中在疾病對人口統計的影響。本項目集中研究一個重要卻被忽略的主題：鼠疫下，公共衛生措施相對於改革關稅這經濟議題的關係，以及衛生措施對在英國統治下的亞洲地區的政治經濟安排的關係。項目目的有兩個：第一，比較兩大殖民城市中，官員對疫症的反應，藉此探索政策之間的矛盾關係：一方面堅信自由流通不可或缺， 另一方面則恐怕自由流通會影響帝國的凝聚力。 第二，分析評論家和官僚精英之間的爭論，展示不同的事件如何被解構成「危機」，突顯衛生、經濟效率和財富之間的相互關係。本項目將探討在多大程度上公共衛生策略取決於經濟假設，以及經濟學的分釋如何受公共衛生模式 （這模式逐漸建立於對流行病的新理解──從微生物角度認識流行病）影響。 研究所得的論文將探討「大流行」：「大流行」不單只是災難性的生物事件，亦是一個文化出產的本土及跨國「危機」，為社會經濟和政治關係訂下框架，從而對各種推動政策的意識形態假設，提出重要的見解。

752011.label: Realisation of objectives
752011.value: The project 'Infective Economies: Plague and the Crisis of Empire' has shed new light on critical aspects of the Third Plague Pandemic across sites in Asia. All of the objectives set out in the original application have been achieved. Peer reviews have recognised the originality of approach, the innovative argument presented, and the research's impressive grounding in the archives. Specifically, in terms of the original objectives, the project has brought a new focus on the deployment of novel technologies to manage the plague (including the use of photography) and the countervailing effects of colonial state interventions. It has explored the ways in which plague epidemics were interpreted as economic/health crises and, in addition, shown the extent to which such interpretations fed back into policy with consequences for the evolving situation 'on the ground.' A key component of the project has involved tracking the Third Plague Pandemic in relation to broader contemporaneous economic debates about 'free trade' and empire. Here, the project has provided a wholly new vantage. The project has also contributed, theoretically, to mobility studies, showing how different kinds of mobility interrelated. It has further demonstrated the ways in which epidemics are compounded biological, social, and economic events. In short, in achieving the six original objectives, 'Infective Economies' has broken new ground and provided an original comparative analysis of this critical historical event.

752011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
752011.value: ‘Infective Economies’ provides a fresh perspective on the history of the Third Plague Pandemic, a catastrophic event that is estimated to have killed 15 million people worldwide. Adopting a comparative approach, the project investigates colonial responses to the plague in two major trading hubs of the British Empire: Hong Kong and Bombay. Drawing on extensive archival material, it demonstrates how anxieties about the diffusion of disease became intertwined with economic concerns about disruptions to trade. This is the first study to show how economic and public health preoccupations converged on the dangers of infective flows. It illustrates how economic and public health discourses were co-produced, as well as the extent to which the crisis was instrumental in promoting new forms of trans-colonial cooperation. While the project represents a substantial contribution to existing literature on the bubonic plague, its significance and value extend beyond this. ‘Infective Economies’ develops a novel theoretical framework within which to elucidate pandemic crises. The research suggests that responses to adverse events are determined by a pre-history of crises, with the present analogized in relation to the past. These insights are of particular relevance to the present, given current pandemic concerns across Asia.

752011.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
752011.value: In 2014, I received an HKU Faculty of Arts Award in recognition of the quality and impact of my research over the last three years. Aside from a single-authored book, two book chapters, and two papers in a top-ranked peer reviewed journal, my GRF project ‘Infective Economies: Plague and the Crisis of Empire’ has had a number of other significant impacts in relation to the creation of a dynamic research environment through collaborations with top-tier international institutions and the wider social impact of research in the community. Impacts include: 1) University of Cambridge Research Collaboration The RGC-funded project on the Third Plague Pandemic has led to a research collaboration with the University of Cambridge’s Centre for Research in the Arts, Social Sciences and Humanities (CRASSH), specifically through the interdisciplinary research project ‘Visual Representations of the Third Plague Pandemic.’ This project aims to collect and analyse photographs and other visual documents relating to the third plague pandemic from 1855 to 1959. Archival material from the University of Hong Kong’s special collections has been integrated into the database and in December 2014 I participated in the workshop at Cambridge ‘Plague and the City: Disease, Epidemic Control and the Urban Environment’ (5-6 December 2014) where I gave a keynote speech entitled ‘Plagued in Hong Kong: Disease in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction.’ The aim is to further develop these collaborative research initiatives with an annual Hong Kong-Cambridge research event focused on the history of zoonotic diseases in Asia. London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine Research Collaboration 2) The plague project has led to the development of research ties with colleagues at the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) who have a particular interest in infectious disease in Hong Kong and China. In December 2013, a Memorandum of Agreement was signed between the Centre for the Humanities and Medicine (which I co-direct), the School of Public Health at HKU and the LSHTM. My GRF project ‘Infective Economies’ has provided the impetus for developing collaborative research ties between both institutions. In 2015, a PhD student of mine is spending time at LSHTM’s International Diagnostics Centre as a Visiting Scholar (working on the history of dengue epidemics in Asia) and I will also spend time at LSHTM as honorary faculty with a view to furthering the collaboration. King's College London Research Collaboration 3) The RGC-funded project has given rise to a collaboration with King’s College London and specifically to a project that investigates the role of nurses in the Third Plague Pandemic. I am co-supervising a PhD under the joint HKU-KCL PhD programme (with Professor Anne Marie Rafferty) of a student working on nursing and the plague in Hong Kong and Cape Town between 1894 and 1900. University of Exeter Research Collaboration 4) The project has also led to a developing collaboration with the University of Exeter’s Centre for Medical History. I am currently co-supervising a PhD student on the history of infectious disease in Asia with colleagues at Exeter. I am also collaborating with my colleague Professor Mark Jackson at CMH on The Routledge History of Disease, contributing a chapter on the history of epidemics in Asia. Knowledge Exchange and Public Forum 5) The GRF-funded project has led to the creation of an online platform, which focuses on the history of infectious diseases and epidemics, and makes the plague research available to fellow researchers, as well as to the broader community (www.ghdm.hku.hk). The aim is ultimately to build a searchable database and furnish an interactive space for those working on the Third Plague Pandemic and other comparative epidemics in Asia. The Global Histories of Disease and Medicine website will have significant societal impact and extend the reach of our research findings to the public. Press and Media Coverage 6) The GRF project has also led to press and media coverage, including a special report for which I was interviewed in the South China Morning Post to mark the 120th anniversary of the Hong Kong plague outbreak (‘When death came calling: how the plague swept through Hong Kong,’ SCMP, 22 June 2014).

752211.label: Realisation of objectives
752211.value: The aim of this project was to develop a valid and reliable scale that could identify surgeon trainees who have psychomotor and/or decision-making skills that tend to be disrupted by common surgery-related stressors. Using the well-researched concept of reinvestment from the motor learning and sports science literature, we first examined the role of movement specific reinvestment in psychomotor skills performance of surgeons in training (Objective 1). Having established that an individual’s propensity to reinvest tends to impact surgery skills performance, the items from the previously validated MSRS and DSRS were modified to specifically suit a surgery context (Objective 2). For example, the item from the MSRS “I reflect about my movement a lot” was modified to “I reflect about my surgical technique a lot” and the item from the DSRS “When I am reminded about poor decisions I have made in the past, I feel as if they are happening all over again” was modified to “When I am reminded about poor decisions I have made in the OT in the past, I feel as if they are happening all over again”. To establish face validity (Objective 3), the scales with modified items were presented to a panel of experienced surgical educators for their input regarding the comprehensiveness and appropriateness of the scale. As per the panel’s recommendations, additional items were included in both the MSRS and DSRS, which were deemed more appropriate to a surgical context than the original items. It was further recommended that separate scales for the psychomotor and decision-making aspects of surgery be developed, due to the (1) unique nature of each of these components and (2) concern about the lengthiness of a combined scale. Consequently, all further analysis was conducted for two separate scales. Given that the surgery-specific scales used items from previously validated scales (i.e., MSRS and DSRS), it was deemed unnecessary to run an exploratory factor analysis, and construct validity was established using confirmatory factor analysis (Objective 3). Predictive validity (Objective 4) was evaluated in relation to performances in an objective structured clinical exam (OSCE). The surgery-specific decision-making scale did not predict decision-making skills, but the movement specific scale component did predict laparoscopic task performance. This suggests the direction of future work that will continue to expand this area of research. It is also noted that a request for change of PI was made due to staff changes, just prior to the final six months of the project. Approval of the request was received three months prior to the end date of the project. Consequently, a six-month extension was requested by the replacement PI, during which the final objective of the study was realised.

752211.label: Major findings and research outcome
752211.value: The propensity to monitor and control movements (i.e., measured by the MSRS) has been shown to affect performance in normal and movement disordered populations. Similarly, monitoring and controlling the decision-making process as well as ruminating on previous poor decisions (i.e., measured by the DSRS), have been shown to affect performance on decision making tasks. Applying the said concepts in the context of surgeons in training, this research established that surgeons in training, with a high individual propensity to reinvest displayed less capability (than low reinvestors) to meet the demands imposed by time pressure during a laparoscopic task (Malhotra, Poolton, Wilson, Ngo, & Masters, 2012). Specifically, low reinvestors performed significantly faster when under time pressure, whereas high reinvestors showed no change in performance. Low reinvestors also tended to display greater performance efficiency (shorter path lengths, fewer hand movements) than high reinvestors. Furthermore, this research found that the two constructs of movement specific reinvestment have unique effects on surgical skills performance. Those with a higher propensity for movement self-consciousness (MS-C) tended to have slower performance times on novel and well-practiced laparoscopic tasks (Malhotra, Poolton, Wilson, Fan, & Masters, 2014). For complex surgical techniques, conscious motor processing (CMP) played a more influential role in performance than MS-C. When examined in relation to a more challenging condition of an OSCE, those with a higher propensity for CMP displayed faster rates of learning a laparoscopic skill (Malhotra, Poolton, Wilson, Leung, Zhu, Fan, & Masters, 2015). The differential roles of MS-C and CMP in psychomotor performance were further verified in a related study using a complex motor skill (i.e., golf putting), wherein MS-C and CMP were found to influence performance at different stages of practice (Malhotra, Poolton, Wilson, Omuro, & Masters, 2015). The development of surgery-specific versions of the MSRS and DSRS in this project has been evidence-based, on account of the major findings reported thus far. Construct and predictive validity was subsequently tested (Malhotra, Poolton, Capio, Fan, & Masters, 2015). Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) for the surgery-specific MSRS revealed an acceptable absolute fit (GFI= 0.94, RMSEA = 0.05, SRMR =0.06) and an acceptable relative fit (CFI = 0.96), meeting the criteria recommended by Hu and Bentler (1999). CFA for the surgery specific DSRS similarly revealed an acceptable absolute fit (GFI=0.87, RMSEA=0.09, SRMR=0.09) and relative fit (CFI=0.09). Predictive validity of the scales revealed that lower scores on the MS-C factor of the surgery-specific MSRS in particular, were associated with worse performance on a suturing task under pressure during OSCE (r=.42, p=.01). Scores on the surgery-specific DSRS did not predict decision-making performance under pressure.

752211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
752211.value: This research led to the development of surgery-specific MSRS and DSRS. We sufficiently established face and construct validity, while predictive validity has been shown only for the surgery-specific MSRS. Predictive validity was tested among medical students attending a practical exam (i.e., OSCE). We note that it is possible that the OSCE environment was not stressful enough to induce decision reinvestment or decision rumination processes captured by the DSRS. Although the OSCE has been shown to raise levels of anxiety, it cannot be likened to performance pressure in real-world settings, in which the consequences of a mistake could be fatal. Therefore, future research will aim to examine the association between surgeons’ scores on the surgery-specific scales, and their psychomotor and decision-making skills performance in the operating theatre where intra-operative stressors are ubiquitous (e.g., time pressure, distractions, evaluation apprehension). Other directions for further development would include applications in dental surgeon training, thereby expanding the utility of the surgery-specific scales. Members of the research team had begun to explore collaborative work with dental surgeon educators.

752211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
752211.value: Research from human performance domains, such as sport, has revealed that an individual’s propensity for conscious monitoring and control of movements (i.e., measured by the movement specific reinvestment scale; MSRS) and conscious monitoring and control of decisions (i.e., measured by the decision-specific reinvestment scale; DSRS) can impact performance under pressure. This research aimed to develop surgery-specific versions of the reinvestment scales to contribute towards identifying surgeons and surgical trainees that are more likely to experience performance changes under pressure. The findings suggest that surgeons in training who have a higher tendency for conscious monitoring and control of movements are less capable of adapting their laparoscopic skill to time pressured situations. Furthermore, trainees who have a higher tendency for conscious control appear less able to transfer their skills to the performance of new, more complex surgical techniques. However, a higher tendency for conscious control was associated with faster rates of laparoscopic skill learning. The research indicates the importance of considering personality and individual differences when designing surgical training programs or appraising the capability of a surgical trainee. Bespoke training design could potentially result in the more effective development of competent surgeons who are able to manage the inherent pressures associated with their tasks.

752911.label: Project Objectives
752911.value: Adopt a more holistic approach to the study of Godden's writing by making religion a central as opposed to peripheral category of inquiry into her work. Explore how Godden's hybrid and migratory identity as a British-Indian gave rise to a deep interest in different religions and to a spirit of pilgrimage inspired by Krishna's words in the Bhagavad-Gita: "however men approach me, even so do I welcome them, for the path men take from every side leads to me." Investigate the writers and mentors who influenced her literary and religious formation or whose ideas inspired individual books. Examine how Godden's exploratory interests in different religions and spiritual traditions, in women's religious life and practices, and in the psychic drama of interiority make themselves felt throughout her writing. Consider how these religious interests affect her representation of the subjects that have received significant critical attention such as childhood, women's social circumstances, and colonial India, and how these subjects, in turn, form, alter or transform her religious consciousness. Produce a monograph on Rumer Godden.

752911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
752911.value: Rumer Godden was a prolific and versatile writer who published sixty books from 1935 to 1997. Her life spanned the twentieth century and her writing evolved from a British colonial life that would vanish after India gained independence in 1947. The transient and migratory pattern of British-Indian identity made Godden a pilgrim who not only moved across genres like autobiography and fiction, adult and children's literature, but also travelled across country borders, cultures, and religions. Despite her postwar popularity, Godden has only recently become the subject of greater critical attention with the development of postcolonial studies and the growing interest in life writing, empire histories, and modern women writers marginalized as middlebrow. However the scholars who are now investigating her work tend to focus on two recurrent subjects: the passage from childhood to adulthood and the passing of Anglo-India. They disregard the fact that Godden had "always been deeply interested in religion" and do not consider how a subject of such personal importance might have influenced her writing. This is a serious critical oversight. It means that three significant novels, Black Narcissus, In This House of Brede, and Five for Sorrow, Ten for Joy, have not been studied closely for their insight into religious life or a spirituality pointing East and West. Moreover it overlooks Godden's acculturation to the sacred stories and landscapes of India and her lifelong search for "something, far beyond myself to hold to. For a long time I thought it would be Hinduism." Finally it discounts the Christian roots of life writing in spiritual autobiography and narratives of conversion. Godden's own conversion experience took her from a Quaker and High-Anglican family background to an unorthodox Catholicism that in her mind did not "shut out being a Hindu" or exclude "Muslims, Buddhists, Zoroastrians" as fellow pilgrims. In this project I hope to achieve a more holistic study of Godden's life work by considering how her respect for India's long tradition of religious pluralism and her perception of spirituality as an inner journey leading East and West are manifest in her writing; how her interests in religion, childhood, women's life experiences, and colonial India are inter-related; and how her work as a whole honors the Indian axiom: "Everyone is a house with four rooms, a physical, a mental, an emotional and a spiritual. ... Unless we go into every room everyday ... we are not a complete person."

752911.label: Realisation of objectives
752911.value: Last July I explored the Rumer Godden collection at Boston University library and found valuable primary source material central to this project. I had been feeling under par for some time but was taken seriously ill at the end of this trip and on immediate return to Hong Kong was diagnosed with cancer. I was operated on and have been undergoing aggressive chemotherapy since then. Though I have not been able to do any serious work and have had to focus my energies on getting through treatment, I was pleased that Veiled Desires, the book funded by my previous GRF, was published in August 2013 and began to receive excellent reviews. I am expecting an influential review to appear shortly in the widely read American paper, The National Catholic Reporter. Should the panel wish to see this review, I will be happy to forward it.
