753211.label: Project Title(Chinese)
753211.value: 抓住物件時對三維形狀的視覺處理

753211.label: Project Objectives
753211.value: Test the accuracy of grasp points when the amount of visual information is varied. Test the relative contributions of binocular and monocular shape cues for selection of grasp points. Compare perceptual judgments of 3D shape to performance of a visual-motor task that depends on the 3D shape of an object.
rows: Test the accuracy of grasp points when the amount of visual information is varied.
Test the relative contributions of binocular and monocular shape cues for selection of grasp points.
Compare perceptual judgments of 3D shape to performance of a visual-motor task that depends on the 3D shape of an object.

753211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
753211.value: Grasping an object is common behavior that requires sophisticated visual processing of 3D shape. When picking up an object with precision grip, we unconsciously select appropriate contact points for the fingers that would produce a stable grip. Determining these stable grasp points for a novel object based on visual information is a challenging problem, yet this is something that our brain accomplishes on a daily basis. The proposed studies will investigate how visual cues to 3D shape contribute to selection of grasp points. Specifically, I will test whether some effects observed for perceptual judgments of 3D shape are also evident in grasping. Perceptual judgments of 3D shape often reveal large systematic errors, particularly when limited depth information is available. Based on these observations, one might expect corresponding errors in grasp points. On the other hand, there is evidence that distinct neural processing underlies visual perception and visual control of action. Grasping might remain accurate even in conditions that produce large biases in perceptual judgments of 3D shape. I will compare perceptual judgments and grasping performance for conditions with varied amount of 3D information. Another question is the relative contribution of different 3D cues for purposes of shape perception or grasping. Perceptual studies have generally found that the visual system uses any available 3D information, and that cues are weighted according to their reliability. Use of 3D cues for grasping might be different. For example, some evidence suggests that binocular information is especially important for control of grasping. I will measure grasping performance under conditions with conflicting monocular and binocular information to test whether cues are integrated in a manner that is consistent with perceptual judgments. 抓住物件是人類的一種普遍活動，需要對目標的三維形狀作先進的視覺處理。當我們準確地抓住並提起一件物件時，我們能夠下意識地找出適合的接觸點讓手指穩定地抓住物件。找出前所未見的物件的穩定接觸點是一條具挑戰性的問題，然而，這是我們大腦每天都能夠成功處理的問題。 本建議研究將會找出有關三維形狀的視覺資料怎樣被用作找出抓住物件的接觸點。具體上，我將會測試一些三維形狀感知的判斷結果是否同樣發現於抓住物件的測試。 我們對三維形狀在感知上的判斷，特別於有限的深度資訊可用的情況下，經常都會出現很大的系統誤差。基於這點，有些人可能會認為我們在同樣的情況下抓住物件都會出現同樣的誤差。與此同時， 研究發現我們使用不同的神經處理視覺感知和視覺對於行為的控制，因此我們於某一些情況下，即使三維形狀的感知判斷存有很大的誤差，我們亦可能準確的抓住該物件。我將會於不同三維資訊的情況下，比較感知判斷和抓住物件的表現。 另一條問題是不同三維信息對於用作感知物件形狀和抓住物件分別的貢獻是多少。普遍關於感知的研究都發現我們視覺系統會使用任何可用的三維信息去感知物件，而每項信息所佔的影響力是根據其可信性而決定的。不過我們在抓住物件時使用三維信息的方法可能有所不同。例如有些研究結果提出雙眼的資訊對抓住物件的控制是特別重要。我將會於不同的情況， 包括當單眼和雙眼的資訊不一致時， 量度抓住物件的表現， 籍此去測試人類會否以感知物件相同的方式去整合不同的視覺信息。

753211.label: Realisation of objectives
753211.value: Recently reported results (APCV 2015) addressed two of the main goals: testing the role of monocular and binocular cues for control of grasping, and the relationship between perception and action. We found that both monocular and binocular slant cues affected grasping movements, in a manner that would be expected based on perceptual judgments of slant. Consistent effects were observed on both the slant of the grip axis during transport and the contact points used to grasp the objects. Unlike some previous studies that found dissociated effects on perception and action, we observed agreement between perception and grasping performance. We are preparing a manuscript reporting this work. We also tested the relationship between perception and action using a virtual grasping paradigm (VSS 2015). We used backward masking to present subliminal target objects during movements, and found that subjects responded to these targets even though they were not seen. In these conditions, there was a dissociation between conscious perception and use of visual information for control of action. We argue that backward masking differentially affects the dorsal and ventral streams due to differing temporal sensitivity. We used the virtual grasping paradigm to address a related question that was not part of the original goals. In normal conditions, grasp points could be preplanned prior to movement. We used a perturbation method to test whether the visualmotor system is capable of identifying appropriate grasp points during an ongoing movement. We found that subjects could make fast corrective adjustments in response to perturbations, demonstrating that visual shape processing for grasp point selection can occur during online control (VSS 2014, EBR 2015). The question of how visual information affects the accuracy of grasp points was only addressed in a limited way. We did find that binocular viewing leads to more accurate adjustments of the grip orientation, but we could not assess the effect on the optimality of grasp points. A difficulty is that grasp points were strongly affected by the natural orientation of the hand, and showed considerable variability even for a frontal view. Consequently, the optimality of grasp points relative to an object’s shape is not a sensitive measure of the use of visual depth cues.

753211.label: Major findings and research outcome
753211.value: Chen & Saunders (APCV 2015) tested whether visual slant cues affected grasping movements in a way consistent with the effects on slant perception. Subjects grasped slanted planar objects under monocular and binocular viewing, and with and without conflicting slant cues. We found that the slant of the grip axis was reduced in monocular conditions, consistent with underestimated slant, and grasp points shifted in a corresponding manner. For distorted objects that present conflicting slant cues, the slant of the grip axis and the grasp points were consistent with an integrated percept of slant. Another study, not yet reported, found similar results for rectangular and skew-symmetric objects. These results indicate that visual information about 3D slant is used in similar ways for perceptual judgments and control of grasping. Chen & Saunders (VSS 2014, EBR 2015) used a virtual grasping paradigm to test whether the shape of an object could be analyzed during online control for selection of grasp points. On perturbed trials, a new random grasping target was presented during an ongoing movement and subjects had to adjust their movement to touch the new target. The new target shape was only visible after movement initialization, so grasp points had to be determined online. Subjects made automatic adjustments toward appropriate grasp points, with no reduction in the optimality of final grasp points. The results demonstrate online processing of shape information for grasp point selection. Saunders & Chen (VSS 2014) extended this finding to the case of target shapes defined by illusory contours. Determining object shape from illusory contours is potentially more complex, but this did not appear to affect grasping performance. Subjects were still able to respond to shape perturbations and guide their fingers to appropriate grasp points, with no difference in optimality compared to luminance-defined targets. Chen & Saunders (VSS 2015, submitted to EBR) tested whether grasping movements can be influenced by subliminal targets. We briefly presented perturbed grasping targets during movements, and used backward masking to prevent subjects from being able to see the perturbed stimuli. Despite being unaware of these stimuli, subjects made automatic adjustments to the orientation and size of their grip. This demonstrates that online control of the hand can be driven by visual information that is not consciously perceived.

753211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
753211.value: The apparatus and methodology developed for these studies can easily be modified for follow-up studies. There has been little research on how depth cues are integrated for visualmotor control, so this remains a promising direction. Because of the time required to develop the methodology, we only tested a limited range of depth cue conditions. A straightforward extension would be to vary the available cues and their reliability. One possible extension of Chen & Saunders (2015) would be to vary the stimuli in ways that would selectively affect ventral or dorsal processing, such as using shapes defined by isoluminant contours. Another possibility would be to vary the timing of the perturbations to test whether control of grasp points is a continuous process. As part of his PhD thesis work, my student Chen Zhongting further investigated conscious vs unconscious influences on control of grasping using a paradigm in which subjects are instructed to intentionally stop their hand movement when a perturbation is detected. These results will be reported at VSS in 2016. Human grasp point selection remains an open problem. Kleinholdermann et al. (2013) recently proposed a model that was able to predict grasp points across a set of test objects. Otherwise, there has been no empirical investigation of grasp point selection. The grasp points observed for our random objects could be used to evaluate this model and compare to other possible variants.

753211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
753211.value: Previous evidence suggests that the brain has separate visual processing streams for perception and control of actions. This was a motivation for investigating the use of visual information for control of grasping movements. One set of studies measured the trajectory of fingers when reaching to pick up a slanted object and varied the visual information about 3D slant. The orientation of the hand during movements and the grasp points used to pick up the objects were affected by visual cues in a manner that is consistent with perceptual judgments of slant. This suggests that depth cues are used in a similar way for perception and control of grasping. Another set of studies used a virtual grasping task to investigate how visual information is used for online control. When a target object was unexpectedly changed during movement, subjects automatically corrected their movement to grasp the new target at appropriate points. This demonstrates that the brain can quickly analyze the shape of an object to determine grasp points. We further found that subjects adjust their movements in response to a new target even when the it cannot be seen due to visual masking, demonstrating that grasping can be influenced by unconscious stimuli.

753411.label: Project Title(Chinese)
753411.value: 廣東焰口 — 通過研究廣東焰口來理解香港人的生死觀

753411.label: Project Objectives
753411.value: To reveal, by means of an ethnographic research, how Yujia Yankou profoundly roots in the social life of the local Chinese community; To study the development of Yujia Yankou and to understand how Yujia Yankou interacts with the funeral service in Hong Kong; and To study the uniqueness of Yujia Yankou as performed in Guangdong style that differs from the mainstream of Buddhist ritual performance.
rows: To reveal, by means of an ethnographic research, how Yujia Yankou profoundly roots in the social life of the local Chinese community;
To study the development of Yujia Yankou and to understand how Yujia Yankou interacts with the funeral service in Hong Kong; and
To study the uniqueness of Yujia Yankou as performed in Guangdong style that differs from the mainstream of Buddhist ritual performance.

753411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
753411.value: The proposed project will be an ethnographic research that aims to reveal how a death ritual of Chinese Buddhism profoundly roots in the social life of local Chinese communities and interacts with the funeral service in Hong Kong. This ritual which is named as Yujia Yankou (瑜伽焰口) is mainly aimed at saving the flaming-mouth hungry ghosts. In the Chinese community, people take the matters related to death very seriously. Believing in different religions, yet Chinese people insist to find the ritual specialists to perform the death ritual for the deceased. As the presumption of Chinese people, most of them believe that ritual is an effective way to cultivate merit for the spirit of the deceased to escape from the suffering of underworld and can get rebirth in the better realms or Western Pure Land. Aside from Buddhists, those who believe in Chinese folk religion also ask for the ritual service performed by monastic Buddhists. Buddhist ritual therefore comprises an important part of the funeral services in contemporary Hong Kong. The research will try todevelop a comprehensive understanding of the development of Yujia Yankou and its future in contemporary Hong Kong. The project will be carried out in three stages: (1) to have a critical review of the historical development of the death ritual (Yujia Yankou) of Chinese Buddhism in contemporary Hong Kong. This will contribute toward the understanding of local development of both Chinese Buddhist ritual and the funeral services. This also contributes to understand how the skill of performing such ritual by the monastic Buddhists in Hong Kong; (2) to study the uniqueness of Guangdong style Yujia Yankou that differs from the mainstream of Buddhist ritual performance; (3) to have an ethnographic study of the ritual itself including the ritual procedure, its religious, cultural and social significance and meaning, and the motivations of its performers and participants. This will contribute to show the whole picture of Yujia Yankou and its significances in both religious and social aspects. 「瑜伽焰口」是佛教喪葬儀式的其中一項，其主要目的是對餓鬼進行救拔普渡，以期能藉此功德冥陽兩利。是次研究的題目為《廣東焰口研究 — 通過研究廣東焰口來理解香港人的生死觀》，希望透過研究廣東的「瑜伽焰口」，來揭示佛教的喪葬儀式如何根深蒂固地植根於本土社會文化，及其與香港殯儀服務之間的互動。在中國人的社會裡，人們在處理有關死亡事宜的問題上，都是抱著非常嚴肅、恭敬的態度。因為大部分的中國人相信，只有透過進行某些特定的宗教儀式，為亡者超度，方可令他們脫離地獄的苦難，早日往生善道，或得生西方極樂淨土。故即使宗教信仰的背景有所不同，中國人也會在先人離世後，堅持找喪葬專家，為亡者舉辦宗教喪葬儀式。 除了佛教徒外，亦有部份相信民間宗教的民眾，會尋求佛教僧侶幫忙，為先人進行佛教的喪葬儀式。因此，佛教的喪葬儀式是構成當代香港殯儀服務的一個重要部分。是項研究將嘗試為廣東「瑜伽焰口」的發展作全面的了解，及探索其在香港的現在與未來展望。 研究將分為三個階段進行： （1）回顧與批評：廣東系的「瑜伽焰口」在香港的發展歷史。此舉將有助於了解中國佛教儀式和殯儀服務在香港的發展。這也有助於了解僧侶如何施行此儀式； （2）研究廣東系的「瑜伽焰口」獨特風格； （3）探究廣東系的「瑜伽焰口」之儀式程序、它在宗教、文化、社會上的影響及其意義，同時亦會以及它的施行者及參與者的動機和意義。這將有助於展示「瑜伽焰口」儀式的全貌，及其在宗教、社會方面的影響。

753411.label: Realisation of objectives
753411.value: Objective 1 Ethnographic investigation which comprised of interviews and participant-observation, is the major method of data collection in this research. Through interviews with our key informants – the Guangdong Yankou ritual specialists and monastic masters, we are able to identify and record the historical development of a ritual that constitutes a significant part of social life in Hong Kong. During its golden age of popularity from the 1950s to 1980s, both Buddhists and non-Buddhists sought for well-being by employing the ritual as a means to accumulate merit and/or to transfer blessing. The ritual has been employed for a variety of purposes such as better childbirth, job placement, birthday, house warming, and funerary purposes. However, its popularity started to decrease since the beginning of the 1990s. In order to identify the reasons contributing to decrease in popularity, we conducted participant-observation on families during ritual performances of funerals and interviewed professionals of funerary industry and ritual specialists. Based on these data, we are able to record the latest mortuary practice in Hong Kong and to examine the Buddhist cosmology and people’s understanding, attitude, and values towards afterlife, death ritual and ritual specialists. Objective 2 In the course of research, we can confirm that Guangdong Yankou as a Buddhist death ritual is inextricably and continuously intertwined with the changing funeral industry and preferences of bereaved families. These factors in turn have contributed to the decline of the ritual. Specifically, it is partly due to the practice of the funeral industry, namely the funeral parlour, which aims to increase profit by providing one-stop funeral service and favouring other ritual of Chinese popular religion. Moreover, the secular cosmological belief and the usual practice of short funeral process curtails the customarily lengthy mourning rituals and decreases the number of occasions that Guangdong Yankou can be employed. Objective 3 Attributes unique to Guangdong Yankou in comparison with its counterparts in Mainland China and Taiwan have been documented and investigated in this project. Guangdong Yankou is distinctive in a few regards: I) the operatic chanting and hymns are conducted in Cantonese and by ritual specialists in Guangdong lineages; II) the background music has been heavily influenced by Cantonese opera; III) the performing sequence, the esoteric elements of the ritual content and the guiding ritual scripture differ from its provincial counterparts; IV) the design and motif of symbolic paraphernalia; V) the training and initiation ceremony of new presiding ritual masters; VI) the “Four Great Continents of Yuqie Yankou” is an exclusive form originated in Guangdong Yankou which adds endorsement masters for the empowerment over the ritual. For this research, the existing lineages of the ritual specialists including monastics and lay Buddhists in Hong Kong have been interviewed and recorded. In conclusion, we have achieved adequate data collections, contributed to the documentation and preservation of a distinctive yet extinctive Buddhist cultural heritage of Hong Kong and reached our project objectives.

753411.label: Major findings and research outcome
753411.value: 1) Currently Hong Kong is the only place that has preserved the unbroken lineages of monastic ritual specialists of Guangdong Yankou in Chinese Buddhism whereas the tradition in Mainland China was interrupted during Cultural Revolution. 2) Distinctive features of Guangdong Yankou are described in item 5.3 (Realisation of the objectives). 3) Guangdong Yankou was one of the most popular death rituals in Hong Kong and constituted a significant part of the religious and social life of Hong Kong from the 1950s to 1980s. Its downfall since early 1990s profoundly reflects the social change of the society in terms of the funerary practice and religious believes of the people. 4) The waning popularity of Guangdong Yankou in Hong Kong is caused by both external socio-cultural factors and internal factors of the Buddhist community. (I) External socio-economic reasons include: hectic life style in Hong Kong, commercialization of the funeral industry, usual practice of short funeral process and the secular cosmological belief; (II) Internal factors of the Buddhist community include: a critical shortage of ritual specialists, competition from other Buddhist rituals. 5) Nowadays the ritual is unknown to commoners. Bereaved families who employ “Guangdong Yankou” as death rituals in funerary occasions are mostly not for religious purposes; instead they adopt the ritual mainly due to filial piety. 6) The “Four Great Continents Yuqie Yankou” is a unique form of Guangdong Yankou of the Guangdong Buddhist tradition, its origination is inseparable from the Qingyun Monastery (慶雲寺) at Dinghu Moutain (鼎湖山) and its abbot Qihe (棲壑) in the early Qing Dynasty. 7) The current development of “Four Great Continents Yuqie Yankou” in Hong Kong is moving towards a new direction: the performing form and casting incorporate both local and provincial monastics as well as both male and female monastics in one ceremony. 8) The development of Chinese Buddhism in Hong Kong began in the early 1920s when an influx of monks and nuns came to Hong Kong from Mainland China. Apart from the Guangdong tradition, there were monastics belonging to the lineages of master Taixu (太虛) as well as the Tiantai school (天台宗). These monastics have contributed tremendously to the propagation of Chinese Buddhism in Hong Kong. 9) The Buddhist lineage of Taixu, which advocates “Humanistic Buddhism” (人間佛教) and de-emphasizes liturgy, has a subtle impact on the Chinese sangha in Hong Kong. Together with the prevalent secular atmosphere in Hong Kong, the scholastic monastics and liturgical monastics are differentiated in the sangha as the latter is considered a secondary order within the sangha. 10) Given the declining condition of Guangdong Yankou, surviving monastic specialists strive to preserve the ritual under the constraints of the monastic structure that places liturgical monastics in a secondary order of the sangha.

753411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
753411.value: The development of the Guangdong style Yuqie Yankou in Hong Kong is ongoing. There are at least two developments worth further research: 1) According to our observation the performing form of “Four Great Continents Yuqie Yankou” was transformed gradually, it incorporates both local and provincial monks and both male and female monastics due to the scarcity of local ritual adepts. Such co-performance of monks and nuns in rituals, on the one hand, is considered inappropriate and rarely appeared in the rituals in the past. Under this new trend it is worth to further investigate on how monastics break the gender boundary for the sake of preserving the ritual and the tactics they have employed. A continuous ethnographic investigation for nine to twelve months is necessary. 2) Regarding the Guangdong Buddhist sangha in Hong Kong, we find that the lineages of female liturgical monastics in Guangdong tradition is under the threat of extinction due to the severe hardship of recruiting new successors. Since female liturgical monastics are the integral part of the ritual and since Hong Kong may be the only city preserving the Guangdong lineages of female monastics that encompasses a wide range of socio-cultural and religious meanings, thorough historical documentation and investigation on their current conditions need to be carried out, the earlier the better. Due to the fact that much of the ritual is yet to be investigated, continuous observation and ethnographic research for 1 or 1.5 years deserve to be conducted in the following years.

753411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
753411.value: This ethnographic study investigates, documents and analyses the features, history, and the ups and downs of a Buddhist death ritual “Guangdong style Yuqie Yankou” in Hong Kong. The significance of the study is threefold: 1) it reports the downfall and the current predicament of “Guangdong Yankou” as an intangible cultural heritage in Hong Kong. It also researches and documents the history and particularities of the ritual at large. 2) The study reflects the social change of Hong Kong, including the accelerated pace of lifestyle, commercialization of the funeral industry, a culture of short mortuary practice by the bereaved families, and the changing cosmological belief of people in the society. 3) The study also addresses the lingering problem of the shortage of Cantonese speaking monks, particularly the ritual specialists of Guangdong tradition. With all the factors of 2) & 3) working together, the ritual is struggling to survive. Above all, this research has brought a marginalized Buddhist ritual to a more visible position of scholastic attention; it contributes to the preservation of an intangible cultural heritage in Hong Kong and the documentation of funerary culture and the social history of the people.

753911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
753911.value: 是否付出代價以採集更多的信息從而作出更加明智的決定,是統計學中一個經典的取捨問題。其最佳的解決方法表現為一種停止規則:當積累的事實足夠以某種方式支撐兩個備選方案中的一個的時候,決策者應停止收集信息;如若不然,他則應繼續。同樣的思維方式亦可應用在群體決策中。委員會審議的過程可以視為發掘信息的過程,其中便自然存在何時停止的問題。例如,在對全球變暖應對措施的商議過程中,參與國可能會尋求專家組的幫助,那麼問題便在於在採取措施之前應投入多少時間等待事實及證據的積累。 在這樣的情境下, 群體決策和個人決策的主要區別在於,在群體決策的過程中,其中一個個體意願等待的時間取決於其他成員意願。假設，個體A如果作為唯一的決策者,便會選擇等待積累更多的信息,然後再作出決定α。但如果他僅僅是一個決策群體中的一員,並且群體中存在一些耐性不足的成員,情況就會有所不同。如果A認為另一個選擇β即使在事實支撐不足的情況下亦會被通過,那麼他便可能即刻停止信息的採集,支援決定α,以免β因新信息的變動而過早地獲得通過。這種策略上的考慮提升了多重均衡甚至決策過程完全崩潰的可能。 群體決策和個人決策的另一個區別在於,在群體中,個人的決定並不總是左右群體決策的關鍵。要研究群體決策的過程,我們必須確定其中最關鍵的成員。然而,當成員們有不同的折現成本,並且對兩種備選方案有不同的偏好時,這通常是十分困難的。本課題提出了一個綜合了個體異質性及策略性互動的群體決策模型,模型中的行動者共同作出選擇——當即採取措施還是等待更多信息的採集。我們希望解決下列問題:在群體停止信息採集的決定中,策略性互動的性質(即最佳反應函數的特性)是怎樣的?在怎樣的條件下會形成決策過程崩潰的均衡?投票制度(簡單多數制或絕大多數制)對信息採集的深度以及決策成員的福利有什麼影響?

753911.label: Realisation of objectives
753911.value: We have developed a model of information acquisition that generalizes Wald's sequential analysis to a collective setting. The utility for an arbitrary agent with fixed cutoffs for adopting two alternatives can be derived from the analysis of first passage times. The Nash equilibrium requirement can be posed as a constrained maximization problem in which each agent chooses his cutoffs subject to the cutoffs chosen by others. We find that the interaction among agents can exhibit both strategic complementarity and strategic substitution. Suppose agent 1 "controls" the adoption of alternative A, and agent 2 chooses when to adopt alternative B in response. If agent 1 chooses to adopt A too early (from agent 2's perspective), then the value of waiting for agent 2 falls, and agent 2 will choose to adopt B earlier as well. This is the case of strategic complementarity--early adoption of one alternative causes early adoption of the other. But if agent 1 chooses to adopt A too late, then the value of waiting for agent 2 also falls, and agent 2 will choose to adopt B earlier. This is strategic substitution--delayed adoption of one alternative causes other agents to moderate their threshold standard for adopting the other alternative. Strategic complementarity raises the possibility of a collapse of deliberations. Suppose there is one impatient agent in the group, and the decision rule is majority rule. This impatient agent is prepared to support either A or B as long as an alternative is chosen quickly. He would be an easy target of alliance for the group that supports A as well as for the group that supports B. Each group of agents are prepared to push forward their preferred adoption threshold for fear that the other group would capture the support of the impatient agent first, and this effect is magnified by strategic complementarity. As long as there exists one very impatient agent in the group, then there always exists an equilibrium in which a decision is made with virtually no deliberation, regardless of the size of the group and their static preferences and time preferences. While we show that majority rule is fragile with respect to the presence of impatient voters, it has the advantage that the decision made always respects the static preferences of a majority of voter. Super-majority rule does not have this property, because some agents may approve an alternative merely to avoid too much delay.

753911.label: Major findings and research outcome
753911.value: The collective decision problem is a two-sided stopping problem, but we find that it can be reduced to a fixed point problem involving the solution to a more tractable one-sided stopping decision. Our working paper provides a necessary and sufficient condition that characterizes equilibrium, and show the equilibrium always exists but may not be unique. A key finding is that strategic interaction can exhibit both complementarity and substitution. Strategic substitution leads to a moderation effect, which tends to limit excessive deliberations. Strategic complementarity, on the other hand, raises the possibility of a collapse of deliberations. Majority rule is fragile to the presence of impatient voters. Its advantage is that it always produces decisions which accord with the static preferences of a majority of voters. Moreover, in a symmetric environment, majority rule is unanimously preferred by all agents to super-majority rule. When the group's decision imposes externalities on other agents, however, we may want to use super-majority rule to make sure that deliberations are longer and the resulting decisions are more accurate. The drawback of using super-majority rule is that it may produce forced consensus as agents who do not want too much delay yield to their more extreme peers. One compromise is to adopt a two-stage decision process with separate deliberation rule and decision rule. Such a process always produce decisions that accord with majority preferences, but the deliberation time may be longer. We also apply our analytical framework to shed some light on extant empirical evidence of jury decision making as well as decision making in standard setting organizations. Much of this evidence is consistent with our model. The review process has taken much more time than is expected. It has gone through three rounds of revision at the Review of Economic Studies, and we have re-submitted the paper for the fourth round of review in February 2015. We expect a final editorial decision to be made shortly.

753911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
753911.value: The research work conducted with the support of this grant lays down the theoretical foundation for studying collective decision with public information acquisition. One direction for future research is to test the implication of our model experimentally. For example, a stark prediction of the model is that one impatient agent can cause the whole group to rush to a decision under majority rule. The PI and the Co-I are investigating the possibility of exploring this implication in a laboratory setting. In the current model, agents in the group only vote to adopt a decision or vote to delay a decision. In legislative or other contexts, agents may also engage in log-rolling or even vote-buying. The possibility of making side payments to influence the decision of fellow group members raises a host of interesting issues that are worth exploring.

753911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
753911.value: Juries, boards of directors, standard-setting organizations, congressional and university committees, and government agencies such as the FDA or the EPA serve as examples of committees that spend time deliberating issues and gathering information before reaching a decision or issuing a recommendation. We present a simple model of deliberation that captures some key features of the deliberative process. We abstract from private information and concentrate on how the dynamics of information collection responds to conflicting preferences. An important aspect of this problem involves weighing the cost of obtaining additional information against the value of making more accurate decisions. At each date agents decide whether to vote to adopt one of two alternatives or continue to collect more information. The process stops when a qualified majority vote for an alternative. Three main insights emerge from our analysis. First, majority rule is more fragile than super-majority rules to impatient committee members. Second, more diverse preferences, more consensual deliberation rules, or more unanimous decision voting rules lead to lengthier deliberation and more accurate decisions. Last, balanced committees unanimously prefer to delegate deliberation power to a moderate chairman rather than be governed by a deliberation rule such as unanimity.

754511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
754511.value: The actual value of nature-based tourism is unknown for a couple of reasons. Most nations do not collect data specific to this form of tourism. More fundamentally, there is no widely accepted operational definition as to what actually constitutes nature-based tourism. Nonetheless, the economic magnitude of nature-based tourism is likely to be immense. The International Ecotourism Society (TIES) in 2006 suggested that it is growing from 10% to 12% per annum in the international market. Ecotourism is one specific category of nature-based tourism and is becoming increasing popular around the world. TIES (2006) indicated that beginning in 1990s, ecotourism has been growing between 20% and 34% per year. Many researchers in many nations endeavor to understand ecotourism from different perspectives; however, limited research has been published on the rapidly developing Asian ecotourism market. Although statistic data on the ecotourism market in East Asia is limited, its potential can be reflected on the rapidly growing tourism market of East Asia. The region of Asia and the Pacific has generated from 21 million tourist arrivals in 1980 to over 181 million arrivals in 2009. The average annual growth rate of tourist arrivals in the region from 2000 to 2009 is 5.7%, which performed above the world average of 2.9% (WTO, 2010). The fast growing tourism market and uncontrolled tourists activities have cause negative impacts on many fragile ecosystems in protected areas. As a result, the concept of sustainable tourism has been proposed, which is fundamentally links to the idea of sustainable development. Ecotourism is a form of sustainable tourism. Ecotourism, properly operated and managed, balances both nature conservation and the needs of tourism development. Better understanding the needs and attitudes of ecotourists who travel in parks and protected areas would help develop appropriate management plans and strategies. Such plans and strategies could contribute to positive interactions among resource managers, tour operators, local residents, and visitors, encouraging effective management of protected areas and proper ecotourism products and services of tour operators (Tao et al., 2004a). With the trends in mind, this study aims to develop a profile of ecotourists in China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan including their socio-demographic characteristics, on-site experiences, benefits sought, travel motivations and environmental attitudes and identify their similarities and differences among the three regions.

754811.label: Project Objectives
754811.value: To compile all significant descriptions of, and all Western images of, Yuanming Yuan’s art and architecture in French and British sources, from the first European contacts with the palace in the 1740s through the late 19th century, when the palace’s treasures were dispersed in Europe. Using these texts and images as a focal point, to describe how French and British audiences perceived and interpreted Chinese visual arts, including calligraphy and painting, sculpture, architecture, gardens, and decorative arts in porcelain, jade, and related materials. To analyze how different segments of the French and British population viewed Chinese visual arts differently, distinguishing differences based on nationality, social status, political ideology, and professional interest (artists, collectors, politicians, missionaries). To trace changes in such group tastes and values over time, correlated to changes in social and political contexts during the formation of European modernity (Enlightenment debates over secular governance, revolution and empire, imperialism, the Opium Wars, etc.). To compare this reception of Chinese art with the reception of Indian and Japanese art as known in secondary sources. By doing all the above, to develop more precise understanding of how different parts of “Asia” were viewed differently, how different segments of “the West” viewed Asia differently, and how these various views evolved with the formation of Western modernity.

754811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
754811.value: This project examines the French and British reception of visual arts originating in the famed Chinese palace complex of Yuanming Yuan. It focuses on Yuanming Yuan because it was a vast repository of imperial culture whose plundering remains a topic of heated debate within China. It focuses on France and England because these countries had the most contact with Yuanming Yuan and produced the most images and texts about it. And the period examined begins with the 1740s, when the palace was largely completed by Emperor Qianlong and European Jesuits first worked there; continues through the 1790s and early 1800s, when several European embassies visited, and through 1860, when French and British troops looted the palace and the British army burned it down; and concludes in the late 19th century, when looted objects circulated in Europe and Europeans visited the grounds and published texts and images about the palace. The project’s primary goal is to use Yuanming Yuan as a case study for exploring the rich complexity of European responses to Chinese visual arts. By focusing on one extraordinary site with plentiful primary source material, the project can demonstrate how Europeans evaluated different Chinese art media differently, from painting, calligraphy, and sculpture to architecture, gardens, and various decorative arts. By examining the same rich site over time, it will show how European attitudes towards Chinese art evolved with the development of European modernity, from Enlightenment admiration to imperialist aggression. And by focusing intently on the way different agents of interaction – missionaries, diplomats, soldiers, art experts, etc. – viewed Yuanming Yuan differently, it will show how different countries, and different individuals within each country, interpreted Chinese culture in different ways, for different aims. As an art historical project, this study – and the book that will emerge from it – will greatly advance our still limited understanding of China’s impact on Western visual culture, a subject far less studied than the impact from Japan and India. By shifting attention from art production to art reception, including the visual representation, museological display, political use, and commercial exchange of foreign art objects, it forges new art historical approaches to intercultural interaction. And it adds significant complexity to intercultural studies generally, by emphasizing the countless subtle differences that existed among different agents in different countries at different times in history. 圓明園是知名的宮廷園林。本研究將探研園內的視覺藝術品在法國與英國的接受情況。本研究以圓明園為重心，因為園內極富皇室文化事物，而搶掠圓明園一事，在中國依然聚訟紛紜。本研究專門探討法、英兩國，因為兩國與圓明園的接觸最繁密，所製成有關的圖像、所撰寫相關的文字也最多。本研究由一七四零年代起開始探析。圓明園在乾隆前已頗具格局，耶穌會會士率先在此工作。一七九零年代至一八零零年代初，幾位歐洲大使到訪圓明園。至一八六零年，圓明園被法、英兩軍搶掠，並遭英軍焚毀。研究以十九世紀末作結。此時，所掠奪的物品在歐洲流傳。歐洲人到遺跡參觀，並出版關於圓明園的專文和圖像。 本研究的主要目標，是以圓明園為例，探討歐洲對中國視覺藝術林林總總的反應。圓明園有很多第一手的材料，着力研究，可以看到歐洲人如何衡量中國不同的藝術表現手法，包括書畫、彫刻、建築、園林以及各種裝飾藝術。探研圓明園不同時期的變化，可以看到歐洲對中國藝術的態度怎樣隨着歐洲現代性的發展而衍變 ─ 由啟蒙時期對中國藝術的仰慕，到帝國主義時期對中國藝術的侵略。此外，本研究又諦視不同的文化交流主導者對圓明園的看法，他們包括傳教士、外交官、士兵、藝術專家等，從而看到不同國家、各國不同的人為各自目的、各師各法地闡釋中國文化。 較之日本與印度對西方視覺藝術的衝擊，中國對西方視覺藝術文化所造成的衝擊，目前所知不多，這方面的研究也極少。這項藝術史研究，以及隨之出版的專書，將大大有助我們了解箇中的衝擊。本研究專門從藝術接受的角度來探討，包括視覺表象、博物館展覽、政治用途、外國藝術品商業交易，而不是藝術製作，是藉藝術史探研跨文化交流的另一新徑。此外，本研究特別點出歷史上不同時間、不同國家、不同媒介之間都有無數微妙的差異，令跨文化的整體研究更多彩多姿。

754811.label: Realisation of objectives
754811.value: Objective 1: I've completed gathering texts and images that depicted Yuanming Yuan in this period, including those previously published and those previously unknown to scholars. This was achieved by reviewing existing scholarship and doing extensive archival research to find rare and unique objects and texts in France, England, Germany, and the United States. Objectives 2-4: These objectives involves organizing and synthesizing the research findings from objective #1. I've finished organizing the research materials according to western people's interest in various forms of Chinese art; according to different tastes among various western groups; and according to different periods within my time span of c.1700 to c.1900. I've also formulated my arguments and outlined their presentation in my book manuscript. So I'm in the final stage of actually writing the book, which is at an advanced stage but not yet complete. I expect no barriers to completion other than time constraints. Objective 5: I ended up not pursuing this objective as fully as the others, as it's less central to the main aims of the project and turns out to be less important for understanding the material. The book is also already very long and detailed, so there's not room for this material to be included. It might be a subject for a smaller publication in the future. Objective 6: This objective is fully achieved by the in-depth analysis of the Yuanming Yuan case study. Here again, I've completed the research, organization of the material, and synthesis of the arguments, and the written outcomes are being drafted. Since this objective and this issue are very large, covering a wide span of time, people, and materials, they can only be treated in a book-length study, as originally planned.

754811.label: Major findings and research outcome
754811.value: The central aim of the project is to use the case study of the Yuanming Yuan site as a way of understanding how European perceptions of Chinese culture evolved and varied across different time periods, nations, and individuals. The book that I'm drafting will present the full findings, while publication #1 (in part C) summarizes some of the main points of this survey. The first section of the book shows how Jesuit missionaries from France and Italy first described Yuanming Yuan in very positive terms and worked alongside artists and architects of the Qing court in the late 18th century. Their positive views were related to their mission to introduce Christianity to China. Their mixing of European and Chinese systems of representation and ornament were discussed in conference papers #4 and #5 (see part C). The second section of the book shows how European ambassadors viewed Yuanming Yuan in more negative terms and criticized Chinese forms of painting and architecture, in part because of their diplomatic and economic competition with China. It also shows how more positive images of Yuanming Yuan circulated in travel books, even when the first Opium War of 1839-42 led many Europeans to condemn China in negative terms. These research results have not yet been publicly presented. The third section of the book focuses on the looting and destruction of Yuanming Yuan during the second Opium War of 1857-60. It shows how soldiers misunderstood the relative value of Chinese art forms and how the British and French armies took imperial artifacts to bolster their own monarchs' imperial status. The looting and its effect in Europe is discussed in conference paper #2. The subsequent display of looted art in France and England, which re-cast Chinese culture as highly refined and royal, is analyzed in papers #1 and #3, which also formed the basis for publication #2. The fourth and final section of the book examines how Europeans reacted to the destruction of Yuanming Yuan and the spread of looted art objects through the art market. This material has been touched on in paper #2 but not otherwise presented in public.

754811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
754811.value: The published book will make a major contribution to our understanding of China's artistic reputation in the west and to our methods for studying intercultural interactions more generally. It will thus be possible for scholars to extend the China research to see how western views of China evolved after 1900. And it will be possible to use some of the models of intercultural interaction that are developed in the book to examine intercultural interactions between Europe and other areas of the world. For my own work, I expect to write one or two further essays about European views of Chinese culture in the later 19th century, possibly in comparison to European views of India and Japan.

754811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
754811.value: This book project examines the history of European perceptions of China and Chinese culture between c.1700 and c.1900. Its central focus is the imperial palace complex of Yuanming Yuan, which formerly stood outside Beijing and served as the second most important palace after the Forbidden City. By tracing the history of European encounters with Yuanming Yuan, the book shows how different segments of European society viewed China differently, and how these views changed over time. It explains, for example, how Jesuit missionary artists from France and Italy praised the palace's cultural sophistication when they worked there in the 18th century, while British diplomats visiting in the 1790s disparaged the same palace as exotic and backward. It explains how the French and British armies later looted the palace in 1860, taking objects they considered financially valuable, while collectors across Europe later collected these looted objects as examples of great art. The book contributes to our understanding of current international relations by revealing how China's reputation developed through western representations. It also makes a broader contribution to the discipline of art history by analyzing a number of different ways in which foreign cultures can interact with one another.

755111.label: Realisation of objectives
755111.value: The research project involved four groups of English speakers: L1 Cantonese-L2 English-L3 French (CEF), L1 Cantonese-L2 English (CE), L1 French-L2 English (FE), and L1 English (E). Among these speakers, the research project focused on the comparison between the CEF group and the other three groups, with the aim of identifying any traces of interaction of three languages in the multilingual CEF’s minds, particularly cross-linguistic influence from L3 French to L2 English. To achieve the above aim and the objectives listed, three timed off-line experimental tasks were used: grammaticality judgement-correction task, multiple-choice cloze task, and free writing task. The three experimental tasks helped discern the judgement on and production of three English structures among the four groups of speakers. Besides the three experimental tasks, a questionnaire was used to understand the language background and language learning history of the CEF, CE and FE speakers. The information collected from the questionnaire helped indicate the possible impact of learning experience on the judgement on, production of, and perception towards the languages involved (i.e., Cantonese, English and French for the CEF group, Cantonese and English for the CE group, French and English for the FE group). The analyses of the collected data indicated that the aim of the study was largely achieved. As to be detailed in Section 6.1, certain statistically significant differences (1) between the CEF and CE groups, (2) within the CE group (but not within the CEF group), and (3) between the CE group and the FE group (but not the CEF and FE groups) indicated possible influence from L3 French to L2 English among the CEF participants. The extent of such influence was found to vary, depending on the language structure (e.g., nominal plural marking vs. past simple tense marking) and the nature of usage of the languages (e.g., judgement vs. free production). Meanwhile, since statistical significance was not obtained in all the comparisons made, a bigger pool of CEF participants with a more advanced level of L3 French would help discern more robust differences between CEF and CE speakers. Also, as stated in the annual progress report, only offline tasks were conducted because of insufficient computers for the installation of E-prime at the home university. It is suggested that online tasks could be conducted in an extended study so as to examine the potential cross-linguistic influence from L3 French to L2 English from a psycholinguistic perspective.

755111.label: Major findings and research outcome
755111.value: Given that the main concern of the study was the difference between the CEF and CE participants, this section presents the key findings regarding the two groups’ judgement on and production of the three test language structures: Nominal plural marking 1. While no significant differences were noted between the CEF and CE groups in the judgement-correction task and multiple-choice cloze task, the two groups showed significant difference in the free production of target/ non-target instances of nominal plural marking. 2. Significant difference between the non-target missing and redundant plural marking instances was noted among the CE participants but not the CEF counterparts in the free production task, implying the role of L3 French in enhancing the CEF participants’ sensitivity to morphological marking. Past simple tense 1. While no significant differences were noted between the CEF and CE/FE groups in the judgement-correction task, the CE and FE groups showed significant difference in the judgement of non-target past tense instances in the task. 2. The free production task showed differences in the nature of the non-target past tense instances produced by the CEF and CE participants. The CEF group produced significantly more present perfect instances (instead of the target past simple ones) than the CE group, suggesting possible influence of L3 French in L2 English. The two groups also differed in terms of their morphological marking of the verb forms. Adverb placement No statistically significant differences for adverb placement were noted between the CEF and CE groups in all three experimental tasks. This finding possibly echoes Lardiere’s (2009) remark about word order being one of the structures which can be successfully acquired. To sum up The above findings concerning the three test structures revealed a number of differences between the CEF participants and their CE counterparts. In light of these findings, it is postulated that the knowledge of French as a third language may have resulted in certain observed differences between the two groups. The potential role of L3 French on L2 English (i.e., positive or negative cross-linguistic influence) seemed to hinge on the complexity of the language structure (e.g., past simple tense involving both morphology and semantics vs. plural marking with morphology only) and the nature of usage of the target language (e.g., judgement vs. free production). Meanwhile, more advanced French CEF participants would be needed to bring about more statistically significant differences between the two groups of English learners. Please refer to Part C for the research output.

755111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
755111.value: In light of the major findings and research outcome of the project, the following list of possible research areas or directions are suggested: 1. Structures at different linguistic levels (e.g., phonetics, morphology, and semantics) can be tested to collect further evidence for possible cross-linguistic influence from L3 French to L2 English. This enhances our understanding of how pervasive such influence is. 2. Online tasks can be conducted to investigate from a psycholinguistic perspective the patterns observed in the present study. This helps understand cross-linguistic influence from L3 French to L2 English from distinctive theoretical concerns. 3. Various tasks can be conducted so as to disentangle two distinct but closely related linguistic levels, namely morphosyntax and semantics, in L2 English tense marking. This is of particular interest when the learners’ L1 has a less robust morphological system than English and realises tense marking in a different way (e.g., Cantonese).

755111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
755111.value: The proposed study aimed to look into the interaction of three languages in a multilingual’s mind in Hong Kong: L1 Cantonese, L2 English, and L3 French, with particular focus on the effect of L3 French on the acquisition and use of L2 English. Through the analysis of the learners’ judgement on and production of English nominal plural marking, position of manner/frequency adverbs and past simple tense, the study (1) studied to what extent the L1 Cantonese-L2 English-L3 French speakers’ data were similar to or different from those of L1 Cantonese-L2 English speakers, L1 English speakers, and L1 French-L2 English speakers, and (2) addressed the question of transfer or influence from one non-native language to another non-native language. From the pedagogical perspective, the study contributed to the teaching of English as a second language in the multilingual Hong Kong. The learner participants would have a better profile of their understanding and learning of English, particularly the three language properties concerned.

755211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
755211.value: BACKGROUND: Bipolar disorder (BD) is a mood disorder characterised by two extreme phases: the manic, characterised by a sustained high mood and impaired judgement; and the depressive which involves low mood and, frequently, the presence of suicidal ideation. Advances in medical and psychosocial treatment have helped reduce the symptom burden for people with BD, but this has not led to a comparable improvement in levels of social functioning and many never regain their pre-illness social and vocational roles and statuses. AIMS AND DESIGN: Using a recovery framework, the proposed study will pursue a new line of investigation to focus not only on individual pathology but also on the ways in which mental health services could establish strong recovery-enhancing programmes, a focus they currently lack. This study represents a first attempt internationally to identify systematic links between the subjective experiences of recovery of people with BD and the objective measures of recovery. The research design includes a matched group of people with schizophrenia allowing, through comparison, the identification of the unique recovery experiences of those with BD. A random sample of 150 Chinese participants will be recruited from various treatment and rehabilitation facilities across Hong Kong. Half will have been diagnosed with BD and half with schizophrenia. None will have active symptoms currently. Consenting participants will be briefly interviewed about their personal history and asked to complete questionnaires focusing on elements of recovery, recovery markers and organisational features of healthcare services; these will be completed in one 45-60 minutes meeting. With the participants’ consent, significant others (nominated by the participants) will be contacted by telephone to confirm the participants’ highest and current residential and vocational levels. Classification tree modelling, a form of data mining will be used to identify systematic relations between variables. SIGNIFICANCE: Understanding how recovery is interpreted and experienced by people with BD should provide clues as to why social functioning and, thus, quality of life, lags behind symptom reduction. This information should allow the design of more relevant and focused psychosocial rehabilitation services for this group to ensure that public money spent on them is invested in strategies that are relevant and effective. The study will also lay a solid foundation for further local and international research in developing more sophisticated approaches to ameliorating the psychosocial sequelae of an illness that afflicts millions worldwide. 研究背景：興奮抑鬱症是由兩種極端不同的心境而得名的：興奮是一種持續亢奮的心境，伴有判斷力缺損；抑鬱是一種低落心境，通常伴有自殺意念。醫學和心理社會學的治療已經可以幫助患者緩解症狀，然而，患者在社會功能上並未能得到對應程度的恢復，而且很多患者不能恢復病前的社會地位和職業角色。 研究目標和研究設計：本研究採用復元理論(Recovery Theory)作為研究架構，從一個新的角度出發，不僅關注個體病理學，同時也關注精神健康服務如何能提高康復效果，填補該研究領域的空缺。本研究是國際上第一次嘗試有系統的聯繫興奮抑鬱症患者對復康的主觀體驗和客觀的復康測量進行研究。研究者從香港各種治療和復康機構隨機招募150名中國人參與研究，一半參與者被診斷為興奮抑鬱症，另一半被診斷為精神分裂症（匹配組），目前都沒有發病。通過兩組比較，探索興奮抑鬱症患者的獨特復元經驗。研究者與復康者將進行一個45-60分鐘的會晤，包括兩個部分內容：第一是關於其個人經歷的簡略訪談，第二部分是填寫問卷。這個問卷關於復康的各方面要素，改善的標誌和所接受的醫療服務的機構特點。在取得參與者同意後，研究者將聯繫由參與者指定的家人或有關的人，確定參與者的最高和目前的居住和職業水平。採用分類樹模型(Tree Model)作為探索數據的主要形式，以系統地確定變量之間的關係。 意義：理解興奮抑鬱症患者對復元的解釋和體驗，可以幫助了解為什麽其社會功能乃至生活質量的提升落後於症狀的改善。這些信息可以幫助設計更多相關的心理復康服務給患者，使公帑用得其所。同時，本研究為本土和國際的進一步研究奠定基礎，促使發展出更有效的方法，以幫助世界上幾百萬的患者緩解這種疾病的後遺症。

755211.label: Realisation of objectives
755211.value: In order to achieve the project objectives #1-3 as stated in section 5.1 above, we have successfully interviewed 150 clinically remitted patients (75 with BD and 75 with SCH) between February to December, 2012 at the Western Psychiatric Centre outpatient clinic. The Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D) (Zheng et al., 1988), the Young’s Mania Rating Scale (YMRS) (only participants with BD) (Young et al., 1978), the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) (only participants with SCH) (Kay et al., 1987), and the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV Disorders (SCID; only the schizophrenia and mood disorders sections) (First et al., 2002) were administered to confirm their diagnosis and remission status. A questionnaire was also administered to the participants to assess their subjective recovery experiences, objective functional recovery, important elements of recovery, features of health services that promote recovery, sociodemographic variables and clinical variables. For objective #4 as stated in section 5.1, we originally planned to use the whole scale of The Recovery-Enhancing Environment Measure (Campbell-Orde et al., 2005), which contains three sections that assess participants’ subjective recovery experiences, features of health services, and important elements of recovery. However, in order to enhance the study design, the section on subjective recovery experience was replaced by a Chinese validated scale called SRS (Song and Hsu, 2011), and the section on perceived importance of recovery elements was replaced by a Chinese validated scale called REAQ (Siu et al., 2012). OCS was retained to assess elements in the social environment of the treatment setting that are conducive to recovery.

755211.label: Major findings and research outcome
755211.value: 1. Differences in recovery experiences between those who achieved objective functional recovery and those who did not Among the whole sample (N=150), 38 participants (25.3%) were functionally recovered in terms of able to live independently and obtain a full-time job at expected level. Four stages of recovery were derived from the total score on the SRS. The higher the stages, the more advanced the subjective recovery progress was. Among those who were functionally recovered (N=38), none were classified as Stage 1 subjective recovery, 18.4% were in Stage 2 recovery, 50.0% were in Stage 3 recovery, and 31.6% were in Stage 4 recovery. No significant differences were revealed in the following between those who were functionally recovered and those who were not: subjective recovery outcome, features of health services that promote recovery, and perceived importance of elements of recovery. 2. Differences in the subjective recovery experiences between those with BD and those with SCH Among those with BD, the average of the SRS score was 106.64 (SD = 19.76, range = 56-135). Two participants (2.7%) were classified in Stage 1 recovery, 12 participants (16.0%) in Stage 2, 38 participants (50.7%) in Stage 3, and 23 participants (30.7%) in Stage 4. By using Tree Model method of analysis, The most important recovery element endorsed was “respect, hope, and self-directed empowerment” (refers to respecting the person’s rights, interests, and culture, providing him or her with the opportunity to make informed choices, general wellness and hope). Among those with SCH, the overall recovery score was 98.2 (SD = 25.85, range = 40 - 135). Six participants (8.0%) were classified in Stage 1 recovery, 24 participants (32.0%) in Stage 2, 26 participants (34.7%) in Stage 3, and 19 participants (25.3%) in Stage 4. Logistic regression results indicated that the most important differentiators of recovery stage endorsed by the participants were “having a meaningful role" and age. 3. Relationships between subjective recovery experiences and objective functional recovery Among those with BD, subjective recovery experience (as measured by SRS) and objective functional recovery (operationalized as current residential and employment statuses) were not significantly correlated with each other. Among those with SCH, subjective recovery experience was significantly correlated with residential status (rs=0.266, P=0.021) but not employment status. For the combined sample of those with BD and SCH, the subjective recovery experience significantly correlated with both current residential (rs=0.277, P=0.001) and employment statuses (rs=0.205, P=0.015).

755211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
755211.value: There are two potential areas of research. The first focuses on further exploring the phenomenon of subjective recovery and functional recovery using more sophisticated approaches. Since this study only includes those who are in clinical remission, future studies should explore the phenomenon of subjective recovery among those who are still suffering from multiple symptoms and explore whether progress in subjective recovery would be different from those who are in clinical remission. It would also be useful to examine the longitudinal patterns of subjective and functional recovery to further explore how the journey of recovery unfolds and what factors may facilitate or hinder the recovery. The second area focuses on examining the family, particularly the caregivers, of those with BD. As our current results revealed that those who were married, had higher family income, and endorsed social roles as less important to their recovery were more likely to achieve better subjective and functional recovery, it would be important to examine the caregiving roles played by family members in promoting or hindering the recovery in BD. Given the lack of research in this area, especially within Chinese culture, both qualitative and quantitative methods would be necessary.

755211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
755211.value: This study aims to examine the recovery experiences of clinically stable patients with bipolar disorder (BD) and schizophrenia (SCH) in Hong Kong. Data were collected from 75 participants with BD and 75 with SCH. Those with BD subjectively recovered better than those with SCH (e.g. better well-being, social functioning, more hopeful), and the factors that were associated with better recovery were not the same between these groups. Although all of the participants were deemed as clinically stable, only 25.3% of them were able to live independently and obtain a full-time job. Furthermore, the functioning level was only weakly associated with how they perceived their own recovery progress. Females, married counterparts, those with higher family income, and those who perceived social roles as less important were more likely to subjectively feel better and achieve better functioning. These results demonstrate that BD and SCH tend to have different recovery trajectories, and thus future studies on recovery should separately examine these two groups. Furthermore, since functioning level and subjective recovery were different constructs, both measures should be used to provide a more comprehensive account of recovery outcome. The factors that were found to facilitate better recovery can also be incorporated into healthcare services.

755511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
755511.value: 追求社会认同维持社会联系是人类的一个基本需求。然而，人们实现这种需求的努力并不会总是很顺利。比如在工作中被同事冷淡对待，在恋爱交往中被对方拒绝，参加聚会被其他人冷落。当事人在这些状况里遭遇了社会排斥。社会排斥在当今社会中是一个常见现象。 过去的心理学文献中记载了社会排斥可能带来的广泛的行为后果。比如，被社会排斥的个人变得好斗并富有侵略性 ， 帮助别人的意愿降低了， 自我克制力差了。另一方面，这个经历社会排斥的个人也表现出对群体意愿更加服从，更有兴趣建立新的社会关系。 最近有一些研究和消费者行为有关系。 这些研究发现被社会排斥增强了个人对金钱的欲望。和金钱有关的一项重要的消费者行为是财务决策（比如，金融投资决策）。财务决策通常涉及到金钱汇报和风险之间的权衡取舍，对消费者福利有很大的影响。本项研究项目主要研究社会排斥对消费者财务决策的影响。 消费者在作财务投资决策时常常需要在高风险高回报产品（比如股票）和低风险低回报产品（比如国家债券）中做出选择。以往的研究表明消费者对投资产品风险程度的接受取决于他们是注重可能赢取的回报还是可能发生的损失。最近的研究发现社会排斥会导致个人对金钱的欲望增强因为金钱被视为一种从社会体系里获取好处的手段。当个人被在社会关系中受挫时，他们就会更重视金钱的这一作用。 基于财政决策文献和社会排斥文献，我们提出假设：社会排斥会加强消费者对金钱的追求从而注重在财政投资中可能赢得的回报，因此经历社会排斥会提高消费者对高风险财政投资产品的偏好。我们进一步假设，如果消费者不再认为金钱有从社会体系中获取好处的作用时，这种偏好就会减弱。并且，如果财政投资产品特别强调可能带来的金钱损失，或者消费者自身的投资理财知识，或者他们对自己运气判断，都有可能影响他们是否把注意力放在可能赢取得回报上，从而影响种偏好的强弱。 我们将采取实验的方法检验我们的研究假设。这项研究的发现将对社会排斥研究和财政金融决策研究方面的文献做出贡献，也对理解金融市场产品和保护消费者福利有意义。

755511.label: Realisation of objectives
755511.value: The current research proposes four research objectives. All the four objectives have been achieved. Objective 1 is to test the proposition that social exclusion increases consumers’ preferences for the high-risk options in financial decisions. I conducted a series of laboratory experiments and one field study in Hong Kong, using different forms of manipulations and measures adapted from the literature or developed in the marketing context, and employing different types of financial decision tasks (e.g., lottery, investment plan). The results from these studies provide supports to our proposition. Objective 2 is to examine the underlying mechanism for the proposed effect. In a series of experiments using participants recruited in Hong Kong and North America, I document the following mechanisms: • The effect of social exclusion on preferences for high-risk financial product is driven by individuals’ perception that money is instrumental for having control in life. • Desire for social affiliation and desire for protecting the personal control would drive the effect of social exclusion on money spending under different conditions. Objective 3 is to examine the boundary conditions for the effect of social exclusion on financial decisions. Using a series of laboratory experiments and survey study, I document the following boundary conditions: • Participants’ lay belief about money’s role (e.g., whether money is good or bad to one’s well-being) • Individuals’ perceived personal control (e.g., the salience of past experience of exerting control; service employees’ perceived servicing empowerment delegated by the company). • Individuals’ perception of self-worth (e.g., self-affirmation) Objective 4 is to examine the alternative mechanism and the related consequences on consumer decision. I have the following findings. • A series of experiments show that social exclusion could trigger the psychological perception of self-uniqueness which in turn influences their consumption choice by preferring unique options. The occurrence of this mechanism and the consequence on consumer choice depends on 1) participants’ perception of their financial resources and 2) participants’ appraisal of the stability of the cause of exclusion. • A series of experiments and one survey study show that different types of social exclusion at the workplace influence service employees’ co-production performance (indicated by customers’ perceived control value and relational value), through the mechanism of threatened efficacy needs versus relational needs. • We find that mood cannot account for the effects documented in this project.

755511.label: Major findings and research outcome
755511.value: Findings from this project are reported in one journal publications, six conference presentations (see Part C), and two working papers. The first set of research studies (five laboratory experiments and one field study) shows that experience social exclusion (vs. non-exclusion) increases individuals’ preferences for high-risk/high-return options in their financial decisions (e.g., lotteries, investment plan). It further documents that individuals’ perception of money as instrumental to acquire social benefit underlies this effect. Moreover, this effect is found to be moderated by individuals’ lay belief about money’s role. Specifically, when individuals believe that money does not always lead to positive impact on one’s well-being, they would not increase their preference for high-risk options in their financial decisions after being socially excluded. The second set of research studies (five laboratory experiments and one study conducted at Amazon Mechanic Turk) shows that experience social exclusion influences individuals’ financial spending, depending on their assessment of whether the purchase decision provides the opportunity for social affiliation. When the consumption decision provides the opportunity for social affiliation, social exclusion increases consumers’ willingness to spend money, and this effect is mediated by their intention to acquire social affiliation through product purchase. However, when the consumption decision does not provide the affiliation opportunity, social exclusion decreases consumers’ willingness to spend money, and this effect is mediated by consumers’ perception that the money is a source of personal control. The third set of research studies (four laboratory experiments) finds that social exclusion influences consumers’ choice of unique versus common options. When individuals perceive that they have rich financial resources or when they appraise the cause of exclusion as stable, they will be more likely to choose unique products when they are socially excluded than included. This effect is drive by a self-uniqueness perception. The fourth set of research studies (two laboratory experiments and one survey study) finds that social exclusion by different sources at the workplace (supervisor ostracism versus coworker ostracism) would influence customers’ perceived cocreation values in their coproduction with the service agents. Specifically, supervisor ostracism decreases customers’ perceived control value, and coworker ostracism increases customers’ perceived relational value. These effects are driven by service agents’ perceived loss in their efficacy needs versus relational needs, and are moderated by high servicing empowerment and the extendedness of customer relationships. The fifth set of research studies (three experiments) shows that self-affirmation can moderate the effect of social exclusion on consumer decision.

755511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
755511.value: One potential extension for this research is to examine the order of priority for need fortification in social exclusion. Findings from the current research project show that social exclusion can lead to a variety of behavioral consequences due to individuals’ motivation to fortify the threatened needs such as the need for belongingness, control, the efficacy need (power, meaningful existence), and the need to maintain self-esteem. Behavior to satisfy different needs might go to opposite directions. To examine which need might get the priority, we can manipulate social exclusion and examine individuals’ behavior in a task which allows us to see opposite pattern for satisfying different needs. For example, excluded individuals would donate more money if they want to strengthen their belongingness need by building social affiliation with the charity work, but they would donate less money if they want to protect their control need by keeping the money that would allow them to have more control over life. Observing consumers’ first reaction to social exclusion on these consumption activities would allow us to infer the priority of the needs fortification.

755511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
755511.value: In daily life people encounter incidents in which they are left out, rejected, ignored by other people or social groups. When these incidents occur, they may feel lonely, loss of control, lowered self-esteem, and they may complain that life is meaningless. Would these feelings alter people’s consumption decisions? The current research examines the impact of social exclusion on consumer decision, especially those decisions involving financial consequences, reveal the underlying mechanisms, and suggest ways to counteract these effects. Findings from this research have significant implications for consumer well-being. First, feeling socially excluded may lead consumers to prefer risky investment options, because of their strong desire to acquire more money, rather than based on their careful assessment of these financial products. In such situations, consumers need to strengthen their belief about the values they uphold in their life, or to empower themselves in alternative ways, so that they wouldn’t rush into risky decisions. Second, past research shows that sometimes people behave aggressively in order to cope with the unpleasant experience of social exclusion. The current research suggests that people can use choosing unique products to help themselves because doing so gives them a justification of the exclusion experience: they are unique people.

756011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
756011.value: The aim of this study is to empirically examine the social status, experience(s) of prejudice, and social stress/resiliency among Hong Kong Chinese sexual minority people (i.e., gay, lesbian, bisexual & transgender), as well as the impact on their behavioral and mental health. The knowledge obtained from this study will guide social and public health policy, sexual minority-targeted interventions, and public- and school-based sexual and gender diversity education programs. Although several decades of Western research on sexual minorities has firmly established the link between social stress and adverse health and wellbeing, such research on sexual minority people in Hong Kong is limited. Given the recent and significant increase in HIV infections among gay and bisexual men in Hong Kong, combined with the cultural uniqueness of minority stress in the Hong Kong Chinese context, there is an urgent need to understand the impact of minority stress and identify possible ways to enhance resiliency within this population. This study uses a case-control, mixed-methodological design and is guided by a framework adapted from the Minority Stress Model. Stemming from the disadvantaged social status of sexual minority people, which leads to adverse behavioral and mental health outcomes, two interdependent constructs related to stress processes are examined: (1) sexual minority stress that is manifested through objective discrimination events, expectations of rejection, and internalization of sexual prejudice; and (2) sexual minority resilience, whereby sexual minority people present personal and collective strengths in proactively coping with societal-based prejudicial attitudes and beliefs grounded in heteronormativity (i.e., the institutionalized assumption of compulsory heterosexuality and gender conformity that is considered to be inherently superior and preferable to any and all other orientations). The findings of this study will inform theory related to social stress, prejudice and discrimination in the Chinese context. The findings can also be utilized to develop culturally sensitive interventions aimed at enhancing sexual minority people’s resiliency and establishing an accepting and supportive social environment. Importantly, this study has significant implications for informing social and public policy, such as antidiscrimination legislation, which would fundamentally improve their currently disadvantaged social status, and consequently re-shape the meanings socially constructed for sexual minority people in Hong Kong. 本研究旨在利用實証研究方法調查香港華籍性少數族群(包括男同性戀者、女同性戀者、雙性戀者和換性人)的社會地位、特有的生活經歷 （包括遭受的偏見、社會壓力、和其本身的復原力），以及對他們的行為和心理造成的影響。研究獲得的知識，將成為訂定社會和公共健康政策、推動以性少數族群為目標的協助措施，以及製作有關性和性別差異的公共和校本教育課程的指引。 過去數十年，有關性少數族群的西方研究雖已證實了社會壓力和身心健康損壞的關係；同樣的本地研究卻非常有限。因應近年男同性戀者和雙性戀者感染愛滋病的個案顯著上升，再加上少數族群在香港華人社會遭受的壓力的獨特文化，我們急需理解這些壓力對少數族群所產生的影響，以及識別能促進少數族群復原能力的可行方法。 本研究運用病例對照研究設計和混合的研究方法，利用改進後的少數族群的壓力模式作為研究框架指導本研究。基於對性少數族群社會地位低微而引發的逆向行為和心理健康結果的考慮，本研究會調查兩個與壓力形成過程有關且相互關連的概念：(1) 性少數族群壓力（表現為客觀存在的歧視事件、預期遭到的拒絕和內化的性偏見）；(2) 性少數族群本身的復原力：主動應對建基於性和相關道德規範下衍生出的社會偏見和歧視性態度。 本研究成果不但會為理解中國社會里的壓力，偏見和歧視提供理論貢獻，於此同時還會為未來開展適應本地文化的提升少數性族群復原力的干預手斷和構建更為積極和接受的社會環境提供科學依據。更為重要的是，為能根本改善少數性族群的生存狀態，本研究對於未來推動和制定香港的反歧視法案有直接意義。

756011.label: Realisation of objectives
756011.value: Framed within the Hong Kong Chinese cultural context, this study investigated 47 sexual minority (gay, lesbian, bisexual, or transgender) peoples’ experiences of prejudice and discrimination across personal, social and institutional dimensions. This study have succeeded in exploring participants’ self-assessment of the processes of internalizing sexual stigma as well as its impact on well-being. We also aimed to interrogate the predominant minority stress model by contrasting the ways in which sexual prejudice manifests within the Hong Kong Chinese cultural context with the personal and social coping strategies employed following one’s self-realization of non-heterornormativity, ‘coming out’. Unlike western societies, sexual orientation-based violence and aggressive acts targeting sexual minority people are rarely reported in Hong Kong. One could argue that the rarity of explicit, aggressive discrimination against sexual minority people can be attributed to the rather non-aggressive nature of Hong Kong society as a whole, but rather may be a consequence of the concealable nature of one’s sexual minority status and the actual and/or perceived costs of coming out. In order to develop an analytical view of minority stress processes and coping strategies, this study have delved deeply into the lives of participants across psychological, emotional, behavioral and social domains. Our findings reveal how the multiplicity of everyday stressful experiences can manifest a negative self-assessment, which if persisting in a chronic state, can render a cascading effect on their view of life chances, sexual opportunities, personal capabilities, achievable social recognition, deserved resources and entitlement, as well as visions for the future. Participants in the study contend that it is possible to escape explicit prejudice and discrimination by concealing their sexual identities, but such coping strategies may also manifest a devalued sense of self that in turn progressively amplifies perceptions of a delegitimized social status. We have made important theoretical implications through our critique on Myer’s minority stress model, which is a social psychological model with reference to a social interactionist framework that focuses on the reflexive process of self in relation to prevailing social cultural discourses. The project also contributes to the development of a new perspective on social justice that will take into overlooked injustices in the personal relationships including Church life. The study has enabled us to take up a government study to understand the experience of discrimination against sexual minorities which has helped inform the proposed legislative reforms. We will continue to explore the role of gay celebrities in the movement.
