756011.label: Major findings and research outcome
756011.value: We will publish three papers. One paper on Gay Christians is under review by Gender, Place and Culture. One paper on erotic justice to be submitted to Feminism and Psychology at the end of Dec., 2015. One paper under preparation. An abstract to Celebrities Studies Journal Conference has been accepted and will prepare a paper for submission, possibly to Feminist Media Studies. "Loss or Gain: A study on celebrities and civic engagement in Hong Kong." We have been conducting data collection in the past year on celebrity culture and civic engagement. A total of 32 informants were interviewed. Interview themes include: celebrity identity, fandom culture, civic engagement, LGBT politics, human rights, democracy, Umbrella Movement, social meaning of money. We were proud to have received a government grant to launch a territory wide study entitled “A Study on Discrimination Experienced by Sexual Minorities in Hong Kong” jointly with the Policy 21 Ltd. 200+ interviews were conducted. The report has been submitted to the Constitutional and Mainland Affairs Bureau (CMAB) and the Advisory Group on Eliminating Discrimination against sexual minorities for their consideration. The findings and experience have made it possible for us to submit develop a new model for understanding minority stress. We have also promoted the idea of intimate justice and erotic justice for identifying micro-aggression, subtle forms of discrimination and injustices that have been overlooked and ignored. The study help examine different forms of injustices – inequalities, discrimination and various forms of exclusion and violence in gender, love, sex, marriage and family that goes beyond resource re-distribution and policy changes to social status, social recognition and cultural representations (Fraser, 1997; Ho, 2015). These inequalities affect people’s social capital, life chances and opportunities available important for the development of capabilities and self-esteem especially for disadvantaged groups (Ho, 2013, Ho, et.al. 2014; Ho, 2015). Thus, it is important that we identity these unjust practices, hidden or evident, in different life domains of personal life – marriage, love relationships, family life, school life, peer relationships, religious life as well as other sites of social engagement. To address these injustices my work calls for the imagination of new modalities of political action beyond those that are historically recognized or culturally sanctioned as being “political” and various forms of social actions and educational activities. The study also present alternatives to those that currently dominate social and political discourse in Hong Kong through conferences and community education activities.

756011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
756011.value: The research team has conducted the largest number of qualitative interviews on sexual minorities in Hong Kong leading to academic publications and policy reports that have policy implications. We will continue to advocate for legislation that will protect sexual minorities from discrimination in various aspects of their lives. We will also continue to raise awareness through public education programmes. In these respects, we will continue to work with the Advisory Committee of the sexual minorities, Big Love Alliance whom we have worked together on "Love is Equal" project and other events to help advocate for diversity and democracy. We will be presenting at the Celebrities Studies Journal Conference and explore the role of celebrities and gay icons in advocacy for the rights of the sexual minorities and community building. We are glad that we can use what we have learnt from the GRF project and the government study to develop the concept of intimate justice and erotic justice to capture the experiences of injustices in relationships. We will continue to promote these concepts and express our concerns through Faculty initiative entitled "The Good Life series" including reaching out to youth workers alerting them to the problems of "self-harm" among sexual minorities.

756011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
756011.value: The research team has conducted the largest number of qualitative interviews on sexual minorities in Hong Kong leading to academic publications that have legal and policy implications. Our major theoretical contributions are: (1) a new model of minority stress; (2) a new concept of social justice that has taken into consideration injustices in personal life and interpersonal relationships including close ones. We are glad that we can use what we have learnt from the GRF project to come up with a conceptual framework that will help understand the lived experience of sexual minorities in Hong Kong. The research team feel strongly that it is our responsibility to contribute to a study that will make it possible for HK to identify the next step to anti-discrimination ordinance. We will continue to push the government to improve legislation that will protect sexual minorities from discrimination in various aspects of their lives including church life. The study has also helped us develop new ideas about the role of gay icons and celebrities in social movements. We will continue to work with the LGBT community to raise social awareness on issues of diversity and democracy as well as prevention of self-harm among sexual minorities.

756211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
756211.value: The essential characteristics of an aborted attempt include 1) an intent to kill oneself, 2) a change of mind immediately before the actual attempt, and 3) an absence of serious injury. Studying aborted suicide attempts has an advantage of knowing the actual thoughts and actions that have stopped these individuals implementing their plans. There are however only a handful of studies that have investigated this phenomenon. The majority of the psychological models on suicidal behavior are based on the diathesis-stress-hopelessness paradigm. A range of underlying diatheses, i.e., problem-solving deficits, and cognitive rigidity, have been identified and that triggered by stress may lead to suicide attempt. Little is known about what psychological attributes help to enhance individuals’ resilience to suicidal urges. Using a mixed-methods approach and drawing on the diathesis-stress-hopelessness theory, the primary goals of this study are to explore the accounts of those with an aborted suicide attempt and to construct an empirical-based model to describe aborted suicide attempts in Hong Kong. This study has three major aims: 1) to explore why and what led these individuals aborted their attempts; 2) to identify the psychological vulnerabilities and resilience, between stress and aborted suicide attempts; and 3) to explore the reactions, reasons for participation, and impact of interviews on participants after the interviews. There are two stages in this study: (1) face-to-face interviews, and (2) follow-up telephone interviews. Participants will be recruited through the Police Negotiation Cadre (PNC). Participants will be included if they are 18-59 years old and whose suicide attempts are voluntarily aborted after the negotiation with the PNC. Participants will be excluded if they have psychosis and their suicide attempts are forcefully aborted. Verbal consents of study participation will be sought by the PNC after the negotiation. The PNC will notify the PI with the contact information of the consented participants. The PI will then approach the participants by telephone and invite them for interviews. Stage one will first have the participants to describe their suicidal process narratively and then fill in a questionnaire. Stage two will include two consecutive telephone follow-up interviews (one month and three months after). This study will provide important data on the cross-cultural generalizability of established theories of suicide attempt based primarily on Western data and provide guiding information on the future development of evidence-based crisis intervention. 中止「企圖自殺」行為的基本特徵包括：1）意圖殺害自己；2）在作出自殺行為前改變主意，和3）嚴重傷害自己的程度較低。 研究這個題目的好處讓社會人士知道使當時人停止執行自殺行為的真正想法和行為。然而，只有少數人對這一現象作出的研究。透過心理模型對自殺行為的理解，大部份都是建基於「個人因素－壓力－無望感模式」（diathesis-stress-hopelessness paradigm）。在一連串與個人因素有關的情況下，包括缺乏解決問題的能力、較封閉的想法，再加上壓力這個誘因，便促使人作出自殺的行為。很少研究顯示由哪項心理因素提升當時人的抗逆力，以致降低其自殺的意念。 透過使用混合方法的模式和「個人因素－壓力－無望感模式」，最主要是探究停止作出自殺行為的原因，並建構一個以實為本的模型，從而解釋出現在香港的中止自殺行為的現象。這項研究有三個主要目標：1）探討原因和促成當時人停止作出自殺行為的因素； 2）在壓力因素及停止自殺行為之間，確定這類對象的心理弱點及抗逆力的心理；3）探索的當時人的即時反應、參與研究計劃的原因，以及事後訪談對當時人的影響。 這項研究分為兩個階段：（1）面談；（2）跟進電話訪談。受訪對象為經警察談判組招募而成。他們的年齡屆乎18-59歲、曾作自殺行為但經警察談判專家游說下而中止作出此一行為。患有精神病及使用武力而中止自殺行為的個案不包括在本研究之內。談判專家於事後取得受訪人士的口頭同意，並將聯絡資料轉交予負責本研究計劃的研究員。研究員透過電話邀請受訪者接受訪問。 在第一階段，受訪者將會細緻地描述他們的自殺過程，並填寫一份問卷。 在第二階段，受訪者將在第一及第三個月內接受電話訪談。這項研究將提供重要的數據及資訊：１）透過西方的資料建立跨文化的理論；２）為日後的防止自殺工作提供更多指導性的資訊。

756211.label: Realisation of objectives
756211.value: A number of local studies have investigated the profiles and risk factors of suicide attempts in hospital settings and among adolescents. Researchers have not often investigated the lived experiences of people in Hong Kong who have self-harmed. More, in most suicide attempt studies, researchers have contacted participants through hospital staff. Our study was probably the first in Hong Kong in which researchers recruited highly lethal suicide attempters through the law enforcement agency. The recruitment process of the present research began in June 2012. Prior to the recruitment, two briefing sessions were conducted in August 2011 and March 2012 with about 70 police negotiators to introduce the details of the project and the means of recruitment. The research team and the Police Negotiator Carde (PNC) had collaboratively developed the inclusion and exclusion criteria for potential study participants to ensure that the recruitment method was ethical and created little disturbance to the normal operation of the PNC. We also developed a turn-out record form to monitor the progress and potential adverse events during the study period. Hence, the record form included the date of the incident, profile of the subjects, nature of the incident, handling team, resolution of the incidents, duration of negotiation, primary reasons for the attempt, and the presence of suicide notes was developed by the PNC and the form was completed immediately after every turn-out by the PNC. The utilization of this form becomes a standard procedure of the PNC. In this study, we only recruited suicide attempters who had been engaged by the police negotiators and who had aborted their attempts after crisis negotiation. The inclusion criteria were: (i) subjects who were at least 18 years of age, (ii) who were Cantonese speaking, and (iii) who voluntarily aborted their suicide attempts after the negotiation with the PNC. The participants were excluded if (i) the other police officers or fire officers had forcefully interrupted and aborted their suicide attempts, (ii) they were involved with criminal cases that may lead to subsequent prosecution, and (iii) suffered from known schizophrenia spectrum and other psychotic disorders. After the negotiation, a police negotiator at the scene gave the aborted attempters an introductory letter about the study and a self-developed manual on managing self-harm before the attempters were escorted by the ambulance to the closest hospitals for medical assessment and treatment. A police negotiator then sought written consent from the aborted attempters for forwarding the name and contact details to the research team. If consented, a PNC member would pass a copy of the written consent to the research team within two working days. The research team then contacted the consented aborted attempters for study participation and interviews through a telephone call and invited the participants for interviews within one to two weeks after the negotiation at a convenience place suggested by the consented participants. Besides of the face-to-face interviews, we also invited participants to participate follow-up telephone interviews one month and three months after the initial interviews. We also conducted a face-to-face interview one year after the initial interviews. The narrative and semi-structured interviews to achieve Objectives 1, 2, and 4 The face-to-face interview comprised a narrative interview part and a semi-structured interview part. The interviews were audio- or/and video-taped with the participants’ written consent. Having signed a consent form, the research team first asked the participants to talk about their aborted suicide attempts in chronological order, starting with statements or questions such as “I would like you to tell me in your own words,” “I would like to hear the story behind your suicide attempt”, or “So how is your life now after the aborted attempt?”. Once each participant had completed the narrative interview, the research team then used the semi-structured interview part to explore any relevant issues that had not already emerged. We classified the examined themes of the semi-structured interview part into four broad domains: (I) socio-demographic characteristics (i.e., marital status, educational status, ethnicity, living arrangement, and employment status), (II) clinical factors (i.e., history of psychiatric disorders, previous psychiatric treatment, previous suicide attempts using the Chinese version of the Beck Suicide Intent Scale, and the Reasons for Attempting Suicide Questionaire, (III) life events (i.e., relationship, family, work, physical health, and legal issues), and (IV) psychological and cognitive factors (i.e., Social Problem-Solving Inventory, the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support, the Zimbardo Time Perspective Inventory, the Reasons for Living Inventory). The themes were considered and generated based on the constructs of the stress-diathesis theory and the suicidal process model. At the end of the interviews all participants received HKD300 (about USD40) to compensate for their time or travelling costs. However, despite the fact that all participants consented to audio-taping of the interviews for research purposes, only 2 participants consented to video-taping of the interviews. Hence, Objective 4 was underachieved. The follow-up interviews to achieve Objective 3 We conducted the follow-up telephone interviews one month and three months after the initial interviews. We also conducted a face-to-face interview one year after the initial interviews. Through the follow-up interviews, we aimed to identify the presence of further risk for attempting suicide. Example questions were as follows: “Do you have a wish to die now?”, “Have you thought of killing yourself recently?” We also aimed to explore the participants’ emotional responses and comments after participating in the study because of ethical concerns for our participants being distressed by the interviews. We based the items asked in the telephone interviews about participants’ experiences of participating in the study on a questionnaire developed by Hawton and colleagues in the United Kingdom, which Wong and colleagues adopted and modified in their previous psychological autopsy study. Interviews with the negotiators to achieve Objectives 1 and 2 We conducted interviews with the police negotiators who were involved as soon as possible after the negotiations to minimize the recall bias. We adopted an unstructured format, and we asked the negotiators to describe the incidents that our study participants were involved in a chronological order starting with the question “Can you tell me what happened during the call-out from the time you received the call to the time the incident ended?”. We also asked about any potential impact of the incidents on the negotiators.

756211.label: Major findings and research outcome
756211.value: (I) From 1 June 2012 to 31 December 2014 (31 months), the PNC received a total of 231 suicide attempt call-outs. The PNC intervened in 118 cases. Eighty one cases aborted their attempts after negotiations with the PNC. Among the 81 aborted suicide attempt cases, 11 cases consented to the PNC for being contacted by the research team. However, two cases refused to participate after their initial phone contact with the research team; hence, the research team interviewed nine aborted suicide attempters. The research team conducted eight one-month and seven three-month telephone follow-up interviews and only two one-year face-to-face follow-up interviews. The main reasons for the low number of one-year follow-up interviews included refusal to be interviewed again (n = 4) and loss of contact (n = 3). The research team interviewed 10 (two females) police negotiators who were involved in the crisis negotiations of the study participants (see Research Output No.3 for the details of the findings of the methodology and reactions to study participation). (II) (a) Findings on the psychology of aborted suicide attempters - Although the number of study participants was small, with the in-depth narrative and semi-structured interviews with both the aborted suicide attempters and the involved police negotiators, we found that problem-solving deficits and cognitive rigidity were the commonality deficits among the attempters. Also, the sense of "social disconnectedness" initiated by betrayal of the intimate partners and separation from the children was a common feeling among the attempters. The feeling was reinforced by the thinking that there was a great discrepancy between the efforts they put in but leading to poor relationship outcomes. (b) Findings on what contributed to the abortion of the suicide attempt - the Behavioral Influence Stairway Model (BISM) developed by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and implemented by the PNC was the key to the success of aborting the suicide. The BISM aims to establish communication with the subjects, verbal containment to keep the subjects occupied, defusing subject’s intense emotions, and facilitating subject’s problem-solving ability. We found that most of the participants appreciated that they had a way to share their thoughts and sadness and the negotiators provided a wider thinking perspective so that they discovered the negative consequences of completing the attempt. (The findings will form Research Output 4 which is in preparation at the moment, please see attached).

756211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
756211.value: This research fund has helped in developing the self-help materiel, the questionnaire for the initial and follow-up interviews, the turn-out record to be used by the PNC, and training sessions had been conducted for local and international police negotiators. If resources allow, the PNC may continue this research as an in-house study that can further enhance their crisis suicide intervention work. Also, this study can be conducted in other countries with similar issues, like the Singapore and some cities in the Mainland. The findings of this study has significant practical implications for crisis suicide interventions because many of such interventions remain untested.

756211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
756211.value: The phenomenon of suicide is democratic in that it affects every segment of our society and it should be seen as everybody’s business. Traditionally, suicide prevention has been seen as the responsibility of medical and allied health professionals. This study found that when individuals who are severely suicidal, if they are given an opportunity to be intervened with trained paraprofessionals who can conduct crisis suicide intervention in a caring and timely manner, suicide is preventable. We found that since the sense of social disconnectedness was common and strong when the participants were suicidal, a problem-solving perspective in relationship improvement introduced during the crisis negotiation was helpful and brought hopeful thinking to the attempters. Also, many of the participants refused referred services for them after their attempts, but they appreciated that this study had given them an opportunity to talk to the research team who was also experts in suicide prevention.

756411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
756411.value: Engaging with recent theorizations of pornography’s relation to early modernity in Europe, this project aims to revise our present understanding of early Chinese modernity through the lens of pornographic and libertine cultural expression in the late Ming (here defined as the period between 1522 - 1680, Ming 1368 - 1644). A study of the role of pornographic writing and images in late Ming Chinese cultural history promises to reveal significant insight into early developments in Chinese modernity. In eighteenth-century Europe the anti-clerical and anti-establishment mood of the Enlightenment was often expressed through the open eroticism of the libertine novel and other forms of pornographic expression; the anti-establishment strain within late-Ming thought can similarly be understood to express a nascent Chinese modernity that produced an interest in iconoclastic representations of sexuality, albeit approximately a hundred years earlier in the late-sixteenth and early-seventeenth century. Involved as they are in both reflecting and shaping their time, pornographic texts from the period provide an opportunity to examine late Ming reconstitution of norms relating to subjectivity, morality, materiality and the social body. Employing methods from literary and cultural history, this transdisciplinary project therefore aims to analyse the cultural importance of “pornographic dissent” in shaping this key moment in China’s early modern history, and in turn contributing to modifying the dominant Europe-centered paradigms of modernity that currently dominate scholarship. 回應近年來關於歐洲早期現代化與色情作品關係的研究，本課題通過對晚明色情作品和當時社會上的縱欲思潮的考察，致力於重新理解中國早期的現代化（晚明在這裡是一個文化史的概念而不限於朝代的更換，大致指公元1522-1668）。 對晚明色情作品在文化史上角色的研究可以幫助我們對中國早期現代化的發展獲得更深刻的理解。在十八世紀的歐洲，反教會權力和反傳統權威的啟蒙主義思潮經常通過自由主義小說中的赤裸裸的色情描寫以及其他的色情形式表現出來，而晚明思想界中的反傳統權威的傾向——經常也是通過反對正統觀念的性愛描寫——也可以被理解為中國本土現代化的萌芽之一，儘管這發生在比歐洲約早一百多年的十六世紀晚期和十七世紀的早期。 晚明的色情作品為我們考察這個時期的主體意識、道德觀念和具有社會性的肉體的重構提供了一個機會，它們既反映了這種社會思潮，同時也在形成這種社會思潮。本課題的最根本的目的在於證明“色情呐喊”在中國早期現代化史上的重要性，尤其是在文化方面。同時也期望借此以解構長期以來主宰著現代化話語的、以西方為中心的現代化模式。

756711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
756711.value: China’s economic reforms have resulted in spectacular growth on a scale unparalleled in world history; however, at the same time, inequality in China has increased rapidly, making China one of the most unequal economies in the world. Arguably, the most successful market reform strategy implemented in China was local competition among jurisdictions and experiments by local governments. This strategy, however, has also led to an increase in inequality. One of the most striking developments under the local government initiatives is the emergence of industrial clusters in numerous small towns in coastal provinces; each involving thousands of private entrepreneurs. Not long ago these were poor rural towns; now they have become world centers of manufacturing. The products of each town have a substantial share of the world (or national) market. Local governments have played important roles in this extraordinary development. However, as some rural towns have grown extremely rapidly and become rich, many have lagged behind. Moreover, opportunities to households are becoming more unequal. Associated with the widening disparities of productivity across towns and of opportunities to households, the inequalities of household wealth levels across Chinese towns and within each town have enlarged dramatically. This project intends to address many important questions on the factors that contribute to the spectacular growth of town level industrial clusters and the associated extraordinarily fast growing gaps of disparities in productivity and in wealth. Why can some towns develop that fast? What motivates township officials there to work hard and to try new ideas? Why do other towns lag behind so much? Why are those local officials not motivated? In this project, we plan to conduct in-depth field surveys of county/township governments, town level industrial clusters and firms through a stratified random sampling survey. With the data collected, we will study the incentives given to local officials and the effectiveness of the incentives to understand the roles of local officials in the development of town level industrial clusters. We will also study the “corporate” governance of clusters and the effectiveness of this governance structure. Furthermore, we also plan to study wealth inequality at the household level in developed towns and underdeveloped towns. Based on a combination of this research, we plan to address the growth-versus-inequality problem at a micro level. A thorough understanding of these questions is not only interesting academically, but also very important for the policy debates on the sustainability of China’s growth. 改革开放给中国经济带来了前所未有的发展。与此同时，中国经济中的不平等问题却日益严重，中国现已成为全世界最缺乏平等的经济体之一。如果说中央政府引导下的地方竞争和地方试验是中国市场经济改革成功的锦囊秘诀，那么这种秘诀同时也是加剧经济不平等的根本原因。 在地方政府的积极促进下，沿海省份涌现出众多由乡镇企业构成的产业集群和数以千计的民营企业家。一个个曾经的贫穷乡镇，摇身一变成为行业的全球制造中心。每一个看似不起眼的乡镇，都可能在全国乃至全世界的市场份额中占有一席之地。在这个“麻雀变凤凰”的过程中，地方政府显然发挥了重要作用。但是，在一部分乡镇飞速致富的同时，我们发现还有许多乡镇远远地落在后面。更为不幸的是，落后乡镇往往没有得到平等的发展机会。随着不同乡镇生产力与发展机会的差距越拉越大，乡镇间以及村民间的贫富差异也愈加悬殊。 面对乡镇产业集群的飞速发展以及由此带来的生产力差异和贫富悬殊，本课题提出以下重要问题：部分乡镇发展迅速的原因何在？这些乡镇的官员积极协调和勇于创新的动机是什么？其他地区远远落后的原因在哪里？落后乡镇的官员们为什么无法产生上述动机？ 在本课题中，我们将对县、乡、镇政府进行深入的实地调查，对乡镇产业集群中的企业进行分层抽样调查，以期研究地方官员的行为激励及其效果，并由此进一步了解地方官员在乡镇产业集群发展中所发挥的作用。同时，我们将研究产业集群中的企业治理及其效率。我们还将调查不同发展程度的乡镇中的贫富差异情况。基于以上研究，我们将对乡镇中的“发展-不平等”问题做出综合的微观经济学分析。此类综合分析不仅具有学术价值，更能为中国经济的持续发展提供观点支持和政策参考。

756711.label: Realisation of objectives
756711.value: This project makes substantial contributions to the following literatures: economic growth and inequality; new economic geography: industrial clusters; Chinese institutions. One of the most important engines which drive China’s growth in the past three decades is the industrial clusters that thousands of specialized small towns developed into “world factories.” Yet, income inequality in China has worsened rapidly during the same period of time that China becomes one of the most unequal economies in the world. Is the tradeoff between growth and equality unavoidable at early stage of economic development, as suggested by Simon Kuznets six decades ago? This is the first study in the literature that systematically examines the effects of China’s industrial clusters on local economic growth and inequality at firm-county level. The leading indices of economic clusters developed in the new economic geography literature capture the features in market economies well. However, China’s institution is featured by half market half bureaucracy. To captures the key features of clusters developed under the institutional constraints in China, we construct a series of indices to measure industrial clusters. Based on the results derived using these measurements as applied to a combination of firm- and county-level panel data sets from 1998 to 2007, we find that clustering enhances local economic growth. In particular, counties with strong clusters and clusters consisting of a more developed non-state sector experience higher economic growth. Moreover, urban–rural income inequality is substantially lower within counties with clusters consisting of advanced non-state sector than in other counties because of the increased income of rural residents. The results remain robust after addressing the endogeneity issues using the two-stage Heckman estimation.

756711.label: Major findings and research outcome
756711.value: This study systematically examines the effects of China’s industrial clusters on local economic growth and inequality. We find that clustering enhances local economic growth. In particular, counties with strong clusters and clusters consisting of a more developed non-state sector experience higher economic growth. Moreover, urban–rural income inequality is substantially lower within counties with clusters consisting of advanced non-state sector than in other counties because of the increased income of rural residents. We also examine how clustering affects the productivities of firms in China and explore the potential mechanisms through which clustering matters. Based on a firm-level panel data set, we find that firms in counties with industrial clusters generate higher total factor productivity (TFP). Meanwhile, firms in counties with stronger clusters and clusters consisting of a more advanced private sector generate higher TFP than others. Furthermore, we find smaller firms and younger firms are benefited from clustering more than other firms. We interpret the results by exploring the financial constraints of firms based on both the firm-level panel data set and the fata from a questionnaire survey on clusters in Zhejiang in 2013. We find that clustering helps relax liquidity constraints faced by small and young firms and consequently help small and young firms to lift TFP. Furthermore, we examines the effects of clustering on household income and income inequality in China. Specifically, based on data from nation-wide household income surveys in 1995, 2002 and 2007 and a questionnaire survey on clusters in Zhejiang in 2013, we examine how the existence of industrial clusters and the features of such clusters affect rural household income and the major components of the income, and, the inequality of total income and income components. We find that rural household in counties with industrial clusters have significantly higher total income than those in counties without clusters. Furthermore, we find the increase of total income of rural household in counties with clusters is mainly driven by the increase of wage income and non-farming business activities. More interestingly, we find that clustering not only leads to higher rural household income but also reduces within-county income inequality, in particular seen with total income inequality and the inequality in wage income and income from non-farming business activities. Finally, the clustering effects on total income, income components and income inequality are observed stronger in counties with stronger industrial clusters and clusters consisting of advanced non-state sector than in other counties.

756911.label: Project Objectives
756911.value: Develop a non-behavioral theory for the puzzle that the defense attornies' contracts typically do not have a contingent fee. Draw insights on the welfare implications of potential polices that encourage or discourage a contingent fee in attorney contracts.

756911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
756911.value: In US tort and contract litigation, a defendant's attorney is typically paid by a fixed hourly rate, despite there being a contractible instrument, the settlement amount or the judgment amount, that is eventually realized. In contrast, a plaintiff's attorney is typically paid by a fee contingent on that amount. It has been recognized in the literature that the lack of a contingent fee (CF) on the defendant's side is difficult to explain. Dana and Spier (1993) observes that “... virtually all defense attorneys are paid by the hour. This fact is somewhat puzzling, since many of the commonly accepted explanations for contingent fee apply equally well to both the plaintiff and the defendant.” Zamir and Ritov (2010) also elaborates in detail their view that “this paradoxical behavior is puzzling because many of the explanations for the use of CFs apply equally to both plaintiffs and defendants”. We want to find a non-behavioral explanation for the puzzle and in particular, we are intereted in a signaling explanation. As is well known, the client faces the problem of not being able to observe the effort level of the attorney, which is called moral hazard in economics. Moral hazard makes the attorney willing to offer a positive CF as a way to commit to exerting effort. However, the attoney, by his/her professional experience, is better informed about the merit of the case, and thus the value of his/her service. This gives the attorney an incentive to use the contract offer as an instrument to signal to the client if the value of the service is high. The attorney cannot simply tell the client that his/her service is valuable, because any attorney who knows otherwise can mimic those languages. However, an appropriate contract can be a credible signal because it links the attorney's final payoff to the outcome of the case. A zero contingent fee contract in particular has the potential to be such a signaling device, because it means that the attorney refuses to share the downside of the case with the client, so the case must be very unfavorable to the client and thus hiring an attorney is important. We aim to show that a flat fee contract is observed on the equilibrium and is sometimes unique. Moreover, the same reasoning will lead to only CF-contract on the plaintiff's side. 被告的律师的报酬结构: 一个发送信号的解释 在美国侵权法和合同诉讼中，被告的律师的报酬通常是一个固定的每小时的金额，尽管有一个可以写进合同的结果: 最终实现的谈判或审判达到的数额。相反，原告的律师的报酬通常是取决于这一数额。 在学术文献上人们已经认识到被告方的缺乏或然费用（CF）是难以解释的。Dana and Spier（1993）指出 “... ...几乎所有辩护律师都是按小时支付。这其实是有点令人费解，因为许多普遍接受的或然费用的解释也同样适用于原告和被告方。” Zamir and Ritov（2010）也详细的阐述他们的观点: “这自相矛盾的行为是令人费解，因为许多使用或然费用的解释，同样适用于原告和被告双方”。 我们希望找到一个非行为学的解释，特别希望是一个发送信号的解释。众所周知，客户面临不能够观察到的律师的努力程度的问题，这就是所谓的经济学中的道德风险。道德风险使得律师愿意提供一个积极的CF承诺施加努力。然而，律师基于他/她的专业经验更好地了解诉讼的实力，并他/她服务的价值。这让服务价值是高的律师有动机使用合同作为一种工具发送信号给客户。律师不能简单地告诉客户他/她的服务是有价值的，因为任何律师可以模仿这些语言。但是，一个合适的合同可以是一个可信的信号，因为它链接律师的最终收益与诉讼结果。零或然费用的合同尤其可能成为这样一个信号装置，因为它意味着律师拒绝与客户分享诉讼的失败，这样的情况下诉讼必须是对客户非常不利，意味着聘请律师是很重要的。我们希望显示固定费用合同会出现在平衡状态中，有时是唯一的平衡状态。此外，同样的道理会导致原告方只使用CF合同。

756911.label: Major findings and research outcome
756911.value: We study an expert, who at the time of contract offering privately knows not only the outcome if the client accepts the contract, but also the outcome if the client rejects it. We show that the contract has very different signaling roles in the following complementary parameter cases: the same pairing parameter case where a higher (lower) value of service is paired with a better (worse) service outcome and the reverse pairing parameter case where a higher (lower) value of service is paired with a worse (better) service outcome. First, in any separating equilibrium, in the same pairing case a higher-value expert offers a more contingent contract, while in the reverse pairing case a higher-value expert offers a less contingent contract. Second, in any separating equilibrium, in the same pairing case both a higher-value and a lower-value expert receive their full-information first-best payoff, while in the reverse pairing case full separation incurs distortion. Third, in the unique pooling equilibrium, in the same pairing case both expert types offer a contingent contract, while in the reverse pairing case both types offer a flat-fee contract. The results can be used to address the existence of contingent and flat-fee contracts offered by experts.

757211.label: Project Title(Chinese)
757211.value: 折衝之術：十八、十九世紀中國女性道德典範的情感表達

757211.label: Project Objectives
757211.value: To uncover a significant body of literature by "exemplary women" in 18th-and-19th-century China; To reveal their emotional lives, as framed by their own personal collections; To exemplify the rhetorical strategies of these texts, and the specific purposes they were serving as the women dealt with concrete life situations; To illustrate these women’s engagement with larger social, cultural, and literary discourses and, hence, their acts of mediation and agency; To establish them as powerful writing subjects, and to identify their connections with the “New Women.”
rows: To uncover a significant body of literature by "exemplary women" in 18th-and-19th-century China;
To reveal their emotional lives, as framed by their own personal collections;
To exemplify the rhetorical strategies of these texts, and the specific purposes they were serving as the women dealt with concrete life situations;
To illustrate these women’s engagement with larger social, cultural, and literary discourses and, hence, their acts of mediation and agency;
To establish them as powerful writing subjects, and to identify their connections with the “New Women.”

757211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
757211.value: The “Mediations of Expression” project centers on a solid body of literature, hitherto unexplored, by a number of “exemplary women” in 18th-and-19th-century China. It aims to uncover the emotional worlds of these women, as framed by their own life-writing. Above all, it highlights the rhetorical strategies that these women exploited, and probes into the ways in which they mediated between, on the one hand, a prescriptive language of female virtue and the social, cultural, and literary norms that shaped their expressions of emotions, and, on the other hand, their individual experiences and feelings. By illuminating these acts of mediation and agency, this study counters the standard interpretation of the “exemplary women” as submissive victims of patriarchy and establishes them, rather, as powerful writing subjects of their own emotional lives. While historical records in China abound in accounts of honorable deeds and sacrifices of women, little is known of what was lying beneath the unflinching stoicism of these paragons of female virtue. Thanks to the trends of publishing women’s writings during the late imperial era, a number of these women had the opportunities to write their own lives and pass their life stories on to later generations in the form of “bieji” 別集, or personal collections. Once read closely, their writings would reveal a surprisingly emotionally-charged quality: If they were said to handle excruciating life situations with aplomb, wise judgments, high moral standards, or, even, with ease and elegance, their own writings would testify to all kinds of emotional afflictions they were put through. The “Mediations of Expression” project focuses on the exact ways in which these women gave expression to their “negative” emotions - anger, frustration, regret, anxiety, or fear - while bending such expression towards the very end of polishing their “exemplary” appearances. The inevitable tension, i.e. traces or gaps left by these very acts of mediation, would bear witness to their struggles: how they strove for the greatest effects of their life stories, so as to demand attention, to solicit sympathy, and to plead for recognition of their dilemmas and sacrifices. The strong sense of the “self” that emerges from their struggles would also provide an important perspective for the part of recent scholarship that reexamines late imperial China and sees in this recent “past” the seeds of the “modern”: The “exemplary women” as powerful writing subjects anticipated, paradoxically, the rise of the “New Women.” 本課題以大量有待發掘的閨秀別集為研究對象，藉以探討十八、十九世紀間被奉為道德典範的女性如何塑造自我與表達情感，尤其關注這些女性頻頻使用的“折衝之術”，即，在自己人生經歷的撰述中借助修辭策略對婦德要求與自身情感表達施以調和，回旋於社會、文化與文學等諸多規範中，折衝平衡，以為己用。揭示這種種折衝策略與技巧將有助於我們重新審視女性道德典範的歷史形象：與通常的想像相左，她們並非男權體制下順從而默然的犧牲者，而正是自身情感經歷的有力敘述者。 諸如孝女、賢婦、良母乃至貞婦、烈女等女性道德典範形象本於中國歷代史傳中屢見不鮮，然而一直以來，她們堅忍外表之下的內心世界卻罕有人知。明清才媛文化盛極一時，又尤以清為甚，才媛以別集傳世者為數眾多。考量其生平，相當部分並非僅以才名聞世，而或以孝行、或以賢名、或以貞烈留名於方志史冊，為親族鄉里之榮。探究其文字，常可見驚人之筆。如果史傳中的女性道德典範常以堅忍鎮定甚或嫻雅姿態面對人生的慘酷經歷，十八、十九世紀才媛筆下卻不乏面對困境時情感的激蕩與迸發。 本課題關注的正是這些女性抒寫情感的確切方式：她們如何表達諸如憤怒、挫敗、懊悔、焦慮、恐懼等“負面”情感，又如何扭轉其“負面”性，令其服務於塑造自我“典範”形象的目的？她們於折衝平衡間製造的文字張力將是她們掙扎於困境之中的最好見證，透露她們獲取自我呈現的最大效果、追索讀者的關注與同情、以及尋求自我犧牲的社會承認等諸多努力。滲透於她們努力之中的是對“自我”的強烈關注，而這正可為有關“現代性”的重新思考提供又一側面的佐證：作為強有力書寫主體的女性道德典範或許悖論式地預示著“新女性”在下一世紀之初的出現。

757211.label: Realisation of objectives
757211.value: In conducting this research project, PI made trips to the major archives, libraries, and museums in mainland China and has located relevant primary sources in line with Objective 1. These sources include: Qing-Dynasty women’s collections of writings, paintings, self/-portraits, and albums of pictorial autobiographies. PI has also gathered a significant number of reprints of relevant primary sources, including both texts and images. For images to be used in publications, PI has obtained the permission from the National Library of China and the Palace Museum of Beijing. PI has conducted research on this corpus of materials, in line with Objectives 2 and 3. This includes: recuperating lives of the female authors from their personal collections; analyzing their self-empowerment strategies; and examining these writings in the broader scope of the social relations and competitions in which they were embedded. PI has situated this corpus of materials within larger contexts, in line with Objective 4. This includes: locating biographical sources from dynastic histories, local gazetteers, and family genealogies; excavating the female authors’ social lives by locating their familial and social connections; incorporating a variety of materials to illustrate their literary and artistic activities (eg.: in the cases where the female authors were known as both poets and professional painters, PI incorporates, and compares, information from both anthologies of women’s poetry and treatises on painting). PI has related the project to current scholarly discussions on the rise of feminism in China and the selfhood of Chinese women, in line with Objective 5. This includes: engaging with recent publications in these areas; and addressing a broader audience by participating in recent discussions of feminism/s in light of the anti-essentialist awareness and an emphasis on particularities of women’s situations in different cultural and historical contexts.

757211.label: Major findings and research outcome
757211.value: PI presented research findings and organized panels in numerous international conferences, including the AAS (Association for Asian Studies) and its regional conferences in the U.S. PI has also published a number of research articles in top-ranking, internationally-refereed academic journals. Among the journals, three (Modern China, Nan Nü: Men, Women and Gender in China, Journal of Women’s History) are ranked “A+,” “A+,” and “A” in the Australia journal-ranking list. PI has developed these research results into a book, Mediations of Expression: Self-Writings of “Exemplary Women” in 18th-and-19th-Century China (working title). This book has been accepted for publication by University of Washington Press -- one of the most prestigious university presses in the U.S., and a leading publisher of scholarly works on Chinese literature and history. (Please refer to Part C: Research Output.) Below are a few quotations from the anonymous reviews: “…. Mediations of Expression is the first book-length study that makes systematic use of these newly available materials…. As such the book has the potential of taking the field of Chinese women’s literature and history to the next decade.” “[I]t is a daring, path-opening book…. Many aspects of the lives of these women are new to scholars. Of the most interest to me is Yang’s skillful evocation of the women’s economic activities (as professional painters for example) and fiscal transactions in and out of the family. Scholars have long been interested in this topic but precious few were as skilled as Yang in their sleuthing.” “Exemplary women are one of the central topics for the studies of Chinese history and traditional culture. However, most of the studies have been concentrated on the construction of female exemplarity in official historical records. Mediations of Expression will be the first book-length study examining exemplary women’s own accounts of their lives…. The author’s approach is interdisciplinary, bridging fields of literature, art history, social history, and medicine.”

757211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
757211.value: To further develop the research findings of this project, PI applied for a new GRF grant in October, 2014. The project is titled: Money, Culture, and Social Ascendancy: Learned Women in Mercantile Lineages from Huizhou, 1700-1850. It continues PI’s research interest in women’s changing roles in the Chinese family system, highlighting in particular the rise of learned womanhood in mercantile lineages as both the reflection of massive social changes and a significant transformative force in early modern China. PI is currently gathering primary sources and conducting initial analyses for this new project.

757211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
757211.value: Mediations of Expression establishes a number of exemplary women from the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries as powerful writing subjects of their own lives, and closely examines the rhetorical strategies they exploited to the best advantage of their self-representation. This study focuses particularly on the ways in which these female authors mediated between, on the one hand, the dominant discourse of female exemplarity that defined their existence and that shaped their self-expressions, and, on the other hand, their own individual experiences and feelings. This study also adopts an interdisciplinary approach to examine how these female authors crossed the boundaries of domains that were traditionally assumed to be closed to them - not only the boundaries of genre, but also those that defined knowledge, economic roles, political engagement, as well as ritual and cultural authority. Mediations of Expression re-evaluates the significance of female exemplarity to women’s self-representation, and, in this sense, reshapes our understanding of the radical breakaway from these moral values as represented by the “arrival” of feminism around the turn of the twentieth century.

757511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
757511.value: This project will examine transformative witnessing and cultural memory in Chinese films, memoirs and television documentaries. As theorized in memory studies, cultural memory is collective, interpretive and pertaining to the future, while witnessing entails acts of recall grounded in everyday life. In a market-oriented, global culture of the 21st century, the Chinese homelands of the late Cold War era have become a contested space of reflection, question, nostalgia, derision and reference in films, memoirs and television documentaries. A post-nationalist examination of this contested space recognizes the limits of attachments to trauma and nostalgia in cultural memory, and it proposes a model of transformative witnessing as creative and ethical acts open to the needs and hopes of the others. Transformative witnessing in cultural memory connects the work of moving-images and writing to the micro-ethics of an open, civil society. This project will develop an interdisciplinary approach to examine the transformative agency of witnessing in Chinese films, memoirs and television documentaries. Taking stock of the usual allegories of nation and modernization, it will reexamine state objectification of memory in films made during the Cold War era and it will trace the emergence of ethical alternatives in ordinary, everyday settings that transform the state objectification and their popular nostalgic correlatives. It will examine the quotidian chronotope and its implications in the following contexts: (1) narratives of homelands, (2) reflections of individual and collective identity, (3) encounters with the others, and (4) witnessing, activism and care. It will draw conceptual tools from film theory, memory studies, Holocaust studies, cultural criticism and Chinese film studies. At present, studies exist of Chinese film representation of atrocities and trauma related to the War of Resistance with Japan and the Cultural Revolution, and of urban memories in Chinese film. However, little work has been done on the transformative agency of witnessing and memory with a quotidian focus that pertains to activism involving hope and the needs of the other. My study will develop an interdisciplinary model to discuss this subject and will give emphasis to the following in the analysis of witnessing: (1) biopolitics, (2) time and imagination, (3) affect and poetics, and (4) micro-ethics involving risk and hope. An original approach to the study of Chinese cultural memory and Chinese cultural texts will be put forward, and the ethics of alterity in memory pertinent to the making of an open civil society will be considered.

757811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
757811.value: Vocal fatigue is generally associated with frequent and intensive voice use. It is a common occupational hazard in the teaching profession. As there are currently (2009/2010) 63,438 teachers in Hong Kong (Education Bureau, 2010), the economic and health impacts of vocal fatigue on this large occupational group cannot be underestimated. Vocal fatigue is best understood as a subjective perception of increased vocal effort, especially in high-demand phonatory conditions, such as high-pitched falsetto or low-pitch creaky voices. It may or may not be accompanied by identifiable signs, but the condition will improve upon voice rest. The physiology and the nature of vocal fatigue are not fully understood. It has been hypothesized that vocal fatigue may originate from i) neuromuscular fatigue, ii) tissue fatigue or iii) viscosity change on the vocal fold surface. These changes would affect the vibration of the vocal fold during phonation. High-speed imaging technique is the most useful tool to study the vocal fold vibration as human eyes are unable to follow the rapid vibratory movement of the vocal folds. Current available high speed endoscopic digital imaging system allows up to 4000 to 8000 frames of motion to be captured in one second. Such technique allows the vibratory pattern of vocal folds to be studied using slow motion play back or frame-by-frame analysis. A more important use of high speed digital imaging technique is that it allows capturing and studying of the irregular or “aperiodic” vocal fold vibrations, as found in sub-optimal or pathological voices. Data on the vocal fold vibratory patterns in normal and pathological voices are very limited as there are only a few sets of these high speed systems available world-wide. The Voice Research Laboratory at the University of Hong Kong is among the few centers in the world that has such instrumentation. The HKU team has developed a “High-Speed Video Processing” (HSVP) Program for quantifying vocal fold movements. This study proposes to investigate the vocal fold vibration during modal, falsetto and creaky voice production using the high-speed digital imaging system. It is hypothesized that fatigued voice would demonstrate atypical vocal fold vibratory pattern. 聲線疲勞一般和運用聲線的頻密有關。科學家對聲線疲勞的生理成因仍未能充分瞭解。 一般假設為 i) 肌肉疲勞， ii) 聲帶表面組織疲勞，或 iii) 聲帶黏壁膜表面變化而引起。 在發聲期間， 肉眼無法辨別聲帶的急速振動，所以要依賴能高速拍攝的技術。現代聲帶高速攝影技術系統能在一秒內拍錄4000個到8000個錄像。 這技術足以捕捉聲帶高速的振動 。 現時聲帶高速攝影系統只有少數科研中心擁有 。香港大學聲線研究所卻已應用了這門技術多年。 這項研究建議運用高速攝影系統研究聲帶在不同的情況下（包括高調假聲、低調聲和正常聲）的振動狀態，與及如何受聲線疲勞的應響。

757811.label: Realisation of objectives
757811.value: The project recruited 60 subjects (33 females; 27 males) aged 18-37 years. Four subjects were not able to produce a full set of data and only 56 subjects (30 females; 26 males) with a mean age of 22.57 (sd=3.35 years) were included in the final analysis. The subjects undertook continuous karaoke singing until they felt tired and could not sing anymore. The mean singing time was found to be 111.23 minutes (sd=12.23 minutes; range 85 to 150 minutes). High-speed laryngoscopy which recorded the phonation of /i/ sounds was carried out before and after the singing. A “High Speed Video Processing Program” has been developed for analyzing color images (HSVP-C). Glottal length-to-width ratio, perturbation measures, color and asymmetry measurements were included in the High Speed Video Processing Program. Based on the initial data of 20 subjects, we carried out preliminary analyses and found significant difference in the geometric shape of the glottis, in terms of glottal length-to-width ratio, before and after vocal fatigue (p<0.05). This suggests a shorter or wider glottal configuration following vocal fatigue. There were, however, no significances in the perturbation, color and symmetry measures. We have published the data in 2013 (Journal of Voice). We subsequently analysed the full set of data from the 56 subjects and the findings were the same, i.e. only the glottal length-to-width ratio showed a significant change following vocal fatigue. We have also attempted to analyse “phonation onset and offset” configuration to determine if there are signs which could be indicative of vocal fatigue. However, given the limitation of high-speed imaging, in which only at most 2 seconds of recording can be made, some subjects presented difficulty for capturing both phonation onset and offset in the same recording. Future advances in technology should allow recording of a longer recording for such analysis. Based on the results, we therefore concluded that we have achieved the project objective, namely, we have identified the feature of vocal fold vibratory pattern in vocal fatigue. Instead of relying on merely the subjective perception of individuals who experience vocal fatigue, high-speed laryngoscopic analysis examining the glottal configuration can be an objective measure in identifying vocal fatigue.

757811.label: Major findings and research outcome
757811.value: We have published 2 international refereed journal papers (2012, an abstract in the Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, 2013, a full paper in the Journal of Voice) directly from this project. We have also published a full paper based on a spin-off project using the High-speed Video Processing (HSVP) Program developed from the project. It is found that the glottal length-to-width ratio is a useful parameter to measure the vocal fold configuration which is sensitive to vocal fatigue. A shorter or wider glottal configuration is expected following vocal fatigue. Other laryngoscopic measures, which include perturbation, color and symmetry measures, are not sensitive to capture vocal fatigue. In summary, this project has determined that high-speed laryngoscopy using the HSVP program is an effective tool in identifying vocal fatigue by analyzing the vocal fold configuration (glottal length-to-width ratio).

757811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
757811.value: We contend that high-speed laryngoscopy with appropriate image analysis program would be a useful technique to objectively quantify vocal fatigue, which is an otherwise, subjective perception of the person who experiences vocal fatigue him/herself. This will have a potential clinical implication for professional voice users such as singers and teachers, in which objective quantification of vocal fatigue can be determined and recommendations based on the degree of vocal fold configuration changes following vocal fatigue can be made. Further research to develop a standard protocol for high-speed laryngoscopic examination and normative data for vocal fatigue would be necessary before a full implementation in clinical setting.

757811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
757811.value: Vocal fatigue is an invisible symptom experienced by professional voice users such as singers and teachers. They often experience tiredness in their voice use but there is still not an objective measurement of vocal fatigue that could quantify their perception of vocal tiredness. High-speed imaging of the vocal fold vibration can be a useful technique in identifying and quantifying vocal fatigue. The vocal folds would appear shorter or wider following vocal fatigue. This technique would be useful in research area for identifying vocal fatigue. It would also be useful as an objective clinical tool to quantify the degree of vocal fatigue.

758211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
758211.value: In this project we aim to investigate telegenetic counseling communication in Hong Kong. Genetic counseling is a complex interactional activity in which counselors inform their clients at risk of a genetic disorder about that disorder and available testing, and facilitate the clients’ decisions of whether to pursue genetic testing or not (Sarangi, 2000). Telegenetic counseling falls under the telemedicine framework and refers to counseling mediated by distant technologies (e.g. telephone, internet). The proposed project builds on the research team’s previous work on face-to-face genetic counseling in which a substantial need to investigate alternative ways of providing these services was noted. This need arises from an increasing demand for genetic counseling services and limited available workforce in Hong Kong and neighboring China. While telemedicine has been applied and researched widely in various healthcare settings, research on telegenetic counseling, in particular in Hong Kong context, has been scarce. In addition, the implications of telemedicine have been surrounded by some ambivalence: the advantages advocated in some studies have been shown to contain potential pitfalls in other studies. The ambivalence surrounding telemedicine points to its multifaceted nature and suggests the need for further studies. In this project rather than focusing on the outcomes of telecounseling, we will employ a discourse analytic perspective to examine the actual processes of telecounseling and how these outcomes are negotiated by participants in interaction. In order to achieve that we will video-and audio-record interactions between genetic counselors and clients, and collect other data of interactions mediated by distant technologies. Our analysis will be supplemented by semi-structured interviews with participants that will provide useful background information. By using these diverse sources of data we will explore the complexities and challenges of telegenetic counseling and how they are mediated by participants of these encounters. Our interdisciplinary team includes both “outsiders” (i.e. discourse analysts) and “insiders” (genetic counselors), and our research has a strong applied orientation. The findings of the project will be communicated to the professional community through a number of channels: presentations at research sites and professional conferences; and by running a workshop. The findings could also be used to develop training materials for genetic counselors. The project outcomes will also be of interest to academics working in a variety of fields as it will shed light on the complex phenomenon of telegenetic counseling and offer a methodological approach to analyzing it. 本項目從話語分析的角度，調查在香港的電話遺傳輔導。遺傳輔導是一項複雜的互動溝通：輔導員向潛在遺傳性疾病風險的客戶講解遺傳性疾病，和現行的測試方法，協助他們決定是否接受遺傳測試（Sarangi, 2000）。電話遺傳輔導從屬於電話醫療的框架，是指用遙距技術（如電話或互聯網）的方式提供輔導。 這項目是建基於研究小組在早前進行的面對面遺傳輔導時的發現。小組在輔導時發覺有迫切需要研究另一種方式來提供輔導服務。這是因為遺傳輔導服務的需求不斷上升，而且人手有限。儘管電話醫療已在不同的醫療領域中受到廣泛應用和研究，電話遺傳輔導(特別在香港)的研究非常短缺。電話醫療應用當中存有矛盾：一些研究顯示電話醫療能帶來功效，但另一些研究卻指出功效潛在隱患。圍繞著電話醫療的矛盾心態指向其多面性的本質，顯示有進一步研究的需要。這項目的重點不在於電話輔導的效果，而是集中在電話輔導的過程，參與者如何從互動的協商達致輔導的成效。為了實現此目的，我們將用視像和錄音， 記錄遺傳輔導員和客戶之間的的互動，並收集其他利用遙距技術作溝通的數據。我們會與參加者進行面試，作為輔助我們分析的工具，好使我們獲得有用的背景資料。我們的目標是探索電話輔導的複雜性和挑戰性、和其溝通的方法，最終克服輔導的缺點。我們將研究參與者採用的的策略，以提升溝通的質素，實致輔導的目標。 我們跨學科的團隊，既包括「外人」（即話語分析員），也包括「內人」（遺傳輔導員）。我們的研究以應用為本。項目的研究結果將透過研究網站、工作坊、專業研討會，在專業社群中發表。研究的結果也可以用於開發教材，培訓遺傳輔導員。這項目有助說明電話輔導的複雜現象，並提供以方法學的方式，分析這些數據，對其他領域的學者也有用途。

758211.label: Realisation of objectives
758211.value: The project team has successfully achieved all of the objectives of the study. The database of genetic counselling consultations for G6PD deficiency (face-to-face and telephone) was created to be used for the purposes of research and training of genetic counselling professionals (Objective 6). The supplementary data corpus compiled during the project includes clients’ questionnaires and interviews with genetic counselling professionals. The team has examined the data corpus using established discourse analytic methodologies (Objective 1). The data analyses included identifying the main themes of these consultations (Objective 2); exploring their complexities/ challenges (Objective 3); and identifying discourse strategies that can contribute to enhancing communication (Objective 4). The results of the data analyses were summarized in the form of manuscripts published in prestigious journals and edited volumes (both linguistic and medical professional); several manuscripts are under review and in preparation at the time of the submission of the current report (see part C for further detail). The results of the project have also been disseminated at international interdisciplinary and professional conferences (see part C). The project team ran a workshop “Genetic Consultations / Counselling in South Asia” at the 10th Asia-Pacific conference on Human Genetics that brought together leading genetic professionals and communication scholars from 5 countries in South Asia (Hong Kong, Malaysia, the Philippines, Indonesia and Thailand) and the UK. The team also organized two large-scale and a number of smaller scale workshops for professionals in Hong Kong. The PhD student who was recruited to work on the project successfully completed and submitted her PhD thesis. The team also provided research experience to one undergraduate student. The PI established the Winter School on Health Communication, and during the project the team organized two Winter Schools (December 2012 and 2013). The School was specifically targeted at professional practitioners, healthcare educators, researchers and others engaged in the field of healthcare communication. Feedback from participants commended the applicability of communication knowledge to the professional practice. The Winter School incorporated some findings of the project. The findings of the project were also incorporated into teaching MMedSc in Genetic Counselling programme (HKU). The PI mentored undergraduate students and a PhD student who developed a leaflet for clients with G6PD deficiency. Focus group meetings with professionals and client representatives to validate the leaflets were organized. The leaflet has now been approved by the Department of Health (HK Government) for use in all public hospitals in Hong Kong.

758211.label: Major findings and research outcome
758211.value: While there is a substantial body of communication-oriented research on face-to-face genetic counselling, studies that have examined tele- (or distant) mode of counselling are scarce, particularly in the non-English dominant context such as Hong Kong. The project has made a considerable contribution to the existing body of research by investigating this mode of counselling in the designated context. The project has highlighted some important benefits of counselling using distant devices that can potentially have a major impact on the professional practice, particularly when genetic counselling services are increasingly used across various healthcare settings, and there is limited available professional workforce. The project has shown that unlike wide-spread beliefs that face-to-face counselling is more beneficial to clients, distant counselling presents a viable (and at times preferred) option. While in distant mode of communication professionals and clients lack non-verbal means of communication, these are compensated for by other discourse and rhetorical strategies (e.g. repetition) so that the goals of communication are successfully met. The project examined authentic data of audio- and video-recorded consultations and identified several major analytic themes of telegenetic counselling that include communicating risk and uncertainty; explanation- and advice-giving; decision-making; responsibility (parental and professional); reassurance (following receiving bad news/ diagnosis). The team also investigated the issues of professional roles and identities in the context of tele-medicine; and how genetic counselling in intercultural contexts differs from mono-cultural and mono-lingual genetic counselling (for specific outputs see the list of publications in Part C). By examining these analytic themes the team identified a range of linguistic (discourse and rhetorical) strategies that the participants of these tele-encounters employ to achieve their goals and to mediate potential challenges of communication. These findings have been incorporated into training activities that the team has organized during the running of the project and after its completion (workshops for professionals; the Winter School on Health Communication; MSc teaching). The findings have been reported in a number of publications in peer-reviewed linguistic and professional journals and prestigious edited volumes. The findings have also informed the development of client information resources (leaflet for clients with G6PD deficiency and their family/ carers). It is planned that the database of telegenetic counselling consultations that has been created during the project will be used for further research, teaching and training activities. Among project outputs are also a successful completion of a PhD thesis; provision of research experience for an undergraduate student.

758211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
758211.value: There are several potential for further developments of the project after its completion. First, the team has submitted another application to RGC for funding to investigate risk communication and decision making in genetic counselling across the lifespan of an individual. This future project will bring together the data corpora that the team has collected in the previous projects (in addition to a newly collected data in a different genetic counselling setting) to formulate more generalizable strategies that can be used by professionals regardless of the specific genetic context they are working in. The PI and other team members will continue to work on publications based on the collected data. It is also expected that the data will be included in presentations at local and international events (e.g. training activities for professionals; professional and interdisciplinary conferences). The results of the study will also be further disseminated to the student and professional community through the PI’s involvement into the MMedSc teaching programme at the Li Ka Shing Faculty of Medicine (HKU).

758211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
758211.value: The project took a communication-oriented perspective to investigate genetic counselling provided by distance (via telephone). In genetic counselling professionals meet with clients at risk of or diagnosed with a genetic disorder and discuss that disorder, clients’ risks and available testing. While face-to-face counselling has been widely researched, the distant mode has not received much attention. In addition, until recently there has been little research on counselling in non-English dominant contexts such as Hong Kong. The project has shown that while in counselling by telephone the participants do not have access to non-verbal means of communication (e.g. gestures), they employ a range of linguistic/ communication strategies that help them meet the aims of these consultations. The project has identifies some major themes of tele-counselling, such as communicating risk and uncertainty; responsibility (professional and parental); explanation- and advice-giving; decision-making. It has investigated the issues of professional roles and responsibilities; and the specifics of counselling in the designated non-English dominant context. The projects findings have been disseminated at local and international events (for language scholars and professionals) and published in prestigious international journals and edited collections. The findings have also been incorporated into teaching and training activities for medical students and professionals.

758211.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
758211.value: The PI was awarded the Faculty Knowledge Exchange Award (Faculty of Arts, HKU, 2013) for the project ‘Language and Communication in Genetic Counselling Settings in Hong Kong and South Asia’ The team ran two workshops for professionals involved in the provision of genetic counseling services in Hong Kong. The details of the workshops are as follows: Workshop “Communication in Genetic Counselling: Telephone Mode of Communication”, 20 August 2012 (Clinical Genetic Services, HK). Workshop “Discourse Analysis of Healthcare Communication”, 23 December 2011 (Clinical Genetic Services, HK). The PI established the Winter School on Health Communication targeted at professional practitioners, healthcare educators, researchers and others engaged in the field of healthcare communication. Feedback from participants commended the applicability of communication knowledge to the professional practice. The Winter Schools in 2012 and 2013 incorporated some findings of the project. The PI ic chairing Communication, Medicine and Ethics (COMET) conference that will take place at the University of Hong Kong on 25-27 June 2015. As part of the conference programme, the PI and other team members are organizing a panel on genetic counselling communication in Hong Kong and South East Asia. The findings of the project were also incorporated into teaching MMedSc in Genetic Counselling programme (HKU). Dr. Zayts mentored a group of undergraduate students and a PhD student (Alice Ho) who worked on building a website for professionals and caretakers of clients with genetic disorders and developing a leaflet campaign for the general public. The website was designed for two purposes: to disseminate project findings to practitioners and to provide an information resource for clients. Focus groups with clinicians and clients took place in May 2013. The team received constructive feedback on the design of the website and the leaflet. In the meetings it was decided that the leaflet would be passed to the Clinical Genetic Services of Hong Kong (Department of Health) for their consideration for use by medical professionals.

759011.label: Project Title(Chinese)
759011.value: 中国公司市场和科技能力的培养和价值：一个纵向和多层次的研究

759011.label: Project Objectives
759011.value: To understand how institutional environments affect the development of marketing and technology capabilities in emerging economies over time. To examine how the effects of institutional environments on marketing and technology capabilities vary for local versus foreign firms. To investigate which capability, marketing or technology, is more effective in fostering performance under different industrial dynamics. To provide important managerial implications for both local and foreign firms on how to develop marketing and technology capabilities to deal with dynamic institutional transitions and industrial uncertainties in China.

To examine how the effects of institutional environments on marketing and technology capabilities vary for local versus foreign firms.
To investigate which capability, marketing or technology, is more effective in fostering performance under different industrial dynamics.

To provide important managerial implications for both local and foreign firms on how to develop marketing and technology capabilities to deal with dynamic institutional transitions and industrial uncertainties in China.

759011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
759011.value: A firm’s growth and success depends critically on its core capabilities such as marketing and technology capabilities. Developing core capabilities also represents a vital strategy for firms operating in emerging economies. Considering the example of China, foreign invested firms contributed 27.2% of the total R&D expenditure in 2008 and the total number of R&D centers established by foreign firms has surged to 1,200 by the end of 2009 (Ministry of Commerce, China). Multinational companies also spend aggressively in their marketing campaigns to expand in the Chinese market. In response, local firms actively pursue R&D and marketing activities to survive the tough competition brought by foreign companies. Through learning and absorbing advanced technologies and marketing skills from their foreign counterparts, local firms update their technologies, develop their own unique know-how, and improve their marketing efficacy, which further intensify the competition and create significant challenges for foreign firms. Despite the great interest in the role of firm capabilities, limited attention has been paid to the development and contingent values of such capabilities. In this project, we focus on two critical firm capabilities: marketing and technology, and assess their growth and performance impacts in China. With a longitudinal dataset and a multilevel analysis, we will examine how institutional development affects marketing and technology capabilities for local and foreign firms differentially. We will also investigate how marketing and technology capabilities impacts firm performance differentially in changing industrial environments. Findings from this project will enhance our understanding of how to develop marketing and technology capabilities, especially in the context of Chinese fast-transition institutional environments. Moreover, the findings of this project will reveal under what conditions marketing and technology capabilities matter more in fostering firm performance. Therefore, this project will generate significant insights for both local and foreign firms competing in the Chinese market. 公司成长关键在于其核心能力（如营销能力和科技能力）。培养核心能力对新兴市场公司尤其重要。以中国为例，外资企业投入了巨额的研发投资并建立了在中国的研发中心；跨国公司同时也在中国展开了非常积极的营销战役。迫于其压力，本土公司积极地获取高新技术和营销技能。这引发了一系列的竞争，并对外资公司造成巨大挑战。 尽管当今文献对公司能力及其重视，在如何培养公司能力及对其价值的分析还有待研究。在这个项目里，我们着重于公司营销和科技能力的增长及绩效。通过一个纵向和多层次的分析，我们研究制度发展如何不同地影响本土和外资企业的营销和科技能力，以及营销和科技能力如何在变化的市场环境里影响公司绩效。 本项目的发现将会提高我们对如何培养市场和科技能力的理解，尤其在中国的转型经济中。本项目的发现也会展示市场和科技能力在什么情况下更加重要。因此，本项目会对本土和外资企业在中国的竞争和发展提供重要启示。

759011.label: Major findings and research outcome
759011.value: Major findings: 1) The improvement of institutional environments enhances the development of technology capability. Also, when competition intensifies or technology changes rapidly, firms increasingly develop their marketing or technology capabilities. 2) Companies in China also develop imitation capabilities. Creative imitation has a stronger positive effect on financial performance (i.e., lagged return on assets) than pure imitation. Furthermore, pure imitation and creative imitation, when coupled with strong marketing capability, positively affect market performance (i.e., market share). Compared with their local counterparts, foreign firms operating in China benefit less from pure and creative imitations in terms of financial performance. 3) As the market development progresses, marketing capability has a persistent effect on firm performance and technology capability exerts a stronger impact on performance. 4) Dysfunctional competition enhances the effect of technological speed, but legal inadequacy hinders the impact of technological radicalness on firm performance. Market growth strengthens the performance effect of technological speed but restrains the effect of technological radicalness. Technological radicalness demonstrates stronger effects on firm performance when demand uncertainty is high. 5) Technology capability leads to stronger differentiation advantage when foreign equity control is higher or operational control is greater. In contrast, marketing capability is more beneficial for differentiation advantage when foreign operational control is lower or social control is greater. 6) Technological diversity in supplier network positively affects buyer firms’ new product creativity. Such positive effect is enhanced by buyer–supplier relational strength but inhibited by supplier network density; competitive intensity positively moderates this effect, and technological turbulence negatively moderates it. Outcome: five papers published in peer-reviewed journals. 1) Gao GY, E Xie, KZ Zhou (2015), “How Does Supplier Network Drive Innovation of Buyer Firms? Technological Diversity, Network Features, and Market Forces,” Journal of Operations Management, 36(May), 165-177. 2) Zhou, KZ, JJ Li, S Sheng, and AT Shao (2014), “The Evolving Role of Managerial Ties and Firm Capabilities in an Emerging Economy: Evidence from China,” Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, 42(6), 581-595 (lead article) 3) Chen X, X Chen, KZ Zhou (2014), “Strategic Orientation, Foreign Parent Control, and Differentiation Capability Building of International Joint Ventures in an Emerging Market,” Journal of International Marketing, 22(3), 30-49 4) Sheng S, KZ Zhou, and Leopold Lessassy (2013), “NPD speed vs. innovativeness: The contingent impact of institutional and market environments,” Journal of Business Research, 66(11), 2355-2362. 5) Lee RP, and KZ Zhou (2012), “Is Product Imitation Good for Firm Performance? An Examination of Product Imitation Types and Contingency Factors,” Journal of International Marketing, 20(3), 1-16 (lead article).

759011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
759011.value: Based on the results of this project, we are working on a project: “Technology Spillovers between Foreign and Local Firms: Moderating Role of Geographic Proximity.” We plan to submit this paper to top-tier journals such as Strategic Management Journal.

759011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
759011.value: This project advances a framework to study the effects of marketing and technology capabilities in China. In particular, we have the following major findings: 1) Companies in China develop stronger marketing and technological capabilities to deal with environmental uncertainty. 2) The improvement of institutional environments motivates firms to develop technology capability. 3) Marketing capability has a persistent effect and technology capability exerts a stronger impact on performance when the market development progresses. 4) Local firms can benefit more from pure and creative imitations in terms of financial performance than foreign firms in China. 5) Technological radicalness has a stronger impact on performance when legal system improves and demand uncertainty is high. 7) Technological capability is more beneficial under tight control, whereas marketing capability is more effective with loose control. 8) Technological diversity is more valuable when competitive intensity is high and technological turbulence is low. The findings of this project not only enrich our understanding of the effects of marketing and technology capabilities in China, but also provide important managerial implications for both foreign and local companies on how to develop marketing and technology capabilities to deal with dynamic institutional transitions and industrial uncertainties in China.
