759111.label: Project Title(Chinese)
759111.value: 在金融危机时期的企业内部资本市场的有效性

759111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
759111.value: An important issue in corporate finance is the efficiency of internal capital markets. On one hand, firms can benefit from internal capital markets by carrying out transactions within the organization, thus avoiding possibly costly open-market transactions and achieving efficient resources allocation. On the other hand, internal capital allocations can be inefficient due to agency costs, because managers at the different levels in a firm may pursue private benefits at a cost to the firm. The empirical literature of internal capital markets has extensively examined conglomerate firms. With a few to several business segments, a conglomerate firm can realize resources allocations, through internal capital transfer, in a way that a stand-alone firm cannot. The evidence so far is inconclusive about the efficiency of internal capital markets. This project attempts to study internal capital markets by examining conglomerate firms around financial crises. In spite of a number of existing studies on the role of internal capital markets, little has been done to examine the time variation of this role. Both theory and intuition suggest that the functioning of internal capital markets changes with the availability of external capital that in turn fluctuates with the volatile financial market. When external financing becomes difficult, as during a financial crisis, one expects internal capital markets to become crucially important. Indeed, previous studies have found substantial changes in corporate investment and financing decisions during financial crises. By focusing on a comparison between crisis and non-crisis years, this study attempts to identify the role of internal capital markets in external-financing conditions that highlight its importance. It may also identify some effects that do not show up in previous studies that use samples dominated by normal market conditions. This study will address two related issues. First, are internal capital markets more (or less) active and efficient during crisis periods than during non-crisis periods? To answer this question, I will compare the size of internal capital markets and internal fund transfer mechanisms between crisis and non-crisis periods. Second, what is the effect of internal capital markets on the value of conglomerates and whether or how this effect differs between crisis and non-crisis periods? By addressing these issues, this study will provide evidence on the role of internal capital markets in contrasted external-financing conditions, and identify their effect on conglomerate valuation, in particular, during financial crises. 企业内部资本市场的有效性是企业金融领域的一个重要问题。一方面，通过内部资本市场，企业可以将有些交易在公司内部完成，从而避免外部市场交易的高成本，并实现资本资源的有效配置。另一方面，内部市场的代理人成本却会降低内部资本配置的有效性。代理人成本的发生取决于企业内部不同行业部门的管理层寻求不同于公司整体利益的决策。内部资本市场的实证文献已经对托拉斯（或集团公司）企业进行了广泛的研究。通过拥有若干个业务部门，集团公司可以实现单一行业公司所不能实现的资源配置。但是，现有的实证发现还不足以给内部资本市场的有效性下结论。 这项研究旨在通过考察金融危机时期的集团公司来分析企业内部资本市场的有效性。大量的研究已经分析了内部资本市场的作用。但是这种作用的时变性却没有受到关注。理论和常识告诉我们，内部资本市场的运作会随着外部金融市场状况的波动而变化。当外部融资变得很困难的时候（也就是当金融危机来临的时候），人们期望内部资本市场的作用变得尤其重要。的确，有研究表明，金融危机时期的企业投资和融资的决策行为是很不一样的。这个研究项目的目的就是通过比较有金融危机和没有金融危机时内部资本市场的区别，来突显其重要性。同时，这种比较还有可能使我们发现某些正常市场条件下不能发现的规律。 这个项目将会研究两个相关的问题。第一，在金融危机期间，内部资本市场是否变得更加活跃和更加有效？第二，内部资本市场如何影响企业业绩，并且这种对业绩的影响在金融危机期间是否变得更加显著？

760111.label: Co - Investigator(s)
760111.value: Prof Chan, Danny Prof Cheung, Kenneth Man Chee Dr Yan, CH

760111.label: Project Objectives
760111.value: To define the best combination of construct design and co-culture conditions for in vitro formation of osteochondral interface; To investigate the mechanism underlying the in vitro formation of the osteochondral interface; To evaluate the effectiveness of the optimized osteochondral constructs in a rabbit cartilage repair model.
rows: To define the best combination of construct design and co-culture conditions for in vitro formation of osteochondral interface;
To investigate the mechanism underlying the in vitro formation of the osteochondral interface;
To evaluate the effectiveness of the optimized osteochondral constructs in a rabbit cartilage repair model.

760111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
760111.value: Cartilage injuries are very common and a significant portion of them require surgical management. Existing surgical treatments have significant drawbacks. Tissue engineering offers great hope in cartilage repair but none has so far stood the test of time. In particular, the lack of an intact osteochondral interface with proper zonal organization in the construct design remains a major problem, among others. Engineering osteochondral interfaces have been receiving increasing attention recently. Different fabrication technologies, biomaterials and cells have been employed, but the results are far from being able to achieve the ultimate goal of simulating the structural zonal organization and the functional mechanical properties of the native osteochondral interface. Many challenges including establishing the optimal combination of cells and scaffolds, and achieving intimate integration with the host cartilage, remain to be tackled. The rationale of our proposed study is based on the observations that there are instructive cell-cell interactions between undifferentiated mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and their differentiated counterparts. Specifically, we aim to generate a biological osteochondral interface with zonal organization and mechanical properties simulating those of the native tissue in vitro. We have obtained encouraging preliminary data on the in vitro formation of a calcified cartilage zone as the interface between a non-calcified cartilage layer and a calcified bone layer in a bioengineered osteochondral construct made from MSCs and collagen. We will optimize the co-culture conditions to improve the performance of the interface and investigate the underlying mechanisms of the in vitro interface formation. The effectiveness of the optimized osteochondral construct will be evaluated in vivo using a well-established rabbit cartilage defect model. In the short term, this study leads to the development of engineered osteochondral constructs with biological interface and therefore may improve the outcomes of MSCbased cartilage repair. In the long run, this study shall contribute to the development of innovative technology for engineering complex tissues with multiple components and tissue interfaces, to offer better options for treating defective tissues. 在本項目中，我們旨在以生物工程學方法研制，用生物材料和病人自身間葉幹細胞合成的骨和軟骨的組織介面。研製穩固的組織介面是完善軟骨組織工程的先決條件。

760111.label: Realisation of objectives
760111.value: We have realized all objectives: Objective 1 We have studied many parameters during the construct design and the entire fabrication process including cell density, collagen concentration, time to differentiate and differentiation status of MSCs. Objective 2 We have studied the presence of secreted growth factors at different layers of construct with the hope to find out the gradients of such factors across the interface. We have also studied how the MSCs interact with the collagen material during the collagen microencapsulation process as we hypothesize that collagen microencapsulation recapitulates some early events during endochondral ossification and therefore facilitates osteochondral tissue engineeirng. Apart from those listed in Output section, one more manuscript is in preparation. Objective 3 We have conducted thorough rabbit animal study by inducing a large focal cartilage defect, which represents >85% area of the entire femoral condyle, and repaired by our osteochondral construct by comparing with two clinically relevant controls namely bone marrow stimulation and autografting (clinical gold standard). Since there are >100 animals in this study, we have just finished all analyses and the manuscript is being drafted but the results have been presented in some conferences.

760111.label: Major findings and research outcome
760111.value: Objective 1 We found that some parameters are crucial for the optimal fabricationA higher cell density such as 1e6 cells per ml, several days after microencapsulation such as 3 days, and preconditioning of the MSCs by differentiating them into chondrogenic and osteogenic for 14-21 days are important. We also find that presence of the osteochondral interface in vitro and serial application of the osteochondral and then chondrogenic layers during implantaton are able to regenerate the osteochondral interface, marked by the tidemark, at 1 month post-implantation. These parameters helped us to define the conditions for optimal construct fabrication. Objective 2 We found that the MSCs present in the middle layer highly expressed signaling molecules involved in terminal differentiation into hypertrophic chondrocytes including TGFbeta and BMP2, suggeting that these cells might secrete these molcules and act in an autocrinal manner on themselves in the interface. Moreover, we found that collagen microencapsulation but not coating culture dish with collagen induced early differentiation of MSCs towards chondrogenic and osteogenic lineages by elevation of sox9 and Runx2, crucial transcription factors governing chondrogenic and osteogenic differentiation. We did demonstrate that collagen microencapsulation recapitulates mesenchymal condensation, which represents early endochondral ossification. These mechanistic insights helped us to understand the outcomes of the current osteochondral tissue engineering approach. Objective 3 The results are excitingly promising. We have demonstrated that our osteochondral construct resulted in rapid regeneration of proper zonal organization including tidemark in 1 month's time, where the bone marrow stimulation was still filled with fibrous tissue. The presence of nice hyaline cartilage and bone integration persisted from 1 month to 6-12 months. The matrix composition and all the mechanical properties are comparable with the clinical gold standard autografting throughout the study period. The intrinsic advantage of our technology is that it does not need to hurt the patient's own cartilage and there is no size limit for the defect to be repaired.

760111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
760111.value: The collagen microencapsulation used during cartilage regeneration developed by this work may involve integrin and other matrix driven signaling events for MSC chondrogenesis and osteogenesis. The cell matrix interactions warrent research investigations in order to understand extracellular matrix driven influence on cell fate determination in stem cells. A GRF application as a further development on this part has been submitted in 2015-2016 round. On the application side, we are conducting a large animal model to evaluate the efficacy of the the osteochondral construct in minipigs and are preparing for clinical trials by working with orthopaedic surgeons.

760111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
760111.value: Cartilage injuries and diseases are very common. Cartilage has no blood vessels and therefore cannot heal on its own once injured. In the worst case, the knee joint has to be replaced by an artificial joint. This work contributes to a new cartilage regeneration technology, which is to grow cartilage tissues complete with underlying bone tissues in vitro, using the patient's own stem cells isolated from clinically accessible sources such as bone marrow. This "complex tissue plug" mimics the structural organization of native cartilage-bone tissues. By doing so, autografts are not required. Animal studies in rabbits have shown that replacing defects in knee joint cartilage with these tissue engineered cartilage-bone tissue plugs gives rapid and sustained regeneration of high quality cartilage with structure, composition and mechanical properties comparable to that of the clinical gold standard autografts. The use of these regenerative complex tissue plugs allows surgeons to use the same autograft surgical procedure to repair cartilage damages without the need to hurt the patients’ own cartilage. Currently, by working with orthopaedic surgeons, the research team is preparing to translate this technology for human applications.

760411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
760411.value: 細胞經常遇到內外的應激反應，包括內質網應激、低氧應激、氧化應激及核內應激。細胞在進化過程中需要為了存活而發展出各種機制來減輕或適應各種應激條件，否則其死亡程序會被啓動。內質網是細胞合成分泌性蛋白的工廠，細胞在內質網腔內進化出特定的膜蛋白來感應內質網承載量的變化。內質網應激通常可幫助細胞暫時降低蛋白質合成，並將有問題的蛋白質重新折疊或清除。目前對內質網應激的了解和認識都來自體外實驗，我們對體內的反應以及細胞在不同的發育和環境條件下的應激還知道得很少。我們過去對13del-MCDS突變型小鼠的研究表明，膠原X的突變可影響內質網中的蛋白質折疊，在生長板的肥大軟骨細胞中激活內質網應激，並導致疾病。值得注意的是，處於應激的細胞避免了凋亡，並啓動了細胞重分化的程序或回複到較早的不再表達膠原X的狀態，從而得以存活。軟骨中沒有血管，軟骨細胞處於低氧環境，需要激活低氧應激反應來保證細胞存活。此外，最近已發現低氧條件可在産生iPS細胞時促進細胞的重編程。因此我們假設，作為13del 小鼠中肥大軟骨細胞生存策略的一部分，內質網應激可激活低氧應激的一些通路。采用基因芯片進行基因表達分析，已表明13del小鼠生長板中確有特異的低氧反應基因被激活。通過比較我們的內質網應激體內分析結果及低氧條件下的培養細胞的類似結果，發現iASPP可能是連接這些應激反應通路的候選基因。此外，與我們的假設相符，iASPP在增生的軟骨細胞中正常表達，在肥大化時表達降低，但在13del小鼠中則因內質網應激的活化而維持。在本項研究中，我們的目標是研究低氧應激是否可抑制13del小鼠肥大軟骨細胞中ATF4和HIF1的表達，從而為應激狀態下的肥大軟骨細胞的存活所必需。我們也將研究正常和應激條件下iASPP作為橋梁分子的作用。同時，我們將采用我們已經建立的已適應內質網應激的ATDC5 軟骨祖細胞系作為體外模型，找出並測試在此信號串流過程中與iASPP特異性相互作用的蛋白質。細胞中的內質網應激和低氧應激對於保持正常發育的穩態非常重要，其失調可引致多種退行性疾病及癌症。我們的研究可提供新的知識，以便更好地了解細胞在決定其存活與分化時如何應對各種組合的應激信號，因此在其他器官的健康與疾病中也有更廣泛的價值和意義。

760411.label: Realisation of objectives
760411.value: Objective 1: To determine the relationship between ER and hypoxic stress in the regulation of hypertrophic chondrocyte adaptation to ER stress. A key reagent is the 13del-MCDS mice that we have generated with the expression of misfolded collagen X in hypertrophic chondrocytes activated the unfolded protein response (UPR) as part of the ER stress signal for survival. In this objective of the proposal, we have systematically asked a series of questions relating to the potential involvement and/association with ER stress that lead to survival and re-differentiation of hypertrophic chondrocytes, providing mechanistic insights into the pathology of MCDS. Its relevant to human MCDS is established through our detailed analysis of the skeletal abnormalities in the 13del-MCDS that recapitulated all know human characteristics of the disease. We performed qualitative and quantitative assessments of the 13del-MCDS skeletons and growth plate changes leading the chondrodysplasia outcome. We clearly showed and confirmed activation of ER stress in the developing and postnatal growth plates of long bone, with expansion of the hypertrophic zone that is dosage dependent for the mutant allele. This expression and level of changes also correlated with the re-differentiation of hypertrophic chondrocytes to proliferative chondrocyte. We also showed for the first time that a hypertrophic chondrocyte’s has the capacity for “complete” re-differentiation to a proliferating cell. As hyaline cartilages are avascular and are normally under hypoxia, we ask the question of the involvement of the hypoxic response in the survival mechanism of hypertrophic chondrocytes under ER stress. Indeed, using the EF5 assay for an in vivo assessment of cellular metabolism, we showed that there are more cells within the upper hypertrophic zone that are hypoxic, and this correlated with an up-regulated level of HIF1a and HIF2a proteins, major transducers of the hypoxic response pathway. Interestingly, we showed that up-regulation of HIF proteins is not related to their transcription, but more likely due to stabilization of the HIF proteins that were already present in the proliferative chondrocyte, capturing an existing survival pathway. Furthermore, there is a relationship with activation of FGF21 as part of the survival network of genes, with deletion of FGF21 in 13del mice leads to enhancement of apoptosis. Of significant interest is the presence of increase hypoxic signals in hypertrophic chondrocytes, and we showed that this is mostly related to an intrinsic change in cellular energy demand, with reduced dependent on mitochondrial function and more reliance on rapid flex in energy demand through maintenance of glucose level; thus, mimicking a hypoxic response with up-regulation of downstream targets such as Glut1, Hyou1, PGK1, VEGFA, Stc2, and Galectin3. This intrinsic response was further supported from a study using mouse chimeras containing both normal and 13del-MCDS chondrocytes in growth plates of long bones, clearing showing activation of hypoxic response in 13del-MCDS cells with neighboring normal cells being unaffected. Next, we ask possible relationship between cell survival and cell cycle reentry of “terminally differentiated” hypertrophic chondrocytes since its exit from the cell cycle may be related to the p53 pathway. Given that p53 is also involve in ER stress, it was logical and we again showed a correlation with the maintenance of survival and differential stabilization of iASSP proteins in hypertrophic chondrocytes under ER stress, similar to HIF proteins, although the exact mechanism was not determined. In this 13del-MCDS-mouse model, we showed for the first time that hypertrophic chondrocytes could be induced to become proliferative chondrocytes via activation of ER stress. This was evidence in 4-week-old 13del-MCDS homozygous mice that has not been detected with other mouse models previously described. This provided an ideal opportunity for us to assess a unique observation of two consecutive rounds of chondrocyte proliferation, follow by hypertrophy within one growth plate. Here, we identified a complete clearance of intracellular misfolded collagen X proteins prior to progression of the cell cycle through the S phase that were positive for BrdU labeling. Importantly, we showed a clear correlation with activation of autophagy, a highly efficient cellular system for degradation and recycling of cellular protein. Objective 2: To test the role of ATF4/iASSP in integrating ER and hypoxic stress pathways. In this objective, an initiate focus was on the iASSP protein. However, given the significant finding we have with the HIF proteins and the availability of the iASSP mice, we redirect a focus on the PERK pathway as in hypoxic response, this sensor of the UPR is utilized for cell survival. Therefore, it was intriguing to ask whether the reverse is also possible, and this was supported from a publication in cells that if cells were first primed under hypoxic condition cultured under low oxygen tension, they can better manage ER stress for survival. Given that the major transducer of the PERK sensor is the preferential translation of ATF4, this was a clear candidate for further assessment. The involvement of ATF4 was assessed in vivo by the generation of transgenic mice over-expression ATF4 in hypertrophic chondrocytes under the regulation of the Col10a1 promoter (Col10a1-ATF4). These mice showed growth plate changes similar to 13del-MCDS mice with an expanded hypertrophic zone; and significantly, maintained a high level of HIF1a and HIF2a proteins. This supports a major role of the PERK sensor and ATF4 in capturing the hypoxic response of proliferative chondrocytes as they enter hypertrophy in 13del-MCDS mice. Similarly, iASSP proteins are also maintained in hypertrophic zone of Col10a1-ATF4 mice, suggesting again, a relationship with protein stabilization in the survival mechanism and possible involvement of the p53 pathway in cell cycle reentry. Objective 3: To assess the role of ATF4/iASSP in endochondral ossification The expanded hypertrophic zone in Col10a1-ATF4 transgenic mice also correlates with up-regulation of many chondrogenic genes as assessed by in situ hybridization. This included Sox9, Col2a1, Acan, and Ihh. This is analogous with the observation of cellular re-differentiation of hypertrophic chondrocytes back to proliferative chondrocytes in 13del-MCDS mice. This suggests that chondrocyte re-differentiations involves in part if not all are contributed by the expression/translation of ATF4 upon activation of ER stress in 13del-MCDS mice. Given that Sox9 is a major or master transcriptional regulator of chondrocytes; using a combination of tools and cell assays, we showed that the presence of ATF4 binding sites within the Sox9 promoter, directly binding of the ATF4 to these sites and transactivation the Sox9 gene in reporter assays. Thus, this is a major finding in providing a new role for ATF4 in the regulation of chondrocyte differentiation and endochondral ossification. Furthermore, using a similar approach, we showed that ATF4 could also transcriptionally activate Fgf21. Whether Fgf21 has a role in endochondral ossification is not clear, but a role in bioenergetics of cell survival under stress conditions is established from our finding.

760411.label: Major findings and research outcome
760411.value: The major findings in this project can be divided into three conceptual areas representing one publication and two manuscripts at the final stage of refinement for submission. These are all included in this report as reference. Manuscript titled “Interplay between survival signals of cellular stress pathways in the pathogenesis of Metaphyseal Chondrodysplasia type Schmid ” showed that our mouse model for MCDS truly represents the human disease, and we provided descriptive and functional assessments of the 13del-MCDS mice demonstrating the involvement or activation of multiple cellular stress pathways that included the PERK sensor of the unfolded protein response (UPR), the role of ATF4 in stabilization of HIF proteins and iASSP that link the survival to cell cycle retry, and the clearance of unfolded protein through autophagy in an integrated and synergistic mechanism for survival. Manuscript entitled “The PERK pathway attenuates ER stress in hypertrophic chondrocytes via SOX9 and FGF21” highlighted the major finding that ATF4 is a key regulator of Sox9 and Fgf21 transcription, linking its role in chondrogenesis and thus the re-differentiation of hypertrophic chondrocytes via activation of Sox9; and Fgf21 for cell survival and possibility involved in the metabolic switch in energy demand. Publication entitled “Label-Free Quantitative Proteomics Reveals Survival Mechanisms Developed by Hypertrophic Chondrocytes under ER Stress” provided the link to uncoupling of the mitochondria to ER, and the maintenance of glucose supply for a rapid energy supply needed to alleviate cellular stress. The major findings in this project have been presented at many regional and international conferences that were well received. A best poster prize was received in one of the conferences.

760411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
760411.value: The findings from this project open a number of fundamental questions that need further studies. An interest is the role of FGF21 in the survival strategy of cellular stress, and the mechanism involved. FGF21 have other functions such as the browning of white/beige adipose tissues, in the switch between the utilization of metabolic process in the generation of energy (oxidative phosphorylation or glycolysis), and the cell’s need for energy, balancing rate and flex of energy supply for cell survival. This part is currently being tested in another funded GRF project aiming to understanding this from proteomic and metabolic changes in 13del-MCDS mice with an inactive Fgf21 gene. The finding from this project will also have implications in patients with obesity and diabetes. Given that we have demonstrated a significant contribution of the PERK sensor in the disease mechanism for MCDS, pharmacological treatment of the disease become feasible and can be consider with chemicals that targets this sensor specifically. This possibility is further supported by the characteristic of the 13del-MCDS mice having all the phenotypes of the human disease, a “clinical trial” in mice can be considered, and we propose to apply for an HRMF grant for this particular study.

760411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
760411.value: Cells, as in our daily life, are constantly under different types of stress, and like us, stress needs to be managed, otherwise, problems will develop. In the context of a cell, it could affect its survival, differentiation/changes that could be detrimental. How cells can manage stress is an important subject to understand and we have provide insights using a mouse model for a human disease causing dwarfism. We showed that cells in a growing bone could capture survival signals in the cell to carry out its task for an integrated stress management. However, this may not always be a good sign, as if this happens in the wrong context in development or disease progression, the problem could further escalate. However, by knowing what the changes are, we can understand how to help cells to manage the stress and direct it towards a positive outcome, and in drug development for rare and common diseases. Given that there are drugs available that target specific stress signals in cells, these can be tested in the future, not only for the skeletal disorder studied in this project, but could have far reaching implications to control cell fate of other diseases including cancer cells.

760511.label: Realisation of objectives
760511.value: All the objectives have been completed and some were even overfullfil. To aim 1, due to the reduced budget, the size exclusion chromatography (SEC) assay to identify AMPK complex and free form of AMPK-γ2 hasn’t been performed. However, we had performed immuno-depletion and fluorescent gel retardation assays and confirmed that AMPK-γ2 could be exist as free form. Additionally, we also found that AMPK-γ1 is higher affinity to form AMPK complex than AMPK-γ2. Besides, the overexpression of R531G AMPK-γ2 mutant showed that the CBS motifs on AMPK-γ2 are required for binding of ZMP/AMP. On the other hand, instead of using radioisotope of AMARA to measure the in vitro AMPK activity, we demonstrated AMPK-γ2 is stronger than AMPK-γ1 in suppression of AMP-induced AMPK activity using in vitro AMPK Kinase Assay (CycLex AMPK Kinase Assay). Extra works also included the Q-PCR analysis to evaluate all the isoforms of AMPK in ovarian cancer, endometrial cancer, cervical cancer and choriocarcinoma cells. Of course, the roles of AMPK-γ2 in ovarian cancer cells was performed accordingly. To aim 2, the functional roles of wildtype and R531G mutant AMPK-γ2 as well as AMPK-γ1 were examined using ovarian cancer cell models and in vivo mouse model. To aim 3, we further confirmed that AICAR-overexpressing A2780cp cells had less tumor suppressive effect mediated by AICAR by in vivo mouse model. Moreover, given that AMPK-γ2 suppresses AMPK activity via completely binding of ZMP or AMP, we tested other pharmaceutical AMPK activators e.g. metformin, A23187 and A 769662 and showed that AMPK-γ2 inhibits AMPK activity by ATP-dependent manner. Finally, we used ovarian cancer tissue arrays to show that the expression of AMPK-γ2 is inversely correlated with p-AMPK level and is significantly correlated with advanced stage ovarian cancer. In summary, all the aims have been finished. However, our collaborator, Prof. Hardie, have discussed the data recently and suggested that if we want to publish in high-tier impact journals such as Cancer cell or Cell Metabolism, extra works need to be done. He suggested that we need to use mass spectrometry to confirm the AMPK-γ2 isoforms, and what other interacting partners exist to stabilize AMPK-γ2 as a free form. We also need to knockdown AMPK-γ1 to determine whether it is dominant form AMPK complex or it could be replaced by AMPK-γ2. These extra works are ongoing and hopefully they can be completed within 3 months (before Jan. of 2016).

760511.label: Major findings and research outcome
760511.value: The major findings of this study include: 1. The increased expression of AMPK-γ2 subunit leads to differential responses of AMPK activity in ovarian cancer cells under micro-environmental stresses. 2.Hypoxia or glucose starvation stresses could reduce AMPK-γ2 expression and increase AMPK activity in some but not all of ovarian cancer cells. 3. Increased expression of AMPK-γ2 and reduced AMPK activity are associated with advanced-stage ovarian cancers. 4. Increased AMPK-γ2 promotes ovarian cancer cell growth, cell survival, anchorage-independent growth capacity and in vivo tumor growth. 5. AMPK-γ2 but not AMPK-γ1 subunit could inhibit AICAR-mediated AMPK activation. 6. Mutation at CBS of AMPK-γ2 impairs its capacity in inhibition of AICAR-mediated AMPK activation. 7. AMPK-γ2 subunit forms free form and completes with AMPK complex for AMP/ZMP binding. 8. AMPK-γ2 could not affect other pharmaceutical AMPK activators such as A23187, metformin and A769662. The research outcome: 1. One PhD project which include part of AMPKg2 findings. 2. A number of peer-reviewd abstracts presented in local and international conferences. 3. Increase collaboration and assisted in other projects in grant application such as Prof. Hardie's AMPK proposal for UK Cancer Council and HMRF proposals about using natural AMPK e.g. bitter melon extract or its bioactive compound MAP30 in targeting ovarian cancer chemoresistance. 4. One paper is under preparation for high impact factor journals.

760511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
760511.value: We and others have found that AMPK activity is higher in early stage of tumor formation but is gradually reduced during tumor progression. Hence, it is commonly found that advanced stage human cancer cells prefer low AMPK activity to sustain their high cell proliferation and tumor growth rate. Our study report that AMPK-γ2 acts as an inhibitor to fine turn AMPK activity from early to advanced stage of ovarian cancer, suggesting that we provide new direction for not only understanding the tumor progression but also assisting the development of new therapeutic interventions for this disease. On the other aspect, according to the recent studies and clinical trials, the pharmacologic AMPK activators have great potential used as novel agents in the treatment of human cancers. However, the inherent variability of the sensitivity to growth arrest by the AMP-mimeric AICAR in different cancer cells may hinder the feasibilities of using these pharmacologic AMPK activators as cancer therapeutic agents. The understanding of the molecular mechanism and functional roles of AMPK-γ2 could help to improve the application of pharmacologic AMPK activators as therapeutic agents in ovarian cancer.

760511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
760511.value: Despite advances in diagnosis and treatment, the incidence of ovarian cancer is rising and the associated mortality rate has not been improved significantly over the past decade. Therefore, discovery of novel targets for therapies will improve the quality of life of patients. Targeting cancer cell metabolism with chemotherapeutics is a new promising strategy. AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) is an energy-sensor that maintains energy homeostasis in eukaryotic cells. Accumulating evidence has shown that AICAR, the common pharmacological AMPK activator, can suppress cancer cell growth and may be a potential therapeutic drug against cancer. However, the inhibitory response of AICAR varies in different cancer cell types, and the reason for this inherent variability remains unclear. In this study, we provided evidence showing AMPK-γ2, a subunit of AMPK, is aberrantly overexpressed. The overexpressed AMPK-γ2 not only inhibits the activity of AMPK induced by AICAR but also enables the progression of ovarian cancer. We believe the understanding of the underlying molecular mechanism and functional roles of AMPK-γ2 in modulation of AMPK activity will significantly advance our understanding of carcinogenesis and improving the application of pharmacologic AMPK activators as therapeutic agents in ovarian cancer.

760911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
760911.value: 肝細胞癌（HCC）香港是香港最普遍癌症中的一種。在切除術以外的現有對肝癌的治療，最初可能使腫瘤縮小，但未能予以根治。病情復發乃由於腫瘤起始細胞，或又稱癌症幹細胞的耐藥性。這些含幹細胞樣特徵和數量有限的癌症幹細胞能夠擊敗常規療法。我們和其他人已經確定了肝癌症幹細胞的特點是其表面CD133的表型和包括能夠自我更新，分化成非肝細胞樣及血管肌細胞樣系列細胞，和在體內啟動腫瘤等等功能。這些細胞被發現能透过激活AKT / PKB和Bcl-2的生存途徑来促進細胞的化療耐藥性，并可能代表着化療後的腫瘤復發源。通過对CD133+肝癌細胞作基因表達圖譜分析，連同Genespring和Ingenuity Pathway Analysis等分析，我們最近發現了白細胞介素8（IL-8）能顯著改變信令網。我們還在从新鮮切除的人體臨床標本隔離以及肝癌細胞株的CD133+癌症幹細胞觀察到內源性和分泌性兩種IL-8的先取上調。我們已經有初步證據顯示上調的IL-8在CD133+癌症幹細胞起著部分提高自我更新，誘導腫瘤生長和促進血管內皮細胞生成血管等機能。我們假設CD133+肝癌症幹細胞可能通過上調產生的IL-8来維護和發展癌症幹細胞。在這項研究中，我們的目標是（1）測量和比较在臨床新鮮肝癌組織整理出的CD133+癌症幹細胞和CD133-細胞和病人血清標本中的內源性和分泌性IL-8;（2）澄清IL-8在CD133+肝癌症幹細胞中能否起到推動肝癌的作用，（3）在動物體內檢验單獨或與傳統的化療藥物使用IL-8作為一個對付CD133+癌症幹細胞的潛在治療靶點。這將是第一個探討IL-8和CD133+癌症幹細胞驅動肝癌關係的研究。我們的研究將進一步让我們了解這個肝癌症幹細胞和肝癌的演化過程，並对這一致命疾病的靶向治療开展一道新的曙光。

760911.label: Realisation of objectives
760911.value: 1. Serum specimens, fresh human liver tumor and adjacent non-tumor tissues were obtained from 12 patients undergoing hepatectomy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Analyses showed a positive correlation between CD133 and endogenous and secreted IL-8 in these patients. Preferential expression of both endogenous and secreted IL-8 was identified in CD133+ subpopulations, compared to the CD133- subpopulations. Objective 1 has been fully achieved. 2. A series of laboratory experiments on liver cancer cell lines were carried out. We observed a strong relationship between the expression of CD133, IL-8, NTS and CXCL1 in CD133+ liver cancer initiating cells and a panel of HCC cell lines with varying CD133 expression. Our in vivo study revealed that these CD133- repressed clones possessed reduced tumorigenic potential, as indicated by reduced tumor incidence and size, reduced tumor angiogenesis and proliferation, and increased apoptosis, as indicated by immunostaining for CD34, PCNA and TUNEL. These results suggest that CD133, apart from serving as a marker for liver TICs, also possesses a functional role in TIC properties. The function appears to be mediated, at least in part, by the NTS-induced IL-8 signaling cascade. Objective 2 has been fully achieved. 3. IL-8 neutralizing antibody commercially purchased, alone or in combination with cisplatin, was administered to immunodeficient mice xenografted with CD133 expressing Huh7 HCC cells and CD133 expressing patient-derived xenograft. As expected, mice treated with IL-8 neutralizing antibody showed a marked regression in tumor volume; while mice treated with IL-8 neutralizing antibody and cisplatin in combination showed an additive effect in reducing tumor size. The findings show that IL-8 neutrolizing antibodies could be effective in the treatment of HCC. Objective 3 has been fully achieved.

760911.label: Major findings and research outcome
760911.value: 1. Screening a panel of liver cell lines revealed that IL-8 expression was strongly correlated with the expression of CD133. We found a positive correlation between CD133 and endogenous and secreted IL-8 across the panel of liver cell lines. Preferential expression of both endogenous and secreted IL-8 was identified in CD133+ subpopulations isolated from Huh7 and PLC8024 cell lines, compared to the CD133- subpopulations. Similar observations were also consistently found in CD133+ cells isolated from human HCC samples. 2. We determined the mechanistic pathway linking CD133 and IL-8 after having observed a strong relationship between the expression of CD133, IL-8, NTS and CXCL1 in CD133+ liver TICs and a panel of HCC cell lines with varying CD133 expression. We found that in CD133 knockdown cells, down-regulation of IL-8, NTS, CXCL1 and RAF-1 was observed. Suppression of IL-8 signaling by CD133 knockdown resulted in a significant reduction in the ability of these cells to self-renew, as demonstrated by spheroid formation in vitro. Our in vivo study revealed that these CD133-repressed clones possessed reduced tumorigenic potential, as indicated by reduced tumor incidence and size, reduced tumor angiogenesis and proliferation, and increased apoptosis, as indicated by immunostaining for CD34, PCNA and TUNEL. These results suggest that CD133, apart from serving as a marker for liver TICs, also possesses a functional role in TIC properties. The function appears to be mediated, at least in part, by the NTS-induced IL-8 signaling cascade. 3. IL-8 neutralizing antibody, alone or in combination with cisplatin, was administered to immunodeficient mice xenografted with CD133 expressing Huh7 HCC cells and CD133 expressing patient-derived xenograft. Mice treated with IL-8 neutralizing antibody showed a marked regression in tumor volume; while mice treated with IL-8 neutralizing antibody and cisplatin in combination showed an additive effect in reducing tumor size. The findings show that IL-8 neutralizing antibodies could be effective in the treatment of HCC.

760911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
760911.value: Following the exciting in vitro and in vivo findings based on this funded project, we recently began collaboration with Cormorant Pharmaceuticals (Sweden) for the use of a humanized IL-8 antibody (HuMAX IL-8) in the targeting of liver cancer stem cells.

760911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
760911.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a common and deadly liver cancer. Our studies aimed at establishing the mechanisms of how CD133 expression in some of the HCC cancer cells could lead to their enhanced resistance to the usual anti-cancer drugs. The linkage of CD133 expression with IL-8 production in HCC was determined and our studies further determined some of the mediators in their inter-related pathway. A clear understanding of the IL-8 activation pathway can provide a rational approach to a search of effective means of treating HCC. We evaluated the use of IL-8 neutralizing antibody in the treatment of human HCC transplanted into mouse and had observed a promising treatment response that would be followed up by further studies. Our studies have made significant contribution to the current understanding of HCC and open up new hopes to finding effective new therapy against this deadly cancer.

761511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
761511.value: C-type lectin receptors (CLRs) constitutes a family of heterogeneous proteins on cell surface that bind a wide variety of micro-organisms and play an important role in shaping the immune responses against invading pathogens. Recent evidence also shows that some CLRs can recognize endogenous ligands that associated with damaged cells and contribute to autoimmunity. Upon ligand interaction, CLRs induce specific gene expression to initiate a diverse range of immunological responses including cytokines/chemokines production and modulation of functions and differentiation of other immune cells; and thus play a key role in immunity. C-type lectin domain family 16 member A (CLEC16A) is a newly identified but un-characterized CLR-like protein which is known to have genetic association with a number of autoimmune disorders including type I diabetes, multiple sclerosis, rheumatoid arthritis and Crohn’s disease. Our genome-wide association study also shows that this gene may contribute to the development of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), a chronic and potentially fatal autoimmune inflammatory disease commonly seen in Chinese. CLEC16A is expressed exclusively in immune cells including dendritic cells, the key controller of immune responses; however its role in the immune system has never been revealed. In this project, we will characterize the function(s) of this novel CLR-like protein and map out its contribution in the immune response initiation/modulation processes. To further delineate the functional connection of CLEC16A in SLE development, we will also examine its expression in SLE patients’ immune cells and correlate with disease susceptibility as well as severity. Currently, the powerful clinical application of CLR immunobiology is gaining momentum but yet largely un-explored. This study will undoubtedly open up a new and resourceful avenue for exploring and identifying potential therapeutic targets for immunological intervention, particularly in the area of immunotherapy and vaccine delivery/targeting. Furthermore, this study also signifies the importance of establishing a platform to incorporate expertise in molecular genetics and cellular biology in order to substantiate the findings in genetic studies, so as to bring us one-step closer to the realization of the promises beheld in genomics research. 研究概要 C-型凝集素受體群組是由一撮駁雜的細胞表皮蛋白質組成。不同的C-型凝集素受體會與不同的微生物結合，並引發一連串的免疫反應以對抗病原體的入侵。最近的研究發現某類C-型凝集素受體能識別由破損細胞產生的內生配體，並與自體免疫病變的產生有關。當C-型凝集素受體與相應的配體連合時，會令相關連的基因轉錄及表達，因而誘發多種免疫反應，包括細胞因子或趨化因子的製造、免疫細胞功能的調節及轉化等，所以，C-型凝集素受體在免疫系統上扮演一個相當重要的角色。 C-型凝集素區域群組16分子A (CLEC16A) 是一個剛被發現的擬C-型凝集素受體。有研究發現它跟多種自體免疫病變，如一型糖尿病、多發性硬化症、類風濕性關節炎和克隆氏症等疾病有基因聯系。早前，我們的全基因組關聯分析發現CLEC16A基因可能與系統性紅斑狼瘡症的形成有關。系統性紅斑狼瘡症是一種可致命的慢性自體免疫炎症，在華人中比較常見。 CLEC16A 只在免疫細胞表達，而免疫系統的主要指揮樹突細胞是其中之一。鑑於至今科學界對於CLEC16A的功能仍未了解，我們會針對它於免疫反應的誘發以及調節機制作出深入研究。同時，我們將檢閱CLEC16A在系統性紅斑狼瘡症病人免疫樹突細胞裏的表達，以了解它跟病發與病情進展的關係。現在，有愈來愈多文獻針對研究C-型凝集素受體的功能，但其臨床運用並未被深入探索。這研究項目可為治療自體免疫症的方法開拓嶄新的研究方向，特別為免疫療法及疫苗輸送方面帶來新的研究意念。此研究亦是一個分子遺傳學及細胞生物學的融合平台，用以確立基因研究的結果，從而進一步實現基因組學的研究成果。

761511.label: Realisation of objectives
761511.value: The primary goal of objective 1 was to elucidate the function of the novel CLEC16A protein. As mentioned in the last progress report, the CLEC16A protein was found to be an intracellular protein rather than as originally speculated, a cell surface protein. Thus we re-designed new experiments to investigate its functions, which may deviate from our original hypothesis. First, by immunofluorescence staining, the exact subcellular localization of this protein was revealed. Judging from its vesicular appearance and re-distribution under nutrient deprivation, we tested a new hypothesis on its involvement in autophagy. Using both CLEC16A over-expressing and knockdown cell lines and tested with two different approaches of autophagy induction, our results showed that this protein indeed was involved in autophagy pathway. Along the same objective, we also identified the molecular target in the autophagy signaling pathway by which CLEC16A might act upon, and mediate modulation in autophagy response. Thus, a mechanism for its function in autophagy was also established. Overall, the goal of objective 1 was achieved. The goal of objective 2 was to study CLEC16A isoforms expressions in peripheral blood leukocytes in relation to SLE disease development. In total, we enrolled 190 SLE patients and 86 healthy controls for blood donation. We established a molecular platform to quantitatively measure the expression levels of the two major spliced variants of CLEC16A. Statistical analyses were performed to correlate CLEC16A expression levels with SLE susceptibility, disease severity and twelve relevant clinical parameters. A significant association was found in the expression level with SLE susceptibility. Therefore, objective 2 was also completed.

761511.label: Major findings and research outcome
761511.value: For objective 1, the major findings were: a) CLEC16A was found to be an intracellular protein expressed in special vesicles; b) under steady state, some of the CLEC16A protein was found in vesicles of the Golgi network; c) in nutrient-deprived state, CLEC16A re-localized peri-nuclearly with increase co-localization with Golgi vesicles; d) by total nutrient starvation and serum deprivation, over-expressing CLEC16A cells exhibited delayed and reduced autophagy; while CLEC16A knockdown cells displayed enhanced autophagic flux; e) CLEC16A mediated inhibition of autophagy was found to be associated with an increase in phosphorylation of ULK, which is an upstream signaling molecule involved in the mTOR-mediated autophagy A manuscript (title: Golgi-associated CLEC16A negatively regulates starvation-induced autophagy) consolidating these findings is now in preparation and is anticipated to be ready for submission in 2015. An abstract of the manuscript is submitted in Part C. For objective 2, the major findings were: a) two alternatively spliced isoforms of CLEC16A RNA transcripts, namely V1 and V2, were expressed by peripheral leukocytes from healthy controls and SLE patients; b) the longer V1 was significantly more abundant than the shorter V2 isoform; c) a significantly lower expression levels of both V1 and V2 was found in SLE patients than in controls; d) a significant correlation was observed between V1 expression and SLE disease activity; e) no significant correlation was found between expression levels of either V1 or V2 with the 12 clinical parameters analysed. These findings has yielded a manuscript titled “Systemic lupus erythematosus patients exhibit reduced CLEC16A expression in peripheral leukocytes”, which has been submitted for consideration of publication (Response from IJMS Journal Editor and the submitted manuscript are attached in part C).

761511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
761511.value: Autophagy is a fundamental homeostasis process dealing with stress and thus also plays an important role in infection, inflammation and immunity. Several recent publications have unraveled a negative regulatory role of autophagy in the activation of inflammasomes, which are unique molecular scaffolds of cytosolic protein complexes that mediate the activation cleavage of inflammatory cytokine IL-1β an innate immune response. Our findings in the involvement of CLEC16A in autophagy have paved the way for a new project to study the role of CLEC16A in linking these two important pathways. We have already performed knockdown experiments to study CLEC16A in inflammasome induction in cells of immune origin (a monocyte cell line). Preliminary results showed that inflammasome induction was also dysregulated in the absence of CLEC16A. Based on these preliminary results, a completely new proposal has been drawn up (title: CLEC16A in autophagy and inflammation) and submitted for application of RGC General Research Fund in 2015-16 to the study how CLEC16A link up and mediate cross-regulation in these two pathways. Results from this new proposal will likely to have significant implications in understanding the role of CLEC16A in the pathogenesis of SLE, or in other autoimmune disorders that are genetically-linked with CLEC16A polymorphisms.

761511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
761511.value: CLEC16A is genetically linked to many autoimmune disorders including lupus (SLE), but the function of this novel protein is largely unknown. Aiming to elucidate its functions by constructing cell line models that either over-expressed or deficient in CLEC16A, this project has demonstrated a significant role of CLEC16 in autophagy – an evolutionary conserved cellular recycling process that promotes cell survival under stress conditions. In addition, a significant reduction in CLEC16A expression in the peripheral blood cells of SLE patients has been found, suggesting that this novel gene may functionally contribute to lupus disease development. The impact of these findings can be envisaged at two levels: CLEC16A is playing a functional and active role in a fundamental process that shapes cellular homeostasis, and thus may have pathological implications in organismic developmental processes. This is in accordance to the developmental defects seen in mice with CLEC16A deficiency. Second, CLEC16A dysregulated expression may perturb the immunological balance maintained in physiological conditions, and thereby enhances disease susceptibility in autoimmunity in general. Our findings serve to warrant further investigations to unravel the underlying mechanisms, and by which may potentially source new therapeutics for clinical application.

761711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
761711.value: 我們假設，在發育關鍵期間，丘腦利用前庭訊息來執行空間導航。我們將首先探索老鼠丘腦內的空間圖譜在發育時如何形成，並確定丘腦的方向細胞對空間認知的反應。我們並測試在初生老鼠前庭核內，減低谷氨酸突觸或氨基丁酸突觸的功能，是否能夠改變丘腦內的空間圖譜及丘腦內方向細胞的相關反應，另外，我們將探討發育關鍵期對建立從前庭核到丘腦的神經通路所扮演的角色，以及其對空間定位學習的影響。總括而言，我們這項研究的結果將會讓我們更了解丘腦細胞在發育期內的可塑性，並且能進一步揭示此等神經細胞在處理三維空間和空間行為認知的運作機制。

761711.label: Realisation of objectives
761711.value: Using the expression of immediate early gene c-fos as an indicator for functionally activated neurons, we revealed that topographic maps representing gravity-and canal-related head movements in three dimensions are generated in relay stations of the central vestibular pathway, such as the thalamus and inferior olive, during postnatal maturation of rats. With the use of neuronal tracing technique, we further verified that both neural regions received direct projection from the vestibular nucleus. To investigate the relationship between the firing patterns of thalamic neurons and head orientation, extracellular recording was conducted in thalamic nuclei. In anaesthetized rats, individual thalamic neurons in response to 360o off-vertical axis rotation were found to exhibit best response orientations. To correlate the firing patterns of thalamic neurons with directional heading during spatial navigation, multichannel extracellular recording was conducted in the anterodorsal thalamic nucleus of freely moving rats during spatial reckoning test. We observed that thalamic neurons discharge as a function of head direction. The responsiveness of these neurons to preferred head directions became finely tuned after the third postnatal week. To study the role of thalamus on spatial navigation, the impact of lesion of specific thalamic subnuclei was evaluated. Electrolytic lesion of different thalamic subnuclei resulted in impairment of different parameters of spatial reckoning behavioral task, indicating that thalamic subnuclei exhibit differential roles in spatial navigation. To determine whether glutamatergic or GABAergic transmission within the vestibular nucleus is crucial for developmental display of spatial navigation, Elvax slice loaded with MK801 or bicuculline was implanted at postnatal day 1 over the ventricular side of the vestibular nucleus. These rats, upon reaching adulthood, exhibited impairments in motor co-ordination (as indicated by rota-rod test) and in spatial navigation (as indicated by dead reckoning test). These rats also exhibited a derangement in spatial maps within the thalamus and inferior olive. Such deficits in both the topographic spatial map and sensori-motor behaviors were not observed in adult rats if MK801- or bicuculline-loaded Elvax was implanted after the second postnatal week. We have therefore identified a critical period of susceptibility for the refinement of central vestibular circuitry that is responsible to the execution of spatial navigation.

761711.label: Major findings and research outcome
761711.value: We revealed within the thalamus and inferior olive a spatial topography that encodes translational and rotational movements in three dimensions. Such topographic maps are established progressively during postnatal maturation. By delivering sinusoidal wobble rotations, that simultaneously activate otolith organ and semicircular canal, to conscious adult rats, we demonstrated that synergistic input derived from the integration of head velocity and direction signals enhances the recruitment of thalamic neurons for encoding spatiotemporal cues of balance. In freely moving rats, thalamic neurons were found to discharge as a function of head direction, thereby encoding head orientations. Narrowly tuned thalamic neurons to preferred head directions emerged after the third postnatal week. The role of the thalamus on spatial navigation was revealed with lesion of specific thalamic subnuclei. The mediodorsal thalamic nucleus and zone incerta of rats were found to be essential for spatial navigation whereas the subparafascicular thalamic nucleus appeared to be more important for updating head directional information for precise spatial reckoning. We have thus illustrated that comprehensive capability in spatial navigation is dependent on normal functioning of the thalamic nuclear complex. We revealed for the first time that refinement of glutamatergic and GABAergic transmission in neonatal vestibular nucleus is crucial for the formation of a central vestibular network, that includes thalamus and inferior olive, for spatial topography that impacts on behavioral expression of vestibular functions in adult rats. We further identified a postnatal critical period for the establishment of such a functional neural circuitry for the display of spatial navigation.

761711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
761711.value: We are the first group to demonstrate that an internal neural representation for spatial perception exists in the central vestibular circuitry. Our findings open up a novel research direction about the role of the thalamus in integrating sensory information for spatial navigation. Research in these directions will shed light on the design of drugs for thalamus-based strategies that could rescue disorders for restoration of balance function. Furthermore, our findings provide the basis for investigations on the processing of cross-modal plasticity mediated by the sensory thalamus. In the future, optogenetics technique can be used to delineate the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the transformation of sensory cues of balance into head-direction signals during maturation of the central vestibular circuitry. Data made available will unveil our understanding on interaction among neural pathways, and in turn their contribution to the realization of a neural representation of space contributing to spatial navigation.

761711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
761711.value: We made novel observation that postnatal refinement of thalamic and inferior olivary networks associated with the vestibular system is crucial for establishment of an internal 3-dimensional spatial reference map and for the emergence of the capability in spatial navigation. We further identified a neonatal period of susceptibility during which perturbation of excitatory or inhibitory neural transmission in the brainstem vestibular nucleus exerted lasting impacts on both the formation of spatial maps in the brain and the expression of navigational behavior into adulthood. These deficits were not observed in animals if perturbation was introduced after the critical period has lapsed. Our study has uncovered cellular mechanisms underlying postnatal tuning of the vestibular network for the execution of navigational behavior in adults.

762111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
762111.value: The burden of brain diseases is expected to significantly increase in the near future as the population ages. Assessing brain function, possibly before symptoms even arise is challenging, and has driven the development of a number of brain monitoring technologies. A very recent advance in neuroimaging is to acquire EEG and fMRI simultaneously, since combined EEG/fMRI potentially provides good spatial and temporal resolution and cognitive function relies on integration between brain areas at different spatiotemporal scales. However, as the EEG and fMRI rely on electrical activity and hemodynamics respectively, advanced signal processing methods must be employed to meaningfully combine the information obtained to make full use of this cutting-edge technique. With access to the sole simultaneous EEG/fMRI recording system in Hong Kong and with the special expertise of a cross-disciplinary international research team, there is a rare opportunity to develop novel signal processing methods to extract meaningful information from EEG/fMRI data that will provide important information to researchers investigating brain connectivity, which is critical for the understanding and assessment of brain functioning in normal and disease states. The specific aims of this project are to develop a novel, efficient data-driven brain connectivity framework using simultaneous EEG/fMRI neurological data and characterize the correspondence between EEG and fMRI. We propose a PLS-ICA framework by combining a novel extension of partial least square (PLS) modeling and independent component analysis (ICA). It is also extended to address key practical challenges such as sparsity and non-linearity. Crucially, we will evaluate and validate the proposed brain connectivity analysis framework on both simulations and real simultaneous EEG/fMRI data sets collected in a few newly designed cognitive science studies. This cross-disciplinary initiative combines expertise in statistical signal processing & modeling, neuroimaging, cognitive neuroscience, and clinical medicine. This research has significant impact: It will make a fundamental theoretical and practical contribution to modeling brain connectivity. The models developed here will contribute significantly toward understanding brain functions, and be widely applicable to different neurological disorders. 不久的將來，隨著人口老齡化，可以預期大腦疾病帶來的社會負擔將會顯著增長。對大腦功能進行評估，甚或在病症發生之前，是一件非常具有挑戰性的事情，這也促進了一些大腦功能監控技術的發展。腦成像技術的一個新進展是同步獲取EEG和fMRI信息。 EEG和fMRI數據的結合有望同時獲得高空間分辨率及高時間分辨率，而大腦認知功能恰恰依賴於大腦各功能區在不同時空層面上的有機整合。然而，由於EEG反應大腦的電活動而fMRI反應大腦的血流動力學活動，若要充分利用EEG/fMRI同步測量這一前沿科技，必須運用先進的信號處理方法將這兩方面的信息有效地結合起來。擁有全港唯一的一套EEG/fMRI同步測量系統以及一個國際化交叉領域研究團隊所具備的該方面的研究專長，這對我們是一個罕有的機遇去開發新的信號處理方法以從EEG/ fMRI數據中提取有意義的信息，進而為探索大腦連接性的研究者們提供重要的相關信息，而大腦連接性對我們理解及評估健康和疾病狀態下的大腦功能極其重要。本項目的具體目標是發展一個基於EEG/fMRI同步測量數據的新的有效的數據驅動的大腦連接性分析框架並揭示EEG和fMRI之間的關係。通過改進偏最小二乘(PLS)建模方法並將其與獨立分量分析(ICA)相結合，我們提出一個分析EEG/fMRI數據的PLS-ICA框架。我們亦將進一步拓展此分析框架以解決稀疏性和非線性等一些關鍵的實際問題。重要的是，我們將通過對模擬數據及在幾個新設計的大腦認知研究的實驗中所獲得的實際EEG/fMRI同步測量數據的分析，評估及驗證我們所提出的大腦連接性分析框架。此交叉領域研究結合了包括統計信號處理與建模、腦成像、認知神經科學、以及臨床醫學等各方面的研究專長。此項研究意義重大。它將在大腦連接性建模方面做出基礎的理論及實用貢獻。本研究所發展的模型有助於理解大腦功能，在各類不同的神經疾病的探索方面有廣泛的應用。

762111.label: Realisation of objectives
762111.value: Objective 1: At the beginning of the project, we strived to set up a simultaneous EEG/fMRI recording system (the first of its kind in HK as far as we were aware) with considerable effort made to address the coupling problem from the MRI scanner to the EEG measurements. Two pilot experiments (a block-designed visual stimulation experiment and a visual oddball experiment) were carried out on eight subjects to ensure the successful installation of the MR-compatible EEG equipment. Self-developed algorithms and existing toolkits were applied to remove MR-induced and pulse-related artifacts from EEG and to identify EEG and fMRI patterns activated in the two experiments. Our analyses show that the activation patterns of EEG and fMRI in the pilot experiments are highly consistent with those in the literature, suggesting that the simultaneous EEG/fMRI equipment has been well installed and the data pre-processing pipeline is well developed. Hence, the first objective of this study is successfully achieved. Objective 2: To estimate the causal relationship between brain regions based on the concept of Granger causality, we have developed several new methods to address difficulties (such as model order selection, model validation to avoid spurious discoveries, extension to non-stationary causality, etc.) in the application of Granger causality to infer brain connectivity. Further, the connections between EEG and fMRI data are also investigated with a novel extension of partial least squares modeling and independent component analysis. In addition, statistical testing methods for group-level inference of brain connectivity were also developed. Thus, second objective is achieved. Objective 3: A new EEG/fMRI experiment was designed to estimate and compare brain connectivity patterns from simultaneously-recorded EEG/fMRI data in two resting-state conditions (eyes-open and eyes-closed). Simultaneous EEG/fMRI data were collected from twelve participants to validate the hypothesis that EEG/fMRI connectivity is modulated by resting conditions. We also applied the proposed data analysis methods in a collaborative project to study EEG/fMRI connectivity activated by painful laser stimulation. The performance of the proposed methods is evaluated in these two data sets (resting-state data and laser-evoked data). Results show that proposed methods can effectively identify the connectivity patterns of EEG/fMRI data in both resting-state and event-related experiments, whereby Objective 3 is accomplished.

762111.label: Major findings and research outcome
762111.value: (1) Advanced data pre-processing pipeline has been developed and implemented (i) to remove MR-induced artifacts and heartbeat-induced artifacts from EEG, (ii) to pre-process simultaneously recorded EEG and fMRI data, and (iii) to extract quantitative EEG and fMRI features for data integration and connectivity analysis. The EEG processing methods and relevant applications (such as brain-computer interface and EEG-based brain decoding) have been published in journal papers [J1,J6,J7] and conference papers [C1,C5,C6,C8] listed in Part C of this report. (2) We have developed new data-driven methods based on the concept of Granger causality to identify functional brain connectivity from EEG and fMRI, with capability of extracting dynamic and causal interactions between brain regions. The Granger causality-based connectivity analysis methods are of a general nature developed in association with inference of gene regulatory network [C3,J5]. These methods have been successfully applied to identify features that reveal the laser-evoked brain connectivity [J2,J3,C2], EEG source connectivity of human somatosensory system [J4], and visual-task-related transient fMRI connectivity [C4, C7]. (3) By applying the proposed methods to analyze EEG/fMRI data recorded in the newly-designed resting-state experiments, we found that (i) resting-state fMRI connectivity exhibits very large temporal variations that are closely correlated with structural connectivity of the brain [C9], and (ii) resting-state fMRI connectivity is correlated with certain EEG spectral features and such correlation is modulated by resting conditions (eyes-open or eyes-closed). We also applied the proposed methods to investigate EEG/fMRI connectivity evoked by painful laser stimulation, and we have successfully identified pain-evoked EEG casual connectivity between contralateral and ipsilateral somatosensory areas [J2,J3].

762111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
762111.value: In this project, we have successfully set up a system to acquire simultaneous EEG/fMRI data and an effective data analysis pipeline to estimate brain connectivity from EEG/fMRI data. The system and the methods will enable many potential collaborative studies that require a high-resolution temporal-spatial description of brain connectivity. This is of immense interest to neuroscientists and clinicians, and may have potential clinical applications. For example, the current project would enable a novel EEG/fMRI framework for localizing epileptic seizure activity with both high temporal resolution and spatial resolution, which is currently unavailable but will be particularly useful for epilepsy surgery. The methodologies developed in this project are of a general nature and will pave the way for further studies in brain connectivity under specific paradigms.

762111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
762111.value: The human brain has billions of neural cells that interact over time and space to support our mental activities, such as perception and cognition. Brain connectivity is fast becoming one of the most important research fields for its promise to yield scientific, clinical, and economic benefits, such as diagnosis and therapy of mental diseases. Simultaneous electroencephalography and functional magnetic resonance imaging (EEG/fMRI) is a cutting-edge multi-modality technology that can image brain activity with a millisecond temporal resolution (EEG) and a millimeter precision (fMRI). However, it is still very challenging to read brain connectivity from huge amount of noisy and complex EEG/fMRI raw data. This project is aimed at developing novel signal processing methods that can identify and extract brain connectivity patterns from EEG/fMRI data. Such methods enable the construction of a new dynamic and high-resolution picture of brain activities showing how different brain regions work in symphony at rest or in response to external stimulation. The models developed in the project will contribute towards a better understanding of how brain connectivity supports normal brain functions and how brain connectivity might be altered by neurological disorders.

762811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
762811.value: I型人类免疫缺陷病毒（HIV）是引起获得性免疫缺陷病综合症（艾滋病，AIDS）的病原体。HIV-1主要通过非保护的性接触传播，目前仍在蔓延。在尚未找到治愈艾滋病方法的今天，我们的终极目标就是研发出安全，有效又经济的HIV-1疫苗，从而取得这场抗HIV/AIDS战役的胜利。传统的疫苗策略无法阻止HIV-1的感染，因此必须开展基础研究设计新型疫苗。由于HIV-1主要通过成年人的阴道和直肠传染，而粘膜组织不仅是HIV-1感染的重要部位，更是病毒进行早期增殖和扩散的储存库，我们认为有效的疫苗必须能诱导出持续性的免疫反应， 调动粘膜免疫系统阻止病毒进入和扩散，并且清除病毒储存库。我们在猴模型中发现一种新的免疫方式，本研究将检验这种全新的能够诱导出很强的针对HIV-1感染的免疫反应，通过粘膜途径初免-肌肉注射加强的艾滋病疫苗策略的免疫调控能力。该模型利用一种称为猴免疫缺陷病毒（SIV）的猴艾滋病毒感染猴子，模拟HIV-1感染人类的情况。我们发现新的免疫方式能有效地控制致病性SIVmac239病毒在猴子体内的复制。与没有免疫过疫苗的对照组相比，免疫组的猴子能长久地保持高水平的免疫反应，四只中有三只猴子血液中的病毒载量低于对照组100倍，而另外这只猴子得到了完全保护，其血液中根本检测不到病毒。重要的是，其他研究者用不同的抗SIVmac239疫苗联合免疫时观察到相似的保护效果，这进一步强调了以T细胞为基础的艾滋病疫苗的重要性。在此基础上，我们将从以下方面研究这种有效的免疫方法的潜在机理：（1）进一步研究rMVTTSIVgpe/rAd5SIVgpe体系诱导出的系统和粘膜免疫反应对于通过直肠途径攻毒的SIVmac239的保护情况；（2）在小动物模型中优化rMVTTSIVgpe/rAd5SIVgpe体系。这些研究结果不仅对免疫学和疫苗学贡献卓著，而且对于成功研发疫苗抵御HIV/AIDS至关重要。值得一提的是，我们的疫苗策略经过合适的优化，也将有助于攻克其他难以治愈的传染性疾病，如TB，疟疾，HCV等。

762811.label: Realisation of objectives
762811.value: The overall objective of this project is to investigate the immune control of a promising mucosal prime intramuscular boost AIDS vaccine regimen. With our key emphasis on the immune control of a pathogenic SIVmac239 infection and the mechanism of mucosal vaccination, we propose a focused research program with two specific aims: (1) To further study systemic and mucosal immune responses elicited by the rMVTTSIVgpe/rAd5SIVgpe regimen against the rectal SIVmac239 challenge; (2) To optimize the rMVTTSIVgpe/rAd5SIVgpe regimen in small animals. To achieve these goals, we hypothesized that both T cell and antibody responses might contribute to the significantly enhanced immunogenicity of the rMVTTSIVgpe/rAd5SIVgpe regimen. To test this hypothesis, we have conducted proposed and additional experiments under aims 1 and 2. We consistently found that the strongest immune responses were induced by a heterologous mucosal prime with a modified replicating vaccinia virus Tiantan strain (rMVTTSIVgpe) and an intramuscular boost with a nonreplicating adenovirus strain (rAd5SIVgpe), the above mentioned rMVTTSIVgpe/rAd5SIVgpe regimen, based on extensive data generated in mice (oral presentation at the AAI meeting in 2011 by Xian Tang). Moreover, we found that this regimen elicited robust cellular immune responses with enhanced magnitudes, sustainability, and polyfunctionality, which might contribute to the protection against high-dose intrarectal pathogenic SIVmac239 infection (JV 2013). In particular, the protective effects correlated with the vaccine-elicited SIV-specific CD8+ T cell responses against Gag and Pol. The manuscript on data generated in mice will be published soon. In addition, to better investigate the role of SIV-specific antibodies, we spent great efforts on a novel yeast surface displayed antigen library of entire SIVmac239 envelope (Env) glycoprotein although it was not in the original experimental design. This new platform allowed us to determine the major antigenic determinants (MAD) in monkey sera elicited by the rMVTTSIVgpe/rAd5SIVgpe regimen and SIV infection. We found that this regimen induced a uniquely predominant antibody response against a distinct MAD in variable region 2 (V2) as compared with the controls (JAIDS 2015). This MAD was associated with a higher titer of anti-V2 antibody responses, which was inversely correlated with peak and set-point viral loads. Interestingly, the pathogenic SIVmac239 challenge evaded the vaccine-elicited anti-V2 antibody response. In summary, we have worked very hard on the proposed study with two SCI publications acknowledging this grant support, while another paper is in preparation. We revealed not only a promising vaccine strategy but also some mechanisms underlying the vaccine efficacy. This study also resulted in one patent and two excellent (top 10%) Ph.D. students at HKU.

762811.label: Major findings and research outcome
762811.value: In this study, we focus on a promising mucosal prime and intramuscular boost AIDS vaccine regimen because mucosal surfaces have not been targeted by most human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) vaccines, despite being major routes for HIV-1 transmission. Specifically, we discovered a novel vaccination regimen consisting of a mucosal prime with a modified replicating vaccinia virus Tiantan strain (MVTTSIVgpe) and an intramuscular boost with a nonreplicating adenovirus strain (Ad5SIVgpe) based on extensive data generated in mice (oral presentation at the AAI meeting in 2011 by Xian Tang). Moreover, we found that this regimen elicited robust cellular immune responses with enhanced magnitudes, sustainability, and polyfunctionality, as well as higher titers of neutralizing antibodies against the simian immunodeficiency virus SIVmac1A11 in rhesus monkeys (JV 2013). The reductions in peak and set-point viral loads were significant in most animals, with one other animal being protected fully from high-dose intrarectal inoculation of SIVmac239. Furthermore, the animals vaccinated with this regimen were healthy, while 75% of control animals developed simian AIDS. The protective effects correlated with the vaccine-elicited SIV-specific CD8+ T cell responses against Gag and Pol. Our study provides a novel strategy for developing an HIV-1 vaccine by using the combination of a replicating vector and mucosal priming. Subsequently, besides T cell responses we conducted a comprehensive analysis on antigenic determinants recognized by specific antibody responses generated by vaccination and SIVmac239 infection (poster presentation at the AAI meeting in 2013 by Jia Guo, JAIDS 2015). A novel yeast surface displayed antigen library of entire SIVmac239 envelope (Env) glycoprotein was established and validated to map the major antigenic determinants (MAD) in monkey sera elicited by vaccination and infection. MAD-directed antibody responses were further analyzed for correlation of protection. We found that the yeast surface displayed library allows the mapping of SIV-specific linear and conformational MAD. The MVTTgpe-based regimen induces antibodies targeting mainly to 6 antigenic domains covering the entire gp160. Critically, this regimen induced a uniquely predominant antibody response against a distinct MAD in variable region 2 (V2) as compared with the Ad5gpe-based vaccine and SIVmac239 infection. This MAD was associated with a higher titer of anti-V2 antibody responses, which was inversely correlated with peak and set-point viral loads. Unexpectedly, the pathogenic SIVmac239 challenge evaded the vaccine-elicited anti-V2 antibody response. Instead of recalling B-cell memory responses to the V2 MAD, viral infection directed anti-V1V2 antibodies primarily to V1 region. Moreover, the anti-V1V2 antibody responses diminished significantly in infected macaques after they enter the stage of simian AIDS. Our findings have critical implications to AIDS vaccine efforts with focus on V2 region.

762811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
762811.value: We are seeking for research funding to study a promising mucosal prime and intramuscular boost AIDS vaccine regimen in humans. The key discovery made by us is to enhance vaccine immunogenicity by delivering HIV antigen through two viral vectors, namely MVTTSIVgpe and Ad5SIVgpe. After four years of study, we demonstrated that this vaccine strategy has resulted in high levels of qualitatively enhanced HIV-specific CD8+ cytotoxic T cells, which confer significant protection in mice and monkeys after lethal viral challenges. The study also revealed underlying mechanisms of this new discovery, which have significant implication to AIDS vaccine and vaccines against other pathogens. With this critical discovery in the world, the ultimate goal of future proposal is to bring this promising mucosal prime and intramuscular boost AIDS vaccine regimen into human trials, phase I as the first step and phase II/III as the second step. Once the new vaccine works in human with reliable safety profiles during phase I, it will warrant for further phase II/III human studies. The new discovery will be useful not only for preventing HIV infection but also for immunotherapy of curing 33 millions of infected people because a high frequency of HIV-specific CD8+ cytotoxic T cells is important for both suppressing viral replication and clearing persistent infection (so-called HIV latency).

762811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
762811.value: Since 1981, AIDS pandemic has led to 35 million deaths and another 35 million people currently living with HIV, the AIDS virus, worldwide. To date, this pandemic still grows in a speed of over 2 million new infections each year while there remains the lack of therapeutic cure and effective vaccine. Currently, most failed AIDS vaccines are weak and not protective in humans. In this study, the discovery made by us is to enhance vaccine potency by a promising mucosal prime and intramuscular boost AIDS vaccine regimen. After four years of study, we demonstrated that this vaccine regimen resulted in high levels of qualitatively enhanced viral specific T cell and antibody responses, which may confer significant protection in mice and monkeys after lethal viral challenges. The study also revealed some correlates of protection on our new discovery, which may have significant implication to AIDS vaccine and vaccines against other pathogens.
