763111.label: Realisation of objectives
763111.value: Objective 1: This objective was successfully achieved by a series of in vitro experiments. Conditioned medium from Id1-overexpressing ESCC (esophageal squamous cell carcinoma) cells was collected and added to cultured fibroblasts. Western blot analysis was used to detect α-SMA (a marker of fibroblast activation) in the fibroblast cells. The results showed up-regulation of α-SMA in the fibroblasts and the effect was partially attenuated by either knockdown of IGF2 in the ESCC cells using shIGF2 (short hairpin RNA against IGF2) or addition of IGF2-neutralizing antibody. MTT cell proliferation and chamber migration assays were then performed to study the effect of conditioned medium from Id1-overexpressing ESCC cells on the proliferation and migratory potentials of fibroblasts. The data demonstrated that the conditioned medium from Id1-overexpressing cells did not stimulate fibroblasts to proliferate, but could actively attract fibroblasts to migrate. Similar results were obtained using synthesized recombinant human IGF2. IG2-knockdown in the Id1-overexpressing ESCC cells, or the addition of IGF2-neutralizing antibody partially abrogated these effects. Objective 2: This objective was successfully accomplished using in vitro assays. In our mid-term report, we described the experiments performed to study the paracrine effects of IGF2-activated fibroblasts on the proliferation, tube-formation and migration abilities of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) cells, and to prove that fibroblast-secreted VEGF mediated these effects. We also mentioned how we mimicked the tumor microenvironment by co-culturing fibroblasts with ESCC cell lines expressing Id1, Id1-shIGF2 or empty vector in vitro, and found that CM harvested from the fibroblasts co-cultured with Id1-expressing ESCC cells promoted the proliferation and migration of HUVEC, compared with the medium conditioned by fibroblasts co-cultured with control cells or ESCC cells with IGF2-knockdown. We also studied the effect of fibroblast-secreted VEGF on invasive potential of ESCC cells in vitro. Subsequently, we completed this objective by studying the effects of IGF2-activated fibroblasts on migration of bone marrow-derived vascular progenitor cells, the conditioned media was collected from esophageal fibroblasts treated with recombinant human IGF2, as well as co-cultured with the ESCC cell lines expressing Id1, Id1-shIGF2 or empty vector. The ability of the various conditioned media to attract the migration of bone marrow-derived VEGFR1+ and VEGFR2+ cells (sorted from the mouse bone marrow cells by flow cytometry using anti-mouse VEGFR1 and VEGFR2 antibodies) was compared using chamber migration assay. Bone marrow-derived cells (BMDCs) were also treated with VEGFR1 and VEGFR2 neutralizing antibodies to determine whether blockade of these receptors could inhibit their migration toward the fibroblast-conditioned medium. Objective 3: This objective was accomplished using in vivo models. In one of the experiments, we determined whether Id1-expressing tumor could mobilize and home BMDCs to tumor and pre-metastatic sites. A traceable system was established by transplanting the bone marrow of transgenic mice expressing green fluorescent protein (GFP) into groups of lethally irradiated recipient nude mice. The recipient nude mice were then inoculated subcutaneously with human ESCC (KYSE150) cells expressing Id1, Id1-shIGF2 and control vectors, respectively, to establish tumors. We found a significant enrichment of GFP+/VEGFR1+ cells in the bone marrow, tumor xenografts and lungs (which is a common site of ESCC metastasis) and of mice bearing Id1-expressing tumors, compared with the Id1-shIGF2 and the vector control groups. These results not only confirmed that VEGFR1+ BMDCs were recruited to the “primary” tumor and secondary sites, but also suggested that Id1-induced IGF2 plays an important role in activating and mobilizing VEGFR1+ BMDCs. In addition, our data showed that the bone marrow cells from the Id1 group could increase the in vivo tumorigenicity of untransfected ESCC cells if co-injected subcutaneously into nude mice. In another experiment, we tested our hypothesis that the perturbation/enrichment of host bone marrow by Id1-overexpressing tumor may also facilitate the mobilization and homing of host VEGFR1+ hematopoietic progenitor cells to distant organs to initiate metastasis of ESCC, ESCC cells with ectopic luciferase (luc) gene expression were mixed with bone marrow from the Id1, Id1-shIGF2 and control groups respectively, and injected intravenously into the tail vein of nude mice. Metastatic activity was monitored using in vivo bioluminescence imaging. We found that lung metastasis occurred most rapidly in the group injected with cancer cells mixed with the bone marrow “primed” by Id1-overexpressing tumor xenograft. Our next step was to further confirm the role of the Id1/IGF2/VEGF cascade in bone marrow activation and to study the effects of VEGFR1 and VEGFR2 inhibition on preventing distant metastasis of ESCC. Experimental metastasis was performed in which a sub-group of mice injected with cancer cells mixed with the bone marrow “primed” by Id1-overexpressing tumor xenograft were given intraperitoneal injections of anti-mouse VEGFR1 neutralizing antibodies MF1; ImClone Systems Inc., NY). Metastatic activity was monitored by bioluminescent imaging. We found that lung metastasis developed most readily in the Id1 group and that treatment with MF1 significantly decreased the colonization of intravenously injected ESCC cells to the lungs. Objective 4: As mentioned in the mid-term report, various experiments were performed to test our hypothesis that miR-127 targets VEGF mRNA, but our results did not show convincing binding of miR-127 to the 3’-UTR of VEGF. However, we were able to identify, by in silico prediction, another candidate microRNA (i.e. miR-29c) that could regulate VEGF. This objective was fully addressed by gain- and loss-of-functions experiments, as well as luciferase report assay, which validated that miR-29c could inhibit VEGF expression in esophageal fibroblasts. In the cells co-transfected with miR-29c, a reduction of luciferase activity in wild-type 3’-UTR transfected cells, but not in the mutant 3’-UTR transfected cells, was observed, which strongly suggests the direct binding of miR-29c to VEGF 3’-UTR. RT-PCR and ELISA confirmed the regulation of VEGF by miR-29c. The role of miR-29c in mediating IGF2-induced fibroblast activation and VEGF secretion was also explored. Gain- and loss-of-function experiments using miR-29c mimic and inhibitor confirmed the regulation of VEGF by miR-29c in fibroblasts. In the luciferase reporter assay, overexpression of miR-29c led to a dose-dependent decrease in VEGF 3’UTR reporter expression, but there was no repression of luciferase activity in the fibroblasts co-transfected with miR-29c and mutant VEGF 3’UTR, indicating that miR-29c directly binds to the 3’UTR of VEGF. At the functional level, Boyden chamber assay showed that the enhanced migration of fibroblasts induced by IGF2 could be attenuated by overexpression of miR-29c. The mechanism by which IGF2 negatively regulates miR-29c expression was also investigated. Results from TaqMan pri-miRNA assay suggested that IGF2 regulates miR-29c at transcriptional level. In silico target prediction analysis showed three potential p53 binding sites in the promoter region of miR-29c. Subsequent experiments including the use of p53-/- mouse embryonic fibroblasts confirmed that regulation of miR-29c by IGF2 is p53-dependent.

763111.label: Major findings and research outcome
763111.value: (i) Id1-induced IGF2 secreted from ESCC cells activates fibroblasts in a paracrine manner: Id1-overexpressing tumor cells overexpressed IGF2 due to competitive binding between Id1 and Cdc20 to stabilize E2F1. Tumor-cell secreted IGF2 activated normal fibroblasts to produce and secrete VEGF, which in turn exerted pro-angiogenic effects on endothelial cells in the tumor microenvironment. (ii) Esophageal cancer patients with high serum IGF2 and VEGF expressions had shorter survival: Concomitant elevation of serum IGF2 and VEGF was also significantly associated with T3/T4 stages and distant metastasis. (iii) miR-29c mediates the regulation of IGF2 on VEGF in fibroblasts: Genetic enforcement of miR-29c abrogated the upregulation of VEGF expression induced by IGF2 in a p53-dependent manner. (iv) Id1-overexpressing tumor systemically instigates VEGFR1+ BMDCs to promote cancer progression: We found a significant enrichment of VEGFR1+ cells in the bone marrow, as well as in the lungs and tumor xenografts of nude mice bearing Id1-expressing ESCC tumors, compared with mice bearing Id1-expressing tumors with IGF2-knockdown. These results showed that Id1-induced IGF2 plays an important role in activating and mobilizing VEGFR1+ BMDCs to primary and secondary sites. (v) Targeting VEGFR1+ and VEGFR2+ non-tumor cells is essential for esophageal cancer therapy: Using mouse models and mouse-specific antibodies against VEGFR1 and VEGFR2, we found that targeting host VEGFR1 and VEGFR2 could decrease tumor angiogenesis and reduce the number of bone marrow hematopoietic and endothelial progenitor cells. We also found significant correlation between pathological TNM staging and expression levels of VEGF receptors in human ESCC specimens. These findings highlight the importance of therapeutic strategies that can disrupt host-tumor interactions. (vi) CXCL5/CXCR2 axis contributes to formation of pre-metastatic niche in lungs: The lungs of mice bearing Id1-expressing tumors had elevated expression of CXCL5 cytokine, which exerted strong chemotactic effect on invasion of ESCC cells and therefore favored metastatic colonization of cancer cells. Blockade of its receptor CXCR2 on ESCC cells significantly abrogated this effect. The results under points (i) and (v) were reported in Clinical Cancer Research and in Oncotarget (see Part C). The findings under points (i)-(iv) and (vi) are included in a manuscript which is currently in revision for re-submission to Nature Communications (see Part C). An invited review on the potential of targeted anti-angiogenesis therapies in the treatment of esophageal cancer was published in Gastrointestinal Cancer: targets and Therapy (see Part C).

763111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
763111.value: (i) Relatively little is known about what makes metastatic sites receptive to incoming cancer cells. Our in vivo experiments showed that Id1 increases the potential of intravenously injected ESCC cells to colonize the lungs, and that there was upregulation of CXCL5 in the lungs of nude mice xenografted with Id1-expressing ESCC tumors. CXCL5 was first identified as an inflammatory peptide with neutrophil-activating properties and was subsequently demonstrated to participate in various cellular functions associated with cancer development. The significance of CXCL5 in esophageal cancer has not been reported.. We hope to obtain research funding to extend our investigation to determine whether serum CXCL5 may be a predictive biomarker for distant metastasis of ESCC. (ii) In silico target prediction algorithms showed that in addition to VEGF, the 3’-UTR of a putative oncogene FBXO31 also contains potential binding sites for miR-29c. We previously reported that FBXO31 can protect ESCC cells from stress-induced apoptosis by suppressing the MKK6-p38 signaling pathway (Journal of Biological Chemistry 2014, 289:21508-21518. We therefore initiated a new project to study the role of miR-29c/FBXO31 as a key regulatory mechanism in esophageal cancer chemoresistance. This project was awarded a research grant of RMB740,000 from the 2014 National Nature Science Foundation of China (NSFC) grant– General Program.

763111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
763111.value: Esophageal cancer is amongst the top ten leading causes of cancer death in Hong Kong and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is the predominant form. We previously reported that ESCC cells that overexpress Id1 protein secrete IGF2. In this study, we found that IGF2 secreted by tumor cells could exert paracrine effects on nearby fibroblasts and stimulate them to produce VEGF. This mechanism was regulated by a microRNA named miR-29c. VEGF is an important growth factor involved in forming new blood vessels to nourish the growing tumor. Our data showed that increased levels of IGF2 and VEGF in the serum of patients with ESCC were associated with poorer survival. In mouse models, Id1-expressing ESCC tumors were found to influence the bone marrow, leading to enrichment of hematopoietic and endothelial cells that express VEGF receptors VEGFR1 and VEGFR2. These bone marrow-derived cells were mobilized and recruited to the lungs and primary tumors of the mice to promote cancer progression and metastasis. We found that treatment with specific antibodies that target VEGFR1 and VEGFR2 could significantly inhibit the growth of ESCC tumor in nude mice, which suggests that therapies that target VEGFR1/VEGFR2 may be beneficial for patients with aggressive ESCC.

763211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
763211.value: 妊娠滋養細胞疾病 (GTD) 涵蓋源於胎盘滋養細胞的異質群體疾病, 包括葡萄胎(易於發展成需要化療的持續性滋養細胞腫瘤), 以及明顯的惡性腫瘤(如絨毛膜癌)。由於GTD在東方人的病發率較高, 進一步了解尚未清晰的GTD病變過程對疾病的治療至關重要。我們的科研中心已收集大量臨床樣本及相關數據。最近的研究結果顯示, 致癌基因和幹細胞相關的轉錄因子的差異表達譜與表觀遺傳狀態俱在GTD的病變及惡性發展過程中扮演重要角色。其中, 野生型p53和相關基因與滋養細胞的增殖及凋亡有密切關聯。 FBI-1(又名Pokemon)是POK轉錄因子家族的成員, 主要負責調控p53的功能, 在多種癌症中擔當致癌基因的角色。 我們的初步研究發現, 相對正常滋養細胞, FBI-1在會發展爲惡性腫瘤的絨毛膜癌和葡萄胎有較高的核糖核酸及蛋白質表達。體外實驗顯示, 轉染FBI-1可促進絨毛膜癌細胞的遷移與侵襲, 並通過控制與凋亡有關的蛋白質抑制細胞凋亡。 我們假設: 過度表達的FBI-1可透過與p53和幹細胞相關轉錄因子的相互作用, 引起異常的滋養細胞凋亡與侵襲, 從而導至GTD的惡性發展。 我們計劃 (1)研究FBI-1在胎盘及GTD的細胞分布與亞細胞定位; (2)辨認控制FBI-1在胎盘及GTD表達的機制; (3) 研究FBI-1如何控制滋養細胞的凋亡與侵襲; (4) 透過體內實驗研究FBI-1對絨毛膜癌細胞致癌性的影響; (5) 評估FBI-1與幹細胞相關的轉錄因子之間的相互作用。

763211.label: Realisation of objectives
763211.value: Overall we have achieved all of our objectives in this study. For objective 1, we performed immunohistochemical staining of FBI-1 in 102 trophoblastic tissue samples. We also ectopically expressed GFP-FBI-1 for observation of FBI-1’s subcellular localization in vitro. FBI-1 expression could be found in cytotrophoblasts, syncytiotrophoblasts, villous intermediate trophoblasts (IT), extravillous implantation site and chorionic IT in first trimester placentas and GTD samples. FBI-1 immunoreactivity could be found in both nuclear and cytoplasmic cellular compartments of those FBI-1 positive trophoblasts, but nuclear staining was generally more intense. Similar cellular expression pattern could be observed in vitro. For objective 2, genetic, epigenetic and microRNA regulation of FBI-1 were investigated. Our results indicated that FBI-1 gene (ZBTB7A) was not amplified in GTD. On the other hand, FBI-1 expression was down-regulated in CCA cell lines JEG-3 and JAR upon treatment by the HDAC inhibitor trichostatin A (TSA). In addition, more significant reduction in cell survival was found in TSA than in 5-aza-dc treatment. This may be related to the decrease in FBI-1 expression after TSA treatment. These results suggested that histone modification may play a role in the regulation of FBI-1 expression in gestational choriocarcinoma cells. In addition, an inverse relationship between miR-125 family, including both miR-125a and miR-125b, and FBI-1 was demonstrated. Transfecting miR-125 mimics down-regulated FBI-1 expression level in both JAR and JEG-3, suggesting that miR-125 may regulate FBI-1 through a direct interaction. Taken together our investigation indicates that in choriocarcinoma cells, FBI-1 gene is not amplified but its expression is affected by histone acetylation and microRNA regulation. For objective 3, ectopic overexpression of FBI-1 reduced the number of cell undergoing apoptosis in both JEG-3 and JAR. We analyzed the apoptosis pathways involved and found both intrinsic and extrinsic apoptosis pathways were suppressed by FBI-1. Thus, for the extrinsic pathway, Fas, caspase 8 and caspase 10 were markedly suppressed by FBI-1, whereas for the intrinsic pathway, the pro-apoptotic Bcl-2 protein BAK, poly (ADP ribose) polymerase (PARP) and caspase 9 were downregulated. FBI-1 overexpression enhances JEG-3 and JAR cell migration and invasion. We found that FBI-1 can activate Akt through inducing its phosphorylation at amino acid Serine 473. FBI-1 achieves this by specifically downregulating the p85β regulatory subunits of PI3K, the upstream kinase of Akt. p85β downregulation leads to the upregulation of the activity of p110 catalytic subunit of PI3K and subsequently Akt activation. This signaling pathway is implicated in FBI-1 induced trophoblast migration since pharmacological inhibition of PI3K by LY294002 abolished FBI-1 mediated cell migration and invasion. For objective 4, JAR stably expressing a shRNA against FBI-1 (sh-FBI-1-JAR) and control cells (sh-NC) were inoculated subcantaneously nude mice. The growth rate of tumors formed in mice inoculated with sh-FBI-1-JAR was significantly less than that in tumors formed by control sh-NCcells. The total tumor weight was significantly less in the sh-FBI-1-JAR cell injected mice than in the control mice as well. These results support our findings in in vitro models that FBI-1 is instrumental to the growth of CCA. For objective 5, the relative levels of a panel of stem cell related genes, including Sonic hedgehog (Shh), Patched, Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Kif7, Nanog, Oct4, Sox2, and Stat3, were assessed after knockdown of FBI-1 gene by quantitative real time PCR. Shh was found to be consistently downregulated in JEG-3 and JAR transfected with FBI-1 shRNA constructs while consistent change was not observed in other genes being tested. This suggested that, in contrast to our expectation, FBI-1 predominantly affects the SHH signalling pathway.

763211.label: Major findings and research outcome
763211.value: Immunohistochemical studies revealed that FBI-1 is overexpressed in GTD. FBI-1 expression could be found in cytotrophoblasts, syncytiotrophoblasts, villous intermediate trophoblasts (IT), extravillous implantation site and chorionic IT in first trimester placentas and GTD samples. This immunoreactivity pattern indicates that FBI-1 may not be involved in the differentiation of trophoblasts but instead in the more fundamental cellular processes (Mak et al., 2015, in press). We demonstrated that FBI-1 gene (ZBTB7A) was not amplified in the CCA cell lines JEG-3 and JAR, in comparison with an immortalized trophoblast cell line HTR-8/SVneo. No gene amplification could be detected in the tissue samples as well. Therefore, although FBI-1 is overexpressed in GTD, the overexpression is unlikely to be caused by gene amplification (Tam, 2014). Instead, FBI-1 expression is regulated by histone acetylation as treatment of HDAC inhibitor TSA down-regulated FBI-1 in JEG-3 and JAR (Chan, 2014). Moreover, we demonstrated that the miR-125 family (miR-125a and miR-125b) could down-regulate FBI-1. An inverse relationship between miR-125 family and FBI-1 could be observed (Yu, 2014). Taken together, our results suggested that in choriocarcinoma FBI-1 gene is not amplified but its expression is affected by histone acetylation and microRNA regulation. Ectopic overexpression of FBI-1 reduced the number of cell undergoing apoptosis in both JEG-3 and JAR. We analyzed the apoptosis pathways involved and found both intrinsic and extrinsic apoptosis pathways were suppressed by FBI-1. Thus, for the extrinsic pathway, Fas, caspase 8 and caspase 10 were markedly suppressed by FBI-1, whereas for the intrinsic pathway, the pro-apoptotic Bcl-2 protein BAK, poly (ADP ribose) polymerase (PARP) and caspase 9 were downregulated. These findings suggested FBI-1 is involved in the survival of trophoblasts in GTD, and the mechanisms by which FBI-1 contributes to cell survival are diverse (Mak et al., 2015, in press). FBI-1 overexpression also enhances JEG-3 and JAR cell migration and invasion. We found that FBI-1 can activate Akt, a kinase important for the survival and migration ability of cells, through inducing its phosphorylation at amino acid Serine 473. FBI-1 achieves this by specifically downregulating the p85β regulatory subunits of PI3K, the upstream kinase of Akt. p85α, another form of the regulatory subunit, and PTEN, which is the phosphatase antagonizing the action of PI3K, were not affected. p85β downregulation leads to the upregulation of the activity of p110 catalytic subunit of PI3K and subsequently Akt activation. This signaling pathway is implicated in FBI-1 induced trophoblast migration since pharmacological inhibition of PI3K by LY294002 abolished FBI-1 mediated cell migration and invasion (Mak et al., 2015, in press). To investigate the in vivo effects of FBI-1, JAR stably expressing a shRNA against FBI-1 (sh-FBI-1-JAR) and control cells (sh-NC) were generated and inoculated into nude mice subcantaneously. The growth rate of tumors formed in mice inoculated with sh-FBI-1-JAR was significantly less than that of tumors formed by control sh-NCcells. The total tumor weight was significantly less in the sh-FBI-1-JAR cell einjected mice than in the control mice as well. These results support our findings in in vitro models that FBI-1 is instrumental to the growth of CCA cells (Mak et al., 2015, in press). By MTT assay, the proliferation rates of JAR and JEG-3 were found to decrease when FBI-1 was downregulated by shRNA approach with statistical significance reached in JEG-3 (p < 0.05). To explore the mechanism involved, the relative levels of a panel of stem cell related genes, including Shh, Patched, Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Kif7, Nanog, Oct4, Sox2, and Stat3, were assessed after knockdown of FBI-1 gene by quantitative real time PCR. Shh was found to be consistently downregulated in JEG-3 and JAR transfected with FBI-1 shRNA constructs (Cheung, 2013).

763211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
763211.value: Our research clearly demonstrated that decreasing FBI-1 signaling in choriocarcinoma can lead to cell death and decreased invasiveness of the malignant cells. In addition, our results have revealed the upstream regulators of FBI-1 expression. Therefore, our research has implied novel strategies to tackle this malignant disease. For example, viral delivery of miR-125 family may control the expression of FBI-1 in choriocarinoma. The knowledge that FBI-1 increase cell invasiveness through PI3K signaling also suggests that drugs targeting this pathway such as rapamycin and XL147 may be useful in the management of this disease. Such new possibilities in choriocarcinoma treatment would be invaluable for treating rare chemoresistant choriocarcionoma. As a transcription factor, FBI-1 is expected to mediate the various cellular effects through transcriptionally regulating other genes. Currently little is known about the transcription targets of FBI-1 in GTD. With our cell line models, it would be interesting to map the majority of FBI-1’s transcription targets through combination of chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) and RNA-seq. Briefly, the sites bound by FBI-1 on the genome will be revealed by ChIP whereas those genes directly and indirectly regulated by FBI-1 is revealed by RNA-seq of the transcriptome. These experiments will deepen our understanding of the role of FBI-1 in GTD.

763211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
763211.value: Gestational trophoblastic disease (GTD) is a family of heterogeneous trophoblastic lesions with different malignant propensity. Hydatidiform mole is the commonest GTD whereas choriocarcinoma is the most malignant one. FBI-1 is an oncogenic protein overexpressed in several solid tumors. We propose that FBI-1 is involved in the pathogenesis of choriocarcinoma. Indeed, we demonstrated that FBI-1 protein expression was increased in GTD, especially in choriocarcinoma, when compared with normal placentas. Such overexpression is not caused by amplification of the gene encoding FBI-1, but due to epigenetic modification of the gene and the effect of a group of microRNA regulators called miR-125 family. High level of FBI-1 protects the malignant cells from cell death, as well as increases their invasiveness while knockdown of FBI-1 reduces cell proliferation. The specific signaling pathway activated by FBI-1 has been pinpointed, opening possibility of interfering FBI-1 action by pharmacological means. As a proof of concept, we successfully impeded the invasion of choriocarcinoma cells by the drug LY294002. Genetic manipulation of the FBI-1 in choriocarcinoma cells also showed that decreasing FBI-1 rendered the cells less capable of forming tumors. Our research deepened the understanding on the pathogenesis of GTD and enabled exploration of alternative therapy for the patients.

763411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
763411.value: In Hong Kong, the prevalence of chronic pain was 45.9%. Another reports revealed that more than 0.6 million peoples are suffering from chronic pain in Hong Kong. Impacts on daily life included mood, mobility and work performance. Many chronic pain patients are suffering from neuropathic pain. A recent study conducted in Canada noticed that chronic pain was present in 35% of the surveyed population. 17.9% of them presented with neuropathic pain symptoms. The substantial costs to society of neuropathic pain derive from direct medical costs, loss of ability to work, loss of caregivers’ ability to work and greater need for institutionalization or other living assistance. Endothelin-1 (ET-1) is a sequence of 21-amino acid peptides which is expressed ubiquitously in vascular endothelium, central nervous system (CNS), peripheral nervous system (PNS), and a variety of other cell types such as smooth muscle cells, neurons, and astrocytes. Due to its potential important role in the pain processing system, the mechanism of ET-1 had been studied on animal models but the underneath mechanism remains elusive. We have successfully produced GET transgenic mice model. Transgenic ET-1 mice appears normal under physiological condition, and its overexpression of ET-1 is about 18 fold more than the non-transgenic littermates in the brain. With the use of GET-1 transgenic mice, we can study the role of the endogenous astrocytic ET-1 on neuropathic pain. As ET-1 is suggested to be antinociceptive in the CNS and the pathway and source of the pain-inhibiting endogenous ET-1 remains unknown, studying neuropathic pain on the GET-1 transgenic mice model may give further implications to these questions. 763411.label: Realisation of objectives
763411.value: The four proposed objectives have been fully achieved through two consecutive studies. In our first study, by using targeted over-expression of astrocytic ET-1 in mice (GET-1) mice, we demonstrated that targeted over-expression of astrocytic ET-1 alleviated sciatic nerve ligation (SNL)-induced neuropathic pain significantly, providing evidence to support the notion that central ET-1 is play an important role in ameliorating neuropathic pain. To get an in-depth understanding of the beneficial effects of central ET-1 in neuropathic pain, antagonists of the two subtypes of ET-1 receptor, ETA-R and ETB-R were employed to examine which subtype mediate the observed effects of over-expressed astrocytic ET-1-in attenuating neuropathic pain in our above-mentioned experiments. We showed that antagonism of ETA-R but not ETB-R significantly reversed the pain-relieving effect of over-expressed astrocytic ET-1, indicating that over-expressed astrocytic ET-1 conferred protective effects in neuropathic pain mainly through ETA-R. Previous studies showed that glutamate was the key neurotransmitter in pain transmission and that ET-1 could modulate glutamate transporter, the excitatory amino acid transporter-2 (EAAT-2). As much as important as the excitation of synaptic activity by glutamate, EAAT-2 is mandatory in the maintenance of glutamate homeostasis in the synapse. Thus, we also evaluated the involvement of this glutamate-associated effect under modulation by over-expressed astrocytic ET-1 in neuropathic pain. In our second study, we demonstrated that, in GET- mice (with over-expressed astrocytic ET-1) but not non-transgenic mice, post-SNL EAAT-2 level was significantly up-regulated associated with less pain response than non-transgenic mice. We specifically looked into the role of glutamate transporter in the protective effects of ET-1 in neuropathic pain as demonstrated in our second study. At this stage, we have provided strong evidence that central ET-1 modulates neuropathic pain processing via ETA-R with mechanism involving the modulation of glutamate transporter (i.e. EAAT-2). Through these two studies, we not only provided in-depth understanding of the pathophysiology of neuropathic pain but also provided evidence to facilitate the development of ET-1 axis into future drug target in neuropathic pain treatment.

763411.label: Major findings and research outcome
763411.value: The endothelin system has emerged to be important in pain processing in recent years, but less is known on its mechanism, especially in the central nervous system. Our studies, with the advantage of utilizing TET-1 and GET-1 transgenic mice, not only clarify the role of astrocytic ET-1 in inflammatory pain suppression, but also warrant the use of GET-1 model for insight mechanistic study in treatment of neuropathic pain. In our first study, we investigated the role of astrocytic ET-1 in neuropathic pain using GET-1 mice. For the first time, we demonstrated that targeted over-expression of ET-1 in the astrocytes improved allodynia and hyperalgesia in the sciatic nerve ligation (SNL) induced-neuropathic pain. Moreover, over-expression of astrocytic ET-1 conferred anti-allodynic and anti-hyperalgesic effects through the inhibition of ERK1/2 and Akt signaling transduction pathways via ETA-R. This key finding has been published in the journal of Molecular and Cellular Neuroscience, which recognizes original research of exceptional significance in areas of neurosciences, particularly in synaptic activity and neuron-glia communication. Our study has also been authenticated with significant novelty that it was invited to be featured in the Global Medical Discovery [ISSN 1929-8536] series as a key scientific article contributing to excellence in biomedical research. Last but not least, we have recently published our second study on the significance of astrocytic ET-1 on glutamate transporter regulation. In this study, we demonstrated that endogenous over-expression of ET-1 in astrocytes exerts analgesic effect on SNL-induced neuropathic pain by up-regulating expression of EAAT-2 (Glutamate transporter) at the spinal cord levels. The most interesting outcome of this study is that EAAT-2 expression was induced under chronic overexpression of astrocytic ET-1 condition in which it exerts analgesic effect against neuropathic pain. This finding suggests, for the first time, a positive regulation of EAAT-2 by ET-1 in pain processing in in vivo neuropathic pain model, which is contrarily to the reported negative regulation of EAAT-2 by ET-1 in vitro. Taken together, we provide strong evidence that higher amount of central ET-1 plays a critical role in pain inhibition via ETA-R involving down-regulation of ERK1/2, Akt and up-regulation of EAAT-2. Our studies give additional rationale for developing ET-1 as a therapeutic target to intervene neuropathic pain. The related studies in this project have led to 2 full-length publications and 2 abstracts. In addition, 2 more studies, which are mostly based on the outcome of this project, are being under preparation.

763411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
763411.value: High potential for further development of the research is suggested, as the action of central ET-1 in pain modulation still remains largely unexplored. Also, in addition to our current findings, the mapping of the cellular expression pattern and level of ET-1 in central nervous system is important in attempts to explain the differential action of ET-1 on its receptors, as well as the structure of ET-1 receptors. We propose that further study is needed to confirm the source of the inhibitory central ET-1 in pain processing. Furthermore, the differential regulation of EAAT-2 in vivo and in vitro by ET-1 implies the complexity of endothelin system in the regulation of EAAT-2. Thus, our finding gives an implication that there are other mechanisms contribute to ET-1 modulation on neuropathic pain and that verification of these potential mechanisms in multiple models of neuropathic pain is warranted .

763411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
763411.value: Neuropathic pain (NP) can be difficult to be managed because of the complexity and multiplicity of its nature. In clinical practice, the treatment of NP is often inadequate because effective pharmacological therapy is not always available or its application is limited by its adverse side effects. Therefore, investigations of the underlying mechanisms of NP and new potential therapeutic target for its treatment are important future directions to improve the quality of life of the patients as well as its economic burden on society. ET-1, a well-known vasoconstrictor and neuromodulator has been suggested to alleviate pathological pain. However, the working mechanism of ET-1 remains unclear. Our project has revealed that higher amount of ET-1 in the central nervous system plays a critical role in NP suppression, which gives additional rationale for developing therapeutic targets to intervene NP that could be beneficial to the treatment of NP. These findings not only expand our understanding of the role of ET-1 in the development of NP but also show important insights into the molecular-genetic mechanisms that may facilitate the development of new strategies for the prevention and treatment of NP.

763811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
763811.value: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a common form of dementia involving slowly developing degeneration of neurons in the brain. AD is affecting more than 30 million people worldwide and the number of affected individual will quadruple by 2050. The causes of AD are still not clear, but mutations in some proteins that result in early-onset cases of the disease provide clues for the origin of the disease. One of these proteins, presenilin, causes the amount of calcium in cells to be abnormally regulated. Because calcium is a key signaling molecule that regulates many brain functions, this abnormality may be a key part of the disease. Calcium is stored in a special compartment, endoplasmic reticulum (ER), within the cell. Calcium releases from ER to intracellular space upon stimulation and the emptied calcium store has to be replenished from the outside of cell before another stimulation kicks in. These calcium release and entry machineries provide signals for other downstream cellular processes. Calcium in cells is precisely regulated, because it is toxic if its concentration is too high or too low. Chronic abnormal calcium regulation as a result of mutations in presenilin may therefore cause cellular toxicity that leads to neurodegeneration. Experimental data demonstrated that mutant forms of presenilin which cause AD influence both calcium release and entry pathways. However, the mechanisms of how mutant presenilins affect these pathways are largely unknown, especially for the calcium entry pathway. The recent identification of ER calcium sensor, STIM1, and calcium conductive protein, Orai1, provide a mechanistic framework for the regulation calcium entry pathway. In addition, our recent discovery of a molecular interaction between presenilin and STIM1 suggests that they may cooperate with each other to regulate calcium homeostasis in cells. We plan to study how presenilin interacts with this important calcium sensor to alter its function, and how altered calcium entry pathway in turn affects synaptic functions in the brain. These studies should provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms of AD pathogenesis and into the development of novel targets for therapeutic interventions. 阿爾茨海默氏症（Alzheimer’s disease，老人癡呆症）是一種常見及發展緩慢，由大腦神經元衰退所引發的癡呆症。現時世界上約有三千萬人受 老人癡呆症 影響。到2050年病人的數量將會是現時的四倍。 老人癡呆症 的致病原因至今仍然是一個謎，但研究由某些蛋白質突變所引發的早發性老人癡呆（FAD）會為我們提供老人癡呆病發之線索。早老因子（PRESENILIN）是這些蛋白之其中一員，此蛋白的突變會使細胞內鈣離子調控失衡。由於鈣是一個重要的信號分子，它調控很多腦功能，鈣離子調控失衡可能是老人癡呆症之發病誘因。鈣離子儲存於一個特殊的細胞器，內質網（ER）內。當細胞受刺激而從內質網釋放所有鈣離子到細胞腔，空的內質網必須從細胞外引入鈣離子來填補所失去的鈣。這個鈣離子的釋放與補充機制為細胞提供了必須的下游信號。細胞內的鈣離子必須精確地調節，因為鈣離子濃度的過高或過低都是有毒的。早老因子所誘發的持續性鈣調控失衡，可能導致老人癡呆、神經細胞衰退的原因。實驗數據表明，早老因子突變會影響鈣離子的釋放及流入機制。然而，早老因子突變如何影響這些機制還是未知的，特別是其對鈣流入機制之研究可謂少之又少！近期所鑑定的內質網鈣離子傳感器（STIM1）及鈣離子導電蛋白（Orai1)，提供了一個鈣釋出及流入的調控機理框架。此外，我們發現早老因子和STIM1會接合在一起。由此推斷，它們可能會相互協調來調控細胞內鈣的動態平衡。我們將會研究早老因子如何與鈣傳感器接合及改變其功能，以及早老因子之突變如何影響鈣離子流入之機理，及其對大腦突觸功能之影響。通過是次之研究我們將會為老人癡呆症的發病原因提供一些新的線索 ，並為其藥物治療提供可干預之目標。

763811.label: Realisation of objectives
763811.value: 1. To determine the effect of PS1 mutations on capacitative calcium entry We generated stable human neuroblastoma lines SH-SY5Y expressing either wild-type or mutant PS1 by retroviral infection. After we obtained stable cell lines, we performed single-cell Ca2+-imaging on these cell lines. Capacitative Ca2+ entry was triggered by depleting the ER Ca2+ with 5 µM carbachol in the absence of extracellular Ca2+. We revealed that CCE in PS1M146L was attenuated as compared to PS1WT expressing cells or cells infected with GFP virus. Several other FAD-linked PS1 mutations (PS1-V97L, -A136G and -A246E) also showed attenuation in CCE. We also investigated whether the attenuated CCE is a gamma-secretase-dependent process. With the pretreatment of gamma-secretase inhibitor DAPT, attenuated CCE in mutant PS1 was restored. In addition, we observed potentiation of CCE in PS1WT and control cell lines suggesting CCE is negatively regulated by gamma-secretase. 2. To determine the molecular players involved in FAD PS linked CCE deficits STIM1 and Oria1 are two essential players involved in the CCE process. To determine whether mutant PS1 affects the expression of STIM1 and Orai1, we performed western blots using cell lysates obtained from the stable cell lines that we have generated. Our results indicated the expression of STIM1 and Orai1 were similar in all cell lines which suggest the attenuation of CCE is not due to down-regulation of the expression of STIM1 or Orai1 by mutant PS1. 3. To determine the biochemical interaction of PS1, STIM1 and Orai1 Instead, we found interaction between PS1 and STIM1 by co-immunoprecipitation when these proteins were co-expressed in HEK293 cells. We further demonstrated endogenous interaction of PS1 and STIM1 in native SH-SY5Y cells by in situ proximity ligation assay. Furthermore, using FRET microscopy, we found mutant PS1 inhibited STIM1 oligomerization during ER Ca2+ store depletion thus leading to attenuation of CCE. Since STIM1 and APP are type I transmembrane protein, we reasoned that STIM1 may be a substrate of gamma-secretase. Therefore we performed in vitro secretase assay and provided evidence that STIM1 is a substrate fro gamma-secretase. 4. To determine the relevance of CCE deficits in AD pathogenesis We investigated the effect of PS1 expression on neuronal spine morphology in cultured rat hippocampal neurons and found mutant PS1 reduced mature dendritic spines. This reduction can be rescued by gamma-secretase inhibitor or STIM1 overexpression. Taken together, we identified a new physiological of gamma-secretase in regulating CCE and our result suggest a novel therapeutic target for the treatment of AD.

763811.label: Major findings and research outcome
763811.value: Calcium dysregulations in presenilin (PS) mutation associated familial Alzheimer’s disease (FAD) can be attributed by exaggerated calcium (Ca2+) release and attenuated Ca2+ entry (CCE). Over the pass decade, several mechanisms have been proposed to describe exaggerated Ca2+ release but the pathogenic mechanism for CCE deficits remains elusive. Here, we showed that PS1 mutation associated CCE deficits is a conserved phenotype and dependent on the γ-secretase activity. Expression of mutant PS1 did not affect STIM1 and Orai1 expressions, instead, we demonstrated endogenous interaction between PS1 and STIM1 in SH-SY5Y cells. Sequence analysis revealed that STIM1 and APP transmembrane domains showed high similarity and mutant PS1 enhanced γ-secretase cleavage of STIM1. Our results suggest a molecular mechanism of CCE deficits that Mutation in PS1 enhances γ-secretase cleavage of STIM1 and thereby reduces the recruitment of Orai1, resulting in CCE attenuation. The PS1 mutation induced CCE attenuation destabilized neuronal spine maturation and treatment of γ-secretase inhibitor or ocerexpression of STIM1 rescued spine deformity. Taken together, our findings suggested a physiological role of PS1/γ-secretase which modulates the availability of STIM1 and provided novel therapeutic target for the treatment of AD. We are at the final stage of submitting our findings for publication (will be submitted to PNAS, see attached manuscript in Part C). In addition, we have investigated the effect of two Chinese specific PS1 mutations (V97L and A136G) on cellular Ca2+ homeostasis. Consistent with other FAD-linked PS1 mutation, these Chinese specific PS1 mutations also showed Ca2+ disruption. We have secured a NSFC grant to support our further investigation on the mechanisms for Ca2+ disruption in these two Chinese specific PS1 mutations. After we confirmed the disrupted Ca2+ homeostasis in human fibroblast harboring these two mutations from patient donors, we will submit our observations for publication. Furthermore, two postgraduate research students are trained by the support of this funding (Part C). We have presented our findings in some international and regional scientific symposia, including Gordon Research Conference, in the form of invited oral and poster presentations (Part C). Research student, Mr. Benjamin Tong has been awarded the best poster presentation in two scientific conferences (Part C). We have generated stable cell lines and presenilin mutation constructs that are available upon requested.

763811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
763811.value: We have studied 4 FAD-linked PS1 mutations and all of these mutations showed attenuation in CCE. The consistent results suggest that CCE deficits may be a conserved phenotype for PS-mutation associated AD. If this assumption is true, this attenuation in CCE can be used as a diagnostic method to detect familial AD. In addition, the identification of STIM1 as a substrate for gamma-secretase may suggest a novel therapeutic target for the treatment of AD. We have submitted a HMRF proposal to the Department of Health for seeking funding to continue the current study on the Ca2+ disruption in AD. In collaborating with Prof Jia JP in Xuanwu Hospital (Part C), we can access the human fibroblasts isolated from familial AD patients and the clinical relevance of disrupted Ca2+ homeostasis to AD can be addressed further. Furthermore, mutation in PS also impaired neuronal autophagy pathway. However the underlying mechanism is yet to be defined. Since we have already generated many cell lines and reagents with the support of this RGF fund, we will make good use of these resources to elucidate the pathogenic mechanism of impaired autophagy in AD. Results from this study should suggest new therapeutic targets for treating the disease.

763811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
763811.value: Alzheimer’s disease is the most common type of dementia with brain cells damage and the pathogenic cause is yet to be defined. Evidence has suggested that disruption in neuronal calcium (Ca2+) balance due to impaired Ca2+ entry (CCE) plays a proximal role in AD pathogenesis. However the molecular mechanism of CCE deficits is unclear. This research aimed to elucidate the mechanism in attenuated CCE and its relevance to AD pathology. We demonstrated presenilin-1 (PS1) interacts with cellular Ca2+ sensor, STIM1 and FAD-linked PS1 mutation enhances γ-secretase-mediated STIM1 cleavage. As a result, STIM1 failed to activate the membrane Ca2+ channel resulting in the attenuation of CCE. To correlate CCE deficits and AD pathology, neuronal spine morphology has been studied in rat hippocampal neurons. Expression of FAD-linked PS1 mutation reduced mature spine density that can be rescued by the treatment of γ-secretase inhibitor or overexpression of STIM1. This study revealed a new physiological role of γ-secretase that linking the attenuation of CCE to destabilization of mature spine. The identification of STIM1 as a substrate of γ-secretase suggest novel therapeutic target for AD treatment.

764111.label: Realisation of objectives
764111.value: Objective 1. Determine the effect of GEP antibody targeted therapy: 100% achieved. The effect of targeted therapy using GEP antibody has been examined in vivo and in vitro. The orthotopic animal model implanted with human liver cancer Hep3B cells into the liver organ has been used. High-dose of GEP antibody (10 mg/kg, twice weekly) inhibited intrahepatic tumor growth and enhanced cell apoptosis in the current study. [Compared to our previous study on subcutaneous model that low-dose of GEP antibody (2 to 5 mg/kg, twice weekly) only reduced tumor proliferation with no significant effect on apoptosis induction]. Notably, high-dose of GEP antibody revealed no health concerns on the tumor-bearing animals including disability or weight loss. No impairment on the vital organs and no tissue damage such as fibrosis in the normal livers. In vivo, GEP antibody treatment reduced the serum GEP levels in the animals bearing the GEP-positive liver tumor. In vitro, GEP antibody decreased the secretary GEP levels in the culture supernatant, reduced the binding of exogenous GEP onto liver cancer cell surface, and diminished the phosphorylation of AKT and ERK1/2. In summary, GEP antibody treatment alone was consistently able to inhibit the tumor growth but unable to eliminate the established intrahepatic tumor. Objective 2. Evaluate the role of GEP on liver cancer chemo-resistance: 100% achieved. The therapeutic value of GEP antibody targeted therapy, in combination with chemo-therapeutic agents, has been examined in vivo (orthotopic mouse model) and in vitro. Both in vivo and in vitro, liver cancer cells that survived after chemotherapy, including chemo-therapeutic agents cisplatin and doxorubicin, demonstrated up-regulation of hepatic cancer stem cell markers CD133/GEP/ABCB5. The chemotherapy selected liver cancer cells showed enhanced cancer stem cell properties, including colony formation and spheroid formation abilities. Importantly, combination of GEP antibody therapy and chemo-therapy reversed the phenotypes induced by chemo-therapy alone in the liver cancer cells and also the chemo-resistant subpopulations. Furthermore, combination therapy counteracted the chemotherapy-induced GEP/ABCB5 expressions and Akt/Bcl-2 signaling. In the orthotopic xenograft models, combination of GEP antibody (10 mg/kg, twice weekly) with low dose of cisplatin (3.75 mg/kg, once weekly) resulted in significant synergistic effect on proliferation inhibition and apoptosis induction compared to single agent treatment. Notably, combination of GEP antibody (same dose, 10 mg/kg, twice weekly) with high dose of cisplatin (5 mg/kg, once weekly) resulted in the eradication of all established intrahepatic tumor in three weeks. Throughout the monitoring period (nine weeks after treatment stop), all the animals remained tumor-free and there was no tumor recurrence in any animals in the combination group that had received GEP antibody plus high dose cisplatin.

764111.label: Major findings and research outcome
764111.value: Granulin-epithelin precursor (GEP) is a growth factor and its over-expression has been revealed in many cancers by us and other research groups. Recently, we demonstrated that GEP regulated chemo-resistance and cancer stem cell (CSC) properties. In the present study, we have investigated the combined effect of GEP antibody and chemotherapeutic agent using hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells in vitro and orthotopic models in vivo. We demonstrated that HCC cells that survived under chemotherapeutic agents showed upregulation of hepatic CSC markers CD133/GEP/ABCB5, and enhanced colony and spheroid formation abilities (Molecular Cancer Therapeutics 2014). Importantly, GEP antibody sensitized HCC cells to the apoptosis induced by chemotherapy for both HCC cell lines and the chemoresistant subpopulations, and counteracted the chemotherapy-induced GEP/ABCB5 expressions and Akt/Bcl-2 signaling. In human HCC orthotopic xenograft models, GEP antibody treatment alone was consistently capable of inhibiting the tumor growth. Notably, combination of GEP antibody with high dose of cisplatin resulted in the eradication of all established intrahepatic tumor in three weeks (Molecular Cancer Therapeutics 2014). The research platforms and assays on GEP antibody that have been developed in the present study has essentially facilitated the characterization of GEP binding partners / receptors (Carcinogenesis 2014; PLoS One 2012). GEP blockage by antibody has reversed the cancer phenotype on escape of immune destruction (OncoImmunology 2015; Cancer Immunology Research 2014) and resisting cell death (Cancer Cell International 2014). Furthermore, the present study has expedited the work that GEP overexpression has been partly contributed by increased gene copy number (BMC Cancer 2015). The application of GEP antibody as cancer therapeutics have been detailed (Molecular Cancer Therapeutics 2014; OncoImmunology 2015). In summary, this preclinical study demonstrated that GEP antibody sensitized HCC cells to apoptosis induced by chemotherapeutic agents. Combination treatment with GEP antibody and chemotherapeutic agent has the potential to be an effective therapeutic regimen for human cancers. The result of the present study has been published in Molecular Cancer Therapeutics 2014. The fundamentals of this study has strengthened the research platforms on cancer growth and chemo-resistance characterization, which directly supported the publication of additional six referred research articles.

764111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
764111.value: Development of clinical therapeutics against granulin-epithelin precursor (GEP): The current study has demonstrated proof-of-principle that systemic delivery of GEP antibody as drug to inhibit liver cancer growth. The present study further showed that combination of GEP antibody with chemotherapy drug resulted in the regression and elimination of liver cancers established in the liver organs. We would work in collaboration with industry to humanize the antibody for clinical use. The research platforms and assays built would further facilitate the research work on identification of GEP receptor (unknown in cancer cells in the literatures), characterization of GEP signaling pathway, and development of small molecule inhibitors as cancer drugs.

764111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
764111.value: Granulin-epithelin precursor (GEP) is a growth factor and its over-expression has been revealed in many cancers by us and other research groups. Recently, we have demonstrated that GEP regulated chemo-resistance and cancer stem cell properties. In the present study, we have investigated the combined effect of GEP antibody and chemotherapy drug. Liver cancer cell models and animal models were used to examine the functions and signaling molecules. We demonstrated that liver cancer cells that survived under chemotherapy drugs showed up-regulation of liver cancer stem cell markers CD133/GEP/ABCB5, and enhanced cancer stem cell properties. Importantly, GEP antibody enhanced the effect of chemotherapy drug by sensitizing the liver cancer cells to cell death and suppression of cancer stem cell related signaling molecules. In animal models, GEP antibody treatment alone was consistently able to inhibit the growth of liver cancer. Notably, combination of GEP antibody with chemotherapy drug resulted in the regression and elimination of liver cancers established in the liver organs. This preclinical study demonstrated that GEP antibody enhanced the functions of chemotherapy drugs. Combination treatment with GEP antibody and chemotherapy drug has the potential to be an effective approach for cancer treatment.

764411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
764411.value: 被套細胞淋巴腫瘤的微小核糖核酸甲基化研究 套细胞淋巴瘤是一种B细胞淋巴瘤。最初曾认为它是惰性淋巴瘤，后逐渐确定它是一种侵袭性极强的非霍奇金淋巴瘤。发病机制涉及细胞周期蛋白D1表达上调和特殊的染色体异位t (11;14)(q13;q32)，近来又发现包括拷贝量变化的其他遗传学改变也可能参与发病。套细胞淋巴瘤的中位生存期只有3年，随着对其生物遗传学认识的加深,急需寻找新型治疗方案。 MicroRNA(miRNA)是一类由内源基因编码的，长度约为22-25个核苷酸的非编码单链RNA 分子。它们会导致目标蛋白的降解，而miRNA的异常表达调控会导致肿瘤的发生。miRNA可被称为致癌miRNA (oncomir)或抑癌miRNA，这取决于miRNA的靶基因是抑癌基因或致癌基因。近来研究表明miRNA的表达受启动子的DNA甲基化调控。 DNA甲基化是指在甲基转移酶（DNMTs）的催化下，DNA的CG两个核苷酸的胞嘧啶环的第5位碳原子被选择性地添加甲基，形成5－甲基胞嘧啶。抑癌基因的启动子相关CpG岛的高甲基化，会导致转录抑制，这进一步造成基因失活而参与肿瘤发生。在血液系统肿瘤中，相关信号通路研究发现，基因启动子的高甲基化可能导致细胞周期调控以及JAK/STAT信号通路的失活。 在基因表达的表观遗传学调控中，组蛋白修饰和启动子的DNA甲基化密切相关。H3和H4组蛋白N端赖氨酸和精氨酸残基，可以被甲基化，乙酰化和磷酸化修饰，从而激活或沉默相关基因的表达。关于组蛋白密码基因表达的大部分结果来自发育生物学的研究，因此肿瘤学中组蛋白标记对基因表达, 尤其对于miRNA表达调控的研究，仍处于初步阶段。 随着表观遗传治疗的愈加成熟，肿瘤学研究中，对于其表观遗传变化的认识也显得更加重要。在骨髓增生异常综合征的临床治疗中，5-氮杂胞苷和地西他滨的应用能够提高病人的药物反应率和生存期。伏瑞思特，作为组蛋白去乙酰化抑制剂，现已被批准用于皮肤T细胞淋巴瘤的治疗。因此，在套细胞淋巴瘤的治疗中，表观遗传治疗可能也起到重要作用。为此，我们计划研究DNA高甲基化在套细胞淋巴瘤中的作用，这将为以后关于高甲基化抑癌miRNAs的组蛋白修饰的作用相关研究打下基础，也有助于我们进一步理解在套细胞淋巴瘤中miRNAs的表观遗传学变化。

764611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
764611.value: 剛射精後的精子不能直接令卵細胞受精，而是需要在女性生殖道裡經過活能過程從而獲得受精能力。這一過程中精子發生生理和生化的變化，包括精子表面上巰基數量的增加。活能化的精子與卵細胞外殼（透明帶）結合而開始受精過程。男性不育的其中一個主要原因就是由於精子與透明帶結合缺陷。這種缺陷影響了約80%精子數量較少的男性。 儘管精子-透明帶的結合至為重要，其調控機制尚未明確。為了解決這一難題，研究人員嘗試在精子表面鑑定出負責精子透明帶結合的分子（受體）。儘管部分潛在的受體已經被確定，但越來越多的證據表明，受體可能是一個需要多種蛋白質來調控其功能的多分子受體復合物。 我們未發表的數據顯示精子表面巰基數目的增加會提高人類精子的透明帶結合能力。我們亦從活能化的精子表面上分離了幾個能與透明帶結合的受體複合物。蛋白質二硫鍵異構酶家族A,成員3(ERp57)的酶被鑑定為這些受體複合物的其中一個組成分子。 ERp57在其他細胞中具有增加細胞表面巰基數目的功能。用ERp57的抗體去阻礙ERp57的功能能夠顯著地抑制人類精子的透明帶結合能力。一些可能與ERp57相關的透明帶受體複合物的組成分子亦已被鑑定。抑制它們中至少一個的功能也能夠抑制精子透明帶結合。 我們推測精子在活能化後,細胞表面上ERp57的表達能夠調節透明帶受體複合物上的巰基狀態，從而調控人類精子與透明帶間的結合。我們將通過以下三個方面來檢驗該假設：（1）分析精子活能化、ERp57活動、精子表面上巰基狀態變化與透明帶結合的相互關係;（2）分析ERp57相關的透明帶受體複合物組成分子的巰基狀態與透明帶結合的相互關係;以及（3）臨床輔助生育中巰基狀態與受精率的聯繫。 這個項目的成果將會讓我們更深入地理解精子與透明帶間的相互作用。它能首次直接證明精子上的透明帶受體為分子復合物。此項目對於是否能夠通過提高精子表面的巰基來提高臨床輔助生育的受精率,與及是否能夠通過檢測精子表面上巰基含量來預測精液樣本的生育能力這兩個問題提供指示。

764611.label: Realisation of objectives
764611.value: Human fertilization begins when a spermatozoon binds to the ZP. With the use of ultrasensitive mass spectrometry, we have identified sialyl-Lewis(x) (SLEX) sequence (NeuAcα2-3Galβ1-4(Fucα1-3)GlcNAc) as the most abundant terminal sequence on the glycans of human ZP [6]. SLEX is also the major carbohydrate ligand for human spermatozoa-ZP binding Thiol (S-H)-Disulfides (S-S) status is crucial to protein structure, folding, localization and function. ERp57 belongs to the protein disulphide isomerase (PDI) family important in modulating the thiol status at the cell surface of several cell types. The thiol content of spermatozoa is associated with sperm maturation and infertility in humans. Capacitation induces surface thiol-disulfide exchange increasing the sperm surface thiol content. However, the role of such change in thiol status in fertilization is unknown. We hypothesize that capacitation enables translocation of ERp57 to the sperm surface and form ERp57-associated zona pellucida (ZP) receptor complex, and that ERp57 can modulate spermatozoa-ZP interactions through regulation of the thiol status of the receptor complex. Objective 1. To establish the relationship between capacitation, sperm surface reductase activity, thiol status and spermatozoa-ZP binding. In this objective, we demonstrated for the first time an association between sperm surface thiol content and ZP-binding capacity of human spermatozoa with four observations. First, capacitated spermatozoa had a higher ZP binding capacity and sperm surface thiol content when compared to uncapacitated spermatozoa. Second, capacitation induced an increase in thiol content at the acrosomal region of human spermatozoa, a region important for ZP-binding. Third, the ZP-binding capacity of uncapacitated spermatozoa was up-regulated by increasing the sperm surface thiol content (by thioredoxin) or PDI surface expression (by calyculin A). Finally, inhibition of the sperm surface PDI activity (by bacitracin) and/or thiol formation (by diamide) suppressed the ZP-binding capacity of capacitated spermatozoa. Objective 2. To characterize the formation of ERp57-associated ZP receptor complex. Blue native polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (BNG) and Western ligand blotting were developed and used to identify the solubilized ZP/SLEX-binding complexes on capacitated spermatozoa. The identified ZP/SLEX-binding complexes were resolved by a second-dimension of polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis followed by mass spectrometric analysis to identify the components of the complexes. The localization and expression of sperm surface thiol and ERp57 was studied by immunostaining and sperm surface protein biotinylation followed by Western blotting. We demonstrated that at least two protein complexes on capacitated spermatozoa possess solubilized ZP-binding capacities. One of which contains four protein components (HSPA2, SPACA3, CALR and ERp57). The results provided direct evidences on the existence of multimolecular ZP receptor complexes on capacitated human spermatozoa. Our immunostaining results localized the ERp57 expression to the head, midpiece and tail region of human spermatozoa. There is no significant difference in the total ERp57 expression between uncapacitated and capacitated spermatozoa. However, Western blot analysis of the biotinylated sperm surface proteins indicated an up-regulation on the sperm surface ERp57 expression after capacitation. Although the mechanism for the capacitation-induced relocalization is unknown, the successful ERp57 surface relocalization induced by calyculin A (a phosphatase 1/2A inhibitor) in uncapacitated spermatozoa indicates that the event may be associated with phosphatase inhibition. Objective 3. To determine the role of ERp57-associated ZP receptor complex components in spermatozoa-ZP interaction. We demonstrated for the first time that the sperm surface ERp57 is important in regulating the sperm surface thiol content and spermatozoa-ZP binding. ERp57 is translocated to the sperm surface at the acrosomal region during in vitro capacitation. Since acrosomal region is responsible for spermatozoa-ZP binding, the up-regulation of acrosomal ERp57 expression highlights the importance of ERp57 in spermatozoa-ZP binding. Furthermore, up-regulation of the ERp57 surface expression in vitro stimulated the surface thiol formation and ZP-binding capacity of human spermatozoa. On the other hand, blocking of ERp57 function by specific antibody or inhibitors against ERp57 reduced the surface thiol content and ZP-binding capacity of human spermatozoa. Our results further demonstrated the ERp57-calreticulin (CALR) interaction on human sperm plasma membrane by immunofluorescence staining and co-immunoprecipitation followed by Western blotting. Sperm surface ERp57 can regulate the thiol status of CALR, on the capacitated sperm surface. CALR has been shown to mediate human sperm functions including A23187-induced acrosome reaction and spermatozoa-ZP binding. To conclude, our results provide first evidence that sperm surface ERp57-CALR interaction is involved in human fertilization. 4. To determine the relationship between sperm surface thiol content, ERp57 surface expression and fertilization rate in vitro. In this study, semen samples from men visiting the subfertility clinics at Queen Mary Hospital after standard semen analysis were used. Normozoospermic and asthenozoospermic semen samples according to WHO criteria (WHO, 2010) were processed by Percoll discontinuous (45% and 90%) density gradient centrifugation. Asthenozoospermic samples had significantly (P<0.05) lower percentage of motile spermatozoa than normozoospermic samples. Percoll processing recovered a population enriched with motile spermatozoa and a population with less motile spermatozoa from the interface between the 45% and the 90% layers. We demonstrated that normozoospermic sample has a higher sperm surface ERp57 expression and thiol content than that of asthenozoospermic sample. In addition, poor quality sperm isolated from a percoll gradient have decreased expression of ERp57 and consequently defective ZP-binding capacity, a well know indication of successful fertilization. These data suggest that reduction in sperm surface thiol content and ERp57 expression is a possible cause of fertilization problem in reproduction.

764611.label: Major findings and research outcome
764611.value: - By using BNG/SDS-PAGE and Western ligand blotting technique followed by mass spectrometric analysis (Part C, Section 8, No. 1), we demonstrated that there are protein complexes on capacitated spermatozoa which possess solubilized ZP/SLEX-binding capacities (Part C, Section 8, No. 2-4; Section 9, No. 1). One of which contains four protein components (HSPA2, SPACA3, CALR and ERp57). The results provided direct evidences on the existence of multimolecular ZP receptor complexes on capacitated human spermatozoa (Part C, Section 8, No. 4; Section 9, No. 2 and 3; Section 10, No. 1). - Sperm surface thiol and ERp57 immunoreactivity were demonstrated to be localized at the head region of capacitated spermatozoa, a region responsible for ZP-binding (Part C, Section 8, No. 4; Section 9, No. 2 and 3; Section 10, No. 1). Up-regulation of the surface thiol content or ERp57 surface expression in vitro stimulated ZP-binding capacity of human spermatozoa (Part C, Section 8, No. 4; Section 9, No. 2 and 3; Section 10, No. 1). - Capacitation significantly increased the sperm surface thiol content, acrosomal thiol distribution and ERp57 expression on sperm surface (Part C, Section 8, No. 4; Section 9, No. 2 and 3; Section 10, No. 1). - ERp57 is translocated to the sperm surface at the acrosomal region during in vitro capacitation. It is important in regulating the sperm surface thiol content and spermatozoa-ZP binding (Part C, Section 8, No. 4; Section 9, No. 2 and 3; Section 10, No. 1). - Sperm surface ERp57 can regulate the thiol status of CALR, on the capacitated sperm surface. CALR has been shown to mediate human sperm functions including spermatozoa-ZP binding (Part C, Section 8, No. 5; Section 10, No. 1). - Normozoospermic sperm sample has a higher sperm surface ERp57 expression and thiol content than that of asthenozoospermic sample (Part C, Section 9, No. 3). - Poor quality sperm isolated from a percoll gradient have decreased expression of ERp57 and consequently defective ZP-binding capacity, a well know indication of successful fertilization (Part C, Section 9, No. 3).

764611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
764611.value: - The present study demonstrated that increased thiol content on sperm surface via thiol-disulphide exchange is involved in the capacitation-induced acquisition of sperm fertilizing capability. The mechanism for the stimulatory effect of sperm surface thiol formation on sperm-ZP binding is unknown. One possibility is that the thiol-disulphide exchange of sperm surface protein may modulate the intracellular signalling pathway activation, and thereby the capacitation process and ZP-binding capacity. - Our results suggest that increase in sperm surface thiol groups may enhance fertilization in assisted reproduction. In fact, a positive role of thiol modulation of sperm proteins on success of in vitro fertilization or enhancement of fertilizing ability of spermatozoa from different mammalian species have been demonstrated with the use of reduced glutathione (a reducing agent). Treatment with reduced glutathione decreases reactive oxygen species (ROS)-induced disulphides level in sperm proteins. Therefore, apart from the widely accepted protective role of reduced glutathione against ROS-induced sperm damage, the beneficial effects of reduced glutathione treatment on sperm fertilizing ability may also be mediated by its thiol-disulphide modulating activity on sperm surface proteins as demonstrated in the present study. Further studies are required to confirm this hypothesis.

764611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
764611.value: Successful fertilization depends on proper functioning of a spermatozoon and an oocyte. It is initiated by the binding of the capacitated spermatozoa to the zona pellucida (ZP) of the oocyte. The mechanisms of spermatozoa-ZP binding are unclear. Accumulated evidence suggested that the sperm ZP-receptor is a composite structure requiring coordinated action of different proteins that are assembled into a functional complex during the capacitation. Our results provided direct evidence for the expression of a multimeric protein complex on the plasma membrane of capacitated human spermatozoa that is capable of binding to the ZP. ERp57 was a component of the complex. We further demonstrated that thiol-disulphide exchange is a crucial event in capacitation which is modulated by ERp57, and primes for the successful fertilization to take place. The outcome of this project gives a better understanding on the spermatozoa-ZP binding. Clinically, the results support the hypothesis that modulating the surface thiol content of the sperm sample of subfertile men may help to increase fertilization rate in assisted reproduction.

764711.value: 自七拾年代，多溴聯苯醚已被廣泛用於阻燃劑上。而現今海洋環境中的多溴聯苯醚有增加的趨勢。其中，南中國地區更成為世界主要的電子廢料棄置區。這些電子廢料含有多溴聯苯醚，因此在海水、沉積物、魚體、海洋哺乳動物及海洋無脊椎動物也錄得非常高濃度的多溴聯苯醚。 有不少文獻記錄多溴聯苯醚如何影響哺乳類和魚類，而數據顯示多溴聯苯醚能導致哺乳類(包括人類)及魚類發育不正常和生殖障礙。因此多溴聯苯醚開始引起研究重視。可是，關於多溴聯苯醚對海洋無脊椎動物的影響近乎一無所知。只有極少資料提出多溴聯苯醚能對貽貝的卵泡和卵母細胞造成損害和抑制海蝨幼生生長。從我們最近的研究顯究，當多溴聯苯醚在環境臨界濃度下，能夠改變海洋多毛類幼生的著床行為和著床後的成長。因此，多溴聯苯醚極有可能減弱海洋無脊椎動物的適合度性狀，並且帶來生態上的嚴重後果。 文獻指出在哺乳動物和魚類裡，多溴聯苯醚能從母體傳至下一代。可是，它對下一代的影響仍然是未知之數。而我們亦不清楚多溴聯苯醚能否從海洋無脊椎動物的母體傳至下一代及母源性傳遞的多溴聯苯醚會否削弱子代的發展和適合度性狀。 拖鞋舟螺，是一種海洋腹足動物，常見於南美及北美太平洋沿岸，中國，日本和香港。它在底棲浮遊聯結中扮演著重要的角色。我們將會以拖鞋舟螺為模式無脊椎動物族群來進行研究，我們假設當海洋無脊椎動物長期暴露在與現實環境多溴聯苯醚濃度相同的情況下，它們的適合度性狀會被影響。此外，我們亦假設母源性傳遞的多溴聯苯醚會影響幼生成長並削弱子代的適合度性狀。我們將會研究 在幼生，幼體和成蟲的攝多溴聯苯醚動力學和多溴聯苯醚的生物累積，以及量化在幼生體內的母源性傳遞多溴聯苯醚。 本計劃是首個針對母源性傳遞多溴聯苯醚在海洋無脊椎動物及其跨代的影響進行的科學研究。我們將會運用系統性研究來評估多溴聯苯醚對海洋無脊椎動物的適合度性狀的影響，並對此在海洋裡日益漸增的污染物進行環境風險評估。

764711.label: Realisation of objectives
764711.value: The project has been successfully completed and all the four project objectives fully met. Furthermore, we have carried out additional experiments to (a) determine the effects of PBDEs on two other important marine invertebrates (i.e. barnacle and serpulid worm), and (b) study the proteomic changes of C. onyx and identify differential expression of eight proteins in response to PBDEs. Overall, we demonstrated that dietary exposure to PBDEs could not only cause a higher mortality rate, smaller size of juveniles and delay in sexual maturity in F0, but also a higher embryonic mortality and malformation in the F1 generation. Our finding further revealed that PBDEs could reduce the bacterial abundance in biofilms and hence, alter the settlement pattern of marine invertebrate larvae.

764711.label: Major findings and research outcome
764711.value: 1) Water exposure to BDE-47 (up to 1 µg L−1) throughout the entire larval stage did not affect settlement, development or growth of C. onyx (Chiu et al. 2012). Additional experiment was carried out to test whether BDE-47 would affect other marine invertebrates from different phyla and the results showed that larval settlement, development and growth of Hydroides elegans and Balanus amphitrite were also not affected. 2) However, bioaccumulation was clearly evident in all three species (measured body burden ranging from approximately 7 to 13 µg BDE-47 g−1 lipid) (Chiu et al. 2012). 3) BDE-47 reduced the bacterial abundance in biofilms and resulted in a concomitant change in the settlement pattern of marine invertebrate larvae (Chiu et al. 2012). 4) Despite growth and development of C. onyx larvae were not affected by water exposure, results of 2-DE proteomics studies (coupled with triple quadrupole and high-resolution TOF-MS) revealed that larval proteome was altered by BDE-47 treatment. Furthermore, eight proteins related to cytoskeletal architecture, stress tolerance, metabolism and energy production were found differentially expressed in response to BDE-47. It was suggested that C. onyx larvae may have a proteome plasticity to cope with BDE-47 toxicity (Mukherjee et al. 2013). 5) In the chronic dietary exposure experiment, the microalgae Isochrysis galbana were collected for chemical analysis after they were exposed to BDE-47. Interestingly, OH-PBDEs and BDE-28 were found at the high concentration treatment (i.e. 1 mg L-1). For the first time, we demonstrated that microalgae could convert PBDEs into OH-PBDEs, which are more toxic than PBDEs. This finding may have significant implications pertaining to the origin and environmental risk of PBDEs in the marine environment. 6) Ca. 4.9% of the PBDEs accumulated in C. onyx when they were fed with I. galbana containing 366 µg BDE-47 (and 0.098 µg BDE-28) g−1 lipid. The treated F0 generation exhibited a higher mortality rate, smaller juvenile size and delay in sexual maturity. They also produced more embryos that failed to develop into larvae (embryo death rate ~30% in the treatment group compared to ~10% in the control). Even when the larvae hatched successfully, these F1 individuals showed a threefold increase in malformation rate. Similar adverse effects on F1 embryos were also observed in the low concentration treatment, where C. onyx were fed with I. galbana containing 35 µg BDE-47 g−1 lipid. The F1 individuals accumulated 1.85 and 60.1 µg BDE-47 g−1 lipid in the low and high concentration treatments, respectively.

764711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
764711.value: The fire retardants PBDEs have become ubiquitous in the marine environment. This study showed that despite water exposure to PBDEs did not affect settlement, development or growth of marine invertebrates (slipper limpet, barnacle and serpulid worm) at environmental realistic concentrations, they might reduce the bacterial abundance in biofilms and hence, alter larval settlement pattern. In contrast, dietary exposure to PBDEs did not only cause a higher mortality rate, smaller juvenile size and delay in sexual maturity in F0 of C. onyx, but also a higher embryo death rate and malformation of the F1 generation, suggesting trans-generational effects. Furthermore, for the first time, we demonstrated that the microalgae Isochrysis galbana could convert PBDEs into OH-PBDEs, which are more toxic than their precursors. Overall, results of this study have significant implications in the origin and environmental risk assessment of PBDEs in the marine environment.

765011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
765011.value: 在生物自遠古海洋向多樣的陸地生態環境演化過程中，為保護細胞免受外界液體影響，滲透壓調節機制需要不斷進化。陸生哺乳動物具有精密的生理和行為機制以保持體內滲透壓穩定：生理機制包括腎臟對於水分和電解質的調節，這一過程主要由抗利尿激素（VP）控制；在行為方面則由所謂致渴激素----血管緊縮素（ANGII）調節。特定的神經細胞受到體液滲透壓變化的刺激，引起上述的滲透壓調節過程。近年研究表明，胰泌素（SCT）在滲透壓調節神經細胞中有顯著表達，並參與體液平衡調節的多個過程。在GRF支持下，我們研究團隊已經證實胰泌素可在身體失水後，由垂體後葉分泌。因此，胰泌素可能控制一個獨立於抗利尿激素的滲透壓調節過程，這也是研究人員長期尋找的。胰泌素這一新功能合理解釋了諸如腎源性尿崩症，D-型抗利尿不當綜合症等臨床症狀。我們最新的研究說明，腦內注射胰泌素可刺激動物飲水。有鑑於此，我們計畫深入研究腦部胰泌素在體內通過怎樣的過程調節動物飲水。此外，作為兩種功能部分重迭的激素，胰泌素和血管緊縮素如何協同調節動物飲水也是尚待解決的問題。現時研究表明，G蛋白偶聯受體可形成同質或異質寡聚體，從而產生重要的生理功能。胰泌素受體（SCTR）以及血管緊縮素受體（AT1R）都可以與其他多種受體結合形成異質寡聚體。基於初步的研究結果，我們提出以下假設：胰泌素和血管緊縮素在腦部神經細胞中，通過受體的異質寡聚過程，調節受體的功能和細胞內遷移，從而協同控制動物飲水。這一研究，連同其他功能和結構的研究，有助於從生理和行為方面進一步瞭解人體的體液調控機制。

765011.label: Realisation of objectives
765011.value: Objective 1: In vivo mechanisms of central SCT in stimulating water intake Our group has substantiated a role of secretin(SCT) at all levels of the hypothalamus-pituitary-kidney axis to regulate body water homeostasis. Data from our group showed that central injection of SCT could directly stimulate water intake in wild type and SCT-/-, but not SCTR-/-. Based on this and other information, in our proposal, we hypothesized that central SCT is a dipsogenic peptide. To substantiate this, we used immunohistochemical(IHC) to quantify c-fos gene expression in in brain regions that are involved in osmoregulation, including SFO, OVLT, MnPO, PVN. We found increased numbers of cells with Fos-IR in both the lamina terminalis and these regions along with localization of SCT and SCTR proteins and transcripts. More importantly, we worked on exploring the effect of SCTR/AT1aR complex on hyperosmolality-induced drinking in mice. To perform this, we employed selected transmembrane(TM) peptides of SCTR and AT1aR that were able to interact with their respective receptors alone as well as within complexes in our initial in-vitro studies. Hyperosmolality-induced drinking is suppressed by i.c.v. injection of angiotensin receptor TM-1(ATM-1) peptide indicating an in vivo effect of the SCTR/AT1aR complex. Our data clearly show that AT1aR/SCTR heterooligomer formation is critical and plays a crucial physiological role in central water homeostatic pathway. Objective 2: In vitro mechanism of SCT as a dipsogen In this objective, we wanted to identify the mechanism underneath the overlapping functions of SCT and ANGII in inducing drinking. Potential cross-activation between SCT and ANGII pathways could be explained by the formation of SCTR/AT1aR receptor oligomers. Therefore, this objective focuses on verifying this dimerization event in vitro. Firstly, we confirmed the dimerization of SCTR/AT1R by BRET assay using other receptors AT2R and CCKR as controls. It was further found that SCTR and AT1aR associate to form heterocomplexes that reduce cAMP responses to SCT. Our data also indicated that when AT1aR is active, either by mutation or by binding ANGII, the active conformation of the SCTR was favored and the cAMP response was rescued. Furthermore, we investigated the effect of transmembrane (TM) peptides of SCTR and AT1aR in competitive BRET assays to understand their role in the formation of the SCTR/AT1R heterocomplex and their effect in cAMP response. We found that SCTR TM-4 and AT1aR TM-1 and TM-4 are able to interact with and inhibit the formation and cAMP signaling of the SCTR-AT1aR heterocomplex.
