765011.label: Major findings and research outcome
765011.value: Through the support from this GRF grant, we have worked on exploring the effect of SCTR/AT1aR complex on hyperosmolality-induced drinking in mice and its role in dipsogenic effect of central SCT. Firstly, in-vitro studies confirmed the dimerization of SCTR/AT1R by BRET assay. We detected a robust BRET signal with the cells co-expressing SCTR with mAT1aR while no interaction could be found in AT2R and in other receptors including cholecystokininB receptor confirming the specificity of the results. The cAMP levels in SCTR/AT1aR co-transfected cells when stimulated with a low concentration of SCT peptide was reduced. Co-expression of SCTR with AT2R had no effect. Our data also indicated that when AT1aR is active, either by mutation or by binding ANGII, the cAMP response was rescued. Furthermore, we used synthetic peptides corresponding to 7 TM-segments of SCTR and AT1aR in BRET assay to understand their role in the formation of the SCTR/AT1R heterocomplex. The peptides corresponding to the sequences of SCTR-TM-2(STM-II) and TM-4(STM-IV), as well as AT1aR-TM-1(ATM-1) and TM4(ATM-4) significantly inhibited BRET. These effects were found to be specific as their mutants with substitutions at their lipid exposed faces and TM peptide from AT2R(AT2R-TM4) had no effect on the BRET signal. Our data indicate that STM-IV, ATM-1 and ATM-4 are able to interact with and inhibit the formation and cAMP signaling of the SCTR-AT1aR heterocomplex. More importantly, hyperosmolality-induced drinking was suppressed by i.c.v. injection of ATM-1 peptide, indicating an in vivo effect of the SCTR/AT1aR complex. Under hyperosmotic condition, significant increases in water intake were found in SCTR+/+ mice but not in SCTR-KO or H-89 injected mice, establishing that the hyperosmolality-induced drinking is mediated via the SCTR-cAMP-PKA pathway. To demonstrate in vivo effects of receptor oligomerization, STM-II, STM-IV, ATM-1, and ATM-4 and their mutated counterparts were injected into the lateral ventricles, and water intake was monitored. STM-IV and ATM-4 that inhibit both homo- and heterooligomer formation, as well as cAMP production by SCTR in vitro, were able to strongly suppress water intake, while their mutated peptides had no effect. ATM-1 and STM-II, which affected only the BRET signal from the heterocomplex of AT1aR/SCTR, was still capable of strongly suppressing water intake. In summary, our data clearly shows that the heterocomplex of AT1aR/SCTR plays a pivotal role in mediating water-drinking behavior. These results have been published as a research article in FASEB Journal(Leo et al., 2014) and discussed as review articles(part C).

765011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
765011.value: To further understand the effect of TM peptides on SCTR/AT1aR complex, we have performed preliminary experiments that show TM (ATM1) peptide to be inhibiting central SCT/ANG2 induced vasopressin release into circulation. We will perform detailed research on the effect of central SCT/ANG2 in specific regions of the brain such as PVN and SFO that are related to osmoregulation and the role of SCTR/AT1aR hetero-oligomer complex and TM peptides in these specific regions and their effect in water homeostasis. We believe it could lead us to detailed mechanistic insight into the role of SCTR/AT1aR dimer in physiology. In continuation of our interest in exploring oligomeric GPCR complexes, we have also started studying the dimerization of SCTR and AVPR (vasopressin receptor). A library of GPCR has been constructed in our laboratory during the past two years and we plan to study in details the hetero-oligomeric GPCR complexes in long-term.

765011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
765011.value: Water/salt homeostasis is one of the three fundamental issues, together with reproduction and growth/metabolism, in the study of life sciences. As the most important gene family in bridging extracellular conditions with intracellular responses, GPCRs are the target of one-third of therapeutic drugs on the market. Our findings clearly show that AT1aR/SCTR hetero oligomer formation is critical in water homeostatic pathway and that it plays a crucial physiological function in our body. Our data also importantly show that TM peptides are potentially useful tools that can modulate GPCR functions by interaction and/or disruption of oligomeric complexes. These peptides are specific in their action, since they are structurally homologous to part of the target GPCRs. The functional specificity of each TM peptide has the potential to be applied in vivo to gain insights into whether these processes occur in that setting. In addition, these peptides, like the ATM-1 peptide, can be used to specifically inhibit physiological functions due to the formation of certain receptor complexes. Our work is fundamental to the area of water homeostasis and is important in understanding actions of SCT, ANGII and water homeostasis in our body.

765111.value: 摘要研究 背景: 臨床試驗發現氟化胺銀能防止及硬化兒童的牙冠齲。這項簡單和價格低廉的治療方注在過去十年間愈受重視。世界衛生組織亦正在研究其應用於齲病的控制。牙根齲現在巳越來越普遍，但一般難以用常規方法處理。氟化銀胺可能是一個實制的牙根齲治療方法。對於氟化銀胺在牙根礦物質和垢膜微生物的影响，現今的科學研究並不多。 目標: 是項實驗利用人工口腔系統，研究氟化胺銀對正常及有齲牙根表面的礦物質含量和垢膜微生物動態及結構上的影響。 方法: 從拔掉的人體磨牙制成齒根方塊。一半數量的齒根方塊將被接種致齲垢膜造形齒根齲。所有的齒根方塊會被平均分為三組，並塗上：甲）氟化胺銀，乙）氟化鈉（陽性對照），或丙）蒸餾水（陰性對照）。塗後的齒根齲方塊將接種致齲垢膜，並在無氧人工口腔系統內定期 “餵”與蔗糖三週。實驗的根齲方塊將會在基線及每週後量度齒根的硬度，礦物元素及有機物質成份，垢膜微生物動態及結構。 可能的結果和影響: 氟化胺銀在人工口腔系統內能有效保護齒根對垢膜致齲細菌的損害，若跟進的體內研究確認實驗結果，氟化胺銀可能是一種有效防止和控制齒根齲的方法。由於塗氟化胺銀在齒根齲是無痛，簡單及成本低廉，它可以廣泛推薦來替代傳統的根面齲治療方法，尤其是在那些難以接受常規牙科護理，或有特殊需要的患者及長者身上。因為氟化胺銀有助保護牙齒，它的長期效益可以很大。

To validate, using targeted assays, the DNA methylation pattern of selected candidate genes in larger cohort of SLE and control cases.

To compare the epigenomic/epigenetic variants identified in this study with the multiple genetic risk factors contributing to SLE susceptibility identified through our genome-wide association study in Chinese SLE patients.

765311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
765311.value: SLE is an autoimmune disease with multi-system damage and significant morbidity and mortality. It affects > 7,000 people in Hong Kong and many more in other Asian countries. Experimental evidence suggests that genetic and environmental factors, mediated by epigenetic factors, are involved in the pathogenesis. Epigenetics refers to changes in gene expression that are not accompanied by a change in primary nucleotide sequence. Epigenetic marks include alterations in DNA methylation, chromatin conformation, and noncoding RNA transcripts. Mammalian DNA methylation is the most stable type of epigenetic modification and different evidence point to the possible involvement of DNA methylation in the pathogenesis of SLE:- 1) Global loss of DNA methylation in T cells is associated with autoimmunity in humans with idiopathic and drug-induced SLE. 2) T cells from patients with active SLE are found to have sequence-specific DNA hypomethylation and overexpression of autoimmune-related genes, resulting in autoreactivity, excessive B-cell stimulation and cytotoxicity. 3) A recent study in monozygotic twins discordant for SLE showed changes in DNA methylation by genome-wide profiling. We hypothesize that epigenetic alterations in critical genomic regions can contribute significantly in the pathogenesis of SLE. We predict that in our patients with SLE, there will be enrichment for epigenetic alterations in genes with important immune functions which may lead to autoimmunity. Our objective is to characterize the genome-wide DNA methylation pattern in Chinese patients with SLE compared to controls. We include 40 SLE patients and 40 controls from the cohort already in place from our previous SLE genetics study. We use a new high-throughput technology- The Illumina HumanMethylation27 which allows the interrogation of DNA methylation levels spanning more than 14,000 genes per sample at single-nucleotide resolution. The data will be analyzed using the Illumina analysis software and other bioinformatic pipelines that generate quantitative methylation data for thorough downstream analysis. The top 10 candidate epigenomic/epigenetic variants will be validated in larger SLE cohort and compared with the genetic risk factors identified to have contribution to SLE susceptibility through our previous genome-wide association study. The data will enable us to generate a genome-wide comprehensive map of DNA methylation in Chinese SLE patients. Since epigenetic regulation controls the expression of genes, epigenomic/epigenetic variants could have the same consequences as genetic polymorphisms. However, importantly in contrast to genetic sequence variations, epigenetic changes are potentially reversible. This information will provide more insight in the pathogenesis and may identify epigenetic targets for pharmacologic interventions.

765311.label: Realisation of objectives
765311.value: All objectives have been achieved. For objective 1, we had successfully recruited patients with SLE and also the age- sex, and ethnicity-matched controls to carry out genome-wide DNA methylation analysis by microarray. Instead of using the Illumina HumanMethylation27 micorarray which is stated in the original proposal, the Illumina HumanMethylation450 BeadChip was used for genome-wide DNA methylation analysis because it is the more recent version of microarray and covers more CpG sites and genes than previous version of microarray. The use of this new version of microarray allowed the discovery of a total of 36 CpG sites showing loss of DNA methylation and 8 CpG sites showing gain of DNA methylation, representing 26 genes and 7 genes respectively. The unique DNA methylation pattern of SLE patients has been identified by gene oncology analysis, where type I interferon related genes were hypomethylated in SLE patients. Regarding objective 2, four genes have been selected for validation and replication by bisulfite pyrosequencing, in a larger cohort of 100 patients and 100 controls, which achieved the second objective of this project. In fact, we further investigated the effect of hypomethylation in these genes by quantifying the mRNA expressions in the replication cohort, and found that these genes have increased in expressions. Lastly, the epigenetic variants identified have been compared with the genetic variants identified in our department's genome-wide association study on SLE, but we did not identify any overlapping genes, suggesting that genetic variants and epigenetic variants in SLE are located in different genes, each has its unique role in contributing to the pathogenesis of SLE.

765311.label: Major findings and research outcome
765311.value: To characterize the genome-wide DNA methylation changes in SLE patients, the Illumina HumanMethylation450 BeadChip was used. It was found that there were 36 CpG sites with differential loss of DNA methylation while 8 CpG sites with differential gain of DNA methylation, representing 26 genes and 7 genes respectively. Gene Onology suggested that hypomethylated genes were overrepresented in type I interferon. And it is important to note that type I interferon has long been implicated in the pathogenesis of SLE, therefore our finding suggests the importance of type I interferon from the epigenetic point of view. The location where the loss of DNA methylation in the genome was also examined, and it was found that nearly half of the hypomethylated CpG sites were located in the CpG island shores, where CpG island shore is found to be associated with most tissue specific differential DNA methylation, and also in disease such as breast cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma and type 2 diabetes. To replicate and validate the results of our microarray study, an additional cohort of 100 SLE patient and 100 healthy controls were recruited for confirmation by bisulfite pyrosequencing. Four hypomethylated genes were selected for validation and replication, and confirmed the results in microarray that loss of DNA methylation was associated in SLE patients. Moreover, to test the effect of hypomethylation on gene expressions, real time PCR has performed in the replication cohort, and we found that loss of DNA methylation was associated with increased in mRNA expression in corresponding genes. Besides, since it is known that DNA methylation can be affected by ethnicity, our study recruited patients of Chinese ethnicity only, and therefore our 450k microarray provides the specific genome-wide DNA methylation map on Chinese SLE patients, which is different from other studies which make use of mixed ethnicity for analysis. This allows the discovery of genes pathways important in Chinese only.

765311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
765311.value: The identification of hypomethylation of type I interferon related genes in whole blood opens the door for further investigation on the effect of loss of DNA methylation in SLE. And it would also be interesting to study whether the hypomethylation of type I interferon related genes is the cause or the effect of the SLE. Moreover, blood composed of multiple cell types, and different cell types have its unique role in SLE pathogenesis. Therefore, the unique DNA methylation pattern from each specific immune cell could be investigated. This will allow the discovery of unique DNA methylation change in each cell type, and could help understanding more about the role of each cell type in SLE. In fact, we are going to study the DNA methylation of each immune cell types.

765311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
765311.value: We have found that the loss of DNA methylation in type I interferon related genes resulted in increased gene expression in corresponding genes, providing more insight in SLE pathogenesis. Furthermore, our study gives us the unique genome-wide DNA methylation pattern that specifically on Chinese SLE patients, which is different from other studies which make use of mixed ethnicity for analysis. All these findings allow the discovery of epigenetic changes and their related biological pathways important in Chinese patients with SLE and our findings may have diagnostic, prognostic and therapeutic implications in the future.

765511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
765511.value: 在模式植物擬南芥中存在一個由六個基因組成的酰基輔酶A結合蛋白家族，命名為ACBP1至ACBP6。這些蛋白都有一個保守的能夠結合長鏈酰基輔酶A的酰基輔酶A結合區。這些蛋白有著不同的亞細胞定位，這就意味著它們在脂類代謝的過程中可能有不同的功能。ACBP1和ACBP2在內質網和細胞膜表達； ACBP4, ACBP5和ACBP6是細胞溶質蛋白；而ACBP3是細胞外蛋白。因為這些蛋白可以轉運脂類物質，我們希望能夠通過研究進而確定它們在脂類代謝過程中的作用。本研究項的目標是：（1）確定擬南芥酰基輔酶A結合蛋白在植物表皮（角質層）脂類合成過程中的生物學功能；（2）研究ACBP1及其可能的互作蛋白間的相互作用。同ACBP1一樣，這些可能的互作蛋白也預計在細胞膜上表達。這項研究很有可能在擬南芥中發現新的成脂代謝體。疏水的角質層由表皮素（蠟狀質）和角質層蠟質組成，它們能夠保護植物不受外界環境的傷害，因此，更好的了解表皮和角質層的脂類合成能夠指導如何提高植物防止非氣孔失水以及對植物病原體和食草動物的抵抗能力。我們初步的掃描電鏡結果表明：缺失ACBP1蛋白的突變體的蠟質層結晶模式與野生型的擬南芥不同。隨後的分析進一步證明這個突變體的表皮蠟質成分少於野生型。相似的研究方法將用於研究其它的酰基輔酶A結合蛋白是否也參與了表皮脂類代謝。微量量熱學方法將用於研究這些酰基輔酶A結合蛋白與表皮脂類合成前體體外結合作用。已經由酵母雙雜交實驗確定的ACBP1的互作蛋白將采用體外結合實驗以及農桿菌侵染煙草葉片瞬時表達熒光標記蛋白實驗進一步確定。這些互作蛋白的T-DNA插入突變體以及RNA幹擾突變體將用來研究它們的功能。脂質譜分析的方法將用來研究這些突變體脂類成分的變化。這些互作蛋白的抗體將用於免疫定位實驗來確定它們的空間表達模式以及它們與ACBP1在脂類代謝中的功能。

765511.label: Realisation of objectives
765511.value: The project has fulfilled its 2 objectives. Arabidopsis ACYL-COA-BINDING PROTEIN1 (AtACBP1) plays important roles in embryogenesis, seed and seedling development, as well as in abiotic stress responses. It interact with long-chain (LC) acyl-CoA esters, the precursors of cuticular lipid biosynthesis. AtACBP1 function in stem cuticle formation was investigated using transgenic Arabidopsis transformed with an AtACBP1pro::GUS construct and these studies revealed β-glucuronidase (GUS) expression on the stem (but not leaf) surface, suggesting its specific role in stem cuticle formation. Isothermal titration calorimetry results revealed that recombinant AtACBP1 interacted with LC acyl-CoA esters and very-long-chain (VLC) acyl-CoA esters (24:0-,25:0-, and 26:0-CoAs). VLC fatty acids have been demonstrated as precursors in wax biosynthesis. Gas chromatography (GC)–flame ionization detector (FID) and GC–mass spectrometry (MS) analyses revealed that acbp1 mutant showed reduction in stem and leaf cuticular wax and stem cutin monomer composition in comparison with the wild type. The acbp1 mutant showed fewer wax crystals on the stem surface in scanning electron microscopy and an irregular stem cuticle layer in transmission electron microscopy in comparison with the wild type. Mutant stems consistently showed a decline in expression of cuticular wax and cutin biosynthetic genes in comparison with the wild type, and mutant leaves were more susceptible to infection by the necrotrophic pathogen Botrytis cinerea. We suggest that AtACBP1 participates in Arabidopsis stem cuticle formation by trafficking VLC acyl-CoAs. AtACBP1 was shown to interact with PHOSPHOLIPASE Dα1 (PLDα1), and was induced by ABA. Transgenic Arabidopsis AtACBP1-over-expressors showed increased sensitivity to ABA during germination and seedling development, whereas the acbp1 mutant showed decreased ABA sensitivity during these processes. RNA assays showed that AtACBP1 over-production in seedlings up-regulated the expression of PLDα1 and three ABA/stress-responsive genes: ABA-RESPONSIVE ELEMENT BINDING PROTEIN1 (AREB1), RESPONSE TO DESICCATION29A (RD29A) and bHLH-TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR MYC2(MYC2). AREB1 and PLDα1 expression was suppressed in acbp1 in comparison with the wild type post-ABA treatment. PLDα1 promotes ABA signal transduction by producing phosphatidic acid, an important lipid messenger in ABA signaling. Seeds and seedlings of AtACBP1-over-expressing lines were shown to accumulate more phosphatidic acid post-ABA treatment, in contrast to lower phosphatidic acid in acbp1. Bimolecular fluorescence complementation assays indicated that AtACBP1 interacts with PLDα1 at the plasma membrane. Their interaction was further confirmed by yeast two-hybrid analysis. As recombinant AtACBP1 binds phosphatidic acid and phosphatidylcholine, ACBP1 can promote PLDα1 action. We suggest that AtACBP1 participates in ABA-mediated seed germination and seedling development.

765511.label: Major findings and research outcome
765511.value: The roles of Arabidopsis acyl-CoA-binding proteins particularly AtACBP1and its protein interactors in plant lipid metabolism including cuticular lipid biosynthesis have been established. The major findings include: 1. In Du et al (2013) we demonstrated that AtACBP1 plays important roles in seed and seedling development. AtACBP1 was shown to interact with PLDα1 using bimolecular fluorescence complementation assays and yeast two-hybrid analysis. As recombinant AtACBP1 binds phosphatidic acid and phosphatidylcholine, ACBP1 can promote PLDα1 action. ABA-inducible AtACBP1 likely participates in ABA-mediated seed germination and seedling development. 2. In Du and Chye (2013), the interaction between various AtACBPs and their protein interactors including that described in Du et al (2012) are reviewed. 3. In Xue et al (2014) we showed that recombinant AtACBP1 interacts with very long-chain acyl-CoA esters, the precursors of cuticular lipid biosynthesis and AtACBP1 functions in stem cuticle formation. Analysis of the acbp1 mutant confirmed its defects in cuticular wax biosynthesis using SEM and TEM. 4. In Chen et al (2014), the potential applications of AtACBPs and their protein partners in mediating abiotic stresses are discussed. 5. In Du et al (2015), the roles of AtACBP1 and AtACBP4 as potential candidates for phytoremediation are described. AtACBP1 and AtACBP4, were observed to be induced by lead [Pb(II)] in shoots and roots in qRT-PCR analyses and uantitative GUS (β-glucuronidase) activity assays. AtACBP1 and AtACBP4 were further compared in Pb(II) uptake using Brassica juncea, a potential candidate for phytoremediation with its high biomass and good capacity to accumulate heavy metals. Atomic absorption analyses on transgenic B. juncea expressing AtACBP1 or AtACBP4 indicated Pb(II) accumulation in roots. Subsequent Pb(II)-tracing assays confimed Pb(II) accumulation in the cytosol of root tips and vascular tissues of transgenic B. juncea AtACBP1-overexpressors (OXs) and AtACBP4-OXs and transgenic Arabidopsis AtACBP1-OXs. Lipid hydroperoxide measurements of B. juncea AtACBP1-OX and AtACBP4-OX roots indicated that AtACBP1 and AtACBP4 can protect lipids against Pb(II)-induced lipid peroxidation. 6. In Lung and Chye (submitted), we have described the various roles of AtACBPs and their partners in plant development. 7. In Lung et al (manuscript in preparation), the interactions of ACBP1 and ACBP2 with protein interactor STEROL-C4-METHYL OXIDASE1 at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and plasma membrane in Arabidopsis are reported. They appear to function together at the ER and plasma membrane in lipid transfer in sterol metabolism.

765511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
765511.value: The identification of sterol-C4-methyl oxidases as new interactors of AtACBP1 and AtACBP2 in sterol biosynthesis warrant further investigations. Three members of the STEROL-C4-METHYL OXIDASE1 (SMO1) family were identified as novel protein-protein interactors with ACBP1 and ACBP2 in yeast two-hybrid studies. Whilst one of the three recurring ANK units was sufficient to mediate protein-protein interaction, deletion of the acyl-CoA-binding (ACB) domain abolished this interaction. Establishment of the precise domain(s) for interaction between each SMO1 member and each of AtACBP1 and AtACBP2 will help us further understand the basis of their interaction. So far the protein-interacting motifs of SMO1-1 were mapped to its two cytoplasmic loops, in agreement with the topological prediction of ACBP1, ACBP2 and SMO1-1. More precise mapping using site-directed mutagenesis at the ANK domain will help is better relate these loops with protein-protein function. Site-directed mutagenesis of the ACB domain of ACBP2 (i.e. Y136A, K140A, K162A and Y181A) that had been shown to disrupt palmitoyl-CoA binding also prohibited protein-protein interaction with SMO1 but not AtFP6, another ACBP2-interactor. Thus an understanding on the significance of lipid-binding in protein-protein interaction needs to be achieved. In agroinfiltrated tobacco leaves, the enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP)-fusion proteins with SMO1 were co-localized with DsRed2-fusion proteins with ACBP1 and ACBP2 at the perinuclear and tubular endoplasmic reticulum (ER) networks and the plasma membrane. In transgenic Arabidopsis, SMO1::EGFP was associated with DsRed2::ACBP1 and DsRed2::ACBP2 at the ER cisternae of hypocotyls and spherical ER bodies of root cells. Hence, the significance for the differential localization of DsRed2::ACBP1 and DsRed2::ACBP2 in association with SMO1::EGFP needs to be studied, to further understand the relationship of these AtACBP proteins in plant sterol biosynthesis via their protein-protein interactions with SMO1. Also various mutants of the three SMO1 genes need to be identified for use in elucidating the function of each in association with each AtACBP.

765511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
765511.value: Lipids play widespread biological roles in energy storage and provision, cellular structure formation and signal transduction. ACBPs, as lipid-transfer proteins, they contribute to a numerous processes in plant growth and development, besides in stress responses. ACBP binding to lipids such as very long chain acyl-CoA esters supported a role in cuticular wax biosynthesis as shown in this study. In addition, investigations on the interaction between AtACBPs and their protein partners have revealed novel roles for AtACBPs. These include functions in mediating oxidative stress responses, heavy metal tolerance and ABA signalling during germination and seedling development. In this study, a variety of biochemical, reverse genetics and molecular biology techniques were used to specifically show that AtACBPs can interact with protein partners in seed and seedling development, in cuticular wax synthesis and sterol biosynthesis. The identity of the protein partners indicates the functions of AtACBPs and how they can participate, together with their protein interactors, in plant lipid metabolism and plant development. Subsequently, it is hoped that findings from ACBPs in Arabidopsis can be extended to crop plants.

765811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
765811.value: Background: Human influenza viruses are associated with considerable morbidity and mortality globally. There is little data on the efficacy of face masks or respirators to filter influenza viruses as a source control to prevent transmission. Purpose: To examine the comparative efficacy of alternative face masks in preventing airborne transmission of influenza virus. Design and subjects: We will recruit 500 participants with influenza-like illness from local outpatient clinics in Hong Kong in 2010-2011, and apply a rapid test to identify 100 subjects with influenza virus infection. Those 100 subjects will proceed to five experiments using a device capable of sampling bioaerosols in exhaled air: 1) 5 voluntary coughs over a 1-2 minute period with no face mask; 2) 5 voluntary coughs over a 1-2 minute period with a surgical face mask; 3) 5 voluntary coughs over a 1-2 minute period with an antimicrobial face mask; 4) 5 voluntary coughs over a 1-2 minute period with an N95 respirator (not fit-tested); 5) 5 voluntary coughs over a 1-2 minute period with no face mask (repeat). Specimens collected from the device, and nose and throat swabs from each participant will be subjected to further laboratory testing for influenza viruses. 背景： 人類流感病毒在全球各地引致相當高的發病率及死亡率。現時較少數據評估口罩透過過濾流感病毒作為源頭控制以防止流感傳播的成效。 目的： 就各類型口罩於防止流感病毒經空氣傳播的相對成效作出評估。 研究方法及對象： 我們將於２０１２至２０１３年間，從本地普通科門診邀請５００名流感樣疾病患者參與此研究，並以快速測試從中核實１００名感染流感病毒的患者。此１００名流感患者將會利用一部能採集從參與者口腔呼出氣體中之懸浮微粒的儀器進行五個實驗： １） 於１－２分鐘內不戴口罩自主咳嗽５次； ２） 於１－２分鐘內配戴醫學外科口罩自主咳嗽５次； ３） 於１－２分鐘內配戴抗菌口罩自主咳嗽５次； ４） 於１－２分鐘內配戴醫用防護口罩（俗稱N95口罩）自主咳嗽５次（未經密合度測試）；及 ５） 於１－２分鐘內不戴口罩自主咳嗽５次（重複）。 從儀器、鼻腔和喉嚨分別採集得來的樣本將被送往實驗室進行流感病毒化驗。

765811.label: Realisation of objectives
765811.value: We successfully achieved all of our planned objectives. We collaborated with Prof Donald Milton at the University of Maryland and Dr James McDevitt at Harvard School of Public Health to purchase a custom-built “Gesundheit-II” (G-II) aerosol sampling device, and used the device in Hong Kong to determine the presence and concentration of aerosols in exhaled breath and the efficacy of surgical face masks in reducing aerosol concentration. From 16/01/2013 to 11/03/2014 we enrolled 195 patients and collected exhaled breath samples from 22 patients with confirmed influenza A virus infection age ≥11 years old while wearing a surgical face mask or not using the G-II machine, finding support for our hypotheses that influenza virus can be cultured from fine particle aerosols in exhaled breath of patients with influenza, and that surgical masks reduce the amount of influenza virus-laden coarse particles. The realization of each of the objective is as follows: 1) In total 59 exhaled breath samples were collected from 40 participants positive by an influenza rapid test and an additional 5 participants testing negative, with 30 samples collected with a surgical mask and 29 samples without. We detected a significant difference in the effect of surgical mask on viral shedding of influenza A virus in the coarse (≥ 5 µm) (p-value: 0.02) but not the fine (< 5 µm) (0.71) fraction of exhaled breath. 2) Viral shedding in fine and coarse fraction of exhaled breath without a surgical mask was observed from tidal breathing with or without cough during the 30-minute exhaled breath collection. Viral shedding in the fine fraction of exhaled breath collected with a surgical mask was observed at 7 or more counts of cough, and none in coarse fraction even with a maximum of 36 counts of cough during collection. Infectious influenza A/H3N2 virus (2 log10 TCID50/0.1mL) was found in the fine fraction of exhaled breath in one subject who had the highest viral load by RT-PCR (4.45 log10 copies/mL). 3) We recovered influenza virus in the exhaled breath fine particles in 4/27 (15%) adults age ≥ 18 years old, and in 0/3 (0%) children/ teenagers age <18 years old; we recovered influenza virus in the exhaled breath coarse particles in 5/26 (19%) adults age ≥18 years old, and in 0/3 (0%) children/ teenagers age <18 years old. We did not identify any significant differences in viral shedding in exhaled breath comparing children and adults.

765811.label: Major findings and research outcome
765811.value: Our research has led to a series of conference presentations, and a draft manuscript. These are attached in Part C. The major findings of the study are as follows. Influenza A virus was detected in fine fraction of exhaled breath (<5μm) in 4/29 (14%) samples collected without a surgical mask compared with 3/30 (10%) samples with a surgical mask, and in coarse fraction of exhaled breath (≥5μm) in 5/29 (17%) samples collected without a surgical mask compared with 0/30 (0%) samples with a surgical mask, with a significant reduction of influenza virus shedding by the surgical face mask only in coarse fraction but not the fine fraction. Infectious influenza A/H3N2 virus was found in the fine fraction of exhaled breath in one subject who had the highest viral load by RT-PCR. Surgical face masks were effective in reducing influenza virus A dissemination in human exhaled breath in the coarse (≥5 µm) but not the fine (<5 µm) fraction, and infectious influenza A/H3N2 virus can be found in fine particle aerosols, indicating that surgical masks might not be able to provide complete protection against transmission if worn by infected persons. In addition we are preparing a second paper which is a 3-country comparison of influenza virus in exhaled breath in Hong Kong, Singapore, and Maryland, with the preliminary observation that virus concentration in fine particles was much higher in Maryland – consistent with the hypothesis that aerosols play a greater role in influenza transmission in temperate locations. We are preparing a third paper which is an analysis of the diagnostic sensitivity and specificity of the rapid point-of-care diagnostic test used in our study. We presented preliminary results of our research at the following international conferences: 1) One oral, and one poster presentation in Options for the Control of Influenza VIII (Cape Town, 2013), the largest conference in influenza research held every three years. 2) One oral-poster presentation in Indoor Air 2014 - The 13th International Conference on Indoor Air Quality and Climate (Hong Kong, 2014), the largest conference in aerobiology held every three years. In addition, preliminary results were presented at the following local conferences in Hong Kong: 1) One poster presentation in the Annual Scientific Meeting, Hong Kong College of Community Medicine (Hong Kong, 2013) In addition, this grant supported the training of a PhD student, Nancy Hiu Lan Leung (2012-15).

765811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
765811.value: In 2014 the PI was awarded a grant of HK$1m from the Health and Medical Research Fund (Hong Kong), for a project entitled “Efficacy of face masks to prevent respiratory virus transmission (Ref: 13120592)”. Whereas our RGC project focused on influenza viruses, this new project expands the scope to other common respiratory viruses and will provide novel data on the potential for aerosol transmission of pathogens such as rhinovirus, parainfluenza and adenovirus. We are planning further grant applications to maximize the value of the G-II machine, including a grant to examine longitudinal changes in virus shedding in exhaled breath (i.e. take serial measurements on the same patients), and a grant to examine cytokines in exhaled breath as a marker of the inflammatory immune response to infection, in comparison to inflammatory markers measured in nasal washes and peripheral blood.

765811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
765811.value: Around 10% to 20% of people suffer influenza virus infections every year. Most infections are very mild and do not require medical attention, but a small fraction of infections lead to severe disease, or exacerbate underlying conditions such as heart disease, and at the population level the burden of influenza is substantial. Around 750 deaths and many thousands of hospitalizations are associated with influenza virus infections each year in Hong Kong. There are still many uncertainties about how influenza viruses spread between people, or which approaches can effectively control transmission. One controversial issue is whether influenza virus can spread through very small particles, called aerosols, which can remain airborne for prolonged periods and can pass through or around the sides of surgical masks. In our study we enrolled 22 patients with confirmed influenza A virus infection, and identified influenza viruses in the exhaled breath of 4 of those patients. We found no evidence that surgical face masks could filter out influenza virus that was detected in fine particles in exhaled breath, indicating that surgical masks cannot provide complete protection against transmission if worn by infected persons.

766211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
766211.value: We and others have demonstrated that Coptidis rhizoma (huanglian 黄连 in Chinese) and its major active compound, berberine, possess broad spectrum of anti-cancer activities. Most of these anti-tumour studies of berberine were conducted in in vitro cell culture systems. Scanty information is available on the effects of berberine on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in vivo. We have performed a pilot study to examine the effects of berberine on HCC cells using both in vitro and in vivo cancer models. Berberine inhibited growth of multiple cell lines of HCC in vitro. Expression of Id-1 in multiple HCC cells was inhibited by berberine at non-cytotoxic doses. The effect of berberine on the growth of a human HCC xenograft tumour (MHCC-97L) orthotopically implanted in the liver of athymic mice was monitored by a live animal optical imaging system (Xenogen IVOS). We observed that berberine could inhibit growth of the orthotopically implanted tumors during the treatment course. Our previous publications have shown Inhibitor of Differentiation/DNA synthesis (Id-1) can act as an oncogene to promote liver tumor progression and metastasis. It induces both cell proliferation and angiogenesis (by activation of HIF-1and VEGF) in HCC cells. Our preliminary results demonstrated that berberine is a potent suppressor of Id-1 expression in HCC cell lines. Furthermore, suppression of Id-1 expression by berberine is associated with downregulation of cyclin D1, VEGF, HIF-1and NF-κb signaling. Suppression of tumor angiogenesis could be observed in mice treated with berberine. We also found that berberine could potently suppress the activation STAT3, which has been reported to be one of the upstream regulators of Id-1. We hypothesize that suppression of Id-1 expression and its downstream signaling pathways may play an important role in the anti-tumour actions of berberine. 766211.label: Realisation of objectives
766211.value: The objective 1 has been fully achieved. We have conducted animal study with orthotropic hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) implantation model with different liver cancer cell lines expressing luciferease reporter. While MHCC97L could successfully generate implanted tumor, most of other cell lines are not tumorigenic in vivo. Consistent inhibition on tumor growth by berberine could be observed across liver tumor generated by different cancer cell lines, and both oral administration and intraperitoneal injection of berberine exhibit anti-tumor effect. In addition, berberine could enhance the anti-tumor effect of 5-Fu on orthotropic growth of HCC. The objective 2 has been achieved. Both in vitro and in vivo studies have been conducted to evaluated the role of Id1 in berberine’s action. Overexpression of Id-1 in HCC cell lines was established, and use this cell line we have observed that the anti-tumor effect of berberine in vitro and in vivo could be attenuated by restoration of Id1 expression. This conclusion could be strengthened by the evidenced by in Id1-overexpressing HCC cells, inhibition of VEGF and Cyclin D1 expression could hardly be found. qPCR and ELISA assay have been conducted to measured the expression of VEGF in vitro and in vivo, and immunoblotting assay was performed to probe Cyclin D1. Histological analysis on the liver section (including tumor) supports our conclusion. The objective 3 has been achieved in line with our hypothesis. We have conducted EMSA assay to see if the transcriptional activity of STAT3 was blocked by berberine. And we have assessed that Id1 promoter binding with STAT3 was blocked by berberine treatment. We also examined that NF-κB binding activity was blocked by berberine with EMSA assay. And using the Id1-overexpressing HCC cells, we found that the NF-κB binding activity could be restored in berberine-treated HCC cells. All the proposed experiments have been conducted and research questions have been elaborated.

766211.label: Major findings and research outcome
766211.value: 6.1.1 The anti-tumor effect of berberine has been systematically evaluated in pre-clinical model of HCC implanted mice. Berberine was found to be a potent inhibitor of liver tumor, and both intraperitoneal injection and oral administration of berberine could significantly suppress tumor growth. In addition, co-treatment of berberine with common chemotherapeutics, 5-Fu, could potently enhance tumor inhibition. Please refer to Part C conference papers entitled “Berberine: an old drug but new use for liver diseases” and “Differential inhibitory effect of berberine on human hepatocellular carcinoma”. 6.1.2 We observed that Id1 is a key regulatory that get involved in the anti-tumor effect of berberine on liver cancer. Tumor inhibition by berberine could be attenuated by restoration of Id1. This part of study has been concluded and manuscript is under preparation. In addition, we found that inhibition of VEGF expression by berberine relies on multiple layers of regulation. Besides the action of Id1, berberine could also block the translation elongation and nascent synthesis of VEGF protein. Please refer to Part C publication on peer reviewed journal entitled “Suppression of Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor via Inactivation of Eukaryotic Elongation Factor 2 by Alkaloids in Coptidis rhizoma in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.” 6.1.3 We observed that berberine exhibits multiple mechanisms in inhibiting liver cancer. Besides Id1, berberine could target on microRNAs to inhibit liver tumor growth. We identified miR-23a as a potential target of berberine in liver cancer, and miR-23a may regulate the chemosensitivity of liver cancer cells. Please refer to Part C publication on peer review journal entitled “MiR-23a-mediated inhibition of topoisomerase 1 expression potentiates cell response to etoposide in human hepatocellular carcinoma”. 6.1.4 We found that the inflammation-related pathway may have correlation with berberine’s anti-tumor effect. STAT3 activation by pro-inflammatory cytokine IL6 could be blocked by berberine, and inhibition of STAT3 could suppress tumor growth. This indicated that berberine may be able to block the communication between surrounding tissue and tumor. Please refer to Part C publication on peer reviewed journal entitled “Berberine suppresses tumorigenicity and growth of nasopharyngeal carcinoma cells by inhibiting STAT3 activation induced by tumor associated fibroblasts.” 6.1.5 With the experiment platform established in this grant, we examined the pharmacological effect of other natural compounds on liver cancer. Please refer to Part C publication on peer review journal entitled “Up-regulation of TIMP-1 by genipin inhibits MMP-2 activities and suppresses the metastatic potential of human hepatocellular carcinoma” and “A novel mechanism of XIAP degradation induced by timosaponin AIII in hepatocellular carcinoma.”

766211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
766211.value: This study has revealed the anti-tumor potential of berberine and provided a fundamental evidence of tumor inhibitory effect with multiple mechanisms may be involved. It was noticed that berberine is a potent inhibitor of inflammation, and the last part of this study has revealed that berberine may be able to block communication between tumor and its surrounding tissues. Inflammation is the case that gets involved in cancer progression, so the potential of berberine in regulating tumor microenvironment could be further direction. It may be possible that berberine could regulate the infiltration, differentiation and cytokine secretion of tumor-associated macrophages, either by direct action on macrophage or by regulating chemoaxis factors secreted by tumor cells. Further study may focus on exploring the mechanism underlying IL6-mediated communication between microenvironment and tumor cells in the presence of berberine.

766211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
766211.value: Coptis, Huanglian in Chinese, is a commonly used Chinese herbal Medicine in Chinese Medicine prescriptions, and berberine is the major and active component in coptis. Berberine has been used as over-the-counter medication to treat gastrointestinal disorder in some countries. Here in our study, we systematically evaluate the anti-tumor potential of berberine on liver cancer. A pre-clinical model that well bioimitated human liver cancer, the orthotropic HCC implantation mice model, was established, and we observe that berberine treatment, via either oral administration or intraperitoneal injection, could remarkably inhibit the orthotropic growth of liver tumor. This effect of berberine is dose-dependent and related to inhibition of tumor cell proliferation and tumorial angiogenesis. In addition, we found that combination use of berberine with common chemotherapeutics could enhance the therapeutic outcome. The oncogene Id1 plays a central role in regulating berberine’s anti-tumor actions, and inhibition of Id1 by berberine results in reduced tumor expansion. Our study provides comprehensive pre-clinical evidence of anti-tumor effect of berberine on liver cancer, and sheds lights on the potential of berberine as a novel chemopreventive medicine. The data in our study could be translatable in future clinical trials and drug development.

766511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
766511.value: Parent-of-origin effects, also known as ‘genomic imprinting’, is an important epigenetic factor. More and more genes are found to show parent-of-origin effects. It is believed that more than 1% of all mammalian genes are imprinted. Imprinting effects have been demonstrated in some complex diseases such as Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome, Prader-Willi Syndrome and Angelman Syndrome. Statistical tests for imprinting have been proposed in the literature. However, to our knowledge, all these tests are applied to imprinting in autosomal chromosome and none of them can be used for testing for imprinting in X-chromosome. In this project, we are going to fill this gap and propose statistical tests for imprinted genes in X-chromosome. Another aim of this project is to construct statistical tests for association under imprinting for quantitative traits in autosomal chromosome. The existing transmission disequilibrium test for quantitative traits (QTDT) does not take imprinting effects into account. We will propose statistical tests that take such effects into consideration. Our aim is to establish a theoretical and empirical foundation for using QTDT-like statistics to test for association under imprinting. Finally, we will apply the proposed methods to analyse real data on X-linked imprinting on cognitive status of patients with Turner’s Syndrome, and on Framingham Heart Study utilizing blood pressure traits having significant imprinting effects. 親源效應（亦稱作遺傳印記）是一種重要的外遺傳因數。越來越多的基因被發現具有遺傳印記效應。在哺乳動物中，超過1%的基因是具有遺傳印記效應的。目前，已經發現Beckwith-Wiedemann 綜合症、Prader-Willi 綜合症、Angelman 綜合症等複雜疾病與印記基因相關。一些文獻中也提出了遺傳印記的檢測方法，但這些方法只適用於常染色體，並不適用於X性染色體。因此，本項目將填補這項空白，並提出一種X性染色體上印記基因的檢測方法。另一方面，通常的常染色體上數量性狀傳遞不平衡檢驗Q-TDT並沒有將遺傳印記效應的資訊合併到關聯分析中來。為了充分利用所得到的資訊以提高檢驗效能，本項目將構造出一種常染色體上基於印記效應的數量性狀關聯分析方法。最後，本項目打算將兩種檢測方法分別運用於 Turner 綜合症與 Framingham 心血管疾病資料，以對這兩種方法進行實例驗證。

766511.label: Realisation of objectives
766511.value: Genomic imprinting, also known as “parent-of-origin” effects, is an important epigenetic factor which can lead to complete or partial deactivation of the maternally or paternally inherited copy of a gene. In this project, we aim to construct statistical tests for parent-of-origin effects for qualitative traits on the X chromosome and for association under imprinting on autosomal chromosomes. For objective 1, we have completely achieved it. We have successfully constructed tests for parent-of-origin effects on the X chromosome for complete as well as incomplete families, families with single affected daughter and families with multiple affected daughters. Notice that tests for parent-of-origin effects on autosomes have been constructed for more than 15 years, yet no tests have been proposed for the X chromosome. We should be the first group of researchers who have successfully tackled this problem. For objective 2, we have also fully achieved it, see Paper 2 (Part C). Empirical investigation demonstrates that our methods outperform existing statistical tests in the detection of association for quantitative traits in the presence of parent-of-origin effects. The proposed tests can still have a good performance even when Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium is violated. For objective 3, we have applied to analyse real data of the Framingham Heart Study which have shown to have significant parent-of-origin effects. However, the data set of Turner’s Syndrome on X-linked imprinting were difficult to be obtained. Although we had contacted the authors for data, unfortunately we could only obtain the summary statistics but not the full data set. Our methods cannot be applied based on the summary statistics, and so we cannot analyse the Turner’s Syndrome data. Instead, we applied our methods to analyse the rheumatoid arthritis data set of the North American Rheumatoid Arthritis Consortium. The data set was found to have imprinting effects. In general, the project was conducted smoothly.

766511.label: Major findings and research outcome
766511.value: In this project, we have written three papers (see Part C). The first two have appeared, while the third one has been submitted for publication. The major findings and research outcome are given as follows: The parental-asymmetry test based on nuclear families with both parents and its extension to deal with missing parental genotypes are simple but powerful methods to test for parent-of-origin effects. However, these methods only use case (affected) children in nuclear families and thus do not make full use of information on control (unaffected) children, if available, in these families. In paper 1, we proposed a novel parent-of-origin effects test by using both the control and case children in nuclear families with one or both parents. Simulation studies demonstrated that our test outperformed existing tests having only affected children. Paper 2 is on test for association on quantitative trait loci incorporating parent-of-origin effects. Existing methods need the assumption of Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium or only use information from families with one child. In paper 2, we proposed testing methods which did not require the assumption of Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium and could apply to families with multiple affected children. The validity of the methods were investigated thoroughly by simulations. The proposed powerful methods were applied to analyse the Framingham Heart Study data. Methods for detecting parent-of-origin effects have been developed primarily for autosomal markers. However, no method is available in the literature to test for parent-of-origin effects on the X chromosome. In paper 3, the parental-asymmetry test on the X chromosome was first developed to test for parent-of-origin effects for qualitative traits, based on family trios each with both parents and their daughters. Then, we proposed 1-XPAT to deal with parent-daughter pairs. Finally, C-XPAT was constructed to handle both family trios and parent-daughter pairs. Simulation results demonstrated that the methods performed well in controlling the size and in power investigation.

766511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
766511.value: In this project, we have constructed various tests for parent-of-origin effects and for association incorporating imprinting. The proposed tests are non-parametric orientated. In future research, we shall work on the more powerful parametric methods. Moreover, we shall extend our imprinting tests on the X chromosome from qualitative traits to quantitative traits. Moreover, we are working on the extension of our methods to deal with the general pedigree data.

766511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
766511.value: Genomic imprinting, also known as “parent-of-origin” effects, is an important genetic factor in the study of genetic traits. More than 1% of mammalian genes are believed to show parent-of-origin effects. In this project, we have constructed various statistical tests for detecting parent-of-origin effects in human genes. Empirical studies show that our methods can outperform some other existing approaches. Although imprinting tests on autosomes have been developed for more than 15 years, no statistical test for imprinting effects on the X chromosome is available in the literature. In this project we proposed the parental-asymmetry tests on X chromosome to test for such imprinting effects. The methods performed well in simulations and in real data analysis.

766611.value: 在所研究的疾病分離系譜保留完整的情況下，連鎖分析不失是一個研究孟德爾遺傳疾病的好辦法。然而，對少量的個體或家系的罕見疾病，連鎖分析僅能發掘出少於50%的能引起疾病的基因異常變化，因為大多數的罕見疾病是由於影響蛋白功能的罕見基因突變引起的。一個可以備選的識別罕見基因突變的方法是外顯子組測序（全基因組外顯子區域測序）只需要少量的疾病個體就可能對散發的或家系病例中進行致病基因的發掘和識別。最近對來孟德爾紊亂疾病包括弗-謝二氏綜合征，米勒綜合征，非綜合性聽力缺失和歌舞伎綜合征的自不同家系的受累病人進行基因組外顯子測序發現其能夠發掘和識別潛在的致病基因。 尾部退化綜合症是一種罕見的先天性的疾病，表現為尾部脊椎不同程度的發育不全。 尾部退化綜合症常伴有其他畸形，其中肛門直腸畸形最為常見。它的一個亞型是Currarino 綜合征，常伴有尾部脊椎部分發育不良，如第一骶椎不全（‘鐮刀形骶椎’=半骶椎），肛門直腸畸形和骶前腫塊。家系尾部退化綜合症伴常染色體顯性遺傳，到目前為止，除了其亞型Currarino綜合徵發現是基因MNX1=HLXB9突變引起並有遺傳異質性，在家系病例和散發病例中分別占80%和50%。其它類型沒有發現致病基因。我們現在有一些來自家系的顯性遺傳的尾部退化綜合症或Currarino 綜合征病人標本和散發的尾部退化綜合症或Currarino綜合征病人標本。 重要的是， 一些尾部退化綜合症病人的臨床特性或表型和一些 Currarino 綜合征病人的臨床特性或表型相似。 因此，我們計畫對這組病人進行全基因組外顯子測序來發掘和識別潛在的Currarino綜合征和或尾部退化綜合症其它亞型的致病或相關基因。用於外顯子測序的標本共37例包括3個家系（9個受累病人，7個非受累個體）和8個散發病人和他們非受累父母。所有的個體都是正常的染色體組型，沒有發現基因HLXB9=MNX1突變和其母親均無糖尿病病史。本課題對遺傳諮詢，產前診斷和對病人的治療有重大益處。基於發現的基因突變和致病基因有利於尾部退化綜合症的臨床診斷和描述

766611.label: Realisation of objectives
766611.value: I believe the project objectives have almost been achieved. For the exome sequencing of the familial cases was difficult to pinpoint the causative mutation in the genes. The difficulty may be due to: A: No coverage of all the genes of the genome B: Low depth coverage C: Mutation could be in non-exonic regions. To overcome this, we combined exome sequencing with copy number variation analysis. This has revealed several linkage peaks currently being investigated. A couple of publications are also being prepared (see Section C; uploaded document). Details on the screening of trios can also be found in section C. In brief, the genes most likely to cause disease are related with susceptibility to diabetes. Importantly, this is in line with the higher rate of CRS babies born to diabetic mothers.

766611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
766611.value: We have investigated the genome of a group of patients affected with Caudal Regression Syndrome (CRS). CRS is a rare and severe congenital disorder attributed to abnormal fetal development. Affected babies have spinal cord problems together with other anomalies being anorectal malformations (ARMs) the most common. The cause is not known but it is attributed to mutations in the genome. We have screened a group of patients for mutations in their genome and found some relevant genes. However, more research is to be done for our results to be conclusive. Our data will eventually bring benefits in counselling, prenatal diagnosis and care of the patients. Diagnosis and delineation of the CRS clinical features will be immensely improved as those could be based on the mutation/s and gene/s identified.

766811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
766811.value: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is one of the most common cancers worldwide. Deletion of the short arm of chromosome 3 (3p) is one of the most frequent chromosomal alterations in ESCC. Using a recently developed high-throughput SNP-Mass-Spec-Genotyping, loss of heterozygosity (LOH) at 3p in 100 primary ESCC cases has been studied and four commonly deleted regions have been identified including a locus at 3p26.3. One candidate tumor suppressor gene (TSG), named cell adhesion molecule with homology to L1 (CHL1), was further investigated. Our preliminary data strongly suggest that CHL1 is the target TSG within the 3p26.3 for the following reasons: 1) LOH of CHL1 locus is deleted in more than 50% of primary ESCCs; 2) down-regulation of CHL1 has been detected in 32/60 (53.3%) of ESCCs and 6/8 ESCC cell lines; 3) the inactivation of CHL1 in ESCC cell line KYSE30 and KYSE510 is caused by the loss of one allele and methylation for the remaining allele, suggesting that both DNA-copy-loss and hypermethylation contribute to the CHL1 inactivation in ESCC; and 4) CHL1 has been found to cooperate with Npn1 as a co-receptor for Sema3B, which has been characterized as tumor suppressor by inhibiting the phosphorylation of Akt and Erk-1/2 and subsequently suppress the tumor. Therefore, we hypothesize CHL1 is a novel TSG and its inactivation plays important roles in the development and progression of ESCC. In order to elucidate the tumor suppressing function of CHL1, we propose to do following studies: 1) to further characterize the mechanisms (such as deletion, methylation and mutation) of CHL1 inactivation in ESCC; 2) to investigate the tumor suppressing function of CHL1: including its role in ESCC development and progression, as well as its tumor suppressive mechanism; and 3) to study the association between the down-regulation of CHL1 and clinicopathological features (e.g. age, clinical stage, metastasis, overall and disease-free survivals) of ESCC using tissue microarray. A better understanding of the physiological and pathophysiological roles of CHL1 will significantly improve our knowledge in ESCC pathogenesis, and may lead to a much more effective management of ESCC with down-regulation of the CHL1. 766811.label: Realisation of objectives
766811.value: Down-regulation of CHL1 has been frequently detected in ESCC. For the first objective, the mechanism of the inactivation of CHL1 in ESCC was investigated by methylation specific PCR and loss of heterozygocity (LOH). The results indicated that CHL1 down-regulation was closely related with both promoter methylation and allele loss. Direct sequencing analysis was applied to screen mutation status of CHL1 in 10 primary ESCC tissues and no mutation was detected. For the second objective, tumor suppressing function of CHL1 was investigated by both in vitro and in vivo assays including cell growth assay, foci formation assay, soft agar assay, and tumor formation in nude mouse. The results demonstrated that CHL1 had a strong tumor suppressive function as supported by following evidences: 1) CHL1 transfected cells were able to form less colonies in soft agar; 2) CHL1 transfected cells were able to decrease cell growth rate; and 3) CHL1 transfected cells were able to inhibit tumor formation in nude mouse. The inhibit effect of CHL1 on tumor invasion and metastasis was also revealed in this study. The results indicated that CHL1 could effectively inhibit cell migration and invasion. Further study found that CHL1 could interact with Npn1 and subsequently inhibit Erk-1/2 phosphorylation. For the third objective, tissue microarray was used to study the clinical significance of CHL1 down-regulation. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) staining with anti-CHL1 antibody showed that CHL1 down-regulation was significantly associated with ESCC clinical stage, metastasis and poor prognosis.

766811.value: Down-regulation of CHL1 is frequently detected in human ESCC, which is correlated with tumor metastasis and poor outcome of ESCC. 766911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
766911.value: TRPM2是瞬时受体电位（TRP）通道的M-家族成员, 在家族的第一个成员，抑癌的melastatin（现在称TRPM1）之后命名。它已被证明参与调节许多生理过程，如胰岛素的分泌，温度感应，以及激活趋化肽，如氧化爆发和中性粒细胞趋化。在这项研究中，我们提出将澄清环化ADP-核糖（cADPR），一个普识的钙离子信使分子，以及其水解产物ADP-核糖（ADPR）调控TRPM2通道的机制。环化ADP-核糖是产生于NAD的一种新型的环核苷酸。过去十年中的研究成果证明它是一个跨越三个生物王国细胞体系的普识的钙离子存储迁移信使。 cADPR调节的功能也同样多种多样，从调解植物对脱落酸信号的应激反应到通过调制oxyntocin分泌影响小鼠的社会行为。令人惊讶的是，持续的结果表明，cADPR不仅可以导致细胞内的钙离子存储迁移，而且还可以激活几种类型细胞的钙离子内流。这种双重性和越来越多的证据表明，内流是通过TRPM2通道协同cADPR和ADPR激活的。这项研究的具体目标是：（1）表征TRPM2配体结合域（NUDT9-H）的酶的活性;（2）确定NUDT9-H的晶体结构;（3）研究TRPM2的结构/功能。解决这些具体目标将大大增强我们有关TRPM2通道的生物学功能的理解，并将对细胞信号传导有深远影响。

766911.label: Realisation of objectives
766911.value: Objective 1. To characterize the enzymatic activity of the ligand binding domain of TRPM2 (NUDT9-H). We have shown that TRPM2 possesses NADase activity, which has not been reported before. However, the NADase activity is very low, as compared to the published ADPRase activity. Therefore, this part of work has not been submitted for publication. We must prove that the TRPM2 preparations are free of defective proteins with minor or artifactually altered enzymatic properties. In collaboration with Dr Jianbo Yue (CityU), we demonstrated that oxidative stress triggered TRPM2-dependent Ca2+ influx to inhibit the induction of early autophagy, which renders cells more susceptible to death.On the other hand, oxidative stress induced autophagy (and not cell death) in the absence of the TRPM2-mediated Ca2+ influx. The manuscript reporting this work is under minor revision at the journal Autophagy. Objective 2. To determine the crystal structure of NUDT9-H. We have systematically screened for crystallization conditions for NUDT9-H domain. For the 6xHis construct of human TRPM2 NUDT9-H domain, we have performed ~ 700 screens each for the enzymatic domain on its own and in combination with NAD+, AMP, ribose-5-phosphate, ADPR respectively. We have obtained crystals and the preliminary x-ray diffraction indicated that these are protein crystals. However, these crystals did not yield diffraction patterns with sufficient quality for structure determination. The crystallization conditions are currently being optimized to produce bigger, better, diffraction quality crystals. As a backup plan, we have studied the crystal structure of another NADase, CD38. We determined the complex structure of CD38 with a nanobody using a novel crystallographic phasing method (Acta Cryst. D, 2015). We also determined the X-ray crystallographic structures of porcine CD38 and were able to observe conformational flexibility at the base of the active site of the enzyme which allow the NAD+ reaction intermediate to adopt conformations resulting in both hydrolysis and cyclization forming linear ADPR and cADPR respectively (Protein Science, 2015). Crystallographic analysis of the CD38:8-amino-N9-butyl-cIDPR complex unexpectedly revealed an N1-hydrolyzed ligand in the active site, suggesting that it is the N6-imino form of cADPR that is hydrolyzed by CD38 (J. Med. Chem., 2014).

766911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
766911.value: The human TRPM2 NUDT9-H domain contains 10 cysteines which may form intra-molecular disulfide bonds. The fact that we could get a large amount of NUDT9-H protein but not crystals suggests that the protein might not have folded properly during the E. coli. expression. We plan to use an insect cell expression system to produce recombinant protein and then perform enzymatic measurements and crystallization screening.

766911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
766911.value: TRPM2 is a member of the transient receptor potential (TRP) channels. It has been shown to be involved in regulating many physiological processes, such as insulin secretion, temperature sensing, as well as critically contributing to the activating effects of chemoattractant peptides, such as the oxidative burst and chemotaxis in neutrophils. In this study, we revealed the role of TRPM2-mediated Ca2+ influx in the oxidative stress-mediated autophagy regulation. We studied the structural biology of a related enzyme, CD38. We used a novel crystallographic method to determine the complex structure of human CD38 with a simplified antibody (nanobody). We also determined the crystal structure of porcine CD38 and revealed a new enzymatic mechanism.

767511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
767511.value: 脊髓型頸椎病是一種退變性脊柱病變，可造成脊髓壓迫和損傷。這是老年人的常見病，隨著香港老齡化的加速，其發病率和手術量在近年來急劇增加。手術治療見效快、效果好，但需要非常準確的病灶診斷。因為脊髓型頸椎病大多受到多節脊髓節段壓迫，確定臨床症狀病灶是非常重要的。目前所使用的診斷方法主要是影像學方法，但不能提供脊髓神經功能的準確診斷。 在脊髓皮層測量的誘發電位可以提供相關的節段測量，但這種有創測量只能在手術中實施，並不能提供術前診斷和術後評估。我們的前期研究已經證明體感誘發電位包含豐富的時頻譜成份，可能提供脊髓生理功能的許多有用資訊。本項研究將進一步研究體感誘發電位時頻譜成份及其組合與脊髓不同位置的功能狀態之間的相關性，從而可能提供脊髓不同位置的功能與病患資訊。我們建議使用高解析度時頻譜分析技術來研究體感誘發電位時頻譜成份細節，並用模式識別分析建立不同成分與脊髓型頸椎病節段病變的相關性。這一研究不僅可以提供脊髓型頸椎病的準確診斷，為脊髓型頸椎病的神經生理檢測具有長遠與重要的價值，而且為研究脊髓型頸椎病的病生理機制提供有益的工具。

767511.label: Realisation of objectives
767511.value: In this project, we have developed a novel method to increase signal to noise ratio and extract single trial somatosensory evoked potentials (SEP). After fast extraction of SEP, a high-resolution time-frequency analysis (TFA) method using a matching pursuit (MP) decomposition algorithm will be used to reveal a number of detailed time-frequency components of SEP and provide a multivariate time-frequency feature set for subsequent pattern recognition. The developed technology has well achieved the first objective to extract various components in SEP signals from animal models. We applied this new technology in clinical application. Furthermore, we developed a more effective method based on expectation maximization approach for single trial SEP measurement in human. The 2nd objective is to identify and localize each component to the injuries in different cervical spinal cord level. To achieve this objective, we firstly established and validated of cervical spinal cord injury model. Then, we investigated the time frequency components of SEP in well established animal models with either acute or chronic spinal cord injury. Our results proved that changes in the time–frequency pattern of SEPs are correlated with the location of neurological deficits in both acute and chronic injury. It provides substantial evidence that the time-frequency patterns of SEPs can be developed for location detection of spinal cord injury. To achieve the 3rd objective, we have developed an effective classification method to classify time frequency patterns of SEP in distinct injury to the cervical spinal cord. A classification system was built according to the distributional distinction of these time-frequency components (TFC) among different levels using a support vector machine (SVM). In the multivariate pattern classification, all the components of SEP in the time-frequency domain were compared in three categories: high-energy, middle-energy, and low-energy TFCs. High-energy TFCs correspond to the main component (main peak) which has been proved to be useful in reflecting whether there is an injury to the spinal cord. Middle-energy and low-energy TFCs, i.e. the small components mentioned above, were found to be useful in locating the site of injury in the spinal cord. Using these two kinds of TFCs, a multi-level classifier was established to distinguish the injury to different location of cervical spinal cord.

767511.label: Major findings and research outcome
767511.value: One of major research outcomes is new signal processing technology for single trial somatosensory evoked potentials (SEP) extraction. We developed a one-unit second-order blind identification with reference (SOBI-R) algorithm for short transient signal extraction[J1,C4]. The proposed algorithm was applied to single trial extraction of SEP in rats [J3]. The experimental results demonstrated its effectiveness of SOBI-R on SEP extraction. Compared with one-unit the independent component analysis with reference (ICA-R), the proposed SOBI-R algorithm shows high robustness under conditions with low signal-to-noise ratios and less sensitivity to the reference signal. In addition, the high-resolution time-frequency decomposition algorithm has been developed [J5.J6, C1, C3, C6, C7]. The developed method has been partially applied in clinical application [J4, C5, C6]. Another major research outcome is the establishment and validation of Experimental Platform for chronic spinal cord injury [J2,C2,C6]. A basis of this study is to establish the single level cervical spinal cord injury model and to validate its chronic pathology progression. We further developed the water-absorbing material by encasing in a sustained-release membrane to control the expanding rate and speed, as well as longer-term maintenance of a consistent pressure, to produce a gradual expansion to maximum volume in 24 hours [J2]. The major finding of this study is that the identification of each component to the injuries in different cervical spinal cord levels [J5, J6, J8, C6, C8]. Time–frequency patterns of SEP are found to be different between the injury groups and the normal group[J5, C6]. The time–frequency patterns of SEPs are consistently associated with the location of the SCI. Each injury level in the cervical cord has a specific distribution pattern that can be distinguished from that of the normal cord [J5, C6]. This finding was further confirmed with chronic compressive spinal cord injury [J6, C8]. It will be performed on features of the stable time-frequency components extracted pre-injury and during different injury models will be learned from different sub-groups to establish representative patterns for normal and myelopathy models [J8, C8]. In this study, a robust clustering of time-frequency components leave out spurious components and identify stable components from different injury models [J8]. This finding explored the knowledge of components in SEP, which extend the clinical applications of a non-invasive technique for investigating the afferent somatosensory pathways. The classification system proposed in this study will contribute to a more precise diagnosis of myelopathy level before and after surgery[J8, C8].

767511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
767511.value: The outcomes of this study can help us further develop a new technology to precisely detect the location of myelopathic cord in patients with cervical myelopathy. Cervical myelopathy is the most common spinal cord disorder affecting the elderly. Surgical decompression is considered as the mainstay of treatment for cervical myelopathy patients to relieve their symptoms and signs, but it requires the accurate diagnosis of the location (spinal level) of the myelopathy. As degeneration commonly affects multiple levels of the spine, accurate localization of the responsible level is very important. We will verify the developed method with somatosensory evoked potentials recorded from patients with single level cervical stenosis. Then, we are planning to conduct a clinical trial to prove the application of time-frequency analysis techniques of somatosensory evoked potentials as a non-invasive level diagnosis of cervical myelopathy. It will provide useful and more accurate diagnosis of cervical myelopathy for surgeons to select the most appropriate treatment for patients, and greatly reduce the extra risk. In addition, developed techniques of fast somatosensory evoked potentials extraction technique can also be used for fast detection of intraoperative spinal cord injury during spine surgery and early diagnosis and precise evaluation of cervical myelopathy.

767511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
767511.value: Somatosensory evoked potentials (SEP) are a useful, noninvasive means of assessing somatosensory systemfunctioning, which is used to detect and monitor the integration of spinal cord function. By convention, SEPs are evaluated in terms of measured amplitude (voltage), latency (time), and morphology (shape). The present study is the first time to investigate the time-frequency features in SEP and its physiological mechanism. Results from the present study explored a potential means for localizing lesions within the somatosensory pathways using time-frequency distribution patterns of these small components. Features in time-frequency components of SEP include location message of cervical spinal cord injury. A SEP-based classifier was designed to identify the level-specific injury to the cervical spinal cord. This finding broadens the knowledge about the physiological mechanism of SEP and extends the clinical applications of non-invasive diagnosis of myelopathy level. Outcomes of this project are new techniques and findings with potential use in non-invasive level diagnosis of cervical myelopathy. The relevance, significance and value of this study are that it will provide useful and more accurate diagnosis of cervical myelopathy surgeons to select the most appropriate treatment for patients, and greatly reduce the extra risk.

We will measure the time-dependent Nanog-GFP histograms from non-equilibrated cell populations. We will formalize hypotheses into specific forms of mathematical models and perform hypothesis testing using the experimental data. The best model and the parameters will be used to compute the rates of transition and proliferation. To directly measure the rates of state transition and proliferation using microfluidics and live-cell microscopy. We will design a microfluidic chip to isolate and culture thousands of single ES cells and track them with live-cell fluorescence microscopy. From these experiments we will directly compute the rates of transition and proliferation and compare the results with the model predictions. To validate the quantitative results by comparing experiments with predictions. We will first validate if the model assumptions that cell population grow exponentially and the reverse transition is history-independent. We will also verify if Nanog expression level alone characterizes the process within experimental uncertainty. We will then test if the probability of ES cell colony formations from FACS sorted low-Nanog cells is consistent with model predictions.

767711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
767711.value: We aim to study fate control of mouse embryonic stem (ES) cell in single cell and cell population using a combined experimental and computational approach, focusing on how the gene circuit, stochastic gene expression (noise) and cell proliferation affecting ES cell self-renewal, differentiation and dedifferentiation. ES cell fate control is associated with core genetic circuits, including transcriptional factors Nanog, Oct4 and Sox2. Their auto-activations and cross-activations result in experimental observed heterogeneity in a cell population. Cells expressing Nanog gene at high levels (high-Nanog) and low levels (low-Nanog) have different differentiation potential, indicating that heterogeneous gene expressions may control cell fate. Using a mouse ES cell line expressing green fluorescent protein (GFP) controlled by a Nanog promoter, we have identified that low-Nanog cells differentiated by retinoic acid spontaneously reverts back to undifferentiated high-Nanog cells. This transition is reversible. It plays a role for a cell population to balance self-renewal and differentiation and may be due to Nanog gene regulation and noise. Nanog promotes cell proliferation and could tip the balance by amplifying the transitions to high-Nanog cells. Uncontrolled transitions may promote growth of undifferentiated cells and induce cancer. Therefore it is crucial to quantify the transition and proliferation rates. However, the entanglement of reversible transitions and cell proliferation prevents quantifications from flow cytometry or clonal analyses of heterogeneous Nanog expressions. Regular live-cell microscopy cannot track enough cells. We construct a stochastic mathematical model of state transitions, proliferation, and changes in Nanog distributions. It will be determined and validated by biological experiments. The transition and proliferation rates will be computed from the model. The specific aims are: (1) to quantify the rates of transition between low-Nanog and high-Nanog states and Nanog-dependent cell proliferation using mathematical model; (2) to directly measure the rates of state transition and proliferation using microfluidics in addition to live-cell microscopy; (3) to validate the quantitative results by comparing biological experiments with model predictions. This study will advance our understanding of ES cell self-renewal, differentiation and dedifferentiation. It is the first to disentangle cellular and molecular mechanisms of state transitions from state-dependent cell proliferation. The same entanglement may be important in adult stem cell, cell reprogramming and cancer researches. With better characterization of cellular states, state transitions and proliferations in a cell population, our method could improve the screening for pharmacological and genetic factors, and design better therapeutic treatments to control cell reprogramming, cell differentiation or eliminate tumor-initiating cells. 我们的目的是用实验和计算生物学的组合研究单细胞和细胞群体中小鼠胚胎干细胞命运的控制。这个研究将集中于基因回路，随机基因表达（噪声）以及细胞增殖对胚胎干细胞自增殖，分化及逆分化的影响。 胚胎干细胞命运的控制是与包括Nanog，Oct4和Sox2的核心基因回路相关的。这些转录因子之间的自激发及互激发导致了实验观察到的细胞群体中的非均质性。表达不同水平Nanog的细胞有不同的分化能力，这显示了基因表达非均质性可能也会决定细胞的命运。我们在小鼠胚胎干细胞中将Nanog启动子和绿色荧光蛋白连接起来从而可以通过绿色荧光强度来表示Nanog基因表达。我们用这个细胞系发现，当它被retinoic acid 诱导后，分化了的低Nanog的细胞可以回归了高Nanog的未分化的细胞。这个过程是可逆的，且在胚胎干细胞群体平衡自增殖和分化中起到重要的作用。它可能是通过Nanog的基因调控及噪声决定的。Nanog激发细胞增殖，通过放大从低Nanog态到高Nanog态的转变来调节细胞群体的平衡。缺乏控制的细胞态的转变可能通过未分化的细胞的过度增殖而导致癌症。所以定量刻画细胞态转变率及增殖率至关重要。然而，可逆转变跟细胞增殖的纠缠阻止了用流式细胞仪及细胞纯系分析定量的可能性。常规的活细胞显微技术有不能跟踪足够的细胞个数。 我们构建了一个关于细胞态转变，增殖及Nanog分布动力学的随机数学模型，它将由生物实验来验证。这个模型可以用来计算出细胞态转变及增殖率。这个研究的三个目标是：（1）用数学模型量化低Nanog和高Nanog态之间的转变率，及增殖率与Nanog的关系； （2）直接用微流体技术及活细胞显微技术测量细胞态之间的转变率和不同细胞态的增殖率；（3）通过比较生物实验和模型预言来校验定量结果。 这个研究将会推进我们对胚胎干细胞自增殖，分化及逆分化。这将是第一个解开胚胎干细胞增殖和细胞态转变之间的纠缠的细胞核分子机制的研究。类似的纠缠可能出现在成体干细胞，细胞重编码及癌症研究中。我们的方法可以改进对细胞态，态转变及细胞增殖的刻画，从而对控制细胞重编码和消除肿瘤干细胞的治疗中改进药物和基因的筛选。

767711.label: Realisation of objectives
767711.value: For Aim 1, we have successfully generated time-dependent Nanog-GFP distribution dynamic data during the dedifferentiation process from primitive endoderm to ES cell using flow cytometry and carefully developed methods for fluorescent signal and cell proliferation quantifications. Measurement variances, critical for statistic analysis, were vigorously determined. We established a Bayesian statistic inference method for comparing competing models with experimentally determined data. The parameter determinations were carried out with computational intensive Markov Chain Monte Carlo method. We specifically implemented the parallel tempering method to improve the speed and effectiveness of the computational methods. We then identified the most likely model to characterize the dedifferentiation process. From the model and the parameters, we computed the cellular transition rate between the differentiated state and the ES cell states. We also performed similar experiments to delineate the effects of the 2i factors on ES cells and the naive ground state, with the statistic analysis and data analysis currently underway. For Aim2, we have developed the technical platform for live cell imaging, genetic labeling for facilitating live cell imaging, automatic imaging processing and data analysis. We designed several PDMS-and-glass microfluidics chips, but single ES cell cannot survive in microfluidics chips. We then implemented an perfusion device on regular multi-well plate to reduce the media exchange rate but still maintain constant cell culture conditions. In order to facilitate automatic imaging processing of fluorescent imaging and identify cellular state, we implemented transposson-based multiplex gene transfer to ES cell and established cell lines with multiple nuclear-targeted fluorescent protein reporters. On the measurement side, We built our own microscope to include autofocus, computer controlled excitation, emission filter, and camera, as well as motorized XY stage, and an environment chamber. We developed a unique and robust laser-aid autofocus system to overcome the focus drift issue, with the axial (z) resolution 10 times higher than the commercial ones. We have been able to culture ES cells and continue imaging them for as long as 7 days with this setup, and successfully observed the single cell dynamics of dedifferentiation and observed ~1% of dedifferentiation and doubling time of 12-14 hours, comparable with indirect results from aim 1. For Aim3, our statistical and data analysis is based on our novel diffusion-drift-growth model which is an expansion and quantification of the Waddington landscape. We systematically validated the model hypothesis as well as the nontrivial model predictions. Our results suggest that, we captured intrinsic dynamic properties of the earlier stages of differentiation and dedifferentiation processes for ES cells. We extend this study by using an exciting new technology, optogenetics to quantitatively perturb the landscape. This ongoing study could lead to major discovery in ES cell landscape.
