773711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
773711.value: Further research to find out the optimal frequency of application of SDF solution to prevent and control dental caries in adults is needed. Clinical studies to look for alternative agents and approaches to SDF application is also warranted. There are plans to carry out more clinical studies and grant applications are submitted

773711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
773711.value: This randomized clinical trial provides high level clinical evidence to support the use of annual application of silver diamine fluoride (SDF) solution to prevent and to control tooth decay among older adults. It was also found that application of potassium iodide (KI) after SDF application will not affect its effectiveness or change the colour of arrested tooth decay lesion, and thus this procedure is not needed. Regular application of SDF solution onto tooth surfaces is a simple and effective approach to prevent and to control tooth decay. This will benefit the adults in Hong Kong and worldwide.

774011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
774011.value: 腸道神經系統（ENS）調節腸道蠕動，異常的ENS發育導致先天性巨結腸症（HSCR）。HSCR兒童因腸道缺乏神經節而導致功能性梗阻。HSCR是一個複雜的先天性遺傳疾病，有顯著的種族差異，而亞洲人的發病率最高（於10萬活產嬰兒，其中28嬰兒診斷為HSCR病兒）。 RET是主要的HSCR基因，及RET的表達對ENS的發展至關重要。其他迄今發現的HSCR基因編碼的蛋白質主要是參與開發的腸道神經節相互關聯的信號通路成員：RET，內皮素受體 B（EDNRB）和轉錄調節 SOX10信號通路。有證據表明，HSCR基因編碼的蛋白質之間的相互作用改變RET表達, 最終可能導致HSCR表型的改變。 我們以前曾報導說： 一） HOXB5轉錄因子介導RET在人和鼠ENS發育的表達; 二）有HOXB5缺陷的小鼠發展 HSCR表型。 我們的後續研究表示： 一）HOXB5和RET基因表達的關鍵監管區域結合 (promoter and intronic enhancer MSC +9.7) 並調節RET的表達; 二）HOXB5與其他轉錄因子合作調控RET的表達和; 三）HOXB5監管RET的區域的序列變異會導致RET的表達活動受損。兩者加起來，我們的數據表明，HOXB5單獨或協調與 NKX2 - 1和SOX10，對RET表達和HSCR起著至關重要的作用。 我們推測HOXB5激活RET表達的缺陷導致 RET表達減少並最終體現在HSCR的表型。因此，我們建議闡明HOXB5單獨; HOXB5與 NKX2-1和SOX10在調控 RET的表達的調節機制的相互作用。 此外，我們確定了新的RET調控區序列變異之後，我們將評估這些新的RET調控區序列變異和HSCR表型之間的關聯。 這個研究應查出HSCR基因的相互作用及其對HSCR表型的影響，並為其他遺傳性疾病提供重要的見解。

774011.label: Realisation of objectives
774011.value: Objective 1: We have identified and functionally evaluated a number of RET intron 1 sequence variants, and discovered that these variants influence the HOXB5 induction of RET gene from the RET promoter. Objectives 2: We have sequenced part of the RET intron 1 which encompasses these sequence variants in Hirschsprung's patients and normal controls. We discovered strong associations of some of these variants with the disease. Taken all these suggested that some of these RET intron 1 variants influenced the transcription induction of HOXB5 of RET gene, which could lead to sub-optimal RET expression and function and the occurrence of the Hirschsprung's disease.

774011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
774011.value: Potential for further development:- The identification, functional evaluation and sequence analysis of known and newly identified sequence variants of the RET intron 1 has generated a list of HSCR associated variants, that could be tested in details in the context of known RET promoter disease-associated sequence variants. Proposed course of action: The relevance of these RET intron 1 sequence variants in combinations with the known sequence variants of the RET promoter in the association with the Hirschsprung's disease should be studied in different ethnic groups in future to study the additive effects of these variants in the etiology of the Hirschsprung's disease. Such study of different ethnic groups is in progress in the Hirschsprung's disease consortium, which is consisted of 6 major Hirschsrung's disease research centres in the world (Our centre is the only centre in Asia).

774011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
774011.value: RET gene is crucial for the development of enteric nervous system, and dys-regulation of RET expression causes Hirschsprung Disease (HSCR). HSCR patients lack intestinal peristalsis and develop a life-threatening condition of intestinal obstruction. HOXB5 regulates RET transcription, and abnormal transcriptional regulation by HOXB5 caused reduced RET expression and defective enteric nervous system development. The mechanisms by which HOXB5 regulate RET transcription are unclear. Thus, unraveling the regulatory mechanisms of HOXB5 on RET transcription could lead to a better understanding of the etiology of Hirschsprung's Disease. In this study, we identified and confirmed HOXB5 binding to the multi-species conserved sequence (MCS+9.7) in the first intron of the RET gene. We discovered that (i) HOXB5 physically bound to MCS+9.7 and regulated the expression of RET, (ii) Expression of RET was mediated by a complex regulatory network of transcription factors functioning in a synergistic, additive and/or independent manners. Hence, dys-regulation of RET expression by HOXB5 could result in insufficient RET expression and Hirschsprung's Disease.

774211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
774211.value: 脊髓型頸椎病（頸髓病）是一種最常見的慢性脊髓壓迫疾患，可能造成慢性的非創傷麻痹或癱瘓。快速老年化正使香港面臨脊髓型頸椎病所帶來的巨大社會和經濟問題。手術減壓是目前主要的臨床治療手段，但治療效果並不總是令人滿意。研究手術減壓對頸髓病的治療機制可能為臨床治療提供準確預後效果。 以往研究採用傳統MRI（T1/T2）觀察術後頸髓病脊髓的變化，發現椎管已經擴大，T2高信號也會降低。然而，傳統MRI並不能提供微觀結構的變化，沒有髓鞘、軸突再生或神經可塑性等反映脊髓功能恢復的指標。 2008年以來，在RGC基金資助下，我們已經成功地建立了研究慢性脊髓壓迫下脊髓功能性磁共振成像研究手段。我們初步發現頸髓病BOLD信號增加，DTI顯示很多橫向神經纖維。有理由假設：(1) 頸髓病所造成的脊髓功能缺失有可能因補償機制而在術後恢復正常，(2) 軸突再生與否可能和殘留神經功能有關。 本項研究將對頸髓病人進行術前和術後6個月的功能性磁共振成像跟蹤研究，從而研究術前神經活動與術後恢復的關係。 研究成果將有助於對慢性脊髓壓迫病患的手術治療及其神經功能恢復的機制，為提高治療效果和研究新治療方案提供依據。

774211.label: Realisation of objectives
774211.value: The first objective of this study is to evaluate the neuronal activities and the axons regeneration by a longitudinally monitoring in cervical myelopathy (CM) patients using BOLD and diffusion tensor images (DTI). A total of 51 patients with CM requiring surgical decompression have been recruited for post-operative fMRI/DTI test. Clinical examination, including neurological evaluation, Japanese Orthopaedic Association (JOA) scoring assessment, and clinical electrophysiological evaluation were performed. The functional recovery was determined by recovery rate (RR) calculated with Hirabayashi method. With respect to the relationship between postoperative DTI metrics and the postoperative JOA scores, DTI variables were significantly correlated with the postoperative neurological status indicated by JOA scores. In evaluation with fMRI changes, intrinsic functional organization was investigated by resting state fMRI (rsfMRI) in cervical spinal cord. Functional connectivity (FC) was calculated to measure the alteration of intrinsic functional organization. Lower FC was found to be correlated to poor recovery. The novel spinal cord rsfMRI investigation facilitates to understand the mechanism of neurological development of CM. The second objective of this study is to correlate the preoperative neuronal activities of the myelopathic cord with axonal regeneration. Firstly, microstructural damages of chronic compressive spinal cord lesion can be precisely evaluated by DTI, which predicts clinical severity and surgical prognosis of CM. Spinal tracts were not uniformly affected in myelopathic cord. DTI analysis of spinal tracts, rather than analysis of spinal cord as a whole, could provide specific information for clinical diagnosis CM. In this study, loss of microstructural integrity was detected in lateral and posterior column. Degeneration of particular column of white matter correlated with the functional deficits. DTI exhibited potential clinical value for in-vivo evaluation of the severity of CM. Based on precise evaluation of severity of CM, diffusion magnetic resonance imaging of the myelopathic spinal cord is superior to the current clinical and radiological assessments in predicting surgical outcome. Secondly, functional neural image of cervical spinal cord would provide precise diagnosis of myelopathic level for clinical management. When combined level diagnosis result of compression ratio and DTI, it demonstrated the high accuracy and sensitivity to determine the pathological spinal cord levels in multilevel CM. This information should help spine surgeons in deciding the optimal surgical strategy.

774211.label: Major findings and research outcome
774211.value: Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) in the cervical spinal cord can provide a precise evaluation of the severity of myelopathy and accurate prognosis for surgical management of cervical myelopathy (CM) [J1,J3,J5,C1,C3]. Firstly, we introduced a reliable morphologic analysis approach for diffusion tensor fiber tractography to detect the pathological changes in CM, which provides a quantitative criteria in diagnosis of CM[J1]. Tractography-based quantification was capable of evaluating the subtle pathological insult within white matter on a column-specific basis, which is in vivo evaluation of the severity of CM[J5]. Then, we demonstrated that DTI correlates well with the clinical severity of myelopathy [J3,C1,C3]. Furthermore, the average FA of the entire myelopathic cord predicted the response to surgical intervention. DTI was superior to the current clinical electrophysiological and routine anatomic MRI assessment in terms of sensitivity and specificity in providing the prognosis of surgical outcomes[J3]. Our findings indicate the clinical utility of DTI in the diagnosis and prognostication of CM by adding value to existing clinical and radiological assessments[J3,C3]. DTI can also provide regional diagnosis of neurological deficits in CM[J2, J6,J8,J9,C2]. Spinal tracts are not uniformly affected in the myelopathic cervical cord [C2]. Changes in diffusion indices could delineate focal or extensive myelopathic lesions in CM [J2]. To make DTI applicable in clinical diagnosis, a normal database of cervical spinal cord diffusion tensor in healthy Chinese was established [J8]. DTI has been demonstrated as a useful tool to determine the pathological spinal cord levels in multilevel CM [J9]. We developed a newly designed machine learning based classifier in automatic identification of myelopathic levels [J6]. The application of newly developed method should help spine surgeons in deciding the optimal surgical strategy. Another major finding is neural plasticity in patients with CM[J4,J7, C3, C4]. One finding is hyperconnectivity in the thalamocortical system associated with earlier stage disease and mild spinal cord structural injury[J7], which are consistent with and expand upon previous reports. Another finding is that patients with CM showed decreases in metabolites and increased motor-related but decreased sensory-related activation of the sensorimotor cortex [J4]. These findings suggest a complex and diverging relationship of cortical functional reorganization and distal spinal anatomical compression in patients with CM. In the spinal cord [C3,C4], FC values of healthy subjects are significantly higher than patients with CM. However, CM patients after surgical treatment presented a significant increase of FC, demonstrating the neural network recovery during the treatment.

774211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
774211.value: This study conducted to monitor the functional and structural changes of myelopathic cord after surgical decompression in human beings. The knowledge gained from this study contributed to our understanding on the plasticity of spinal cord with a chronically compressed lesion. Results of this study established the solid scientific foundation for improving the prognosis of CM patients. We will further examine whether DTI variables can be correlated with surgical outcomes of CM. We are planning to develop a novel multivariable prediction model based on various DTI variables at different regions of interest (ROI), and to verify the prediction model by analyzing the relationship between the outcome and neurological functional recovery in post-operative CM. The relevance, significance and value of this study are to give surgeons the precise information to assess whether surgical intervention is the most appropriate treatment for CM.

774211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
774211.value: Cervical myelopathy is the most common cause of nontraumatic paraparesis/quadriparesis among the elderly. It results from a chronically compressive spinal cord lesion. Hong Kong is facing a heavy social economic burden from cervical myelopathy with the rapidly aging population. Surgical decompression is considered as the mainstay of treatment for cervical myelopathy patients to relieve their symptoms and signs. The better understanding of the exact mechanism of surgical decompression on the recovery of myelopathic cord is needed in order to improve the prognosis of cervical myelopathy patients. In this study, we found the good prognosis of surgical treatment of cervical myelopathy depends in part on the amount of residual neural status. We have developed a new technology for evaluating diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) of the cervical spinal cord. Based on the basic knowledge of neurological changes in spinal cord before and after surgery on cervical myelopathy, we can provide a precise prognosis of cervical myelopathy patients. It helps the surgeon to select the optimal therapeutic strategy to improve the prognosis of cervical myelopathy patients.

774411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
774411.value: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a deadly cancer with an especially high incidence in China. Five-year survival rates in Hong Kong are only ~14%. Changes in morphology and behavior of tumor cells leading to loss of epithelial characteristics and acquisition of the mesenchymal phenotype having a greater propensity to migrate, known as epithelial-mesenchymal-transition (EMT), hallmark a metastatic cascade of events leading to deadly metastatic tumors. We identified a gene, DNAJB6, which is expected to play an important role in ESCC metastasis. DNAJ (Hsp40) homologue subfamily B member 6 (DNAJB6) is a member of the Hsp40 family of co-chaperones. Recent DNAJB6 studies in human tumors show its loss is associated with cell invasion and metastasis in breast cancers. It plays an essential role in EMT, inhibits the Wnt/ß-catenin signaling pathway, and contributes to tumor metastasis. Our preliminary studies indicate DNAJB6 is down-regulated in ESCC. We propose to elucidate the potential role of DNAJB6 and investigate its predicted role in inhibiting cell invasion, migration, EMT, and metastasis in ESCC. We also intend to identify molecular targets and signaling pathways for DNAJB6 in ESCC. Interestingly, DNAJB6 was first identified in our ESCC studies through a yeast-two hybrid (Y2H) screen of potential interacting partners for another candidate tumor suppressor gene, Deleted in Esophageal Cancer 1 (DEC1), which we had earlier identified through a functional chromosome 9 complementation study. Our subsequent studies indicated DEC1 plays an important tumor-suppressive role in ESCC. We aim to investigate the specific interaction of DNABJ6 with DEC1 and determine how this may contribute to ESCC tumorigenesis. Preliminary studies now identified a nine amino acid sequence on DNAJB6 responsible for this interaction with DEC1. Indeed, our earlier studies show that down-regulated DEC1 expression is significantly associated with metastatic ESCC. Our preliminary evidence indicates that DNAJB6 is also a promising predictive biomarker for ESCC patient survival. The proposed studies are expected to provide mechanistic insight into the role DNAJB6 plays in ESCC development and metastasis and its possible future clinical utility as a novel promising biomarker to hallmark metastatic tumors that require clinical intervention. Tumor metastasis often leads to incurable disease. Since ESCC is such a deadly cancer, these studies are, therefore, expected to contribute to our understanding and improved control of ESCC.

774411.label: Realisation of objectives
774411.value: 1) To determine the tumor-suppressive role of DNAJB6 in ESCC tumorigenesis, we performed in vivo and in vitro functional assays with DNAJB6 over-expression or knockdown. We showed that ESCC cell lines overexpressing nuclear DNAJB6 isoform DNAJB6a, but not the cytoplasmic DNAJB6b, suppressed tumorigenicity in subcutaneous nude mouse models and cells expressing mutant DNAJB6a did not localize to the nucleus. DNAJB6 knockdown in ESCC cell lines promoted tumor growth in mice. Cells overexpressing DNAJB6a reduced proliferation and cell cycle progression in vitro, while DNAJB6 knockdown enhanced this. We performed in vivo experimental metastasis assays and showed that DNAJB6a over-expression did not affect lung metastasis formation. These results confirm DNAJB6a role as a tumor suppressor, rather than a metastasis suppressor in ESCC. To determine the mechanism for tumor suppression and anti-proliferations, we performed mutagenesis and molecular signaling profiling assays. We showed that a highly conserved DNAJ protein family motif of histidine/proline/aspartic acid (HPD) in the J domain of DNAJB6a was required for its tumor-suppressive anti-proliferative effects and signaling via the oncogenic AKT signaling pathway; mutant DNAJB6a with the HPD motif was not tumor-suppressive as compared to WT DNAJB6a. Increased DNAJB6a expression in cancer cell lines caused down-regulated AKT signaling, while loss of DNAJB6a upregulated AKT signaling in ESCC and immortalized esophageal epithelial cells. Constitutively active AKT1 expression restored overexpressing DNAJB6a tumor cell proliferation; DNAJB6a formed a complex with AKT1 in living cells. The expression level of DNAJB6a affected AKT signaling in other cancer types, including lung and liver cancers. These data suggest that AKT regulation by DNAJB6a is a general phenomenon in cancer. 2) We showed that only DNAJB6a, but not the DNAJB6b isoform is tumor-suppressive and focused on DNAJB6a in subsequent studies. To verify protein-protein interactions between DEC1/DNAJB6a in ESCC cells, we performed co-immunoprecipitation and bimolecular fluorescence complementation live-cell imaging assays using different DEC1 and DNAJB6a constructs and protein expression methods. We overcame the difficulty of stably expressing and detecting DEC1 proteins in cells with a lentiviral expression system with protein-tagging. These well-controlled assays did not show evidence to support interactions between DEC1 and DNAJB6a, as originally hypothesized due to our findings from yeast-two hybrid assays. In light of this, therefore, we concluded that it is unlikely that these two proteins physically interact with each other in ESCC cells. With this conclusion, as a consequence, no follow-up functional characterizations of this interaction could be performed.

774411.label: Major findings and research outcome
774411.value: The current study verified the tumor suppressive role of DNAJB6 in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) using both well-controlled in vivo and in vitro functional and molecular assays. Only one specific DNAJB6 isoform, DNAJB6a, was able to suppress tumor formation and induce anti-cancer effects. The DNAJB6a is localized in the nucleus, which is crucial for its tumor suppression function. In the mouse model, expression of wild type nuclear DNAJB6a with an intact HPD motif suppresses tumor growth; loss of DNAJB6a expression enhances tumor growth. In an in vitro cell culture model, wild type DNAJB6a expression, but not DNAJB6b or mislocalized DNAJB6a, leads to reduced cell cycle progression and cellular proliferation. The molecular mechanism of tumor suppression associated with DNAJB6a was also elucidated. DNAJB6a interacts with and regulates the well-known oncogenic AKT signaling. Expression of DNAJB6a suppresses the activity of AKT signaling leading to reduced cellular proliferation. Expression of constitutively active AKT1 counteracts the anti-proliferation effect and downstream molecular alterations by DNAJB6a. DNAJB6a expression enhances PP2A-dependent AKT1 dephosphorylation. DNAJB6a expression negatively modulates cellular sensitivity to Akt inhibition in ESCC. The impact of DNAJB6a expression has also been examined in other cancer types including liver and lung cancers. The results suggested that the regulation of AKT signaling by DNAJB6a is a general phenomenon. A manuscript based on this research project is now in press in the high-impact journal Gastroenterology. This project has been presented in the form of poster presentation in two renowned international cancer research conferences, American Association for Cancer Research Annual Meetings 2012 and 2014, held in the United States.

774411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
774411.value: The current results suggest a regulatory role of DNAJB6a on the important oncogenic AKT-related signaling pathway in cancer. Targeted therapy has been considered effective, in addition to traditional chemoradiotherapy. In ESCC, therapeutic potential for targeting AKT-related signaling has been proposed as an important anti-cancer approach. The DNAJB6a protein expression status may serve as a biomarker for AKT-related signaling and indicate the possible therapeutic potential in ESCC patients. Large-scale ESCC patient tissue sample analyses using methods such as immunohistochemical staining are needed to further elucidate and verify this possible utility. The current study also suggested a potential tumor suppression role of DNAJB6a in other cancer types such as esophageal adenocarcinoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, lung adenocarcinoma, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Further functional and mechanistic analyses are needed to verify the tumor suppressive effect of DNAJB6a in these other cancer types.

774411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
774411.value: We studied the tumor suppressive effect of the gene DNAJB6 in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, a form of esophageal cancer that has its highest incidence in Chinese and is common in Hong Kong and Mainland China. We found that only one specific form of the protein encoded by this gene, called DNAJB6a, possesses anti-cancer function. We performed various assays to analyze in detail how DNAJB6a suppresses tumor formation to exert this anti-cancer effect. We found that DNAJB6a regulates the activity of important cancer-promoting molecular players inside cancer cells and this regulation is generally applicable in other cancer types such as liver and lung cancers. These finding increase our understanding of how esophageal cancer progresses and allows future development of biomarker and therapeutic applications to aid in the diagnosis and targeted treatment of esophageal cancer.

775011.label: Realisation of objectives
775011.value: Orthotopic liver transplantation (OLT) has been regarded as the best curative treatment for the patients with end stage of liver diseases including advanced liver cirrhosis and acute liver failure. Because of the severe shortage of grafts from brain-death donors and the importance of timely operation on recipients, living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) offers the unique opportunity of early transplantation with theoretically unlimited source of liver grafts. Since the first successful adult to adult LDLT in Hong Kong in 1994, this surgical innovation has been well established locally and relieved the organ donor shortage. However, a liver graft from a living donor is frequently small-for-size for the recipient. The acute phase small-for-size liver grafts injury will trigger a series of inflammatory cascades, which may subsequently mobilize the circulating endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) after liver transplantation. The endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) play important roles of neovascularization, which is critical for the healing of injured tissues as well as proliferation of carcinoma cells in vivo because both processes require a supply of growth factors, nutrients as well as oxygen. The EPCs mobilized by surgical stress resulted from liver transplantation in small-for size liver graft may play both of the roles for tissue repair and tumor recurrence. Therefore, understanding the molecular response controlling the mobilization and differentiation of circulating endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) in marginal liver grafts will be crucial to promote early phase tissue repair and to prevent late phase tumor recurrence. In this GRF project, we have successfully addressed the following issues (the aims of the study): 1. The impact of surgical stress on mobilization of circulating endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) and underlying molecular signaling pathway 2. The roles of EPCs on liver repair as well as tumor recurrence after liver transplantation and liver resection 3. The potential therapy of promotion of the role of EPCs on tissue repair and diminishing the risk of tumor recurrence The populations of circulating EPCs mobilized by surgical stress after transplantation using different liver grafts have been investigated. Significant higher populations of circulating EPCs and intragraft infiltration and differentiation of EPCs presented in small-for-size liver graft. Over-expression of CXCL10, the chemokine which was found to be over-expressed in small-for-size liver graft, played an important role of circulating EPCs mobilization in small-for-size liver graft. The direct role of CXCL10 on EPCs mobilization, intragraft infiltration and differentiation have been also explored in a series of in vivo (CXCL10 knockout mice and a rat orthotopic liver cancer model with major hepatectomy and hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury) and in vitro (bone-marrow cells) functional studies. The kinetics of EPCs involving angiogenesis were further examined in vivo. The new therapeutic strategies have been explored to prevent tumor recurrence by decrease of circulating EPCs in rat liver cancer models. All the objectives have been successfully achieved through clinical association studies, various animal models and in vitro functional experiments.

775011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
775011.value: Elucidating the precise molecular mechanism of mobilization of circulating EPCs by surgical stress will lay the foundation for the further development of therapeutic strategies to prevent tumor angiogeness and promote tissue repair. Investigation of potential novel treatments in animal models will provide important information for future clinical application, especially in LDLT using marginal grafts. It will also open a new window for the Research & Development for local and overseas pharmaceutical companies. Therefore, there will be potential commercial benefit for local R&D industries. We are currently developing the new treatments to attenuate liver graft injury at early phase and prevent tumor recurrence at late phase after LDLT.

775011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
775011.value: Orthotopic liver transplantation has been regarded as the best curative treatment for the liver cancer patients. However, tumor recurrence is the major obstacle for the long term survival after transplantation. Therefore, understanding the molecular mechanism regulating liver graft injury and tumor recurrence will be crucial to develop new therapeutics attenuating acute phase liver graft damage and late phase tumor recurrence after transplantation. In present study, we have demonstrated that significant higher populations of circulating EPCs play important roles on liver tumor recurrence after transplantation. Novel targeting therapies may not only attenuate acute phase liver graft injury but also prevent the tumor recurrence in animal models.

775111.label: Project Objectives
775111.value: To investigate whether or not PPAR-alpha agonists, Wy14643 and fenofibrate, acutely inhibit endothelium-dependent contractions in the SHR aorta through activation of PPAR-alpha. Classical PPAR-alpha is known to affect gene expression and transcription [Delerive et al., 1999; Touyz and Schiffrin, 2006; Leibovitz and Schiffrin, 2007]. Whether or not the acute vascular actions involve genomic or non-genomic mechanisms will be examined by comparing the gene and protein expressions and activities of key enzymes involved in the release of endothelium-derived contracting factor (EDCF), namely phospholipase A2, cyclooxygenase and prostanoid synthases [Tang et al., 2007; Tang and Vanhoutte, 2009; Wong et al., 2010] following acute (30 minutes) treatment with Wy14643 (10 µM) and fenofibrate (10 µM). To elucidate the non-genomic mechanism(s) through which PPAR-alpha agonists acutely reduces the release of EDCF in the SHR aorta. Our previous findings suggest that endothelium-dependent contractions are regulated by calcium signaling in response to acetylcholine and A23187 [Kruse et al., 1994; Tang et al., 2007]. Therefore, the present proposal will focus on examining the acute effect of Wy14643 on capacitative calcium entry and/or calcium release from intracellular stores. To study the acute effect of PPAR-alpha agonists on the oxidative stress of the SHR aorta. The level of reactive oxygen species have been implicated in the release of EDCF [Shi et al., 2007; Tang et al., 2007; Tang and Vanhoutte, 2009]. 775111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
775111.value: Western styled diet, with high fat and cholesterol intake in developed societies including Hong Kong, is associated with an increased risk of atherosclerosis and cardiovascular diseases. Furthermore there is a high incidence of metabolic syndrome characterized by hyperlipidemia and hyperglycemia, and is often associated with hypertension. Metabolic syndrome is recognized as one of the major risk factors of vascular disorders. It is now known that endothelial dysfunction precedes atherosclerosis and vascular disorders. The normal endothelium regulates vasomotor tone through the release of many vasoactive substances such as nitric oxide, endothelium-derived hyperpolarizing factor, prostacyclin, endothelin-1 and vasoconstrictor prostanoids [endothelium-derived contracting factors (EDCF)]. Endothelial dysfunction occurs when there is an imbalance between relaxing and contracting factors. As such, the therapeutic strategy for metabolic syndrome should involve not only the management of the plasma lipid and glucose levels, but also an improvement in endothelial function. Peroxisome proliferators-activated receptors (PPAR) are ligand-activated nuclear receptor involved in gene regulation. Two commonly used lipid- and glucose-lowering drugs, fibrates (PPAR-alpha agonists) and glitazones (PPAR-gamma agonists) mediate their therapeutic effects by regulating gene expression (genomic mechanisms) and hence with a slow onset of action. These drugs have also been reported to possess beneficial vascular actions. In preliminary studies, we demonstrated that PPAR-alpha agonists, Wy14643 and fenofibrate, exerted direct vascular actions through non-genomic mechanisms. Specifically, these PPAR-alpha agonists inhibited EDCF-mediated contractions in the aorta of spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR) by reducing the activity of cyclooxygenase, the enzyme responsible for the synthesis of EDCF. Therefore, the present proposal aims to explore the vascular protective effect of PPAR-alpha agonists and to examine whether or not the PPAR-alpha is involved. The non-genomic signaling pathway involved in the improvement of endothelial function in the hypertensive animal model, SHR (potential action via affecting calcium entry and modulating oxidative stress) will be investigated. In view of the previous report suggesting that PPAR-alpha and PPAR-gamma agonists produce certain genomic actions in a synergistic manner, the present proposal will also study whether or not the acute vascular actions of PPAR-alpha agonist can be potentiated by PPAR-gamma agonist. 775111.label: Realisation of objectives
775111.value: In order to examine the acute vascular effects of PPAR-alpha agonists in spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR), aortae of SHR of age 38-42 week old were isolated and suspended in organ chamber for measurement of isometric tension. Endothelium-dependent contractions were elicited in quiescent SHR aortae with acetylcholine (10-8 to 10-4 M) in the presence of nitric oxide synthase, L-NAME (10-4 M). The results of the experiments demonstrated that both Wy14643 and fenofibrate, at 10-4 M and after one hour of incubation, inhibited endothelium-dependent contractions, but not endothelium-independent contraction to the thromboxane-prostanoid (TP) receptor agonist, U46619 (10-10 to 10-5 M), in SHR aortae. The inhibition by Wy14643 and fenofibrate were reduced in the presence of PPAR-alpha antagonist MK886 (10-4 M), but not PPAR-gamma antagonist GW9662 (10-4 M), thus suggesting that the inhibitory effect was mediated through activation of PPAR-alpha receptors [Objective 1]. Since the PPAR-alpha agonists did not affect contractions to U46619, they likely inhibited endothelium-dependent contractions through a mechanism that is upstream of the activation of TP receptors. The release of endothelium-dependent contracting factors (EDCF) in SHR aortae depends on activation of cyclooxygenase. Therefore, biochemical measurements were performed to examine whether or not acute exposure (one hour) to Wy14643 or fenofibrate affected the degree of activation of cyclooxygenase and the amount of prostanoids released by acetylcholine, using commercially available enzyme immunoassay kits. Our data suggest that PPAR-alpha agonists reduce the release of EDCF by reducing cyclooxygenase-1 activity in hypertensive rat aorta, thereby resulting to a reduced release of prostacyclin and thromboxane A2 [[Objective 2]. Previous studies from our laboratory demonstrate that oxidative stress is involved in the release of EDCF. In the present study, hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) was used to mimic oxidative stress in the vascular system. H2O2 (10-8–10-4 M) induced endothelium-independent contractions in both SHR aortae; this contraction was inhibited by calcium-dependent and calcium-independent PLA2 inhibitors, AACOCF3 (10-4 M) and BEL (3×10-6 M), respectively, cyclooxygenase inhibitor indomethacin (510-6 M), and TP receptor antagonist, S18886 (10-7 M). These results suggest that H2O2 acts upstream of PLA2 for the activation of cyclooxygenase to produce contraction. Wy14643 (10-4 M) inhibited H2O2-induced contraction only in SHR aortae with endothelium, suggesting that it acted on the endothelium, and not on the smooth muscle, to inhibit the effect of oxidative stress. Results from biochemical assay indicated that Wy14643 did not affect the catalase activity in SHR aortae [Objective 3]. To examine whether or not concomitant activation of PPAR-gamma affected the vascular effects of PPAR-alpha agonists, SHR aortic rings with endothelium were exposed to both fenofibrate (10-4 M) and rosiglitazone (PPAR-gamma agonist, 10-4 M). Rosiglitazone alone did not affect endothelium-dependent contractions to acetylcholine, the activity of cyclooxygenase-1 and the release of prostanoids by acetylcholine in SHR aorta rings with endothelium. The addition of rosiglitazone to fenofibrate did not cause greater inhibition on endothelium-dependent contractions, cyclooxygenase-1 activation and prostanoids release than the latter alone. Therefore, activation of PPAR-gamma unlikely offers any protection against endothelial dysfunction in hypertension, either alone or in addition to activation of PPAR-alpha [Objective 4].

775111.label: Major findings and research outcome
775111.value: The major findings from the present study are 1. In isolated thoracic aorta of spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR), Wy14643 and fenofibrate activates PPAR-alpha antagonist to cause endothelium-dependent relaxations. These relaxations are mediated through activation of AMPK, which causes the phosphorylation of endothelial nitric oxide synthase to release nitric oxide, leading to the activation of cyclic GMP signaling pathway. Wy14643, but not fenofibrate, also activates smooth muscle PPAR-gamma to induce relaxation. These relaxations are the result of activation of inwardly rectifying potassium channels in vascular smooth muscle. Because also of the ability to activate PPAR-gamma, Wy14643 offers additional protection against vascular dysfunction of spontaneous hypertension compared to fenofibrate. [These findings are published in Eur J Pharmacol (item 1 of Section 8)]. 2. Endothelium-dependent contractions evoked by acetylcholine in quiescent SHR aorta in the presence of L-NAME were reduced by Wy14643 and fenofibrate but not by the PPAR-gamma agonist rosiglitazone. MK886 (PPAR-alpha antagonist), but not GW9662 (PPAR-gamma antagonist), prevented this effect. Wy14643 and fenofibrate inhibited acetylcholine-induced prostanoid release to the same extent. The addition of rosiglitazone to fenofibrate did not cause greater inhibition on endothelium-dependent contractions, cyclooxygenase-1 activation and prostanoids release than the latter alone. Based on these findings, it appears that PPAR-alpha agonists reduce the release of endothelium-derived contracting factor by reducing cyclooxygenase-1 activity in hypertensive rat aorta. Activation of PPAR-gamma unlikely offers any protection against endothelial dysfunction in hypertension, either alone or in addition to activation of PPAR-alpha. [These findings are published in Eur J Pharmacol (item 1 of Section 8)]. 3. Acetylcholine-induced contractions in SHR aorta were inhibited by Tiron (a scavenger of superoxide anion) plus DETCA (an inhibitor of superoxide dismutase), thus suggesting the involvement of H2O2 in the contractions. Moreover, contractions to H2O2 in SHR aortae were abolished by cyclooxygenase inhibitor. Therefore, oxidative stress likely acts upstream of cyclooxygenase activation in inducing endothelium-dependent contractions in hypertensive animals. As such, Wy14643 and fenofibrate may inhibit the production of H2O2 or its downstream mechanism to reduce acetylcholine-induced contractions. [These findings were presented in International conference (item 1 and 2 of Section 9)]. 4. Wy14643 and fenofibrate reduced contractions to H2O2; this was observed only in SHR aortic rings with endothelium, but not in those without endothelium, indicating that they act in the endothelium to produce their inhibitory effects. Deferoxamine (an iron chelator that scavenges hydroxyl radical) further reduced H2O2-induced contraction in the presence of Wy14643 and fenofibrate, suggesting that the PPAR-alpha agonists inhibit the direct effect of H2O2 but not the effect due to the formation of hydroxyl radical. The PPAR-alpha agonists did not affect the activity of catalase (an enzyme that is responsible for metabolizing H2O2) in these preparations. Therefore, they do not acutely affect the degree of oxidative stress per se; instead, they reduce the vascular dysfunction due to oxidative stress [These findings were presented in international conference (item 3 of Section 9)]. 5. Phospholipase A2 (PLA2) is involved in the cascade for producing arachidonic acid for the action of cyclooxygenase. It likely acts downstream of H2O2 in inducing contraction, since both calcium-dependent and calcium-independent PLA2 inhibitors, AACOCF3 and BEL, respectively, inhibited the contraction to H2O2. Wy14643 and fenofibrate further reduced H2O2-induced contraction in the presence of BEL. The findings thus suggest that the PPAR-alpha agonists do not inhibit calcium-independent PLA2 to produce their inhibitory effect on contractions due to oxidative stress.

775111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
775111.value: The findings from the present study suggest that Wy14643 and fenofibrate acutely inhibit endothelium-dependent contraction in SHR aortae. While the mechanism through which the PPAR-alpha agonists produce beneficial vascular effect in hypertension has been studied in the present study, whether or not they can produce beneficial vascular effects also in other conditions associated with increased oxidative stress, such as aging and diabetics, remains to be examined. Therefore, functional studies with organ chamber techniques and/or biochemical assays with immunoassays [similar approaches to those reported in the present study] can be utilized to examine the vascular effects of PPAR-alpha agonists in normotensive rats at different ages, and in those with diabetics [induced by streptozotocin administration]. Moreover, only the acute vascular effects of PPAR-alpha agonists were examined in the present study. Whether or not the beneficial vascular effects (namely, inhibition of endothelium-dependent contraction and induction of endothelium-dependent relaxation) persists after chronic administration of PPAR-alpha agonists can be further investigated. This can be achieved by long term treatment of SHR with Wy14643, followed by measurement of arterial blood pressure as well as the examination of vascular responses to different endothelium-dependent and –independent contracting and relaxing agents.

775111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
775111.value: Metabolic syndrome is a common medical problem in developed societies such as Hong Kong. It includes hyperlipidemia and hyperglycemia, and is associated with hypertension. PPAR-alpha and PPAR-gamma agonists have been used in the management of plasma lipid and glucose levels, respectively. The present findings demonstrate that PPAR-alpha agonists acutely improve endothelial function in hypertensive animals. This fast onset of vascular protective action of PPAR-alpha agonists may add to the therapeutic advantage, in particular for use in patients with hyperlipidemia and hypertension, to reduce the risk of the development of vascular complications, such as atherosclerosis. While PPAR-gamma agonists appear not to enhance the protective effect of PPAR-alpha agonists on endothelial function, they increase PPAR-alpha agonist-induced smooth muscle relaxation. Therefore, the combination of PPAR-alpha and PPAR-gamma agonists may result in an acute vasodilator effect; this may be beneficial when vasodilatation is needed, but may also lead to a sudden drop in blood pressure and hence reflex tachycardia. As the two drugs may be prescribed together in the management of metabolic syndrome, the possible interaction between them on acute vascular actions needs to be taken into consideration in the design of the therapeutic regime.

775711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
775711.value: The introduction of 2-4 molecules (transcription factors) into somatic cells can transform (reprogram) them into stem cells known as induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). These cells are of great interest in regenerative medicine because they can differentiate into various cell types. Therefore, they can potentially be used to repair damage tissue. The clinical application of iPSCs is hampered by the low efficiency and the slow kinetics of reprogramming, resulting in the formation of partially reprogrammed cells. Recent studies show that the reprogramming efficiency can be improved by inclusion of small molecules that modulate chromatin structure causing inherited change in gene expression without changing the gene sequences (epigenetic modification). How these molecules work are largely unclear. Our data showed that a protein, sirtuin 1 (Sirt1) is involved in reprogramming. Sirt1 can modify histone proteins around the genes, thereby modulate gene expression epigenetically. Its level was low in the somatic cells but was high in iPSCs. Resveratrol, an activator of Sirt1, increased the efficiency of reprogramming from mouse fibroblasts. Conversely, suppression of Sirt1 level decreased the efficiency. The role of Sirt1 in reprogramming is not clear. We hypothesize that Sirt1 functions as a positive epigenetic regulator in the reprogramming of mouse fibroblasts to iPSCs. We propose that exogenously added Sirt1 will enhance reprogramming in two ways. First, Sirt1 modifies histone directly, leading to reduced expression of developmental genes. Second, Sirt1 modifies another protein p53 resulting in (1) increase in cell division and decrease in cell death; and (2) production of Nanog, a molecule important in maintenance of stem cells. We further postulate that exogenous Sirt1 enhances the expression of endogenous Sirt1 boosting its own facilitatory action during reprogramming. There are three objectives to test the hypothesis. They are 1) to characterize the facilitatory action of Sirt1 on iPSC formation; 2) to study the mechanism of action of Sirt1 in enhancing iPS formation; and 3) to determine the role of Sirt1 in the formation of fully reprogrammed iPSCs. Dissecting the molecular events behind the onset and progression of reprogramming for improving the efficiency and generation of high quality reprogrammed cells is crucial to the production of patient-specific stem cells for disease modeling, drug screening and ultimately regenerative medicine. The results of the study will provide insight into the molecular mechanism of cellular reprogramming and the possible use of epigenetic regulatory molecules in improving the efficiency of iPSC production. 引入2-4個分子(轉錄因子)進體細胞中能把它們變換(重整)成幹細胞，名為誘導性多功能幹細胞(iPSCs)。再生醫學對這些細胞有極大的興趣，因為它們能分化成多種各式各樣的細胞。所以它們具有修復受損組織的潛在能力。 誘導性多功能幹細胞在臨床上的應用受制於低效率的重整轉化過程，結果只能形成部分己重整的細胞。最新研究發現重整的效率能透過同時引入一些細小分子而被提升，而這些細小分子能調控核染色質的結構從而引起基因表現出現遺傳上的改變而又不會影響基因的順序(基因外修飾)。但現在還未清楚這些分子是怎樣起作用。 根據我們的數據顯示一種蛋白質乙酰化酶Sirtuin 1 (Sirt1)參與在重整過程中。Sirt1能修改在組織蛋白外圍的基因，所以能外在地調控基因表達。其生物程度可低至體細胞，但又可高至誘導性多功能幹細胞(iPSCs)的水平。白藜蘆醇(逆轉醇)是Sirt1的活化劑，它能提升從小鼠纖維組織母細胞重整的效率。相反地，它能透過抑制Sirt1的水平來降低其重整效率。但Sirt1在重整過程中的角色還未清晰。 我們假設Sirt1在小鼠纖維組織母細胞重整成誘導性多功能幹細胞中的功能是正向基因外修飾的調控者。我們提議外源性地加入Sirt1可從兩方面提高重整效率。第一，Sirt1會直接地修改組織蛋白，從而減少發育遺傳基因的表達。第二，Sirt1會修改其他蛋白p53，從而導致(1)增加細胞分裂和減少細胞凋亡；和(2)產生Nanog，它是維修幹細胞的重要分子。另外我們進一步假設這外源性的Sirt1在重整過程中能提升內源性的Sirt1的表達從而提升其自我促進的作用。 測試上述的假設有三項目標。1) 了解Sirt1在iPSCs生成過程中的促進作用的特性；2) 研究Sirt1在促進iPSCs生成時的作用機理；和3) 確定Sirt1在iPSCs完全重整的生成過程中的角色。 在改善重整的效率和生產高質素的重整細胞的開始和過程背後，仔細分析分子活動對於製造病人專特的幹細胞來改善病情、藥物篩選和終極的再生醫學具有非常重要的價值。本研究的結果會為我們對細胞重整的分子作用機理提供更深入了解。同時，也為表觀基因調控分子在改善iPSCs製造效率中的應用提供可行的建議。

775711.label: Realisation of objectives
775711.value: In the study, we hypothesized that a histone deacetylase sirtuin 1 (Sirt1) functions as a positive regulator in the reprogramming of mouse fibroblasts to iPSCs. An efficient secondary mouse embryonic fibroblast (2oMEF) reprogramming system using Doxycycline (DOX) inducible Yamanaka’s transcription factors was used. The 3 objectives of the project were addressed as follows: Objective 1: To characterize the facilitatory action of Sirt1 on iPSC formation Among the seven family members of sirtuins (Sirt1 to Sirt7), the Sirt1 mRNA was induced most prominently during reprogramming of 2oMEF (2°1B miPSCs). The expression decreased upon differentiation. It is demonstrated that Sirt1 knock down (Sirt1-KD) inhibited iPSCs formation from 2oMEF, while Sirt1 activation by resveratrol (RSV) and Sirt1 over-expression (Sirt1-OE) promoted its production. The effect of RSV was also proved in the primary reprogramming system using lentivirus to deliver those transcription factors. To define the period of Sirt1 actions, the expression level of Sirt1 during reprogramming from day 1 to day 20 was studied. The expression of Sirt1 mRNA increased significantly from day 6 onwards and reached highest on day 20, though the level was much less than that in mESCs. Sirt1 protein was undetectable in 2oMEF, but became detected at a low level upon DOX treatment for 15 days. While SIRT1 protein was reduced in the serial passaged primary MEF, its expression was up-regulated with serial passaging in 2°1B miPSCs after reprogramming, suggesting its role during reprogramming process. The result also showed that Sirt1 effect is most pronounced in the early phases of reprogramming processes, as Sirt1-KD on day 1, but not on day 6 decreased iPSCs formation. In consistent with it, the effect of RSV was also most prominent from day 1 to day 5, confirming that Sirt1 exerted its effects during initiation phase of reprogramming process. Our data further showed that Sirt1 did not affect the mesenchymal–epithelial transition (MET) process as Sirt1-OE had no effect on cdh1 and snail2 expressions. Further, SIRT1 cannot accelerate the miPSCs formation from initiation phase to maturation phase. Objective 2: To study the mechanisms of action of Sirt1 in enhancing iPSC formation a. SIRT1 acts as a histone deacetylase We found that Sirt1-facilitated iPSC formation was attenuated by NAD-dependent HDAC inhibitor nicotinamide. Using chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)-PCR assay, enrichments in the promoters of nestin and Sfrp2 were found in Sirt1 antibody hybridized DNA during initial phase of reprogramming. The Sirt1-enriched nestin was also enriched by the antibodies against H3K27ac, H3K9ac and H4K16ac, known Sirt1 deactylation histone targets. We also demonstrated enrichment in another promoter SFRP1 whose inactivation contributed to aberrant Wnt signaling activation in human breast cancer cell lines, suggesting a possible effect of Sirt1 in the Wnt signaling pathway during reprogramming. To further explore the novel Sirt1 bound promoter, the Sirt1 immunoprecipitated DNA fragments were subjected to next generation sequencing. Gene ontology (GO) analysis indicated that SIRT1-bound promoters were enriched for GO terms related to ion binding, metabolic homeostasis, cell morphogenesis and neuron differentiation. Among them, we validated that Sirt1 bound to the promoters of Cyclin-Dependent Kinase 14 (cdk14) which acts as a cell-cycle regulator of Wnt signaling pathway during G2/M phase, and SLIT And NTRK-Like Family Member 5 (slitrk5) which expressed predominantly in neural tissues. b. SIRT1 acts as a non-histone deacetylase We also identified SIRT1 interacting non-histone proteins using Co-immunoprecipitation assay and mass spectrometry. KEGG pathway analysis indicated Sirt1 bound to proteins involved in repair of double strand break (DSB). We speculated that SIRT1 might promote DNA repair through binding to the complex of DSB repair proteins. Indeed, the levels of the SIRT1 interacting DSB repair proteins (SIRT1-DSB) were up-regulated in the MEF upon DOX induction. We also demonstrated that RSV treatment significantly reduced the reprogramming induced 53BP1 loci which are the classic DNA damage response marker. To this end, we knocked down three of these SIRT1-DSBs at the onset of reprogramming and the down-regulation of these SIRT1-DSBs suppressed the iPSC colony formation. These data supported that SIRT1 activated the SIRT1-DSBs in the initial phase of reprogramming process leading to increase in colony formation. We are preparing the manuscript of this part. c. SIRT1 deacetylates p53 Our results also showed that RSV/ Sirt1-OE led to decreased level of acetylated p53 level, while Sirt1-KD up-regulated its level. However, Sirt1-OE did not affect the proliferation of the cells. Also, Nanog but not p21 mRNA expression was significantly decreased by Sirt1-KD but increased by RSV treatment. Furthermore, Sirt1-OE cells had significantly higher Nanog but lower p21 expression. Tenovin-6, a p53 activator through Sirt1 inhibition, suppressed the iPSCs formation. On the other hand, RSV could compromise the inhibitory effect of nutlin-3a (another p53 activator) on iPSCs formation. As such, Sirt1 may alleviate the suppressive role of p53 on Nanog expression during reprogramming. d. Sirt1 is regulated by miRNAs during reprogrammin Sirt1 has been reported to be a direct downstream target of miR-34a and miR135a. In our study, it was found that Sirt1 expression was up-regulated upon treatment with miR-34a/miR135a inhibitor, while down-regulated upon treatment with their corresponding precursors. Furthermore, miR-34a/miR135a precursor inhibited the iPSC formation, while miR-34a/miR135a inhibitor increased the formation of iPSC in both primary and secondary reprogramming system. Our data also demonstrated miR135a precursor reduced the RSV stimulated iPSC formation, further suggested the involvement of miRNA in Sirt1 manipulated reprogramming progress.  Objective 3: To determine the role of Sirt1 in the formation of ground state iPSCs The pluripotent state of iPSC formed after RSV treatment were first characterized using standard ESC characterization assays. RSV treated iPSCs showed ES like morphology and stained positively with pluripotent markers. These iPSCs also showed high level of alkaline phosphatase activity. Our preliminary data showed that very few intact EB could be formed from normal iPSC. To determine if Sirt1 improved the ground state development of iPSC, we compared the EB formation in control or RSV treated iPSC lines after continuously cultured for 5 passages and 15 passages. However, we found that both lines possessed similar potential in beating cells and gut-like structures formation in the EB, suggesting that Sirt1 may only be involved in inducing the number of partially reprogrammed iPSC colony during early reprogramming process. In addition, our data also demonstrated that RSV/Sirt1-OE did not facilitate the DOX independent growth during the reprogramming process. It is thus postulated that Sirt1 had no pronounced effect on chimera formation. “2i” medium containing GSK-3β inhibitor and MEK inhibitor promotes the ground state formation of iPSCs (Silva et al., 2008). We found that GSK3β inhibitor, but not the MEK inhibitor, promoted the iPSCs formation during initiation phase of reprogramming. On the other hand, the stimulatory effect of MEK inhibitor was found in the maturation phase of the reprogramming process. We further study the effect of Sirt1 overexpression and RSV treatment on reprogramming together with these two inhibitors. We first found that the two inhibitors had no additive effects on RSV stimulated iPSC formation. However, additive effects were found when 2i treatment was performed in the maturation phase after RSV treatment in the initiation phase. These data suggested RSV treated cells may have prepared the cells for the 2i selection to achieve ground state. The data was further supported by the increased expression of Nanog.

775711.label: Major findings and research outcome
775711.value: We have addressed all the objectives proposed in the project. The major findings are as follow: 1) We found that SIRT1 is involved in iPSC formation. SIRT1 knockdown decreased while resveratrol (RSV) increased the efficiency of iPSC formation. The treatments were associated with altered acetylated p53 and its downstream Nanog but not p21 expression. The stimulatory effect was also confirmed by SIRT1 over-expression, which stimulated the formation of colonies with induced Nanog and reduced p21 expression. Furthermore, the effects of RSV and SIRT1 knockdown on reprogramming were most pronounced during the initiation phase of reprogramming. 2oF/1B MEF transfected with a potential regulator of SIRT1, miR-34a inhibitor increased but miR-34a precursor reduced the iPSC formation. The stimulatory effect of SIRT1 during reprogramming was also confirmed in the primary MEF. RSV increased while tenovin-6, a small molecule that activates p53 through SIRT1 inhibition, suppressed reprogramming. These data was published in PLoS One (2013). 2) The mechanisms of action of Sirt1 in enhancing iPSC formation were studied. We found that SIRT1 acts as a histone deacetylase as Sirt1 binding was enriched in the promoters of differentiation related genes like nestin, Sfrp2 and slitrk5 and Wnt signaling pathway molecules like SFRP1 and cdk14. On the other hand, Sirt1 protein was found to interact with DNA repair moleucles. The fact that RSV reduced the reprogamming induced DNA damage suggested that Sirt1 may be involved in the process of DNA repair during iPSC formation. We are preparing a manuscript for these data. 3) One MPhil student and one PhD student working on projects related to the project have fulfilled all requirements of their and graduated (refer to Part C).

775711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
775711.value: This study demonstrated that SIRT1 affected the reprogramming processes, partly through deacetylating p53 leading to the changes of its transactivation activities. It may also promote DSB repair and epigenetically regulate gene expression during reprogramming. Further study on whether Sirt1 directly deacetylates DSB repair molecules leading to the rescue of partially reprogramming cells from DNA damage is required. Although the stimulatory effect of Sirt1 mainly lied in the initiation phase of the reprogramming, our data showed that the strongest stimulatory effect of RSV occurs when the treatment covered all the three phases of reprogramming during which SIRT1 may have different functions. It is speculated that SIRT1 binds to different genes in the three phases. Target ChIP assay can be considered to determine the genes targeted by SIRT1 in different phases of reprogramming. It is also worthwhile to study the Sirt1 interacting protein molecules during different phases of reprogramming. In the middle of this study, another research group has demonstrated a combination of 7 small molecules in replacing the transgene approach for the reprogramming. The facilitatory roles of RSV in that system would be worth for further investigation.

775711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
775711.value: Reprogramming of adult somatic cells into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC) is one of the most significant scientific breakthroughs in recent years. Small molecules that remodel chromatin and alter gene expression increase the reprogramming efficiency in iPSC production. In this study, we demonstrated that sirtuin 1 (SIRT1), a member of the sirtuin family of NAD+-dependent protein deacetylases, is involved in inducing iPSC formation. By using an efficient mouse secondary fibroblasts reprogramming system with doxycycline (DOX) inducible Yamanaka’s transcription factors delivered by piggyBac (PB) transposition (2oF/1B MEF), we show that SIRT1 knockdown decreased while resveratrol (RSV)/SIRT1 over-expression increased the efficiency of iPSC formation. We found that Sirt1 may stimulate the reprogramming process through its deacetylase activity in suppressing differentiation markers or involving in the DNA repair process. The current data suggest the use of Sirt1 in large scale of iPSC formation, which potentially be used to generate patient-specific stem cells for regenerative medicine and to develop a model for studying disease processes using iPSCs generated from the patient of interest.

775811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
775811.value: 肝癌（肝細胞癌，HCC）是全球最主要的惡性腫瘤之一。在東南亞，中國內地和香港，由於B型肝炎病毒的高感染率，肝癌是第二種最常見的致命癌癥。盡管對於肝癌病人的治療方法及效果近年來已經有了長足的進步，但總體而言，由於發現較晚以及頻繁的術後復發，肝癌的預後仍欠滿意。人們對於新的肝癌輔藥療法期待甚殷。因此，有關肝癌的發生、發展潛在的細胞和分子靶點的研究就具有其重要意義，因為這方面的知識可以為肝癌的治療提供新的機會。 從我們對肝癌中DLC/Rho/Rock通路的長期研究中，我們發現RhoE在HCC病例中頻繁（79%）且顯著的呈下調狀態。此外，在體外肝癌細胞系中抑制RhoE的表達可以促進細胞遷移及侵襲。穩定抑制RhoE的表達可以提高肝癌細胞中對細胞收縮力至關重要的肌球蛋白磷酸酶目標亞基1（MYPT1）的磷酸化水平，同時這種提高的效果又被ROCK的抑製劑Y27632所抑制。進一步實驗表明，Y27632還可以抑制因為RhoE的表達抑止所導致的細胞加速遷移。據報導，MYPT1在Thr850位點上特異性地由Rock介導進行磷酸化，因此我們的發現表明RhoE在肝癌細胞中可直接與Rock1相互作用並抑制其活性。有趣的是，作為一個新發現，我們觀察到肝癌細胞中的內源性RhoE不僅分佈在細胞質裡，也分佈在細胞核內。這種內源性RhoE在細胞核內的分佈還從來沒有被報導過，並不同於以往其他研究小組所報導的在不同細胞系中內源性RhoE只分佈在細胞質與細胞膜上。此外，通過亞細胞結構分級分離以及蛋白印跡試驗分析，我們證實了RhoE在細胞核中的存在，而不是僅僅分佈在細胞質中。有趣的是，我們還證實了內源性ROCK1在細胞核中也有分佈。 我們這個研究計劃旨在確立RhoE在肝癌中的作用以及其發揮作用的分子通路。我們計劃 1）從體內方面評估RhoE在肝癌中抑制癌症轉移的能力；2）描繪RhoE在肝癌中參與的細胞信號通路；以及 3）表徵細胞核RhoE的功能意義。我們對肝癌中RhoE功能作用的表徵研究是原創性的，並會對肝癌的發病機理提供新的見解。鑒於治療肝癌對於香港的重要性以及我們研究團隊現有的實力，我們的研究很可能會為建立肝癌治療的新策略以及有效的治療方法提供更深入的見解。

775811.label: Realisation of objectives
775811.value: To evaluate the metastasis suppressing ability of RhoE in HCC in vivo, we have found that low expression of RhoE in the tumors was significantly associated with shorter disease-free survival (P = 0.020) of the patients. Disease-free survival in HCC is usually associated with tumor recurrence due to metastasis, which is usually intrahepatic but also can be extra-hepatic. In addition, we have demonstrated that knockdown of RhoE by shorthairpin RNA using a lentiviral approach led to increased cell motility and invasiveness in SMMC7721 and BEL7402 HCC cells. This suggested that RhoE is related to suppression of HCC cell migratory and invasive abilities. Furthermore, in the in vivo orthotopic liver injection model in nude mice, we demonstrated that knockdown of RhoE enhanced local invasion of HCC cells in the livers, in terms of more invasive tumor front and increased incidence of venous invasion. To address the cell signaling pathways involved by RhoE in HCC, mechanistically, we employed stable knockdown of RhoE in HCC cells. The stable knockdown of RhoE in HCC cells significantly enhanced the phosphorylation of myosin phosphatase, promoted assembly of stress fibers, and increased the formation of plasma membrane blebbings, all these changes and activities being associated with activation of the Rho/Rho-kinase (ROCK) pathway. From these findings, we concluded that RhoE was frequently down-regulated in predominantly HBV-associated HCCs and this down-regulation was associated with a more aggressive HCC phenotype. RhoE regulated the cytoskeleton remodeling and suppressed HCC motility and invasiveness by way of inhibiting the Rho/ROCK axis. Furthermore, based on our findings that Rho/ROCK signaling was highly activated in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), we demonstrated that downregulation of RhoE, a RhoA antagonist, and upregulation of ROCK enhanced resistance to chemotherapy in HCC in both in vitro cell and in vivo murine xenograft models, whereas a ROCK inhibitor was able to profoundly sensitize HCC tumors to cisplatin treatment. Specifically, the ROCK2 isoform but not ROCK1 maintained the chemoresistance in HCC cells. We further identified two downstream molecular pathways which were involved in Rho/ROCK-induced chemoresistance. Mechanistically, we demonstrated that activation of ROCK2 enhanced the phosphorylation of JAK2 and STAT3 through increased expression of IL-6 and the IL-6 receptor complex. We also identified IKKβ as the direct downstream target of Rho/ROCK, and activation of ROCK2 significantly augmented NF-κB transcription activity and induced IL-6 expression. These data indicate that Rho/ROCK signaling activates a positive feedback loop of IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6/STAT3 which confers chemoresistance to HCC cells and is a potential molecular target for HCC therapy. Finally, we showed that ROCK inhibition attenuated Erk1/2 activation. Literature searching suggested nuclear PTEN as a potential candidate for inactivating Erk1/2. We demonstrated that inhibition of ROCK increased the population of nuclear PTEN while overexpressing ROCK2 decreased it. Overexpression of nuclear PTEN alone could already reduce Erk activation in HCC cells. Our findings indicated that RhoE/ROCK may exert their effects on chemoresistance in HCC via regulating the IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 and PTEN/Erk pathways.

775811.label: Major findings and research outcome
775811.value: Deregulation of Rho guanosine triphosphatase (GTPase) pathways plays an important role in tumorigenesis and metastasis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Small Rho GTPase (Rho) and its immediate effector Rho kinase (ROCK) are reported to regulate cell survival, but the detailed molecular mechanism remains largely unknown. RhoE/Rnd3 belongs to an atypical subfamily of the RhoGTPase, the Rnd family, as it lacks the intrinsic GTPase activity and remains always in its active GTP-bound form. We investigated the role of RhoE in HCC. We examined the expression of RhoE in primary HCC samples from patients and found that the RhoE mRNA level was frequently down-regulated (83.1%, 59/71) in HCCs. Low expression of RhoE in the tumors was significantly associated with shorter disease-free survival (P=0.020) of the patients. Knockdown of RhoE by shorthairpin RNA using a lentiviral approach led to increased cell motility and invasiveness in SMMC7721 and BEL7402 HCC cells. Moreover, in vivo an orthotopic liver injection model in nude mice further demonstrated that knockdown of RhoE enhanced local invasion of HCC cells in the livers, with more invasive tumor front and increased incidence of venous invasion. Mechanistically, knockdown of RhoE in HCC cells significantly enhanced the phosphorylation of myosin phosphatase, promoted assembly of stress fibers, and increased the formation of plasma membrane blebbings, all these changes and activities being associated with activation of the ROCK pathway. From these findings, we concluded that RhoE was frequently down-regulated in predominantly HBV-associated HCCs and this down-regulation was associated with a more aggressive HCC phenotype. RhoE regulated the cytoskeleton remodeling and suppressed HCC motility and invasiveness by way of inhibiting the Rho/ROCK axis (Ma W et al., Hepatology 2012013;57:152-161). Along this line and from our findings that Rho/ROCK signaling was highly activated in HCC, we further demonstrated that downregulation of RhoE, a RhoA antagonist, and upregulation of ROCK enhanced resistance to chemotherapy in HCC in both in vitro and in vivo murine xenograft models, whereas a ROCK inhibitor was able to profoundly sensitize HCC tumors to cisplatin treatment. Specifically, the ROCK2 isoform but not ROCK1 maintained the chemoresistance in HCC cells. Mechanistically, we demonstrated that activation of ROCK2 enhanced the phosphorylation of JAK2 and STAT3 through increased expression of IL-6 and the IL-6 receptor complex. We also identified IKKβ as the direct downstream target of Rho/ROCK, and activation of ROCK2 significantly augmented NF-κB transcription activity and induced IL-6 expression. These data indicate that Rho/ROCK signaling activates a positive feedback loop of IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6/STAT3 which confers chemoresistance to HCC cells and is a potential molecular target for HCC therapy (Ma W, et al. Oncotarget 2016; May 18).

775811.value: In this study, we found that RhoE was frequently down-regulated in predominantly HBV-associated HCCs and this down-regulation was associated with a more aggressive HCC phenotype. RhoE regulated the cytoskeleton remodeling and suppressed HCC motility and invasiveness by way of inhibiting the Rho/ROCK axis. In addition, Rho/ROCK signaling activates a positive feedback loop of IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6/STAT3 which confers chemoresistance to HCC cells and is a potential molecular target for HCC therapy. To further confirm the functional significance of ROCK in HCC, the use of model resembling the clinical HCC would be highly relevant. Recently, a number of patient-derived HCC xenograft model (PTDX) in immunodeficient mice has been established in our laboratory. It would be interesting to investigate and explore RhoE underexpression and ROCK overexpression in these HCC xenograft models. By stratifying the HCC PTDX model with or without RhoE underexpression and ROCK overexpression, it would provide a useful model for comparing their drug sensitivity towards e.g. Sorafenib or other potential kinase inhibitors, which has been shown to prolong HCC patient survival by blocking kinase activity. Rho/ROCK expression may serve as a prognostic marker to predict the HCC cell sensitivity to kinase inhibitor treatment.

775911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
775911.value: 在香港乳腺癌的發病率是20人中有1個。雖然中國婦女的發病率比西方婦女要低，但近年呈上升趨勢。乳腺癌是全球三大婦女的癌症，直到現在快速丶可靠和準確的血液篩選試驗是缺乏的。乳腺癌篩查可盡早診斷惡性腫瘤，從而有可能降低死亡率。雖然乳房X光檢查診斷是目前常用的非侵入性檢查工具，但由於費用和檢查所需的專業知識阻礙了這個程序的廣泛應用。因此，至今仍有必要制定一個成本效益和準確的檢查方法。 據估計，高達70％的人類基因轉錄成RNA，但只有1〜2％的人類基因組含有蛋白質編碼RNA (mRNA)。因此，基因組包含的非蛋白質編碼RNA（ncRNA）比蛋白質編碼RNA更多。其中許多是進化上保留的ncRNA，有高效表達並具體表明其功能的意義。其中微小RNA（miRNA）是最知名的小ncRNA，但許多其他長ncRNA是存在的。差分ncRNA的表達模式與相關癌症診斷或預後可作為一種新的生物標誌物的來源。我們是第一個研究小組報告血漿miRNA作為有潛力的大腸癌診斷標誌物。有趣的是，最近的研究還表明，外來體（從細胞釋放的小膜泡）包含的ncRNA可能成為癌症診斷更好的生物標誌物。 我們研究小組過往已率先進行血漿RNA/miRNA的分析丶診斷和生物應用。最近，我們制定了一個捕捉腫瘤相關血漿中包含特定表面標誌（如EpCAM）的外來體的辦法。使用這種發展，我們已經成功地豐富了腫瘤相關血漿外來體和異型那些包含小ncRNA的外來體。這項研究是為了檢驗一個假設：乳腺癌患者的血漿外來體的miRNA/ncRNA可以反映同一腫瘤組織中的miRNA/ncRNA。在這項研究中，我們相信是第一個建議分析在乳腺癌患者血漿中外來體ncRNA。我們還在200多個乳腺癌患者樣本中，有系統地驗證有潛力的生物標誌物。我們的最終目標是發展一個早期發現和監測乳腺癌進展的方法。這種發展將有利於高危人群篩查時作為監測，或病人患有乳腺癌時在疾病進展監測的使用。

775911.label: Realisation of objectives
775911.value: We have identified the blood processing conditions in terms of incubation time and temperature conditions. With these information, the stability of plasma exosomal can be optimizied. We have proven that the miRNA profile in plasma exosome was similar to those in tissues, implicating that these miRNAs were derived from breast tumors. We adopted two approaches to profile ncRNAs in plasma exosomes: PCR-based arrays and massive parallel sequencing. Altogether, there were 17 miRNAs/lincRNAs that were selected for futher validation. The putative miRNA biomarkers selected were verified in pre- and post-operative plasma samples. Large cohort validation were then carried out in 300 breast cancer patients and 300 normal control susbjects. Results showed that 10 miRNA/lincRNAs were significantly upregulated in breast cancer patients when compared with normal control subjects. Since the area under curve (AUC) for single marker were below 0.8, combination of markers were shown to have improved AUC, sensitivity and specificity. With these combined markers, there is no association with tumor stage and breast cancer subtypes. Taken together, this combined markers could be potentially used as a diagnostic marker for breast cancer.

775911.label: Major findings and research outcome
775911.value: The stability of exosomal small RNAs upon different temperature, ie, room temperature and 4C, in either plasma or whole blood incubations were similar. However, this was not the case for whole blood exosomal small RNAs, most of the miRNAs had a significant decrease in expression levels after incubation for 24 hrs. It implicated that exosomal RNAs are more stable in plasma than whole blood, hence, plasma samples were used for the study. We further compared different markers, EpCAM and CD220, for the enrichment of plasma exosomes in this study. We found that EpCAM enriched exosomal miRNAs resulted in higher RNA yield (50% more) and broader range of miRNAs could be detected. Surprisingly, there was a higher overlap of miRNAs between total exosomes in plasma and tissues samples. Hence, we performed small RNA-seq by Illumina MiSeq sequencing on plasma exosomes from breast cancer patients normal control subjects. There were 17 miRNAs/ncRNAs differentially expressed in the plasma of breast cancer patients, and were validated in 300 independent breast cancer cases for candidate selection. Since 4 of the markers (lincRNA225210, 234715, 245466 and 246066) had lower expression in breast cancer patients when compared with the healthy controls, therefore the remaining putative markers identified (miR-16, miR-21, miR-27a, miR-210, miR-451, lincRNA199753, 202314, 242008, 230257, 233400, 242516, 235398, and 246532) were validated on these independent set of plasma samples. Since plasma ncRNA alone as a marker did not generate satisfactory ROC values, the best combination (p<0.0001) for breast cancer detection was miR-210 and lincRNA 199753. We demonstrated that such combined marker in breast cancer patients were significantly discriminated normal control subjects. Such combined markers yielded a ROC curve area of 0.901 (95% CI 0.879-0.924). The optimal sensitivity and specificity were 90.5% (95% CI 87.9%-92.7%) was 76% (95% CI 70.3%-80.4%) in discriminating breast cancer including benign tumors from normal control. Results showed that there was no association between the expression levels and the tumor stage in breast cancer patients. The levels of combined markers did not vary significantly across different breast cancer subtypes (p=0.675; Kruskal-Wallis Test). It showed that plasma levels of the markers seemed to be specific to breast cancer, as the expression levels did not show any statistical difference in other cancer types such as esophagus, gastric, lung, liver and colorectal cancers.

775911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
775911.value: Results from this study provide evidence that plasma exosomal ncRNAs were derived from tumor, since miRNA profile in plasma was consistent with those in tissues. Also, From our data, we found that combined marker had an improved sensitivity and specificity than one single marker, suggesting this combined markers of ncRNAs could be a potential biomarker to discriminate breast cancer patients from healthy controls. We have examined the specificity of this marker in other cancer types, eg. gastric, colon, liver etc, more sample numbers are warranted to confirm the specific of this marker. The prognostic value of this marker warrants further investigation. In addition, understand the underlying mechanism of these markers would provide framework for better design of targeted therapy, and might use as a marker for diease monitoring and treatment efficacy.

775911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
775911.value: Breast cancer is one of the leading cancers in the world, a rapid and accurate blood-based screening test is lacking. Screening for breast cancer allows early diagnosis and thus effectively reduce mortality. Though mammagraphy diagnosis for breast cancer is commonly used as non-invasive screening tool, the cost incurred and expertise required for mammogram has prevented wide application of this procedure. Hence, there is a pressing need for the development of a cost-effective and accurate screening method for breast cancer. This project demonstrated that the conditions of blood processing and different exosome enrichment methodologies were important in the study of miRNAs/ncRNAs. MiRNAs/ncRNAs profiling were performed by PCR-based array and massive parallel sequencing (RNA-seq) in both plasma and tissues samples of breast cancer patients. These platforms provide valuable information on the correlation of these ncRNAs in the circulation and breast tumors. We found that combined ncRNAs is a better predictive diagnostic marker than a single ncRNA. The significance of this study provide the basis of the usefulness of plasma as a non-invasive tools to discriminate breast cancer patients from healthy controls.
