776011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
776011.value: Total laryngectomy is the surgical removal of a pathological voice box, usually as a treatment for laryngeal cancer. As the entire voicing mechanism is removed, the laryngectomized patient suffers the loss of ability to talk. Therefore, learning to use an alternative voice to speak again becomes an important part of post-laryngectomy rehabilitation. Currently, four alaryngeal voicing methods are available: esophageal, tracheoesophageal, electrolaryngeal, and pneumatic artificial laryngeal speech. It has been estimated that there are over 50,000 laryngectomees in the U.S., 65,000 in China, and 2500 in Hong Kong. Using an unfamiliar voicing method, the cancer survivors often face a number of difficulties. Studies have revealed that the poor alaryngeal speech is strongly related to poor performance in different aspects of speech production. For example, electrolaryngeal speakers exhibit poor tone production and esophageal speakers often speak with a poor voice quality. To be able to talk proficiently again, alaryngeal speakers need to spend a long period of time to learn and practice with the new voicing mechanism. This involves continuous drilling and overcoming the difficulties associated with different alaryngeal speaking methods. According to Theories of Motor Learning, focused and repetitive drilling, combined with implicit and explicit learning with appropriate feedback will help alaryngeal speakers enhance the learning process. They need to be aware of the problem areas and repeatedly learn to improve those areas. Being able to assess the speech performance and identify the problem areas by means of a comprehensive and standardized assessment will provide them with explicit information and is very important in the effective acquisition of alaryngeal speech. However, such an assessment tool is currently not available despite the large number of alaryngeal speakers worldwide. Developing such an assessment tool for alaryngeal speakers is imminent and will be beneficial to a large population of laryngectomees. The proposed research will develop a comprehensive tool to assess alaryngeal speech proficiency of all kinds with inputs from experts such as speech therapists, Ear-Nose-Throat doctors, speech scientists, and laryngectomees themselves. The assessment tool will be multidimensional in nature, covering all aspects of speech production, and it should be easily adaptable to other languages. To develop the tool, speech aspects will be carefully researched, identified and validated. Proficiency in various speech aspects will be objectively evaluated. After tested for internal validity and test-retest reliability, the assessment tool will be evidence-based and will objectively identify the problem areas in alaryngeal speech production. 作為喉癌最終的治療手段，全喉切除術是把整個病變喉頭切除的一項外科手術。由於在手術過程中整個喉頭結構已被切除，術後病人會完全喪失發聲能力，不能說話。所以，病人在手術後學習怎樣利用其他方法重新發聲成為無喉康復中一個重要的部份。目前病人在手術後可以採用四種不同的無喉發聲：（1）食管發聲，（2）食氣管發聲，（3）人工電子喉發聲，及（4）氣動式人工喉發聲法。據統計，美國現有無喉者超過50,000人，中國65,000，而香港則有超過2,500名無喉者。因為需要使用一個嶄新的發聲方法說話，這些喉癌倖存者往往覺得非常困難和困擾。研究發現，無喉者說話的水平，跟他們各個語言範疇的能力有直接的關係。例如電子喉的聲調改變能力較差、食管發聲的嗓音比較沙啞等。無喉者要說話好起來，就要通過長時間不斷的練習，克服新的發聲機制帶來的困難。根據運動學習理論，集中和重複學習，加上伴有反饋的內隱和外顯學習訓練，可幫助無喉者更好的利用新發聲方法說話。要有效的學習無喉發聲，無喉者本人需要知道問題出在那裡，然後圍繞著這些問題方向重覆訓練、加以改善。要知道問題出在那裡，需要一個可以客觀評估他們語言各方面能力的標準測試。儘管我們有大量的無喉者正在努力學習不同的無喉語，可是到目前為止還是沒有這樣的一個標準評估。所以，研發一個可以客觀地評估無喉者說話能力的測試是必須的、刻不容緩的。 本研究將基於各方有關的專家如言語治療師、耳鼻喉醫生、言語科學家和無喉者本人的專業意見，研發一套可以客觀地評估不同廣東話無喉發聲者的說話水平的綜合測試。這套綜合的評估測試考慮到使用者不同語言範疇的能力，而且通過簡單的改動，便可用於其他語言。該測試會對使用者的各個語言範疇作客觀的評估，來測試使用者的無喉語言的水平。研發該評估時，通過檢驗內在效度、測驗再測驗可信度來提高評估工具的準確性，這樣研發出來的無喉語言能力評估將會是客觀的、且具有實證效力的。

776011.label: Realisation of objectives
776011.value: There are three objectives attempted in the project and all of them have been successfully completed. The first objective involved identifying the speech areas that are directly associated with poor speech performance in different types of alaryngeal speech. We have consolidated them into eight aspects: (1) voice quality, (2) pitch and loudness, (3) fluency, (4) audible distraction, (5) coordination, (6) placement of coupling device, and (7) overall proficiency. Voice quality refers to the overall impression of the voice. Under voice quality, acoustical and non-acoustical measurements describing voice quality are: maximum phonation time, hoarseness, breathiness, effortfulness, and phonation breaks (sudden stoppage of sound during phonation). Pitch and loudness include both averages and variations. Fluency indicates the smoothness of speech flow. It includes speech rate and phrase length measurements. Audible distraction refers to the unwanted noise generated during speech production. The noise may come from the stoma of patients, or the poor coupling of electrolarynx. Coordination may refer to the coordination in coupling speech devices, or in occluding the stoma (during tracheoesophageal speech), or between breathing and phonation. Placement of coupling device includes the accuracy in coupling, and the consistency of coupling device. The second and third objectives involved developing and validating an assessment tool to evaluate speech performance associated with alaryngeal speech. They have been achieved by a number of reliability and validity measures. For example, intra-rater reliability was high (r = 0.884), indicating a good test-retest consistency of the test. Convergent validity was used to determine if the items are truly indicating the targeted speech aspects. In the project, statistically significant and moderate-to-strong correlation was found.

The third objective of the project involves testing the assessment tool for validity and reliability. Content validity, face validity and test-retest reliability will be assessed. This needs to be carried out to ensure that the tool is accurate and valid, and results obtained using the test are reliable and consistent.

776011.label: Major findings and research outcome
776011.value: The major part of the project was to develop and validate a comprehensive assessment tool for the laryngectomized patients. Different important aspects of speech that are associated with poor speech proficiency were first identified and confirmed with professionals. Under each important speech area, items that are reflected by different acoustical parameters were developed. These items were validated and correlated with each other. This was to make sure the items are relevant and useful. Finally the entire assessment was test-retested and validated by using data from laryngeal and different alaryngeal speakers. With the assessment tool, speech therapists or health professionals can objectively describe the speech performance associated with patients who have undergone totally laryngectomy and are using different speaking methods. The results have been presented at an international conference (ref: Part C, 9.3) and a manuscript is currently under preparation for later submission for publication (ref: Part C, 8.4). During the development of the assessment tool, some acoustical and non-acoustical measurements were obtained. For example, to better understand the articulation among alaryngeal speakers, articulatory pressure measurements were also obtained. Subsequent analyses revealed that labial and lingual contact pressures were higher in alaryngeal speakers than normal laryngeal speakers (ref: Part C, 9.4). In addition, aerodynamic data were also collected in order to compare between esophageal and tracheoesophageal speakers. Data revealed that despite the use of the same sound source, esophageal speakers’ had greater neoglottal resistance to airflow than tracheoesophageal speakers (ref: Part C, 8.2). Acoustic data were analyzed in the study and some analysis results showed that alaryngeal speakers performed differently when producing speech vs. non-speech sentences (ref: Part C, 8.3). This indicates that speech and non-speech (such as singing) activities are of different modalities. At the same time, it also indicates the potentials of neoglottis in producing speech. By analyzing the acoustical signals associated with alaryngeal speakers using non-linear dynamics, it was found that beside traditional perturbation measurements, different alaryngeal speech sounds could be nicely distinguished by using non-linear dynamical parameters (ref: Part C, 8.1). This shed light in using different analytic methods in classifying alaryngeal voices.

776011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
776011.value: This project only served as the first step in developing and validating an objective assessment tool for evaluating speech proficiency of laryngectomized patients. As only male alaryngeal speakers were recruited in the present study, there is a need for further study involving also female alaryngeal speakers, although this might be very difficult due to the limited number of female laryngeal cancer patients. In addition, future study may also include parameters other than acoustical measurements. For example, aerodynamic or other physiological measurements may be included to provide a more comprehensive perspective of how speech is produced by alaryngeal speakers. Regardless, the present study was the first to develop an objective assessment for all kinds of alaryngeal speech. It will help front line speech therapists or health professionals objectively and holistically evaluate alaryngeal speech proficiency.

776011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
776011.value: Laryngeal cancer survivors after total laryngectomy learn to speak using an alternative method. Being able to objective assess their speech performance can certainly improve their learning. The project is the first step in developing and validating an objective assessment tool to evaluate how well/poor alaryngeal speakers speak. By identifying various areas of speech that are associated with poor speech performance, the tool is able to report which areas that speaker is weak (and strong) at, thus helping speech therapists, health professionals, or patients themselves to improve their speech rehabilitation regime, rendering their speech training more effective and efficient. The speech areas included: (1) voice quality, (2) pitch and loudness, (3) fluency, (4) noise during speech, (5) articulation, (6) coordination of hand/finger and speech, and (7) overall intelligibility of speech. Speech parameters were then developed under each area to indicate different aspects of speech. Parameters were validated and correlated with each other, in order to make sure they are relevant and useful. Finally a chart indicating the different patient’s speech performance can be established.

776411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
776411.value: 於西方國家包括香港，卵巢癌是女性其中一項致死的病因。卵巢癌主要治療方法包括細胞減量性切除及以鉑類化合物為基礎的化學治療。儘管於初期進行治療，癌症復發是十分普遍兼且難以預斷的。發展新的疹斷及治療卵巢癌方法是十分迫切。因此，清楚了解卵巢癌成因的分子機理是非常重要的。 利用酵母菌兩雜合系統，我們最近發現了乳癌相關基因3 (BCA3)為p73之互動拍擋，且證明了它們的互動増加了子宮頸癌細胞對電療所引致的細胞凋亡反應。 我們的實驗結果顯示p73蛋白與其他蛋白之互動可能改變p73蛋白本身作為控制細胞生存以及對治療反應的功能。在此建議研究，我們的目標是要研究我們之前通過酵母菌兩雜合系統找到的p73蛋白另一個互動拍擋：染色體17開放讀碼框架37(C17ORF37)或C35。C35蛋白於各類癌症包括乳癌及前列腺癌都是高度表達及對癌細胞增長和擴散扮演非常重要的角色。我們的初步實驗結果顯示卵巢癌內的C35蛋白也是高度表達。此外，C35高度表達加強了卵巢癌細胞的増長及擴散能力，細胞不著地生長測驗及裸鼠體內腫瘤試驗皆證實了C35促進卵巢癌細胞於體外或體內之致癌能力。通過暫時性及穩定性基因轉染技術在卵巢癌細胞內同時表達C35蛋白和DNp73蛋白時，相對單一蛋白表達，對藥物的抗藥性增加了。因此，我們假定DNp73和C35共同合作引致癌細胞惡化。在此提出之研究，我們將會通過以下四點去研究DNp73-C35互動對卵巢癌之重要性： 1）證實DNp73和C35之互動。 2）測試抑制C35之表達對卵巢癌細胞的生理性影響。 3）闡明DNp73-C35對卵巢癌細胞之藥物敏感性的影響。及 4）研究DNp73-C35於卵巢癌之臨床重要性。 我們相信通過對DNp73和C35蛋白功能上之了解將會顯著地加強我們對卵巢癌病變的認知，對日後發展新及有效的療法有莫大幫助。

776411.label: Realisation of objectives
776411.value: A) Binding activity of C35 with DNp73 We performed co-immunoprecipitation assay to map the interacting site between C35 and p73. The result indicated that C35 preferentially interacts with DNp73 at the N-terminal. Immunofluorescence staining revealed that C35 and DNp73 co-localized at the peri-nuclear region. We also included the C35 Y39F/Y50F mutant in the co-immunoprecipitation assay. We found that DNp73 physically interacted with the C35 Y39F/Y50F mutant. The binding activity of C35 and p53 was also investigated. However, no physical interaction was found between C35 and p53 in ovarian cancer cells. B) Functional characterization of C35 by knockdown of the endogenous C35 We attempted to establish C35 knockdown stable clone with shRNA. However, cells were not viable after transfection of C35 shRNA. Alternatively, to study the silencing effects of C35 in ovarian cancer, transient transfection using siRNA of C35 was performed to knockdown endogenous C35 expression in ovarian cancer cells. The siRNA targeting C35 was efficient in knocking down C35 expression in ovarian cancer cells. Our data demonstrated that silencing of C35 contributed to inhibition of cell migration, cell proliferation and cell migration. In addition, we also found that knockdown of C35 sensitized the response of ovarian cancer cell line to cisplatin treatment. C) Functional significance of DNp73-C35 interaction in response to cisplatin treatment in ovarian cancer cells We examined the effect of DNp73 on the cisplatin-induced apoptosis of stable C35-overexpressing clone by TUNEL assay. A significant reduction in the number of apoptotic cells was observed in DNp73-transfected OV-C35-M3 cells (C35 overexpressing stable clone) compared with OV-MV1 cells (vector control stable clone) and the parental OV2008 cells. In addition, we evaluated the viability of OV-C35-M3, OV-MV-1 and OV2008 cells after cisplatin treatment. We observed that only the OV-C35-M3 cells survived; the OV-MV1 and parental OV2008 cells died following cisplatin treatment. These observations further support the roles of C35 and DNp73 in promoting the chemo-resistance of ovarian cancer. We observed that cisplatin treatment induced the expression of total AKT in parental OV2008 and OV-MV1 cells. In contrast, AKT expression was increased in OV-C35-M3 cells prior to cisplatin treatment, suggesting that the stable expression of C35 enhanced the basal level of AKT expression in OV2008 cells. The phosphorylation of AKT was measured for the AKT activity. After cisplatin treatment, AKT phosphorylation was dramatically enhanced in OV-C35-M3 cells compared with OV2008 and OV-MV1 cells. We also demonstrated that transfection of DNp73 further enhanced AKT activity in OV-C35-M3 cells in response to cisplatin treatment. Because NFkB is one of the major targets of activated AKT and has been suggested to promote cellular resistance to anti-cancer drugs, we examined the level of NFkB expression in OV2008, OV-MV1 and OV-C35-M3 cells. Prior to cisplatin treatment, higher NFB expression was found in OV-C35-M3 cells than in OV-MV1 or parental OV2008 cells. After cisplatin treatment, we observed that NFkB expression was greatly enhanced in OV-C35-M3 cells. The transfection of OV-C35-M3 cells with DNp73 markedly activated the expression of NFkB in response to treatment with cisplatin. We have examined the expressions of NFkB downstream target genes including MMP, VEGF and UPA. However, no significant different in their expression was found. D) Clinicopathological significance of C35 in ovarian cancer The mRNA expression of C35 was determined by quantitative real time PCR. The correlation of C35 expression with clinicopathological data in ovarian cancer was performed. However, no significant correlation with the clinicopathological parameters (histological types, stage, grade and age) was found.

776411.label: Major findings and research outcome
776411.value: Clinical significance of C35 in ovarian cancer Overexpression of C35 was found in human ovarian cancer tissues and ovarian cancer cell lines. This observation suggested that C35 may function as an oncogene in ovarian cancer. (British Journal of Cancer 2013, The 2012 Croucher Advanced Study Institute Conference 2012) Oncogenic properties of C35 in ovarian cancer We applied both overexpression and knockdown approaches to characterize the functional roles of C35 in ovarian cancer. Stable expression of C35 was found to promote cell proliferation, cell migration, in vitro and in vivo tumorigenicity of ovarian cancer cells. Furthermore, knockdown of endogenous C35 expression in chemo-resistant ovarian cancer cell line sensitized the response to cisplatin treatment and inhibited cell migration. These data suggested the role of C35 as a key regulator in the tumorigenesis and drug-resistance of ovarian cancer. (British Journal of Cancer 2013, The 2012 Croucher Advanced Study Institute Conference 2012) Co-operative role of C35 and DNp73 in promoting chemo-resistance in ovarian cancer By yeast two-hybrid screening, C35 was identified as a protein binding partner of DNp73. Co-immunoprecipitation revealed that C35 preferentially bound to DNp73 through the N-terminal region. Co-immunofluorescence staining also confirmed their co-localization to the peri-nulcear region. To investigate the co-operative effects of C35-DNp73 interaction, we performed functional assays with co-expression of C35 and DNp73 in ovarian cancer cell line. We examined the effect of DNp73 on the cisplatin-induced apoptosis of C35-expressing stable clones. A significant reduction in the number of apoptotic cells was observed in DNp73-transfected C35 stable clone compared with vector control stable clone and the parental cells. In addition, we also evaluated the effect on cell growth of these cells after cisplatin treatment. We observed that only the C35 stable clone cells survived; the vector control stable clone and parental cells died following the cisplatin treatment. These observations further support the roles of C35 and DNp73 in promoting the chemo-resistance of ovarian cancer. (British Journal of Cancer 2013, The 2012 Croucher Advanced Study Institute Conference 2012) Mechanisms underlying the oncogenic roles of C35-DNp73 interaction To study the possible mechanistic pathway, we studied the involvement of the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway in C35 mediated oncogenesis. Proetin expression of total AKT and the level of AKT phosphorylation were examined in DNp73-transfected C35 stable clone, vector control stable clone and parental ovarian cancer cells. After cisplatin treatment, AKT phosphorylation was dramatically enhanced in DNp73- transfected C35 stable clone as compared with vector stable clone and parental cell. We further evaluated the expression of NFB (one of the major targets of activated AKT) in C35-DNp73 expressing cells in response to cisplatin treatment. Western blot analysis revealed that the expression levels of p-AKT and nuclear NFkB were greatly enhanced in DNp73 and C35 co-expressing cells treated with cisplatin. Our current findings suggest that the C35–DNp73 interaction enhances the activation of AKT and the activity of NFkB after cisplatin treatment, ultimately diminishing the apoptotic response to cisplatin. (British Journal of Cancer 2013, The 2012 Croucher Advanced Study Institute Conference 2012)

776411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
776411.value: The novel findings presented in this study delineate a possible mechanistic pathway for the promotion of oncogenesis in ovarian cancer by the C35–DNp73 complex. Since C35 is highly expressed in ovarian cancer cells and tumor tissues, the potential role of C35 as a diagnostic or prognostic marker in detecting ovarian cancer is warrant to be further investigated. C35 augments the functions of DNp73 in tumor progression and chemo-resistance by activating AKT and nuclear NFkB. The downstream targets are thus worth for further investigation with the aim to identify potential drug targets for cancer treatment. Future studies of the functional importance of the C35–DNp73 interaction using animal model will be necessary to validate the in vivo functions of these proteins in ovarian cancer.

776411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
776411.value: In this study, we demonstrated the possible mechanism for the promotion of oncogenesis in ovarian cancer by the C35–DNp73 complex. Our investigation of C35 expression in ovarian cancer tissues suggest that C35 is highly expressed in ovarian cancer suggesting its oncogenic role in ovarian cancer. Functional characterizations of C35 in ovarian cancer cell lines reveal that overexpression of C35 enhances cell proliferation, cell motility and transforming ability in ovarian cancer cell. In addition, C35 potentiates the functions of DNp73 in tumor progression and chemo-resistance by activating other oncogenic proteins such as AKT and NFkB. This study is the first to illustrate a possible mechanistic pathway by which DNp73 and C35 contribute to the chemo-resistance of ovarian cancer cells. Our findings strongly suggest that DNp73 cooperate with C35 to promote tumor progression and contribute to chemo-drug (cisplatin) resistance in ovarian cancer. Further studies of the functional importance of the C35–DNp73 interaction in other cancers will be essential to gain better insight into the roles of these proteins in carcinogenesis.

776611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
776611.value: Pandemic influenza A virus is generated by virus reassortments. The unpredictability of this virus can be highlighted by the emergence of pandemic H1N1/2009 virus with genes derived from avian, swine and human sources. Interestingly, all viral polymerase from the last 3 pandemics contain PB2, PB1 and PA polymerase subunits of different host origins. Extensive studies on avian viral polymerase genes have identified several crucial amino acid residues for host adaptations. However, the underlying biological advantages for these zoonotic introductions of polymerase genes into these pandemic viruses remain to be fully determined. In particular, the impacts of these previous reassortments on viral polymerase activity are yet to be elucidated. Besides, the subsequent biological properties changes of seasonal viral polymerase in the post-pandemic era are largely unknown. Here, we propose to characterize the viral polymerase complexes from 1957 (H2N2), 1968 (H3N2) and 2009 (H1N1) pandemic viruses. For H2N2 and H3N2 polymerase studies, polymerase complexes derived from a series of pandemic and seasonal strains circulated during 1957 to 1995 will be analyzed. Polymerase activities of these viruses and their “chimeric” mutants will be characterized. These studies will allow better understanding of the nature history of viral polymerase activity of human influenza viruses. Moreover, natural single, or possibility co-evolved, mutations that might be important for modulating seasonal viral polymerase activity are expected to be identified. As the pandemic H1N1/2009 virus has only been circulated in humans for a very short time, swine isolates that are genetically related to this pandemic strain will be tested in the investigation. This work will be the first systematic demonstration on the compatibility between swine and human viral polymerase subunits. More importantly, this might also help to reveal some biological properties of the pandemic H1N1/2009 virus before its circulation in humans. Our preliminary data have indicated that pandemic viral polymerase might have stronger activities than seasonal ones. This interesting observation suggests that the viral polymerase activity might have an impact on the genesis of pandemic strains. Alternatively, these pandemic viral polymerase might need to refine their activities after adapting to a new host. We therefore intend to test these hypotheses by passaging infectious polymerase mutants in several in vitro and in vivo selection systems. Progeny viruses from these passages will be characterized. 776611.label: Realisation of objectives
776611.value: This study tried to characterize viral polymerase complexes (vRNPs) derived from various pandemic, seasonal, and animal viruses. The following work was performed during the study: Objectives A & B Viral PB2, PB1, PA and NP genes from pandemic (H1N1/2009; H2N2/1958; H3N2/1968), seasonal (H1N1, N=2; H2N2, N=5; H3N2, N=2) and animal (swine =1; avian =2) were cloned in plasmid expression vectors. These vRNPs and their derivatives were characterized in different host cells (e.g. human and avian) at various culturing conditions (e.g. 33 C, 37 C and 39 C). Over 200 different polymerase mutants were characterized in the study and their polymerase activities were determined by luciferase reporter assays previously established in this laboratory. Objective C Using the determined viral polymerase activities as above and data from our phylogenetic analysis, we identified a number of mutations that have effects on viral polymerase activity in human H2N2 polymerase complex. Some of these mutations were found to be co-evolved in the seasonal H2N2 viral polymerase. To test this hypothesis, we generated a panel of mutants and determined their activities. Apart from conducting experimental work, we also tried to use statically approach to identify possible co-evolved mutations. H2N2 viral PB2, PB1, PA viral genes were analyzed by random matrix theory analysis (in collaboration with Dr Matthew McKay, HKUST). Using publicly available viral sequences, we identified an interesting polymorphism in viral PB2 gene (PB2-627). As this residue is a well-known marker for interspecies transmission, we therefore generated a panel of PB2-627 mutants. The PB2 mutants were experimentally characterized in various in vivo and in vitro conditions. Objectives D & E Two panels of vRNP mutants: 1) chimeric H2N2 series and 2) PB2-627 series were generated by reverse genetics. Over 25 infectious virus mutants were rescued and their growth kinetics were characterized in cell models. Over 15 infectious viruses were subsequently studied in mouse models to test for their virulence. In addition, recombinant viruses passaged in mice were sequenced. De novo mutations identified from these progeny viruses were also studied as described above (see Objectives A and B). In order to determine the possible effects of viral polymerase activity on viral fitness, representative mutants were serially passaged in the presence of oseltamivir. This was to test their abilities to generate drug-resistant mutations under selective environments.

776611.label: Major findings and research outcome
776611.value: a) Viral polymerase activity might modulate viral fitness (Chin et al., in preparation) We demonstrated that vRNPs of H2N2 and H3N2 pandemic viruses had higher polymerase activity than seasonal H2N2 viruses. The recombinant virus with H2N2 pandemic vRNP also showed faster growth kinetics in the early stage of viral replication and better adaptability to the selective environment with neuraminidase inhibitor than the recombinant virus with H2N2 seasonal vRNP, which had a lower polymerase activity. Further sequence analysis and experimental work demonstrated that some of these mutations were co-evolved in the H2N2 vRNPs. Our results demonstrated that the viral polymerase activity has a direct impact to virus fitness and virus adaptive potential. We are currently preparing a manuscript to report our findings (Chin et al., in preparation). b) Development of a novel statistical approach to study viral polymerase compatibility (Chin et al., Influenza Other Respir Viruses, 2013) Over 200 recombinant vRNPs were characterized in various experimental settings. We used some of the representative datasets to develop a novel strategy to study viral polymerase compatibility. Specifically, we used a statistical method, namely full factorial design, to identify factors that have significant effects on polymerase activity. Several single viral polymerase subunits and their interactions were identified to be critical determinants for viral polymerase activities. c) Use of the established statistical approach to study human H7N9 polymerase complex (Chin et al., Influenza Other Respir Viruses2014) In the course of this study, there was a pandemic concern of human H7N9. We used our newly statistical approach to study recombinant vRNPs with subunits derived from human H1N1, H3N2, and H7N9 viruses. Our results demonstrated that some reassortant vRNPs with subunits derived from the H7N9 and other human viruses can have much higher polymerase activities than the wild-type levels. d) Sequence plasticity of PB2-627 position (Chin et al., Virology 2014) We used a site-directed random mutagenesis method to demonstrate that PB2-627 position has a high sequence plasticity. These PB2-627 mutants showed various polymerase activities and replication kinetics in mammalian and avian cells as well as pathogenicity in mice. Serially passaging these mutants in MDCK cells generated some compensatory PB2 mutations that can restore polymerase activities of the PB2-627 mutants. Of these, PB2-D309N was identified as a novel one. E) Others (Wong et al., Clin Chem 2013): A diagnostic assay specific for human H7N9 virus was developed. The protocol was published and shared with the World Health Organization.

776611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
776611.value: a) The statistical approaches developed in this study can help to study emerging influenza viruses of pandemic concern. Results generated from the analysis can provide relevant information for pandemic influenza risk assessment; b) The random mutagenesis method used in the study can be applied to other key viral markers. Mutants generated from this approach would be important tools to study influenza biology. c) Recent findings suggested that PB2-627 positive might interact with cellular importins. The PB2-627 mutants generated from this study will be used to study this biological event.

776611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
776611.value: Influenza A virus is a constant threat to human health. The last 4 human influenza pandemic viruses contain viral polymerase subunits derived from animal sources. Understanding how the influenza virus polymerase complex (vRNP) might contribute to the interspecies transmission and virus fitness help us to control this disease. In this study, we characterized a large number viral polymerase complexes (vRNPs) derived from various pandemic, seasonal, and animal influenza viruses. Specifically, we studied these vRNPs and their derivatives in various models. We also introduced several site-directed mutations into representative vRNPs to study the impact of these mutations on virus fitness and virus replications. Our results indicated that recombinant viruses with high viral polymerase activities are more capable to generate adaptive mutations under a new selection pressure. These findings would help to understand the viral determinants for zoontoic transmission and virus evolution. In the course of this study, we also developed two analytic methods and a mutagenesis method to study viral polymerase activities. These research tools would be useful to study influenza vRNPs and viral RNA synthesis.

776811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
776811.value: Helicases are ubiquitously expressed enzymes that catalyze the unwinding of double-stranded DNA, RNA or DNA-RNA hybrids. SNF2 family proteins, although share a common feature of containing an ATPase subunit with high sequence similarity to DExx box helicases, usually do not possess classical helicase activity but function as ATP-dependent translocases involved in chromatin remodeling. Over the last two decades at least 20 subclasses of human SNF2 family enzymes have been identified that play distinct roles in various fundamental cellular processes such as transcriptional regulation, DNA replication, recombination and repair. Mutations or mis-regulation of these SNF2 family members have been implicated in many developmental defects and human diseases such as premature aging and cancer. To unravel the mechanistic basis of how these enzymes function is critical for gaining insight into the related human diseases. In this grant application, we propose to characterize a functionally unique human SNF2 family ATPase SMARCAL1 (SWI/SNF-related, matrix-associated actin-dependent regulator of chromatin subfamily A-like 1, also known as HARP). This enzyme shares sequence similarity with other chromatin remodelers, but has recently been identified as the first “helicase” capable of annealing complementary single-stranded DNA bound by replication protein A (RPA). SMARCAL1 is also the only identified gene mutated in Schimke immunoosseous dysplasia (SIOD), a multisystem disorder characterized by skeletal dysplasia, renal failure, T-cell immunodeficiency, and death within the first two decades of life. Several studies have revealed that the N-terminus of SMARCAL1 physically interacts with replication protein A (RPA) complex, which helps recruit SMARCAL1 to stalled replication forks to counter DNA damage and replication stress. Despite recent progress toward understanding the role of SMARCAL1 in DNA damage response, the precise molecular mechanism by which SMARCAL1 maintains replication fork stability remains to be elucidated. In this project we will develop a new structure-based paradigm for functional profiling of SMARCAL1 including the following aims: (1) To determine the crystal structure of SMARCAL1, with or without fork-like DNA. (2) To elucidate the mechanism of ssDNA rewinding by SMARCAL1. (3) To characterize molecular interactions between SMARCAL1 and associated RPA complex. The results from our proposed studies will provide important insights into the catalytic mechanism of SMARCAL1, and further define the molecular basis of SMARCAL1/RPA interactions that play a critical role in maintaining replication fork stability during DNA replication. 解旋酶是广泛存在且对细胞生长，分裂起重要作用的关键酶。 解旋酶种类较多，但功能不尽相同。 不同的解旋酶可使DNA双链，或 RNA，或 DNA/RNA解链。 SNF2家族蛋白虽然含有DExx解旋酶特征, 却主要在染色質重組裝中起转位酶的作用。 过去二十年，至少有20种SNF2家族酶已经确定，并发现在各种基本细胞生命过程，如转录调控，DNA复制，重组和修复中发挥独特的作用。这些SNF2家庭成员的突变或调节不当会导致多种人类疾病如发育缺陷，过早衰老和癌症等。 此次申请我们提出深入研究一个功能独特的SNF2家族蛋白ATP酶SMARCAL1。 这种酶与其他染色质重塑蛋白序列相似，但最近被确定为第一个能够复合互补单链DNA的“解旋酶”。 SMARCAL1也是唯一确定在Schimke immunoosseous dysplasia（SIOD）这种疾病中发现有突变的基因。最近的研究发现表明， SMARCAL1 与RPA有相互作用，两蛋白的结合有助于引导SMARCAL1到停滞的复制叉去对抗及修复DNA损害。尽管最近取得了一些初步进展，但SMARCAL1如何能够复合互补的单链DNA的分子机制， 以及 SMARCAL1同RPA一起如何在DNA损害的情况下稳定复制叉尚待阐明。 鉴于此我们希望在项目支持期间完成以下目标 ：（1）解析SMARCAL1, 以及同核酸结合的复合物的三维晶体结构 。 （2）解析SMARCAL1和RPA的复杂的分子间相互作用。 我们研究结果将会明确SMARCAL1不同与传统解旋酶的催化机制，并进一步确定SMARCAL1同RPA相互作用的分子机理。研究结果无疑推动我们进一步了解Schimke immunoosseous dysplasia（SIOD）这种疾病关键分子机制。

776811.label: Realisation of objectives
776811.value: Human SMARCAL1 (SWI/SNF-related, matrix-associated actin-dependent regulator of chromatin subfamily A-like 1, also known as HARP) is a functionally unique SNF2 family ATPase. Though sharing the sequence similarity with other SNF2 family members, SMARCAL1 has recently been identified as the first “helicase” capable of annealing complementary single-stranded DNA bound by replication protein A (RPA). Biallelic mutations of SMARCAL1 have been identified in Schimke immunoosseous dysplasia (SIOD), a multisystem disorder characterized by skeletal dysplasia, renal failure, T-cell immunodeficiency, and death within the first two decades of life. Several studies have revealed that the N-terminus of SMARCAL1 physically interacts with replication protein A (RPA) complex, which helps recruit SMARCAL1 to stalled replication forks to counter DNA damage and replication stress. Despite recent progress toward understanding the role of SMARCAL1 in DNA damage response, the precise molecular mechanism by which SMARCAL1 maintains replication fork stability remains to be elucidated. Over the funding period, (1) We determined the high-resolution crystal structure of RPA32 in complex with SMARCAL1 N-terminal region. (2) We found that RPA32 binding motif defined in previous published paper (Mer G et al. Cell. 103, 449-456) is incomplete, and we therefore redefined the common recognition pattern shared by RPA32 interacting proteins. (3) For the first time, we observed RPA32 undergoes conformational rearrangements upon SMARCAL1 binding. This conformational changes induced by SMARCAL1 binding might be important to trigger RPA heterotrimer released from ssDNA and eventually facilitate SMARCAL1 annealing reaction to proceed processively. (4) We determined the crystal structure of SMARCAL1 N-terminal HARP1 domain. HARP1 domain adopts a globular fold with five anti-parallel β-sheet bridged by two α helices and two short hairpins. Two α helices stabilize each other and pack on one side of β-sheet surface. The complementary biochemical analysis is ongoing. (5) We have established the baculovirus expression system for three SMARCAL1 fragments containing ATPase domain, the structural characterization of these SMARCAL1 fragments is underway.

776811.label: Major findings and research outcome
776811.value: (1) We found that RPA32 binds to a 26-amino-acid-long SMARCAL1 N-terminus much stronger than a 19-amino-acid-long one. Interestingly, this 19-amino-acid SMARCAL1 peptide is designed based on a previously highly cited Cell paper in which the authors defined a consensus motif for RPA32 binding proteins. This has raised a question if previous determined RPA32 binding motif is valid. (2) We determined crystal structure of human RPA32 C-terminal domain (RPA32C) in complex with SMARCAL1 N-terminal 26-amino-acid-long peptide (residues: Leu5-Ala30) at 1.95Å resolution. The structure revealed that 26-aa peptide of SMARCAL1 adopts an almost perfect right-handed α-helix structure with the highly conserved 11 residues aligned on one face of the α helix showing extensive interactions with the RPA32C domain. Extensive mutagenesis experiments were performed to corroborate the interactions observed in crystal structure. (3) Nuclear magnetic resonance-based study has indicated that the RPA32C-SMARCAL1 interaction induces the conformational changes in RPA32C, this is consistent with the findings in the crystal structure. This conformational changes induced by SMARCAL1 binding might be important to trigger RPA heterotrimer released from ssDNA and eventually facilitate SMARCAL1 annealing reaction to proceed processively. (4) Based on the structural analysis, isothermal titration calorimetry and NMR titration in combination with extensive mutagenesis, we provided convincing evidence that redefines the common recognition pattern shared by RPA32 interacting proteins. (5) We also carried out structural analysis of human SMARCAL1 HARP1 domain, and HARP1-HARP2 double domain that precede ATPase domain and are critical for its annealing helices activity. SMARCAL1 HARP1 domain adopts a globular fold with five anti-parallel β-sheet bridged by two α helices and two short hairpins. Two α helices stabilize each other and pack on one side of β-sheet surface. HARP1 binds stronger to dsDNA than to ssDNA. The crystallization of HARP1-HARP2 double domain turned out to be challenging. (6) We have established the baculovirus expression system for three SMARCAL1 fragments containing ATPase domain. SMARCAL1_I (aa: 230-870), SMARCAL1_II (aa: 230-954) and SMARCAL1_III (aa: 324-954) were cloned into pFastBac-HT-B vector respectively. Soluble proteins were expressed in SF9 cells. The large-scale protein expression of these SMARCAL1 fragments for the structural characterization is underway.

776811.value: More recent studies have shown that SMARCAL1 reversal in response to replication stress, but the detailed mechanism by which SMARCAL1 contributes to the restart of stalled replication fork remains to be determined. In addition, several studies showed that SMARCAL1 is important for DNA double-strand breaks repair and telomere maintenance, It will be interesting to determine which other DNA damage response factors work together with SMARCAL1 and RPA to participate in these processes.

776811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
776811.value: Faithful transmission of genetic and epigenetic information from parent to daughter cells is central for eukaryotic life. However, eukaryotic cells are constantly facing challenges from both environmental insults and endogenous toxins, defects in DNA replication pathways are a major cause of cancers and premature aging. Cells have an elaborate machinery to duplicate the vast quantity of genetic information stored in DNA; at the same time, cells also rely heavily on specialized enzymes to accurately and efficiently repair the damaged DNA. A number of DNA helicase enzymes have been implicated in the repair of double-strand breaks and damaged replication forks, but little is known regarding the molecular mechanisms by which helicases promote damaged DNA repair and facilitate replication. As a distant member of SNF2 ATPase, SMARCAL1 represents a newly recognized type of annealing helicase with a distinct function in DNA repair at stalled replication forks. Our proposed study will provide the molecular mechanism of SMARCAL1-RPA interaction and SMARCAL1-DNA interactions required for damaged DNA repair associated with DNA replication. The completed study will reveal the molecular basis of SIOD caused by mutations in SMARCAL1.

777111.value: 1) The 3D morphological and clinical assessment of population-based study subjects with Schmorl’s nodes: Utilizing high resolution 3D T2-weighted MRI and segmentation software, a 3D morphological illustration will be generated and the quantitative volumetric acquisition of the surface area of the endplate and Schmorl’s node will be obtained and correlated with the degree of disc degeneration. Clinical reassessment will also be performed at the time of 3D MRI assessment. 2) Assessment of the population-based study subjects with Schmorl’s nodes for the presence and severity of lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration by use of T1-rho MRI: Utilizing T1-rho MRI with matched T2-weighted MRI, the study will address the biochemical profile of intervertebral segments with and without Schmorl’s nodes and attempt to discern if T1-rho MRI allows for earlier detection of disc changes. As such, knowledge gained from the current study will broaden the understanding of low back pain and degenerative disc disease, and has the potential to address preventative and novel therapeutic modalities regarding endplate defects/abnormalities.

777111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
777111.value: Low back pain is a leading cause of disability worldwide, presenting detrimental socioeconomic and health-care consequences. Intervertebral disc degeneration commonly occurs in the lumbar spine and is an etiological factor associated with the development of low back pain. The vertebral endplate is regarded as the main regulator for intervertebral disc nutrition and integral in the common pathway of disc degeneration. Diffusion studies of the lumbar spine have noted altered diffusion in degenerated discs and in the setting of vertebral endplate irregularities/changes, such as Schmorl’s nodes. Schmorl’s nodes are focal abnormalities of the endplate with invagination of intervertebral disc material. For the past two decades, disc degeneration and Schmorl’s nodes, have been assessed via conventional T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Studies have suggested that Schmorl’s nodes of the lumbar spine have a genetic predisposition and may be related to low back pain. Recent evidence based on the investigators’ large-scale population-based study of Southern Chinese noted that the severity of disc degeneration based on conventional T2-weighted MRI of the lumbar spine increases with the presence of Schmorl’s nodes; however, intervertebral segments with Schmorl’s nodes existed that did not exhibit disc degeneration. Previous work by the investigators has also noted the unique morphological and topographical variants of Schmorl’s nodes, suggestive of a unique component in the pathogenesis of endplate changes. Moreover, the investigators’ have noted that disc degeneration severity may be dependent upon Schmorl’s node morphology. Based on the investigators’ population-based cohort study, the current proposal will address the extent of endplate involvement and function of Schmorl’s nodes in relation to disc degeneration and clinical profile. The aims of the proposal will address the following: 1) the three-dimensional (3D) morphological and clinical assessment of Schmorl’s nodes and its relation to disc changes; 2) the assessment of intervertebral segments with alternative T1-rho MRI matched to T2-weighted MRI to determine early stages of disc degeneration in relation to Schmorl’s nodes; 3) postcontrast MRI diffusion study to assess endplate integrity and function, primarily in relation to Schmorl’s nodes, additional risk factors that may affect the diffusion process, and disc degeneration. Findings from this initiative will further define the phenotype of Schmorl’s node and facilitate genome-wide association studies to identify genes responsible for such nodes and their implications upon the disc and low back pain. 777111.label: Realisation of objectives
777111.value: The project’s set-backs have been the loss of 2 key Radiology investigators who relocated to other institutes and not enough funding provided by RGC from the start to complete this study. We have recently found a new collaborator in the Department of Diagnostic Radiology, Dr. Edward Hui, to assist with the imaging acquisition. However, he is quite new and this project is not his main priority. In addition, it has been a challenge to find dedicated students to devote time to assist in the project. Nonetheless, considering that circumstance, the project has progressed and has had some interesting developments of clinical importance. Below is an assessment of the objectives: 1) With respect to the 3D imaging assessment of the endplate phenotype, we have collaborated with RUSH University, Chicago, USA and have developed a novel platform to assess the 3D phenotype of endplate abnormalities. Subjects have been imaged and the computer software program has been developed. The technological aspects have been overcome. We are currently working with a student that will obtain the data acquisition and analyses during the months of June and July, thereby seeing this project to completion. 2) With respect to assessing the Schmorl’s nodes with T1-rho imaging, this has been completed. We have presented our findings on the use of T1-rho and its application to the disc segment at various local and international meetings. We have drafts of this work prepared for journal submission. 3) With respect to post-contrast MRI diffusion, we have recently obtained an AOSpine grant that will facilitate the assessment of subjects for this arm of the study. This AOSpine grant took over 1 year for the contract to be approved by HKU, as such the funds could not be utilized until now. In addition, since we did not have dedicated Radiology investigators until recently (i.e. Dr. Edward Hui), this arm of the study could not have been properly addressed. Of further note, the original post-contrast diffusion protocol was rather intrusive to the subjects, taking over 24 hours of in-house stay for assessment. To address these concerns, we have developed a new protocol and technology to assess the diffusion of the endplate that will only consist of 10 minutes, is reliable and more efficient. We have identified appropriate subjects for recruitment and our Radiology collaborator is properly positioned to assist. 4) With respect to defining the phenotype of Schmorl’s nodes and its genetic basis, we have further refined the phenotyping of Schmorl’s node and have reported the findings. We have also investigated the relationship between these Schmorl’s nodes and genetic factors in our database. However, we did not find any significant genetic factors. With deeper appreciation of this phenotype and genetic analytical techniques, we will continue to re-visit this platform in the future. On another positive note, this project has led to the discovery of some unexpected findings and additional research directions. 1. The imaging utilized in this project has led to the identification of a unique imaging biomarker on MRI that is related to more spine degeneration but is also noted in subjects with more severe low back pain and disability in comparison to traditional MRI techniques. This is a major breakthrough in “imaging pain” that will have immeasurable clinical impact in the medical community. We have presented this work at regional and international meetings and have written up an initial paper for journal submission highlighting our findings. A MMedRes student has devoted his studies to this platform and we have also submitted a 2015-2016 RGC research grant application to investigate this technique even further. 2. The novel imaging utilized in this study has also led to the mapping of fatty infiltration of paraspinal muscles, in particular in relation to spine degeneration and pain. These findings have further refined the phenotype of paraspinal muscle changes and have sparked interest in the field of the importance of muscles with regards to pain development. We have presented our findings at various meetings and have drafted manuscripts for journal submission. In summary, although we have had various challenges throughout this project, we sought creative means to fulfill our objectives. In so doing, we have been able to further explore upon the technology and data we have collected to discover and develop new imaging biomarkers. Based on this work, new research lines have been developed and grant funding sought.

777111.label: Major findings and research outcome
777111.value: 1. We have discovered the ultra-short time-to-echo disc sign (UDS) based on UTE MRI. The UDS is a novel imaging biomarker highly associated with spine degeneration and more severe low back pain and disability. The UDS has tremendous clinical impact as being a tool to identify problematic spines and location of pain, which may replace traditional MRI sequences and have a global impact. In short, the UDS serves as a new imaging phenotype that broadens our understanding of degenerative disc changes and may possess substantial potential clinical utility. 2. Utilizing T1-rho MRI, we were the first to report in humans the quantitatively assessment of the “proteoglycan profile” of lumbar disc displacement. A decrease in proteoglycan concentration on T1-rho MRI was noted in the presence of disc displacement at all disc levels. Level-specific values have been identified that may have predictive utility at the index or adjacent disc levels as well as aid in the classification, etiology, natural history, and therapeutics of disc displacement. Further assessment has been conducted of discs in the presence of Schmorl’s nodes, noting if early disc changes were present in the presence of endplate changes. 3. Our work was the first to note the spatial distribution of paraspinal muscle fat content of the lumbar spine in Asians, noting that fat distribution was more prevalent in the lower lumbar spine and that level-specific quartile variations were not evident. In this population, spatial distribution of lumbar paravertebral fat content was not related to the presence of disc degeneration, other spinal phenotypes (e.g. Schmorl’s nodes/endplate changes), and subject demographics. This study further sheds light on the potential role of paraspinal muscle fat content throughout the lumbar spine and provides new direction with respect to its etiology and potential clinical implications. Based on this work we have further validated the technology utilized to assess paraspinal fatty muscle infiltration.

777111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
777111.value: We will further build on the UTE MRI technology to assess the disc and endplates. As our work has shown, the clinical implications of this technology are immense. We have applied for a new funding to pursue future, large-scale prospective studies in patients utilizing UTE, T1-rho, and conventional MRI in patients to further assess clinical relevance of our “pain imaging” platform. We will also utilize this technology to assess the treatment algorithm of new minimally invasive biological therapies for the disc. This work has also led to a novel platform of biomechanical assessment of the spine in the context with such novel imaging. We will further explore other spinal phenotypes, such as the paraspinal muscle integrity in the context of clinical symptoms. Along this line, we have formed a collaborative consortium of muscle experts throughout the world to pool resources and expertise to develop novel approaches to muscle assessment and treatment. We will endeavor to realize to completion the 3D phenotype assessment of Schmorl’s nodes and the diffusion profile of the endplate within the next 2-3 months.

777111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
777111.value: Low back pain is the world’s most debilitating condition with tremendous socioeconomic health-care consequences. Spinal changes and degenerative findings have been found to be related to pain, but may not be synonymous. Our project has further refined the understanding of endplate abnormalities (e.g. Schmorl’s nodes) and other relevant spinal phenotypes, such as disc degeneration and fatty infiltration of paraspinal muscles, that may be related to pain. Our work has made new discoveries in the field of “pain imaging”, whereby we have identifies new imaging biomarkers on MRI that are related to the severity of degenerative changes, pain and disability in comparison to previous traditional imaging methods. These imaging biomarkers are able to identify the source of the pain and can assist in future personalized management and treatment options for patients with low back pain that may also be cost-effective.

777211.label: Project Objectives
777211.value: To reconstruct the phylogeny of Disepalum and related members of the annonoid clade based on molecular data using maximum parsimony (MP), maximum likelihood (ML) and Bayesian inference (BI) methods. To use the resultant phylogenies to test hypotheses of generic monophyly, particularly with regard to the inclusion of Enicosanthellum in Disepalum. To test hypotheses of morphological character evolution, particularly with regard to: (a) the evolutionary reduction in sepal and petal number; (b) the evolutionary fusion of petals (petal-to-petal and petal-to-receptacle); and (c) the evolution of carpophores. To undertake field and laboratory-based experiments on the reproductive biology of selected Disepalum species to test hypotheses of fly pollination and determine breeding systems. To use the molecular phylogenies to investigate the inferred evolutionary shift in pollination system from beetles to flies. To use the molecular phylogenies to test hypotheses of historical biogeography, particularly with regard to: (a) the origin and dispersal of Disepalum in South-east Asia; and (b) the broader-scale origin and dispersal of the annonoid clade.

777211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
777211.value: Molecular phylogenies are an invaluable tool in comparative biology as a conceptual framework for interpreting data from various disparate areas of research. Phylogenetic studies of early-divergent lineages are of particular importance for understanding broader evolutionary patterns as they enable inferences regarding the ancestral condition of features. The proposed study focuses on the ‘annonoid’ clade of the early-divergent angiosperm family Annonaceae, and the genus Disepalum in particular. A robust and well-resolved phylogeny of the annonoid clade will be reconstructed using sequences of a broad range of nuclear and chloroplast DNA regions. This phylogeny will be used to test hypotheses in four distinct ways, as follows: (1) Genus-level taxonomy. Generic circumscription in the annonoid clade (particularly the inclusion of Enicosanthellum in Disepalum) will be reassessed by evaluating putative monophyly. (2) Morphological evolution and function in Disepalum. Evolutionary changes in selected characters will be revealed by mapping morphological data onto the phylogeny, thereby highlighting characters of particular functional importance and potential key evolutionary innovations. Characters of particular interest include: the reduction in sepal and petal number; the fusion of petals; the origin of different types of fruitlet attachment; and characters of functional importance in pollination biology. (3) Pollination ecology and breeding systems in Disepalum. Variation in floral morphology in the genus is indicative of the existence of contrasting pollination systems, with some species inferred to be beetle-pollinated, and others to be fly-pollinated. Novel empirical data on the phenology and pollination ecology of exemplar species will be used to determine pollination systems. The breeding systems of these species will be evaluated using a combination of field-based controlled-pollination experiments and lab-based molecular studies using inter-simple sequence repeat (ISSR) markers. The molecular phylogeny will be used as a framework for testing the hypothesised shift from beetle pollination to fly pollination; it has been speculated that such evolutionary changes have occurred in several disparate lineages in the family, resulting in convergence in floral structure. (4) Historical biogeography. The most probable ancestral geographical areas for internal nodes in the phylogeny will be inferred, thereby enabling the probable direction of migration events to be deduced. Relaxed molecular clock methods will be used to estimate divergence times, enabling the putative migration events to be correlated with geological and palaeoclimatic data. Previous biogeographical hypotheses will be tested, including: the origin of the annonoid clade in Africa; the Asia-to-America migration of the Annona-Asimina-Disepalum lineage; and the reverse America-to-Asia migration in the Disepalum lineage.

777211.label: Major findings and research outcome
777211.value: This research has given rise to three important journal articles, either published (#1), in press (#2) or about to be submitted (#3): (1) The first paper (“Phylogenetic reconstruction, morphological diversification and generic delimitation of Disepalum (Annonaceae)”) included the first molecular phylogenetic reconstruction of Disepalum, based on sequences from four chloroplast and two nuclear DNA regions. The phylogeny was used as a framework for clarifying taxonomic delimitation and assessing evolutionary transitions in key morphological characters. Generic monophyly was confirmed, and two sister clades recognised as subgenera (subgen. Disepalum and subgen. Enicosanthellum) based on a detailed evaluation of morphological synapomorphies. We evaluated changes in petal morphology in relation to hypotheses of the genetic control of floral development and suggested that the compression of two petal whorls into one and the associated fusion of contiguous petals (observed in subgen. Disepalum) may be associated with the loss of the pollination chamber, which in turn may be associated with a shift in primary pollinator. We also discussed: the evolution of pollen octads in relation to pollinator visitation frequency and the existence of an extragynoecial compitum to enable intercarpellary growth of pollen tubes; and the independent evolution of monocarp fruit stalks in the genus, that may facilitate effective seed dispersal. (2) The second paper (“Contrasting pollination ecology of Disepalum species (Annonaceae): evolutionary loss of the floral chamber and partial breakdown of protogyny associated with a shift in pollination system”) is currently in press. This work follows up on the hypotheses relating to changes in pollination system associated with changes in floral morphology, raised in paper #1. We used detailed field observations of representative species from the two subgenera in Disepalum to show that a shift in primary pollinator is likely, from nitidulid beetle and drosophilid fly pollination to bee pollination. This is associated with a breakdown in protogyny, enabling the meliponine bees (which are attracted by pollen) to effectively transfer pollen to the stigma during the sexual overlap phase. (3) The third paper (“Historical biogeography and ecological niche modelling of the Asimina-Disepalum clade (Annonaceae): role of ecological differentiation in Neotropical-Asian disjunctions and diversification in Asia”) is nearing completion, and will soon be submitted to BMC Evolutionary Biology. We conclude that a vicariance event resulting in a Neotropical-Asian disjunction likely coincided with climatic deterioration at the Eocene-Oligocene boundary. Geographical isolation caused by geographical and palaeoclimatic events seems to be more significant than climate niche differentiation in driving diversification in Disepalum.

777211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
777211.value: This project is part of a series of broad-ranging investigations that focus on the early-divergent flowering plant family Annonaceae. It is my objective to provide extensive integration of these studies, thereby enabling effective knowledge transfer. The project reported here, for example, integrates molecular phylogenetics (paper #1), floral morphology (paper #1) and pollination ecology (paper #2); parallel studies that focus on evolutionary changes in the floral transcriptome of selected Annonaceae species will provide genetic data that will help determine whether the hypotheses presented in paper #1 can be explained by reference to the disruption of the homeotic genetic control of organ identity during floral development. Similarly, the biogeographical contribution (paper #3) integrates well with other studies of genera (previously and currently studied) that show intercontinental disjunction. The work reported here included several methodologies that were new to my lab: the knowledge gained on ecological niche and phyloclimatic modelling of species will be invaluable for future research.

777211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
777211.value: Understanding the evolutionary relationships of early-divergent lineages is key to understanding broader evolutionary patterns. This research project is part of a larger, integrated study of the early-divergent flowering plant family Annonaceae. We have focused on the relatively small genus Disepalum, which shows an intriguing diversity in floral morphology (with two very distinct floral forms, with and without extensive petal fusion) and fruits that possess stalks that are developmentally very unusual. We reconstruct the evolutionary tree of the genus based on analysis of DNA sequence data, and then use this tree as a basis for inferring evolutionary patterns and processes. We were able to interpret evolutionary transitions in important morphological characters, and to integrate this with field-based ecological studies that showed that the origin of petal fusion was correlated with a shift in primary pollinator. We also used the evolutionary tree to better understand the geographical origin and dispersal of the genus in relation to its close relatives, showing that the lineage once occupied a broad north latitudinal distribution, with North American and East Asian lineages diversifying as a result of climatic deterioration at the Eocene-Oligocene boundary.

777411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
777411.value: The Branchio-Oto-Renal (BOR) syndrome is an autosomal dominant congenital disorder caused by mutations in the genes coding for the Six1 homeobox transcription factor and its interacting partner Eya1. Patients with BOR display craniofacial anomalies, deafness and renal malformations due to abnormal development of the branchial arches, ear structures, and kidney. Craniofacial morphogenesis involves the crosstalk of transcription and signaling factors, in their function in the interaction of epithelium, mesenchyme and neural crest cells during branchial arch development. Hox genes are essential patterning genes branchial arch and craniofacial development. The role of Notch signaling pathway genes in branchial arch development is less well understood. By mouse mutant analysis, we have discovered that in Six1 null mutant, the expression of Hoxb3 is ectopically up-regulated in the second branchial arch. Moreover, ectopic expression of Hoxb3 in transgenic mice leads to up-regulation of the Notch ligand Jag1, as well as branchial arch abnormalities similar to those observed in Six1 mutant. Therefore, we hypothesize that there could be crosstalk between Hoxb3 and Jag1 in mediating second branchial arch derived abnormalities in Six1 and Eya1 mutants. The aim of this project is to elucidate the functions and genetic interaction of the Hoxb3 and Jag1 genes in abnormal branchial arch development in Branchio-Oto-Renal (BOR) syndrome, using Six1 and Eya1 mutant mice as the disease models. The objectives of this project are: (1) To investigate the second branchial arch defects and expression patterns of Hox and Notch signaling pathway genes in Six1 and Eya1 mouse mutants; (2) To investigate the functions of Six1 and Eya1 as negative regulator of Hoxb3 by molecular and genetic approaches; (3) To investigate the function and regulation of Jag1 in the second branchial arch by molecular and transgenic mouse mutant analysis. From this project, the interaction of Hoxb3 and Jag1 in the molecular pathogenesis of branchial arch abnormalities will be revealed, the hierarchy of genetic interactions between Hoxb3 and Jag1 in Six1-Eya1 associated branchial arch defects in BOR syndrome will be elucidated. 腮耳腎發育不良症候群（以下簡稱BOR症候群）是由Six1和Eya1的基因突變而導致的顯性遺傳病。患有BOR症候群的病人表現有顱面部異常，耳聾和腎臟畸形。這些是由於腮弓，耳部結構和腎臟的非正常發育而導致的。 顱面部的器官形態發育包括了轉錄和信號因數的相互作用和影響，特別是這些因數在腮弓發育過程中的上皮細胞，間葉細胞和神經脊細胞之間的相互影響和作用。Hox是腮弓和顱面部發育過程中十分重要的基因，然而我們目前對Notch信號通路中的基因在腮弓發育過程中的作用並不是十分瞭解。通過小鼠的突變分析，我們發現在Six1突變鼠中，Hoxb3在第二腮弓的表達量有異常的增加。而且，在Hoxb3轉基因小鼠中Notch通路其中的一個配體Jag1的表達量有著顯著的上調。同時，在Hoxb3轉基因小鼠中，腮弓的變異也和我們在Six1突變鼠中所觀察到的十分相似。因此，我們假設在Six1和Eya1突變所導致的第二腮弓變異過程中Hoxb3和Jag1之間有著相互作用。 這個研究的目標是：利用Six1和Eya1基因突變小鼠作為疾病模型，來闡明在BOR症候群中，Hoxb3 和Jag1基因在腮弓發育不良過程中的功能和基因的相互作用。通過這個研究我們將會達到以下目的：（1）在Six1和Eya1突變鼠中，瞭解第二腮弓的缺陷以及Hox基因和Notch信號通路基因的表達情況；（2）通過分子和遺傳方法來研究Six1和Eya1基因作為Hoxb3基因負調控因數的作用；（3）通過分子和轉基因突變小鼠來研究Jag1基因在第二腮弓中的作用和調控。通過這個課題，我們可以解釋清楚腮弓異常發育的分子發病機理，和在Six1-Eya1相關的BOR症候群中，腮弓缺陷下Hoxb3 和Jag1基因的相互作用。

777411.label: Realisation of objectives
777411.value: Objective 1. To investigate the second branchial arch (BA) defects and expression patterns of Hox and Notch signaling pathway genes in Six1 and Eya1 mouse mutants, in order to assess the roles of Hoxb3 and Jag1 in mediating BA abnormalities in BOR syndrome. We examined the phenotypes of Six1-/- and Eya1-/- mutant embryos. Six1-/- mutant had slightly reduced BA2, but Eya1-/- mutant had severely reduced BA2 and stronger phenotype. We examined several Hox genes and found that only Hoxb3 was specifically up-regulated in BA2 of Six1-/- mutants. In Six1-/-mutants, Jag1 was up-regulated in the endothelium of BA2. On the contrary, in Eya1-/-mutants, Jag1 expression was mostly lost. Therefore, we concluded that Six1 and Eya1 genes have common as well as distinctive roles during BA development. We have achieved Objective 1 as planned. Objective 2. To investigate the functions of Six1 and Eya1 as negative regulator of Hoxb3 by molecular and genetic approaches, in order to understand the Six1-Eya1 gene regulatory mechanism in BA development. By molecular approach, using in vitro ChIP and in ovo luciferase assays, we demonstrated that Six1 could function as a repressor of Hoxb3. By genetics approach, we crossed the Six1-/- mutant with the Hoxb3-/- mutant, and found that removal of Hoxb3 could restore the size of the BA2 of the Six1-/- mutant. Interestingly, we found that Eya1 not only function as a transcription cofactor of Six1, but also function independently as a phosphatase and contributed to more severe BA defects. We concluded that the Six1-independent function of Eya1 was mediated by Notch signaling. We have achieved Objective 2 as planned. Objective 3. To investigate the function and regulation of Jag1 in BA2 by molecular and transgenic mouse mutant analysis in order to elucidate the interaction of Hoxb3 and Jag1 in the molecular pathogenesis of BA abnormalities. By expression and molecular analyses of Hoxb3Tg mutants, we demonstrated that ectopic expression of Hoxb3 could lead to upregulation of Jag1 expression in the BA. Using a revised bioinformatics strategy, we identified novel Hoxb3 binding sites on the Jag1 gene. We performed in vivo ChIP assays using P19 cells and BA2 tissues extracted from Hoxb3Tg mutant embryos, and demonstrated that Hoxb3 could interact directly with the binding site on the Jag1 gene. Therefore, we concluded that the upregulation of Jag1 in the BA2 of Hoxb3Tg mutant embryos could be through direct Hoxb3 binding. We have achieved Objective 3 as planned.

777411.label: Major findings and research outcome
777411.value: The aim of this study is to elucidate the crosstalk of several key transcription factors (Hoxb3, Six1/Eya1) and signaling molecules (Jag1 and other Notch signaling factors) as well as the genetic interaction pathways underlying the disease mechanisms for human Branchio-Oto-Renal (BOR) syndrome, which is caused by mutations in SIX or EYA genes. We hypothesized that Hoxb3, Jag1 and other Notch signaling pathway members might function downstream of Six1 and Eya1 genes during the development of the second branchial arch (BA). In this project, we have addressed our working hypothesis and made several novel discoveries. Firstly, we have provided evidence that the Six1 and Eya1 genes have overlapping, but also distinct functions in the pathogenesis of the BOR syndrome. As transcription cofactors, Six1/Eya1 co-regulate downstream transcriptional target genes, including repression of Hoxb3, in the branchial arches. In the Six1 mutant, ectopic upregulation of Hoxb3 in the branchial region would lead to multiple branchial arch defects, as shown by our study of the Hoxb3Tg mutant mice (see manuscript by Wong et al.). This study provided a novel pathogenic mechanism for the craniofacial malformations in the BOR syndrome patients. Secondly, our investigations using the Hoxb3Tg transgenic mutant and our molecular studies have demonstrated that Hoxb3 could directly bind to a specific site on the genomic region of Jag1, thereby regulate Jag1 expression. The results based on our studies of the Hoxb3Tg mutant have been described in the manuscript entitled “Hoxb3 regulates Jag1 expression in mouse branchial arch during craniofacial development” by Wong et al. to be submitted to Scientific Reports for publication. Thirdly, we found that in addition to function as a transcription cofactor, Eya1 phosphatase activity is essential for the development of branchial epithelium and for branchial arch segmentation. We have discovered that phosphorylated Notch1 receptor intracellular domain (N1ICD) is a novel substrate for Eya1 phosphatase. We further demonstrated that de-phosphorylation of of N1ICD by Eya1 would stabilize N1ICD, leading to enhanced Notch signaling activity. The functions of Notch1 receptor and Jag1 in branchial arch development are previously unknown. Therefore, in this project, we have elucidated the functions of Eya1, and unraveled the contributions of signaling factors of the Notch pathway in branchial arch development. This results of part of the project have been described in a major manuscript “Eya1 modulates Notch signaling in branchial epithelium during mammalian craniofacial development” by Zhang et al. to be submitted to Developmental Cell for publication.

777411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
777411.value: One of our major discovery in this study is that Eya1 could function as a phosphatase, and that the Notch receptor (N1ICD) is a novel substrate of Eya1. We have shown that dephosphorylation of N1ICD by Eya1 could stabilize the Notch receptor protein. This finding opens up a novel possibility of modulating the strength of Notch signaling function in normal development and in disease conditions. Based on our discovery in this project, we applied and were awarded a new RGC GRF grant 2015/16 to further investigate the molecular functions of Eya1 and Notch signaling. (GRF 17113415 “The interactions of Eya1 and Notch signaling in the branchial epithelia during mammalian craniofacial development”) As Notch signaling is essential for multiple developmental and disease processes, the implication of our discovery that Eya1 phosphatase could modulate Notch signaling is profound. We will explore further applications of Eya1 and modulation of Notch signaling in tissue regeneration studies. We will expand our fund source to include applications to Healthcare and Medical Research Funds (HMRF) and Innovation and Technology Funds (ITF) for our future studies.

777411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
777411.value: Mutations of the Six1 or Eya1 genes lead to Branchio-Oto-Renal (BOR) syndrome in humans, patients display a range of craniofacial malformations due to abnormal branchial arch development during early embryogenesis. However, how Six1 and Eya1 interact with downstream genes and signaling factors in the developing branchial arches are not well understood. In this study, we have found that Six1 and Eya1 have overlapping as well as distinctive functions. The Six1 transcription factor negatively regulates the Hoxb3 gene, up-regulation of Hoxb3 could ectopically activate Jag1, and lead to a series of cellular defects in the branchial epithelia and neural crest cells in the developing second branchial arch. On the other hand, we have discovered that Eya1 has Six1-independent function in branchial arch development. As a phosphatase, Eya1 could de-phosphorylate the Notch1 intracellular domain (N1ICD) protein, thereby enhancing Notch signaling activity in the branchial epithelial cells. Our discovery of novel molecular mechanisms underlying Six1 and Eya1 functions have led to better understanding of the pathogenesis of BOR syndrome. We have demonstrated for the first time that Six1 and Eya1 are involved in modulating Notch signaling in the branchial arches. This study unravels new paradigms for tissue regeneration in human craniofacial malformations.

777511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
777511.value: Human genetics aims to characterize the DNA sequence variants that, together with environmental factors (including medical interventions), determine the occurrence, course and outcome of diseases. Knowledge of these sequence variants has the potential to offer individualized assessment of disease-risk and medical-response profiles. To date, hundreds of disease risk variants for complex diseases have been discovered by genome-wide association studies, and although these so far explain only a modest proportion of the population variation in disease susceptibility, it is certain that further progress will be made in the next few years. It is therefore timely to develop the statistical and computational analysis toold that will facilitate the translation of the new genetic knowledge for clinical use. The availability of such tools will accelerate the development of personalized medicine and has the potential to improve the health of the community. The proposed project aims to develop a methodology and a computer program for personal risk profiling of complex diseases, combining information on the individual’s genomic sequence, past history, epidemiological risk factors and family history. The proposed method for risk prediction is based on the well-established liability-threshold model of complex diseases, where the liability is determined by multiple genetic and environmental predictor variables. A convenient statistical framework is offered by assuming a multivariate normal distribution for all the variables, and the effect of conditioning of the predictor variables on liability to disease is calculated through repeated applications of the Pearson-Aitken formula. This statistical framework has many advantages, including flexibility in dealing with a large number of predictor variables, both in individual and family members. A computer program will be developed with Hirschsprung’s disease, systemic lupus erythematosis, and osteoporosis as examples of complex diseases. It is envisaged that the computer program will have the potential to be further developed into a platform for personal risk profiling in clinical practice. 人類遺傳學研究很重要的一個目標就是鑒定引起人類疾病的DNA序列變異，以及相關的環境因素（包括醫療干預等）。認識這些DNA序列變異的對我們評估個人疾病和醫療反應風險都很有幫助。迄今為止，全基因組關聯分析（Genome-wide association studies，GWAS）已經發現了成百上千的影響複雜疾病風險的DNA變異。雖然這些變異目前大體上還只能解釋人群中較小比例的疾病易感性差異，但可以肯定的是，隨著更多疾病易感DNA變異的不斷被發現，在未來的幾年裡他們總體能解釋的比例將會大大增加。因此，及時開發一些能充分利用這些DNA序列變異的知識來幫助指導臨床實踐的統計分析工具是目前一項很有必要的工作。這些工具的使用可以加速個體化醫療的發展，造福人類健康。 該專案旨在開發一個複雜疾病個人風險預測的方法和電腦程式，它能夠對DNA變異，個人病史，相關流行病學風險因素和家族史等多類資訊進行綜合評估。我們將會基於行內認可的複雜疾病傾向性閾值模型（Liability-threshold model）開發構建一個統計學疾病風險預測分析框架。在傾向性閾值模型中，一個人的患病傾向性由多個遺傳和環境預測變數決定。可以比較合理地假設這些變數服從多元正態分佈，在給定其他變數的條件下某個變數對患病傾向性的影響可以方便地通過Pearson-Aitken公式計算得之。該統計分析框架將會有靈活考慮個人和家庭的很多個預測變數等多項優點。我們將會以赫斯朋氏病(Hirschsprung's disease)， 紅斑狼瘡症(Systemic Lupus Erythematosus)，骨質疏鬆症(Osteoporosis)為參考案例，設計開發相應的疾病風險預測程式。該程式將來很有可能進一步發展成為應用於臨床實踐的個人患病風險預測軟體平臺。

777511.value: In this project we have developed a software tool that can incorporate multiple sources of information, including genetic information, to calculate the risk of future disease development in an individual. The calculated disease risks can have multiple uses, including the identification of individuals at high-risk of developing disease who may benefit from preventive measures or regular monitoring and early intervention.
