777611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
777611.value: Stroke is the leading cause of disability and the secondary killer in human diseases worldwide. Tissue-plasminogen activator (t-PA) is the only FDA-approved thrombolytic drug for acute ischemic stroke. Early recanalization after t-PA infusion can improve patient outcome. However, systemic thrombolysis with t-PA administered beyond the 3 hour therapeutic window after ischemic stroke carries a potential risk of hemorrhagic transformation and potentiates neuronal damage. The activation of matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), a proteolytic zinc-containing enzyme family, and the induction of blood brain barrier (BBB) hyper-permeability are critical pathological processes in hemorrhagic transformation during thrombolytic treatment for acute ischemic stroke. Rebuilding circulation by thrombolysis is accompanied by cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. Ischemia-reperfusion produces free radicals including reactive oxygen species (ROS) and reactive nitrogen species (RNS). As the major components of RNS, nitric oxide (NO) and peroxynitrite (ONOO-) can activate MMPs, attack tight junction-associated proteins and increase BBB permeability. Since RNS are simultaneously present in the t-PA-treated ischemic brains, it is important to address the questions whether the MMPs activations, the BBB disruption and hemorrhagic transformation are due to the actions of t-PA itself, RNS or the synergistic effects of RNS and t-PA, and how the MMPs activations and related molecular cascades are induced in the process. Our studies revealed that caveolin-1, a 22 kDa integral membrane protein, can inhibit RNS production, MMPs activations and BBB disruption, whereas over-production of NO from the ischemic brains can down-regulate caveolin-1, activate MMPs and increase BBB permeability. Several synthesized and natural RNS inhibitors revealed to inhibit the MMPs activations and reduce BBB permeability in an experimental ischemic stroke animal model with t-PA treatment. Following this line, we will test the hypothesis that the RNS inhibitors can up-regulate caveolin-1 expression, inhibit MMPs activations reduce BBB permeability, and prevent hemorrhagic transformation in t-PA treated ischemic stroke animal model. If the hypothesis can be validated, we logically expect that the antioxidant therapy for inhibiting RNS production can be used to reduce the risk of hemorrhagic transformation and extend the therapeutic time window of t-PA for acute ischemic stroke. Subsequently, the antioxidant therapy can be an add-on therapeutic strategy with t-PA treatment for acute ischemic stroke patients. As t-PA is the only thrombolytic drug clinically used for acute ischemic stroke patients and antioxidants are commonly used healthy supplements, the study will highlight their therapeutic value for stroke treatment. Therefore, the study will be highly innovative and has a multitude of application potentials. 中風是人類疾病的第二位殺手，t-PA是FDA批准的唯一溶栓劑，用於缺血性中風治療。早期溶栓能提高病人的治療效果，而中風3小時後的溶栓治療存在腦出血的危險性。研究表明，髓質金屬蛋白酶（MMP）的活化以及血腦屏障高通透性是溶栓治療腦出血的重要環節，同時溶栓以及重建血流供應可產生活性氧和活性氮自由基而造成腦缺血再灌注損傷。一氧化氮和過氧亞硝基是活性氮的重要組成部分，它們能活化MMP，攻擊緊密連接蛋白，增加血腦屏障通透性。由於t-PA和活性氮均能造成上述病理變化，因此，我們提出溶栓治療所致腦出血究竟是t-PA的直接作用的結果還是活性氮自由基所致的問題。我們的實驗證據顯示活性氮自由基清除劑能抑制t-PA引起的MMP的活化，減少血腦屏障通透性。因此，我們設計有關實驗以測試是否活性氮自由基清除劑能減少t-PA引起的血腦屏障破壞和腦出血的形成。如果該假說能成立，抗氧化治療就能作為t-PA溶栓治療的輔助療法，以減少溶栓併發症。由於t-PA是目前唯一的溶栓藥物，而抗氧化劑也是常用的保健品，本研究為抗氧化劑提供了新的治療方向。

777611.label: Realisation of objectives
777611.value: Objective 1. (1)We used mice brain microvascular endothelial cells (BMECs) and investigated the synergistic effect of tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) and RNS on cell death under oxygen and glucose deprivation (OGD) condition, which mimics cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in vitro. (2)We conducted in vivo animal experiments by using SD rat middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO)-induced cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury model. Using this model, we investigated the effect of early and delayed t-PA treatment on hemorrhagic transformation, 3-NT formation and MMPs activation. Then we tested the effect of FeTMPyP, a representative peroxynitrite decomposition catalyst, on hemorrhagic transformation, MMP-9/-2 activation and neurological function in ischemic stroke with delayed t-PA treatment. Objective 2. (1) We investigated the role of caveolin-1 in mediating MMP-9 activation, tight junction disruption and blood brain barrier (BBB) damage in SD rat MCAO model. We further compared the BBB damage in wild type and caveolin-1 knockout mice in MCAO model. (2) We investigated the role of caveolin-1 in regulating MMP-9 by caveolin-1 knockdown in cultured BMEC. (3) We tested the effect of NG-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester [L-NAME, a non-selective nitric oxide synthase (NOS) inhibitor] on caveolin-1 expression, MMP-9 activation, tight junctions’ expression and BBB damage in both wild type and caveolin-1 knockout mice. (4) We investigated Calycosin-7-O-β-D-glucoside, an isoflavones derived from AstragaliRadix. We evaluated its effect on nitric oxide/caveolin-1/matrix metalloproteinases pathway mediated BBB damage and brain injury in rat MCAO model. Objective 3 (1) We developed diarylamine-based fluorogenic probes for detection of peroxynitrite. (2) We investigated the direct scavenging effect of baicalin on peroxynitrite by using Mass spectroscopy. We further investigated the peroxynitrite scavenging effect of baicalin in human SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells under the challenges of 3-morpholinosydnonimine (SIN-1, a peroxynitrite donor). Finally, we investigated the effects of baicalin on 3-nitrotyrosine formation in rat MCAO brains. (3) We studied the effects of baicalin on reducing neurotoxicity induced by peroxynitrite. We further investigated baicalin’s effect on brain infarct volume and neuronal apoptosis in rat MCAO model. (4) We investigated the effect of baicalin on attenuating hemorrhagic transformation, improving neurological outcome, reducing mortality rate, inhibiting MMP-9 activation, and preserving tight junction ZO-1expression in rat MCAO model with delayed t-PA treatment. (5) We investigated Sodium Danshensu (SDSS), a representative active compound from salvia miltiorrhiza. We evaluated the potential effects of SDSS on scavenging peroxynitrite (ONOO-) and protecting neuronal cells from ischemia reperfusion injury in human SH-SY5Y cells in vitro and MCAO model in vivo.

777611.label: Major findings and research outcome
777611.value: 1. We developed a highly sensitive probe for peroxynitrite detection in vitro and in vivo In this study, we developed diarylamine-based fluorogenic probes for detection of peroxynitrite which only generate fluorescence in presence of peroxynitrite without cross-reaction with other free radicals like hydroxyl radical. The results have been published in J Am Chem Soc, 136(33), 11728-11734. 2. Peroxynitrite plays an important role in mediating delayed tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) treatment induced hemorrhagic transformation (HT) in ischemic brains via regulating MMPs activation The study proves that early t-PA reduces 3-NT (a peroxynitrite biomarker) formation, while delayed t-PA treatment exacerbates 3-NT formation in ischemic brains and induces HT. FeTMPyP, a representative peroxynitrite decomposition catalyst, significantly reduces HT via inhibiting MMP-9/-2 activation. These results have been published in CNS Neurosci Ther 21(7):585-590, 2015. 3. Caveolin-1 plays an important role in mediating blood brain barrier damage in ischemic stroke via regulating MMPs activity We found that caveolin-1 was down regulated in ischemic stroke, leading to activation of MMPs, disruption of tight junction ZO-1 and subsequently BBB damage. L-LAME treatment partially restored the expression of caveolin-1 and down regulated MMP-9 activity, preserved tight junction ZO-1, thus protected blood brain barrier. These results have been published in J Neurochem. 120(1):4-6, 2012. 4. Calycosin-7-O-β-D-glucoside regulates nitric oxide/caveolin-1/matrix metalloproteinases pathway and reduced BBB damage in ischemic stroke The study found that Calycosin-7-O-β-D-glucoside inhibited nitric oxide, secured expression of caveolin-1 and inhibited MMP-9/-2 activity in rat MCAO model and in cultured BMECs, hence, reduced brain infarct volume and BBB damage in vivo and attenuated BMECs death in vitro. These results have been published in J Ethnopharmacol, 155(1), 692-701, 2014. 5. Baicalin could directly scavenge peroxynitrite and reduce neuronal apoptosis in ischemic stroke The study found that baicalin, a flavonoid compound isolated from Scutellaria baicalensis G, could directly scavenge peroxynitrite in vivo and in vitro. Moreover, baicalin attenuated peroxynitrite induced neurotoxicity in vitro and reduced the brain infarct volume in vivo. These results have been published in Journal of Ethnopharmacology 150(1):116-124, 2013. 6. Baicalin co-treatment significantly reduced hemorrhagic transformation induced by delayed t-PA treatment in ischemic stroke, via inhibiting peroxynitrite mediated MMP-9 activation The study found that baicalin co-treatment with t-PA significantly attenuated HT, ameliorated brain edema, reduced mortality rate, and improved the neurological outcomes. Moreover, baicalin co-treatment reduced 3-NT formation, attenuated MMP-9 activation and preserved ZO-1 expression in ischemic brains with delayed t-PA treatment. The manuscript is in preparation.

777611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
777611.value: Based on the achievements of our studies, we expect following potential directions for further studies: (1) To further explore the molecular mechanism of how t-PA reduced or exacerbated 3-NT formation at different treatment time points in ischemic stroke model; (2) To compared the effect of baicalin with baicalein on attenuating hemorrhagic transformation induced by delayed t-PA treatment in ischemic stroke; (3) To investigate the potential roles of peroxynitrite in mediating hyperglycemia induced hemorrhagic transformation in ischemic stroke. Due to the limitation of funding and research period, we could not achieve the goals. We plan to seek for more funds from RGC GRF grants or other funding sources to continue our studies in this direction.

777611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
777611.value: Stroke is a leading cause of disability in human diseases and is one of the major disease burdens worldwide. Tissue plasminogen activator is the only FDA approved agent for acute ischemic stroke treatment, with limited time window of 4.5 hours. Treatment beyond the time window significantly induces hemorrhagic transformation (HT), which is a severe complication resulting in worsened outcomes. Thus, developing approaches to reduce HT is timely important. With the support of RGC GRF grant, we conducted a series of experiments to test our hypothesis that peroxynitrite plays an important role in mediating hemorrhagic transformation induced by delayed t-PA treatment in ischemic stroke. We demonstrate that peroxynitrite is increased in ischemic brains by delayed t-PA treatment and scavenging peroxynitrite significantly reduces hemorrhagic transformation. Caveolin-1 may be the downstream of peroxynitrite, and mediated blood brain barrier (BBB) damage in ischemic stroke. Baicalin is a natural compound isolated from Traditional Chinese Medicine. Baicalin directly scavenges peroxynitrite, significantly reduces hemorrhagic transformation and improves the overall outcomes. Therefore, peroxynitrite is an important target for reducing hemorrhagic transformation in ischemic stroke with delayed t-PA treatment. This project yields 7 original articles, 2 articles in preparation, 6 review articles and trained 5 postgraduate students.

777911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
777911.value: The present study targets roles attributable to neuronal proheparanase in synaptic plasticity. We were among the first to report expression of heparanase in neurons of the spinal cord and brain regions including the hippocampus. With the hippocampus as our model, our preliminary study found neuronal secretion of proheparanase, not heparanase and that proheparanase binding at the neuronal surface mediated uptake of ionotropic glutamate receptor clusters that are important for synaptic transmission. The present study aims firstly to consolidate the findings with (i) identification of proheparanase binding sites on the neuronal surface as key components that target ionotropic glutamate receptor clusters for endocytosis and (ii) documentation of whether neuronal expression, secretion or endocytosis of proheparanase is activity-dependent. Secondly, we aim to find key conditions by which neuronal proheparanase-mediated endocytosis of ionotropic glutamate receptor impacts synaptic plasticity in the context of synaptic scaling for homeostasis. Because endocytosis of ionotropic glutamate receptor is known to affect spatial memory, we aim also to use the Morris water maze task to test for the effect of proheparanase on spatial memory consolidation/ retrieval. This work not only promises new knowledge on proheparanase as a mediator of synaptic plasticity, but also adds significance to synaptic/ peri-synpatic heparan sulfate moieties of proteoglycans as a major player in proheparanase-mediated synaptic plasticity. 本研究的目標是要找出神經細胞分泌之乙酰肝素酶原對於突觸可塑性之影響。我們領先發表中樞神經系统內的細胞表達並存有乙酰肝素酶。我們初步發現分泌自海馬神經細胞的乙酰肝素酶原，綁定於細胞表面某受體以誘動其集群式內吞，從而使神經細胞表面的谷氨酸受體下調，並改變突觸傳遞及其可塑性。為進深探索此課題，我們擬首先找出 (i)乙酰肝素酶原受體，並其對神經細胞集群式內吞作用之影響，以及對谷氨酸受體下調的作用; (ii) 神經細胞表達、分泌、回吞乙酰肝素酶原是否因應神經細胞的活動程度而產生相關的調節。另外，我們擬辨明乙酰肝素酶原引動神經細胞內吞谷氨酸受體之關鍵因素，從而影響突觸的缩放及神經通路的動態平衡。既然內吞谷氨酸受體已知可影響空間記憶，我們擬利用水迷宮測試乙酰肝素酶原對鞏固或回取空間記憶之影響。除此等新知識外，本研究结果意味觸突周邊蛋白多糖的硫酸乙酰肝素基團對於調控突觸可塑性扮演着一主要角色。

779611.label: Realisation of objectives
779611.value: The project objectives have been fully achieved by applying cell culture and molecular techniques as well as animal models of diabetic nephropathy. The details are presented in section 6.1 and the research output list are detailed in Part C. The kallikrein-kinin system (KKS) has been linked to cellular inflammatory process in many diseases, but has been under-studied in diabetic nephropathy. We filled this gap in by performing related investigations. First, Tissue kallikrein (KLK1) expression is up-regulated in human diabetic kidney tissue and induced by high glucose (HG) in human proximal tubular epithelial cells (PTEC). Recombinant KLK1 stimulated the production of inflammatory cytokines in PTEC via the activation of numerous intracellular signaling pathways and also the expression of protease-activated receptors (PARs). Most notable, activation of PAR-4 by a selective agonist was found to elicit the pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic phenotypes in PTEC while blockade of the receptor by specific antagonist attenuated high glucose-induced IL-6, CCL-2, CTGF and collagen IV expression. Calcium mobilization by the PAR-4 agonist in PTEC was desensitized by pretreatment with KLK1.These findings suggest that PTEC in close proximity to endothelial cells could affect vascular leakage and inflammation via PAR activation, and the findings were reported in PloS One. Next, the KKS related molecule kallistatin is a serine protease inhibitor with anti-inflammatory, anti-angiogenic and anti-oxidative properties. We performed more advanced gene transfer experiments utilizing ultrasound-microbubble-mediated techniques to confirm that indeed overexpression of renal kallistatin conferred renoprotective effects in the diabetic kidney via a novel AGE-RAGE-ROS axis. Such findings were just published in Nov 2015 in a high-impact nephrology journal (Kidney International).

779611.label: Major findings and research outcome
779611.value: The kallikrein-kinin system (KKS) mediates the inflammatory process during the development of diabetic nephropathy (DN). Recombinant KLK1 stimulated the production of inflammatory cytokines in PTEC via p42/44 and p38 MAPK signaling. Molecular knockdown of endogenous KLK1 in PTEC attenuated advanced glycation end-products (AGE)-induced IL-8 and ICAM-1 productions in vitro. Exposure of PTEC to KLK1 induced the expression of protease-activated receptors (PARs). Activation of PAR-4 elicited the pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic phenotypes in PTEC. There was a markedly up-regulation of tubular PAR-4 expression in human diabetic renal cortical tissues (Output 1). Kallistatin, a related molecule of the KKS, is a serine protease inhibitor with anti-inflammatory, anti-angiogenic and anti-oxidative properties. Using ultrasound-microbubble-mediated gene transfer in db/db mice, kallistatin overexpression reduced serum creatinine and BUN levels, ameliorated glomerulosclerosis and tubulointerstitial injury, attenuated renal fibrosis by inhibiting TGF-β signaling and the downstream PAI-1 and Col I and IV expression and partially suppressed renal inflammation via inhibiting NF-κB signaling and decreasing tissue kallikrein activity. Kallistatin attenuated oxidative stress as evidenced by suppressed levels of oxidative markers in diabetic renal tissue. Kallistatin inhibited expression of RAGE in both the diabetic kidney and AGE-stimulated cultured proximal tubular cells, reduced AGE-induced ROS generation, reflecting an anti-oxidative mechanism via the AGE-RAGE-ROS axis (Output 2). In the kidney, toll-like receptors (TLRs) are widely expressed in a variety of cell types. Emerging evidence demonstrates the participation of TLRs in the activation of these cells during renal fibrosis. TLRs and their endogenous ligands participate in the pathogenesis of renal fibrosis as observed in ureteral obstruction and diabetic nephropathy as models of chronic kidney disease (Output 3). Four recently described cellular receptors mediate DN. Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor- attenuates STAT-1 activation and has shown promise in renoprotection. The bradykinin receptor 2 of the KKS mediates DN and its blockade conferred renoprotective effects in animal models. The related protease activated receptor, especially receptor 4, participate in DN. Finally, TLR4 and TLR2 play a significant sensor of and reactor to hyperglycemia and other diabetic substrates that orchestrate interstitial inflammation in DN (Output 4). One major barrier for developing a more effective therapeutic protocol is our incomplete understanding of the processes determining DN progression, as reflected by a paucity of successful treatment and tribulations encountered in various once-promising clinical trials (Output 5). The results from our work shed light on some of the novel molecular culprits of DN to drive further drug discoveries.

779611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
779611.value: Together, the results generated from this project suggest that tampering the KKS, an under-investigated area in kidney disease, is worthy of further pursuit. Indeed, up-regulation of KLK1 in tubular epithelial cells may mediate pro-inflammatory pathway and PAR activation during diabetic nephropathy and this observation provides a new therapeutic target for further investigation. This has laid a foundation for further research into the role of PAR in diabetic nephropathy and we will formulate this for application of another competitive research grant in 2016. In addition, as oxidative stress plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of diabetic nephropathy (DN), we investigated the effect and mechanisms of action of kallistatin superinduction and showed a renoprotective role of kallistatin against DN via multiple mechanisms including suppression of oxidative stress, anti-fibrotic and anti-inflammatory actions leading to reduced TGF-β and NFκB signaling, respectively, and finally blood pressure lowering. These results lay a solid foundation for studying other biologic aspects of kallistatin in the realm of chronic kidney disease and we have already submitted another GRF application on this area for 2015/16 exercise.

779611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
779611.value: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is the major cause of chronic kidney disease (CKD), rising from being the 36th commonest cause of death worldwide in 1990 to the 19th position in 2013. This speed was second only to that of HIV/AIDS. Modern diabetes management including avid blockade of the renin-angiotensin system, and stringent control of blood glucose, blood pressure, and lipids, have only achieved limited success in retarding the progression of DN to end-stage renal disease (ESRD). To date, DN remains the number one cause of ESRD in Hong Kong and other developed countries, accounting for 48% of all new patients requiring dialysis every year. In other parts of the world, the figure is around 40 – 60%. The results from our work shed light on novel molecular culprits, namely high glucose, glycated proteins, and novel pathways such as the kallikrein-kinin system and Toll-like receptor signaling, among many others that may be activated by diabetes to cause injurious signals in the kidney. Such findings open the door for the development of new therapeutic targets to retard or even halt the progression of DN to ESRD, and thus have the potential of saving millions of diabetic patients worldwide from having to undergo dialysis.

780511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
780511.value: Many halogenated compounds were synthesised for various human activities. These include pesticides, organic solvents and fire retardants. Others were generated accidentally, for example, during the disinfection of water and as intermediate reagents for manufacturing purposes. In general, halogenated compounds are resistant to complete mineralization due to the stability of carbon-halogen bond and many ended up as haloacids. Monochloroacetate (MCA) is an example and is mutagenic and abundant in the environment. Microorganisms are responsible for the bioremediation of these man-made chemicals. A bacterium, Burkholderia caribensis MBA4, was isolated from soil on its ability to degrade haloacids. This bacterium produced an enzyme, dehalogenase, which cleaves the carbon-halogen bond and renders the transformed products utilisable. Previous works had been concentrated on the purification and characterization of the enzyme. Recent works are focused on the genetics of the degradation process. The production of the dehalogenase is regulated. The enzyme was only found in cells grown in medium containing haloacids. Since MCA is toxic and affects the general metabolic pathway it was hypothesised that the degradation was similar to detoxification and subject to simple positive or negative regulation mediated by a regulatory protein. In order to identify the regulatory protein gene a transposon mutagenesis approach was used. While genes involved in various biosynthetic and regulatory pathways were identified to affect the expression of the dehalogenase the targeted regulatory gene is still under search. Preliminary characterisation of the promoter has also identified features of house-keeping genes. In order to understand the response of the cell it deems necessary to use a holistic approach. A proteomic analysis was used to identify differentially expressed proteins in cells degrading various haloacids. It was found that different expression patterns were observed in cells degrading different types of haloacids. However, due to the lack of a genomic sequence, the identities of many of these differentially expressed proteins were not established. In this proposal I would like to utilise a high-throughput sequencing method to investigate the responses of the MBA4 cell to degradation of various haloacids. A complete genomic sequence will be achieved and annotated. Total RNA will be isolated from cells growing in various substrates and the expressed genes examined quantitatively. The information obtained will be able to show the adaptability of the microbe to environments containing various haloacids. 780511.label: Realisation of objectives
780511.value: All the objectives have been attempted and generally achieved. The most difficult part was the acquisition of the complete genome sequence of the bacterium. With a relatively high GC content and presence of many repetitive sequences, the use of short reads sequencing platform failed to materialize the assembly of a complete genome even when the coverage was well over 500x. In order to help assemble and complete the genomic sequence of Burkholderia caribensis MBA4, additional approaches were adopted. Data from transcriptomic analysis were also used to help connect adjacent contigs into scaffolds. Genomic sequence of a type-strain, MWAP64, was also considered in order to enhance the chance of joining adjacent contigs into scaffold by means genomic similarity. Long read sequencing platforms were also employed. The completed sequence was ultimately achieved with a coverage of 850x and deposited to GenBank and DOE Joint Genome Institute for public access. Objectives 2 and 3 were to identify up- and down-regulated genes in degradation of haloacetate and halo-propionate. The lack of a completed sequence has hindered the initial progress of the project in analyzing the gene expression profiles of the bacterium in various carbon sources. Nonetheless, cells were grown in pyruvate, glycolate, chloroacetate, lactate or bromopropionate and RNA-seq data were obtained. Two biological samples were considered in order to evaluate the reproducibility of the analyses. A commercial software CLC-Bio Genomic Workbench was used to determine the Reads Per Kilobase per Million mapped reads (RPKM) value of each gene and Kal’s Z-test was used to calculate the significance of the differences between a pair of data. Previous analyses using proteomic approach have only identified a handful of differentially expressed proteins. The use of transcriptome analysis has achieved similar outcome plus identification of many more differentially expressed genes. This is mainly due to the higher sensitivity of RNA-seq technology and to the limitation of proteomic analysis for membrane proteins which are generally existed in insoluble fraction and in small quantities. The transcriptome data has confirmed the differential expression of the dehalogenase and associated permease and discovery of at least two membrane proteins that were highly expressed in haloacid-grown cells. Reverse-transcription quantitative PCR was utilized to confirm the expression levels of some of the genes. The genes for the two inducible membrane proteins are organized as an operon and located next to a glycolate oxidase operon which is haloacetate-inducible. Comparative genomic analysis with the type-strain MWAP64 revealed the clustering of these haloacid-inducible genes of MBA4 in a genomic island that is likely to be originated from horizontal transfer. Incidentally, the haloacid operon is also located in this region. Hierarchical cluster analysis was used to group the genes according to their differential expression levels in the various growth conditions. Pathway Tools version 19.5 was used to exploit the biochemical relationship of these gene products that exhibit similar responses. In summary, the four objectives of the proposed project have been achieved and have confirmed certain unique properties of the haloacid-degrading bacterium MBA4. The identification of specific haloacid-induced genes and/or operons in MBA4 and not in the type-strain established that it is a well-adapted bacterium that specialized in degradation of haloacid. Further characterization of the regulatory system and corresponding regulatory protein(s) would reveal the first notification of haloacid-bound DNA-binding proteins.

780511.label: Major findings and research outcome
780511.value: Determination of the genomic sequence of Burkholderia caribensis MBA4 shows that it has 9.4 Mb bases and encode for more than nine thousand genes. Its GC content is 62.5%. The assembly, however, was found difficult because of the presence of many repetitive sequences. The completely assembled genome (Pan et al., 2015 SIGS) consists of three replicons: CP012746, CP012747 and CP012748. The first two are treated as chromosome while the last one is treated as a mega-plasmid. The genome of the type-strain MWAP64 (Pan et al., 2016 GenoA) consists of two chromosomes: CP013102 and CP013103 and two plasmids: CP013104 and CP013105. Its size is 9 Mb with a GC content of 62.6% and encodes for less than eight thousand genes. Comparative analysis shows that MBA4 contains one more glycolate oxidase operon (glc) in chromosome CP012747 where the haloacid operon that mediates the degradation of haloacid is located. In this extra glc operon, genes for glycolate oxidase and malate synthase G are grouped together. Pathway Tools analysis showed that these genes are used for metabolism of glycolate to glyoxylate and to malate which is an intermediate molecule in the di- and tri-carboxylic acid cycles. Since monochloroacetate will be dehalogenated to glycolate, the expressions of this operon for cells grown on chloroacetate and glycolate were expected to be similar. Transcriptome analysis revealed that this glc operon was turned-on only in the presence of chloroacetate and not in glycolate. Another glc operon, identified in plasmid CP012748, was found to be expressed for cells grown on glycolate or chloroacetate but not on pyruvate. Other genes in the glycerate pathway required for metabolism of glyoxylate were also induced in the presence of chloroacetate or glycolate. The overall result is that enzymes required for metabolism of glycolate will be produced when it is present, either administered directly or through dehalogenation of haloacetate. The uniqueness is the glc operon with a malate synthase G gene that is not found in the type-strain was induced by chloroacetate and not by glycolate. Previous studies showed that the expression of bacterial glc operon is regulated by GntR-like transcriptional activator GlcC. A gene encoding for a putative GlcC was indeed found immediately upstream of the unique glc operon in MBA4. Preliminary results showed the binding of this putative GlcC upstream of the glc operon when haloacetate was present. This is the first report of such a haloacetate-responsive regulatory protein.

780511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
780511.value: The use of next-generation sequencing technique enables the collective analysis of the responses of a cell in different environment. The identification of a chloroacetate-binding regulatory activator has demonstrate the versatility of the bacterium in degradation of haloacid. Since this is the first report of such type of DNA-binding protein, it will be worth characterizing this transcriptional regulator. The gene encoding for this GlcC-like protein can be cloned and expressed in E. coli with an aim to obtain purified protein for structural and functional analysis. Purified recombinant protein can be used for bandshift assay to confirm its binding to upstream noncoding region of the haloacetate-inducible glc operon. DNase I footprinting could also be used to locate the exact binding site. Isothermal calorimetry can also be used to confirm the interaction of the regulator with haloacetate and not with glycolate. Site-directed or saturated mutagenesis can then be used to reveal the domains required for DNA- and substrate-binding of the protein.

780511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
780511.value: Next-generation sequencing technique was used to determine the genome of a haloacid-degrading bacterium, Burkholderia caribensis MBA4. It belongs to a genus of microbes including animal and plant pathogens, plant-growth promoting species and xenobiotics degraders that can be found in various niches. Comparative analysis has verify the plasticity of the genomes of members of this genus. Transcriptome analysis of MBA4 illustrated that its ability to metabolize haloacid relied on its acquisition of a genomic island that produced a series of enzymes that ensure the transformation of the putatively toxic haloacid to commonly metabolizable substrate. Genes encoding for dehalogenase, haloacid-uptake proteins, glycolate oxidase, malate synthase G and cytochrome oxidase in electron transport system were specifically induced in the presence of chloroacetate. The production of an array of putative transcriptional regulators was also found to be enhanced in the presence of haloacid. In particular a GlcC-like transcriptional activator was found to regulate the expression of a glycolate oxidase operon only in the presence of chloroacetate and not with glycolate. This illustrate the specificity of a DNA-binding protein that would interact with halogenated substrate. This is the first report of such a type of regulatory protein.

780911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
780911.value: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a common cancer among Cantonese populations living in Hong Kong and southern regions of China. It is closely associated with Epstein-Barr virus infection. EBV infection is considered a major etiological factor of NPC. Although EBV infection is commonly detected in NPC, EBV infection in normal nasopharyngeal epithelium is uncommon. In vitro, EBV readily infects and transforms B lymphocytes into lymphoblastoid cell lines. However, in vitro infection of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells often induces cell cycle arrest and cellular senescence phenotype. EBV-infected nasopharyngeal epithelial cells are readily lost in culture and difficult to propagate. The current concept of NPC pathogenesis postulates that genetic alterations in premalignant nasopharyngeal epithelial cells confer susceptibility to EBV infection. EBV infection drives the malignant transformation of premalignant nasopharyngeal epithelial cells into cancer cells. Hence, establishment of persistent infection of EBV represents an early and critical step in NPC development. Our laboratories have been involved in the establishment of premalignant nasopharyngeal epithelial cell systems for EBV infection study. Our preliminary observations show that overexpression of cyclin D1, a common event in NPC, may represent an important event to support persistent EBV infection in premalignant nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. We observed that cyclin D1 overexpression facilitates telomerase mediated immortalization of primary nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Interestingly, cyclin D1 overexpression also supports EBV infection in immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells and the propagation of EBV-infected cells. EBV infection commonly induces cellular senescence in telomerase-immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. DNA damage repair (DDR) response has been shown to induce cell cycle arrest and senescence. Cyclin D1 is involved in the activation of Cdk4 to promote cell cycle progression. DNA damage signaling response has been reported to degrade cyclin D1 and arrest cell cycle progression. EBV infection and expression of EBV genes could induce DDR response. Cyclin D1 over-expression in nasopharyngeal epithelial cells may by pass the cell cycle arrest and senescence induced by EBV infection to support persistent infection of EBV. In this proposal, we will use our immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cell system to define the role of cyclin D1 in supporting persistent EBV infection in premalignant nasopharyngeal epithelial cell models. EBV infection of premalignant nasopharyngeal cells represents an early and crucial step in NPC pathogenesis. Defining the events which facilitate persistent EBV infection in nasopharyngeal epithelial cells will contribute to the understanding of pathogenesis of NPC. 細胞週期蛋白D1在癌前鼻咽上皮細胞感染EBV病毒的的作用。 摘要 鼻咽癌（NPC）是中國南部地區(包括香港)常見的癌症。它和EB病毒感染關係非常密切。 EB病毒感染被認為是鼻咽癌的其中一個主要成因。EB病毒很容易在體外感染B淋巴細胞。相反地，EB病毒在體外感染鼻咽上皮細胞 的效率非常低。被EB病毒感染的鼻咽上皮細胞無法長期傳代, 病毒亦容易丟失。目前鼻咽癌發病機制的概念是，癌前鼻咽癌上皮細胞發生基因變異令鼻咽癌上皮細胞可以被EB病毒感染。 EB病毒感染了鼻咽癌癌前上皮細胞之後, 透過病毒感基因的表達, 誘發癌前鼻咽上皮細胞其他變化，最終將癌前鼻咽癌上皮細胞轉化成癌細胞。因此，EB病毒的持續感染是早期鼻咽癌的發病機制重要的一步。我們的實驗室對 EB病毒感染鼻咽上皮細胞進行了長期研究，以了解EB病毒感染在鼻咽癌發病病理的作用。我們的初步觀察表明，細胞週期蛋白D1的高表達可能在支持在鼻咽上皮細胞癌前EB病毒持續感染有重要的作用。我們觀察到細胞週期蛋白D1與 端粒酶結合, 可以有效地把原代培養的鼻咽上皮細胞變變成永生細胞。此外，我們觀察到高表達細胞週期蛋白D1可以支持被EB病毒感染的永生化鼻咽上皮細胞的長期體外傳代。我們還觀察到EB病毒感染可以抑制DNA的損傷反應信號。細胞週期蛋白D1通過活化CDK4，促進細胞週期分裂。細胞週期蛋白D1在鼻咽癌上皮細胞的高表達可能抑制EB病毒感染引起的細胞衰老和抑制細胞週期的信息傳遞，支持EB病毒在體外感染鼻咽上皮細胞的長期持續感染。在此研究建議，我們會用我們建立的永生鼻咽上皮細胞系統來研究支持EB病毒感染的持久性的機制，這將增加我們對鼻咽癌癌變的認識。

780911.label: Realisation of objectives
780911.value: Little is known on the regulation of latent and lytic infection of EBV in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). The contribution of latent and lytic EBV infection to the pathogenesis of NPC remains poorly understood. It has been difficult to establish stable EBV infection in normal nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Using immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cell models established in our laboratory, we have able to address some of these important issues relating to persistent EBV infection in NPC. In this study, we have addressed an important issue in NPC pathogenes - If genetic alterations, such as cyclin D1 over expression, may support stable EBV infection in premalignant nasopharyngeal epithelial. First of all, we demonstrated that cyclin D1 over expression is common in premalignant nasopharyngeal epithelium in clinical specimens and is closely associated with EBV infection as visualized by the expression of EBER (EBV-encoded RNA). Then we examined if over expression of cyclin D1 may support persistence infection of EBV. Using telomerase-immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells, we observed that EBV infection readily induced senescence and cell cycle arrest in infected nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Over-expression of cyclin D1 suppressed cellular senescence and overcome cell cycle arrest to support stable EBV infection in nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Futhermore, stable EBV infected cell lines were established in immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells using FACS (fluorescence activated cell sorting) to sort out EBV-infected cells. The EBV used in this study was tagged with a GFP expressing gene which allow identification and sorting of EBV-infected nasopharyngeal epithelial cells for long-term propagation. We then explored the mechanisms involved by cyclin D1 to support EBV infection. Cyclin D1 over-expression suppressed differentiation induction by serum. Cyclin D1 overexpressing nasopharyngeal epithelial cells could be grown in serum- supplemented medium which normally will induce terminal differentiation of immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Furthermore, cyclin D1 overexpression induced resistance to induction of cellular senescence after H2O2 treatment and DNA damage. Examination of EBV gene expression revealed stable expression of latent EBV genes including EBNA1, EBER and LMP1. Expression of lytic EBV genes was suppressed in EBV stably infected nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Most of the objectives proposed in this study have been achieved. The key findings of this study has been accepted for publication in PNAS and its implications are elaborated in several invited reviews.

780911.label: Major findings and research outcome
780911.value: Our key findings demonstrated that genetic alterations e.g. cyclin D1 expression, p16 inactivation or cdk4 activation, in premalignant nasopharyngeal epithelial cells support latent infection of EBV which has long been postulated as an early event in pathogenesis of nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Over-expression of cyclin D1 over-rides many growth arrest effects induced by EBV infection of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Among the EBV stably infected nasopharyngeal epithelial cells, we were able to detected expression of latent genes including the viral microRNA which may play essential role to the malignant transformation of the precancerous lesion of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Furthermore, our study has also established multiple cell models of EBV infection to study regulation of latent and lytic infection of EBV in nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. We have investigated the effects of over expression of cyclin D1 in nasopharyngeal epithelial cells and showed that cylcin D1 expression inhibited terminal differentiation of squamous epithelial cells which may explain the close association of EBV infection with undifferentiated NPC. The results from this study has been published in PNAS in November 2012. The implication of findings of this study in nasopharyngeal carcinoma has been further elaborated in the invited review manuscripts attached (Seminar in Cancer Biology 2012, Oral Oncology 2014, J. Pathology 2015).

780911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
780911.value: The ability to establish stable EBV infection in vitro has provided investigation cell models to study regulation of latent and lytic infection. The regulation of EBV gene expression in latently infected cells is poorly understood. The EBV-infected cell system established in this study enable investigators to study how tumor microenvironment may regulate the expression of latent and lytic EBV genes. In particular, the expression of EBV micorRNA has been shown to be expressed at high levels in nasopharynegeal carcinoma. Our EBV-infected cell lines could be used to study the effects of host cell signaling factors and inflammatory cytokines present in tumor stroma on regulation of micro RNA expression. The differential gene expression on nasopharyngeal epithelial cells upon latent infection of EBV is now under active pursue in our laboratory using high throughput cDNA microarray and RNA seq investigation to deduce alteration of signaling pathways in EBV infected cells. All these will contribute to the understanding of role of EBV infection in the development of nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

780911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
780911.value: The role of EBV infection in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is poorly understood. EBV infection of epithelial cells exhibits a specific viral gene expression profile referred as Latency Type II. Latent type II infection of EBV is associated with epithelial malignancies and Hogkin's disease. The lack of EBV-infected nasopharyngeal epithelial cell system has hampered research investigation to understand the role of EBV infection in NPC. EBV infection in normal epithelial cells is predominantly lytic in nature. The ability of EBV to establish latent infection represent a major switch of host/virus relationship. Expression of latent EBV such as LMP1 and LMP2 has long been postulated to have oncogenic properties. The recent identification of EBV-encoded miRNA is believed to play an important role to promote growth of epithelial cancer in vivo. The identification of cyclin D1 over-expression to support stable and latent EBV infection has contributed to the understanding of the pathogenic role of EBV in NPC carcinogenesis. Our study has also provided researchers a relevant EBV-infection cell model to study the biology and pathological role of EBV in human diseases.

781111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
781111.value: 经皮冠脉介入再灌注治疗以及血管紧张素酶抑制剂联合β受体阻滞剂的应用可以有效治疗心梗后心肌， 但是仍然会有高达30%的患者会逐渐恶化成心力衰竭。越来越多的急性心肌梗死的幸存者导致心衰的发病率及病死率在全球范围不断攀升。据估计，全世界有超过一千五百万心衰患者，其中大部分由冠状动脉病变进展而来。心衰的患病率每十年将会翻一番。渐进性的左心室膨胀，偏心性肥厚以及梗死瘢痕导致的室壁薄弱引发左室几何结构发生改变。 日益恶化的左室重构致使心衰加剧，所以心肌梗死后的患者临床表现也随之每况愈下。 心衰患者中，自主神经功能失调受到关注，其表现为交感神经亢奋，迷走神经受到抑制，从而致使心衰严重，病死率升高。了解了中枢交感神经兴奋在心衰进展中的作用后，β受体阻滞剂被用来针对抑制交感神经系统而在临床广泛应用。β受体阻滞剂的单一处方就可以降低35%的死亡率。然而临床上没有能直接提高副交感神经功能的药物。所以，临床迫切需要一种独特的治疗方法，它能通过调节自主神经系统，恢复交感神经和副交感神经系统之间的平衡， 从而减轻临床症状。 近来的对缺血性心衰的动物实验表明，通过对高位胸部脊髓的电刺激，能直接调节分布到心脏的自主神经， 不但可以有效地阻止恶性室性心律失常， 还能提高左心功能。通过安装可植入性的神经刺激仪的脊髓神经电刺激疗法已经被广泛应用于缓解顽固性心绞痛的临床症状以及慢性疼痛综合征。然而，该疗法针对于心衰的治疗效果尚没有定论。所以我们将在与临床密切相关的大型动物模型上，开展针对脊髓刺激疗法相对于短期的血液动力学影响，长期的心脏功能改变以及左室重构方面的研究。此外, 我们也将深入探讨脊髓电刺激疗法在改善心肌重构和提升心脏功能的可能的潜在的机制。本项研究对洞悉新兴的非药物治疗方法--脊髓电刺激疗法在心梗后心衰改善重构，提升心肌功能领域，提供重要的依据和经验。

781111.label: Realisation of objectives
781111.value: To address Objective 1, we performed thoracic SCS (T1-T2 level) followed by 4 weeks of rapid ventricular pacing in 9 adult pigs with ischemic heart failure (HF) induced by myocardial infarction (MI). Echocardiogram revealed significant decrease in LVEF (33.8+/-1.8% vs. 66.5+/-1.7%, P<0.01) after induction of MI+HF. Compared with MI+HF, acute SCS significantly increased LVEF and +dP/dt (all P<0.05). Withdrawal of SCS during recovery decreased +dP/dt, but not LVEF that increased again with repeated SCS. Myocardial oxygen consumption also significantly decreased during SCS compared with MI+HF (P=0.006) without any change in serum norepinephrine level (P=0.9). These findings suggest that acute SCS improved global and regional LV contractile function and intraventricular dyssynchrony, and decreased myocardial oxygen consumption without elevation of norepinephrine level in a porcine model of ischemic HF. To address Objective 2, we performed chronic thoracic SCS at T1-T2 level (50Hz frequency, pulse width 0.2ms) in 30 adult pigs with ischemic HF induced by myocardial infarction (MI) via coronary embolization of left circumflex artery followed by rapid ventricular pacing for 4 weeks (MI+HF). Then all animals were treated with daily oral metoprolol ZOK (50 mg) plus ramipril (2.5 mg), and randomized into control group (n=10), intermittent SCS (4 hours x3, n=10) or continuous SCS (24 hours, n=10) for 10 weeks. Echocardiogram showed significant increase in LVEF and +dP/dt at 10 wks in both intermittent SCS group and continuous SCS group as compared with control group (P<0.05). However, there were no significant differences in LVEF and +dP/dt between intermittent vs. continuous SCS group (P>0.05). Nevertheless, only continuous SCS group had significant decreased in serum norepinephrine and BNP at 10wks as compared with control group (P<0.05). In conclusion, addition of either intermittent or continuous SCS to medical therapy Improves LV contractile function compared with medical therapy alone in a porcine model of ischemic HF. To address Objective 3, we performed detail immunohistochemical staining and showed that both SCS groups induced diffuse sympathetic nerve spouting over the infarct, peri-infarct and normal regions rather than only the peri-infarct and infarct regions in controls. In addition, sympathetic innervation at the peri-infarct and infarct regions was increased following SCS, but decreased at the peri-infarct and infarct regions in the controls. Moreover, chronic SCS increased myocardial expression of adrenengic receptor and SERCA-2a mRNA and protein over the peri-infarct and infarct regions.

781111.label: Major findings and research outcome
781111.value: In a porcine model of HF induced by ischemic cardiomyopathy, we first demonstrated that acute SCS at T1-3 level results in rapid and sustained improvement in LV contractile function as measured by serial invasive hemodynamic assessment and detailed echocardiographic examination without increasing myocardial oxygen consumption (Publication 1). Then we further confirm these findings in our chronic animal study. The major findings of the long-term SCS study are (1) both intermittent and continuous chronic SCS result in early and sustained improvement in LV contractile function as determined by serial echocardiographic and invasive hemodynamic assessment in a porcine model of ischemic HF. There was no significant difference in these beneficial effects on LV function for intermittent versus continuous SCS; (2) while medical therapies with ACEI and beta-blocker reduce the serum norepinephrine level, only continuous SCS significantly decreased the serum level of BNP and myocardial norepinephrine spillover; (3) chronic SCS induced significant remodeling of the cardiac sympathetic myocardial innervation with diffuse and more homogenous sympathetic nerve spouting; and sympathetic re-innervation over infarct and peri-infarct regions; (4) there were no significant changes in the pattern of parasympathetic innervation after chronic SCS; and (5) chronic SCS increased myocardial expression of SERCA-2a mRNA and protein (Publication 2). Taken together, our findings offer the novel insight that SCS improve LV function in ischemic cardiomyopahty via remodeling of sympathetic nerve spouting and re-innervation in ischemic myocardium. These changes in cardiac sympathetic innervation are associated with decreased norepinephrine spillover, and enhanced SERCA-2a expression in the failing myocardium, and thus contribute to the improvement in LV contractile function after chronic SCS.

781111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
781111.value: Our results provide novel insight into the potential mechanisms by which SCS improves left ventricular function in heart failure. We provide the first experimental evidence to indicate that chronic thoracic SCS promotes sympathetic re-innervation in a porcine model of ischemic cardiomyopathy. The long-term safety and therapeutic efficacy of chronic SCS will be addressed by our ongoing pilot human trials: The SCS HEART (Spinal cord stimulation for Heart Failure, NCT01362725).

781111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
781111.value: Heart failure (HF) secondary to coronary artery disease has become more prevalent due to the improved survival of patients following acute myocardial infarction. A significant proportion of such patients develop intractable HF due to progressive left ventricular (LV) remodeling. In this project, we studied the acute hemodynamic effects as well as the long-term effects on LV function and remodeling of thoracic spinal cord stimulation (SCS) in a clinically relevant large animal model of ischemic HF. Our results provide novel insight into the potential mechanisms by which SCS improves LV function in HF. It has been postulated that long-term modulation of the imbalance between sympathetic and parasympathetic activity is the major mechanism of beneficial effects of SCS. Nevertheless, this chronic neuromodulation effect of SCS cannot account for the acute improvement in LV contractile function observed in the acute hemodynamic studies. Our long-term results showed that chronic SCS is novel non-pharmacological therapy to improve myocardial function in post-MI HF via remodeling of sympathetic innervation over the peri-infarct and infarct myocardium.

781211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
781211.value: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infects over 95% of the population worldwide, and is associated with several human malignancies, including nasopharyngeal carcinoma, a common cancer in southern China. Infections in immunocompromised patients can cause uncontrolled lymphoproliferative disease with significant morbidity and mortality. Both innate and adaptive immunities play critical roles against EBV, and directly manipulating immune system can control EBV infection. Immunotherapy with EBV-specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) has promise for treatment of EBV-related disorders. However, the clinical application of adoptive transfer of EBV-specific CTLs is hampered by the lack of in vivo expansion of infused CTLs. Therefore, developing alternative strategies to enhance host immunity against EBV have obvious benefits to treat EBV infection. Human gammadelta-T cells, as the first line of defenses, have fast and potent antiviral activities, but the underlying mechanisms remain unknown. Pamidronate, as a commonly used drug for the treatment of osteoporosis, can selectively expand and induce them to produce antiviral cytokines. Our preliminary data indicate that pamidronate-activated gammadelta-T cells can effectively kill EBV-infected B cells. Here, using a humanized mouse model, we will test our hypothesis that human gammadelta-T cells have antiviral activities against EBV infection through their cytotoxic and/or non-cytolytic mechanisms, and pamidronate can control EBV infection and prevent EBV-related disorders through boosting human gammadelta-T-cell immunity. This study will clarify the mechanisms of using pamidronate as a novel therapeutic approach to fight EBV infection.

781211.label: Realisation of objectives
781211.value: Objective 1. Using phosphoantigen pamidronate (PAM) to expand human Vgamma9Vdelta2-T cells, we found that PAM can selectively activate and expand human Vgamma9Vdelta2-T cells, and up-regulate the expression of TRAIL, NKG2D and perforin in Vgamma9Vdelta2-T cells. When cocultured PAM-expanded Vgamma9Vdelta2-T cells with EBV-transformed human autogolous B cells (EBV-LCLs), we demonstrated that the PAM-expanded human Vgamma9Vdelta2-T cells can efficiently recognize and kill the autologous EBV-LCLs and signiﬁcantly inhibited viral replication in vitro. The cytotoxicity of Vgamma9Vdelta2-T cells against EBV-LCLs was dependent on gamma/delta-TCR and NKG2D receptor triggering, and Fas and TRAIL engagement. Objective 2. Rag2-/-gammac-/- mice were inoculated with EBV-LCLs subcutaneously. These Rag2-/-gammac-/- mice were received with PAM-expanded autologous Vgamma9Vdelta2-T cells by intravenous adoptive transfer post inoculation of EBV-LCLs. The mice of control group were treated with an equivalent volume of PBS. Our data indicated that adoptive transfer of Vgamma9Vdelta2-T cells can control the development of EBV-LPD in vivo, reduce the risk of mortality and morbility and prolong the survival time significantly. We also found that adoptive transfer of PAM-expanded Vgamma9Vdelta2-T cells could induce EBV-LPD regression in EBV+ tumor-bearing Rag2-/-gammac-/- mice. Objective 3. The model for the latent EBV infection was established in Rag2-/-gammac-/- mice by adoptive transfer of PBMCs from buffy coats of healthy EBV IgG+ human blood donors. Using humanized mice reconstituted with EBV IgG+ huPBMCs without Vgamma9Vdelta2-T cells, we found that most of these mice had developed EBV-LPD during 3-4 months of observation, while most of the humanized mice reconstituted with EBV IgG+ whole huPBMCs did not develop EBV-LPD during same time of observation. Furthermore, humanized mice without Vgamma9Vdelta2-T cells had significantly higher mortality and morbility compared with the mice with Vgamma9Vdelta2-T cells. Our data indicated that the depletion of Vgamma9Vdelta2-T cells can break the latency and accelerate the development of EBV- LPD during the latent EBV infections in humanized mice model. Objective 4. Using humanized inoculated with EBV-LCL, we found that all PBS-treated humanized mice developed EBV-LPD with subcutaneous tumors and all humanized mice died within 100 days of observation. In contrast, treatment with pamidronate significantly prolonged the survival of humanized mice. Importantly, humanized mice receiving pamidronate treatment had significantly lower tumor incidence and reduced tumor volume, compared with PBS-treated humanized mice. In addition, pamidronate had no such effects in humanized mice reconstituted with Vgamma9Vdelta2-T-depleted huPBMC. These data demonstrated that pamidronate can effectively control the development of EBV-LPD in humanized mice through a Vgamma9Vdelta2-T-cell dependent manner.

781211.label: Major findings and research outcome
781211.value: In this project, we have demonstrated for the first time that the aminobisphosphonate pamidronate-expanded human Vgamma9Vdelta2-T cells efficiently killed EBV-transformed autologous lymphoblastoid B cell lines (EBV-LCL) through gamma/delta-TCR and NKG2D receptor triggering, and Fas and TRAIL engagement. By inoculation of EBV-LCL in Rag2-/-gammac-/- mice and humanized mice, we established the lethal EBV-LPD with characteristics close to the human disease. We further found that adoptive transfer of pamidronate-expanded Vgamma9Vdelta2-T cells alone effectively prevented Epstein-Barr virus-induced lymphoproliferative disease (EBV-LPD) in Rag2-/-gammac-/- mice and induced EBV-LPD regression in EBV+ tumor-bearing Rag2-/-gammac-/- mice. Finally, we demonstrated that pamidronate treatment could inhibit EBV-LPD development in humanized mice through selective activation and expansion of Vgamma9Vdelta2-T cells. Our study provides proof-of-principle for a novel therapeutic approach using pamidronate to control EBV-LPD through Vgamma9Vdelta2-T-cell targeting. From this study, we have already published one paper in the top medical journal “Cancer Cell”. One patent based on this study has been filed.

781211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
781211.value: Our study revealed herein that the aminobisphosphonate pamidronate can control EBV-LPD by enhancing human Vgamma9Vdelta2-T-cell immunity. As pamidronate has been already used for decades in osteoporosis treatment, this ‘new application of an old drug’ potentially offers a safe and readily available option for the treatment of EBV-LPD.

781211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
781211.value: Epstein-Barr virus-induced lymphoproliferative disease (EBV-LPD) after transplantation remains a serious and life-threatening complication. Current treatment strategies for EBV-LPD include restoring EBV-specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTL) and depleting the B cells with monoclonal antibodies or chemotherapy. However, Restoration of EBV-specific CTL is limited by the difficulties in generating enough numbers of EBV-specific CTL in vitro and the lack of in vivo expansion of infused CTL. Antibody-mediated targeting EBV-infected B cells and chemotherapy have unwanted side-effects and lead to general immunosuppression. In this study, we demonstrated that pamidronate could control EBV-LPD in humanized mice by enhancing human gammadelta-T cell immunity. Our study provides a strong preclinical proof of principle for a novel therapeutic approach using pamidronate to boost human Vgamma9Vdelta2-T-cell immunity against EBV-LPD. Pamidronate is commonly used clinically for the treatment of osteoporosis and Paget’s disease, and the use of a human equivalent dose of pamidronate can effectively control EBV-LPD in humanized mice, suggesting rapid translation to human clinical trials. This ‘new application of an old drug’ potentially offers a safe and readily available option for the treatment of EBV-LPD.

781311.value: 血管內皮細胞不僅是一個在血液和血管壁之間的物理屏障。它還擁有其它的保護功能, 包括維持非凝血表面以及調節血管動態平衡。內皮功能障礙造成的一氧化氮（NO）生產不足會影響內皮依賴性血管舒張，降低內皮再生能力，促進血管收縮和血栓形成。這種功能障礙是心血管疾病（CVD）的主要標誌。 SIRT1是一種具有抗衰老功能的III類去乙酰酶。SIRT1的內皮保護活性已被細胞和動物研究證實。然而，潛在的分子機制和信號通路還沒有完全闡明。 我們最近的研究證據表明SIRT1, 通過調節LKB1及其下游AMP活化蛋白激酶（AMPK）, 可以阻止血管內皮細胞的衰老，提高增殖能力。內皮細胞特異性 SIRT1的轉基因小鼠表現出更為有利的血管反應; 而小鼠內皮細胞特異表達的AMPK或SIRT1（H363Y）突變體能夠引起損傷。SIRT1和AMPK被視為重要的能量和氧化還原感應分子，並可以刺激內皮型一氧化氮合成酶（eNOS）. 另一方面，SIRT1和AMPK之間的相互作用在很大程度上仍然不明確。我們計劃用已經建立的轉基因動物模型以及原代內皮細胞培養對SIRT1, LKB1, AMPK和eNOS通路進行研究。此項課題會針對這些分子信號的交叉調控以及他們在內皮依賴性血管舒張和收縮所發揮的功能進行深入探討.

781311.label: Realisation of objectives
781311.value: Both objectives have been achieved for this project. For objective 1, we have discovered that SIRT1 promotes the ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of LKB1 in endohelial cells. This effect is highly dependent on a critical lysine (K) residue 64 of LKB1 and a key serine (S) residue 47 of SIRT1. The acetylation of LKB1 facilitates its nuclear translocation and degradation by SIRT1-dependent mechanism, whereas the phosphorylation of SIRT1 at S47 by CDK5 abolishes its interaction with LKB1. For objective 2, three lines of transgenic mice have been established for endothelial overexpression of wild type human SIRT1, the dominant negative mutant H363Y, and constitutively active AMPKalpha. The vascular and metabolic phenotypes of these mice have been thoroughly characterized. The results revealed that endothelial overexpression of SIRT1 enhances and endothelial overexpression of H363Y attenuates vasodilatory responses. The mice have also been backcrossed to eNOS and ApoE deficient backgrounds for evaluating the vascular responses and the development of atherosclerosis. On the other hand, AMPK activation in endothelial cells causes vascular inflammation and facilitates dietary obesity-induced liver injury. Taken together, the study suggest that SIRT1 and AMPK counter-regulate endothelial function and vascular responses, which may play an important role in maintaining the vascular homeostasis.

781311.label: Major findings and research outcome
781311.value: Major finding 1: SIRT1 is phosphorylated by CDK5, which negatively regulates the anti-senescent activity of SIRT1 in endothelial cells. Major finding 2: Endothelial SIRT1 elicits vasoprotective activity against ageing-induced damages, including atherosclerosis. Major finding 3: LKB1/AMPK pathway mediates the stress responses of the endothelial cells. However, prolonged activation of this pathway is harmful. Major finding 4: SIRT1 antagonizes LKB1/AMPK signaling to maintain vascular homeostasis. Research outcome 1: Publications in journals including "Circulation", "Physiological genomics", "Hypertension", "Pharmacology and Therapeutics", "British Journal of Pharmacology", "JAHA: Journal of the American Heart Association" and "Arteriosclerosis, Thrombosis, and Vascular Biology". Research outcome 2: More than ten presentations were delivered in international conferences. Research outcome 3: Three PhD students and one MPhil student successfully graduated.

781311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
781311.value: The project has opened a very important application field for ageing-related vascular abnormalities by targeting endothelial SIRT1. In particular, using the animal models, we have confirmed that overexpression of endothelial SIRT1 is able to prevent vascular remodeling independent of eNOS, thus a potential target for early vascular ageing. We are currently working on and developing expertise in this field. In addition, inhibition of CDK5-mediated phosphorylation of SIRT1 may represent an approach for later stage of vascular ageing-associated diseases by restoring the anti-inflammatory and anti-atherosclerotic activity of endothelial SIRT1. The research on both areas are currently being carried out in our laboratory.

781311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
781311.value: Abnormalities in blood vessels are the major culprits for many ageing-related diseases, including atherosclerosis, heart attack, stroke, kidney failure etc. However, there lacks effective drug target for the prevention and treatment of these diseases. The identification of SIRT1 in endothelial cells as a potent vasoprotective agent has revealed a new direction of drug development in combating ageing-related diseases.

781511.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
781511.value: The interaction between a transcription factor (TF) and its DNA binding sites (TFBS) is a critical step for gene regulation. Binding of general TFs in the core promoter region of a gene determines the initiation of gene transcription, while binding of TFs in the distal promoter region determines the efficiency of transcription in temporal and spatial specific manners. Mutation in either TF or TFBS elements may weaken the interactions and cause genetic disorders in animals. For instance, mutations in c-myc, a basic Helix-Loop-Helix (bHLH) oncogene, have been associated with 20% of all human cancers, such as Burkitt’s lymphoma, breast and prostate cancers. During evolution, bHLH has expanded to 125 members in humans, and 94 of them are conserved in mice. These members have protein sequences with various levels of sequence identity; similarly, their TFBS are different in various degrees. We hypothesize that the evolutions of a TF and its TFBS are correlated. Furthermore, we can develop computational methods to identify the co-evolved residues/bases that are important to protein-DNA interactions. To test this hypothesis, we propose to: 1) perform SELEX experiment to map out the binding sites for 15 TFs in the bHLH family; 2) test the co-evolution of TFs and TFBS in the bHLH family; 3) develop a novel method to identify the co-evolved residue and base pairs. This research will provide the first evidence to show the co-evolutionary relationship between TF and TFBS. It will provide novel insights into the dynamic relationship between TFs and TFBS during evolution. This deeper understanding will help us to delineate transcription regulatory networks, predict the functional consequences of TF and TFBS mutations, and rational design of drugs for the treatment of human diseases. Our large scale SELEX experiments will systematically discover binding sites for many TFs in bHLH family, which will be deposited to public database and benefit other researchers. 轉錄因子（TF）和DNA結合位點（TFBS）之間的相互作用是基因調控的關鍵步驟。轉錄因子在基因核心啟動子區域與DNA的結合決定了轉錄起始，而在遠端啟動子區域的結合決定了轉錄的效率，以及在不同時間和空間上對轉錄的控制。在TF或TFBS上的突變可能削弱它們的相互作用，並導致各種遺傳性疾病。例如， c - myc基因的突變與20％的癌症有關，這些癌症包括伯基特淋巴瘤，乳腺癌和前列腺癌。在進化過程中， BHLH轉錄因子家族在人體中已有125名成員，其中94名在小鼠也存在。這些成員的蛋白質序列有不同程度相似性。它們的TFBS也有不同程度相似。 我們推測TF和TFBS的進化是相關的。我們將開發計算方法來確定TF-TFBS的共進化關係。為了驗證這一假說，我們將：1）用SELEX實驗繪製出15個BHLH家族轉錄因子的DNA結合位點; 2）測試BHLH家庭中TF和TFBS的協同進化關係; 3）開發新方法來確定蛋白質殘基和DNA鹼基對的共同進化。 這項研究將首次提出TF和TFBS協同進化關係的理論。它將為TFS和TFBS在進化過程中的動態關係提供新的見解。這將有助於我們預測TF和TFBS突變對基因功能的影響，從而更深入的了解基因轉錄調控網絡。我們可以把這些理論用於設計藥物，治療疾病。另外，我們的SELEX實驗將系統地發現BHLH家庭許多轉錄因子的DNA結合位點，這些將被存入公共數據庫中使和其他研究人員受益。

781511.label: Realisation of objectives
781511.value: 1. We selected 15 human bHLH TFs based on the human bHLH protein catalog, cloned, expressed the TFs and mapped their binding sites with high throughput SELEX (Jolma, et al., 2010). We used Consensus/MEME software to discover the motif and construct Position Weight Matrix (PWM) for each TF. These PWM were used for the subsequent co-evolution analysis and discovery of co-evolved residues and DNA base pairs as well as developing our methods. 2. To test the co-evolution between TFs and TFBS in the bHLH family, we first created an evolutionary tree from protein sequences that have PWMs available. We then calculated sequence and PWMs similarities for creating a distance matrix for all protein sequences and PWMs. The two distance matrices were used to calculate the Pearson’s correlation coefficient, which measures the co-evolution of the protein sequences and PWMs. We found that protein domain sequences are significantly co-evolved with their binding sites in mammalian, eukaryotes and CAEEL bHLH family datasets. We further validated these findings using other three protein families, Homeo (100 members), HMG (15 members) and TRP(11 members). The results suggested significant co-evolution at both whole and domain sequence level. 3. To identify co-evolved protein residue-DNA base pairs and to develop algorithms to measure the dependency of residue-base pairs, we used protein–DNA complexes with solved 3D structure to test whether structurally determined interacting residue base pairs are co-evolved. We collected structurally annotated interactions from the BIPA database. For the eukaryote bHLH members, out of 19 interacting position pairs, 14 were identified as highly co-evolving position pairs by the MI method, which showed a significant overlap with P<0.001. Both MI selected residues and BIPA annotated residues showed significant correlations with TFBSs, which indicates the critical roles the important residues that play in TF–TFBS interactions. One interesting position at eukaryote alignment that was identified by both BIPA and MI in this study is position 13. Residues at position 13 dramatically correlated with different binding preferences in the E-box region. When arginine is at this position, the corresponding TF will bind to canonical CACGTG E-box; for any other amino acid, the corresponding TF will bind to different E-box motifs other than canonical CACGTG. Our prediction is consistent with previous studies on the important role of this position in E-box binding affinity. All aims were successfully achieved and the results were reported in Yang et al, Bioinformatics 27(21):2972-2978. Bioinformatics is a leading journal in my field.

781511.label: Major findings and research outcome
781511.value: 1. We found that protein domain sequences are significantly co-evolved with their binding sites in mammalian, eukaryotes and CAEEL bHLH family datasets. The protein domain sequences show stronger co-evolution than the whole protein sequences. The validation using other three protein families, Homeo (100 members), HMG (15 members) and TRP(11 members) suggested significant co-evolution at both whole and domain sequence level. We also took into account the position effect on amino acid composition of the TF family by permuting the protein sequences in a position specific way to calculate the P-value and excluding the effects of speciation by calculating the PCC between the bHLH’s binding profiles and the domain sequences from proteins other than bHLH family (Homeo domain) or inversing synonymous change distance matrix. The results from all these methods produce significant P-values, indicating that our discovery on the co-evolution between TFs and their binding sites is general and reliable. For the eukaryote bHLH members, out of 19 interacting position pairs, 14 were identified as highly co-evolving position pairs by the MI method, which showed a significant overlap with P<0.001. Both MI selected residues and BIPA annotated residues showed significant correlations with TFBSs, which indicates the critical roles the important residues that play in TF–TFBS interactions. These results were published in Bioinformatics and BMC Systems Biology (YangS, 2011; Yalamanchili, 2012). 2. This study about co-evolution in bHLH family, proved the co-evolutionary relationship of TFs and developed PCC and MI value to effectively score the significance of TF domain/residue and motif/DNA on TFBS that affected functional specificity of TFs. This method was further used to score the significance of genetic variants in the TF binding sites in our subsequent study about GWAS SNP annotation and enhanced our academic output as well as commercial collaboration. The GWASdb/GWASrap databases developed by our team provided a comprehensive tools for SNP annotation (Li MJ, 2012; Xu Feng, 2012; Li MJ, 2013; Li MJ, 2014; Wang W, 2014; Yalamanchili, 2014; Li MJ, 2015 ). In addition, studying the evolution of TF-BS interaction aided our understanding of the dynamic interaction between TF families and their binding targets, therefore boosted TF-BS centered regulatory network(Wang LY, 2011; Qin J,2013; Wang P, 2013; Qin J, 2014, Yalamanchili, 2014, Wang P, 2015).

781511.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
781511.value: This study about co-evolution in bHLH family, proved the co-evolutionary relationship of TFs and developed PCC and MI value to effectively score the significance of TF domain/residue and motif/DNA on TFBS that affected functional specificity of TFs. One application of this method is to score the significance of genetic variants in the TF binding sites. Our group has worked in this field and gained good results in GWAS SNP annotation by utilizing this method. This work enhanced our academic output as well as commercial collaboration. The other potential future work will be to predict DNA binding sites from a TF's protein sequence, based on the TF-BS correlation-ship we discovered in this study. Currently, there are only small parts of TFs with profiled binding sites from each TF family. Identification of specific binding sites from the same TF family is also a difficult question. Since this co-evolution method can find correlated residue and DNA base pair on TFBS in a TF family with PCC and MI value, TF binding sites can be inferred by the binding information of other TFs in the same family.

781511.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
781511.value: The protein sequences' variation determines the binding sites specification, thus the functional specialization. Studying the evolution of TF-BS interaction can aid our understanding of the dynamic interaction between TF families and their binding sites, and the functional specialization of these factors. The co-evolution between TF and TFBS was estimated in this study by calculating the correlation between the similarity of protein sequences and the similarity of binding motifs (PCC value). The co-evolved protein residues and DNA base pairs were identified by testing the dependence of protein residues and DNA base pairs (MI value). In this study, bHLH and other protein family was used to establish the method and test the co-evolution relation. The results supported co-evolution between TFs and their binding sites is general and reliable. The method identified co-evolved base pairs positions, 14 and 13, on the binding sites of bHLH family, which have been proved to be important for the functional specificity of bHLH family. This method was further used to score the significance of genetic variants in the TF binding sites in our subsequent study about GWAS SNP annotation and enhanced our academic output as well as commercial collaboration.
