781911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
781911.value: An estimated 2 billion people suffer from periodontal disease. This spectrum of chronic inflammatory gum diseases are caused by ‘detrimental’ populations of bacteria that infect and induce destruction of the tissues surrounding and supporting the tooth. Untreated, these persistent subgingival (below-the-gumline) infections cause progressively serious inflammation, gum recession and bone loss; ultimately leading to tooth-loss. Numerous studies have established that elevated populations of the spirochete bacterium Treponema denticola are strongly associated with the occurrence and severity of periodontal disease. However, its precise roles in disease initiation or progression are poorly-understood. Efforts to better-define its disease-associations are significantly hindered by the lack of definitive methods to discriminate-between its diverse constituent strains. Supported by our preliminary findings, we hypothesize that a certain subset of T. denticola strains possess enhanced ‘periodontal disease-promoting’ abilities. Here, we will develop and utilize a powerful combination of genetic analyses and aptamer-based molecular-recognition approaches to directly investigate this issue. In preliminary work, we surveyed genetic diversity within a comprehensive collection of T. denticola isolates. Our data indicated that the cell-surface major sheath protein (Msp), and the gene that encodes it, were both ideal ‘molecular targets’ for highly discriminatory T. denticola strain identification and ‘typing’ methodologies. In the first stage of this proposal, we will analyze the diversity of msp gene sequences encoded by T. denticola strains present within subgingival bacterial samples from subjects with severe periodontal disease (n=25), versus periodontal disease-free controls (n=25). This will enable us to identify the most common Msp ‘isoforms’ (variants) encoded by T. denticola strains within the local population. From the data generated, it may be possible to associate distinct Msp ‘isoforms’ with periodontal health status. In the second stage, we will develop ‘anti-Msp’ aptamers capable of recognizing specific Msp protein isoforms on the T. denticola cell-surface. Aptamers are synthetic DNA/RNA molecules that are functionally-equivalent to antibodies; but offer major practical advantages. ‘Anti-Msp’ aptamers tagged with molecular ‘reporter groups’ will be utilized as specific cell-labeling agents, enabling T. denticola cells expressing different Msp isoforms to be independently detected and visualized. This will enable us to determine differences in T. denticola strain populations within periodontally-diseased, versus disease-free sites. The innovative combination of analytical approaches described here, will enable the relationship between T. denticola and periodontal disease to be dissected in far-greater detail than previously possible. Our approach will be directly applicable for investigating the diversity, ecology and disease-associations of many other species of bacteria. 摘要: 全球約有二十億人罹患牙周疾病。口腔細菌中的'有害'菌群被視為這牙齦/周慢性炎症性疾病的致病原素。這些細菌感染牙周支持組織並誘導組織破壞。如不予治療，持續性的齦下感染會進一步引致嚴重炎症、牙齦退縮、牙骨喪失，最終將導致牙齒脫落。研究顯示齒垢密螺旋體的增加與牙周疾病的發生及其嚴重程度有頗強的相關性。然而齒垢密螺旋體之於牙周炎發病原理尚未清楚。要進一步研究這種多樣性細菌的致病機理，研究人員需從建立一種完善的菌株區分方法開始。目前這種檢測方法的缺乏大大影響了齒垢密螺旋體及牙周病相關性的研究。據我們初步實驗結果推測，齒垢密螺旋體的某些特定菌株具有較強的牙周致病性。本課題將結合基因分析方法以及應用適配子為基礎的分子識別方法來研究上述的科研問題。 在前期工作中，我們詳盡地分析了一組齒垢密螺旋體分離菌株的基因多樣性。結果顯示細菌表面主要蛋白(Msp)以及編碼該蛋白的基因是鑑定和分類齒垢密螺旋體高度分化的理想'分子靶標'。 本提案的第一階段將納入二十五位嚴重牙周疾病患者以及二十五位對照健康人士為研究對象，分析其齦下菌斑中齒垢密螺旋體的Msp基因序列多樣性。從而鑑定出齦下環境中齒垢密螺旋體菌株的常見Msp編碼類型。及某些與牙周健康狀態相關的Msp類型可能性。於第二階段，我們會篩選出能識別不同Msp類型的適配子。適配子是有類似抗體功能的脫氧核糖核酸或者核糖核酸的合成物，具許多應用優勢。帶有報告分子的抗Msp適配子可作為特異性的細菌標記物，用於特異性的鑑定和可從視化表達不同Msp亞型的齒垢密螺旋體。這種技術可幫助我們確定牙周疾病位點與健康位點中齦下齒垢密螺旋體的菌群差異。 上述的創新分析方法的，可助我們更加深入解構齒垢密螺旋體與牙周疾病的關係。本實驗方法將來亦可以直接應用於其他細菌種類多樣性、生態學以及疾病相關性之微生物學研究。

781911.label: Realisation of objectives
781911.value: We assembled a highly-diverse set of ca. 50 oral treponeme strains belonging to phylogroups 1 and 2, in order to study their genetic diversity, focusing on the major surface protein gene (objective 2). This collection included Treponema denticola, Treponema medium, Treponema putidum, ‘Treponema vincentii’, as well as novel proposed species (e.g. ‘Treponema plautii’, ‘Treponema sinensis’). The sequences of 16S rRNA, msp and several ‘housekeeping’ genes were determined. This enabled us to assemble a comprehensive ‘reference set’ of msp gene sequences. Firstly, this enabled us to design highly selective broad-range PCR primers targeting the msp genes from phylogroup 1&2 treponeme taxa. These primers were used to investigate treponeme msp genetic diversity in subgingival plaque sampled from a cohort of 20 chronic periodontitis and control subjects, using a clone-based approach (objective 1). 626 clinical msp sequences were obtained, which were clustered into 21 ‘msp genotypes’ (95% sequence identity). Msp genotype diversity was significantly higher in periodontitis subjects compared to controls. Intriguingly, the msp genotype corresponding to T. denticola ATCC 35405 was the most prevalent, widely-distributed in both periodontitis and healthy controls. Furthermore, healthy controls harboured higher T. vincentii proportions. Three msp genotypes were highly prevalent in periodontitis. One disease-associated genotype (NP5_2) was closely-related to Msp from T. denticola OTK. We are in the process of submitting these findings to PLoS One (draft version attached). A SELEX approach was used to develop anti-Msp aptamers, using the T. denticola ATCC 35405 Msp as target (Objective 3). Several G-quadruplex and non G-quadruplex anti-msp aptamers were successfully identified. Their binding characteristics were analyzed using ELISA-based approaches. Two aptamers (Apt2, Apt5) bound T. denticola ATCC 35405, OTK and NP5_2 Msp protein with nanomolar affinity, and had negligible binding against control proteins. A manuscript is in preparation (draft attached). Their cell-binding activities were probed against a wide range of oral, especially periodontal, bacteria (objective 4). After concerted effort, we were unable to observe satisfactory levels of specificity under any conditions tested. Other sets of aptamers were developed, and tested. Their cell-binding affinities and specificities were also unsatisfactory. Interestingly (but a great hindrance to our progress), we found that P. gingivalis cells have a high affinity for binding certain DNA sequences. New sets of aptamers are currently being developed to try to overcome this challenging hurdle. Furthermore, we are currently developing gel-based aptamer detection approaches (analogous to Western blotting), for identifying T. denticola proteins in proteome samples.

781911.label: Major findings and research outcome
781911.value: Major Findings. We performed a systematic genetic analysis of a large set of human oral phylogroup 1 and 2 treponeme strains of diverse geographical and clinical origin, which included all common reference strains. After assigning taxonomy through 16S rRNA analysis, we analyzed the composition and phylogeny of the msp gene. This revealed that all strains possessed a highly conserved 20aa signal peptide. Notably, there was considerable variation in the sequence, predicted secondary structure and domain composition of the encoded Msp proteins. Interestingly, some of the msp genotypes corresponded closely to previously-identified Msp seroptypes: i.e. the ATCC 35405, ATCC 33520, OTK strains. The msp protein encoded by T. putidum strains was most related to those encoded by T. denticola OTK, GM-1 and MS25; indicative of a common genetic origin. Furthermore, our msp genotype analysis results clearly show that individuals commonly harbor multiple T. denticola and T. vincentii ‘strains’ in their oral cavities, which may be highly distinct. Single-stranded DNA aptamers capable of specifically recognizing Msp proteins from multiple T. denticola strains were successfully developed. Unfortunately, we were not able to develop a T. denticola cell-labelling strategy utilizing these aptamers that had sufficiently good sensitivity or specificity. We are still actively working on this technically-challenging problem. Based on our gene sequencing of conserved (housekeeping) genes, we developed a robust multilocus sequence analysis (MLSA) system for characterizing and identifying T. denticola strains. This was published in BMC Microbiology. We subsequently determined the full genome sequence for 5 diverse reference strains. The genomes of T. putidum OMZ758T, and Treponema sp. OMZ 8383 (‘T. sinensis’) were published; the first genomes for these ‘species’. More comprehensive genome analyses are currently underway. Research Outcomes. Five papers have been published, which have directly arisen from this grant. One is currently under submission, and another is under preparation. Two PhD students have been trained through this grant: Dr. Fiona Meng YOU (graduated 2012; thesis details attached) and Dr. Hawkins Yongbiao HUO. Fiona is now an Assistant Professor at Sichuan University, School of Stomatology, China. Hawkins will submit his PhD in September 2015. Another PhD student has recently started in this area. The PI was awarded the research prize in Microbiology / Immunology / Periodontology, IADR South‐East Asian Division (IADR SEA) Annual General Meeting, for research findings supported directly by this grant. This grant also directly helped me secure tenure in January 2015, and I am extremely grateful for that!

781911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
781911.value: This trove of msp genetic information is extremely valuable for the future development of more highly discriminatory methods for oral treponeme identification. The variability of the msp gene (and protein) makes it ideal for strain discrimination, and epidemiological studies. Its phylogenetic patterns are very different to those of proteins with ‘housekeeping’ functions. This is consistent with its direct role in disease-related processes; possibly host adaptation. Furthermore, it will be invaluable for the dissection of molecular processes that directly involve the Msp protein; e.g. determining surface-exposed regions required for intergeneric bacterial cell binding (e.g. with Porphyromonas gingivalis or Fusobacterium nucleatum), or with proteoglycan matrix components of host tissue (e.g. fibronectin, laminin). Furthermore, we envisage that there may be a correlation between the sequence composition or domain structure of the Msp protein and those of the corresponding components of the cell-surface chymotrypsin-like protease complex. We plan to actively pursue this avenue in the future. Regarding the aptamers, we believe that they may not be ideally suited for specific cell-labelling and visualization applications, but may be better suited for protein detection applications within oral fluids (e.g. saliva, gingival crevicular fluid). We also plan to initiate investigations into this area in the near future.

781911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
781911.value: Periodontitis is caused by chronic, multi-species bacterial infections of the tissues that surround and support teeth. Species of Treponema bacteria are widely-thought to play key roles in disease pathology. Here, we developed molecular approaches that could be used to identify and distinguish Treponema bacteria associated with periodontitis. This was based on the highly-abundant major surface protein (Msp) of Treponema. We first characterized the msp gene sequences for a large collection of Treponema strains, revealing high levels of genetic diversity. This genetic ‘reference-set’ was used to characterize the msp gene sequences of Treponema bacteria present in the dental plaque of patients with periodontitis, versus healthy controls. We consequently identified certain msp sequences that were highly-elevated in disease. We then developed diagnostic aptamers (single-stranded DNA-based molecular recognition molecules) that were able to specifically detect Treponema msp proteins. Our results greatly improve our general understanding of the strains and species of Treponema that may play important roles in periodontitis and other oral infectious diseases. Our ultimate goal is to use aptamer technologies to develop test-kits that people can use at home to diagnose early-stage periodontitis or gum disease. This would greatly improve treatment options and treatment outcomes for the general public.

782011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
782011.value: 氣候變化當之為愧已成為現代發展的主要環境問題，它給人類及其賴以生存的自然生態系統 帶來巨大影響。生物學家致力於研究生物如何應對氣候變化及預測未來變暖地球上能夠幸存的優勢種。 未來生態系統的構型將取決於成功存留的生物種類組成，這有助於我們從根本上理解自然世界將如何應對氣候變化。 一般情況下，窄分布的物種對環境條件的適應能力受本土環境遺傳基因的影響，其環境耐性較差，該物種不能耐受高溫環境，切換到新的代謝途徑后缺乏生理可塑性及快速適應的基因特性，所以很可能被淘汰。相對來講，優勢種具有本土表型及基因型多樣性特性，分布范圍較廣 ，使其能夠更靈活地適應環境變化的壓力。 未來的生物群落中，優勢種將發展為主導力量，而劣勢種將面臨被淘汰甚至滅絕。那些分布廣、生存在其生理極限環境下的物種有利於研究上述變化，如那些可能受氣候變化影響的物種。 很多海洋生物都適合作為研究氣候變化的建模物種，尤其是蝸牛屬Echinolittorina。該物種廣泛分布於從日本到印度尼西亞的太平洋西北部，生活在高岩相潮間帶、極端物理環境中，位於海洋生物生理耐性的極限。Echinolittorina malaccan、 E. radiata 以及 E. vidua 這三個物種既有垂直分布的重疊性也有緯度方向分布的搭接點。 E. radiata 隸屬於偏北方物種而E. malaccana 生活於偏熱帶環境中； E. vidua 分布較廣泛，可稱之為全球化的海洋生物。在生物維度分布范圍內，種群表現為遺傳和生理差異性，利用其作為理想的測試生物可以判定基因型還是表型決定了生物對氣候變化的反應。 該研究課題採用一套生理和遺產學方法，闡述表型（緯度與生理耐性范圍的關係）和基因型（種群間的遺傳差異）的不同在預測優勢或劣勢種群的相對重要性，進而可以判定氣候變化影響下大緯度梯度范圍內的種群容量。

782011.label: Realisation of objectives
782011.value: Overall, littorinid snails were sampled from two sites at 11 locations from Qingdao, China to Singapore covering over 35° of latitude. Samples were collected in the thermally Stressful (hot) and Non-Stressful (cool) seasons, as determined by local experts, at all sites. Two species were abundant, Echinolittorina malaccana from Singapore to Taiwan and E. radiata from Vietnam to Qingdao and were collected for the analyses, with the aid of local collaborators. The involvement of a network of collaborators was essential to successfully sample animals from different locations. After a series of preliminary test and trials, animals collected were either fixed in alcohol (for genetic analysis; Objectives 2 and 3); in RNALater (for hsp expression); or returned live to Hong Kong where they were tested under standardized conditions (Objective 1). Some issues were experienced in transport of the samples, and some samples were lost in transit and had to be re-sampled / replaced. Preliminary trials showed no effect of the transportation process on samples. The genetic relatedness of the populations was assessed using mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COI) gene as a DNA marker (Objective 2). Neighbor-joining phylogenetic trees based on the identified haplotypes revealed that all the individuals were phylogenetically close in both species. As such, no subclades were identified and no obvious genetic structure was detected (fulfilling Objective 2). These results, therefore, revealed very little genetic structuring between populations and suggested any observed differences in thermal tolerance would be associated with local acclimation as opposed to adaptation (at the genetic levels investigated, Objectives 3 and 4). Therefore, it could be concluded that the observed patterns were associated with phenotypic and not genotypic variation between populations (fulfilling Objective 4). For each of the two species, Lethal temperatures; hsp expression and enzyme function (for MDH, LDH and CS) were estimated (fulfilling Objective 1). The Arrhenius Breakpoint Temperature of heart rate was also investigated as an addition to the original proposal. These assays allowed an assessment of the thermal performance of the two species over the latitudinal gradients, but also within location (between sites) and possible seasonal acclimation (stressful/non-stressful seasons). It also allowed assessment of the vulnerability of the two species (fulfilling Objective 4). Based on the lack of any genetic differentiation between populations (Objective 2), differences seen between populations could be related to either local (between sites) or regional (between location) phenotypic acclimation and with seasonal acclimation (fulfilling Objective 3).

782011.label: Major findings and research outcome
782011.value: Two species of littorinids (Echinolittorina malaccana, E. radiata) were sampled from 11 locations from Qingdao to Singapore (35° latitude, Objective 1). Assessment of genetic differentiation between populations of both species showed high haplotype diversity and low nucleotide diversity (Objective 2). Overall genetic structuring between the populations is weak, which is consistent with their pelagic larval stages and patterns of ocean currents. This lack of genetic structure suggests any pattern of thermal variation between populations is not related to genotype, but phenotypic acclimation (Objective 4). Some small-scale genetic differentiation was observed (between Hong Kong/Taiwan: E. malaccana; Hong Kong/Japan: E. radiata), probably due to the effects of multiple factors such as local water currents and physical barriers. These small scale differences were further studied in E. malaccana by investigating transcriptomic variation in response to thermal stress, which indicated some levels of variation, but a high degree of similarity (conservation of certain responses) in key expression levels (Wang et al under review, Objective 3). Thermal responses (Lethal Temperature, LT 50, Arrhenius Breakpoint Temperatures, ABT, of heart rate, hsp expression and enzyme activity of three key enzymes) were assayed (Objective 1, Williams et al. in prep). Thermal tolerance was extremely high (>50°C for LT50), and in E. malaccana a latitudinal pattern was evident, but not in E. radiata. Both species, however, showed acclimation with season (higher tolerances in the stressful season), suggesting phenotypic variation in response (Objective 4). Enzyme activities were also extremely stable under high temperatures (55°C), but showed no clear latitudinal variation. ABT limits were lower, but still remarkably high (>45°C), but in general did not show predictable latitudinal gradients (Williams et al in prep). Heat shock expression was more variable, and very site and location specific, likely representing local conditions. These indicators reveal very high tolerance, but still fall below extreme temperatures in the snail habitats, suggesting the role of other mechanisms for survival (model proposed in Ng et al, in submission). Tolerance between populations varied but this was not related to genetic patterns (Objectives 3 and 4) but may be related to extreme local conditions (acclimation, Objectives 3 and 4) which are often neglected in assessments of thermal stress (see Helmuth et al 2014). Overall, therefore, there was little evidence for any genetic differentiation between populations, but there was variation in thermal response (phenotypic acclimation), which was not strongly related to latitude, but rather local environmental conditions (Objective 4).

782011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
782011.value: This work highlighted that littorinid snails are incredibly resilient to thermal stress in terms of their physiological performance. On reason for this is related to their enzyme performance and investigation of the thermal lability of isoforms of these enzymes is ongoing, coordinated by YW Dong (Xiamen University, Co-I of this project) and G Somero (Stanford University). Initial results indicate cMDH of E. malaccana has much higher thermal stability and Km as compared to E. radiata and further work will investigate their structure. Although the littorinids have high thermal tolerance, environmental conditions exceed these limits, which suggests that these animals have other means of combatting these environmental extremes which will impart energetic costs. To estimate the exact thermal conditions these animals experience temperature loggers have been deployed at most of the locations studied to get real-time data. To investigate the costs and the role of behaviour in combating thermal stress a new RGC project was funded in 2015 (Environmentally induced changes in behavioural responses and selection pressures: predicting the fate of high shore snails under a warming climate; RGC 17121914) which builds on the techniques of the present project and investigates how thermal stress impacts the overall fitness of these snails.

782011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
782011.value: As our climate warms we need to know how species can respond to thermal stress; whether they have a genetically determined, fixed tolerance (i.e. are adapted), or whether their tolerance can change (acclimate) with season and location. To examine this, genetic relatedness and thermal tolerance were investigated in high shore snails, which inhabit extreme thermal environments and are widely dispersed. Thermal tolerances were tested over a latitudinal range from Qingdao to Singapore to test if performance varies in relation to environmental conditions, and whether this was associated with genetic differences between populations or acclimation to different environments. Snail populations showed very little genetic differentiation, suggesting populations were very closely related. Thermal tolerance levels were extremely high for all populations, suggesting these were conserved. Snails had high lethal temperatures, breakpoints of heart failure, and enzyme activities and produced heat shock proteins as part of their defence mechanisms. Thermal responses varied between locations, although this generally did not fit a latitudinal pattern, suggesting snail populations acclimated to local conditions and this could vary with season. These snails, therefore, are extremely well adapted to high temperatures, but also show local acclimation at different sites and with season suggesting they may tolerate climate change.

782111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
782111.value: 大約90%的癌症死亡個案是由腫瘤轉移引致的，因此，明白腫瘤轉移的機制非常重要。在腫瘤轉移的過程中，癌細胞要在沒有附着的環境下存活的先決條件是能夠形成多細胞聚合(Multicellular aggregates/spheroids, MCS)。但到目前為止，對控制MCS形成過程的因素仍所知甚少，越來越多證據顯示微環境中的信號在癌症演進中非常重要。卵巢癌是一種極具轉移能力的癌症，透過腹膜散播和產生腹水而提供一個充滿各種可溶性生長因子的微環境予癌細胞，我們已於早前證明了這些生長因子對細胞的活動有重大的影響，而於最近，我們的實驗結果更顯示p70S6K，一個磷脂酰醇3-激酶/AKT的下游受應器, 在細胞內扮演着信號傳遞的角色，協調多個生長因子的作用。此外，我們亦首次證實p70S6K 除了控制細胞分裂和生長外，更可涉及於其他腫瘤演進的關鍵過程，包括遠端轉移。我們已經建立了一個三維的受體外模型以模擬癌細胞在體內沒有附着的生長環境，希望藉此發現及建構出腫瘤轉移的機制。我們的實驗顯示p70S6K在MCS的形成過程是關鍵的調節物。再者，N-cadherin的高表達在此過程中看來是必須的，而這細胞間的黏附分子通常在較後期的癌症及腹膜性轉移才出現，由此，我們猜想p70S6K可能透過增加MCS的形成和散播而在卵巢癌的早期演進有着關鍵性的作用，我們更猜想MCS的形成和散播可能由N-cadherin作傳遞或管制媒介， 在此研究中，我們會(i)研究N-cadherin在細胞內所介導的事項，以建立其於p70S6K表達細胞中誘導腫瘤轉移的角色; (ii)闡明其隱含機制，特別是N-cadherin在調節連結蛋白，受體酪氨酸蛋白激及非典Wnt信號; 及(iii)解釋p70S6K調控N-cadherin的機制。這個研究將令我們更清楚MCS在腫瘤轉移的角色及機制及為研制新的醫療方法提供方向。

782111.label: Realisation of objectives
782111.value: Objective 1: Multicellular spheroid (MCS) is a critical feature of ovarian cancer whose adhesive abilities have not been elucidated. During the past years, using a 3-dimensional culture, we have successfully shown for the first time that p70S6K plays a pivotal role in the formation of ovarian carcinoma MCS, which is mediated by N-cadherin, and suggest that the subsequent adhesion to the peritoneal mesothelium, which is the first rate-limiting step in ovarian cancer metastasis, is a P-cadherin-dependent event. We also present evidence that a novel interplay linking P-cadherin to regulation of b1 integrin activation via an induction of the Golgi glycosyltransferase ST6Gal-I, which mediates b1 integrin hypersialyation in this process. Percentage achieved: 100% Objective 2: Despite its significance, the key signals and molecular events regulating the formation and expansion of MCS remain elusive. Our results show that N-cadherin has a dominant effect over other cadherins on MCS formation of ovarian cancer cells. In addition to cell-cell adhesion, we show that N-cadherin can activate specific downstream signal transduction. We identify a novel role for N-cadherin in non-canonical Wnt/Ca2+ pathway. Furthermore, whereas b-catenin and Ca2+ can transduce the non-canonical Wnt signaling pathway independently, we show that N-cadherin acts via b-catenin and Ca2+ in a coordinated interdependent manner, suggesting that crosstalk in Wnt/b-catenin and Wnt/Ca2+ activation as a mechanism of N-cadherin and MCS formation. Percentage achieved: 100% Objective 3: In search of how p70S6K may regulate N-cadherin, we show that this is mediated through activation of the transcription factors Twist and Sox9. Interestingly, we found that this upregulation of Twist and Sox9 is not the result from changes in rate of transcription, but mRNA stabilities. Twist and Sox9 do not epistatically interact and more likely be each have an essential role in regulating N-cadherin expression. Using computational and experimental approaches, we thus identify a role of miR-145 in coregulating both Twist and Sox-9 to enhance N-cadherin expression due to p70S6K activation. We also provide mechanistic insights suggesting that this tumorigenic activity is associated with the ability of p70S6K to regulate miRNA biogenesis through a Dicer-tristetraprolin interaction. 782111.label: Major findings and research outcome
782111.value: Objective 1: Using a 3-dimensional culture, we have identified for the first time that p70S6K is an important regulator for the seeding and metastatic spread of MCS on the peritoneum. We further demonstrated that two mechanisms are operated in sequence: the initial requirement of N-cadherin in the formation of MCS, and the later involvement of P-cadherin in the subsequent adhesion to the peritoneal mesothelium, which is in support of the sequential steps of the ovarian metastatic cascade. Moreover, we provide evidence of a novel interplay linking P-cadherin to the regulation of b1 integrin activation via the induction of the Golgi glycosyltransferase ST6Gal-I in this process. While these are seen as distinct systems, there is increasing evidence that a fine-tuned crosstalk between cadherins and integrins can generate a high degree of specificity in cell adhesion than the intrinsic specificity of individual receptors. Publications: Journal article: #2 Conference proceeding: #1 [awarded ECCO Fellowship Grant] Objective 2: We show for the first time that N-cadherin has a dominant effect over other cadherins on MCS formation of ovarian cancer cells. In addition to cell-cell adhesion, we show that N-cadherin can activate specific downstream signal transduction via Wnt/b-catenin and Wnt/Ca2+ crosstalk. This may indicate how an increase in N-cadherin expression in MCS is likely to promote the progression of ovarian cancer. Journal article: #2, #5 Objective 3: On exploring how p70S6K may regulate N-cadherin, we show that this is activated through two critical transcriptional regulators Twist and Sox9. Interestingly, we found that this activation of Twist and Sox9 is not the result from changes in rate of transcription, but mRNA stabilities. Using computational and experimental approaches, we identify a role of miR-145 in coregulating both Twist and Sox-9 to enhance N-cadherin due to p70S6K activation. We also provide evidence that this tumorigenic activity is associated with the ability of p70S6K to regulate miRNA biogenesis through tristetraprolin/Dicer interaction. To date, while the downstream targets of miRNAs are well defined, the underlying mechanisms of how miRNAs are deregulated are largely unknown. Our results shed new light on the p70S6K as a novel, important regulator of miRNA biogenesis that may underlie poor outcome in ovarian cancer. Journal article: #4 Conference proceedings: #2 [awarded ECCO Fellowship Grant], #3 Taken together, our data strongly support the important role for p70S6K in ovarian cancer metastasis and provide a mechanistic rationale for targeting p70S6K or its associated signaling in the treatment of metastatic ovarian cancer. Journal article: #1, #3 Book chapter: #6

782111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
782111.value: We reveal the novel identification of p70S6K regulation on both MCS formation and MCS-matrix adhesion that have pivotal roles in the metastatic progression of ovarian cancer. This reveals a new direction for understanding the oncogenic role of p70S6K in ovarian cancer metastasis and implicate that p70S6K could be a promising therapeutic target. Given the potential side effects of mTOR inhibitors, it is of great interest to develop a safe and effective therapeutic approach. We and others have demonstrated the use of siRNA to efficiently and specifically downregulate “undruggable” genes. However, one major limitation is targeted RNA delivery. We have developed vesicle-like nanostructures based on dendrimers as effective carriers for siRNA delivery in novel RNAi therapeutic applications (Kala et al., (2014) J. Med. Chem. 57: 2634-2642). We are actively pursuing in this direction. To expand our understanding of the complex mechanisms of action of p70S6K, we plan to take a proteomic approach to reveal a portrait of the entire signaling network. We will also examine p70S6K mediated bidirectional interactions between ovarian cancer cells and tumor microenvironment, leading to increased malignancy. These findings should highlight the functional importance of tumor-host crosstalk in impacting malignant cell behavior and implies important clinical implications.

782111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
782111.value: Ovarian cancer is highly lethal and the major form of cancer death of all gynecological malignancies. No effective therapy is currently available, with a poor 5-year survival rate (<25%). Thus, there is a need for new therapeutic targets and a better understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying the progression of ovarian cancer. MCS mimic most of the in vivo properties and key hallmarks of cancer. Several of our new findings of this project indicate that p70S6K may contribute to the MCS formation and expansion and that it could be a promising target. (i) We show for the first time a new role for p70S6K on MCS formation through N-cadherin, modulating both adhesion and outside-in signaling. (ii) We also present evidence suggesting p70S6K in the tumor microenvironment, such as MCS-mesothelium communication, which is a rate-limiting step for the onset of the metastatic cascade. (iii) We identify p70S6K as a novel regulator of global miRNA biogenesis that may underlie the poor outcome in ovarian cancer. These results reveal a new direction for understanding the oncogenic roles of p70S6K and highlight its importance as a viable therapeutic target. Targeting p70S6K may thus be a useful approach in the treatment of ovarian cancer metastasis.

782411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
782411.value: 肝癌（肝細胞癌，HCC）是全世界最主要的惡性腫瘤之一，尤其多見於亞洲。肝癌極具侵略性，且往往由於發現較晚以及頻繁的腫瘤轉移而預後較差。更好的了解肝癌發生及轉移過程中潛在的分子機理至關重要，因為這可以為開發新的診斷工具和治療措施提供新的機會。表觀遺傳改變和microRNA（miRNA）的調節紊亂是人類癌症發生的標誌，在腫瘤轉移過程中也發揮重要作用。最近的研究結果表明，表觀遺傳改變可能會促進microRNA的調節紊亂。多梳性蛋白抑制複合物2（PRC2），包括EZH2，EED，SUZ12和RBBP4/7，是一類重要的表觀遺傳調節器，用來控制特定的基因在胚胎發育和細胞走向中的表達模式。由PRC2介導的多梳性抑制的特點是H3K27的甲基化，这个甲基化是一種由EZH2介導的阻遏性組蛋白修飾。PRC2的成員在人類癌症中常常過度表達，並與癌症轉移緊密關聯。與此一致的是，我們發現PRC2的成員也常常在人类肝癌中過度表達。尤其是EZH2的高表達，明顯在肝癌的發生及轉移中發揮重要作用。以往的研究解釋了多梳性抑制在腫瘤抑制基因失活中的功能作用。然而，多梳性抑制是否對人類癌症中miRNA失調發揮作用尚未有明確解決。通過利用EZH2基因沉默模型，我們發現了肝癌中一小類被多梳性抑制的miRNA。在這些miRNA中，miR-139作為一種腫瘤抑制miRNA，卻於所有EZH2沉默的細胞裡表達一致升高。此外，EZH2和miR-139在原發性肝癌樣本中的表達水平呈負相關關係。根據這些初始數據，我們進一步推測miR-139可能是肝癌中多梳性抑制的一個重要靶點，而且肝癌中高表達的EZH2是通過抑制miR-139來行使其致癌作用的。此研究計劃旨在研究多梳性抑制在miRNA失調中的深層意義，並利用miR-139作為“原理論證”模型來解釋這些microRNA是怎樣有助於EZH2在人肝癌中的致癌作用。我們相信，我們計劃中的工作會對肝癌發生及轉移的分子機理提出新的見解。在這項研究中產生的數據可能會促進對此致命癌症新的診療措施的發展。

782411.label: Major findings and research outcome
782411.value: 1. EZH2 mediated polycomb silencing and miR-139 down-regulation We previously showed that miR-139 was frequently down-regulated in human HCC. To test whether EZH2 is involved in epigenetic silencing of miR-139, HCC cell lines were treated with EZH2 inhibitor, 3-deazaneplanocin A (DZNep) or siRNA against EZH2. We found that inactivation of EZH2 successfully restored miR-139 expression in HCC cell lines. With ChIP assay, we further demonstrated the direct binding of EZH2 and its consequent H3K27methylation enrichment at miR-139 promoter region. Knockdown of EZH2 not only reduced EZH2 binding to miR-139 promoter but also suppressed H3K27methylation at that region. With the above findings, we concluded that EZH2 binds to miR-139 promoter and suppresses miR-139 expression via H3K27 methylation. 2. EZH2 mediated miR-139 repression and HCC metastasis We identified ROCK2 as a downstream target of miR-139. ROCK2 was frequently up-regulated in human HCC and was significantly correlated with HCC metastatic features. Loss of miR-139 expression in HCC was associated with EZH2 and ROCK2 overexpressions. Treatment of EZH2 inhibitor (DZNep) significantly induced miR-139 expression and concomitantly suppressed ROCK2 expression. As a consequence of ROCK2 inhibition, we also observed a phenotypic change on cytoskeletal reorganization in HCC cell lines, including loss of focal adhesion and suppression of stress-fiber formation. The data obtained in this study supported our hypothesis that EZH2-miR-139 pathway is important for HCC metastasis. 3. The pathological implication of EZH2-mediated microRNA repression in human HCC. Base on the miRNA expression profile change upon stably EZH2 depletion in three different HCC cell lines, we identified a subset of EZH2-regulated microRNAs. These miRNAs exhibited a general trend of down-regulation in human HCCs. Significant down-regulation was observed for 7 miRNAs, namely miR-139-5p, miR-125b, miR-101, miR-511, miR-99a*, let-7c and miR-200b, suggesting that EZH2-mediated silencing of these miRNAs may be critical to HCC development. In silico analysis revealed that EZH2-regulated miRNAs can potentially modulate cell motility through Rho/ROCK cytoskeleton reorganization axis. In addition to miR-139, we demonstrated that miR-200b, another EZH2-regualted microRNA, also negatively regulates RhoA and ROCK2, two master regulators of actin cytoskeletal reorganization. Re-expression of miR-200b suppressed Rho/ROCK mediated stress-fiber and focal adhesion formation and abolished in vitro cell migration ability and lung metastasis in mouse model. These experimental findings were in line with the above mentioned in silico prediction and confirmed that EZH2 overexpression contribute to HCC metastasis by epigenetics silencing of multiple tumor suppressive microRNAs. The above findings have been published in peer-reviewed journals, listed in Part C.

782411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
782411.value: In this study, we identified a subset of EZH2-regualted microRNAs. Among these, miR-101, miR-200b and Let-7 have been previously reported as negative regulators of EZH2 itself or other PRC2 components. This observation suggests that EZH2/PRC2 and its microRNA targets may form a self-reinforce feed-forward loop in driving liver cancer metastasis. This interesting hypothesis is definitely worth for further investigation.

782411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
782411.value: Liver cancer (Hepatocellular carcinoma, HCC) is a common and lethal cancer in Hong Kong and Main land China. It is commonly believed that accumulation of genetic alterations, epigenetic abnormalities and microRNA deregulations are the driving force of liver cancer initiation and development. We found that EZH2, a H3K27 specific histone methyltransferase, was frequently up-regulated in liver cancer and implicated in cancer metastasis. However the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. In this study, we tested the hypothesis that overexpression of EZH2 contribute to microRNA deregulation in liver cancer. By compare the microRNA expression profiles in EZH2 knock-down HCC cell lines, we identified a subset of EZH2-regualted microRNAs. We further showed that EZH2 silenced the expression of tumor suppressive microRNAs, miR-139 and miR-200b in liver cancer. Interestingly, we found that both miR-139 and miR-200b functioned as negative regulators of Rho/ROCK signaling pathway. Rho/ROCK signaling pathway is the central regulator of actin cytoskeletal reorganization and is crucial for cell motility. Loss of miR-139 and miR-200b resulted in hyper-activation of Rho/ROCK signaling pathway and thereby contributed to facilitate liver cancer metastasis. In conclusion, we demonstrated in this study, EZH2 overexpression promoted liver cancer metastasis by suppressed the expression of multiple tumor suppressive microRNAs.

782811.label: Project Objectives
782811.value: To investigate the association between the various health-related events during the different stages of early childhood, and the occurrence of three main types of DDE at both the subject and the tooth levels in a group of 15-year-old children who have been participants of the ‘Hong Kong Children of 1997’ birth cohort.

782811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
782811.value: The enamel of the tooth is the hardest substance in the human body. Enamel is formed during a certain period of the tooth development and is irreplaceable. Developmental defects of enamel (DDE) are deviations from the normal appearance and texture of the enamel as a result of abnormal enamel production. The DDE are irreversible, possibly causing tooth sensitivity and pain, and individuals can experience social stigma. Lengthy treatment may be required to improve the appearance and function of the affected teeth. Although DDE are preventable, data on the causal factors is generally very limited and conflicting. Reported putative factors are health-related events during tooth development in early childhood including excess ingestion of fluoride and infectious diseases. However, these suggested factors have been predominately obtained from unreliable parental recall in retrospective studies of small sample sizes. Most of the children that participated in those studies were younger than 10 years, before all of the permanent teeth had erupted. Given the relatively high prevalence of DDE in Hong Kong children (70% - 99%) and its dental, psychological and financial burdens, the local investigation into the causes of DDE is warranted. Therefore, the aim of this study is to examine the risk factors for the occurrence of DDE among children in Hong Kong. The 1600 participants in our study will be recruited from the ‘Hong Kong Children of 1997’ birth cohort. This specific group will provide a representative sample of Hong Kong children, and also provide prospectively and accurately documented information of health-related events in their early childhood. This represents a unique opportunity to study DDE in full sets of permanent teeth in 15-year-old children. The teeth of the children that participate will be examined for the presence of DDE according to the World Health Organization’s recommended criteria. This will be performed by one trained and calibrated examiner with no knowledge of the children’s health-related events. Correlations between the occurrence of DDE and any health-related events during tooth development, which will be extracted from the ‘Hong Kong Children of 1997’ database, will be statistically analysed. The risk factors identified in our study will add to the scant body of knowledge on the aetiology of DDE. The findings of the study can help the clinicians when explaining and discussing the presence of DDE with patients and their parents. Targeting risk factors could assist in implementation of community strategies to limit the occurrence of DDE. 研究背景： 牙釉質是最硬的人體組織。牙釉質是在牙齒發育的特定時期形成並且不能更替。牙釉質發育缺陷 (Developmental defects of enamel，DDE) 是牙齒發育過程中硬組織基質的形成和礦化的紊亂所導致的牙釉質的形態和質地的異常。牙釉質發育缺陷是不可逆的，可導致牙齒敏感和疼痛，而且影響外觀。爲了改善美觀和功能，患牙常需進行冗長的治療。牙釉質發育缺陷可以預防，但是關於其致病因子的研究相當有限並且結論迥異。文獻報導過的可能影響因素均為幼兒在牙齒發育時期的一些健康相關事件，包括過量攝入氟化物和羅患感染性疾病。然而，這些影響因素絕大部份來自于單憑家長事後回憶的小樣本回顧性研究，缺乏可靠性。再者，由於大部份參與這些研究的兒童小於10歲，其恒牙並未全部萌出。基於牙釉質發育缺陷在香港的高發生率（70% - 99%）和其在牙科、心理和治療費用的沉重負擔，牙釉質發育缺陷的致病因子值得深入研究。因此，本研究的目的在於檢測導致香港兒童牙釉質發育缺陷的危險因子。 材料和方法： 本研究將從“香港九七的兒女”出生隊列中隨機抽取1600名兒童。“香港九七的兒女”出生隊列是香港代表性的人群，從其出生開始就準確地記錄了大量的健康相關事件。這為研究香港15歲學童全口恒牙牙釉質發育缺陷提供了獨一無二的機會。參與本研究的學童將接受牙釉質發育缺陷的檢查，檢查方法將按照世界衛生組織推薦的標準進行。所有的學童將由1名受過培訓和校準的檢查者進行檢查。15歲學童牙釉質發育缺陷的發生與從 “香港九七的兒女”數據庫中獲取的牙齒發育期間健康相關事件的相互關係將通過統計分析解答。 研究意義： 本研究所篩選出導致釉質發育缺陷的危險因子將增進學界對釉質發育缺陷病因學的瞭解。本研究結果將幫助臨床醫生更好地與患者以及其家長就其釉質發育缺陷的發生進行溝通。靶中的牙釉質發育缺陷危險因子更將有助於公共衛生計劃的制定以減低牙釉質發育缺陷的發生率。

782811.label: Realisation of objectives
782811.value: 1. Sample selection The participants in this study were a representative sample of Hong Kong children that offered an opportunity to study the risk factors for the occurrence of DDE of permanent teeth that have developed with the current 0.5ppm fluoride level in the drinking water. A random sample of 1600 children was recruited from secondary schools. Parents were asked to provide written informed consent and students were asked for their assent. The exclusion criteria were students who had inherited defects of the enamel (amelogenesis imperfecta), who wore fixed orthodontic appliance, or who could not complete the clinical examination. 2. Data collection: Clinical examinations to assess DDE in the permanent teeth The clinical examinations of the children were carried out in their secondary schools. The presence of DDE in the 28 permanent teeth (two incisors, one canine, two premolars, and two molars in each quadrant) of participating children was assessed by two trained and calibrated examiner who were blind to the information of the children’s health-related events. Before the examination, each tooth was cleaned with gauze to remove major plaque or food deposits. A portable fibre-optic examination light, a mouth mirror, and a blunt probe were used in the clinical examinations. The probe was used to detect or confirm the presence of any discontinuity of the enamel surface of the teeth. The diagnostic criteria were based on the modified FDI (DDE) Index for use in general screening purposes (FDI 1992). The modified FDI (DDE) Index recognized three main types of DDE, namely, demarcated opacities, diffuse opacities, and hypoplasia. A tooth was excluded from the final analyses if less than one third of the tooth surface was visible during the examination. Five percent of children were randomly selected and re-examined to continuously monitor intra- and inter-examiner reproducibilities. 3. Data collection: Extraction of data of health-related events in the early childhood The information of health-related events were obtained from extant data of the ‘Hong Kong Children of 1997’ birth cohort. Socio-demographic information, mother’s health and health-related habits, family history of diseases, birth characteristics, feeding habits, and child’s growth, development, illnesses, medications, hospitalization, diet, and health-related habits have been documented for this group of children since birth (assessed and recorded at 0, 3, 9, 12 months and then annually). Moreover, the information of health-related events were also obtained by questionnaires filled by the parents.

782811.label: Major findings and research outcome
782811.value: The response rate was 84.8% (n/N = 1357/1600). The levels of intra- and inter- and examiner agreement for the diagnoses of DDE at the tooth level were almost perfect (Kappa value > 0.80). The mouth prevalence of DDE was 90.3%. The mouth prevalence of the three main types of DDE, namely demarcated opacities, diffuse opacities, and hypoplasia, was 8.7 %, 89.8 %, and 1.9 %, respectively (Paper No. 1). The association between the occurrence of DDE and health-related events in the early childhood based on parental questionnaires was not statistically significant (Conference Abstract No. 6). Significant results were obtained when statistical analyses were conducted only on children who had the full set of record of health-related events (n=514). Of the various possible aetiological factors considered (Paper No. 2), only experience of severe diseases during the period 0–3 years was associated with the occurrence of ‘any defect’ (p = 0.017) and diffuse opacities (p = 0.044). The children with experience of severe diseases before 3 years of age were 7.89 times more likely to be affected by ‘any defect’ compared with those who did not have the experience (OR 7.89; 95% CI 1.07, 58.14; p = 0.043). However, after adjusting for confounding factors, the association no longer existed (Paper No. 3). Further statistical analyses were conducted to investigate the association between birth weight and infant growth during the first year of life, and the occurrence of DDE in the permanent dentition. In the unadjusted model, infants who had birth weights closer to the WHO average and rapid growth were more likely to have demarcated opacities (p < 0.05); and the first three months of life was the ‘critical period’ to develop demarcated opacities in permanent dentition. However, after adjusting for the confounders (gender, gestational age, mode of delivery, type of feeding, parental education, and health status), significant association with the occurrence of demarcated opacities (p < 0.05) remained only for the children of Trajectory V (heavier birth weights and rapid growth); no ‘critical period’ was found significantly associated with DDE (Paper No. 4).

782811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
782811.value: Future studies could be designed to gather specific detailed information and other potential risk factors for DDE. However, investigations into the effect of antibiotics on DDE are not straightforward because the illness for which the antibiotic was prescribed may have caused the DDE and thereby serve as a confounding factor. Other investigations, especially longitudinal studies, as well as experimental dose response studies and research on the molecular mechanisms triggering the abnormal function of ameloblasts could also be conducted to further expand our knowledge of the aetiology and pathology of DDE.

782811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
782811.value: Developmental defects of enamel (DDE) are deviations from the normal appearance of the enamel as a result of abnormal enamel production. The DDE are irreversible, possibly causing tooth sensitivity and pain. Lengthy treatment may be required to improve the appearance and function of the affected teeth. Our uniquely large prospective cohort study among randomly selected Hong Kong children expands the current knowledge on the aetiology of DDE. We found that experiences of severe diseases experienced during 0–3 years of age were associated with DDE. Our results also indicated that infants with a heavy birth weight and rapid growth during the first year of life were more vulnerable to the occurrence of DDE. The first year of life was a critical period for the formation of DDE. The findings of the study can help the clinicians when explaining and discussing the presence of DDE with patients and their parents. Targeting risk factors could assist in implementation of community strategies to limit the occurrence of DDE. A decrease in the prevalence of DDE could thus reduce the financial burden of dental treatments and of lost time at work and at school, and could also benefit children who experience social stigma.

To identify genes and pathways involved in the regulation of stemness/differentiation axis of lung cancer cells using expression profiling and bioinformatics analysis.

To investigate the role of the candidate stemness/differentiation pathways by correlating their expression with clinicopathological features and testing for effects of gene manipulation on malignant properties of experimental lung cancer models.

783011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
783011.value: Lung cancer is common and has a high mortality due to presentation at advanced stage and lack of curative chemotherapy. Most lung cancers occur in smokers but non-smoking women in Hong Kong have a high incidence. The risk factors in non-smokers are unclear while the genetic mechanism is mostly due to EGFR activating mutations. Despite treatment with anti-EGFR targeted therapy, long term survival is rare because of frequent drug resistance. Recently, the “cancer stem cell” (CSC) theory has been proposed to explain why tumour eradication has not been achieved despite advances in therapy. It proposes that tumours are sustained by a subpopulation of cancer cells, designated as tumor propagating cells (TPC), which can perpetually replicate and possess other cancer-related properties. The non-TPC cells are progenies which have undergone differentiation without replication ability and which have finite life spans. Conventional chemotherapy targets only the non-TPC cells while the TPC survive. To achieve ultimate cure, the TPC must also be targeted. We hypothesize that the CSC model is applicable to lung cancers. The purpose of our study is to identify treatment targets directed against the TPC, or cause the TPC to differentiate to become non-TPC. Our approach is to identify the TPC and non-TPC using protein markers expressed on their cell surface that can be selected by flow cytometry, then isolate them in experimental systems to study their biology and regulatory mechanisms. The profile of expressed genes in TPC and non-TPC would be compared using high-throughout genome-wide analysis platforms and specialized bioinformatics/biostatistics tools. By finding sets of genes which are expressed in TPC but repressed in non-TPC, the mechanisms controlling cell renewal and perpetuate cancer growth could be derived. To further select genes of high importance, their expression levels would be assessed in human lung cancers and correlated with parameters including tumour stage and patient survival. We would also test the role of the identified targets by gene manipulation in cell lines and animal models and observe for their effects especially on cancer cell renewal, tumor maintenance and growth response to, respectively, conventional chemotherapy, anti-EGFR therapy, or combination therapy with anti-TPC treatment. If beneficial effects of disrupting the identified pathways are demonstrated, then these might be potential useful targets against which specific therapy can be designed. In the long run, the anti-TPC therapy could be used as definitive or adjunctive treatment in lung cancer patients.

783011.label: Realisation of objectives
783011.value: This project investigates the molecular pathways that regulate tumour initiating cells (TIC) and tests if these pathways could be manipulated to affect cancer growth. The strategy consists of comparison between TIC and non-TIC in lung cancer cells to identify differentially expressed pathways, followed by validation of the candidate pathways using in vitro and in vivo cancer models. As there is no universal TIC marker, we first investigated multiple candidate markers including CD44, ALDH, CD24, CD166, and CD133 (Objective 1). Cells showing the highest and lowest expression of these candidate markers were designated as TIC and non-TIC, respectively. Using in vitro methods including cell sphere essay, anchorage independent growth and pleuripotency genes expression, etc., and in vivo xenograft models, we demonstrated significantly enhanced tumorigenesis properties of cells showing combined high expressions of ALDH and CD44, implicating these are valid TIC markers in lung cancer. We then investigated for active pathways in TIC regulation by isolating ALDHhighCD44high and ALDHlowCD44low cell populations for comparison of expression profiles using Affymetrix H133 microarrays and pathway mapping by the KEGG databases (Objective 2). The results indicated there is up-regulation of the non-canonical Wnt/Calcium pathway. To evaluate the involvement of this pathway, we selected two mediators NFATc2 and CaMK2A and performed manipulation studies in lung cancer cell lines using genetic knock-in and knock-down, followed by in vitro and in vivo mouse tumorigenicity studies. Indeed, the results corroborated with our hypothesis and demonstrated both candidates play a role in lung cancer tumorigenesis. To demonstrate the clinical relevance of these TIC pathways in human cancers, we postulate tumours showing a high proportion or strong expression of TIC markers and TIC regulators would demonstrate more aggressive phenotype with poorer survival. We studied this by analyzing the expression of CD44/ALDH, NFATc2 and CaMK2 expression in human lung cancers (Objective 3). Patients whose tumours showed higher proportions of CD44/ALDH co-expressing cells, as well as higher NFATc2 expression had lower disease-free survival compared to those with no or low expression, supporting their importance in clinical lung cancers. Overall, this study has achieved 100% success in all 3 objectives. It has identified TIC markers, TIC regulatory pathways as well as demonstrated their clinical relevance in lung cancer.

783011.label: Major findings and research outcome
783011.value: Objective 1-To identify the molecular pathways that regulate tumour initiating cells (TIC), multiple candidate TIC markers were initially tested using flow cytometry isolation and in vitro functional assays, which identified the combined markers ALDH and CD44 were potential lung TIC markers. Expression array comparison showed the ALDHhighCD44high population had upregulation of multiple genes along the non-canonical Wnt/Ca2+ pathway and findings were validated using qPCR. In vitro and in vivo models demonstrated these TIC candidates had enhanced tumorigenicity, drug resistance, cell survival, motility and stemness genes expressions. The results indicated ALDH, CD44 and Wnt/Ca pathways are involved in TIC induction and maintenance (Outputs 8-1, 9-1, 9-2, 10-1, 10-2). Objective 2–To investigate the roles of WNT/calcium pathway genes in TIC activation, 2 candidates were tested. A. Nuclear Factors of Activated T-cells (NFAT) - NFAT consists of 4 homologues (NFATc1-c4) and are calcium-dependent transcription factors activated upon dephosphorylation by the protein phosphatase calcineurin. To study their roles in regulating TIC properties, calcineurin and NFAT were inhibited by pharmacological and stable knockdown using lentiviral shRNA, which led to inhibited in vitro and in vivo tumorigenecity as shown in soft agar colony formation and mice xenografts compared to control (Outputs 9-3, 10-3). B. Calmodulin dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) - Specific pharmacological inhibition by KN93 and/or lentiviral stable knockdown of CaMKII led to attenuated cell spheres in stem cell culture conditions and significantly inhibited anchorage independent growth. In vivo, CaMKII knocked-down cancer cells gave rise to significantly smaller xenografts and insufficient cells for serial passage compared to equal loading of control cells. At the molecular level, lower mRNA expression of SOX2, OCT4 and NANOG were observed in multiple CaMKII-inhibited cell lines (Output 9-4). Objective 3-To explore the clinical relevance of CD44/ALDH and calcium signaling genes, quantitative PCR and immunohistochemistry were used to analyze their expression in human resected lung cancers. Results showed patients whose tumours showed higher proportions of CD44/ALDH co-expressing cells, as well as higher proportion of NFATc2 expression had lower disease-free survival compared to those with no or low expression, supporting their importance in clinical lung cancers. For CaMK2A, although its expression was upregulated in lung cancer compared to normal lung, no statistically significant correlation with survival was detected. These points were illustrated in Outputs 8-1, 9-2, 9-3. Overall, this study has identified ALDH/CD44 over-expression as TIC markers, and shown calcium signaling is involved in TIC regulation, with clinical relevance in lung cancer.

783011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
783011.value: We have shown calcium signaling mediators including NFATc2 and CaMKII are involved in regulation of ALDH/CD44 over-expressing TIC in lung cancer. There are 2 aspects worth further investigation: 1) Evaluate how NFATc2 and CaMKII are linked to pleuripotency pathways. While “stemness” pathways are known to be important for embryonic development, aberrant “stemness” activities could be important for TIC regulation. Finding a link between calcium signaling mediators and aberrant “stemness” genes activities would provide further evidence of their roles in TIC. Along this line, our preliminary data of genetic and luciferase reporter studies show NFATc2 might regulate SOX2 transcription. 2) Evaluate the role of oxidative stress in calcium signaling and TIC induction. The origin of TIC is not well understood. In leukaemia, TIC might arise from adult tissue stem cells but cellular plasticity under stressful growth conditions in cancers might also activate TIC. Since calcium signaling is a known physiological response to intracellular stresses, it would be strategically positioned in the cell signaling network for TIC induction. This can be investigated by subjecting cancer cells to oxidative stress and evaluating whether NFATc2 and CaMKII abrogation by stable knockdown would reduce TIC populations.

783011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
783011.value: It has been hypothesized cancers encompass a tumour intiating cells (TIC) population with tumorigenesis and drug resistance capabilities while non-TIC has limited life span and lower tumour-propagation functions. To test this, we have evaluated multiple candidate TIC markers and observed cells with the highest over-expression of ALDH and CD44 fulfill the criteria as TIC. Expression profile analysis revealed the WNT/calcium signaling pathway might be involved in TIC regulation. We further tested two mediators of this signaling pathway, NFATc2 and CaMKII as potential candidates. Using pharmacological and genetic manipulation, we demonstrated their involvement in maintaining TIC properties including cell spheres formation, cell survival, motility, tumorigenicity and drug resistance, etc., in in vitro and in vivo xenograft models. Assessment of protein expression levels showed patients whose tumours had higher proportions of CD44/ALDH co-expressing cells, as well as higher proportions of NFATc2 expression had lower disease-free survival compared to those with no or low expression, supporting their importance in clinical lung cancers. Although CaMK2A expression was upregulated, no statistically significant correlation with survival was detected. Together, this study has shown the importance of CD44/ALDH and calcium pathway mediators in lung TIC maintenance. Elimination of TIC through targeting these pathways would benefit cancer management.

783111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
783111.value: 背景：口腔疾病仍是香港人口常見的病患。研究指出口腔健康與全身健康可能有某些與生活方式和健康行為有關的共同危險因素；不僅如此，這些危險因素也可能共同存在於同一個家庭的成員之間。爲了更好的理解上述危險因素的內在關係，大量關於社會人口學特徵、生活模式、口腔健康及全身健康的相關行為，以及口腔和全身健康狀況的資料需要被收集分析。“愛+人”計劃是一個由香港賽馬會贊助香港大學公共衛生學校執行的大規模家庭項目。大量關於社會人口學特徵，生活模式，全身健康相關行為和全身健康狀態的資料已經在上述項目中被收集。現在，我們正在收集“愛+人”計劃中有5-7歲兒童的家庭中家庭成員的口腔健康相關行為和口腔健康狀況的資料，預計在2011年初將完成500個家庭的資料收集。通過將兩個數據庫的資料合併，我們可以建立一個社會行為健康模型解釋上述內在關係。申請此項基金，是爲了進行三年的追蹤調查這500個家庭。這樣我們就可以有更多的數據建立新模型，並觀察口腔健康的變化是否會影響已建立的模型的穩定性和一致性。定期齒科檢查是香港牙科健康宣傳中最常提到的建議之一，但是在成年人中，關於定期齒科檢查是否能預測口腔健康變化和由此變化產生的健康影響的研究調查非常少見。 目的：這項研究的目的是建立並檢驗一個包括同一個家庭中家庭成員的社會人口學特徵、生活模式、口腔健康及全身健康的相關行為、口腔和全身健康狀況的社會行為健康模型的穩定性和一致性；研究定期齒科檢查是否能預測三年後的口腔健康變化，並探索在基線時可以預測三年後口腔健康變化的危險因素。 方法：在2011年初將完成調查香港賽馬會贊助的“愛+人”計劃中有5-7歲兒童的家庭作為基線調查對象。所有已參與基線調查的家庭將獲邀參與此次三年的追蹤調查。通過基線和跟蹤調查的資料，結構方程模型 (Structural Equation Modeling) 將用於建立並檢驗包括同一個家庭中家庭成員的社會人口學特徵、生活模式、口腔健康及全身健康的相關行為，以及口腔和全身健康狀況的社會行為健康模型的穩定性和一致性。廣義線性模型 (General Linear Models) 將用於研究定期齒科檢查在平衡了基線時其他危險因素如口腔健康知識、態度、行為和牙科保險等的作用後是否能預測三年後的口腔健康變化。 可能的結果和意義：本研究產生的信息對於瞭解香港人口的口腔健康狀況有巨大意義。這是首次也是難得的可以建立和驗證一個有關家庭成員的社會行為健康模型的機會。同時，也可以觀察牙科服務使用對成人口腔健康狀況是否有影響。本次研究的結果有助於正確審查口腔健康和其相關行為與全身健康兩者之間的關係。研究結果亦可為香港今後口腔健康策略和口腔健康推廣項目，特別是怎樣將其融入到全身健康推廣項目提供有用的信息並提高其效率。上述幾點都將對本港人口的口腔健康促進起到巨大貢獻。

783111.label: Realisation of objectives
783111.value: The project aimed to follow up all 432 families participated in the baseline study. Telephone calls were made during December 2012 to August 2014 to arrange visits to their homes to obtain written consent and collect survey and clinical data. Altogether, 354 families were successfully contacted after three years and 209 families (59%) with 161 fathers, 195 mothers and 209 children were followed up. For objective 1, structural equation models were fitted to the follow-up data to assess the stability and consistency of the socio-behavioural oral health models built using baseline data. For objective 2, regular dental visit was used as one of the independent variables in the generalized linear models to predict 2 oral health outcomes, new caries and the number of new or deeper pocket developed over 3 years. For objective 3, changes of each oral health behaviour (tooth brushing frequencies, use of dental floss, mouth rinse, regular dental visit, dental insurance and smoking habit) were tested by McNemar tests or paired t-tests. Logistic regression was conducted to explore baseline factors, such as socio-demographics (age, household income, and education), oral health related behaviors (tooth brushing frequency, habit of flossing, use of mouth rinse, smoking habit, dental insurance coverage and snacking habit), oral health knowledge and attitude, and visible plaque index (VPI%) that were associated with the change of regular dental check-up over 3 years. Generalized linear models were used to evaluate the effect of risk factors at baseline mentioned above together with regular dental visit on the 2 oral health outcomes (new caries and the number of new or deeper pocket developed over 3 years).

783111.label: Major findings and research outcome
783111.value: The socio-behavioural oral health models were generally stable and consistent over 3 years for both fathers and mothers, except that the association of smoking on oral health status was not significant. Hypothesized pathways from socio-economic status and modifiable factors to the oral health status in fathers and mothers in Hong Kong are not rejected. For caries (tooth decay) conditions, the outcome was measured by the number of new caries (NC) developed. More than one third of the children, more than half of the fathers and mothers developed NC over 3 years. Children with higher baseline snack score (IRR=1.16, p=0.021); fathers with higher baseline VPI% (IRR=1.15 for every 10% increase, p=0.005); and mothers with lower baseline household income (IRR>1, p=0.025) were found to predict higher NC. (refers to Publication 2) For periodontal conditions, the outcome was mainly measured by Gingival Bleeding Index (GBI) to assess the gingival health status for children and the number of sextants with new or deeper pockets (NDP) to assess the change in periodontal condition for adults. The mean GBI (%) of the children was around 23% at both baseline and follow up and not much changes had occurred over the 3 years. Around 60% of the fathers and 50% of the mothers had formation of NDP (mean numbers of sextants with NDP = 1.7 and 1.0 respectively). Tooth brushing habit and household income at baseline were found to predict periodontal disease progression for the mothers. While for fathers, baseline oral hygiene status predicted periodontal disease progression. The correlation of deteriorated periodontal status was identified among members in the families. (refers to Publication 1) For oral health behaviours, more fathers (from 34% to 45%) and mothers (from 33% to 47%) reported having regular dental check-up after three years. Significant positive correlations between the fathers, mothers and their children’s tooth brushing habit, use of dental floss and dental utilization were found at baseline and follow up (except for the use of dental floss between the parents and their children). Logistic regressions were conducted to assess the baseline factors that were associated with the transition from no regular dental visit to regular dental visit for fathers and mothers. For fathers, no significant predictors were identified. Mother from families with higher family income were found to have a lower chance to change to visiting dentists regularly than mothers from families with lower income (odds ratio=0.07, p<0.001). (refers to Publication 2)

783111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
783111.value: This study is the only prospective study that followed a substantial group of married couples with children in Hong Kong. It provides a unique opportunity in investigating the oral health behaviors and status among members in a family (fathers, mothers and their children) and seeking for further development of oral health policies and promotion programmes in Hong Kong. Our findings suggest that oral health promotion should focus on the whole family instead of individuals. In future oral health promotion activities the whole family members should be involved to improve the effect of such promotion. We also suggest that oral health education programs may improve oral health status. In this study, fathers and mothers who were in higher socio-economic status had better oral health knowledge and attitudes. Since socio-economic status cannot change easily, these findings suggest that oral health education activities should pay more attention to people in poor socio-economic status. Hopefully, this can improve their oral health knowledge and attitudes, help them to adopt better oral health behaviors, and subsequently improve their oral health. More large-scale prospective studies with collection of longitudinal data of longer follow up periods are needed for better understanding of oral disease progression and its predicting factors.

783111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
783111.value: This study is the only prospective study in Hong Kong that followed a substantial group of married couples with children over 3 years to explore the changes of oral health behaviors and status among family members over time, their possible correlations and to identify the baseline factors in predicting change in oral health behaviors and status. It provides a unique opportunity in investigating the oral health behaviors and status among members in a family (fathers, mothers and their children) and seeking for further development of oral health policies and promotion. Our findings have shown that oral health behaviors and status among family members are correlated. We suggest that oral health promotion activities should focus and involve the whole family in order to improve the effect of such promotion. In this study, fathers and mothers who were in higher socio-economic status had better oral health knowledge and attitudes. Since socio-economic status cannot change easily, we suggest that oral health education activities should pay more attention to people in poor socio-economic status. Hopefully, this can improve their oral health knowledge and attitudes, help them to adopt better oral health behaviors, and subsequently improve their oral health.

783611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
783611.value: Over 60% of pathogenic viruses in humans originate from animals. Transmissions of these viruses from animals to humans require one or more steps of interspecies jumping. A better understanding of the diversity of different families of viruses in humans and animals, their genomics, phylogenetic relationships and evolutionary histories and the molecular mechanisms of interspecies jumping is of great biological interests and has major practical values. In the past 5 years, our group has been one of the most active groups in the discovery, complete genome sequencing, comparative genomics and phylogenetic studies in novel human and animal positive-sense single stranded RNA viruses, including coronaviruses and picornaviruses. Although picornaviruses have been found in a variety of animals, there are still animals where picornaviruses have never been discovered or rarely reported. Therefore, we hypothesized that previously unrecognized picornaviruses may be present in these animals. Furthermore, we also hypothesized that some of these previously unrecognized picornaviruses may be closely related to existing picornaviruses. The hypothesis is supported by our recent discovery of turdiviruses 1, 2 and 3 from dead wild birds in Hong Kong and proposal of two novel genera, Orthoturdivirus and Paraturdivirus, in the Picornaviridae family. Furthermore, preliminary results we obtained from our pilot molecular epidemiology study, in over 500 bats sampled in various regions in Hong Kong, are also in line with our hypothesis. Three novel bat picornaviruses that appear to represent novel picornavirus genera were observed. With the complete genome sequencing of these novel bat picornaviruses, as well as other novel picornaviruses that we found in our on-going surveillance studies, comparative genomics and phylogenetic analysis can be performed. Such studies will lead to an in-depth understanding on the evolutionary history and what has happened at the molecular level at the crucial moments of interspecies jumping in the evolution of picornaviruses.

783611.label: Realisation of objectives
783611.value: For the first objective, we have performed complete genome sequencing on a total of 12 novel bat and animal picornaviruses. Three novel picornaviruses were discovered in bats, one from cats, two from dogs and six from chickens. For the second objective, we have annotated the genomes of these 12 novel bat and animal picornaviruses. For the third objective, we have performed comparative genomics and phylogenetic studies on the novel and existing picornaviruses. The results of these discoveries have been published in five papers in international refereed journals.

783611.label: Major findings and research outcome
783611.value: In these studies, we have identified a total of 12 novel picornaviruses from bats and other animals. In the first study, among 1108 bats of 18 species studied, three novel picornaviruses (group 1, 2 and 3) were identified from alimentary specimens of 12 bats from five species and four genera. In the second study, among 662 cats, FePV was detected in fecal samples of 14 cats and urine samples of two cats. In the third study involving 1472 samples from 368 dogs over a 22-month period, we identified a novel picornavirus (PDLV), with a genome structure in between those of the Dicistroviridae and Picornaviridae families, from 47 fecal and urine samples. In the fourth study, we discovered a novel canine picornavirus in fecal, nasopharyngeal and urine samples of dogs. In the fifth study, 6 novel picornaviruses were identified from 900 chickens. In these 5 studies, one or more than one genome of each novel picornavirus was sequenced. Phylogenetic analysis revealed a previously unrecognized high diversity of picornaviruses. In particular, in the third study, sequencing and phylogenetic analysis of three complete genomes revealed that although it seems that PDLV was most closely related to other picornaviruses, P1, P2 and P3 of PDLV possessed very low amino acid identities of <20%, <20% and <30% to the P1, P2 and P3 of all other known picornaviruses and there were <35% amino acid identities between the 3Dpol of PDLV and all other picornaviruses. Distinct from other picornaviruses, the genomes of PDLV contain two open reading frames, encoding two polyprotein precursors (844 and 1406 amino acids), separated by an intergenic region (IGR) of 588 bases. Dual-luciferase activity assay by DNA and RNA transfection revealed that both IRESes were functional. This is the first report of natural occurrence of two functional IRESes in non-dicistroviruses.

783611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
783611.value: To understand a virus family, one of the first steps is to understand its diversity, genomics and phylogeny. In this study and our previous studies on picornaviruses, we have built up a phylogenetic map for picornaviruses. These have laid down an important foundation for studying picornavirus diversity, phylogeny and interspecies jumping events. Further surveillance studies of different animal species from different parts of the world will help to build up a more detail phylogenetic map for picornaviruses.

783611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
783611.value: In the past ten years, our group has discovered a total of 16 novel human and animal picornaviruses, including turdivirus 1, 2 and 3; rhinovirus C; bat picornavirus 1, 2 and 3; feline picornavirus; canine picodicistrovirus; canine picornavirus; chicken picornavirus 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5; and chicken gallivirus 1. Among these discoveries, we are the first in the world to report picornaviruses in bats, cats and dogs. In addition to discovering the viruses, we have also performed complete genome sequencing on all these novel viruses. These have helped us understand the diversity of this important family of virus and have laid down the foundation for future downstream studies. In the basic molecular biology point of view, we have discovered the first natural occurrence of two functional internal ribosomal entry sites in non-dicistroviruses, which is considered revolutionary in this field.

783711.label: Project Objectives
783711.value: Develop and optimize a cellular MRI protocol to characterize SVZ NSP cell migratory activities in rodent brains: We will minimize image susceptibility distortions by MPIO infusion using an implanted pump, and we will increase labeling efficiency with a transfection agent. We will implement and optimize the MRI acquisition and analysis protocol on a 7T rodent MRI scanner, including high-resolution T2*-weighted imaging, recently developed quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM), and analysis of NSP cell migration trajectories and characteristics. MRI of NSP cell activities in normal developing brains: We will evaluate and validate the MRI protocol by monitoring NSP cell migration during brain development between postnatal day 7 (P7) and P90. MRI results will be analyzed for detecting and characterizing the changes in NSP cell migratory activities, and then correlated and validated with immunohistochemical analyses. The study will provide a comprehensive documentation of neonatal SVZ neurogenesis for the first time. MRI of NSP cell activities in injured developing brains: We will employ the MRI protocol to investigate the NSP cell migratory activities in well-established mild and severe neonatal injury models. Upon hypoxic-ischemic insult at P7, brains will be examined for NSP cell activities in both acute and subacute injury phases. NSP cell migratory characteristics and their alterations will be analyzed and correlated with immunohistochemical analyses.

783711.label: Realisation of objectives
783711.value: Objective #1. This technical Objective has been largely met. We have developed and optimised a cellular MRI protocol to characterize SVZ NSP cell migratory activities. We have designed schemes to minimise the image susceptibility distortions due MPIO infusion using an implanted pump. We have implemented and optimized the MRI acquisition and analysis protocol on a 7T rodent MRI scanner. Our new protocol development included T2*-weighted imaging, QSM and more quantitative analysis of NSP cell migration trajectories and characteristics. Our efforts have also led to more MRI methodological developments, which are published in leading journals of MRI physics/applications and international MRI conferences. Objective #2. This Objective has been met with mostly met as well. We have investigated the NSP cell activities in normal developing brains with the proposed MRI neurogenesis imaging method. We evaluated and MRI protocol by monitoring NSP cell migration during brain development between P7 and P90. MRI results have been analyzed for detecting and characterizing the changes in NSP cell migratory activities, and then correlated with immunohistochemical analyses. The results provided a comprehensive documentation of neonatal SVZ neurogenesis. Our efforts here have also led to new insights, particularly regarding the brain functions. Objective #3. This Objectively have been met with partial success. We employed the MRI protocol to investigate the NSP cell migratory activities in well-established mild and severe neonatal injury models. We observed alterations in NSP cell activities and migration patterns. However, the results varied greatly among individual subjects, preventing us from a better understanding of the exact effects on NSP neurogenesis. However, the preliminary results have led us to explore how to proactively modulate neurogenesis activities, for example, by ontogenetic stimulations. This thought has led to our recent development of optogenetic manipulation of brain activities, including neurogenesis, connectivity and functions.

We employed the MRI protocol to investigate the NSP cell migratory activities in well-established mild and severe neonatal injury models. We observed alterations in NSP cell activities and migration patterns.
