However, the preliminary results have led us to explore how to proactively modulate neurogenesis activities, for example, by ontogenetic stimulations.

783711.label: Major findings and research outcome
783711.value: 1. We have successfully developed and validated a novel MRI method to use MPIO to label NSP cells in vivo, and then high-resolution and quantitative MRI to track and visualise sub ventricular neural progenitor stem (NSP) cells. We achieve this by optimising the MPIO labeling strategies that include (1) both the single-bolus subventricular injection and slow and programmed delivery by implantable infusion pump into subventricular region; (2) image quantification and analysis algorithms; and (3) histological verifications. Positive results have been obtained through persistent efforts. The optimized protocols have been applied to monitor and quantify the NPC activities as proposed in the original applications. 2. Results from these efforts, new research directions have been developed. In particular, ,anganese-enhanced MRI (MEMRI) have been pursued to monitor and image the NPC and other cell activities and structures in vivo. This approach, together with diffusion tensor MRI, has led to a number of interesting findings in then normal and abnormal or injured brains in this project. 3. Resulting from this project, BOLD fMRI and resting-state fMRI (rsfMRI) and ontogenetic neuromodulation have been explored and pursued recently as an alternative way to study brain functions and structures (such as auditory functions and brain networks in addition to endogenous NPC activities)under normal and manipulated conditions. Further, efforts have been made to improve the MRI signal to noise ratio, which may lead to better MRI image quality and more reproducible results in this project. NOTE that some of the findings from these three areas are published recently in international conferences (ISMRM annual meetings) and top neuroimaging journals (Neuroimage & Magnetic Resonance in Medicine), and leading international MRI conference (i.e., International Society for Magnetic Resonance in Medicine - ISMRM).

783711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
783711.value: 1. Research collaborations with Xian Jiaotong University in Mainland China are currently under way to determine if the MRI method developed in this project could be employed to study SVZ NPC migration with respect to glioma presence. The outcome of this collaboration, if positive, can lead to important clinical implications regarding the glioma progression in patients. 2. A new research direction has been created from this study. That is whether otpogenetic modulation can alter neurogenesis. The development of our neurogenesis MRI, functional MRI such as BOLD and connectivity imaging will offer us an powerful platform to visualise the effects of ontogenetic modulations and their effects on brain functions and neurogenesis. A number of conference presentations have been made in this regard, few journal publications are currently under preparation.

783711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
783711.value: This research is to develope MRI tracking of endogenous neural stem and progenitor (NSP) cell migration in vivo as a new approach to characterization of endogenous neurogenesis that is undetectable by techniques now in use. Modulation of neurogenesis can be a fundamental mechanism of cellular and functional brain repair. Development of imaging methods to track and monitor these endogenous NSP cells in vivo would be essential to understanding their intrinsic migration activities under normal, developing, diseased, and genetically or pharmacologically modified conditions. Our primary hypothesis is that cellular MRI, by labeling endogenous NSP cells in situ in the subventricular zone with micron-sized iron oxide particles (MPIOs), will provide a sensitive means to detect and characterize endogenous neurogenesis in normal, developing and pathological brains in vivo. Here we developed a new cellular MRI approach to characterize the migration of endogenous NSP cells from the SVZ in normal developing and injured brains. This cellular MRI approach will substantially augment the usefulness of preclinical MRI as a new means of characterizing endogenous cell migratory activities in the brain in vivo.

783811.label: Project Title(Chinese)
783811.value: 以建模評估市民對疫苗引起不良情況的反應對全人口接種計劃的影響

783811.label: Project Objectives
783811.value: To develop a new decision framework for public health officials to incorporate public reactions against post-vaccination adverse events into the operational management of population-wide vaccination against novel pathogens. To evaluate the performance of this new decision framework under a wide range of plausible assumptions regarding vaccine safety, epidemic characteristics and public willingness to vaccinate.
rows: To develop a new decision framework for public health officials to incorporate public reactions against post-vaccination adverse events into the operational management of population-wide vaccination against novel pathogens.
To evaluate the performance of this new decision framework under a wide range of plausible assumptions regarding vaccine safety, epidemic characteristics and public willingness to vaccinate.

783811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
783811.value: Vaccine is the long-term solution for reducing morbidity and mortality associated with emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases. Uptake of vaccination by the general public may be adversely influenced by the discrepancy between the expected and observed frequency of post-vaccination adverse events. For example, during the 2009 influenza pandemic in Hong Kong and Taiwan, post-vaccination adverse events occurred shortly after population-wide vaccination began. In response, the general public immediately casted doubts on the safety of the vaccine and consequently vaccination rate dropped precipitously thereafter. Our goal in this proposed study is to develop and evaluate a new decision framework for incorporating public reactions against post-vaccination adverse events into the operational management of population-wide vaccination against emerging or re-emerging infectious diseases (such as pandemic influenza or SARS). Specifically, we consider the scenario where public health officials are obliged to inform the public on the expected level of post-vaccination adverse events before launching the vaccination program by announcing that as vaccinations are being administered to the population, the program will be halted if the observed frequency of post-vaccination adverse events exceeds a pre-defined threshold θ. We propose the following steps for choosing the optimal value of θ: (1) Obtain the best available evidence on vaccine safety and efficacy from historical data, vaccine trials and expert opinions. (2) Conduct a population survey to gather data on public willingness to vaccinate against the disease for a plausible range of probabilities of post-vaccination adverse events. (3) Choose the value of θ that will best achieve a given objective, e.g. maximizing vaccination coverage or minimizing the number of infections. This study will focus on building and testing a mathematical decision model for step 3 assuming a wide range of plausible scenarios from steps 1 and 2. This new decision framework can serve as a risk management tool for public health officials to assess the expected outcome of the vaccination program which would in turn be useful for informing vaccine procurement, e.g. given the probability distribution of vaccination coverage associated with the optimal θ, how many vaccines should be purchased (in order to avoid large leftover from potential premature termination of the vaccination program)? 每當社會上流行新或舊的傳染病，疫苗是降低發病率和死亡率的長遠解決方案。一般來說，公眾注射疫苗的意願很可能會受觀察到的接種後不良情況(adverse event)所影響。例如2009年流感大流行期間在香港和台灣，疫苗接種計劃開始後不久出現了接種後不良反應的個案，社會上立即出現了對疫苗安全性極大的疑慮，而自此以後疫苗接種率急劇下降。為此，這個研究的目的是考慮如何在一個疫苗計劃中（如流感大流行或SARS），加入考慮市民對不良情況的反應及其影響的元素。具體來說，我們假切以下的情況: 在一個疫苗接種計劃展開之前公共衛生官員須要向公眾宣佈接種後出現不良情況的水平預測，以致如果觀察到的接種後不良事件的頻率超過預先定義的水平θ接種計劃將停止。我們建議以下列步驟計算θ的理想值：（1）從歷史數據、疫苗測試和專家意見獲取最準確的疫苗安全性和有效性的資料。（2）進行人口調查，以收集公眾在合理範圍內的不良情況水平下願意接種疫苗的數據。（3）計算θ的理想值以達到疫苗計劃的既定目標，如最大限度地提高疫苗接種率或盡量減少感染。是次研究的重點是為上述第3步建立一個數學框架。這個新的決策框架可以作為一種風險管理工具以供公共衛生官員評估疫苗接種計劃的預期成果，並能為疫苗採購提供有用的指引，例如：假切已知理想值θ與疫苗接種率的概率分佈，有關當局應購買多少疫苗（以避免潛在提前終止接種計劃所導致的資源浪費）？

783811.label: Realisation of objectives
783811.value: We achieve objective 1 by developing a novel framework for incorporating public reactions to adverse events following immunization (AEFI) into the planning and operations of large-scale vaccination campaigns. This framework is specified as follows: (i) Before the campaign, an estimate of AEFI risk p is available to the policymaker (e.g. based on expert opinions and pre-campaign vaccine trials) in the form of a probability density function (pdf) denoted by f(p) which has mean p_mean and variance p_var. (ii) AEFI risk is monitored in real-time by the maxSPRT algorithm as the campaign proceeds. (iii) The policymaker announces a safety threshold theta on AEFI risk such that the campaign will be halted when the maxSPRT algorithm indicates that the observed AEFI risk exceeds theta (a safety alert). (iv) The policymaker perceives that after theta has been set, the proportion of vaccine target population willing to accept vaccination is A(theta) (e.g. based on population surveys). (v) The policymaker chooses theta to maximize the expected vaccine coverage or minimize the expected infection attack rate (IAR). We achieve objective 2 by evaluating the expected outcomes (probability of safety alert P_SA, expected vaccine coverage E[VC] and expected IAR E[IAR]) of this framework in an illustrative but realistic example which spans a wide range of AEFI risk, pathogen transmissibility and vaccine acceptability. Specifically, the illustrative case makes the following structural assumptions: (i) f(p) is a beta distribution. (ii) Vaccine acceptability A decreases exponentially with the safety threshold theta in the form of A(theta) = A_0*exp(-lambda*theta^kappa) where A_0, lambda and kappa are constants. (iii) Mixing (with respect to disease transmission) is homogeneous and the whole population is targeted for vaccination when the objective is to minimize E[IAR]. We define the default safety threshold theta_def = p_mean and denote the associated vaccine acceptability by A_def. Let theta_VC and theta_IAR be the optimal thresholds for E[VC] and E[IAR] optimization, respectively. We compare the expected outcomes under theta_def, theta_VC, theta_IAR for 10,000 scenarios randomly generated (using Latin-hypercube sampling) from a wide range of vaccine target population size (N), pre-campaign estimates of AEFI risk (pmean and pvar), and vaccine acceptability (A_0, lambda, kappa). From these scenarios, we determine how the expected outcomes depend on model parameters. For ease of exposition, we reparameterize the vaccine acceptability using (i) A_def/0 = A_def /A_0 and (ii) gamma which is the smallest safety threshold above which no one is willing to be vaccinated (see below).

783811.label: Major findings and research outcome
783811.value: Tables and figures in this section refer to that in the attached manuscript. Under theta_def, the pdf of VC resembles a string of wedges followed by a pole at VC = A(theta_def) (Figure 2A). This is the general form of the VC pdf for any selected theta where (i) the ith wedge (from left to right) corresponds to a safety alert triggered by the ith AEFI and (ii) the pole at VC = A(theta) corresponds to completion of the campaign without safety alert. Figure 4 shows that the optimal thresholds and expected outcomes are (i) sensitive to the vaccine acceptability function via mostly A_0 and A_def/0 but not gamma and (ii) sensitive to the target population size and pre-campaign pdf of AEFI probability via the product of N and p_mean but not p_var. Furthermore, differences in expected outcomes under the default and optimal thresholds diminish as N*p_mean increases. In particular, the default threshold is practically optimal if N*p_mean > 20. As such, we describe the characteristics of the optimal thresholds and expected outcomes in the (A_0, A_def/0) plane while fixing N*p_mean, gamma and p_var at some base case values (Table 1). Under theta_def, P_SA remains below 0.2 in all vaccine acceptability scenarios (Figure 3C). Under theta_VC or theta_IAR, P_SA can reach as high as 0.55 when A_def/0 is small (i.e. vaccine acceptability drops sharply as the safety threshold increases from 0 to p_mean¬). In VC optimization, the gain in E[VC] is largest (up to 25%) when A_0 is large and A_def/0 is small (Figure S1). However, such gain is achieved at the expense of substantially increasing P_SA (by as much as 0.5; Figure S1). The increase in E[IAR] in the upper-right quadrant of the (A_0, A_def/0) plane (Figure S1) is a consequence of this tradeoff: in this parameter regime, both A(theta_VC) and A(theta_def) are above the critical coverage VC_crit (the minimal vaccine coverage required for preventing an epidemic; Figure 3B) and hence IAR = 0 under both theta_VC and theta_def if there is no safety alert. Because P_SA is much higher for theta_VC (Figure 3D), E[IAR] under theta_VC becomes higher than that under theta_def. IAR optimization (with R0 = 1.5) exhibits similar characteristics except when A(theta_IAR) is above VC_crit, in which case it is possible to have reductions in both E[IAR] and P_SA when both A_0 and A_def/0 are large (Figure S1).

783811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
783811.value: Our proposed framework can serve as a first step for incorporating public reactions to AEFI into the planning of large-scale vaccination campaigns. We present this framework by analyzing an illustrative case. Our study has several limitations that stem directly from the assumptions made in the illustrative case. First, we assume that the pre-campaign pdf of AEFI risk is a beta distribution. As such, the scenarios considered here do not include situations where expert panel members have disparate a priori estimates of the risk of AEFI (e.g. spanning different orders of magnitude). Second, we consider VC and IAR optimization without any constraints. As shown in our results, the probability of safety alert may be unacceptably high under the optimal thresholds in some scenarios. Finally, we assume only one “type” of AEFI, the risk of which is the same for all individuals in the vaccine target group. In practice, multiple types of AEFIs are monitored in post-market vaccine safety surveillance and vaccine target groups are stratified (e.g. by age) if their risks of AEFIs are expected to be substantially different (e.g. differential baseline risks). Further development of this research should address these limitations.

783811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
783811.value: Public reactions to adverse events following immunization (AEFI) has a large impact on the outcome of large-scale vaccination campaigns. In the future, it is likely that there will be continual increase in public pressure for the safety of new vaccines to be well communicated by public health policymakers before vaccinations begin. Here, we envisage a hypothetical situation in which policymakers proactively incorporate public reactions to AEFI into the planning of vaccination campaign by announcing a safety threshold before the campaign begins such that vaccinations would be halted if the observed frequency of AEFIs exceeds this threshold. We propose and analyze a framework for predicting the outcome of the campaign under different safety thresholds and choosing the optimal threshold for maximizing vaccination coverage or minimizing the number of infections. This framework requires (i) an estimate of the probability distribution of AEFI risk, (ii) an estimate of how vaccine acceptability changes with the threshold, and (iii) a real-time surveillance algorithm for detecting elevated AEFI risk. We illustrate this framework using a realistic case study to elicit some general principles of safety threshold selection. This framework can serve as a step forward for helping policymakers manage public trust in vaccines.

784011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
784011.value: 心肌梗死是围手术期重要的并发症，在糖尿病患者中具有较高的发病率及死亡率。再灌注治疗可以恢复冠脉血流，但再灌注又可能导致致死性组织损伤，称作“缺血再灌注损伤（ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury，IRI）”。 缺血预处理（ischemic preconditioning，IPC）是指在较长的缺血期前给予反复多次短暂的心肌缺血/再灌注，它是保护缺血心肌、减轻IRI的一种有效措施。但由于IPC需在心肌缺血前进行，并需接触冠状动脉血管，因此限制了它的临床应用。针对IPC临床应用的局限性，2003年提出了缺血后处理（ischemic postconditioning，IPostC）的概念，即在长时间的缺血后再灌注即刻给予一次或多次短暂的再灌注/缺血处理可以显著减轻心肌IRI。IPostC和IPC有相似的心肌保护作用，并且，与IPC相似，IPostC心肌保护作用机制与磷脂酰肌醇-3激酶(phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase，PI3K）-Akt信号通路（即Reperfusion Injury Salvage Kinase, RISK通路）活化有关。由于IPostC可在缺血发生后再灌注时实施，可用于突发的不可预见的心肌缺血的治疗，故具有极大的研究意义和临床应用前景。 然而，糖尿病心脏对IPostC敏感性降低，其机制目前还不是很清楚。已证实一氧化氮（nitric oxide，NO）是IPostC的重要调节因子。糖尿病心肌PI3K-Akt信号通路，特别是新证实的生存活化因子增强（Survivor Activating Factor Enhancement，SAFE）途径，即JAK/STAT-3信号通路在糖尿病心肌中受损，这使得通过预处理或后处理保护糖尿病心脏的可行性降低。我们假设糖尿病心脏JAK/STAT-3信号通路受损，继之出现NO的生物利用率降低，可能是糖尿病心肌对IPostC的敏感性缺失的主要机制。 脂联素（adiponectin，APN）是一种来源于脂肪细胞的血浆蛋白，具有抗糖尿病及抗炎症的作用。2型糖尿病患者血浆APN水平降低。研究表明，APN 补充治疗可以增加NO的生成，从而减轻正常小鼠（非糖尿病）心肌IRI。然而，APN对于糖尿病心肌损伤的作用，尤其是糖尿病心脏对IPostC敏感性的影响还未见报道。因此，我们假设APN 可以通过活化新证实的JAK/STAT-3信号通路，增加NO的生成量来恢复糖尿病心脏对IPostC的敏感性。 因此，本课题主要是在1型与2型糖尿病大鼠模型上，探讨糖尿病心脏对IPostC敏感性降低的原因，并研究糖尿病疾病不同发展阶段APN补充治疗减轻心肌IRI及恢复糖尿病心肌对IPostC敏感性的作用及其机制。本课题的实施及完成，将为糖尿病患者在再灌注干预过程中进行药物治疗提供理论及实验依据，对减轻糖尿病心肌梗死的程度及减少心血管并发症将有重要意义。

784111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
784111.value: Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) such as coronary heart disease, stroke and peripheral artery disorders, rank among the top cause of death and disability in our rapidly ageing population. Endothelial dysfunction, which is characterized by an impaired ability to evoke endothelium-dependent vasodilatation and a propensity to endothelium-dependent vasoconstriction, is a key early event of atherosclerosis. Both clinical and animal studies have demonstrated that endothelial dysfunction is a central mediator that links obesity, diabetes and CVD. Therefore, therapeutic interventions targeting at endothelial dysfunction may represent an appealing strategy for prevention of CVD associated with obesity and diabetes. Fibroblast growth factor (FGF21) is a metabolic hormone secreted predominantly by the liver. A large body of animal studies demonstrates that FGF21 possesses multiple beneficial effects against obesity-related metabolic disorders in both rodents and monkeys. Elevation of the circulating levels of FGF21 by either genetic or pharmacological approaches prevents diet-induced obesity and insulin resistance and causes sustained alleviation of hyperglycemia, dyslipidemia and fatty liver disease. In addition to its metabolic functions, recent studies from our laboratory showed that FGF21 can exert its direct actions on endothelial cells where it enhances nitric oxide production, prevents high glucose-induced oxidative stress and apoptosis as well as promotes cell migration and formation of new blood vessels, suggesting that FGF21 is a novel regulator of endothelial function and a potential therapeutic target for cardiovascular disease. Therefore, the primary objective of this proposal is to investigate the physiological roles of FGF21 in modulating vascular homeostasis in animals, and to further delineate the molecular pathways underlying the endothelial actions of FGF21. Furthermore, we will explore the potential of using recombinant FGF21 as a therapeutic agent for treating diabetic vascular injury and endothelial dysfunction in a genetically inherited obese mice with type-2 diabetes. The findings from this study will shed new light on the hormonal regulation of cardiovascular homeostasis and will provide an evidence-base for the future development of novel drug candidates for treating and/or preventing the cardiovascular complications of obesity and diabetes. 在當今老齡化程度快速增長的情況下，心血管疾病，包括冠心病、中風以及外周血管功能異常，已經成為了人群致死和致殘的最主要原因之一。上述疾病一旦到達了晚期就很難逆轉。血管內皮功能障礙——主要表現為內皮細胞依賴性的血管舒張反應受損，以及內皮細胞依賴性的血管收縮趨於加強——是動脈粥樣硬化發生早期的主要事件。臨床學和動物實驗均表明血管內皮細胞功能障礙是聯接肥胖、糖尿病和心血管疾病之間的關鍵介導因素。因此，針對血管內皮細胞功能障礙的靶向治療很可能成為預防肥胖與糖尿病相關的心血管疾病的極為有效的策略。 成纖維細胞生長因子21 （Fibroblast growth factor，FGF21）是一種主要由肝臟分泌的代謝相關的激素。多個動物研究結果表明在哺乳動物和猴子中，FGF21能夠在多方面發揮對抗肥胖相關的代謝紊亂疾病的有益作用。利用遺傳學手段或藥物學方法升高血液中FGF21的含量可防止飲食引起的肥胖和胰島素抵抗，並持續性的改善高血糖，血脂紊亂以及脂肪肝。除了代謝相關的功能，最近我們研究組的研究結果表明FGF21可直接作用於血管內皮細胞，增強一氧化氮的產生，防止高血糖誘導的氧化應激反應和細胞雕亡，並促進細胞遷移和血管生成。上述結果表明FGF21是一個血管內皮細胞功能的新型調節分子，可作為治療心血管疾病的潛在靶點。因此，本項目的首要目標即是研究FGF21在調控動物血管內平衡中的生理學功能，並進一步闡明FGF21作用於血管內皮細胞的分子機制。此外，我們還將在肥胖2型糖尿病的遺傳學小鼠模型中探索FGF21重組蛋白作為藥物治療糖尿病血管損傷和功能異常的可行性。該研究成果將對激素分子調節心血管內穩態的機制提供新的啟示，並為進一步的研發預防及治療肥胖和糖尿病心血管並發癥的新藥先導化合物提供理論基礎。

784111.label: Realisation of objectives
784111.value: 1): Elucidation of molecular pathways underlying endothelial actions of FGF21. In both human and mouse endothelial cells, we have demonstrated that FGF21 dose-dependently induces nitric oxide (NO) production via phosphorylation-dependent activation of eNOS, and also suppresses high glucose and toxic lipids-induced oxidative stress and apoptosis. Using both siRNA-mediated knockdown and cross-linking analysis, we have found that the endothelial actions of FGF21 are mediated by the FGFR1c-βklotho receptor complex. Furthermore, we have observed a synergistic action of FGF21 and adiponectin in inducing NO production and in protecting high glucose-induced apoptosis in endothelial cells. Mechanistically, FGF21 and adiponectin exert additive effect on activation of AMP-activated protein kinase and on expression of PGC-1α, which in turn mediates the anti-oxidant activity of FGF21 by increasing the nuclear abundance of nuclear factor Nrf2 and subsequent up-regulation of several antioxidant genes. 2); Demonstration of FGF21 as a physiological protector of vascular functions. We have compared the vascular functions between FGF21 knockout mice and wild-type littermates. Our myograph analysis demonstrated that acetylcholine-induced endothelium-dependent relaxation of both aorta and small mesenteric arteries in FGF21 knockout mice was markedly attenuated compared to wild type mice. Using adiponectin KO mice, we have found that the effect of FGF21 administration on endothelium-dependent vasodilation is greatly attenuated, suggesting that endothelial actions of FGF21 is partly dependent on adiponectin in vivo. To further elucidate the vascular protective effects of FGF21, we crossed FGF21 knockout mice with apolipoprotein E(-/-) mice to generate apoE/FGF21 double knockout (DKO) mice. Our results demonstrated that the size and area of atherosclerotic plaques in DKO mice are significantly bigger than apoE(-/-) mice, which is accompanied by augmented macrophage infiltration and accelerated mortality. The exacerbated atherosclerosis in DKO mice is completely reversed by replenishment with recombinant FGF21, and is partly reversed by adiponectin. 3): Effect of FGF21 on endothelial repair and wound healing: Using a wire-induced carotid denution model established in our laboratory, we evaluated the impact of FGF21 deficiency on endothelial regeneration (re-endothelialization) in diabetic conditions. Using flow cytometry analysis, we found that the mobilization of EPCs from bone marrow to bloodstream in FGF21 knock mice was significantly decreased. Furthermore, the capacity of re-endothelialization was also impaired in FGF21 KO mice, suggesting that FGF21 may act as an endogenous regulator of vascular regeneration. In type-2 diabetic mice, treatment with FGF21 can alleviate diabetes-associated impairment in wound healing and reendotheliazation, and such beneficial effects are partly abrogated by adiponectin deficiency.

784111.label: Major findings and research outcome
784111.value: With the support of this grant, we have uncovered a novel role of FGF21 as a physiological protector against various types of vascular diseases, and elucidated the molecular mechanisms underlying the vascular protective effects of FGF21. 1. FGF21 protects against both obesity-induced endothelial dysfunction and atherosclerosis in mice. FGF21 deficiency exacerbates dietary obesity-induced endothelial dysfunction of both aortas and small mesenteric arteries, as determined by wire myograph analysis of acetylcholine-induced endothelium-dependent vasodilatation. Similarly, FGF21 deficiency also aggravates atherosclerotic plaque formation and vascular inflammation, and accelerates premature death in apoE(-/-) mice. These changes can be reversed by chronic administration of recombinant FGF21. In addition, FGF21 deficiency accelerates diabetes-induced impairment in endothelial regeneration and wound healing, which can also be reversed by chronic administration with recombinant FGF21. 2. Adiponectin acts as an important downstream target mediating the vascular protective effects of FGF21. In adiponectin KO mice, the effects of FGF21 on improving endothelial functions and on reducing diabetes-induced impairment in wound healing and reendothelization are partially abrogated. Conversely, administration of recombinant adiponectin can alleviate the exacerbated atherosclerosis and endothelial dysfunction in FGF21 KO mice. 3. FGF21 and adiponectin can act in a synergistic manner in endothelial cells to induce NO production by activation of eNOS, and to prevent high glucose- and toxic lipids-induced oxidative stress and apoptosis. The latter effect of FGF21 is attributed to its ability in inducing the expression of PGC1α, which in turn induces the expression of the transcription factor NRF2 and subsequent expression of several anti-oxidant genes. The synergistic effects of FGF21 and adiponectin may be mediated by their activation of AMP-activated protein kinase. 4. FGF21 also exerts its anti-atherosclerotic activities by reducing hypercholesterolemia. The cholesterol-lowering effects of FGF21 are attributed to its inhibitory effect on hepatic expression of sterol regulatory element-binding protein-2 (Srebp-2), which is a key player of cholesterol biosynthesis. Such a hepatic action of FGF21 on suppression of cholesterol biosynthesis is mediated by the FGFr2-β-klotho complex. The key findings were published in Circulation (2015,;131(21):1861-71)., a top-ranked journal in this field (see part C for details).

784111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
784111.value: FGF21 is a potential drug candidate for treatment of obesity and diabetes. Several pharmaceutical companies are developing FGF21 analogs or agonists for therapeutic applications. However, a recent phase-2b clinical trial only showed a marginal effect on hyperglycemia in patients with obesity and diabetes. Instead, an obvious improvement in lipid profiles and in circulating adiponectin has been observed in FGF21 analog-treated patients. Our present study, which is the first to show the vascular protective effect of FGF21, suggest that this hormone may be more effective for treatment and/or prevention of endothelial dysfunction and atherosclerosis, instead of glycemic control. Therefore, our findings raise the hope for the use of FGF21 or its agonists as a therapeutic agent for cardiovascular disease. Based on our findings, we are negotiating with Servier (An Europe-based international pharmaceutical company) to jointly develop FGF21-based therapeutics for cardiovascular disease, using the animal models and high throughput platform established in our laboratory. We will also apply for HMRF grant to test whether the beneficial effect of physical exercise on vascular system is mediated by induction of FGF21 and its signaling pathways.

784111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
784111.value: Cardiovascular diseases (CVD), including coronary heart disease, stroke and microvascular disorders, remain to be the top cause of death and disability in our rapidly ageing population. Due to the multi-factorial nature of CVD, the therapeutic interventions targeting a single risk factor (eg, the use of statins to decrease hypercholesterolemia) are often insufficient to block the progression of this disease. In this study, we demonstrated that the liver-secreted hormone fibroblast growth factor (FGF) 21 potently alleviates endothelial dysfunction and atherosclerotic plaque formation and decreases premature death in apolipoprotein E−/− mice via several mechanisms. First, FGF21 induces the production of adiponectin, which in turn acts on the blood vessels directly to inhibit neointima formation and macrophage inflammation. Second, FGF21 exerts its autocrine actions in the liver to suppress lipid biosynthesis, thereby reducing hypertriglyceridemia and hypercholesterolemia. Third, FGF21 can directly act on endothelial cells to promote its regeneration. Notably, FGF21 is a downstream effector for both the nuclear receptors peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) α and γ, the agonists of which are effective for treatment of both metabolic and vascular diseases. Therefore, our results raise the possibility that FGF21 or its analogs may represent a promising cure for CVD via its multiple actions in adipose tissue, blood vessels, and liver.

784611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
784611.value: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease characterized by production of autoantibodies and multiple organ damage. It mainly affects women of child-bearing age and genetic factors are known to play important role in the disease. Identifying these genetic factors predisposing people to SLE holds much promise to the understanding of the disease and its personalized treatment. Recently, genome–wide association study (GWAS) conducted in our laboratory on Hong Kong SLE patients identified ETS1, WDFY4, ELF1, and CD247 associated with the disease. Our collaborator, Professor Xue-Jun Zhang in Anhui, China also reported their GWAS on SLE, which identified 9 novel susceptibility loci. There are common loci found in these two Asian studies that have not been reported in previous Caucasian studies, suggestive of potentially Asian-specific susceptibility genes. However, the susceptibility genes found so far only explain a small proportion of disease heritability, and it is predicted that there are more genes associated with the disease that are yet to be identified. Undoubtedly, the genetic variants to be discovered are likely to be of lower effect size and/or lower allele frequencies. Their detection demands an increase in sample size and cross-validation among multiple independent cohorts to increase power and to avoid false positive findings. There is much debate on the future steps after initial GWAS as whether to increase sample size or to move to detection of rare variants. To us, meta-analysis of the two Asian GWAS seems to be the project to go with promises of novel findings without incurring additional genome-wide genotyping cost. Initial findings by meta-analysis will be thoroughly analyzed and a number of SNPs meeting pre-set criteria will be selected for replication in other independent cohorts, with the patient number reaching over eight thousands. To our knowledge, no large-scale meta-analysis of SLE GWAS data has been reported. The reported studies all used older version of genotyping platforms and had sample sizes in the hundreds or lower thousands in their discovery panels. SLE is a disease with higher genetic loading than most other complex diseases, and there is still much to gain with meta-analysis considering the small proportion of heritability explained by the genes identified so far. In light of the higher disease prevalence and severity of SLE in Asians, this study could also shed light on the ethnic differences of the disease. 系統性紅斑狼瘡（SLE）是一種自身免疫性疾病.其特點是生產自身抗體和多臟器損害。它主要影響生育年齡婦女。 眾所周知，遺傳因素对系統性紅斑狼瘡發揮重要作用。 確定這些誘發 SLE的遺傳因素对了解這一疾病及其個性化的治療会有重要作用。 最近，我們實驗室進行了有關香港SLE患者的全基因組關聯研究（GWAS），確定了ETS1，WDFY4，ELF1和CD247与疾病的關聯性。 我們的合作者，張學軍教授也報告了他們的GWAS，確定了9个新的易感基因位點。有的基因位點仅出現在這兩個亞洲研究中，从未在以前的高加索人的研究中報告过，暗示潛在的亞洲特有的易感基因的存在。 然而，至今發現的易感基因只解釋一小部分疾病的遺傳性。對我們來說，這兩個亞洲 GWAS的薈萃分析承諾發現新的易感基因，而不會產生額外的全基因組基因分型成本。比起大多數其他複雜的疾病，系統性紅斑狼瘡是一種有較高的遺傳負荷的疾病， 薈萃分析有很大的机会会有许多新的发现。亞洲人有較高的發病率和较嚴重的临床表现，因此這項研究也可能会揭示出此疾病的種族差異。

785611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
785611.value: 糖尿病正逐漸成為嚴重危害人們健康的殺手，即使在沒有冠心病的情況下，糖尿病也可造成心肌纖維化和心功能異常而形成糖尿病性心肌病。重要的是糖尿病性心肌病引起的心功能異常是預測糖尿病人死亡的獨立危險因素。然而到目前為止,心肌纖維化程度和心功能異常的關係還懸而未決。 雖然機理不明，但人體腎素-血管緊張素系統(RAS)在形成糖尿病性心肌病中起關鍵作用，而且腎素-血管緊張素系統和其他心血管疾病如高血壓的心肌纖維化形成有關。因此，腎素-血管緊張素系統的主要活性物質血管緊張素ǁ成為預防和治療糖尿病性心肌病的標靶。目前保護糖尿病心臟的藥物治療包括血管緊張素轉換酶抑制劑(ACEIs)和血管緊張素受體拮抗劑(ARB)，兩者分別在不同層面阻斷腎素-血管緊張素的活性。 然而血管緊張素轉換酶抑制劑和血管緊張素受體拮抗劑又會代償性增加腎素的分泌。目前，有研究表明腎素抑制劑-Aliskiren在糖尿病人中具有保護腎功能和改善血管的作用。這項研究的目的是觀察Aliskiren能否增效ACEIs/ARB的作用來預防和轉歸糖尿病心臟纖維化。

785611.label: Realisation of objectives
785611.value: Regarding the 1st and 2nd objectives, we have evaluated the degree of myocardial fibrosis and cardiac dysfunction in relation with renin angiotensin system and extracellular matrix (ECM) regulation.A total of 264 subjects with T2DM, as defined by World Health Organization criteria, were recruited from Queen Mary Hospital, Hong Kong. Patients were excluded if they had a known history of cardiovascular disease including coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction, stroke or peripheral vascular disease, underlying malignancy, pregnancy, or if they refused to participate (n=78). Exercise echocardiography was performed in the remaining 186 patients. A total of 50 patients had regional wall motion abnormality during stress testing, suggestive of significant ischemic heart disease and 13 patients had suboptimal stress images for analysis. The population with suitable exercise echocardiography images for analysis was thus 123 (62 female, 60.8±8.8 years). The results demonstrated that in patients with T2DM, TIMP-1, an ECM regulator, is independently associated with myocardial diastolic dysfunction both at rest and during stress. This finding suggests that increased ECM turnover affects the myocardial response during stress and cardiac performance. Whether TIMP-1 contributes to adverse cardiovascular events nonetheless requires future prospective studies. Measures that could reduce TIMP-1 level may thus improve myocardial function. The finding has been presented in the European Society of Cardiology 2015 annual scientific meeting and the full manuscript has been submitted for international peer review. For the 3rd objective, we have successfully carried out a double-blind randomized trial, comparing aliskiren with placebo, in patients with T2DM. In total, 37 patients received aliskiren and 37 patients received placebo. Patients were follow up after 1 year of randomization and none had developed adverse events, including hyperkalaemia and renal dysfunction. The baseline echocardiography parameters were compared with the follow-up parameters. In particular, both diastolic function, systolic function and myocardial fibrosis evaluated by calibrated integrated backscatter was analyzed. The results demonstrated that the use of aliskiren, but not placebo, resulted in improved in myocardial function evaluated by strain analysis. The final results has been presented in the RGC abstract presentation, 2016 and full manuscript is in preparation.

785611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
785611.value: Based on the results, we have demonstrated that TIMP-1 correlates closely with myocardial dysfunction in patients with T2DM. Further, aliskiren, a direct renin inhibitor, improves myocardial function in these patients. A larger randomized study should be done to evaluate the prognostic role of alikiren in patients with T2DM.

785611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
785611.value: Patients with T2DM suffers from myocardial dysfunction before they develop cardiovascular adverse events. It was demonstrated that, TIMP-1, an extracellular matrix regulator correlates closely with myocardial dysfunction in these patients (Objective 1 and 2). Importantly, the use of aliskiren, a direct renin inhibitor, may improve myocardial function in patients with T2DM. None of the patients who received aliskiren developed significant side effects. Future studies thus should be done to evaluate the prognostic value of aliskiren in these patients.

785811.label: Project Objectives
785811.value: Address the critical engineering challenges in realizing high-frame-rate ultrasound color flow imaging clinically: This will include achieving objectives #2 and #3 of this proposal. Design novel system hardware that can facilitate real-time realization of high-frame-rate color flow imaging: We will achieve this by building upon the channel-domain imaging research platform that our team has been developing. 785811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
785811.value: 本項目的大方向是要研發目前醫學診斷所缺乏的實時無創高幀率血流影像技術。從臨床角度看來，研發此技術是相當重要的，因它能在無創情況下實時為醫學診斷提供新的生理信息如血管或心臟內的湍流及其瞬時變化過程。我們提出的方案是要將超聲血流成像打造成為一項高幀率血流影像技術。此方案的可行性早前已被初步証明：其方法是利用合成孔徑或平面波等廣域發收模式進行高幀率影像數據採樣。然而，其臨床實現仍有很多技術難題尚待突破。 為使高幀率超聲血流成像能邁向臨床應用，本項目將會致力探討如何解決幾項關於此影像技術之基礎理論與系統研究課題。首先，我們會探討有關使用廣域發收模式時必會面對的高強度雜訊。我們會研究如何能利用主要向量分析的機理來設計自適應雜訊濾波器，從而確保高血流檢測的敏感性。接著會探討的是高幀率超聲血流成像之系統技術問題。實時實現此影像技術並非一般超聲影像系統能做到的，因廣域發收模式需要重新配置每個發收通道的運作及其運算量是相當高。為解決此技術問題，我們會運用一個早前自製的超聲影像研究系統及其高速處理平台來發展實時高幀率超聲血流成像。我們下一步會利用此成果進行一系列的狹窄血管仿體實驗，分析高幀率超聲血流成像對湍流檢測的實際效用及其臨床價值。 本項目的意義在於為醫學人員帶來高幀率超聲血流成像臨床研究所需之基礎技術。這有助發展此影像技術的生物醫學應用。

785811.label: Realisation of objectives
785811.value: Our team has successfully addressed various essential engineering challenges in realizing high-frame rate ultrasound imaging. In particular: (a) Objective #1 has been met by completing Objectives #2, #3, and #4, as described in the next three points. (b) Objective #2 has been achieved with the following specific achievements: - Developed a novel technique for complex flow visualization. We called this imaging innovation as color-encoded speckle imaging (CESI). - Investigated adaptive beamforming solutions for high-frame-rate imaging. We have pursued the use of minimum variance beamforming in synthetic aperture ultrasound imaging. Also, a new joint transmit-receive eigen-beamformer has been developed in collaboration with colleagues at Fudan University. - Co-developed new motion estimation methods for high-frame-rate imaging. We have proposed the use of transverse oscillation principles to estimate vascular motion vectors in collaboration with colleagues at University of Montreal and University of Lyon. (c) Objective #3 has been achieved with these specific achievements: - Established a composite ultrasound imaging research platform needed for high-frame-rate ultrasound imaging based on broad-view data acquisition principles. - Devised a novel real-time computing paradigm for achieving synthetic aperture imaging in collaboration with colleagues at University of Coimbra. The method is based on high-level synthesis of FPGA beamformers. - Built a real-time adaptive beamforming platform for synthetic aperture imaging. Solution involved the use of a multi-GPU array. - Developed a real-time adaptive clutter filtering framework for effective color flow imaging. Solution is also based on the use of GPUs. (d) Objective #4 has been achieved by completing the following broad series of carotid bifurcation imaging studies: - Analyzed the complex flow visualization performance of the CESI method that we developed. We were able to coherently track complex flow features such as flow jet and recirculation in the carotid bifurcation. - Designed a new anatomically realistic phantom fabrication framework. It is based on direct rapid prototyping of vessel geometries. - Designed a new tunable compliant vascular phantom design framework for motion vector estimation innovations (phantom design was led by our team, and the products were shared with colleagues at the University of Lyon). It involved the use of a polyvinyl alcohol cross-linking protocol. - Conducted a receiver operating characteristics analysis of adaptive clutter filtering for color flow imaging. The study involved the establishment and use of a well-calibrated vascular model with known pulsatile dynamics and tissue motion. Related research outcomes are described later in this report.

785811.label: Major findings and research outcome
785811.value: Our team has published six journal articles and has made a number of conference presentations on our research achievements in this grant project. Here is a summary of our research output: Journal #1: Presented our new color encoded speckle imaging framework for high frame rate flow imaging (Objective #2), our channel-domain ultrasound imaging research platform hardware (Objective #3), and carotid bifurcation complex flow experiments with 2,000 fps frame rate (Objective #4). Conference presentations #1, #2, #3, and #6 are related work. We also received a Young Scientist Award for this work at the 2012 Symposium on Ultrasonic Electronics. Journal #2: Presented our new framework for designing anatomically realistic flow phantoms based on rapid prototyping, and applied it to study complex flow dynamics in vascular scenarios with multiple pathological features (Objective #4). Conference presentation #4 is related work. Journal #3: Reported a new adaptive beamforming method for high frame rate imaging (Objective #2), and described how it can be realized in real-time using a multi-GPU array computing approach (Objective #3). Conference presentations #7 and #8 are related work. Journal #4: Described a novel real-time FPGA-based beamformer design for high frame rate imaging using high level synthesis principles (Objective #3). This work involved collaboration with colleagues at University of Coimbra. Conference presentation #9 is related work. Journal #5: Proposed a new motion estimation method for high-frame-rate imaging using transverse oscillation principles (Objective #2), and designed a new tunable compliant vascular phantom testbed for motion vector estimation innovations (Objective #4). The work involved collaboration with colleagues at University of Montreal and University of Lyon. Journal #6: Proposed a new eigen-beamformer method to derive high-quaity ultrasound images (Objective #2). The work involved collaboration with colleagues at Fudan University. Conference presentations #5, #10, #11: Presented our initial achievements in performing adaptive clutter filtering for ultrasound color flow imaging (Objective #2), designing robust motion vector estimators using a least-squares fitting approach (Objective #2), formulating real-time GPU solutions for adaptive clutter filtering (Objective #3), and investigating the practical efficacy of adaptive clutter filtering in anatomically realistic flow phantom models (Objective #4).

785811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
785811.value: With the technical achievements realized in this project, the logical next step would be to push forward our solutions toward clinical practice. For this effort, there will be a need to develop a live color encoded speckle imaging platform that can allow bedside use of our solutions, and conducting in vivo pilot studies in vascular patients with various disease conditions. We anticipate that the scope of such work would be a suitable topic for HMRF grant applications. There is also opportunity to translate our technical achievements to the ultrasound industry. Such industrial translation effort would fall within the scope of ITF funding schemes.

785811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
785811.value: As a biomedical engineering research project, this work has addressed the critical engineering bottlenecks related to clinical realization of high frame rate ultrasound imaging of vascular flow. We have demonstrated the possibility of using ultrasound to track complex hemodynamics in the carotid bifurcation at very high frame rates of >1,000 fps. This achievement is made possible by a number of original engineering contributions that we achieved in this project, including robust signal processing frameworks for motion estimation, new beamforming techniques, enabling system hardware, real-time computing paradigms, and anatomically realistic flow phantom design. These technical innovations will ultimately enable clinicians to make more informed diagnostic decisions on vascular pathologies such as atherosclerosis. In turn, vascular patients will be the principal beneficiaries.

785911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
785911.value: The mobilization of intracellular Ca2+ stores is involved in diverse cellular functions, including cell proliferation and differentiation [1-5]. At least three endogenous Ca2+ mobilizing messengers have been identified, including inositol trisphosphate (IP3), cyclic adenosine diphosphoribose (cADPR), and nicotinic adenine acid dinucleotide phosphate (NAADP). Similar to IP3, NAADP can mobilize calcium release in a wide variety of cell types and species, from plants to animals. Moreover, it has been previously shown that NAADP but not IP3-mediated Ca2+ increases can potently induce neuronal differentiation in PC12 cells [6, 7]. Recently, two pore channels (TPCs) have been identified as a novel family of NAADP-gated calcium release channels in endolysosome [3, 4]. Herein, we explore the role and mechanisms of NAADP/TPC2 in the neural differentiation of mouse embryonic stem (ES) cells. We found that the expression of TPC2 is markedly decreased during the initial ES cell entry into neural progenitors, and the levels of TPC2 gradually rebound during the late stages of neuronal genesis. Correspondingly, perturbing the NAADP signaling by TPC2 knockdown accelerates mouse ES cell differentiation into neural progenitors but restrains these neural progenitors from committing the final neuronal lineages. We hypothesize that the NAADP/TPC2-mediated Ca2+ signaling pathway plays a temporal and dichotomic role in modulating the neural lineage entry of ES cells, in that NAADP signaling antagonizes ES cell entry to early neural progenitors, but promotes late neuronal differentiation. Therefore we propose to: (1) establish the role of NAADP in neural differentiation of ES cells, and (2) decode the molecular mechanisms of NAADP signaling in the neural commitment of ES cells. The in vitro generation of neural lineage cells from ES cells is a promising approach to produce cells suitable for neural tissue repair [8-12]. The success of this project will increase our understanding of the role of Ca2+ signaling in embryonic neural development, and encourage the application of therapies based on ES cells in the treatment of neurological diseases. 细胞内钙的流动参与多种细胞功能，包括细胞增殖和分化。 至少有三个内源性的钙的流动使者已经确定，包括三磷酸肌醇（IP3），环腺苷二磷酸核糖（cADPR），和腺嘌呤烟碱酸核苷酸磷酸（NAADP）。与IP3类似，NAADP可以在从植物到动物的多种类型的细胞和物种中调动钙离子释放。此外，先前已被证明，NAADP，而不是IP3 ，所介导的钙增加可以强烈诱导PC12细胞的神经元分化。 最近，两孔通道（TPCs）已被确定为NAADP在內體和溶酶體上的钙调控释放通道。在这里，我们将探讨NAADP/TPC2通路在小鼠胚胎干细胞的神经分化中的作用。我们发现，TPC2的表达在最初的胚胎干细胞进入神经祖细胞的过程中有显着下降，但TPC2的表达水平在神经元细胞的后期起源阶段逐步回升。与此相对应，我们发现通过击倒TPC2来干扰NAADP信号能加速小鼠胚胎干细胞分化进入神经祖细胞，但也抑制了这些神经前体细胞分化成最后的神经细胞谱系。我们认为NAADP/TPC2所介导的钙信号通路在调节胚胎干细胞的神经谱系分化中根据时间起着不同的作用： NAADP信号拮抗胚胎干细胞进入早期神经祖细胞，但促进神经祖细胞的后期神经元的分化。因此，本项目将：（1）建立NAADP在胚胎干细胞的神经分化中的作用，（2）解码NAADP在胚胎干细胞的神经分化中的分子机制。胚胎干细胞在体外生成神经细胞系是一个有前途的神经组织的细胞修复方法。这一项目的成功将增加人们对钙信号在胚胎神经系统发育中的作用的认识，并鼓励应用胚胎干细胞疗法去治疗神经系统疾病。

785911.label: Realisation of objectives
785911.value: Objective 1. To determine the role of NAADP in the neural differentiation of mouse ES cells. Here we examined the role of NAADP/TPC2 signaling in the neural differentiation of mouse embryonic stem (ES) cells. We found that the expression of TPC2 was markedly decreased during the initial ES cell entry into neural progenitors, and the levels of TPC2 gradually rebounded during the late stages of neurogenesis. Correspondingly, perturbing NAADP signaling by TPC2 knockdown accelerated mouse ES cell differentiation into neural progenitors but inhibited these neural progenitors from committing to neurons. Overexpression of TPC2, on the other hand, inhibited mouse ES cell from entering the early neural lineage. Interestingly, TPC2 knockdown had no effect on the differentiation of astrocytes and oligodendrocytes of mouse ES cells. Taken together, our data indicate that TPC2 signaling plays a temporal and differential role in modulating the neural lineage entry of mouse ES cells, in that TPC2 signaling inhibits ES cell entry to early neural progenitors, but is required for late neuronal differentiation. Thus, we have successfully completed the objective 1, a manuscript entitled “Two pore channel 2 differentially modulates neural differentiation of mouse embryonic stem cells” was published on journal of Plos One, 8: e66077 (2013). Objective 2. To dissect the molecular mechanisms of NAADP signaling in the neural commitment of mouse ES cells. Subsequently, we explored the molecular mechanisms of the role of NAADP/TPC2 in the neural commitment of ES cells. We found that autophagy was markedly induced during neural differentiation of mouse ES cells. Moreover, NAADP/TPC2 signaling alkalinizes lysosomal pH via Ca2+ release from lysosomes to suppress fusion between autophagosome and lysosome, thereby suppressing autophagy progression during neural differentiation of ES cells. Our results indicate downregulation of TPC2 during early neural differentiation of ES cells facilitates the fusion between autophagosome and lysosome, thereby enabling faster energy recycling to be utilized for target differentiation. On the other hand, TPC2 overexpression blocks the fusion to prevent energy recycling and inhibits neural differentiation. Along this line, we found that TPC2 overexpression induced apoptosis during neural differentiation of mouse ES cells. Since TPC2 overexpression suppressed autophagy progression and autophagy defects could lead to apoptosis, apoptosis induced by TPC2 overexpression might be due to autophagy suppression as well. Thus, we have successfully completed the objective 2, a manuscript entitled “Two Pore Channel 2 (TPC2) Inhibits Autophagosomal-Lysosomal Fusion by Alkalinizing Lysosomal pH” was published on J. Biol. Chem. 288, 24247-24263 (2013).

785911.label: Major findings and research outcome
785911.value: 1. The mouse ES cells are responsive to NAADP and possess the key components of NAADP-signaling pathway. 2. The TPC2 expression pattern during neural differentiation is well regulated and specific. 3. TPC2 knockdown or overexpression does not affect the stemness and self-renewal of the ES cells. 4. TPC2 knockdown accelerates mouse ES cell differentiation into neural progenitors, whereas TPC2 overexpression significantly blocks neural lineage entry. Thus, NAADP/TPC2 signaling pathway antagonized ES cell differentiation into neural progenitors. 5. TPC2 overexpression caused severe cell loss during neural differentiation of mouse ES cells. 6. TPC2 knockdown inhibits late neuronal differentiation of ES cells, but has no effects on differentiation of mouse ES cells into astrocytes and oligodendrocytes. 7. In summary, our data suggest that neural differentiation of mouse ES cells is temporally and differentially regulated by TPC2 signaling, in that TPC2 signaling antagonizes ES cell entry to early neural progenitors, but is required for late neuronal differentiation. The findings about the role of NAADP/TPC2 in neural differentiation of ES cells were published journal of Plos One, 8: e66077 (2013). 8. Autophagy is markedly induced during neural differentiation of mouse ES cells. 9. During neural differentiation of mouse ES cells, autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion is facilitated by TPC2 knockdown but inhibited by TPC2 overexpression, indicating that TPC2/NAADP signaling negatively inhibits autophagy during neural differentiation of ES cells. 10. TPC2 overexpression in ES cells raises lysosomal pH and TPC2 knockdown decreases lysosomal pH. Moreover, transient reacidified lysosomal pH mitigates the autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion blockage in TPC2 overexpressing cells. These data demonstrate that TPC2 signaling suppresses autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion by alkalizing the lysosomal pH. 11. TPC2 signaling prevents the recruitment of Rab-7 to autophagosomes by alkalizing lysosomal pH to inhibit autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion. 12. TPC2 signaling does not inhibit the general endosomal-lysosomal degradation. The findings on the mechanisms of NAADP/TPC2 in neural differentiation of ES cells were published J. Biol. Chem. 288, 24247-24263 (2013).

785911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
785911.value: To further determine the molecular mechanisms underlying NAADP/TPC2-mediated autophagy arrest during neural differentiation of mouse ES cells, we have purified the TPC2 complex from HeLa cells that stably express TPC2-Flag-His6 by tandem affinity purification. Mass spectrometry analyses from three independent experiments identified TPC2 and ten other proteins with high fidelity in the complex. We have generated shRNAs against these ten genes with three distinct shRNAs per gene. We have been verifying their roles in TPC2 signaling using both LC3-II accumulation and NAADP-induced Ca2+ release as readouts in both HeLa cells and mouse ES cells. We have also been verifying whether these positive hits interact with TPC2 or NAADP. We have actually already identified one TPC2 positive interacting protein, which is a pseudo protein kinase and has been found to be associated with varied intracellular vesicles. We plan to systematically dissect the role of this novel protein in NAADP/TPC2-mediated Ca2+ signaling, especially on autophagy regulation and neural differentiation of ES cells.

785911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
785911.value: Nicotinic acid adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NAADP) is an endogenous Ca2+ mobilizing nucleotide presented in various species. NAADP mobilizes Ca2+ from acidic organelles through two pore channel 2 (TPC2) in many cell types and it has been previously shown that NAADP can potently induce neuronal differentiation in PC12 cells. Here we examined the role and mechanism of NAADP/TPC2 signaling in the neural differentiation of mouse embryonic stem (ES) cells. We found that TPC2 signaling plays a temporal and differential role in modulating the neural lineage entry of mouse ES cells, in that TPC2 signaling inhibits ES cell entry to early neural progenitors, but is required for late neuronal differentiation. Moreover, we found that that TPC2/NAADP/Ca2+ signaling alkalinizes lysosomal pH to specifically inhibit the later stage of basal autophagy progression. Our results indicate downregulation of TPC2 during early neural differentiation of ES cells facilitates the fusion between autophagosome and lysosome, thereby enabling faster energy recycling to be utilized for target differentiation. The success of this project not only increases our understanding of the role of Ca2+ signaling in embryonic neural development, but also encourages the application of therapies based on ES cells in the treatment of neurological diseases.

786611.label: Project Objectives
786611.value: To identify brain regions that exhibit significantly abnormal glucose metabolic levels at baseline in MDD patients compared to healthy subjects. Through this identification, abnormal brain regions associated with the pathogenesis of MDD will be defined. To identify brain regions displaying overlapping response to both sham and active DCEAS and only response to sham or active DCEAS using the whole-brain PET-scanned data analysis. Through this analysis, we determine whether active DCEAS additional treatment could produce more widespread effect in normalizing abnormal brain areas observed in MDD patients. All the brain regions displaying the overlapping response to both sham and active DCEAS are defined as region of interest (ROI). We will examine whether active DCEAS has greater effects in reversing abnormal metabolic levels in each region of ROIs compared to sham DCEAS. We analyze correlation between changes in the severity of clinical depressive symptoms and changes in glucose metabolic levels in each of active DCEAS-associated brain regions at endpoint to determine which brain regions are associated with the clinical improvement. The brain areas with only or greater response to active DCEAS and associated with the clinical improvement will be defined for constitutive structures of central network for antidepressant effects of DCEAS.

786611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
786611.value: 雖然過去四十年針刺研究已取得顯著進展﹐但大多數研究集中於針刺鎮痛, 而對於針刺的其它作用和機製了解甚少。 葉已顯示﹐針刺對各種精神疾患具有廣泛的治療益處。我們最近的薈萃分析證實﹐針刺對緩解各種抑鬱症狀有效。 我們最近兩項臨床對照研究進一步顯示﹐一種稱為密集顱部密集電针刺激(DCEAS)的新型针刺方式，与代表性抗抑郁药物选择性5-羟色胺(5-HT)重摄取拮抗剂(SSRIs)合用，可加速临床反应的出现，并产生比单独SSRIs更显著的抑郁改善作用。有证据显示，病理状态下的针刺作用与调节由相关脑区所构成的网络有关。由此提出的一个重要问题是: 与DCEAS抗抑郁作用相关的脑区网络是什么? 我们拟定的研究旨在探明与DCEAS抗抑郁作用相关的脑区网络。该研究将首次探讨针刺鎮痛之外治疗作用背后的机制，以便从神经科学角度理解这一古老的治疗疾病艺术。 抑郁症是世界和香港的主要精神健康问题。虽然各种抗抑郁药已用于临床，但疗效并不完全。这很大程度是因为抑郁症是一多系统病症，主要表现为脑内5-HT缺少，下丘脑-垂体-肾上腺轴功能紊乱和相关脑区的形态学改变。然而，几乎所有抗抑郁药仅具备单一的药理作用。大量的证据提示，针刺不仅可加速中枢5-HT的释放，而且还强烈调节神经内分泌功能，尤其是下丘脑-垂体-肾上腺轴。神经影像研究进一步显示，针刺能广泛调节与感觉、运动、自主神经、情绪和认知功能有关的脑区活动。针刺治疗也能纠正各种疾病的异常功能活动。我们在DCEAS治疗重性抑郁病人的正电子断层扫描(PET)前期研究中，也获得了相似结果。 因此，我们有理由推定，在治疗重性抑郁病人中，与单纯SSRIs比较，DCEAS结合SSRIs應能在更广泛的脑区内更强地纠正异常脑活动。而且这种更强的纠正作用与强烈的抗抑郁作用有关。 正电子断层扫描(PET)是一种强大的神经影像技术。在探测脑区葡萄糖代谢水平的细微变化上具有高度的空间分辨优势。我们前期研究证明，PET用于解构与针刺抗抑郁作用相关的中枢脑区网络上是一种有效的探测手段。 通过对82位重性抑郁患者接受为期6周的SSRI结合真性和假性DCEAS的对照研究，我们将应用PET技术去检验上述推定。研究的主要目标是确定在多大范围和多大程度上DCEAS的附加治疗可纠正抑郁病人相关脑区的异常活动。那些只对真性DCEAS起反应或其反应大于假性针刺，同时与临床改善相关的脑区定义为与DCEAS抗抑郁作用相关脑区。这些脑区即构成DCEAS抗抑郁作用相关中枢网络。该研究所获得的结果将不仅进一步确定DCEAS是治疗重性抑郁的有效附加疗法，而且能帮助我们更好地理解针刺抗抑郁作用的神经机制。

We have compared neuroimaging profile between the two groups using the whole brain analysis. We have compared the two groups using the whole brain analysis. [4] Objective # 4 has been fully achieved: we have completed brain region correlates of the symptom severity and clinical improvement using regions of interest (ROI) analysis.

786611.label: Major findings and research outcome
786611.value: [1] In single-blind, randomized controlled trial, a total of 107 subjects with major depressive disorder (MDD) were screened and 36 treatment-resistant MDD were recruited in the study. The patients randomly received sham (n = 17) or active (n = 19) DCEAS additional treatment for 3 sessions per week over 6 weeks. Neuroimaging scan was conducted in baseline and endpoint. Meanwhile, 12 healthy subjects were recruited to serve as neuroimaging controls. Treatment outcomes were measured using the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17), Zung’s Self Rating Depression Scale (SDS), the Clinical Global Impression - Severity scale (CGI-S), and the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI). Active DCEAS produced a significantly greater reduction in SDS score from Week 4 through endpoint compared to sham DCEAS. The incidence of adverse events was not different in the two groups. These results, once again, confirm the clinical efficacy of active DCEAS in reducing depressive symptoms with high safety profile. [2] PET data further showed that at wakeful rest, depressed patients showed glucose hypermetabolism in distributed brain regions, most of which are involved in the default mode network (DMN), compared to healthy controls. In fMRI scan, under a sad-face paradigm, the hypometabolism was observed in several brain regions that are associated with the processing of mood signals. These results suggest that treatment-resistant depressed patients have abnormally heightened DMN activity resulting in aberrant wakefulness and alertness and reduced activity in brain regions associated with the processing of negative mood signals. [3] While both sham and active DCEAS significantly reversed abnormal metabolism of brain regions in depressed patients observed in both neuroimaging approaches, the reversal effect of active DCEAS was much more distributed in the sad-face paradigm and in active DCEAS compared to wakeful rest and sham DCEAS, respectively. Furthermore, significant correlates between baseline-to-endpoint change in the severity of depression symptoms and endpoint metabolic level was found in several brain regions in the sad-face paradigm. These results suggest that antidepressant efficacy of DCEAS is mainly associated with its effects in modulating widespread brain regions, in particularly those related to the processing of negative mood signals.

786611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
786611.value: While the present study once again demonstrates the antidepressant efficacy of DCEAS, it has provided further neuroimaging evidence to help us better understand brain mechanisms underlying acupuncture effects. These findings will encourage us to further compare the efficacy and neuroimaging profile of DCEAS alone and in combination of body acupuncture through a controlled trial. Meanwhile, we also will propose to develop a novel trigeminal nerve innervated acupoint stimulation.

786611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
786611.value: Depression is a serious public health issue. Conventional medication treatment often results in unsatisfactory outcomes and causes undesirable side effects. Acupuncture is a traditional therapeutic therapy that may have the potential in reducing depressive symptoms. Our previous studies have demonstrated the antidepressant effects of a novel acupuncture therapy called DCEAS. The present study once again confirms the antidepressant efficacy of DCEAS and the brain mechanisms using neuroimaging approaches. These results provide further evidence in the support of the introduction of acupuncture into the treatment of depressive disorders, creating an additional option for depressed patients.

786911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
786911.value: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is an important human pathogen, infecting one third of world population. Although a highly effective vaccine has been available, it does not help for the estimated 400 million chronically infected people, including about 0.7 million of chronic patients in Hong Kong, which represents 8~10% of the local population. Chronic infection can lead to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and cause about 2 to 3 million deaths annually worldwide. Hepatitis B virus is a small DNA virus with a circular genome of about 3.2kb that encodes at least seven viral proteins. The expression of HBV genes is regulated by four promoters and two enhancers that depend on host factors for the transcription and regulation. HBV surface and core promoter are critical for viral morphogenesis and replication. Moreover, it has been well known that the development of liver cirrhosis and HCC, is closely related to viral replication level. Therefore, identification of host factors that direct HBV gene expression and replication is of vital importance. Our previous studies demonstrated that some of the SP1/KLF family transcription factors, which share the highly conserved DNA binding domain, bind to HBV surface promoter in a yeast 1-hybird screening. We have further found that KLF15, one of the SP1/KLF family members and highly expressed in human liver, can enhance HBV surface and core antigen expression. The proposed study, therefore, will extend our previous work towards further investigation of whether the liver-enriched transcription factor KLF15 regulates HBV gene expression and viral replication. The objectives of this study are to (1) evaluate the role of KLF15 in HBV gene expression and viral replication in vitro by over-expressing or knocking down KLF15 expression; (2) identify and characterize the interaction of KLF15 with HBV surface promoter and core promoter, and (3) in vivo assess the role of KLF15 for HBV gene expression and viral replication in HBV carrier mouse model. Our work will generate valuable information on how host transcription factor is involved in HBV viral repliction and may provide rationale to develop potential new therapeutic strategies to combat chronic HBV infection. 乙型肝炎病毒是一種對人類很危險的病源體, 它感染了世界三分之一的人口. 雖然目前已經有了很有效的疫苗以預防感染, 但是對於全球四十億, 包括七十萬香港的慢性乙肝病人 (約占香港人口的8-10%), 疫苗并沒有任何幫助. 慢性乙肝可能導致肝硬化和肝癌,據估計, 世界上每年有2-3百萬人死於乙肝及其并發症. 乙肝病毒是一種小的DNA病毒, 其環狀的基因組只有約3200bp，編碼至少７個病毒蛋白. 乙肝病毒基因的表達受４個啟動子和２個增強子的調控，它們衕時又依賴宿主因子的幫助．目前，有證據表明病毒的復制水平與肝硬化和肝癌的發生有密切的關系.因此，發現調控乙肝病毒基因表達和病毒復制的宿主因子是一個至關重要的課題．SP1/ KLF 轉錄因子家族具有高度保守的DNA結合區， 通過酵母雜交篩選，我們表明， SP1/ KLF 轉錄因子家族其中的一些因子結合乙肝病毒表面抗原的啟動子.此外，我們還發現,在肝臟高度表達的KLF15可以增強表面抗原和核心抗原的表達.此項研究旨在進一步探索KLF15能否調節乙肝病毒基因表達和病毒復制．研究的目的是: 1. 通過內外過表達和降低表達 以評價KLF15在病毒基因表達和病毒復制中所起的作用. 2. 研究KLF15與乙肝病毒表面抗原及核心抗原啟動子之間的相互作用. 3. 在乙肝病毒的老鼠模型中, 評價KLF15在病毒基因表達和病毒復制中所起的作用. 此項研究將揭示宿主的轉錄因子如何參與乙肝病毒基因表達和病毒復制, 為治療慢性乙肝提供寶貴的理論依據.

786911.label: Realisation of objectives
786911.value: To understand the role of KLF15 for the viral gene expression and viral replication of hepatitis B virus (HBV), we proposed in vitro and in vivo studies, aiming to 1) to evaluate the role of KLF15 in HBV gene expression and viral replication in vitro; 2) to characterize and identify the interaction of KLF15 with HBV core promoter and/or surface promoter(s) in vitro; 3) to validate the role of KLF15 in HBV gene expression and viral replication in HBV mouse model. Generally, all the three objectives have been achieved. We demonstrated that overexpression of KLF15 can robustly activated HBV core and surface promoter. Accordingly, the expression of HBV core, surface protein and viral replication were enhanced. Additionally, knockdown endogenous KLF15 by siRNA reduced HBV core and surface promoter activity, as well as surface protein production. In EMSA and ChIP assays, we characterized the interaction of KLF15 with core and surface promoter. The KLF15 binding site in HBV core promoter was identified. Hydrodynamic injection of HBV-expressing plasmid via the mouse tail veil was established as a HBV mouse model. We validated the findings of in vitro studies and demonstrated that in vivo knockdown resulted in reduced viral gene expression and viral replication in a dose-dependent manner in HBV mouse model. Moreover, the engineered HBV with the mutated KLF15 binding site in core promoter displayed the compromised viral replication compared to the wild virus. In summary, our study shows that KLF15 is an essential host factor that functions to support HBV gene expression and viral replication in vitro and in vivo. Although we have sufficient data demonstrating trans-activation of KLF15 on HBV surface promoter and the physical interaction of KLF15 and surface promoter, the HBV binding site in surface promoter has not been clarified. It may exist several possibilities. KLF15 may cooperate with other host factors and may indirectly interact with the surface promoter. Alternatively, there is other uncharacterized KLF15 binding sequence in the surface promoter that mediates the effect of KLF15 on this promoter. This is definitely an interesting question for our further study.

786911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
786911.value: Hepatitis B virus is a small DNA virus that infects human liver cells and cause acute and chronic viral hepatitis. Around 1/3 of world population has once been infected. In those with chronic hepatitis B, liver cirrhosis and liver cancer may eventually develop. Due to the small genome, the virus requires human proteins for its growth in the infected individuals. In a screen study, we found that a liver-enriched protein KLF15 interacting with HBV surface promoter, one of the viral elements that can promote viral growth in human cells. In this study, we performed a series of studies. We showed that KLF15 can indeed activate the viral elements and support viral growth in culture cells. We found the physical interaction between KLF15 and the viral elements. Additionally, in HBV mouse model, we demonstrated that KLF15 indeed support HBV growth and propagation in these experimental animals. Therefore, we identified an important cellular protein that is exploited by HBV for its growth in human cells. This work advanced our understanding towards this disease-causing virus. Additionally, inhibition of KLF15 can be developed into a potential therapeutics for HBV infection.

787011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
787011.value: Isthmin is a novel secreted protein which contains a thrombospondin type 1 repeat (TSR) and an adhesion-associated domain in MUC4 and other proteins (AMOP). It is coexpressed with Fgf8 at the midbrain-hindbrain boundary (isthmic organizer) where many important signaling molecules are secreted. Isthmins are unique to chordates and highly conserved among Zebrafish, mouse and human. Except for the expression profile in Xenopus, little is known about the function of Isthmin. In an effort of systematic study of the biological role of Isthmin, we raised polyclonal antibodies specifically recognizing mouse Isthmin. By In Situ hybridization, immunohistochemistry and Western blotting, we have examined the spatial-temporal expression of Isthmin in mouse during embryonic and postnatal development. Our preliminary data revealed that Isthmin is highly expressed in brain and lung throughout the development. Furthermore, our In Vitro experiments showed that Isthmin enhances Fgf-stimulated Erk1/2 phosphorylation, indicating a role for Isthmin in Fgf signaling. In addition, Isthmin inhibits Nodal signaling in a Luciferase assay and the phosphorylation of Smad2. Isthmin does not have obvious effects on TGF-beta, BMP or Wnt signaling. To further address the roles for Isthmin in Fgf/Nodal signaling and to understand its biological functions, we initiated the generation of Isthmin conditional knockout mice. In this study, we will characterize Isthmin homozygous mutants to investigate the biological function of Isthmin in embryogenesis and development including Neurogenesis, lung morphogenesis, eye development and angiogenesis. In addition, FGF and Nodal signaling and relevant biological processes will be investigated in Isthmin deficient mice to understand how Isthmin affects these signaling in vivo. We will investigate how Isthmin potentiates Fgf signaling and inhibits Nodal signaling using full length and various domain-deleted Isthmins. The proposed work will provide fundamental knowledge of Isthmin and allow us to elucidate the molecular mechanisms for Isthmin to modulate Fgf and Nodal signaling. This work will provide insights into novel molecular mechanism by which Isthmin regulates embryogenesis and possibly also to human diseases related to FGF signaling. 787011.label: Realisation of objectives
787011.value: Objective 1 has been fully addressed and a manuscript is ready for submission to a journal. The role of ISM1 in NODAL signaling is examined by Western blotting to detect changes in pSMAD2 stimulated by NODAL. Signaling by other members of the TGFb superfamily, such as ACTIVIN and TGFß1 was examined by pSmad2 in response to relevant growth factor. To understand how ISM1 inhibits NODAL signaling, we performed several co-IP experiments to examine the interaction of ISM1 with the different components of the NODAL signaling pathway. Additionally, ectopic ISM1 and recombinant ISM1 was employed to further demonstrate which signaling ISM1 is involved in and how ISM1 contribute to the the regulation of specific signaling. Objective 2. The in vivo biological role has been fully addressed using ISM1 transgenic mice. A manuscript has been published (Osório, Wu and Zhou, 2014; Cell Cycle, 13(10): 1571-1582) and another manuscript is under preparation (Osório et al.). During the course of this project, two independent ISM1 conditional knockout mice have been generated. In our first attempt, we found that one of the loxP sites was lost in the targeting construct and these mice were no further analyzed. To overcome this challenge, we designed a new conditional gene targeting construct and ISM1 conditional knockout has been successfully generated. Several chimeras were produced and germline transmission was confirmed. The mice are now being crossed to several mouse cre lines, such as actin-cre. Unfortunately, number of mice were available for analyses were not enough at this point. To safeguard the completion of the project, we took an alternative approaches to address the in vivo function of ISM1: (1) To use the chick embryo as an alternative model to evaluate the role of ISM1 during embryonic development; (2) To generate ISM1 BAC transgenic mice and examine the effects of gain-of function of ISM1 in tissue formation and homeostasis. In the chick embryo, we analysed ISM1 expression. We also performed gain-of-function studies in which HH3/4 embryos cultured ex ovo were treated with either MOCK or ISM1 CM. We further examine ISM1 ability to antagonize NODAL signaling using a beads assay. With ISM1 BAC transgenic mice and we examine the effects of gain-of function of ISM1 in tissue formation and homeostasis. We examined various phenotypes and analysed the potential functions of ISM1 in tumorigenesis and stem cell functions.

787011.label: Major findings and research outcome
787011.value: 1. ISM1 is novel extracellular nodal signaling antagonist. Recombinant ISM1 protein inhibits phosphorylation of SMAD2 induced by NODAL.Ectopic ISM1 inhibits the transcriptional activity of SMAD2/ FOXH1 in a luciferase assay. ISM1 interacts with NODAL ligand as well as with the ECD of its type I receptor ACVR1B through its AMOP domain. ISM1 is transiently and asymmetrically expressed in the right side of Hensen’s node during gastrulation. ISM1 treatment causes down-regulation of several targets of NODAL signaling and consequently aberrant heart laterality, both in morphology as well as in molecular identity. NODAL-soaked beads, when implanted in the right LPM of chick embryos at HH5-6, induce ectopic expression of NODAL in about 50% embryos. In agreement, 58% (7 out of 12) of the embryos implanted with rNODAL+PBS beads showed ectopic NODAL expression, in contrast to 14% (2 out of 14) of the embryos implanted with rNODAL+rISM1 beads, these data support that. ISM1 as an antagonist of NODAL signaling in vivo 2. Mechanistically, ISM1 compromises NODAL-ACVR1B interaction, a novel molecular mechanism for NODAL signalling regulation. Further evidence of the biological role of ISM1 as an antagonist of NODAL signalling came from experiments conducted in the chick embryo 3. ISM1 does not affect ACTIVIN or TGF-beta signaling. 4. ISM1 is a positive modulator of FGF2/MAPK-ERK1/2 signaling pathway. ISM1 increases the phosphorylated levels of FRS2α (pFRS2α) and ERK1/2 (pERK1/2) induced by FGF2. ISM1 interacts with FGF2 as well as with the extracellular domain (ECD) of FGFR1. ISM1 may thus facilitate the ligand-receptor interaction. 5. ISM1 is critical for development and homeostasis. Phenotypic analyses of ISM1 transgenic mice have revealed an important role of ISM1 in the development and homeostasis of several tissues, such as the urogenital system. ISM1 transgenic mice showed subfertility, hydrometrocolpos and hydronephrosis. Increased levels of phosphorylated ERK1/2 was found in ISM1 transgenic mice. FGF signaling plays fundamental roles in the proper development of these tissues. This supports our previous finding of ISM1 acting as a positive modulator of FGF signaling.

787011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
787011.value: We also found ISM1 transgenic mice developed polycystic kidney diseases, suggesting the abnormal signaling caused by ISM1 contributes to polycystic kidney diseases. This is a novel finding and will likely lead to identification of novel genetic alteration for this disease. We are now trying to investigate the molecular mechanism. In addition we also identified defects in uterus, suggesting critical role for ISM1 in reproductive system. We are now preparing an manuscript and will look into this defect further particularly the mechanism and signaling pathway which is affected.
