840211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
840211.value: Abstract The rapid development and globalization of online social media services since the turn of the century has opened up new opportunities for informal second and foreign language (SFL) learning. These opportunities may be especially valuable to young English language learners in Asia, where opportunities for face-face-interaction with users of English have traditionally been limited. Using a multiple case study methodology, this project aims to identify and investigate evidence for SFL learning on YouTube, currently one of the fastest growing global social media services. The project investigates interactions surrounding language-related videos posted on YouTube by Chinese-speaking users of English. It aims to identify evidence of informal SFL teaching and learning and to account for its contexts, typical practices, and discourse features. Using observation and interview methods derived from the emerging field of online ethnography, the project comprises ten in-depth case studies, each of which involves systematic investigation of a focal video, related video postings, and text comments made by other users. Observational data gathered from YouTube are complemented by interviews with key participants in SFL learning events. The findings of the study are expected to provide insight into the potential of YouTube and other social media environments for informal SFL learning. They will also deepen our theoretical understanding of the nature of informal out-of-class SFL learning, in an age in which online SFL social interaction is becoming part of everyday life, and the ways in which it differs from and complements classroom learning. 社交網路媒體於本世紀全球化的迅速發展為第二語言學習者及外國語言學習者帶來非正式的學習機會。由於亞洲人與英語使用者面對面溝通的機會較少， 這些機會可能對在亞洲年輕的英語學習者來說特別寶貴。本研究計劃以多案例研究方法去分析及探討於社交網路媒體 – YouTube 內的外國語言學習的證據。 本計劃研究者將透過觀察及訪問的方法收集數據。研究者所選的十部YouTube影片都會是跟語言相關的，並由以中文作為母語的英語使用者上載。計劃將透過外國語言學習者用戶於該影片的互動交流(包括留言評論及相關影片等) 探討他們的交流模式與話語特徵。 計劃的研究結果能夠驗證外國語言學習者於社交網路媒體進行非正式語言學習的可能性，並為此研究領域提供更深入的理據。

840211.label: Realisation of objectives
840211.value: 1. Achieved. The study identified 10 categories of YouTube videos involving the use of English and Chinese, and analyzed 8,850 written comments on these videos. It has been shown that ‘translanguaging’ (or the problematization of language differences) in a video tends to generate substantial numbers of comments on language issues in response to the video comments (more than 30% of the comments on the identified videos were language-related). These comments often lead to longer sequences of exchanges on language issues. Analysis of the relationship between videos and comments suggests that (a) SFL learning takes place in the context of comments on videos that involve translanguaging and (b) such videos construct contexts for SFL learning by functioning as opening moves in multimodal interactional exchanges that begin with the video and continue into the written comments. 2. Achieved. In depth analysis of 2,840 language and culture related comments revealed a number of discursive features associated with interactional learning. These include (a) a prevalence of interactional acts related to information transfer; (b) frequent use of acts indicating uptake of information; (c) frequent prolonged sequences of comment exchanges indicating negotiation of meaning; (d) frequent marking of comments for affective and epistemic stance, indicating both orientation towards engagement in interaction and changes in affective and cognitive state. 3. Achieved. Analysis of the content of exchanges shows the presence of a number of different practices associated with SFL learning. These include (a) evaluation of language performance by self and others; (b) questioning of language accuracy and other-correction; (c) explicit teaching; (d) language play; (e) discussion of language differences; (f) discussion of social and cultural aspects of language use. An important finding of the study is that, although direct SFL learning and teaching is common, YouTube comments may play a more important role as a forum for discussion of language differences and relationships between language and culture. 4. Achieved. This objective is largely interpretive and based on reflection on findings related to objectives 1-3. The interactional learning processes in the study are sometimes intentional and explicit, but mostly incidental and/or tacit. There is little evidence that commenters view transactional videos for the purpose of SFL learning. But there is a good deal of evidence that viewing and commenting on them provides opportunities for interest-driven, situated and informal SFL communication and learning that are difficult to provide in the classroom.

840211.label: Major findings and research outcome
840211.value: It is widely acknowledged that the achievement of high levels of second or foreign language (SFL) proficiency depends on opportunities to use the language in authentic communicative contexts. The lack of such opportunities presents a considerable barrier to SFL learners who are learning languages at a distance from communities of those who use them in everyday communication. However, the growth of globalized social media services such as YouTube has begun to lower these barriers, by creating opportunities for interaction with users of the target language across geographical distance, and by allowing access to transnational online communities in which the target language is the medium of communication. As yet, however, there is little real evidence on what and how languages are learned in such communities. The significance of this study is that it is among the first to provide direct evidence of SFL learning in the context of participation in a globalized social media service. The study has shown, firstly, how YouTube videos with ‘translingual’ content create contexts for discussion of language issues in the comments they attract. An analysis of 8,850 comments on 10 groups of videos with translingual (Chinese and English) content showed that 32% of the comments were language-related. In-depth discourse analysis of these language-related comments revealed evidence of SFL learning, indicated by (a) a prevalence of interactional acts related to information transfer; (b) frequent use of acts indicating uptake of information; (c) frequent prolonged sequences of comment exchanges involving negotiation of meaning; (d) frequent marking of comments for affective and epistemic stance, suggesting both orientation towards engagement in interaction and changes in affective and cognitive state. Analysis of the content of exchanges showed that the practices involving SFL learning included (a) evaluation of language performance by self and others; (b) questioning of language accuracy and other-correction; (c) explicit teaching; (d) language play; (e) discussion of language differences; and (f) discussion of social and cultural aspects of language use. An important finding of the study is that, although direct SFL learning and teaching is common, YouTube comments may play a more important role as a forum for discussion of language differences and relationships between language and culture. In sum, the study has demonstrated the potential of globalized social media services to provide opportunities for interest-driven, situated and informal SFL communication and learning that are difficult to provide in the language classroom in many parts of the world.

840211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
840211.value: This study shows the potential that globalized social media services provide for informal SFL communication and learning and offers a discourse analysis framework for identifying learning in practice. It points the way towards a language education research programme that will investigate a range of online contexts for informal SFL learning, including media sharing sites, online games and social networking services. In this context it shows the importance of going beyond the potential for learning towards a better understanding of how sites for SFL learning are constructed in the landscape of social media and how SFL learning is achieved interactionally. The limitation of the study is that it is confined to publically available textual evidence and the particular context of comments on video. A valuable complementary research direction that the PI aims to pursue is through observational and narrative case studies of individual SFL learners using the target language across a range of online activities and contexts. Research that tests the robustness of the analytical framework for identifying interactional learning in other online contexts would also be of great value.

840211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
840211.value: For people who learn languages at a distance from those who use them in everyday communication, opportunities for authentic interaction can be rare. The growth of globalized social media services, however, has begun to open up new opportunities for interaction in transnational online communities in which the target language is the medium of communication. This study has examined direct evidence of language learning in comments on YouTube videos with ‘translingual’ (Chinese and English) content. It shows how these videos create contexts for discussion of language issues in the comments they attract. In-depth discourse analysis of language-related comments revealed frequent use of discourse features associated with interactional learning. It also revealed a variety of language learning practices, including (a) evaluation of language performance, (b) questioning of language accuracy, (c) explicit teaching, (d) language play, (e) discussion of language differences, and (f) discussion of social and cultural aspects of language use. In sum, the study demonstrates the potential of social media services for interest-driven, situated and informal foreign language learning that are difficult to provide in the language classroom alone. It points the way for further research across a wider range of social media platforms.

840611.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
840611.value: 海南省的語言十分豐富和特殊，島上住了說不同語言和漢語方言的居民，自古以來，他們長期交流，語言互相影響。當中值得我們留意的是西部東方市的哥隆話（又叫村語）。哥隆話有幾項較為突出的語言特徵： 1. 有研究指出哥隆話擁有漢語和黎語的成份，這是當地的黎族居民和漢人語言長期接觸的成果。哥隆話可以說是一種混合語(creole language)。漢語和黎語在哥隆話這種混合語形成過程中扮演什麼角色：哥隆話是漢化了的黎語，還是受黎語影響的漢語呢？它的底層成分是什麼？ 2. 除了哥隆話，東方市流通的語言也不少，它們有不同的社會功能，我們發現部分說哥隆話的居民為了增加自己在社會上的競爭力，陸續放棄自己的母語，轉用普通話（目標語），出現了「語言轉移」情況。根據我們之前在三亞市和廣西地區進行的大型社會語言學調查，「語言轉移」(language shift)是由多個「語言飄離」(language drift)的過渡階段積累而成的。母語和目標語的使用比例會因應不同的環境而有所不同。東方市哥隆話的語言轉移情況會是怎樣呢？它跟中國其他多語城市，如三亞和廣西地區，有什麼異同的地方？ 3.語言轉移可以進一步影響語言內部結構，尤其是當接觸的兩種語言有明顯的類型學差異時。以雙賓句為例，哥隆話跟大部份漢語南方方言一樣，直接賓語出現在間接賓語之前，如「我給一本書你」，普通話的語序則相反，即「我給你一本書」。在語言接觸下，哥隆話會否採用普通話語序呢？換句話說，普通話對哥隆話的語法結構和詞匯有什麼影響？ 基於以上的初步觀察，本項目將從社會語言學和語言類型學角度調查哥隆話，當中有三個課題。 1. 重新調查哥隆話，藉此梳理出哥隆話、黎語、漢語和東方市內其他方言／語言之間的互動關係； 2. 通過社會語言學調查了解東方市的語言環境和各種語言的使用狀況，並探討哥隆話語言轉移和語言流失(language loss)等情況； 3. 跟不同年齡段的哥隆話居民進行田野調查，內容主要集中在那些跟現代漢語有明顯類型學差異的語法結構和詞匯，藉此了解和分析哥隆話的發展和演變。 我們希望通過以上三個課題來增加我們對語言發展的了解，包括當中的過程和涉及的語言內部和外在因素等；混合語發展過程中，各種語言扮演的角色等。此外，我們也希望進一步提升由語言轉移而引發瀕危語言現象的敏感度和認識。

840611.label: Major findings and research outcome
840611.value: This project investigated Gelong (哥隆話) spoken in the multi-lingual Dongfang city located in western Hainan from the perspectives of typology and sociolinguistics in the context of language contact. The project ran from 10-2011 to 3-2015. The project outcomes in relation to the four objectives are summarized below. Objective 1: The inter-relationship among Gelong, Chinese and Li was explored through linguistic fieldworks. The materials used consist of about 3,000 lexical items and 150 sentences. These data was then compared with the Li language and Gelong previously collected with an aim to find out any variations in the Gelong language. Chin (2015) examined 100 basic vocabulary items to explore the inter-relationship and the possible genetic affiliations among Gelong, Li and Chinese. Objective 2: Besides language structure, the impact of language contact can also be observed through the languages spoken in this multi-lingual speech community which are socio-linguistically stratified. In Dongfang, Putonghua, Hainanese and Gelong (including other dialects) serve different social functions. This unequal sociolinguistic status of language varieties causes some speakers to shift to using Putonghua as their dominant language. This phenomenon is not only found in public settings, but also in family. The project team conducted two sociolinguistic surveys to examine the rate and the extent of the shift. The surveys involved Gelong students in urban and rural areas. Around 400 students participated in the survey focuses on the use of students’ L1 (Gelong) and other linguistic varieties. Our concern is the usage frequency between L1 and Putonghua in different domains. The use of Putonghua by the informants across generations are 0.19 (grandparents’ generation), 0.24 (parents’ generation), and 0.40 (students’ own generation). A paper describing this sociolinguistic phenomenon is under preparation. Objective 3: The influence of Putonghua on local languages not only affects language use, but also the linguistic structure. As reported under Objective 1, the fieldwork with 2,800 lexical items and 150 sentences allow us to observe some ongoing changes in the language. Some of the results have been reported in Chin (2015) which is attached in this report. Since the data of the middle-aged informant does not have significant differences from the data collected three decades ago, the project team then placed more focus on the affiliation of Gelong and the language shift and loyalty issues. Objective 4: Intra-linguistic and extra-linguistic factors (such as language contact) lead to the development of Gelong have been explored in Chin (2015) and the forthcoming paper.

840611.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
840611.value: The multilingual situation of the Hainan Province provides us with a very important platform for studying Chinese linguistics/dialectology and relevant sociolinguistic issues such as language shift and language loyalty. However, the linguistic situation of Hainan has not been well documented and evaluated. According to the Language Atlas of China published in 1987, only five Chinese dialects and two non-Sinitic languages were mentioned in the Sanya community. In fact, according to the project team’s prior investigation, there are at least 8 languages/dialects (including Gelong) spoken in the community. Such a complex multilingual situation deserves our attention, especially in the current context in which Putonghua, the lingua franca of the country, is gradually displacing the local dialects. The socio-economic and demographic factors accelerate the disappearance of the dialects. In addition, there are also non-Sinitic languages spoken in Hainan. Hlai (generally known as Li) has the longest history and its influence on the formation and development of other languages/dialects should not be under-estimated. It is expected that more work in the domains of linguistics, anthropology and sociology can be conducted in order to preserve the languages and dialects together with their associated histories and cultures.

840611.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
840611.value: This project offers an opportunity to look at how language evolves in a complex multilingual community, especially when the speaker population of the language concerned is not significantly large. Gelong was chosen in this project for (1) its relationship with the indigenous non-Sinitic language, Li; (2) its interaction with other languages and dialects such as Putonghua or Hainanese. The sociolinguistic surveys allow us to understand how loyal younger speakers toward their mother tongue. Combing this set of data with the data previously collected by the project team, a better and clearer picture on the language ecology of Hainan, especially the Sanya region can be obtained. Sanya has become an international city which elevates its socio-economic status and enhances the living standard of the local people. On the other hand, it has exerted negative impact on the language eco-system because of the dominant use of Putonghua to facilitate inter-group communication. More young speakers are giving up their own dialects and shifting to Putonghua due to its prestigious status. Such an outcome is unfavorable and should deserve the attention of the local community and the government. It is expected that some remedial measures can be proposed to impede the increasing rate of language loss.

840711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
840711.value: From the 25 December 1941 to 15 August 1945, Hong Kong was occupied by the Japanese army. During this period, most of the writers staying in prewar Hong Kong had left. Only a few such as Dai Wangshu (戴望舒, 1905–1950) and Ye Lingfeng (葉靈鳳, 1904–1975) remained and continued to publish their works. Writers from the pro-Japan camp published many literary works classified as “Peace Literature.” This project aims at collecting and reorganizing the Hong Kong literature published during the Japanese occupation, including literary works and critiques on newspapers and magazines such as “Hua Qiao Ri Bao,” “Xiang Dao Ri Bao,” “Xianggang Ri Bao,” “South China Daily News,” “New Asia,” and “Da Tong Hua Bao,” and at analyzing and studying the literary works and critiques related to the “Peace Literature” published by Dai Wangshu and Ye Lingfeng during that period. This paper will systematically organize the literary documents published during the Japanese Occupation to view their value and discuss the theory of "Peace Literature" and other related works. The research will mainly focus on Dai Wangshu and Ye Lingfeng, accompanied by Chen Jun Bao (陳君葆, 1898–1982), Huang Lu (黃魯), and other writers, to determine how the writers implicitly expressed the resistance by writing with metaphors and the use of enigmatic language and symbols. 1941年12月25 日至1945年8 月15日期間，香港被日軍佔領。在這特殊時期，戰前在港作家大部份離港，只有少數作家如戴望舒（1905-1950）和葉靈鳳（1904-1975）留港並繼續發表文章，另方面親日陣營作者則發表大量「和平文藝」論述和作品。本計劃擬捜集、整理日治時期香港文學資料，包括文藝作品及評論文章，集中對戴望舒、葉靈鳳這時期發表的作品以及有關和平文藝的論爭作出分析研究。 透過此項研究，本計劃期望有系統地整理長期埋沒的日治時期香港文學史料，檢視其文學價值；探討香港「和平文藝」理論及相關作品；再以戴望舒、葉靈鳳為中心，旁及陳君葆、黃魯等作家，探討香港日治時期作家如何透過曲筆、隱語和象徵，表達「內化的抵抗」。

840911.value: 广州市珠江水污染的环境外部性：空间特征价格模型分析

To investigate the spatial variations of river water pollution on housing values
To explore the effects of different dimensions of water pollution (proximity, visibility, clarity, and odour) on housing values
To quantify the environmental externalities induced by urban river water pollution
To identify residents’ attitudes towards river revitalization projects and preferences of ecosystem services provided by these projects

840911.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
840911.value: Three decades of unprecedented rapid industrialization and urbanization in China have increased prosperity and population in many cities. In tandem with these remarkable economic and social achievements, Chinese cities are facing challenging environmental problems. The decline of water quality in rivers running through Chinese cities has reached an alarming level. Apparently, the impact of poor water quality is confined to the water bodies themselves. However, their spillover environmental consequences have generated rather extensive negative externalities on the urban social sphere with serious negative impacts on the quality of urban life. The hedonic pricing method has been widely used to estimate non-market goods, serving as a powerful tool to infer the cost of environmental externalities from observable market behaviours. In comparison with other environmental externalities, water pollution has received little attention in the hedonic literature. This lack of interest might be attributed to the fact that water pollutants (such as dissolved oxygen, nitrogen and phosphorous) are usually unobservable and commonly will not directly impair the ecosystem services homeowners could derive from water (such as recreational opportunities and amenities). Especially in China, there is little robust evidence about the Chinese people’s perception and evaluation of the environmental externalities associated with urban river water pollution. However, this apparent general apathy probably contradicts the expressed behaviour of consumers who regard the proximity to surface water bodies as a key environmental component in house pricing. The primary objective of this research is to apply spatial hedonic models to estimate the externality of river water pollution, and the price elasticity of demand for river revitalization in China. Such environmental improvement schemes have been promoted recently by various governments at the central, provincial and municipal levels, including both river water quality improvement and natural landscape enhancement at river banks. Guangzhou, a major city in South China with 231 polluted watercourses embedded within its territory, has been adopted for a case study. Two econometric models will be constructed to evaluate the spatial dependence of variables: (a) spatial lag model, and (b) spatial error model. The linkages between urban river quality and home buying behaviours in the newly established housing market in China will be explored. Methodologically, the reliability, applicability and consistency of hedonic spatial models can be investigated in the context of China. Practically, the study can assess the efficiency of public resources and related policies with a view to maximizing the well-being of citizens in Chinese society.

840911.label: Realisation of objectives
840911.value: 1. A novel “cube contiguity” consisting a 3-dimensional spatial matrix is developed to incorporate spatial effects in hedonic price models. For a certain apartment, a “cube contiguity” is created, containing the storey which the house is located, as well as the two storeys above and the two storeys below if any. All apartment units within the cube contiguity would be considered as neighbors. This method can capture all spatial impacts at both vertical and horizontal dimensions. Based on the constructed spatial weighting matrix, Lagrange Multiplier (LM) and Robust LM tests are performed to diagnose the existence of spatial effects and determine whether spatial error model or spatial lag model could be used to account for spatial autocorrelation in Guangzhou's commercialized residential housing market. The development of “cube contiguity” method paves the way for rigorous and robust spatial hedonic study of apartments in similar high-rise and compact urban context. 2. The spatial variations of river water pollution on housing values have been investigated using the spatial hedonic models. Significant spatial dependence (either spatial error or spatial lag) can be found at a micro level analysis, which suggests that spatial effects should be taken into account, especially those associated with river pollution, to improve the estimates of the marginal values of spatial environmental amenities/disamenities. 3. The effects of various dimensions of urban river pollution, such as proximity, visibility and odour, are investigated using spatial hedonic models. No significant variation in water clarity can be observed in the study area, as all urban rivers in the study area are heavily polluted. In the restored watercourses, the water quality is at Grade IV level, still black. Thus this variable is excluded from spatial hedonic models. 4. The negative environmental externalities induced by urban river water pollution and the positive environmental externalities brought by river restoration have been explored via both basic hedonic pricing model and spatial hedonic model. 5. Guangzhou residents' attitudes towards river restoration (including water quality improvement and riverbank greening) have been investigated, through estimating their willingness-to-pay for riparian restoration and better water quality and the capitalization of such willingness-to-pay in Guangzhou’s residential housing market.

840911.label: Major findings and research outcome
840911.value: Major findings: 1. At the micro neighbourhood level, significant spatial effects can be identified, thus spatial hedonic models should be applied to estimate the marginal implicit prices of the attribute variables on housing prices. At the municipal level, insignificant spatial effects have been detected, indicating the absence of any serious autocorrelation and heteroskedasticity. 2. Proximity to heavily polluted urban streams could lower the property prices, and this negative impact will be gradually diminishing with the increase of distance. The impacts of proximity vary considerably in high-rise, compact urban context.View of urban river fails to command a premium. The impacts of proximity and view might be associated with the hydro-morphological feature and riverine landscape, as well as homebuyers’ subjective perception of river pollution. 3. River restoration could reverse negative environmental externalities of polluted urban rivers to positive externalities, especially for those apartments located on the 10th floor or lower. River restoration (including river bank greening and water quality improvement) could increase property values by 4.61%, demonstrating a preference of Guangzhou residents for greening riverscapes. Research outcome: 1. Environmental externalities of urban river pollution and restoration: a hedonic analysis in Guangzhou (China). Landscape and Urban Planning (ranked 1st out of 40 in Urban Studies), minor revision has been suggested and the revised manuscript has been submitted. 2. Impacts of urban stream pollution: a spatial hedonic analysis of high-rise residential buildings in Guangzhou, south China. Land Use Policy (top 10% journal in Environmental Studies), under review. 3. The third paper is under preparation.

840911.value: 1. To explore whether including interactive terms (such as between proximity and view) in spatial hedonic models could improve the statistical performance and generate robust evidence.

840911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
840911.value: Urban rivers, as one of the scarce natural landscape elements in compact cities, are suffering from pollution in the course of city expansion and densification, especially in developing countries like China. Yet whether and how urban river pollution might affect high-rise residential property values have seldom been investigated. This study evaluates the environmental externalities associated with water pollution and river restoration in Guangzhou in southern China. Results show that (1) river restoration could reverse negative externalities of polluted watercourses to positive externalities, especially for those apartments located on the 10th floor or lower; and (2) view of urban stream fails to command a premium, and the impacts of proximity to urban streams vary considerably in high-rise, compact urban context, which might be associated with the hydro-morphological feature and riverine landscape, as well as homebuyers’ subjective perception of river pollution. Assessing the impacts of urban stream pollution could provide the basis for understanding the negative externalities of urban river pollution, establishing priorities for restoring polluted urban streams, and planning the provision of multi-functional green-blue spaces.

841311.label: Project Objectives
841311.value: To test which language-related cognitive tasks can best distinguish compensated and uncompensated dyslexic adolescents from chronological age (CA) matched controls. To investigate the extent to which dyslexic adolescents have compensated for their early reading difficulties, both at the level of reading and at the level of cognitive processes that support reading by testing for remaining residual difficulties in compensated dyslexics. To examine to what extent compensated and uncompensated dyslexics exhibit cognitive profiles that are similar to or different from their childhood profiles. 841311.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
841311.value: Dyslexia is a major stressor on children’s personal, emotional and social development and affects about 10% of the school population. Research has revealed a number of problems associated with dyslexia in children, but little follow up into adolescence has been done on this learning disability. However, we do know that around 25% of the dyslexic population with diagnosed childhood dyslexia will compensate in adolescence to the point that their reading is well within the normal range, at least in alphabetic languages. The proposed project will examine the cognitive and neurophysiological levels of linguistic sensitivity in a group of Hong Kong Chinese-speaking compensated and uncompensated dyslexic adolescents. The proposed project will thus have four aims: (1) to examine which language-related cognitive tasks are best for distinguishing compensated and uncompensated dyslexic adolescents from normal readers; (2) to investigate the extent to which compensated dyslexics have overcome deficiencies in reading and language-related cognitive processes and what residual difficulties still remain; (3) to examine the extent to which compensated and uncompensated dyslexics exhibit cognitive profiles that are similar or different from their childhood profiles; and (4) to use electrophysiological measures to investigate various cognitive aspects of linguistic processes that underlie both groups. The project will adopt a multi-dimensional approach that considers reading problems as a manifestation of a complex disorder involving multiple dimensions of cognitive and neurological processing. In phase 1, various cognitive measures associated with reading difficulty will be tested to obtain clear cognitive profiles of all participants. A total of 120 Hong Kong secondary school students will be recruited in three groups: 40 uncompensated dyslexics (UD), 40 compensated dyslexics (CD) and 40 chronological age matched (CA). In Phase II, the 120 students from Phase I (40 per group) will participate in different experiments involving linguistic stimuli and ERP to test the extent to which compensated and uncompensated Chinese adolescent dyslexics show different pre-attentive processes in response to verbal stimuli. The findings of this project will have significant theoretical and educational implications. In practical terms, understanding compensation could provide important information about variability in adolescent literacy development. In theoretical terms, the results will enhance our understanding of the characteristics of both dyslexic groups in the Chinese-speaking population. Furthermore, the project will identify neurobiological markers of Chinese developmental dyslexia, and potentially further clarify the pathophysiology of this disorder. 讀寫障礙是兒童個人、情緒及社交發展的主要壓力源。根據統計，約百分之十的在學學生正受讀寫障礙的困擾。研究指出兒童讀寫障礙與多個問題有關，但至今為止仍相對缺乏針對在兒童時期有讀寫障礙的青少年的學習能力的跟進研究。與此同時，研究發現約百分之二十五在幼時被評估為有讀寫障礙的青少年拼音文字語言的閱讀能力能達到正常水平。本研究計劃的主要對象為以粵語為母語的香港青少年，他們分別為於小學及中學階段皆被評估為有讀寫障礙的初中生，以及於小學階段被評估為有讀寫障礙但於中學階段的評估結果未顯示為有讀寫障礙的初中生。透過分析這批學生在認知和腦部功能兩方面的語言敏感度，本計劃旨在﹕(一) 找出能有效地辨別曾經被評估為有讀寫障礙的初中生和一般初中生的語言認知測驗；(二) 分析於小學階段被評估為有讀寫障礙但於中學階段的評估結果未顯示為有讀寫障礙的初中生的閱讀能力和與語言有關的認知過程的改善程度，同時找出他們持續面對的困難；(三) 測量曾經被評估為有讀寫障礙的學生的認知能力，從而比較這批學生幼時和現時的認知能力的異同；(四) 利用腦電圖測試，分析曾經被評估為有讀寫障礙的學生在不同認知範疇的語言處理歷程。 本研究視閱讀困難為一複合性障礙的表現，包含不同層面的認知和腦神經處理歷程。在第一階段，為清楚了解學生的認知能力，所有參與研究的學生會接受一次有關中文讀寫能力及與閱讀有關的認知能力的測試。為數一百二十人的香港初中生會被平均分成三組﹕(一) 於小學及中學階段皆被評估為有讀寫障礙的初中生；(二) 於小學階段被評估為有讀寫障礙但於中學階段的評估結果未顯示為有讀寫障礙的初中生； (三) 年齡對照組。在第二階段，所有參與研究的學生會接受包括語言刺激和腦電圖在內的測試，從而得知在面對言語刺激時，組別(一)及組別(二)的學生在多大程度上顯示出不同的前注意處理歷程。 是次研究結果具有多重意義。在應用層面上，通過分析組別(二)的初中生在閱讀能力和與語言有關的認知過程上的改進，從而得知青少年在讀寫能力發展的多變性。在理論層面上，是次研究能增加我們對以粵語為母語、且曾經被評估為有讀寫障礙的學生的了解。此外，本研究能鑑定發展性讀寫障礙的神經生物學標記，以進一步釐清此障礙的病理。

841311.label: Realisation of objectives
841311.value: All four objectives stated in the project were achieved. This project attempted to examine both the cognitive and neurophysiological levels of linguistic sensitivity. A total of 294 Hong Kong Chinese-speaking adolescents with dyslexia and typically developing students were recruited for this project. They were followed from Grade 2 to Grade 10. Among the 294 students, 228 dyslexic students, 28 students with high-functioning dyslexics (or compensated dyslexics), and 40 typically developing students were assessed in Grade 2 (Time 1) and in Grade 8 (Time 2) in Phase I. A wide range of measures for cognitive, linguistic and literacy skills were developed and administered to these students individually for Time 1 and Time 2. The measures used included literacy skills, phonological awareness, visual-orthographic knowledge, morphological skills, syntactic skills, discourse skills, oral vocabulary knowledge, working memory, rapid naming, and executive functioning. In Phase II, 50 dyslexic students, 8 of whom were high-functioning students, and 40 typically developing students were recruited and administered behavioral and event-related potential (ERP) measures. Pilot studies were carried out using a small sample to try out the measures. A series of data analyses was conducted. Based on the pilot studies and longitudinal data collected, Three papers were published in the top journals in the field. A book chapter, a newsletter, and a Master of Philosophy thesis were published. Five papers were also presented at local professional workshops and international conferences. Another paper is in preparation for Child Development and Brain and Language.

841311.label: Major findings and research outcome
841311.value: This project investigated various core and universal cognitive-linguistic processes that might distinguish the high-functioning dyslexics from the dyslexics, and typically developing peers, and examined their profiles. Behavioral data showed that the high-functioning dyslexics performed better than the dyslexics in visual-orthographic knowledge, word reading, one-minute reading, writing, and reading comprehension. Results also found that both high-functioning dyslexics and dyslexics performed more poorly than their typically developing peers in rapid naming, visual-orthographic knowledge, morphological skills, verbal working memory, reading and writing skills. Compared to the dyslexics, the high-functioning dyslexics showed greater improvement in visual-orthographic knowledge and reading skills over time. Additionally, over half of the high-functioning dyslexics and dyslexics exhibited deficits in rapid naming which frequently appeared in association with other cognitive and linguistic deficits. Most high-functioning dyslexics were found to have residual problems in rapid naming and morphological skills. Findings underscore the importance of rapid naming, visual-knowledge knowledge, and morphological skills underlying the manifestations of high-functioning dyslexics and dyslexics. Similar to the behavioral findings, ERP evidence suggests that the high-functioning dyslexics, dyslexics, and typically developing students have different component neurocognitive mechanisms. A study comparing the high-functioning dyslexics and dyslexics on the visual-orthographic knowledge found that the high-functioning dyslexics demonstrated a slightly larger P200 however, suggesting a possibility of improvement in visual-orthographic knowledge from Time 1 to Time 2. A plausible explanation is that most high-functioning dyslexics may compensate for their poor orthographic knowledge and skills through use of context, general knowledge, and vocabulary. Through exposure to print, reading experience, and remedial programs, individuals with dyslexia may also continue to show gradual improvement in visual-orthographic development and learning over time. ERP data also revealed that the dyslexics showed a smaller N400 compared to the typically developing students. Furthermore, the dyslexic students displayed a reduced pattern on semantic and morphological consolidation, as reflected by a late positive ERP component, suggesting that dyslexic readers may use a backtrack stage and semantic information in their working memory during morphological and semantic processing. Such results suggest a possible weakness of morphological and semantic processing in dyslexic students. The ERP measures of N400 and LPC could be used to discriminate dyslexics from typically developing students. Finally, compared to their peers, the dyslexics showed deficits in executive functioning by displaying a smaller N100 and P300. These findings generally underscore the importance of morphological and semantic processing, and executive functioning in Chinese reading for adolescents with dyslexia.

841311.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
841311.value: Future studies are needed to confirm the present findings especially longitudinal studies with more time points and increasing sample size in order to better understand the nature of high-functioning dyslexics, particularly in EEG and FMRI studies. Furthermore, the neurophysiological distinction between the high-functioning, dyslexics, and typically developing students is needed to be further investigated. Further studies that analyze comorbidities and additional cognitive-linguistic processes are needed to replicate our findings in a larger sample size.

841311.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
841311.value: The present project examined the reading-related cognitive-linguistic processes that might distinguish among the high-functioning dyslexics, dyslexics, and typically developing adolescents, and identify their profiles using behavioral and Event-Related Potentials (ERPs) methodology. The high-functioning dyslexics are sometimes known as resilient readers who have a history of childhood dyslexia but as young adults can comprehend text well despite residual difficulties in cognitive-linguistic skills, for example, rapid naming and morphological skills. Compared to the dyslexics, the high-functioning dyslexics showed a greater improvement in visual-orthographic knowledge and reading skills. Both high-functioning dyslexics and dyslexics performed worse than their typically developing peers in all cognitive-linguistic and literacy measures. Neural differences were also found between the dyslexic and typically developing adolescents and these differences may suggest different brain markers of dyslexia in Chinese. These findings generally underscore the importance of morphological and semantic processing, and executive functioning in Chinese reading for adolescents with dyslexia. The outcome of this project enhances our understanding of the characteristics of high-functioning dyslexics and dyslexics and thus helps us design appropriate training and intervention methods. Furthermore, the project offers insight into the pathophysiology of dyslexia in Chinese adolescents that may yield neurobiological markers of the cause(s) of dyslexia in Chinese.

841711.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
841711.value: ‘Instructional leadership’ first achieved currency in the USA during the early 1980s based on results of research on instructionally effective schools. Over subsequent decades, this construct has shaped research, policy and practice in education reform throughout the world. Its importance was recently reaffirmed in a meta-analysis which concluded that instructional leadership provided a more robust explanation for linkages between leadership and learning than competing models (Robinson, Lloyd & Rowe, 2008). These and related findings have established instructional leadership as a significant domain in educational management. Progress in a global program of research over the past 30 years has been facilitated by the development of conceptual and methodological tools. One such tool has been the Principal Instructional Management Rating Scale (Hallinger, 1983). Another recent review concluded that use of the PIMRS has been strong and consistent across the period from 1983 to 2010 (Hallinger, in press). Since 1983 the PIMRS has been employed in over 140 empirical studies in 10 countries, thereby establishing it as the most widely used scale in the study of instructional leadership around the world. Yet, the PIMRS was developed 30 years in an American context that differs from the global education context in which the instrument is being used today. For example, compared with the 1980s, school systems are now emphasizing greater accountability for results and the need for collaboration in leadership. Thus, there is a need to reassess the validity of the PIMRS and refine its capacity as a tool for research and practice in today's schools. This project has three goals. First, we will reassess the validity of the PIMRS from both conceptual and statistical perspectives. Second, we will explore the cross-cultural validity of the PIMRS by reanalyzing secondary data from studies conducted outside of the United States. Third, we will conduct a meta-analysis of PIMRS studies to explore the impact of principal gender on the exercise of instructional leadership. The project will draw upon datasets obtained from previously completed studies. This will enable in-depth analysis into the properties of the PIMRS instrument using statistical methods (i.e., Rasch modeling) that were unavailable at the time of its original validation. This project will, therefore, both contribute to substantive knowledge on a specific facet of instructional leadership (i.e., gender) and enhance the capacity for conducting future research on instructional leadership through enhancement of its capacities as a research tool. 「教學領導」於八十年代在美國開始流行，來源於學校效能改進的研究所得。幾十年來，這個理論影響了全球對教育改革的研究與政策實施。它的重要性在最近的一項綜合分析研究中再次驗證，這項研究總結出，比起其他競爭的理論模型，「教學領導」對領導力與學習的聯繫提供了更強大的解釋（Robinson, Lloyd & Rowe,2008)。這些相關研究建立了教學領導理論在教學管理中的支配地位。 這三十年來理論和方法工具的發展充實了全球關於教學領導的研究。其中一個研究工具名為「校長教學管理量表」（PIMRS）(Hallinger, 1983)。另外一個近期的研究總結了從1983年到2010年採用PIMRS的研究，證明它是強大而且一致的(Hallinger, 發表中)。自1983年起，PIMRS被十個國家超過140項實證研究採用，所以，這是世界上對教學領導研究最廣泛應用的量表。 但是，PIMRS發展三十年來建基于美國背景，與把這個量表應用到其他地區的教育背景不同。比如，相比八十年代，現在的學校機制更加強調對結果的問責和合作領導的需要。所以，現在有重新評估PIMRS有效性的需要，和完善它用於今天的學校研究和實踐的能力。 這個項目有三個目的。首先，我們會重新評估PIMRS在觀念和統計方面的有效性。其次，我們將通過重新分析美國以外的輔助數據來檢驗PIMRS跨文化的有效性。最後，我們將進行一次PIMRS研究的綜合分析，以探討性別對教學領導工作的影響。 這個項目會採用已完成的研究所得的數據庫。并將會採用數據分析方法（比如羅氏模型）深入分析PIMRS工具的有效性，這在原有的研究無法驗證其效度。因此，這個項目不但有助於充實關於教學領導具體方面（比如性別）的實質知識，而且通過加強其作為研究工具的能力，提高它應用在未來教學領導研究的效能。

841711.label: Realisation of objectives
841711.value: For the first objective we conducted the most comprehensive reliability study that we are aware of for any extant leadership instrument, inside or outside of education (see Hallinger et al., 2013, 2015). We used a more accurate reliability test based on Generalizability Theory rather than Cronbach's alpha test for data collected with the Teacher Form. Then we conducted a meta-analytic reliability study using data from 50+ independent studies. The meta-analysis reaffirmed high reliability (>.90) for the PIMRS teacher and principal forms at all construct levels. We then assessed the internal validity of the PIMRS from multiple perspectives using CFA, Rasch analysis, Wright Maps, and discriminant analysis of data obtained from multiple data sources. These meta-analytic studies of reliability and validity established that the PIMRS meets recommended standards for use in research, performance appraisal and needs assessment. Users now have access to published information fully establishing the reliability and validity of the PIMRS. The second objective sought to establish a empirical basis for using the PIMRS outside of the USA where it was first developed. Although 70+ studies had used the PIMRS outside of the USA, no studies had examined its validity when used in these contexts. Although our basic validity study established 'measurement invariance' for several Asian countries (Hallinger et al., 2015),we expanded on this analysis through in-depth studies using new data collected in Chile and Turkey. The results reinforced the findings published in Hallinger et al. (2015) both with respect to reliability and validity. We humbly submit that these studies of the reliability and validity of the PIMRS have not only provided comprehensive empirical results supporting continued use of the PIMRS by researchers internationally, but also demonstrated a new standard for assessing the viability of leadership instruments. The third objective sought to understand if and how gender influences principal instructional leadership. We conducted a meta-analysis (Hallinger, Li & Wang, submitted for review) using data obtained from 40 independent data sets. The results for all construct levels clearly established that gender exerts a small (i.e., effect size > .20) but statistically significant (p > .01) and practically meaningful effect on principal instructional leadership. We found that female principals tend to exercise more active instructional leadership than male counterparts. This effect was consistently observed across the different dimensions measured by the PIMRS and in three different national contexts (Hallinger, Li, & Wang, submitted for review).

841711.label: Major findings and research outcome
841711.value: The first two objectives of this project concerned instrument development rather than 'substantive findings' related to school leadership. With this in mind, the major findings were as follows. 1. A meta-analytic study (Hallinger et al., 2013, 2015) of the reliability of the PIMRS affirmed that the instrument meets high standards of reliability required for use in research, needs assessment and principal appraisal. Moreover, the reliability results were consistent across multiple national contexts including the USA, Thailand, China, Taiwan, Turkey, Malaysia, and Chile. 2. A series of validation analyses (Bellibas et al., submitted for review; Fromm et al., submitted for review; Hallinger et al., 2015) similarly affirmed that the PIMRS meets standards of content, construct and discriminant validity required for similar purposes. Again, the validity results were quite consistent across multiple national contexts including the USA, Turkey, and Chile. Taken together, the reliability and validity results suggest that the PIMRS meets a 'gold standard' as an instrument for collecting data on principal instructional leadership. 3. In addition to these substantive findings, the project also demonstrated a more comprehensive approach to assessing the reliability and validity of a leadership instrument than is typical in our field. Thus, researchers may find the research procedures detailed in our reports of equal interest. 4. The project yielded a shortened 23 item version of the PIMRS Teacher Form. This will be especially useful when researchers use the scale in combination with other construct measures, as is often the case in school leadership research. 5. As an unexpected outcome of our cross-cultural validation studies, we demonstrated a new approach to 'mapping' instructional leadership at the national level. Using nationally representative data for Turkey (Bellibas et al., submitted for review) and Thailand (Hallinger & Lee, 2013, 2014), we provided 'instructional leadership profiles' of principals that detailed patterns of perceived practice. This is, arguably, a more valid measure of principal leadership than relying on the several items included in international secondary data sets such as PIRLS or TALIS. 6. For 30 years, anecdotal reports from individual studies have suggested gender differences between female and male principals. Our meta-analytic results were conclusive that female principals tend to be more actively engaged in this role than male principals. The finding holds implications for principal selection for school systems seeking to strengthen instructional leadership capacity.

841711.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
841711.value: Five lines of inquiry are indicated by the results of this project. First, we recommend a meta-analytic study of the student achievement results embodied in the database of 249 independent PIMRS studies collected in this project. Second, the validation study conducted within the scope of the current project should be expanded to include an assessment of external validity. Third, the cross-cultural validation of the instrument should be applied systematically to additional national contexts. Fourth, the cross-cultural validation of the PIMRS already completed in this project should facilitate the efforts of researchers in undertaking cross-cultural comparative studies of principal leadership. This approach has been severely lacking in our field, in part due to the lack of validated instruments. We suggest that as the discipline of educational leadership becomes more 'global' in scope, cross-cultural studies represent the 'new frontier' of knowledge. Finally, the study demonstrated two approaches to 'mapping' instructional leadership capacity at the national level. These approaches hold potential for assisting policymakers in understanding progress that arises (or doesn't) from investments in initiatives aimed at strengthening leadership capacity at different system levels.

841711.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
841711.value: Over the past 20 years, research findings have confirmed that few, if any, significant improvements in school learning outcomes come about without quality leadership. This has spurred researchers to engage in studies that seek to understand the means by which leadership makes a difference in the quality of teaching and learning. This research project sought to support this global effort at understanding the nature of effective school leadership by strengthening one of the key research tools used in studies of school leadership, the Principal Instructional Management Rating Scale (PIMRS). Over the past 30 years, the PIMRS has been used by more than 250 researchers to study school leadership in 35 countries. This project analyzed data gathered in more than 70 of these studies for the purposes of assessing the accuracy of the instrument as a tool for research and principal appraisal. The study affirmed that this research instrument can be used for these purposes across different cultural contexts. In addition, the study demonstrated the feasibility of using the instrument for evaluating leadership not only at the school level, but also at the national level. Thus, the results study have potential to enhance the quality of future leadership research and practice.

842011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
842011.value: Error Analysis (EA) responded to how contrastive analysis (CA) failed to predict second language (L2) errors from L1 and L2 contrasts (e.g. Richards 1971; 1974a; 1974b, Corder, 1973; 1981, Dulay and Burt, 1974, James, 1998). Interest in EA waned because it assessed learner language from a non-developmental perspective and found identifying the sources of errors problematic (e.g. Shachter and Celce-Murcia, 1977; Ellis and Barkhuizen, 2007). Cognitive Linguistics (CL) renews interest, however, by treating all form as meaningful and meaning as originating in the conceptualizations through which an enactive cognition structures experience (e.g. Talmy, 1978, Lakoff, 1987, Langacker 1990). CL has revitalised Sapir (1949) and Whorf’s (1956) proposition that different languages give cultures different ways of structuring reality (e.g. Lucy and Gaskins, 1979; Lucy and Shweder 2001) thus emphasizing how language learners must cross a conceptual divide. Concomitantly, some L2 errors begin in the use of second language forms with first language meanings and the conceptualizations that these carry (Slobin, 1985; 1996, Valeva, 1996; Holme, 2004) requiring from the student what has come to be called ‘conceptual fluency’ (Valeva, 1996). This project has two phases. In Phase 1 we exploit a one million word corpus of academic writing from Chinese L1 users of academic English compiled in a previous internally financed project. We use this corpus to search for consistent errors and place them on the lexico-grammatical continuum categorizing them as grammatical and semantically schematic or lexical and semantically substantive. We search the error type to determine its relative frequency, disregard the infrequent and thus compile an inventory of significant errors and their exemplars for this learner group. In phase 2 we translate the errors into Chinese and search for their frequency on the ICLE (International Corpus of Learner English) looking at files from non-Chinese learners. Errors will be treated as products of interference or of a different conceptual knowledge if translation evidences a ‘fit’ with Chinese lexico-grammar and ICLE searches show them to be infrequent or non-existent in the cognate language corpus. The ICLE search thus helps determine how the errors are specific to interference from the conceptual and semantic patterning of the Chinese language. Last we analyse this inventory of errors to determine how far they are products of the Chinese language’s different conceptual and semantic systems and so produce an empirically founded inventory of constructions that Chinese learners find difficult and a CL based analysis of why. 當對比分析(CA)通過比較母語(L1)和二語(L2)卻無法預測二語(L2)錯誤時, 錯誤分析(EA)這個研究領域就應運而生了(如Richards，1971; 1974a; 1974b；Corder，1973; 1981；Dulay和Burt，1974；詹姆斯，1998)。大家對EA的興趣減退是因為它從一個非發展性的角度去評估二語學習者語言，並且發現通過EA很難找出錯誤的起源(即Shachter和Celce-Murcia，1977; Ellis和Barkhuizen，2007)。然而，認知語言學(CL)認為所有形式都有含義，並且認為含義是起源於由法定的認知來認識世界這一概念化過程，從而使人們重新對EA產生興趣(即Talmy，1978；Lakoff，1987；Langacker，1990)。認知語言學(CL) 使薩皮爾Sapir (1949) 和沃爾夫Whorf (1956) 的論點復蘇, 該論點認為，不同的語言促使不同的文化通過不同的方法來建構現實, 因此一些專家強調第二語言學習者必須跨越一個由不同文化產生的概念性的鴻溝(如Lucy和Gaskins，1979; Lucy和Shweder，2001)。隨之而來的是一些L2錯誤的形成，它們來源於使用第二語言的形式來傳達母語的含義及這些含義所包含的概念(Slobin，1985; 1996；Valeva，1996; Holme，2004)，因此有專家提出學生需要懂得什麼是所謂的“概念性流暢（Valeva，1996）。 這個研究項目分為兩個階段。在第一階段中，我們探索一個一百萬字的學術英語語料庫。作為不久前一個學院內部提供經費的項目的研究成果，該語料庫由漢語為母語的學生寫作的學術英語文章構成。我們從中搜尋反復出現的錯誤，然後將收集的錯誤放置在一個詞彙－語法連續體上(lexico-grammatical continuum)，最後將它們分類成語法和語義概括的或詞彙和語義上的獨立體(substantive)。我們搜尋到不同的錯誤種類再確定它們的相對頻率，不考慮低頻錯誤，從而匯總出反映這個學習者群體所犯的顯著錯誤及相應的範例。在第二階段，我們將這些含有錯誤的例句翻譯成漢語，並且在ICLE（學習者英語國際語料庫）中搜尋來自非漢語為母語的學習者所提供的文集中出現的類似錯誤及確定錯誤的頻率。假若發現相應的漢語翻譯與中文詞彙語法相“吻合”，並且在ICLE的同源語料庫中搜尋亦顯示這些錯誤罕見或是不存在，這些錯誤將被認為是受到母語幹擾或是源於不同的概念性知識。在ICLE中進行搜尋有助於確定這些錯誤是如何受到來自特定的漢語的概念和語義模式特點的幹擾而形成的。最後我們分析匯總的錯誤以確定它們究竟有多大程度是由於漢語和英語不同的概念和語義系統互相干擾而導致的，從而提供一個基於實證的錯誤匯總；它收集了中國學生們難以掌握的語言結構，並且從認知語言學(CL)的角度對這些錯誤進行解答分析。

842111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
842111.value: 癌症治療上的進展大大延長了病患者的壽命。由於癌症治療逐步從醫院轉移到家庭或社區環境，家庭照顧者在提供各種支持上面對不少困難。他們還跟病患者分擔一些性命悠關的生活責任。儘管家庭照顧者需要支持以減少適應失調的風險，過去很少研究在中國人社會進行。這12個月的前瞻性研究，旨在探討癌症患者及其家庭照顧者適應過程中的生理和社會認知的基礎和流程。取得倫理委員會的批准後，共有250對癌症患者及其主要家庭照顧者將接受三次訪問（基線、6個月和12月跟進）。收集數據之前每位參與者會提供知情同意書。我們將評估照顧者以下方面：生理反應（即唾液樣本中皮質醇水平）、同理心的準確性（即能夠推斷正確的其他人的想法和感受，並產生類似水平的情感與其他人）和照顧投入度（即在執行一個重要的生命任務時，表現出普遍並持久的、積極的情感和精神狀態）。患者及照顧者亦會報告社會支持的成效（即對需求的支持和接收／提供的支持的合的滿意度程度）和適應結果（即社會關係的質量與焦慮和抑鬱症狀）。該項目將在華人癌症照顧者的生理反應、社會認知和支持的過程和結果提供前瞻性證據。我們亦測試良好的同理心準確性會否提高照顧者提供社會支持的效率，從而提高照顧者和患者的社會關係質量及減低焦慮和抑鬱症狀。此外，照顧投入度作為一種新的行為適應結果將被引入到癌症心理學有關文獻。總體而言，這個項目提供重要資訊以發展照顧者教育和訓練，加強照顧者的技能支持癌症患者，從而促進患者和照顧者積極地適應癌症及其帶來的困難。

842111.label: Realisation of objectives
842111.value: All the four objectives have been fully achieved. Details of how each objective was realized are given below. Objective 1 and 2. Empathic accuracy or social cognition is one of the essential elements in this project. To begin with, we sought to identify cognitive tasks that were suitable for assessing empathic accuracy/social cognition among cancer patients and caregivers, who could be older and with lower education level. We identified Frith-Happé Animations, a nonverbal task for assessing different aspects of social cognition, translated it into Chinese, and validated the protocol in collaboration with the authors of the task. In the project period that followed, we collected prospective data on empathic accuracy, social support, adjustment outcomes among 263 cancer patients and 155 cancer caregivers. This is one of the largest samples that have been reported for cancer patients and caregivers in all Chinese populations. The dataset has been analyzed and used in the submissions of four manuscripts, among which two have been published and two are currently under review. In one of our prospective studies, we found that social cognition of cancer caregivers prospectively predicted higher patients’ and caregivers’ biopsychosocial functioning. Caregiver's mentalizing accuracy (i.e., how accurate caregivers could infer thoughts and feelings of others from subtle social cues) was associated with higher patient-reported dyadic relationship quality and anxiety symptoms and caregiver-reported caregiving burden. Caregiver's sensitivity to others’ mental states (i.e., how sensitive caregivers are with regard to social cues) predicted lower levels of depressive symptoms and higher levels of life satisfaction among caregivers. Our prospective study is the first of its kind to assess social cognition and its demographic and psychosocial correlates among cancer caregivers. Our findings provide an important evidence base for subsequent research on social cognitive and communication processes in cancer caregiving among Chinese populations. Objective 3. In another prospective study, we found that concordance of social support, meaning the extent to which patient-reported and caregiver-reported social support matched with each other in terms of quantity and quality, prospectively predicted higher psychological functioning among both cancer patients and their caregivers. Specifically, social cognition was found to moderate the association between concordance of social support and caregivers' psychological functioning. The positive association between concordance of received/provided support and depressive symptoms and the inverse association between concordance of social provisions (i.e., provisions of warmth, reassurance, and attachment between patients and caregivers) and anxiety symptoms was significant only among caregivers with lower social cognition. The findings suggest that higher social cognition of caregivers could have a buffering effect of the negative psychological impact of mismatched social support on cancer caregivers. This study extended the current literature by examining the concordance of patient-reported and caregiver-reported social support. We also added to the current literature by investigating whether and how social support transactions between patients and caregivers impact patients’ and caregivers’ psychological distress and well-being. More importantly, this project provided novel evidence on the role of caregivers’ social cognition in the association between support transactions and psychological outcomes, which is applicable to improving quality of life of people with chronic medical conditions and their caregivers. Objective 4: Like the objective task for assessing caregivers’ social cognition, we have validated a Chinese scale for assessing caregiving engagement among Chinese cancer patients and their caregivers in Hong Kong. All caregivers in this project were administered the newly developed scale on caregiving engagement. The scale was found to be highly internally consistent (Cronbach’s alpha > .80) and validly associated with other personality and social variables and psychosocial and biological outcome measures. We have been assessing caregiving engagement in all subsequent studies we conducted.

842111.label: Major findings and research outcome
842111.value: 1. We have investigated the prospective associations of caregivers' empathic accuracy with patient-reported and caregiver-reported outcomes (Part C, 8.1). Our longitudinal analysis showed that increased sensitivity to others’ mental states predicted lower levels of depressive symptoms and higher levels of life satisfaction among caregivers, whereas more accurate mentalizing for others’ emotions predicted lower levels of caregiving burden. This project is the first of its kind to assess social cognition and its demographic and psychosocial correlates among cancer caregivers. Our studies provide an important evidence base for subsequent research on the social cognitive processes in Chinese cancer caregiving. A family-assisted model could be adapted and modified for cancer caregivers and their ill social partners. 2. This project produced findings that extend the current literature on the concordance of patient-reported and caregiver-reported social support (Part C, 8.2). We investigated whether and how social support transactions between patients and caregivers impact caregivers’ psychological adaptation. Previous studies have only investigated perceptions of social support separately among patients and caregivers, not to mention analysis on the extent to which their perceptions match with each other. In addition, novel evidence is provided for the role of caregivers’ social cognition in the association between support transactions and psychological outcomes among people with chronic medical conditions and their caregivers. Despite the fact that social cognitive skills are important for effective interpersonal communication and efficiency of social support transactions, there were only studies among patients with schizophrenia and their family members but not other medical patients and their social partners. Our findings on the moderating effect of cancer caregivers' social cognition on the inverse association between concordance of social provisions and caregivers’ anxiety symptoms could inform studies of supportive care needs and psychosocial adaptation among cancer caregivers. 3. We have also reported additional psychosocial processes that could contribute to social support and psychological well-being among the study samples (Part C, 8.3-8.4). What we highlighted in the two papers is the importance of savoring positive moments in everyday life for cancer patients and their caregivers. Savoring intervention is recommendable for symptom management among cancer patients and stress management among their caregivers. 4. Two undergraduate students were funded by the budget and they successfully completed their participation in the project. Now they are able to develop/translate psychometric instruments, administer questionnaires to different population face-to-face, perform statistical analyses, and present in academic conferences/meetings.

842111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
842111.value: This project generated an evidence base for developing novel intervention or support group programs for cancer patients and their caregivers. Family-oriented social cognition has been found to improve psychotic symptoms, quality of life, and interpersonal relationship among outpatients with schizophrenia and their family members. Cancer patients and their untrained family caregivers could be instructed on how to seek support and provide timely support to each other with reference to exposure to differential cancer stressors including receipt of diagnosis, adherence to medical regimens, and adjustment in their everyday life. AT the same time, patients and caregivers could then receive structured psychosocial interventions on social cognition coupled with social-emotional skills such as emotion recognition. Such dyadic training protocols would best be administered to patients and caregivers during the initial stage of cancer process, i.e., at the time they receive the cancer diagnosis and enter the medical regimens. Patients with a terminal diagnosis and their family members/caregivers could be equipped with the necessary interpersonal skills for enhancing psychological and social well-being when facing palliative treatments. Patients with better prognosis could apply the acquired skills to cope with other life changes or cancer-related stressors like recurrence that emerge in the course of long-term survivorship.

842111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
842111.value: Because of diagnosis and treatment advancement, the prompt outcome of cancer death in the past is now replaced by long-term treatment. Informal caregivers are voluntarily forced to take up the major role of caring and shoulder the life-and-death responsibility for their ill social partners. If caregivers could provide appropriate amount of support without unnecessary or excessive effort and patients could optimally receive the support, better psychosocial adjustment in both patients and caregivers could be warranted. Cost-effective provision of timely social support requires precise identification of patients’ needs and emotional states. This questionnaire-based study offered longitudinal evidence on the extent to which caregivers could accurately sense their ill social partners' needs and how the accuracy contributes to physical and psychological well-being. This study was the first of its kind among Chinese cancer patients and caregivers. Our findings provided an important evidence base for subsequent research on patient-caregiver communication in cancer caregiving. A family-assisted model could be adapted and modified into a family-based or dyadic training protocols for cancer caregivers and their ill social partners.

842211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
842211.value: Civic and citizenship education is primarily constructed on Western models of politics and the state. It has been argued that such models are at odds with conceptions of citizenship in Asian countries (Lee, 2004; 2008). Nevertheless, successive international civic assessment projects (Torney, Oppenheim & Farren, 1975; Torney-Purta et al., 2001) have neglected alternative views of citizenship on the assumption that only the paradigm of liberal democracy is capable of driving citizenship development. The International Civic and Citizenship Study (ICCS) (Schulz et al., 2010) recognized the importance of eliciting diverse views of citizenship by including five Asian societies whose student samples completed both an International Survey and a specific Asian Regional Module (ARM). In cultural terms, this has created a two-dimensional data set: Asian students’ responses to the set of questions that students from 33 other countries also answered, and their specific responses to questions posed in the ARM. This unique data set provides the means to investigate empirically Asian students’ conceptions of citizenship and assess the distinctiveness or otherwise of these views. These empirical analyses will provide the first step in a theory building process the end point of which is to test the theoretical validity of the identified constructs. The theoretical outcomes of the proposed project will advance the field of citizenship education by expanding current conceptions of citizenship to embrace traditions and values that cannot be accommodated by various forms of Western liberalism. This expanded view of citizenship will also raise important issues about the role and function of the state in Asian societies. Given the significant role that Asia now plays in economic and political events, the specific aims of this project are to: • analyze Asian students’ conceptions of citizenship from multiple perspectives; • investigate the determinants of these attitudes; • compare these attitudes both within the region and beyond; • investigate the theoretical adequacy of the psychometrically derived constructs; and • evaluate the outcomes in relation the nature and purpose of citizenship education and the consequent implications for understanding conceptions of the state in Asian contexts. The results of this study will provide baseline data on Asian students’ conceptions ofcitizenship and lead to important theoretical understandings. Its comparative methodology will highlight the significance of understanding citizenship issues from multiple perspectives. It will provide important insights into the way future citizens think about citizenship in one of the most strategic regions in the world. 公民教育最初源自於西方的政治與國家模式。 一直以來都有爭論，認為西方這一個模式和亞洲國家所認知的公民教育概念有所不同。(Lee， 2004; 2008) 然而，以往的國際公民研究計劃(Torney， Oppenheim & Farren， 1975; Torney-Purta et al.， 2001)假設只有自由民主的範式方可以推動公民發展，卻忽略其他看法。 國際公民教育研究(Schulz et al.， 2010) 確信不同意見的重要性，並同時給兩份問卷予五個來自亞洲社會的學生作答，一份是和其他地區一樣的「國際問卷」，另外一份則是「亞洲問卷」。從文化角度而言，是次問卷調查同時收集了兩方面的數據：分別來自亞洲和其他33國家學生共同回答的問卷，以及來自亞洲學生回答的「亞洲問卷」。這些獨特的數據有助研究亞洲學生的公民概念，從而評估其獨特性和其他方面。這些分析同時是理論建構過程中的第一步，有助驗證其理論架構的有效度。藉擴展現有關於公民意識的概念和揉合傳統價值和西方的自由主義思想，預期計劃可提升公民教育理論方面的研究。此擴展亦有助關於「國家」在亞洲社會的角色和功能的討論。隨著亞洲現今在政治和經濟上都舉足輕重，此研究計劃的目標如下 ：１）從不同角度分析亞洲學生的公民概念；２）探討不同態度的成因；３）比較區內、外的表現；４）探討以心理測量學分析的結構理論特質；５）評核研究結果對公民教育的性質和目的以及對「國家」這概念在亞洲的啟示。研究結果將會提供一系列有關於亞洲學生對於公民教育概念的基數和帶來重要的理論認識。它的比較研究方法會從多角度突顯瞭解公民教育理念的重要性。這研究會為一個重要策略性地區於未來公民如何思考「公民」這概念上帶來重要啟示。

842211.label: Realisation of objectives
842211.value: Objective 1: Secondary data analysis was employed to develop measures using the Main Student Survey (participating societies in the International Civics and Citizenship Education Study (ICCS), Teacher Survey (teachers in the Asian societies participating in ICCS), the Principals’ Survey (Principals in the Asian societies participating in ICCS), the Asian Regional Module(students from the Asian societies participating in ICCS), the European Regional Module(students from the European societies participating in ICCS) and the Latin American module(students from the Latin American societies participating in ICCS). Raw data was used to develop measures (thus the research did not rely on the existing measures in the ICCS data base). The majority of studies used Plausible Values (PV) methodology to determine measures of Civic Knowledge. For each study, measures of civic values and dispositions were derived from the raw data. Their psychometric properties were reported in the research outputs. A range of statistical techniques was used but in particular different forms of multilevel modeling to recognize the hierarchical nature of the data set (students nested within schools). Each study conducted incorporated an extensive theoretical analysis ensuring the theoretical validity of constructs alongside their psychometric validity. Objective 2: Data from the Asian Regional Module (ARM) in particular was analyzed to achieve this objective, including from the Hong Kong Module (a special module designed for Hong Kong students focusing on national identity.) The analysis of ARM data (that included all student responses ffrom the five participating Asian societies) enabled the development of what the project called “traditional citizenship values” for Asian students. A theoretical analysis of these constructs resulted in a somewhat different interpretation of their meaning that that proposed in the ICCS study. Objective 3: Statistical models were developed to show the relationship between key variables from the Main Student Survey and the Asian Regional Module. For some studies this involved comparisons between students in Asian societies using the Main Survey data, others comparisons were made using ARM data only and for others comparisons were made using both Main Survey and ARM data. Objective 4: A cross-regional study was undertaken comparing the civic knowledge, civic values and future intentions for civic engagement of students from Asia, Europe and Latin America. Latent Profile Analysis was used to identify similar groups within each region and models using Personal Investment Theory were developed to assess students’ intentions regarding future civic engagement. A common model across regions could not be identified.

842211.label: Major findings and research outcome
842211.value: This project was developed from the theoretical assumption that there are distinctive conceptions of citizenship in Asia. Such a view challenges universalistic conceptions of citizenship values. The purpose of the project was to investigate whether empirical evidence, based on the views of adolescent Asian students, supported the theoretical literature. The key results of multiple studies indicated that: 1. Traditional values in Asian societies are based on various wisdom traditions. The samples of young people surveyed endorsed such values. Yet levels of endorsement differed across the region. Students from Indonesia and Thailand tended to endorse traditional values more strongly that students from Korea, Hong Kong and Taiwan thus creating what appeared to be a geographic split. Yet within the East Asian countries, levels of endorsement also differed with Korean students endorsing such values less emphatically than their Chinese peers. 2. Using person-centred analytic techniques (for example cluster analysis and Latent Profile Analysis) the regional differences identified above were further problematized. These techniques identified similar groups or clusters of students within each society and these groups displayed a considerable diversity in terms of civic knowledge, civic values and potential for civic engagement. This indicated that difference rather than similarity characterized attitudes to citizenship and these differences were as significant within countries as they were across countries and across the region. 3. A characteristic of these person-centred studies was the inclusion of forms of civic engagement such as illegal protest. Such forms are often neglected and the focus is on conventional forms of engagement such as voting or writing a letter to the newspaper. Yet our person-centred studies identified two key outcomes: European, Asian and Latin American males are more likely to be attracted to illegal forms of protest than females and these males are characterized by low levels of civic knowledge, negative attitudes to democratic values and negative aspects of traditional values. Other studies have found this group to be ‘disengaged’; while the current study has found them to be attracted to negative forms of engagement. This is a major finding. 4. A number of studies was conducted to explore the role of schools in supporting students’ civic development. A key finding has been that school leadership plays an important role in developing an environment in which civic knowledge and civic values can develop. We have called this ‘leading for civic learning’ thus charting a new direction in school leadership research.

842211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
842211.value: One distinctive feature of this research was the use of interviews with same age/different cohort students. While this was innovative methodologically, it also suggests that in the future qualitative interviews should be included alongside the survey. This is not practical for international large scale assessments such as ICCS but it could be done with local surveys. The benefits of multiple data sources would make it well worthwhile. Research to data has been cross sectional in nature and even the addition of interviews as suggested above, while enhancing understanding, doesn’t remove the limitations of such research. Future research needs to consider longitudinal studies with the same cohort. This is particularly important because so much emphasis is placed on future civic engagement. Longitudinal research would enable actual civic engagement to be studied alongside adolescent intentions to provide a valid measure of ‘preferred’ and ‘actual’ engagement. To move in this direction the team that has worked on the current research has proposed a qualitative study to explore the development of civic consciousness in Hong Kong adolescents and young adults. ICCS measures will be used as a baseline and interviews will seek to uncover trajectories of civic development from early adolescents.

842211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
842211.value: While students in Asia may occupy a common geographic space, there are many differences when it comes to their attitudes to civic values and civic action. Students in countries like Indonesia and Thailand, for example, tend to be more active yet also more traditional but with lower levels of civic knowledge than their peers from East Asia. Yet it cannot be assumed that within countries all students have the same civic attitudes and dispositions. There are as many differences within countries as there are across the region. It is diversity rather than similarity that characterizes Asian students’ attitudes to citizenship and civic values. There are common values across the region that influence students’ attitudes, but they do so in different ways depending upon the student’s context and experience. Families remain important influences on students’ civic development as are schools, particularly where efforts are made to create an open and inclusive environment. Particular efforts need to be made to support the civic development of disaffected students, immigrant students and socioeconomically disadvantaged students. These students are at risk of social exclusion unless they are helped to feel part of a civic community to which they can contribute and that values their participation.

842411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
842411.value: Research findings show that both Web 2.0 tools and Assessment for Learning (AfL) have great potential in enhancing teaching and learning. If teachers are to raise the standards of their students, they should make AfL an essential component of classroom work (Assessment Reform Group, 1999, 2002; Berry, 2008, Black et al, 2003, 2004; Black & William, 1988; Marshall & Drummond, 2006). Our preliminary research (Lai & Ng, 2010, in press) on pre-service teachers confirms that Web 2.0 tools such as wikis can facilitate different forms of feedback, self- and peer assessment, and multidimensional assessment methods advocated in AfL. These online tools allow students to work together outside school hours to explore common interests and give feedback to each other about their experiences. The study aims to integrate AfL strategies in wiki-based learning activities for primary and secondary school pupils. The study will help us identify effective pedagogy and assessment strategies in these kinds of online learning activities. By the end of the study, we will develop basic guiding principles for using AfL in wiki-based activities and adapt some learning models that can be applied to other online collaborating tools (e.g., Office Live Workspace and Google Docs ) and social networking websites (e.g., Facebook, Twitter, Google Buzz, etc.) The study should be able to provide examples of good practices of e-learning implementation in school environments. Bringing AfL beyond the walls of the classroom by connecting it with Web 2.0 tools is an important step. 研究結果表明，Web 2.0工具和促進學習的評估（AFL）對提升教學效能甚有幫助。如果教師要提高學生的水平，就應該讓促進學習的評估成為課堂教學的重要部分（Assessment Reform Group, 1999, 2002; Berry, 2008, Black et al, 2003, 2004; Black & William, 1988; Marshall & Drummond, 2006）。我們曾對職前教師進行初步的研究（Lai & Ng, 2010，2011），發現Web 2.0工具（如維基平台）能增強多種促進學習的評估策略，例如反饋、自評、互評，及多面向評估等。而這些在線工具讓學生課餘也能一起學習，探索共同興趣，實現互相交流，並分享彼此的經驗。 本研究旨在從各種網上學習活動中識別有效的教學法和評估策略。研究完成後，我們將發展出一套以維基平台為基礎整合促進學習的評估的指導原則，以及調適至可應用在其他在線協作工具與社交網站的學習模式。本研究還能提供一些在學校應用電子學習的優質方案，供教師參考。以Web 2.0工具作為連結的橋樑，讓促進學習的評估超越教室，是推進教育發展的重要一步。
