842811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
842811.value: Cantonese opera is facing a crisis of transmission. Traditionally, Cantonese opera employs oral tradition in transmitting their artistry to the new generation. Learning occurs in a master-apprentice relationship, wherein apprentices serve as followers of the master to develop personal artistry through informal tuition. Apart from artistry, the apprentice will learn about the socio-cultural context of the genre through long-term immersion during the apprenticeship. In recent decades, training artists for the profession has been influenced by the Western conservatory tradition. Different aspects of the genre are taught by different specialists during a limited length of time. Learning is limited to knowledge and skills instead of socio-cultural practices and creativity in artistry, which take time and a specific context to learn. Teaching Cantonese opera in Hong Kong schools has been encouraged to promote the Chinese culture. However, major problems include the lack of systematic pedagogy. Thus, this study addresses the issue of transmission of Cantonese opera in professional training as well as in school education. This 20-month study will adopt a mixed-method approach in three phases. In Phase One, semi-structured interviews will be conducted with five artists with backgrounds in oral tradition and five artists trained in conservatories. Researchers will also undertake research visits to institutions of Cantonese opera in Hong Kong and Guangdong Province to interview teachers and students after class observations and seek their views on the characteristics of their training programs. The findings will help in formulating pedagogy models of oral and conservatory traditions to provide a theoretical framework for the next phase. Phase Two will be a multi-case study that investigates the teaching effectiveness of tutors with both pedagogy models in two primary and two secondary schools with Cantonese opera programs. The researchers will observe the classes, collect program documents, and interview school teachers, Cantonese opera tutors, and students about the pedagogy and learning process. Video recording of the teaching and learning process will be undertaken for repeated observation, analysis, and triangulation with the interviews. A questionnaire on how students perceive the pedagogy will also be administered to all participating students. Based on the findings from previous phases, a new pedagogy model for the teaching and learning of Cantonese opera in nurturing artists from school to professional levels will be developed in Phase Three. The model will shed light on developing a new pedagogy system for nurturing professional artists of Cantonese opera with personal styles and artistic creativity. 粵劇現正面對傳承方面的危機。傳統上，粵劇界以口傳心授的方式把藝術傳授予新一代。學員在一個師徒關係中學習，他們透過非正式學習模式，以學徒的身份侍候師傅，得以學習個人的藝術。此外，學徒亦透過長期的沉浸學到粵劇的社會文化背景。 近數十年，粵劇在訓練專業演員方面受到西方學院傳統之影響，其中，粵劇的各個層面由不同的專家作有限時間的教習，因此學習只限於知識與技能，而粵劇的社會文化實踐和藝術創意等需要較長時間和特定環境才能培養和發展的層面往往被忽略。 香港學校教育現正鼓勵教習粵劇以推動中國文化傳統；然而，主要問題是學校缺乏有系統的教學法。因此，本研究計劃針對粵劇傳承的問題，並擬為專業訓練和學校教育兩方面著手。 這個歷時二十月的計劃將採用一個分三階段的混合研究方法。第一階段將運用半結構性訪談方式訪問五位以口授傳統方式學習的藝人和五位以學院傳統方式學習的藝人；另外，我們亦將訪問本港和廣東的粵劇學校，透過課堂觀察和訪問教師和學生以探究他們對課程特色的觀點。研究結果將有助建構口授傳統和學院傳統的教學法模式以提供一個理念架構作下一階段之研究。 第二階段是一個多個案研究，調查兩間中學和兩間小學的粵劇導師以兩種不同傳統教授學生的有效性。我們將觀察課堂，蒐集課程文件，和訪問教師、粵劇導師和學生有關教學法和學習過程。另外，我們將攝錄教學過程以便我們可重複觀察和分析，並以訪談作為三角測定；再以問卷調查學生對教學發有何觀感。 第三階段將建基於以上的研究結果，並發展出一個粵劇教學模式以培養學生以至專業學員。該教學模式將為培養具個人藝術風格和創意的教學系統提供參考。

842811.label: Realisation of objectives
842811.value: 1. The Chinese oral tradition was documented by interviewing five master artists with apprenticeship background. Their experiences, beliefs, learning processes and pedagogical practices were investigated and documented in a journal article which has been accepted. For the Western conservatory tradition, we have visited the Guangdong Cantonese Opera School, and also the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts for data collection. The former allowed us to observe class teaching and interview staff and students. However, the latter did not respond to our request of visit officially. We could only interview the Acting Dean of the School of Chinese Theatre, Professor Chan Sau Yan with an informal observation of one singing class. In general, objective 1 has been well achieved. 2. Characteristics of both oral and conservatory traditions have been investigated and identified. The Legitimate Peripheral Participation (Lave & Wenger, 1991) as a model of oral tradition was applied as a theoretical framework for the study. Findings not only echo but also supplement the framework. The conservatory tradition was examined by the concepts of formal learning, informal learning and non-formal learning. 3. One primary and one secondary school were invited for a cross-case study to investigate the current situation and pedagogy employed by Cantonese opera artists, who intended to teach the school children with their personal experiences learnt from conservatory tradition. Teaching effectiveness is found when the curriculum is highly compartmentalized. In addition, it is found that many school students participated in some children troupes in the community; we thus further invited two children troupes for another case study to investigate the pedagogy issues. 4. After compiling all the findings from the different sources, a Model of Transmission of Cantonese opera has been built with different key concepts and elements that are regarded to be important. This study generates this model as the ultimate output so as to shed light on how the new generation of artists can be nurtured from the school level to the professional level, with reference to the traditional practice found in the oral tradition and community settings.

842811.label: Major findings and research outcome
842811.value: The interview study of the master artists on the Chinese oral tradition found that the parent-like relationship between the master and the apprentice was critical in successful transmission of personal artistry; the master transmit his artistry mainly for prolongation of personal style. Informal learning was the major learning mode where the apprentice relied on observation, imitation, trial-and-error on stage, and proactive inquiry with his own and other masters (Leung, in press). The case study of two institutes nurturing Cantonese opera artists reveals the application of Western conservatory tradition in Cantonese opera, which is characterized by highly specialization of teaching with specific experts in different areas; learners are required to learn industriously with a regular and focused curriculum in a lengthy immersion of learning and self-practice. Formal and standardized learning was found that each aspect was divided into different developmental learning stages. Graduation from the institute implies that graduates can face the challenges of professional requirements. The case study of two local schools which offer Cantonese opera in the co-curricular activity and formal curriculum reveals that the tutors employ a compartmentalized curriculum with their own learning experiences as the basis of pedagogy, and voluntary students are more motivated in learning when they find it interesting and discretional to learn. Only a few students would like to pursue professional practice in their future. The secondary students tend not to pursue professional practice than the primary students. The research team further explored the pedagogy issues in two children troupes in the community setting where students learn the genre as an extra-curricular activity. Findings reveal that, similarly, tutors tend to employ their learning experiences in their teaching in a highly compartmentalized curriculum. Non-formal learning was the main characteristic that no predetermined learning targets were set, and students learn by doing and practices. Compiling the findings, a Model of Transmission of Cantonese Opera has been proposed with strengths and advantages from the different modes. Facing the modernization and globalization, the oral tradition has faded out from the practice while the conservatory tradition is and will be the main stream for nurturing professional artists. Four main elements are identified as crucial in the model: curriculum, teachers, students, and internship. The institute must collaborate with the professional field of Cantonese opera for early immersion of learners, while a graduate school should be included for research on theory and practice, as well as nurturing teachers for sustainability.

842811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
842811.value: Creativity of Cantonese opera has been identified by this study when one of the master artists mentioned that personal style can be developed in three developmental stages: inheritance, development, and innovation. Transmission with oral tradition may generate artistic creativity when informal and non-formal learning were applied so that more space for personal development was allowed. Since the oral tradition has been faded out, it might be difficult for the new generation to develop their personal style within the limitation of the conservatory curriculum where benchmarking is emphasized. The issue of how personal style can be nurtured in the conservatory tradition should be further studied. Since the findings are considered to be useful for the field of Cantonese opera, the PI plans to organize a public seminar to disseminate the findings. Stakeholders including the Chinese Artists Association of Hong Kong, Cantonese Opera Development Fund, local academics, and the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts will be invited to discuss the findings. We hope that the project can inform the field of Cantonese opera in contributing to successful transmission in the conservatory mode. Details of how students are taught for quality learning within and outside the classroom could be further studied.

842811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
842811.value: This study investigates the nature and characteristics of two main transmission modes of Cantonese opera, namely, oral and conservatory traditions. In addition, transmission in formal curriculum and co-curriculum in primary and secondary schools, as well as children troupes in the community are also studied. A model of transmission of Cantonese opera has been proposed for reference of different stakeholders, including Cantonese opera institutes, professional and practicing artists from the field, the schools which offer Cantonese opera in their formal curriculum and co-curriculum, and the children troupes in the community. Nurturing creative artists effectively relies on the collaboration among the stakeholders aforementioned. For instance, practicing artists should be responsible for collaborating with the institutes in providing internship for professional students, while teaching artists should consider refining the pedagogy in teaching primary and secondary students. Informal learning, non-formal learning should be introduced to the curriculum of the institute so that students may immerse into the practices in a lengthy period of time. Hong Kong Government may refer to the model when formulating and implementing their policy concerning transmission of Cantonese opera which has been identified as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Hong Kong.

843411.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
843411.value: Teacher leadership has gained momentum in the past two decades. Today teachers are required to assume more leadership roles and carry out a wider variety of instructional leadership functions than ever before, globally and in Hong Kong. There has been a discernable global policy shift towards the support of new leadership arrangements in schools. Concurrently, an empirical literature has begun to describe characteristics of teacher leaders, dimensions of teacher leadership, natural patterns and planned organizational arrangements of teacher leadership, conditions that promote and challenge teacher leadership, and the effects of teacher leadership. A review of this literature, however, reveals that most studies of teacher leadership have been conducted in Western contexts and almost exclusively in primary and secondary schools. This overlooks the fact that a similar trend aimed at strengthening teacher leadership is evidenced in early childhood education (ECE) settings. For example, in Hong Kong, recent school improvement initiatives (e.g., vouchers, school quality review) encourage ECE to develop teacher leadership as a tool for school improvement. Yet, the literature on teacher leadership currently offers little directly relevant information on the development of teacher leadership in ECE. This represents the focus and potential contributions of this proposed research: the practice and effects of teacher leadership in early childhood education. The objectives of the research are to: 1. Describe patterns of teacher leadership used in early childhood programs. 2. Examine the impact of different patterns of teacher leadership on teachers’ instructional, professional, and organizational development. 3. Investigate how the particular context of early childhood education settings shapes the exercise of teacher leadership. The research will examine the practices of teacher leadership in early childhood programs in Hong Kong using quantitative and qualitative methodologies. The participants engaged in the study will work collaboratively with the researcher over a period of 24 months to generate and collect data linking teacher leadership with ECE context. The contributions of this research lie in the fine-grained description of teacher leadership practices as they emerge in ECE settings. The research will contextualize these descriptions in terms of ECE as a “context for school leadership”. The location of the research in Hong Kong creates further value in terms of the findings, not only for local policy and practice, but also as a “case” of teacher empowerment and leadership in Asia where educational systems have traditionally operated in a hierarchical manner. 摘要 促進學習領導--了解幼教界教師領導發展 過去二十年，教師領導的討論成為趨勢。相比以往，不論在全球或在香港，現今的教師須承擔更多領導角色和履行廣泛的教學領導功能。故此，全球政策出現支持新的領導安排的傾向。 現時，文獻開始描述教師領袖的特徵、教師領導的層面、領導模式、有計劃的教師領導組織安排、促進和挑戰教師領導的條件、及教師領導的影響。然而，文獻探討發現大部分教師領導的研究源於西方背景及幾乎只在小學和中學進行。 這忽略了一個事實──旨在加強教師領導的類似趨勢也體現於幼兒教育的業界。舉例說，在香港，近期的學校改善計劃（例如學劵、學校質素評核）鼓勵幼兒教育發展教師領導，作為改善學校的工具。但現時教師領導的文獻提供很少直接有關在幼教界發展教師領導的資訊。這正是今次提出的研究（幼兒教育教師領導的實踐和影響）的焦點和潛在貢獻所在。 這項研究的目標是： 1. 說明幼兒教育的教師領導模式。 2. 檢視不同模式的教師領導對教師的教學、專業和學校發展的影響。 3. 研究個別學校的背景如何形成教師領導的行使。 本研究將透過量化和質化方法探討教師領導在香港幼兒教育的實踐。參與計劃者會與研究員在24個月內緊密合作，以產生和收集連繫教師領導與幼兒教育背景的數據。 本研究的貢獻在於仔細地描述教師在幼兒教育業界中出現的領導行為，以探索幼兒教育教師領導的背景。本研究在香港進行，有關發現不只能反映本地教師領導的政策和實踐。並可能有更大的價值作為亞洲傳統以階層方式運作的教育系統中，賦權予教師和教師領導的個案。

843411.label: Realisation of objectives
843411.value: Objective 1: The study surveyed over 300 kindergartens in Hong Kong. The survey was administered in 2012. Data was analyzed and revealed that there is a general recognition of the importance of teacher leadership (Li, 2012), which has been advocated as effective ways of bringing about substantial changes in practices, in kindergartens of Hong Kong. The present study has been designed to examine how teacher leaders conceive their role within current school leadership models.Factor analysis, however, was unable to replicate the clear patterns found in Western countries which broadly differentiated between transactional and transformational approaches of leadership. Instead a mix of styles was more often reported (Li, 2014). The 4 clusters of leadership approaches (Li, 2014) might reflect 'culturally appropriate practice' on the one hand and that teacher leadership has not been institutionalized in kindergartens on the other hand. Objective 2: Case-study visits (direct observation of classrooms, teacher lunchrooms, teacher meetings, and principal-teacher meetings throughout the day; interviews with principals, key staff, and teachers.) were designed to identify the impact of different approaches of teacher leadership on teachers' instructional, professional and organizational development. In all cases, teacher leaders tended to view the role of a leader as the one to make decisions and move things forward as well as the one to ‘mind manage’ for the purpose of creating a secure environment. In interviews, teacher leaders talked about their expression of views on teaching arrangement including outdoor class activities at meetings, their share of students' learning at breaks and their commitment to carry out their work. Signs of informal leadership and core team management have been identified (Li, 2012). Objective 3: Further detailed analyses of context have been made to demonstrate how contexts have been at work in shaping the development of teacher leadership in early childhood settings.The absence of clear hierarchies among teachers and the principal’s role has been to make all the important decisions resulted that teachers do not assume leadership roles or sought involvement in decision making (Li, 2012). Kindergarten teachers saw themselves as a group who ‘were all the same in the teaching rank’ Typically, teachers were not in the habit of meeting or interacting formerly to share their experiences, opinions, and challenges (Li, 2014). The aim has been to uncover the development of the culture of teacher leadership for the Hong Kong context that can serve as baseline data of the current operation and adaptation of kindergarten teachers who practiced during the time Hong Kong has launched a variety of education reforms that focus on development of teacher leadership.

843411.label: Major findings and research outcome
843411.value: There are three broad outcomes that can be highlighted: 1. We have shown that several leadership approaches that have been advocated as effective ways of bringing about substantial changes in practices were introduced to kindergarten teachers in Hong Kong.Factor analysis, however, was unable to replicate the clear patterns found in Western countries which broadly differentiated between transactional and transformational styles of leadership. Instead a mix of styles or 'laissez-faire' style was more often reported (Li, 2014). This calls for further investigation of the importance of teacher leadership knowledge in general. The issue for teacher leadership is how best to develop informed teacher leaders but these findings suggest that at least in some cases being 'informed' is not the key link to empowerment. 2.The present study reported that how teacher leaders conceive and carry out their role within current school leadership models. In terms of expected empowerment, teachers as curriculum coordinator or year group leader are less likely to engage in professional development activities and even less likely to engage in organizational development activities. In general, teachers tend to assume instructional development as leadership development. 3.We have found an interesting pattern whereby what most supports the development of teacher leadership does not always support the capacity for empowerment/leadership distribution/participation in school professional and organizational activities. In terms of empowerment, for example, role taking requires formal positions in hierarchical inclined organizations but wok commitment and division of labour does not (Li, 2014).

843411.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
843411.value: Using the statistically based clustering procedures on survey data, ‘4 clusters’ of leadership approaches were identified. In general, a mixture of leadership approaches operates in Hong Kong kindergartens and they did not match with western practices reflected in literature. This could simply be a methodology issue - cluster analysis from a different data set. Advances such as Rasch model that adopt a person oriented rather than a construct oriented approach to data analysis have the potential to yield quite different results. Thus innovation with new analytic approaches has the potential for further development of the research.Yet it could also reflect different conceptions of leadership held by Hong Kong kindergarten teachers. There is literature to suggest that Asian teachers brought up in distinctive social contexts may well have distinctive attitudes and adaptation to leadership. This needs to be an area of future investigation.

843411.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
843411.value: There has been a general recognition of the importance of teacher leadership while Hong Kong has launched a variety of education reforms that focus on quality of learning and teaching. The present study reported how teacher leaders conceive their role within current school leadership models. In general, a mixture of leadership approaches operates in Hong Kong kindergartens. The results also suggest that the leadership approach of participants did not match with the western practices reflected in literature, albeit of primary and secondary schools, rather than kindergartens, though there were increased incentives in and support for teacher leadership in kindergartens. Teacher leadership in relation to leading the community (organisational learning) when considering school-wide issues or as sharing and realizing a clear vision for the school was almost non-existent. Teacher leaders tend to adopt a mix and match approach suggesting it is difficult to identify just what a leader might do in any given circumstance so that leadership roles are highly situational. The prevalence of these potential problems in the findings suggest that teacher leadership is not yet institutionalized in the majority of these survey schools and the full potential of teacher leadership as a tool for school change has not been harnessed.

843411.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
843411.value: Policymakers can have access to the key findings of this project: There is a general recognition of the development of teacher leadership among kindergarten teachers but teachers are not keen in taking up leadership roles in schools. There are contextual factors influencing the current teacher leadership operating in Hong Kong kindergartens. Efforts have to be made to identify and promote specific approaches to teacher leadership designed to bring about desired improvements at the early childhood stage. The setting up of formal leadership roles such as Vice-principal, curriculum coordinators has been seriously considered and mentioned in the 15- year Free Education Report (June 2015). The data is publicly available and can be accessed by researchers, policymakers and public.The data can be referred to as the beginning of a wider local initiative to monitor and better understand kindergarten teachers' developing leadership culture.

843911.label: Realisation of objectives
843911.value: All schools in Hong Kong were faxed an invitation to complete a survey on teacher commitment. Schools were invited to complete either a hard copy or an on-line form of the questionnaire. 41 schools (21 Primary and 20 Secondary) responded positively to the invitation with 30 requesting a hard copy, and 11 electing to complete the form on-line. Collection of data took approximately 10 months. In the proposal we suggested that the lower boundaries needed for single level analyses would be in the order of 300-400 participants. Our success at recruiting participants was very healthy consisting of 1109 teachers from primary (46.4%) and secondary (53.6%) schools in Hong Kong. 966 of the participants did the study in paper format and 143 participants completed the study online. Further details on the participants are in the various technical reports. Each of the six proposed objectives has been achieved. 1. To critically evaluate the Meyer & Allen (1997) Three-Component Model of Organizational and Occupational Commitment when applied to the Hong Kong teaching profession; (Technical Reports 1, 2, and 3, 6, Educational Psychology, Journal of Management, Asian Pacific Journal of Management, Teaching and Teacher Education, American Psychological Association Conference); 2. To validate an Educator Motivation and Attribute Profile Scale (EdMAPS) (Technical Report 1); 3. To use the EdMAPS to investigate motivational and attribute characteristics of teachers and administrators at the primary and secondary levels and their relations with affective, continuance and normative commitment to the organization (school) and occupation (teaching) (Technical Report 1); 4. To evaluate the extent to which commitments, motivational and attribute characteristics vary as a function of school type, career level, career duration, and academic discipline (Technical Report 2, Journal of Management, Asian Pacific Journal of Management, Teaching and Teacher Education); 5. To evaluate the manner in which commitment, motivation and attribute characteristics relate to outcome measures: job satisfaction, psychological health and well-being, intention to remain in the profession (Technical Reports 1, 2 and 3, Journal of Management, Asian Pacific Journal of Management, Educational Psychology); 6. To complete multilevel analyses to determine the extent that commitment and EdMAP ‘climate’ varies for different ‘groups’ and environments (schools, departments), and the extent to which these vary for groups within the same level (Technical Reports 1 and 2).

843911.label: Major findings and research outcome
843911.value: • The EdMap has construct validity and good reliability (1)* (Technical Report 1). • Class teachers have the lowest levels of aspirations for administrative duties (1)* (Technical Report 1). • Both the first-order and second-order factors of the EdMAP scale predict teachers’ psychological well-being (and its five subtypes), intention to quit, job satisfaction, and job self-concept. The covariates family income, and to a lesser extent, teachers’ education levels, also play an important role in predicting teachers’ adjustment (1)* (Technical Report 1). • Hong Kong teachers on average do not have a strong intention to quit the teaching profession nor the school (1)* (Technical Report 1). • Male teachers with more children have lower levels of aspirations for administrative duties, whereas female teachers’ aspirations for administrative duties increase with their number of children. Male teachers on average have higher aspirations for administrative duties than female teachers, regardless of the number of children they have (1)* (Technical Report 1). • Both genders appear to be proportionately represented in administrative positions (1)* (Technical Report 1). • The Three-Component Model of Organizational and Occupational Commitment (affective, normative and continuance) has good construct validity and reliability (2,3,4,6)* . • Results indicate the importance of nurturing dual commitments to the organization and occupation among employees. The optimal combination appears to involve high levels of moral commitment to both the occupation and the organization (1,3,4,6)* . • Commitment to occupation alone is insufficient to trigger the psychological well-being of Hong Kong teachers. Teachers must also feel committed to the organization. (1,3,4,6)* . • School administrators should provide teachers with a working environment that facilitates the development and maintenance of emotional attachment loyalty and obligation to remain to both their schools and the teaching profession in general (1,3,4,6)* • Affective commitment to occupation and organization is an important negative predictor of turnover intentions (1,3,4,6)* . • Normative commitment is a strong negative predictor of intentions to leave current school and the profession. 843911.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
843911.value: • An understanding of Hong Kong teachers’ commitment should help inform school administrators on the ways in which multi-dimensions of commitment relate to psychological well-being, and by using this information consider how they might further sustain and/or improve positive teacher commitment (1,3,4,6)* . • School administrators should provide teachers with a working environment that facilitates the development and maintenance of emotional attachment loyalty and obligation to remain to both their schools and the teaching profession in general (1,3,4,6)*. To enhance the psychological well-being of Hong Kong teachers, it is essential to nurture a healthy organizational climate in schools (1,3,4,6)* . Teachers must also feel committed to the organization because this strongly influences psychological well-being in the workplace. To enhance the psychological well-being of Hong Kong teachers, it is essential to nurture a healthy organizational climate in schools. • School administrators who wish to keep good teachers need to create an environment tailored to improve teachers’ love for teaching and love for school (affective commitment organization and occupation) (1,3,4,6)* . Each of these matters should be further investigated in research projects, and development programs produced to enhance the commitment of teachers to both their profession and schools.

843911.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
843911.value: This project was designed to examine a). The nature of teacher commitments, b). The relations among affective, continuance, and normative commitment to the school (organization) and teaching profession, and c). The relations between the three forms of commitment and motivational and aptitude characteristics of teachers within the teaching profession of Hong Kong. These variables were also related to teachers’ intentions to continue in the teaching profession and psychological well-being. Examination of these relationships is especially important for the Hong Kong school system as it strives to provide the strongest teaching force. Preliminary findings indicate that school and institutional environments powerfully shape teachers’ commitment. Key predictors of intention to continue in the teaching profession as well as psychological well-being are affective and normative commitment to both the profession of teaching and the particular institution.

844011.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
844011.value: 在西方國家進行的無數研究已經證明自我主導學習的重要性，並指出教師與同儕回饋對小學生的成績有極大影響。但這些結果有多大程度能轉移並應用於香港的小學生身上，則仍有待查證。香港學校競爭氣氛激烈，課堂亦傾向以教師為中心，在這種文化背景下，儘管政府強調要學生學懂如何學習，但培養小學生的自我主導學習能力仍甚具挑戰性。雖然新興的本地研究結果令人鼓舞，但過份依賴一次性的橫切面研究，若欠缺適當的研究控制，難以科學確定研究干預的影響。本研究使用26個月的“縱向追蹤”法，結合定量和定性的研究策略，以期找出：（1）回饋、自我主導學習及學習成效的性質和質量；（2）各變量之間的因果關係。本研究重點針對小學生，因為小學階段乃發展元認知、學習習慣和自我效能感的關鍵時期。是次研究將評估 2,560位來自32間學校的P3和P4學生，並追蹤他們的發展，研究為期兩年。干預措施包括修訂的滲透方法（Infusion method; Swartz & Parks, 1994），在自然教室內進行準實驗設置，以確保研究的生態效度。研究將比較實驗組和對照組在發展元認知、自我主導學習能力、學習動機、學習自我效能和數學成績的差異，並作出各變量因果關係的推論。本研究嚴密遵照香港教育學院的道德守則進行。研究數據包括前測和後測問卷、學習日誌、教師反思日誌、焦點訪談，和數學評估。定量數據將使用多層結構方程模型(Multilevel SEM) 分析，而定性數據則使用內容分析。是次研究的預期成果包括：（1）深入理解在本地小學教室使用回饋和自我學習的成效;（2）找出有證據作的有效自我主導學習法。

844011.label: Realisation of objectives
844011.value: Summary: All objectives of this project have been met. The outputs from the project include four published journal articles, nine conference presentations, one journal article under review, two journal articles in preparation, one PhD thesis submitted and one ongoing EDD thesis (expected completion 2016). Financial support from GRF acknowledged. Details: Effective approaches for the implementation of self-directed learning in schools were identified and tentative model developed based on literature review (Objective 1). A conceptual framework on feedback, self-directed learning, and school achievement was established (Objective 2). Based on the conceptual framework, an intervention study, as specified in the proposal, was carried out with 4,570 students from 26 participating HK primary schools. Five waves of data were collected from the students. Teacher feedback practice and students’ self-directed learning in local classrooms were evaluated (Objective 3). The data collected were analysed for effect of teacher feedback and self-directed learning on students’ mathematics achievement (Objective 4). The findings were published in two refereed journals articles (Mok & Zhu, 2014; Mok, Wong, Su, Tognolini, & Stanley, 2014), and five conference papers (Wong, Mok, Yao, Paris, Stanley, Tognolini, August 2012; Zhu, Mok, Yao, & Wong, July 2013; Mok, Wong, Su, Paris, Tognolini, & Stanley, August 2013; Zhu & Mok, January 2014; Zhu & Mok, February 2015). The study developed and validated a mathematics achievement vertical scale to chart mathematics growth of primary students. Further, attitude scales on self-directed learning and feedback were also developed and validated. Results were reported in two refereed journal articles (Mok, Wong, Yao, Paris, Stanley, & Tognolini, 2012; Yao & Mok, 2013), and four conference papers (Yao & Mok, August 2012; Zhu & Mok, September 2012; Wong, Mok, Paris, Tognolini, & Stanley, August 2013; Mok, Wong & Xu, November 2014).

844011.label: Major findings and research outcome
844011.value: As reported in Section 5.3, this project generated four published journal articles, nine conference presentations, one journal article under review, two journal articles in preparation, one submitted PhD thesis and one ongoing EDD thesis (expected completion in 2016). Each partner schools were given a confidential school report after each wave of data collection. In addition, 44 teacher development workshops were conducted for project and other schools. The study collected data from 4,570 students in primary 3 to primary 5 from 26 schools in Hong Kong. The students were followed longitudinally for 24 months and five waves of data were collected, including students’ achievement in mathematics, personal best goals, attitudes toward academic feedback, use of feedback and self-regulation learning practices. Teachers’ attitudes toward feedback were also collected. A vertical scale in mathematics was developed and validated for charting longitudinal growth of students across year levels. The results were reported in a journal article (Yao & Mok, 2013) and a conference paper. Further, scales to measure students’ self-directed learning and attitudes toward feedback were developed and validated. The results were reported in a journal article (Mok, Wong, Yao, Paris, Stanley, & Tognolini, 2012). Longitudinal data were analysed to achieve the research objectives. Major findings from the study are as follows: 1. Effect of students’ personal best goals on achievement: After controlling for student gender and grade level, the study found that students’ personal best goal predicted their subsequent mathematics achievement. In contrast, self-regulation affected mathematics achievement only indirectly via students’ personal best goals. The implication is that merely changing learning strategies without changing students’ motivation and aspiration for education would not lead to an increase in achievement. This finding was reported in a journal article (Mok, Wong, Su, Tognolini, & Stanley, 2014). 2. Relationship between feedback and achievement: Cluster analysis of attitudes towards feedback and mathematics achievement found that while low achieving students had the lowest attitudes toward feedback, intermediate (instead of high) achieving students had the highest attitudes towards feedback. The study also found that feedback was necessary, but not sufficient, for positive effects on learning. The receivers’ self-efficacy and perceived usefulness of feedback were also important factors for feedback to be effective. The findings were reported in a journal article (Mok & Zhu, 2014). 3. Differences between the students’ and teachers’ perceptions of feedback: Analysis of students’ and teachers’ attitudes toward feedback found that whereas students and teachers had similar perceptions of what constituted good feedback, they had major differences on the frequency of feedback given/received, feedback effectiveness, function of feedback, the basis of feedback and expectations of feedback. Findings were reported in a conference paper (Wong, Mok, Yao, Paris, Stanley, & Tognolini, 2012, August). 4. Effect of feedback on self-regulated learning: Analysis of students’ perceived usefulness of feedback and self-regulated learning found that the effect of feedback on self-regulated learning was moderated by students’ year level. Whereas feedback had a positive effect on self-regulated learning for primary 3 students, ignoring students’ perception of the usefulness of feedback would mean feedback might have a negative effect on their self-regulated learning. The findings were reported at a conference (Zhu & Mok, 2014, January). 5. Students’ expectations and perceptions of the quality of teachers’ feedback practices: The study found that students valued feedback from their teachers more than from their peers. They preferred feedback that was directed toward their learning strategies and based on their potentialities in the form of dialogues rather than toward their performances or in written form. These findings were reported in a journal article (Mok, Wong, Yao, Paris, Stanley, & Tognolini, 2012).

844011.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
844011.value: One urgent follow up task is the publication of research findings in journal articles. Two articles are in preparation for this purpose. Further, the study has opened up many opportunities for future research, one of which is the collection of qualitative data through interview or diary writing in order to provide in-depth understanding of the reasons underpinning the students’ perceptions of feedback. One major finding in this study is the identification of personal best goals as a crucial factor affecting students’ self-regulated learning and mathematics achievement. Personal best goals are an under-researched area in Hong Kong, even though they have been reported (e.g. Martin, 2006; Martin, 2013; Liem, Marsh, Martin, McInerney, & Yeung, 2013) to be of critical importance to students’ learning and achievement in Australia, China and Singapore. Research into correlates of personal best goals for Hong Kong students should bring new insights to the area of learning motivation in local education contexts. This is one direction of the research team for the next phase of their research. In addition, this study found that students’ attitudes towards feedback had an effect on their feedback uptake. It is therefore interesting to examine contributing factors to feedback attitudes. Further, this study identified discrepancies between teachers’ and students’ attitudes toward feedback and found that students’ attitudes were moderated by their achievement level and grade level. It is important for researchers to follow-up on effective delivery strategies in order to cater to students with different achievement levels and grade levels. Research into the three important topics noted above, namely, personal best goals, feedback and self-regulated learning in mathematics, could be extended to other subjects at different year levels, cultural backgrounds and geographical locations for significant contributions to educational and psychological fields.

844011.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
844011.value: There is strong consensus among governments that building the capacity for self-directed learning is a key education pursuit. Although the positive effects of self-directed learning on academic outcomes have been established across Western countries, few studies have been conducted in Asia; and it is not clear to what extent these results are transferrable to Chinese learners. Further, whereas conceptually self-directed learning has been embraced at the policy level, implementation strategies that support teachers putting self-directed learning theories into practice are limited. This project is the first large-scale longitudinal study in Hong Kong conducted in naturalistic classrooms with the aim of informing educators about factors that impact the development of self-directed learning at the primary levels and how self-directed learning affects school outcomes. This study focused its attention on primary students because the primary years are crucial for the development of metacognition, learning habits and self-efficacy. Investigation into self-directed learning is particularly necessary in Confucian Asian areas, such as Hong Kong, because there are strong societal and familial expectations for children to succeed academically. Findings from this study could serve as major references for further research on the promotion of self-directed learning in Hong Kong.

844011.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
844011.value: In addition to achieving the objectives of the project, we also valued the teacher development and knowledge transfer. We held 31 workshops for 26 partner schools to share the relevant knowledge (questioning and feedback, self-directed learning) and technologies used in the project (WINSTEPS, SP Xpress). In total, 576 participants attended the workshops. While we made an effort in teacher development, we also provided opportunities for our partner schools to share their experiences. Sixteen presenters from six partner schools joined the Assessment Conference in 2013 to present the ways they implemented self-directed learning in their schools. Moreover, 13 workshops were also held for schools other than the partner schools in the project. There were 1,623 participants from 33 primary schools and 12 secondary schools. On the other hand, two secondary schools and a special education school started the collaboration projects with us. A common aim of these projects was to investigate the schools’ current situation, implementation and future development of self-directed learning.

844311.value: 本研究旨在反思在全球化時代高等教育的功能和公民教育的本質。 作為殖民文化的傳承，在過去幾十年間， 香港高等教育沿襲了西方高等教育模式，置身公民教育領域之外。 從西方學術傳統來看，公民教育主要在中小學實施，而在大學並無一席之地。 學者們普遍認為公民教育是一種由國家政府主導的政治社會化行為，直接影響年輕人的政治意識和觀念，在大學實施公民教育和有任何政治傾向的活動都是對於學術自由的威脅。 但是近年來，國際學術社會對大學生的公民意識和公民社會參與的關注日增。香港的大學也不例外。例如，香港大學為提升學生的學習經歷而提出的策略方針之一是開設“著重培育環球公民的課程”，旨在培育學生“成為盡責的公民，為廣大社群作出貢獻”，並且“裝備學生成為環球公民”。 香港教育學院亦將 “倡導公民及道德教育”作為 “主導價值”之一。 我們過往在香港和中國大陸的研究發現，政府對於大學的政治影響通常會引致大學學者的強烈不滿和反對。大學管理層亦因此而陷入進退兩難的矛盾。 那麼，面對目前香港的大學校園裡新興的公民教育文化，大學生和大學管理層是如何看待呢？ 這股興起在大學裡的公民教育在哪些方面折射出全球化和去殖民化的潮流對於香港高等教育的影響？ 與香港自1997年以來在政治、經濟、 高等教育領域的變遷有何關係？ 為了回答這些問題，我們將採用文獻分析，問卷調查和深入訪談等方法在收集資料。 研究發現亦將與歐洲和美國近年來相關研究進行比較，並反思在全球化時代高等教育與公民教育的關係。

844811.label: Project Title(Chinese)
844811.value: 《詩經》與金文文獻語言的對比分析研究

844811.label: Co - Investigator(s)
844811.value: Dr Poon, Hon Fong Dr Yuen, Kwok Wa

844811.label: Project Objectives
844811.value: 詞匯學研究：本計劃的語言分析及對比擬以詞匯學的研究為主體，將《詩》和金文的詞匯作全面整理，根據其地域和時代製作語匯庫，從而描寫上古方言的共時性及歷時性特徵。 語法學及音韻學研究：除詞匯研究外，本計劃會亦兼及語法學及音韻學的考察。語法研究方面，本計劃擬借助《詩》和金文部分虛詞的語法功能的對比分析，歸納上古漢語方言語法的特點，以及其歷時發展的軌跡。音韻研究則主要於前人韻讀的基礎上，集中比較及分析《詩》和金文用韻方式的異同。待兩者皆取得初步成果後，研究人員可再申請研究經費，於這兩方面作進一步的重點分析研究。 文字學研究：通過《詩》和金文詞匯的「二重証據」對比，結合古音通假及漢字構形等理論，採用互証的方法釋讀《詩》和金文所見的疑難字詞。 文獻學研究：運用研究所得的上古漢語的方言和時代性特徵，探討《詩》和金文中具分域及斷代問題的篇章，並通過《詩》和金文語言現象的對比，結合古書的記述，探討兩者間在文獻產生上的關係。 語文學研究：《詩》〈風〉口語色彩較濃，〈雅〉〈頌〉及金文的語言較為典雅，當屬先秦語言的書面語表達形式，本計劃擬透過兩者的比較，探討上古口語與書面語在語言的運用情況。

844811.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
844811.value: 《詩經》為我國第一部的詩歌總集，屬傳世古書；至於金文則指刻鑄在青銅器上的文字，屬出土的先秦文獻，其年代久遠，是未經後世篡改的原始材料，表面上，兩者為截然不同的兩種文體。但是，倘若細審兩者的性質，則又會發現當中存在有不謀而合和可參照之處：金文有不少習用語可見於《詩》，而《詩》乃是上古的樂歌；至於金文的載體青銅器，乃先秦皇室貴族用於祭祀追孝、朝聘賞賜、燕饗祝嘏的禮器，此等禮儀活動均多配樂。因此，《詩》和金文在產生時代、背景用途、應用對象、遣詞造句等諸方面皆是相類的。比年以來，學者雖然已開始意識將兩者作互証對比研究的重要性，但前人的探討仍主要局限於傳統小學和文獻學的考察，並運用隨文釋義注疏或選釋詞語專注的研究方法，解決當中的名物訓釋、字詞通讀或史事考証等問題，故其討論較為零散，全盤和系統的語言比較迄今未見。 本計劃旨在對《詩經》和金文作全面的語言對比分析，當中以詞匯的考察為主，並兼及語法及音韻現象的比較，並通過上古漢語共時和歷時性特徵的歸納，對文獻中具分域及斷代問題的作品作重新討論；而且，本計劃亦擬藉著《詩經》和金文「二重証據」的對照，探討當中疑難字詞的釋讀，說明《詩經》和金文的文獻產生及形成關係，以及上古文言及白話語體的運用及發展情況。因此，本計劃的研究結果不僅能為《詩》學和金文學提供珍貴的資料，其貢獻更會影響及中國文獻學與語文學的研究，而上古文獻語言的深入考察，亦能有助我們瞭解我國傳統文化的源流與發展，對中華文化的傳承與弘揚具有重要的意義。此外，本計劃主要利用現代語言學的考察，以解決傳統小學和文獻學問題作為最終的目標，故計劃的進行具有跨材料、跨領域、跨學科的特色。 Shijing, the first anthology of Chinese poetry, belongs to traditional document. Bronze inscriptions, referring to the characters cast or carved on ancient bronze objects, are regarded as unearthed and unrevised original documents with a long history. Although the two are seemingly in distinctly different literary forms, if a more in-depth investigation into their nature is conducted, we could well discover a certain extent of coincidence and resemblance between them. For example, a number of idioms in bronze inscriptions could also be found in Shijing, which is regarded as a book of odes of the ancient period. Similarly, bronze objects, the carriers of inscriptions, are usually used as ritual vessels in ritual occasions such as the rites of sacrifice, audience and grant, as well as feast and pray, which are usually harmonized with music. The two are therefore similar in many aspects, including their periodization, background and purpose of uses, targets of application, usage of words and sentences, etc. In the past several years, scholars have already recognized the importance of carrying out contrastive research between them, however, such studies are still somewhat restrained by traditional philological and documentary methods. Discussions are either in forms of traditional commentaries or explanations of selected words, and their ultimate aims are merely the illustration of word meanings and historical events. Discussions are thus scattered, comprehensive and systematic research is still absent so far. This project aims at conducting a comprehensive contrastive study on the language of Shijing and bronze inscriptions, in which focus mainly lays on the lexical phenomena, supplemented by grammatical and phonological analysis. With the conclusion of synchronic and diachronic features of the language, this project will also proceed to re-examine the works having controversies in their periodization and regionization. Moreover, by the utilization of “dual-evidence method”, this project will further discuss the meanings of some problematic characters, the relationship of formation between Shijing and bronze inscriptions, as well as the evolution of classical and vernacular Chinese in ancient period. Accordingly, the outputs of this project could not only provide valuable reference for the studies of Shijing and bronze inscriptions, but also have a great impact on studies of traditional philology and documentation. Furthermore, our thorough investigation into the language would also be conducive to a better understanding towards the origin and development of traditional Chinese culture, which hence contribute to its inheritance and dissemination. As our ultimate aim is solving traditional philological and documentary problems by modern linguistic approach, this project is thus distinctive for its cross-material, cross-domain and interdisciplinary features.

844811.label: Realisation of objectives
844811.value: 本計劃旨在對《詩》與金文作全面的語言對比分析。計劃的研究以詞匯為主，並且兼及語法與音韻現象的比較。而且，在詞匯、語法及音韻研究的基礎上，本計劃亦嘗就《詩》與金文的文字釋讀、文獻形成及語體異同等問題上進行分析。總括而言，研究人員能夠完成計劃書所擬定的全部五項目標，研究過程大致順利。茲就各項目標的達成情況詳述如下： 1. 在詞匯學方面，為便於對《詩經》與金文的語言作全面的對比，本計劃成功建構一個資料完備的電子語匯庫。本計劃的語匯庫共有17,968頁，除了《詩經》原文與金文內容的對照外，語匯庫亦列出各銘文所屬的年代及國別。透過電腦系統的篩選功能，本計劃亦已準確及全面地歸納出具有特殊時代及地域特點的語匯，並已就各語匯所反映的共時與歷時性特徵作出分析。 2. 在語法學方面，本計劃主要選取《詩經》及金文的使用頻率較高及討論空間較多的共見虛詞作出詳細探討，當中包括「于（於）」、「以」、「用」、「其」、「既」、「取」、「不」、「無」、「之」等。除了語法功能的探究外，本計劃亦嘗就各虛詞於《詩經》及金文使用情況的異同作出比較，參考歷代經學家的訓詁，然後對照銘文和詩篇的具體年代，分析及討論各虛詞的歷時發展演變。至於音韻學方面，本計劃的研究集中於韻式的考察。首先，本計劃在前人韻讀的基礎上，抽取殷周金文中188篇有韻彝銘作主要材料，分別就其韻部、換韻情況及用韻位置作出分析與統計，從而比較《詩經》的用韻情況。研究結果發現，《詩經》與金文的用韻情況存在異同參半的情況。 3. 在文字學方面，本計劃綜合了前人於《詩經》與金文「二重証據」的運用，就其互証成果作出回顧與綜述。建基於語匯庫所歸納的資料，本計劃將《詩經》與金文的共見語匯作出排比對照，並且透過兩者間的比較，解決部分字詞的釋讀問題。具體的研究成果包括兩方面：一是借助《詩經》的辭例考釋金文，為金文中部分字詞的釋讀提出新見解；二是以金文文例解決《詩經》文句的訓詁問題，並且就部分詩篇的詩義探討提供新材料。 4. 在文獻學方面，本計劃建基於詞匯學研究歸納所得的方言與時代性特徵，對部分具分域與斷代問題的銘文與詩篇作出深入討論。此外，除了殷周金文材料外，近年發表的楚簡資料（如上博簡、清華簡）亦能為《詩經》的文獻產生問題提供重要資料。因此，在金文研究的基礎上，本計劃亦嘗結合戰國楚簡及傳世古書等資料，就《詩經》所反映的祭祀與樂舞性質進行詳細論述，分析《詩經》與金文於文獻產生上的關係。 5. 在語文學方面，本計劃的討論焦點主要集中於書面語與口語的表達形式的問題上。在前人討論的基礎上，本計劃從語言學的角度（當中包括詞匯、套語、句子長短、韻腳等），比較《詩經》與金文於文體上的異同。本計劃的研究結果是：《詩經》〈風〉的文體與〈雅〉、〈頌〉存在頗大差異；至於在〈雅〉〈頌〉兩部分中，〈頌〉（尤其是〈周頌〉）與金文相當接近，其次為〈大雅〉和〈小雅〉。

844811.label: Major findings and research outcome
844811.value: 本計劃已出版的論文共七篇，另有兩篇已經通過評審，將於2015年出版，並正進一步整理計劃的研究成果，期望能以專著形式出版，書名暫擬為《〈雅〉〈頌〉與出土文獻新證》。本計劃的研究工作於研資局審批結果公佈後立刻展開，茲述本計劃全部的階段性研究成果如下： 第一，研究文獻的蒐集與整理：本階段集中蒐集前人相關的研究文獻，資料已整理為文獻回顧，收錄於《〈雅〉〈頌〉與出土文獻新證》第一章的引論部分。又隨著2010年底清華簡的出版，當中包括不少《詩》類的文獻，大部分更為前人所未見的古佚詩，此類文獻可資與金文及《詩》作對比參證，故在清華簡在金文與《詩》以外，本計劃亦嘗整理清華簡所見的新材料。 第二，詞匯學研究：本計劃製作《詩》與金文資料庫，合共500多頁。為求研究結果的全面，本計劃亦蒐集近年新見銘文資料，又因學界於部分銘文釋讀意見分歧，本計劃於研究展開前曾對銘文作詳細探討，相關成果見〈山西翼城大河口出土鳥形盉銘文考釋〉，該文結合《詩》等辭例，探討「自無」、「襄」、「亦」及「出棄」等辭。又本計劃已建構17,968頁的電子語匯庫，列出各彝銘所屬年代及國別，展示語匯的地域及時代特徵。 第三，語法學及音韻學研究：本計劃的語法分析集中於十數個虛詞的研究，當中認為「不」、「無」較具探討價值，故將成果撰寫〈歷代經學家對《詩經》所見語助詞「不」、「無」的訓釋〉出版，文章在回顧歷代經學家於「不」、「無」的訓詁後，結合金文例子再次確立「不」、「無」於《詩經》中的語助詞用法。音韻方面，本計劃通過有韻金文材料的考察，認為大概由於《詩經》屬韻文體，與金文於用韻現象上可比性不高，但其所反映的押韻情況卻遠較金文複雜。 第四，文字學研究：本計劃通過《詩》與金文類似結構語匯的對比，就詞義訓釋提出新見解，較主要成果已撰寫為論文出版發表。〈《詩》《書》古義與金文新證二則〉在研究人員早期研究工作的基礎上，借助本計劃的成果作進一步修正，主要藉金文辭例及前人論述的補充，證成「假以溢我」之「溢」當讀為「賜」。〈《周頌‧大武樂章》之「武德」與戰國戈銘「大武闢兵」〉透過〈周頌‧大武〉的考察，提出〈大武戈〉銘宜讀為「大武弭兵」。〈《周頌》所見重言詞與兩周金文互證〉就金文與《詩經》共見重言詞的訓釋及時地特徵提出新見解。又〈從商周金文談《雅》《頌》所見「將」之用例〉主要借助〈雅〉、〈頌〉與殷周金文間的互證，就上古漢語「將」的用法及其演變作詳細的剖析與探索。清華簡收錄不少古佚詩，本計劃採用了金文、《詩》及楚簡之參照，就三種材料中部分可對照的字詞的釋讀提出新見解，如〈讀清華簡《耆夜》所見古佚詩小識〉確定「紝任兄弟」、「虎士奮甲」、「憂心陶陶」等之釋讀，而〈《清華簡三‧周公之琴舞》“非天含德”與《詩‧周頌》所見誡勉之辭〉考釋「含德」、「非」、「造」等的內涵，又〈談清華簡〈芮良夫毖〉「毖」詩所見之諍諫〉探討「敬哉君子，天猶畏矣」、「間隔若否」、「毋憂聞宥」等語。至於〈歷代經學家對《詩經》所見語助詞「不」、「無」的訓釋〉在語助詞探討的基礎上，就「不遐」、「遐不」提出新見解。 第五，文獻學研究：本計劃認為，在《詩》〈風〉、〈雅〉、〈頌〉三部分，〈雅〉、〈頌〉與金文的關係較為密切，而〈風〉的可比性較少。〈《周頌‧大武樂章》之「武德」與戰國戈銘「大武闢兵」〉結合金文材料，綜述〈大武〉樂舞於西周至春秋期間從歌功頌德發展偃武修文及彰顯武功之嬗變。〈《清華簡三‧周公之琴舞》“非天含德”與《詩‧周頌》所見誡勉之辭〉借助金文、《詩經》與楚簡中誡勉之辭的對比參證，說明〈周頌〉內容雖以歌功頌德為主，但於武王崩後，部分詩篇亦反映成王初嗣帝位遭逢國亂之嘆息，有須秉持先祖遺訓之誡勉，而類似題材亦見於兩周金文。〈談清華簡《芮良夫毖》「毖」詩所見之諍諫〉)則通過〈芮良夫毖〉、金文與《詩經》的對比，說明「毖詩」一類的題材即《詩經》中所謂的「變雅」。

844811.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
844811.value: 本計劃的研究成果擬於將來以專書的形式出版，專書的核心內容現已基本完成，正進行整合及文句修飾的工作，並且期望能於本年內將書稿交予出版社，安排評審事宜。除此之外，由於本計劃的進行相當成功，故其研究方法亦可運用於將來的研究項目之中。待將來時機合適，本計劃研究人員擬從以下的方向繼續申請及開展研究計劃： 1. 《詩》與金文語法現象的比較：本計劃雖以《詩》與金文文獻語言的對比分析研究為題，但焦點集中於詞匯的對比上。本計劃的語法對比僅以十多個虛詞為主，故在虛詞的研究上仍有許多可作進一步探討的空間；而且，語序亦是語法研究的重要課題，但由於時間及資源所限，本計劃亦未嘗就此方面作出討論。又語法現象的歸納與比較能有助於文本時代的判定，將來的研究項目可以考慮以《詩》與金文語法現象的比較為題。 2. 《尚書》與金文的對比分析：除了《詩》外，與金文在語言上較為接近的先秦古書尚有《尚書》，《尚書》雖然文字「詰屈聱牙」，古奧難懂，但是，倘若與金文對照，便會發現兩者有許多可參證之處，並且透過相近文例的對照，更可有助解決《尚書》中部分疑難字詞的釋讀問題。 3. 其他出土文獻與《詩》互證：除金文之外，戰國楚簡及漢簡中亦蘊含不少《詩》學的材料，而本計劃亦已酌量採用了清華簡中可與金文與《詩》共同參照的部分作出探討。事實上，除了清華簡外，上博簡、郭店簡、馬王堆漢墓帛書、阜陽漢簡等均有不少《詩》異文或《詩》學研究資料，故日後的研究亦可結合更多的出土文獻，就《詩》學問題作進一步的討論。

844811.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
844811.value: 本計劃以《詩經》與金文作全面的語言對比分析，當中以詞匯學的研究為主，並且兼及語法與音韻的考察。總括而言，本計劃的價值和意義大致可歸納為以下幾方面： 第一，本計劃對《詩經》與金文的共見詞匯作全盤的整理，揭示兩者具有不少可以相互參證之處；而且，透過兩者的比對，本計劃更為《詩經》及金文中不少疑難字的訓詁與釋讀問題帶來新見解。 第二，在虛詞的使用上，《詩經》與金文之間亦有不少可比觀的地方，借助兩種材料中虛詞現象的比較，本計劃就部分虛詞的性質及語法功能提出新的觀點。 第三，本計劃透過銘文語匯與其時代、地域的參照，歸納及綜合出具特殊時、地色彩的語匯，為上古方言現象的探討提供重要資料。 第四，本計劃借助金文的探討，並再結合新見的楚簡資料，就《詩經》中部分久懸未決的文獻問題提出新的看法。

845111.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
845111.value: Multifaceted data are very common in the human sciences. For example, according to rating criteria, student essays are graded by teachers; teachers’ performances are judged by students; singing contest participants are rated by experts; house appliances are rated by customers; employees’ performances are evaluated by managers; and client behavior is assessed by clinical psychologists. Often, these responses or performances are dichotomously (e.g., pass or fail) or polytomously scored (e.g., poor, satisfactory, good, or outstanding), which are now widely analyzed with item response theory (IRT). Standard IRT approaches to the analysis of multifaceted data are simplistic and may fail to reveal important information about measurement. First, most or all facets are treated as fixed effects. In reality, elements in a facet (e.g., clients, clinical psychologists, and behaviors) may be randomly selected from a population and should be treated as such. Second, interactions between facets are largely ignored. For example, in practice different raters may prefer different types of performances and they may exhibit different degrees of severity on different occasions. Standard IRT approaches do not consider interactions between facets and thus fail to describe and retrieve in-depth information about measurement. Third, an assumption of a uni-level data structure in standard IRT approaches fails to account for data with a multilevel structure (e.g., items are nested within an item family; repeated measures nested within a student, who is nested within a school). Fourth, no parameters are available to quantify directly the effect of differential facet functioning. In this project, I will develop a new framework using four major axes in order to integrate existing IRT models for multifaceted data, and to create new ones to resolve the above four major problems. Axis 1 concerns the effect of a facet, fixed or random; Axis 2 concerns interaction between facets; Axis 3 concerns data structure: uni-level or multi-level; and Axis 4 concerns assessment of differential facet functioning. This new framework will enable researchers to reassess the literature and develop new research lines, which will certainly accelerate the development of IRT models for multifaceted data. I will derive parameter estimation procedures, develop computer programs for estimation, and conduct a series of simulations to assess the effectiveness of parameter recovery and statistics for model comparison and model-data fit. Publicly accessible data sets will be analyzed to demonstrate the implications and applications of the new framework. 在人文科學中，多面相資料非常普遍，例如：教師依循評分規則，對學生的文章給予分數，學生評量教師的表現，專家對歌唱比賽的參賽者進行評分，消費者評價家電用品，管理人評量員工表現，以及臨床心理師評估求診者的行為表現等。這些表現可以是二元計分（例如成功或失敗），或是多元計分（例如不良、尚可、良好、優秀）。如今已廣泛地藉由試題反應理論（item response theory; IRT）來加以分析。一般的IRT取向在分析多相資料時過於簡化，以致未能得到重要的測量訊息。首先，多數、甚至是所有的面相都被視為固定效果；實際上，任一面相的組成（例如，求診者、心理師和行為）可能是從一母體中隨機抽樣，因此應視為隨機效果。再者，面相間的交互作用大多被忽略。例如：不同的評分者可能偏好不同的表演形式，也可能在不同的時間有著不同的嚴苛度。一般的IRT取向並未考量面相間的交互作用，因此未能描述與擷取更深層的測量訊息。第三，一般IRT取向中的單一資料層次假設無法說明資料的多層次結構（例如，試題嵌套於題族之中；對同一學生進行重複測量，且學生從屬在學校層級之下）。第四，一般IRT取向的模型中未有參數能直接量化差別面相功能的影響。 在這個計劃中，我將沿著四個主軸來發展新的架構，以求整合既有的多面相資料的IRT模式，並創造新的架構以解答上述的四個重要課題。第一個主軸是，各面相是固定效果，抑或隨機效果；第二個主軸關心各面相間的交互作用；第三個主軸關心的是資料結構，是單一層次，抑或多層次；第四個主軸則關心差別面相功能的評量。這個新的架構將使研究者能夠再次回顧文獻並發展新的研究路線，並促使多面相資料IRT模式的發展。我將推導出參數估計算則、發展用以參數估計的電腦程式，並進行一系列的模擬研究以評估參數回復的效果，及模式比較與模式─資料適配度的統計量。最後，我將分析可公開取得的數據資料，用以說明新架構的意涵與應用時機。

845111.label: Realisation of objectives
845111.value: I have successfully achieved the five major objectives during the proposed duration. The shortcomings of existing IRT models have been identified and critiqued by theoretical analysis, which include (a) ignorance of interaction among raters, (b) ignorance of rater-ratee interaction, (c) suitable for unidimensional and unilevel data, but not feasible for multidimensional and multilevel data, (d) suitable for uniorder latent traits, but not feasible for higher-order latent traits, (e) ignorance of effects of positively- and negatively-worded items, and others. A new IRT framework has been developed, which also allows for users to generate their own customized models for new issues. Specifically, I have published four journal articles and one under review to tackle each of these five issues. Objective 1 and 2 were mainly completed during months 1-6. Parameter estimation procedures (e.g., MCMC methods) have been documented and tested with simulation studies. Good parameter recovery has been observed. Model comparison and model-data fit statistics for the new models have been investigated. Objective 3 and 4 were mainly completed during months 7-18. Finally, all these new initiatives have been demonstrated with various empirical examples, ranging from international large-scale assessments such as PISA and TIMSS to high stake exams such as Basic Competence Tests for Junior High School Students in Taiwan and others. In addition to four journal articles and one article under review, seven presentations have been made at international conferences. Objective 5 was completed during the second year of the project. The finance of this project was well managed. Journal Papers (* corresponding author): 1. Wang, W.-C.*, Chen, H.-F., & Jin, K.-Y. (2015). 845111.label: Major findings and research outcome
845111.value: Existing IRT models for facets data have certain limitations. In this project, I have developed a new and general framework of item response theory to tap at each of the five issues. In the new framework, all of these five issues can be successfully resolved. That is, interaction among raters and between raters and ratees can be considered, modeling multidimensional and multilevel data becomes feasible, higher-order latent traits can be properly accounted for, and the wording effect can be investigated. The parameters can be well recovered and the new models improved the accuracy of item and person estimation. The reliability, validity and fairness are thus ensured. The new initiatives are readily for applied to educational practice, including in Hong Kong. The following are the abstracts of the five articles: 1. Item Response Models for Local Dependence among Multiple Ratings By adding random-effect parameters to the facets model, we propose a class of generalized rater models to account for the local dependence among multiple ratings and intrarater variation in severity. An empirical example is provided. 2. A Multidimensional and Multilevel Extension of a Random-Effect Approach to Subjective Judgment in Rating Scales This study develops a multidimensional and multilevel version of the random-effect rating scale model (RERSM). An empirical example of the application of the multidimensional and multilevel RERSM to 2006 Program for International Student Assessment inventories about attitudes toward learning sciences is provided. 3. Higher-Order Item Response Models for Hierarchical Latent Traits This study aimed to develop a new class of higher order item response theory models for hierarchical latent traits. Two empirical examples of achievement and personality assessments were given to demonstrate applications and implications of the new models. 4. Item Response Theory Models for Wording Effects in Mixed-Format Scales In this study, we commented on the drawbacks of existing approaches to wording effect in mixed-format scales and used bi-factor IRT models to test the assumption of reverse coding and evaluate the magnitude of the wording effect. Two empirical examples from the Program for International Student Assessment and the Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study were given. 5. Assessment of Differential Rater Functioning When Ratee's Group Membership is Latent Differential rater functioning (DRF) may occur when the group membership of ratees is unknown (latent). In this study, we developed a new mixture DRF model to assess DRF when the membership is latent. An empirical example was provided.

845111.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
845111.value: In each of these five journal articles, my co-authors and I have listed a few suggestions for further development, such as exploring rater interaction within the framework of the hierarchical rater model, investigating differential facet functioning when group membership is observed or latent, integrating multidimensional and multilevel models, missing data mechanisms, combining higher-order latent traits and multilevel data structure, exploring wording effects of double negative items, and among others. In this project, I have developed new IRT models to tackle complicated issues. I plan to further extend these new IRT models to the framework of cognitive diagnostic models, which can provide fine-grained diagnostic profile information of test-takers. Our pilot study has been presented in an international conference (Li & Wang, 2013). Further attempts are underway. My team has been working on some of these further developments and hopefully we can yield more research findings and generate more publications in the near future.

845111.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
845111.value: Facets data are common in social and educational context. For example, students' papers are rated by teachers, performances are rated by judges. Conventional IRT models for facets data have many limitations and may not be feasible for complicated test data. In reality, testings are often very complicated, such as raters may be interacted with one another, different rater may exhibit different severity for different ratees, latent traits may have a hierarchical structure, ratees may be sampled from multiple stages, and positively and negatively worded items may somewhat induce different effects. If these kinds of complexity are not properly accounted for, the resulting parameter estimates would be biased, which in turn will lead to incorrect decisions. In this project, I have successfully developed a new framework to account for the complexity that is often faced in practice. All the five major goals have been successfully achieved. Empirical examples are provided to demonstrate implications and applications of these new initiatives, making knowledge transfer readily available. Moreover, these new initiatives create new research lines. Thanks to the continued support from the RGC, HKIEd, and my collaborators, I was installed in the 2014 Class of the American Educational Research Association (AERA) Fellows.

845211.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
845211.value: 人類的判斷與決策既包含了認知的“冷”處理過程，也包含了情感的“熱”處理過程。冷和熱的雙處理系統提供了一個理解社會行為的整體及連貫的框架。本研究嘗試有系統地調查“冷”的認知觀點採擇和“熱”的情感觀點採擇對兒童分配公平的影響。分配公平是指人們如何看待什麼是公正的人與人之間的貨物分配。公平分配有三個原則：1平等原則，即平均分配的原則；2公平原則，即基於貢獻按比例分享的原則；和3需要原則，即以每人的需要為基礎的分享原則。影響兒童公平分配的有兩個關鍵因素：認知上的觀點採擇，即所謂的心智理解，以及同理心。心智理解關注的是兒童如何理解其他人的觀點，所以是社會性兒童的理智層面；而同理心關注的是兒童如何對他人感同身受，所以是社會性兒童的情感層面。其他影響公平分配的因素包括年齡，性別，社會經濟地位和家庭特徵。本研究提出，心智理解和同理心是兩個理論上有相關但又同時有截然區別的概念；他們同時影響兒童的分配公平。在三個概念上有漸進性的研究裡，本研究將檢視冷和熱的雙重加工系統對兒童的分配公平發展的影響。 研究1的目的是確認心智理解和同理心是兩個不同的概念，並且為後續研究開發可靠和有效的測量方法。採用多特質多方法的測量手段，心智理解和同理心的測量將包括家長報告，兒童報告，以及兒童行為。研究2採用遊戲的範式，研究心智理解和同理心以及其他變量對兒童分配公平的影響。研究2包括兩個研究設計。 研究2.1探討心智理解和同理心，以及年齡，性別，社會經濟地位和家庭特徵對兒童在經濟遊戲中與他人分享的比例的預測能力。研究2.2使用實驗設計的模式誘導心智理解和同理心，以確定心智理解和同理心及分配公平之間的因果關係 。研究3考察心智理解和同理心對兒童選擇分配原則的影響，即平等原則，公平原則，和需要原則。本研究預計，心智理解和同理心都會影響兒童與他人分享的比例和分配原則。不過，心智理解可能與分配過程中的認知計算有關，而同理心就和關心他人利益及需要原則有關。年齡可預測兒童分享的比例份額。越年長的兒童越有可能願意分享。年長的兒童也更可能採用更複雜的分配原則，如公平原則或需要原則。性別可能與同理心有關。女孩可能比男孩更能移情。來自富裕家庭的兒童可能比來自貧困家庭的兒童更大方。家庭大小和出生順序可能也影響兒童的分配，但是現在還不確定有兄弟姐妹會使得兒童更願意分享還是相反。這項研究的結果將展現分配過程的認知和情感的加工處理，促進理解兒童關心他人利益的心理起源和發展機制。結果將對幼兒德育及公民教育有啟示意義，並且對發展下一代的社會責任感以及政治和經濟穩定，個體和集體的繁榮有長遠影響。

845211.label: Realisation of objectives
845211.value: The first objective was to establish measures for the cognitive and affective factors that influence children’s distributive justice. Two rounds of data were collected in developing a parent questionnaire: the Empathy and Theory of Mind Scale (EToMS). The reliability and validity of the EToMS were established in relation to child measures, making it a useful assessment of children’s social predispositions. The second objective was to identify the relationship between these factors and children’s sharing behavior. The results demonstrated that children’s theory of mind was related to children’s performance in the Ultimatum Game but not in the Dictator Game, in accordance to the hypothesis. Moreover, inducing theory of mind in children increased their sharing in the Ultimatum Game, suggesting that theory of mind is a causal factor in children’s sharing. The third objective was to examine the developmental changes and gender differences in children’s sharing behavior, and the effect of social economic status and personal attributes including birth order and number of siblings. The results found that age, social economic status, and language ability were significantly correlated to children’s sharing behavior, but not gender or family size. The last objective was to examine the development of children’s distributive principles based on fairness, respective contribution, and need, and its relationship with ToM and empathy development. Preliminary data analysis found that empathy could predict distributive principle based on need, yet the effect of theory of mind was inconclusive. In addition to achieving these objectives, we managed to collect extra parental interview data when parents were waiting outside of the lab while their children doing the testing. The collection of the extra data did not require extra resources, by the transcribing and coding of the data were labor intensive, for which we needed to extend the duration of the project. This data turned out to be very informative in terms how parenting attitude affects children's prosocial behavior, directly or indirectly. This adds the much needed social context to the developmental nature of the study.

845211.label: Major findings and research outcome
845211.value: The EToMS was a reliable and valid measure of parent report on child theory of mind and empathy. This rationale of the questionnaire design was presented at Chinese Psychological Association annual conference in Guangzhou in 2012; and the data were presented at the 18th Biennial Conference of the Australasian Human Development Association in 2013. The final paper was published in a peer refereed journal in 2015. As part of the study 1, we also collected data on children’s social behavior in the attempt to validate the parent questionnaire. We found that children’s false belief understanding did not predict their lie telling behavior, contrary to others’ results. We argue lying is an act of breaking (adhering in some cases) social norms that does not necessarily involve mental state understanding. This data was presented at Society of Research in Child Development (SRCD) Biennial conference in 2015, and currently under review by a peer reviewed journal. We also found that theory of mind and inhibitory control predicted children’s social behaviors such as keeping a secret and practical joke. This finding was presented at Society for Research in Human Development (SRHD) Biennial Meeting in 2014. The full paper is in preparation. In study 2 we examined children’s sharing behavior and its relation with theory of mind and empathy. Contrary to our hypothesis, empathy was not a significant predictor for sharing. However, we did find theory of mind as a significant predictor of sharing behavioral, especially when theory of mind was induced in the participants by asking them to consider what the opponent in the game would think about them before they make the sharing decision. This result is very exciting since it demonstrates the causal effect of theory of mind in sharing behaviors. This part of the data were presented in an invited symposium at the 23rd Biennial Meeting of the International Society for the Study of Behavioural Development (ISSBD) in 2015. The full paper is in preparation. In study 3 we found that children's prevalent distributive principle was equality, yet empathy was related to need based sharing principle. This part of the study is being presented at the conference in July 2016. From the parental interview, we found that parental mindmindedness (to what extend the parents regard their children as mental agents) significantly predicted both children's theory of mind and their sharing behavior. This part is being submitted to a conference in 2016.

845211.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
845211.value: Currently we are still in the process of writing manuscripts based on the data achieved from this project. We expect to submit 3-4 more full papers from the data. This project demonstrated the importance of theory of mind and empathy in children's prosocial development. We extended this idea and developed another proposal on the emergence of strong reciprocity (upholding social norms at own cost) and its relationship with child characteristics including theory of mind and empathy. This proposal is funded by GRF (reference 18612415) and is scheduled to start from January 2016. In this new study we are testing the ethical stance hypothesis in strong reciprocity, and examining both the positive strong reciprocity and the negative reciprocity simultaneously. we hypothesized that children who score high on theory of mind and delayed gratification, but low on empathy are more likely to punish the norm violators, while those high on empathy are more likely to reward the norm followers.

845211.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
845211.value: This project demonstrated the importance of hearts and minds in children's prosocial sharing behaviors. By simply asking children to think about what their recipient would think of them before they make the decision of how much to share with them could significantly increase children's sharing proportion. Even though asking children to consider others' misfortune did not significantly increase their sharing proportions, empathy was related to their sharing principle choice. This project also demonstrated the social and cultural context's effect in children's prosocial development, in this case, the parenting attitude. Those parents who treat their children as independent agent with a mind of their own tend to have children who are more considerate and share more with peers. The findings lend support to what the educators believe about moral discipline. Induction is the most effective way to instill a moral responsibility in young children. Parents and teachers should focus on helping children to see things from others' perspective in order to foster a more empathetic, prosocial generation.
